# A fixed quadratic core with an exact terminal affine cap

Status: complete new candidate derivation, unverified. Worker: max3.
This repairs one specific deficiency of the verified outward-ray construction:
the prefix may return inside a previously visited region arbitrarily many
times, because one fixed quadratic governs all those returns.

## Legal function and exact trajectory

Fix any n>=1 and nonnegative finite schedule h, any lambda in (0,1], a sign
sigma in {-1,+1}, and an index j in {0,...,n-1}. Define prefix polynomials

\[
p_0(\lambda)=1,\qquad p_t(\lambda)=\prod_{r<t}(1-h_r\lambda).
\]

Define

\[
R=\max\{0,\sigma p_t(\lambda):0\leq t\leq j\},\qquad
A=\sigma p_{j+1}(\lambda),\qquad T=\sum_{r>j}h_r.
\]

Assume A>0 and A>=(1+lambda T)R. Choose a cap radius

\[
r\in[R,A/(1+\lambda T)].
\]

The explicit function is

\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}
\lambda x^2/2,&\sigma x\leq r,\\
\lambda r\sigma x-\lambda r^2/2,&\sigma x\geq r.
\end{cases}
\tag{1}
\]

The two branches and their derivatives agree at sigma x=r. Its derivative
is continuous, nondecreasing, and lambda-Lipschitz, hence at most1-Lipschitz;
it is convex and differentiable and has minimum0 at0. These properties also
hold when r=0, in which case one side is flat. The entire function is fixed
before the GD run, after observing the predetermined schedule.

Start x_0=1. For every query through j, sigma p_t(lambda)<=r. An induction
therefore gives x_t=p_t(lambda) and f'(x_t)=lambda p_t(lambda) through that
prefix. All sign changes and inner returns in the prefix are legal without
resetting the function or dropping older values. The update at j gives
sigma x_{j+1}=A. On the suffix the derivative is the fixed value
sigma lambda r. Nonnegative steps and A>=(1+lambda T)r imply that every
suffix iterate stays in the capped region, since its signed coordinate is at
least A-lambda rT>=r. Thus

\[
\sigma x_n=A-\lambda rT,\qquad
2f(x_n)=2\lambda rA-\lambda(1+2\lambda T)r^2.
\tag{2}
\]

The initial squared distance to the minimizer is1. Multiplying (1) by L
gives the same normalized error for the original h_t/L steps at arbitrary
L>0. The best radius in the displayed interval is

\[
r_{\rm opt}=\max\{R,A/(1+2\lambda T)\}.
\tag{3}
\]

The right endpoint is never exceeded by (3), because T>=0. This gives a
fully explicit lower-bound functional after maximizing over feasible
(lambda,sigma,j). The record R is essential: choosing a smaller radius would
change the already used prefix function and invalidate the polynomial formula.

## A strict improvement beyond outward rays plus quadratics

Take the exact four-step schedule h=(8/5,8/5,13,1), choose lambda=1,
sigma=-1 and j=2. The core prefix is

\[
x_0=1,\quad x_1=-3/5,\quad x_2=9/25,\quad x_3=-108/25.
\]

Thus R=3/5, A=108/25, T=1 and r_opt=36/25. Formula (1) is simply the
unit-curvature quadratic above -36/25, continued affinely below that point.
The final step gives x_4=-72/25, and the normalized error is exactly

\[
2f(x_4)=\frac{A^2}{3}=\frac{3888}{625}.
\tag{4}
\]

This strictly exceeds the combination of the previously considered two
channels on this schedule, as the following exact comparisons establish.

### Exact outward-ray value

Use the functional F_ray_4 from verified fact1fca3e5dd555cb4a. Any feasible
chain with two or more checkpoints uses only the first three steps: a final
checkpoint equal to1 gives nonpositive distance budget and cannot satisfy the
positive old-slope requirement. Chains with zero or one checkpoint give

\[
K_4(h)=\max\{5/177,9/805,9/4901,400/147,0\}=400/147.
\]

For two checkpoints at indices(0,1), the terminal budget is9/25 whereas its
required lower bound is15, so it is infeasible. For indices(0,2), the verified
recurrence gives m_0=1,m_1=3/13,O_1=0,z_term=36/13,s_2=1,m_old=1.
Its optimizing q is1 and the payoff is33/13. For indices(1,2), it gives
m_0=5/13,m_1=3/13,O_1=8/13,z_term=28/13,s_2=1,m_old=5/13,
e_term=40/169; its optimum payoff is1024/507. The three-checkpoint choice
(0,1,2) has m_2=9/25<m_0=1 and is infeasible. This exhausts all eligible
sets. Both33/13 and1024/507 are less than400/147. Therefore

\[
F_{\rm ray,4}(h)=400/147.
\]

### A sufficient exact quadratic upper bound

For this h the full quadratic-class error is

\[
Q_4(h)=\max_{0\leq t\leq1}
t(1-8t/5)^4(1-13t)^2(1-t)^2.
\]

For 0<=t<=1, |(1-13t)(1-t)|<=36/13. On [0,1/13] the product is at
most1 in absolute value; on [1/13,1] its magnitude is the concave quadratic
(13t-1)(1-t), whose maximum36/13 is attained at t=7/13.
If t<=5/8 then |1-8t/5|<=1 and the displayed objective is at most
(5/8)(36/13)^2=810/169. If t>=5/8 then |1-8t/5|<=3/5 and the objective
is at most(3/5)^4(36/13)^2=104976/105625<1. Thus

\[
\max\{F_{\rm ray,4}(h),Q_4(h)\}\leq810/169
<3888/625.
\]

The last inequality is exact: their ratio is4056/3125>1. The new witness
therefore adds a real legal interaction beyond a maximum of the old channels.
This fixed-horizon improvement in a lower-bound family is not a resolution
of the asymptotic minimax problem.

## Remaining target obligation

No claim is made that the supremum of (2), even together with F_ray_n and Q_n,
matches the exact ZJ profile for every schedule. The specific new mechanism
is a legal quadratic prefix, including inner returns, followed by a nonlinear
continuation constrained by an exact remote-excursion record. A next extension
could allow a fixed two-curvature core or repeated cap exits and returns, but
must preserve the old record and values instead of independently resampling
curvature. Any uniform profile comparison still needs an actual proof.

evidence:
# P5 retains inner returns that the outward-ray family omits
Status: new analytic candidate; not verifier-accepted. The only cited correctness bricks are facts 1fca3e5dd555cb4a and b98bb807d514e80d. This document gives a self-contained legal-function calculation, without relying on another unverified construction as a brick.

For n>=8 let h_t=(t+1)/2 for 0<=t<n. Set c=2/5 and define the global derivative
q(x)=x for x<=2/5,
q(x)=2/5 for 2/5<=x<=1,
q(x)=x-3/5 for x>=1.
Let f(x)=integral_0^x q(z)dz. The derivative is continuous, nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz, with q(0)=0. Thus f is convex differentiable, 1-smooth, minimized at0 with value0. The initial point is1, so the normalized error is2f(x_n).

The exact first eight steps are
x_0=1, x_1=4/5, x_2=2/5, x_3=-1/5,
x_4=1/5, x_5=-3/10, x_6=3/5, x_7=-4/5, x_8=12/5.
Direct substitution into q and x_{t+1}=x_t-h_t q(x_t) verifies all these values.
In particular x_4 and x_6 return inside the previous positive-ray record1. An adversary restricted to successive outward ray records cannot follow this chronology.

For every t>=8 the signs alternate and |x_t|>=12/5. If x_t<0 then
|x_{t+1}|=((t-1)/2)|x_t| >= (t/4)|x_t|.
If x_t>0 then
x_{t+1}= -((t-1)/2)x_t+3(t+1)/10.
Using x_t>=12/5 gives
|x_{t+1}| >= [(t-1)/2-(t+1)/8]|x_t|
 =((3t-5)/8)|x_t| >= (t/4)|x_t|.
The last bound holds for t>=5; with t>=8 it also preserves the magnitude lower bound and proves the claimed alternating signs. Hence
|x_n| >= (12/5) product_{t=8}^{n-1}(t/4).

For x<0, 2f(x)=x^2. For x>=1,
2f(x)=(x-3/5)^2+12/25.
This is at least x^2/4: the difference is
(3/4)x^2-(6/5)x+21/25
=(3/4)(x-4/5)^2+9/25 >0.
Therefore the legal one-dimensional objective satisfies
W_n(h)>=2f(x_n)>=(36/25)[product_{t=8}^{n-1}(t/4)]^2.
The product is (n-1)!/[7! 4^(n-8)] for n>=8. This grows faster than any fixed power. No computation or exhaustive search is part of the proof.

## Membership in the concrete P5 action tree
The seed j=2 in P5 forces c=1/(1+h_0+h_1)=2/5, agreeing with the displayed first three queried gradients. Thereafter taking the signed steep envelope at every step reproduces q. Here is the direct envelope check, so this assertion is not a reliance on an unverified earlier finding.

The stored knots at(0,0),(2/5,2/5),(1,2/5) force the upper gradient envelope on the positive half-line to be exactly q there: the origin bounds it by x, the knot at2/5 bounds it by2/5 for smaller x and by x for larger x, and the knot at1 bounds it by2/5 below1 and by x-3/5 above1. Taking the minimum gives the displayed q. Every other positive queried knot lies on q, so cannot tighten this envelope below q. On the negative half-line the lower envelope supplied by the origin is x. All positive knots have v<=y, so v-(y-x)<=x and cannot raise it. Every negative knot on q(x)=x likewise preserves that envelope. Thus every subsequent signed steep query equals q(x_t), including the interior returns.

Consequently this single leaf is present in P5. Under the original fair law its probability is2^{-(n-3)}, which already leaves a diverging lower bound after multiplication by the factorial-square payoff. Under the separately derived power tilt its expected payoff is within2^{-1/n} of the maximum leaf; that probability repair is an unverified companion candidate, not needed for the present legal-function lower bound.

## Scope
Finding97c780b4975678c7 gives an unverified analytic argument that the accepted functional F_ray_n from fact1fca3e5dd555cb4a collapses to K_n and is O(n^-2) on this same half-linear family. The present construction does not depend on that argument: it independently establishes a large legal objective and membership in the richer P5 tree. It shows that failing the outward-record restriction is not a reason to abandon scalar envelope branching.

No all-schedule comparison to U_n^ZJ is claimed. In particular an instability test on this family does not supply the still-missing inequality on schedules with bounded worst-case objective.

claim: Candidate full-certificate stationary energy invariant at genuine global minimizers: boundary, duality and degeneracy arguments supplied; exact one-step primal-dual check passes.
evidence:
# Global minimizers and a stationary energy identity for full PEP certificates

Status: exploratory, unverified proof package. No extra verifier submission is authorized. The selected initial submission was used for fact dfde2fa326c908bf. This document does not establish the exact-profile target.

## 1. Claim under investigation

For each fixed horizon n>=1, the project minimization over h in [0,infinity)^n has a global minimizer, and every global minimizer has strictly positive steps. At any such minimizer there exist a full interpolation upper certificate (q,lambda), a legal primal Gram matrix G and values f_i, attaining q=W_n^*, for which

    <g_t,z_t>=0, 0<=t<n,                                      (S)
    q=(1/2) sum_{i,j} lambda_ij ||g_i-g_j||^2.                 (E)

Here the Euclidean vectors realize G, x_*=g_*=0, ||x_0||=1, and

    z_t=sum_{i>t}(mu_i+sum_{j<=t}lambda_ij)g_i
        -sum_{i<=t}(sum_{j>t}lambda_ij)g_i,                    (Z)
    mu_i=lambda_{i,*}.

Every unstarred sum ranges over 0,...,n; directed pairs are distinct. The assertion retains the full certificate PSD constraint and the full primal interpolation constraints. It does not claim that these displayed identities alone characterize global minimizers.

The proof below supplies the compactness, zero-step exclusion, strong-duality and multiplier-regularity arguments rather than assuming interiority or nonsingular multipliers.

## 2. Fixed-horizon compactness and positive optimal steps

Normalize L=1, x_*=0 and f_*=0. For any fixed finite h, the estimates ||g_i||<=||x_i|| and ||x_{i+1}||<= (1+h_i)||x_i|| imply W_n(h)<=prod_i(1+h_i)^2. Every fixed legal function and initial point has an error continuous in h, by continuity of its gradient. A supremum of continuous functions is lower semicontinuous, so W_n is lower semicontinuous.

Write Poly_n(z)=prod_{t<n}(1-h_t z). For n+1 distinct nodes a_k=k/(n+1), 1<=k<=n+1, the quadratic f(x)=a_k x^2/2 from x_0=1 gives

    a_k Poly_n(a_k)^2 <= W_n(h).

Define the Lagrange polynomials L_k(z)=prod_{l!=k}(z-a_l)/(a_k-a_l). On the sublevel W_n(h)<=1, interpolation of a polynomial of degree at most n gives

    sum_t h_t = -Poly_n'(0)
      <= sum_k |L_k'(0)|/sqrt(a_k) =: C_n < infinity.

Nonnegativity of the steps therefore bounds each h_t by C_n. The sublevel is closed, bounded, and nonempty because h=0 has W_n=1. Lower semicontinuity on this compact set proves attainment of the global infimum.

For positivity, first note the explicit Huber lower bound. Put S=sum h_t and delta=1/(2S+1). The function f(x)=x^2/2 for |x|<=delta, and delta|x|-delta^2/2 otherwise, is convex and 1-smooth. From x_0=1, every iterate is x_i=1-delta sum_{t<i}h_t>=delta; its terminal error is 2f(x_n)=1/(2S+1)>0.

Suppose a globally minimizing length-n schedule contains a zero. Delete that zero to obtain h' of length n-1 with exactly the same terminal point and worst-case value q>0. Set B=prod_{t<n-1}(1+h'_t), so every normalized legal instance has terminal radius at most B. If its terminal function gap is F, convexity gives F<=B||g||, and a final unit step gives

    F_new <= F-||g||^2/2 <= F-F^2/(2B^2).

We have 0<=F<=q/2<=B^2/2. The displayed scalar function is increasing on this interval. Thus appending a unit step to h' produces another length-n schedule satisfying

    W_n(h',1) <= q-q^2/(4B^2) < q,

contradicting global minimality. Therefore every minimizing step is positive. This argument also handles the all-zero proposed minimizer and uses no differentiability of W_n.

## 3. Exact finite-dimensional primal formulation

Let I={*,0,...,n}. For i!=j define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

The primal variables are the Gram matrix G of (x_0,g_0,...,g_n), with G>=0 and G_00<=1, together with the real values f_0,...,f_n. The remaining positions are defined by x_i=x_0-sum_{t<i}h_t g_t, and the optimum sample is zero. Impose Q_ij<=0 for every ordered pair. Maximize 2f_n.

For completeness, the interpolation sufficiency has the following explicit proof. Given such finite vector/value data, put a_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i and

    H(v)=max_i {a_i+<x_i,v-g_i>+||v-g_i||^2/2}.

At v=g_i, the i-th expression is a_i and every j-th expression is at most a_i, because that comparison is exactly -Q_ij>=0. Hence H(g_i)=a_i and x_i belongs to the convex subdifferential of H at g_i. The function H is finite and 1-strongly convex, with quadratic growth. Its conjugate f=H^* is finite everywhere, convex, differentiable and 1-smooth, and satisfies f(x_i)=f_i and grad f(x_i)=g_i. Indeed, strong convexity makes the maximizing vector in the conjugate unique; the strong monotonicity of the subgradient relation bounds the distance between two such maximizing vectors by the distance between their arguments. This gives the claimed gradient Lipschitz constant. The zero sample makes zero a minimizer. Thus the primal optimum is exactly W_n(h), with dimension at most n+2.

The feasible primal set is compact: the radius/gradient estimates above bound all Gram entries; the two optimum interpolation inequalities imply 0<=f_i<=||x_i||^2/2. It is closed and nonempty, so its optimum is attained.

For positive h, the primal admits strict interpolation inequalities and G positive definite. Take n+2 distinct numbers theta_k in (0,1), the quadratic with diagonal Hessian diag(theta_k), and an initial vector having every coordinate nonzero and norm less than one. The columns x_0,g_0,...,g_n are evaluations of 1,zPoly_0(z),...,zPoly_n(z) at these nodes, times nonzero coordinate factors. Their distinct degrees and nonzero leading coefficients make this matrix invertible. No two sampled positions agree, because their different prefix polynomials cannot agree at n+2 distinct nodes. None equals zero for the same degree reason. Direct substitution gives

    Q_ij=-(1/2)sum_k theta_k(1-theta_k)(x_{i,k}-x_{j,k})^2 <0

for every distinct pair, including *. The norm inequality is also strict.

Source context: Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur, arXiv:1502.05666, Theorem 4 and Theorem 6 treat smooth-convex interpolation and strong duality for fixed-step methods using the latest gradient with nonzero coefficient. Their proof uses a full-rank quadratic transcript. The preceding Vandermonde construction and the separation argument below provide the needed hypotheses and conclusion directly here; no general-step extension is presumed.

## 4. Full dual attainment by finite-dimensional separation

Let T_ij(G) denote the gradient/position part of Q_ij, so Q_ij=f_i-f_j+T_ij(G). Consider the open convex set of triples (a,b,c) for which some G>=0 and some f satisfy

    a_ij>Q_ij(f,G), b>G_00-1, c<2f_n.

The point (0,0,q), where q is the finite primal optimum, is outside this set. A separating hyperplane, using the independent upward variations of a,b and downward variation of c, has nonnegative coefficients lambda_ij, q_0, alpha, not all zero, and yields

    sum lambda_ij Q_ij(f,G)+q_0(G_00-1)-alpha*2f_n >= -alpha*q

for all G>=0 and all f. The strict primal point constructed above rules out alpha=0: substituting it would make the left side strictly negative whenever lambda or q_0 is nonzero. Thus normalize alpha=1.

The arbitrary f coordinates force

    out_i-in_i=2*1_{i=n}.

The arbitrary PSD matrix G then forces

    M(q_0,lambda,h)=q_0 E_00+sum lambda_ij T_ij >=0.

Taking G=f=0 gives q_0<=q. Conversely the flow and PSD constraints give an upper certificate W_n(h)<=q_0. Therefore q_0=q and the full dual is attained.

This argument establishes the direction needed here: at a minimizing positive schedule there is a certificate with q exactly equal to its true worst-case value. A feasible upper certificate by itself is never interpreted as a lower bound.

## 5. A strictly feasible certificate at every finite h

A regularity direction is needed because the optimal certificate can have many zero multipliers and singular PSD slack. We now construct a certificate with all directed multipliers positive and M positive definite at the same fixed h.

For each finite i, adding equal weight to lambda_{i,*} and lambda_{*,i} preserves the flow. Their quadratic sum is

    Q_{i,*}+Q_{*,i}=||g_i||^2-<g_i,x_i>.

Let H_max=max_t h_t, r=1/(2H_max+3), and w_i=r^(2i)>0. The gradient block A_w of the weighted sum of these cycles has diagonal w_i and, for i>t, off-diagonal w_i h_t/2. With D=diag(w_i), the matrix D^(-1/2) A_w D^(-1/2) has diagonal one and off-diagonal h_t r^(i-t)/2. Each row's absolute off-diagonal sum is at most H_max*r/(1-r)<1/2. Hence A_w is positive definite, as follows also by bounding each cross term with the two corresponding squared coordinates.

Start with lambda_{n,*}=2, and add weight one to every directed finite-to-finite pair. Those paired edges are flow-balanced. Next add K w_i to each of lambda_{i,*} and lambda_{*,i}. All directed multipliers are now positive and the required flow holds. For sufficiently large finite K, their gradient block A is positive definite, because K A_w dominates the fixed remaining symmetric matrix. The full matrix has form

    M=[[q,-mu^T/2],[-mu/2,A]],  mu_i=lambda_{i,*}.

Choosing q>mu^T A^(-1)mu/4 makes M positive definite. This constructs strict feasibility with no assumptions on which multipliers of the optimum vanish.

## 6. KKT without assumed nondegeneracy

Take a global minimizing positive schedule h and an attained certificate (q,lambda). It is also a global minimizer of q over the joint variables (q,lambda,h), subject to flow, lambda>=0 and M>=0: every such certificate upper-bounds a true W_n(h)>=W_n^*.

Here is the finite-dimensional separation argument giving the needed multipliers. Restrict directions d to the linear flow-null space. Let J be the set of zero lambda entries, and let K_0=ker M. If a direction satisfies

    dq<0, d lambda_e>0 for e in J,
    (DM[d]) restricted to K_0 is positive definite,

then a sufficiently small positive step along it is feasible and improves q. To justify the matrix assertion, decompose into K_0 and its orthogonal complement. The complementary block of M is positive definite, the kernel block has a positive first-order term, and cross blocks are first order. The Schur complement subtracts only a second-order term. The dependence on h and lambda is polynomial, so its Taylor remainder is also second order. Positivity of h persists for sufficiently small steps. Such a descent direction is therefore impossible.

Separating the image of the direction space from the open cone defined by these three strict inequalities gives an objective multiplier alpha>=0, numbers r_e>=0 supported on J, and a PSD matrix G supported on K_0, not all zero, annihilating every flow-null direction:

    alpha*dq - sum r_e*d lambda_e - <G,DM[d]> =0.

Move from the optimal certificate toward the strictly feasible certificate from section 5 while holding h fixed. That direction has every d lambda_e>0 on J and has positive compression of DM to K_0. Substituting it rules out alpha=0, unless r=G=0, which would contradict nontrivial separation. Normalize alpha=1.

Extending the annihilator by flow multipliers written as -f_i gives the coefficient identities

    G_00=1,
    f_i-f_j+T_ij(G)=-r_ij<=0,
    lambda_ij r_ij=0,
    M G=0,
    <G,partial M/partial h_t>=0 for every t.

The PSD matrix G is consequently a legal normalized primal Gram matrix by section 3. The interpolation inequalities and lambda complementarity imply sum lambda_ij Q_ij=0. Taking the trace of M G then gives q=2f_n. Thus G realizes an actual worst-case transcript. Degenerate lambda and singular M were allowed throughout.

If either J or K_0 is empty, omit its corresponding strict-cone factor and multiplier. The same argument applies in these zero-dimensional cases.

## 7. The resulting quantitative identities

Let x_0,g_0,...,g_n be Euclidean vectors with Gram matrix G. Expanding the derivative with respect to h_t gives exactly

    partial/partial h_t [sum lambda_ij T_ij]
      = <g_t,
          sum_{i>t}(mu_i+sum_{j<=t}lambda_ij)g_i
          -sum_{i<=t}(sum_{j>t}lambda_ij)g_i >.

The stationary equations are therefore (S) with z_t defined in (Z), including every edge that crosses the chronological cut t.

The x_0 row of M G=0 and G_00=1 give

    sum_i mu_i <x_0,g_i>=2q.                                  (X)

The full quadratic trace can be expanded as

    0=<M,G>
     =q-sum_i mu_i<x_0,g_i>
       +sum_{t<n}h_t<g_t,z_t>
       +(1/2)sum_{i,j}lambda_ij||g_i-g_j||^2.

Using (S) and (X) yields the announced energy identity (E). The energy is nonnegative, and all chronological cut terms have been justified individually rather than discarded.

These equations constrain both a full feasible dual certificate and a full feasible primal transcript at an actual global minimizer. They do not supply a uniform numerical comparison with the Zhang--Jiang recurrence yet.

## 8. Exact one-step primal-dual check

For n=1, h_0=3/2, q=1/4, take

    lambda_{0,*}=lambda_{1,*}=lambda_{1,0}=1,

with all other multipliers zero. Direct expansion yields

    M = v v^T, v=(1/2,-1,-1).

A matching stationary primal Gram matrix is

    G=[[1,1/3,1/6],
       [1/3,1/6,0],
       [1/6,0,1/12]],
    (f_0,f_1)=(1/4,1/8).

It is the convex combination with weights 8/9 and 1/9 of two legal one-dimensional transcripts, each starting at x_0=1:

* Huber threshold 1/4: (g_0,g_1)=(1/4,1/4), (f_0,f_1)=(7/32,1/8).
* Quadratic f(x)=x^2/2: (g_0,g_1)=(1,-1/2), (f_0,f_1)=(1/2,1/8).

The direct sum after coordinate scaling by the square roots of the weights is itself one legal two-dimensional instance, so the combination is not merely a formal averaging device. In detail, for weights a,b and scalar functions H,Q, use F(u,v)=a H(u/sqrt(a))+b Q(v/sqrt(b)) and initial point (sqrt(a),sqrt(b)); this preserves smoothness one and gives exactly the displayed Gram matrix and values.

The full matrix equality M G=0 holds. The cut vector is z_0=2g_1 and <g_0,g_1>=0, verifying stationarity. The directed energy is

    (1/2)(||g_0||^2+||g_1||^2+||g_1-g_0||^2)
      =1/6+1/12=1/4=q.

Global one-step optimality follows directly: the Huber lower bound is at least 1/4 for h_0<=3/2, and the quadratic lower bound (h_0-1)^2 is at least 1/4 for h_0>=3/2. The displayed certificate attains 1/4.

A hostile check is useful: the pure Huber transcript is worst-case for this very same optimal schedule and dual certificate, but has <g_0,g_1>=1/16 and fails stationarity. Thus it is invalid to assume that an arbitrary active worst-case function supplies the stationary primal matrix. The multiplier-separation construction selects a suitable primal matrix, and an admissible direct sum may be essential.

## 9. Exact remaining obstruction

The current identities do not force q to equal the sum-based Huber level, do not show lambda_{*,i}=0 at a global minimizer, and do not imply that all temporal gradients are orthogonal. Each such additional simplification would require its own proof or counterexample test.

A route to the target would still need a quantitative estimate combining the full PSD slack, all interpolation inequalities, the cut equations (S), and the energy (E), uniformly in horizon, whose constant matches the exact recurrence. Merely defining that missing estimate is not a result. The package above establishes a candidate rigorous interface at genuine global minimizers, with exact feasible-data checks, and records the current obstruction.

evidence:
# The exact DP already dominates every reset-doubling candidate

Status: self-contained unverified route rejection. Uses only the universal Huber lower bound in accepted fact 0be8b54e0a33381c and elementary algebra of the original DP. No new verification allocation is requested.

For every k,j>=0, the reset-doubling schedule q^(k,j) from research/max4_reset_seed_boundary_certificate.md satisfies
W_(len q^(k,j))(q^(k,j)) > U_(len q^(k,j))^ZJ.
Thus the entire stated family fails as a direct negative construction, including the smaller seed depths left open by the asymmetric-Huber test. No assertion about other richer joins or a modified family is made.

Notation: lambda=1+sqrt(2), A=lambda^k, B=beta_k-1, R=A+B+2, A=2B^2+B. The length n and shifted sum of the candidate are
n+1=2^j(2^k+2), 1+sum q^(k,j)=lambda^j R.
Write P_n=S_circle(n)+1 and D_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 (D_n is the benchmark B_n, renamed here only to avoid conflict with the seed parameter B). The shifted joins are
F(X,Y)=(X+Y+sqrt(X^2+6XY+Y^2))/2,
G(X,D)=2X+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8XD)/2.
Both are increasing in their arguments. F(X,X)=lambda X.

First, D_n>=2P_n-1 for all n. To check the needed comparison, take X,Y>=1 and C=F(X,Y), so C^2-(X+Y)C-XY=0. The polynomial whose larger root is G(X,2Y-1) is
q(z)=z^2-(4X+2Y-1)z+4X^2.
Direct substitution gives
q(2C-1)=2[X-(2X+1)(C-X-Y)].
Here C-X-Y=XY/C. Moreover C<X+2Y<=Y(2X+1), since 2XY-X-Y>=0 for X,Y>=1. Hence q(2C-1)<0. Therefore G(X,2Y-1)>2F(X,Y)-1. Induct on n along a maximizing primitive split and use the increasing dominant join. The case n=0 is equality. This proves the claim without assuming that the dominant DP literally lists every primitive schedule.

Balanced primitive splits also give P_(2^r-1)>=lambda^r for each r>=0. For our n, use the legal dominant split
m=2^(k+j)-1, ell=2^(j+1)-1, n=m+ell+1.
It follows that
D_n >= G(lambda^(k+j),2lambda^(j+1)-1)
     = lambda^j G(A,2lambda-u), where u=lambda^(-j) in (0,1].

It remains to compare this with the candidate's Huber denominator 2lambda^j R-1. Set d=2lambda-u and c=8-2lambda-u. We have d>1, c>0, d-c=4lambda-8>0, and d+c=8-2u>0. Using A=2B^2+B gives the exact identity

d^2+8Ad-(4B+c)^2
=16(d-1)B^2+8(d-c)B+(d-c)(d+c)>0.

All quantities under comparison are positive. Taking square roots and substituting into G gives
G(A,2lambda-u)>2A+2B+4-u=2R-u.
Consequently D_n>2lambda^j R-1.

Finally the Huber lower bound from fact_id 0be8b54e0a33381c yields
W_n(q^(k,j)) >=1/(2lambda^j R-1)>1/D_n=U_n^ZJ.
This is a pointwise rejection for every member of the concrete family, so it is stronger than merely ruling out a fixed asymptotic improvement. The same sum argument applies to a permutation of any such schedule, but does not establish how to modify its steps successfully.

Relation to the requested spectral screening in master_guidance ac69664acf0dee30:
For a quadratic f_mu(x)=mu x^2/2, 0<mu<=1, the candidate has the exact scalar recursion
p_(j+1)(mu)=p_j(mu)^2 [1-(1+lambda^(-1)R_j)mu], R_j=lambda^j R,
p_0(mu)=p_pi^(k)(mu)(1-beta_k mu)(1-mu).
Equivalently,
p_j(mu)=p_0(mu)^(2^j) product_(r=0)^(j-1)[1-(1+lambda^(r-1)R)mu]^(2^(j-1-r)).
The vanishing at mu=1 does not control the rest of this interval. No full-interval stability theorem is claimed. Since the exact profile comparison above already rules out every member as a direct negative schedule, neither a numerical spectrum sweep nor a large boundary-certificate search is needed to make this route decision.

evidence:
# P5 extension: exact history-aware plateau actions
Status: new complete construction and quantitative tests; unverified. No new verifier allocation requested. The uniform exact-profile comparison is still BLOCKED.

## 1. History and orientation
Work at L=1, minimizer0, initial point1. A finite history H contains(0,0) and gradient knots(y,v) satisfying 0<=v-w<=y-z whenever y>=z. Define
ell_H(r)=max_(y,v in H)[v-(y-r)_+],
u_H(r)=min_(y,v in H)[v+(r-y)_+].
The extrema of nondecreasing1-Lipschitz functions are again nondecreasing1-Lipschitz. The history inequalities show that both envelopes interpolate every knot. Hence a new gradient at r is legal exactly in[ell_H(r),u_H(r)]. Integrating either envelope gives a global convex1-smooth function with minimizer0. For a completed path ending at x, its largest possible normalized value is
Phi(H,x)=2 integral_0^x u_H(r)dr for x>=0,
Phi(H,x)=-2 integral_x^0 ell_H(r)dr for x<=0.
This follows by the pointwise envelope inequalities and is attained by integrating the indicated entire envelope. Every previous queried gradient is preserved.

For a nonzero current point, reflect if necessary so that it becomes a positive radius x: replace every knot(y,v) by(sigma y,sigma v), where sigma is the sign of the current point. All formulas below concern this reflected positive coordinate. Multiply selected magnitudes by sigma to obtain the original gradient. At x=0 choose gradient0.

## 2. Exact feasibility of a constant-gradient future block
Fix a nonnegative proposed block mass S. A magnitude q>=0 can be imposed on the entire interval[x-Sq,x] consistently with the old history exactly when
q belongs to I(H,x,S):=[ell_H(x), C(H,x,S)],
where
C(H,x,S)=min_(y,v in H) max{v,(x-y+v)/(1+S)}.                 (1)
The interval may be empty.

To prove this, add endpoint knots(x,q) and(z,q), where z=x-Sq. Monotonicity of the envelopes makes their joint feasibility equivalent to
q>=ell_H(x), q<=u_H(z).
The origin knot implies that the latter inequality with q>0 forces z>=q>0. For q=0, z=x>0. Thus the imposed plateau stays on the selected ray. For one old knot the upper inequality is
q<=v+(x-y-Sq)_+.
The continuous function on the right minus q is strictly decreasing, with unique zero
max{v,(x-y+v)/(1+S)}.
Indeed if x-y<=Sv the zero is v; otherwise it is(x-y+v)/(1+S). Intersecting these inequalities proves(1). The origin knot also gives ell_H(x)>=0 and C(H,x,S)<=x/(1+S).

Once both endpoint knots are feasible, the derivative has to be constant q between them; adding any intermediate knot with value q preserves legality. Hence every nonnegative step block of total mass S follows this plateau, in its actual chronological order. No individual stepsize bound is needed.

## 3. Exact optimal completion by a constant-gradient tail
For a tail of total mass S, any q in I(H,x,S) has exact maximal normalized terminal value
A(H,x,S;q)=2 integral_0^(x-Sq) min{u_H(r),q}dr.             (2)
Adding the two endpoint knots makes the new upper envelope on[0,x-Sq] exactly min{u_H(r),q}. Integrate that global new envelope. The resulting function attains(2), realizes the entire constant-gradient tail and every old gradient, and has initial squared distance1.

This optimum is a concrete finite calculation from the old knots. The function u_H is continuous piecewise affine with slopes0 or1 and finitely many pieces. On a rising piece write u_H(r)=r-d. For q whose level lies in that piece, put
E=integral_0^(q+d)u_H(r)dr-q^2/2;
E is constant as q varies through that rising piece. Formula(2) becomes
A=2E+2q(x-d)-(1+2S)q^2.                                 (3)
Its only interior stationary point is
q=(x-d)/(1+2S).                                          (4)
An optimizing q can therefore be selected by checking:
- the endpoints of the nonempty interval I(H,x,S);
- the finitely many plateau heights of u_H that belong to I;
- the values(4) whose level lies in the associated rising piece and in I.
The formula also covers zero levels by including the interval endpoints. Comparing these finitely many exact values selects q_stop(H,x,S). No numerical enumeration of trajectories or optimization over all functions is being assumed.

The offsets d and retained areas E in(3) are compulsory history data. The former proposal x/(1+2S) silently replaced d by0 and need not be optimal even when it is feasible.

## 4. A specified finite enlarged action tree
At time t, with current point x_t and full gradient history H_t, retain the old P5 actions:
(a) the signed steep envelope;
(b) the projection of x_t/(1+2S_t) onto the complete feasible interval, where S_t=sum_(r=t)^(n-1)h_r.

Add the following actions:
(c) the signed value q_stop for S=S_t, whenever I is nonempty;
(d) for each future checkpoint j in{t,...,n-1}, the signed value C(H,|x_t|,S_(t,j)), whenever I is nonempty, where
S_(t,j)=sum_(r=t)^(j-1)h_r.
History is reflected as in Section1 for(c),(d). Choose any listed action, add its knot, and apply the given h_t. At the end use Phi.

This is an explicit finite tree, with at most n+3 listed actions at each time, at most(n+3)^n leaves, and no free continuum of gradient choices. It starts from H_0={(0,0)}, x_0=1, rather than requiring a preselected seed. Every action is pathwise legal by the formulas above. Thus every completed leaf is a single globally defined legal one-dimensional function, and its displayed payoff is at most W_n(h).

Let M_new(h) be the maximum leaf payoff. A genuine probability law whose expectation loses a uniformly vanishing factor is obtained by giving a leaf of value Z>=0 mass proportional to Z^(n^2), for n>=1. If all values vanish, use any law. With N leaves and p=n^2, Jensen's inequality for a->a^(1+1/p) gives
[sum Z^(p+1)]/[sum Z^p] >= [N^(-1)sum Z^p]^(1/p)
 >= N^(-1/p) max Z.
Consequently the expected normalized payoff T_new satisfies
(n+3)^(-1/n) M_new(h) <= T_new(h) <= M_new(h) <= W_n(h).   (5)
The factor tends to1 independently of h. This distribution can be sampled as conditional branch probabilities using sums of descendant pth powers; their products telescope to the leaf law. This is a symbolic specification, not a computation performed here. The schedule is fixed before the law or any function is chosen.

For n=0 take f(x)=x^2/2, with normalized error1.

## 5. Inclusion of the old policy and the accepted ray construction
The tree contains all original forced-prefix P5 leaves. Indeed choosing checkpoint j initially gives C=1/(1+P_j), where P_j=sum_(r<j)h_r. If q=C was chosen for a block of mass S and a first step of mass a<=S has been performed, q is still feasible for the residual block from x-aq. The new knot(x,q) gives the residual upper bound C_new<=q, while feasibility gives C_new>=q. Thus C_new=q. Repeating the same lookahead checkpoint keeps exactly the old constant-gradient prefix. At the checkpoint itself S=0, so C=u_H at the query, again equal to q. Thereafter the two original actions are retained.

It also contains the exact alternating-ray leaves in accepted fact1fca3e5dd555cb4a. At a new outward stage let(A_old,w_old) be the previous record on that ray, d=A_old-w_old, and let the current radius satisfy x=d+(1+S)m with m>=w_old. Every earlier same-ray knot(y,v) satisfies y-v<=d and v<=w_old. The opposite-ray knots satisfy y-v<=0<=d. Formula(1) therefore gives C>=m, while the record knot gives C<=max(w_old,(x-d)/(1+S))=m. Thus the future-checkpoint action is exactly m. The residual-block argument then follows every plateau in that fact. At the terminal stage the stored knots force the same old upper derivative envelope as its slope1 ramps and flat segments. Formula(3) has its exact retained area e_term and offset d; q_stop is precisely its q_opt. Therefore
M_new(h)>=F_ray_n(h)>=K_n(h)
using the accepted fact, without discarding any ray feasibility condition.

This inclusion is a comparison of constructions, not a second independent claim that the ray family solves the target. The added actions are also available at non-record states, and the old P5 inner-return branches are preserved.

## 6. Exact strict improvement over the best old P5 leaf
Take h=(1,5,3,1). In the old P5 tree, seed j=0 reaches0 at its first step; seed j=3 also reaches0 at the last step. Seed j=2 has c=1/7 and its best last-step leaf gives4/147. For seed j=1, c=1/2 and the points through its forced prefix are1,1/2,-2.

At -2 the old interior choice is -2/9, because the remaining mass is4. It stays on this plateau and yields4/9. The old steep choice is -2 and sends the point to4. At4, the old positive upper envelope is
u(r)=r on[0,1/2], 1/2 on[1/2,1], r-1/2 forr>=1.
The last old steep action takes gradient7/2 and ends at1/2, giving1/4. The last old interior action takes gradient4/3 and ends at8/3. Its maximal normalized value is
1/2+2(4/3)(7/2)-3(4/3)^2=9/2.
These cases exhaust the old tree, so its maximum leaf payoff is exactly9/2; its K_4 fallback is at most4/9.

At the same history, the new optimal tail uses d=1/2, E=1/4, S=1. Formula(4) gives q=7/6, which lies in I=[1/2,7/4]. The new terminal value is
1/2+(7/2)^2/3=55/12 >9/2.
A complete global realizing derivative is
q_global(x)=x for x<=1/2;
1/2 for1/2<=x<=1;
x-1/2 for1<=x<=5/3;
7/6 forx>=5/3.
It is continuous, nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz. Its trajectory is
1,1/2,-2,4,17/6,
and direct integration gives normalized error55/12. The terminal gain over9/2 is exactly1/12. This verifies a real geometric improvement, not a change in averaging weights.

## 7. Checkpoint lookahead test
For h=(1,5,1,9,1), choose the checkpoint5 from the initial state, giving magnitude1/2 through its prefix. At the resulting point-2 choose future checkpoint9; the ordinary intervening mass is1, so formula(1) gives magnitude1. The next two points are-1 and8. The exact tail optimizer at8 has d=1/2,E=1/4,S=1 and q=5/2, giving
2E+(8-d)^2/3=77/4.
This reproduces the accepted fact1fca3e5dd555cb4a example. The old two-action rule at-2 offered only magnitudes2 and2/23; neither was the needed1. The new action is derived from complete-history feasibility, not inserted to fit this example.

## Target status
No uniform comparison of M_new(h) with U_n^ZJ has been proved. Equation(5) removes probability-weight loss; the new formulas repair two concrete omissions of the geometry. A theorem that M_new(h)>=(1-o(1))U_n^ZJ uniformly for every finite nonnegative h would still be a target-strength theorem and remains BLOCKED. The finite examples above do not establish such a statement or an asymptotic negative answer.

evidence:
# Exact optimality screen for a three-copy, two-bridge primitive join

Status: complete unverified construction-class obstruction, not a statement about unrestricted minimax optimality. No fact submission under the current allocation.

A concrete candidate was
c=2/3, d=(5sqrt(7)-11)/6, M=3+c+d=(11+5sqrt(7))/6,
J(a)=[a,1+cA,a,1+dA,a], A=1+sum a.
It has cdM=1 and M>F(1,1+sqrt(2)), where F is the exact shifted primitive join. Thus it passes the full-curvature product balance and suggests a larger primitive capacity than two ordinary binary joins. It is nevertheless invalid. The general argument below screens all positive c,d in this motif and proves that none can exceed the existing binary factor when the seed is quadratic-balanced.

Definitions. At L=1 write x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i). For a nonnegative schedule h with sum s=R-1 define its saturated intrinsic primitive energy
V_h=2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sR||g_n||^2.
The primitive property means V_h>=0 on every smooth convex trajectory. The following necessary tests are explicit legal one-dimensional functions, so no conjectural composition theorem is used.

1. An exact cut constraint for every primitive schedule.
Choose any step b>=1, let P be the sum of preceding steps, and T the sum of following steps. Set a_minus=(b-1)/(T+1). Use f'(x)=clip(x,-a_minus,1), f(0)=0, and x_0=P+1. Its prefix stays on the positive affine ray and arrives at1. The b-step arrives at -(b-1). All tail iterates stay on the negative affine ray, and the final point is -a_minus. This follows from nonnegative partial sums and (T+1)a_minus=b-1. The degenerate b=1 case is harmless.
At each sample, Q_(i,star)=f_i-g_i x_i+g_i^2/2=0, since the function is quadratic in its core and affine with the matching offset on each tail. A direct expansion using the GD recursion yields
V_h=x_0^2-x_n^2-2s f_n-sR g_n^2+2 sum_i h_i Q_(i,star).
Thus this trajectory gives V_h=(P+1)^2-R^2 a_minus^2. If h is primitive it follows that
(b-1)R <= (P+1)(T+1).                                      (CUT)
This is a necessary primitive-energy inequality, not merely the objective single-cut lower bound.

2. Full-curvature condition.
For f(x)=x^2/2 and x_0=1, all Q_(i,star)=0, and V_h=1-R^2 product_i(1-h_i)^2. Hence a primitive schedule must obey
R |product_i(1-h_i)| <=1.                                  (QUAD)

3. The three-copy motif cannot exceed the ordinary two-join factor.
Let a be any nonnegative block with shifted sum A>0 and |product_i(1-a_i)|=1/A. This includes each standard quadratic-balanced basic primitive block. Form J(a) with c,d>0 and put M=3+c+d, so its shifted sum is R=MA.
The two bridge instances of (CUT) give
Mc<=2+d, Md<=2+c.
Condition (QUAD) gives Mcd<=1, because the endpoint quadratic multiplier has magnitude cd/A.
Writing t=c+d=M-3 and u=(M-1)/(M+1), the cut conditions are exactly c,d<=u. If M<=4 there is already no gain over F(1,1+sqrt(2))>4. Suppose M>4. Both c,d lie in [t-u,u]. At a fixed sum t, the product c(t-c) is concave, so
cd >= u(t-u)=(M-1)(M^2-3M-2)/(M+1)^2.
Combining this with Mcd<=1 gives
M^4-4M^3-1<=0.
This polynomial is strictly increasing for M>3, and has one root M_*>4. Put lambda=1+sqrt(2) and C=F(1,lambda). Its defining equation C^2-(1+lambda)C-lambda=0 gives lambda=C(C-1)/(C+1). Substitution into lambda^2-2lambda-1=0 gives C^4-4C^3-1=0. Therefore M_*=F(1,lambda), and necessarily
M<=F(1,1+sqrt(2)).
The existing two-step binary parenthesizations of three copies attain this scalar factor. This argument rules out a larger primitive factor for the displayed three-copy motif, regardless of a proposed richer certificate.

4. Exact hostile instance for the displayed new constants.
Take a=[sqrt(2)], A=lambda, c=2/3 and d=(5sqrt(7)-11)/6. One has 0<d<2/3. Use f'(x)=clip(x,-1/4,1), f(0)=0, and x_0=A. The first sqrt(2)-step reaches1; the first bridge reaches -cA. Every remaining step stays on the negative affine ray because their total is T=(2+d)A-1 and
-cA+T/4 <= -1/4 iff d<=2/3.
The endpoint is x_5=-cA+[(2+d)A-1]/4. On the negative affine ray, the primitive terminal expression x_5^2+2s f_5+sR g_5^2 equals (x_5-s/4)^2. Since s=MA-1,
x_5-s/4=-A[c+(1+c)/4]=-(13/12)A.
Thus V_J=A^2-(13A/12)^2=-(25/144)A^2<0. This is a direct failure of the proposed primitive certificate in dimension one. It does not rely on reversing schedules or on a general H-duality assertion.

Search record and scope.
Matlas returned unrelated statements for the requested primitive/H-duality composition search. The downloaded GSW paper arXiv:2410.16249 was checked: its Section 3.1 states H-duality for basic schedules, so no unsupported universal reversal closure was assumed. A tiny SDP check was considered, but cvxpy, numpy, scipy, clarabel, and scs are absent; no numerical solver, exhaustive search, or installation was run. The exact cut construction made one unnecessary.

The obstruction uses the seed's exact quadratic balance and the three-copy/two-bridge form. It does not close non-balanced seeds, independently chosen blocks, four-block joins, or a direct objective certificate. Those would require their own feasible certificate and exact-profile comparison. Any proposed reopening must identify which hypothesis changes and retain the cut test as a mandatory hostile example.

Set lambda=1+sqrt2, sigma=1/lambda, A=lambda^k, B=(sqrt(1+8A)-1)/4 and R=A+B+2. Then A=2B^2+B. The reset seed is q0=[pi^(k),B+1,1], where pi^(k) has length2^k-1 and sumA-1. m0=1/A, m1=B/(2A), O1=(A-1)/A,
z_term=[sigma R B/2-A+1]/A, e_term=(A-1)/A^2, m_old=1/A.

author: max2
claim: New exact joint-perturbation inequality: at a full stationary primal-dual tuple, any certificate descent must pay inactive-interpolation costs through a bilinear schedule-flow term. One-step q>tau data give actual full descent and show star-outgoing flow cannot simply be removed.
evidence:
# Exact cost of a joint certificate perturbation above the Huber level

Status: unverified quantitative derivation, following the updated q>tau assignment. The historical GS interface is not re-proved. The initial verification allowance is already used.

## 1. Definitions and the exact finite-perturbation inequality

Normalize L=1, x_*=g_*=f_*=0. For a fixed positive length-n schedule h, let (q,lambda,G,f) be a full stationary primal-dual tuple. Explicitly:

* lambda_ij>=0 for distinct i,j in I={*,0,...,n}, with out_i-in_i=2*1_{i=n};
* M(q,lambda,h)>=0 is the matrix of q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum lambda_ij Q_ij after GD substitution;
* G>=0 is the Gram matrix of (x_0,g_0,...,g_n), G_00=1, and Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0;
* M G=0 and lambda_ij Q_ij=0;
* <g_t,z_t(lambda)>=0 for t<n, where
  z_t(b)=sum_{i,j} b_ij(1_{t<i}-1_{t<j})g_i.
  The indicator is zero for the star, and g_*=0.

All objects in these conditions refer to the SAME full legal transcript. No subset of these conditions is used as a replacement for the full system.

Set sigma_ij=-Q_ij>=0. Consider ANY second feasible upper certificate (q',lambda',h'), where h'>=0 and lambda' has the same flow. The new certificate need not be optimal. Put a=h'-h and b=lambda'-lambda. Define the explicit bilinear form

    B_G(a,b)=sum_{t<n} a_t <g_t,z_t(b)>.

Because M is affine separately in h and lambda, its exact finite expansion, paired with the original G, is

    <M(q',lambda',h'),G>
      = (q'-q)-sum_{i,j}lambda'_ij sigma_ij+B_G(a,b).           (1)

To verify the formula, the first-order h term vanishes by stationarity. The lambda term is sum b_ij T_ij(G), with T_ij=Q_ij-(f_i-f_j). Flow equality cancels the f differences, while sum lambda_ij Q_ij=0 changes sum b_ij Q_ij to -sum lambda'_ij sigma_ij. The only remaining mixed term is B_G(a,b). The q coefficient is G_00=1. There are no higher-order terms.

Both matrices in the left side are PSD. Therefore EVERY new feasible certificate satisfies

    q'-q >= sum lambda'_ij sigma_ij - B_G(h'-h,lambda'-lambda). (2)

This is a concrete quantitative obstruction to a proposed joint descent. A descent by Delta=q-q'>0 must obey

    B_G(h'-h,lambda'-lambda)
       >= Delta+sum lambda'_ij sigma_ij.                       (3)

In particular:

* Holding h fixed cannot lower q, as expected from matching primal feasibility.
* Holding lambda fixed cannot lower q for ANY new h, not just for a small change: then both terms on the right of (2) vanish.
* The gain from simultaneous motion has to overcome the exact cost of placing multiplier mass on interpolation inequalities that are strict for the old stationary primal.

Let R_g=max_i ||g_i||. Direct Cauchy--Schwarz bounds give

    |B_G(a,b)|<=R_g^2 ||a||_1 ||b||_1,
    Delta+sum lambda'_ij sigma_ij
       <=R_g^2 ||h'-h||_1 ||lambda'-lambda||_1                 (4)

for every feasible descent. Thus joint movement, not a single-block update, is essential. This is a necessary inequality, not a proof that a descent exists when q exceeds tau.

For a differentiable path through a stationary tuple, any first-order newly positive multiplier on an edge with sigma_ij>0 costs first order, while the useful bilinear term starts at second order. Hence a path with q'(0)=0 must have zero first derivative on every such inactive edge. This conclusion also follows directly from (2) by dividing by the path parameter.

## 2. One-step q>tau certificates with unavoidable star-outgoing flow

The full one-step system provides a useful hostile test of attempts to remove lambda_{*,i} without moving the schedule.

Take h_0=1+a with a>=1. The true worst-case value is q=a^2, certified by

    lambda_{0,*}=2a^2,
    lambda_{*,0}=2a^2-2,
    lambda_{1,0}=2,

and all other multipliers zero. The flow equations hold. Its entire PSD identity is

    q||x_0||^2-2f_1+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
      =a^2||x_0-g_0||^2+||a g_0+g_1||^2.                    (5)

The quadratic f(x)=x^2/2 from x_0=1 gives g_0=1, g_1=-a, f_1=a^2/2 and makes the right side zero. Thus primal and dual match and W_1(1+a)=a^2. This value is strictly above tau=1/(2a+3) for a>=1.

For a>1, every tight certificate at this very same schedule needs nonzero star-outgoing flow. To prove this, suppose nu_i=lambda_{*,i}=0. Then mu_0+mu_1=2, where mu_i=lambda_{i,*}. Pairing the optimal PSD slack with the matching quadratic vector (1,1,-a) gives M(1,1,-a)^T=0. Its x_0 row yields

    mu_0-a mu_1=2a^2.

Combining with mu_0+mu_1=2 gives

    mu_1=2(1-a)<0,

a contradiction. Thus a general-q proof cannot simply remove all star-outgoing multipliers while holding h and q fixed.

There IS an actual full feasible descent in this example. For any 0<epsilon<a-1, replace a by a-epsilon in all displayed variables. The nonnegative multipliers, both squares in (5), the chronological GD equation and the matching quadratic primal all remain valid. The objective drops by

    a^2-(a-epsilon)^2=2a epsilon-epsilon^2>0.

This verifies a schedule-and-flow motion with the full cone and the same legal function, rather than just a formal linearized descent. These tuples are not stationary, so the example does not decide the hypothetical global-minimizer question.

For completeness, the path continues below a=1. For 1/2<=a<=1 take

    lambda_{0,*}=2a, lambda_{1,*}=2(1-a), lambda_{1,0}=2a,

all other multipliers zero, and q=a^2. The gradient block is [[2a,1],[1,1]], while mu=(2a,2(1-a)). Its Schur complement is

    Z=(2a-1) [[1,1/a],[1/a,1/a^2]] >=0.

The quadratic again annihilates the full slack and attains q. Decreasing a keeps all constraints feasible until a=1/2, at which point q=tau=1/4. Thus the full one-step non-Huber region has an explicit piecewise-algebraic descent to the Huber-tight optimum. The change of formula at a=1 is necessary to preserve nonnegative multipliers.

## 3. Why the general-q residual alone has not supplied the descent

For an arbitrary full feasible certificate, the earlier exact Huber evaluation is

    eta=(1,tau e)^T M(1,tau e)
       =q-tau-tau sum_i nu_i[1-tau(P_i+1)]>=0,
    tau=1/(2S+1), S=sum h_t, P_i=sum_{t<i}h_t.

Its residual estimates control M applied to this one explicit Huber vector. A feasible descent from a stationary certificate also has to control the ENTIRE nullspace of M and the cost of activating strict primal interpolation inequalities. Formula (2) makes the missing interaction concrete: a positive value of q-tau by itself neither gives an allowed first-order multiplier support nor a positive value of B_G large enough to pay the required costs.

Two attempted shortcuts therefore fail for explicit reasons:

1. Freeze the optimal multipliers and use the Huber slack to move only h: equation (2) proves that q cannot decrease for any h'.
2. Remove star-outgoing flow at fixed h and q: the exact a>1 example proves such a tight certificate need not exist.

These are restrictions on the indicated operations. They do not refute a general simultaneous feasible descent theorem at global minimizers. The old full stationary tuple must remain attached to (2); using source/cut/energy identities with a nonlegal Gram would invalidate the inequality.

The current open task is to build a simultaneous variation with a favorable explicit B_G and PSD feasibility from the specific GD structure, or obtain a different quantitative consequence from the complete matrix. No Huber-tightness or asymptotic profile comparison has been proved here.

# Coupled-coordinate instability on the recursive screening family

Status: unverified source-based derivation, not a new accepted fact.
Worker: max3. This is a companion to max3_recursive_channel_obstruction.md;
it is not a negative answer to the minimax target.

## Statement

Define c=13/5, a=c^(-17), b_r=a c^r and
H_0=(), H_m=(H_(m-1),b_(m-1),H_(m-1)). Its length is N_m=2^m-1 and
its sum is s_m=a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2).

There is a fixed integer r, independent of m, for which the explicit
Ye--Liu coupled-coordinate construction yields

    W_(N_m)(H_m) >= (98/81)^(2^(m-r-3)) / [2(1+s_r)]

for all m>=r+4. In particular this genuine worst-case error tends to infinity,
even though the restricted ray, quadratic, one-cap, and two-curvature functionals
in the companion candidate tend to zero. Both claims remain unverified here.

## External input, definitions, and normalization

The source is Yuhan Ye and Kaizhao Liu, Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for
Gradient Descent, arXiv:2609.09152v2, Section3.1, Lemmas3.1--3.2 and the
pre-weakening construction for Lemma2.2; its proof is AppendixA.1--A.3.
The PDF and extracted text are in this worker's downloads directory. The
definitions, the two-coordinate proof, the global assembly, and the terminal
objective calculation have been read. A Matlas search for the local transfer
statement returned unrelated results, none used. The direct source is
https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09152 .

The exact input used is as follows. For epsilon,gamma>0 put
chi=sqrt(1+2gamma+epsilon^2). There exist finite constants A_YL and B_YL,
depending only on those two parameters, such that for every finite nonnegative
schedule and every chosen chronological checkpoint set with all checkpoint
sizes z_i>=B_YL, a finite-dimensional convex 1-smooth function with a minimizer
at zero and initial point e_1 has normalized objective at least

    [1/(2(1+S_tail))] product_i
           [z_i/(chi(A_YL+S_i)+epsilon z_i)]^2.

Here S_i is the sum of ordinary steps after the previous checkpoint and before
z_i, and S_tail is the sum after the last checkpoint. The normalization is
W=2(f(x_N)-min f)/||x_0||^2. Section3.1 computes unnormalized final gap
D^2/[4(1+S_tail)] at initial squared distance1; multiplying by2 gives the
displayed coefficient. The paper then deliberately weakens its statement by
dropping that factor2. No normalization inference from the label R_n is used.

Applicability details: each local function is a translated/scaled unit Moreau
envelope of the support function of a finite convex hull of gradient vectors
and zero. Its gradient is Euclidean projection onto that convex hull, hence
it is convex and 1-smooth. The prescribed two-coordinate trajectories have
nonnegative first-coordinate descent and second-coordinate ascent. Two exact
zero regions ensure that old components and future components are inactive
throughout the full GD trajectory. The global objective is one half the sum of
these adjacent-coordinate functions and a final one-sided Huber term. Each
coordinate appears in at most two terms, giving global smoothness constant1;
the local steps are therefore h_t/2. All component offsets are nonnegative,
so the origin is a common minimizer. These checks preserve arbitrary finite
nonnegative steps and the entire checkpoint sequence. Dimension is the number
of checkpoints plus one, finite at every fixed horizon.

The paper permits B_YL=2(1+epsilon^(-2)) and sufficiently large finite A_YL.
Only finiteness and these hypotheses are used below; neither parameter is sent
to zero with m, and no constant is hidden in an asymptotic notation.

## Exact checkpoint calculation

Choose epsilon=1/100 and gamma=2099/20000, so chi=11/10. Fix any permitted
finite A_YL. Choose r large enough that

    b_r>=B_YL=20002,   chi A_YL/b_r<=1/100.

Such a fixed r exists since b_r=a c^r tends to infinity. In H_m choose every
step whose level is at least r. All ordinary blocks between consecutive selected
steps, as well as the first and last ordinary blocks, are exact copies of H_r.
Thus every S_i and S_tail equals s_r. Set M=m-r.

The selected step sizes are b_r c^ell, with level ell occurring
2^(M-ell-1) times for ell=0,...,M-1. Since

    s_r/b_r=(1-(2/c)^r)/(c-2)<=5/3,

the fixed normalized denominator satisfies

    d=chi(A_YL+s_r)/b_r<=1/100+11/6=553/300<37/20.

Every transfer is at least

    G_ell=c^ell/[37/20+c^ell/100].

This expression increases with ell. Direct rational comparisons give

    G_0>=1/2, G_1>=4/3, G_2>=7/2, G_3>=8,

and G_ell>=1 for every ell>=4. For M>=4, the total transfer product is
therefore at least

    [(1/2)^8 (4/3)^4 (7/2)^2 8]^(2^(M-4))
       =(98/81)^(2^(M-4)).

Squaring and multiplying the exact terminal coefficient from the source gives

    W_(N_m)(H_m)>=(98/81)^(2^(M-3))/[2(1+s_r)],

which is the claimed bound. All constants r,A_YL,s_r are fixed independently
of m. The exponent equals (N_m+1)/2^(r+3), so the lower bound grows
exponentially in the horizon, despite its very small fixed growth constant.

## What this identifies and what it does not

This is a strict separation of mechanisms on a concrete schedule family. The
coupled-coordinate witness can undergo many shrinking transfers and then grow
through larger checkpoints, without having to revisit the previously defined
one-dimensional ray. In the binary level counts the first four transfer types
already have product greater than one. The verified ray construction cannot
execute even its first outward return on the same family. A two-curvature
homogeneous core becomes a scalar contraction after its two signs collapse or
interchange; that is also insufficient on these schedules.

This calculation is not a constant/profile lower bound for arbitrary schedules
and is not intended to reproduce the known silver-exponent theorem. Its use is
to locate a real geometric difference that a stronger exact construction must
retain. The local additive price A_YL and checkpoint threshold B_YL remain
fixed costs of the cited mechanism; nothing here removes them or shows that
they are negligible at the desired leading-constant scale.

## 1. Explicit persistent-error family
Let m>=1 and choose arbitrary real b_0,...,b_(m-1) in[5,11/2].
Use the predetermined length2m schedule
h=(1,b_0,1,b_1,...,1,b_(m-1)).
In R^(m+1) take the standard orthonormal basis e_0,...,e_m, set
rho_i=1/(1+b_i) for0<=i<m,
w_i=rho_i(e_i-e_(i+1)) for0<=i<m,
w_m=e_m/6,
and set eta=1/36. Define one fixed function
J(z)=max{0, max_(0<=i<=m)(<w_i,z>-eta)},
f(x)=min_z {J(z)+(1/2)||x-z||^2}.                           (1)
Start at x_0=e_0 and choose minimizer0. All quantities in(1) are fixed once h is known. This is not a sequence of independently changed objectives or Hessians.

The function J is finite nonnegative convex and J(0)=0. Its Moreau envelope f is convex, differentiable and1-smooth, with f>=0,f(0)=0. To spell out the local certification used below, if w belongs to the subdifferential of J at z and x=z+w, then z is the unique minimizer in(1), grad f(x)=w, and f(x)=J(z)+||w||^2/2. The minimum is unique by the quadratic's strong convexity. Monotonicity of subgradients at two such pairs gives
||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2<=<grad f(x)-grad f(y),x-y>,
which proves the required Lipschitz bound. The differentiability follows directly by comparing the unique minimizing values at x and x+v; the linear term is <x-z,v> and the remainder is bounded by a constant times||v||^2. Convexity follows from joint convexity in(x,z) and partial minimization.

e_i-(1+b_i)w_i=e_(i+1),                                  (2)

The i-th affine plane at z has value

The current plane minus it is

When i=m-1 the same formula uses1/6 in place of rho_(i+1), because the terminal plane is w_m=e_m/6, and the same bound holds.

The previous plane, when i>=1, has value
-rho_(i-1)[1-c rho_i]-eta<0.
Every other non-current plane has value -eta, since its two-coordinate support is disjoint from z. The zero plane has value0. Thus the current affine plane dominates EVERY stored plane. It follows that w_i belongs to the subdifferential of J at z. This proves the claimed gradients at both queries and hence(2), including all chronological interactions with old and future planes.

At x_(2m)=e_m set z=(5/6)e_m. The terminal plane has value

The only other possibly nonzero inner product is with w_(m-1), and it is negative. All remaining planes have value-eta, while the zero plane has value0. Therefore grad f(e_m)=w_m and

The intermediate objective values are also explicit:
f(e_i-u w_i)=rho_i-(2u+1)rho_i^2-eta, u=0,1.
Thus the construction supplies positions, gradients, values and a global function; it does not stop at a PSD matrix or local inequalities.

## 3. Actual growing dimension and nonseparability
The visited block-start points are the m+1 vectors e_0,...,e_m. The vectors w_0,...,w_m are linearly independent: their coordinate matrix is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Their Gram matrix is explicitly real PSD because they are the displayed Euclidean vectors. Its only off-diagonal entries at distinct stages are
<w_i,w_(i+1)>=-rho_i rho_(i+1) for i<m-1,
<w_(m-1),w_m>=-rho_(m-1)/6.
Each w_i is queried twice, so the temporal Gram matrix also has positive repeated-gradient correlations. Energies are2rho_i^2 on the relay stages and1/36 at the terminal point. They vary with the chosen b_i. In particular the accepted orthogonal-moment obstruction0e7e78056dc6258c does not apply.

The function cannot be written as a sum of univariate functions in any fixed orthonormal coordinates. Indeed linear independence of the w_i lets us choose, for any i, a point z with <w_i,z>=eta and <w_j,z><eta for every j!=i. In a neighborhood of z, J is exactly max{0,<w_i,z>-eta}. At x=z+theta w_i with0<theta<1 and sufficiently small surrounding perturbations, its envelope has Hessian
P_i=w_i w_i^T/||w_i||^2.
For two neighboring, nonparallel w_i,w_(i+1), their inner product is nonzero, so the rank-one projectors P_i and P_(i+1) do not commute. All Hessians of a function separable in a fixed orthonormal basis would be diagonal in that basis and would commute wherever they exist. This contradiction proves genuine nonseparability, not merely a rotated scalar witness or an orthogonal direct sum.

For any scalar quadratic f_lambda(x)=lambda x^2/2 with0<=lambda<=1, one block's multiplier is

For0<=lambda<=1/6 and5<=b<=11/2, it is nonnegative and at most1-lambda<=exp(-lambda).

The latter expression increases with b>1, and its endpoint value at b=11/2 is81/88. These statements also follow by checking the vertex and endpoints of the quadratic p_b on the given interval.

Consequently the worst normalized objective over every scalar quadratic satisfies

 <=max{1/(2 e m),(81/88)^(2m)} ->0.                       (4)
The first term comes from maximizing lambda exp(-2m lambda). A general finite-dimensional convex quadratic diagonalizes orthogonally, and its normalized error is a convex combination of these scalar errors; zero-curvature directions contribute no objective. Thus(4) controls the full quadratic class uniformly in the varying b_i, whereas(3) stays1/4 on the explicitly nonseparable nonlinear function.

This does not assert that scalar nonlinear witnesses fail on these schedules. The point is to give a concrete globally consistent variable-energy high-dimensional trajectory surviving mixed short/long steps even when every quadratic channel converges.

(block_0,b_0,...,block_(m-1),b_(m-1),block_m),

M_i=s_i+b_i>0, rho_i=1/M_i for i<m, and choose rho_m>0.

0<=eta_i<=rho_i-2c_i rho_i^2                         for i<m, (5)
eta_i-eta_(i+1)<=rho_i-c_i(2rho_i^2+rho_i rho_(i+1)) for i<m, (6)

    q||x_0-x_*||^2-2f_n+sum lambda_ij Q_ij = M >=0,

Suppose

    nu=lambda_{*,n-1}>0.

For any 0<epsilon<=nu/(nu+2), put c=1-epsilon and replace ONLY the last step by

    b_new=c b+epsilon.

Then the new predetermined GD schedule has the rigorous uniform bound

    W_n(h_0,...,h_{n-2},b_new) <= c q < q.                    (D)

At the largest allowed epsilon this reads

    b_new=(2b+nu)/(nu+2),       q_new=2q/(nu+2).

The strict inequality is meaningful whenever q>0; every valid finite-horizon objective upper bound has q>0 by the canonical Huber witness.

## 2. Direct proof for all smooth convex functions

Fix any legal function and initial point, using the old and new schedules with the same prefix. Write

    x=x_{n-1}, g=grad f(x),
    z=x-b g                    (old endpoint),
    y=x-g                      (unit-step point),
    z_new=c z+epsilon y         (new endpoint),
    delta=f(x)-||g||^2/2 >=0.

Because Q_{*,n-1}=-delta, isolating this term in the original full PSD certificate yields

    2f(z)+nu delta <= q||x_0-x_*||^2.                        (A)

The remaining terms have the correct signs: the PSD quadratic form is nonnegative and every other -lambda_ij Q_ij is nonnegative.

The unit-step descent inequality gives f(y)<=delta. Convexity then yields

    2f(z_new) <=2c f(z)+2epsilon f(y)
                <=2c f(z)+2epsilon delta
                <=c[2f(z)+nu delta]
                <=c q||x_0-x_*||^2,

where 2epsilon<=c nu was the only restriction on epsilon. This proves (D) without selecting any hard function, differentiating W, or assuming a stationary worst-case primal.

The unit-step inequality can itself be derived from a single smooth-convex interpolation constraint:

    Q_{y,x}=f(y)-f(x)+<grad f(y),g>
              +||grad f(y)-g||^2/2
           =f(y)-delta+||grad f(y)||^2/2 <=0.

Thus the proof uses precisely the full smooth-convex class and is dimension-independent.

## 3. Explicit nonnegative-multiplier, PSD certificate

The construction is stronger than a sign argument: it gives an explicit enlarged interpolation certificate for the changed schedule. The two auxiliary points are the old endpoint z and the unit-step point y. The new algorithm still uses n steps and no auxiliary oracle calls; auxiliary points appear only in the proof and are defined from the same penultimate point and gradient.

Let g_z,g_y,g_new denote their actual gradients, and put

    d=c nu-2epsilon >=0.

Keep c times every old multiplier except lambda_{*,n-1}; assign d to Q_{*,n-1}. Add the new nonnegative multipliers

    2c       on Q_{z_new,z},
    2epsilon on Q_{z_new,y},
    2epsilon on Q_{y,x}.

All function-value terms cancel against the new objective -2f(z_new). After substituting z_new=c z+epsilon y and y=x-g, the full polynomial identity is

    c q||x_0-x_*||^2-2f(z_new)
      +c sum_{(i,j)!=(star,n-1)}lambda_ij Q_ij
      +d Q_{*,n-1}
      +2c Q_{z_new,z}+2epsilon Q_{z_new,y}
      +2epsilon Q_{y,x}

    = c M
      +c||g_new-g_z||^2
      +epsilon||g_new-g_y||^2
      +epsilon||g_y||^2.                                    (PSD)

The right side is an explicit PSD quadratic form, including the original full matrix M, not only its row sums or energy trace. The left side uses nonnegative multipliers throughout. All interpolation data concern the same globally legal function; no incompatible local transcript is glued in.

To check the identity, combine the first two new inequalities with weights c,epsilon. Their gradient-position terms cancel because z_new=c z+epsilon y. Then combine Q_{y,x}=f(y)-delta+||g_y||^2/2. The coefficient d is exactly what balances the old nu delta term.

The displayed certificate uses auxiliary analysis points. It is not asserted to be an explicit parameter-by-parameter map into the minimal n+2-point dual. Its full PSD identity proves the actual uniform upper bound directly, so it is already sufficient for a global-minimizer contradiction. When the new steps are positive, exact finite interpolation duality also gives a minimal-format certificate at its true worst-case value, but that existential statement is not needed for (D).

## 4. Consequence at global minimizers

Suppose h is a globally minimizing length-n schedule and its full certificate is tight: q=W_n(h)=W_n^*. If lambda_{*,n-1}>0, formula (D) constructs a length-n nonnegative predetermined schedule with strictly smaller true worst-case value. This contradicts global minimality.

Consequently EVERY tight full certificate at a global minimizer must satisfy

    lambda_{*,n-1}=0.                                      (V)

The contradiction uses an actual globally valid changed algorithm, so it is not merely a stationarity-implies-tightness shortcut. It does not need q=tau or a bound on the total step mass. It also handles a final step already equal to one: then the schedule does not change and (D) would improve the allegedly tight q itself.

This conclusion leaves lambda_{*,i} for i<n-1, lambda_{*,n}, and the PSD Schur-complement defect completely open. In particular it does not establish Huber tightness of a global minimizer.

## 5. Exact checks and the remaining q>tau case

For the one-step certificate at h_0=1+a, a>1, take

    q=a^2, lambda_{0,*}=2a^2,
    lambda_{*,0}=2a^2-2, lambda_{1,0}=2,

all other multipliers zero. Its exact slack is

    a^2||x_0-g_0||^2+||a g_0+g_1||^2,

and f(x)=x^2/2 attains q. The new formula gives c=1/a^2, h_new=1+1/a and the certified bound q_new=1. This is strictly smaller than a^2. The formula preserves nonnegativity and PSD through the explicit identity above; smaller epsilon gives a continuous descent.

The hypothesis nu>0 cannot be silently replaced by q>tau. For 1/2<a<1, the tight one-step certificate at h_0=1+a has q=a^2>tau=1/(2a+3), but no star-outgoing multipliers:

    lambda_{0,*}=2a, lambda_{1,*}=2(1-a), lambda_{1,0}=2a.

Its gradient block is [[2a,1],[1,1]], its star-directed vector is mu=(2a,2(1-a)), and its full Schur complement is

    Z=(2a-1)[[1,1/a],[1/a,1/a^2]] >=0.

The quadratic matches q. Thus the remaining non-Huber defect can be carried entirely by nonzero PSD slack even when all star-outgoing weights vanish. This example is not globally optimal; it is a hostile test of extending (V) into an unsupported general tightness claim.

## 6. Related terminal extension

If a certificate instead has lambda_{*,n}=nu>0, the same argument applied to an appended step gives, for 0<=epsilon<=nu/(nu+2),

    W_{n+1}(h,epsilon) <= (1-epsilon)q.

Here use the convex combination of x_n and x_n-grad f(x_n), and isolate the terminal residual delta_n=f_n-||g_n||^2/2 in the old certificate. This is a length-(n+1) improvement and must not be counted as a length-n contradiction. It may be useful for upper-bound composition, but no asymptotic comparison with the exact Zhang--Jiang profile follows automatically.

evidence:
# Quantitative final-step descent from a terminal pair in the PSD Schur range

Status: unverified candidate. It extends the concrete descent search to certificates with no star-outgoing multipliers. It is not a general q>tau descent theorem.

## 1. Full-certificate hypothesis

Normalize L=1, x_*=f_*=0, and ||x_0||=1. Let a length-n schedule h, n>=1, have final step b=h_{n-1}>0 and a full feasible upper certificate (q,lambda), using all smooth-convex inequalities Q_ij<=0 and a PSD slack matrix

    M=[[q,-mu^T/2],[-mu/2,A]],   mu_i=lambda_{i,*}, q>0.

Let Z=A-mu mu^T/(4q)>=0 be its complete gradient Schur complement. This is the actual matrix from the full certificate, not a surrogate formed from a few minors.

Suppose there exist kappa>0, a>0 and s in {+1,-1} such that

    Z >= kappa v v^T,
    v = a e_{n-1}+s e_n.                                   (H)

The indices e_i refer to gradient coordinates. The sign s=+1 will give a decrease of the final step; s=-1 will give an increase.

Define the finite radius bounds

    B_prev=prod_{t<n-1}(1+h_t),    B=(1+b)B_prev,
    C=q/(2B^2)+1/kappa.

Choose any d>0 satisfying

    d<=a/C,
    d<=q^2/(8a B^2 B_prev^2),                               (d)
    d<b                  if s=+1.

The changed schedule, with all preceding steps fixed, is

    b_new=b-s d.

Then the actual worst-case value obeys the explicit strict improvement

    W_n(h_0,...,h_{n-2},b_new)
       <= q-d q^2/(8a B^2) < q.                            (D)

No Huber-tightness, vanishing star-outgoing flow, stationarity, or rank assumption on the old primal is needed. The sufficient condition is the concrete full-matrix domination (H).

## 2. Uniform proof, including nearly worst-case instances

Fix any legal function. Put E=2f(x_n), p=g_{n-1}, g=g_n, and r=a p+s g. The complete certificate identity and every interpolation sign give

    q-E >= M evaluated on the actual vectors
          >= g_all^T Z g_all
          >= kappa ||r||^2.                               (1)

Here the second inequality follows by completing the square in x_0 in the full matrix. Thus ||r||^2<=(q-E)/kappa; the formula remains valid for every instance, not only for a maximizing one.

The elementary bounds ||p||<=B_prev, ||x_n||<=B, and convexity yield

    ||g||^2 >= E^2/(4B^2).                                 (2)

The identity ||r||^2=a^2||p||^2+||g||^2+2s a<p,g> implies

    -2s <p,g> >= (||g||^2-||r||^2)/a.                     (3)

The new endpoint is x_n+s d p. Smoothness gives

    E_new <= E+2s d<p,g>+d^2||p||^2
           <= E-(d/a)[E^2/(4B^2)-(q-E)/kappa]
                    +d^2 B_prev^2.                        (4)

For every E, the scalar inequality E^2>=q^2-2q(q-E) is simply (E-q)^2>=0. Inserting it into (4) gives

    E_new <= q-d q^2/(4a B^2)
               -[1-(d/a)C](q-E)+d^2 B_prev^2.

Since E<=q and d<=a/C, the middle term is nonpositive. The other restriction in (d) then gives (D). Taking the supremum over all legal functions and dimensions proves the uniform bound.

Thus this is an actual stepsize perturbation with an explicit certified new value. It is not a first-order assertion evaluated only on a guessed active function. The elementary smoothness upper inequality in (4) also follows from Q_{new,old}<=0 by completing the square
||g_new-g-s d p||^2/2, so the argument is consistent with the full interpolation cone.

The proof provides a uniform analytic certificate for the new schedule. It does not claim an explicit closed formula for its minimal-format interpolation multipliers. Such a formula is unnecessary to conclude that a purported globally optimal schedule has been strictly improved.

## 3. A range exclusion at global minimizers

Let T=span{e_{n-1},e_n}. For a PSD matrix Z and a nonzero v in range(Z), one has

    Z >= kappa v v^T,   kappa=1/(v^T Z^dagger v)>0.

Indeed write v=Z^(1/2)w with w=Z^(dagger/2)v, and use (w^T Z^(1/2)u)^2<=||w||^2 u^T Z u. Thus any vector in range(Z) supported on the last two coordinates, with both entries nonzero, can be rescaled to condition (H). Either sign of their ratio is allowed.

A vector with only the last coordinate nonzero is incompatible with a tight positive certificate: its square would force g_n=0 on a matching worst-case instance, hence f_n=0. A vector with only coordinate n-1 nonzero likewise forces g_{n-1}=0, making x_n=x_{n-1} a minimizer. Matching worst cases exist in the finite full interpolation formulation; alternatively, the quantitative argument below rules these cases out without assuming attainment.

For the last coordinate alone, q-E>=kappa||g_n||^2>=kappa E^2/(4B^2). This uniform inequality implies E<=r<q, where r is the positive root of r+kappa r^2/(4B^2)=q. It improves the allegedly tight upper bound. For the penultimate coordinate alone, use ||g_n||<=(1+b)||g_{n-1}|| to get the same conclusion with kappa replaced by kappa/(1+b)^2.

Consequently every tight full certificate at a globally minimizing positive schedule satisfies

    range(Z) intersect T = {0}.                             (R)

In particular

    rank(Z)<=n-1.

For n=1 this forces Z=0. For larger n, it does not force the whole Schur complement to vanish: its range may involve earlier gradients in every nonzero vector.

An equivalent exact matrix formulation uses the earlier-coordinate set J={0,...,n-2}. The generalized Schur complement of Z with respect to its J block must vanish:

    Z_TT-Z_TJ Z_JJ^dagger Z_JT=0.                           (SC)

For a PSD block matrix, completing squares gives the factorization into a block supported on the J rows and a residual supported only on T. The latter is PSD and its nonzero range lies in range(Z) intersect T. Conversely, if that residual is zero, the factorized range has no nonzero vector with zero J coordinates. This proves the equivalence, including singular Z_JJ. For n=1, J is empty and (SC) means Z=0.

This range restriction retains all history-dependent entries of Z; it does not replace Z by a two-by-two principal minor.

## 4. Exact one-step checks, including nu=0 above the Huber level

For b=1+a with 1/2<a<1, there is a tight certificate with

    q=a^2,
    lambda_{0,*}=2a, lambda_{1,*}=2(1-a), lambda_{1,0}=2a,

and all other multipliers zero. Its Schur complement is

    Z=(2a-1)[[1,1/a],[1/a,1/a^2]]
      =[(2a-1)/a^2] (a,1)^T(a,1).

Thus (H) holds with s=+1, kappa=(2a-1)/a^2, even though every star-outgoing multiplier vanishes. Formula (D) gives an explicit strict descent by decreasing b. The matching legal quadratic has g_1=-a g_0, exactly the relation exposed by the PSD square.

For 0<b<3/2, the tight Huber certificate with lambda_{0,*}=lambda_{1,*}=lambda_{1,0}=1 has

    q=1/(2b+1), Z=(3-2b)[[1,-1],[-1,1]]/4.

Here (H) holds with a=1, s=-1. The final step increases and the uniform bound strictly improves. This is consistent with the exact one-step optimum b=3/2, where Z=0 and this descent disappears.

These checks also show why q>tau alone is neither the hypothesis nor the conclusion of this result: the range mechanism can detect a suboptimal Huber-tight schedule, and it detects a non-Huber certificate with nu=0.

## 5. Remaining obstruction

Together with the penultimate-flow descent in research/max2_penultimate_flow_descent.md, the new constraints rule out two concrete ways for a globally minimizing tight certificate to carry slack: lambda_{*,n-1}>0 and any Schur-range vector supported on the final two gradients.

They leave earlier star-outgoing multipliers, the final star-outgoing multiplier, and a Schur range intertwined with earlier gradients. There is no proved implication from (R) to q=tau, no proved capacity bound by S_bullet(n), and no exact-profile conclusion. The next mechanism would have to control that earlier-coordinate dependence without treating the final two-coordinate Schur complement as the full matrix.

A_i(c):=<w_i,z>=(1-r)/M_i [1-2t],                         (4)

<w_(i+k),z>=(1-r)r^(k-1)/M_(i+k) [r+t(1-r)],              (5)
<w_(i-k),z>=(1-r)r^(k-1)/M_(i-k) [-1+t(1-r)].             (6)

<w_m,u_m>=(1-r)/5=7/25,

f(u_m)=7/25-7/125-1/50=51/250,

W_(2m)(h)>=2f(u_m)=51/125.                               (9)

f(u_i-u w_i)=(1-r)/M_i-(2u+1)(1-r)/M_i^2-eta, u=0,1.

<w_i,w_j>=-(1-r)^2 r^(k-1)/(M_i M_j).                    (10)
They are nonzero at every separation and alternate in sign. The two equal gradients inside each block add positive temporal correlations. The Gram matrix is explicitly PSD because(1) constructs real vectors, not because of a guessed covariance condition.

The normals w_0,...,w_m are linearly independent: the coefficient of the new basis vector e_(i+1) in w_i is nonzero, while all earlier normals lack that coordinate. The number of independent sampled gradient directions therefore grows with m.

The Moreau envelope is genuinely nonseparable in any fixed orthonormal coordinates. For each i, linear independence of the normals allows a point z satisfying <w_i,z>=eta and <w_j,z><eta for j!=i.
