Neighboring normals are neither orthogonal nor parallel by(1),(10), so these two projectors do not commute. A function separable in one orthonormal basis has commuting Hessians at all points where they exist. This proves the claim.

This family is thus outside both the scalar constructions and the exact orthogonality hypotheses of fact0e7e78056dc6258c.

max{1/(2 e m),(4/5)^(2m)} ->0,                           (11)
uniformly in all the varying b_i. Orthogonal diagonalization extends this bound to every finite-dimensional convex quadratic. Equation(9) is therefore a nonlinear, nonseparable persistent-error construction on mixed short/long schedules whose full quadratic channel converges. It is not a claim that scalar nonlinear witnesses are small on this particular class.

Now take a common block mass M>0 and common ordinary-block sum s>=0, so the checkpoint is b=M-s. Use M_i=M also for the terminal virtual normal, a common offset eta, and r=-a with0<=a<1. At the final ordinary query put t=(s+1)/M. Formula(4) has normalized current value C=1-2t.

a[1-t(1+a)].
It is dominated by C exactly when
t<=1/(2+a),                                             (12)
provided a<1. The largest future comparison is max{A,-a A}, where A=-a+t(1+a). Its lag1 requirement C>=A is exactly
t<=(1+a)/(3+a).                                         (13)
The other requirement C>=-a A is t<=(1+a)/(2+a), which is weaker than(12).
Thus every plane comparison, including arbitrary past and future lags, is satisfied precisely at
t<=min{1/(2+a),(1+a)/(3+a)}                              (14)
for a chain containing the relevant lag2 and future1 comparisons; in any shorter chain it is a sufficient condition. The zero plane additionally requires eta<= (1+a)(1-2t)/M, so a strictly positive common offset is available throughout(14).

The first term in(14) decreases with a, the second increases. Their crossing solves a^2+2a-1=0, namely a=sqrt2-1. The largest allowed t is therefore sqrt2-1, and the least admissible common mass ratio is
M/(s+1)=1+sqrt2.                                        (15)

For a varying block partition, formulas(4)--(6) remain explicit with the actual M_i and actual endpoint query values c=1,s_i+1. With nonnegative plane offsets eta_i, full legality is the finite system
A_i(c)-eta_i>=0,
A_i(c)-eta_i>=<w_j,u_i-cw_i>-eta_j for every j,
at those two c endpoints. The comparisons are affine in c, so they cover all intermediate nonnegative partial sums. This is a precise extension mechanism with all remote planes retained. The robust interval construction above is an actual solved nonstationary case of that system.

## 7. Target-scale limitation still visible
The threshold(15) alone does not imply that arbitrary schedules admit a strong relay decomposition. In particular it requires a selected checkpoint b to satisfy
b >= sqrt2 s+(1+sqrt2)
in the stationary case, so it does not capture arbitrary smaller checkpoints after large ordinary blocks. The intended lower-bound profile is not obtained by asserting that these decompositions always exist.

The next mutation must use variable block-start distances, nonstationary correlations, or within-block changing gradients while keeping the full comparisons(4)--(6) or their exact replacement. The concrete achievement here is a globally legal correlated family that repairs the previous relay's hostile(1,4) test, survives arbitrary parameter changes b_i in[4,5], and exposes an exact correlation-versus-history tradeoff. # Earlier reset weights: a quantitative bound and an exact obstruction to naive propagation

Status: unverified supplement to the full-certificate descent search. All claims below are proved directly; no earlier unverified finding is used as an assumed theorem.

## 1. A reset criterion for any earlier star-outgoing multiplier

Normalize L=1, f_*=0. Consider a full feasible certificate at level q for a length-n schedule h. Let nu_i=lambda_{*,i}>0 for some i<n. Define

    delta_i=f(x_i)-||g_i||^2/2 >=0,
    A_i=prod_{t=i+1}^{n-1} max{1,(h_t-1)^2}.

The full PSD certificate, with the term nu_i Q_{*,i}=-nu_i delta_i isolated, gives for every legal function

    2f(x_n)+nu_i delta_i <= q||x_0-x_*||^2.                 (1)

Replace h_i by one, leaving every other step in place. The changed trajectory agrees with the old one through x_i and reaches y=x_i-g_i at the next iteration. Unit-step descent gives f(y)<=delta_i.

For any nonnegative step a and any current point z, smoothness gives

    f(z-a grad f(z)) <= f(z)+(a^2/2-a)||grad f(z)||^2.

When 0<=a<=2, this is at most f(z). When a>2, use ||grad f(z)||^2<=2f(z) to obtain an upper bound (a-1)^2 f(z). Thus the unchanged suffix multiplies the objective by at most A_i, and

    W_n(h with h_i replaced by 1) <= (2A_i/nu_i) q.          (2)

In particular nu_i>2A_i gives a genuine fixed-length strict improvement. Every tight certificate at a globally minimizing schedule must therefore obey

    nu_i<=2A_i, 0<=i<n.                                    (3)

At i=n-1, direct endpoint convexity gives the much stronger conclusion nu_{n-1}=0 by the explicit last-step descent already recorded separately. Bound (3) is useful for earlier indices but does NOT assert that their multipliers vanish.

The product A_i is a proved worst-case growth bound, not a guess about conditional history. It can be large and does not itself yield the exact Zhang--Jiang profile.

## 2. Exact failure of carrying final-step convexity through even one later unit step

A tempting extension is to move an earlier step toward one and then use convexity to average the two resulting terminal objective values after the unchanged suffix. This fails for a single unchanged unit step.

Define an everywhere finite convex 1-smooth function on the real line by

    f(x)=x^2/2,                       x<=1;
         x-1/2,                       1<=x<=2;
         (x-1)^2/2+1,                 2<=x<=3;
         2x-3,                        x>=3.

Its derivative is, respectively, x, 1, x-1, and 2. It is continuous, nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz. The unique minimum is f(0)=0.

Write T(x)=x-f'(x), the unit GD update, and F(x)=f(T(x)). The following exact values hold:

    F(3/2)=1/8,
    F(5/2)=1/2,
    F(2)=1/2 > (F(3/2)+F(5/2))/2 =5/16.                   (4)

Thus f composed with a unit GD step is not convex, even though f itself is convex and 1-smooth.

The points in (4) arise from exactly the proposed schedule interpolation. Start at x_0=9/2, where g_0=2. The first step b=3/2 gives x_1=3/2. Replacing it by the unit step gives x_1=5/2. Taking their midpoint step b=5/4 gives x_1=2. Follow all three by the same final unit step. Their final objective values are respectively 1/8, 1/2, and 1/2. Hence the middle schedule's value exceeds the convex average of the endpoint schedules by 3/16, with a common function and common initial point.

This refutes the exact propagation step needed to extend the penultimate convex-blend proof unchanged to earlier times. It does not refute a different simultaneous schedule/certificate perturbation, and the example is not claimed to be a matching worst-case stationary tuple.

## 3. Consequence for the active program

The final-step descent uses literal convexity of f along the final update line. Earlier reset changes enter a nonlinear suffix, so that proof cannot simply be repeated backward. The quantitative fallback (2) survives, but requires sufficiently large multiplier weight relative to the proved suffix-growth factor.

Likewise the terminal-pair Schur-range descent controls a perturbation at the final point directly; an earlier gradient relation cannot be treated as if the rest of the GD trajectory were affine. Any propagation mechanism must retain or bound the actual suffix response. This is the concrete obstruction to the attempted backward extension, not a conclusion that all full-certificate approaches fail.

evidence:
# Explicit forward transfer of optimum-outgoing multipliers

Status: unverified new certificate operation. It preserves the standard full matrix and nonnegative interpolation multipliers under the stated capacity condition.

## 1. One adjacent transfer

Use the signed smooth-convex quantities

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0,

with the optimum sample * equal to zero. Fix a positive step h_i=a>0, so x_{i+1}=x_i-a g_i. A direct expansion gives the polynomial identity

    Q_{*,i+1}+(1/a)Q_{i+1,i}+((1-a)/a)Q_{i,i+1}
       -Q_{*,i}
       =(1/a)||g_{i+1}-(1-a)g_i||^2.                       (I)

For clarity, write delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2. Then
Q_{i+1,i}=delta_{i+1}-delta_i+||g_{i+1}||^2+(a-1)<g_i,g_{i+1}>,
and
Q_{i,i+1}+Q_{i+1,i}=(1-a)||g_i||^2+||g_{i+1}||^2+(a-2)<g_i,g_{i+1}>.
Substitution yields (I), including all coefficients and signs.

Take any full feasible upper certificate with multipliers lambda and PSD slack M. Choose t>0 satisfying

    t<=lambda_{*,i},
    t<=a lambda_{i,i+1}/(a-1)       when a>1.                (C)

When 0<a<=1 the second condition is absent. Change only these four multipliers:

    lambda'_{*,i}=lambda_{*,i}-t,
    lambda'_{*,i+1}=lambda_{*,i+1}+t,
    lambda'_{i+1,i}=lambda_{i+1,i}+t/a,
    lambda'_{i,i+1}=lambda_{i,i+1}+t(1-a)/a.                (T)

All multipliers remain nonnegative by (C), and each node's flow divergence is unchanged. The schedule h and certificate level q are unchanged. The FULL slack changes by

    M'=M+(t/a)||g_{i+1}-(1-a)g_i||^2 >=0.                  (P)

Thus (T) is an explicit feasible motion in the original certificate variables, not merely a reduced row-sum operation. It neither assumes stationarity nor removes any PSD constraint.

For a<=1, the transfer adds or preserves the forward-edge multiplier. For a>1 it consumes exactly t(a-1)/a of the existing forward edge lambda_{i,i+1}. At a=1 the added square is t||g_{i+1}||^2 and no forward capacity is consumed.

## 2. Transport across a whole interval

Suppose lambda_{*,i}>0 for some i<n-1. Assume that for every j=i,...,n-2, either

    0<h_j<=1,

or

    h_j>1 and lambda_{j,j+1}>0.                             (A)

Choose t>0 at most lambda_{*,i} and at most every finite capacity

    h_j lambda_{j,j+1}/(h_j-1),  j in [i,n-2] with h_j>1.

There are finitely many strictly positive capacities, so such a t exists. Apply (T) successively at j=i,...,n-2, always transferring the same amount t. Intermediate optimum-outgoing weights receive t and then pass it on, while the consumed adjacent forward edges are distinct. The resulting standard-format certificate has

    lambda'_{*,i}=lambda_{*,i}-t,
    lambda'_{*,n-1}=lambda_{*,n-1}+t>0,

and unchanged other optimum-outgoing weights, schedule, objective level and flow divergence. Its full matrix is

    M'=M+sum_{j=i}^{n-2}(t/h_j)
             ||g_{j+1}-(1-h_j)g_j||^2 >=0.                 (B)

No arbitrary chronological crossing edge has been discarded; the operation modifies only the stated adjacent multipliers and retains the rest of the original matrix exactly.

## 3. A resulting actual descent of the algorithm

Write nu=lambda'_{*,n-1}>0 and b=h_{n-1}. Isolating Q_{*,n-1}=-(f_{n-1}-||g_{n-1}||^2/2) in the transferred certificate gives

    2f_n+nu delta_{n-1}<=q||x_0-x_*||^2.

At x=x_{n-1}, the unit-step point y=x-g_{n-1} satisfies f(y)<=delta_{n-1}. The old endpoint is z=x-b g_{n-1}. For epsilon=nu/(nu+2), c=1-epsilon, the new final step b_new=c b+epsilon gives z_new=c z+epsilon y. Convexity yields

    2f(z_new)<=2c f(z)+2epsilon delta_{n-1}
                =c[2f(z)+nu delta_{n-1}]
                <=c q||x_0-x_*||^2.

Thus the concrete predetermined schedule with final step

    b_new=(2b+nu)/(2+nu)

has the strict uniform bound

    W_n(h_0,...,h_{n-2},b_new)<=2q/(2+nu)<q.

This is a genuine fixed-length improvement. The transfer phase stayed within the minimal full interpolation certificate, and the final convexity argument is valid for the same function in every instance. If desired, its explicit enlarged PSD certificate is obtained by adding the old endpoint and unit-step point as auxiliary analysis samples; its identity is given in research/max2_penultimate_flow_descent.md.

## 4. A forced blocking pattern at global minimizers

For a globally minimizing positive schedule and ANY tight full certificate, lambda_{*,n-1}=0. Moreover, if lambda_{*,i}>0 with i<n-1, then there must exist at least one j in [i,n-2] such that

    h_j>1 and lambda_{j,j+1}=0.                             (Block)

Otherwise (A) would transport positive weight to the penultimate point and the preceding explicit schedule change would strictly improve the global value.

This is a necessary pattern in the actual full certificate. It does not say that every star-outgoing weight vanishes: an overrelaxed step with a zero forward edge can block this particular transfer. The final weight lambda_{*,n} is also outside the fixed-length transport argument.

## 5. Tightness and matching primal data

If the original q is tight at the fixed h, every matching legal primal remains matching after any feasible transfer: h and q have not changed and the new certificate is globally valid. Because M' is the sum of M and the nonnegative squares in (B), each transferred square must vanish on that matching primal:

    g_{j+1}=(1-h_j)g_j

at every transfer edge. The new positive star weights also require delta_j=0 wherever they are placed. These are consequences of the full certificate and primal complementarity, not assumptions used to discard other inequalities.

This explains the restrictive nature of the transport. In particular, the earlier nonlinear-suffix counterexample does not invalidate (I): its relevant tight-certificate capacity conditions are not supplied. Conversely, it remains invalid to bypass a zero forward edge merely by claiming that the composed objective is convex.

## 6. Scope of the new mechanism

The operation supplies a concrete way to exploit some earlier optimum-outgoing weights while preserving PSD and every multiplier sign. It isolates exact barriers h_j>1, lambda_{j,j+1}=0 rather than an unspecified missing separator.

It still does not show that a q>tau global minimizer must have a transferable weight, or that the full Schur defect can always remove a blocking edge. Those are distinct open structural questions. No implication to the exact profile U_n^ZJ is asserted.

# Active analytic interface: retain a squared gradient-aggregate residual

Status: self-contained unverified certificate algebra and two exact tests. This is an analytic mechanism after the600-evaluation discovery cap, not a claimed improved schedule family. No numerical scan extension or new verifier submission.

Work at L=1. For a nonnegative schedule h of length n, use x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i). Let u=(u_0,...,u_n) be nonnegative proof weights with D=sum u_i>0. These are certificate coefficients, not algorithmic state or additional GD updates. Define
U=sum_i u_i g_i, d=x_0-x_n, e=U-d,
E_h(u)=2sum_i u_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_i u_i||g_i||^2+2sum_i u_i<g_i,x_0-x_i>-||U||^2.

For any minimizer x_star, direct expansion gives
||x_0-x_star||^2+2sum_i u_i Q_(i,star)-2D(f_n-f_star)
=||x_n-x_star-e||^2+E_h(u),
where Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0. Hence any bound
E_h(u)>=nu||e-kappa g_n||^2, nu>=0,                 (A)
implies W_n(h)<=1/D. Unlike a saturated primitive certificate, D is independent of the physical sum and can be strictly below2sum(h)+1. The square preserves vector information about the difference between the certificate gradient aggregate and actual GD displacement.

For completeness Q_ij<=0 follows by applying the smooth descent inequality to F(z)=f(z)-<g_i,z>: x_i minimizes F, and F(x_j-grad F(x_j))<=F(x_j)-||grad F(x_j)||^2/2. This gives the displayed interpolation inequality; the smooth descent inequality follows by integrating the Lipschitz gradient along a segment.

1. Exact tested one-step family.
Let t=1+r with1/2<=r<=1 and take h=[t], u_0=1/r, u_1=(1-r)/r^2. Then D=1/r^2 and direct coefficient comparison gives
E_h(u)=(2/r)(-Q_10)+((2r-1)/r^4)||r g_0+g_1||^2.
Both coefficients are nonnegative. Moreover
e-g_1=((1-r-r^2)/r^2)(r g_0+g_1).
If1-r-r^2!=0, (A) therefore holds with
kappa=1, nu=(2r-1)/(1-r-r^2)^2.
If1-r-r^2=0, e-g_1 vanishes identically, so any finite nu>=0 is allowed in (A). The objective bound is W_1(t)<=r^2, attained by f(x)=x^2/2. Thus this is a real unsaturated objective certificate rather than a proposed potential with no examples.

A convenient rational seed is t=5/3, u=(3/2,3/4), D=9/4, kappa=1, nu=27. Its exact identity is
E_[5/3](u)=3(-Q_10)+(27/16)||(2/3)g_0+g_1||^2
          =3(-Q_10)+27||e-g_1||^2.

2. Exact one-step transport as a3-by3 matrix condition.
Suppose (A) is available for a block. Append a predetermined step t>=0. Put g=g_n, q=g_(n+1). Keep the old weights except increase u_n by alpha, and append the new weight beta. Require
u_n+alpha>=0, beta>=0, D'=D+alpha+beta>0,
where nu_n in this line means the old terminal weight u_n, not the coefficient nu. Equivalently, the first condition is simply u_n+alpha>=0. Define
u'>=0, kappa' real, e'=e+(alpha-t)g+beta q.
Choose mu>=0 with 2(D+alpha)+mu>=0.

Let M be the symmetric3-by3 coefficient matrix in the vector variables(e,g,q) with entries
M_ee=nu-nu',
M_eg=-nu kappa-alpha-nu'(alpha-t),
M_eq=-beta-nu'(beta-kappa'),
M_gg=nu kappa^2+D+alpha+alpha(1-alpha)-nu'(alpha-t)^2-mu(t-1),
M_qq=D+alpha+beta(1-beta)-nu'(beta-kappa')^2+mu,
M_gq=(D+alpha)(t-1)+beta(t-alpha)-nu'(alpha-t)(beta-kappa')-(mu/2)(2-t).

If M is positive semidefinite, the extended schedule satisfies
E_(h,t)(u')>=nu'||e'-kappa' q||^2.
This is an explicit sufficient matrix test with fixed dimension. Its identity is
E_(h,t)(u')-nu'||e'-kappa'q||^2
=E_h(u)-nu||e-kappa g||^2
 +[2(D+alpha)+mu](-Q_(n+1,n))+mu(-Q_(n,n+1))
 +(e,g,q)^T M(e,g,q).
The matrix quadratic form means the same coefficients paired with Euclidean inner products, so PSD suffices in every dimension.

To check the identity before imposing positivity, the exact energy increment is
E_(h,t)(u')-E_h(u)
=2(D+alpha)(f_n-f_(n+1))+alpha(1-alpha)||g||^2+beta(1-beta)||q||^2
 +2beta(t-alpha)<g,q>-2<e,alpha g+beta q>.
Substituting the two interpolation expressions gives the displayed matrix. No unknown interpolation theorem or numerical feasibility claim is hidden in this transport rule.

3. A nontrivial exact transport test.
For the rational seed in part1, append t=1 and choose alpha=0,beta=1,nu'=27,kappa'=28/27,mu=0. Then
M=diag(0,9/4,239/108)>=0.
Thus h=(5/3,1) with proof weights(3/2,3/4,1), D'=13/4, has the exact bound
E_h(u')>=27||e'-(28/27)g_2||^2,
so W_2(5/3,1)<=4/13. This bound is deliberately reported at its actual value; it is weaker than the project benchmark and supplies no negative answer to(P). Its role is to test that the new residual state transports with a nonzero coefficient and nonnegative interpolation multipliers.

4. Necessary tests and the unresolved propagation issue.
For an all-affine Huber trajectory with constant sampled gradient and s=sum h,
E_h(u)=D(2s+1-D)||g||^2, e=(D-s)g.
Thus (A) must obey
nu(D-s-kappa)^2<=D(2s+1-D).
For f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1, define p_i=product_(j<i)(1-h_j), p=p_n and w=sum_i u_i p_i. Then it must also obey
1-Dp^2-(1-w)^2>=nu[w-1+(1-kappa)p]^2.
These give immediate exact hostile tests for any proposed coefficient recursion.

The one-step matrix has M_ee=nu-nu', so this particular adjacent-interpolation update cannot increase nu. A proposed long-block rule must address this restriction, rather than claim that repeated application already gives the desired rate. No growth law for D has been proved. In particular no D_n>B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 has been obtained.

A concrete extension to investigate is discounting old proof weights and retaining the full displacement as a vector coordinate. For0<=eta<=1,
E_h(eta u)=eta E_h(u)+eta(1-eta)||U||^2.
If new weights are u'=(eta u+alpha at the old terminal sample,beta at the new sample), then
E_(h,t)(u')=eta E_h(u)+eta(1-eta)||U||^2
 +2(eta D+alpha)(f_n-f_(n+1))+alpha(1-alpha)||g||^2+beta(1-beta)||q||^2
 +2beta(t-alpha)<g,q>+2<d-eta U,alpha g+beta q>.
The retained coordinates(d,U,g) transform linearly to(d+tg,eta U+alpha g+beta q,q). This gives a concrete next matrix interface; it is not a proved accelerated closure. Nonlocal interpolation links within concatenated blocks may be necessary to regain sufficient residual control. A complete candidate still needs a feasible infinite recursion, an actual objective upper bound, and an exact comparison with the true B_n profile.

evidence:
# Variable-energy Markov gradients with positive affine offsets
Status: complete new construction and exact quantitative test; unverified.
No new verifier allocation requested. This is a mutation of the fixed-radius relay, not a claim that its sufficient conditions hold for arbitrary h.

## 1. A finite max-affine construction with a closed history criterion
Partition a predetermined nonnegative schedule chronologically as
(block_0,b_0,...,block_(m-1),b_(m-1),block_m),
where block_i has sum s_i, following the project notation.
Choose positive amplitudes alpha_i and positive virtual budgets t_i with
t_i>=s_i+1,0<=i<=m.
Put
B_i^M=(s_i+b_i-t_i)alpha_i for0<=i<m,
r_i^M=-t_(i+1)alpha_(i+1)/B_i^M,
and require B_i^M>0 and -1<r_i^M<0.
Choose unit vectors recursively in R^(m+1):
zeta_0=e_0,
zeta_(i+1)=r_i^M zeta_i+sqrt(1-(r_i^M)^2)e_(i+1).
Define omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i. Their correlations are explicitly
C_ij=<zeta_i,zeta_j>=product_(l=min(i,j))^(max(i,j)-1)r_l^M
for i!=j, and C_ii=1.
This gives a real PSD Gram matrix and linearly independent gradients.

Let nonnegative offsets eta_i be chosen and define the ONE fixed function
J(z)=max{0,max_(0<=i<=m)(<omega_i,z>-eta_i)},
f(x)=min_z {J(z)+||x-z||^2/2}.                            (1)
Start at X_0=t_0 alpha_0 zeta_0. One may impose t_0 alpha_0=1 for exact initial normalization; otherwise divide the final payoff by(t_0 alpha_0)^2.
The function f is convex differentiable1-smooth, minimized at0 with value0. These facts follow directly from the Moreau minimization of the finite nonnegative convex J. In particular, if plane i is active at z=x-omega_i, then the subgradient optimality condition gives grad f(x)=omega_i and
f(x)=<omega_i,x>-||omega_i||^2/2-eta_i.                   (2)
This directly realizes all values; no interpolation theorem is being invoked as an unverified black box.

Define the intended block-start points by
X_(i+1)=X_i-(s_i+b_i)omega_i.
Set Z_i=X_i-t_i omega_i.
The following three EXPLICIT conditions are sufficient for every intended gradient and hence the exact supplied GD trajectory:
(a) D_i^M:=B_i^M(1-(r_i^M)^2) satisfies
    D_i^M>=|r_i^M|D_(i+1)^M,0<=i<m-1;                  (3)
(b) C_ij alpha_j<=alpha_i for every distinct i,j;      (4)
(c) with delta_i=t_i-s_i-1>=0,
    0<=eta_i<=delta_i alpha_i^2,
    eta_i-eta_j<=delta_i alpha_i(alpha_i-C_ij alpha_j)
    for every distinct i,j.                           (5)

These are conditions on a specified frame and specified affine offsets. Their feasibility at the target scale for arbitrary schedules is NOT assumed.

## 2. Why the entire history is retained
The defining r_i^M gives the exact recurrence
Z_0=0,
Z_(i+1)=Z_i-B_i^M(zeta_i-r_i^M zeta_(i+1)).              (6)
A direct induction using the Markov products gives
<Z_i,zeta_j>=0 for j>=i,
and, for j<i,
<Z_i,zeta_j>=-sum_(l=j)^(i-1)D_l^M C_(j,l).             (7)
To verify(7), note that for j<=i,
<zeta_i-r_i^M zeta_(i+1),zeta_j>
=(1-(r_i^M)^2)C_(j,i),
whereas it is zero for j>=i+1.

The sum on the right of(7) is nonnegative. Pair its terms at l=j,j+1, then j+2,j+3, and so on. Each even-position product C_(j,l) is positive, and the paired contribution equals
C_(j,l)[D_l^M-|r_l^M|D_(l+1)^M]>=0
by(3). A possible final unpaired term is positive. Thus
<Z_i,omega_j><=0 for j<i,
<Z_i,omega_j>=0 for j>=i.                               (8)
The second line means equality to0, not positivity; equivalently, it is =0.
No old plane has been discarded.

At a query in block i let u be the partial ordinary step sum already used, so0<=u<=s_i. The intended point is x=X_i-u omega_i, and
z=x-omega_i=Z_i+d omega_i,
d=t_i-u-1>=delta_i.
The current plane has value d alpha_i^2-eta_i>=0.
By(8), any other plane has value at most
d alpha_i C_ij alpha_j-eta_j.
Its difference from the current plane is therefore at least
d alpha_i(alpha_i-C_ij alpha_j)-eta_i+eta_j.
Condition(4) allows replacing d by its lower bound delta_i; then(5) proves nonnegativity. Consequently plane i dominates all other planes and the zero plane at every query. Formula(2) gives exactly the intended constant gradient throughout block_i, including its checkpoint query. The actual update reaches X_(i+1), completing the induction. Repeated points from zero steps cause no difficulty.

The terminal ordinary block follows omega_m in the same way. Its exact normalized value is
W_n(h)>=
 [2(t_m-s_m-1/2)alpha_m^2-2eta_m]/(t_0 alpha_0)^2.      (9)
Every sampled value is explicitly
f(X_i-u omega_i)=(t_i-u-1/2)alpha_i^2-eta_i.
The construction is a finite-dimensional global function, so every cross-time smooth-convex interpolation inequality and the optimum sample are satisfied.

The amplitude recursion can be written
alpha_(i+1)=|r_i^M| (s_i+b_i-t_i)alpha_i/t_(i+1).          (10)

## 4. Nonseparability and the quadratic comparison
The gradients omega_0,...,omega_m are linearly independent by their nonzero fresh coordinates in the Markov recursion. Adjacent inner products are

which are nonzero. The normals are independent and adjacent ones are nonorthogonal, so these projectors do not commute. Simultaneous diagonal Hessians would be necessary for orthogonal separability.

For the same schedules, the full quadratic-class normalized error tends uniformly to0. On a scalar eigenvalue lambda in[0,1], each block multiplier is

The key addition is the signed-sum formula(7) and its global control by(3), together with positive face margins and the explicit cross-plane inequalities(4)--(5). Choosing only a locally valid AR covariance would not prove them.

For example, the old constant-energy rule on the single-step schedule(2,3) corresponds formally to ordinary sums0, budgets t_i=1, amplitudes1, and correlations -1 and-1/2. Equations(9)--(10) are a genuine multiplicative high-dimensional transfer with full legality conditions. The present solved range is a stability/instability test for mixed short/long schedules, not the exact minimax theorem. No claim is made that a partition, amplitudes, virtual budgets and correlations meeting(3)--(5) with payoff(1-o(1))U_n^ZJ exist for every h.

The conditions reveal specific costs: the virtual budget t_i must cover every ordinary-block query; the history weights D_i^M must control alternating past sums; and positive offsets must remain below the actual face margin. The next search is to vary these quantities on the recursive hostile schedules, or to replace the paired sufficient condition by a sharper exact signed-sum analysis. Simply postulating the needed choice would be theorem-strength and remains BLOCKED.

# Exact conditional amplification of a primitive seed

Status: complete unverified argument responding to master_guidance 56a30fdd80e74d9e. No seed meeting the hypothesis is known, and this is not a resolution of the unrestricted target. No additional verifier call is authorized.

## Claim and interfaces

Use the project's exact S_circle, S_bullet, B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 and U_n=1/B_n. Put lambda=1+sqrt(2) and rho=log_2(lambda). Suppose a nonnegative primitive schedule a of length r>=1 has shifted capacity A=1+sum(a) satisfying

    A>(r+1)^rho.                                      (1)

Then there are predetermined nonnegative schedules H_n of length (r+1)n, constructed solely with the usual ConPP/ConPD operations and repeated copies of a, such that

    W_((r+1)n)(H_n)
      <=[sqrt(A B_n)-(sqrt(A)-1)]^(-2).                (2)

Moreover,

    liminf_(n->infinity) W_((r+1)n)(H_n)/U_((r+1)n)
      <=(r+1)^rho/A<1.                                (3)

Thus this stronger finite seed hypothesis is sufficient for the negative answer required by the project, along an infinite subsequence, without assuming convergence of B_n/n^rho or replacing the exact DP by a decimal profile.

The analytic schedule interfaces invoked here are the following standard Zhang–Jiang closure statements, stated to remove ambiguity about the hypotheses. At L=1 write Q_(i,star)=f_i-f_star-<g_i,x_i-x_star>+||g_i||^2/2. A schedule h with s=sum(h) is primitive if

  ||x_0-x_star||^2+2sum_(i<n) h_i Q_(i,star)-2s(f_n-f_star)
  >=||x_n-x_star||^2+s(s+1)||g_n||^2

for every legal smooth convex GD trajectory. A schedule h is dominant if there are nonnegative weights u_0,...,u_n summing to 2s+1 such that

  ||x_0-x_star||^2+2sum_i u_i Q_(i,star)-2(2s+1)(f_n-f_star)
  >=||x_0-x_star-sum_i u_i g_i||^2.

The empty schedule has both properties. If a,b are primitive, ConPP(a,b)=[a,phi(sum(a),sum(b)),b] is primitive. If a is primitive and b is dominant, ConPD(a,b)=[a,psi(sum(a),sum(b)),b] is dominant. Dominance implies W(h)<=1/(2sum(h)+1), since all Q_(i,star)<=0. Sources: Zhang–Jiang, arXiv:2410.12395, definitions and ConPP/ConPD theorems; the downloaded HTML numbers these Theorems11 and12 and the dominant objective implication Theorem6 (the published/new-paper numbering is3.1,3.2 and2.6). These closure proofs were read in the preceding max4 rounds; this new amplification argument does not assert their promotion to new project facts. Any future verification package must include their proper external-reference metadata or verified predecessors.

The only accepted project fact used below is 0be8b54e0a33381c, for the explicit scalar G join and its square-root nonexpansiveness. Other ingredients are proved here. The proof of the scalar power inequality is adapted, with notation changed, from Liu–Chen–Jiang–Wang arXiv:2609.11788v1, Lemma5.1 and AppendixC.1; its full proof is included below, so no phase theorem is assumed. Two Matlas queries, including the exact title/identifier, returned unrelated results; no Matlas grounding is falsely claimed.

## 1. A finite positive benchmark limsup

For shifted primitive masses x,y>=0 set

  F(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt(x^2+6xy+y^2))/2.

Let q=1/rho. The inequality

  F(x,y)^q<=x^q+y^q                                  (4)

holds. Here is an elementary proof. Zero arguments give equality. For positive arguments write x=exp(m-t), y=exp(m+t), t>=0, using symmetry. Then

  F(x,y)=exp(m+arsinh(cosh(t))).

Inequality(4) is equivalent to J(t)>=0, where

  J(t)=q^(-1)log(2cosh(qt))-arsinh(cosh(t)).

Because 2^(1/q)=lambda, J(0)=0; direct exponential asymptotics give J(t)->0 as t->infinity. Its derivative is

  J'(t)=tanh(qt)-sinh(t)/sqrt(1+cosh(t)^2).

Define alpha(t)=artanh(sinh(t)/sqrt(1+cosh(t)^2)). Its derivative is cosh(t)/sqrt(1+cosh(t)^2), strictly increasing from1/sqrt(2) to1. Also1/sqrt(2)<q<1: lambda>2 gives the upper inequality; lambda^3=7+5sqrt(2)<16 gives q>3/4>1/sqrt(2). Hence alpha(t)-qt is strictly convex, vanishes at0, initially decreases, and tends to infinity. Its derivative increases to1-q>0, so it has exactly one positive zero t_0. Monotonicity of tanh implies J'>0 on(0,t_0) and J'<0 on(t_0,infinity). The two zero endpoint limits imply J(t)>0 for t>0, proving(4).

Write P_k=1+S_circle(k). Every primitive DP tree with k+1 leaves has root capacity at most(k+1)^rho by(4) and induction from unit leaves. Thus

  P_k<=(k+1)^rho.                                    (5)

The shifted dominant join is

  G(x,d)=2x+d/2+sqrt(d^2+8xd)/2.

Since sqrt(d^2+8xd)<=d+4x, one has G(x,d)<=d+4x. Unroll an optimizing dominant tree along its unique dominant continuation. If the attached primitive subtrees have leaf counts l_1,...,l_t, then each l_i>=1 and sum_i l_i=n. The final dominant leaf has mass1. By(5),

  B_n<=1+4sum_i l_i^rho<=1+4n^rho.                    (6)

The final inequality follows by repeated(a+b)^rho>=a^rho+b^rho for a,b>=0 and rho>1; for fixed a its difference has nonnegative derivative in b and vanishes at b=0.

Conversely, balanced primitive trees with2^k leaves attain shifted mass lambda^k, since F(x,x)=lambda x. For n=2^k the legal dominant split consisting of this(n-1)-step primitive prefix, one ConPD bridge, and an empty continuation gives

  B_n>=G(lambda^k,1)>=2lambda^k=2n^rho.              (7)

Consequently the real number

  K=limsup_(n->infinity) B_n/n^rho

exists in the extended-real sense and satisfies2<=K<=4. In particular it is finite and strictly positive. No single normalized limit or periodic-phase theorem is used.

## 2. Replace every primitive leaf; retain the terminal dominant leaf

For each n>=1 choose one fully expanded optimizing dominant DP tree T_n. It has n internal nodes and n+1 leaves. Exactly one leaf, at the end of its dominant continuation, has dominant type. All other n leaves have primitive type. This count follows inductively: at each dominant node the left subtree is a pure primitive tree and the right subtree contains exactly one dominant leaf; all-primitive nodes have two primitive children.

Replace each of the n primitive empty leaves by the certified schedule a. Keep the single dominant terminal leaf empty. Re-evaluate every bridge with phi or psi from its new child sums. This specifies a concrete nonnegative schedule H_n independent of the objective. Closure gives a primitive schedule at every primitive node and a dominant schedule at every dominant node. The original n bridge steps remain, and the inserted copies contribute rn steps. Therefore

  length(H_n)=(r+1)n.                                (8)

Positive homogeneity of F implies that every primitive subtree's mass is now exactly A times its old mass. Let D_n=2sum(H_n)+1. Along the dominant continuation compare the true construction with an auxiliary scalar evaluation having the same scaled primitive children but terminal scalar mass A instead of1. Homogeneity of G says that the auxiliary root mass is exactly A B_n.

For fixed x>=0 let

  T_x(z)=(z+sqrt(z^2+8x))/2.

Accepted fact0be8b54e0a33381c proves sqrt(G(x,d))=T_x(sqrt(d)) and that T_x is increasing and1-Lipschitz on nonnegative arguments. The true and auxiliary terminal square-root masses differ by sqrt(A)-1. Propagate both through the identical sequence of T_x maps. The difference remains between0 and sqrt(A)-1. Hence

  sqrt(A B_n)-(sqrt(A)-1)<=sqrt(D_n)<=sqrt(A B_n).    (9)

The lower bound is at least1 because B_n>=1. Dominance gives W(H_n)<=1/D_n, which proves(2). This handles the unmatched dominant leaf explicitly rather than scaling a nonexistent terminal schedule.

## 3. The input/output subsequences and exact comparison

Put m=r+1. Choose integers n_j->infinity with B_(n_j)/n_j^rho->K. From(9) and B_n=O(n^rho),

  D_(n_j)/n_j^rho->A K.

Indeed the difference A B_n-D_n is bounded above by2(sqrt(A)-1)sqrt(A B_n), hence is O(n^(rho/2)) and becomes zero after division by n^rho. On the output horizons mn_j, the definition of the same global limsup gives

  limsup_j B_(mn_j)/(mn_j)^rho<=K.

Both statements concern the same input subsequence and its multiplied output subsequence. Their inequality directions therefore yield

  limsup_j W_(mn_j)(H_(n_j))/U_(mn_j)
  <=limsup_j B_(mn_j)/D_(n_j)
  <=m^rho/A.

This proves(3). Under(1), choosing delta=(1-m^rho/A)/2>0 ensures W_(mn_j)(H_(n_j))<=(1-delta)U_(mn_j) for all sufficiently large j. The lengths mn_j are unbounded, as required.

## What this does and does not change

The stronger seed score A/m^rho>1 is now accompanied by a complete amplification and exact-profile comparison. A seed merely exceeding P_r, but failing this stronger score, is not settled by this argument. No such above-power primitive seed was found in the authorized600-call experiment. The numerical cap remains exhausted; this conditional result does not authorize restarting that search. The current weighted-gradient residual approach addresses a different, nonsaturated certificate class and still lacks a competitive infinite recursion.

evidence:
# Variable-step interval matrices and their first exact obstruction

Status: unverified analytic identities and a complete three-step test, not an improved schedule. This extends the matrix construction in Zhao, arXiv:2609.11784v1, Sections3.1–3.3, whose definitions and proof were read from a local downloaded/extracted copy. No external theorem is needed for the calculations below. The authorized numerical budget remains exhausted.

Work at L=1 with x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, i=0,...,n-1. Define the trajectory matrix T by T_ii=1, T_ij=h_j for j<i, and T_ij=0 for j>i. The symbol T is used to avoid confusion with the benchmark denominator B_n. Thus (Tg)_i=g_i+x_0-x_i.

For any matrix C with zero row sums, write b=C^T1 and H=CT+T^TC^T. Define the nonnegative interpolation quantity

  I_ij=2f_i-2f_j-2<g_j,x_i-x_j>-||g_i-g_j||^2.

It equals -2Q_ji in the project's sign convention. Direct expansion gives

  sum_(i,j) C_ji I_ij
  =2sum_i b_i f_i+sum_(i,j) H_ij<g_i,g_j>-sum_i b_i||g_i||^2.    (A)

Diagonal entries of C are immaterial to the sum because I_ii=0. If C has nonnegative off-diagonal entries, the left-hand side is nonnegative on every legal trajectory.

## 1. Interval diagonalization survives arbitrary steps

Fix0<=a<b<=n and positive numbers w_a,...,w_b. Put

  L_i=sum_(a<=j<i)w_j, R_i=sum_(i<j<=b)w_j,
  u_i=h_i(L_i+w_i)-w_i,
  v_i=w_i+h_i R_i.

At i=n choose any auxiliary h_n: all formulas in which it could affect the matrix cancel because R_n=0 and no entry lies above its diagonal. Define C^(a,b;w), zero outside the interval, by

  C_ij=u_i w_j for a<=i<j<=b,
  C_ij=v_i w_j for a<=j<i<=b,
  C_ii=-u_i R_i-v_i L_i.

Its row sums vanish. For i<j in the interval,

  (CT)_ij=u_i(w_j+h_j R_j)=u_i v_j,
  (CT)_ji=v_j(w_i-h_i(L_i+w_i))=-v_j u_i.

For a column before a, its entries vanish because the row sum is zero; for a column after b, its entries vanish by triangularity. Hence H=CT+T^TC^T is diagonal, with

  H_ii=2[(h_i-1)u_i R_i-v_i L_i].                    (B)

If h_i>=1 for a<=i<b, all off-diagonal entries of this interval matrix are nonnegative. For the special choice w_i=1, put s=i-a and t=b-i. Formula(B) becomes

  H_ii=2[(h_i-1)^2(s+1)t-s(t+1)].                   (C)

This is the constant-step paper's diagonal formula with the actual local step h_i inserted; no equality of the steps was needed for diagonalization.

## 2. The primitive coefficient target

Let S=sum_(i<n)h_i. The saturated primitive intrinsic potential is

  V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
      +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-S(S+1)||g_n||^2.

Thus(A) equals V_h exactly when

  b=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),-S),
  H=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_(n-1)(2-h_(n-1)),-S(S+2)).   (D)

Nonnegative off-diagonal entries of C then certify V_h>=0. This is a sufficient certificate class with zero PSD remainder, not a necessity claim for arbitrary primitive schedules.

There is an algebraic prerequisite for(D). Set p_0=1 and p_(i+1)=(1-h_i)p_i. Then Tp=1, so C1=0 implies p^THp=0. For the target(D), telescoping gives

  p^THp=1-(S+1)^2p_n^2.

Therefore a certificate of this exact diagonal form requires |p_n|=1/(S+1). A schedule with strict slack in the full-curvature quadratic test requires a nonzero PSD remainder or another quadratic coefficient pattern. This is a structural limit of the ansatz, not a failure of the schedule itself.

## 3. Positive interval coefficients exclude the basic three-step silver block

Let a=sqrt(2), lambda=1+a, and h=(a,2,a). Use the unweighted modes C^[i,j] from part1 with w=1, and write their coefficients as z_01,z_12,z_23,z_02,z_13,z_03.

Suppose all six z are nonnegative and the target(D) is matched. At index0 the diagonal equation gives

  z_01+2z_02+3z_03=lambda.

The column-sum equation b_0=a gives

  (2-a)z_01+(6-2a)z_02+(10-2a)z_03=a.

Since (2-a)lambda=a, subtracting the first equation times(2-a) yields

  2z_02+(4+a)z_03=0.

Nonnegativity forces z_02=z_03=0 and z_01=lambda. The diagonal equation at index1 becomes

  z_12+2z_13=lambda.

The cumulative column sum through cut1 is a+2. With z_02=z_03=0, only the [1,3] mode has a nonzero cut flow; that flow is a per unit coefficient. Therefore a z_13=a+2, so z_13=lambda and z_12=-lambda, a contradiction.

Consequently the direct positive-mode generalization of the constant-step proof is too narrow even for this basic silver schedule. This is a hostile test of the proposed proof class, not a counterexample to silver validity.

Signed interval coefficients repair the problem while every actual interpolation multiplier remains nonnegative. Choose

  C=lambda C^[0,1]-lambda C^[1,2]
      +lambda C^[1,3]+2lambda^2 C^[2,3].             (E)

Its only nonzero off-diagonal entries are

  C_01=1, C_10=lambda, C_13=lambda,
  C_21=2+a, C_23=5+3a,
  C_31=lambda, C_32=7+5a.

Every listed entry is positive. Setting each diagonal to minus its row sum gives b=(a,2,a,-2lambda). Formulas(C) give H=diag(2a-2,0,2a-2,-(2lambda)(2lambda+2)), so(D) is met. Hence(A) is an exact conic interpolation certificate for the three-step silver block. The apparent negative coefficient in(E) is only a coordinate in the interval basis; it is not a negative interpolation multiplier.

## 4. Explicit elimination of the lower-triangular unknowns

For arbitrary h_i>1, any zero-row-sum matrix C with diagonal CT+T^TC^T is uniquely determined by its strict upper triangle U_ij=C_ij, i<j. Write r_i=h_i-1. For a row j>i define L_(j,i)=sum_(k<=i)C_jk, with L_(j,-1)=0. The off-diagonal equation at(i,j) is exactly

  r_i L_(j,i)+L_(j,i-1)
    =U_ij+h_j sum_(k>j)U_ik.                        (F)

For j=n the sum is empty, so h_n is again immaterial. Starting at i=0, equation(F) gives the lower entries C_ji=L_(j,i)-L_(j,i-1) without matrix inversion. Conversely this recursion and the zero row sums make every off-diagonal entry of CT+T^TC^T vanish, so there are no omitted constraints.

All interpolation coefficients are nonnegative precisely when U_ij>=0 and every computed difference L_(j,i)-L_(j,i-1)>=0. The remaining column sums and diagonal conditions(D) are linear equations in U for a fixed step vector. Thus this specific zero-remainder certificate class has an exact system of scalar linear equalities and inequalities, with no PSD feasibility test left over. This does not assert that the class captures the full primitive PEP or that the step optimization is convex.

The next analytic task, if this interface is pursued, is a variable-step family and a symbolic solution of those inequalities, including aggregate positivity after signed interval cancellation. Producing the interface alone is not asymptotic progress. Any candidate must still beat the exact benchmark or meet the sufficient amplification threshold proved conditionally in research/max4_primitive_seed_amplification.md.

evidence:
# One-envelope arc relay with exact closest-minimizer normalization
Status: complete constructive candidate, UNVERIFIED. No additional verifier call.
Worker max. The source of the local circular-arc idea is Ye and Liu, "Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent", arXiv:2609.09152v2, Lemma3.1 and AppendixA.1. That PDF and its proof were downloaded and read. Matlas queries did not retrieve the exact paper. The necessary local statement is re-proved below; no unverified external theorem is used as a black box. The one-envelope coupling, activation buffer, exact scale and minimizer-distance calculation below are the proposed mutation.

## 1. Statement and exact computable bound
Partition a prescribed finite nonnegative schedule as
(block_0,b_0,...,block_(k-1),b_(k-1),block_k),
with ordinary sums s_i. Fix epsilon>0,gamma>0 and require
b_i>=1+epsilon^(-2), 0<=i<k.
Define c=sqrt(1+2gamma+epsilon^2), R=sqrt(epsilon^2+(1+gamma)^2).

For each ordinary block independently, the finite backward recursion in Section2 supplies horizontal and vertical displacements P_i^arc,Q_i^arc. They are exact deterministic functions of the ordered steps in that block. Define
A_i^arc=P_i^arc+epsilon+(1+Q_i^arc)/epsilon,
M_i^arc=P_i^arc+max{epsilon b_i,epsilon+(1+Q_i^arc)/epsilon},
rho_i^arc=1/M_i^arc.
Put
D_0=1, D_(i+1)=D_i rho_i^arc(b_i-1).
Here D_i is an activation length, not the Markov residual weight from earlier findings.

There is one finite max-affine nonnegative J on R^(k+1), and f=env_1 J, whose exact GD trajectory for the whole supplied schedule starts at e_0. Its closest minimizer x_star is explicitly identified, with
||e_0-x_star||^2
=(rho_0^arc)^2[(epsilon+P_0^arc)^2+(1+Q_0^arc)^2].
Its terminal value is
2 f(x_n)=D_k^2/(1+2s_k).
Consequently, for k>=1,
W_n(h)>=
 (b_0-1)^2 / {[(epsilon+P_0^arc)^2+(1+Q_0^arc)^2](1+2s_k)}
 times product_(i=1)^(k-1)[(b_i-1)/M_i^arc]^2.           (1)
For k=0 the construction is the ordinary one-sided Huber witness1/(1+2s_0).

There are explicit mass-only bounds. Set
T_arc=c(1+gamma)/(epsilon gamma),
H_arc=exp(T_arc)-1,
A_arc=epsilon+exp(T_arc)/epsilon.
Then P_i^arc<=c s_i, Q_i^arc<=H_arc, and
M_i^arc<=c s_i+max{epsilon b_i,A_arc}.
Thus (1) implies the uniform, still restricted-checkpoint bound
W_n(h)>=
 (b_0-1)^2 / {[(epsilon+c s_0)^2+exp(2T_arc)](1+2s_k)}
 times product_(i=1)^(k-1)[(b_i-1)/(c s_i+max{epsilon b_i,A_arc})]^2.  (2)
There is no factor1/2 multiplying the component gradients: all nonsmooth pieces are assembled first and one Moreau envelope gives global smoothness. The exact cost is the activation buffer, which changes each transfer numerator to b_i-1.

## 2. Local arc trajectory, proved from explicit normals
Let V(q)=(p(q),-q), where
p(q)=sqrt(R^2-(q+gamma)^2), 0<=q<=1.
Then V(0)=(c,0), V(1)=(epsilon,-1),
epsilon<=p(q)<=c, and 0<=q/p(q)<=1/epsilon.
Let K be the convex hull of0 and this compact arc. It lies in the disk centered at(0,gamma) with radius R, and in the half-plane with second coordinate<=0.

For a block with m ordinary steps alpha_1,...,alpha_m, set
r_m=(u_m,-y_m)=(epsilon,-1), v_m=V(1).
Work backward. Given r_j, set Delta_j=y_j+gamma-alpha_j gamma.
If Delta_j<=u_j gamma/c, set v_(j-1)=(c,0).
Otherwise set
E_j=sqrt(u_j^2+Delta_j^2),
p_(j-1)=R u_j/E_j,
q_(j-1)=R Delta_j/E_j-gamma,
v_(j-1)=(p_(j-1),-q_(j-1)).
Finally set r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha_j v_(j-1).
This is a finite textual recursion, not a numerical optimization or feasibility assumption.

We prove inductively u_j>=epsilon, y_j>=1, y_j/u_j<=1/epsilon, v_j in the arc, and v_j the Euclidean projection of r_j onto K. At j=m these statements hold. In the turning branch,
gamma/c<Delta_j/u_j<=(1+gamma)/epsilon.
The increasing function t -> Rt/sqrt(1+t^2)-gamma takes values0 and1 at the two displayed endpoints. Hence0<q_(j-1)<=1 and the formula indeed gives V(q_(j-1)). In the other branch it gives V(0). Adding alpha_j times a vector with p>=epsilon,q>=0 preserves u>=epsilon,y>=1; the new ratio y/u is a convex combination of the preceding y/u and q/p, so remains<=1/epsilon.

In the turning branch, direct substitution gives
r_(j-1)-v_(j-1)
=[E_j/R+alpha_j-1][v_(j-1)-(0,gamma)].
The coefficient is nonnegative: the reverse triangle inequality gives
E_j>=sqrt(u_j^2+(y_j+gamma)^2)-alpha_j gamma>=R-alpha_j gamma,
so the coefficient is>=alpha_j(1-gamma/R)>=0.
The vector in brackets is an outward disk normal and therefore a normal to K at v_(j-1). In the capped branch put mu=u_j/c+alpha_j-1. Its branch inequality gives y_j<=gamma mu, so mu>0, and
r_(j-1)-(c,0)=mu(c,-gamma)+(0,gamma mu-y_j).
Both summands are nonnegative multiples of normals to K at(c,0). Thus, in both branches,
<r_(j-1)-v_(j-1),w-v_(j-1)><=0 for every w in K.
Expanding squared distances proves the claimed projection property directly. These formulas additionally prove u_j>=p_j at every index.

Set
P^arc=sum_j alpha_j p_(j-1), Q^arc=sum_j alpha_j q_(j-1).
Then r_0=(epsilon+P^arc,-1-Q^arc), and P^arc<=c sum_j alpha_j.
Once the capped branch occurs, it persists toward the beginning: after a capped update y stays fixed, u increases by alpha_j c, and y+gamma<=gamma u_new/c; subtracting any subsequent nonnegative alpha gamma preserves the cap criterion. Thus every positive q contribution belongs to one contiguous turning portion.

Here is a self-contained, crude bound for that portion. Write sigma_j=(y_j+gamma)/u_j. At a turning update,
sigma_(j-1)=sigma_j-alpha_j gamma/u_j,
log(u_(j-1)/u_j)
=log(1+alpha_j p_(j-1)/u_j)
<= (c/gamma)(sigma_j-sigma_(j-1)).
Summing over the turning portion gives its total multiplicative increase of u at most exp(T_arc), because the terminal sigma is(1+gamma)/epsilon and the final sigma is nonnegative. Since each turning increase of u is at least epsilon alpha_j, the sum of its alpha_j is at most exp(T_arc)-1. The cap contributes q=0, so
Q^arc<=exp(T_arc)-1.
This proves all bounds stated in Section1 without the paper's more delicate turning estimate.

## 3. One local max-affine piece and its proximal margins
For one block suppress the index i and use its exact P^arc,Q^arc,b,M^arc,rho^arc. Put
z_circ=(1,0)-rho^arc r_0,
U=1-rho^arc(P^arc+epsilon b)>=0,
Y=rho^arc Q^arc.
Let V_fin consist of0,(c,0),v_0,...,v_m and define
phi(z)=rho^arc max_(v in V_fin)<v,z-z_circ>.
All data are fixed once the block and checkpoint are given.
The projection inequality from Section2 remains true after restricting K to conv(V_fin), since each projected vector v_j remains in that smaller set. Therefore v_j maximizes <v,r_j-v_j> over V_fin. At
x_j=z_circ+rho^arc r_j,
the point x_j-rho^arc v_j is a proximal point of phi, and grad env_1 phi(x_j)=rho^arc v_j. This follows from the subgradient optimality equation, not from an independent interpolation assertion.

The local GD path starts at(1,0), has first coordinate nonincreasing and second coordinate nondecreasing through the ordinary block, reaches
(U+rho^arc epsilon b,Y),
and the checkpoint reaches
(U,Y+rho^arc b).
The following exact zero regions and proximal margins are needed for global gluing:
(a) phi(x,y)=0 whenever x<=0,y>=0;
(b) phi(U,y)=0 whenever y>=Y;
(c) every ordinary or checkpoint-query proximal point x_j-rho^arc v_j has first coordinate>=U>=0 and second coordinate in[0,Y+rho^arc].

To prove(a), each nonzero v=(p,-q) has p>=0,q>=0,q<=p/epsilon. At(0,0),
<v,-z_circ>=-p+rho^arc[p(epsilon+P^arc)+q(1+Q^arc)]
<=-p+rho^arc p A^arc<=0.
Monotonicity in the two coordinates then proves the whole region.
At(U,Y), each affine argument is
rho^arc[(1-b)epsilon p+q]<=0
because b>=1+epsilon^(-2); increasing y preserves this, proving(b).
For(c), the proximal first coordinate minus U equals
rho^arc[epsilon(b-1)+u_j-p_j]>=0.
Its second coordinate is rho^arc(1+Q^arc-y_j+q_j), which lies between0 and rho^arc(1+Q^arc): y_j<=1+Q^arc, q_j>=0 give the lower bound, while y_j>=1>=q_j gives the upper bound.
All these checks concern the nonsmooth piece phi, as needed for the one-envelope construction.

## 4. Global maximum and the activation buffer
Set ell_0=0 and recursively
ell_(i+1)=D_i rho_i^arc(1+Q_i^arc)=D_i(Y_i+rho_i^arc).
On coordinates0,...,k define
Phi_i(z)=D_i^2 phi_i((z_i-ell_i)/D_i,z_(i+1)/D_i), i<k.
Let delta=D_k/(1+2s_k), and define the terminal affine hinge
Phi_k(z)=delta max{z_k-ell_k,0}.
Now take the ONE nonsmooth function
J(z)=max{Phi_0(z),...,Phi_k(z)}
and its ONE envelope
f(x)=min_z{J(z)+||x-z||^2/2}.
Each Phi_i is nonnegative finite max-affine; all its nonzero affine pieces have nonpositive value at0 by Section3(a), since ell_i>=0. Hence J>=0,J(0)=0. Its envelope is globally finite, convex, differentiable and1-smooth. To verify the last assertions directly, the unique proximal minimizer z(x) exists by the quadratic's coercivity and strict convexity. The subgradient equation x-z(x) in partial J(z(x)), the two minimizing inequalities, and subgradient monotonicity yield grad f(x)=x-z(x) and
||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2<=<grad f(x)-grad f(y),x-y>.
Thus every stated sample, including the minimum, belongs to one globally legal function.

Inductively, at the beginning of block i, coordinates j<i are frozen at ell_j+D_j U_j, coordinate i equals ell_i+D_i, and all coordinates j>i are0. During the current block use the local path of Section3 in coordinates i,i+1. At its candidate GLOBAL proximal point:
- the current piece Phi_i has the prescribed local subgradient;
- piece i-1, if present, has its first argument frozen at U_(i-1), and its second argument at least ell_i/D_(i-1)>=Y_(i-1), because the current proximal first coordinate is>=ell_i; Section3(b) makes it0;
- all earlier pieces stay in their post-checkpoint zero regions;
- piece i+1, if present, has first coordinate at most ell_(i+1) by Section3(c), and its second coordinate0; Section3(a) makes it0;
- every later piece is also0 by Section3(a), or by the terminal hinge's threshold.
Thus the current piece dominates all other pieces at the candidate proximal point, even when its value is0. Its subgradient is consequently a subgradient of J. This proves every actual gradient and GD update, with no old or future affine plane discarded.

After checkpoint i, the new coordinate equals
D_i(Y_i+rho_i^arc b_i)=ell_(i+1)+D_i rho_i^arc(b_i-1)
=ell_(i+1)+D_(i+1),
and coordinate i is frozen at ell_i+D_i U_i, proving the induction.
The buffer D_i rho_i^arc is exactly what prevents future activation at the previous proximal query.

In the terminal block the only moving coordinate has initial height D_k above ell_k. The constant gradient delta is legal at every query and at the terminal point, because for every cumulative partial sum0<=u<=s_k,
D_k-(u+1)delta>=0.
All earlier pieces remain0 by the same post-checkpoint check. Therefore
f(x_n)=delta D_k-(s_k+1/2)delta^2=D_k^2/[2(1+2s_k)].

## 5. The actual nearest minimizer
The minimizer set of f equals {J=0}: both terms in its defining minimum are nonnegative, and the minimum is attained.
Define x_star by its first two coordinates
(x_star)_0=1-rho_0^arc(epsilon+P_0^arc),
(x_star)_1=rho_0^arc(1+Q_0^arc)=ell_1,
and all later coordinates0.
This is the first component's translated center z_circ. Hence Phi_0(x_star)=0. The next component has first input0 and second input0, so is0 by Section3(a); all later components are0 as well. For k=1 the terminal coordinate is exactly its threshold ell_1. Thus x_star is a GLOBAL minimizer, regardless of later block choices.

It is the closest one. Every affine piece of Phi_0 is active with value0 there. Moreover
e_0-x_star=rho_0^arc(epsilon+P_0^arc,-1-Q_0^arc,0,...,0)
is the following nonnegative combination of two active normal vectors:
[(P_0^arc-epsilon Q_0^arc)/c] rho_0^arc(c,0,0,...)
 +(1+Q_0^arc) rho_0^arc(epsilon,-1,0,...).
The first coefficient is nonnegative since every p_j>=epsilon q_j. For any minimizer z, its inner product with z-x_star is therefore nonpositive. Squared-distance expansion proves
||e_0-z||^2>=||e_0-x_star||^2.
This establishes the EXACT initial distance in Section1. Dividing the terminal value by it cancels the first local scale, and gives(1). It does not assume the origin is closest.

## 6. An explicit unbounded-horizon test with all quadratic errors vanishing
Take epsilon=gamma=1/10. Then c=11/10,T_arc=121,
A_arc=1/10+10 exp(121).
Choose any fixed integer N>=max{10,A_arc}. For each m>=1 consider m repetitions of a block of N unit steps followed by checkpoint3N, with no terminal ordinary steps.
The checkpoint condition3N>=101 holds. For every block,
P_i^arc<=11N/10, A_i^arc<=11N/10+A_arc<=21N/10,
M_i^arc<=11N/10+max{3N/10,A_arc}<=21N/10.
The initial distance factor also obeys
sqrt((epsilon+P_0^arc)^2+(1+Q_0^arc)^2)
<=A_0^arc<=21N/10:
the first inequality follows from 1+Q>=0 and epsilon<=1, since the sum P+epsilon+(1+Q)/epsilon dominates the Euclidean norm.
Thus every normalized transfer factor is at least
(3N-1)/(21N/10)>=29/21.
The explicit high-dimensional nonlinear construction gives
W_(m(N+1))(h)>=(29/21)^(2m).                            (3)

For the same schedules, a scalar quadratic eigenvalue lambda in[0,1] has block multiplier
q_N(lambda)=(1-lambda)^N(1-3N lambda).
If0<=lambda<=1/(3N), its magnitude is at most exp(-N lambda).
If lambda>=1/(3N), it is at most
(3N lambda-1)exp(-N lambda)<=3exp(-4/3)<4/5.
The last strict inequality follows already by summing the degree5 Taylor lower bound for exp(4/3), which exceeds15/4. Therefore every finite-dimensional convex quadratic has normalized terminal objective at most
max{1/(2 e m N),(4/5)^(2m)} ->0.
The dimension of the nonlinear witness is m+1 and its sampled checkpoint gradients contain m independent directions proportional to epsilon e_i-e_(i+1), followed by the terminal e_m direction.

The function is nonseparable in every fixed orthonormal coordinate system. Each coupled endpoint normal epsilon e_i-e_(i+1) can be exposed alone against the zero plane: choose a recession direction with all coordinates negative, with t_(j+1)<epsilon t_j for j!=i and t_(i+1)=epsilon t_i for j=i, where the coordinates are -t_j. Every other local arc normal then has negative inner product with that direction, while the selected endpoint has zero inner product. Starting on the selected affine hyperplane and moving sufficiently far along this direction makes every other nonzero plane strictly negative. The terminal normal e_m is exposed similarly with final coordinate0 and sufficiently negative preceding coordinates. Near each resulting hinge, the envelope has the rank-one Hessian projector onto that normal. Adjacent coupled normals, or the last coupled normal and e_m, are nonorthogonal and nonparallel, so the corresponding projectors do not commute. A function separable in one orthonormal basis would have commuting Hessians. This proves the assertion.

## 7. What remains open
This mutation permits arbitrary nonnegative ordinary steps and varying within-block gradient directions, retains all planes, gives exact nonzero offsets, supplies a finite real PSD Gram realization, and computes the true closest-minimizer distance. It has a concrete exponential-error family whose quadratic channel converges.

It does NOT prove the exact profile. The constants c>1,A_arc and the checkpoint threshold remain; the norm/cost bounds do not yet imply an arbitrary-schedule comparison to(1-o(1))U_n^ZJ. Taking epsilon,gamma small makes c approach1 but makes A_arc very large. No claim is made that optimizing the partition and parameters eliminates that loss. Formula(1), not a postulated covariance-feasibility assertion, is the new exact candidate interface.

author: max
claim: Positive checkpoint values repair a genuine signed-history failure: a parameterized alternating-energy Markov relay keeps every plane legal even when old residuals are positive. Rational repeated(1,463/135,1,131/30) has explicit W>=85/121, while all quadratic errors tend to0.
evidence:
# Positive-value periodic Markov relay with signed history
Status: complete explicit construction, UNVERIFIED. No new verifier call.
This tests the specific repair suggested after the minimum-reset and residual-sign obstructions: allow positive proximal function values, and check actual past-plane deficits even when the signed residual is positive.

## 1. A parameterized model
Fix a in(0,1), chi>=1, T>=2, and kappa in[0,T-2]. Assume
T>=2a chi,                                               (1)
(T-2-kappa)-(T-kappa)chi^2+T chi/a>=0.                     (2)
For any number m>=1 of blocks, in R^(m+1) set
zeta_0=e_0,
zeta_(i+1)=-a zeta_i+sqrt(1-a^2)e_(i+1).
Define alpha_i=chi for even i and alpha_i=1 for odd i, omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i. Thus
<zeta_i,zeta_j>=(-a)^|i-j|
and all omega_i are independent.

Each real block consists of one unit step followed by
b_i=T-1+(T/a)alpha_(i+1)/alpha_i.
Take the ONE finite max-affine function
J(z)=max{0,max_(0<=i<=m)(<omega_i,z>-kappa alpha_i^2)}
and f=env_1 J. Start at X_0=T alpha_0 zeta_0.
We prove that block i queries X_i and X_i-omega_i with gradient omega_i at both, and that
X_(i+1)=X_i-(1+b_i)omega_i.
The terminal point is X_m with gradient omega_m.

The function f is legal globally: J is finite nonnegative convex with J(0)=0, and its envelope is finite convex differentiable1-smooth. For precision, the proximal minimization has a unique minimizer by the quadratic term; its subgradient equation implies grad f(x)=x-prox_J(x), and monotonicity gives
||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2<=<grad f(x)-grad f(y),x-y>.
At any point where plane i is active at x-omega_i, that subgradient equation yields the claimed gradient and value
f(x)=<omega_i,x>-alpha_i^2/2-kappa alpha_i^2.
Thus it remains to compare every affine plane at the indicated proximal points.

## 2. Exact signed residuals
Let Z_i=X_i-T omega_i and put
B_i=(T/a)alpha_(i+1), D_i=B_i(1-a^2).
The update gives
Z_0=0,
Z_(i+1)=Z_i-B_i(zeta_i+a zeta_(i+1)).
Direct multiplication of Markov correlations proves
<Z_i,zeta_j>=0 for j>=i,
<Z_i,zeta_j>=-S_(j,i) for j<i,
where
S_(j,i)=sum_(l=j)^(i-1)D_l(-a)^(l-j).                     (3)
Indeed zeta_l+a zeta_(l+1) is orthogonal to all zeta_j with j>=l+1, and its inner product with earlier zeta_j is(1-a^2)(-a)^(l-j). This proves(3) by summing the update; no sign of S is assumed.

At a real query x=X_i-u omega_i with u=0 or1, its proposed proximal point is
Z_i+d omega_i, d=T-u-1>=T-2.
The terminal query has d=T-1 and obeys the same lower bound.
The current affine plane has value(d-kappa)alpha_i^2>=0.
The current-minus-j-th plane difference is
d alpha_i(alpha_i-C_ij alpha_j)
 +alpha_j S_(j,i)-kappa alpha_i^2+kappa alpha_j^2          (4)
for j<i, with C_ij=(-a)^(i-j); for j>i the same formula has S=0.
Every coefficient of d is positive: at even separation the amplitudes agree and C<1, while at odd separation C<0. Hence it suffices to check d=T-2.

Future planes are already controlled. At even separation their offsets agree and their deficit is d alpha_i^2(1-C)>=0. At odd separation the deficit is
(d-kappa)alpha_i^2+kappa alpha_j^2+d a^|i-j| alpha_i alpha_j>=0.
The substantive point is the full past history.

## 3. All past planes, including positive residuals
For even separation i-j=2q, q>=1, let z=alpha_j=alpha_i and y be the opposite amplitude. Formula(3) is the exact geometric sum
S_(j,i)=(T/a)(y-a z)(1-a^(2q)).
Substituting into(4) gives, at d=T-2,
(1-a^(2q)) z[-2z+(T/a)y]>=0
by(1), since z/y is either chi or1/chi.

For odd separation i-j=2q+1, q>=0, let z=alpha_j and y=alpha_i be the opposite amplitude. Now
S_(j,i)=(T/a)[y-a z+a^(2q)(a z-a^2 y)].
Substitution into(4), still at d=T-2, gives
F_infty(y,z)+a^(2q)[T z^2-2a yz],                       (5)
where
F_infty(y,z)=(T-2-kappa)y^2-(T-kappa)z^2+(T/a)yz.
The second term in(5) is nonnegative by(1).
Among the two choices(y,z)=(1,chi),(chi,1), the first has smaller F_infty: the difference is
2(T-1-kappa)(chi^2-1)>=0.
Its nonnegativity is precisely(2). This proves every old-plane comparison, at every lag, with the signed residual retained. Together with the future and zero-plane checks it proves the entire trajectory in Section1.

The exact sampled values are
f(X_i-u omega_i)=(T-u-1/2-kappa)alpha_i^2.
At a checkpoint query u=1, the nonsmooth proximal value is
J(X_i-2omega_i)=(T-2-kappa)alpha_i^2.                    (6)
It is strictly positive whenever kappa<T-2. Thus these checkpoints are not minimum resets.

## 4. Closest minimizer and payoff
The minimizer set of f is exactly
P_min={z:<omega_i,z><=kappa alpha_i^2 for every i}.
The point y_proj=kappa alpha_0 zeta_0 lies in P_min: for even i the amplitude equals alpha_0 and the correlation is at most1; for odd i the correlation is negative. Constraint0 is active, and
X_0-y_proj=(T-kappa)omega_0
is a positive multiple of its normal. For any z in P_min this gives
<X_0-y_proj,z-y_proj><=0,
so squared-distance expansion proves that y_proj is the unique closest minimizer and
dist(X_0,P_min)^2=(T-kappa)^2 alpha_0^2.
The normalized terminal value of this one instance is therefore exactly
2(T-kappa-1/2)alpha_m^2 / [(T-kappa)^2 alpha_0^2].        (7)
For even m, alpha_m=alpha_0 and this is
[2(T-kappa)-1]/(T-kappa)^2.
All smooth-convex interpolation inequalities, including the optimum sample, hold because all samples have been checked on this one explicit envelope.

## 5. Rational parameters, quadratic stability, and a strict failure of the old test
Choose
a=9/10, chi=6/5, T=23/10, kappa=1/10.
Condition(1) has positive margin
T-2a chi=7/50.
The left side of(2) is exactly37/375>0.
The alternating checkpoint sizes are
b_even=463/135, b_odd=131/30,
both in[3,5]. Therefore for m=2r and every integer r>=1 the length4r schedule
(1,463/135,1,131/30) repeated r times
has the explicitly realized normalized error
W_(4r)(h)>=85/121.                                     (8)
At every checkpoint its proximal value is alpha_i^2/5>0.

This model violates the earlier nonpositive-residual criterion. For any even j with j+2<=m,
S_(j,j+2)=(T/a)(1-a^2)(1-a chi)<0
because a chi=27/25>1. Thus
<Z_(j+2),zeta_j> >0,
and D_j>=a D_(j+1) is false at every such pair. Nevertheless the exact plane comparisons above hold. This is an explicit repair, not an assumption that local correlation checks suffice.

For comparison, each quadratic block multiplier is(1-lambda)(1-b_i lambda).
For0<=lambda<=1/5 it is nonnegative and at most exp(-lambda).
For1/5<=lambda<=1, its positive value is at most8/25, since b_i>=3; the magnitude of its negative minimum is at most4/5, since b_i<=5 and max_(b<=5,b>=3)(b-1)^2/(4b)=4/5.
Hence the full finite-dimensional quadratic normalized objective after m blocks is at most
max{1/(2 e m),(4/5)^(2m)} ->0.
The nonlinear persistent value is not a large quadratic product.

The omega_i are independent, adjacent ones have negative inner product, and their nonnegative-offset max-affine system has isolated zero/plane hinges. At such hinges the envelope has rank-one Hessian projectors onto omega_i. Adjacent projectors do not commute, proving that this function is nonseparable in every fixed orthonormal basis. Independence permits exposing each hinge by solving for one affine value0 and all others strictly negative. The dimension m+1 grows with the horizon and the gradient energies alternate between36/25 and1.

## 6. Scope
This is a parameterized, fully signed-history construction with positive checkpoint values and a concrete rational periodic test outside the earlier residual-sign interface. It does not claim that(1)--(2), or a generalization of them, can realize an arbitrary schedule at the benchmark profile. The endpoint values of the exact all-past comparison now show where positive residuals can be paid for by real face margins and offsets. A future extension must solve those inequalities quantitatively for nonperiodic data, rather than imposing S>=0 again or assuming feasibility at target strength.

author: max2
claim: Actual fixed-length joint descent for triangular full certificates: transporting one star-outgoing multiplier column and rescaling the suffix preserves every mixed PSD entry and adds a diagonal gradient energy. The required cut-profile condition is automatic for two remaining steps.
evidence:
# Joint suffix deformation with exact PSD preservation

Status: complete conditional derivation, UNVERIFIED. It is a new J1 candidate,
not a claim that all global minimizers have the hypotheses. No further
verification allocation has been made.

## Full certificate and the additional triangular hypothesis

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be
nonnegative and finite. For distinct indices in I={star,0,...,n}, set

Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Assume a complete upper certificate (q,lambda,h): q>0, lambda_ij>=0,
out_i-in_i=2 1_(i=n) at finite indices, and the quadratic form

M=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij

after x_j=x_0-sum_(t<j)h_t g_t is positive semidefinite. It is a
quadratic form in the independent formal vectors (x_0,g_0,...,g_n);
flow cancels every function-value coefficient. Thus 2f_n<=q||x_0||^2
on every legal trajectory.

For this candidate ONLY, additionally assume

lambda_ij=0 whenever 0<=i<j<=n.                         (T)

All finite-index multiplier flow goes backward. Star edges may go either
way. Write mu_j=lambda_(j,star), nu_j=lambda_(star,j), and, for t<j,

c_(t,j)=mu_j+sum_(l=0)^t lambda_(j,l).

Every c is nonnegative. The complete matrix entries are

M_(x_0,x_0)=q,   M_(x_0,g_j)=-mu_j/2,
M_(g_j,g_j)=out_j-1_(j=n),
2 M_(g_t,g_j)=h_t c_(t,j)-lambda_(j,t),   t<j.          (1)

To check (1), the squared-gradient terms contribute
(out_j+in_j)/2=out_j-1_(j=n) on the diagonal. A backward
edge j->t contributes -lambda_(j,t)<g_j,g_t> from the squared
difference, and h_t times the total flow from j to star or an index at
most t contributes h_t c_(t,j)<g_j,g_t>. The star pair contributes
-mu_j<x_0,g_j>. This accounts for every term; no principal submatrix
replaces M.

## Deformation

Fix k<n with nu_k>0. Define C=sum_(j>k)c_(k,j). By summing flow over
{k+1,...,n}, hypothesis (T) gives C=2+sum_(j>k)nu_j>0.
Put p_j=c_(k,j)/C for j>k, so p_j>=0 and sum p_j=1.

Assume the following explicit proportionality condition on later cuts:

for every k<t<n there is r_t>=0 such that
p_j=r_t c_(t,j) for all j>t.                           (P)

Zero p entries are allowed. If all p_j vanish beyond t, one may take
r_t=0. Set r_k=1/C.

Choose any 0<eta<=nu_k. Change only these multipliers:

nu'_k=nu_k-eta,
nu'_j=nu_j+eta p_j             (j>k),
lambda'_(j,k)=lambda_(j,k)+eta p_j   (j>k).             (2)

Keep every mu_j and every other finite edge unchanged. Change the schedule by

h'_t=h_t                                      (t<k),
h'_k=(h_k+eta r_k)/(1+eta r_k),
h'_t=h_t/(1+eta r_t)                           (k<t<n). (3)

All new steps and multipliers are nonnegative. At k the increased
incoming backward flow eta cancels the removed incoming star flow eta;
at j>k the new outgoing edge eta p_j cancels the new incoming star
edge eta p_j. Thus every flow equation stays exact.

The NEW full matrix, on the same formal vector coordinates, satisfies

M(q,lambda',h') =
M(q,lambda,h)+eta sum_(j>k)p_j ||g_j||^2.               (4)

Proof: diagonal j>k increases by eta p_j, while all x_0 entries and
all other diagonals stay fixed. For t<k, c_(t,j), h_t and lambda_(j,t)
are unchanged. At t=k,

h'_k(c_(k,j)+eta p_j)-(lambda_(j,k)+eta p_j)
=h_k c_(k,j)-lambda_(j,k),

using p_j=r_k c_(k,j). At t>k the edge lambda_(j,t) is unchanged and

h'_t(c_(t,j)+eta p_j)=h_t c_(t,j),

using (P). Therefore EVERY mixed entry is unchanged, proving (4).
In particular the whole new matrix remains PSD, including every old
kernel direction. No forward edge is created and no preexisting edge
is decreased except the explicitly available star multiplier nu_k.

## Strict worst-case improvement

Identity (4) gives, on every trajectory of the NEW schedule,

q R^2-2f_n >= eta sum_(j>k)p_j ||g_j||^2,               (5)

where R=||x_0||>0. Here the old M on the right of (4) is PSD on arbitrary
formal vectors; the new transcript need not be a trajectory of the old
schedule.

Set B=product_(t=0)^(n-1)(1+h'_t) and
D_j=product_(t=j)^(n-1)(1+h'_t), with D_n=1.
These finite positive quantities are deliberately crude.

Since g_star=0 and the gradient is 1-Lipschitz, ||g_t||<=||x_t||, hence
||x_n||<=B R. Convexity gives f_n<=<g_n,x_n><=B R||g_n||.
The same Lipschitz property gives
||g_(t+1)||<=||g_t||+||x_(t+1)-x_t||=(1+h'_t)||g_t||,
so ||g_n||<=D_j||g_j||.

Writing E=2f_n/R^2, these inequalities and (5) yield

q-E >= gamma E^2,
gamma=eta/(4B^2) sum_(j>k) p_j/D_j^2 >0.              (6)

Consequently the actual fixed-length new schedule obeys

W_n(h') <= 2q/[1+sqrt(1+4 gamma q)] < q.               (7)

This is a uniform bound over every dimension and every legal function,
not a calculation on the old active instance. Neither stationarity nor
q=1/(2sum h+1) was used. In particular, if the old certificate is tight
at a globally minimizing schedule, hypotheses (T),(P),nu_k>0 cannot
hold simultaneously.

## Two remaining steps: condition (P) is automatic

Take k=n-2. Define

c_1=mu_(n-1)+sum_(l<=n-2)lambda_(n-1,l),
c_2=mu_n+sum_(l<=n-2)lambda_(n,l),
c_3=mu_n+sum_(l<=n-1)lambda_(n,l)=2+nu_n>0.

Then C=c_1+c_2, p_(n-1)=c_1/C, p_n=c_2/C, and
r_(n-1)=p_n/c_3 satisfies (P), including c_2=0. Formula (3) changes
BOTH of the final two steps:

h'_(n-2)=(C h_(n-2)+eta)/(C+eta),
h'_(n-1)=h_(n-1)c_3/(c_3+eta p_n).

The complete slack gains exactly
eta p_(n-1)||g_(n-1)||^2+eta p_n||g_n||^2.
Thus for a triangular tight certificate at a global minimizer,
nu_(n-2) must vanish. At horizon n=2 this excludes nu_0>0 under (T).
This is a genuine earlier-step joint deformation, not the already
recorded final-step convex blend.

## Precise limitation

For k<t<n, if positive ratios p_j/c_(t,j) differ as j varies, no single
h'_t can satisfy h'_t(c_(t,j)+eta p_j)=h_t c_(t,j) for all j>t when
h_t>0. Thus this one-column transport cannot simply be declared to
work on arbitrary longer suffixes. Additional multiplier changes,
a non-diagonal PSD residual, or a different mechanism would be needed.

Nor is (T) established for arbitrary optimal certificates. Forward
edges produce additional mixed terms when suffix steps change.
The candidate does NOT establish global Huber tightness or the
Zhang--Jiang exact-profile lower bound.

## Hostile checks within the derivation

- No division by h_t, h_t-1, p_j, or nu_j for j>k is used.
  Zero steps, zero weights, and steps on either side of1 are covered.
- If h_k=1, that coordinate stays fixed; positive later r_t can still
  change the suffix. If every affected coordinate were unchanged,
  (5)--(7) would show that q was not a tight certificate.
- Even p_n=0 leaves gamma>0, since some earlier p_j is positive and
  D_j is finite.
- The old matching primal is never reused as if it satisfied new GD
  recursions. Uniform legality enters only in (5)--(7).

claim: Whole-tail residual transport now has an exact nonlocal certificate and a quantitative failed calibration. Summing all tail-to-bridge interpolation inequalities yields a 3x3 objective-residual update; a rational/radical three-step test passes.
