evidence:
# Whole-tail residual transport: exact rule and balanced-doubling failure

Status: self-contained unverified certificate algebra, a finite valid test, and a quantitative limitation of one explicitly specified recursion. The conclusion concerns the bound produced by this certificate rule, not the true worst case of the resulting schedules. No new numerical evaluation or verifier call.

Work at L=1. For any block h with nonnegative proof weights u on its iterates define D=sum u_i, d=x_start-x_end, U=sum u_i g_i, e=U-d, and

  E_h(u)=2sum_i u_i(f_i-f_end)+sum_i u_i||g_i||^2
         +2sum_i u_i<g_i,x_start-x_i>-||U||^2.

For every minimizer x_star, expansion gives

  ||x_start-x_star||^2+2sum_i u_i Q_(i,star)-2D(f_end-f_star)
     =||x_end-x_star-e||^2+E_h(u),

where Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0. Therefore E_h(u)>=0 implies W(h)<=1/D.

## 1. An aggregate interpolation identity across the full tail

Let a prefix finish at y, with g=grad f(y), function value f_y, and certificate state(D,e,E_a). Take a bridge step tau>=0 to y'=y-tau g. Run a tail block from y' to z. Write its nonnegative proof weights as v, its mass as D_b, its gradient aggregate as U_b, and its intrinsic energy as E_b. Summing all Q_(i,y) over the tail, with weights v_i, gives exactly

  2D_b(f_y-f_z)
   =E_b+||U_b||^2+2(tau-1)<U_b,g>+D_b||g||^2
       +2sum_i v_i(-Q_(i,y)).                        (1)

To check this, substitute y-x_i=tau g+(y'-x_i) into the Q expression. The tail terms 2sum v_i(f_i-f_z)+sum v_i||g_i||^2+2sum v_i<g_i,y'-x_i> combine to E_b+||U_b||^2; the remaining cross terms are2(tau-1)<U_b,g> and D_b||g||^2. All interpolation terms on the right of(1) are nonnegative.

Unlike the adjacent-only update, this identity uses every tail iterate and retains the actual aggregate U_b.

## 2. Exact matrix transport with a primitive tail

Assume the prefix has the residual certificate

  E_a>=nu||e-K g||^2, nu>0.                         (2)

Let b be primitive with shifted physical capacity A=1+sum(b). Use its standard proof weights v=(b_0,...,b_(ell-1),A). Then

  D_b=2A-1,
  U_b=(y'-z)+Aq, q=grad f(z),
  E_b=V_b>=0,

where V_b=2sum b_i(f_i-f_z)+sum b_i(1-b_i)||g_i||^2-(A-1)A||q||^2 is precisely its primitive potential.

Increase the old terminal proof weight by eta and scale all tail weights by beta. Require old_terminal_weight+eta>=0 and beta>=0. The new weights have mass

  D'=D+eta+beta D_b,

and their residual satisfies

  e'-Aq=e+(eta-tau)g+(beta-1)U_b.                   (3)

Direct expansion of E for the joined block gives

  E'=E_a+beta E_b+2(D+eta)(f_y-f_z)
      +eta(1-eta)||g||^2-2eta<e,g>
      +beta(1-beta)||U_b||^2
      +2beta<U_b,(tau-eta)g-e>.                     (4)

Choose c=(D+eta)/D_b>=0 and nu'>=0. Substituting(1) into(4), and subtracting nu' times the squared residual in(3), gives the exact identity

  E'-nu'||e'-Aq||^2
  =E_a-nu||e-Kg||^2+(beta+c)E_b
     +2c sum_i v_i(-Q_(i,y))+(e,g,U_b)^T M(e,g,U_b),

where the symmetric3-by3 matrix is

  M_ee=nu-nu',
  M_eg=-nu K-eta-nu'(eta-tau),
  M_eU=-beta-nu'(beta-1),
  M_gg=nu K^2+D+2eta-eta^2-nu'(eta-tau)^2,
  M_gU=c(tau-1)+beta(tau-eta)-nu'(eta-tau)(beta-1),
  M_UU=c+beta(1-beta)-nu'(beta-1)^2.

Thus M>=0 suffices for another residual certificate, with new K'=A and mass D'. In particular it gives an actual objective bound1/D'. This algebra does not assume that D=2sum(a)+1.

## 3. A closed scalar subrule and an exact finite test

Keep nu'=nu fixed and set

  k=1+1/nu, beta=1/k, eta=(tau-K)/k.

The e row and column of M then vanish. The remaining matrix is

  [ D+((K-1)^2-(tau-1)^2)/k    c(tau-1) ]
  [ c(tau-1)                  c         ].

Put X=kD, r=tau-1, and X'=kD'=X+r+1-K+D_b. Subject to c>=0, this matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when

  r^2 X'<=D_b[X+(K-1)^2].                           (5)

For c>0 this is its Schur-complement condition after multiplication by kD_b. When c=0, X'=D_b and(5) is exactly the remaining diagonal condition. The state update is K'=A.

For a genuine finite example, use the prefix a=(5/3), weights u=(3/2,3/4), D=9/4, K=1, nu=27. Its identity is

  E_a=3(-Q_10)+27||e-g_1||^2.

Choose the primitive tail b=(sqrt(2)), whose capacity is A=1+sqrt(2), and use tau=1. The primitive tail certificate is explicitly

  V_b=2(1+sqrt(2))(-Q_10)+2(-Q_01),

with local tail indices. Then eta=0, beta=27/28 and the remaining transport matrix is diagonal with entries9/4 and(9/4)/(1+2sqrt(2)), both positive. Consequently the actual three-step schedule

  h=(5/3,1,sqrt(2))

has nonnegative proof weights (3/2,3/4,27sqrt(2)/28,27(1+sqrt(2))/28), and the certified bound

  W_3(h)<=14/(45+27sqrt(2)).

This is weaker than the exact ZJ benchmark. It tests the block rule but provides no improvement.

## 4. Balanced primitive-tail doubling cannot be competitive under this subrule

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2), and start with any finite valid state of length1. At round j append a bridge and the standard silver primitive tail of the same length n_j=2^(j+1)-1, so n_(j+1)=2n_j+1. Its shifted capacity is A_j=lambda^(j+1), obtained by repeated ConPP using F(x,x)=lambda x. Use the fixed-nu subrule of part3 with any parameters satisfying its actual weight and PSD conditions.

For j>=1 the reset K_(j+1)=A_j gives K_j=lambda^j=A_j/lambda. Write X_j=kD_j. The recurrence and(5) become

  X_(j+1)=X_j+2A_j+r_j-K_j,
  r_j^2 X_(j+1)<=(2A_j-1)[X_j+(K_j-1)^2],
  X_(j+1)>=2A_j-1.                                 (6)

The last inequality follows from c>=0. Hence r_j<=sqrt(X_j+(K_j-1)^2), and since K_j>=1,

  X_(j+1)<=X_j+2A_j+sqrt(X_j).

Choose M sufficiently large that X_1<=M A_1 and(lambda-1)M>=2+sqrt(M). Induction gives X_j<=M A_j, so x_j=X_j/A_j is bounded. Let L=limsup_j x_j. If L=0 there is nothing to prove. Otherwise take a subsequence with x_(j+1)->L. Put t_j=r_j/A_j. From(6),

  lambda x_(j+1)=x_j+2-1/lambda+t_j,
  t_j^2 lambda x_(j+1)
    <=(2-1/A_j)[x_j/A_j+(1/lambda-1/A_j)^2].         (7)

Along a further subsequence x_j converges to a number at most L; thus t_j has a limit at least(lambda-1)L-2+1/lambda. Passing to the limit in(7) yields

  L*[(lambda-1)L-2+1/lambda]_+^2<=2/lambda^3.        (8)

Let L_0 be the unique solution, above(2-1/lambda)/(lambda-1), of the corresponding equality. The left side is strictly increasing on that interval, so L<=L_0. At L=sqrt(2), its value times lambda^3 equals lambda sqrt(2)=2+sqrt(2)>2; hence

  limsup_j D_j/lambda^(j+1)<=L_0/k<sqrt(2)/k.        (9)

The exact benchmark along these same dyadic horizons has liminf B_(n_j)/lambda^(j+1)>=2. A short scalar proof avoids importing any phase theorem. A complete balanced primitive tree with2^K unit leaves has capacity lambda^K. Replace one leaf by zero and collapse its parent using F(x,0)=x; the resulting legal tree has2^K-1 leaves. The map F is2-Lipschitz in each coordinate (differentiate its explicit formula, whose partial derivatives lie in[1,2]), so this single leaf replacement decreases the root by at most2^K. Thus P_(2^K-2)>=lambda^K-2^K. The admissible dominant split with that prefix and an empty tail gives

  B_(2^K-1)>=G(P_(2^K-2),1)>=2lambda^K-2^(K+1).

Since2/lambda<1, the claimed normalized lower limit follows. Combining with(9), the value1/D_j certified by this transport satisfies

  liminf_j (1/D_j)/U_(n_j)>=2k/L_0>sqrt(2)k>1.

Therefore this specific whole-tail rule, under the displayed constant-nu and equal-horizon recursion, cannot certify an improvement even over the basic primitive rate. This does not lower-bound W(h_j), does not exclude other parameter recursions, and does not show that all residual certificates fail.

## 5. What the next block interface must retain

The aggregate-only expression depends on(e,g,U_b) but not independently on q. Therefore a positive new residual coefficient forces K'=A unless another q-dependent certificate is retained: subtracting nu'||e'-K'q||^2 would otherwise give a negative q^2 coefficient in a variable absent from the original matrix. This explains the forced reset in the tested rule.

A source-supported extra piece is the primitive dual residual

  2(f_start-f_end)-2(A-1)||q||^2
     >=||g_start-(d_b+q)/A||^2.                     (10)

The proof in Grimmer–Shu–Wang arXiv:2410.16249, AppendixA.1 Lemma17, was read in full; before adding the optimum interpolation inequality it gives exactly(10), using the primitive potential plus nonnegative interpolation sums. That derivation uses the primitive potential itself and A=1+sum(b), not an assumed equality of primitive and dominant ambient classes. A future proof may rederive this combination explicitly rather than appeal to the final gradient-norm statement. No verifier promotion is claimed here. The next test is to retain both this dual residual and the objective residual through a join, with the bridge gradient and tail initial gradient distinct. A coarse sum of the bridge descent estimate and(10) has not recovered the basic large silver bridge, so it is not yet a replacement recursion.

# Robust nonstationary positive-value relay with exponential growth
Status: complete explicit construction, UNVERIFIED; no new verifier allocation.
This extends the periodic signed-history example by allowing independently varying modulation at every stage and a strictly growing gradient scale. All proof ingredients are included here.

## 1. Schedule class and value
Fix
a=9/10, T=23/10, kappa=1/10, chi=6/5, q_g=901/900.
Choose any m>=1 and ANY numbers v_i in[1,chi],0<=i<=m, with v_0=1.
Define alpha_i=q_g^i v_i and
b_i=T-1+(T/a)alpha_(i+1)/alpha_i,0<=i<m.
The supplied schedule is h=(1,b_0,...,1,b_(m-1)), of length2m.
Every b_i belongs to[3,5]; these are variable checkpoints, not a constant schedule.

Then one explicitly defined nonseparable convex1-smooth function in R^(m+1) gives
W_(2m)(h)>=(85/121) q_g^(2m) v_m^2
          >=(85/121)(901/900)^(2m).                     (1)
Its exact closest-minimizer normalization is used. Meanwhile the entire quadratic-class objective is at most
max{1/(2 e m),(4/5)^(2m)} ->0.                           (2)
Thus the nonlinear error grows exponentially on a robust nonstationary class with freely chosen v_i.

Equivalently, this is an explicit condition on a supplied checkpoint schedule: the multiplicative partial products
v_i=product_(j=0)^(i-1) [(9/(23 q_g))(b_j-13/10)]
must all lie in[1,6/5]. The empty product v_0=1 is fixed. This condition is sufficient, not asserted for arbitrary schedules.

## 2. One global function and exact residual identity
Let zeta_0=e_0 and
zeta_(i+1)=-a zeta_i+sqrt(1-a^2)e_(i+1).
Their Gram matrix is real PSD with
<zeta_i,zeta_j>=(-a)^|i-j|.
Set omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i and
J(z)=max{0,max_i(<omega_i,z>-kappa alpha_i^2)}, f=env_1 J.
This is one finite nonnegative convex max-affine function, so its envelope is convex, differentiable and1-smooth, with minimum0. The direct proximal optimality condition proves that if plane i is active at x-omega_i then
grad f(x)=omega_i, f(x)=<omega_i,x>-(1/2+kappa)alpha_i^2.
Subgradient monotonicity gives the1-Lipschitz gradient estimate, ensuring full global legality, not only local interpolation.

Start at X_0=T alpha_0 zeta_0=T zeta_0, and set the intended block starts
X_(i+1)=X_i-(1+b_i)omega_i.
Let Z_i=X_i-T omega_i. Define
B_i=(T/a)alpha_(i+1), D_i=B_i(1-a^2).
Then
Z_0=0, Z_(i+1)=Z_i-B_i(zeta_i+a zeta_(i+1)).
Consequently
<Z_i,zeta_j>=0 for j>=i,
<Z_i,zeta_j>=-S_(j,i) for j<i,
S_(j,i)=sum_(l=j)^(i-1)D_l(-a)^(l-j).                   (3)
This follows by taking inner products of the update: zeta_l+a zeta_(l+1) is orthogonal to every later zeta_j, and its earlier inner products are(1-a^2)(-a)^(l-j).

At either real query x=X_i-u omega_i,u=0,1, the proposed proximal point is Z_i+d omega_i with d=T-u-1. The terminal query has d=T-1. Put delta=T-2=3/10, so all these d are>=delta.
The current plane has value(d-kappa)alpha_i^2>=alpha_i^2/5>0.
For an old index j its deficit relative to the current plane is
d alpha_i(alpha_i-C_ij alpha_j)
 +alpha_j S_(j,i)-kappa alpha_i^2+kappa alpha_j^2,        (4)
where C_ij=(-a)^(i-j). Future indices have the same expression with S=0.

## 3. Uniform estimates for the signed history
Put theta=a q_g=901/1000 and K=(T/a)(1-a^2)=437/900.
For L=i-j>0,
S_(j,i)/q_g^j=K q_g sum_(r=0)^(L-1)(-theta)^r v_(j+r+1).
Define the negative constant
S_floor=K q_g(1-theta chi)/(1-theta^2).
Using v in[1,chi] on positive and negative terms gives:
if L is even,
S_(j,i)/q_g^j >= S_floor(1-theta^L);                    (5)
if L is odd,
S_(j,i)/q_g^j >= S_floor
 +K q_g theta^(L-1)(theta chi-theta^2)/(1-theta^2)
 >=S_floor.                                           (6)
Thus old residuals may be positive; only their exact quantitative cost is bounded.

The following rational bounds will suffice:
theta^2<13/16, theta^2>4/5,
theta chi-1<13/160,
K q_g<39/80,
|S_floor|<169/800.                                     (7)
For the last inequality divide the product of the preceding bounds by
1-theta^2>3/16:
(39/80)(13/160)/(3/16)=169/800.
All numbers here are exact finite rational inequalities.

Every coefficient of d in(4), including future comparisons, is positive.
For even separation in a past comparison,
C_ij alpha_j/alpha_i=(a/q_g)^L v_j/v_i<=a^2 chi<1.
For a future even separation the ratio is
theta^L v_j/v_i<=theta^2 chi<39/40<1.
Odd correlations are negative. Therefore checking d=delta suffices.

Future planes pass for arbitrary amplitude ratios. At even separation their deficit at d=delta is
(delta-kappa)alpha_i^2+kappa alpha_j^2-delta C_ij alpha_i alpha_j.
This quadratic form is positive definite because
delta^2 C_ij^2<=delta^2 a^4=59049/1000000
 <4kappa(delta-kappa)=80000/1000000.
At odd separation every term has a nonnegative sign.

For past comparisons normalize(4) by q_g^(2j). Set
z=q_g^L v_i>=v_i>=1, y=v_j in[1,chi].
If L is odd, (6) and the positive cross term give the lower bound
(delta-kappa)z^2+kappa y^2+S_floor y
 >=3/10-(169/800)(6/5)=93/2000>0.                       (8)

If L is even, the part
(delta-kappa)z^2-delta a^L z y
increases with z>=1, since its derivative is at least
2/5-(3/10)a^2 chi>0.
Replace z by v_i; then replace a^L by the larger theta^L to lower the expression further. Using(5), the result is
F(v_i,y,w)=(delta-kappa)v_i^2+kappa y^2
 -delta w v_i y+S_floor(1-w)y,
where w=theta^L lies in[0,theta^2].
This is affine in w, so only endpoints need checking.
At w=0, the estimate in(8) applies.
At w=theta^2, F increases with v_i on[1,chi]:
2(delta-kappa)v_i-delta theta^2 y
 >=2/5-(3/10)(13/16)(6/5)>0.
It decreases with y on that interval, since
2kappa y-delta theta^2 v_i+S_floor(1-theta^2)
 <6/25-(3/10)(4/5)=0.
Its minimum is therefore at v_i=1,y=chi. By(7),
F(1,chi,theta^2)
>43/125-(3/10)(13/16)(6/5)-(39/80)(13/160)(6/5)
=127/32000>0.                                          (9)
This proves every old-plane comparison at every lag, including those with S<0.

The zero, current, past and future checks establish all prescribed gradients. In particular at each checkpoint
J(X_i-2omega_i)=alpha_i^2/5>0,
so the new mechanism carries a positive proximal value rather than resetting to the minimum.

## 4. Exact minimizer distance and objective
The minimizer set equals
P_min={z:<omega_i,z><=kappa alpha_i^2 for all i}.
Because alpha_0=1 and alpha_i>=1, y_proj=kappa zeta_0 belongs to P_min: odd correlations are negative; even ones are at most1. Constraint0 is active and
X_0-y_proj=(T-kappa)omega_0.
This is a nonnegative active-normal certificate, so y_proj is the exact closest minimizer. The squared initial distance is
(T-kappa)^2=(11/5)^2=121/25.
The exact terminal value is
2f(X_m)=2(T-kappa-1/2)alpha_m^2=(17/5)alpha_m^2.
Dividing gives(1).

The gradients omega_0,...,omega_m are independent with adjacent nonzero correlations, and their squared norms alpha_i^2 vary. Independence allows each zero/plane hinge to be isolated; its envelope Hessian is the rank-one projector onto omega_i. Adjacent projectors do not commute, proving nonseparability in every fixed orthonormal basis.

## 5. Actual negative history and the quadratic comparison
This family strictly escapes the old sign restriction. Choose any eligible consecutive modulation pattern
v_j=chi,v_(j+1)=1,v_(j+2)=chi.
Then
S_(j,j+2)=K q_g^(j+1)(1-theta chi)<0.
Nevertheless(8)--(9) certify the full old plane. The construction therefore does not merely hide a nonpositive-residual assumption behind new notation.

The checkpoints obey
13/10+(23/9)q_g(5/6)<=b_i<=13/10+(23/9)q_g(6/5),
an interval contained in[3,5]. For the quadratic multiplier
(1-lambda)(1-b_i lambda),
on0<=lambda<=1/5 it is nonnegative and<=exp(-lambda); on1/5<=lambda<=1 its absolute value is<=4/5 by the endpoints and its single quadratic vertex. Thus spectral diagonalization gives(2) for every finite-dimensional convex quadratic.

This is a rigorous candidate lower bound for the displayed nonstationary class, not the exact target theorem. The bounded-modulation/partial-product condition is explicitly retained; no claim says arbitrary schedules satisfy it or can be partitioned into such blocks without losing the target constant.

# Compatibility screen: interval matrices and full joint descent

Status: UNVERIFIED algebraic screen requested by master_guidance31b8d52469caa452.
It uses max4's cd0f93f08a50828f as a lead, not as a verified building block.
All identities needed below are derived explicitly. No numerical or verifier
allocation is used.

## 1. Exact dictionary, including the star edges

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Use
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.
A full certificate has lambda>=0, finite flow out-in=2 e_n, and
M(q,lambda,h)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum lambda_ij Q_ij>=0.

Let C be an (n+1)-square real matrix with C1=0; its off-diagonal
entries may have either sign. Put b=C^T1. Define T(h) by T_ii=1,
T_ij=h_j when j<i, and T_ij=0 when j>i, and set
H(C,h)=CT(h)+T(h)^T C^T.

The exact sign dictionary is

2 sum_(i!=j) C_ij Q_ij
  =-2 sum_i b_i f_i - sum_(i,j)H_ij<g_i,g_j>
    +sum_i b_i||g_i||^2.                             (1)

For verification, the function terms are -2b^Tf because row sums
vanish. The position term is 2sum C_ij<g_i,x_j-x_i>
=2sum C_ij<g_i,x_j>, since C1=0. Substituting
x_j=x_0+g_j-(Tg)_j and again using C1=0 gives
2sum C_ij<g_i,g_j>-2sum(CT)_ij<g_i,g_j>.
The squared-gradient difference contributes
b^T(||g_i||^2)-2sum C_ij<g_i,g_j>. Combining proves (1).

Thus the following simultaneous finite/star multiplier change preserves
all flow equations and keeps mu_i=lambda_(i,star) fixed:

lambda'_ij=lambda_ij+2C_ij   (finite distinct i,j),
nu'_i=nu_i-2b_i,             nu_i=lambda_(star,i).     (2)

Indeed finite out-in changes by -2b_i, which is canceled by the
change -2b_i in incoming star flow. Also sum b_i=0.

At a FIXED schedule, the exact complete matrix change is simply

M(q,lambda',h)-M(q,lambda,h)=-H(C,h),                  (3)

embedded in the gradient block, with the x_0 row unchanged. The
function terms and b_i||g_i||^2 terms in (1) cancel against
sum(-2b_i)Q_(star,i). This is why the star adjustment must not be
omitted.

The ACTUAL sign constraints are

lambda_ij+2C_ij>=0  (i!=j),   nu_i-2b_i>=0.           (4)

They are neither positivity of interval coordinates nor positivity of
every C entry. Negative C entries are allowed exactly to the extent
that the old finite multipliers supply them.

## 2. Simultaneously changing the schedule

Let h'=h+a>=0. Define the full cut vector

z_t(lambda)=sum_(i,j)lambda_ij
 (1_(t<i)-1_(t<j))g_i,

where either indicator is zero at the star. Define the quadratic form

K(a;lambda)=sum_(t<n)a_t<g_t,z_t(lambda)>.

Then (1)--(3), now applied at h', give the exact identity

M(q',lambda',h') =
M(q,lambda,h)+(q'-q)||x_0||^2+K(a;lambda)-H(C,h').    (5)

This includes all remote forward-cut terms. For i<j, the matrix entries
of K in the gradient block are

2K_ij=a_i[mu_j+sum_(l<=i)lambda_(j,l)]
       -a_j sum_(l>j)lambda_(i,l),
K_ii=-a_i sum_(j>i)lambda_(i,j).                     (6)

The expression in (6) follows directly by collecting the two cut
contributions to <g_i,g_j>.

Consequently a diagonal H(C,h') does NOT diagonalize the full
joint perturbation: K still has the mixed entries (6). The exact
zero-mixed-entry target is H_ij=K_ij for i!=j, not H_ij=0.

For example, if every finite forward edge is zero, (6) becomes
2K_ij=a_i c_(i,j), where
c_(i,j)=mu_j+sum_(l<=i)lambda_(j,l).
Summing flow over the suffix shows sum_(j>i)c_(i,j)
=2+sum_(j>i)nu_j>0. Thus if H is diagonal AND K-H is
required to have no mixed entries, each a_i must be zero.
This is a precise incompatibility of those two simultaneous
requirements. It does not rule out allowing a non-diagonal PSD
remainder in (5).

## 3. Inactive-constraint costs survive this coordinate change

Suppose the old full certificate matches one legal stationary primal:
||x_0||=1, 2f_n=q, M vanishes on its data, lambda_ij Q_ij=0, and
<g_t,z_t(lambda)>=0. Put sigma_ij=-Q_ij>=0 on these SAME data.

If (4) holds, evaluating the fixed-h change (3) on the old data gives

sum_(i,j)H(C,h)_ij<g_i,g_j>
 =sum_(i,j)lambda'_ij sigma_ij>=0.                  (7)

The sum on the right includes the star edges. At the new schedule,
PSD of (5) necessarily gives

q'-q >= sum_(i,j)H(C,h')_ij<g_i,g_j>.                (8)

Writing DeltaT=T(h')-T(h), the right side is exactly the nonnegative
cost in (7) plus

2 sum_(i,j)(C DeltaT)_ij<g_i,g_j>.

Thus a descent q'<q must pay every inactive-interpolation cost through
this bilinear term. Diagonalization does not erase the earlier
joint-descent obstruction.

## 4. The triangular elimination can be made inhomogeneous

Assume h'_i>1 for i<n. Specify the strict upper entries U_ij=C_ij.
For j>i define L_(j,i)=sum_(l<=i)C_(j,l), L_(j,-1)=0.
The desired off-diagonal matrix H has the exact equation

(h'_i-1)L_(j,i)+L_(j,i-1)
 =U_ij+h'_j sum_(l>j)U_(i,l)-H_ij.                 (9)

At j=n the displayed sum is empty and the auxiliary h'_n is irrelevant.
Indeed (CT)_ij=U_ij+h'_j sum_(l>j)U_(i,l), while
(CT)_ji=-(h'_i-1)L_(j,i)-L_(j,i-1), proving (9).

Taking H_ij=K_ij makes (9) a scalar elimination for the mixed
cancellation in (5). After it, one STILL has to check every sign in
(4), all diagonal entries or the full remaining PSD matrix, and
strict output improvement. Nothing in the elimination proves those
conditions automatically.

## 5. Compatibility with the actual new deformation

The independently derived candidate8c998d29efd3da99 uses
C_(j,k)=eta p_j/2 for j>k and C_(j,j)=-eta p_j/2, with all other
entries zero. It has b_k=eta/2 and b_j=-eta p_j/2.
These are exactly the star changes in that candidate.

Its H(C,h') is generally NOT diagonal. The specific suffix step
rescalings make its mixed entries equal to K_ij, and its remaining
diagonal difference is eta diag(p). This is a concrete solution of
(5), whereas max4's homogeneous H_ij=0 modes do not by themselves
supply that cancellation.

Conclusion of the bounded screen: the interval coordinates give a
useful exact dictionary and an inhomogeneous elimination, but the
published zero-remainder interval subclass is not a ready-made repair
for the new deformation's cut-profile mismatch. It retains the same
aggregate-sign and inactive-cost obligations. No all-schedule descent,
Huber saturation, or exact-profile lower bound follows.

## 2. Explicit finite deformation allowing local forward edges

Assume (R), a>1, and nu_k>0. First suppose c_2>0. Choose v>0 and define

u=(v/c_2)[c_1 - b r_02(c_2+v)/((a-1)(c_3+v))].       (1)

Require u>=0 and u+v<=nu_k. Change

nu'_k=nu_k-u-v,   nu'_(k+1)=nu_(k+1)+u,
nu'_n=nu_n+v,
lambda'_(k+1,k)=lambda_(k+1,k)+u,
lambda'_(n,k)=lambda_(n,k)+v,                         (2)

with all other multipliers unchanged, and set

a'=(a c_2+v)/(c_2+v),   b'=b c_3/(c_3+v).            (3)

Keep all earlier steps fixed. All new coefficients are nonnegative,
flow is preserved, a'>1, and 0<=b'<=b.

The complete matrix identity is

M(q,lambda',h')-M(q,lambda,h)
 =(a-a')(r_01+r_02)||g_k||^2
  +[u+(b-b')r_12]||g_(k+1)||^2+v||g_n||^2.           (4)

Every coefficient is nonnegative and v>0.

Here are all mixed-entry checks. For the pair (k,n), the coefficient
change is (a'-a)c_2+v(a'-1)=0. For (k+1,n), it is
(b'-b)c_3+b'v=0. For (k,k+1), it is
(a'-a)c_1+u(a'-1)-(b'-b)r_02=0 by (1).
Every pair involving an earlier prefix index is unchanged by (R):
a change of a or b could only couple to such an index through one
of the forward edges excluded by (R). The only changed outgoing
finite masses are +u at k+1 and +v at n; the diagonal dependence
on the changed steps contributes the remaining terms in (4).
The x_0 row is unchanged because every mu_j is unchanged.

The condition in (1) is explicit. In particular, if

(a-1)c_1 c_3 > b r_02 c_2,                            (5)

then all sufficiently small v>0 have u>=0, and they also satisfy
u+v<=nu_k. If r_02=0, (1) reduces to u=v c_1/c_2>=0
without needing a strict inequality in (5). Thus adjacent forward
edges do not obstruct this move; the skip edge k->n is different.

If c_2=0, then c_1>0 by the cut flow. Choose 0<u<=nu_k,
take v=0, and instead set

a'=(a c_1+u)/(c_1+u),   b'=b.

The same changes (2) give
M_new-M_old=(a-a')(r_01+r_02)||g_k||^2+u||g_(k+1)||^2>=0.
No division by c_2 is used in this case.

These identities imply an actual strict worst-case improvement,
not just feasibility at level q. For c_2>0 let
B=product_(t<n)(1+h'_t). On every new legal trajectory with
R=||x_0||>0 and E=2f_n/R^2, one has ||x_n||<=BR and
f_n<=||g_n||||x_n||. Therefore (4) implies

q-E>=v E^2/(4B^2),

hence
W_n(h')<=2q/[1+sqrt(1+v q/B^2)]<q.                   (6)

For c_2=0 use ||g_n||<=(1+b')||g_(k+1)|| to obtain the
same conclusion with v replaced by u/(1+b')^2.
These elementary bounds use the full old PSD matrix evaluated on
the new formal vectors. They do not pretend that the old matching
primal follows the new schedule.

## 3. A stronger necessary condition at a full stationary tuple

Now DROP (R). Suppose the certificate matches a SINGLE legal primal
transcript with ||x_0||=1, 2f_n=q>0, M zero on its data, and
lambda_ij Q_ij=0. Assume positive last steps and all cut stationarity
equalities <g_t,z_t(lambda)>=0, where

z_t(lambda)=sum_(j>t)(mu_j+sum_(l<=t)lambda_(j,l))g_j
            -sum_(i<=t)(sum_(j>t)lambda_(i,j))g_i.

First, <g_(n-1),g_n>=0. This follows from the complete system,
without differentiability of W: vary only the last step by s in
both signs on the same legal function. Its new final gradient
changes by O(|s|), and f_n(s)=f_n-s<g_(n-1),g_n>+O(s^2).
The old PSD form has value O(s^2) on the changed formal vectors
because it annihilates the old data. The first-order change of the
matrix itself has zero pairing by the last cut equality, so its
new value is also O(s^2). Since all new Q_ij<=0 and the same lambda
is nonnegative, the certificate identity implies
2f_n(s)<=q+O(s^2). Taking s in both signs gives the orthogonality.

Suppose nu_k>0. Complementarity gives

f_k=||g_k||^2/2.

The descent inequality then shows y=x_k-g_k is a minimizer. If
0<a<1, Lipschitz continuity of the gradient at the two endpoints
y and x_k forces g_(k+1)=(1-a)g_k: the two Lipschitz inequalities
have lengths summing to ||g_k||, so equality in the triangle
inequality fixes the vector. At a=1 the next point is a minimizer.
For 0<a<1, the last orthogonality makes g_n perpendicular to g_k,
while x_n-y=(1-a)(1-b)g_k; cocoercivity against y then forces
g_n=0. Both cases contradict q>0. Therefore

a>1.                                                 (7)

Put d=||g_k||^2, A=||g_(k+1)||^2, Bn=||g_n||^2,
u0=<g_k,g_(k+1)>, v0=<g_k,g_n>, and
F_i=lambda_(i,k+1)+lambda_(i,n) for i<=k.
All d,A,Bn are positive when q>0.

Interpolation Q_(k+1,k)<=0 and Q_(n,k)<=0, using f_k=d/2
and last-gradient orthogonality, gives

-(a-1)u0>=f_(k+1)+A/2,
-(a-1)v0>=f_n+Bn/2.                                  (8)

The kth cut stationarity equality is

c_1 u0+c_2 v0-F_k d-sum_(i<k)F_i<g_k,g_i>=0.

Combining with (8) yields the quantitative REMOTE-flow obligation

-sum_(i<k)F_i<g_k,g_i>
 >=F_k d+
   [c_1(f_(k+1)+A/2)+c_2(f_n+Bn/2)]/(a-1)
 >0.                                                  (9)

For strict positivity, summing the cut flow gives
c_1+c_2=2+nu_(k+1)+nu_n+sum_(i<=k)F_i>0,
and f_(k+1)+A/2 and f_n+Bn/2 are strictly positive.

Thus some earlier index i<k must satisfy BOTH F_i>0 and
<g_i,g_k><0. If there is no such remote forward edge, nu_k
cannot be positive at a full stationary tuple. In particular:

- At n=2, the sum in (9) is empty, so every full positive-step
  stationary tuple with q>0 has nu_0=0. No triangular-multiplier
  hypothesis is needed.
- At arbitrary n, a positive nu_(n-2) requires a genuine earlier
  forward edge into the last two samples and an oppositely directed
  earlier gradient. Local forward edges alone cannot support it.
- This gives the exact failure point for extending a suffix-only
  multiplier argument: the missing term is the signed remote sum
  in (9), not an unspecified PSD or regularity issue.

The conclusion does not eliminate terminal nu_n, does not force
q=1/(2sum h+1), and does not resolve the exact benchmark profile.
It only narrows the full-feasible obstruction.

All elementary inequalities used above follow from convexity and
1-smoothness. In particular, f(x-gnabla f(x))<=f(x)-||gnabla f(x)||^2/2;
and <grad f(x),x-y>>=||grad f(x)||^2 at any minimizer y follows by
adding the two smooth-convex interpolation inequalities with y.

claim: Sharp repeated-block boundedness threshold: for arbitrary ordinary steps in[0,1] of total s followed by b, each block is Fejer when b<=s+2; a Huber cycle persists at equality; above it, a growing-dimensional Markov Moreau construction gives W>=((2s+1)/(s+1)^2)((b-1)/(s+1))^m.
evidence:
# Exact boundedness threshold for small-step blocks followed by one long step
Status: complete candidate, UNVERIFIED. No additional verifier call.
This is a scoped matching upper/lower classification, not the unrestricted exact-profile target.

## 1. Statement
Let A=(a_1,...,a_l) be a finite list with0<=a_j<=1 and total s. Repeat the block(A,b) with fixed b>=0.
For every finite-dimensional convex differentiable1-smooth function with a minimizer, one complete block never increases the distance to that minimizer whenever
b<=s+2.                                                 (1)
Consequently W_(m(l+1))((A,b)^m)<=1 for every m>=1 in this range.

At b=s+2, a single fixed symmetric Huber objective gives, at every block endpoint, normalized error
(2s+1)/(s+1)^2>0.                                        (2)
For every b>s+2 and every m>=1, an explicit nonseparable convex1-smooth function in R^(m+1) realizes
W_(m(l+1))((A,b)^m)
 >=[(2s+1)/(s+1)^2][(b-1)/(s+1)]^m,                     (3)
which grows exponentially.
The lower constructions only require the ordinary steps to be nonnegative with total s; the upper implication(1) additionally requires each a_j<=1. The distinction is retained.

## 2. Self-contained inequalities for the upper bound
Normalize the chosen minimizer to0 and minimum to0.
The descent estimate follows by integrating the1-Lipschitz gradient along a segment. Applied to the convex function f(z)-<grad f(y),z>, which is minimized at y, it gives
f(x)>=f(y)+<grad f(y),x-y>+||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2/2.    (4)
Adding its two orientations gives cocoercivity.
Against a minimizer, (4) yields
<x,g(x)>>=f(x)+||g(x)||^2/2, f(x)>=||g(x)||^2/2.          (5)

Consider a small step x_next=x-alpha g with0<alpha<=1 and let v=g(x_next). Cocoercivity implies
alpha<g-v,g>>=||g-v||^2,
and hence <g-v,v>>=(1/alpha-1)||g-v||^2>=0.
Thus <g,v>>=||v||^2 and ||g||>=||v||. Formula(4) also gives
f(x)-f(x_next)>=alpha||v||^2.
A zero step has the same properties directly.

Let x_t be the ordinary-block points, y its endpoint, and k=g(y). Put P_t equal to the sum of ordinary steps preceding x_t. Summing the preceding estimates gives
||g(x_t)||>=||k||,
f(x_t)>=f(y)+(s-P_t)||k||^2.                             (6)
For one ordinary step of size alpha, (5) gives
||x_next||^2-||x||^2
<=-2alpha f(x)+alpha(alpha-1)||g(x)||^2.
Because alpha(alpha-1)<=0, (6) may be substituted into both terms. Summing all ordinary steps and using
2 sum_t a_t(s-P_t)=s^2+sum_t a_t^2
yields
||y||^2-||x_0||^2<=-2s f(y)-s(s+1)||k||^2.              (7)
For the long step z=y-bk, (5) gives
||z||^2-||y||^2<=-2b f(y)+b(b-1)||k||^2.
Together with(7), this is the precise block inequality
||z||^2-||x_0||^2
<= -2(s+b)[f(y)-||k||^2/2]
   +(b-s-2)(b+s)||k||^2.                                (8)
Both terms are nonpositive under(1), proving the distance assertion. Applying it at every block keeps the endpoint distance bounded by its initial value. Integrating the gradient from a minimizer also gives f(z)<=||z||^2/2, so the normalized endpoint objective is at most1.

No last-iterate convergence rate below the threshold is asserted here; (8) proves boundedness and its exact boundary.

## 3. Boundary witness
Let tau=1/(s+1) and
f(x)=x^2/2 for |x|<=tau,
f(x)=tau|x|-tau^2/2 for |x|>=tau.
Its derivative clips x to[-tau,tau], so it is convex differentiable1-smooth.
Start at x_0=1. Through an ordinary block the derivative is constantly tau and the points decrease from1 to tau, because the cumulative ordinary sum lies in[0,s]. The step b=s+2 then sends tau to
tau-(s+2)tau=-1.
On the next block the signs reverse. Thus block endpoints alternate between1 and-1 for all repetitions. Their normalized objective is
2tau-tau^2=(2s+1)/(s+1)^2,
establishing(2) on one fixed scalar function.

## 4. Exponential high-dimensional witness above the boundary
Assume b>s+2 and put
T=s+1, q=sqrt((b-1)/(s+1))>1, a=1/q in(0,1).
Construct independent Markov directions in R^(m+1):
zeta_0=e_0,
zeta_(i+1)=-a zeta_i+sqrt(1-a^2)e_(i+1).
Let
alpha_i=q^i/T, omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i,
J(z)=max{0,max_(0<=i<=m)<omega_i,z>}, f=env_1 J.
Start at X_0=T omega_0=e_0 and define
X_(i+1)=X_i-(s+b)omega_i.
We verify that every query in ordinary block i and its checkpoint has gradient omega_i, and that the terminal gradient is omega_m.

Set Z_i=X_i-T omega_i. A direct update gives
Z_0=0,
Z_(i+1)=Z_i-B_i(zeta_i+a zeta_(i+1)),
B_i=(b-1)alpha_i=Tq^2 alpha_i.
Write D_i=B_i(1-a^2)=T(q^2-1)alpha_i.
Then D_(i+1)=q D_i, so D_i=aD_(i+1).
Taking Markov inner products shows
<Z_i,zeta_j>=0 for j>=i,
<Z_i,zeta_j>=-sum_(l=j)^(i-1)D_l(-a)^(l-j)<=0 for j<i.
For the last inequality, consecutive terms cancel exactly because aD_(l+1)=D_l; an odd-length sum has a positive final singleton. Thus every old residual is nonpositive, and this fact has been proved for all lags.

At a query after ordinary cumulative sum u in[0,s], the proposed proximal point is
X_i-(u+1)omega_i=Z_i+d omega_i,
where d=T-u-1=s-u>=0.
The current plane has value d alpha_i^2>=0.
For a future plane j>i,
<omega_j,omega_i>/alpha_i^2=(-a)^(j-i)alpha_j/alpha_i=(-1)^(j-i),
so its value is at most the current value, with equality at even separation.
For a past plane j<i, its residual term is nonpositive and
<omega_j,omega_i>/alpha_i^2=(-1)^(i-j)q^(-2(i-j))<=1;
again it is at most the current value. Thus ALL planes, and the zero plane, are dominated. The active-plane subgradient condition gives grad f=omega_i, and the block update is exact.

At the terminal point X_m the same check has d=T-1=s>=0, giving
f(X_m)=(T-1/2)alpha_m^2.
The Moreau envelope is globally convex differentiable1-smooth by the proximal optimality and monotonicity argument. Its minimum is0 on the cone where every normal has nonpositive inner product. The origin is the closest minimizer to X_0: X_0=T omega_0 is a positive multiple of an active normal at0, so for any minimizing z,
<X_0,z><=0 and ||X_0-z||^2>=||X_0||^2=1.
Consequently
2f(X_m)=(2T-1)q^(2m)/T^2,
which is exactly(3).

The omega_i are independent, with nonzero adjacent inner products. Isolated hinges against the zero plane have noncommuting rank-one Hessian projectors, so this is nonseparable in any fixed orthonormal basis and uses genuinely growing dimension. The ordinary gradients are constant on each block, but the energies grow geometrically from block to block. This is not a sequence of independently selected Hessians.

## 5. Relation to the central target
The threshold b=s+2 is exact for boundedness of the repeated prescribed block with ordinary steps in[0,1]. It is not an exact formula for W at a finite horizon, and it does not cover arbitrary long-step chronology. In particular it cannot substitute for a uniform lower bound matching U_n^ZJ. It supplies a sharp structural test for one class, with matching global upper and high-dimensional lower arguments.

claim: Corrected two-sided residual join now recovers the ordinary ConPP certificate exactly. It keeps both blocks' gradient-aggregate residuals and uses four aggregate interpolation identities; an auxiliary endpoint coefficient may be negative only where a positive aggregate coefficient offsets it on the same actual interpolation edge. evidence:
# Two-sided residual join with aggregate interpolation cancellation

Status: unverified exact certificate identity and successful recovery of the ordinary ConPP join on its structural subspace. No improved recursive family has been found. This continues the failed aggregate-only rule4be2737d7e8764a6 without silently reusing its insufficient positivity restrictions.

For a GD block and nonnegative proof weights u, write D=sum u_i, d=x_start-x_end, U=sum u_i g_i, e=U-d, and

  E=2sum_i u_i(f_i-f_end)+sum_i u_i||g_i||^2
      +2sum_i u_i<g_i,x_start-x_i>-||U||^2.

Then E>=0 implies the objective guarantee W<=1/D by the squared-distance identity reproduced in research/max4_nonlocal_tail_transport.md. All formulas below use Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0, at smoothness1.

## 1. Two arbitrary blocks and the exact new state

Let block a end at y with gradient g. A bridge of physical length tau>=1 moves to y'=y-tau g, and block b starts there and ends at z with gradient q. Let the blocks have states(D_a,e_a,E_a) and(D_b,e_b,E_b); denote the tail gradient aggregate by U_b and its displacement by d_b, so e_b=U_b-d_b. The tail's proof-weight vector is v and its terminal entry is v_end. Assume certificates

  E_a>=nu_a||e_a-K_a g||^2,
  E_b>=nu_b||e_b-K_b q||^2,

where the nu coefficients are nonnegative. Exact structural relations such as e_a=K_a g may instead be retained as relations, without replacing them by a finite quadratic penalty.

Form new proof weights by keeping the prefix weights, adding eta to the prefix terminal entry, scaling all tail weights by beta, and adding gamma to the final entry. Require

  beta>=0,
  prefix_terminal_weight+eta>=0,
  beta*v_end+gamma>=0,
  D_c=D_a+eta+beta D_b+gamma>0.

The new residual is exactly

  e_c=e_a+(eta-tau)g+(beta-1)U_b+e_b+gamma q.         (1)

The change in energy, before eliminating the function difference Delta=f_y-f_z, is

  E_c=E_a+beta E_b+2(D_a+eta)Delta+R_0,

where

  R_0=eta(1-eta)||g||^2-2eta<e_a,g>
      +beta(1-beta)||U_b||^2
      +2beta<U_b,(tau-eta)g-e_a>
      +gamma(1-gamma)||q||^2
      -2gamma<q,e_a+(eta-tau)g+(beta-1)U_b+e_b>.      (2)

Equation(2) follows by expanding the definition of E under the displayed changes of proof weights; it involves no smoothness inequality yet.

## 2. Four aggregate interpolation identities

Define

  A_y=-2sum_(i in tail) v_i Q_(i,y),
  A_z=-2sum_(i in tail) v_i Q_(i,z),
  P=-2Q_(z,y), N=-2Q_(y,z).

Substitution of y-x_i=tau g+(y'-x_i) and d_b=U_b-e_b gives

  A_y=2D_b Delta-E_b-||U_b||^2
         -2(tau-1)<U_b,g>-D_b||g||^2,

  A_z=-E_b+||U_b||^2-2<U_b,e_b-q>-D_b||q||^2,

  P=2Delta-||g||^2-||q||^2+2(1-tau)<g,q>
          -2<q,U_b>+2<q,e_b>,

  N=-2Delta+(2tau-1)||g||^2-||q||^2
           +2<g,U_b>-2<g,e_b>+2<g,q>.              (3)

Choose scalars c,m,t_y,t_z satisfying

  c>=0, m>=0, t_z>=0, t_y+c*v_end>=0,
  c D_b+t_y-t_z=D_a+eta.                            (4)

Although t_y can be negative, the actual interpolation multipliers in c A_y+m A_z+t_y P+t_z N are all nonnegative. At the edge(z,y), A_y already contributes terminal coefficient c*v_end, so the total coefficient is c*v_end+t_y. At each other tail-to-y edge the coefficient is c*v_i; at tail-to-z edges it is m*v_i; and the edge(y,z) has coefficient t_z. Self-edges vanish. These are the signs that matter, rather than the signs of all four aggregate coordinates separately.

The function-coefficient equality in(4) eliminates Delta from(2).

## 3. A finite-dimensional sufficient certificate test

Define the following quadratic form in(e_a,e_b,g,U_b,q):

  R=R_0
    +c[||U_b||^2+2(tau-1)<U_b,g>+D_b||g||^2]
    +m[-||U_b||^2+2<U_b,e_b-q>+D_b||q||^2]
    +t_y[||g||^2+||q||^2+2(tau-1)<g,q>
                       +2<q,U_b>-2<q,e_b>]
    +t_z[-(2tau-1)||g||^2+||q||^2-2<g,U_b>
                       +2<g,e_b>-2<g,q>].          (5)

Equations(2)–(4) give the exact identity

  E_c=E_a+(beta+c+m)E_b+R
                  +c A_y+m A_z+t_y P+t_z N.        (6)

Consequently, for any nu_c>=0 and real K_c, it suffices that the quadratic form

  R+nu_a||e_a-K_a g||^2
      +(beta+c+m)nu_b||e_b-K_b q||^2
      -nu_c||e_a+(eta-tau)g+(beta-1)U_b
                          +e_b+(gamma-K_c)q||^2    (7)

be positive semidefinite. Any exact structural relations from the input blocks may first be substituted into(7); imposing positivity only on that known subspace is then legitimate. For free residual variables, positivity means the full symmetric5-by5 coefficient matrix is PSD, in every Euclidean dimension. This implies E_c>=nu_c||e_c-K_c q||^2 and W<=1/D_c.

This is a certificate construction, not a new algorithm with auxiliary state: all u,v and residuals are proof quantities. The actual algorithm is precisely the predetermined concatenation[a,tau,b].

## 4. Exact ordinary-ConPP calibration

Take genuinely primitive input blocks of capacities K=1+sum(a) and A=1+sum(b), with their standard proof weights(a,K) and(b,A). Then

  D_a=2K-1, D_b=2A-1,
  e_a=K g, e_b=Aq,
  E_a=V_a>=0, E_b=V_b>=0.

Let r>0 be the unique root

  r^2+(A+K)r-AK=0,

so the usual bridge is tau=1+r. Since r<A, set

  J=K+r,
  beta=1, eta=tau-K, gamma=J,
  K_c=K+A+r,
  c=m=J/(A-r),
  t_y=c(1-A), t_z=c r.                             (8)

All actual weight conditions hold: the new bridge weight is K+eta=tau; the final weight is A+gamma=K_c. The interpolation conditions(4) also hold, because

  t_y+c*v_end=c(1-A)+c A=c>0,
  c D_b+t_y-t_z=c(A-r)=J=D_a+eta.

After substitution of e_a=Kg and e_b=Aq, the quadratic remainder(5) vanishes identically. One can check this by the equivalent two scalar identities

  r(K+A+r)=KA,
  K+r=2Ar/(A-r).

Indeed the resulting energy identity is exactly

  V_c=V_a+(1+2c)V_b
          -2c sum_(i in tail, i!=end) h_i(Q_(i,y)+Q_(i,z))
          -2c Q_(z,y)-2cr Q_(y,z),                 (9)

where V_c is the saturated primitive energy for the combined physical sum K+A+r-1. Every multiplier on -Q in(9) is nonnegative. Thus the rule recovers the successful ordinary ConPP certificate on its actual structural identities, with capacity F(K,A)=K+A+r.

The negative aggregate coefficient t_y in(8) is essential when A>1, even though the final multiplier on its interpolation edge is positive. Earlier screens that required every aggregate coefficient nonnegative excluded this calibration. This is the same distinction exposed by the signed interval-coordinate test cd0f93f08a50828f.

## Remaining task

The calibration does not prove closure for arbitrary finite residual penalties. At the exact primitive point e_a=Kg and e_b=Aq are identities, not estimates with a finite nu. A candidate involving nonprimitive blocks must either retain its actual additional boundary relations or satisfy the full matrix(7). No parameters giving a competitive recursive nonprimitive family have been found, and no claim of an improved denominator is made. The endpoint-only weight template is separately refuted by12ea2963a6e53e67; it cannot be substituted for this full internal-weight accounting.

evidence:
# Positive-value periodic Markov relay with signed history
Status: complete explicit construction, UNVERIFIED. No new verifier call.
This tests the specific repair suggested after the minimum-reset and residual-sign obstructions: allow positive proximal function values, and check actual past-plane deficits even when the signed residual is positive.

## 1. A parameterized model
Fix a in(0,1), chi>=1, T>=2, and kappa in[0,T-2]. Assume
T>=2a chi,                                               (1)
(T-2-kappa)-(T-kappa)chi^2+T chi/a>=0.                     (2)
For any number m>=1 of blocks, in R^(m+1) set
zeta_0=e_0,
zeta_(i+1)=-a zeta_i+sqrt(1-a^2)e_(i+1).
Define alpha_i=chi for even i and alpha_i=1 for odd i, omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i. Thus
<zeta_i,zeta_j>=(-a)^|i-j|
and all omega_i are independent.

Each real block consists of one unit step followed by
b_i=T-1+(T/a)alpha_(i+1)/alpha_i.
Take the ONE finite max-affine function
J(z)=max{0,max_(0<=i<=m)(<omega_i,z>-kappa alpha_i^2)}
and f=env_1 J. Start at X_0=T alpha_0 zeta_0.
We prove that block i queries X_i and X_i-omega_i with gradient omega_i at both, and that
X_(i+1)=X_i-(1+b_i)omega_i.
The terminal point is X_m with gradient omega_m.

The function f is legal globally: J is finite nonnegative convex with J(0)=0, and its envelope is finite convex differentiable1-smooth. For precision, the proximal minimization has a unique minimizer by the quadratic term; its subgradient equation implies grad f(x)=x-prox_J(x), and monotonicity gives
||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2<=<grad f(x)-grad f(y),x-y>.
At any point where plane i is active at x-omega_i, that subgradient equation yields the claimed gradient and value
f(x)=<omega_i,x>-alpha_i^2/2-kappa alpha_i^2.
Thus it remains to compare every affine plane at the indicated proximal points.

## 2. Exact signed residuals
Let Z_i=X_i-T omega_i and put
B_i=(T/a)alpha_(i+1), D_i=B_i(1-a^2).
The update gives
Z_0=0,
Z_(i+1)=Z_i-B_i(zeta_i+a zeta_(i+1)).
Direct multiplication of Markov correlations proves
<Z_i,zeta_j>=0 for j>=i,
<Z_i,zeta_j>=-S_(j,i) for j<i,
where
S_(j,i)=sum_(l=j)^(i-1)D_l(-a)^(l-j).                     (3)
Indeed zeta_l+a zeta_(l+1) is orthogonal to all zeta_j with j>=l+1, and its inner product with earlier zeta_j is(1-a^2)(-a)^(l-j). This proves(3) by summing the update; no sign of S is assumed.

At a real query x=X_i-u omega_i with u=0 or1, its proposed proximal point is
Z_i+d omega_i, d=T-u-1>=T-2.
The terminal query has d=T-1 and obeys the same lower bound.
The current affine plane has value(d-kappa)alpha_i^2>=0.
The current-minus-j-th plane difference is
d alpha_i(alpha_i-C_ij alpha_j)
 +alpha_j S_(j,i)-kappa alpha_i^2+kappa alpha_j^2          (4)
for j<i, with C_ij=(-a)^(i-j); for j>i the same formula has S=0.
Every coefficient of d is positive: at even separation the amplitudes agree and C<1, while at odd separation C<0. Hence it suffices to check d=T-2.

Future planes are already controlled. At even separation their offsets agree and their deficit is d alpha_i^2(1-C)>=0. At odd separation the deficit is
(d-kappa)alpha_i^2+kappa alpha_j^2+d a^|i-j| alpha_i alpha_j>=0.
The substantive point is the full past history.

## 3. All past planes, including positive residuals
For even separation i-j=2q, q>=1, let z=alpha_j=alpha_i and y be the opposite amplitude. Formula(3) is the exact geometric sum
S_(j,i)=(T/a)(y-a z)(1-a^(2q)).
Substituting into(4) gives, at d=T-2,
(1-a^(2q)) z[-2z+(T/a)y]>=0
by(1), since z/y is either chi or1/chi.

For odd separation i-j=2q+1, q>=0, let z=alpha_j and y=alpha_i be the opposite amplitude. Now
S_(j,i)=(T/a)[y-a z+a^(2q)(a z-a^2 y)].
Substitution into(4), still at d=T-2, gives
F_infty(y,z)+a^(2q)[T z^2-2a yz],                       (5)
where
F_infty(y,z)=(T-2-kappa)y^2-(T-kappa)z^2+(T/a)yz.
The second term in(5) is nonnegative by(1).
Among the two choices(y,z)=(1,chi),(chi,1), the first has smaller F_infty: the difference is
2(T-1-kappa)(chi^2-1)>=0.
Its nonnegativity is precisely(2). This proves every old-plane comparison, at every lag, with the signed residual retained. Together with the future and zero-plane checks it proves the entire trajectory in Section1.

The exact sampled values are
f(X_i-u omega_i)=(T-u-1/2-kappa)alpha_i^2.
At a checkpoint query u=1, the nonsmooth proximal value is
J(X_i-2omega_i)=(T-2-kappa)alpha_i^2.                    (6)
It is strictly positive whenever kappa<T-2. Thus these checkpoints are not minimum resets.

## 4. Closest minimizer and payoff
The minimizer set of f is exactly
P_min={z:<omega_i,z><=kappa alpha_i^2 for every i}.
The point y_proj=kappa alpha_0 zeta_0 lies in P_min: for even i the amplitude equals alpha_0 and the correlation is at most1; for odd i the correlation is negative. Constraint0 is active, and
X_0-y_proj=(T-kappa)omega_0
is a positive multiple of its normal. For any z in P_min this gives
<X_0-y_proj,z-y_proj><=0,
so squared-distance expansion proves that y_proj is the unique closest minimizer and
dist(X_0,P_min)^2=(T-kappa)^2 alpha_0^2.
The normalized terminal value of this one instance is therefore exactly
2(T-kappa-1/2)alpha_m^2 / [(T-kappa)^2 alpha_0^2].        (7)
For even m, alpha_m=alpha_0 and this is
[2(T-kappa)-1]/(T-kappa)^2.
All smooth-convex interpolation inequalities, including the optimum sample, hold because all samples have been checked on this one explicit envelope.

## 5. Rational parameters, quadratic stability, and a strict failure of the old test
Choose
a=9/10, chi=6/5, T=23/10, kappa=1/10.
Condition(1) has positive margin
T-2a chi=7/50.
The left side of(2) is exactly37/375>0.
The alternating checkpoint sizes are
b_even=463/135, b_odd=131/30,
both in[3,5]. Therefore for m=2r and every integer r>=1 the length4r schedule
(1,463/135,1,131/30) repeated r times
has the explicitly realized normalized error
W_(4r)(h)>=85/121.                                     (8)
At every checkpoint its proximal value is alpha_i^2/5>0.

This model violates the earlier nonpositive-residual criterion. For any even j with j+2<=m,
S_(j,j+2)=(T/a)(1-a^2)(1-a chi)<0
because a chi=27/25>1. Thus
<Z_(j+2),zeta_j> >0,
and D_j>=a D_(j+1) is false at every such pair. Nevertheless the exact plane comparisons above hold. This is an explicit repair, not an assumption that local correlation checks suffice.

For comparison, each quadratic block multiplier is(1-lambda)(1-b_i lambda).
For0<=lambda<=1/5 it is nonnegative and at most exp(-lambda).
For1/5<=lambda<=1, its positive value is at most8/25, since b_i>=3; the magnitude of its negative minimum is at most4/5, since b_i<=5 and max_(b<=5,b>=3)(b-1)^2/(4b)=4/5.
Hence the full finite-dimensional quadratic normalized objective after m blocks is at most
max{1/(2 e m),(4/5)^(2m)} ->0.
The nonlinear persistent value is not a large quadratic product.

The omega_i are independent, adjacent ones have negative inner product, and their nonnegative-offset max-affine system has isolated zero/plane hinges. At such hinges the envelope has rank-one Hessian projectors onto omega_i. Adjacent projectors do not commute, proving that this function is nonseparable in every fixed orthonormal basis. Independence permits exposing each hinge by solving for one affine value0 and all others strictly negative. The dimension m+1 grows with the horizon and the gradient energies alternate between36/25 and1.

## 6. Scope
This is a parameterized, fully signed-history construction with positive checkpoint values and a concrete rational periodic test outside the earlier residual-sign interface. It does not claim that(1)--(2), or a generalization of them, can realize an arbitrary schedule at the benchmark profile. The endpoint values of the exact all-past comparison now show where positive residuals can be paid for by real face margins and offsets. A future extension must solve those inequalities quantitatively for nonperiodic data, rather than imposing S>=0 again or assuming feasibility at target strength.

## 7. Uniform survival of one arbitrary final step
For the rational parameters in Section5, let m be even and m>=32. Append ANY prescribed finite nonnegative step t after the2m-step periodic prefix. The same one fixed function above gives
W_(2m+1)(h,t) >= (245/19008)^2 >1/10000,                 (9)
uniformly in t and m.
This uses actual old planes and does not assume a monotone terminal objective.

Write L_j(z)=<omega_j,z>-kappa alpha_j^2 for the affine pieces of J and set c_tail=a^m. Since m is even, alpha_m=alpha_0=6/5. At the endpoint X_m, the exact residual sums from Section3 give
L_0(X_m)=38/375+(46/15)c_tail,
L_(m-1)(X_m)=-19/6.
The directional slopes along omega_m are
<omega_0,omega_m>=(36/25)c_tail,
<omega_(m-1),omega_m>=-27/25.
For clarity, the first value follows from
S_(0,m)=-(46/225)(1-c_tail),
<Z_m,omega_0>=(92/375)(1-c_tail),
<omega_m,omega_0>=(36/25)c_tail,
and X_m=Z_m+T omega_m. The second follows directly from the preceding block update.

Define
lambda_tail=3/(3+4c_tail),
w_tail=lambda_tail omega_0+(1-lambda_tail)omega_(m-1),
eta_tail=lambda_tail kappa alpha_0^2+(1-lambda_tail)kappa alpha_(m-1)^2.
The affine combination L_tail=lambda_tail L_0+(1-lambda_tail)L_(m-1) has zero slope along omega_m, since
lambda_tail(36/25)c_tail-(1-lambda_tail)(27/25)=0.
Thus, for EVERY real t,
L_tail(X_m-t omega_m)
=[38/125-(52/15)c_tail]/(3+4c_tail).                     (10)

For m>=32, c_tail<=1/20. Indeed a^8<9/20 and(9/20)^4<1/20. Consequently the numerator in(10) is at least49/375 and its denominator is at most16/5, so
L_tail(X_m-t omega_m)>=49/1200=:d_tail.
Moreover convexity of the squared norm gives
||w_tail||^2<=lambda_tail alpha_0^2+(1-lambda_tail)alpha_(m-1)^2<=36/25=:C_tail.

Here is the envelope lower bound without an external formula. Since J is at least both0 and L_tail, it is at least theta_tail L_tail for any theta_tail in[0,1]. Completing the square in its Moreau minimization gives, at x=X_m-t omega_m,
f(x)>=theta_tail L_tail(x)-theta_tail^2||w_tail||^2/2.
Take theta_tail=d_tail/C_tail=49/1728<1. Then
2f(x)>=d_tail^2/C_tail.
The initial squared distance to the exact nearest minimizer, from Section4, is4356/625. Division yields
2f(x)/(4356/625)
 >=[(49/1200)/( (6/5)(66/25) )]^2
 =(245/19008)^2>1/10000.
Because grad f(X_m)=omega_m was proved above, x=X_m-t omega_m is exactly the result of the appended GD step. This proves(9), including t=0 and arbitrarily large finite t.

The construction is therefore robust to any one-step terminal repair of this periodic prefix. A general arbitrary-length suffix is not covered by this argument: after the first appended step its gradient can change, so the cancellation of one fixed direction cannot be reused without a new proof.

evidence:
# Exact retained storage from a two-step primitive block

Status: unverified research identities. No new verifier or numerical PEP call has been used. These formulas do not yet certify an asymptotic improvement.

All functions below are convex and differentiable with 1-Lipschitz gradient. Write

    Q_ij = f_i-f_j + <g_i,x_j-x_i> + ||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <= 0.

## 1. Primitive dual residual, with the actual interpolation coefficients

For a GD block of nonnegative physical steps h, let S=sum h_i, A=S+1, d=x_0-x_n, p=g_0 and q=g_n. Define its saturated primitive energy

    V = 2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)
        + sum_(i<n) h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2 - S A ||q||^2.

The identity below is algebraic for every block; the primitive assumption is V>=0. Put

    H = 2(f_0-f_n)-2S||q||^2-||p-(d+q)/A||^2,
    A_start = -2[sum_(i<n) h_i Q_(i,0)+Q_(n,0)],
    A_end   = -2 sum_(i<n) h_i Q_(i,n).

Then

    H = (2A-1)/A^2 V + A_start/A + (A-1)/A^2 A_end.       (1)

In particular H>=0 for an actual primitive block. This follows without importing a quadratic-product condition or identifying the ambient primitive and s-composable classes.

For a direct check, put Z=d+q and use proof weights (h,1). Their intrinsic energy is V+A(A-1)||q||^2. Expanding the two interpolation sums gives

    A_start = 2A(f_0-f_n)-V-A(A-1)||q||^2
              -||Z||^2+2<Z,p>-A||p||^2,
    A_end = -V+||Z||^2-A^2||q||^2.

Substituting proves (1). This is the exact identity obtained before the optimum interpolation is added in Grimmer--Shu--Wang, arXiv:2410.16249, Appendix A.1, Lemma17. That proof was read, including its definitions and Proposition6 input; the calculation here checks applicability to the present V definition.

## 2. The pair (3/2,3/2) has a sharp nonzero boundary remainder

For this specific two-step block let p=g_0, m=g_1, q=g_2. Its displacement is d=(3/2)(p+m), and S=3, A=4. Define the retained displacement error

    t=d-3q=(3/2)(p+m-2q).

The exact certificate is

    V = 4(-Q_10)+9(-Q_12)+16(-Q_21)+(-Q_02)
        + ||t||^2/9.                                (2)

All coefficients are nonnegative. Expanding each Q verifies the function coefficients (3,3,-6), gradient diagonal coefficients (-3/4,-3/4,-12), and zero off-diagonal coefficients after adding the displayed square. Thus

    V >= ||d-3q||^2/9.                               (3)

The coefficient 1/9 is sharp over all legal functions. Take the one-dimensional function with derivative g(x)=x for x<=1 and g(x)=1 for x>=1, normalized by f(0)=0. It is convex, 1-smooth, and minimized at zero. Starting at x_0=5/2 gives x_1=1, x_2=-1/2, gradients (1,1,-1/2), and values (2,1/2,1/8). Therefore V=9/4 and t=9/2, giving V=||t||^2/9.

This is a new retained term, not merely a second naming of the objective residual. It vanishes on both the flat-gradient and full-curvature equality trajectories, but need not vanish on a general trajectory.

## 3. Objective and dual slacks are correlated

For the same pair, set r=p-(d+q)/4 and H=2(f_0-f_2)-6||q||^2-||r||^2. Equation (1) becomes

    H = (7/16)V + (3/4)(-Q_10)+(1/2)(-Q_20)
                    +(9/16)(-Q_02)+(9/16)(-Q_12).   (4)

There is also the exact reverse-side combination

    V-(4/5)H
      = (2/5)(-Q_01)+(9/5)(-Q_10)+(26/5)(-Q_12)
          +(48/5)(-Q_21)+||t||^2/36.                (5)

Thus this actual block supplies both H>=0 and

    V >= (4/5)H + ||t||^2/36.                        (6)

Unlike separate assumed squared penalties, (5) preserves a concrete correlation between the objective energy and the dual slack. Every actual interpolation multiplier is displayed; no negative interpolation inequality is used.

Equivalently, with Delta=f_0-f_2 and boundary vector (p,d,q),

    V-(8/5)Delta >= (p,d,q)^T J (p,d,q),

    J = [ -4/5    1/5     1/5  ]
        [  1/5   -1/45   -2/15 ]
        [  1/5   -2/15   -23/5 ].                   (7)

Here the matrix is an inherited storage term and is not asserted PSD. Discarding it or resetting its displacement coordinate at a later join would be invalid. The same clipped-quadratic example in part2 attains (5) at equality: H=135/64, V=9/4 and t^2/36=9/16.

For checking (2) and (5), the following one-parameter coefficient identity is useful. For any real kappa,

    V = (1-4kappa)(-Q_01)+(1/2+2kappa)(-Q_02)
        +(7/2+2kappa)(-Q_10)+(17/2+2kappa)(-Q_12)
        +(1-4kappa)(-Q_20)+(14+8kappa)(-Q_21)
        + kappa ||p+m-2q||^2.                       (8)

Equation (2) uses kappa=1/4. Combining (8) with (4), using kappa=5/52 in the factor (13/20)V, proves (5). This was checked by a fixed nine-equation rational coefficient calculation, not by an optimization or numerical search.

## 4. Calibration also recovers the full dominant recursion

The existing exact join in max4_two_sided_residual_join.md recovers ConPP. Its ordinary ConPD specialization does not require an independent tail residual penalty.

Let the prefix be genuinely primitive with capacity K, energy V_a and weights (a,K), so D_a=2K-1 and e_a=K g. Let the tail have arbitrary nonnegative intrinsic proof weights v, mass D_b>0 and energy E_b>=0. Define

    beta=(1+sqrt(1+8K/D_b))/2,
    c=2K/D_b=beta^2-beta,
    tau=1+K/beta.

Keep the prefix physical weights, change its terminal weight from K to K+1, and scale every tail weight by beta. Its new mass is

    D_new=2K+beta D_b=beta^2 D_b=G(K,D_b).

For A_y=-2 sum_(i in tail) v_i Q_(i,y), where y is the bridge start, direct expansion gives

    E_new=V_a+beta^2 E_b+c A_y.                       (9)

Indeed the general join has eta=1, gamma=0, m=t_y=t_z=0; its quadratic remainder has coefficients -2K+cD_b=0 on g^2, beta(1-beta)+c=0 on U_b^2, and beta(tau-1-K)+c(tau-1)=0 on <g,U_b>. All actual weights and interpolation coefficients are nonnegative. The standard squared-distance identity therefore gives W<=1/D_new.

Consequently the exact boundary interface recovers both scalar F and G operations and hence every finite-horizon DP denominator B_n, not merely a dyadic exponent or a rate with a fixed asymptotic loss. Equations (2)--(7) are extra block information; their profitable propagation is the outstanding construction task.

## 5. Terminal-storage literature: a precise finite reduction

Scherer, arXiv:2207.01363, Theorem5.1 in the HTML numbering (Theorem11 in the main-agent PDF pointer), equations30--35 and AppendixA.5, reduces its finite terminal-cost expression to a doubly hyperdominant matrix M: off-diagonal entries are nonpositive and all row and column sums are nonnegative. Its filter is initialized at zero. The proof and the conjecture in Section7 were read; no completeness conjecture or nonzero-initial-state extension is used here.

The connection to the project's actual interpolation cone can be checked directly. For samples including a minimizer, translate x_star=0 and f_star=0 and set

    z_i=x_i-g_i, F_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.

Then Q_ij=F_i-F_j+<g_i,z_j-z_i>. For a doubly hyperdominant M on the non-optimum samples define weights

    a_ij=-M_ij (i!=j),
    a_i,star=sum_j M_ij,
    a_star,i=sum_j M_ji.

All weights are nonnegative. Their incoming and outgoing masses agree at every vertex, including the optimum. Thus the F coefficients cancel, and exactly

    sum_(i,j) a_ij(-Q_ij)=sum_(i,j) M_ij<g_i,z_j>.   (10)

The finite hyperdominant terminal form therefore gives an actual combination of the existing smooth-convex interpolation inequalities. It is a potentially useful parametrization of retained correlations, not an additional nonlinear premise. Equation (10) says nothing about completeness of the five-variable join or of any finite memory compression.

At a split, a one-step memory example already shows what must be retained:

    sum_(i=m)^n <g_i,z_i-z_(i-1)> -(F_n-F_(m-1))
      =sum_(i=m)^n (-Q_(i,i-1)) >=0.                (11)

Both z_(m-1) and F_(m-1) are inherited. Replacing them by zero at an internal join changes the identity. For this project, the concrete new candidate storage is (7), with the displacement and both endpoint gradients retained, rather than a bare appeal to a stability theorem.

## Current boundary

There is still no closed improving family. The next direct attempt is to transport the actual pair storage through more than one bridge while permitting an indefinite intermediate storage matrix, and to require a valid nonnegative final certificate in the original objective normalization. All intermediate identities in this note remain unverified; they must be supplied in full in any eventual verification package.

# Complete-certificate obstruction to the unchanged remote-edge extension

Status: UNVERIFIED exact counterexample. This refutes one specified extension
of the suffix transport, not the existence of some descent and not Huber
tightness at global minimizers. It directly addresses TASK.md's unrestricted
two-step-suffix test.

## 1. A complete tight certificate

Take n=3, L=1, h=(2,9/4,3), q=25/4, and zeta=sqrt(78)/5.
Use Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2, with
x_star=g_star=f_star=0. All unspecified multipliers below are zero:

mu_0=lambda_(0,star)=25/2+5sqrt(78)/8,
mu_1=lambda_(1,star)=5sqrt(78)/8,
nu_0=lambda_(star,0)=5sqrt(78)/4+1,
nu_1=lambda_(star,1)=9/2,
nu_2=lambda_(star,2)=5,

lambda_10=25/2-5sqrt(78)/8,
lambda_21=8, lambda_32=2,
lambda_02=5, lambda_20=4.                            (1)

All are nonnegative; lambda_10>0 because sqrt(78)<9.
The finite flow equations can be checked explicitly:
at0, out=in=35/2+5sqrt(78)/8;
at1, out=in=25/2;
at2, out=in=12;
at3, out-in=2.

For independent formal vectors (x_0,g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3), define

R0=x_0-g_0,
U=g_0+g_1,
V=g_2+(5/4)g_1,
Z=g_3+2g_2.

The FULL matrix has the exact sum-of-squares representation

M=q||x_0||^2-2f_3+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
 =(25/4)||R0-(sqrt(78)/20)U||^2
   +(1/32)||U-16V||^2+||Z||^2.                     (2)

Here GD substitution and the displayed flows cancel every f coefficient.
Thus this is a full PSD certificate, with no omitted prefix or remote entry.

A short derivation of (2) also checks every coefficient. At the first step2,
the multiplier set
mu_0=2+zeta/2, mu_1=zeta/2, nu_0=zeta,
lambda_10=2-zeta/2
gives the identity
||x_0||^2-2f_1+sum lambda Q
 =||R0||^2-(zeta/2)<R0,U>+||U||^2.
Multiply it by25/4. For a step of length1+r, r>=1, direct expansion gives

2r^2 f_i-2f_(i+1)+2Q_(i+1,i)+2(r^2-1)Q_(star,i)
 =||r g_i+g_(i+1)||^2.

Add four times this identity with i=1,r=5/4 and once with i=2,r=2.
This gives a base certificate with the same q and the same multipliers
as (1), except lambda_02=lambda_20=0, nu_0=5sqrt(78)/4,
and nu_2=6. Its slack is

M_base=(25/4)[||R0||^2-(zeta/2)<R0,U>+||U||^2]
        +4||V||^2+||Z||^2.                         (3)

Finally add the exact zero-flow multiplier change
5Q_02+4Q_20+Q_(star,0)-Q_(star,2).
Its quadratic form is
-5||U||^2-<U,V>+4||V||^2.
Combining with (3), and using
(25/4)(1-zeta^2/16)=161/32, gives (2).

The certificate is TIGHT on the globally legal one-dimensional function
f(x)=x^2/2, with x_0=1. Its GD data are

(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)=(1,-1,5/4,-5/2),
(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)=(1,-1,5/4,-5/2),
(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)=(1/2,1/2,25/32,25/8).

Every Q_ij, including star pairs, is zero on these data, (2) vanishes,
and 2f_3=q. Thus W_3(h)=25/4. This is a complete legal matching
primal, not merely a PSD principal block.

The selected star multiplier is nu_(n-2)=nu_1=9/2>0.
There is a genuine remote prefix-to-suffix edge lambda_02=5.

## 2. The precise extension being refuted

Apply the previously valid c_2=0 two-step transport to k=1 while
leaving the remote edge unchanged. In this certificate,

c_1=mu_2+lambda_20+lambda_21=12,
c_2=mu_3+lambda_30+lambda_31=0,
c_3=lambda_32=2.

For any 0<eta<=9/2, the proposed extension changes

h'_1=(27+eta)/(12+eta),    h'_0=2, h'_2=3,
lambda'_21=8+eta,
nu'_1=9/2-eta, nu'_2=5+eta,                          (4)

and leaves every other multiplier and q unchanged. All steps and
multipliers remain nonnegative, and every flow equation remains exact.
Thus the only issue is the full PSD condition.

Direct expansion gives

M_new-M
 =eta||g_2||^2
   +[25 eta/(4(12+eta))]<g_0,g_1>.                  (5)

The second term is the previously absent remote cut contribution
(h_1-h'_1)lambda_02<g_0,g_1>. It cannot be discarded.

## 3. Exact negative direction in the OLD full kernel

Use one-dimensional formal vectors with

g_0=47/40,  g_1=-7/40,  g_2=9/32,  g_3=-9/16,
x_0=47/40+sqrt(78)/20.                              (6)

These need not be a legal new primal: they are a legitimate test of
PSD, which is required on ALL formal vectors.

Here U=1, V=1/16, Z=0, and R0=sqrt(78)/20.
Consequently the OLD FULL slack (2) is exactly zero.
On (6), equation(5) is exactly

M_new=eta(81 eta-344)/[1024(12+eta)].                (7)

It is negative for every 0<eta<344/81. In particular eta=1 is allowed
by (4), all actual multipliers remain nonnegative, but
M_new=-263/13312<0. There is therefore no sufficiently small positive
move of this unchanged transport that preserves PSD.

On the actual matching quadratic data from Section1, in contrast,
(5)/eta is 25/16-25/[4(12+eta)]>0. Thus checking only the
matching primal would falsely suggest a gain. The second full-kernel
direction is essential.

## 4. Scope and a different successful action on this example

This is NOT a stationary tuple and NOT a globally optimal schedule.
It does not refute some other simultaneous descent. Indeed one exists
with a different certificate re-selection.

First continuously undo the last zero-flow adjustment in Section1,
moving from (1) to its base certificate (3) at the SAME h,q.
Every intermediate actual multiplier is nonnegative, and every
intermediate slack is a convex combination of the PSD matrices (2)
and (3). The same legal quadratic remains matching throughout.
The base slack (3) has no extra kernel beyond that quadratic direction,
because zeta^2/16=39/200<1.

Now use the schedule h'=(2,28/13,3), corresponding to eta=1 in (4).
An explicit full certificate with value q'=900/169<25/4 is obtained
by keeping the first-step multiplier pattern
(mu_0,mu_1,nu_0,lambda_10)
=(2+zeta/2,zeta/2,zeta,2-zeta/2),
multiplying it by q'=4(15/13)^2, and then adding the two
function-growth identities from Section1:
four times the i=1 identity with r=15/13, and once the i=2
identity with r=2.

Its slack is

q'[||R0||^2-(zeta/2)<R0,U>+||U||^2]
 +4||(15/13)g_1+g_2||^2+||2g_2+g_3||^2 >=0,

all multiplier signs hold since15/13>1 and zeta<4, and its
function-value flow is exactly2e_3. The quadratic again attains q'.
This is a real fixed-length improvement for this example.

The obstruction therefore distinguishes two mechanisms:
the same sparse transport can fail at an unnecessarily degenerate
optimal dual certificate, whereas reselecting the dual certificate
inside the fixed-h optimum face can make a different descent available.
No theorem is claimed that such re-selection removes remote edges
for every schedule, nor that the maximal-rank dual face always has
the needed kernel structure.

Next action: analyze certificate re-selection together with the
inactive-interpolation costs before attempting a universal descent.
Do not add a remote-edge-absence hypothesis and call the original
extension repaired. The eventual exact-profile mass-cap issue remains
separate even if global Huber tightness were established.

## 5. A continuous repair that RETAINS the remote edges

The same obstruction can be repaired by a different, explicit simultaneous
reweighting, without first setting the remote multipliers to zero.
This supplies a concrete alternative mechanism on this example only.

For 1<=r<=5/4, take h(r)=(2,1+r,3), q(r)=4r^2, retain
zeta=sqrt(78)/5, and set z(r)=64r^2/25. Choose

mu_0=4r^2(2+zeta/2),  mu_1=2r^2 zeta,
nu_0=4r^2 zeta+z(r)(r-1),
nu_1=8(r^2-1),        nu_2=6-z(r)(r-1),

lambda_10=4r^2(2-zeta/2),  lambda_21=8, lambda_32=2,
lambda_02=r z(r),          lambda_20=z(r).            (8)

All unlisted multipliers are zero. They are nonnegative throughout the
interval: z<=4, r-1<=1/4, so nu_2>=5; and zeta<4.
Direct substitution gives out-in=0 at0,1,2 and2 at3. At r=5/4
these are exactly (1), and both remote edges stay positive for
every r in the interval.

Use R0=x_0-g_0, U=g_0+g_1, V_r=g_2+r g_1, Z=g_3+2g_2.
The full slack is

M(r)=4r^2||R0-(zeta/4)U||^2+||Z||^2
     +A(r)||U||^2-(r-1)z(r)<U,V_r>+(4+z(r))||V_r||^2,

A(r)=r^2(161-128r)/50.                              (9)

To derive (9), scale the first-step identity by4r^2, use the two
function-growth identities with factors r and2, and add the
finite/star flow change corresponding to
C_02=r z/2, C_20=z/2.
Its quadratic contribution is
-z[r||U||^2+(r-1)<U,V_r>-||V_r||^2].
Completing the same first square yields (9).

The remaining two-by-two matrix in (U,V_r) has positive A(r), and
its determinant is exactly

r^2(5-4r)(512r^3+1664r^2+16r+3220)/1250 >=0.          (10)

Thus the FULL M(r) is PSD. It has a positive determinant in this
remaining block when r<5/4, so the extraneous kernel responsible
for (7) is removed. The legal quadratic f(x)=x^2/2 follows
(1,-1,r,-2r), satisfies every active interpolation equality, and
attains q(r)=4r^2. Consequently (8)--(10) give the exact identity

W_3(2,1+r,3)=4r^2  for 1<=r<=5/4.

In particular moving r downward from5/4 is a continuous strict
same-length descent starting from the original degenerate certificate,
with nonnegative flow and both remote finite edges retained.
The failed sparse update and this successful update start from the
SAME full certificate. Their difference is the simultaneous scaling
of the prefix-source coefficients and the remote weights (quadratic
and cubic in r), which changes the full kernel correctly.

This does not assert that a comparable homogeneous reweighting exists
for an arbitrary near-optimal schedule. It identifies a genuinely
different concrete mechanism from keeping prefix multipliers fixed.
