claim: Linear-length arbitrary-suffix protection on the SAME periodic prefix: a new growing-energy Markov Moreau function gives W_(2m+k)>=(5/198)^2 for every suffix of k arbitrary nonnegative finite steps with k L_prop<=m-2600. Explicit old affine guards force bounded backward propagation of active gradient indices.
evidence:
# Correlated Moreau relay surviving arbitrary suffixes of linear length
Status: complete new constructive candidate, UNVERIFIED. No additional verifier call.
This responds to the fixed-witness two-step failure50b0bb4cd67cac9f and the quantifier reminder d7b99ad37dff6ae5. The adversary is replaced by a different correlated function on the SAME periodic prefix. The stronger uniform suffix property is proved below, not imposed as a requirement on all adversaries.

## 1. Precise statement
Fix rational constants
a_0=9/10, q=10001/10000, a=a_0 q,
theta=a q=a_0 q^2,
chi=6/5, T=23/10, kappa=1/10.
Define the integer
L_prop=1+ceil(max{log(2400)/(2log q), log(9600)/log(10/9)}).   (1)
Let m>=2600 be even. Take the2m-step prefix
h_pre=(1,463/135,1,131/30) repeated m/2 times.
Let k>=0 satisfy
k L_prop<=m-2600,
and append ANY prescribed finite nonnegative suffix(t_1,...,t_k).
There is one explicitly defined convex differentiable1-smooth function in R^(m+1), already fixed by m, which gives
W_(2m+k)(h_pre,t_1,...,t_k)>=(5/198)^2=25/39204.            (2)
Thus even arbitrary and unbounded suffix entries cannot repair this prefix within the stated linear number of steps. All constants are absolute and the threshold is independent of the suffix.
This is a restricted schedule theorem, not the unrestricted exact-profile target.

The fixed function used here differs from the one annihilated in50b0bb4cd67cac9f. Its gradient amplitudes grow by q and its negative correlation changes from-a_0 to-a=-a_0 q, leaving the actual prefix steps unchanged.

## 2. Explicit function and prefix data
In R^(m+1) construct
zeta_0=e_0,
zeta_(i+1)=-a zeta_i+sqrt(1-a^2)e_(i+1).
Put v_i=chi at even i and v_i=1 at odd i,
alpha_i=q^i v_i, omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i,
E_i=alpha_i^2,
L_i(x)=<omega_i,x>-kappa E_i,
J(x)=max{0,L_0(x),...,L_m(x)},
f(x)=min_z{J(z)+||x-z||^2/2}.
This gives one finite max-affine function with explicit nonnegative offsets and an explicitly real PSD Gram matrix
<omega_i,omega_j>=alpha_i alpha_j(-a)^|i-j|.
The vectors omega_i are independent.

The envelope is globally convex differentiable1-smooth: its unique proximal minimizer exists by the quadratic term, the optimality equation gives grad f(x)=x-prox_J(x), and subgradient monotonicity gives
||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||^2<=<grad f(x)-grad f(y),x-y>.
Its minimum is0 and its minimizer set is
P_min={x:L_i(x)<=0 for all i}.
For every x, its gradient belongs to conv{0,omega_0,...,omega_m}; more precisely it is a convex combination of normals active at prox_J(x).

Start at X_0=T omega_0. Set
b_i=T-1+(T/a)alpha_(i+1)/alpha_i
    =T-1+(T/a_0)v_(i+1)/v_i.
These are exactly463/135 at even i and131/30 at odd i, because the q factors cancel.
Define X_(i+1)=X_i-(1+b_i)omega_i. We now prove that these are the actual block starts, with both block-i queries having gradient omega_i.

## 3. Complete legality check of the prefix
Let Z_i=X_i-T omega_i,
B_i=(T/a)alpha_(i+1), D_i=B_i(1-a^2).
Then
Z_0=0, Z_(i+1)=Z_i-B_i(zeta_i+a zeta_(i+1)).
Taking inner products gives
<Z_i,zeta_j>=0 for j>=i,
<Z_i,zeta_j>=-S_(j,i) for j<i,
S_(j,i)=sum_(l=j)^(i-1)D_l(-a)^(l-j).                    (3)

Write delta=T-2=3/10 and Lambda=(T/a)(1-a^2)q.
The following exact rational inequalities hold:
4/5<theta^2<13/16,
theta chi-1<13/160,
Lambda<=437/900<39/80.
For the first two use9/10<theta<901/1000. For the third,
Lambda=(T/a_0)(1-a_0^2 q^2)<(T/a_0)(1-a_0^2)=437/900.
Define
S_floor=Lambda(1-theta chi)/(1-theta^2)<0.
Then
|S_floor|<(39/80)(13/160)/(3/16)=169/800.                 (4)

At a query X_i-u omega_i,u=0 or1, the proposed proximal point is
Z_i+d omega_i,d=T-u-1>=delta.
The terminal query X_m has d=T-1 and is also covered.
The current plane has value(d-kappa)E_i>=E_i/5>0.
For j<i, its deficit above plane j is
d alpha_i(alpha_i-C_ij alpha_j)+alpha_j S_(j,i)
 -kappa E_i+kappa E_j, C_ij=(-a)^(i-j);                  (5)
future indices use the same expression with S=0.

The coefficient of d is positive. At even separation, for a past j the ratio C_ij alpha_j/alpha_i is at most a_0^2 chi<1, and for a future j it is at most theta^2 chi<39/40. At odd separation C_ij<0. Hence d=delta is the worst endpoint.

Future comparisons at even separation are positive definite quadratic forms:
(delta-kappa)alpha_i^2+kappa alpha_j^2-delta C_ij alpha_i alpha_j>0,
since delta^2 C_ij^2<=delta^2 a^4<(9/100)(13/16)^2<4kappa(delta-kappa).
At odd separation all three displayed terms have nonnegative signs.

For the past, put ell=i-j and normalize the deficit by q^(2j). Write z=q^ell v_i>=1 and y=v_j in[1,chi]. Finite geometric sums, using v in[1,chi], give
S_(j,i)/q^j>=S_floor(1-theta^ell) if ell is even,
S_(j,i)/q^j>=S_floor if ell is odd.                       (6)
For odd ell, the cross term is positive, so the deficit is at least
(delta-kappa)z^2+kappa y^2+S_floor y
 >=3/10-(169/800)(6/5)=93/2000>0.
For even ell, the expression
(delta-kappa)z^2-delta a^ell z y
increases with z>=1. Replace z by v_i, and then replace a^ell by the larger theta^ell. The resulting lower bound is
F=(delta-kappa)v_i^2+kappa y^2
 -delta w v_i y+S_floor(1-w)y, w=theta^ell in[0,theta^2].
It is affine in w. At w=0 the preceding93/2000 bound applies. At w=theta^2 it increases with v_i and decreases with y on[1,chi], since
2/5-(3/10)(13/16)(6/5)>0,
and
6/25-(3/10)(4/5)=0
while the omitted S_floor term is strictly negative.
Its minimum is at v_i=1,y=chi and exceeds
43/125-(3/10)(13/16)(6/5)-(39/80)(13/160)(6/5)
=127/32000>0.
Thus all old, future and zero planes are controlled. The active-plane subgradient equation proves every prescribed gradient and the entire prefix.

This verification uses the signed sums themselves. They can be negative; no nonpositive-residual hypothesis is substituted.

The initial closest minimizer is y_star=kappa omega_0. For even j,
<omega_j,y_star>/ (kappa E_j)=(a/q)^j=a_0^j<=1,
and odd inner products are negative. Thus y_star belongs to P_min. Constraint0 is active and
X_0-y_star=(T-kappa)omega_0
is its positive normal. Squared-distance expansion proves that y_star is closest. Its squared distance is
(T-kappa)^2 E_0=(11/5)^2(6/5)^2=4356/625.                (7)

## 4. Exact endpoint affine values
Put
B_even=S_floor/chi,
B_odd=Lambda(chi-theta)/(1-theta^2),
A_even=-B_even-kappa,
A_odd=-B_odd-kappa,
C_end=T+B_even.
For even m, equation(3) gives at X_m:
L_j(X_m)/E_j=A_even+C_end theta^(m-j) if j is even,
L_j(X_m)/E_j=A_odd-chi C_end theta^(m-j) if j is odd.     (8)
These are obtained by summing the two-period geometric series; for an even j,
S_(j,m)/alpha_j=B_even(1-theta^(m-j)),
while an odd j has
S_(j,m)/alpha_j=B_odd+chi B_even theta^(m-j).

We need the following uniform bounds:
A_even>=19/270, |A_even|<1, |A_odd|<=22/25<1.             (9)
The last two follow from(4) and
B_odd<(39/80)(3/10)/(3/16)=39/50.
For the first, put z=q^2. Direct algebra gives
B_even(q)-B_even(1)
=(T/chi)(z-1)(a_0 z-chi)/(1-a_0^2 z^2)<=0,
because a_0z=theta<chi.
At q=1, B_even(1)=-23/135, so A_even>=23/135-1/10=19/270.

## 5. Affine guards annihilating every later direction
Fix an even index j with j+51<=m. Let
r_guard=chi a_0^51,
lambda_guard=1/(1+r_guard),
w_j=lambda_guard omega_j+(1-lambda_guard)omega_(j+51),
G_j=lambda_guard L_j+(1-lambda_guard)L_(j+51).
Then G_j is an affine lower bound for J.
The normal w_j is orthogonal to EVERY omega_l with l>=j+51:
the Markov products cancel because51 is odd and
(1-lambda_guard)alpha_(j+51)=lambda_guard alpha_j a^51.

Equation(8) therefore gives, with all decaying endpoint terms cancelling,
G_j(X_m)=q^(2j) d_guard,
d_guard=[chi^2 A_even-chi theta^51(B_odd+kappa)]/
        [1+chi a_0^51].                                (10)
Now theta^51<1/100: theta<1-99/1000 gives theta^51<exp(-5), while the degree6 Taylor sum for exp(5) exceeds100. Also a_0^51<1/100 and q^51<chi; for the latter,
q^51<=(1-51/10000)^(-1)<6/5,
using the binomial bound by the geometric series.
Consequently
d_guard>=[38/375-132/12500]/(253/250)
=1702/18975>2/25.                                      (11)
The guard normal has ||w_j||^2<=E_j, since both constituent normals have norm at most alpha_j (q^51<chi).

For later use, its inner products obey the explicit bounds
|<w_j,omega_l>|<=E_j a_0^(j-l) for l<j,
|<w_j,omega_l>|<=E_j theta^(l-j) for j<=l<j+51,
<w_j,omega_l>=0 for l>=j+51.                            (12)
To check the middle formula before taking absolute values, it is
lambda_guard alpha_j alpha_l(-a)^(l-j)
 [1-a^(2(j+51-l))].
For l<j replace that last factor by1-a^102 and use the corresponding Markov product. The amplitude factors then give (12).

## 6. A uniform lower bound on the proximal value after any late-direction perturbation
For r>=2600, let
V_r=span{omega_i:r<=i<=m}.
Take ANY x in X_m+V_r, with no bound on the coefficients of its displacement. Put g=grad f(x), z=x-g=prox_J(x).

Choose the largest even J_0 with J_0+51<=r. Take50 guards with starts
J_0, J_0-52,...,J_0-52*49.
All starts are nonnegative because r>=2600, and each guard is constant on X_m+V_r by its orthogonality. Let E_top=chi^2 q^(2J_0).
Their energies are at least(12/25)E_top, because
q^(-5096)>=1-5096/10000>12/25.
By(10)--(11), each guard value at x is at least E_j/18. Hence their average value is at least(2/75)E_top.

For any one normal omega_l, (12) bounds the sum of the50 absolute guard inner products by(100/99)E_top. Here is a direct justification of the uniform sum bound. The starts are52 apart, every guard to the left of l by at least51 contributes0, and at most one interval can contain l. At position d in[0,51] within that interval the remaining geometric bound is
theta^d+a_0^(52-d)/(1-a_0^52).
This is a convex function of d, so its maximum is at an endpoint. At d=0 it is1/(1-a_0^52)<100/99; at d=51 it is less than1/100+(9/10)/(1-1/100)<100/99. Before all intervals the single geometric-series bound is also<100/99.
Because g belongs to conv{0,omega_0,...,omega_m}, the average guard normal has inner product with g at most(2/99)E_top.

Since J(z) is at least the average guard value at z=x-g, we obtain
J(prox_J(x))>= (2/75-2/99)E_top=(16/2475)E_top.
Also r-J_0<=52 and q^(-104)>49/50, so
E_top>=(49/50)chi^2 q^(2r).
In particular
J(prox_J(x))> chi^2 q^(2r)/200.                         (13)
This holds for every x in the whole affine space X_m+V_r, independently of its displacement size. It is the key difference from a merely local covariance check.

## 7. Bounded backward propagation of active indices
Let E_r^ref=chi^2 q^(2r). For j<r, the Markov structure and(8) imply that at x in X_m+V_r there is one real scalar Q_x such that
L_j(x)/E_j=A_even+(chi/v_j)Q_x theta^(r-j) for even j,
L_j(x)/E_j=A_odd-(chi/v_j)Q_x theta^(r-j) for odd j.       (14)
For completeness one may take
Q_x=C_end theta^(m-r)+
    (-1)^r <zeta_r,x-X_m>/(chi q^r).
For j<r the inner product with any later normal factors through zeta_r, giving(14).

For ANY gradient g=grad f(x), the full Gram matrix gives
|<omega_j,g>|<=chi E_j,
because |<omega_j,omega_l>|/E_j is at most
chi theta^(l-j) for l>=j or chi a_0^(j-l) for l<j.
Thus for ell=r-j>0,
L_j(prox_J(x))/E_r^ref
 <=3q^(-2ell)+chi |Q_x| a_0^ell.                       (15)

If |Q_x|<10, (13) is a lower bound E_r^ref/200 for the active level.
If |Q_x|>=10, choose j in{r-1,r-2} with even parity for Q_x>0 or odd parity for Q_x<0. Equations(9),(14) and the bound on <omega_j,g> give
L_j(prox_J(x))
 >=E_j[(4/5)|Q_x|-11/5]
 >=(|Q_x|/2)E_j
 >=(|Q_x|/4)E_r^ref,                                   (16)
where the last inequality uses q^(-4)/chi^2>1/2.

By the definition(1),
q^(-2L_prop)<1/2400, a_0^L_prop<1/9600.
For ell>=L_prop, (15) is therefore< E_r^ref/400 if |Q_x|<10. If |Q_x|>=10, its value divided by |Q_x| is< E_r^ref/4000. In either case it is strictly below the active level furnished by(13) or(16).
Therefore no plane with index j<=r-L_prop is active at prox_J(x). The zero plane is not active either by(13). We conclude
grad f(x) belongs to span{omega_i:i>=r-L_prop}
for every x in X_m+V_r and r>=2600.                    (17)

This is a proved restriction on actual gradients of the one global function. It retains all old planes; the index exclusion comes from comparing their values with a certified positive active level.

## 8. Arbitrary suffix and normalized lower bound
Run any prescribed finite suffix steps from X_m. After t suffix steps, induction using(17) shows
x^(t) belongs to X_m+V_(m-t L_prop)
as long as m-t L_prop>=2600. Indeed each update adds a scalar multiple of a gradient in the displayed larger span; the scalar can be arbitrarily large.

The guard G_0 uses normals0 and51, and is orthogonal to every omega_i with i>=51. Hence it remains CONSTANT throughout every allowed suffix, with value d_guard>=2/25. Its normal satisfies ||w_0||^2<=chi^2=36/25.
To transfer this affine lower bound through the envelope, note that J is at least both0 and G_0. For any lambda in[0,1], completing the square gives
f(x)>=lambda G_0(x)-lambda^2||w_0||^2/2.
Take lambda=(2/25)/(36/25)=1/18. At the terminal point this yields
2f(x)>= (2/25)^2/(36/25)=1/225.
Divide by the exact initial squared distance4356/625 from(7):
2f(x)/||X_0-y_star||^2 >=(1/225)/(4356/625)
=25/39204=(5/198)^2.
This proves(2) for every allowed suffix, including zero steps and arbitrarily large finite entries.

Independence of the omega_i and their nonzero adjacent correlations also show nonseparability: isolate each zero/plane hinge, whose envelope Hessian is the rank-one projector onto omega_i. Adjacent such projectors do not commute. Thus no fixed orthonormal coordinates separate the function.

The unrestricted problem is still open here. No assertion says an arbitrary near-optimal schedule contains this periodic prefix, or can be transformed to it without cost. The new reusable mechanism is the explicit affine guards and the finite backward propagation estimate(17), with all matrix, value, minimum and suffix conditions included.

# A genuine finite objective residual and its exact block transport

Status: unverified exact identities and a scoped limitation. No solver or verifier calls. The eleven-step rule with bridge factors(7/10,1,1/5) is closed by max3's explicit counterexample, which was read and matches the present primitive energy definition. None of the constructions below attempts to repair that rule.

Use smoothness1 and Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0. For nonnegative proof weights u on a GD block write

    D=sum u_i, d=x_start-x_end, U=sum u_i g_i, e=U-d,
    E=2sum u_i(f_i-f_end)+sum u_i||g_i||^2
       +2sum u_i<g_i,x_start-x_i>-||U||^2.

For any minimizer, direct expansion gives

    ||x_start-x_star||^2+2sum u_i Q_(i,star)-2D(f_end-f_star)
       =||x_end-x_star-e||^2+E.                      (1)

Thus E>=0 yields the original last-iterate bound W<=1/D.

## 1. A nonprimitive proof-weight state with no loss of Huber mass

The physical schedule is the pair(3/2,3/2). Write its three gradients as p,m,q, its displacement as d=(3/2)(p+m), and define

    t=d-3q, r=p-(d+q)/4.

For 0<epsilon<=1/64, choose actual proof weights

    u=(3/2-epsilon, 3/2, 4+epsilon).

Then D=7 and

    e=4q-epsilon(p-q), v=e-4q=-epsilon(r+t/4).       (2)

These are not the primitive weights(h,4), although the physical block is primitive. All three weights are positive. The exact interpolation identity is

    E=(21epsilon/2)(-Q_01)+(1-5epsilon/4)(-Q_02)
        +(4+29epsilon/4)(-Q_10)
        +(9+29epsilon/4)(-Q_12)+(16+4epsilon)(-Q_21)
        +(r,t)^T M_epsilon (r,t),                    (3)

where the full symmetric matrix is

    M_epsilon =
      [ 2epsilon-epsilon^2, -31epsilon/12-epsilon^2/4 ]
      [ -31epsilon/12-epsilon^2/4,
                         1/9+7epsilon/36-epsilon^2/16 ].

Every actual interpolation coefficient in (3) is nonnegative. Equation (3) follows either by expanding E and the five Q terms directly, or by the following retained-slack derivation, which also explains the cross term.

Let V be the pair's physical primitive energy and H=2(f_0-f_2)-6||q||^2-||r||^2. Define the adjacent cycle quantities C_01=-Q_01-Q_10 and C_12=-Q_12-Q_21. They satisfy

    C_01=3<q,r>-<q,t>/4-||r||^2
                         +(7/6)<r,t>-13||t||^2/144,
    C_12=-(3/2)<q,r>+(5/8)<q,t>+||r||^2/2
                         -(5/12)<r,t>+25||t||^2/288.

The correlated identity in max4_joint_boundary_storage.md gives, more generally,

    V-epsilon H
      =(epsilon/2)(-Q_01)+(1-5epsilon/4)(-Q_02)
        +(4-11epsilon/4)(-Q_10)
        +(9-19epsilon/4)(-Q_12)+(16-8epsilon)(-Q_21)
        +(16-15epsilon)||t||^2/144.                  (4)

This can be checked using the one-parameter primitive identity there with
kappa=(16-15epsilon)/(64-28epsilon), so that
(1-7epsilon/16)kappa=(16-15epsilon)/64.

The exact change from V to E has q-cross terms 12epsilon<q,r>+5epsilon<q,t>. The nonnegative combination 10epsilon C_01+12epsilon C_12 has exactly those same q-cross terms. Subtracting its quadratic expression, and adding it to the actual interpolation coefficients in (4), yields (3). This is why keeping only the two scalar slack bounds would have missed the finite objective state: the adjacent cycles supply the required correlations with q.

Set nu=1/(2epsilon). The matrix after subtracting nu||v||^2 from (3) is

    M_epsilon-(epsilon/2)(1,1/4)(1,1/4)^T.           (5)

Its first diagonal entry is (3/2)epsilon-epsilon^2>0, and its determinant is

    epsilon[1/6-(1037/144)epsilon-(29/18)epsilon^2]. (6)

For epsilon<=1/64 the bracket is at least1321/24576>0. Thus (5) is positive definite, proving the concrete finite residual certificate

    E >= nu ||e-4q||^2, D=7, nu=1/(2epsilon).        (7)

The mass7 is exactly the physical Huber mass2sum(h)+1. No limiting argument is used to make (7) valid: every indicated positive epsilon gives an actual finite certificate. The family has nu tending to infinity as the weights tend to the primitive weights.

## 2. A transport with a nonprimitive input and an inherited quadratic term

Let a prefix have nonnegative weights, D_a=2K-1 with K>=1, and the actual finite certificate

    E_a >= nu||e_a-Kg||^2, nu>0,

where g is the gradient at its endpoint y. The pair construction above provides K=4 and any nu=1/(2epsilon), epsilon<=1/64.

Take an arbitrary tail block, starting at y'=y-tau g and ending at z. Its own nonnegative weights v have mass D_b>0, gradient aggregate U_b, energy E_b>=0, start gradient p_b and final gradient q_b. The four vectors g,p_b,q_b,U_b remain distinct. Nothing below identifies the tail start gradient with the bridge gradient, or replaces its aggregate by an endpoint gradient.

Put

    sigma=1/(nu+1), k=1+1/nu, eta=1-sigma=1/k,
    c=(2K-sigma)/D_b,
    beta=(1+sqrt(1+4k c))/(2k),
    tau=1+K/(k beta).

Thus k beta^2=beta+c. Add eta to the prefix terminal proof weight and scale every tail weight by beta. All new proof weights are nonnegative and

    D_new=2K-sigma+beta D_b=k beta^2 D_b.             (8)

Write v_a=e_a-Kg. The actual tail-to-anchor interpolation sum is

    A_y=-2sum_(i in tail) v_i Q_(i,y)
       =2D_b(f_y-f_z)-E_b-||U_b||^2
          -2(tau-1)<U_b,g>-D_b||g||^2.              (9)

Expansion of the new intrinsic energy and substitution of (9) gives exactly

    E_new=(E_a-nu||v_a||^2)+(beta+c)E_b+c A_y
          +(1/nu)||nu v_a-eta g-beta U_b||^2
          +sigma(2K-1)||g||^2.                      (10)

This is a finite-horizon certificate with actual multipliers c v_i on -2Q_(i,y). It preserves the squared boundary quantity nu v_a-eta g-beta U_b; resetting it at a join is not part of the identity. The tail's p_b and q_b have zero explicit rows in the quadratic remainder because (9) has eliminated the full tail value sum exactly, not because those gradients were equated.

For completeness, the full nonzero boundary matrix in(v_a,g,U_b) is

    [ nu,       -eta,                         -beta          ]
    [ -eta, eta^2/nu+sigma(2K-1),          eta beta/nu       ]
    [ -beta,   eta beta/nu,                  beta^2/nu      ].

It is the sum of the outer product (nu,-eta,-beta)(nu,-eta,-beta)^T/nu and diag(0,sigma(2K-1),0), hence PSD in every Euclidean dimension. If the independent gradients p_b,q_b are added to the boundary vector, their rows and columns are zero. Equation (1) now gives W<=1/D_new for the actual concatenated physical schedule.

To verify (10) without trusting a completion of squares, the raw quadratic coefficients before subtracting the square are

    ||v_a||^2: nu,
    <v_a,g>: -2eta,       <v_a,U_b>: -2beta,
    ||g||^2: sigma(2K-sigma),
    ||U_b||^2: c+beta-beta^2=beta^2/nu,
    <g,U_b>: 2[beta(tau-eta-K)+c(tau-1)]
               =2eta beta/nu.

The g-diagonal remainder equals sigma(2K-1), using eta=nu/(nu+1).

## 3. Calibration succeeds, but this closed subrule cannot improve ConPD

For fixed K and D_b, as nu tends to infinity the parameters in part2 tend to the ordinary ConPD parameters and

    D_new -> G(K,D_b).

There is no fixed calibration loss forced by a finite nonprimitive input: the actual pair family in part1 supplies arbitrarily large finite nu while retaining D_a=7. If desired, nu may be selected separately for each prescribed horizon.

Nevertheless, the specific transport in part2 always gives strictly LESS mass than the ordinary ConPD join. Let b_0>0 solve b_0^2-b_0=2K/D_b, so G(K,D_b)=2K+b_0 D_b. Since k>1 and c=(2K-sigma)/D_b<2K/D_b, its positive root beta satisfies beta<b_0. Hence

    D_new=2K-sigma+beta D_b < G(K,D_b).               (11)

Thus (10) is an actual finite-residual propagation and calibration test, not an improving upper-bound rule. Repeating this inequality with no further correlations cannot certify a strict gain over the corresponding primitive-prefix G operations.

There is also a legal hard-instance explanation for the lack of a free local gain. For a prefix with physical sum K-1, one bridge tau=1+r, and a tail with physical sum T, the accepted one-cut fact b98bb807d514e80d gives

    W >= r^2/[K^2(2T+1)].

If a proposed certificate were Huber-tight with mass2(K+T+r)+1, it would have to satisfy

    r^2[2(K+T+r)+1] <= K^2(2T+1).                  (12)

When the tail's own mass is2T+1, ordinary ConPD meets this condition at equality. The affine prefix and tail portions of this witness have t=H=0 for every embedded pair. Consequently the retained pair terms cannot by themselves permit a larger Huber-tight single bridge. This statement concerns this binary setting and does not exclude coordinated multi-bridge certificates or nonsaturated objective weights.

## Current next step

The candidate storage is now an actual finite-weight state with a full PSD transport, rather than just a formal five-variable test. Its unchanged scalar subrule is quantitatively dominated by ConPD. Further work must use additional cross-block interpolation or the explicit inherited vector nu v_a-eta g-beta U_b to produce a different closed state; retuning the parameters in (10) cannot give the required strict improvement.

# Whole optimal-certificate set: quantitative terminal rigidity and a common barrier

Status: UNVERIFIED, self-contained candidate calculations. No new verifier
allocation is assumed. This is the bounded face-level output requested by the
updated TASK.md. It neither proves Huber tightness nor resolves the exact
Zhang--Jiang profile comparison.

## 1. Full setting and a matching stationary instance

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Fix a positive length-n schedule h,
n>=1, and q>0. For distinct sample indices i,j in {star,0,...,n}, use

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.

A full certificate has lambda_ij>=0, finite-node flow

    sum_j lambda_ij - sum_j lambda_ji = 2*1_(i=n),

and a PSD quadratic form after x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t:

    M_lambda=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
            =q||x_0||^2-<x_0,sum_i mu_i g_i>
                         +sum_(i,j) A_ij <g_i,g_j>,

where mu_i=lambda_(i,star). Let C(h,q) denote ALL such certificates. Its
gradient Schur complement is Z_lambda=A-mu mu^T/(4q)>=0.

Assume there is an ACTUAL legal convex 1-smooth function, normalized by
||x_0||=1, whose GD trajectory attains 2f_n=q. Suppose one certificate
lambda^0 in C(h,q) satisfies every stepsize stationarity equation

    D_t(lambda^0;g)=0, 0<=t<n,

where D_t is the derivative, with all formal vectors fixed, of M_lambda
with respect to h_t. This is a full matching stationary tuple hypothesis.
It does not assert that arbitrary fixed schedules or arbitrary matching
primals are stationary. A globally minimizing schedule to which the usual
full stationary interface applies satisfies this hypothesis.

Every lambda in C(h,q) matches THIS SAME actual instance: its quadratic
value is sum lambda_ij Q_ij<=0, and PSD makes it nonnegative. Consequently

    lambda_ij Q_ij=0 for all i,j,
    sum_i mu_i g_i=2q x_0,                         (1)
    Y Z_lambda=0,                                 (2)

where Y is the linear map from R^(n+1) to the ambient Euclidean space
defined by Y r=sum_i r_i g_i. To prove (1)--(2), complete the square:

    M_lambda=q||x_0-(sum_i mu_i g_i)/(2q)||^2
                    +sum_(i,j)(Z_lambda)_ij <g_i,g_j>.

Both summands are nonnegative and have sum zero. The second gives
Y Z_lambda^(1/2)=0, hence (2). No strict-complementarity assumption is made.

Write p=g_(n-1), g=g_n and b=h_(n-1)>0. Last-step stationarity implies

    <p,g>=0.                                      (3)

Here is a proof retaining the full matrix. Change only the final step by
a small signed u on the SAME actual function. Its terminal point changes
by -u p; its terminal gradient changes by O(u), and
f_n(u)=f_n-u<p,g>+O(u^2). Let v_u be the full formal-vector realization.
PSD and matching give M_lambda(v_0)=0 and M_lambda v_0=0, so
M_lambda(v_u)=O(u^2). Since the matrix is affine in the final step,

    q-2f_n(u)+sum lambda_ij Q_ij(u)
       =u D_(n-1)(lambda;g)+O(u^2).

Every Q_ij(u)<=0. Taking both signs of u proves

    D_(n-1)(lambda;g)=2<p,g>                      (4)

for EVERY lambda in C(h,q). Applying stationarity for lambda^0 gives (3).
Thus last-cut stationarity, unlike unproved earlier-cut stationarity,
survives re-selection with this same matching instance.

Define B_i=product_(t<i)(1+h_t), with B_0=1. Gradient Lipschitzness and
g_star=0 give ||x_i||,||g_i||<=B_i. Convexity and 2f_n=q give

    ||g||>=q/(2 B_n)>0,
    ||p||>=||g||/(1+b)>=q/[2B_n(1+b)].           (5)

The second inequality uses ||g-p||<=b||p||.

## 2. A quantitative invariant of the ENTIRE certificate set

Choose any reference certificate lambda^r in C(h,q), with source mu^r, and put

    L_face=span( {range Z_lambda : lambda in C(h,q)}
                  union {mu-mu^r : lambda in C(h,q)} ).

This is an ordinary linear span in the finite-dimensional gradient
coefficient space R^(n+1). Equations (1)--(2) imply

    L_face subset ker Y.                          (6)

Let J={0,...,n-2}, and T={n-1,n}; J is empty if n=1.
Let H_J=(<g_i,g_j>)_(i,j in J), which is the actual prefix-gradient Gram
matrix, not an assumed replacement for the full primal.

For EVERY r in L_face, including every source difference, (3) and (6) give
the exact identity

    ||p||^2 r_(n-1)^2 + ||g||^2 r_n^2
            = r_J^T H_J r_J.                      (7)

Indeed r_(n-1)p+r_n g=-sum_(i in J)r_i g_i; square both sides and use
<p,g>=0. In particular,

    r_n^2 + r_(n-1)^2/(1+b)^2
       <= [4 B_n^2/q^2] (sum_(i in J) B_i |r_i|)^2. (8)

This explicit estimate says how much earlier source coefficients must
change to permit a specified change of the two terminal source coefficients.
It is simultaneous over every optimal certificate; it does not require
the reselected certificate to be stationary on all earlier cuts.

Consequences include

    L_face intersect span{e_(n-1),e_n}={0},
    dim L_face<=n-1,                              (9)

and injectivity of mu -> mu_J on the entire source-coefficient set.
For n=1 every source coefficient is fixed across the whole set, and every
Z_lambda is zero. For larger n the conclusion allows nonzero earlier
Schur slack and source variation. It does not imply Z_lambda=0.

Applying (7) to the columns of a PSD square root of any Z_lambda gives
the additional exact identity

    ||p||^2 (Z_lambda)_(n-1,n-1)
       +||g||^2 (Z_lambda)_(n,n)
           = trace(H_J (Z_lambda)_JJ).             (10)

Thus, for example,

    (Z_lambda)_(n,n)
      +(Z_lambda)_(n-1,n-1)/(1+b)^2
    <= [4 B_n^2/q^2] (sum_(i in J)B_i^2)
                                  trace((Z_lambda)_JJ). (11)

Equations (7), (8), (10), (11) are quantitative restrictions on the full
optimal set, not a claim that its common kernel equals the observed
primal range. Additional common kernel directions are permitted.

The fixed-coordinate graph formulation is also useful. Because projection
L_face -> R^J is injective, the terminal coordinates of r in L_face are
linear functions of r_J. These functions can be extended to R^J. Hence
there are fixed vectors u,v in R^J such that

    r_(n-1)=-u^T r_J,  r_n=-v^T r_J for all r in L_face.

The vectors k_p=(u,1,0), k_n=(v,0,1) annihilate every Z_lambda, and
mu^T k_p and mu^T k_n are constant over C(h,q). In particular

    Z_JT=-Z_JJ [u v],
    Z_TT=[u v]^T Z_JJ [u v]                       (12)

for every certificate in the set, with the SAME u,v. This uses the full
Schur matrix, including singular prefix blocks.

## 3. Certificate mixing gives an explicit descent test without stationarity

The exact covariance identity explains why different certificates cannot
be inspected in isolation. For finitely many certificates lambda^a at
the same h,q, positive weights theta_a summing to one, and their average,

    Z_bar=sum_a theta_a Z_a
          +(1/(4q))sum_a theta_a(mu^a-mu_bar)(mu^a-mu_bar)^T. (13)

This follows by expanding A_bar-mu_bar mu_bar^T/(4q). Every multiplier
of the average is nonnegative, its flow is correct, and its FULL matrix
is PSD, being the average of the full matrices.

By choosing finitely many certificates whose ranges and source differences
span L_face, one gets range Z_bar=L_face. One direct justification is
that the range of a sum of PSD matrices is the sum of their ranges;
the covariance range is the span of the included source differences.

For completeness, a terminal vector in this range yields an actual
same-length descent, without a stationary-instance assumption.
Suppose for some averaged certificate

    Z_bar >= kappa (a e_(n-1)+s e_n)(a e_(n-1)+s e_n)^T,

where kappa>0, a>0 and s in {+1,-1}. Put B=B_n, Bprev=B_(n-1), and

    C=q/(2B^2)+1/kappa.

Choose a positive d with

    d<=a/C,
    d<=q^2/(8 a B^2 Bprev^2),
    d<b if s=+1.

Replace b by b-s d, leaving every earlier step fixed. Then

    W_n(h_0,...,h_(n-2),b-s d)
        <=q-d q^2/(8 a B^2)<q.                    (14)

Here is the full uniform argument. For ANY legal instance normalized by
||x_0||=1, put E=2f_n and R=a p+s g. The averaged PSD certificate gives
q-E>=kappa||R||^2. Convexity gives ||g||^2>=E^2/(4B^2).
The identity for ||R||^2 gives

    -2s<p,g> >= (||g||^2-||R||^2)/a.

The new endpoint is x_n+s d p, so smoothness gives

    E_new<=E-(d/a)[E^2/(4B^2)-(q-E)/kappa]+d^2 Bprev^2.

Insert E^2>=q^2-2q(q-E), then the displayed d bounds. This proves (14)
uniformly over dimensions and functions. The smoothness inequality can
also be written as one additional interpolation inequality plus the
nonnegative square ||g_new-g-s d p||^2/2. Thus the argument retains a
full interpolation/PSD certificate with an auxiliary old endpoint.

A vector supported only on e_n in range Z_bar contradicts tightness:
q-E>=kappa||g||^2>=kappa E^2/(4B^2) uniformly forces E<=r<q.
A vector supported only on e_(n-1) gives the same contradiction with
kappa/(1+b)^2. Consequently a nonzero intersection of L_face with the
terminal two-coordinate plane either improves the tight bound at the
same schedule or gives the genuine final-step descent (14).

For exactly TWO certificates, if their source difference is
Delta mu=A e_(n-1)+B0 e_n with A*B0!=0, the equal-weight average has

    kappa=B0^2/(16q),
    a=|A/B0|, s=sign(A/B0)

after rescaling the direction. Formula (14) is therefore an explicit
quantitative way of exploiting re-selection. It cannot occur under
the matching stationary hypothesis of Sections1--2, by (8).

## 4. A common strict forward-edge barrier two steps from the end

Assume now n>=2, set k=n-2 and a=h_k, and retain the actual stationary
instance of Section1. Suppose SOME certificate in C(h,q) has

    nu_k=lambda_(star,k)>0.

Complementarity for that certificate on the common instance forces

    delta_k=f_k-||g_k||^2/2=0.                    (15)

Meanwhile Q_(n,n-1)<=0 and (3) imply

    delta_(n-1)=f_(n-1)-||p||^2/2
                  >=q/2+||g||^2/2>0.              (16)

First a>1. To see this, the unit-step descent inequality from (15) shows
that y=x_k-g_k is a minimizer. For 0<=a<=1, Lipschitz gradient equality
between x_k and y forces p=(1-a)g_k. A detailed justification: the two
Lipschitz bounds along the segment sum to ||g_k||, so equality in the
triangle inequality forces the stated vectors. At a=1, p=0 contradicts
f_n>0. At a<1, (3) implies <g_k,g>=0; since x_n=x_k-a g_k-b p, the
constraint Q_(n,k)<=0 becomes q/2+||g||^2/2<=0, again impossible.
Thus a>1.

Define sigma_ij=-Q_ij>=0 for the common actual instance. Direct expansion
of the exact GD relation x_(k+1)=x_k-a g_k gives

    Q_(star,k+1)+(1/a)Q_(k+1,k)+((1-a)/a)Q_(k,k+1)
           -Q_(star,k)
      =(1/a)||p-(1-a)g_k||^2.

Using (15) and (16),

    sigma_(k,k+1)
      =[a delta_(k+1)+sigma_(k+1,k)
                     +||p+(a-1)g_k||^2]/(a-1)
      >=[a/(a-1)](q/2+||g||^2/2)
      >=[a/(a-1)](q/2+q^2/(8B_n^2))>0.          (17)

Therefore EVERY certificate in C(h,q) has

    lambda_(k,k+1)=0,  nu_(k+1)=0.                (18)

The first is a common strict inactive edge, not a missing edge in one
bad extreme certificate. Re-selection at unchanged h,q cannot restore
that adjacent capacity. This obstruction is compatible with remote
forward edges and does not prove that a simultaneous full motion fails.

## 5. The inactive cost remains after re-selection

The precise finite joint-perturbation identity is recorded here to prevent
a representation change from hiding the cost in (17). Use the stationary
base lambda^0 and its common actual instance. For a new full certificate
(q',lambda',h'), let dh=h'-h and dlambda=lambda'-lambda^0. Define

    z_t(lambda)=sum_(j>t)[mu_j+sum_(l<=t)lambda_(j,l)]g_j
                   -sum_(i<=t)[sum_(j>t)lambda_(i,j)]g_i,
    B_mix=sum_(t<n)dh_t <g_t,z_t(dlambda)>.

Here z_t is linear in lambda, and D_t(lambda;g)=<g_t,z_t(lambda)>.
The full matrix is affine separately in h and lambda; pairing it with
the OLD Gram realization, using flow, old matching, and all old
stationarity equations, gives exactly

    <M(q',lambda',h'),G_old>
       =q'-q-sum_ij lambda'_ij sigma_ij+B_mix.

Full PSD therefore requires

    q'-q >= sum_ij lambda'_ij sigma_ij-B_mix.      (19)

In the setting of Section4 this includes the explicit charges

    sum_ij lambda'_ij sigma_ij
       >= lambda'_(k,k+1) [a/(a-1)](q/2+q^2/(8B_n^2))
                     +nu'_(k+1)(q/2+q^2/(8B_n^2)). (20)

The two edges are distinct and every omitted charge is nonnegative.
If one instead uses a reselected base certificate that is not stationary
on this same primal at earlier cuts, the linear term
sum dh_t D_t(lambda_reselected;g) must be retained. Formula (19) with
the original stationary base already includes it inside B_mix.
No unsupported stationarity transfer across all cuts has been made.

## 6. Scope

The identities and explicit bounds (7)--(14), together with the strict
common barrier (17)--(20), are new face-level quantitative constraints.
They survive arbitrary re-selection in the full nonnegative-flow/PSD set.
They allow extra kernel directions, all remote edges, and non-Huber
levels q>1/(2sum h+1).

They do not show that a global minimizer has a positive nu_(n-2), that
every other star-outgoing multiplier vanishes, that the full slack is
rank one, or that q equals the Huber value. Even Huber tightness would
still leave the exact/asymptotic DP mass restriction. The remaining
search must pay (20) by a genuine joint schedule/flow motion, or obtain
a different uniform comparison; convex-face terminology alone does
not supply that bridge.

# Exact terminal re-selection through the fixed-prefix maximal extension

Status: UNVERIFIED self-contained candidate. No new fact_submit is allocated.
This is a precise positive support result for the full optimal certificate set.
It removes only incoming edges at the UNQUERIED final sample, not arbitrary
remote forward edges at queried samples. No descent or profile theorem is claimed.

## 1. The reduced primal retains the complete prefix

Normalize L=1, x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be a
finite positive schedule, n>=1, and let P={star,0,...,n-1}.
As usual x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t, and

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Consider the full Gram primal on (x_0,g_0,...,g_n), with G>=0,
||x_0||^2<=1, and objective maximize 2f_n. Keep

    Q_ij<=0 for every distinct i,j in P,
    Q_(n,j)<=0 for every j in P.                    (1)

Delete every Q_(j,n)<=0, j in P, including Q_(star,n).
No other constraint is removed. In particular all remote forward and
backward interpolation constraints inside the prefix remain.

The value of this reduced primal equals the true unrestricted W_n(h).

## 2. Exactness by an explicit globally legal extension

Take any feasible reduced transcript and realize its Gram matrix by
finite-dimensional Euclidean vectors. For j in P put

    a_j=<g_j,x_j>-f_j,
    H_j(v)=a_j+<x_j,v-g_j>+||v-g_j||^2/2,
    H(v)=max_(j in P) H_j(v),
    F(x)=sup_v {<x,v>-H(v)}.                       (2)

Each H_j is a quadratic with Hessian I, so H is finite, continuous and
1-strongly convex. Its quadratic growth makes the supremum defining F
finite and attained at a unique vector v(x). The optimality relation is
x in partial H(v(x)). Strong convexity gives

    <x-x',v(x)-v(x')> >= ||v(x)-v(x')||^2,

and hence ||v(x)-v(x')||<=||x-x'||. The maximizing affine functions in (2)
then show grad F(x)=v(x): the lower bound from testing v(x) and upper
bound from testing v(x') squeeze the first-order difference, with an
O(||x-x'||^2) error. Thus F is globally convex, differentiable, and
1-smooth.

For any i,j in P,

    H_j(g_i)-a_i=Q_ij<=0.

Consequently H(g_i)=a_i, and x_i is a subgradient of H at g_i, since the
i-th quadratic is active there and has gradient x_i. It follows that
grad F(x_i)=g_i and F(x_i)=f_i. The star sample gives F(0)=0 and
grad F(0)=0, so zero is a global minimizer. This proves legality of the
complete prefix without invoking an external interpolation black box.

Because GD through x_n uses only g_0,...,g_(n-1), the SAME predetermined
schedule on F follows all the supplied positions through x_n.
The retained terminal inequalities say

    H_j(g_n)<=<x_n,g_n>-f_n for every j in P.

Therefore

    f_n<=<x_n,g_n>-H(g_n)<=F(x_n).                  (3)

The new actual terminal value is at least the reduced transcript's
objective. Thus every reduced feasible value is at most W_n(h).
Conversely any legal trajectory is reduced feasible, proving exactness.

The constructed F is also the pointwise maximal smooth-convex extension
of the fixed prefix. Indeed, for any legal extension K, the elementary
smooth-convex interpolation inequality between each fixed sample j and
an arbitrary sample x with gradient grad K(x) gives
K(x)<=<x,grad K(x)>-H(grad K(x))<=F(x).
Maximality is useful motivation but (3) alone proves reduced-PEP exactness.

At an optimal reduced transcript, 2f_n=W_n(h), both inequalities in (3)
are equalities. Uniqueness of the conjugate maximizer implies
g_n=grad F(x_n) and f_n=F(x_n). Hence an optimal reduced primal is itself
fully interpolable: the deleted incoming terminal inequalities hold at
optimality. This statement is about optimal transcripts, not all reduced
feasible transcripts.

## 3. The reduced dual attains the SAME value

Here are the necessary finite-dimensional details, so re-selection is
not an appeal to an unattained dual infimum.

A strict reduced primal exists when every h_t>0. Choose n+2 distinct
numbers theta_l in (0,1), take a quadratic with diagonal Hessian
diag(theta_l), and an initial vector with every coordinate nonzero and
norm less than one. The columns x_0,g_0,...,g_n are evaluations of

    1, z, z product_(t<1)(1-h_t z), ...,
                       z product_(t<n)(1-h_t z)

at the distinct nodes, times nonzero initial coordinates. These n+2
polynomials have degrees 0,1,...,n+1 with nonzero leading coefficients,
so their evaluation matrix is invertible. Thus G is positive definite.

No two positions among star and 0,...,n are equal: their distinct
prefix polynomials, each of degree at most n, cannot agree at all n+2
distinct nodes; none of those polynomials vanishes at all nodes either.
For the strictly convex quadratic with Hessian strictly below I,
direct substitution gives

    Q_ij=-1/2 (x_i-x_j)^T Hquad(I-Hquad)(x_i-x_j)<0

for every distinct pair. In particular every retained inequality is strict.

The reduced optimal value is finite by Section2 and the elementary GD
bound W_n(h)<=product_t(1+h_t)^2. Its dual attainment now follows directly
from separating an open convex set, as follows. Let E_red be the retained
ordered pairs. The open convex set of (a,b,c) satisfying, for some G>=0,f,

    a_ij>Q_ij(f,G) (ij in E_red),
    b>G_00-1,
    c<2f_n

does not contain (0,0,q), where q=W_n(h). A separating hyperplane has
nonnegative coefficients lambda_ij,r,eta, not all zero, and yields

    sum_(E_red) lambda_ij Q_ij(f,G)
             +r(G_00-1)-eta*2f_n >= -eta*q

for all G>=0,f. The strict primal point rules out eta=0. Normalize eta=1.
Arbitrary values f then force out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n), and arbitrary PSD G
forces the full matrix M(r,lambda,h)>=0. Testing G=f=0 gives r<=q;
weak duality and reduced exactness give r>=q. Thus r=q and the dual
attains the exact objective value.

Extend this reduced certificate to the original full format by setting
all omitted multipliers to zero. We have proved the precise re-selection:

    At every positive h there EXISTS a tight full certificate with
        lambda_(j,n)=0 for ALL j in P.             (4)

In particular nu_n=0 can be imposed, and the remaining outgoing
terminal weights sum to exactly two. This does not say that every
optimal certificate already has this support. It does not assert that
a source vector can be held fixed during the re-selection.

This argument is the ordinary finite-dimensional separation proof only
for the reduced system just justified. It does not repeat or claim as
new the historical global minimizer/KKT interface.

## 4. Exact terminal square and monotone probability coordinates

For a certificate satisfying (4), write

    alpha_j=lambda_(n,j)/2 >=0, j in P,
    sum_(j in P)alpha_j=1,
    y_j=x_j-g_j,  delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2,
    V_alpha=x_n-sum_(j in P)alpha_j y_j.            (5)

Let lambda^P denote the unchanged multipliers on ordered pairs inside P.
Direct expansion, with delta_star=y_star=0, gives the FULL identity

    M(q,lambda,h)
      =||g_n-V_alpha||^2+R_alpha,                  (6)

where

    R_alpha=q||x_0||^2
                  -2sum_(j in P)alpha_j delta_j-||V_alpha||^2
                  +sum_(i,j in P)lambda^P_ij Q_ij. (7)

The prefix flow cancels all function values in R_alpha. In detail,
for each finite i<n it is

    out_i^P-in_i^P=2alpha_i,

because the removed terminal outgoing edge n->i supplied incoming flow
2alpha_i in the full certificate. R_alpha is thus a quadratic form
in (x_0,g_0,...,g_(n-1)).

Full PSD is EQUIVALENT to R_alpha>=0: one direction follows from (6),
and the other follows by minimizing the full quadratic over the
independent formal vector g_n. This is an exact Schur complement,
not the omission of an unobserved kernel direction.

The same identity is a necessary-and-sufficient certificate
parameterization of this selected subface: nonnegative prefix
multipliers with the displayed prefix flow, alpha in the probability
simplex, and the complete PSD remainder R_alpha.

For explicit chronological coefficients define

    w_(-1)=alpha_star,
    w_t=alpha_star+sum_(j=0)^t alpha_j, 0<=t<n.

Then 0<=w_(-1)<=w_0<=...<=w_(n-1)=1, and

    V_alpha=alpha_star x_0
            -sum_(t<n)[h_t w_t-(w_t-w_(t-1))]g_t. (8)

This keeps all earlier gradient coordinates. In particular
lambda_(n,star)=2alpha_star<=2. The formula is not a scalar-mass
replacement for the prefix PSD condition (7).

On ANY actual matching worst case for this selected certificate,

    g_n=V_alpha,  R_alpha=0,
    alpha_j Q_(n,j)=0, lambda^P_ij Q_ij=0.          (9)

Thus re-selection gives an actual terminal gradient formula for the
matching primal. It does not impose such a formula on every legal
trajectory; away from equality the square in (6) measures its defect.

## 5. Relation to the remote-edge obstruction and source variation cost

For a two-step suffix k=n-2, the selected support eliminates remote
forward edges i->n and the local edge (n-1)->n. It does NOT eliminate
remote i->(n-1) for i<k. Those edges are within the complete prefix
and remain in (7). In particular the old three-step counterexample
at h=(2,9/4,3) already has no incoming edges at its final sample3:
its hostile edge0->2 survives this reduction unchanged.

At a full stationary matching tuple with nu_k>0, the common strict
barrier derived directly from interpolation still applies:
lambda_(k,k+1)=0 across the full optimal set, with positive old slack.
The terminal re-selection may alter earlier source coefficients and
may alter which actual matching primal supplies earlier-cut stationarity.
One cannot transport all stationarity equations to an arbitrarily
chosen reselected certificate.

For any joint change from a fixed stationary base, the exact old-primal
identity remains

    q'-q >= sum lambda'_ij(-Q_ij(old))
                  -sum_t (h'_t-h_t)<g_t,z_t(lambda'-lambda)>.

Neither the terminal square (6) nor dropping the redundant terminal
incoming inequalities cancels this inactive cost or bilinear term.

## 6. Literature check and scope

The explicit maximum-of-quadratics conjugate construction is consistent
with Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur, Smooth strongly convex interpolation
and exact worst-case performance of first-order methods,
arXiv:1502.05666, Theorem4 and Remark2. Their Theorem6 uses a full-rank
quadratic transcript to establish fixed-step PEP duality. Those sections
were read in the downloaded paper. All construction, reduced-system
exactness, separation, and full square identities needed here are
written out, rather than imported as unexplained external theorems.
A targeted Matlas query returned unrelated results; no such result was used.

This is a concrete, validly scoped route to re-selection and a complete
matrix parameterization of the resulting subface. It is not a descent
theorem at a global minimizer, does not remove the surviving remote
prefix edges, and does not resolve Huber tightness or the exact DP mass
restriction.

# Exact cross-block moments and an endpoint-state collision

Status: unverified exact identities and an explicit counterexample to a proposed compression. No new optimization or verifier call. A competitive closed moment certificate is not yet available.

Work at smoothness1 with

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.

Define transformed sample coordinates and values

    z_i=x_i-g_i, F_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.

Then the actual interpolation slack is

    I_ij=-Q_ij=F_j-F_i-<g_i,z_j-z_i> >=0.           (1)

## 1. A finite exact moment tuple

For any nonnegative weights u on actual samples define

    D=sum u_i, U=sum u_i g_i, Z=sum u_i z_i,
    M=sum u_i F_i,
    N=sum u_i(<g_i,z_i>-F_i),
    C=M+N=sum u_i<g_i,z_i>.

The letters M,N here denote weighted function moments, not a PSD matrix or a horizon. N is the conjugate-value moment; this notation avoids reusing the primitive capacity K.

For a block beginning at x_start and ending at x_end with value f_end, its intrinsic objective energy satisfies exactly

    E=2<U,x_start>-||U||^2-2N-2D f_end.             (2)

For two weighted sets a,b of samples from the SAME function, rank-one sums of every directed cross edge satisfy

    T_ab=sum_(i in a,j in b) u_i v_j I_ij
        =D_a M_b+D_b N_a-<U_a,Z_b> >=0,
    T_ba=D_b M_a+D_a N_b-<U_b,Z_a> >=0.             (3)

These equations follow by expanding (1) and factoring the product weights. In particular the internal all-pairs sum is

    T_aa=D_a C_a-<U_a,Z_a> >=0.                    (4)

The moment tuple has an exact additive update. If the old head weights are scaled by alpha, the tail weights by beta, and extra weights eta,gamma are placed at the bridge point y and final point z, then

    D_new=alpha D_a+beta D_b+eta+gamma,
    U_new=alpha U_a+beta U_b+eta g_y+gamma g_z,
    Z_new=alpha Z_a+beta Z_b+eta z_y+gamma z_z,
    M_new=alpha M_a+beta M_b+eta F_y+gamma F_z,
    N_new=alpha N_a+beta N_b
             +eta(<g_y,z_y>-F_y)+gamma(<g_z,z_z>-F_z). (5)

Here z_y=y-g_y and z_z=z-g_z; the repeated z is a point name in the subscript and a transformed coordinate on the right. All positions and function values in (5) refer to their actual common global coordinates. There is no reset at the start of the tail. The actual final proof weights must be nonnegative. Equation(2) then computes the combined objective energy exactly.

This supplies a precise interface for the all-cross plan. It does not establish that the elementary inequalities(2)--(4) characterize all legal moments or provide a closed accelerated certificate.

## 2. Endpoint information, even including the dual slack, does not determine (3)

Consider the fixed physical schedule h=(1,1,1), start x_0=12/5, minimizer0 and proof weights u=(1,1,1,1). Construct two one-dimensional convex1-smooth functions A and B, each with f(0)=0. Their sample data are:

|i|x_i for A|g_i for A|f_i for A|x_i for B|g_i for B|f_i for B|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|0|12/5|1|293/200|12/5|1|293/200|
|1|7/5|7/10|123/200|7/5|23/30|47/72|
|2|7/10|1/2|39/200|19/30|13/30|283/1800|
|3|1/5|1/5|1/50|1/5|1/5|1/50|

Both columns satisfy x_(i+1)=x_i-g_i exactly.

For function A, linearly interpolate the displayed gradients between successive points. The three slopes from the first interval to the last are3/10,2/7,3/5, all in[0,1]. Set g(x)=x for x<=1/5 and g(x)=1 for x>=12/5. Integrating this continuous monotone1-Lipschitz derivative gives precisely the displayed values: its three drops f_i-f_(i+1) are17/20,21/50,7/40.

For function B, on each interval[x_(i+1),x_i] let L_i=g_i be its length, let delta_i=g_i-g_(i+1), and place a slope1 ramp of length delta_i after a lower flat piece of length a_i. Before the ramp the derivative is g_(i+1); after it the derivative is g_i. Choose

    (a_0,a_1,a_2)=(289/420,11/100,1/10).

The corresponding (L_i,delta_i) are(1,7/30),(23/30,1/3),(13/30,7/30). Each a_i lies in[0,L_i-delta_i]. The area under the derivative on such an interval is

    g_i L_i-delta_i^2/2-delta_i a_i.

It is respectively731/900,223/450,247/1800 for the three intervals, yielding the displayed function values from f_3=1/50. Extend the derivative by x below1/5 and by1 above12/5. This again gives one globally defined continuous, nondecreasing1-Lipschitz derivative, and its integral is minimized at zero. Thus both constructions satisfy the full function assumptions, not just adjacent interpolation tests.

## 3. All proposed endpoint data agree, but a needed reverse sum differs

For both trajectories,

    D=4, d=x_0-x_3=11/5, U=12/5, e=U-d=1/5,
    p=g_0=1, q=g_3=1/5,
    f_0=293/200, f_3=1/50, f_0-f_3=289/200,
    E=443/100.

The physical primitive energy, for S=3 and capacity4, is V=E-12q^2=79/20 on both instances. Their primitive dual expression is also the same:

    H=2(f_0-f_3)-6q^2-|p-(d+q)/4|^2=249/100.

These equalities use the direct definitions; they do not assume any unverified primitive theorem for the schedule.

Nevertheless their weighted proximal-point sums and primal moments differ:

    Z_A=23/10, M_A=281/200,
    Z_B=67/30, M_B=2497/1800.

The conjugate moment N is the same, as equation(2) already implies from the shared endpoint data. At the terminal point z_3=x_3-g_3=0 and F_3=f_3-q^2/2=0. Consequently the reverse-anchor sum is

    sum_i u_i I_(3,i)=M-qZ.

It equals189/200=1701/1800 on A and1693/1800 on B, a difference of1/225. Thus no formula depending only on the common tuple(D,E,d,U,e,p,q,f_0,f_3,V,H) can recover this reverse interpolation sum for all legal trajectories.

This is a counterexample to exact endpoint compression, not to inequalities that bound that sum using the tuple, and not to carrying the larger moment tuple from part1.

## 4. The open quantitative step

Equation(3) makes the missing quantities explicit. Substituting M=C-N trades the missing primal value moment for the within-block mixed moment C=sum u_i<g_i,z_i>. The inequality(4) provides only a lower bound on C. In a proposed energy certificate the coefficient of C after subtracting a positive cross-edge sum can have the opposite sign, so (4) cannot silently be used as an upper bound.

A successful all-cross join must retain a valid bound with the correct sign for this moment, or preserve C and its function-value counterpart through the next join. Additivity(5) alone is not that bound. This is the precise remaining mechanism in the moment plan; no exact-profile improvement is claimed.

# Selected terminal reduction package, including zero and empty schedules

Status: UNVERIFIED; ONE fact_submit authorized by TASK.md and master_guidance aa9a56da67cdfc12.

## Statement

Exact unqueried-terminal reduction and full-certificate re-selection for arbitrary nonnegative gradient-descent schedules.

For every integer n>=0, every L>0, and every finite h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) in [0,infinity)^n, let W_n(h) be the supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over all finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, convex differentiable functions f with L-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer x_star, and x_0!=x_star, with x_(t+1)=x_t-(h_t/L)grad f(x_t). The empty schedule n=0 is allowed.

For the following finite formulations use normalized smoothness1, x_star=g_star=f_star=0, normalized sampled values f_i, formal gradients g_i, and x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t. Put I_n={star,0,...,n}, J_pre={star,0,...,n-1}, and Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 for distinct i,j in I_n. When n=0, J_pre={star}.

(a) The finite Gram maximization of 2f_n subject to G_pr>=0, G_pr_(x0,x0)<=1, all Q_ij<=0 with distinct i,j in J_pre, and all Q_(n,j)<=0 with j in J_pre, has attained optimal value W_n(h). Here G_pr is the full Gram matrix of the n+2 formal vectors (x_0,g_0,...,g_n), with no rank constraint. No incoming terminal inequality Q_(j,n)<=0 is imposed. For any feasible prefix jets in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, define cjet_j=<g_j,x_j>-f_j, H_j(v)=cjet_j+<x_j,v-g_j>+||v-g_j||^2/2, H(v)=max_(j in J_pre)H_j(v), and F(x)=sup_v(<x,v>-H(v)). Then F is an everywhere finite convex differentiable 1-smooth function interpolating all prefix jets, F(0)=0=min F, and it is the pointwise maximal such prefix interpolant. For every reduced-feasible terminal pair (g_n,f_n), F(x_n)>=f_n. At an optimal reduced transcript, F(x_n)=f_n and grad F(x_n)=g_n; hence every optimal reduced transcript is fully interpolable and obeys the deleted incoming terminal inequalities.

(b) There exist nonnegative multipliers lambda_ij on all distinct pairs in I_n, with lambda_(j,n)=0 for every j in J_pre, finite-node flow sum_j lambda_ij-sum_j lambda_ji=2*1_(i=n), and a FULL positive semidefinite quadratic certificate
M_cert=W_n(h)||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij
after the GD substitution. This certificate is PSD on the original formal space (x_0,g_0,...,g_n), including every gradient at a zero step, without imposing equality between duplicated formal gradients. Thus some tight full certificate has no incoming edge at the unqueried terminal sample for every nonnegative schedule. For schedules with positive steps this follows from an explicit strict primal and a separation argument. If there are zero steps, choose the original index of each positive step as the representative of its compressed query and the original index n as the terminal representative; embedding a certificate for the positive-step compression gives the asserted full-space certificate. The all-zero and empty schedules have W_n(h)=1 and the direct certificate lambda_(n,star)=2, all other lambda zero, with M_cert=||x_0-g_n||^2.

(c) For any real certificate level q_cert and any h as above, certificates with no incoming terminal multipliers are parameterized exactly as follows. Choose alpha_j>=0 for j in J_pre, with sum_j alpha_j=1, and nonnegative prefix multipliers lambda^pre_ij for distinct i,j in J_pre whose finite prefix flow is out_i^pre-in_i^pre=2alpha_i for 0<=i<n. Define y_j=x_j-g_j, delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2, V_alpha=x_n-sum_(j in J_pre)alpha_j y_j, with y_star=delta_star=0, and
R_alpha=q_cert||x_0||^2-2sum_(j in J_pre)alpha_j delta_j-||V_alpha||^2+sum_(i!=j in J_pre)lambda^pre_ij Q_ij.
The prefix flow cancels all f_i in R_alpha. Set lambda_(n,j)=2alpha_j, all incoming terminal multipliers zero, and retain lambda^pre. The complete identity is
M_cert=||g_n-V_alpha||^2+R_alpha.
Consequently full PSD of M_cert is equivalent to PSD of the entire prefix quadratic R_alpha in (x_0,g_0,...,g_(n-1)). For n>=1, with w_(-1)=alpha_star and w_t=alpha_star+sum_(j=0)^t alpha_j, one has 0<=w_(-1)<=w_0<=...<=w_(n-1)=1 and
V_alpha=alpha_star x_0-sum_(t<n)[h_t w_t-(w_t-w_(t-1))]g_t.
For n=0, alpha_star=1, V_alpha=x_0, and R_alpha=(q_cert-1)||x_0||^2. Any actual normalized trajectory attaining a feasible q_cert has g_n=V_alpha, R_alpha=0, and multiplier complementarity.

This result deletes no interpolation inequalities inside the queried prefix. It asserts existence of a selected optimal certificate, not that every optimal certificate has the selected support. It neither establishes Huber tightness nor removes earlier remote forward edges, transfers earlier-cut stationarity under arbitrary re-selection, or proves the project's asymptotic exact-profile conjecture.

## Proof

1. Normalization, interpolation necessity, and elementary bounds.

For an original instance let R=||x_0-x_star||>0. The normalized function
F_0(z)=[f(x_star+R z)-f(x_star)]/(L R^2)
is convex differentiable with gradient Lipschitz constant1, a minimizer0,
and initial norm1. Its GD uses the same h and its normalized objective
is 2F_0(z_n). This also proves the converse scaling correspondence.
We may work with smoothness1 and the optimum sample zero.

For a differentiable function K with 1-Lipschitz gradient, integration
of its gradient along a segment gives
K(x+d)<=K(x)+<grad K(x),d>+||d||^2/2.
For convex K, apply this to K(z)-<grad K(x_i),z>, whose minimum is
at x_i, taking a unit negative-gradient step from x_j. Its minimum
value is no larger than the stepped value, so
K(x_j)-K(x_i)-<grad K(x_i),x_j-x_i>
    >=||grad K(x_j)-grad K(x_i)||^2/2.
This is exactly Q_ij<=0 for the actual samples, with our stated
orientation of Q.

For a normalized legal instance, put D_i=product_(t<i)(1+h_t), D_0=1.
Since grad K(0)=0, ||g_i||<=||x_i|| and ||x_(i+1)||<=(1+h_i)||x_i||.
Thus ||x_i||,||g_i||<=D_i, and
0<=K(x_i)<=||x_i||^2/2.
In particular W_n(h)<=D_n^2<infinity.
It is strictly positive: choose the scalar quadratic K(x)=kappa*x^2/2
with kappa=1/[2(1+sum_t h_t)] in (0,1], starting at1.
Every factor 1-kappa h_t is positive, and its normalized error is
kappa*product_t(1-kappa h_t)^2>0.

2. Explicit interpolation and the maximal prefix extension.

Let any finite collection of prefix jets (x_j,g_j,f_j), j in J_pre,
satisfy every ordered prefix inequality and include the zero optimum jet.
Define cjet_j,H_j,H,F as in the statement, on the same finite-dimensional
Euclidean space. The function H(v)-||v||^2/2 is the maximum of finitely
many affine functions and hence is convex. H is continuous, finite,
1-strongly convex, and has quadratic growth. For each x, the function
<v,x>-H(v) therefore has a unique maximizer, denoted v(x).

The maximizer condition is x in partial H(v(x)). For any x,x',
the two strong subgradient inequalities for H, added together, give
<x-x',v(x)-v(x')>>=||v(x)-v(x')||^2.
Consequently ||v(x)-v(x')||<=||x-x'||.
The definition of F, evaluated at v(x) and v(x'), gives
0<=F(x')-F(x)-<v(x),x'-x>
    <=<v(x')-v(x),x'-x><=||x'-x||^2.
Thus F is differentiable with grad F(x)=v(x), and its gradient is
1-Lipschitz. It is convex as a supremum of affine functions and finite
by the stated quadratic growth.

For i,j in J_pre direct expansion gives H_j(g_i)-a_i=Q_ij.
The term with j=i equals zero and every other term is nonpositive;
hence H(g_i)=a_i. The active quadratic H_i has gradient x_i at g_i,
and H>=H_i with equality there, so x_i is a subgradient of H at g_i.
The unique maximizer defining F(x_i) is consequently g_i, and
F(x_i)=<x_i,g_i>-a_i=f_i. This proves interpolation of all prefix jets.
In particular F(0)=0 and grad F(0)=0, so zero is a global minimizer.
The same construction, for any finite index set including the zero
jet, proves sufficiency of ALL pairwise Q inequalities for a legal
convex 1-smooth interpolant; repeated positions cause no exception.

If K is any other legal function interpolating the prefix, apply the
necessity calculation in paragraph1 between its sample at an arbitrary
x and each prefix jet j. Writing g=grad K(x), those inequalities give
H_j(g)<=<x,g>-K(x) for every j. Thus
K(x)<=<x,g>-H(g)<=F(x).
This proves the claimed pointwise maximality without importing an
interpolation or conjugacy theorem from a paper.

3. Exact value of the reduced Gram problem and primal attainment.

Realize any feasible Gram matrix by vectors in dimension at most n+2;
if its rank is zero, one may embed its zero vectors in R.
The complete prefix inequalities give the function F of paragraph2.
Its gradients at every queried prefix point equal the supplied g_i,
so the GD recursion reaches the same supplied x_n. No terminal gradient
is used to determine x_n, even when some steps vanish.

For the reduced terminal pair, the retained inequalities give
H_j(g_n)<=<x_n,g_n>-f_n for all j in J_pre. Therefore
f_n<=<x_n,g_n>-H(g_n)<=F(x_n).
If ||x_0||>0, normalization of this actual function yields
2F(x_n)<=W_n(h)||x_0||^2<=W_n(h).
If ||x_0||=0, all actual prefix iterates and x_n are the minimizer0,
so F(x_n)=0 and 2f_n<=0<W_n(h).
Thus the reduced supremum is at most W_n(h).
Every actual legal normalized trajectory is feasible for the reduced
Gram problem, so the reverse inequality holds.

For clarity the supremum is attained. Consider first the FULL Gram
problem, including every incoming terminal inequality. Its feasible
set is closed. Paragraph2 applied to the entire finite index set
I_n realizes every feasible point as a legal function; hence paragraph1
bounds all sampled gradients, all Gram entries by Cauchy--Schwarz,
and all values 0<=f_i<=D_i^2/2. The feasible set is therefore compact
in finite-dimensional matrix/value space. It is nonempty and has an
objective maximizer. Necessity and the interpolation construction
show its value is exactly W_n(h). The same full optimizer is reduced
feasible, so it also attains the reduced value.

At any reduced optimizer, the chain
W_n(h)=2f_n<=2F(x_n)<=W_n(h)||x_0||^2<=W_n(h)
has equal endpoints and W_n(h)>0. Thus ||x_0||=1,
f_n=F(x_n), and <x_n,g_n>-H(g_n)=F(x_n).
The maximizer of that conjugate expression is unique, so
g_n=grad F(x_n). The supplied terminal jet therefore belongs to the
same legal F as the prefix and satisfies every deleted incoming
inequality. This also proves the assertion for every reduced optimizer,
not just one optimizer chosen from the full feasible set.

4. Dual attainment for positive schedules, by separation.

Assume n>=1 and h_t>0 for every t<n. Let E_red be the retained
ordered pair set:
{(i,j): i,j in J_pre, i!=j} union {(n,j):j in J_pre}.
Use the matrix/value variables of the reduced primal.

There is a strictly feasible point with G_pr positive definite,
G_pr_(x0,x0)<1, and every retained Q strictly negative.
Choose n+2 distinct real theta_l in (0,1), let A_quad be the diagonal
matrix with these entries, let K(x)=<x,A_quad x>/2, and choose x_0
with every coordinate nonzero and norm less than1.
Write Poly_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z), including Poly_0=1.
The columns (x_0,g_0,...,g_n) are evaluations at the theta_l of the
n+2 polynomials 1,z Poly_0,...,z Poly_n, times nonzero initial
coordinate factors. These polynomials have distinct degrees
0,1,...,n+1 and nonzero leading coefficients. A polynomial of degree
at most n+1 vanishing at n+2 distinct nodes is zero, so the evaluation
matrix is invertible and G_pr is positive definite.
For i!=j finite, Poly_i-Poly_j is a nonzero polynomial of degree
at most n; it cannot vanish at all chosen nodes. Poly_i cannot vanish
at all nodes either. Thus all finite sample positions are distinct
from each other and from star. Direct substitution for this quadratic
gives
Q_ij=-<x_i-x_j,A_quad(I-A_quad)(x_i-x_j)>/2<0.
This proves the full stated strictness.

Let w_opt=W_n(h), which is finite by paragraph1. Consider the open
convex set O of tuples (s,t,c) for which there exist G_pr>=0 and real
sample values f with
s_ij>Q_ij(f,G_pr) for ij in E_red,
t>G_pr_(x0,x0)-1, and c<2f_n.
It is open since it is a union of open orthants; it is convex by
linearity of every Q in the Gram/value variables and convexity
of the PSD cone. The point (0,0,w_opt) is not in O.
Finite-dimensional separation of a point from a nonempty open convex
set gives a nonzero linear functional, chosen nonnegative on O
relative to that point. Independent upward changes of each s_ij
and of t, and downward changes of c, force its coefficients to be
(lambda_ij,rho,-eta) with lambda_ij,rho,eta>=0.
Taking limits to the boundary of each strict inequality yields,
for ALL G_pr>=0 and ALL real sample values f,
sum_(E_red)lambda_ij Q_ij(f,G_pr)
    +rho(G_pr_(x0,x0)-1)-eta*2f_n >= -eta*w_opt.       (S)

If eta=0, some lambda_ij or rho is positive, since the functional is
nonzero. Substitution of the strict primal point constructed above
makes the left side of (S) strictly negative, a contradiction.
Hence eta>0 and we divide the coefficients by eta to set eta=1.

The f_i are unrestricted real variables in (S). Their coefficients
must vanish:
out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n), for 0<=i<=n.
After their cancellation, (S) says
trace(M_cert(rho,lambda,h) G_pr)-rho>=-w_opt for every G_pr>=0.
If this matrix had a negative quadratic direction, scaling the
corresponding rank-one PSD G_pr would contradict this inequality.
It is therefore PSD. Taking G_pr=0 gives rho<=w_opt.
Conversely the flow, lambda>=0, and full PSD give, for every reduced
feasible point,
2f_n<=rho G_pr_(x0,x0)<=rho
because rho>=0. Thus w_opt<=rho. Equality follows.
Setting lambda_(j,n)=0 on the omitted pairs gives the required
tight full certificate on the original positive-step formal space.

5. Zero-step compression and lifting in the ORIGINAL formal space.

Suppose n>=1 and exactly m>=1 of the original steps are positive.
List their original indices as
0<=i_0<i_1<...<i_(m-1)<=n-1,
and define the positive compressed schedule hhat_s=h_(i_s),
0<=s<m. Deleting zero steps changes no actual iterate; therefore
W_m(hhat)=W_n(h) by the same function/initial-point trajectories in
both directions.

Apply paragraph4 to hhat, obtaining a tight incoming-terminal-free
certificate lambdahat on {star,0,...,m}.
Define the injective index map
iota(star)=star, iota(s)=i_s for 0<=s<m, and iota(m)=n.
On the original formal space define
xhat_0=x_0, ghat_s=g_(i_s) for s<m, ghat_m=g_n.
Its compressed formal positions satisfy
xhat_s=x_0-sum_(r<s)h_(i_r)g_(i_r)=x_(i_s) for s<m,
and
xhat_m=x_0-sum_(r<m)h_(i_r)g_(i_r)=x_n.
These are polynomial identities in independent original formal vectors:
the omitted coefficients h_t are ZERO. They do not use any equality
between gradients sampled at identical actual positions.

Put lambda_(iota(s),iota(t))=lambdahat_(s,t) on mapped pairs, and
put every other original multiplier equal to zero.
At each mapped finite node the original flow equals its compressed
flow; at each unmapped node both in-flow and out-flow vanish.
The mapped terminal is n, so the original finite flow is exactly
out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n). No multiplier points into original n.
Every mapped Q expression equals the corresponding compressed
Q expression after identifying the mapped values, whose coefficients
cancel by flow.

Let T_pick be the linear map selecting
(x_0,g_(i_0),...,g_(i_(m-1)),g_n)
from (x_0,g_0,...,g_n). The ORIGINAL full certificate matrix is precisely
T_pick^T Mhat_cert T_pick and is PSD because Mhat_cert is PSD.
Unmapped gradient columns are zero. No duplicate-gradient constraint
or auxiliary squared penalty is imposed or needed. This proves the
claimed original-index, full-formal-space lift, including leading,
interior, and trailing zero steps.

If m=0, including the empty schedule n=0, every actual iterate is x_0.
Smoothness at the minimizer gives 2f(x_0)<=||x_0||^2, and the scalar
quadratic x^2/2 attains equality. Thus W_n(h)=1.
Set lambda_(n,star)=2 and every other multiplier to zero.
It has exactly the required flow and no incoming terminal edges.
Since x_n=x_0 as a formal identity, its full quadratic is
||x_0||^2-2f_n+2Q_(n,star)=||x_0-g_n||^2.
This treats all-zero schedules and n=0 without any Slater assertion
about duplicated points. Parts(a) and the maximal extension remain
valid independently for these schedules by paragraphs2--3.

6. Exact terminal-square and full prefix-PSD parameterization.

Take ANY certificate whose incoming terminal multipliers vanish.
The finite terminal flow gives sum_(j in J_pre)lambda_(n,j)=2.
Consequently alpha_j=lambda_(n,j)/2 is a nonnegative probability
vector. All other multipliers lie inside the prefix, and their finite
flow is out_i^pre-in_i^pre=2alpha_i for i<n.
For any such alpha and prefix multipliers define y_j,delta_j,V_alpha,
R_alpha as in the statement, taking the star quantities equal to zero.

Expanding the outgoing terminal sum gives
2sum_j alpha_j Q_(n,j)
 =2f_n-2sum_j alpha_j f_j
       +2<g_n,sum_j alpha_j x_j-x_n>
       +sum_j alpha_j||g_n-g_j||^2
 =2f_n-2sum_j alpha_j delta_j
       +||g_n-V_alpha||^2-||V_alpha||^2.
Substituting into the full certificate proves
M_cert=||g_n-V_alpha||^2+R_alpha.
In R_alpha the coefficient of each finite f_i is
(out_i^pre-in_i^pre)-2alpha_i=0; it contains no f_n.
It is the complete quadratic form on ALL original prefix vectors.
The vector V_alpha is independent of the formal terminal gradient g_n.
Hence full PSD is equivalent to prefix PSD: prefix PSD implies full
PSD from the square identity, and full PSD implies prefix PSD by
setting the free formal vector g_n equal to V_alpha.
This is true even with zero-step duplicates; it is not a test only
on legal transcripts.

Conversely any alpha and nonnegative prefix multipliers with the
stated prefix flow define a full multiplier family by
lambda_(n,j)=2alpha_j and incoming terminal multipliers zero.
Their full finite flow is the required objective flow. If R_alpha
is PSD the full square identity certifies it. This proves both
directions of the parameterization for any real q_cert.

For n>=1, expand positions in
V_alpha=x_n-sum_(j in J_pre)alpha_j(x_j-g_j).
The coefficient of x_0 is
1-sum_(j=0)^(n-1)alpha_j=alpha_star.
For t<n, the coefficient of g_t is
-h_t+alpha_t+h_t sum_(j=t+1)^(n-1)alpha_j
 =-h_t[alpha_star+sum_(j=0)^t alpha_j]+alpha_t.
With w_t as in the statement, alpha_t=w_t-w_(t-1), giving
the claimed chronological formula and the nondecreasing w sequence.
For n=0 the probability simplex contains only alpha_star=1,
there are no prefix pairs, V_alpha=x_0, and
R_alpha=(q_cert-1)||x_0||^2.

Finally take an actual normalized trajectory attaining a feasible
certificate level q_cert. The certificate identity evaluated there is
M_cert=sum lambda_ij Q_ij<=0, while full PSD makes it nonnegative.
Every term lambda_ij Q_ij is nonpositive, so each is zero.
The square identity and prefix PSD then imply
g_n=V_alpha and R_alpha=0. This is an assertion about matching
actual trajectories, not a presumed rank condition on a primal.

7. Scope and proof dependencies.

The proof uses elementary smoothness, the displayed explicit convex
conjugate construction, finite-dimensional linear algebra, compactness
of the bounded finite Gram system, and a fully specified separating
hyperplane argument. No historical project KKT claim or unverified
finding is a premise. No external paper theorem is used as a black
box. In particular the separation argument is used only for genuinely
positive compressed steps, and the zero-step conclusion is obtained
by an explicit embedding into the original formal space.

Only incoming constraints at n, which is unqueried by the recursion,
are removed. Every ordered interpolation constraint inside J_pre
remains. The statement implies neither Huber tightness nor a removal
of earlier remote edges or a transfer of earlier-cut stationarity
under arbitrary re-selection; it does not decide the asymptotic
exact-profile problem.

glossary.Q_ij: Signed normalized smooth-convex interpolation residual f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||²/2.
glossary.J_pre: Prefix sample index set {star,0,...,n-1}, or {star} for n=0.
glossary.E_red: All distinct ordered prefix pairs together with all outgoing terminal pairs (n,j), j in J_pre.
glossary.M_cert: Full formal-vector quadratic certificate q_cert||x_0||²-2f_n+sum lambda_ij Q_ij after GD substitution.
glossary.q_cert: A real objective upper-certificate level; selected tight level is W_n(h).
glossary.w_opt: The exact reduced/full objective value W_n(h) used in the separating-hyperplane argument.
glossary.H_j: Conjugate lower quadratic cjet_j+<x_j,v-g_j>+||v-g_j||²/2 for a prefix jet.
glossary.v(x): Unique vector maximizing <x,v>-H(v) in the explicitly constructed conjugate F.
glossary.A_quad: Diagonal positive quadratic Hessian with distinct eigenvalues strictly between0 and1, used for strict feasibility.
glossary.alpha_j: Nonnegative terminal outgoing probability lambda_(n,j)/2 for j in J_pre.
glossary.lambda^pre: Nonnegative interpolation multipliers on the complete queried prefix.
glossary.y_j: Prefix proximal point x_j-g_j, with y_star=0.
glossary.V_alpha: x_n-sum_(j in J_pre)alpha_j y_j, independent of the formal terminal gradient.
glossary.R_alpha: The complete prefix quadratic remainder in M_cert=||g_n-V_alpha||²+R_alpha.
glossary.w_t: Cumulative terminal probability alpha_star+sum_(j=0)^t alpha_j, with w_(-1)=alpha_star.
glossary.hhat: Positive-step compression of the original nonnegative schedule.
glossary.i_s: Original index of the s-th positive step in the zero-step compression argument.
glossary.iota: Injection of compressed sample indices into the original indices, mapping the compressed terminal to original n.
glossary.T_pick: Linear coordinate-selection map from all original formal vectors to those used by the compressed certificate.
glossary.lambdahat: Tight full certificate for the positive compressed schedule.
glossary.Mhat_cert: Full PSD certificate matrix for the positive compressed schedule.
glossary.cjet_j: Conjugate jet value <g_j,x_j>-f_j in this terminal-extension result.
glossary.G_pr: Full primal Gram matrix of the formal vectors (x_0,g_0,...,g_n), or its fixed point in the separation argument.
glossary.lambda_ij: Nonnegative multiplier for the signed ordered interpolation residual Q_ij.
