claim: The mixed-gradient-moment storage P_theta has an exact nonnegative physical bridge law and a complete 2x2 terminal objective certificate. Its price is a factor 1+theta. For every finite balanced Silver horizon, the certified bound becomes strictly worse under its positive infinitesimal deformation; the derivative loss has an explicit uniform positive lower bound. This rules out that local route, not finite deformations or the unrestricted target.
evidence:
# Mixed gradient-moment storage: exact transport and local loss

Status: candidate derivation, not verifier-accepted. No solver or new verifier
call is used. This completes the unfinished calculation in the previous round's
local notes. It does not establish the project's unrestricted target.

## Definitions

Normalize smoothness to 1. For a nonnegative GD block h with samples x_i,
g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i), let

    S=sum h_i, A=S+1, q=g_n,
    V_h=2 sum_(i<n) h_i(f_i-f_n)
        +sum_(i<n) h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-S A||q||^2,
    b_h=sum_(i<n) h_i(h_i-2),
    B_h=sum_(i<n) h_i(h_i-2)||g_i||^2,
    P_theta(h)=V_h-theta(B_h-b_h||q||^2).

Here B_h is a trajectory quantity, whereas b_h is a schedule scalar; neither is
the project's benchmark denominator B_n. For actual samples of the same convex
1-smooth function set

    I_ij=f_j-f_i-<g_i,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2/2 >=0.

The proof of this inequality can be given without an external theorem: subtract
the affine function with gradient g_i from f, so x_i is a minimizer of the
resulting convex 1-smooth function. Its one-step descent bound from x_j with
step 1 gives f_j-f_i-<g_i,x_j-x_i> >= ||g_j-g_i||^2/2.

## 1. A complete objective certificate, including the price

Translate a chosen minimizer to zero and its value to zero. Write X=x_n.
Telescoping squared distances and expanding the optimum slacks gives

    V_h=||x_0||^2-||X||^2-2S f_n-S A||q||^2
        -2 sum h_i I_(i,*),
    B_h=||X||^2-||x_0||^2
        +2 sum h_i[I_(i,*)+I_(*,i)].

Thus the following is an EXACT equality:

    (1+theta)||x_0||^2-2(2S+1)f_n
      =P_theta(h)
       +2(1+theta) sum h_i I_(i,*)
       +2theta sum h_i I_(*,i)+2A I_(n,*)
       +(X,q)^T M_theta (X,q),                         (1)

    M_theta = [[1+theta, -A],[-A, A^2-theta b_h]].

For theta>=0 all displayed optimum-edge coefficients are nonnegative. The
matrix is PSD exactly when theta[A^2-(1+theta)b_h]>=0. Therefore, if

    P_theta(h)>=0 on every legal block trajectory,
    theta>=0,  b_h<=A^2/(1+theta),

then W_n(h)<=(1+theta)/(2A-1). In particular the extra factor 1+theta cannot be
omitted. Equation (1) gives the actual full boundary matrix and all new
interpolation multipliers, not only a distance estimate.

Negative theta is not certified by this conversion: its incoming optimum
coefficients are negative. Even the boundary matrix fails for -1<theta<0,
since b_h<=S^2-2S=A^2-4A+3<A^2 and hence
theta[A^2-(1+theta)b_h]<0. This is a restriction on (1), not on every conceivable
conversion of P_theta.

## 2. Generalized physical primitive join with all actual multipliers

Take physical head a of capacity K=1+sum a_i, ending at y with gradient g,
then a bridge of length 1+r, then physical tail b of capacity A=1+sum b_i,
ending at z with gradient q. Tail internal indices i mean all its gradient
query samples before z. Let

    0<=r<A,
    c=(K+r)/(A-r),  k=1+2c,
    Delta=r(K+A+r)-KA,
    J=2c[sum_(i internal to b) b_i(I_(i,y)+I_(i,z))
          +I_(z,y)+r I_(y,z)].

Every multiplier in J is nonnegative. Repeated or coincident samples are
interpreted as the actual sample data; no inherited point or value is reset.
Direct expansion yields

    V_(a,1+r,b)=V_a+k V_b+c Delta(||q||^2-||g||^2)+J.   (2)

For checking (2), subtract V_a+k V_b from the left. Its function part is
2(K+r)(f_y-f_z)-4c sum b_i(f_i-f_z). Its gradient part is

    (K^2-K-r-r^2)||g||^2
    -2c sum b_i(1-b_i)||g_i||^2
    +[-(K+A+r-1)(K+A+r)+k(A-1)A]||q||^2.

Expand J, use x_i=y-(1+r)g-sum_(j<i in b)b_j g_j and
z=y-(1+r)g-sum_(j in b)b_j g_j. The terms containing internal gradient products
cancel because c(A-r)=K+r. The remaining coefficients are precisely the
displayed ones after c Delta(||q||^2-||g||^2) is added.

Moreover

    b_(a,1+r,b)=b_a+b_b+r^2-1,
    B_(a,1+r,b)=B_a+B_b+(r^2-1)||g||^2.

Consequently (2) gives the exact new storage identity

    P_theta(a,1+r,b)=P_theta(a)+k P_(theta/k)(b)+J
       +[c Delta+theta(b_a+r^2-1)](||q||^2-||g||^2).    (3)

The scalar closure equation is therefore

    c Delta+theta(b_a+r^2-1)=0.                       (4)

Inputs require DIFFERENT labels theta and theta/k. Same-label copying is not a
valid consequence of (3). At theta=0, (4) is the usual primitive join, including
its exact Silver scaling. No loss is inserted into that calibration.

## 3. Nontrivial finite calibration and an exact equality test

For two empty inputs K=A=1, equation (4) reduces to

    (1-theta)r^2+2(1+theta)r-(1+theta)=0.

At theta=1 it gives r=1/2, i.e. the step h=3/2, and (3) reads

    P_1(3/2)=6 I_10+3 I_01 >=0.

At theta=0 it gives h=sqrt(2). This exhibits a real capacity gain when theta
is added, but the objective certificate at theta=1 is only 2/4=1/2.

For any block and the legal full-curvature function f(x)=||x||^2/2, define
Pi_h=product_(i<n)(1-h_i). Then

    P_theta(h)=[1+theta-(A^2+theta(1-b_h))Pi_h^2]||x_0||^2. (5)

This follows directly from the two identities in section 1: every optimum
slack vanishes and q=x_n=Pi_h x_0. If a recursively constructed block is built
from empty blocks using only (3)-(4), all interpolation slacks also vanish on
this quadratic, so the bracket in (5) must be exactly zero. It is a useful
hostile equality check for any proposed parameters; no numerical search is
needed.

## 4. The balanced deformation has a well-defined finite first variation

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2), t=sqrt(2)-1=1/lambda. For each fixed m, define a local
family h_m(theta), of length 2^m-1, recursively near theta=0:

    h_0(theta)=(),
    h_(m+1)(theta)=(h_m(theta),1+r,h_m(theta/k)),

where r,k solve (4) and k=1+2(K+r)/(A-r), with

    K=A_m(theta), A=A_m(theta/k),
    A_m(theta)=1+sum h_m(theta).

This is an implicit finite family, not an assertion that a common fixed
positive theta works for every m. Its smooth local existence follows
inductively from the implicit-function theorem. At theta=0, one has

    K=A=lambda^m, r=t lambda^m, c=lambda, k=lambda^2.

The partial derivative of the first equation with respect to r is
2lambda sqrt(2)lambda^m>0. Its derivative with respect to k is zero: the tail
argument theta/k has zero k-derivative at theta=0. The derivative of the second
equation with respect to k is 1 for the same reason. Thus the two-by-two
Jacobian is invertible. All physical steps, k and A-r remain positive in a
small neighborhood for each fixed m. Inductively (3) then supplies a complete
nonnegative interpolation certificate for P_theta. The input labels retain
the sign of theta. For sufficiently small theta>=0, the objective matrix in
(1) is also PSD because b_h<A^2 at theta=0.

Define a_m=A_m'(0) and write b_m=b_(h_m(0)). The undeformed recurrence gives

    b_0=0, b_(m+1)=2b_m+t^2 lambda^(2m)-1,
    b_m=beta lambda^(2m)-gamma 2^m+1,
    beta=(8sqrt(2)-11)/7,
    gamma=(8sqrt(2)-4)/7.

Differentiating the capacity join at theta=0 yields

    a_0=0,
    a_(m+1)=sqrt(2)a_m
       -[b_m+t^2 lambda^(2m)-1]/[2lambda sqrt(2)lambda^m]. (6)

To see every derivative in (6), the standard capacity map
Omega(K,A)=(K+A+sqrt((K+A)^2+4KA))/2 has both first derivatives lambda/2
at K=A. The derivatives of the two child capacities are a_m and
a_m/lambda^2, so their combined contribution is sqrt(2)a_m. The direct
theta-derivative of (4) is the second term of (6); derivatives of c disappear
there because Delta=0.

Put eta=sqrt(2)/lambda=2-sqrt(2), d=beta+t^2=(10-6sqrt(2))/7, and
v_m=a_m/lambda^m. Then exactly

    v_(m+1)=eta v_m+[-d+gamma eta^(2m)]/[2lambda^2 sqrt(2)],
    v_m={-d(1-eta^m)/(1-eta)
           +gamma(eta^m-eta^(2m))/(eta-eta^2)}
          /[2lambda^2 sqrt(2)].                       (7)

In particular

    lim_(m->infty) v_m=-(10-6sqrt(2))/[14lambda sqrt(2)]<0. (8)

The operations here are: differentiate at theta=0 for each finite m, then
take the m-limit of the exact formula (7). No interchange with an unproved
fixed-theta asymptotic limit is being used.

## 5. Every finite balanced first variation loses after objective conversion

Compare the certified bound to its own undeformed primitive bound:

    R_m(theta)=(1+theta)(2lambda^m-1)/(2A_m(theta)-1).

For m>=1,

    R_m'(0)=1-2a_m/(2lambda^m-1).                    (9)

This is strictly positive for every m. An explicit uniform derivative bound
is available. Formula (7) gives v_1=1/(lambda^3 sqrt(2)). For m>=1 its forcing
term is at most the m=1 forcing term, and

    gamma eta^2-d < (1-eta)(gamma-d),

because the difference is gamma(eta^2+eta-1)-d eta<0, with
eta^2+eta-1=7-5sqrt(2)<0. Induction therefore gives v_m<=v_1 for all m>=1.
If v_m is negative, (9) is greater than 1. Otherwise the factor
2lambda^m/(2lambda^m-1) is at most its m=1 value. Hence

    R_m'(0)>=1-2/[lambda^2 sqrt(2)(2lambda-1)]>0.    (10)

Thus for EACH fixed finite balanced horizon, this concrete deformation is
worse for every sufficiently small positive theta. Its large-horizon
derivative has the limit

    lim R_m'(0)=1+(10-6sqrt(2))/[14lambda sqrt(2)]>1. (11)

This closes the proposed infinitesimal balanced improvement in the specific
P_theta storage and conversion (1). It does not rule out finite deformations,
unbalanced trees, another conversion, or more general moment storage. In
particular (10) alone supplies no common neighborhood in theta for all m.

## Literature and scope

The active mechanism was checked against the already downloaded exact text of
Fazlyab et al., arXiv:1705.03615, Theorem 3.1 and its full proof. Its method
requires a proved supply inequality, nonnegative coefficients, and an actual
terminal PSD bound. Equations (1)-(4) give those objects for this narrower
candidate; that paper supplies no completeness theorem or asymptotic
improvement. Matlas returned no relevant long-step composition result on the
new targeted query, and web search provided no additional useful mechanism.
No external theorem is a proof premise of the algebra above.

The practical next question is whether a function-value-coupled moment can be
transported without paying the same initial factor, or whether a concrete
nonlocal correlation changes the bridge closure. Re-optimizing (4) near the
balanced zero-label branch cannot supply the desired improvement.

claim: Exact last-step minimax candidate from accepted terminal fact: for every fixed nonnegative prefix, the best fixed final-step worst case equals the unrestricted worst case with exact final line search; an attained maximal interpolant in dimension<=n+1 supplies a common last-step stationary primal and forces lambda_(star,n-1)=0 in EVERY tight full certificate.
evidence:
# Exact terminal hull and one-step minimax continuation

Status: complete candidate derivation, NOT verifier-accepted. The only proof
predecessor is fact `1252b8823bb5a290`. The selected terminal-reduction submission
was already accepted in the preceding round; its one-request allocation is used.
This file contains one self-contained follow-on candidate and no new submission.

## 1. Quantifiers and the complete prefix

Fix an integer n >= 1 and any fixed nonnegative prefix

    h_pre = (h_0,...,h_(n-2)).

The prefix is empty when n=1. Set k=n-1. The last step b_last ranges over
[0,infinity), and the full schedule is (h_pre,b_last). Use the normalized
setting L=1, x_star=g_star=f_star=0 and initial squared distance at most one.
The quantity W_n is exactly the normalized, arbitrary-finite-dimensional
worst-case objective in fact 1252b8823bb5a290.

Let C_pre be the set of pairs C=(G_pre,(f_i)_(0<=i<=k)) satisfying:

* G_pre is the PSD Gram matrix of all formal vectors (x_0,g_0,...,g_k);
* its x_0 diagonal is at most one;
* x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t for 0<=i<=k;
* EVERY ordered inequality Q_ij<=0 is retained on J_pre={star,0,...,k},
  where Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

These conditions are imposed on Gram/value coordinates, so C_pre is a
finite-dimensional convex closed set. It is compact: the interpolation
construction in the cited fact realizes every feasible set of prefix jets
as a legal convex 1-smooth function. With D_i=product_(t<i)(1+h_t),
one has ||x_i||,||g_i||<=D_i and 0<=f_i<=D_i^2/2. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds
every Gram entry. The set contains the zero data and is nonempty.
This argument allows all zero steps and imposes no strictness condition.

Write Delta_pre for the probability simplex on J_pre. For every C and
alpha in Delta_pre set

    y_j=x_j-g_j,    delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2,
    y_star=0,      delta_star=0,
    X_alpha=x_k-sum_j alpha_j y_j,
    z_pre=g_k,
    Phi_term(C,b_last,alpha)
      =2 sum_j alpha_j delta_j+||X_alpha-b_last z_pre||^2.       (1)

Norms and inner products in this display are Gram expressions, independent
of the choice of a vector realization. For fixed (b_last,alpha), (1) is
linear in C. For fixed C, it is convex jointly in (b_last,alpha), because
its vector inside the squared norm is affine and its other term is linear.
The function is continuous in all finite coordinates. Moreover delta_j>=0
follows from Q_(star,j)=-delta_j<=0.

## 2. The exact hull formula, with its proof

The maximal prefix interpolant in the cited fact is F_C=H_C^*, where

    H_C(v)=||v||^2/2+max_(j in J_pre)(<y_j,v>-delta_j).

For every x in the realizing Euclidean space,

    2F_C(x)=min_(alpha in Delta_pre)
                  [2 sum_j alpha_j delta_j
                    +||x-sum_j alpha_j y_j||^2].              (2)

Here is a direct proof, including attainment. Let v=grad F_C(x), the unique
maximizer of <x,v>-H_C(v) supplied by the predecessor. Let A be the nonempty
set of indices maximizing <y_j,v>-delta_j. One has

    x-v in conv{y_j:j in A}.                                  (3)

To prove this without a subgradient formula, suppose (3) fails. Separation
from the finite convex hull gives a vector d such that
<x-v,d> > max_(j in A)<y_j,d>. For small positive epsilon, the right
derivative of the maximum of the affine functions at v in direction d is
max_(j in A)<y_j,d>: the finitely many strictly inactive indices remain
inactive for all sufficiently small epsilon. The right derivative of
<x,v+epsilon d>-H_C(v+epsilon d) is therefore positive. This contradicts
maximality of v. Thus choose alpha supported on A with
x-v=sum alpha_j y_j. Its value in the right side of (2) equals 2F_C(x),
because the weighted active affine values equal their maximum and

    F_C(x)=<x,v>-||v||^2/2
              -sum alpha_j(<y_j,v>-delta_j)
          =||v||^2/2+sum alpha_j delta_j.

Conversely, for any alpha, H_C(u)>=||u||^2/2+
<sum alpha_j y_j,u>-sum alpha_j delta_j for every u. Maximizing
<x,u>-H_C(u) gives the upper bound in (2). The constructed active alpha
attains it. For ANY minimizing alpha in (2), completing the square gives

    grad F_C(x)=x-sum_j alpha_j y_j.                           (4)

Indeed equality in the upper bound at the unique conjugate maximizer
requires precisely that equality of vectors; alternatively strict
convexity in the barycenter proves that all minimizing barycenters agree.

The predecessor says F_C interpolates the entire prefix, is convex and
1-smooth, and is pointwise maximal among all such interpolants. Therefore

    W_n(h_pre,b_last)
       =max_(C in C_pre) min_(alpha in Delta_pre)
                           Phi_term(C,b_last,alpha).          (5)

For the <= direction, any original function produces a prefix in C_pre
and is bounded above at the resulting terminal point by F_C. For the >=
direction, F_C is itself legal and has the prescribed prefix and terminal
position. If ||x_0||<1, its unnormalized value is bounded by W times
||x_0||^2, and scaling every vector and every value gives the converse
normalization at any positive maximizer. A zero initial vector gives zero
data by the recursion. Maxima exist by compactness and (2).

Each such maximizing function lives in dimension at most n+1, the number
of prefix formal vectors. All information at the unqueried terminal is
constructed in this same space. No queried-prefix inequality is removed.

## 3. An elementary compact minimax lemma

The following finite-dimensional argument will be used here, rather than
an unexplained imported minimax theorem. Let C and A be nonempty compact
convex sets and let P(c,a) be continuous, affine in c, and convex in a.
Then

    max_c min_a P(c,a)=min_a max_c P(c,a),                      (6)

and both extrema are attained. To prove this, put m=max_c min_a P(c,a).
For each c let K_c={a in A:P(c,a)<=m}. Suppose some finite collection
c_1,...,c_s has empty intersection of these sets. The set

    U={u in R^s: some a in A has u_i>=P(c_i,a)-m for all i}

is convex, by convexity in a, and closed, by compactness of A. It does not
contain zero. It has a closest point u_* to zero, with ||u_*||>0. Since
U is invariant under addition of any vector with nonnegative coordinates,
the projection inequality <u_*,u-u_*>>=0 for u in U implies every coordinate
of u_* is nonnegative. Let p_i=(u_*)_i/sum_j(u_*)_j. These are nonnegative
and sum to one. Evaluating the same projection inequality at
u=(P(c_i,a)-m)_i gives, for every a,

    sum_i p_i P(c_i,a)
      >=m+||u_*||^2/sum_i(u_*)_i > m.

But c_bar=sum_i p_i c_i belongs to C, and the left side is P(c_bar,a).
This contradicts the definition of m. Thus the closed sets K_c have the
finite intersection property in compact A and have a common point a_*.
It satisfies max_c P(c,a_*)<=m. The reverse inequality is the direct
min-max inequality. Continuity and compactness give all stated extrema.

Applying (6) to (5) gives the exact terminal-weight minimax formula

    W_n(h_pre,b_last)
      =min_(alpha in Delta_pre) max_(C in C_pre)
                           Phi_term(C,b_last,alpha).          (7)

This retains the full prefix Gram matrix. It does not identify that state
with any scalar statistic of the prefix schedule.

## 4. Unbounded final steps, attainment, and one legal saddle function

Define

    rho_last(h_pre)=inf_(b_last>=0) W_n(h_pre,b_last).

The value function in b_last is continuous. This follows from (5), since
Phi_term is uniformly continuous on C_pre times Delta_pre times any
bounded closed stepsize interval. It is convex: in (7), the maximum over
C of the jointly convex functions in (1) is convex, and partial
minimization over the convex simplex preserves convexity. Equivalently,
(5) is a maximum over C of the convex functions 2F_C(x_k-b_last g_k).

The outer infimum is attained at a finite b_last. For a direct coercivity
check choose

    theta=1/[2(1+sum_(t<k)h_t)],
    P_theta=product_(t<k)(1-theta h_t)>0.

The scalar legal function f(x)=theta x^2/2 starting at one yields

    W_n(h_pre,b_last)>=theta P_theta^2(1-theta b_last)^2,

which tends to infinity. Continuity now gives an attained minimum.
Its value is positive: for each finite full schedule the cited fact proves
W_n>0 (or choose a sufficiently small positive curvature avoiding all
finitely many roots). Positivity at an attained minimizer gives rho_last>0.

The exact unbounded minimax relation is

    rho_last(h_pre)
      =max_(C in C_pre) min_(b_last>=0, alpha in Delta_pre)
                              Phi_term(C,b_last,alpha).       (8)

Here are all compactness details. For each positive integer B, apply (6)
to C_pre and [0,B] times Delta_pre. Let rho_B be the common value and
let C_B maximize the inner minimum. The values rho_B decrease to
rho_last by (7). Along a subsequence with B tending to infinity,
C_B converges to C_* in compact C_pre. For every fixed finite b_last
and every fixed alpha, the defining inequality
Phi_term(C_B,b_last,alpha)>=rho_B holds for all sufficiently large B.
Passing to the limit proves Phi_term(C_*,b_last,alpha)>=rho_last for
every pair. This and the direct min-max inequality prove (8).

Choose ANY optimal finite b_* and any alpha_* attaining (7) there.
Then

    Phi_term(C,b_*,alpha_*)<=rho_last
      =Phi_term(C_*,b_*,alpha_*)
      <=Phi_term(C_*,b_last,alpha)                             (9)

for every feasible C,b_last,alpha. The equality follows by applying the
two inequalities to each other at the middle point. Thus an actual saddle
pair exists without a strictly feasible Gram hypothesis and without any
compactness assumption on the last-step ray.

By (2), the SINGLE maximal prefix interpolant F_(C_*) satisfies

    min_(b_last>=0) 2F_(C_*)(x_k-b_last g_k)
      =2F_(C_*)(x_k-b_* g_k)=rho_last.                        (10)

Its initial norm is one: if it were smaller and nonzero, scaling its
prefix to norm one would scale its positive inner minimum upward,
contradicting (8). If the initial vector were zero, the inner value would
be zero. The constructed function needs dimension at most n+1.

Consequently, in the ORIGINAL normalization and arbitrary finite
dimensions, with the first n-1 GD steps fixed in advance,

    inf_(b>=0) W_n(h_pre,b)
      =sup_(legal f,x_0,x_star)
          inf_(b>=0) 2[f(x_k-(b/L)grad f(x_k))-f(x_star)]
                           /(L||x_0-x_star||^2).             (11)

The supremum on the right is attained by the function in (10), after
normalization. Its inner infimum is attained at b_*. For an arbitrary
legal f, maximal extension bounds its values at EVERY point of this
ray by F_C for the same prefix, so its inner infimum is bounded by the
right side of (8). Conversely F_(C_*) attains (8). This proves (11)
directly; it does not exchange a stepsize with the changing earlier GD
queries. Thus optimizing the final fixed step has exactly the unrestricted
worst-case value of allowing exact line search for that final step.

## 5. Explicit geometry and a consequence for the complete dual set

The inner minimum in (8) has the closed form

    min_(alpha in Delta_pre) [2sum alpha_j delta_j+||X_alpha||^2
                      -(<X_alpha,z_pre>_+)^2/||z_pre||^2]    (12)

when z_pre!=0; the fraction is replaced by zero when z_pre=0. This is
obtained by minimizing a scalar quadratic in b_last, whose minimizing
step is <X_alpha,z_pre>_+/||z_pre||^2. Here t_+=max(t,0).
For z_pre=0, the actual point x_k is a minimizer of F_C and the inner
value is zero (also choose alpha_k=1). Thus z_pre!=0 at C_*.

Let v_*=grad F_(C_*)(x_k-b_* z_pre). Since the value in (10) is positive,
v_*!=0. The minimizing last step is interior: at b=0 the derivative of
F_(C_*)(x_k-b z_pre) is -||z_pre||^2<0. Differentiability and (10) give

    <v_*,z_pre>=0.                                           (13)

Adding the two interpolation inequalities between x_k and its terminal
point gives
<z_pre-v_*,b_* z_pre>>=||z_pre-v_*||^2. Therefore

    b_* >= 1+||v_*||^2/||z_pre||^2 > 1.                     (14)

This holds for EVERY minimizing last step, since any one of them can be
paired with C_* in (9). The outgoing terminal-to-k interpolation inequality
also gives

    delta_k >= rho_last/2+||v_*||^2/2 > 0.                 (15)

Indeed its gradient-position term is b_*<v_*,z_pre>=0, and
||v_*-z_pre||^2=||v_*||^2+||z_pre||^2.

Now take ANY tight full nonnegative-flow PSD certificate at the schedule
(h_pre,b_*), not necessarily one with the terminal support selected in
the predecessor. Evaluate its full quadratic identity on the actual
normalized trajectory of F_(C_*). The objective gap equals its certificate
level rho_last, every Q_ij is nonpositive, and the quadratic is PSD.
Thus every nonnegative multiplier satisfies complementarity. Since
Q_(star,k)=-delta_k is strictly negative by (15), EVERY such certificate
has

    lambda_(star,k)=0.                                       (16)

For certificates with no incoming terminal multipliers, the accepted
square identity gives v_*=V_alpha. Their formal last-step matrix derivative
evaluated on this same transcript is 2<z_pre,v_*>=0. Thus one common
actual primal supplies last-step stationarity for every selected optimal
certificate. No corresponding earlier-cut stationarity is claimed.

## 6. A complete two-dimensional test and the role of dimension

Take n=1 and in R^2 choose

    x_0=(1,0),
    z_pre=(1/3,sqrt(2)/6),
    y_0=x_0-z_pre=(2/3,-sqrt(2)/6),
    delta_0=1/6,    f_0=1/4.

Then ||z_pre||^2=1/6, <x_0,z_pre>=1/3, and the two prefix inequalities
are Q_(0,star)=0 and Q_(star,0)=-1/6. Define the fixed legal function by

    F(x)=[v -> ||v||^2/2+max(0,<y_0,v>-1/6)]^*(x).

The cited fact proves that it is convex and 1-smooth, interpolates the
stated initial jet, and has minimum zero at the origin. Formula (2) is

    2F(x)=min_(0<=alpha<=1) [alpha/3+||x-alpha y_0||^2].

At b=3/2 and alpha=1/2, the residual is

    v_*=(1/6,-sqrt(2)/6),
    ||v_*||^2=1/12,
    <z_pre,v_*>=0,
    <y_0,v_*>=1/6.

Both derivatives of the jointly convex quadratic
alpha/3+||x_0-b z_pre-alpha y_0||^2 vanish at this pair. It is feasible,
so its global minimum on b>=0, alpha in [0,1] is 1/6+1/12=1/4.
This is an explicit function whose normalized error after exact line
search is 1/4.

For the matching universal upper bound at b=3/2, all unlisted multipliers
zero, set lambda_(0,star)=lambda_(1,star)=lambda_(1,0)=1. They have the
correct nonnegative flow, and on the FULL formal space

    (1/4)||x_0||^2-2f_1+Q_(0,star)+Q_(1,star)+Q_(1,0)
           =||(1/2)x_0-g_0-g_1||^2.

This proves the exact value rho_last(empty)=1/4 without an external
one-step performance theorem.

In dimension ONE, by contrast, exact line search from any nonoptimal
point reaches a minimizer: the derivative has the same sign as its
displacement from any chosen minimizer, so the nonnegative negative-
gradient ray contains that minimizer. If the derivative is zero, the
point is already a minimizer. This applies after ANY fixed prefix.
Hence the scalar supremum of the exact-line-search error is zero.
The positive value (11) therefore depends essentially on permitting
higher finite dimensions; its minimax interchange must not be applied
to a rank-one-restricted Gram set, which is not convex.

## 7. Scope, literature audit, and unresolved bridge

This candidate derives (2), (7), and (11) together with the explicit
attained saddle and all boundary details in a single proof. Its only
verified building block is 1252b8823bb5a290. All additional arguments are
included here; none is being silently promoted from an earlier finding.

For background the Matlas convex-conjugacy/minimax query returned generic
duality results, none needed as a proof premise. Maurice Sion's original
"On general minimax theorems", Pacific J. Math. 8 (1958), pp.171-176,
especially Section3, was downloaded and its definitions and proof read
through the browser's PDF extraction. Its broader one-compact-set theorem
is consistent with this finite convex setting, but Section3 above supplies
the particular elementary separation proof used here, and Section4 supplies
the unbounded-ray limit and attainment separately. No paper theorem is
used as a black box.

The full queried-prefix state remains in C_pre. Earlier steps change this
feasible set, so (11) cannot be iterated backward as a scalar recurrence.
Neither (12) nor (16) establishes Huber tightness, eliminates remote forward
prefix edges, or proves the Zhang--Jiang exact-profile lower bound. The next
target-facing question is whether the geometric inner value (12) admits
a useful lower bound under a realizable, explicitly constructed family
of full prefixes. Its dimension-two one-step witness shows why restricting
that question to scalar exact-line-search adversaries would lose everything.

author: max4
claim: Unequal-block extension of the two-bridge primitive obstruction: for any three independently chosen nonnegative quadratic-balanced blocks with capacities A,B,C, every primitive join(a,1+r,b,1+s,c), r,s>=0, has total capacity at most max{Omega(Omega(A,B),C),Omega(A,Omega(B,C))}. The three exact quadratic/cut tests already have this sharp scalar maximum.
evidence:
# Unequal quadratic-balanced blocks cannot improve a two-bridge primitive join

Status: self-contained candidate obstruction, not verifier-accepted. This
extends finding2599c72fdf8542a0 from three identical blocks to three independent
blocks. No solver or verifier call is used.

Let a,b,c be finite nonnegative physical GD blocks, with capacities

    A=1+sum a_i, B=1+sum b_i, C=1+sum c_i.

Assume each block is quadratic-balanced in the explicit sense

    |product_i(1-a_i)|=1/A,
    |product_i(1-b_i)|=1/B,
    |product_i(1-c_i)|=1/C.                           (1)

Empty blocks are allowed. For r,s>=0, form

    h=(a,1+r,b,1+s,c), T=1+sum h_i=A+B+C+r+s.

If h is primitive, in the exact sense that the energy

    V_h=2 sum_i h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
        -(T-1)T||g_n||^2

is nonnegative for every convex 1-smooth GD trajectory, then

    T <= max{Omega(Omega(A,B),C),Omega(A,Omega(B,C))}, (2)

where Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2. This Omega is the exact shifted
primitive recurrence in verified fact b98bb807d514e80d. The obstruction below
does not require the individual blocks to be primitive; only (1) and their
nonnegative physical steps are needed.

## 1. The three exact necessary tests

For a general nonnegative primitive schedule with capacity T, choose a step
1+u, u>0, having prefix sum P and tail sum R. Define

    a_minus=u/(R+1), g(x)=min(1,max(-a_minus,x)),
    f(x)=integral_0^x g(t)dt, x_0=P+1.

The derivative is continuous, monotone, and 1-Lipschitz. The prefix stays on
the positive affine ray and ends at1. The selected step lands at-u. Since
(R+1)a_minus=u and all tail partial sums lie in[0,R], the tail stays on the
negative affine ray and ends at-a_minus. Every sample satisfies

    f_i-g_i x_i+g_i^2/2=0,

and the terminal point is in the quadratic core. Expanding the GD squared
distance telescope gives exactly

    V_h=(P+1)^2-T^2 a_minus^2.

Consequently

    T u <= (P+1)(R+1).                              (3)

At u=0 the same inequality is automatic. Applied to the two bridges, (3)
gives

    T r <= A(B+C+s),  T s <= C(A+B+r).               (4)

On the full-curvature quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1, the same expansion gives
V_h=1-T^2 product_i(1-h_i)^2. By (1), this implies

    T r s <= ABC.                                   (5)

All three tests use actual fixed one-dimensional functions.

## 2. Solve the scalar feasible region exactly

Put H=A+B+C and R=T-H=r+s. For fixed T the cut constraints (4) are precisely

    r<=u_A(T)=A(T-A)/(T+A),
    s<=u_C(T)=C(T-C)/(T+C).                          (6)

Let M be the right side of (2), and suppose for contradiction T>M.
Because Omega(B,C)>B+C and Omega(A,B)>A+B, monotonicity of Omega gives

    T>Omega(A,B+C), T>Omega(C,A+B).

These inequalities are equivalent to

    T(T-H)>A(B+C), T(T-H)>C(A+B),

respectively. They imply R>u_A(T) and R>u_C(T). Thus any feasible r must lie
in the nonempty interval

    L=R-u_C(T) <= r <= U=u_A(T),   0<L<=U<R.         (7)

The product r(R-r) is concave in r, so its minimum on (7) is attained at L
or U. At U the first cut is an equality. Writing s_U=R-U, this equality and
the total-capacity equation give

    B+C+s_U=F_A(T),  F_A(T)=T(T-A)/(T+A).

For T>=A this function is strictly increasing: its derivative is
1-2A^2/(T+A)^2>=1/2. If D=Omega(B,C), the defining quadratic equation for
Omega gives F_A(Omega(A,D))=D. Since T>Omega(A,D),

    s_U>D-B-C.

The positive number rho=D-B-C solves rho(B+C+rho)=BC. Therefore

    T U s_U=A(B+C+s_U)s_U>ABC.                     (8)

At L the second cut is an equality. The identical argument with A and C
interchanged gives r_L>Omega(A,B)-A-B and

    T L(R-L)=C(A+B+r_L)r_L>ABC.                    (9)

Concavity now implies T r(R-r)>ABC throughout (7), contradicting (5).
This proves (2), including r=0 or s=0 since under T>M the interval is
strictly inside(0,R).

## 3. Sharpness of the necessary-test bound

For the parenthesization a,(b,c), put

    D=Omega(B,C), s=D-B-C,
    T=Omega(A,D), r=T-A-D.

Both bridges are positive, Tr=A(B+C+s), and Trs=ABC. The other cut also
holds. One direct check is as follows: the binary equations give rT=AD and
sD=BC, so Ts=ABC/r. The required Ts<=C(A+B+r) is equivalent to
AB<=r(A+B+r). Since r(T)=AD and T=A+B+C+r+s, subtracting gives

    r(A+B+r)-AB = AD-r(C+s)-AB
                           = (A-r)(C+s)>0,

since r=AD/T<A. Interchanging A and C proves feasibility for the other
parenthesization as well. Hence M is the exact maximum of the three scalar
tests. If the input blocks themselves are primitive, the usual binary
composition constructs primitive schedules attaining these capacities; the
upper bound (2) needs no such assumption or attainment claim.

The scalar quantity in (2) is exactly the larger capacity of the two binary
parenthesizations. In particular unequal block sizes cannot evade the earlier
equal-copy obstruction while each block retains exact quadratic balance.

## Scope and next opening

This is a primitive-energy obstruction, not a bound on every direct objective
certificate. It also does not apply when any input has
|product(1-h_i)|<1/(1+sum h_i). Then (5) weakens. The next candidate is a
slightly shortened two-step block (u,u), u<3/2, whose exact additional
gradient-variation storage is derived separately. Its loss of quadratic
balance is real and quantitative; it cannot be ignored when testing bridges.

No external theorem is required for the proof. Matlas returned no relevant
result for the targeted query. The exact local GSW2410.16249 definitions of
balanced composability provide terminology only; no general equivalence with
this primitive definition is assumed.

claim: A concrete nonsaturated primitive input now retains a stronger joint objective/dual matrix. For the physical pair(u,u),29/20<=u<=3/2, exact nonnegative interpolation identities give V>=0,H>=0 and V>=(4/5)H+(p,m,q)^T J_u(p,m,q), with explicit PSD J_u and two positive gradient-difference directions when u<3/2. evidence:
# Extra storage from shortening the primitive pair

Status: complete candidate identity, not verifier-accepted. This is a proposed
input for the remaining joint boundary transport, not an improved schedule.
No solver or verifier call is used.

For 0<=u<=3/2 consider the physical pair h=(u,u). Write
p=g_0, m=g_1, q=g_2 and define

    K=1+2u,
    V=2u(f_0+f_1-2f_2)+u(1-u)(||p||^2+||m||^2)
        -2u(1+2u)||q||^2,
    epsilon=(3/2-u)(u+1/2)>=0,
    I_ij=f_j-f_i-<g_i,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

On samples of one convex 1-smooth function I_ij>=0. The following exact
identity retains two independent gradient differences:

    V=I_02+(1+2u)I_10+(3+4u)I_12+(4+8u)I_21
       +(1/4)||p+m-2q||^2
       +epsilon[||p-m||^2+4||m-q||^2].               (1)

All four actual interpolation coefficients are nonnegative, and every square
coefficient is nonnegative in the stated range. Thus this is a full candidate
primitive certificate for the pair. At u=3/2 it reduces to the existing pair
identity in finding b750ce63e2821fa8; the epsilon term is the new retained
slack from changing the physical steps, not the proof weights.

For completeness, here is a coefficient proof of (1). Use x_1=x_0-u p and
x_2=x_0-u(p+m). Then

    I_02=f_2-f_0+(u-1/2)||p||^2+u<p,m>+<p,q>-(1/2)||q||^2,
    I_10=f_0-f_1-(1/2)||p||^2-(1/2)||m||^2+(1-u)<p,m>,
    I_12=f_2-f_1+(u-1/2)||m||^2+<m,q>-(1/2)||q||^2,
    I_21=f_1-f_2-(1/2)||m||^2-(1/2)||q||^2+(1-u)<m,q>.

The weighted sum in (1) has function coefficients(2u,2u,-4u). Subtracting
its gradient part from V leaves a quadratic form on a=p-q and b=m-q:

    (a,b)^T R_u(a,b),
    R_u=[[alpha,1/2-alpha],[1/2-alpha,5alpha-1]],
    alpha=1+u-u^2=1/4+epsilon.

Therefore

    R_u=(1/4)[[1,1],[1,1]]+epsilon[[1,-1],[-1,5]],

which is the sum of squares in (1). Its determinant is
4alpha^2-1/4 and its trace is6alpha-1. At u<3/2 it is positive definite,
because alpha>1/4; at u=3/2 it has rank1. More explicitly,
[[1,-1],[-1,5]] has determinant4 and positive upper-left entry1, so its
quadratic form is ||a-b||^2+4||b||^2.

## Quadratic slack and the precise changed hypothesis

The pair's quadratic response is Pi_u=(1-u)^2. Its quadratic-balance ratio is

    kappa(u)=K Pi_u=(1+2u)(1-u)^2.

For 0<u<3/2, kappa(u)<1, since

    1-kappa(u)=u^2(3-2u)>0.

At u=3/2, kappa=1. If u=3/2-delta with delta small and positive,

    K=4-2delta,
    kappa=1-(9/2)delta+6delta^2-2delta^3,
    epsilon=2delta-delta^2.

Thus shortening the pair supplies explicit positive gradient-variation
storage and strictly weakens the quadratic product test. The unequal-block
obstruction requiring exact quadratic balance cannot be applied to these
inputs without changing its hypotheses.

For three equal copies with bridges1+cK and1+dK, put M=3+c+d. The two
necessary cut tests remain

    Mc<=2+d, Md<=2+c,

while the quadratic test becomes

    Mcd<=kappa(u)^(-3)                              (2)

when kappa(u)>0; at u=1 the quadratic response is zero and this test is
vacuous. Passing (2) is not sufficient for a primitive certificate. It only
identifies a concrete unresolved regime not closed by the balanced result.

## Joint objective and primitive-dual storage

There is also an exact correlated-slack identity throughout the explicit
interval 29/20<=u<=3/2. Define

    H=2(f_0-f_2)-4u||q||^2
         -||p-(u(p+m)+q)/K||^2.

First, direct expansion gives the primitive-dual identity

    H=(4u+1)V/K^2+(2u/K)I_10+(2/K)I_20
                          +(4u^2/K^2)(I_02+I_12).   (3)

Together with (1), it proves H>=0 for this actual pair. More information is
retained by the following identity:

    V-(4/5)H
      =(2/5)I_01+(2u-6/5)I_10
        +(4u-4/5)I_12+(8u-12/5)I_21
        +(1/4)[P||z||^2+2D<z,w>+Q||w||^2],         (4)

where the ACTUAL gradient combinations and scalar coefficients are

    z=p+m-2q, w=p-m,
    P=(-20u^2+36u-8+4/K^2)/5,
    Q=4(3-2u)(5u-1)/5,
    D=-4(3-2u)(5u^2+u-1)/(5K).

The four interpolation coefficients in (4) are nonnegative on the stated
interval. The quadratic matrix (1/4)[[P,D],[D,Q]] is PSD, and is positive
definite when u<3/2. Here is an explicit check. Put delta=3/2-u, so
0<=delta<=1/20. Since K=4-2delta,

    P=[1+24delta-20delta^2+4/K^2]/5>=1/4.

For delta>0, Q>0 and

    D^2/Q=4(3-2u)(5u^2+u-1)^2/[5K^2(5u-1)]
          <=4418/38025 <1/4 <=P.

The displayed upper bound uses 3-2u<=1/10,
5u^2+u-1<=47/4, K>=39/10, and 5u-1>=25/4. Thus its determinant is strictly
positive. At delta=0, P=1/4 and D=Q=0, leaving ||z||^2/16. This is exactly
the older u=3/2 correlated storage, and the second eigenvalue becomes
positive on shortening the physical steps.

For a full matrix on the distinct variables(p,m,q), set

    t11=(P+Q+2D)/4, t12=(P-Q)/4, t22=(P+Q-2D)/4.

Then the remainder in (4) is

    (p,m,q)^T J_u(p,m,q),
    J_u=[[t11,t12,-t11-t12],
         [t12,t22,-t12-t22],
         [-t11-t12,-t12-t22,t11+2t12+t22]].          (5)

It is PSD by (4); its kernel is the constant-gradient subspace when
u<3/2. Equivalently, one may replace m by d_block/u-p to carry the actual
displacement d_block=u(p+m). No initial or terminal gradient of a neighboring
block is identified with these variables.

For a coefficient audit of (4), the following two-parameter identity is
convenient. Choose scalars b0,e0 and put

    a0=2-2b0, c0=2u+2-b0-e0,
    d0=4+4u-b0-e0, f0=4+8u-2e0.

These lower-case subscripted letters in this audit are interpolation
coefficients, not function values or block capacities. The exact expansion is

    V=a0 I_01+b0 I_02+c0 I_10+d0 I_12+e0 I_20+f0 I_21
       +(p-q,m-q)^T R(p-q,m-q),

    R11=2-u^2-(1-u)b0,
    R22=6+4u-5u^2-(2-u)(b0+e0),
    2R12=-[4-2u^2+(2u-3)b0-(1-u)e0].

Set L0=20u^2+4u+1, b0=16u^2/L0 and e0=8K/L0. Substitute this expansion
in (1-(4/5)(4u+1)/K^2)V and then subtract the other terms of (4/5)H from
(3). The I_02 and I_20 coefficients cancel exactly; the four remaining
coefficients are those in (4). Rewriting the remainder using z,w gives P,D,Q
as displayed. These are algebraic identities, not appeals to an unverified
primitive residual lemma.

## What a next join must prove

The retained variables in (1) and (4) are the ACTUAL p,m,q of each block. Since
d_block=u(p+m), they can also be stored as(p,d_block,q) for u>0, without
identifying the next block's start gradient with the bridge gradient. An
attempt to spend the epsilon term across two bridges must preserve these
distinct variables and the four displayed interpolation coefficients. It
must finish with a nonnegative full matrix and an original-objective bound.
No such two-bridge completion or asymptotic improvement is proved here.

author: max2
claim: Quantitative final-stage candidate for EVERY nonnegative prefix: one explicit fixed 2D Huber/capped-quadratic product has error >=q_S+kappa_S(b-b_S)^2 for every appended b>=0, with b_S=psi(S,0), q_S=1/[1+2(S+b_S)], and its full-prefix maximal terminal extension has exact optimized value q_S.
evidence:
# A quantitative final-stage guard for every nonnegative prefix

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No new submission is
authorized. This proof constructs and analyzes the function directly. It does
not use the unverified minimax finding 40601f4c6f496ab8 as a premise. The final
maximal-extension identification uses only accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Statement in the original normalization

Fix any integer k>=0, any L>0, and any finite nonnegative predetermined prefix
h_pre=(h_0,...,h_(k-1)). The empty prefix is allowed. Write S=sum_t h_t. Define

    t_S=(sqrt(8S+9)-1)/4,
    b_S=1+t_S=(3+sqrt(8S+9))/4,
    c_S=1/(S+1),
    q_S=1/(2t_S+1)^2=1/[1+2(S+b_S)],
    omega_S=1/(1+q_S t_S),
    kappa_S=q_S^2/[t_S(1+q_S t_S)].                      (1)

All these quantities are positive, 0<omega_S<1, and t_S>=1/2. The identities

    t_S(2t_S+1)=S+1,
    c_S^2 t_S^2=q_S                                   (2)

will be used repeatedly.

There is an explicit SINGLE convex differentiable L-smooth function f on R^2,
with a minimizer x_star=0 and an initial point x_0 of norm one, such that for
EVERY nonnegative final stepsize b, the GD trajectory for (h_pre,b) obeys

    2[f(x_(k+1)(b))-f(x_star)]/L
             >= q_S+kappa_S(b-b_S)^2.                    (3)

Equality with q_S holds at b=b_S, which is therefore the unique exact-line-
search minimizer for this one function after the supplied prefix. In particular,

    inf_(b>=0) W_(k+1)(h_pre,b) >= q_S.                   (4)

The complete fixed-prefix maximal-interpolation game for the particular jets
constructed below has EXACT optimized normalized value q_S. Thus (4) is backed
by one fixed realizable prefix and a tight terminal completion, not merely by
choosing a different scalar adversary after observing b.

For the Zhang--Jiang bridge notation in the project, b_S=psi(S,0). This is
a final-stage bound depending on the actual prefix sum S; it asserts no bound
on that sum in terms of k and does not prove the all-schedule exact profile.

## 2. The fixed two-dimensional function

It suffices first to set L=1. Define the even scalar Huber function A_S and
the one-sided capped quadratic C_S by

    A_S(u)=u^2/2                         if |u|<=q_S,
           q_S|u|-q_S^2/2               if |u|>=q_S;

    C_S(u)=u^2/2                         if u<=c_S,
           c_S u-c_S^2/2                if u>=c_S.

Their derivatives are respectively the clamp of u to [-q_S,q_S] and min(u,c_S).
They are continuous, nondecreasing, and 1-Lipschitz. The functions are convex
and differentiable, nonnegative, and minimized at zero.

Use the fixed product function and initial point

    F(u,v)=omega_S A_S(u/sqrt(omega_S))
              +(1-omega_S) C_S(v/sqrt(1-omega_S)),

    x_0=(sqrt(omega_S),sqrt(1-omega_S)).                   (5)

Its gradient is 1-Lipschitz: each coordinate gradient has Lipschitz constant
at most one in that coordinate, so the sum of squared gradient differences
is at most the squared Euclidean displacement. It is convex, differentiable,
and has minimum zero at the origin. The initial squared distance is exactly
one. The two scalar coordinates evolve independently under the SAME supplied
stepsizes, starting at scalar value one in both coordinates.

## 3. Every supplied prefix step is legal, in its actual order

Let P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t for 0<=i<=k. Nonnegativity gives 0<=P_i<=S. In the two
scalar coordinates the entire prefix trajectory is

    u_i=1-q_S P_i,    grad A_S(u_i)=q_S,
    v_i=1-c_S P_i,    grad C_S(v_i)=c_S.                  (6)

Indeed c_S=1/(S+1) gives v_i>=c_S, including equality at i=k. Also

    q_S(S+1)=t_S/(2t_S+1)<1,

so u_i>=1-q_S S>q_S. Thus the derivative formulas justify (6) inductively
under every step, regardless of its magnitude or its position in the prefix.
Zero steps merely repeat the same legal data; no strictness assumption occurs.

After the prefix the two scalar coordinates are

    u_k=1-q_S S,    v_k=c_S.

For a final step b>=0 they become

    u_(k+1)(b)=1-q_S(S+b),
    v_(k+1)(b)=c_S(1-b).                                (7)

The second coordinate always belongs to the quadratic region u<=c_S, including
arbitrarily negative values. Consequently its normalized error curve is exactly

    B(b):=2C_S(v_(k+1)(b))=c_S^2(1-b)^2.                 (8)

Let A(b):=2A_S(u_(k+1)(b)). This is a convex differentiable function of b,
being a convex differentiable scalar function composed with an affine map.

## 4. A uniform bound against every final step

At b=b_S the identities (1)-(2) give

    u_(k+1)(b_S)=(1+q_S)/2>q_S,
    A(b_S)=q_S,
    A'(b_S)=-2q_S^2,

    v_(k+1)(b_S)=-c_S t_S,
    B(b_S)=q_S,
    B'(b_S)=2c_S^2 t_S.                                (9)

Convexity supplies a GLOBAL tangent lower bound

    A(b)>=q_S-2q_S^2(b-b_S)                             (10)

for every b>=0, even when (7) has left the Huber linear region or crossed zero.
The exact quadratic (8) expands as

    B(b)=q_S+2c_S^2 t_S(b-b_S)+c_S^2(b-b_S)^2.          (11)

The choice of omega_S in (1) is precisely

    omega_S q_S^2=(1-omega_S)c_S^2 t_S.                 (12)

Multiplying (10) by omega_S and (11) by 1-omega_S cancels the linear terms.
For the ACTUAL single product function (5), its normalized error is
omega_S A(b)+(1-omega_S)B(b). We obtain

    2F(x_(k+1)(b))
       >=q_S+(1-omega_S)c_S^2(b-b_S)^2
        =q_S+kappa_S(b-b_S)^2.

At b=b_S both channel values equal q_S, so the error is exactly q_S.
Since kappa_S>0, this minimizer is unique. This proves (3) and (4) for L=1.
For arbitrary L take f=L F; the iteration x_next=x-(h/L)grad f(x) is the same
normalized iteration, and the division by L in (3) cancels the rescaling.

The terminal gradients also expose why the construction resists line search:

    g_k=(sqrt(omega_S)q_S, sqrt(1-omega_S)c_S),
    g_(k+1)=(sqrt(omega_S)q_S,
                         -sqrt(1-omega_S)c_S t_S).

Equation (12) makes their inner product zero, while the objective stays
q_S/2>0. Both coordinates belong to one fixed legal function throughout.

## 5. The maximal completion of this full prefix is also tight

Apply fact1252b8823bb5a290 to ALL the queried prefix jets of (5), including
their actual values, and let F_max be the pointwise maximal interpolant.
It is legal and agrees with F on every queried point. Since its gradient
at x_k is the same, its possible final points are still (7). Pointwise
maximality and (3) imply

    2F_max(x_(k+1)(b))>=q_S+kappa_S(b-b_S)^2.             (13)

We prove equality at b_S directly by its conjugate construction. Let w be
the terminal gradient of F at b_S, and use the usual prefix y_j=x_j-g_j
and delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2. The two outgoing terminal residuals are

    Q_(k+1,star)=Q_(k+1,k)=0.                           (14)

For the Huber coordinate, both the last query and the terminal point lie
on the same positive linear region, giving equality in both inequalities.
For the capped coordinate, the last query is c_S and the terminal point
is negative, both lying in its quadratic region, again giving equality.
Weighted addition of the two scalar residuals yields (14).

All other prefix residuals with this terminal sample are nonpositive

remote planes. It does not prove the unrestricted exact-profile target.

shared Markov examples and the recursive family are motivation, not premises.
The only accepted result invoked is the definition of the exact benchmark
recursions in fact 0be8b54e0a33381c. No external paper is a black box.

## 1. An exact adjacent criterion for a structured profile class

Write an actual prescribed schedule in chronological order as

    (block_0,b_0,block_1,...,b_(m-1),block_m),

where every block is a finite list of nonnegative steps, s_i is its sum,
and the b_i are checkpoints. Put

    T_i=s_i+1,    A_i=b_i-1,

and assume A_i>=T_(i+1) for 0<=i<m. Thus this part covers the explicit
regime b_i>=s_(i+1)+2; it is not a condition on the unrestricted problem.

Choose positive parameters beta_i with

    beta_i<=A_i/T_(i+1),
    R_i=A_i-T_(i+1) beta_i>=0,                            (1)
    beta_i beta_(i+1)<=1,
    R_i>=beta_i R_(i+1),             0<=i<m-1.            (2)

The last two inequalities are absent when m=1. Define

    q_i=sqrt(A_i beta_i/T_(i+1)),
    a_i=sqrt(T_(i+1) beta_i/A_i),
    alpha_0=1/T_0, alpha_(i+1)=q_i alpha_i,
    zeta_0=e_0,
    zeta_(i+1)=-a_i zeta_i+sqrt(1-a_i^2)e_(i+1),
    omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i.                               (3)

The e_i are an orthonormal basis of R^(m+1). Equations (1) ensure
0<a_i<=1, so every zeta_i is unit and these are genuine Euclidean data.
Fix the SINGLE polyhedral function and its SINGLE Moreau envelope

    J(z)=max(0,<omega_0,z>,...,<omega_m,z>),
    f(x)=min_z[J(z)+||x-z||^2/2].                         (4)

Start at X_0=T_0 omega_0=e_0, and set

    X_(i+1)=X_i-(s_i+b_i)omega_i,
    Z_i=X_i-T_i omega_i.                                 (5)

Then every query within ordinary block i, and the following checkpoint
query, has gradient omega_i. In particular all individual entries of each
ordinary block are executed; their order and their size need not be bounded.
At the endpoint after the final ordinary block, the exact normalized gap is

    V(h,beta)=1/T_0^2 product_(i=0)^(m-1)
                         [A_i beta_i/T_(i+1)].           (6)

The origin is an actual closest minimizer, with ||X_0||=1. Therefore (6)

If s_i>0 for 0<=i<=m-2, conditions (2) are also NECESSARY for the
prescribed data (3)--(5) to be supported by (4). This exactness concerns
this Markov, homogeneous-plane class, with A_i>=T_(i+1). It does not
claim that the three-profile state for general affine histories collapses.

The Markov formula gives

    <zeta_i,zeta_j>=(-1)^(j-i) product_(l=i)^(j-1) a_l,
                                                        i<j.

Since T_(i+1)alpha_(i+1)=A_i alpha_i a_i, (5) yields

    Z_0=0,
    Z_(i+1)=Z_i-A_i alpha_i(zeta_i+a_i zeta_(i+1)).        (7)

Every summand at index l in (7) is orthogonal to zeta_j for j>=l+1.
Hence <Z_i,zeta_j>=0 for every j>=i. For j<i, taking the other
inner products in (7), and using a_l q_l=beta_l, gives exactly

    <omega_j,Z_i>=-alpha_j^2 H_(j,i),
    H_(j,i)=sum_(l=j)^(i-1) (-1)^(l-j) R_l
                              product_(v=j)^(l-1) beta_v. (8)

Every adjacent pair of summands, starting at an even offset from j, is
its nonnegative product weight times R_l-beta_l R_(l+1). If the number
of summands is odd, its last summand is nonnegative. Thus (2) proves
H_(j,i)>=0 for EVERY lag. No inherited plane has been discarded.

At a query after an ordinary cumulative sum u in [0,s_i], the proposed
proximal point is

    X_i-(u+1)omega_i=Z_i+d omega_i,  d=s_i-u>=0.

The current plane has value d alpha_i^2. For a future plane j>i its
value is

    d alpha_i^2 (-1)^(j-i) product_(l=i)^(j-1) beta_l.

At odd separation it is nonpositive; at even separation the product
is at most one by grouping the adjacent factors in (2). Thus EVERY
future plane is at most the current one, including arbitrarily distant
ones and the final plane.

For a past plane j<i, its residual (8) is nonpositive, and

    <omega_j,omega_i>/alpha_i^2
       =(-1)^(i-j) product_(l=j)^(i-1) [T_(l+1)/A_l].

At odd separation it is nonpositive; at even separation the product is
at most one because A_l>=T_(l+1). Consequently every past plane is
also at most the current plane. The zero plane is dominated since d>=0.

It follows that omega_i is an active-plane subgradient at the proposed
proximal point. Adding ||x-z||^2/2 to its subgradient inequality proves

every actual gradient and GD update in the supplied chronological schedule.

convex defining expression. Existence and uniqueness of the proximal point
follow from coercivity and strict convexity. Adding two proximal
subgradient inequalities gives
||g(x)-g(y)||^2<=<g(x)-g(y),x-y>, with g=x-prox_J(x).
The two minimizing inequalities then identify the derivative as g, and
the displayed bound gives its 1-Lipschitz property.

At the final endpoint u=s_m, the proximal point is Z_m and J(Z_m)=0;
thus 2f(x_n)=alpha_m^2, yielding (6). The minimum of f is zero and its
minimizer set is exactly {J=0}. For any such minimizer z,
<omega_0,z><=0. Since X_0=T_0 omega_0=e_0,

    ||X_0-z||^2=1+||z||^2-2<X_0,z>>=1.

Origin itself is a minimizer, proving the exact normalization.

For necessity of (2), at the checkpoint proximal point Z_(i+2) the
current height is zero. Formula (8) at lag two forces
R_i-beta_i R_(i+1)>=0. At the beginning of ordinary block i, with
s_i>0, the future plane i+2 has value
s_i alpha_i^2 beta_i beta_(i+1), whereas the current value is
s_i alpha_i^2. This forces beta_i beta_(i+1)<=1. Conditions (1) are
the requirement a_i<=1 in the specified Euclidean realization. Together
these prove the asserted exact local criterion.

### A completely explicit policy for every schedule in this regime

One need not assume parameters satisfying (2) exist. Set a temporary
R_m=0, and work backward by

    beta_i=min(1,A_i/[T_(i+1)+R_(i+1)]),
    R_i=A_i-T_(i+1) beta_i.                              (9)

This gives 0<beta_i<=1<=A_i/T_(i+1), all neighboring products are
at most one, and R_i>=beta_i R_(i+1) by the displayed choice. Formula
(6) is its exact computable payoff in the supplied steps. There is no
claim that (9) attains the benchmark or optimizes the complete criterion.

In fact imposing beta_i<=1 loses useful constructions. The quantitative
policy below has beta_i=3/2 at every other checkpoint. Future comparisons
require the PAIR products in (2), not the unjustified individual cap.

## 2. Robust nonperiodic transmission at fixed ordinary sum

Fix any common ordinary sum S>0 and put T=S+1. The ordinary lists may
be completely nonidentical as long as each has that sum. Choose 2k
checkpoints, in pairs indexed by j=0,...,k-1, with

    b_(2j)=T+1,
    b_(2j+1)=rho_j T+1,
    9/4<=rho_j<=5/2.                                    (10)

All rho_j may be chosen independently from this interval after the whole
schedule is prescribed. Set

    beta_(2j)=1/2,  beta_(2j+1)=3/2.

Then the residual coefficients in (1) are

    R_(2j)=T/2,
    R_(2j+1)=T(rho_j-3/2).

The critical-to-large inequality in (2) is exactly rho_j<=5/2. The
large-to-next-critical inequality is exactly rho_j>=9/4. Every adjacent
beta product is 3/4. The final residual is nonnegative too. Hence all
conditions are checked for arbitrary nonperiodic variation of the rho_j,
without a perturbative assumption or a discarded remote comparison.

Each pair has the squared-scale multiplier

    q_(2j)^2 q_(2j+1)^2=3rho_j/4>=27/16.

The precise whole-schedule payoff is consequently

    W_n(h)>=T^(-2) product_(j=0)^(k-1)(3rho_j/4)
                            >=(27/16)^k/T^2.             (11)

The cost T^2 is the actual initial-distance normalization at gradient
scale 1/T. It cannot be silently omitted when S grows with the horizon.
The next section keeps that cost explicitly while making both the total
ordinary complexity and the checkpoint amplitudes grow.

## 3. A prescribed growing family and the COMPLETE benchmark comparison

Define c=13/5, a=c^(-17), and finite words

    H_0=(), H_(r+1)=(H_r,a c^r,H_r).

Let s_r=sum H_r. The exact length and sum are

    |H_r|=2^r-1,
    s_r=a(c^r-2^r)/(c-2).                                (12)

For each integer k>=1, set

    r=floor(k/4)+18,
    block=16 concatenated copies of H_r,
    S=16s_r, T=S+1,
    rho_j=9/4+1/[4(j+1)],   0<=j<k.                     (13)

Take 2k+1 copies of this block with the checkpoints (10) between them.
The rho_j in (13) make an explicitly nonperiodic schedule. More generally,
all conclusions about the lower bound hold for ANY choices in the interval
(10). The length of the complete prescribed schedule is

    N_k=16(2k+1)(2^r-1)+2k.                              (14)

The local criterion constructs one global function on R^(2k+1), with
every gradient and query fixed and with origin its actual closest minimizer.
From (12), a=c^(-17), and r<=k/4+18,

    T<=1+(80/3)a c^r<=(211/3)c^(k/4).

Thus (11) gives the explicit bound

    W_(N_k)(h)>= (9/44521)[27/(16 sqrt(c))]^k
                 >=(9/44521)(27/26)^k.                  (15)

The last comparison uses c<169/64, so sqrt(c)<13/8. It does not hide a
parameter-dependent loss. The right side tends to infinity.

For clarity this provides a comparison to the WHOLE exact B_n sequence,
not just its exponent. In the benchmark recursions of accepted fact
0be8b54e0a33381c, B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1>=1, hence U_n^ZJ=1/B_n<=1.
The binomial expansion gives (27/26)^26>2. For k>=338=13*26,

    (9/44521)(27/26)^k > (9/44521)2^13 >1.

Consequently this explicit nonperiodic family satisfies

    W_(N_k)(h)>1>=U_(N_k)^ZJ    for every k>=338.          (16)

The result is confined to the specified family; it says nothing about the
infimum over all schedules at N_k or other horizons.

## 4. The simple benchmark witnesses are weak on the SAME family

Define the full quadratic channel and the sum/single-cut channel by

    Q_n(h)=max_(0<=lambda<=1) lambda product_(t<n)(1-lambda h_t)^2,

    K_n(h)=max{1/[1+2sum h_t],
        max_j (h_j-1)_+^2/
           [(1+sum_(t<j)h_t)^2(1+2sum_(t>j)h_t)]}.

These are the usual quadratic and single-cut Huber lower-bound functionals.
We will prove, on the SAME schedules (13)--(14),

    K_(N_k)<=c^2/(2S),
    Q_(N_k)<=max{1/(4 e k S),(2/3)^(4k)},                (17)

where e=exp(1), and

    max(K_(N_k),Q_(N_k))/U_(N_k)^ZJ ->0.                (18)

This assertion bounds those channels, not the actual worst case, which
grows by (15). It does not assert an upper bound on all scalar functions
or on the verified multi-cut alternating-ray channel.

### Quadratic product estimate for H_r, with all constants

Write b_u=a c^u, and set

    P_r(lambda)=product_(u=0)^(r-1)(1-b_u lambda)^(2^(r-u-1)).

For lambda in (0,1], put z=a lambda and choose the integer v>=17 with
c^v z<=1<c^(v+1)z. Let y=c^v z, so 1/c<y<=1. If a product factor
is zero all the desired upper bounds hold. Otherwise, for r>v,

    log|P_r|/2^(r-v-1)
        =sum_(j=-v)^(r-v-1)2^(-j)log|1-c^j y|.

For j<0 use log(1-c^j y)<=-c^j y. For j>=1 use
log|1-c^j y|<=j log c+log y; these upper bounds are nonnegative,
so extending just their sum to infinity increases it. The resulting bound is

    -2y[1-(2/c)^v]/(c-2)+log[y(1-y)]+2log c
      <=-(13/4)y+log(1/4)+2log c
      <=-5/4+log(169/100)
      <=-5/4+69/100=-14/25<-1/2.                        (19)

To justify the numerical coefficient in the first inequality, since
2/c=10/13 and v>=17, one has (10/13)^v<1/40. For example
(10/13)^5<27/100 and (10/13)^2<3/5, hence its seventeenth power
is less than (27/100)^3(3/5)<1/40. Substitution into
2[1-(2/c)^v]/(c-2) makes it at least 13/4. Also y>1/c=5/13
and y(1-y)<=1/4. Finally log t<=t-1 at t=169/100 proves the last
inequality. These prove (19) without a decimal estimate.

It follows that

    |P_r(lambda)|<=exp(-2^(r-v-2)) for r>v.

For r<=v all factors lie in [0,1], so |P_r|<=1. In particular
|P_r|<=1 always, including lambda=0.

### Quadratic estimate for every complete ordinary/checkpoint pair

First S>35 for r>=18. Indeed the three highest levels of H_18 give
s_18>=1+10/13+100/169=399/169, and S>=16s_18>35. Every checkpoint B
in (10) therefore satisfies

    B<=(5/2)(S+1)+1<=(13/5)S=cS.

If lambda b_(r-1)<=1, all factors of P_r are nonnegative and
|P_r|^16<=exp(-S lambda). For B lambda<=1 the entire macro factor
|P_r|^16|1-B lambda| is at most exp(-S lambda). Otherwise it is at
most (cS lambda-1)exp(-S lambda), whose maximum for nonnegative
S lambda is c exp(-1-1/c)<2/3. The latter exact inequality follows
from

    exp(18/13) > sum_(j=0)^4 (18/13)^j/j!
               =112495/28561 >39/10=(3/2)c.

If lambda b_(r-1)>1, put d=r-v>=1. The preceding polynomial estimate,
lambda S<=(80/3)c^d, and B<=3S give

    |P_r|^16|1-B lambda|
       <=80 c^d exp(-16*2^(d-2))
       <=80 exp(-7d)<5/8<2/3.                           (20)

Here c<e, as e>1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3>c; also 2^d>=2d and e>2.
These justify each inequality in (20). Therefore every ordinary/checkpoint
macro, including either type and every supplied rho_j, has scalar factor

    <=max(exp(-S lambda),2/3).

There are 2k such macros. The terminal ordinary block has factor at most
one. After squaring, multiplying by lambda<=1, and maximizing, this proves
the Q bound in (17), since max_(lambda>=0)lambda exp(-4kS lambda)
=1/(4 e k S). Orthogonal diagonalization of a positive semidefinite
quadratic Hessian shows that its normalized objective is a weighted
average of these scalar objectives, so this controls all convex quadratics
in every dimension.

### Every single-cut term

For all levels u, b_u-1<=s_u. When u<=17, b_u<=1 proves it. For
u>=18, (2/c)^u<=2/5, so s_u/b_u=[1-(2/c)^u]/(c-2)>=1.
At a level-u step within a copy of H_r, both its local prefix and its
local suffix contain a whole H_u, so both have sum at least s_u.

For a checkpoint cut, its size is at most cS, and its complete prefix and
suffix sums are each at least S. Its term is at most c^2/(2S).
For an ordinary cut outside the final ordinary block, its complete suffix
contains that final block, hence has sum at least S. Its own H_u prefix
and b_u-1<=s_u bound the other ratio by one; its term is at most 1/(2S).
For an ordinary cut inside the final block, its complete prefix sum is at
least S, while the H_u suffix gives

    (b_u-1)_+^2/(1+2 suffix_sum)
          <=s_u^2/(1+2s_u)<=s_u/2<=S/32.

Its term is at most 1/(32S). The global sum Huber term is at most
1/(2S). This proves the K bound in (17), covering every cut.

### Comparison to the exact DP profile

Here is a direct algebraic bound on the same exact recursions, included
to avoid using an unverified asymptotic formula. Put C_n=S_circle(n)+1.
The shifted primitive and dominant joins from fact 0be8b54e0a33381c are

    Omega(A,D)=(A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD))/2,
    Gmass(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

They join C_k,C_(n-k-1) and C_k,B_(n-k-1), respectively, and are
increasing in their positive arguments. For t in [0,1],

    t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1.              (21)

One proof sets x=t^(1/3), y=(1-t)^(1/3) and uses x^3+y^3=1 to write

    1-x^4-y^4-x^4y^4
      =x^3y^3[1/(1+x+x^2)+1/(1+y+y^2)-xy]>=0.

The two reciprocals are each at least 1/3, whereas xy<=2^(-2/3)<2/3.
This also covers the endpoints. Since Omega is the positive root of
X^2-(A+D)X-AD=0, substituting
t=A^(3/4)/(A^(3/4)+D^(3/4)) into (21) proves

    Omega(A,D)<=(A^(3/4)+D^(3/4))^(4/3).

Induction in the exact primitive recursion gives C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3).
Also Gmass(A,D)<=D+4A. Induction in the exact dominant recursion,
using C_0=B_0=1, now gives

    B_n<=1+4n^(4/3).                                    (22)

For a split at k, the inductive upper bound is
1+4[(n-k-1)^(4/3)+(k+1)^(4/3)]<=1+4n^(4/3), proving (22)
for its maximum as well.

Finally N_k<=48k 2^r and, for r>=18,
S>= (40/3)a c^r. Multiplying (17) by (22) bounds the K ratio by
a constant times k^(4/3)(2^(4/3)/c)^r and the first Q ratio by a
constant times k^(1/3)(2^(4/3)/c)^r, plus smaller terms. These tend
to zero since r=floor(k/4)+18 and c^3=2197/125>16. The remaining
Q ratio is bounded by a constant times

    k^(4/3)[2^(1/3)(2/3)^4]^k,

which tends to zero because its bracket is less than one. This proves
(18) with the normalization, horizon dependence, and full B_n sequence
kept throughout.

## 5. Exact scope and the next unresolved interface

The new reusable invariant is (1)--(2), with the exact residual formula
(8) and payoff (6). It checks both cross-plane directions for all lags
and computes the genuine closest-minimizer normalization. Formula (9)
is a prescribed feasible policy for every supplied schedule satisfying
the next-block condition. Equations (10)--(18) give a substantially
stronger explicit nonperiodic policy and a growing example beyond the
quadratic and single-cut channels.

This is a structured subclass of the geometric profile state, with
homogeneous planes and zero-height checkpoint proximal points. It does
not reinstate the disproved compression of general positive-level affine
histories. Those still require Phi,Psi, the actual boundary gradient,
and their distance/sublevel profiles.

The condition b_i>=s_(i+1)+2 is a real remaining restriction. When it
fails, the old-plane correlation product T_(i+1)/A_i can exceed one;
the zero residual sign alone no longer dominates old planes at new
positive-height queries. One must use actual retained height/slack data
there. The current proof supplies neither a partition satisfying this
condition for arbitrary near-optimal schedules nor a uniform B_n
comparison outside it. All results here remain unverified research
evidence until the verifier accepts an allocated submission.

## 6. Exact retained loss when the next-block condition fails

The proof above also identifies the complete additional constraint for
arbitrary A_i=b_i-1>0, including A_i<T_(i+1). Keep definitions (1),
(3)--(8), the Euclidean constraint 0<beta_i<=A_i/T_(i+1), and
T_i=s_i+1. Define the empty products to be one and, for j<i, put

    P_(j,i)=product_(l=j)^(i-1) beta_l,
    Q_(j,i)=product_(l=j)^(i-1) [A_l/T_(l+1)].

The exact old-plane comparison on the whole of ordinary block i is

    H_(j,i)>=s_i[(-1)^(i-j) P_(j,i)
                              -P_(j,i)Q_(j,i)]_+,
    H_(j,i)>=0.                                         (23)

Indeed at its proximal point Z_i+d omega_i the old plane minus the
current plane, divided by alpha_j^2, equals

    -H_(j,i)+d[(-1)^(i-j)P_(j,i)-P_(j,i)Q_(j,i)].

This is affine in d in [0,s_i], whose two endpoints are actual samples.
Thus (23) is necessary and sufficient. Future comparisons are still the
even-lag product constraints P_(i,j)<=1 whenever s_i>0. At odd lag the
sign already makes the future plane nonpositive. These are exact all-plane
conditions; in particular the positive-part term in (23) must be kept
when a product of A_l/T_(l+1) is less than one.

They give a concrete interval for appending a new block to a legal prefix.
Suppose block i has already been constructed and A=A_i>0 and the entire
next block, with T=T_(i+1)=s_(i+1)+1, are prescribed. Its only new scalar
is beta=beta_i. For every j<i with i-j odd, use the already retained
quantities

    p_j=P_(j,i)>0,  q_j=Q_(j,i)>0,
    c_j=H_(j,i)/p_j>=0.

The exact admissible interval is

    0<beta<=Upper,
    beta>=Lower,

    Upper=min{A/T,
                  min_(j<i, i-j odd, s_j>0) 1/p_j},
    Lower=max{0,
                  max_(j<i, i-j odd)
                 (A-c_j)/[T-s_(i+1)(1-A q_j/T)_+]}.     (24)

An empty inner minimum is +infinity and an empty inner maximum contributes
zero. Each denominator is at least T-s_(i+1)=1. A nonpositive candidate
for Lower is harmless. These formulas keep every old query and do not
assert that the interval is nonempty.

To check them, (8) gives, at the new even lag from j,

    H_(j,i+1)/p_j=c_j-A+T beta.

Substituting this and the new products p_j beta and q_j A/T into (23)
is exactly the lower bound in (24). If its numerator is nonpositive the
new residual is nonnegative automatically; otherwise the same bound also
implies that nonnegativity. At a new odd lag the old nonnegative residual
is increased by a nonnegative summand and the bracket in (23) is negative,
so there is no extra condition. The immediately preceding plane likewise
has residual A-T beta>=0. A future new plane at an old positive-height
query gives beta p_j<=1 precisely for the indicated even separations;
this proves Upper. Its comparisons at zero-height old proximal points
hold by the exact forward orthogonality in (7). This proves both necessity
and sufficiency of (24) for appending the supplied complete block.

For any sequence of accepted intervals, the same fixed-origin normalization
and product payoff (6) remain exact, with all directions fixed before the
actual GD run. Choosing the largest allowed beta maximizes the immediate
new squared gradient for that retained prefix; no greedy optimality for
the entire remaining schedule is claimed.

### A precise test of the omitted positive-height term

Take three one-step ordinary blocks, each (1), and two bridges each 2.
Thus the complete schedule is (1,2,1,2,1), T_0=T_1=T_2=2 and
A_0=A_1=1. The tempting parameters beta_0=beta_1=1/2 have
R_0=R_1=0, beta_0 beta_1=1/4, so every zero-residual test and
every future-plane test passes. But (23) at (j,i)=(0,2) requires

    0 >= 1*(1/4-1/16)=3/16,

which fails. Concretely their gradients are omega_0=e_0/2,
omega_1=-e_0/4, omega_2=e_0/8. At the initial query e_0/4 of the
last ordinary block, the intended proximal point is e_0/8. The old
plane omega_0 has value 1/16 there, while the proposed current plane
omega_2 has value 1/64. This is the exact old-at-new violation.

With beta_0=1/2 retained, (24) gives Lower=4/5>Upper=1/2,
so no choice of the next correlation fixes that prefix within this
specified geometry. Re-selecting the earlier parameter does: take

    beta_0=8/19, beta_1=1/2.

Now H_(0,2)=3/19 and the right side of (23) is also 3/19;
all the other comparisons hold. Formula (6) gives payoff 1/76.
This is even the maximum in this two-parameter Markov class: its only
nonautomatic old comparison is

    beta_0(3-5 beta_1/4)<=1,

with 0<beta_0,beta_1<=1/2. The objective beta_0 beta_1/16 increases
up to beta_1=1/2, where beta_0=8/19 is its largest feasible value.
This restricted calculation is not the true W_5 of that schedule.

Thus the arbitrary-schedule obstacle has an explicit additional term and
a concrete failed extension, rather than a presumed missing feasibility
theorem. The nonperiodic family of Sections 2--4 avoids that term by an
actual prescribed mass condition. A uniform policy that controls (23)--(24)
while attaining the complete B_n benchmark remains unresolved.

evidence:
# Terminal reduction does not repair the mixed-moment sign by itself

Status: candidate full-identity calculation and scoped obstruction. Accepted
fact1252b8823bb5a290 is the sole external mathematical premise. No solver or
verifier call is used.

Normalize x_star=g_star=f_star=0 and smoothness1. Partition the queried
prefix indices0,...,n-1 into disjoint groups a. Three chronological groups
may be separated by the two bridges under study; bridge samples can be
single-element groups. Every coordinate below is its actual GLOBAL
coordinate, without a reset at a join.

Give each queried sample i in group a a nonnegative weight u_i. Put

    D_a=sum_(i in a)u_i,
    U_a=sum_(i in a)u_i g_i,
    Z_a=sum_(i in a)u_i(x_i-g_i),
    M_a=sum_(i in a)u_i(f_i-||g_i||^2/2),
    N_a=sum_(i in a)u_i[<g_i,x_i-g_i>-f_i+||g_i||^2/2],
    C_a=M_a+N_a=sum_(i in a)u_i<g_i,x_i-g_i>.

These are the actual additional moments from finding6dd1df44d30531f8.
Take D_a>0 for groups that will be divided by their mass; zero-mass groups
can be omitted. Choose scalars t_a>=0 with sum_a t_a D_a<=1 and set the
terminal probabilities

    alpha_i=t_a u_i for i in a,
    alpha_star=1-sum_a t_a D_a.

Choose ACTUAL nonnegative rank-one prefix edge coefficients k_ab>=0 for
every ordered pair of distinct groups, and actual optimum-outgoing
coefficients nu_a>=0. Set

    eta_a=2t_a+nu_a-sum_(b!=a)k_ab D_b
                           +sum_(b!=a)k_ba D_b.

Require eta_a>=0. Define prefix multipliers by

    lambda_(i,j)=k_ab u_i u_j  (i in a,j in b,a!=b),
    lambda_(i,star)=eta_a u_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_a u_i,

with other prefix multipliers zero. Add outgoing terminal multipliers
lambda_(n,j)=2alpha_j, including j=star; add no incoming terminal edges.
All actual multipliers are now nonnegative, and the finite prefix flow at i
is exactly2alpha_i. No signed aggregate coefficient is being mistaken for
an actual interpolation weight.

## Exact complete two-bridge/multi-group identity

For any proposed certificate level q_cert, define

    L_a=2t_a+nu_a+sum_(b!=a)k_ba D_b>=0,
    V_alpha=x_n-sum_a t_a Z_a.

Then accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 and direct expansion give

    q_cert||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i,j)lambda_ij Q_ij
        =||g_n-V_alpha||^2+R,

    R=q_cert||x_0||^2-||x_n-sum_a t_a Z_a||^2
       -sum_a L_a C_a+sum_(a!=b)k_ab<U_a,Z_b>.      (1)

The entire initial-distance term is retained. A valid full certificate
requires this R to be PSD on the full original prefix formal space; the
terminal square does not weaken that condition.

Here is a sign audit. With I_ij=-Q_ij, the exact cross-edge sum is

    sum_(i in a,j in b)u_i u_j I_ij
          =D_a M_b+D_b N_a-<U_a,Z_b>.

Also sum_(i in a)u_i Q_(i,star)=-N_a and
sum_(i in a)u_i Q_(star,i)=-M_a. In the terminal prefix formula, the initial
value coefficient is-2t_a M_a. After adding all star and cross terms, the
coefficient of M_a is

    -2t_a-nu_a-sum_b k_ba D_b=-L_a.

The coefficient of N_a is

    -eta_a-sum_b k_ab D_b=-L_a.

Thus they combine as-L_a C_a, proving(1) and recording every surviving
cross term. Internal all-pairs cycles k_aa>=0 can also be included: add
k_aa D_a to L_a and+k_aa<U_a,Z_a> to the last sum. Their flow is zero.

## The proposed elimination has the wrong direction for every choice in this class

The within-group all-pairs slack gives

    D_a C_a-<U_a,Z_a>=0.                            (2)

But L_a>=0 in EVERY member of the class above, including arbitrary allowed
optimum-outgoing multipliers. Hence(2) implies

    -L_a C_a <= -(L_a/D_a)<U_a,Z_a>.

Replacing C_a by its all-pairs lower bound in(1) therefore yields an UPPER
bound on R. Positivity of that replacement cannot be used as a proof of
positivity of R. The problem is strict whenever L_a>0 and the group's
all-pairs slack is positive. Actual nonnegative cross edges and optimum
flows cannot reverse this coefficient. If t_a>0 then L_a>=2t_a>0, so it
cannot even be set to zero for a group carrying terminal probability.

For a completely legal strict example, take the scalar function f(x)=x^2/4
and schedule(1,0), starting at1. Use the queried prefix samples0 and1 as one
group of weights1,1. Their positions are1,1/2, gradients1/2,1/4, and
proximal points1/2,1/4. Thus

    D_a=2, U_a=Z_a=3/4, C_a=5/16,
    D_a C_a-U_a Z_a=1/16>0.

Set t_a=1/4 and nu_a=0, with no cross edges. Then alpha_star=1/2,
eta_a=L_a=1/2, x_n=1/2, and V_alpha=5/16. At q_cert=63/256 the TRUE
prefix expression in(1) is

    R=63/256-25/256-40/256=-1/128,

whereas replacing C_a by<U_a,Z_a>/D_a gives

    R_replaced=63/256-25/256-36/256=1/128.

This demonstrates the sign reversal on legal prefix data. It does not assert
that R_replaced is PSD on every formal prefix; the false step being tested
is treating it as a lower bound on R.

## What remains possible

Equation(1) is an exact full terminal closure with all moment data retained.
The scoped failure is the proposed deletion of C_a using(2). A useful
implementation must either retain C_a with a valid upper supply bound,
retain an additional signed value/storage inequality, or use richer local
prefix multipliers whose contribution is accounted for in full. Adding the
accepted terminal square alone does not fix this missing sign.

For physical weights u_i=h_i over a contiguous block, one exact alternative
is C_a=(||x_start||^2-||x_end||^2+B_h)/2, where
B_h=sum h_i(h_i-2)||g_i||^2. It retains the gradient moment B_h and the
global-position dependence. Bounding that moment by the earlier scalar
P_theta mechanism pays its explicitly recorded initial-distance factor;
one cannot silently discard it here either.
