evidence:
# Complete normal spectral mixtures remain insufficient after free completion

Status: complete candidate proof, UNVERIFIED. No fact_submit is allocated.
Accepted inputs:1252b8823bb5a290 (interpolation and maximal completion),
dfde2fa326c908bf (complex orbit notation and necessary interpolation), and
b98bb807d514e80d (the exact benchmark recursions). The recursive family and
the real-product method were recalled from PUBLIC candidate79f6ce08b41616b5;
no unverified result is used below. Every needed estimate is included.

The final result is stronger than the supporting individual-mode statement
in Sections1--5: Sections6--7 prove a common unit-step O(c^(-m)) upper bound
for EVERY jointly legal finite normal spectral mixture, with arbitrary complex
spectra, arbitrary horizon-dependent weights and dimension, arbitrary legal
prefix values, and a fully free terminal completion. NO individual-mode
legality is assumed in that final result. A single common interpolation
cycle controls all troublesome modes simultaneously. The exact benchmark
comparison is included, so this is a full obstruction for the stated normal
polynomial-prefix ansatz, not just for separately realizable modes.

## Supporting individual-mode result

Put c=13/5, a=c^(-17), b_j=a c^j, and define

    H_0=(),  H_(m+1)=(H_m,b_m,H_m),
    N_m=2^m-1,
    S_m=sum H_m=a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2).

For a complex z, let x_i=P_i(z) be the chronological prefix polynomial
orbit of H_m, starting from x_0=1, and g_i=z x_i for i=0,...,N_m. Include
the optimum jet (0,0,0). Its complete-block polynomial is

    p_m(z)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-b_j z)^(2^(m-j-1)).

Suppose this FULL prefix is interpolable by a convex differentiable
1-smooth function with minimum zero at the origin. Its values may be ANY
legal interpolating values, not only the maximal path values of the
complex-orbit construction. At the appended final point, use ANY convex
1-smooth interpolant F of the chosen jets, including the pointwise maximal
one and with no condition on its terminal gradient. Then the COMMON unit
step satisfies

    2F(x_(N_m)-g_(N_m)) <= 2c^11/(a c^m).                      (1)

This holds for every m>=1, with deliberately nonoptimal constants.
It also holds for any finite orthogonal mixture of such INDIVIDUALLY legal
complex orbits with squared initial weights summing to one, even if the
joint legal function values and final interpolant are not separable.

The canonical sum-only Huber channel on the appended schedule (H_m,1)
is also O(c^(-m)). The exact recursions imply

    B_n<=1+4n^(4/3),

so, since c^3>16, the maximum of the entire stated witness class and that
Huber channel, divided by U_(2^m)^ZJ, tends to zero.

This supporting result is a scoped upper bound on the stated witness family,
NOT on actual W_(2^m)(H_m,1). It uses full schedule-dependent legality, with
no universal spectral lens. By itself it does not cover jointly legal
mixtures of individually illegal modes. Sections6--7 remove that restriction
using one common cycle. General nonnormal kernels remain outside the scope
even after that extension.

## 1. Universal last-query inequalities and the free unit step

Write z=alpha+i beta and sigma=|z|^2. For z=0 all gradients vanish and
convexity makes every queried value, and the appended unchanged value,
zero. Hence assume z!=0. Interpolation between x_0=1 and the optimum gives

    sigma<=alpha,  alpha>0,  |z|<=1,
    f_0<=alpha-sigma/2.                                      (2)

For any queried i it likewise gives

    f_i<= (alpha-sigma/2)|x_i|^2.                             (3)

The unit-step descent inequality, obtained by integrating a 1-Lipschitz
gradient along -g_i, gives F(x_i-g_i)<=f_i-|g_i|^2/2. Thus for the last
query, independently of all earlier value choices,

    2F(x_(N_m)-g_(N_m))
       <=2(alpha-sigma)|p_m(z)|^2.                           (4)

This includes the maximal terminal completion in accepted1252b8823bb5a290.

## 7. One common complete cycle controls ALL normal modes

Consider ANY finite list of complex numbers z_l and weights w_l>=0 with
sum_l w_l=1. Form the real direct-sum data for the entire H_m prefix by

    x_i=(sqrt(w_l)P_i(z_l))_l,
    g_i=(sqrt(w_l)z_l P_i(z_l))_l,
    x_star=g_star=0.                                        (27)

Real scalar modes are included as beta_l=0. Constant phases in individual
planes can be absorbed by orthogonal rotations. There is no assumption on
the individual spectra or their separate legality. Assume only that these
JOINT data admit actual convex1-smooth interpolation values f_i, with the
given optimum, and let F be ANY legal interpolant of them.

Define constants depending only on c by

    C_aux=K_E c^37+2c[1+4c^2/(c^2-2)],
    C_norm=2c^11+256 C_aux.                                  (28)

We prove the uniform upper bound

    2F(x_(N_m)-g_(N_m))<=C_norm/(a c^m).                     (29)

The spectra, weights, number of modes, and legal values may all depend on
m. This upper bound includes the pointwise maximal terminal completion.

### 7a. The common cycle and its exact recurrence

For any mode z=alpha+i beta, put sigma=|z|^2, kappa=alpha-sigma, and let

    L_r(z)=sum_(i in H_r) h_i |P_i(z)|^2,
    E_r(z)=sum_(i in H_r) h_i^2 sigma |P_i(z)|^2.

Define its reverse-chronological optimum cycle weight by

    D_r(z)=sum_(i in H_r)
                 h_i sigma(1-h_i alpha+h_i sigma/2)|P_i(z)|^2
                  +(sigma/2)|p_r(z)|^2-alpha+sigma/2.        (30)

The cycle goes from the optimum to the end of H_r, backwards through its
queries to its start, then to the optimum. The reverse query edges have
the algebraic weights in(10). Its area and energy alternatively give

    D_r(z)=beta^2 L_r(z)
                 -(kappa/2)[1+|p_r(z)|^2+E_r(z)].            (31)

To check(31), each forward GD edge has area
Im(conj(P_i)P_(i+1))=-h_i beta|P_i|^2. Reversing the path changes the
sign, and the two optimum edges contribute zero area. The cycle energy is
1+|p_r|^2+E_r. The complex cycle identity of accepteddfde2fa326c908bf is
purely algebraic and therefore applies even to an individually illegal mode.

If alpha>0, telescoping squared norms yields

    1-|p_r|^2=2alpha L_r-E_r.

Put d= sigma(1+alpha)-2alpha^2. Substitution into(31) gives

    D_r=[d/(2alpha)](1+E_r)
                    -[sigma(1-alpha)/(2alpha)]|p_r|^2.

Using(22), p_(r+1)=R_r p_r, and
b_r^2sigma|p_r|^2-|R_r|^2=(2b_r alpha-1)|p_r|^2, one obtains the EXACT
recurrence

    D_(r+1)=(1+|R_r|^2)D_r
                         +|p_r|^2[kappa+b_r d].             (32)

For clarity, in the substitution the constant-coefficient difference is
[sigma(1-alpha)-d]/(2alpha)=kappa. Thus no sign in(32) is inferred from
legality or a guessed potential.

Now use the LAST copy of H_(m-1) inside H_m. Its start polynomial is
R_(m-1), and its end polynomial is p_m=R_(m-1)p_(m-1). The SAME indexed
cycle on the full joint prefix has weight

    sum_l w_l D_(m-1)(z_l)|R_(m-1)(z_l)|^2.

Joint interpolation requires

    sum_l w_l D_(m-1)(z_l)|R_(m-1)(z_l)|^2<=0.               (33)

No different cycle is selected for different spectral modes in(33).

### 7b. Classification of every complex parameter

Partition the active modes into the following three groups.

beta^2 L_r>=0 and the bracketed energy is nonnegative. These modes can

complex parameters outside the cocoercivity disk and the zero mode.

    2kappa|p_m|^2<=2c^11/b_m.                               (34)

Also each term in(30) is at least-alpha h_i^2sigma|P_i|^2, so
-D_r<=alpha(1+E_r). With(24),(26), this yields

    D_r(z)>=alpha[(1-exp(-(11/2)q^2))/(2q^2)-1].              (36)

The bracket decreases as q^2>0 increases: differentiating

       >=(9/8)(1-exp(-22/9))-1

## 8. Exact scope of the completed normal-mixture obstruction

Every real finite-dimensional normal operator is orthogonally decomposable
into real scalar blocks and planar complex-multiplication blocks. For a
normalized initial vector, the squared block-coordinate norms give exactly
the weights in(27); initial phases are harmless planar rotations. Therefore
(29) applies equivalently to EVERY jointly legal prefix of the form

    x_i=P_i(A)x_0,  g_i=A x_i,

with one real normal operator A, arbitrary real Gram dimension, arbitrary
legal values, and arbitrary free terminal completion. No spectral restriction
on A is imposed. The finite direct-sum formulation(27) also states the
whole result without using operator terminology.

The horizon after the unit step is2^m. Multiplying(29) and the canonical
Huber bound(20) by B_(2^m)<=1+4*2^(4m/3), proved in Section5, makes both
ratios tend to zero, since c^3>16. This is a full rigorous candidate
obstruction for the chosen NORMAL spectral-mixture ansatz. It does not
upper-bound unrestricted W or exclude a genuinely NONNORMAL kernel.

## Remaining possible repairs

1. Jointly repairing illegal normal modes works in the finite3D calibration,
   but Sections6--7 show it cannot restore the benchmark uniformly on H_m.
   More such normal modes or altered legal values do not avoid(29).
2. A definite nonnormal polynomial kernel can have correlations absent from
   every normal spectral mixture. Replacing it by an arbitrary Gram form
   would merely restate the original problem and is not a quantitative repair.
3. The legal growing Chebyshev constructions remain valid scoped candidates.
   They do not supply the missing uniform comparison on this recursive family.

Multiplying every interpolant by an arbitrary prescribed L>0 restores the
project's smoothness normalization without changing these normalized bounds.

evidence:
# An entire nonnormal affine-gradient obstruction

Status: complete candidate argument, not verifier-accepted. No new verification
allocation is used. Accepted facts 1252b8823bb5a290 and b98bb807d514e80d are the
only graph inputs; all new algebra and the example are proved below. In
particular no earlier unverified obstruction is a premise.

## 1. Class and result

Fix a finite nonnegative prefix h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), allowing zero steps. Set

    s_i=sum_(t<i) h_t,       S=s_n,
    e_i=sum_(0<=r<t<i) h_r h_t.

Suppose real vectors x_0,v,w give queried data at every index 0<=i<=n by

    x_i=x_0-s_i v+e_i w,        g_i=v-s_i w.             (1)

Assume there are values f_i such that all these jets and (0,0,0) have a convex
differentiable 1-smooth interpolant. The values are arbitrary, and the terminal
completion after query n is unrestricted. Normalize ||x_0||<=1.

Assume either S=0, or the LAST POSITIVE entry of h is at most one. Then EVERY
interpolant F of the queried jets with F(0)=min F=0 satisfies

    2 F(x_n-g_n) <= 1/[2(S+1)].                         (2)

Thus (2) applies to the maximal interpolant in fact1252b8823bb5a290 and bounds
the best uniform-in-final-stepsize lower witness in this entire class. It does
not impose any linear relation at the new endpoint x_n-g_n.

For any real linear operator A with A^3 x_0=0, the usual polynomial prefix
x_i=P_i(A)x_0, g_i=A x_i, P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z), has exactly (1), with
v=A x_0 and w=A^2 x_0. Therefore (2) covers every such nilpotent Krylov prefix,
without any bound on dimension, operator norm, conditioning, or dependence of
the data on n. More generally it covers (1) even when no single A realizes it.

This class genuinely contains nonconstant gradients and nonnormal operators;
Section 4 supplies an actual fixed legal function for every nonempty schedule.

## 2. Proof retaining the actual last positive step

Write r=g_n=v-Sw and

    M=sum_(t<n) h_t(S-s_t)=(S^2+sum_(t<n)h_t^2)/2>=0.

Direct substitution in (1), or summation of the actual GD steps, gives

    g_i=r+(S-s_i)w,       x_n=x_0-Sr-Mw.               (3)

The GD recursion itself holds because e_(i+1)=e_i+h_i s_i.

For any two legal query indices i,j, add the two interpolation inequalities
Q_ij<=0 and Q_ji<=0 from fact1252b8823bb5a290. Their function values cancel,
yielding

    <g_i-g_j,x_i-x_j> >= ||g_i-g_j||^2.                (4)

Suppose S>0 and let ell be the index of the last positive step, with
delta=h_ell in (0,1]. Trailing zero steps repeat the same point and gradient.
Hence

    g_ell=r+delta w,
    x_ell=x_n+delta r+delta^2 w.

Use (4) on indices ell,n and divide by delta^2>0. This gives exactly

    <r,w> >= (1-delta)||w||^2 >=0.                    (5)

No other gradient correlation was assumed. In particular it is the final
small step, rather than nilpotence by itself, that supplies the sign.

The optimum interpolation inequality at index n gives

    f_n <= <r,x_n>-||r||^2/2.

For completeness, 1-smoothness gives the one-step descent estimate
F(x_n-r)<=f_n-||r||^2/2: integrate the gradient along x_n-t r, 0<=t<=1,
and bound <grad F(x_n-t r)-r,-r> by t||r||^2 using Lipschitz continuity.
Consequently (3) and (5) imply

    2F(x_n-r)
      <=2<r,x_0>-2(S+1)||r||^2-2M<r,w>
      <=2||r||-2(S+1)||r||^2
      =1/[2(S+1)]-2(S+1)(||r||-1/[2(S+1)])^2.

This proves (2). If S=0, (3) has M=0 and the same last calculation applies
without (5). It also covers r=0 and w=0. All trailing and internal zero steps
were retained, and no division by a gradient or operator parameter occurred.

## 3. Quantitative unbounded-horizon consequence

For each n>=2 take the explicit n-step prefix

    h^(n)=(1,2,...,n-1,1).

Its sum is S=n(n-1)/2+1 and its final step is one. For ANY legal prefix (1),
including all horizon-dependent nilpotent operators above, the same final
choice b=1 therefore obeys

    2F(x_n-g_n)<=1/[n(n-1)+4].                        (6)

The exact benchmark in accepted factb98bb807d514e80d is U_N^ZJ=1/B_N, with
B_N<=1+4N^p and p=log_2(3)<2. Divide (6) by U_(n+1)^ZJ to obtain

    (1+4(n+1)^p)/[n(n-1)+4] ->0.

Thus this entire nonnormal polynomial class cannot supply a uniform matching
lower bound for arbitrary schedules. This is an ansatz obstruction, not an
upper bound on unrestricted W_(n+1)(h^(n),1).

More broadly, (2) applies to EVERY permutation of a multiset whose final
positive element is at most one. Its significance is that adding the second
elementary symmetric moment and a nonconstant affine gradient still leaves a
sum-scale bound whenever the supplied chronology ends with a small step.

## 4. Explicit nonconstant legal realization for every finite schedule

We construct unnormalized data in R^3, then normalize. For any S>=0 put

    q=v0=1/[4(S+1)],          eta=v0/[2(S+1)],
    X0=(1,1,1),              V=(q,v0,0),   W=(0,eta,0),
    X_i=(1-q s_i, 1-v0 s_i+eta e_i, 1),
    G_i=(q,v0-eta s_i,0).

Set Y_i=1-v0 s_i+eta e_i and V_i=v0-eta s_i. We have Y_i>=3/4,
0<V_i<=v0<=1/4, and the first coordinate of X_i is at least3/4>q.

If s_i<s_j, then

    0<Y_i-Y_j=(s_j-s_i)[v0-eta (e_j-e_i)/(s_j-s_i)],
    V_i-V_j=eta(s_j-s_i).

The increment identity for e gives
0<=(e_j-e_i)/(s_j-s_i)<=S. It follows that

    0 < (V_i-V_j)/(Y_i-Y_j)
      <= eta/(v0-eta S)=1/(S+2)<=1.

Repeated values of s_i give identical Y_i,V_i and can be merged in the
following scalar definition. Let phi be the continuous piecewise affine
function through the knots (0,0),(Y_n,V_n),...,(Y_0,V_0), listed in increasing
first coordinate. Set phi(y)=0 for y<=0 and phi(y)=v0 for y>=1. The first
segment has slope V_n/Y_n<=1/3; every other segment has slope in [0,1] by
the preceding calculation. Thus phi is nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz.

Define

    C_q(u)=u^2/2                 for u<=q,
           q u-q^2/2            for u>=q,
    B(y)=integral_0^y phi(t)dt,
    F0(u,y,z)=C_q(u)+B(y).

Both scalar derivatives are nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz. Squaring the two
coordinate gradient differences shows that F0 is convex and 1-smooth, with
minimum zero at the origin. Its gradient at X_i is exactly G_i. Hence all
sample values F0(X_i) satisfy EVERY ordered smooth-convex interpolation
inequality, not only the adjacent inequalities. The actual recursion for
the prescribed steps holds by the displayed increment identity.

Normalize using x_i=X_i/sqrt(3), g_i=G_i/sqrt(3), and
F(x)=F0(sqrt(3)x)/3. Then ||x_0||=1, the smoothness remains one, and the
whole construction is still a single fixed function.

The three vectors X0,V,W are linearly independent: W has a nonzero second
coordinate, V has a nonzero first coordinate, and X0 has a nonzero third
coordinate. Define a linear operator A on this basis by

    A X0=V,      A V=W,      A W=0.

Then A^3=0, A^2 X0=W!=0, and A X_i=G_i. It is a nonzero nilpotent operator
and cannot be real normal: a real normal nilpotent matrix has all zero
eigenvalues and hence is zero by its orthogonal spectral decomposition.
If S>0, gradients change at every positive step. This proves that the
obstructed class has actual curved, nonconstant-gradient legal examples.

## 5. Scope and retrieval

The last-positive-step assumption is essential to the sign proof; nothing
here bounds all nilpotent prefixes ending with a large jump. The result does
not cover higher-degree gradient clocks, nonzero-eigenvalue Jordan blocks,
or an arbitrary changing-generator kernel. It does not use the unverified
normal-mixture candidate as a lemma.

Matlas retrieval for affine-gradient/nilpotent interpolation returned
arXiv:2003.04201 Corollary3.9 (self-contracted small-step sequences),
arXiv:1405.7741 Proposition3 (pseudocontractivity), and arXiv:2111.07720
Lemma5.1 (projected gradient). They do not supply the asserted class bound
and none is imported. A web search located operator-interpolation work and
the standard smooth-convex interpolation paper, but no external result is
used: the needed interpolation inequalities come from the accepted fact.

# A complete candidate obstruction for one real Jordan eigenvalue

Status: unverified candidate. No new fact_submit allocation is used. All new
lemmas needed below are proved in this document; no previous unverified
finding is used as a premise. Graph inputs are accepted1252b8823bb5a290
(smooth-convex interpolation and maximal completion) and b98bb807d514e80d
(the exact benchmark recursions).

## 1. Exact class, recursive family, and conclusion

Set c=13/5, a=c^(-18), b_j=a c^j, and define ordered schedules

    H_0=(),       H_(m+1)=(H_m,b_m,H_m).

Their length is N_m=2^m-1 and their sum is

    S_m=a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2).

For every m>=1 consider ANY finite real Euclidean space, a unit initial
vector x0, a real number lambda, and a real linear operator

    A=lambda I+N,          N^2 x0=0.

The condition is only on the initial Krylov space; arbitrary other action
of A is allowed. At all N_m+1 query indices use the exact polynomial jets

    x_i=P_i(A)x0,       g_i=A x_i,
    P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z),       h=H_m.

Suppose these jets and the optimum sample (0,0,0), with SOME values f_i,
are jointly interpolable by a convex differentiable 1-smooth function.
The values are arbitrary. Let F be ANY such interpolant, including the
maximal one from fact1252b8823bb5a290. Write x_end=x_(N_m), g_end=g_(N_m).

With K=3250 and the finite absolute constant

    C_J=1020+(16/7)c^11(1+8K)(1+9K),

the SAME appended step b=1 satisfies

    2F(x_end-g_end) <= C_J/b_m.                            (1)

No linear-operator constraint is imposed at the new endpoint. Dimension,
lambda, N, conditioning and values may all depend on m. The canonical
sum-based Huber channel is also O(1/b_m). Section7 proves directly from
the accepted benchmark recurrence that B_n<=1+4n^(4/3), so the ratio of
these bounds to U_(2^m)^ZJ tends to zero because c^3>16.

This is a bound on the specified Jordan class, not on unrestricted W.
It does NOT include jointly legal mixtures of different Jordan eigenvalues.

## 2. Exact polynomial identities and a necessary eigenvalue interval

Put u=N x0 and U=||u||. Finite binomial expansion, using N^2 x0=0, gives

    x_i=P_i(lambda)x0+P_i'(lambda)u,
    g_i=lambda P_i(lambda)x0+[P_i(lambda)+lambda P_i'(lambda)]u.  (2)

These identities do not divide by P_i and include repeated polynomial roots.
In particular g0=lambda x0+u and

    A g0=2lambda g0-lambda^2 x0.                           (3)

Let d0=<x0,g0> and e0=||g0||^2. The two optimum interpolation inequalities
imply d0>=e0. The first step of H_m is a>0. Adding its two ordered
interpolation inequalities and dividing by a^2 gives

    <A g0,g0> >= ||A g0||^2 >=0.                          (4)

By (3), the left side is 2lambda e0-lambda^2 d0. If e0=0, then g0=0 and
(3) implies lambda=0; all jets are then stationary. If e0>0, lambda<0
is impossible. For lambda>0 the inequalities d0>=e0 and (4) give

    0<=lambda(2-lambda)e0,

so 0<=lambda<=2. We use this closed interval and do not require endpoint
strictness. Neither an operator-norm bound nor individual eigendirection
legality was assumed.

## 3. A short actual prefix controls the nilpotent component

Consider any initial nonnegative prefix of the same jets, with total sum
T>0 satisfying lambda T<=1/20. For its query indices define

    p_i=product_(t<i)(1-lambda h_t),
    t_i=sum_(t<i)h_t/(1-lambda h_t).

All denominators are positive, and

    19/20<=p_i<=1,       0<=lambda t_i<=1/19.

The lower product bound follows inductively from product(1-r_j)>=1-sum r_j
when r_j>=0 and their sum is at most1. Equation(2) now reads

    g_i=p_i[lambda x0+(1-lambda t_i)u],
    A g_i=p_i[lambda^2 x0+lambda(2-lambda t_i)u].            (5)

Suppose U>=4lambda and U>0. Then

    ||g_i|| >=(9/10)U-(19/20)lambda >=U/2,
    ||g_i|| <=lambda+U <=5U/4,
    ||A g_i||<=lambda^2+2lambda U <=(9/4)lambda U.

At an actual step h_i, reverse ordered interpolation gives

    f_i-f_(i+1)
      >= <g_(i+1),h_i g_i>+||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2/2
       =h_i||g_i||^2-h_i^2<A g_i,g_i>+h_i^2||A g_i||^2/2
      >=h_i U^2/4-3lambda h_i^2 U^2
      >=h_i U^2/10.                                     (6)

The last step uses lambda h_i<=1/20; zero steps cause no division. Sum(6)
over the full chosen prefix. Its terminal value is nonnegative, while
optimum interpolation at the initial query gives

    f0<=<g0,x0>-||g0||^2/2<=lambda+U<=5U/4.

Thus U<=25/(2T). Combining with the alternative U<4lambda proves

    U<=max{4lambda,25/(2T)}<=4lambda+13/T.                 (7)

If lambda=U=0 this conclusion is immediate. The estimate comes from the
actual full-prefix function-value budget, not an imposed normality or
bounded-conditioning hypothesis.

Apply this to H_m with tau=1/100. There are two cases.

LOW FREQUENCY: b_m lambda<tau. Then lambda S_m<tau/(c-2)=1/60, and
S_m>=b_m/c for m>=1. Using(7) on the entire prefix gives

    U<=4lambda+13/S_m,
    ||x_end||<=1+(20/19)S_m U<15,
    ||g_end||<=lambda+U<=5lambda+13/S_m<34/b_m.             (8)

The position bound uses x_end=p_end(x0-t_end u), t_end<=20S_m/19,
and lambda S_m<=1/20. The gradient bound follows directly from(5).

SCALE REACHED: b_m lambda>=tau. Since 2a<tau, there is a first integer
r in[1,m] with b_r lambda>=tau, and b_r lambda<c tau. The actual initial
block of H_m of this depth is H_r. Its sum satisfies

    1/260=tau/c<=lambda S_r
            <c tau/(c-2)=13/300<1/20.

Indeed S_r/b_r=(1-(2/c)^r)/(c-2) lies between1/c and1/(c-2).
Apply(7) to this initial block to obtain the horizon-independent bound

    U<=K lambda,       K=3250.                           (9)

Define the full-block polynomial

    p_m(z)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-b_j z)^(2^(m-j-1)).

For EVERY complex z with 0<|z|<=9/4 and Re(z)/|z|>=2/3, we prove

    |z||p_m(z)|^2<=c^11/b_m.                            (10)

This is an algebraic estimate, independent of any interpolation legality.
Choose the unique integer k with b_k|z|<=1<b_(k+1)|z| and set
y=b_k|z| in(5/13,1]. Because a=c^(-18), |z|<=9/4<c, we have k>=17.
Write q=Re(z)/|z| and z/|z|=exp(i theta).

If m<=k, each factor has magnitude at most one: for t=b_j|z|<=1,
1-2qt+t^2<=1 because q>=2/3. Hence |z||p_m(z)|^2<=1/b_m.

Now m>k. A zero factor proves(10) immediately. Otherwise multiplicities give

    log|p_m(z)|/2^(m-k-1)
      =sum_(j=-k)^(m-k-1)2^(-j)log|1-c^j y exp(i theta)|.  (11)

For j<0, log(1+t)<=t applied to the squared magnitude bounds each term
by -q c^j y+(c^j y)^2/2. Put d=2/c=10/13. We have d^17<1/40: d^3<1/2
and d^2<4/5 imply d^17=(d^3)^5 d^2<1/40. Thus the sum of negative-index
terms is at most

    -(13/4)q y+(25/119)y^2.

Here sum_(r=1)^k(2/c)^r>=13/4 and

    B(y)=900y^4-5841y^3+11372y^2-8925y+2142.

    16B((1+t)/2)
      =-2422-11870t+15842t^2-8082t^3+900t^4
      <=-2422+t[-11870+15842t-7182t^2]
      <=-2422-3210t<0.

The last inequality uses that 15842t-7182t^2 increases on[0,1] and its

We obtain

    |p_m(z)|<=exp(-2^(m-k-1)/128).

Let r=m-k>=1. Since |z|<=c^r/b_m,

    |z||p_m(z)|^2<=(1/b_m)c^r exp(-2^(r-1)/64).

For1<=r<=11 the extra factor is at mostc^11. For r>=12,
2^(r-7)>=r, by induction from12, and log c<1 since exp(1)>8/3>c.
The extra factor is then at most1. This proves(10), including all roots.

## 5. Polynomial derivatives and the free terminal completion

In the scale-reached case lambda>0. Consider the circle

    z=lambda+(lambda/8)exp(i t),       0<=t<=2pi,

and let M0 be the maximum of |p_m| on this circle. Every point satisfies
7lambda/8<=|z|<=9lambda/8<=9/4 and Re(z)/|z|>=7/9>2/3.
Equation(10) therefore implies

    lambda M0^2 <=8c^11/(7b_m).                          (12)

The finite polynomial expansion around lambda gives the exact coefficient
identities

    p_m(lambda)=(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2pi)
                       p_m(lambda+(lambda/8)exp(i t))dt,
    (lambda/8)p_m'(lambda)=(1/(2pi))integral_0^(2pi)
                       p_m(lambda+(lambda/8)exp(i t))exp(-i t)dt.

To verify them, expand the polynomial in powers of (z-lambda) and integrate
each monomial: every nonconstant Fourier mode has integral zero. No external
complex-analysis theorem and no division by p_m(lambda) is needed. Hence

    |p_m(lambda)|<=M0,        lambda|p_m'(lambda)|<=8M0.

Together with(2),(9), this gives

    ||x_end|| <=(1+8K)M0,
    ||g_end|| <=lambda(1+9K)M0.                           (13)

For every interpolant F, optimum interpolation and unit-step descent give

    2F(x_end-g_end)
       <=2<x_end,g_end>-2||g_end||^2
       <=2||x_end||||g_end||.                            (14)

Unit-step descent follows by integrating the1-Lipschitz gradient along the
unit gradient step; it does not assume that the new gradient equals A times
the new point. Apply(8) to(14) in the low-frequency case, and(12),(13) in
the scale-reached case. Their bounds are respectively1020/b_m and
(16/7)c^11(1+8K)(1+9K)/b_m. Their sum C_J/b_m proves(1).

## 6. An explicit legal genuinely nonnormal calibration

This section is not used in the upper bound. It shows that the class has
nontrivial legal prefixes for every supplied nonnegative schedule, with a
single fixed strongly convex function and a uniform final-step lower witness.

For total sum S choose lambda=1/[10(S+1)], eta=lambda/10,
x0=(0,1), and A=[[lambda,eta],[0,lambda]]. Thus N^2=0 and N!=0.

    x_i=(s_i,tcoord_i)=(-eta p_i t_i,p_i).

The use of tcoord_i as a coordinate is distinct from the sum t_i above.
We have p_i>=9/10 and lambda t_i<=1/9. Delete only repeated knots caused
by zero steps. Along every positive step,

    (s_(i+1)-s_i)/(tcoord_(i+1)-tcoord_i)
          =(eta/lambda)(1-lambda t_i) in[0,1/10].

Join these query knots and(0,0) by a continuous piecewise affine graph
s=psi(t). The segment from(0,0) to the last query has slope
-eta t_end with magnitude at most1/90. Extend psi constantly outside the
extreme knots. Then psi(0)=0 and psi is globally1/10-Lipschitz.

Define on R^2 the single function

    F0(s,t)=lambda(s^2+t^2)/2+eta s t-eta integral_0^t psi(v)dv.

Its gradient is (lambda s+eta t,lambda t+eta(s-psi(t))). Thus at every query
it equals A x_i exactly. On an affine piece of psi its Hessian is

    [[lambda,eta],[eta,lambda-eta psi'(t)]].

For any real vector(a0,b0), the absolute value of the perturbation quadratic
2eta a0 b0-eta psi'(t)b0^2 is at most(11/10)eta(a0^2+b0^2). Integrating
the piecewise Hessian along line segments proves that F0 is globally
(89lambda/100)-strongly convex and has gradient Lipschitz constant at most
111lambda/100<1. Its gradient at0 is zero, so F0(0)=min F0=0. All query
values are its actual values; therefore all ordered interpolation inequalities
and the unit initial-distance normalization hold for the SAME data.

For clarity the resulting all-final-step lower bound can also be quantified.
Let x=x_end, g=g_end and z be the orthogonal projection of x onto g-perp.
Here g!=0 and

    |det(x,g)|=eta p_end^2,
    ||g||<=lambda+eta,
    ||z||^2>=p_end^4/121>=1/242.

The determinant identity follows by expanding(2); the terms with t_end
cancel. Strong convexity gives, for every real final b and hence for b>=0,

    2F0(x-bg)>= (89lambda/100)||z||^2
               >=89/[242000(S+1)]>1/[3000(S+1)].           (15)

There is also one test vector satisfying every maximal-interpolant anchor:
put mu=89lambda/100 and w=mu z. Then <w,g>=0. Since F0>=mu||x||^2/2,
its conjugate is at most||w||^2/(2mu). Every quadratic conjugate anchor
H_j from accepted1252b8823bb5a290 lies below F0*, because F0 interpolates
the queried data. Thus, with y_j=x_j-g_j and delta_j=f_j-||g_j||^2/2,

    2delta_j+2<x-y_j,w>-||w||^2
       =2<x,w>-2H_j(w)>=mu||z||^2

for EVERY query and optimum anchor. The maximal completion inherits(15).
This merely calibrates the sum-scale strength of this class; it is weaker
than existing general sum-based lower bounds and is not a new target claim.

## 7. Exact-profile comparison derived from the accepted recursions

Write C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 as in acceptedb98bb807d514e80d.
Their two increasing join maps become

    Omega(A,D)=(A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

For0<=t<=1,

    t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1.                (16)

Indeed put x=t^(1/3), y=(1-t)^(1/3), so x^3+y^3=1. Direct factorization is

    1-x^4-y^4-x^4y^4
      =x^3 y^3[1/(1+x+x^2)+1/(1+y+y^2)-xy]>=0.

Each reciprocal is at least1/3 and xy<=2^(-2/3)<2/3, the latter checked
by cubing. The endpoint cases hold as well. Since Omega is the positive
root of X^2-(A+D)X-AD, inequality(16) yields

    Omega(A,D)<=(A^(3/4)+D^(3/4))^(4/3).

Induction in the primitive recurrence gives C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3). Also
sqrt(D^2+8AD)<=D+4A implies G(A,D)<=D+4A. The dominant recurrence therefore
gives, for each split k and by induction,

    B_n<=1+4[(n-k-1)^(4/3)+(k+1)^(4/3)]<=1+4n^(4/3).

The last inequality follows from superadditivity of t^(4/3), obtained by
integrating its increasing derivative. Initial values are C_0=B_0=1.
Consequently

    (C_J/b_m)/U_(2^m)^ZJ
       <=(C_J/a)[c^(-m)+4(2^(4/3)/c)^m] ->0,

because c^3=2197/125>16. The canonical Huber value on(H_m,1) is at most
1/(2S_m)<=c/(2b_m), so adding it does not change this conclusion.

## 8. Retrieval and remaining boundary

Matlas search for Jordan polynomial interpolation returned arXiv:1802.06355
Lemma7, arXiv:2111.06105 LemmaA.4 and arXiv:2209.07235 Proposition2. None
states the result needed here and none is imported. The polynomial derivative
identity, sector bound, short-prefix coercivity and benchmark comparison are
all proved above. No numerical sweep, symbolic computation, or solver is used.

The proof bounds one real eigenvalue with a nilpotent part of index2 on the
initial Krylov space. It does not silently extend(7) to separately illegal
components of a mixed prefix. Several eigenvalues, higher Jordan order, and
changing-generator/nonlinear correlations remain outside this theorem.

evidence:
# Nonlinear failure of the two-copy ruler despite the quadratic tests

Status: source-based candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No new solver or
fact_submit. The checkpoint application and projection conversion below
are derived afresh; earlier unverified C27 and C29 are not premises.
The external checkpoint construction is the one explicitly permitted in
PROBLEM.md, Section 7, with its source and applicability checked below.

## Statement

Put c=13/5, a=c^(-17), b_j=a c^j, H_0=(),
H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j), and

    s_m=sum H_m=a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2),
    G_m=(H_m,H_m), L_m=2(2^m-1), S_m=2s_m.

There is one fixed integer r such that, for every m>=r+4, an actual
finite-dimensional convex differentiable 1-smooth function f with
f(0)=min f=0, started at a unit vector, satisfies on the whole G_m run

    2f(x_(L_m))
      >= (98/81)^(2^(m-r-2)) / [8(1+s_r)].           (1)

In particular the error grows without bound. For the intrinsic energy

    V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
        +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
        -S(S+1)||g_n||^2,

the same instance has

    V_(G_m)
      <=1-[s_m/(4(1+s_r))](98/81)^(2^(m-r-2))<0.   (2)

Moreover, a negative-energy instance for this identical ordered schedule
can be realized as F_C(x)=(||x||^2-dist(x,C)^2)/2 on a simplex C with
L_m+2 vertices in dimension L_m+1. The sampled gradients are distinct
vertices, and every normal inequality against a different retained vertex,
including zero, is strict. This last conversion retains the sign of V;
it makes NO assertion preserving (1) after normalizing the new initial
distance.

Together with the independently proved, still unverified quadratic/cut
calculations in C29, this supplies an ACTUAL nonlinear rejection of that
test-safe family. The proof of (1)--(2) does not rely on C29. Neither this
example nor C29 decides primitive capacity for arbitrary schedules or
the original unrestricted Zhang--Jiang exact-profile question.

## 1. External construction, constants, and hypotheses

Source: Yuhan Ye and Kaizhao Liu, Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for
Gradient Descent, arXiv:2609.09152v2, Section 3.1, Lemmas 3.1--3.2 and
the pre-weakening final-value calculation proving Lemma 2.2; proofs in
Appendix A.1--A.3. URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09152v2 . The PDF
and extracted text are in downloads/ye-liu-2609.09152.{pdf,txt}. The
arc construction, projection proof, displacement bound, zero regions,
assembly, and terminal calculation were reread for this application.
A fresh Matlas checkpoint-transfer query returned unrelated fixed-step
results, none used. The direct source's identity and version were checked.

The exact input, also given in PROBLEM.md Section 7, is this. Fix positive
epsilon and gamma, and chi=sqrt(1+2gamma+epsilon^2). There are finite
constants A_YL and B_YL, depending only on these fixed parameters, such
that any nonnegative finite schedule with selected checkpoint sizes
z_i>=B_YL admits a finite-dimensional legal function, minimizer zero,
and initial point e_1, with

    2f(x_n)>=1/[2(1+T)]
               product_i [z_i/(chi(A_YL+u_i)+epsilon z_i)]^2. (3)

Here u_i is the sum after the preceding selected checkpoint and before
checkpoint i, and T is the sum after the last selected checkpoint.
The first u_i includes the whole initial ordinary block.

For completeness, the source's local functions are translated/scaled
parameter-one Moreau envelopes of finite support functions. Their
gradients are projections onto finite convex hulls. The backward arc
construction yields the prescribed trajectory for arbitrary intervening
nonnegative steps and a bounded second-coordinate displacement. For a
local checkpoint b>=1+epsilon^(-2), its first coordinate stops at U>=0,
and the function vanishes both when x<=0,y>=0 and when x=U,y>=Y.
Those regions keep every future and past component inactive during the
appropriate part of the concatenated trajectory. The global function is
half the sum of adjacent-coordinate local functions and a terminal
one-sided Huber function. Each coordinate occurs in at most two terms,
so the global smoothness bound is one. Its local steps are h/2, accounting
for B_YL=2(1+epsilon^(-2)). The initial point is e_1 and all activation
offsets are nonnegative, so zero is a common minimizer. There are one
more coordinates than selected checkpoints. If the final transferred
distance is D, the terminal Huber value is D^2/[4(1+T)], yielding (3)
after multiplication by two. No inference from the paper's notation
for its performance measure is used.

Choose epsilon=1/100 and gamma=2099/20000, so chi=11/10 and
B_YL=20002. Choose any permitted fixed finite A_YL. Then choose a
fixed integer r>=18 sufficiently large that

    b_r>=20002,  chi A_YL/b_r<=1/100.

In particular s_r>1. Indeed s_r/b_r>=13/8 for r>=17:
(10/13)^17<1/40 and (c-2)^(-1)=5/3 give this estimate.
All constants are fixed independently of m.

## 2. The one changed ordinary block at the copy boundary

Choose every step of level at least r in EACH copy of H_m. Put M=m-r.
Within each copy, every ordinary block between selected checkpoints is
exactly H_r. The initial and terminal ordinary blocks are also H_r.
At the junction of the two copies, the one intervening ordinary block
is (H_r,H_r), of sum 2s_r. There is exactly one such exceptional block.
The selected level-ell step b_r c^ell occurs 2^(M-ell-1) times in each
copy, for 0<=ell<M. The terminal ordinary sum of the full word is s_r.

For a usual ordinary block,

    chi(A_YL+s_r)/b_r
       <=1/100+(11/10)(5/3)=553/300<37/20.

Hence each transfer factor at level ell is at least

    q_ell=c^ell/[37/20+c^ell/100].

This increases with ell, and direct rational comparisons give

    q_0>=1/2, q_1>=4/3, q_2>=7/2, q_3>=8;
    q_ell>=1 for ell>=4.

When M>=4 the transfer product over one copy, using ordinary block sum
s_r throughout, is therefore at least

    [(1/2)^8(4/3)^4(7/2)^2 8]^(2^(M-4))
       =(98/81)^(2^(M-4)).                         (4)

For the exceptional block, at its actual following checkpoint z, the
ratio of the actual factor to the factor using ordinary sum s_r is

    [chi(A_YL+s_r)+epsilon z]
      /[chi(A_YL+2s_r)+epsilon z]>=1/2.              (5)

All summands are nonnegative, so the denominator is at most twice the
numerator. The full transfer product is thus at least

    (1/2)(98/81)^(2^(M-3)).

Substituting its square and T=s_r in (3) proves (1). All selected
checkpoints exceed B_YL. The special ordinary block is accepted by the
local construction with its actual doubled chronological step list;
no replacement of that list by a single artificial step is made.

## 3. From the objective blowup to a negative primitive energy

For any normalized legal run with minimizer zero and f(0)=0, smooth
convex interpolation (accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290) gives

    I_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2>=0.

Expanding ||x_(i+1)||^2=||x_i-h_i g_i||^2 and summing gives the exact
identity

    V_h=||x_0||^2-||x_n||^2-2sum_(i<n)h_i I_i
                      -2S f_n-S(S+1)||g_n||^2.

For nonnegative steps and S this is at most ||x_0||^2-2S f_n. Using
||x_0||=1, S=2s_m, and (1) proves the first inequality in (2).
Since s_m>=2^M s_r, M>=4, and s_r>1, its subtracted term is greater
than 4s_r/(1+s_r)>2. Thus (2) is strictly negative at every stated
horizon, not just eventually.

## 4. A finite strict simplex witness, with normalization loss visible

Here is the conversion in full, without invoking an unverified reduction.
Write n=L_m; every step of G_m is positive. Let the energy of the actual
nonlinear run above be -v<0. For ell=0,...,n choose
theta_ell=(ell+1)/(2(n+2)), let A_aux=diag(theta_ell), and run
psi(z)=<z,A_aux z>/2 from z_0=(1,...,1) under the same schedule.
The gradients w_i have components theta_ell P_i(theta_ell), where
P_i(t)=product_(j<i)(1-h_j t). Distinct degrees 0,...,n and n+1
distinct theta_ell imply that the w_i are linearly independent. They
also imply that the z_i are pairwise distinct. Since 0<A_aux<I,

    Q_ij^aux=-(1/2)<z_i-z_j,A_aux(I-A_aux)(z_i-z_j)><0, i!=j,

in the convention Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Let E_aux be the finite auxiliary energy and put
delta=v/[2(v+|E_aux|)]. The actual product function
f_mix(x,z)=f(x)+delta psi(z/sqrt(delta)), initialized at
(x_0,sqrt(delta)z_0), has jets
(x_i,sqrt(delta)z_i), (g_i,sqrt(delta)w_i), f_i+delta psi_i.
It remains 1-smooth, its gradient vectors G_i are independent, all its
finite Q_ij are strict, and its energy is at most -v/2. Denote its
points and values by Z_i,F_i for the remainder of this section.

Choose f_* = min_i(F_i-||G_i||^2/2)-1. Independence makes the following
linear equations soluble for z_* in the span of the G_i:

    <G_i,z_*>=f_*-F_i+<G_i,Z_i>-||G_i||^2/2.

Set X_i=Z_i-z_*, V_i=F_i-f_*. Then
V_i=<G_i,X_i>-||G_i||^2/2 and

    <X_i-G_i,G_j-G_i>=Q_ji<0,  i!=j,
    <X_i-G_i,-G_i>=-V_i+||G_i||^2/2<=-1.

Consequently G_i is the projection of X_i onto
C=conv{0,G_0,...,G_n}: the displayed inequalities are the normal
condition against EVERY vertex, hence by convex combinations against
every point of C. Orthogonally project the X_i to the gradient span;
the GD equations, inner products, and all normal inequalities are
unchanged. That span has dimension n+1 and the listed n+2 vertices
are affinely independent.

The function F_C(x)=max_(u in C)(<x,u>-||u||^2/2) is differentiable,
convex, and 1-smooth with gradient P_C: the projection variational
inequalities imply firm nonexpansiveness, and comparison of the two
maxima gives its derivative. It has minimum zero at zero and takes
values V_i at X_i. Translation and common value shifts leave the
intrinsic energy unchanged, so the new energy is at most -v/2.

Finally F_C(X_i)=<G_i,X_i>-||G_i||^2/2 makes every I_i zero, and
expansion of the preceding telescope gives

    V_h=||X_0||^2-||X_n+S G_n||^2<0.

The perturbation and z_* shift need not preserve ||x_0||. Thus the
large normalized objective in (1) belongs to the original source
instance; only the negative sign is asserted for the simplex instance.

# A fixed two-dimensional elliptic function with infinitely many legal copies

Status: complete unverified candidate. This is a positive cross-scale gluing
mechanism and calibration, not the unrestricted exact-profile result. The
alternating test below is already unstable on quadratics. No previous
unverified calibration is used as a premise: all core inequalities, cross
inequalities and the infinite realization are proved here. The accepted
interpolation convention and conjugate construction are fact1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Explicit statement

Set

    A=[[1/2,-4/5],[1/5,1/2]],     x0=(1,0),
    h=1001/1000,    b=1001,    R=-40982041/100000,
    mu=1/10000.

There is ONE everywhere-defined convex differentiable function F:R^2->R
with1-Lipschitz gradient, strong-convexity modulus mu, F(0)=min F=0, and
the following infinite GD trajectory for the fixed alternating steps h,b:

    x_(2k)=R^k x0,       g_(2k)=R^k g0,
    x_(2k+1)=R^k x1,     g_(2k+1)=R^k g1,

where

    g0=(1/2,1/5),
    x1=x0-hg0=(999/2000,-1001/5000),
    g1=A x1=(40991/100000,-1/5000).

Its values at these points are R^(2k) times respectively17/50 and1/10.
The initial norm is one. For every k>=0 and EVERY replacement final step
beta>=0 after the query at time2k+1, this same function satisfies

    2F(x_(2k+1)-beta g_(2k+1))
                   >= |R|^(2k)/4000000.                  (1)

The proof also supplies an explicit orthogonal test vector for each such
terminal query and verifies every maximal-completion anchor inequality.

## 2. A strict finite core, with all perturbation bounds

First use h_old=1 and keep f0=17/50,f1=1/10. The old next point and gradient
are x1_old=(1/2,-1/5), g1_old=(41/100,0). With
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2, direct calculation gives

    Q_(0,star)=-3/200,       Q_(star,0)=-39/200,
    Q_(1,star)=-419/20000,   Q_(star,1)=-319/20000,
    Q_(0,1)=-519/20000,      Q_(1,0)=-219/20000.

Here ||g0||^2=29/100, ||g1_old||^2=1681/10000, and
||g0-g1_old||^2=481/10000, which verify the displayed residuals directly.

Now set epsilon=1/1000 and h=1+epsilon. We have

    x1=x1_old-epsilon g0,
    g1=g1_old-epsilon A g0,      A g0=(9/100,1/5).

All old vectors x1_old,g0,g1_old,A g0,g0-g1_old have norm at most1.
Thus ||x1-x1_old|| and ||g1-g1_old|| are at most epsilon. The two
residuals involving only query0 and the optimum are unchanged. Expanding
the bilinear and squared-norm terms bounds the absolute changes in the
other four residuals as follows:

    Q_(star,1):  epsilon+epsilon^2/2 <.001001,
    Q_(1,star):  3epsilon+3epsilon^2/2 <.003002,
    Q_(0,1):     2epsilon+epsilon^2/2 <.002001,
    Q_(1,0):     3epsilon+3epsilon^2/2 <.003002.

These estimates respectively use the expansions of ||g1||^2/2,
-<g1,x1>+||g1||^2/2, <g0,x1>+||g0-g1||^2/2, and
<g1,x0-x1>+||g0-g1||^2/2. Therefore the new core satisfies

    Q_(i,star),Q_(star,i)<=-delta,     delta=14/1000,
    Q_(0,1),Q_(1,0)<=-eta,            eta=7/1000.          (2)

Also ||x_i||<=1 and ||g_i||<=1 for i=0,1. For query1 this follows from
||x1_old||<3/5, ||g1_old||<1/2, and the preceding perturbation bounds.
Write y_i=x_i-g_i; then ||y_i||<=2.

## 3. Every cross-copy inequality, in both directions

For every integer k>=0 prescribe scaled core data

    X_(k,i)=R^k x_i,       G_(k,i)=R^k g_i,
    V_(k,i)=R^(2k) f_i,       i=0,1.

Add the optimum (0,0,0). Within one copy, all Q residuals are R^(2k)
times the corresponding core residuals. Now take two distinct copies
with absolute scale factors L>s>0; their signs can be either positive or
negative. Since |R|>400, we have L>=400s.

Define the positive optimum margins of any jet by

    delta_i^+=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
    delta_i^-=<x_i,g_i>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2.

Both core margins are at least delta by(2), and scaling multiplies them
by the squared scale. The exact cross residual for a large jet u and
small jet v is

    Q_uv=-delta_u^- -delta_v^+ +<G_u,X_v-G_v>.

Consequently, regardless of signs and chosen core indices,

    Q_uv<=-delta(L^2+s^2)+2Ls,
    Q_vu<=-delta(L^2+s^2)+2Ls.                           (3)

No old/future plane or cross-copy inequality has been dropped.

We will need strong convexity as well. For any sampled jets define

    G_i'=(G_i-mu X_i)/(1-mu),
    V_i'=(V_i-mu||X_i||^2/2)/(1-mu).

Direct expansion of the interpolation residual gives the exact identity

    (1-mu)^2 Q_ij'
       =(1-mu)Q_ij+(mu/2)||(X_i-G_i)-(X_j-G_j)||^2.       (4)

Within one nonzero copy the right side is at most

    [-eta(1-mu)+8mu] L^2<0,

because the difference of the two core y vectors has norm at most4.
Against the optimum it is at most[-delta(1-mu)+2mu] L^2<0. For two
distinct copies, ||L y_i-(+/-s)y_j||^2<=8(L^2+s^2), so(3),(4) give

    (1-mu)^2 Q_uv'
      <=-[delta(1-mu)-4mu](L^2+s^2)+2Ls
      <=-(27/2000)(L^2+s^2)+2Ls<0.                       (5)

Here delta(1-mu)-4mu=.0135986>27/2000=.0135, and
2Ls<=L^2/200 because L>=400s. The same estimate holds for Q_vu'.
This proves ALL transformed interpolation inequalities for the entire
countably infinite set of scaled jets and the optimum.

## 4. One global interpolant for the infinite set

For each transformed sample put

    y_i'=X_i-G_i',          d_i'=V_i'-||G_i'||^2/2,
    H_i'(v)=||v||^2/2+<y_i',v>-d_i'.

The optimum anchor is H_star'(v)=||v||^2/2. The transformed strict optimum
residuals proved above imply d_i'>0 on the two unscaled core jets. For the
kth copy, y_i' scales by R^k and d_i' by R^(2k). Hence, for each fixed v,

    <R^k y_i',v>-R^(2k)d_i' -> -infinity.

The same convergence is uniform on any bounded set of v. Therefore

    H'(v)=sup_i H_i'(v),       F'(x)=sup_v(<x,v>-H'(v))     (6)

defines an everywhere finite continuous1-strongly convex H'. Locally it
is the maximum of finitely many anchors. Moreover H'(v)>=||v||^2/2,
H'(0)=0, and H' is minimized at0.

For each x the conjugate supremum has a unique maximizer g(x): existence
follows from the quadratic lower bound on H', and uniqueness from its
strong convexity. The optimality inequalities for two points x,y imply
<g(x)-g(y),x-y>>=||g(x)-g(y)||^2, hence ||g(x)-g(y)||<=||x-y||.
The two supremum inequalities also bound the remainder in
F'(x+d)-F'(x)-<g(x),d> between0 and
<g(x+d)-g(x),d>, which is at most||d||^2. Thus F' is differentiable
with gradient g and1-Lipschitz gradient. It is convex and has minimum0 at0.

All interpolation inequalities Q_ij'<=0 say that at v=G_i' the i-th
anchor attains the supremum in(6). Its gradient there is X_i. Thus
X_i belongs to the subgradient of H' at G_i'; conjugate equality gives
F'(X_i)=V_i' and grad F'(X_i)=G_i'. This checks every sample, including
the infinite collection. Finally set

    F(x)=(1-mu)F'(x)+mu||x||^2/2.                        (7)

It interpolates all ORIGINAL scaled jets, is mu-strongly convex, and has
gradient Lipschitz constant at most(1-mu)+mu=1. It is one fixed function,
independent of the horizon at which the trajectory is inspected.

## 5. The actual alternating trajectory

The characteristic identity for A is

    A^2-A+(41/100)I=0.

Since h+b=hb, we obtain the exact matrix identity

    (I-bA)(I-hA)=[1-(41/100)hb]I=R I.                  (8)

Indeed hb=1002001/1000 and 1-(41/100)hb=-40982041/100000. Starting
at x0, the h step reaches x1 and the b step reaches R x0. Repetition
of(8) proves the full trajectory in Section1. Equation(7) is the SAME
function at all these query times; no oracle or function is reset.

## 6. Uniform terminal payoff and all anchors

The complex representation A=T B T^(-1), with T=diag(1,1/2) and
z=1/2+(2/5)i, gives

    |det(x1,g1)|=(1/5)|1-hz|^2.

Both |Re(1-hz)|=999/2000 and |Im(1-hz)|=1001/2500 exceed2/5.
Thus |1-hz|^2>8/25 and |det(x1,g1)|>8/125>1/20. Because ||g1||<=1,
the distance from x1 to span(g1) is greater than1/20.

Let x=R^k x1, g=R^k g1 and let z_perp be the orthogonal projection of
x onto g-perp. Then ||z_perp||^2>|R|^(2k)/400. Strong convexity of(7)
and its minimizer0 imply, for every real beta,

    2F(x-beta g)>=mu||x-beta g||^2
                  >=mu||z_perp||^2>|R|^(2k)/4000000,

which proves(1). In particular the final gradient is not forced to follow
the linear operator beyond this last query.

For the finite prefix through this query, define the ordinary conjugate
anchors H_j(v)=||v||^2/2+<x_j-g_j,v>-(f_j-||g_j||^2/2). Since F is
an actual1-smooth interpolant, H_j<=F* for every query and optimum anchor,
as in accepted1252b8823bb5a290. Strong convexity gives
F*(w)<=||w||^2/(2mu). With w=mu z_perp we therefore have <w,g>=0 and

    2(f_j-||g_j||^2/2)+2<x-(x_j-g_j),w>-||w||^2
       =2<x,w>-2H_j(w)>=mu||z_perp||^2

for EVERY anchor. Hence the same lower bound is visible in the requested
orthogonal-terminal-vector formulation as well as in the fixed function.

## 7. What this proves and what it does not

The proof gives a concrete way to glue an infinite family of legal scaled
copies while retaining every crossing constraint and a common strong
convexity modulus. Strict optimum margins pay for the cross terms when
radial scale ratios are large. This is a sufficient condition with an actual
fixed realization; it is not lossless gluing of arbitrary boundary jets.

The alternating schedule already has huge quadratic error, for example
its pair multiplier at scalar curvature1/2 is
(1-h/2)(1-b/2)=-(999/2000)(999/2), whose magnitude exceeds one.
Therefore this example does not establish a new family where the quadratic
channel misses the benchmark. Its role is to make the positive elliptic
copy mechanism concrete. For the geometric ruler family at a dyadic
resonance, the still-missing step is a legal expanding finite core and
quantitative control of its rotated copies.

author: max2
claim: Quantitative obstruction on the ASSIGNED near-critical ruler: the ENTIRE elliptic parabolic regime z_m=1-u_m/m+i v_m/sqrt(m), with u_m bounded and v_m in any fixed positive compact interval, has superexponentially small free-terminal payoff for every horizon-dependent SPD metric. Full legality forces u_m>=[1+sqrt2/(3-sqrt2)]v_m²-o(1), and then every final b in[0,2], including the original d0, gives error <=(2304/v_-²)m exp[-2^(m+1)/(3m)]=o(U_(2^m-1)^ZJ). evidence:
# Near-critical ruler: a quantitative parabolic elliptic obstruction

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or new
fact_submit is used. Accepted facts1252b8823bb5a290 and b98bb807d514e80d
supply the interpolation convention and the benchmark definition/bound.
Every new phase, averaging, polynomial and conditioning estimate is proved
below. In particular the earlier isotropization counterexample and the
earlier elliptic interface are not invoked as unverified lemmas.

## 1. The actual assigned schedule and the entire parameter regime

For each integer m>=128 put

    s=1+sqrt(2),      c=c_m=s(1+1/m),
    a=a_m=(1-1/m)/c,  d_j=1+a c^j,
    H_0=(),          H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1.

All parameters remain fixed as j varies within this horizon. Let h_pre be
H_m with its last d_0 removed, so it has n-1 steps. All n queried prefix
points, including the last point x_(n-1), will be retained.

Fix arbitrary finite constants U>0 and 0<v_-<=v_+. For each m allow ANY
real u_m and v_m with |u_m|<=U and v_-<=v_m<=v_+, and set

    alpha_m=1-u_m/m,     beta_m=v_m/sqrt(m),
    z_m=alpha_m+i beta_m.

Choose ANY real invertible2x2 matrix T_m with ||T_m e1||=1. Its norm and
condition number may depend arbitrarily on m. At the actual prefix query
indices use the elliptic polynomial data

    x_i=T_m(Re P_i(z_m),Im P_i(z_m)),
    g_i=T_m(Re[z_m P_i(z_m)],Im[z_m P_i(z_m)]),
    P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_pre,t z).

Assume that SOME values f_i make these same real jets and(0,0,0) fully
interpolable by a convex differentiable1-smooth function. For every such
interpolant F, with F(0)=min F=0, and every final step b in[0,2], we prove
the uniform estimate, for all sufficiently large m,

    2F(x_(n-1)-b g_(n-1))
      <= (2304/v_-^2)m exp[-2^(m+1)/(3m)].                (1)

The threshold in m depends only on U,v_-,v_+. Thus even with arbitrary
horizon-dependent metrics, values and free terminal completion, this
ENTIRE compact parabolic regime has payoff o(U_n^ZJ). The interval[0,2]
includes both the common comparison step1 and the original final d_0.

A necessary condition for legality, uniformly over the same regime, is

    u_m >= (1+A0)v_m^2-o(1),
    A0=sqrt(2)/(3-sqrt(2)).                              (2)

This is not an exclusion of all elliptic frequencies, an upper bound on
unrestricted W, or a resolution of the original exact-profile problem.

## 2. Complete-cycle averaging over actual early copies

For this proof abbreviate alpha=alpha_m, beta=beta_m, z=z_m and
M=T_m^T T_m. Then M is positive definite and M_11=1. Multiplication by z
has real matrix B=[[alpha,-beta],[beta,alpha]]. Define the full partial
word polynomials and copy multipliers

    p_j(z)=product_(ell<j)(1-d_ell z)^(2^(j-ell-1)),
    R_j(z)=p_j(z)(1-d_j z).

Every query position in H_j, in complex coordinates, is a product of a
subset of R_0,...,R_(j-1). Indeed the right copy in H_(j+1) multiplies
every old position by R_j, whereas the left copy leaves it unchanged.

The entire first H_(m-1) is contained in h_pre. It contains2^(m-2)
copies of the two-query word H_1=(d_0), with starting multipliers equal
to all subset products of R_1,...,R_(m-2). All these multipliers are
nonzero because z is nonreal and all d_j are real.

Consider the directed triangle star -> next query -> first query -> star
in any one of these copies. Sum the full interpolation inequalities on
that triangle, eliminating the values. Divide by the squared modulus of
its starting multiplier. Its legality becomes the same base triangle
tested with the rotated metric R_theta^T M R_theta, where theta is the
argument of the starting multiplier and R_theta is planar rotation.
Averaging all these ACTUAL cycle inequalities therefore gives legality
of the base triangle under one effective metric M_bar.

Put tau=tr(M)/2. Rotation averaging preserves its scalar part tau I. On
the traceless part, each binary copy average multiplies its norm by
|cos(arg R_j)|. To verify this directly, identify a traceless symmetric
matrix[[q,r],[r,-q]] with q+i r. Rotation conjugation multiplies it by
exp(+/-2i theta), and averaging identity and this rotation multiplies
its modulus by |(1+exp(2i theta))/2|=|cos theta|. Consequently

    M_bar=tau I+E,
    ||E||_op<=tau Gamma_m,
    Gamma_m=product_(j=1)^(m-2)|cos(arg R_j(z))|.          (3)

The bound on the initial traceless part uses only positive definiteness:
its eigenvalues have magnitude at most tau. It is uniform in conditioning.

## 3. A finite-horizon averaging estimate that includes resonances

For m>=128, the inequalities12/5<s<17/7 give
c<=2193/896<5/2 and a>=(127/128)/(5/2)=127/320>3/8;
also c>12/5. The bounds on s follow by squaring7/5 and10/7 to bound
sqrt(2). For all sufficiently large m, uniformly in our parameter range, alpha>=3/4,
alpha<=2, beta<=1/8, and |1-alpha|<=a/4. Thus

    alpha d_j-1=alpha a c^j-(1-alpha)>=a c^j/2>0.

Choose the principal factor phases

    phi_j=arg(1-d_j z)
          =-pi+arctan[beta d_j/(alpha d_j-1)],
    Phi=sum_(j>=0)2^(-j-1)phi_j=-pi+delta.

The series converges by the bounded phases and summable weights. Since
alpha<=2, alpha>=3/4 and a>=3/8, the arctangent arguments are bounded
between beta/2 and8beta. For sufficiently small beta, arctan t is between
t/2 and t for this range. Therefore

    beta/4<=delta<=8beta.                                (4)

As j grows, phi_j decreases to phi_infinity=-pi+arctan(beta/alpha).
The difference of its two arctangent arguments is exactly

    beta[d_j/(alpha d_j-1)-1/alpha]
      =beta/[alpha(alpha d_j-1)]<=8beta c^(-j).

Since arctan is1-Lipschitz,
0<=phi_j-phi_infinity<=8beta c^(-j). Direct summation of polynomial
multiplicities gives an unwrapped phase identity

    arg R_j=2^j Phi+epsilon_j,
    epsilon_j=phi_j-sum_(ell>=0)2^(-ell-1)phi_(j+ell),
    0<=epsilon_j<=8beta c^(-j).                          (5)

Choose k so that2^k delta lies in[pi/4,pi/2). For large m this integer
satisfies1<=k<=m-2 and2^k<=8/beta, by(4). Discarding earlier cosine
factors only increases the product. Because2^j Phi differs from2^j delta
by an integer multiple of pi, the1-Lipschitz property of |cos| and a
telescoping difference of products of numbers in[0,1] give

    Gamma_m
      <=product_(j=k)^(m-2)|cos(2^j delta)|
                          +sum_(j=k)^(m-2)epsilon_j
      <=[1/(2^(m-1-k)|sin(2^k delta)|)]
                          +8beta c^(-k)/(1-c^(-1)).      (6)

The product identity in the last line follows by iterating
sin(2t)=2sin(t)cos(t); its denominator is nonzero because
2^k delta is in[pi/4,pi/2). This calculation works unchanged at exact
dyadic resonance, where the numerator may vanish.

Let r0=log_2(12/5)>0. Since2^(-k)<=4delta/pi<=11beta, c<=5/2 and
c>=12/5, the bounds above imply, for an absolute constant C,

    Gamma_m<=C[2^(-m)/beta+beta^(1+r0)].                  (7)

For example c^(-k)=(2^(-k))^(log_2 c)<=C beta^r0, since beta<1 and
log_2 c lies in a fixed compact interval. Because beta is bounded above
and below by positive constants times m^(-1/2), (7) yields

    Gamma_m/beta ->0                                    (8)

uniformly in all the stated parameters. This is a FINITE-HORIZON bound
in this specific regime, not the false assertion that every fixed nonreal
parameter has a vanishing infinite tail product.

## 4. The averaged triangle forces the parabolic legality constant

Write d=d_0, e1=(1,0), v0=B e1, r1=e1-d v0 and v1=B r1. The base
triangle weight under a metric M is tr(M Z), with the symmetric matrix

    Z=(v1 v1^T)/2+d sym(v0 v1^T)
          +(v0-v1)(v0-v1)^T/2-sym(e1 v0^T)+(v0 v0^T)/2,
    sym(C)=(C+C^T)/2.                                  (9)

This follows by writing its three edge weights: ||v1||_M^2/2,
d<v1,v0>_M+||v0-v1||_M^2/2, and-<v0,e1>_M+||v0||_M^2/2.
For M=I, direct expansion gives

    tr(Z)=d beta^2-(alpha-|z|^2)(1-d alpha+d^2|z|^2).    (10)

We also need an error bound uniform in M. At z=1, Z=0 for every d.
When |z|<=2 and1<=d<=2, put w=z-1. Then
||v0-e1||<=|w|, ||r1-(1-d)e1||<=2|w|, and
||v1-(1-d)e1||<=7|w|; also||v0||<=2, ||v1||<=10.
Applying ||aa^T-bb^T||_op<=(||a||+||b||)||a-b|| to(9), and expanding
its mixed product, bounds its five differences from z=1 by respectively
38.5|w|,34|w|,56|w|,|w| and1.5|w|. Thus

    ||Z||_op<=132|w|<=264beta                            (11)

for all sufficiently large m, since |alpha-1|=O(m^(-1))=o(beta).

The averaged legal triangle from Section2 satisfies tr(M_bar Z)<=0.
Using(3),(11), and |tr(E Z)|<=2||E||_op||Z||_op, gives

    d beta^2-(alpha-|z|^2)(1-d alpha+d^2|z|^2)
                  <=528 Gamma_m beta=o(beta^2).         (12)

Here tau>0 cancels; no condition-number loss occurs. Now d tends to
sqrt(2), alpha tends to1, and |z|^2 tends to1, so the denominator
1-d alpha+d^2|z|^2 tends to3-sqrt(2)>0. Moreover

    alpha-|z|^2=(u_m-v_m^2)/m-u_m^2/m^2.

Divide(12) by beta^2=v_m^2/m. This proves precisely the uniform
necessary condition(2).

## 5. The full polynomial potential, with a uniform remainder

Put w=z-1, t_j=d_j/(d_j-1)=1+1/(a c^j), and N=2^m-1. For m>=128,
1<=t_j<4. Factor each complex magnitude exactly as

    |1-d_j z|=a c^j |1+t_j w|.

The level multiplicities satisfy sum_j2^(m-j-1)=N and
sum_j j2^(m-j-1)=N-m. Define

    L_m(w)=log(ac)+Re sum_(j>=0)2^(-j-1)log(1+t_j w),

where the logarithms use their convergent power series near1. For
|w|<=1/8, their cubic remainders are at most128|w|^3: bound the terms
of degree>=3 by2|t_j w|^3. Summing the linear and quadratic terms yields

    L_m(w)=log(1-1/m)+D_m Re(w)-(J_m/2)Re(w^2)+O(|w|^3),
    D_m=1+1/[a(2-c^(-1))],
    J_m=1+2/[a(2-c^(-1))]+1/[a^2(2-c^(-2))].            (13)

All remainder constants are uniform over the compact parameter regime.
Because w=-u_m/m+i v_m/sqrt(m),

    L_m(w)=[-1-u_m D_m+(v_m^2/2)J_m]/m+O(m^(-3/2)).     (14)

At the limits c=s, a=1/s, use s^2=2s+1 to obtain

    D=lim D_m=2+2/(2s-1)>5/2,
    J=lim J_m=6+4/(2s-1)+2/(4s+1)<15/2.                (15)

For the inequalities,12/5<s<5/2 implies2s-1<4 and
4/(2s-1)+2/(4s+1)<20/19+10/53<3/2. Also

    1+A0=3/(4-s)>15/8.

By(2),(15), the coefficient in(14) is at most

    -1-[(1+A0)D-J/2]v_m^2+o(1)
          <=-1-(15/16)v_m^2+o(1).

In particular legality forces L_m(w)<=-1/(2m) for sufficiently large m.

The exact finite product differs from its infinite weighted sum only by
a controlled tail:

    log|p_m(z)|
      =2^m L_m(w)-log(ac)-m log c
             -2^m Re sum_(j>=m)2^(-j-1)log(1+t_j w).

The absolute value of the last term is at most8|w|, since
|log(1+t_j w)|<=2t_j|w|<=8|w|. Therefore, uniformly over all legal
parameters under consideration,

    log|p_m(z)|<=-2^m/(3m)                              (16)

for all sufficiently large m. This includes zeros without a division;
in fact nonreal z makes every factor nonzero here.

## 6. Conditioning, the deleted last step, and free completion

The two initial optimum interpolation inequalities give
<x0,g0>>=||g0||^2. Since ||x0||=1, this implies ||g0||<=1. But

    g0=alpha T_m e1+beta T_m e2,

so ||T_m e2||<=(1+|alpha|)/beta<=3/beta. Hence

    ||T_m||_op<=1+3/beta<=4/beta.                       (17)

This bounds the actual two-vector realization despite arbitrary initial
conditioning. Let p_pre(z)=p_m(z)/(1-d_0 z), the polynomial of the
actual queried prefix. From Section3,
|1-d_0 z|>=alpha d_0-1>=a/2>=3/16, so

    |p_pre(z)|<=6|p_m(z)|,
    ||x_(n-1)||<=4|p_pre(z)|/beta,
    ||g_(n-1)||<=8|p_pre(z)|/beta.                      (18)

No condition at a later gradient is used. For any convex1-smooth
interpolant of these queried data, optimum interpolation gives
f_(n-1)<=<x_(n-1),g_(n-1)>-||g_(n-1)||^2/2. Smoothness along a final
step b in[0,2] gives F(x-bg)<=f_(n-1)-b(1-b/2)||g||^2<=f_(n-1).
Equations(16)--(18) now imply

    2F(x-bg)<=2||x||||g||
       <=2304|p_m(z)|^2/beta^2
       <=(2304/v_-^2)m exp[-2^(m+1)/(3m)],

proving(1) for EVERY completion and every final b in the stated interval.

## 7. Exact benchmark comparison and remaining scope

Acceptedb98bb807d514e80d gives B_n<=1+4n^(log_2 3). Since n<2^m,
the ratio of(1) to U_n^ZJ=1/B_n is at most

    (2304/v_-^2)m(1+4*3^m) exp[-2^(m+1)/(3m)] ->0.

The exponential dominates because2^m/m grows faster than any constant
multiple of m, which follows for example by successive doubling after
a fixed sufficiently large index. This uses the actual accepted B_n
bound, not a guessed dyadic benchmark constant.

The obstruction covers all horizon-dependent elliptic metrics in the
entire compact regime alpha=1-O(1/m), beta comparable to m^(-1/2).
It specifically closes the natural near-unit polynomial-growth attempt:
the same cycles that allow a free terminal completion force damping of
the chronological polynomial before that completion. Other imaginary
scales, other real parts, multiple modes and changing generators are not
covered. The arbitrary-schedule exact-profile target is unchanged.

For EVERY endpoint interval-projection witness, full-curvature quadratic, middle-cut interval, one-sided Huber witness in its stated domain, and orthogonal mixed witness, the assigned values obey f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2 and the final query obeys x_3=g_3. This reproduces the mathematical ingredients below rather than adopting an unverified finding as a fact.

# A necessary asymmetric region for a three-step capacity improvement

Status: complete candidate reductions and a scoped optimization result;
NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or fact_submit. The public max4 candidates
5b4359baa88bf3e4 and 500d209094028aef suggested the witnesses; all needed
legal data and deductions are included here, not used as unverified facts.
Accepted input: smooth-convex interpolation in 1252b8823bb5a290.

## 1. Statement

For h=(u,v,w) in [0,infinity)^3 put T=1+u+v+w. Write V_h for the
intrinsic primitive energy defined below. Call h primitive if V_h>=0
on every finite-dimensional convex differentiable 1-smooth GD run with
a minimizer. Put t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, and T_0=lambda^2=3+2t.

If h is primitive and T>=T_0, then either

    h=(t,2,t), T=T_0,

or necessarily

    t<u<7/4,   1<v<2,   1<w<t,
    T_0<=T<7,  u+w>=2T/lambda-2.                   (1)

The scalar constraints below further restrict the remaining region.
This does NOT exclude region (1) and does NOT prove the global
three-step capacity bound. It is a global, orientation-sensitive
reduction beyond the existing local and fixed-middle-step results.

For the remaining region, the one-parameter completion of the mixed
two-dimensional witness in Section5 cannot strengthen its original
endpoint choice. Every finite interpolation inequality is checked.

## 2. Actual witnesses and all their legality conditions

For any legal run use

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0,
    V_h=2sum_(i<3)h_i(f_i-f_3)
         +sum_(i<3)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
         -(T-1)T||g_3||^2.

For data with f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2 and x_3=g_3, set
y_i=x_i-g_i. Expansion gives

    Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>, Q_(i,3)=0,
    V_h=||x_0||^2-T^2||g_3||^2.                   (2)

All witnesses used below have these properties and include the legal
optimum jet (0,0,0). Besides the finite Q conditions, optimum legality
requires <g_i,y_i>>=0; the other direction is saturated by the value
formula. A feasible finite array is realized by the conjugate maximum
of quadratics in accepted 1252b8823bb5a290. Thus the arrays specify
fixed globally smooth convex functions with a minimizer.

The interval-projection witness at any selected step b, with ordinary
sums P,Q, has gradient 1 before b and -(b-1)/(Q+1) after it, starting
at P+1 and ending at its negative threshold, when b>1. Formula (2)
gives the necessary cut condition

    T(b-1)_+<=(P+1)(Q+1).                         (3)

This is a direct fixed clipped-derivative construction, including zero
ordinary steps. Apply it at the first and last step to obtain

    u,w<=M(T):=2T/(T+1)<2.                        (4)

For u,v,w>1 abbreviate

    a=u-1, A=u+1, r=v-1, D=w+1, eta=r/D;
    T=A+D+r.

The full-curvature quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1, gives

    F_Q=1-T^2 a^2 r^2(w-1)^2>=0.                  (5)

The middle-cut interval, with x=(A,1,-r,-eta) and
g=(1,1,-eta,-eta), gives

    F_B=A^2-T^2 eta^2>=0, or Tr<=AD.              (6)

If r(w-1)<=1, the one-sided Huber derivative min(x,1), started at A,
has x=(A,1,-r,r(w-1)) and g=(1,1,-r,r(w-1)). It gives

    F_C=A^2-T^2 r^2(w-1)^2>=0.                   (7)

When eta a<1, a two-dimensional mixed witness gives

    F_N=a u F_B+(1+eta)u^2(2-u^2)>=0.             (8)

Here is its complete verification. Combine the middle-cut base array
from (6) with the auxiliary scalar array

    x_aux=(1,-a,ra,eta a),
    g_aux=(1,-a,eta a,eta a),
    f_aux,i=x_aux,i*g_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

The auxiliary proximal points are (0,0,w eta a,0). Its only positive
finite residual is Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-eta a)w eta a. Every optimum
inequality is legal because g_aux,i*y_aux,i>=0. The base proximal
points are (u,0,-w eta,0); its Q_(0,2)=-(1+eta)w eta and all its
residuals are nonpositive. With

    epsilon=(1+eta)/[a(1-eta a)],

take the orthogonal sum of the base and sqrt(epsilon) times the
auxiliary points and gradients, with the summed values. Residuals add;
the sole positive auxiliary edge is exactly canceled and every other
edge is nonpositive. The energy equals

    F_B+epsilon(1-T^2 eta^2 a^2)
       =F_N/[a(1-eta a)].                         (9)

For the algebra use 1-a^2 A^2=u^2(2-u^2). This proves (8) with
all actual edges, rather than an assumed two-dimensional interpolant.

## 3. A uniform box where all four witnesses apply

Assume T>=T_0 and all the cut conditions (3). First v>1. Otherwise
T=1+u+v+w<=2+2M(T), so T^2-5T-2<=0. At T=T_0 this polynomial
equals 2t>0 and it increases thereafter, a contradiction.

Thus r>0 and the middle cut (6) applies. As T=A+D+r,

    T(T-A-D)<=AD<=(A+D)^2/4,
    T<=lambda(A+D)/2<=lambda(M(T)+1).

Consequently

    T^2+(1-3lambda)T-lambda<=0.                    (10)

Its left side increases for T>=T_0, and at T=7 equals
56-22lambda>0 because lambda<5/2. Hence T<7 and (4) gives
u,w<7/4.

Both u and w exceed1. If, for example, u<=1, then A<=2, D<11/4,
so r=T-A-D>T-19/4. But

    Tr>T(T-19/4)>=T_0(T_0-19/4)
       =11/4+5t/2>11/2>AD,

contradicting the middle cut. The argument for w is identical.

On this entire necessary box the extra hypotheses of (7) and (8) hold:

    r(w-1)<=A(w^2-1)/T<363/(64T_0)<1,
    eta a<=Aa/T=(u^2-1)/T<33/(16T_0)<1.           (11)

For the first strict numerical comparison, 363<64T_0 is equivalent
to 171<128sqrt(2), and squaring gives 29241<32768. Thus no local
neighborhood restriction is being silently used in this global screen.
The earlier inequality T<=lambda(A+D)/2 also gives

    u+w>=2T/lambda-2>=2t.                         (12)

## 4. Excluding three of the four endpoint orientations

Suppose u<=t. By (12), w>=t. Since T>=T_0 and w<2, the difference
between the two sides of the necessary inequality Tr(w-1)<=A is
at least

    T_0(T_0-t-w-2)(w-1)-(t+1)
       =T_0(w-t)(2-w)>=0.                         (13)

It is strictly positive unless u=w=t and T=T_0. In that exceptional
case v=2. Hence every other candidate must have u>t.

Suppose next that also w>=t. On the rectangle [t,M(T)]^2 consider

    q_T(u,w)=T(u-1)(w-1)(T-u-w-2).

This function is strictly concave in either endpoint with the other
fixed. Its minimum is attained at a corner. At T=T_0, M(T_0)=1+t/2,
the corner values are

    q_(T_0)(t,t)=1,
    q_(T_0)(t,M(T_0))=q_(T_0)(M(T_0),t)=lambda/2>1,
    q_(T_0)(M(T_0),M(T_0))=lambda/2>1.

Each corner value strictly increases with T>=T_0. All its positive
factors increase; in particular the derivatives of
T-t-M(T)-2 and T-2M(T)-2 are respectively
1-2/(T+1)^2 and 1-4/(T+1)^2, both positive.
Thus q_T>1 except at the single point T=T_0,u=w=t. This contradicts
the quadratic condition (5). Every nonexceptional candidate therefore
satisfies u>t>w.

Finally its middle step is less than2. For u>t the expression F_N in
(8), with u,w held fixed, strictly decreases as r>0 increases: the
negative squared term in F_B decreases, while u^2(2-u^2)<0.
At r=1 a direct expansion gives

    D^2 F_N/u
       =P_u(D):=u^2 D^2+(4-2u^2-u^3)D-(u-1)(u+2)^2.

This polynomial has one positive and one negative root, since its
leading coefficient is positive and its constant term negative. Also

    P_u(lambda)=-(lambda+1)u^3-2u^2+4(lambda+1)<0

for u>t: the right side vanishes at t and has strictly negative
derivative for u>0. Its positive root is therefore beyond lambda,
and P_u(D)<0 for 0<D<=lambda. Since w<t gives D<lambda, F_N<0
at r=1 and at every r>=1. Necessarily r<1, proving (1).

The remaining constraints can be written without a mixed-energy
abbreviation. In the box (1), a primitive candidate must satisfy

    Tr<=AD,
    T a r(w-1)<=1,
    u^2+u-1+u(2-u^2)eta-(u-1)T^2 eta^2>=0.        (14)

The last expression is F_N/u after expansion. No sufficiency of (14)
is asserted, and no global feasibility or infeasibility conclusion for
this remaining box is claimed.

## 5. Optimizing a continuous auxiliary completion does not improve F_N

Work in box (1) and assume the scalar tests F_B,F_Q>=0. Keep the same
base array in (6), but vary the auxiliary third gradient. Put k=ra<1
and choose z in [k/(w+1),k]. Use

    x_aux=(1,-a,k,k-wz),
    g_aux=(1,-a,z,k-wz),
    f_aux,i=x_aux,i*g_aux,i-g_aux,i^2/2.

Every GD equation is exact. The sole possibly nonzero proximal point
is y_aux,2=k-z>=0. The residuals entering query2 are

    Q_aux,(0,2)=(1-z)(k-z),
    Q_aux,(1,2)=(-a-z)(k-z)<=0,
    Q_aux,(3,2)=(k-(w+1)z)(k-z)<=0.

Every other finite residual is zero, and every optimum constraint is
valid. For z<k the complete legal range of mixing coefficients is

    0<=epsilon<=epsilon_max(z)
       =(1+eta)w eta/[(1-z)(k-z)].                 (15)

The same active edge is exactly canceled at the upper endpoint.
The mixed energy is

    F_B+epsilon[1-T^2(k-wz)^2].                    (16)

Let q=k-wz, A_0=w-k>0, B_0=k(w-1)>0. The quadratic test says
T B_0<=1. Since q ranges from q_0=k/(w+1) down to -B_0, the bracket
in (16) can be negative only when q>1/T. In that case epsilon_max
is optimal. Apart from its positive constant factor, the improvement
over F_B is

    R(q)=(T^2 q^2-1)/[(q+A_0)(q+B_0)].

For q>1/T its derivative has numerator

    T^2(A_0+B_0)q^2+2(T^2 A_0B_0+1)q+(A_0+B_0)>0.

The greatest improvement is therefore at the largest q=q_0, namely
z=k/(w+1)=eta a. This is exactly the auxiliary choice in (8)--(9).
If q_0<=1/T there is no negative auxiliary energy anywhere in the
family. At z=k all auxiliary proximal points are zero and its energy
is F_Q>=0, so this boundary supplies no additional improvement.

Thus the original mixed witness is already optimal in this whole
one-parameter completion family, with arbitrary admissible mixture
weight. Repairing the remaining region (1) requires another change of
geometry or a separate algebraic argument, rather than this retuning.

## 6. Reversal caution

The downloaded and read Grimmer--Shu--Wang paper arXiv:2410.16249v2,
Section3.1, and Zhang--Jiang arXiv:2410.12395, Proposition5.5, establish
reversal properties for their recursively constructed basic schedules.
The checked statements do not supply reversal invariance for every
primitive schedule. No reversal theorem is used in Sections1--5.
The asymmetric region (1) cannot be discarded by silently swapping
u and w.
