# Near-critical ruler: the whole elliptic unit-eigenvalue neighborhood

Status: complete unverified candidate. No numerical computation or new
fact_submit is used. The entire proof is given here, rather than invoking
the earlier unverified parabolic result as a lemma. Accepted facts
1252b8823bb5a290 and b98bb807d514e80d provide the interpolation convention
and benchmark bound only.

## 1. Uniform statement, including every imaginary scale

For each m>=128 put

    s=1+sqrt(2),      c=s(1+1/m),      a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j,      H_0=(),         H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1.

These parameters stay fixed over the whole horizon. Let h_pre be H_m
with its last d_0 removed. At its n queried indices0,...,n-1 put

    P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_pre,t z),
    x_i=T(Re P_i(z),Im P_i(z)),
    g_i=T(Re[zP_i(z)],Im[zP_i(z)]),

where T is ANY invertible real2x2 matrix with ||T e1||=1. The metric,
its conditioning, z, and the values f_i may all depend on m.

Set epsilon0=10^(-6). There is an absolute integer m0 such that the
following holds for every m>=m0 and EVERY z=alpha+i beta in the fixed rectangle

    |alpha-1|<=epsilon0,       |beta|<=epsilon0.           (1)

If the same queried real jets, some f_i, and the optimum(0,0,0) are fully
interpolable by a convex differentiable1-smooth function, then EVERY
interpolant F with minimum0 at0 satisfies, for every final b in[0,2],

    2F(x_(n-1)-b g_(n-1))
          <=100000 n^2 exp[-2^(m+1)/(3m)].                (2)

The ratio of this bound to the exact U_n^ZJ tends to zero. The interval
of final steps includes the original d_0 and the common comparison step1.
There is no restriction tying the new endpoint gradient to the operator.

In particular this excludes a WHOLE fixed neighborhood of the natural
unit-eigenvalue mechanism, not just beta proportional to m^(-1/2). The
result still does not cover frequencies outside(1), multiple modes,
changing generators, or unrestricted W.

We prove the stronger intermediate legality restriction, with the explicit
constant C=5000000000 and all large m,

    1-alpha >= (8/5)beta^2-C/n.                          (3)

No fitted numerical threshold or compactness assumption on T is used.

## 2. A common finite-cycle average and a uniform phase bound

Conjugating z and replacing T by T diag(1,-1) leaves the physical data
unchanged, so first take beta>0. Put M=T^T T, tau=tr(M)/2, and
B=[[alpha,-beta],[beta,alpha]]. The full partial-word polynomial is

    p_j(z)=product_(ell<j)(1-d_ell z)^(2^(j-ell-1)),
    R_j(z)=p_j(z)(1-d_j z).

The query positions of H_j in complex coordinates are precisely the subset
products of R_0,...,R_(j-1): the left copy is unchanged and the right copy
is multiplied by R_j. The first H_(m-1) lies inside h_pre, and its2^(m-2)
copies of H_1=(d_0) start at all subset products of R_1,...,R_(m-2).

In each copy sum the ordered interpolation inequalities on the triangle
star -> second query -> first query -> star. Function values cancel.
Divide by the squared modulus of the nonzero starting multiplier. The
result is the base triangle evaluated in the metric R_theta^T M R_theta.
Average these actual inequalities over all copies. Its effective metric is

    M_bar=tau I+E_M,
    ||E_M||_op<=tau Gamma_m,
    Gamma_m=product_(j=1)^(m-2)|cos(arg R_j(z))|.          (4)

Indeed a traceless symmetric matrix[[q,r],[r,-q]], represented by q+i r,
is multiplied under rotation conjugation by exp(+/-2i theta); binary
averaging multiplies its modulus by |cos theta|. The traceless norm of
the original positive definite M is at most tau. This argument uses one
common metric and is uniform over all its condition numbers.

Here are bounds valid on a fixed small box around1. The inequalities
12/5<s<17/7 imply, for m>=128,

    12/5<c<5/2,       3/8<a<1/2,
    11/8<d_0<3/2.                                    (5)

For example c<=2193/896<5/2 and a>=127/320>3/8. The upper bound a<1/2
follows from c>12/5. Our epsilon0 is less than1/100. Then
alpha d_j-1>=a c^j/2. Define

    phi_j=arg(1-d_j z)
           =-pi+arctan[beta d_j/(alpha d_j-1)],
    Phi=sum_(j>=0)2^(-j-1)phi_j=-pi+delta.

The series converges uniformly by its bounded terms and summable weights.
The arctangent arguments lie between beta/2 and8beta. Since arctan t lies
between t/2 and t on[0,1],

    beta/4<=delta<=8beta.                              (6)

The phases decrease to phi_infinity=-pi+arctan(beta/alpha), and

    0<=phi_j-phi_infinity
      <=beta/[alpha(alpha d_j-1)]<=8beta c^(-j).

The first inequality uses the1-Lipschitz property of arctan. Exact
multiplicities give

    arg R_j=2^j Phi+epsilon_j,
    epsilon_j=phi_j-sum_(ell>=0)2^(-ell-1)phi_(j+ell),
    0<=epsilon_j<=8beta c^(-j).                         (7)

Choose an integer k with2^k delta in[pi/4,pi/2). If1<=k<=m-2,
discard the earlier factors in(4), compare each remaining |cos| with its
unperturbed value using its1-Lipschitz property, and telescope the
difference of products of numbers in[0,1]. This gives

    Gamma_m<=product_(j=k)^(m-2)|cos(2^j delta)|
                                  +sum_(j=k)^(m-2)epsilon_j
       <=1/[2^(m-1-k)|sin(2^k delta)|]
                                  +8beta c^(-k)/(1-c^(-1)).

it includes exact dyadic resonances. From(6),2^k<=8/beta and
2^(-k)<=11beta. Let r0=log_2(12/5)>5/4, the last inequality following
from(12/5)^4>32. We can take C1=32 and C2=1000 in the bound

    Gamma_m<= C1/(n beta)+C2 beta^(1+r0)                (8)

whenever k<=m-2. Indeed the first term is at most16sqrt(2)/(n beta),
and the second is at most14beta c^(-k). Since11beta<1 and
1<r0<=log_2 c<3/2, we have c^(-k)<=44beta^r0; hence1000 is a valid
second constant. Here sin(2^k delta)>=1/sqrt2. Take K=2000000.
If beta>=K/n, the bound2^k<=8/beta ensures k<=m-2 for all large m.
Our epsilon0 ensures k>=1. Thus(8) is valid throughout
the large-beta case beta>=K/n; it does not make an infinite-tail claim.

## 3. The triangle estimate for beta>=K/n

Put xi=1-alpha, d=d_0, v0=B e1, r1=e1-d v0 and v1=B r1. For a metric
M the triangle weight is tr(M Z), where

    Z=(v1v1^T)/2+d sym(v0v1^T)+(v0-v1)(v0-v1)^T/2
                            -sym(e1v0^T)+(v0v0^T)/2,
    sym(C)=(C+C^T)/2.

Expanding its three edge weights gives

    tr(Z)=d beta^2-(alpha-|z|^2)E,
    E=1-d alpha+d^2|z|^2.                              (9)

At z=1, Z=0 for every d. For |z|<=2 and1<=d<=2, write w=z-1.
The differences of v0,r1,v1 from their z=1 values have norms at most
|w|,2|w|,7|w|. Also||v0||<=2,||v1||<=10. Bounding the five outer or
mixed products in Z gives respectively38.5,34,56,1,1.5 times |w|.
Thus

    ||Z||_op<=132(|xi|+beta).                           (10)

For epsilon0<=1/100, E>=1 and1+d/E>=7/4. Here is a direct uniform check.
At alpha=1,beta=0, E0=1-d+d^2>=97/64. In the small box,
|E-E0|<=7epsilon0. Also4d-3E0=7d-3d^2-3>=3/4 for
d in[11/8,3/2]. Hence4d-3E>=3/4-21epsilon0>0, as required.

The averaged legal triangle gives tr(M_bar Z)<=0. Equations(4),(9),(10),
with |tr(E_M Z)|<=2||E_M||_op||Z||_op, imply

    -xi+xi^2+(1+d/E)beta^2
                   <=264 Gamma_m(|xi|+beta).             (11)

For beta>=K/n, (8) is at most
32/2000000+1000epsilon0^(1+r0)<1/26400; the second term is at most10^(-9).
Write q=264Gamma_m<=1/100. Drop
xi^2 in(11). If xi>=0, divide by1+q; if xi<0, divide by1-q. In both
cases the inequalities(7/4)/(1.01)>5/3 and1/(1-q)<=2 give

    xi >=(5/3)beta^2-528Gamma_m beta.

Since r0>5/4, epsilon0^r0<10^(-7), so
528C2 epsilon0^r0<.0528<1/15. Using(8),

    xi >=(8/5)beta^2-C3/n,
    C3=528C1,              beta>=K/n.                  (12)

No lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue of M was needed.

## 4. Tiny imaginary parts: two actual optimum inequalities suffice

Assume0<beta<=K/n. If alpha<=1, then xi>=0 and(3) follows for this
case with the stated C and n>=32000. Suppose alpha>1
and write e=alpha-1>0. Put

    u=g0-alpha x0=beta T e2,       V=||u||.

The initial optimum inequalities give<x0,g0>>=||g0||^2, so||g0||<=1
and V<=3. Expanded at alpha=1+e, the same condition gives

    alpha e+V^2<=-(2alpha-1)<x0,u><=3V,
    e<=3V.                                             (13)

Choose the actual prefix query index

    ell=min(n-1,floor(1/(100beta))).

Our epsilon0 is below1/200, so the floor is at least half its argument.
For large n, ell>=n/(200K). Every factor of its prefix is
-(positive modulus) times exp(i arctan[beta h/(alpha h-1)]). By the
same bounds as(6), the sum theta of these small positive angles obeys

    ell beta/4<=theta<=8ell beta<=.08.

Let t=tan(theta)/beta. Since theta<=tan(theta)<=2theta in this interval,

    ell/4<=t<=16ell.                                   (14)

After dividing its point and gradient by their common nonzero scalar
(-1)^ell |P_ell(z)| cos(theta), the query has vectors

    X=x0+t u,
    G=(alpha-beta^2 t)X+(1+beta^2 t^2)u.                 (15)

This is obtained by expanding real and imaginary parts of P_ell and
zP_ell. Its optimum cocoercivity inequality remains<G,X>>=||G||^2.

If e<=beta^2 t, then(14) and ell<=1/(100beta) give
e<=.16beta<=.16K/n. Otherwise put A0=alpha-beta^2t>1 and
k0=1+beta^2t^2>0. Substitution of(15) into the optimum inequality gives

    A0(1-A0)||X||^2+(1-2A0)k0<X,u>-k0^2 V^2>=0.

nonpositive, and equality would require X=u=0, which would contradict

    D=2+2/(2s-1)>5/2,
    J=6+4/(2s-1)+2/(4s+1)<15/2.

The bounds follow from12/5<s<5/2 and
20/19+10/53<3/2. Thus for all large m,

    5/2<=D_m<=4,       J_m<=15/2.

|1-d_0(alpha+i bta)|>=alpha d_0-1>=a/2>=3/16,

    |p_pre(alpha+i bta)|<=6E_m.                         (21)

      <=8n |p_pre(alpha+i bta)|<=48n E_m.               (22)

therefore zero, and integration of its derivative along the segment gives

    |Im p_pre(z)|/beta<=48n E_m,
    |Im[z p_pre(z)]|/beta<=102n E_m.                    (23)

p_pre+z p_pre', and |z|<=2. These bounds remain uniform as beta tends

Use u=g0-alpha x0=beta T e2 with||u||<=3. The physical endpoint vectors

    g_(n-1)=Re[zp_pre(z)]x0+[Im[zp_pre(z)]/beta]u.

Equations(21)--(23) imply

    ||x_(n-1)||<=150n E_m,       ||g_(n-1)||<=320n E_m.  (24)

For beta=0, the physical data are x_i=P_i(alpha)x0 and g_i=alpha x_i.
Initial optimum interpolation forces0<=alpha<=1. Hence(17) holds with

       <=96000 n^2 E_m^2
       <=100000 n^2 exp[-2^(m+1)/(3m)],

K=2000000 and C=5000000000 satisfy all displayed restrictions.

# C34. Exact coordinate-path projection relay and its near-critical obstruction

Status: UNVERIFIED joint candidate. No verifier or numerical solver was used.
This is an exact obstruction for the defined coordinate-flow family, not an
upper bound on unrestricted W and not a primitive-capacity theorem.

## 1. Actual correlated real vectors and the whole trajectory

Partition a nonnegative schedule into N ordinary blocks of masses S_i,
separated by checkpoints b_i>1, 0<=i<N-1. Each ordinary block can be an
arbitrary ordered list with that mass. Set M_i=S_i+1, L_i=b_i-1 and
T_i=S_i+b_i=M_i+L_i for i<N-1. Choose an artificial terminal parameter
T_(N-1)>=M_(N-1). Let e_0,...,e_(N-1) be the standard orthonormal basis.

Choose alpha_i>0, beta_i>=0 for i<N-1, with beta_(N-1)=0, and impose

    T_(i+1) alpha_(i+1)=T_i beta_i.

For a nonzero terminal payoff all beta_i must be positive. Define

    p_i=alpha_i e_i-beta_i e_(i+1)  (i<N-1),
    p_(N-1)=alpha_(N-1)e_(N-1),
    C=conv(0,p_0,...,p_(N-1)),
    F(x)=max_{p in C} (<x,p>-||p||^2/2).

The strict concavity of the maximization gives its unique maximizer P_C(x).
The projection variational inequality proves
||P_C(x)-P_C(z)||^2<=<P_C(x)-P_C(z),x-z>, hence F is convex and
differentiable with 1-Lipschitz gradient P_C. Differentiability follows by
bounding the two maximization differences between the corresponding linear
forms and then using the displayed Lipschitz estimate. F>=0 and F(0)=0.

Start at x_init=T_0 alpha_0 e_0. At phase i, after ordinary partial mass
u in [0,S_i], prescribe

    x_i(u)=(T_i-u)alpha_i e_i+u beta_i e_(i+1).

At the checkpoint, subtracting b_i p_i gives T_i beta_i e_(i+1), which is
the next prescribed start. Thus the SAME whole GD trajectory is realized
if P_C(x_i(u))=p_i at every actual partial mass.

Write y_i(u)=x_i(u)-p_i. Its two coordinates are
(T_i-u-1)alpha_i and (u+1)beta_i, both nonnegative. Put

    delta_i(u)=<y_i(u),p_i>
              =(T_i-u-1)alpha_i^2-(u+1)beta_i^2.

For j<=i-2 and j>=i+2, <y_i(u),p_j>=0. For j=i-1 this inner
product is -beta_(i-1)(T_i-u-1)alpha_i<=0. For j=i+1 it is
(u+1)beta_i alpha_(i+1). The comparison with zero is 0<=delta_i(u).

Consequently ALL normals against ALL vertices and zero hold if and only if

    L_i alpha_i^2-M_i beta_i^2
                    >= M_i beta_i alpha_(i+1),     i<N-1,       (1)

together with T_(N-1)>=M_(N-1). Necessity uses the actual last query in
each ordinary block, including an empty block's only query. Sufficiency
uses the fact that delta_i(u)-(u+1)beta_i alpha_(i+1) decreases with u.
The terminal phase has only its nonnegative own normal and nonpositive
comparison with its preceding vertex. Thus no remote condition is omitted.

Using the transfer relation, (1) is precisely

    (beta_i/alpha_i)^2
          <= L_i T_(i+1)/[M_i(T_i+T_(i+1))].                    (2)

The term M_i beta_i^2 in (1) records the mass already accumulated in the
next coordinate during the ordinary block. Replacing it by beta_i^2
would give a false, much stronger relay.

The correlations are explicit:
<p_i,p_(i+1)>=-beta_i alpha_(i+1)<0, all nonadjacent correlations zero.
The p_i are linearly independent because their coordinate matrix is
triangular with positive diagonal. Thus C is an actual N-simplex,
not a formal Gram matrix.

## 2. Actual normalization and exact optimal payoff

The minimizer set is C^polar={z:<p_i,z><=0 for all i}: these inequalities make every maximand nonpositive, while if <p_i,z>>0, a sufficiently small positive multiple of p_i in C gives a positive maximand. The terminal
inequality forces z_(N-1)<=0. Backward substitution then forces every
coordinate z_i<=0. Therefore 0 is a closest minimizer to x_init, whose
true squared distance to the minimizer set is T_0^2 alpha_0^2.

At the final point, with D=2S_(N-1)+1,

    2F_end / dist(x_init,argmin F)^2
      = (2T_(N-1)-D)/T_(N-1)^2
                         product_(i=0)^(N-2)(beta_i/alpha_i)^2. (3)

For fixed T_(N-1), equality in every bound (2) maximizes this expression.
It gives legal positive parameters recursively from any alpha_0>0. Thus
the exact optimum for this family is

    E(T)=(2T-D)/T^2
        product_(i=0)^(N-2) [L_i T_(i+1)/(M_i(T_i+T_(i+1)))].   (4)

For N>=2 let C_last=T_(N-2). All T dependence in (4), up to a positive
constant, is

    phi(T)=(2T-D)/[T(T+C_last)],  T>=M_(N-1).

Its derivative has numerator -2T^2+2DT+D C_last. Therefore its unique
maximum occurs at

    T_opt=(D+sqrt(D^2+2D C_last))/2 >= D >= M_(N-1),

and

    phi(T_opt)=2/[D+C_last+sqrt(D^2+2D C_last)].

For N=1, (3) is maximized at T=D and gives 1/D, the global Huber value.

The primitive defect is tracked on the same normalized trajectory. Let s be
the mass of the ENTIRE schedule and let
V=2 sum_t h_t(F_t-F_end)+sum_t h_t(1-h_t)||g_t||^2
  -s(s+1)||g_end||^2.
At every projection query F_t=<x_t,g_t>-||g_t||^2/2, so
2h_t F_t+h_t(1-h_t)||g_t||^2
=||x_t||^2-||x_(t+1)||^2. Telescoping gives

    V=||x_init||^2-||x_end+s g_end||^2,

and therefore, with T=T_(N-1),

    V/dist(x_init,argmin F)^2
      =1-[(T-S_(N-1)+s)/T]^2
                   product_(i<N-1)(beta_i/alpha_i)^2.           (5a)

Equations (3) and (5a) report BOTH the normalized objective and the normalized
primitive defect; neither is inferred from the sign of the other.

## 3. Every dyadic-depth version fails on the near-critical word

Fix m>=128, lambda=1+sqrt(2),
c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c, and
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j).
Let S_j be its mass and M_j=S_j+1. Direct geometric summation gives

    M_j=A c^j+(1-A)2^j,  A=a/(c-2).

Here 0<A<1: c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1 while ac=1-1/m<1.
Also 2<c<49/20 and c-2<9/20. For example sqrt(2)<99/70 gives
lambda<169/70, and (169/70)(129/128)<49/20.

Choose any r in [0,m-1]. Partition H_m into N=2^k copies of H_r, where
k=m-r, separated by its actual higher-level checkpoints. Then all M_i=M=M_r
and

    L_i=a c^(r+nu_2(i+1)),  0<=i<N-1,
    q=a c^r/M <= c-2 < 9/20,
    T_i=M(1+q c^(nu_2(i+1))).

Here nu_2(j) is the exponent of2 dividing the positive integer j.
In particular the first and last nonterminal T_i equal T_0=M(1+q).
Put D=2M-1. Exact counting of binary valuations gives

    product_(i<N-1)(L_i/M)=q^(N-1)c^(N-k-1)
                         =(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k).                   (5)

For internal transitions i<N-2, every checkpoint of level ell>=1
is flanked by two level0 checkpoints. Therefore

    product_(i<N-2)(1+T_(i+1)/T_i)
      = product_(ell=1)^(k-1)
          [(T_0+T_ell)^2/(T_0 T_ell)]^(2^(k-ell-1))
      >= 2^(N-2),                                           (6)

where T_ell=M(1+q c^ell). Each bracket is at least4 by
(T_0-T_ell)^2>=0. There are (N-2)/2 brackets, with multiplicity.

Telescoping the T_(i+1)/T_i factors in (4) and retaining the terminal
factor gives the exact formula

    E_opt = phi(T_opt) (qc)^(N-1)c^(-k) /
            product_(ell=1)^(k-1)
             [(T_0+T_ell)^2/(T_0 T_ell)]^(2^(k-ell-1)).        (7)

In particular phi(T)<= (2T-D)/T^2 <=1/D, so

    E_opt <= [2/(D c^k)] (qc/2)^(N-1).                       (8)

Let K=1/(2M_m-1). From the formula for M_j and q<=c-2,

    M_m=M[(1-q/(c-2))2^k+(q/(c-2))c^k] <=M c^k.

Consequently for k>=2,

    E_opt/K <= 4 (qc/2)^(N-1)
             <4 (441/800)^(N-1)
             <=4 (441/800)^3 <1.                            (9)

Every genuinely multitransition dyadic-depth relay in this family is thus
strictly below K, uniformly in its free scalar parameters. If k tends to
infinity, its ratio to K tends to0 at least geometrically in 2^k.

For completeness k=1 is also below K. Set epsilon=1/M in (0,1]. The exact
two-phase optimum divided by K is

    2q[2(2+q)-epsilon] /
     [3+q-epsilon+sqrt((2-epsilon)(4+2q-epsilon))].

It is bounded above by

    R(q)=4q(2+q)/[2+q+sqrt(3+2q)].

This function increases for q>=0: write it as
4q/[1+sqrt(3+2q)/(2+q)]; the ratio in the denominator decreases,
since its derivative has numerator -(1+q). Therefore

    R(q)<R(9/20)=441/[245+10sqrt(390)]<1;

the last inequality follows from 196^2<39000.

Allowing r=m gives the single-phase Huber construction and attains K.
Thus the optimal payoff of the UNION of all these dyadic-depth incidence
relays is exactly K. This does not claim that all simplex walks, all
correlated walks, or all smooth-convex functions have payoff at most K.

## 4. Why the obstruction is useful and what it does not close

The family is legal in dimension N with every old/future normal retained,
uses N distinct mutually overlapping gradients, and has an exact
closest-minimizer calculation. Its failure is quantitative; no translated
negative-energy sign is used. The penalty in (6) comes from adjacent
coordinate transfer and survives the near-critical perturbation qc=1+O(1/m).

A tree transfer can avoid following N consecutive fresh coordinates, but it
must retain waiting coordinates. Every waiting future vertex then contributes
a positive normal comparison throughout the intervening phases. That is a
different construction class, not covered by (9).

## 1. General finite-prefix statement

    g_i=A x_i, 0<=i<=q.

Here A is a fixed real linear map on the invariant span of these vectors.

    |S alpha|<=delta, 0<=S^2 sigma<=delta^2,

There is no restriction on the gradient at the unqueried point x_q-b g_q.

alpha=Re z, sigma=|z|^2 and

# A concrete affine completion for the variable-matrix repair lane

Status: new self-contained candidate algebra, NOT verifier-accepted. This is
an explicit parameterization for the next proof attempt, not a re-selection
theorem or a strict cone separation. No numerical solver or fact_submit.

## Definitions and full matrix identity

Fix h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1))>=0 with sum s>0. All n+1 formal gradients are independent.
Let x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t, and define the actual Q_ij and intrinsic V_h by

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                               -s(s+1)||g_n||^2.

Define the column e of n+1 ones, the lower triangular matrix A with A_ii=1
and A_it=h_t for t<i, and r=A^(-1)e. Thus r_0=1 and
r_(i+1)=(1-h_i)r_i. The vectors e,r are independent because s>0.
Write omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T and

 D_quad=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_(n-1)(2-h_(n-1)),-s(s+2)),
 c_quad=1-(1+s)^2 r_n^2.

For a real off-diagonal multiplier array lambda, put
L=diag(lambda e)-lambda. Value cancellation in V_h+sum lambda Q is exactly
L^T e=omega. By definition L e=0. The COMPLETE formal gradient matrix is

                 M=D_quad+sym(L A),                 (1)

where sym(B)=(B+B^T)/2. To check this, the position contribution is
sym(L(A-I)). The squared-difference terms are sym(L)-diag(omega)/2.
Adding the diagonal terms in V_h gives exactly (1).

## Which PSD matrices admit some real multiplier representation?

Claim. A symmetric PSD matrix M has a real multiplier representation (1)
with the actual value cancellation if and only if

                    M e=0, r^T M r=c_quad.           (2)

This permits arbitrary real multiplier signs; the actual sign restrictions
for a primitive or E_theta certificate remain separate and are not deleted.

Necessity: evaluating the value-canceling identity on the affine Huber run
with every gradient equal to1 gives e^T M e=0, hence M e=0 by PSD.
The full-curvature quadratic trajectory has gradients r_i and every Q_ij=0.
Telescoping h_i(2-h_i)r_i^2=r_i^2-r_(i+1)^2 gives
r^T D_quad r=1-(1+s)^2 r_n^2=c_quad, and evaluating the same identity on
that legal quadratic gives the second assertion in (2).

Here is an explicit sufficiency construction. Put C=M-D_quad and set

 U=[e,r], Z=[C e-A^T omega,-C r], H=U^T U, W=U^T Z.

The two-by-two matrix H is positive definite. The matrix W is skew-symmetric:

 e^T C e=omega^T A e=s^2+sum h_i^2,
 r^T C r=0,
 e^T(-C r)+r^T(C e-A^T omega)=-omega^T A r=-omega^T e=0.

The first equality uses M e=0 and the displayed diagonal D_quad, and the
second uses r^T M r=r^T D_quad r. Define

 K_0=Z H^(-1)U^T-U H^(-1)Z^T
                          -U H^(-1)W H^(-1)U^T.     (3)

It is skew-symmetric, and multiplication by U gives K_0 U=Z: the last
two correction terms cancel because Z^T U=-W. Now put

 B=C+K_0, L=B A^(-1), lambda_ij=-L_ij for i!=j, lambda_ii=0.

The relations K_0 r=-C r and K_0 e=C e-A^T omega give
L e=B r=0 and L^T e=A^(-T)B^T e=omega. Thus L is precisely the row
Laplacian of its extracted off-diagonal array, and its flows cancel every
actual value coefficient. Also sym(L A)=C, proving (1).

All representations of this same M arise by replacing K_0 with K_0+S,
where S is any skew-symmetric matrix satisfying S e=S r=0. Indeed their
difference must be skew after multiplying L by A, and must kill both e,r;
the converse follows from the same equations. This also recovers directly
the fixed-remainder obstruction already independently proved earlier.

Consequently a PSD real-multiplier identity with no sign restrictions exists
if and only if c_quad>=0. For sufficiency, let
z=r-e(e^T r)/(e^T e), so z!=0 and r^T z=||z||^2. The rank-one choice

                 M=c_quad z z^T/(r^T z)^2

satisfies (2); use (3). The case c_quad=0 allows M=0. This consequence is
NOT a smooth-convex validity theorem: unrestricted negative multipliers can
invalidate such an implication. It merely separates the full PSD condition
from the indispensable actual interpolation sign inequalities.

## Concrete next interface for four positive steps

If n=4 and the schedule is quadratic-balanced, c_quad=0, every permitted PSD
matrix must annihilate both e and r. The space orthogonal to span{e,r} has

All twenty actual multipliers are then EXPLICIT affine functions of these

The actual E_theta requirements remain

Ordinary primitivity requires lambda_i4>=0 as well. A successful repair must

## 1. A genuine real tree family with all normal inequalities

Partition a schedule into N ordinary blocks of masses S_i and checkpoints
b_i>1 after each block except the last. Set M_i=S_i+1, L_i=b_i-1 and
T_i=M_i+L_i for i<N-1. Choose T_(N-1)>=M_(N-1).

Choose ANY rooted tree on vertices 0,...,N-1 with root0 and with each parent
strictly earlier than its children. Write Ch_i for the children of i, and
W_i={j>i:parent(j)<i} for the waiting vertices at phase i. Define positive
energies E_i and actual vectors in the standard basis of R^N:

    alpha_i=sqrt(E_i)/T_i,
    beta_ij=sqrt(E_j)/T_i  (j in Ch_i),
    p_i=alpha_i e_i-sum_(j in Ch_i) beta_ij e_j.                (1)

The vector matrix is triangular with positive diagonal, hence these are
linearly independent vectors with an explicit positive definite real Gram
matrix. Distinct normals have negative inner product exactly along a tree
edge, and zero inner product otherwise. Let C=conv(0,p_i) and

    F(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2).

Its maximizer is the Euclidean projection P_C(x). The projection variational
inequalities give firm nonexpansiveness, hence Lipschitz continuity, of P_C.
Bounding maximization differences with the two maximizing linear forms gives
grad F=P_C. Thus F is one fixed everywhere-defined convex 1-smooth function.

Start at x_init=sqrt(E_0)e_0. At the beginning of phase i the nonzero
coordinates are sqrt(E_j) for the current vertex i and for j in W_i.
During ordinary partial mass u the current coordinate is
(T_i-u)alpha_i, each waiting coordinate stays sqrt(E_j), and each child
coordinate is u beta_ij. After the checkpoint, the current coordinate
vanishes and every child coordinate becomes sqrt(E_j). This is the
prescribed GD recursion whenever its projection normals hold.

For y=x-p_i, all its coordinates are nonnegative. Its own normal value is

    delta_i(u)=(T_i-u-1)alpha_i^2
                         -(u+1)sum_(j in Ch_i)beta_ij^2.      (2)

A past vertex has nonpositive dot product with y: its positive coordinate
has been exhausted, and all its remaining coordinates are nonpositive.
A future vertex j has no mass yet in its children, since the tree has a
unique parent. Thus its dot product with y is exactly

    E_j/T_j                      if j in W_i,
    (u+1)sqrt(E_j)alpha_j/T_i     if j in Ch_i,
    0                            otherwise.

The comparison with zero is also required. The own value (2) decreases in u;
the child comparisons increase; the waiting comparisons are constant.
Therefore ALL comparisons against ALL past/future vertices and zero are
equivalent to the following endpoint conditions for i<N-1:

    L_i E_i-M_i sum_(j in Ch_i)E_j >=
       T_i^2 max(0,
           max_(j in W_i) E_j/T_j,
           (M_i/T_i) max_(j in Ch_i) E_j/T_j).                 (3)

Empty maxima are zero. The terminal phase has no children or waiting
vertices, and its condition is just T_(N-1)>=M_(N-1).
These checks include every actual ordinary query and checkpoint query.
They construct a fixed legal smooth-convex function, without oracle resets.

The minimizer set is C^polar: a violated dot-product inequality yields a
positive maximand at a small multiple of the corresponding vertex.
Its inequalities force every coordinate of a minimizer nonpositive, by
backward induction through the tree. Thus 0 is a closest minimizer to
sqrt(E_0)e_0, with true squared initial distance E_0.

Writing T=T_(N-1) and D=2S_(N-1)+1, the exact normalized objective is

    score=(2T-D) E_(N-1)/(T^2 E_0).                            (4)

For fixed tree, phase masses, T and terminal energy E_(N-1)=1, setting (3)
to equality in decreasing order of i constructs the componentwise least
positive feasible E_i. Indeed every right hand side is a nondecreasing
function of already-set future energies. This proves, without numerical
optimization, that the recursion attains the best score in this exact class.
There is always a positive future waiting or child energy until the last
phase, so the constructed E_i are positive.

The primitive defect is also exact on the SAME normalized trajectory.
At each projection query F_t=<x_t,g_t>-||g_t||^2/2. Consequently

    2h_t F_t+h_t(1-h_t)||g_t||^2
                         =||x_t||^2-||x_(t+1)||^2.

If s is the entire schedule mass and
V=2sum_t h_t(F_t-F_end)+sum_t h_t(1-h_t)||g_t||^2
  -s(s+1)||g_end||^2, then

    V/E_0=1-[(T-S_(N-1)+s)/T]^2 E_(N-1)/E_0.                 (5)

No raw negative sign is substituted for objective or distance control.

## 2. A chronology bound valid for EVERY tree shape

Put H_i=E_i/T_i. The next chronological vertex i+1 is either a child of i
or already waiting. If it is waiting, (3), even after dropping all child
costs, implies

    H_(i+1)/H_i <= L_i/T_i.

If it is a child, retaining its own term in the child sum and its own
normal comparison gives

    H_(i+1)/H_i <= L_i T_i/[M_i(T_i+T_(i+1))].

Hence every legal tree relay satisfies

    H_(i+1)/H_i <=
        max(L_i/T_i, L_i T_i/[M_i(T_i+T_(i+1))]).             (6)

This is only a necessary bound; the constructive recursion (3) still keeps
every other comparison. The upper bound (6) is used only to exclude payoff.

## 3. Uniform quantitative exclusion on H_m

Fix m>=128, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m),
a=(1-1/m)/c, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j).
Let S_j be the mass of H_j and M_j=1+S_j. Geometric summation gives

    M_j=A c^j+(1-A)2^j,  A=a/(c-2) in (0,1).

Choose ANY dyadic blocking depth r<m. Put k=m-r, N=2^k, M=M_r and
q=a c^r/M. The N ordinary blocks are all copies of H_r and

    L_i=M q c^(nu_2(i+1)),
    T_i=M(1+q c^(nu_2(i+1)))  (i<N-1).                       (7)

The following simple uniform bounds will suffice:

    12/5<c<39/16,      2/5<q<=c-2<7/16.                    (8)

For the upper bound, sqrt(2)<99/70 and
(169/70)(129/128)<39/16. Also a<c-2 because ac<1<c(c-2).
This gives 0<A<1 and q<=c-2. Since M_r<=c^r, q>=a.
Finally a=(m-1)/[lambda(m+1)] >=127/(129lambda)
>2540/6321>2/5, using lambda<49/20. This proves (8).

Every even index i<N-1 has the low checkpoint q_i=q. In (6), its
waiting option is at least its child option. For a nonterminal next phase
this is q+q^2<=1+q_(i+1), which follows from q<1 and q_(i+1)>=q.
For the terminal next phase it follows from q+q^2<1<=T/M.
Thus every such low transition obeys

    H_(i+1)/H_i <= q/(1+q).                                  (9)

Every odd index has q_i=q c^ell for some ell>=1, and is followed by
a low checkpoint. Its child option dominates the waiting option:
q_i^2+q_i>1+q, because q_i>24/25 while q<7/16.
Therefore

    H_(i+1)/H_i <= q c^ell / D_ell,
    D_ell=(2+q+q c^ell)/(1+q c^ell)>1.                       (10)

There are N/2 low transitions and 2^(k-ell-1) transitions of level ell>=1.
Counting binary valuations gives

    product_(i<N-1)q c^(nu_2(i+1))=(qc)^(N-1)c^(-k).

Since (2T-D)/T<2, (4), (9), and (10) yield

    score < [2/(M(1+q)c^k)]
             (qc)^(N-1) /
             [(1+q)^(N/2) product_(ell=1)^(k-1)
                           D_ell^(2^(k-ell-1))].             (11)

Let K=1/(2M_m-1), the global Huber score. The exact mass relation is

    M_m=M[(1-q/(c-2))2^k+(q/(c-2))c^k] <=M c^k.

It follows that score/K<B_k, where

    B_k=4(qc)^(2^k-1) /
       [(1+q)^(2^(k-1)+1)
          product_(ell=1)^(k-1)D_ell^(2^(k-ell-1))].          (12)

For k=2,

    B_2=4(qc)^3(1+qc)/[(1+q)^3(2+q+qc)].

This increases in both q and c. Its logarithmic q derivative is
3/[q(1+q)]+(c-1)/[(1+cq)(2+(1+c)q)]>0. Its logarithmic c
derivative is 3/c+q/(1+cq)-q/(2+(1+c)q)>0. Consequently (8) gives

    B_2 <
      273^3*529/[1024*23^3*897]
      =10763254593/11175730176 =: eta <1.                    (13)

The recurrence is exact:

    B_(k+1)/B_k^2 = (qc)(1+q)/(4D_k)
                  <6279/16384 =: zeta <1.                  (14)

Thus, for every k>=2,

    score/K < B_k
             <=zeta^(2^(k-2)-1) eta^(2^(k-2)) <1.            (15)

This excludes EVERY ordered rooted tree and EVERY legal positive energy
choice in the specified family. If k grows, the ratio tends to zero
exponentially in 2^k. In particular no choice of tree shape avoids the loss.

When k=1 the sole tree is the two-vertex path. The exact endpoint condition
gives, with T_0=M(1+q) and D=2M-1,

    score=q(2T-D)/[T(T+T_0)].

The maximum is attained at T=(D+sqrt(D^2+2D T_0))/2. Writing epsilon=1/M
its ratio to K is

    2q[2(2+q)-epsilon] /
       [3+q-epsilon+sqrt((2-epsilon)(4+2q-epsilon))]
      <=4q(2+q)/[2+q+sqrt(3+2q)].

The last expression increases in q>=0 because
sqrt(3+2q)/(2+q) decreases. As q<9/20 it is less than
441/[245+10sqrt(390)]<1; the latter inequality is 196^2<39000.

Allowing r=m leaves just one vertex and one ordinary block. The choice
T=2S_m+1 attains K. Therefore the union over ALL blocking depths, ALL
ordered rooted trees and ALL legal parameters has exact best score K.

## 4. The obstruction and the next genuinely different mechanism

Tree branching reduces the number of edges from root to terminal, but it
creates waiting coordinate masses. Their supporting planes must be below
the active plane at every intervening query. Inequality (9) is the
quantitative price at each low checkpoint, independent of the chosen tree.

The unique-parent condition is load-bearing. With two parents contributing
to one child coordinate, two earlier gradient vectors can have positive
correlation. A future plane can then have a negative term from a child
already preloaded by another parent. The waiting comparison E_j/T_j used
above is no longer correct, so (6) and (15) do not cover directed acyclic
split-and-merge constructions. Nor do they cover signed coordinate mass,
revisiting exhausted coordinates, other simplex geometries, or general
smooth-convex functions. The original all-schedule minimax target is open.

## 1. General acyclic nonnegative coordinate flow

There are N chronological phases, ordinary masses S_i and checkpoints b_i>1
for i<N-1. Set M_i=S_i+1, L_i=b_i-1 and T_i=M_i+L_i. The artificial
terminal T_(N-1) is at least M_(N-1). Choose nonnegative transfer amounts
a_ij for 0<=i<j<N. Put R_0>0 and R_j=sum_(i<j)a_ij>0 for j>=1, and define

    p_i=(R_i e_i-sum_(j>i)a_ij e_j)/T_i.

These are explicit independent real vectors, so C=conv(0,p_i) is a simplex.
The function F(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2) is convex and 1-smooth
with grad F=P_C: the maximization is strictly concave in p, the projection
variational inequality gives firm nonexpansiveness, and maximization
differences give differentiability.

Start at R_0 e_0. At the start of phase i, define
r_j^(i)=sum_(ell<i)a_(ell,j) for j>=i; the current coordinate is R_i,
all processed coordinates vanish, and each future coordinate is r_j^(i).
After ordinary partial mass u, the current coordinate is
(1-u/T_i)R_i and future coordinate j is r_j^(i)+(u/T_i)a_ij.
The checkpoint exhausts coordinate i and adds a_ij to each future coordinate.

For y=x-p_i the current coordinate is (1-(u+1)/T_i)R_i and the future
coordinates are r_j^(i)+((u+1)/T_i)a_ij. All are nonnegative. Its own
normal value is

    delta_i(u)=[(T_i-u-1)R_i^2
        -T_i sum_(j>i)a_ij r_j^(i)
        -(u+1)sum_(j>i)a_ij^2]/T_i^2.                        (1)

Every past vertex has nonpositive dot product with y. For future j>i,

    <p_j,y>=
      [R_j(r_j^(i)+(u+1)a_ij/T_i)
       -sum_(k>j)a_jk(r_k^(i)+(u+1)a_ik/T_i)]/T_j.           (2)

ALL normal inequalities are therefore exactly delta_i(u)>=0 and
delta_i(u)>=(2), for every future j, at BOTH u=0 and u=S_i.
Each difference is affine in u, so these two actual endpoint queries suffice.
The terminal condition is T_(N-1)>=M_(N-1). This supplies a complete
same-function realization test, not a local-correlation surrogate.

The negative second term in (2) is the inherited-coordinate cancellation
absent from unique-parent trees. Explicit positive correlations occur when
two vertices share a child:

    <p_i,p_j>=[-a_ij R_j+sum_(k>j)a_ik a_jk]/(T_i T_j), i<j.

Thus this construction genuinely goes beyond pairwise orthogonality and
the negative-edge tree Gram class.

Backward induction in <p_i,z><=0 shows every coordinate of a minimizer is
nonpositive. Hence 0 is closest to R_0e_0, with distance R_0.
At the terminal sample, writing S=S_(N-1), T=T_(N-1), s=sum of ALL steps,

    score=2F_end/R_0^2=(2T-2S-1)R_(N-1)^2/(T^2 R_0^2),     (3)
    V/R_0^2=1-[(T-S+s)/T]^2 R_(N-1)^2/R_0^2.               (4)

To prove (4) directly, use F_t=<x_t,g_t>-||g_t||^2/2 in
2h_t F_t+h_t(1-h_t)||g_t||^2=||x_t||^2-||x_(t+1)||^2,
then telescope the definition of V. Both the cost and defect are retained.

## 2. The four-phase diamond

Take four equal ordinary masses S=M-1 with checkpoint excesses
Mq, M(b), Mq, where

    2/5<q<7/16,  12/5<c<39/16,
    b=cq,  A=1+q,  B=1+b,
    T_0=T_2=MA, T_1=MB, T_3=Mt,  t>=1.

These include the ACTUAL four copies of H_(m-2) inside H_m for every
m>=128, with c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c and
q=a c^(m-2)/(1+sum H_(m-2)). Indeed
M_j=[a/(c-2)]c^j+[1-a/(c-2)]2^j, 0<a<c-2, so a<=q<=c-2.
The elementary bounds
lambda<169/70, c<39/16 and
a>=127/(129lambda)>2540/6321>2/5 give the displayed ranges.

Normalize R_0=1. Use exactly the four edges

    a_01=x, a_02=y, a_13=v, a_23=w,

where x,y>0, v,w>=0 and R=v+w>0. All other transfers vanish. The gradients are

    p_0=(e_0-x e_1-y e_2)/(MA),
    p_1=(x e_1-v e_3)/(MB),
    p_2=(y e_2-w e_3)/(MA),
    p_3=R e_3/(Mt).

When vw>0, the two middle gradients have the strictly positive correlation

    <p_1,p_2>=vw/(M^2 AB).

The necessary endpoint normals from (1)-(2) give

    q >= (1+A/B)x^2+y^2,              q >=x^2+2y^2,          (5)
    b x^2 >=v^2+(B^2/A)y^2-(B/A)vw,                         (6)
    q y^2 >= A wv+w^2+(A^2/t)R(v+w/A).                     (7)

These are exact for every finite M, not large-M limits: at the final
ordinary query u=S=M-1, one has u+1=M.

The remaining necessary normals are NOT being discarded as sufficient.
They will all be checked on the replacement construction below.

## 3. Removing the merge preserves every payoff and defect

For fixed R,t write z=v/R in [0,1]. Inequalities (6)-(7) imply

    y^2/R^2 >= Y(z)=(1+qz)(1-z+A/t)/q,
    x^2/R^2 >= X(z)=[z^2-(B/A)z(1-z)+(B^2/A)Y(z)]/b.       (8)

The function Y is concave and

    Y(0)-Y(1)=1/q-A/t >=1/q-A>0.

Therefore Y(z)>=Y(1)=A^2/(qt) throughout [0,1].

Next,

    b X'(z)=2[1+B/A-B^2/A]z
                  +(B/A)[-1+B(1-1/q+A/t)].                 (9)

Both coefficients on the right are strictly negative in the stated ranges.
For the coefficient of z, B>49/25 and b>24/25 imply
B b>1176/625>23/16>A. For the constant, t>=1 gives

    1-1/q+A/t <1-16/7+23/16=17/112,
    B(17/112)<(529/256)(17/112)=8993/28672<1.

Thus X decreases and X(z)>=X(1), where

    Y_1=A^2/(qt),
    X_1=[1+B^2 A/(qt)]/b.                                   (10)

Given ANY fully legal diamond, replace it by

    v'=R, w'=0, x'=R sqrt(X_1), y'=R sqrt(Y_1).

Equation (8) gives x'<=x and y'<=y. The two root conditions (5) therefore
remain true. The replacement is a unique-parent tree:
0 has children1 and2, vertex1 has child3, and vertex2 is a leaf.

Here is the full legality check, independently of any unverified tree lemma.
At the root, the only positive future comparisons are with p_1 and p_2;
(5) is precisely their endpoint condition. The comparison with p_3 is zero.
During phase1 the endpoint comparison with p_2 is equality because

    b x'^2-R^2=(B^2/A)y'^2.

Its comparison with p_3 is also valid, since

    b x'^2-R^2=(B^2 A/(qt))R^2 >= (B/t)R^2,

using BA>q. During phase2 the endpoint comparison with p_3 is equality:

    q y'^2/A^2=R^2/t.

Its other future comparisons are absent. Every comparison with a past
vertex is nonpositive, and every own endpoint value is nonnegative.
In this replacement, distinct gradient inner products are nonpositive.
Hence the difference between an own normal and any future normal decreases
with u; checking the last query checks every query in each phase.
The terminal phase has positive own normal, nonpositive comparisons with
all past vertices, and t>=1. Thus ALL comparisons against every vertex
and zero hold on the SAME whole trajectory.

The replacement has identical R_0=1, R_3=R and t. Formulas (3)-(4) show
that it has exactly the same normalized terminal objective AND primitive
defect, with the same actual closest-minimizer distance. The diamond's
positive middle-gradient correlation is therefore unnecessary for either
performance criterion in this regime.

## 4. Standalone quantitative bound after deletion

For the replacement write E_i=R_i^2, H_i=E_i/T_i.
Its low transitions i=0 and i=2 satisfy H_(i+1)/H_i<=q/(1+q):
a next waiting coordinate obeys that bound directly from its normal;
a next child obeys q T_i/(T_i+T_(i+1)), which is no larger, since
q+q^2<1<=T_3/M and q^2<1 for the other low transition.
The high transition i=1 to the waiting vertex2 satisfies H_2/H_1<=b/B.
In particular it obeys the larger bound bB/(A+B), because B b>A.

    score <2/[MA] * [q/(1+q)]^2 * bB/(A+B).

The actual full word mass satisfies M_m=M[(2+q)^2+(c-2)q]
=M[4+q(c+2)]<=M c^2, since q<=c-2. With K=1/(2M_m-1),

    score/K <
      4(qc)^3(1+qc)/[(1+q)^3(2+q+qc)]
      <=10763254593/11175730176 <1.                         (11)

For the first inequality, multiplying the previous score bound by
2M_m-1<2M c^2 gives exactly its displayed expression.
The last rational bound follows because the expression increases in both
q and c: its logarithmic q derivative is
3/[q(1+q)]+(c-1)/[(1+cq)(2+(1+c)q)]>0, and its logarithmic c
derivative is 3/c+q/(1+cq)-q/(2+(1+c)q)>0. Substitute
q=7/16,c=39/16 to obtain the rational number.

Consequently EVERY legal nonnegative four-phase diamond on this actual

not an exponent-only or asymptotic-loss argument. This excludes only the

claim: Complete VARIABLE-FULL-MATRIX re-selection candidate for an unbounded-length class: any signed intrinsic certificate with arbitrary negative incoming-terminal coefficients becomes an ordinary certificate whenever the schedule has a finite chain of saturated right-tail cuts ending in <=2 positive steps. The earlier prefix blocks are arbitrary; their ordinary certificates are forced by the input. At each cut the full matrix splits and theta transports as theta_b=1-(1-theta)(D/T)^2; replacing the leaf matrix and rebuilding gives every actual nonnegative coefficient. evidence:
# Variable-matrix terminal-credit repair along saturated right tails

Status: complete self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No numerical
solver and no fact_submit call. This is a certificate theorem in a specified
unbounded-length class, not the unrestricted primitive-cone theorem and not an
objective-profile bound. The only accepted background used is the actual
interpolation inequality from fact 1252b8823bb5a290. All additional algebra and
the short-leaf repair are proved here rather than imported from findings.

## 1. The exact certificate class and result

For a positive list h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), write s=sum h_i, C=1+s,
x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t, and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                                   -sC||g_n||^2,
 J_h=sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n),   E_theta(h)=V_h-theta J_h.

All n+1 formal gradients are independent. A signed terminal certificate is
an array lambda_ij on distinct finite pairs such that:

 (a) V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij cancels EVERY formal f_i coefficient;
 (b) the resulting FULL quadratic form M_h is positive semidefinite;
 (c) lambda_ij>=0 whenever j!=n, while lambda_(i,n) may be any real number.

An ordinary certificate additionally has lambda_(i,n)>=0. A nonnegative
certificate for E_theta is exactly a signed certificate with
lambda_(i,n)>=-theta h_i: to pass from the signed to the actual E_theta
array, add theta h_i on i->n. No interpolation inequality is replaced.

Define a class R of positive schedules recursively. Every list of length at
most two belongs to R. A longer list belongs to R if it has a decomposition

 h=(a,1+r,b),   A=1+sum a,   D=1+sum b,
 T=1+sum h=A+D+r,   r>0,   rT=AD,                 (1)

where a is ANY positive list (possibly empty) and b belongs to R. No
primitivity assumption is imposed on a. Fix one such finite decomposition
chain when a schedule has several choices. The word "right" only indicates
that the recursion continues inside b. The earlier lists a can be arbitrarily
long and need not themselves have a decomposition.

Candidate theorem. Every signed terminal certificate for any h in R can be
converted explicitly into an ordinary certificate for that SAME h. The
construction is allowed to change the full PSD remainder. More precisely,
at each cut (1), a supplied certificate forces an ordinary certificate for a
and a signed certificate for b. If the input has the E_theta lower bounds,
0<=theta<1, then the inherited tail bounds are exactly those of E_theta_b,
where

 kappa=(T/D)^2=(A/r)^2,
 theta_b=1-(1-theta)/kappa.                        (2)

The construction uses every actual multiplier, value flow, and full matrix.
It remains valid for nonnegative schedules whose positive compression is in
R, with a final certificate on all original independent gradients.

The assumptions include existence of the stated finite certificate. No dual
attainment theorem identifying arbitrary universal validity with this
certificate class is asserted.

## 2. A saturated cut has two explicit equality trajectories

Fix (1). Let L be the bridge query, so a occupies steps 0,...,L-1.
Call queries 0,...,L the prefix group P. The tail group B comprises the query
immediately after the bridge, all subsequent tail queries, and final query z.
Use local tail indices j=0,...,m, with z=m, and always embed them into the
original list when they occur in Q. Put p=g_L, q=g_z,
H_b=sum_(j<m)b_j g_j, and eta=r/D=A/T.

First use a scalar unit-threshold Huber function, starting sufficiently far
out on its positive affine ray that every query has gradient 1. It is convex,
differentiable, and 1-smooth. Every finite Q is zero and

 V_h=2sum_i h_i sum_(t=i)^(n-1)h_t
          +sum_i h_i(1-h_i)-s(s+1)=0.

Here 2sum_i h_i sum_(t=i)^(n-1)h_t=s^2+sum_i h_i^2.

The second scalar function is obtained by integrating

 f'(x)=min(1,max(x,-eta)),   f(0)=0,

and starts at x_0=A. Its derivative is continuous, nondecreasing, and
1-Lipschitz, so it is a legal convex 1-smooth function with minimizer 0.
If R_i^a is the remaining prefix step sum at query i in P, its prefix data are

 x_i=1+R_i^a,   g_i=1,   f_i=R_i^a+1/2.

At L, R_L^a=0. The bridge lands at -r. At a tail query with remaining tail
sum R_j^b, the data are

 x_j=-eta(1+R_j^b),   g_j=-eta,
 f_j=eta^2(R_j^b+1/2).

In particular x_z=g_z=-eta. All same-group Q are zero. Expanding the displayed
data gives every cross residual:

 Q_(i,j)=-(1+eta)eta R_j^b,   i in P, j in B,
 Q_(j,i)=-(1+eta)R_i^a,       i in P, j in B.        (3)

For example the first expression is
R_i^a+1/2-eta^2(R_j^b+1/2)-eta(1+R_j^b)
 -(1+R_i^a)+(1+eta)^2/2. The second expression follows by swapping the
roles in the definition of Q and equals -(1+eta)R_i^a.

Every incoming-terminal residual is zero: j=z has R_z^b=0 and same-group
tail residuals are zero. At every query one also has
f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2. Telescoping squared positions therefore gives

 2sum_(i<n)h_i f_i+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
     =||x_0||^2-||x_z||^2,

and consequently V_h=A^2-T^2 eta^2=0 by eta=A/T.

## 3. Complementarity forces the full mixed block, even with signed credit

Let lambda be any supplied signed certificate from Section 1. On either
equality trajectory, V_h=0 and every term having a potentially negative
coefficient has Q_(i,z)=0. All other coefficients are nonnegative and their
actual Q are nonpositive, by (3) or fact 1252b8823bb5a290. Hence

 0<=M_h=V_h+sum lambda Q<=0.

Every term with a strictly negative Q must therefore have coefficient zero.
Because the steps inside each list are positive, (3) leaves only these cross
edges:

 nu_i=lambda_(i,z), i in P;     mu_j=lambda_(j,L), j in B.     (4)

The nu_i are initially allowed either sign; all mu_j are nonnegative.
The two equality gradient vectors are e_P+e_B and e_P-eta e_B. A PSD matrix
annihilates a vector on which its quadratic form is zero (diagonalize the
real symmetric matrix, whose eigenvalues are nonnegative). Since eta>0,
both block indicators e_P and e_B lie in the kernel of the FULL M_h.

The only mixed prefix-tail terms remaining after (4) are

 -sum_(i in P)nu_i <g_i,H_b+q>
       +r sum_(j in B)mu_j <p,g_j>.                (5)

To check (5), the prefix-to-terminal position term has tail contribution
-<g_i,H_b>, and its squared difference contributes -<g_i,q>.
For j->L, the position contribution involving p is (1+r)<g_j,p>, while the
squared difference contributes -<g_j,p>, leaving r<g_j,p>.
All within-group Q and V_h have no mixed term.

For i<L, row i of M_h e_B is -D nu_i/2. Thus
nu_i=0 for every i<L. Rows j in B of M_h e_P then give

 mu_j=(nu_L/r)b_j for j<m,    mu_z=nu_L/r.          (6)

Value cancellation in V_h+sum lambda Q means that outgoing minus incoming
flow at every nonterminal index i is -2h_i. Summing through P yields
sum_j mu_j-nu_L=2(A+r). Using (6) gives

 nu_L=2r(A+r)/(D-r)=r(kappa-1),
 mu_j=(kappa-1)b_j (j<m),     mu_z=kappa-1.         (7)

Here D>r, kappa>1, and
(kappa-1)(D-r)=2(A+r), obtained by substituting rT=AD and T=A+D+r.
All mixed coefficients in (5) now vanish individually. Thus the full
prefix-tail matrix is zero, not just its value on the equality trajectories.

This proof permits arbitrary negative incoming-terminal coefficients. Their
signs never enter the complementarity step because the corresponding Q all
vanish on both equality runs.

## 4. Full energy identity and the exact inherited credit

Let

 J_b=sum_(j<m)b_j Q_(j,z),
 C_cross=sum_(j<m)b_j Q_(j,L)+Q_(z,L)+r Q_(L,z).

The identity needed for restriction and rebuilding is

 V_h=V_a+kappa V_b-(kappa-1)(C_cross+J_b).          (8)

Here V_a has terminal query L, and V_b uses the original tail queries.
For a full coefficient check put C_aux=C_cross+J_b. Its value and gradient
parts respectively are

 C_aux,f=2sum_(j<m)b_j f_j+(r-D)f_L+(2-D-r)f_z,
 C_aux,g=sum_(j<m)b_j(1-b_j)||g_j||^2
          +[(D-r)/2-r^2]||p||^2+(D+r)||q||^2/2.    (9)

The identity
2sum_j b_j<g_j,sum_(i<j)b_i g_i>
 =||H_b||^2-sum_j b_j^2||g_j||^2
gives (9) by expanding the four kinds of Q in C_aux; the mixed products
in p,H_b,q cancel. Inserting (9) into (8) matches the prefix coefficients
unchanged. It matches the bridge value and squared-gradient coefficients
2(1+r) and -r(1+r), and terminal coefficients -2(T-1) and -T(T-1).
These matches use

 (kappa-1)(D-r)=2(A+r),  kappa r^2=A^2,  kappa D^2=T^2.

Let lambda^a, lambda^b be the supplied within-group arrays. Define

 lambda_hat^b_ij=lambda^b_ij/kappa
                   -(1-1/kappa)b_i 1_(i<m,j=z).    (10)

Equations (7)-(8) give the exact formal identity

 M_h=M_a+kappa M_b,
 M_a=V_a+sum lambda^a_ij Q_ij,
 M_b=V_b+sum lambda_hat^b_ij Q_ij.                 (11)

The prefix and tail values are disjoint, so cancellation of all original
values implies separate cancellation in (11). Their formal gradients are
disjoint, and the mixed block is zero, so PSD of the full M_h implies PSD of
BOTH full blocks. The prefix coefficients are nonnegative because their
targets differ from z. The tail coefficients are nonnegative except possibly
those into z. Thus (11) is an ordinary certificate for a and a signed one
for b, as claimed.

If lambda_(i,z)>=-theta h_i, then (10) gives

 lambda_hat^b_(i,z)>=-[1-(1-theta)/kappa]b_i.

Every other tail sign remains nonnegative. This proves (2), with
0<=theta_b<1 when 0<=theta<1. No lower bound on the signed terminal entries
is needed for the unrestricted signed-certificate statement.

For reference, in the actual nonnegative E_theta multiplier array Lambda,
the forced cross entries are exactly

 Lambda_(i,z)=theta a_i                         (i<L),
 Lambda_(L,z)=r(kappa-1)+theta(1+r),
 Lambda_(j,L)=(kappa-1)b_j                      (j<m),
 Lambda_(z,L)=kappa-1,

with all other cross entries zero. This lists the ACTUAL interpolation
coefficients rather than a formal enlargement of their allowed signs.

## 5. Repair of the terminal leaf, with all value-flow equations retained

An empty schedule has V=0 and needs no multiplier. For one positive step u,
let c=lambda_01. Value cancellation gives lambda_10=c+2u. The constant
gradient equality puts (1,1) in the PSD kernel. Its second row equals
u(c-2)/2, so c=2. The full form is

 (2-u^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.

Thus PSD forces u<=sqrt(2), and both coefficients are already nonnegative.

For two positive steps (u,v), put s=u+v and
c=lambda_02, d=lambda_20, a=lambda_01, b=lambda_12.
Here c,b can be signed, whereas a,d,lambda_10,lambda_21 are nonnegative.
Value cancellation and the constant-gradient PSD kernel give respectively

 lambda_10=a+c-d+2u,       lambda_21=b+c-d+2s,
 u a+s c=2u,              v(b+c)+u d=2s(u+1).

For example these kernel equations follow by expanding the first and last
rows in the following six residuals, where F_ij=f_i-f_j:

 Q_01=F_01+(1/2-u)||g_0||^2+||g_1||^2/2-<g_0,g_1>,
 Q_10=F_10+(||g_0||^2+||g_1||^2)/2+(u-1)<g_0,g_1>,
 Q_12=F_12+(1/2-v)||g_1||^2+||g_2||^2/2-<g_1,g_2>,
 Q_21=F_21+(||g_1||^2+||g_2||^2)/2+(v-1)<g_1,g_2>,
 Q_02=F_02+(1/2-u)||g_0||^2+||g_2||^2/2
                                     -v<g_0,g_1>-<g_0,g_2>,
 Q_20=F_20+(||g_0||^2+||g_2||^2)/2
                                   +(u-1)<g_0,g_2>+v<g_1,g_2>.

Solving the four scalar equations gives

 a=2-(s/u)c,
 b=2s(u+1)/v-c-(u/v)d,
 lambda_10=2(u+1)-(v/u)c-d,
 b=2(u+1)+(u/v)lambda_10>0.                       (12)

Write U=g_0-g_1, Z=g_1-g_2. Since the constant gradient is in the kernel,
the entire full form is obtained by setting g_2=0 and expanding the six
displayed residuals. The result is

 [2-u^2+v(u-1)c/u]||U||^2
  +[c-(u-1)d]<U,Z>+[C_0-(u/v)d]||Z||^2,
 C_0=s[2(u+1)/v-s].                               (13)

If c>=0, all supplied coefficients are nonnegative, by (12), so retain them
and their full PSD matrix. If c<0, PSD in (13) forces C_0>=0 because d>=0.
It also forces u<=sqrt(2): this holds directly when u<1, and when u>=1 the
c contribution to the first diagonal is nonpositive, so 2-u^2>=0.
Replace the supplied array by

 lambda'_01=2, lambda'_10=2+2u,
 lambda'_12=2s(u+1)/v, lambda'_21=2s(u+1)/v+2s,
 lambda'_02=lambda'_20=0.                         (14)

Every coefficient is nonnegative, all value-flow equations remain valid,
and the full remainder, by (13) with c=d=0, is

 (2-u^2)||U||^2+C_0||Z||^2>=0.                    (15)

This deliberately changes the whole leaf matrix; no fixed-matrix repair is
claimed.

## 6. Explicit bottom-up reconstruction on arbitrarily long schedules

Repeatedly apply Sections 2-4 to the fixed decomposition chain. This extracts
ordinary certificates (lambda^a,M_a) for every earlier prefix block, and one
signed certificate for the final leaf. Apply Section 5 to that leaf.

At a cut, suppose sigma^b is the newly obtained ordinary tail array and
N_b its full PSD matrix. Define the rebuilt parent array by:

 within P: use lambda^a;
 within B: use kappa sigma^b_ij+(kappa-1)b_i 1_(i<m,j=z);
 cross: use (kappa-1)b_j on j->L for j<m,
        kappa-1 on z->L, and r(kappa-1) on L->z;
 every other cross entry: zero.                   (16)

All actual coefficients in (16) are nonnegative. Equation (8) gives, with
every value term retained,

 V_h+sum lambda_new,ij Q_ij=M_a+kappa N_b>=0.       (17)

The right side is a block-diagonal full PSD matrix on all original gradient
coordinates at this level. Repeat (16) until the root is rebuilt. The
recursion is finite because each tail is strictly shorter. This proves the
candidate theorem without a solver, a removed interpolation edge, or an
assumed tail coefficient floor.

Along multiple cuts the retained credit also has the exact telescoping law

 1-theta_leaf=(1-theta_root)(C_leaf/C_root)^2,       (18)

since each factor 1/kappa is the squared capacity ratio. This states credit
transport only; validity and repair come from the full coefficient proof.

## 7. Original-index zero steps

For a nonnegative schedule, partition query indices into classes at identical
positions caused by consecutive zero steps. Restrict the supplied full
certificate to the subspace where each such class has equal f and g. This is
a linear congruence of its PSD matrix. Between members of one class Q=0.
For different classes, aggregate all coefficients between the two classes.
Every nonterminal-target coefficient remains nonnegative. Only the terminal
class can have signed incoming coefficients. For an E_theta certificate its
aggregated lower bound is -theta times the sum of h_i in the source class,
which is the corresponding positive compressed step.

The restricted energy is exactly the positive-compressed V. Apply the theorem
to this compressed signed certificate. To lift the ordinary output, choose
the original positive-step query as representative of each nonterminal
class, and original n as terminal representative. Put each compressed
multiplier on the corresponding original pair, and all others zero. The
selected positions agree as formal identities because omitted steps have
zero coefficient. Thus the output energy and interpolation sum give the
compressed PSD quadratic on the selected independent gradients; every unused
original gradient has a zero row and column. No equality between distinct
formal gradients is imposed in the final certificate. The empty compression
has V=0 and the all-zero certificate.

## 8. An explicit unbounded family where this move changes the matrix

For any integer k>=0 take a to be k unit steps and b=(1,1). Put A=k+1,
D=3, and choose the positive root r of r(A+3+r)=3A. Let T=A+3+r and
kappa=(T/3)^2. This gives an (k+3)-positive-step schedule in R.
The prefix has the explicit ordinary adjacent certificate

 lambda^a_(i,i+1)=2(i+1)^2,
 lambda^a_(i+1,i)=2(i+1)(i+2), 0<=i<k,
 M_a=sum_(i<k)(i+1)^2||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2.

Substitution of the unit-step residuals verifies cancellation and this
identity; at query i the net flow is -2, and at query k it is 2k.

Set c=-1+1/(2kappa), so -1<c<0. On the two-unit-step tail use

 lambda^b_01=2-2c, lambda^b_10=4-c,
 lambda^b_12=8-c,  lambda^b_21=12,
 lambda^b_02=c,   lambda^b_20=0.

Its full remainder is ||U||^2+c<U,Z>+4||Z||^2, equal to
||U+(c/2)Z||^2+(4-c^2/4)||Z||^2, so it is PSD. Build a signed parent by
the formulas (16), using this signed tail instead of an ordinary tail.
The parent's only negative coefficient is

 lambda_(tail 0,z)=kappa c+(kappa-1)=-1/2.

All other nonterminal-target coefficients are nonnegative, and all other
terminal coefficients are nonnegative. It is therefore an E_(1/2)
certificate: adding h_i/2 to every incoming-terminal coefficient leaves
every actual multiplier nonnegative (the displayed negative entry becomes
exactly zero). Its full matrix is

 M_a+kappa[||U||^2+c<U,Z>+4||Z||^2].

The repair (14)-(16) yields the ordinary full matrix

 M_a+kappa[||U||^2+4||Z||^2].

The difference is -kappa c<U,Z>, an indefinite quadratic when c!=0.
Thus this is a genuine change of the PSD matrix, not the addition of an
automatically PSD term or a claim that all old coefficients already met the
ordinary floor. No claim that every possible fixed-matrix repair fails on
this example is made. No capacity gain or asymptotic improvement is claimed.

A rational calibration is k=1, giving h=(1,2,1,1), r=1, T=6, kappa=4,
c=-7/8. The ACTUAL nonnegative E_(1/2) coefficients are

 Lambda_01=2, Lambda_10=4,
 Lambda_21=Lambda_31=Lambda_41=3, Lambda_14=4,
 Lambda_23=15, Lambda_32=39/2,
 Lambda_34=39, Lambda_43=48, Lambda_04=1/2,

with every unlisted entry zero. Its full remainder is

 ||g_0-g_1||^2+4||g_2-g_3||^2
 -(7/2)<g_2-g_3,g_3-g_4>+16||g_3-g_4||^2.

The ordinary repaired coefficients are

 lambda'_01=2, lambda'_10=4,
 lambda'_21=lambda'_31=lambda'_41=lambda'_14=3,
 lambda'_23=8, lambda'_32=16,
 lambda'_34=35, lambda'_43=48, lambda'_24=3,

with every unlisted entry zero. Its full remainder is
||g_0-g_1||^2+4||g_2-g_3||^2+16||g_3-g_4||^2.
Expanding the ten possible scalar Gram monomials and five independent
function values verifies both identities exactly. A trivial rational
coefficient check reproduced these expansions; it is not the proof, an SDP
solve, or a verification-service verdict.

## 9. Exact scope and the unresolved interface

The local rigidity requires rT=AD. Without this equality, the second Huber
trajectory has energy A^2-T^2r^2/D^2 instead of zero, and it supplies neither
the two kernel vectors nor (7). The theorem therefore cannot be used to
repair a schedule with no such saturated decomposition.

Even for a saturated decomposition ending in a longer irreducible tail, the
restriction (10) only yields another signed certificate, with precisely the
increased credit (2). It is not an ordinary certificate until that remaining
tail is separately repaired. In particular, this proof does not settle a
general four-step leaf, general terminal-saturation of primal witnesses, or
the unrestricted exact B_N objective comparison. Its useful output is a
constructive, full-matrix repair on the specified class, and a narrower
remaining location for any strict cone separation.

glossary.R: Local class of positive schedules with a recursively saturated chain of right tails ending in a list of at most two entries; not the universal real-number symbol R in mathematical typesetting.
glossary.E_theta: V_h-theta J_h, with actual coefficient signs retained.
glossary.A,D,T: Capacities 1+sum a, 1+sum b, 1+sum h at the specified saturated cut.
glossary.r: Positive bridge excess satisfying rT=AD and bridge step1+r.
glossary.P,B: Disjoint formal-gradient query groups: prefix through bridge query, and tail after bridge through final query.
glossary.lambda_hat^b: Tail signed array obtained by dividing within-tail coefficients by kappa and subtracting (1-1/kappa)b_i on incoming-terminal entries.
glossary.M_a,M_b: Full PSD quadratic remainders of the extracted prefix and signed tail certificates.
glossary.C_cross: Weighted sum sum b_j Q_(j,L)+Q_(z,L)+r Q_(L,z) of actual cross inequalities.

Every free completion and b in[0,2] obeys2F<=[1+|z|²(S_pre²+sum h_pre²)/2]²/(2S_pre+1); hence limsup benchmark ratio<=578/(225e)<0.96. evidence:
# A chronological obstruction for every wide-angle elliptic frequency

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. No new fact_submit, solver evaluation,
numerical sweep, or external theorem is used. The proof below is self-contained
apart from the interpolation convention and benchmark recursions in accepted
facts1252b8823bb5a290 and b98bb807d514e80d. The earlier small-frequency and
unit-neighborhood candidates are NOT premises.

## 1. Statement on the assigned family

For each m>=128 define, with parameters fixed over that whole horizon,

    s=1+sqrt(2), c=s(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1.

Retain the n-1 steps of H_m after deleting its last d_0, and all n queried
jets at indices0,...,n-1. Write S for this retained stepsize sum and S2 for
its squared-step sum. Consider any complex z=alpha+i beta and any invertible
real2x2 map T, with ||T e_1||=1, giving

    P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z),
    x_i=T(Re P_i,Im P_i),
    g_i=T(Re[zP_i],Im[zP_i]).

Assume these SAME real data, some values f_i, and the optimum jet(0,0,0)
are fully interpolable by a convex differentiable1-smooth function. There
is no bound on T or its conditioning, and all parameters may depend on m.
The unqueried final point is x_(n-1)-b g_(n-1), with a completely free
interpolating function and endpoint gradient.

If z!=0, put r=|z| and omega=alpha/r. This candidate excludes the ENTIRE
angular sector

    0<omega<=7/40,                                     (1)

at every spectral magnitude. Indeed full legality forces

    S < (143/100)[2alpha/|z|^2-1/2],
    r S <1001/2000.                                   (2)

Moreover EVERY convex1-smooth interpolant F of the queried jets satisfies,
for EVERY b in[0,2], the explicit finite-horizon estimate

    2F(x_(n-1)-b g_(n-1))
       <= [1+|z|^2(S^2+S2)/2]^2/(2S+1).               (3)

In particular, uniformly over this entire sector, all metrics, legal values
and free completions,

    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) 2F(x_(n-1)-b g_(n-1))
          <=578/(225e)<24/25<1.                       (4)

The original last step d_0 belongs to[0,2]. Nonpositive alpha is impossible
for a nonzero z on a legal prefix of this form; z=0 gives objective zero.
No conclusion is claimed here for omega>7/40, several distinct modes,
changing generators, or unrestricted W.

## 2. A physical initial budget, with no matrix condition number

Let A=T [[alpha,-beta],[beta,alpha]] T^(-1), so g_i=A x_i and

    A^2-2alpha A+sigma I=0, sigma=|z|^2>0.

Set t_0=<x_0,g_0> and R_0=||g_0||. Invertibility gives R_0>0.
The two optimum interpolation inequalities give

    t_0>=R_0^2,
    0<=f_0<=t_0-R_0^2/2.                              (5)

The first step h_0=d_0 is positive. Adding the two interpolation inequalities
between queries0 and1 and dividing by h_0^2 gives

    <A g_0,g_0>>=||A g_0||^2>=0.

The quadratic identity for A therefore implies

    2alpha R_0^2-sigma t_0>=0.

Consequently alpha>0 and, on putting

    hcrit=2alpha/sigma,

one has hcrit>=1, t_0<=hcrit R_0^2, and the stronger initial-value budget

    f_0<=(hcrit-1/2)R_0^2.                            (6)

This budget is what the chronological prefix will violate. It is derived
from the actual Euclidean vectors and holds for every similarity metric.

## 3. Exact two-vector coefficients on a positive prefix

For an arbitrary beginning of the retained schedule let s_i=sum_(t<i)h_t.
There are real coefficients C_i,V_i such that

    x_i=(C_i+2alpha V_i)x_0-V_i g_0,
    g_i=C_i g_0+sigma V_i x_0,
    C_0=1, V_0=0,
    V_(i+1)=V_i+h_i C_i,
    C_(i+1)=C_i-2alpha h_i C_i-sigma h_i V_i.           (7)

Substitution verifies both recurrences using A^2=2alpha A-sigma I.
If a prefix has total mass T and

    2alpha T+sigma T^2/2<1,                            (8)

then induction in (7) gives, at every one of its queries,

    0<C_i<=1, 0<=V_i<=s_i,
    C_i>=1-2alpha s_i-sigma s_i^2/2.                   (9)

Here is the induction detail. While the preceding C's are positive, V is
nondecreasing with increments at most h_i, and C is nonincreasing. Summing
the C increments, using C_t<=1 and V_t<=s_t, gives

    C_i>=1-2alpha s_i-sigma sum_(t<i)h_t s_t
        >=1-2alpha s_i-sigma s_i^2/2>0.

Thus positivity is maintained and the argument reaches the last query.

Because t_0>=0, the representation in (7) implies

    <g_(i+1),g_i>>=C_(i+1)C_i R_0^2.

The ordered interpolation inequality gives

    f_i-f_(i+1)
      >=h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>+||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2/2.

Let e_i=2alpha s_i+sigma s_i^2/2. Under (8), (9) and
(1-e_i)(1-e_(i+1))>=1-e_i-e_(i+1) yield

    f_0-f_end
      >=[T-2alpha T^2-sigma T^3/2]R_0^2.              (10)

In detail, the telescoping identities needed for this sum are

    sum_i h_i(s_i+s_(i+1))=T^2,
    sum_i h_i(s_i^2+s_(i+1)^2)
         =(2/3)T^3+(1/3)sum_i h_i^3<=T^3.

Thus (10) uses the WHOLE chronological value drop, not just a local
cocoercivity condition or a radial polynomial bound.

## 4. The first actual crossing contradicts the budget

We need an actual queried prefix with controlled mass, not an artificial
subdivision of a large step. On the assigned ruler,

    2<c<49/20, 0<a<c-2.                               (11)

For the first bound, s<17/7 and m>=128 give
c<2193/896<49/20. For the second, s(s-2)=1,
c(c-2)>1, and ac=1-1/m<1.

Write S_j=sum H_j. Direct summation gives

    1+S_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j,
    A_mass=a/(c-2) in(0,1).

Every occurrence of a level-j step d_j has at least the mass S_j before it:
its first occurrence follows H_j and all later occurrences have more
preceding nonnegative steps. Hence for EVERY actual retained step, with
preceding mass u,

    h_t=1+a c^j<=(c-2)u+c-1.                          (12)

Put k=143/100 and assume, for contradiction, that

    S>=k(hcrit-1/2).

Choose the FIRST actual queried index whose accumulated mass T reaches
this threshold. Such an index exists in the retained prefix. By (12), its
mass obeys

    k(hcrit-1/2)<=T<(c-1)[k(hcrit-1/2)+1].

Let tau=1/hcrit in(0,1] and v=T/hcrit. Then

    L(tau)<=v<U(tau),
    L(tau)=k(1-tau/2),
    U(tau)=(29/20)[k+(1-k/2)tau].                      (13)

In particular U(tau)<=U(1)=9947/4000<5/2. Since
omega^2<=(7/40)^2=49/1600<1/32,

    2alpha T+sigma T^2/2
        =omega^2(4v+2v^2)<(1/32)(10+25/2)=45/64<1.

The coefficient and value-drop proof above applies to this actual prefix.
Its endpoint value is nonnegative. Dividing (10) by hcrit R_0^2 and using
(6) therefore imposes

    1-tau/2 >= v-omega^2(4v^2+2v^3)
              >=E(v),
    E(v)=v-(49/1600)(4v^2+2v^3).                     (14)

We show that (13) gives the strictly opposite inequality. E is concave
for v>=0. Both E(L(tau))-1+tau/2 and E(U(tau))-1+tau/2 are concave
functions of tau. It suffices to check their endpoints tau=0,1.

At tau=0, exact arithmetic gives

    E(143/100)-1=313657/800000000>0,
    E(4147/2000)-1=5062894373/6400000000000>0.          (15)

At tau=1, L(1)=143/200<3/4 and U(1)=9947/4000 lies in(12/5,5/2).
Using49/1600<1/32 gives the explicit lower estimates

    E(L(1)) >143/200-99/1024>1/2,
    E(U(1)) >12/5-225/128>1/2.                        (16)

Concavity therefore makes E exceed1-tau/2 at BOTH endpoints in (13),
and then at every v in that interval. This contradicts (14). We conclude

    S<k(hcrit-1/2).

Multiplying by r and using r hcrit=2omega gives

    rS<2k omega(1-1/(2hcrit))<=2*(143/100)*(7/40)
        =1001/2000,                                  (17)

which proves both assertions in (2).

## 5. The signed coefficient formula controls free completion

For the full retained prefix, (2) implies S/hcrit<k<5/2. The positivity
condition (8) consequently holds just as in Section4. Thus (7)--(9) apply
to EVERY queried jet; C_i decreases and V_i increases.

Write q=n-1 and g=g_q. From (7) and (5),

    <g,g_0>=C_q R_0^2+sigma V_q t_0>=0,
    <g,x_0>=C_q t_0+sigma V_q>=0.

The exact signed difference of two gradients is

    g-g_i=-(C_i-C_q)g_0+sigma(V_q-V_i)x_0.

Moreover V_q-V_i=sum_(t=i)^(q-1)h_t C_t<=S-s_i. Therefore the complete
terminal-correlation correction satisfies

    sum_(i<q)h_i<g,g-g_i>
       <=sigma<g,x_0>sum_(i<q)h_i(S-s_i)
       =sigma(S^2+S2)<g,x_0>/2.                       (18)

The nonpositive term containing C_i-C_q was discarded with its correct
sign. This estimate is sharper than simply bounding total gradient
variation in norm and retains the schedule's squared-step mass.

The outgoing last-query interpolation inequality to the optimum yields

    2f_q<=2<x_q,g>-||g||^2
         =2<x_0,g>-(2S+1)||g||^2
                       +2sum_i h_i<g,g-g_i>.

By (18), ||x_0||=1 and completing the square in ||g||,
