# C38. Free unqueried-terminal completion does not rescue the tree or diamond

Status: UNVERIFIED joint candidate, no solver or fact_submit. This addresses
the precise relaxation of the C35/C36 data: retain ALL actual queried jets and
the optimum jet (0,0,0), but allow an arbitrary smooth-convex terminal gradient
and value as in accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290. This is a MULTIPHASE construction
screen and does not repeat the separate two-cell calculation.

## 1. Defined family and objective convention

Fix m>=128, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j). Write M_j=1+sum H_j.
For a dyadic depth r with 0<=r<=m-2, put k=m-r, N=2^k, M=M_r,
q=a c^r/M, A=1+q and

    T_i=M(1+q c^(nu_2(i+1)))  (0<=i<N-1), T_(N-1)=T>=M.

There are N actual copies of H_r, with their original physical step order,
separated by the actual higher ruler checkpoints. Put S=M-1.
Choose any ordered rooted tree on 0,...,N-1, parents earlier than children.
For positive masses R_i, define

    p_i=(R_i e_i-sum_(j child of i)R_j e_j)/T_i,
    C=conv(0,p_i), F_C(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2),
    x_init=R_0 e_0.

Assume this tree relay is legal with p_i the gradient throughout ordinary
block i and its checkpoint, including the original prescribed p_(N-1)
at the terminal sample. This legality is equivalent to the following
explicit inequalities; hence the family is concrete, not arbitrary Gram data.

Let E_i=R_i^2, M_i=M, L_i=T_i-M, Ch_i the children and
W_i={j>i:parent(j)<i}. At the final ordinary query in phase i, the own
normal is

    [L_i E_i-M sum_(j in Ch_i)E_j]/T_i^2.

Past-vertex normals are nonpositive. Future normals are E_j/T_j for
j in W_i, (M/T_i)E_j/T_j for j in Ch_i, and zero otherwise.
These comparisons with the own normal, together with comparison with zero,
are necessary and sufficient at ALL queries: the own normal decreases,
waiting values stay fixed, and child values increase during the block.
At the terminal block T>=M suffices. These facts follow by following the
nonnegative coordinate masses, which move from a parent to its children
when its checkpoint exhausts the parent coordinate.

All p_i are actual independent real vectors; F_C is convex and 1-smooth
with grad F_C=P_C by the projection variational inequality. Every original
queried value is therefore

    f_j=<x_j,g_j>-||g_j||^2/2.                              (1)

Now retain the complete queried prefix and (0,0,0), and let f be ANY convex
1-smooth extension. Its true normalization is dist(x_init,argmin f).
Every f allowed by the exact maximal completion of accepted1252b8823bb5a290
is included. No terminal plane or terminal gradient is imposed on f.

## 2. Necessary tree height bounds, derived internally

Put H_i=E_i/T_i. Vertex i+1 is either waiting or a child of i. The complete
normal comparisons above imply respectively

    H_(i+1)/H_i <= L_i/T_i,
    H_(i+1)/H_i <= L_i T_i/[M(T_i+T_(i+1))].                (2)

For the child case keep its own E_(i+1) contribution in the child sum.
Dropping other nonnegative costs gives the bound. These are necessary
bounds on the retained original family, not a new sufficiency claim.

Geometric summation gives

    M_j=[a/(c-2)]c^j+[1-a/(c-2)]2^j,
    2/5<q<=c-2<7/16,  12/5<c<39/16,  M_m<=M c^k.          (3)

For completeness a<c-2 follows from ac<1<c(c-2).
Also M_r<=c^r implies q>=a>2540/6321>2/5, using
a>=127/(129lambda), lambda<49/20. The c upper bound follows from
lambda<169/70 and (169/70)(129/128)<39/16.
The exact mass relation giving the last inequality is
M_m=M[(1-q/(c-2))2^k+(q/(c-2))c^k].

At each even i the low checkpoint has L_i/M=q. Its waiting bound in
(2) dominates its child bound, since q^2<1 for a nonterminal next phase,
and q+q^2<1<=T/M for a terminal next phase. Thus its height multiplier
is at most q/A. At a high level ell>=1, followed by a low checkpoint,
the child bound dominates and is at most

    q c^ell/D_ell,  D_ell=(2+q+q c^ell)/(1+q c^ell)>1.

Indeed q c^ell>24/25 and its square plus itself exceeds1+q, which is
exactly the comparison of the two alternatives in (2).
There are N/2 low checkpoints and 2^(k-ell-1) high level-ell checkpoints.

Define

    Btree_k=4(qc)^(2^k-1) /
       [A^(2^(k-1)+1) product_(ell=1)^(k-1)
                        D_ell^(2^(k-ell-1))].              (4)

The following uniform estimates are algebraic:

    Btree_2<=eta=10763254593/11175730176<1,
    Btree_(k+1)<zeta Btree_k^2,
    zeta=6279/16384<1.                                    (5)

To check the base case,
Btree_2=4(qc)^3(1+qc)/[(1+q)^3(2+q+qc)] increases in q,c.
Its logarithmic q derivative is
3/[q(1+q)]+(c-1)/[(1+cq)(2+(1+c)q)]>0;
the c derivative is 3/c+q/(1+cq)-q/(2+(1+c)q)>0.
Substitution of q=7/16,c=39/16 gives eta.
The exact recurrence ratio is (qc)(1+q)/(4D_k), which is less than zeta.
Thus Btree_k<=zeta^(2^(k-2)-1)eta^(2^(k-2)) for all k>=2.

Let K=1/(2M_m-1). This is the global Huber score, with no assumption about
unrestricted W or the exact benchmark ratio.

## 3. Nonempty ordinary blocks: unchanged bound for EVERY completion

Suppose r>=1. Every p_i, including the old terminal p_(N-1), occurs at an
ACTUAL queried point, because each H_r has at least one step.
For any minimizer z of f, the accepted smooth-convex interpolation inequality
applied to (1) and (z,0,0) gives <p_i,z><=0. Backward induction through
the tree forces all coordinates of z nonpositive. Since x_init=R_0e_0
and0 is still a minimizer, the TRUE initial distance is exactly R_0.

The original final step is h_last=1+a. Its preceding gradient is
p_(N-1)=R_(N-1)e_(N-1)/T. Since the original polytope has this gradient
both at that query and at the endpoint, its values differ by
-h_last||p_(N-1)||^2. Smoothness of ANY new extension at the retained last
query therefore gives

    2f(x_n) <= 2F_C(x_n)+h_last^2||p_(N-1)||^2
             =[2T-D+h_last^2] E_(N-1)/T^2,
    D=2M-1.                                                (6)

This is an upper bound valid for every full completion, regardless of
attainability of the smoothness bound. It does not discard any prefix
constraint as sufficient.

Crucially D-h_last^2>0. Indeed M>=M_1=2+a, so

    D-h_last^2>=2(2+a)-1-(1+a)^2=2-a^2>0.

Thus [2T-D+h_last^2]/T<2. Multiplying all the height bounds in
Section2 and using M_m<=Mc^k gives, exactly as a finite product,

    2f(x_n)/dist(x_init,argmin f)^2 < Btree_k K < K,        (7)

for every r>=1 and k>=2. No small-o term or untracked terminal parameter
is needed. The same uniform margin eta and recursive decay hold even after
the final gradient and value are freed completely.

## 4. Empty ordinary blocks: retain the changed distance explicitly

Now r=0, so M=1, k=m, every original phase consists of just its checkpoint,
and the old terminal p_(N-1) is NOT a queried gradient. One cannot use it
to constrain the new minimizer set. We use a separate bound.

Let i=N-2, the last queried phase. Its T_i=A=1+q and its checkpoint is A.
It has either the terminal vertex as its sole child or no children.
In the child case, its position is R_i e_i and
p_i=(R_i e_i-R_(N-1)e_(N-1))/A.
In the leaf case, its position is R_i e_i+R_(N-1)e_(N-1) and
p_i=R_i e_i/A. Equation(1) and one smoothness step imply in either case

    2f(x_n) <= (1-A^(-2))E_i.                              (8)

For a child there is the additional term
[1-2/A-1/A^2]E_(N-1), which is negative since A<23/16;
dropping it gives (8). For a leaf, (8) is the exact smoothness bound.

The new closest-minimizer distance need not be R_0. Nevertheless the
retained initial gradient has norm at least R_0/A. Its1-Lipschitz property
and its vanishing at every minimizer give

    dist(x_init,argmin f)^2 >= E_0/A^2.                    (9)

There are N/2-1 low transitions before phase i and the same high transitions
as in Section2. Since T_i=T_0=A, their product bounds E_i/E_0.
Using (8)-(9), M_m<=c^k, and (4) gives

    [2f(x_n)/dist(x_init,argmin f)^2]/K
         < A^2(1+q/2) Btree_k
         <= (20631/8192) Btree_k.                         (10)

For every k>=3 this is already below1. Indeed (5) gives
Btree_k<zeta, and
(20631/8192)(6279/16384)<1. Here k=m>=128.
This proves the free-terminal exclusion also for empty ordinary blocks,
without silently retaining an unqueried terminal normal or the old distance.

## 5. The split-and-merge diamond also stays excluded

For clarity, the exact deletion argument needed here is reproduced.
Use four equal blocks M-1 and checkpoint excesses Mq,Mcq,Mq,
with A=1+q, B=1+cq, T_last=Mt. The real normals are

    p_0=(e_0-x e_1-y e_2)/(MA),
    p_1=(x e_1-v e_3)/(MB),
    p_2=(y e_2-w e_3)/(MA),
    p_3=(v+w)e_3/(Mt).

For any fully legal original diamond let R=v+w>0 and z=v/R.
All-normal endpoint necessities imply

    q >=(1+A/B)x^2+y^2,   q>=x^2+2y^2,
    y^2/R^2 >=Y(z)=(1+qz)(1-z+A/t)/q,
    x^2/R^2 >=X(z)=[z^2-(B/A)z(1-z)+(B^2/A)Y(z)]/(B-1).

These follow by direct dot products with the zero and future planes; no
remote comparisons are declared sufficient. The concave Y satisfies
Y(0)>Y(1), since Y(0)-Y(1)=1/q-A/t>0. Also

    (B-1)X'(z)
       =2[1+B/A-B^2/A]z+(B/A)[-1+B(1-1/q+A/t)]<0.

For the coefficient of z, B(B-1)>1176/625>A; for the constant,
B(1-1/q+A/t)<(529/256)(17/112)<1. Hence set

    v'=R, w'=0,
    y'=R sqrt(A^2/(qt)),
    x'=R sqrt([1+B^2 A/(qt)]/(B-1)).

Then x'<=x,y'<=y, so both root comparisons remain valid. In phase1
the comparison with p_2 is equality, and its comparison with p_3 follows
from BA>q. In phase2 the p_3 comparison is equality. All past comparisons
are nonpositive, all own values nonnegative, and every nonterminal
difference decreases across its ordinary block because the replacement
has nonpositive distinct-normal correlations. Thus every normal at every
query and terminal point is legal. This is an actual tree replacement.

The replacement leaves R,T_last and the ENTIRE last-block positions,
gradients and values unchanged. When r=m-2>=1, all four original normals
are queried. In the original diamond, their triangular inequalities
<p_i,z><=0 force all coordinates of any new minimizer nonpositive, so
the closest-minimizer distance remains1 even for a free completion.

For ANY free completion of the original diamond, the last-query bound (6)
is therefore the SAME expression as for the tree replacement. Applying
the proof of (7) to that replacement's parameters gives

    [2f(x_n)/dist(x_init,argmin f)^2]/K < eta<1.             (11)

The replacement does not purport to preserve the other queried jets.
It is used only to bound their shared terminal-position/last-query
parameters. Every original completion is bounded by (6), and this same
upper expression is bounded via the fully legal replacement.

## 6. Scope

Equations(7),(10) close free maximal-prefix completion for EVERY multiphase
ordered fresh-child tree in the stated dyadic family. Equation(11) closes
the exact four-edge diamond 01,02,13,23, including its positive middle
correlation. No final gradient is prescribed to the newly completing
function. The true initial distance is proved exactly for nonempty blocks
and lower-bounded explicitly when empty blocks remove a queried normal.

This does not close arbitrary shared-coordinate DAGs, changed queried
prefixes, or the original minimax problem. The k=1 two-cell family is
deliberately outside this result; it is another worker's separate task.

# An explicit terminal-saturation lift and its geometric obstruction

Status: self-contained candidate evidence, NOT verifier-accepted. No numerical
solver or fact_submit. This is a definite primal construction with checkable
hypotheses, together with an exact four-positive-step obstruction to making
it universal. It does not prove general terminal saturation or strict
enlargement of the E_theta cone.

The accepted interpolation background is fact 1252b8823bb5a290. No external
theorem is needed below. A Matlas cyclic-monotonicity search was background
only; the finite calculations and the interpolating function are explicit.

## 1. Data, rescaled normals, and the two hypotheses of the lift

Let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be positive, n>=1, and let
(x_i,g_i,f_i), 0<=i<=n, be an actual convex differentiable 1-smooth GD
trajectory, x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i. Define

 s=sum h_i, C=1+s, P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, R_i=s-P_i,
 y_i=x_i-g_i, H_g=sum_(i<n)h_i g_i,
 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 J_h=sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n),
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                                    -sC||g_n||^2,
 D_old=||H_g+g_n||^2-C^2||g_n||^2=V_h-2J_h.         (1)

To check the last equality, expand 2J_h and use
2sum_i h_i<g_i,sum_(t>=i)h_t g_t>
 =||H_g||^2+sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2. All value and nonterminal diagonal
terms then cancel in V_h-2J_h.

Choose real numbers d_0,...,d_n, with d_n=0. Put

 Delta=sum_(i<n)h_i d_i,
 t_j=sum_(u=j)^(n-1)h_u d_u-d_j,
 A_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j-y_n>+R_j(d_i-d_j),
 B_ij=(d_i-d_j)t_j.                               (2)

Here t_n=0. The two hypotheses are

 A_ij<0 for all j<n and i!=j, 0<=i<=n,             (3)
 epsilon=-(D_old+2C Delta)>0.                      (4)

These are explicit strict linear inequalities in the d_i, apart from the
fixed supplied geometric coefficients. They are sufficient conditions only;
not every negative V_h trajectory satisfies them.

## 2. Construction and every interpolation residual

Take any positive Lambda with

 Lambda^2 >= max{1, 2Delta^2/epsilon,
               max_(j<n,i!=j) 2(B_ij)_+/(-A_ij)},  (5)

where u_+=max(u,0). Define one new scalar gradient coordinate and its exact
GD positions by

 c_i=Lambda+d_i/Lambda,
 z_0=C Lambda,  z_(i+1)=z_i-h_i c_i,
 X_i=(x_i,z_i), G_i=(g_i,c_i).

Set the new terminal value F_n=0 and all earlier values to

 F_i=<G_i,X_i-X_n>-||G_i-G_n||^2/2.               (6)

Every incoming-terminal residual Q^new_(i,n) is then exactly zero by
definition. The new positions and gradients obey the original h exactly.
No old interpolation edge is deleted.

The following three-point identity follows by expanding the definition of Q
on any three finite jets:

 Q_ij-Q_(i,n)+Q_(j,n)
       =<g_i-g_j,(x_j-g_j)-(x_n-g_n)>.             (7)

Use (7) on the new data. The appended normal difference is

 (z_j-c_j)-(z_n-c_n)=R_j Lambda+t_j/Lambda.

Consequently EVERY finite ordered residual is exactly

 Q^new_ij=A_ij+B_ij/Lambda^2.                     (8)

For j=n this is zero. For j<n, i!=j, inequalities (3)-(5) give
Q^new_ij<=A_ij/2<0 if B_ij>0, and Q^new_ij<=A_ij<0 if B_ij<=0.
Thus all finite interpolation inequalities, including every outgoing
terminal edge, are checked.

## 3. A genuine minimizer and one fixed smooth convex function

Define adjusted new values Delta_i^val=F_i-||G_i||^2/2. Choose an index k
minimizing them, and add the optimum jet

 X_star=X_k-G_k,  G_star=0,  F_star=Delta_k^val.

For every i direct expansion gives

 Q^new_(i,star)=Q^new_(i,k)<=0,
 Q^new_(star,i)=Delta_k^val-Delta_i^val<=0.

These relations check every missing pair with the optimum. Translate X_star
and F_star to zero. Applying the finite construction in accepted fact
1252b8823bb5a290 to these complete jets gives one everywhere finite convex
differentiable 1-smooth function with that actual minimizer. Explicitly, in
the translated coordinates, set

 H_new(v)=max_(j in {star,0,...,n})
   {<G_j,X_j>-F_j+<X_j,v-G_j>+||v-G_j||^2/2},

The accepted fact proves that this function interpolates all displayed jets.

Its incoming-terminal Q are still zero after translation. Applying (1) to
the new data with J_new=0, and using d_n=0, gives the exact energy

 V_new=D_old+2C Delta+Delta^2/Lambda^2
      =-epsilon+Delta^2/Lambda^2<=-epsilon/2<0.    (9)

Here the extra-coordinate part follows directly from
sum h_i c_i+c_n=C Lambda+Delta/Lambda and c_n=Lambda.
This is a legal negative-V witness with all incoming-terminal Q zero.
No initial-distance or normalized objective preservation is asserted.

For each j<n put w_j=(y_j-y_n)/R_j; R_j>0. Conditions (3) imply, for any
two different nonterminal indices i,j,

 <g_i-g_j,w_i-w_j>>0.                             (10)

cancel. More general directed cycles give analogous necessary cyclic

There is a stronger quantitative statement that does not assume the specific

z_(i+1)=z_i-h_i c_i. Suppose some values F_i make the augmented jets legal
and every incoming-terminal residual zero. Let

 e_i=c_i-c_n, U_j=sum_(t>=j)h_t e_t-e_j.

Thus e_n=0 and
(z_j-c_j)-(z_n-c_n)=R_j c_n+U_j. Identity (7) and the two actual inequalities

## 1. General theorem, any dimension and any nonnegative schedule

Let h_0,...,h_(q-1)>=0, S=sum h_i, and let the queried real jets

vectors, not merely orthogonal gradients. A witness exceeding (2), or

We re-prove the chronological restriction needed for this conclusion.

R_0=||g_0||>0. Let t_0=<x_0,g_0>. Initial optimum inequalities give
t_0>=R_0^2 and f_0<=t_0-R_0^2/2. The first step d_0 is positive.

The ordered interpolation inequalities give

                              +||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2/2.

## 5. Uniform constant gap against the exact benchmark

For the assigned family the complete ruler sum is

    S_full=2^m-1+a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2), S=S_full-d_0.

Since a/(c-2) tends to1, c^m/s^m tends to e, and 2/s<1, one has

    S/s^m ->e.                                        (21)

We include the needed sharper benchmark estimate rather than using an
unverified shared lemma. Put rho=log_2 s and C_n=S_circle(n)+1. The
accepted recursions have increasing primitive and dominant joins

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
    Gjoin(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

For V(t)=(1+t)^rho-1, differentiation with t=exp(u) gives

    d^2/du^2 log V(exp(u))
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/V(t)^2>0.

The bracket is positive because rho>1. Convexity at u and -u gives
V(t)V(1/t)>=V(1)^2=(s-1)^2=2. With
t=(A/B)^(1/rho), D=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho this is
(D-A)(D-B)>=2AB, so Omega(A,B)<=D. Zero arguments follow by continuity.
Induction on the primitive split k+l=n-1 proves C_n<=(n+1)^rho.
Since sqrt(D^2+8AD)<=D+4A, one has Gjoin(A,D)<=4A+D. Induction on
the dominant split gives

    B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^rho+l^rho]<=1+4n^rho.               (22)

The sufficient region2Re(z)S+|z|^2 S^2/2<1 can be used directly as well.
The coefficient criterion C_i>=0 for all queried indices is broader than

## 6. What the next mechanism must change

A successful near-critical common-metric witness outside these bounds
must have at least one negative coefficient C_i, unless it already leaves
the homogeneous single-mode class. More geometrically, the general theorem
requires either a negative transverse pair correlation or a negative
initial-direction gradient projection. Keeping every transverse queried
gradient on the same nonnegative ray while all initial-direction
projections remain nonnegative cannot give the missing constant, even
though the function values and terminal gradient are fully free.

The general theorem allows many transverse directions with pairwise
nonnegative correlations. It does not cover a signed transverse pattern,
negative longitudinal projections, all mixtures, or unrestricted W.
Nothing here proves the original arbitrary-schedule exact-profile target.

# Exact elliptic energy barrier and an intermediate-scale exclusion

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. This finishes the in-flight single-mode
derivation allowed by guidanceea594a814f06f984; the next task is the JOINT
near-critical mixture audit. No new fact_submit or numerical evaluation.
Only accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the interpolation convention below.
No previous unverified frequency result is used as a premise.

## 1. A necessary amplitude barrier for every actual query

Let h_0,...,h_(N-1)>=0 be arbitrary, P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z), and
let queried data0,...,N be

    x_i=T(Re P_i,Im P_i),
    g_i=T(Re[zP_i],Im[zP_i]), ||T e_1||=1,

for an arbitrary invertible real2x2 map T. Include the optimum jet(0,0,0)
and assume full convex1-smooth interpolation by some values f_i.
Put z=alpha+i beta, sigma=|z|^2>0, and

    omega=alpha/sqrt(sigma), 0<omega<=1/2.              (1)

Then EVERY actual queried polynomial obeys

    |P_i(z)|^2>=1-2omega.                              (2)

All metrics, spectra and values may vary with the horizon. This is a
single common-metric theorem. Its proof does not impose individual-mode
budgets on a jointly legal mixture and cannot be applied that way.

## 2. Exact energy identity and interpolation drop

Set A=T [[alpha,-beta],[beta,alpha]] T^(-1). Thus g_i=A x_i and
A^2-2alpha A+sigma I=0. The positive definite matrix

    Nmat=sigma I+A^T A

satisfies the exact identity

    A^T Nmat+Nmat A=4alpha A^T A.                      (3)

Indeed (A^T)^2 A+A^T A^2=4alpha A^T A-sigma(A+A^T), which cancels the
other two terms. Define the quadratic energy

    J(x)=[sigma||x||^2+||A x||^2]/(4alpha).

For a step x_+=x-hg with g=A x and g_+=g-hA g, (3) gives

    J(x)-J(x_+)
       =h||g||^2-h^2[sigma||g||^2+||A g||^2]/(4alpha).

The reverse ordered interpolation inequality is

    f(x)-f(x_+)
       >=h||g||^2-h^2<g,A g>+h^2||A g||^2/2.

The difference between its right side and J(x)-J(x_+) is h^2 times

    [(1+2alpha)/(4alpha)]
          ||A g-[2alpha/(1+2alpha)]g||^2
       +[sigma/(4alpha)-alpha/(1+2alpha)]||g||^2.       (4)

By (1), sigma>=4alpha^2, so the final coefficient is nonnegative.
Thus every actual step, of arbitrary size, obeys

    f_i-f_(i+1)>=J(x_i)-J(x_(i+1)).

After summing, f_i>=0 and f_0<=<x_0,g_0>-||g_0||^2/2 imply

    sigma||x_i||^2+||g_i||^2
       >=sigma+(1+2alpha)||g_0||^2-4alpha<x_0,g_0>.    (5)

No operator-norm estimate or metric averaging has entered (3)--(5).

## 3. Eliminate the physical Gram parameters

Fix an actual query and write P_i=u+i v. Since beta is nonzero under(1),
put

    V=-v/beta, C=u+alpha v/beta, U=u-alpha v/beta,
    d=sigma V^2, R=|P_i|^2=UC+d,
    t=<x_0,g_0>, Q=||g_0||^2.

Then U-C=2alpha V and the exact physical representations are

    x_i=U x_0-V g_0, g_i=C g_0+sigma V x_0.

Expanding the left side of(5) yields

    sigma(U^2+d)+(C^2+d)Q-4alpha d t.

Therefore, with

    A0=1-C^2-d, B0=1-U^2-d, A1=A0+2alpha,

inequality(5) is equivalent to

    A1 Q-4alpha(1-d)t+sigma B0<=0.                    (6)

Suppose, contrary to(2), that R<1-2omega. The quadratic forms C^2+d
and U^2+d in(u,v) each have eigenvalues1/(1+omega),1/(1-omega).
For example C=u+(alpha/beta)v and d=sigma v^2/beta^2, so the form's
trace is2/(1-omega^2) and its determinant1/(1-omega^2). It follows that

    C^2+d, U^2+d <=R/(1-omega)<1.

Thus A0,B0,A1 are positive. Since ||x_0||=1, Q>=t^2, so(6) requires

    A1 t^2-4alpha(1-d)t+sigma B0<=0.                  (7)

But direct expansion using U-C=2alpha V and UC+d=R gives

    A0 B0=(1-R)^2-4omega^2 d(1-d).

The discriminant of(7), divided by4sigma, is consequently

    4omega^2(1-d)^2-A1 B0
      =4omega^2(1-d)-(1-R)^2-2alpha B0
      <=4omega^2-(1-R)^2<0.

A quadratic with positive leading coefficient and negative discriminant
is positive for every real t, contradicting(7). This proves(2).

## 4. Consequence on the actual near-critical ruler

For each m use

    s=1+sqrt(2), c=s(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    b_j=a c^j, d_j=1+b_j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), n=2^m-1.

Retain H_m with its last d_0 deleted, all its actual queried data, and
let S_pre be its sum. There is NO sequence of fully legal single-mode
common-metric prefixes with m tending to infinity for which

    7/40<=Re(z_m)/|z_m|<=49/100,
    |z_m| ->0, |z_m|S_pre ->infinity.                 (8)

This is a precise intermediate-scale legality obstruction. It neither
decides order-one scaled frequencies nor gives a mixed-mode theorem.
We prove it directly from(2) and the actual first subword at a spectral scale.

Suppose(8) holds. Write r=|z_m|, omega=Re(z_m)/r and L=11/2.
Choose the first level j with b_j r>=L omega. For all sufficiently large m
this level exists with j<=m-1, because

    b_(m-1)/S_pre ->(s-2)/s>0.

Also j tends to infinity since r tends to0 and a stays bounded away from0.
Minimality gives, with v=b_j r and w=v/omega,

    L<=w<cL.                                          (9)

The complete prefix H_j and its endpoint occur inside the retained word:
H_j is inside the first H_(m-1). Its polynomial is

    p_j(z)=product_(ell<j)(1-d_ell z)^(2^(j-ell-1)).

If any factor vanishes, (2) is violated immediately. Otherwise applying
log(1+x)<=x to each squared factor gives

    log|p_j(z)|^2 <=-2Re(z) S_j+|z|^2 T_j,             (10)

where the exact first and second step sums of H_j are

    S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2),
    T_j=2^j-1+2a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2)
                         +a^2(c^(2j)-2^j)/(c^2-2).

Because b_j r=v stays in a positive compact interval, r2^j tends to0.
Explicitly, c^j=v/(ar) and
r2^j=r(v/(ar))^(log_c 2), with log_c 2 bounded strictly below1.
The other omitted terms vanish as well, so(10) gives uniformly

    log|p_j(z)|^2
       <=-omega^2[2w/(c-2)-w^2/(c^2-2)]+o(1).        (11)

At the limiting c=s, the bracket is the concave quadratic

    F(w)=2s w-w^2/(2s-1), L<=w<=sL.

Both endpoint values exceed18. The exact differences are

    F(L)-18=(39-12s)/[4(2s-1)]>0,
    F(sL)-18=(83-34s)/[4(2s-1)]>0,

using s<17/7. Concavity makes the bracket exceed18 throughout that compact
interval. Continuity in c and(9), followed by(11), therefore yields, for
all sufficiently large m,

    |p_j(z)|^2 <=exp(-17omega^2).                      (12)

The harmless o(1) is absorbed uniformly because omega>=7/40.

On the whole interval[7/40,49/100],

    exp(-17omega^2)<1-2omega.                          (13)

For a fully explicit check, D(omega)=1-2omega-exp(-17omega^2) has
D''=34exp(-17omega^2)(1-34omega^2)<0 on that interval. At7/40,
the exponent833/1600 exceeds1/2, so its exponential exceeds
1+1/2+1/8=13/8>20/13. At49/100 the exponent40817/10000 exceeds4,
and exp(4)>(8/3)^4>50, since exp(1)>8/3. Thus D is positive at both
endpoints, and concavity proves(13). Equations(12),(13) contradict(2)
at an ACTUAL queried endpoint. This proves the asserted impossibility(8).

## 5. Scope and handoff

The amplitude barrier is metric-uniform and uses a real physical energy,
not a normal decomposition. The near-critical application rules out a
diverging mass-scaled frequency in the stated angle interval when |z|
tends to0. It does not rule out bounded |z|S_pre, angles above49/100,
frequencies away from0, or joint repair between different modes.

In particular, one cannot sum(2) with mixture weights: its derivation uses
an initial/terminal value budget for ONE operator with ONE quadratic
minimal polynomial. A jointly legal mixture need not admit those separate
budgets. The new assignment requires a genuinely common cycle on the
direct sum; that audit is the next work item.

Fact search found no accepted version of this energy barrier. Matlas
returned arXiv2006.09946,2104.12931,1509.09102, none used here. All new
identities and inequalities needed for the conclusion are displayed above.
The complete original exact-profile theorem remains open.

Status: UNVERIFIED joint candidate. No solver, sweep or fact_submit.
This screens an actual growing family with a merge at every phase.
The proved range is explicit: m>=65536 and at least4096 phases.
Smaller phase counts, varying split fractions and longer memory are not closed.

## 1. One real simplex and its entire chronological transcript

Put lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), n=2^m-1.

All their individual steps are retained in their actual order.

Choose positive R_i, let E_i=R_i^2, and define nonnegative transfers

    C=conv(0,p_0,...,p_(N-1)),

# A genuinely joint logarithmic-spectrum obstruction on the actual word

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate, without a new fact_submit allocation.
All new estimates are proved below. Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the
interpolation convention and free terminal completion; accepteddfde2fa326c908bf
supplies the algebraic complex-cycle identity; acceptedb98bb807d514e80d
supplies only the exact benchmark recurrences. No unverified spectral
exclusion is used as a premise.

## 1. Actual schedule, finite ansatz, and uniform result

Let m>=128, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), n=2^m-1, and D=d_(m-1).
The parameters c,a are fixed at this horizon. Use the retained prefix

index is q=n-1. Let P_i(z) be the chronological prefix polynomial, 0<=i<=q.

Here is one definite finite probability ansatz. Set angular parameters
t_1=1/32 and t_2=1/64, and, for 0<=j<m and ell in{1,2}, put

    r_(j,ell)=t_ell/(1000d_j),
    z_(j,ell)=r_(j,ell)[t_ell+i sqrt(1-t_ell^2)].       (1)

Choose ANY nonnegative weights w_(j,ell) summing to1 and form ACTUAL
real vectors in R^(4m): the two coordinates in block(j,ell) are

    x_i^(j,ell)=sqrt(w_(j,ell))(Re P_i(z_(j,ell)),Im P_i(z_(j,ell))),
    g_i^(j,ell)=sqrt(w_(j,ell))(Re[z_(j,ell)P_i(z_(j,ell))],
                              Im[z_(j,ell)P_i(z_(j,ell))]).    (2)

Thus ||x_0||=1 and the actual queried recursion is x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i.
Include the optimum jet(0,0,0). Values f_i are ARBITRARY JOINTLY legal
values: all ordered interpolation inequalities must hold for these same
vectors. Individual component legality and separability are NOT assumed.

For EVERY legal choice of weights and values, every interpolant F of
the whole queried prefix, and EVERY b in[0,2], the result is

    2F(x_q-b g_q) <= 1/(64D).                           (3)

In particular this includes the original b=d_0, since 1<d_0<3/2, and
the maximal free completion of accepted1252b8823bb5a290. No constraint
is placed on the new terminal gradient. The bound holds uniformly in
the weights, dimension, and values, not merely mode by mode.

More generally (3) follows from the following whole-spectrum statement.
Fix any 0<t_max<=1/2. Allow ANY finite list of complex numbers z with

    r=|z|>0, t=Re(z)/r in(0,t_max], r<=t/(1000d_0),     (4)

and optionally z=0, with arbitrary probability weights and the vectors(2).
All jointly legal such prefixes obey

    2F(x_q-b g_q)<=16t_max^2/D, b in[0,2].             (5)

Both signs of the imaginary part are allowed in (4). Formula(1) is a
specific finite family contained in it, with two different angular types
and all logarithmic physical scales d_j. The theorem does not include
all normal spectra, all common metrics, or unrestricted W_n.

## 2. Elementary uniform schedule estimates

For m>=128,

    12/5<c<5/2, a>1/3, a/(c-2)<1.

Indeed lambda>12/5 follows from sqrt(2)>7/5; lambda<5/2 follows from
sqrt(2)<3/2, and its actual value also gives lambda(129/128)<5/2
(squaring sqrt(2)<191/129 proves the last assertion). The a bound follows
from (127/128)/(5/2)>1/3. Since lambda(lambda-2)=1, c(c-2)>1 and
a/(c-2)=(1-1/m)/[c(c-2)]<1.

Let S_k and T_k be the sum and squared-step sum of full H_k. Counting
multiplicities gives

    S_k=2^k-1+a(c^k-2^k)/(c-2),
    T_k=(2^k-1)+2a(c^k-2^k)/(c-2)
                             +a^2(c^(2k)-2^k)/(c^2-2).

The positivity of 1-a/(c-2) implies

    S_k >= [d_k-(c-1)]/(c-2).

Also 2^k<=c^k, 1/a<3 and 1/(c-2)<5/2 imply S_k<6d_k.
Consequently, whenever d_k>=2000,

    S_k>=(19/10)d_k,
    T_k<=d_k^2/(c^2-2)+2S_k
         <=[25/94+12/2000]d_k^2 <(7/25)d_k^2.          (6)

## 3. One common indexed cycle and exact algebra

For a single parameter z=alpha+i beta define sigma=|z|^2,

The actual word recursion gives

      =d_0 sigma[1-alpha-d_0 kappa]|p_k^-|^2.          (11)

For clarity, the removed reverse edge has weight

The remaining nonzero modes have D<h_c. All factors throughout H_m

# Variable-matrix repair of a terminal-chord certificate class

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No new solver or
fact_submit call. All identities below are proved directly. The theorem has
arbitrary positive length and does not require a saturated composition cut.
It is a support-and-cumulative-sign theorem, not general credit re-selection.

## 1. Definitions and exact statement

Let n>=1 and let h_0,...,h_(n-1)>0. Put

 P_i=sum_(t<i) h_t, p_i=1+P_i, s=P_n, C=1+s,
 R_i=sum_(t>=i) h_t=C-p_i, with R_n=0.

Use the actual GD substitutions x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                            -s(s+1)||g_n||^2.

Suppose a real signed array lambda cancels every value coefficient in
V_h+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij and its FULL remainder M is PSD on independent
g_0,...,g_n. Suppose its only possibly nonzero entries are

 lambda_(i,i+1)=a_i, lambda_(i+1,i)=b_i       (0<=i<n),
 lambda_(i,n)=c_i                           (0<=i<n-1).

The latter are the nonadjacent terminal chords; the adjacent last incoming
edge is a_(n-1), not another c entry. Set c_(n-1)=0 for summation and

 zeta_k=sum_(i<=k)c_i,     0<=k<n.

Assume the following cumulative condition at each long nonfinal step:

           zeta_k<=0 whenever k<n-1 and h_k>1.             (1)

Then the following array is an ordinary nonnegative certificate for V_h:

 a_i^0=2P_(i+1)p_i/h_i,
 b_i^0=2P_(i+1)p_(i+1)/h_i,                              (2)

on the two adjacent directions, with all other entries zero. Its complete
formal remainder is

          M^0=sum_(i<n) w_i ||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2,            (3)
 w_i=(P_(i+1)/h_i)[p_i-(h_i-1)p_(i+1)]>=0.

In particular, if the input is an actual E_theta certificate represented
by lambda, with lambda_(i,n)>=-theta h_i, 0<=theta<1, and all other entries
nonnegative, it can be repaired to the ordinary certificate (2). The proof
does not need the numerical bound theta once the displayed support, full
PSD, flow and cumulative condition are assumed. The incoming chords c_i
can have both signs; only their indicated cumulative sums are restricted.

No property is asserted for a certificate with extra remote prefix edges,
extra outgoing terminal edges, or positive zeta_k at a step h_k>1. All these
are genuine remaining cases for the general cone question.

## 2. Full affine-kernel identity and weighted circulation

This section holds for any full-support real multiplier array. Let e be
the all-one column, L=diag(lambda e)-lambda the row Laplacian, and let A

 omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T,
 D_quad=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_(n-1)(2-h_(n-1)),-s(s+2)).

Value cancellation is exactly L^T e=omega, and expansion gives

                M=D_quad+sym(L A),   sym(B)=(B+B^T)/2.         (4)

For completeness, the position terms in sum lambda Q are sym(L(A-I)).
The squared-gradient differences contribute sym(L)-diag(omega)/2.
Adding the diagonal gradient terms of V gives (4).

Evaluating this value-canceling quadratic on a constant-gradient legal
affine segment gives e^T M e=0: all Q vanish, and V=0. Such a segment can
be realized by a scalar Huber function started sufficiently far along an
affine ray. Since M is PSD, M e=0. Equivalently this follows by considering
the quadratic on e+t v for arbitrary v and both signs of t.

As A e=p, equation M e=0 yields

                 Lp=-2D_quad e-A^T omega=diag(p)omega.         (5)

Here, for i<n,

 (A^T omega)_i=-2h_i+2h_i P_(i+1),
 -2h_i(2-h_i)-(A^T omega)_i=-2h_i p_i;

and the terminal component is 2s(s+1). These explicitly verify (5).
Combining (5) with L^T e=omega shows that

                 mu_ij=lambda_ij p_j                    (6)

has equal incoming and outgoing sums at every node. Indeed (5) says
sum_j lambda_ij p_j=p_i sum_j lambda_ji. Thus mu is a real circulation,
though its terminal edges can still be negative.

The separate value-flow condition must be retained: with u_i=1/p_i,

          sum_j mu_ij(u_j-u_i)=omega_i.                  (7)

Circulation alone does not imply (7), positivity, or PSD.

## 3. The input adjacent coefficients are forced by the chords

Sum the exact value flows over vertices 0,...,k. The only crossing edges
are the adjacent pair k,k+1 and the terminal chords from this prefix, so

               a_k-b_k+zeta_k=-2P_(k+1).                 (8)

Sum the circulation balances (6) over the same prefix:

               a_k p_(k+1)-b_k p_k+C zeta_k=0.           (9)

For k=n-1 the formula counts the last adjacent incoming edge only in a_k;
c_(n-1)=0 prevents double counting. Solving (8)-(9) gives

 a_k=a_k^0-(R_k/h_k)zeta_k,
 b_k=b_k^0-(R_(k+1)/h_k)zeta_k.                         (10)

This retains all actual coefficients rather than selecting an assumed
matrix. It follows from the full input PSD through its affine kernel.

## 4. A diagonal test in the full gradient-difference coordinates

For each k<n let z^(k) be the formal gradient column equal to1 on indices
0,...,k and0 thereafter. This is a legitimate direction in the FULL
original gradient space, regardless of whether it is itself a legal run.
For ANY real array satisfying value cancellation and (5), a direct
calculation yields

 (z^(k))^T M z^(k)
     =-P_(k+1)^2
          +sum_(i<=k<j)lambda_ij[1+p_j-p_(k+1)].         (11)

Here are all terms of that calculation. Set every value to zero. In a Q
with both indices in the prefix, the gradient coefficient is p_i-p_j.
For a prefix-to-suffix pair it is p_i-p_(k+1)+1/2. For a suffix-to-prefix
pair it is1/2, and it is0 inside the suffix. Sum (5) over prefix rows to
replace the first group and the p_i-p_j part of the forward crossing group
by -2sum_(i<=k)h_i p_i. The remaining forward coefficient is
p_j-p_(k+1)+1/2. By the value cut flow, the total reverse crossing mass is
the forward mass plus2P_(k+1); this adds another1/2 to each forward weight
and contributes P_(k+1). Finally

 sum_(i<=k)h_i(1-h_i)-2sum_(i<=k)h_i p_i+P_(k+1)
       =-sum_(i<=k)h_i^2-2sum_(i<=k)h_i P_i
       =-P_(k+1)^2.

This proves (11) without suppressing any matrix direction.

For the stated adjacent-plus-terminal support, (11) becomes

 (z^(k))^T M z^(k)
       =-P_(k+1)^2+a_k+(1+R_(k+1))zeta_k
       =w_k+[(h_k-1)R_(k+1)/h_k]zeta_k.               (12)

The second equality follows from (10), R_k=h_k+R_(k+1), and
a_k^0-P_(k+1)^2=w_k. Because M is PSD, the left side is nonnegative.

If h_k>1 and k<n-1, (1) makes the last term in (12) nonpositive, whence
w_k>=0. If k=n-1 it vanishes because R_n=0, with the same conclusion.
If 0<h_k<=1, the formula

 w_k=(P_(k+1)/h_k)[(2-h_k)p_k+h_k(1-h_k)]

is strictly positive directly. Thus every w_k in (3) is nonnegative.

## 5. Complete repaired certificate

The coefficients (2) are nonnegative. Across edge k their net forward
flow is a_k^0-b_k^0=-2P_(k+1), so the difference between adjacent cuts
is -2h_k, with the terminal flow2s. Hence every original value coefficient
cancels. Direct expansion of the adjacent Q terms gives a tridiagonal
gradient matrix. Its affine kernel vanishes, as can be checked from (2)
or (9) with zeta=0. Its off-diagonal entry on edge k is

 [ -a_k^0+(h_k-1)b_k^0 ]/2=-w_k.

Therefore the full matrix is precisely the weighted path Laplacian (3):
the diagonal entries are w_(k-1)+w_k, with endpoint conventions. Since
all w_k>=0, (3) proves PSD on ALL independent original gradients. No equality
between two formal gradients, no rank-one test, and no primal-witness-only
PSD inference is used.

The construction actually changes the matrix. It does not assert that
M^0-M is PSD, and the next family shows that difference can be indefinite.

## 6. A nonsaturated signed input family at every positive length n>=2

Take h_i=t=4/3 for all i<n, let d_i=g_i-g_(i+1), and put

 w_k=(k+1)[2-t^2+k t(2-t)],
 epsilon=(2-t^2)/(4t n^2)=1/(24n^2),
 theta=epsilon/t=1/(32n^2).

Start with (2) and add these four signed changes:

 Delta lambda_01=n epsilon,
 Delta lambda_10=(n-1)epsilon,
 Delta lambda_0n=-epsilon,
 Delta lambda_1n=epsilon.                              (13)

For n=2 the last change is added to the existing adjacent coefficient.
Every actual E_theta multiplier is nonnegative: add theta h_i=epsilon
to every incoming terminal edge. In particular the only negative signed
entry, lambda_0n=-epsilon, becomes0. Value flow is unchanged at every node.
For n>=3 the chord cumulative sums are zeta_0=-epsilon and zeta_k=0 for
k>=1. For n=2 the sole relevant cumulative sum is zeta_0=-epsilon.
Thus (1) holds.

For a complete independent check of input PSD, expand (13):

 Delta M=epsilon[nQ_01+(n-1)Q_10-Q_0n+Q_1n]
   =-epsilon(n-1)(t-1)||d_0||^2
      -epsilon sum_(k=1)^(n-1)[1+t(n-1-k)]<d_0,d_k>.    (14)

This follows by collecting g_0^2, g_1^2 and g_0g_1 and then using
g_j-g_1=-sum_(k=1)^(j-1)d_k. All value coefficients in (14) are zero.
Write beta_k=1+t(n-1-k). Completing squares gives

 M=sum_(k=1)^(n-1) w_k ||d_k-epsilon beta_k d_0/(2w_k)||^2
       +[w_0-epsilon(n-1)(t-1)
                   -epsilon^2/4 sum_(k=1)^(n-1)beta_k^2/w_k]||d_0||^2.
                                                                  (15)

Here w_0=2-t^2=2/9, w_k>=(k+1)w_0>0, beta_k<tn, and
sum_(k=1)^(n-1)beta_k^2/w_k<t^2 n^3/w_0. Consequently the two deductions
from w_0 in the last coefficient of (15) are respectively less than
w_0/4 and w_0/(64n). Their sum is strictly less than w_0, so the last
coefficient is positive. This proves full input PSD (strict positivity
in the difference coordinates) for every n>=2.

The repair (2) removes (13), producing sum w_k||d_k||^2. By (14), M^0-M
has a nonzero d_0 d_1 coefficient but zero d_1^2 coefficient. Restricting
to (d_0,d_1) gives determinant -epsilon^2 beta_1^2/4<0. Thus the matrix
change is indefinite, even though both complete endpoint matrices are PSD.

There is no saturated cut in any nonempty constant-t block. For a cut at
step i, let A_cut=1+it, D_tail=1+(n-i-1)t and r=t-1=1/3. Since A_cut,D_tail>=1 and
A_cut+D_tail=2+(n-1)t, their product is minimized at an endpoint and obeys

 A_cut D_tail>=1+(n-1)t=(4n-1)/3,
 rC=(4n+3)/9,
 A_cut D_tail-rC>=(8n-6)/9>0.

Thus lengths n>=3 in this family are outside the recursive class requiring
an exactly saturated first cut and a <=2-step eventual continuation leaf.
The new support-based repair is not merely that saturated-cut argument.

## 7. Scope and remaining interface

Condition w_k>=0 is equivalent to

 h_k<=[1-p_k+sqrt(p_k^2+6p_k+1)]/2<2.

Thus every schedule admitted by this repair theorem has C<1+2n. This is
an unbounded-length re-selection class, not an improving primitive seed
family or an asymptotic separation from the exact objective profile.

The circulation equations (6)-(7) isolate why deleting negative chords
arbitrarily is invalid: both conservation and reciprocal-p drift must hold.
The argument succeeds here because the support forces (10) and the full
PSD then forces each coefficient of the independent repaired path squares.
Section 8 below allows arbitrary backward edges and also gives an explicit
weighted-cut criterion for full-support arrays. No result here is claimed
as a new fact until verifier acceptance; no verifier allocation was used.

## 8. General full-support cut identity and a stronger repair theorem

Return to a real array with FULL support, exact value cancellation, full
PSD, and nonnegative entries except possibly into the terminal. Define,
for each k<n, the following weighted actual forward and backward cut sums:

 F_k=sum_(i<=k<j)lambda_ij[p_j-p_(k+1)],
 B_k=sum_(j<=k<i)lambda_ij[p_k-p_j].                       (16)

The adjacent edge contributes zero to either sum. Every term in B_k is
nonnegative; F_k can be negative only through signed incoming-terminal
edges. There is no omitted interpolation coefficient in these definitions.

The exact FULL matrix identity on the cut direction is

 (z^(k))^T M z^(k)=w_k+[(h_k-1)F_k-B_k]/h_k.             (17)

To derive it, let O_k and I_k be the total forward and backward crossing
masses without weights. The value-flow cut says O_k-I_k=-2P_(k+1).
The weighted circulation cut says

 sum_(i<=k<j)lambda_ij p_j
                   =sum_(j<=k<i)lambda_ij p_j.

The left side is p_(k+1)O_k+F_k and the right side is p_k I_k-B_k.
Using p_(k+1)-p_k=h_k therefore gives

 O_k=[2p_k P_(k+1)-F_k-B_k]/h_k.

Formula (11) equals -P_(k+1)^2+O_k+F_k, which becomes (17) because
2p_k P_(k+1)/h_k-P_(k+1)^2=w_k. This proves (17) for the complete
multiplier array and full original matrix.

**Full-support repair criterion.** If at every k with h_k>1 the input
array satisfies the explicit inequalities

                       (h_k-1)F_k<=B_k,                 (18)

then the ordinary array (2) and full PSD remainder (3) repair it.
Indeed (17) and full input PSD force w_k>=0 at such k; at h_k<=1 the
direct positive formula in Section 4 does so. Section 5 checks every
actual coefficient, value flow and formal PSD direction of the output.
Condition (18) is a checkable sufficient condition on a supplied full
certificate, not a proposed characterization of all credit certificates.

**Arbitrary backward edges.** In particular, the original repair remains
valid if ANY additional nonnegative backward edges i->j with i>j are
allowed. Assume every forward edge with j<n is adjacent, while arbitrary
signed incoming-terminal chords obey (1). Then

 F_k=R_(k+1) zeta_k, B_k>=0.

At a long nonfinal step (1) gives F_k<=0; at the final step F_(n-1)=0.
Thus (18) holds. Extra terminal-to-prefix edges and long backward prefix
edges are all covered, with no assumption that their coefficients vanish.
The signed constant-4/3 family in Section 6 supplies nonordinary inputs at
arbitrarily large lengths in this class, outside the saturated-cut class.

**Quantitative constraint on genuinely long steps.** Conversely, if
w_k<0, then (17) forces

                    (h_k-1)F_k-B_k>=-h_k w_k>0.          (19)

Such a step necessarily has h_k>1. Hence some positive forward multiplier
crosses the cut and lands strictly beyond k+1; adjacent-only forward mass
cannot supply (19). If the input is an actual E_theta certificate with
nonnegative multipliers Lambda, so that

 lambda_(i,n)=Lambda_(i,n)-theta h_i,

and other lambda entries equal their actual Lambda entries, define
F_k^actual by (16) with Lambda. Then the exact conversion is

             F_k=F_k^actual-theta P_(k+1)R_(k+1),

and (19) becomes

 (h_k-1)F_k^actual-B_k
      >=theta(h_k-1)P_(k+1)R_(k+1)-h_k w_k.              (20)

Thus terminal credit does not eliminate the positive forward-cut weight
obligation for these long steps. It increases its required actual weight
by the displayed amount. Equation (20) is a necessary coefficient bound,
not a bound on what those weights can achieve and not a universal repair.
No conclusion about asymptotic objective minimax follows from it alone.

glossary.P_i: Sum of physical steps strictly before query i.
glossary.R_i: Sum of physical steps from i onward; R_n=0.
glossary.C: 1+sum h_i, the physical capacity in this finding.
glossary.L: Row Laplacian diag(lambda e)-lambda of a real signed multiplier array.
glossary.D_quad: Diagonal matrix in equation(4), defining the complete value-canceling gradient remainder.
glossary.mu_ij: Destination-weighted signed interpolation multiplier lambda_ij p_j.
glossary.zeta_k: Cumulative signed nonadjacent incoming-terminal chord sum through index k.
glossary.w_i: Coefficient of the i-th independent gradient-difference square in the repaired certificate, equation(3).
glossary.F_k: Weighted signed forward cut sum in equation(16), not an objective function.
glossary.B_k: Weighted backward cut sum in equation(16), not the benchmark sequence B_n; the evidence defines both scope and index.
glossary.Lambda: Actual nonnegative E_theta interpolation multipliers; lambda subtracts theta h_i from incoming-terminal entries.
glossary.beta_k: 1+t(n-1-k), the cross-term coefficient in the explicit constant-step input family.

evidence:
# Growing near-unit modes cannot be repaired to benchmark strength by slow modes

Status: complete UNVERIFIED candidate. No new verifier, solver, numerical
probe or round allocation. Accepted inputs:1252b8823bb5a290 (full prefix
interpolation and free completion), dfde2fa326c908bf (algebraic cycle
identity), and b98bb807d514e80d (exact benchmark recurrences). All other
steps needed here are proved in this document.

## 1. A whole joint spectral class on the actual schedule

Fix m>=4096, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), and n=2^m-1.
Keep c,a fixed within this horizon. Remove the original final d_0 step
to form the queried prefix H_m^-, whose length is q=n-1. Let S=sum H_m^-
and let P_i be its chronological polynomials, 0<=i<=q. In particular
the last two executed steps of this retained prefix are d_0,d_1, where
d_1=2-1/m. Its original terminal displacement is x_q-d_0 g_q.

Let 0<R<=1/8 be fixed. Allow ANY finite probability mixture supported on
the union of these two sets:

    Slow_m(R)={z in C: |z|<=R/S},

    Fast_m={1-u/m +/- i sqrt(u-theta)/sqrt(m):
                           5<=u<=6, 1/2<=theta<=1}.       (1)

The words slow and fast refer only to these displayed sets. No component
is presumed legal. For weights w_z>=0 summing to1, use actual real vectors

    x_i=(sqrt(w_z) Re P_i(z), sqrt(w_z) Im P_i(z))_z,
    g_i=(sqrt(w_z) Re[zP_i(z)],sqrt(w_z) Im[zP_i(z)])_z.   (2)

Include the optimum(0,0,0), and allow ANY JOINT values f_i satisfying
ALL ordered interpolation constraints for these same vectors. Let F be
ANY legal convex1-smooth interpolant, including the maximal completion.
Then uniformly for every b in[0,2],

    2F(x_q-b g_q)
       <=exp(2R)[2R/S+(5/4)m R^3/S^3].                 (3)

For R=1/8 this gives a whole-class constant gap from the exact benchmark:

    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) 2F(x_q-b g_q)
                    <=exp(-3/4)<1/2.                  (4)

The supremum over mixtures, dimension, values and b in[0,2] may be taken
inside this limsup. This includes the original final step d_0. It does
not bound W_n for arbitrary gradients or arbitrary normal spectra.

Section5 gives a definite finite mixture from this class, with POSITIVE
weights on individually illegal exponentially growing fast modes, checks
every ordered pair including the optimum, and constructs one fixed F with

    2F(x_q-b g_q)>=3/(64S) for EVERY real b.             (5)

Thus this is also an explicit fixed-prefix, all-final-step witness of
the benchmark's order, with its non-sharp constant loss quantified.

## 2. One triangle made of the last three actual queries

For a scalar parameter z=alpha+i beta set sigma=|z|^2 and
kappa=alpha-sigma. Starting locally at1, the last two steps have positions

    v_0=1, v_1=1-d_0 z, v_2=(1-d_0 z)(1-d_1 z).

The forward triangle0->1->2->0 has signed doubled area

    Im(conj(v_0)v_1+conj(v_1)v_2+conj(v_2)v_0)
                          =-d_0^2 d_1 sigma beta.      (6)

To check it, the first two path-edge areas are -d_0 beta and
-d_1 beta|1-d_0 z|^2, while the return edge contributes
beta(d_0+d_1-2d_0d_1 alpha). Their sum is(6).
The triangle's squared-chord energy is sigma E(z), where

    E(z)=d_0^2+d_1^2|1-d_0 z|^2
                       +|d_0+d_1-d_0d_1 z|^2.         (7)

Hence the REVERSE triangle, by the exact cycle identity in accepted
dfde2fa326c908bf, has weight

    K(z)=sigma[d_0^2 d_1 beta^2-(kappa/2)E(z)].        (8)

Put A(z)=P_(q-2)(z). The same three ACTUAL indices q-2,q-1,q, with
the same reverse orientation, give the JOINT necessary condition

    sum_z w_z |A(z)|^2 K(z)<=0.                        (9)

There is no optimum vertex in this cycle. Nevertheless the optimum
remains imposed elsewhere on the joint prefix. All function values
cancel in(9); no separate component values are chosen in using it.

## 3. Positive fast defects and cubic slow credit

For the parameters in(1), elementary bounds valid for m>=4096 are

    11/8<=d_0<=3/2, 31/16<=d_1<=2,
    1-6/m<=alpha<=1, |beta|<=1/20,
    sigma>=49/50, 0<kappa<=1/m, beta^2>=4/m.           (10)

For kappa, expand it exactly as theta/m-u^2/m^2. For sigma use
sigma>=alpha^2>49/50. The step bounds follow directly from a,c, and
beta^2<=(11/2)/4096<1/400.

Since d_0 alpha>1 and d_1 alpha>1, (10) gives

    |1-d_0z|<=1/2+(3/2)(1/20)<3/5,
    |1-d_1z|<=1+2/20=11/10.

Also 0<d_0+d_1-d_0d_1<=3/4 on the step rectangle in(10), and

    |d_0+d_1-d_0d_1z|
       <=3/4+3(6/m+|beta|)<1.

Consequently E(z)<9/4+4(3/5)^2+1<5. Since
d_0^2d_1>7/2, equations(8),(10) imply

    K(z)>=(49/50)(14-5/2)/m>10/m,
    |(1-d_0 z)(1-d_1 z)|^2<1/2.                       (11)

Thus each fast mode contributes at least(20/m)|P_q(z)|^2 to the
common cycle(9), regardless of its own illegal prefix.

For a slow mode, all prefix polynomials have modulus at most exp(R):
use |1-hz|<=1+h|z| and product(1+h|z|)<=exp(|z|S). In particular
|A(z)|^2<=exp(2R). Since |z|<=1/8, (7) gives

    E(z)<=9/4+4(19/16)^2+(31/8)^2<25.

The negative part of K(z) is at most

    (sigma/2) max(kappa,0) E(z)<= (25/2)|z|^3.

Here max(kappa,0)<=max(alpha,0)<=|z|; no sign assumption on a slow
mode's real part is needed. Its total possible negative contribution
to(9), after summing all slow probabilities, is therefore at most

    (25/2)exp(2R) R^3/S^3.                             (12)

Combining(9),(11),(12) yields the genuinely JOINT endpoint bound

    sum_(fast z) w_z |P_q(z)|^2
                         <=(5/8)m exp(2R)R^3/S^3.    (13)

This is the cubic credit constraint missed by an optimum cycle alone.
It allows positive weights on illegal fast components, but those weights
times their terminal amplification are uniformly controlled.

For any legal interpolant, optimum interpolation at q and final-step
smoothness give, for b in[0,2],

    2F(x_q-b g_q)
       <=sum_z w_z[2alpha-(1+b(2-b))sigma]|P_q(z)|^2.

On fast modes alpha<=1, so(13) bounds their contribution by twice its
right side. On slow modes alpha<=|z|<=R/S and |P_q|<=exp(R), so their
contribution is at most2R exp(2R)/S. This proves(3), with every queried
anchor and the actual last displacement retained.

## 4. Benchmark estimate, and why the fast modes are relevant

The exact recursions from acceptedb98bb807d514e80d have mass joins

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
    G(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

Write rho=log_2 lambda and V(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. For t=exp(s),

    d^2/ds^2 log V(exp(s))
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)[(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/V(t)^2>0.

Thus V(t)V(1/t)>=V(1)^2=2. Substituting t=(A/B)^(1/rho) shows
Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho. Continuity covers zeros.
Induction gives C_k=S_circle(k)+1<=(k+1)^rho. Since G(A,B)<=4A+B,
induction and superadditivity of t^rho give B_k<=1+4k^rho.

The exact retained sum is

    S=2^m-1+a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2)-d_0.

Here a/(c-2)->1, c^m/lambda^m->e and (2/lambda)^m->0; hence
S/lambda^m->e. In particular m/S^2->0. Multiply(3) by B_n to obtain
limsup<=8R exp(2R-1), which gives(4) at R=1/8.
The strict inequality exp(-3/4)<1/2 follows from
exp(3/4)>1+3/4+9/32+27/384>2.

Every fast parameter in(1) has exponentially growing ACTUAL queried
polynomial for sufficiently large m, uniformly in its displayed compact
parameter set. Here is the calculation, to avoid appealing to an
unverified earlier counterexample. Put

    L_m(z)=sum_(j>=0)2^(-j-1) log|1-d_j z|,
    A_j=1+1/(a c^j),
    D_m=1+1/[a(2-c^(-1))],
    J_m=1+2/[a(2-c^(-1))]+1/[a^2(2-c^(-2))].

All A_j<=4 for sufficiently large m. For z=1+v in(1), expand
log(1+A_jv)=A_jv-A_j^2v^2/2+O(|v|^3), with remainder uniformly
bounded by2|A_jv|^3 when |A_jv|<=1/2. The weights sum to1, so

    mL_m(z)=-1-uD_m+(u-theta)J_m/2+O(m^(-1/2)).

The limits are D=1+D1, J=1+2D1+D2 with
D1=lambda^2/(2lambda-1), D2=lambda^4/(2lambda^2-1). One has
D1<8/5 and D2>31/10, by 12/5<lambda<5/2 and the increasing functions
t^2/(2t-1), t^4/(2t^2-1) on t>1 (at12/5 the latter is20736/6575>31/10).
The limiting coefficient increases with u because J/2-D=(D2-1)/2>0,
and decreases with theta. Its minimum is therefore

    -1-5D+2J=-4-D1+2D2>3/5.

Thus L_m(z)>=1/(2m) uniformly for large m. The tail j>=m omitted from
the actual finite product, multiplied by2^m, is O(m), since its terms
are bounded above by C+j log c. The removed last factor |1-d_0z| stays
bounded above and away from0. Hence uniformly on Fast_m,

    log|P_q(z)|>=2^m/(3m)

for all sufficiently large m. This is a polynomial-growth statement;
legality is supplied only for joint constructions such as the next one.

## 5. Definite positive weights, every ordered constraint, and one global F

Use R=1/8. Choose exactly two fast modes

    z_fast,1=1-5/m+2i/sqrt(m),
    z_fast,2=1-6/m+i sqrt(5)/sqrt(m).

For every j=0,...,m-1 choose two slow modes

    r_j=d_0/(8S d_j),
    z_(j,ell)=r_j[t_ell+i sqrt(1-t_ell^2)],
    t_1=3/4, t_2=1/2.                                  (14)

evidence:
# General removal of terminal credit with an explicit physical contraction

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. This result changes
the physical steps and does not prove same-schedule credit re-selection.
It uses all actual interpolation coefficients and a full PSD identity.
No solver or verifier call, and no external theorem used as a premise.

## 1. Statement, including zero steps

Fix n>=0 and a nonnegative physical schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)). Write
s=sum h_i, C=1+s. On independent formal gradients g_0,...,g_n and values
f_0,...,f_n, substitute x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and put

 Q_ij^h=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                            -s(s+1)||g_n||^2,
 J_h=sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n)^h,
 E_theta=V_h-theta J_h.

Suppose 0<=theta<2 and actual nonnegative multipliers Lambda_ij for all
distinct finite pairs give an exact certificate

              E_theta+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij^h=M,       (1)

where all value coefficients vanish and M is PSD on the FULL independent
gradient space. This includes the project range 0<=theta<1.

Define positive parameters and the contracted schedule by

 a=1-theta/2,
 kappa=theta C/(2-theta),
 t=1/(1+kappa)=(2-theta)/(2+theta s),
 c=2/(2+theta s),
 h'_i=t h_i,     Lambda'_ij=c Lambda_ij.                  (2)

Then Lambda' is an ordinary nonnegative certificate for V_(h') with the
complete PSD remainder

 V_(h')+sum Lambda'_ij Q_ij^(h')
       =(t^2/a)[M+kappa(S_Lambda+a Var_h)],               (3)

where

 S_Lambda=(1/2)sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij||g_i-g_j||^2,
 Var_h=sum_(i<n)h_i||g_i||^2+||g_n||^2
                     -(1/C)||sum_(i<n)h_i g_i+g_n||^2.   (4)

Both added forms are PSD, with no missing gradient directions. Every
actual output multiplier is nonnegative because c>0. Zero steps remain
zero, and the proof works on the original formal space without identifying
duplicate gradients or invoking compression. Empty and all-zero schedules
are included.

The actual physical capacity after this same-length conversion is exactly

             C'=1+sum h'_i=2C/[2+theta(C-1)].             (5)

No prefix or bridge is appended. The loss in (5) must be charged before
claiming an improving ordinary seed.

## 2. Two identities before changing the schedule

Put H_g=sum_(i<n)h_i g_i and define the rank-at-most-two quadratic

                    D_h=||H_g+g_n||^2-C^2||g_n||^2.

Direct expansion gives

                    V_h-2J_h=D_h,                       (6)
                    E_theta=a V_h+(1-a)D_h.

Here is an explicit verification of (6). The value terms cancel. Write
x_n-x_i=-sum_(j=i)^(n-1)h_j g_j in J_h. Expanding 2J_h and canceling the
diagonal norm terms in V_h leaves

 2sum_(i<=j<n)h_i h_j<g_i,g_j>-sum_(i<n)h_i^2||g_i||^2
     +2<H_g,g_n>-[s(s+1)+s]||g_n||^2.

The first two terms equal ||H_g||^2, and s(s+1)+s=C^2-1. The displayed
expression is therefore D_h, proving (6).

Also define the formal scalar value combination

                    F_h=sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n).

The value part of E_theta is 2a F_h. Exact cancellation in (1) forces

              sum Lambda_ij(f_i-f_j)=-2a F_h.            (7)

This checks the complete finite-node flow, not only its total sum.

## 3. Complete coefficient identity under contraction

All query differences scale by t, so, as an identity in independent
values and gradients,

 Q_ij^(h')=t Q_ij^h
                +(1-t)[f_i-f_j+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].         (8)

Let K_h=sum_(i<n)h_i||g_i||^2-s||g_n||^2. The value and gradient terms of
V_(h') give exactly

                 V_(h')=t^2 V_h+t(1-t)(2F_h+K_h).       (9)

Using Lambda'=c Lambda, equations (1), (6), (7), and (8) now yield

 V_(h')+sum Lambda'_ij Q_ij^(h')
  =V_(h')+ct[M-aV_h-(1-a)D_h]
                         +c(1-t)[-2aF_h+S_Lambda].      (10)

The parameter identities t=ac, ct=t^2/a, 1-t=kappa t and
1-a=a kappa/C are exact consequences of (2). Substitute (9) into (10):
the V_h coefficients cancel since cta=t^2, and the F_h coefficients cancel
since ca=t. The remaining expression is

 ct M+t(1-t)K_h-ct(1-a)D_h+c(1-t)S_Lambda
   =ct[M+kappa S_Lambda+a kappa(K_h-D_h/C)].              (11)

Finally K_h-D_h/C is precisely Var_h, because C-s=1. Equations (11) and
ct=t^2/a prove the entire formal identity (3).

## 4. Positivity on the full formal space

S_Lambda is a nonnegative sum of squared gradient differences. For Var_h,
assign weights w_i=h_i for i<n and w_n=1, whose sum is C>0. Expanding
the squared differences gives

 Var_h=(1/C)sum_(0<=i<j<=n)w_i w_j||g_i-g_j||^2>=0.     (12)

This remains valid when any h_i vanishes. Since a,t>0 and kappa>=0, (3)
and the assumed full PSD of M prove full PSD of the repaired matrix.
All output interpolation coefficients are positive scalar multiples of
actual nonnegative coefficients, so none of their signs is omitted.
The cancellation of the independent F_h terms in Section 3 explicitly
checks the new value flow. This establishes the statement in Section 1.

For an all-zero schedule, t=a, c=1, Var_h=0, and the input value flow is
zero. Its remainder is M=S_Lambda, so (3) reduces to the same matrix M.
For n=0 every sum of distinct finite pairs is empty and M=0. Thus these
boundary cases satisfy the formula directly.

## 5. Explicit target-relevance cost

Summing the contracted physical steps gives (5). Let K>1 be any desired
capacity threshold for an ordinary seed of this same length. Algebra shows

 C'>K
   iff (2-theta K)C>K(2-theta).                         (13)

Consequently a necessary condition is theta<2/K. When theta<2/K,
condition (13) is equivalent to the explicit input requirement

                    C>K(2-theta)/(2-theta K).            (14)

If theta>=2/K and theta<2, no finite C>=1 can satisfy C'>K: the left side
of (13) is nonpositive and its right side is strictly positive. In
particular, for the previously proposed useful primitive-seed threshold
K=(n+1)^rho, rho=log_2(1+sqrt2), this same-length conversion requires
theta<2/(n+1)^rho and then (14). This is only an exact cost comparison;
the conditional asymptotic amplification argument is not invoked here as
a verified premise, and no seed meeting the threshold has been found.

When theta>0 is fixed and C tends to infinity, C' tends to2/theta. Thus
fixed positive credit cannot yield unbounded ordinary capacity by THIS
conversion. An improving sequence by this mechanism must control theta
at the corresponding inverse-capacity scale. Other conversions with
prefixes or bridges may behave differently and are not excluded.

## 6. A useful corollary about uniform contraction

Given an ordinary nonnegative certificate for h, adding theta h_i to
every incoming-terminal multiplier makes (1) hold with the SAME M for
any 0<=theta<2: those additions cancel -theta J_h. For any prescribed
0<t<=1, choose

                    theta=2(1-t)/(1+t s).

It lies in [0,2), and (2) gives exactly that t. Therefore every uniform
contraction t h of a certified ordinary schedule has the explicit ordinary
certificate (3). This statement concerns certificates on the full formal
space, including zero steps, and does not assert that enlarging steps is
safe or that arbitrary independent contractions preserve the property.

## Remaining issue

This general transformation removes credit by paying an exact physical
sum loss. It neither fixes h nor proves that E_theta and V_h have the same
certificate cone. The same-schedule problem remains open outside the
saturated-cut and weighted-cut repair classes. Any target-level use must
produce a concrete E_theta family surviving (5), an exact ordinary
certificate as above, and the full infinite-horizon benchmark comparison.

Also checked all original independent coefficients with an interior zero-step h=(1,0),theta=3/5 and an all-zero h=(0,0),theta=3/2. All three fixed rational audits passed; no SDP/PEP or verifier call. The tiny exact audit is local_memory/check_credit_contraction.py, results credit_contraction_exact_audit.json.

glossary.S_Lambda: Half the Lambda-weighted sum of squared gradient differences, equation(4).
glossary.Var_h: Weighted variance of all original independent gradients with weights(h_0,...,h_(n-1),1).
glossary.D_h: ||sum h_i g_i+g_n||²-C²||g_n||², equal identically to V_h-2J_h.

It lies in [0,2), and (2) gives exactly that t. Therefore every uniform
contraction t h of a certified ordinary schedule has the explicit ordinary
certificate (3). This statement concerns certificates on the full formal
space, including zero steps, and does not assert that enlarging steps is
safe or that arbitrary independent contractions preserve the property.

## 7. The cost is forced for every proportional-multiplier conversion

Assume s>0. Suppose an ordinary certificate for SOME nonnegative schedule
q=(q_0,...,q_(n-1)) uses multipliers c_0 Lambda with a single c_0>0 and
has a PSD remainder on the full independent-gradient space. Then q and
c_0 must be EXACTLY the h' and c in (2). Thus (5) is not merely one
conservative choice within this proportional-multiplier class.

Indeed (7) and ordinary value cancellation require, separately at every
nonterminal index, q_i=c_0 a h_i. Hence q=t_0 h with t_0=c_0 a>0.
The expansion (10)-(11), before imposing the special value of t, gives
the complete output matrix

 M_out=c_0 t_0 M+t_0(1-t_0)K_h
       -c_0 t_0(1-a)D_h+c_0(1-t_0)S_Lambda.              (15)

Let e be the all-one formal gradient column and v=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),-s)^T.
The input M has M e=0: evaluate its value-canceling identity on a legal
constant-gradient affine Huber segment to get e^T M e=0, then use full
PSD. Also S_Lambda e=0, K_h e=v and D_h e=Cv, where quadratic forms
are identified with their symmetric matrices. Consequently

 M_out e=t_0[(1-t_0)-c_0(1-a)C]v.                       (16)

All four terms of (15) have zero quadratic value on e, so e^T M_out e=0.
The assumed full output PSD forces M_out e=0. Since s>0, v is nonzero;
since t_0>0, equation (16), together with c_0=t_0/a, uniquely forces

          1-t_0=t_0(1-a)C/a,
          t_0=a/[a+(1-a)C]=(2-theta)/(2+theta s).

It then forces c_0=t_0/a=c. This proves the uniqueness claim, including
schedules with some zero steps. In particular, when theta>0 and s>0,
simply normalizing or globally rescaling the ACTUAL E_theta multipliers
cannot repair the original unchanged physical schedule. Any such repair
must also change the relative multiplier array or use a different method.
The all-zero case is excluded from this uniqueness assertion because
v=0, and its physical schedule remains zero under every scaling.

## Remaining issue

This general transformation removes credit by paying an exact physical
sum loss. It neither fixes h nor proves that E_theta and V_h have the same
certificate cone. The same-schedule problem remains open outside the
saturated-cut and weighted-cut repair classes. Any target-level use must
produce a concrete E_theta family surviving (5), an exact ordinary
certificate as above, and the full infinite-horizon benchmark comparison.
