evidence:
# General removal of terminal credit with an explicit physical contraction

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. This result changes
the physical steps and does not prove same-schedule credit re-selection.
It uses all actual interpolation coefficients and a full PSD identity.
No solver or verifier call, and no external theorem used as a premise.

## 1. Statement, including zero steps

Fix n>=0 and a nonnegative physical schedule h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)). Write
s=sum h_i, C=1+s. On independent formal gradients g_0,...,g_n and values
f_0,...,f_n, substitute x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and put

 Q_ij^h=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                            -s(s+1)||g_n||^2,
 J_h=sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n)^h,
 E_theta=V_h-theta J_h.

Suppose 0<=theta<2 and actual nonnegative multipliers Lambda_ij for all
distinct finite pairs give an exact certificate

              E_theta+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij^h=M,       (1)

where all value coefficients vanish and M is PSD on the FULL independent
gradient space. This includes the project range 0<=theta<1.

Define positive parameters and the contracted schedule by

 a=1-theta/2,
 kappa=theta C/(2-theta),
 t=1/(1+kappa)=(2-theta)/(2+theta s),
 c=2/(2+theta s),
 h'_i=t h_i,     Lambda'_ij=c Lambda_ij.                  (2)

Then Lambda' is an ordinary nonnegative certificate for V_(h') with the
complete PSD remainder

 V_(h')+sum Lambda'_ij Q_ij^(h')
       =(t^2/a)[M+kappa(S_Lambda+a Var_h)],               (3)

where

 S_Lambda=(1/2)sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij||g_i-g_j||^2,
 Var_h=sum_(i<n)h_i||g_i||^2+||g_n||^2
                     -(1/C)||sum_(i<n)h_i g_i+g_n||^2.   (4)

Both added forms are PSD, with no missing gradient directions. Every
actual output multiplier is nonnegative because c>0. Zero steps remain
zero, and the proof works on the original formal space without identifying
duplicate gradients or invoking compression. Empty and all-zero schedules
are included.

The actual physical capacity after this same-length conversion is exactly

             C'=1+sum h'_i=2C/[2+theta(C-1)].             (5)

No prefix or bridge is appended. The loss in (5) must be charged before
claiming an improving ordinary seed.

## 2. Two identities before changing the schedule

Put H_g=sum_(i<n)h_i g_i and define the rank-at-most-two quadratic

                    D_h=||H_g+g_n||^2-C^2||g_n||^2.

Direct expansion gives

                    V_h-2J_h=D_h,                       (6)
                    E_theta=a V_h+(1-a)D_h.

Here is an explicit verification of (6). The value terms cancel. Write
x_n-x_i=-sum_(j=i)^(n-1)h_j g_j in J_h. Expanding 2J_h and canceling the
diagonal norm terms in V_h leaves

 2sum_(i<=j<n)h_i h_j<g_i,g_j>-sum_(i<n)h_i^2||g_i||^2
     +2<H_g,g_n>-[s(s+1)+s]||g_n||^2.

The first two terms equal ||H_g||^2, and s(s+1)+s=C^2-1. The displayed
expression is therefore D_h, proving (6).

Also define the formal scalar value combination

                    F_h=sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n).

The value part of E_theta is 2a F_h. Exact cancellation in (1) forces

              sum Lambda_ij(f_i-f_j)=-2a F_h.            (7)

This checks the complete finite-node flow, not only its total sum.

## 3. Complete coefficient identity under contraction

All query differences scale by t, so, as an identity in independent
values and gradients,

 Q_ij^(h')=t Q_ij^h
                +(1-t)[f_i-f_j+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].         (8)

Let K_h=sum_(i<n)h_i||g_i||^2-s||g_n||^2. The value and gradient terms of
V_(h') give exactly

                 V_(h')=t^2 V_h+t(1-t)(2F_h+K_h).       (9)

Using Lambda'=c Lambda, equations (1), (6), (7), and (8) now yield

 V_(h')+sum Lambda'_ij Q_ij^(h')
  =V_(h')+ct[M-aV_h-(1-a)D_h]
                         +c(1-t)[-2aF_h+S_Lambda].      (10)

The parameter identities t=ac, ct=t^2/a, 1-t=kappa t and
1-a=a kappa/C are exact consequences of (2). Substitute (9) into (10):
the V_h coefficients cancel since cta=t^2, and the F_h coefficients cancel
since ca=t. The remaining expression is

 ct M+t(1-t)K_h-ct(1-a)D_h+c(1-t)S_Lambda
   =ct[M+kappa S_Lambda+a kappa(K_h-D_h/C)].              (11)

Finally K_h-D_h/C is precisely Var_h, because C-s=1. Equations (11) and
ct=t^2/a prove the entire formal identity (3).

## 4. Positivity on the full formal space

S_Lambda is a nonnegative sum of squared gradient differences. For Var_h,
assign weights w_i=h_i for i<n and w_n=1, whose sum is C>0. Expanding
the squared differences gives

 Var_h=(1/C)sum_(0<=i<j<=n)w_i w_j||g_i-g_j||^2>=0.     (12)

This remains valid when any h_i vanishes. Since a,t>0 and kappa>=0, (3)
and the assumed full PSD of M prove full PSD of the repaired matrix.
All output interpolation coefficients are positive scalar multiples of
actual nonnegative coefficients, so none of their signs is omitted.
The cancellation of the independent F_h terms in Section 3 explicitly
checks the new value flow. This establishes the statement in Section 1.

For an all-zero schedule, t=a, c=1, Var_h=0, and the input value flow is
zero. Its remainder is M=S_Lambda, so (3) reduces to the same matrix M.
For n=0 every sum of distinct finite pairs is empty and M=0. Thus these
boundary cases satisfy the formula directly.

## 5. Explicit target-relevance cost

Summing the contracted physical steps gives (5). Let K>1 be any desired
capacity threshold for an ordinary seed of this same length. Algebra shows

 C'>K
   iff (2-theta K)C>K(2-theta).                         (13)

Consequently a necessary condition is theta<2/K. When theta<2/K,
condition (13) is equivalent to the explicit input requirement

                    C>K(2-theta)/(2-theta K).            (14)

If theta>=2/K and theta<2, no finite C>=1 can satisfy C'>K: the left side
of (13) is nonpositive and its right side is strictly positive. In
particular, for the previously proposed useful primitive-seed threshold
K=(n+1)^rho, rho=log_2(1+sqrt2), this same-length conversion requires
theta<2/(n+1)^rho and then (14). This is only an exact cost comparison;
the conditional asymptotic amplification argument is not invoked here as
a verified premise, and no seed meeting the threshold has been found.

When theta>0 is fixed and C tends to infinity, C' tends to2/theta. Thus
fixed positive credit cannot yield unbounded ordinary capacity by THIS
conversion. An improving sequence by this mechanism must control theta
at the corresponding inverse-capacity scale. Other conversions with
prefixes or bridges may behave differently and are not excluded.

## 6. A useful corollary about uniform contraction

Given an ordinary nonnegative certificate for h, adding theta h_i to
every incoming-terminal multiplier makes (1) hold with the SAME M for
any 0<=theta<2: those additions cancel -theta J_h. For any prescribed
0<t<=1, choose

                    theta=2(1-t)/(1+t s).

It lies in [0,2), and (2) gives exactly that t. Therefore every uniform
contraction t h of a certified ordinary schedule has the explicit ordinary
certificate (3). This statement concerns certificates on the full formal
space, including zero steps, and does not assert that enlarging steps is
safe or that arbitrary independent contractions preserve the property.

## 7. The cost is forced for every proportional-multiplier conversion

Assume s>0. Suppose an ordinary certificate for SOME nonnegative schedule
q=(q_0,...,q_(n-1)) uses multipliers c_0 Lambda with a single c_0>0 and
has a PSD remainder on the full independent-gradient space. Then q and
c_0 must be EXACTLY the h' and c in (2). Thus (5) is not merely one
conservative choice within this proportional-multiplier class.

Indeed (7) and ordinary value cancellation require, separately at every
nonterminal index, q_i=c_0 a h_i. Hence q=t_0 h with t_0=c_0 a>0.
The expansion (10)-(11), before imposing the special value of t, gives
the complete output matrix

 M_out=c_0 t_0 M+t_0(1-t_0)K_h
       -c_0 t_0(1-a)D_h+c_0(1-t_0)S_Lambda.              (15)

Let e be the all-one formal gradient column and v=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),-s)^T.
The input M has M e=0: evaluate its value-canceling identity on a legal
constant-gradient affine Huber segment to get e^T M e=0, then use full
PSD. Also S_Lambda e=0, K_h e=v and D_h e=Cv, where quadratic forms
are identified with their symmetric matrices. Consequently

 M_out e=t_0[(1-t_0)-c_0(1-a)C]v.                       (16)

All four terms of (15) have zero quadratic value on e, so e^T M_out e=0.
The assumed full output PSD forces M_out e=0. Since s>0, v is nonzero;
since t_0>0, equation (16), together with c_0=t_0/a, uniquely forces

          1-t_0=t_0(1-a)C/a,
          t_0=a/[a+(1-a)C]=(2-theta)/(2+theta s).

It then forces c_0=t_0/a=c. This proves the uniqueness claim, including
schedules with some zero steps. In particular, when theta>0 and s>0,
simply normalizing or globally rescaling the ACTUAL E_theta multipliers
cannot repair the original unchanged physical schedule. Any such repair
must also change the relative multiplier array or use a different method.
The all-zero case is excluded from this uniqueness assertion because
v=0, and its physical schedule remains zero under every scaling.

## 8. Incoming mass floor and failure of monotone coefficient repair

Assume s>0 and retain the ACTUAL nonnegative array Lambda in (1). Let
P_i=sum_(j<i)h_j, R_i=s-P_i. The full affine kernel forces

               sum_(j<n)Lambda_(n,j) R_j=2sC.            (17)

To check this directly, identify each gradient quadratic with its symmetric
matrix and multiply by the all-one vector e. Each squared-difference form
in a Q kills e. Positions have no g_n coefficient. Thus only a Q with source
n contributes to row n of the position part, and its contribution to the
row sum is R_j/2. The terminal row of the V_h gradient diagonal contributes
-sC, while the terminal row sum of J_h is0. Since M e=0, this gives (17).

Write Out_n=sum_(j<n)Lambda_(n,j) and In_n=sum_(i<n)Lambda_(i,n).
Because 0<=R_j<=s and every actual coefficient is nonnegative, (17) yields
Out_n>=2C. The terminal value-flow equation is

                Out_n-In_n=(2-theta)s.

It follows that EVERY full E_theta certificate for s>0 satisfies

                    In_n>=2+theta s.                    (18)

In particular every ordinary intrinsic certificate requires incoming-terminal
mass at least2. A theorem eliminating all incoming terminal inequalities
for a LAST-OBJECTIVE certificate cannot be applied unchanged to this intrinsic
energy certificate. Equation (18) is about actual formal certificates; it
does not say which incoming coefficients of a signed V array are negative.

There is also an obstruction to a simple variable-matrix repair: when
theta>0, NO ordinary certificate mu for the SAME physical h can satisfy
mu_ij>=Lambda_ij for every ordered pair. This allows the entire PSD matrix
to change; it rules out repair by only adding nonnegative coefficients.

For strictly positive h, (17) applies equally to mu and Lambda, with R_j>0
for every j<n. Entrywise domination therefore forces mu_(n,j)=Lambda_(n,j)
for every j<n. But ordinary terminal flow requires its total incoming mass
to be smaller by exactly theta s, contradicting entrywise domination.

Here is the full zero-step argument. Let T={i:P_i=s}, the final group of
indices after the last positive step, including n, and I its complement.
For any i in T other than n, h_i=0. Its row in the V_h diagonal vanishes;
its row sum in J_h is zero; and every position coefficient of g_i vanishes
because h_i=0. The affine-kernel equation therefore gives

                sum_j Lambda_ij(s-P_j)=0.

All summands are nonnegative, so Lambda_ij=0 whenever i is in T other than
n and j is in I. The same holds for any ordinary mu. Equation (17) and
entrywise domination force mu_(n,j)=Lambda_(n,j) for j in I, because their
weights R_j are positive. Thus the total flow OUT OF the set T is unchanged,
while its incoming flow under mu cannot be smaller. Its net outgoing flow
under mu is therefore at most its net outgoing flow under Lambda. Summing
the value-flow equations over T instead makes these two net flows respectively
2s and (2-theta)s. Since theta s>0, this is a contradiction. This handles
every possible leading, interior and trailing zero step on the full original
formal space.

This obstruction does not refute same-schedule repair: a successful repair
may subtract some old coefficients while adding others. The proportional
contraction (2), for example, has c<1 when theta s>0 and also changes the
physical steps. Neither construction violates the obstruction just proved.

## Remaining issue

This general transformation removes credit by paying an exact physical
sum loss. It neither fixes h nor proves that E_theta and V_h have the same
certificate cone. The same-schedule problem remains open outside the
saturated-cut and weighted-cut repair classes. Any target-level use must
produce a concrete E_theta family surviving (5), an exact ordinary
certificate as above, and the full infinite-horizon benchmark comparison.

Ordinary prefix capacity A and credited tail can also be joined at ANY r>=0 with r(A+D+r)<=AD, using an explicit credit budget and a nonnegative cross-block square. evidence:
# Full certificates for gradient-stable prepending and subcritical credit joins

Status: complete candidate identities, NOT verifier-accepted. No new SDP or
verifier call. These are actual coefficients on all independent gradients;
the result neither asserts general reversal nor an improving objective family.

## 1. Notation

Normalize smoothness to1. Let a and b be nonnegative physical step lists,
of capacities A=1+sum a_i and D=1+sum b_j. The actual joined schedule is

                       h=(a,1+r,b),   T=A+D+r.

Let L be the query just before its bridge, p=g_L, and z its final query,
q=g_z. Tail indices B run from the query just after the bridge through z.
Write H_b=sum_(j<z,j in B)b_j g_j and W_b=H_b+q. Thus the physical bridge
and tail relations are x_(L+1)=x_L-(1+r)p and x_z=x_(L+1)-H_b.

Every Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 uses these actual joined
positions. V_a and V_b are the respective intrinsic energies

 V_c=2sum c_i(f_i-f_end)+sum c_i(1-c_i)||g_i||^2
                                   -(sum c_i)(1+sum c_i)||g_end||^2,

and J_b=sum_(j<z,j in B)b_j Q_(j,z), E_theta,b=V_b-theta J_b.
The prefix endpoint L belongs to V_a; all tail gradients are independent
of the prefix gradients. Empty lists are allowed, with intrinsic energy0.

For concise interpolation sums put

 G_b=sum_(j<z,j in B)b_j Q_(j,L)+Q_(z,L),
 C_r=G_b+r Q_(L,z)+J_b.                                (1)

Assume the input certificates, when invoked, have exact value cancellation
and full PSD remainders:

 V_a+sum mu_ij Q_ij=M_a,      mu_ij>=0,
 E_theta,b+sum Lambda_ij Q_ij=M_b,      Lambda_ij>=0.     (2)

Their finite pairs are embedded in their original prefix and tail indices.

## 2. Direct identities valid without any certificate hypothesis

Expand (1) using the displayed GD relations. The value and gradient parts
of C_r are exactly

 C_r,f=2sum b_j f_j+(r-D)f_L+(2-D-r)f_z,
 C_r,g=sum b_j(1-b_j)||g_j||^2
               +[(D-r)/2-r^2]||p||^2+(D+r)||q||^2/2.     (3)

For the gradient calculation, sum the position terms and use
2sum_j b_j<g_j,sum_(i<j)b_i g_i>
    =||H_b||^2-sum_j b_j^2||g_j||^2.
The terms involving p,H_b,q cancel in (3); the remaining coefficients
are the displayed ones. Also direct expansion of V_b and J_b gives

                V_b-2J_b=||W_b||^2-D^2||q||^2.          (4)

The interpolation sum with coefficient D on Q_(L,z), regardless of the
physical bridge r, is C_D=G_b+D Q_(L,z)+J_b. Since

 Q_(L,z)=f_L-f_z-(r+1/2)||p||^2+||q||^2/2-<p,W_b>,

subtracting (D-r)Q_(L,z) from V_b-C_r in (3) gives

        V_b-C_D=Dr||p||^2-D^2||q||^2+(D-r)<p,W_b>.     (5)

These are formal identities in EVERY value and gradient, not just identities
on equality examples.

## 3. Gradient-norm stability from a credited tail

Suppose 0<=theta<1 and the tail certificate in (2) is supplied. Choose

              theta D/(2-theta)<=r<=D,
 eta=(D-r)/(2D), K=D(D+r)/2,
 gamma=r/D-(1-eta)theta>=0.                             (6)

Then the physical schedule (1+r,b) has the following complete nonnegative
certificate for ||p||^2-||q||^2>=0:

 K(||p||^2-||q||^2)
    +G_b+D Q_(L,z)+gamma J_b
    +(1-eta)sum Lambda_ij Q_ij
        =(1-eta)M_b+eta||W_b-Dp||^2.                    (7)

Every coefficient on the left is nonnegative, and the right is PSD on the
full independent p and tail gradient space. Thus one actual smooth convex
trajectory obeys ||g_z||<=||g_L||. No reset or change of its function occurs.

To prove (7), subtract eta times (4) from (5). Since
D-r=2D eta and K=(1-eta)D^2, completing the one square gives

 K(||p||^2-||q||^2)
   =(1-eta)V_b-[G_b+D Q_(L,z)+(r/D)J_b]
                                          +eta||W_b-Dp||^2.

Substitute V_b=E_theta,b+theta J_b and then (2). This is exactly (7).
The lower bound on r in (6) is equivalent to gamma>=0. This supplies all
signs, not only the PSD congruence. For theta=0, the entire interval0<=r<=D
is allowed. In particular a primitive tail of capacity D can be preceded
by any bridge in [1,D+1] without increasing the gradient norm from the
pre-bridge query to the final query.

## 4. Subcritical primitive join with an exact credit budget

Let r>=0 satisfy the physical subcritical condition

                         rT<=AD.                        (8)

It implies r<D. Define

 kappa=T^2/D^2,
 delta=(A+r)(AD-rT)/[D^2(D+r)]>=0,
 u=2T(A+r)/[D(D+r)],
 v=2A(A+r)/(D+r),
 j=kappa-1-delta
   =2(A+r)[(D+r)^2+Ar]/[D^2(D+r)]>0.                  (9)

The FULL identity is

 V_h=V_a+kappa V_b-u G_b-v Q_(L,z)-j J_b
                                      +delta||W_b-Dp||^2. (10)

Here is an independent derivation from the preceding formal expansions.
Let kappa_0=1+2(A+r)/(D-r) and
alpha=A^2-kappa_0 r^2=(A+r)(AD-rT)/(D-r). Value matching and (3) give

 V_h=V_a+kappa_0 V_b-(kappa_0-1)C_r
                                 +alpha(||p||^2-||q||^2). (11)

To check the remaining diagonal coefficients, kappa_0(D-r)=2A+D+r,
so the p-square discrepancy is A^2-kappa_0 r^2=alpha and the q-square
discrepancy is kappa_0 D^2-T^2=-alpha. All other coefficients already
match (3). Substitute the identity preceding (7) with theta=0 into (11).
The V_b coefficient becomes kappa_0+alpha/D^2=T^2/D^2. The square
coefficient becomes alpha(D-r)/[D^2(D+r)]=delta. The G_b coefficient is
kappa_0-1+2alpha/[D(D+r)]=u; the Q_(L,z) coefficient is
r(kappa_0-1)+2alpha/(D+r)=v. The J_b coefficient is
kappa_0-1+2r alpha/[D^2(D+r)]=j. These exact equalities yield (10).

Consequently, if the two input certificates (2) are supplied and

                         theta<=j/kappa,                (12)

then the ordinary certificate for the actual h is

 V_h+sum mu_ij Q_ij+kappa sum Lambda_ij Q_ij
         +u G_b+v Q_(L,z)+(j-kappa theta)J_b
                 =M_a+kappa M_b+delta||W_b-Dp||^2.       (13)

Every ACTUAL coefficient in (13) is nonnegative, and its entire formal
remainder is PSD. If several terms use the same ordered pair, add their
nonnegative coefficients. This also covers empty inputs, singleton inputs
and zero steps within the input blocks on the original independent-gradient
space. The boundary gradient p is not identified with any tail gradient.

At rT=AD, delta=0 and j/kappa=1-D^2/T^2, recovering the saturated credit
join. At r=0 (a physical unit bridge), the budget is

                    j/kappa=2AD/(A+D)^2.                (14)

Thus (13) gives a concrete nonsaturated full-matrix construction with a
nonzero PSD cross-block square. It does not infer nonsaturated necessity
or extend the complementarity-based C_spine extraction theorem.

## 5. An explicit reversal class at arbitrary lengths

Define a recursive class from the empty schedule: if a,b belong to it,
adjoin h=(a,1+r,b) for ANY r>=0 satisfying r(A+D+r)<=AD, using the ACTUAL
capacities of the chosen children. Formula (13) with theta=0, starting
from the empty zero certificate, constructs an ordinary full certificate
at every node. Thus every schedule in this class is certified primitive.

Reversing h gives (reverse(b),1+r,reverse(a)). Inductively its children
belong to the same class, and the condition r(A+D+r)<=AD is symmetric
in A,D. Applying (13) to the reversed children supplies all actual
nonnegative coefficients and a full PSD matrix for the reversed schedule.

# Exact intrinsic reversal involution: full PSD congruence and precise signs

Status: candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or verifier call.
This proves an explicit transformation of UNSIGNED intrinsic certificates,
with a necessary and sufficient sign test for this particular output. It
does not assert that all schedules admit a certificate passing that test.
Every identity below is derived here, with no unverified finding as a lemma.

## 1. The complete intrinsic affine matrix system

Let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be nonnegative, s=sum h_i, D=1+s, and use
x_i=x0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t with independent formal gradients g_0,...,g_n.
The interpolation quantities and energy are

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                         -sD||g_n||^2.

An unsigned certificate is a real off-diagonal array lambda such that

             V_h+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij=g^T M g,

with ALL value coefficients zero and M PSD on the FULL n+1 gradient space.
Write e=(1,...,1)^T, e_n=(0,...,0,1)^T, hbar=(h,0)^T, w=hbar+e_n,
p_i=1+sum_(t<i)h_t. Let A be lower triangular with A_ii=1 and
A_it=h_t for t<i, so A e=p and e_n^T A=w^T. Define the row Laplacian
L_ij=-lambda_ij for i!=j and L_ii=sum_(j!=i)lambda_ij. Value cancellation
is exactly

 L^T e=omega,             omega=-2hbar+2s e_n.           (1)

Define the nonsymmetric grounded matrix

 K=L+diag(hbar)-hbar e_n^T+diag(w).                     (2)

Here and below sym(B)=(B+B^T)/2. Direct expansion gives

                 M=sym(K A)-D^2 e_n e_n^T.             (3)

To verify it fully, the gradient part of Q_ij is
<g_i,(A g)_i-(A g)_j>+(||g_j||^2-||g_i||^2)/2.
Thus its weighted sum has matrix sym(L A)-diag(omega)/2. Adding V_h
gives sym(L A)+diag(h_i(2-h_i),1-D^2). On the other hand,
sym([diag(hbar)-hbar e_n^T+diag(w)]A)
=diag(h_i(2-h_i),1): all off-diagonal terms cancel, proving (3).

Equations (1)--(2) imply

 K e=w,             K^T e=D e_n.                       (4)

It follows from (3) that e^T M e=D p_n-D^2=0. Since M is PSD,
M e=0 (apply nonnegativity to e+t z for every real t). Therefore

 K p=-D w+2D^2 e_n.                                   (5)

If K is invertible, (4)--(5) give the useful fixed inverse boundaries

 K^(-1)w=e,
 K^(-1)e_n=(p+D e)/(2D^2),
 e_n^T K^(-1)=e^T/D.                                  (6)

All these equations hold for signed as well as ordinary multipliers.

## 2. Reverse the actual schedule, with an explicit array

Let hrev=(h_(n-1),...,h_0), and put wrev=(hrev,1)^T,
p_rev,i=1+sum_(t<i)hrev_t. Define the symmetric invertible matrix

 Delta_ij=1_(j=n-i)-1_(j=n-i-1),                       (7)

where out-of-range indicators are0, and write P=Delta^(-1).
The following identities follow directly from these entries:

 Delta e=e_n, Delta p=wrev, Delta p_rev=w,
 P e_n=e,             Delta A_rev=A^T Delta.            (8)

The last identity can be checked one row at a time: row i<n of
Delta A_rev is row n-i minus row n-i-1 of A_rev, and row n is
row0. The resulting two adjacent column entries agree with A^T Delta.

Assume K is invertible. Put vrev=wrev+2D e_n and define

 K_rev=4D^2 Delta K^(-1) Delta-vrev e_n^T.              (9)

Define the ACTUAL off-diagonal array for the reversed schedule by

 lambda_rev,ij=-4D^2(Delta K^(-1) Delta)_ij,  i!=j.     (10)

This is a signed array until its signs are checked. From (6)--(8),

 K_rev e=wrev,        K_rev^T e=D e_n,                  (11)
 K_rev p_rev=-D wrev+2D^2 e_n.

For example, the row-sum identity is
4D^2 Delta K^(-1)e_n-vrev=2(wrev+D e_n)-vrev=wrev;
the column sum uses e^T vrev=3D. The p_rev identity follows from
Delta p_rev=w and K^(-1)w=e.

The matrix in (9) is exactly the grounded matrix (2) of (10): off
the last column this follows entrywise; in that column the subtracted
wrev_i equals hrev_i for i<n, precisely the required grounding term.
The diagonals then follow from the row sums. The column equation in
(11) now proves ALL reversed value flows

 out_i^rev-in_i^rev=-2hrev_i for i<n, and 2s for i=n.    (12)

No formal value or zero-step gradient has been dropped.

## 3. Full PSD is preserved by a displayed congruence

Let M_rev be the entire remainder associated with (10), so by the direct
expansion (3), M_rev=sym(K_rev A_rev)-D^2 e_n e_n^T.
Then

 M_rev=4D^2 Delta K^(-1) M K^(-T) Delta.               (13)

Indeed, substitute (9) into M_rev. Its non-rank-one term is
4D^2 sym(Delta K^(-1) A^T Delta), by (8). Its remaining terms equal

 -sym((wrev+2D e_n)wrev^T)-D^2 e_n e_n^T
                       =-(wrev+D e_n)(wrev+D e_n)^T.

Substituting (3) into the right side of (13) gives exactly those terms:
the first by symmetrization, and the second by
Delta K^(-1)e_n=(wrev+D e_n)/(2D^2). This proves (13).
Thus the remainder is PSD on ALL independent reversed gradients.
This proof needs no external H-duality theorem or strong-convexity limit.

## 4. This matrix map is an involution, not a one-way relaxation

Let B=4D^2 Delta K^(-1) Delta. Then
B^(-1)=P K P/(4D^2). Equations (4)--(8) show

 B^(-1)vrev=(p_rev+2D e)/(4D),
 e_n^T B^(-1)=e^T/(4D),
 e_n^T B^(-1)vrev=3/4.

Consequently K_rev=B-vrev e_n^T is invertible, and direct rank-one
inversion yields

 K_rev^(-1)=[P K P+(p_rev+2D e)e^T]/(4D^2).           (14)

This formula may alternatively be verified by multiplying by (9);
the denominator in rank-one inversion is1-3/4=1/4, so it cannot vanish.
Apply (9) to K_rev with hrev in place of h. Equations (8),(14) give

 4D^2 Delta K_rev^(-1)Delta-(w+2D e_n)e_n^T=K.          (15)

Thus the map is an involution on the stated affine/full-PSD domain.

## 5. Actual coefficient signs: the entire remaining condition

The output of this particular map is an ORDINARY reversed certificate
if and only if

          (Delta K^(-1)Delta)_ij<=0 for every i!=j.      (16)

If one wants an E_eta certificate instead, (10) shows the exact test:
all entries targeting j!=n must still be nonnegative, while
lambda_rev,(i,n)>=-eta hrev_i for i<n. This does not license negative
internal entries. Equation (13) supplies the full PSD condition separately.

For an actual E_theta input with 0<=theta<1, let Lambda be its nonnegative
array and set lambda_(i,n)=Lambda_(i,n)-theta h_i, leaving other entries
unchanged. Then it has exactly the intrinsic flow and full M used above.
If every physical h_i is positive, K has nonpositive off-diagonal entries:
K_(i,n)=-Lambda_(i,n)-(1-theta)h_i and all other off-diagonals are
-Lambda_ij. Its row-sum surplus is w_i>0. Strict diagonal dominance
therefore proves invertibility and makes (9)--(16) applicable without
an additional invertibility assumption. With zero steps, the same full
formulas hold whenever K is invertible; universal invertibility in that
case is NOT asserted and no duplicated formal gradients are identified.

The ordinary input family in local candidate37622e6cdcb606e6 supplies an
explicit failure of (16) at every n>=4; that separate proof gives all
input coefficients and the positive-square remainder independently.
Hence (16) cannot be discarded, even for a full ordinary input. Conversely,
the signed E_(1/2) calibration h=(1,2,1,1) passes this sign test; its exact
5x5 audit also checks all flows, congruence and involution. Neither example
proves existential certificate re-selection for arbitrary h.

## 6. Relation to the actual G,G/D,D performance interface

The matrix identity can also be understood without guessing a performance
functional. For a tail of capacity D, prepend physical step D+1. The exact
gradient-norm identity is

 D^2(||g_pre||^2-||g_n||^2)
 +sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,pre)+Q_(n,pre)+D Q_(pre,n)
 +sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n)+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=M.

Its grounded, normalized G,G matrix is -K/(2D^2). Reversing the physical
schedule produces (hrev,D+1). For ANY intrinsic signed array lambda_rev,
the corresponding distance identity for that appended schedule is

 ||x0-xstar||^2-||x_out-xstar||^2
 +2sum_(i<n)hrev_i Q_(i,star)+2(D+1)Q_(n,star)+4D Q_(star,n)
 +sum lambda_rev,ij Q_ij=M_rev,                        (17)

where x_out=x_n-(D+1)g_n and the optimum jet is zero after translation.
To check (17), set H=sum hrev_i g_i. Expand the distance difference
2<x0,H+(D+1)g_n>-||H+(D+1)g_n||^2 and the displayed optimum Q terms.
The x0 and H cross terms cancel; the remaining value and square terms
are precisely V_hrev. This proves the identity on the full original space.
After division by2, its reduced D,D matrix has finite off-diagonals
lambda_rev/2, optimum outgoing weights (hrev,D+1), and optimum incoming
weight2D at n. These are exactly the inverse-difference matrix's row
and column deficits. This explicitly explains both performance endpoints.

Sources motivating this derivation, not used as black-box premises:
Shu--Wang, arXiv:2609.03281v1, Sections4.4--4.5; source applicability
and the q>0 check are separately written in37622e6cdcb606e6. Matlas and
the fact graph were queried; no accepted intrinsic reversal theorem was
found. All new identities here remain candidate evidence.

repair on the SAME physical schedule, not just an SDP restatement. It is
conditional on two explicit sign tests, and no capacity improvement is claimed.

Let A have diagonal1 and A_it=h_t for t<i, and let L be the row Laplacian

The constant-gradient form is zero. PSD therefore makes the constant

                      sum_(j=1)^n P_j lambda_(0,j)=2.   (5)

 P_j Q01+(P_j-1)Q10-Q_(0,j)+Q_(1,j)

x1=x0-g0 and x_j=x1-sum_(t=1)^(j-1)h_t g_t in the gradient terms.

lambda^0_(k,k+1)=2(k+1)^2, lambda^0_(k+1,k)=2(k+1)(k+2).

The theorem permits arbitrary nonnegative tail steps and arbitrary other

# Directed full-matrix moves: exact intervals, a square move, and sign repair

Status: candidate proofs, NOT verifier-accepted. No SDP or fact_submit call.
These screen plans8a9fe85173280c05 and e8ab4e3f583a448e by actual algebra.
They do not prove that a legal improving pivot always exists.

## 1. A concrete family preserving all affine conditions

Use nonnegative h, s=sum h, D=1+s, independent gradients g0,...,gn,
original Q_ij, intrinsic V_h, and a value-cancelling signed array lambda.
Let A have diagonal1 and A_it=h_t for t<i, e=(1,...,1), p=A e, and
let L be the row Laplacian of lambda. Expanding every Q gives

 M=diag(h_i(2-h_i),-s(s+2))+sym(L A).

Thus for a coefficient change with zero value flow, the full matrix
change is sym(delta L A). Put
K=L+diag(hbar)-hbar e_n^T+diag(w), hbar=(h,0), w=(h,1).

Choose real vectors u,v satisfying e^T u=0, v^T e=0, v^T p=0. The
actual change

 delta lambda_ij=-t u_i v_j (i!=j),  delta L=t u v^T,
 delta K=t u v^T,  delta M=t sym(u z^T), z=A^T v       (1)

preserves row sums, every value flow, and the constant-gradient kernel.
Indeed delta L e=0, delta L^T e=0 and delta L p=0, while z^T e=0.
The off-diagonal rule and v^T e=0 also give the stated Laplacian diagonal.
Every actual E_theta multiplier is Lambda_ij-t u_i v_j. Its signs give
explicit scalar half-intervals, one for EACH ordered pair; no sign is dropped.

Assume u,z lie in the range of M. Let M^+ mean the inverse on that range
and zero on its kernel. Put alpha=u^T M^+u, beta=z^T M^+z,
sigma=u^T M^+z, d=sqrt(alpha beta). The exact PSD interval for (1) is

             -2/(sigma+d)<=t<=2/(d-sigma),             (2)

where a zero lower denominator means no lower bound, and a zero upper
denominator means no upper bound. If either vector vanishes, every t is allowed.
To prove (2), congruence by the inverse square root of M on its range
reduces the condition to I+t sym(U Z^T)>=0. The only possibly nonzero
eigenvalues of sym(U Z^T) are (sigma+d)/2 and (sigma-d)/2, as follows
by restricting to span{U,Z}, or from its trace sigma and determinant
(sigma^2-alpha beta)/4. Intersection with every coefficient interval is
therefore an EXACT legal one-parameter move. For a remainder positive
definite on e-perp, the range assumptions follow from the displayed
orthogonality conditions. Singular faces need their actual range checked.

For invertible K write Phi=-Delta K^(-1)Delta, with
Delta_ij=1_(j=n-i)-1_(j=n-i-1). If 1+t c is nonzero, where
c=v^T K^(-1)u, then direct rank-one inversion gives

 Phi(t)=Phi+[t/(1+t c)] x y^T,
 x=Delta K^(-1)u,   y^T=v^T K^(-1)Delta.               (3)

Multiplication of K+t u v^T by the displayed inverse verifies (3).
On a positive-step E_theta sign-feasible interval, theta<1, K(t) has
nonpositive off-diagonals and strictly positive row-sum surplus, so is
invertible; the denominator cannot cross zero there. This supplies an
exact targeted inverse-entry test, but not a universal existence theorem.

## 2. Square-producing moves require no range hypothesis

For ANY v perpendicular to e,p, set u=A^T v. Then e^T u=0 and

                    delta M=t u u^T>=0 for t>=0.       (4)

This gives a legal full-PSD update whenever all actual coefficient signs
survive. Its maximal nonnegative parameter is the minimum of
Lambda_ij/(u_i v_j) over all u_i v_j>0; omit zero products. The move
is useful only when the desired coefficient increases and every required
donor is present. It does not contradict the impossibility of a universal
one-direction matrix-order repair.

There is a particularly explicit local version. For THREE consecutive
queries j,j+1,j+2, put a=h_j>0,b=h_(j+1)>0 and take, on those coordinates,

 v=(b,-a-b,a),
 u=(b(1-a),-a-b(1-a),a),                              (5)

and zero elsewhere. Direct summation shows v^T e=v^T p=0 and u=A^T v,
including all earlier and later original coordinates. The six changes,
with row/column labels0,1,2 local to these three queries, are

 delta lambda01= t b(1-a)(a+b),
 delta lambda02=-t ab(1-a),
 delta lambda10= t b[a+b(1-a)],
 delta lambda12= t a[a+b(1-a)],
 delta lambda20=-t ab,
 delta lambda21= t a(a+b).                            (6)

Every value flow cancels and the FULL remainder increases by
t||b(1-a)g_j-[a+b(1-a)]g_(j+1)+a g_(j+2)||^2.

If a=1, the backward edge j+2->j can ALWAYS be deleted. Set
t=lambda_(j+2,j)/b>=0. Formula (6) only decreases that one actual
nonterminal-directed coefficient; all other changes are nonnegative.
The exact underlying interpolation identity is

 b Q_(j+1,j)+(b+1)Q_(j+2,j+1)+Q_(j+1,j+2)-b Q_(j+2,j)
                              =||g_(j+2)-g_(j+1)||^2. (7)

It holds in every formal dimension using the physical consecutive steps
1,b. Thus this is a genuine directed coefficient elimination on arbitrary
longer schedules, independent of any symmetric graph assumption.

For 0<a<=1 the same deletion is allowed if the forward donor obeys
lambda_(j,j+2)>=(1-a)lambda_(j+2,j), using ordinary input coefficients.
For a>1 and b<=a/(a-1), (6) instead increases the forward remote edge.
If j+2=n and q=-lambda_(j,n)>0, it removes that negative terminal
coefficient with t=q/[ab(a-1)] provided

 lambda_(n,j)>=q/(a-1),
 lambda_(j,j+1)>=q(a+b)/a.                            (8)

All other changed entries then increase. If every unchanged coefficient
is already ordinary, (8) gives an ordinary SAME-SCHEDULE repair with a
displayed positive square. These donor conditions are assumptions, not
consequences of PSD claimed without proof.

## 3. Compound repair strengthens the first-unit-step pinching theorem

Assume h0=1,h1=b>0. Start with a full signed certificate. The four-edge
redistribution eliminating all outgoing0->j, j>=2, gives

 lambda'_01=2, lambda'_0j=0,
 lambda'_10=4-sum_(i>=2)lambda_(i,0),
 lambda'_1j=lambda_(1,j)+lambda_(0,j),                  (9)

and changes the full difference matrix [[1,bvec^T],[bvec,C]] to diag(1,C).
Here is a direct check: the identity
P_j Q01+(P_j-1)Q10-Q0j+Q1j
=-<g0-g1,sum_(k=1)^(j-1)(1+P_j-P_(k+1))(g_k-g_(k+1))>
with P_j=sum_(t<j)h_t, multiplied by lambda0j and summed, removes
exactly that cross block; the constant-gradient kernel gives
sum_j P_j lambda0j=2. Thus (9) is a full formal PSD pinching even if
its10 coefficient is temporarily negative.

Now let d=lambda20>=0 and add (d/b) times (7) with j=0. This removes
the backward20 edge, increases10 by d,12 by d/b,21 by(1+b)d/b,
and adds (d/b)||g2-g1||^2 to the full remainder. The final array has

 lambda''_10=4-sum_(i>=3)lambda_(i,0), lambda''_20=0,   (10)

with all other changes as explicitly stated. Hence the original mass
condition is relaxed to sum_(i>=3)lambda_(i,0)<=4. All nonterminal signs
are then nonnegative. The only terminal test is

 lambda1n+lambda0n+1_(n=2)d/b>=0,

along with unchanged lambda_(i,n)>=0 for 2<=i<n. This is a concrete
compound repair with an indefinite pinching followed by a positive square;
the final full matrix and every actual coefficient are checked.

For the earlier failing credited input h=(1,1/2), whose signed array is
lambda01=11/4,10=3/20,02=-1/2,20=41/10,12=43/10,21=27/10,
pinching gives10=-1/10. Adding only1/5 times (7) already makes10=0,

whose full remainder is ||g0-g1||^2+(7/4)||g1-g2||^2. Thus the isolated
pinching failure is repaired by a complete legal certificate, not by
dropping the negative entry or by changing the physical schedule.

## 4. Exact screening against the inverse-sign counterexample

Use the n=4 unit schedule. To make this example self-contained, its complete
nonzero input array is
lambda01=29/15,10=58/15,02=1/30,20=1/10,12=469/60,21=469/40,
13=1/40,31=1/20,23=717/40,32=239/10,34=32,43=40.
All remaining entries are0. Its flows are(-2,-2,-2,-2,8), and direct
substitution into Q gives the full remainder
(59/60)||g0-g1||^2+(1/60)||g0-g2||^2
+(929/240)||g1-g2||^2+(1/80)||g1-g3||^2
+(143/16)||g2-g3||^2+16||g3-g4||^2.
This is the input also discussed in37622e6cdcb606e6; its full data and
positive-square proof are supplied here independently.

The first pivot u=e0-e1, v=e0-2e1+e2 only rescales its bad inverse entry:

          Phi13(t)=-3/[4(168373+42990t)].               (11)

Thus it has no finite zero crossing in its sign-feasible interval. An exact

Instead use the backward-skip deletion (7) on indices1,2,3, with a=b=1.
The actual backward coefficient lambda31=1/20 is deleted using t=1/20.
The only other changes are +1/20 on21, +1/20 on23, and +1/10 on32.
Every input coefficient remains nonnegative, and the full remainder gains
(1/20)||g3-g2||^2. Set Knew=K+(1/20)(e3-e2)(e1-2e2+e3)^T.
Its EXACT Phi=-Delta Knew^(-1)Delta is the following rational matrix:

 [-1/40, 0, 0, 0, 1/200],
 [1/160, -1/24, 0, 0, 37/2400],
 [1/160,18919/1350744,-4760/56281,120/56281,5698397/135074400],
 [1/160,18679/1350744,2440/56281,-14250/56281,22930397/135074400],

claim: Complete candidate theorem at arbitrary length, including ZERO steps: every actual E_theta certificate with0<=theta<1 and ZERO full independent-gradient remainder is ALREADY an ordinary intrinsic certificate in the same signed array. Positive short steps force M_ii>=h_i>0, so every positive step on this face is>1; terminal-column identities then force all credited incoming coefficients nonnegative. evidence:
# Zero full remainder leaves no terminal-credit enlargement

Status: complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or
fact_submit call. This solves the scoped mathematical target of plan
max4_zero_remainder_directed_reselection; it does not solve general repair.

## Statement

Let h=(h0,...,h_(n-1)) be ANY finite nonnegative schedule, including zero
steps and the empty list. Normalize smoothness to1 and put

 x_i=x0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 s=sum h_i,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                          -s(s+1)||g_n||^2,
 J_h=sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n), E_theta=V_h-theta J_h.

Suppose 0<=theta<1 and an ACTUAL nonnegative array Lambda cancels every
formal value coefficient in E_theta+sum Lambda_ij Q_ij and leaves the
ZERO quadratic form on ALL n+1 independent formal gradients. Define

 lambda_(i,n)=Lambda_(i,n)-theta h_i for i<n,
 lambda_ij=Lambda_ij on all other distinct pairs.

Then EVERY lambda_ij is already nonnegative. Thus the SAME signed array
is an ordinary certificate V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=0. No re-selection,
change of physical steps, discarded gradient, or new PSD matrix is needed.
In addition every positive physical step is strictly larger than1.
Any zero-step query i<n is isolated in the entire array: all outgoing
and incoming lambda entries at i vanish.

## Full matrix expansion

Let A have diagonal1, A_it=h_t for t<i, and zero above the diagonal.
Let L be the row Laplacian of lambda, so L_ii=out_i=sum_(j!=i)lambda_ij
and L_ij=-lambda_ij for i!=j. Value cancellation gives

                    out_i-in_i=-2h_i  (i<n),
                    out_n-in_n=2s.

The gradient part of Q_ij is
<g_i,(A g)_i-(A g)_j>+(||g_j||^2-||g_i||^2)/2.
Summing and inserting the value flows yields the entire symmetric matrix

             M=diag(h_i(2-h_i),-s(s+2))+sym(L A).       (1)

This derivation uses all original formal indices, even at zero steps.

## Diagonal constraints exclude positive short steps

For i<n put Back_i=sum_(j<i)lambda_ij>=0. Since column i of A is zero
above i and equal to h_i below i,

 M_ii=h_i(2-h_i)+(1-h_i)out_i+h_i Back_i.              (2)

All outgoing coefficients are nonnegative except possibly lambda_(i,n),
which is bounded below by -theta h_i. Thus out_i>=-theta h_i.
If 0<h_i<=1, then (2) gives

 M_ii>=h_i[(2-h_i)-theta(1-h_i)]+h_i Back_i
       =h_i[(2-theta)-(1-theta)h_i]+h_i Back_i
       >=h_i>0.                                      (3)

This contradicts M=0. Consequently every positive h_i is greater than1.
If h_i=0, every outgoing lambda_ij is nonnegative, including the
terminal entry because its floor is0. Equation (2) reduces to
M_ii=out_i=0, forcing every outgoing entry to vanish. Its value flow is0,
so all incoming entries, also nonnegative because i is nonterminal, vanish.
This proves the stated zero-step isolation without identifying gradients.

## Terminal-column constraints force the credited signs

For i<n put R_i=sum_(k=0)^i lambda_(n,k). Every summand is nonnegative
because its target is nonterminal. The two off-diagonal entries of L A
needed for (1) are

 (L A)_(i,n)=-lambda_(i,n),
 (L A)_(n,i)=-lambda_(n,i)+h_i R_i.

For the second formula, use sum_(k>i)L_(n,k)=R_i, a consequence of
the zero row sum of L. Thus

              2M_(i,n)=h_i R_i-lambda_(n,i)-lambda_(i,n). (4)

Since M=0, if h_i>1 this gives

 lambda_(i,n)=(h_i-1)lambda_(n,i)
                         +h_i sum_(k<i)lambda_(n,k)>=0. (5)

If h_i=0 its outgoing entries already vanish. These are all possibilities
by (3), and all other signed coefficients were nonnegative from the start.
This proves the claim, including the empty and all-zero schedules.

## Two useful quantified extensions

For ANY full PSD E_theta remainder, not necessarily zero, (3) still holds:
a positive step at most1 forces M_ii>=h_i. Such a step cannot occur on
a zero-diagonal face at that query.

If M is PSD and M_nn=0, its entire terminal column vanishes: for every
coordinate i, nonnegativity on e_n+t e_i rules out a nonzero linear term.
Consequently, if all physical steps are at least1, (4)--(5) already show
that the supplied signed array is ordinary even when M is NONZERO.

More quantitatively, for any index with h_i>=1 and an actually negative
lambda_(i,n)=-q, q>0, equation (4) gives M_(i,n)>=q/2. The2x2 PSD
principal minor then forces

                         M_ii M_nn>=q^2/4.            (6)

So such credit requires a nonzero terminal diagonal and nonzero matrix
coupling; it cannot live on the terminal-kernel face. For h_i=0 the credit
floor already forbids negativity. The full zero-remainder theorem needs
no extra step-range assumption because (3) supplies it automatically.

## Scope and retrieval

A strictly enlarged E_theta cone, if it exists, must exploit a NONZERO
full PSD remainder. The theorem neither moves a general certificate to
zero remainder nor asserts that an optimal schedule has zero remainder.
It does not classify the ordinary zero-remainder schedules or settle the
objective profile. Generic inverse-map signs also remain a separate issue.

Fact search found no accepted theorem for this intrinsic zero-remainder
claim. Matlas returned unrelated1306.6419 Theorem3.1 and2102.07922 Lemma6;
neither is used. Equations (1)--(6) give the proof without external premises.

Let delta=1-2/lambda=3-2sqrt(2). Direct summation gives

 S_m=2^m-2-a_m+a_m(c_m^m-2^m)/(c_m-2),
 S_m/lambda^m -> e/[lambda(lambda-2)]=e.                 (8)

Consequently, for each fixed integer j>=0,

 d_(m-1-j)/S_m -> delta lambda^(-j).                     (9)

In the left H_(m-1) copy, d_(m-1-j) occurs2^(j-1) times for j>=1.
Hence, for either zeta=zeta_l,

 L(zeta)=product_(j>=1)(1-delta lambda^(-j)zeta)^(2^(j-1)),
 p_l,m -> p_l=L(zeta_l),
 v_l,m -> v_l=(1-delta zeta_l)p_l,
 t_l,m -> t_l=(1-delta zeta_l)p_l^2=p_l v_l.              (10)

Here are convergence details, including the many small steps. Write
e_j,m=d_(m-1-j)/S_m=1/S_m+A_m c_m^(-j), where
A_m=a_m c_m^(m-1)/S_m ->delta and is bounded. The summed contribution
of the1/S_m terms in the left copy is at most2^m/S_m ->0. The tail
sum of the remaining terms over j>=J is bounded by a constant times
sum_(j>=J)(2/lambda)^j, tending to zero uniformly as J->infinity.
For all large m, max_(j>=1)|zeta_l e_j,m|<1/2. On that disk the
absolutely convergent series for log(1-u) obeys
|log(1-u)|<=2|u|. Fixed-j convergence from(9), followed by the tail
bound, proves convergence of the log products and their exponentials.
The identities for v and t use the finite identities

 v_l,m=(1-d_(m-1)z_l)p_l,m,
 t_l,m=(1-d_(m-1)z_l)p_l,m^2/(1-d_0 z_l).

The latter denominator tends to1, since d_0 is bounded and S_m->infinity.
This explicitly retains the removed original d_0 and never replaces it
by an appended unit step. Therefore D_l,m and K_m converge to D_l and K
obtained by inserting p_l,v_l,t_l into(5)--(6).

## 4. Rational enclosures for the limiting two-by-two matrix

The needed numerical-looking bounds below are rational inequalities,
with a finite power-series derivation. They do not rely on a solver.
Since the left factors have power sums

 mu_r=sum_(j>=1)2^(j-1)(delta lambda^(-j))^r
       =delta^r/(lambda^r-2),

the absolutely convergent logarithm is

       log L(zeta)=-sum_(r>=1)mu_r zeta^r/r.              (11)

Put A_4(zeta)=-sum_(r=1)^4 mu_r zeta^r/r. The maximum left coefficient
is delta/lambda and eta=|zeta|delta/lambda<3/20 for both zeta values.
Also mu_2<1/125 and |zeta|^2<=17/4. Bounding mu_r by
mu_2(delta/lambda)^(r-2), the tail obeys

 |log L-A_4| <= mu_2 |zeta|^2 eta^3/[5(1-eta)]
             <27/10^6.                                 (12)

The inequality eta<3/20 follows from |zeta|<=sqrt(17)/2<21/10
and delta/lambda<1/14. The inequality mu_2<1/125 follows by substituting
lambda=1+sqrt(2), or the square-root enclosure immediately below.

For complete finite arithmetic details, enclose sqrt(2) by

 14142135623/10^10 < sqrt(2) < 14142135624/10^10,

whose squared endpoints straddle2. Form lambda,delta,mu_1,...,mu_4
using interval addition, multiplication, and reciprocal of positive
intervals; form A_4. Its real part is negative and its modulus is<1.
Evaluate E_12(A)=sum_(j=0)^12 A^j/j! by the recurrence t_0=1,
t_j=t_(j-1) A/j and E_12=sum t_j. Ordinary rational interval arithmetic
gives the following outward enclosures (every finite decimal is exact):

| zeta | Re E_12(A_4) | Im E_12(A_4) |
|---|---|---|
| (1+i)/2 | [.79526080,.79526082] | [-.16872576,-.16872574] |
| (4+i)/2 | [.42009743,.42009746] | [-.09205447,-.09205445] |

The exponential-series tail is bounded by e/13!<3/13!. Because
Re A_4<0, changing A_4 by the log tail changes its exponential by
at most (27/10^6)/(1-27/10^6). The sum of these two errors is<31/10^6.
Thus the following coarser intervals safely enclose the exact p_l:

| l | Re p_l | Im p_l |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [.7952,.7953] | [-.1688,-.1686] |
| 2 | [.4200,.4202] | [-.0921,-.0920] |

For clarity, the arithmetic in the last substitution can be reproduced
without complex transcendental operations. For intervals a,b,c,d use
(a+ib)(c+id)=(ac-bd)+i(ad+bc), with conjugation negating the imaginary
interval. Use delta in[.17157,.17158], set v_l=(1-delta zeta_l)p_l
and t_l=p_l v_l, then evaluate(5)--(6) by these operations. The resulting
outward rational bounds are

 0<D_1<209/1000,        0<D_2<209/1000,
 -101/1000<K_11<-97/1000,
 -57/1000<K_22<-54/1000,
 -64/1000<K_12=K_21<-61/1000.                            (13)

These deliberately loose bounds avoid relying on printed floating digits.
They imply K_11<0 and

 det K >[(97)(54)-64^2]/10^6=1142/10^6>0.

Completing the square in a real two-variable quadratic now proves K is
negative definite. Since all its entries and D_l,m converge, for all
sufficiently large m, K_m is negative definite and D_l,m<21/100.
This is uniform in w_m,C_m because these parameters do not enter the
coefficient limits. In particular C_m is allowed to diverge arbitrarily
fast: trace(C_m K_m)<=0 holds at the EXACT finite m, before any limit.
Equation(7) gives F(x_q)<=21/(100S_m).

For audit convenience only, two_anchor_interval_check.py repeats the
displayed finite rational operations in a few milliseconds. Its output
is not a replacement for(11)--(13) and their explicit remainder bounds.
The first script attempt had a Python Interval/ComplexInterval dispatch
TypeError; reversing a scalar-complex multiplication repaired it. The
corrected script exits0 and checks all the displayed enclosures. No
optimization call was made in this arithmetic check.

## 5. Free terminal step and the exact original benchmark

For any actual interpolating F, integrating its1-Lipschitz gradient on
the segment from x_q to x_q-b g_q gives

 F(x_q-b g_q)<=F(x_q)-b(1-b/2)||g_q||^2<=F(x_q),

for every b in[0,2]. The terminal gradient is unrestricted. This proves(2).

We include the benchmark estimate rather than importing an unverified
comparison. Put r=log_2 lambda, C_k=S_circle(k)+1, and B_k=2S_bullet(k)+1.
The accepted recursions in factb98bb807d514e80d give

 C_0=B_0=1,
 C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
 B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)),
 Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,
 G(A,B)=2A+B/2+sqrt(B^2+8AB)/2.

For V(t)=(1+t)^r-1, direct differentiation gives

 d^2/du^2 log V(exp u)
 =r t(1+t)^(r-2)[(1+t)^r-1-r t]/V(t)^2>0,  t=exp u.

The final strict positivity follows by differentiating
(1+t)^r-1-r t, which vanishes at0 and has positive derivative for t>0.
Midpoint convexity at u,-u implies
V(t)V(1/t)>=(2^r-1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2.
For A,B>0 set t=(A/B)^(1/r) and M=(A^(1/r)+B^(1/r))^r.
Then (M-A)(M-B)>=2AB, so M>=Omega(A,B), by the positive root of
the quadratic and M>max(A,B). Induction yields C_k<=(k+1)^r.
Also sqrt(B^2+8AB)<=B+4A gives G(A,B)<=4A+B. Using
u^r+v^r<=(u+v)^r for nonnegative u,v, induction yields B_n<=1+4n^r.
That elementary inequality follows by differentiating (1+t)^r-t^r.

At n=2^m-1, n^r/lambda^m->1, while(8) gives S_m/lambda^m->e.
Combining this with(2) proves the first bound in(3). Finally
e>1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3 gives42/(25e)<63/100.

## 6. What remains open

This closes the concrete order-one two-block proposal, more broadly for
every PSD coupling of the real and imaginary mode differences. It does
not close all PSD additions annihilating the initial vector. That larger
zero-initial subspace has dimension3: one may also independently combine
Im P_i(z_1) and Im P_i(z_2), instead of requiring opposite coefficients.
The same two-anchor matrix on that three-dimensional space is not negative
semidefinite; a specific positive direction is screened separately.
Neither such a positive certificate coefficient nor the finite solver
diagnostics supplies a legal trajectory. The next actual object must still
pass every joint prefix/optimum constraint and all terminal anchors, with
the original normalized profile constants.

Explicit q_3 is given in (26a), with all value/Gram coefficients and optimum edges. evidence:
# Direct objective gluing on the actual critical words

Status: UNVERIFIED joint calculation and certificate-space obstruction.
No solver and no fact_submit. The negative formal vectors below are NOT legal
smooth-convex trajectories. They refute a specified full multiplier array and
its stated repairs, not the schedule or the original profile conjecture.

The only mathematical predecessor used is accepted fact
`1252b8823bb5a290` for interpolation, and `b98bb807d514e80d` for the
Huber/cut witnesses and the exact benchmark recursions. The recursive pattern
was suggested by Altschuler--Parrilo, arXiv:2309.16530, Theorem 3.4; all
identities needed here are derived below rather than imported from it.

## 1. Normalization and a fully specified multiplier array

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. For every sample let

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0,
    C_ij=-2 Q_ji
        =2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.

Every position is substituted using the actual GD steps. In the full formal
quadratic, x_0,g_0,...,g_n are independent; they are not restricted to any
chosen primal family.

Fix positive numbers a,c, with c>2. Write

    d_j=a c^j,  H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

Throughout this calculation require d_j<M_j at the levels being used.
Define the following exact scalar recurrence:

    Z_0=1, t_0=1,
    z_j=(M_j+d_j)/(M_j-d_j),
    r_j=1+2z_j=(3M_j+d_j)/(M_j-d_j),
    Z_(j+1)=r_j Z_j,
    t_(j+1)=(1+sqrt(4 Z_(j+1)-3))/2,
    delta_j=Z_j-r_j d_j^2.                              (1)

Thus Z_j=t_j^2-t_j+1. All r_j>1, so the square roots are real and
t_j>=1. This fixes every parameter; there is no numerical optimization.

Here is the actual nonnegative array lambda^(j) on C_ij. Its base has only
lambda^0_(star,0)=1. Suppose its block has length n=n_j, sum S=S_j,
and put p=n, q=2n+1, b=1+d_j, z=z_j, r=r_j, t=t_j, t'=t_(j+1).

1. Embed the old array on the left sample indices {0,...,p,star}.
2. Add r times the old array on {p+1,...,q,star}.
3. For each right queried index i=p+1,...,q-1, whose physical step is h_i,
   add z h_i to entries (p,i) and (q,i), and subtract 2z h_i from (star,i).
4. Add the following six sparse corrections:

    (p,q): z,                 (q,p): z d_j,
    (p,star): -S,             (q,star): 2S+b-rS,
    (star,p): b-t,            (star,q): t'-rt.           (2)

The corrections individually may be signed, but the FINAL array is
nonnegative. In fact its optimum entries are exactly

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i for i<q,
    lambda_(star,q)=t',
    lambda_(i,star)=0 for i<q,
    lambda_(q,star)=2S+b.                                (3)

To verify this inductively, left interior entries are unchanged, the old
left terminal entry t becomes b, right interior entries become
(r-2z)h_i=h_i, and the right terminal entry becomes t'. Incoming optimum
entries at the left terminal cancel, and the right terminal entry becomes
2S+b. Every other update either embeds a nonnegative old coefficient or
adds z h_i, z, or z d_j. This proves actual coefficient signs, including
all optimum edges, rather than just signs of an auxiliary matrix.

## 2. Complete identity and calibration

There is an exact gradient-only remainder E_j, defined on all the formal
gradients of the block, such that

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-t_j g_end||^2-2t_j f_end
       =sum lambda^(j)_ik C_ik + E_j.                  (4)

Its recursion is

    E_0=0,
    E_(j+1)=E_j(left)+r_j E_j(right)
                         +delta_j ||g_p||^2.            (5)

Here each child is evaluated at its actual chronological sample indices.
In particular E_j contains no terminal-gradient term of its own: its
variables are only the midpoint gradients of all internal recursion nodes.

We verify (4)--(5) without omitting any function coefficient. Denote the
left endpoint and gradient by x,g and the right endpoint and gradient by
y,v. Their values are f,F. The weighted right displacement is

    w=sum_(p<i<q) h_i g_i=x-bg-y.

The rank-one correction in step 3 sums to

    2zS(f+F)-zS(||g||^2+||v||^2)
                         -2z<w,x+y-g-v>.               (6)

Combine the two child identities, the correction (6), and (2). The
coefficient of f is

    2[(z-1)S-b+z-zd_j]=0,

because z(S+2-b)=S+b. The coefficient of F is -2t', and every
interior value has already canceled within its child and (6). The
optimum value is zero under normalization; before normalization the
total value flow cancels it against the terminal coefficient.

The x^2, <x,g>, <x,v>, <y,g>, and <g,v> coefficients all cancel.
The remaining expression is

    ||x_start||^2-||y-t'v||^2-2t'F
       +(r d_j^2-Z_j)||g||^2
       +(Z_(j+1)-r Z_j)||v||^2
       -E_j(left)-r E_j(right).

The last gradient coefficient is zero by (1). This is exactly (4)--(5).
This calculation also follows by direct expansion of (6); the cancellations
use only z(S+2-b)=S+b and r=1+2z.

The calibration is exact. Set lambda=1+sqrt(2), a=1/lambda, c=lambda.
Then M_j=lambda^j, d_j=lambda^(j-1), z_j=lambda, r_j=lambda^2,
Z_j=M_j^2, and delta_j=0 at every level. Thus E_j=0 and (4) is a
valid full initial-distance certificate at the undeformed silver word.
It is the canonical endpoint-square guarantee, not a claim that this
particular certificate attains the sharper Huber constant.

For an arbitrary real q_cert, the SAME nonnegative array supplies the
following fully value-canceled candidate objective matrix:

    q_cert ||x_0||^2-2 f_n
       +sum_(i!=k) [2 lambda^(m)_ki/t_m] Q_ik
     =(q_cert-1/t_m)||x_0||^2
       +[||x_n-t_m g_n||^2+E_m]/t_m.                 (7)

This explicitly includes the true initial vector and the optimum index.
Its validity as an upper bound depends on FULL PSD of the right side.

## 3. An exact negative midpoint for the assigned parameters

Now set m>=128, epsilon=1/m, and use the assigned family

    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c.

For these parameters 2<c<3 and 0<a<c-2<1. The exact mass formula is

    M_j=A c^j+(1-A)2^j,  A=a/(c-2),                 (8)

so 0<A<1 and M_j-d_j=A(3-c)c^j+(1-A)2^j>0.
Thus every coefficient in the proposed array is defined and nonnegative.

Nevertheless delta_2<0. Here is a finite exact proof with an explicit
parameter interval, not a limiting differential equation. Put s=sqrt(2).
For j=0,1,2, write r_j=N_j/D_j, where

    N_0=(2+s)+(4-s)epsilon,
    D_0=(2-s)+s epsilon,
    N_1=(4+3s)+(9-3s)epsilon-epsilon^2,
    D_1=s+(3-s)epsilon+epsilon^2,
    N_2=(10+7s)+(19-5s)epsilon-(4+s)epsilon^2
                                                 -(1+s)epsilon^3,
    D_2=(2+s)+(5-3s)epsilon+s epsilon^2
                                                 +(1+s)epsilon^3.

All denominator coefficients are positive. Since d_2=lambda(1-epsilon^2),

    delta_2=P(epsilon)/(D_0 D_1 D_2),
    P=N_0 N_1 D_2-lambda^2(1-epsilon^2)^2 N_2 D_0 D_1.

The coefficients of P, in increasing degree 0 through 10, are

    0,
    -112-96s,
    -96-84s,
    640+12s,
    528+368s,
    88+92s,
    -320-167s,
    -202-158s,
    -2-4s,
    42+30s,
    10+7s.                                           (9)

These coefficients follow by multiplying the displayed degree-at-most-three
polynomials. A tiny exact Q(sqrt(2)) polynomial multiplication independently
checked the list; the displayed identity is the mathematical evidence.
Using s<3/2, the sum of absolute upper bounds for coefficients of degree
at least two is 3311. Consequently, for 0<epsilon<=1/128,

    P(epsilon)/epsilon
       <=-112-96s+3311 epsilon
       <-112+3311/128<0.                             (10)

For comparison, the first derivative is

    delta_2=-(48+28sqrt(2))epsilon+O(epsilon^2).

The same negative coefficient occurs at the finite diagnostic m=3:

    P(1/3)=(-1059632-2141552sqrt(2))/59049<0.

The three relevant denominators are positive there as well. This agrees
with failure of the ARRAY even though max3's unrestricted numerical H_3
diagnostic reported a Huber match. That diagnostic is not used as a premise.

## 4. Negative FULL formal directions, and limits of repairs

Every occurrence of a level-two midpoint contributes

    omega_i delta_2 ||g_i||^2

to E_m, with omega_i>0, a product of right-child weights r_j from its
ancestors. There are K=2^(m-3) such indices. Their actual step is the same
number b_2=1+d_2. No other term of E_m uses any of those gradient
coordinates, by the diagonal recursion (5).

First choose one such index i, set x_0=0, g_i=v!=0, all other queried
gradients zero, and g_n=-(b_2/t_m)v. Then

    x_n=-b_2 v, x_n-t_m g_n=0, E_m=omega_i delta_2||v||^2<0.

Thus (7) is not PSD for ANY q_cert. Merely increasing the initial-distance
coefficient does not repair the proposed array.

There is a larger obstruction when m>=4. Work first with scalar formal
gradients, put x_0=g_n=0, allow arbitrary g_i at the K selected indices
subject to sum_i g_i=0, and set every other gradient to zero. This is a
subspace D of dimension K-1 on which

    x_n=0, g_(n-1)=0,
    E_m=delta_2 sum_i omega_i g_i^2<0

for every nonzero vector. The weights need not coincide. It follows that:

* Any added quadratic depending only on x_0,x_n,g_n,g_(n-1) vanishes on D.
* Replacing only the final physical step leaves every position unchanged
  on D, because g_(n-1)=0. With the same array, the negative evaluation
  persists for every prescribed final-step replacement and every q_cert.
* Any PSD matrix addition of rank less than K-1 has a nonzero kernel vector
  in D, by dimension counting, and therefore cannot repair the full matrix.

The last statement is about additions to this fixed matrix. Changing
relative interpolation multipliers may have an indefinite difference and
is NOT excluded. Likewise a correction of growing rank is not excluded.
The selected vectors deliberately do not satisfy the interpolation
constraints; no legal lower witness, no W upper bound, and no impossibility
theorem for H_m is inferred.

## 5. Fixed-constant deformations: the same ansatz always fails for tau>0

Consider the allowed neighboring family

    c=lambda(1+tau/m), a=(1-sigma/m)/c,                (11)

with fixed real tau,sigma, for all sufficiently large m. Positivity and
d_j<M_j hold uniformly over the word once 0<a<1 and 2<c<3: indeed

    M_j/d_j=1/(c-2)
               +[1/a-1/(c-2)](2/c)^j

lies between 1/a and 1/(c-2), both greater than one.

If tau>0, the specified multiplier recursion always develops a negative
coefficient at a FIXED level as m tends to infinity. If sigma+tau<0,
then d_0>1/lambda and delta_0=1-r_0 d_0^2<0, since
d maps to d^2(3+d)/(1-d) is strictly increasing for 0<d<1 and equals
one at d=1/lambda.

For sigma+tau>=0 the fixed level j=4 suffices. To show this, temporarily
regard epsilon as a real variable tending to zero and set

    u=2/lambda, D=sigma+(1+lambda^2)tau,
    T_j=lambda^2 tau-D u^j.

Differentiation at epsilon=0 of the explicit finite formulas gives

    M_j(0)=lambda^j,
    (d/depsilon)log M_j |0=j tau-D(1-u^j),
    (d/depsilon)(d_j/M_j)|0=(1/lambda)T_j.

For r(x)=(3+x)/(1-x), (d/dx)log r at x=1/lambda equals 2.
Using 1-u=1/lambda^2 and
2(1/lambda-1/lambda^2)/(1-u)=2sqrt(2), equation (1) therefore gives

    (d/depsilon)[delta_j/M_j^2]|0
       =2sqrt(2)[tau(j-lambda^2)-D(1-2u^j)].          (12)

One can also verify (12) by summing the finite geometric series for T_j.
At j=4, 4-lambda^2<0 and 1-2u^4>0. The latter follows from
u^4=272-192sqrt(2)<1/2; squaring 543<384sqrt(2) verifies it with
positive sides. Moreover D>=lambda^2 tau>0. Thus (12) is strictly
negative. The expression is an analytic finite rational function near
zero, so delta_4<0 for every sufficiently large m. This uses a derivative
at one fixed finite depth, not an unproved continuum recurrence.

The same full-vector argument as in Section 4 then excludes the array and
its stated endpoint or fixed-rank patches. This generalization does not
exclude a different full certificate for any of the deformed schedules.

## 6. Rechecking the exact comparison and an actual deformation filter

Set rho=log_2(lambda). From the accepted exact recursions, primitive shifted
mass C_n=S_circle(n)+1 has join

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,

and the benchmark B_n has join

    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

Here is a proof of C_n<=(n+1)^rho and B_n<=1+4n^rho, retained rather
than assuming the earlier draft comparison. Define F(t)=(1+t)^rho-1.
For t=exp(z), direct differentiation gives

    d^2/dz^2 log F(exp(z))
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
        [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/F(t)^2>0.

The numerator bracket is positive since rho>1 and its derivative is
rho[(1+t)^(rho-1)-1]>0. Convexity at z,-z gives
F(t)F(1/t)>=F(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. With A=t^rho B and
E=(1+t)^rho B, this implies (E-A)(E-B)>=2AB, so

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho.

Induction in the primitive recursion gives its claimed bound. Also
G(A,D)<=4A+D. If k+l+1=n, the dominant induction now gives

    B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^rho+l^rho]<=1+4n^rho.

The last inequality follows from superadditivity of t^rho on nonnegative
arguments, which follows by integrating its increasing derivative.

For (11), the exact mass formula (8) gives

    M_m/lambda^m
      =(1+tau/m)^m [A+(1-A)(2/c)^m] -> exp(tau).       (13)

Thus the actual benchmark satisfies

    limsup B_(2^m-1)/(2M_m-1)<=2 exp(-tau).             (14)

In particular tau=1 recovers 2/e. This comparison alone is not an
objective upper bound; the failed matrix in Section 4 cannot supply one.

There is also a useful LOWER bound for the exact benchmark. Balanced
primitive joins give C_(2^j-1)>=lambda^j. Put b_0=1 and

    b_(j+1)=G(1,b_j)/lambda.

Balanced dominant joins imply B_(2^j-1)>=b_j lambda^j. The map in this
recursion is strictly increasing. Its fixed point above one is

    b_infty=sqrt(2)(1+lambda^(-1/2))>2.                (15)

To verify the fixed point, squaring the equation G(1,b)=lambda b
gives lambda(lambda-1)b^2-4lambda b+4=0; the positive root (15)
satisfies the original equation, whereas the smaller algebraic root does
not. Alternatively uniqueness above one follows because
G(1,b)/b=2/b+1/2+sqrt(1+8/b)/2 is strictly decreasing. Since
1<b_1=4/lambda<b_infty, monotonicity shows b_j increases to b_infty.

This yields an ACTUAL legal-witness filter even when the final step is
replaced arbitrarily. Let P_m=S_m-(1+d_0) be the sum of the queried prefix
before that final step, and prescribe any b_m>=0. For P_m>=1, the two
accepted Huber/cut witnesses give

    W_(n_m)(H_m with final step b_m)
       >=max{1/(2P_m+2b_m+1),
                    (b_m-1)_+^2/(P_m+1)^2}
       >=1/(2P_m+3+2sqrt(P_m)).                       (16)

For b_m<=1+sqrt(P_m), the first term proves (16). For larger b_m, the
second is at least P_m/(P_m+1)^2, which is at least its right side
because P_m^2+P_m+2P_m sqrt(P_m)-1>=0 for P_m>=1.
Equations (13), (15), and (16) prove the uniform statement

    liminf_m B_(n_m) W_(n_m)(modified word)
                     >=b_infty/(2 exp(tau)).           (17)

Consequently no fixed asymptotic separation below the benchmark is possible
within these fixed-constant deformations, even with an arbitrary final step,
when tau<=log(b_infty/2). This is a legal lower-bound conclusion for that
parameter region. It is distinct from the formal-matrix obstruction for
tau>0, and does not settle the assigned tau=1 family.

## 7. A richer exact join, with the unresolved full-matrix issue exposed

The following calculation records the next concrete repair interface. It
does not assert that a scalar local condition closes the target.

Replace the canonical child storage by

    I=||x_start||^2-||x_end-u0 g_end||^2-2v0 f_end
       =sum lambda C+E,
    Z=(u0-1)^2+v0,
    k=S+u0-v0>=0.

Assume its optimum entries are h_i on (star,i), u0 on the terminal
(star,end), zero on other (i,star), and k on (end,star); retain the
ENTIRE gradient remainder E. These properties hold for the calibrated
canonical family. They are assumptions of this interface, not all full
certificates.

Use two nonnegative correction weights A0,B0. Scale the right child by
r=1+A0+B0. For each right queried i add A0 h_i on (p,i), B0 h_i on
(q,i), and -(A0+B0)h_i on (star,i). Choose cross coefficients p0,q0>=0
with

    p0-q0=b+(1-A0)S.

Adjust optimum entries to physical h_i, terminal u1, and
k1=2S+b+u1-v1>=0 exactly as in (2), with child k in place of S.
Thus the actual final array is nonnegative provided the named scalar
coefficients and u1,k1 are nonnegative. Put

    d=b-1, M=S+1, t=A0-B0,
    H=M+d-B0(M-d)-t M,
    ell=p0-B0-t,
    Z1=(u1-1)^2+v1,
    V=x_p-x_q-g_p+g_q.

Full coefficient expansion, including all function values, gives

    E_new=E_left+r E_right
       +t||V||^2+2<V,(H-ell)g_p+ell g_q>
       +(Z-rd^2)||g_p||^2+(rZ-Z1)||g_q||^2.           (18)

For example the canonical construction sets A0=B0=z, p0=z,
q0=zd, H=ell=t=0 and Z1=rZ, recovering (5).
To check (18), first use D=x_p-x_q. The local coefficients of
D^2, D g_p, D g_q are t,-2(ell+t-H),2(ell+t).
Substituting D=V+g_p-g_q makes the g_p g_q coefficient zero and gives
exactly the displayed diagonal and cross terms. The value coefficient
at p is 2[(A0-1)S-b+p0-q0]=0 and the terminal coefficient is -2v1.

Demanding the isolated three-vector matrix in (18) be PSD is only a
SUFFICIENT restriction. It forces Z>=rd^2 and Z1<=rZ, and risks
repeating the already recorded scalar-deficit failure. The useful open
question is whether the FULL child remainders can pay for an indefinite
local term.

There is a finite exact way to retain that information for this array
class. Define the gradient moment z_block=sum h_i g_i+g_end. If a child
remainder is decomposed into nonnegative internal squares plus the sharp
two-variable form

    a0||z_block||^2+2b0<z_block,g_end>+c0||g_end||^2,

then the parent remainder before elimination is the explicit four-variable
form, in L=z_left, g=g_p, R=z_right, e=g_q,

    a0||L||^2+2b0<L,g>+c0||g||^2
      +r[a0||R||^2+2b0<R,e>+c0||e||^2]
      +t||d g+R||^2+2<d g+R,(H-ell)g+ell e>
      +(Z-rd^2)||g||^2+(rZ-Z1)||e||^2.                (19)

The parent moment is exactly z_parent=L+d g+R. Substituting
L=z_parent-dg-R and completing squares in g,R gives its next
two-variable form when the corresponding eliminated block is PSD and
the cross columns lie in its range. Negative eliminated directions are
full-matrix obstructions and must not be dropped. This is an explicit
recursively generated multiplier family and exact remainder interface;
no choice of its free parameters or uniform constant establishing the
requested asymptotic separation has yet been proved.

The original target remains open. The finished result of this attempt is
the fully exhibited obstruction to (1)--(7), the exact parameter filter
(17), and the identified need to change the full recursive array rather
than inflate its endpoint bound.

## 8. A constructive cross-block repair, and its exact finite-depth limit

There is an actual positive repair of the first bad join in Section 3.
It is useful to record it before diagnosing its later failure. Everything
in this section remains part of the same unverified joint calculation.

First an elementary seed, including its full initial-distance certificate.
For one physical step h with 0<h<=sqrt(2), put M=1+h. Direct expansion
of the interpolation expressions gives

    V_h=2h(f_0-f_1)+h(1-h)||g_0||^2-hM||g_1||^2
       =M C_(0,1)+C_(1,0)+(2-h^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.

Adding h C_(star,0)+M C_(star,1) gives

    ||x_0||^2-||x_1-Mg_1||^2-2(2M-1)f_1
       =sum lambda C+(2-h^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.             (20)

All four displayed multipliers are nonnegative. Its parameters in Section
7 are u0=M, v0=2M-1, Z=M^2, k=0. Its exact remainder is
a0||z_block-Mg_1||^2 with a0=(2-h^2)/h^2.

Here is an explicit subcritical join that builds the H_2 child needed next.
Suppose a block of mass M has u0=M,v0=2M-1,Z=M^2,k=0 and a full PSD
remainder E. Put x=d/M, assume 0<x<sqrt(2)-1, and set

    A0=1/x, B0=2+x, r=3+x+1/x,
    t=1/x-2-x>0,
    eta=x^2+2x-1<0,
    ell=M eta/x, p0=(1+M eta)/x, q0=M,
    u1=2M+d, v1=2(2M+d)-1, Z1=(2M+d)^2.             (21)

Require p0>=0. These parameters satisfy the value-flow and optimum-edge
conditions of Section 7. If the child remainder is at least
a0||z_block-Mg_end||^2, then the FULL new remainder is at least

    a0||U||^2+(r a0+t)||V||^2
                    +M^2(-eta)||g_p-g_q||^2,          (22)

where U=z_left-Mg_p and V=z_right-Mg_q. All omitted terms here are
the actual nonnegative child remainders after their stated lower forms
are removed. Formula (22) follows by substituting (21) into (18);
the mixed coefficient between V and g_p-g_q is A0 d-M=0.
The parent moment obeys

    z_parent-(2M+d)g_q=U+V+(M+d)(g_p-g_q).

Weighted completion of squares therefore also gives the sharp condensed
lower form a1||z_parent-(2M+d)g_q||^2, where

    1/a1=1/a0+1/(r a0+t)+(1+x)^2/(-eta).             (23)

There is no discarded negative direction in this completion: the
difference between the three squares in (22) and (23) is a sum of
nonnegative squares, or follows by expanding weighted Cauchy--Schwarz.

Apply (20) with h=1+d_0 for the assigned epsilon=1/m<=1/128.
Here 1<h<sqrt(2). At the next bridge d_1=1-epsilon,

    d_1-(sqrt(2)-1)M_1
      =-epsilon[1-2(sqrt(2)-1)^2/(1+epsilon)]<0.

Thus (21) is subcritical. Also 3/8<x<sqrt(2)-1 and M_1<5/2, so
eta>=-7/64 and 1+M_1 eta>=1-35/128>0. All actual multipliers in
(21) are therefore nonnegative. This proves a full H_2 certificate with
Z_2=M_2^2 and a positive condensed coefficient a1, directly from (20)--(23).

The next bridge is genuinely supercritical. With r0=sqrt(2)-1,

    d_2-r0 M_2
      =epsilon[(4-7r0)-2epsilon-lambda epsilon^2]
                                                   /(1+epsilon)>0. (24)

The numerator bracket is positive since 4-7r0>1 and epsilon<=1/128.
Also x=d_2/M_2<1/2: the ratios d_j/M_j increase to c-2<1/2.

For ANY primitive child with mass M and any bridge ratio

    sqrt(2)-1 < x=d/M <= (sqrt(5)-1)/2,

choose instead

    r=1/x^2,
    A0=1/x, B0=1/x^2-1-1/x>=0,
    t=A0-B0=(x^2+2x-1)/x^2>0,
    ell=H=0, p0=A0, q0=B0 d,
    Z1=M^2/x^2.                                     (25)

Choose u1>=0 solving u1^2-u1+(2M+d)=Z1, and put
v1=2M+d-1+u1, whenever that root is real and v1>0. At the present
H_2-to-H_3 join this holds: x<1/2 and M=M_2>4 give
Z1>4M^2>2M+d. Thus u1=(1+sqrt(1+4(Z1-2M-d)))/2>1,
v1>0, and k1=0.

The relation p0-q0=b+(1-A0)S is exact. All actual multipliers are
nonnegative, and (18) becomes

    E_new=E_left+r E_right
                   +t||x_p-x_q-g_p+g_q||^2 >=0.       (26)

Both endpoint diagonal residuals in (18) vanish because Z=M^2,
r=1/x^2, and Z1=rZ. This is a FULL valid initial-distance objective
certificate, with q_cert=1/v1 and multipliers 2lambda_ki/v1 on Q_ik.
Its matrix is

    [||x_n-u1 g_n||^2+E_new]/v1,

on the full original formal vectors. It repairs the first failed midpoint
of the canonical array. The claim is for the finite H_3 subblock with the
parameters of the assigned m, not an asymptotic bound for H_m.

The same explicit construction ALSO applies to the original finite m=3
diagnostic, without the small-epsilon estimates. In that case

    d_0=(sqrt(2)-1)/2, d_1=2/3, d_2=8lambda/9,
    M_1=2+(sqrt(2)-1)/2,
    M_2=11/3+sqrt(2), M_3=(74+26sqrt(2))/9,
    Z_3=(10707-1022sqrt(2))/64.

For the subcritical join, 8/27<d_1/M_1<sqrt(2)-1 and M_1<9/4.
Thus 1+M_1 eta>1-(9/4)(233/729)>0. At the next join
d_2-(sqrt(2)-1)M_2=[7-16(sqrt(2)-1)]/9>0 and d_2/M_2<1/2.
Every sign condition in (20)--(26) therefore holds. An exact upper level is

    q_3=1/[M_3-1+(1+sqrt(1+4(Z_3-M_3)))/2].          (26a)

This level exceeds the Huber value because Z_3<M_3^2. It is an exact
finite full certificate, not a reconstruction or validation of max3's
floating optimal dual, and not a benchmark improvement.

For completeness, (26) retains more information than an endpoint scalar.
If both children have sharp remainder a1||z-Mg||^2, its condensed
remainder is

    a2||z_parent+(M/x)g_q||^2,
    1/a2=2/a1+(1+x)^2/(x^2+2x-1).                   (27)

To verify this, set U=z_left-Mg_p, V=z_right-Mg_q,
T=x_p-x_q-g_p+g_q=d g_p+z_right. Then
z_parent+(M/x)g_q=U-V/x+(1+1/x)T, while (26) is bounded below by
a1||U||^2+(a1/x^2)||V||^2+[(x^2+2x-1)/x^2]||T||^2.
Weighted completion gives (27). The positive sign of the terminal term
in (27) matters; replacing it by z_parent-M_new g_q loses the state.

One natural continuation of this repair has a precise limit. Keep H=ell=0
in (18), and certify the new local term separately by its three
nonnegative square coefficients. For arbitrary child storage Z, the
conditions are

    t>=0, Z>=r d^2, Z1<=rZ,
    A0=(M+rd)/(M+d),
    B0=[rM-2M-d]/(M+d)>=0.                           (28)

Consequently r>=2+d/M and Z1<=Z^2/d^2. Choosing the largest
admissible r=Z/d^2 and Z1=rZ gives an actual recursive full certificate
as long as B0,t>=0 and the endpoint root defining u1 remains admissible.
It preserves the full child matrices in (26); the following failure is
not caused by deleting them.

At the first supercritical input j=2, Z_2=M_2^2. Under the maximal rule
put Y_j=Z_j/d_j^2. Because d_(j+1)=c d_j, its exact recurrence is

    Y_(j+1)=Y_j^2/c^2,
    Y_j=c^2 T^(2^(j-2)),
    T=M_2^2/(c^2 d_2^2).                             (29)

For epsilon<=1/128 one has T<=1-epsilon/2. An explicit check is as
follows. The ratio M_2/(c d_2) has numerator

    lambda^2+(8-2lambda)epsilon-epsilon^2

and denominator lambda^2(1-epsilon)(1+epsilon)^3. The denominator
times (1-epsilon/2), minus the numerator, is

    epsilon[(5lambda-13/2)+(1-lambda^2)epsilon
                    -2lambda^2 epsilon^2+(lambda^2/2)epsilon^4]>0.

Indeed 5lambda-13/2>5, lambda^2<6, and the negative terms have
magnitude less than 5/128+12/128^2. Squaring the resulting positive
ratio bound gives T<=(1-epsilon/2)^2<=1-epsilon/2.

Using c<5/2, equation (29) implies

    Y_j <= (25/4) exp[-2^(j-2)/(2m)].                 (30)

For j=ceil(log_2 m)+4, the right side is at most (25/4)exp(-2)<2,
because exp(2)>1+2+2^2/2=5>25/8. But (28) requires
Y_j>=r>=2+d_j/M_j>2. Hence this continuation must fail no later
than that level; for m>=128 the level is strictly below m.

The same upper recurrence bounds ANY continuation within the isolated
PSD-local-square restriction (28) that starts at Z_2<=M_2^2: smaller
Z or smaller r cannot improve the later bound. Such a continuation can
fail earlier, including from an endpoint root or a different coefficient
sign, but cannot survive to the required horizon. This is a limitation
of (28), not of the general full recurrence (18). Allowing H or ell to
be nonzero and using the entire indefinite local/positive child matrix
interaction remains outside this obstruction.

An independent tiny rational coefficient audit in
`research/direct_gluing_exact_audit.py` checked the one-step seed, a
subcritical three-step join, and a supercritical seven-step join. It matched
EVERY function and FULL Gram coefficient exactly and checked every final
multiplier sign using Fraction arithmetic. The audit is an algebra check
on the displayed construction, not verifier acceptance or a substitute
for the written derivation.
