evidence:
# C53: a formal template defeats the entire mixed-boundary repeated-copy join

Status: complete joint proof candidate, **not verifier-accepted**. No solver
or verifier call is allocated. The only mathematical input from the fact graph
is `1252b8823bb5a290`, for the interpolation convention and full formal-vector
certificate interpretation. The construction suggested by shared finding
`c7f10ed5dc99275b` is defined and expanded here; that finding is not a premise.

The conclusion concerns a specified recursively generated certificate family.
The formal vectors in this proof are NOT legal smooth-convex transcripts. In
particular, the conclusion below is neither a lower bound for unrestricted
W_n nor a decision of the original exact-profile problem.

## 1. The certificate family, including all its available parameters

Use smoothness one and optimum jet x_star=g_star=f_star=0. For every ordered
pair of distinct samples put

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    C_ij=-2Q_ji
        =2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2.

The accepted fact implies C_ij>=0 on every legal trajectory. All identities
below, however, are identities in independent formal vectors after the GD
substitution; no interpolation constraints are imposed on test vectors.

Fix a>0,c>0 and define

    d_j=a c^j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The initial block in the certificate recursion is H_1=(1+a), not H_0.
For each block choose real u_j,v_j, with final v_m>0, and a multiplier array
lambda^(j) on its samples and star. Require the following star pattern:

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i             for every queried i<n_j,
    lambda_(star,n_j)=u_j,
    lambda_(i,star)=0               for i<n_j,
    lambda_(n_j,star)=s_j,
    s_j=S_j+u_j-v_j.                                      (1)

Here s_j is only an incoming optimum multiplier, not the stepsize sum S_j.
All final actual multipliers must be nonnegative if the array is to certify
an objective bound. We will prove a necessary condition even without using
those signs. Assume exact cancellation of every function-value coefficient
in the identity defining the gradient-only remainder E_j:

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-u_j g_end||^2-2v_j f_end
            =sum lambda^(j)_ik C_ik+E_j.                  (2)

Put

    Z_j=(u_j-1)^2+v_j,
    z_j=sum_(i<n_j) h_i g_i+g_end.                         (3)

The seed may be ANY one-step array satisfying (1)--(2). Its remainder need
not be PSD. In particular this includes the primitive one-step seed in the
shared construction, with u_1=M_1,v_1=2M_1-1 and
E_1=(2-(1+a)^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.

Here is the permitted join. Write n=n_j,p=n,q=2n+1,S=S_j,
d=d_j,b=1+d,M=M_j. Choose parameters A,B,P,Q with

    r=1+A+B,
    P-Q=b+(1-A)S.                                       (4)

Embed one copy of the old array on the left block and r times the same
array on the right block. For every right queried index i=p+1,...,q-1 add

    A h_i to (p,i), B h_i to (q,i),
    -(A+B)h_i to (star,i).                               (5)

Add the following six sparse corrections:

    (p,q): P,                    (q,p): Q,
    (p,star): -s_j,              (q,star): s_(j+1)-r s_j,
    (star,p): b-u_j,             (star,q): u_(j+1)-r u_j.  (6)

No restriction to H=ell=0, greedy choices of Z, PSD local terms, rank-one
child remainders, or PSD child remainders is imposed. The final objective
matrix must still be PSD on the full formal space. Nonnegative actual
coefficients, when they hold, include all the star coefficients in (1);
requiring A,B,P,Q>=0 is a sufficient way to preserve the other signs.

The desired result is a necessary condition for ANY such recursion. It is
therefore valid for every choice of its parameters that passes all actual
sign tests, including choices depending on the target horizon.

## 2. The complete local identity

Define

    t=A-B,
    H=M+d-B(M-d)-t M,
    ell=P-A,
    V=x_p-x_q-g_p+g_q.

The exact recursion for the entire gradient remainder is

    E_(j+1)=E_j(left)+r E_j(right)
       +t||V||^2+2<V,(H-ell)g_p+ell g_q>
       +(Z_j-rd^2)||g_p||^2+(rZ_j-Z_(j+1))||g_q||^2.    (7)

We verify both the value and quadratic coefficients. Write x=x_p,g=g_p,
y=x_q,e=g_q, and w=sum_(p<i<q)h_i g_i=x-bg-y. Summing (5) gives

    2AS f_p+2BS f_q-AS||g||^2-BS||e||^2
                      -2<w,A(x-g)+B(y-e)>.             (8)

This follows by expanding a summand: the coefficient of each f_i and of
each ||g_i||^2 cancels, leaving the displayed linear and bilinear terms.
The value coefficient at p in the two children plus (5)--(6) is

    -2v_j+2AS+2(P-Q)-2s_j-2(b-u_j)
       =2[(A-1)S+P-Q-b]=0.

The coefficient at q is

    -2r v_j+2BS-2(P-Q)+2(s_(j+1)-r s_j)
                         -2(u_(j+1)-r u_j)=-2v_(j+1).

This uses (1),(4) and r=1+A+B. All other values have already canceled.

For completeness, the quadratic parts of the six expressions used in (6)
are respectively

    C_pq: 2<e,y-x>-||g-e||^2,
    C_qp: 2<g,x-y>-||g-e||^2,
    C_pstar: -||g||^2,       C_qstar: -||e||^2,
    C_starp: 2<g,x>-||g||^2,
    C_starq: 2<e,y>-||e||^2.

Subtract their weighted sum and (8) from the new potential minus the two
child potentials. With D=x-y, all dependence on the separate x,y cancels.
The resulting coefficients, using the convention that cross coefficients
multiply twice the stated inner product, are

    ||D||^2: t,
    <D,g>: H-ell-t,               <D,e>: ell+t,
    ||g||^2: Z_j-rd^2+t-2H+2ell,
    ||e||^2: rZ_j-Z_(j+1)+t+2ell,
    <g,e>: H-2ell-t.

Substituting V=D-g+e gives (7). Thus (7) concerns the full original
gradient space, not only a condensed boundary form.

## 3. A formal template on which all mixed terms vanish

Define nonzero signed scalars

    k_1=2+a=M_1,
    k_(j+1)=-k_j^2/d_j,       j>=1.                       (9)

For each block H_j and each vector e, there is an explicit formal gradient
assignment, linear in e, with terminal gradient e such that

    z_j=k_j e,
    E_j=(k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2.                              (10)

Crucially this is true for EVERY parameter choice in (4)--(6). The same
template (9) works after a change of the storage variables, multiplier
weights, or mixed boundary terms.

First check the seed carefully. From (1)--(2), subtraction of the star
terms gives the intrinsic identity

    E_j=2sum_(i<n_j)h_i(f_i-f_end)
          +sum_(i<n_j)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
          +(M_j-Z_j)||g_end||^2
          -sum_(i!=k finite)lambda^(j)_ik C_ik.          (11)

To obtain (11), use
||x_start||^2-||x_end||^2
 =2sum h_i<g_i,x_i>-sum h_i^2||g_i||^2
and s_j=S_j+u_j-v_j. This also verifies that no hypothesis s_j=0 is needed.

Assign both seed gradients equal to e, and set the formal values
f_i=<e,x_i>-||e||^2/2. Every finite C_ik is then zero. More generally,
for a constant-gradient block with prefix sums P_i,
f_i-f_end=(S_j-P_i)||e||^2 and

    2sum h_i(S_j-P_i)+sum h_i(1-h_i)=S_j(S_j+1).

The latter equality follows from
sum_i h_i sum_(t>=i)h_t=(S_j^2+sum_i h_i^2)/2.
Equation (11) therefore evaluates to (M_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2.
For H_1, z_1=(2+a)e=k_1 e, proving (10). The auxiliary values merely
evaluate a polynomial identity; they are not claimed to be feasible jets.

Suppose (10) holds at level j. In the right child use its template with
terminal vector e. In the left child use its template with terminal vector

    g=-k_j e/d_j.

The block displacement gives exactly

    V=d_j g+z_right=0,
    z_parent=z_left+d_j g+z_right=z_left=k_j g=k_(j+1)e.  (12)

Evaluating the ENTIRE right side of (7), rather than discarding any child
part, now gives

    E_(j+1)
      =(k_j^2-Z_j)||g||^2+r(k_j^2-Z_j)||e||^2
           +(Z_j-rd_j^2)||g||^2+(rZ_j-Z_(j+1))||e||^2
      =[(k_j^2-rd_j^2)k_j^2/d_j^2+r k_j^2-Z_(j+1)]||e||^2
      =(k_j^4/d_j^2-Z_(j+1))||e||^2.

This is (10) at the parent. Neither E_j>=0 nor Z_j=k_j^2 was used.
In particular reducing Z at an earlier join does not remove the test:
its resulting positive template energy is carried exactly into the next
calculation and cancels with that join's storage terms.

## 4. Even changing the final initial-distance coefficient cannot repair it

Write u=u_m,v=v_m>0,k=k_m,Z=(u-1)^2+v. The full objective certificate
generated by the final array, at any proposed level q_cert, is

    M_cert=q_cert||x_0||^2-2f_n
                         +sum_(i!=j) (2lambda^(m)_ji/v) Q_ij
       =(q_cert-1/v)||x_0||^2
                         +[||x_n-u g_n||^2+E_m]/v.       (13)

The whole formula follows from (2) and C_ij=-2Q_ji. Its actual
interpolation multipliers are nonnegative when the lambda array is.

Apply (10), keep the initial formal vector x_0 independent, and write e
for the terminal template vector. Since z_m=k e,

    x_n-u g_n=x_0-(k+u-1)e.

Set beta=k+u-1. The restriction of v M_cert to the two independent
scalar coordinates in x_0,e has matrix

                    [ q_cert v      -beta       ]
                    [   -beta       2k beta-v   ].       (14)

Indeed its second diagonal is
beta^2+k^2-Z=2k(k+u-1)-v. Full PSD requires (14) PSD.
Its lower diagonal cannot be zero: PSD would then force beta=0, making
that diagonal -v<0. Consequently 2k beta-v>0, and its determinant gives

    q_cert >= beta^2/[v(2k beta-v)] >= 1/k^2.             (15)

For the last inequality use the exact identity

    k^2 beta^2-v(2k beta-v)=(v-k beta)^2>=0.

Both denominators are positive. Thus (15) holds whether E_m is PSD or
indefinite, whether q_cert equals 1/v or is increased, and whether any
child storage was selected greedily. All nonlinear mixing parameters in
(7) have vanished from the necessary bound.

This is a full-space certificate obstruction. Passing the test on legal
sampled trajectories alone would not suffice, since the formal gradient
assignment used in (10) is generally not a legal transcript.

## 5. Quantitative growing-horizon consequence for the assigned words

Fix an integer m>=128, set epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2), and use the
actual assignment

    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=(1-epsilon)c^(j-1), 1<=j<=m.

The symbol d_m is used only to express the recurrence solution; H_m uses
the bridges d_0,...,d_(m-1). Put

    R=(2+a)/[c(1-epsilon)].

Solving (9) in absolute value gives

    |k_j|=(1-epsilon)c^j R^(2^(j-1)),   1<=j<=m.          (16)

To check (16), divide |k_j| by c d_j. This ratio is R at j=1 and
is squared at every next step, since d_(j+1)=c d_j.

There is a strict gap below one in R, with an explicit uniform constant:

    1-R = epsilon[2-lambda^2 epsilon(1+epsilon)]
                  /[lambda^2(1+epsilon)^2(1-epsilon)]
          > epsilon/4.                                  (17)

For the equality multiply by c^2(1-epsilon). Its numerator is
lambda^2(1+epsilon)^2(1-epsilon)
 -[lambda^2+(2lambda-1)epsilon]
 =2epsilon-lambda^2 epsilon^2(1+epsilon),
using lambda^2=2lambda+1. For the inequality, lambda^2<6 and
epsilon<=1/128 imply

    2-lambda^2 epsilon(1+epsilon)>7/4,
    lambda^2(1+epsilon)^2(1-epsilon)<7.

Also R>0 from its definition. The bound 1-x<=exp(-x), proved for
0<=x<1 by integrating the derivative of log(1-x), now yields

    |k_m| < c^m exp[-2^(m-3)/m].                         (18)

Here c<5/2: sqrt(2)<10/7 gives
c<(17/7)(129/128)=2193/896<5/2. Combining (15),(18) gives

    q_cert > (2/5)^(2m) exp[2^(m-2)/m] -> infinity.       (19)

The limit follows because 2^m/m^2 tends to infinity: its successive ratio
is 2m^2/(m+1)^2>3/2 for all m>=7. In particular the exponential term in
the logarithm of (19) dominates the linear term 2m log(5/2).

Already for every m>=128, (18) gives |k_m|<1 and hence q_cert>1.
For an explicit elementary comparison, exp(1)>1+1+1/2+1/6>5/2, so
log(5/2)<1, while 2^(m-3)>m^2 for every m>=16 by checking m=16
and noting that 2m^2/(m+1)^2>1 thereafter. Thus the exponent in (18),
after bounding c^m by exp(m), is negative.

No upper coefficient from this family can therefore approach the small
objective levels needed for a comparison with the exact Zhang--Jiang
profile. This is stronger than failure of the previously chosen H=ell=0
rule: all the mixed terms, all retained child matrices, all earlier
storage choices, and arbitrary q_cert were included in the derivation.

## 6. Scope and the surviving repair directions

The obstruction covers exactly the repeated-copy array (4)--(6), started
from any H_1 seed with the star pattern (1). The identity requires neither
PSD child remainders nor local PSD checks, and the final test includes x_0
and every original gradient coordinate. It also permits nonzero incoming
terminal optimum weights s_j and arbitrary u_j,v_j consistent with (1).

It does NOT exclude another complete interpolation array for H_m. In
particular C51's finite H_3 certificate uses a different unrestricted
array, and is consistent with this result. The obstruction also does not
automatically cover independent internal coefficient changes at a parent,
additional interpolation edges or corrections outside (5)--(6), a
different star pattern, or a different seed size allowed to grow with m.

The concrete repair requirement is now an algebraic one: a useful changed
array must act nontrivially on the template (10)--(12). Altering only the
local V-dependent terms cannot do that. Nor can changing Z alone, since
the precise earlier template energy is propagated in (10).

For literature context, the gluing-plus-rank-one-plus-sparse architecture
is present in Altschuler--Parrilo, arXiv:2309.16530v1, Theorem 3.4 and its
proof in Sections 3.1--3.2. The exact paper was downloaded and read. No
statement from that paper is imported into this proof, and its certificate
for the undeformed silver schedule is not claimed to apply after the
present parameter deformation.

All new claims here remain candidates until verifier acceptance. The
original unrestricted target remains unresolved.

## 7. Changing only a fixed or moderately growing seed also fails

The one-step starting point is not essential. Permit an arbitrary seed
certificate for the entire block H_r, 1<=r<=m, with the same star pattern
(1), all its finite interpolation entries free, and any gradient remainder.
Above that seed use the repeated-copy join (4)--(6).

By (11), the constant-gradient assignment on the seed gives

    z_r=M_r e, E_r=(M_r^2-Z_r)||e||^2.

Start the template with k_r=M_r and repeat (12). Every subsequent identity
and the full-matrix lower bound (15) remain valid. The exact solution is

    |k_m|=(1-epsilon)c^m R_r^(2^(m-r)),
    R_r=M_r/(c d_r).

In fact R_r<=R_1 for EVERY r>=1 at the assigned parameters. To see this,
the mass recurrence M_(j+1)=2M_j+a c^j gives

    M_j=A c^j+(1-A)2^j, A=a/(c-2),
    R_j=[A+(1-A)(2/c)^j]/(1-epsilon).

One has 0<A<1: a>0,c>2, and

    c(c-2)-(1-epsilon)
       =(2lambda+3)epsilon+lambda^2 epsilon^2>0.

Thus the displayed R_j is decreasing. Combining with (17) gives the uniform
seed-size estimate

    |k_m|<c^m exp[-2^(m-r)/(4m)],
    q_cert>(2/5)^(2m) exp[2^(m-r-1)/m].                   (20)

Consequently no such certificate sequence can provide a bounded useful
upper level whenever 2^(m-r_m)/m^2 tends to infinity. This includes every
fixed seed depth and, more strongly, every choice

    r_m<=m-3 ceil(log_2 m)

for all sufficiently large m. The conclusion permits a different completely
free seed array at each horizon; it is not a finite-library assumption.

A correction confined to a fixed H_3 or H_4 seed therefore cannot repair
the growing certificate. A useful modification must continue to act at
growing recursion levels, or leave this repeated-copy architecture.

## 8. An explicit violated pair and an actual array change outside the family

This section independently checks that the template is not a legal
adversary, and exhibits a concrete multiplier direction that the previous
obstruction does not cover. It does NOT assert full PSD after that change.

For the original one-step template define b0=1+a and M1=2+a. At every
one-step leaf its two gradients coincide. Moreover all leaf endpoints have
the same proximal point Y=x_end-g_end: (12) says the left and right child
endpoints have equal proximal points, so induction propagates the common
value to every leaf. A leaf with gradient w thus has endpoint Y+w and
start Y+M1 w.

Look at the rightmost H_3 copy, which has terminal template vector e. Put

    T=M1^2/(d_1 d_2)>0.

Its left H_2 endpoint gradient is T e, while its last one-step leaf has
gradient e. In the full word these samples are j=n_m-4 (the earlier
endpoint) and i=n_m-1 (the last queried point). Hence

    g_j=T e, x_j=Y+T e,
    g_i=e,   x_i=Y+M1 e.

Adding the two interpolation expressions eliminates values exactly:

    C_ij+C_ji
       =2<g_i-g_j,x_i-x_j>-2||g_i-g_j||^2
       =2b0(1-T)||e||^2.                                (21)

For m>=128 the actual parameters have T>8/5. Indeed M1>2,
d_1 d_2=lambda(1-epsilon)(1-epsilon^2)<lambda<5/2, so
T>4/(5/2)=8/5. Thus (21) is strictly negative for e!=0.
Every legal smooth-convex transcript has both C_ij and C_ji nonnegative,
independently of the choice of function values. This gives an explicit
violated pair; no choice of values or optimum can turn this template into
an actual lower witness.

There is also a concrete, sign-preserving change of the multiplier array:
add gamma>=0 to both lambda_ij and lambda_ji. It preserves every value
flow and every star coefficient. The gradient remainder changes by

    -gamma(C_ij+C_ji)
      =2gamma[||g_i-g_j||^2-<g_i-g_j,x_i-x_j>].           (22)

On the template, the lower-right entry in (14) increases by
2gamma b0(T-1). For ANY prescribed q_cert>0 and v>0, set beta=k+u-1
as before and choose

    gamma=max(0,
       [beta^2/(q_cert v)-(2k beta-v)]/[2b0(T-1)]).        (23)

This makes that particular two-variable restriction PSD, by its Schur
complement. The increment is a real nonnegative interpolation multiplier
change, not a projection of a negative eigenvalue or a free PSD addition.

The complete matrix remains to be controlled. In fact the update (22)
itself is indefinite: setting only g_i nonzero gives a positive value,
whereas setting only g_j nonzero gives
2gamma(1-h_j)||g_j||^2<0 when gamma>0, since h_j=1+d_2>1.
This explicitly prevents treating (23) as a full certificate repair.

The indices i,j are queried samples, so the change introduces no incoming
terminal edge. The pair is already present in the unrestricted model of
accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290; it was the recursive parameterization that
failed to allow this independent change. Equation (20) also shows why a
useful implementation cannot stop at correcting only a bounded seed.

An exact extension for further work is to add, at each growing join, both
edges between p and q-1. Write w=g_(q-1), so x_(q-1)=x_q+b0 w. Its local
remainder update is

    2gamma<g_p-w,g_q+a w-V>,                             (24)

obtained by substituting x_p-x_(q-1)=V+g_p-g_q-b0 w in (22).
This term depends on the last queried gradient separately from z_block and
g_end. A boundary state that retains (z_block,g_end,g_last_query) can
represent (24); the two-variable state alone does not retain that data.
Choosing gamma and the old join parameters with full PSD at every growing
level remains an OPEN construction problem, not a conclusion of this file.

## 9. A concrete three-variable starting state for the surviving construction

The added pair can be represented with an exact, attained boundary state;
there is no need to assume an unspecified positive child remainder. The
following formulas initialize such an analytic attempt at H_2 for the
actual parameters m>=128.

Write b0=1+a,M=1+b0,d=d_1,x=d/M,eta=x^2+2x-1, and

    a0=(2-b0^2)/b0^2.

Then 1<b0<sqrt(2), 3/8<x<sqrt(2)-1, and eta<0. For the upper bound on x,
put s=sqrt(2)-1 and compute
d-sM=-epsilon[1-2s^2/(1+epsilon)]<0. For the lower bound use
d>=127/128 and M<5/2. Thus a0>0.

Start from the seed in Section 1. At the H_1-to-H_2 join set

    A=1/x, B=2+x, r=3+x+1/x, t=1/x-2-x,
    P=(1+M eta)/x, Q=M,
    u_2=M2=2M+d, v_2=2M2-1.

All actual multipliers are nonnegative: t>0, A,B,Q>0, and
1+M eta>=1-35/128>0 since eta>=-7/64 and M<5/2. Both incoming
optimum weights s_1,s_2 are zero, and the corrections (5)--(6) preserve
the star pattern as already checked in Section 2.

For H_2 gradients g0,g1,g2,g3 put

    U=b0(g0-g1), V0=b0(g2-g3), D0=g1-g3.

Substitution in (7) gives the complete remainder

    E_2=a0||U||^2+(r a0+t)||V0||^2+M^2(-eta)||D0||^2.   (25)

To check the substitution, these parameter choices give
H=-t(M+d), ell=-tM, Z_1=M^2,Z_2=M2^2. In the variables
V=d g1+z_right and g1,g3, the cross coefficient between V0 and D0
is A d-M=0, and the D0 diagonal is M^2(1-2x-x^2)=M^2(-eta).
Together with the exact two seed remainders this gives (25).

Retain the three boundary vectors (z,e,w)=(z_2,g3,g2). They are independent
coordinates because b0>0 allows g0 to vary z while holding g2,g3 fixed.
The relation is

    z-M2 e=U+V0+(M+d)D0.

The SHARP attained boundary form obtained by minimizing (25) over g0,g1 is

    K_2(z,e,w)
       =A2||z-M2 e-b0(w-e)||^2+B2||w-e||^2,
    A2=[1/a0+(1+x)^2/(-eta)]^(-1),
    B2=(r a0+t)b0^2.                                    (26)

For exact attainment and the remaining PSD part, put c0=M^2(-eta),l=M+d.
The scalar/vector square identity

    a0||U||^2+c0||D0||^2
      =[a0 c0/(c0+a0 l^2)]||U+lD0||^2
          +||a0 l U-c0 D0||^2/(c0+a0 l^2)

proves (26), and the second square can be set to zero for any supplied
boundary data. In particular (26) is not a test confined to a primal span.

At a subsequent modified join let a sharp child form be K(z,e,w). The
complete six-boundary-variable form before eliminating internal variables is

    K(L,g,u)+r K(R,e,w)
      +t||d g+R||^2+2<d g+R,(H-ell)g+ell e>
      +(Z-rd^2)||g||^2+(rZ-Znext)||e||^2
      +2gamma<g-w,e+a w-d g-R>.                         (27)

Here u is the left last-query gradient; w is the right last-query gradient,
and the parent boundary is (z,e,w), z=L+d g+R. All earlier internal PSD
squares are retained, with the right ones multiplied by r>0. Replace
L by z-d g-R and eliminate (g,u,R). Full PSD requires the eliminated
3x3 block to be PSD, its cross columns to lie in its range, and its Schur
complement in (z,e,w) to be PSD. If the eliminated block is positive
definite, this is the explicit update K_next=C-B^T A_elim^(-1)B, where
A_elim,B,C are the coefficient blocks of (27) in the indicated order.
If it is singular the range condition is essential and cannot be omitted.

Equations (26)--(27), gamma>=0, the actual coefficient signs from (4)--(6),
and the new balanced pair give a definite growing-horizon construction
problem. A sufficient target is a final v_m>=M_m, E_m>=0; (13) would then
give q_m=1/v_m<=1/M_m. No choice of all the parameters establishing this
target is asserted here. The point of (26)--(27) is to retain the variable
on which the missing real interpolation pair acts, instead of repeating
the excluded two-boundary recurrence.

evidence:
# One shared array for all chronological three-block tests

Status: self-contained candidate, **not verifier accepted**. This continuation
uses no optimization, new launch, installation, or fact_submit. The accepted
dependency is `1252b8823bb5a290`, for smooth-convex interpolation and the
original finite full-objective formulation. Every new statement below is
proved within this document. In particular an earlier unverified cut identity
or recursive identity is not a correctness premise.

The requested decision at q=1/M_m is NOT obtained: no feasible common array,
and no infeasibility proof for the entire collection, is asserted. What is
obtained is an exact attained legal-primal interpretation of the collection,
its common two-jump matrix, a quantitative optimum-source budget, and a
quantitative rejection of one explicitly constructed scalable common array
family by two cuts already in the collection.

## 1. Exact collection and notation

Let n>=2, h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) have nonnegative finite entries, and put
S=sum h_i, M=1+S, P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, including P_n=S. Normalize L=1 and
x_star=g_star=f_star=0. The original independent formal vectors are
(x_0,g_0,...,g_n); x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t. For distinct sample indices
in I={star,0,...,n}, write

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Choose ONE finite nonnegative array lambda_ij with finite-node flow

 sum_j lambda_ij-sum_j lambda_ji=2*1_(i=n).                 (1)

Its value-free quadratic polynomial is

 C_lambda=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.        (2)

For every 1<=k<l<=n, require (2) to be nonnegative whenever

 g_i=u for i<k, g_i=v for k<=i<l, g_i=w for i>=l,         (3)

with x_0,u,v,w independent arbitrary formal vectors. The same array is used
for every (k,l). This is the collection A_2. One-block and two-block tests
are included by equality of block values. All the earlier queried-j/tail
tests are included: for j>0 use k=j,l=j+1,u=0; for j=0 use a two-block
specialization. No position moment, optimum edge, or initial coordinate is
discarded in (2).

## 2. One common matrix, with all singular cases

Introduce chronological jumps d_k=g_k-g_(k-1), 1<=k<=n, and b=g_0. Then
g_i=b+sum_(k<=i)d_k. This is an invertible linear coordinate change. Write
the matrix of (2) in coordinates (x_0,b,d_1,...,d_n) as

              [ C       R ]
 A_lambda =   [ R^T     T ],                              (4)

where C is 2 by 2, r_k is column k of R, and T is n by n. A restriction
(3) is EXACTLY the principal block of (4) on x_0,b,d_k,d_l. Thus the entire
collection is equivalent to

 C>=0;
 r_k in Range(C) for every k;
 Z_kk>=0 and Z_kl^2<=Z_kk Z_ll for every k<l,              (5)
 Z_kl=T_kl-r_k^T C^+ r_l.

Here C^+ inverts positive eigenvalues and vanishes on Ker(C). To prove the
singular statement, diagonalize C. A nonzero component of any r_k in its
kernel makes the corresponding quadratic unbounded below in a free base
variable. Once every such component vanishes, complete the squares in the
positive base coordinates. The remaining two-variable quadratic has matrix
[[Z_kk,Z_kl],[Z_kl,Z_ll]], whose PSD criterion is exactly (5). This proves
both implications, including zero diagonal entries and C=0.

There are n(n-1)/2 coupled pair tests of ONE residual matrix Z. This is not
independent per-partition feasibility. It is also not full PSD of Z.

Here is an explicit matrix-only distinction. In any three jump coordinates
take diagonal entries 1 and all off-diagonal entries -3/4, with every other
jump diagonal 1 and other off-diagonals zero; take C=I_2 and R=0. Every
two-jump principal matrix is positive definite, but the vector with these
three jumps equal to 1 has quadratic value 3-9/2=-3/2. This exhibits the
three-jump correlation absent from A_2. It does NOT assert that this matrix
is realized by a nonnegative interpolation array for a particular h.

## 3. Quantitative budget for actual optimum-source edges

Set mu_i=lambda_(i,star), nu_i=lambda_(star,i), and nu=sum_i nu_i.
Summing (1) gives sum_i mu_i=2+nu. On the constant-gradient subspace
g_i=b, direct expansion gives

 C = [ q                -(2+nu)/2 ]
     [ -(2+nu)/2        1+2S+sum_i(1+P_i)nu_i ].          (6)

For the lower-right coefficient, finite edges contribute
sum_i P_i(out_i^finite-in_i^finite)
=2S-sum_i P_i mu_i+sum_i P_i nu_i. The finite-to-star position terms
add back sum_i P_i mu_i; the optimum-edge norm terms add 1+nu. The x_0
coupling is -(sum_i mu_i)<x_0,b>. These are exactly (6).

At the proposed q=1/M, positivity of C is equivalent to

 sum_i (S-P_i)nu_i + (M/4)nu^2 <= S.                     (7)

Indeed its determinant is
1-1/M-sum_i(S-P_i)nu_i/M-nu^2/4, and its first diagonal is positive.
In particular nu<=2sqrt(S/M), with a stricter penalty on early
optimum-source mass. This uses the actual optimum edges, not a choice to
delete them. The budget alone does not prove infeasibility, since nu=0
remains allowed.

## 4. The legal primal cone represented by the collection

Let V_(k,l) be the subspace of real coordinate lists
(X,G_0,...,G_n) in which G is constant on the three blocks (3), while X is
free. Define the cone

 K_2=sum_(1<=k<l<=n) { positive semidefinite matrices with range in V_(k,l) }.
                                                                    (8)

Equivalently, K_2 consists of finite sums vv^T where each scalar gradient
list in v has at most two chronological jumps. This follows by diagonalizing
each positive semidefinite summand. Conversely each such vv^T lies in one
of the summands, after inserting an unused cut if necessary.

Thus G belongs to K_2 if and only if it has a Gram realization in a finite
Euclidean space with an orthonormal coordinate system in which every
coordinate of (g_0,...,g_n) changes at most twice. Different coordinates may
use different cuts. The x_0 coordinate in each of these directions is free.
This is substantially more flexible than a whole vector gradient with only
two jumps: many cut patterns coexist in a single trajectory.

The cone is closed. If G_r converges and G_r=sum_a G_(r,a) is a decomposition
over the finitely many summands of (8), each summand is PSD and has trace at
most trace(G_r). In fixed finite dimension every PSD matrix has norm bounded
by its trace. Pass to a common subsequence on which all summands converge;
their ranges remain in their closed subspaces and their limits are PSD.
Their sum is the limit of G_r and belongs to K_2.

The cone is full dimensional in the space of symmetric (n+2)-matrices. In
jump coordinates every pair of coordinates occurs in one allowed block
{x_0,b,d_k,d_l}. Therefore the linear map from the direct sum of the
symmetric block spaces onto the ambient symmetric space is surjective.
It has a linear right inverse. Starting from identity matrices on all these
blocks, sufficiently small ambient perturbations can be lifted by this
right inverse while every block remains positive definite. The sum of the
embedded identities is consequently an interior point of K_2.

For n>=3 this is a PROPER subcone of the full PSD cone. Choose v with three
nonzero jumps. If vv^T=sum_a G_a with all G_a PSD, then every vector orthogonal
to v has zero quadratic value in each G_a, so Range(G_a) is contained in
span(v). Every nonzero summand is therefore a positive multiple of vv^T.
Such a summand cannot be supported on an allowed two-jump subspace. Hence
vv^T is not in K_2. This is a cone statement, not a claim that the particular
v is a legal GD transcript.

Finally, by (8), a matrix has nonnegative pairing with every G in K_2 if and
only if every restriction (3) is PSD. Thus (5) is exactly the dual-cone
condition K_2^*, with the original array flows imposed separately.

## 5. Exact attained equality on the actual positive-step family

Assume now h_i>1 for every i<n, as holds for every critical H_m below. Let
w_2(h) be the maximum of 2f_n over G in K_2, G_(x0,x0)<=1, and every original
ordered constraint Q_ij<=0 including the optimum. Then

 w_2(h) = min { q : some common lambda>=0 satisfies (1) and A_2 at q }.
                                                                    (9)

Both extrema are attained. The left side is an actual legal smooth-convex
GD performance over the coordinate class described above, not an aggregate
of independently chosen functions. In particular w_2(h)<=W_n(h).

Here is a proof including strict feasibility rather than an assumed generic
strong-duality theorem.

First construct a strict interpolation point within K_2. Put

 kappa=min(1,min_i(h_i-1))/4 >0,
 r=kappa/[2(kappa+1)], a_i=r^i,
 g_i=sqrt(a_i)e_i, f_i=(kappa+1/2)a_i,
 x_0=(kappa+2)sum_(i=0)^n sqrt(a_i)e_i+e_extra,             (10)

where the displayed coordinate vectors are orthonormal. For i<j, write
delta_i=f_i-a_i/2=kappa a_i. Direct substitution of orthogonality into the
two finite interpolation constraints shows they are strict exactly when

                   a_j < delta_i-delta_j < (h_i-1)a_i.   (11)

For the lower inequality use a_j/a_i<=r and
kappa(1-r)-r=kappa/2>0. For the upper use
delta_i-delta_j<kappa a_i<(h_i-1)a_i. The optimum residuals are
Q_(i,star)=-a_i and Q_(star,i)=-kappa a_i. Thus ALL ordered residuals are
strict. The extra coordinate makes the full Gram matrix positive definite.
Each gradient coordinate in (10) is supported on one query, hence has at
most two jumps; the extra coordinate has zero gradients. The Gram matrix
lies in K_2. Scale all vectors and the square roots of all values by one
small positive number to make the radius inequality strict as well.

This point may be on the boundary of K_2. Add a sufficiently small positive
multiple of the interior point constructed in Section 4 to its Gram matrix,
holding the values fixed. Finitely many strict linear inequalities remain
strict for small enough perturbations, including the radius. A point of a
convex cone plus an interior point lies in its interior: translate a small
ball in the cone by the cone point. This gives full conic strict feasibility.

The primal feasible set is compact. Every feasible Gram matrix is a genuine

f_i=t-(P_i+1/2)t^2. Finite-pair and finite-to-star residuals vanish, while

array feasibility in (9).

For a schedule a of sum A-1, define the intrinsic polynomial

 V_a=2sum_i a_i(f_i-f_end)+sum_i a_i(1-a_i)||g_i||^2
                                      -(A-1)A||g_end||^2.

Take two identical step lists of capacity A, separated by a physical bridge
1+r, and put t=r/A, T=(2+t)A. Let p be the bridge gradient, z the final
gradient, and H the weighted sum of gradients at the right-child steps.
Set W=H+z, and use right-child indices j in

 G=sum_j a_j Q_(j,p)+Q_(z,p),
 J=sum_j a_j Q_(j,z),

 jcoef=2+6t+2t^2, delta=2-(1+t)^2.

                                      +delta||W-Ap||^2.  (12)

actual positions gives

                  +[(A-r)/2-r^2]||p||^2+(A+r)||z||^2/2,

                   k=2^(m-1), l=3*2^(m-2).             (16)

                             +delta_(m-2)V^2/U^2 }||v0||^2
      < -8 M_m^2/(25m) ||v0||^2.                       (18)

For any 0<alpha<=1/S with S=M_m-1, multiply the intrinsic array by alpha,
add lambda_(i,star)=2alpha h_i for i<n, add

The vector (17) is not a legal adversary: it is a negative test direction
for this particular coefficient family. Only a proof excluding EVERY
nonnegative common array, together with (9), would produce the claimed
legal lower obstruction. No such exclusion has been established here.

## 7. Remaining decision and next interface

The task's central dichotomy remains open. Section 5 converts it exactly to
an attained legal performance problem on a specified proper Gram cone;
Section 6 rejects an explicit scalable candidate at every q. Neither gives
the common feasible-array formula or the collection-wide lower bound at
1/M_m that the assignment requests.

Adding all four-interval partitions would test every three-jump principal
block in the common matrix (4). It adds the determinant/correlation excluded
by the explicit example after (5), without yet reverting to arbitrary
singleton PEP. This names the new constraint precisely; it is not a claim
that those extra partitions are sufficient for the quantitative target.
The exact all-schedule F/G comparison and the original target are unchanged.

# One shared array for all chronological three-block tests

Status: self-contained candidate, **not verifier accepted**. This continuation
uses no optimization, new launch, installation, or fact_submit. The accepted
dependencies are `1252b8823bb5a290`, for smooth-convex interpolation and the
original finite full-objective formulation, and `0e7e78056dc6258c` only for
the explicit orthogonal-subclass limit in Section8. Every new statement below is
proved within this document. In particular an earlier unverified cut identity
or recursive identity is not a correctness premise.

The requested decision at q=1/M_m is NOT obtained: no feasible common array,
and no infeasibility proof for the entire collection, is asserted. What is
obtained is an exact attained legal-primal interpretation of the collection,
its common two-jump matrix, a quantitative optimum-source budget, and a
quantitative rejection of one explicitly constructed scalable common array
family by two cuts already in the collection.

## 1. Exact collection and notation

Let n>=2, h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) have nonnegative finite entries, and put
S=sum h_i, M=1+S, P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, including P_n=S. Normalize L=1 and
x_star=g_star=f_star=0. The original independent formal vectors are
(x_0,g_0,...,g_n); x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t. For distinct sample indices
in I={star,0,...,n}, write

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Choose ONE finite nonnegative array lambda_ij with finite-node flow

 sum_j lambda_ij-sum_j lambda_ji=2*1_(i=n).                 (1)

Its value-free quadratic polynomial is

 C_lambda=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.        (2)

For every 1<=k<l<=n, require (2) to be nonnegative whenever

 g_i=u for i<k, g_i=v for k<=i<l, g_i=w for i>=l,         (3)

with x_0,u,v,w independent arbitrary formal vectors. The same array is used
for every (k,l). This is the collection A_2. One-block and two-block tests
are included by equality of block values. All the earlier queried-j/tail
tests are included: for j>0 use k=j,l=j+1,u=0; for j=0 use a two-block
specialization. No position moment, optimum edge, or initial coordinate is
discarded in (2).

## 2. One common matrix, with all singular cases

Introduce chronological jumps d_k=g_k-g_(k-1), 1<=k<=n, and b=g_0. Then
g_i=b+sum_(k<=i)d_k. This is an invertible linear coordinate change. Write
the matrix of (2) in coordinates (x_0,b,d_1,...,d_n) as

              [ C       R ]
 A_lambda =   [ R^T     T ],                              (4)

where C is 2 by 2, r_k is column k of R, and T is n by n. A restriction
(3) is EXACTLY the principal block of (4) on x_0,b,d_k,d_l. Thus the entire
collection is equivalent to

 C>=0;
 r_k in Range(C) for every k;
 Z_kk>=0 and Z_kl^2<=Z_kk Z_ll for every k<l,              (5)
 Z_kl=T_kl-r_k^T C^+ r_l.

Here C^+ inverts positive eigenvalues and vanishes on Ker(C). To prove the
singular statement, diagonalize C. A nonzero component of any r_k in its
kernel makes the corresponding quadratic unbounded below in a free base
variable. Once every such component vanishes, complete the squares in the
positive base coordinates. The remaining two-variable quadratic has matrix
[[Z_kk,Z_kl],[Z_kl,Z_ll]], whose PSD criterion is exactly (5). This proves
both implications, including zero diagonal entries and C=0.

There are n(n-1)/2 coupled pair tests of ONE residual matrix Z. This is not
independent per-partition feasibility. It is also not full PSD of Z.

Here is an explicit matrix-only distinction. In any three jump coordinates
take diagonal entries 1 and all off-diagonal entries -3/4, with every other
jump diagonal 1 and other off-diagonals zero; take C=I_2 and R=0. Every
two-jump principal matrix is positive definite, but the vector with these
three jumps equal to 1 has quadratic value 3-9/2=-3/2. This exhibits the
three-jump correlation absent from A_2. It does NOT assert that this matrix
is realized by a nonnegative interpolation array for a particular h.

## 3. Quantitative budget for actual optimum-source edges

Set mu_i=lambda_(i,star), nu_i=lambda_(star,i), and nu=sum_i nu_i.
Summing (1) gives sum_i mu_i=2+nu. On the constant-gradient subspace
g_i=b, direct expansion gives

 C = [ q                -(2+nu)/2 ]
     [ -(2+nu)/2        1+2S+sum_i(1+P_i)nu_i ].          (6)

For the lower-right coefficient, finite edges contribute
sum_i P_i(out_i^finite-in_i^finite)
=2S-sum_i P_i mu_i+sum_i P_i nu_i. The finite-to-star position terms
add back sum_i P_i mu_i; the optimum-edge norm terms add 1+nu. The x_0
coupling is -(sum_i mu_i)<x_0,b>. These are exactly (6).

At the proposed q=1/M, positivity of C is equivalent to

 sum_i (S-P_i)nu_i + (M/4)nu^2 <= S.                     (7)

Indeed its determinant is
1-1/M-sum_i(S-P_i)nu_i/M-nu^2/4, and its first diagonal is positive.
In particular nu<=2sqrt(S/M), with a stricter penalty on early
optimum-source mass. This uses the actual optimum edges, not a choice to
delete them. The budget alone does not prove infeasibility, since nu=0
remains allowed.

Let V_(k,l) be the subspace of real coordinate lists
(X,G_0,...,G_n) in which G is constant on the three blocks (3), while X is
free. Define the cone

 K_2=sum_(1<=k<l<=n) { positive semidefinite matrices with range in V_(k,l) }.
                                                                    (8)

Equivalently, K_2 consists of finite sums vv^T where each scalar gradient
list in v has at most two chronological jumps. This follows by diagonalizing
each positive semidefinite summand. Conversely each such vv^T lies in one
of the summands, after inserting an unused cut if necessary.

Thus G belongs to K_2 if and only if it has a Gram realization in a finite
Euclidean space with an orthonormal coordinate system in which every
coordinate of (g_0,...,g_n) changes at most twice. Different coordinates may
use different cuts. The x_0 coordinate in each of these directions is free.
This is substantially more flexible than a whole vector gradient with only
two jumps: many cut patterns coexist in a single trajectory.

jump coordinates write a candidate Gram matrix as [[A,B],[B^T,D]], with
the first two coordinates x_0,b. It lies in K_2 if and only if it is PSD

column of V supported on at most two indices. Full PSD gives

column is in an allowed subspace, proving the claim, including singular D.

give the displayed determinant condition. Conversely insert the PSD matrix
[[z_ij,D_ij],[D_ij,z_ji]] on each pair and add the nonnegative leftover
diagonal entries. The resulting sum is exactly D. This does not require
that the two-jump coordinate components be individually interpolable:
the full summed Gram matrix and the common function values obey the
interpolation constraints together.

The cone is closed. If G_r converges and G_r=sum_a G_(r,a) is a decomposition
over the finitely many summands of (8), each summand is PSD and has trace at
most trace(G_r). In fixed finite dimension every PSD matrix has norm bounded
by its trace. Pass to a common subsequence on which all summands converge;
their ranges remain in their closed subspaces and their limits are PSD.
Their sum is the limit of G_r and belongs to K_2.

The cone is full dimensional in the space of symmetric (n+2)-matrices. In
jump coordinates every pair of coordinates occurs in one allowed block
{x_0,b,d_k,d_l}. Therefore the linear map from the direct sum of the
symmetric block spaces onto the ambient symmetric space is surjective.
It has a linear right inverse. Starting from identity matrices on all these
blocks, sufficiently small ambient perturbations can be lifted by this
right inverse while every block remains positive definite. The sum of the
embedded identities is consequently an interior point of K_2.

For n>=3 this is a PROPER subcone of the full PSD cone. Choose v with three
nonzero jumps. If vv^T=sum_a G_a with all G_a PSD, then every vector orthogonal
to v has zero quadratic value in each G_a, so Range(G_a) is contained in
span(v). Every nonzero summand is therefore a positive multiple of vv^T.
Such a summand cannot be supported on an allowed two-jump subspace. Hence
vv^T is not in K_2. This is a cone statement, not a claim that the particular
v is a legal GD transcript.

only if every restriction (3) is PSD. Thus (5) is exactly the dual-cone
condition K_2^*, with the original array flows imposed separately.

 w_2(h) = min { q : some common lambda>=0 satisfies (1) and A_2 at q }.

value-free intrinsic remainders, the joined remainder is exactly

 R_join=R_left+kR_right+delta||W-Ap||^2.                  (13)

Now fix m>=128 and, for this WHOLE horizon, set

 sigma=1+sqrt(2), c=sigma(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
 H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j),
 r_j=a c^j, M_j=1+sum H_j,
 t_j=r_j/M_j, delta_j=2-(1+t_j)^2.                       (14)

The parameters are not recomputed inside the recursion. Counting gives

 M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j,
 A_mass=a/(c-2),
 t_j=(c-2)/[1+B(2/c)^j],
 B=(1-A_mass)/A_mass
   =[(sigma^2+2)m+sigma^2]/[m(m-1)].                    (15)

For m>=128, 0<B<8/m, 2/c<5/6 and 0<c-2<1/2. The first estimate follows
from sigma^2=3+2sqrt(2)<35/6 and m>83; the others follow from
12/5<sigma<17/7 and m>=128. For j=m-2 or m-1, we have j>=12 and
(2/c)^j<(5/6)^12<1/8. Using 1/(1+x)>=1-x in (15) gives

 t_j>(c-2)-(c-2)/m
     =(sigma-2)+[sigma-(c-2)]/m
     >(sigma-2)+1/m.

Therefore delta_j<-2/m for these two levels.

Use the actual three-block cuts

                   k=2^(m-1), l=3*2^(m-2).             (16)

Write U=M_(m-1), V=M_(m-2), r=r_(m-1), s=r_(m-2).
Set all gradients on the three blocks to respectively

        u0=-(V+s)/(U+r) v0,       v0,       0,           (17)

where v0 is any nonzero scalar or vector. The full step displacement is
D=sum h_i g_i=(U+r)u0+(V+s)v0=0, and g_n=0. All node squares in (13)
vanish except those at the root and its right child: every smaller node
has constant gradients. Thus

 R_Hm=M_m^2 { delta_(m-1)(V+s)^2/(U+r)^2
                             +delta_(m-2)V^2/U^2 }||v0||^2
      < -8 M_m^2/(25m) ||v0||^2.                       (18)

For the last inequality use both negative deltas and U/V=2+t_(m-2)<5/2.

The obstruction survives the whole following objective conversion family.
For any 0<alpha<=1/S with S=M_m-1, multiply the intrinsic array by alpha,
add lambda_(i,star)=2alpha h_i for i<n, add
lambda_(n,star)=2beta with beta=1-alpha S>=0, and take ANY q. Every
coefficient is nonnegative and (1) holds. Direct expansion gives

 C_lambda=q||x_0||^2-2<x_0,alpha D+beta g_n>
          +alpha||D||^2+2beta<D,g_n>
          +(alpha S M_m+beta)||g_n||^2+alpha R_Hm.       (19)

To check (19), expand 2sum h_i Q_(i,star)-V_h as
||D||^2-2<x_0,D>+2S f_n+S M_m||g_n||^2, and then add 2beta Q_(n,star).
The values cancel because alpha S+beta=1. On (17), set x_0=0; then
(19)=alpha R_Hm<0 independently of q. In particular this array does NOT
pass A_2 at q=1/M_m. Its failure is quantitative and occurs in the already
requested collection, with actual moments and full original flows.

The vector (17) is not a legal adversary: it is a negative test direction
for this particular coefficient family. Only a proof excluding EVERY
nonnegative common array, together with (9), would produce the claimed
legal lower obstruction. No such exclusion has been established here.

## 7. Remaining decision and next interface

The task's central dichotomy remains open. Section 5 converts it exactly to
an attained legal performance problem on a specified proper Gram cone;
Section 6 rejects an explicit scalable candidate at every q. Neither gives
the common feasible-array formula or the collection-wide lower bound at
1/M_m that the assignment requests.

Adding all four-interval partitions would test every three-jump principal
block in the common matrix (4). It adds the determinant/correlation excluded
by the explicit example after (5), without yet reverting to arbitrary
singleton PEP. This names the new constraint precisely; it is not a claim
that those extra partitions are sufficient for the quantitative target.
The exact all-schedule F/G comparison and the original target are unchanged.

## 8. General strict feasibility: equality (9) extends to every h>=0

The restriction h_i>1 in Section5 can be removed. Define the collection for
compressed horizons n<=2 to contain the entire original formal space; this
is exactly the condition of at most two chronological jumps at those horizons.
With that convention, (9), primal attainment and common-array attainment hold
for EVERY finite nonnegative schedule. Here is an explicit proof.

First assume every h_i>0 and n>=1. Write h_min=min_i h_i, S=sum h_i>0, and
choose the following strictly positive scalar:

 theta=min{1/4, 1/(4S), min(h_min^2,1)/[64S^2(S+1)]}.     (20)

Use the scalar quadratic with curvature theta as a starting transcript:

 X_i=product_(t<i)(1-theta h_t),
 gamma_i=theta X_i, f_i=theta X_i^2/2, X_0=1.

All X_i lie in [1/2,1]. Indeed every factor is positive, and induction gives
product_(t<i)(1-theta h_t)>=1-theta P_i>=3/4. The weaker 1/2 bound suffices.
The scalar increments are

 d_i=gamma_i-gamma_(i-1)=-theta^2 h_(i-1) X_(i-1)<0,
 eta_i=|d_i|sum_(j!=i)|d_j|, 1<=i<=n.                    (21)

Enlarge the space to have orthonormal coordinates e_0,e_1,...,e_n and set

 x_0=e_0,
 g_i=gamma_i e_0+sum_(k<=i)sqrt(eta_k)e_k,
 x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t.                              (22)

Keep the scalar values f_i unchanged. The Gram matrix is PSD because the
vectors are explicit. Its incremental Gram matrix is

                   D=d d^T+diag(eta_1,...,eta_n).        (23)

This matrix has an explicit two-index PSD decomposition: on each pair i<j
insert [[|d_i d_j|,d_i d_j],[d_i d_j,|d_i d_j|]], and on coordinate i
insert the remaining singleton d_i^2. Thus the Gram matrix of (22) lies
in K_2 by the exact marginal criterion in Section4. That criterion was
proved directly there and is part of this same candidate proof.

Every original interpolation residual remains STRICTLY negative. To check
it quantitatively, the scalar quadratic has, for finite i!=j,

 Q_ij^base=-theta(1-theta)(X_i-X_j)^2/2.

For i<j,
X_i-X_j=theta sum_(i<=t<j) h_t X_t
        >=theta(P_j-P_i)/2>=theta h_min/2.
Since theta<=1/4, it follows that

 Q_ij^base<=-theta^3 h_min^2/16.

Both optimum residuals of this quadratic satisfy
Q_(i,star)^base=Q_(star,i)^base
=-theta(1-theta)X_i^2/2<=-theta/16.

On the added coordinates, sum eta_i<=theta^4 S^2. Consequently each added
gradient has norm at most theta^2 S, and each added position has norm at
most theta^2 S^2. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the absolute added contribution
to any finite or optimum interpolation residual by

                         2theta^4 S^2(S+1).             (24)

For finite pairs, (20) makes (24) at most
theta^3 h_min^2/32. For optimum pairs it is at most theta/32: use theta<=1
and 2theta^3 S^2(S+1)<=2theta S^2(S+1)<=1/32. These estimates leave every
residual strictly negative, with the original common values f_i. The
coordinate components need not be individually legal; their joint residuals
have just been checked in full.

Scale the vectors and values to give strict radius, and add a sufficiently
small interior K_2 Gram matrix as in Section5. This supplies the missing
strict feasible point for every positive schedule, however small its steps.
The compactness and explicit separation proof in Section5 now proves (9)
and both attainments for every positive schedule.

For zero steps, compress to the chronological positive-step indices i_0,
...,i_(p-1), retaining original n as the terminal representative. The
interpolation constraints at two identical positions force identical
gradients, since their summed residual is ||g_i-g_j||^2; the individual
residuals then force identical values. Deleting such repetitions preserves
the coordinate property of at most two jumps, and duplicating them in an
existing Gram realization also preserves it. Hence w_2 for the original
and compressed schedules is the same, and primal attainment lifts.

Take an attained common array for the positive compression and embed its
coefficients on the original representative indices, setting all other
coefficients zero. Every original value flow is correct. Each embedded Q
has precisely its compressed polynomial after selecting those gradients,
because all omitted steps have coefficient zero. An original two-jump
gradient list remains a two-jump list on the representative subsequence.
The embedded array consequently passes every original test and attains the
same q. This argument takes place on the original independent formal
gradient space and does not impose duplicate-gradient identities in the
dual. If there are no positive steps, w_2=1 and lambda_(n,star)=2 supplies
the full identity ||x_0-g_n||^2 at q=1.

The explicit orthogonal point (10) is a strict-feasibility device, not a
quantitative lower witness at the requested scale. More generally, accepted
fact `0e7e78056dc6258c` bounds EVERY legal orthogonal-gradient trajectory by
2/n^2. On the actual critical family, M_m<=c^m, n=2^m-1 and c<5/2 for
m>=128. Hence M_m times this whole subclass's normalized error is at most
2c^m/(2^m-1)^2, which tends to zero. A useful legal K_2 obstruction must
use correlations; strict feasibility alone cannot establish it.

claim: Complete all-depth FULL Silver calibration, plus two scoped whole-array continuation obstructions. The actual AP array gives q=2/(1+sqrt(4M^2-3)) and its exact rank-one remainder; a separately derived sharp full array gives q=1/(2M-1). evidence:
# Full Silver calibration and whole-array continuation tests

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof draft. No fact_submit or numerical optimization.
This does not establish the original exact profile converse or a separation.
Every mathematical assertion below is proved in this draft; no unverified
shared finding is used as a correctness premise. The accepted interpolation
and full-certificate framework is fact `1252b8823bb5a290`.

The source starting point is Altschuler--Parrilo, *Acceleration by Stepsize
Hedging II: Silver Stepsize Schedule for Smooth Convex Optimization*,
arXiv:2309.16530 (2023), equations (3.1)--(3.9), Theorem 3.4 and its proof.
Its C>=0 convention is C_ij=-2Q_ji in the present notation. The exact local
PDF and extracted text were read. We reconstruct the needed identities,
including the complete objective and remainder, instead of importing a
distance-only statement. The generic skew-completion idea has an earlier
intrinsic-potential analogue in shared candidate666b5b9b14038a0f; the new
tests here concern actual full objective certificates and the assigned path.

## 1. Exact coefficients at every depth

Set rho=1+sqrt(2), n_j=2^j-1, and define the undeformed word by

 H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+rho^(j-1),H_j).

Its mass is M_j=1+sum H_j=rho^j, since M_(j+1)=2M_j+rho^(j-1).
Normalize smoothness to1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. All formal vectors
x_0,g_0,...,g_n remain independent. Put

 x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 C_ij=-2Q_ji=2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2.

Here is one finite-node array L^(j), without optimum entries. At depth0 it
is zero. In a join let p=n_j, q=2n_j+1, M=rho^j, d=M/rho, and b=1+d.
Embed L^(j) on the left and rho^2 L^(j) on the right. Let right weights
w_i=h_i for p<i<q and w_q=1. For every p<i<=q add rho w_i to L_(p,i)
and to L_(q,i), omitting the diagonal entry L_(q,q). Add M to L_(q,p).
All coefficients are explicitly nonnegative. Repeated contributions add.

Define

 J_j=2sum_(i<n_j)h_i(f_i-f_(n_j))
                       +sum_(i<n_j)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2.

The full finite identity is

 J_j=sum_(i!=k)L^(j)_ik C_ik+M_j(M_j-1)||g_(n_j)||^2.       (1)

Here is an induction with every nontrivial cancellation displayed. It is
zero=zero at j=0. In a join write g=g_p, e=g_q,
P=sum_(p<i<q)h_i g_i, W=P+e, and S=M-1. The quadratic parts of the two
weighted fans, before multiplication by rho, are respectively

 sum_i w_i C_(p,i): -M||g||^2-2d<g,W>-||W||^2
                                      +sum_right h_i(h_i-1)||g_i||^2,
 sum_i w_i C_(q,i):  ||W||^2-M||e||^2
                                      +sum_right h_i(h_i-1)||g_i||^2.

The quadratic part of C_(q,p) is
(1+2d)||g||^2-||e||^2+2<g,W>.
These formulas follow by expanding the definitions and using
2sum_i<h_i g_i,sum_(p<t<i)h_t g_t>=||P||^2-sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2.
Thus the added fans and M C_(q,p) have zero g,W cross coefficient
because M=rho d. Their g and e diagonal coefficients are
M(1+2d-rho) and -(rho+1)M. Their interior diagonal coefficients are
2rho h_i(h_i-1), exactly the difference between the parent and
rho^2 times the right child. Their value coefficients are

 f_p: 2M(rho-1)=2(S+b),
 f_q: 2rho(M-2)+2M=2[(rho^2-2)S-b],
 f_i, p<i<q: -4rho h_i=2(1-rho^2)h_i.

They therefore equal all value coefficients of J_(j+1)-J_left-rho^2 J_right.
After using both child identities, the g diagonal left over is

 M(M-1)-d(1+d)-M(1+2d-rho)=0,

and the e diagonal is
rho^2 M(M-1)+(rho+1)M=(rho M)(rho M-1).
This proves (1) at every depth.

Write M=M_m, S=M-1, v=2M-1. A sharp full objective array in the current
Q convention is

 Lambda_ik=2L^(m)_ki/v for finite i!=k,
 Lambda_(i,star)=2h_i/v for i<n,
 Lambda_(n,star)=2M/v,
 Lambda_(star,i)=0 for all finite i.

Its COMPLETE certificate, not just a primitive consequence, is

 (1/v)||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum Lambda_ik Q_ik
                         =||x_n-Mg_n||^2/v.                 (2)

To check this multiply by v and use (1). The query optimum entries give
2sum h_i f_i-2sum h_i<g_i,x_i>+sum h_i||g_i||^2. The terminal optimum
entry gives2M f_n-2M<g_n,x_n>+M||g_n||^2. The finite array gives
-J_m+M(M-1)||g_n||^2. All values cancel because v=M+S. The remaining
query terms telescope by
||x_0||^2-2sum h_i<g_i,x_i>+sum h_i^2||g_i||^2=||x_n||^2.
The terminal terms complete the displayed square. This verifies every
original formal-space coefficient. The scalar Huber function with slope
1/v, quadratic core radius1/v, and x_0=1 attains2f_n=1/v: its iterates
are x_i=1-(sum_(t<i)h_t)/v>=M/v>1/v. Thus (2) is tight.

The actual canonical AP objective certificate is different. Define

 t=(1+sqrt(4M^2-3))/2, so t^2-t+1=M^2.

In the C convention its finite coefficients are the SAME L^(m), and its
optimum entries are C_(star,i):h_i for i<n, C_(star,n):t,
C_(n,star):S, with the other C_(i,star) coefficients zero. In Q notation,

 Lambda_ik=2L^(m)_ki/t,
 Lambda_(i,star)=2h_i/t (i<n), Lambda_(n,star)=2,
 Lambda_(star,n)=2S/t, Lambda_(star,i)=0 (i<n).

All are nonnegative, and the exact full identity is

 (1/t)||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum Lambda_ik Q_ik
                         =||x_n-tg_n||^2/t.                 (3)

Indeed (1) and the same norm telescope give the C sum
||x_0||^2-||x_n||^2+2t<x_n,g_n>-2t f_n
                         -(M^2+t-1)||g_n||^2.
Since M^2+t-1=t^2 this is the required identity. The source paper uses
f_n<=r_m||x_0||^2 with r_m=1/(2t); our normalized objective coefficient
is 2r_m=1/t. No factor2 is suppressed.

Both (2) and (3) have rank-one complete remainder. Their kernels are,
respectively, x_0=sum h_i g_i+M g_n and x_0=sum h_i g_i+t g_n. The
kernel dimension is n+1 in scalar formal coordinates. These are actual
all-depth baseline arrays, with different objective constants and optimum
incidence; they must not be identified with one another.

## 2. Full coordinates and exact singular conditions

Let N=n+1, e the vector of N ones, e_n the last coordinate, and
V=I+T with T_it=h_t for t<i. For an arbitrary real N by N array A put

 b=Ae, a=A^T e-2e_n,
 G=sym(AV)-e_n e_n^T, sym(D)=(D+D^T)/2.

The actual multipliers are Lambda_ij=-A_ij (i!=j), Lambda_(i,star)=b_i,
Lambda_(star,i)=a_i. All actual signs and flows hold precisely when

 A_ij<=0 (i!=j), b>=0, a>=0.                              (4)

Expanding Q, or first canceling its value coefficients by these flows,
gives the complete matrix

 Mcert(q,A,h)=[[q,-b^T/2],[-b/2,G]].                       (5)

At either baseline put w0=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),tau), where tau=M or t,
and q0=1/v or1/t, as appropriate. Make the invertible fixed-coordinate
substitution x_0=z+w0^T g. At any nearby parameters the matrix becomes

 [[q,r^T],[r,D]],
 r=q w0-b/2,
 D=G+q w0w0^T-(w0b^T+bw0^T)/2.

For q>0 its PSD condition is EXACTLY

                    D-r r^T/q >=0.                     (6)

At the baseline r=D=0. If q,A,h are analytic in s, write
r=s r1+s^2 r2+..., D=s D1+s^2 D2+.... Then D1>=0 is necessary, but
on ker D1 one also needs D2-r1 r1^T/q0>=0. At any subsequent singular
block [[B,C],[C^T,E]], the exact conditions are B>=0,
range(C) contained in range(B), and E-C^T B^dagger C>=0. Here B^dagger
inverts B on its range and is zero on its kernel. To see the range
condition, a vector in ker B must have zero mixed product with every
other vector under a PSD form; completing squares on range B then gives
the last condition. Thus there is no license to discard mixed blocks.

At an initially zero A_ij, a one-sided feasible derivative requires
dot A_ij<=0; at an initially zero component of a or b, the corresponding
derivative must be nonnegative. Positive coefficients allow signed
variations only while their FINAL values satisfy (4).

## 3. An explicit dense rank-one transport, with no unknown PSD

Here we attempt continuation from the sharp baseline (2). The chosen
physical path is exactly the assignment, with epsilon=s/m:

 c=rho(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
 H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), j<m.

Let h be that word, M=1+sum h, v=2M-1, q=1/v, and
p=V^(-1)e. Thus p_0=1 and p_(i+1)=(1-h_i)p_i.
In a neighborhood of epsilon=0 define

 mu=1-sqrt(1-v p_n^2),
 wphys=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),M),
 delta=(mu-wphys^T p)/h_0,
 w=wphys+delta(e_0-e_1).                                (7)

This is analytic at zero, since there 1-v p_n^2=(M-1)^2/M^2>0,
and delta(0)=0. It satisfies e^T w=v and w^T p=mu. All w_i are
positive sufficiently near zero. For n=1 the second coordinate is the
terminal; the formula still applies.

Put S0=e_n e_n^T+q w w^T and define

 U=[e,p], H=U^T U,
 R=[e_n+w-2V^T e_n, q(2-mu)w-p_n e_n],
 P=U H^(-1)U^T,
 Kpart=R H^(-1)U^T-U H^(-1)R^T
                             -U H^(-1)(U^T R)H^(-1)U^T.

The two columns of U are independent because h_0>0. Directly,
U^T R is skew: its first diagonal uses sum w=v=1+2sum h, the second
uses q mu(2-mu)=p_n^2, and its mixed entries sum to zero using Vp=e.
It follows by multiplication that Kpart is skew and Kpart U=R.

At the undeformed baseline let A0 be the exact array from (2), V0 its
V, and K0=(A0 V0-V0^T A0^T)/2. Define the ACTUAL proposed full array

 K=Kpart+(I-P)K0(I-P),  A=(S0+K)V^(-1).                  (8)

There is no support deletion in (8); it generally creates dense interior
entries. It preserves A(0)=A0. Indeed every skew matrix with KU=R has
the form Kpart+(I-P)Omega(I-P), where Omega is arbitrary skew, because
the difference annihilates U on both sides. Taking Omega=K0 recovers
K0 at zero by this decomposition. Also

 Ae=2q w, A^T e=2e_n, sym(AV)=e_n e_n^T+q w w^T.

Consequently the FULL matrix (5) is identically
q[1;-w][1;-w]^T. All nullspace, mixed-block and range requirements hold
exactly. Optimum signs hold locally because w>0 and a=0. The remaining
indispensable condition is A_ij<=0 for EVERY distinct pair. It is not
implied by the identities just proved.

## 4. Exact sign failure, including all free skew repairs at three steps

For m=2 write r=sqrt(2). At epsilon=0, h=(r,2,r), M=3+2r,
v=5+4r. The baseline A0, with all entries divided by7, is

 [[6-2r, 10-8r, 0, 0],
  [-6+2r, -8+12r, 0, -6+2r],
  [0, 4-6r, 10+6r, 2-10r],
  [0, -6+2r, -10-6r, 18+8r]].

The physical derivative with respect to epsilon is
dot h=(-2/rho,-1,-2/rho). Formula (7) gives dot delta=1-4r.
Differentiating the EXPLICIT formula (8), using only product and inverse
rules, gives

 dot A_02=(-302+467r)/98,
 dot A_30=(-187+221r)/49.                               (9)

For reproducibility K0, with all entries divided by7, is

 [[0,-6+2r,10-8r,-4-r],
  [6-2r,0,-12+4r,-8-2r],
  [-10+8r,12-4r,0,-2-11r],
  [4+r,8+2r,2+11r,0]].

The values (9) can thus be checked by substituting into (7)--(8),
with d(X^(-1))=-X^(-1)(dX)X^(-1). The first value is positive, since
sqrt(2)>1 and467>302. Because A0_02=0, formula (8) makes the actual
multiplier Lambda_02=-A_02 negative for every sufficiently small positive
epsilon. This is an exact sign counterexample to this proposed transport.

More strongly, keeping the boundary weights (7), NO choice of the free
skew part can repair this derivative at depth2. At zero put

 u=(r-2,1-r,1,0)^T,
 z=(2r-3,2-2r,0,1)^T.

They span the orthogonal complement of e,p, where
p=(1,1-r,r-1,2r-3)^T. Hence all alternative skew first derivatives,
while retaining the same A0 and dot w, differ by gamma(u z^T-z u^T).
After multiplication by V0^(-1), their changes at entries02 and30 are
respectively gamma and -r gamma. Therefore every such derivative obeys

 r dot A_02+dot A_30=(40+10r)/7>0.                       (10)

Both baseline entries are zero, so both derivatives would need to be
nonpositive. Equation (10) rules this out. This test permits EVERY finite
interpolation pair and every free skew direction for the specified w.
It does NOT exclude changing w differently, creating a nonzero PSD
remainder, relaxing q, or choosing another baseline certificate.

The accompanying tiny exact Q(sqrt(2)) audit checks all value flows,
complete matrices and derivatives at one and three steps. It is an
arithmetic audit, not a solver and not a correctness authority; the
displayed exact matrices and formulas are the mathematical evidence.

## 5. All-depth stiffness of any rank-one continuation

There is a separate quantitative necessity that does not fix the two-weight
choice (7) or the free skew part. It describes rank-one continuation at the
sharp Huber rate, not arbitrary PSD continuations.

At depth m let N=2^m and M0=rho^m. For an integer i let pop(i) be the
number of ones in its binary expansion. On the undeformed Silver word,

 p_i=(-1)^i rho^(-pop(i)),
 dot p_i=-(i+pop(i))p_i,                                (11)

where dots denote derivatives in epsilon=s/m at zero. To verify this,
sum_(t=1)^i nu_2(t)=i-pop(i): summing floor(i/2^k) over k gives the
left side and summing the binary expansion gives the right side.
The product of h_t-1 therefore has exponent -pop(i). Under the physical
path the logarithmic derivative of h_t-1 is nu_2(t+1)-2, whose sum is
-i-pop(i). This proves (11), including p_n=-1/M0 and
dot p_n=(N+m-1)/M0.

Let D=rho^2+2=2rho+3. The physical mass has exact formula

 M(epsilon)=A(epsilon)c^m+(1-A(epsilon))2^m,
 A(epsilon)=a/(c-2).

Here A(0)=1, dot A(0)=-D, and hence

                    dot M=M0(m-D)+D N.                (12)

Suppose ANY differentiable full certificate, with every pair available,
has q=1/(2M(epsilon)-1), a rank-one remainder q||x_0-w^Tg||^2, and
starts at (2). No multiplier formula or support pattern is assumed.
On the actual full-curvature quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, all Q_ij are zero,
x_0=1 and g_i=p_i. Thus

 q(1-w^T p)^2=q-p_n^2.

The baseline selects the analytic minus branch, so w^T p=mu in (7).
Let dot wphys=(dot h_0,...,dot h_(n-1),dot M), and let
zeta=dot w-dot wphys. Differentiating the preceding scalar equality gives

 p^T zeta=(dot M-M0(N+m-1))/(M0-1)=:Delta_m.             (13)

For detail, dot mu=[dot M-(2M0-1)(N+m-1)]/[M0(M0-1)].
Also wphys^T p=1+(M-1)p_n, whose derivative is
-dot M/M0+(M0-1)(N+m-1)/M0. Subtracting gives (13).

Tightness at q=1/(2M-1) additionally forces every optimum-source
multiplier to vanish: on the attaining Huber trajectory every Q_(star,i)
is strictly negative, while all finite Q and all Q_(i,star) are zero.
The PSD certificate must have zero value there, so complementarity gives
this assertion. Then A^T e=2e_n and sum w=2M-1, whence sum zeta=0.
Since max_i p_i=1 and min_i p_i=-1/rho, this also yields

 sum_i |zeta_i| >=sqrt(2)|Delta_m|.                    (14)

Indeed subtract the midpoint of the range of p before applying the
triangle inequality, and use sum zeta=0. The two-weight derivative (7)
attains (14), so its failure in Section4 is not caused by excessive
total redistribution in this particular norm.

More significantly, put w0=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),M0). Since all h_i>1,
h_i|p_i|=|p_i|+|p_(i+1)|. Also
sum_(i=0)^n |p_i|=(1+1/rho)^m=(sqrt(2))^m. Therefore

 sum_i (w0)_i |p_i|=2(sqrt(2))^m-1/M0.

It follows that every such rank-one continuation satisfies

 max_i |zeta_i|/(w0)_i
       >= |Delta_m|/[2(sqrt(2))^m-1/M0].               (15)

By (12), Delta_m/N tends to -1 as m tends to infinity. Consequently,
in the original s parameter the right side of (15) is asymptotic to

                         (sqrt(2))^m/(2m).            (16)

Thus no horizon-uniform bound on the componentwise relative FIRST
derivative of this rank-one boundary vector is possible, even with the
complete coefficient array available. Natural physical weights have
bounded relative s derivatives at zero, so the same divergence cannot
be hidden by merely counting their physical variation.

This is NOT a bound on total finite-path change: an analytic path may
have a very thin boundary layer. It is NOT an obstruction to PSD
remainders of higher rank. Such a remainder can absorb the quadratic
probe, so (13) need no longer hold as an equality.

The same phenomenon occurs at the actual canonical source baseline (3).
Keep q(epsilon)=1/t(epsilon), t^2-t+1=M(epsilon)^2, and assume the
complete remainder remains rank one starting at (3). Set
wphys=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),t). The quadratic calibration again forces
w^T p=1-sqrt(1-t p_n^2). Differentiation gives

 p^T(dot w-dot wphys)
                   =(dot M-M0(N+m-1))/(t0-1),         (17)

where t0=(1+sqrt(4M0^2-3))/2. To check, use
dot t=2M0 dot M/(2t0-1),
sqrt(1-t0/M0^2)=(t0-1)/M0,
and (t0-1)^2+t0=M0^2. The weighted denominator is now
2(sqrt(2))^m-1+(t0-1)/M0, so the same asymptotic lower bound (16)
holds. This calculation allows both directions of optimum incidence;
it uses only the rank-one full remainder and the specified rate.

## 6. What remains open

The canonical full baseline has now been calibrated at every depth, and
the sharper full baseline is separately explicit. The dense proposal
(7)--(8) solves its full PSD and all mixed-block conditions identically,
but its ACTUAL coefficient signs fail. Even arbitrary free skew changes
cannot fix its prescribed boundary-weight derivative at three steps.
Any rank-one continuation at either displayed rate also has the growing
relative-derivative requirement (16). These are scoped obstructions,
not a claim that every optimal certificate has either shape.

The assignment permits a higher-rank PSD remainder, different boundary
weights, nonzero optimum sources, and a relaxed q. Those freedoms are
not excluded here. To obtain a separation, one must control the FINAL
signs and the exact finite-path Schur remainder uniformly in m, with
limsup q_m M_m<e/rho at s=1 (or the corresponding strict fixed-s gap).
Neither a derivative, the rank-one scalar moment, nor the real-skew
parameterization supplies that remaining estimate. No such certificate
or unrestricted obstruction has been proved in this round.

in the original s parameter the right side of (15) is asymptotic to

                         (sqrt(2))^m/(2m).            (16)

Thus no horizon-uniform bound on the componentwise relative FIRST
derivative of this rank-one boundary vector is possible, even with the
complete coefficient array available. Natural physical weights have
bounded relative s derivatives at zero, so the same divergence cannot
be hidden by merely counting their physical variation.

This is NOT a bound on total finite-path change: an analytic path may
have a very thin boundary layer. It is NOT an obstruction to PSD
remainders of higher rank. Such a remainder can absorb the quadratic
probe, so (13) need no longer hold as an equality.

The same phenomenon occurs at the actual canonical source baseline (3).
Keep q(epsilon)=1/t(epsilon), t^2-t+1=M(epsilon)^2, and assume the
complete remainder remains rank one starting at (3). Set
wphys=(h_0,...,h_(n-1),t). The quadratic calibration again forces
w^T p=1-sqrt(1-t p_n^2). Differentiation gives

 p^T(dot w-dot wphys)
                   =(dot M-M0(N+m-1))/(t0-1),         (17)

where t0=(1+sqrt(4M0^2-3))/2. To check, use
dot t=2M0 dot M/(2t0-1),
sqrt(1-t0/M0^2)=(t0-1)/M0,
and (t0-1)^2+t0=M0^2. The weighted denominator is now
2(sqrt(2))^m-1+(t0-1)/M0, so the same asymptotic lower bound (16)
holds. This calculation allows both directions of optimum incidence;
it uses only the rank-one full remainder and the specified rate.

## 6. A complete higher-rank analytic repair, with unaffordable exact cost

There is no qualitative obstruction to analytic continuation when the
objective coefficient is unrestricted. The following construction gives
an explicit full-array path from EITHER baseline, at every m>=2, with
all actual pairs and both optimum directions strictly positive for s>0.
Its objective cost is far too large. This is a quantified failed repair,
not the uniform rate conclusion requested in TASK.

Use N=2^m, n=N-1, M0=rho^m, and set

 Hmax=1+3M0, Lmax=6M0, R=(1+4Hmax)^2,
 d_i=8R^(n-i), D=diag(d_i), Qsafe=4sum_i d_i,
 eta0=1/[2N(1+n Hmax)],
 Asafe=D+eta0(NI-ee^T).

All physical h_i(s) lie below Hmax, and |h_i(s)-h_i(0)|<=Lmax s.
For the latter, differentiate
rho^(j-1)(1-s/m)(1+s/m)^(j-1), j=0,...,m-1. The j=0 derivative is
at most2/(m rho) in magnitude. For j>=1 its magnitude is at most
(j/m)rho^(j-1)(1+1/m)^(j-1)<=3M0. Both asserted bounds follow.
The bound (1+1/m)^m<3 follows by expanding the binomial and using
binom(m,k)/m^k<=1/k! and sum_(k>=0)1/k!<3.

First omit the eta0 term. The gradient block is sym(DV)-e_n e_n^T.
After congruence by D^(-1/2), its off-diagonal entries have absolute
values at most (Hmax/2)R^(-|i-j|/2). The sum of absolute off-diagonal
entries in each row is at most Hmax/(sqrt(R)-1)=1/4. Its diagonal is1,
except the terminal value1-1/8=7/8. The inequality
2|z_i z_j|<=z_i^2+z_j^2 therefore proves

 sym(DV)-e_n e_n^T >= D/4.

For every scalar z and gradient vector g, weighted Cauchy--Schwarz gives

 Qsafe z^2-z sum_i d_i g_i+g^T[sym(DV)-e_n e_n^T]g
 >=(Qsafe/2)z^2+[1/4-(sum_i d_i)/(2Qsafe)]sum_i d_i g_i^2
 >=z^2+sum_i g_i^2.

Here Qsafe=4sum d_i and min d_i=8. Thus the complete matrix before
the eta0 term is at least the identity, including its initial row.
The eta0 term has zero row and column sums, so it changes only the
gradient block by eta0 sym((NI-ee^T)V). Its norm is at most
eta0 N(1+n Hmax)=1/2: NI-ee^T has norm N, and
||V||<=1+||T||_F<=1+n Hmax. Consequently

                    Mcert(Qsafe,Asafe,h(s)) >= I/2.     (18)

Its actual finite multipliers are all eta0>0. Its optimum multipliers
are b_i=d_i and a_i=d_i-2*1_(i=n), all strictly positive. This proves
the full signs and PSD directly, without an appeal to Slater theory.

Let A0,q0 be either FULL baseline in Section1, and let
C_A=sum_(i,j)|A0_ij|, K=2 C_A N Lmax. Define

 A(s)=[A0+K s Asafe]/(1+K s),
 q(s)=[q0+K s Qsafe]/(1+K s).                            (19)

The physical h(s) stays the assigned word. The frozen baseline array
changes its full matrix by a gradient block sym(A0(T(s)-T(0))). Its
norm is at most C_A N Lmax s=K s/2. Hence

 Mcert(q0,A0,h(s))>=-(K s/2)I.

Convexly combining this with (18) proves FULL PSD of (19) at every
s in[0,1]. All final multiplier signs hold by convex combination, and
every pair is positive for s>0. The matrix and array are real analytic;
the baseline singular kernel and all mixed directions are included in
the displayed bounds. Everything is predetermined by m and s.

The exact cost explains why this does not solve the research task.
C_A>=sum b_i>=2 for either baseline, so K tends to infinity. For every
fixed s>0, the fraction K s/(1+K s) eventually exceeds1/2. Therefore

 q(s)>=Qsafe/2>=16(1+4Hmax)^(2n).                       (20)

The resulting certificate level diverges rather than being O(1/M_m).
This specific dense repair is feasible but fails the scalar comparison
by an enormous margin. It rules out interpreting singularity of the
chosen baseline as an absolute obstruction to whole-array analytic
continuation; an obstruction relevant to TASK must be quantitative.
No optimality is claimed for (19), and its cost is not a lower bound on
other higher-rank repairs.

## 7. What remains open

The canonical full baseline has now been calibrated at every depth, and
the sharper full baseline is separately explicit. The dense proposal
(7)--(8) solves its full PSD and all mixed-block conditions identically,
but its ACTUAL coefficient signs fail. Even arbitrary free skew changes
cannot fix its prescribed boundary-weight derivative at three steps.
Any rank-one continuation at either displayed rate also has the growing
relative-derivative requirement (16). These are scoped obstructions,
not a claim that every optimal certificate has either shape.

The explicit higher-rank path (19) uses every such sign direction and
is feasible at every depth, but its actual objective coefficient (20)
is unaffordable. The assignment permits other higher-rank PSD remainders,
different boundary weights, nonzero optimum sources, and a relaxed q.
Those freedoms are not excluded here. To obtain a separation, one must control the FINAL
signs and the exact finite-path Schur remainder uniformly in m, with
limsup q_m M_m<e/rho at s=1 (or the corresponding strict fixed-s gap).
Neither a derivative, the rank-one scalar moment, nor the real-skew
parameterization supplies that remaining estimate. No such certificate
or unrestricted obstruction has been proved in this round.
