# C59: a fully specified legal H6 adversary above 4/M6

Status: **exact finite reconstruction and joint proof candidate; UNVERIFIED**.
No new fact is claimed and no verifier submission is allocated. The only
accepted mathematical predecessor is `1252b8823bb5a290`, for full
smooth-convex interpolation and its explicit conjugate construction.

This is a finite diagnosis of the actual H6 word, not an asymptotic theorem.
The word here uses epsilon=1/6. It is not the length-63 subword obtained by
fixing epsilon=1/m for a much larger horizon m.

## 1. Statement and exact input object

Put

    c=(7/6)(1+sqrt(2)), a=5(sqrt(2)-1)/7,
    H0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<6,
    h=H6, n=63, S=sum_(i<63)h_i, M6=1+S.

There is a completely specified convex differentiable 1-smooth function
on R^66 with unique minimizer0 and an actual GD trajectory for this h
such that

    2(F(X_63)-F(0))/dist(X_0,argmin F)^2
             > 56/2711 > 1/50 > 4/M6.              (1)

In particular, this finite word cannot have a full valid upper certificate
at level1/M6. No assertion is made about eventual large-m feasibility.

The rational construction data are the lower-triangular integer matrix T
of order65 and the64 integer values v_i in

    research/max3_c59_h6_rational_primal.json.

The PUBLIC file's SHA256 is

    7376e26ca81edc6438c0563e008c845ce439e424bd42f9f65c37a07867d6b113.

Its fields `coordinate_integer_rows_lower_triangular` and
`function_value_numerators` are part of the definition, with the common
denominator D=10^15. For reproducibility the complete defining integer
data are also appended to the shared proof finding. No numerical solver
claim is used as a premise of the construction below.

Let the rational vectors in R^65 be

    v_start=T[0,:]/D,  q_i=T[i+1,:]/D (0<=i<=63),
    u_i=v_i/D.

Define the core positions by the EXACT algebraic GD recursion

    z_0=v_start,
    z_(i+1)=z_i-h_i q_i.                            (2)

Here q_63 is not used in (2), but will be the core terminal gradient.
The original numerical Gram is not treated as an exact Gram. These
rational vectors define their own positive semidefinite Gram by dot
products, regardless of any properties of the source solver output.

## 2. The finite exact checks, with their integer certificate

For these core data include the zero optimum jet. Define

    Q^core_ij=u_i-u_j+<q_i,z_j-z_i>+||q_i-q_j||^2/2,
    delta^core_i=u_i-||q_i||^2/2,

with the star's position, gradient and value all zero. The following
strict bounds are verified by integer comparisons of the defining data:

    Q^core_ij < eta=1/500000000000 for EVERY i!=j,
    delta^core_i > -eta for every finite i,
    ||v_start||^2 < 1001/1000,
    u_63 > 21/2000,
    200<S<256,  h_i>1 for every i.                  (3)

The first line checks all65*64=4160 ordered pairs, including both optimum
directions and both terminal directions. Here are the exact formulas used
to audit (3), so the finite part is not a feasibility-tolerance assertion.

The data file gives each step as

    h_t=(A_t+B_t sqrt(2))/54432

with integer arrays A_t,B_t. These are exactly the recursively defined
steps: arithmetic in Q(sqrt(2)) with a=(-5/7,5/7) and c=(7/6,7/6)
produces those integer pairs. Let

    G_ab=sum_k T[a,k]T[b,k].

Thus <q_i,q_j>=G_(i+1,j+1)/D^2 and
<q_i,v_start>=G_(i+1,0)/D^2. Set Hden=54432 and define integer arrays

    R_ij=Hden G_(i+1,0)-sum_(t<j) A_t G_(i+1,t+1),
    I_ij=                  -sum_(t<j) B_t G_(i+1,t+1).

Then <q_i,z_j>=(R_ij+I_ij sqrt(2))/(Hden D^2).
When j=star, set both of these numerators to zero. When i=star, every
term containing q_i is zero. Set v_star=0 and the corresponding gradient
Gram entries to zero. The exact pair numerator formula is

    Qa_ij=2 Hden D(v_i-v_j)+2(R_ij-R_ii)
                   +Hden(G_(i+1,i+1)+G_(j+1,j+1)-2G_(i+1,j+1)),
    Qb_ij=2(I_ij-I_ii),
    Q^core_ij=(Qa_ij+Qb_ij sqrt(2))/(2 Hden D^2),    (4)

using the displayed star conventions. The missing diagonal terms for a
star index in (4) are zero.

For the radical, use the rational interval

    Lrad/10^50 < sqrt(2) < (Lrad+1)/10^50,
    Lrad=141421356237309504880168872420969807856967187537694.

Its validity follows by squaring the two positive integer endpoints.
For each pair an upper-bound numerator with denominator
2 Hden D^2*10^50 is

    Qa_ij*10^50+Qb_ij*(Lrad+1)  if Qb_ij>=0,
    Qa_ij*10^50+Qb_ij*Lrad      if Qb_ij<0.          (5)

The data file contains all4160 integer triples from (4)--(5). Every one
satisfies `upper_numerator*500000000000 < denominator`. The largest
upper bound occurs at the directed pair (31,30) and is approximately
1.371014491112536e-12; the exact numerator and denominator are retained
in `audit.max_Q_upper_numerator` and `audit.max_Q_upper_denominator`.
This decimal is descriptive, whereas the integer comparison proves the
inequality used in (3).

The other checks in (3) use the same radical interval for S and each h,
and use, without a radical,

    delta^core_i=(2v_i D-G_(i+1,i+1))/(2D^2),
    ||v_start||^2=G_00/D^2.

The minimum core delta is already positive in these data (approximately
8.5986e-11), but only the weaker stated lower bound is needed. The audit
script is PUBLIC at `research/max3_c59_h6_exact_primal_repair.py`.
Its single finite integer check completed in under0.1second and used no
optimization, search, eigenvalue clipping, or large symbolic computation.
This is a transparent finite arithmetic component of an unverified proof
candidate; it is not a substitute for the verifier's acceptance.

## 3. One controlled auxiliary coordinate repairs all pairs

Choose

    kappa=1/512, t0=1/8,
    xi_0=1, xi_(i+1)=(1-kappa h_i)xi_i.

Every factor is positive since h_i<=S<256. For any initial segment,
the elementary product inequality

    product_t(1-a_t)>=1-sum_t a_t  (a_t>=0, sum a_t<1)

follows inductively from (1-a)(1-b)>=1-a-b. It gives

    1>=xi_i>=1-kappa S>1/2.

For i<j, positivity and h_i>1 imply

    xi_i-xi_j>=xi_i-xi_(i+1)=kappa h_i xi_i>kappa/2.

The distance to the optimum sample xi_star=0 is also greater than
kappa/2. Thus these bounds cover every distinct pair, including star.

Define the66-dimensional jets and values

    X_i=(z_i,t0 xi_i),
    G_i=(q_i,t0 kappa xi_i),
    f_i=u_i+t0^2 kappa xi_i^2/2
       =u_i+xi_i^2/65536, 0<=i<=63,
    X_star=G_star=0, f_star=0.                      (6)

Their GD recursion is EXACT by (2) and the recursion for xi. The full
interpolation residual separates by coordinates into

    Q_ij=Q^core_ij
          -t0^2 kappa(1-kappa)(xi_i-xi_j)^2/2.      (7)

This is a polynomial identity, not a claimed separability of the final
function. The second term is the residual for the single quadratic
auxiliary coordinate at the displayed samples. Since1-kappa>1/2,
its magnitude is strictly greater than

    t0^2 kappa^3/16=2^(-37)>eta.

Combining with (3) proves Q_ij<0 for ALL4160 ordered pairs simultaneously.
The same common values and coordinates are used in every pair.

## 4. One global function and the true initial distance

For each finite sample put

    Y_i=X_i-G_i, delta_i=f_i-||G_i||^2/2.

Equation (6) gives

    delta_i=delta^core_i+t0^2 kappa(1-kappa)xi_i^2/2
             >-eta+t0^2 kappa/16>0.                (8)

Add the star with Y_star=0,delta_star=0, and define

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max_(i in {star,0,...,63})
                              [<Y_i,v>-delta_i],
    F(X)=sup_v[<X,v>-H(v)].                         (9)

By accepted1252b8823bb5a290 and (7), this is one globally defined finite
convex differentiable function with1-Lipschitz gradient, interpolating
every value and gradient in (6). Therefore its GD trajectory is the one
already specified, with the actual ordered word H6.

The finite set of strict gaps in (8) makes the star's zero affine function
uniquely active in a neighborhood of v=0. Hence H(v)=||v||^2/2 there and
partial H(0)={0}. The maximizing-vector condition for (9) identifies the
minimizers of F with partial H(0), as in the accepted predecessor. Thus
argmin F={0}; no remote or nonclosest minimizer is used in normalization.

The true squared distance and terminal value satisfy

    R^2=||v_start||^2+1/64 < 1001/1000+1/64
                              =8133/8000,
    2F(X_63)=2u_63+t0^2 kappa xi_63^2 >21/1000.

Consequently

    2F(X_63)/R^2> (21/1000)/(8133/8000)
                 =56/2711>1/50>4/(1+S),

which proves (1), subject only to the explicitly supplied finite integer
checks on the defining data. If a unit initial norm is desired, use
F_unit(x)=F(Rx)/R^2 and initial point X_0/R; the smoothness remains1,

## 5. A concrete feature of the surviving geometry

The rational core gradients have the exact inner product

    <q_35,q_36>
      =-14715168270572693173715883215/10^30
      <-14/1000.

The extra coordinate changes this by at most t0^2 kappa^2=2^(-24),
since0<xi_i<=1. Thus

    <G_35,G_36><-1/100.

Both indices are queried. The actual object retains substantial signed
gradient correlation; it is not a Huber common-gradient line, a mutually
orthogonal gradient transcript, or an all-gradients acute-cone trajectory.
The auxiliary coordinate repairs small interpolation errors in an already
strong correlated core, in contrast to attempting to repair the grossly
illegal fixed scalar C55 template. No claim is made that this description
is a scalable generating rule.

There is also a basis-independent distinction from a bounded-jump
coordinate construction. Let d_i=G_i-G_(i-1),1<=i<=63, and let J be their
Gram matrix. If an orthonormal coordinate system makes every coordinate
of the gradient list change at most k times, then

    2 sum_(i<j)|J_ij| <= (k-1) trace(J).             (10)

Indeed each scalar coordinate of the jump list has at most k nonzero
entries. Cauchy--Schwarz gives (sum|a_i|)^2<=k sum a_i^2, hence
2sum_(i<j)|a_i a_j|<=(k-1)sum a_i^2. Sum over coordinates and apply the
triangle inequality to the resulting off-diagonal entries. Since J is
unchanged by orthogonal changes of physical coordinates, (10) applies to
every such representation.

For the exact rational core, the integer increment Gram is saved PUBLICLY
in `research/max3_c59_exact_increment_gram.json`. Its entries follow
directly from the rational vectors already defined, with denominator D^2.
Exact integer summation gives

    trace(J_core) approximately 0.44249400386221016,
    2sum_(i<j)|J_core_ij| approximately 2.306374594722243,
    2sum_(i<j)|J_core_ij|-5trace(J_core)>9/100.       (11)

Only the last, rational inequality is used. The auxiliary jump vector is
a_i=t0 kappa(xi_i-xi_(i-1)); all entries are negative and

triangle inequality, adding aa^T can lower the left side of (11) by at
most

    2sum_(i<j)|a_i a_j|+5sum_i a_i^2
           <=5(sum_i|a_i|)^2<5*2^(-24).

Thus the full repaired J still satisfies
2sum_(i<j)|J_ij|>5trace(J). Equation (10) rules out every representation
in which all coordinate gradients have at most SIX chronological jumps.
In particular this actual finite adversary is outside the common two-jump
primal cone. The large core margin in (11) ensures this distinction is
not caused only by the tiny auxiliary quadratic coordinate.

## 6. Scope and next open interface

This candidate is finite, exact in its definitions, and includes all
function values, gradients, positions, actual GD equations, and the true
distance. It does not rely on a numerically feasible Gram or a nearly
positive semidefinite dual. The source solver arrays are preserved
unchanged; the rational data and added coordinate are separately labeled

as the enclosing horizon changes. The missing scalable interface is an
analytic rule for the correlated core that controls ALL interpolation
pairs and distance under those parameter changes. Repeating this finite
data set, extrapolating its numerical eigenvectors, or fixing only one
turning pair would not provide that rule.

No routine verification allowance was used. This remains a complete
finite proof candidate, not an accepted fact.

## 10. A partial repair using only ordinary interpolation, not normals

Return to data (1) and the common quadratic values (6), with A>=I, but now
assume ONLY every ordinary Q_ij<=0. The normals (4) are not assumed, and no
metric-distance representative or effective smoothness is inferred. Let
j>=3 be the highest nonzero level, d=d_j, w=w_j, and set

            a_w=<w,A w>/||w||^2, r_w=<v,w>/||w||^2.

Then the actual ordinary inequalities alone force

                         a_w >= d-261/16 > d-17.    (28)

This is an approximate scalar curvature cost, not the missing full gradient
or initial-distance budget. It applies to arbitrary conditioning of A.

Here is a direct proof. Throughout the isolated right block, R_t=p_t w,
Z_t=d p_t w. At an even queried index t before the last positive p, the
next physical step is h=d_0 and p'=p_t(1-h/d)>0. Expanding BOTH Q inequalities
using (8), which is an algebraic identity independent of (4), gives

       <=r_w

Choose the actual even indices I=2^(j-1) and K=2^j-2. Both pairs I,I+1 and
K,K+1 precede the annihilating step, and lower modes have vanished. Put
p_I=P_I(1/d) and p_K=P_K(1/d). The subword between these two query indices
is H_(j-1) with its last d_0 removed. Since j>=3, it includes a d_(j-2).
Every factor is in (0,1), so 1-z<=exp(-z) gives

 p_K/p_I<=exp(-d_(j-2)/d)<=exp(-4/25)<=25/29.         (30)

For the middle inequality, d_j<c^2 d_(j-2) and c<5/2. The last follows
from exp(4/25)>=1+4/25. Thus p_I-p_K>=(4/29)p_I.
Also d>=d_3>3 and h=d_0<3/2, so 1-h/d>1/2 and
p_I^2/p_(I+1)<2p_I, while p_K<=p_I.

If a_w>=d, (28) already holds. Otherwise use the upper bound (29) at I and
the lower bound at K. Since a_w>=1, they imply

    <=(a_w-1)h[p_I^2/p_(I+1)+p_K]/(2d^2)
    <(a_w-1)(9/4)p_I/d^2.

With (30), this yields

 d-a_w <= (261/16)(a_w-1)/d <=261/16,

is no continuous-time limit or sum of purported independent level charges.

claim: Signed interval construction completed and quantitatively excluded in its explicit zero-height class: each coordinate starts at Aamp_j, reflects to -Bamp_j for one dyadic cell, then vanishes. One finite common interpolant satisfies ALL original pairs with true initial distance; every legal member at every cutoff of actual H_m has V_ref<3/M_m² and B_(2^m-1)V_ref<=15[3/(1+sqrt(2))²]^m→0. evidence:
# Signed interval gradients: a legal construction and its quantitative loss

Status: **self-contained draft candidate, not verifier accepted**. This round
uses no optimization, installation, or fact submission. The accepted
dependencies are `1252b8823bb5a290` (smooth convex interpolation, including
its explicit conjugate construction) and `b98bb807d514e80d` (the exact
benchmark B_n and its bound B_n<=1+4 n^(log_2 3)). Every new assertion below
is proved within this one candidate. Neither the prior cone interface nor
C57 is adopted as a correctness premise.

The generating rule is different from C57's ordered repair: each coordinate
has a positive initial amplitude, an opposite amplitude for one cell, and
then vanishes. Amplitudes may be unequal. These gradients have negative
cross inner products in the explicit construction, and are not ordered in
an acute cone. They are correlated, even across remote cells. Every scalar
coordinate changes at most twice, so the increment Gram has an explicit
sum of PSD blocks on at most two increment indices.

The scope restriction that causes failure is explicit: the gradient is
constant on each selected ordinary block, and its jet at the end of every
such block has **zero proximal height**. The entire resulting class on the
actual H_m, over every dyadic cutoff, has normalized payoff <3/M_m^2.
This is not a bound on arbitrary signed interval mixtures or on W_n(H_m).
Section 7 gives the exact charged inequality when endpoint heights are
allowed to be positive; it does not assert that these charges can be met.

## 1. The actual schedule and one finite coordinate rule

Fix m>=128 and, for this whole horizon, set

 sigma=1+sqrt(2), c_rul=sigma(1+1/m),
 a_rul=(1-1/m)/c_rul,
 H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_rul c_rul^j,H_j),
 M_j=1+sum H_j, n=2^m-1.

The parameters are not recomputed within the recursion. Choose an integer
cutoff 0<=ell<m. Put q=m-ell, k=2^q-1 and C=M_ell. The actual word is

 H_m=(H_ell,1+r_0,H_ell,...,1+r_(k-1),H_ell),
 r_j=a_rul c_rul^(ell+nu_2(j+1)), 0<=j<k,                 (1)

where nu_2(v) is the largest integer d>=0 with 2^d dividing the positive
integer v. There are k+1 ordinary cells, numbered 0,...,k. Each contains
the exact steps H_ell, of mass C-1. No final step has been changed: the
last ordinary cell includes the original last step of H_m.

In an orthonormal coordinate system e_0,...,e_k choose real amplitudes
Aamp_j>=0 for 0<=j<=k and Bamp_j for 0<=j<k. Define the cell gradients

 p_0=sum_(j=0)^k Aamp_j e_j,
 p_i=-Bamp_(i-1)e_(i-1)+sum_(j=i)^k Aamp_j e_j,
                                      1<=i<=k.          (2)

Thus coordinate j<k equals Aamp_j in cells 0,...,j, equals -Bamp_j in
cell j+1, and equals zero thereafter. Coordinate k stays Aamp_k. Zero
amplitudes are permitted; choosing a coordinate orientation makes the
initial amplitudes nonnegative without loss within this rule. The Bamp
amplitudes are initially unrestricted in sign.

Use the same gradient p_i at every query in cell i and at its endpoint.
For i<k that endpoint is the query immediately before checkpoint 1+r_i;
for i=k it is the terminal sample after the complete original word. Denote
these endpoint positions by Z_i. Define Y_i=Z_i-p_i. The actual recursion
forces

 Y_(i+1)=Y_i-r_i p_i-C p_(i+1).                          (3)

Indeed the checkpoint sends Z_i=Y_i+p_i to Y_i-r_i p_i,
and the next ordinary cell uses mass C-1 of p_(i+1). A sample in cell i
with remaining ordinary mass u in [0,C-1] has position

 X_(i,u)=Y_i+(1+u)p_i.                                  (4)

Define the tail energy, squared norms and cross inner products by

 Eref_i=sum_(j=i)^k Aamp_j^2,
 Nref_0=Eref_0,
 Nref_i=Eref_i+Bamp_(i-1)^2,                 1<=i<=k,
 Cref_i=Eref_i-Aamp_(i-1)Bamp_(i-1),         1<=i<=k.

Direct coordinate multiplication gives

 ||p_i||^2=Nref_i,    <p_i,p_j>=Cref_j for every i<j.    (5)

These are generally nonzero, signed correlations between remote cells.

## 2. Explicit membership in the two-jump increment cone

For j<k-1, the only gradient changes in coordinate j occur just after
checkpoints j and j+1. Their amplitudes are respectively
-(Aamp_j+Bamp_j) and Bamp_j. The corresponding incremental Gram summand
is the outer product of this two-supported scalar list with itself.
Coordinate k-1 changes only at the final checkpoint, and coordinate k
does not change. Summing these real PSD summands is the complete increment
Gram. This is a decomposition, not an inferred membership from numerics.

The initial-vector and initial-gradient rows are retained: the full Gram
is obtained from the actual vectors X_0,p_0,...,p_k and their repetitions
at the original query indices. For the explicit member in Section 4,
X_0=C p_0. Appending its coordinate to each scalar list gives the full
Gram decomposition with the base rows included.

## 3. Zero endpoint heights impose an exact energy contraction

Consider ANY legal convex differentiable 1-smooth function F realizing
(1)--(4), normalized by min F=0. Impose only the stated endpoint-height
condition

                  F(Z_i)=Nref_i/2, 0<=i<=k.             (6)

Intermediate values in a constant-gradient cell are forced to be

                  F(X_(i,u))=(u+1/2)Nref_i.             (7)

For proof, the two interpolation inequalities between equal gradients
force the value difference to equal their inner product with the position
difference. Condition (6), smoothness on the unit step from Z_i, and
minimality imply F(Y_i)=0. All Y_i are genuine minimizers.

The accepted interpolation inequalities between endpoint jets are exactly

                     <p_i,Y_j-Y_i><=0.                (8)

In particular, the inequality from endpoint i+1 to endpoint i, combined
with (3),(5), is

 (C+r_i)Eref_(i+1)+C Bamp_i^2
                         <=r_i Aamp_i Bamp_i.           (9)

This is one necessary joint interpolation pair inside the actual history;
it is independent of an assumed separable function. Completing its square
and using Aamp_i^2=Eref_i-Eref_(i+1) gives

 (2C+r_i)^2 Eref_(i+1)
   +4C^2[Bamp_i-r_i Aamp_i/(2C)]^2 <=r_i^2 Eref_i.      (10)

Consequently, with

 gamma_ref_i=[r_i/(2C+r_i)]^2,

                  Eref_(i+1)<=gamma_ref_i Eref_i.       (11)

There is also a useful bound on the whole next gradient:

                  Nref_(i+1)<=(r_i/C)^2 Aamp_i^2.       (12)

If Aamp_i=0, (9) forces Bamp_i=Eref_(i+1)=0, so (12)
holds. Otherwise (9) forces 0<=Bamp_i<=r_i Aamp_i/C.
Solving (9) for Eref_(i+1) yields

 Nref_(i+1)<=r_i Bamp_i(Aamp_i+Bamp_i)/(C+r_i),

an increasing function of Bamp_i on that interval. Substitution of its
upper endpoint proves (12). Thus allowing either sign of Bamp initially
does not evade (9): legality itself forces the reflected sign unless the
subsequent gradient is zero.

The true initial distance is also fixed, rather than reset at a later cut.
By (4), X_0=Y_0+C p_0. For any minimizer z, smooth convex interpolation
between Z_0 and z gives <p_0,z-Y_0><=0. Therefore

 ||X_0-z||^2>=C^2 Nref_0,
 dist(X_0,argmin F)^2=C^2 Nref_0,                       (13)

with equality at the genuine minimizer Y_0. This proof permits additional
minimizers; it does not silently assume uniqueness. If Nref_0=0, (9)
forces the entire terminal value to be zero, and there is no positive
normalized witness. For Nref_0>0 the normalized terminal payoff is

 V_ref=Nref_k/(C^2 Nref_0).

Applying (11) up to i=k-2 and then (12) gives the uniform bound

 V_ref <= r_(k-1)^2/C^4 * product_(i=0)^(k-2)gamma_ref_i.
                                                               (14)

For k=1 the product is empty. This is a bound for EVERY legal member of
the generating rule with (6), regardless of how it was constructed.

## 4. An explicit finite member satisfies ALL original pairs

The zero-height class above is nonempty and contains genuine signed,
correlated trajectories. Here is a deterministic finite formula, without
solving an interpolation or matrix optimization problem.

For this construction only, set r_k=0 and define, for 0<=j<k,

 zeta_j=r_j/[4(C+r_(j+1))],
 Lref_j=zeta_j(r_j-C zeta_j)/(C+r_j)>0.

Write r_min=min_(j<k)r_j, r_max=max_(j<k)r_j,
Lref_min=min_(j<k)Lref_j, and choose

 eta^2=min{1/4, Lref_min/[2(1+Lref_min)],
                                      r_min/(2r_max)}.  (15)

Set Aamp_j=eta^j for j<k, Aamp_k=0, and
Bamp_j=zeta_j Aamp_j. Define p_i by (2), Y_0=0, and Y_i by (3).
All these are exact finite real formulas. In fact 0<eta<1 and Bamp_j>0.

For every j<k, a finite geometric-series estimate gives

 Eref_(j+1)<=eta^2 Aamp_j^2/(1-eta^2)
                         <Lref_j Aamp_j^2.              (16)

To check the strict inequality, (15) implies
eta^2/(1-eta^2)<=Lref_min/(2+Lref_min)<Lref_min.
Thus (9) is satisfied strictly. Moreover Lref_j<zeta_j, so

                 Cref_(j+1)<0.                         (17)

It remains to prove the remote normal constraints (8), rather than infer
them from adjacent checks. For i<j, iterating (3) gives

 Y_j-Y_i=-r_i p_i-sum_(u=i+1)^(j-1)(C+r_u)p_u-C p_j.
                                                               (18)

For the later gradient, (5) implies

 <p_j,Y_i-Y_j>
  =[r_i+sum_(u=i+1)^(j-1)(C+r_u)]Cref_j+C Nref_j.

The bracket is at least r_(j-1). Since Cref_j<0, this is at
most r_(j-1)Cref_j+C Nref_j, which is negative by (9),(16).

For the earlier gradient, (18) gives the desired inequality precisely
when

 r_i Nref_i+sum_(u=i+1)^(j-1)(C+r_u)Cref_u+C Cref_j>=0.   (19)

Since |Cref_(u+1)|<=zeta_u Aamp_u^2 and
(C+r_(u+1))zeta_u=r_u/4, the total absolute value of the
negative terms in (19) is at most

                 (1/4)sum_(u=i)^(j-1)r_u Aamp_u^2.

The choice of eta makes consecutive r_u Aamp_u^2 decrease by a factor
at most 1/2: r_(u+1)eta^2/r_u<=1/2. Therefore the last display is
at most r_i Aamp_i^2/2, whereas the positive term is at least
r_i Aamp_i^2. This proves (19), strictly. It also includes i=0,
so every Y_j is in the supporting halfspace <p_0,Y_j><=0.

Give EVERY original sample, including the terminal, the single value
array (7), position (4), and gradient p_i. Add the optimum jet (0,0,0).
For two samples in cells i,j with remaining ordinary masses u,v,
direct substitution into

 Q_ab=F_a-F_b+<g_a,X_b-X_a>+||g_a-g_b||^2/2

gives

 Q_((i,u),(j,v))
       =<p_i,Y_j-Y_i>+v[<p_i,p_j>-Nref_j].              (20)

If i=j both terms vanish. If i!=j the first is nonpositive by
(8),(19) and the second is nonpositive by (17). This covers every
remote earlier pair in both orientations, not only successive cells.
For the optimum pairs the exact residuals are

 Q_((i,u),star)=-<p_i,Y_i><=0,
 Q_(star,(i,u))=-u Nref_i<=0,                            (21)

where the first follows from (8) with Y_0=0. Thus all original
interpolation inequalities hold simultaneously with one shared array.

For an explicit globally defined function, index these finite jets by a.
Put g_a=p_i, f_a=(u+1/2)Nref_i, X_a=Y_i+(1+u)p_i, add
the optimum jet, and define

 Href(v)=||v||^2/2+max_a[<X_a-g_a,v>-(f_a-||g_a||^2/2)],
 Fref(x)=sup_v[<x,v>-Href(v)].                          (22)

By the fully proved conjugate construction in accepted fact
1252b8823bb5a290, (20)--(21) imply that Fref is everywhere finite,
convex, differentiable and 1-smooth, and interpolates ALL these jets.
Its actual GD trajectory is the displayed one by (3)--(4). Formula
(13) proves that its true initial distance is C sqrt(Nref_0), attained
at the original optimum 0. Its exact positive payoff is

 V_ref=Bamp_(k-1)^2/[C^2 sum_(j=0)^(k-1)eta^(2j)].      (23)

No averaging of incompatible functions is used. Finite dimension k
suffices after deleting the zero final coordinate. The construction
has unequal, signed gradient changes and negative remote correlations.

## 5. Uniform loss on H_m, including every dyadic cutoff

The elementary mass count from (1) and the definition of H_j gives

 M_j=A_mass c_rul^j+(1-A_mass)2^j,
 A_mass=a_rul/(c_rul-2).                               (24)

For m>=128, sigma<c_rul<5/2 and
3/8<a_rul<sigma-2<c_rul-2<1/2. Consequently

 3/4<A_mass<1,
 (3/4)c_rul^j<M_j<=c_rul^j,
 t:=a_rul c_rul^ell/C<=c_rul-2<1/2.                    (25)

For example sigma<17/7 yields c_rul<2193/896<5/2;
a_rul>(127/128)/(5/2)=127/320>3/8; and
a_rul<1/sigma=sigma-2. These prove all bounds used in (25).

The last checkpoint is an odd occurrence, so r_(k-1)/C=t.
For each earlier checkpoint write t_i=r_i/C=t c_rul^(nu_2(i+1)).
Then gamma_ref_i=[t_i/(2+t_i)]^2<=t_i^2/4. The exact valuation sum is

 sum_(v=1)^(2^q-2)nu_2(v)=2^q-q-1.

One proof counts the multiples of 2^d for each d>=1. The same sum up
to 2^q-1 is sum_(d=1)^(q-1)(2^(q-d)-1)=2^q-q-1,
and the omitted last integer is odd. This includes q=1 with empty sums.
Substitution into (14) gives

 V_ref <=(t^2/C^2)c_rul^(2(1-q))
                         (t c_rul/2)^(2(2^q-2)).       (26)

Because t c_rul/2<5/8, the last factor is at most 1. Using
C>(3/4)c_rul^ell and q+ell=m proves

 V_ref <(4/9)c_rul^2 c_rul^(-2m)
        <3 c_rul^(-2m)<=3/M_m^2.                      (27)

The omitted cutoff ell=m has no checkpoints and a constant gradient;
its zero terminal height gives payoff exactly1/M_m^2, so the same
uniform bound includes it as well.

This is below1/M_m whenever M_m>3, in particular throughout the stated
range. More decisively, the accepted exact benchmark bound gives

 B_(2^m-1)V_ref
   <3(1+4*3^m)c_rul^(-2m)
   <=15[3/(1+sqrt(2))^2]^m ->0.                       (28)

This uses the actual B_n, not a fitted constant or an asymptotic phase.
The convergence is uniform over the cutoff, all amplitudes, and all
legal interpolants in the specified zero-height generating class.

## 6. Why this is not a result for the entire increment cone

The cone also permits general pairs of changes in each coordinate,
arbitrary initial amplitudes, different net changes, overlapping
intervals, and shared positive endpoint heights. Equations (9)--(14)
use the specific history in (2), constant ordinary-cell gradients,
and zero endpoint heights. A general cone member need not satisfy them.
The result therefore does not upper-bound W_n(H_m), refute another
worker's unrestricted primal, or decide common-array feasibility at1/M_m.

The explicit construction supplies an actual legal function but its
payoff is far too small. It is a completed failure of this new generating
rule, not a successful lower bound for the original problem.

## 7. The exact height charge that a changed construction must pay

Retain only the coordinate rule and the constant-gradient ordinary cells,
but now allow the endpoint heights

 delta_i=F(Z_i)-Nref_i/2>=0

of ONE jointly legal function to be arbitrary. Formula (3) still holds.
The same endpoint interpolation pair becomes

 (C+r_i)Eref_(i+1)+C Bamp_i^2-r_i Aamp_i Bamp_i
                                    <=delta_i-delta_(i+1).

Equivalently, with omega_ref_i=4C/(2C+r_i)^2,

 Eref_(i+1)+[4C^2/(2C+r_i)^2]
                    [Bamp_i-r_i Aamp_i/(2C)]^2
       <=gamma_ref_i Eref_i
                       +omega_ref_i(delta_i-delta_(i+1)).       (29)

In particular, retaining Eref_(i+1)>=theta Eref_i requires

 delta_i-delta_(i+1)
  >=C[(2+t_i)^2 theta-t_i^2]Eref_i/4
                      +C[Bamp_i-t_i Aamp_i/2]^2.       (30)

At any lowest-level checkpoint of (1), t_i=t<1/2. If at least
one quarter of the untouched tail energy is to survive that checkpoint,
(30) forces delta_i-delta_(i+1)>=C Eref_i/4. Indeed
(2+t)^2/4-t^2=1+t-3t^2/4>=1 for 0<=t<=1/2.
These are charges in a shared value sequence, not separately selectable
per-cut credits; other checkpoints may replenish a height only subject
to that same sequence and the remaining interpolation pairs.

For any 0<=s<k, iterating (29) after discarding its nonnegative square
also gives the exact necessary weighted budget

 Eref_(s+1)<=Eref_0 product_(i=0)^s gamma_ref_i
  +sum_(i=0)^s omega_ref_i(delta_i-delta_(i+1))
                                  product_(u=i+1)^s gamma_ref_u. (31)

Finally the initial value is delta_0+(C-1/2)Nref_0. Interpolation
with any chosen minimizer x_star gives

 <p_0,X_0-x_star>>=C Nref_0+delta_0,
 dist(X_0,argmin F)^2
                >=(C Nref_0+delta_0)^2/Nref_0,         (32)

when Nref_0>0. Thus an initial height cannot be inserted without its
actual distance cost. Equations (29)--(32) are necessary conditions,
not a sufficient construction or a payoff bound for positive heights.
They identify a concrete next interface: meet all remote pairs with
this same height budget, or change the coordinate-history rule so that
the fixed cross correlation in (5) no longer forces (29).

## 8. An exact countercheck against removing the height hypothesis

The bound (27) is false if one removes (6), even without changing the
coordinate-history rule. This is a useful guard against overstating the
obstruction. Write S=sum H_m=M_m-1, tau=1/(2S+1), and define the scalar
Huber function

 F_H(x)=x^2/2 if |x|<=tau,
        tau|x|-tau^2/2 if |x|>=tau.

It is convex and differentiable, its derivative is 1-Lipschitz, and its
unique minimizer is 0. Start at X_0=1. At every original query and at
the terminal, x_i=1-tau sum_(t<i)h_t>=tau, hence g_i=tau and
f_i=tau x_i-tau^2/2. This obeys the same coordinate rule (2) by taking
Aamp_k=tau and every other Aamp and Bamp to be zero. Its exact payoff
and true squared distance are

              2F_H(x_n)=1/(2M_m-1),  R^2=1.            (33)

For M_m>=6 this exceeds3/M_m^2, since M_m^2>6M_m-3.
The actual endpoints have delta_j=tau Z_j-tau^2>0, and

              delta_j-delta_(j+1)=(C+r_j)tau^2.

Thus every height inequality (29) is met with equality in its original
unsquared form, using Eref_j=tau^2 and Aamp_j=Bamp_j=0 for j<k.
The initial cost (32) is also exact: delta_0=tau-C tau^2, so
(C Nref_0+delta_0)^2/Nref_0=1. This does not furnish an improvement
over Huber or solve the positive-height rule; it refutes only the
unjustified extension of (27) to arbitrary endpoint heights.

For a finite algebraic sanity check of Section 4, two fixed rational
fixtures used c_rul=5/2, a_rul=2/5, m=3, and ell=0 or1. These values
test the general construction formulas, not the asymptotic assumptions
m>=128. Exact Fraction arithmetic checked all72 ordered original pairs
(including the optimum) in each fixture, all residuals nonpositive,
the complete actual step word, and positive terminal payoff. Both checks
together took0.00492 seconds. No numerical optimization or large search
was run; the symbolic arguments above, rather than these fixtures, are
the evidence for the general statements.

The original all-schedule exact-profile target remains open. Routine
verification is closed by the current TASK/master guidance; this entire
candidate remains shared evidence until an authorized verifier accepts it.

evidence:
# C60: a nonlinear two-state legal trajectory with dense turning gradients

Status: **new explicit construction and scoped calculations; UNVERIFIED**.
No solve or verifier call is used. The numerical allocation is closed.
This branch follows the finite C59 reconstruction by seeking an analytic
correlated core. It does not assume that the C59 data belong to this family.

The construction works for every finite nonnegative schedule, including
zeros and arbitrarily large entries, with one fixed globally convex
1-smooth function. Its all-pair law and true closest-minimizer distance
are explicit. The quantitative payoff on the critical H_m remains open.

## 1. The global function, its gradients, and its minimizers

In R^2 let

    C_par={(t,s): s>=t^2/sqrt(2)},
    F_par(X)=sup_(g in C_par) [<X,g>-||g||^2/2].      (1)

The set is closed, convex and nonempty, and contains0. Completing the
square shows that the maximizer in (1) is the Euclidean projection of X
onto C_par. It exists and is unique because the squared-distance objective
is coercive and strictly convex. Thus F_par is finite and convex.

For completeness write p(X) for that projection. Its elementary normal
condition is

    <X-p(X),g-p(X)><=0 for every g in C_par.

Applying this twice and adding gives

    ||p(X)-p(Y)||^2<=<p(X)-p(Y),X-Y>.

Thus p is1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizers in (1) gives

    0<=F_par(Y)-F_par(X)-<p(X),Y-X>
        <=<p(Y)-p(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

Consequently F_par is differentiable, its gradient is p, and it is
1-smooth. This proof supplies the needed global property directly.

The minimizers are exactly

    argmin F_par={(0,y):y<=0}.                      (2)

Indeed F_par>=0 by the feasible vector0. For X=(0,y), y<=0, every g=(t,s)
in C_par has <X,g>=ys<=0, so the maximum in (1) is0. Conversely, if
the vertical coordinate y>0, taking g=(0,s) with small s>0 makes the
objective positive. If the horizontal coordinate x is nonzero and y<=0,
take g=(t,t^2/sqrt(2)) with sufficiently small nonzero t of the sign of x:
the linear term xt dominates the terms of quadratic and quartic order.
This again makes the objective positive. These cases prove (2).

This F_par is not a convex quadratic: its minimizer set is a ray, whereas
the nonempty minimizer set of an unconstrained convex quadratic is an
affine subspace.

## 2. Coordinates that make every interpolation pair explicit

For a real r and v>=0, put

    u=v+r^2,
    X(r,v)=(r(1+v+r^2), -v/sqrt(2)),
    G(r)=(r,r^2/sqrt(2)).                           (3)

Then X-G=u(r,-1/sqrt(2)). For any (t,s) in C_par,

    <X-G,(t,s)-G>
      =u[r(t-r)-(s-r^2/sqrt(2))/sqrt(2)]
      <=-(u/2)(t-r)^2<=0.

The normal condition therefore proves that G(r) is the actual gradient
of F_par at X(r,v). Direct substitution into (1) gives

    F_par(X(r,v))=r^2(1+v)/2+3r^4/4.                (4)

For any two sampled states r_i,v_i and r_j,v_j, with the actual values
from (4), the complete signed interpolation residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =-(u_j/2)(r_i-r_j)^2<=0.                   (5)

The first equality after Q follows by substituting
f_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2. The second uses the displayed parabolic
coordinates. This proves EVERY ordered pair simultaneously for one
function; no local, adjacent, or cycle relaxation is being used.

For an initial nonzero r_0 and v_0>=0, the closest minimizer in (2) is

    X_star=(0,-v_0/sqrt(2)),
    R_0^2=dist(X_0,argmin F_par)^2
            =r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2.                (6)

The optimum sample fits the same formulas with r_star=0, v_star=v_0,
u_star=v_0. Thus (5) includes both of its directions. Choosing the origin
instead would generally overestimate the true initial distance; (6) is
the normalization used throughout.

## 3. The exact GD transition, with no interpolation optimization

For ANY step h>=0, starting from state(r,v), define

    v_plus=v+h r^2,
    r_plus^3+(1+v_plus)r_plus
                      =r(1+v+r^2-h).              (7)

The cubic's left side is strictly increasing from minus infinity to
plus infinity because its derivative is1+v_plus+3r_plus^2>=1. Thus (7)
defines exactly one real r_plus, by an explicit scalar algebraic rule.
There is no nearest-feasible-trajectory problem hidden in this definition.

The vertical coordinate of X-hG is -v_plus/sqrt(2), and its horizontal
coordinate is the right side of (7). Hence

    X(r_plus,v_plus)=X(r,v)-h G(r).

This proves actual GD for the same global function. In particular h=0
leaves the state unchanged, and every finite positive step gives finite
new state. All v_i remain nonnegative, regardless of gradient sign changes.

For a supplied finite nonnegative schedule h_0,...,h_(n-1), iterate (7)
from any r_0!=0,v_0>=0. Its exact normalized payoff is

    P_par(h;r_0,v_0)
       =[r_n^2(1+v_n)+(3/2)r_n^4]
                        /[r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2].  (8)

The function (1), all values(4), gradients(3), positions(3), and initial
distance(6) are fixed together. Thus (8) is an actual lower witness for
W_n(h), albeit not yet a profile-strength one on the critical schedules.

Some immediate identities expose the changing geometry:

    u_plus-u=(h-1)r^2+r_plus^2,
    X_plus,horizontal=X_horizontal[1-h/(1+u)].      (9)

In particular, for schedules with all h>=1, the normal parameter u is
nondecreasing, but r and the horizontal gradient can turn repeatedly.
The Hessian direction changes with r; this is not a fixed linear spectral
transcript. The vertical state accumulates h r^2 rather than discarding
previous turns.

## 4. Exact dense-jump calibration on a different schedule

Take any sigma in(0,1), v_0>=0, and define

    U_0=1+v_0+sigma,
    rho=(1+sigma)/(1-sigma),
    h_i=2U_0 rho^i/(1-sigma),
    r_i=(-1)^i sqrt(sigma),
    v_i=U_0 rho^i-1-sigma.                         (10)

These v_i are nonnegative. Substitution into (7) gives
v_(i+1)-v_i=h_i sigma and
r_(i+1)(1+v_(i+1)+sigma)=r_i(1+v_i+sigma-h_i),
so (10) is an exact trajectory of F_par. Its payoff is

    P_par=rho^n/U_0+sigma/(2U_0^2).                 (11)

This calibration is legal and can have large payoff. It is a geometric
step sequence, NOT the critical ruler word, so (11) proves no claim about
H_m or the original profile. It only checks that the mechanism supports
correlated turns without a feasibility repair.

There are n nonzero collinear gradient jumps in (10):

    G_i-G_(i-1)=(2(-1)^i sqrt(sigma),0), 1<=i<=n.

Their Gram J has trace4sigma n and twice the absolute off-diagonal sum
4sigma n(n-1). For any Gram realizable with at most k nonzero jumps in
each orthonormal coordinate, Cauchy--Schwarz coordinate by coordinate
implies2sum_(i<j)|J_ij|<=(k-1)trace(J). Hence this trajectory requires
some coordinate with at least n jumps in every orthonormal realization.
Dense chronological correlation does not require a large ambient dimension.

For a completely rational parameter example, sigma=1/4 and v_0=0 give
rho=5/3, h_0=10/3, h_1=50/9, and r_i=(-1)^i/2. Formula (11) is then
an exact expression, not a numerical simulation.

## 5. Two simple parameter limits do not yet give the desired mechanism

First fix a finite schedule and fix v_0=A>=0. Let r_0=t tend to zero.
Induction in (7) gives

    v_i=A+O(t^2),
    r_i=t product_(j<i)[1-h_j/(1+A)]+O(t^3).

At each induction step, the inverse cubic has nonzero derivative1+A
at zero, and its cubic term is O(t^3), giving the displayed expansion.
Thus the payoff tends to the ordinary scalar quadratic value

    [1/(1+A)] product_(j<n)[1-h_j/(1+A)]^2.         (12)

The implicit constants here depend on the entire fixed finite schedule.
They have NOT been bounded uniformly along growing H_m. Consequently
(12) is a calibration and an explanation of why an infinitesimal core
does not itself add a new mechanism; it is not a class obstruction.

Second put S=sum h_i and sigma=r_0^2. If v_0>=S, no horizontal sign flip
occurs and |r_(i+1)|<=|r_i|. Indeed h_i<=v_i and the right side of (7)
has the sign of r_i. Evaluating the increasing cubic at r_i shows that
its excess over that right side is h_i r_i(1+r_i^2), with the appropriate
sign, so the claimed decrease in absolute value follows. Hence

    v_n<=v_0+S sigma,
    P_par <= [1+v_0+S sigma+(3/2)sigma]
                                  /(1+v_0+sigma)^2. (13)

Along any growing-horizon choices with
v_0/[S(1+sigma)] tending to infinity, this gives S P_par tending to zero.
Thus placing the initial state arbitrarily far down the flat minimizer
direction also loses the desired scale. This rules out only the displayed
parameter regime; intermediate coupled regimes remain open.

## 6. The concrete remaining critical-word problem

For the actual critical word fix, within each horizon m,

    c_m=(1+sqrt(2))(1+1/m), a_m=(1-1/m)/c_m,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_m c_m^j,H_j).

Let T_h denote the explicit two-state transition (7). The full block map
is defined EXACTLY by

    Phi_0=identity,
    Phi_(j+1)=Phi_j composed with T_(1+a_m c_m^j)
                                     composed with Phi_j.

The central task in this branch is to select explicit r_0(m),v_0(m), or
prove a useful uniform upper bound for this mechanism, while controlling
the exact payoff (8) under Phi_m. The model is already an actual legal
function for every such selection, so no separate interpolation optimization
is required. What is missing is the QUANTITATIVE estimate on that nonlinear
recursion. Neither (11), the small-amplitude calibration, nor (13) fills it.

An open subgoal is to compare the increase in v across both copies of a
dyadic block with the horizontal sign and gain at its central bridge.
The state v must remain shared between the copies; restarting it, freezing
the curvature, or replacing the two copies by independent instances would
change the function and lose the construction.

## 7. Source grounding and verification scope

Jiang, Yue and Zhou, arXiv:1911.12545v2 (2021), Theorem2.2, gives the
Euclidean projection onto S={(x,y):||x||^2<=y}: inside S it is the point,
and outside it is(x/(1+mu),y+mu/2), where mu>=max(0,-2y) is the unique
solution of ||x||^2/(1+mu)^2=y+mu/2. The paper's surrounding definition
of S and full proof were read. It supplies a closely matched projection
mechanism, not a GD complexity result for the present function. Its
cubic-regularization convergence theorem is not invoked.

Sections1--6 derive the two-dimensional specialization and all required
properties directly. No external theorem is used as a black box, and no
unverified earlier project result is a premise. The finite C59 data merely
motivated seeking dense turning gradients. Every new statement here remains
a draft until accepted by the verifier; no claim is made that this family
solves the all-schedule exact-profile problem.

`1252b8823bb5a290` supplies the full formal-vector certificate convention and
interpolation necessity. The baseline reconstruction follows the proofs in
Zehao Zhang and Rujun Jiang, *Accelerated Gradient Descent by Concatenation of
Stepsize Schedules*, arXiv:2410.12395v2 (14 February 2026), Definitions 2.4--2.7,
Theorems 3.1/3.2, Lemmas 3.5/3.6. The exact PDF and extracted text were read.
Its HTML uses different theorem numbers. Matlas returned unrelated results;
no Matlas grounding is claimed. The identities needed here are derived below.

## 1. Notation, normalization, and deterministic step words

Normalize smoothness to one and the minimizer to zero. Thus

    x_i = x_0 - sum_{t<i} h_t g_t,
    Q_ij = f_i-f_j + <g_i,x_j-x_i> + ||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    Q_i* = f_i-<g_i,x_i>+||g_i||^2/2.

An actual trajectory has every Q_ij <= 0. A full upper certificate at level q
is the identity

    q||x_0||^2 - 2f_n + sum lambda_ij Q_ij = R,

with all lambda_ij >= 0 and R PSD in the ORIGINAL vectors
(x_0,g_0,...,g_n). An upper bound derived this way uses the true initial
distance; translating/scaling back gives the project's normalization
2(f_n-f_star)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2).

Write P_n = C_n = 1+S_circle(n), D_n = B_n = 1+2S_bullet(n). These aliases
are used only in this note. Their exact recurrences are

    P_0=D_0=1,
    P_n=max_{0<=k<n} Omega(P_k,P_{n-k-1}),
    D_n=max_{0<=k<n} G(P_k,D_{n-k-1}),
    Omega(A,C)=(A+C+sqrt((A+C)^2+4AC))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

Let k_P(n), respectively k_D(n), be the SMALLEST index attaining the
corresponding maximum. These are exact real comparisons among a finite list
of nested radicals, with a specified tie rule, independent of the objective.
Set p^(0)=d^(0)=(). Recursively define the complete words

    p^(n) = (p^(k), phi(P_k-1,P_l-1), p^(l)),
        k=k_P(n), l=n-k-1,
    d^(n) = (p^(k), psi(P_k-1,(D_l-1)/2), d^(l)),
        k=k_D(n), l=n-k-1.

Here phi and psi are exactly those in accepted b98bb807d514e80d. Induction
gives length n, sums P_n-1 and (D_n-1)/2, respectively. All entries exceed
one: at a primitive join b-1 is the positive root of
r^2+(A+C)r-AC=0; at a dominant join b=1+A/r with r>1 below.
Thus these are actual predetermined legal words at EVERY horizon, with no
assumption on maximizing split patterns. Sections 2--4 specify every one of
their certificate coefficients, not just their scalar values.

## 2. Primitive finite-array identity

For a segment from sample a to sample z, with steps h_a,...,h_(z-1) and sum s,
define

    E_P = (||x_a||^2-||x_z||^2)/2
          + sum_{a<=i<z} h_i Q_i* - s f_z
          - s(s+1)||g_z||^2/2.

We construct a nonnegative finite-node array L_P with zero diagonal such that

    E_P = -sum_{a<=i,j<=z; i!=j} L_P(i,j) Q_ij.          (P)

The empty segment has L_P=0 and E_P=0. All arrays below are embedded at their
actual chronological indices and added if supports overlap.

For a join, let p be the last left sample, p+1 the first right sample, and z
the final sample. Let the left/right step sums be x,y, and b=phi(x,y). Put

    t=(x+b)/(y+2-b)>0.

The denominator is positive: substituting the defining radical gives
1<b<y+2. Let L_L,L_R be the child arrays. The complete recursion is

    L_P = L_L + (1+2t)L_R
          + t sum_{p<i<z} h_i (E_(i,p)+E_(i,z))
          + t(b-1)E_(p,z) + t E_(z,p),                 (P-array)

where E_(i,j) denotes one unit at the indicated ordered pair. Empty sums are
zero. Every displayed coefficient is nonnegative.

Here is the polynomial identity behind the recursion. Put C_R=y(y+1) and
F_j=sum_{p<i<z} h_i Q_(i,j), for j=p,z. Direct substitution of the definition
of Q gives, for ANY bridge b,

    (y+2-b)(f_p-f_z)
      -(y+3b-2b^2)||g_p||^2/2
      -(2y^2+3y+b)||g_z||^2/2
    = 2 E_R - F_p-F_z-(b-1)Q_(p,z)-Q_(z,p).          (P-decrease)

To check it without a black-box inequality, substitute twice the identity

    sum h_i Q_i* = F_j+y(f_j-||g_j||^2/2)
                  + <x_(p+1)-x_z,g_j-x_j>

into 2E_R, then use x_(p+1)=x_p-bg_p. Adding the two last Q terms cancels
the mixed product involving x_(p+1)-x_z and leaves exactly the displayed
two squared-gradient coefficients.

With s=x+b+y and C_L=x(x+1), C=s(s+1), expansion also gives

    E_P = E_L+E_R+(x+b)(f_p-f_z)
          +(C_L+b-b^2)||g_p||^2/2+(C_R-C)||g_z||^2/2.

The defining quadratic b^2+(x+y)b-(xy+2x+2y+2)=0 yields

    (x+b)(y+3b-2b^2)/(y+2-b)=b^2-b-C_L,
    (x+b)(2y^2+3y+b)/(y+2-b)=C-C_R.

Inserting (P-decrease) proves (P-array) and (P) by induction. This proves
the primitive certificate on every formal vector, not merely on a compressed
endpoint matrix.

## 3. Dominant finite-array identity

For a segment with sum y, let its mass be D=2y+1. We construct positive
weights v_i on ALL its samples, summing to D, and a nonnegative finite array
L_D such that

    E_D := ||x_a||^2/2 + sum v_i Q_i* - D f_z
           - ||x_a-sum v_i g_i||^2/2
         = -sum L_D(i,j) Q_ij.                        (D)

For the empty segment take v_a=1 and L_D=0. The identity then follows by
expanding Q_a*.

Join a primitive left segment of sum x to a dominant right segment of mass
D=2y+1, with its weights v and array L_R. Set A=x+1 and

    mu=2A/D,
    r=(1+sqrt(1+8A/D))/2,
    lambda=r^2=r+mu,
    gamma=A+1=x+2,
    b=1+A/r=psi(x,y).

The new weights u and finite array are

    u_i=h_i                  (i<p),
    u_p=gamma,
    u_i=r v_i                (p<i<=z),
    L_D=L_L+lambda L_R+mu sum_{p<i<=z} v_i E_(i,p).   (D-array)

They have the exact mass

    M=sum u_i=x+gamma+rD=2A+rD=Dr^2
      =G(A,D)=2(x+b+y)+1.

For completeness, the whole algebra follows from the more general identity
in section 6. Setting these parameters makes all three entries of its mixed
matrix K zero: gamma=A+1 gives K_11=0, lambda=r^2 gives K_22=0, and
lambda b=mu+gamma r gives K_12=0. The value-flow equality is mu D=x+gamma.
Thus (D) follows from (P), the right child identity, and the displayed fan.
There is no discarded nonnegative square or omitted mixed term.

## 4. The actual full certificate at exactly 1/B_n

Apply section 3 recursively to the deterministic word d^(n). Its mass is
M=B_n. On I_n={*,0,...,n}, set

    lambda_(i,*)=2u_i/B_n,
    lambda_(*,i)=0,
    lambda_(i,j)=2L_D(i,j)/B_n  (finite i!=j).

Then the exact full identity is

    ||x_0||^2/B_n - 2f_n + sum lambda_ij Q_ij
       = ||x_0-sum u_i g_i||^2/B_n.                  (Full)

Every coefficient and every formal-vector term has now been specified.
The function-value flow is out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n), by equating the independent
f_i coefficients in (D). The remainder is a full rank-one PSD quadratic.
Its kernel is x_0=sum u_i g_i. It is not a PSD assertion on a quotient.

The actual source array has no incoming terminal edge. This follows
inductively from (D-array): its left subtree is strictly before the final
sample, and every new edge involving that sample leaves it. Also
u_n=sqrt(B_n), by the dominant recursion u_n=r v_n and B_n=r^2 D.
Consequently, in the exact terminal framework of accepted1252b8823bb5a290,

    alpha_star=1/sqrt(B_n), alpha_j=L_D(n,j)/B_n (j<n),
    V_alpha=(x_0-sum_{i<n}u_i g_i)/sqrt(B_n),
    R_alpha=0 IDENTICALLY on the entire original prefix space.       (Terminal)

The probabilities sum to one by the terminal value flow. Indeed (Full) is
exactly ||g_n-V_alpha||^2, and the terminal identity of that accepted fact
then gives the displayed zero prefix remainder. This records the full
baseline kernel and its mixed-block normalization explicitly; the claim is
not just that R_alpha vanishes on one extremal trajectory.

The legal canonical Huber instance in accepted0be8b54e0a33381c, with
x_0=1, x_star=0, threshold 1/B_n, gives 2f_n=1/B_n for this physical word.
Consequently the constructed upper bound is attained: W_n(d^(n))=1/B_n.

Some explicit horizons also check the orientation and normalization. Put
rho=1+sqrt(2).

* n=1: d=(3/2), B_1=4, u=(2,2), L_(1,0)=2.
  Thus lambda_(1,0)=lambda_(0,*)=lambda_(1,*)=1 and the remainder is
  ||x_0-2g_0-2g_1||^2/4.
* n=2: put z=sqrt(9+8sqrt(2)). The maximizing split is k=1 and
  d=(sqrt(2),(3+z)/4), B_2=(5+4sqrt(2)+z)/2.
  The weights are u=(sqrt(2),2+sqrt(2),(1+z)/2).
  The ONLY finite entries are L_(0,1)=1, L_(1,0)=rho,
  L_(2,1)=2rho. The full multipliers are 2L/B_2 and 2u/B_2.
* n=3: the maximizing split is k=1,
  d=(sqrt(2),1+sqrt(2),3/2), B_3=6+4sqrt(2),
  u=(sqrt(2),2+sqrt(2),2+sqrt(2),2+sqrt(2)).
  The ONLY finite entries are
  L_(0,1)=1, L_(1,0)=rho, L_(2,1)=rho,
  L_(3,1)=rho, L_(3,2)=rho^2.

Here the small split comparisons can themselves be checked exactly. At n=2,
G(1,4)=4+2sqrt(3)<15/2, whereas G(rho,1)>15/2: use
sqrt(2)>45/32 and sqrt(2)>7/5 to obtain
sqrt(9+8sqrt(2))>9/2 and the latter strict bound. At n=3, B_2<8 since
rho<5/2 and G(5/2,1)=(11+sqrt(21))/2<8. Thus
G(1,B_2)<G(1,8)=6+4sqrt(2). Also
P_2=(2+sqrt(2)+sqrt(10+8sqrt(2)))/2<(4+3sqrt(2))/2,
because (2+2sqrt(2))^2=12+8sqrt(2)>10+8sqrt(2).
The inverse relation G(A,1)=M iff A=(M-sqrt(M))/2 shows
G(P_2,1)<6+4sqrt(2), while G(rho,4)=6+4sqrt(2).

## 5. A second exact tight instance and full-array implications

For a primitive source word of mass A,

    product_i |1-h_i|=1/A.                            (Q-P)

Indeed it is 1 for the empty word. At a primitive join, put C=Omega(A,E)
and d=b-1. Then C=A+E+d and dC=AE, so the joined product is
d/(AE)=1/C. Similarly the dominant source word satisfies

    product_i |1-h_i|=1/sqrt(B_n).                    (Q-D)

The dominant induction is d/(A sqrt(D)) with d=A/r and B_n=Dr^2.
The actual scalar function f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1, therefore gives exactly
2f_n=product_i(1-h_i)^2=1/B_n. It is a second normalized tight instance.

Any full certificate, however its multipliers and rank are reselected, obeys
for a changed nonnegative word h'=h+e

    q B_n >= max{B_n/(B_n+2sum e_i),
                 product_i(1+e_i/(h_i-1))^2}.        (Two tests)

The second expression is valid without assuming h'_i>1 because it is
squared; when logs are used below require h'_i>1. The first is the canonical
Huber bound with the TRUE new step sum, the second the actual unit quadratic.
In particular qB_n<=1-delta, delta in (0,1), requires

    sum e_i >= delta B_n/[2(1-delta)],
    sum log(1+e_i/(h_i-1)) <= log(1-delta)/2           (if h'_i>1).

For a differentiable one-sided continuation h(t),q(t) at t=0 this gives

    q'(0) >= -2 B_n^(-2) sum h_i'(0),
    q'(0) >= (2/B_n) sum h_i'(0)/(h_i-1).            (Tangent tests)

These are NECESSARY only. At the exact baseline, complementarity on the
Huber instance forces every optimum-source multiplier lambda_(*,i) to be
zero, for n>=1: Q_(*,i)=tau(tau-x_i)<0, since s(h)>0 and
x_i>tau. This conclusion applies to every tight baseline certificate,
not merely the particular source array. It does NOT force those entries
to remain zero after a perturbation with non-Huber worst-case behavior.

## 6. Exact obstruction for a relaxed one-fan dominant join

This class changes the source coupling and bridge, including signed
perturbations of every positive parameter within their final sign constraints.
It is strictly more general than fixing b=psi or fixing the rank-one remainder.
It still retains a specified interface and a single cross fan; it is not the
full cone of arbitrary cross-copy interpolation edges.

Take ANY primitive left certificate of the form

    E_L+sum L_L Q = R_L,

and ANY sharp dominant right certificate of the form

    E_R+sum L_R Q = R_R,

where E_L and E_R have the definitions above, D=2y+1, sum v_i=D,
the child finite arrays are nonnegative, and R_L,R_R are full PSD quadratics.
The steps and arrays inside either child need not be their source selections.
Allow an arbitrary bridge b>=0 and parameters

    gamma>=0, lambda>=mu>=0, r=lambda-mu,
    mu D=x+gamma.                                   (Flow)

The new optimum-sink weights and finite array are

    u=(h_left,gamma,r v),
    L=L_L+lambda L_R+mu sum v_i E_(i,p),
    M=x+gamma+rD>0.

Positive child weights and multipliers may be independently reselected so
long as their displayed child identities remain true. No sign restriction
is placed on their DERIVATIVES; only the final nonnegative arrays are required.
Let V=sum_{right} v_i g_i and A=x+1. Direct expansion on the original space
gives the exact identity

    ||x_0||^2/2 + sum u_i Q_i* - M f_z + sum L_ij Q_ij
    = ||x_p-gamma g_p-rV||^2/2
      + R_L+lambda R_R
      + (K_11||g_p||^2+2K_12<g_p,V>+K_22||V||^2)/2, (Join)

where the ENTIRE mixed block is

    K_11=A^2-(gamma-1)^2,
    K_22=lambda-r^2,
    K_12=lambda b-mu-gamma r.                        (K)

To verify the identity, use

    sum v_i Q_i* = sum v_i Q_(i,p)
                  +D(f_p-||g_p||^2/2)+<V,g_p-x_p>,

multiply the right certificate by lambda, subtract mu times this identity,
add the left certificate and gamma(Q_p*-f_z), and substitute
x_(p+1)=x_p-bg_p. The coefficient of f_p-f_z is
x+gamma-mu D and hence is zero. Completing the indicated square leaves
x(x+1)+mu D+gamma-gamma^2=A^2-(gamma-1)^2,
lambda-r^2, and lambda b-mu-gamma r as claimed.

The condition K PSD is necessary for the FULL parent quadratic to be PSD,
even if both child remainders have arbitrarily large ranks. Here is why this
is stronger than an unsupported endpoint compression. Put all left formal
gradients, INCLUDING g_p, equal to an arbitrary vector a, and all right
gradients equal to an independent arbitrary vector c. Choose affine function
values separately on each child: f_i=f_child_end+(remaining child step sum)
times its constant gradient norm squared. All within-child Q vanish. Direct
substitution gives E_L=0 and E_R=D(2y+1-D)||c||^2/2=0. Thus
R_L=R_R=0 on this restriction for EVERY such child certificate. Moreover
V=Dc, and choosing x_0=(x+gamma)a+rDc makes the first square zero.
All choices of a,c are still available, so the restriction is precisely K.
This is a legitimate test of a full formal PSD matrix; it does not claim these
independent constants are one legal primal trajectory.

It follows that

    gamma<=A+1,
    r^2-r-(x+gamma)/D<=0.

Let w=x+gamma. Then w<=2A and

    M=w+rD <= w+(D+sqrt(D^2+4Dw))/2 <= G(A,D).        (Mass cap)

Both scalar expressions are strictly increasing in w>=0. Equality forces

    gamma=A+1, mu=2A/D,
    r=(1+sqrt(1+8A/D))/2, lambda=r^2.

At equality both diagonals of K are zero. PSD then forces the mixed entry
to vanish too, giving b=(mu+gamma r)/lambda=1+A/r=psi(x,y).
Thus the exact source mass is the UNIQUE maximizing local parameter choice
within this relaxed join, including its bridge. A positive extra remainder
does not buy a larger mass because the independently constant child modes
annihilate every sharp child remainder.

This is a finite inequality, not an infinitesimal one. Apply it at any number
of dominant nodes with primitive prefix sums at most S_circle of their
lengths and sharp dominant children. At a node of total length n, the exact
DP monotonicity gives M<=G(P_k,B_l)<=B_n inductively. The root need only have
the displayed valid certificate of level 1/M; it need not itself be sharp.
Consequently this entire recursive one-fan family cannot certify
q B_n<1 at ANY horizon. It allows changes at unboundedly many scales and a
changed bridge rule, so its obstruction is not just the fixed finite
terminal-library result. Its retained hypotheses are the sharp child
interfaces, the physical primitive prefix weights, and the single cross fan.
Non-Huber children, independent history weights, extra interior cross edges,
and couplings outside this construction remain open.

## 7. A separate global schedule class, with unrestricted full re-selection

Let n>=1, h=d^(n), and a_i=h_i-1>0. Let T be ANY n-by-n doubly stochastic
matrix (nonnegative entries; every row and column sums to one), and c>=0.
Define a new actual word in its new chronological order by

    h'_i=1+c(Ta)_i.                                  (Mix)

Then

    W_n(h')>=1/B_n.                                  (Mix obstruction)

No hypothesis whatsoever is made here on its certificate array, its rank,
or its worst-case function. This class includes every permutation, arbitrary
mixing of different scales, and any common dilation or contraction of the
positive step gaps; most such words are not ConPD words.

Proof. Since column sums of T equal one,
s(h')=n+c sum a_i. If 0<=c<=1, the actual Huber lower bound is at least
1/(1+2s(h))=1/B_n. If c>=1, log concavity gives

    sum_i log((Ta)_i)
      >=sum_(i,j) T_ij log(a_j)=sum_j log(a_j).

The unit quadratic therefore gives

    W_n(h') >= c^(2n) product_i((Ta)_i)^2
             >= c^(2n) product_i a_i^2=c^(2n)/B_n.

This proves the finite, uniform claim. It does not exclude making the
normalized gap vector more dispersed, or incomparable in the majorization
order, nor any schedule with some entries below one.

## 8. What is still blocked

The original target asks for either a uniform matching all-schedule lower
bound, or one fixed delta>0 and a certified finite continuation with
q_n B_n<=1-delta on an explicit unbounded sequence. Neither follows here.

The all-horizon source word and full array are now explicit. The one-fan
closure and global gap mixing classes have exact finite obstructions.
The remaining useful variation must leave those classes. Passing (Two tests)
or (Tangent tests) alone is not a PSD continuation. In particular positive
optimum-source multipliers and a higher-rank remainder after deformation
are allowed by the original problem and must not be excluded by inference
from sharp baseline complementarity.

No verification authority was added by this reconstruction. This file and
all of its new conclusions remain draft evidence until selected verification.

evidence:
# C60: a nonlinear two-state legal trajectory with dense turning gradients

Status: **new explicit construction and scoped calculations; UNVERIFIED**.
No solve or verifier call is used. The numerical allocation is closed.
This branch follows the finite C59 reconstruction by seeking an analytic
correlated core. It does not assume that the C59 data belong to this family.

The construction works for every finite nonnegative schedule, including
zeros and arbitrarily large entries, with one fixed globally convex
1-smooth function. Its all-pair law and true closest-minimizer distance
are explicit. The quantitative payoff on the critical H_m remains open.

## 1. The global function, its gradients, and its minimizers

In R^2 let

    C_par={(t,s): s>=t^2/sqrt(2)},
    F_par(X)=sup_(g in C_par) [<X,g>-||g||^2/2].      (1)

The set is closed, convex and nonempty, and contains0. Completing the
square shows that the maximizer in (1) is the Euclidean projection of X
onto C_par. It exists and is unique because the squared-distance objective
is coercive and strictly convex. Thus F_par is finite and convex.

For completeness write p(X) for that projection. Its elementary normal
condition is

    <X-p(X),g-p(X)><=0 for every g in C_par.

Applying this twice and adding gives

    ||p(X)-p(Y)||^2<=<p(X)-p(Y),X-Y>.

Thus p is1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizers in (1) gives

    0<=F_par(Y)-F_par(X)-<p(X),Y-X>
        <=<p(Y)-p(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

Consequently F_par is differentiable, its gradient is p, and it is
1-smooth. This proof supplies the needed global property directly.

The minimizers are exactly

    argmin F_par={(0,y):y<=0}.                      (2)

Indeed F_par>=0 by the feasible vector0. For X=(0,y), y<=0, every g=(t,s)
in C_par has <X,g>=ys<=0, so the maximum in (1) is0. Conversely, if
the vertical coordinate y>0, taking g=(0,s) with small s>0 makes the
objective positive. If the horizontal coordinate x is nonzero and y<=0,
take g=(t,t^2/sqrt(2)) with sufficiently small nonzero t of the sign of x:
the linear term xt dominates the terms of quadratic and quartic order.
This again makes the objective positive. These cases prove (2).

This F_par is not a convex quadratic: its minimizer set is a ray, whereas
the nonempty minimizer set of an unconstrained convex quadratic is an
affine subspace.

## 2. Coordinates that make every interpolation pair explicit

For a real r and v>=0, put

    u=v+r^2,
    X(r,v)=(r(1+v+r^2), -v/sqrt(2)),
    G(r)=(r,r^2/sqrt(2)).                           (3)

Then X-G=u(r,-1/sqrt(2)). For any (t,s) in C_par,

    <X-G,(t,s)-G>
      =u[r(t-r)-(s-r^2/sqrt(2))/sqrt(2)]
      <=-(u/2)(t-r)^2<=0.

The normal condition therefore proves that G(r) is the actual gradient
of F_par at X(r,v). Direct substitution into (1) gives

    F_par(X(r,v))=r^2(1+v)/2+3r^4/4.                (4)

For any two sampled states r_i,v_i and r_j,v_j, with the actual values
from (4), the complete signed interpolation residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =-(u_j/2)(r_i-r_j)^2<=0.                   (5)

The first equality after Q follows by substituting
f_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2. The second uses the displayed parabolic
coordinates. This proves EVERY ordered pair simultaneously for one
function; no local, adjacent, or cycle relaxation is being used.

For an initial nonzero r_0 and v_0>=0, the closest minimizer in (2) is

    X_star=(0,-v_0/sqrt(2)),
    R_0^2=dist(X_0,argmin F_par)^2
            =r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2.                (6)

The optimum sample fits the same formulas with r_star=0, v_star=v_0,
u_star=v_0. Thus (5) includes both of its directions. Choosing the origin
instead would generally overestimate the true initial distance; (6) is
the normalization used throughout.

## 3. The exact GD transition, with no interpolation optimization

For ANY step h>=0, starting from state(r,v), define

    v_plus=v+h r^2,
    r_plus^3+(1+v_plus)r_plus
                      =r(1+v+r^2-h).              (7)

The cubic's left side is strictly increasing from minus infinity to
plus infinity because its derivative is1+v_plus+3r_plus^2>=1. Thus (7)
defines exactly one real r_plus, by an explicit scalar algebraic rule.
There is no nearest-feasible-trajectory problem hidden in this definition.

The vertical coordinate of X-hG is -v_plus/sqrt(2), and its horizontal
coordinate is the right side of (7). Hence

    X(r_plus,v_plus)=X(r,v)-h G(r).

This proves actual GD for the same global function. In particular h=0
leaves the state unchanged, and every finite positive step gives finite
new state. All v_i remain nonnegative, regardless of gradient sign changes.

For a supplied finite nonnegative schedule h_0,...,h_(n-1), iterate (7)
from any r_0!=0,v_0>=0. Its exact normalized payoff is

    P_par(h;r_0,v_0)
       =[r_n^2(1+v_n)+(3/2)r_n^4]
                        /[r_0^2(1+v_0+r_0^2)^2].  (8)

The function (1), all values(4), gradients(3), positions(3), and initial
distance(6) are fixed together. Thus (8) is an actual lower witness for
W_n(h), albeit not yet a profile-strength one on the critical schedules.

Some immediate identities expose the changing geometry:

    u_plus-u=(h-1)r^2+r_plus^2,
    X_plus,horizontal=X_horizontal[1-h/(1+u)].      (9)

In particular, for schedules with all h>=1, the normal parameter u is
nondecreasing, but r and the horizontal gradient can turn repeatedly.
The Hessian direction changes with r; this is not a fixed linear spectral
transcript. The vertical state accumulates h r^2 rather than discarding
previous turns.

## 4. Exact dense-jump calibration on a different schedule

Take any sigma in(0,1), v_0>=0, and define

    U_0=1+v_0+sigma,
    rho=(1+sigma)/(1-sigma),
    h_i=2U_0 rho^i/(1-sigma),
    r_i=(-1)^i sqrt(sigma),
    v_i=U_0 rho^i-1-sigma.                         (10)

These v_i are nonnegative. Substitution into (7) gives
v_(i+1)-v_i=h_i sigma and
r_(i+1)(1+v_(i+1)+sigma)=r_i(1+v_i+sigma-h_i),
so (10) is an exact trajectory of F_par. Its payoff is

    P_par=rho^n/U_0+sigma/(2U_0^2).                 (11)

This calibration is legal and can have large payoff. It is a geometric
step sequence, NOT the critical ruler word, so (11) proves no claim about
H_m or the original profile. It only checks that the mechanism supports
correlated turns without a feasibility repair.

There are n nonzero collinear gradient jumps in (10):

    G_i-G_(i-1)=(2(-1)^i sqrt(sigma),0), 1<=i<=n.

Their Gram J has trace4sigma n and twice the absolute off-diagonal sum
4sigma n(n-1). For any Gram realizable with at most k nonzero jumps in
each orthonormal coordinate, Cauchy--Schwarz coordinate by coordinate
implies2sum_(i<j)|J_ij|<=(k-1)trace(J). Hence this trajectory requires
some coordinate with at least n jumps in every orthonormal realization.
Dense chronological correlation does not require a large ambient dimension.

For a completely rational parameter example, sigma=1/4 and v_0=0 give
rho=5/3, h_0=10/3, h_1=50/9, and r_i=(-1)^i/2. Formula (11) is then
an exact expression, not a numerical simulation.

## 5. Two simple parameter limits do not yet give the desired mechanism

First fix a finite schedule and fix v_0=A>=0. Let r_0=t tend to zero.
Induction in (7) gives

    v_i=A+O(t^2),
    r_i=t product_(j<i)[1-h_j/(1+A)]+O(t^3).

At each induction step, the inverse cubic has nonzero derivative1+A
at zero, and its cubic term is O(t^3), giving the displayed expansion.
Thus the payoff tends to the ordinary scalar quadratic value

    [1/(1+A)] product_(j<n)[1-h_j/(1+A)]^2.         (12)

The implicit constants here depend on the entire fixed finite schedule.
They have NOT been bounded uniformly along growing H_m. Consequently
(12) is a calibration and an explanation of why an infinitesimal core
does not itself add a new mechanism; it is not a class obstruction.

Second put S=sum h_i and sigma=r_0^2. If v_0>=S, no horizontal sign flip
occurs and |r_(i+1)|<=|r_i|. Indeed h_i<=v_i and the right side of (7)
has the sign of r_i. Evaluating the increasing cubic at r_i shows that
its excess over that right side is h_i r_i(1+r_i^2), with the appropriate
sign, so the claimed decrease in absolute value follows. Hence

    v_n<=v_0+S sigma,
    P_par <= [1+v_0+S sigma+(3/2)sigma]
                                  /(1+v_0+sigma)^2. (13)

Along any growing-horizon choices with
v_0/[S(1+sigma)] tending to infinity, this gives S P_par tending to zero.
Thus placing the initial state arbitrarily far down the flat minimizer
direction also loses the desired scale. This rules out only the displayed
parameter regime; intermediate coupled regimes remain open.

## 6. The natural geometric calibration is small on the entire critical word

One tempting choice is to match the geometric growth ratio rho in(10)
to the physical critical parameter c_m. This means

    m>=128, epsilon=1/m,
    c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    sigma=(c-1)/(c+1), r_0=sqrt(sigma), v_0=0.       (14)

For THIS particular starting rule, the full actual H_m trajectory obeys

    P_par(H_m;r_0,0)
              < (2500/m^2) 2^(-2^m).              (15)

The same is true with the opposite initial horizontal sign, by symmetry.
This does not bound the family over other choices of r_0,v_0.

Here is a proof that tracks all later queried states, rather than inferring
the answer only from the first cancellation. Elementary parameter bounds are

    12/5<c<5/2, 2/5<a<3/7,
    2/5<sigma<3/7, 7/5<b0=1+a<10/7.

For the lower bound on a, use 1+sqrt(2)<17/7 and
(1-epsilon)/(1+epsilon)>=127/129, giving a>889/2193>2/5.
The other inequalities follow by direct comparison of positive fractions.
Since c is greater than1+sqrt(2),

    0<sigma-a
      =epsilon[2lambda(lambda-1)+lambda^2 epsilon+c+1]
                                               /[c(c+1)]
      <2epsilon, lambda=1+sqrt(2).                 (16)

For the last bound the numerator in brackets is less than12, using
lambda<5/2 and epsilon<=1/128, while c(c+1)>204/25>8.

At the first actual step b0, (7) gives

    14/25<v_1=b0 sigma<30/49<5/8,
    r_1(1+v_1+r_1^2)=r_0(sigma-a),
    0<r_1<2/m.                                    (17)

We now prove that the entire remaining trajectory stays in the region

    1/2<=v<=3/4, |r|<=1/10.                        (18)

Inside this region the exact step rule gives explicit amplitude bounds.
For a level-zero step b0, the numerator factor
1+v+r^2-b0 is positive and at most1+3/4+1/100-7/5=9/25.
The denominator1+v_plus+r_plus^2 is at least3/2, so

    |r_plus| <= L0 |r|, L0=1/4.

For a level j>=1 step b_j=1+a c^j, one has b_j>=2-epsilon>1.76,
whereas1+v+r^2<=1.76. The numerator is therefore negative, and

    |r_plus| <= Lj |r|, Lj=(2/7)c^j.               (19)

Indeed its absolute value is less than a c^j and its denominator is at
least3/2, while a<3/7. These bounds use the current state in (18) but
do not require the next state to be in that region.

Let P_j be the product of these scalar bounds over the full word H_j,
with P_0=1, and put A0=2/7 and beta=c^2/14<1/2. For j>=1,

    P_j=beta^(2^(j-1))/(A0 c^(j+1)),
    theta_j=P_j Lj=beta^(2^(j-1))/c<1.             (20)

This follows either by multiplying the known counts of each ruler level
or by P_(j+1)=P_j^2 Lj and P_1=1/4. Every prefix product in every H_j
is at most1: it is true for H_0; in the right child the left-child and
central-step prefactor is P_j Lj=theta_j<1, and the induction applies
inside both children. At j=0 that prefactor is1/4.

For the accumulated vertical drift, let E_j be the weighted prefix sum

    E_j=sum_(i in H_j) h_i [product_(t<i)L_(level(t))]^2.

Then E_1=b0<3/2 and, for j>=1,

    E_(j+1)=(1+theta_j^2)E_j+P_j^2 b_j.            (21)

The two needed infinite bounds are elementary. Since c>2,beta<1/2,

    sum_(j>=1)theta_j^2
        <(1/4)sum_(j>=1)2^(-2^j)<=1/8.

Also b_j<c^j for j>=1: both a and c^(-j) are less than3/7. Therefore

    sum_(j>=1)P_j^2 b_j
       <sum_(j>=1)49*2^(-2j-5)=49/96.

For this estimate insert(20), use A0^(-2)=49/4, c>2,
beta^(2^j)<2^(-2^j), and2^j>=j+1. Finally
product(1+theta_j^2)<=1/[1-sum theta_j^2]<8/7,
as follows by expanding the finite products and bounding their elementary
symmetric sums by powers of the total sum. Passing to the limit preserves
the bound. Equations(21) consequently imply

    E_j<(3/2+49/96)(8/7)=193/84<3                 (22)

for every j.

In the suffix of H_m after its first step, every prefix product is at
most4, because reinserting that first L0 multiplies it by1/4. The suffix
weighted drift sum is at most16E_m<48. Hence, as long as(18) has held,

    |r_i|<=4r_1<8/m<=1/16<1/10,
    v_i<=v_1+48r_1^2<5/8+192/m^2<3/4.

The lower bound v_i>=v_1>1/2 follows from v_plus=v+h r^2. These strict
bounds prove(18) throughout by a first-exit argument: the same estimates
control a proposed first exiting step, which is impossible.

At the terminal sample the entire suffix product is4P_m. From(17),(20),

    r_n^2<(64/m^2)P_m^2.

The numerator of(8) is less than2r_n^2 by(18), and the initial denominator
sigma(1+sigma)^2 exceeds98/125>3/4. Thus

    P_par<3r_n^2<(192/m^2)P_m^2
          <(2352/m^2)2^(-2^m),

which proves(15). For the exact benchmark, accepted factb98bb807d514e80d
gives B_n<=1+4n^(log_2 3), so this particular parabolic witness divided
by U_n^ZJ tends to zero. Only this fixed starting rule is excluded.

The responsible state variable is visible in(17): matching the geometric
ratio makes the critical first step almost annihilate the horizontal
coordinate. The subsequent normal state remains near its post-first-step
value, and the complete ruler-product/drift bounds above prevent recovery.
This is a statement about the entire actual legal trajectory, not a
one-pair dual test or a comparison with an independently reset right child.

## 7. The concrete remaining critical-word problem

For the actual critical word fix, within each horizon m,

    c_m=(1+sqrt(2))(1+1/m), a_m=(1-1/m)/c_m,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_m c_m^j,H_j).

Let T_h denote the explicit two-state transition (7). The full block map
is defined EXACTLY by

    Phi_0=identity,
    Phi_(j+1)=Phi_j composed with T_(1+a_m c_m^j)
                                     composed with Phi_j.

The central task in this branch is to select explicit r_0(m),v_0(m), or
prove a useful uniform upper bound for this mechanism, while controlling
the exact payoff (8) under Phi_m. The model is already an actual legal
function for every such selection, so no separate interpolation optimization
is required. What is missing is the QUANTITATIVE estimate on that nonlinear
recursion. Neither (11), the small-amplitude calibration, nor (13) fills it.

An open subgoal is to compare the increase in v across both copies of a
dyadic block with the horizontal sign and gain at its central bridge.
The state v must remain shared between the copies; restarting it, freezing
the curvature, or replacing the two copies by independent instances would
change the function and lose the construction.

## 8. Source grounding and verification scope

Jiang, Yue and Zhou, arXiv:1911.12545v2 (2021), Theorem2.2, gives the
Euclidean projection onto S={(x,y):||x||^2<=y}: inside S it is the point,
and outside it is(x/(1+mu),y+mu/2), where mu>=max(0,-2y) is the unique
solution of ||x||^2/(1+mu)^2=y+mu/2. The paper's surrounding definition
of S and full proof were read. It supplies a closely matched projection
mechanism, not a GD complexity result for the present function. Its
cubic-regularization convergence theorem is not invoked.

Sections1--6 derive the two-dimensional specialization and all required
properties directly. No external theorem is used as a black box, and no
unverified earlier project result is a premise. The finite C59 data merely
motivated seeking dense turning gradients. Every new statement here remains
a draft until accepted by the verifier; no claim is made that this family
solves the all-schedule exact-profile problem.
