evidence:
# Positive-height signed interval simplexes: construction and a scoped loss

Status: **complete joint draft, not verifier accepted**. No optimization,
installation, or fact submission is used. Accepted facts
`1252b8823bb5a290` and `b98bb807d514e80d` supply, respectively, the
smooth-convex interpolation convention and the exact benchmark recursions.
Every other assertion used below is proved in this document. The sharper
benchmark comparison was recalled from shared finding `70e9da73936cb7b3`
as a lead; its complete elementary proof is included here and that finding
is not a correctness premise.

This is a new positive-height construction, rather than an extension of
the previous zero-height bound. It gives one explicit finite-dimensional
projection function, one value array, the actual initial distance, all
original interpolation pairs, and a two-increment Gram decomposition.
All endpoint heights after the first can be strictly positive.

The quantitative conclusion is a failure of a precisely specified rule:
after a coordinate vanishes from the gradient, its proximal coordinate is
set to zero. Uniformly over every dyadic cutoff and every legal amplitude
choice in this rule, on the actual H_m with m>=128,

    V_can < (275/648)/M_m < 1/(2M_m) < 1/(2M_m-1).

Here V_can is the normalized last objective. For the exact benchmark,

    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup V_can
        <= 275/[162 exp(1)] < 1.

This does not bound the unrestricted W_n(H_m), all positive-height
reflection/extinction histories, or the full two-increment cone.
Section 8 identifies the missing signed residual and an exact necessary
propagation condition. Section 9 refutes a forward-only repair on the
actual H_m with an explicit positive residual in an original pair.

## 1. The physical schedule and the generating rule

Fix m>=128. Throughout this whole horizon, put

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), c_rul=sigma(1+1/m),
    a_rul=(1-1/m)/c_rul,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_rul c_rul^j,H_j),
    M_j=1+sum H_j, n=2^m-1.

The parameters are not recomputed inside the recursion. Choose an integer
0<=ell<m, and put q=m-ell, k=2^q-1, C=M_ell. Then the exact word is

    H_m=(H_ell,1+r_0,H_ell,...,1+r_(k-1),H_ell),
    r_j=a_rul c_rul^(ell+nu_2(j+1)), 0<=j<k.             (1)

The integer nu_2(v) is the largest d for which 2^d divides v. Each of
the k+1 ordinary cells has mass C-1. Its ending query is the checkpoint
query, except in the last cell, where it is the original terminal sample.
In particular the physical final step is never changed.

In R^k with its orthonormal coordinate vectors e_0,...,e_(k-1), choose
positive amplitudes Aamp_j,Bamp_j for 0<=j<k, and define

    p_0=sum_(l=0)^(k-1) Aamp_l e_l,
    p_j=-Bamp_(j-1)e_(j-1)+sum_(l=j)^(k-1)Aamp_l e_l,
                                                    1<=j<=k.       (2)

Thus coordinate l is initially Aamp_l, becomes -Bamp_l in cell l+1,
and then vanishes. There is no persistent extra coordinate in this rule.
Set

    P_can=conv{p_0,...,p_k},
    F_can(x)=max_(v in P_can)(<x,v>-||v||^2/2),
    X_0=C p_0.                                                     (3)

The family being screened consists of actual trajectories of this ONE
function starting from this X_0 and having the gradients in (2) on their
whole respective cells. The initial endpoint has proximal point zero.

Let Z_j be the endpoint of cell j and Y_j=Z_j-p_j. Actual GD with these
cell gradients requires

    Y_0=0,  Y_(j+1)=Y_j-r_j p_j-Cp_(j+1).                         (4)

A query inside cell j, with remaining ordinary mass u in [0,C-1], has

    X_(j,u)=Y_j+(1+u)p_j.                                         (5)

Introduce one freely chosen parameter r_k>=0. It is a terminal shape
parameter, NOT an additional physical step. Define

    wpre_0=r_0,  wpre_j=C+r_j (1<=j<=k),
    Rpre_j=sum_(v=0)^(j-1)wpre_v (1<=j<=k+1),
    Lpre_j=Rpre_j+C.

The extra hypothesis of the cancellation rule is

    Bamp_(j-1)=Rpre_j Aamp_(j-1)/(C+r_j), 1<=j<=k.                 (6)

For j<k this says exactly that coordinate j-1 of the proximal point
becomes zero after that coordinate leaves the gradient. For j=k,
(6) just parameterizes the terminal amplitude with nonnegative terminal
height. Indeed that height is
Rpre_k Aamp_(k-1)Bamp_(k-1)-C Bamp_(k-1)^2.
Every positive terminal amplitude with nonnegative height has a unique
r_k>=0 in (6).

Directly expanding (4) coordinate by coordinate gives

    Y_j=-r_j Bamp_(j-1)e_(j-1)
               -Lpre_j sum_(l=j)^(k-1)Aamp_l e_l, 1<=j<=k.        (7)

For example, an older coordinate l<j-1 has coefficient
-Rpre_(l+1)Aamp_l+(C+r_(l+1))Bamp_l=0 by (6). The current coordinate
is C Bamp_(j-1)-Rpre_j Aamp_(j-1)=-r_j Bamp_(j-1).
An untouched coordinate l>=j accumulates the coefficient -Lpre_j.

Put

    Ecan_j=sum_(l=j)^(k-1)Aamp_l^2,  Ecan_k=0,
    Ncan_0=Ecan_0, Ncan_j=Ecan_j+Bamp_(j-1)^2 (j>=1),
    Kcan_j=Ecan_j-Aamp_(j-1)Bamp_(j-1) (j>=1).

Coordinate multiplication gives

    ||p_j||^2=Ncan_j,
    <p_i,p_j>=Kcan_j whenever i<j.                                (8)

These are correlated gradients, generally with negative cross products.
Their full initial norm is C^2 Ecan_0. Also, independently of r_k,

    M_m=Rpre_k+2C.                                                (9)

Both sides equal (k+1)C+sum_(j<k)r_j by counting the physical cells.

## 2. One explicit amplitude law and one smooth convex function

Choose any r_k>0, for example r_k=C. All Rpre_j,Lpre_j are now explicit
finite real numbers. Set Aamp_0=1. Use (6) to determine Bamp_0. For
j=1,...,k-1 recursively set

    Aamp_j^2 = r_j Bamp_(j-1)^2 /
                 [Lpre_j(1+Rpre_(j+1)/(C+r_(j+1)))],
    Aamp_j = positive square root of the preceding expression,
    Bamp_j = Rpre_(j+1) Aamp_j/(C+r_(j+1)).                       (10)

Every amplitude is positive. These are finite formulas; no feasibility
problem or optimization is hidden in the definition. Their key identity is

    Lpre_j Aamp_j(Aamp_j+Bamp_j)=r_j Bamp_(j-1)^2,
                                                       1<=j<k.  (11)

We first justify the function in (3). Projection onto the compact convex
set P_can has a unique minimizer of squared distance. Completing the
square in (3) makes this projection its unique maximizing v. A vector p
in P_can is the projection of x precisely when

    <x-p,v-p><=0 for every v in P_can.                            (12)

Necessity follows by considering the segment from p to v. Sufficiency
follows by expanding ||x-v||^2. Applying (12) at x and x' and adding gives
||p-p'||^2<=<p-p',x-x'>, hence the projection is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing
the two maxima in (3) gives

    0<=F_can(x')-F_can(x)-<p,x'-x>
        <=<p'-p,x'-x><=||x'-x||^2.

Thus F_can is everywhere finite, convex, differentiable, and 1-smooth,
with gradient the projection onto P_can.

The origin is in the interior of P_can. To exhibit its barycentric
coefficients, choose alpha_0>0 and recursively set

    alpha_(l+1)=(Aamp_l/Bamp_l)sum_(i=0)^l alpha_i,

then choose alpha_0 so the total sum is 1. Every coefficient is positive,
and the l-th coordinate of sum alpha_i p_i is zero. The vectors
p_1,...,p_k are linearly independent: their coordinate matrix is triangular
with nonzero diagonal -Bamp_0,...,-Bamp_(k-1). The same coordinate
recursion makes the space of linear relations among all k+1 vertices
one-dimensional. Its positive generating relation has nonzero sum, so
there is no affine dependence. Consequently P_can is a full-dimensional
simplex and the displayed positive convex combination is interior.

Since 0 is an interior point, the only vector x satisfying
<x,v><=0 for all v in P_can is 0. By (12) this is precisely the set
of x with projection zero. Therefore F_can has UNIQUE minimizer 0,
F_can(0)=0, and its true initial squared distance is C^2 Ecan_0.

## 3. All original interpolation pairs, with shared positive heights

Define delta_can_j=<Y_j,p_j>. For j>=1, (7) gives

    delta_can_j=r_j Bamp_(j-1)^2-Lpre_j Ecan_j.                  (13)

For every s<j, coordinate multiplication gives

    <Y_j,p_s>=-r_j Aamp_(j-1)Bamp_(j-1)-Lpre_j Ecan_j
                 <=delta_can_j.                               (14)

For every s>j the corresponding value is

    <Y_j,p_s>=-Lpre_j Kcan_s.                                   (15)

To control ALL future vertices at once, use (6) and (11) to compute

    Kcan_(j+1)-Kcan_j
       =Aamp_(j-1)Bamp_(j-1)-Aamp_j(Aamp_j+Bamp_j)
       =C Bamp_(j-1)(Aamp_(j-1)+Bamp_(j-1))/Lpre_j >0.           (16)

Moreover Kcan_k=-Aamp_(k-1)Bamp_(k-1)<0, so every Kcan_j is negative.
Equation (11) also gives, for 1<=j<k,

    delta_can_j=-Lpre_j Kcan_(j+1)>0.                           (17)

Thus (15) is at most delta_can_j for every s>j, by (16).
The terminal height is delta_can_k=r_k Bamp_(k-1)^2>0. At j=0,
Y_0=0 satisfies every normal comparison with equality. Equations
(14)--(17) establish (12) at every endpoint, including against vertex 0,
which belongs to the convex hull. They retain both orientations and every
older and later vertex.

The same argument covers all original samples inside each ordinary cell.
For any i,j, <p_j,p_i-p_j><=0. For i<j, this follows from
Kcan_j-Ncan_j=-Bamp_(j-1)(Aamp_(j-1)+Bamp_(j-1))<0.
For i>j, Kcan_i<=Ecan_i<=Ecan_j<=Ncan_j. Add u times this inequality
to the endpoint normal, with u>=0. Thus (12) holds at every position (5),
and its actual gradient is p_j. Equations (4)--(5) now verify every
physical GD step on the original word.

There is ONE value array, namely

    f_(j,u)=delta_can_j+(u+1/2)Ncan_j.                          (18)

This is its actual value under F_can. For an explicit all-pair check,
the residual convention in accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290 is

    Q_ab=f_a-f_b+<g_a,X_b-X_a>+||g_a-g_b||^2/2.

Substituting (5),(18) gives exactly

    Q_((i,u),(j,v))=<Y_j+v p_j,p_i-p_j><=0.                   (19)

The inequalities against the optimum jet (0,0,0) are

    Q_((j,u),star)=0,
    Q_(star,(j,u))=-delta_can_j-u Ncan_j<=0.                   (20)

No independent selection of values for different pairs has occurred.
The normalized terminal objective is exactly

    V_can=(1+2r_k)Bamp_(k-1)^2/(C^2 Ecan_0).                 (21)

Finally, this legal trajectory belongs to the requested increment cone
by an explicit decomposition. In coordinate l<k-1 the only gradient
changes are -(Aamp_l+Bamp_l) at the transition from cell l to l+1,
and Bamp_l at the transition from cell l+1 to l+2. Coordinate k-1
has only its first change before the terminal sample. The Gram of all
gradient increments is the sum, over l, of the outer products of these
two-supported lists. Each is a real PSD block. For the full Gram retain
also the initial-vector and initial-gradient entries C Aamp_l and Aamp_l
in the same scalar coordinate lists. No original initial row or gradient
has been removed; every weight in this finite decomposition is 1.

## 4. Necessary product loss for EVERY legal cancellation-rule member

The amplitudes need not follow (10) in this section. Suppose any positive
amplitudes satisfying (6) give an actual trajectory of (3). The endpoint
normal comparing current j to future vertex j+1 is necessary. Equations
(13),(15) show that it is exactly

    Lpre_j Aamp_j(Aamp_j+Bamp_j)<=r_j Bamp_(j-1)^2,
                                                   1<=j<k.      (22)

Define

    lambda_can_j=r_j Rpre_j/[(C+r_j)(C+Rpre_j)] in (0,1).

Substituting (6) into (22) gives

    Aamp_j^2/Aamp_(j-1)^2
       <= [wpre_(j+1)/wpre_j] lambda_can_j
                                  [Rpre_j/Rpre_(j+2)].          (23)

Indeed Rpre_(j+2)=Rpre_(j+1)+wpre_(j+1), and the right side
expands to r_j Rpre_j^2 wpre_(j+1) divided by
wpre_j^2 Lpre_j(Rpre_(j+1)+wpre_(j+1)). This is precisely the
coefficient obtained from (22).

The products in (23) telescope, giving

    Bamp_(k-1)^2/Aamp_0^2
      <= Rpre_k r_0 Rpre_2 /
             [wpre_k wpre_1(Rpre_k+wpre_k)]
                     * product_(j=1)^(k-1)lambda_can_j.         (24)

For k=1 the empty-product identity still holds, with
Rpre_2=Rpre_1+wpre_1. For k>=2, the quantities r_0,Rpre_2,wpre_1
are physical prefix data, independent of the terminal shape parameter.

Let d_can=2C-1>=1. Combining Ecan_0>=Aamp_0^2 with (21),(24) yields

    V_can <= Rpre_k r_0 Rpre_2/(C^2 wpre_1)
          * (2wpre_k-d_can)/[wpre_k(Rpre_k+wpre_k)]
          * product_(j=1)^(k-1)lambda_can_j
      < 2r_0 Rpre_2/(C^2 wpre_1)
          * product_(j=1)^(k-1)lambda_can_j,  k>=2.              (25)

The last strict inequality follows from d_can>0 and Rpre_k>0.
It is uniform in every legal terminal amplitude and in all amplitudes
before it. Positive endpoint heights have not been set to zero.

## 5. Uniform loss on the actual ruler, over every cutoff

The physical mass recursion is M_(j+1)=2M_j+a_rul c_rul^j. Hence

    A_mass=a_rul/(c_rul-2),
    M_j=A_mass c_rul^j+(1-A_mass)2^j.                           (26)

For m>=128,

    sigma<c_rul<5/2,  3/8<a_rul<sigma-2<c_rul-2<1/2,
    3/4<A_mass<1,
    (3/4)c_rul^j<M_j<=c_rul^j.                                (27)

For explicit rational checks, sigma<17/7 implies
c_rul<2193/896<5/2; a_rul>(127/128)/(5/2)=127/320>3/8;
and a_rul<1/sigma=sigma-2. These prove every inequality used in (27).
Set t_can=a_rul c_rul^ell/C. Then

    0<t_can<c_rul-2<1/2,  M_m/C<(4/3)c_rul^q.                 (28)

For q>=2, the first three checkpoint excesses are
r_0=t_can C, r_1=c_rul t_can C, r_2=t_can C. Therefore

    2r_0 Rpre_2/(C^2 wpre_1)
       =(2t_can/C)[1+t_can/(1+c_rul t_can)]<3/(2C),
    lambda_can_1
       =[c_rul t_can/(1+c_rul t_can)]
           [t_can/(1+t_can)]<5/27.                            (29)

There are exactly 2^(q-1)-1 lowest-level checkpoints among indices
1,...,k-1. Each has lambda_can_j<1/3, because r_j=t_can C.
Index 1 is the first high checkpoint and is not among them. All other
factors are less than 1. Equations (25),(28),(29) give, for q>=3,

    M_m V_can
      < (10/27)(5/2)^q 3^(-(2^(q-1)-1))
      <=625/2916.                                             (30)

At q=3 the expression is 625/2916. Its ratio at q+1 to its value at q
is (5/2)3^(-2^(q-1))<1, proving the last inequality for every q>=3.

When q=2, k=3 and

    M_m/C=4+(2+c_rul)t_can<25/4,
    Rpre_2/C=1+(1+c_rul)t_can<11/4,
    lambda_can_2< (1/3)(11/15)=11/45.

The same product bound now gives the sharper estimate

    M_m V_can < (25/4)(3/2)(5/27)(11/45)=275/648.             (31)

When q=1, there is just one checkpoint. Writing A=Aamp_0,B=Bamp_0,
the terminal numerator before normalization is

    2r_0 AB-(2C-1)B^2 <= r_0^2 A^2/(2C-1).

Since M_m=(2+t_can)C and C=M_(m-1)>=2, this gives

    M_m V_can <=(2+t_can)t_can^2 C/(2C-1)<5/12.              (32)

As 5/12<275/648 and 625/2916<275/648, (30)--(32) prove

    sup_(all cutoffs and legal cancellation amplitudes)
          M_m V_can < gamma_can:=275/648<1/2.                (33)

The no-checkpoint, constant-gradient extension with terminal proximal
point zero has payoff 1/M_m^2 and also obeys this bound for m>=128.
It can be realized by the projection function for the segment [0,p],
starting at M_m p; zero is a closest minimizer. This degenerate extension
is not needed for the simplex construction in Sections 1--3.

In particular (33) is below the legal Huber witness 1/(2M_m-1), whose
existence is part of accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d. The new construction
therefore supplies no gain even over that baseline.

## 6. Comparison with the actual exact benchmark

For completeness, the required sharper scalar bound follows directly
from the EXACT recursions in accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d. Let
rho=log_2(sigma)>1. Their primitive shifted mass C_n=S_circle(n)+1
has join

    Omega(A,B)=[A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB)]/2,

and their dominant denominator B_n has join

    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

We prove

    C_n<=(n+1)^rho, B_n<=1+4n^rho.                            (34)

For t>0 set J(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. Differentiating with t=exp(z) gives

    d^2/dz^2 log J(exp(z))
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
            [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/J(t)^2 >0.

The bracket is positive because it vanishes at 0 and its derivative
rho[(1+t)^(rho-1)-1] is positive. Convexity at z and -z implies
J(t)J(1/t)>=J(1)^2=(sigma-1)^2=2. For A=t^rho B and
D=(1+t)^rho B, this says (D-A)(D-B)>=2AB, so
D^2-(A+B)D-AB>=0. The positive root of that polynomial is Omega(A,B).
Thus

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho,

including zero arguments by continuity. Induction in the exact primitive
recursion proves the first bound in (34). Also G(A,D)<=4A+D, since
sqrt(D^2+8AD)<=D+4A. Induct in the dominant recursion and use
(k+1)^rho+(n-k-1)^rho<=n^rho to prove its second bound. The last
power inequality follows by integrating the increasing derivative of
x^rho; it includes a zero summand.

Equation (26) gives, with e=exp(1),

    M_m/sigma^m
      =(1+1/m)^m[A_mass+(1-A_mass)(2/c_rul)^m] -> e.           (35)

Indeed a_rul tends to 1/sigma=sigma-2, so A_mass tends to 1,
and 2/c_rul is bounded above by 2/sigma<1. Consequently (33)--(35)
prove the finite and asymptotic exact-profile bounds

    B_n V_can < gamma_can [1+4(2^m-1)^rho]/M_m,
    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup V_can
       <=4 gamma_can/e=275/(162e)<1.                          (36)

The supremum includes all legal amplitudes and all cutoffs. If q=m-ell
tends to infinity, the right side of (30) tends to zero, so the exact-B
ratio tends to zero as well. No fitted dyadic constant or assumed
asymptotic phase for B_n was used.

## 7. What has, and has not, been excluded

The constructor (10) proves nonemptiness and simultaneous attainability
of every original pair, including optimum and remote pairs. The bound
(33) applies more broadly to every legal projection trajectory satisfying
the stated cancellation rule, even when (22) is strict. It does not assume
an acute cone: in the explicit constructor every distinct-gradient cross
inner product is strictly negative by (16).

The assumptions of the obstruction include (2), the fixed initial point
X_0=Cp_0 (equivalently Y_0=0), the one projection function (3), and the
extinguished-coordinate cancellation in (6). Positive endpoint heights
alone do not evade it. General joint value arrays, different initial
proximal points, a persistent final coordinate, different two-change
histories, and nonzero extinct-coordinate residuals are outside its scope.
No unrestricted upper certificate and no common-array A2 separator is
claimed.

## 8. Exact residual equations for a changed rule

Drop cancellation but retain (2)--(5), positive amplitudes, and the same
projection function. For 1<=j<=k define its effective endpoint parameter

    tau_eff_j=Rpre_j Aamp_(j-1)/Bamp_(j-1)-C.                 (37)

Here Rpre_j uses ONLY physical r_0,...,r_(j-1). If the data are legal,
the optimum normal requires tau_eff_j>=0; it is strictly positive for
j<k, since Ecan_j>0. The frozen proximal coordinate l<k-1 is

    z_ext_l=(r_(l+1)-tau_eff_(l+1))Bamp_l.                    (38)

The exact endpoint coordinates are now z_ext_l for l<j-1,
-tau_eff_j Bamp_(j-1) at l=j-1, and -Lpre_j Aamp_l for l>=j.
Its height is

    delta_j=tau_eff_j Bamp_(j-1)^2-Lpre_j Ecan_j.

For future vertices s>j the normal inequalities are exactly

    Lpre_j(Ecan_j-Kcan_s)<=tau_eff_j Bamp_(j-1)^2.            (39)

For every old vertex 0<=s<j they are exactly

    -1_(s>=1) Bamp_(s-1)z_ext_(s-1)
      +sum_(l=s)^(j-2)Aamp_l z_ext_l
      <=tau_eff_j Bamp_(j-1)(Aamp_(j-1)+Bamp_(j-1)).         (40)

These formulas follow by multiplying the displayed endpoint coordinates
by p_s-p_j. An empty sum is zero. They retain all old residuals, including
their signs. Cancellation is exactly z_ext_l=0.

In particular the next-future inequality and the next-old inequality
give a necessary propagation condition. For 1<=s<k, they read

    Lpre_s Aamp_s(Aamp_s+Bamp_s)
                <=tau_eff_s Bamp_(s-1)^2,
    (tau_eff_s-r_s)Bamp_(s-1)^2
                <=tau_eff_(s+1)Bamp_s(Aamp_s+Bamp_s).

Substitute Bamp_s/Aamp_s=Rpre_(s+1)/(C+tau_eff_(s+1)) and
Rpre_(s+1)=Lpre_s+r_s. If tau_eff_s>r_s, cancel the positive
Bamp_(s-1)^2 and rearrange; if tau_eff_s<=r_s, use tau_eff_(s+1)>=0.
The resulting necessary condition in both cases is

    tau_eff_(s+1)
       >= C Lpre_s(tau_eff_s-r_s)_+
                       /[r_s(Lpre_s+tau_eff_s)].               (41)

Thus a negative extinct residual can increase the future budget in (39),
but the same residual imposes a positive cost in the next old comparison.
Equation (41) is only necessary; it does not replace the remote sums in
(40) or establish a competitive construction.

## 9. An actual-ruler countercheck against forward-only repair

For every actual H_m above with q>=2, the following exact relaxed data
pass ALL future endpoint normal comparisons and ALL optimum comparisons,
with strictly positive later endpoint heights, yet fail an old pair.
They are a counterexample to sufficiency of that one-sided test, NOT a
legal lower-bound witness.

Use the same physical Rpre_j,Lpre_j, and choose

    tau_eff_1=2r_1, tau_eff_2=r_2/100,
    tau_eff_j=r_j for 3<=j<k, and tau_eff_k=C.                 (42)

For k=3 the last assignment is just tau_eff_3=C. Set Aamp_0=1,
Bamp_0=Rpre_1/(C+tau_eff_1), and, for 1<=j<k, set

    Aamp_j^2=tau_eff_j Bamp_(j-1)^2 /
                [Lpre_j(1+Rpre_(j+1)/(C+tau_eff_(j+1)))],
    Bamp_j=Rpre_(j+1)Aamp_j/(C+tau_eff_(j+1)).                 (43)

All amplitudes are positive. The same algebra as in (16), now using
(37),(43), shows that Kcan_(j+1)-Kcan_j is strictly positive and
delta_j=-Lpre_j Kcan_(j+1)>0 for j<k. Since Kcan_k<0 and
delta_k=tau_eff_k Bamp_(k-1)^2>0, every future normal in (39) and
every optimum comparison holds. Adding ordinary remaining mass preserves
these inequalities because <p_j,p_s-p_j><=0, as proved in Section 3.

But the endpoint-2 normal against vertex 1, equivalently the original
residual Q_((1,0),(2,0)), equals

    (tau_eff_1-r_1)Bamp_0^2
       -tau_eff_2 Bamp_1(Aamp_1+Bamp_1)
      =r_1 Bamp_0^2
         [1-2tau_eff_2 Rpre_2/((C+tau_eff_2)Lpre_1)].           (44)

Here r_0=t_can C, r_1=c_rul t_can C, r_2=t_can C. Thus

    Rpre_2/Lpre_1=1+c_rul t_can/(1+t_can)<11/6,
    tau_eff_2/(C+tau_eff_2)<1/200.

The bracket in (44) is greater than 589/600. This is a strictly positive
violation on the actual schedule for every q>=2 and m>=128. One cannot
repair the cancellation rule by independently increasing an endpoint
height and clearing its propagated cost at the following checkpoint.
All the heights belong to the same proposed array, but that array is
incompatible with the retained earlier-vertex inequality.

The remaining quantitative task is to choose nonzero residuals satisfying
ALL of (39)--(40), or change another stated generating-rule assumption,
and obtain an actual payoff at the exact benchmark scale. The original
all-schedule exact-profile target is unresolved. Current TASK and guidance
allocate no routine verifier call, so this entire document remains a draft.

## 10. Tiny exact sanity checks

The local script `check_positive_height_cancellation.py` checks only three
fixed fixtures, with rational c_rul=5/2 and a_rul=2/5. These coefficients
check the general algebra and are not asserted to be the m>=128 parameters.
Rational multiples of sqrt(Aamp_j^2) represent the coordinates, so every
inner product and residual is an exact rational number.

For H_3 at ell=0 and ell=1, the constructor (10) with r_k=C passes all
72 ordered original interpolation pairs, including the optimum, and has
respectively seven and three strictly positive later endpoint heights.
The full original step lists agree. The exact normalized payoffs are
1562301543/5336489025232 and 828765625/160552296576. A third H_2 fixture
checks (42)--(44): all future and optimum comparisons hold, while the old
residual is exactly 6932/395325>0. All three checks together took 0.00521
seconds. They are finite sanity checks; the symbolic proof above, not
these computed values, is the evidence for the universal statements.

claim: Uniform all-horizon obstruction at the actual exact ZJ word: dilating its positive step gaps by a fixed factor off any o(n) arbitrary exceptional indices forces B_n W_n to diverge exponentially, despite unrestricted whole-array re-selection. An explicit one-exception family improves Huber and makes the unit quadratic zero, yet fails exponentially.
evidence:
# Exact benchmark obstruction to dilation with arbitrary exceptional steps

Status: **self-contained, unverified proof candidate**, cumulative round 15.
No optimization or verifier call was made. This is a restriction on a specified
variation class, not the original unrestricted asymptotic theorem.

Correctness premises: accepted `b98bb807d514e80d` supplies the exact benchmark
recurrences and the bound C_j <= (j+1)^p, p=log_2(3). Accepted
`1252b8823bb5a290` supplies the full-certificate convention. All other claims
needed below, including the polynomial estimate, are proved in this package.
Earlier unverified findings are not premises.

## 1. Actual source words and the new variation class

Let C_n=1+S_circle(n) and B_n=1+2S_bullet(n), with C_0=B_0=1, and write

    Omega(A,E)=(A+E+sqrt((A+E)^2+4AE))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

Thus C_n=max_k Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)) and
B_n=max_k G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)). At every node choose the SMALLEST maximizing
index, comparing these exact real numbers. Define the primitive and dominant
words recursively, starting from empty words:

    p^(n)=(p^(k), phi(C_k-1,C_l-1), p^(l)),
    d^(n)=(p^(k), psi(C_k-1,(B_l-1)/2), d^(l)),

where l=n-k-1, and k is the relevant predetermined maximizing index. The
functions phi and psi have exactly the definitions in the accepted fact.
These choices do not depend on the function queried. No eventual split
pattern is assumed.

The actual full multiplier recursion for this same word was reconstructed in
`max_exact_zj_baseline_and_variations.md`, sections 2--4. That draft is not
used as a truth premise here: the present lower bound needs only the explicit
word just defined and the identities proved below. In particular it does not
substitute Silver, a scalar limiting profile, or a different schedule for d^(n).

Put h=d^(n), sigma_i=h_i-1, and rho=1+sqrt(2). Fix c>1. Choose ANY set
E_sub of m indices among 0,...,n-1, and ANY nonnegative finite word h' such that

    h'_i >= 1+c sigma_i       for i not in E_sub.             (V)

There is NO condition on h'_i for i in E_sub other than nonnegativity and
finiteness. The set and its entries may depend on n, c, the complete source
tree, and one another. The exceptional entries can be zero, equal to one,
or arbitrarily large. Their number need not be bounded. Condition (V) also
includes full-step dilation h'_i>=c h_i off E_sub.

Every interpolation multiplier, both optimum incidences, every value flow,
the terminal probabilities, and the entire PSD remainder may be reselected
arbitrarily at h'. The result below is a legal primal lower bound and thus
constrains every valid full upper certificate, regardless of its support or rank.

This class changes an unbounded collection of scales and permits an unbounded
exceptional library. It does not retain the original ConPD rule or the primitive
physical sum caps. Hence the finite-terminal-library obstruction does not
already decide it. A unit exceptional step can make the unit-curvature
quadratic vanish, so that single quadratic cannot decide it either.

Define the exact constants

    eta_c=(c+1)/2,
    tau_c=(eta_c+rho)/(c+rho),
    r_c=(1+sqrt(tau_c))/(1-sqrt(tau_c)).

They satisfy eta_c>1 and 0<tau_c<1. With the conventions 0!=1 and a^0=1,
the claimed FINITE inequality is

    B_n W_n(h') >= tau_c eta_c^(2(n-m)) r_c^(-2m)
                         [m!/(2n)^m]^(2p).                  (F)

The same bound holds with W_n(h') replaced by any valid full certificate
level q. Here W_n uses the original normalized error
2(f(x_n)-f_star)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), not an intermediate reset distance.

Consequently, for any fixed c>1 and any sequence m_n=o(n), the lower bound
in (F) tends to infinity exponentially. In particular no fixed relative
improvement q_n B_n<=1-delta, delta>0, is possible in this variation class.

One explicit uniform subcase is

    c=2,  m<=n/100   ==>   B_n W_n(h') > (3/4) exp(2n/5).   (F2)

For a concrete word at every n>=3, choose the earliest index i_min having
the smallest source gap and set

    h'_i=1+2 sigma_i  (i!=i_min),       h'_(i_min)=1.          (Example)

The total step sum increases by sum sigma_i-2 sigma_(i_min), which is at
least (n-2)sigma_(i_min)>0. Its canonical Huber payoff is therefore smaller
than 1/B_n, and its unit-curvature quadratic payoff is ZERO. Nevertheless,
there is just one exception, so (F2) applies for every n>=100. This is a
fully predetermined all-horizon family for which the interval of genuine
quadratic curvatures detects failure missed by those two individual tests.

Neither claim excludes perturbations with a sufficiently large proportion
of undilated steps, or with c_n decreasing to one too quickly. The exact
finite bound (F), rather than an unproved derivative argument, governs those
regimes as well.

## 2. Source gap identities and a counting estimate independent of splits

At a primitive node with child masses A,E>=1, let C=Omega(A,E) and let d
be the bridge minus one. Direct substitution gives

    C=A+E+d,       d C=AE,
    d^2+(A+E)d-AE=0.                                 (P)

The last polynomial is increasing at d>=0. Its value at sqrt(2)-1 is at
most zero: as a function of A,E>=1 it is decreasing in either variable
there, and its value at A=E=1 is zero. Thus d>=sqrt(2)-1. Also
d=AE/C<min(A,E).

At a dominant node, put

    r=(1+sqrt(1+8A/D))/2,       d=A/r.

The defining formulas give

    r^2-r=2A/D,       G(A,D)=D r^2,
    2d^2+Dd=AD.                                      (D)

The left-minus-right polynomial in the last equation has value
1/2+D/2-AD<=0 at d=1/2, for A,D>=1. Hence d>=1/2>
sqrt(2)-1, and d<A since r>1.

Induct on the construction tree, beginning with the empty product one.
At a primitive join the product of all positive gaps is
d/(AE)=1/C. At a dominant join it is
d/(A sqrt(D))=1/sqrt(G(A,D)). Therefore the actual benchmark word satisfies

    sigma_i >= sqrt(2)-1=1/rho,
    product_(i<n) sigma_i = 1/sqrt(B_n).              (Product)

We now prove, for every z>0,

    #{i<n: sigma_i>z} <= 2n z^(-1/p).                (Count)

Every primitive component with k steps is a full binary tree with k+1
empty leaves. A primitive bridge exceeding z has each child mass exceeding
z, by (P). A child with a_steps steps has mass at most
(a_steps+1)^p, by the accepted bound on C. Thus BOTH children have at
least K leaves, where K=floor(z^(1/p))+1.

For a full binary tree with N leaves, the number of nodes whose two
children each have at least K leaves is at most

    max(0,floor(N/K)-1).                             (Tree count)

Here is a complete induction. If N<K, no node qualifies. Otherwise write
N=N_L+N_R at the root. When both child leaf counts are at least K, induction
bounds their qualified nodes by floor(N_L/K)-1 and floor(N_R/K)-1; adding
the qualifying root gives at most floor(N/K)-1. If only one child has at
least K leaves, the root does not qualify and the same bound for that
child is at most floor(N/K)-1. If neither child has K leaves, the count
is zero, which is at most floor(N/K)-1 whenever N>=K. A one-leaf tree
has zero qualified nodes and satisfies the assertion directly.

The dominant construction has a single chain of right dominant children.
If their left primitive lengths are k_1,...,k_J, then

    sum_(j=1)^J (k_j+1)=n,

because each dominant node contributes its left steps and one bridge,
and the final dominant child is empty. The primitive components thus
have a total of n empty leaves. The preceding tree estimate bounds the
number of primitive bridges above z by n/K.

Each dominant bridge above z requires its left primitive mass above z,
by d<A in (D); hence that left component has at least K leaves. The
components are disjoint and their leaf counts sum to n. At most n/K
dominant bridges qualify. The combined count is at most 2n/K,
which is at most 2n z^(-1/p). This proves (Count), including z<1 and
empty primitive components.

If sigma_(1)>=...>=sigma_(n) are the sorted source gaps, (Count) implies

    sigma_(j) <= (2n/j)^p,
    product_(i in E_sub) sigma_i <= [(2n)^m/m!]^p.    (Exceptional product)

Indeed, if the first inequality failed, choose z strictly between its
right side and sigma_(j). Then at least j gaps exceed z, contradicting
(Count). Multiplying the first m sorted bounds bounds the product on
any m-element subset. No distribution or balancing hypothesis on the
maximizing splits entered this argument.

## 3. The polynomial estimate, with an explicit finite curvature selection

Let 0<tau<1 and let R be a real polynomial of degree at most m with R(0)=1.
Put r=(1+sqrt(tau))/(1-sqrt(tau)). There is a theta in [tau,1] such that

    |R(theta)| >= 1/T_m((1+tau)/(1-tau)) >= r^(-m).  (Cheb)

For m=0 this holds at every point. For m>=1 define T_0(x)=1,T_1(x)=x,
T_(j+1)(x)=2xT_j(x)-T_(j-1)(x). The cosine addition formula proves
T_m(cos t)=cos(mt). Define

    x_j=cos(j*pi/m),
    theta_j=(1+tau)/2+(1-tau)x_j/2,  0<=j<=m,
    x_ext=-(1+tau)/(1-tau).

Let L_j be the Lagrange cardinal polynomial for these distinct descending
nodes x_j. The numerator of L_j(x_ext) has sign (-1)^m and its denominator
has sign (-1)^j. Thus L_j(x_ext) has sign (-1)^(m-j).
Interpolation of T_m, whose value at x_j is (-1)^j, gives

    sum_j |L_j(x_ext)|=|T_m(x_ext)|.

Apply interpolation to P(x)=R((1+tau)/2+(1-tau)x/2), noting P(x_ext)=1:

    1 <= max_j |R(theta_j)| sum_j |L_j(x_ext)|.

This proves the first inequality in (Cheb), and shows that a suitable
theta can be selected from the EXPLICIT m+1 points theta_j. The first
maximizer of |R(theta_j)| is a deterministic selection after h' is fixed.

For X=(1+tau)/(1-tau)>1, the recurrence for T_m gives

    T_m(X)=(r^m+r^(-m))/2,
    r=X+sqrt(X^2-1)=(1+sqrt(tau))/(1-sqrt(tau)).

The displayed expression follows by checking m=0,1 and the recurrence.
It is at most r^m, proving the second inequality. No external extremal
polynomial theorem is a premise of this proof.

## 4. Actual quadratic adversary and the full-array conclusion

Fix h' and its exceptional set. Apply (Cheb) on [tau_c,1] to

    R(theta)=product_(i in E_sub)(1-theta h'_i),

which has degree at most m and R(0)=1, including exceptional zero steps.
For i outside E_sub and theta>=tau_c, condition (V) and (Product) give

    theta h'_i-1 >= c theta sigma_i-(1-theta)
      >= [c theta-rho(1-theta)] sigma_i
      >= eta_c sigma_i >0.                          (Amplification)

The last equality at theta=tau_c is the definition of tau_c. Thus, at the
selected theta_j in section 3,

    |product_(i<n)(1-theta_j h'_i)|
      >= eta_c^(n-m) r_c^(-m)
                        /[sqrt(B_n) product_(i in E_sub) sigma_i].

Use the one-dimensional function f(x)=L theta_j x^2/2, with x_0=1 and
x_star=0. It is convex, has gradient Lipschitz constant at most L, and
has UNIQUE minimizer zero since theta_j>=tau_c>0. Its actual GD trajectory
for h' has x_n=product_(i<n)(1-theta_j h'_i), and its normalized error is
theta_j x_n^2. The true initial distance is exactly one. The last displayed
bound and (Exceptional product) prove (F).

If a full certificate has level q, its nonnegative interpolation weights
and full PSD remainder imply q>=W_n(h'), as in accepted1252b8823bb5a290.
In particular no moving coefficient, new edge, optimum-source incidence,
kernel change, or higher-rank remainder can evade this legal instance.
This is why no unproved continuation radius or sign repair is needed
to obtain the stated negative conclusion for class (V).

## 5. Uniformity, finite constants, and the boundary of the obstruction

For m>=1, integrating the increasing function log(x) gives
log(m!)>=m log(m)-m; equivalently m!>=(m/e)^m. Set s=m/n and define

    F_c(s)=(1-s)log(eta_c)-s log(r_c)-p s log(2e/s),  0<s<=1,
    F_c(0)=log(eta_c).

Then (F) implies the exact, slightly weaker convenient bound

    B_n W_n(h') >= tau_c exp(2n F_c(m/n)).          (Rate)

Since s log(1/s) tends to zero as s decreases to zero,
F_c(m_n/n) tends to log(eta_c)>0 when m_n=o(n). This proves exponential
divergence with constants depending on c alone; exact B_n has already
cancelled by (Product). No decimal approximation or profile limit for B_n
was used.

There is a unique s_c in (0,1) with F_c(s_c)=0. Indeed F_c(0)>0,
F_c(1)<0, and for 0<s<=1 its derivative is

    -log(eta_c)-log(r_c)-p[log(2e/s)-1]<0.

Thus any sequence in (V) whose ratios B_n W_n(h') stay bounded must obey
liminf m_n/n>=s_c. This is a positive-density cost of the exceptional
repair, not merely an exclusion of a fixed finite terminal library.

For (F2), c=2 gives eta_c=3/2 and
tau_c=1-1/(6+2sqrt(2)), so 3/4<tau_c<9/10. Consequently
sqrt(tau_c)<19/20 and r_c<39. The elementary estimates
log(3/2)>2/5, log(39)<4, p<2, and log(200e)<7 show for 0<=s<=1/100 that

    F_2(s) > (99/100)(2/5)-(1/100)4-2(1/100)7
             =27/125 >1/5.

Here s log(2e/s) is increasing on [0,1/100] and is interpreted as zero
at s=0. For completeness, log(3/2)>2/5 follows by integrating 1/x and
the strict convexity of 1/x on [1,3/2]; e^4>39 follows from the terms
through degree five of its positive power series; and e^6>200 follows
from the terms through degree six. These imply the two remaining log
estimates. Substitution in (Rate) proves (F2).

An actual finite path may set c=1+t for t in a fixed positive interval
and choose arbitrary nonnegative exceptional entries at every t. For
every fixed t>0, the obstruction is uniform in horizon if m_n=o(n).
It also holds uniformly over t>=t_min>0, by using c=1+t_min in (V).
If t=t_n tends to zero, (F) still holds but need not diverge. Such a
vanishing-radius path, or a change to a positive fraction of the steps
outside (V), is explicitly outside the claimed no-go.

## 6. Literature check and scope

The source word is the actual Zhang--Jiang primitive/dominant construction:
Zehao Zhang and Rujun Jiang, *Accelerated Gradient Descent by Concatenation
of Stepsize Schedules*, arXiv:2410.12395v2, Theorems 3.1--3.2 and
Definitions 4.1/4.3. Its local PDF and both concatenation proofs were read
in the previous round; the present proof uses the accepted exact recurrences.

Matlas returned Rachid Ait-Haddou, *New Stability Results for Explicit
Runge--Kutta Methods*, arXiv:1804.09896, Theorem 4.1, concerning polar-form
coefficients of bounded polynomials. It prompted the interval-polynomial
screen, but that polar-form theorem is NOT used here. Section 3 proves
the exact needed Lagrange/Chebyshev estimate directly.
The exact paper was downloaded and extracted with the existing local
pypdf reader; Definition 2.1, Theorem 4.1, and its application in the proof
of Theorem 4.2 were read. The paper quotes Theorem 4.1 from Lubinsky--Ziegler
rather than reproving it. No imported assertion from that theorem is needed
in this package.

The full original target remains OPEN. The theorem-shaped assertion above
is an unverified candidate about (V). It does not infer global minimax
optimality, Huber tightness of an altered word, or a universal first-order
separator from failure of this specified dilation class.

claim: max2 complete identity and partial joint-storage proof: the all-query weighted budget has explicit nonnegative original-Q multipliers, exact recursive K/T composition, a positive two-mode Schur base, and a conditional exact-B gap lambda/e. evidence:
# Joint chronological storage for the full double-zero interface

Status: UNVERIFIED research package. The certificate-family obstruction in
Section 3 and the identities in Sections 2 and 4 are complete derivations.
The PSD assertion in Section 5 is OPEN; consequently this file does not
exclude the full quotient class and does not establish the original target.
No optimization, installation, or fact submission was used. Accepted inputs:
1252b8823bb5a290 (the ordinary interpolation inequalities) and
b98bb807d514e80d (the exact benchmark recursions). Every other assertion
needed below is derived here; earlier unverified findings are not premises.

## 1. Actual chronology and one common set of data

Let m>=128, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c, and

 d_j=1+a c^j,  H_0=(),  H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j).

Let n=2^m-1, q=n-1, and h_0,...,h_(q-1) be H_m with its last d_0 removed.
The last, unqueried step is b in [0,2]. Write

 s_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=s_q,
 p_ij=product_(t<i)(1-h_t/d_j), 0<=j<m,
 R_i=sum_j p_ij w_j, Z_i=sum_j d_j p_ij w_j,
 x_i=u-s_i v+Z_i, g_i=v+R_i, ||x_0||=1.

All vectors belong to ONE real Euclidean space with an arbitrary common PSD
Gram matrix. All values f_i belong to ONE array, with the optimum sample
x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Assume EVERY original ordered queried interpolation
inequality

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.

For an actual function these follow from accepted fact 1252b8823bb5a290.
Conversely that fact gives a common interpolant when the entire array is
legal. No subset of the inequalities below is asserted sufficient for
legality. The normalization is with respect to an actual minimizer; one
may choose the closest minimizer and then normalize its distance to one.

The first d_j step has index 2^j-1. Every step before it is smaller than d_j.
Thus 0<p_ij<=1 before its annihilation and p_ij=0 for i>=2^j. In particular
R_q=Z_q=0 and g_q=v. Also

 Z_i-Z_(i+1)=h_i R_i,  sum_i h_i p_ij=d_j.                 (1)

The sums run over 0<=i<q. These identities hold in the original coordinates;
there is no orthogonalization or change of values.

For comparison with the previous height interface, set
C_min=f_q-<v,x_q>, eta=-C_min-||v||^2/2, and
delta_i=f_i-<v,x_i>-C_min-||R_i||^2/2.
Tilting the actual function by -<v,.> gives a convex 1-smooth function with
gradient zero at x_q. Its optimum inequalities give delta_i>=0 and eta>=0.
Expanding Q_(0,star) gives exactly

 eta>=delta_0+||R_0||^2+<v,R_0>-<R_0,x_0>.              (2)

Neither eta nor any of the shared heights is set to zero below.

## 2. What the unweighted chronological chain actually charges

Define

 E_i=h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>+||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2/2,
 A_j=sum_i (h_i^2/d_j)p_ij,
 K_jk=sum_i p_ij p_ik
       [h_i-h_i^2(d_j+d_k-1)/(2d_j d_k)],
 C_jk=1+2K_jk.

The forward inequality is Q_(i+1,i)=f_(i+1)-f_i+E_i<=0.
Consequently f_q<=f_0-sum_i E_i. Direct expansion using (1) gives

 sum_i E_i=S||v||^2+<v,sum_j(2d_j-A_j)w_j>
                             +sum_jk K_jk<w_j,w_k>.     (3)

The coefficient K_jk contains every modal cross term. It is not obtained
by summing independently interpolable one-mode instances.

Before a mode dies, h_i<=d_j and 0<=p_ij<=1. Hence

 0<=A_j<=sum_i h_i p_ij=d_j.                            (4)

Telescoping p_ij^2-p_(i+1,j)^2 gives

 K_jj=d_j/2-(d_j-1)/(2d_j^2) sum_i h_i^2 p_ij^2
       <=d_j/2,
 C_jj<=1+d_j.                                         (5)

For the first mode only i=0 contributes: K_00=1/2 and C_00=2.
No assertion that the entire K matrix is PSD is made here.

## 3. A complete obstruction to ONE scalar initial-budget mixture

This section concerns a precisely specified certificate family, not the
full legal quotient class. Mix, with a scalar theta in [0,1], the two valid
upper estimates

 f_q<=<v,x_q>-||v||^2/2,
 f_q<=<g_0,x_0>-||g_0||^2/2-sum_i E_i.

Use the actual final-step descent
2F(x_q-bv)<=2f_q-b(2-b)||v||^2. Put

 D=2S+1+b(2-b), c_j(theta)=(1+theta)d_j-theta A_j+theta.

The resulting necessary upper estimate is exactly

 2F(x_q-bv)<=2<v+theta R_0,x_0>-D||v||^2
       -2<v,sum_j c_j(theta)w_j>
       -theta sum_jk C_jk<w_j,w_k>.                    (6)

To certify an upper level gamma from (6) by a common PSD quadratic form
requires the following form to be nonnegative on the formal vector space:

 M_theta=gamma||x_0||^2-2<v+theta R_0,x_0>+D||v||^2
       +2<v,sum_j c_j(theta)w_j>
       +theta sum_jk C_jk<w_j,w_k>.                    (7)

For EVERY theta and b for which (7) is PSD, necessarily

 gamma >= d_(m-1)^2/[2D(1+d_(m-1))].                  (8)

Proof. If theta=0, the w_(m-1) diagonal in (7) is zero but its coupling to
v equals d_(m-1)>0. The corresponding 2x2 principal matrix is indefinite.
For theta>0, the principal matrix in (x_0,w_0) is

 [ gamma, -theta; -theta, 2theta ],

so gamma>=theta/2. The principal matrix in (v,w_(m-1)) gives

 D theta C_(m-1,m-1)>=c_(m-1)(theta)^2.

By (4), c_(m-1)(theta)>=d_(m-1), and by (5), C_(m-1,m-1)<=1+d_(m-1).
Thus theta>=d_(m-1)^2/[D(1+d_(m-1))]. Combining proves (8).
These are genuine necessary PSD conditions, with no mode independence
assumption. If a condition fails, its 2x2 negative direction supplies a
real rank-one Gram counterexample to the proposed quadratic certificate.
It is NOT claimed to be an interpolable adversarial trajectory.

To see the quantitative failure, the actual mass satisfies

 1+sum H_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j,
 A_mass=a/(c-2).

This solves the defining recurrence 1+sum H_(j+1)=2(1+sum H_j)+a c^j.
Since A_mass->1 and c^m/lambda^m->exp(1),

 S/lambda^m->exp(1),  d_(m-1)/S->1/lambda^2.

The limit is uniform in b in [0,2], since 0<=b(2-b)<=1. Therefore every
sequence of PSD certificates (7) has

 liminf gamma >=1/(4lambda^2)>0.                       (9)

In particular this specific use of the common initial budget cannot even
give a vanishing error bound. The issue is not a small loss in the highest
mode charge: suppressing its v-coupling forces theta to remain of order one,
and that same theta attaches order-one weight to the first mode. Additional
earlier/earlier or optimum inequalities remain available and can change
this conclusion. Optimizing theta separately on already legal data is also
outside the unconditional PSD family (7).

## 4. A genuinely joint replacement using EVERY optimum budget

The exact positive quadrature in (1) suggests weights h_i/S rather than one
common theta at the initial query. There is a direct identity which avoids
introducing any new unknown heights. Define the known quadratic form

 J_h(g)=sum_(i<q){
       2s_(i+1) h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
       +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2
       +h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2 }.

Then, for arbitrary formal data satisfying the GD equations, without any
legality assumption, one has

 ||x_0||^2-2S f_q
    +2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)
    +2sum_i s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)
              =||x_q||^2+J_h(g).                     (10)

Proof. The GD norm identity gives

 2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)
 =2sum_i h_i f_i-||x_0||^2+||x_q||^2
                         +sum_i h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2.

Discrete summation by parts, using s_0=0 and s_q=S, gives

 2sum_i s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)
 =2S f_q-2sum_i h_i f_i+2sum_i s_(i+1)E_i.

Adding proves (10). All multiplier signs are nonnegative. In particular
the common values cancel exactly, rather than being chosen mode by mode.
The true initial distance remains the coefficient ||x_0||^2. The optimum
constraints include every queried index, and no projection is performed.

If J_h(g)>=0 holds for all vector outputs in the prescribed quotient, (10)
would give 2f_q<=1/S and, for every b in [0,2],

                   2F(x_q-bv)<=1/S.                 (11)

All of the original interpolation inequalities are still required of any
legal transcript. Equation (10) merely chooses a sufficient nonnegative
combination for an upper certificate; it does not delete unused pairs from
the definition of the class.

## 5. The exact remaining deterministic kernel question

Introduce a constant temporal column r_i,inf=1 and r_i,j=p_ij for 0<=j<m.
For indices a,b in {inf,0,...,m-1}, define the explicit symmetric matrix

 T_ab=sum_(i<q){
   s_(i+1)h_i(r_i,a r_(i+1),b+r_(i+1),a r_i,b)
   +s_(i+1)(r_i,a-r_(i+1),a)(r_i,b-r_(i+1),b)
   +h_i(1-h_i)r_i,a r_i,b }.

Thus J_h(g)=sum_ab T_ab<z_a,z_b>, with z_inf=v and z_j=w_j. This is ONE
known matrix depending only on the physical word and its Newton factors;
there are no unknown interpolation multipliers or values in its definition.

The open sufficient claim is

             T is PSD for every actual m>=128.        (12)

It is not the original all-schedule minimax question in disguise. It is a
specific sufficient certificate on a proper (m+2)-dimensional temporal
quotient for the specified words. Failure of (12) would reject this chosen
certificate, not construct a legal trajectory or decide the quotient class.
Conversely, (12) has NOT been established by this package. This is BLOCKED
research, not a routine remaining check.

Here is why the elementary scalar-storage proof does not finish it. For a
step h beginning at time t, add a carried term alpha||g_i||^2. Its weighted
one-step form is

 A||g_i||^2+2B<g_i,g_(i+1)>+C||g_(i+1)||^2,
 A=alpha+t+h(2-h), B=(t+h)(h-1), C=t+h.

When A>0 its exact square completion carries

 alpha'=t+h-(t+h)^2(h-1)^2/[alpha+t+h(2-h)].          (13)

This recurrence is legitimate algebra, but it discards positive squares
containing dependent future mode values. It can encounter a negative next
pivot even when the restriction to the Newton columns is positive. Keeping
the discarded squares as a non-scalar conditional covariance is therefore
essential if this route works. No positivity of the actual matrix follows
from entrywise positive Newton factors or from a change of modal basis.

For the analogous unweighted chain, the scalar recurrence is especially
transparent. Starting alpha=0 and completing the one-step chain square gives

 alpha' = 1/2-(h-1)^2/(4alpha+2).                      (14)

At the actual first steps d_0,d_1,d_0,d_2, the first three updates are valid
and at most 1/2. Indeed 11/8<d_0<3/2 and 1<d_1<2 give alpha_1>3/8,
alpha_2>3/14, and alpha_3>0. Since lambda>241/100 and
(241/100)(1-1/16384)>12/5, one has d_2-1=lambda(1-1/m^2)>12/5 for m>=128,
so the fourth update satisfies alpha_4<1/2-(12/5)^2/4<-1/2. The next scalar
pivot fails. This rules out that particular discarded-square argument,
not PSD of the full restricted K or T kernels.

### 5.1 Exact composition without expanding the exponentially long word

For a finite word W, let P_W(z)=product_(h in W)(1-hz), S_W=sum W, and
let K_W(z,w), T_W(z,w) be the unweighted and weighted kernels defined
above, evaluated at arbitrary real rate variables z,w. Their time starts
at zero. For concatenation U,V, direct separation of the sums gives

 K_UV=K_U+P_U(z)P_U(w)K_V,
 T_UV=T_U+P_U(z)P_U(w)[T_V+2S_U K_V].                 (15)

The second identity retains the elapsed-time offset; omitting it gives
the wrong storage matrix. For one step h,

 K_[h](z,w)=h-h^2(z+w-zw)/2,
 T_[h](z,w)=h(h+1)-h^3(z+w-zw).                      (16)

Thus for the actual recursive full word, write L=P_Hj(z)P_Hj(w),
r=(1-d_j z)(1-d_j w), s=S_Hj, k=K_[d_j], t=T_[d_j]. Then

 K_H(j+1)=(1+Lr)K_Hj+Lk,
 T_H(j+1)=(1+Lr)T_Hj+L[t+2s k+2(s+d_j)r K_Hj].       (17)

These are exact algebraic recursions, not numerical optimization or an
invocation of an unproved kernel property.

There is a useful terminal simplification. At every residual rate 1/d_j,
the queried-prefix polynomial is zero. Removing the last d_0 from H_m
therefore changes none of the modal/modal or constant/modal entries of T.
Only the constant/constant entry changes, from
(S+d_0)(S+d_0+1) to S(S+1). This follows from (15) with the last one-step
word; its correction is multiplied by P_pre(z)P_pre(w), which vanishes
whenever at least one argument is a residual rate. In particular the
constant-gradient suffix still contributes to the decisive constant
diagonal, and cannot be discarded from the budget.

Each modal/modal entry and each constant/modal entry stabilizes once the
first of its residual modes dies: subsequent products and differences for
that mode vanish identically. This supplies a nested sequence of KNOWN
matrices. If A_m denotes its residual block and t_m its constant/modal
column, the exact remaining PSD test, when A_m is positive definite, is

                 t_m^T A_m^(-1)t_m <=S(S+1).         (18)

No positivity or bound in (18) is assumed. The covariance at every level
has to include the contributions of the repeated lower-level steps in
(17); scalar carry (13) loses them.

For a fully analytic base check, let t=d_0 and u=d_1, both in (1,2), and
r=1-t/u>0. The first two residual columns give

 T_00=A=t(2-t),
 T_01=A+B r,  B=t(t-1),
 T_11=A+2B r+[u(2-u)+2t]r^2.

The Schur complement of T_00 is exactly

 r^2[u(2-u)+2t-t(t-1)^2/(2-t)].                      (19)

For the actual t<3/2, (t-1)^2/(2-t)<1/2, so (19) is greater than
(3/2)t r^2>0. This proves the first two residual columns are positive
definite, while keeping their cross term. It supplies an induction base,
not the missing uniform claim for growing m or the constant column.

## 6. Exact benchmark consequence IF the open kernel claim is proved

This section is conditional on (12); it must not be quoted as a completed
upper bound. It records the actual target constant rather than silently
replacing B_n by a sum-based benchmark.

From accepted b98bb807d514e80d, put P_n=S_circle(n)+1. Its recursions are

 P_0=B_0=1,
 P_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(P_k,P_l),
 B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(P_k,B_l),
 Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
 G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

We now prove B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1). Write alpha=2lambda-1 and
Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Its two coefficients exceed one and

 alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
                     =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

It follows that Llin>=Omega(x,y). At z=lambda Omega(x,y),

 z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
        =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2. Thus z lies to the right of the
larger root G(x,lambda y), proving G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y).
Monotonicity of G in its second argument and induction give B_n<=lambda P_n.

Set rho=log_2(lambda)>1 and Dpow(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. For
ell(z)=log Dpow(exp z), differentiation with t=exp z gives

 ell''(z)=rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
       [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/Dpow(t)^2>0.

The bracket is positive because it starts at zero and has positive
derivative for t>0. Convexity gives Dpow(t)Dpow(1/t)>=Dpow(1)^2=2.
For x,y>0, Z=(x^(1/rho)+y^(1/rho))^rho then satisfies
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy and Z>=x+y, so Omega(x,y)<=Z. Zero arguments follow by
substitution. Induction yields P_n<=(n+1)^rho; balanced joins give equality
at n=2^m-1. This proves the claimed exact-B upper comparator.

Combining this comparator, S/lambda^m->exp(1), and the CONDITIONAL bound
(11) would yield

 limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup_(full quotient,completions,b)
                         2F(x_q-bv) <=lambda/exp(1)<15/16<1.

The rational strict comparison follows from lambda<5/2 and exp(1)>8/3.
This would exclude the ENTIRE stated double-zero quotient with arbitrary
joint heights and arbitrary common PSD Gram, with no conditioning policy.
It would still say nothing decisive about the original all-h target.

## 7. Literature audit and current stopping point of the argument

Matlas returned Liao--Liu--Zhao, arXiv:2210.12514, Lemma 2.3, as a possible
discrete-energy analogy. Its proof was read from the exact PDF. It uses
summation by parts and nonnegative kernel differences; its row/column
monotonicity and algebraic-convexity hypotheses have NOT been established
for T. It is not an external premise of any proof here. The PDF is retained
at downloads/2210.12514.pdf. Local pdftotext and Python PDF readers were
absent; the arXiv HTML endpoint returned a cache miss; browser PDF extraction
succeeded. No installation was made. Further Newton and silver-energy
Matlas searches supplied no applicable theorem.

Two fixed, tiny four-mode, eight-step Schur-pivot checks on the first four
ACTUAL m=128 modes found positive residual K and T pivots. A final fixed
eight-mode, 128-step check of T also had positive scaled pivots, ending near
0.0928. These are numerical intuition only, not a proof of (12), and do not
test the constant column or unbounded horizons. There was no optimization
or sweep; no further numerical evaluation is planned in this round.

Complete new result: the single-initial scalar-mixture family (7) cannot
produce any vanishing bound, with the quantitative obstruction (8)--(9).
Open new mechanism: prove or refute the fixed known T kernel in (12), keeping
the conditional covariance from repeated lower-level steps. Neither an
isolated highest-mode cost nor an unproved total-positivity assertion fills
this gap. The full project target and the requested whole-interface charge
remain unresolved.

claim: Actual ZJ tight-face package: full complementarity yields legal projection-on-a-convex-set realizations; an exact n=3 finite path lowers Huber, unit quadratic and active root cut but a fourth legal function raises payoff; maximizing roots satisfy bridge-gap>=sqrt(B_n)/4, and an unchanged scalar plateau-to-quadratic lift fails on an explicit unbounded set of horizons.
evidence:
# Tight faces, a three-test counterexample, and exact root geometry

Status: **joint unverified candidate**, cumulative round 15. No solver or
verifier call. These are scoped interfaces and counterexamples, not a full
answer to the original asymptotic problem.

Accepted premises: `1252b8823bb5a290` for the complete interpolation and
certificate convention, and `b98bb807d514e80d` for the exact recurrences,
the Huber/single-cut bounds, and C_n<=(n+1)^p with p=log_2(3)<2.
All additional identities used here are proved in this package. No earlier
unverified finding is treated as a fact.

## 1. A precise consequence of positive optimum-directed weights

Normalize L=1, x_star=g_star=f_star=0, and ||x_0||=1. Suppose an actual
trajectory attains a full certificate level q and that this particular
certificate has lambda_(i,star)>0 at every finite sample i. Write

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    y_i=x_i-g_i.

The certificate equality at an attaining trajectory reads
sum lambda_ij Q_ij=M_cert>=0, while every summand is nonpositive.
Consequently M_cert=0 and each positively weighted Q is zero. In particular

    Q_(i,star)=0,      f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2.

Substitution, including the zero optimum jet, gives the complete identity

    Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>.                              (N)

Let K=conv{0,g_0,...,g_n}, a compact convex subset of the same Euclidean
space. For every i the full interpolation inequalities and (N) imply

    <v-g_i,y_i><=0   for every v in K.                (Normal)

Conversely these inequalities characterize the fact that g_i is the
Euclidean projection of x_i onto K. Indeed, for v in K,

    ||x_i-v||^2-||x_i-g_i||^2
      =||v-g_i||^2-2<y_i,v-g_i>>=0,

with strict inequality unless v=g_i. Define the global function

    F_K(x)=max_(v in K) {<x,v>-||v||^2/2}.

Its unique maximizing vector is Proj_K(x). The projection variational
inequalities at x and x', added, imply
||Proj_K(x)-Proj_K(x')||<=||x-x'||. Evaluating the two maxima at each
other's maximizing vectors then proves differentiability, with this
projection as the gradient. Hence F_K is convex and 1-smooth. Since
0 belongs to K, F_K(0)=0=min F_K. At every supplied x_i it has gradient
g_i and value <g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2=f_i. Thus every attaining trajectory
under the stated positive-weight hypothesis has a legal realization by
this particular projection function, with the SAME initial point and
optimum zero.

This does not assert that K is an interval, a box, or a product of
one-dimensional components. It need not give a unique minimizer. More
importantly, an arbitrary trajectory of F_K need not attain the certificate:
the positively weighted finite-edge equalities and M_cert=0 still have
to hold. Merely replacing the unknown tight primal by an arbitrary
projection trajectory supplies no stationary separator.

## 2. The actual three-step exact benchmark

Put s=sqrt(2), rho=1+s and B=6+4s. The exact source word at n=3 is

    h=(s,1+s,3/2),       B_3=B.

Here is a split check directly from the accepted recurrences. C_1=rho,
B_1=4 and C_2=(2+s+sqrt(10+8s))/2. Both candidates for B_2 are below8:
G(1,4)=4+2sqrt(3)<8, and G(rho,1)<G(5/2,1)<8. Thus the k=0 candidate
at n=3 is below G(1,8)=B. The k=2 candidate is below B because
C_2<(4+3s)/2, by squaring sqrt(10+8s)<2+2s, and
G((4+3s)/2,1)=B. The k=1 candidate equals G(rho,4)=B. It is therefore
the unique maximizing root split, and its bridge is 1+s.

For reference the complete certificate of this actual word is finite and
explicit. Let u=(s,2+s,2+s,2+s), and let the only nonzero finite entries
of an array L be

    L_01=1, L_10=rho, L_21=rho, L_31=rho, L_32=rho^2.

Set lambda_(i,star)=2u_i/B, lambda_(star,i)=0, and
lambda_ij=2L_ij/B for finite i!=j. All coefficients are nonnegative.
The finite-node differences out_L-in_L are
(-s,-(2+s),-(2+s),4+3s), so adding u gives (0,0,0,B).
Thus all value coefficients cancel in

    ||x_0||^2/B-2f_3+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
       =||x_0-s g_0-(2+s)(g_1+g_2+g_3)||^2/B.      (Certificate)

The Gram identity can also be checked directly: after multiplication by B,
the x_0 coefficient is1, its mixed matrix entries with g_i are -u_i,
the g_0 diagonal is2, every other gradient diagonal is B, the three
g_0--g_i mixed matrix entries are 2+2s, and the other three mixed gradient
matrix entries are B. These are exactly the entries of (1,-u)(1,-u)^T.
The GD substitutions used are x_1=x_0-s g_0,
x_2=x_1-(1+s)g_1 and x_3=x_2-(3/2)g_2.

The canonical Huber function and the unit quadratic both give 2f_3=1/B,
so the certificate is tight. All its optimum-directed weights are positive,
and section 1 applies to every attaining trajectory for this certificate.

## 3. A finite coordinated deformation that passes three tests but is worse

For 0<t<=1/100 define the actual nonnegative word

    h(t)=(s-t, 1+s-t/5, 3/2+31t/25).                (Path)

Its total sum increases by t/25. Thus its canonical Huber payoff is
1/(B+2t/25)<1/B.

The unit quadratic payoff, divided by 1/B, is

    [(1-t/(s-1))(1-t/(5s))(1+62t/25)]^2.           (Q)

All factors are positive in the stated interval. Using log(1+v)<=v for
v>-1, its unsquared logarithm is at most

    t[-1/(s-1)-1/(5s)+62/25]
       =t(37s-55)/(25s)<0,

because (37s)^2=2738<3025=55^2. Hence (Q) is strictly below one.

The legal single-cut payoff at the MIDDLE/root step, divided by 1/B, is

    R(t)=(1-t/(5s))^2 (1-t/(1+s))^(-2)
                                    (1+31t/50)^(-1).        (Root)

It is also strictly below one throughout this finite interval. Indeed

    (log R)'/2=-1/(5s-t)+1/(1+s-t)
                              -(31/100)/(1+31t/50).

Use 7/5<s<10/7 and 0<=t<=1/100. The three terms on the right are at
most -7/50, strictly below21/50, and strictly below-3/10, respectively:
1/(1+s-t)<=100/239<21/50, and
(31/100)/(1+31t/50)>=1550/5031>3/10. Their sum is strictly below-1/50.
Since R(0)=1, this proves the assertion without relying only on a derivative
at zero.

Nevertheless there is a fourth explicit, UNIQUE-minimizer legal instance
whose payoff increases. Set a=s-1 and define

    F(x)=x^2/2                      if x<=a,
         a x-a^2/2                 if x>=a.

The derivative min(x,a) is continuous, nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz.
Zero is the unique minimizer. Start at x_0=1. The entire three-step
trajectory for (Path) is

    g_0=a,
    x_1=a(1+t)>a,                  g_1=a,
    x_2=a(-s+6t/5)<0,              g_2=x_2,
    x_3=a[s/2+(31s/25-3/5)t-(186/125)t^2].          (Trajectory)

The last point is in (0,a). Its bracket is positive, and its upper bound
s/2+(31s/25)t is at most 5/7+31/1750<1. Thus the stated formulas use
the correct piece of F at EVERY query and at the terminal value.

At t=0, 2F(x_3)=a^2/2=1/B. At positive t its exact payoff ratio is

    B*2F(x_3)
       =[1+(62/25-6/(5s))t-(372/(125s))t^2]^2
       >=(1+3t/2)^2>1.                             (Bad)

For the inequality, the coefficient of t inside the bracket is bounded
below after subtracting its quadratic correction by
284/175-(372/175)(1/100)>3/2, using s>7/5. All squared expressions
are positive. The true initial distance is one, and multiplication of F
by L gives the same normalized statement at arbitrary L.

Consequently ANY full certificate for h(t), however its array or PSD rank
changes, obeys q B>1. This is a finite counterexample to sufficiency of
the Huber/unit-quadratic/root-cut screen, even when all three improve
simultaneously and both children are changed. It is a three-step result,
not an asymptotic obstruction to arbitrary joint deformations.

## 4. A root rotation inequality for exact maximizing trees

For A>0,z>=0 define T_A(z)=(z+sqrt(z^2+8A))/2, so
sqrt(G(A,D))=T_A(sqrt(D)). This section applies to EVERY maximizing root
in the exact recurrence, without assuming which split is selected.

Suppose the right dominant child is nonempty and itself has first left
primitive mass C and final dominant mass z^2. Write

    u=T_C(z)=sqrt(D), v=T_A(u), E=Omega(A,C).

The alternative legal tree first forms a primitive join of masses A,C and
then a dominant join with z^2. Its primitive mass is at least E, because
that join is an allowed split in the exact primitive recurrence. The two
complete trees have the same number of steps.

The defining equations give

    E^2=(A+C)E+AC,    u^2=z u+2C,
    v(v-u)=2A,       v(v-z)/2=A+C(v/u).

Also E=A+C(1+A/E). Since w(w-z)/2 is increasing at w>=z, it follows that

    T_E(z)>v
       iff v/u<1+A/E
       iff u^2(E+A)>2E^2
       iff z u(E+A)>2AE.                           (Rotation)

For the middle equivalence, set r=v/u>1 and use
r(r-1)=2A/u^2 and the strict monotonicity of r(r-1) at r>1.
The final equivalence follows by substituting u^2=z u+2C and the
displayed defining equation for E.

At a maximizing root, the strict improvement in (Rotation) is impossible.
Therefore z u<=2AE/(E+A)<2A. Since z>=1,

    sqrt(D)<2A.                                    (Balance)

If the right child is empty, D=1 and the same strict bound follows from
A>=1. Thus (Balance) holds at every maximizing dominant root with n>=1.

Let d=bridge-1 at this root and u=sqrt(D). Direct substitution gives

    A=d+2d^2/u^2,       sqrt(B_n)=u+2d/u.

We claim d>=sqrt(B_n)/4. Set d_0=u^2/(4u-2), which is positive since
u>=1. The increasing function d+2d^2/u^2 at d=d_0 equals
A_0=u^3/(2u-1)^2. For 1<=u<=2, A_0<=1 because

    (2u-1)^2-u^3=-(u-1)(u^2-3u+1)>=0.

For u>=2, A_0<=u/2 because
(2u-1)^2-2u^2=2u^2-4u+1>0. We have A>=1 and A>u/2 by (Balance),
so A>=A_0 and d>=d_0. This is equivalent to

    4d>=u+2d/u=sqrt(B_n).                           (Root growth)

All source steps exceed one by their defining quadratics, so B_n>=2n+1.
Thus the source root gap diverges at least as sqrt(2n+1)/4. This is an
exact structural estimate, not evidence for a fixed or dyadic split pattern.

## 5. Why a plateau followed by an entirely quadratic suffix cannot lift

There is an explicitly defined UNBOUNDED set of horizons at which the
chosen exact source root has a nonempty dominant suffix: take all n with
k_D(n)<=n-2, where k_D chooses the smallest maximizing split.

To prove unboundedness, suppose instead that every sufficiently large n
has an empty chosen suffix. Then the root value G(C_(n-1),1) must be at
least the legal candidate G(C_(n-2),4). Set z=T_(C_(n-2))(2). Since
T_(C_(n-1))(1)>=z, the defining root equations imply

    C_(n-1)-C_(n-2)>=z/2
       =(1+sqrt(1+2C_(n-2)))/2>=sqrt(C_(n-2)/2).

Let v_j=sqrt(C_j)>=1. This forces, for all sufficiently large j,

    v_j-v_(j-1)
      >=1/[sqrt(2)(sqrt(1+1/sqrt(2))+1)]>0.

Indeed substitute the lower bound C_j>=C_(j-1)+sqrt(C_(j-1)/2),
take square roots and rationalize their difference. It follows that
C_j grows at least quadratically in j, contradicting the accepted
C_j<=(j+1)^p with p<2. The specified set is therefore unbounded.

Now take one of these horizons. A proposed scalar lifting rule uses the
one-sided Huber function with derivative min(x,c_plus), starts at1, and
uses a constant-gradient prefix ending at the root with x_root=c_plus.
For the actual source prefix this forces c_plus=1/A. The root bridge
1+d maps it to -d c_plus. The first suffix step h_next is a source step,
so h_next-1>=sqrt(2)-1. If the suffix were entirely in the quadratic
region, its next point would be

    d(h_next-1)c_plus.

For B_n>16rho^2, (Root growth) gives d>rho=1/(sqrt(2)-1), so this point
is STRICTLY above c_plus. The alleged entirely quadratic suffix has
already left its defining region after its first step. If that point is
terminal, the asserted quadratic terminal VALUE is still false.

The lower gap bound used here follows directly from the node equations:
at a primitive node, d^2+(A+E)d-AE is nonpositive at d=sqrt(2)-1 for
A,E>=1, and at a dominant node, 2d^2+Dd-AD is nonpositive at d=1/2.
The polynomials increase at nonnegative d. Hence every source step has
gap at least sqrt(2)-1, as claimed.

This refutes the stated plateau-to-quadratic lifting rule on an explicit
unbounded set of genuine maximizing words. It does NOT refute the legal
one-sided Huber function itself, a more detailed piecewise trajectory,
or a multidimensional projection set K. It explains why the finite
counterexample in section 3 cannot simply be replicated up the source
tree while suppressing its region conditions.

## 6. Remaining interface

Positive optimum-directed weights give the complete normal-cone equations,
but no joint family satisfying all active source edges and the required
stationarity equations has been constructed here. Two routes were screened:
using only the three standard active tests fails by section 3; lifting
their extra one-sided quadratic branch as an unchanged scalar block fails
by sections 4--5. These failures do not establish a separator for the
whole full-certificate cone.

Any proposed all-horizon first-order separator from this face remains
BLOCKED until it supplies one legal Gram/value array satisfying every
prefix interpolation inequality, source complementarity, and the claimed
coefficient inequalities. A quantitatively useful finite continuation
outside the separate sparse-exception dilation obstruction remains OPEN.
