evidence:
# Actual Newton chronology: a birth chain and a joint covariance charge

Status: UNVERIFIED proof candidate and partial storage argument. The exact
coordinate identities and ordered-kernel result below are complete candidates.
The covariance domination in Section 5 is OPEN. In particular there is no
whole-interface error bound, no legal benchmark-scale construction, and no
resolution of the original exact-profile problem in this file. No optimization,
numerical experiment, installation, or fact submission was used in this round.

Accepted mathematical inputs: ordinary smooth interpolation and scaling in
fact 1252b8823bb5a290, and the benchmark definitions in b98bb807d514e80d.
The total-nonnegativity assertion also uses the explicitly identified and
audited published theorem in Section 3. No earlier unverified max2 result is
a premise: the identities needed for this argument are derived here.

## 1. The actual interface and notation

For an integer m>=128, put

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
 d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j).

Set n=2^m-1 and q=n-1. The queried steps h_0,...,h_(q-1) are the word
H_m with its final d_0 deleted. The actual final step is b in [0,2]. Define

 s_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=s_q,
 p_ij=product_(t<i)(1-h_t/d_j),
 R_i=sum_(j<m)p_ij w_j, Z_i=sum_(j<m)d_j p_ij w_j,
 x_i=u-s_i v+Z_i, g_i=v+R_i, 0<=i<=q.

All these vectors use ONE arbitrary real PSD Gram matrix. The values f_i
form ONE array; the optimum jet is x_star=g_star=f_star=0; ||x_0||=1 is
the distance normalization relative to the chosen actual minimizer. Every
original queried inequality is retained:

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.       (1)

The first d_j occurs at step 2^j-1. Thus p_ij is positive before query
2^j and zero thereafter, and R_q=Z_q=0. The recursion gives

 Z_i-Z_(i+1)=h_i R_i, sum_i h_i p_ij=d_j.             (2)

Here and below unqualified time sums range over 0<=i<q.

For clarity about the original value budget, define

 C_min=f_q-<v,x_q>, eta=-C_min-||v||^2/2,
 delta_i=f_i-<v,x_i>-C_min-||R_i||^2/2.

On an actual legal function, tilting by -<v,x> makes x_q a minimizer;
the smooth optimum inequalities give delta_i>=0. Also eta>=0 follows
from Q_(q,star). Expanding Q_(0,star) gives the exact common budget

 eta>=delta_0+||R_0||^2+<v,R_0>-<R_0,x_0>.          (3)

No height is set to zero and neither eta nor the norm of x_0 is discarded.

## 2. A lossless stochastic change of coordinates

Define polynomials

 phi_k(z)=product_(r<k)(1-d_r z), 0<=k<=m.

Work modulo z phi_m(z), which has the m+1 distinct nodes
0,1/d_0,...,1/d_(m-1). The double zero in the position quotient leaves
exactly this simple-zero gradient quotient. Put

 V_k=v+sum_(j<m)phi_k(1/d_j) w_j, 0<=k<=m.

Then V_0=g_0 and V_m=v. This change from (w_0,...,w_(m-1),v) to
(V_0,...,V_m) is invertible: the evaluation matrix
phi_k(1/d_j), with columns ordered j=0,...,m-1, then the node0, is
upper triangular with strictly positive diagonal.

There are coefficients B_ik determined by B_00=1, B_0k=0 for k>0 and

 B_(i+1),0=(1-h_i/d_0)B_i0,
 B_(i+1),k=(1-h_i/d_k)B_ik+(h_i/d_(k-1))B_i,(k-1), 0<k<m,
 B_(i+1),m=B_im+(h_i/d_(m-1))B_i,(m-1).             (4)

Although an unused factor 1-h_i/d_k can be negative for a dead state,
it always multiplies zero. More precisely, if r_i distinct ruler levels
have occurred before query i, induction gives B_ik=0 for k<r_i.
The next step has level at most r_i, so h_i<=d_k on every occupied
state k<m. If it is the first d_(r_i), the mass at r_i moves entirely
to r_i+1. Consequently all B_ik are nonnegative, every row sums to one,
and after the first d_(m-1) the row is the point mass at state m.

The polynomial identity

 (1-hz)phi_k=(1-h/d_k)phi_k+(h/d_k)phi_(k+1)

for k<m, together with (1-hz)phi_m=phi_m modulo z phi_m, proves

 g_i=sum_(k=0)^m B_ik V_k.                           (5)

Thus B is exactly the marginal law of a time-inhomogeneous pure-birth
chain: from occupied state k<m it stays with probability 1-h_i/d_k
and advances one state with probability h_i/d_k; m is absorbing.
This probability space is auxiliary. No state vector V_k is assumed
to be a gradient at an additional sample of the legal function.

The positions are equally explicit. Let U_k=V_k-v and

 Y_k=sum_(r=k)^(m-1)d_r U_r, Y_m=0.

The conditional expected change of Y at step i is -h_i U_k when the
state is k. Hence sum_k B_ik Y_k changes by -h_i R_i. Initially

 Y_0=sum_k d_k U_k=sum_j d_j w_j=Z_0,

where the middle equality follows by telescoping
d_k phi_k(z)=(phi_k(z)-phi_(k+1)(z))/z at z=1/d_j.
Therefore

 Z_i=sum_k B_ik Y_k, x_i=u-s_i v+sum_k B_ik Y_k.      (6)

In particular the troublesome coupling remains, explicitly,

 <v,Z_0>=sum_(k<m)d_k<v,U_k>.                        (7)

Equations (5)-(6) preserve the original vectors, not just their norms.
Substitution in (1) gives EXACTLY

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j
   +<sum_k B_ik V_k, (s_i-s_j)v+sum_k(B_jk-B_ik)Y_k>
   +(1/2)||sum_k(B_ik-B_jk)V_k||^2.                  (8)

All earlier/earlier, suffix, and optimum conditions remain in this one
array. In particular (5) does not authorize independent state heights,
orthogonality of state vectors, or projected legality.

Two occupation identities retain quantitative physical costs:

 sum_i h_i B_ik=d_k,                                (9)
 sum_i s_(i+1)h_i B_ik=d_k sum_(r<=k)d_r, 0<=k<m.    (10)

To prove (9), sum the flow equation (4). State0 has initial mass1 and
final mass0, so its total outflow is1. Successive transient states have
equal total inflow and outflow, so their total outflows are also1.
For (10), write M_k=sum_i s_(i+1)h_i B_ik and M_(-1)=0.
Summation by parts gives

 sum_i s_(i+1)(B_(i+1),k-B_ik)=-sum_i h_i B_ik=-d_k.

Using (4), M_k/d_k-M_(k-1)/d_(k-1)=d_k, with the second term zero
at k=0. Induction proves (10). The terminal occupation is
sum_i h_i B_im=S-sum_(k<m)d_k; it is nonnegative and keeps the full
constant-gradient suffix in the budget.

## 3. Total nonnegativity for the ACTUAL chronological evaluations

This is a theorem about temporal coefficient matrices, not yet the
weighted energy matrix. It holds for arbitrary strictly increasing positive
levels d_0,...,d_(m-1) with the same ordered first-occurrence rule.

Let P be the matrix with chronological rows i=0,...,q and columns
p_i0,...,p_i,(m-1),1, in that order. Then P is totally nonnegative:
every square minor, with its inherited row and column order, is >=0.
The same is true of B, and of the jump matrix

 A_ij=(h_i/d_j)p_ij, 0<=i<q, 0<=j<m.                (11)

Every column of A sums to1 by (2).

External theorem used, with its local definitions made explicit:
David Galvin and Adrian Pacurar, *Total non-negativity of some combinatorial
matrices*, arXiv:1807.08658v3 (2019), Theorem1.2; published JCTA172 (2020),
105179. For a nondecreasing real sequence a_l, define C_ik by
product_(t<=i)(X-e_t)=sum_k C_ik product_(l<=k)(X-a_l).
Then C is totally nonnegative iff e is restricted growth relative to a:
the cap initially is a_1, an e_t below the cap leaves it unchanged,
an equality advances it to the next a_l, and exceeding it is forbidden.
The proof constructs a planar path matrix; zero pivots at cap hits move
all negative edge weights out of the network without changing its path
matrix. Disjoint-path determinant cancellation then proves the minor signs.

The exact PDF and extracted text were read, including Definition1.1,
Theorem1.2, the pivot lemmas3.7/3.9, and the complete proof of1.2.
Files: downloads/1807.08658v3.pdf and downloads/1807.08658.txt.
Matlas was queried repeatedly for this statement and title but did not
return the paper; the primary arXiv text, not a fabricated Matlas hit,
grounds this citation. No verifier acceptance is claimed for this application.

Here is the complete applicability check. Set

 a_1=-1/d_0<...<a_m=-1/d_(m-1)<a_(m+1)=0,

and continue the a sequence with zeros as far as necessary. Set
e_(i+1)=-1/h_i. A first occurrence of d_j is exactly a hit of the
current cap a_(j+1). Between first occurrences, every level is smaller
and hence its e is strictly below the next cap. After all levels have
appeared, every e is negative and the cap remains0. Thus the theorem's
restricted-growth condition is satisfied, with actual repetitions and
the actual deleted last d_0, not an ordered surrogate schedule.

Let N_k(X)=product_(r<k)(X+1/d_r), so
phi_k(z)=(product_(r<k)d_r)N_k(-z). The exact Newton expansion gives

 B_ik=(product_(t<i)h_t) C_ik/(product_(r<k)d_r),
 0<=k<=m.                                          (12)

The coefficients with k>m vanish upon evaluation at the m+1 nodes
-1/d_0,...,-1/d_(m-1),0. Positive row and column scaling and truncation
preserve all minor signs, proving that B is totally nonnegative.

For completeness the node-evaluation matrix V_kj=phi_k(1/d_j), with
the node0 last, is also totally nonnegative. After positive row scaling,
its transpose is L_jk=product_(r<k)(a_(j+1)-a_(r+1)). It is lower
triangular. In Neville elimination its pivot in row i,column k is

 product_(r=i-k)^(i-1)(a_(i+1)-a_(r+1))>0, i>=k.

Indeed the pivot is the ratio of determinants on consecutive rows
i-k,...,i and initial columns0,...,k, and on rows i-k,...,i-1 and
columns0,...,k-1. These determinants are Vandermonde determinants:
the monic Newton polynomials differ from monomials by a triangular
column change with diagonal1. Cancelling gives the displayed pivot.
All elimination multipliers are positive. Reversing the elimination
expresses L as a product of elementary lower bidiagonal matrices with
nonnegative off-diagonal entries and a positive diagonal matrix.
Each factor is totally nonnegative, as follows directly by expanding
its minors, and products preserve this property by Cauchy--Binet.
Thus V is totally nonnegative. Now P=BV, proving the assertion for P.
Finally A is a row and column positive scaling of P's residual submatrix,
so A has the asserted minor signs and stochastic column sums.

The chronological matrix has full column rank: the queries immediately
before first d_j, followed by any query after first d_(m-1), give a square
upper triangular evaluation submatrix with strictly positive diagonal.
Thus none of these representations has silently removed a modal direction.

## 4. Exact cancellation of ALL shared heights

Define the elapsed-time quadratic form

 J=sum_i [2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
          +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].

The original interpolation inequalities have the algebraic identity

 ||x_0||^2-2S f_q+2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)
       +2sum_i s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)=||x_q||^2+J.        (13)

To check it, GD gives
2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)=2sum_i h_i f_i-||x_0||^2
 +||x_q||^2+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2.
Also Q_(i+1,i)=f_(i+1)-f_i+h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
 +||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2/2. Summation by parts with s_0=0 and s_q=S
cancels the displayed common values and proves (13). All multipliers
are nonnegative. This is a sufficient certificate combination and does
not claim that its selected constraints are sufficient for legal data.

## 5. A Brownian-bridge covariance with the full diagonal cost

Put D_i=g_i-g_(i+1)=sum_j A_ij w_j, where A is (11). Define increasing
clock knots and nonnegative penalties

 beta_i=s_(i+1)(s_i+1), 0<=i<q,
 beta_q=S(S+1), beta_(-1)=0,
 c_i=(h_i-1)s_(i+1).

All h_i>1, so c_i>=0, and beta_0<...<beta_q. Expanding the squared
differences in J gives

 J=sum_(i=0)^q(beta_i-beta_(i-1))||g_i||^2
                          -sum_(i<q)c_i||D_i||^2. (14)

For example the coefficient of ||g_i||^2 at an interior node is
s_i(h_(i-1)+h_i)+h_i; that of ||g_q||^2 is S h_(q-1).
These are exactly the differences of beta in (14).

Since g_i=v+sum_(r>=i)D_r, changing the order of finite sums yields

 J=beta_q||v||^2+2<v,sum_i beta_i D_i>
        +sum_(i,l<q)beta_min(i,l)<D_i,D_l>
        -sum_i c_i||D_i||^2.

Define

 Kbr_(i,l)=beta_min(i,l)-beta_i beta_l/beta_q.

Completing the ONE constant-mode square proves the exact joint identity

 J=beta_q||v+(sum_i beta_i D_i)/beta_q||^2
       +sum_(i,l<q)Kbr_(i,l)<D_i,D_l>
       -sum_i c_i||D_i||^2.                         (15)

The kernel Kbr is a real covariance kernel. For a direct elementary
construction, take independent centered random variables xi_r of variances
beta_r-beta_(r-1), 0<=r<=q, let Z_i=sum_(r<=i)xi_r, and set
Zbr_i=Z_i-(beta_i/beta_q)Z_q. Direct expansion gives
E[Zbr_i Zbr_l]=Kbr_(i,l). Consequently Kbr is PSD. This use of
probability creates no randomness in the legal instance or its shared Gram.

The remaining sufficient claim is the EXPLICIT known-matrix domination

 A^T Kbr A >= A^T diag(c_i) A                        (16)

in the real PSD order, for the actual nearcritical ruler words. It is
equivalent to J>=0 on this temporal quotient, because the constant square
in (15) can be minimized by a freely chosen formal vector v. Every cost
is present, including all repeated small steps, the large-step penalties,
and the final constant-gradient suffix through beta_q.

Thus (16), IF PROVED, combines with (13) and ||x_0||=1 to give
2f_q<=1/S, and the ordinary smooth descent inequality then gives
2F(x_q-bv)<=1/S for every b in [0,2]. The previous draft's exact-B
comparison would have to be included in a complete eventual submission;
its conditional target constant is lambda/exp(1)<1. Neither (16) nor
that resulting whole-interface bound is asserted established here.

Equation (16) is a fixed, concrete covariance inequality on stochastic
Newton columns. It has no unknown interpolation multipliers or heights.
It remains a hard restricted weighted Hardy inequality, not a routine
check and not an equivalent restatement of the original all-h minimax goal.

## 6. Why total nonnegativity does NOT settle the energy sign

Here is an exact counterexample to that GENERIC implication. It is not a
counterexample to (16) for the actual m-dependent parameters.

Take levels t=3/2 and u=4 and the ruler word (t,u,t). On its first two
steps, choose the single residual column at rate1/u, namely

 g_0=1, g_1=5/8, g_2=0, v=0.

The post-annihilation third step contributes zero. The ordered Newton
matrix and birth matrix are totally nonnegative by the same construction
as above. Nevertheless the first step contributes

 2t^2(5/8)+t(3/8)^2+t(1-t)=291/128,

and the second contributes

 (t+u)(5/8)^2+u(1-u)(5/8)^2=-325/128.

Therefore J=-17/64<0. The hypotheses used to prove the temporal minor
signs all hold, but weighted-energy positivity fails. These scalar data
are a formal certificate test, not an asserted legal interpolation array.

Accordingly, a planar network for A cannot by itself be called a proof of
(16). A successful path argument must ALSO absorb the explicit costs c_i
using the actual relation between ruler levels and chronological mass.

## 7. Current proof state

Complete draft structure: lossless finite birth chain; invariant occupation
budgets (9)-(10); audited total nonnegativity of the actual temporal and
jump matrices; common-height cancellation (13); and the exact conditioned
covariance formula (15), with all cross terms and all penalties retained.

Still open: the uniform quantitative domination (16), or an actual legal
positive-height object escaping its intended bound. Two direct attempts
did not prove it: local scalar square completion discards required past
covariance; comparison to a continuous positive Laplace kernel has no
proved uniform error bound on signed modal combinations. The new ordered
kernel result does not fill this quantitative gap, as Section6 demonstrates.

No whole-interface charge or benchmark-scale legal construction has been
completed. The original problem remains unresolved, and no new fact entered
the graph. The fourth launch's second round does not authorize another round,
numerical budget, or verifier submission.

evidence:
# C67: an exact moving-normal clock and a failed scalar-clock transfer

Status: COMPLETE UNVERIFIED statements and proofs below; the proposed
full-horizon power-epigraph program remains PARTIAL. No fact_submit,
trajectory experiment, optimization, installation, or new allocation.
C65 and C66 are not mathematical premises. All power-epigraph claims
used here are derived in this document.

## 1. Statements and scope

For any real p>2 put phi_p(r)=|r|^p/p and define the single global function

    K_p={(r,s):s>=phi_p(r)},
    F_p(X)=max_(g in K_p)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2).

For r real and v>=0 use the states

    eta=v+phi_p(r),
    u=eta*|r|^(p-2),
    X_p(r,v)=(r(1+u),-v),
    G_p(r)=(r,phi_p(r)).

F_p is globally convex and differentiable with 1-Lipschitz gradient.
Its minimizer set is {(0,y):y<=0}, its minimum value is zero, and

    grad F_p(X_p(r,v))=G_p(r),
    2F_p(X_p(r,v))
      =r^2+2(p-1)v|r|^p/p+(2p-1)|r|^(2p)/p^2.             (1)

For every nonzero initial r_0 and v_0>=0 the true initial squared
closest-minimizer distance is

    R_0^2=r_0^2[1+(v_0+|r_0|^p/p)|r_0|^(p-2)]^2=x_0^2.  (2)

Here x is the horizontal coordinate of X_p. All p,r,v,u,eta and clock
symbols in this document are local variables, not redefinitions of the
accepted project glossary.

For an actual consecutive run with nonnegative steps of total mass T,
whose nonzero horizontal gradients all have the same sign, the normalized
payoff with its TRUE entry horizontal distance obeys, if T>=1/(2p-2),

    2F_p(X_end)/x_entry^2 <= E_p(T),
    E_p(T)=[(2p-2)T+2p-1]^2
             /[4p(p-1)(T+1)^2(2T+1)].                    (3)

No v-coordinate is reset when applying this to a later block. Its ratio
to the ORIGINAL initial payoff includes x_entry^2/x_0^2 explicitly.

Define, for r>0 and v>=0,

    C_p(r,v)=log r+(p-1)v*r^(p-2)/(p-2)
                    +(2p-1)r^(2p-2)/[p(2p-2)].           (4)

At a single sign-preserving step h>0 the exact moving-state identity
in Section4 implies

    C_p(|r_plus|,v_plus)-C_p(|r|,v)
       <=-h+|r|^(p-2)(v_plus-v)/(p-2)
       =-h+h|r|^(2p-2)/[p(p-2)].                         (5)

For a whole one-sign interval [A,B] this gives the inherited-state budget

    C_p(|r_B|,v_B)-C_p(|r_A|,v_A)
       <=-T+J_(A,B)
       <=-T+|r_A|^(p-2)(v_B-v_A)/(p-2),                 (6)
    J_(A,B)=sum_(i=A)^(B-1)
                 |r_i|^(p-2)(v_(i+1)-v_i)/(p-2).

The tempting stronger statement with J omitted is FALSE, even at the
first actual small step of H_m. For p=4, r_0=2 and v_0=0, the first
step of every actual H_m, m>=128, preserves the positive sign and has

    C_4(r_1,v_1)-C_4(2,0)>3.                             (7)

Thus the fixed-profile scalar rule that every noncrossing step decreases
its clock by at least h does not transfer to this changing normal state.
This does not refute a full-horizon power-epigraph payoff bound, nor C65.

## 2. Global legality, values, and every ordered interpolation pair

The epigraph K_p is nonempty, closed and convex. Completing the square
in the definition of F_p gives a coercive, strictly convex projection
problem, so there is a unique maximizing gradient Pi_(K_p)(X).
Adding the two projection normal inequalities gives

    ||Pi_(K_p)(X)-Pi_(K_p)(Y)||^2
       <=<Pi_(K_p)(X)-Pi_(K_p)(Y),X-Y>.

Thus the projection is 1-Lipschitz. Comparison of the two defining
maxima bounds the first-order remainder of F_p between zero and
||Y-X||^2. This proves differentiability and the stated gradient.
Convexity follows from the supremum-of-affine-functions definition.

The difference X_p-G_p equals eta*(phi_p'(r),-1). For any (t,s) in K_p,

    <X_p-G_p,(t,s)-G_p>
       <=eta*[phi_p'(r)(t-r)-phi_p(t)+phi_p(r)]<=0.

The final inequality is the defining tangent inequality for the convex
differentiable function phi_p. This proves the gradient formula. Direct
substitution into <X_p,G_p>-||G_p||^2/2 proves (1).

For arbitrary two such states, write f_i=F_p(X_i). The complete ordered
interpolation residual, with no restriction on chronological distance, is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
       =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
       =eta_j*[phi_p'(r_j)(r_i-r_j)-phi_p(r_i)+phi_p(r_j)]
       <=0.                                               (8)

Every point (0,y), y<=0, has F_p=0 by testing zero and bounding all other
feasible inner products. For x!=0, testing (t,phi_p(t)) for sufficiently
small t with the sign of x gives a positive value: the linear term xt
dominates the terms of orders two and higher. For x=0 and y>0, a small
positive vertical gradient gives positive value. These tests determine
the minimizer set exactly and prove (2).

At a physical step h>=0 the exact GD recurrence is

    v_plus=v+h|r|^p/p,
    x_plus=x-hr,
    x_plus=r_plus+v_plus*r_plus*|r_plus|^(p-2)
                         +r_plus*|r_plus|^(2p-2)/p.        (9)

The last right-hand side is odd, continuous, strictly increasing and
surjective. Its derivative off zero is
1+(p-1)v_plus|r_plus|^(p-2)+(2p-1)|r_plus|^(2p-2)/p>=1;
the derivative at zero is 1. Thus (9) defines the unique actual next
state of the SAME function. Its normal coefficient satisfies

    eta_plus-eta=(h-1)phi_p(r)+phi_p(r_plus)>=0 for h>=1.   (10)

The effective turning variable u=eta|r|^(p-2) need not increase.

## 3. The no-turn payoff retains accumulated v and the entry radius

By symmetry suppose the whole block is on the positive ray. For fixed
v define T_v(r)=r+v r^(p-1)+r^(2p-1)/p on r>=0. At each noncrossing
positive step, x_plus<=x and v_plus>=v, so its inverse in (9) gives
0<r_plus<=r. Consequently, with terminal r>0 and u=v*r^(p-2)+r^(2p-2)/p,

    x_entry=x_end+sum h_i r_i >=r(T+1+u),
    v_end=v_entry+sum h_i r_i^p/p >=T r^p/p.               (11)

Set z=r^(2p-2)/p and w=v_end*r^(p-2), so u=w+z and w>=Tz.
Equation (1), divided by r^2, is

    2F_p(X_end)/r^2=1+(2-2/p)u+z/p.

Since z<=u/(T+1), the ratio in (3) is at most

    [1+k_T u]/[T+1+u]^2,
    k_T=2-2/p+1/[p(T+1)].                                (12)

For u>=0 the derivative in (12) has the sign of
k_T(T+1)-2-k_T u. When T>=1/(2p-2), its maximum is attained at
u=T+1-2/k_T>=0 and equals k_T^2/[4(k_T(T+1)-1)]. Simplification is
exactly (3). Negative-ray blocks give the same result by reflection.
An absorbing endpoint has zero payoff and requires no logarithmic clock.

For p=2 the rational expression E_p(T) formally reduces to the parabolic
expression, but this argument and the clock statements here are stated
for p>2. For fixed p>2,

    lim_(T->infinity) T E_p(T)=(p-1)/(2p).                (13)

This is a no-turn result, not a full-family bound in the presence of
repeated turns. It does not assume a fresh v=0 at a later block.

## 4. Exact horizontal clock and the positive vertical-state cost

Let g_v be the inverse of T_v on the positive half-line and set
Psi_p(x,v)=C_p(g_v(x),v), for x>0. Direct differentiation gives

    d C_p(r,v)/dr=T_v'(r)/r,
    partial Psi_p(x,v)/partial x=1/g_v(x),
    partial Psi_p(x,v)/partial v=g_v(x)^(p-2)/(p-2).       (14)

For the last identity, differentiating T_v(g_v(x))=x at fixed x gives
partial g_v/partial v=-g_v(x)^(p-1)/T_v'(g_v(x)). The chain rule then
subtracts r^(p-2) from (p-1)r^(p-2)/(p-2), leaving the last expression
in (14). It is POSITIVE.

For one positive noncrossing step, write x_plus=x-hr>0. The exact split
into horizontal motion at the old v followed by the actual v increment is

    C_p(r_plus,v_plus)-C_p(r,v)
       =-integral_(x_plus)^x [dy/g_v(y)]
        +1/(p-2)*integral_v^(v_plus) g_s(x_plus)^(p-2) ds. (15)

The first integral is at least (x-x_plus)/r=h, since g_v(y)<=r.
For the second integral, x_plus<=x and s>=v imply g_s(x_plus)<=r.
This proves (5); summing it over the same-sign interval proves (6),
because its gradient magnitudes decrease. By evenness the same
calculation applies to a negative interval using absolute radii.

The cost J is an actual weighted vertical increment. It is not a
freely chosen auxiliary value or a discarded initial height. A proposed
block argument for power epigraphs must bound it, or replace this clock
with a potential that pays for it. Merely knowing that eta grows does
not justify deleting the positive second integral in (15).

## 5. An exact actual-H_m counterexample to omitting the cost

For m>=128 keep the enclosing-horizon physical parameters

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j).

The elementary bounds 2/5<a<5/12 give
7/5<h=1+a<17/12<3/2 for the first actual step. For completeness,
sqrt(2)<99/70 gives c<(169/70)(129/128)<73/30 and hence
a>(127/128)(30/73)>2/5. Also a<sqrt(2)-1<5/12.

Fix p=4,r_0=2,v_0=0. Then

    X_0=(34,0), R_0^2=1156,
    x_1=34-2h>31,
    v_1=4h>28/5.

The unique positive r_1 is determined by T_(v_1)(r_1)=x_1, where
T_v(r)=r+v r^3+r^7/4. At r=3/2,

    T_(v_1)(3/2)=3/2+(27/2)h+2187/512,
    x_1-T_(v_1)(3/2)=65/2-(31/2)h-2187/512
                     >37/4-2187/512>0.

Strict monotonicity implies r_1>3/2. Also r_1<2 follows from x_1<x_0
and v_1>v_0. Thus the step is genuinely positive and sign-preserving.
By (4),

    C_4(r_1,v_1)-C_4(2,0)
       >log(3/4)+(3/2)(28/5)(9/4)
                    +(7/24)[729/64-64]
       =log(3/4)+189/10-23569/1536
       >-1/3+189/10-23569/1536>3.                        (16)

Here log(4/3)<1/3 follows by integrating 1/t<1 on (1,4/3).
The final rational difference above 3 is 1707/7680=569/2560>0.
No scalar root was approximated or trajectory numerically evaluated.
Equations (1),(2),(8),(9) give the global function, true denominator,
every ordered interpolation pair, and actual prescribed step.

This refutes any universal claim C_plus-C<=-kappa h with kappa>=0
for this moving-state clock. It is not a counterexample to payoff
convergence or to the separate parabolic argument.

## 6. Literature grounding and the open quantitative interface

The exact power projection equation agrees with Propositions3.2--3.3
of Chierchia, Pustelnik, Pesquet and Pesquet-Popescu, "Epigraphical
splitting for solving constrained convex formulations of inverse
problems with proximal tools", arXiv:1210.5844v3. Its exact downloaded
paper and extracted text are in downloads/c66_epigraph_projection_1210.5844.
The Hilbert product is Euclidean, the generator has full domain and is
proper closed convex, and their parameters beta=p,tau=1/p,zeta=-v give
T_v(r)=x. The definitions and both projection proofs were re-read.
No theorem from that paper is a premise of this self-contained proof.

The precise failure is a proof migration from a FIXED scalar gradient
profile to an epigraph whose vertical coordinate changes along the
same legal trajectory. Equation (15) supplies the omitted term.
There is still no estimate of the sum of the J costs and crossing
gains over every chronological block on H_m, in terms of R_0 and the
exact benchmark. Consequently the full p>2 family, including quartic
multiple-turn trajectories, remains open. No new original-target
claim or verifier allocation follows from this result.

evidence:
# The proposed signed product weights fail for every positive amplitude law

Status: **one self-contained, unverified round-15 candidate**. No verifier,
optimization, parameter search, or installation was used. The mathematical
predecessors are accepted facts `1252b8823bb5a290` (necessary smooth-convex
interpolation) and `b98bb807d514e80d` (the exact benchmark and its crude upper
bound). The round-14 drafts are motivation, not proof premises. All further
calculations used in this candidate are supplied here.

This resolves the proposed policy in finding `9c015a3328a5fcf9` more broadly
than requested: the weights are fixed, but the positive chronological
amplitudes, common anchor, values, and realizing function are arbitrary.
Neither adjacent equality nor a specific amplitude recurrence is assumed.
This does not exclude other real character weight policies.

## Statement and notation

Fix an integer m>=64. Put

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c_chr=sigma(1+1/m), a_chr=delta/c_chr,
    N=2^m, n=N-1.

The actual chronological word is

    H_chr,0=(),
    H_chr,j+1=(H_chr,j,1+a_chr c_chr^j,H_chr,j), 0<=j<m.

The parameters a_chr,c_chr are fixed by the enclosing m in every subword.
Write h=H_chr,m, so h_i=1+a_chr c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0<=i<n, where nu_2(v)
is the exponent of 2 dividing the positive integer v. These are n physical
steps and N sampled gradients. No sample or algorithm step is padded.

Give sample i its standard m-bit binary label. For s in {0,1}^m define

    chi_s(i)=(-1)^(sum_(l=0)^(m-1) s_l i_l),
    rho_0=-1/2, rho_l=1-2^(-l-10) for 1<=l<m,
    w_s=2^(-m) product_(l=0)^(m-1)(1+rho_l(-1)^(s_l)).       (1)

Every w_s is strictly positive and their sum is one. For ANY positive
numbers Gamma_0,...,Gamma_n prescribe

    g_i=(Gamma_i sqrt(w_s) chi_s(i))_s.                     (2)

The conclusions below also hold for any Euclidean realization of the same
Gram matrix. Suppose that these really are all the gradients along GD on
ONE convex differentiable 1-smooth function F with a minimizer:

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad F(X_i), 0<=i<=n,

where the recursion uses only i<n. The function and anchor are unrestricted.
Let R_dist=dist(X_0,argmin F)>0 and F_star=min F. Then

    ||g_i||<=||g_0|| for all 0<=i<=n,                       (3)

and the actual normalized objective satisfies

    V_chr := 2(F(X_n)-F_star)/R_dist^2
          < 5(99/100)^((n+1)/8).                          (4)

In particular, for the original exact benchmark B_n from accepted fact
`b98bb807d514e80d`, with p=log_2(3),

    B_n V_chr
      < 5(1+4n^p)(99/100)^((n+1)/8) -> 0.                 (5)

The bound is uniform over all positive amplitudes and all actual legal
realizations of (2). Thus this precise product-weight policy cannot supply
a uniform all-schedule lower witness matching 1/B_n. This is not an upper
bound on the unrestricted W_n(h). A legal realization of this policy is
explicitly given at the end, so the assertion is not merely vacuous.

For L-smooth objectives, apply the statement to F=f/L and g_i=grad f(X_i)/L;
the recursion is the original one with steps h_i/L, and (4) has the original
denominator L R_dist^2.

## 1. Real kernel and the original inequalities

Summing (1) separately in each bit gives sum_s w_s=1. The same finite
factorization gives

    <g_i,g_j>=Gamma_i Gamma_j
                 product_(l: i_l != j_l) rho_l.           (6)

In particular ||g_i||=Gamma_i. No interpolation property is inferred from
this factorization. All gradients in (2) are independent, because the full
character matrix is invertible and all its row and column scaling factors
are nonzero. Independence is not needed for the obstruction.

For actual values f_i=F(X_i)-F_star, accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290` gives
every original ordered inequality

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.        (7)

The argument uses necessary sums of these inequalities. It does not assert
that those sums are sufficient for a trajectory. In particular every legal
function in the statement must also obey all the unused pairs and optimum
comparisons.

For consecutive samples with step h=1+v, normalized correlation d, and
gradient norm ratio r_amp>0, summing the two inequalities (7) gives

    r_amp^2+(v-1)d r_amp-v <=0.                            (8)

It follows from this necessary condition that, for every v>=0 and -1<=d<=1,

    r_amp<=max(1,v).                                      (9)

Indeed the polynomial in (8) has a single positive root when v>0. At 1
its value is (1-v)(1-d), nonnegative if v<=1. At v its value is
v(v-1)(1+d), nonnegative if v>=1. We use (9) only for v>0.

## 2. A two-step cap allowing arbitrary adjacent slack

Use local indices 0,1,2 for three consecutive samples. Suppose their steps
are 1+t,1+u and their normalized correlations are

    corr(g_0,g_1)=-1/2,
    corr(g_0,g_2)=z,
    corr(g_1,g_2)=-z/2.                                  (10)

Assume

    2/5<=t<1, u>=29/5, 1023/1024<=z<=1.                  (11)

Put A=Gamma_0, r_amp=Gamma_1/Gamma_0, q_amp=Gamma_2/Gamma_0, and let
R_leaf(t) be the positive root of

    R_leaf^2+(1-t)R_leaf/2-t=0.                           (12)

The first adjacent sum gives 0<r_amp<=R_leaf. Substitution of 1/2 into
the polynomial (12) gives 1/2-5t/4<=0, so R_leaf>=1/2.

Consider the ORIGINAL directed three-sample cycle

    T_cyc=Q_02+Q_10+Q_21.

The three function values cancel. Substitution of the two actual steps in
(7) gives, with K_ij=<g_i,g_j>,

    T_cyc=-t K_00+K_11+K_22
                 +(t-u-1)K_01+u K_12-K_02.

Using (10), this is exactly

    T_cyc/A^2=P(q_amp,r_amp),
    P(q,r)=q^2-zq-t+r^2+r(1+u-t-u zq)/2.                 (13)

No equality has been imposed on either adjacent edge. Define

    q_cap=u R_leaf/2.

Then q_cap>=29/20>1. For q>=q_cap and 0<=r<=R_leaf,

    dP/dr <= R_leaf(2-z u^2/4)+(1+u-t)/2
           <=13/10+u/2-(1023/1024)u^2/8
           <=-183/204800 <0.                             (14)

For the second inequality, the coefficient 2-z u^2/4 is negative under
(11), so R_leaf>=1/2 and t>=2/5 give the indicated upper bound. The scalar
quadratic on the second line decreases for u>=29/5, and its value at
29/5 is exactly -183/204800. This proves every inequality in (14).

Consequently P(q,r_amp)>=P(q,R_leaf) for q>=q_cap. Equation (12) simplifies
the latter expression to

    P(q,R_leaf)=q^2-zq(1+q_cap)+q_cap
       =(q-1)(q-q_cap)+(1-z)q(1+q_cap).                  (15)

If q>q_cap this is strictly positive, contradicting T_cyc<=0 from (7).
Therefore every legal local triple obeys

    Gamma_2/Gamma_0 <= (u/2) R_leaf(t).                   (16)

If z<1, equality is also impossible. In quantitative form, any attempt with
q_amp>q_cap has an original ordered residual among Q_02,Q_10,Q_21 at least

    (A^2/3)[(q_amp-1)(q_amp-q_cap)
                  +(1-z)q_amp(1+q_cap)] >0.              (17)

This is independent of the anchor and of every assigned value. It is a
constraint on the precise new PRIMAL Gram, not a tensor-dual obstruction.

## 3. Every large bridge of the actual word satisfies the hypotheses

Set t=a_chr and write u_k=a_chr c_chr^k=delta c_chr^(k-1) for the level-k
bridge. Leaves have k=0, and their next sample differs only in bit 0.
Thus every leaf has correlation -1/2 and gradient norm ratio at most

    R_leaf=R_leaf(a_chr).                                (18)

For m>=64,

    2/5<a_chr<sqrt(2)-1<1.

For the lower bound, sigma<29/12 gives
a_chr> (63/65)(12/29)=756/1885>2/5. The upper bound follows from
a_chr=(sqrt(2)-1)(m-1)/(m+1).

A level-k bridge with k>=1 has an immediately preceding leaf. At the
three samples straddling this pair, the first change flips bit 0, the
outer change flips exactly bits 1,...,k, and the second change flips
bits 0,...,k. Formula (6) therefore gives (10) with

    z=z_k=product_(l=1)^k(1-2^(-l-10)).

The elementary finite inequality product_l(1-e_l)>=1-sum_l e_l for
0<=e_l<=1 follows by induction after multiplying one more factor.
It yields z_k>1-2^(-10)=1023/1024; also z_k<1.

For every k>=3,

    u_k>=u_3=sigma^2(1-1/m)(1+1/m)^2>sigma^2>29/5.

The strict middle inequality uses
(1-e)(1+e)^2=1+e-e^2-e^3>1 for 0<e<=1/64.
The last inequality follows from sqrt(2)>7/5.
Hence (16) applies at every such bridge, wherever that bridge occurs.

The two smaller bridge levels need only adjacent inequalities:

* u_1=delta<1, so its gradient norm ratio is at most 1 by (9).
* 1<u_2=delta c_chr=sigma(1-1/m^2)<sigma<5/2. Its adjacent correlation
  is -z_2/2 with 0<z_2<=1. The polynomial in (8) at r_amp=2 is
  4-(u_2-1)z_2-u_2>=5-2u_2>0, so its ratio is at most 2.

These comparisons refer to the original m-dependent word. No subword is
given a reset physical parameter or a different initial function.

## 4. An exact full-block product and a uniform strict contraction

Write

    Theta_chr=R_leaf^4 delta c_chr^3.                     (19)

For any occurrence of H_chr,j in the actual word, j>=3, pairing each
nonleaf bridge with its immediately preceding leaf and leaving the final
leaf unpaired gives

    Gamma_after/Gamma_before
      <= 2 delta^(-1)c_chr^(-j) Theta_chr^(2^j/8).          (20)

Here is the complete count. There are 2^(j-1) leaves. Level 1 contributes
no further factor, level 2 contributes at most 2 once for each of its
2^(j-3) occurrences, and each level k>=3 contributes u_k/2 in addition
to the R_leaf for its preceding leaf. The remaining counts are

    sum_(k=3)^(j-1)2^(j-k-1)=2^(j-3)-1,
    sum_(k=3)^(j-1)(k-1)2^(j-k-1)=3*2^(j-3)-j.

Both equalities follow by induction in j, starting with the empty sums
at j=3. Thus the product is

    R_leaf^(2^(j-1)) 2^(2^(j-3))
       delta^(2^(j-3)-1)c_chr^(3*2^(j-3)-j)
       2^(-(2^(j-3)-1)),

which is the right side of (20). In particular this identity includes j=3.

We next prove, uniformly in the enclosing m,

    0<Theta_chr<5926527/6002500<99/100.                    (21)

Let t_inf=1/sigma=sqrt(2)-1 and R_inf=R_leaf(t_inf).
Dividing (12) by t and writing y=R_leaf(t)/sqrt(t) gives

    y^2+A(t)y-1=0, A(t)=(1-t)/(2sqrt(t)).

For positive t the function A(t) decreases, whereas the positive root
(-A+sqrt(A^2+4))/2 decreases as A increases. Consequently
R_leaf(t)/sqrt(t) increases with t. Since
t=a_chr=t_inf delta/(1+1/m),

    Theta_chr
      <= R_inf^4 sigma^3 delta^3(1+1/m)
      < R_inf^4 sigma^3.                                (22)

The last inequality uses (1-e)^3(1+e)<1 for 0<e<1.

For explicit rational bounds, sqrt(2)<99/70 because 99^2>2*70^2, so
t_inf<29/70. The polynomial in (12), at t=29/70 and R=18/35, is
1/1225>0. It decreases as t increases and increases as R>0 increases
for t<1. Hence R_inf<18/35. Also sigma<29/12, since sqrt(2)<17/12.
It follows that

    R_inf^4 sigma^3
      < (18/35)^4(29/12)^3
      =5926527/6002500 <99/100.

This proves (21) without any numerical parameter selection.

The short blocks separately satisfy

    H_chr,1: Gamma_after/Gamma_before<=R_leaf<1,
    H_chr,2: Gamma_after/Gamma_before<=R_leaf^2<1.          (23)

## 5. No prefix gradient exceeds the initial gradient

We prove by induction on j that every gradient encountered inside any
occurrence of H_chr,j has norm at most the norm at that occurrence's
start. This compares the actual inherited amplitude at each boundary;
no trajectory state is reset.

The empty word has only its initial sample, and the one-step word obeys
(18). In H_chr,j+1=(H_chr,j,1+u_j,H_chr,j), the induction hypothesis bounds
every sample in the left block. It suffices to show that the gradient just
after the middle bridge is no larger than the gradient at the start of
the left block. The same induction hypothesis will then apply to the
right block with its inherited starting norm.

For j=1, combine the first line of (23) with u_1<1 and (9).
For j=2, combine the second line with (9) and u_2<sigma:

    R_leaf^2 u_2 < (18/35)^2(29/12)=783/1225<1.

For j>=3, the middle bridge has u_j=delta c_chr^(j-1)>1. Multiply (20)
by its generic adjacent expansion bound u_j from (9). The result is

    (2/c_chr)Theta_chr^(2^j/8)<1                         (24)

because c_chr>2 and Theta_chr<1. This completes the induction and proves
(3) at every sample of the entire original H_chr,m.

At its terminal sample, (20) gives the stronger specific bound

    Gamma_n/Gamma_0
      <=2 delta^(-1)c_chr^(-m)Theta_chr^(N/8).             (25)

## 6. Convert to the true-distance objective without a Gram inverse

The minimizer set of F is nonempty and closed. In finite dimension the
distance from X_0 is attained: a minimizing sequence can be restricted to
a bounded closed ball, which has a convergent subsequence. Let X_star be
a closest minimizer, so ||X_0-X_star||=R_dist. Differentiability gives
grad F(X_star)=0. Smoothness then gives

    Gamma_0<=R_dist.                                     (26)

The exact mass of the original word is

    M_chr=1+sum_(i=0)^(n-1) h_i
         =N+a_chr(c_chr^m-N)/(c_chr-2)<c_chr^m.            (27)

To verify the equality, the number of level-k entries is 2^(m-k-1),
and summing their geometric series gives
sum_k 2^(m-k-1)c_chr^k=(c_chr^m-N)/(c_chr-2).
For the strict inequality, c_chr>sigma>2 and
sigma(sigma-2)=1 imply c_chr(c_chr-2)>1>delta. Thus
0<a_chr<c_chr-2. The expression in (27) is a strict convex combination
of N and c_chr^m, and c_chr^m>N.

The actual chronological update, (3), and (26) yield

    ||X_n-X_star||
       <=R_dist+sum_i h_i Gamma_i
       <=M_chr R_dist<c_chr^m R_dist.                    (28)

Convexity at X_n gives
F(X_n)-F_star<=<g_n,X_n-X_star><=Gamma_n||X_n-X_star||.
Using (25), (26), and (28),

    V_chr < (4/delta)Theta_chr^(N/8)
          < 5(99/100)^(N/8),                             (29)

since delta>=63/64 implies 4/delta<=256/63<5. This proves (4).
Every radius in this argument is the TRUE closest-minimizer distance.
No equality with b^T K^(-1)b, no unknown polar maximizer, and no chosen
nonclosest minimizer is used. The lower estimate R_dist>=Gamma_0 is
explicit in (26); its loss is already included in (29).

Accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d` defines B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 using the
project's exact primitive/dominant recursions and proves
B_n<=1+4n^p, p=log_2(3). Multiplication gives (5). The limit follows, for
example, by taking logarithms: p log n+((n+1)/8)log(99/100) tends to
negative infinity. Thus the conclusion is at the exact original B_n,
not a mass surrogate or a padded horizon.

## 7. A nonempty legal family for these very weights

This paragraph verifies nonvacuity only; it is not offered as a competitive
payoff construction. Fix the same original word and the same weights (1).
Write H_max=max_i h_i and set

    kappa_chr=min(1,(min_i h_i-1)/4)>0,
    eta_chr=kappa_chr/[8(H_max+kappa_chr+1)],
    Gamma_i=eta_chr^i,
    f_i=(kappa_chr+1/2)Gamma_i^2.                         (30)

Use gradients (2) and their invertible Gram K. Define

    b_i=(kappa_chr+1)Gamma_i^2+sum_(t<i)h_t K_ti,
    X_0=sum_i (K^(-1)b)_i g_i,
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t.                            (31)

All these quantities are finite explicit formulas in the predetermined
word. There is no parameter optimization or adaptive gradient oracle.
In particular <g_i,X_i>=(kappa_chr+1)Gamma_i^2. If desired the common
anchor has the character-coordinate formula

    (X_0)_s=[1/(N sqrt(w_s))]sum_i (b_i/Gamma_i)chi_s(i),  (32)

by finite character orthogonality. No norm of this anchor is identified
with the true distance.

For i<j, direct expansion of the original residuals gives

    Q_ij=(kappa_chr+1-h_i)Gamma_i^2-kappa_chr Gamma_j^2
             -sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_it-K_ij,

    Q_ji=(kappa_chr+1)Gamma_j^2-kappa_chr Gamma_i^2
             +(h_i-1)K_ij+sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_jt.            (33)

Here |K_it|<=Gamma_i Gamma_t by (6). Since h_i-1>=4kappa_chr and
eta_chr<1/2, the first line of (33), divided by Gamma_i^2, is at most

    -3kappa_chr+H_max eta_chr/(1-eta_chr)+eta_chr
    <=-3kappa_chr+2(H_max+1)eta_chr
    <=-11kappa_chr/4<0.

The second line, divided by Gamma_i^2, is at most

    -kappa_chr+(kappa_chr+1)eta_chr^2
                       +H_max eta_chr/(1-eta_chr)
    <=-kappa_chr+(2H_max+kappa_chr+1)eta_chr
    <=-3kappa_chr/4<0.                                  (34)

Set the optimum jet to (0,0,0). Equation (31) gives exactly
Q_(i,star)=0 and Q_(star,i)=-kappa_chr Gamma_i^2<0.
Thus every original ordered pair, including both optimum directions,
has been retained.

For an explicit single function let C_chr=conv(0,g_0,...,g_n) and define

    F_chr(X)=max_(v in C_chr)(<X,v>-||v||^2/2).            (35)

The squared-distance minimizer P_C(X) is the unique maximizer in (35).
The normal condition for that minimizer is
<X-P_C(X),v-P_C(X)><=0 for all v in C_chr. Adding this condition for
two projected points proves
||P_C(X)-P_C(Y)||^2<=<X-Y,P_C(X)-P_C(Y)>;
therefore projection is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizing
expressions at X and X+d then bounds the difference from
<P_C(X),d> between 0 and ||d||^2. Hence F_chr is differentiable with
gradient P_C and is convex and 1-smooth.

At the prescribed samples, (31) and (33) give

    <X_i-g_i,g_j-g_i>=Q_ji<=0,
    <X_i-g_i,-g_i>=-kappa_chr Gamma_i^2<0.

Every convex combination also satisfies these normal comparisons, so
P_C(X_i)=g_i and F_chr(X_i)=f_i. Thus the actual GD trajectory of the
ONE function (35) is exactly the specified trajectory, with no free
function values assigned separately to characters. The function is
nonnegative and minimized at 0, since 0 is a vertex. Its actual initial
distance is positive because g_0 is nonzero. It falls under the uniform
true-distance bound (29); no explicit polar-distance equality is claimed
for this nonvacuity example.

## 8. Scope, checks, and the remaining direction

The obstruction covers the fixed product weights (1), all positive
amplitudes, every anchor and value assignment that actually arises from
one legal function, and the unchanged dyadic words for every m>=64.
It does not cover rho_0 close to +1 or -1, arbitrary signed high-bit
correlations, the proposed dependent conditional-prefix weights, or all
character measures. The root rho_0=-1/2 and the lower bound on the outer
correlations enter quantitatively in (13)-(14); removing them is unjustified.
There is no fixed bound on how often a character coordinate changes sign.

Zero steps and nondyadic words are outside this statement. The failure on
this dyadic subsequence already suffices to exclude an all-h matching
claim based on this fixed policy. It does not imply an upper bound on
unrestricted minimax performance and does not conflict with accepted
finite witness `e9a55f57461f253c`, which has no such character restriction.

Two Matlas searches in this round returned no applicable theorem. A web
search recalled the smooth-convex interpolation literature; its necessary
inequalities are already available as accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` and no
external theorem is imported. This is the same product-Walsh regime whose
exact paper arXiv:2304.05053 was downloaded and read in round 14, not a new

The original all-schedule exact-profile target remains unresolved. The

No further launch, computation, or verifier allocation is inferred.

evidence:
# The conditional-prefix sign policy has a uniform all-amplitude obstruction

Status: **self-contained unverified round-16 candidate**. The only correctness
predecessors are accepted facts `1252b8823bb5a290` (necessary ordered
smooth-convex interpolation) and `b98bb807d514e80d` (the exact benchmark and
its bound). Previous character drafts and the proposed policy
`35ed2eb7df2b2b56` motivate the question; none is a proof premise. No optimizer,
parameter search, installation, or fact submission is used.

The conclusion concerns the explicitly specified DEPENDENT, horizon-dependent
measure below. It allows every positive amplitude law, arbitrary adjacent
slack, every common anchor, and every actual realizing function. It does not
exclude other dependent measures, signed amplitudes, different label maps, or
the unrestricted worst-case value.

## 1. Statement, actual steps, and every probability

Fix an integer m>=1024. Define

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c_chr=sigma(1+1/m), a_chr=delta/c_chr,
    N=2^m, n=N-1, epsilon=1/N, p_chr=1-epsilon.

The physical step word is

    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_chr c_chr^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Every subword retains these ORIGINAL enclosing-m parameters. Equivalently,
h_i=1+a_chr c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0<=i<n. Here nu_2(k) is the exponent of 2
dividing a positive integer k. Put

    t=a_chr, l=1+t, u_k=delta c_chr^(k-1) for k>=1,
    D_chr=1+l p_chr, beta_chr=7/10.

Thus every leaf has physical step l, and a level-k nonleaf bridge has
physical step 1+u_k. No step is deleted, permuted, or padded.

Give sample i its standard m-bit binary label i=(i_0,...,i_(m-1)). For a
character index s=(s_0,...,s_(m-1)) in {0,1}^m, define

    chi_s(i)=(-1)^(sum_l s_l i_l),
    B(s)=(-1)^s_0,
    C_j(s)=(-1)^(s_1+...+s_j), 1<=j<m,
    w_s=[(1+p_chr B(s))/2]
             product_(j=1)^(m-1) [(1+C_j(s)(1/10-4 B(s)/5))/2].   (1)

The map s -> (B,C_1,...,C_(m-1)) is bijective: s_0 is recovered from B,
(-1)^s_1=C_1, and (-1)^s_j=C_(j-1)C_j for j>=2. Formula (1) is therefore
an explicit probability law. Its conditional means are

    P(B=1)=1-epsilon/2, P(B=-1)=epsilon/2,
    E[C_j | B=1]=-7/10, E[C_j | B=-1]=9/10,

with the C_j conditionally independent given B. Every finite weight is
strictly positive and the weights sum to one. The bits s_j themselves are
not independent under this law.

For arbitrary positive numbers Gamma_0,...,Gamma_n, prescribe real vectors

    g_i=(Gamma_i sqrt(w_s) chi_s(i))_s.                    (2)

The conclusion also holds for any Euclidean realization of the same Gram.
Assume these are the gradients of ONE convex differentiable 1-smooth
function F with a nonempty minimizer set along the actual GD trajectory:

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad F(X_i).

Write R_dist=dist(X_0,argmin F)>0 and F_star=min F. Then

    Gamma_i <= (6/5) Gamma_0 for every original sample i,          (3)
    V_chr:=2(F(X_n)-F_star)/R_dist^2
             <7(199/200)^((n+1)/8).                             (4)

Consequently, at the original exact benchmark B_n of accepted fact
`b98bb807d514e80d`, with p_bench=log_2(3),

    B_n V_chr <7(1+4n^p_bench)(199/200)^((n+1)/8) ->0.             (5)

This is an upper bound on this precise adversary family along the specified
dyadic diagnostic words. It is not an upper bound on unrestricted W_n(H_m),
and it does not settle the original all-h minimax problem. Failure on this
unchanged subsequence already precludes an all-h matching claim based on
this policy. The conclusion holds with F=f/L and g_i=grad f(X_i)/L for any
L>0, giving the original normalization 2(f(X_n)-f_star)/(L R_dist^2).

## 2. Exact kernel and numerical constants proved analytically

For a binary difference d=i xor j, set d_m=0 and
k(d)=sum_(r=1)^(m-1) (d_r xor d_(r+1)). Since
chi_s(d)=B(s)^d_0 product_r C_r(s)^(d_r xor d_(r+1)), conditioning on B gives

    <g_i,g_j>/(Gamma_i Gamma_j)
      =(1-epsilon/2)(-7/10)^k(d)
           +(epsilon/2)(-1)^d_0(9/10)^k(d).                       (6)

In particular ||g_i||=Gamma_i. At an odd-sample transition consisting of
a level-k bridge and its following leaf, the three signs, after multiplication
by the first sign, are 1, B C_k, C_k. Thus their correlations are

    w_chr=E[B C_k]=-7/10-epsilon/10,
    p_chr=E[B]=1-epsilon,
    z_chr=E[C_k]=-7/10+4epsilon/5.                               (7)

At two consecutive odd transitions of levels 1 and 2, the three odd signs
are 1,C_1,C_1 C_2. The two intervening even signs are B C_1 and B C_1 C_2.
The additional correlations are

    z2_chr=E[C_1 C_2]=49/100+4epsilon/25,
    w2_chr=E[B C_1 C_2]=49/100-13epsilon/20.                      (8)

These statements also hold in every translated occurrence of the corresponding
ruler pattern: multiplying each character coordinate by its sign at the
first odd sample cancels that prefix from every inner product. The two
changed prefix variables are still C_1,C_2.

The following rational bounds will be used:

    0<epsilon<=1/1000000, 999/1000<delta<1,
    413/1000<t<83/200,
    1413/1000<l<283/200,
    12/5<c_chr<2417/1000,
    603/250<D_chr<483/200,
    2413/1000<u_2<483/200.                                     (9)

Here 707/500<sqrt(2)<99/70 follows by squaring positive rationals.
The lower bound for t follows from
t>(70/169)(1023/1025)>413/1000, and t<sqrt(2)-1<29/70<83/200.
The upper bound for c_chr follows from
c_chr<(169/70)(1025/1024)<2417/1000. The lower bound for D_chr follows
from D_chr>1+(1413/1000)(999999/1000000)>603/250.
Finally u_2=sigma(1-1/m^2), so
u_2>(1207/500)(1-1/1024^2)>2413/1000 and u_2<169/70<483/200.
The remaining bounds follow directly from m>=1024, including
epsilon=2^(-m)<2^(-20)<1/1000000. No machine search enters these bounds.

## 3. Original pair constraints, with the intervening gradient retained

For the actual values f_i=F(X_i)-F_star, accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`
gives EVERY ordered inequality

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.             (10)

We use necessary sums of these original inequalities, not a sufficient
surrogate. Every function in the statement must also obey all unused pairs
and both optimum directions.

At consecutive samples with step 1+u, normalized correlation d, and norm
ratio r>0, the sum of the two ordered inequalities is

    r^2+(u-1)d r-u<=0.                                      (11)

For u>0 and -1<=d<=1 this implies r<=max(1,u): the polynomial has one
positive root; its value at 1 is (1-u)(1-d)>=0 if u<=1, and its value
at u is u(u-1)(1+d)>=0 if u>=1. In particular every leaf has next norm
at most its preceding norm, since t<1. This step uses no saturation.

Now take one bridge of excess u=u_k and its following leaf. Let A be the
norm at the original odd sample before the bridge, rA the norm at the
intervening even sample, and qA the norm at the following odd sample.
The leaf bound gives r>=q. The two physical updates are retained:

    X_after-X_before=-(1+u)g_before-l g_middle.

Summing (10) just for the two odd endpoints, and substituting (7), gives
exactly

    [Q_(before,after)+Q_(after,before)]/A^2
      =q^2-u+(u-1)z_chr q+l r(p_chr q-w_chr).                  (12)

Since p_chr q-w_chr>0, replacing r by its lower bound q makes the
right side no larger. Using (7) then yields the necessary inequality

    D_chr q^2+beta_chr(D_chr-u)q
                    +(4epsilon/5)(u+t)q-u <=0.                (13)

All terms involving the discrepancy have their displayed signs. In
particular the last positive term can be dropped for a weaker NECESSARY
bound. Define R_chr(v), for v>0, to be the positive root of

    R_chr(v)^2+(7/10)(1-v)R_chr(v)-v=0.                        (14)

Then every such odd-to-odd transition obeys q<=R_chr(u/D_chr).
This cap does not discard the middle vector: (12) is its exact contribution
and r>=q is a proved inequality on its amplitude.

We need the following explicit consequences of (9),(14):

    level 1: q<=r_low:=59/125,
    level 2: q<=501/500,
    level k>=3: q<eta_chr u_k/D_chr, eta_chr:=9/10.             (15)

For level 1, u_1=delta<1. At q=r_low the left side of (13) without its
positive discrepancy term is at least
(603/250)(r_low^2+(7/10)r_low)-1-(7/10)r_low>0.
For level 2, (14) and the argument for (11) give
R_chr(u_2/D_chr)<=max(1,u_2/D_chr)<(483/200)/(603/250)<501/500.
For k>=3, v=u_k/D_chr is at least u_3/D_chr, which is greater than
[(999/1000)(12/5)^2]/(483/200)>37/18. At q=(9/10)v, the polynomial
in (14) equals v[(9/50)v-37/100]>0. This proves the last cap.

For later use the physical level-2 bridge itself satisfies

    norm_after_bridge <=(15/7) norm_before_bridge.             (16)

Indeed its correlation is w_chr. In (11), at r=15/7, its polynomial is
bounded below by
(15/7)^2-(283/200)(7/10+1/10000000)(15/7)-483/200>0,
using u_2-1<283/200 and -w_chr<=7/10+1/10000000.

## 4. A three-odd-sample cycle forces a fixed loss for ALL amplitudes

Consider consecutive odd samples before and after a level-1 transition and
then a level-2 transition. At the first H_3 occurrence these are the ORIGINAL
samples 1,3,5, with ORIGINAL intervening even samples 2,4. Use temporary
names O_0,O_1,O_2 for these odd samples and E_1,E_2 for the two even samples.
Their gradient norms are

    ||g_(O_0)||=A,
    ||g_(O_1)||=r A, ||g_(O_2)||=q A,
    ||g_(E_1)||=a A, ||g_(E_2)||=b A.                          (17)

The already derived original comparisons give

    a>=r, q<= (501/500)r, r<=59/125,
    b<= (15/7)r,
    q<= (501/500)(59/125)<473/1000.                            (18)

Let u=u_1=delta and v=u_2. Form one ORIGINAL directed cycle

    T_cyc=Q_(O_0,O_2)+Q_(O_1,O_0)+Q_(O_2,O_1).                (19)

All values and the common anchor cancel. The two actual displacements are

    X_(O_1)-X_(O_0)=-(1+u)g_(O_0)-l g_(E_1),
    X_(O_2)-X_(O_1)=-(1+v)g_(O_1)-l g_(E_2).

Expanding (19) with these displacements and (7),(8) gives EXACTLY

    T_cyc/A^2 = -u+r^2+q^2+(u-v-1)z_chr r
                +v z_chr r q-z2_chr q
                +l a(p_chr r-w_chr)+l b(p_chr q-w2_chr).     (20)

The intervening vectors have not been merged or identified with an odd
gradient. Both a and b remain in this identity. By (9),(18),

    p_chr r-w_chr>0,
    p_chr q-w2_chr<473/1000-(49/100-13/20000000)<0.

Therefore a>=r and b<=(15/7)r imply

    T_cyc/A^2 >= -u+D_chr r^2+q^2+C_chr r+E_chr r q-z2_chr q,
    C_chr=(u-v-1)z_chr-l w_chr-(15/7)l w2_chr,
    E_chr=v z_chr+(15/7)l p_chr.                            (21)

The constants obey

    C_chr>119/100, E_chr>4/3, z2_chr<491/1000.               (22)

For C_chr, since u<=1, (7),(8) give the lower bound

    C_chr >= v(7/10-4epsilon/5)-(7/20)l
             > (2413/1000)(7/10-4/5000000)
                         -(7/20)(283/200)>119/100.

The discarded epsilon contribution in -w_chr-(15/7)w2_chr is positive;
its zero-epsilon value is -7/20. For E_chr,

    E_chr >= -(7/10)v+(15/7)l(1-epsilon)
             >-(7/10)(483/200)
               +(15/7)(1413/1000)(999999/1000000)>4/3.

The last bound in (22) follows directly from (8),(9).

Suppose q>=2/5. By (18), r>=(500/501)q>(499/500)q. Dropping only
positive quantities in (21),(22) gives

    T_cyc/A^2 >= P_chr(q),
    P_chr(q)=[(12/5)(499/500)^2+1+(4/3)(499/500)]q^2
                +[(119/100)(499/500)-491/1000]q-1.           (23)

Both displayed coefficients are positive, so P_chr increases for q>=0.
Direct rational arithmetic at q=2/5 gives

    P_chr(2/5)=1594697/46875000 >3/100.                     (24)

Thus T_cyc>3 A^2/100. At least one of the THREE original ordered residuals
in (19) is greater than A^2/100. This contradicts (10), regardless of the
anchor and of every assigned function value. Every legal realization must
therefore satisfy the strict compound cap

    Gamma_(O_2)/Gamma_(O_0)<2/5.                           (25)

This argument allowed arbitrary nonsaturating amplitudes and all the
slack they could supply at BOTH intervening leaves. It is a direct
obstruction in the actual primal Gram, not an imported tensor-dual sign
condition or an assumption of bounded conditioning.

## 5. Pay the total loss over the entire original word

It is convenient to index the odd samples by r, writing
O_r=Gamma_(2r+1), 0<=r<N/2. Between O_r and O_(r+1) there are exactly
the original bridge of level 1+nu_2(r+1) and its following leaf. This is
indexing only: all the underlying gradients remain in (12),(20).

Let J_0 be the empty list and J_j=(J_(j-1),j,J_(j-1)). The list of these
odd-transition levels is J_(m-1). A block J_2=(1,2,1) first obeys (25)
and then the level-1 cap in (15), so its total amplitude ratio is less than

    Q_chr=(2/5)(59/125)=118/625.                            (26)

For any occurrence of J_(j-1), j>=3, multiply this bound over its
2^(j-3) disjoint J_2 blocks, and the last bound in (15) over the remaining
levels k>=3. The exact counts are

    sum_(k=3)^(j-1)2^(j-k-1)=2^(j-3)-1,
    sum_(k=3)^(j-1)(k-1)2^(j-k-1)=3*2^(j-3)-j.              (27)

These follow by induction in j, starting at j=3 where both sums are empty.
Since u_k=delta c_chr^(k-1), the resulting bound is

    O_after/O_before <= L_j,
    L_j=[D_chr/(eta_chr delta)] c_chr^(-j)
                            Theta_chr^(2^j/8),
    Theta_chr=Q_chr eta_chr delta c_chr^3/D_chr.             (28)

No overlapping transition is charged twice. In particular the first leaf
of the ORIGINAL H_j is outside this odd-transition block and only contributes
an extra factor at most one.

The bounds (9) imply

    0<Theta_chr
      < (118/625)(9/10)(2417/1000)^3/(603/250)
      <199/200.                                           (29)

This is an explicit rational inequality; delta<1 was dropped upwards.
Formula (28) quantifies the TOTAL loss, including every repeated low block
and every high bridge of the unchanged original horizon. In particular

    Gamma_n/Gamma_0
      <=[D_chr/(eta_chr delta)]c_chr^(-m)
                                  Theta_chr^(N/8).         (30)

## 6. Prefix control includes the even samples

First every odd sample has norm at most Gamma_0. To prove this, induct on
the recursive list J_j. For J_1 the cap is r_low<1. For J_2, the norm after
its middle level-2 transition is at most r_low(501/500) times its start,
which is less than one, and the two level-1 edges contract. For j>=3,
the left J_(j-1) has norm ratio at most L_j by (28). Its following level-j
transition has norm ratio less than eta_chr delta c_chr^(j-1)/D_chr.
Their product is

    c_chr^(-1) Theta_chr^(2^j/8)<1.                        (31)

The induction hypothesis controls every prefix in the left block; (31)
controls the starting norm of the right block, where the same induction
hypothesis applies. Initially O_0<=Gamma_0 by the first leaf comparison.
This proves the claim for ALL original odd samples with inherited state.

Every remaining even sample except X_0 lies immediately after one bridge.
For a level-1 bridge, (11) gives even norm at most the preceding odd norm,
since u_1<1. For a level-2 bridge the preceding J_1 supplies a factor r_low;
(11) gives even norm at most u_2 r_low Gamma_0, with

    u_2 r_low<(483/200)(59/125)<6/5.

For a level-j bridge with j>=3, the preceding J_(j-1) and (11),(28) give

    even norm/Gamma_0 <=u_j L_j
       =[D_chr/(eta_chr c_chr)]Theta_chr^(2^j/8)
       <(483/200)/[(9/10)(12/5)]<6/5.                     (32)

At every occurrence the starting odd norm is already at most Gamma_0.
Together these estimates prove (3), including every original intermediate
gradient that was not an endpoint in the cycle calculation.

## 7. True closest-minimizer normalization

The minimizer set is nonempty and closed. Its distance from X_0 is attained:
a minimizing sequence may be restricted to a bounded closed ball in the
finite-dimensional Euclidean space and hence has a convergent subsequence.
Take a closest minimizer X_star, without assuming it is the origin. Since
grad F(X_star)=0, smoothness implies

    Gamma_0<=R_dist.                                      (33)

The exact original mass is

    M_chr=1+sum_(i<n)h_i
         =N+a_chr(c_chr^m-N)/(c_chr-2)<c_chr^m.             (34)

The equality follows by counting the 2^(m-k-1) level-k steps, including
leaves, and summing the geometric progression. The inequality follows from
c_chr>sigma>2 and c_chr(c_chr-2)>sigma(sigma-2)=1>delta,
so 0<a_chr<c_chr-2. Thus the displayed expression is a strict convex
combination of N and c_chr^m, the latter being larger.

Using (3),(33), the actual chronological updates give

    ||X_n-X_star|| <=R_dist+sum_(i<n)h_i Gamma_i
       <=[1+(6/5)sum_(i<n)h_i] R_dist
       <=(6/5)M_chr R_dist<(6/5)c_chr^m R_dist.             (35)

Convexity at X_n gives F(X_n)-F_star<=<g_n,X_n-X_star>.
Combine (30),(33),(35) to obtain

    V_chr < (12/5)[D_chr/(eta_chr delta)]Theta_chr^(N/8)
      <7(199/200)^(N/8),                                 (36)

because (12/5)(483/200)/[(9/10)(999/1000)]<7. This proves (4).
Every radius in this argument is the TRUE distance. If F is an anchored
projection interpolant its minimizers form the appropriate polar cone;
X_star may be nonzero. No inverse-Gram expression for the radius, forced
positive-cone anchor, or origin-distance substitute is used. The cost of
the conservative bound R_dist>=Gamma_0 and the path estimate is visible
in the finite prefactor in (36).

Accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d` gives B_n<=1+4n^log_2(3). This proves (5).
For completeness its right side tends to zero because the logarithm of
its exponential factor is ((n+1)/8)log(199/200), whereas the logarithm of
its polynomial factor is O(log n). This keeps the original B_n and horizon.

## 8. Scope and proof status

The proposed low-bit discrepancy epsilon=1/N does NOT cure the fixed
conditional-prefix policy (1), even if one chooses an arbitrary positive
nonsaturating amplitude law. The obstruction does not use continuity at
a singular Gram: every finite measure has all weights positive, every
finite trajectory must satisfy (10), and the same explicit constants work
for every original m>=1024. No condition-number assumption is made.

This is a quantified necessary-condition obstruction. It need not choose an
