evidence:
# C68: a global chronological budget for the actual quartic epigraph

Status: COMPLETE UNVERIFIED candidate, fifth launch round 1 (cumulative 12).
No fact_submit, trajectory evaluation, numerical optimization, installation,
or new allocation was used. The only accepted mathematical predecessor is
b98bb807d514e80d, used for the exact benchmark recursions. All function,
trajectory, block, and combinatorial assertions used below are proved here.
C65, C66, and C67 are context, not proof premises.

## 1. Definitions and result

Throughout this document the power is FIXED at 4. For each integer m>=512 set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/m,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The H_j here are local schedule words, not the conjugate quadratics called
H_j in a different accepted fact. Every embedded word uses this SAME a,c.
Index physical steps by t=1,...,n. Let nu_2(t) be the exponent of 2 in t and
b(t) the number of 1 bits in the binary expansion of t, with b(0)=0. Then

    h_t=1+d_(nu_2(t)).                                     (1)

Define the single global function and its state coordinates by

    K_4={(r,s) in R^2:s>=r^4/4},
    F_4(X)=max_(g in K_4) (<X,g>-||g||^2/2),
    eta=v+r^4/4, u=eta r^2=vr^2+r^6/4,
    X(r,v)=(r(1+u),-v), G(r)=(r,r^4/4), v>=0.

Here r,v,u,eta and X,G denote local state variables. Write x for the
horizontal coordinate of X and R=|x|. Start from arbitrary r_0!=0 and
v_0>=0, and run the given H_m on this same F_4:

    X_t=X_(t-1)-h_t grad F_4(X_(t-1)), 1<=t<=n.

Section 2 proves global legality, the unique actual recurrence, and

    min F_4=0, argmin F_4={(0,y):y<=0},
    R_0=dist(X_0,argmin F_4)=|r_0|(1+u_0),
    2F_4(X(r,v))=r^2+(3/2)v r^4+(7/16)r^8.               (2)

A turn is a step t with x_(t-1)x_t<0. The following bounds hold jointly
for EVERY such initial state, without restricting the number or levels of
turns:

    R_t<=R_0 for every t,
    R_t<=c^(-b(t))R_0 at every turn t,                    (3)
    P_4:=2F_4(X_n)/R_0^2 <=3/(8S_m).                     (4)

The retained clock cost, including the nonnegative contributions at every
step, is

    J_all=(1/2)sum_(t=1)^n |r_(t-1)|^2(v_t-v_(t-1))
         =(1/8)sum_(t=1)^n h_t |r_(t-1)|^6.

It satisfies the explicit global charge

    J_all <= min{
       |r_0|^2(v_n-v_0)/2,
       R_0 |r_0|^5 [2(1+1/c)^m-1]/8
    },                                                   (5)

and, using only the original closest-minimizer distance,

    J_all <=4^(5/7) R_0^(12/7)[2(1+1/c)^m-1]/8.           (6)

No assertion that J_all vanishes, or that a logarithmic clock decreases
across zero, is made. The quantitative objective bound (4) uses the
chronological block budget directly; it does not delete J_all.

For the EXACT Zhang--Jiang denominator B_n defined in accepted fact
b98bb807d514e80d, Section 8 proves

    B_(2^m-1) P_4 <625/1536<1/2       for all m>=512,      (7)
    limsup_(m->infinity) sup_(r_0!=0,v_0>=0)
        B_(2^m-1) P_4 <=3lambda/(8e)<3/8.                (8)

This excludes the whole stated quartic epigraph family as a matching
adversary on these schedules. It is NOT an upper bound for unrestricted
W_n and does not settle the original all-schedule profile problem.

## 2. The global function, ordered pairs, distance, and physical recursion

K_4 is nonempty, closed, and convex. Completing the square in the defining
maximum shows that its unique maximizing g is the Euclidean projection
Pi_(K_4)(X). The normal inequalities at projections of X and Y give

    ||Pi_(K_4)(X)-Pi_(K_4)(Y)||^2
       <=<Pi_(K_4)(X)-Pi_(K_4)(Y),X-Y>.

Thus the projection is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the defining maxima gives

    0<=F_4(Y)-F_4(X)-<Pi_(K_4)(X),Y-X>
      <=<Pi_(K_4)(Y)-Pi_(K_4)(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

It follows that F_4 is differentiable with gradient Pi_(K_4), hence has
1-Lipschitz gradient. Convexity follows from its supremum of affine
functions representation.

For phi(r)=r^4/4, one has

    X(r,v)-G(r)=eta*(phi'(r),-1).

For any (z,s) in K_4 its inner product with (z,s)-G(r) is at most

    eta*[phi'(r)(z-r)-phi(z)+phi(r)]<=0.

The last inequality is the tangent inequality for the convex function
phi. This proves grad F_4(X(r,v))=G(r). Substitution into the maximum
proves the value in (2). In particular, if f_i=F_4(X_i), every ordered
pair of states in this construction has the exact residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =eta_j*[r_j^3(r_i-r_j)-r_i^4/4+r_j^4/4]<=0.      (9)

There is no restriction on temporal separation in (9).

If x=0 and y<=0, the maximum is zero: zero is feasible, and every feasible
g=(r,s) has s>=0, so ys-||g||^2/2<=0. If x!=0, test g=(r,r^4/4)
with sufficiently small r of the sign of x; the positive term xr
dominates the terms of order 2 or higher. If x=0 and y>0, a sufficiently
small g=(0,s), s>0, gives positive value. This proves the exact minimizer
set in (2). Its closest point to (x,-v), v>=0, is (0,-v), proving the
true distance formula without retaining a spurious initial vertical norm.

The actual GD step of size h>=0 is exactly

    v_plus=v+h r^4/4,
    x_plus=x-hr,
    x_plus=T_(v_plus)(r_plus),
    T_v(r)=r+v r^3+r^7/4.                               (10)

T_v is odd and strictly increasing onto R, since

    T_v'(r)=1+3vr^2+7r^6/4>=1.

It therefore determines the unique actual r_plus. In particular
sign(r)=sign(x). If r reaches zero, x=0 and G(r)=0, so the trajectory is
absorbed with zero subsequent objective and clock cost.

On any interval where all states are nonzero and have the same sign,
R decreases and v increases. Equation (10) then shows that |r| decreases.
Reflection allows every such interval to be treated on the positive ray.

For later use, smoothness and the minimizer (0,-v) give 2F_4(X)<=R^2.
This can also be checked from the explicit state formula: with z=r^6/4,

    2F_4(X)/r^2=1+(3/2)u+z/4,
    R^2/r^2=(1+u)^2,

and their difference is u/2+u^2-z/4>=u/4+u^2>=0 because 0<=z<=u.

## 3. A no-turn block pays for the loss of normal state

Consider any actual occurrence of H_l, l>=1, along which every state is
nonzero and has the same sign. No entry v is reset. Let r>0 and u>0 be
the terminal gradient magnitude and effective normal state, and let
rho>0 and u_mid be their counterparts immediately BEFORE the middle
step 1+d_(l-1). Since that step does not turn or annihilate,

    u_mid>d_(l-1).                                      (11)

Monotonicity on this interval gives rho>=r and v_mid<=v_end. Consequently

    u_mid=v_mid rho^2+rho^6/4
          <=(rho/r)^6 (v_end r^2+r^6/4)
          =(rho/r)^6 u.                                (12)

Let Apre_l=S_(l-1)+1+d_(l-1)=M_(l-1)+d_(l-1) be the sum of steps
through the middle step. Every gradient used by those steps has
magnitude at least rho; every later gradient has magnitude at least r.
Telescoping the actual horizontal motion, with R_entry its input radius,
therefore gives

    R_entry/r
      >=M_l+u+Apre_l*((d_(l-1)/u)^(1/6)-1)_+.            (13)

Here (z)_+=max(z,0). If u>=d_(l-1)/2, the explicit u in (13) is at
least d_(l-1)/2. If u<d_(l-1)/2, then

    (d_(l-1)/u)^(1/6)>2^(1/6)>11/10,

because (11/10)^6=1771561/1000000<2. Since Apre_l>=d_(l-1), the
last term in (13) exceeds d_(l-1)/10. Thus in both cases

    R_entry >=Aend_l |r_end|,
    Aend_l:=M_l+d_(l-1)/10.                             (14)

For the empty word define Aend_0=1; the same gradient bound is the state
identity R=|r|(1+u)>=|r|. If an endpoint is absorbed, the gradient bound
with its zero terminal gradient holds as well.

This is the key replacement for a frozen-normal argument. A decrease in
terminal u is permitted. Equation (12) charges that decrease to earlier
gradient magnitudes, and equation (13) charges those magnitudes to the
TRUE horizontal entry distance. No inequality u_end>=u_mid is used.

## 4. Uniform capacity of every no-turn H_l in the enclosing word

The word recursion implies M_(l+1)=2M_l+d_l and M_0=1. Set

    A_mass=a/(c-2).

Solving this elementary recurrence gives

    M_l=A_mass c^l+(1-A_mass)2^l.                        (15)

Since lambda(lambda-2)=1 and c>lambda, one has c(c-2)>1>1-epsilon.
It follows that 0<A_mass<1. In particular,

    M_l/d_l>=1/(c-2).                                  (16)

For m>=512, sqrt(2)<99/70 gives

    c<(169/70)(513/512)<121/50.

The function z-1/(z-2)-1/(10z) is strictly increasing for z>2. At
z=121/50 its value is -289/127050<0. Therefore

    1/(c-2)+1/(10c)>c.

Combining this with (14) and (16) proves

    Aend_l>=c d_l=a c^(l+1)        for l>=1.             (17)

For l=0 the same conclusion holds because

    Aend_0=1>ac=1-1/m.                                  (18)

Equations (17)--(18) are uniform over the block position, initial state,
and l. They use the enclosing a,c throughout.

## 5. A binary interval lemma and chronological turn accounting

We first prove the combinatorial statement required to combine real
one-sign intervals. If integers 0<=s<t satisfy

    q=b(t-1)-b(s)>=1,

then [s,t] contains an aligned closed dyadic interval [A,A+2^q], where
A is a multiple of 2^q.

Proof. Put B=2^q, write s=kB+r with 0<=r<B, and suppose no such
interval is contained. If r=0, the first possible interval starts at s,
so t<s+B. Then t-1 has high binary part k and a low part at most B-2;
hence b(t-1)-b(s)<=q-1, a contradiction.

If r>0, the first possible start is (k+1)B, so t<(k+2)B. If t-1
has high part k, its low part has at most q ones, whereas b(r)>=1,
again giving difference at most q-1. If t-1 has high part k+1, its
low part is at most B-2 and has at most q-1 ones. Adding 1 to k
increases its bit count by at most 1. Thus the difference is at most
1+(q-1)-b(r)<=q-1. This contradiction proves the lemma.             (19)

An aligned interval [A,A+2^q] corresponds to the actual subword H_q
at physical step indices A+1,...,A+2^q-1: for 0<j<2^q,
nu_2(A+j)=nu_2(j). This uses the same physical a,c.

Now let s<t be consecutive actual turn times, allowing s=0 for the
initial boundary before the first turn. The steps s+1,...,t-1 form
one same-sign interval. Set

    q=max{0,b(t-1)-b(s)}, ell=nu_2(t).

If q>=1, (19) finds an actual no-turn H_q inside this interval. Its
entry horizontal radius is at most R_s, and its terminal gradient
magnitude is at least |r_(t-1)|, by monotonicity on the entire interval.
Equations (14) and (17) therefore give

    R_s>=Aend_q |r_(t-1)|>=a c^(q+1)|r_(t-1)|.           (20)

For q=0, use R_s>=|r_(t-1)| and (18) to get the same result. At the
actual turn t, equation (10) gives

    R_t=(d_ell-u_(t-1))|r_(t-1)|
        <=a c^ell |r_(t-1)|
        <=c^(ell-q-1)R_s.                              (21)

The elementary binary identity

    b(t-1)=b(t)-1+nu_2(t)

and q>=b(t-1)-b(s) imply

    R_t<=c^(b(s)-b(t))R_s.                              (22)

Starting at s=0 and telescoping (22) over the ACTUAL turns proves the
second part of (3). Between turns the radius decreases, proving the
first part of (3). This argument allows arbitrary repeated rises and
falls in turn level. It neither optimizes right copies independently
nor assumes that u is monotone.

## 6. Global payment of the retained moving-normal cost

For context, on a positive one-sign interval define the local clock

    C_4(r,v)=log r+(3/2)vr^2+(7/24)r^6,
    Psi(x,v)=C_4(T_v^(-1)(x),v), x>0.

Differentiating T_v(r)=x gives

    partial_x Psi=1/r, partial_v Psi=r^2/2.

For one positive noncrossing step, first move horizontally at the old v
and then increase v at the new horizontal coordinate. Monotonicity of
T_v^(-1) bounds the two resulting integrals and yields

    C_4(r_plus,v_plus)-C_4(r,v)
       <=-h+(r^2/2)(v_plus-v).                          (23)

Reflection covers a negative one-sign interval. This derivation retains
the positive cost, and does not extend the logarithm across annihilation
or sign changes.

The global radius result (3), together with v_t>=v_0 and monotonicity of
T_v on the positive ray, implies

    |r_t|<=|r_0|  for every t.                           (24)

The first bound in (5) now follows by summing the defining weighted
vertical increments of J_all.

To obtain the second bound, set TV_x=sum_(t=1)^n h_t|r_(t-1)|, the
total absolute horizontal displacement. At a nonturn step (including
one that reaches zero), its contribution is R_(t-1)-R_t. At a turn it
is R_(t-1)+R_t. Consequently the exact telescoping identity is

    TV_x=R_0-R_n+2 sum_(t a turn) R_t.                   (25)

Use (3), and expand the product over the m independent binary digits:

    sum_(t=0)^(2^m-1)c^(-b(t))=(1+1/c)^m.

It follows that

    TV_x<=R_0[2(1+1/c)^m-1].                            (26)

Since J_all=(1/8)sum h_t|r_(t-1)|*|r_(t-1)|^5, (24)--(26) prove
the second bound in (5). Finally R_0>=|r_0|^7/4 by the state formula,
so R_0|r_0|^5<=4^(5/7)R_0^(12/7), proving (6).

Thus the sum of all one-sign J costs is bounded by (5)--(6), since it
is no larger than J_all. The bounds retain the initial radius and,
in the first version, the actual terminal vertical state. They remain
valid for trajectories that annihilate; their subsequent contributions
are zero. No lower bound on nonzero |r_t| is needed.

## 7. Terminal payoff, with every entry-radius factor retained

Consider any nonzero same-sign interval with total step mass T>=1/6.
Write r>0 for its terminal gradient magnitude and u=vr^2+r^6/4 for
its terminal normal state. The actual recursion, without resetting v,
gives

    R_entry>=r(T+1+u),
    v_end>=T r^4/4.

Put z=r^6/4. Then z<=u/(T+1), and (2) implies

    2F_4(X_end)/R_entry^2
       <=[1+k_T u]/(T+1+u)^2,
    k_T=3/2+1/[4(T+1)].

The derivative of the last rational function has the sign of
k_T(T+1)-2-k_T u. Since T>=1/6, its maximum on u>=0 is attained at
u=T+1-2/k_T and equals

    E_4(T)=(6T+7)^2/[48(T+1)^2(2T+1)]<=3/(8T).          (27)

For the last comparison the numerator of the difference, over denominator
48T(T+1)^2(2T+1), is 6T^2+23T+18>0. An absorbing terminal state has
zero payoff and satisfies the desired bound separately.

If the full run is nonabsorbed, let s be its last actual turn, or let
s=0 if it has no turns. Set b=b(s) and q=m-b. Apply (19) with
t=2^m. The final same-sign interval contains an actual H_q. If q>=1,
its full mass T is at least S_q>=S_1>1, so (3) and (27) give

    P_4<=c^(-2b)*3/(8S_q).                              (28)

The factor c^(-2b) in (28) is the ACTUAL entry-radius ratio bounded in
terms of the original R_0. A later block has not been renormalized as a
fresh problem.

For j>=1, (15) gives

    S_(j+1)-c S_j=c-1-(c-2)(1-A_mass)2^j<=c-1.

Since S_j>1 and c>1, this implies

    S_(j+1)<(2c-1)S_j<c^2 S_j.

Iterating yields S_m<=c^(2b)S_q, so (28) is at most 3/(8S_m).

If q=0, then b(s)=m and s=n, so the last step turns. Use the terminal
state bound 2F_4<=R_n^2 and (3) to obtain P_4<=c^(-2m). Since (15)
gives S_m<c^m and c^m>8/3 for m>=512, this is smaller than 3/(8S_m).
This proves (4) for every initial state, including all turn patterns.

## 8. The exact benchmark and the uniform comparison

Accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d defines the exact primitive and dominant
benchmark recursions. In their mass coordinates C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and
B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 they are

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(C_k,B_l),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

We prove directly from these recursions that

    B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).                             (29)

Set alpha=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda) and
Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Both coefficients in Llin exceed 1, so
Llin>=x+y. Direct expansion, using lambda^2=2lambda+1, gives

    alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
      =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

Thus Llin>=Omega(x,y), the positive root of z^2-(x+y)z-xy. At
z=lambda Omega(x,y), the polynomial with larger root G(x,lambda y) is

    z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
      =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, so z is to the right of that
polynomial's vertex. Hence G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y).
Induction in the exact recursions proves B_n<=lambda C_n.

Put gamma=log_2(lambda)>1, D(t)=(1+t)^gamma-1, and
ell(z)=log D(exp z). For t=exp z, differentiation gives

    ell''(z)=gamma*t*(1+t)^(gamma-2)
      *[(1+t)^gamma-1-gamma*t]/D(t)^2>0.

The last bracket has value zero at t=0 and positive derivative for t>0.
Convexity therefore implies D(t)D(1/t)>=D(1)^2=2. For x,y>0 set
Z=(x^(1/gamma)+y^(1/gamma))^gamma. Taking t=(y/x)^(1/gamma) shows
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy. Thus Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0; also Z>=x+y, by convexity
of the positive power. Consequently Omega(x,y)<=Z. The zero cases
follow by direct substitution. Induction yields C_n<=(n+1)^gamma,
which, with B_n<=lambda C_n, proves (29).

For a finite comparison, c<121/50 and m>=512 imply

    A_mass=(1-1/m)/[c(c-2)]
      >(511/512)/(2541/2500)>49/50.

Since c>2 and m>=512, c^(-m)<1/50. Equation (15) therefore gives

    S_m/c^m>24/25.

The first three binomial terms show

    (1+1/m)^m>=2+(m-1)/(2m)>=12/5,

where the final inequality already holds for m>=5. Combining (4),
(29), lambda<5/2, and (lambda/c)^m<=5/12 gives

    B_n P_4
       <(3/8)*(5/2)*(5/12)*(25/24)
       =625/1536<1/2,

proving (7).

As m tends to infinity, A_mass tends to 1, c tends to lambda, and

    S_m/c^m=A_mass+(1-A_mass)(2/c)^m-c^(-m) ->1,
    (lambda/c)^m=(1+1/m)^(-m) ->1/e.

Every bound above is uniform over r_0!=0,v_0>=0, so (4) and (29)
give (8). Finally e>1+1+1/2=5/2>lambda, proving 3lambda/(8e)<3/8.
No limiting formula for the exact sequence B_n has been assumed.

## 9. Scope, literature, and symbolic audit

The proof addresses the whole unscaled quartic epigraph model stated in
Section 1, at all initial horizontal radii and nonnegative vertical
states, including horizon-dependent choices. Its global charge and
payoff combine arbitrary actual turn histories. Lower-level reactivation
is allowed. This is a proper-family exclusion, not a conclusion about
all functions, other powers, or the original all-h target.

The projection background is consistent with Propositions 3.2--3.3 of
Chierchia, Pustelnik, Pesquet, and Pesquet-Popescu, "Epigraphical splitting
for solving constrained convex formulations of inverse problems with
proximal tools", arXiv:1210.5844v3. Their Hilbert product is Euclidean;
their scalar generator has full domain and is proper closed convex;
beta=4, tau=1/4, zeta=-v yield T_v(r)=x. The exact locally downloaded
paper's definitions and projection proof were read. No external result
from it is used as a proof premise. The dedicated theorem searches for
the moving-state budget and the binary interval lemma returned no usable
result; both have been proved directly here.

Symbolic boundary checks:

* Consecutive actual turns have an empty intervening H_0. The necessary
  charge is exactly Aend_0>=ac; no unqueried lower-level step is invented.
* The aligned case [s,t]=[A,A+2^q] uses the full actual H_q, with no
  missing first or last step and no change of enclosing parameters.
* Negative binary-count differences are handled by q=max(0,difference)
  in (20)--(22), not by a fictitious word of negative length.
* A turn at the final step has q=0 and uses the smoothness bound, not
  formula (27) at zero mass.
* Exact zero is absorbing. No logarithm is evaluated there, and the
  main payoff proof uses no logarithm at all.
* Very small nonzero gradients cause no reciprocal estimate with an
  uncontrolled constant; (13) charges small terminal u explicitly.
* The proof does not freeze v, assume monotonicity of u, or discard the
  positive moving-normal cost. The complete all-pair function and true
  denominator were established before the block argument.

The separate possible concave-clock integral explored in rough local
notes is unnecessary here and is not a premise. No verification success

# Chronological kernel: an explicit local square decomposition

Status: **unverified proof draft**, fifth launch, first continuation round.
There is a complete algebraic factorization below, including the constant
gradient column and the original initial-position variable. Its coefficient
signs have passed an outward-interval evaluation at the actual depth128.
This is not a uniform proof for all m>=128, a verifier-accepted fact, or a
solution of the original minimax problem. No fact_submit was allocated or used.

The new theoretical question is the sign of explicitly displayed scalar
coefficients in the birth coordinates. This is a sufficient condition for
the old covariance inequality; equivalence of their positivity is NOT claimed.

## 1. Original word, shared data, and exact certificate identity

For an integer m>=128 set epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2),
c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c, d_j=1+a*c^j, and
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j). Let q=2^m-2 and let h_0,...,h_(q-1)
be H_m with its final d_0 removed. Define s_i=sum_(r<i)h_r and S=s_q.
For real vectors v,w_0,...,w_(m-1), all using one arbitrary common Gram,
put p_ij=product_(r<i)(1-h_r/d_j), g_i=v+sum_j p_ij*w_j, and
x_i=x_0-sum_(r<i)h_r*g_r. The first d_j kills its column at query2^j.
Thus g_q=v and x_q=x_0-S*v-sum_j d_j*w_j.

For one common array of sampled values and the zero optimum jet, use
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2. Necessity and sufficiency
of the entire interpolation array are in accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290.
Define, purely algebraically,

 J=sum_(i<q) [2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
             +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].

The GD norm identity and summation by parts give

 ||x_0||^2-2S*f_q+2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)
                  +2sum_i s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)=||x_q||^2+J.       (1)

Indeed the optimum terms equal
2sum h_i f_i-||x_0||^2+||x_q||^2+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2;
the chain terms equal 2S f_q-2sum h_i f_i plus the first two terms of J.
All selected multipliers are nonnegative. No unused original interpolation
constraint is deleted from the definition of legal data.

Let T be the symmetric matrix of J in (w_0,...,w_(m-1),v). For a word W,
put P_W(z)=product_(h in W)(1-hz) and S_W=sum W. The zero-clock kernels
K,T satisfy, for concatenated words U,V,

 K_UV=K_U+P_U(z)P_U(w)K_V,
 T_UV=T_U+P_U(z)P_U(w)[T_V+2S_U K_V],                         (2)
 K_[h]=h-h^2(z+w-zw)/2,
 T_[h]=h(h+1)-h^3(z+w-zw).

These follow by separating the defining time sums, retaining the offset
S_U in every second-block clock. At z=1/d_j and z=0 these compute the
actual matrix with O(m^3) scalar operations, without enumerating2^m steps.
Deletion of the last d_0 changes only T_(v,v), to S(S+1), because all
residual columns are already zero. This final diagonal is retained below.

For comparison with the earlier covariance formulation, D_i=g_i-g_(i+1),
A_ij=h_i*p_ij/d_j, beta_i=s_(i+1)(s_i+1), beta_q=S(S+1), and
c_i=(h_i-1)s_(i+1). Expansion of J and completion of the constant square give

 J=beta_q||v+sum_i beta_i D_i/beta_q||^2
       +sum_(i,l)[beta_min(i,l)-beta_i beta_l/beta_q]<D_i,D_l>
       -sum_i c_i||D_i||^2.                                    (3)

For example the coefficient of ||g_i||^2 after collecting adjacent terms
is beta_i-beta_(i-1); this proves (3) by writing g_i=v+sum_(r>=i)D_r.
Consequently positivity of T is exactly the old covariance domination,
including its constant-mode charge. This is only an equivalence of formal
quadratic forms, not a test of whether a negative formal direction is legal.

## 2. Lossless birth coordinates and exact sparsity

Define phi_k(z)=product_(r<k)(1-d_r*z),
V_k=v+sum_j phi_k(1/d_j)w_j for0<=k<=m, and U_k=V_k-v.
In particular V_m=v and U_m=0. The triangular node-evaluation matrix has
positive diagonal, so these coordinates lose no modal direction.

The identity
(1-hz)phi_k=(1-h/d_k)phi_k+(h/d_k)phi_(k+1)
gives g_i=sum_k B_ik V_k, where B starts at the point mass at0 and
at step h moves mass from state k to k+1 with fraction h/d_k.
An occupied state has d_k>=h. Lower states have already been killed by
their first physical level. Thus B_ik>=0, sum_k B_ik=1, and

 B_ik=0 if k>i or i>=2^k, for k<m.                           (4)

The first zero follows because one step advances at most one state; the
second follows by induction on first physical occurrences.

Set xi_j=d_j*w_j, z=(S+1)v, and y_k=d_k U_k. Then y=R*xi, with

 R_kj=(d_k/d_j)phi_k(1/d_j) for j>=k; R_kj=0 for j<k.

Let M=diag(1/d_0,...,1/d_(m-1),1/(S+1)) T diag(same).
Define the symmetric matrix

 H=diag(R^(-T),1) M diag(R^(-1),1)
       = [ E, ell ; ell^T, D ],       D=S/(S+1).               (5)

Thus J=sum_kl E_kl<y_k,y_l>+2sum_k ell_k<y_k,z>+D||z||^2.
All scalings are positive and R is invertible. The vectors remain in one
real Euclidean space, with their original cross terms.

There are useful EXACT zeros:

                 E_kl=0 if l>2^k and k<l<m.                  (6)

Each term in J uses only g_i and g_(i+1). If its state-k coefficient is
nonzero, (4) forces i+1<=2^k. All states at either query are then <=2^k,
so state l>2^k cannot enter that term. In particular rows0,1 have no
off-diagonal entries beyond columns1,2 respectively. Numerical arithmetic
may be replaced by zero at precisely these positions because of this proof;
no other small entries are discarded.

## 3. Exact square-factor lemma, with the complete constant load

The following is an algebraic identity for ANY symmetric real m-by-m matrix
E and real column ell, with m>=3. Define

 e_i=E_(i,i+2),                    0<=i<=m-3,
 b_i=E_(i,i+1)-2(e_(i-1)+e_i),    0<=i<=m-2,
 r_i=E_ii-E_(i-1,i)-E_(i,i+1)+e_(i-2)+e_i
                   -sum_(|k-i|>=3)|E_ik|, 0<=i<m.             (7)

An out-of-range e or adjacent entry is zero. Put alpha_(-1)=0 and

 alpha_i=ell_i-alpha_(i-1), 0<=i<m,
 C=sum_(i<m-1)alpha_i^2/b_i + alpha_(m-1)^2/r_(m-1),
 Delta=D-C.                                                   (8)

If b_i>0 and r_(m-1)>0, with no other sign assumption yet, then

 J=sum_(i<m-1)r_i||y_i||^2
     +r_(m-1)||y_(m-1)+(alpha_(m-1)/r_(m-1))*z||^2
     +sum_(i<m-1)b_i||y_i+y_(i+1)+(alpha_i/b_i)*z||^2
     +sum_(i<m-2)e_i||y_i+2y_(i+1)+y_(i+2)||^2
     +sum_(k<l, l-k>=3)|E_kl| ||y_k+sgn(E_kl)y_l||^2
     +Delta||z||^2.                                          (9)

For a zero long-range coefficient use sgn(0)=0; its whole term is zero.

Proof. The triple squares supply off-diagonal entry e_i at distance2 and
entries2e_i at each of its two neighboring pairs. Subtracting them leaves
the adjacent coefficient b_i in (7). Their diagonal contributions, together
with those of the pair squares, are
E_(i-1,i)+E_(i,i+1)-e_(i-2)-e_i. Each long-range square contributes
|E_ik| to the corresponding diagonal. The remaining diagonal is exactly r_i.
This proves the residual identity. Finally

 sum_i ell_i y_i=sum_(i<m-1)alpha_i(y_i+y_(i+1))
                                      +alpha_(m-1)y_(m-1)

by ell_i=alpha_i+alpha_(i-1). Completing precisely those displayed squares
spends C and leaves Delta. This proves (9), including all cross terms.

Therefore the explicit scalar conditions

 e_i>=0, b_i>0, r_i>=0 (all i), r_(m-1)>0, Delta>=0            (10)

are SUFFICIENT for the full T to be positive semidefinite. This supplies an
actual square-factor formula, not an LDL recurrence with unknown pivots.
The constant column is paid by the exact alternating loads (8), without a
matrix inverse or pseudoinverse. No individual adjacent-swap sign is used.

The original certificate in (1) has the additional square

 ||x_0-S*z/(S+1)-sum_j xi_j||^2.                              (11)

The change from x_0 to that square's vector is an invertible unit triangular
change of coordinates. Thus (9) plus (11) is a factorization on the FULL
original formal space, including x_0. There is no hidden range condition.

## 4. Uniform exact boundary calculation: a coefficient vanishes as 1/m

Write t=d_0, u=d_1, d=d_2. The first three gradients in birth coordinates
are V_0,V_1,V_2. Direct expansion of the first two physical steps gives

 E_00=(2-t)/t, E_01=(t-1)/u,
 E_11=[2t+u(2-u)]/u^2,
 E_12=(t+u)(u-1)/(u*d).                                     (12)

By (6), e_0=e_1=0 and both rows have no longer tails. Consequently
r_0=E_00-E_01 and r_1=E_11-E_01-E_12. Also b_0=E_01,b_1=E_12.
The actual parameters are

 t=sqrt(2)-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)],
 u=2-epsilon, d=sqrt(2)+2-lambda*epsilon^2.

For 0<epsilon<=1/128, one has 7/5<t<283/200, 199/100<u<2, and d<7/2.
The bound on t follows, for instance, from sqrt(2)>141/100 and
2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]<5/768. Thus

 r_0>117/283-83/398>1/5,       b_0>1/5,       b_1>12/25.       (13)

For b_1, use (t+u)(u-1)> (339/100)(99/100) and
u*d<683/100, since sqrt(2)<283/200 gives d<683/200.

More significantly,

 r_1>3epsilon/2, and r_1/epsilon -> (3sqrt(2)-1)/2.            (14)

Here is a direct sign proof. Put delta=d-t-2. Then
delta/epsilon=2/[lambda(1+epsilon)]-lambda*epsilon>3/4,
using lambda<5/2 and epsilon<=1/128. Multiplication by the positive u^2*d
gives

 u^2*d*r_1
 =epsilon[(t+4)(t+2)+2-epsilon(2t+7)+epsilon^2]
       +[2+epsilon(1+t)-epsilon^2]*delta.

The bracket in the first term exceeds509/25-5/64, and the coefficient
of delta is at least2. The total therefore exceeds21epsilon, whereas
u^2*d<14. This proves the first assertion of (14). Dividing by epsilon
and taking the explicit parameter limits gives
(8+10sqrt(2))/(8+4sqrt(2))=(3sqrt(2)-1)/2.

In particular the finite observed minimum around .01267 cannot be promoted
to a uniform positive lower bound for every r_i. The factorization only
needs r_1>=0; its constant-column completion uses r_(m-1), not r_1.

The first constant loads are also exact:

 ell_0=1/(S+1),
 ell_1=[t^2/u+t+1]/(S+1),
 alpha_0=1/(S+1), alpha_1=[t^2/u+t]/(S+1).                    (15)

These follow by summing the U_0-v and U_1-v coefficients in the same two
steps. No independent scalar heights have been chosen.

## 5. Bounded computation, complete definitions, and its limits

The public ledger is research/max2_chronological_kernel_budget.json.
It records attempts BEFORE evaluation and measured cost afterward. Eight of
twelve cases used53.087538152998604 of120 measured seconds. All software was

6. Full word m128, precision150, explicit local factor coefficients (7)-(8).
7. Outward intervals, embedded H_4 at enclosing m128, precision70: interval
   calibration, containment of the previous90-digit reference, and all factor

8. Outward intervals, full word m128, precision100: all factors in (10) passed.

The point m128 test has min residual LDL pivot .0355585548633133 and final
constant-column pivot .744470636576883 in the positive scaling preceding(5).
No pivot is used as a uniform theorem. At precision150 the smallest physical

The interval run encloses each exact algebraic entry using rounded-down and

 min_i b_i > .13631289401543,
 min_i r_i > .01266933924856,
 Delta > .70074138549148,

and its absolute diagonal cost. All defining matrices, factor coefficients,
and precision data are retained in the public raw JSON outputs. This is

for the required uniform textual coefficient bounds.

Sources are retained by SHA256 in the shared research directory:
max2_chronological_kernel_b0fdefe309f1.py and
max2_chronological_kernel_interval_9114d6105f73.py. For reproduction copy

## 6. Precise remaining work

# A finite-moment obstruction for dependent character measures, including singular limits

Status: **self-contained unverified round-17 joint candidate**. This final
allowed round extends the measure screen and includes the full proof below.
The only correctness predecessors are accepted facts `1252b8823bb5a290`
(necessary ordered interpolation) and `b98bb807d514e80d` (the exact benchmark
and its bound). The previous draft03abbfd5bd957e79 is motivation, not a
mathematical premise. No optimizer, parameter sweep, installation, or fact
submission is used.

The criterion is applied to TWO entirely specified probability laws in
Section 8, including a dependent low-prefix distribution and a common-sign
coarse tail with vanishing full support. It is a necessary-condition
obstruction, not a claimed parameterization or solution of arbitrary Grams.
All positive amplitude laws and all actual common anchors are covered.

## 1. Statement, actual steps, and the exact finite-moment hypotheses

Fix an integer m>=1024. Define

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c_chr=sigma(1+1/m), a_chr=delta/c_chr,
    N=2^m, n=N-1.

Choose ANY epsilon in [0,1/1000000] and put p_chr=1-epsilon. The physical
step word is

    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_chr c_chr^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Every subword retains these ORIGINAL enclosing-m parameters. Equivalently,
h_i=1+a_chr c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0<=i<n, where nu_2(k) is the exponent of 2
dividing a positive integer k. Put

    t=a_chr, l=1+t, u_k=delta c_chr^(k-1) for k>=1,
    D_chr=1+l p_chr, beta_chr=7/10.

Every leaf has physical step l, and a level-k nonleaf bridge has physical
step 1+u_k. No step is deleted, permuted, or padded. Give original sample i
its standard m-bit binary label (i_0,...,i_(m-1)). For a character index
s=(s_0,...,s_(m-1)) in {0,1}^m define

    chi_s(i)=(-1)^(sum_l s_l i_l),
    B(s)=(-1)^s_0,
    C_j(s)=(-1)^(s_1+...+s_j), 1<=j<m.

Take any finite probability weights w_s>=0 summing to one that satisfy
EXACTLY these first and joint moment conditions:

    E B =1-epsilon,
    E C_k=-7/10+4epsilon/5 for every 1<=k<m,
    E[B C_k]=-7/10-epsilon/10 for every 1<=k<m,
    E[C_1 C_2]<=1/2, E[B C_1 C_2]<=1/2.                    (1)

Here E is the finite sum against the specified weights. The map
s -> (B,C_1,...,C_(m-1)) is bijective: (-1)^s_1=C_1 and
(-1)^s_j=C_(j-1)C_j for j>=2. Thus specifying a probability on these signs
specifies every character weight. Section 8 gives concrete formulas satisfying
(1). No conditional independence is assumed in the theorem, and zero weights
are allowed.

For arbitrary positive numbers Gamma_0,...,Gamma_n prescribe real vectors

    g_i=(Gamma_i sqrt(w_s) chi_s(i))_s.                    (2)

The conclusion also holds for any Euclidean realization of the same Gram.
Assume these really are gradients of ONE convex differentiable 1-smooth
function F with a nonempty minimizer set along the actual GD trajectory:

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad F(X_i).

Write R_dist=dist(X_0,argmin F)>0 and F_star=min F. Then

    Gamma_i <=(6/5)Gamma_0 for every original sample i,          (3)
    V_chr:=2(F(X_n)-F_star)/R_dist^2
              <7(199/200)^((n+1)/8).                          (4)

Consequently the ORIGINAL benchmark B_n in accepted fact
`b98bb807d514e80d`, with p_bench=log_2(3), satisfies

    B_n V_chr <7(1+4n^p_bench)(199/200)^((n+1)/8) ->0.           (5)

All constants are uniform for epsilon in the displayed CLOSED interval,
all measures satisfying (1), all positive amplitudes, and all actual common
anchors and realizing functions. In particular epsilon may depend on the
original horizon in any way and may equal zero. The proof makes no passage
to a limiting Gram and assumes no condition-number bound.

This only bounds this measure class on the unchanged dyadic diagnostic
words. It is not an upper bound on unrestricted W_n(H_m) and does not settle
the original all-h minimax question. The conclusion for F=f/L,
g_i=grad f(X_i)/L gives the original normalized objective
2(f(X_n)-f_star)/(L R_dist^2) for every L>0.

## 2. Kernel identities and analytic rational bounds

For a binary difference d=i xor j put d_m=0. The character identity is

    chi_s(d)=B(s)^d_0 product_(r=1)^(m-1) C_r(s)^(d_r xor d_(r+1)),
    <g_i,g_j>/(Gamma_i Gamma_j)=E[chi_s(i xor j)].            (6)

This follows by inserting (-1)^s_j=C_(j-1)C_j with C_0=1. In particular
||g_i||=Gamma_i. At an odd-sample transition comprising a level-k bridge and
its following leaf, the three signs relative to the first sign are
1,B C_k,C_k. The moments in (1) therefore give their correlations

    w_chr=E[B C_k]=-7/10-epsilon/10,
    p_chr=E[B]=1-epsilon,
    z_chr=E[C_k]=-7/10+4epsilon/5.                           (7)

At two consecutive odd transitions of levels 1 and 2, the three odd signs
are 1,C_1,C_1 C_2 and the two even signs are B C_1,B C_1 C_2. Define

    z2_chr=E[C_1 C_2]<=1/2,
    w2_chr=E[B C_1 C_2]<=1/2.                               (8)

These identities apply at every translated occurrence of that ruler pattern.
Multiplying each coordinate by its sign at the first sample does not change
any inner product; the changed prefix variables are still C_1,C_2. Thus no
independence or distributional symmetry of higher prefixes enters (7),(8).

We shall use

    0<=epsilon<=1/1000000, 999/1000<delta<1,
    413/1000<t<83/200,
    1413/1000<l<283/200,
    12/5<c_chr<2417/1000,
    603/250<D_chr<483/200,

D_chr>1+(1413/1000)(999999/1000000)>603/250. Finally

These are finite analytic estimates, including epsilon=0.

## 3. Original pair constraints, with the intervening gradient retained

gives EVERY ordered inequality

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.             (10)

We use necessary sums of these original inequalities, not a sufficient
surrogate. Every function in the statement must also obey all unused pairs
and both optimum directions.

At consecutive samples with step 1+u, normalized correlation d, and norm

    r^2+(u-1)d r-u<=0.                                      (11)

For u>0 and -1<=d<=1 this implies r<=max(1,u): the polynomial has one

Now take one bridge of excess u=u_k and its following leaf. Let A be the

We need the following explicit consequences of (9),(14):

    level 1: q<=r_low:=59/125,
    level 2: q<=501/500,

## 4. The original directed cycle needs only the two moment upper bounds

transition and then a level-2 transition. At the first occurrence they are
samples1,3,5, and the intervening even samples E_1,E_2 are samples2,4.
These names are temporary indices, not new iterates. Set

    ||g_(O_0)||=A,
    ||g_(O_1)||=r A, ||g_(O_2)||=q A,
    ||g_(E_1)||=a A, ||g_(E_2)||=b A.                        (17)

The original comparisons in Section3 give

    a>=r, q<=(501/500)r, r<=59/125,
    b<=(15/7)r,
    q<=(501/500)(59/125)<473/1000.                          (18)

Let u=u_1=delta, v=u_2 and form the ORIGINAL directed cycle

    T_cyc=Q_(O_0,O_2)+Q_(O_1,O_0)+Q_(O_2,O_1).              (19)

All function values and the common anchor cancel. The displacements are
exactly

    X_(O_1)-X_(O_0)=-(1+u)g_(O_0)-l g_(E_1),
    X_(O_2)-X_(O_1)=-(1+v)g_(O_1)-l g_(E_2).

Substitution into (19), retaining both original even gradients and using
(7),(8), yields

    T_cyc/A^2 = -u+r^2+q^2+(u-v-1)z_chr r
                +v z_chr r q-z2_chr q
                +l a(p_chr r-w_chr)+l b(p_chr q-w2_chr).   (20)

By (18), p_chr q-1/2<0; therefore b<=(15/7)r gives

    T_cyc/A^2 >= -u+D_chr r^2+q^2+C_chr r+E_chr r q-q/2,
    C_chr=(u-v-1)z_chr-l w_chr-(15/14)l,
    E_chr=v z_chr+(15/7)l p_chr.                           (21)

The constants obey

    C_chr>29/25, E_chr>4/3.                               (22)

For C_chr, since u<=1, (7),(9) give

    C_chr >= v(7/10-4epsilon/5)-(13/35)l
       >(2413/1000)(7/10-4/5000000)
                           -(13/35)(283/200)>29/25.

The discarded epsilon contribution in -w_chr-(15/14) is epsilon/10>=0.
For E_chr, the lower estimate is

    E_chr >= -(7/10)v+(15/7)l(1-epsilon)
       >-(7/10)(483/200)
          +(15/7)(1413/1000)(999999/1000000)>4/3.

Suppose q>=2/5. Then (18) gives r>=(500/501)q>(499/500)q. Equations
(21),(22), u<=1 and D_chr>12/5 imply

    T_cyc/A^2 >= P_chr(q),
    P_chr(q)=[(12/5)(499/500)^2+1+(4/3)(499/500)]q^2
                 +[(29/25)(499/500)-1/2]q-1.              (23)

Both coefficients are positive. Hence P_chr increases on q>=0, and

    P_chr(2/5)=216143/11718750>1/100.                      (24)

It follows that T_cyc>A^2/100. One of the THREE ORIGINAL ordered residuals
in (19) exceeds A^2/300. This is illegal for any function obeying (10),
regardless of the anchor and all chosen values. Thus every actual legal
trajectory must obey

    Gamma_(O_2)/Gamma_(O_0)<2/5.                           (25)

This is an all-amplitude constraint. Both intervening leaf losses were
allowed to vary freely and both intervening even gradients were retained.
It uses only the finite moment upper bounds (8), not conditional independence,
strict Gram definiteness, a saturated adjacent inequality, or a limiting
continuity argument.

## 5. Pay the total loss over the entire original word

It is convenient to index the odd samples by r, writing
O_r=Gamma_(2r+1), 0<=r<N/2. Between O_r and O_(r+1) there are exactly
the original bridge of level 1+nu_2(r+1) and its following leaf. This is
indexing only: all the underlying gradients remain in (12),(20).

Let J_0 be the empty list and J_j=(J_(j-1),j,J_(j-1)). The list of these
odd-transition levels is J_(m-1). A block J_2=(1,2,1) first obeys (25)
and then the level-1 cap in (15), so its total amplitude ratio is less than

    Q_chr=(2/5)(59/125)=118/625.                            (26)

For any occurrence of J_(j-1), j>=3, multiply this bound over its
2^(j-3) disjoint J_2 blocks, and the last bound in (15) over the remaining
levels k>=3. The exact counts are

    sum_(k=3)^(j-1)2^(j-k-1)=2^(j-3)-1,
    sum_(k=3)^(j-1)(k-1)2^(j-k-1)=3*2^(j-3)-j.              (27)

These follow by induction in j, starting at j=3 where both sums are empty.
Since u_k=delta c_chr^(k-1), the resulting bound is

    O_after/O_before <= L_j,
    L_j=[D_chr/(eta_chr delta)] c_chr^(-j)
                            Theta_chr^(2^j/8),
    Theta_chr=Q_chr eta_chr delta c_chr^3/D_chr.             (28)

No overlapping transition is charged twice. In particular the first leaf
of the ORIGINAL H_j is outside this odd-transition block and only contributes
an extra factor at most one.

The bounds (9) imply

    0<Theta_chr
      < (118/625)(9/10)(2417/1000)^3/(603/250)
      <199/200.                                           (29)

This is an explicit rational inequality; delta<1 was dropped upwards.
Formula (28) quantifies the TOTAL loss, including every repeated low block
and every high bridge of the unchanged original horizon. In particular

    Gamma_n/Gamma_0
      <=[D_chr/(eta_chr delta)]c_chr^(-m)
                                  Theta_chr^(N/8).         (30)

## 6. Prefix control includes the even samples

First every odd sample has norm at most Gamma_0. To prove this, induct on
the recursive list J_j. For J_1 the cap is r_low<1. For J_2, the norm after
its middle level-2 transition is at most r_low(501/500) times its start,
which is less than one, and the two level-1 edges contract. For j>=3,
the left J_(j-1) has norm ratio at most L_j by (28). Its following level-j
transition has norm ratio less than eta_chr delta c_chr^(j-1)/D_chr.
Their product is

    c_chr^(-1) Theta_chr^(2^j/8)<1.                        (31)

The induction hypothesis controls every prefix in the left block; (31)
controls the starting norm of the right block, where the same induction
hypothesis applies. Initially O_0<=Gamma_0 by the first leaf comparison.
This proves the claim for ALL original odd samples with inherited state.

Every remaining even sample except X_0 lies immediately after one bridge.
For a level-1 bridge, (11) gives even norm at most the preceding odd norm,
since u_1<1. For a level-2 bridge the preceding J_1 supplies a factor r_low;

    u_2 r_low<(483/200)(59/125)<6/5.

For a level-j bridge with j>=3, the preceding J_(j-1) and (11),(28) give

    even norm/Gamma_0 <=u_j L_j
       =[D_chr/(eta_chr c_chr)]Theta_chr^(2^j/8)
       <(483/200)/[(9/10)(12/5)]<6/5.                     (32)

At every occurrence the starting odd norm is already at most Gamma_0.
Together these estimates prove (3), including every original intermediate
gradient that was not an endpoint in the cycle calculation.

## 7. True closest-minimizer normalization

The minimizer set is nonempty and closed. Its distance from X_0 is attained:
a minimizing sequence may be restricted to a bounded closed ball in the
finite-dimensional Euclidean space and hence has a convergent subsequence.
Take a closest minimizer X_star, without assuming it is the origin. Since
grad F(X_star)=0, smoothness implies

    Gamma_0<=R_dist.                                      (33)

The exact original mass is

    M_chr=1+sum_(i<n)h_i
         =N+a_chr(c_chr^m-N)/(c_chr-2)<c_chr^m.             (34)

The equality follows by counting the 2^(m-k-1) level-k steps, including
leaves, and summing the geometric progression. The inequality follows from
c_chr>sigma>2 and c_chr(c_chr-2)>sigma(sigma-2)=1>delta,
so 0<a_chr<c_chr-2. Thus the displayed expression is a strict convex
combination of N and c_chr^m, the latter being larger.

Using (3),(33), the actual chronological updates give

    ||X_n-X_star|| <=R_dist+sum_(i<n)h_i Gamma_i
       <=[1+(6/5)sum_(i<n)h_i] R_dist
       <=(6/5)M_chr R_dist<(6/5)c_chr^m R_dist.             (35)

Convexity at X_n gives F(X_n)-F_star<=<g_n,X_n-X_star>.
Combine (30),(33),(35) to obtain

    V_chr < (12/5)[D_chr/(eta_chr delta)]Theta_chr^(N/8)
      <7(199/200)^(N/8),                                 (36)

because (12/5)(483/200)/[(9/10)(999/1000)]<7. This proves (4).
Every radius in this argument is the TRUE distance. If F is an anchored
projection interpolant its minimizers form the appropriate polar cone;
X_star may be nonzero. No inverse-Gram expression for the radius, forced
positive-cone anchor, or origin-distance substitute is used. The cost of
the conservative bound R_dist>=Gamma_0 and the path estimate is visible
in the finite prefactor in (36).

Accepted fact `b98bb807d514e80d` gives B_n<=1+4n^log_2(3). This proves (5).
For completeness its right side tends to zero because the logarithm of
its exponential factor is ((n+1)/8)log(199/200), whereas the logarithm of
its polynomial factor is O(log n). This keeps the original B_n and horizon.

## 8. Two explicit weight laws and an actual vanishing-support sequence

All formulas below are probabilities on the signs (B,C_1,...,C_(m-1)),
converted uniquely to weights w_s by the bijection in Section1. These are
finite real vectors (2), not an arbitrary unspecified Gram.

First, the conditional-product proposal is exactly

    w_s=[(1+(1-epsilon)B(s))/2]
          product_(j=1)^(m-1)[(1+C_j(s)(1/10-4B(s)/5))/2].  (37)

The first moment identities (1) follow by conditioning on B. Given B=1,
each C_j has mean -7/10; given B=-1, its mean is9/10. Directly,

    E C_1 C_2=49/100+4epsilon/25<=1/2,
    E B C_1 C_2=49/100-13epsilon/20<=1/2.

Thus (37) satisfies every hypothesis for ANY epsilon in [0,10^(-6)]. In
particular it covers the original specified sequence epsilon=N^(-1), any
other sequence epsilon_m eventually in this interval, and the exact boundary
epsilon=0. For positive epsilon all weights are positive. The proof is
uniform over all of these choices without using continuity.

Second, here is a genuinely nonproduct low-prefix distribution and a highly
dependent coarse-tail mixture. Choose eta in [0,1]. For b in {-1,1} set

    mu_1=-7/10, mu_(-1)=9/10,
    tau_1=1/2-epsilon, tau_(-1)=9/10,
    pi_b(c_1,c_2)=[1+mu_b(c_1+c_2)+tau_b c_1 c_2]/4.       (38)

These four probabilities are explicit. For b=1 they are
(1/10-epsilon)/4 for(++), (1/2+epsilon)/4 for each mixed pair, and
(29/10-epsilon)/4 for(--). For b=-1 they are37/40 for(++) and1/40 for
each of the other three pairs. All are positive in the stated epsilon range,
and their sum is one. Their two means are mu_b and their product mean is
tau_b, as follows by summing these four values.

Let c_tail=(c_3,...,c_(m-1)); m>=1024 ensures this tail is nonempty. Define

    T_b(c_tail)=(1-eta)[(1+mu_b)/2 * 1_(all tail signs=1)
                        +(1-mu_b)/2 * 1_(all tail signs=-1)]
                    +eta product_(j=3)^(m-1)(1+mu_b c_j)/2. (39)

Here 1_(condition) is1 if the condition holds and0 otherwise. The first
part assigns one common sign to EVERY tail prefix. The second part is a
finite product distribution with full support. Both parts give each tail
sign mean mu_b; their probabilities sum to one. The complete weight is

    w_s=[(1+(1-epsilon)B(s))/2]
             pi_(B(s))(C_1(s),C_2(s))
             T_(B(s))(C_3(s),...,C_(m-1)(s)).              (40)

This specifies every atom. Each prefix has the conditional mean mu_b, so
the first moments in (1) are identical to those for (37). The low joint
moments are now

    E C_1 C_2=1/2-(4/5)epsilon+epsilon^2/2<=1/2,
    E B C_1 C_2=1/2-(17/10)epsilon+epsilon^2/2<=1/2.        (41)

Thus (40) satisfies the theorem for EVERY eta in [0,1], regardless of
how strongly its tail prefixes depend on one another. It is not the
conditional-product policy (37): already pi_b has a different product mean,
and for eta<1 the tail variables share a common component.

One definite original-horizon policy is

    epsilon=N^(-1), eta=N^(-2), standard chronological labels. (42)

For every finite N=2^m all weights in (40),(42) are strictly positive:
P(B=b)>0, all four pi_b are positive, and the eta product component is
positive at every tail pattern. Its full-support tail component tends to
zero at the specified rate, and its low-bit discrepancy also tends to
zero. Nevertheless EVERY positive-amplitude realization on actual H_m that
is legal for one global function has the bound (4),(5). No tuning of a
nonsaturating amplitude or choice of common anchor is left out of that bound.

The exact singular boundary epsilon=eta=0 also satisfies (1): at each
finite m it is supported on eight sign patterns (B=1, four low pairs,
two constant tails). The same inequalities (12),(20),(28),(35) apply
there directly and give the same bound. This makes no continuity assertion
between ambient spaces or between inverse Gram matrices.

## 9. What is closed and what is still open

The proof excludes the two explicit policies (37),(42), all rates at which
their displayed epsilon and eta approach zero, and more generally every
finite sign measure satisfying the moment hypotheses (1). It allows zero
weights, unbounded conditioning, all positive amplitudes with arbitrary
slack, every common anchor, and nonzero closest minimizers. The quantitative
loss pays for every repeated low block and all high bridges at the actual
original horizon. C62 and any proposed Gram-inverse distance formula are not
used. The accepted fixed C59 witness is not constrained by (1) and is not
contradicted.

This is NOT an obstruction to all dependent character constructions. For
example, keep the same law of B, choose ONE sign V conditionally of mean
mu_B, and put C_j=V for every j. Its four atom probabilities are
P(B=b)(1+mu_b v)/2 for b,v in {-1,1}. It has all the required FIRST moments
but E C_1 C_2=1 and E B C_1 C_2=1-epsilon, so it violates the two joint
moment upper bounds. Mixing this law with (37) with coefficient eta=N^(-2)
retains full support at positive epsilon and keeps the first joint moment
strictly above1/2. No legal trajectory, amplitude rule, useful payoff, or
common anchor for that different policy is asserted here. It is a precise
unresolved escape from this theorem's hypotheses, not a counterexample to
its conclusion.

Within the fixed first-moment chart and positive-amplitude convention,
a competitive construction must therefore violate at least one of
E C_1 C_2<=1/2 and E B C_1 C_2<=1/2, or change its labels or the stated
first moments. Arbitrary further dependence of the higher prefixes alone
cannot escape this result while (1) is retained. Changing the two lowest
prefix joint moments still needs a new full interpolation and true-distance
argument; Gram positivity alone says nothing about that missing feasibility.
