# C69: a joint chronological budget for quartic and horizon-dependent power epigraphs

Status: COMPLETE UNVERIFIED joint candidate, fifth launch round 1 (cumulative 12).
Sections 1--9 contain the full quartic proof; Section 10 derives the general
power extension. No component is imported as an unverified predecessor.
No fact_submit, trajectory evaluation, numerical optimization, installation,
or new allocation was used. The only accepted mathematical predecessor is
b98bb807d514e80d, used for the exact benchmark recursions. All function,
trajectory, block, and combinatorial assertions used below are proved here.
C65, C66, and C67 are context, not proof premises.

## 1. Definitions and result

In Sections 1--9 the power is FIXED at 4. For each integer m>=512 set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/m,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
    d_j=a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

The H_j here are local schedule words, not the conjugate quadratics called
H_j in a different accepted fact. Every embedded word uses this SAME a,c.
Index physical steps by t=1,...,n. Let nu_2(t) be the exponent of 2 in t and
b(t) the number of 1 bits in the binary expansion of t, with b(0)=0. Then

    h_t=1+d_(nu_2(t)).                                     (1)

Define the single global function and its state coordinates by

    K_4={(r,s) in R^2:s>=r^4/4},
    F_4(X)=max_(g in K_4) (<X,g>-||g||^2/2),
    eta=v+r^4/4, u=eta r^2=vr^2+r^6/4,
    X(r,v)=(r(1+u),-v), G(r)=(r,r^4/4), v>=0.

Here r,v,u,eta and X,G denote local state variables. Write x for the
horizontal coordinate of X and R=|x|. Start from arbitrary r_0!=0 and
v_0>=0, and run the given H_m on this same F_4:

    X_t=X_(t-1)-h_t grad F_4(X_(t-1)), 1<=t<=n.

Section 2 proves global legality, the unique actual recurrence, and

    min F_4=0, argmin F_4={(0,y):y<=0},
    R_0=dist(X_0,argmin F_4)=|r_0|(1+u_0),
    2F_4(X(r,v))=r^2+(3/2)v r^4+(7/16)r^8.               (2)

A turn is a step t with x_(t-1)x_t<0. The following bounds hold jointly
for EVERY such initial state, without restricting the number or levels of
turns:

    R_t<=R_0 for every t,
    R_t<=c^(-b(t))R_0 at every turn t,                    (3)
    P_4:=2F_4(X_n)/R_0^2 <=3/(8S_m).                     (4)

The retained clock cost, including the nonnegative contributions at every
step, is

    J_all=(1/2)sum_(t=1)^n |r_(t-1)|^2(v_t-v_(t-1))
         =(1/8)sum_(t=1)^n h_t |r_(t-1)|^6.

It satisfies the explicit global charge

    J_all <= min{
       |r_0|^2(v_n-v_0)/2,
       R_0 |r_0|^5 [2(1+1/c)^m-1]/8
    },                                                   (5)

and, using only the original closest-minimizer distance,

    J_all <=4^(5/7) R_0^(12/7)[2(1+1/c)^m-1]/8.           (6)

No assertion that J_all vanishes, or that a logarithmic clock decreases
across zero, is made. The quantitative objective bound (4) uses the
chronological block budget directly; it does not delete J_all.

For the EXACT Zhang--Jiang denominator B_n defined in accepted fact
b98bb807d514e80d, Section 8 proves

    B_(2^m-1) P_4 <625/1536<1/2       for all m>=512,      (7)
    limsup_(m->infinity) sup_(r_0!=0,v_0>=0)
        B_(2^m-1) P_4 <=3lambda/(8e)<3/8.                (8)

This excludes the whole stated quartic epigraph family as a matching
adversary on these schedules. It is NOT an upper bound for unrestricted
W_n and does not settle the original all-schedule profile problem.

## 2. The global function, ordered pairs, distance, and physical recursion

K_4 is nonempty, closed, and convex. Completing the square in the defining
maximum shows that its unique maximizing g is the Euclidean projection
Pi_(K_4)(X). The normal inequalities at projections of X and Y give

    ||Pi_(K_4)(X)-Pi_(K_4)(Y)||^2
       <=<Pi_(K_4)(X)-Pi_(K_4)(Y),X-Y>.

Thus the projection is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the defining maxima gives

    0<=F_4(Y)-F_4(X)-<Pi_(K_4)(X),Y-X>
      <=<Pi_(K_4)(Y)-Pi_(K_4)(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

It follows that F_4 is differentiable with gradient Pi_(K_4), hence has
1-Lipschitz gradient. Convexity follows from its supremum of affine
functions representation.

For phi(r)=r^4/4, one has

    X(r,v)-G(r)=eta*(phi'(r),-1).

For any (z,s) in K_4 its inner product with (z,s)-G(r) is at most

    eta*[phi'(r)(z-r)-phi(z)+phi(r)]<=0.

The last inequality is the tangent inequality for the convex function
phi. This proves grad F_4(X(r,v))=G(r). Substitution into the maximum
proves the value in (2). In particular, if f_i=F_4(X_i), every ordered
pair of states in this construction has the exact residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =eta_j*[r_j^3(r_i-r_j)-r_i^4/4+r_j^4/4]<=0.      (9)

There is no restriction on temporal separation in (9).

If x=0 and y<=0, the maximum is zero: zero is feasible, and every feasible
g=(r,s) has s>=0, so ys-||g||^2/2<=0. If x!=0, test g=(r,r^4/4)
with sufficiently small r of the sign of x; the positive term xr
dominates the terms of order 2 or higher. If x=0 and y>0, a sufficiently
small g=(0,s), s>0, gives positive value. This proves the exact minimizer
set in (2). Its closest point to (x,-v), v>=0, is (0,-v), proving the
true distance formula without retaining a spurious initial vertical norm.

The actual GD step of size h>=0 is exactly

    v_plus=v+h r^4/4,
    x_plus=x-hr,
    x_plus=T_(v_plus)(r_plus),
    T_v(r)=r+v r^3+r^7/4.                               (10)

T_v is odd and strictly increasing onto R, since

    T_v'(r)=1+3vr^2+7r^6/4>=1.

It therefore determines the unique actual r_plus. In particular
sign(r)=sign(x). If r reaches zero, x=0 and G(r)=0, so the trajectory is
absorbed with zero subsequent objective and clock cost.

On any interval where all states are nonzero and have the same sign,
R decreases and v increases. Equation (10) then shows that |r| decreases.
Reflection allows every such interval to be treated on the positive ray.

For later use, smoothness and the minimizer (0,-v) give 2F_4(X)<=R^2.
This can also be checked from the explicit state formula: with z=r^6/4,

    2F_4(X)/r^2=1+(3/2)u+z/4,
    R^2/r^2=(1+u)^2,

and their difference is u/2+u^2-z/4>=u/4+u^2>=0 because 0<=z<=u.

## 3. A no-turn block pays for the loss of normal state

Consider any actual occurrence of H_l, l>=1, along which every state is
nonzero and has the same sign. No entry v is reset. Let r>0 and u>0 be
the terminal gradient magnitude and effective normal state, and let
rho>0 and u_mid be their counterparts immediately BEFORE the middle
step 1+d_(l-1). Since that step does not turn or annihilate,

    u_mid>d_(l-1).                                      (11)

Monotonicity on this interval gives rho>=r and v_mid<=v_end. Consequently

    u_mid=v_mid rho^2+rho^6/4
          <=(rho/r)^6 (v_end r^2+r^6/4)
          =(rho/r)^6 u.                                (12)

Let Apre_l=S_(l-1)+1+d_(l-1)=M_(l-1)+d_(l-1) be the sum of steps
through the middle step. Every gradient used by those steps has
magnitude at least rho; every later gradient has magnitude at least r.
Telescoping the actual horizontal motion, with R_entry its input radius,
therefore gives

    R_entry/r
      >=M_l+u+Apre_l*((d_(l-1)/u)^(1/6)-1)_+.            (13)

Here (z)_+=max(z,0). If u>=d_(l-1)/2, the explicit u in (13) is at
least d_(l-1)/2. If u<d_(l-1)/2, then

    (d_(l-1)/u)^(1/6)>2^(1/6)>11/10,

because (11/10)^6=1771561/1000000<2. Since Apre_l>=d_(l-1), the
last term in (13) exceeds d_(l-1)/10. Thus in both cases

    R_entry >=Aend_l |r_end|,
    Aend_l:=M_l+d_(l-1)/10.                             (14)

For the empty word define Aend_0=1; the same gradient bound is the state
identity R=|r|(1+u)>=|r|. If an endpoint is absorbed, the gradient bound
with its zero terminal gradient holds as well.

This is the key replacement for a frozen-normal argument. A decrease in
terminal u is permitted. Equation (12) charges that decrease to earlier
gradient magnitudes, and equation (13) charges those magnitudes to the
TRUE horizontal entry distance. No inequality u_end>=u_mid is used.

## 4. Uniform capacity of every no-turn H_l in the enclosing word

The word recursion implies M_(l+1)=2M_l+d_l and M_0=1. Set

    A_mass=a/(c-2).

Solving this elementary recurrence gives

    M_l=A_mass c^l+(1-A_mass)2^l.                        (15)

Since lambda(lambda-2)=1 and c>lambda, one has c(c-2)>1>1-epsilon.
It follows that 0<A_mass<1. In particular,

    M_l/d_l>=1/(c-2).                                  (16)

For m>=512, sqrt(2)<99/70 gives

    c<(169/70)(513/512)<121/50.

The function z-1/(z-2)-1/(10z) is strictly increasing for z>2. At
z=121/50 its value is -289/127050<0. Therefore

    1/(c-2)+1/(10c)>c.

Combining this with (14) and (16) proves

    Aend_l>=c d_l=a c^(l+1)        for l>=1.             (17)

For l=0 the same conclusion holds because

    Aend_0=1>ac=1-1/m.                                  (18)

Equations (17)--(18) are uniform over the block position, initial state,
and l. They use the enclosing a,c throughout.

## 5. A binary interval lemma and chronological turn accounting

We first prove the combinatorial statement required to combine real
one-sign intervals. If integers 0<=s<t satisfy

    q=b(t-1)-b(s)>=1,

then [s,t] contains an aligned closed dyadic interval [A,A+2^q], where
A is a multiple of 2^q.

Proof. Put B=2^q, write s=kB+r with 0<=r<B, and suppose no such
interval is contained. If r=0, the first possible interval starts at s,
so t<s+B. Then t-1 has high binary part k and a low part at most B-2;
hence b(t-1)-b(s)<=q-1, a contradiction.

If r>0, the first possible start is (k+1)B, so t<(k+2)B. If t-1
has high part k, its low part has at most q ones, whereas b(r)>=1,
again giving difference at most q-1. If t-1 has high part k+1, its
low part is at most B-2 and has at most q-1 ones. Adding 1 to k
increases its bit count by at most 1. Thus the difference is at most
1+(q-1)-b(r)<=q-1. This contradiction proves the lemma.             (19)

An aligned interval [A,A+2^q] corresponds to the actual subword H_q
at physical step indices A+1,...,A+2^q-1: for 0<j<2^q,
nu_2(A+j)=nu_2(j). This uses the same physical a,c.

Now let s<t be consecutive actual turn times, allowing s=0 for the
initial boundary before the first turn. The steps s+1,...,t-1 form
one same-sign interval. Set

    q=max{0,b(t-1)-b(s)}, ell=nu_2(t).

If q>=1, (19) finds an actual no-turn H_q inside this interval. Its
entry horizontal radius is at most R_s, and its terminal gradient
magnitude is at least |r_(t-1)|, by monotonicity on the entire interval.
Equations (14) and (17) therefore give

    R_s>=Aend_q |r_(t-1)|>=a c^(q+1)|r_(t-1)|.           (20)

For q=0, use R_s>=|r_(t-1)| and (18) to get the same result. At the
actual turn t, equation (10) gives

    R_t=(d_ell-u_(t-1))|r_(t-1)|
        <=a c^ell |r_(t-1)|
        <=c^(ell-q-1)R_s.                              (21)

The elementary binary identity

    b(t-1)=b(t)-1+nu_2(t)

and q>=b(t-1)-b(s) imply

    R_t<=c^(b(s)-b(t))R_s.                              (22)

Starting at s=0 and telescoping (22) over the ACTUAL turns proves the
second part of (3). Between turns the radius decreases, proving the
first part of (3). This argument allows arbitrary repeated rises and
falls in turn level. It neither optimizes right copies independently
nor assumes that u is monotone.

## 6. Global payment of the retained moving-normal cost

For context, on a positive one-sign interval define the local clock

    C_4(r,v)=log r+(3/2)vr^2+(7/24)r^6,
    Psi(x,v)=C_4(T_v^(-1)(x),v), x>0.

Differentiating T_v(r)=x gives

    partial_x Psi=1/r, partial_v Psi=r^2/2.

For one positive noncrossing step, first move horizontally at the old v
and then increase v at the new horizontal coordinate. Monotonicity of
T_v^(-1) bounds the two resulting integrals and yields

    C_4(r_plus,v_plus)-C_4(r,v)
       <=-h+(r^2/2)(v_plus-v).                          (23)

Reflection covers a negative one-sign interval. This derivation retains
the positive cost, and does not extend the logarithm across annihilation
or sign changes.

The global radius result (3), together with v_t>=v_0 and monotonicity of
T_v on the positive ray, implies

    |r_t|<=|r_0|  for every t.                           (24)

The first bound in (5) now follows by summing the defining weighted
vertical increments of J_all.

To obtain the second bound, set TV_x=sum_(t=1)^n h_t|r_(t-1)|, the
total absolute horizontal displacement. At a nonturn step (including
one that reaches zero), its contribution is R_(t-1)-R_t. At a turn it
is R_(t-1)+R_t. Consequently the exact telescoping identity is

    TV_x=R_0-R_n+2 sum_(t a turn) R_t.                   (25)

Use (3), and expand the product over the m independent binary digits:

    sum_(t=0)^(2^m-1)c^(-b(t))=(1+1/c)^m.

It follows that

    TV_x<=R_0[2(1+1/c)^m-1].                            (26)

Since J_all=(1/8)sum h_t|r_(t-1)|*|r_(t-1)|^5, (24)--(26) prove
the second bound in (5). Finally R_0>=|r_0|^7/4 by the state formula,
so R_0|r_0|^5<=4^(5/7)R_0^(12/7), proving (6).

Thus the sum of all one-sign J costs is bounded by (5)--(6), since it
is no larger than J_all. The bounds retain the initial radius and,
in the first version, the actual terminal vertical state. They remain
valid for trajectories that annihilate; their subsequent contributions
are zero. No lower bound on nonzero |r_t| is needed.

## 7. Terminal payoff, with every entry-radius factor retained

Consider any nonzero same-sign interval with total step mass T>=1/6.
Write r>0 for its terminal gradient magnitude and u=vr^2+r^6/4 for
its terminal normal state. The actual recursion, without resetting v,
gives

    R_entry>=r(T+1+u),
    v_end>=T r^4/4.

Put z=r^6/4. Then z<=u/(T+1), and (2) implies

    2F_4(X_end)/R_entry^2
       <=[1+k_T u]/(T+1+u)^2,
    k_T=3/2+1/[4(T+1)].

The derivative of the last rational function has the sign of
k_T(T+1)-2-k_T u. Since T>=1/6, its maximum on u>=0 is attained at
u=T+1-2/k_T and equals

    E_4(T)=(6T+7)^2/[48(T+1)^2(2T+1)]<=3/(8T).          (27)

For the last comparison the numerator of the difference, over denominator
48T(T+1)^2(2T+1), is 6T^2+23T+18>0. An absorbing terminal state has
zero payoff and satisfies the desired bound separately.

If the full run is nonabsorbed, let s be its last actual turn, or let
s=0 if it has no turns. Set b=b(s) and q=m-b. Apply (19) with
t=2^m. The final same-sign interval contains an actual H_q. If q>=1,
its full mass T is at least S_q>=S_1>1, so (3) and (27) give

    P_4<=c^(-2b)*3/(8S_q).                              (28)

The factor c^(-2b) in (28) is the ACTUAL entry-radius ratio bounded in
terms of the original R_0. A later block has not been renormalized as a
fresh problem.

For j>=1, (15) gives

    S_(j+1)-c S_j=c-1-(c-2)(1-A_mass)2^j<=c-1.

Since S_j>1 and c>1, this implies

    S_(j+1)<(2c-1)S_j<c^2 S_j.

Iterating yields S_m<=c^(2b)S_q, so (28) is at most 3/(8S_m).

If q=0, then b(s)=m and s=n, so the last step turns. Use the terminal
state bound 2F_4<=R_n^2 and (3) to obtain P_4<=c^(-2m). Since (15)
gives S_m<c^m and c^m>8/3 for m>=512, this is smaller than 3/(8S_m).
This proves (4) for every initial state, including all turn patterns.

## 8. The exact benchmark and the uniform comparison

Accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d defines the exact primitive and dominant
benchmark recursions. In their mass coordinates C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and
B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 they are

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(C_k,B_l),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

We prove directly from these recursions that

    B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).                             (29)

Set alpha=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda) and
Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha. Both coefficients in Llin exceed 1, so
Llin>=x+y. Direct expansion, using lambda^2=2lambda+1, gives

    alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
      =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

Thus Llin>=Omega(x,y), the positive root of z^2-(x+y)z-xy. At
z=lambda Omega(x,y), the polynomial with larger root G(x,lambda y) is

    z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
      =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, so z is to the right of that
polynomial's vertex. Hence G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y).
Induction in the exact recursions proves B_n<=lambda C_n.

Put gamma=log_2(lambda)>1, D(t)=(1+t)^gamma-1, and
ell(z)=log D(exp z). For t=exp z, differentiation gives

    ell''(z)=gamma*t*(1+t)^(gamma-2)
      *[(1+t)^gamma-1-gamma*t]/D(t)^2>0.

The last bracket has value zero at t=0 and positive derivative for t>0.
Convexity therefore implies D(t)D(1/t)>=D(1)^2=2. For x,y>0 set
Z=(x^(1/gamma)+y^(1/gamma))^gamma. Taking t=(y/x)^(1/gamma) shows
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy. Thus Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0; also Z>=x+y, by convexity
of the positive power. Consequently Omega(x,y)<=Z. The zero cases
follow by direct substitution. Induction yields C_n<=(n+1)^gamma,
which, with B_n<=lambda C_n, proves (29).

For a finite comparison, c<121/50 and m>=512 imply

    A_mass=(1-1/m)/[c(c-2)]
      >(511/512)/(2541/2500)>49/50.

Since c>2 and m>=512, c^(-m)<1/50. Equation (15) therefore gives

    S_m/c^m>24/25.

The first three binomial terms show

    (1+1/m)^m>=2+(m-1)/(2m)>=12/5,

where the final inequality already holds for m>=5. Combining (4),
(29), lambda<5/2, and (lambda/c)^m<=5/12 gives

    B_n P_4
       <(3/8)*(5/2)*(5/12)*(25/24)
       =625/1536<1/2,

proving (7).

As m tends to infinity, A_mass tends to 1, c tends to lambda, and

    S_m/c^m=A_mass+(1-A_mass)(2/c)^m-c^(-m) ->1,
    (lambda/c)^m=(1+1/m)^(-m) ->1/e.

Every bound above is uniform over r_0!=0,v_0>=0, so (4) and (29)
give (8). Finally e>1+1+1/2=5/2>lambda, proving 3lambda/(8e)<3/8.
No limiting formula for the exact sequence B_n has been assumed.

## 9. Scope, literature, and symbolic audit

The proof addresses the whole unscaled quartic epigraph model stated in
Section 1, at all initial horizontal radii and nonnegative vertical
states, including horizon-dependent choices. Its global charge and
payoff combine arbitrary actual turn histories. Lower-level reactivation
is allowed. This is a proper-family exclusion, not a conclusion about
all functions, other powers, or the original all-h target.

The projection background is consistent with Propositions 3.2--3.3 of
Chierchia, Pustelnik, Pesquet, and Pesquet-Popescu, "Epigraphical splitting
for solving constrained convex formulations of inverse problems with
proximal tools", arXiv:1210.5844v3. Their Hilbert product is Euclidean;
their scalar generator has full domain and is proper closed convex;
beta=4, tau=1/4, zeta=-v yield T_v(r)=x. The exact locally downloaded
paper's definitions and projection proof were read. No external result
from it is used as a proof premise. The dedicated theorem searches for
the moving-state budget and the binary interval lemma returned no usable
result; both have been proved directly here.

Symbolic boundary checks:

* Consecutive actual turns have an empty intervening H_0. The necessary
  charge is exactly Aend_0>=ac; no unqueried lower-level step is invented.
* The aligned case [s,t]=[A,A+2^q] uses the full actual H_q, with no
  missing first or last step and no change of enclosing parameters.
* Negative binary-count differences are handled by q=max(0,difference)
  in (20)--(22), not by a fictitious word of negative length.
* A turn at the final step has q=0 and uses the smoothness bound, not
  formula (27) at zero mass.
* Exact zero is absorbing. No logarithm is evaluated there, and the
  main payoff proof uses no logarithm at all.
* Very small nonzero gradients cause no reciprocal estimate with an
  uncontrolled constant; (13) charges small terminal u explicitly.
* The proof does not freeze v, assume monotonicity of u, or discard the
  positive moving-normal cost. The complete all-pair function and true
  denominator were established before the block argument.

The separate possible concave-clock integral explored in rough local
notes is unnecessary here and is not a premise. No verification success
is asserted until an authorized fact_submit actually accepts this joint
statement and proof.

## 10. Joint extension to horizon-dependent powers

This section extends the result to every real power satisfying

    2<p<=m/256, with m an integer and m>=512.             (30)

The power p may depend on m, but is FIXED during the entire trajectory.
All a,c,d_j,H_j,S_j,M_j retain their enclosing-m definitions in Section 1.
The sufficient range (30) is not claimed to be necessary. For p=4,
Sections 1--9 already give the stronger threshold m>=512.

The resulting complete joint claim is

    P_p:=2F_p(X_n)/R_0^2<=1/(2S_m),                      (31)
    B_n P_p<125/256<1/2,                                (32)
    limsup_(m->infinity) sup_(2<p<=m/256,r_0!=0,v_0>=0)
        B_n P_p<=lambda/(2e)<1/2.                       (33)

In particular every fixed real p>2 is eventually covered. The supremum
in (33) permits horizon-dependent initial states and powers throughout
the displayed range. Powers outside that range remain unaddressed by
this sufficient argument. Sections 10.1--10.5 derive all additional
function and trajectory formulas; the elementary binary interval and
benchmark proofs already included in Sections 5 and 8 are part of this
same joint proof, not unverified external premises.

### 10.1. The general power function and exact inherited state

For real p>2 define

    phi_p(r)=|r|^p/p,
    K_p={(r,s):s>=phi_p(r)},
    F_p(X)=max_(g in K_p)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2),
    eta=v+phi_p(r), u=eta |r|^(p-2),
    X_p(r,v)=(r(1+u),-v), G_p(r)=(r,phi_p(r)), v>=0.

The epigraph K_p is nonempty, closed, and convex. Completing the square
makes the maximizing gradient its unique Euclidean projection.
The two projection normal inequalities give

    ||Pi_(K_p)(X)-Pi_(K_p)(Y)||^2
       <=<Pi_(K_p)(X)-Pi_(K_p)(Y),X-Y>.

Comparing the defining maxima bounds the first-order remainder between
zero and ||X-Y||^2, as in the explicit derivation in Section 2. Hence
F_p is everywhere finite, convex, differentiable, and has 1-Lipschitz
gradient equal to the projection.

Since phi_p'(r)=r|r|^(p-2), one has

    X_p-G_p=eta*(phi_p'(r),-1).

Its inner product with any feasible displacement (z,s)-G_p is at most
eta*[phi_p'(r)(z-r)-phi_p(z)+phi_p(r)]<=0. This proves the exact
gradient formula at every state, and substitution gives

    2F_p(X_p(r,v))
      =r^2+(2-2/p)v|r|^p+(2p-1)|r|^(2p)/p^2.            (34)

For arbitrary two such states, their ordered interpolation residual is

    Q_ij=eta_j*[phi_p'(r_j)(r_i-r_j)-phi_p(r_i)
                                  +phi_p(r_j)]<=0.       (35)

This follows by expanding the residual to
<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>, so includes every ordered pair, not merely neighbors.

Zero is feasible in the maximum. At (0,y), y<=0, every feasible
inner product minus the squared norm is nonpositive. At x!=0, choose a
sufficiently small r of the sign of x; the positive linear term xr
dominates terms of order 2,p,2p. At x=0,y>0 a small positive vertical
gradient gives positive value. Therefore

    min F_p=0, argmin F_p={(0,y):y<=0},
    R_0=dist(X_p(r_0,v_0),argmin F_p)=|r_0|(1+u_0).       (36)

The actual transition is

    v_plus=v+h|r|^p/p, x_plus=x-hr,
    x_plus=T_(p,v_plus)(r_plus),
    T_(p,v)(r)=r+v r|r|^(p-2)+r|r|^(2p-2)/p.            (37)

The last map is odd, continuous, strictly increasing onto R; off zero
its derivative is
1+(p-1)v|r|^(p-2)+(2p-1)|r|^(2p-2)/p>=1, and its derivative at
zero is 1. Thus the next state is uniquely that of the same F_p.

On a same-sign nonzero interval, R and |r| decrease while v increases.
At zero the state is absorbing. Put z=|r|^(2p-2)/p. Then

    2F_p(X)/r^2=1+(2-2/p)u+z/p,
    0<=z<=u.

It follows that 2F_p(X)<=R^2, since the difference after division by
r^2 is (2/p)u+u^2-z/p>=u/p+u^2>=0.

### 10.2. General-power endpoint capacity with every p factor explicit

Set

    delta_p=2^(1/(2p-2))-1.

Since p>2, one has 0<delta_p<sqrt(2)-1<1/2. Consider a nonzero
one-sign actual H_l, l>=1. Use r,u for its terminal magnitude and normal
state, and rho,u_mid immediately before its middle step. Equation (37)
and preservation of sign imply u_mid>d_(l-1). Monotonicity gives

    u_mid
       <=(rho/r)^(2p-2) u.

Indeed the v term has exponent p-2 and v_mid<=v_end, while rho/r>=1;
the pure-power term has exponent 2p-2. Summing horizontal displacements
through the middle step and the rest of the same actual block yields

    R_entry/r>=M_l+u
       +Apre_l*((d_(l-1)/u)^(1/(2p-2))-1)_+,
    Apre_l=M_(l-1)+d_(l-1)>=d_(l-1).                    (38)

If u>=d_(l-1)/2, its contribution alone is at least
delta_p d_(l-1), because delta_p<1/2. Otherwise the last factor in
(38) is greater than delta_p. Thus

    R_entry>=Aend_(p,l)|r_end|,
    Aend_(p,l)=M_l+delta_p d_(l-1) for l>=1,
    Aend_(p,0)=1.                                      (39)

Here the subscript p distinguishes this coefficient from the quartic
rational lower bound in Section 3.

We now prove the capacity needed for all actual turn gaps:

    Aend_(p,l)>=c d_l for every l>=0.                   (40)

For l=0, use ac=1-1/m<1. For l>=1, equation (15), derived from the
word recurrence and independent of p, gives

    Aend_(p,l)/d_l>=1/(c-2)+delta_p/c.

Thus it suffices to prove

    delta_p>= [c/(c-2)]*[c(c-2)-1].                     (41)

The constants in (41) are controlled explicitly. Since
lambda>12/5 and z/(z-2) decreases for z>2,

    c/(c-2)<6.

Also

    c(c-2)-1
      =2lambda(lambda-1)/m+lambda^2/m^2
      <(15/2)/m+(25/4)/m^2<8/m,

where the last inequality uses m>=512. The right side of (41) is
therefore less than 48/m. On the other hand log(2)>1/2, by integrating
1/t>1/2 on (1,2), and exp(z)-1>z for z>0. Hence

    delta_p>1/[4(p-1)]>1/(4p)>=64/m

under (30). This proves (41) and (40). No p-dependent loss is hidden
inside an asymptotic term.

### 10.3. Combining all sign changes and paying the full cost

The binary interval lemma (19) was proved for integers alone. For
consecutive actual turns s<t, with s=0 allowed initially, set

    q=max{0,b(t-1)-b(s)}, ell=nu_2(t).

If q>=1, that lemma locates a real, aligned, nonturn H_q inside
steps s+1,...,t-1. Its input radius is at most R_s and its endpoint
gradient magnitude is at least |r_(t-1)|. Formula (40) gives

    R_s>=a c^(q+1)|r_(t-1)|.

If q=0, this follows from R_s>=|r_(t-1)| and ac<1. At turn t,
the exact recurrence (37) gives

    R_t=(d_ell-u_(t-1))|r_(t-1)|
       <=c^(ell-q-1)R_s
       <=c^(b(s)-b(t))R_s.

The last inequality uses b(t-1)=b(t)-1+ell. Induction over the ACTUAL
turns, followed by monotonicity between them, proves

    R_t<=c^(-b(t))R_0 at every turn,
    R_t<=R_0, |r_t|<=|r_0| at every state.               (42)

The last assertion follows from v_t>=v_0 and monotonicity of the inverse
in (37). Nothing in this proof restricts the chronology of turn levels.

For the original power clock on a single positive interval,

    C_p(r,v)=log r+(p-1)v r^(p-2)/(p-2)
                         +(2p-1)r^(2p-2)/[p(2p-2)],

implicit differentiation at fixed horizontal x gives the positive
vertical derivative r^(p-2)/(p-2). Splitting a noncrossing step into
horizontal motion and then its actual vertical increment yields

    C_p(r_plus,v_plus)-C_p(r,v)
       <=-h+|r|^(p-2)(v_plus-v)/(p-2).

Accordingly define the full, nonnegative retained cost by

    J_(p,all)
      =sum |r_(t-1)|^(p-2)(v_t-v_(t-1))/(p-2)
      =sum h_t |r_(t-1)|^(2p-2)/[p(p-2)].

The exact total-variation identity is still
TV_x=R_0-R_n+2 sum_(t a turn) R_t. Expanding over all m binary digits
and using (42) gives TV_x<=R_0[2(1+1/c)^m-1]. Therefore

    J_(p,all)<=min{
      |r_0|^(p-2)(v_n-v_0)/(p-2),
      R_0|r_0|^(2p-3)[2(1+1/c)^m-1]/[p(p-2)]
    }.                                                  (43)

Since R_0>=|r_0|^(2p-1)/p, one also has the radius-only charge

    J_(p,all)
       <=p^(-2/(2p-1)) R_0^((4p-4)/(2p-1))
                         [2(1+1/c)^m-1]/(p-2).           (44)

The factor 1/(p-2) is explicit in every version. The charge (44) can
diverge as p approaches 2; no contrary uniform bound is asserted.
The objective proof below does not absorb this factor into o(1).
Absorbed trajectories have zero subsequent cost, and no logarithm is
taken across a zero or a sign change.

### 10.4. Uniform no-turn payoff and the full-word conclusion

On a same-sign nonzero interval of mass T, the exact recurrence gives

    R_entry>=r(T+1+u),
    v_end>=T r^p/p,
    z=r^(2p-2)/p<=u/(T+1).

Combining this with (34), and maximizing the resulting rational
function of u>=0, gives for T>=1/(2p-2)

    2F_p(X_end)/R_entry^2<=E_p(T),
    E_p(T)=[(2p-2)T+2p-1]^2
              /[4p(p-1)(T+1)^2(2T+1)].                  (45)

For completeness, the rational function is
[1+k_T u]/[T+1+u]^2 with
k_T=2-2/p+1/[p(T+1)]. Its derivative has the sign of
k_T(T+1)-2-k_T u; the displayed condition makes its maximizing
u=T+1-2/k_T nonnegative and substitution yields (45).

There is a bound independent of p>2:

    E_p(T)<=1/(2T).                                    (46)

To check it, put A=p-1>1 and clear the positive denominator
4pA T(T+1)^2(2T+1). The numerator of the difference between the
right and left sides of (46) is

    4A T^3+(2A^2+6A)T^2+(4A^2+4A-1)T+2A(A+1)>0.

If s is the last turn, or s=0 for no turns, put b=b(s), q=m-b.
When q>=1, the final interval contains a real H_q by (19). Its mass
T>=S_q>1 is above the threshold in (45), since p>2. Retaining the
original input radius via (42) gives

    P_p<=c^(-2b)/(2S_q)<=1/(2S_m).

The second inequality follows from S_(j+1)<c^2 S_j for j>=1,
proved directly from the word recurrence in Section 7. If q=0, the
last step turns and P_p<=c^(-2m)<1/(2S_m), since S_m<c^m and
c^m>2. Absorption gives P_p=0. This proves (31) for all initial
states and every allowed p, without excluding reactivation.

### 10.5. Exact benchmark, uniformity, and the remaining power range

Section 8 proved directly from the accepted exact benchmark recursions
that B_n<=lambda^(m+1), and that S_m/c^m>24/25 for m>=512.
For a slightly sharper finite comparison than used there, the first
five binomial terms give

    (1+1/m)^m
      >2+49/100+4/25+1/25=269/100>8/3.

Indeed all three factors 1-j/m, j=1,2,3, exceed 99/100 for
m>=512. The second-, third-, and fourth-order binomial terms then
exceed, respectively, 49/100, (99/100)^2/6>4/25, and
(99/100)^3/24>1/25. Consequently (lambda/c)^m<3/8, and (31)
implies

    B_n P_p
       <(1/2)*(5/2)*(3/8)*(25/24)
       =125/256<1/2.

This proves (32). The limiting comparison uses only quantities
independent of p:

    S_m/c^m->1, (lambda/c)^m->1/e.

Thus (31) gives (33) uniformly over the entire range (30), with
no p-dependent factor inside its limiting argument. Since e>5/2>lambda,
the limiting constant lambda/(2e) is strictly below 1/2.

This complete joint extension still excludes only the stated global
power-epigraph functions. It does not upper-bound W_n or decide the
original exact-profile conjecture. It leaves p>m/256 outside its stated
sufficient range. A failed application of (41) in that range would
only be a failure of this capacity estimate, not a proof that the
power model succeeds or fails there.

All statements remain UNVERIFIED. The prior C68 shared finding is not
a predecessor; its component proofs have been reproduced inside this
joint artifact, and every additional general-power ingredient was
derived explicitly above. No fact_submit, experiment, or new allocation
has been inferred from this extension.

# Chronological kernel: an explicit local square decomposition

Status: **unverified proof draft**, fifth launch, first continuation round.
There is a complete algebraic factorization below, including the constant
gradient column and the original initial-position variable. Its coefficient
signs have passed an outward-interval evaluation at the actual depth128.
This is not a uniform proof for all m>=128, a verifier-accepted fact, or a
solution of the original minimax problem. No fact_submit was allocated or used.

The new theoretical question is the sign of explicitly displayed scalar
coefficients in the birth coordinates. This is a sufficient condition for
the old covariance inequality; equivalence of their positivity is NOT claimed.

## 1. Original word, shared data, and exact certificate identity

For an integer m>=128 set epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2),
c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c, d_j=1+a*c^j, and
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j). Let q=2^m-2 and let h_0,...,h_(q-1)
be H_m with its final d_0 removed. Define s_i=sum_(r<i)h_r and S=s_q.
For real vectors v,w_0,...,w_(m-1), all using one arbitrary common Gram,
put p_ij=product_(r<i)(1-h_r/d_j), g_i=v+sum_j p_ij*w_j, and
x_i=x_0-sum_(r<i)h_r*g_r. The first d_j kills its column at query2^j.
Thus g_q=v and x_q=x_0-S*v-sum_j d_j*w_j.

For one common array of sampled values and the zero optimum jet, use
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2. Necessity and sufficiency
of the entire interpolation array are in accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290.
Define, purely algebraically,

 J=sum_(i<q) [2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
             +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].

The GD norm identity and summation by parts give

 ||x_0||^2-2S*f_q+2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)
                  +2sum_i s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)=||x_q||^2+J.       (1)

Indeed the optimum terms equal
2sum h_i f_i-||x_0||^2+||x_q||^2+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2;
the chain terms equal 2S f_q-2sum h_i f_i plus the first two terms of J.
All selected multipliers are nonnegative. No unused original interpolation
constraint is deleted from the definition of legal data.

Let T be the symmetric matrix of J in (w_0,...,w_(m-1),v). For a word W,
put P_W(z)=product_(h in W)(1-hz) and S_W=sum W. The zero-clock kernels
K,T satisfy, for concatenated words U,V,

 K_UV=K_U+P_U(z)P_U(w)K_V,
 T_UV=T_U+P_U(z)P_U(w)[T_V+2S_U K_V],                         (2)
 K_[h]=h-h^2(z+w-zw)/2,
 T_[h]=h(h+1)-h^3(z+w-zw).

These follow by separating the defining time sums, retaining the offset
S_U in every second-block clock. At z=1/d_j and z=0 these compute the
actual matrix with O(m^3) scalar operations, without enumerating2^m steps.
Deletion of the last d_0 changes only T_(v,v), to S(S+1), because all
residual columns are already zero. This final diagonal is retained below.

For comparison with the earlier covariance formulation, D_i=g_i-g_(i+1),
A_ij=h_i*p_ij/d_j, beta_i=s_(i+1)(s_i+1), beta_q=S(S+1), and
c_i=(h_i-1)s_(i+1). Expansion of J and completion of the constant square give

 J=beta_q||v+sum_i beta_i D_i/beta_q||^2
       +sum_(i,l)[beta_min(i,l)-beta_i beta_l/beta_q]<D_i,D_l>
       -sum_i c_i||D_i||^2.                                    (3)

For example the coefficient of ||g_i||^2 after collecting adjacent terms
is beta_i-beta_(i-1); this proves (3) by writing g_i=v+sum_(r>=i)D_r.
Consequently positivity of T is exactly the old covariance domination,
including its constant-mode charge. This is only an equivalence of formal
quadratic forms, not a test of whether a negative formal direction is legal.

## 2. Lossless birth coordinates and exact sparsity

Define phi_k(z)=product_(r<k)(1-d_r*z),
V_k=v+sum_j phi_k(1/d_j)w_j for0<=k<=m, and U_k=V_k-v.
In particular V_m=v and U_m=0. The triangular node-evaluation matrix has
positive diagonal, so these coordinates lose no modal direction.

The identity
(1-hz)phi_k=(1-h/d_k)phi_k+(h/d_k)phi_(k+1)
gives g_i=sum_k B_ik V_k, where B starts at the point mass at0 and
at step h moves mass from state k to k+1 with fraction h/d_k.
An occupied state has d_k>=h. Lower states have already been killed by
their first physical level. Thus B_ik>=0, sum_k B_ik=1, and

 B_ik=0 if k>i or i>=2^k, for k<m.                           (4)

The first zero follows because one step advances at most one state; the
second follows by induction on first physical occurrences.

Set xi_j=d_j*w_j, z=(S+1)v, and y_k=d_k U_k. Then y=R*xi, with

 R_kj=(d_k/d_j)phi_k(1/d_j) for j>=k; R_kj=0 for j<k.

Let M=diag(1/d_0,...,1/d_(m-1),1/(S+1)) T diag(same).
Define the symmetric matrix

 H=diag(R^(-T),1) M diag(R^(-1),1)
       = [ E, ell ; ell^T, D ],       D=S/(S+1).               (5)

Thus J=sum_kl E_kl<y_k,y_l>+2sum_k ell_k<y_k,z>+D||z||^2.
All scalings are positive and R is invertible. The vectors remain in one
real Euclidean space, with their original cross terms.

There are useful EXACT zeros:

                 E_kl=0 if l>2^k and k<l<m.                  (6)

Each term in J uses only g_i and g_(i+1). If its state-k coefficient is
nonzero, (4) forces i+1<=2^k. All states at either query are then <=2^k,
so state l>2^k cannot enter that term. In particular rows0,1 have no
off-diagonal entries beyond columns1,2 respectively. Numerical arithmetic
may be replaced by zero at precisely these positions because of this proof;
no other small entries are discarded.

## 3. Exact square-factor lemma, with the complete constant load

The following is an algebraic identity for ANY symmetric real m-by-m matrix
E and real column ell, with m>=3. Define

 e_i=E_(i,i+2),                    0<=i<=m-3,
 b_i=E_(i,i+1)-2(e_(i-1)+e_i),    0<=i<=m-2,
 r_i=E_ii-E_(i-1,i)-E_(i,i+1)+e_(i-2)+e_i
                   -sum_(|k-i|>=3)|E_ik|, 0<=i<m.             (7)

An out-of-range e or adjacent entry is zero. Put alpha_(-1)=0 and

 alpha_i=ell_i-alpha_(i-1), 0<=i<m,
 C=sum_(i<m-1)alpha_i^2/b_i + alpha_(m-1)^2/r_(m-1),
 Delta=D-C.                                                   (8)

If b_i>0 and r_(m-1)>0, with no other sign assumption yet, then

 J=sum_(i<m-1)r_i||y_i||^2
     +r_(m-1)||y_(m-1)+(alpha_(m-1)/r_(m-1))*z||^2
     +sum_(i<m-1)b_i||y_i+y_(i+1)+(alpha_i/b_i)*z||^2
     +sum_(i<m-2)e_i||y_i+2y_(i+1)+y_(i+2)||^2
     +sum_(k<l, l-k>=3)|E_kl| ||y_k+sgn(E_kl)y_l||^2
     +Delta||z||^2.                                          (9)

For a zero long-range coefficient use sgn(0)=0; its whole term is zero.

Proof. The triple squares supply off-diagonal entry e_i at distance2 and
entries2e_i at each of its two neighboring pairs. Subtracting them leaves
the adjacent coefficient b_i in (7). Their diagonal contributions, together
with those of the pair squares, are
E_(i-1,i)+E_(i,i+1)-e_(i-2)-e_i. Each long-range square contributes
|E_ik| to the corresponding diagonal. The remaining diagonal is exactly r_i.
This proves the residual identity. Finally

 sum_i ell_i y_i=sum_(i<m-1)alpha_i(y_i+y_(i+1))
                                      +alpha_(m-1)y_(m-1)

by ell_i=alpha_i+alpha_(i-1). Completing precisely those displayed squares
spends C and leaves Delta. This proves (9), including all cross terms.

Therefore the explicit scalar conditions

 e_i>=0, b_i>0, r_i>=0 (all i), r_(m-1)>0, Delta>=0            (10)

are SUFFICIENT for the full T to be positive semidefinite. This supplies an
actual square-factor formula, not an LDL recurrence with unknown pivots.
The constant column is paid by the exact alternating loads (8), without a
matrix inverse or pseudoinverse. No individual adjacent-swap sign is used.

The original certificate in (1) has the additional square

 ||x_0-S*z/(S+1)-sum_j xi_j||^2.                              (11)

The change from x_0 to that square's vector is an invertible unit triangular
change of coordinates. Thus (9) plus (11) is a factorization on the FULL
original formal space, including x_0. There is no hidden range condition.

## 4. Uniform exact boundary calculation: a coefficient vanishes as 1/m

Write t=d_0, u=d_1, d=d_2. The first three gradients in birth coordinates
are V_0,V_1,V_2. Direct expansion of the first two physical steps gives

 E_00=(2-t)/t, E_01=(t-1)/u,
 E_11=[2t+u(2-u)]/u^2,

 r_0>117/283-83/398>1/5,       b_0>1/5,       b_1>12/25.       (13)

 r_1>3epsilon/2, and r_1/epsilon -> (3sqrt(2)-1)/2.            (14)

delta/epsilon=2/[lambda(1+epsilon)]-lambda*epsilon>3/4,

 =epsilon[(t+4)(t+2)+2-epsilon(2t+7)+epsilon^2]

The first constant loads are also exact:

# Two actual children in one projection body

Status: joint proof draft, **UNVERIFIED**. Eighth launch, cumulative round18.
No solver, parameter sweep, installation or verifier was used. The original
all-schedule exact-profile target is unresolved. Accepted facts
1252b8823bb5a290 and b98bb807d514e80d specify the original interpolation model,
performance W_n, and exact comparison B_n; every new construction below is
derived here. Earlier unverified packages are not premises.

## 1. Full input, function, values, and true distance

A child consists of a nonnegative finite word p of length ell, actual vectors
x_i,g_i for 0<=i<=ell, and the optimum sample x_*=g_*=0. Set

    K=conv(0,g_0,...,g_ell), y_i=x_i-g_i,
    x_(i+1)=x_i-p_i g_i,
    <g_j-g_i,y_i><=0 for every i,j,
    <g_i,y_i>>=0 for every i,
    x_ell=g_ell=w !=0.                                      (1)

Include ALL samples, even duplicated ones or those at zero steps. Nonzero
residuals y_i are permitted. Set

    A=1+sum p_i, R_i=sum_(t=i)^(ell-1) p_t,
    R^2=||x_0||^2, Delta=A^2||w||^2-R^2,
    kappa=A^2||w||^2/R^2.

The values and common function are specified, not freely shifted:

    F_K(x)=max_(g in K)(<x,g>-||g||^2/2),
    f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2, f_*=0.                        (2)

The maximizer is the unique Euclidean projection onto K: completing the
square proves this, and its exact optimality condition is (1). Adding the
two projection normals for x,x' proves
||P_K(x)-P_K(x')||^2<=<x-x',P_K(x)-P_K(x')>. Thus it is 1-Lipschitz.
Evaluation of the defining maxima at each other's maximizers bounds the
differentiability remainder by ||x-x'||^2. Consequently F_K is finite,
convex, differentiable and 1-smooth, with gradient P_K and values (2).

The minimizer set is exactly K^polar={z:<z,g><=0 for every g in K}.
The forward implication follows by using epsilon*g in (2) and sending
epsilon down to0; the reverse implication follows directly from (2).
The endpoint and GD identity give

    x_0=w+sum_(i<ell) p_i g_i.                              (3)

Hence <x_0,z><=0 for every minimizer z, so 0 is a closest minimizer and
dist(x_0,argmin F_K)^2=R^2. No arbitrary chosen-optimum normalization is used.
For the original signed interpolation residual of fact1252b8823bb5a290,
substitution of (2) gives the identity

    Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>.                                    (4)

This includes Q_i*=0 and Q_*i=-<g_i,y_i><=0. Thus checking (1) checks EVERY
original interpolation inequality, including both optimum incidences.

The input contains these vectors and values, not merely Delta or kappa.

## 2. A real cross Gram block and its exact legality conditions

Take two inputs L,R with capacities A,C, initial squared distances R_L^2,
R_R^2, and endpoints w_L,w_R. Choose a bridge 1+r with r>0. Write
e=w_L/||w_L|| and d=x_R,0/R_R. Embed the two spaces in
R direct-sum e^perp direct-sum d^perp by

    J_L u=(<u,e>, u-<u,e>e, 0),
    J_R v=(-<v,d>, 0, v-<v,d>d),
    a_scale=r||w_L||/R_R.                                 (5)

Both J are real isometries. Use J_L x_L,i,J_L g_L,i for the complete left
transcript and a_scale J_R x_R,j,a_scale J_R g_R,j for the complete right
transcript. The bridge is exact because

    J_L w_L-(1+r)J_L w_L=-r J_L w_L=a_scale J_R x_R,0.

All child updates are unchanged. The endpoint is a_scale J_R w_R. The
cross Gram block, on any pair of child vectors, is explicitly

    <J_L u,a_scale J_R v>
       =-r <u,w_L><v,x_R,0>/R_R^2.                         (6)

Real PSD follows from (5), not from an unspecified positive block matrix.
Left values are unchanged; right values are a_scale^2 f_R,j. Let the parent
body be the convex hull of0 and EVERY displayed parent gradient, including
the left bridge gradient J_L w_L and the terminal gradient.

Within-child and optimum normals remain (1), with the right ones scaled
by a_scale^2. The only additional inequalities are, for every i,j,

    -r <g_R,j,x_R,0><w_L,y_L,i>/R_R^2
          <= <g_L,i,y_L,i>,                               (7L)
    -<g_L,i,w_L><x_R,0,y_R,j>
          <= r||w_L||^2 <g_R,j,y_R,j>.                     (7R)

These follow by substituting (6) into the two cross normals; conversely they
are those normals. They include every old gradient against every new residual
and the bridge gradient against all right samples. Thus (7L)-(7R) are exact
necessary and sufficient conditions for this SPECIFIED function and data.
When they hold, (2)-(4) provide the common function, values, all Q inequalities,
and true initial distance R_L, since (3) uses retained left gradients.

The physical parent capacity is P=A+C+r. Its exact ratio is

    kappa_P=P^2 r^2 kappa_L kappa_R/(A^2 C^2).              (8)

For the source primitive bridge rP=AC, equivalently
r=(-A-C+sqrt((A+C)^2+4AC))/2, this is

    kappa_P=kappa_L kappa_R,
    Delta_P=R_L^2[(1+Delta_L/R_L^2)(1+Delta_R/R_R^2)-1].    (9)

The cross term in (9) is an exact consequence of a legal construction ONLY
when (7) holds. No favorable interaction is presumed from two scalar defects.

## 3. The planar core blocks even arbitrary transverse correlations

Here is the previously detected planar core, rederived. Set s=sqrt2,
lambda=1+s, theta=s-1. At its source word (s,2,s), take

    U=1/lambda^2, eta=-(1/2+theta)/s,
    u=(1/lambda,0), v=(eta,sqrt(1/2-eta^2))/lambda,
    w=-u-s v,

We have eta=-1+1/(2s), so eta^2<1/2. The residuals are s u,0,-u-v,0.
At sample0 all four vertex normals against0,u,v,w are nonpositive:
<v,u>=eta U<U and <w,u>=(s-3/2)U<U. At sample2,
<v,y>=(1/2-1/(2s))U>0, the u normal is -U/2, and

Thus (10) satisfies the full input contract. It has R^2=1,

Consider ANY isometric endpoint-aligned splice with this right child,
regardless of how transverse coordinates are correlated. The actual bridge
gradient necessarily represents -x_R,0/r in right-child units. At right
sample2 its required normal is

    <-x_R,0/r-v,y_2><=0,

The equality follows from

## 4. A second actual core retains its nonzero first post-step residual

For arbitrary a>=0, b>1 put c=a, H=a+1, z=b-1, xi=z/H>0, and take
orthogonal vectors U=(1,0), V=(0,sqrt(xi)). The word is (a,b,a), and

The body is conv(0,U,V). At sample0 the V normal is z-(a+b-1)=-a.

Writing D=1+3xi+xi^2, its exact data are

## 1. Statement and notation

    J_all<=p^(-2/(2p-1)) R_0^((4p-4)/(2p-1))
                         [2(1+1/c)^m-1]/(p-2).           (5)

Every factor p-2 is retained. No uniform assertion about J_all as p
decreases to 2 is made. The objective estimate does not use (5) as an
o(1) error. This is a proper-family exclusion, not a bound on W_n for
all convex smooth functions and not a solution of the original target.

Section 4 also gives an explicit sufficient condition wider than (1).
Asymptotically it covers every range 2<p<=kappa m log(m) with fixed
0<kappa<1/[4lambda^2], once m is sufficiently large.

## 2. Global legality, all ordered pairs, and the actual state

K_p is closed, convex, and nonempty. Completing the square shows that
the defining maximum is finite and attained uniquely at Pi_(K_p)(X),
the Euclidean projection. Its two normal inequalities imply

    ||Pi_(K_p)(Y)-Pi_(K_p)(X)||^2
       <=<Pi_(K_p)(Y)-Pi_(K_p)(X),Y-X>.

In particular the projection is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two defining
maxima gives

    0<=F_p(Y)-F_p(X)-<Pi_(K_p)(X),Y-X>
      <=<Pi_(K_p)(Y)-Pi_(K_p)(X),Y-X><=||Y-X||^2.

The remainder divided by ||Y-X|| tends to zero, proving differentiability
with gradient the projection. F_p is convex as a supremum of affine
functions and has 1-Lipschitz gradient.

Since phi_p'(r)=r|r|^(p-2),

    X_p(r,v)-G_p(r)=eta*(phi_p'(r),-1).

For any (z,s) in K_p the inner product of this vector with
(z,s)-G_p(r) is at most
eta*[phi_p'(r)(z-r)-phi_p(z)+phi_p(r)]<=0 by convexity.
Thus grad F_p(X_p(r,v))=G_p(r), and direct substitution gives

    2F_p(X_p(r,v))
      =r^2+(2-2/p)v|r|^p+(2p-1)|r|^(2p)/p^2.             (6)

For any ordered pair of such states, putting f_i=F_p(X_i), its exact
smooth-convex interpolation residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =eta_j*[phi_p'(r_j)(r_i-r_j)-phi_p(r_i)
                                        +phi_p(r_j)]<=0. (7)

This includes every pair, regardless of temporal separation.

Zero is feasible in the maximum. At (0,y), y<=0, all feasible inner
products minus half the squared norm are nonpositive. At x!=0 a
sufficiently small r with the sign of x gives a positive value, since
xr dominates the terms of orders 2,p,2p. At x=0,y>0 a sufficiently
small positive vertical g gives a positive value. Therefore

    min F_p=0, argmin F_p={(0,y):y<=0},
    dist(X_p(r,v),argmin F_p)=|r|(1+u)=R.                 (8)

The actual step, with the original v inherited, is

    v_plus=v+h|r|^p/p, x_plus=x-hr,
    x_plus=T_(p,v_plus)(r_plus),
    T_(p,v)(r)=r+v r|r|^(p-2)+r|r|^(2p-2)/p.             (9)

This T is odd and strictly increasing onto R. Off zero its derivative
is 1+(p-1)v|r|^(p-2)+(2p-1)|r|^(2p-2)/p>=1; at zero the derivative
is 1. Thus (9) uniquely determines the true next state on this same
global F_p. Zero is absorbing. Along any nonzero one-sign interval,
R and |r| decrease and v increases, directly from (9).

Put z=|r|^(2p-2)/p. Then 0<=z<=u and

    2F_p(X)/r^2=1+(2-2/p)u+z/p<=(1+u)^2=R^2/r^2,        (10)

because the difference is (2/p)u+u^2-z/p>=u/p+u^2.

## 3. The exact no-turn tradeoff

Consider an actual one-sign nonzero occurrence of H_l, l>=1, with
terminal magnitude r>0 and normal variable u>0. Let rho and u_mid
be the corresponding values immediately before its middle step
1+d_(l-1). Nonturning and nonabsorption imply u_mid>d_(l-1).
Since rho>=r and v_mid<=v_end,

    u_mid<=u*(rho/r)^(2p-2).                             (11)

Indeed the v term has exponent p-2 and the pure-power term exponent
2p-2, and rho/r>=1. Let Apre_l=M_(l-1)+d_(l-1), the mass of the
steps through the middle step. All gradients used by those steps
have magnitude at least rho; the later ones have magnitude at least r.
Telescoping actual horizontal displacements therefore proves

    R_entry/r>=M_l+u
       +Apre_l*((d_(l-1)/u)^(1/(2p-2))-1)_+.             (12)

Here (w)_+=max(w,0). The radius is the true entry radius of this
particular block; its vertical state has not been reset.

For k>0 and beta>0 define the explicit scalar minimum

    mu(k,beta)=min_(t>0) [t+beta*(t^(-1/k)-1)_+]
      =1,                                      if k<=beta;
      =(k+1)*(beta/k)^(k/(k+1))-beta,            if k>beta. (13)

For t>=1 the minimum is 1 at t=1. For 0<t<1 the derivative is
1-(beta/k)t^(-1-1/k). If k<=beta it is nonpositive throughout this
interval, again giving the boundary minimum 1. Otherwise it changes
sign at t=(beta/k)^(k/(k+1)), giving (13).
The minimum is nondecreasing in beta and nonincreasing in k because
each function being minimized has those monotonicities.

The mass recursion M_(l+1)=2M_l+d_l, M_0=1, solves to

    M_l=A c^l+(1-A)2^l, A=a/(c-2).                      (14)

Since c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1>1-epsilon, one has 0<A<1.
Consequently M_l/d_l>=1/(c-2), and

    Apre_l/d_(l-1)>=beta_c:=(c-1)/(c-2).

Taking k=2p-2, t=u/d_(l-1) in (12) gives

    R_entry>=Aend_l |r_end|,
    Aend_l=M_l+mu(2p-2,beta_c)d_(l-1), l>=1;
    Aend_0=1.                                           (15)

For a zero terminal gradient this inequality holds without division;
the trajectory has already been absorbed.

## 4. Quantitative power range and the sharper sufficient condition

Define

    D_c=[c/(c-2)]*[c(c-2)-1].

By (14)--(15), the condition

    mu(2p-2,beta_c)>=D_c                                (16)

implies Aend_l>=c d_l for l>=1. For l=0 the same inequality follows
from Aend_0=1>ac=1-epsilon. We next prove (16) throughout (1).

For m>=512, sqrt(2)<99/70 gives

    c<(169/70)*(513/512)<121/50<5/2.

Thus beta_c>3. Also lambda>12/5 and z/(z-2) decreases for z>2,
so c/(c-2)<6. Expanding about lambda gives

    c(c-2)-1=2lambda(lambda-1)/m+lambda^2/m^2<8/m,
    D_c<48/m.                                          (17)

For the first strict inequality, use lambda<5/2, lambda-1<3/2,
and (15/2)+(25/4)/512<8.

Put q=2p-1>3 and Q=m log(m)/32. From (1), q<Q. With beta=1 in
(13), since k=q-1>2,

    mu(q-1,1)=q(q-1)^(-(q-1)/q)-1>log(q)/q.              (18)

To check this, the logarithm of the positive expression before minus
1 equals log(q/(q-1))+log(q-1)/q, which exceeds log(q)/q;
use exp(z)-1>=z. Since beta_c>3>1, (18) is a lower bound for (16).
If 3<q<=9 it yields

    mu(2p-2,beta_c)>log(3)/9>1/9>48/512>=48/m.

The elementary strict inequality log(3)>1 follows by integrating the
strictly convex function 1/t on [1,3] and using its midpoint lower
bound. If q>=9, apply (13) with beta=3 instead. Its logarithmic form
gives

    mu(q-1,3)>3 log(q/3)/q.

Indeed log[(mu(q-1,3)+3)/3]
=log(q/(q-1))+log((q-1)/3)/q>log(q/3)/q.
The function log(q/3)/q decreases on [9,infinity), since log(3)>1.
Also sqrt(m) log(m)>96: at m=512 use sqrt(512)>16 and
log(512)=9log(2)>6, where log(2)>2/3 follows from the strict midpoint
bound on [1,2]; both factors increase with m. Hence

    log(Q/3)=log(m log(m)/96)>log(m)/2,
    mu(2p-2,beta_c)>=mu(q-1,3)
       >3 log(Q/3)/Q>48/m>D_c.                          (19)

This proves (16) uniformly over (1), without a hidden p-dependent
constant.

There is also a sharper asymptotic consequence of the explicit test
(16). Fix 0<kappa<1/(4lambda^2) and put p=kappa m log(m). Then
beta_c tends to beta_*=(lambda-1)/(lambda-2)=2+sqrt(2), and

    m D_c ->2lambda^2 beta_*.

For q=2p-1 set
L_m=log(q/(q-1))+log((q-1)/beta_c)/q. Formula (13) gives
mu(2p-2,beta_c)=beta_c*(exp(L_m)-1). Direct limits give
L_m->0 and m L_m->1/(2kappa). Therefore

    m mu(2p-2,beta_c)->beta_*/(2kappa)>2lambda^2 beta_*.

Condition (16) holds for sufficiently large m at this endpoint power.
Its monotonicity in p proves the same statement UNIFORMLY for every
2<p<=kappa m log(m). For kappa>1/(4lambda^2), the displayed sufficient
test fails eventually at the endpoint power; that fact concerns only
this test and is not a trajectory counterexample. No conclusion at
equality is asserted.

## 5. Actual chronological turns

We need an elementary binary interval lemma. If integers 0<=s<t obey
q=b(t-1)-b(s)>=1, then [s,t] contains an interval [A_0,A_0+2^q]
whose left endpoint is a multiple of 2^q.

Proof: put B=2^q and s=kB+r, 0<=r<B. If r=0 and no such interval
fits, t<s+B, so t-1 has the same high part k and a low part at most
B-2. Its digit sum exceeds that of s by at most q-1. If r>0 and
no interval fits, t<(k+2)B. When t-1 has high part k, its low part
has at most q ones while r has at least one. When it has high part
k+1, its low part is at most B-2 and has at most q-1 ones, while
b(k+1)-b(k)<=1 and b(r)>=1. Both cases again give at most q-1,
contradicting the definition of q.

The physical steps A_0+1,...,A_0+2^q-1 in such an interval are the
actual H_q, since nu_2(A_0+j)=nu_2(j) for 0<j<2^q.

Let s<t be consecutive actual turns, allowing s=0 before the first.
Their intervening steps form a one-sign interval. Set

    q=max(0,b(t-1)-b(s)), ell=nu_2(t).

For q>=1 the lemma locates a real no-turn H_q inside that interval.
Its entry radius is at most R_s and its terminal gradient magnitude
is at least |r_(t-1)|. Equations (15)--(16) imply

    R_s>=a c^(q+1)|r_(t-1)|.

For q=0 use R_s>=|r_(t-1)| and ac<1 to get the same bound. At the
turn, (9) gives

    R_t=(d_ell-u_(t-1))|r_(t-1)|
       <=c^(ell-q-1)R_s<=c^(b(s)-b(t))R_s,               (20)

using b(t-1)=b(t)-1+ell. Induction over the actual turns yields
the turn estimate in (2). The radius decreases between turns, and
b(t)>=1 at each positive turn time, so R_t<=R_0 everywhere.
Since v_t>=v_0 and T_(p,v) increases with v at each positive r,
(9) also gives |r_t|<=|r_0| everywhere. This proof permits arbitrary
increases and decreases in turning level and never resets a right copy.

## 6. Paying all retained normal costs

On a positive one-sign interval define

    C_p(r,v)=log r+(p-1)v r^(p-2)/(p-2)
                  +(2p-1)r^(2p-2)/[p(2p-2)].

At x=T_(p,v)(r), implicit differentiation of C_p(T_(p,v)^(-1)(x),v)
gives partial_x=1/r and partial_v=r^(p-2)/(p-2). For a positive
noncrossing step, first decrease x by hr at fixed v and then increase
v at the resulting fixed x. The inverse r decreases during both
motions. The first integral is therefore at most -h, while the
second is at most r^(p-2)(v_plus-v)/(p-2), with r from before the
step. Reflection proves the negative-ray version. This retains the
positive cost and uses no logarithm at zero or across a turn.

Equation (9) gives

    J_all=sum h_t |r_(t-1)|^(2p-2)/[p(p-2)].

The bound |r_t|<=|r_0| proves the first part of (4). For the other
part, the exact total horizontal variation is

    TV_x:=sum h_t|r_(t-1)|=R_0-R_n+2sum_(t a turn)R_t.

A nonturn step contributes the radius difference, including a step
that reaches zero; a turn contributes the radius sum. Summing gives
the equality. By (20) and the product expansion over m binary digits,

    sum_(t=0)^(2^m-1)c^(-b(t))=(1+1/c)^m,
    TV_x<=R_0[2(1+1/c)^m-1].                            (21)

Combine |r|^(2p-2)=|r|*|r|^(2p-3) with (21) to prove (4).
Finally R_0>=|r_0|^(2p-1)/p gives (5). This also bounds the sum
of J over all noncrossing intervals, as those terms are a subset of
J_all. Absorbing states contribute zero thereafter.

## 7. Terminal payoff without loss of the original radius

On a nonzero one-sign interval of total mass T, terminal magnitude
r and terminal normal u satisfy, by the same exact displacement sum,

    R_entry>=r(T+1+u), v_end>=T r^p/p,
    z=r^(2p-2)/p<=u/(T+1).

Equation (6) gives the upper bound [1+k_T u]/[T+1+u]^2 on
2F_p(X_end)/R_entry^2, where k_T=2-2/p+1/[p(T+1)]. For
T>=1/(2p-2), the derivative has the sign of
k_T(T+1)-2-k_T u and maximization yields

    E_p(T)=[(2p-2)T+2p-1]^2
               /[4p(p-1)(T+1)^2(2T+1)]<=1/(2T).         (22)

For the last inequality, put A_1=p-1>1 and clear the positive
denominator 4p A_1 T(T+1)^2(2T+1). The difference numerator is
4A_1 T^3+(2A_1^2+6A_1)T^2+(4A_1^2+4A_1-1)T+2A_1(A_1+1)>0.

For a nonabsorbed full run let s be its last turn, or 0 for no
turns, and put b=b(s), q=m-b. If q>=1, the binary lemma applied
with t=2^m gives an actual H_q in the final one-sign interval.
Its mass T>=S_q>1 is sufficient for (22), and its entry radius is
at most c^(-b)R_0. Hence

    P_p<=c^(-2b)/(2S_q).                                (23)

This is the actual radius ratio; the block has not been renormalized
as a separate trajectory. From (14), for j>=1,

    S_(j+1)-c S_j=c-1-(c-2)(1-A)2^j<=c-1.

Since S_j>1, it follows that S_(j+1)<(2c-1)S_j<c^2 S_j.
Iteration in (23) proves P_p<=1/(2S_m). If q=0 then s=n,
and (10),(20) give P_p<=c^(-2m)<1/(2S_m), since S_m<c^m and
c^m>2. Absorption gives P_p=0 directly. This proves all of (2).

## 8. Exact benchmark comparison

The accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d defines C_n=S_circle(n)+1,
B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1. Its exact recursions are

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(C_k,B_l),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

We derive B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1). Set
alpha=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda), Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/alpha.
Both coefficients in Llin exceed 1. Expansion using lambda^2=2lambda+1
gives

    alpha^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
       =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda y)^2>=0.

Thus Llin>=Omega(x,y). At z=lambda Omega(x,y), the polynomial
whose larger root is G(x,lambda y) has value

    z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
       =x[4x+lambda^2 y-alpha Omega(x,y)]>=0.

Moreover z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, so it is to the right
of the vertex. Consequently G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y),
and induction in the exact recursions gives B_n<=lambda C_n.

Put gamma=log_2(lambda)>1, D(t)=(1+t)^gamma-1 and ell(z)=log D(exp z).
For t=exp z, differentiation gives

    ell''(z)=gamma*t*(1+t)^(gamma-2)
         *[(1+t)^gamma-1-gamma*t]/D(t)^2>0.

The last bracket has value zero at 0 and strictly positive derivative
for t>0. Hence D(t)D(1/t)>=D(1)^2=2 by convexity. For x,y>0,
Z=(x^(1/gamma)+y^(1/gamma))^gamma therefore satisfies
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy, so Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0 and Z>=x+y.
This proves Omega(x,y)<=Z; the zero cases follow by substitution.
Induction gives C_n<=(n+1)^gamma, and hence

    B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).                             (24)

The finite constants are independent of p. From c<121/50,

    A=(1-1/m)/[c(c-2)]>(511/512)/(2541/2500)>49/50.

Also c^(-m)<1/50. Thus (14) implies S_m/c^m>24/25. The first
five binomial terms, using 1-j/m>99/100 for j=1,2,3, give

    (1+1/m)^m>2+49/100+4/25+1/25>8/3.

Combining (2),(24), lambda<5/2, and (lambda/c)^m<3/8 proves
B_n P_p<(1/2)*(5/2)*(3/8)*(25/24)=125/256.

As m tends to infinity, A->1 and
S_m/c^m=A+(1-A)(2/c)^m-c^(-m)->1, while
(lambda/c)^m=(1+1/m)^(-m)->1/e. This proves (3), uniformly in all
admissible powers and initial states. The same uniform limiting
comparison holds in every asymptotic range from Section 4. Finally
e>1+1+1/2=5/2>lambda, so lambda/(2e)<1/2.

## 9. Scope and audit

The expanded range (1) replaces the earlier sufficient range m/256
by m log(m)/64. Condition (16) is explicitly checkable and can be
used beyond the simpler stated range. A failure of (16) alone is
not a failed trajectory or a result about the whole power family.

All endpoints, zero states, consecutive turns, and negative digit-sum
differences were retained in the proof. All functions are one global
objective per run and all embedded blocks retain the enclosing a,c.
The positive clock cost is paid with the original horizontal radius
and optional actual terminal vertical state. No p-dependent factor
has been placed in an unspecified error term.

The literature search returned generic fixed-short-step descent and
the usual silver-schedule background, not a result covering this
moving-state inequality on the present perturbed word. No external
paper is a premise. Projection definitions and proofs were already
audited locally in arXiv:1210.5844v3, Propositions 3.2--3.3; Section 2
above supplies the needed proof in full.

This remains an UNVERIFIED proof candidate. The exact all-horizon,
all-schedule profile theorem is unresolved. No fact-graph promotion,
publication, or finalization is claimed.
