evidence:
# Common-prefix characters: strict local slack and a remote-pair obstruction

Status: **self-contained, unverified joint candidate from the user-directed
continuation after the prior seventeen-round launch**. No solver, parameter
sweep, installation, fact submission, new launch, or finalization is used.
The sole correctness predecessor is accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`, for
the necessity and orientation of the original interpolation inequalities.
Earlier common-prefix findings motivate the construction; they are not proof
premises. All identities needed below are derived here.

This specifies one new dependent, horizon-dependent probability law and one
positive amplitude law with strict local backoff. The latter is impossible:
four original remote interpolation inequalities cannot all hold. It does
**not** exclude every amplitude law for this probability distribution, and
does not establish either resolution of the original minimax problem.

## 1. Complete finite policy and the claim

Fix an integer m>=65536. Set

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m, c_chr=sigma(1+1/m),
    a_chr=delta/c_chr, N=2^m, n=N-1,
    epsilon=1/N, eta=1/N^2,
    l=1+a_chr, p_chr=1-epsilon, alpha=1-2epsilon,
    beta=7/10, D_chr=1+l p_chr,
    u_k=delta c_chr^(k-1), k>=1.

The actual algorithm uses

    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_chr c_chr^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Equivalently, its original step i is
h_i=1+a_chr c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0<=i<n. A leaf has nu_2(i+1)=0
and step l; a level-k bridge, k>=1, has step 1+u_k. Every subword below
retains the same enclosing-m parameters. No chronological index, step,
physical horizon, or benchmark is changed.

Give sample i its standard m-bit binary label (i_0,...,i_(m-1)). For a
character index s=(s_0,...,s_(m-1)) in {0,1}^m define

    chi_s(i)=(-1)^(sum_j s_j i_j),
    B(s)=(-1)^s_0,
    C_j(s)=(-1)^(s_1+...+s_j), 1<=j<m.

The map s -> (B,C_1,...,C_(m-1)) is bijective: (-1)^s_1=C_1 and
(-1)^s_j=C_(j-1)C_j for j>=2. Thus the following specifies EVERY atom.
Write mu_1=-7/10 and mu_(-1)=9/10, and for b in {-1,1} put

    A_b(c_1,...,c_(m-1))
       =[(1+mu_b)/2] 1_(all c_j=1)
          +[(1-mu_b)/2] 1_(all c_j=-1),
    P_b(c_1,...,c_(m-1))=product_(j=1)^(m-1)(1+mu_b c_j)/2,

    w_s=[(1+p_chr B(s))/2]
          [(1-eta) A_(B(s))(C_1(s),...,C_(m-1)(s))
              +eta P_(B(s))(C_1(s),...,C_(m-1)(s))].       (1)

Here 1_(condition) equals one or zero according to the displayed condition.
Each conditional factor is a probability law. Their mixture sums to one;
every w_s is strictly positive since epsilon,eta>0 and |mu_b|<1.
The first component makes ALL prefix signs equal, including the two lowest
ones. The second component gives full support at a stated rate.

Define the positive odd-to-odd amplitude ratios

    q_1=47/100, q_2=99/100, q_3=21/10,
    q_4=9/2, q_5=99/10,
    q_k=(69/100)u_k/D_chr, k>=6.                          (2)

The amplitudes of EVERY original sample are fixed before the trajectory:

    Gamma_0=1,
    Gamma_(i+1)=alpha Gamma_i                  at a leaf,
    Gamma_(i+1)=(q_k/alpha) Gamma_i             at a level-k bridge.
                                                                    (3)

Prescribe the actual real vectors in R^N

    g_i=(Gamma_i sqrt(w_s) chi_s(i))_s, 0<=i<=n.            (4)

For any common anchor X_0 and ANY real values f_0,...,f_n, define the original
positions and residuals

    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i) h_t g_t,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.            (5)

The claim has two parts.

* Every adjacent cocoercivity sum Q_(i,i+1)+Q_(i+1,i) is strictly negative.
  Every sum between the two odd endpoints of a bridge and its following
  leaf is also strictly negative. These sums do not depend on f or X_0.
* Let K=2^10=1024. At least one of

      Q_(0,K), Q_(K,0), Q_(3,K+3), Q_(K+3,3)              (6)

  is greater than 1/50, for EVERY f and EVERY X_0.

Thus (1)--(4) cannot be the gradient transcript of one convex differentiable
1-smooth function, with or without a minimizer. The first assertion is only
about necessary pair sums; it does not assert interpolation from local tests.
The second assertion retains four actual ordered inequalities and is a
uniform, finite-horizon obstruction to this entire specified policy.

## 2. Exact kernel moments and bounds

For a binary difference d=i xor j, put d_m=0. Inserting the inverse relations
between s and its prefix signs gives

    chi_s(d)=B(s)^d_0 product_(j=1)^(m-1) C_j(s)^(d_j xor d_(j+1)),
    <g_i,g_j>/(Gamma_i Gamma_j)=E chi_s(i xor j).            (7)

Expectations here are finite sums against (1). Conditional on B=b, every
C_j has mean mu_b in BOTH components of (1). Consequently

    E B=p_chr=1-epsilon,
    E C_k=z_chr=-7/10+4epsilon/5,
    E[B C_k]=w_chr=-7/10-epsilon/10.                       (8)

At a bridge of level k and its following leaf, the relative character
signs at the three ORIGINAL samples are 1,B C_k,C_k. Their correlations
are w_chr,p_chr,z_chr, respectively. At a leaf, the adjacent correlation is
p_chr. Multiplication by any starting character cancels in all these
inner products, so these identities hold at every occurrence.

This law lies outside the previous low-joint-moment chart:

    E C_1 C_2=1-eta+eta(49/100+4epsilon/25)>1/2.            (9)

To check (9), the common component has product one, and the independent
component has conditional product mu_B^2. Averaging over B gives
49/100+4epsilon/25. The final inequality uses eta<=10^(-6).

We use only the following rational bounds:

    0<epsilon<=10^(-6), 9999/10000<delta<1,
    12/5<c_chr<2417/1000,
    1413/1000<l<283/200,
    12/5<D_chr<483/200,
    999/1000<alpha<1, alpha>=1-2*10^(-6).                  (10)

For completeness 707/500<sqrt(2)<99/70 follows by squaring positive
rationals. Hence c_chr>1207/500>12/5 and, using m>=1024,
c_chr<(169/70)(1025/1024)<2417/1000. Also
a_chr>(70/169)(1023/1025)>413/1000 and
a_chr<sqrt(2)-1<29/70<83/200, giving the bounds on l.
Then D_chr>1+(1413/1000)(999999/1000000)>12/5 and D_chr<483/200.
The stronger lower bound on delta follows from m>=65536>10000.
The bounds on epsilon and alpha follow directly from their definitions.

Define D_tilde=1+l p_chr/alpha and C_tilde=-z_chr-l w_chr/alpha.
The same inequalities give

    D_tilde<4831/2000,
    C_tilde<1691/1000,
    z_chr<-699999/1000000,
    D_tilde/D_chr<=1/alpha<1001/1000,
    1/alpha<100001/100000.                                (11)

For the first two, use l/alpha<(283/200)/(1-2*10^(-6)),
-z_chr<=7/10, and -w_chr<=7/10+10^(-7). The ratio bound follows from
D_tilde=D_chr/alpha+1-1/alpha<=D_chr/alpha. Each strict numerical comparison
in (11) is a rational inequality with positive denominators.

## 3. Strict local slack without saturation

Accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290` states that an actual smooth-convex
transcript must obey every Q_ij<=0, with exactly the sign convention (5).
For adjacent samples with step 1+u, unit-direction correlation d, and
positive norm ratio r, adding its two original inequalities gives

    [Q_(i,i+1)+Q_(i+1,i)]/Gamma_i^2
          =r^2+(u-1)d r-u.                                (12)

At a leaf u=a_chr, d=p_chr, r=alpha. Substitution yields

    alpha^2+(a_chr-1)p_chr alpha-a_chr
       =-(1+3a_chr)epsilon+(2+2a_chr)epsilon^2<0.           (13)

Now let u=u_k and q=q_k. The bridge has next norm ratio q/alpha;
the following leaf produces norm ratio q from the original odd starting
sample. Directly expanding the pair sum between those odd endpoints gives

    [Q_(before,after)+Q_(after,before)]/Gamma_before^2
       =D_tilde q^2+(z_chr u+C_tilde)q-u.                  (14)

The intervening gradient has norm (q/alpha)Gamma_before and is included:
X_after-X_before=-(1+u)g_before-l g_middle. Substituting (8) into this
exact displacement gives (14), not an identification or deletion of the
middle vector.

For k=1,...,5 define the explicit lower bound

    u_low(k)=(9999/10000)(12/5)^(k-1).

By (10),(11), (14) is bounded above by

    (4831/2000)q_k^2
       +[1691/1000-(699999/1000000)u_low(k)]q_k-u_low(k).   (15)

All five rational expressions (15) are negative. Their negativity can be
checked by inserting the five fractions (2), multiplying by the positive
denominators, and comparing integers. The accompanying fixed audit records
these five comparisons; no optimization or parameter search is involved.

For the bridge alone at k=1, put r_hi=(100001/100000)q_1. Since u_1<1,
(12) is at most

    r_hi^2+(700001/1000000)(1-u_low(1))r_hi-u_low(1)<0.     (16)

For k=2,...,5, where u_k>1, replace only the positive square upwards and
the negative product downwards. The resulting upper bound is

    [(100001/100000)q_k]^2
           -(7/10)(u_low(k)-1)q_k-u_low(k)<0.             (17)

Again these are four fixed rational comparisons, supplied by the fractions
in (2). There is no saturation at any of these levels.

For k>=6, write gamma=69/100, so q=gamma u/D_chr. In (14), (11) gives

    D_tilde q^2+z_chr u q
       <=[(1001/1000)(69/100)-699/1000]u q<0,
    C_tilde q-u<[(1691/1000)(69/100)/(12/5)-1]u<0.         (18)

This proves strictness for every such odd endpoint comparison, including
arbitrarily high bridges of the ORIGINAL horizon. For the bridge itself,
r=q/alpha<(3/10)u and u>=u_low(6)>2. Since w_chr<=-7/10,

    r^2+(u-1)w_chr r-u
       <-(4/10)u r+(7/10)r-u<0.                          (19)

Equations (13)--(19) prove all stated local slacks. They do not rely on a
maximal adjacent root, nor on either low joint moment being at most 1/2.

## 4. An expanded copy inside the original fixed prefix

Let J_0=() and J_j=(J_(j-1),j,J_(j-1)) be a list of bridge levels. This
only indexes odd-to-odd transitions, with both actual steps retained in
(3) and (14). Set

    T_0=1, T_j=q_j T_(j-1)^2.                             (20)

Counting the transitions before sample 2^j-1 gives
Gamma_(2^j-1)=alpha T_(j-1). The next bridge has level j, so

    Gamma_(2^j)=q_j T_(j-1).                              (21)

For j=10 write r=Gamma_K with K=1024. We show r>2 using small rational
lower bounds alone. Formula (2) and (10) give

    q_6>(69/100)(9999/10000)(12/5)^5/(483/200)>4549/200.

Since q_(k+1)/q_k=c_chr>12/5 for k>=6, valid lower bounds for q_6,...,q_10
are, in order,

    227/10, 109/2, 131, 314, 754.                         (22)

Starting with T_0=1, lower bounds for T_1,...,T_9 are

    47/100, 21869/100000, 10043/100000,
    4538/100000, 2038/100000, 942/100000,
    483/100000, 305/100000, 292/100000.                    (23)

For each entry its predecessor squared, multiplied by the corresponding
q in (2) or the lower bound (22), is at least that entry. These nine
inequalities are integer comparisons after clearing denominators. Thus

    r=q_10 T_9>754*(292/100000)>2.                         (24)

The first three steps after K have levels 0,1,0, exactly as at the start.
Consequently the first and repeated four-sample amplitude patterns are

    (Gamma_0,Gamma_1,Gamma_2,Gamma_3)=(1,alpha,q_1,alpha q_1),
    (Gamma_K,Gamma_(K+1),Gamma_(K+2),Gamma_(K+3))
                        =r(1,alpha,q_1,alpha q_1).        (25)

All these are actual indices well before n. No terminal padding, restart,
rescaling of the second subproblem's physical parameters, or new algorithm
is involved.

## 5. Matched original pairs in the exact reference Gram

Introduce an AUXILIARY reference probability: B=1 and C_1=...=C_(m-1)=V,
where P(V=1)=3/20 and P(V=-1)=17/20. Its direction vectors repeat

    e_+, e_+, e_-, e_-, ...,
    e_+=(sqrt(3/20),sqrt(17/20)),
    e_-=(sqrt(3/20),-sqrt(17/20)),
    <e_+,e_->=-beta.                                     (26)

Indeed only character bit s_1 can be nonzero under this measure.
Use exactly the SAME amplitudes (3), steps, values, and sample indices
as in the finite policy. Only the direction Gram is changed in this
auxiliary calculation. It is not assumed legal or obtained by a limiting
argument.

Let Z=X_K-X_0 in this reference transcript. Positive amplitudes and steps
give

    Z=-P_+ e_+-P_- e_-, P_+,P_->=0.                       (27)

Put q=q_1, g=alpha q, and

    A_len=l+(1+delta)alpha, B_len=l q,
    d_3=A_len e_++B_len e_-.

By the first three actual updates, X_3=X_0-d_3. By (25),
X_(K+3)=X_K-r d_3, and the two matched gradient pairs are
(e_+,r e_+) and (g e_-,r g e_-).

Write R_i^0=Q_(i,K+i)^0+Q_(K+i,i)^0 for i=0,3, where the superscript
marks only this reference Gram. Adding the two original ordered residuals
cancels all values and gives

    R_0^0=(r-1)[(r-1)-<e_+,Z>],
    R_3^0=(r-1)g[(r-1)(g+<e_-,d_3>)-<e_-,Z>].            (28)

With the POSITIVE weight beta/g, their sum is EXACTLY

    S^0=R_0^0+(beta/g)R_3^0
       =(r-1)[(r-1)kappa+(1-beta^2)P_+],                 (29)
    kappa=1+beta q(alpha+l)-beta^2[l+(1+delta)alpha].

To check the final term, <e_++beta e_-,e_->=0 and
<e_++beta e_-,e_+>=1-beta^2. Substituting (27) therefore gives
-<e_++beta e_-,Z>=(1-beta^2)P_+>=0. This is the specific geometric
information provided by the common-prefix law.

Using (10), q=47/100, and (1+delta)alpha<2,

    kappa>1+(7/10)(47/100)(999/1000+1413/1000)
               -(49/100)(283/200+2)
         =60099/500000>3/25.                             (30)

Equations (24),(27),(29) imply S^0>3/25. This lower bound depends on
neither anchor nor values. It is a sum of four original ordered residuals,
not a chosen objective, a norm to the origin, or a surrogate distance.

The same exact identity yields a useful narrower interface: in the
two-ray reference, ANY repeated pattern (1,alpha,q,alpha q) with kappa>0
cannot expand by a factor r>1 after positive steps, regardless of all the
other amplitudes. With the parameter bounds (10), every q>=2/5 has

    kappa>1+(7/10)(2/5)(999/1000+1413/1000)
                  -(49/100)(283/200+2)=201/100000>0.       (31)

The finite full-support statement proved next concerns the definite law
(2),(3); (31) alone is not a general perturbation theorem for arbitrary
amplitudes or arbitrarily late repeated blocks.

## 6. Finite full support: explicit perturbation bound

The weight of the B=1 common component in (1) is
(1-epsilon/2)(1-eta). Conditional on this component the measure is exactly
(26). Hence for ALL binary labels i,j, the normalized kernels satisfy

    |K_ij-K_ij^0|<=epsilon+2eta=:d_err<=2epsilon.           (32)

This follows by writing the probability as its displayed reference
component plus the remaining probability. Every character product is in
[-1,1], so the difference of expectations is at most twice the remaining
mass. It is a direct finite probability bound, including high binary
labels; no condition number or inverse Gram is used.

Here are deliberately conservative bounds on the fixed prefix through K+3.
The largest bridge level there is ten. Since c_chr<5/2,

    u_k<(5/2)^9<2^12, h_i<2^13,
    q_k<2^12, q_k/alpha<2^13                       (k<=10).

There are fewer than K+4 updates before any of those samples. Thus, putting

    U=2^(14(K+4)),

we have Gamma_i<U there, and

    sum_(t<K+3) h_t Gamma_t<(K+4)2^13 U<2^24 U.            (33)

These loose bounds are not computational estimates; they follow by
multiplying the scalar ratio bounds. Their only purpose is to make the
finite perturbation cost explicit.

For any two samples i<j in this prefix, their pair sum has the original
formula

    R_ij=||g_i-g_j||^2
             -sum_(t=i)^(j-1) h_t <g_i-g_j,g_t>.          (34)

The diagonal norm terms are unchanged because both probability measures
sum to one. Equations (32),(33) give

    |R_ij-R_ij^0|
       <=2d_err Gamma_i Gamma_j
           +d_err(Gamma_i+Gamma_j)sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t Gamma_t
       <2^26 d_err U^2.                                 (35)

Use the SAME positive coefficient beta/g on the finite-policy pair sum,

    S=R_(0,K)+(beta/g)R_(3,K+3).

Since alpha>999/1000 and q=47/100, beta/g<3/2. In particular its total
weight is less than four, so (35) yields

    |S-S^0|<2^28 d_err U^2
              <=2^(29-m+28(K+4))=2^(28813-m)<2^(-100).    (36)

The final inequality holds for every original m>=65536. Although very
conservative, it is uniform in the original horizon. Combining (30),(36),

    S>3/25-2^(-100)>11/100.                              (37)

If all four ordered residuals in (6) were at most 1/50, their positive
weighted sum would be at most

    [2+2beta/g]/50<5/50=1/10,

contradicting (37). At least one is therefore greater than 1/50, as claimed.
Every function value and every common anchor was arbitrary. Positive defects
have not been hidden in a vanishing perturbation or discarded as negligible.

One can also set epsilon=eta=0 in the definitions and take alpha=1. The
reference and proposed Gram then coincide; (20)--(30) give the obstruction
directly at that boundary, while the leaf pair sums equal zero. The positive
finite laws are already excluded by (32)--(37), independently of any
continuity claim at the singular measure.

## 7. Scope, checks, and the remaining policy problem

The explicit law has positive weights at every finite horizon, depends on
the ORIGINAL horizon through epsilon and eta, couples the two lowest
prefix signs, and uses nonsaturating positive amplitudes. It changes the
hypotheses that supported the previous moment obstruction. Nevertheless,
the two retained remote pairs detect an impossible repeated expansion.
Every unused original normal and interpolation inequality remains a
requirement; four of them already suffice to rule out this candidate.

This is an infeasibility result for (1)--(4), so it asserts no payoff for an
illegal trajectory. There is no closest-minimizer distance to replace by
the anchor norm. The contradiction holds before selecting any function,
anchor, or polar minimizer, and consequently also covers an anchored
projection construction with a nonzero closest polar point. C62 is not
used. Accepted finite C59 and unrestricted character constructions are
outside the asserted scope.

In particular, the probability measure (1) is STILL OPEN for other
amplitude laws. The present rule has a uniform ratio on all occurrences
of a given physical level; that creates the matched copy (25). Avoiding
this obstruction requires a different history-dependent amplitude rule,
enough backoff to avoid the expanded copy, or a change of the specified
measure/labels. Formula (31) shows a real cost of repeated-shape expansion
in the singular two-ray geometry; it is not an all-policy payoff bound.

The fixed audit `check_common_prefix_remote_pairs.py` checks five local
odd-endpoint and bridge estimates, the nine rational growth comparisons,
one exact matched-pair identity, a 32-atom finite mixture fixture, and the
displayed exponent arithmetic. All checks passed in about 0.002 seconds.
They are transcription checks on the proof's fractions, not an optimizer,
sampled maximum, or a replacement for verification.

Matlas returned a self-contracted-gradient theorem with steps at most 1/L
or backtracking, hypotheses violated by H_m, and other inapplicable
constant-step results. Web background returned smooth convex interpolation;
its needed necessity is already proved in the read accepted predecessor
`1252b8823bb5a290`. No external theorem is a mathematical premise here.

The entire package remains **UNVERIFIED**. No fact submission is authorized
by the current task. The original all-schedule minimax question and a fixed
asymptotic algorithmic improvement remain unresolved.

evidence:
# C72: full primitive cone, a lossless optimum lift, and the exact reuse threshold

Status: self-contained research draft, UNVERIFIED. Sixth launch, first round,
cumulative round 14. No verifier call is authorized. All new results are proved
jointly here; shared findings are reference evidence, not predecessors.
Accepted background: b98bb807d514e80d (benchmark definitions),
0be8b54e0a33381c (square-root mass contraction), and 1252b8823bb5a290
(full smooth-convex interpolation and its explicit conjugate interpolant).

## 1. The intrinsic property and every original vector

Normalize L=1. For a nonnegative word h of length n let s=sum h_i,
H_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t, and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                      -s(s+1)||g_n||^2.

Call h primitive if V_h>=0 on every actual smooth convex run. This is exactly
Zhang--Jiang's primitive property: expansion of their difference of squared
positions cancels x_0 and all mixed gradient terms and leaves V_h. No norm
of x_0 is being substituted for the original objective distance.

Let e denote the n+1 column of ones; define A_ii=1, A_it=h_t for t<i,
and A_it=0 for t>i. The formal gradients g_0,...,g_n are independent.
Choose ALL n(n+1) ordered finite multipliers lambda_ij>=0, i!=j; their
zero diagonal is conventional. Define L=diag(lambda e)-lambda and

 omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T,
 D=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_(n-1)(2-h_(n-1)),-s(s+2)).

Then the full sufficient cone is exactly

 L^T e=omega,                 M=D+(LA+A^T L^T)/2 >=0.            (1)

Indeed value cancellation in V_h+sum lambda Q is the displayed flow.
The position terms have matrix sym(L(A-I)); the squared-difference terms
have matrix sym(L)-diag(omega)/2. Adding V's diagonal gives (1), with

                  V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g)>.          (2)

Thus (1) implies V_h>=0 because Q_ij<=0. All incoming terminal edges are
present. There is no rank, symmetry, child, sparsity, or fixed-remainder
restriction on lambda or M. In particular accepted terminal reduction
1252b8823bb5a290 is NOT used to delete primitive constraints.

Adding optimum indices to this certificate cannot enlarge its feasible
cone. With x_star=g_star=f_star=0, the x_0 squared coefficient remains
zero. Its mixed coefficient with g_i is -lambda_(i,star). A PSD matrix with
a zero diagonal entry has that entire row zero (test the corresponding
2x2 principal minors). Therefore all lambda_(i,star)=0. The sum of finite
value-flow equations is then -sum lambda_(star,i)=0, since the V value
coefficients sum to zero. Nonnegativity forces all lambda_(star,i)=0.
Consequently the full optimum/position column is forced to be identically
zero; (1) preserves the entire remaining cone, not a guessed reduction.

A unit-slope Huber run started beyond 1+s has g_i=1, Q_ij=0, and V_h=0.
For any certificate (1) this gives e^T M e=0 and hence M e=0. This is an
EXACT equality kernel, never a positive full-space eigenvalue margin. The
numerical formulation below uses the full matrix without a kernel quotient.

## 2. Lossless intrinsic primal: explicitly restore a minimizer

For arbitrary finite sample jets obeying every Q_ij<=0 and the GD recursion,
there is a legal smooth convex function with a minimizer and the SAME V_h.
This justifies the intrinsic model at the level of actual functions as well
as the preceding full-certificate column argument.

Fix epsilon>0 and append one coordinate. Put

 g'_i=(g_i,epsilon), x'_i=(x_i,T-epsilon H_i),
 f'_i=f_i+c-epsilon^2 H_i.

The GD recursion remains exact, and direct substitution shows Q'_ij=Q_ij:
the extra function difference -epsilon^2(H_i-H_j) cancels the extra
position term epsilon^2(H_i-H_j). Choose the finite constants

 c>=max_i{-f_i+epsilon^2 H_i+(||g_i||^2+epsilon^2)/2},
 epsilon T>=max_i{f_i+c-<g_i,x_i>+(||g_i||^2+epsilon^2)/2}.

After adding the optimum jet (0,0,0), these are exactly Q'_(star,i)<=0
and Q'_(i,star)<=0. The full conjugate interpolation construction in
accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies an everywhere finite convex
1-smooth interpolant with this optimum and every displayed jet. Thus it
is a genuine same-function GD run with an actual minimizer.

The additional V contribution is epsilon^2 times

 2sum_i h_i(s-H_i)+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)-s(s+1)=0,

because 2sum_i h_i(s-H_i)=s^2+sum_i h_i^2. Hence V'_h=V_h exactly.
This lift does NOT preserve the original distance or normalized objective,
and is used ONLY for intrinsic primitive validity. Zero steps and n=0
cause no exception; identical original queries stay identical after a zero
step. All formal original gradients remain in the final cone model.

It follows that minimizing V_h over the full Gram G>=0, trace(G)=1, all
ordered Q_ij<=0, and a harmless value gauge f_n=0 detects primitive failure
exactly at the sign level. Every negative feasible V yields a legal failure
by the lift. Conversely every nonzero-gradient legal failure can be divided
by its positive total squared gradient to meet trace(G)=1. Zero-gradient
jets cannot have negative V, since all values then agree. A common-gradient
Huber transcript has V=0, so this minimum is always <=0.

For positive steps the primal also has strict feasibility: use a diagonal
quadratic with n+1 distinct curvatures in (0,1) and nonzero initial
coordinates, then scale to trace(G)=1. The gradient polynomial columns
z product_(t<i)(1-h_t z) have distinct degrees 1,...,n+1 and are independent
at n+1 nonzero distinct nodes (divide by z). Every finite distinct-query
residual is strictly negative. This is the same Vandermonde argument as in
accepted1252b8823bb5a290. Values are bounded after fixing f_n because the
two ordered residuals bound every f_i-f_n and trace(G)=1 bounds every Gram
entry. Thus no unbounded objective is concealed by the gauge.

## 3. Composition identities, including arbitrary PSD child remainders

These identities are rederived from the Q definition and coincide with the
proofs of Zhang--Jiang, arXiv:2410.12395v2, Theorems3.1/3.2. Their exact
local paper, definitions, and both proofs were reread. No external result
with unexamined hypotheses is needed for the algebra below.

Primitive join. Let a,b be primitive, A=1+sum a, C=1+sum b. Let d>0 solve

 d(A+C+d)=AC; T=A+C+d, kappa=(T/C)^2.

Form h=(a,1+d,b). Let p be the bridge query and z the terminal query, and
let j range over the nonterminal queries in b. Direct expansion gives

 V_h=V_a+kappa V_b-(kappa-1)[sum_j b_j Q_(j,p)+Q_(z,p)
                                  +d Q_(p,z)+sum_j b_j Q_(j,z)]. (3)

One way to audit all coefficients is to call the bracket C_aux; its value
part is 2sum_j b_j f_j+(d-C)f_p+(2-C-d)f_z, and its gradient part is

 sum_j b_j(1-b_j)||g_j||^2+[(C-d)/2-d^2]||g_p||^2
                                          +(C+d)||g_z||^2/2.

Insert these in (3), and use (kappa-1)(C-d)=2(A+d), kappa d^2=A^2,
kappa C^2=T^2. The mixed terms cancel. Since C>d and kappa>1, every
bracket coefficient is nonnegative. Child certificates with matrices M_a,
M_b produce the FULL parent remainder M_a+kappa M_b on disjoint original
child-gradient sets. They may have arbitrary PSD rank. Its mass is

 T=Omega(A,C)=(A+C+sqrt((A+C)^2+4AC))/2.

Dominant join. Define, for weights u_i>=0 of mass D=2sum h+1,

 J_(h,u)=||x_0||^2+2sum_i u_i Q_(i,star)-2D f_z
                              -||x_0-sum_i u_i g_i||^2.

Dominance means J>=0 on every legal run; it implies W(h)<=1/D by Q_i*<=0.
The empty word has u=1 and J=0. A primitive word is dominant with
u=(h,s+1), because expanding the last square gives J=V_h exactly.
For a primitive left child of mass A, and a dominant right child of mass D
and weights v, put

 mu=2A/D, r=(1+sqrt(1+8A/D))/2, gamma=A+1, beta=1+A/r.

The parent word is (a,beta,b). Its weights are u=(a,gamma,r v), all
nonnegative, of total G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2=Dr^2. Its identity is

 J_parent=V_a+r^2 J_right-2mu sum_(i>p) v_i Q_(i,p).             (4)

To verify the equality expand both sides. The value flow uses
mu D=(sum a)+gamma=2A. The gradient coefficients reduce to
(sum a)(sum a+1)+mu D+gamma=gamma^2,
r^2=r+mu, and r^2 beta=mu+gamma r; these cancel every mixed term and
leave the defining parent square. This proves (4), including empty
children. It proves exactly the ConPD rule in accepted benchmark notation.

## 4. A finite seed threshold that compares the ORIGINAL exact B_n

Let lambda=1+sqrt(2), rho=log_2(lambda), q=1/rho. Suppose an actual
nonnegative primitive word a has length r_seed and A_seed=1+sum a. Put
m_seed=r_seed+1. The sufficient target condition is

                       A_seed>m_seed^rho.                      (5)

A gain merely above C_(r_seed) does not imply (5).
Here are the full amplification argument and the parameter losses.
First Omega(x,y)^q<=x^q+y^q for x,y>=0. For positive arguments use
x=exp(u-t), y=exp(u+t), t>=0. It becomes J(t)>=0 where

 J(t)=q^(-1)log(2cosh(qt))-arsinh(cosh t).

J(0)=0 and J(t) tends to zero at infinity. Its derivative has the sign
of qt-alpha(t), where alpha=artanh(sinh(t)/sqrt(1+cosh(t)^2)). Direct
differentiation gives alpha'=cosh(t)/sqrt(1+cosh(t)^2), strictly increasing
from 1/sqrt(2) to1. Also 1/sqrt(2)<q<1: lambda>2 and lambda^3<16 imply
1>q>3/4>1/sqrt(2). Thus alpha-qt starts by decreasing, has strictly
increasing derivative, and tends to infinity; it crosses zero once on
t>0. Therefore J first increases and then decreases to zero, proving the
inequality. Zero arguments follow directly from Omega(x,0)=x.

Induction on each primitive binary tree now gives C_k<= (k+1)^rho.
Unrolling a maximizing dominant tree, its primitive side branches have
leaf counts l_1,...,l_t summing to n. Since G(A,D)<=D+4A,

 B_n<=1+4sum l_i^rho<=1+4n^rho.

Balanced primitive trees give C_(2^k-1)=lambda^k, by the preceding upper
bound and Omega(A,A)=lambda A. Hence B_(2^k)>=G(lambda^k,1)>=2lambda^k.
The number K=limsup B_n/n^rho thus satisfies 2<=K<=4. No phase limit is
assumed and this is the ORIGINAL exact DP sequence.

Take a fully expanded optimizing dominant tree at length n, with smallest
maximizing split as deterministic tie rule. It has exactly n primitive
empty leaves and one final dominant empty leaf: induction on the unique
right dominant chain proves this count. Replace every primitive empty
leaf by a and recompute all physical bridges by (3)-(4). Leave the final
dominant empty leaf unchanged. The actual resulting word H_n has length
m_seed n and is dominant. Homogeneity of Omega makes each primitive mass
exactly A_seed times its former mass.

Let D_n=2sum H_n+1. In an auxiliary scalar evaluation also change the
terminal dominant mass from1 to A_seed. Homogeneity of G makes that
auxiliary root A_seed B_n. Accepted0be8b54e0a33381c proves
sqrt(G(A,d))=(sqrt(d)+sqrt(d+8A))/2 and that this is increasing and
1-Lipschitz as a function of sqrt(d). Propagating the unchanged terminal
leaf discrepancy therefore gives

 sqrt(A_seed B_n)-(sqrt(A_seed)-1)<=sqrt(D_n)<=sqrt(A_seed B_n). (6)

Choose n_j with B_(n_j)/n_j^rho tending to K. Equation(6) gives
D_(n_j)/n_j^rho tending to A_seed K, whereas by the SAME global limsup
limsup B_(m_seed n_j)/(m_seed n_j)^rho<=K. Consequently

 limsup_j B_(m_seed n_j) W_(m_seed n_j)(H_(n_j))
                           <= m_seed^rho/A_seed <1.            (7)

For delta=(1-m_seed^rho/A_seed)/2>0, every sufficiently large output
horizon in this subsequence has ratio <=1-delta. This is a fixed relative
all-function upper separation and suffices to refute the original uniform
asymptotic matching claim, conditional on the actual certified seed.
The unused dominant leaf and its O(sqrt(B_n)) mass loss are explicit.

## 5. Before-solve design, calibration signs, and scope

The new discovery lane searches length15 only, with every coordinate free
and fixed capacity A_target=(1+eta)lambda^4, initially eta=1/1000. The
known Silver word has length15 and exactly lambda^4 capacity, so (5) has
zero baseline threshold gap. Source order, unequal step magnitudes, and the
full all-pair sensitivity guide proposals; no symmetry or tensor class is
imposed. Length4 is used only for two exact model calibrations.

Calibration expected signs BEFORE any solve:
* h=(1,2,1,1) has min V=0. Its nonzero lambda entries are 01:2,10:4,
  21:3,31:3,41:3,14:3,23:8,32:16,34:35,43:48,24:3. Expansion gives
  M=|g0-g1|^2+4|g2-g3|^2+16|g3-g4|^2. Huber attains0.
* h=(3,1,1,1) is nonprimitive. Use x=(1,-2,-3/2,-1,-1/2),
  g=(1,-1/2,-1/2,-1/2,-1/2), f_i=g_i x_i-g_i^2/2. This is the
  convex1-smooth function with derivative clipped to[-1/2,1]. Direct
  substitution gives V=-45/4 and sum||g_i||^2=2. The trace-one model
  therefore has min V<=-45/8. Every actual query and optimum Q<=0.
* The full exact length15 Silver word has min V=0 by (3), starting with
  empty leaves. Its full nonnegative array is generated by (3), with
  identically zero PSD remainder. Its e kernel is not made strict.

The primal objective is NOT normalized objective error. Only an exactly
reconstructed nonnegative certificate satisfying (1) and (5), followed by
(3)-(7), could settle the original negative route. Solver feasibility,
positive residual tolerances, clipped eigenvalues, or a finite capacity
gain below (5) do not do so. All original statuses and raw primal/dual
arrays must be retained. The allowance is at most72 evaluations,120 measured
build-plus-solve seconds,n<=15,40 distinct nonbaseline words. No old budget
is renewed and no verifier call is made.

it does not assume the remaining thirteen-band estimates.

## 1. Definitions and the coefficient that is being estimated

Fix an integer m>=128 and keep epsilon=1/m fixed throughout. Set

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
 d_k=1+a*c^k  (k>=0), H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j).

The extension of d_k past m-1 is only a coefficient device. The actual
queried word is H_m with its last d_0 removed. Write h_i for its steps,
s_i=sum_(r<i)h_r, and s'=s_i+h_i when discussing a single step.

On the infinite original ruler word define B_00=1 and

 B_(i+1),k=(1-h_i/d_k)B_ik+(h_i/d_(k-1))B_i,(k-1),

with a zero second term at k=0. For each occupied state k, h_i<=d_k:
the first occurrence of d_j kills state j, and all smaller states have
already died. This also proves B_ik>=0, sum_k B_ik=1, and
B_ik=0 for i>=2^k or k>i.

For arbitrary formal vectors y_k put g_i=sum_k v_ik*y_k, where
v_ik=B_ik/d_k. The row-finite symmetric matrix E is defined by

 sum_(k,l)E_kl<y_k,y_l>
 =sum_i [2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
       +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].   (1)

Each coefficient is a finite sum: a term containing state k occurs by
the step immediately before query2^k. In particular E_kl=0 for k<l
and l>2^k. The m-principal block is the actual finite residual kernel.
The coefficient convention in (1) means that an off-diagonal entry
appears twice in the quadratic form.

## 2. Two elementary bounds for the actual chronological word

First, 2<c<3 and 1<d_0<2. Also

                         d_(k+1)>2d_k  (k>=2).            (2)

Indeed d_(k+1)-2d_k=(c-2)a*c^k-1. At k=2 the quantity
before subtracting1 is (1-epsilon)c(c-2), and

 c(c-2)=1+2lambda(lambda-1)epsilon+lambda^2 epsilon^2
        >1+6epsilon.

Consequently (1-epsilon)c(c-2)>1+5epsilon-6epsilon^2>1.
The expression increases with k, proving (2).

Second, every original physical step satisfies

                             h_i<s_i+2.                  (3)

Let S_j=sum H_j and C_j=S_j+2-d_j. Then C_0=2-d_0>0.
The recurrences S_(j+1)=2S_j+d_j and
d_(j+1)=c*d_j-(c-1) give the exact identity

 C_(j+1)=2C_j+(3-c)(d_j-1)>0.

The prefix before the FIRST d_j is H_j, so (3) holds there. Every later
occurrence has a larger elapsed clock and the same step size. This proves
(3) at every position, without changing the enclosing epsilon.

## 3. Nonnegative off-diagonal entries, term by term

For a fixed step h=h_i, write v_k=v_ik and v_(-1)=0. The scaled birth
recurrence is

 v'_k=v_k+(h/d_k)(v_(k-1)-v_k).

For k<l, expansion of that step's contribution to E_kl gives exactly

 C_kl*v_k*v_l
 +[s'h^2(d_l-1)/(d_k*d_l)]v_(k-1)*v_l
 +[s'h^2(d_k-1)/(d_k*d_l)]v_k*v_(l-1)
 +[s'h^2/(d_k*d_l)]v_(k-1)*v_(l-1),                     (4)

where

 C_kl=h[2s'+1-h-s'h(1/d_k+1/d_l-1/(d_k*d_l))].           (5)

To check (4), the first term of (1) contributes
s'h(v'_k*v_l+v_k*v'_l), the second contributes
s'(v'_k-v_k)(v'_l-v_l), and the third contributes
h(1-h)v_k*v_l. Expanding these three expressions gives (4)-(5).

The last three coefficients in (4) are nonnegative. Suppose k>=2.
If v_k*v_l=0, the possibly signed coefficient C_kl costs nothing.
Otherwise state k is occupied, so h<=d_k. Equation (2) gives
d_l>=d_(k+1)>2d_k and hence

 h(1/d_k+1/d_l-1/(d_k*d_l))<3/2.

It follows from (3) that

 C_kl>h(s'/2+1-h)=(h/2)(s_i+2-h)>0.                     (6)

Thus every physical step contributes a nonnegative amount to E_kl
when 2<=k<l. This proof keeps the signed terms of the original step
until they combine into C_kl; it does not take their absolute values.

For k=0,1, support leaves only E_01 and E_12. The first two steps,
whose unscaled state vectors are successively V_0,V_1,V_2, give

 E_01=(d_0-1)/d_1>0,
 E_12=(d_0+d_1)(d_1-1)/(d_1*d_2)>0.

These calculations and (4)-(6) prove

                    E_kl>=0 for every k!=l.              (7)

In particular the actual second-neighbor weights obey e_0=e_1=0 and

                    e_k=E_(k,k+2)>0 for k>=2.             (8)

For strictness, just before the first d_k both B_ik and B_i,(k+1)
are positive when k>=2. For B_ik, use the path that takes a birth on
each of its first k steps and then stays. All those birth probabilities
are positive, and every subsequent step before the first d_k is smaller
than d_k. For B_i,(k+1), take the first k+1 births and then stay; this
is possible because k+1<=2^k-1, and all later pre-d_k steps are smaller
than d_(k+1). At the d_k step, the third term in (4) with l=k+2 is
strictly positive: s'>0, d_k>1, v_k>0, v_(k+1)>0. This proves (8).

No uniform lower bound such as e_k>=1/15 is proved by this strictness
argument: the displayed positive path probabilities have not been
estimated uniformly.

## 4. Exact consequences for the unresolved row margins

For all nonnegative indices define

 A_i=E_(i,i+1), e_i=E_(i,i+2),
 b_i=A_i-2(e_(i-1)+e_i),
 u_i=E_ii-A_(i-1)-A_i+e_(i-2)+e_i
                         -sum_(|l-i|>=3)|E_il|,

with negative subscripts equal to zero. Let F_i=sum_l E_il be the
finite unweighted row sum, and ellhat_i=sum_l E_il*d_l the constant
load obtained by polarizing (1) against the constant gradient.

Equation (7) removes all absolute values from the far off-diagonal
sum. Therefore the exact full-row identity is

                     u_i=2E_ii+2(e_(i-2)+e_i)-F_i.         (9)

In particular a proof of u_i does not need to identify alternating
signs of individual far entries. It still needs signed cancellation
between the diagonal, the neighboring entries, and the row sum.
Nonnegative entries do not imply either b_i>=2/15 or u_i>=0.

This does not discard a terminal coefficient. In the inherited finite
decomposition, the triple starting at m-2 remains the square
e_(m-2)||y_(m-2)+2y_(m-1)||^2. Its coefficient now has the sign in (8).
The last diagonal remains

 u_(m-1)+sum_(l>=m+2)E_(m-1,l)+b_(m-1)+e_(m-1).

Neither its required quantitative lower bound nor the completed
constant-column remainder follows from (7) alone.

## 5. A scalar constant-load formula with the signed difference retained

For this section all sums run over the infinite coefficient word, but
every state-specific sum is finite. Set

 mu_ik=h_i B_ik/d_k,
 L_k=sum_(r=0)^k d_r,
 M_k=sum_i h_i*mu_ik,
 N_k=sum_i s_(i+1)*h_i*mu_ik,

and put M_(-1)=N_(-1)=0. The flow equation is
B_(i+1),k-B_ik=mu_i,(k-1)-mu_ik. Summing it proves
sum_i mu_ik=1 for each transient state. Weighting it by s_(i+1)
and summing by parts gives

 sum_i s_(i+1)(mu_ik-mu_i,(k-1))=sum_i h_i B_ik=d_k.

Starting with a zero predecessor moment shows
sum_i s_(i+1)mu_ik=L_k. Thus M_k and N_k are respectively the mean
exit step and the mean product of exit clock and exit step for state k.

Polarizing (1) against the constant gradient gives

 ellhat_k=sum_i h_i[(s_i+1)v_ik+s_(i+1)v_(i+1),k].         (10)

For example, the first term in (1) contributes
s'h(v_ik+v_(i+1),k), its increment-square term contributes zero,
and its last term contributes h(1-h)v_ik. Their sum is (10).
Substitute the birth recurrence into (10), then use the two occupation
identities just proved. The result is

             ellhat_k=2L_k+1-M_k-(N_k-N_(k-1))/d_k.        (11)

In detail, before the recurrence contribution the sum is
2L_k+1-M_k. The remaining term is
sum_i s'h_i^2(v_i,(k-1)-v_ik)/d_k
=(N_(k-1)-N_k)/d_k. This checks its sign and its denominator.

Formula (11) is an identity, not a new condition replacing the load
inequalities. It identifies the chronological mixed moment that must
be estimated. Bounding N_k and N_(k-1) separately loses the signed
quantity needed for the desired 2d_k<=ellhat_k<=11d_k/4.

## 6. An exact reduction that distinguishes the original lower-level order

Put t=d_0, ell=c-1, gamma=ell-t, and

 Z(z)=c*z/(1+ell*z),
 A(z)=(1-t*z)(1+ell*z)=1+gamma*z-t*ell*z^2.

These are new scalar functions, unrelated to the adjacent entries A_i.
They are well-defined at every nonnegative reciprocal physical node.
The affine-geometric node relation gives

 (1-t*z)(1-d_(j+1)*z)=A(z)(1-d_j*Z(z)),
 Z(1/d_(j+1))=1/d_j.                                    (12)

Write the original infinite step word in consecutive pairs. The exact
pair at position r is (t,d_(nu_2(r+1)+1)), where nu_2 is the exponent
of2 in a positive integer. After removing every t and lowering the
remaining level by1, the compressed word is the same original ruler
word, with the SAME epsilon. For its first r steps write
P_r(z)=product_(i<r)(1-h_i*z) and s_r=sum_(i<r)h_i. Then

 P_(2r)(z)=A(z)^r P_r(Z(z)),
 P_(2r+1)(z)=(1-t*z)A(z)^r P_r(Z(z)),
 s_(2r)=c*s_r-gamma*r,
 s_(2r+1)=c*s_r-gamma*r+t.                               (13)

All four identities follow by multiplying or summing the individual
pairs in (12). This is a chronological identity, not an identity of
the full multiset alone. The foil that exchanges the third and fourth
steps destroys the displayed consecutive-pair description.

The Newton factors also transform exactly:

 phi_(k+1)(z)=(1-t*z)(1+ell*z)^k phi_k(Z(z)),              (14)

where phi_k(z)=product_(j<k)(1-d_j*z). At epsilon=0, interpreted only
as a coefficient limit, t=ell=sqrt(2), gamma=0, and A(z)=1-2z^2.
At every actual epsilon>0 the linear term gamma*z and the clock defect
-gamma*r in (13) must both be retained. In fact

 gamma=lambda*epsilon+2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]>0.

Equations (12)-(14) do not yet establish a bound for E or the mixed
moments in (11). They give an exact original-order transformation in
which those estimates can be pursued without replacing an embedded
block's parameters by epsilon=1/j.

## 7. Scope and remaining work

The new proved-in-draft part of the stated interface is e_i>=0 for
every required index. The stronger entrywise result (7) and the
identities (9), (11), and (13) have explicit proofs above.

The unresolved claims remain b_i>=2/15, u_i>=0, the quantitative
e_i>=1/15 and u_i>=1/16 at the required terminal indices, and the
two-sided constant-load bounds. This document does not prove the full
kernel positive semidefinite, and it is not a counterexample to those
remaining actual-word claims. Even their proof would only concern the
specified reciprocal-level temporal quotient, not arbitrary legal GD.

The existing same-multiset foil is still a useful warning: its first
few steps also satisfy h_i<s_i+2, and entrywise off-diagonal positivity
alone does not distinguish its negative diagonal-margin behavior.
Thus (7) must not be promoted into a substitute for the original-order
estimates. The exact pair identity (13), unlike that coarse envelope,
does distinguish the original word.

evidence:
# The fixed common-prefix law fails for every positive amplitude history

Status: **complete joint candidate, UNVERIFIED**. This continues the eighth
max4 assignment. No solver, parameter sweep, installation, or fact submission
is used. The only correctness predecessors are accepted facts
`1252b8823bb5a290` (original smooth-convex interpolation) and
`b98bb807d514e80d` (the exact benchmark and its elementary bound). All other
arguments used here are supplied within this document. In particular the
earlier named-amplitude obstruction is not a predecessor.

The amplitudes below are arbitrary positive numbers. They may depend on the
entire known chronological history, the enclosing horizon, and the full word.
No two copies of a subword are assumed to have matching amplitude profiles.

## 1. Statement, unchanged word, and every probability atom

Fix an integer m >= 1024. Define

    sigma = 1+sqrt(2), delta = 1-1/m,
    c_chr = sigma(1+1/m), a_chr = delta/c_chr,
    N = 2^m, n = N-1, epsilon = 1/N, eta = 1/N^2,
    l = 1+a_chr, k = 1+delta.

The actual word is H_chr,0 empty and

    H_chr,j+1 = (H_chr,j, 1+a_chr*c_chr^j, H_chr,j), 0 <= j < m.

Thus h_i = 1+a_chr*c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0 <= i < n, where nu_2(q)
is the exponent of 2 dividing the positive integer q. Every subword retains
the same enclosing-m parameters. There are n physical steps and N samples.

Give sample i its standard m-bit binary label (i_0,...,i_(m-1)). For
s in {0,1}^m define

    chi_s(i) = (-1)^(sum_j s_j i_j),
    B(s) = (-1)^s_0,
    C_j(s) = (-1)^(s_1+...+s_j), 1 <= j < m.

These are real signs. The map from s to (B,C_1,...,C_(m-1)) is bijective:
(-1)^s_1=C_1 and (-1)^s_j=C_(j-1)C_j for j>=2. Put

    mu_+ = -7/10, mu_- = 9/10, p_chr = 1-epsilon,

    A_b(c_1,...,c_(m-1))
      = (1+mu_b)/2 * 1_(all c_j=1)
          + (1-mu_b)/2 * 1_(all c_j=-1),
    P_b(c_1,...,c_(m-1)) = product_j (1+mu_b*c_j)/2,

    w_s = (1+p_chr*B(s))/2
             * [(1-eta) A_(B(s))(C_1(s),...,C_(m-1)(s))
                     + eta P_(B(s))(C_1(s),...,C_(m-1)(s))].       (1)

Each conditional law sums to one. Every atom is strictly positive because
epsilon,eta>0 and both conditional means lie strictly between -1 and 1.
This is exactly the assigned finite probability law.

For ANY positive amplitudes Gamma_0,...,Gamma_n, prescribe

    g_i = (Gamma_i*sqrt(w_s)*chi_s(i))_s, 0 <= i <= n.              (2)

Suppose these are the actual gradients of ONE finite-dimensional convex
differentiable 1-smooth function F with a minimizer, along its actual GD:

    X_(i+1) = X_i-h_i*g_i, g_i = grad F(X_i), 0 <= i <= n,

where only i<n is used in the recursion. The same assertion covers any
Euclidean realization of the Gram matrix in (2). The anchor, function, and
values are unrestricted apart from these requirements. Define

    R = dist(X_0,argmin F), F_star = min F,
    V_chr = 2(F(X_n)-F_star)/R^2,
    T_path = sum_(i<n) h_i*Gamma_i.

Then R>0, and the claimed bounds are

    T_path < 800 R,                                         (3)
    ||X_i-X_star|| <= 129 R for every i,                     (4)
    Gamma_n <= R[(3/5)^(N/8)+2^23/N^2],                     (5)
    V_chr <= 512(3/5)^(N/8)+2^32/N^2.                       (6)

Here X_star is a true closest minimizer. Since the exact original benchmark
obeys B_n <= 1+4*n^p, p=log_2(3), by fact `b98bb807d514e80d`,

    B_n V_chr <= (1+4*n^p)[512(3/5)^((n+1)/8)
                                      +2^32/(n+1)^2] -> 0.     (7)

The bounds are uniform over ALL positive amplitudes and all actual legal
realizations of (2). They concern this fixed witness class, not unrestricted
W_n(h). Failure on these original dyadic words prevents this class from
establishing the all-schedule matching lower bound. It does not decide the
project's minimax question.

For L-smooth functions, take F=f/L and g_i=grad f(X_i)/L. The same proof then
uses the required normalization 2(f(X_n)-f_star)/(L R^2).

## 2. Necessary original inequalities and short-step consequences

The set of minimizers is nonempty and closed. A bounded minimizing sequence
for distance from X_0 has a convergent subsequence, so a closest minimizer
X_star exists. Positive Gamma_0 implies X_0 is not a minimizer, hence R>0.

Write f_i=F(X_i)-F_star. Accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290` supplies all
original ordered inequalities, including the optimum:

    Q_ij = f_i-f_j + <g_i,X_j-X_i> + ||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <= 0.

Adding the two orientations gives

    ||g_i-g_j||^2 <= <g_i-g_j,X_i-X_j>.                         (8)

In particular <g_i,X_i-X_star> >= ||g_i||^2. Norms in (2) are exactly
Gamma_i. Smoothness and grad F(X_star)=0 also give
Gamma_i <= ||X_i-X_star||. For a physical step 0<h<=2, (8) gives

    ||X_(i+1)-X_star||^2
       <= ||X_i-X_star||^2-h(2-h)||g_i||^2,
    ||g_(i+1)|| <= ||g_i||.                                  (9)

For the second assertion, put d=g_(i+1)-g_i. Then
-h<d,g_i> >= ||d||^2, and expansion of ||g_i+d||^2 gives an increment
at most (1-2/h)||d||^2 <= 0. These facts will only be applied to the
explicit short physical steps l,k,l, all strictly between 0 and 2.

We will use the following rational bounds:

    7/5 < l < 3/2, 1 < k < 2, delta*c_chr < 5/2,
    epsilon < 1/65536, eta < 1/65536,
    p_chr >= 999/1000.                                      (10)

For example sqrt(2)<99/70 by squaring, so
c_chr<(169/70)(1025/1024)<49/20. Also delta>99/100, giving
delta/c_chr>(99/100)/(49/20)>2/5; c_chr>2 gives the upper bound on l.
Finally delta*c_chr=sigma(1-1/m^2)<sigma<5/2. The bounds on epsilon,eta
follow from m>=1024. No decimal approximation is needed.

## 3. A uniform movement bound before taking any small-mixture estimate

Select in (1) the component B=1 and all prefix signs common. Its mass is

    lambda = (1-epsilon/2)(1-eta), omega = 1-lambda.

Conditional on it, the only variable sign is C_1, with mean -7/10; all
character bits except s_1 are zero. Thus its unit sample directions are
two unit vectors a_0,b_0, in the exact period a_0,a_0,b_0,b_0, with
<a_0,b_0>=-beta_0, beta_0=7/10. The remaining measure has mass omega.
In a direct-sum Euclidean realization of the SAME Gram matrix,

    g_i = Gamma_i (sqrt(lambda)*u_i, sqrt(omega)*z_i),
    u_i in {a_0,b_0}, ||z_i||=1.                             (11)

Splitting a probability mixture proves this representation directly. An
isometry of gradient spans, extended to the initial displacement and any
orthogonal component, preserves every scalar product and the initial
distance. Thus it is legitimate for every realization in the statement.

Fix a block start t=4r, 0<=r<N/4. Before t put

    P_a = sum_(j<t,u_j=a_0) h_j*Gamma_j,
    P_b = sum_(j<t,u_j=b_0) h_j*Gamma_j, T=P_a+P_b.

Translate X_star to zero. If X_0=(x^c,x^r), then

    X_t = (x^c-sqrt(lambda)(P_a*a_0+P_b*b_0),
                         x^r-sqrt(omega)*W), ||W||<=T.

Define normalized coarse coordinates

    A_x = <a_0,x^c>/sqrt(lambda)-P_a+beta_0*P_b,
    B_x = <b_0,x^c>/sqrt(lambda)-P_b+beta_0*P_a.

The first two steps in the block have sizes l,k and both coarse directions
a_0. Their total amplitude-weighted mass is

    D_a = l*Gamma_t+k*Gamma_(t+1)>0.

Their displacement is (sqrt(lambda)*D_a*a_0,sqrt(omega)*Z), ||Z||<=D_a.
Both are short steps. The two distance inequalities in (9), added or
applied successively, therefore give

    lambda*D_a^2
       <= 2 lambda*D_a*A_x
            +2 sqrt(omega)(R+sqrt(omega)*T)*D_a.

With e=omega/lambda and r_0=sqrt(omega)*R/lambda, division gives

    D_a <= 2 A_x+2(r_0+eT).                                 (12)

At sample t+2 the coarse gradient direction is b_0. Its optimum
inequality <g_(t+2),X_(t+2)> >= ||g_(t+2)||^2 > 0 implies, after
bounding the remainder component by its norm,

    B_x+(beta_0+e)D_a+r_0+eT >= 0.

Substitution of (12), with positive coefficient beta_0+e, yields

    B_x+2(beta_0+e)A_x+[1+2(beta_0+e)](r_0+eT) >= 0.          (13)

Here omega<=epsilon/2+eta<1/65536, so

    e<1/1000, 1/sqrt(lambda)<1001/1000,
    sqrt(omega)/lambda<1/255.

Expanding (13) gives a bound on the nonnegative masses:

    c_a P_a+c_b P_b
       <= <b_0+2(beta_0+e)a_0,x^c>/sqrt(lambda)
                           +[1+2(beta_0+e)]r_0,

    c_a = beta_0+(1-2beta_0)e-2e^2,
    c_b = 1-2beta_0^2-(1+4beta_0)e-2e^2.                    (14)

Both coefficients exceed 1/64: their lower bounds at 0<=e<=1/1000
are 699598/1000000 and 16198/1000000. Also

    ||b_0+2(beta_0+e)a_0||^2 = 1+4e(beta_0+e)
                                      < (1002/1000)^2,
    1+2(beta_0+e)<5/2.

The right side of (14) is less than
[(1002/1000)(1001/1000)+(5/2)/255]R < 2R. Therefore

    T < 128 R at EVERY block start.                         (15)

This bound has been derived with arbitrary amplitudes still present; no
bounded-amplitude hypothesis or conditioning assumption has been imposed.
At a block start ||X_t||<=R+T<=129R. Its three short steps l,k,l preserve
this bound by (9). These blocks cover every sample 0,...,n, proving (4).
Every Gamma_i<=129R as well. At the last block the mass added after its
start is at most (2l+k)129R<5*129R. Thus

    T_path < (128+645)R < 800R,
    K_path := R+T_path < 1024R.                             (16)

In particular every gradient norm and every subinterval's total mass is
bounded by K_path. This estimate precedes the perturbation argument below.

## 4. Keep the finite epsilon component exactly: four coarse directions

Now split (1) in a DIFFERENT way: keep the whole common-prefix component,
of mass 1-eta, and regard only the conditional-product component of mass
eta as the remainder. In the common component write C_j=V for every j.
The four unit directions for indices modulo 4 are

    a_e=1, a_o=B, b_e=V, b_o=B V                              (17)

in the finite real probability space of (B,V). Their correlations are

    p = E B = 1-epsilon,
    z = E V = -7/10+4epsilon/5,
    w = E B V = -7/10-epsilon/10,

    <a_e,a_o>=<b_e,b_o>=p,
    <a_o,b_o>=<a_e,b_e>=z,
    <a_e,b_o>=<a_o,b_e>=w.                                 (18)

These formulas average the stated conditional means in (1). In particular
finite epsilon has NOT been replaced by zero. Put beta=-z. We have

    69/100 <= beta <= 7/10, p>0, p-z*w>0,
    1-k*z^2 >= 1-2(7/10)^2 = 1/50.                         (19)

The positivity p-zw follows already from p>=999/1000,
|z|<=7/10 and |w|<701/1000.

Let v_i denote the coarse direction (17) at sample i, and let u_i denote
its unit direction under the FULL measure (1). Splitting the probability
mixture gives, for ALL original i,j,

    |<u_i,u_j>-<v_i,v_j>| <= 2 eta.                         (20)

For a pair with amplitudes A,B and intervening total mass T_ij, replacing
all its directions by their coarse versions changes the cocoercivity
expression <g_i-g_j,X_i-X_j>-||g_i-g_j||^2 by at most

    2 eta(A+B)T_ij +4 eta A B
           <= 4 eta K_path(A+B).                           (21)

The first term comes from the actual displacement sum, one scalar product
at a time; the second comes from the cross term in the squared gradient
difference. Individual squared norms are unchanged. The final inequality
uses (16) and 2AB<=K_path(A+B). Thus (21) accounts explicitly for the
whole amplitude-weighted trajectory, rather than merely the Gram entries.

## 5. Every consecutive odd-b return can grow only by O(eta K_path)

Let j=4r+3 and suppose j+4<=n. These are consecutive odd-b samples.
Their four intervening steps and directions are

    j:     H on b_o, amplitude B_0=Gamma_j,
    j+1:   l on a_e, amplitude A_0=Gamma_(j+1),
    j+2:   k on a_o, amplitude C_0=Gamma_(j+2),
    j+3:   l on b_e, amplitude E_0=Gamma_(j+3),
    j+4:            b_o, amplitude D_0=Gamma_(j+4).

The physical H may be arbitrarily large. No amplitude ratios are imposed.
Temporarily set a=a_o, b=b_o, tau=<a,b>=z=-beta, and

    Z = -H B_0 b-l A_0 a_e,
    X = <b,Z>, Y=<a-tau*b,Z>.

By (18),(19),

    Y = -l A_0(p-z*w) <= 0.                                (22)

The ORIGINAL pair between j and j+2, together with (21), therefore gives

    C_0^2+B_0^2-2tau B_0 C_0
       <= (tau C_0-B_0)X+C_0 Y+e_0(C_0+B_0)
       <= (tau C_0-B_0)X+e_0(C_0+B_0),                     (23)

where e_0=4 eta K_path. Suppose Delta=D_0-B_0>0. The ORIGINAL pair
between j and j+4 similarly gives

    Delta[X-k C_0 tau-l E_0 p]
       >= Delta^2-e_0(D_0+B_0).

Consequently

    X >= Delta+k C_0 tau+l E_0 p-e_0(D_0+B_0)/Delta.         (24)

Substitute (24) into (23). Its coefficient tau C_0-B_0 is negative.
Putting M=B_0+beta C_0>0 gives exactly

    (1-k*tau^2)C_0^2 + tau(k-2)B_0 C_0+B_0^2
           +M Delta+M l E_0 p
       <= e_0(C_0+B_0)+M e_0(D_0+B_0)/Delta.                (25)

Every discarded term on the left is nonnegative: tau<0, k<2, p>0.
It follows from (19) that the left side is at least

    (C_0^2+B_0^2)/100 + M Delta.

On the right, D_0+B_0=Delta+2B_0, so it is at most

    e_0[(1+beta)C_0+2B_0] + (2e_0/Delta)B_0 M
       <= 4e_0 M + (3e_0/Delta)(C_0^2+B_0^2).             (26)

Here beta>=69/100 proves the first bound, and
B_0 M <= (3/2)(B_0^2+C_0^2) proves the second.
If Delta>=1024e_0, (26) is at most

    M Delta/256 + (3/1024)(C_0^2+B_0^2),

strictly less than the lower bound for (25). This is a contradiction.
Thus every such return obeys

    Gamma_(j+4) <= Gamma_j + d_amp,
    d_amp = 4096 eta K_path <= 2^22 eta R.                  (27)

This uses two pairs of ORIGINAL samples and their actual displacement
sums. The profiles on either side need not match in any way. If eta=0,
the same argument with zero error directly rules out Delta>0, so the
exact four-ray boundary has nonincreasing odd-b amplitudes.

## 6. Every other return contracts by 3/5, for the full finite measure

For any original bridge of level q>=1 and its following leaf, let the
three amplitudes be A,M,D and the two steps 1+u,l. The relative character
signs of the three samples are 1,B C_q,C_q. This follows because adding
one to an odd binary label with q trailing ones flips bits 0,...,q; the
following leaf flips bit 0 once more. Therefore the FULL law, including
its conditional-product part, gives correlations w,p,z in that order.
Both mixture components have the same individual conditional prefix mean.

The two original inequalities between the endpoints give the exact sum

    0 >= -u A^2+D^2+(u-1)z A D+l M(pD-wA).                 (28)

The following leaf is short, so (9) gives M>=D. Since p>0 and w<0,
pD-wA>0. Hence the ratio q_amp=D/A satisfies

    F_u(q_amp) <= 0,
    F_u(q) = (1+lp)q^2+[(u-1)z-lw]q-u.                    (29)

This is a necessary inequality with arbitrary adjacent slack. Its positive
leading coefficient and negative constant term give exactly one positive
root; F_u(q)<=0 for positive q places q below that root.

At level 1, u=delta<1. Bounds (10),(18) give

    1+lp >= 11993/5000,
    (u-1)z-lw >= (7/10)l >= 49/50,
    F_delta(1/2) >= 1793/20000 > 0.

Thus every low bridge followed by its leaf has gain less than 1/2.

At level 2, u=delta*c_chr lies between 1 and 5/2. Since z>=-7/10,
w<=-7/10 and l>7/5,

    (u-1)z-lw >= (7/10)(1+l-u) >= -7/100,
    F_u(6/5) >= 108748/125000 > 0.

Thus every level-2 bridge followed by its leaf has gain less than 6/5.
If the H in section 5 has level 2, its return is exactly the concatenation
of this compound step and a level-1 compound step. Therefore

    Gamma_(j+4) <= (3/5) Gamma_j at every level-2 return.    (30)

No value, anchor, copy profile, or equality assumption was used in this
calculation. The even samples and their physical leaves are retained.

## 7. The exact block count, terminal objective, and benchmark

There are K=N/4 odd-b samples. Put B_r=Gamma_(4r+3), 0<=r<K.
For 0<=r<K-1 the bridge at index 4r+3 has level

    nu_2(4r+4)=2+nu_2(r+1).

It has level 2 precisely when r is even. Since K is even, (27),(30) give

    B_(2s+1) <= theta B_(2s), theta=3/5,
    B_(2s+2) <= B_(2s+1)+d_amp,

whenever the indicated indices exist. The final return is a contraction.
Iteration of these scalar inequalities, keeping the actual K, yields

    B_(K-1) <= theta^(K/2) B_0
                   + [theta/(1-theta)] d_amp
             = theta^(N/8) B_0+(3/2)d_amp.                 (31)

The first three steps are l,k,l<2, so B_0=Gamma_3<=Gamma_0<=R.
Equations (16),(27),(31) prove (5), since
(3/2)*2^22 < 2^23 and eta=N^-2. The terminal sample is exactly
n=4(K-1)+3. Neither a discarded suffix nor a free extra terminal sample
is present.

Convexity at X_n gives

    F(X_n)-F_star <= <g_n,X_n-X_star>
                     <= 129R Gamma_n.

After division by the TRUE distance squared, this gives
V_chr<=258[(3/5)^(N/8)+2^23/N^2], which implies (6).
There is no replacement of distance by an inverse-Gram anchor norm.

For the original B_n, accepted `b98bb807d514e80d` gives (7). Its first
term tends to zero because a geometric exponential in N dominates N^p;
its second does because p=log_2(3)<2. Both limits hold uniformly over the
entire amplitude/anchor/function class. The horizon remains n=2^m-1.

## 8. The fixed finite class is nonempty

This is a nonvacuity construction, not a competitive lower witness. It also
shows that the obstruction does not mean the Gram itself is illegal.
For the SAME full-support weights (1) and the SAME actual word, put

    H_max=max_i h_i,
    kappa_chr=min(1,(min_i h_i-1)/4)>0,
    q_decay=kappa_chr/[8(H_max+kappa_chr+1)],
    Gamma_i=q_decay^i, f_i=(kappa_chr+1/2)Gamma_i^2.

All N characters are present and have positive weight, so the character
matrix is invertible. Indeed
sum_s chi_s(i)chi_s(j)=N for i=j and 0 otherwise, by pairing the sign
of a differing bit. Hence the Gram K_ij=<g_i,g_j> is positive definite.
Define

    b_i=(kappa_chr+1)Gamma_i^2+sum_(t<i)h_t K_ti,
    X_0=sum_i (K^(-1)b)_i g_i,
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t.

These finite formulas fix one anchor before GD is run. They give
<X_i,g_i>=(kappa_chr+1)Gamma_i^2. For i<j direct expansion gives

    Q_ij=(kappa_chr+1-h_i)Gamma_i^2-kappa_chr Gamma_j^2
                          -sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_it-K_ij,
    Q_ji=(kappa_chr+1)Gamma_j^2-kappa_chr Gamma_i^2
                          +(h_i-1)K_ij+sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_jt.

Using |K_it|<=Gamma_i Gamma_t, q_decay<1/2 and h_i-1>=4kappa_chr,
the first residual divided by Gamma_i^2 is at most

    -3kappa_chr+H_max*q_decay/(1-q_decay)+q_decay
       <= -3kappa_chr+2(H_max+1)q_decay
       <= -11kappa_chr/4 < 0.

The second is at most

    -kappa_chr+(kappa_chr+1)q_decay^2
                             +H_max*q_decay/(1-q_decay)
       <= -kappa_chr+(2H_max+kappa_chr+1)q_decay
       <= -3kappa_chr/4 < 0.

For the optimum jet (0,0,0), Q_(i,star)=0 and
Q_(star,i)=-kappa_chr Gamma_i^2<0. Thus ALL original ordered pairs,
including the optimum and terminal, have been checked.

For an explicit one-function realization, let

    C_poly=conv(0,g_0,...,g_n),
    F_poly(X)=max_(v in C_poly) [<X,v>-||v||^2/2].

The unique maximizer is the nearest-point projection P_(C_poly)(X).
Its normal condition is <X-P_(C_poly)(X),v-P_(C_poly)(X)><=0 for every
v in C_poly. Adding this condition at X and Y proves that the projection
is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizing expressions bounds the
first-order remainder for F_poly between 0 and ||X-Y||^2, so F_poly is
differentiable with gradient P_(C_poly), convex, finite, and 1-smooth.

At each prescribed sample the displayed residuals say
<X_i-g_i,g_j-g_i>=Q_ji<=0, and
<X_i-g_i,-g_i>=-kappa_chr Gamma_i^2<0. Thus the normal condition holds
on every vertex and their convex hull: grad F_poly(X_i)=g_i and
F_poly(X_i)=f_i. The fixed function therefore follows the stated GD.
It is nonnegative and minimized at zero. Its full minimizer set is
{Z:<Z,g_i><=0 for all i}, by the same normal condition at the zero vertex.
The true distance to this polar cone is positive and is the R used in
(3)--(7); no claim equates it with ||X_0||.

## 9. Scope and unresolved changes

The exclusion covers EVERY positive amplitude choice for (1),(2), including
unbounded, history-dependent, nonsaturating, and nonmatching choices, all
anchors and values that actually interpolate, and every m>=1024. It keeps
the B=-1 mass exactly in the return argument and pays only the product
mixture eta=N^-2 there. The separate initial mass proof pays the full
epsilon/2+eta remainder before bounding ANY amplitudes.

The same derivation also covers the exact eta=0 boundary, and epsilon=0
when considered with the same physical word: zero perturbation yields
nonincreasing returns directly. It does not assume positive definiteness
for the upper bound. Positive definiteness is used only for the separate
full-support nonvacuity example.

Different measures and different binary labels remain outside. In
particular the coercive margins 1-2*(7/10)^2 and 1-k*z^2 are essential;
a geometry at or beyond absolute ray correlation 1/sqrt(2) is not covered
by this proof. Nor does a larger arbitrary full-support component come
with a vanishing exact-B_n comparison: the estimate retains its eta term.
No claim is made about arbitrary schedules, free unprescribed terminal
gradients, or the accepted unrestricted finite H6 witness.

Matlas and web searches for long-step cone/length bounds and gradient-norm
monotonicity did not supply an applicable external theorem. The returned
short-step theorems cannot be applied to this whole word. Every short-step
fact actually used is derived above from accepted interpolation. This
remains the already audited finite interpolation regime; no additional
unread body of external theory is a premise.

The result is a full scoped OBSTRUCTION CANDIDATE, not an accepted fact.
The current assignment prohibits fact_submit. The original all-h minimax
target remains unresolved and is not finalized.

glossary.Gamma_i: Arbitrary positive norm of actual gradient at original sample i; the whole sequence may depend on the known chronological history.
glossary.w_s: The exact finite common-prefix/conditional-product character probability law in equation (1) of the evidence.
glossary.V_chr: Actual normalized terminal error 2(F(X_n)-min F)/dist(X_0,argmin F)^2 for the restricted character realization.
glossary.T_path: Total chronological amplitude-weighted mass sum_(i<n) h_i Gamma_i.
glossary.K_path: R+T_path, derived to be less than 1024R before any perturbation estimate.
glossary.R: True distance dist(X_0,argmin F), with X_star a closest minimizer.
glossary.c_chr: (1+sqrt(2))(1+1/m), held fixed through every original H_m subword.
glossary.H_chr,j: Recursive original word H_chr,0 empty and H_chr,j+1=(H_chr,j,1+a_chr c_chr^j,H_chr,j).
glossary.epsilon: The finite low-bit discrepancy 2^-m in the assigned measure.
glossary.eta: The finite full-support conditional-product mixture weight 2^-2m.
glossary.a_e, a_o, b_e, b_o: The four unit real common-prefix directions represented by 1,B,V,BV in order of the sample index modulo 4.
glossary.p, z, w: Local coarse correlations EB=1-epsilon, EV=-7/10+4epsilon/5, EBV=-7/10-epsilon/10; local p here is not the benchmark exponent, which is explicitly restated where used.
glossary.d_amp: Uniform additive growth allowance 4096 eta K_path for each consecutive odd-b return.
glossary.theta: The strict alternating return cap 3/5.
glossary.C_poly: Convex hull of zero and all prescribed gradients in the separate explicit nonvacuity example.
glossary.F_poly: The single convex 1-smooth projection-conjugate function used to realize the nonvacuity example.

evidence:
# A changed three-vector core and its next rank-one join

Status: **UNVERIFIED self-contained joint candidate**, max round 20.
This directly screens proposed continuation23ee0fbf649c851f. The assigned
fixed-child63 problem was already resolved at draft level in0f103d4354799b9e;
that unverified finding is motivation, not a premise. No new optimization,
installation, verifier call, or subagent is used here. The accepted fact
1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original Q convention and necessity only.

## 1. Exact data on the same physical three-step word

Let s=sqrt2, lambda=1+s, theta=s-1=1/lambda, and fix

    a=(311s-16)/300, b=(590+8s)/300,
    rho=599/600, eps=1/100, E=eps^2=1/10000,
    Klen=a+rho, z=b-1, m=a+b, eta=z/Klen,
    A=1+2a+b.

Take mutually orthogonal unit vectors u,v,q, and put

    U=u, V=sqrt(eta)*v, W=rho*V+eps*q.

Define the four samples by

    g_0=g_1=U, g_2=V, g_3=W,
    x_3=W, x_2=W+aV,
    x_1=W+aV+bU, x_0=W+aV+(a+b)U.                     (1)

They have precisely the word (a,b,a), the same t=1/100 word as in the
fixed-child tests. Unlike those tests, the ACTUAL vectors have changed.
The residuals y_i=x_i-g_i are

    y_0=(m-1)U+Klen V+eps*q,
    y_1=zU+Klen V+eps*q,
    y_2=(Klen-1)V+eps*q, y_3=0.

The updates follow by subtracting aU, then bU, then aV. Their squared
initial and endpoint norms are

    R^2=m^2+Klen*z+E, N=||W||^2=rho^2*eta+E.           (2)

## 2. Every seed normal, actual function, and true distance

At sample0, the normals against V and0 are -a and -(m-1).
The normal against W is -a-(1-rho)z+E. At sample1, the normals against
V and0 are0 and -z, and the normal against W is -(1-rho)z+E.
At sample2 the normals against U and0 both equal -(Klen-1)eta, and
the normal against W is -(1-rho)(Klen-1)eta+E. Normals against the
sample's own gradient vanish. At sample3 every normal vanishes because
y_3=0. This lists every vertex in conv(0,U,V,W), including duplicates.

For the two possibly delicate signs, squaring shows7/5<s<10/7, hence
139/100<a<143/100 and2<b<201/100. Therefore z>1,
Klen>238/100, Klen<243/100, and eta>2/5. Thus

    (1-rho)z>1/600>E,
    (1-rho)(Klen-1)eta>1/1500>E.

All displayed normals are nonpositive. The normal energies are
e_0=m-1>0, e_1=z>0, e_2=(Klen-1)eta>0, e_3=0.

For a complete construction, let B=conv(0,U,V,W) and define

    F(x)=max_(g in B)(<x,g>-||g||^2/2).

Completing the square identifies its unique maximizer with P_B(x).
Adding two projection optimality inequalities gives
||P_B(x)-P_B(x')||^2<=<x-x',P_B(x)-P_B(x')>, so P_B is1-Lipschitz.
Evaluation of the defining maxima at each other's maximizers yields
0<=F(x+d)-F(x)-<P_B(x),d><=||d||^2. Hence F is finite convex
differentiable and1-smooth, with gradient P_B. The normals just proved
make P_B(x_i)=g_i and fix f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2.

The original Q of fact1252b8823bb5a290 expands to
Q_ij=<g_i-g_j,y_j>; also Q_i,star=0 and Q_star,i=-e_i.
Thus every original interpolation row is checked, including the optimum0.
The minimizers of F are B^polar: sufficiency follows from the displayed
maximum; necessity follows by testing epsilon*g and sending epsilon to0.
Since x_0=W+(a+b)U+aV is a nonnegative combination of the actual gradients,
<x_0,x_star><=0 for every minimizer x_star. The closest-minimizer distance
is exactly R; the minimum is attained at0.

The core ratio is kappa=A^2 N/R^2, and it is strictly greater than
1+1/2000. Here is a purely algebraic sign check. If the q component is
omitted, let Rbar^2=m^2+Klen*z and Nbar=rho^2*eta. Direct substitution
gives

    A^2 Nbar/Rbar^2-1=(-P+Q*s)/D0,
    P=19019047380837966731,
    Q=13474265781546157318,
    D0=40842989603870102500.

The exact positive square difference is

    2(2000Q)^2-(2000P+D0)^2
       =2441206548123238434623351342332719331750000>0.

Both compared numbers are positive. Hence the ratio without q already
exceeds1+1/2000. Moreover Rbar^2>Nbar because
Rbar^2-Nbar=m^2+eta(Klen^2-rho^2)>0. Adding the same E>0 to Nbar and
Rbar^2 strictly raises their ratio. This proves the stated bound for kappa.

No nonzero-residual seed sample has gradient parallel to W: its gradient
is U or V, while W has a nonzero q component. The only gradient W occurs
at sample3, whose residual is zero. Thus this seed has NO sample
g_i=gamma W,y_i=delta W with gamma,delta>0. Its positive initial/endpoint
pairing is

    k=<x_0,W>/R^2=(rho*z+E)/R^2>0.                      (3)

It therefore escapes the endpoint-facing-sample hypothesis; it does not
escape by changing the sign of (3).

## 3. A fully legal first join without transverse correlation

Write e=W/||W|| and d=x_0/R. In
R direct-sum e^perp direct-sum d^perp define isometries

    J_L u=(<u,e>,u-<u,e>e,0),
    J_R v=(-<v,d>,0,v-<v,d>d).

The cross block is real PSD by these explicit coordinates; no rank
repair is applied. Set r_0=theta A, alpha_0=r_0||W||/R. Keep all left
data under J_L and all right data under alpha_0 J_R. The bridge1+r_0
is exact because alpha_0 J_R x_0=-r_0 J_L W.

All four seed pairing lists are nonnegative:
<g_i,W>, <y_i,W>, <x_0,g_i>, <x_0,y_i>.
For the first list, its entries are0,0,rho*eta,N. For the second, its
nonzero entries are rho*z+E,rho*z+E,rho(Klen-1)eta+E. For the last two
lists, all coordinate coefficients in the orthogonal basis (u,v,q) are
nonnegative, so the pairings are nonnegative.

Use f_i unchanged on the left and alpha_0^2 f_i on the right. For every
left residual i and every right gradient j the cross normal is

    -r_0 <W,y_i><g_j,x_0>/R^2-e_i<=0.

For every left gradient i and right residual j the other cross normal is

    -r_0 <g_i,W><x_0,y_j>/R^2-alpha_0^2 e_j<=0.

These cover the complete cross lists, including the bridge endpoint.
Within-child and optimum normals are inherited, with the right ones
scaled by alpha_0^2. Taking the convex hull of0 and ALL parent gradients
and applying the explicitly proved projection construction gives an
actual common function for the seven-step word

    h[1]=(a,b,a,1+r_0,a,b,a).

Its true initial distance remains R, since the retained left gradients
still positively generate the initial point. Its capacity is lambda A
and its endpoint norm is alpha_0||W||. Because
r_0*(lambda A)=A^2, its core ratio is kappa^2>1. This verifies the
first join at proof-draft level with a real function, not just a PSD Gram.

## 4. Exact failure of the next unchanged rank-one operation

Let w_1 be the endpoint of this actual seven-step child. Its two boundary
quantities at child indices2 and1 respectively are

    a2_child=<g_2,w_1>/||w_1||^2
        =-[k/(r_0 zeta)] aV,
    zeta=N/R^2, aV=<V,W>/N=rho*eta/N,
    D1_child=<x_0,y_1>/e_1=m+Klen+E/z.                  (4)

The first identity follows by substituting the explicit rank-one cross
block in section3 and ||w_1||^2=r_0^2 N^2/R^2. The second identity uses
the retained left copy: <x_0,y_1>=z(m+Klen)+E and e_1=z.

At the next balanced join, r_1=theta*(lambda A)=A. Let alpha_1 be its
positive right-child scale. Left vertex2 and right residual1 have original
parent indices2 and8+1=9. The original cross interpolation row equals

    Q_(2,9)=alpha_1^2 e_1 [Charge_15-1],
    Charge_15=[k/(r_0 zeta)] aV D1_child/A.              (5)

Both2 and9 are queried indices in the proposed15-step parent. This row
cannot be discarded as an unqueried-terminal incoming inequality.

The quantity in brackets is strictly positive. Substituting the exact
constants gives

    Charge_15-1=(-P15+Q15*s)/D15,
    P15=62679865992522500222116809754931367,
    Q15=44355009819493057998585531075725000,
    D15=41805029741611646378138793800301367.

All three integers are positive, and

    2 Q15^2-P15^2
       =5968191334072563126460341778961364339118130652105277351376369511311>0.

Thus Q_(2,9)>0 in this specified second rank-one join, even though both
seven-step children are actual legal positive-defect instances. This is
an exact original-row obstruction, not a floating infeasibility flag.
