## 4. An actual seven-step parent with the residual retained

Choose r_0=theta*A>2. For any r>1 the true outgoing vector is

    d_r=v-rw=-r*rho*V+((1-r)eps/2)*q_axis,
    Z(r)=||d_r||^2=r^2*Nbar+(r-1)^2*E/4.                 (17)

Every seed gradient and residual has nonnegative coordinates in
(u,v_axis,q_axis), and d_r has nonpositive coordinates. Moreover
<x_0,g_i> and <x_0,y_i> are nonnegative. Both inequalities(8L),(8R)
hold for every pair at r=r_0: their left sides are nonpositive and their
right sides are nonnegative. This includes i=3 or j=3, so the actual
queried joining gradient and its nonzero residual are checked.

Set alpha_0^2=Z(r_0)/R^2 and use the explicit embeddings(6). The convex
hull construction is one actual smooth convex function for

    h[1]=(a,b,a,1+r_0,a,b,a).                             (18)

Its closest distance is R by the retained cone representation(14).
Its terminal data are

    w_1=alpha_0*J_R w, v_1=alpha_0*J_R v,
    J_1=alpha_0^2*J, A_1=lambda*A.

The nonzero terminal residual survives in the parent. Every left e_i is
retained and every right e_i is multiplied by alpha_0^2; none is deleted.

For this seed put tau=E/(4N). Equation(15) gives nu=tau, and the terminal
shape is invariant under the right-copy scaling. Since Nbar>39/100 and
E<=1/10000, one has

    0<tau<1/15000.

On the formal balanced word recurrence

    A_j=lambda^j*A, r_j=theta*A_j,
    h[j+1]=(h[j],1+r_j,h[j]),

the unchanged construction, if legal, would have exactly

    kappa_N,j+1=(1-2tau/r_j+tau/r_j^2)*kappa_N,j^2,
    kappa_E,j=(1+2tau)*kappa_N,j,
    kappa_E,j+1=[(1-2tau/r_j+tau/r_j^2)/(1+2tau)]
                    *kappa_E,j^2.                       (19)

Here kappa_N,j=A_j^2*||w_j||^2/R^2 and
kappa_E,j=A_j^2*J_j/R^2. For r_j>1 the first factor in the first line
exceeds1-tau. Thus the scalar energy calculation alone stays positive:

    kappa_N,j >= (1-tau)^(2^j-1)*kappa_N,0^(2^j)>1,       (20)

because(1-1/15000)(1+1/2000)>1. Equations(19)-(20) do NOT supply
legality at j>=2. The next sections exhibit the missing original rows.
They explain why the scalar surplus cannot be interpreted as a parent.

## 5. The next specified rank-one join fails at queried rows

Retain the actual seven-step child(18), including its specified first
embeddings and values. Its initial point is the retained left p=x_0,
with norm R. The next balanced bridge has r_1=theta*A_1=A. Abbreviate

    Z0=Z(r_0), Z1=Z(r_1), D=m+Klen=A-delta,
    H0=r_0*rho*z+(r_0-1)E/2,
    H1=r_1*rho*z+(r_1-1)E/2.

The true outgoing vector of the seven-step child is

    d_1=v_1-r_1*w_1=alpha_0*J_R d_(r_1),
    ||d_1||^2=alpha_0^2*Z1,
    alpha_1^2=||d_1||^2/R^2.                             (21)

The prospective fifteen-step parent has eight samples from the left
child, then eight samples from the right child; its right-child index j
has original parent index8+j. In the rank-one construction(6), expanding
the two cross rows gives

    Q_(2,9)=alpha_1^2*z*(C2-1),
    C2=r_0*rho*eta*H1*(D+E/z)/(Z0*Z1),                  (22)

    Q_(6,13)=alpha_1^2*alpha_0^2*z*(C6-1),
    C6=r_1*rho*eta*H0*(D+E/z)/(Z0*Z1).                 (23)

For(22), child gradient2 is J_L V, while its residual1 and initial point
are retained from the seed. Use

    <J_L V,d_1>=r_0*rho*eta*H1/R^2,
    <p,y_1>=zD+E, e_1=z.

For(23), child gradient6 and residual5 are
alpha_0*J_R V and alpha_0*J_R y_1. Therefore

    <g_6,d_1>=-alpha_0^2*r_1*rho*eta,
    <p,y_5>=-H0*(zD+E)/R^2,
    e_5=alpha_0^2*z.

Substitution in(7) and(5) gives(22)-(23), without suppressing any
within-child row or optimum row. Every index2,9,6,13 is queried in the
fifteen-step word.

Here is a common exact lower bound for C2 and C6. At E=0 both equal

    C0=Klen*(A-delta)/(theta*A^2*rho^2).                  (24)

The numerator factors in(22)-(23) increase with E. Also
Z(r)<=r^2*(Nbar+E/4) for r>1. Consequently

    C2,C6 >= C0/(1+E/(4Nbar))^2.                         (25)

Squaring rational endpoints proves14142/10000<s<14143/10000.
Substitution into a,b,A yields Klen>2.411, A-delta>5.828,
A<5.8301, theta<.4143, and rho^2<.9967. All terminating decimals here
are exact rationals. Thus

    Klen*(A-delta)>2.411*5.828=14.051308,
    theta*A^2*rho^2<.4143*(5.8301)^2*.9967<14.036,
    14.036*(1+1/1000)=14.050036<14.051308.

This proves C0>1+1/1000. Since E/(4Nbar)<1/15000,

    (1+1/15000)^2<1+1/7000,
    (1+1/2000)(1+1/7000)<1+1/1000,

and(25) proves

    C2>1+1/2000, C6>1+1/2000.                            (26)

The next rank-one join is therefore illegal for the entire interval
0<eps<=1/100, despite the positive scalar recursion(20).

## 6. A quantitative angle bound on every transverse coupling

This section allows ALL transverse couplings in the fifteen-step join,
while keeping the actual seven-step child(18) fixed. The first parent
has its explicit embeddings(6). No claim about changing that earlier
embedding is made.

Let L,R be arbitrary linear isometries of the two copies of this child
into any common Euclidean space, and keep left scale1. A legal bridge
forces

    alpha_1*R p=L d_1,

where alpha_1 is necessarily the positive number in(21). Let P_d denote
orthogonal projection perpendicular to d_1 inside the left child space,
and P_p perpendicular to p inside the right child space. Orthogonal
decomposition gives the exact identity

    <L g_6,alpha_1*R y_5>
      =<g_6,d_1><p,y_5>/R^2
          +alpha_1*<L P_d g_6,R P_p y_5>.                (27)

Both mixed parallel/perpendicular terms vanish by the forced alignment.
By the ordinary Cauchy-Schwarz inequality the second term is bounded
below by -alpha_1*||P_d g_6||*||P_p y_5||. This is valid in every
dimension and for every real positive-semidefinite completion; no
particular contraction or matrix rank is imposed.

Because g_6=alpha_0*J_R V and d_1=alpha_0*J_R d_(r_1),
the transverse norm is exactly

    ||P_d g_6||
      =alpha_0*sqrt(eta-r_1^2*rho^2*eta^2/Z1)
      =alpha_0*(r_1-1)*eps*sqrt(eta)/(2sqrt(Z1)).         (28)

Further ||P_p y_5||<=alpha_0*||y_1||. Divide the possible correction
in(27) by the positive row scale alpha_1^2*e_5, where e_5=alpha_0^2*z.
Equations(21),(28) imply the upper bound

    Tcorr <= R^2*(r_1-1)*eps*sqrt(eta)*||y_1||
                     /(2sqrt(Z0)*Z1*z)
          <= R^2*(r_1-1)*eps*||y_1||
                     /(2r_0*r_1^2*rho^3*eta*z).         (29)

The second inequality uses Z0>=r_0^2*rho^2*eta and
Z1>=r_1^2*rho^2*eta. From the rational bounds in section3,

    R^2<15, ||y_1||<2, r_1-1<5,
    r_0>2, r_1>5, rho^3>97/100, eta>2/5, z>1.

For the first two bounds, explicitly
R^2<(3.44)^2+2.43*1.01+.0001<15 and
||y_1||^2<1.01^2+2.43*1.01+.0001<4.
It follows from(29) that

    Tcorr <[150/(2*2*25*(97/100)*(2/5))]*eps<4eps.       (30)

The aligned contribution of(27) is still exactly(23). Thus for EVERY
coupling with the required physical alignment and the prescribed values,

    Q_(6,13)/(alpha_1^2*e_5) >= C6-1-Tcorr
                              >1/2000-4eps.             (31)

In particular at the explicit eps=1/10000,

    Q_(6,13)/(alpha_1^2*e_5)>1/10000>0.                  (32)

This is an exact original-row separation for all transverse choices at
the next join of these fixed actual seven-step children. Both children
are individually legal, have nonzero terminal residual, and retain the
strict energy surplus(16); their prospective fifteen-step parent cannot
exist with this alignment, internal data, and value prescription.

More generally any successful next join inside this parametrized family
must satisfy the explicit compatibility condition

    alpha_1*||P_d g_6||*||P_p y_5||
           >=alpha_1^2*e_5*(C6-1).                      (33)

For0<eps<=1/100 the bounds above give the simpler necessary condition
eps>1/8000. It is only necessary. Increasing eps beyond this bound does
not prove feasibility. The obstruction is to arbitrarily small changes
of this specified geometry, not to every nonlinear geometry.

## 7. The retained terminal normal gives a stronger four-row separation

The original interpolation rows give more information than the norm bound
in section6. This section excludes the next join for the entire interval
0<eps<=1/100, including the original q-coordinate amplitude1/100.
The actual seven-step child and its first embeddings remain fixed.

Two exact vector identities in that child are decisive:

    d_1=-r_1*rho*g_6-(r_1-1)*v_1,
    y_5=z*g_4+(a-rho)*g_6+2*g_7.                         (34)

For the first identity, use w_1=rho*g_6+v_1 and d_1=v_1-r_1*w_1.
For the second, use the seed identity
y_1=zU+(a-rho)V+2w, and apply alpha_0*J_R.
Every coefficient in the second identity is positive. The energy of the
left endpoint residual v_1 is

    e_7=<g_7,v_1>=alpha_0^2*E/4.

Let

    k=(r_1-1)/(r_1*rho)>0, T_y=z+(a-rho)+2=m+delta.

Use arbitrary second-join isometries L,R with
alpha_1*R p=L d_1, as in section6, and write G_i,Y_i for the resulting
parent gradient and residual at original index i. The first identity(34)
implies

    <G_6,Y_13>=-alpha_1^2*<p,y_5>/(r_1*rho)
                        -k*<L v_1,Y_13>.

The second identity(34) says

    Y_13=z*G_12+(a-rho)*G_14+2*G_15.

Since Q_(j,7)=<G_j,L v_1>-e_7 for j=12,14,15, the following nonnegative
combination of ORIGINAL interpolation rows has no free transverse term:

    S_rows=Q_(6,13)+k[z*Q_(12,7)+(a-rho)*Q_(14,7)+2*Q_(15,7)]
          =alpha_1^2[-<p,y_5>/(r_1*rho)-e_5]-k*T_y*e_7
          =alpha_1^2*e_5*[I-1-k*T_y*E/(4z*alpha_1^2)],   (35)

where

    I=H0*(D+E/z)/(r_1*rho*Z0).                           (36)

Here e_5=alpha_0^2*z and the initial pairing <p,y_5> was calculated
explicitly in section5. The identity does not impose a rank or an angle
condition. The queried row(6,13) and the rows entering the queried bridge
endpoint7 all must hold. The term(15,7) is OUTGOING from the unqueried
final sample, so even the accepted unqueried-terminal reduction retains
it. There is no use of a deleted incoming-final row.

At E=0 expression(36) equals C0 from(24). Its numerator factors increase
with E, and Z0<=r_0^2*(Nbar+E/4). Hence

    I>=C0/(1+E/(4Nbar))>1+1/1200,                       (37)

because C0>1+1/1000, E/(4Nbar)<1/15000, and
(1+1/1200)(1+1/15000)<1+1/1000.

The terminal-normal charge is bounded without dropping it. We have
k<1 because r_1*delta<6/600<1, and T_y<7/2. Also r_0>12/5 and
r_1>29/5 follow from the rational bounds on s and A. Equations(17),(21),
Nbar>39/100, and R^2<15 give

    alpha_1^2=Z0*Z1/R^4
       >[(12/5)^2*(29/5)^2*(39/100)^2]/225>1/8.          (38)

The final rational comparison in(38) is, on clearing denominators,
8*144*841*1521>625*10000*225; the two sides are1473593472 and1406250000.
Consequently

    0<k*T_y*E/(4z*alpha_1^2)<7E<=7/10000.

Combining this with(35),(37) gives the strict positive separation

    S_rows/(alpha_1^2*e_5)>1/1200-7/10000=1/7500>0.      (39)

All four coefficients in S_rows are positive. Therefore all four original
rows cannot be nonpositive. This excludes EVERY transverse coupling at
the next join of the displayed actual seven-step children for every
0<eps<=1/100. The terminal residual was not erased: its original normal
is the source of the finite charge in(35), and this charge is too small
to repair the compatibility gap.

More generally the exact necessary compatibility condition for the same
first-parent family is

    I-1 <= k*T_y*E/(4z*alpha_1^2).                        (40)

Within0<eps<=1/100, the coarse estimates already require
E>1/8400, in conflict with E<=1/10000. This is a necessary condition
only; satisfying(40) would not imply the other original rows or a parent.

## 8. Exact scope and the smallest unresolved object

There are now three distinct statements, all at UNVERIFIED draft level:

1. For every0<eps<=1/100, (12) is an actual changed terminal seed and(18)
   is one actual seven-step parent. All original interpolation rows,
   values, the physical bridge, both child effects, normal energies, and
   true closest distance are supplied explicitly.
2. For that fixed first parent, the next rank-one operation fails at
   original queried rows(2,9) and(6,13) throughout this interval.
3. For every0<eps<=1/100, EVERY transverse coupling at the next join
   fails by the nonnegative four-row combination(35)-(39). This permits
   arbitrary ambient dimension, but fixes the first parent's data and
   all displayed values. The weaker angle estimate remains a separately
   derived diagnostic; it is not the scope of the final separation.

The next concrete unresolved instance can be specified without a solver:
take the SAME formulas(12),(17),(18) with eps=1/25, preserving the word,
rho, and all other definitions. This is still an actual legal seed and
first parent. Indeed Klen>12/5 and eta>2/5 imply
delta*(Klen-1)eta>7/7500>1/1250=E/2, and delta*z>1/600>E/2.
These verify the only potentially delicate seed normals; the sign proof
of(8L),(8R) still applies. The positive cone, terminal price, and exact
energy law are unchanged. Formula(16) remains valid because its monotonic
ratio argument holds for every E>0. This larger amplitude is not excluded
by the bounds used to prove(39), and no legality of its fifteen-step join
is asserted. Its smallest pending parent is the explicit word h[2] with
the true alignment(21), all prescribed values, and all original Q rows.

Another remaining freedom is to change the FIRST seven-step embedding,
even at eps=1/100, and then form a parent. Sections6-7 do not cover
arbitrary earlier couplings. General value-height changes are also outside
this result. Thus this is a proper-family obstruction, not a claim that
all terminal residuals or all nonlinear geometry are impossible.

The physical word was retained throughout. A_j=1+sum h[j] is its actual
shifted stepsize sum, NOT the exact Zhang-Jiang objective denominator
B_(4*2^j-1). The actual seed and seven-step objective lower bounds are
respectively J/R^2 and Z0*J/R^4. No identification of these numbers with
1/B_n is made, no new horizon-dependent word is substituted, and no
asymptotic implication for the original target follows from this finite
construction or this proper-family obstruction.

evidence:
# Positive off-diagonal entries and exact chronological decimation

Status: **unverified proof draft**, sixth launch, first continuation round.
No kernel evaluation, optimizer, installation, or fact submission was used.
The uniform positive-semidefinite conclusion and the original minimax Goal
remain open. This document proves some of the actual coefficient claims;
it does not assume the remaining thirteen-band estimates.

## 1. Definitions and the coefficient that is being estimated

Fix an integer m>=128 and keep epsilon=1/m fixed throughout. Set

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c,
 d_k=1+a*c^k  (k>=0), H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j).

The extension of d_k past m-1 is only a coefficient device. The actual
queried word is H_m with its last d_0 removed. Write h_i for its steps,
s_i=sum_(r<i)h_r, and s'=s_i+h_i when discussing a single step.

On the infinite original ruler word define B_00=1 and

 B_(i+1),k=(1-h_i/d_k)B_ik+(h_i/d_(k-1))B_i,(k-1),

with a zero second term at k=0. For each occupied state k, h_i<=d_k:
the first occurrence of d_j kills state j, and all smaller states have
already died. This also proves B_ik>=0, sum_k B_ik=1, and
B_ik=0 for i>=2^k or k>i.

For arbitrary formal vectors y_k put g_i=sum_k v_ik*y_k, where
v_ik=B_ik/d_k. The row-finite symmetric matrix E is defined by

 sum_(k,l)E_kl<y_k,y_l>
 =sum_i [2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
       +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].   (1)

Each coefficient is a finite sum: a term containing state k occurs by
the step immediately before query2^k. In particular E_kl=0 for k<l
and l>2^k. The m-principal block is the actual finite residual kernel.
The coefficient convention in (1) means that an off-diagonal entry
appears twice in the quadratic form.

## 2. Two elementary bounds for the actual chronological word

For the elementary parameter bounds used below, lambda>12/5 and
lambda<29/12 give 12/5<c<39/16. The upper comparison follows from
(29/12)(129/128)=3741/1536<39/16. Consequently
a>(127/128)/(39/16)=127/312>2/5. Moreover

 d_0=sqrt(2)-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)],
 d_2=2+sqrt(2)-lambda*epsilon^2,

so 7/5<d_0<3/2 and d_2<7/2; for the first lower bound use
sqrt(2)>141/100 and 2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]<5/768.
In particular 2<c<3 and 1<d_0<2. Also

                         d_(k+1)>2d_k  (k>=2).            (2)

Indeed d_(k+1)-2d_k=(c-2)a*c^k-1. At k=2 the quantity
before subtracting1 is (1-epsilon)c(c-2), and

 c(c-2)=1+2lambda(lambda-1)epsilon+lambda^2 epsilon^2
        >1+6epsilon.

Consequently (1-epsilon)c(c-2)>1+5epsilon-6epsilon^2>1.
The expression increases with k, proving (2).

Second, every original physical step satisfies

                             h_i<s_i+2.                  (3)

Let S_j=sum H_j and C_j=S_j+2-d_j. Then C_0=2-d_0>0.
The recurrences S_(j+1)=2S_j+d_j and
d_(j+1)=c*d_j-(c-1) give the exact identity

 C_(j+1)=2C_j+(3-c)(d_j-1)>0.

The prefix before the FIRST d_j is H_j, so (3) holds there. Every later
occurrence has a larger elapsed clock and the same step size. This proves
(3) at every position, without changing the enclosing epsilon.

There is a sharper envelope that does exclude the recorded swap foil.
Put rho=c-2 and gamma=rho-a=c-1-d_0>0. The exact word-sum formula gives

 rho(S_j+1)+1-d_j=gamma*2^j.

Thus every original occurrence h_i=d_j obeys

 rho(s_i+1)+1-h_i=gamma*2^j+rho(s_i-S_j)>=0.              (3a)

If the third and fourth steps are exchanged, the first d_2 has
s_i=d_0+d_1 instead of S_2=2d_0+d_1. Its slack in (3a) becomes
4gamma-rho*d_0<13/128-14/25<0. Here rho>2/5, d_0>7/5, and
gamma<(13/4)epsilon, as proved explicitly in Section7 below. This
distinguishes the original chronology from that particular foil.
Equation (3a) alone is not asserted to prove b_i or u_i.

## 3. Nonnegative off-diagonal entries, term by term

For a fixed step h=h_i, write v_k=v_ik and v_(-1)=0. The scaled birth
recurrence is

 v'_k=v_k+(h/d_k)(v_(k-1)-v_k).

For k<l, expansion of that step's contribution to E_kl gives exactly

 C_kl*v_k*v_l
 +[s'h^2(d_l-1)/(d_k*d_l)]v_(k-1)*v_l
 +[s'h^2(d_k-1)/(d_k*d_l)]v_k*v_(l-1)
 +[s'h^2/(d_k*d_l)]v_(k-1)*v_(l-1),                     (4)

where

 C_kl=h[2s'+1-h-s'h(1/d_k+1/d_l-1/(d_k*d_l))].           (5)

To check (4), the first term of (1) contributes
s'h(v'_k*v_l+v_k*v'_l), the second contributes
s'(v'_k-v_k)(v'_l-v_l), and the third contributes
h(1-h)v_k*v_l. Expanding these three expressions gives (4)-(5).

The last three coefficients in (4) are nonnegative. Suppose k>=2.
If v_k*v_l=0, the possibly signed coefficient C_kl costs nothing.
Otherwise state k is occupied, so h<=d_k. Equation (2) gives
d_l>=d_(k+1)>2d_k and hence

 h(1/d_k+1/d_l-1/(d_k*d_l))<3/2.

It follows from (3) that

 C_kl>h(s'/2+1-h)=(h/2)(s_i+2-h)>0.                     (6)

Thus every physical step contributes a nonnegative amount to E_kl
when 2<=k<l. This proof keeps the signed terms of the original step
until they combine into C_kl; it does not take their absolute values.

For k=0,1, support leaves only E_01 and E_12. The first two steps,
whose unscaled state vectors are successively V_0,V_1,V_2, give

 E_01=(d_0-1)/d_1>0,
 E_12=(d_0+d_1)(d_1-1)/(d_1*d_2)>0.

These calculations and (4)-(6) prove

                    E_kl>=0 for every k!=l.              (7)

In particular the actual second-neighbor weights obey e_0=e_1=0 and

                    e_k=E_(k,k+2)>0 for k>=2.             (8)

For strictness, just before the first d_k both B_ik and B_i,(k+1)
are positive when k>=2. For B_ik, use the path that takes a birth on
each of its first k steps and then stays. All those birth probabilities
are positive, and every subsequent step before the first d_k is smaller
than d_k. For B_i,(k+1), take the first k+1 births and then stay; this
is possible because k+1<=2^k-1, and all later pre-d_k steps are smaller
than d_(k+1). At the d_k step, the third term in (4) with l=k+2 is
strictly positive: s'>0, d_k>1, v_k>0, v_(k+1)>0. This proves (8).

No uniform lower bound such as e_k>=1/15 is proved by this strictness
argument: the displayed positive path probabilities have not been
estimated uniformly.

## 4. Exact consequences for the unresolved row margins

For all nonnegative indices define

 A_i=E_(i,i+1), e_i=E_(i,i+2),
 b_i=A_i-2(e_(i-1)+e_i),
 u_i=E_ii-A_(i-1)-A_i+e_(i-2)+e_i
                         -sum_(|l-i|>=3)|E_il|,

with negative subscripts equal to zero. Let F_i=sum_l E_il be the
finite unweighted row sum, and ellhat_i=sum_l E_il*d_l the constant
load obtained by polarizing (1) against the constant gradient.

Equation (7) removes all absolute values from the far off-diagonal
sum. Therefore the exact full-row identity is

                     u_i=2E_ii+2(e_(i-2)+e_i)-F_i.         (9)

In particular a proof of u_i does not need to identify alternating
signs of individual far entries. It still needs signed cancellation
between the diagonal, the neighboring entries, and the row sum.
Nonnegative entries do not imply either b_i>=2/15 or u_i>=0.

This does not discard a terminal coefficient. In the inherited finite
decomposition, the triple starting at m-2 remains the square
e_(m-2)||y_(m-2)+2y_(m-1)||^2. Its coefficient now has the sign in (8).
The last diagonal remains

 u_(m-1)+sum_(l>=m+2)E_(m-1,l)+b_(m-1)+e_(m-1).

Neither its required quantitative lower bound nor the completed
constant-column remainder follows from (7) alone.

## 5. A scalar constant-load formula with the signed difference retained

For this section all sums run over the infinite coefficient word, but
every state-specific sum is finite. Set

 mu_ik=h_i B_ik/d_k,
 L_k=sum_(r=0)^k d_r,
 M_k=sum_i h_i*mu_ik,
 N_k=sum_i s_(i+1)*h_i*mu_ik,

and put M_(-1)=N_(-1)=0. The flow equation is
B_(i+1),k-B_ik=mu_i,(k-1)-mu_ik. Summing it proves
sum_i mu_ik=1 for each transient state. Weighting it by s_(i+1)
and summing by parts gives

 sum_i s_(i+1)(mu_ik-mu_i,(k-1))=sum_i h_i B_ik=d_k.

Starting with a zero predecessor moment shows
sum_i s_(i+1)mu_ik=L_k. Thus M_k and N_k are respectively the mean
exit step and the mean product of exit clock and exit step for state k.

Polarizing (1) against the constant gradient gives

 ellhat_k=sum_i h_i[(s_i+1)v_ik+s_(i+1)v_(i+1),k].         (10)

For example, the first term in (1) contributes
s'h(v_ik+v_(i+1),k), its increment-square term contributes zero,
and its last term contributes h(1-h)v_ik. Their sum is (10).
Substitute the birth recurrence into (10), then use the two occupation
identities just proved. The result is

             ellhat_k=2L_k+1-M_k-(N_k-N_(k-1))/d_k.        (11)

In detail, before the recurrence contribution the sum is
2L_k+1-M_k. The remaining term is
sum_i s'h_i^2(v_i,(k-1)-v_ik)/d_k
=(N_(k-1)-N_k)/d_k. This checks its sign and its denominator.

Formula (11) is an identity, not a new condition replacing the load
inequalities. It identifies the chronological mixed moment that must
be estimated. Bounding N_k and N_(k-1) separately loses the signed
quantity needed for the desired 2d_k<=ellhat_k<=11d_k/4.

### 5.1 The first required constant-load row is settled uniformly

The row k=2 can be evaluated and bounded without estimating the higher
birth states. Put t=d_0, u=d_1, d=d_2, and theta=1-t/d. The nonzero
values of B_n2 before its extinction are B_22=1 and B_32=theta.
Also B_12=0 and B_42=0. Substitution in (10), using the original
first four steps (t,u,t,d), gives

 ellhat_2=[u(t+u)+t(t+u+1)
                 +(t(2t+u)+d(2t+u+1))*theta]/d.

Collecting its terms, with no inequality, gives

 ellhat_2/d=((t+u)/d)^2+(2t+u+1)/d-t^2(2t+u)/d^3.         (11a)

The actual parameters obey
7/5<t<3/2, 199/100<u<2, and 17/5<d<7/2.
The only new lower bound, d>17/5, follows from
d=2+sqrt(2)-lambda*epsilon^2,
sqrt(2)>141/100, and lambda*epsilon^2<(5/2)/128^2<1/100.

For a lower bound in (11a), its three displayed positive magnitudes
obey, in order,

 ((t+u)/d)^2>(339/350)^2>9/10,
 (2t+u+1)/d>579/350>33/20,
 t^2(2t+u)/d^3<(45/4)/(75/2)=3/10.

Here d^3>(17/5)^3>75/2. Hence ellhat_2/d>9/4.
For the upper bound, the corresponding comparisons are

 ((t+u)/d)^2<(35/34)^2<17/16,
 (2t+u+1)/d<30/17<177/100,
 t^2(2t+u)/d^3>(49/25)(19/4)/43=931/4300>21/100.

The last line uses 2t+u>19/4 and d^3<(7/2)^3<43. Therefore

                   9/4<ellhat_2/d_2<1049/400<21/8.        (11b)

In particular the required interval [2,11/4] holds at k=2 for every
actual m>=128. The unresolved constant-load rows start at k=3.

### 5.2 A clock-slack identity, with the nonmonotone term exposed

Put rho=c-2, alpha_clock=rho/(1+rho), tau_i=s_(i+1), and

 omega_i=alpha_clock*tau_i+1-h_i
        =[rho(s_i+1)+1-h_i]/(c-1)>=0,
 Z_k=sum_i mu_ik*omega_i,
 W_k=sum_i mu_ik*tau_i*omega_i,
 H2_k=sum_i mu_ik*tau_i^2.

Take all predecessor quantities with index-1 to be zero. The sharp
original clock inequality (3a) supplies omega_i>=0. Weighting the
birth flow by tau_i^2 and summing by parts gives

 H2_k-H2_(k-1)=sum_i(2tau_i*h_i-h_i^2)B_ik
              =d_k(2L_k-M_k).

The definitions also give
M_k=alpha_clock*L_k+1-Z_k and
N_k=alpha_clock*H2_k+L_k-W_k. Substitution in (11) yields the exact
signed formula

 ellhat_k=c*L_k/(c-1)^2-1/(c-1)
                  +Z_k/(c-1)+(W_k-W_(k-1))/d_k.           (11c)

The explicit level sum is
L_k=c*d_k/(c-1)+k-1+gamma/(c-1). Thus the first two terms on the
right of (11c) equal

 [c^2/(c-1)^3]d_k+c(k-1)/(c-1)^2
                         +c*gamma/(c-1)^3-1/(c-1).       (11d)

For k>=2 this exceeds2d_k: c^2/(c-1)^3 decreases for c>1,
and its value at39/16 is24336/12167=2+2/12167. The remaining
non-gamma terms are at least1/(c-1)^2, and gamma>0.

This calculation does NOT prove the lower load bound. Although
Z_k>=0 and W_k>=0, the difference W_k-W_(k-1) has not been signed.
Its summand cannot be treated as increasing just because birth-state
exit times increase. In fact it has a large decrease in the ORIGINAL
actual word: at the third step, i=2 and h_2=t=d_0,

 tau_2*omega_2=(2t+u)[gamma+rho(t+u)]/(c-1)>4,

whereas at the fourth step, the first d_2,

 tau_3*omega_3=(2t+u+d_2)*4gamma/(c-1)<1.

For the first comparison use 2t+u>47/10 and
rho(t+u)/(c-1)>(2/5)(339/100)/(3/2)>9/10.
For the second use 2t+u+d_2<17/2 and
4gamma/(c-1)<13/[128(7/5)]=65/896. These hold for every
actual m>=128. The expected difference in (11c) may still be
nonnegative, but a proof must use the original exit distribution;
pathwise monotonicity of this clock weight is false.

## 6. An exact reduction that distinguishes the original lower-level order

Put t=d_0, ell=c-1, gamma=ell-t, and

 Z(z)=c*z/(1+ell*z),
 A(z)=(1-t*z)(1+ell*z)=1+gamma*z-t*ell*z^2.

These are new scalar functions, unrelated to the adjacent entries A_i.
They are well-defined at every nonnegative reciprocal physical node.
The affine-geometric node relation gives

 (1-t*z)(1-d_(j+1)*z)=A(z)(1-d_j*Z(z)),
 Z(1/d_(j+1))=1/d_j.                                    (12)

Write the original infinite step word in consecutive pairs. The exact
pair at position r is (t,d_(nu_2(r+1)+1)), where nu_2 is the exponent
of2 in a positive integer. After removing every t and lowering the
remaining level by1, the compressed word is the same original ruler
word, with the SAME epsilon. For its first r steps write
P_r(z)=product_(i<r)(1-h_i*z) and s_r=sum_(i<r)h_i. Then

 P_(2r)(z)=A(z)^r P_r(Z(z)),
 P_(2r+1)(z)=(1-t*z)A(z)^r P_r(Z(z)),
 s_(2r)=c*s_r-gamma*r,
 s_(2r+1)=c*s_r-gamma*r+t.                               (13)

All four identities follow by multiplying or summing the individual
pairs in (12). This is a chronological identity, not an identity of
the full multiset alone. The foil that exchanges the third and fourth
steps destroys the displayed consecutive-pair description.

The Newton factors also transform exactly:

 phi_(k+1)(z)=(1-t*z)(1+ell*z)^k phi_k(Z(z)),              (14)

where phi_k(z)=product_(j<k)(1-d_j*z). At epsilon=0, interpreted only
as a coefficient limit, t=ell=sqrt(2), gamma=0, and A(z)=1-2z^2.
At every actual epsilon>0 the linear term gamma*z and the clock defect
-gamma*r in (13) must both be retained. In fact

 gamma=lambda*epsilon+2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]>0.

Equations (12)-(14) do not yet establish a bound for E or the mixed
moments in (11). They give an exact original-order transformation in
which those estimates can be pursued without replacing an embedded
block's parameters by epsilon=1/j.

## 7. The decimation multiplier changes sign around one

It is false that the multiplier A at all required physical nodes can
be discarded by a uniform inequality A<=1, or by a uniform inequality
A>=1. Both failures occur at every actual m>=128, without using a
standalone-depth parameter in an embedded block.

For z=1/d_j,

             A(1/d_j)-1=(gamma*d_j-t*ell)/d_j^2.           (15)

We have 7/5<t<3/2, t<ell<3/2, and

 2epsilon<gamma
   <(lambda+2/lambda)epsilon
   =(3sqrt(2)-1)epsilon<(13/4)epsilon.                    (16)

At j=2, d_2<7/2, so
gamma*d_2<91/1024<49/25<t*ell. Therefore A(1/d_2)<1.
At the actual highest level j=m-1,

 gamma*d_(m-1)>(4/5)2^(m-1)/m>9/4>t*ell.

Here a>2/5 and c>2 give the first bound. For the second, 2^(m-1)/m
is increasing for m>=2, and even 2^10/128=8 already exceeds45/16.
This proves A(1/d_(m-1))>1. Both indices are in the original residual
coordinate set. These are counterexamples only to discarding the
decimation factor in one direction, not to the desired band bounds.

There is nevertheless a useful uniform estimate. For k>=8 define

 X_k=(65/16)epsilon*(2/c)^k+(225/32)*(2/c^2)^k.

Then, for every 0<=z<=1/d_k and every integer 0<=r<=2^(k-1),

 0<A(z),
 r|A(z)-1|<=X_k<1/80,
 |A(z)^r-1|<=(80/79)X_k<1/79,
 0<=gamma*r/d_k<=(65/16)epsilon*(2/c)^k.                 (17)

For r=0 all expressions with r vanish. For positive r, (16),
t*ell<9/4, a>2/5, and d_k>a*c^k give

 r|A(z)-1|
 <=2^(k-1)[gamma/d_k+t*ell/d_k^2]
 <(65/16)epsilon*(2/c)^k+(225/32)*(2/c^2)^k.

Also c>12/5, so 2/c<5/6 and 2/c^2<3/8. For k>=8, the exact rational
comparisons (5/6)^8<1/4 and (3/8)^8<1/2500 show

 X_k<65/8192+9/3200<1/80.

Positivity follows from z<=1/d_k<1/t. With delta=|A(z)-1|, if A(z)>=1
the binomial expansion gives

 A(z)^r-1<=sum_(j>=1)(r*delta)^j<=X_k/(1-X_k).

If A(z)<1, 1-A(z)^r<=r*delta<=X_k. These prove the third estimate in
(17); the last follows from the linear part of the same calculation.

Thus the multiplier and clock defects are uniformly small far up the
actual spectrum, despite the change of sign in (15). Their precise
rates include BOTH epsilon*(2/c)^k and (2/c^2)^k. This does not yet
control E: converting pointwise spectral estimates to a birth coefficient
requires retaining the signed divided differences, not taking a large
absolute bound on the entire inverse Newton matrix.

## 8. An early-time bound for the entire nearby band

This localization is in PHYSICAL TIME, in addition to the earlier
localization in matrix-column distance. It controls the part of a near
entry accumulated before the low reciprocal columns die.

Fix j>=2 and let E^early_kl be the contribution to (1) of the first
2^j steps, namely the prefix (H_j,d_j). If k,l>=j+6, then

                         |E^early_kl|<10^(-10).           (18)

Here is a uniform proof. Write T=sum(H_j,d_j). The exact word sum is

 sum H_j=a*c^j/(c-2)+(1-a/(c-2))*2^j-1.

Because 0<a/(c-2)<1 and 2<c, this sum is less than c^j-1.
Consequently T<(1+1/a)d_j<(7/2)d_j. All steps in the prefix are at
most d_j, and d_j>3.

For an integer r>=0 define

 p_r=min{1,(7/2)^r/[r!*2^(r(r-1)/2)]}.

At each query of this prefix, the probability of state j+r is at most
p_r. To prove this, condition on a birth path's first arrival at j.
Reaching j+r requires r subsequent births on increasing distinct
steps. Each specified set has probability at most the product of its
steps divided by d_j...d_(j+r-1); all stay factors are at most one.
The sum of those step products is at most T^r/r!, and (2) bounds the
denominator below by d_j^r*2^(r(r-1)/2). This proof applies at either
end of every step and for every arrival time.

The sequence p_r decreases for r>=3. Thus, for k>=j+6,

 0<=v_ik,v_(i+1),k<=p_6/d_k,
 |v_(i+1),k-v_ik|<=h_i[(5/2)p_5+p_6]/d_k^2.

For the second line, apply the birth recurrence and use
d_k/d_(k-1)<c<5/2. Define Q_6=(5/2)p_5+p_6. The exact fractions give

 p_5=16807/3932160<1/230,
 p_6=117649/1509949440<1/12500,
 Q_6<1/92+1/12500<11/1000.

The first and last terms of (1), polarized for a general k,l, are at
most [T^2+2d_j*T]p_6^2/(d_k*d_l) in absolute value. This uses
2sum_i s_(i+1)h_i=T^2+sum_i h_i^2 and
sum_i h_i^2<=d_j*T. The increment-square term is at most
T^2*d_j*Q_6^2/(d_k^2*d_l^2), since
sum_i s_(i+1)h_i^2<=T^2*d_j. These statements also apply when k=l.

Now d_k,d_l>2^6*d_j. The two contributions are respectively less than

 77/[4*2^12*12500^2] < 1/30000000000,
 49*121/[12*2^24*1000^2] < 1/30000000000.

Their sum is less than10^(-10), proving (18). Every estimate is
uniform in both the row indices and the enclosing m.

For a thirteen-entry row centered at i>=14, take j=i-12. Then both
indices of each entry E_(i,i+r), -6<=r<=6, are at least j+6, so (18)
controls its entire initial prefix through the first d_(i-12). This
does not remove any of the later repeated low steps; their physical
order and elapsed clock remain part of the late contribution.

## 9. Only eighteen reciprocal nodes remain in the late contribution

For this section fix an ACTUAL required row 24<=i<=m-1, put j=i-12,
and consider l=i+r with -6<=r<=6. Extended indices l>=m are only the
same-epsilon coefficient device, as in Section1. All contributing
physical steps are still through the first d_i and are in the original
queried word.

Define R_kb=(d_k/d_b)phi_k(1/d_b) for b>=k, and zero for b<k.
Its triangular inverse D has entries

 D_bk=product_(0<=r<=k,r!=b)(1-d_r/d_b)^(-1),  0<=b<=k,
 D_bk=0 for b>k.                                         (19)

One direct check uses Lagrange interpolation at the distinct nodes
1/d_0,...,1/d_k. Comparing highest-degree coefficients shows that the
weights reciprocal to the products of node differences annihilate
polynomials of degree below k and recover the leading coefficient
at degree k. Apply this identity to phi_r, whose leading coefficient
is (-1)^r product_(s<r)d_s, and rescale by d_b/d_k. The resulting
inverse of R is exactly (19).

Writing P_n(z)=product_(t<n)(1-h_t*z), the corresponding scalar
coefficient identity is

                  v_nk=sum_(b=0)^k D_bk*P_n(1/d_b)/d_b.  (20)

Indeed P_n(z)=sum_k B_nk phi_k(z), by the birth recurrence. Evaluation
at the first k+1 reciprocal nodes kills every phi_r with r>k, and
inversion by (19) gives (20).

For every query n>=2^j and every b<=j, P_n(1/d_b)=0 exactly; the same
is true at the following query. Thus all such nodes disappear from
the late part of (1). Define M^late_ab to be the quadratic coefficient
of the normalized modal columns P_n(1/d_a)/d_a and P_n(1/d_b)/d_b,
using only physical steps 2^j<=n<2^i, with their ORIGINAL elapsed
clocks s_n. Then (20) gives the exact identity

 E_il=E^early_il
          +sum_(a=j+1)^i sum_(b=j+1)^l D_ai*M^late_ab*D_bl. (21)

For l<i every term vanishes already by query2^l; for l>=i the first
column vanishes by query2^i. Consequently the displayed final cutoff
is correct in both cases and adds no physical step beyond the original
trajectory. Only the eighteen nodes i-11,...,i+6 can occur in (21).

Crucially, the remaining inverse columns have a uniform absolute sum.
For each k in [i-6,i+6],

                         sum_(b=j+1)^k |D_bk|<6.          (22)

To prove this, put q_c=1/c and P^q_s=product_(r=1)^s(1-q_c^r),
with P^q_0=1. Factoring each difference in (19) gives

 |D_bk|=q_c^((k-b)(k-b+1)/2)
             *(d_b/(d_b-1))^k/(P^q_b P^q_(k-b)).

Since q_c<5/12, the elementary inequality
product_r(1-x_r)>=1-sum_r x_r for 0<=x_r<=1 gives
P^q_s>=1-q_c-q_c^2>59/144>2/5 for s>=1.
Also P^q_1>7/12. For b>=i-11 and k<=i+6,

 k/(a*c^b)<(5/2)(i+6)/2^(i-11)<=75/8192<1/100.

The middle expression decreases with i>=24. Hence
(d_b/(d_b-1))^k<=exp(k/(a*c^b))<exp(1/100).
Summing with r=k-b and then extending the positive sum to all r>=0,

 sum_b |D_bk|
 <(5/2)exp(1/100)
       *[1+5/7+(5/2)*sum_(r>=2)(5/12)^(r(r+1)/2)]
 <=(5/2)exp(1/100)[1+5/7+625/3206]
 <5 exp(1/100)<500/99<6.

For the second line, ratios of successive terms starting at r=2
are at most(5/12)^3, so their sum is at most125/1603. For the last
line, exp(x)<=1/(1-x) for 0<=x<1 follows by comparing its power
series with the geometric series. This proves (22).

For example, if an analytic approximation changes every normalized
late modal coefficient in this eighteen-node window by at most eta,
then (21)-(22) change each reconstructed near entry by at most36eta.
Discarding the early part costs an additional10^(-10), by (18).
This is a genuine uniform coefficient-stability estimate; no small
fixed-index inverse coefficient is included in its norm.

The pointwise decimation bound (17) is only needed while a reciprocal
column is alive. For the node 1/d_b it is identically zero after
query2^b, so its even-query formula only requires r<=2^(b-1), exactly
the range of (17). Multiplying that bound by an unnecessarily longer
horizon would lose the extinction information.

This leaves a specific analytic step: control the signed late K/T
coefficients under (12)-(14), with the original clock, and bound the
resulting finite window uniformly. Neither (21) nor (22) asserts those
remaining estimates or the signs of b_i and u_i.

## 10. A uniform lower bound for the surviving mass at a killing step

Let pi_k=B_(2^k-1),k be the probability still in state k immediately
BEFORE the original first d_k. Then, at all actual m>=128 and every
same-epsilon coefficient index k>=0,

                              pi_k>17/100.                (23)

This is a quantitative probability bound, not the required quantitative
second-neighbor bound e_k>=1/15.

Here is a product proof. Put q_c=1/c and n_exp,k=2^k-1-k.
All smaller states have died before the first d_k. Evaluating
P_(H_k)(z)=sum_r B_(2^k-1),r phi_r(z) at z=1/d_k therefore gives

 pi_k=product_(r=1)^k (1-d_(k-r)/d_k)^(2^(r-1)-1)
     =(1-1/d_k)^(n_exp,k)
           product_(r=1)^k(1-q_c^r)^(2^(r-1)-1).           (24)

The second equality uses
1-d_(k-r)/d_k=(1-1/d_k)(1-q_c^r). In particular pi_0=pi_1=1,
pi_2=1-d_0/d_2>19/34, and
pi_3=(1-d_0/d_3)^3(1-d_1/d_3)>(3/4)^3(7/10)>17/100.
For the last comparison, d_3>34/5: the formula
d_3=1+lambda^2(1+epsilon-epsilon^2-epsilon^3) exceeds
1+lambda^2=4+2sqrt(2)>34/5. The bounds on d_0,d_1 are in Sections2,5.

For k>=4 define the positive convergent product

 Phi(q)=product_(r>=1)(1-q^r)^(2^(r-1)-1),  0<q<1/2,
 S_1(q)=sum_(r>=1)(2^(r-1)-1)q^r
       =q/(1-2q)-q/(1-q).

Convergence, as well as the termwise differentiations below on the
closed parameter interval, follows by comparison with sum_r r(2q)^r.
Using log(1-x)>=-x/(1-x) and -log(1-x)>=x in (24) gives

 log(pi_k)-log Phi(q_c)
 >=-n_exp,k/(d_k-1)+sum_(r>k)(2^(r-1)-1)q_c^r
 =-[gamma/(a(c-2))](2q_c)^k
           +[(k+1)/a-1/(c-1)]q_c^k
 >-(325/16)epsilon*(5/6)^k.                              (25)

Here gamma=c-2-a, a>2/5, c-2>2/5, gamma<(13/4)epsilon,
and 2q_c<5/6. The second bracket is positive.

We compare Phi(q_c) with its critical parameter q_0=1/lambda=sqrt(2)-1.
For 0<=epsilon<=1/128, q_c=q_0/(1+epsilon), and

 d/d epsilon log Phi(q_c)
 =1/(1+epsilon) sum_(r>=1)
             (2^(r-1)-1)r q_c^r/(1-q_c^r)
 >=[q_c/(1+epsilon)]S_1'(q_c)>11.                         (26)

Indeed q_c>16/39>41/100 implies q_c/(1+epsilon)>2/5.
Also q_c<5/12 and

 S_1'(q_c)=1/(1-2q_c)^2-1/(1-q_c)^2
          >2500/81-144/49>55/2.

Integrating (26) from0 to epsilon and combining with (25) proves

 log(pi_k)>log Phi(q_0)
              +[11-(325/16)(5/6)^k]epsilon
          >=log Phi(q_0),

since (325/16)(5/6)^4=203125/20736<11.

Finally Phi(q_0)>17/100 follows from elementary bounds, with no
infinite-product evaluation. For 0<=x<1,
-log(1-x)<=x+x^2/[2(1-x)]. The r=1 exponent is zero, and
q_0^2<1/5. Thus

 -log Phi(q_0)<=S_1(q_0)+(5/8)S_1(q_0^2)
 =1+sqrt(2)/2+(5/8)(5-3sqrt(2))/14
 <12/7+11/320<7/4.

The last inequalities use sqrt(2)<10/7 and sqrt(2)>141/100.
The exponential series gives exp(1)<11/4: the sum through degree4
is65/24, and its remaining tail is at most1/100. It also gives
exp(3/4)<17/8: the sum through degree3 is269/128, and the tail
starting at degree4 is at most135/8704; their sum is18427/8704,
which is smaller than17/8. Hence

 exp(7/4)<(11/4)(17/8)=187/32<100/17,
 Phi(q_0)>exp(-7/4)>32/187>17/100.

This finishes (23), including the small indices handled separately.
The cancellation in (25) retains the additive1 in d_k and the actual
epsilon dependence. Bounding the two product factors in (24)
independently would lose that cancellation.

## 11. Scope and remaining work

The new proved-in-draft part of the stated interface is e_i>=0 for
every required index. The stronger entrywise result (7), the identities
(9), (11), and (13), the uniform decimation estimates (17), and the
time localization and stable finite inverse (18)-(22), the row2 load
bound (11b), and the uniform surviving-mass bound (23) have explicit
proofs above.

For a fixed original m, the inherited-boundary identity only requires
e_i>=0, u_i>=0 and b_i>=2/15 at 0<=i<=m-1, the stronger e_i>=1/15
and u_i>=1/16 at the SINGLE index i=m-1, and the load bounds at
2<=i<=m-1. The early formulas already handle b_0,b_1,b_2 and
u_0,u_1,u_2; they are recorded in the preceding boundary draft and
are not replaced here by a positive margin independent of epsilon.
Uniform claims at all i>=127 with fixed epsilon would be stronger
than the quantitative terminal bounds actually used at i=m-1.

After (8) and (11b), the unresolved claims remain b_i>=2/15 and
u_i>=0 for 3<=i<=m-1, the stronger e_(m-1)>=1/15 and
u_(m-1)>=1/16, and the load bounds for 3<=i<=m-1.
This document does not prove the full
kernel positive semidefinite, and it is not a counterexample to those
remaining actual-word claims. Even their proof would only concern the
specified reciprocal-level temporal quotient, not arbitrary legal GD.

The existing same-multiset foil is still a useful warning: its first
few steps also satisfy h_i<s_i+2, and entrywise off-diagonal positivity
alone does not distinguish its negative diagonal-margin behavior.
Thus (7) must not be promoted into a substitute for the original-order
estimates. The exact pair identity (13), unlike that coarse envelope,
does distinguish the original word.

evidence:
# A sharper original-step angular boundary, with a finite mass bound at equality

Status: complete joint proof candidate, **UNVERIFIED**. Ninth max4 launch,
first round (cumulative20). No numerical evaluation, optimizer, installation,
or fact submission is used. This document gives all new arguments together;
earlier unverified common-prefix drafts are not correctness predecessors.
The accepted inputs are `1252b8823bb5a290` (original interpolation and maximal
terminal completion) and `b98bb807d514e80d` (exact benchmark definitions and
the bound B_n<=1+4 n^(log_2 3)).

The old 1/sqrt(2) boundary is not the boundary of the original-step argument.
Retaining the physical leaf preceding the level1 bridge changes it. Moreover,
the movement bound need not divide by its vanishing angular coefficient:
one-block look-ahead controls the missing mass at equality. These assertions
are scoped to the explicit measure below. A separate two-ray construction
shows the limiting sharper boundary is sharp for a local four-step return;
that construction is NOT a full-word construction for the positive mixture.

## 1. Word, measure, normalization, and quantitative statement

Let m>=1024 be an integer, and define

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m, c_chr=sigma(1+1/m),
    a_chr=delta/c_chr, N=2^m, n=N-1,
    epsilon=1/N, eta=1/N^2, l=1+a_chr, k=1+delta.

Use the ACTUAL word H_chr,0=() and

    H_chr,j+1=(H_chr,j,1+a_chr*c_chr^j,H_chr,j), 0<=j<m.

Every subword keeps these enclosing-m parameters. Equivalently the original
step at index i<n is h_i=1+a_chr*c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), where nu_2 is the exponent
of2 in a positive integer. Set rho=1-epsilon/2 and gamma=9/10.

For a bit vector s=(s_0,...,s_(m-1)) define

    chi_s(i)=(-1)^(sum_j s_j i_j),
    B(s)=(-1)^s_0, C_j(s)=(-1)^(s_1+...+s_j), 1<=j<m,

where i_j are the standard binary digits of the original index i. The map
s -> (B,C_1,...,C_(m-1)) is bijective. Choose beta in(0,1), and set
mu_+=-beta, mu_-=gamma. Conditional on B=b, define

    A_b(c)=(1+mu_b)/2 * 1_(all c_j=1)
                +(1-mu_b)/2 * 1_(all c_j=-1),
    P_b(c)=product_(j=1)^(m-1) (1+mu_b c_j)/2,
    w_s=(1+(1-epsilon)B(s))/2
                 *[(1-eta)A_(B(s))(C(s))+eta P_(B(s))(C(s))].       (1)

These are positive weights summing to1. Define the following explicit
finite-m quantities BEFORE choosing beta:

    lambda=rho(1-eta), omega=1-lambda, e=omega/lambda,
    d_mass=(l+k)/(l+1+(1-l)e),
    beta_M=sqrt((1-e)/d_mass)-e,
    p=1-epsilon, d_eps=gamma epsilon/2,
    r_leaf=[(2-l)p+sqrt((2-l)^2 p^2+4(l-1))]/2,
    L_leaf=l/r_leaf,
    beta_R=[k d_eps+sqrt((k+L_leaf)(1+L_leaf p)
                                  +L_leaf^2 d_eps^2)]
                          /[(k+L_leaf)rho].                       (2)

The candidate theorem covers EVERY

    7/10 <= beta <= beta_R,                                      (3)

including the endpoint beta=beta_R. In particular4/5<beta_R<6/7 and
beta_R tends to2^(-1/4), strictly beyond1/sqrt(2). The auxiliary beta_M
is the zero of the simpler mass coefficient; the complete proof crosses
it and reaches beta_R by retaining the actual final level2 bridge.

Prescribe only QUERIED gradients

    g_i=(Gamma_i sqrt(w_s) chi_s(i))_s, 0<=i<n,                    (4)

with arbitrary positive amplitudes Gamma_i. Suppose a finite-dimensional
convex differentiable1-smooth function F realizes (4) along its actual GD
trajectory X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i, and has a minimizer. The anchor, values,
amplitudes and unqueried terminal gradient are otherwise unrestricted.
All isometric realizations of the Gram matrix in(4) are included. Let

    X_star be a true closest minimizer to X_0,
    R=||X_0-X_star||, F_star=min F,
    T_path=sum_(i<n)h_i Gamma_i,
    V_chr=2(F(X_n)-F_star)/R^2.

Then the claimed bounds, uniform over(3), are

    R>0,  T_path<8192 R,
    ||X_i-X_star||<512 R for every0<=i<=n,                        (5)
    ||grad F(X_n)|| <= R[2(3/5)^(N/8)+3*2^17*m/N^2],              (6)
    V_chr <=2048(3/5)^(N/8)+2^29*m/N^2.                          (7)

The comparison uses the exact original benchmark and its normalized
objective2(F(X_n)-F_star)/R^2, preserving the project's factor of2:

    B_n V_chr <=(1+4n^(log_2 3))
                       [2048(3/5)^((n+1)/8)+2^29*m/(n+1)^2]
                   ->0,  n=2^m-1.                              (8)

For L-smooth f apply the theorem to F=(f-f_star)/L, so the normalized
objective is exactly2(f(X_n)-f_star)/(L R^2). No surrogate denominator
or inverse-Gram anchor norm replaces the true closest-minimizer distance.

## 2. Original inequalities and elementary finite bounds

A closest minimizer exists because the nonempty minimizer set is closed,
and a distance-minimizing sequence can be chosen bounded in finite dimension.
The positive initial gradient makes R>0. Translate X_star to0.
Accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` gives all actual original inequalities

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0,
    f_i=F(X_i)-F_star.

The optimum sample has position, gradient and value0. Adding orientations
gives, for any two actual samples,

    ||g_i-g_j||^2 <= <g_i-g_j,X_i-X_j>.                           (9)

In particular <g_i,X_i>>=||g_i||^2, and smoothness gives
||g_i||<=||X_i||. A physical step0<h<=2 therefore satisfies

    ||X-hg||^2<=||X||^2-h(2-h)||g||^2,
    ||grad F(X-hg)||<=||g||.                                    (10)

For the second assertion put d_g=grad F(X-hg)-g in(9):
-h<d_g,g>>=||d_g||^2. Expanding ||g+d_g||^2 gives the assertion.
For h>=2 the same optimum inequality gives instead

    ||X-hg||^2<=||X||^2+h(h-2)||g||^2
                  <=(h-1)^2||X||^2.                            (11)

All applications below distinguish these two regimes.

The enclosing parameters satisfy

    7/5<l<3/2, 199/100<k<2,
    1<delta*c_chr<5/2,
    e<1/1000, 1/sqrt(lambda)<1001/1000,
    sqrt(omega)/lambda<1/255, 1-epsilon>999/1000.                 (12)

For example sqrt2<99/70, c_chr<49/20 and delta>99/100 give l>7/5;
c_chr>2 gives l<3/2. Also delta*c_chr=sigma(1-1/m^2)<5/2 and is>1.
The powers of2 give omega<=epsilon/2+eta<1/65536, which implies the
displayed mixture bounds. These estimates require no numerical evaluation.

Because l>1 and e>=0,

    d_mass>1+(99/100)/(5/2)=349/250>11/8,
    d_mass<3/2.                                                (13)

For the second inequality, subtract l+2 from
(3/2)[l+1-(l-1)e]; the result is (l-1)(1/2-3e/2)>0.
Thus

    beta_M>sqrt(333/500)-1/1000>4/5,
    beta_M<sqrt(8/11)<6/7.                                    (14)

The first last comparison follows from (801/1000)^2<333/500; the second
follows from392<396.

We also need a finite bound for beta_R BEFORE the mass proof. Define,
for a trial beta in[0,1],

    z=-rho beta+d_eps, w=-rho beta-d_eps,
    alpha_ret=1-k z^2+L_leaf(p-zw),
    alpha_0=(l+1)-(l+k)beta^2.

The quadratic alpha_ret has negative leading coefficient, positive
constant term, and exactly one positive root, the beta_R in(2).
The polynomial in(25) below, evaluated at p and1, gives
p<=r_leaf<1 and therefore l<=L_leaf<=l+3epsilon. Direct substitution gives
z^2>=beta^2-2epsilon and p-zw<=1-beta^2+epsilon. Consequently

    alpha_ret<=alpha_0+9epsilon for0<=beta<=1.                 (14a)

Indeed the extra upper bound is
2k epsilon+3epsilon(1-beta^2)+l epsilon+3epsilon^2<9epsilon.
At beta=6/7 this gives
alpha_ret< -157/2450+9epsilon<0, using l<3/2,k>199/100.
At beta=4/5, z^2<=beta^2,zw<=beta^2 and p-zw>0 give instead
alpha_ret>=alpha_0-l epsilon>28/125-(3/2)epsilon>0.
Thus4/5<beta_R<6/7. For every beta in(3), alpha_ret>=0, and(14a) implies

    (l+k)beta^2<=l+1+9epsilon.                               (14b)

Finally epsilon,e->0, r_leaf->1,l->sqrt2,k->2. Both beta_M and beta_R
tend to sqrt((1+sqrt2)/(2+sqrt2))=2^(-1/4).

## 3. Movement without division by a vanishing angular margin

Split the SAME probability measure into the component B=1 with all prefix
signs common, of mass lambda, and its remaining component of mass omega.
In the first component the unit directions repeat a_0,a_0,b_0,b_0 and
<a_0,b_0>=-beta. Hence the full gradients admit the direct-sum realization

    g_i=Gamma_i(sqrt(lambda)u_i,sqrt(omega)z_i),
    u_i in{a_0,b_0}, ||z_i||=1.                                (15)

An isometry on the gradient span, extended to the initial displacement,
preserves the Gram data and true radius; thus this representation loses
no actual realization. Write X_0=(x^c,x^r).

At a block start t=4r,0<=t<=N-4, let P_a and P_b be the total previous
amplitude-weighted physical step masses on a_0 and b_0, respectively.
Put T=P_a+P_b and

    A_x=<a_0,x^c>/sqrt(lambda)-P_a+beta P_b,
    B_x=<b_0,x^c>/sqrt(lambda)-P_b+beta P_a,
    r_0=sqrt(omega)R/lambda.

The remainder displacement before t has norm at most sqrt(omega)T.
Let A=Gamma_t,C=Gamma_(t+1). The first physical leaf gives A>=C by(10).
At the QUERIED sample t+1, its optimum inequality yields

    A_x >= l A+C/lambda-r_0-e(T+l A)
         = l(1-e)A+(1+e)C-r_0-eT.                            (16)

Indeed the remainder contribution to <g_(t+1),X_(t+1)>/C is at most
sqrt(omega)[R+sqrt(omega)(T+l A)]. Division by lambda proves(16).

The mass of the first two physical steps is D_a=l A+k C. For0<=C/A<=1,
the function (l+k r)/[l(1-e)+(1+e)r] is increasing: its derivative has
the sign of k(1-e)-(1+e)>0 by(12). Its value at1 is d_mass. Consequently

    D_a<=d_mass(A_x+r_0+eT).                                 (17)

At the QUERIED sample t+2, the coarse direction is b_0. Dropping its
positive norm term from the optimum inequality gives

    B_x+(beta+e)D_a+r_0+eT>=0.                               (18)

Substituting(17), then expanding A_x,B_x,T, gives EXACTLY

    c_a P_a+c_b P_b
       <=<b_0+d_mass(beta+e)a_0,x^c>/sqrt(lambda)
                         +[1+d_mass(beta+e)]r_0,
    c_a=(beta+e)[d_mass(1-e)-1],
    c_b=1-e-d_mass(beta+e)^2.                                (19)

Throughout(3),

    c_a>(7/10)[(11/8)(999/1000)-1]>1/4.

Since beta+e<1, the right side of(19) is<4R by(12),(13).
When c_b>=0 this already gives P_a<16R at every block start, including
equality c_b=0. To cover the entire interval(3), let
xi=max(0,-c_b). Equation(14b), epsilon<=2e, and the denominator
D_mass=l+1+(1-l)e>9/4 imply

    xi <=[9epsilon+10e+3e^2]/D_mass<13e<13/1000.              (19a)

For this calculation, the exact numerator of
d_mass(beta+e)^2-(1-e) is
(l+k)beta^2-(l+1)+[2(l+k)beta+2l]e+(k+1)e^2;
the last two coefficients are<10 and<3, respectively.

We do not divide by c_b. First rearrange(18):

    (1-e)P_b <=<b_0,x^c>/sqrt(lambda)
                            +(beta+e)(P_a+D_a)+r_0.           (21)

Write A_rad=(1/sqrt(lambda)+sqrt(omega)/lambda)/(1-e)<2 and
v_mass=(beta+e)/(1-e)<2. If the next block start exists, its a-mass is
exactly P_a+D_a. Thus(21) reads P_b<=A_rad R+v_mass P_a(next).

For the LAST block start t_last=N-4, use its preceding block t_prev=N-8.
The bridge between them has ORIGINAL level2, H_2=1+delta*c_chr<7/2.
Writing C=Gamma_(t_prev+1), the two following short steps k,l imply
Gamma_(t_prev+2),Gamma_(t_prev+3)<=C. The b-mass added between these
block starts is therefore at most(l+H_2)C. Since the a-mass added there
is D_a=l Gamma_(t_prev)+k C, the added b-mass is at most
[(l+H_2)/k]D_a<3D_a. It follows from(21) at t_prev that

    P_b(last)<=2R+5P_a(last).                               (20a)

If c_b<0, apply(19) only at this last start and substitute(20a):

    [c_a-5xi]P_a(last)<=(4+2xi)R<5R.

By(19a), c_a-5xi>1/4-65/1000>1/8. Hence P_a(last)<40R.
If c_b>=0, the earlier bound16R applies instead. In either case,
the nonnegative chronological a-mass is nondecreasing, so

    P_a<64R at EVERY block start.                            (20)

For each t<=N-8, (21) and the bound at its next block start now give
P_b<2R+2*64R=130R. Hence

    T<194R and ||X_t||<195R at every block start t<=N-8.       (22)

The three following steps are l,k,l<2, so their samples also obey195R.
This covers every sample before the final block. From t=N-8 the next
fourth step, at N-5, has ORIGINAL level2 and size1+delta*c_chr.
Equation(11) bounds the norm after it by (delta*c_chr)195R<512R.
The final three short steps keep this bound. Thus all samples obey(5).

There are just seven physical steps left from N-8 to n. Their total
stepsize is4l+2k+(1+delta*c_chr)<14. Every gradient there has norm<512R.
Therefore

    T_path<194R+14*512R<8192R,
    K_path:=R+T_path<2^14 R.                                (23)

This mass bound is obtained BEFORE estimating any eta perturbation.
It remains uniform as c_b decreases through zero to the range(19a).
No factors1/c_b,
1/(1-2beta^2),1/(1-beta),1/epsilon, or1/eta are concealed in(23).

## 4. Exact finite-epsilon correlations and the physical-leaf threshold

For the return argument split(1) differently: the entire common-prefix
component has mass1-eta. Write its common prefix sign as V. Its four unit
directions, in the original order modulo4, are

    a_e=1,a_o=B,b_e=V,b_o=BV.

Set

    p=E B=1-epsilon,
    z=E V=-rho beta+gamma epsilon/2,
    w=E(BV)=-rho beta-gamma epsilon/2.                        (24)

The correlations are <a_e,a_o>=<b_e,b_o>=p,
<a_o,b_o>=<a_e,b_e>=z, and <a_e,b_o>=<a_o,b_e>=w.
All finite-epsilon terms are retained. The full measure has these same
three correlations whenever only B and one individual prefix sign occur.

At ANY original leaf with amplitude ratio r>0, (9) is exactly

    r^2+(l-2)p r-(l-1)<=0.

Let r_leaf be its unique positive root. Evaluation at p and1 gives

    p<=r_leaf<1,
    r_leaf=[(2-l)p+sqrt((2-l)^2 p^2+4(l-1))]/2.                (25)

The relevant original-step return coefficient is

    alpha_ret=1-k z^2+(l/r_leaf)(p-zw).                       (26)

To state its finite-m zero exactly, put L_leaf=l/r_leaf and
d_eps=gamma epsilon/2. Substitution in(26) gives

    alpha_ret=1+L_leaf p-(k+L_leaf)rho^2 beta^2
                   +2k rho d_eps beta+(L_leaf-k)d_eps^2.

Its positive zero is

    beta_R=[k d_eps+sqrt((k+L_leaf)(1+L_leaf p)
                                  +L_leaf^2 d_eps^2)]
                          /[(k+L_leaf)rho].                  (27)

In contrast, the old coefficient1-kz^2 has positive zero
(1/sqrt(k)+d_eps)/rho. Replacing either by1/sqrt2 at finite m is
incorrect. The limit of(27) is2^(-1/4), while the old zero tends1/sqrt2.

For(3), alpha_ret>=0 by its exact positive root(27). Also -z>=2/3, p>0, and
p-zw>=p-beta^2>0 by(12),(14). Also z^2<=beta^2, zw<=beta^2 and
L_leaf>=l. To compare the auxiliary mass boundary with this return
boundary, specialize temporarily to beta<=beta_M. Then

    alpha_ret >=(l+1)-(l+k)beta^2-l epsilon
       >=2l e-(l-1)e^2-l epsilon.                            (28)

The second inequality uses beta^2<=(1-e)/d_mass and the exact denominator
in(2). Since omega>=epsilon/2, epsilon<=2e/(1+e); the last expression in
(28) is at least e^2[2l/(1+e)-(l-1)]>0. In particular beta_M<=beta_R.
The two explicit finite thresholds need not coincide. The strengthened
mass proof in section3 covers their gap, including beta=beta_R. Neither
threshold is asserted to be the full-word feasibility boundary beyond
the obstruction interval for positive epsilon and eta.

## 5. Original return pairs, with no inverse-alpha loss

For any original i,j the full direction correlation differs from its
common-prefix correlation by at most2eta. If endpoint amplitudes are A,B
and the intervening total physical mass is T_ij, the resulting difference
in the cocoercivity expression is at most

    2eta(A+B)T_ij+4eta AB <=4eta K_path(A+B).                  (29)

Here T_ij<=T_path<K_path and A,B<=K_path, which were proved first.
Let e_0=4eta K_path.

Take an original queried odd-b return j=4r+3 with j+4<n. Write its
physical steps and gradient amplitudes as

    j: H on b_o with B_0,
    j+1: l on a_e with A_0,
    j+2: k on a_o with C_0,
    j+3: l on b_e with E_0,

M=B_0+bbar C_0 and Delta=D_0-B_0. In the common component set

    Z=-H B_0 b_o-l A_0 a_e,

       <=(tau C_0-B_0)X-l A_0 C_0(p-zw)+e_0(C_0+B_0).       (30)

                      +M Delta+M l E_0 p
       <=e_0(C_0+B_0)+M e_0(D_0+B_0)/Delta.                 (32)

l A_0 C_0(p-zw), losing the sharper coefficient.

Because bbar>=2/3, C_0+B_0<=(3/2)M. Suppose Delta>=2m e_0.
The right side of(32) is at most

    (5/2)e_0 M+(1/m)B_0 M
      <=(5/2)e_0 M+B_0^2+(bbar/m)B_0 C_0.

The left side is at least B_0^2+(bbar/m)B_0 C_0+M Delta, since
2-k=1/m and alpha_ret>=0. Cancellation forces Delta<=(5/2)e_0,
contradicting m>=1024. Thus EVERY such original return satisfies

    Gamma_(j+4)<=Gamma_j+d_amp,
    d_amp=2^17*m*eta*R,                                     (33)

by(23). This proof also works with alpha_ret=0. It retains the explicit
factor m=1/(2-k), rather than hiding it in a perturbation symbol.
There is no1/alpha_ret loss. For eta=0 the same calculation directly
forbids Delta>0 whenever alpha_ret>=0 and the stated signs hold.

## 6. Uniform contractions at actual low bridges

For any original bridge of level q>=1 and its following leaf, let their
three amplitudes be A,M,D and steps1+u,l. The relative character signs are
1,B C_q,C_q. Therefore the FULL law gives correlations w,p,z, respectively,
and the original endpoint-pair sum is

    0>=-u A^2+D^2+(u-1)z A D+l M(pD-wA).                     (34)

The leaf is short, so M>=D. Also pD-wA>0. The positive ratio t=D/A
therefore satisfies

    F_u(t):=(1+lp)t^2+[(u-1)z-lw]t-u<=0.                   (35)

This polynomial has one positive root. On(3), -w>=beta and -z<=beta,
because beta<6/7<gamma. Also1+lp>239/100.

    F_delta(1/2)>239/400+49/100-1=35/400>0.

## 7. Actual last steps, free terminal, and the exact benchmark

Let K=N/4. The queried odd-b amplitudes are

    B_r=Gamma_(4r+3),0<=r<=K-2.

                      <=2theta^(N/8)R+3d_amp.                (37)

## 8. Nonvacuity for these same positive weights

This calibration is not a competitive lower bound. For the same actual
word and weights, additionally prescribe the terminal character gradient.
Let H_max=max_i h_i, kappa=min(1,(min_i h_i-1)/4)>0 and

    q_decay=kappa/[8(H_max+kappa+1)], Gamma_i=q_decay^i,
    f_i=(kappa+1/2)Gamma_i^2, 0<=i<=n.

The full gradient Gram G is positive definite: the full character matrix
is invertible, as summing chi_s(i)chi_s(j) over s is N for i=j and0
otherwise, and every weight and amplitude is positive. Define

    b_i=(kappa+1)Gamma_i^2+sum_(t<i)h_t G_ti,

An explicit global function is

    C_poly=conv(0,g_0,...,g_n),
    F_poly(X)=max_(v in C_poly)[<X,v>-||v||^2/2].

Its maximizer is the Euclidean projection P_(C_poly)(X). The projection

At X_i the displayed Q inequalities are precisely the projection normal
conditions at each vertex (and the optimum). Thus the function realizes

Its minimizer set is the polar cone {Z:<Z,g_i><=0 for all i}. The true
distance to that set is positive and is the R used in the theorem; no
identity with||X_0|| or with an inverse-Gram expression is asserted.

## 9. Sharp local scope test beyond the limiting boundary

The following exact construction tests a proposed extension of return
nonexpansion to all beta<1. It is for the two-ray boundary epsilon=eta=0,
and uses a whole global function on its own four-step segment.
It is not a realization of the finite positive mixture over H_chr,m.

Fix1<l<2,1<k<2, unit vectors a,b with<a,b>=-beta,0<beta<1, and set

    t=l+1, s=l+k, E_ang=s beta^2-t.

Suppose E_ang>0. For a positive number J with J E_ang>t^2, set

    H=1+J, A=beta J/t, D=J E_ang/t^2>1,
    C_triangle=conv(0,Aa,Db),
    F_triangle(X)=max_(v in C_triangle)[<X,v>-||v||^2/2].       (38)

By the argument in section8 this is one convex differentiable1-smooth
function. Start at X_0=b and take the ACTUAL four steps H,l,k,l. The
claimed gradients and positions are

    g_0=b, g_1=Aa, g_2=Aa, g_3=Db, g_4=Db,
    X_1=-Jb, X_2=-Jb-lAa,
    X_3=-Jb-sAa, X_4=-(J+lD)b-sAa.                            (39)

ordered interpolation inequality through the same global function.

At X_1 the residual X_1-Aa has a-projection lA>0 and b-projection

-J(1-beta^2)<0; both vertex normals again hold.

beta D-(k-1)A<0. The latter follows from

    D/A=E_ang/(beta t)<(k-1)beta/t.

X_4-Db has b-projection0 and a-projection

    t beta D-(k-1)A=-s(1-beta^2)A<0.

The normals hold at all vertices and their convex hull, proving(39).

The minimizers form the polar cone of C_triangle. For any minimizer Z,
<b,Z><=0; hence||b-Z||^2>=1, with equality at0. Thus the TRUE initial
distance is1. Since <X_4,b>=D, the terminal value is D^2/2 and the

For the actual enclosing-m values l,k, the local condition is exactly

    beta^2>(l+1)/(l+k).                                     (40)

An original level q>=2 bridge has J=a_chr*c_chr^q and is followed by
l,k,l. Thus the four physical steps coincide with such an actual segment
whenever q<m and a_chr*c_chr^q*E_ang>(l+1)^2. This exposes the entire
angular-gap cost J>(l+1)^2/E_ang. It does not assume that the segment can

Conversely at epsilon=eta=0, (25) has r_leaf=1 and (26) becomes
alpha_ret=(l+1)-(l+k)beta^2. Equation(32), with zero error, forbids ANY
positive return growth when alpha_ret>=0. Therefore(40) is the exact
boundary for the existence of an expanding two-ray four-step return
with arbitrarily selectable high step H. This establishes local
sharpness, not a finite-mixture or full-word threshold.

### The explicit expanding triangle cannot pass the next actual leaf

There is a concrete compatibility failure for the SAME function(38),
not merely an absent proof of concatenation. Suppose its expanding
segment starts at an actual bridge of level q>=3. The next bridge,
four indices later, necessarily has level2; write H_2=1+delta*c_chr.
Starting from X_4 in(39), its next position is

    X_5=X_4-H_2 Db=-(J+(l+H_2)D)b-sAa,
    <X_5,a>/A=-(k-1)+(l+H_2)E_ang/t.

Since beta<1, E_ang<s-t=k-1=delta. Hence

    <X_5,a>/A <delta(H_2-1)/t
                       <(5/2)/(12/5)=25/24<l.               (41)

For the original prescribed ray pattern, the next two gradients must
both lie on the positive a ray. If g_5=C a with0<C<A, projection onto
C_triangle and the two vertices0,Aa force <X_5,a>=C. The next actual
leaf gives <X_6,a>=(1-l)C<0. If g_5=Aa instead, (41) gives

its normal with the zero vertex would require <X_6,a>>=||g_6||>0.
If g_5 is not on that ray, the prescribed pattern has already failed.

An original level2 choice cannot satisfy J E_ang>t^2 in(38), since
J=delta*c_chr<5/2,E_ang<delta<1 and t^2>(12/5)^2. Thus ANY expanding
segment of(38) embedded at an actual bridge has q>=3, and the above
two queried samples actually exist in the following block. Therefore
this explicit sharp local constructor cannot continue through the next
level2 bridge and leaf for ANY beta<1. It is not a candidate full-word
adversary. A different function, changing its same-ray gradient/value
geometry, would have to repair precisely this next-leaf compatibility.

## 10. Remaining compatibility condition and budget scope

The interval[7/10,beta_R] includes a fixed supercritical neighborhood of
the OLD1/sqrt2 threshold, and the explicit law beta_m=beta_R is the exact
finite-m zero of the original-step return coefficient. It tends
to the sharper2^(-1/4) boundary. Equations(5)--(8) exclude all its positive
amplitude histories, all anchors and values, and all terminal completions.

There is no full-word counterexample at beta>beta_R here. The concrete
remaining issue is to reconcile expanding high returns beyond(26) with
one function's earlier and later ray data, the alternating actual level2
returns, and a true-distance payoff surviving the exact B_n comparison.
The triangle in(38) uses one fixed cap on each ray and fails the explicit
next-leaf compatibility(41). The finite gap between beta_M and beta_R has been included
in the obstruction by the actual final-bridge mass calculation(20a).

No claim is made that failure of(19) or(26) proves whole-word feasibility.
The original all-schedule minimax target remains open. The task allocates
no verifier call, so this document and its shared copy are candidates,
not facts. All external retrieval hits required short steps or a different
flow regime; no external theorem is used. The only new machinery is
algebra in the already audited original finite-interpolation regime.

## 1. The exact unchanged seed and every seed interpolation row

# C77. A finite-base uniform ray enclosure for the exact scalar benchmark

Status: COMPLETE JOINT PROOF CANDIDATE, UNVERIFIED. This is not a fact in the
project graph. No verifier is allocated or called. The finite certificate
below was produced by the four explicitly authorized benchmark runs; it is
an exact integer enclosure computation, not a floating-point extrapolation.
Its source, every finite DP row, base-test slacks, and source hashes are public.
The proof still requires independent mathematical/verifier acceptance.

Seventh max3 launch, first round, cumulative round 16. The four-run option is
now CLOSED. Its measured computation, including saved-table certificate
postprocessing, is 32.344760773994494 seconds, below 60; all indices are at most
4095. No seed optimization, installation, or fact_submit was performed.

## 1. Definitions and exact scope

Use the exact recurrences in accepted facts 0be8b54e0a33381c and
b98bb807d514e80d. Set

    P_n = 1+S_circle(n),  B_n = 1+2S_bullet(n),  P_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(a,b) = (a+b+sqrt((a+b)^2+4ab))/2,
    G(a,d) = 2a+d/2+sqrt(d^2+8ad)/2,
    P_n = max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(P_k,P_l),
    B_n = max_(k+l=n-1) G(P_k,B_l).

All maxima run over nonnegative integer k,l, with EVERY original split
retained. Write lambda=1+sqrt(2), rho=log_2(lambda), s=sqrt(lambda), and
q_n=sqrt(B_n). In this document q_n is a square-root mass, not an objective
coefficient. To discuss leaf counts, also write U_N=P_(N-1) and V_N=B_(N-1)
for N>=1, and U_0=0. The source paper's W_N equals V_N, not the project's
worst-case functional W_n(h).

The target scalar claim is

    Z_b = lim_(j->infinity) lambda^(-j) B_(b*2^j-1),
    Z_15 < (773/100) Z_3.                                  (E5)

The proof below derives existence of these limits as well as their enclosure.
It does not need the source's qualitative objective phase theorem.

The stronger conjecture B_(2n)<=lambda B_n for all n is NOT used. The
argument allows a rigorously bounded positive defect beyond the finite base.
The source's global one-pivot support envelope and the zero-prefix loophole
in C75 are not used.

## 2. Precisely matched literature input

The only non-elementary external input is balanced optimality of the
SYMMETRIC scalar recurrence, as proved in Corollary 4.2 of:

Yu Liu, Kang Chen, Rujun Jiang, Tianyu Wang (2026), *Optimal Recursive
Composition and Dyadic Phase Laws for Gradient Descent with Predetermined
Stepsizes*, arXiv:2609.11788v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2609.11788v1 .

Its complete statement used here is: for U_0=0, U_1=1 and
U_N=max_(1<=m<N) Omega(U_m,U_(N-m)), the sequence is increasing and

    U_(2a)=lambda U_a,
    U_(2a+1)=Omega(U_a,U_(a+1)),  a>=0.                    (2.1)

The second identity includes U_1=Omega(U_0,U_1). The source defines its
kernel K by exactly our Omega. Proposition 2.5 and identical initial values
match its U_N to P_(N-1), by induction. No assertion about equality of ambient
primitive and s-composable certificate classes is imported. In particular,
balanced splitting is NEVER assumed for the asymmetric B recurrence.

The exact paper was downloaded in the prior round; its local text is
downloads/liu_chen_jiang_wang_2609.11788v1.txt. Section 2, Theorem 3.1 and
its proof, Theorem 4.1/Corollary 4.2 and their proofs, and the adjacent-ratio
proof in Appendix C.2 were read. Matlas returned unrelated statements;
this reference is grounded directly in the primary arXiv paper, not falsely
represented as a Matlas hit. No external_refs submission is made because no
fact_submit is authorized. The subsequent scalar estimates are proved here.

## 3. Elementary growth and adjacent-value bounds

First, 1<rho<4/3: lambda>2 and lambda^3=7+5sqrt(2)<16. Thus s>3/2
and lambda^(3/2)<4.

For completeness, Omega(x,y)<=(x^(1/rho)+y^(1/rho))^rho for x,y>=0.
For positive x,y, put A=x^(1/rho), C=y^(1/rho), and T=(A+C)^rho.
Let D(t)=(1+t)^rho-1. For g(z)=log D(exp z), differentiation gives

    g''(z) = rho*t*(1+t)^(rho-2)
             *((1+t)^rho-1-rho*t)/D(t)^2 > 0,  t=exp z.

The last bracket has value zero at t=0 and strictly positive derivative for
t>0. Hence D(t)D(1/t)>=D(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. It follows that
(T-x)(T-y)>=2xy, or T^2-(x+y)T-xy>=0. Since T>=x+y and Omega is the
positive root of that polynomial, T>=Omega(x,y). Zero arguments follow by
continuity. Induction in the full primitive recurrence gives U_N<=N^rho.
Balanced dyadic joins give U_(2^j)=lambda^j; monotonicity then yields

    N^rho/lambda <= U_N <= N^rho,  N>=1.                  (3.1)

Also G(a,d)>=Omega(a,d) for a,d>=0. Indeed, after multiplying their
difference by two, the required inequality is
3a+sqrt(d^2+8ad)>=sqrt(a^2+6ad+d^2); squaring the nonnegative sides
leaves 8a^2+2ad+6a sqrt(d^2+8ad)>=0. Induction gives V_N>=U_N.

Here is the adjacent primitive estimate derived from (2.1). Let
R_N=U_(N+1)/U_N, Delta(r)=sqrt(r^2+6r+1), and

    T0(r)=(1+r+Delta(r))/(2lambda),
    T1(r)=lambda*(Delta(r)-r-1)/2.

Then R_(2N)=T0(R_N), R_(2N+1)=T1(R_N). Both maps fix 1 and have positive
derivative at most 1/2 on [1,lambda]: their derivatives are
(1+(r+3)/Delta(r))/(2lambda) and lambda*((r+3)/Delta(r)-1)/2;
(r+3)/Delta(r) has derivative -8/Delta(r)^3. Starting at R_1=lambda,
binary induction gives

    0<R_N-1 <= (lambda-1)/2^floor(log_2 N) <= 2sqrt(2)/N.

Using (3.1), U_(N+1)-U_N<=2sqrt(2) N^(rho-1). With U_0=0 this implies
U_m-U_(m-1)<=2sqrt(2) m^(rho-1) for every m>=1.

The full dominant recurrence now gives

    0 < V_(N+1)-V_N <= 8sqrt(2) N^(rho-1).                (3.2)

For the upper bound, take a maximizing prefix m for V_(N+1). If m>=2,
compare it to the admissible split (m-1,N+1-m) for V_N. If m=1, use
G(U_0,V_N)=V_N. The derivative of G with respect to its first variable is
2+2d/sqrt(d^2+8ad)<=4. Since m<=N, the bound follows. Strict increase
follows by choosing prefix 1 in the recurrence.

Consequently, with Delta_n=q_(n+1)-q_n and barq_n=(q_n+q_(n+1))/2,

    Delta_n <= 4sqrt(2lambda) (n+1)^(rho/2-1),
    delta_n := Delta_n^2/(4barq_n)
             <= 8lambda^(3/2) (n+1)^(rho/2-2)
             < 32 n^(-4/3),  n>=1.                       (3.3)

The denominator bound used here is q_n>=sqrt(U_(n+1))
>=(n+1)^(rho/2)/sqrt(lambda). No concavity of q_n is asserted.

## 4. Exact merge inequality and contraction along maximizing trees

Let a,b,d>0, write Q=sqrt(d), u=T_b(Q), t=T_a(u), where

    T_a(v)=(v+sqrt(v^2+8a))/2,  T_a(v)^2=G(a,v^2).

If a<=d, then

    G(a,G(b,d)) < G(Omega(a,b),d).                        (4.1)

To prove this, u>Q and Q(u+Q)>2Q^2>=2a. Since t is the positive
solution of t^2-ut=2a, this implies t<u+Q. Set r=t/u and c=a+br.
The polynomial defining Omega gives

    c^2-(a+b)c-ab = ab*(t-u-Q)/u < 0.

Here r(r-1)=2a/u^2 and 2b/u^2=1-Q/u were substituted to obtain the
identity. Thus c<Omega(a,b). Finally,
t^2-Qt=2a+(u-Q)t=2(a+bt/u)=2c<2Omega(a,b), so T_Omega(a,b)(Q)>t.
Squaring proves (4.1).

Consider two successive right-continuation joins in ANY maximizing B tree.
Let their primitive leaf counts be m1,m2 and the remaining leaf count be R.
Their values are a=U_m1, b=U_m2, d=V_R. The same total leaf count permits
merging the two primitive blocks: Omega(a,b)<=U_(m1+m2). Therefore (4.1)
would strictly improve the maximizing tree if a<=d. Necessarily a>d.
By (3.1) and V_R>=U_R,

    m1^rho >= a > d >= R^rho/lambda,
    R < 2m1,
    R < (2/3)(m1+m2+R).                                  (4.2)

Thus the remaining leaf count decreases by a factor less than 2/3 every
TWO edges along a maximizing right spine. This is an optimality argument
for the exact full DP, not a restriction imposed on allowed splits.

## 5. A one-step rounding defect inequality

Extend P_-1=0. Let v(x) be linear interpolation of q_n on nonnegative
integers: v(n+theta)=(1-theta)q_n+theta q_(n+1), 0<=theta<=1. Define

    e_t = max(0, q_t/s - v(t/2)),  t>=0.                  (5.1)

For a maximizing split k+l=t-1, the claim is

    e_t <= e_l                              if t is even,
    e_t <= e_l+delta_floor(t/2)              if t is odd. (5.2)

Only t>4095 will require the odd formula, so delta_0 need not be bounded.

The primitive bounds from (2.1) are

    P_(2a+1)/lambda=P_a,
    P_(2a)/lambda<= (P_(a-1)+P_a)/2.                      (5.3)

For a>=1 the second follows from
Omega(x,y)<=lambda(x+y)/2, obtained using 4xy<=(x+y)^2. For a=0,
P_0/lambda<=1/2=(P_-1+P_0)/2 because lambda>2.

The exact dominant split inequality can be written without a radical:

    2P_i+q_j q_m <= q_m^2,  i+j=m-1.                    (5.4)

It is equivalent to T_(P_i)(q_j)<=q_m. We additionally permit the formal
boundary i=-1,j=m, where (5.4) is equality.

If t=2n and k=2a+1,l=2b, then a+b=n-1. Use (5.4) directly. If
k=2a,l=2b+1, then a+b=n-1; average (5.4) at the two splits

For t=2n+1, set Qbar=(q_n+q_(n+1))/2. If k=2a+1,l=2b+1,
then a+b=n-1. Average the inequalities with parent/split
(n;a,b) and (n+1;a,b+1). For u=P_a and w=(q_b+q_(b+1))/2, this gives

    2u+Qbar*w-Qbar^2 <= (Delta_n^2-Delta_n*Delta_b)/4
                       <= Delta_n^2/4.

If k=2a,l=2b, then a+b=n. Average parent/split
(n;a-1,b) and (n+1;a,b). With u=(P_(a-1)+P_a)/2 and w=q_b,
the corresponding upper bound is Delta_n^2/4. Boundary a=0 uses the
formal equality in (5.4). In both cases w<=Qbar. The derivative of
y^2-wy-2u for y>=Qbar is at least Qbar. Its positive root is therefore
at most Qbar+Delta_n^2/(4Qbar)=Qbar+delta_n.

Finally, T_a is increasing and 1-Lipschitz in its nonnegative argument:
T_a'(v)=(1+v/sqrt(v^2+8a))/2<=1. Homogeneity and
q_l/s<=v(l/2)+e_l imply

           <= T_(P_k/lambda)(v(l/2))+e_l.
