evidence:
# An endpoint-box exclusion in the full four-step primitive cone

Status: complete joint research DRAFT, not verifier accepted. This is the
one analytical round authorized by TASK.md and master guidance
98d603742ebc21e3. The completed-round count advances from 25 to 26; the
one earlier interrupted attempt is retained separately. No solver,
numerical/model evaluation, word scan, fixed replay, installation, or
fact_submit was used. All calculations below are symbolic proof text.

The accepted inputs are facts 04219554e41d9750, Section 10, and
1252b8823bb5a290 for the interpolation orientation. Drafts
443f4b4325a9901d and 554ec17f7f590bf0 were read for direction, not used
as correctness premises. Every other assertion needed here is proved
within this document. In particular no compact-domain, clipping-branch,
or triangle claim from an unverified draft is a premise.

## 1. Result and exact scope

Let h=(h_0,h_1,h_2,h_3) have arbitrary nonnegative real entries, let
s=sum h_i and C=1+s. There is no full primitive certificate from
accepted fact 04219554e41d9750 with

    C >= 193/25,     7/5 <= h_0,h_3 <= 3/2.                 (1)

All twenty ordered multipliers remain arbitrary and nonnegative, and
positive semidefiniteness is required on all five original formal
gradients. No support, rank, ordering, symmetry, saturation, fixed
capacity, or primitive-prefix assumption is made.

Write a=h_0-1, b=h_1-1, c=h_2-1, d=h_3-1. A stronger quantitative
statement gives an explicit witness alternative. Under (1), either
one of the two middle cut tests fails, giving the explicit scalar
clipped-gradient function in Section 3, or

    C*a*b*c*d > 78744/78125 = 1+619/78125.                 (2)

In the latter case the actual function f(x)=x^2/2, started at x_0=1,
has primitive energy

    V_h < 1-(78744/78125)^2 < 0.                           (3)

This is an exclusion of step data in the full certificate cone, not
failure of a multiplier construction ansatz. It decides a region that
lies strictly outside the previously excluded paired-endpoint region:
every word in (1) satisfies

    d_pair(h) >= 9/25 > 1/20,                             (4)

where

    d_pair(h)=min{max(|h_1-h_0|,|h_2-h_3|),
                  max(|h_2-h_0|,|h_1-h_3|)}.

The proof does not assume bc>=1. It applies to the remaining bc<1
branch too. It is obtained by jointly using necessary cut and quadratic
tests; it is not claimed to be a new scalar test independent of those
tests. No point satisfying all earlier necessary tests is claimed in
the excluded region.

An additional full-matrix necessary endpoint inequality is proved in
Section 6. Its independence from all earlier scalar tests has not been
established. Section 7 audits the sign, rank, zero-step, and congruence
identities in the previous full-support construction interface.

No improving seed or unrestricted four-step nonexistence theorem is
proved. The original all-schedule exact-profile target remains open.

## 2. Full certificate and the actual primitive energy

Indices i,j run from 0 to 4. Put e=(1,1,1,1,1)^T,
P_i=sum_{t<i} h_t, P_0=0, P_4=s. Let T have diagonal 1,
T_it=h_t for t<i, and zero above the diagonal. Define

    omega=(-2h_0,-2h_1,-2h_2,-2h_3,2s)^T,
    D=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_3(2-h_3),-s(s+2)),
    L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
    M=D+sym(LT),          sym(A)=(A+A^T)/2.

The required full certificate has Lambda_ii=0,

    Lambda_ij>=0 (i!=j),       L^T e=omega,       M>=0.     (5)

Here M>=0 means positive semidefinite on all of R^5. For actual
smooth convex data with smoothness 1 and x_{i+1}=x_i-h_i g_i, put

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2 sum_{i<4} h_i(f_i-f_4)
        +sum_{i<4} h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-s(s+1)||g_4||^2.

The accepted full-space identity is

    V_h+sum_{i!=j} Lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g_0,...,g_4)>.

Every actual smooth convex trajectory has Q_ij<=0. Thus (5) implies
V_h>=0 on every such trajectory. We use only this sufficient-certificate
implication; no unproved dual attainment or certificate necessity enters.

For data satisfying f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2, expansion of the GD
update gives

    sum_{i<4}[2h_i<x_i,g_i>-h_i^2||g_i||^2]
       =||x_0||^2-||x_4||^2.

Substitution in V_h then gives

    V_h=||x_0||^2-||x_4+s g_4||^2.                        (6)

When x_4=g_4, this is ||x_0||^2-C^2||g_4||^2.

## 3. Every needed cut inequality, including boundary cases

Fix j in {0,1,2,3}. Let v=h_j, let p=sum_{i<j} h_i and
r=sum_{i>j} h_i. If v>1, set alpha=(v-1)/(1+r)>0 and define

    f_alpha(x)=x-1/2                    for x>=1,
               x^2/2                   for -alpha<=x<=1,
               -alpha*x-alpha^2/2      for x<=-alpha.

Its derivative clamp(x,[-alpha,1]) is continuous, nondecreasing,
and 1-Lipschitz. This is one convex differentiable 1-smooth function,
with unique minimizer 0. Start at x_0=1+p. The gradients through
query j are all 1 and x_j=1. After its step,
x_{j+1}=-(1+r)alpha. Every remaining step has gradient -alpha,
and the terminal point is x_4=g_4=-alpha. Nonnegative step lengths
ensure all intermediate points stay on the stated pieces, including
zero-step repetitions. Every sampled value has the form used in (6).

Consequently

    V_h=(1+p)^2-C^2*(v-1)^2/(1+r)^2.

Any full certificate must therefore obey

    C*(h_j-1)_+ <= (1+sum_{i<j}h_i)(1+sum_{i>j}h_i).       (7)

For h_j<=1 the inequality holds automatically; no division by
h_j-1 was used in that case. Strict failure of (7) is an explicit
negative-energy function, with every original interpolation pair legal.

The actual quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, started at 1, has
x_i=g_i=product_{t<i}(1-h_t). Formula (6) gives

    V_h=1-C^2*product_{i=0}^3(1-h_i)^2.

Hence every full certificate also requires

    C*|product_{i=0}^3(1-h_i)| <= 1.                      (8)

Both (7) and (8) were proved for the original nonnegative-step domain.
Neither uses a second formal kernel or assumes equality in (8).

## 4. A coupled endpoint bound from the two middle cuts

Assume (1). Use a,b,c,d as in Section 1, so

    2/5<=a,d<=1/2,    C=5+a+b+c+d.

At this point b and c have not been assumed positive. Define

    A=2+a,   D_end=2+d,   t=a+d,   S=b+c=C-5-t.

The middle cuts (7) imply Cb<=A(3+c+d) and
Cc<=D_end(3+a+b), since replacing a positive part by the underlying
real number only weakens their left sides. As
3+c+d=C-A-b and 3+a+b=C-D_end-c, these are equivalent to

    b <= A(C-A)/(C+A),
    c <= D_end(C-D_end)/(C+D_end).                        (9)

All denominators are positive. For fixed C>=193/25, the function
z(C-z)/(C+z) has derivative

    (C^2-2Cz-z^2)/(C+z)^2.

On 12/5<=z<=5/2, we have z/C<1/3 because C>15/2; the derivative
is positive since 1-2(z/C)-(z/C)^2>2/9. Thus (9) yields

    b,c <= U(C),      U(C)=(5/2)*(C-5/2)/(C+5/2).          (10)

Put K(C)=C-5-U(C). Both U and K increase strictly on this capacity
range: U'(C)=(25/2)/(C+5/2)^2 is positive and less than 1/8,
so K'(C)>7/8. At C_0=193/25 their exact values are

    U(C_0)=1305/1022 > 51/40,
    K(C_0)=36871/25550 > 36/25.                           (11)

For the first strict comparison the cross-product difference is
1305*40-1022*51=78. For the second it is
36871-36*1022=79. Therefore, at every C>=C_0,

    U(C)>51/40,       K(C)>36/25.

Since 4/5<=t<=1, the sum constraint and (10) imply

    b=S-c>=S-U=K-t>11/25>0,
    c=S-b>=S-U=K-t>11/25>0.                              (12)

In particular the two middle steps are strictly greater than 1 as a
consequence, not a hypothesis. Every zero-step boundary has been handled.

Multiplying the nonnegative factors U-b and U-c gives

    0 <= (U-b)(U-c)=U^2-U*S+bc,
    bc >= U(S-U)=U(K-t).                                (13)

To keep the endpoint product coupled to their sum, use both elementary
inequalities

    (a-2/5)(d-2/5)>=0,      (1/2-a)(1/2-d)>=0.

They imply

    ad >= (2/5)t-4/25,
    ad >= t/2-1/4.                                       (14)

The first lower bound is larger for 4/5<=t<=9/10; the second is
larger for 9/10<=t<=1. Each is positive on its stated interval.
On the first interval the product

    ((2/5)t-4/25)*(36/25-t)

is a concave quadratic, so its minimum is attained at one of the two
ends. The two values are 64/625 and 27/250. On the second interval
the same argument for

    (t/2-1/4)*(36/25-t)

gives endpoint values 27/250 and 11/100. Both latter values exceed
64/625. Equations (11), (14), and positivity therefore give

    ad*(K-t) > 64/625.                                  (15)

Now use (12)--(15), keeping all multiplication factors positive:

    C*a*b*c*d >= C*U(C)*ad*(K(C)-t)
               > (193/25)*(51/40)*(64/625)
               = 78744/78125 > 1.                       (16)

All four shifts are positive, so (16) contradicts (8). If either
middle cut did not hold, Section 3 had already supplied a legal negative
energy witness. This proves the full statement, including (2)--(3).

The capacity was arbitrary throughout C>=193/25. Monotonicity in
(11) justifies comparison to its lower endpoint; no fixed-capacity
slice or attained endpoint of a feasibility interval was substituted.

## 5. Separation from the previous excluded region and remaining domain

For every word satisfying (1), even before testing any cut,

    b+c=C-5-a-d>=193/25-6=43/25.

One of b,c is at least 43/50. Both a,d are at most 1/2, so this
interior shift differs from either endpoint shift by at least
43/50-1/2=9/25. In each of the two possible pairings in the definition
of d_pair, that interior shift must be paired to an endpoint. This
proves (4). Thus the excluded box is disjoint from d_pair<=1/20.

The proof also implies that any actual threshold seed must satisfy

    h_0 outside [7/5,3/2] OR h_3 outside [7/5,3/2].         (17)

This restriction is compatible with retaining the shared candidate
focus bc<1, with the full lower-clipping and lifted-return conditions.
Those other conditions are not dropped: a positive construction outside
the box still has to satisfy every actual legal-function test and all
twenty signs. The present argument makes no claim about existence or
emptiness outside (17), or about the unrestricted asymptotic minimax
question. The excluded step box contains an interval of possible
endpoint data around h_0=h_3=sqrt(2), not merely an equality face.

## 6. An additional necessary inequality from the full PSD endpoint block

Here h is any nonnegative four-step word with
u=h_0>1, v=h_3>0, s>v, and a full certificate (5). Set

    delta_u=2C-(C+1)u,
    delta_v=2C-(C+1)v,
    B_end=s-v.

Then

    2u(u-1)v B_end
       <= u*delta_u*B_end^2+(u-1)^2*s^2*v*delta_v.         (18)

All signs and PSD directions are retained. In particular, simultaneous
saturation delta_u=delta_v=0 is impossible under the stated positive
denominators. No claim of independence from all earlier witness tests
is made for (18).

To prove it, first obtain the constant kernel without an assumption.
The identity sum h_i P_i=(s^2-sum h_i^2)/2 and Te=e+P give
e^T M e=0 whenever the flow holds. PSD then forces Me=0: inserting
e+tau z into the quadratic form for both signs of small tau forces
z^T Me=0 for every z. Its row equations are

    sum_j Lambda_ij(P_j-P_i)=2h_i(1+P_i), i<4,
    sum_{j<4}Lambda_4j(s-P_j)=2sC.                        (19)

Let z_j=Lambda_0j for 1<=j<=4, y_j=Lambda_4j for 0<=j<=3,
m_0=M_00, and m_4=M_44. Put Z=sum_{j=1}^3 z_j. The initial
moment and its diagonal yield exactly

    s*m_0=u*delta_u-(u-1)*sum_{j=1}^3(s-P_j)z_j.

Because s-P_j>=v and all z_j>=0,

    Z <= (u*delta_u-s*m_0)/((u-1)v),
    z_4=(2u-sum_{j=1}^3 P_j z_j)/s
       >=2u/s-B_end*(u*delta_u-s*m_0)/(s*(u-1)v).        (20)

The terminal diagonal is m_4=sum_{j<4}y_j-s(s+2).
Its moment in (19) gives

    v*m_4+sum_{j=0}^2(P_3-P_j)y_j=s*delta_v.

Since P_3=B_end and all y_j are nonnegative,

    y_0 <= (s*delta_v-v*m_4)/B_end.                      (21)

Directly from the full matrix definition,
2M_04=(u-1)y_0-z_4. Its principal 2-by-2 PSD condition therefore
implies z_4<=(u-1)y_0+2sqrt(m_0*m_4). Combine (20)--(21):

    L_0+A_end*m_0+m_4/A_end <=2sqrt(m_0*m_4),
    A_end=B_end/((u-1)v)>0,
    L_0=2u/s-B_end*u*delta_u/(s*(u-1)v)
                   -(u-1)*s*delta_v/B_end.

The difference A_end*m_0+m_4/A_end-2sqrt(m_0*m_4) is
(sqrt(A_end*m_0)-sqrt(m_4/A_end))^2>=0. Hence L_0<=0.
Multiplication by the positive s*(u-1)*v*B_end proves (18).
This proof includes m_0=0 or m_4=0 without dividing by either.

## 7. Audit of the full-support PSD/skew interface used for construction

The purpose of this section is to check the fragile identities in
443f4b4325a9901d, not to claim a second coordinate reformulation as
the outcome. The substantive regional exclusion is Sections 1--5.

Assume s>0. Choose mu strictly between the last distinct nonterminal
prefix P_k with h_k>0 and s. Put phi_i=1+P_i,

    w_i=2h_i/(mu-P_i) when h_i>0, w_i=0 when h_i=0 (i<4),
    w_4=2s/(s-mu), W=sum_i w_i,
    Lambda^c_ij=phi_i*w_i*w_j/W for i!=j.

All nonzero weights are positive. Summing w_i(P_i-mu) gives zero,
so sum w_i P_i=mu W and sum phi_i w_i=(1+mu)W. Therefore
out_i-in_i=w_i(P_i-mu)=omega_i, with this exact flow sign.
Also sum_j Lambda^c_ij(P_j-P_i)=phi_i w_i(mu-P_i), which is
the row moment in (19). Thus M_c e=0; no PSD conclusion follows.
When all h_i>0 the twenty coefficients are strictly positive. When
some h_i=0, their formal coordinates still remain in the matrices.

Let e_i be the standard columns of R^5. Let E have columns e_i-e_4,
i=0,...,3, and let F have columns

    e_j-(1-P_j/s)e_0-(P_j/s)e_4, j=1,2,3.

E is a basis of e-perp. F has three independent middle coordinate
columns and is a basis of span(e,P)-perp, including at repeated
prefixes. An arbitrary homogeneous flow/kernel perturbation Delta L
must satisfy Delta L e=0, Delta L^T e=0, Delta L P=0. Conversely
these equations preserve flow and the kernel. They are equivalent to

    Delta L=E X F^T, X an arbitrary real 4-by-3 matrix.

The signs are precisely

    (E X F^T)_ij <= Lambda^c_ij, every i!=j.               (22)

Let B be the 5-by-4 matrix with columns e_0,...,e_3. Put
R=F^T T B, K_c=B^T M_c B. Since B^T E=I,

    K=K_c+sym(XR).

The constant kernel determines the full matrix as

    M=[K,-K*1; -1^T*K,1^T*K*1].                          (23)

Its quadratic form is (g_0-g_4,...,g_3-g_4)^T K times that same
column. Hence full M>=0 is equivalent to K>=0. This is a full-space
identity, without imposing any equality between formal gradients.

Define p_0=1, p_{i+1}=(1-h_i)p_i and
q=(p_0-p_4,...,p_3-p_4)^T. Direct substitution gives Tp=e and
T^{-1}P=e-p. Since s>0, p and e are independent. Therefore
ker(F^T T)=span(e,p); intersecting with the subspace having last
coordinate zero shows ker R=span(q), q!=0, and rank R=3.
This proof remains valid at zero steps and at h_i=1.

The telescope h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_{i+1}^2 yields

    q^T K_c q=p^T M_c p=1-C^2 p_4^2=:c_quad.

For a proposed symmetric K with q^T Kq=c_quad, let H=K-K_c and

    S_0=[q(Hq)^T-(Hq)q^T]/(q^T q).

The sign check is S_0 q=-Hq, because q^T Hq=0. Every real completion
of the symmetric equation, with no signs imposed yet, is

    X=(H+S_0+Z)R^T(RR^T)^{-1},
    Z^T=-Z, Zq=0.                                       (24)

Indeed A=H+S_0+Z annihilates q, and R^T(RR^T)^{-1}R is the
orthogonal projection onto q-perp, so XR=A. Conversely XR-H is
skew and has value -Hq on q, leaving exactly such a Z. The skew
operators on the three-dimensional q-perp have three independent
coordinates. No rank assumption on K entered.

At c_quad>0 no second kernel is forced. At c_quad=0, and only with
K>=0, the identity q^T Kq=0 forces Kq=0 by the same quadratic-form
argument used for e. Choosing a calibrated PSD K does not establish
any of the twenty inequalities (22). The center, calibration, and
three skew coordinates remain an unsolved construction problem outside
the newly excluded endpoint box.

## 8. Scope checks, unsuccessful completion, and handoff

The direct construction attempt kept every entry of X free and did
not infer PSD from the positive center or signs from PSD calibration.
It produced no actual K,Z,Lambda satisfying the full threshold
requirements. The full-cone witness alternative in Section 4 was the
successful branch of this round. It rules out every K and every skew
completion for the stated step region, not just the center or a
rank-one choice.

The fragile points were checked textually against possible counterexamples:

* b,c were permitted to be nonpositive until (12) ruled them out.
  Thus the quadratic-product sign was not silently assumed.
* The endpoints a,d were coupled to their sum in (14)--(15). Using
  their separate worst bounds would lose the claimed strict gap.
* Both intervals in the concave-product argument were retained, with
  all four endpoints evaluated by the displayed exact expressions.
* C was free. U and K monotonicity, rather than a numerical capacity
  slice, justifies (11) over the entire unbounded requested range.
* Formula (18) uses only u>1, v>0, s>v. It does not divide by a PSD
  diagonal, assert tail heredity, or require either endpoint to saturate.
* The zero-step/rank/congruence audit in Section 7 retains all formal
  gradients. The new exclusion itself forces positive middle shifts.

No counterexample to the stated restricted claims was found by these
symbolic checks. This is not verifier acceptance. Broadening the box
or inferring full four-step infeasibility has no proof here.

Next construction region: C>=193/25, d_pair>1/20, with at least
one of h_0,h_3 outside [7/5,3/2], and every applicable clipping and
lifted test still retained. In the current shared positive-shift
coordinates this means a or d outside [2/5,1/2]. The exact full
coefficient problem is still (22)--(24) together with K>=0.

The round ends with a complete scoped obstruction, not a seed. The
verifier gate remains closed; no result in this document is a new fact.
There is no automatic renewal of the one-round allocation.

evidence:
# C89: a conditional three-sign law and an exact selected-history obstruction

Status: **one complete joint draft, UNVERIFIED**. This is the one newly
authorized round after the C88 recovery: completed baseline20, ceiling21;
the historical interrupted attempt remains separate. There was no numerical
evaluation, word search, solver, fixed replay, installation, or fact submission.
All new assertions below belong to this single candidate, not to the accepted
fact graph. The original unrestricted exact-profile target remains open.

Correctness predecessors are `1252b8823bb5a290` (the original finite
smooth-convex inequalities and the maximal queried-prefix interpolant),
`0e7e78056dc6258c` (the scalar sequence and normalization argument in the
orthogonal-moment theorem), and `b98bb807d514e80d` (the original benchmark).
The whole transcript below is NOT orthogonal, so the orthogonal-moment
theorem cannot simply be applied to it. Section3 supplies the missing
selected-sample argument, including all skipped-gradient contributions.
Earlier character drafts are scope information, not proof premises.

## 1. Original word and the claim

Fix an integer m>=4. Set

    N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2), delta=1-1/m,
    c_chr=sigma(1+1/m), a_chr=delta/c_chr.

Use the actual chronological words

    H_chr,0=(),
    H_chr,j+1=(H_chr,j,1+a_chr*c_chr^j,H_chr,j), 0<=j<m.

Thus h=H_chr,m has exactly n steps and

    h_i=1+a_chr*c_chr^(nu_2(i+1)), 0<=i<n,

where nu_2(v) is the exponent of2 dividing the positive integer v. Every
subword retains the displayed enclosing-m parameters. There is no reset,
padding, or permutation of physical steps. In particular its last physical
step is h_(n-1)=1+a_chr in(1,2).

Section2 specifies strictly positive probabilities w_s on s in{0,1}^m.
Write chi_s(i)=(-1)^(sum_l s_l i_l), using the ordinary binary digits i_l
of the original sample index. Prescribe ONLY the queried gradients by

    g_i=(Gamma_i*sqrt(w_s)*chi_s(i))_s, 0<=i<n,             (1)

where every Gamma_i is arbitrary and positive. All Euclidean realizations
of the same Gram matrix are included. The amplitudes may depend on the
whole word and the enclosing horizon. There is no adjacent saturation
assumption and no common amplitude profile in repeated subwords.

Suppose ONE finite-dimensional convex differentiable1-smooth function F
with a minimizer realizes these gradients along

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i*g_i, 0<=i<n.

The anchor, the values, the function, and the terminal gradient are otherwise
unrestricted. Let X_star be a closest minimizer, and define

    R=||X_0-X_star||, F_star=min F,
    V_C89=2(F(X_n)-F_star)/R^2.

The claim is

    R>0,
    V_C89 <= beta_(N/4-1) <= 128/N^2,                    (2)

where the accepted notation is

    c_0=0, c_(k+1)=c_k+2+2sqrt(c_k+1),
    beta_k=4/(1+sqrt(1+2c_k))^2.                         (3)

Consequently, for the ORIGINAL exact benchmark B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1,

    0 <= B_n V_C89
       <= 128(1+4n^p)/(n+1)^2 ->0,
    p=log_2(3)<2.                                      (4)

The bound B_n<=1+4n^p is from `b98bb807d514e80d`. This is an obstruction
to the specified finite probability law, uniformly over all its legal
positive amplitude histories. It is not an upper bound on unrestricted
W_n(H_chr,m). Section6 proves the class nonempty by giving all original
jets of one explicit function. Section7 gives the non-dyadic and arbitrary
schedule version of the obstruction, with its last-step factor explicit.

For L-smooth objectives, apply the proof to F=f/L and g_i=grad f(X_i)/L.
Then (2) has exactly the denominator L*dist(X_0,argmin f)^2.

## 2. Every probability atom, its correlations, and the removed hypotheses

Put p_bias=1-1/N. For s in{0,1}^m let

    B_sig=(-1)^s_0, C_sig=(-1)^s_1, D_sig=(-1)^s_2,
    mu_+=1/2, mu_-=1/4.

The exact joint law is as follows. B_sig has mean p_bias; conditional on
B_sig, C_sig is unbiased; conditional on B_sig=b and C_sig=c, the sign
D_sig has mean mu_b*c. All bits s_3,...,s_(m-1) are independent unbiased
bits, independent of the first three signs. Explicitly,

    w_s=2^(-(m-3)) * (1+p_bias*B_sig)/2
                         * (1/2) * (1+mu_(B_sig)*C_sig*D_sig)/2.       (5)

All factors are strictly positive. Summing in the order D_sig,C_sig,B_sig,
then in the higher bits, proves sum_s w_s=1. This is a real probability
law; no assertion of real positivity is inferred from finite-field algebra.

Its only nonzero nonconstant character moments are

    E B_sig=p_bias,
    E(C_sig D_sig)=q_mix=(3+p_bias)/8,
    E(B_sig C_sig D_sig)=r_mix=(1+3p_bias)/8.               (6)

Indeed conditional averaging first gives E(D_sig|B_sig,C_sig)=mu_(B_sig)
C_sig and E(C_sig|B_sig)=0. Also mu_b=(3+b)/8. These formulas give (6),
while E C_sig=E D_sig=E(B_sig C_sig)=E(B_sig D_sig)=0. A nonempty product
of higher signs has expectation0, independently of the first three signs.
Equivalently the density is exactly

    w_s=N^(-1)[1+p_bias B_sig+q_mix C_sig D_sig
                                      +r_mix B_sig C_sig D_sig].      (7)

Let XOR mean bitwise addition modulo2 of label vectors, and let

    H_corr={0,1,6,7}=span_(F_2){1,6}.                     (8)

Here 1 is binary001, 6 is binary110, and any higher bits are zero.
The real normalized correlation kernel is

    k(0)=1, k(1)=p_bias, k(6)=q_mix, k(7)=r_mix,
    k(d)=0 for d outside H_corr,
    <g_i,g_j>=Gamma_i Gamma_j k(i XOR j).                 (9)

This follows by multiplying the two real characters, and using (6).
In particular every queried Gram entry is nonnegative. The matrix is
positive semidefinite because (1) is an actual real vector realization.
It is positive definite at distinct labels: for any nonzero coefficients
a_i, the squared norm of sum_i a_i g_i equals
sum_s w_s(sum_i a_i Gamma_i chi_s(i))^2>0. For the strict inequality,
character orthogonality gives independence of the distinct character rows.
That orthogonality follows by pairing s with s+e_l at a bit where two
labels differ, so their signed sum is zero.

The law is nonproduct even after an invertible linear change of sign
coordinates. To see this, its nonzero Fourier support is the rank2 subgroup
H_corr. A product law in some linear sign coordinates with this support
would have exactly two nonzero coordinate means, and one of the three
nonconstant moments on H_corr would be the product of the other two.
None is:

    r_mix-p_bias*q_mix=(1-p_bias^2)/8>0,
    q_mix-p_bias*r_mix=3(1-p_bias^2)/8>0,
    p_bias-q_mix*r_mix>0.                               (10)

The last inequality uses p_bias>=15/16 and q_mix,r_mix<1/2. A product law
with more nonzero means would have larger Fourier support, and a product
law with fewer would have smaller support. Full support of the probability
also rules out a deterministic coordinate introduced by a change of basis.

The differences from the earlier laws are visible in the ORIGINAL pairs.
Every leaf has correlation p_bias approaching1, instead of the old fixed
root correlation -1/2. At the first level2 bridge, samples2,3,4 have

    corr(g_2,g_3)=p_bias,
    corr(g_2,g_4)=q_mix,
    corr(g_3,g_4)=r_mix != p_bias*q_mix.                  (11)

Thus the product triangle identity with the third correlation equal to
the product of the first two cannot be imported. At a level-k bridge
with k>=3, the three samples 2^k-2,2^k-1,2^k instead have correlations
p_bias,0,0: the two label differences crossing the bridge contain a
nonzero high bit. The old near-unit outer correlation is absent.

The common-prefix return mechanism is also absent. For m>=4,
corr(g_0,g_4)=k(4)=0, whereas the old common-prefix component repeats its
first coarse direction after four samples and its full-law correlation
there is close to1. In (5), higher prefix characters are not forced to
share a common sign. These are changes of actual queried Gram entries,
not scalar amplitude reweighting of the old fixed law.

Removing these hypotheses does not establish interpolation. The exact
obstruction below uses a different property: the many orthogonal selections
left by sparse, nonnegative correlations.

## 3. Original queried selections with nonnegative past correlations

Here is the general calculation used in this joint proof. Work on one
actual trajectory of a convex differentiable1-smooth F, translated so that
a true closest minimizer is0 and F_star=0. A closest minimizer exists:
argmin F is closed and nonempty, and a bounded sequence approaching its
distance from X_0 has a convergent subsequence in finite dimension.

Choose original queried indices

    j_0<...<j_(M-1),

whose gradients v_r=g_(j_r) are nonzero and pairwise orthogonal. Assume
that each selected gradient has nonnegative scalar product with every
earlier queried gradient:

    <v_r,g_t> >=0 whenever t<j_r.                       (12)

Let f_r=F(X_(j_r)), q_r=||v_r||^2>0, and D_0=X_0-X_star. These f_r and
q_r are local names for the selected values and energies in this section.
No physical query or step has been deleted or compressed.

Accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` gives, on every actual ordered pair,

    Q_ij=F(X_i)-F(X_j)+<g_i,X_j-X_i>
                                      +||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.          (13)

For successive selected indices, the inequality with the LATER gradient
and the earlier point gives

    f_r >= f_(r+1) + (q_r+q_(r+1))/2
                + sum_(t=j_r)^(j_(r+1)-1) h_t <v_(r+1),g_t>
        >= f_(r+1)+(q_r+q_(r+1))/2.                    (14)

All terms in the displayed original displacement are present. Their
nonnegativity, not a fictitious compressed GD identity, justifies the
second line. Orthogonality is used only for the squared gradient difference.

The original optimum comparison similarly gives

    <D_0,v_r> = <X_(j_r)-X_star,v_r>
                       +sum_(t<j_r)h_t <g_t,v_r>
              >= f_r+q_r/2.                            (15)

Also f_(M-1)>=q_(M-1)/2. Put b=f_(M-1)-q_(M-1)/2>=0 and

    T_r=b+sum_(s=r)^(M-1)q_s.

Summing (14) and using (15) gives <D_0,v_r> >= T_r>0 for every r.
Expansion of the nonnegative squared norm
||D_0-sum_r(<D_0,v_r>/q_r)v_r||^2 now gives

    R^2=||D_0||^2 >= sum_(r=0)^(M-1) T_r^2/q_r.         (16)

This is the TRUE initial-distance norm of the given legal function.
No inverse Gram anchor or distance to an arbitrary minimizer replaces it.

For completeness the exact scalar elimination from the accepted
orthogonal-moment proof is reproduced. Inductively,

    sum_(r=0)^(k-1) T_r^2/q_r >= c_k T_k,
    0<=k<=M-1.                                        (17)

The initial case is0>=0. Since T_k=q_k+T_(k+1), adding the next term to
the inductive bound gives

    c_k T_k+T_k^2/q_k
       =(c_k+1)q_k+(c_k+2)T_(k+1)+T_(k+1)^2/q_k
       >=[c_k+2+2sqrt(c_k+1)]T_(k+1).

The last inequality is the nonnegativity of
(sqrt(c_k+1)*sqrt(q_k)-T_(k+1)/sqrt(q_k))^2. This proves (17).
Let c=c_(M-1), z=T_(M-1)/q_(M-1)>=1, and
r_cap=(1+sqrt(1+2c))/2. Equations (16)-(17) imply

    R^2 >= q_(M-1) z(z+c),
    2f_(M-1)=q_(M-1)(2z-1).

Because c=2r_cap(r_cap-1),

    z(z+c)-r_cap^2(2z-1)=(z-r_cap)^2>=0.

Therefore

    2F(X_(j_(M-1)))/R^2 <= beta_(M-1).                 (18)

The formula includes M=1, where beta_0=1. If a selected gradient were
zero, its point would be a minimizer, every subsequent iterate would
remain there, and the terminal objective would be0 instead.

For k>=1, induction in (3) gives c_k>=k^2. Since
c_k=2r_cap(r_cap-1)<=2r_cap^2, this also proves

    beta_k <= 2/k^2.                                   (19)

The new content relative to the accepted all-gradients-orthogonal fact is
precisely (14)-(15): nonorthogonal gradients at the skipped original samples
are allowed, with their full chronological contributions retained.

## 4. Apply the calculation to the law and the actual free terminal

There are N/4 cosets of H_corr among all N binary labels, each of size4.
Deleting the one terminal label N-1 leaves every coset represented by
queried labels. Choose the largest queried index in each coset, and sort
these choices in increasing chronological order. Thus M=N/4 and the last
selected index is n-1=N-2. More explicitly, in each complete group of eight
labels the representatives are8r+5 and8r+7; in the last group use N-3 and
N-2, because N-1 is unqueried.

Different selected labels lie in different cosets, so their differences
are outside H_corr and their gradients are orthogonal by (9). Every
scalar product with an earlier gradient is nonnegative by that same
formula. Hence (18) gives

    2(F(X_(n-1))-F_star)/R^2 <= beta_(N/4-1).             (20)

For a1-smooth function, integration along a segment gives

    F(X-h grad F(X)) <= F(X)-h(1-h/2)||grad F(X)||^2.

The last ORIGINAL step is1+a_chr<2, so F(X_n)<=F(X_(n-1)). This statement
uses the actual function; it makes no restriction on grad F(X_n).
Combining it with (20) proves the first inequality in (2). For N>=16,
N/4-1>=N/8, and (19) gives beta_(N/4-1)<=128/N^2. This proves (2)-(4).
Since ||g_0||=Gamma_0>0, X_0 is not a minimizer and R>0.

The same estimate controls maximal queried-prefix interpolation, without
adding an incoming terminal constraint. For any legal complete queried
prefix and an optimum jet, `1252b8823bb5a290` constructs one maximal
1-smooth interpolant and bounds every reduced-feasible terminal value by
its actual value at the fixed X_n. The preceding argument applies to that
function and its own closest-minimizer distance. If the original supplied
anchor has norm at most1 relative to its optimum jet, that true distance
is at most1, so twice the reduced-feasible terminal value is also at most
beta_(N/4-1). Free terminal selection cannot repair this law.

## 5. The smallest cross-cycle and why PSD alone is not being used

For three consecutive original samples, temporarily call them0,1,2,
with steps1+t,1+u and normalized correlations P,Z,W in the order01,02,12.
Let A=||g_0||, x=||g_1||/A, y=||g_2||/A. Expansion of the actual directed
cycle in (13), with values and the anchor cancelling, gives

    (Q_02+Q_10+Q_21)/A^2
       =-t+x^2+y^2+(t-u-1)P*x+u*W*x*y-Z*y.             (21)

Indeed before division the diagonal terms are -t K_00+K_11+K_22,
and the cross terms are (t-u-1)K_01+u K_12-K_02.

At samples0,1,2 of the actual word, P=p_bias and Z=W=0. At the first
level2 cross-cycle, samples2,3,4, formula (11) gives

    t=a_chr, u=delta*c_chr,
    P=p_bias, Z=q_mix, W=r_mix.                         (22)

Thus the mixed term in this actual cycle includes r_mix, not the product
p_bias*q_mix. The two moments E B_sig and E(C_sig D_sig) alone do not
determine this third-order term in a necessary original cycle. We do not
claim that any local root rule is sufficient.

Section6 now gives explicit amplitudes and values for which EVERY ordered
pair in both these triples is strictly negative, as are all other distinct
finite queried pairs. In particular (21) and its reverse are strictly
negative on that one specified complete construction. This resolves actual
cross-cycles and full interpolation together; it does not infer either
from the real PSD property alone.

## 6. Nonvacuity: an explicit common anchor and one global function

This part only establishes nonemptiness; it is not a competitive payoff
claim. In fact it works for every finite schedule with h_i>1 and the same
kind of nonnegative kernel. For the dyadic word above retain its exact
weights and additionally prescribe a character gradient at the terminal.
Write

    H_max=max_(i<n) h_i,
    kappa=min(1,(min_(i<n)h_i-1)/4)>0,
    eta=kappa/[8(H_max+kappa+1)],
    Gamma_i=eta^i, f_i=(kappa+1/2)Gamma_i^2, 0<=i<=n,
    K_ij=<g_i,g_j>.

Here eta<1/8 and h_i>=1+4kappa. Define

    b_i=(kappa+1)Gamma_i^2+sum_(t<i)h_t K_ti,
    (X_0)_s=[1/(N sqrt(w_s))]
                              sum_(i=0)^n (b_i/Gamma_i)chi_s(i),
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t.                           (23)

Character orthogonality proves <X_0,g_i>=b_i, hence

    <X_i,g_i>=(kappa+1)Gamma_i^2.                       (24)

For i<j, direct expansion of the ORIGINAL residuals gives

    Q_ij=(kappa+1-h_i)Gamma_i^2-kappa Gamma_j^2
                          -sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_it-K_ij,

    Q_ji=(kappa+1)Gamma_j^2-kappa Gamma_i^2
                          +(h_i-1)K_ij+sum_(i<t<j)h_t K_jt.          (25)

By (9), 0<=K_it<=Gamma_i Gamma_t. The first line of (25) is at most
-3kappa Gamma_i^2. The second, divided by Gamma_i^2, is at most

    -kappa+(kappa+1)eta^2+H_max*eta/(1-eta)
       <=-kappa+(2H_max+kappa+1)eta
       <-3kappa/4.                                    (26)

The second line uses eta<1/2; the final inequality follows on inserting
the exact eta and using2H_max+kappa+1<2(H_max+kappa+1).
These inequalities include the first actual cross-cycle and both
orientations of every remote queried or terminal pair. With the optimum
jet (0,0,0), (24) gives exactly

    Q_(i,star)=0, Q_(star,i)=-kappa Gamma_i^2<0.          (27)

For a concrete ONE static function, fixed before the run, let

    C_grad=conv(0,g_0,...,g_n),
    F_C89(X)=max_(v in C_grad)(<X,v>-||v||^2/2).          (28)

Completing the square identifies its unique maximizing vector with the
Euclidean projection P_C_grad(X). Projection onto this compact convex set
is characterized by <X-P_C_grad(X),v-P_C_grad(X)><=0 for every v in C_grad.
Adding those normal inequalities at two points proves
||P_C_grad(X)-P_C_grad(Y)||^2<=<X-Y,P_C_grad(X)-P_C_grad(Y)>;
hence projection is1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizing expressions

For strictly positive steps define an array supported only on adjacent
pairs by

and calibrated-K/skew numerical implementations. It is far below the
target threshold and is not proposed as an improving seed.

    1<=h_i<=17/16, i=0,1,2,3.                           (17)

    mu=(P3+s)/2,
    v_i=2h_i/(mu-P_i), i<4; v4=2s/(s-mu); W=sum_i v_i,

These are rational functions of the four steps. All twenty entries of
Lambda are strictly positive, with the explicit uniform bound

    Lambda_ij>1/688128, i!=j.                            (19)

PSD. In the gradient-difference coordinates (g0-g4,...,g3-g4), its

    K >= (941/16384) I4.                                (20)

The following proves all of these assertions inside this one document.

last is2s. Hence sum_i v_i P_i=mu W and sum_i p_i v_i=(1+mu)W.

## 1. Result and the full model in which the construction sits

For clarity, the FULL released affine parent model has arbitrary

## 2. Exact atom and its original rows

## 9. One global function and the TRUE radius

Let yhat_i=Z_i-J_i and Deltahat_i=fhat_i-||J_i||^2/2. On the same R^5
define

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max(0,max_(0<=i<=15)(<yhat_i,v>-Deltahat_i)),
    F_parent(Z)=sup_v(<Z,v>-H(v)).                  (22)

All rows just proved, together with accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`,
show that this is one finite, everywhere differentiable, convex,
1-smooth function satisfying F_parent(Z_i)=fhat_i, grad F_parent(Z_i)=J_i,
and F_parent(0)=0=min F_parent. Its trajectory from Z_0 is exactly (2).

Only samples 3,7,11,15 have Deltahat_i=0; their residuals are
0,E_top t,0,B_top t. All other Deltahat_i are strictly positive.
It follows directly that

    argmin F_parent=conv{0,E_top t,B_top t}.         (23)

For completeness, at sufficiently small epsilon>0 in any fixed
direction v,

    H(epsilon v)=epsilon^2||v||^2/2
       +epsilon max(0,<E_top t,v>,<B_top t,v>).

Every point of the displayed convex hull has conjugate value zero.
If Z is outside it, let z be its closest point and v=Z-z. The elementary
projection inequality gives <Z,v> greater than the maximum of the
three support values. The displayed local expression then gives

The exact nearest-minimizer distance is R. Indeed

    <E_top P,B_top t>=<P,d><P,t>/R^2<=0.

Hence <Z_0,z><=0 for every minimizer z in (23), and
||Z_0-z||^2=R^2+||z||^2-2<Z_0,z>>=R^2.
Zero attains equality. At sigma<1 the internal residuals are nonzero;
they have not been identified with zero or hidden in a surrogate radius.

The endpoint value is fhat_15=nscale k N/2. Thus (3)'s exact payoff is

evidence:
# A quantitative first-row gap for the full primitive certificate

Status: complete joint proof DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max4 round28,
the final round allocated by TASK.md and guidance8211d6128deabdf3,
with the corrected accounting instructions c9ebc26382c63e1d.
No fact_submit is authorized. The accepted mathematical input is
04219554e41d9750, namely its original full five-gradient primitive
certificate identity. All other assertions used here are proved below.

The new obstruction couples a lifted middle-cut energy to the actual
first row of the full PSD matrix and its unit-quadratic energy. It keeps
all twenty nonnegative multipliers, all five formal gradients, and every
flow equation. No rank, support, order, symmetry, or quadratic equality
is assumed. It does not construct a threshold seed or prove that every
threshold seed is impossible.

## 1. Statement and notation

Write a positive-excess four-step word as

    h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,1+d),    a,b,c,d>0,
    C=1+sum h=5+a+b+c+d.

Suppose it admits the full primitive certificate of accepted fact
04219554e41d9750. Suppose additionally that a>sqrt(2)-1. Define

    u=1+a,             delta=u^2-2,
    H=3+c+d,           eta=b/H,
    R=a+3+1/a,         k=u*delta/a,
    nu=(1+eta)*(1-a*eta)/a,
    Erow=R-k*eta-C^2*eta^2,
    Qenergy=1-C^2*a^2*b^2*c^2*d^2,
    Wrow=max(1+b,1+b*c*d),
    Krow=max(u,a*Wrow).

Full feasibility forces a<1, a*eta<1, nu>0, and
0<=Qenergy<1. The following quantitative necessary condition holds:

    u*delta <= Krow*Erow/nu + 2*sqrt(Qenergy*Erow/nu).          (A)

In particular,

    Erow >= nu * [u*delta /
          (sqrt(Qenergy+Krow*u*delta)+sqrt(Qenergy))]^2 > 0.  (B)

Thus equality in the previously used lifted middle-cut condition Erow>=0
is impossible throughout this initial-step regime. A version avoiding
square roots is

    Erow>=0,
    [max(u*delta*nu-Krow*Erow,0)]^2 <= 4*Qenergy*Erow*nu.     (C)

If a*b<=1 and c*d<=1, the simpler strict necessary inequality is

    Erow > nu*delta^2/u^2,                                 (D)

equivalently

    b < (a+3)*(C-a-2) / ((a+1)*(C+a+2)).                (E)

The last two product assumptions are explicit hypotheses of this
simplification. They are not silently declared lossless for the
original problem. Conditions(A)--(C) do not require them. The separate
assumption a,b,c,d>0 is also retained explicitly; no assertion about a
zero step or a step at most one is being imported from an unverified
compactness draft.

## 2. Original formal certificate and its constant kernel

Put P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, s=P_4=C-1, and let e be the five-entry all-ones
column. Write e_i for the i-th original standard coordinate of R^5,
with indices0 through4. Let T have diagonal1, entry h_t at(i,t) for t<i, and zero
entries above the diagonal. The original twenty multipliers satisfy

    Lambda_ij>=0 for i!=j, Lambda_ii=0,
    L=diag(Lambda*e)-Lambda,
    omega=(-2h0,-2h1,-2h2,-2h3,2s)^T,
    D=diag(h0(2-h0),h1(2-h1),h2(2-h2),h3(2-h3),-s(s+2)),
    L^T e=omega,
    M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 >=0 on ALL of R^5.               (1)

The identity in accepted04219554e41d9750 is

    V_h+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij
                      =sum_(i,j) M_ij <g_i,g_j>,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f4)
          +sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-s(s+1)||g4||^2,
    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i.                                (2)

Since Te=e+P and sum_(i<4)h_i P_i=(s^2-sum h_i^2)/2,

    e^TDe=-s^2-sum h_i^2,
    omega^TTe=s^2+sum h_i^2,
    e^TMe=0.

For every real v, the nonnegative quadratic(e+t*v)^T M(e+t*v)
has zero constant coefficient. Considering both signs of t forces
v^TMe=0, hence Me=0. The initial row of this identity is

    sum_(j>0)Lambda_0j P_j=2h0.                        (3)

To check(3) without any suppressed flow condition, direct expansion
gives(Me)_i=h_i(1+P_i)+(LP)_i/2 for i<4. At i=0,
P0=0 and(LP)_0=-sum_(j>0)Lambda_0j P_j.

Let Aout=sum_(j>0)Lambda_0j and m=M00. Its original diagonal is

    m=1-a^2-a*Aout.                                    (4)

Indeed the first column of T is(1,u,u,u,u)^T, so(LT)_00
=(1-u)Aout=-a*Aout. Since m,Aout>=0 and a>0, (4) gives
a<=1. Equality would give m=Aout=0, contradicting(3). Thus a<1.

For any positive semidefinite real matrix, the two-vector inequality

    |v^T M w|^2 <= (v^T M v)*(w^T M w)                 (5)

follows by applying nonnegativity to(v+t*w)^T M(v+t*w).
If w^T M w=0, the linear coefficient must vanish; otherwise minimizing
in t proves(5). This argument does not assume positive definiteness.

## 3. Two exact scalar energies

Here clamp(x,[-eta,1]) means min(1,max(-eta,x)).
The scalar function with this derivative and minimum0
has the actual trajectory

    x=(2+a,1,-b,-(2+d)*eta,-eta),
    g=(1,1,-eta,-eta,-eta).

Here b=(3+c+d)*eta. Its derivative is continuous, nondecreasing, and
1-Lipschitz. At every displayed sample its value is
f_i=x_i*g_i-g_i^2/2. The first step gives x1=1; the other three GD
updates follow directly from the displayed relation for b.

For any GD data with saturated values
f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2, telescoping the squared distances gives

    V_h=||x0||^2-||x4+s*g4||^2.                        (6)

In detail, the first two sums in(2) reduce to
2sum h_i<x_i,g_i>-sum h_i^2||g_i||^2-2s*f4;
the first two terms telescope to||x0||^2-||x4||^2.
Substitution of f4 then gives(6). The scalar trajectory has x4=g4,
so its energy is(2+a)^2-C^2*eta^2. By(1)--(2) it is nonnegative.
Consequently

    C*eta<=2+a,
    a*eta<=a*(2+a)/C<3/5<1,                           (7)

because 0<a<1 and C>5. This proves nu>0.

Next define the actual unit-quadratic gradient column

    p=(1,-a,a*b,-a*b*c,a*b*c*d)^T.

It satisfies Tp=e. Since Le=0,

    p^T M p=p^T D p=1-C^2*p4^2=Qenergy.               (8)

For the telescoping equality, p_(i+1)=(1-h_i)p_i gives
h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2; the terminal diagonal
then supplies-s(s+2)p4^2. Full PSD gives Qenergy>=0.
All a,b,c,d are positive, so Qenergy<1.

## 4. Complete lifted-cut data and its exact multiplier cost

Let U=(1,0), V=(0,1) be orthonormal physical vectors. Set

    z=-eta*U+sqrt(nu)*V.

Then

    ||z||^2=[1+(1-a)*eta]/a,
    <U,z>+a||z||^2=1-a*eta.

Use the five two-dimensional data

    X=(U+u*z, U, -b*U, -(2+d)*eta*U, -eta*U),
    G=(z, U, -eta*U, -eta*U, -eta*U),
    F_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2.                         (9)

Every GD update has the original step length. For these saturated
values the original ordered interpolation residual is exactly

    Q_ij=<G_i-G_j,X_j-G_j>.

Here is a check of all twenty ordered finite pairs, grouped by their
target j. Targets1 and4 have zero normal. At target0 the normal is
U+a*z. The incoming pair(1,0) has residual0, whereas each incoming
pair(i,0), i=2,3,4, has residual-a*nu. At target2 the normal is
-(b-eta)U. The only nonzero finite residual there is
Q_12=-(1+eta)(b-eta). At target3 the normal is
-(1+d)*eta*U. The only nonzero finite residual there is
Q_13=-(1+eta)(1+d)*eta. Thus all twenty residuals are nonpositive.
The zero optimum jet can also be added: Q_(i,star)=0 by the chosen
values; the opposite inequalities follow from the same normals and
a*eta<1. These optimum pairs are not additional multipliers in(1).

For completeness these are actual jets of one global smooth convex
function. Let Kphys=conv{0,z,U,-eta*U} and define

    F(X)=max_(G in Kphys)(<X,G>-||G||^2/2).

The comparisons just made say that X_i-G_i is an outward normal
to Kphys at G_i. Completing the square identifies the unique maximizer
as the Euclidean projection of X onto Kphys. If projections at X,Y
are G,H, adding their normal inequalities gives
||G-H||^2<=<G-H,X-Y>, and hence ||G-H||<=||X-Y||.
To see differentiability directly, optimality at X and X+v bounds
F(X+v)-F(X)-<G,v> between0 and<G(X+v)-G,v>, which is at most||v||^2.
Thus the gradient is the projection and is1-Lipschitz. The function
is convex as a maximum of affine functions of X; it has minimum0 at0
because0 belongs to Kphys. It realizes all of(9).

By(6), its primitive energy is

    ||U+u*z||^2-C^2*eta^2
      =a+3+1/a-(u*delta/a)*eta-C^2*eta^2=Erow.            (10)

Let

    Bin=Lambda20+Lambda30+Lambda40.

In the U coordinate the gradient column is-eta*e+(1+eta)*e1;
in the V coordinate it is sqrt(nu)*e0. The constant kernel proved
in Section2 therefore gives the full matrix remainder
(1+eta)^2*M11+nu*m. Substituting every nonzero residual above into
the original identity(2) yields the exact accounting identity

    Erow=nu*(m+a*Bin)+(1+eta)^2*M11
       +(1+eta)*eta*((2+c+d)*Lambda12+(1+d)*Lambda13). (11)

Every term on the right is nonnegative. In particular

    0<=m<=m+a*Bin<=Erow/nu.                              (12)

No incoming coefficient has been set to zero. Identity(11) prices the
original incoming coefficients explicitly.

## 5. The original first row couples the two energies

Define the weighted incoming combination

    Bweight=(1+b)*Lambda20+(1-b*c)*Lambda30
                                    +(1+b*c*d)*Lambda40.

The exact first-row identity is

    2*e0^T M p = u*(m-delta)+a^2*Bweight.             (13)

Here e0 denotes the original first coordinate column of R5. A direct
derivation avoids any coordinate reduction. Since Tp=e and Le=0,
Mp=Dp+T^T L^T p/2. Also Te0=u*e-a*e0, giving

    2*e0^T M p=2(1-a^2)-a*p^T L e0.

The flow at node0 gives Lambda10=Aout+2u-Bin. Hence

    p^T L e0
      =Aout+a*Lambda10-a*b*Lambda20
                        +a*b*c*Lambda30-a*b*c*d*Lambda40
      =u*Aout+2a*u-a*Bweight.

Finally substitute a*Aout=1-a^2-m from(4). The constant term becomes

    (2-u)(1-a^2)-2a^2*u
      =u*((1-a)^2-2a^2)=-u*delta,

which proves(13), with all row and flow contributions retained.

All three incoming multipliers are nonnegative. Since b,c,d>0,
each coefficient in Bweight is at most Wrow. This remains true even
if 1-b*c is negative. Thus Bweight<=Wrow*Bin. Applying(5) with e0,p,
and using(8), gives from(13)

    u*delta <= u*m+a^2*Wrow*Bin+2*sqrt(m*Qenergy)
             <= Krow*(m+a*Bin)+2*sqrt(m*Qenergy)
             <= Krow*Erow/nu+2*sqrt(Qenergy*Erow/nu).        (14)

This is(A). Put t=sqrt(Erow/nu). Because Krow,u,delta are positive,
(14) says

    Krow*t^2+2*sqrt(Qenergy)*t-u*delta>=0.

Solving this increasing quadratic for t>=0 and rationalizing its
positive root gives(B). Its numerator is strictly positive, so Erow>0.
Multiplying(A) by nu and squaring only when its left side after
subtraction is positive gives exactly(C). There is no sign-losing
squaring in this formulation.

## 6. A rational strengthened middle-cut boundary

If c*d<=1, then Wrow=1+b. If also a*b<=1, then
a*Wrow=a+a*b<=1+a=u, so Krow=u. Since Qenergy<1 and Erow>0,
(14) implies the strict inequality

    u*delta < u*t^2+2t,       t=sqrt(Erow/nu)>0.

The right side is strictly increasing for t>=0. Its value at
t=delta/u is

    delta^2/u+2delta/u=delta*(delta+2)/u=u*delta,

because delta+2=u^2. It follows that t>delta/u, which is(D).
The exact algebraic identity

    Erow-nu*delta^2/u^2
      =[(a+3-delta*eta)^2-u^2*C^2*eta^2]/u^2          (15)

can be checked by expanding the constant, linear, and quadratic
coefficients in eta. Those coefficients in the numerator are
(a+3)^2, -2(a+3)*delta, and delta^2-u^2*C^2.

The first factor a+3-delta*eta is positive: by a*eta<1,

    a+3-delta*eta > a+3-delta/a = 1+1/a >0.

Thus(D) and(15) give

    a+3 > (u*C+delta)*eta.

Substitute eta=b/(C-2-a-b), whose denominator is H>0. Since
delta+a+3=(a+1)(a+2), the result is exactly(E). Every denominator
in(E) is positive.

In particular this is a necessary bound on an entire step region,
not a condition on a sparse coefficient family. The exact stronger
condition(A) still retains the actual Qenergy rather than discarding
it in favor of the upper bound1.

## 7. Adversarial scope checks

The initial-step hypothesis is substantive. At a=sqrt(2)-1 the
quantity delta is zero, and(A) supplies no positive gap. This agrees
with the possibility of saturated basic certificates at that endpoint.
We do not extend the strict conclusion by continuity across delta=0.

If b*c>1, the coefficient of Lambda30 in(13) is negative. The proof
does not replace this coefficient by its absolute value or infer a
false lower bound. It uses only the valid upper bound Bweight<=Wrow*Bin.
Thus(A)--(C) still apply in that regime. The simplified statement(E)
requires only its explicitly stated a*b and c*d hypotheses.

If Qenergy=0, formula(B) reduces to Erow>=nu*u*delta/Krow;
no division by Qenergy occurs. If a multiplier vanishes or M has
additional kernels, the semidefinite form of(5) still applies. No
strict complementarity, full rank, or strictly positive support was used.

Here is a purely symbolic test family showing why the separate tests
Erow>=0 and Qenergy>=0 cannot justify the omitted coupling. It is an
analytical counterexample to that shortcut, not a numerical seed proposal
or a claim to survive the other existing necessary inequalities. Take

    a=1/2, eta=7/24, C=39*sqrt(2)/7,
    H=24*(C-5/2)/31, b=7*(C-5/2)/31, Ktail=H-3,
    0<d<min(Ktail/2,1/Ktail,1/(C*a*b*Ktail)), c=Ktail-d.

Here sym(A)=(A+A^T)/2. No formal gradient is identified with another,
even if a physical step is zero.

 x02 t1<=x01 t2.                                     (8)

These are products of actual directed coefficients and the actual
row surpluses. Full PSD has not been substituted for any of (8).

Let hcol=(h0,h1,h2)^T and e0small=(1,0,0)^T, and define

                  z=A^(-1)(e0small-hcol/C).           (9)

 F03=-z2, F13=z2-z1, F23=z1-z0.                       (10)

## 5. A scalar capacity bound when both orientations pass the core-ended tests

This section requires only nonnegative intrinsic energy on specific
legal trajectories whose incoming-terminal residuals Q_(i,3) are all0.
It therefore applies to a signed certificate satisfying (1): every
negative coefficient multiplies0, while all other Q have nonnegative
multipliers in the certificate. It applies in particular to an ordinary
certificate. No general signed-terminal repair is assumed.

Write the three physical steps as (u,v,w), total capacity T=1+u+v+w,
t=sqrt(2), ell=1+t, and T0=ell^2=3+2t. Suppose both (u,v,w) and
(w,v,u) are nonnegative on the core-ended trajectories below.
Then

                         T<=T0.                      (12)

Here is a complete proof. At a chosen step b>1 with sums P before
and R after it, use the scalar function with derivative
clip(x,[-(b-1)/(R+1),1]), starting at P+1. It has constant gradient1
before the chosen step and constant gradient-(b-1)/(R+1) after it,

 r(w-1)<=A0(w^2-1)/T<363/(64T0)<1.

 T0(T0-t-w-2)(w-1)-(t+1)=T0(w-t)(2-w)>=0.

          q_T(u,w):=T(u-1)(w-1)(T-u-w-2)<=1.          (16)

On [t,m(T)]^2 this function is strictly concave in either endpoint

 q_T0(m(T0),m(T0))=ell/2>1.

For T>=T0 every corner value strictly increases: each positive factor

## 6. Extraction from a saturated FIRST cut of a full four-step array

Let b=(b0,b1,b2)>0, D=1+b0+b1+b2, and let r>0 satisfy

 r(1+D+r)=D. Put Cpar=1+D+r, kappa=(Cpar/D)^2=1/r^2.

The four-step word is hpar=(1+r,b0,b1,b2). Suppose it has a full
ordinary twenty-multiplier certificate Lambda. Define theta=1-r^2;
since r<1, this lies in(0,1).

The scalar function with derivative clip(x,[-1/Cpar,1]), started at1,
has gradient1 at the first query and-1/Cpar at all four tail queries,
ending at its lower quadratic endpoint. Its primitive energy is0.
Together with the constant-gradient equality data, PSD places the

For tail j=1,2,3, let R_j be its remaining tail-step sum. Direct
substitution gives Q_(0,j)=-(1+1/Cpar)R_j/Cpar<0. Complementarity
with Lambda>=0 and the zero energy therefore forces
Lambda_(0,j)=0 for j=1,2,3. Let nu=Lambda_(0,4).
Expanding the rows of the full matrix against the first-query indicator
gives

 0=(r Lambda_(j,0)-nu b_(j-1))/2 for j=1,2,3,

The node0 flow is nu-(nu/r)D=-2(1+r). Using rCpar=D gives

 Lambda_(0,4)=r(kappa-1),
 Lambda_(j,0)=(kappa-1)b_(j-1), j=1,2,3,

in accepted fact04219554e41d9750, applied as an algebraic identity,

 lambda_ij=Lambda_(i+1,j+1)/kappa
                 -theta b_i 1_(i<3,j=3), i!=j,       (18)

and the parent remainder equals kappa times its full four-gradient
remainder, with a zero first row and column. Therefore (18) cancels

No claim that every entry of (18) is nonnegative is made.

If (18) passes tests (8),(11), Sections2--4 produce an ordinary full
certificate for rev(b). Join rev(b) to the empty right child with the

As Cpar=Omega(1,D), this bounds the parent strictly below193/25.
For a direct rational check of the threshold separation, if instead

 D=Cpar(Cpar-1)/(Cpar+1)>=16212/2725>41/7>3+2sqrt(2).

The first function is strictly increasing for Cpar>=1; the middle

Thus at a saturated first cut, EVERY threshold full parent array must

array exists.

## 7. Saturated LAST cuts and exact limitations

For hpar=(b0,b1,b2,1+r) with the same positive b and rCpar=D,
the saturated clipped trajectory and its constant-gradient counterpart
likewise put the two block indicators in the full kernel. Complementarity
forces tail-to-prefix edges only into the bridge query and prefix-to-tail
edges only from it. The same row calculation as in Section6, with the
empty right child of capacity1, gives the cross coefficients of the
accepted primitive join. Subtracting them leaves the ordinary full
certificate of b on its original four gradients; there is no terminal
credit because b is the left child.

For explicit cross entries, put kappa_last=Cpar^2, let index3 be the
bridge query and index4 the empty tail query. The only cross terms are

 Lambda_(3,4)=r(kappa_last-1),
 Lambda_(4,3)=kappa_last-1;

all Lambda_(i,4),Lambda_(4,i) with i<3 vanish. Indeed complementarity
first gives Lambda_(4,i)=0 for i<3; the row i<3 against the final-block
indicator is-Lambda_(i,4)/2, forcing the other direction to vanish.
Node4 flow gives Lambda_(4,3)-Lambda_(3,4)=2(Cpar-1), and the
kernel equation gives Lambda_(3,4)=r Lambda_(4,3). The displayed
solution follows from (1-r)(Cpar+1)=2, which is equivalent to
rCpar=D and Cpar=1+D+r. The retained prefix array is ordinary by
nonnegativity, and its full matrix is the corresponding PSD block.

If that child passes (8),(11) with theta=0, its reverse is ordinary,
and the accepted join with the empty left child reverses the parent.
Section5 again gives D<=3+2sqrt(2), so this class also has capacity
below193/25. Therefore every threshold full parent on this face must
fail a test in EVERY supplied extracted array.

The six tests do not have a proved universal selection theorem. In
particular, (8) asks for genuine comparisons of directed coefficient
products; they do not follow merely from nonnegative entries, value
flow, or the displayed congruence. The terminal conditions (11) remain
separate. Sections6--7 state positive-child hypotheses; the following
section handles all zero-step threshold parents by actual functions.

The independent joint draft full_primitive_reversal_boundary_blocks.md
excludes actual threshold words in both orientations of a different
boundary block, with no saturation or sign-test restriction. Those
exclusions were proved from legal functions and do not use the map here.
Neither result decides general four-step reversal, constructs a feasible
threshold seed, excludes the whole seed domain, or solves the original
asymptotic exact-profile problem. No new fact is asserted.

## 8. No zero-step threshold parent is omitted

Every nonnegative three-step word with capacity T>=7 fails at least
one of its three scalar cut tests from Section5. Here is a proof that
does not assume either orientation is primitive. If all tests held,
the endpoint bounds would give u,w<=m(T)=2T/(T+1)<2. If v<=1,
then T=1+u+v+w<6, a contradiction. Thus v>1; the middle cut and
the capacity identity give, just as above,

 T<=ell(m(T)+1), hence T^2+(1-3ell)T-ell<=0.

At T=7 this polynomial equals56-22ell>0, since ell=1+sqrt(2)<5/2.
Its derivative2T+1-3ell is positive for T>=7. This contradiction
proves that some cut fails. The corresponding explicitly given clipped
scalar function has strictly negative intrinsic energy.

Now take any nonnegative four-step word containing a zero step and
with capacity Cpar>=193/25>7. Delete all zero updates and, if needed,
pad the resulting word with zero updates to length3. The capacity is
unchanged, so the preceding argument supplies an actual scalar
negative-energy trajectory for the compressed word. Removing padding
and reinserting the original zero steps repeats the same query point,
gradient and value at each zero update. It preserves the entire GD run
and the primitive energy, since zero steps contribute nothing and the
terminal point is unchanged. This lifts the negative-energy function
to the original four-step word.

By the full identity in fact04219554e41d9750, such a word cannot have
twenty nonnegative multipliers, exact flow, and full ambient R^5 PSD.
This is an actual-function exclusion, not an identification of formal
gradients inside a proposed full certificate. Consequently every
threshold parent considered at a saturated endpoint necessarily has
all steps strictly positive. Sections6--7 cover its positive child
without a zero-step gap, while their six-test selection problem remains.

evidence:
# Exact value-flow prices and two complete redundancy results

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof draft. This is max2's first analytical round
after completed baseline22, under TASK.md and guidance f7608aa358751108.
No numerical evaluation, solver, parameter scan, replay, machine algebra,
formal verification, installation, or subordinate agent was used.

Accepted inputs: 04219554e41d9750, Section10 (the ORIGINAL primitive
certificate), and 1252b8823bb5a290, proof paragraphs1--2 (all-pair smooth
convex interpolation and its actual conjugate construction). Everything
else needed below is proved in this document. Earlier C82/C83 and coupling
drafts are comparison targets, never accepted premises.

The required concrete outcome is exact redundancy of value pricing on
the ENTIRE unit-curvature repaired-cut family, including all its legal
repair amplitudes, arbitrary nonnegative words, zero steps, and all
original coordinates. The lifted-cut geometry in2948d4cd3660413f also has
identically zero price. A separate C82 calculation gives an exact price
and a fully minimized formula in a specified parameter domain. It proves
redundancy there when a^2+a<=1; its complementary regime is not asserted
to resolve a surviving full-cone region.

The original asymptotic target, existence/nonexistence of a threshold
seed, and general four-step cone reversal remain OPEN. No new fact is
asserted and no theorem below is promoted past the verifier gate.

## 1. Original orientation, objective, and formal coordinates

Let n>=0, h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be a finite nonnegative word, s=sum h_i,
C=1+s, and I={0,...,n}. Keep every original gradient coordinate, including
the terminal coordinate and every coordinate at a zero step. Fixed
physical vectors x_i,g_i in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space obey

    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i.

For sampled values f_i put

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V(f)=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sC||g_n||^2.       (1)

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 proves Q_ij<=0 for every ordered pair of actual
smooth convex samples, and constructs a single interpolant from these
inequalities. Assume initially that all these finite inequalities hold.
An optimum sample will be retained explicitly when it is part of the
fixed geometry; Section3 also handles the case where its location is free.

For the original nonnegative multipliers Lambda_ij, put Lambda_ii=0 and

    L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T,
    L^T e=omega.                                         (2)

Here e is the (n+1)-entry all-ones column. Thus omega_i is outgoing minus
incoming flow. The TERMINAL is the source, of mass2s, and index i<n is
a sink of mass2h_i. Reversing these arrows gives the wrong value problem.

With T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, and T_it=0 for t>i, let

    D=diag(h_i(2-h_i) for i<n, -s(s+2)),
    M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2.

Accepted04219554e41d9750 gives, on every physical realization,

    V(f)+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>.   (3)

The full certificate requires M PSD on ALL of R^(n+1). Nothing below
deletes a coordinate, restricts Lambda support in that feasibility
question, or identifies formal gradients at zero steps. Sparse flows
constructed below solve an auxiliary transport minimum; they are NOT
claimed to have PSD matrices.

## 2. An exact finite price, with elementary proof and attained flow

Fix legal base values f_i and put w_ij=-Q_ij>=0 for distinct i,j. Regard
w_ij as the cost of the directed arc i->j. Let d_i be the least cost of
a path from n to i, with d_n=0. The complete finite graph makes every
distance finite. A minimizing path exists: a repeated-vertex segment
has nonnegative cost and can be deleted, so it is enough to consider
finitely many simple paths.

For replacement values f_i+z_i, the complete constraints are exactly

    z_i-z_j<=w_ij.                                      (4)

Summing along an n->i path gives z_n-z_i<=its cost. Therefore

    z_i-z_n>=-d_i,
    V(f+z)>=V(f)-Pflow,
    Pflow=2sum_(i<n)h_i d_i.                             (5)

All h_i are nonnegative, including possibly zero. The simultaneous
choice z_i=-d_i attains every lower bound in(5): the distance inequality
d_j<=d_i+w_ij is precisely its feasibility in(4). Thus this is an
attained minimum of the value problem, not only a lower bound from a
dual program.

The same number is the exact minimum slack cost of the ORIGINAL flow:

    min_{Lambda>=0, L^T e=omega} sum Lambda_ij w_ij
       =Pflow.                                         (6)

To prove the lower bound, multiply w_ij>=d_j-d_i by Lambda_ij and sum.
The result is

    sum Lambda_ij w_ij >= -sum_i omega_i d_i
                         =2sum_(i<n)h_i d_i.

For attainment, choose a shortest n->i path for every i<n with h_i>0
and send mass2h_i along that path. Sum these path flows. Intermediate
vertices have equal incoming and outgoing mass; the endpoints give
exactly(2). Each path contributes2h_i d_i. Zero-weight sinks need no
path, but their vertices and all their available arcs remain present.

Combining(3) with(6) gives a necessary condition for any full certificate:

    V(f)>=Pflow.                                        (7)

The selected optimal values give the same condition as V(f-d)>=0. Indeed
their new slacks are w'_ij=w_ij+d_i-d_j, and every prescribed-flow array
satisfies

    sum Lambda_ij w'_ij=sum Lambda_ij w_ij-Pflow.

The Gram matrix and the formal certificate matrix do not change with
the values. The full PSD restriction can impose more than the minimum
over flows in(6); it has not been dropped from the original problem.

### Zero costs, coincident gradients, and fixed optimum constraints

No strict positivity of costs is needed. A zero-cost directed cycle
has every arc of cost zero, and(4) then forces equal shifts around that
cycle. Distances and the path-flow construction remain valid without
choosing a unique shortest path.

If two base gradients coincide, Q_ij+Q_ji=0, so legality forces BOTH
residuals to vanish. Hence replacement shifts at these two samples are
equal, even when their positions differ. If two base positions coincide,
the sum of the two residuals is ||g_i-g_j||^2; legality first forces
coincident gradients and then coincident values. These are properties of
actual jets, not extra formal equations in the PSD certificate.

One may also include a fixed optimum jet x_star=g_star=f_star=0 as an
extra graph vertex. Let d_i^* be distances in this larger graph. Then
z_i=d_star^*-d_i^* is feasible, has z_star=0, and minimizes the same
value objective subject to ALL finite and optimum pairs. Its improvement
is2sum h_i d_i^*. In general d_i^*<=d_i, so this price need not equal
the original finite-flow price. They WILL agree in every concrete family
below. The distinction is important: optimum edges are not original
primitive multipliers and cannot silently be used as such.

## 3. The optimized finite values give one static function and real minima

This section also explains why(5), without a fixed optimum vertex, is
not merely a formal jet result. For any legal replacement values f'_i
on the finite samples, set

    y_i=x_i-g_i, beta_i=||g_i||^2/2-f'_i,
    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max_(i in I){<y_i,v>+beta_i},
    F(x)=sup_v{<x,v>-H(v)}.                              (8)

This is the construction in accepted1252b8823bb5a290, written out here
to identify its minimizers. H is finite, continuous, 1-strongly convex,
and has quadratic growth. The supremum has one maximizer v(x). Strong
subgradient inequalities give

    <x-x',v(x)-v(x')>>=||v(x)-v(x')||^2,

and the maximizing inequalities give

    0<=F(x')-F(x)-<v(x),x'-x>
      <=<v(x')-v(x),x'-x><=||x'-x||^2.

Thus F is everywhere finite, convex, differentiable and1-smooth, with
gradient v(x). The all-pair inequalities say that at v=g_i the i-th
quadratic in H is active and has gradient x_i. Consequently v(x_i)=g_i
and F(x_i)=f'_i. This is ONE fixed F used for all steps.

Let beta_max=max_i beta_i, and A={i:beta_i=beta_max}. The exact minimizer
set of F is

    argmin F=conv{y_i:i in A},   min F=-beta_max.          (9)

Indeed gradient F(x)=0 is equivalent to x being a subgradient of H at0.
The subgradients there are exactly the convex hull of the active affine
slopes y_i. To check the reverse inclusion without an unproved formula,
if x is outside that convex hull, a separating vector u has
<x,u> greater than every <y_i,u> for i in A. For sufficiently small
positive t, inactive affine pieces remain inactive at tu, and
H(tu)-H(0)=t max_(i in A)<y_i,u>+t^2||u||^2/2,
contradicting the subgradient inequality for x. The forward inclusion
follows by convexly combining the active supporting inequalities.

In particular a real minimizer always exists, even if none was fixed in
the graph. The true initial distance is exactly

    dist(x_0,conv{y_i:i in A}).                           (10)

No arbitrary radius or changed function is inserted into the GD run.
The specific families below either preserve the optimum0 or identify
the closest minimizer explicitly.

## 4. Entire unit-curvature repaired-cut family: price exactly zero

This is the main complete redundancy result. It works for any n>=1,
any nonnegative word, and any cut j with0<=j<n and h_j>1. Put

    P_j=sum_(t<j)h_t, T_j=sum_(t>j)h_t,
    eta=(h_j-1)/(1+T_j)>0,
    p_0=1, p_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t) for0<=i<=j.

Choose an amplitude epsilon>=0. Define two scalar coordinate arrays:

    xB_i=1+sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t, gB_i=1        (i<=j),
    xA_i=gA_i=p_i                            (i<=j),

    R_k=sum_(t=k)^(n-1)h_t                    (k>j),
    xB_k=-eta*(1+R_k), gB_k=-eta              (k>j),
    xA_k=p_j*xB_k, gA_k=-eta*p_j              (k>j).

Empty sums have value zero. At the cut,
xB_(j+1)=1-h_j=-eta*(1+T_j), and the same equality multiplied by p_j
holds for coordinate A. Before the cut the A coordinate follows unit
quadratic GD. After it both coordinates have constant gradients. Hence
the vectors

    X_i=(xB_i,sqrt(epsilon)*xA_i),
    G_i=(gB_i,sqrt(epsilon)*gA_i),
    F_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2                            (11)

obey every original GD equation. Include X_star=G_star=F_star=0.

Here are ALL interpolation pairs. For saturated values(11),

    Q_ik=<G_i-G_k,X_k-G_k>.

For a prefix target k<=j, its normal is

    X_k-G_k=(sum_(t=k)^(j-1)h_t,0).

Every prefix source has residual zero. Every tail source has residual
-(1+eta)sum_(t=k)^(j-1)h_t<=0. The optimum source has residual
-sum_(t=k)^(j-1)h_t<=0.

For a tail target k>j, its normal is

    X_k-G_k=-eta R_k*(1,sqrt(epsilon)*p_j).

Every tail source has residual zero. A prefix source i<=j has residual

    -eta R_k*[1+eta+epsilon*p_j*(p_i+eta*p_j)].           (12)

The optimum source has residual
-eta^2 R_k*(1+epsilon*p_j^2)<=0. Every pair into the optimum is zero.
These cases exhaust all directed finite and optimum pairs.

If T_j>0, legality is EXACTLY the finite set of inequalities

    1+eta+epsilon*p_j*(p_i+eta*p_j)>=0   for i<=j.        (13)

The necessity follows by using target j+1, where R_(j+1)=T_j>0.
If T_j=0, every tail normal vanishes and no condition(13) is necessary.
Zero p_j, zero epsilon, zero intermediate steps and repeated gradients
cause no exception in these formulas. This specifies the full legal
repair-amplitude family, rather than only its most-used endpoint.

For EVERY legal epsilon, the finite zero-cost arcs include

    n->j,
    j->i for every i<j,
    n->k for every j<k<n,
    i->n for every i<n.                                 (14)
