evidence:
# Exact value-flow prices and two complete redundancy results

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof draft. This is max2's first analytical round
after completed baseline22, under TASK.md and guidance f7608aa358751108.
No numerical evaluation, solver, parameter scan, replay, machine algebra,
formal verification, installation, or subordinate agent was used.

Accepted inputs: 04219554e41d9750, Section10 (the ORIGINAL primitive
certificate), and 1252b8823bb5a290, proof paragraphs1--2 (all-pair smooth
convex interpolation and its actual conjugate construction). Everything
else needed below is proved in this document. Earlier C82/C83 and coupling
drafts are comparison targets, never accepted premises.

The required concrete outcome is exact redundancy of value pricing on
the ENTIRE unit-curvature repaired-cut family, including all its legal
repair amplitudes, arbitrary nonnegative words, zero steps, and all
original coordinates. The lifted-cut geometry in2948d4cd3660413f also has
identically zero price. A separate C82 calculation gives an exact price
and a fully minimized formula in a specified parameter domain. It proves
redundancy there when a^2+a<=1; its complementary regime is not asserted
to resolve a surviving full-cone region.

The original asymptotic target, existence/nonexistence of a threshold
seed, and general four-step cone reversal remain OPEN. No new fact is
asserted and no theorem below is promoted past the verifier gate.

## 1. Original orientation, objective, and formal coordinates

Let n>=0, h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be a finite nonnegative word, s=sum h_i,
C=1+s, and I={0,...,n}. Keep every original gradient coordinate, including
the terminal coordinate and every coordinate at a zero step. Fixed
physical vectors x_i,g_i in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space obey

    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i.

For sampled values f_i put

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V(f)=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sC||g_n||^2.       (1)

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 proves Q_ij<=0 for every ordered pair of actual
smooth convex samples, and constructs a single interpolant from these
inequalities. Assume initially that all these finite inequalities hold.
An optimum sample will be retained explicitly when it is part of the
fixed geometry; Section3 also handles the case where its location is free.

For the original nonnegative multipliers Lambda_ij, put Lambda_ii=0 and

    L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T,
    L^T e=omega.                                         (2)

Here e is the (n+1)-entry all-ones column. Thus omega_i is outgoing minus
incoming flow. The TERMINAL is the source, of mass2s, and index i<n is
a sink of mass2h_i. Reversing these arrows gives the wrong value problem.

With T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, and T_it=0 for t>i, let

    D=diag(h_i(2-h_i) for i<n, -s(s+2)),
    M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2.

Accepted04219554e41d9750 gives, on every physical realization,

    V(f)+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>.   (3)

The full certificate requires M PSD on ALL of R^(n+1). Nothing below
deletes a coordinate, restricts Lambda support in that feasibility
question, or identifies formal gradients at zero steps. Sparse flows
constructed below solve an auxiliary transport minimum; they are NOT
claimed to have PSD matrices.

## 2. An exact finite price, with elementary proof and attained flow

Fix legal base values f_i and put w_ij=-Q_ij>=0 for distinct i,j. Regard
w_ij as the cost of the directed arc i->j. Let d_i be the least cost of
a path from n to i, with d_n=0. The complete finite graph makes every
distance finite. A minimizing path exists: a repeated-vertex segment
has nonnegative cost and can be deleted, so it is enough to consider
finitely many simple paths.

For replacement values f_i+z_i, the complete constraints are exactly

    z_i-z_j<=w_ij.                                      (4)

Summing along an n->i path gives z_n-z_i<=its cost. Therefore

    z_i-z_n>=-d_i,
    V(f+z)>=V(f)-Pflow,
    Pflow=2sum_(i<n)h_i d_i.                             (5)

All h_i are nonnegative, including possibly zero. The simultaneous
choice z_i=-d_i attains every lower bound in(5): the distance inequality
d_j<=d_i+w_ij is precisely its feasibility in(4). Thus this is an
attained minimum of the value problem, not only a lower bound from a
dual program.

The same number is the exact minimum slack cost of the ORIGINAL flow:

    min_{Lambda>=0, L^T e=omega} sum Lambda_ij w_ij
       =Pflow.                                         (6)

To prove the lower bound, multiply w_ij>=d_j-d_i by Lambda_ij and sum.
The result is

    sum Lambda_ij w_ij >= -sum_i omega_i d_i
                         =2sum_(i<n)h_i d_i.

For attainment, choose a shortest n->i path for every i<n with h_i>0
and send mass2h_i along that path. Sum these path flows. Intermediate
vertices have equal incoming and outgoing mass; the endpoints give
exactly(2). Each path contributes2h_i d_i. Zero-weight sinks need no
path, but their vertices and all their available arcs remain present.

Combining(3) with(6) gives a necessary condition for any full certificate:

    V(f)>=Pflow.                                        (7)

The selected optimal values give the same condition as V(f-d)>=0. Indeed
their new slacks are w'_ij=w_ij+d_i-d_j, and every prescribed-flow array
satisfies

    sum Lambda_ij w'_ij=sum Lambda_ij w_ij-Pflow.

The Gram matrix and the formal certificate matrix do not change with
the values. The full PSD restriction can impose more than the minimum
over flows in(6); it has not been dropped from the original problem.

### Zero costs, coincident gradients, and fixed optimum constraints

No strict positivity of costs is needed. A zero-cost directed cycle
has every arc of cost zero, and(4) then forces equal shifts around that
cycle. Distances and the path-flow construction remain valid without
choosing a unique shortest path.

If two base gradients coincide, Q_ij+Q_ji=0, so legality forces BOTH
residuals to vanish. Hence replacement shifts at these two samples are
equal, even when their positions differ. If two base positions coincide,
the sum of the two residuals is ||g_i-g_j||^2; legality first forces
coincident gradients and then coincident values. These are properties of
actual jets, not extra formal equations in the PSD certificate.

One may also include a fixed optimum jet x_star=g_star=f_star=0 as an
extra graph vertex. Let d_i^* be distances in this larger graph. Then
z_i=d_star^*-d_i^* is feasible, has z_star=0, and minimizes the same
value objective subject to ALL finite and optimum pairs. Its improvement
is2sum h_i d_i^*. In general d_i^*<=d_i, so this price need not equal
the original finite-flow price. They WILL agree in every concrete family
below. The distinction is important: optimum edges are not original
primitive multipliers and cannot silently be used as such.

## 3. The optimized finite values give one static function and real minima

This section also explains why(5), without a fixed optimum vertex, is
not merely a formal jet result. For any legal replacement values f'_i
on the finite samples, set

    y_i=x_i-g_i, beta_i=||g_i||^2/2-f'_i,
    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max_(i in I){<y_i,v>+beta_i},
    F(x)=sup_v{<x,v>-H(v)}.                              (8)

This is the construction in accepted1252b8823bb5a290, written out here
to identify its minimizers. H is finite, continuous, 1-strongly convex,
and has quadratic growth. The supremum has one maximizer v(x). Strong
subgradient inequalities give

    <x-x',v(x)-v(x')>>=||v(x)-v(x')||^2,

and the maximizing inequalities give

    0<=F(x')-F(x)-<v(x),x'-x>
      <=<v(x')-v(x),x'-x><=||x'-x||^2.

Thus F is everywhere finite, convex, differentiable and1-smooth, with
gradient v(x). The all-pair inequalities say that at v=g_i the i-th
quadratic in H is active and has gradient x_i. Consequently v(x_i)=g_i
and F(x_i)=f'_i. This is ONE fixed F used for all steps.

Let beta_max=max_i beta_i, and A={i:beta_i=beta_max}. The exact minimizer
set of F is

    argmin F=conv{y_i:i in A},   min F=-beta_max.          (9)

Indeed gradient F(x)=0 is equivalent to x being a subgradient of H at0.
The subgradients there are exactly the convex hull of the active affine
slopes y_i. To check the reverse inclusion without an unproved formula,
if x is outside that convex hull, a separating vector u has
<x,u> greater than every <y_i,u> for i in A. For sufficiently small
positive t, inactive affine pieces remain inactive at tu, and
H(tu)-H(0)=t max_(i in A)<y_i,u>+t^2||u||^2/2,
contradicting the subgradient inequality for x. The forward inclusion
follows by convexly combining the active supporting inequalities.

In particular a real minimizer always exists, even if none was fixed in
the graph. The true initial distance is exactly

    dist(x_0,conv{y_i:i in A}).                           (10)

No arbitrary radius or changed function is inserted into the GD run.
The specific families below either preserve the optimum0 or identify
the closest minimizer explicitly.

## 4. Entire unit-curvature repaired-cut family: price exactly zero

This is the main complete redundancy result. It works for any n>=1,
any nonnegative word, and any cut j with0<=j<n and h_j>1. Put

    P_j=sum_(t<j)h_t, T_j=sum_(t>j)h_t,
    eta=(h_j-1)/(1+T_j)>0,
    p_0=1, p_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t) for0<=i<=j.

Choose an amplitude epsilon>=0. Define two scalar coordinate arrays:

    xB_i=1+sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t, gB_i=1        (i<=j),
    xA_i=gA_i=p_i                            (i<=j),

    R_k=sum_(t=k)^(n-1)h_t                    (k>j),
    xB_k=-eta*(1+R_k), gB_k=-eta              (k>j),
    xA_k=p_j*xB_k, gA_k=-eta*p_j              (k>j).

Empty sums have value zero. At the cut,
xB_(j+1)=1-h_j=-eta*(1+T_j), and the same equality multiplied by p_j
holds for coordinate A. Before the cut the A coordinate follows unit
quadratic GD. After it both coordinates have constant gradients. Hence
the vectors

    X_i=(xB_i,sqrt(epsilon)*xA_i),
    G_i=(gB_i,sqrt(epsilon)*gA_i),
    F_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2                            (11)

obey every original GD equation. Include X_star=G_star=F_star=0.

Here are ALL interpolation pairs. For saturated values(11),

    Q_ik=<G_i-G_k,X_k-G_k>.

For a prefix target k<=j, its normal is

    X_k-G_k=(sum_(t=k)^(j-1)h_t,0).

Every prefix source has residual zero. Every tail source has residual
-(1+eta)sum_(t=k)^(j-1)h_t<=0. The optimum source has residual
-sum_(t=k)^(j-1)h_t<=0.

For a tail target k>j, its normal is

    X_k-G_k=-eta R_k*(1,sqrt(epsilon)*p_j).

Every tail source has residual zero. A prefix source i<=j has residual

    -eta R_k*[1+eta+epsilon*p_j*(p_i+eta*p_j)].           (12)

The optimum source has residual
-eta^2 R_k*(1+epsilon*p_j^2)<=0. Every pair into the optimum is zero.
These cases exhaust all directed finite and optimum pairs.

If T_j>0, legality is EXACTLY the finite set of inequalities

    1+eta+epsilon*p_j*(p_i+eta*p_j)>=0   for i<=j.        (13)

The necessity follows by using target j+1, where R_(j+1)=T_j>0.
If T_j=0, every tail normal vanishes and no condition(13) is necessary.
Zero p_j, zero epsilon, zero intermediate steps and repeated gradients
cause no exception in these formulas. This specifies the full legal
repair-amplitude family, rather than only its most-used endpoint.

For EVERY legal epsilon, the finite zero-cost arcs include

    n->j,
    j->i for every i<j,
    n->k for every j<k<n,
    i->n for every i<n.                                 (14)

The first and last groups hold because X_j=G_j and X_n=G_n. The second
group holds because both sources and targets are prefix samples. The
third holds because all tail gradients coincide. Thus every original
sample is in the zero-cost component of n, so

    d_i=d_i^*=0 for EVERY i,
    Pflow=0.                                           (15)

Equivalently, all feasible value replacements have z_i=z_n. With the
fixed zero optimum, Q_(n,star)=Q_(star,n)=0 also forces z_n=0. Thus ALL
sampled values in(11) are forced, not merely optimal for this objective.

An explicit attaining ORIGINAL flow sends2sum_(i<=j)h_i from n to j,
sends2h_i from j to i for i<j, and sends2h_k directly from n to k for
j<k<n. Its other entries vanish. The balance is(2), and every used arc
is in(14). It has zero cost. This does not assert its matrix is PSD.

There is one actual static smooth convex witness for every legal
amplitude: use(8) with the zero optimum included. For its prefix samples,
beta_i=-sum_(t=i)^(j-1)h_t; for its tail samples,
beta_k=-eta^2 R_k*(1+epsilon*p_j^2). These constants are nonpositive,
and equality in either formula implies that the corresponding normal
is zero. The optimum sample also has constant and normal zero. Thus(9)
gives the UNIQUE minimizer0 for this single conjugate interpolant. Its
TRUE squared initial distance is(1+P_j)^2+epsilon, in every case above.

The projection construction used in the earlier drafts is also valid:
let K=conv({0} union {G_i}) and define

    F(X)=max_(G in K){<X,G>-||G||^2/2}.                  (16)

The complete normal list proves that the optimizer at X_i is G_i.
Projection onto K is1-Lipschitz: add the two projection normal
inequalities to obtain ||G-H||^2<=<G-H,X-Y>. The same maximizing
inequalities used in Section3 prove differentiability. Since0 is in K,
F>=0=F(0). This is a real minimizer, and(11) are its actual values.

The saturated-value telescoping identity is

    V=||X_0||^2-||X_n+sG_n||^2.

To check it, use2h_i F_i+h_i(1-h_i)||G_i||^2
=||X_i||^2-||X_(i+1)||^2, sum, and substitute F_n.
Here X_n=G_n, so the family gives exactly

    V=(1+P_j)^2+epsilon
         -C^2 eta^2*(1+epsilon*p_j^2).                  (17)

Reoptimizing values adds NO inequality to nonnegativity of(17), for
any legal epsilon, word, cut or zero-step pattern. Consequently it adds
none to an existing collection of necessary conditions that already
includes this ENTIRE family. This is a family-level exact redundancy
claim, not global redundancy for arbitrary queried geometries.

### The actual four-step C83 member and true radius

Take h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,1+d), a,b,c,d>0, j=2, and

    C=5+a+b+c+d, Q=3+a+b, eta=c/(2+d), p_2=ab.

The only possibly negative coefficient in(13) is i=1, where p_1=-a.
If b eta<1, the full amplitude interval is

    0<=epsilon<=(1+eta)/(a^2 b(1-b eta)).                (18)

The other two coefficients have positive p_i. The endpoint in(18)
is exactly the repaired-cut value used in d3abee1b17da52da; there is
no new function-value freedom at ANY amplitude in this interval.

For0<ab<1 and epsilon>0, the two prefix gradients
(1,sqrt(epsilon)) and(1,-a sqrt(epsilon)) have G_2 in the relative
interior of their segment. Since G_3=-eta G_2, zero is in the interior
of their nondegenerate triangle with G_3. Thus the minimizer of(16) is
uniquely0: a nonzero normal at0 would have positive pairing with a
point of an open ball in K. The TRUE squared distance is Q^2+epsilon.
At epsilon=0 the instance is scalar and0 is again the closest minimizer
to the displayed initial point. No benchmark ratio is inferred from V.

## 5. The lifted-cut coupling geometry also has zero value price

This section reconstructs the actual geometry used in draft
2948d4cd3660413f, independently of that draft's quantitative matrix gap.
Let a,b,c,d>0, put u=1+a, C=5+a+b+c+d, H=3+c+d, eta=b/H,
and assume a eta<1. Define

    nu=(1+eta)(1-a eta)/a>0,
    U=(1,0), Z=-eta U+sqrt(nu)*(0,1),
    X=(U+uZ, U, -bU, -(2+d)eta U, -eta U),
    G=(Z, U, -eta U, -eta U, -eta U),
    F_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2.                         (19)

The original four updates follow from b=H eta. Include the zero optimum.
The normals at targets1 and4 vanish. At target0 the normal is U+aZ;
the source1 residual is zero, and each source2,3,4 residual is -a nu.
The optimum-source residual there is -(1-a eta)<0. At target2 the
normal is -(b-eta)U: source0 has residual zero, source1 has residual
-(1+eta)(b-eta), and tail sources have residual zero. At target3 the
normal is -(1+d)eta U: source0 has residual zero, source1 has residual
-(1+eta)(1+d)eta, and tail sources have residual zero. Optimum-source
residuals at2,3 are respectively -eta(b-eta) and-(1+d)eta^2.
Every residual into the optimum is zero. This checks every pair.

In particular the zero-cost finite paths are

    4->1->0, 4->2, 4->3, and i->4 for every i<4.        (20)

All value differences are therefore forced, and the optimum pairs fix
their common shift. Both finite-flow and fixed-optimum prices vanish.
The function(16) with K=conv{0,Z,U,-eta U} realizes these samples.
Its minimizer set is{(0,t):t<=0}; the initial second coordinate is
u sqrt(nu)>0, so0 is the closest minimizer. Its true squared initial
distance is ||U+uZ||^2, not an independent calibration variable.

The energy is exactly

    Erow=||U+uZ||^2-C^2 eta^2
        =a+3+1/a-[(1+a)(a^2+2a-1)/a]eta-C^2 eta^2.     (21)

Value-flow pricing returns only Erow>=0. It cannot recover a strictly
positive lower bound on Erow on this SAME geometry: the auxiliary flow
minimum is attained at zero and the values have no remaining freedom.
The further full-matrix restrictions in2948d4cd3660413f use PSD coupling
with a different quadratic direction and the first row. This result
neither assumes that unverified coupling theorem nor refutes it; it
identifies exactly what the present price can and cannot add to it.

## 6. C82 triangle: exact nonzero price and a real interpolant

Here keep canonical h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,1+d) with a,b,c,d>0, and let

    C=5+a+b+c+d, D=2+d, eta=bc/D,
    ell=max{0,c(1+d)(D-bc)/D^2},
    t=a v-1, Htri(v)=(v+1)(a v-1).

Use parameters v>=b and z>=0 with ell<=z^2<=Htri(v). For nondegenerate
triangles take z>0; the boundary z=0 is legal by the same normal checks.
These inequalities imply t>=0. Define

    X_0=((1+a)v-1,z), G_0=(v,0),
    X_1=G_1=(-1,z),
    X_2=(b,-bz),     G_2=(b,0),
    X_3=(-bc,-bz),   G_3=(-eta,0),
    X_4=(-eta,-bz),  G_4=(-eta,0),
    F_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2.                         (22)

Every GD equation has the original four step lengths. For completeness,
K=conv{G_0,G_1,G_3} contains0. At target0 the residual normal is(t,z).
Its comparisons with G_1,G_2,G_3 and0 are, respectively,

    z^2-(v+1)t, (b-v)t, -(eta+v)t, -v t,

all nonpositive. At target1 the normal vanishes. At target2 the normal
is(0,-bz), so all horizontal-gradient sources give zero and source1
gives -bz^2. At target3 the normal is(-(1+d)eta,-bz). Its source1
residual is b*[c(1+d)(D-bc)/D^2-z^2]<=0; its horizontal-gradient
sources and optimum source are nonpositive. At target4 the normal is
(0,-bz), again giving zero for horizontal-gradient sources and -bz^2
for source1. Every residual into the optimum is zero. Thus all finite
and optimum pairs hold, and(16) gives one actual base function.

The finite zero-cost arcs4->1,4->2,4->3 show d_1=d_2=d_3=d_4=0.
The least cost into0 is

    Dprice=min{(v-b)t, (v+1)t-z^2}.                      (23)

The other incoming costs, (v+eta)t and v t from the optimum, are no
smaller than(v-b)t. Every path into0 has a final incoming arc, while
each minimizing source1 or2 is reached at cost zero. Therefore

    d_0=d_0^*=Dprice, all other d_i=d_i^*=0,
    Pflow=2(1+a)Dprice.                                 (24)

The complete fixed-geometry value optimum is attained by

    F'_0=F_0-Dprice, F'_i=F_i for1<=i<=4, F'_star=0.      (25)

All incoming residuals at0 increase by Dprice and stay nonpositive
by(23); all outgoing residuals from0 decrease. All other pairs are
unchanged. This is a direct check of all thirty ordered pairs including
the optimum, independently confirming the path calculation.

For the actual function use(8) with these values and the optimum.
Its affine constants beta_i are

    beta_0=-v t+Dprice<=-b t,
    beta_1=beta_2=beta_4=beta_star=0,
    beta_3=-(1+d)eta^2<0.

When t>0, the active normals in(9) are0 and(0,-bz). Therefore its
minimizer set is the segment joining these two points, and0 is the
closest minimizer to X_0, whose second coordinate z is nonnegative.
If t=0, z=0 and the initial normal also vanishes, with the same
closest minimizer0. Thus the true squared initial distance is

    ((1+a)v-1)^2+z^2.

The base telescoping energy and the exact optimized energy are

    Ebase(v,z)=((1+a)v-1)^2+(1-b^2)z^2-C^2 eta^2,
    Eprice(v,z)=Ebase(v,z)-2(1+a)Dprice.                 (26)

In particular a generic claim that saturated projection values are
always rigid is FALSE. Formula(23) gives a strictly positive price
whenever v>b, t>0, and z^2<(v+1)t. This is a statement about a fixed
actual geometry, not yet about improvement over an optimized family.

## 7. Full C82 minimum for0<a<1,0<b<=sqrt(3),ab<=1

Assume0<a<1,0<b<=sqrt(3),ab<=1, and keep c,d>0 arbitrary and ell as
above. This domain includes the compact-domain inequalities used in the
earlier threshold drafts, when those inequalities are taken as explicit
hypotheses; no unverified global reduction is being assumed here. Put

    R=[1-a+sqrt((1+a)^2+4a ell)]/(2a),
    v_cross=[1+ell/(b+1)]/a,
    v_stationary=a/(1-a),
    v_best=min{v_cross,max{R,v_stationary}},
    K=C^2 eta^2.                                       (27)

Then R>=1/a>=b and R<=v_cross. The first assertion follows because
Htri has its nonnegative zero at1/a and is increasing thereafter. For
the second, Htri(R)=ell implies(b+1)(aR-1)<=ell.

The exact infimum of(26) over EVERY legal triangle parameter is

    Enew=(1-a^2)v_best^2-2(1+a)a v_best+1+2(1+a)
                +[2(1+a)+1-b^2]ell-K.                 (28)

If ell>0 the minimizing triangle has z=sqrt(ell)>0 and v=v_best.
If ell=0 the same formula is attained by the displayed degenerate
legal data; alternatively it is the limit of nondegenerate triangles.

Here is the complete minimization. For fixed v>=R, the price switches
at z^2=(b+1)t, which is no larger than Htri(v) because v>=b. Below
this value its coefficient of z^2 is1-b^2; above it the coefficient
is1-b^2+2(1+a)>=2a>0. If b<=1, z^2=ell is a minimizer. If b>1, the
minimizer is z^2=max{ell,(b+1)t}. Thus for R<=v<=v_cross BOTH cases
use z^2=ell, the second term in(23) is the minimum, and(26) becomes

    J_left(v)=(1-a^2)v^2-2(1+a)a v+1+2(1+a)
                         +[2(1+a)+1-b^2]ell-K.         (29)

For v>=v_cross and b<=1 it becomes

    J_right(v)=(1-a^2)v^2+2(1+a)ab v+1-2(1+a)b
                              +(1-b^2)ell-K.           (30)

J_right has strictly positive derivative on that half-line. If b>1,
the corresponding expression for v>=v_cross is instead

    J_kink(v)=(1-a^2)v^2
        +a[2(1+a)b+(1-b^2)(b+1)]v
        +1-2(1+a)b-(1-b^2)(b+1)-K.                    (30a)

Its derivative is positive for v>=1/a. To see this, divide that
derivative by a and use v>=1/a and ab<=1:

    J_kink'(v)/a
      >=2/a^2-2+2(1+a)b-(b^2-1)(b+1)
      >=2(1+a)b-(b^2-1)(b-1)
      >=2(1+a)b-2(b-1)=2(ab+1)>0.

The last inequality uses b^2<=3 and b>1. Each right expression agrees
with J_left at v_cross. Hence in either b regime no minimum occurs
strictly after v_cross. J_left is a strictly convex quadratic with
stationary point a/(1-a). Clipping that point to[R,v_cross] proves
(27)--(28), including both endpoint cases.

The original unpriced C82 minimum in this domain is

    Eold=((1+a)R-1)^2+(1-b^2)ell-K,                    (31)

For b<=1 its energy increases in v and is minimized at z^2=ell. For
b>1 its minimizing z^2 at fixed v is Htri(v). The resulting quadratic
has leading coefficient(1+a)^2+(1-b^2)a>=1+a^2>0 and derivative at
v=1/a equal to(1+a)[2/a+1-b^2]>0, since a<1 and b^2<=3. Its derivative
therefore stays positive for v>=R>=1/a, and its minimum is at R too.
At v=R, Htri(R)=ell makes Dprice=0, and J_left(R)=Eold.

Consequently value pricing adds EXACTLY NO information to this fully
optimized C82 condition whenever

    R>=a/(1-a).                                        (32)

In particular(32) holds throughout a^2+a<=1, because R>=1/a.
The positive root of a^2+a=1 is(sqrt(5)-1)/2. This includes the
first-step projection range39/100<=a<=41/100 from d3abee1b17da52da,
with its b range79/100<=b<=81/100. The C83 price was already zero there
by Section4, independently of this comparison.

When ell>0 and R<a/(1-a), one has v_cross>R and v_best>R, so the
optimized energy is strictly smaller. The precise positive reduction is

    Eold-Enew=(1-a^2)*[(R-v_stationary)^2
                                 -(v_best-v_stationary)^2]>0. (33)

Equivalently this strict-improvement regime is

    a^2+a>1,
    0<ell<(a^2+a-1)/(1-a)^2.                            (34)

This proves a strict improvement of the C82 FAMILY VALUE in its stated
domain. It does NOT prove that a word satisfying all the other current
necessary conditions is rejected by(28). In particular(34) alone is
not a surviving full-cone region and must not be advertised as one.

## 8. Comparison, resources, and the precise remaining interface

* C83: Section4 completely resolves the proposed value-price mechanism

# C93: curvature costs and an exact single-region obstruction for static ridge sums

Status: **UNVERIFIED JOINT PROOF DRAFT**. Current runtime round is 1 of
the new allocation, completed baseline 23 and completed ceiling 25. This
round would bring the completed count to 24 after the runtime returns.
No numerical/model evaluation, sweep, solver, replay, installation,
subordinate agent, or verifier call was used. The original problem is open.

Accepted mathematical predecessors used here are `1252b8823bb5a290`
(necessity of every original smooth-convex interpolation inequality),
`b98bb807d514e80d` (the exact scalar Huber/single-cut lower bound and the
original benchmark), `1fca3e5dd555cb4a` (the explicit alternating-ray
construction), and `04219554e41d9750` (the original dyadic benchmark limit).
All new assertions are proved together below. No shared unverified result
is a mathematical predecessor.

The shared ruler audit `bf591e52671f6d33` suggested the activated-product
quantity used in Section 5. Its needed estimates are rederived here, and
the new conclusion is a resolvent inequality, rather than its quadratic
objective bound. The accepted finite C59 fact `e9a55f57461f253c` and max's
shared actual31 construction `7ffb4d0516ace32f` were read for scope. Neither
is inserted as a child, used as an asymptotic premise, or replayed.

## 1. Family, definitions, and resolved scope

All vector spaces are finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces. Matrices
are symmetric unless otherwise specified, and matrix inequalities refer
to positive semidefinite order. The identity matrix is denoted I.

For positive radii r_minus,r_plus, define the scalar asymmetric Huber
function phi by phi(0)=0 and

    phi'(s)=max(-r_minus,min(s,r_plus)).                 (1)

Thus phi(s)=s^2/2 inside [-r_minus,r_plus],
phi(s)=r_plus*s-r_plus^2/2 for s>=r_plus, and
phi(s)=-r_minus*s-r_minus^2/2 for s<=-r_minus.
Both joins include their boundaries, where the values and derivatives agree.

Consider ONE STATIC function

    F(x)=x^T A0 x/2 + sum_(j=1)^r alpha_j phi_j(u_j^T x), (2)

where r is any nonnegative integer, A0>=0, every u_j is a unit vector,
alpha_j>0, and every phi_j has its own positive radii. Assume

    H0=A0+sum_j alpha_j u_j u_j^T <= I.                 (3)

The number of ridges, dimension, matrices, directions, and both radii may
depend arbitrarily on the horizon. The ridges need not be orthogonal.
The quadratic part need not commute with any ridge matrix.

For a fixed finite nonnegative word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), set

    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, K=1/(1+2S),
    P_h(t)=product_(i<n)(1-h_i*t),
    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i grad F(x_i), 0<=i<n.                (4)

The normalized payoff is

    V=2F(x_n)/dist(x_0,argmin F)^2,                     (5)

and initial points in the minimizer set are omitted.

A **fixed-region run** means that, for EACH ridge separately, all samples
x_0,...,x_n, INCLUDING the actual unqueried terminal sample, belong to one
of that ridge's three closed intervals: its core, its positive outer ray,
or its negative outer ray. Different ridges may choose different regions.
At a shared boundary either compatible region may be chosen. No condition
is imposed on signs or correlations of the full gradients.

The main quantitative conclusion of this joint draft is:

* If P_h(t)^2 <= 1/(1+2S*t) for every t in [0,1], every fixed-region run
  of (2) has V<=K. This includes all true normalization costs.
* On the ORIGINAL diagnostic H_m defined in Section 5, for every m>=128,
  that polynomial inequality holds, and the supremum of V over the entire
  fixed-region class is EXACTLY K_n(H_m)=1/(1+2 sum H_m).
* Its exact original-benchmark ratio tends to Z_1/(2e)<4/5. Here
  Z_1=lim_(m->infinity)(1+sqrt(2))^(-m) B_(2^m-1), as in accepted
  `04219554e41d9750`, and e is the exponential of 1.

This closes the full fixed-region subclass with arbitrary quadratic
coupling and any number of subunit-curvature ridges. It does NOT close
trajectories that change a ridge region, including a change only at the
terminal sample. Section 8 gives a genuinely coupled static example
with two physical sign changes and actual noncommuting region visits.
It refutes dropping the fixed-region premise even on a word satisfying
the same polynomial inequality. Its payoff is explicitly compared with
the stronger already accepted scalar construction and is NOT presented
as new lower-bound strength.

## 2. Global legality, minimizers, and every original pair

Each phi_j is differentiable, convex, nonnegative, and zero only at zero.
For any x,z, monotonicity and the Lipschitz bound in (1) provide numbers
d_j in [0,alpha_j] such that

    grad F(x)-grad F(z)
      =[A0+sum_j d_j u_j u_j^T](x-z).

If u_j^T(x-z)=0 its contribution is zero and d_j may be taken as zero.
The displayed matrix lies between zero and H0, and hence between zero
and I. Its operator norm is at most 1. This proves global 1-smoothness;
convexity also follows directly from the sum in (2).

Conversely, all radii are positive, so a ball about zero lies in every
core. In that ball F(x)=x^T H0 x/2. Thus global 1-smoothness forces (3).
Condition (3) is exact for this centered model, not merely a sufficient
trace bound.

The minimizer set is precisely the subspace

    N=ker(A0) intersect intersection_j u_j^perp.        (6)

Indeed every summand of (2) is nonnegative, and their simultaneous
vanishing is exactly (6). Let z_0 be the orthogonal projection of x_0
onto N and replace every x_i by x_i-z_0. The objective, gradient, ridge
coordinates, GD recursion, and fixed-region condition are unchanged,
because all gradients lie in N^perp. The initial squared norm after
this replacement equals the TRUE squared distance in (5). We therefore
work below with x_0 in N^perp and denominator ||x_0||^2.

The pair convention is the original one:

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    f_i=F(x_i), g_i=grad F(x_i), x_star=g_star=f_star=0.

Every Q_ij is nonpositive, including both terminal directions and both
optimum directions. To spell out the accepted necessity argument from
`1252b8823bb5a290`, fix i and define
J(z)=F(z)-<g_i,z>. Convexity and grad J(x_i)=0 make x_i a global
minimizer of J. Smoothness gives
J(x_j-grad J(x_j))<=J(x_j)-||grad J(x_j)||^2/2.
The minimum J(x_i) is at most this value. Rearranging gives Q_ij<=0.
This one argument checks every ordered pair of the actual trajectory;
no subset of remote, zero-step, optimum, or terminal rows is discarded.

## 3. A sharp curvature price, including shifted ridge cores

This section treats a broader geometry than (2): allow an additional
linear term and shifts in every ridge argument, and let each scalar
convex ridge have a nonempty open interval where its second derivative
is the constant alpha_j>0. Assume the whole sum is globally 1-smooth
and its quadratic Hessian A0 is positive semidefinite.

At a point in one ridge core, second differences in an arbitrary
direction z, using nonnegativity of the second differences of all
other convex terms, give

    A0+alpha_j u_j u_j^T <= I.                         (7)

For two NONPARALLEL directions u,v, their shifted open core slabs
intersect. In fact the map x -> (u^T x,v^T x) is surjective onto R^2:
on span(u,v) its matrix has determinant 1-<u,v>^2>0. Thus any desired
pair of interior core arguments can be achieved simultaneously.
At such a point the same second-difference argument gives

    A0+alpha u u^T+beta v v^T <= I.                    (8)

These arguments require no differentiability of other summands at that
point. For sufficiently small real t the two selected core terms have
second differences exactly t^2 alpha<u,z>^2 and t^2 beta<v,z>^2,
while 1-smoothness bounds the total symmetric second difference by
t^2||z||^2.

Writing rho=<u,v>, the largest eigenvalue of
alpha uu^T+beta vv^T on their span is

    [alpha+beta+sqrt((alpha-beta)^2+4alpha beta rho^2)]/2.

Consequently (8) implies alpha,beta<=1 and the sharp necessary bound

    alpha beta rho^2 <= (1-alpha)(1-beta).             (9)

To obtain (9), square the nonnegative inequality
sqrt((alpha-beta)^2+4alpha beta rho^2)<=2-alpha-beta
and cancel. With A0=0 it is also sufficient for this pair's matrix to
be bounded by I, so this numerical curvature price is sharp.

There is a sharp bound on coupling to A0 as well. For one ridge let
s=1-alpha and write A0 relative to u and u^perp as

    A0 = [ a  b^T ; b  C ].

If b is nonzero, put v=b/||b|| and c=v^T C v. Positivity of A0 and
of I-A0-alpha uu^T, restricted to span(u,v), gives

    ||b||^2<=a c,  ||b||^2<=(s-a)(1-c),
    0<=a<=s, 0<=c<=1.

If a<=s(1-c), the first bound is at most s c(1-c). If
a>=s(1-c), the second bound is at most that same quantity. Hence

    ||(I-uu^T)A0 u|| <= sqrt(1-alpha)/2.              (10)

The case b=0 already satisfies this. Equality is attained in dimension
two by u=e_1 and

    A_s=(1/2)[s,sqrt(s);sqrt(s),1], alpha=1-s,
    0<s<1.                                          (11)

Both A_s and I-A_s-alpha e_1e_1^T are rank-one positive semidefinite
matrices. This is an ACTUAL available coupling, not a forbidden one.

In particular a ridge of full individual curvature alpha=1 satisfies
A0 u=0: (7) gives u^T A0 u=0, and positive semidefiniteness implies
A0 u=0. Any two nonparallel full-curvature ridge directions are
orthogonal by (9). Parallel shifted ridge terms must be grouped into
one scalar function; they need not have overlapping cores.

It follows that a sum consisting entirely of full-curvature convex
ridges plus a PSD quadratic, with any shifts and any linear term,
separates orthogonally into scalar ridge groups and an independent
quadratic on their orthogonal complement. If its minimum is attained,
its minimizer set is the Cartesian product of the scalar minimizer
sets and the quadratic minimizer affine subspace. Squared distance to
that product is the sum of squared component distances. GD separates
in the same coordinates. For every h the true-distance payoff is
therefore a weighted average of the actual scalar-group payoffs and
quadratic eigenmode payoffs

    t * product_(i<n)(1-h_i*t)^2, 0<=t<=1.             (12)

A component starting in its minimizer set stays there and contributes
zero to both numerator and denominator. This proves that rotating or
adding such full-curvature ridges cannot yield a genuinely coupled
multidimensional improvement over the best component on the SAME word.
It does not bound arbitrary scalar multi-return profiles by K_n(h).

## 4. Exact terminal algebra and the fixed-region bound

Return to the centered model (2). For a fixed-region run absorb all
always-core ridges into the quadratic matrix and write

    A=A0+sum_(j in Core) alpha_j u_j u_j^T,
    b=sum_(j in Outer) epsilon_j q_j u_j,
    D0=sum_(j in Outer) q_j^2/alpha_j,                 (13)

where epsilon_j is +1 or -1 for its chosen outer ray, and
q_j=alpha_j times its radius on that ray. Every actual sample satisfies

    f_i=x_i^T A x_i/2+b^T x_i-D0/2,  g_i=A x_i+b.    (14)

Condition (3) becomes

    A+sum_(j in Outer) alpha_j u_j u_j^T <= I.         (15)

Let L=I-A. For every vector z, scalar Cauchy--Schwarz and (15) give

    (b^T z)^2 <= D0 * z^T L z.                       (16)

Consequently b is orthogonal to ker L. Define L^dagger by reciprocating
its positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to its zero eigenvalues.
Putting z=L^dagger b in (16), or treating b=0 separately, proves

    D0 >= b^T L^dagger b.                            (17)

Thus the intercept cost required by global smoothness is retained even
when many nonorthogonal ridge forces add in the same direction.

Define polynomials (with their continuous values at t=0)

    R_h(t)=(1-P_h(t))/t, R_h(0)=S,
    T_h(t)=(1-P_h(t)^2)/t, T_h(0)=2S.

Unrolling g_i=A x_i+b yields

    x_n=P_h(A)x_0-R_h(A)b.                           (18)

This identity is also proved inductively using
R_(prefix+h)(t)=(1-h*t)R_prefix(t)+h. Substituting (18) into (14),
and using I-A R_h(A)=P_h(A), gives the EXACT identity

    2f_n=x_0^T A P_h(A)^2 x_0
           +2b^T P_h(A)^2 x_0-D0-b^T T_h(A)b.        (19)

No radius, value, forcing term, or terminal quantity has been removed.

Assume now the polynomial condition

    P_h(t)^2 <= 1/(1+2S*t), 0<=t<=1.                 (20)

Diagonalize A orthogonally. For one eigenvalue t in (0,1), abbreviate
p=P_h(t)^2 and

    d=1/(1-t)+(1-p)/t.

By (17), its contribution to the right side of (19) is bounded by

    t p X^2+2p X B-d B^2,                            (21)

where X,B are the coordinates of x_0,b on this eigenvector. We claim
(21)<=K X^2. First d>0 by (20), and
t p<=t/(1+2S*t)<=K. The determinant needed to complete the square is

    (K-t p)d-p^2
       =[K-p(K+t(1-K))]/[t(1-t)] >=0,               (22)

because K/[K+t(1-K)]=1/(1+2S*t). Thus the two-variable quadratic
K X^2-(21) is positive semidefinite.

At t=0, p=1, and its contribution is at most
2XB-(1+2S)B^2<=K X^2 by completing a square. At t=1, (16) gives
B=0, and the contribution is P_h(1)^2 X^2<=K X^2 by (20).
Summing all eigenvector inequalities proves 2f_n<=K||x_0||^2.
Section 2 identified that norm with the true closest-minimizer distance.
This proves the first quantitative claim in Section 1, including zero
eigenvalues, unit eigenvalues, empty outer sets, and zero physical steps.

Equality is attained by the actual scalar global Huber witness for ANY
nonnegative word: take A0=0, one unit ridge of curvature 1, both radii
q=1/(1+2S), and initial point x_0=1. All iterates are
x_i=1-q sum_(t<i)h_t >=(1+S)/(1+2S)>=q. The fixed positive outer
region condition includes the terminal point. Direct substitution gives
2F(x_n)=1/(1+2S), the initial true distance is 1, and the minimizer is
unique. Hence whenever (20) holds the restricted supremum is exactly K.

## 5. The resolvent inequality on the ORIGINAL H_m, with all curvatures

Fix an integer m>=128, and keep the following enclosing-horizon
parameters fixed in EVERY child word:

    sigma=1+sqrt(2), c=sigma(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    d_j=1+a*c^j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

The actual physical word is h=H_m, of length n=2^m-1. Write
S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j, r_c=c-2, and A_mass=a/r_c. Counting the
occurrences of each bridge gives

    M_j=A_mass*c^j+(1-A_mass)*2^j,
    P_j(t)=product_(l=0)^(j-1)(1-d_l*t)^(2^(j-l-1)).   (23)

Here P_j is the polynomial of the complete physical word H_j; P_0=1.

The following bounds follow from squaring the rational comparisons
7/5<sqrt(2)<10/7 and using m>=128:

    12/5<c<49/20, 3/8<a<sigma-2<c-2<9/20,
    127/128<=ac<1, 0<A_mass<1, c*r_c<5/4.            (24)

For the upper c bound, c<(17/7)(129/128)=2193/896<49/20.
For the lower a bound, a>(127/128)/(49/20)>3/8. The upper bound on
a follows from a=(m-1)/[(m+1)sigma]<1/sigma=sigma-2.
In particular (23) gives M_j<=c^j and

    t*S_j >= a*c^j*t/r_c-t.                          (25)

We prove (20) for this exact h. At t=0 it is equality. Fix t in (0,1].
If every d_l*t<1 for 0<=l<m, all factors are nonnegative and
1-z<=exp(-z) gives

    P_m(t)^2 <= exp(-2S_m*t) <= 1/(1+2S_m*t).        (26)

If a factor is zero the required conclusion is immediate. Otherwise
let j be the first level with d_j*t>=1. Set

    v_l=a*c^l*t, Y_l=c*v_l*|P_l(t)|.

If j=0 then Y_0=ac*t<=1. If j>=1, all factors of P_j are on their
nonnegative side, and t<1/d_0<8/11. From (25),

    Y_j<=c*v_j*exp(-v_j/r_c+t)
         <=c*r_c*exp(t-1)<1.                         (27)

The middle bound maximizes v exp(-v/r_c) over v>=0, with maximum
r_c/e. The last inequality uses c*r_c<5/4 and
exp(3/11)>1+3/11=14/11>5/4.

For every l>=j, the exact physical recursion in (23) gives

    Y_(l+1)=[1-(1-t)/v_l]*Y_l^2 <=Y_l^2<=1.          (28)

The bracket is between zero and one, since d_l*t>=1 and t<=1.
Consequently, with z=a*c^m*t,

    P_m(t)^2 <= 1/(c^2*z^2).                         (29)

Activation implies t>=1/d_(m-1). Since m>=3, (24) implies

    z>=c*[a*c^(m-1)]/[1+a*c^(m-1)]
       >(12/5)*(54/25)/(1+54/25)=648/395>3/2.        (30)

Also S_m<c^m by (23). Therefore

    (1+2S_m*t)P_m(t)^2
       <=[1+(16/3)z]/[(144/25)z^2]
       <=25/36<1.                                  (31)

For the final inequality the function z^(-2)+(16/3)z^(-1) decreases
for z>0, and its value at z=3/2 gives 25/36 after multiplication by
25/144. Equations (26) and (31) cover EVERY t in [0,1]. In particular
there was no curvature grid, schedule replay, or fixed-curvature premise.

## 6. Same-word scalar comparison and the ORIGINAL benchmark

We also rederive that the best accepted Huber/single-cut value on this
word is the global Huber value, so the comparison is on the SAME word.
For a cut at level j its squared numerator is (a*c^j)^2. Holding the
total S_m and bridge d_j fixed, the denominator is

    (1+P)^2[1+2(S_m-d_j-P)],

where P is the actual preceding mass. Its logarithm has strictly
negative second derivative in the interior of the allowed mass range.
Thus its minimum over the interval between the first and last occurrence
is at an endpoint. The palindrome H_m makes the following mass at its
first occurrence at least S_(m-1), and its preceding mass is S_j. At
the last occurrence the preceding mass is at least S_(m-1), and the
following mass is S_j. Put M=M_(m-1).

From (23), a*c^j<=r_c*M_j, M_j<=M, and M_m<=c*M. The first-occurrence
cut is at most r_c^2/(2M-1). The last-occurrence cut is at most

    r_c^2*M_j^2/[M^2(2M_j-1)] <= r_c^2/(2M-1),

because x^2/(2x-1) is nondecreasing for x>=1. Finally c<5/2,
r_c<1/2, and M>=1 give

    r_c^2(2M_m-1) <=(5M-1)/4 <=2M-1.

Every cut in accepted `b98bb807d514e80d` is therefore no larger than
1/(2M_m-1). Its global Huber term attains that value. Hence

    sup_fixed-region V = K_n(H_m)=1/(2S_m+1).         (32)

For the limit, divide (23), at j=m, by sigma^m. Since a/(c-2)->1,
(1+1/m)^m->e, and (2/sigma)^m->0, one gets

    M_m/sigma^m -> e.

The accepted ray theorem `04219554e41d9750` supplies
B_(2^m-1)/sigma^m -> Z_1. Thus the exact restricted ratio has limit

    B_(2^m-1)*sup_fixed-region V -> Z_1/(2e).         (33)

For an explicit strict gap, its accepted upper enclosure at b=1,j=0
gives Z_1<=(sqrt(B_1)+3/100)^2. The accepted original recurrence gives
B_1=4. Therefore Z_1<=41209/10000. The positive exponential series
gives e>1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3, whence

    Z_1/(2e)<123627/160000<4/5.                      (34)

No fit, substituted recurrence, internal capacity, or scalar radius
of a higher-dimensional witness is used in this comparison.

## 7. The coupled fixed-region class is nonempty on every word

Here is a fully specified genuinely coupled instance satisfying its
region hypothesis for ANY finite nonnegative h. It is included to rule
out a merely vacuous obstruction. Work in R^2 and put

    u=e_1, w=(e_1+e_2)/sqrt(2),
    eta=1/[8(1+S)], A0=eta*w*w^T,
    alpha=1/2, q=eta, r_minus=r_plus=q/alpha,
    F(x)=x^T A0 x/2+alpha*phi(u^T x), x_0=e_1.       (35)

The matrices A0 and uu^T do not commute. Also
A0+alpha uu^T <=(eta+alpha)I<=5I/8<I. The minimizer is unique zero,
since the two distinct directions w and u span R^2.

To check the actual gates without numerical evaluation, first run the
explicit affine recursion z_(i+1)=(I-h_i A0)z_i-h_i q u, z_0=e_1.
Every factor I-h_i A0 has norm at most one, because
0<=h_i eta<=S/[8(1+S)]<1. Consequently
||z_i||<=1+q sum_(t<i)h_t<=9/8. Its displacement from e_1 satisfies

    ||z_i-e_1||<=sum_(t<i)h_t(eta*9/8+q)<17/64.

Thus u^T z_i>47/64, whereas r_plus=1/[4(1+S)]<=1/4.
Every sample including z_n is strictly in the positive outer region.
It follows inductively that z_i IS the actual GD run of the single
function (35). Section 2 supplies all original pairs and true radius 1.
The payoff need not equal (32); Section 4 shows that on H_m it cannot
exceed (32). This is not a scalar copy hidden behind a coordinate change:
its actual outer Hessian A0 and central Hessian A0+alpha uu^T do not
commute, although this particular run only visits the outer region.

## 8. A static multiple-sign escape, and its honest payoff comparison

The next example attacks the fragile extension that the polynomial
condition alone might bound ALL trajectories of (2) by the global Huber
value. It preserves that condition and releases the fixed-region premise.
It also shows that the curvature rigidity at alpha=1 is not valid for
arbitrarily small positive slack. It is a scope example, not a new
competitive lower bound on H_m or on arbitrary words.

Take the fixed physical word

    h=(1,4,1,4,1), S=11, K=1/23.                    (36)

Its polynomial is P_h(t)=(1-t)^3(1-4t)^2. For 0<=t<=1/4, all factors
are nonnegative, so P_h(t)^2<=exp(-22t)<=1/(1+22t). For t>=1/4 put
z=1-t in [0,3/4]. Then P_h(t)=z^3(3-4z)^2. Its derivative as a
function of z is z^2(3-4z)(9-20z), and the maximum is

    (9/20)^3*(6/5)^2=6561/50000<1/7.

It follows that (1+22t)P_h(t)^2<=23/49<1 on this second interval.
Thus (20) holds on ALL of [0,1] for the same word (36).

Let phi have radii r_minus=3/4 and r_plus=1/2. Fix ANY
0<epsilon<=1/1000000 before the run, put s=epsilon^2, and define

    F_epsilon(x,y)=(epsilon*x+y)^2/4+(1-s)*phi(x),
    (x_0,y_0)=(5/4,0).                              (37)

Its quadratic is A_s from (11), its ridge direction is e_1, and its
ridge curvature is 1-s. Thus it is globally convex and 1-smooth. Its
unique minimizer is (0,0), giving true initial squared distance 25/16.
Its outer and central Hessians are

    A_s=(1/2)[s,epsilon;epsilon,1],
    C_s=A_s+(1-s)e_1e_1^T.

They do not commute for epsilon>0. Both are PSD and bounded by I, since
I-C_s=(1/2)(epsilon,-1)(epsilon,-1)^T.

At epsilon=0, the exact first-coordinate trajectory on (36) is

    5/4, 3/4, -5/4, -1/2, 3/2, 1,                  (38)

and the second coordinate stays zero. The corresponding first gradient
coordinates are

    1/2, 1/2, -3/4, -1/2, 1/2, 1/2.

Its ridge regions are positive outer, positive outer, negative outer,
core, positive outer, positive outer. Every listed point has distance
at least 1/4 from the boundary of its specified open region.

Here is a uniform TEXTUAL perturbation bound establishing those SAME
actual region visits for every epsilon in the specified interval.
The matrix change A_s-A_0 has norm at most epsilon, and |phi'|<=3/4.
At every unperturbed sample, whose norm is at most 3/2, this gives

    ||grad F_epsilon(z_i^0)-grad F_0(z_i^0)||<=3epsilon.

Let E_i=||z_i^epsilon-z_i^0|| for the actual GD runs, and put
D_i=product_(t<i)(1+h_t). Global 1-smoothness gives
E_(i+1)<=(1+h_i)E_i+3epsilon*h_i, and hence

    E_i<=3epsilon(D_i-1)<=597epsilon<1/1000.          (39)

The product at n=5 is exactly 2*5*2*5*2=200. Equation (39) is a
five-step analytic perturbation estimate, not a numerical replay.
It preserves every strict gate in (38). In particular the actual run
visits A_s,C_s,A_s at queried indices 2,3,4. It has TWO actual sign
changes in both the first position coordinate and first gradient
coordinate, with gradient signs +,+,-,-,+,+.

The correlations are not constant, and the gradients are not collinear.
For the first two actual gradients, which use the positive outer region,
direct substitution gives

    g_0=(1/2+s/8,5epsilon/8),
    g_1=((1-s)(1/2+s/16),epsilon(1-s)/16),
    det(g_0,g_1)=-epsilon(1-s)(9+s)/32 !=0.           (40)

Their inner product is positive. The error of any actual gradient from
its unperturbed counterpart is at most E_i+3epsilon<=600epsilon.
Thus <g_1,g_2><0: its unperturbed value is -3/8, while the absolute
change is at most (5/4)(600epsilon)+(600epsilon)^2<1/100.
This proves distinct normalized correlations as well as noncollinearity.

All original ordered Q rows, including the actual terminal rows, follow
from Section 2 applied to (37). No Hessian is chosen online.

The payoff comparison must keep the true radius. At z_5^0=(1,0),

    F_epsilon(1,0)=3/8-s/8,
    grad F_epsilon(1,0)=(1/2,epsilon/2).

This gradient has norm less than one. Convexity, smoothness and (39)
therefore give |F_epsilon(z_5^epsilon)-3/8|<1/100. Since the true
squared radius is 25/16,

    9/20 < V_epsilon=(32/25)F_epsilon(z_5^epsilon)<1/2. (41)

For example the stronger bounds from 3/8 plus or minus 1/100 are
2336/5000<V_epsilon<2464/5000, which imply (41).
This strictly exceeds the global Huber value 1/23 despite (20), so
dropping the fixed-region premise of Section 4 is refuted.

On this SAME word the exact accepted single-cut maximum is

    K_5(h)=max(1/23,9/52,3/49)=9/52<9/20.            (42)

Nevertheless the stronger accepted scalar construction
`1fca3e5dd555cb4a` already gives 73/48>1/2. Its two checkpoints are
4 and 4, with all three ordinary masses equal to 1. The fact's exact
parameters are m_0=1/2,m_1=3/4,O_1=1/2,z_term=7/4,e_term=1/4,
and q_opt=7/12. Feasibility is z_term>=2m_0=1, and its payoff is

    2e_term+z_term^2/3=1/2+49/48=73/48.              (43)

Thus (37) is an actual nonlinear, noncommuting, multiple-sign scope
example with a checked quantitative gap over the single-cut calibration.
It is DOMINATED by an already accepted scalar witness and is not new
lower-bound strength. The word (36) is not H_m and supplies neither the
arbitrary-h nor the non-dyadic quantifiers of the project goal.

## 9. Interface left for the next authorized round

The fixed-region mechanism on the original H_m is exactly Huber-tight,
even with an arbitrary number of centered ridges, arbitrary dimension,
subunit ridge curvatures, and noncommuting quadratic coupling. The
full-curvature relay is additionally forced to split into scalar groups.
These are separate scoped exclusions; neither excludes all static ridge
sums.

The explicit escape (37) shows the remaining mechanism is real: a
subunit ridge can visit its core between opposite outer visits, while
the background quadratic generates changing correlations. What remains
missing is a fixed static gated construction on ORIGINAL H_m with a
terminal value exceeding its accepted scalar baseline, with all region
visits and true distance controlled uniformly. The matrices and affine
forcing are fixed by (37), not freely selectable at each bridge. There
is no authorized numerical search or verifier call for that step.

For max's actual31 state, this result supplies a price only if a proposed
realization is specifically a centered Huber-ridge sum of (2). No claim
is made that its conjugate interpolant has that representation. Its
positive endpoint state, changed values, residuals, and minimizer hull
cannot be inserted into (19) without proving the representation and
the fixed-region hypothesis. C59 likewise is not claimed to belong to
this family, and its fixed H6 parameters were never replaced by those
of another enclosing horizon.

# Exact terminal-covariance completion in the original primitive cone

Status: complete joint proof DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max4 analytical
round29, the first of the two rounds authorized after completed baseline28
by TASK.md and master_guidance f7608aa358751108. Numerical, solver,
replay, installation and formal-verifier allowances are all closed.
The only accepted mathematical input is fact04219554e41d9750, Section10,
for the original primitive identity. No other draft is a premise.

The original high-capacity seed and the original exact-profile goal remain
open. The result here is an exact decision of a full-interface affine
fiber: all twenty original coefficient signs and PSD on all five formal
gradients are tested simultaneously, including every singular boundary.
The line is not asserted to cover the whole cone. Its unresolved freedom
and its relation to the existing complete coordinates are explicit below.

## 1. Original interface and the earlier coupled gap

Let h=(h0,h1,h2,h3) be a nonnegative four-step word, P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t,
s=P_4>0, and C=1+s. The five standard coordinate columns are e_i,
indices0 through4; e is their sum. Set

    T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
    omega=(-2h0,-2h1,-2h2,-2h3,2s)^T,
    D=diag(h0(2-h0),h1(2-h1),h2(2-h2),h3(2-h3),-s(s+2)).

The original array has Lambda_ii=0 and twenty off-diagonal entries.
Write L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda and M=D+sym(LT), where
sym(A)=(A+A^T)/2. Full feasibility means

    Lambda_ij>=0 for all i!=j, L^T e=omega, M>=0 on R^5.       (1)

The exact identity in accepted04219554e41d9750 is

    V_h+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij = <M,Gram(g0,...,g4)>,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                                   -s(s+1)||g4||^2,
    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i.                                    (2)

Every formal gradient is retained. In particular, a zero step does not
authorize an equality between formal coordinates.

The flow forces e^T M e=0: Te=e+P,
2sum h_i P_i=s^2-sum h_i^2, and

    e^T D e=-s^2-sum h_i^2,
    e^T LT e=omega^T(e+P)=s^2+sum h_i^2.

PSD then implies Me=0, by considering (e+t*z)^T M(e+t*z) for
both signs of t. Conversely, later in this document the flow and Me=0
are imposed before testing PSD; this does not assert that either implies
PSD. The row moments equivalent to Me=0 under the flow are

    sum_j Lambda_ij(P_j-P_i)=2h_i(1+P_i), i<4,
    sum_(j<4)Lambda_4j(s-P_j)=2sC.                           (3)

Define the quadratic column by

    p0=1, p_(i+1)=(1-h_i)p_i.

Then Tp=e, so Le=0 gives

    p^T M p=p^T D p=1-C^2*p4^2=:Qenergy.                    (4)

The last equality telescopes h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2.
Thus (4) holds for every real array with the flow, without assuming PSD.

For the positive-excess regime, write

    h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,1+d), a,b,c,d>0,
    u=1+a, delta=u^2-2, eta=b/(3+c+d),
    nu=(1+eta)(1-a*eta)/a,
    Erow=a+3+1/a-(u*delta/a)*eta-C^2*eta^2,
    Wrow=max(1+b,1+b*c*d), Krow=max(u,a*Wrow).

When a>sqrt(2)-1, full feasibility forces a<1, a*eta<1,
nu>0 and 0<=Qenergy<1. The complete earlier first-row result is

    u*delta<=Krow*Erow/nu+2*sqrt(Qenergy*Erow/nu),             (5)
    Erow>=nu*[u*delta/
       (sqrt(Qenergy+Krow*u*delta)+sqrt(Qenergy))]^2>0.       (6)

With the ADDITIONAL hypotheses a*b<=1 and c*d<=1, it gives

    Erow>nu*delta^2/u^2,
    b<(a+3)*(C-a-2)/((a+1)*(C+a+2)).                        (7)

No hypothesis in these bounds is removed. The proof of the earlier
joint draft2948d4cd3660413f is reproduced in Appendix A, not cited as
an accepted fact. In particular its exact accounting identity is

    Erow=nu*(M00+a*(Lambda20+Lambda30+Lambda40))
         +(1+eta)^2*M11
         +(1+eta)*eta*((2+c+d)*Lambda12+(1+d)*Lambda13).      (8)

The new completion below preserves EVERY term on the right of (8),
the exact first-row/quadratic cross term, and the endpoint principal
block. Thus (5)--(8) remain simultaneous conditions, rather than a
replacement for either the original signs or the full PSD condition.

## 2. Direct terminal identities and the unpriced covariance

Put v=h3>0 and B=P3=s-v. Write y_j=Lambda_4j for j<4,
n=M44, and delta_v=2C-(C+1)*v. The terminal diagonal is

    n=sum_(j<4)y_j-s(s+2).

Using (3) gives the exact nonnegative budget

    v*n+sum_(j=0)^2(P3-P_j)*y_j=s*delta_v.                  (9)

For PSD arrays this includes n>=0 and every y_j>=0, so delta_v>=0.
There is no division by delta_v or n. If delta_v=0 and h0,h1,h2>0,
then n=0 and y0=y1=y2=0. Full PSD then forces the entire terminal
row of M to vanish. The case of zero prefix steps retains the displayed
weights: a vanishing weight cannot be cancelled to deduce y_j=0.

The exact terminal/quadratic covariance is

    2*e4^T M p=(n-s(s+2))*p4-sum_(i<4)Lambda_i4*p_i.        (10)

Indeed Mp=Dp+T^T L^T p/2 and Te4=e4, while
(L^T p)_4=(sum y_j)*p4-sum_(i<4)Lambda_i4*p_i.
The weighted INCOMING terminal sum in (10) is not priced by (9),
which involves OUTGOING terminal coefficients. Its odd quadratic
coefficients can have the opposite sign from its even coefficients.
Replacing that sum by a nonnegative total mass would lose information.

The endpoint cross term is independently

    2*M04=(h0-1)*Lambda40-Lambda04.                        (11)

These formulas use original rows, not any reversal theorem. They show
where the new cross term enters, but alone do not prove that it is free.
The next section exhibits the precise freedom in the actual array.

## 3. A four-edge motion preserving the already coupled energies

Assume w=h2>0 and v=h3>0. Start with ANY real base array Lambda^0
having the original flow and M^0 e=0. It need not be PSD. For a real
parameter theta change only these four original coefficients:

    Lambda23(theta)=Lambda23^0+(1+v/w)*theta,
    Lambda24(theta)=Lambda24^0-theta,
    Lambda32(theta)=Lambda32^0+(v/w)*theta,
    Lambda34(theta)=Lambda34^0+theta.                       (12)

All other off-diagonal coefficients stay exactly as in the base array.
The diagonal is still zero. Define

    v_move=e2-e3,
    w_move=(v/w)*e2-(1+v/w)*e3+e4.

The change of the row Laplacian is exactly

    L(theta)-L^0=theta*v_move*w_move^T.                     (13)

Both e^T v_move and w_move^T e vanish, and

    w_move^T P=(v/w)*(P2-P3)+(P4-P3)=-v+v=0.

Consequently (13) preserves L e=0, L^T e=omega, and Me=0.
This proves every flow and constant-kernel equation, including those at
the nodes touched by the motion.

Let t_move=T^T w_move. Its only nonzero coordinates are

    (t_move)_2=v/w-v,
    (t_move)_3=v-1-v/w,
    (t_move)_4=1.                                         (14)

For i=0,1, the sum of the later coordinates of w_move is zero,
so (t_move)_i=0. Equations (13)--(14) give the full matrix identity

    M(theta)=M^0+theta*J_move,
    J_move=sym(v_move*t_move^T).                           (15)

In particular both ENTIRE rows0 and1 of M are fixed. Also

    (J_move)_44=0, (J_move)_24=1/2, (J_move)_34=-1/2,
    p^T J_move p=(p^T v_move)*(w_move^T T p)=0,
    e4^T J_move p=(p2-p3)/2=:kappa_move.                    (16)

Thus the terminal diagonal and endpoint block, the quadratic energy,
the first-row/quadratic covariance, and the first-row lifted-cut budget
(8) are all fixed. The last claim also follows entry by entry: none of
Lambda20,Lambda30,Lambda40,Lambda12,Lambda13 changes. Every outgoing
terminal coefficient stays fixed, so the complete budget (9) stays fixed.
The second-row/quadratic covariance e1^T M p stays fixed too.

The four-edge motion is not a PSD-order repair: the principal2by2
submatrix of J_move on coordinates2,4 has determinant -1/4. Thus
J_move is indefinite for EVERY positive w,v. Neither sign of theta
can be declared PSD-preserving without the full test below.

If the sixteen unchanged coefficients are nonnegative, the twenty
original signs hold exactly when

    theta_sign_low<=theta<=theta_sign_high,
    theta_sign_low=max(-Lambda23^0/(1+v/w),
                       -w*Lambda32^0/v,-Lambda34^0),
    theta_sign_high=Lambda24^0.                            (17)

No strict positivity is assumed. If this interval is empty the entire
fiber is infeasible. If it is a singleton that is the only sign-allowed
array; an open perturbation must not be inferred on that boundary.

## 4. Full five-dimensional PSD is one covariance interval

Assume in addition p2!=p3, so kappa_move!=0. This holds throughout
the positive-excess regime because p2-p3=a*b*(1+c)>0.

The five columns e,e0,e1,e4,p form a basis of R^5. Indeed a linear
dependence has, at coordinates2 and3, equations alpha+beta*p2=0 and
alpha+beta*p3=0. Subtraction gives beta=0 and then alpha=0; the
remaining three standard-coordinate coefficients vanish. With Me=0,
full PSD on all R^5 is therefore equivalent to PSD of the following
4by4 matrix in the ordered columns e0,e1,e4,p:

    H(theta) = [ A_piv   r_vec      q_vec
                 r_vec^T n         z(theta)
                 q_vec^T z(theta) Qenergy ],               (18)

where

    A_piv=[[M00^0,M01^0],[M01^0,M11^0]],
    r_vec=(M04^0,M14^0)^T,
    q_vec=(e0^T M^0 p,e1^T M^0 p)^T,
    n=M44^0, z(theta)=z_base+kappa_move*theta,
    z_base=e4^T M^0 p.

All entries except z(theta) are fixed by (15)--(16). This is a basis
change on the original formal space, not a quotient that identifies
any gradients. In particular checking (18) tests the WHOLE M(theta),
not merely the principal block on e0,e4,p.

Here is a complete, boundary-safe way to calculate three scalars

    r_cost, q_cost, center_cov.

First require A_piv>=0. Also require r_vec and q_vec to lie in its
column space. When those conditions hold, define the costs by the
following disjoint cases. Write m=M00^0, k=M01^0, j=M11^0,
r_vec=(r0,r1)^T, q_vec=(q0,q1)^T.

* If det(A_piv)>0, use
  r_cost=r_vec^T A_piv^(-1)r_vec,
  q_cost=q_vec^T A_piv^(-1)q_vec, and
  center_cov=r_vec^T A_piv^(-1)q_vec. The inverse denominator is
  strictly positive in this case.
* If det(A_piv)=0 and m>0, impose
  r1=k*r0/m and q1=k*q0/m. Put
  r_cost=r0^2/m, q_cost=q0^2/m, center_cov=r0*q0/m.
* If m=0 and j>0, PSD of A_piv forces k=0. Impose r0=q0=0
  and put r_cost=r1^2/j, q_cost=q1^2/j, center_cov=r1*q1/j.
* If m=j=0, PSD forces k=0. Impose r_vec=q_vec=0 and set
  r_cost=q_cost=center_cov=0.

These cases exhaust PSD2by2 pivots. A failed column-space requirement
means no theta can work. Define the residual energies

    alpha_res=n-r_cost, beta_res=Qenergy-q_cost.            (19)

Full PSD holds if and only if all the pivot/column-space conditions hold,
alpha_res>=0, beta_res>=0, and

    center_cov-sqrt(alpha_res*beta_res)
       <= z_base+kappa_move*theta
       <= center_cov+sqrt(alpha_res*beta_res).              (20)

To prove necessity of the column-space conditions, a vector in the
kernel of A_piv has zero quadratic energy in (18), so its mixed terms
must vanish. For sufficiency and the remaining necessity, complete the
square in the pivot variables. In the nonsingular case this is ordinary
matrix completion of the square. In the rank1 cases only the displayed
positive scalar pivot is used; the other pivot direction has zero mixed
terms by the column-space requirements. In rank0 there is no pivot term.
The remaining quadratic form on the last two coordinates is exactly

    [[alpha_res,z(theta)-center_cov],
     [z(theta)-center_cov,beta_res]].

A real symmetric2by2 matrix is PSD exactly when both diagonal entries
are nonnegative and the squared off-diagonal is at most their product.
This proves (19)--(20), including alpha_res=0 or beta_res=0. In either
zero-energy case the covariance is forced to center_cov; there is no
division by a vanishing energy and no strict-complementarity assumption.

Let theta_PSD_low and theta_PSD_high be the smaller and larger of

    (center_cov-sqrt(alpha_res*beta_res)-z_base)/kappa_move,
    (center_cov+sqrt(alpha_res*beta_res)-z_base)/kappa_move.   (21)

The ENTIRE ORIGINAL full-certificate fiber (12) is feasible if and
only if the sixteen unchanged signs, the pivot conditions, and (19)
hold and

    max(theta_sign_low,theta_PSD_low)
       <= min(theta_sign_high,theta_PSD_high).             (22)

When they hold, either endpoint or any point of this closed intersection
gives an exact array with all20 signs, original flow, and fullR5 PSD.
When they fail, no array ON THIS FIBER can be a full certificate. This
does not exclude other fibers or the whole cone.

If p2=p3, the basis argument above fails: one must NOT substitute
kappa_move=0 into (21). The following independent basis gives a complete
replacement, including zero steps, rather than deleting those regimes.

### 4.1. An exact fallback retaining zero steps and dependent quadratic columns

This subsection allows ANY w=h2>=0 and v=h3>=0. Replace theta by
w*tau when w>0, and define the motion directly for every w,v by

    Delta Lambda23=(w+v)*tau, Delta Lambda24=-w*tau,
    Delta Lambda32=v*tau,    Delta Lambda34=w*tau.           (23a)

Its Laplacian is tau*(e2-e3)*[v*e2-(w+v)*e3+w*e4]^T.
The right factor annihilates e and P, since
v*(P2-P3)+w*(P4-P3)=-v*w+w*v=0. Therefore exact flow and Me=0
are preserved even at w=0 or v=0. No division by either step occurs.
The exact twenty signs are the sixteen unchanged signs together with

    Lambda23^0+(w+v)*tau>=0, Lambda24^0-w*tau>=0,
    Lambda32^0+v*tau>=0,     Lambda34^0+w*tau>=0.           (23b)

The columns e,e0,e1,e2,e3 ALWAYS form a basis of R5. Thus with Me=0,
full PSD is equivalent to the leading4by4 block in e0,e1,e2,e3.
Its first2by2 pivot is the same A_piv as above. Its two mixed columns

    U2=(M02^0,M12^0)^T, U3=(M03^0,M13^0)^T

are fixed by the motion. Require A_piv>=0 and U2,U3 in its column
space. Use the same rank0/rank1/rank2 cost formulas as above, now
with r_vec=U2 and q_vec=U3. If the costs are c22,c33,c23, set

    R_two=[[r,s23],[s23,t]],
    r=M22^0-c22, t=M33^0-c33, s23=M23^0-c23.

Completing the square in the pivot reduces full PSD exactly to

    R_two+tau*[[j_move,k_move],[k_move,l_move]]>=0,
    j_move=v*(1-w), k_move=-j_move-w/2, l_move=j_move+w.    (23c)

To check the formula, the last three entries of the right factor
after multiplication by T^T are (j_move,-w-j_move,w).
Symmetrizing with e2-e3 gives precisely (23c). The determinant of
its coefficient matrix is -w^2/4, including the zero value at w=0.

Write

    d_zero=r*t-s23^2,
    d_one=r*l_move+t*j_move-2*s23*k_move.

The COMPLETE remaining PSD conditions are

    r+j_move*tau>=0, t+l_move*tau>=0,
    d_zero+d_one*tau-w^2*tau^2/4>=0.                      (23d)

For w>0, if d_one^2+w^2*d_zero<0 the fiber is infeasible.
Otherwise the last condition is exactly the closed interval with endpoints

    2*(d_one-sqrt(d_one^2+w^2*d_zero))/w^2,
    2*(d_one+sqrt(d_one^2+w^2*d_zero))/w^2.                (23e)

For w=0, the last condition in (23d) is the LINEAR inequality
d_zero+d_one*tau>=0. Intersect it with the two displayed diagonal
conditions and (23b). Every linear inequality A*tau+B>=0 is processed
by sign: for A>0 it is a lower bound, for A<0 an upper bound, and
for A=0 it requires B>=0 without division. This also covers w=v=0,
when the motion is zero and the conditions simply test the unchanged
full array. All singular-pivot range conditions remain in force.

Therefore (23b)--(23e), the sixteen unchanged signs, and the pivot/range
conditions decide the entire original fiber for every nonnegative h.
They preserve every original formal gradient at zero steps. On the
nondegenerate domain they are equivalent to (17)--(22), because both
are exact congruence tests of the same full matrix. This extension adds
no positivity, reversal, saturation, or formal-coordinate-identification
assumption to the original problem.

## 5. This is an actual full-cone freedom, not just a formal covariance

We give a symbolic example of two distinct full certificates on the same
word for which all the preserved data in Section3 agree and the terminal
covariance differs. This tests the false shortcut that those data already
determine the terminal covariance. The example has small capacity; it is
NOT a threshold seed or a claim to survive high-capacity screening.

Set epsilon=1/10000 and h_i=epsilon for i<4. Thus P_i=i*epsilon.
Let mu=7*epsilon/2 and define the five positive weights

    wgt=(4/7,4/5,4/3,4,16), Wgt=sum_i wgt_i=2384/105<24,
    phi_i=1+i*epsilon,
    Lambda^c_ij=phi_i*wgt_i*wgt_j/Wgt for i!=j.              (23)

For clarity these wgt_i are weights, not the step w=h2 in Section3.
They satisfy

    wgt_i=2h_i/(mu-P_i), i<4,
    wgt_4=2s/(s-mu),
    sum_i wgt_i(P_i-mu)=0.

Consequently sum_i wgt_i P_i=mu Wgt and
sum_i phi_i wgt_i=(1+mu)Wgt. The outgoing minus incoming mass at i
in (23) is wgt_i(P_i-mu)=omega_i, with the prescribed sign.
Its row moment is phi_i*wgt_i*(mu-P_i), which equals the relevant
right side of (3), including -2sC for the last row. Hence the base
array has the full flow and M^c e=0. All20 signs are strictly positive.

It remains to prove full PSD, rather than infer it from those facts.
Let

    L_zero=diag(wgt)-wgt*wgt^T/Wgt,
    J_index=diag(0,1,2,3,4),
    N_low be the5by5 matrix with ones strictly below the diagonal
          and zeros elsewhere.

Then L^c=(I+epsilon*J_index)L_zero and T=I+epsilon*N_low.
Let D_one=diag(2,2,2,2,-8) and D_two=diag(-1,-1,-1,-1,-16).
The exact matrix expansion is

    M^c=L_zero
       +epsilon*(D_one+sym(J_index*L_zero+L_zero*N_low))
       +epsilon^2*(D_two+sym(J_index*L_zero*N_low)).        (24)

For any z perpendicular to e,

    z^T L_zero z
      =sum_(i<j)wgt_i*wgt_j*(z_i-z_j)^2/Wgt
      >=(16/(49*24))*5*||z||^2
      =(10/147)||z||^2>(1/15)||z||^2.                   (25)

Here min_i wgt_i=4/7 and sum_(i<j)(z_i-z_j)^2=5||z||^2.
Also 0<=L_zero<=diag(wgt), so its Euclidean operator norm is at
most16. The norms of J_index and N_low are at most4; for N_low,
the sum of squared entries is10, so even its Frobenius norm is below4.
The norms of D_one,D_two are8,16. Thus (24) gives

    ||M^c-L_zero||<=136*epsilon+272*epsilon^2<1/50.         (26)

Equations (25)--(26) prove that M^c is positive definite on e-perp
with lower bound7/150, and Me=0 supplies PSD on allR5.

In (12), v=w=epsilon, so the four coefficient changes are
2theta,-theta,theta,theta. Every base coefficient is at least
16/(49*24)=2/147. For either theta=epsilon or theta=-epsilon,
each changed coefficient remains positive because 2epsilon<2/147.
The sixteen other coefficients stay positive.

In (14) the nonzero t_move coordinates are
(1-epsilon,-2+epsilon,1). Its norm is below sqrt(6), so
||J_move||<=||v_move||*||t_move||<sqrt(12)<4.
For either sign of theta=epsilon, the perturbation norm is below
4epsilon<1/1000. The lower bound7/150 from (26) remains positive.
Both arrays therefore satisfy all20 signs, exact flow, and fullR5 PSD.

For this word p_i=(1-epsilon)^i and
p2-p3=epsilon*(1-epsilon)^2>0. The terminal covariances of the two
arrays differ by

    epsilon*(p2-p3)=epsilon^2*(1-epsilon)^2>0.             (27)

Every quantity listed as invariant in Section3 agrees exactly. This is
a full-cone counterexample to covariance determination by those data.
The first-row positive-excess hypotheses of (5) do not hold for this
small-step example, and no such claim is made. The algebraic invariance
(12)--(16), and the full-fiber decision (22), DO apply in the intended
positive-excess regime. If a threshold fiber is sign-saturated or has
a singular PSD interval, it can have only one allowed theta or none;
the small-step example does not imply an open interval there.

## 6. Connection to the complete full-support coordinates

This section identifies exactly how the fiber sits in the ORIGINAL full
cone. It does not reduce the original problem to the one chosen center.
For simplicity assume all h_i>0, as in the positive-excess target regime.
Choose P3<mu<s and set

    phi_i=1+P_i,
    wgt_i=2h_i/(mu-P_i), i<4; wgt_4=2s/(s-mu),
    Wgt=sum_i wgt_i,
    Lambda^c_ij=phi_i*wgt_i*wgt_j/Wgt, i!=j.               (28)

The same two weighted-sum calculations used for (23) prove exact flow,
Me=0 and strict positivity of all20 coefficients. PSD is a separate
requirement. With zero steps, choose mu between the last prefix preceding
a positive step and s, and give zero weights to zero-step indices;
the algebra still works, but strict positivity is no longer asserted.

Define the5by4 matrix E_diff with columns e_i-e4, i0 through3,
and the5by3 matrix F_null with columns

    e_j-(1-P_j/s)e0-(P_j/s)e4, j1 through3.

The columns of E_diff are a basis of e-perp. Those of F_null are
independent from their middle coordinates and are a basis of the vectors
annihilating both e and P under transpose. Every real flow/kernel
completion, without imposing signs yet, is uniquely

    L=L^c+E_diff*X*F_null^T, X any real4by3 matrix.          (29)

Indeed the difference must satisfy Delta e=0, Delta^T e=0 and Delta P=0;
the last identity follows from (M-M^c)e=Delta P/2. Expanding columns
and rows in the two displayed bases proves (29) in both directions.
The original signs are exactly

    (E_diff*X*F_null^T)_ij<=Lambda^c_ij, every i!=j.         (30)

Let B_pick have columns e0,e1,e2,e3, set R=F_null^T*T*B_pick,
and K_c=B_pick^T*M^c*B_pick. Then

    K=K_c+sym(XR),
    M=[[K,-K*1],[-1^T*K,1^T*K*1]].                        (31)

Thus K>=0 is equivalent to full M>=0, not a substitute for (30).
Let q_diff=(p0-p4,p1-p4,p2-p4,p3-p4)^T. The identity
T^(-1)P=e-p gives ker(F_null^T T)=span(e,p), and restriction to
columns with terminal coordinate0 gives rank(R)=3 and
ker(R)=span(q_diff). Here q_diff!=0 when s>0, since otherwise
p=e and the recurrence would force all h_i=0. Calibration (4) becomes

    q_diff^T K q_diff=Qenergy.                            (32)

For completeness, if a proposed symmetric K has (32), put Hdiff=K-K_c
and

    S_zero=[q_diff*(Hdiff*q_diff)^T
              -(Hdiff*q_diff)*q_diff^T]/(q_diff^T*q_diff).

Then S_zero*q_diff=-Hdiff*q_diff. All real completions of this K are

    X=(Hdiff+S_zero+Z)*R^T*(RR^T)^(-1),
    Z^T=-Z, Z*q_diff=0.                                  (33)

The inverse is valid because rank(R)=3. Multiplication by R verifies
(33), as R^T(RR^T)^(-1)R projects onto q_diff-perp. Conversely XR-Hdiff
is skew, annihilates q_diff after adding Hdiff, and must have the
displayed form. The remaining Z-space is the three-dimensional skew
space on q_diff-perp. Every one of the20 signs (30) is still required.
If Qenergy=0 AND K>=0 then K*q_diff=0; otherwise no second kernel
is imposed. This reproduces the relevant complete-coordinate proof,
rather than treating draft443f4b4325a9901d as an accepted premise.

The motion (13) is a NONZERO member of the12-dimensional space (29).
It therefore may be chosen as one direction in a basis of that space.
For each fixed choice of the other11 real coordinates, Sections3--4
decide its entire remaining theta fiber by (17)--(22), or by the complete
fallback (23a)--(23e), provided the unchanged signs and pivot conditions
are checked. This is an exact
elimination of one full-interface parameter. It is not a restriction
to X=0, proportional coefficients, rank1 K, or a fixed skew triple.

It also explains the remaining difficulty precisely. The entries of
A_piv,r_vec,q_vec,n and the sixteen unchanged signs depend on those
other11 coordinates and on h. Their feasible high-capacity joint range
is not determined by (5)--(9). Choosing the positive center does not
prove its pivot or residual energies nonnegative. Choosing a calibrated
PSD K does not prove (30). Choosing a nonempty sign interval does not
prove the PSD interval meets it. Each of these missing matches can fail
independently; none is supplied by the unproved general reversal theorem.

## 7. Direct-proof screens, exact scope and handoff

Three routes were screened in this round.

1. Terminal-cut energy plus the unit quadratic alone: substituting a
   quadratic prefix and constant formal terminal gradient simply recovers
   the already calibrated identity (4). No additional obstruction is
   claimed from that computation.
2. Infer the terminal covariance from the initial lifted cut and endpoint
   budgets: false as an algebraic determination claim. The actual
   four-edge family (12), and the two fully feasible arrays in Section5,
   give a precise counterexample. The missing term is exactly the incoming
   weighted terminal sum in (10).
3. Keep that covariance and impose full PSD jointly: complete on every
   fiber (12) with p2!=p3, with the full alternative (23a)--(23e) also
   covering dependent quadratic columns and zero steps. The exact
   range/pivot conditions and interval intersections retain all20 signs
   and all of R5. Zero and saturated residual energies are handled
   explicitly, without division by them.

Here is the full redundancy calculation for the first screen. Put
Apre=1+P3=C-v, d_last=v-1, and
w_const=(p0,p1,p2,p3,p3)^T. Give the first four samples their actual
unit-quadratic prefix jets. Append a FORMAL constant-gradient step with
g4=g3=p3 and f4=f3-v*p3^2. In (2), V_h then equals the prefix energy
Qpre=1-Apre^2*p3^2. All prefix Q vanish, outgoing terminal residuals
vanish, and Q_i4=v*(p3-p_i)*p3 for i<3. Hence

    Qpre=w_const^T M w_const
             -v*p3*sum_(i<3)Lambda_i4*(p3-p_i).             (34)

The direct original off-diagonal identity is

    Lambda_i4=(h_i-1)*y_i+h_i*sum_(j<i)y_j-2*M_i4.

For each j<3, telescoping h_i*p_i=p_i-p_(i+1) gives

    sum_(i=j)^2 h_i*(p3-p_i)-(p3-p_j)=(P3-P_j)*p3.

Also Me=0 gives sum_(i<3)M_i4*(p3-p_i)=-w_const^T M e4.
Thus the sum in (34) is

    p3*sum_(j<3)(P3-P_j)*y_j+2*w_const^T M e4.

Complete the square in (34) and use (9). Because
w_const-v*p3*e4=p, the result is exactly

    Qpre=Qenergy-s*v*delta_v*p3^2.                         (35)

This is already the polynomial identity
Apre^2-C^2*d_last^2=s*v*delta_v, since
Apre-C*d_last=delta_v and Apre+C*d_last=s*v. The formal extension
in this calculation is not asserted to be an actual function. It is
used only inside the exact full formal identity (2). Accordingly this
specific attempted extra test is redundant, rather than a new witness.

This resolves the covariance/sign/PSD interface along an original-array
direction and identifies the uncovered full-interface freedom. It does
not decide the remaining high-capacity step region, construct an actual
C>=193/25 seed, prove cone reversal, or prove full-cone nonexistence.
No excluded endpoint square/prism is re-scanned or used as a premise.
Capacity C is a variable throughout Sections1--4 and6; only the separate
counterexample of Section5 fixes a small-step word.

All derivations are textual and exact. No numerical/model evaluation,
solver, finite replay, machine algebra, installation, consult, subordinate
agent or fact_submit was used. The initial Matlas retrieval returned
unrelated noisy-GD/constrained-dynamics results; web fallback recovered
the already audited composition literature. A later targeted matrix
query found the generalized Schur-complement statement in Zhaosong Lu
and Ting Kei Pong, "Computing Optimal Experimental Designs via Interior

the Moore-Penrose inverse C^dagger and the column-space requirement:
for symmetric A,C, the block [[A,B^T],[B,C]] is PSD exactly when
C>=0, Range(B) is contained in Range(C), and A-B^T C^dagger B>=0.
This is background matching, not an imported premise: Section4 proves
the required rank0/rank1/rank2 version directly. The exact PDF was
downloaded; the local pdftotext executable was absent. The arXiv HTML
was then saved and extracted with the standard-library HTML parser,

The paper states this lemma with a book reference, without a proof of
