## Part I. Complete input construction, rederived jointly

The section numbers1--19 and their references in this part are local to
Part I. They establish the current31 input, including all values, original
rows, global interpolation and true radius. Their next-parent discussion
concerns the rich31 input; the heterogeneous actual63 follows in Part II.
No assertion in this part is treated as a verified predecessor.

## 1. Input fifteen-step construction and its full affine model

For every sigma in [9999/10000,1], the changed seven-step geometry
defined below has a legal fifteen-step parent on its specified next
word. The parent uses an explicit rank-one cross coupling and changes
only two values in its left copy:

    f_2 -> f_2-d_atom,
    f_6 -> f_6-alpha^2 d_atom,
    d_atom=(1-rho)(K-1)eta>0.                         (1)

Every position and gradient of both children is retained. All other
values are retained with their appropriate spatial-square scaling.
One explicit static, globally defined, convex 1-smooth function realizes
all sixteen samples. All 272 distinct original ordered interpolation
pairs, including the optimum, hold. The exact minimizer set is a convex
hull of three specified residuals; the true initial distance is R.

The physical word is

    h_3=(a,b,a),
    h_7=(h_3,1+r_0,h_3),
    h_15=(h_7,1+r_1,h_7).                            (2)

Its true-distance normalized payoff V_15 and capacity state satisfy

    W_15(h_15) >= V_15 = beta^2 alpha^2 N/R^2,
    kappa_15=(lambda^2 A)^2 V_15 > 1+1/1000.         (3)

This is a finite capacity surplus, not a comparison replacing the
original denominator B_15 by capacity squared. The exact original
benchmark ratio of this witness is B_15 V_15. It supplies neither an
arbitrary-h result nor an all-depth construction.

For clarity, the FULL released affine parent model has arbitrary
similarities E,F of the fixed child space with E^T E=ell I and
F^T F=nu I, ell,nu>=0, arbitrary cross Gram, and physical relative
translation t_join=E d-F P. Its left samples are (E X_i,E G_i), its
right queried samples are (t_join+F X_j,F G_j), and its final point is
t_join+F X_7 with a free terminal gradient. Every value and one common
minimizer are free; the full Gram, including optimum and terminal
vectors, is PSD. All original rows are imposed. The normalization uses
distance to an actual common minimizer, and a claimed witness must price
its nearest-minimizer distance.

We construct a point of this full model by choosing ell=1, nu=beta^2,
t_join=0 and an explicit F. This is a SUFFICIENT CONSTRUCTION, not a
restriction asserted lossless for the full model. The model's free
terminal gradient is legally selected as F G_7. Its incoming rows are
checked too. Independent scales, translations, values, and PSD range
conditions are not discarded in an impossibility claim.

## 2. Exact atom and its original rows

Use Euclidean inner products throughout. Define

    s=sqrt(2), lambda=1+s, theta=s-1,
    a=(311s-16)/300, b=(590+8s)/300, rho=599/600,
    z=b-1, K=a+rho, m=a+b, eta=z/K,
    A=1+2a+b=(143+105s)/50,
    r_0=theta A=(67+38s)/50, r_1=A,
    Dlen=m+K=A-1/600.

Take orthogonal U,V in R^2, with ||U||=1 and ||V||^2=eta.
Put w=rho V and p=m U+K V. The atom is

    g=(U,U,V,w),
    x=(p,bU+KV,KV,w),
    f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2, 0<=i<=3.

It obeys the three updates (a,b,a). Its residuals y_i=x_i-g_i
and energies E_i=<g_i,y_i> are

    y_0=(m-1)U+KV, E_0=m-1,
    y_1=zU+KV,     E_1=z,
    y_2=(K-1)V,    E_2=e=(K-1)eta,
    y_3=0,         E_3=0.

For any jet define aheight_i=f_i-<g_i,x_i>+||g_i||^2/2 and
Delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2. The original convention is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =aheight_i-Delta_j+<g_i,y_j>.                (4)

For the atom aheight_i=0 and Delta_i=E_i. Its complete table of
<v-g_j,y_j>, for receiver j and possible source gradient v, is

| j | v=0 | v=U | v=V | v=w |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | -(m-1) | 0 | -a | -a-(1-rho)z |
| 1 | -z | 0 | 0 | -(1-rho)z |
| 2 | -e | -e | 0 | -(1-rho)e |
| 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

All entries are nonpositive. The duplicate U occurs at both actual
indices 0 and 1. This checks every atom pair and every optimum pair.
Write

    R^2=||p||^2=m^2+Kz,
    N=||w||^2=rho^2 eta,
    D=<p,w>=rho z,
    d_atom=(1-rho)e=e/600.                          (5)

The symbol R here is a coordinate radius, distinct from the project's
objective convention W=2R.

## 3. The internally translated seven-step geometry

Fix sigma in [9999/10000,1]. Put

    delta=1-sigma, chi=delta/sigma,
    alpha=sigma r_0 sqrt(N)/R, k=alpha^2.

Let e_axis=w/sqrt(N), p_axis=p/R. In the Euclidean direct sum
the real line direct-sum e_axis^perp direct-sum p_axis^perp define isometries

    L u=(<u,e_axis>,u-<u,e_axis>e_axis,0),
    T v=(-<v,p_axis>,0,v-<v,p_axis>p_axis).

Thus

    <L u,alpha T v>
        =-sigma r_0 <u,w><p,v>/R^2.                 (6)

Define the INTERNAL translation t=-delta r_0 Lw. In particular
t=chi alpha T p. The seven-step jets are

    X_i=Lx_i, G_i=Lg_i, F_i=f_i,                  0<=i<=3,
    X_(4+i)=t+alpha T x_i,
    G_(4+i)=alpha T g_i, F_(4+i)=k f_i,           0<=i<=3.

The bridge lands at -r_0 Lw=t+alpha T p. Hence this is an actual
trajectory on h_7. Write P=X_0=Lp and w_1=G_7=alpha T w.
Its endpoint is X_7=w_1+t, not w_1.

Let Y_i=X_i-G_i and use aheight_i,Delta_i for these seven-step jets.
For 0<=j<=3 one has

    Y_j=Ly_j, aheight_j=0, Delta_j=E_j,
    Y_(4+j)=alpha T(chi p+y_j),
    aheight_(4+j)=-chi k <p,g_j>,
    Delta_(4+j)=k E_j.                             (7)

All original child pairs hold. Within each atom this follows from the
table and spatial scaling; translation cancels within the right atom.
For a left source i and right receiver 4+j, (4) gives

    Q_(i,4+j)=-kE_j+<Lg_i,t+alpha T y_j> <=0.

For a right source 4+i and left receiver j it gives

    Q_(4+i,j)=-<alpha T g_i,t>-E_j
                                  +<alpha T g_i,Ly_j> <=0.

Every atom gradient and residual has nonnegative U,V coordinates.
Thus (6) makes the mixed terms nonpositive, while
<Lg_i,t><=0 and <alpha T g_i,t>=chi k<p,g_i>>=0.
Finally aheight<=0 and Delta>=0 check all optimum rows.

## 4. The two allowed value changes inside the left child

Set c_2=d_atom, c_6=k d_atom, and c_i=0 at every other child index.
The modified left child has values F_i-c_i, unchanged X_i,G_i,

    aheight_i^L=aheight_i-c_i,
    Delta_i^L=Delta_i-c_i.                          (8)

Every child interpolation row remains nonpositive. The only rows that
can increase are those into receiver 2 or 6. For receiver 2, its own
atom's other sources have slacks e,e,d_atom. Every source from the
other atom has slack at least e, by the second displayed cross formula
in section 3. Thus adding c_2=d_atom is legal; decreasing the source's
value can only help. For receiver 6, its own atom's other sources have
slacks k e,k e,k d_atom, and every source from the other atom has slack
at least k e, by the first displayed cross formula. Adding c_6 is legal.
These statements also cover the row between the two changed samples.

The optimum rows remain legal: aheight_i^L<=0, and the changed positive
energies are Delta_2^L=rho e and Delta_6^L=k rho e. No endpoint value
changes. In particular both endpoint energies Delta_3,Delta_7 stay zero.

These are changes to one final list of jets. We do not change a function
online while an algorithm runs; section 9 builds a single function from
the entire list before the actual run.

## 5. Top bridge and explicit full Gram realization

The actual outgoing vector at the next bridge is

    d=t-r_1 w_1=alpha T(chi p-r_1 w).

Use the auxiliary scalars

    omega=r_1 rho-chi K,
    Mout=r_1 D-chi R^2,
    Hout=||chi p-r_1 w||^2
        =r_1^2 N-2chi r_1 D+chi^2 R^2,
    beta=||d||/R, nscale=beta^2=k Hout/R^2.         (9)

All are positive except chi, which may be zero. In particular d!=0.
In the real line direct-sum d^perp direct-sum P^perp define

    E_top u=(<u,d/||d||>,u-<u,d/||d||>d/||d||,0),
    T_top v=(<v,P/R>,0,v-<v,P/R>P/R),
    B_top=beta T_top.

These maps give a realization in dimension five and satisfy

    B_top P=E_top d,
    <E_top u,B_top v>=<u,d><P,v>/R^2.               (10)

The actual parent samples are

    Z_i=E_top X_i, J_i=E_top G_i, fhat_i=F_i-c_i,    0<=i<=7,
    Z_(8+j)=B_top X_j, J_(8+j)=B_top G_j,
    fhat_(8+j)=nscale F_j,                           0<=j<=7.

The bridge equality in (10) verifies the step 1+r_1. All other steps
follow from the child recursions. The complete Gram of these vectors
and optimum zero is PSD by this explicit Euclidean factorization; all
range conditions are present. The final gradient J_15 is an allowed
choice for the full model's free unqueried gradient.

## 6. Rational scalar estimates used in the full pair check

The following deliberately loose rational bounds follow from
14142/10000<sqrt(2)<14143/10000, proved by squaring, and the defining
formulas:

    341/100<m<171/50, 241/100<K<121/50,
    1<z<201/200, 29/5<Dlen<59/10,
    29/5<r_1<6, 12/5<r_0<49/20,
    14<R^2<71/5, 2/5<N<21/50, 0<D<11/10,
    e>1/2, rho>99/100, 0<=chi<=1/9999.             (11)

For example R^2> (341/100)^2+241/100>14 and
R^2<(171/50)^2+(121/50)(201/200)<71/5.
Since rho^2>99/100, N>99/242>2/5; also
N<eta<(201/200)/(241/100)<21/50.
The bound e>1/2 follows from (K-1)eta>(141/100)(50/121)>1/2.

Consequently omega>0, Mout>0, and

    Hout>67/5, 1/8<nscale<1/5.                     (12)

Indeed Hout>(29/5)^2(2/5)-2(1/9999)6(11/10)>67/5.
Using sigma^2>999/1000, the lower estimate for nscale is greater than

    (999/1000)(12/5)^2(2/5)(67/5)/(71/5)^2 >1/8.

For the upper estimate discard the negative term in Hout and use
chi^2 R^2<1/1000000. The upper bound becomes

    (49/20)^2(21/50)[36(21/50)+1/1000000]/14^2 <1/5.

Define the auxiliary quantities

    Caff=K Dlen/(r_0 r_1 rho^2),
    Tfirst=Mout Dlen/(sigma r_0 rho Hout),
    Lcoef=omega eta sigma r_0 D/R^2,
    Tsecond=Lcoef Dlen/(R^2 nscale).

The crucial strict endpoint bound is

    rho Caff<1.                                    (13)

It has the exact algebraic certificate

    r_0 r_1 rho-K Dlen
       =(-381891+284836 sqrt(2))/9000000>0,

where already sqrt(2)>7/5 proves positivity. In particular
Caff<600/599 and Caff-1<1/599.

We also have

    Tfirst<=Caff,
    Tsecond-Tfirst < (11/5)chi   if chi>0,
    Lcoef/z<1/2,
    Tsecond+chi(Lcoef-z)/(nscale z)<=Caff.           (14)

At chi=0 the second difference is zero and the other non-strict
relations continue to hold. Here are derivations. The inequality
Tfirst<=Caff is equivalent to

    (1+chi)(r_1 D-chi R^2)r_1 N <= D Hout.

After cancelling the constant terms, the difference of the left side
and right side is

    chi r_1 [r_1 DN-R^2 N+2D^2]
                 -chi^2 R^2(r_1 N+D) <=0.

The bracket is negative because R^2 N>28/5, whereas
r_1 DN+2D^2<6(11/10)(21/50)+2(11/10)^2<28/5.
Next z omega=Mout+chi m^2, so

    Tsecond-Tfirst=chi m^2 Dlen/(sigma r_0 rho Hout).

The coefficient is less than 11/5 by (11)-(12): its numerator is
less than (171/50)^2(59/10), and its denominator exceeds
(999/1000)(12/5)(99/100)(67/5); comparison of these two rational
products gives the asserted bound. Also

    Lcoef/z <= r_0 r_1 N/R^2
             < (49/20)6(21/50)/14 <1/2.

Thus chi(1-Lcoef/z)/nscale >=(5/2)chi, with strict inequality when
chi>0. Subtracting this from the second bound gives the last part of
(14). These estimates keep the internal residual cost; it is precisely
the term chi(Lcoef-z) that must not be dropped at the critical row.

For later use, Tfirst,Tsecond<6/5. This follows from Caff<600/599,
the second difference bound, and chi<=1/9999. Moreover

    nscale z(Caff-1)<d_atom/2.                      (15)

If Caff<=1 it is immediate. Otherwise the left side is less than
(1/5)(201/200)/599=201/599000, while d_atom/2>1/2400;
the comparison is 482400<599000.

Put b_j=<p,y_j> and l_j=<w,y_j> for the atom. Their table is

| j | E_j | b_j | l_j |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | m-1 | R^2-m | D |
| 1 | z | z Dlen | D |
| 2 | e | (K-1)z | rho e |
| 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

For j=0,1,2 one has b_j<R^2 and l_j/E_j<=rho. Also
b_1/E_1=Dlen, while b_j/E_j<(4/5)Dlen for j=0,2.
For j=0, the numerator is less than 54/5 and
(4/5)Dlen(m-1)>(4/5)(29/5)(12/5)>54/5.
For j=2, b_2/E_2=K<(4/5)Dlen follows from (11).

Finally the two bounds needed in the reverse orientation are

    sigma r_0 r_1 D m rho/R^4 <1/3,
    (sigma r_0 D/R^4) Mout <1/10<nscale.             (16)

For the first, bound its numerator by (49/20)6(11/10)(171/50)
and its denominator below by 196. For the second, use
Mout<=r_1D and bound the numerator by (49/20)6(11/10)^2.
Both resulting rational inequalities are strict.

## 7. Every forward cross row

Abbreviate the following four exact child correlations:

    u_i=<G_i,d>, v_i=<P,G_i>,
    p_i=<P,Y_i>, q_i=<d,Y_i>.

From (6)-(9) their entries are

    u_0=u_1=0,
    u_2=sigma r_0 rho eta Mout/R^2, u_3=rho u_2,
    u_4=u_5=k chi m, u_6=-k omega eta, u_7=rho u_6;

    v_0=v_1=m, v_2=z, v_3=D,
    v_(4+j)=-(sigma r_0 D/R^2)<p,g_j>;

    p_j=b_j,
    p_(4+j)=-sigma r_0 D(chi+b_j/R^2);

    q_j=sigma r_0 Mout l_j/R^2,
    q_(4+j)=k[-chi Mout+chi b_j-r_1 l_j],           0<=j<=3.
                                                               (17)

In particular p_0,p_1,p_2>0, p_3=0, p_4,p_5,p_6<0,
and p_7<=0. All q_0,q_1,q_2>0, q_3=0, q_4,q_5,q_6<0,
and q_7=-k chi Mout<=0. To see the strict late signs, use
chi b_j<=chi R^2<1/600, while r_1 l_j>1 for j=0,1,2.

Equation (4) and the cross identity (10) give every forward cross row:

    Q_(i,8+j)=aheight_i-c_i-nscale Delta_j+u_i p_j/R^2.
                                                               (18)

All aheight_i-c_i are nonpositive. Therefore only positive products
u_i p_j need further consideration; zero products cause no problem.

First let the receiver be j=0,1,2. Positive products can have source
i=2,3,4,5. For i=4,5, aheight_i=-chi k m and u_i=chi k m,
so their sum with the mixed term is chi k m(b_j/R^2-1)<=0.
For i=2 the ratio of u_2 b_j/R^2 to nscale E_j is

    Tfirst * b_j/(Dlen E_j).

At j=0,2 it is less than (6/5)(4/5)<1. At j=1, (14)-(15)
give Q_(2,9)<=nscale z(Caff-1)-d_atom<-d_atom/2.
For i=3 the same ratio is multiplied by rho, and (13)-(14)
make it strictly smaller than one, including at j=1.

Now let the receiver be 4+j, for atomic j=0,1,2,3. A positive product
can only have source i=6 or 7. Formula (18) becomes exactly

    Q_(6,12+j)/k
       =chi(Lcoef-z)+Lcoef b_j/R^2-nscale E_j-d_atom,
    Q_(7,12+j)/k
       =rho[chi(Lcoef-z)+Lcoef b_j/R^2]-nscale E_j.
                                                               (19)

For j=3, E_j=b_j=0 and Lcoef<z, so both are nonpositive.
For j=0,2 drop the nonpositive chi term and use
Tsecond b_j/(Dlen E_j)<(6/5)(4/5)<1.
For j=1 use the last inequality of (14). It gives

    Q_(6,13)/k <=nscale z(Caff-1)-d_atom<-d_atom/2,
    Q_(7,13)/k <=nscale z(rho Caff-1)<0.

Receivers with p_j=0 and products of opposite signs were already
covered by (18). This exhausts all 64 forward cross rows, including
every row into the actual final sample 15.

## 8. Every reverse cross row and the total original system

The other orientation is

    Q_(8+i,j)=nscale aheight_i-Delta_j+c_j+v_i q_j/R^2.
                                                               (20)

For early receivers j=0,1,2, a positive product requires i=0,1,2,3.
Their v_i are at most m. The positive term divided by E_j is at most

    m sigma r_0 Mout rho/R^4
       <=m sigma r_0 r_1 D rho/R^4<1/3.

But Delta_j-c_j>=rho E_j, so (20) is nonpositive. Other source signs
only help. Receiver j=3 has q_j=Delta_j=c_j=0, leaving
nscale aheight_i<=0.

For a late receiver 4+j, a positive product requires a late source
4+i. Set Patom_i=<p,g_i>, which is one of m,m,z,D and is positive.
Using (7) and (17), combine the source height and mixed term exactly:

    nscale aheight_(4+i)+v_(4+i)q_(4+j)/R^2
      = k Patom_i {chi[-nscale+(sigma r_0 D/R^4)Mout]
               +(sigma r_0 D/R^4)[-chi b_j+r_1 l_j]}.
                                                               (21)

For j=3 the last bracket is zero; (16) makes (21) nonpositive.
For j=0,1,2 discard its nonpositive chi terms. The remaining term,
divided by k E_j, is at most

    m sigma r_0 r_1 D rho/R^4<1/3.

The receiver has Delta_(4+j)-c_(4+j)>=k rho E_j. Thus (20) is
nonpositive. Early sources have v_i>0 and q_(4+j)<=0, so they are
already safe. This checks all 64 reverse cross rows, including rows
whose source is the final gradient.

Sections 3-4 check all 56 ordered within-left rows; section 3 and
scaling check all 56 within-right rows. Sections 7-8 check all 128
cross rows. The 32 optimum incidences hold because every aheight is
nonpositive and every Delta is nonnegative, including after (1).
Thus all 272 distinct ordered rows on {star,0,...,15} are proved.
No sampled gradient, remote pair, or original position has been removed.

## 9. One global function and the TRUE radius

Let yhat_i=Z_i-J_i and Deltahat_i=fhat_i-||J_i||^2/2. On the same R^5
define

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max(0,max_(0<=i<=15)(<yhat_i,v>-Deltahat_i)),
    F_parent(Z)=sup_v(<Z,v>-H(v)).                  (22)

All rows just proved, together with accepted fact `1252b8823bb5a290`,
show that this is one finite, everywhere differentiable, convex,
1-smooth function satisfying F_parent(Z_i)=fhat_i, grad F_parent(Z_i)=J_i,
and F_parent(0)=0=min F_parent. Its trajectory from Z_0 is exactly (2).

Only samples 3,7,11,15 have Deltahat_i=0; their residuals are
0,E_top t,0,B_top t. All other Deltahat_i are strictly positive.
It follows directly that

    argmin F_parent=conv{0,E_top t,B_top t}.         (23)

For completeness, at sufficiently small epsilon>0 in any fixed
direction v,

    H(epsilon v)=epsilon^2||v||^2/2
       +epsilon max(0,<E_top t,v>,<B_top t,v>).

Every point of the displayed convex hull has conjugate value zero.
If Z is outside it, let z be its closest point and v=Z-z. The elementary
projection inequality gives <Z,v> greater than the maximum of the
three support values. The displayed local expression then gives
F_parent(Z)>0. This proves both inclusions in (23).

The exact nearest-minimizer distance is R. Indeed

    <P,t>=-delta r_0 D<=0,
    <P,d>=sigma r_0 D Mout/R^2>0,
    <E_top P,B_top t>=<P,d><P,t>/R^2<=0.

Hence <Z_0,z><=0 for every minimizer z in (23), and
||Z_0-z||^2=R^2+||z||^2-2<Z_0,z>>=R^2.
Zero attains equality. At sigma<1 the internal residuals are nonzero;
they have not been identified with zero or hidden in a surrogate radius.

The endpoint value is fhat_15=nscale k N/2. Thus (3)'s exact payoff is
2F_parent(Z_15)/dist(Z_0,argmin F_parent)^2=nscale k N/R^2.
Rescaling F_parent(RZ)/R^2 makes the true initial distance one without
changing this normalized payoff or any step. Multiplying the function
by a desired L_smooth>0 gives the same normalized payoff with steps
h_i/L_smooth. This is the original doubled-gap W=2R convention.

## 10. Paid state, retained value costs, and the next question

The atom's state is kappa_3=A^2 N/R^2. Its exact defining expressions are

    m=(574+319s)/300, K=(567+622s)/600,
    z=(145+4s)/150,
    R^2=(620189+458670s)/90000,
    N=358801(145+4s)/[90000(567+622s)].

Multiplication using s^2=2 gives

    kappa_3-1=(-8324118905+8781249146s)
                     /(2305581607500+1614558620000s)>1/2000.

The denominator is positive. Two thousand times its numerator minus
its denominator equals 15947939672000s-18953819417500; using s>7/5
gives the positive lower bound 3373296123300.

The actual capacities are A_1=lambda A and A_2=lambda^2 A. The seven-
step endpoint and the new fifteen-step endpoint satisfy

    N_1=kN, kappa_7=A_1^2 N_1/R^2=sigma^2 kappa_3^2,
    N_2=nscale N_1, kappa_15=A_2^2 N_2/R^2
                   =[Hout/(r_1^2 N)] kappa_7^2.     (24)

Since sigma kappa_3>(9999/10000)(2001/2000)>1+1/3000,
kappa_7>1+1/1500. Put tau=<w_1,t>/N_1=chi D/N and

# C95: weak-background static Huber ridge dynamics

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED DRAFT. Formal verifier allowance is zero.
This work belongs to completed round 26 (baseline 25, ceiling 27).
Accepted mathematical sources: b98bb807d514e80d (single cuts),
1fca3e5dd555cb4a (alternating rays), e9a55f57461f253c (finite original H6).
C93/C94 are motivation only. Every new assertion used here is derived below.

## Static model and exact legality

For positive radii r_- and r_+, let phi(0)=0 and
phi'(s)=max(-r_-,min(s,r_+)). Thus phi=s^2/2 on the core,
phi=r_+ s-r_+^2/2 to the right, and phi=-r_- s-r_-^2/2 to the left.
Let A be a symmetric PSD matrix, u_j unit vectors, and alpha_j>0.
Define one static function

    F(x)=x^T A x/2 + sum_j alpha_j phi_j(u_j^T x),
    C=A+sum_j alpha_j u_j u_j^T,   0<=C<=I.

Every scalar clip is monotone and 1-Lipschitz. For any x,y its difference
is theta_j u_j^T(x-y), with 0<=theta_j<=1. Therefore

    grad F(x)-grad F(y)=(A+sum_j alpha_j theta_j u_j u_j^T)(x-y).

The matrix in parentheses lies between zero and I, so its norm is at
most one. This proves global 1-smoothness; convexity also follows termwise
from monotonicity of each scalar derivative and A>=0. No local Hessian
rescaling of the physical steps is permitted or needed.

Every summand is nonnegative, and phi_j(s)=0 iff s=0. Consequently

    argmin F=ker A intersect intersection_j u_j^perp=ker C,
    min F=0.

The initial distance is the norm of the orthogonal projection onto
(ker C)^perp. When C is positive definite this is exactly ||x_0||;
the one-dimensional calibration also has its unique minimizer at zero.
All matrices below have explicit rational certificates, with no eigenvalue
clipping. A small eigenvalue is not silently removed from the distance.

Useful exact planar directions are

    u_+=(4/5,3/5), u_-=(4/5,-3/5), v=(0,1).

Weights alpha_+=alpha_-=25/32 give total matrix diag(1,9/16).
Adding weight 7/16 on v gives I. With A=mu I and multiplying every
ridge weight by 1-mu, 0<=mu<1, these become respectively
diag(1,mu+(1-mu)9/16) and I. The background floor can be zero or
arbitrarily weak. A fixed gate change changes one rank-one matrix and
can therefore change the principal axes; no independent switching matrix
is supplied to gradient descent.

## Original finite words and references

For m in {6,7,8}, set c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+1/m), beta=1-1/m,
a=beta/c, and H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.
All subwords retain the enclosing-m values c,beta,a. Let h=H_m,
n=2^m-1, S=sum h. Physical GD is x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i grad F(x_i).
The normalized actual objective is V=2F(x_n)/dist(x_0,argmin F)^2.
These finite horizons do not test any m>=128 theorem.

Accepted b98bb807d514e80d gives

    K=max(1/(1+2S), max_j (h_j-1)^2/((1+P_j)^2*(1+2T_j))),

where P_j,T_j are the preceding and following step masses.
At m=6 the stronger accepted e9a55f57461f253c gives
W_63(H_6)>56/2711>1/50. It uses its own actual high-dimensional function;
its 4160 checks are not replayed, and this reference is not transplanted
to m=7 or m=8. Saved original benchmark CSV entries may be read but no
benchmark dynamic program is rerun.

Here is a direct sufficient test for the complete accepted ray family to
equal K. For i<j put P=sum_(t<i)h_t and D=sum_(i<t<j)h_t. If

    (h_i-1)(h_j-1)<(1+P)(1+D)                 (R)

for every i<j, no feasible accepted ray selection has two checkpoints.
Indeed its first two checkpoint gradients are
m_0=1/(1+P), m_1=(h_i-1)m_0/(1+D), with old offset P*m_0.
The second-return budget is (h_j-1)m_1-P*m_0<m_0 by (R).
With exactly two checkpoints the old-gradient requirement is at least
m_0, and with more checkpoints the third magnitude would be below m_0.
Both contradict the explicit feasibility conditions of 1fca3e5dd555cb4a.
Zero and one checkpoint produce exactly K. Any numerical check of (R)
will be labeled numerical until an exact symbolic bound is supplied.

## Calibration and accounting

The initial calibration is the accepted one-dimensional central single cut.
If j=2^(m-1)-1, P=T=sum H_(m-1), b=h_j, choose
r_+=1/(1+P), r_-=(b-1)/((1+P)(1+2T)), A=0, alpha=1, x_0=1.
Its exact payoff is (b-1)^2/((1+P)^2(1+2T)). Its gradient is r_+ until
the central cut and -r_- afterward, with a possible boundary label at
the cut itself. This is one charged calibration, not a free preliminary run.

All forward work is standard-library Python, through the main-owned
bounded_ridge_forward_meter.py and run_ridge_with_remaining_budget.py.
The model source is research/weak_background_forward.py. The allocation is
36 total cases, at most 32 discovery, four total calibration/reconstruction
reserves, 30 measured/accounted seconds across both rounds and all scripts.
No case is run while authoring this draft. Source and request snapshots,
hashes, raw iterates/gradients/values, true distance, static parameters,
gate labels at queried and terminal points, and failures will be shared.

No numerical observation is a verified fact, a minimax disproof, or an
asymptotic conclusion. The original project target remains open.

## Exact finite-word ray comparison, with no exponential enumeration

Write r_j=a*c^j and M_j=1+sum H_j. Then

    M_0=1, M_(j+1)=2*M_j+r_j,
    t_j=r_j/M_j, t_0=a, t_(j+1)=c*t_j/(2+t_j).

For m>=6, c>1+sqrt(2) and beta<1 imply a<c-2. Hence t_j increases
and stays below c-2. Also

    beta-(c-2) = 3-(1+sqrt(2))-(2+sqrt(2))/m
       >= (10-7*sqrt(2))/6 >0,

so t_j>=a>(c-2)/c.

For any two chronological indices i<j with levels u,v, define the ratio
R_ij in (R) with the right side as its denominator. If u>=v, the prefix
before i contains H_u and the gap before j contains H_v; thus
R_ij<=t_u*t_v. The largest level m-1 occurs only once, so at least one
of u,v is at most m-2. It follows that

    R_ij<=t_(m-1)*t_(m-2)<c*t_(m-2)^2.

If u<v, both the prefix before i and the gap from i to j contain H_u.
Their total mass is at least sum H_v-(1+r_u), since the prefix before
j contains H_v. Consequently, putting x=1+P and y=1+D,
x,y>=M_u and x+y>=M_v-r_u. From
(x-M_u)(y-M_u)>=0 we obtain

    x*y>=M_u*(M_v-M_u-r_u).

Let d=v-u>=1 and t=t_u. Directly iterating the recurrence for M gives

    (M_v-M_u-r_u)/M_u
      =2^d-1+t*((c^d-2^d)/(c-2)-1)
      >=c^(d-1)+(c-1)*(2^d-2)/c>=c^(d-1).

The first inequality uses t>=(c-2)/c and the nonnegative coefficient
((c^d-2^d)/(c-2)-1). Therefore R_ij<=c*t_u^2<=c*t_(m-2)^2.
Equality in the complete maximum occurs at the first level-(m-2) bridge
and the immediately following level-(m-1) bridge: both intervening
prefix/gap masses are sum H_(m-2). Thus

    max_(i<j) R_ij = c*t_(m-2)^2.                         (C95.1)

This proves the full pair test symbolically; it does not rely on sampled
pair scans. Here are short rational upper certificates for the three
authorized horizons. Monotonicity of c*t/(2+t) in both positive variables
allows use of the displayed upper parameters throughout.

* m=6: c<17/6 and a<3/10. Four recurrence steps give
  t_4<83521/144462<7/12. Thus c*t_4^2<833/864<1.
  The intermediate bounds are 17/46,289/654,4913/9582,83521/144462.
* m=7: c<83/30 and a<5/16. Bounds for t_1,...,t_5 are respectively
  3/8,7/16,1/2,83/150,3/5. For the last step,
  6889/11490<3/5; hence c*t_5^2<747/750<1.
* m=8: c<68/25 and a<13/40. The upper recurrence has reciprocal at
  its sixth step equal to
  25/18+(395/234)*(25/34)^6. This is greater than 33/20 because
  (25/34)^3>79/200 and (79/200)^2>611/3950. Therefore t_6<20/33,
  and c*t_6^2<27200/27225<1.

All parameter enclosures follow by squaring positive rational bounds for
sqrt(2). In particular sqrt(2)<10/7, sqrt(2)>29/21 prove the m=6
bounds; sqrt(2)<341/240 and sqrt(2)>7/5 prove m=7;
sqrt(2)<319/225 and sqrt(2)>163/117 prove m=8.
Combining (C95.1) with the accepted ray feasibility conditions proves

    F_ray_(2^m-1)(H_m)=K_(2^m-1)(H_m), m=6,7,8.           (C95.2)

No m>=128 result is used here. This is a new UNVERIFIED finite symbolic
comparison derived jointly, not an accepted graph fact.

For completeness the largest single-cut term is the central cut. For a
fixed level u put p=1+P, q=1+T; both are at least M_u and
p+q=M_m-r_u. The denominator p^2*(2q-1) has no interior minimum on
that interval: its derivative is 2p*(2*(M_m-r_u)-3p-1), with at most
one interior critical point, a maximum. The two endpoint denominators
are ordered by monotonicity of z^2/(2z-1) for z>=1, so the earliest
occurrence of level u is best. Its value is

    t_u^2/[2*M_m-2*M_u-2*r_u-1].

The numerator increases and the positive denominator decreases with u.
Thus the central level m-1 maximizes it. In particular K is exactly
the larger of the global Huber term and the central single-cut term;
no choice of untested checkpoints is hidden in the numerical reference.

## Exact capture criterion for a saturated core curvature budget

Assume C=A+sum_j alpha_j u_j*u_j^T=I, and let D be the closed convex
intersection of all core strips -r_(j,-)<=u_j^T x<=r_(j,+).
At every point in D, grad F(x)=x and 2F(x)=||x||^2.

Fix any k>=1 with k<=m, retaining the same enclosing-m parameters. A
run of H_k starting at z stays in D at every query AND at the terminal
point if and only if both z and -a*z lie in D. In that event its exact
iterate after t steps is

    x_t=(-1)^t*beta^t*c^(-s_2(t))*z, 0<=t<=2^k-1,         (C95.3)

where s_2(t) counts binary ones and s_2(0)=0. In particular

    x_end=-beta^(2^k-1)*c^(-k)*z,
    2F(x_end)=beta^(2*(2^k-1))*c^(-2k)*||z||^2.           (C95.4)

Proof: the level at step t-1 is v_2(t), the exponent of 2 dividing t.
The identity sum_(j=1)^t v_2(j)=t-s_2(t) follows either by summing
floor(t/2^q), or by writing t as a sum of distinct powers of 2. Multiplying
the actual scalar factors -a*c^(v_2(j)) yields (C95.3). For positive t,
its absolute multiplier is at most beta/c=a because s_2(t)>=1 and
beta^t<=beta. When t is even the multiplier is nonnegative and at most1;
when t is odd it lies between -a and0. Thus every candidate x_t lies
on one of the segments [0,z] and [0,-a*z], both contained in D. Induction
now proves the actual recursion never leaves D, including the terminal
point. Necessity follows from the first actual step, whose multiplier is
-a when z is in D. At t=2^k-1, s_2(t)=k, giving (C95.4).

The reflection condition is essential for asymmetric ridges. Take one
scalar ridge with r_-=1,r_+=4,A=0,alpha=1,z=4. On any m>=6,
a>=5/(7*(1+sqrt(2)))>1/4. The first actual point -4a lies below -1.
The objective is legal and z is in the core, but all-core invariance fails.
This is an analytical counterexample, not a numerical case or a new fact.

## A scalable, conditional weak-background obstruction

The preceding criterion has an explicit normalization cost. Let d0=||x0||,
which is the true initial distance because C=I, and put

    Gcap=sum_j alpha_j*max(r_(j,-),r_(j,+)),
    hmax=max h_i, Gcap*S_m<=Ccap*d0,
    0<=A<=2*I/hmax,

where Ccap>=0 is a constant independent of m. The radii may be asymmetric.
Since ||I-h_i*A||<=1 and the clipped-ridge gradient has norm at most Gcap,
the true recursion gives ||x_i||<=d0+Gcap*sum_(j<i)h_j<=(1+Ccap)*d0.

Suppose the actual state z at the start of the FINAL H_k suffix satisfies
z,-a*z in D. No condition is imposed on any earlier queried regions.
By (C95.4), the normalized payoff obeys

    V<= (1+Ccap)^2*beta^(2*(2^k-1))*c^(-2k),
    V/K <=2*(1+Ccap)^2*c^(m-2k)*beta^(2*(2^k-1)).         (C95.5)

Here K>=1/(2S_m+1), and M_m<=c^m: the latter follows by induction from
M_(j+1)=2M_j+a*c^j and 2+a<c, proved above.

For m>=16 take k=ceil(log_2(m^2)). Then k<=m, 2^k>=m^2, and the final
suffix has fewer than 2m^2 steps. The elementary inequality log(1-1/m)
<=-1/m and c<3 imply

    V/K <=2*(1+Ccap)^2*exp(2/m)*(3/exp(2))^m ->0.        (C95.6)

The ratio 3/exp(2) is below1, since exp(2)>1+2+2=5. Thus a family meeting
these hypotheses that remains scalar-competitive cannot pass this capture
test at the start of that final suffix for infinitely many unbounded horizons.
This prices weak (even zero) backgrounds and arbitrarily many preceding
gate changes. It does not prove that capture occurs. Cases that stay
outside D, fail the reflected-point condition, have C!=I, or violate the
displayed cap/background hypotheses remain outside the conclusion.

There is no capacity cap and no bound on the number or total mass of tail

Set beta=1/b and m=r/b-1>=0. Choose an integer d>=1, amplitudes
u_1,...,u_d,v>=0, and fixed curvatures satisfying

    0<alpha_q<beta, h_i*alpha_q<=1 for every i,q.

Define p_(0,q)=1, p_(i,q)=product_(t<i)(1-alpha_q*h_t), and the fast
position factors z_0=1, z_1=-m, z_i=0 for2<=i<=n. The actual points and
gradients in R^(d+1) are

    x_i=(u_q*p_(i,q) for1<=q<=d, v*z_i),
    g_i=(alpha_q*u_q*p_(i,q) for1<=q<=d, beta*v*z_i). (2)

They obey every GD update, including the second update because b*beta=1.
They are initially the samples of the ONE quadratic

    F_base(x)=sum_q alpha_q*x_q^2/2+beta*x_(d+1)^2/2.

No time-dependent Hessian is used. Each slow coordinate is nonnegative
and nonincreasing. If b<r and v>0, the fast sampled gradients really
change sign: positive at0, negative at1, zero from2 onwards.

Put

    U_q=alpha_q*(1-alpha_q)*u_q^2/2,
    B=beta*(1-beta)*v^2/2,
    A=sum_q U_q*(p_(1,q)-p_(2,q))*(1-p_(1,q)),
    X25=4r*A, Y25=4r*B*m*(1+m).                         (3)

For slow gradients a_(i,q)=alpha_q*u_q*p_(i,q), write
t_(i,q)=a_(i,q)-a_(i+1,q). Define

    L_slow=sum_(q,i<n) P_(i+1)*t_(i,q)
               *[2(1+P_i)*a_(i,q)-P_(i+1)*t_(i,q)],
    H_fast=beta^2*v^2*[r(2-r)+b(2-b)*m^2].           (4)

Among ALL scalar values on the fixed geometry(2) satisfying ALL directed
finite interpolation inequalities, the exact minimum primitive energy is

    V_min=L_slow+H_fast-min(X25,Y25).                    (5)

The minimum is attained by a single everywhere-defined convex
differentiable function with1-Lipschitz gradient and actual minimizers.
Requiring the actual optimum jet(0,0,0) does not change this minimum.
The explicit values, static function, and true distance are in Section6.

The decisive full-family comparison is

    V_min >= r*(2-r)*[beta^2*v^2
                            +r*sum_q alpha_q^3*u_q^2] >=0. (6)

In fact it is strictly positive whenever r<2 and the initial vector is nonzero.
The bound is uniform over every curvature and amplitude allowed above,
all tail steps satisfying(1), and all legal values, including values of
nonseparable functions. Thus minimization over the ENTIRE stated family
cannot reject any word passing(1). It is not just a comparison at one
chosen amplitude or at unoptimized values.

For an interior two-mode instance with1<b<r, v,u_1>0, and
0<alpha_1<1/max_i h_i, both X25 and Y25 are positive. The exact joint
price gain min(X25,Y25)>0 is then a concrete strict failure of additivity.
Sections4--5 prove why that failure still gives no new obstruction here.

## 2. Original primitive orientation and all-value optimization

Retain every index I={0,...,n}. For any values f_i define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V(f)=2sum_(i<n)h_i*(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n)h_i*(1-h_i)*||g_i||^2-sC*||g_n||^2.

For a nonnegative original finite multiplier array Lambda with zero
diagonal put e=(1,...,1)^T, L=diag(Lambda*e)-Lambda, and

    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T,
    T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
    D=diag(h_i*(2-h_i) for i<n, -s*(s+2)).

The original conditions are

    L^T*e=omega, M=D+(L*T+T^T*L^T)/2 PSD on R^(n+1).

Accepted04219554e41d9750 gives the identity

    V(f)+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij*Q_ij
        =<M,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>.                      (7)

Here omega is OUTGOING minus incoming flow. The terminal index n is the
source of mass2s; each i<n is a sink of mass2h_i. All ordered pairs and
the full formal gradient space remain in this interface. No equality of
formal coordinates at a zero step is imposed on the certificate.

The quadratic base values f_i^0=F_base(x_i) have symmetric nonnegative
slack costs

    w_ij=-Q_ij^0
         =sum_q U_q*(p_(i,q)-p_(j,q))^2+B*(z_i-z_j)^2. (8)

Let d_i be the shortest cost of a directed path n->i in the complete
finite graph with costs(8). Nonnegative costs imply that a shortest
simple path exists, even with zero costs and repeated points.

Replacement values f_i^0+delta_i are legal exactly when
delta_i-delta_j<=w_ij. Every n->i path implies
delta_i-delta_n>=-d_i. Since h_i>=0,

    min_f V(f)=V(f^0)-2sum_(i<n)h_i*d_i.              (9)

The choice delta_i=-d_i attains all these bounds at once: shortest
distances obey d_j<=d_i+w_ij, which is precisely its feasibility.
This proves EVERY directed inequality, not only an adjacent subset.

The same improvement is the exact minimum ORIGINAL slack-flow price.
For any original prescribed flow, w_ij>=d_j-d_i gives

    sum Lambda_ij*w_ij >= -sum_i omega_i*d_i
                           =2sum_(i<n)h_i*d_i.

Sending2h_i along one shortest n->i path for each positive sink h_i
attains equality and satisfies the exact original flow equation.
These auxiliary optimizing flows are not claimed to make M PSD.

## 3. All shortest paths in the incompatible-order geometry

For a scalar ordered list p_0>=...>=p_n and edge costs U*(p_i-p_j)^2,
the distance from n to i is

    U*sum_(k=i)^(n-1)(p_k-p_(k+1))^2.                 (10)

For a proof, an edge crossing several intervening ordered gaps has
cost U*(sum gaps)^2 >= U*sum gaps^2. Every path from p_n to p_i must
cross each gap between them at least once. Summing these lower bounds
over its edges proves(10); the adjacent ordered path attains it. Ties
have zero gap and do not change the argument.

In the isolated fast scalar coordinate, the source position is0, and
the only other positions are1 and-m. The shortest distances are B to0,
B*m^2 to1, and0 to indices>=2: a detour from0 through the opposite-sign
position only adds a nonnegative cost. Define the summed separate-mode
distances

    d_i^sep=sum_q U_q*sum_(k=i)^(n-1)
                          (p_(k,q)-p_(k+1,q))^2
             +B*1_(i=0)+B*m^2*1_(i=1).             (11)

Any joint path has cost at least the sum of these separate minima.
For every i>=1 the chronological path n,n-1,...,i attains(11), including
the fast coordinate. Consequently

    d_i=d_i^sep for1<=i<=n.                          (12)

To reach0, a shortest simple path has a last predecessor j>=1. For j>=2
the best such choice is j=2. Indeed the high coordinate is0 at all these
indices; in each slow coordinate, inserting the intermediate decreasing
points j-1,...,2 into the last edge j->0 weakly decreases squared cost.
For a direct algebraic check, if Delta_k=p_k-p_(k+1)>=0, then

    (1-p_j)^2-(1-p_2)^2
      =2(1-p_2)*sum_(k=2)^(j-1)Delta_k
           +(sum_(k=2)^(j-1)Delta_k)^2
      >=sum_(k=2)^(j-1)Delta_k^2.

Thus it remains to compare exactly two paths: n,...,2,0 and n,...,2,1,0.
Their costs are, respectively,

    d_0^sep+2A,  d_0^sep+2B*m*(1+m).

The first expression uses
(1-p_2)^2-(1-p_1)^2-(p_1-p_2)^2
=2(1-p_1)*(p_1-p_2). The second uses
m^2+(1+m)^2-1=2m(1+m). Therefore

    d_0=d_0^sep+2min(A,B*m*(1+m)).                   (13)

This checks every possible path, without assuming that arbitrary
modewise optimal paths can be combined. Equations(9),(12),(13) show
that the joint price exceeds the sum of the separate prices by EXACTLY

    4r*min(A,B*m*(1+m))=min(X25,Y25).                    (14)

An explicit attaining original flow is also available. If the path
through1 is cheaper, take Lambda_(k+1,k)=2P_(k+1) for0<=k<n and all
other entries zero. If the bypass is cheaper, take

    Lambda_20=2r, Lambda_21=2b, Lambda_10=0,
    Lambda_(k+1,k)=2P_(k+1) for2<=k<n,

with every other entry zero. At equality either flow, or any convex
combination, attains the minimum. Both are nonnegative and have exact
terminal-source flow. They are auxiliary flows, not full PSD certificates.

## 4. The exact separate energies and their sum

Consider one slow coordinate and abbreviate its gradients by a_i and
decrements by t_i=a_i-a_(i+1). Its ordered shortest paths make every
reverse adjacent inequality tight at the optimized values:

    f_i-f_(i+1)=h_i*a_i*a_(i+1)+t_i^2/2.

Substitution into V gives the corresponding summand L_q in(4).
Here is a telescoping audit independent of any previous monotone draft.
The value term becomes sum_i[2P_(i+1)*h_i*a_i*a_(i+1)
+P_(i+1)*t_i^2]. After writing a_(i+1)=a_i-t_i, the coefficient of a_i^2
is h_i*(1+2P_i+h_i), which equals
P_(i+1)*(P_(i+1)+1)-P_i*(P_i+1). Subtracting sC*a_n^2 telescopes it
to sum_i P_(i+1)*(P_(i+1)+1)*(2a_i*t_i-t_i^2).
The remaining terms reduce exactly to

    L_q=sum_i P_(i+1)*t_i*
                 [2(1+P_i)*a_i-P_(i+1)*t_i].        (15)

This derivation proves the exact minimum for a scalar slow mode, because
the distance potentials already satisfy all its nonadjacent inequalities.

For the fast coordinate, the optimized values, with its zero terminal
value, are beta^2*v^2/2 at0 and beta^2*v^2*m^2/2 at1, zero thereafter.
Indeed they are the quadratic base values minus B and B*m^2. Their
exact primitive energy is H_fast in(4).

They are also attained by the explicit one-dimensional function

    F_fast(t)=dist(t,J)^2/2,
    J=[-(1-beta)*v*m, (1-beta)*v].                   (16)

The derivative is t minus its projection onto the interval J; it is
nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz. At v,-v*m,0 it has exactly the stated
gradients and values, and J is its actual full minimizer set.

The base primitive energy is a sum of coordinate energies. Applying
the exact improvement(14) to their separate all-value minima proves(5).
The minimizing JOINT values need not be values of the separable sum of
the coordinate interpolants. Section6 constructs their actual joint
function; no incompatible scalar value assignments are silently glued.

## 5. Full parameter comparison: the coupling gain is absorbed

The prefix bounds in(1) imply nonnegativity of EVERY slow summand in(15).
Indeed 0<=t_i<=a_i and

    2(1+P_i)*a_i-P_(i+1)*t_i
        >=(P_i+2-h_i)*a_i>=0.                       (17)

The FIRST TWO summands cover the entire possible coupling charge. Since
p_1=1-r*alpha and p_2=(1-b*alpha)*p_1, the coordinate contribution X25_q to X25 is

    X25_q=2r^2*b*alpha^3*(1-alpha)*(1-r*alpha)*u^2.

Let l=1-r*alpha in[0,1] and set

    D_b=b*(r+b)/r, A_b=2+2r-D_b.

Since b<=r, D_b<=2r and A_b>=2. The first two summands in L_q,
after dividing by alpha^3*u^2 when u>0, are

    r^2*(2-r^2*alpha)
      +b*(r+b)*l^2*[2(1+r)-b*(r+b)*alpha].

Subtract X25_q/(alpha^3*u^2)=2r^2*b*(1-alpha)*l and use
alpha=(1-l)/r. The resulting EXACT polynomial is

    Delt_q(l)=r^2*(2-r)
       +r*[r^2-2b*(r-1)]*l
       +[b*(r+b)*A_b-2r*b]*l^2
       +[b^2*(r+b)^2/r]*l^3.                       (18)

Every coefficient is nonnegative. The linear coefficient is at least
r^2*(2-r), since b<=r and r>=1. The quadratic coefficient is at least
2b^2, since A_b>=2. The cubic coefficient is positive. In particular

    Delt_q(l)>=r^2*(2-r)*(1+l)+2b^2*l^2>=r^2*(2-r).

If u=0, the same comparison holds after multiplying through by
alpha^3*u^2, without division. All later summands of L_q are
nonnegative by(17). Summing over the slow modes gives

    L_slow>=X25+r^2*(2-r)*sum_q alpha_q^3*u_q^2.      (19)

Meanwhile1<=b<=r<=2 gives

    H_fast>=beta^2*v^2*r*(2-r)>=0.                  (20)

Finally min(X25,Y25)<=X25. Inserting(19)--(20) into the EXACT formula(5)
proves(6). The slow modes alone cover the entire potential coupling
gain; the fast mode contributes a nonnegative remaining energy.
Neither the amplitudes nor the curvatures nor the values remain to be
optimized to decide the sign. The comparison works on the WHOLE range
r<=2 supplied by the first prefix-step bound, not only near one word.

## 6. One static attaining function, actual optimum and true radius

Append the optimum index star with x_star=g_star=f_star=0 to the graph.
Its direct distance from n is

    d_star=D_star=sum_q U_q*p_(n,q)^2.               (22)

This is a shortest path: in every slow coordinate, all finite positions
are at least the terminal position, and there is no finite position
strictly between zero and that terminal position. Formula(10), with
zero inserted at the end, gives a lower bound U_q*p_(n,q)^2 in that
coordinate. The fast coordinate is zero at both endpoints. The direct
arc attains the sum of these lower bounds.

Adding star cannot shorten a finite distance. For every finite j,

    w_(n,j)=D_star+w_(star,j)
                    -2sum_q U_q*p_(n,q)*p_(j,q)
             <=D_star+w_(star,j).

In a path passing through star, its prefix to star has cost at least
D_star. Replace that prefix and its following arc star->j by n->j.
The displayed inequality never increases the cost. Thus the finite
distances remain exactly(12)--(13), and the fixed-optimum price equals
the original finite-flow price, without adding optimum multipliers to(7).

The actual attaining values are now explicit:

    f_i=f_i^0+D_star-d_i, f_star=0.                  (23)

For every ordered pair among the finite and optimum indices, the change
of values is a distance potential. Hence all Q_ij<=0 follow from the
distance inequalities as in Section2, including both directions and
every coincident-point pair.

Let y_i=x_i-g_i, eta_i=||g_i||^2/2-f_i, including y_star=eta_star=0.
Define on R^(d+1)

    H(w)=||w||^2/2+max_i(<y_i,w>+eta_i),
    F(x)=sup_w(<x,w>-H(w)).                         (24)

This is the constructive interpolation form of accepted1252b8823bb5a290.
For completeness, H is finite, continuous,1-strongly convex and has
quadratic growth. There is a unique maximizing w(x) for every x.
The two strong subgradient inequalities imply
<x-x',w(x)-w(x')>>=||w(x)-w(x')||^2. The two maximizing inequalities
then give a differentiability remainder bounded by||x-x'||^2, proving
that F is convex differentiable with gradient w(x) and1-Lipschitz
gradient. The Q inequalities make the i-th branch of H active at g_i,
with subgradient x_i. Thus grad F(x_i)=g_i and F(x_i)=f_i. This is ONE
fixed global F realizing every step of(2), not a sequence of local jets.

The exact minimizer set is

    K_min=conv{y_i:eta_i=0}, min F=0.                (25)

Indeed eta_i<=0 by the optimum inequalities, and eta_star=0. A point x
minimizes F exactly when grad F(x)=0, equivalently x belongs to the
subgradient set of H at0. This set is exactly the convex hull of the
active slopes y_i. To verify the latter equality, a convex combination
of active slopes gives the subgradient inequality directly. For a point
outside that hull, a separating direction and a sufficiently small
positive displacement keep inactive affine branches inactive and
contradict the subgradient inequality. This proves both inclusions.

In particular a real optimum always exists and the TRUE radius is

    R_true=dist(x_0,K_min),                          (26)

with the displayed finite convex hull, not an assumed normalization.
The point x_0 has nonzero gradient whenever some amplitude is positive,
so it is outside K_min and this radius is positive.

There is a simpler exact radius in the generic sign-changing family.
The direct arc bound d_i<=w_(n,i) gives

    eta_i<=-2sum_q U_q*p_(i,q)*p_(n,q).

If any active slow mode has p_(n,q)>0, this is STRICTLY negative at
every finite sample. Therefore K_min={0} and

    R_true^2=sum_q u_q^2+v^2.                       (27)

The entire open family with strict h_i*alpha_q<1 has this property.

For an explicit terminal-zero boundary, take one active slow mode,
u>0, alpha*r<1, and let k>=3 be its first zero index. Put j=k-1.
Then the slow positions are positive through j and zero afterwards;
the fast coordinate has already vanished. The active slopes in(25)
are0 and ((1-alpha)*u*p_j,0), including any repeated copies caused by
zero steps before the killing step. Earlier distinct positions have
strictly smaller eta because their monotone distance path has at least
one intermediate positive position; in particular the path via j
strictly improves their direct squared cost. Hence

    K_min=[0,(1-alpha)*u*p_j] x {0},
    R_true^2=(u-(1-alpha)*u*p_j)^2+v^2.              (28)

For other degenerate amplitude patterns, (25)--(26) already specify
the complete minimizer set and exact true distance without a false
uniqueness assertion. In particular, if every slow amplitude vanishes,
(16) supplies the full fast minimizer interval directly, with closest
distance beta*v from its initial point v.

## 7. Boundaries, scalar-cut comparison, and exact scope

All formulas allow b=1 (unit fast curvature, B=0), r=b (no fast
reversal, m=0), vanishing amplitudes, zero tail steps, and slow products
that first hit zero. Then the corresponding price increment is zero
when dictated by(3); no positive-price claim is retained at a collapsed
boundary. Repeated positions have identical gradients and values by
(2),(8),(23). The optimum graph retains them as separate indices.

Arbitrary additional zero steps can also be inserted anywhere into the
physical word, with all duplicate samples retained. Compression here
is only a description of this actual witness: its positions, gradients,
values, sums, energy, and price do not change. Lift each displayed path
through the zero-cost duplicates, keeping sinks of weight zero if
needed. No compression, quotient, or equality is imposed on the formal
M in(7). At n=4 its ambient space is still all of R^5.

The prefix-step hypothesis in(1) is already weaker than the old actual
single-cut necessary conditions. Here is the complete relevant
reconstruction. For any cut j with h_j>1, put
P=P_j, T=sum_(i>j)h_i, eta=(h_j-1)/(1+T). Use the scalar function

    F_cut(x)=max_(g in[-eta,1]) (x*g-g^2/2)

and x_0=1+P. Before the cut, the gradient is1 and x_j=1. Immediately
afterwards x_(j+1)=-(1+T)*eta; throughout the tail the gradient is-eta,
with x_n=-eta. The derivative is projection onto[-eta,1], so the
function is convex differentiable and1-smooth. Its unique minimizer
is0: the interval contains both a positive and a negative number,
and testing a sufficiently small number of the sign of x makes F_cut(x)>0
for x!=0. Direct insertion of F_cut(x)=x*g-g^2/2 and these two constant
gradient blocks into V yields

    V_cut=(1+P)^2-C^2*((h_j-1)/(1+T))^2.

Thus a full certificate in(7) requires

    C*(h_j-1)<=(1+P)*(1+T).                         (29)

Writing U=1+P and R=1+T gives C=U+R+(h_j-1). If h_j>=P+2, then
h_j-1>=U and C*(h_j-1)>=C*U>R*U, contrary to(29).
Hence every positive step passing(29) satisfies h_j<P_j+2; a step at
most1 satisfies that inequality directly. This proves the comparison
to previously available conditions, without importing an unverified
monotone or cut draft.

For four-step words with 1<=h_1<=h_0<=2, the theorem covers every
fast mode beta=1/h_1 and every collection of slow eigenmodes satisfying
alpha_q*h_i<=1. It is independent of C and so remains valid throughout
the threshold C>=193/25. The old first-cut condition itself forces
h_0<2, so no stronger compact-domain bound or auxiliary draft is needed.
The family still imposes h_1<=h_0 and annihilation at the second step. No claim is
made for the other initial ordering or a fast mode that survives.

The exact information gain is therefore a SCOPED CLOSURE: even genuinely
incompatible spatial orderings and a strictly positive all-value joint
price do not strengthen the old conditions in this entire stated family.
It does not exclude a new remaining h-region, construct any full Lambda,
or establish feasibility of any full PSD certificate. Excluding a witness
family is not a seed, and even excluding every four-step seed would only
close the sufficient negative route of04219554e41d9750, not settle the
original affirmative minimax target.

## 1. Original matrix, notation and exact identities

Let

    h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,v), a,b,c>0, v>=0, bc<=1,
    u=1+a, beta=1+b, w=1+c,
    A=2+a, N=3+a+b, H=2+a+b, H0=1+a+b,
    C=1+sum h=4+a+b+c+v,
    t=c/(1+v), mu=1+t, gamma=w/mu,
    ell=a^2*b*(1-b*t), K=b^2*gamma^2,
    Rcut=ell*N^2+mu-C^2*a^2*b*beta*t^2,
    Dprefix=N^2*b^2-A^2,
    Gap=K*Rcut-ell*Dprefix,
    z=a*b*(w-mu)=a*b*v*t.

Write P_i=sum_(j<i)h_j, s=P_4=C-1, and let e_i be the five original

The accepted polynomial identity is

The flow implies e^T M e=0: Te=e+P,

          +ell*mu*(H*B0+beta*B1)+c03*Lambda03+c23*Lambda23,              (3)

## 2. A family of exact three-vector positive-gap remainders

For ell>0 define

    k0=b^2*w/(ell*mu)=b^2*gamma/ell,
    kold=K/ell,
    U=2*beta*z/(a*u).

Choose a positive number k and a real number theta satisfying

    k>=k0,
    0<=theta<=min(U,2*k*mu*z),
    F(k,theta):=b^2*w^2-z*theta
                  +(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta^2/4-k*ell*mu^2 <=0.          (7)

Put

    Btheta=b*w-a*theta/2,
    Atheta=Avec-theta*B/(2*k*mu),
    cB=k*ell*mu*H-beta*(b*w*H0-u)+a*u*theta/2,
    c1=beta*(k*ell*mu-b^2*w),
    c04=beta*b*v*c-u*(1+v)*theta/2,
    c03new=k*c03-u*theta/2.

There is the EXACT full-array identity

 k*Rcut-Dprefix
   =||beta*J+Btheta*B||_M^2+k*mu*||Atheta||_M^2-F(k,theta)*Tcut
      +cB*B0+c1*B1+beta*u*Lambda20
      +c04*Lambda04+beta*b*v*c*Lambda14
      +c03new*Lambda03+k*c23*Lambda23.                              (8)

All displayed coefficients on the right are nonnegative. For cB,
at k=k0,theta=0 its value is

    b^2*w*H-beta*(b*w*H0-u)=u*(1-bc)>=0;

increasing k or theta adds nonnegative terms. The other coefficients
have exactly the signs in (7).

To check (8), expand its two squares. Their J-B cross coefficient is
2*beta*b*w because -a*theta*beta from the first square cancels
+a*theta*beta from -theta<Avec,B>_M in the second. Their E-B
cross contribution is -u*theta<E,B>_M. The Tcut coefficient is

    (b*w-a*theta/2)^2+a*b*mu*theta+theta^2/(4*k*mu)
                      =k*ell*mu^2+F(k,theta).

Now use (5) in the remaining u*theta<E,B>_M. Its contributions are
+a*u*theta*B0/2,-u*theta*Lambda03/2, and
-u*(1+v)*theta*Lambda04/2. Combining (3) and (4) gives precisely
every coefficient in (8). This proof divides by no matrix energy.

In particular, every full original certificate satisfies

                         Dprefix<=k*Rcut.                            (9)

## 3. The optimal constant in this three-vector relaxation

The minimizer of F(k,theta) before the upper bounds in (7) is

    theta_free(k)=2*z/(a^2+1/(k*mu)).

It always obeys theta_free<=2*k*mu*z. Thus the optimum allowed value
is

    theta_opt(k)=min(theta_free(k),U).                                (10)

For v>0 one has z>0 and k0<kold. At k=k0, even the unrestricted
minimum is strictly positive. Indeed, if Hk=a^2*k0*mu,

    min_theta F(k0,theta)/mu^2
      =b^2*(gamma-1)*(gamma+Hk)/(1+Hk)>0.                            (11)

At k=kold, its allowed minimum is strictly negative: choose any
positive theta smaller than both upper bounds and sufficiently close
to zero, and the constant term vanishes while -z*theta dominates the
positive quadratic term. For each fixed theta,

    partial F/partial k=-ell*mu^2-theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)<0.

Also (10) minimizes over the fixed interval [0,U], since the other
bound is automatic at that minimizer. Thus this minimum is continuous
and strictly decreasing in k. It follows that there is a unique

    kstar in (k0,kold), F(kstar,theta_opt(kstar))=0.                   (12)

This is an exact algebraic number, without a numerical root search.
Here are explicit branches. Define

    Bint=a^2*b^2*mu*(2*gamma-1)-ell,
    kint=(Bint+sqrt(Bint^2+4*a^2*ell*mu*b^2*gamma^2))
                                                       /(2*a^2*ell*mu).

If theta_free(kint)<=U, then kstar=kint. Otherwise define

    V0=b^2*w^2-z*U+a^2*U^2/4,
    V1=U^2/(4*mu),
    kbound=(V0+sqrt(V0^2+4*ell*mu^2*V1))/(2*ell*mu^2).

Then kstar=kbound. These are obtained by multiplying respectively
F(k,theta_free(k))=0 and F(k,U)=0 by their positive denominators.
If the free root violates the cap, the increasing theta_free remains
above U at every larger k; the boundary root is therefore the correct
one. Equality of the branch conditions gives the same root.

At v=0 with ell>0, z=U=0, gamma=1 and k0=kold=b^2/ell. Set
kstar=kold and theta_opt=0; (7)--(9) still hold. No strict gain is
claimed on this boundary.

For v>0,ell>0 the new bound is strictly stronger than the old
two-energy gap bound Dprefix<=kold*Rcut whenever Dprefix>0:

    Rcut>=Dprefix/kstar,
    Gap>= (K/kstar-ell)*Dprefix >0.                                 (13)

Thus it excludes an explicit POSITIVE gap strip, not just Gap=0.
This comparison is ONLY with the previous nested two-energy bound.
It is not a comparison with the entire older necessary system.

The constant kstar is sharp for the following explicitly delimited
relaxation: retain arbitrary PSD Gram data for (E,J,B), (3)--(5),
and nonnegative quantities B0,B1,Lambda20,Lambda03,Lambda04,
Lambda14,Lambda23, but impose no remaining original rows or quadratic
column. This sharpness does not assert a full certificate.

To prove it, work in a one-dimensional Gram space with B=1 and set
Tcut=1, B0=B1=Lambda20=Lambda03=Lambda14=Lambda23=0. Let
k=kstar,theta=theta_opt(kstar), x=b*w-a*theta/2 and J=-x/beta.
If the free branch applies, set E=0,Lambda04=0. The equation
theta=2*k*mu*(a*x-a*b*mu) follows from theta=theta_free.
Consequently both squares in (8) vanish and (5) holds.

On the capped branch put

    q04=2*(a*x-a*b*mu-theta/(2*k*mu))/(u*(1+v)),
    Lambda04=q04, E=-(1+v)*q04/2.

The condition theta=U<=theta_free implies q04>=0. Again both squares
and (5) hold, while c04=0. Define Rcut and Dprefix in this RELAXATION
by (3) and (4), rather than by the step-only values. Then Rcut>0
because ell*mu^2*Tcut>0, and Dprefix=kstar*Rcut. This proves exactly
the stated sharpness and explicitly identifies its missing matching
conditions: its energies have not been equated with the actual
step-only Rcut,Dprefix, and its remaining original array is absent.

## 4. Coupling to the actual quadratic column

For any choice (k,theta) satisfying (7), define

    rho=-F(k,theta)>=0,
    Lk=k*mu/(1+a^2*k*mu)>0,
    Zk=z-(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta/2.

The three matrix-energy terms in (8) dominate sigma*m, where

    sigma=u^2*Lk*rho/(rho+Lk*Zk^2), if rho+Lk*Zk^2>0,
    sigma=u^2*Lk,                   if rho=Zk=0.                    (14)

For the proof let X=beta*J+Btheta*B, Y=Atheta. Then
a*X+Y=u*E+Zk*B. Completing the square in X gives

    ||X||_M^2+k*mu*||Y||_M^2
                        >=Lk*||u*E+Zk*B||_M^2.

If rho+Lk*Zk^2>0, complete the square in B after adding rho||B||_M^2.
The remaining E coefficient is exactly (14). If rho=Zk=0, the
previous display is Lk*u^2*m directly. This covers singular Gram
matrices; no inverse of their entries is used. In particular sigma=0
at the strictly capped kstar branch, but sigma>0 for every k>kstar
with theta=theta_opt(k). On the free kstar branch sigma>0 already.

Combining (8) with (14) leaves the common ORIGINAL coefficient budget

    k*Rcut-Dprefix >= sigma*m+cB*(Lambda30+Lambda40)
                                            +beta*u*Lambda20.       (15)

Assume sigma>0 and define

    xi_cap=min(u/a^2, cB/(a^2*W0)).                                 (16)

If W0=0, omit the second argument of this minimum; its corresponding
incoming coefficients in (6) are both zero. This convention is used
only when that denominator is zero. The derivation itself is the
division-free condition xi*a^2*W0<=cB.

For any real xi satisfying xi<=xi_cap and xi<sigma/u, put

    Zeta=xi^2/(sigma-xi*u)>=0.

The following is a further necessary inequality of the FULL original
cone:

    k*Rcut-Dprefix >= xi*u*delta-Zeta*Q.                             (17)

To check it, subtract xi*u*delta using (6). In (15), the remaining
incoming Lambda20 coefficient is beta*u-xi*a^2*beta>=0. The two
B0 coefficients are at least cB-xi*a^2*W0>=0 if xi>=0; if xi<0
they only increase. The remaining matrix terms after adding Zeta*Q
are

    (sigma-xi*u)*||E||_M^2+2*xi<E,p>_M+Zeta*||p||_M^2
         = ||sqrt(sigma-xi*u)*E
                          +xi*p/sqrt(sigma-xi*u)||_M^2 >=0.

This proof couples the energies to the ACTUAL p in the ACTUAL M.
It is a sufficient full-space separator, not an assumption that
independently selected scalar energies possess a PSD completion.
Negative xi are intentionally allowed. They expose the opposite
first-step regime and the quadratic zero boundary.

For clarity the supremum of the right side of (17) is explicit.
Write Qplus=Q+u^2*delta. If Qplus<0, letting xi tend to -infinity
in (17) is a contradiction. Thus Qplus>=0 is necessary, in addition
to Q>=0. The exact factorization is

    Qplus=a^2*(A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2).

Thus this particular feasibility prerequisite recovers the existing
scalar-return condition Cbc|v-1|<=A; it is not counted as a new
independent obstruction. Suppose Q,Qplus>=0 and xi_cap>0.

If Q>0 and Qplus>0, set

    xi_free=(sigma/u)*(1-sqrt(Q/Qplus)).

When xi_free<=xi_cap the optimized bound is

    Bcal=(sigma/u^2)*(sqrt(Qplus)-sqrt(Q))^2.                         (18)

Otherwise xi_cap<sigma/u and the bound is

    Bcal=xi_cap*u*delta-xi_cap^2*Q/(sigma-xi_cap*u).                 (19)

If Q>0,Qplus=0, the supremum is sigma*Q/u^2, obtained as
xi tends to -infinity. If Q=0, Qplus>=0 means delta>=0, and the
supremum is

    Bcal=u*delta*min(xi_cap,sigma/u).                                (20)

For delta=Q=0 this is zero. These are limits of necessary inequalities
for every finite xi, so nonattainment of a supremum causes no problem.

The optimization follows by putting y=sigma-xi*u>0 in (17):

 xi*u*delta-xi^2*Q/(sigma-xi*u)
   =sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2
         -(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The unconstrained maximum is (18), at
y=sigma*sqrt(Q/Qplus); clipping xi above by xi_cap gives (19).
The displayed boundary formulas follow from the same expression.
The function is increasing up to its unconstrained maximum, so the
clipped value is nonnegative. In the present ell>0 domain cB>0 for
the optimizing choices used above: if v=0 then bc<1, and if v>0
the choice theta_opt>0. Hence xi_cap>0 there. Other allowed parameter
choices with cB=0 are covered by (17) without the positive-cap claim.

For every such choice with sigma>0, the final explicit test is

    Q>=0, Qplus>=0, k*Rcut-Dprefix>=Bcal.                            (21)

When v>0, Dprefix>0 and kstar<k<kold, it gives the positive-gap bound

    Gap >= (K/k-ell)*Dprefix+(K/k)*Bcal.                             (22)

The second term is strictly positive when delta!=0, provided the
displayed feasibility conditions hold. At delta=0 it is zero; no
uniform margin is inferred across that boundary.

## 5. Relation to the earlier first-row budget and the full column

The earlier lifted first-cut identity can be retained simultaneously.
Its exact accounting, reproduced below, uses

    eta=b/(1+w+v), nu=(1+eta)*(1-a*eta)/a,
    Erow=a+3+1/a-(u*delta/a)*eta-C^2*eta^2,
    Erow=nu*(m+a*(Lambda20+B0))+(1+eta)^2*M11
                      +(1+eta)*eta*((w+v)*Lambda12+v*Lambda13).       (23)

It applies when 0<a<1 and a*eta<1. For a full array, a<1 follows
from m=1-a^2-a*O0 and the first row moment
sum_(j>0)P_j*Lambda0j=2u>0. Indeed the index0 entry of
2Me=2Dmat*e+L*(e+P)+T^T*omega is
2(1-a^2)-sum_(j>0)P_j*Lambda0j+2au=0, proving this moment.
For (23) the condition a*eta<1 is retained as an explicit hypothesis;
it is not required for Sections1--4.

Here is a direct check of (23). Let Uphys,Vphys be orthonormal and
gfirst=-eta*Uphys+sqrt(nu)*Vphys. Use actual steps and saturated values
on the arrays

    X=(Uphys+u*gfirst,Uphys,-b*Uphys,-(1+v)*eta*Uphys,-eta*Uphys),
    G=(gfirst,Uphys,-eta*Uphys,-eta*Uphys,-eta*Uphys).

The normals at targets1 and4 are zero. At0 the incoming residual
from1 vanishes and those from2,3,4 equal -a*nu. At2 the only nonzero

||gfirst||^2=[1+(1-a)*eta]/a and
<Uphys,gfirst>+a||gfirst||^2=1-a*eta. All other finite residuals
vanish. The optimum comparisons are nonpositive under a*eta<1.
The saturated telescope gives Erow; the two gradient columns are
nu^(1/2)*e0 and (1+eta)*e1-eta*e. Substituting all costs into (1)
gives (23), since b-eta=(w+v)*eta.

The quantitative2948 constraint is recovered on its original domain,
so it remains simultaneous with the new test. Put

    Wrow=max(beta,W0), Krow=max(u,a*Wrow).

By (23), m+a*(Lambda20+B0)<=Erow/nu. Equation (6) and (2) give

    u*delta<=Krow*Erow/nu+2*sqrt(Q*Erow/nu).                        (26)

Indeed the incoming weighted sum in (6) is at most
Wrow*(Lambda20+B0), and m<=Erow/nu. For delta>0, rationalizing
the positive quadratic root in sqrt(Erow/nu) yields

    Erow>=nu*(u*delta/(sqrt(Q+Krow*u*delta)+sqrt(Q)))^2>0.           (27)

On the original additional domain v>1, ab<=1, c*(v-1)<=1, we have

    Erow>nu*delta^2/u^2,
    b<(a+3)*(C-a-2)/((a+1)*(C+a+2)).                              (28)

For the equivalence in (28), use the exact factorization

 u^2*(Erow-nu*delta^2/u^2)
    =((a+3)-(delta+u*C)*eta)*((a+3)+(u*C-delta)*eta).

The second factor is positive since C>A and u*A>delta. Substituting
eta=b/(C-A-b) into the positive first factor gives the stated bound.
Thus no part of the2948 restriction is silently weakened or assumed
outside its hypotheses. At Q=0, (26)--(27) remain undivided.

The two budgets (15) and (23) constrain the same m,Lambda20,B0.
One cannot minimize each with different incoming arrays and call the
answers a simultaneous certificate. The new inequality (21) is a

For v>0 the columns e,E,J,B,p are a basis: the first four have equal
