# Quantitative positive-gap constraints from the original three-vector energy

Status: complete joint analytical proof DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max4
round31, the first of the two rounds authorized after completed30 by
TASK.md and master_guidance6e0a18d700dcd62f. No numerical evaluation,
solver, replay, installation, subordinate agent, consult or fact_submit
is used. The sole accepted mathematical input is the original full
primitive identity in fact04219554e41d9750, Section10. All additional
identities and optimization arguments used in this draft are proved here.

This draft retains the THREE-vector energy discarded by the earlier
two-energy optimization. It gives an exact positive improvement of that
particular gap bound, and combines it with the actual quadratic column
in the SAME original matrix. All twenty coefficient signs are retained
in the hypotheses. It does NOT show that the new excluded strip contains
a word passing the complete older scalar/triangle/curvature system. It
does NOT solve the remaining full-column/sign completion problem. The
original threshold seed and original exact-profile question remain open.

## 1. Original matrix, notation and exact identities

Let

    h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,v), a,b,c>0, v>=0, bc<=1,
    u=1+a, beta=1+b, w=1+c,
    A=2+a, N=3+a+b, H=2+a+b, H0=1+a+b,
    C=1+sum h=4+a+b+c+v,
    t=c/(1+v), mu=1+t, gamma=w/mu,
    ell=a^2*b*(1-b*t), K=b^2*gamma^2,
    Rcut=ell*N^2+mu-C^2*a^2*b*beta*t^2,
    Dprefix=N^2*b^2-A^2,
    Gap=K*Rcut-ell*Dprefix,
    z=a*b*(w-mu)=a*b*v*t.

Here ell>=0 and gamma>=1. In this stated domain ell=0 if and only if
v=0 and bc=1. Every formula below that divides by ell is explicitly
restricted to ell>0. The case ell=0 is handled separately in Section6.

Write P_i=sum_(j<i)h_j, s=P_4=C-1, and let e_i be the five original
standard coordinate columns, indexed0 through4, and e=sum e_i. Put

    T_ii=1, T_ij=h_j if j<i, T_ij=0 if j>i,
    omega=(-2h0,-2h1,-2h2,-2h3,2s)^T,
    Dmat=diag(h0(2-h0),h1(2-h1),h2(2-h2),h3(2-h3),-s(s+2)),
    L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda, M=Dmat+(LT+T^T L^T)/2.

The hypotheses are the original twenty signs Lambda_ij>=0 for i!=j,
zero diagonal, L^T e=omega, and M>=0 on ALL of R^5. No coordinate,
multiplier, rank or support is removed. In particular v=0 does not
authorize identification of the formal gradients at indices3 and4.

The accepted polynomial identity is

    V_h+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=sum_(i,j)M_ij<g_i,g_j>,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                                 -s(s+1)||g4||^2.       (1)

It is valid on formal data following x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i; formal
substitutions below are not asserted to be actual trajectories unless
their interpolation inequalities are checked.

The flow implies e^T M e=0: Te=e+P,
e^T Dmat e=-s^2-sum h_i^2, and
omega^T(e+P)=s^2+sum h_i^2. Nonnegativity of
(e+r*q)^T M(e+r*q) for both signs of the real number r then gives Me=0.
The same argument gives

    |x^T M y|^2 <= (x^T M x)(y^T M y),
    x^T M x=0 implies Mx=0.                           (2)

Use the shorthand <x,y>_M=x^T M y and ||x||_M^2=<x,x>_M. Set

    E=e0, J=e0+e1, B=e3+e4,
    S=||J||_M^2, Tcut=||B||_M^2, r=<J,B>_M,
    B0=Lambda30+Lambda40, B1=Lambda31+Lambda41,
    Avec=u*E-a*beta*J-a*b*mu*B,
    c03=a*b*u*mu*v*t=u*mu*z,
    c23=a^2*b*beta*mu*v*t.

The next three identities hold for every array satisfying the original
flow and Me=0:

    Rcut=ell*mu^2*Tcut+mu*||Avec||_M^2
          +ell*mu*(H*B0+beta*B1)+c03*Lambda03+c23*Lambda23,              (3)

    Dprefix=beta*((b*w*H0-u)*B0+b^2*w*B1-2*b*w*r-beta*S
                    -u*Lambda20-b*v*c*(Lambda04+Lambda14)),            (4)

    2<E,B>_M=a*B0-Lambda03-(1+v)*Lambda04.                             (5)

Here are full derivations. For (3), take saturated values
f_i=x_i*g_i-g_i^2/2 in the two scalar arrays

    x_base=(N,2+b,1,-c,-t), g_base=(1,1,1,-t,-t),
    x_aux =(1,-a,ab,-abc,-abt), g_aux=(1,-a,ab,-abt,-abt).

Both follow the original h. Their normals x_i-g_i are respectively
(H,beta,0,-vt,0) and (0,0,0,-abvt,0). For saturated values
Q_ij=(g_i-g_j)(x_j-g_j). In the weighted sum ell times the base array
plus mu times the auxiliary array, the complete nonzero residual list is

    Q30=Q40=-ell*mu*H, Q31=Q41=-ell*mu*beta,
    Q03=-c03, Q23=-c23.

All other ordered residuals vanish. In particular Q13 cancels because
ell=a^2*b*(1-bt). At Q03 use
ell+ab*(1+abt)=ab*u, and at Q23 use
ell+a^2*b^2*mu=a^2*b*beta. The position/gradient square telescope in
(1) for saturated values is V_h=||x0||^2-||x4+s*g4||^2. Since x4=g4,
the weighted energy is Rcut. Me=0 gives g_base=-mu*B+e and
g_aux=Avec+ab*e, proving (3). No interpolation inequality is omitted.

For (4), start the scalar two-step cut at x0=A with gradients
(1,1,-b), then extend it FORMALLY with constant gradient -b through
the last two steps and affine function values. The full energy is
A^2-N^2*b^2=-Dprefix. The gradient column is beta*J-b*e.
The only negative residuals are Q20=Q30=Q40=-u*beta. The positive
ones are Q03=Q13=w*b*beta and Q04=Q14=(w+v)*b*beta.
The other ordered residuals vanish. Thus (1) gives

 Dprefix=b*beta*(w*(Lambda03+Lambda13)+(w+v)*(Lambda04+Lambda14))
                  -beta^2*S-u*beta*(Lambda20+B0).

The two original cross rows, obtained by multiplying the displayed T,
are (5) and

    2<e1,B>_M=beta*B0+b*B1-Lambda13-(1+v)*Lambda14.

Their sum eliminates Lambda03+Lambda13+(1+v)(Lambda04+Lambda14).
Because (w+v)-w(1+v)=-vc, the result is exactly (4).
These identities use the original rows; no reversal is invoked.

Finally define the original unit-quadratic column and its energy by

    p=(1,-a,ab,-abc,abc*(v-1))^T,
    Q=1-C^2*a^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2,
    m=||E||_M^2, delta=u^2-2,
    W0=1+bc*(v-1).

We have Tp=e and Le=0. Telescoping
h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2 gives

    ||p||_M^2=Q>=0,
    2<E,p>_M=u*(m-delta)
                +a^2*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40).     (6)

For completeness, put O0=sum_(j>0)Lambda0j and
I0=Lambda20+Lambda30+Lambda40. The diagonal gives
m=1-a^2-a*O0. Node0 flow gives Lambda10=O0+2u-I0.
Using Te0=u*e-a*e0 in Mp=Dmat*p+T^T L^T p/2 yields
2<E,p>_M=2(1-a^2)-a*p^T L e0. Substitute

 p^T L e0=u*O0+2a*u
             -a*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40).

The remaining constant is -u*delta, proving (6). On bc<=1,v>=0,
0<=1-bc<=W0. Consequently every coefficient in the incoming
combination in (6) is nonnegative. This sign assertion includes v<1.

## 2. A family of exact three-vector positive-gap remainders

For ell>0 define

    k0=b^2*w/(ell*mu)=b^2*gamma/ell,
    kold=K/ell,
    U=2*beta*z/(a*u).

Choose a positive number k and a real number theta satisfying

    k>=k0,
    0<=theta<=min(U,2*k*mu*z),
    F(k,theta):=b^2*w^2-z*theta
                  +(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta^2/4-k*ell*mu^2 <=0.          (7)

Put

    Btheta=b*w-a*theta/2,
    Atheta=Avec-theta*B/(2*k*mu),
    cB=k*ell*mu*H-beta*(b*w*H0-u)+a*u*theta/2,
    c1=beta*(k*ell*mu-b^2*w),
    c04=beta*b*v*c-u*(1+v)*theta/2,
    c03new=k*c03-u*theta/2.

There is the EXACT full-array identity

 k*Rcut-Dprefix
   =||beta*J+Btheta*B||_M^2+k*mu*||Atheta||_M^2-F(k,theta)*Tcut
      +cB*B0+c1*B1+beta*u*Lambda20
      +c04*Lambda04+beta*b*v*c*Lambda14
      +c03new*Lambda03+k*c23*Lambda23.                              (8)

All displayed coefficients on the right are nonnegative. For cB,
at k=k0,theta=0 its value is

    b^2*w*H-beta*(b*w*H0-u)=u*(1-bc)>=0;

increasing k or theta adds nonnegative terms. The other coefficients
have exactly the signs in (7).

To check (8), expand its two squares. Their J-B cross coefficient is
2*beta*b*w because -a*theta*beta from the first square cancels
+a*theta*beta from -theta<Avec,B>_M in the second. Their E-B
cross contribution is -u*theta<E,B>_M. The Tcut coefficient is

    (b*w-a*theta/2)^2+a*b*mu*theta+theta^2/(4*k*mu)
                      =k*ell*mu^2+F(k,theta).

Now use (5) in the remaining u*theta<E,B>_M. Its contributions are
+a*u*theta*B0/2,-u*theta*Lambda03/2, and
-u*(1+v)*theta*Lambda04/2. Combining (3) and (4) gives precisely
every coefficient in (8). This proof divides by no matrix energy.

In particular, every full original certificate satisfies

                         Dprefix<=k*Rcut.                            (9)

## 3. The optimal constant in this three-vector relaxation

The minimizer of F(k,theta) before the upper bounds in (7) is

    theta_free(k)=2*z/(a^2+1/(k*mu)).

It always obeys theta_free<=2*k*mu*z. Thus the optimum allowed value
is

    theta_opt(k)=min(theta_free(k),U).                                (10)

For v>0 one has z>0 and k0<kold. At k=k0, even the unrestricted
minimum is strictly positive. Indeed, if Hk=a^2*k0*mu,

    min_theta F(k0,theta)/mu^2
      =b^2*(gamma-1)*(gamma+Hk)/(1+Hk)>0.                            (11)

At k=kold, its allowed minimum is strictly negative: choose any
positive theta smaller than both upper bounds and sufficiently close
to zero, and the constant term vanishes while -z*theta dominates the
positive quadratic term. For each fixed theta,

    partial F/partial k=-ell*mu^2-theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)<0.

Also (10) minimizes over the fixed interval [0,U], since the other
bound is automatic at that minimizer. Thus this minimum is continuous
and strictly decreasing in k. It follows that there is a unique

    kstar in (k0,kold), F(kstar,theta_opt(kstar))=0.                   (12)

This is an exact algebraic number, without a numerical root search.
Here are explicit branches. Define

    Bint=a^2*b^2*mu*(2*gamma-1)-ell,
    kint=(Bint+sqrt(Bint^2+4*a^2*ell*mu*b^2*gamma^2))
                                                       /(2*a^2*ell*mu).

If theta_free(kint)<=U, then kstar=kint. Otherwise define

    V0=b^2*w^2-z*U+a^2*U^2/4,
    V1=U^2/(4*mu),
    kbound=(V0+sqrt(V0^2+4*ell*mu^2*V1))/(2*ell*mu^2).

Then kstar=kbound. These are obtained by multiplying respectively
F(k,theta_free(k))=0 and F(k,U)=0 by their positive denominators.
If the free root violates the cap, the increasing theta_free remains
above U at every larger k; the boundary root is therefore the correct
one. Equality of the branch conditions gives the same root.

At v=0 with ell>0, z=U=0, gamma=1 and k0=kold=b^2/ell. Set
kstar=kold and theta_opt=0; (7)--(9) still hold. No strict gain is
claimed on this boundary.

For v>0,ell>0 the new bound is strictly stronger than the old
two-energy gap bound Dprefix<=kold*Rcut whenever Dprefix>0:

    Rcut>=Dprefix/kstar,
    Gap>= (K/kstar-ell)*Dprefix >0.                                 (13)

Thus it excludes an explicit POSITIVE gap strip, not just Gap=0.
This comparison is ONLY with the previous nested two-energy bound.
It is not a comparison with the entire older necessary system.

The constant kstar is sharp for the following explicitly delimited
relaxation: retain arbitrary PSD Gram data for (E,J,B), (3)--(5),
and nonnegative quantities B0,B1,Lambda20,Lambda03,Lambda04,
Lambda14,Lambda23, but impose no remaining original rows or quadratic
column. This sharpness does not assert a full certificate.

To prove it, work in a one-dimensional Gram space with B=1 and set
Tcut=1, B0=B1=Lambda20=Lambda03=Lambda14=Lambda23=0. Let
k=kstar,theta=theta_opt(kstar), x=b*w-a*theta/2 and J=-x/beta.
If the free branch applies, set E=0,Lambda04=0. The equation
theta=2*k*mu*(a*x-a*b*mu) follows from theta=theta_free.
Consequently both squares in (8) vanish and (5) holds.

On the capped branch put

    q04=2*(a*x-a*b*mu-theta/(2*k*mu))/(u*(1+v)),
    Lambda04=q04, E=-(1+v)*q04/2.

The condition theta=U<=theta_free implies q04>=0. Again both squares
and (5) hold, while c04=0. Define Rcut and Dprefix in this RELAXATION
by (3) and (4), rather than by the step-only values. Then Rcut>0
because ell*mu^2*Tcut>0, and Dprefix=kstar*Rcut. This proves exactly
the stated sharpness and explicitly identifies its missing matching
conditions: its energies have not been equated with the actual
step-only Rcut,Dprefix, and its remaining original array is absent.

## 4. Coupling to the actual quadratic column

For any choice (k,theta) satisfying (7), define

    rho=-F(k,theta)>=0,
    Lk=k*mu/(1+a^2*k*mu)>0,
    Zk=z-(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta/2.

The three matrix-energy terms in (8) dominate sigma*m, where

    sigma=u^2*Lk*rho/(rho+Lk*Zk^2), if rho+Lk*Zk^2>0,
    sigma=u^2*Lk,                   if rho=Zk=0.                    (14)

For the proof let X=beta*J+Btheta*B, Y=Atheta. Then
a*X+Y=u*E+Zk*B. Completing the square in X gives

    ||X||_M^2+k*mu*||Y||_M^2
                        >=Lk*||u*E+Zk*B||_M^2.

If rho+Lk*Zk^2>0, complete the square in B after adding rho||B||_M^2.
The remaining E coefficient is exactly (14). If rho=Zk=0, the
previous display is Lk*u^2*m directly. This covers singular Gram
matrices; no inverse of their entries is used. In particular sigma=0
at the strictly capped kstar branch, but sigma>0 for every k>kstar
with theta=theta_opt(k). On the free kstar branch sigma>0 already.

Combining (8) with (14) leaves the common ORIGINAL coefficient budget

    k*Rcut-Dprefix >= sigma*m+cB*(Lambda30+Lambda40)
                                            +beta*u*Lambda20.       (15)

Assume sigma>0 and define

    xi_cap=min(u/a^2, cB/(a^2*W0)).                                 (16)

If W0=0, omit the second argument of this minimum; its corresponding
incoming coefficients in (6) are both zero. This convention is used
only when that denominator is zero. The derivation itself is the
division-free condition xi*a^2*W0<=cB.

For any real xi satisfying xi<=xi_cap and xi<sigma/u, put

    Zeta=xi^2/(sigma-xi*u)>=0.

The following is a further necessary inequality of the FULL original
cone:

    k*Rcut-Dprefix >= xi*u*delta-Zeta*Q.                             (17)

To check it, subtract xi*u*delta using (6). In (15), the remaining
incoming Lambda20 coefficient is beta*u-xi*a^2*beta>=0. The two
B0 coefficients are at least cB-xi*a^2*W0>=0 if xi>=0; if xi<0
they only increase. The remaining matrix terms after adding Zeta*Q
are

    (sigma-xi*u)*||E||_M^2+2*xi<E,p>_M+Zeta*||p||_M^2
         = ||sqrt(sigma-xi*u)*E
                          +xi*p/sqrt(sigma-xi*u)||_M^2 >=0.

This proof couples the energies to the ACTUAL p in the ACTUAL M.
It is a sufficient full-space separator, not an assumption that
independently selected scalar energies possess a PSD completion.
Negative xi are intentionally allowed. They expose the opposite
first-step regime and the quadratic zero boundary.

For clarity the supremum of the right side of (17) is explicit.
Write Qplus=Q+u^2*delta. If Qplus<0, letting xi tend to -infinity
in (17) is a contradiction. Thus Qplus>=0 is necessary, in addition
to Q>=0. The exact factorization is

    Qplus=a^2*(A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2).

Thus this particular feasibility prerequisite recovers the existing
scalar-return condition Cbc|v-1|<=A; it is not counted as a new
independent obstruction. Suppose Q,Qplus>=0 and xi_cap>0.

If Q>0 and Qplus>0, set

    xi_free=(sigma/u)*(1-sqrt(Q/Qplus)).

When xi_free<=xi_cap the optimized bound is

    Bcal=(sigma/u^2)*(sqrt(Qplus)-sqrt(Q))^2.                         (18)

Otherwise xi_cap<sigma/u and the bound is

    Bcal=xi_cap*u*delta-xi_cap^2*Q/(sigma-xi_cap*u).                 (19)

If Q>0,Qplus=0, the supremum is sigma*Q/u^2, obtained as
xi tends to -infinity. If Q=0, Qplus>=0 means delta>=0, and the
supremum is

    Bcal=u*delta*min(xi_cap,sigma/u).                                (20)

For delta=Q=0 this is zero. These are limits of necessary inequalities
for every finite xi, so nonattainment of a supremum causes no problem.

The optimization follows by putting y=sigma-xi*u>0 in (17):

 xi*u*delta-xi^2*Q/(sigma-xi*u)
   =sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2
         -(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The unconstrained maximum is (18), at
y=sigma*sqrt(Q/Qplus); clipping xi above by xi_cap gives (19).
The displayed boundary formulas follow from the same expression.
The function is increasing up to its unconstrained maximum, so the
clipped value is nonnegative. In the present ell>0 domain cB>0 for
the optimizing choices used above: if v=0 then bc<1, and if v>0
the choice theta_opt>0. Hence xi_cap>0 there. Other allowed parameter
choices with cB=0 are covered by (17) without the positive-cap claim.

For every such choice with sigma>0, the final explicit test is

    Q>=0, Qplus>=0, k*Rcut-Dprefix>=Bcal.                            (21)

When v>0, Dprefix>0 and kstar<k<kold, it gives the positive-gap bound

    Gap >= (K/k-ell)*Dprefix+(K/k)*Bcal.                             (22)

The second term is strictly positive when delta!=0, provided the
displayed feasibility conditions hold. At delta=0 it is zero; no
uniform margin is inferred across that boundary.

### 4.1. Actual full quadratic-column matching on the sharp positive-gap boundary

This concerns Dprefix=kstar*Rcut>0 with v>0. It is a POSITIVE-gap
boundary, because kstar<kold and hence
Gap=(K-ell*kstar)*Rcut>0. It is not the old Gap=0 face.

Put k=kstar,theta=theta_opt(kstar), and retain Zk,Btheta from above.
Define

    rcoef=ell*mu^2+theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)>0,
    Tstar=Rcut/rcoef>0,
    Xcal=Zk^2*Tstar.

Every full original certificate on this boundary necessarily has

    B0=B1=Lambda20=Lambda03=Lambda14=Lambda23=0,
    M*(beta*J+Btheta*B)=0, M*Atheta=0,
    M*E=-(Zk/u)*M*B, M*J=-(Btheta/beta)*M*B,
    Tcut=Tstar, m=Xcal/u^2,
    Lambda04=2*Zk*Tstar/(u*(1+v)).                                  (B1)

Indeed cB,c1,beta*u,beta*b*v*c,c03new,k*c23 in (8) are all strictly
positive here. The only coefficient that may vanish is c04. For
c03new use theta<=theta_free<2*k*mu*z. With F=0, the equality
kRcut-Dprefix=0 makes both PSD energies and all positive costs vanish.
The resulting zero columns give the two linear relations in (B1).
Equation (3) then gives Rcut=rcoef*Tcut, and (5) determines Lambda04.
No division by Q or by an unknown matrix energy was made; Tstar>0
follows from the stated Dprefix>0.

On the free branch Zk=0, (B1) gives ME=0 and Lambda04=0. Equation(6)
now forces delta=0, so a=sqrt(2)-1. Thus arbitrary scalar choices of
a on the free relaxation equality ray cannot be completed to a full
array, irrespective of how the remaining covariance is chosen.

On the strictly capped branch Zk>0, the ENTIRE quadratic cross column
in the basis of Section5 is fixed by (B1) and (6):

    qB:=<B,p>_M=(u^2*delta-Xcal)/(2*Zk),
    <E,p>_M=-(Zk/u)*qB,
    <J,p>_M=-(Btheta/beta)*qB,
    ||p||_M^2=Q.                                                   (B2)

Consequently full PSD on this boundary requires the STEP-ONLY test

                                   <= (sqrt(Qplus)+sqrt(Q))^2.     (B4)

evidence:
# Incompatible mode orderings: a strict joint price and a complete redundancy theorem

Status: UNVERIFIED complete joint proof draft, max2 round25, under
TASK.md and master_guidance6e0a18d700dcd62f. No numerical/model evaluation,
solver, replay, installation, subordinate agent, or fact_submit was used.
The verifier gate remains closed. This document is not a fact.

Accepted inputs: 04219554e41d9750, Section10 (the original primitive
identity on the full formal gradient space), and1252b8823bb5a290,
proof paragraphs1--2 (the interpolation convention and its constructive
sufficiency). All other mathematics used here is proved jointly below.
Previous max2 value-price and monotone drafts are awareness, not premises.

The result addresses an actually incompatible-order family. One matched
quadratic mode reverses at the first step and is annihilated at the second;
any number of slower matched modes remain nonnegative and monotone.
The exact joint price is STRICTLY larger than the sum of the separate
mode prices in the nondegenerate case. Nevertheless the complete
parameter-and-value family supplies NO additional primitive obstruction
when the first step is at most2 and the old prefix-step bounds hold.
In particular there is no need to mistake its positive coupling price
for information beyond the separate scalar tests.

Section8 extends the complete comparison to a reversal at ANY index j,
provided the fast mode is nonnegative before j and is annihilated at j+1.
For arbitrary1<=b=h_(j+1)<=r=h_j, joint pricing is exactly redundant
relative to the separate fast-mode test and the old prefix-step bounds.
If b<=2, that separate fast test is itself already nonnegative under
the old prefix-step bounds. This extension includes middle reversals;
the initial-reversal theorem is not the final scope of the result.

The arbitrary four-step full cone, modes that continue oscillating after
their first sign reversal, delayed annihilation chronologies, planar fractional
repairs, the complementary C82 comparison, and the original all-schedule
exact-profile target remain open. No global no-seed assertion is made.

## 1. Precise family and the claimed all-value minimum

Let n>=2 and let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be any finite nonnegative word with

    h_0=r, h_1=b, 1<=b<=r<=2,
    P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, s=P_n, C=1+s,
    h_i<=P_i+2 for every i<n.                         (1)

There is no capacity cap and no bound on the number or total mass of tail
steps. The result applies at n=4 with all five original gradient indices.
Set beta=1/b and m=r/b-1>=0. Choose an integer d>=1, amplitudes
u_1,...,u_d,v>=0, and fixed curvatures satisfying

    0<alpha_q<beta, h_i*alpha_q<=1 for every i,q.

Define p_(0,q)=1, p_(i,q)=product_(t<i)(1-alpha_q*h_t), and the fast
position factors z_0=1, z_1=-m, z_i=0 for2<=i<=n. The actual points and
gradients in R^(d+1) are

    x_i=(u_q*p_(i,q) for1<=q<=d, v*z_i),
    g_i=(alpha_q*u_q*p_(i,q) for1<=q<=d, beta*v*z_i). (2)

They obey every GD update, including the second update because b*beta=1.
They are initially the samples of the ONE quadratic

    F_base(x)=sum_q alpha_q*x_q^2/2+beta*x_(d+1)^2/2.

No time-dependent Hessian is used. Each slow coordinate is nonnegative
and nonincreasing. If b<r and v>0, the fast sampled gradients really
change sign: positive at0, negative at1, zero from2 onwards.

Put

    U_q=alpha_q*(1-alpha_q)*u_q^2/2,
    B=beta*(1-beta)*v^2/2,
    A=sum_q U_q*(p_(1,q)-p_(2,q))*(1-p_(1,q)),
    X25=4r*A, Y25=4r*B*m*(1+m).                         (3)

For slow gradients a_(i,q)=alpha_q*u_q*p_(i,q), write
t_(i,q)=a_(i,q)-a_(i+1,q). Define

    L_slow=sum_(q,i<n) P_(i+1)*t_(i,q)
               *[2(1+P_i)*a_(i,q)-P_(i+1)*t_(i,q)],
    H_fast=beta^2*v^2*[r(2-r)+b(2-b)*m^2].           (4)

Among ALL scalar values on the fixed geometry(2) satisfying ALL directed
finite interpolation inequalities, the exact minimum primitive energy is

    V_min=L_slow+H_fast-min(X25,Y25).                    (5)

The minimum is attained by a single everywhere-defined convex
differentiable function with1-Lipschitz gradient and actual minimizers.
Requiring the actual optimum jet(0,0,0) does not change this minimum.
The explicit values, static function, and true distance are in Section6.

The decisive full-family comparison is

    V_min >= r*(2-r)*[beta^2*v^2
                            +r*sum_q alpha_q^3*u_q^2] >=0. (6)

In fact it is strictly positive whenever r<2 and the initial vector is nonzero.
The bound is uniform over every curvature and amplitude allowed above,
all tail steps satisfying(1), and all legal values, including values of
nonseparable functions. Thus minimization over the ENTIRE stated family
cannot reject any word passing(1). It is not just a comparison at one
chosen amplitude or at unoptimized values.

For an interior two-mode instance with1<b<r, v,u_1>0, and
0<alpha_1<1/max_i h_i, both X25 and Y25 are positive. The exact joint
price gain min(X25,Y25)>0 is then a concrete strict failure of additivity.
Sections4--5 prove why that failure still gives no new obstruction here.

## 2. Original primitive orientation and all-value optimization

Retain every index I={0,...,n}. For any values f_i define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V(f)=2sum_(i<n)h_i*(f_i-f_n)
          +sum_(i<n)h_i*(1-h_i)*||g_i||^2-sC*||g_n||^2.

For a nonnegative original finite multiplier array Lambda with zero
diagonal put e=(1,...,1)^T, L=diag(Lambda*e)-Lambda, and

    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(n-1),2s)^T,
    T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
    D=diag(h_i*(2-h_i) for i<n, -s*(s+2)).

The original conditions are

    L^T*e=omega, M=D+(L*T+T^T*L^T)/2 PSD on R^(n+1).

Accepted04219554e41d9750 gives the identity

    V(f)+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij*Q_ij
        =<M,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>.                      (7)

Here omega is OUTGOING minus incoming flow. The terminal index n is the
source of mass2s; each i<n is a sink of mass2h_i. All ordered pairs and
the full formal gradient space remain in this interface. No equality of
formal coordinates at a zero step is imposed on the certificate.

The quadratic base values f_i^0=F_base(x_i) have symmetric nonnegative
slack costs

    w_ij=-Q_ij^0
         =sum_q U_q*(p_(i,q)-p_(j,q))^2+B*(z_i-z_j)^2. (8)

Let d_i be the shortest cost of a directed path n->i in the complete
finite graph with costs(8). Nonnegative costs imply that a shortest
simple path exists, even with zero costs and repeated points.

Replacement values f_i^0+delta_i are legal exactly when
delta_i-delta_j<=w_ij. Every n->i path implies
delta_i-delta_n>=-d_i. Since h_i>=0,

    min_f V(f)=V(f^0)-2sum_(i<n)h_i*d_i.              (9)

The choice delta_i=-d_i attains all these bounds at once: shortest
distances obey d_j<=d_i+w_ij, which is precisely its feasibility.
This proves EVERY directed inequality, not only an adjacent subset.

The same improvement is the exact minimum ORIGINAL slack-flow price.
For any original prescribed flow, w_ij>=d_j-d_i gives

    sum Lambda_ij*w_ij >= -sum_i omega_i*d_i
                           =2sum_(i<n)h_i*d_i.

Sending2h_i along one shortest n->i path for each positive sink h_i
attains equality and satisfies the exact original flow equation.
These auxiliary optimizing flows are not claimed to make M PSD.

## 3. All shortest paths in the incompatible-order geometry

For a scalar ordered list p_0>=...>=p_n and edge costs U*(p_i-p_j)^2,
the distance from n to i is

    U*sum_(k=i)^(n-1)(p_k-p_(k+1))^2.                 (10)

For a proof, an edge crossing several intervening ordered gaps has
cost U*(sum gaps)^2 >= U*sum gaps^2. Every path from p_n to p_i must
cross each gap between them at least once. Summing these lower bounds
over its edges proves(10); the adjacent ordered path attains it. Ties
have zero gap and do not change the argument.

In the isolated fast scalar coordinate, the source position is0, and
the only other positions are1 and-m. The shortest distances are B to0,
B*m^2 to1, and0 to indices>=2: a detour from0 through the opposite-sign
position only adds a nonnegative cost. Define the summed separate-mode
distances

    d_i^sep=sum_q U_q*sum_(k=i)^(n-1)
                          (p_(k,q)-p_(k+1,q))^2
             +B*1_(i=0)+B*m^2*1_(i=1).             (11)

Any joint path has cost at least the sum of these separate minima.
For every i>=1 the chronological path n,n-1,...,i attains(11), including
the fast coordinate. Consequently

    d_i=d_i^sep for1<=i<=n.                          (12)

To reach0, a shortest simple path has a last predecessor j>=1. For j>=2
the best such choice is j=2. Indeed the high coordinate is0 at all these
indices; in each slow coordinate, inserting the intermediate decreasing
points j-1,...,2 into the last edge j->0 weakly decreases squared cost.
For a direct algebraic check, if Delta_k=p_k-p_(k+1)>=0, then

    (1-p_j)^2-(1-p_2)^2
      =2(1-p_2)*sum_(k=2)^(j-1)Delta_k
           +(sum_(k=2)^(j-1)Delta_k)^2
      >=sum_(k=2)^(j-1)Delta_k^2.

Thus it remains to compare exactly two paths: n,...,2,0 and n,...,2,1,0.
Their costs are, respectively,

    d_0^sep+2A,  d_0^sep+2B*m*(1+m).

The first expression uses
(1-p_2)^2-(1-p_1)^2-(p_1-p_2)^2
=2(1-p_1)*(p_1-p_2). The second uses
m^2+(1+m)^2-1=2m(1+m). Therefore

    d_0=d_0^sep+2min(A,B*m*(1+m)).                   (13)

This checks every possible path, without assuming that arbitrary
modewise optimal paths can be combined. Equations(9),(12),(13) show
that the joint price exceeds the sum of the separate prices by EXACTLY

    4r*min(A,B*m*(1+m))=min(X25,Y25).                    (14)

An explicit attaining original flow is also available. If the path
through1 is cheaper, take Lambda_(k+1,k)=2P_(k+1) for0<=k<n and all
other entries zero. If the bypass is cheaper, take

    Lambda_20=2r, Lambda_21=2b, Lambda_10=0,
    Lambda_(k+1,k)=2P_(k+1) for2<=k<n,

with every other entry zero. At equality either flow, or any convex
combination, attains the minimum. Both are nonnegative and have exact
terminal-source flow. They are auxiliary flows, not full PSD certificates.

## 4. The exact separate energies and their sum

Consider one slow coordinate and abbreviate its gradients by a_i and
decrements by t_i=a_i-a_(i+1). Its ordered shortest paths make every
reverse adjacent inequality tight at the optimized values:

    f_i-f_(i+1)=h_i*a_i*a_(i+1)+t_i^2/2.

Substitution into V gives the corresponding summand L_q in(4).
Here is a telescoping audit independent of any previous monotone draft.
The value term becomes sum_i[2P_(i+1)*h_i*a_i*a_(i+1)
+P_(i+1)*t_i^2]. After writing a_(i+1)=a_i-t_i, the coefficient of a_i^2
is h_i*(1+2P_i+h_i), which equals
P_(i+1)*(P_(i+1)+1)-P_i*(P_i+1). Subtracting sC*a_n^2 telescopes it
to sum_i P_(i+1)*(P_(i+1)+1)*(2a_i*t_i-t_i^2).
The remaining terms reduce exactly to

    L_q=sum_i P_(i+1)*t_i*
                 [2(1+P_i)*a_i-P_(i+1)*t_i].        (15)

This derivation proves the exact minimum for a scalar slow mode, because
the distance potentials already satisfy all its nonadjacent inequalities.

For the fast coordinate, the optimized values, with its zero terminal
value, are beta^2*v^2/2 at0 and beta^2*v^2*m^2/2 at1, zero thereafter.
Indeed they are the quadratic base values minus B and B*m^2. Their
exact primitive energy is H_fast in(4).

They are also attained by the explicit one-dimensional function

    F_fast(t)=dist(t,J)^2/2,
    J=[-(1-beta)*v*m, (1-beta)*v].                   (16)

The derivative is t minus its projection onto the interval J; it is
nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz. At v,-v*m,0 it has exactly the stated
gradients and values, and J is its actual full minimizer set.

The base primitive energy is a sum of coordinate energies. Applying
the exact improvement(14) to their separate all-value minima proves(5).
The minimizing JOINT values need not be values of the separable sum of
the coordinate interpolants. Section6 constructs their actual joint
function; no incompatible scalar value assignments are silently glued.

## 5. Full parameter comparison: the coupling gain is absorbed

The prefix bounds in(1) imply nonnegativity of EVERY slow summand in(15).
Indeed 0<=t_i<=a_i and

    2(1+P_i)*a_i-P_(i+1)*t_i
        >=(P_i+2-h_i)*a_i>=0.                       (17)

The FIRST TWO summands cover the entire possible coupling charge. Since
p_1=1-r*alpha and p_2=(1-b*alpha)*p_1, the coordinate contribution X25_q to X25 is

    X25_q=2r^2*b*alpha^3*(1-alpha)*(1-r*alpha)*u^2.

Let l=1-r*alpha in[0,1] and set

    D_b=b*(r+b)/r, A_b=2+2r-D_b.

Since b<=r, D_b<=2r and A_b>=2. The first two summands in L_q,
after dividing by alpha^3*u^2 when u>0, are

    r^2*(2-r^2*alpha)
      +b*(r+b)*l^2*[2(1+r)-b*(r+b)*alpha].

Subtract X25_q/(alpha^3*u^2)=2r^2*b*(1-alpha)*l and use
alpha=(1-l)/r. The resulting EXACT polynomial is

    Delt_q(l)=r^2*(2-r)
       +r*[r^2-2b*(r-1)]*l
       +[b*(r+b)*A_b-2r*b]*l^2
       +[b^2*(r+b)^2/r]*l^3.                       (18)

Every coefficient is nonnegative. The linear coefficient is at least
r^2*(2-r), since b<=r and r>=1. The quadratic coefficient is at least
2b^2, since A_b>=2. The cubic coefficient is positive. In particular

    Delt_q(l)>=r^2*(2-r)*(1+l)+2b^2*l^2>=r^2*(2-r).

If u=0, the same comparison holds after multiplying through by
alpha^3*u^2, without division. All later summands of L_q are
nonnegative by(17). Summing over the slow modes gives

    L_slow>=X25+r^2*(2-r)*sum_q alpha_q^3*u_q^2.      (19)

Meanwhile1<=b<=r<=2 gives

    H_fast>=beta^2*v^2*r*(2-r)>=0.                  (20)

Finally min(X25,Y25)<=X25. Inserting(19)--(20) into the EXACT formula(5)
proves(6). The slow modes alone cover the entire potential coupling
gain; the fast mode contributes a nonnegative remaining energy.
Neither the amplitudes nor the curvatures nor the values remain to be
optimized to decide the sign. The comparison works on the WHOLE range
r<=2 supplied by the first prefix-step bound, not only near one word.

## 6. One static attaining function, actual optimum and true radius

Append the optimum index star with x_star=g_star=f_star=0 to the graph.
Its direct distance from n is

    d_star=D_star=sum_q U_q*p_(n,q)^2.               (22)

This is a shortest path: in every slow coordinate, all finite positions
are at least the terminal position, and there is no finite position
strictly between zero and that terminal position. Formula(10), with
zero inserted at the end, gives a lower bound U_q*p_(n,q)^2 in that
coordinate. The fast coordinate is zero at both endpoints. The direct
arc attains the sum of these lower bounds.

Adding star cannot shorten a finite distance. For every finite j,

    w_(n,j)=D_star+w_(star,j)
                    -2sum_q U_q*p_(n,q)*p_(j,q)
             <=D_star+w_(star,j).

In a path passing through star, its prefix to star has cost at least
D_star. Replace that prefix and its following arc star->j by n->j.
The displayed inequality never increases the cost. Thus the finite
distances remain exactly(12)--(13), and the fixed-optimum price equals
the original finite-flow price, without adding optimum multipliers to(7).

The actual attaining values are now explicit:

    f_i=f_i^0+D_star-d_i, f_star=0.                  (23)

For every ordered pair among the finite and optimum indices, the change
of values is a distance potential. Hence all Q_ij<=0 follow from the
distance inequalities as in Section2, including both directions and
every coincident-point pair.

Let y_i=x_i-g_i, eta_i=||g_i||^2/2-f_i, including y_star=eta_star=0.
Define on R^(d+1)

    H(w)=||w||^2/2+max_i(<y_i,w>+eta_i),
    F(x)=sup_w(<x,w>-H(w)).                         (24)

This is the constructive interpolation form of accepted1252b8823bb5a290.
For completeness, H is finite, continuous,1-strongly convex and has
quadratic growth. There is a unique maximizing w(x) for every x.
The two strong subgradient inequalities imply
<x-x',w(x)-w(x')>>=||w(x)-w(x')||^2. The two maximizing inequalities
then give a differentiability remainder bounded by||x-x'||^2, proving
that F is convex differentiable with gradient w(x) and1-Lipschitz
gradient. The Q inequalities make the i-th branch of H active at g_i,
with subgradient x_i. Thus grad F(x_i)=g_i and F(x_i)=f_i. This is ONE
fixed global F realizing every step of(2), not a sequence of local jets.

The exact minimizer set is

    K_min=conv{y_i:eta_i=0}, min F=0.                (25)

Indeed eta_i<=0 by the optimum inequalities, and eta_star=0. A point x
minimizes F exactly when grad F(x)=0, equivalently x belongs to the
subgradient set of H at0. This set is exactly the convex hull of the
active slopes y_i. To verify the latter equality, a convex combination
of active slopes gives the subgradient inequality directly. For a point
outside that hull, a separating direction and a sufficiently small
positive displacement keep inactive affine branches inactive and
contradict the subgradient inequality. This proves both inclusions.

In particular a real optimum always exists and the TRUE radius is

    R_true=dist(x_0,K_min),                          (26)

with the displayed finite convex hull, not an assumed normalization.
The point x_0 has nonzero gradient whenever some amplitude is positive,
so it is outside K_min and this radius is positive.

There is a simpler exact radius in the generic sign-changing family.
The direct arc bound d_i<=w_(n,i) gives

    eta_i<=-2sum_q U_q*p_(i,q)*p_(n,q).

If any active slow mode has p_(n,q)>0, this is STRICTLY negative at
every finite sample. Therefore K_min={0} and

    R_true^2=sum_q u_q^2+v^2.                       (27)

The entire open family with strict h_i*alpha_q<1 has this property.

For an explicit terminal-zero boundary, take one active slow mode,
u>0, alpha*r<1, and let k>=3 be its first zero index. Put j=k-1.
Then the slow positions are positive through j and zero afterwards;
the fast coordinate has already vanished. The active slopes in(25)
are0 and ((1-alpha)*u*p_j,0), including any repeated copies caused by
zero steps before the killing step. Earlier distinct positions have
strictly smaller eta because their monotone distance path has at least
one intermediate positive position; in particular the path via j
strictly improves their direct squared cost. Hence

    K_min=[0,(1-alpha)*u*p_j] x {0},
    R_true^2=(u-(1-alpha)*u*p_j)^2+v^2.              (28)

For other degenerate amplitude patterns, (25)--(26) already specify
the complete minimizer set and exact true distance without a false
uniqueness assertion. In particular, if every slow amplitude vanishes,
(16) supplies the full fast minimizer interval directly, with closest
distance beta*v from its initial point v.

## 7. Boundaries, scalar-cut comparison, and initial-reversal scope

All formulas allow b=1 (unit fast curvature, B=0), r=b (no fast
reversal, m=0), vanishing amplitudes, zero tail steps, and slow products
that first hit zero. Then the corresponding price increment is zero
when dictated by(3); no positive-price claim is retained at a collapsed
boundary. Repeated positions have identical gradients and values by
(2),(8),(23). The optimum graph retains them as separate indices.

Arbitrary additional zero steps can also be inserted anywhere into the
physical word, with all duplicate samples retained. Compression here
is only a description of this actual witness: its positions, gradients,
values, sums, energy, and price do not change. Lift each displayed path
through the zero-cost duplicates, keeping sinks of weight zero if
needed. No compression, quotient, or equality is imposed on the formal
M in(7). At n=4 its ambient space is still all of R^5.

The prefix-step hypothesis in(1) is already weaker than the old actual
single-cut necessary conditions. Here is the complete relevant
reconstruction. For any cut j with h_j>1, put
P=P_j, T=sum_(i>j)h_i, eta=(h_j-1)/(1+T). Use the scalar function

    F_cut(x)=max_(g in[-eta,1]) (x*g-g^2/2)

and x_0=1+P. Before the cut, the gradient is1 and x_j=1. Immediately
afterwards x_(j+1)=-(1+T)*eta; throughout the tail the gradient is-eta,
with x_n=-eta. The derivative is projection onto[-eta,1], so the
function is convex differentiable and1-smooth. Its unique minimizer
is0: the interval contains both a positive and a negative number,
and testing a sufficiently small number of the sign of x makes F_cut(x)>0
for x!=0. Direct insertion of F_cut(x)=x*g-g^2/2 and these two constant
gradient blocks into V yields

    V_cut=(1+P)^2-C^2*((h_j-1)/(1+T))^2.

Thus a full certificate in(7) requires

    C*(h_j-1)<=(1+P)*(1+T).                         (29)

Writing U=1+P and R=1+T gives C=U+R+(h_j-1). If h_j>=P+2, then
h_j-1>=U and C*(h_j-1)>=C*U>R*U, contrary to(29).
Hence every positive step passing(29) satisfies h_j<P_j+2; a step at
most1 satisfies that inequality directly. This proves the comparison
to previously available conditions, without importing an unverified
monotone or cut draft.

For four-step words with 1<=h_1<=h_0<=2, the theorem covers every
fast mode beta=1/h_1 and every collection of slow eigenmodes satisfying
alpha_q*h_i<=1. It is independent of C and so remains valid throughout
the threshold C>=193/25. The old first-cut condition itself forces
h_0<2, so no stronger compact-domain bound or auxiliary draft is needed.
The family still imposes h_1<=h_0 and annihilation at the second step. No claim is
made for the other initial ordering or a fast mode that survives.

The exact information gain is therefore a SCOPED CLOSURE: even genuinely
incompatible spatial orderings and a strictly positive all-value joint
price do not strengthen the old conditions in this entire stated family.
It does not exclude a new remaining h-region, construct any full Lambda,
or establish feasibility of any full PSD certificate. Excluding a witness
family is not a seed, and even excluding every four-step seed would only
close the sufficient negative route of04219554e41d9750, not settle the
original affirmative minimax target.

Literature grounding: Matlas returned1910.01845 Theorem5, the standard
smooth-convex interpolation equivalence, rather than a result about
competing mode orders. Web search recovered Taylor--Hendrickx--Glineur,
arXiv1502.05666. The exact primary PDF was downloaded locally and its
Theorem4 proof, constructive Remark2, Corollary1 and cycle Remark3 were
read. These concern all directed interpolation inequalities; they do not
assert separability or common modewise shortest paths. No new external
result is imported as a premise beyond accepted1252b8823bb5a290.

## 8. General single reversal followed immediately by annihilation

This section extends the complete theorem rather than importing another
draft. Keep an arbitrary nonnegative word and all old prefix bounds
h_i<=P_i+2. Choose0<=j<=n-2 and write

    P=P_j, r=h_j, b=h_(j+1),
    1<=b<=r, H_j=P+r, beta=1/b,
    h_i<=b for i<j.                                (30)

The last hypothesis makes the fast quadratic trajectory nonnegative up
to j. Its position factors are

    t_i=product_(k<i)(1-beta*h_k) for i<=j,
    t_(j+1)=-m*t_j, m=r/b-1,
    t_i=0 for i>=j+2.

Use any number of slower modes with0<alpha_q<beta and
alpha_q*h_i<=1 for every i. Their positions and gradients are still
u_q*p_(i,q) and alpha_q*u_q*p_(i,q). The fast position and gradient
are v*t_i and beta*v*t_i. These are samples of ONE fixed diagonal
quadratic before values are re-selected. A genuine sign reversal
requires r>b, v>0, t_j>0; every degenerate boundary remains allowed.

Set U_q and B as in(3), and now define

    A_j=sum_q U_q*(p_(j,q)-p_(j+1,q))
                         *(p_(j+1,q)-p_(j+2,q)),
    X25_j=4H_j*A_j,
    Y25_j=4H_j*B*t_j^2*m*(1+m).                     (31)

Let a_i^f=beta*v*t_i for i<=j and let

    E_pref=sum_(i<j) P_(i+1)*(a_i^f-a_(i+1)^f)
              *[2(1+P_i)*a_i^f
                          -P_(i+1)*(a_i^f-a_(i+1)^f)],
    K_j=(1+P)^2-(r-1)^2+b*(2-b)*m^2,
    H_fast,j=E_pref+K_j*(a_j^f)^2.                  (32)

Then the exact all-value minimum is

    V_min=L_slow+H_fast,j-min(X25_j,Y25_j),          (33)

and the COMPLETE coupling comparison is

    L_slow>=X25_j,
    V_min>=H_fast,j.                               (34)

Therefore, for this fixed word and fast curvature, nonnegativity over
ALL the displayed slow curvatures, amplitudes and legal joint values
is EQUIVALENT to nonnegativity of the separate fast scalar minimum
H_fast,j. One implication is(34); for the other set every slow amplitude
to zero. This is an exact redundancy theorem, not a bare new condition
with an unresolved joint sign. The scalar fast test can still be useful;
adding monotone slow modes and all their joint value freedom cannot
strengthen it in this entire family.

If additionally b<=2, then

    H_fast,j>=0                                    (35)

already follows from the old prefix bounds. Thus the WHOLE family,
including its fast scalar part, is redundant under the old cuts in
this subcase. No condition r<=2 is needed at a later reversal: the old
bound here is r<=P+2.

### 8.1 Exact shortest distances and the attainable price

The isolated slow distances are still(10). The isolated fast distances
from the zero terminal position are

    d_i^f=B*[t_j^2+sum_(k=i)^(j-1)(t_k-t_(k+1))^2] for i<=j,
    d_(j+1)^f=B*m^2*t_j^2,
    d_i^f=0 for i>=j+2.                             (36)

To prove these expressions, insert the source0 into the sorted scalar
list. The positive prefix t_0>=...>=t_j>=0 is on one side of0; the
single negative value-m*t_j is on the other side. The ordered-gap proof
of(10) applies on each side, and detouring through the opposite side
adds a nonnegative cost. This includes zero products and ties.

Write d_i^sep for the sum of(36) and all slow scalar distances. For
i>=j+1 the chronological path n,...,i attains this sum, so the joint
distance equals d_i^sep. For each i<=j, there are exactly two relevant
paths: the chronological path, and the chronological path that bypasses
the single vertex j+1. Their costs are

    d_i^sep+2B*t_j^2*m*(1+m),
    d_i^sep+2A_j.                                  (37)

Here is an all-directed-pair proof that no omitted path can be shorter.
Set delta=2min(A_j,B*t_j^2*m*(1+m)). Propose distances d_i^sep+delta
on i<=j, and d_i^sep on i>=j+1. Sums of the separate scalar distance
potentials always obey d_i^sep-d_k^sep<=w_(k,i), since each scalar
potential obeys its own distance inequality and the edge costs add.

Within either index group, the proposed constant shift cancels. From
a prefix index to a later index, it makes the distance inequality
weaker. Only inequalities bounding a prefix distance by a later
distance plus an edge need checking. For i<=j and k>=j+1, the scaled
position of k is coordinatewise at most that of j, and the positions
of j,j-1,...,i are coordinatewise nondecreasing. Expanding the sums of
nonnegative coordinate gaps gives

    w_(k,i)>=w_(k,j)+sum_(l=i)^(j-1)w_(l+1,l),
    d_i^sep=d_j^sep+sum_(l=i)^(j-1)w_(l+1,l).

Thus it suffices to check the target i=j. For k=j+1 the exact slack
is d_(j+1)^sep+w_(j+1,j)-d_j^sep=2B*t_j^2*m*(1+m).
For k>=j+2, insert the coordinatewise ordered tail indices k-1,...,j+2
into the edge k->j. The gap-square inequality in Section3 gives

    d_k^sep+w_(k,j)>=d_(j+2)^sep+w_(j+2,j)
                         =d_j^sep+2A_j.

Both lower bounds are at least delta, by its definition. Every directed
distance inequality is now checked, including those that could have
used an extra tail vertex after the negative sample. Summing these
inequalities along any path from n proves that its cost is at least
the proposed terminal-to-target distance. The paths(37) attain that
distance, proving exactly

    d_i=d_i^sep+2min(A_j,B*t_j^2*m*(1+m)) for i<=j. (38)

Multiplying this common increment by2sum_(i<=j)h_i=2H_j yields the
exact original-flow price gain min(X25_j,Y25_j). An attaining flow
sends each prefix sink along its cheaper path in(37), and each later
sink along its chronological path. Both complete choices have the
original terminal-source flow, all nonnegative entries, and all
zero-weight vertices retained. Again no PSD property is asserted for
these auxiliary flows.

### 8.2 Exact separate fast energy

The all-value fast minimum has terminal value0, value(a_j^f)^2/2 at j,
value(m*a_j^f)^2/2 at j+1, and zero values afterwards. For i<j its
successive value differences satisfy the tight ordered relation

    f_i^f-f_(i+1)^f
      =h_i*a_i^f*a_(i+1)^f+(a_i^f-a_(i+1)^f)^2/2.

These are precisely the quadratic base values minus the distances(36),
so they satisfy EVERY scalar pair. The first j steps have primitive
energy E_pref by the complete derivation(15). Expanding the remaining
two steps, while retaining the weights on f_j from all earlier steps,
adds

    [P(P+1)+(P+r)+r(1-r)]*(a_j^f)^2
                       +b(2-b)*m^2*(a_j^f)^2
      =[(1+P)^2-(r-1)^2+b(2-b)*m^2]*(a_j^f)^2.

This proves(32) as an exact all-value scalar minimum. Subtracting the
joint price gain just computed proves(33).

### 8.3 The complete slow-mode budget at an arbitrary reversal

Fix one slow mode alpha,u and set l=1-r*alpha in[0,1]. All its energy
terms outside j,j+1 are nonnegative by(17). With H=H_j=P+r and

    A_jb=2(1+P+r)-b*(H+b)/r,

the two terms at j,j+1 minus their contribution to X25_j, after
removing the nonnegative factor alpha^3*u^2*p_j^2, equal

    H*r*(P+2-r)
      +H*[r*H-2b*(r-1)]*l
      +[b*(H+b)*A_jb-2H*b]*l^2
      +[b^2*(H+b)^2/r]*l^3.                       (39)

This identity follows by substituting alpha=(1-l)/r into

    H*r*[2(1+P)-H*r*alpha]
      +(H+b)*b*l^2*[2(1+P+r)-(H+b)*b*alpha]
      -2H*r*b*(1-alpha)*l.

It remains valid when the removed factor is zero by multiplying back;
no division by a vanished trajectory value is used in the conclusion.
All coefficients in(39) are nonnegative:

* The constant is nonnegative because r<=P+2.
* The linear coefficient is at least H*r*(P+2-r), because1<=b<=r.
* Since b<=r, A_jb>=2+P+r-b>=P+2. The quadratic coefficient is at
  least b*[P*H+b*(P+2)]>=0.
* The cubic coefficient is positive.

Thus these two slow terms alone cover the whole possible bypass price
X25_j. Summation proves the first assertion in(34), and (33) gives the
second. This is the full comparison, including arbitrary slow amplitudes
and any number of slow modes. It does not rely on a shared scalar
ordering at the exceptional negative vertex.

Finally E_pref>=0 by(17), applied to the nonnegative fast prefix, using
beta*h_i<=1 for i<j. If b<=2, b(2-b)>=0; and r<=P+2 with r>=1 implies
(r-1)^2<=(P+1)^2. Every term in(32) is then nonnegative, proving(35).

### 8.4 Attainment, boundaries and the four-step consequence

Use the distances(36)--(38) and the quadratic base on the generalized
geometry. The fixed optimum0 still cannot shorten a finite distance:
all slow positions are at least their terminal positions, the fast
terminal coordinate is0, and the exact argument(22)--(23) is unchanged.
Consequently the values(23), with these new distances, satisfy all
finite and optimum directed inequalities and attain(33).

The single static conjugate function(24), its COMPLETE actual minimizer
set(25), and its TRUE radius(26) apply verbatim with the new jets. If
at least one active slow mode survives to the terminal, (27) still
gives the unique optimum0 and true squared distance sum u_q^2+v^2.
Otherwise (25)--(26) retain every active slope and do not assert a
false unique minimizer or transfer the special segment formula(28)
outside its stated initial-reversal setting.

All coincident points, zero step indices, zero products, b=1, r=b,
and vanishing amplitudes are retained as in Section7. Strict price
gain occurs whenever the two quantities in(31) are both positive;
that positivity does not imply a new primitive obstruction, by(34).

For a four-step word this covers j=0,1,2 whenever the explicit prefix
order h_i<=h_(j+1) for i<j holds and h_j>=h_(j+1)>=1. The fast
curvature is the actual reciprocal1/h_(j+1), not a fitted sequence of
Hessians. Under the old cuts, every killing step at most2 gives the
complete redundancy(35). If the killing step exceeds2, the possible
new information is exactly the ONE separate fast scalar test(32);
coupling it with all allowed monotone modes and optimizing ALL values
does not strengthen it. This conclusion is uniform in C, including
the remaining threshold C>=193/25, with all original h,Lambda,flow and
ambient R^5 PSD coordinates preserved.

The general case of a fast mode which remains nonzero after its first
sign reversal, or has multiple sign reversals, is not covered. The
original target remains open. All new conclusions in this whole
document remain UNVERIFIED joint drafts.

# C96: persistent outer gates with an exact transverse cost

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED DRAFT, not a fact-graph result. Formal
verification is forbidden by the current allocation. The original target is
OPEN. This is the second and last allocated round (completed ceiling 27).

Accepted sources used: b98bb807d514e80d (single-cut and Huber bounds),
1fca3e5dd555cb4a (ray feasibility and objective), e9a55f57461f253c (the
stronger fixed H6 reference), and 04219554e41d9750 (the unconditional
original-denominator limit Z_1). No conditional seed from the last fact is
assumed. C93--C95 are motivation, never proof premises. All new assertions
used in this draft are proved together below.

## 1. Static model, physical word, and parameters

Fix an integer m>=6. Put lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda*(1+1/m),
beta=1-1/m, a=beta/c, and ell=1+a. Define H_0=() and

    H_(k+1)=(H_k,1+a*c^k,H_k), 0<=k<m.

Every subword uses these SAME enclosing-m parameters. Let

    j=2^(m-1)-1, n=2^m-1, P=sum H_(m-1),
    r=a*c^(m-1), b=1+r, d=1/(P+1), sigma=r*d/(2P+1),
    Kcut=r^2*d^2/(2P+1),
    p=12/13, q=5/13, rho=q^2/p^2=25/144,
    kappa=1/ell, J=1+rho*ell, w=1/(2p^2)=169/288.

The symbol Kcut is the accepted central single-cut value on this exact word;
it is not the entire worst-case functional W_n and need not equal the Huber
value. Choose dimensionless constants

    0<epsilon<=1/4, |eta|<=1/4.

For positive Rminus,Rplus define phi(0)=0 and
phi'(s)=clip(s,[-Rminus,Rplus]). Explicitly phi(s)=s^2/2 in the core,
phi(s)=Rplus*s-Rplus^2/2 on the positive outer interval, and
phi(s)=-Rminus*s-Rminus^2/2 on the negative outer interval.

Use u_+=(p,q), u_-=(p,-q), positive radii

    Rplus_+=p*d*(1+epsilon), Rplus_-=p*d*(1-epsilon),
    Rminus_+=p*sigma*(1+eta), Rminus_-=p*sigma*(1-eta),

and the corresponding two functions phi_+,phi_-. Define ONE static function

    F(x,y)=kappa*y^2/2+w*phi_+(p*x+q*y)+w*phi_-(p*x-q*y).

Run actual GD from X_0=(1,0) using L=1 and exactly the word H_m. There is
no objective switch, stepsize adaptation, or local curvature rescaling.

## 2. Global legality and the actual minimizer

The useful uniform parameter bounds are

    2/7<a<sqrt(2)-1<1/2, 9/7<ell<3/2,

## 3. Exact prefix and its central queried gate

Write X_i=(x_i,y_i). Put

    delta=epsilon*p*d, zeta=eta*p*sigma,
    y_plus=-epsilon*(q/p)*d*ell,
    y_minus=eta*(q/p)*sigma*ell,
    Lcut=epsilon*d*J/2.

As long as both ridges are in the positive outer intervals, the gradient is

    grad F=(d,kappa*y+delta*q/p^2).

The FIRST physical step is ell=1/kappa. It sends y_0=0 exactly to y_plus,
the stationary value of this affine scalar recursion. Every subsequent
step preserves y_plus until a ridge changes gate, irrespective of its size.
The proposed prefix is therefore

    x_i=1-d*sum_(t<i) h_t,
    y_0=0, y_i=y_plus for 1<=i<=j.                 (C96.2)

Here is an induction validating every proposed gate, rather than assuming
the affine formula remains applicable. At i=0 both projections are p, while
Rplus_+<=5p/(4(P+1))<p. For 1<=i<j, the remaining prefix mass includes its
last step ell, so x_i-d>=ell*d. Hence

    p*x_i+q*y_plus-Rplus_+
       >=p*d*(ell-epsilon*J)>0.

The other projection is even larger than p*x_i, and Rplus_-<p*d. This
proves that both ridges remain strictly positive outer before index j.
Thus (C96.2) follows from the ACTUAL recursion, and x_j=d.

At index j the first ridge projection is

    p*d+q*y_plus=p*d*(1-epsilon*(J-1)).

It is positive because epsilon*(J-1)<3/40, and strictly less than
Rplus_+. It therefore lies strictly in that ridge's core. The second
projection is p*d*(1+epsilon*(J-1))>Rplus_-, so the second ridge is still
positive outer. Direct differentiation now gives

    grad F(X_j)=(d-Lcut,-(q/p)*Lcut),
    x_(j+1)=-r*d+b*Lcut,
    y_(j+1)=epsilon*(q/p)*d*(b*J/2-ell).          (C96.3)

The last y-coordinate is positive by b>10 and ell<3/2. In particular the
central gradient is noncollinear with the stationary precentral gradient
(d,0). The actual gate Hessians diag(0,kappa) and
diag(0,kappa)+w*u_+*u_+^T do not commute: their off-diagonal commutator
has nonzero magnitude kappa*w*p*q.

    x_(j+1)+(q/p)*abs(y_(j+1))
      <=d*(-r+b*epsilon*J*(1+rho)/2)

All forward results retain the global Huber term, every single-cut value,

## Appendix: complete same-word finite scalar comparison

This appendix is included in the present joint derivation. It has no
unverified predecessor. Here K is the accepted functional K_n(H_m), and
F_ray is the complete accepted family from fact1fca3e5dd555cb4a.

Write r_j=a*c^j and M_j=1+sum H_j. Then

These statements follow on putting y=sigma-xi*u>0: the objective is

 sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2-(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The earlier first-row budget is also retained, on its stated domain
0<a<1 and a*eta<1, where

    eta=b/(1+w+v), nu=(1+eta)*(1-a*eta)/a,
    Erow=a+3+1/a-(u*delta/a)*eta-C^2*eta^2.

Its exact identity is

 Erow=nu*(m+a*(Lambda20+B0))+(1+eta)^2*M11
                 +(1+eta)*eta*((w+v)*Lambda12+v*Lambda13).        (15)

Here is a direct derivation. For orthonormal physical vectors U,V set
gfirst=-eta*U+sqrt(nu)*V and use saturated values on

 Xphys=(U+u*gfirst,U,-b*U,-(1+v)*eta*U,-eta*U),
 Gphys=(gfirst,U,-eta*U,-eta*U,-eta*U).

The nonzero residuals are Q20=Q30=Q40=-a*nu,
Q12=-(1+eta)*(b-eta), and Q13=-(1+eta)*v*eta. Every other finite
residual is zero. Use ||gfirst||^2=[1+(1-a)*eta]/a and
<U,gfirst>+a||gfirst||^2=1-a*eta to check the target0 residuals.
The energy telescope gives Erow and the two gradient columns modulo
e are sqrt(nu)*E and (1+eta)*e1, proving (15).

In particular, for EVERY lambda>=0, (14) holds with its left side
eps+lambda*Erow, sigma replaced by sigma+lambda*nu, and cap replaced
by

 min((c20+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*beta),
                         (cB+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*W0)).              (16)

This follows by adding the TWO exact budgets before using (13), so
the same m and original incoming coefficients must pay for both.
It does not replace any of the older2948 conditions. For example,
putting Wrow=max(beta,W0), Krow=max(u,a*Wrow) in (13),(15),(2) gives

 u*delta<=Krow*Erow/nu+2*sqrt(Q*Erow/nu).

For delta>0, v>1, ab<=1 and c(v-1)<=1, Krow=u and Q<1. These imply
Erow>nu*delta^2/u^2 and

    b<(a+3)*(C-a-2)/((a+1)*(C+a+2)).

To see the latter equivalence, the direct factorization is

 u^2*(Erow-nu*delta^2/u^2)
    =((a+3)-(delta+u*C)*eta)*((a+3)+(u*C-delta)*eta).

The second factor is positive since C>A and u*A>delta. Substituting
eta=b/(C-A-b) in the positive first factor gives the displayed
bound. All its hypotheses remain.

## 5. A further matched full-column inequality near equality

In this section v>0 and all constants are the ones already defined.
Let

    dphys=a*b*c*v=(1+v)*z,
    nbar=s*(2C-(C+1)*v)/v>=0,
    rcoef=ell*mu^2+mu*hcoef^2>0,
    Lnorm=sqrt((u-a*alpha)^2/sigma+a^2/(1+Hbar)),
    Lterm=sqrt((alpha-beta)^2/sigma+1/(1+Hbar)),
    Kterm=(dphys/x)*Lterm*sqrt(nbar), Jfee=a/(2*x),
    Pcost=max(ell*mu*Hpre/cB,ell*mu*beta/c1,c03old/c03,1/k),
    Gcost=max(mu*Lnorm^2,Pcost).

All denominators are strictly positive. If nbar<0, the original
terminal budget (9) already excludes the word; it is never square-rooted.

Every full original array satisfies the following explicit scalar test.
Write y=sqrt(eps), which requires eps>=0, and set

 tau_max(y)=(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y
       +sqrt((sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)^2+4*jcoef*(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)))
                                                            /(2*jcoef),
 Psi(y)=rcoef*tau_max(y)^2
            +2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*tau_max(y)*y+Gcost*y^2.

Then

                              R<=Psi(sqrt(eps)).                 (17)

Here is the full derivation retaining the actual quadratic column.
The vector identity, checked in all five coordinates, is

    pquad=uE-aX-jcoef*B+dphys*e4+ab*e.

The original terminal rows give

    2<E,e4>_M=a*Lambda40-Lambda04,
    2<J,e4>_M=2<E,e4>_M+beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14.

Since X=Y+alpha E, they imply

 x<B,e4>_M=(alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M
                              -beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/2.

Taking the inner product of pquad with B therefore gives

 <B,pquad>_M=(u-a*alpha)<E,B>_M-a<Y,B>_M-jcoef*Tcut
       +(dphys/x)*((alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M)
       -dphys*beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/(2*x).       (18)

Let eps_G=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)||Y||_M^2 and let eps_C be the cost sum
in (12). Thus eps=eps_G+eps_C with both nonnegative. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz gives

 ||(u-a*alpha)E-aY||_M<=Lnorm*sqrt(eps_G),
 ||(alpha-beta)E+Y||_M<=Lterm*sqrt(eps_G).

Also ||e4||_M^2<=nbar by (9), and
c14=beta*dphys/a. Drop the negative Lambda40,Lambda41 terms in
(18), use Lambda14<=eps_C/c14, and use
<B,pquad>_M>=-sqrt(Tcut*Q). The result is

 jcoef*Tcut<=sqrt(Tcut*Q)
        +(Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut)+Kterm)*sqrt(eps_G)+Jfee*eps_C.          (19)

For the other direction (4) and Avec=(u-a*alpha)E-aY+hcoef*B give

 R<=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps_G)
                                    +mu*Lnorm^2*eps_G+Pcost*eps_C
  <=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps)+Gcost*eps.           (20)

The cost bound follows by comparing each cost in (4) to the cost of
the SAME multiplier in (12); their maximum ratio is precisely Pcost.
Thus costs and energies have not been chosen from different arrays.
Replacing eps_G,eps_C separately by eps in (19) gives, for
tcut=sqrt(Tcut)>=0,

 jcoef*tcut^2-(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)*tcut-(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)<=0.

Its nonnegative root is tau_max(y). The right side of (20) increases
with tcut>=0, which proves (17).

This supplies a quantified positive-gap exclusion test. Psi is
continuous and strictly increasing on [0,infinity), tends to infinity,
and

    Psi(0)=rcoef*Q/jcoef^2.

Consequently, if R>rcoef*Q/jcoef^2, there is a unique y0>0 with
Psi(y0)=R, and every full array must have

                           eps>=y0^2>0.                         (21)

Strict increase follows from the explicit nondecreasing positive
coefficients in tau_max and Gcost>0. This is an algebraic definition
and proof; no numerical root finding is used. In particular Q=0,R>0
forces a positive eps, even when delta=0 and the first-row bound
(14) alone is zero. This prices a further original cross column.
No uniform lower bound as v,ell,R,Q or other factors vanish is claimed.

## 6. COMPLETE original-array matching on the new equality locus

Assume eps=0 and R>0, still with a,b,c>0,bc<=1,0<v<2. Equation(12)
forces ME=MY=0, hence MX=0, and

    B0=B1=Lambda20=Lambda03=Lambda14=Lambda23=0.

Equation(6) now gives Lambda04=0, and (7) gives Lambda02=0.
The first moment in (3) forces Lambda01=2; node0 flow then gives
Lambda10=2A. Its diagonal is m=1-a^2-2a, so

                         a=sqrt(2)-1, a*A=1.                    (22)

Set

    Tstar=R/rcoef>0, r13=2*rho*Tstar, Bphys=Hpre+w, s=Bphys+v.

On this locus EVERY original multiplier is forced as follows:

    Lambda01=2, Lambda10=2A, Lambda13=r13,
    Lambda12=(2*A*Hpre-(beta+w)*r13)/beta,
    Lambda21=2*Hpre+Lambda12+r13,
    Lambda24=(2*w*N+beta*Lambda21)/(w+v),
    Lambda42=Lambda24/c,
    Lambda32=2*Bphys+r13+(c-1)*Lambda42,
    Lambda43=(2*s*C-(w+v)*Lambda42)/v,
    Lambda34=(1-c)*Lambda42+Lambda43-2*s,                         (23)

and the other TEN off-diagonal coefficients are zero:

    02,03,04,14,20,23,30,31,40,41.

Let

    nstar=Lambda42+Lambda43-s*(s+2),
    vcol=(0,-rho,rho-1,1,0)^T, dcol=(0,0,0,-1,1)^T.

For this array the ENTIRE original matrix is

                  M=Tstar*vcol*vcol^T+nstar*dcol*dcol^T.          (24)

Thus a word on eps=0,R>0 has a full original certificate if and
only if (22) holds and the explicit array (23) has

    Lambda12,Lambda32,Lambda34,Lambda43>=0, nstar>=0.              (25)

All other surviving signs then follow from their displayed formulas.
In particular Lambda21>0, Lambda24>0, Lambda42>0. This is an
actual all-twenty-entry matching, not a supplied covariance-fiber test.

Here is the proof of necessity and sufficiency of these formulas.
From E=0 and X=0 in the M seminorm, MJ=-rho*MB. Equations(4),(8)
give Tcut=Tstar. The original row <e1,B> gives Lambda13=r13.
Node1's moment and flow give respectively Lambda12 and Lambda21
in (23). Since M14=0 and MJ=-rho MB with rho>0, MB has fourth
component zero. Hence M24=0 too, because e2=e-J-B. The original
entry 2M24=c*Lambda42-Lambda24 gives their displayed relation.
Node2's moment and flow give Lambda24 and Lambda32. Node4's
moment and flow give Lambda43 and Lambda34. There is no free
covariance or multiplier left.

Conversely impose (22), eps=0,R>0 and define (23), allowing real
coefficients temporarily. The node0,1,2,4 flows and moments hold by
construction. For node3 the flow follows by summing the other flows.
Its moment can be checked explicitly: substituting (23) gives

 -w*Lambda32+v*Lambda34
   =-2*w*Bphys-w*r13-c*(w+v)*Lambda42+2*s*(C-v)
   =-2*(w+N)*Bphys+2*s*(C-v)=2*v*(1+Bphys),

where c(w+v)Lambda42=2*N*Bphys-w*r13 and
w+N=C-v=1+Bphys. Thus the full flow and Me=0 hold.

The original first row vanishes because aA=1; also M14=M24=0,
M13=-rho*Tstar. Direct substitution of Lambda12 gives

    M11=-D/beta^2+2*b*w*rho*Tstar/beta=rho^2*Tstar.

For the constant term in this identity use A^2=2A+1:
1-b^2+2A-2*A*b*Hpre/beta=-D/beta^2.
For the second equality use eps=0 and (8), which give
D=(2*b*w*x-x^2)*Tstar. The kernel then determines M12.
Finally (4), with all its costs zero and E row zero, determines
Tcut=Tstar: its positive Tcut coefficient is
ell*mu^2+a^2*b^2*mu^3, and (8) gives exactly that same coefficient
after subtracting the known J terms from R=rcoef*Tstar.
Me=0 now fixes every remaining entry except M44=nstar and proves
(24). The vectors vcol and dcol are independent, so full PSD is
equivalent to nstar>=0. This proves sufficiency as well as necessity.

The matched quadratic calibration has no extra freely selectable term:

    Q=jcoef^2*Tstar+dphys^2*nstar.                              (26)

Indeed pquad^T vcol=-jcoef and pquad^T dcol=dphys, by (8). Equation(13)
applies to the flow-correct array, so (24) proves (26). Consequently
nstar>=0 is equivalently Q>=jcoef^2*R/rcoef. At Q=0 this is
impossible when R>0; the WHOLE zero quadratic column is retained.

No word at C>=193/25 is exhibited satisfying eps=0 and (22)--(25).
Nor is it proved here that their entire high-capacity region is empty.

## 7. Zero boundaries and the unresolved complete comparison

At v=0 with ell>0, z=theta=qcorr=0, k=k0=kold=b^2/ell. Identity
(10) still holds and its Gram has sigma>0, but some displayed costs
vanish. Strict-cost conclusions, Pcost, jcoef divisions, (17)--(26),
and the positive-gap equality classification above are NOT used there.
One retains the undivided identities (1)--(7),(10),(13),(15).

At ell=0 in this domain one necessarily has v=0,bc=1. Then pquad=Avec,
R=mu*Q, and the old undivided gap is b*beta*Q. No division by ell,
v,jcoef,c1,c03 or c23 is made on this boundary. No formal gradient
is deleted at v=0. At R=0 or Q=0, use the undivided norm identities;
zero M-energy always kills its WHOLE original column.

The complete older step system includes the compact-domain cuts,
full quadratic and return tests, all clipping branches, all adjacent
and lifted triangles, C82/C84, the entire C83/C86 curvature families,
the later lifted return, the2948 first-row test and its stated
hypotheses, and the previously recorded scoped exclusion regions.
Shared19f1d27c0eb8a588 and554ec17f7f590bf0 were reread to retain this
complete list. Their entries are awareness, not accepted proof inputs.
The projected-core prism d3abee1b17da52da fails retained C82/C83;
the earlier scalar-family survivor b1592acfdb474277 /480b207356f9095f

Direct attempt one, completed algebraically, matches the ORIGINAL
rows at sharp equality and yields the explicit array (23). Direct
attempt two prices departures from it by (12)--(21), including the

Neither attempt establishes a point surviving ALL older conditions

Counterexample screening of those shortcuts is supplied by the two

The exact remaining STEP comparison is now the conjunction, for the

The concrete simultaneous obstruction is therefore NOT a free choice

claim: C97 COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED draft: an explicit two-state nonstationary Markov law gives positive affine values, dense signed correlations, real nonzero paid transverse action, ALL original pairs, one static smooth function and exact radius for every word with min h>1. A whole larger class is excluded on original H_m: aligned initial anchor, arbitrary varying 1<eta_i<h_i, tight queried optimum upper rows and arbitrary Markov product correlations imply V<=(a+2)beta^(2^m-1)c^(-m), so original B_n V->0, even with FREE terminal.
