evidence:
# C97: a chronological Markov construction with positive affine values

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED DRAFT. Actual runtime round 1 of the
current two-round wave; baseline 27, completed ceiling 29, attempted ceiling
30 including the historical interruption. No numerical evaluation, solver,
machine algebra, replay, subordinate agent, or formal verifier is used.
The original arbitrary-schedule exact-profile Goal remains OPEN.

The only accepted mathematical predecessors used are
`1252b8823bb5a290`, for the original all-directed-pair interpolation
convention and its explicit static conjugate, and `b98bb807d514e80d`,
for the original benchmark convention and its crude exact bound.
All new results below are proved jointly. No C90--C96 assertion is a
mathematical predecessor. Probability is a coordinate construction,
not a replacement for any interpolation inequality.

## 1. Definitions and the three scoped conclusions

Work with smoothness 1 on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space.
For a supplied finite word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), actual GD means

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i,  g_i=grad F(X_i),
    f_i=F(X_i)-min F,  V=2f_n/dist(X_0,argmin F)^2.

The optimum is denoted star, with X_star=g_star=f_star=0. Define the
original residual, for every distinct ordered pair including star, by

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.       (1)

Define the positive affine value reserve

    delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.

Here are the conclusions, each limited to its stated class.

A. Every nonempty supplied word with min_i h_i>1 has the explicit
two-state, time-dependent Markov construction in Sections 2--5. All
sampled value reserves are positive, the original gradients have dense
signed product correlations and real independent innovations, and every
ordered row (1) is proved. One fixed convex 1-smooth function realizes
the entire run and has unique minimizer 0 and exact initial distance eta.
The normalized payoff and a paid append rule are explicit.

B. For the original recursive diagnostic words H_m, the ENTIRE broader
class of queried Markov product correlations with an aligned initial
point and tight queried optimum upper rows has negligible original-B
payoff, under the varying support-ratio conditions of Section 7. This
allows arbitrary varying positive support ratios, arbitrary correlations,
arbitrary amplitudes, and a completely free terminal gradient and value.
It is not only a bound on the displayed safe rule.

C. The exact small example in Section 9 refutes replacing the distant
rows by adjacent rows, optimum rows, positive affine values, real PSD,
and even all reverse chronological rows. A remote forward row fails.

Neither A nor B nor C is a theorem about unrestricted W_n(h). In
particular min h>1 is already a restriction for A; the additional
geometric hypotheses for B are essential and are identified explicitly.

## 2. The bounded rule, genuine joint law, and real coordinates

Fix n>=1 and h_i>1. Choose two scalar parameters

    1<eta<min_i h_i,  0<theta<1,

and set a bookkeeping value h_n=eta. This h_n is NOT a physical step.
For example, the completely specified choice

    eta=(1+min_i h_i)/2, theta=(n+1)/(n+2)

depends only on the supplied word. Keeping the two scalar parameters
visible makes the continuation law and its bounds clearer. Define

    b_i=(h_i-eta)/eta,
    t_i=theta*min{1,(h_i-eta)/h_(i+1)},
    r_i=-sqrt(t_i/b_i),                         0<=i<n,
    A_0=1, A_(i+1)=sqrt(t_i*b_i)*A_i.                (2)

No Gram entry is a free parameter. The fixed rule reads only successive
physical steps and the two common scalars. Because h_(i+1)>=eta>1,

    0<t_i<=theta<1,
    t_i/b_i<=theta*eta/h_(i+1)<=theta<1,
    h_i-t_i*h_(i+1)>=eta,
    h_i-t_i>=eta.                                   (3)

The third inequality follows from t_i<=(h_i-eta)/h_(i+1).
The fourth follows because h_(i+1)>1. Thus -1<r_i<0.

Let S_0 be a fair sign and let B_0,...,B_(n-1) be independent signs,
independent of S_0, with P(B_i=1)=(1+r_i)/2. Put S_(i+1)=S_i B_i.
The complete finite joint law on sign strings s=(s_0,...,s_n) is

    p(s)=2^(-n-1) product_(i<n)(1+r_i*s_i*s_(i+1)).   (4)

Every atom is positive, and summing successively over the last sign
proves that the probabilities sum to 1. Independent bond signs give

    E[S_i S_j]=product_(k=i)^(j-1)r_k, i<j.          (5)

For example, literal real coordinates u_i(s)=sqrt(p(s))*s_i realize
(5). A smaller explicit realization uses the orthonormal basis
e_0,...,e_n of R^(n+1):

    u_0=e_0,
    u_(i+1)=r_i*u_i+sqrt(1-r_i^2)*e_(i+1).           (6)

Induction gives ||u_i||=1 and (5) as its actual real inner products.
Thus all PSD requirements are proved by coordinates. Every new
direction has a nonzero innovation, and all distinct inner products
are nonzero with sign (-1)^(j-i). The transition law changes when its
successive-step formula changes; it is not a fixed one-initial-sign
constant-correlation law. Section 6 gives a concrete changing example.

Set, in these SAME coordinates,

    g_i=A_i*u_i,
    X_0=eta*u_0,
    X_i=X_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t,
    q_i=A_i^2,
    f_i=(eta-1/2)*q_i, delta_i=(eta-1)*q_i.           (7)

Every q_i and delta_i is strictly positive. These are data at all the
original samples, including the terminal. No subword is reset.

For later use define, for i<=j,

    P_ij=product_(k=i)^(j-1)(-t_k),
    E_ij=product_(k=i)^(j-1)(t_k*b_k)=q_j/q_i,        (8)

with empty products 1. Since A_(k+1)*r_k/A_k=-t_k,

    <g_i,g_j>=q_i*P_ij, i<j.                        (9)

## 3. Actual support and every original directed inequality

First prove the actual support identity

    <X_i,g_i>=eta*q_i, 0<=i<=n.                     (10)

It holds at i=0. The new basis vector e_(i+1) is orthogonal to X_i
and g_i, since both are in span(e_0,...,e_i). Hence

    <X_(i+1),u_(i+1)>=r_i*(eta-h_i)*A_i
                           =eta*A_(i+1),

where (2) was used. This proves (10) by induction. It proves support
along the actual GD displacement; it is not an independently assigned
inner product.

The optimum rows are now exactly

    Q_(i,star)=0,
    Q_(star,i)=-(eta-1)*q_i<0.                       (11)

For every i<j, all future innovations in u_j are orthogonal to X_i,
so <X_i,g_j>=eta*<g_i,g_j>. Expanding (1), (7), and (10) gives

    Q_(j,i)=(eta-1)*q_i*(P_ij-1).                   (12)

If j-i is odd then P_ij<0. If j-i is even, 0<P_ij<1 by (3).
Thus every reverse chronological row is strictly negative.

For the other orientation keep the whole physical displacement:

    Q_(i,j)/q_i
      =eta-sum_(k=i)^(j-1)h_k*P_ik-P_ij
                                      -(eta-1)*E_ij. (13)

No old step is omitted from this expression. We show

    sum_(k=i)^(j-1)h_k*P_ik+P_ij>=eta.              (14)

For even d=j-i, pair the physical terms consecutively:

    sum_(k=i)^(j-1)h_k*P_ik+P_ij
      =sum_(r=0)^(d/2-1)P_(i,i+2r)
          [h_(i+2r)-t_(i+2r)*h_(i+2r+1)]+P_ij.

Each even-prefix product is positive. Every bracket is at least eta
by (3), and the first product is 1. The last term P_ij is positive,
which proves (14).

For odd d=2v+1, the analogous identity is

    sum_(r=0)^(v-1)P_(i,i+2r)
          [h_(i+2r)-t_(i+2r)*h_(i+2r+1)]
        +P_(i,j-1)*[h_(j-1)-t_(j-1)].

If v=0, the only bracket is at least eta by (3). If v>=1,
the first paired bracket is at least eta and every remaining term
is positive. This proves (14) in every case. Equation (13) is
therefore at most -(eta-1)*E_ij<0.

Equations (11)--(14) prove ALL ordered original rows, including every
old/new cross row and both directions at the unqueried terminal.

## 4. One static function and the true radius

Define y_i=X_i-g_i and form, once for the complete supplied word,

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max{0,max_(0<=i<=n)(<y_i,v>-delta_i)},
    F(X)=sup_v(<X,v>-H(v)).                          (15)

This is the explicit full-data conjugate of accepted
`1252b8823bb5a290`. To match its notation, expand

    <X_i,g_i>-f_i+<X_i,v-g_i>+||v-g_i||^2/2
       =||v||^2/2+<X_i-g_i,v>-delta_i.

The established all-pair inequalities therefore imply that F is
everywhere finite, convex, differentiable and 1-smooth, and that
F(X_i)=f_i and grad F(X_i)=g_i for EVERY i. Consequently its actual
GD visits precisely the prescribed samples. The function is fixed
before the first update.

Every delta_i is strictly positive. The maximum in (15) therefore
equals 0 in a neighborhood of v=0. Since H(v)>=||v||^2/2, F(0)=0.
For any X!=0 choose a sufficiently small s in (0,1) with sX in that
neighborhood. Then

    F(X)>=(s-s^2/2)||X||^2>0.

Thus argmin F={0}, and the true initial squared distance is exactly
||X_0||^2=eta^2. It has not been replaced by a projected or reset radius.
The exact payoff is

    V=(2eta-1)/eta^2 * product_(i<n)(t_i*b_i).        (16)

Every queried i>=1 produces actual paid transverse action. The point
X_i has zero e_i coordinate, whereas the new coordinate of g_i is
A_i*sqrt(1-r_(i-1)^2)>0. Thus the e_i component of X_(i+1)-X_i is

    -h_i*A_i*sqrt(1-r_(i-1)^2),                     (17)

which is nonzero. In particular a two-step segment already has a
nonzero displacement transverse to its first gradient. All of it is
inside (7), (10), (13), and the distance calculation above.

For arbitrary smoothness L>0 use L*F and physical steps h_i/L; the
same normalized W=2R payoff (16) follows.

## 5. The paid continuation rule and its limit

For a jointly planned chronological segment [r,s), the amplitude and
value transfer is exactly

    q_s=q_r*E_rs, f_s=f_r*E_rs,
    X_s=X_r-sum_(i=r)^(s-1)h_i*A_i*u_i.              (18)

The direction is propagated by (6), keeping the old coordinates.
The state consists of the actual X_r,u_r,A_r, the common eta, and the
last physical-step guard; no independent Gram block or free mode is
chosen. The vector dimension grows by the prescribed orthogonal
innovation. Its coefficient is fixed by (2).

For a literal append to already fixed jets 0,...,k, the sufficient
join condition inherited from (3) is

    t_(k-1)*h_k<=h_(k-1)-eta,                       (19)

when k>=1. Here h_k is the first NEW physical step. Retain all old
jets and transition coefficients, require h_k>eta, and choose every
new transition by (2) using the supplied future word. All old guards
then remain true and (19) supplies the missing boundary guard.
The proofs of (10)--(14) apply to every pair straddling the boundary.

This proves existence of a single interpolant for the extended full
history. It does NOT mean changing the running objective at a join,
nor that the old interpolant (15) on a shorter data set already has
the required behavior outside its samples. In the intended use the
entire word, all guards and (15) are fixed before GD starts.

The old artificial value h_k=eta used to terminate a shorter word
cannot simply be replaced for free by a larger physical h_k. If (19)
fails, this sufficient append rule gives no extension claim. The
exact all-pair formula (13) remains available, but adjacent constraints
alone cannot repair it, as Section 9 demonstrates.

For perspective, even the safe family itself is extremely weak on
the original H_m of Section 8. Put ell=1+a. Every even physical index
has h_i=ell; there are N/2 such steps and the last step is even.
Let b_low=(ell-eta)/eta<a. Pair each low step except the last with
the following step H>ell. Equations (2) give

    (t_low*b_low)*(t_high*b_high)
      <=theta^2*b_low^2*(H-eta)/H<=b_low^2.

The unpaired last step has t_last=theta*b_low and contributes
theta*b_low^2<=b_low^2, since b_low<a<1. The prefactor in (16) is
at most 1 because eta^2-(2eta-1)=(eta-1)^2. Thus

    V<=b_low^N<a^N.                                 (20)

This is only the displayed guard rule. The next result treats a much
larger family, without imposing that guard or a constant eta.

## 6. Concrete legal changing segment

For h=(3,10), choose eta=2 and theta=1/2. Then

    b=(1/2,4), t=(1/20,1/2),
    r=(-1/sqrt(10),-1/(2sqrt(2))),
    q=(1,1/40,1/20), f=(3/2,3/80,3/40).

One exact real realization is

    g_0=e_0,
    g_1=(-e_0+3e_1)/20,
    g_2=(e_0-3e_1+sqrt(70)e_2)/40,
    X_0=2e_0, X_1=-e_0, X_2=-(e_0+3e_1)/2.

These are actual positions from the stated steps. The reserves are
delta=(1,1/40,1/20). All six non-optimum ordered residuals are

    Q_01=-39/40, Q_10=-21/20,
    Q_02=-23/40, Q_20=-39/40,
    Q_12=-19/80, Q_21=-3/80.

The optimum rows are (11). Thus the fixed function (15) realizes
the segment, has unique minimizer 0, true squared distance 4, and
normalized payoff V=3/80. Its second displacement has e_1 component
-3/2, and its two transition correlations are different. This is a
complete legal coupled segment, not a correlation-only example.
It is not claimed stronger than the older tests on this word.

## 7. A whole-class obstruction with varying positive affine values

The following hypothesis class is substantially broader than (2).
Let an ACTUAL convex 1-smooth function with minimum 0 at 0 generate
a nonzero queried trajectory g_i=A_i*u_i, A_i>0, ||u_i||=1,
for 0<=i<n. Suppose:

  (i) The initial point is X_0=eta_0*g_0.
 (ii) For every queried i there is 1<eta_i<h_i such that

          <X_i,g_i>=eta_i*q_i,
          f_i=(eta_i-1/2)*q_i, q_i=A_i^2.           (21)

(iii) There are real r_0,...,r_(n-2) in [-1,1] with

          <u_i,u_j>=product_(k=i)^(j-1)r_k, i<j<n. (22)

There is NO constraint on the terminal gradient or value beyond
being generated by the same legal function. No sufficient guards,
stationarity, common amplitude ratio, common eta, or full-support
probability assumption is imposed on this class.

First, the true initial distance is exactly eta_0*A_0. Indeed (21)
at i=0 implies f_0+q_0/2=eta_0*q_0. For any minimizer z, the
necessary smooth interpolation row gives

    f_0+q_0/2<=<g_0,X_0-z>=eta_0*q_0-<g_0,z>.

Hence <g_0,z><=0 and
||X_0-z||^2=eta_0^2*q_0-2eta_0<g_0,z>+||z||^2
>=eta_0^2*q_0. The minimizer 0 attains this distance. Thus the
denominator is proved even when the minimizer is not unique.

The Markov product identity and X_i in span(g_0,...,g_i) give

    <X_(i+1),u_(i+1)>=r_i*(eta_i-h_i)*A_i.

Combining with (21) at i+1 forces r_i<0 and gives

    b_i=(h_i-eta_i)/eta_(i+1)>0,
    A_(i+1)=-r_i*b_i*A_i,
    t_i=r_i^2*b_i>0,
    q_(i+1)=t_i*b_i*q_i,       0<=i<n-1.            (23)

The b_i in this section are the varying-ratio generalization of (2),
not an assumption that eta_i is constant. For i<j<n, (22) also gives
<X_i,g_j>=eta_i<g_i,g_j>. Full expansion of the ORIGINAL row yields

    Q_(j,i)=(eta_i-1)*q_i
             [product_(k=i)^(j-1)(-t_k)-1].         (24)

All occurrences of eta_j cancel in this identity. Thus for any two
queried indices of the same parity,

    product_(k=i)^(j-1)t_k<=1.                      (25)

This is a necessary remote-row restriction, irrespective of how the
correlations and support ratios are selected from the full word.
It is NOT asserted sufficient for interpolation.

If n is odd, its last queried index n-1 is even. Taking (i,j)=(0,n-1)
in (25), or using the empty product for n=1, gives

    q_(n-1)/q_0<=product_(i=0)^(n-2)b_i
                        <=product_(i=0)^(n-2)(h_i-1). (26)

The last inequality follows individually from eta_i>1 and
eta_(i+1)>1. Thus no fixed positive floor eta_i-1 is needed; the
bound remains uniform when every reserve ratio tends to zero.

For a final physical step ell=h_(n-1) in (1,2), smoothness gives

    2f_n<=2f_(n-1)-ell*(2-ell)*q_(n-1)
          =[2(eta_(n-1)-1)+(ell-1)^2]*q_(n-1)
          <[(ell-1)^2+2(ell-1)]*q_(n-1).           (27)

This uses the actual terminal value, without specifying its gradient
or requiring any terminal analogue of (21). Equations (26)--(27)
are the complete-class obstruction used next.

## 8. Exact comparison on the ORIGINAL enclosing-m words

For m>=4 define

    N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m,
    c=sigma*(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.     (28)

The word is exactly h=H_m, with the SAME enclosing m in every child.
Its smallest and last step is ell=1+a, and 0<a<1/2, so ell<2.
The offset product is

    D_m:=product_(h_i in H_m)(h_i-1)
        =a^(N-1)*c^(N-m-1)
        =beta^(N-1)*c^(-m).                         (29)

One direct proof is induction from D_0=1 and
D_(j+1)=D_j^2*a*c^j. The displayed expression at general j is
a^(2^j-1)c^(2^j-j-1). Thus the product through the last queried
transition, omitting the final physical step, is D_m/a.

For EVERY legal instance in Section 7, divide (27) by the true
eta_0^2*q_0 and apply (26) and (29). It follows that

    V <= (a+2)*beta^(N-1)*c^(-m).                   (30)

The strict version follows when n>=1 and the ratios in (21) are
strict, but the weak inequality is the convenient uniform statement.
It holds uniformly over arbitrary horizon-dependent correlations,
amplitudes, functions, dimensions and eta_i satisfying the class
hypotheses. The terminal is entirely free.

Let B_n and U_n^ZJ=1/B_n be the ORIGINAL all-split denominator and
benchmark in accepted `b98bb807d514e80d`. That fact gives
B_n<=1+4n^(log_2 3)<1+4*3^m. Since beta^(N-1)<=exp(-(N-1)/m),

    B_n*V <= (a+2)*(1+4*3^m)*c^(-m)*exp(-(2^m-1)/m)
             ->0.                                  (31)

For completeness, c>2 and a+2<5/2 bound the logarithm of all factors
except the final exponential by a constant plus m*log(3/2).
The quantity 2^m/m divided by m tends to infinity. This proves the
limit without a numerical evaluation or a benchmark replacement.

Equation (31) closes this precise class as a source of a matching
lower witness on the original diagnostic words. It does NOT show
small unrestricted W_n(H_m), and it does NOT decide the original
all-schedule exact-profile Goal.

## 9. Exact failure of local-only interpolation checks

Take the physical word h=(3,10) and eta=2, but now choose the legal
Markov correlations r_0=-1/sqrt(2), r_1=-1/2. Their corresponding
parameters in (23) are b=(1/2,4), t=(1/4,1). They have t_0*t_1=1/4,
so even the same-parity reverse-row condition holds. Use

    g_0=e_0,
    g_1=(-e_0+e_1)/4,
    g_2=(e_0-e_1)/4+sqrt(3/8)*e_2,
    X_0=2e_0, X_1=-e_0, X_2=(3e_0-5e_1)/2,
    q=(1,1/8,1/2), f=(3/2,3/16,3/4).

These are literal real coordinates, with every innovation nonzero,
and every sample has <X_i,g_i>=2q_i and delta_i=q_i>0.
All optimum rows pass. The adjacent rows are

    Q_01=-7/8, Q_10=-5/4,
    Q_12=-11/8, Q_21=-1/4.

The remote reverse row also passes: Q_20=-3/4. But

    Q_02=3/4>0.                                    (32)

For a direct check, f_0-f_2=3/4,
<g_0,X_2-X_0>=-1/2, and ||g_0-g_2||^2=1.
Thus (32) follows from (1). There is no static convex 1-smooth
interpolant for these jets. This is a counterexample ONLY to the
local-only sufficiency claim, not a legal GD counterexample to any
theorem about actual functions.

## 10. The remaining interface and a priced escape identity

Changing eta_i alone does not escape (30) while the other hypotheses
of Section 7 hold. The crucial conditions are aligned initial support,
the Markov product relation, h_i>eta_i>1, and tight optimum upper rows.
Actual transverse displacement, positive affine values and varying
dependence have all been included in the excluded class.

One precise escape is to retain nonzero optimum slack. Define

    z_i=<X_i,g_i>-f_i-q_i/2>=0,
    eta_i=<X_i,g_i>/q_i,
    f_i=(eta_i-1/2)*q_i-z_i.                         (33)

Under the same aligned-anchor Markov support calculation, the actual
reverse row becomes, by expanding its value difference,

    Q_(j,i)=(eta_i-1)*q_i
             [product_(k=i)^(j-1)(-t_k)-1]+z_i-z_j. (34)

Positive reserves require z_i<(eta_i-1)*q_i. Thus it is invalid to
keep the product amplification while dropping its cost z_j in the
terminal value. Another possible escape introduces an initial anchor
with correlations to future innovations, in which case the support
recursion (23) and (24) acquire additional terms. Allowing support
ratios to cross physical step sizes also changes the sign/parity
argument. None of these broader interfaces is closed by this draft.

The next round should preserve the actual law, every old/new row,
the true distance and the slack cost in (33)--(34). A generic free
Gram matrix or a finite prescribed-word success would not close the
arbitrary-h quantifier gap. No new computational or verifier allowance
is inferred from this candidate.

## 11. Literature and proof-dependency audit

The final memory audit also recovered the older UNVERIFIED public
findings `c035d2edbaffb2c0` and `fd7036b719ef9645`. Their full domains
and coordinate definitions were read. The former treats first
occurrences of consecutive ruler levels, with constant gradients in
the intervening ordinary blocks and a common queried terminal cell;
it already includes positive heights and free affine intercepts in
that domain. The latter prices a negative-then-positive fresh relay.
Those are relevant prior boundaries, not premises of this manuscript.

C97 instead changes gradients at EVERY actual physical sample and
leaves the entire final completion free in its class bound. Its
restriction 1<eta_i<h_i and tight optimum upper rows is stronger in
a different direction. We do not claim that positive affine Markov
relays themselves are new, or that C97 subsumes either older family.
Future slack or mixed-sign work must compare its complete domain with
those older interfaces before claiming an escape.

Status: COMPLETE JOINT DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. Worker max, analytical round34.
No numerical, solver, replay, machine-algebra, or formal-verifier call was
made. No unverified finding is used as a premise. The target remains the
original arbitrary-word, all-sufficiently-large-horizon exact-profile
question, with a threshold independent of the word. This document does
not settle that question.

The result is a concrete legal-history obstruction to universally using
two consecutive constant-gradient cells with a positive reversal scale.
It allows the entire old parallel component, both affine offsets, every
fresh dimension, and even a changed common minimum. On a neighboring
range it solves the joint choices exactly within the retained two-plane
envelope family and prices the changed minimum and closest distance.

Accepted inputs: the smooth-convex interpolation inequality and its
orientation from fact1252b8823bb5a290; the same-word Huber/single-cut
baseline from factb98bb807d514e80d; and the exact B_n recursion from
fact0be8b54e0a33381c. All other arguments appear below.

## 1. Notation and the static interpolation construction

Work with smoothness1 in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, with unit
vector e. Scalar coordinates mean multiples of e; extra coordinates may
be present. Write t=<e,x>. For a finite convex maximum J of affine planes,
its envelope is

    f(x)=min_z [J(z)+||x-z||^2/2].                         (1.1)

If a plane of normal g is active at z and x=z+g, then its supporting
inequality, with the square expanded, shows z uniquely minimizes (1.1).
The resulting value is J(z)+||g||^2/2 and the gradient is g. To justify
the last assertion directly, let z(x) be the unique proximal minimizer
and g(x)=x-z(x). Existence follows from coercivity, and uniqueness from
the strictly convex quadratic. Adding the two subgradient inequalities
for J at z(x),z(y) gives

    ||g(x)-g(y)||^2 <= <g(x)-g(y),x-y>.

The supporting inequality at z(x) gives
f(y)>=f(x)+<g(x),y-x>, while evaluating the proximal objective for y
at z(x) gives the upper remainder bound||y-x||^2/2. Thus f is
differentiable with derivative g; the displayed inequality proves its Lipschitz
constant is at most1. The envelope is convex because its defining
objective is jointly convex. Its minimum and minimizer set coincide
with those of J: equality in J(z)+||x-z||^2/2>=min J requires x=z and
J(z)=min J. These arguments also cover affine ties and flat minimizer
sets. Every construction below specifies one J before the whole run.

For actual smooth jets use the accepted signed residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.      (1.2)

In proximal coordinates z_i=x_i-g_i and H_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
(1.2) is precisely the supporting-plane inequality

    H_j >= H_i+<g_i,z_j-z_i>.

Consequently checking every active affine plane at every proposed
proximal sample checks both directions of every original interpolation
pair, not just adjacent gradient inequalities.

## 2. A legal positive-height history and its exact retained state

Set

    J_old(z)=|<e,z>|=max(0,<e,z>,-<e,z>),
    f_old=env J_old,       x_init=3e.

The scalar formula is f_old(te)=t^2/2 for |t|<=1 and |t|-1/2
for |t|>=1. Its gradient is clip(t,-1,1)e. The minimizer set is
the hyperplane {<e,z>=0}; its true distance from x_init is3.

Apply the prefix steps(1,6). Its queried data, including the sample
used for the next bridge, are

    x_A=3e,   g_A=e,    f_A=5/2,   z_A=2e,    H_A=2;
    x_B=2e,   g_B=e,    f_B=3/2,   z_B=e,     H_B=1;
    x_C=-4e,  g_C=-e,   f_C=7/2,   z_C=-3e,  H_C=3.     (2.1)

Each selected plane is active at its displayed proximal point; the
other signed plane is nonpositive there. This checks all old pairs.
The two updates are 3e-e=2e and 2e-6e=-4e. In particular every old
queried proximal height is strictly positive, all positions are
distinct, and the prefix is a real run of one static function.

Before the next bridge the outgoing state is p=-3e, u=e, G=1, with
current query p-G u=-4e. The complete profiles, in the notation of
the assigned retained-state interface, are

    Phi(t)=J_old(p+t u)=|t-3|,
    Psi(s)=min(2-5s,1-4s,3),
    Xi(t,r)=(t-6)^2    if r>=0 and |t-3|<=r,
             +infinity otherwise.                       (2.2)

Here Xi is the squared distance from x_init to the slice of the
sublevel {J_old<=r} with <u,z-p>=t. Indeed that coordinate fixes
<e,z>=t-3, and setting every perpendicular coordinate to zero

squared distance is9. Thus neither a parallel component nor the
sublevel distance has been reset.

Apply the prescribed bridge13/2 at x_C. The next start is

    X=-4e+(13/2)e=(5/2)e.                                (2.3)

It lies strictly inside the previously sampled equal-gradient
segment[2e,3e], rather than repeating an old point.

## 3. Full-vector rigidity at the first new cell

Let F be ANY convex differentiable1-smooth function in ANY enlarged
finite dimension preserving the three jets(2.1), up to a common
additive constant. It need not have the old minimum or the old
function away from the queries.

For 2<=t<=3, convexity between x_B and x_A gives
F(te)<=t-1/2, after subtracting that common constant. The supporting
inequality at x_B gives the reverse inequality. Hence

    F(te)=t-1/2.

Using the old-to-new instance of(1.2), with v=grad F(te), gives

    Q_(B,t)=||v-e||^2/2 <=0.

Therefore v=e as a FULL vector. Every perpendicular component vanishes.

Now prescribe any nonnegative first ordinary list with total

    0<=S<=1/2.

All its partial sums are in[0,S]. By induction every position is
(5/2-u)e in[2e,5e/2], so every gradient in this actual block, including
its endpoint query, is forced to be e. This conclusion does not even
assume beforehand that the first cell is constant. In the proposed

    ell_1(z)=a_1+<q,z>,    ell_2(z)=a_2-beta<q,z>,

value normalization when ell_1 is the designated active plane. A
redundant first plane could instead have a_1<0, but then it lies below
the already retained plane z and cannot affect any query or minimum.
The active-plane assertion follows from
f(te)=t-1/2, z=(t-1)e and J(z)=t-1. If all values are recentered by
a common minimum mu, the first intercept becomes-mu; it is the same
physical plane and not an additional degree of freedom.

## 4. A quantitative obstruction to the remaining reversal

After that block prescribe a checkpoint b>1, and let

    Y=5/2-S-b.                                           (4.1)

The next position is exactly Ye. Suppose the proposed second cell
starts with gradient-beta e, beta>=0. Apply(1.2) in BOTH directions
between this actual next sample and the retained query B. Function
values and all common additive constants cancel, leaving

    Q_(B,Y)+Q_(Y,B)=(1+beta)(Y-1+beta).                  (4.2)

Thus if Y>1 there is NO beta>=0, no choice of either affine offset,
and no transverse innovation or change of minimum that makes the
two-cell rule legal. If Y=1 there is NO beta>0. This is an obstruction
for arbitrary smooth-convex extensions, stronger than just an empty
interval for a selected max-affine construction.

When Y>1, at least one original ordered row has residual at least
(Y-1)/2. This is a quantitative gap in the actual original rows.
It is not a formal-vector or numerically estimated separator.
For an unrestricted next gradient v, the same pair sum gives

    ||v-(Y/2)e||^2 <= (2-Y)^2/4.                         (4.3)

In the relevant range1<Y<3/2 this implies <v,e>>=Y-1>0.
Allowing the first next gradient to change direction cannot permit a
nonpositive e component without changing the retained history.

The explicit obstruction parameters are

theta<=theta(k)<2*k*mu*z, and theta<=Ucap.

On the strictly capped branch theta=Ucap<theta(k), so F=0 and Z>0.
If kR-D=0 and R>0, the positive costs and the two squares force

    ME=-(Z/u)*MB, MJ=-(x/beta)*MB,
    Lambda20=Lambda03=0.

Here x/beta<1 since bw<=beta and theta>0. Consequently

    M02=(Z/u)*(1-x/beta)*Tcut>0.

The two zero columns also give Tcut>0: otherwise both J and E would
have zero columns and (4), with its positive costs zero, would give
R=0. But the actual original row gives

    2M02=-Lambda02-w*Lambda04<=0.

This is a direct sign contradiction. The old relaxation could select
its Gram energies without satisfying this retained original entry.
The following quantitative argument uses (7) to remove its cap.

## 3. The unrestricted root and the new full-row remainder

Assume v>0 for now. Then ell>0, z>0 and 1-bt>0. Set

    k0=b^2*w/(ell*mu), kold=b^2*w^2/(ell*mu^2).

The minimum of F(k,theta) over all real theta is attained at

    theta(k)=2*z*k*mu/(1+a^2*k*mu).

It is strictly decreasing as a function of k: at each fixed theta,
partial F/partial k=-ell*mu^2-theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)<0, and the minimum
is attained continuously. At k0 the minimum divided by mu^2 is
b^2*(gamma-1)*(gamma+a^2*k0*mu)/(1+a^2*k0*mu)>0,
where gamma=w/mu>1. At kold it is negative, since F(kold,0)=0 and
the negative linear term improves it for small positive theta.
There is therefore a unique root k in (k0,kold).

Here is an explicit definition requiring no root search. Define

    Hbar=(2*b*w-beta
          +sqrt((beta-2*b*w)^2+4*b*w^2*(1-b*t)/mu))/(2*(1-b*t)),
    k=Hbar/(a^2*mu), theta=2*z*k*mu/(1+Hbar),
    x=b*w-a*theta/2=b*(w+Hbar*mu)/(1+Hbar), rho=x/beta,
    hcoef=theta/(2*k*mu), jcoef=a^2*theta/2,
    rstar=u*theta/2.

The positive Hbar solves

    (1-bt)*Hbar^2+(beta-2*bw)*Hbar-b*w^2/mu=0,

which follows by substituting theta(k) into F=0. Also

    0<rho<1, hcoef+jcoef=z,
    a*x-a*b*mu=hcoef, k*ell*mu^2+theta^2/(4*k*mu)
                                            =2*b*w*x-x^2.         (8)

The inequalities use mu<w and bw<=beta, with strictness supplied
by Hbar>0. The identities follow by expansion and F=0.

Full original feasibility itself forces v<2. Indeed the terminal
diagonal is n=||e4||_M^2=sum_(j<4)Lambda4j-s(s+2)>=0.
Every weight in the last row of (3) is at least v. Hence

    v*n<=s*(2C-(C+1)*v), so v<=2C/(C+1)<2.                       (9)

We now work on 0<v<2; v>=2 was already excluded by this original row.
Define the nonnegative correction

    qcorr=max(0,((1+v)*rstar-beta*b*v*c)
                         /(w+(1+v)*(1-rho))),
    rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho),
    X=beta*J+x*B.

The EXACT original-array remainder is

    eps:=k*R-D
       =(1+Hbar)*||X||_M^2
         -2*(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)*<E,X>_M+k*mu*u^2*m
         +cB*B0+c1*B1+c20*Lambda20+qcorr*Lambda02
         +c03*Lambda03+c04*Lambda04+c14*Lambda14+c23*Lambda23,      (10)

where

    cB=k*ell*mu*Hpre-beta*(b*w*H0pre-u)+a*rshift,
    c1=beta*(k*ell*mu-b^2*w), c20=beta*u-a*qcorr,
    c03=k*c03old-rshift+w*qcorr,
    c04=beta*b*v*c-(1+v)*rshift+w*qcorr,
    c14=beta*b*v*c, c23=k*c23old.

To check the identity, first combine (4) and (5). Its Gram part is

 beta^2*||J||_M^2+2*beta*b*w*<J,B>_M+k*ell*mu^2*Tcut
                                                 +k*mu*||Avec||_M^2.

Subtract 2*rshift*<E,B>_M+2*qcorr*<E,J+B>_M from that Gram part.
Restore them using (6) and (7); this gives precisely all costs in
(10). Since rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho), the subtraction differs
from 2*rstar*<E,B> by 2*qcorr*<E,X>/beta. F=0 and (8) turn the
uncorrected Gram into ||X||^2+k*mu*||uE-aX||^2. This proves (10).

Every displayed cost is nonnegative; cB,c1,c20,c03,c14,c23 are
STRICTLY positive. Here is the full sign and PSD check.

Let

    qmax=beta*u*(sqrt(k*mu*(1+Hbar))-a*k*mu).

Then

    0<=qcorr<qmax<beta*u/(2a).                                  (11)

If qcorr=0 this follows from Hbar>0. Otherwise put
tau=sqrt(Hbar/(1+Hbar)) in (0,1), Vprod=vbc, and
Sden=2+b+c+v. Direct substitution gives

    qcorr=(beta/a)*Vprod*(u*tau^2-a*beta)
                              /(Sden-Vprod+Vprod*tau^2),
    qmax=(beta*u/a)*tau/(1+tau).

The numerator of qcorr is positive in this case. The inequality
qcorr<qmax is equivalent to

    Vprod*(1+tau)*(u*tau-a*beta)<u*tau*Sden.

Its left side is smaller than 2*Vprod*u*tau. Moreover
2*Vprod<=2v<2+b+c+v=Sden, using bc<=1 and v<2. This proves the
strict inequality. The upper bound on qmax follows from
tau/(1+tau)<1/2.

Also rshift>0: when qcorr>0 its numerator is less than
(1+v)*rstar, while its denominator is strictly larger than
(1+v)*(1-rho). Thus qcorr<rstar/(1-rho).
At k=k0 the part of cB before a*rshift equals u*(1-bc)>=0;
it strictly increases with k. Hence cB>0. Since k>k0, c1>0.
Equation (11) gives c20>beta*u/2>0. Finally
rstar<k*u*mu*z=k*c03old and rshift<=rstar, proving c03>0.
The definition of qcorr gives c04>=0, and c14,c23>0.

Set

    alpha=(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)/(1+Hbar), Y=X-alpha*E,
    sigma=k*mu*u^2-(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)^2/(1+Hbar)>0.

The positivity of sigma is exactly qcorr<qmax. Thus (10) is

    eps=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)*||Y||_M^2+the nonnegative costs in (10).  (12)

In particular every full original certificate obeys D<=kR. The old
cap theta<=2*beta*z/(a*u) is unnecessary once (7) is retained. On
the old strictly capped branch its root kstar is strictly larger
than this k, so an additional algebraic strip kR<D<=kstar*R is
excluded. This comparison is only with that relaxation, NOT with the
complete older scalar/triangle/curvature conjunction.

## 4. The actual quadratic column and joint first-row budget

Define

    pquad=(1,-a,ab,-abc,abc*(v-1))^T,
    Q=1-C^2*a^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2,
    delta=u^2-2, W0=1+bc*(v-1).

Tp=e and Le=0. Telescoping h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2 gives

    ||pquad||_M^2=Q>=0,
    2<E,pquad>_M=u*(m-delta)
             +a^2*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40).    (13)

For the row formula, let O0=sum_(j>0)Lambda0j and
I0=Lambda20+Lambda30+Lambda40. Then m=1-a^2-aO0 and node0 flow
gives Lambda10=O0+2u-I0. With Te0=u e-a e0 and
Mp=Dmat pquad+T^T L^T pquad/2 one obtains

 pquad^T L e0=uO0+2au-a*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40),
 2<E,pquad>_M=2(1-a^2)-a*pquad^T L e0,

which gives (13). Both incoming weights 1-bc and W0 are nonnegative,
and 1-bc<=W0, including v<1.

By (12), eps>=sigma*m+c20*Lambda20+cB*B0. Define

    xi_cap=min(c20/(a^2*beta), cB/(a^2*W0)),

omitting the second term if W0=0. For every real xi with
xi<=xi_cap and xi<sigma/u,

    eps>=xi*u*delta-xi^2*Q/(sigma-xi*u).                         (14)

Subtract xi*u*delta using (13). All remaining multiplier coefficients
are nonnegative: for xi>=0 this is the definition of xi_cap and the
order of the incoming weights; for xi<0 the coefficients increase.
The remaining Gram expression after adding xi^2Q/(sigma-xi*u) is

    ||sqrt(sigma-xi*u)*E+xi*pquad/sqrt(sigma-xi*u)||_M^2>=0.

Thus this is the same ORIGINAL matrix and column, not independent
energy selections. Let Qplus=Q+u^2*delta. Sending xi to -infinity
shows Qplus>=0, and

    Qplus=a^2*(A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2).

That prerequisite is the old scalar-return condition and is not
counted as an independent improvement.

For completeness, when Q,Qplus>0 the free maximizing xi is
xi_free=(sigma/u)*(1-sqrt(Q/Qplus)). If xi_free<=xi_cap, (14)
has supremum

    Bcal=(sigma/u^2)*(sqrt(Qplus)-sqrt(Q))^2.

Otherwise its supremum is

    Bcal=xi_cap*u*delta-xi_cap^2*Q/(sigma-xi_cap*u).

The latter case automatically has xi_cap<sigma/u. For Q>0,Qplus=0,
the supremum is sigma*Q/u^2. For Q=0,Qplus>=0 it is
u*delta*min(xi_cap,sigma/u), and it is zero when Q=delta=0.
These statements follow on putting y=sigma-xi*u>0: the objective is

 sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2-(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The earlier first-row budget is also retained, on its stated domain
0<a<1 and a*eta<1, where

    eta=b/(1+w+v), nu=(1+eta)*(1-a*eta)/a,
    Erow=a+3+1/a-(u*delta/a)*eta-C^2*eta^2.

Its exact identity is

 Erow=nu*(m+a*(Lambda20+B0))+(1+eta)^2*M11
                 +(1+eta)*eta*((w+v)*Lambda12+v*Lambda13).        (15)

Here is a direct derivation. For orthonormal physical vectors U,V set
gfirst=-eta*U+sqrt(nu)*V and use saturated values on

 Xphys=(U+u*gfirst,U,-b*U,-(1+v)*eta*U,-eta*U),
 Gphys=(gfirst,U,-eta*U,-eta*U,-eta*U).

The nonzero residuals are Q20=Q30=Q40=-a*nu,
Q12=-(1+eta)*(b-eta), and Q13=-(1+eta)*v*eta. Every other finite
residual is zero. Use ||gfirst||^2=[1+(1-a)*eta]/a and
<U,gfirst>+a||gfirst||^2=1-a*eta to check the target0 residuals.
The energy telescope gives Erow and the two gradient columns modulo
e are sqrt(nu)*E and (1+eta)*e1, proving (15).

In particular, for EVERY lambda>=0, (14) holds with its left side
eps+lambda*Erow, sigma replaced by sigma+lambda*nu, and cap replaced
by

 min((c20+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*beta),
                         (cB+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*W0)).              (16)

This follows by adding the TWO exact budgets before using (13), so
the same m and original incoming coefficients must pay for both.
It does not replace any of the older2948 conditions. For example,
putting Wrow=max(beta,W0), Krow=max(u,a*Wrow) in (13),(15),(2) gives

 u*delta<=Krow*Erow/nu+2*sqrt(Q*Erow/nu).

For delta>0, v>1, ab<=1 and c(v-1)<=1, Krow=u and Q<1. These imply
Erow>nu*delta^2/u^2 and

    b<(a+3)*(C-a-2)/((a+1)*(C+a+2)).

To see the latter equivalence, the direct factorization is

 u^2*(Erow-nu*delta^2/u^2)
    =((a+3)-(delta+u*C)*eta)*((a+3)+(u*C-delta)*eta).

The second factor is positive since C>A and u*A>delta. Substituting
eta=b/(C-A-b) in the positive first factor gives the displayed
bound. All its hypotheses remain.

## 5. A further matched full-column inequality near equality

In this section v>0 and all constants are the ones already defined.
Let

    dphys=a*b*c*v=(1+v)*z,
    nbar=s*(2C-(C+1)*v)/v>=0,
    rcoef=ell*mu^2+mu*hcoef^2>0,
    Lnorm=sqrt((u-a*alpha)^2/sigma+a^2/(1+Hbar)),
    Lterm=sqrt((alpha-beta)^2/sigma+1/(1+Hbar)),
    Kterm=(dphys/x)*Lterm*sqrt(nbar), Jfee=a/(2*x),
    Pcost=max(ell*mu*Hpre/cB,ell*mu*beta/c1,c03old/c03,1/k),
    Gcost=max(mu*Lnorm^2,Pcost).

All denominators are strictly positive. If nbar<0, the original
terminal budget (9) already excludes the word; it is never square-rooted.

Every full original array satisfies the following explicit scalar test.
Write y=sqrt(eps), which requires eps>=0, and set

 tau_max(y)=(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y
       +sqrt((sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)^2+4*jcoef*(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)))
                                                            /(2*jcoef),
 Psi(y)=rcoef*tau_max(y)^2
            +2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*tau_max(y)*y+Gcost*y^2.

Then

                              R<=Psi(sqrt(eps)).                 (17)

Here is the full derivation retaining the actual quadratic column.
The vector identity, checked in all five coordinates, is

    pquad=uE-aX-jcoef*B+dphys*e4+ab*e.

The original terminal rows give

    2<E,e4>_M=a*Lambda40-Lambda04,
    2<J,e4>_M=2<E,e4>_M+beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14.

Since X=Y+alpha E, they imply

 x<B,e4>_M=(alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M
                              -beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/2.

Taking the inner product of pquad with B therefore gives

 <B,pquad>_M=(u-a*alpha)<E,B>_M-a<Y,B>_M-jcoef*Tcut
       +(dphys/x)*((alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M)
       -dphys*beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/(2*x).       (18)

Let eps_G=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)||Y||_M^2 and let eps_C be the cost sum
in (12). Thus eps=eps_G+eps_C with both nonnegative. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz gives

 ||(u-a*alpha)E-aY||_M<=Lnorm*sqrt(eps_G),
 ||(alpha-beta)E+Y||_M<=Lterm*sqrt(eps_G).

Also ||e4||_M^2<=nbar by (9), and
c14=beta*dphys/a. Drop the negative Lambda40,Lambda41 terms in
(18), use Lambda14<=eps_C/c14, and use
<B,pquad>_M>=-sqrt(Tcut*Q). The result is

 jcoef*Tcut<=sqrt(Tcut*Q)
        +(Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut)+Kterm)*sqrt(eps_G)+Jfee*eps_C.          (19)

For the other direction (4) and Avec=(u-a*alpha)E-aY+hcoef*B give

 R<=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps_G)
                                    +mu*Lnorm^2*eps_G+Pcost*eps_C
  <=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps)+Gcost*eps.           (20)

The cost bound follows by comparing each cost in (4) to the cost of
the SAME multiplier in (12); their maximum ratio is precisely Pcost.
Thus costs and energies have not been chosen from different arrays.
Replacing eps_G,eps_C separately by eps in (19) gives, for
tcut=sqrt(Tcut)>=0,

 jcoef*tcut^2-(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)*tcut-(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)<=0.

Its nonnegative root is tau_max(y). The right side of (20) increases
with tcut>=0, which proves (17).

This supplies a quantified positive-gap exclusion test. Psi is
continuous and strictly increasing on [0,infinity), tends to infinity,
and

    Psi(0)=rcoef*Q/jcoef^2.

Consequently, if R>rcoef*Q/jcoef^2, there is a unique y0>0 with
Psi(y0)=R, and every full array must have

                           eps>=y0^2>0.                         (21)

Strict increase follows from the explicit nondecreasing positive
coefficients in tau_max and Gcost>0. This is an algebraic definition
and proof; no numerical root finding is used. In particular Q=0,R>0
forces a positive eps, even when delta=0 and the first-row bound
(14) alone is zero. This prices a further original cross column.
No uniform lower bound as v,ell,R,Q or other factors vanish is claimed.

## 6. COMPLETE original-array matching on the new equality locus

Assume eps=0 and R>0, still with a,b,c>0,bc<=1,0<v<2. Equation(12)
forces ME=MY=0, hence MX=0, and

    B0=B1=Lambda20=Lambda03=Lambda14=Lambda23=0.

Equation(6) now gives Lambda04=0, and (7) gives Lambda02=0.
The first moment in (3) forces Lambda01=2; node0 flow then gives
Lambda10=2A. Its diagonal is m=1-a^2-2a, so

                         a=sqrt(2)-1, a*A=1.                    (22)

Set

    Tstar=R/rcoef>0, r13=2*rho*Tstar, Bphys=Hpre+w, s=Bphys+v.

On this locus EVERY original multiplier is forced as follows:

    Lambda01=2, Lambda10=2A, Lambda13=r13,
    Lambda12=(2*A*Hpre-(beta+w)*r13)/beta,
    Lambda21=2*Hpre+Lambda12+r13,
    Lambda24=(2*w*N+beta*Lambda21)/(w+v),
    Lambda42=Lambda24/c,
    Lambda32=2*Bphys+r13+(c-1)*Lambda42,
    Lambda43=(2*s*C-(w+v)*Lambda42)/v,
    Lambda34=(1-c)*Lambda42+Lambda43-2*s,                         (23)

and the other TEN off-diagonal coefficients are zero:

    02,03,04,14,20,23,30,31,40,41.

Let

    nstar=Lambda42+Lambda43-s*(s+2),
    vcol=(0,-rho,rho-1,1,0)^T, dcol=(0,0,0,-1,1)^T.

For this array the ENTIRE original matrix is

                  M=Tstar*vcol*vcol^T+nstar*dcol*dcol^T.          (24)

Thus a word on eps=0,R>0 has a full original certificate if and
only if (22) holds and the explicit array (23) has

    Lambda12,Lambda32,Lambda34,Lambda43>=0, nstar>=0.              (25)

All other surviving signs then follow from their displayed formulas.
In particular Lambda21>0, Lambda24>0, Lambda42>0. This is an
actual all-twenty-entry matching, not a supplied covariance-fiber test.

Here is the proof of necessity and sufficiency of these formulas.
From E=0 and X=0 in the M seminorm, MJ=-rho*MB. Equations(4),(8)
give Tcut=Tstar. The original row <e1,B> gives Lambda13=r13.
Node1's moment and flow give respectively Lambda12 and Lambda21
in (23). Since M14=0 and MJ=-rho MB with rho>0, MB has fourth
component zero. Hence M24=0 too, because e2=e-J-B. The original
entry 2M24=c*Lambda42-Lambda24 gives their displayed relation.
Node2's moment and flow give Lambda24 and Lambda32. Node4's
moment and flow give Lambda43 and Lambda34. There is no free
covariance or multiplier left.

Conversely impose (22), eps=0,R>0 and define (23), allowing real
coefficients temporarily. The node0,1,2,4 flows and moments hold by
construction. For node3 the flow follows by summing the other flows.
Its moment can be checked explicitly: substituting (23) gives

 -w*Lambda32+v*Lambda34
   =-2*w*Bphys-w*r13-c*(w+v)*Lambda42+2*s*(C-v)
   =-2*(w+N)*Bphys+2*s*(C-v)=2*v*(1+Bphys),

where c(w+v)Lambda42=2*N*Bphys-w*r13 and
w+N=C-v=1+Bphys. Thus the full flow and Me=0 hold.

The original first row vanishes because aA=1; also M14=M24=0,
M13=-rho*Tstar. Direct substitution of Lambda12 gives

    M11=-D/beta^2+2*b*w*rho*Tstar/beta=rho^2*Tstar.

For the constant term in this identity use A^2=2A+1:
1-b^2+2A-2*A*b*Hpre/beta=-D/beta^2.
For the second equality use eps=0 and (8), which give
D=(2*b*w*x-x^2)*Tstar. The kernel then determines M12.
Finally (4), with all its costs zero and E row zero, determines
Tcut=Tstar: its positive Tcut coefficient is
ell*mu^2+a^2*b^2*mu^3, and (8) gives exactly that same coefficient
after subtracting the known J terms from R=rcoef*Tstar.
Me=0 now fixes every remaining entry except M44=nstar and proves
(24). The vectors vcol and dcol are independent, so full PSD is
equivalent to nstar>=0. This proves sufficiency as well as necessity.

The matched quadratic calibration has no extra freely selectable term:

    Q=jcoef^2*Tstar+dphys^2*nstar.                              (26)

Indeed pquad^T vcol=-jcoef and pquad^T dcol=dphys, by (8). Equation(13)
applies to the flow-correct array, so (24) proves (26). Consequently
nstar>=0 is equivalently Q>=jcoef^2*R/rcoef. At Q=0 this is
impossible when R>0; the WHOLE zero quadratic column is retained.

No word at C>=193/25 is exhibited satisfying eps=0 and (22)--(25).
Nor is it proved here that their entire high-capacity region is empty.

## 7. Zero boundaries and the unresolved complete comparison

At v=0 with ell>0, z=theta=qcorr=0, k=k0=kold=b^2/ell. Identity
(10) still holds and its Gram has sigma>0, but some displayed costs
vanish. Strict-cost conclusions, Pcost, jcoef divisions, (17)--(26),
and the positive-gap equality classification above are NOT used there.
One retains the undivided identities (1)--(7),(10),(13),(15).

At ell=0 in this domain one necessarily has v=0,bc=1. Then pquad=Avec,
R=mu*Q, and the old undivided gap is b*beta*Q. No division by ell,
v,jcoef,c1,c03 or c23 is made on this boundary. No formal gradient
is deleted at v=0. At R=0 or Q=0, use the undivided norm identities;
zero M-energy always kills its WHOLE original column.

Notation: the printed a,b,c,d,beta,u,v,e,p_i,z_i,k,r,q,l,nu,eta,U,B,
D_i,d_i,D,K,H,J,L_dead,E_mix,j_min,A_i,Conj,MinHull,R_true below

## 1. Complete family and the comparison result

Fix an arbitrary four-step word in the CLOSED domain

    h=(a,b,c,d),  1<=b<=2, 0<=a<=b, 0<=c,d<=2.               (1)

The three other steps may vanish. The condition b>=1 is part of the
specified annihilating curvature, not a deletion of zero-step words
from the original seed problem. There is no symmetry of the word.

Choose ANY beta in[1/b,1] and amplitudes u,v>=0, including zero, and set

    e=1-a/b, p=(1,e,0,0,0),
    z_i=product_(0<=j<i)(1-h_j*beta),
    x_i=(u*p_i,v*z_i), g_i=(u*p_i/b,beta*v*z_i), 0<=i<=4.    (2)

These are samples of ONE static legal base function

    F_base(x,y)=x^2/(2b)+beta*y^2/2.

It is convex and1-smooth, has unique minimizer0, and gives the exact GD
recursion with the supplied original indices. Coordinate reflections
allow arbitrary real initial amplitudes, so u,v>=0 loses no geometry.

The first mode dies by the second update. The second need not die.
For 1<a<b<2, 1/a<beta<1, and 1/beta<c,d<2, its five signs are

    +, -, +, -, +.

Thus the interior contains FOUR genuine reversals with g_4!=0. This
is outside both the one-reversal/annihilation family and round27's
terminal-zero family. All product-zero boundaries remain in(1)--(2).

Put s=a+b+c+d, C=1+s. Keep every function value and EVERY ordered
interpolation inequality on nodes0,...,4. The energy being minimized is

    V=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f_4)
             +sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sC||g_4||^2.    (3)

In particular the terminal gradient term has not been dropped.

Define the nonnegative killed-mode quantities

    D=[a(2-a)+b(2-b)e^2]/b^2,
    K=2a(b-1)e(1-e)/b^2,  L_dead=D+K.                     (4)

Sections3--4 give explicit piecewise POLYNOMIAL formulas for J(beta),
the fully value-optimized separate scalar energy per v^2, and H(beta)>=0.
The complete joint value minimum is

    if 1-a*beta>=0: V_min=u^2 L_dead+v^2 J(beta);
    if 1-a*beta<=0: V_min=u^2 D+v^2 J(beta)
                                 +(u^2 K-v^2 H(beta))_+.   (5)

Both formulas agree at equality. They optimize all values simultaneously,
not only separable values. All twenty finite constraints are retained.
The minimum is attained by one static global smooth convex function.
Its genuine minimizers and true distance are given in Section7.

There is no residual amplitude optimization in the following formula.
If u^2+v^2=1, the first line of(5) has minimum min(L_dead,J).
For the second line, if K+H>0, the minimum is

    min{L_dead,J,(H D+K J)/(K+H)}.                         (6)

If K+H=0, it is min(D,J). The third candidate comes from
u^2=H/(K+H), and includes its endpoints when H or K vanishes.
Section6 removes the remaining curvature parameter by explicit finite
endpoint/polynomial-root rules, without a numerical calculation.

Write E_mix(h) for this exact minimum over beta, all normalized amplitudes,
and all values. Write j_min(h)=min_(beta in[1/b,1]) J(beta). Then

    min(0,E_mix(h))=min(0,j_min(h)).                       (7)

In particular ALL members of this joint family have V>=0 if and only if
ALL its separately value-optimized fast scalar tests have J(beta)>=0.
The killed scalar mode already has L_dead>=0. Any negative normalized
joint minimum equals an already available separate scalar minimum.

Consequently the full collection of optimized separate scalar tests,
even before adding ANY other current full-cone necessary conditions,
implies nonnegativity for this entire joint family. This is a complete
parameter comparison on(1), not a positive-price sample or a new
shortest-path formula without a comparison. No assertion is made that
the older necessary system is itself sufficient for a full certificate.

## 2. All values, original flow, and all directed constraints

For distinct i,j in{0,1,2,3,4}, use the accepted residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Let

    U=(b-1)u^2/(2b^2), B=beta(1-beta)v^2/2.

At the base values, direct substitution gives the symmetric slack

    w_ij=-Q_ij(F_base)=U(p_i-p_j)^2+B(z_i-z_j)^2.           (8)

Both weights can vanish. If f_i=F_base(x_i)+delta_i, ALL directed
inequalities are exactly delta_i-delta_j<=w_ij. Let D_i be the shortest
w cost from ORIGINAL terminal node4 to node i, with D_4=0, in the
COMPLETE five-node graph. Nonnegative cycles can be removed, even when
their cost is zero, so a shortest simple path exists.

Following a path from4 to i gives delta_i-delta_4>=-D_i. Since every
h_i>=0, the simultaneous value minimum is

    V_min=V_base-2sum_(i<4)h_i D_i.                        (9)

It is attained by delta_i=-D_i: the triangle inequality
D_j<=D_i+w_ij gives delta_i-delta_j<=w_ij for every ordered pair.
This also handles h_i=0 and coincident points; no node is discarded.

For the ORIGINAL full certificate, retain all twenty Lambda_ij>=0,
zero diagonal, and set

    ones=(1,1,1,1,1)^T, L_flow=diag(Lambda*ones)-Lambda,
    omega=(-2a,-2b,-2c,-2d,2s)^T,
    T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
    D_prim=diag(a(2-a),b(2-b),c(2-c),d(2-d),-s(s+2)).

Accepted04219554e41d9750 gives

    L_flow^T ones=omega,
    M_prim=D_prim+(L_flow*T+T^T*L_flow^T)/2,
    V+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij
                           =<M_prim,Gram(g_0,...,g_4)>.    (10)

For the auxiliary price problem, Lambda_ij is mass on i->j. Node4
is the source of2s; node i<4 is a sink of2h_i. From
w_ij>=D_j-D_i every such flow has

    sum Lambda_ij w_ij>=2sum h_i D_i.

Sending2h_i along an attaining4->i path gives equality. This verifies
the terminal-source orientation as well as(9). These price flows
are NOT full PSD certificates. The original sufficient condition still
requires M_prim PSD on all of R^5, with no imposed gradient equality,
rank restriction, support restriction, or removed multiplier sign.

## 3. Exact separate scalar distances and energy

For scalar points on a line, a shortest squared-distance path uses
their consecutive spatial gaps between the source and target. Indeed
an edge spanning gaps t_1,...,t_m>=0 costs(sum t_j)^2>=sum t_j^2.
Every source-target path crosses each intervening gap at least once.
Summing gives the lower bound, and the consecutive-gap path attains it.
Repeated points and zero cost weights cause no exception.

For the killed coordinate, the distances from node4 are

    U[e^2+(1-e)^2], U e^2, 0, 0, 0.                       (11)

Their optimized values have f_1=||g_1||^2/2 and f_2=f_3=f_4=0;
the extra amount above ||g_0||^2/2 at0 is2Ue(1-e).
Substitution in(3) gives exactly u^2(D+K). This proves(4), including
nonnegativity, rather than importing a previous draft.

For the fast coordinate put

    k=1-a*beta, r=|k|, l=b*beta-1, q=l*r,
    nu=1-c*beta, eta=1-d*beta.                             (12)

Here 0<=l<=1, 0<=r<=1, 0<=q<=r, and -1<=nu,eta<=1.
Its actual coordinates are

    z=(1,k,-l*k,-l*k*nu,-l*k*nu*eta).                      (13)

Let d_i be the UNWEIGHTED squared-gap scalar distance from z_4 to z_i
using ALL five scalar samples. The following table is exact:

    d_4=0,
    d_3=q^2*nu^2*(1-eta)^2,

    nu>=0:
       d_2=q^2[nu^2(1-eta)^2+(1-nu)^2],
       d_1=(r+q*nu*eta)^2;

    nu<=0:
       d_2=q^2(1-nu*eta)^2,
       d_1=q^2*nu^2*(1-eta)^2+(r+q*nu)^2;

    k>=0: d_0=d_1+(1-k)^2,
    k<=0: d_0=d_2+(1-q)^2.                                (14)

All formulas agree on their shared boundaries. To prove the table,
first take k<0. Node1 is-r, node0 is1, and the tail coordinates are
q,q*nu,q*nu*eta. If nu>=0 their order is4<=3<=2; if nu<=0 it is
3<=4<=2. They all lie in[-r,1], so node1 is a minimum and node0
a maximum. The gap rule gives(14). If k>0, reflect nodes1,2,3,4
through zero. The same d_1,d_2,d_3 result; node1=k now lies between
every tail point and node0=1, which gives the other d_0 formula.
At k=0 all tail points and node1 coincide, proving the boundary too.

The FULL separate scalar energy minimum per squared initial amplitude is

    J(beta)=beta*sum_(i<4)h_i[1+(1-h_i)beta]z_i^2
       -s*beta[1+C*beta]z_4^2
       -beta(1-beta)*sum_(i<4)h_i d_i.                     (15)

The first two terms are the exact base quadratic energy, including the
nonzero terminal term; the last subtracts the complete original-flow
price. Formula(9) and the scalar conjugate construction in Section7
show that it is attained by an actual ONE-dimensional smooth convex
function with a minimizer. It is therefore a necessary scalar test
for any full primitive certificate, not merely a relaxed test.

As a check on conventions, beta=1 has zero slack and(15) reduces by
telescoping to1-C^2*z_4^2. No divisions by z_i, r, q, nu or eta occur.

## 4. Exact joint distances: only two competing paths

Suppose first k>=0. Every fast tail point is<=k<=1. A shortest fast
path from4 to1 uses only tail points before1, and a shortest path to0
continues1->0. Those paths simultaneously attain the killed-coordinate
distances(11). Shortest paths to2 and3 use only tail points, and also
attain(11). Consequently every joint distance is the sum of its separate
scalar distances. Equations(9), (11), and(15) give the first line of(5).

Now suppose k<=0, and put r=-k. Node1 is the minimum-r, node0 the
maximum1, and every tail point lies in[-r,1]. For targets1,2,3,4,
the same argument gives

    D_1=U e^2+B d_1, D_2=B d_2, D_3=B d_3, D_4=0.        (16)

For target0, take a shortest simple path. It either avoids node1,
ends1->0, or uses node1 between two tail nodes i,j. In the last case,
removing that visit decreases the cost by

    2U e^2+2B(z_i+r)(z_j+r)>=0.                           (17)

Thus a shortest path of one of the first two types always exists.
No edge was removed from the original constraints: (17) proves a
permitted simplification of an optimal path, including equality cases.

If node1 is avoided, the best fast route goes through tail maximum
node2 before0. Its cost is U+B d_0. If the last edge is1->0,
the best preceding tail route to1 costs B d_1, and the total is
U[e^2+(1-e)^2]+B[d_1+(1+r)^2]. Hence

    D_0=min{U+B d_0,
                U[e^2+(1-e)^2]+B[d_1+(1+r)^2]}.            (18)

Both candidates are attained by actual original-node paths. With

    Delta=d_1+(1+r)^2-d_0>=0,
    H(beta)=a*beta(1-beta)*Delta,                          (19)

the extra total ORIGINAL flow price above the sum of separate prices is

    2a[D_0-U(e^2+(1-e)^2)-B d_0]
                           =min(u^2 K,v^2 H(beta)).        (20)

Nonnegativity of Delta follows because the path to1 then1->0 is an
available scalar route to0; it cannot be cheaper than d_0. Formula(17)
and the scalar gap proof establish(16)--(18) for ALL amplitudes and
weights, including zero. The first and last expressions in(20) agree
by4aUe(1-e)=u^2K and2aB Delta=v^2H.

Subtract(20) from the sum of the separate energies to obtain

    u^2(D+K)+v^2J-min(u^2K,v^2H)
                         =u^2D+v^2J+(u^2K-v^2H)_+.

This proves the second line of(5). At k=0, r=q=0, d_1=0, d_0=1,
and H=0, so it agrees with the first line. Joint prices are genuinely
positive when K>0, H>0, and both amplitudes are nonzero. Nevertheless
their ENTIRE gain is paid by the explicit killed-mode term u^2 K.

These strict inequalities occur throughout the four-reversal interior
in Section1 when both amplitudes are positive. There K>0, while the
terminal fast coordinate w=z_4 satisfies0<w<=q<1. The scalar gap rule
gives d_0<=(1-w)^2<1, whereas(1+r)^2>1. Thus Delta>0 and H>0
since beta<1. The redundancy is not caused by a vanishing joint price.

## 5. Full amplitude minimum and complete scalar comparison

Homogeneity permits u^2+v^2=1 for deciding signs. This convention is
only an amplitude parametrization; it is NOT a claim that the new
interpolant's true minimizer distance is1. Section7 computes that distance.

For k<=0 set t=u^2. The expression in(5) becomes

    tD+(1-t)J+[tK-(1-t)H]_+, 0<=t<=1.                    (21)

It is affine on either side of t=H/(K+H). A linear function on an
interval takes its minimum at an endpoint unless constant, in which
case the endpoints also attain it. Thus(6) lists EVERY required
candidate. When K+H=0 the positive part vanishes. This derivation
retains the pure scalar endpoints, ties, and flat segments.

Because D,K,H>=0, (5) implies for every beta and normalized amplitude

    V_min>=min(0,J(beta)).                                (22)

For the compatible case use L_dead>=0. For the incompatible case use
u^2D>=0 and the nonnegative positive part; v^2J>=min(0,J).
Taking all minima gives E_mix>=min(0,j_min). Conversely the admissible
choice u=0,v=1 gives E_mix<=j_min. These two bounds prove(7).

This also proves the desired comparison with the COMPLETE older system.
Let N(h) denote its other necessary conditions, whatever additional
full-cone restrictions they impose. On the explicit word domain(1),

    [N(h) and all optimized separate scalar tests pass]
        implies [N(h) and every joint test(2)--(3) passes].

The reverse inclusion after adding the joint family is tautological.
No condition in N was dropped, weakened, or asserted to follow from a
different unverified condition. The implication holds before N is used.
If J(beta)<0, its attaining scalar function already excludes the word;
the joint family cannot make the most negative normalized energy smaller.
If every J>=0, the joint family excludes nothing. No capacity s was
fixed, so this remains true on the threshold subset C>=193/25.

## 6. Exact elimination of the remaining curvature parameter

The word h is the supplied schedule, not an unknown value parameter.
For each such word the following is a finite exact formula for its
complete amplitude/curvature/value minimum. There is no unsolved LP
or search over paths in this formula.

If K=0, equations(5)--(6) give

    E_mix=min(D,j_min).                                   (23)

If K>0, define I_minus={beta in[1/b,1]: a*beta>=1} and

    R_mix(beta)=[H(beta)D+K J(beta)]/[K+H(beta)]
                                           on I_minus.

Then

    E_mix=min{L_dead,j_min, min_(beta in I_minus)R_mix(beta)}. (24)

An empty last set contributes no candidate. K+H is strictly positive,
so this rational expression has no pole. The equality endpoint a*beta=1
is harmless: H=0 and R_mix=J there.

Here is an explicit finite rule for the minima in(23)--(24). Partition
[1/b,1] at those of1/a and1/c that belong to it, omitting a reciprocal
when its denominator is zero. Include both original endpoints, with
singleton intervals permitted. On every resulting interval, choose the
applicable sign of k and nu in(12)--(15). Each z_i and d_i is then a
polynomial in beta, J is a polynomial of degree at most10, and on
I_minus the same is true of H. Their formulas agree at every breakpoint.

For j_min retain all interval endpoints and every interior real zero
of J'(beta). If J' is identically zero on a piece, its endpoints suffice.
Evaluate J at these algebraically defined candidates and take the least.

For the last minimum in(24), use the pieces in I_minus. Retain their
endpoints and the interior zeros of the explicit polynomial

    [K+H(beta)]J'(beta)+H'(beta)[D-J(beta)].                (25)

The derivative of R_mix is K times(25)/(K+H)^2. If(25) is identically
zero, that rational function is constant on the piece and its endpoints
suffice. Otherwise it has finitely many roots. The elementary derivative
condition for an interior extremum proves that this finite list is exact.
There is no division by a zero amplitude, zero step, zero product,
parallel affine slope, or zero cost. No polynomial roots are evaluated
by a computer in this draft.

Thus the formula covers ALL curvature and amplitude parameters, and
(7) gives a simpler complete decision of whether the resulting minimum
contains any information beyond the separate scalar tests.

## 7. One attaining function, actual minimizers, and true radius

For the joint optimum use f_i=F_base(x_i)-D_i. Define on R^2

    c_i=<g_i,x_i>-f_i,
    Conj_i(w)=c_i+<x_i,w-g_i>+||w-g_i||^2/2,
    Conj(w)=max_(0<=i<=4) Conj_i(w),
    F(x)=sup_w[<x,w>-Conj(w)].                            (26)

This uses ALL five finite nodes including terminal4. It does not assert
that the original base minimizer0 remains optimal after value changes.

For completeness, the construction's properties can be checked directly
as in accepted1252b8823bb5a290. Conj is finite and1-strongly convex, and
has quadratic growth. The supremum defining F has a unique maximizer
w(x). Strong convexity at two such maximizers gives

    <x-x',w(x)-w(x')> >= ||w(x)-w(x')||^2.

Hence w(x) is1-Lipschitz. The two maximizer inequalities prove that F
is differentiable with gradient w(x), convex and finite everywhere.
At g_i, expansion gives Conj_j(g_i)-c_i=Q_ij<=0, with equality for j=i.
Thus Conj(g_i)=c_i and x_i is a subgradient of Conj at g_i, proving
F(x_i)=f_i and grad F(x_i)=g_i. Repeated positions force the same jet
through their two directed inequalities, so this argument loses no
coincident-point boundary. The resulting F realizes the actual GD word.

To exhibit its minima, define

    A_i=Conj_i(0)=D_i-U p_i^2-B z_i^2,
    A_max=max_i A_i,
    Active={i:A_i=A_max},
    y_i=x_i-g_i=((1-1/b)u*p_i,(1-beta)v*z_i).               (27)

The directional derivative of the maximum of these finitely many
quadratics at0 is max_(i in Active)<y_i,w>. Its subgradient set is
therefore exactly the convex hull of the active y_i: inclusion of that
hull follows by supporting inequalities, and a point outside it is
separated by a direction for which its proposed subgradient inequality
fails. Consequently

    MinHull=argmin F=conv{y_i:i in Active}, min F=-A_max.   (28)

Indeed grad F(x)=0 exactly when x belongs to the subgradient set of
Conj at0, by the unique-maximizer condition. This proves existence of
actual minimizers without a fixed-optimum assumption.

For nonzero (u,v), x_0 lies strictly outside MinHull. For every i,
since p_i<=1,z_i<=1 and both curvatures are positive,

    <x_0,x_0-y_i>
      =u^2[1-(1-1/b)p_i]+v^2[1-(1-beta)z_i]
      >=u^2/b+beta*v^2>0.                                (29)

Thus R_true=dist(x_0,MinHull)>0. The following is an exact finite
distance formula, with no relaxation. Take the minimum of
||x_0-y_i||^2 over active i and the distances to every nondegenerate
segment between two active y_i,y_j. For such a segment put

    tau_ij=min(1,max(0,<x_0-y_i,y_j-y_i>/||y_j-y_i||^2)),
    dist_ij^2=||x_0-y_i-tau_ij(y_j-y_i)||^2.               (30)

The minimum of this list is R_true^2. A nearest point of a planar
convex hull to an exterior point lies on its boundary, which is a vertex
or an edge; all such edges occur in the listed segments. Every listed
segment also lies inside the hull, proving equality. Coincident vertices
use the vertex candidate and require no division.

In particular the actual normalized terminal objective is exactly

    2[F_base(x_4)+A_max]/R_true^2,                         (31)

because D_4=0. This is in the project's W=2R convention. Translating
a closest minimizer to0, subtracting min F, and scaling by R_true gives
initial distance1 and preserves the schedule and normalized objective.
The sign comparisons for V are unchanged by translations and scale
quadratically, so they did not need to replace true distance by ||x_0||.
The scalar tests use precisely the same construction in one dimension.

## 8. A concrete trap: forcing the base origin to remain optimal

In the genuine four-reversal interior of Section1, take v>0. Then
B>0 and there are positive numbers t,w with z_3=-t,z_4=w. Both killed
coordinates are zero at3,4. Formula(14) gives d_3=(t+w)^2, and(16)
therefore forces at the joint optimum

    delta_4-delta_3=B(t+w)^2.                             (32)

If one also imposed the base point (0,0) as an optimum, its base slack
to nodes3,4 would be B*t^2 and B*w^2. For ANY choice of its value shift
delta_star and any common shift of the finite values, the two ordered
constraints through that optimum would give

    delta_4-delta_3<=B(w^2+t^2),                          (33)

contradicting(32) by2Btw>0. Since d=h_3>0, attaining the full objective
minimum requires equality in the individual lower bound for node3 in(9).
Thus merely choosing other equally good finite values does not repair
this forced-origin problem. The exact finite minimum is legal, but its
minimizer moves. Equations(26)--(30) provide the actual function and
distance. This symbolic counterexample is why the terminal node and the
base optimum must not be silently identified in a retained-terminal case.

## 9. Boundary audit and exact remaining interface

All calculations retain a=0, c=0, d=0, b=1, a=b, beta=1/b, beta=1,
a*beta=1, c*beta=1, d*beta=1, either vanished amplitude, coincident
tail points, and all combinations of those cases. Costs remain
nonnegative and paths are justified by weak inequalities. Formulas
(14), (18), and(5) agree at sign boundaries; no gradient product was
cancelled. If both amplitudes vanish the energy is0. Every original
formal gradient and directed pair remains in the full certificate(10).

The structural reason for redundancy is now precise. The killed mode
has only two nonzero positions. Contraction places all fast tail points
between its two early scalar extrema. Therefore there is only one
incompatible sink, node0, and its entire extra price is bounded by K,
an already present positive scalar energy term. This argument survives
a nonzero terminal gradient and four fast reversals.

The following are NOT closed:

* A later-killed slow mode, with more than two nonzero sampled positions.
* Two retained signed modes, or arbitrary nonseparable base geometry.
* A killing step b>2, where the nonnegative D budget can fail, or a
  tail step beyond2, where the tail may leave the interval between the
  early extrema and the shortcut/path classification can fail.
* Words with a>b, outside the specified monotone killed-coordinate
  chronology, unless a separate argument is supplied.
* Original full h/Lambda/exact-flow/ambient-R^5 PSD feasibility at
  C>=193/25, and the unrestricted all-schedule asymptotic profile Goal.

These are limits of an explicit family, not proved obstructions to the
general problem. No full certificate is inferred from an auxiliary
price flow or from nonnegativity on these prescribed modes.

The counterexample skill was used to attack the forced-origin premise
and the coincident/zero-product boundaries. The former is refuted in

The formula is supported by the proof, not by that unsuccessful attack.

It supplies a proof handoff at intended completion28/attempt29 including
