# C98: paid anchor innovations and arbitrary optimum slack

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED DRAFT, subject to the author audit recorded
in the handoff. This is actual runtime round 2 of the current allocation,
completed baseline 27, completed ceiling 29, attempted ceiling 30 including
one historical interruption. No computation or formal gate is authorized.
The original arbitrary-schedule exact-profile Goal remains OPEN.

The accepted mathematical inputs are `1252b8823bb5a290` (the original
directed interpolation inequalities and its explicit static interpolant)
and `b98bb807d514e80d` (the ORIGINAL benchmark and its crude upper bound).
Every other assertion used below is proved in this joint text. C97 and
the older Markov candidates are context, never mathematical premises.

## 1. Objects, scope, and the new distinction

Use smoothness 1. A supplied word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) generates

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i,  g_i=grad F(X_i),
    f_i=F(X_i)-min F,  q_i=||g_i||^2,
    V=2 f_n / R_init^2,  R_init=dist(X_0,argmin F)>0.

The included optimum is star, with X_star=g_star=f_star=0. The ORIGINAL
directed residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.       (1)

For a nonzero queried gradient put

    A_i=sqrt(q_i), u_i=g_i/A_i,
    eta_i=<X_i,g_i>/q_i,
    delta_i=f_i-q_i/2,
    z_i=<X_i,g_i>-f_i-q_i/2.

The two optimum rows imply

    eta_i>=1,  delta_i>=0,  z_i>=0,
    delta_i+z_i=(eta_i-1)q_i.                         (2)

The affine value reserve is delta_i and the optimum upper-row slack is
z_i. They are different quantities. The constructions below make both
strictly positive. The class bounds allow either to be zero and do not
prescribe any queried value within the legal interval (2).

Three conclusions are proved here.

* Arbitrary slack does not rescue an aligned-anchor Markov trajectory
  satisfying 1<=eta_i<h_i. Its amplitude contraction is already forced
  by its support geometry, independently of all values and remote rows.
* A genuinely future-correlated anchor does escape that contraction.
  Sections 4--6 provide an exact finite family and a bounded rule for
  every word with min h>1, with all pairs, one static function, a true
  radius, a payoff and a paid continuation law.
* Sparse future correlations still cannot supply the original benchmark
  on the original enclosing-m recursive words. Section 8 gives an exact
  weighted bound for arbitrary locations and arbitrary values, a free
  terminal, and even arbitrary signs at the exceptional transitions.
  A nonvanishing benchmark payoff requires order n/m nonzero future
  anchor innovations under the stated support restriction.

The last conclusion does NOT exclude a dense bounded-rule anchor, a
different dependence law, or trajectories whose support ratios cross
the physical steps. It is not an upper bound on unrestricted W.

## 2. The finite sign law and the actual cost of a correlated anchor

For queried indices 0,...,n-1, suppose the unit directions have Markov
product inner products

    <u_i,u_j>=product_(k=i)^(j-1)rho_k, i<j, |rho_k|<=1. (3)

For strictly interior rho_k, these are the moments of a literal finite
two-state sign law. Let S_0 be fair and independently let the bond signs
J_sign_k have P(J_sign_k=1)=(1+rho_k)/2. Set S_(k+1)=S_k J_sign_k. Then

    p(s_0,...,s_(n-1))=2^(-n) product_(k<n-1)
                             (1+rho_k s_k s_(k+1)).   (4)

Successive summation over the last sign normalizes (4); independence
of the bonds gives (3). Real coordinates are explicit:

    u_0=e_0,
    u_(i+1)=rho_i u_i+sqrt(1-rho_i^2)e_(i+1),            (5)

where the e_i are orthonormal. Hence PSD is not an assumption about a
formal Gram matrix. Formula (5) realizes it. The formula also allows
rho_i=+/-1, in which case no new direction is needed at that transition.

Conversely, from (3), when |rho_i|<1 the vector

    e_(i+1)=(u_(i+1)-rho_i u_i)/sqrt(1-rho_i^2)

has unit norm and is orthogonal to every u_j, j<=i. This follows by
substituting <u_j,u_(i+1)>=rho_i<u_j,u_i>. It is consequently orthogonal
to all earlier nondegenerate innovations. Thus (5) describes the
canonical real innovations of any such product-correlation data.

Write w_(i+1)=<X_0,e_(i+1)>. Earlier gradients are orthogonal to
e_(i+1), so actual GD, not an assigned support matrix, gives

    eta_(i+1) A_(i+1)
       =rho_i(eta_i-h_i) A_i+sqrt(1-rho_i^2)w_(i+1).    (6)

The initial e_0 coefficient is eta_0 A_0. Orthogonal decomposition gives
the EXACT identity

    ||X_0||^2 = eta_0^2 q_0
       +sum_(i:|rho_i|<1)
          [eta_(i+1)A_(i+1)-rho_i(eta_i-h_i)A_i]^2
                                  /(1-rho_i^2)
       +||X_perp||^2,                              (7)

where X_perp is the component perpendicular to all queried gradients.
For a degenerate transition the numerator must be zero and there is
no summand. For prescribed A_i, eta_i and rho_i, (7) is the minimal
squared norm realizing those support data when X_perp=0. This is only
a geometric realization statement; it is NOT interpolation sufficiency.

If 0 is not the closest minimizer, (7) is not the true initial radius.
The explicit constructions below have unique minimizer 0. For the
whole-class bounds we instead use

    A_0<=R_init,                                       (8)

which follows from 1-Lipschitzness of grad F between X_0 and ANY
minimizer, followed by taking the infimum of the distances. Thus no
nonclosest minimizer is silently used as the normalization.

## 3. Slack cannot repair the unforced support contraction

Assume every queried eta_i lies in [1,h_i). If w_(i+1)=0, (6) forces
rho_i<0 for nonzero consecutive gradients, and

    A_(i+1)=|rho_i|(h_i-eta_i)A_i/eta_(i+1)
            <=(h_i-1)A_i.                          (9)

For a radial initial point X_0=eta_0 g_0 all future coefficients w_i
are zero. The sharper product before the last inequality in (9) is

    A_j/A_i <= product_(k=i)^(j-1)
                                  (h_k-eta_k)/eta_(k+1). (10)

No f_i or z_i appears. In particular arbitrary optimum slack, even
horizon-dependent and approaching the whole allowed reserve, cannot
change this support obstruction. A zero queried gradient means its
point minimizes F and every later GD iterate stays there; its terminal
error is zero and is already covered separately.

For later use there is also a universal one-step bound, without (3),
any support restriction, or any condition on the initial anchor. Adding
the two adjacent rows (1) yields

    ||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2 <= h_i<g_i-g_(i+1),g_i>.

Completing the square gives the entire necessary disk

    ||g_(i+1)-(1-h_i/2)g_i|| <= (h_i/2)||g_i||.

For h_i>1 this implies

    A_(i+1)<=max{1,h_i-1}A_i.                      (11)

If the adjacent inner product is nonpositive, a stronger bound holds.
Write d=h_i-1>0 and t=-<g_i,g_(i+1)>/q_i>=0.
The same inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz give

    q_(i+1)/q_i <= d+(d-1)t,  t^2<=q_(i+1)/q_i.

Thus (t+1)(t-d)<=0 and 0<=t<=d. Maximizing the affine expression over
that interval gives

    q_(i+1)<=d max{1,d} q_i.                       (12)

These are necessary consequences of the original rows, not claims
that adjacent rows suffice for a legal trajectory.

## 4. An actual correlated-anchor escape: all rows displayed

Take the supplied physical word h=(3,10). For

    8/5<=k<4,  0<epsilon<1/2,

define in R^3

    g_0=e_0,
    g_1=(-e_0+e_1)/2,
    g_2=(k/2)e_0-(k/2)e_1+sqrt(k(4-k)/2)e_2,
    X_0=2e_0+e_1,
    X_1=-e_0+e_1,
    X_2=4e_0-4e_1.

The points obey the supplied GD updates. Their squared gradient norms
are q=(1,1/2,2k), and <X_i,g_i>=2q_i. Prescribe

    f=(3/2,3/4,3k)-epsilon,
    delta_i=q_i-epsilon>0,  z_i=epsilon>0.          (13)

The normalized directions have product correlations with

    rho_0=-1/sqrt(2), rho_1=-sqrt(k)/2.

The projection coefficient of g_2 on g_1 is -k, and its e_2 component
is precisely the positive innovation needed for (5). Also
<u_0,u_2>=rho_0 rho_1, so this is the actual Markov law, not only its
adjacent correlations. Choosing k=8/5 makes rho_0 and rho_1 different.

All six non-optimum residuals are

    Q_01=-1,             Q_10=-1,
    Q_02=4-5k/2,         Q_20=-1,
    Q_12=-4-3k/2,        Q_21=-(1+k)/2.             (14)

For example <g_0,X_2-X_0>=2 and
||g_0-g_2||^2=1+k, giving Q_02=4-5k/2.
Also <g_2,X_0-X_2>=-7k/2, giving Q_20=-1.
The adjacent expansions use <g_0,g_1>=-1/2 and
<g_1,g_2>=-k/2, giving the remaining entries of (14).
Subtracting the same epsilon from all finite values changes none of
these six residuals. The optimum rows are exactly

    Q_(i,star)=-epsilon,  Q_(star,i)=epsilon-q_i<0. (15)

Equations (14)--(15) cover every directed pair. Section 6 constructs
one fixed smooth function realizing all these jets and proves its
unique minimizer is 0. Its true squared initial radius is 5 and its
payoff is

    V=(6k-2epsilon)/5.                             (16)

For the definite choice k=8/5, epsilon=1/8, the terminal value is
187/40 and V=187/100. The second physical displacement has e_1
component -5. Both the positive affine values and the transverse
action are retained.

This legal example falsifies any extension of the ALIGNED estimate
(10) to a free initial anchor: eta_0=eta_1=2, h_0=3 would give
q_1<=q_0/4 in the aligned case, but here q_1=q_0/2. The paid initial
innovation is w_1=1. It is not a translation of the minimizer: the
constructed function has unique minimizer 0 and true radius sqrt(5).

This finite example is not a target-scale improvement. In fact every
member of this displayed family has V<24/5<81/16, while the accepted
single-cut bound on the same word is at least 81/16 (the cut at 10).
It certifies a real escape from a scoped hypothesis, not a stronger
all-schedule adversary.

## 5. A bounded nonstationary rule with a paid initial pulse

Here is a complete construction for EVERY supplied word of length
n>=2 with min_i h_i>1. The function is planned for the full word before
GD begins. Choose

    1<eta<min_i h_i,  0<theta<1,

for example eta=(1+min_i h_i)/2 and theta=1/2. Set the virtual terminal
entry h_n=eta. For i=0,...,n-1 put

    t_i=theta min{1,(h_i-eta)/h_(i+1)}.

Let s=t_0, q_0=1, and set

    q_1=(h_0-1)s/eta,
    v=sqrt(q_1-s^2),
    w=(eta-1)s/v,
    g_0=e_0, g_1=-s e_0+v e_1,
    X_0=eta e_0+w e_1.                             (17)

The quantity v is strictly positive: s<(h_0-eta)/h_1<
(h_0-1)/eta. Thus all coordinates in (17) are real and w>0.
For i>=1 define

    b_i=(h_i-eta)/eta,
    rho_i=-sqrt(t_i/b_i),
    A_i=sqrt(q_i), u_i=g_i/A_i,
    u_(i+1)=rho_i u_i+sqrt(1-rho_i^2)e_(i+1),
    q_(i+1)=t_i b_i q_i, g_(i+1)=sqrt(q_(i+1))u_(i+1). (18)

The initial transition is rho_0=-s/sqrt(q_1), whose square is
s eta/(h_0-1)<1. For i>=1, t_i/b_i<=theta eta/h_(i+1)<=theta<1.
Thus all rho_i lie strictly between -1 and 0, and (4)--(5), now including terminal index n, give
the full law and literal real realization. Every parameter comes from
the supplied word and the two scalars; there is no free Gram matrix
or collection of independently adjustable modes.

Set X_i=X_0-sum_(j<i)h_j g_j. The first support is eta, and

    <X_1,g_1>=(h_0-eta)s+wv=(h_0-1)s=eta q_1.

For i>=1 all future innovations are orthogonal to X_i. Formula (18)
therefore gives <X_i,g_i>=eta q_i by induction using actual GD.

Choose one common slack epsilon with

    0<epsilon<(eta-1)min_(0<=i<=n)q_i,
    f_i=(eta-1/2)q_i-epsilon.                       (19)

For example half the right-hand minimum fixes epsilon from the full
word. Both delta_i=(eta-1)q_i-epsilon and z_i=epsilon are positive.
This slack is not set anew at each join.

We prove EVERY non-optimum pair next. Common epsilon cancels from
each such residual. For 1<=i<=j<=n put

    P_ij=product_(k=i)^(j-1)(-t_k),
    E_ij=product_(k=i)^(j-1)(t_k b_k)=q_j/q_i,
    B_ij=sum_(k=i)^(j-1)h_k P_ik+P_ij,
    P_ii=E_ii=B_ii=1.

The guards imply

    0<t_i<1,
    h_i-t_i h_(i+1)>=eta,
    h_i-t_i>=eta.                                  (20)

For i<j, pairing alternating terms in B_ij proves B_ij>=eta.
For even j-i, group physical terms as
P_(i,i+2r)[h_(i+2r)-t_(i+2r)h_(i+2r+1)], followed by the
positive P_ij. The first group alone is at least eta and all groups
are nonnegative. For odd j-i, the last term after the analogous
pairs is P_(i,j-1)[h_(j-1)-t_(j-1)]; if there are no earlier pairs
this is at least eta, and otherwise the first pair is already at
least eta. Also

    B_ij=h_i-t_i B_(i+1,j)<=h_i,                    (21)

because B_(i+1,j)>0, including B_jj=1. Thus
eta<=B_ij<=h_i for every i<j with i>=1.

Inner products from (18) give <g_i,g_j>=q_i P_ij and
<X_i,g_j>=eta<g_i,g_j> for i>=1. Expanding the ORIGINAL (1) gives

    Q_(j,i)=(eta-1)q_i(P_ij-1)<0,
    Q_(i,j)=q_i[eta-B_ij-(eta-1)E_ij]<0.            (22)

The first inequality uses the alternating sign and |P_ij|<1; the
second uses B_ij>=eta. No history is discarded in B_ij.

It remains to check every pair involving the original query 0.
Let y_0=X_0-g_0. Equation (17) gives <y_0,g_1>=0. Every later
g_j is a scalar multiple of g_1 plus directions e_2,...,e_j, so
<y_0,g_j>=0 for ALL j>=1. The exact original reverse rows are

    Q_(j,0)=-(eta-1), j>=1.                         (23)

For the other orientation, <g_0,g_j>=-s P_(1,j) and direct GD
substitution gives

    Q_(0,j)=eta-h_0+s B_(1,j)-(eta-1)q_j, j>=1.    (24)

For j=1 use B_11=1<=h_1. For j>1 use (21).
Since s h_1<=theta(h_0-eta)<h_0-eta, (24) is strictly negative.
The optimum rows are

    Q_(i,star)=-epsilon,
    Q_(star,i)=epsilon-(eta-1)q_i<0.                (25)

Equations (22)--(25) include the terminal and every chronological
cross pair, in both directions. In particular the argument does not
claim that local tests or a PSD correlation law suffice.

## 6. One static function, exact radius, payoff and continuation

For either construction in Sections 4--5 define, using ALL its jets,

    H(v)=||v||^2/2+max{0,max_(0<=i<=n)
                                 (<X_i-g_i,v>-delta_i)},
    F(X)=sup_v(<X,v>-H(v)).                         (26)

This is exactly the full-data construction in accepted
`1252b8823bb5a290`: expanding its ith quadratic gives
||v||^2/2+<X_i-g_i,v>-delta_i. The proved all-pair rows therefore
give one everywhere finite convex differentiable 1-smooth F with
F(X_i)=f_i, grad F(X_i)=g_i and F(0)=0=min F. It is fixed before GD.

Because all delta_i>0, the maximum in (26) is zero in a neighborhood
of v=0. If X!=0, choose 0<a<1 sufficiently small that aX belongs
to that neighborhood. Then

    F(X)>=(a-a^2/2)||X||^2>0.

Thus argmin F={0}. Section 4 has exact squared radius 5. Section 5
has exact squared radius eta^2+w^2, and its exact payoff is

    q_n=[(h_0-1)s/eta] product_(i=1)^(n-1)(t_i b_i),
    V=[(2eta-1)q_n-2epsilon]/(eta^2+w^2).           (27)

In Section 5 the second GD displacement has nonzero e_1 component
-h_1 v. Subsequent queried innovations also have nonzero coefficients
in the actual displacement. Hence these are paid transverse changes,
including their full cost in the radius, the supports and the values.

The state transfer for every subsequent transition i>=1 is

    q_(i+1)=t_i b_i q_i,
    f_(i+1)+epsilon=(t_i b_i)(f_i+epsilon),
    delta_(i+1)+epsilon=(t_i b_i)(delta_i+epsilon),
    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i,                            (28)

with u_(i+1) propagated by (18) in the SAME growing coordinate system.
For a literal append to already fixed jets through index k>=2, retain
eta, epsilon, w, all old jets and all old transitions. A sufficient
boundary condition for the first new physical step h_k is

    h_k>eta,  t_(k-1)h_k<=h_(k-1)-eta.              (29)

Choose later transitions by (18), and require
epsilon<(eta-1)q_i at every new sample. These conditions preserve
all old guards, add the missing boundary guard, and keep every affine
reserve positive. The SAME proofs (21)--(25) then cover all cross
pairs of the extended history. This is an existence statement for
one interpolant of the jointly planned complete word. It does not
change an already running objective at a join, or assert that a
shorter instance's particular F already has the desired extension.

Replacing a shorter word's virtual terminal step by a physical step
does not come free: (29) and the retained epsilon reserve can fail.
The pulse w is part of X_0, not energy added during the run.

For arbitrary L>0 multiply F by L and use steps h_i/L. Both the
trajectory and normalized W=2R payoff formulas remain the same.

## 7. Entire sparse-anchor class: exact weighted necessary bound

Consider ANY legal nonzero queried trajectory with (3) and

    1<=eta_i<h_i for every queried 0<=i<n.          (30)

Allow arbitrary initial anchors, arbitrary dimensions, all values
permitted by (2), and a completely FREE terminal gradient and value
generated by the same function. No construction guard from Section 5
is imposed. In the canonical innovations define

    I={i in {0,...,n-2}: |rho_i|<1 and w_(i+1)!=0},
    E_anchor=sum_(i in I) log_+(1/(h_i-1)),
    K_anchor=cardinality(I), log_+(x)=max{0,log x}.         (31)

These are the actual support and initial coefficients relative to the
included minimizer 0. Additional components X_perp are allowed.
No claim that 0 is closest is needed, by (8).

Outside I, (9) applies. Inside I, (11) applies. Multiplying the exact
per-step upper bounds gives

    q_(n-1)/q_0 <= [product_(i=0)^(n-2)(h_i-1)]^2
                                             exp(2 E_anchor). (32)

If EVERY adjacent queried inner product is nonpositive, use (12)
inside I instead; the stronger version is

    q_(n-1)/q_0 <= [product_(i=0)^(n-2)(h_i-1)]^2
                                                    exp(E_anchor).  (33)

In (32), nonzero anchor coefficients may cause positive transitions.
Thus (32) does not silently retain an all-negative sign restriction.
The weights in E_anchor show that correlations after steps h_i>=2 receive
no improvement factor at all in this estimate.

For a final physical step ell=h_(n-1) in (1,2), integrating the
1-Lipschitz gradient along that step gives

    2 f_n<=2 f_(n-1)-ell(2-ell)q_(n-1).

The actual optimum upper row and (30) imply
f_(n-1)<=(eta_(n-1)-1/2)q_(n-1), so

    2 f_n < [(ell-1)^2+2(ell-1)]q_(n-1).           (34)

This step leaves the terminal gradient entirely unrestricted. Combined
with (8), equations (32)--(34) are true-distance bounds, even for
functions with a nonunique minimizer and arbitrary optimum slack.

## 8. Uniform comparison on the ORIGINAL enclosing-m words

For m>=4 fix throughout the entire word

    N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m,
    c=sigma(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Set h=H_m with these SAME enclosing-m parameters in every child.
The smallest and last step is ell=1+a, and

    1/5<a<1/2.

Indeed a=(m-1)/[(m+1)sigma]>=3/(5sigma)>1/5, since sigma<3,
and a<1/sigma<1/2, since sigma>2.

Let D be the product of ALL physical offsets h_i-1. The recursion
D_(j+1)=D_j^2 a c^j with D_0=1 proves by induction

    D=a^(N-1)c^(N-m-1)=beta^n c^(-m).              (35)

The product in (32) is D/a, since only the last physical step is
omitted. Use gamma=2 for the general-sign estimate (32), or gamma=1
under the all-nonpositive adjacent hypothesis of (33). Equations
(8), (32)--(35) prove the whole-class upper bound

    V <= (1+2/a) beta^(2n)c^(-2m) exp(gamma E_anchor).     (36)

This includes arbitrary horizon-dependent values, support ratios,
correlations, pulse positions and pulse magnitudes satisfying the
specified class hypotheses. The aligned class has E_anchor=0, so (36)
already closes arbitrary-slack repair and is stronger than the
previous tight-row estimate. Section 5 has only one possible queried
future coefficient, w_1, so it is covered as well.

For the ORIGINAL all-split benchmark, accepted `b98bb807d514e80d`
gives B_n<=1+4 n^(log_2 3)<=1+4*3^m. Therefore

    B_n V <= (1+2/a)(1+4*3^m)c^(-2m)
                             exp(-2n/m+gamma E_anchor).   (37)

We used log(1-1/m)<=-1/m, not an asymptotic replacement of the word
or benchmark. If E_anchor=o(n/m), (37) tends to zero. More quantitatively,
E_anchor<=2n/(gamma m) already forces a zero limit, because c>=sigma and
sigma^2=3+2sqrt(2)>3, while 1+2/a<11.

The exact weights identify where an exception could help. Offset
level 0 is a, level 1 is beta<1, and every level >=2 has offset at
least beta c=sigma(1-1/m^2)>1. Consequently, if K_0 and K_1 count
indices in I following physical levels 0 and 1, then

    E_anchor=K_0 log(1/a)+K_1 log(1/beta)
       <=K_anchor log(1/a).                              (38)

Correlations at higher physical levels contribute zero to this bound.

Suppose, along this sequence of ORIGINAL words, a family from Section
7 has liminf B_n V>0. Take a constant v_0>0 with B_n V>=v_0 for all
sufficiently large m. From the sharper (36) one MUST have

    gamma E_anchor >= 2n log(1/beta)+2m log c
                  -log B_n-log(1+2/a)+log v_0.     (39)

Here m log(1/beta)->1, log(1/a)->log sigma, and all terms of order m
are negligible relative to n/m, since m^2/(2^m-1)->0. Equations
(38)--(39) therefore imply the precise necessary count condition

    liminf_(m->infinity) K_anchor m/n >= 2/(gamma log sigma). (40)

In particular K_anchor=o(n/m), including any fixed number of arbitrarily
located anchor pulses, is excluded. The stronger constant 2/log sigma
applies when all adjacent correlations are nonpositive; the constant
1/log sigma applies when the exceptional transitions have free signs.

Neither (36) nor (40) asserts sufficiency. They do not bound the
unrestricted W_n(H_m), and they do not exclude a finite-state rule
which prepares many nonzero anchor coordinates from the full word.

## 9. Remaining interface, failed extensions and literature audit

The slack-only escape is closed in the complete class (30) with a
radial anchor; it does not require tight optimum rows or a floor on
the positive reserve. Retuning eta_i inside [1,h_i) cannot evade it.
The initial-pulse construction proves that a future-correlated anchor
is a real legal freedom. The finite family (13)--(16) disproves an
unqualified extension of the aligned contraction to that freedom.
The weighted bound then closes sparse-pulse repair on the original
words, even allowing arbitrary pulse locations, values and terminal.

What remains is a bounded rule preparing sufficiently many effective
future correlations, or support ratios crossing the physical steps,
with every chronological interpolation row and the true radius paid.
The identity (7) alone is not such a rule and is not presented as one.
It prices any proposed rule. Likewise (39) is only necessary; enough
nonzero entries does not imply that their amplitudes, cross rows or
actual payoff work. No arbitrary-h matching lower bound follows.

Older UNVERIFIED `c035d2edbaffb2c0` and `fd7036b719ef9645` were read
for their full domains: consecutive first-occurrence ruler blocks,
constant queried gradients within ordinary blocks, and their stated
terminal/intercept restrictions. This draft changes gradients at
every physical sample and studies the initial future correlations.
It neither uses nor claims to subsume those older results.

Matlas queries about Markov gradient slack and innovation norm budgets
returned multi-task gradient surgery, mirror-prox bounds, Brownian
precision matrices and reciprocal Gaussian processes. None establishes
the needed GD inequalities. The built-in web fallback located the
already-local Taylor--Hendrickx--Glineur paper, *Smooth Strongly Convex
Interpolation and Exact Worst-case Performance of First-order Methods*,
arXiv:1502.05666; its definitions, Theorem 4, proof and construction in
Sections 2.1 and 2.5 were read. Its terminology was checked at mu=0,
L=1. Here the interpolation premise is the accepted self-contained
fact `1252b8823bb5a290`, not a newly imported external theorem.

The already-local Ising-chain reading from C97 was recalled solely as
background for the finite sign language. Equations (4)--(7) are
proved directly, so no probability or covariance theorem is a proof
premise. A new covariance-paper download is unnecessary: this branch
has reduced to the same audited finite independent-bond law and
explicit orthogonal decomposition, not a new Gaussian-process result.

All calculations in this text are symbolic author arguments. No
numerical evaluation, solver, machine algebra, replay, subagent,
consult, installation, fact_submit or newly accepted fact was used.

evidence:
# Threshold exclusion of the fully matched original-array locus

Status: complete joint proof DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max4 round34,
the last analytical round allocated by TASK.md and guidance77175b3daa836eea.
No numerical evaluation, machine algebra, optimization, replay, verifier,
consult, installation, or subagent is used. No fact is asserted.

The new result decides the ENTIRE matched eps=0 locus from round32 at
C>=193/25: it has no member with all twenty original coefficient signs,
the original flow, and PSD on all five formal gradients. This is a
restricted-locus exclusion, not a no-seed theorem for the full cone.

A further result on the entire first-step slice h0=sqrt(2), including
positive eps, forces the last step v>sqrt(2). On that slice an explicit
strictly positive lower bound for eps is proved below. The bound is
EXACTLY equivalent to the OLD repaired-cut and unit-quadratic tests on
its stated domain. Thus it is redundant with the COMPLETE older system;
no old-system survivor or independent new scalar separator is claimed.

The accepted inputs are04219554e41d9750, Section10, for the full primitive
identity, and1252b8823bb5a290 for realization of the explicit triangle
jets used in Section5. The previous drafts079d08f058988dc4 and
f2aab392648bc228 are not premises. Their needed algebra is reproduced
as part of this ONE joint proof in the appendices.

## 1. Original coordinates and the precise result

Use h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,v), where a,b,c>0, v>=0, bc<=1. Write

    u=1+a, beta=1+b, w=1+c, A=2+a, N=A+beta,
    C=1+sum h=N+c+1+v, Ecap=1+v,
    t=c/Ecap, mu=1+t, ell=a^2*b*(1-b*t),
    R=ell*N^2+mu-C^2*a^2*b*beta*t^2,
    D=b^2*N^2-A^2.

The original certificate has Lambda_ij>=0 for every distinct i,j in
{0,1,2,3,4}, zero diagonal, L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda, L^T e=omega,
and M=Dmat+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 PSD on ALL of R^5. Here e is the all-ones
column, T is the unit-diagonal prefix matrix, omega and Dmat are the
full flow and diagonal from accepted04219554e41d9750. Their entries
and the exact primitive identity are restated in Appendix B.

For 0<v<2 define Hbar as the positive root of

    (1-bt)Hbar^2+(beta-2bw)Hbar-bw^2/mu=0,
    k=Hbar/(a^2*mu), x=b*(w+Hbar*mu)/(1+Hbar),
    rho=x/beta, eps=kR-D.

Appendix B reproduces the original-row identity proving eps>=0.
On eps=0 with R>0 it forces a=sqrt(2)-1, all twenty original entries,
and the full matrix displayed in Appendix A Section1. The theorem here
is that none of those simultaneous equations and signs can hold at
C>=Cstar:=193/25. The negative algebraic root, R=0, v=0, and other
zero/limit boundaries are addressed in Section4 and Appendix A.

In Sections2--7 set a=sqrt(2)-1 and A=1+sqrt(2); hence aA=1 and
A^2=2A+1. For all b,c>0, bc<=1, 0<v<2, define

    chi=cv/(c+Ecap), gamma=1+chi=w/mu,
    xi=b*mu/x, kappa_eps=b*mu/(Hbar*beta)>0.

The two root identities, valid independently of eps=0, are

    chi*rho^2+rho=bw/beta,
    gamma*xi^2-xi=chi*b*mu/beta.                        (1)

The first follows by rewriting the Hbar polynomial as
beta*Hbar*(Hbar+1)=b*mu*(Hbar+gamma)^2 and using
rho=Hbar/(Hbar+gamma). Substituting xi=b*mu/(beta*rho)
gives the second. Both roots are accounted for in Appendix A Section2;
the negative rho root would make the original Lambda13 negative.

Direct expansion, without any matrix relaxation, gives

    b^2*C^2*c^2
      =Ecap^2*[A^2+(1-xi^2)D-kappa_eps*eps].            (2)

Indeed R/a^2=b*beta*(N^2-C^2*t^2)-mu*D. Inserting
eps=Hbar*R/(a^2*mu)-D, and using
mu*(1+Hbar)/(Hbar*b*beta)=mu^2/x^2, yields (2).

## 2. A uniform bound for the admissible root

Let b0 be the positive root of b0(A+1+b0)=A and N0=A+1+b0.
Then b0>3/5: the defining quadratic at3/5 is
24/25-2A/5<0 because A>12/5.

If b>=b0 and 0<v<=sqrt(2), then

                              xi>7/8.                 (3)

To prove this, evaluate the second polynomial in (1) at7/8. Its value
is [-7+chi*(49-64*b*mu/beta)]/64. Since b/beta>3/8,

 chi*(49-64*b*mu/beta)
   < v*[49t/(1+t)-24t]
   <= v*(73-28sqrt(6))
   < (10/7)*(19/4)=95/14<7.

For the middle inequality put y=1+t>0 and use
24y+49/y>=28sqrt(6), obtained by squaring
sqrt(24y)-7/sqrt(y). The last inequality uses
sqrt(6)>39/16, sqrt(2)<10/7. The constant term of the polynomial
gamma*z^2-z-chi*b*mu/beta is negative, so it has exactly one positive
root and is negative between zero and that root. Its negativity at7/8
therefore proves (3).

A second bound, needed later, is

    b>=10/11 and 0<v<=sqrt(2)  implies  xi>11/12.       (4)

At11/12 the same polynomial has value
[-11+chi*(121-144*b*mu/beta)]/144. Now b/beta>=10/21, so

 chi*(121-144*b*mu/beta)
   <=v*[121t/(1+t)-(480/7)t]
   <=v*(11-sqrt(480/7))^2
   <(10/7)*(121/16)=605/56<11.

The middle inequality follows from the square giving
(480/7)y+121/y>=22sqrt(480/7). Also
33/4<sqrt(480/7)<11; the first squared comparison is7680>7623.
These establish the last strict bound and hence (4). Neither estimate
uses a numerical root evaluation or an independently chosen covariance.

## 3. Uniform exclusion of the entire matched equality locus

On the positive-energy matched locus, Appendix A proves directly from
the full matrix and original signs that

    0<v<sqrt(2), D>0, b>b0,
    Fcap(b)<0,

where

 Fcap(b)=b^5+(2A+3)b^4+(5A+4)b^3+2b^2-(5A+3)b-(2A+1).

That polynomial has exactly one positive root, since Fcap(0)<0,
Fcap'(0)<0, Fcap''(b)>0 for b>=0, and Fcap tends to infinity.
At Bcap:=10/11 its exact value is

    Fcap(Bcap)=(579919-229152*A)/161051>0,

because A<5/2 gives numerator>7039. Thus every actual member has

                            b0<b<Bcap.                (5)

The decisive use of the simultaneous equality is now (2) with eps=0:

    C*c/Ecap=sqrt(N^2-xi^2*D/b^2)
       <Klo(b):=sqrt(15N^2+49A^2/b^2)/8.                (6)

The radicand on the left is the actual positive squared quantity;
the strict inequality uses D>0 and (3). Since Ecap<A and
C>=Cstar, while N+A<2A+2<7<Cstar, we also have

    C*c/Ecap=C(C-N-Ecap)/Ecap
       >=Lcap(b):=Cstar*(Cstar-A-N)/A>0.                (7)

For fixed N, the expression decreases as Ecap increases to A, and
C(C-N-A)/A increases for C>=Cstar. This proves (7) without changing
the step word in the certificate.

The function Klo is convex on b>0. To check this without differentiating
a radical, it is the Euclidean norm of the nonnegative components
sqrt(15)(A+1+b)/8 and7A/(8b). The first component is affine, the
second is convex, the norm increases in each nonnegative component,
and its triangle inequality proves convexity. Since Lcap is affine,
Klo-Lcap is convex. It suffices to bound it at b0 and Bcap.

At b0, A/b0=N0, so Klo(b0)=N0. Define

    C0=Omega(N0,A),
    Omega(z,y)=(z+y+sqrt((z+y)^2+4zy))/2.

The exact rational comparisons

 A<29/12,
 (201/50)^2-(29/12+1)*(201/50)-29/12=131/15000>0,
 (77/10)^2-(201/50+29/12)*(77/10)-(201/50)*(29/12)
                                                    =19/1500>0

give N0<201/50 and C0<77/10<Cstar. Thus
Cstar(Cstar-A-N0)>A*N0, or Lcap(b0)>Klo(b0).

At Bcap use A<80/33 to get N<13/3 and A/Bcap<8/3. Therefore

    Klo(Bcap)^2<5671/576<(157/50)^2,

where the last cross-multiplied difference is
24649*576-5671*2500=20324>0. On the other hand A<169/70 gives

    Lcap(Bcap)>729926/232375>157/50,

where the last cross-multiplied difference is
729926*50-232375*157=13425>0. The bound A<169/70 follows from
9800<9801, and A<80/33 from2178<2209.

Convexity now gives Klo(b)-Lcap(b)<0 on the whole closed interval
[b0,Bcap]. Equations (6)--(7) require the opposite ordering. This is
the promised uniform contradiction. It uses the defining equality,
the original12 sign through Fcap, the terminal PSD restriction through
v<sqrt(2), the original13 sign selecting the root, and the actual full
quadratic identity. No defining condition of the matched locus was
replaced by a free Gram completion.

## 4. Boundaries and the precise scope of the exclusion

Appendix A supplies the following complete boundary checks, with their
proofs reproduced there.

* The negative rho root and the lower positive Ueq root have
  Lambda13<0. They are excluded by an original coefficient sign.
* At eps=0,R=0 the undivided identities force
  bN=A, cC=N(1+v), 0<v<=sqrt(2), so C<=C0<77/10.
* R<0 is impossible by the original repaired-cut energy identity.
  On positive energy Q=0 is impossible by the full quadratic column.
* b=0 gives D<0; c=0 gives eps=A^2(b+1)>0. The matched first step
  is a=sqrt(2)-1, so a=0 cannot be an equality boundary.
* Every original certificate with a zero physical step has C<15/2.
  This is proved by restricting the original PSD identity to merged
  data as a necessary restriction only; no original gradient is deleted
  from the hypothesis. Thus v=0, including ell=0, is excluded at threshold.
* The full original terminal moment and diagonal give v<2. The
  v=sqrt(2) boundary at positive R is already excluded by Q>=0.

The convex endpoint inequalities in Section3 are strict even on the
closed b interval and v<=sqrt(2). Thus sequences approaching b0,
Bcap, or that terminal endpoint cannot recover threshold capacity.
No division by a vanished energy, v, or ell is used in its separate
boundary argument. The complete twenty-entry array and full matrix
are in Appendix A, not merely a compressed sign system.

## 5. The old cut and middle-triangle tests, with actual witnesses

                                                    =19/1500>0

give N0<201/50 and C<77/10<Cstar. Omega increases in each positive
argument by its displayed formula. Thus R=0 is fully excluded at
threshold; R<0 contradicts the repaired-cut energy identity directly.

There is no b=0 or c=0 threshold boundary of the positive-R locus.
At b=0, D=-A^2, whereas eps=0,R>=0 requires D>=0. At c=0,
Hbar=b, mu=w=1 and eps=A^2*(b+1)>0. The a=0 boundary is absent because
the matched locus forces a=sqrt(2)-1. At v>=2 the original terminal
moment/diagonal estimate in Appendix B already forbids full PSD.

In fact EVERY original four-step full certificate with a zero physical
step has C<15/2<Cstar, whether or not it is a limit of this locus.
Here is a direct necessary restriction argument, retaining the original
matrix as the hypothesis. Evaluate its full polynomial identity on the
linear subspace that sets the two gradients and values adjacent to a
zero step equal. The corresponding positions are already equal by GD.
Merge the two sample indices in each interpolation residual: residuals
between the merged pair are zero, and the other new coefficients are
sums of original nonnegative coefficients. The resulting matrix is the
pullback of the full original PSD matrix, hence PSD. This produces a
necessary compressed certificate with at most three positive steps.
It is only a necessary restriction of the original full-space identity;
no claim of sufficiency on the original space is made.

For a positive three-step compressed word (u1,z1,w1), both endpoints
are strictly below2. For the first endpoint, its moment forces a
positive outgoing total O and its diagonal is
u1*(2-u1)+(1-u1)*O, negative if u1>=2. For the last endpoint,
the terminal moment has weights at least w1 and its diagonal is
outgoing-s*(s+2)>=0. Thus w1<=2C/(C+1)<2.
If z1<=1, then C=1+u1+z1+w1<6.
If z1=1+b1 with b1>0, the actual scalar function with derivative
clamp(x,[-b1/(1+w1),1]), started at x0=1+u1, has successive
gradients 1,1,-b1/(1+w1),-b1/(1+w1) and terminal position equal
to its terminal gradient. Integrating this derivative with f(0)=0
gives a convex differentiable1-smooth function with a minimizer at0.
The saturated-value telescope in the original identity gives

 V=(1+u1)^2-C^2*b1^2/(1+w1)^2>=0.

Consequently C*b1<9, and C=2+u1+w1+b1<6+b1<6+9/C.
It follows that C<3+3sqrt(2)<15/2. With one or two positive
compressed steps the endpoint bounds already give C<3 or C<5;
the empty word has C=1. This proves the assertion for every original
zero physical step, without using the singular Lambda43 formula.

A finite limit of positive-R matched members with v<=1 also cannot
retain threshold capacity: the nondifferentiated bound C<=4319/560
proved in Section5 persists in that closure. All original formal
gradients remain distinct in the full-space hypothesis.

The boundary ell=0 in this parameter domain requires v=0,bc=1.
The undivided Appendix B identities remain valid there. It is excluded
from the entire original threshold cone by the zero-step bound, without
division by ell or by v. The R=0 and Q=0 cases above likewise did
not identify or discard formal columns.

One can also obtain a UNIFORM separation from v=sqrt(2) on the
threshold equality locus. Let

 Nmin=Cstar*(Cstar-A)/(Cstar+A), bmin=Nmin-A-1,
 Dmin=bmin^2*Nmin^2-A^2,
 cmin=Cstar-2A-2,
 chimin=cmin/(cmin+A),
 rmax=2/(1+sqrt(1+4chimin)),
 ximax=1-chimin*(1-rmax)/(1+chimin),
 Lmin=(1-ximax^2)*Dmin/A^2.

All these denominators are positive, bmin>b0 and Dmin>0. To see the
latter assertions, Cstar>Omega(N0,A), as just proved, is equivalent
to Nmin>N0. Since Ueq>0, Cc<NEcap; hence
N>C(C-Ecap)/(C+Ecap)>=Nmin. The last fraction increases with C
and decreases with Ecap. Thus b>bmin and D>Dmin.
Also c>cmin>4/5 and v>1 imply chi>chimin. Since bc<=1,
bw/beta<=1, so (3) gives rho<rmax<1. It follows that xi<ximax<1.

Using Q>=0 and (21) with eps=0 yields

                 v <= sqrt(1+1/sqrt(1+Lmin)) < sqrt(2).     (23)

This includes nstar=0; no positive terminal-energy lower bound is
assumed. It also shows that a threshold sequence cannot evade the
positive-energy analysis by taking v to sqrt(2), D to0, or c to0.
Again, (23) follows using the older Q test together with the equality
equations, and is not presented as an independent old-system separator.



# Appendix B. Reproduced full original-row identity and matching

The following proof text derives the original-row remainder and every
entry of the matched full matrix. Its section/equation references are
local to this appendix. All of it is part of the present UNVERIFIED
joint draft. The main Sections3--7 supersede earlier open-locus remarks.

## 1. Original full interface and common identities

Let

    h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,v),  a,b,c>0, v>=0, bc<=1,
    u=1+a, beta=1+b, w=1+c,
    A=2+a, N=3+a+b, Hpre=2+a+b, H0pre=1+a+b,
    s=sum h, C=1+s=4+a+b+c+v,
    t=c/(1+v), mu=1+t,
    ell=a^2*b*(1-b*t), z=a*b*v*t,
    R=ell*N^2+mu-C^2*a^2*b*beta*t^2,
    D=N^2*b^2-A^2.

Let e_i be the five original standard columns, indexed0 through4,
e=sum e_i, and P_i=sum_(j<i)h_j. Define

    T_ii=1, T_ij=h_j for j<i, T_ij=0 for j>i,
    omega=(-2h0,-2h1,-2h2,-2h3,2s)^T,
    Dmat=diag(h0(2-h0),h1(2-h1),h2(2-h2),h3(2-h3),-s(s+2)),
    L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda, M=Dmat+(LT+T^T L^T)/2.

The hypotheses are ALL twenty signs Lambda_ij>=0 for i!=j, zero
diagonal, L^T e=omega, and M>=0 on ALL of R^5. There is no support,
rank, symmetry, reversal, or duplicated-gradient restriction.

The accepted identity is

    V_h+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=sum_(i,j)M_ij<g_i,g_j>,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                                 -s(s+1)||g4||^2, (1)

on formal data with x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i. Formal substitutions below
are used as polynomial identities; no unproved interpolation is assumed.

Te=e+P and the flow give e^TMe=0. Indeed e^TDmat e=-s^2-sum h_i^2
and omega^T(e+P)=s^2+sum h_i^2. Applying PSD to e+r*y for both
signs of the real number r gives Me=0. The same argument proves

    |<x,y>_M|^2<=||x||_M^2*||y||_M^2,
    ||x||_M^2=0 implies Mx=0,                           (2)

where <x,y>_M=x^TMy and ||x||_M^2=x^TMx. Under the flow, the
individual kernel equations are

    sum_j Lambda_ij(P_j-P_i)=2h_i(1+P_i), i<4,
    sum_(j<4)Lambda_4j(s-P_j)=2sC.                       (3)

These follow by expanding 2Me=2Dmat e+L(e+P)+T^T omega.

Put

    E=e0, J=e0+e1, B=e3+e4,
    m=||E||_M^2, S=||J||_M^2, Tcut=||B||_M^2, rJB=<J,B>_M,
    B0=Lambda30+Lambda40, B1=Lambda31+Lambda41,
    Avec=u*E-a*beta*J-a*b*mu*B,
    c03old=u*mu*z, c23old=a^2*b*beta*mu*v*t.

The three exact identities needed here are

    R=ell*mu^2*Tcut+mu*||Avec||_M^2
         +ell*mu*(Hpre*B0+beta*B1)+c03old*Lambda03+c23old*Lambda23, (4)

    D=beta*((b*w*H0pre-u)*B0+b^2*w*B1-2*b*w*rJB-beta*S
                     -u*Lambda20-b*v*c*(Lambda04+Lambda14)),       (5)

    2<E,B>_M=a*B0-Lambda03-(1+v)*Lambda04.                         (6)

To prove (4), use saturated values f_i=x_i*g_i-g_i^2/2 on

    x_base=(N,2+b,1,-c,-t), g_base=(1,1,1,-t,-t),
    x_aux =(1,-a,ab,-abc,-abt), g_aux=(1,-a,ab,-abt,-abt).

For these values Q_ij=(g_i-g_j)(x_j-g_j). In ell times the base
plus mu times the auxiliary, the complete nonzero residual list is

    Q30=Q40=-ell*mu*Hpre, Q31=Q41=-ell*mu*beta,
    Q03=-c03old, Q23=-c23old.

Every other ordered residual is zero. In particular Q13 cancels
because ell=a^2*b*(1-bt); at Q03 use ell+ab(1+abt)=ab*u, and
at Q23 use ell+a^2*b^2*mu=a^2*b*beta. Telescoping (1) gives
R; the two gradient columns modulo e are -mu*B and Avec, proving (4).

For (5), start the scalar two-step cut at x0=A with gradients
(1,1,-b), then extend FORMALLY with constant gradient -b and affine
values through the last two steps. Its energy is -D and its column
modulo e is beta*J. Its negative residuals are
Q20=Q30=Q40=-u*beta, and its positive residuals are
Q03=Q13=w*b*beta, Q04=Q14=(w+v)*b*beta. All others vanish.
Thus (1) gives

 D=b*beta*(w*(Lambda03+Lambda13)+(w+v)*(Lambda04+Lambda14))
                        -beta^2*S-u*beta*(Lambda20+B0).

Besides (6), direct multiplication of T gives

    2<e1,B>_M=beta*B0+b*B1-Lambda13-(1+v)*Lambda14.

Adding these rows, and using (w+v)-w(1+v)=-vc, gives (5).

The additional ORIGINAL row used this round is

    2<E,J+B>_M=-a*Lambda20+Lambda02+w*Lambda03+w*Lambda04.           (7)

In fact e2=e-J-B and
2M02=a*Lambda20-Lambda02-w*(Lambda03+Lambda04). This proves (7)
without any PSD quotient or new support assumption.

## 2. Why the old strictly capped equality ray cannot match

For reference, the earlier three-vector expansion used a positive k
and theta with

    F(k,theta)=b^2*w^2-z*theta+(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta^2/4
                                                     -k*ell*mu^2,
    x=b*w-a*theta/2,
    Z=z-(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta/2.

Here is the expansion, without importing the earlier draft as a premise.
Combining (4)--(6) and expanding two squares gives

 kR-D=||beta*J+x*B||_M^2+k*mu*||Avec-theta*B/(2*k*mu)||_M^2
       -F(k,theta)*Tcut
       +[k*ell*mu*Hpre-beta*(b*w*H0pre-u)+a*u*theta/2]*B0
       +beta*(k*ell*mu-b^2*w)*B1+beta*u*Lambda20
       +[k*c03old-u*theta/2]*Lambda03
       +[beta*b*v*c-u*(1+v)*theta/2]*Lambda04
       +beta*b*v*c*Lambda14+k*c23old*Lambda23.

For v>0, take the unique root obtained by minimizing F in
0<=theta<=Ucap:=2*beta*z/(a*u). The root lies strictly between
k0 and kold, defined below: the unrestricted minimum is already
positive at k0 and a small positive theta makes F negative at kold.
The restricted minimizing theta is min(theta(k),Ucap). Every displayed
cost is nonnegative. For the B0 cost use its value u*(1-bc) at
k0,theta=0; the other signs follow from k>k0,
theta<=theta(k)<2*k*mu*z, and theta<=Ucap.

On the strictly capped branch theta=Ucap<theta(k), so F=0 and Z>0.
If kR-D=0 and R>0, the positive costs and the two squares force

    ME=-(Z/u)*MB, MJ=-(x/beta)*MB,
    Lambda20=Lambda03=0.

Here x/beta<1 since bw<=beta and theta>0. Consequently

    M02=(Z/u)*(1-x/beta)*Tcut>0.

The two zero columns also give Tcut>0: otherwise both J and E would
have zero columns and (4), with its positive costs zero, would give
R=0. But the actual original row gives

    2M02=-Lambda02-w*Lambda04<=0.

This is a direct sign contradiction. The old relaxation could select
its Gram energies without satisfying this retained original entry.
The following quantitative argument uses (7) to remove its cap.

## 3. The unrestricted root and the new full-row remainder

Assume v>0 for now. Then ell>0, z>0 and 1-bt>0. Set

    k0=b^2*w/(ell*mu), kold=b^2*w^2/(ell*mu^2).

The minimum of F(k,theta) over all real theta is attained at

    theta(k)=2*z*k*mu/(1+a^2*k*mu).

It is strictly decreasing as a function of k: at each fixed theta,
partial F/partial k=-ell*mu^2-theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)<0, and the minimum
is attained continuously. At k0 the minimum divided by mu^2 is
b^2*(gamma-1)*(gamma+a^2*k0*mu)/(1+a^2*k0*mu)>0,
where gamma=w/mu>1. At kold it is negative, since F(kold,0)=0 and
the negative linear term improves it for small positive theta.
There is therefore a unique root k in (k0,kold).

Here is an explicit definition requiring no root search. Define

    Hbar=(2*b*w-beta
          +sqrt((beta-2*b*w)^2+4*b*w^2*(1-b*t)/mu))/(2*(1-b*t)),
    k=Hbar/(a^2*mu), theta=2*z*k*mu/(1+Hbar),
    x=b*w-a*theta/2=b*(w+Hbar*mu)/(1+Hbar), rho=x/beta,
    hcoef=theta/(2*k*mu), jcoef=a^2*theta/2,
    rstar=u*theta/2.

The positive Hbar solves

    (1-bt)*Hbar^2+(beta-2*bw)*Hbar-b*w^2/mu=0,

which follows by substituting theta(k) into F=0. Also

    0<rho<1, hcoef+jcoef=z,
    a*x-a*b*mu=hcoef, k*ell*mu^2+theta^2/(4*k*mu)
                                            =2*b*w*x-x^2.         (8)

The inequalities use mu<w and bw<=beta, with strictness supplied
by Hbar>0. The identities follow by expansion and F=0.

Full original feasibility itself forces v<2. Indeed the terminal
diagonal is n=||e4||_M^2=sum_(j<4)Lambda4j-s(s+2)>=0.
Every weight in the last row of (3) is at least v. Hence

    v*n<=s*(2C-(C+1)*v), so v<=2C/(C+1)<2.                       (9)

We now work on 0<v<2; v>=2 was already excluded by this original row.
Define the nonnegative correction

    qcorr=max(0,((1+v)*rstar-beta*b*v*c)
                         /(w+(1+v)*(1-rho))),
    rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho),
    X=beta*J+x*B.

The EXACT original-array remainder is

    eps:=k*R-D
       =(1+Hbar)*||X||_M^2
         -2*(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)*<E,X>_M+k*mu*u^2*m
         +cB*B0+c1*B1+c20*Lambda20+qcorr*Lambda02
         +c03*Lambda03+c04*Lambda04+c14*Lambda14+c23*Lambda23,      (10)

where

    cB=k*ell*mu*Hpre-beta*(b*w*H0pre-u)+a*rshift,
    c1=beta*(k*ell*mu-b^2*w), c20=beta*u-a*qcorr,
    c03=k*c03old-rshift+w*qcorr,
    c04=beta*b*v*c-(1+v)*rshift+w*qcorr,
    c14=beta*b*v*c, c23=k*c23old.

To check the identity, first combine (4) and (5). Its Gram part is

 beta^2*||J||_M^2+2*beta*b*w*<J,B>_M+k*ell*mu^2*Tcut
                                                 +k*mu*||Avec||_M^2.

Subtract 2*rshift*<E,B>_M+2*qcorr*<E,J+B>_M from that Gram part.
Restore them using (6) and (7); this gives precisely all costs in
(10). Since rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho), the subtraction differs
from 2*rstar*<E,B> by 2*qcorr*<E,X>/beta. F=0 and (8) turn the
uncorrected Gram into ||X||^2+k*mu*||uE-aX||^2. This proves (10).

Every displayed cost is nonnegative; cB,c1,c20,c03,c14,c23 are
STRICTLY positive. Here is the full sign and PSD check.

Let

    qmax=beta*u*(sqrt(k*mu*(1+Hbar))-a*k*mu).

Then

    0<=qcorr<qmax<beta*u/(2a).                                  (11)

If qcorr=0 this follows from Hbar>0. Otherwise put
tau=sqrt(Hbar/(1+Hbar)) in (0,1), Vprod=vbc, and
Sden=2+b+c+v. Direct substitution gives

    qcorr=(beta/a)*Vprod*(u*tau^2-a*beta)
                              /(Sden-Vprod+Vprod*tau^2),
    qmax=(beta*u/a)*tau/(1+tau).

The numerator of qcorr is positive in this case. The inequality
qcorr<qmax is equivalent to

    Vprod*(1+tau)*(u*tau-a*beta)<u*tau*Sden.

Its left side is smaller than 2*Vprod*u*tau. Moreover
2*Vprod<=2v<2+b+c+v=Sden, using bc<=1 and v<2. This proves the
strict inequality. The upper bound on qmax follows from
tau/(1+tau)<1/2.

Also rshift>0: when qcorr>0 its numerator is less than
(1+v)*rstar, while its denominator is strictly larger than
(1+v)*(1-rho). Thus qcorr<rstar/(1-rho).
At k=k0 the part of cB before a*rshift equals u*(1-bc)>=0;
it strictly increases with k. Hence cB>0. Since k>k0, c1>0.
Equation (11) gives c20>beta*u/2>0. Finally
rstar<k*u*mu*z=k*c03old and rshift<=rstar, proving c03>0.
The definition of qcorr gives c04>=0, and c14,c23>0.

Set

    alpha=(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)/(1+Hbar), Y=X-alpha*E,
    sigma=k*mu*u^2-(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)^2/(1+Hbar)>0.

The positivity of sigma is exactly qcorr<qmax. Thus (10) is

    eps=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)*||Y||_M^2+the nonnegative costs in (10).  (12)

In particular every full original certificate obeys D<=kR. The old
cap theta<=2*beta*z/(a*u) is unnecessary once (7) is retained. On
the old strictly capped branch its root kstar is strictly larger
than this k, so an additional algebraic strip kR<D<=kstar*R is
excluded. This comparison is only with that relaxation, NOT with the
complete older scalar/triangle/curvature conjunction.

## 4. The actual quadratic column and joint first-row budget

Define

    pquad=(1,-a,ab,-abc,abc*(v-1))^T,
    Q=1-C^2*a^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2,
    delta=u^2-2, W0=1+bc*(v-1).

Tp=e and Le=0. Telescoping h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2 gives

    ||pquad||_M^2=Q>=0,
    2<E,pquad>_M=u*(m-delta)
             +a^2*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40).    (13)

For the row formula, let O0=sum_(j>0)Lambda0j and
I0=Lambda20+Lambda30+Lambda40. Then m=1-a^2-aO0 and node0 flow
gives Lambda10=O0+2u-I0. With Te0=u e-a e0 and

 pquad^T L e0=uO0+2au-a*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40),

which gives (13). Both incoming weights 1-bc and W0 are nonnegative,
and 1-bc<=W0, including v<1.

By (12), eps>=sigma*m+c20*Lambda20+cB*B0. Define

    xi_cap=min(c20/(a^2*beta), cB/(a^2*W0)),

omitting the second term if W0=0. For every real xi with
xi<=xi_cap and xi<sigma/u,

    eps>=xi*u*delta-xi^2*Q/(sigma-xi*u).                         (14)

Subtract xi*u*delta using (13). All remaining multiplier coefficients
are nonnegative: for xi>=0 this is the definition of xi_cap and the
order of the incoming weights; for xi<0 the coefficients increase.
The remaining Gram expression after adding xi^2Q/(sigma-xi*u) is

    ||sqrt(sigma-xi*u)*E+xi*pquad/sqrt(sigma-xi*u)||_M^2>=0.

Thus this is the same ORIGINAL matrix and column, not independent
energy selections. Let Qplus=Q+u^2*delta. Sending xi to -infinity
shows Qplus>=0, and

    Qplus=a^2*(A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2).

That prerequisite is the old scalar-return condition and is not
counted as an independent improvement.

For completeness, when Q,Qplus>0 the free maximizing xi is
xi_free=(sigma/u)*(1-sqrt(Q/Qplus)). If xi_free<=xi_cap, (14)

    Bcal=(sigma/u^2)*(sqrt(Qplus)-sqrt(Q))^2.

Otherwise its supremum is

    Bcal=xi_cap*u*delta-xi_cap^2*Q/(sigma-xi_cap*u).

The latter case automatically has xi_cap<sigma/u. For Q>0,Qplus=0,
the supremum is sigma*Q/u^2. For Q=0,Qplus>=0 it is
u*delta*min(xi_cap,sigma/u), and it is zero when Q=delta=0.
These statements follow on putting y=sigma-xi*u>0: the objective is

 sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2-(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The earlier first-row budget is also retained, on its stated domain

    eta=b/(1+w+v), nu=(1+eta)*(1-a*eta)/a,

 Erow=nu*(m+a*(Lambda20+B0))+(1+eta)^2*M11

Here is a direct derivation. For orthonormal physical vectors U,V set
gfirst=-eta*U+sqrt(nu)*V and use saturated values on

 Xphys=(U+u*gfirst,U,-b*U,-(1+v)*eta*U,-eta*U),
 Gphys=(gfirst,U,-eta*U,-eta*U,-eta*U).

The nonzero residuals are Q20=Q30=Q40=-a*nu,

 min((c20+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*beta),
                         (cB+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*W0)).              (16)

 u*delta<=Krow*Erow/nu+2*sqrt(Q*Erow/nu).

 u^2*(Erow-nu*delta^2/u^2)

## 5. A further matched full-column inequality near equality

In this section v>0 and all constants are the ones already defined.
Let

    dphys=a*b*c*v=(1+v)*z,
    nbar=s*(2C-(C+1)*v)/v>=0,
    rcoef=ell*mu^2+mu*hcoef^2>0,
    Lnorm=sqrt((u-a*alpha)^2/sigma+a^2/(1+Hbar)),
    Lterm=sqrt((alpha-beta)^2/sigma+1/(1+Hbar)),
    Kterm=(dphys/x)*Lterm*sqrt(nbar), Jfee=a/(2*x),
    Pcost=max(ell*mu*Hpre/cB,ell*mu*beta/c1,c03old/c03,1/k),
    Gcost=max(mu*Lnorm^2,Pcost).

All denominators are strictly positive. If nbar<0, the original
terminal budget (9) already excludes the word; it is never square-rooted.

Every full original array satisfies the following explicit scalar test.
Write y=sqrt(eps), which requires eps>=0, and set

 tau_max(y)=(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y
       +sqrt((sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)^2+4*jcoef*(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)))
                                                            /(2*jcoef),
 Psi(y)=rcoef*tau_max(y)^2
            +2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*tau_max(y)*y+Gcost*y^2.

Then

                              R<=Psi(sqrt(eps)).                 (17)

Here is the full derivation retaining the actual quadratic column.
The vector identity, checked in all five coordinates, is

    pquad=uE-aX-jcoef*B+dphys*e4+ab*e.

The original terminal rows give

    2<E,e4>_M=a*Lambda40-Lambda04,
    2<J,e4>_M=2<E,e4>_M+beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14.

Since X=Y+alpha E, they imply

 x<B,e4>_M=(alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M
                              -beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/2.

Taking the inner product of pquad with B therefore gives

 <B,pquad>_M=(u-a*alpha)<E,B>_M-a<Y,B>_M-jcoef*Tcut
       +(dphys/x)*((alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M)
       -dphys*beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/(2*x).       (18)

Let eps_G=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)||Y||_M^2 and let eps_C be the cost sum
in (12). Thus eps=eps_G+eps_C with both nonnegative. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz gives

 ||(u-a*alpha)E-aY||_M<=Lnorm*sqrt(eps_G),
 ||(alpha-beta)E+Y||_M<=Lterm*sqrt(eps_G).

Also ||e4||_M^2<=nbar by (9), and
c14=beta*dphys/a. Drop the negative Lambda40,Lambda41 terms in
(18), use Lambda14<=eps_C/c14, and use
<B,pquad>_M>=-sqrt(Tcut*Q). The result is

 jcoef*Tcut<=sqrt(Tcut*Q)
        +(Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut)+Kterm)*sqrt(eps_G)+Jfee*eps_C.          (19)

For the other direction (4) and Avec=(u-a*alpha)E-aY+hcoef*B give

 R<=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps_G)
                                    +mu*Lnorm^2*eps_G+Pcost*eps_C
  <=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps)+Gcost*eps.           (20)

The cost bound follows by comparing each cost in (4) to the cost of
the SAME multiplier in (12); their maximum ratio is precisely Pcost.
Thus costs and energies have not been chosen from different arrays.
Replacing eps_G,eps_C separately by eps in (19) gives, for
tcut=sqrt(Tcut)>=0,

 jcoef*tcut^2-(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)*tcut-(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)<=0.

Its nonnegative root is tau_max(y). The right side of (20) increases
with tcut>=0, which proves (17).

This supplies a quantified positive-gap exclusion test. Psi is
continuous and strictly increasing on [0,infinity), tends to infinity,
and

    Psi(0)=rcoef*Q/jcoef^2.

Consequently, if R>rcoef*Q/jcoef^2, there is a unique y0>0 with
Psi(y0)=R, and every full array must have

                           eps>=y0^2>0.                         (21)

Strict increase follows from the explicit nondecreasing positive
coefficients in tau_max and Gcost>0. This is an algebraic definition
and proof; no numerical root finding is used. In particular Q=0,R>0
forces a positive eps, even when delta=0 and the first-row bound
(14) alone is zero. This prices a further original cross column.
No uniform lower bound as v,ell,R,Q or other factors vanish is claimed.

## 6. COMPLETE original-array matching on the new equality locus

Assume eps=0 and R>0, still with a,b,c>0,bc<=1,0<v<2. Equation(12)
forces ME=MY=0, hence MX=0, and

    B0=B1=Lambda20=Lambda03=Lambda14=Lambda23=0.

Equation(6) now gives Lambda04=0, and (7) gives Lambda02=0.
The first moment in (3) forces Lambda01=2; node0 flow then gives
Lambda10=2A. Its diagonal is m=1-a^2-2a, so

                         a=sqrt(2)-1, a*A=1.                    (22)

Set

    Tstar=R/rcoef>0, r13=2*rho*Tstar, Bphys=Hpre+w, s=Bphys+v.

On this locus EVERY original multiplier is forced as follows:

    Lambda01=2, Lambda10=2A, Lambda13=r13,
    Lambda12=(2*A*Hpre-(beta+w)*r13)/beta,
    Lambda21=2*Hpre+Lambda12+r13,
    Lambda24=(2*w*N+beta*Lambda21)/(w+v),
    Lambda42=Lambda24/c,
    Lambda32=2*Bphys+r13+(c-1)*Lambda42,
    Lambda43=(2*s*C-(w+v)*Lambda42)/v,
    Lambda34=(1-c)*Lambda42+Lambda43-2*s,                         (23)

and the other TEN off-diagonal coefficients are zero:

    02,03,04,14,20,23,30,31,40,41.

Let

    nstar=Lambda42+Lambda43-s*(s+2),
    vcol=(0,-rho,rho-1,1,0)^T, dcol=(0,0,0,-1,1)^T.

For this array the ENTIRE original matrix is

                  M=Tstar*vcol*vcol^T+nstar*dcol*dcol^T.          (24)

Thus a word on eps=0,R>0 has a full original certificate if and
only if (22) holds and the explicit array (23) has

    Lambda12,Lambda32,Lambda34,Lambda43>=0, nstar>=0.              (25)

All other surviving signs then follow from their displayed formulas.
In particular Lambda21>0, Lambda24>0, Lambda42>0. This is an
actual all-twenty-entry matching, not a supplied covariance-fiber test.

Here is the proof of necessity and sufficiency of these formulas.
From E=0 and X=0 in the M seminorm, MJ=-rho*MB. Equations(4),(8)
give Tcut=Tstar. The original row <e1,B> gives Lambda13=r13.
Node1's moment and flow give respectively Lambda12 and Lambda21
in (23). Since M14=0 and MJ=-rho MB with rho>0, MB has fourth
component zero. Hence M24=0 too, because e2=e-J-B. The original
entry 2M24=c*Lambda42-Lambda24 gives their displayed relation.
Node2's moment and flow give Lambda24 and Lambda32. Node4's
moment and flow give Lambda43 and Lambda34. There is no free
covariance or multiplier left.

Conversely impose (22), eps=0,R>0 and define (23), allowing real
coefficients temporarily. The node0,1,2,4 flows and moments hold by
construction. For node3 the flow follows by summing the other flows.
Its moment can be checked explicitly: substituting (23) gives

 -w*Lambda32+v*Lambda34
   =-2*w*Bphys-w*r13-c*(w+v)*Lambda42+2*s*(C-v)
   =-2*(w+N)*Bphys+2*s*(C-v)=2*v*(1+Bphys),

where c(w+v)Lambda42=2*N*Bphys-w*r13 and
w+N=C-v=1+Bphys. Thus the full flow and Me=0 hold.

The original first row vanishes because aA=1; also M14=M24=0,
M13=-rho*Tstar. Direct substitution of Lambda12 gives

    M11=-D/beta^2+2*b*w*rho*Tstar/beta=rho^2*Tstar.

For the constant term in this identity use A^2=2A+1:
1-b^2+2A-2*A*b*Hpre/beta=-D/beta^2.
For the second equality use eps=0 and (8), which give
D=(2*b*w*x-x^2)*Tstar. The kernel then determines M12.
Finally (4), with all its costs zero and E row zero, determines
Tcut=Tstar: its positive Tcut coefficient is
ell*mu^2+a^2*b^2*mu^3, and (8) gives exactly that same coefficient
after subtracting the known J terms from R=rcoef*Tstar.
Me=0 now fixes every remaining entry except M44=nstar and proves
(24). The vectors vcol and dcol are independent, so full PSD is
equivalent to nstar>=0. This proves sufficiency as well as necessity.

The matched quadratic calibration has no extra freely selectable term:

    Q=jcoef^2*Tstar+dphys^2*nstar.                              (26)

Indeed pquad^T vcol=-jcoef and pquad^T dcol=dphys, by (8). Equation(13)
applies to the flow-correct array, so (24) proves (26). Consequently
nstar>=0 is equivalently Q>=jcoef^2*R/rcoef. At Q=0 this is
impossible when R>0; the WHOLE zero quadratic column is retained.

The main argument of this joint draft proves that this entire
matched equality locus is empty at C>=193/25.

## 7. Zero boundaries and the unresolved complete comparison

At v=0 with ell>0, z=theta=qcorr=0, k=k0=kold=b^2/ell. Identity
(10) still holds and its Gram has sigma>0, but some displayed costs
vanish. Strict-cost conclusions, Pcost, jcoef divisions, (17)--(26),
and the positive-gap equality classification above are NOT used there.
One retains the undivided identities (1)--(7),(10),(13),(15).

At ell=0 in this domain one necessarily has v=0,bc=1. Then pquad=Avec,
R=mu*Q, and the old undivided gap is b*beta*Q. No division by ell,
v,jcoef,c1,c03 or c23 is made on this boundary. No formal gradient
is deleted at v=0. At R=0 or Q=0, use the undivided norm identities;
zero M-energy always kills its WHOLE original column.

evidence:
# C99: dense anchors still need strong long-step projections

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED DRAFT. This is actual runtime round 1
of the allocation launched under master guidance `4226374d0649bf55`.
Completed baseline 29, completed ceiling 31, attempted ceiling 32 with
one historical interruption. No computation or formal verification is
authorized. Every new mathematical assertion below is an author proof,
not a fact. The original arbitrary-word exact-profile Goal remains OPEN;
its normalization W=2R is unchanged.

The mathematical inputs are accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` (necessity of
the original directed interpolation rows), `b98bb807d514e80d` (the
original benchmark and same-word scalar lower bounds), and
`1fca3e5dd555cb4a` (the same-word ray lower bound contains those scalar
lower bounds). Accepted `dfde2fa326c908bf` and `e9a55f57461f253c` are
used only for the explicitly scoped comparisons in Section5. C98/`55b569ca6c4c97a5` is context only. No assertion from
that unverified draft is a premise here.

## 1. The whole class, including dense initial anchors

Let F be any everywhere finite convex differentiable function on a
finite-dimensional Euclidean space, with 1-Lipschitz gradient and a
nonempty set of minimizers. Fix an integer n>=1 and a supplied word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)),
all h_i>1, and one actual trajectory of this SAME function,

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i,   g_i=grad F(X_i),
    f_i=F(X_i)-min F,      q_i=||g_i||^2,
    R_init=dist(X_0,argmin F)>0,   V=2f_n/R_init^2.

The terminal g_n is the actual gradient, though it is not queried by
the algorithm. It has no prescribed dependence on the queried gradients.
If any g_i=0 for i<n, every later iterate stays at a minimizer and V=0.
In the nonzero case define, for all actual transitions 0<=i<n,

    dstep_i=h_i-1,
    t_proj_i=-<g_i,g_(i+1)>/q_i,
    Jval_i=f_i+q_i/2,       kval_i=Jval_i/q_i.

Assume ONLY the following value condition at the short queried steps:

    Jval_i <= h_i q_i       whenever 1<h_i<2.        (A)

There is no support or value-ratio restriction at steps h_i>=2. The
initial point may have arbitrarily many nonzero coordinates, of arbitrary
signs and magnitudes. Gradient directions need not have a Markov law.
Dimensions, affine value reserves, optimum-row slacks, long-step support
ratios, and all terminal data are otherwise unrestricted.

The class is a class of ACTUAL legal functions. All remote directed rows
hold, not merely local rows. The proof below uses necessary local rows
to upper-bound this whole class; it never asserts that these local rows
are sufficient for interpolation.

For comparison with the assigned Markov/support-ratio interface, choose
any included minimizer as the origin and put

    eta_i=<X_i,g_i>/q_i,
    delta_i=f_i-q_i/2,
    z_i=<X_i,g_i>-f_i-q_i/2.

The two optimum rows in accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` give

    delta_i>=0, z_i>=0,
    Jval_i=q_i+delta_i=eta_i q_i-z_i,
    kval_i=1+delta_i/q_i=eta_i-z_i/q_i >=1.          (1)

Thus the old support range 1<=eta_i<h_i implies (A). The new class uses weaker conditions: at short steps it requires only
delta_i<=(h_i-1)q_i, and at long steps it requires neither condition.
Condition (A) is intrinsic to the actual values and gradients; it does
not depend on which minimizer is named as the origin.
Affine reserve delta_i and optimum slack z_i remain distinct throughout.

Define the nonnegative actual long-step projection budget

    E_proj=sum_(i:h_i>=2) log(max{1,t_proj_i}).       (2)

This formula is defined even when t_proj_i is zero or negative. It is
not a count of anchor coefficients and is not a Euclidean radius.

Main conclusion on the ORIGINAL H_m, defined in Section 5:

    V <= ((a_m+2)/(a_m+1)) beta_m^n c_m^(-m)
                                      exp(E_proj). (3)

In particular the ENTIRE stated class with t_proj_i<=1 at every long
step has vanishing original-B payoff and is exponentially weaker than
the accepted scalar witness on the SAME word. This conclusion includes
fully dense, arbitrarily chosen Markov anchors. No sparsity or lower
bound on their nonzero coefficients is imposed.

## 2. The exact local inequality and its two regimes

Accepted `1252b8823bb5a290` supplies the original residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.

Substitute the actual GD step into the REVERSE adjacent row:

    Q_(i+1,i)
       =Jval_(i+1)-Jval_i+[1-dstep_i t_proj_i]q_i.

Consequently, without discarding a slack or replacing a value,

    Jval_(i+1)<=Jval_i+[dstep_i t_proj_i-1]q_i.          (4)

For a zero terminal gradient Jval_n=0, so the same inequality applies.
Adding both adjacent rows instead gives cocoercivity on the actual step,

    ||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2
        <=h_i<g_i-g_(i+1),g_i>.

After division by q_i this is

    q_(i+1)/q_i <= dstep_i+(dstep_i-1)t_proj_i.

Cauchy--Schwarz also gives t_proj_i^2<=q_(i+1)/q_i. Hence

    (t_proj_i+1)(t_proj_i-dstep_i)<=0,
    -1<=t_proj_i<=dstep_i.                              (5)

No sign of the adjacent correlation was assumed in (5).

SHORT STEP. Suppose 0<dstep_i<1 and (A) holds. By (5),
dstep_i t_proj_i-1<=dstep_i^2-1<0. Also q_i>=Jval_i/(1+dstep_i).
Using the negative coefficient in the correct direction in (4) gives

    Jval_(i+1)
       <=Jval_i+(dstep_i^2-1)q_i
       <=[1+(dstep_i^2-1)/(1+dstep_i)]Jval_i
       =dstep_i Jval_i.                                (6)

LONG STEP. Suppose dstep_i>=1. The lower optimum row gives q_i<=Jval_i.
If dstep_i t_proj_i-1>=0, equation (4) yields
Jval_(i+1)<=dstep_i t_proj_i Jval_i. If that coefficient is negative,
(4) gives Jval_(i+1)<=Jval_i. In either case

    Jval_(i+1)<=dstep_i max{1,t_proj_i} Jval_i.           (7)

This argument imposes no upper bound on kval_i or eta_i at a long step.
At h_i=2, (5) forces t_proj_i<=1, and (7) is valid with factor1.

Multiplying (6)--(7) proves, with D_word=product_(i<n)dstep_i,

    Jval_n<=Jval_0 D_word exp(E_proj).               (8)

The same product through index n-2 bounds Jval_(n-1). Every factor is
positive. If the actual terminal objective is zero the desired bounds
are automatic, without taking a logarithm of zero.

## 3. The true initial distance and the unrestricted terminal

For EVERY minimizer X_star, 1-smoothness from its zero gradient gives

    f_0<=||X_0-X_star||^2/2,
    q_0<=||X_0-X_star||^2.

For the first inequality, integrate
<grad F(X_star+s(X_0-X_star)),X_0-X_star> from s=0 to1
and use the Lipschitz bound s||X_0-X_star||^2. The second is directly
gradient Lipschitzness. Add half the second inequality to the first
and take the infimum over ALL minimizers:

    Jval_0<=R_init^2.                               (9)

Thus no chosen minimizer is presumed to be closest, and no part of a
dense initial anchor is omitted from the normalization. From (8)--(9),
one immediate general bound is V<=2D_word exp(E_proj).

There is a sharper final-step bound when h_(n-1)=1+a_tail with 0<a_tail<1 and
(A) holds there. Integrating the Lipschitz gradient on that actual step
gives the descent inequality

    f_n<=f_(n-1)-h_(n-1)(2-h_(n-1))q_(n-1)/2
       =Jval_(n-1)-(1-a_tail^2/2)q_(n-1).

Since q_(n-1)>=Jval_(n-1)/(1+a_tail),

    f_n<=[a_tail(a_tail+2)/(2(a_tail+1))]Jval_(n-1).              (10)

There is no terminal support, angle, Markov or value prescription in
(10). Multiply the preceding factors (6)--(7), omit only the last
offset a_tail, and use (9). This proves the general final-short-step form

    V<=C_tail(a_tail) D_word exp(E_proj),
    C_tail(a_tail)=(a_tail+2)/(a_tail+1)<2.                         (11)

For general smoothness L>0, apply the result to F=f/L and the normalized
gradients grad f/L. The actual steps are h_i/L and V is exactly
2(f(X_n)-f_star)/(L dist(X_0,argmin f)^2), as required by W=2R.

## 4. The full Markov anchor price, retained rather than substituted

This section explains explicitly how the obstruction includes the
assigned dense-anchor models. It is NOT proposed as a new sufficient
construction or a free Gram optimization.

Suppose the nonzero QUERIED gradient directions u_i=g_i/A_i,
A_i=sqrt(q_i), 0<=i<n, satisfy the product law

    <u_i,u_j>=product_(k=i)^(j-1)rho_k, i<j,
    -1<=rho_k<=1.                                  (12)

For |rho_i|<1, the canonical innovation is

    e_(i+1)=(u_(i+1)-rho_i u_i)/sqrt(1-rho_i^2).

Expanding its inner products using (12) shows it has norm1 and is
orthogonal to u_0,...,u_i. It is therefore also orthogonal to all earlier
canonical innovations. Put e_0=u_0. Conversely the literal recursion

    u_0=e_0,
    u_(i+1)=rho_i u_i+sqrt(1-rho_i^2)e_(i+1)         (13)

realizes (12) in real coordinates. Degenerate rho_i=+/-1 means
u_(i+1)=rho_i u_i and contributes no canonical innovation.

The corresponding joint sign law is entirely specified by these same
rho_i: for s_sign_i in {-1,1},

    P_sign(s_sign_0,...,s_sign_(n-1))=2^(-n)
                    product_(i<n-1)(1+rho_i s_sign_i s_sign_(i+1)). (14)

It is nonnegative and normalized: summing the last sign gives a
factor2, successively. Equivalently take a fair initial sign and
independent bond signs of means rho_i; this proves (12) for their
moments. Strictly interior rho_i give full support. Neither positivity
of this law nor (13) is asserted to imply interpolation.

Let 0 be any included minimizer and w_(i+1)=<X_0,e_(i+1)>.
Earlier gradients are orthogonal to the innovation, so actual GD and
the definition eta_i=<X_i,g_i>/q_i imply

    eta_(i+1)A_(i+1)
       =rho_i(eta_i-h_i)A_i+sqrt(1-rho_i^2)w_(i+1).

Orthogonal decomposition gives the COMPLETE norm identity

    ||X_0||^2=eta_0^2 q_0
       +sum_(i:|rho_i|<1)
          [eta_(i+1)A_(i+1)-rho_i(eta_i-h_i)A_i]^2
                                      /(1-rho_i^2)
       +||X_perp||^2,                              (15)

where X_perp is orthogonal to all queried gradients. At a degenerate
transition the numerator must be zero, and there is no summand. Formula
(15) accounts for every actual nonzero initial innovation, including
all of them in a dense rule. It is the norm about the included minimizer;
it equals R_init^2 only when that minimizer is closest. The obstruction
uses (9), which is valid for the true radius in ALL cases, instead of
silently identifying these quantities.

For queried transitions the actual projection coefficient is

    t_proj_i=-rho_i A_(i+1)/A_i.                    (16)

Consequently a bound on |rho_i| alone is not the projection cap.
Even an interior, bounded correlation can have t_proj_i>1 when the
next gradient amplitude grows. Conversely, any real rule of the form
g_(i+1)=-t_i g_i+v_i e_(i+1) has t_proj_i=t_i, regardless of its
initial-anchor coefficients. Thus EVERY dense modification of the
previous bounded-rule class retaining t_i<=1 at long steps and (A)
is excluded by (11), without prescribing its q_i, eta_i, z_i, w_i,
or its permitted remote rows. No tiny-coefficient support count is used.

The terminal is still free: the Markov assumptions in this section stop
at index n-1. For the original H_m its last physical step is short, so
the obstruction does not even impose a long-step projection condition
on the actual terminal gradient.

## 5. ORIGINAL enclosing-m words and exact benchmark comparison

For each integer m>=4 fix the SAME enclosing-m parameters in every
recursive child:

    N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2),
    beta_m=1-1/m, c_m=sigma(1+1/m), a_m=beta_m/c_m,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_m c_m^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

The supplied word is the actual H_m. Parameters are not reset when
passing to a child. Its smallest and last step is 1+a_m, with
0<a_m<1/2. There are N/2^(j+1) steps of level j, for 0<=j<m.

The product of all offsets is

    D_word=a_m^(N-1)c_m^(N-m-1)=beta_m^n c_m^(-m).  (17)

For completeness the exponents follow by induction: the offset
product for H_(j+1) is its H_j product squared, times a_m c_m^j.
Starting from1, its a_m exponent is 2^j-1 and its c_m exponent is

## 6. Quantitative escape requirements, not sufficient conditions

Suppose a family of actual instances satisfying (A) on these words has
liminf B_n V>0. Choose v_0>0 with B_n V>=v_0 eventually. Taking logarithms

    E_proj>=n log(1/beta_m)+m log c_m

    liminf m E_proj/n >=1.                         (22)

# Variable-first-step comparison of the original positive-remainder tests

of calibrated inequalities specified below. It is not another version of
the former Bescape formula, and it does not assert that the remaining
older necessary system has a survivor.

## 1. Domain and the complete comparison statement

Throughout this document let

    h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,v), a,b,c>0, bc<=1, sqrt(2)<=v<2,
    u=1+a, beta=1+b, w=1+c,
    A=2+a, N=3+a+b, C=1+sum h=4+a+b+c+v,
    t=c/(1+v), mu=1+t, gamma=w/mu,

    D=b^2*N^2-A^2,
    Q=1-C^2*a^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2,
    U=A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2, V=Q/a^2.

Here R is the older repaired third-cut energy, Q is the older actual
unit-quadratic energy, and U is the older scalar-return energy. Section2

They are only THREE members of the complete older necessary system.
None of its other tests is discarded in the comparisons below.

Let H be the positive root

 H=(2*b*w-beta
     +sqrt((beta-2*b*w)^2+4*b*w^2*(1-b*t)/mu))/(2*(1-b*t)),
 k=H/(a^2*mu), k0=b^2*w/(ell*mu), eps=k*R-D.

   Thus these two new tests exclude no survivor of the COMPLETE older

2. On this domain with EITHER a>=sqrt(2)-1 OR D>=0, the same three

3. On the concrete subdomain

     sqrt(2)-1<=a<1, ab<=1, c*(v-1)<=1,

Intersecting any of these domains with every other retained cut,
clipping, adjacent/lifted triangle, C82/C84, C83/C86, endpoint or2948
condition preserves the implication. The proof does not use, or claim,

survivor on the relevant domain can witness independence of the stated

## 2. The older inputs, with actual all-pair witnesses

    V_h=||x0||^2-||x4+s*g4||^2, s=C-1.                 (1)

## 3. A positive decomposition in the older energies

Introduce new local comparison scalars

    zeta=b*mu/beta, kappa=zeta/H,

 kappa*eps=theta0*D+(1-zeta)*A^2+zeta/a^2-Y,

## 4. The whole first-row calibration is dominated

row correction in Appendix A.3. There

## 3. The unrestricted root and the new full-row remainder

where gamma=w/mu>1. At kold it is negative, since F(kold,0)=0 and

    Hbar=(2*b*w-beta

The inequalities use mu<w and bw<=beta, with strictness supplied

    v*n<=s*(2C-(C+1)*v), so v<=2C/(C+1)<2.                       (9)

Define the nonnegative correction

where

    rcoef=ell*mu^2+mu*hcoef^2>0,
    Lnorm=sqrt((u-a*alpha)^2/sigma+a^2/(1+Hbar)),
    Lterm=sqrt((alpha-beta)^2/sigma+1/(1+Hbar)),
    Kterm=(dphys/x)*Lterm*sqrt(nbar), Jfee=a/(2*x),
    Pcost=max(ell*mu*Hpre/cB,ell*mu*beta/c1,c03old/c03,1/k),
    Gcost=max(mu*Lnorm^2,Pcost).

All denominators are strictly positive. If nbar<0, the original
terminal budget (9) already excludes the word; it is never square-rooted.

Every full original array satisfies the following explicit scalar test.
Write y=sqrt(eps), which requires eps>=0, and set

 tau_max(y)=(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y
       +sqrt((sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)^2+4*jcoef*(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)))
                                                            /(2*jcoef),
 Psi(y)=rcoef*tau_max(y)^2
            +2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*tau_max(y)*y+Gcost*y^2.

Then

                              R<=Psi(sqrt(eps)).                 (17)

Here is the full derivation retaining the actual quadratic column.
The vector identity, checked in all five coordinates, is

    pquad=uE-aX-jcoef*B+dphys*e4+ab*e.

The original terminal rows give

    2<E,e4>_M=a*Lambda40-Lambda04,
    2<J,e4>_M=2<E,e4>_M+beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14.

Since X=Y+alpha E, they imply

 x<B,e4>_M=(alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M
                              -beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/2.

Taking the inner product of pquad with B therefore gives

 <B,pquad>_M=(u-a*alpha)<E,B>_M-a<Y,B>_M-jcoef*Tcut
       +(dphys/x)*((alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M)
       -dphys*beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/(2*x).       (18)

Let eps_G=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)||Y||_M^2 and let eps_C be the cost sum
in (12). Thus eps=eps_G+eps_C with both nonnegative. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz gives

 ||(u-a*alpha)E-aY||_M<=Lnorm*sqrt(eps_G),
 ||(alpha-beta)E+Y||_M<=Lterm*sqrt(eps_G).

Also ||e4||_M^2<=nbar by (9), and
c14=beta*dphys/a. Drop the negative Lambda40,Lambda41 terms in
(18), use Lambda14<=eps_C/c14, and use
<B,pquad>_M>=-sqrt(Tcut*Q). The result is

 jcoef*Tcut<=sqrt(Tcut*Q)
        +(Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut)+Kterm)*sqrt(eps_G)+Jfee*eps_C.          (19)

For the other direction (4) and Avec=(u-a*alpha)E-aY+hcoef*B give

 R<=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps_G)
                                    +mu*Lnorm^2*eps_G+Pcost*eps_C
  <=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps)+Gcost*eps.           (20)

The cost bound follows by comparing each cost in (4) to the cost of
the SAME multiplier in (12); their maximum ratio is precisely Pcost.
Thus costs and energies have not been chosen from different arrays.
Replacing eps_G,eps_C separately by eps in (19) gives, for
tcut=sqrt(Tcut)>=0,

 jcoef*tcut^2-(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)*tcut-(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)<=0.

Its nonnegative root is tau_max(y). The right side of (20) increases
with tcut>=0, which proves (17).

This supplies a quantified positive-gap exclusion test. Psi is
continuous and strictly increasing on [0,infinity), tends to infinity,
and

    Psi(0)=rcoef*Q/jcoef^2.

Consequently, if R>rcoef*Q/jcoef^2, there is a unique y0>0 with
Psi(y0)=R, and every full array must have

                           eps>=y0^2>0.                         (21)

Strict increase follows from the explicit nondecreasing positive
coefficients in tau_max and Gcost>0. This is an algebraic definition
and proof; no numerical root finding is used. In particular Q=0,R>0
forces a positive eps, even when delta=0 and the first-row bound
(14) alone is zero. This prices a further original cross column.
No uniform lower bound as v,ell,R,Q or other factors vanish is claimed.
