# max36: actual suffix-first inversion of a fixed capped quadratic

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. No fact is asserted.
Project: gd-exact-profile-20260926. Worker: max.
Steering: TASK.md and master_guidance 4226374d0649bf55.
This is the first analytical round of the newly authorized two-round wave:
completed baseline35, proposed completion36, completed ceiling37, attempted
ceiling38 including the historical interruption. No numerical, solver,
machine-algebra, replay, formal-verifier, installation, consult, or subagent
call is used. Operational file and publication checks are separate.

## 1. Scope and accepted interfaces

The original target remains the uniform assertion

    for every epsilon>0, for every sufficiently large n, for EVERY h>=0,
    W_n(h) >= (1-epsilon)/B_n,
    B_n=1+2 S_bullet(n),

or a genuine asymptotic counterexample with a full all-function upper
certificate. Throughout W is 2(f(x_n)-f_star)/(L|x_0-x_star|^2).

This draft does not establish either resolution. It solves one explicit
suffix-first extension problem, gives its paid arbitrary-depth continuation
rule, and proves a COMPLETE two-preceding-step comparison for that family.
The family is a scaled, translated symmetric capped quadratic. The comparison
is uniform in both preceding steps, the whole nonnegative suffix, every scale,
every preserved suffix location/value, every allowed minimum, and EVERY inverse
branch. It is not a theorem about all functions that interpolate these suffix
jets. In particular a nonsymmetric or multidimensional extension is outside the
comparison.

Accepted facts used as external interfaces, rather than unverified findings:

* 1252b8823bb5a290: full ordered smooth-convex interpolation, its actual static
  interpolant, and the exact unqueried-terminal reduction. Here the terminal
  jet is also actual; no incoming terminal inequality is omitted.
* b98bb807d514e80d: the legal scalar lower-bound functional

      K_n(h)=max{1/(1+2 sum h),
                  max_j (h_j-1)_+^2/[(1+sum_{i<j}h_i)^2
                                           (1+2sum_{i>j}h_i)]}.

* 1fca3e5dd555cb4a: the legal alternating-ray functional F_ray_n(h), with
  retained offsets, retained value areas, and K_n(h)<=F_ray_n(h)<=W_n(h).
  The exact two-cut specialization needed below is stated and checked in
  Section9 before it is applied.
* 0be8b54e0a33381c: finite terminal-block improvements wash out for its specified
  ConPD schedule construction and primitive sum caps. This is a separate,
  restricted schedule theorem. It is not a converse for our adversaries and
  does not furnish a comparison for the inverse maps below.

No other mathematical result is imported. The literature check read the
definition/conjugacy discussion, Theorem4 proof and Corollary1 in the already
downloaded Taylor--Hendrickx--Glineur paper arXiv:1502.05666. Matlas also returned
the equivalent interpolation statement as Theorem5 of arXiv:1910.01845. Those
references are background only; the new construction and its full row check
are proved directly below, and accepted1252b8823bb5a290 already supplies the
general interpolation interface.

The old fixed-prefix obstruction48bf4f8bbf4e2b1d, and the failed backward
blending records695cc7b3cda3b59e/9949b0d613e96cde/1350be2cea28858c, informed
the choice of lane but are not proof premises.

A later, more specific recall found e6841b2627f03bfd and53024613ee396747:
an earlier UNVERIFIED binary-word calculation already excluded the whole
full-curvature symmetric-Huber family at the original target scale. That
qualitative obstruction is NOT claimed as new progress here. Section11
reproves a broader soft-threshold composition criterion inside this joint
draft, including the binary specialization and a different descending-linear
word. The new local interface is the exact suffix-preserving two-step domain,
paid inverse rule, full same-word ray comparison, and its anchor jump. The
family must not be reopened as a plausible universal lower-bound route.

## 2. Symbols and the fixed function

Define the dimensionless profile Hcap and its derivative ccap by

    Hcap(z)=z^2/2                       if |z|<=1,
             |z|-1/2                   if |z|>=1,
    ccap(z)=max(-1,min(1,z)).

The two formulas agree with their first derivatives at +/-1. The function
ccap is continuous and nondecreasing, and for u<=v it satisfies

    0 <= ccap(v)-ccap(u) <= v-u.

This follows directly by dividing [u,v] at -1 and1: the slope is either0
or1 on each resulting interval, and the increments add. Hence Hcap is convex,
differentiable, and1-smooth. It is nonnegative and vanishes only at0.

Let L>0 be the prescribed smoothness. Let eta>0 be a spatial scale, xi a
minimizer anchor, and mu a minimum value. Our ONE STATIC function is

    f(x)=mu+L eta^2 Hcap((x-xi)/eta),                 (2.1)
    f'(x)=L eta ccap((x-xi)/eta).

Its gradient is L-Lipschitz by the displayed clipping inequality. Its unique
minimizer is xi and its minimum is mu. For x=xi+eta z, one GD step of size h/L
is exactly

    z -> Tcap_h(z):=z-h ccap(z).                    (2.2)

Thus the construction follows the ORIGINAL supplied word forward. A backward
calculation merely selects its starting point; it does not reverse or replace
the supplied step order.

## 3. Preserved suffix family and its free value/anchor parameters

Fix any finite nonnegative suffix word

    k=(k_0,...,k_(m-1)),  m>=0,
    S=sum_j k_j,
    s_j=sum_{l<j} k_l,  0<=j<=m.

The empty suffix is allowed: m=0, S=s_0=0. No upper bound or positivity
assumption on any k_j is imposed.

Choose arbitrary real X,V and eta>0. These specify ALL the old suffix jets:

    x_(2+j)=X-eta s_j,
    g_(2+j)=L eta,
    f_(2+j)=V-L eta^2 s_j,           0<=j<=m.       (3.1)

The location X and the absolute value V are free, independent parameters.
They are not silently reset when earlier queries are added.

There is also a free relative anchor parameter r satisfying the exact domain

    r>=C:=1+S.                                      (3.2)

Set

    xi=X-eta r,
    mu=V-L eta^2(r-1/2).                            (3.3)

Then the function(2.1) realizes every jet(3.1). Indeed their dimensionless
coordinates are r-s_j>=r-S>=1, where Hcap=r-s_j-1/2 and ccap=1. This also
verifies every original suffix GD update. The terminal gap is positive:

    f_(2+m)-mu=L eta^2(r-S-1/2)>=L eta^2/2.          (3.4)

Changing r while holding X,V,eta fixed changes BOTH the actual minimum value
mu and its actual position xi, but leaves every old suffix jet unchanged.
Both changes will be paid in(6.3). Thus the free suffix value is not mistaken
for a free objective gap.

Within the stipulated positive-affine-suffix family, domain(3.2) is exact:
the final coordinate r-S must be at least1 to have derivative L eta for the
profile(2.1). Equality is legal. If a strictly positive affine reserve beyond
the junction is desired, replace(3.2) by r>C; the boundary statements below
then describe limits where applicable, not an attained strict-reserve optimum.
The task does not require that additional strict inequality.

## 4. Complete one-step predecessor sets, including zero and unit steps

For any h>=0 and target y, all real solutions of Tcap_h(z)=y are exactly
the union of the following sets; coincident boundary entries are counted once:

    {y+h}             if y+h>=1;                    (4.1+)
    {y-h}             if y-h<=-1;                   (4.1-)
    {y/(1-h)}         if h!=1 and |y|<=|1-h|;        (4.1c)
    [-1,1]            if h=1 and y=0.               (4.1u)

Every unlisted branch is absent. In particular(4.1c) is never used at h=1.
Proof: on z>=1 the map is z-h, on z<=-1 it is z+h, and on [-1,1]
it is(1-h)z. Solving these three affine equations WITH their interval
conditions proves necessity and sufficiency of the list. At h=1 the middle
equation is0=y and gives precisely(4.1u). No generic inverse notation hides
the exceptional branch.

For y>0 the same-sign positive branch always exists whenever y+h>=1. If that
inequality fails then h<1 and y<1-h, so the core branch exists. For y<0 use
oddness. For y=0, z=0 is always a preimage. Consequently every real target
has a predecessor for every h>=0. This includes arbitrarily large h.

Define mcap_h(t), for t>=0, as the smallest absolute value of a predecessor
of a target of absolute value t. Oddness makes this independent of its sign.
The exact closed formula is

    mcap_h(0)=0,
    mcap_0(t)=t,
    mcap_1(t)=t+1                           for t>0,

    mcap_h(t)=t/(1-h)                       if 0<h<1, 0<t<=1-h,
                t+h                        if 0<h<1, t>1-h,

    mcap_h(t)=t/(h-1)                       if h>1, 0<t<=h-1,
                t+h                        if h>1, t>h-1.            (4.2)

To check minimality when h>1 and 0<t<=h-1, the core predecessor has modulus
t/(h-1)<=1. The opposite outer predecessor, when distinct, has modulus
h-t>=1, and the same-sign outer predecessor has modulus h+t>1. Thus the
core is minimal, including equality. For t>h-1 only the same-sign outer
predecessor remains. For 0<h<1 there is only the core for t<1-h, only the
same-sign outer predecessor for t>1-h, and they coincide at the boundary.
At h=1,t>0 there is only the same-sign outer predecessor. This proves(4.2)
from the full list rather than deleting an inconvenient inverse branch.

For fixed h, mcap_h is strictly increasing on(0,infinity) and nondecreasing
on[0,infinity). In the small-step case the two formulas meet at value1.
In the large-step case the value at t=h-1 is1, whereas the right limit is
2h-1>1. Both pieces have positive slope, so this is an upward jump and
does not destroy monotonicity. The unit-step map has value0 at0 and right
limit1. The zero-step case is the identity.

A minimizing signed predecessor is explicit: use y/(1-h) on a legal core
branch of(4.2), use sign(y)(|y|+h) on an outer branch, and use0 for y=0.
At h=0 this is just y. Thus the formula chooses actual points, not merely
their possible lengths.

## 5. Solve the TWO preceding steps, without changing an old suffix jet

Let the full word be

    h=(a,b,k_0,...,k_(m-1)),     a,b>=0.             (5.1)

For any r in(3.2), first take a minimizing signed predecessor z_1 of r under
Tcap_b. Then take a minimizing signed predecessor z_0 of z_1 under Tcap_a.
Set z_(2+j)=r-s_j and define ALL new and old values and gradients by(2.1).
The two new queries are x_i=xi+eta z_i, i=0,1. They obey

    Tcap_a(z_0)=z_1,   Tcap_b(z_1)=r,               (5.2)

so they precede the unchanged suffix in its original chronology. Their
values are mu+L eta^2 Hcap(z_i); they are not chosen independently of the
gradient/geometry restrictions.

The exact smallest initial distance among ALL two-step predecessor branches
of this same function and this same suffix is

    Dcap_ab(r):=mcap_a(mcap_b(r)),
    dist(x_0,argmin f)=eta Dcap_ab(r).               (5.3)

Proof of the global, rather than just local, minimum: for any valid z_1 one
has |z_1|>=mcap_b(r). Every predecessor z_0 of that z_1 satisfies

    |z_0|>=mcap_a(|z_1|)>=mcap_a(mcap_b(r)),

where the second inequality uses the monotonicity proved in Section4.
The two displayed signed choices attain equality simultaneously. Since r>0,
both mcap values are positive, so the initial point is not the minimizer.

All parameter choices

    a,b>=0; arbitrary finite k_j>=0; eta>0; X,V real; r>=1+S             (5.4)

are feasible. This is an explicit nonempty domain, not an unsolved feasibility
condition. One can always choose the two same-sign outer predecessors
z_1=r+b,z_0=r+b+a; the minimizing rule may improve them. Both a=0 and b=0
are identity steps with identical repeated jets. The a=1 or b=1 branches
use t+1, never division by zero. Every large-step possibility in(4.1) is
retained in the minimum-radius proof.

## 6. Every ordered interpolation row and the true normalization

Here is a direct row proof for any two real points u,v, with no adjacency
assumption. Write c=ccap. If u>=v, put d=c(u)-c(v)>=0. Lipschitzness gives
d<=u-v and, on [v,u],

    c(t)-c(v) >= max{0,d-(u-t)}.

Integrating the right-hand side over its final interval of length d yields

    Hcap(u)-Hcap(v)-c(v)(u-v) >= d^2/2.             (6.1)

If u<=v, put d=c(v)-c(u)>=0. Then d<=v-u and on [u,v]

    c(v)-c(t) >= max{0,d-(t-u)}.

Integrating over the first interval of length d proves the same inequality
(6.1), now with d^2=(c(u)-c(v))^2. Thus for EVERY ordered pair u,v,

    Hcap(u)>=Hcap(v)+c(v)(u-v)+(c(u)-c(v))^2/2.

Scale by L eta^2 and translate to(2.1). For all sample indices i,j, including
the minimizer and every new/old/terminal index, this says

    f_i>=f_j+g_j(x_i-x_j)+(g_i-g_j)^2/(2L).         (6.2)

The proof holds for both orderings of EACH pair. It therefore covers new-old
rows in both directions, the two new queries against one another, every remote
suffix row, and both optimum rows. A zero step repeats a point and gives
equality. There is no omitted constraint or terminal height surrogate.

The actual minimum is mu and its unique location is xi. Combining(3.4) and
(5.3), the exact best normalized value for the fixed r in this function family
is

    Vcap_ab,k(r)=(2r-2S-1)/Dcap_ab(r)^2.             (6.3)

Every other two-step inverse branch has the same terminal gap and a greater
or equal true initial distance, so its normalized value is no larger.
Neither X nor V nor eta remains in(6.3): their cancellation follows from the
actual minimum and distance formulas, not from resetting the radius.

## 7. Full branch table and exact optimization of the remaining anchor

Put d=2S+1 and C=S+1. Call an inverse branch 'core' when the linear middle
piece of(4.2) is selected. Assign the identity h=0 to the outer label; its
formula t+h=t makes this a harmless unambiguous convention. The unit step
also has the outer label for positive targets.

At r>=C>=1, the step b has a core inverse precisely when b>1 and
r<=t:=b-1. Otherwise it has the outer inverse r+b. For the next inverse,
write u=mcap_b(r): step a is core precisely when

    a in (0,1) union (1,infinity), and u<=|a-1|.

The following four rows partition the entire domain (5.4). The first label
refers to a and the second to b; the backwards calculation still applies b
first and a second.

    labels    domain in addition to r>=C                    Dcap_ab(r)

    CC        b>1, r<=t; a!=0,1, r<=|a-1|t                 r/(|a-1|t)

    OC        b>1, r<=t; a=0 or a=1 or r>|a-1|t             r/t+a

    CO        [b<=1 or r>b-1]; a>1, r+b<=a-1               (r+b)/(a-1)

    OO        [b<=1 or r>b-1];
              [a<=1 or r+b>a-1]                            r+a+b.     (7.1)

In CC, the condition a!=0,1 is read together with a>=0, so a>0. In OC,
the last disjunct is only needed for a not equal to0 or1. Boundaries are
assigned to core except for the identity convention. A row may be empty;
their union is never empty. In particular the OO row contains all sufficiently
large r. At a=0,b=0,r=1, the identity endpoint is assigned to OO and has
value1. No formula that divides by a-1 is applied to that identity step.

The formulas display every division and its strictly positive denominator.
They also show that the only branch breakpoints on r>=C can be drawn from

    b-1, |a-1|(b-1), a-b-1.                         (7.2)

Not every listed number is an active breakpoint, which causes no problem.
On each nonempty interval of the partition, write Dcap_ab(r)=A r+B.
Here A>0 and B>=0. Direct differentiation, within that interval only, gives

    d/dr [(2r-d)/(A r+B)^2]
      =2[B+A(d-r)]/(A r+B)^3.                       (7.3)

Thus its sole possible stationary maximum is r=d+B/A. For the four rows
the possible stationary radii are respectively

    d,  d+a(b-1),  d+b,  d+a+b.                     (7.4)

Consequently an EXACT finite formula for the optimum over every allowed r is

    max_{r in Ecap_ab,S} (2r-d)/[mcap_a(mcap_b(r))]^2,               (7.5)

where Ecap_ab,S is the following explicit list after deleting entries less
than C and deleting repetitions:

    C, b-1, |a-1|(b-1), a-b-1,
    d, d+a(b-1), d+b, d+a+b.                         (7.6)

These are at most eight analytic candidate expressions; this draft does not
numerically enumerate or evaluate a parameter grid. Extra inactive candidates
are allowed because they are still legal radii in the original domain.

For completeness, an excluded right-hand interval endpoint cannot conceal a
larger supremum. On positive arguments mcap_h is left-continuous, with only
upward jumps to its right. Its composition has the same property: if an inner
map jumps across an outer breakpoint, the outer monotonicity preserves the
upward direction. Therefore Vcap has only downward jumps to its right. The
value at a breakpoint is at least the limiting value of any immediately
following interval. Formula(7.3) handles the interiors, C is included, and
Vcap(r) tends to0 at infinity since the final row is OO. Every possible
maximum is therefore attained at a listed breakpoint or stationary point.
The nonempty list contains C. This proves(7.5) even at every zero/unit-step
degeneracy.

## 8. The paid continuation invariant exists at arbitrary depth

For any finite nonnegative prefix word w=(w_0,...,w_(p-1)), define the explicit
map

    Mcap_w(t)=mcap_(w_0)(mcap_(w_1)(...mcap_(w_(p-1))(t)...)),
    Mcap_empty(t)=t.                                 (8.1)

This is composition of the CLOSED formulas(4.2), not an unspecified feasible
set, optimization oracle, or Bellman lemma. It is the exact smallest modulus
of an initial point whose GD run on Hcap under the original w ends at a given
signed target of modulus t. Induction proves this: for the first step,
minimize over possible later starting moduli; monotonicity of mcap_(w_0)
shows that the smallest available later modulus is optimal, and the signed
choice in Section4 attains it. Equivalently one can induct by prepending a
step and apply the two inequalities in Section5.

For words u,v, where u followed by v denotes their original chronological
concatenation,

    Mcap_(u followed by v)=Mcap_u composed with Mcap_v.              (8.2)

All these maps are nondecreasing and strictly increasing for positive input.
Their exact state on(0,infinity) can be kept as at most p+1 intervals with
affine formulas A t+B, A>0,B>=0, and the values at their breakpoints. This
assertion is symbolic, not a computation: start with the single piece t.
Prepending one mcap_h leaves all existing breakpoints and introduces at most
one more, because a strictly increasing inner map can cross its sole positive
threshold |1-h| at most once. If the crossing occurs within an affine piece,
the new threshold is explicitly (|1-h|-B)/A. If a jump crosses it, it uses an
already existing breakpoint. h=0 adds nothing and h=1 is t+1 on positive
inputs, also adding nothing. The composition coefficients remain A>0,B>=0.

For the old suffix jets(3.1), a fixed r>=C, and any such prefix, the actual
function, minimum and suffix remain(2.1),(3.3). The true paid quantities are

    initial distance = eta Mcap_w(r),
    terminal gap = L eta^2(r-S-1/2),
    normalized payoff = (2r-2S-1)/Mcap_w(r)^2.         (8.3)

All gradients and values are actual samples of the SAME static function,
and Section6 still checks every remote row. This proves scalable feasibility
and exact normalization in this restricted family for arbitrary h, including

## 11. All-depth obstruction: exact soft-threshold schedules

This section strengthens the scope of the closure from two preceding steps
to the entire scalar family(2.1), with ANY terminal regime and any initial
point. The earlier unverified binary counterexample e6841b2627f03bfd prompted
a memory check; nothing from it is assumed as a fact. The full proof follows.

For A>=0 write

    Rsh_A(z)=sign(z) max(|z|-A,0),

with Rsh_A(0)=0. This notation is a soft-threshold map, not the project's
objective normalization R_n. If A>=1 and h>=0, then the exact identity

    Rsh_A composed with Tcap_h = Rsh_(A+h)           (11.1)

holds IF AND ONLY IF h<=A+1.

Proof of sufficiency: both sides are odd, so take z>=0. For 0<=z<=1,
Tcap_h(z)=(1-h)z has absolute value at most |1-h|<=A, since h<=A+1
and A>=1. The left side vanishes, as does the right side because A+h>=1.
For z>=1, Tcap_h(z)=z-h. If z-h<0, its negative modulus is h-z<=h-1<=A,
so the left side vanishes, again agreeing with the right side. If z-h>=0,
the left side is max(z-h-A,0), exactly the right side. This proves(11.1)
on every real z. For necessity, if h>A+1, take z=1. The left side equals
-(h-1-A)<0, whereas the right side is0. Thus the identity fails. The zero
step is included in the sufficient condition and gives the identity map.

Now let a nonempty original word w end with a physical unit step, and suppose
each preceding step satisfies the explicit tail-sum condition

    w_i <= 1+sum_{j>i} w_j.                         (11.2)

Let H=sum_i w_i. The last unit step equals Rsh_1. Applying(11.1) successively
backwards proves that the COMPLETE forward GD map under w is Rsh_H. Every
tail used in the induction has sum at least1, so every hypothesis of(11.1)
is met. Zero steps at any preceding positions are allowed. Trailing zero
steps may also be appended without changing the map. No order restriction
beyond(11.2) is needed for this claim.

We next optimize over the ENTIRE family(2.1), including all possible terminal
core points, while paying the true minimum and distance. By translation,
scaling and oddness, let the initial dimensionless radius be z>0. If z<=H,
the terminal point is the minimizer and the payoff is0. If z>H, write the
terminal radius as v=z-H>0. The normalized payoff is

    2 Hcap(v)/(H+v)^2.

For 0<v<=1 this equals v^2/(H+v)^2, an increasing function of v because
H>=1. Its maximum on that interval is1/(H+1)^2. For v>=1 it equals
(2v-1)/(H+v)^2. Differentiation gives

    2(H+1-v)/(H+v)^3,

so its maximum occurs at v=H+1 and equals1/(2H+1). The inequality
(H+1)^2>=2H+1 shows that the latter is the overall maximum. Therefore

    sup over ALL eta,xi,mu,x_0!=xi in family(2.1)
        2(f(x_n)-mu)/(L|x_0-xi|^2) = 1/(1+2H).     (11.3)

The value is attained at dimensionless initial radius2H+1, ending at H+1.
In particular changing the whole-word-dependent scale, moving the minimum,
or using a terminal core instead of the affine suffix cannot repair(11.3).

For a polynomial-size example choose the actual length-n word

    w_dec^(n)=(n,n-1,...,2,1), n>=1,
    H=n(n+1)/2.

A step j>=2 has tail sum j(j-1)/2, and

    j <= 1+j(j-1)/2

is equivalent to (j-1)(j-2)>=0. Thus(11.2) holds. Formula(11.3) gives the
EXACT entire-family value

    Vcap_dec(n)=1/[1+n(n+1)].                       (11.4)

Accepted b98bb807d514e80d supplies B_n<=1+4n^p, p=log_2(3)<2. Its
applicability is only the original benchmark recurrence and the present
length n; no schedule restriction is involved. Hence

    0 <= Vcap_dec(n)/U_n^ZJ
      = B_n/[1+n(n+1)]
      <= (1+4n^p)/[1+n(n+1)] -> 0.                 (11.5)

On EXACTLY the same word, the first-step scalar cut from the same accepted
fact gives, for n>=2,

    W_n(w_dec^(n)) >= K_n(w_dec^(n))
                   >= (n-1)^2/[1+n(n-1)] -> 1.      (11.6)

Therefore the exhibited small restricted-family value says nothing small
about the unrestricted W_n; indeed a previously accepted scalar witness is
already much stronger. Since F_ray>=K, the full accepted ray reference also
dominates this calibration. Equations(11.5)--(11.6) are a scoped obstruction
to the family, not a negative answer to the original minimax question.

For comparison with the RECALLED old finding, descending binary steps
(2^(n-1),2^(n-2),...,1) have H=2^n-1 and satisfy equality in(11.2) at every
preceding position. Formula(11.3), proved here independently, specializes
to1/(2^(n+1)-1), exactly the earlier recorded family obstruction. This is

## 12. What has and has not been closed

Closed in this UNVERIFIED joint draft:

1. A concrete positive-payoff suffix with independent old location/value,
   a free scale, and an explicit range of moving minimum anchors.
2. The ACTUAL two-preceding-step extension on the original word, including
   ALL inverse branches, joint earlier points/values, h=0,h=1 and arbitrarily
   large steps, the full nonempty domain, every ordered row, and true radius.
3. Exact optimization of its remaining relative anchor via at most eight
   analytic candidates, with jumps and boundary ownership accounted for.
4. An explicit paid continuation invariant for this SAME static-function
   family at arbitrary depth, without a hidden feasibility oracle.
5. A complete SAME-word domination theorem for its ENTIRE two-step extension
   family by accepted scalar/alternating-ray references, and a sharp finite
   example showing why comparison only to K is inadequate.
6. An exact all-depth soft-threshold composition criterion, with a complete
   whole-family payoff optimization. It re-establishes the already known
   scoped failure of full-curvature symmetric Hubers and gives a descending
   linear word whose restricted ratio to the ORIGINAL B profile tends to0.

Still OPEN:

* A useful original-B estimate for a genuinely larger continuation family.
  The maps(8.1) are exact feasibility/payoff invariants for their fixed family,
  but Section11 proves that they CANNOT satisfy the required all-word original-B
  lower estimate. That family-level question is closed, not merely unproved.
* Whether a richer suffix family, asymmetric clipping, additional affine
  offsets, or genuine transverse geometry can escape the two-step domination
  while retaining a paid all-row continuation rule. Merely allowing an interior
  terminal jet in the unchanged symmetric family does not escape Section11.
* The original arbitrary-h exact-profile minimax problem in PROBLEM.md.

One must not apply(9.3) repeatedly without a new proof. After a general earlier
inverse step the retained portion contains core and/or alternating gradients,
and is not the positive constant-gradient suffix assumed in Section3. Resetting
the clipping threshold or anchor to restore that assumption would in general
change old jets. Likewise the accepted ConPD washout theorem has schedule
hypotheses not furnished by(8.2); scalar map composition is not an all-function
certificate composition.

Suggested remaining analytical round: retain the paid minimum/jet bookkeeping
but select a genuinely larger concrete suffix family, such as asymmetric
clipping or a jointly constructed nonhomogeneous transverse support. Do not
retune the closed symmetric full-curvature family, its threshold law, or its
moving-minimum parametrization in hope of recovering the target. A lower core
curvature is outside this obstruction but needs a paid whole-word rule, not
a free parameter claim. Any new lemma must be reproved in a new joint draft
or separately accepted before it can be used as a fact.

For (5), start the scalar two-step cut at x0=A with gradients
(1,1,-b), then extend FORMALLY with constant gradient -b and affine
values through the last two steps. Its energy is -D and its column
modulo e is beta*J. Its negative residuals are
Q20=Q30=Q40=-u*beta, and its positive residuals are
Q03=Q13=w*b*beta, Q04=Q14=(w+v)*b*beta. All others vanish.
Thus (1) gives

 D=b*beta*(w*(Lambda03+Lambda13)+(w+v)*(Lambda04+Lambda14))
                        -beta^2*S-u*beta*(Lambda20+B0).

Besides (6), direct multiplication of T gives

    2<e1,B>_M=beta*B0+b*B1-Lambda13-(1+v)*Lambda14.

Adding these rows, and using (w+v)-w(1+v)=-vc, gives (5).

The additional ORIGINAL row used in this derivation is

    2<E,J+B>_M=-a*Lambda20+Lambda02+w*Lambda03+w*Lambda04.           (7)

In fact e2=e-J-B and
2M02=a*Lambda20-Lambda02-w*(Lambda03+Lambda04). This proves (7)
without any PSD quotient or new support assumption.


### Definition needed for the original positive root

For k>0 and real theta, set

    F(k,theta)=b^2*w^2-z*theta
          +(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta^2/4-k*ell*mu^2.

This definition and the original row identities just proved suffice for
the following derivation. No capped optimizer or eps=0 matching is used.

## 3. The unrestricted root and the new full-row remainder

Assume v>0 for now. Then ell>0, z>0 and 1-bt>0. Set

    k0=b^2*w/(ell*mu), kold=b^2*w^2/(ell*mu^2).

The minimum of F(k,theta) over all real theta is attained at

    theta(k)=2*z*k*mu/(1+a^2*k*mu).

It is strictly decreasing as a function of k: at each fixed theta,
partial F/partial k=-ell*mu^2-theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)<0, and the minimum
is attained continuously. At k0 the minimum divided by mu^2 is
b^2*(gamma-1)*(gamma+a^2*k0*mu)/(1+a^2*k0*mu)>0,
where gamma=w/mu>1. At kold it is negative, since F(kold,0)=0 and
the negative linear term improves it for small positive theta.
There is therefore a unique root k in (k0,kold).

Here is an explicit definition requiring no root search. Define

    Hbar=(2*b*w-beta
          +sqrt((beta-2*b*w)^2+4*b*w^2*(1-b*t)/mu))/(2*(1-b*t)),
    k=Hbar/(a^2*mu), theta=2*z*k*mu/(1+Hbar),
    x=b*w-a*theta/2=b*(w+Hbar*mu)/(1+Hbar), rho=x/beta,
    hcoef=theta/(2*k*mu), jcoef=a^2*theta/2,
    rstar=u*theta/2.

The positive Hbar solves

    (1-bt)*Hbar^2+(beta-2*bw)*Hbar-b*w^2/mu=0,

which follows by substituting theta(k) into F=0. Also

    0<rho<1, hcoef+jcoef=z,
    a*x-a*b*mu=hcoef, k*ell*mu^2+theta^2/(4*k*mu)
                                            =2*b*w*x-x^2.         (8)

The inequalities use mu<w and bw<=beta, with strictness supplied
by Hbar>0. The identities follow by expansion and F=0.

Full original feasibility itself forces v<2. Indeed the terminal
diagonal is n=||e4||_M^2=sum_(j<4)Lambda4j-s(s+2)>=0.
Every weight in the last row of (3) is at least v. Hence

    v*n<=s*(2C-(C+1)*v), so v<=2C/(C+1)<2.                       (9)

We now work on 0<v<2; v>=2 was already excluded by this original row.
Define the nonnegative correction

    qcorr=max(0,((1+v)*rstar-beta*b*v*c)
                         /(w+(1+v)*(1-rho))),
    rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho),
    X=beta*J+x*B.

The EXACT original-array remainder is

    eps:=k*R-D
       =(1+Hbar)*||X||_M^2
         -2*(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)*<E,X>_M+k*mu*u^2*m
         +cB*B0+c1*B1+c20*Lambda20+qcorr*Lambda02
         +c03*Lambda03+c04*Lambda04+c14*Lambda14+c23*Lambda23,      (10)

where

    cB=k*ell*mu*Hpre-beta*(b*w*H0pre-u)+a*rshift,
    c1=beta*(k*ell*mu-b^2*w), c20=beta*u-a*qcorr,
    c03=k*c03old-rshift+w*qcorr,
    c04=beta*b*v*c-(1+v)*rshift+w*qcorr,
    c14=beta*b*v*c, c23=k*c23old.

To check the identity, first combine (4) and (5). Its Gram part is

 beta^2*||J||_M^2+2*beta*b*w*<J,B>_M+k*ell*mu^2*Tcut
                                                 +k*mu*||Avec||_M^2.

Subtract 2*rshift*<E,B>_M+2*qcorr*<E,J+B>_M from that Gram part.
Restore them using (6) and (7); this gives precisely all costs in
(10). Since rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho), the subtraction differs
from 2*rstar*<E,B> by 2*qcorr*<E,X>/beta. F=0 and (8) turn the
uncorrected Gram into ||X||^2+k*mu*||uE-aX||^2. This proves (10).

Every displayed cost is nonnegative; cB,c1,c20,c03,c14,c23 are
STRICTLY positive. Here is the full sign and PSD check.

Let

    qmax=beta*u*(sqrt(k*mu*(1+Hbar))-a*k*mu).

Then

    0<=qcorr<qmax<beta*u/(2a).                                  (11)

If qcorr=0 this follows from Hbar>0. Otherwise put
tau=sqrt(Hbar/(1+Hbar)) in (0,1), Vprod=vbc, and
Sden=2+b+c+v. Direct substitution gives

    qcorr=(beta/a)*Vprod*(u*tau^2-a*beta)
                              /(Sden-Vprod+Vprod*tau^2),
    qmax=(beta*u/a)*tau/(1+tau).

The numerator of qcorr is positive in this case. The inequality
qcorr<qmax is equivalent to

    Vprod*(1+tau)*(u*tau-a*beta)<u*tau*Sden.

Its left side is smaller than 2*Vprod*u*tau. Moreover
2*Vprod<=2v<2+b+c+v=Sden, using bc<=1 and v<2. This proves the
strict inequality. The upper bound on qmax follows from
tau/(1+tau)<1/2.

Also rshift>0: when qcorr>0 its numerator is less than
(1+v)*rstar, while its denominator is strictly larger than
(1+v)*(1-rho). Thus qcorr<rstar/(1-rho).
At k=k0 the part of cB before a*rshift equals u*(1-bc)>=0;
it strictly increases with k. Hence cB>0. Since k>k0, c1>0.
Equation (11) gives c20>beta*u/2>0. Finally
rstar<k*u*mu*z=k*c03old and rshift<=rstar, proving c03>0.
The definition of qcorr gives c04>=0, and c14,c23>0.

Set

    alpha=(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)/(1+Hbar), Y=X-alpha*E,
    sigma=k*mu*u^2-(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)^2/(1+Hbar)>0.

The positivity of sigma is exactly qcorr<qmax. Thus (10) is

    eps=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)*||Y||_M^2+the nonnegative costs in (10).  (12)

In particular every full original certificate obeys D<=kR. This
necessity argument uses the actual original rows. Its comparison with
the complete older conditions is supplied by Sections1--9 of the
present joint text, not by a claim about an auxiliary optimizer.

## 4. The actual quadratic column and joint first-row budget

Define

    pquad=(1,-a,ab,-abc,abc*(v-1))^T,
    Q=1-C^2*a^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2,
    delta=u^2-2, W0=1+bc*(v-1).

Tp=e and Le=0. Telescoping h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2 gives

    ||pquad||_M^2=Q>=0,
    2<E,pquad>_M=u*(m-delta)
             +a^2*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40).    (13)

For the row formula, let O0=sum_(j>0)Lambda0j and
I0=Lambda20+Lambda30+Lambda40. Then m=1-a^2-aO0 and node0 flow
gives Lambda10=O0+2u-I0. With Te0=u e-a e0 and
Mp=Dmat pquad+T^T L^T pquad/2 one obtains

 pquad^T L e0=uO0+2au-a*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40),
 2<E,pquad>_M=2(1-a^2)-a*pquad^T L e0,

which gives (13). Both incoming weights 1-bc and W0 are nonnegative,
and 1-bc<=W0, including v<1.

By (12), eps>=sigma*m+c20*Lambda20+cB*B0. Define

    xi_cap=min(c20/(a^2*beta), cB/(a^2*W0)),

omitting the second term if W0=0. For every real xi with
xi<=xi_cap and xi<sigma/u,

    eps>=xi*u*delta-xi^2*Q/(sigma-xi*u).                         (14)

Subtract xi*u*delta using (13). All remaining multiplier coefficients
are nonnegative: for xi>=0 this is the definition of xi_cap and the
order of the incoming weights; for xi<0 the coefficients increase.
The remaining Gram expression after adding xi^2Q/(sigma-xi*u) is

    ||sqrt(sigma-xi*u)*E+xi*pquad/sqrt(sigma-xi*u)||_M^2>=0.

Thus this is the same ORIGINAL matrix and column, not independent
energy selections. Let Qplus=Q+u^2*delta. Sending xi to -infinity
shows Qplus>=0, and

    Qplus=a^2*(A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2).

That prerequisite is the old scalar-return condition and is not
counted as an independent improvement.

For completeness, when Q,Qplus>0 the free maximizing xi is
xi_free=(sigma/u)*(1-sqrt(Q/Qplus)). If xi_free<=xi_cap, (14)
has supremum

    Bcal=(sigma/u^2)*(sqrt(Qplus)-sqrt(Q))^2.

Otherwise its supremum is

    Bcal=xi_cap*u*delta-xi_cap^2*Q/(sigma-xi_cap*u).

The latter case automatically has xi_cap<sigma/u. For Q>0,Qplus=0,
the supremum is sigma*Q/u^2. For Q=0,Qplus>=0 it is
u*delta*min(xi_cap,sigma/u), and it is zero when Q=delta=0.
These statements follow on putting y=sigma-xi*u>0: the objective is

 sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2-(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The earlier first-row budget is also retained, on its stated domain
0<a<1 and a*eta<1, where

    eta=b/(1+w+v), nu=(1+eta)*(1-a*eta)/a,
    Erow=a+3+1/a-(u*delta/a)*eta-C^2*eta^2.

Its exact identity is

 Erow=nu*(m+a*(Lambda20+B0))+(1+eta)^2*M11
                 +(1+eta)*eta*((w+v)*Lambda12+v*Lambda13).        (15)

Here is a direct derivation. For orthonormal physical vectors U,V set
gfirst=-eta*U+sqrt(nu)*V and use saturated values on

 Xphys=(U+u*gfirst,U,-b*U,-(1+v)*eta*U,-eta*U),
 Gphys=(gfirst,U,-eta*U,-eta*U,-eta*U).

The nonzero residuals are Q20=Q30=Q40=-a*nu,
Q12=-(1+eta)*(b-eta), and Q13=-(1+eta)*v*eta. Every other finite
residual is zero. Use ||gfirst||^2=[1+(1-a)*eta]/a and
<U,gfirst>+a||gfirst||^2=1-a*eta to check the target0 residuals.
The energy telescope gives Erow and the two gradient columns modulo
e are sqrt(nu)*E and (1+eta)*e1, proving (15).

In particular, for EVERY lambda>=0, (14) holds with its left side
eps+lambda*Erow, sigma replaced by sigma+lambda*nu, and cap replaced
by

 min((c20+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*beta),
                         (cB+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*W0)).              (16)

This follows by adding the TWO exact budgets before using (13), so
the same m and original incoming coefficients must pay for both.
It does not replace any of the older2948 conditions. For example,
putting Wrow=max(beta,W0), Krow=max(u,a*Wrow) in (13),(15),(2) gives

 u*delta<=Krow*Erow/nu+2*sqrt(Q*Erow/nu).

For delta>0, v>1, ab<=1 and c(v-1)<=1, Krow=u and Q<1. These imply
Erow>nu*delta^2/u^2 and

    b<(a+3)*(C-a-2)/((a+1)*(C+a+2)).

To see the latter equivalence, the direct factorization is

 u^2*(Erow-nu*delta^2/u^2)
    =((a+3)-(delta+u*C)*eta)*((a+3)+(u*C-delta)*eta).

The second factor is positive since C>A and u*A>delta. Substituting
eta=b/(C-A-b) in the positive first factor gives the displayed
bound. All its hypotheses remain.

## 5. A further matched full-column inequality near equality

In this section v>0 and all constants are the ones already defined.
Let

    dphys=a*b*c*v=(1+v)*z,
    nbar=s*(2C-(C+1)*v)/v>=0,
    rcoef=ell*mu^2+mu*hcoef^2>0,
    Lnorm=sqrt((u-a*alpha)^2/sigma+a^2/(1+Hbar)),
    Lterm=sqrt((alpha-beta)^2/sigma+1/(1+Hbar)),
    Kterm=(dphys/x)*Lterm*sqrt(nbar), Jfee=a/(2*x),
    Pcost=max(ell*mu*Hpre/cB,ell*mu*beta/c1,c03old/c03,1/k),
    Gcost=max(mu*Lnorm^2,Pcost).

All denominators are strictly positive. If nbar<0, the original
terminal budget (9) already excludes the word; it is never square-rooted.

Every full original array satisfies the following explicit scalar test.
Write y=sqrt(eps), which requires eps>=0, and set

 tau_max(y)=(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y
       +sqrt((sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)^2+4*jcoef*(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)))
                                                            /(2*jcoef),
 Psi(y)=rcoef*tau_max(y)^2
            +2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*tau_max(y)*y+Gcost*y^2.

Then

                              R<=Psi(sqrt(eps)).                 (17)

Here is the full derivation retaining the actual quadratic column.
The vector identity, checked in all five coordinates, is

    pquad=uE-aX-jcoef*B+dphys*e4+ab*e.

The original terminal rows give

    2<E,e4>_M=a*Lambda40-Lambda04,
    2<J,e4>_M=2<E,e4>_M+beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14.

Since X=Y+alpha E, they imply

 x<B,e4>_M=(alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M
                              -beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/2.

Taking the inner product of pquad with B therefore gives

 <B,pquad>_M=(u-a*alpha)<E,B>_M-a<Y,B>_M-jcoef*Tcut
       +(dphys/x)*((alpha-beta)<E,e4>_M+<Y,e4>_M)
       -dphys*beta*(beta*Lambda40+b*Lambda41-Lambda14)/(2*x).       (18)

Let eps_G=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)||Y||_M^2 and let eps_C be the cost sum
in (12). Thus eps=eps_G+eps_C with both nonnegative. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz gives

 ||(u-a*alpha)E-aY||_M<=Lnorm*sqrt(eps_G),
 ||(alpha-beta)E+Y||_M<=Lterm*sqrt(eps_G).

Also ||e4||_M^2<=nbar by (9), and
c14=beta*dphys/a. Drop the negative Lambda40,Lambda41 terms in
(18), use Lambda14<=eps_C/c14, and use
<B,pquad>_M>=-sqrt(Tcut*Q). The result is

 jcoef*Tcut<=sqrt(Tcut*Q)
        +(Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut)+Kterm)*sqrt(eps_G)+Jfee*eps_C.          (19)

For the other direction (4) and Avec=(u-a*alpha)E-aY+hcoef*B give

 R<=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps_G)
                                    +mu*Lnorm^2*eps_G+Pcost*eps_C
  <=rcoef*Tcut+2*mu*hcoef*Lnorm*sqrt(Tcut*eps)+Gcost*eps.           (20)

The cost bound follows by comparing each cost in (4) to the cost of
the SAME multiplier in (12); their maximum ratio is precisely Pcost.
Thus costs and energies have not been chosen from different arrays.
Replacing eps_G,eps_C separately by eps in (19) gives, for
tcut=sqrt(Tcut)>=0,

 jcoef*tcut^2-(sqrt(Q)+Lnorm*y)*tcut-(Kterm*y+Jfee*y^2)<=0.

Its nonnegative root is tau_max(y). The right side of (20) increases
with tcut>=0, which proves (17).

This supplies a quantified positive-gap exclusion test. Psi is
continuous and strictly increasing on [0,infinity), tends to infinity,
and

    Psi(0)=rcoef*Q/jcoef^2.

Consequently, if R>rcoef*Q/jcoef^2, there is a unique y0>0 with
Psi(y0)=R, and every full array must have

                           eps>=y0^2>0.                         (21)

Strict increase follows from the explicit nondecreasing positive
coefficients in tau_max and Gcost>0. This is an algebraic definition
and proof; no numerical root finding is used. In particular Q=0,R>0
forces a positive eps, even when delta=0 and the first-row bound
(14) alone is zero. This prices a further original cross column.
No uniform lower bound as v,ell,R,Q or other factors vanish is claimed.

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED DRAFT. Actual runtime round2 of the

Accepted inputs are1252b8823bb5a290 for the original directed rows and

benchmark and scalar witnesses. Accepted1fca3e5dd555cb4a,

same-word comparisons. C98 and C99 are unverified context, not premises.
All new mathematical arguments used here are proved together below.

## 1. Actual functions, the enlarged dependence class, and the result

Let F be an everywhere finite convex differentiable function on a finite
Euclidean space, with1-Lipschitz gradient and a nonempty minimizer set.
For a supplied word h of length n consider its actual trajectory

    X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i g_i,  g_i=grad F(X_i),
    f_i=F(X_i)-min F,  q_i=||g_i||^2,
    R_init=dist(X_0,argmin F)>0,  V=2f_n/R_init^2.

All directed interpolation inequalities concern this ONE function.
The actual terminal gradient is unrestricted. If any queried gradient
vanishes then all later iterates minimize F and V=0. In the remaining
case define, at the queried indices,

    delta_i=f_i-q_i/2,  Jval_i=f_i+q_i/2,
    kval_i=Jval_i/q_i=1+delta_i/q_i.

For an included minimizer chosen as origin define separately

    eta_i=<X_i,g_i>/q_i,
    z_i=<X_i,g_i>-f_i-q_i/2.

The optimum rows give delta_i>=0 and z_i>=0, and

    kval_i=eta_i-z_i/q_i.                         (1)

Thus a restriction on kval is a restriction on actual values, not on
support about an arbitrarily named minimizer. No restriction on eta_i,
z_i, anchor density, signs of initial coordinates, or dimension is made.

Use the ORIGINAL enclosing-m words, with parameters fixed throughout
every recursive child:

    m>=4, N=2^m, n=N-1, sigma=1+sqrt(2),
    beta=1-1/m, c=sigma(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

Here h=H_m, 0<a<sqrt(2)-1, and the shortest step is lshort=1+a.
The following value range is the substantive restriction of this draft:

    1+a/2 <= kval_i <= 1+a  for every queried i.  (2)

Assume all adjacent QUERIED gradients have nonpositive inner product.
Set, for0<=i<n-1,

    d_i=h_i-1,
    t_i=-<g_i,g_(i+1)>/q_i >=0.

There is NO cap t_i<=1. For each odd i=1,3,...,n-4 define the signed
departure from the distance-two Markov identity

    defect2_i=<g_i,g_(i+2)>/q_i-t_i t_(i+1).       (3)

The middle physical step in each such pair is h_(i+1)=lshort.
Define for k in[1+a/2,1+a], writing e=k-1,

    Ushort_a(k)=[a-(1-a)e]/[1+(1-a)e],
    Aenv_a(k)=e[k+lshort Ushort_a(k)]/k^2,
    Cenv_a(k)=Ushort_a(k)(lshort-k)/k^2,
    Epair_a(k,d)=Aenv_a(k)+Cenv_a(k)d^2.            (4)

These are explicit real scalar functions; Epair is strictly positive.
For the indicated odd indices put

    eleft_i=|kval_i-kval_(i+1)|,
    eright_i=|kval_(i+2)-kval_(i+1)|,
    D_dep=sum_i d_i max(0,-defect2_i)
                    /[kval_(i+2) Epair_a(kval_(i+1),d_i)],
    E_mix=sum_i [(2/a)eleft_i+(1+4/a^2)eright_i]+D_dep,
    TV_val=sum_(i=0)^(n-2)|kval_(i+1)-kval_i|.

All sums over odd indices above stop at n-4. These quantities are paid
defects of an ACTUAL trajectory; they are neither anchor counts nor a
claim of interpolation sufficiency. For m>=256,

    E_mix <=26 TV_val+D_dep.                       (5)

The principal bound proved below is, for m>=256,

    V <= [64(1+2a)/(45a^3 beta^2)]
          beta^(2n)c^(-2m)(243/256)^(N/8)exp(E_mix)
      < 50 beta^(2n)c^(-2m)(243/256)^(N/8)exp(E_mix). (6)

In particular, the entire class (2) with E_mix=o(n) has B_n V->0.
This includes every constant-kval, arbitrarily dense Markov anchor,
with arbitrary nonstationary nonpositive correlations and arbitrarily
strong permitted long projections. It also includes variable-kval
Markov families with TV_val=o(n). More generally exact Markov dependence
is unnecessary: E_mix=o(n) is sufficient for the same obstruction.

range(2), permitting positive adjacent correlations, paying linear

## 2. Original rows and exact remote slack transport

The accepted original residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,X_j-X_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0. (7)

For a general step h_i=1+d_i>1, adding both adjacent rows gives

    q_(i+1)/q_i <=d_i+(d_i-1)t_i.

Cauchy--Schwarz gives t_i^2<=q_(i+1)/q_i, so

    (t_i+1)(t_i-d_i)<=0,  0<=t_i<=d_i.             (8)

The nonnegative lower bound uses the assumed adjacent sign. In
particular at a shortest step q_(i+1)<=a q_i.

The reverse adjacent slack, a different quantity from z_i, is

    ell_rev_i=-Q_(i+1,i)
       =delta_i-delta_(i+1)+d_i t_i q_i-q_(i+1)>=0. (9)

Suppose for this paragraph the queried unit directions g_i/sqrt(q_i)
have the FULL Markov product law: their inner product at indices r<s
is the product of the adjacent normalized inner products from r to s.
Set p_(r,s)=product_(k=r)^(s-1)(-t_k), with p_(s,s)=1.
The amplitude ratios telescope to give <g_r,g_s>=q_r p_(r,s).
For i+1<j<n, expanding(7) and the GD recursion
gives the exact transport identity

    Q_(j,i)-Q_(j,i+1)
      =(delta_(i+1)-delta_i)(1-p_(i+1,j))
                         -ell_rev_i p_(i+1,j).      (10)

Indeed the difference before substituting(9) is

    delta_(i+1)-delta_i
         +p_(i+1,j)[q_(i+1)-d_i t_i q_i],

which equals(10). In particular the first remote reverse row is

    Q_(i+2,i)=-ell_rev_(i+1)
       +(1+t_(i+1))(delta_(i+1)-delta_i)
       +t_(i+1)ell_rev_i.                          (11)

Thus adjacent reverse equalities at i and i+1 force
delta_(i+1)<=delta_i. With a constant kval>1, they force
q_(i+1)<=q_i; hence t_i>1 is then impossible by Cauchy--Schwarz.
Attempting to saturate adjacent rows while using a strong projection
omits exactly the reserve increase charged by(11).

Equation(11) alone is not assumed sufficient for legality. The
whole-family bound below concerns actual functions satisfying ALL rows.
For the larger non-Markov class we use(3) explicitly instead of
transferring(10) outside its hypothesis.

## 3. A short-step cap that retains the actual value ratios

Consider a shortest step from a queried point of ratio k to another
queried point of ratio k', both in(2), and let its projection be u>=0.
Write r=q_next/q_current. The forward adjacent row is

    (k'-1)r >= (k-1)-a+u.                          (12)

Its sum with the reverse row yields r<=a-(1-a)u by(8).
Combining these inequalities, without replacing either value, gives

    u <= Ushort_a(k')+(k'-k)/[1+(1-a)(k'-1)].       (13)

The numerator of Ushort is positive on the whole range(2). Its derivative
in k equals -(1-a)(1+a)/[1+(1-a)(k-1)]^2, of absolute value at most1.
Consequently

    u<=Ushort_a(k)+2|k'-k|.                        (14)

Also Ushort_a(k)>=a^2/(1+a-a^2)>=a^2/2. The first inequality uses its
monotonic decrease in k, and the second uses1+a-a^2<2.

## 4. Exact two-step envelope, including a changed dependence law

Take an odd index i in the range used in Section1. Abbreviate its three
ratios by k0,k1,k2; put s=q_(i+1)/q_i, r=q_(i+2)/q_i,
t=t_i, u=t_(i+1), d=d_i, and v=defect2_i.
The reverse adjacent row at i gives

    k1 s <= k0-1+d t.                              (15)

The ORIGINAL remote reverse row from i+2 to i, expanded directly, is

    Q_(i+2,i)/q_i=k2 r-(k0-1)+d(tu+v)-lshort u s.

Thus, writing vminus=max(0,-v),

    k2 r <=(k0-1)(1+lshort u/k1)
              +u(lshort-k1)d t/k1+d vminus.        (16)

The coefficient lshort-k1 is nonnegative by(2). Since0<=t<=d,
replace dt by d^2 on the right. In the constant-ratio, v=0 case,
(13) allows u<=Ushort_a(k1);(16) then proves exactly

    r<=Epair_a(k1,d).                              (17)

No limitation on the size of t below its universal bound d was used.

For variable ratios put eleft=|k0-k1| and eright=|k2-k1|.
All coefficients in the right side of(16) after replacing dt are
nonnegative. Therefore its vminus-free part is bounded by Epair times

    (k1/k2) max(1,(k0-1)/(k1-1))
                          max(1,u/Ushort_a(k1)).

Because k1-1>=a/2, (14) and the lower bound following it give

    k1/k2 <=exp(eright),
    max(1,(k0-1)/(k1-1))<=exp(2eleft/a),
    max(1,u/Ushort_a(k1))<=exp(4eright/a^2).

If E0=(2/a)eleft+(1+4/a^2)eright, we have

    r<=Epair exp(E0)+d vminus/k2
      <=Epair exp(E0+d vminus/(k2 Epair)).          (18)

For the second inequality factor Epair exp(E0), use E0>=0 and
1+x<=exp(x) for x>=0. This proves the asserted extension to non-Markov
laws with an explicit signed price. Positive v only strengthens the
remote row and needs no penalty. The terminal gradient is not used.

## 5. Uniform real envelope coefficients

For0<a<=sqrt(2)-1 and k in(2),

    0<Aenv_a(k)<=1/3,   0<=Cenv_a(k)<=a^2/4.        (19)

Here is a direct proof. Set e=k-1 in[a/2,a], D=1+(1-a)e and
U=Ushort_a(k). It is positive and decreasing in e. Hence

    U <= a(1+a)/(2+a-a^2) <=a(1+a)/2.

Also a-e<=a/2 and k>=1+a/2, so

    Cenv=U(a-e)/k^2
       <=a^2(1+a)/[4(1+a/2)^2]<=a^2/4.

For the bound on Aenv, consider A(e)=e[k+(1+a)U]/k^2 on0<=e<=a.
Direct differentiation gives

    A'(e)={k+(1+a)(1-e)U
                -e k(1-a)(1+a)^2/D^2}/k^3.

The middle term is nonnegative. Moreover
e(1-a)(1+a)^2/D^2<=a(1+a)<1, since a<=sqrt(2)-1.
Thus A is increasing. At e=a, using U=a^2/(1+a-a^2),

    A(a)=a/(1+a-a^2)<=1/3,

the last inequality being equivalent to a^2+2a<=1. This proves(19).
In particular

    Epair_a(k,d)<=1/3+(a^2/4)d^2.                  (20)

This envelope holds at every macro separately, even when its k changes.

## 6. The complete norm and the actual closest distance

For the full product-correlated subclass, write A_i=sqrt(q_i) and
u_i=g_i/A_i, for0<=i<n. Its correlations are real numbers rho_i in[-1,0]
with <u_i,u_j>=product_(k=i)^(j-1)rho_k. Actual real coordinates are

    u_0=e_0,
    u_(i+1)=rho_i u_i+sqrt(1-rho_i^2)e_(i+1),       (21)

where each nondegenerate innovation is orthogonal to the past. The
literal finite sign law is

    P(s_0,...,s_(n-1))=2^(-n)
                     product_(i<n-1)(1+rho_i s_i s_(i+1)),
    s_i in{-1,1}.                                 (22)

Summing the last sign successively proves normalization. Equivalently,
start with a fair sign and independent bond signs of means rho_i; this
gives the stated products. Interior rho give positive probability to
every sign word. This law is not a substitute for interpolation.

Conversely the product identities imply that
(u_(i+1)-rho_i u_i)/sqrt(1-rho_i^2) is a unit vector orthogonal to all
earlier u_j, by expanding its inner products. Thus(21) also describes
the canonical coordinates of any such product law.

Let0 be any included minimizer and let X_perp be the component of X_0
perpendicular to every queried gradient. Since previous gradients are
orthogonal to each new innovation, its initial coefficient
w_(i+1)=<X_0,e_(i+1)> satisfies

    eta_(i+1)A_(i+1)=rho_i(eta_i-h_i)A_i
                            +sqrt(1-rho_i^2)w_(i+1).

The initial e_0 coefficient is eta_0 A_0. Orthogonal decomposition
therefore gives the COMPLETE identity

    ||X_0||^2=eta_0^2 q_0+||X_perp||^2
      +sum_(i:|rho_i|<1)
         [eta_(i+1)A_(i+1)-rho_i(eta_i-h_i)A_i]^2
                                             /(1-rho_i^2). (23)

At rho_i=-1 the numerator must vanish and there is no new summand.
Every dense initial coefficient and any perpendicular reserve is paid.
This is a norm about the included minimizer, not automatically the true
closest-minimizer distance. For the whole-class proof we instead use

    q_0<=R_init^2,                                 (24)

which follows from gradient Lipschitzness between X_0 and EVERY minimizer,
followed by taking the infimum. Hence the proof neither drops any initial
cost nor incorrectly declares a conveniently chosen minimizer closest.
The explicit finite interpolants in Section9 have unique minimizer0 and
their true distances are computed from all their coordinates.

## 1. Concrete family and result

Write X_i,G_i,F_i for the actual normalized GD point, its gradient, and its
function value. Work first with smoothness one and minimum value zero. Let e be a unit vector
in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. For a compact convex set C_tri37 containing
zero and e, assume the explicit radial-cap condition

    <e,v> <= 1   for every v in C_tri37.                              (1)

Define the ONE STATIC function

    F_tri37(x) = max_{v in C_tri37} { <x,v> - ||v||^2/2 }.                (2)

Fix two preceding physical steps a37,b37>=0 and a finite following word
tail37=(h_tail37_0,...,h_tail37_(m-1)) with h_tail37_j>=0. Put S37=sum h_tail37_j, s_0=0 and
s_j=sum_(k<j)h_tail37_k. The empty following word is allowed. Fix r37>=1+S37.
The suffix jets to be retained are

    X_(2+j)=(r37-s_j)e, G_(2+j)=e,
    F_(2+j)=r37-s_j-1/2,             0<=j<=m.                    (3)

We solve the following DECLARED FAMILY exactly: the initial point p37 belongs
to C_tri37, so G_0=p37 and F_0=||p37||^2/2; the first two actual updates reach r37 e;
and C_tri37 satisfies (1). This is a genuine restriction, not a claimed necessary
form of every smooth convex extension of the suffix. At r37=1,S37=0, condition
(1) remains an explicit family assumption; it cannot be inferred just from
the endpoint jet at e.

Write A_min37(a37,b37,r37) for the smallest possible squared TRUE initial distance
within this family, when it is nonempty. The following table gives its exact
domain and value. The terminal normalized payoff for its optimal member is

    V(a37,b37,r37,S37) = (2r37-2S37-1)/A_min37(a37,b37,r37).                       (4)

The complete domain is as follows.

* If a37=1, the family is empty, for every b37>=0 and every allowed r37.
* If 0<=a37<1 and b37>1, then

      A_min37 = r37^2 / ((1-a37)^2 (b37-1)^2).

* If 0<=a37<1 and 0<=b37<=1, the only nonempty case is a37=b37=0,r37=1
  (therefore S37=0). Then A_min37=1. This includes any all-zero following word.
* If a37>1 and 0<=b37<=1, put alpha=a37-1. Then

      A_min37 = (r37+b37)^2/alpha^2.

* If a37>1 and b37>1, put alpha=a37-1, beta=b37-1, and

      D=b37 beta + r37(beta-1).

  If D<=0, then A_min37=(r37+b37)^2/alpha^2.
  If D>0 and r37<=alpha beta, then A_min37=r37^2/(alpha^2 beta^2).
  If D>0 and r37>alpha beta, then

      A_min37 = 1 + (r37-alpha beta)(r37+b37+alpha)/(alpha^2 beta).    (5)

At D=0 the scalar and appropriate limiting formulas agree. The formulas
r37^2/(alpha^2 beta^2) and (5) both equal one at r37=alpha beta;
this is a boundary of the minimizing branches only when D>=0. No inverse
division by a37-1 or b37-1 is being used to hide their zero cases.

In particular the following explicit triangular rule is legal, whether or
not it is radius-optimal:

    a37>1, b37>1, r37>=max(1+S37,alpha beta),
    T37^2=(r37-alpha beta)(r37+b37+alpha)/(alpha^2 beta),
    p37=e+T37 w,  q37=-(r37 e+alpha p37)/b37,
    C_tri37=conv{0,p37,q37,e},                                          (6)

where w is a unit vector perpendicular to e and T37 is the nonnegative square
root. Thus there is a concrete nonempty domain for every a37,b37>1 and every
finite nonnegative following word. Its true initial squared distance is
1+T37^2. When T37>0, zero is in the interior of the triangle conv{p37,q37,e}, so the
minimum is unique in the displayed two-dimensional span, which is the
ambient space used in this construction. No dimension, offset or minimum
change is unpriced.

## 2. Direct static realization, minimum and all directed rows

For a compact convex C_tri37 the maximizer in (2) is its unique Euclidean
projection P_tri37(x), since the maximand equals
||x||^2/2-||x-v||^2/2. The projection is characterized by

    <x-g,v-g><=0 for every v in C_tri37,       g=P_tri37(x).              (7)

For completeness, necessity follows by differentiating squared distance
along g+u(v-g),0<=u<=1, at u=0. Sufficiency follows by expanding
||x-v||^2-||x-g||^2=||v-g||^2-2<x-g,v-g>.
Uniqueness follows from strict convexity of squared distance on C_tri37.

Applying (7) at x and z and adding gives
||P_tri37(x)-P_tri37(z)||^2<=<x-z,P_tri37(x)-P_tri37(z)>, hence the projection is
one-Lipschitz. The two maximizing inequalities in (2) give

    0 <= F_tri37(z)-F_tri37(x)-<P_tri37(x),z-x>
      <= <P_tri37(z)-P_tri37(x),z-x> <= ||z-x||^2.

The last bound proves differentiability, with gradient P_tri37(x). Thus F_tri37 is
finite, convex and one-smooth. Convexity also follows directly from (2).

Its exact minimizer set is the polar cone

    C_tri37^polar={z:<z,v><=0 for all v in C_tri37}.                       (8)

Indeed a polar z gives F_tri37(z)=0 by choosing v=0 and bounding all other
terms. If <z,v>>0 for some v in C_tri37, then sufficiently small positive u has
uv in C_tri37 and u<z,v>-u^2||v||^2/2>0, so F_tri37(z)>0. This proves (8).
For p37 in C_tri37 and z in C_tri37^polar,

    ||p37-z||^2=||p37||^2+||z||^2-2<p37,z> >= ||p37||^2.

Since zero is a minimizer, the TRUE distance from p37 to the minimum set is
exactly ||p37||. This also covers degenerate triangles and nonunique minima.

At any sampled point with gradient g_i=P_tri37(x_i), put y_i=x_i-g_i and
f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2. In the orientation of accepted 1252b8823bb5a290,

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<y_j,g_i-g_j>.                                     (9)

Therefore (7) proves EVERY ordered interpolation row, including both
directions of each new-old pair. Include x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Equation
(9) covers all its rows as well. No terminal row is omitted here.

Condition (1) implies P_tri37(u e)=e and F_tri37(u e)=u-1/2 for every u>=1:
the vector (u-1)e satisfies (7) at e. Since r37-s_j>=r37-S37>=1,
the complete suffix (3) is an actual GD suffix on (2), including repeated
points at zero steps. Only its total S37 is used; arbitrary large individual
following steps are allowed subject to the displayed r37>=1+S37.

## 3. Proof of the complete predecessor table

Because p37 is in C_tri37, the first update is X_1=(1-a37)p37. Let q37=P_tri37(X_1).
The second actual update is equivalent to

    r37 e=(1-a37)p37-b37 q37.                                          (10)

If a37=1, then X_1=0 and q37=0, so (10) cannot hold with r37>=1.

Suppose 0<=a37<1. Convexity and 0,p37 in C_tri37 imply
q37=(1-a37)p37. Hence r37 e=(1-b37)(1-a37)p37. If b37=1 it is impossible.
If b37<1, p37 is a positive multiple of e; its scalar multiple is
r37/((1-a37)(1-b37)). By (1) this is at most one. Since r37>=1 and both factors
are at most one, it forces r37=1 and a37=b37=0. If b37>1, the unique possible p37 is

    p37=-r37 e/((1-a37)(b37-1)).

The segment C_tri37=conv{p37,e} contains zero, obeys (1), and contains q37=(1-a37)p37.
It realizes (10). This proves all a37<1 cases, with their exact distances.

Now suppose a37>1 and set alpha=a37-1. If b37=0, then X_1=r37 e, so
p37=-r37 e/alpha and q37=e. This realizes and proves the stated value.

For b37>0, equation (10) gives q37=-(r37 e+alpha p37)/b37. Write

    u=<e,p37>, A=||p37||^2, v=<e,q37>=-(r37+alpha u)/b37.

Condition (1) implies u<=1 and v<=1. The projection condition at q37,
tested against e, is

    0 >= <r37 e+(b37-1)q37,e-q37>
      = r37(1-v)+(b37-1)(v-||q37||^2).                            (11)

If 0<b37<1, use ||q37||^2>=v^2. The right side in (11) is at least
(1-v)[r37+(b37-1)v]. Here 1-v>=0 and
r37+(b37-1)v>=r37+b37-1>=b37>0. Thus v=1. Substituting in (11) gives
(1-b37)(||q37||^2-1)<=0, so q37=e. Equation (10) then forces
p37=-(r37+b37)e/alpha. The segment C_tri37=conv{p37,e} realizes these data.
If b37=1, (11) gives v=1, hence u=-(r37+1)/alpha. Thus
A>=u^2=(r37+1)^2/alpha^2, and the same segment with q37=e attains it.
For b37=1, q37 need not equal e for every other feasible member; only the
displayed minimizing member is asserted to have that gradient.

It remains to handle a37>1,b37>1. Set beta=b37-1>0 and define

    u_- = -(r37+b37)/alpha,       u_+ = r37/(alpha beta).

The cap at q37 and p37 gives u in [u_-,1]. Expanding (11) and using
||q37||^2=(r37^2+2r37 alpha u+alpha^2 A)/b37^2 yields the necessary bound

    A >= ell_bound37(u)
      := r37(r37+b37)/(alpha^2 beta)-[b37 beta+r37(beta-1)]u/(alpha beta)
       = (u_-+u_+)u-u_-u_+.                                 (12)

Also A>=u^2, and

    ell_bound37(u)-u^2=-(u-u_-)(u-u_+).                      (13)

This is now a solved one-variable lower bound, not an implicit feasible-set
oracle. If D=b37 beta+r37(beta-1)<=0, ell_bound37 has nonnegative slope.
On [u_-,min(u_+,1)], (13) gives
max(u^2,ell_bound37(u))=ell_bound37(u), whose minimum is at u_-.
If u_+<=1, on [u_+,1] the maximum is u^2, whose minimum is u_+^2;
D<=0 implies u_+>=-u_-, so this cannot improve u_-^2.
Thus A>=u_-^2. The segment with p37=u_-e,q37=e attains the bound.

If D>0, ell_bound37 has negative slope. The same interval argument gives the minimum
at u=min(u_+,1). If r37<=alpha beta, this is u_+. Take
p37=u_+e and q37=-alpha p37; the segment containing q37 and e also contains p37 and
zero. Since X_1=q37 is in C_tri37, its projection is q37, and (10) holds.
The cap holds because u_+<=1. Its distance is exactly u_+^2.

If D>0 and r37>alpha beta, the minimum is ell_bound37(1). Direct factoring gives

    ell_bound37(1)=1+(r37-alpha beta)(r37+b37+alpha)/(alpha^2 beta).

The triangular construction (6), checked next, attains it. At D=0 the two
root magnitudes coincide, so the endpoint formulas agree. This establishes
all necessity and sufficiency assertions in the table, even for larger C_tri37
and in arbitrary finite dimension satisfying the declared assumptions.

## 4. Complete triangular jet check

For (6) put A=1+T37^2 and retain its p37,q37. The actual points are

    X_0=p37, G_0=p37, y_0=0, F_0=A/2;
    X_1=-alpha p37, G_1=q37,
    y_1=(r37 e-alpha beta p37)/b37;
    X_(2+j)=(r37-s_j)e, G_(2+j)=e,
    y_(2+j)=(r37-s_j-1)e.

The first two update equations follow by substitution. Also <e,p37>=1 and
<e,q37>=-(r37+alpha)/b37<1, so the whole C_tri37 satisfies (1). The squared T37 in
(6) is nonnegative on the entire stated domain.

Here is the complete nontrivial normal table at q37:

    <y_1,p37-q37> = -alpha beta(A-1)/b37 <=0,
    <y_1,e-q37> = 0,
    <y_1,0-q37> = -(r37-alpha beta)/b37 <=0.                       (14)

To see the equality in the middle without assuming it, substituting the
formula for A into (12) gives A=ell_bound37(1), which is equality in (11).
Then <y_1,q37>=<y_1,e>=(r37-alpha beta)/b37. The other two identities in (14)
follow from <y_1,p37>=(r37-alpha beta A)/b37. Thus

    F_1=||q37||^2/2+(r37-alpha beta)/b37,
    ||q37||^2=(r37^2+2r37 alpha+alpha^2 A)/b37^2.                    (15)

At a suffix point let z=r37-s_j-1>=0. Its normal products are

    <z e,p37-e>=0,
    <z e,q37-e>=-z(r37+alpha+b37)/b37<=0,
    <z e,0-e>=-z<=0.                                       (16)

At p37, y_0=0, and at the minimum all normal products vanish. Equations

all directed rows. Suffix-to-suffix products are zero. This is stronger
than checking only neighboring gradients or retaining only the old planes.

If T37>0, p37 and e are linearly independent and
alpha p37+b37 q37+r37 e=0 with all three coefficients positive. Consequently zero
lies in the interior of their triangle in span{e,w}, our chosen ambient
plane, and (8) is {0}. If T37=0, the initial
point lies on its one-dimensional span and the exact-distance argument

## 5. Preserving arbitrary absolute suffix jets and moving the minimum

The preceding construction does not require resetting the suffix's location
or values. Fix L>0, a scale tau37>0, a physical suffix starting point Z, a unit
direction e, and an absolute starting value V_2. Specify once and for all

    x_(2+j)=Z-tau37 s_j e,
    grad f(x_(2+j))=L tau37 e,
    f(x_(2+j))=V_2-L tau37^2 s_j.                              (17)

For every allowed r37 and its concrete C_tri37, put

    z_star=Z-tau37 r37 e,
    v_star=V_2-L tau37^2(r37-1/2),
    f(x)=v_star+L tau37^2 F_tri37((x-z_star)/tau37).                  (18)

It is one static convex L-smooth function, and all jets (17), including the
terminal, are identical as r37 changes. Its minimum value is exactly v_star.
Its two preceding points are z_star+tau37 p37 and z_star+tau37(1-a37)p37.
The update with physical step h/L is exactly the scaled update by h used
above. Its TRUE initial distance is tau37 sqrt(A), and its terminal gap is
L tau37^2(r37-S37-1/2). Thus its normalized payoff is precisely (4).
Both the movement of the minimum and its level have been recomputed.
For T37>0 in the chosen ambient plane, the minimizer is uniquely z_star.
If the example is embedded in a larger space, or the triangle is degenerate,
z_star is still the closest minimizer to the initial point, so the same
true-distance calculation applies.

## 7. Exact paid continuation with every old triangle jet retained

Fix the triangle with a37=b37=2 and r37>1, and any following word with
0<=S37<=r37-1. Retain all the old jets, including p37, q37 and the suffix (3).
Let A=r37^2+2r37-2. The old nonzero normals are

    y_1=(r37 e-p37)/2,
    y_(2+j)=(r37-s_j-1)e.

Because y_2=(r37-1)e is nonzero, an added gradient vector z preserves all
old gradient projections and values if and only if it obeys both

    <e,z><=1,
    <y_1,z><=(r37-1)/2.                                      (26)

Here sufficiency is for any enlarged compact convex C_tri37' containing C_tri37 and
only added vertices satisfying (26). Necessity is the old projection
condition (7); it applies whether a proposed added vertex is later queried
or merely included. The initial normal y_0=0 adds no condition. Every old
value remains <x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2. Since the old triangle contains zero
in its interior, every enlargement still has the SAME unique minimizer0.

Intersect (26) with the line z=t p37. Since

    <e,p37>=1, <y_1,p37>=-(r37-1)(r37+2)/2,

the exact permitted interval is

    -1/(r37+2) <= t <= 1.                                    (27)

Now supply ANY finite preceding word c=(c_0,...,c_(ell-1)) of nonnegative
steps. Restrict the new preceding queries to have gradient equal to their
position, as in the initial member of Section1. This restriction is
explicit: it means each such point lies in C_tri37', and its proximal residual
is zero. The existing first point p37 is the endpoint of this prefix.

There is an exact complete rule, with no optimization oracle:

* No c_j may equal1.
* Define t_ell=1 and, backwards,

      t_j=1 / product_(k=j)^(ell-1)(1-c_k).

* Every t_j,0<=j<ell, must lie in the interval (27).

These conditions are necessary because an actual core query satisfies
X_(j+1)=(1-c_j)X_j, so all new points must be t_j p37; a unit step would
hit zero, which is absorbing. They must also satisfy every retained old
normal, giving (27). They are sufficient by taking

    C_tri37'=conv(C_tri37,{t_j p37:0<=j<ell}).                             (28)

Every new point is in C_tri37', hence has exactly its own position as gradient,
and the recurrence executes the actual preceding word forwards.
Condition (26) preserves EVERY old jet. Formula (9) proves every new-old
row in both directions: new proximal residuals are zero, whereas old
normals tested on new gradients give (26). New-new rows are zero.
The same unique minimum remains0. The TRUE squared initial distance is
t_0^2 A, and the payoff is exactly the old payoff multiplied by

    1/t_0^2=product_(j<ell)(1-c_j)^2.                        (29)

This is a paid continuation invariant for the specified class. It is

3. DOMAIN AND MINIMUM-RADIUS TABLE: NECESSITY, ATTAINMENT, BOUNDARIES

Use the draft's a37,b37>=0, r37>=1+S37, where S37 is the nonnegative
total of the fixed following word. The declared family consists of compact
convex C_tri37 containing 0,e, obeying <e,v><=1 for every v in C_tri37,
and an initial p37 in C_tri37. Its first gradient is p37. Its second
gradient q37 is P_C((1-a37)p37), and reaching the required suffix means

  r37*e=(1-a37)p37-b37*q37.                                  (A6)

The true squared radius is ||p37||^2 by the polar calculation in part 1,
including higher dimensions and nonunique minima. Thus minimizing this
norm is the stated minimum-distance problem, not a surrogate problem.

If a37=1, the first update is zero and every subsequent gradient at zero
is zero, so (A6) cannot reach r37>=1. This is an exact exclusion.

If 0<=a37<1, convexity places (1-a37)p37 in C_tri37, so
q37=(1-a37)p37. At b37=1, (A6) is impossible. At b37<1, (A6) forces
p37=r37*e/((1-a37)(1-b37)); the cap and r37>=1 then force
a37=b37=0,r37=1, with squared radius 1. At b37>1 it forces
p37=-r37*e/((1-a37)(b37-1)), and the segment conv{p37,e} attains the
squared radius r37^2/((1-a37)^2(b37-1)^2). This includes a37=0.

For a37>1 set alpha=a37-1. If b37=0, (A6) forces p37=-r37*e/alpha;
the segment conv{p37,e} has projection e at r37*e and gives exactly
r37^2/alpha^2. No division by b37 has been made at this endpoint.

For b37>0, put A=||p37||^2, u=<e,p37>, and
v=<e,q37>=-(r37+alpha*u)/b37. The cap gives u<=1 and v<=1. The
projection inequality at q37 tested against e is

  r37(1-v)+(b37-1)(v-||q37||^2)<=0.                           (A7)

When 0<b37<1, ||q37||^2>=v^2 bounds the left side below by
(1-v)[r37+(b37-1)v]. The second factor is at least b37>0, so v=1.
Substitution back into (A7) forces ||q37||^2=1, hence q37=e. At b37=1,
(A7) forces v=1 without forcing q37=e, but still implies
u=-(r37+1)/alpha and A>=u^2. In every 0<b37<=1 case the segment
with p37=-(r37+b37)e/alpha and q37=e attains

  A_min37=(r37+b37)^2/alpha^2.

In particular the draft correctly distinguishes the b37=1 lower-bound
argument from the stronger assertion q37=e for every feasible member.

Now b37>1. Set beta=b37-1>0,
u_-=-(r37+b37)/alpha, u_+=r37/(alpha*beta), and
D=b37*beta+r37*(beta-1). The cap at q37 and at p37 gives u in [u_-,1].
Expanding (A7) with
||q37||^2=(r37^2+2r37*alpha*u+alpha^2*A)/b37^2 gives

  A >= ell(u)=(u_-+u_+)u-u_-u_+,
  A >= u^2,
  ell(u)-u^2=-(u-u_-)(u-u_+).                                 (A8)

Thus the lower-bound problem reduces to minimizing max(u^2,ell(u)) on
the actual interval [u_-,1]. The slope of ell is -D/(alpha*beta).

For D<=0 it is nonnegative, and the left root u_- minimizes the linear
piece. If u_+<=1, the remaining parabolic piece begins at u_+>0;
D<=0 implies u_+>=-u_-, so its minimum u_+^2 is no smaller. The segment
p37=u_-*e,q37=e attains A=u_-^2 because its input to the second query
is (r37+b37)e, whose projection onto that segment is e.

For D>0 the line is decreasing. If r37<=alpha*beta, then u_+<=1 and
the minimum is u_+^2. It is attained by p37=u_+*e and
q37=-alpha*p37, in the segment conv{q37,e}. The first updated point
is already q37 in this segment, and q37-b37*q37=r37*e. If
r37>alpha*beta, the minimum is ell(1), equal to

  1+(r37-alpha*beta)(r37+b37+alpha)/(alpha^2*beta).             (A9)

For this last branch let T37 be the nonnegative square root of A9-1,
take a unit w perpendicular to e, put p37=e+T37*w and
q37=-(r37*e+alpha*p37)/b37, and take their convex hull with 0 and e.
The cap is satisfied. The residual at q37 is
y_1=(r37*e-alpha*beta*p37)/b37. Its normal products against p37,e,0 are

  -alpha*beta*(A-1)/b37,  0,  -(r37-alpha*beta)/b37.

They are all nonpositive. At a suffix point the residual is z*e with
z=r37-s_j-1>=0; its products against p37-e,q37-e,0-e are
0, -z*(r37+alpha+b37)/b37, -z. Hence every required projection holds.
The same calculation proves the explicit triangle legal whenever
r37>=max(1+S37,alpha*beta), even when D<=0 makes it nonoptimal.

These explicit realizations close the gap that would arise from using
only necessary inequalities in (A8). They work in finite dimension and
