      =b^2*(gamma-1)*(gamma+Hk)/(1+Hk)>0.                            (11)

At k=kold, its allowed minimum is strictly negative: choose any
positive theta smaller than both upper bounds and sufficiently close
to zero, and the constant term vanishes while -z*theta dominates the
positive quadratic term. For each fixed theta,

    partial F/partial k=-ell*mu^2-theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)<0.

Also (10) minimizes over the fixed interval [0,U], since the other
bound is automatic at that minimizer. Thus this minimum is continuous
and strictly decreasing in k. It follows that there is a unique

    kstar in (k0,kold), F(kstar,theta_opt(kstar))=0.                   (12)

This is an exact algebraic number, without a numerical root search.
Here are explicit branches. Define

    Bint=a^2*b^2*mu*(2*gamma-1)-ell,
    kint=(Bint+sqrt(Bint^2+4*a^2*ell*mu*b^2*gamma^2))
                                                       /(2*a^2*ell*mu).

If theta_free(kint)<=U, then kstar=kint. Otherwise define

    V0=b^2*w^2-z*U+a^2*U^2/4,
    V1=U^2/(4*mu),
    kbound=(V0+sqrt(V0^2+4*ell*mu^2*V1))/(2*ell*mu^2).

Then kstar=kbound. These are obtained by multiplying respectively
F(k,theta_free(k))=0 and F(k,U)=0 by their positive denominators.
If the free root violates the cap, the increasing theta_free remains
above U at every larger k; the boundary root is therefore the correct
one. Equality of the branch conditions gives the same root.

At v=0 with ell>0, z=U=0, gamma=1 and k0=kold=b^2/ell. Set
kstar=kold and theta_opt=0; (7)--(9) still hold. No strict gain is
claimed on this boundary.

For v>0,ell>0 the new bound is strictly stronger than the old
two-energy gap bound Dprefix<=kold*Rcut whenever Dprefix>0:

    Rcut>=Dprefix/kstar,
    Gap>= (K/kstar-ell)*Dprefix >0.                                 (13)

Thus it excludes an explicit POSITIVE gap strip, not just Gap=0.
This comparison is ONLY with the previous nested two-energy bound.
It is not a comparison with the entire older necessary system.

The constant kstar is sharp for the following explicitly delimited
relaxation: retain arbitrary PSD Gram data for (E,J,B), (3)--(5),
and nonnegative quantities B0,B1,Lambda20,Lambda03,Lambda04,
Lambda14,Lambda23, but impose no remaining original rows or quadratic
column. This sharpness does not assert a full certificate.

To prove it, work in a one-dimensional Gram space with B=1 and set
Tcut=1, B0=B1=Lambda20=Lambda03=Lambda14=Lambda23=0. Let
k=kstar,theta=theta_opt(kstar), x=b*w-a*theta/2 and J=-x/beta.
If the free branch applies, set E=0,Lambda04=0. The equation
theta=2*k*mu*(a*x-a*b*mu) follows from theta=theta_free.
Consequently both squares in (8) vanish and (5) holds.

On the capped branch put

    q04=2*(a*x-a*b*mu-theta/(2*k*mu))/(u*(1+v)),
    Lambda04=q04, E=-(1+v)*q04/2.

The condition theta=U<=theta_free implies q04>=0. Again both squares
and (5) hold, while c04=0. Define Rcut and Dprefix in this RELAXATION
by (3) and (4), rather than by the step-only values. Then Rcut>0
because ell*mu^2*Tcut>0, and Dprefix=kstar*Rcut. This proves exactly
the stated sharpness and explicitly identifies its missing matching
conditions: its energies have not been equated with the actual
step-only Rcut,Dprefix, and its remaining original array is absent.

## 4. Coupling to the actual quadratic column

For any choice (k,theta) satisfying (7), define

    rho=-F(k,theta)>=0,
    Lk=k*mu/(1+a^2*k*mu)>0,
    Zk=z-(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta/2.

The three matrix-energy terms in (8) dominate sigma*m, where

    sigma=u^2*Lk*rho/(rho+Lk*Zk^2), if rho+Lk*Zk^2>0,
    sigma=u^2*Lk,                   if rho=Zk=0.                    (14)

For the proof let X=beta*J+Btheta*B, Y=Atheta. Then
a*X+Y=u*E+Zk*B. Completing the square in X gives

    ||X||_M^2+k*mu*||Y||_M^2
                        >=Lk*||u*E+Zk*B||_M^2.

If rho+Lk*Zk^2>0, complete the square in B after adding rho||B||_M^2.
The remaining E coefficient is exactly (14). If rho=Zk=0, the
previous display is Lk*u^2*m directly. This covers singular Gram
matrices; no inverse of their entries is used. In particular sigma=0
at the strictly capped kstar branch, but sigma>0 for every k>kstar
with theta=theta_opt(k). On the free kstar branch sigma>0 already.

Combining (8) with (14) leaves the common ORIGINAL coefficient budget

    k*Rcut-Dprefix >= sigma*m+cB*(Lambda30+Lambda40)
                                            +beta*u*Lambda20.       (15)

Assume sigma>0 and define

    xi_cap=min(u/a^2, cB/(a^2*W0)).                                 (16)

If W0=0, omit the second argument of this minimum; its corresponding
incoming coefficients in (6) are both zero. This convention is used
only when that denominator is zero. The derivation itself is the
division-free condition xi*a^2*W0<=cB.

For any real xi satisfying xi<=xi_cap and xi<sigma/u, put

    Zeta=xi^2/(sigma-xi*u)>=0.

The following is a further necessary inequality of the FULL original
cone:

    k*Rcut-Dprefix >= xi*u*delta-Zeta*Q.                             (17)

To check it, subtract xi*u*delta using (6). In (15), the remaining
incoming Lambda20 coefficient is beta*u-xi*a^2*beta>=0. The two
B0 coefficients are at least cB-xi*a^2*W0>=0 if xi>=0; if xi<0
they only increase. The remaining matrix terms after adding Zeta*Q
are

    (sigma-xi*u)*||E||_M^2+2*xi<E,p>_M+Zeta*||p||_M^2
         = ||sqrt(sigma-xi*u)*E
                          +xi*p/sqrt(sigma-xi*u)||_M^2 >=0.

This proof couples the energies to the ACTUAL p in the ACTUAL M.
It is a sufficient full-space separator, not an assumption that
independently selected scalar energies possess a PSD completion.
Negative xi are intentionally allowed. They expose the opposite
first-step regime and the quadratic zero boundary.

For clarity the supremum of the right side of (17) is explicit.
Write Qplus=Q+u^2*delta. If Qplus<0, letting xi tend to -infinity
in (17) is a contradiction. Thus Qplus>=0 is necessary, in addition
to Q>=0. The exact factorization is

    Qplus=a^2*(A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2).

Thus this particular feasibility prerequisite recovers the existing
scalar-return condition Cbc|v-1|<=A; it is not counted as a new
independent obstruction. Suppose Q,Qplus>=0 and xi_cap>0.

If Q>0 and Qplus>0, set

    xi_free=(sigma/u)*(1-sqrt(Q/Qplus)).

When xi_free<=xi_cap the optimized bound is

    Bcal=(sigma/u^2)*(sqrt(Qplus)-sqrt(Q))^2.                         (18)

Otherwise xi_cap<sigma/u and the bound is

    Bcal=xi_cap*u*delta-xi_cap^2*Q/(sigma-xi_cap*u).                 (19)

If Q>0,Qplus=0, the supremum is sigma*Q/u^2, obtained as
xi tends to -infinity. If Q=0, Qplus>=0 means delta>=0, and the
supremum is

    Bcal=u*delta*min(xi_cap,sigma/u).                                (20)

For delta=Q=0 this is zero. These are limits of necessary inequalities
for every finite xi, so nonattainment of a supremum causes no problem.

The optimization follows by putting y=sigma-xi*u>0 in (17):

 xi*u*delta-xi^2*Q/(sigma-xi*u)
   =sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2
         -(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The unconstrained maximum is (18), at
y=sigma*sqrt(Q/Qplus); clipping xi above by xi_cap gives (19).
The displayed boundary formulas follow from the same expression.
The function is increasing up to its unconstrained maximum, so the
clipped value is nonnegative. In the present ell>0 domain cB>0 for
the optimizing choices used above: if v=0 then bc<1, and if v>0
the choice theta_opt>0. Hence xi_cap>0 there. Other allowed parameter
choices with cB=0 are covered by (17) without the positive-cap claim.

For every such choice with sigma>0, the final explicit test is

    Q>=0, Qplus>=0, k*Rcut-Dprefix>=Bcal.                            (21)

When v>0, Dprefix>0 and kstar<k<kold, it gives the positive-gap bound

    Gap >= (K/k-ell)*Dprefix+(K/k)*Bcal.                             (22)

The second term is strictly positive when delta!=0, provided the
displayed feasibility conditions hold. At delta=0 it is zero; no
uniform margin is inferred across that boundary.

## 1. Original full interface and common identities

Let

    h=(1+a,1+b,1+c,v),  a,b,c>0, v>=0, bc<=1,
    u=1+a, beta=1+b, w=1+c,
    A=2+a, N=3+a+b, Hpre=2+a+b, H0pre=1+a+b,
    s=sum h, C=1+s=4+a+b+c+v,
    t=c/(1+v), mu=1+t,
    ell=a^2*b*(1-b*t), z=a*b*v*t,
    R=ell*N^2+mu-C^2*a^2*b*beta*t^2,
    D=N^2*b^2-A^2.

Let e_i be the five original standard columns, indexed0 through4,
e=sum e_i, and P_i=sum_(j<i)h_j. Define

    T_ii=1, T_ij=h_j for j<i, T_ij=0 for j>i,
    omega=(-2h0,-2h1,-2h2,-2h3,2s)^T,
    Dmat=diag(h0(2-h0),h1(2-h1),h2(2-h2),h3(2-h3),-s(s+2)),
    L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda, M=Dmat+(LT+T^T L^T)/2.

The hypotheses are ALL twenty signs Lambda_ij>=0 for i!=j, zero
diagonal, L^T e=omega, and M>=0 on ALL of R^5. There is no support,
rank, symmetry, reversal, or duplicated-gradient restriction.

The accepted identity is

    V_h+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=sum_(i,j)M_ij<g_i,g_j>,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                                 -s(s+1)||g4||^2, (1)

on formal data with x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i. Formal substitutions below
are used as polynomial identities; no unproved interpolation is assumed.

Te=e+P and the flow give e^TMe=0. Indeed e^TDmat e=-s^2-sum h_i^2
and omega^T(e+P)=s^2+sum h_i^2. Applying PSD to e+r*y for both
signs of the real number r gives Me=0. The same argument proves

    |<x,y>_M|^2<=||x||_M^2*||y||_M^2,
    ||x||_M^2=0 implies Mx=0,                           (2)

where <x,y>_M=x^TMy and ||x||_M^2=x^TMx. Under the flow, the
individual kernel equations are

    sum_j Lambda_ij(P_j-P_i)=2h_i(1+P_i), i<4,
    sum_(j<4)Lambda_4j(s-P_j)=2sC.                       (3)

These follow by expanding 2Me=2Dmat e+L(e+P)+T^T omega.

Put

    E=e0, J=e0+e1, B=e3+e4,
    m=||E||_M^2, S=||J||_M^2, Tcut=||B||_M^2, rJB=<J,B>_M,
    B0=Lambda30+Lambda40, B1=Lambda31+Lambda41,
    Avec=u*E-a*beta*J-a*b*mu*B,
    c03old=u*mu*z, c23old=a^2*b*beta*mu*v*t.

The three exact identities needed here are

    R=ell*mu^2*Tcut+mu*||Avec||_M^2
         +ell*mu*(Hpre*B0+beta*B1)+c03old*Lambda03+c23old*Lambda23, (4)

    D=beta*((b*w*H0pre-u)*B0+b^2*w*B1-2*b*w*rJB-beta*S
                     -u*Lambda20-b*v*c*(Lambda04+Lambda14)),       (5)

    2<E,B>_M=a*B0-Lambda03-(1+v)*Lambda04.                         (6)

To prove (4), use saturated values f_i=x_i*g_i-g_i^2/2 on

    x_base=(N,2+b,1,-c,-t), g_base=(1,1,1,-t,-t),
    x_aux =(1,-a,ab,-abc,-abt), g_aux=(1,-a,ab,-abt,-abt).

For these values Q_ij=(g_i-g_j)(x_j-g_j). In ell times the base
plus mu times the auxiliary, the complete nonzero residual list is

    Q30=Q40=-ell*mu*Hpre, Q31=Q41=-ell*mu*beta,
    Q03=-c03old, Q23=-c23old.

Every other ordered residual is zero. In particular Q13 cancels
because ell=a^2*b*(1-bt); at Q03 use ell+ab(1+abt)=ab*u, and
at Q23 use ell+a^2*b^2*mu=a^2*b*beta. Telescoping (1) gives
R; the two gradient columns modulo e are -mu*B and Avec, proving (4).

For (5), start the scalar two-step cut at x0=A with gradients
(1,1,-b), then extend FORMALLY with constant gradient -b and affine
values through the last two steps. Its energy is -D and its column
modulo e is beta*J. Its negative residuals are
Q20=Q30=Q40=-u*beta, and its positive residuals are
Q03=Q13=w*b*beta, Q04=Q14=(w+v)*b*beta. All others vanish.
Thus (1) gives

 D=b*beta*(w*(Lambda03+Lambda13)+(w+v)*(Lambda04+Lambda14))
                        -beta^2*S-u*beta*(Lambda20+B0).

Besides (6), direct multiplication of T gives

    2<e1,B>_M=beta*B0+b*B1-Lambda13-(1+v)*Lambda14.

Adding these rows, and using (w+v)-w(1+v)=-vc, gives (5).

The additional ORIGINAL row used in this derivation is

    2<E,J+B>_M=-a*Lambda20+Lambda02+w*Lambda03+w*Lambda04.           (7)

In fact e2=e-J-B and
2M02=a*Lambda20-Lambda02-w*(Lambda03+Lambda04). This proves (7)
without any PSD quotient or new support assumption.


### Definition needed for the original positive root

For k>0 and real theta, set

    F(k,theta)=b^2*w^2-z*theta
          +(a^2+1/(k*mu))*theta^2/4-k*ell*mu^2.

This definition and the original row identities just proved suffice for
the following derivation. No capped optimizer or eps=0 matching is used.

## 3. The unrestricted root and the new full-row remainder

Assume v>0 for now. Then ell>0, z>0 and 1-bt>0. Set

    k0=b^2*w/(ell*mu), kold=b^2*w^2/(ell*mu^2).

The minimum of F(k,theta) over all real theta is attained at

    theta(k)=2*z*k*mu/(1+a^2*k*mu).

It is strictly decreasing as a function of k: at each fixed theta,
partial F/partial k=-ell*mu^2-theta^2/(4*k^2*mu)<0, and the minimum
is attained continuously. At k0 the minimum divided by mu^2 is
b^2*(gamma-1)*(gamma+a^2*k0*mu)/(1+a^2*k0*mu)>0,
where gamma=w/mu>1. At kold it is negative, since F(kold,0)=0 and
the negative linear term improves it for small positive theta.
There is therefore a unique root k in (k0,kold).

Here is an explicit definition requiring no root search. Define

    Hbar=(2*b*w-beta
          +sqrt((beta-2*b*w)^2+4*b*w^2*(1-b*t)/mu))/(2*(1-b*t)),
    k=Hbar/(a^2*mu), theta=2*z*k*mu/(1+Hbar),
    x=b*w-a*theta/2=b*(w+Hbar*mu)/(1+Hbar), rho=x/beta,
    hcoef=theta/(2*k*mu), jcoef=a^2*theta/2,
    rstar=u*theta/2.

The positive Hbar solves

    (1-bt)*Hbar^2+(beta-2*bw)*Hbar-b*w^2/mu=0,

which follows by substituting theta(k) into F=0. Also

    0<rho<1, hcoef+jcoef=z,
    a*x-a*b*mu=hcoef, k*ell*mu^2+theta^2/(4*k*mu)
                                            =2*b*w*x-x^2.         (8)

The inequalities use mu<w and bw<=beta, with strictness supplied
by Hbar>0. The identities follow by expansion and F=0.

Full original feasibility itself forces v<2. Indeed the terminal
diagonal is n=||e4||_M^2=sum_(j<4)Lambda4j-s(s+2)>=0.
Every weight in the last row of (3) is at least v. Hence

    v*n<=s*(2C-(C+1)*v), so v<=2C/(C+1)<2.                       (9)

We now work on 0<v<2; v>=2 was already excluded by this original row.
Define the nonnegative correction

    qcorr=max(0,((1+v)*rstar-beta*b*v*c)
                         /(w+(1+v)*(1-rho))),
    rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho),
    X=beta*J+x*B.

The EXACT original-array remainder is

    eps:=k*R-D
       =(1+Hbar)*||X||_M^2
         -2*(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)*<E,X>_M+k*mu*u^2*m
         +cB*B0+c1*B1+c20*Lambda20+qcorr*Lambda02
         +c03*Lambda03+c04*Lambda04+c14*Lambda14+c23*Lambda23,      (10)

where

    cB=k*ell*mu*Hpre-beta*(b*w*H0pre-u)+a*rshift,
    c1=beta*(k*ell*mu-b^2*w), c20=beta*u-a*qcorr,
    c03=k*c03old-rshift+w*qcorr,
    c04=beta*b*v*c-(1+v)*rshift+w*qcorr,
    c14=beta*b*v*c, c23=k*c23old.

To check the identity, first combine (4) and (5). Its Gram part is

 beta^2*||J||_M^2+2*beta*b*w*<J,B>_M+k*ell*mu^2*Tcut
                                                 +k*mu*||Avec||_M^2.

Subtract 2*rshift*<E,B>_M+2*qcorr*<E,J+B>_M from that Gram part.
Restore them using (6) and (7); this gives precisely all costs in
(10). Since rshift=rstar-qcorr*(1-rho), the subtraction differs
from 2*rstar*<E,B> by 2*qcorr*<E,X>/beta. F=0 and (8) turn the
uncorrected Gram into ||X||^2+k*mu*||uE-aX||^2. This proves (10).

Every displayed cost is nonnegative; cB,c1,c20,c03,c14,c23 are
STRICTLY positive. Here is the full sign and PSD check.

Let

    qmax=beta*u*(sqrt(k*mu*(1+Hbar))-a*k*mu).

Then

    0<=qcorr<qmax<beta*u/(2a).                                  (11)

If qcorr=0 this follows from Hbar>0. Otherwise put
tau=sqrt(Hbar/(1+Hbar)) in (0,1), Vprod=vbc, and
Sden=2+b+c+v. Direct substitution gives

    qcorr=(beta/a)*Vprod*(u*tau^2-a*beta)
                              /(Sden-Vprod+Vprod*tau^2),
    qmax=(beta*u/a)*tau/(1+tau).

The numerator of qcorr is positive in this case. The inequality
qcorr<qmax is equivalent to

    Vprod*(1+tau)*(u*tau-a*beta)<u*tau*Sden.

Its left side is smaller than 2*Vprod*u*tau. Moreover
2*Vprod<=2v<2+b+c+v=Sden, using bc<=1 and v<2. This proves the
strict inequality. The upper bound on qmax follows from
tau/(1+tau)<1/2.

Also rshift>0: when qcorr>0 its numerator is less than
(1+v)*rstar, while its denominator is strictly larger than
(1+v)*(1-rho). Thus qcorr<rstar/(1-rho).
At k=k0 the part of cB before a*rshift equals u*(1-bc)>=0;
it strictly increases with k. Hence cB>0. Since k>k0, c1>0.
Equation (11) gives c20>beta*u/2>0. Finally
rstar<k*u*mu*z=k*c03old and rshift<=rstar, proving c03>0.
The definition of qcorr gives c04>=0, and c14,c23>0.

Set

    alpha=(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)/(1+Hbar), Y=X-alpha*E,
    sigma=k*mu*u^2-(k*mu*u*a+qcorr/beta)^2/(1+Hbar)>0.

The positivity of sigma is exactly qcorr<qmax. Thus (10) is

    eps=sigma*m+(1+Hbar)*||Y||_M^2+the nonnegative costs in (10).  (12)

In particular every full original certificate obeys D<=kR. This
necessity argument uses the actual original rows. Its comparison with
the complete older conditions is supplied by Sections1--9 of the
present joint text, not by a claim about an auxiliary optimizer.

## 4. The actual quadratic column and joint first-row budget

Define

    pquad=(1,-a,ab,-abc,abc*(v-1))^T,
    Q=1-C^2*a^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2,
    delta=u^2-2, W0=1+bc*(v-1).

Tp=e and Le=0. Telescoping h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2 gives

    ||pquad||_M^2=Q>=0,
    2<E,pquad>_M=u*(m-delta)
             +a^2*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40).    (13)

For the row formula, let O0=sum_(j>0)Lambda0j and
I0=Lambda20+Lambda30+Lambda40. Then m=1-a^2-aO0 and node0 flow
gives Lambda10=O0+2u-I0. With Te0=u e-a e0 and
Mp=Dmat pquad+T^T L^T pquad/2 one obtains

 pquad^T L e0=uO0+2au-a*(beta*Lambda20+(1-bc)*Lambda30+W0*Lambda40),
 2<E,pquad>_M=2(1-a^2)-a*pquad^T L e0,

which gives (13). Both incoming weights 1-bc and W0 are nonnegative,
and 1-bc<=W0, including v<1.

By (12), eps>=sigma*m+c20*Lambda20+cB*B0. Define

    xi_cap=min(c20/(a^2*beta), cB/(a^2*W0)),

omitting the second term if W0=0. For every real xi with
xi<=xi_cap and xi<sigma/u,

    eps>=xi*u*delta-xi^2*Q/(sigma-xi*u).                         (14)

Subtract xi*u*delta using (13). All remaining multiplier coefficients
are nonnegative: for xi>=0 this is the definition of xi_cap and the
order of the incoming weights; for xi<0 the coefficients increase.
The remaining Gram expression after adding xi^2Q/(sigma-xi*u) is

    ||sqrt(sigma-xi*u)*E+xi*pquad/sqrt(sigma-xi*u)||_M^2>=0.

Thus this is the same ORIGINAL matrix and column, not independent
energy selections. Let Qplus=Q+u^2*delta. Sending xi to -infinity
shows Qplus>=0, and

    Qplus=a^2*(A^2-C^2*b^2*c^2*(v-1)^2).

That prerequisite is the old scalar-return condition and is not
counted as an independent improvement.

For completeness, when Q,Qplus>0 the free maximizing xi is
xi_free=(sigma/u)*(1-sqrt(Q/Qplus)). If xi_free<=xi_cap, (14)
has supremum

    Bcal=(sigma/u^2)*(sqrt(Qplus)-sqrt(Q))^2.

Otherwise its supremum is

    Bcal=xi_cap*u*delta-xi_cap^2*Q/(sigma-xi_cap*u).

The latter case automatically has xi_cap<sigma/u. For Q>0,Qplus=0,
the supremum is sigma*Q/u^2. For Q=0,Qplus>=0 it is
u*delta*min(xi_cap,sigma/u), and it is zero when Q=delta=0.
These statements follow on putting y=sigma-xi*u>0: the objective is

 sigma*delta+2*sigma*Q/u^2-(delta+Q/u^2)*y-Q*sigma^2/(u^2*y).

The earlier first-row budget is also retained, on its stated domain
0<a<1 and a*eta<1, where

    eta=b/(1+w+v), nu=(1+eta)*(1-a*eta)/a,
    Erow=a+3+1/a-(u*delta/a)*eta-C^2*eta^2.

Its exact identity is

 Erow=nu*(m+a*(Lambda20+B0))+(1+eta)^2*M11
                 +(1+eta)*eta*((w+v)*Lambda12+v*Lambda13).        (15)

Here is a direct derivation. For orthonormal physical vectors U,V set
gfirst=-eta*U+sqrt(nu)*V and use saturated values on

 Xphys=(U+u*gfirst,U,-b*U,-(1+v)*eta*U,-eta*U),
 Gphys=(gfirst,U,-eta*U,-eta*U,-eta*U).

The nonzero residuals are Q20=Q30=Q40=-a*nu,
Q12=-(1+eta)*(b-eta), and Q13=-(1+eta)*v*eta. Every other finite
residual is zero. Use ||gfirst||^2=[1+(1-a)*eta]/a and
<U,gfirst>+a||gfirst||^2=1-a*eta to check the target0 residuals.
The energy telescope gives Erow and the two gradient columns modulo
e are sqrt(nu)*E and (1+eta)*e1, proving (15).

In particular, for EVERY lambda>=0, (14) holds with its left side
eps+lambda*Erow, sigma replaced by sigma+lambda*nu, and cap replaced
by

 min((c20+lambda*nu*a)/(a^2*beta),

triangles take z>0; the boundary z=0 is legal by the same normal checks.

    X_1=G_1=(-1,z),

## 7. Full C82 value-and-parameter minimum for0<a<1,0<b<=1

    R=[1-a+sqrt((1+a)^2+4a ell)]/(2a),
    v_cross=[1+ell/(b+1)]/a,
    v_stationary=a/(1-a),
    v_best=min{v_cross,max{R,v_stationary}},
    K=C^2 eta^2.                                       (27)

Htri has its nonnegative zero at1/a and is increasing thereafter. For
the second, Htri(R)=ell implies(b+1)(aR-1)<=ell.

The exact infimum of(26) over EVERY legal triangle parameter is

    Enew=(1-a^2)v_best^2-2(1+a)a v_best+1+2(1+a)
                +[2(1+a)+1-b^2]ell-K.                 (28)

If ell=0 the same formula is attained by the displayed degenerate
legal data; alternatively it is the limit of nondegenerate triangles.

                              +(1-b^2)ell-K.           (30)

    Eold=((1+a)R-1)^2+(1-b^2)ell-K,                    (31)

Htri(R)=ell makes Dprice=0, and J_left(R)=Eold.

optimized C82 condition whenever

    R>=a/(1-a).                                        (32)

first-step projection range39/100<=a<=41/100 from d3abee1b17da52da,

    0<ell<(a^2+a-1)/(1-a)^2.                            (34)

domain. It does NOT prove that a word satisfying all the other current
necessary conditions is rejected by(28). In particular(34) alone is

## 4. A static conjugate construction and its exact minimum set

The following construction will attain(10) and carry complete histories.
For any integer k>=0, choose pairwise orthogonal vectors

    a_1,...,a_k in E-perpendicular, each of norm2,

and work in the actual space E+span{a_1,...,a_k}, of dimension k+2.
Set

    M_0=0, M_j=sum_(l=1)^j a_l for1<=j<=k,
    psi_k(w)=max{0,<nu,w>-1,2<e,w>-2,
                         <M_1,w>,...,<M_k,w>},
    H_k(w)=||w||^2/2+psi_k(w),
    F_k(x)=sup_w {<x,w>-H_k(w)}.                         (11)

When k=0 the list of M planes is empty. This F_0 need not equal the old
triangle projection function at unsampled points. The required invariant
is precisely ALL the old physical jets(1), not global equality to that
projection function. Each complete run below uses one static F_k.

The function H_k is finite and1-strongly convex, and H_k>=||w||^2/2.
Thus for every x its conjugate has a unique maximizing vector g(x).
The maximizing condition is x in the subdifferential of H_k at g(x).
Adding the two strong-subgradient inequalities at x,x' gives

    <x-x',g(x)-g(x')>>=||g(x)-g(x')||^2.

Hence g is1-Lipschitz. The two maximizing inequalities also give

    0<=F_k(x')-F_k(x)-<g(x),x'-x>
       <=<g(x')-g(x),x'-x><=||x'-x||^2.

Therefore F_k is finite, convex, differentiable and globally1-smooth,
with grad F_k=g. This repeats the elementary construction underlying
accepted1252b8823bb5a290 and checks its applicability to(11).

If an affine plane of psi_k with slope y is active at g, then y is a
subgradient of psi_k at g. At x=g+y the actual gradient is g and

    F_k(x)=<x,g>-||g||^2/2-psi_k(g).                     (12)

The same statement holds for any convex combination of active slopes.

The full minimum set and minimum value are exactly

    min F_k=0,
    argmin F_k=P_k:=conv{M_0,M_1,...,M_k}.                (13)

For x in P_k, <x,w><=max_j<M_j,w><=psi_k(w), so the supremum in(11)
is0, attained at w=0. Conversely take x outside P_k and let m_0 be its

projection inequality gives

    <d,M_j><=<d,m_0> for all j,
    <x,d>=<m_0,d>+||d||^2>max_j<M_j,d>.

For sufficiently small epsilon>0, the two affine planes with intercepts

      =epsilon[<x,d>-max_j<M_j,d>]-epsilon^2||d||^2/2>0

# C103: the whole nonradial orthogonal-endpoint family is dominated on the original ruler

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED DRAFT. Worker max3, allocation round1
under master_guidance78e668c9782fc528. Completed baseline33; this return
completes34 of ceiling35. Attempted ceiling36 includes the historical
interruption. No formal or computational allocation is used.

The original target remains the unrestricted all-nonnegative-word,
all-sufficiently-large-horizon lower bound W_n(h)>=(1-o(1))/B_n, with
W=2R in the project's normalization. It is OPEN. This document proves a
candidate obstruction only for the explicitly stated static family.
It is not a fact, and no new intermediate assertion is adopted as an
accepted premise. All new ingredients used together are proved here.

Accepted premises:1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original normalization
and directed interpolation residuals; b98bb807d514e80d supplies the
complete K_n and original benchmark recurrences;1fca3e5dd555cb4a supplies
the complete alternating-ray functional;dfde2fa326c908bf supplies the
Huber-augmented universal-lens reference. C102/bf331df9a833199c is an
unverified starting object, not a predecessor. C99/C100 are not used.

## 1. Exact family and new conclusion

Retain the ORIGINAL physical word and every query, writing

    h=(block_0,b,block_1,d,block_2),
    S_j=sum block_j, j=0,1,2, b>1, d>1.

Each block is a possibly empty list of nonnegative physical steps.
The following symbols are local abbreviations, not changes to B_n:

    T=1+S_0, M=1+S_1, N=1+S_2, sigma=2N-1,
    A=b-1, E=d-1,
    u>=0, v>0, ell>0, alpha>=0, beta>=0, kappa>=0,
    delta=A-Mu-alpha, C=Eu-alpha, Z=Ev-beta-Nell.

In the real plane with its usual orthonormal basis e_1,e_2 put

    p=e_1, q=-u e_1-v e_2, r=ell e_2,
    J(y)=max{0,<p,y>,<q,y>-kappa,<r,y>},
    F(x)=min_y {J(y)+||x-y||^2/2},
    X_0=(T+delta)e_1-(Mv+beta)e_2.                  (1)

The declared family consists of ALL these parameters satisfying

    delta>=0,
    v(Mv+beta)<=(1+u)delta+kappa,
    kappa<=u alpha+v beta,
    ell Z>=max{0,C,-u C-v Z-kappa}.                 (2)

These are exactly the conditions for gradient p on block_0 and its
checkpoint, q on block_1 and its checkpoint, and r on block_2 including
the actual terminal query, for the single static function (1).
Independent alpha,beta include the complete C102 nonradial interface.

The true closest minimizer, squared distance, and payoff are

    x_star=(0,-min{Mv+beta,kappa/v}),
    R_nr^2=(T+delta)^2+(Mv+beta-kappa/v)_+^2,
    V_nr=2F(X_n)/R_nr^2
        =[2ell(Ev-beta)-sigma ell^2]/R_nr^2.        (3)

Here t_+=max(t,0); the symbol R_nr is a distance and is unrelated to the
project's convention W=2R. Multiplying F by any L>0 preserves (3) under
the original steps h_i/L.

The new general word-conditioned bound is: if

    T>=sqrt(2) A,                                  (4)

then EVERY member of (1)--(2) satisfies

    V_nr <= max{ E^2/[sigma(T+A+M)^2],
                 (AE/(TM))^2/sigma }.             (5)

The first term is the accepted single-cut witness at the SECOND actual
checkpoint. The second term retains the actual first, middle and tail
block masses. No parameter optimum is left undecided in the comparison.
An intermediate scalar relaxation below is not asserted to be attained
by a legal homogeneous instance.

For the ORIGINAL enclosing-m ruler use, throughout every child word,

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta_m=1-1/m,
    c_m=lambda(1+1/m), a_m=beta_m/c_m,
    H_0=(), H_(k+1)=(H_k,1+a_m c_m^k,H_k),
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, M_k=1+sum H_k.

The local beta in (1) is NOT beta_m. For every m>=128, every pair of
actual checkpoint indices satisfies (4), and

    sup_(all parameters (2), all pairs on H_m) V_nr
       <= gamma103/(2M_m-1)
        = gamma103 K_n(H_m)
        = gamma103 F_ray_n(H_m),
    gamma103=5949/6088<1,                           (6)

    limsup_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup V_nr
       <=2gamma103/exp(1)<1.                       (7)

Thus even the ENTIRE independent nonradial-middle family is weaker than
the complete same-word Huber/ray reference. The Huber-augmented complete
applicable lens reference also dominates it. This is not an upper bound
on unrestricted W_n(H_m). A distinct endpoint-angle construction is
given in Section12; its profile comparison is not claimed solved.

## 2. The one static function, actual minimum and radius

J is a finite continuous convex nonnegative maximum of affine functions.
For fixed x its defining proximal objective is coercive and strictly
convex, so it has a unique minimizer y(x). Its optimality condition is

    g(x):=x-y(x) in partial J(y(x)).                (8)

For completeness, a minimizer compared to y+t(z-y), convexity of J,
and division by t>0 followed by t down to0 give the subgradient
inequality J(z)>=J(y)+<x-y,z-y>. Conversely that inequality and the
quadratic expansion imply that the objective at z exceeds its value
at y by at least ||z-y||^2/2, proving (8).

Add the two subgradient inequalities at x,x'. With g=g(x),g'=g(x'),
one obtains <g-g',y-y'>>=0 and hence

    ||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>.

Thus g is1-Lipschitz. Evaluating the proximal objective for x' at y
gives the upper bound in

    0<=F(x')-F(x)-<g,x'-x><=||x'-x||^2/2.

For the lower bound, apply the subgradient inequality at y to y' and
expand the two quadratic terms; the remainder is ||g'-g||^2/2.
These inequalities prove differentiability with gradient g and convexity
by the supporting affine function at each x. Therefore F is everywhere
defined, convex and1-smooth.

Its minimum is0 and its minimizer set is exactly

    K={x_1<=0,x_2<=0,-u x_1-v x_2<=kappa}.         (9)

Indeed J is zero precisely there, and F(x)=0 forces both nonnegative
summands at the attained minimum to vanish. For u>0, K is the triangle
with vertices(0,0),(-kappa/u,0),(0,-kappa/v), allowing degeneracy.
For u=0 it is the strip x_1<=0,-kappa/v<=x_2<=0.

Every point of K has x_1<=0 and -kappa/v<=x_2<=0. The stated x_star
lies in K and separately minimizes the two coordinate-square distances
from X_0, whose first coordinate is positive and second is negative.
It is therefore the true unique closest minimizer. This proves both
positive-part branches in (3); no old uncentered norm is substituted.

## 3. All physical gradients and all original directed rows

Give the four slopes p,q,r,0 the affine costs0,kappa,0,0. If slope g_i
is active at y_i=x_i-g_i, then (8) gives its actual gradient and

    f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2-k_i.

For every ordered pair of such samples the residual from accepted
1252b8823bb5a290 expands to

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<g_i-g_j,y_j>-k_i+k_j<=0.                 (10)

The last inequality is exactly activity of j's plane against i's at
y_j. It proves BOTH orientations of every remote row, not merely
adjacent or checkpoint rows. Include the optimum sample with position
x_star and g_star=f_star=k_star=0, so y_star=x_star: the zero plane is
active there and the same argument proves both optimum rows.

At a physical prefix cumulative mass t in[0,S_0], the point and its
proposed proximal point are

    x=(T+delta-t,-Mv-beta),
    y=(delta+S_0-t,-Mv-beta).

At the last prefix query p's plane dominates zero and q's plane exactly
by the first two inequalities in (2); r's plane is negative. Earlier
queries add a nonnegative multiple of p, improving all comparisons
since p's directional slope1 exceeds the others0,-u,0.

The first checkpoint sends the point to(-Mu-alpha,-Mv-beta). At middle
cumulative mass t in[0,S_1],

    x=(-(M-t)u-alpha,-(M-t)v-beta),
    y=(-alpha-(S_1-t)u,-beta-(S_1-t)v).

At t=S_1 the q-plane height is u alpha+v beta-kappa>=0, while p,r
have heights-alpha,-ell beta. Earlier queries add a nonnegative multiple
of q; its directional slope u^2+v^2 exceeds0,-u,-ell v. Thus every

The second checkpoint sends the point to(C,Ev-beta). At tail cumulative

At the actual terminal query t=S_2, (2) compares r's plane against all
three competitors. Earlier tail queries add a nonnegative multiple of

trajectory and (10), including large ordinary steps and zero steps.

Necessity also holds: p,q,r are exposed vertices of the slope hull,
exposed respectively by e_1,-e_2,e_2. A subgradient of a finite affine
maximum is a convex combination of its active slopes: if it were not,
a separating direction would contradict the directional derivative,
which is the largest active directional slope. Thus an exposed slope
as the actual gradient in (8) requires its own plane to be active.
The three ending-query comparisons give precisely (2).

At the terminal query the active-plane value formula gives
f_n=ell(Ev-beta)-(S_2+1/2)ell^2, proving (3). It is positive because
Z>=0 implies Ev-beta>=Nell and hence its numerator is at least ell^2.

## 4. Affine reserve, optimum slack, and paid continuation

The three ending-query affine reserves f_i-||g_i||^2/2 are

    delta, u alpha+v beta-kappa, ell Z.             (11)

They are not the optimum slacks. Put t_star=min(Mv+beta,kappa/v).
For any sample of slope g_i and affine cost k_i the actual optimum
slack is

    <g_i,x_i-x_star>-f_i-||g_i||^2/2
        =k_i-<g_i,x_star>.

It is respectively0, kappa-v t_star, ell t_star for p,q,r. All are
nonnegative, but positive affine reserve does not mean positive optimum

For any appended list of nonnegative physical steps of total mass tau,
the SAME function keeps gradient r at every appended query exactly when

    0<=tau<=Tcarry,
    Tcarry=min{ Z/ell,
                (ell Z-C)/ell^2,
                [(ell+v)Z+u C+kappa]/[ell(ell+v)] }. (12)

All three numbers are nonnegative by (2). The proposed terminal proximal
point becomes(C,Z-tau ell). Its comparisons with zero, the old p-plane,
and the old q-plane give the three bounds separately. Each comparison

Exposedness of r proves necessity. Throughout this legal holding range,

    V_nr(tau)=V_nr(0)-2tau ell^2/R_nr^2.            (13)

The minimizer set and initial distance do not change. No unchanged
gradient is claimed after (12), and a changed-gradient continuation
requires new analysis of the actual function.

## 5. Exact elimination of beta and unsaturated middle intercept

For every member of (1)--(2) change ONLY

    beta'=0, kappa'=u alpha,                       (14)

keeping the same physical word, partition and u,v,ell,alpha. This is a
comparison of complete static instances; the function is not replaced
mid-trajectory. The first two constraints in (2) imply

    Mv^2<=(1+u)delta+u alpha.                      (15)

This is exactly the new first activity condition; the new middle
reserve is0. At the final proximal point Z'=Z+beta, C is unchanged.
The new r-plane height rises by ell beta. The new q-plane height is

    -u C-v Z'-u alpha=-E(u^2+v^2)+Nv ell.

The old q-plane height minus this value is u alpha+v beta-kappa>=0.
Thus all three final comparisons remain valid. This proves legality of
(14) using every physical query, not a formal relaxation.

The original radius is at least the new radius because

    Mv+beta-kappa/v>=Mv-u alpha/v.

The new terminal numerator is the old positive numerator plus2ell beta.
Therefore (14) weakly increases the true-distance payoff. For an upper
bound on the whole family it suffices to consider beta=0,kappa=u alpha:

    delta=A-Mu-alpha>=0,
    Mv^2<=(1+u)(A-Mu)-alpha,
    R_0^2=(T+delta)^2+(Mv-u alpha/v)_+^2.           (16)

Its final constraints still apply, but completing the square gives the
valid upper bound

    V_nr<= E^2 v^2/(sigma R_0^2).                 (17)

The omitted final inequalities in (17) make it an upper relaxation,
never an asserted attainable objective. This distinction is essential
in the next reduction.

## 6. The nonradial scalar comparison, including both radius branches

We prove, under (4), for EVERY parameter in (16),

    v^2/R_0^2<=max{A^2/(M^2T^2),1/(T+A+M)^2}.    (18)

If M<=A, dropping alpha from (16) gives

    v^2<=(1+u)(A-Mu)/M<=(A+M)^2/(4M^2)
        <=A^2/M^2.

The middle inequality follows by completing the square in u; its
vertex (A-M)/(2M) lies in[0,A/M]. Since R_0>=T, this proves the first
alternative in (18), without any assumption on T in this regime.

Now let M>=A. Put

    P=A-Mu, k=1+u, c=uP, d=delta=P-alpha,
    0<=d<=P, x=v^2, H=T+d, c_0=u alpha/M.

For fixed u,alpha, the ratio in (18) is

    x/[H^2+M^2(x-c_0)_+^2/x].                     (19)

On x<=c_0 it is x/H^2 and increases. On x>=c_0 it is

    x^2/[M^2x^2+(H^2-2M^2c_0)x+M^2c_0^2].

The derivative has the sign of
x[(H^2-2M^2c_0)x+2M^2c_0^2]. This is nonnegative since

    2M^2c_0=2M u alpha<=2M u(A-Mu)<=A^2/2<=T^2.

The two formulas agree at their boundary. Consequently (19) is largest

    x=(d+c)/M.

At that endpoint Mx-u alpha=(1+u)d>=0, so the resulting ratio is

    F_u(d)=(d+c)^2 /
            [M(d+c)(T+d)^2+M^2d^2 k^2].           (20)

    S(0)=cT(T-2c)>=0,

because c=u(A-Mu)<=A^2/(4M)<=A/4 and T>=sqrt(2)A. At d=P,

    S(P)=P(1+u) D(u),
    D(u)=(T+P)^2-2P(1+u)(T+A)
        =M[M+2(T+A)]u^2-2A(T+A)u+T^2-A^2.

    D(u)>=T^2-A^2-A^2(T+A)^2/[M(M+2(T+A))]

          =2(T+A)(T^2-2A^2)/(2T+3A)>=0.           (22)

Therefore S(d)>=0 and (20) increases. The possible endpoint c=d=0
is interpreted by its limit0; x>0 excludes it from the actual family.

legitimate on the actual family, with continuity at relaxed boundaries.

It follows that (20) is at most its value at d=P, which is the scalar
expression obtained by setting alpha=0 and saturating (15). This is
ONLY a comparison of upper relaxations: it need not retain the final
gradient's activity condition and is not a homogeneous conversion law.

Writing t=P and C_0=M+A, that expression is

    Psi(t)=t(C_0-t)/[M^2(T^2+(2T+C_0)t)], 0<=t<=A.

Its derivative has the sign of
C_0 T^2-2T^2t-(2T+C_0)t^2, with positive zero

C_0^2/[M^2(2T+C_0)^2]<=A^2/(M^2T^2). If A<=t_0 the maximum is

For the last inequality, the positive-denominator difference equals

This proves (18), and (17) proves (5).

This is the new part of the joint proof. Independent alpha does buy true

## 7. Original ruler mass and every checkpoint pair

Fix the actual enclosing m>=128, abbreviate a=a_m,c_r=c_m,rho=c_r-2,
and write a_k=a c_r^k for a level-k excess. The exact mass recurrence is

    M_0=1, M_(k+1)=2M_k+a c_r^k,

## 8. Complete same-word K, ray and lens comparisons

## 12. An actual acute endpoint-angle law outside the closed family

    zeta=E/2, B=E/2, D=M+zeta,

positive first and second coordinates, so p and r form an ACUTE angle.

    y=([1-(1+t)/(4N)]C,[1-(1+t)/(2N)]V),

u<=Bv^2/(8N) gives V^2>=8NC and therefore

rate of decrease are respectively

    [3C^2+4V^2-12NC]/(16N),

## 2. The one static function, actual minimum and radius

J is a finite continuous convex nonnegative maximum of affine functions.
For fixed x its defining proximal objective is coercive and strictly
convex, so it has a unique minimizer y(x). Its optimality condition is

    g(x):=x-y(x) in partial J(y(x)).                (8)

For completeness, a minimizer compared to y+t(z-y), convexity of J,
and division by t>0 followed by t down to0 give the subgradient
inequality J(z)>=J(y)+<x-y,z-y>. Conversely that inequality and the
quadratic expansion imply that the objective at z exceeds its value
at y by at least ||z-y||^2/2, proving (8).

Add the two subgradient inequalities at x,x'. With g=g(x),g'=g(x'),
one obtains <g-g',y-y'>>=0 and hence

    ||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>.

Thus g is1-Lipschitz. Evaluating the proximal objective for x' at y
gives the upper bound in

    0<=F(x')-F(x)-<g,x'-x><=||x'-x||^2/2.

For the lower bound, apply the subgradient inequality at y to y' and
expand the two quadratic terms; the remainder is ||g'-g||^2/2.
These inequalities prove differentiability with gradient g and convexity
by the supporting affine function at each x. Therefore F is everywhere
defined, convex and1-smooth.

Its minimum is0 and its minimizer set is exactly

    K={x_1<=0,x_2<=0,-u x_1-v x_2<=kappa}.         (9)

       =T^2-A^2+(A-Mu)^2>=0.

at the allowed endpoint x=(d+c)/M. There

       { M[(T+d)^2+M(1+u)^2d^2/(d+c)] }, 0<=d<=P.     (18)

evidence:
# Joint covariance on the original ruler word: exact identity and local obstruction

Status: UNVERIFIED, single joint research draft, max2 round34. No formal
submission, numerical evaluation, solver, machine algebra, replay, consult,
installation, or subagent was used. The assignment is governed by
a23831f2a36b3c4a, with the unchanged max2 allocation confirmed by
48a4276698805f28. This round does not renew itself.

Verdict: the proposed full-covariance mechanism is BLOCKED as a proof of the
whole actual residual kernel. The covariance identity below is exact, but
does not prove its signed domination. There is new uniform negative evidence
against two precise closure rules: declaring every complete child block
nonnegative, and repairing all such blocks with a uniformly bounded number
of linear boundary features. Neither is a counterexample to the complete
original-word kernel. The formal negative directions are explicitly illegal
for the original interpolation array.

The complete block covariance, constant column, signed killing terms, and
final deleted-step correction are retained. The full exact modal state has
m+1 coordinates; the initial position adds one coordinate. A quantitative
boundary payment is proved in Section7. Its availability from the rest of
the original trajectory is NOT proved.

Only accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 is used, for the precise interpolation
necessity/sufficiency and normalization stated below. All other mathematical
ingredients needed here are derived in this one joint draft. In particular
7bc886cf037bdcd4, ff8f8f21b222a81b, and the later load draft
f3d7ccaf615115b7 are research history, not correctness premises.

## 1. Physical word, full shared state, and elementary bounds

Fix an integer m>=128 and set

 epsilon=1/m, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+epsilon),
 a=(1-epsilon)/c, d_j=1+a*c^j,
 H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j).

Let q=2^m-2. The actual queried word h=(h_0,...,h_(q-1)) is H_m with
its LAST d_0 deleted. The separate final unqueried step is b in [0,2].
Write s_i=sum_(r<i)h_r and S=s_q. An embedded H_K always uses these
same parameters epsilon,c,a, rather than replacing epsilon by1/K.

For arbitrary vectors v,w_0,...,w_(m-1) in ONE real Euclidean space,

 p_ij=product_(r<i)(1-h_r/d_j),
 g_i=v+sum_(j<m)p_ij*w_j,
 x_i=x_0-sum_(r<i)h_r*g_r.

There is no diagonal or independence assumption on their common Gram.
For actual data one common value array f_i and the zero optimum sample
are required; f is normalized to have smoothness1 and minimum0.
In the convention of accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290,

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.       (1)

Every ordered original pair remains a legality requirement. The auxiliary
probability space introduced later changes no function values or geometry.

The first d_j occurs at step2^j-1. Every earlier step is less than d_j,
so p_ij>0 until that step, and p_ij=0 from query2^j onwards. Consequently
g_q=v, and telescoping p_ij-p_(i+1),j=(h_i/d_j)p_ij gives

 sum_(i<q)h_i*p_ij=d_j,
 x_q=x_0-S*v-sum_(j<m)d_j*w_j.                       (2)

We will need only the following elementary parameter bounds. Since
12/5<lambda<29/12,

 12/5<c<39/16,  a>127/312>2/5.

Also c(c-2)>1, hence 0<A_mass:=a/(c-2)<1. Solving the word-sum
recursion S_K:=sum H_K, S_(K+1)=2S_K+d_K, gives

 S_K+1=A_mass*c^K+(1-A_mass)*2^K.

For K>=1 this implies

 S_K<c^K,  S_K/d_K<1/a<5/2.                          (3)

The level ratio satisfies

 d_(k+1)>2d_k for k>=2.                              (4)

Indeed d_(k+1)-2d_k=(c-2)a*c^k-1. At k=2 the quantity before
subtracting1 is (1-epsilon)c(c-2). Since
c(c-2)=1+2lambda(lambda-1)epsilon+lambda^2*epsilon^2
>1+6epsilon, its product with1-epsilon exceeds1+5epsilon-6epsilon^2>1.
It increases with k, proving (4).

The first four levels, retaining the same enclosing epsilon, obey

 d_0=sqrt(2)-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]<sqrt(2),
 d_1=2-epsilon<2,
 d_2=2+sqrt(2)-lambda*epsilon^2<2+sqrt(2),
 d_3=1+lambda^2*(1+epsilon-epsilon^2-epsilon^3)>4+2sqrt(2).
                                                               (5)

The last inequality uses1-epsilon-epsilon^2>0. These are strict for
every finite m>=128.

## 2. Original-Q identity and the actual unmatched sufficient claim

For ANY nonempty word W=(h_0,...,h_(N-1)) with local clocks s_i and total S_W,
define, on its complete temporal vector sequence,

 J_W(g)=sum_(i<N)[
   2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
   +s_(i+1)||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].      (6)

For the actual queried word, direct expansion and summation by parts give

 ||x_0||^2-2S*f_q+2sum_(i<q)h_i Q_(i,star)
       +2sum_(i<q)s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)=||x_q||^2+J_h(g).  (7)

Here is the full cancellation. GD gives

 2sum h_i Q_(i,star)
 =2sum h_i f_i-||x_0||^2+||x_q||^2
                          +sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2.

Also Q_(i+1,i)=f_(i+1)-f_i+h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
+||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2/2, and
sum s_(i+1)(f_(i+1)-f_i)=S f_q-sum h_i f_i.
Adding proves (7). All displayed multipliers are nonnegative.

Thus the specific sufficient claim is

 J_h(v,w_0,...,w_(m-1))>=0 for ALL common real vectors, ALL m>=128.
                                                               (8)

If (8) were proved, (7) and the original Q inequalities would imply
2f_q<=||x_0||^2/S. Smooth descent at the last step gives
2f(x_q-bv)<=2f_q-b(2-b)||v||^2<=2f_q. Hence, after true-distance
normalization ||x_0||=1, the entire stated temporal quotient would obey
2f(x_q-bv)<=1/S. This is a conditional quotient bound only. Arbitrary
nonnegative schedules and arbitrary temporal gradients are outside it.

The position square in (7) is exactly (2). Since x_0 is a free formal
vector, including that square does not conceal an extra positivity
assumption: the full quadratic in (x_0,v,w) is PSD iff (8) holds.

## 3. Full conditional-covariance identity, with all coefficients

For a word W as in (6), put Delta_i=g_i-g_(i+1) and

 beta_(-1)=0,
 beta_i=s_(i+1)*(s_i+1), 0<=i<N,
 beta_N=S_W*(S_W+1),
 nu_i=beta_i-beta_(i-1), 0<=i<=N,
 c_i=(h_i-1)*s_(i+1), 0<=i<N.

For the positive ruler steps all nu_i are positive and c_i>=0. More
explicitly nu_0=h_0, nu_N=S_W*h_(N-1), and at an interior query
nu_i=s_i*(h_(i-1)+h_i)+h_i. Expanding adjacent squares proves

 J_W=sum_(i=0)^N nu_i||g_i||^2-sum_(i<N)c_i||Delta_i||^2.
                                                               (9)

For example its diagonal at an interior query is

 kappa_i=2s_i+2h_i-h_i^2,

and its off-diagonal between i and i+1 is
s_(i+1)(h_i-1). The initial diagonal is h_0(2-h_0), and the final
diagonal is S_W. These determine every entry of the temporal tridiagonal
matrix in (6), so (9) also verifies the endpoints.

Let the modal index set be A={infinity,0,...,m-1}, and set
z_infinity=0, z_j=1/d_j. For a prefix polynomial
P_i(z)=product_(r<i)(1-h_r*z), define the row

 r_i=(P_i(z_alpha))_(alpha in A).

Thus r_i,infinity=1, and g_i=sum_alpha r_i,alpha*Z_alpha with
Z_infinity=v and Z_j=w_j. For any nonempty set I of query indices put

 omega_I=sum_(i in I)nu_i,
 ell_I=omega_I^(-1)sum_(i in I)nu_i*r_i,
 Sigma_I=omega_I^(-1)sum_(i in I)nu_i
                   (r_i-ell_I)^T(r_i-ell_I).

These are the complete mean row and covariance matrix of r_i under the
probabilities nu_i/omega_I, not a covariance of independent modal states.
For a disjoint partition I=L union R define
sigma_I=omega_L*omega_R/omega_I. Direct expansion gives

 omega_I*Sigma_I=omega_L*Sigma_L+omega_R*Sigma_R
                +sigma_I*(ell_L-ell_R)^T(ell_L-ell_R). (10)

Indeed each centered row in L is (r_i-ell_L)+(ell_L-ell_I), and the
first cross term sums to zero; the analogous R calculation leaves
omega_L*(ell_L-ell_I)^T(ell_L-ell_I)
+omega_R*(ell_R-ell_I)^T(ell_R-ell_I).
Using ell_I=(omega_L*ell_L+omega_R*ell_R)/omega_I gives the
last matrix in (10), including every off-diagonal entry.

Choose any binary partition tree on {0,...,N}, down to singletons. It
can be aligned with chronological ruler cuts; shared physical endpoints
are assigned to just one of the two query sets. Iterating (10), with
omega_all=beta_N, proves the EXACT identity

 J_W=
  beta_N||sum_alpha ell_all,alpha*Z_alpha||^2
  +sum_(internal I) sigma_I
        ||sum_alpha(ell_L-ell_R)_alpha*Z_alpha||^2
  -sum_(i<N)c_i||sum_alpha h_i*z_alpha*P_i(z_alpha)*Z_alpha||^2.
                                                               (11)

No covariance term has been thrown away. Every coefficient is a finite
sum/product specified above. All the negative killing-step contributions
remain in the last sum. The constant column has coefficient1 in every
ell_I, zero in every ell_L-ell_R, and zero in each jump row. Its full
diagonal is therefore exactly beta_N, and its cross column is retained
in the first square.

Minimizing over the free constant vector v removes only the first square.
Equivalently, (8) asks for the SPECIFIC residual matrix inequality

 sum_(internal I) sigma_I
       (ell_L-ell_R)_res^T(ell_L-ell_R)_res
   >= sum_(i<q)c_i a_i^T a_i,
 a_i=(h_i*p_ij/d_j)_(j<m),                            (12)

on the ACTUAL complete queried word. The left side is beta_q times its
full residual conditional covariance. The right side is its full signed
cost. Equation (12) is an exact restatement, NOT a newly proved bound.
The suffix res denotes restriction to the residual columns0,...,m-1.
In particular positivity of each covariance in (10) does not imply (12).

## 4. Finite full-state transfer and the final boundary

There is no need to enumerate the exponentially many leaves to specify
the complete covariance matrix. For a word W let D_W be the diagonal
matrix with entries P_W(z_alpha), and let K_W,T_W be the symmetric
matrices for the two bilinear kernels

 K_W(z,w)=sum_(i<N)P_i(z)P_i(w)
                     [h_i-h_i^2*(z+w-z*w)/2],

 T_W(z,w)=sum_(i<N)P_i(z)P_i(w)
        [2s_(i+1)h_i-s_(i+1)h_i^2*(z+w-z*w)+h_i*(1-h_i)].

The matrix T_W evaluated at all z_alpha is exactly J_W. This follows
by substituting P_(i+1)(z)=(1-h_i*z)P_i(z) in (6), including its mixed
terms. For a single step d,

 K_[d](z,w)=d-d^2*(z+w-z*w)/2,
 T_[d](z,w)=d(d+1)-d^3*(z+w-z*w).                    (13)

If W=UV, splitting the finite sums at the block boundary gives

 K_UV=K_U+D_U*K_V*D_U,
 T_UV=T_U+D_U*(T_V+2S_U*K_V)*D_U.                    (14)

The offset2S_U*K_V is indispensable: each second-block clock is its
local clock plus S_U. Thus the whole signed child covariance, including
its coupling to every surviving mode and the constant, is transferred.

For H_(k+1)=(H_k,d_k,H_k), abbreviate D=D_Hk, K=K_Hk,
T=T_Hk, s=S_k, and F=diag(1-d_k*z_alpha). Then

 D_H(k+1)=D*F*D,
 K_H(k+1)=K+D*K_[d_k]*D+D*F*K*F*D,
 T_H(k+1)=T+D*(T_[d_k]+2s*K_[d_k])*D
             +D*F*(T+2(s+d_k)*K)*F*D.               (15)

This is an exact finite block identity. It is not claimed that the three
summands are individually PSD. Every matrix entry, including the signed
central contribution, is specified by (13)-(15).

At the last d_0 of H_m, all residual prefix columns have already vanished.
Consequently deleting that step changes ONLY the constant/constant entry:

 K_h=K_Hm-d_0*e_infinity*e_infinity^T,
 T_h=T_Hm-d_0*(2S+d_0+1)*e_infinity*e_infinity^T.      (16)

Here e_infinity is the coordinate unit column. In particular the actual
constant diagonal is S(S+1), not (S+d_0)(S+d_0+1).

The maintained vector-state dimension in (13)-(16) is m+1, and the
augmented original-space dimension including x_0 is m+2. Each symmetric
kernel has (m+1)(m+2)/2 scalar entries. These are finite identities, not
an executed computation or a new computational allowance.
The recursion starts with S_H0=0, D_H0=I, and K_H0=T_H0=0; hence it
specifies all entries without an unknown initial matrix.

The m+1 temporal dimension is genuinely lossless. Take rows at queries
2^j-1 for0<=j<m and at q, and order columns by j followed by infinity.
The residual diagonal at rowj is p_(2^j-1),j>0, its earlier columns are
zero, and the final row is (0,...,0,1). This square evaluation matrix
is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Therefore an exact linear
representation of ALL gradient traces cannot use fewer than m+1
coordinates. This is not a lower bound for every conceivable nonlinear
proof or probability representation.

## 5. Complete negative child blocks on the ACTUAL chronology

The proposed closure rule tested here is precise:

 "For every initial ruler block H_K, its entire signed energy J_HK is
  nonnegative on all inherited surviving reciprocal-mode states, perhaps
  after conditioning on its endpoint gradients and displacement."

This assertion is FALSE. The construction below covers every query of
the complete block. It does not select only a negative individual step.

Fix K>=4 with K+2^K<=m. Put N=2^K-1 and R=N+1=2^K. Use only the R
residual modes j=K,...,K+R-1, so all selected modes survive H_K. Set
v=0 and all other modal coefficients zero. On this ACTUAL prefix the
steps are h_i=d_(nu_2(i+1)), where nu_2 is the exponent of2 in i+1.

Define z_r=1/d_(K+r), 0<=r<R, and the square matrix

 V_(i,r)=P_i(z_r), 0<=i,r<=N.

The polynomials P_i have distinct degrees i and leading coefficients
L_i=(-1)^i product_(t<i)h_t. Hence, by triangular conversion to
monomials and the Vandermonde determinant,

 Ddet:=det V
   =[product_(i=0)^N product_(t<i)h_t]
                        product_(0<=r<s<=N)(z_r-z_s)>0.       (17)

The two signs cancel because there are N(N+1)/2 factors of each sign.
Thus EVERY specified real vector of all block query gradients
A=(A_0,...,A_N) has the following explicit modal coefficients:

 w_(K+r)=Ddet^(-1) sum_(i=0)^N
                (-1)^(i+r) det(V with row i and column r deleted)*A_i.
                                                               (18)

Empty determinants have value1. Every determinant in (17)-(18) denotes
the finite signed permutation sum of its displayed entries; no unknown
equation, root, or numerical inversion is hidden in this specification.
The cofactor identity V*adj(V)=Ddet*I proves g_i=A_i at EVERY query
0<=i<=N. The modal Gram of these scalar coefficients is real PSD
of rank at most1; no negative Gram is used.

For 3<=k<K put i_k=2^k-1 and

 kappa_k=2S_k+2d_k-d_k^2.

Let eta_k be the amplitude of the pulse at query i_k; in the query
vector used in (18), A_(i_k)=eta_k and all other entries vanish.
An isolated pulse has energy exactly kappa_k*eta_k^2. Its preceding
step contributes S_k*eta_k^2, and its d_k killing step contributes
[S_k+2d_k-d_k^2]*eta_k^2. The entire rest of H_K contributes zero.

These complete pulse energies are uniformly negative. At k=3,
S_3=4d_0+2d_1+d_2<6+5sqrt(2), while d_3>4+2sqrt(2) by (5).
The function 2d-d^2 decreases for d>1. Therefore

 kappa_3
 <2(6+5sqrt(2))+2(4+2sqrt(2))-(4+2sqrt(2))^2
 =-(4+2sqrt(2)).                                    (19)

For k>=4, (3)-(5) give d_k>=d_4>2d_3>21/2, whence

 kappa_k<d_k*(7-d_k)<-d_k^2/3.                       (20)

Distinct pulse indices differ by at least8. The temporal matrix in (9)
is tridiagonal, so there are no cross terms between these pulses. On
the entire pulse subspace,

 J_HK=sum_(k=3)^(K-1)kappa_k*eta_k^2<0 for nonzero eta. (21)

This is a (K-3)-dimensional negative subspace of the complete formal
child kernel on the selected high modes. Equations (17)-(18) realize
it without altering a single physical step or its enclosing parameter.

In particular the single fixed block H_4 works for EVERY m>=128:
use modes4,...,19, put A_7=1 and the other15 query values zero. Both
endpoint gradients vanish, and J_H4<-(4+2sqrt(2)).

There is also an explicit zero-displacement counterexample. In H_5 use
modes5,...,36 and prescribe all32 query values by

 g_7=d_4, g_15=-d_3, g_i=0 otherwise.                 (22)

Then g_0=g_31=0 and

 sum_(i<31)h_i*g_i=d_3*d_4-d_4*d_3=0,
 x_31=x_0,
 J_H5=kappa_3*d_4^2+kappa_4*d_3^2
      <-(4+2sqrt(2))*d_4^2-d_4^2*d_3^2/3<0.          (23)

Thus endpoint gradients and positions alone cannot make this entire
signed child nonnegative. The full correlated inherited state matters.

## 6. Unbounded boundary-feature requirement and explicit all-Q failure

On the pulse subspace (21), endpoint gradients already vanish. Its
displacement is -sum_(k=3)^(K-1)d_k*eta_k. Imposing zero displacement
is exactly ONE independent linear relation, leaving dimension K-4
when K>=5. The signed energy is negative definite on that subspace.

Consider ANY proposed extra boundary correction which, on this inherited
modal state, depends on at most r scalar linear features, with any real
symmetric coefficient matrix. Write it as (Lw)^T C (Lw), rank L<=r.
The map L is allowed to depend on the word and all its parameters.
If r<K-4, its kernel intersects the zero-displacement negative subspace
nontrivially. At such a state the correction is exactly zero and J_HK<0.
Hence no such correction can make every inherited child state nonnegative.

This rank argument even allows an arbitrary sign for C. It concerns
linear features and quadratic boundary charges; it does not refute
nonlinear conditioning, arbitrary-dimensional covariance, interblock
couplings, or other uses of original Q inequalities.

For every fixed r, choose K>=r+5 and m>=max(128,K+2^K). Thus a
uniformly bounded feature dimension cannot close all these children.
Choosing the largest K with K+2^K<=m gives a necessary feature count
at least K-4, which grows with m. It is not asserted to be a sharp
minimal dimension for the full original-kernel proof.

The negative directions are NOT legal smooth-convex transcripts. In
any nonzero pulse combination let i be the first nonzero-gradient query.
All earlier gradients, including g_(i-1), are zero, so GD has
x_i=x_(i-1)=x_0. For EVERY choice of shared values,

 Q_(i,i-1)+Q_(i-1,i)=||g_i-g_(i-1)||^2>0.             (24)

The necessary all-pair inequalities (1) therefore fail. In (22) the
specific pair is (6,7), and its sum equals d_4^2. Initial position may
be chosen as1, but that does not repair (24) or turn it into a normalized
legal hard function. For the homogeneous feature-rank argument it may
instead be set to0; scaling the pulse also defeats any fixed endpoint
charge at a nonzero fixed initial position.

These examples also do NOT show T_h is indefinite. After H_K the high
modal state specified by (18) is nonzero and continues along the actual
remaining physical word. Its later energy has not been bounded from
above and may pay the early deficit. The terminal norm of the complete
word is not replaced by that of H_K.

## 7. An explicit paid boundary bound for the growing state

This subsection gives a concrete sufficient local payment, rather than
merely saying to retain more coordinates. It does NOT prove that the
original suffix supplies the payment.

Fix 3<=K<m and use arbitrary common vectors in the modes j>=K, with
all lower modes zero and an arbitrary constant v. Put N=2^K-1,
r=m-K, and let the surviving modal vectors at the end of H_K be

 b_j=P_N(1/d_j)*w_j, K<=j<m.

Every step in H_K is at most d_(K-1)<d_K/2 by (4). For0<=x<=1/2,
log(1-x)>=-2x, obtained by integrating1/(1-x)<=2 from0 to x. Thus

 P_N(1/d_j)>=exp(-2S_K/d_j)>exp(-5),
 0<P_i(1/d_j)/P_N(1/d_j)<=exp(5).                   (25)

All factors are positive and at most1, and (3) gives the exponent bound.
The exact jump is

 Delta_i=h_i sum_(j>=K) [P_i(1/d_j)/(d_j P_N(1/d_j))]*b_j.

Cauchy--Schwarz in the finite j sum, retaining arbitrary common vector
cross terms, gives

 ||Delta_i||^2 <= r*exp(10)*h_i^2/d_K^2
                                      *sum_(j>=K)||b_j||^2.

Furthermore c_i=(h_i-1)s_(i+1)<=h_i*s_(i+1), and

 sum_i c_i*h_i^2
 <=d_(K-1)^2 sum_i s_(i+1)h_i
 =d_(K-1)^2*(S_K^2+sum_i h_i^2)/2
 <=d_(K-1)^2*S_K^2 <d_K^2*S_K^2/4.

Dropping only the nonnegative first sum in (9) proves the actual bound

 J_HK >= -[r*exp(10)/4]*S_K^2*sum_(j>=K)||b_j||^2.   (26)

The price is explicit, applies to the complete correlated high-mode
state and arbitrary v, and grows linearly with r in this chosen state
norm. It is not asserted to be sharp. For the example (22), ANY valid
boundary payment must in particular exceed the positive magnitude
displayed in (23).

Keeping the full state therefore avoids an algebraic information loss,
but does not provide a free energy budget. In the complete original
trajectory every residual b_j is ultimately killed. One cannot simply
attach (26) to an intermediate boundary and erase its cost at the last
boundary. No telescoping family of available payments has been proved.

## 8. Direct attempts, comparison with the scalar approach, and remaining gap

Attempt A retained all the conditional covariance in (10)-(11) and tried
to certify each whole ruler child as nonnegative before recombination.
This is refuted by (17)-(21), already at the ACTUAL complete H_4 prefix.
Its failure includes the lower-step contributions preceding the killing
step and the full block endpoint; it is stronger than the old observation
that an individual killing summand can be negative.

Attempt B allowed arbitrary quadratic repairs from endpoints and a fixed
number of extra linear boundary features. The complete H_5 example
(22)-(23) defeats endpoints alone, and Section6 defeats every uniform
finite feature count on larger actual prefixes. These are precise
failures of the tested local rules, not a prohibition on probability.

Attempt C kept the full m+1-dimensional transfer and all its covariances.
Equations (13)-(16) are exact and (26) prices a local repair, but the
global signed inequality (12) remains unmatched. This is where the
mechanism is BLOCKED. No available bound shows that the cross-block
variance squares dominate every original killing cost after the actual
constant square is minimized and the final d_0 is deleted.

Unlike the old scalar carry, no child covariance is discarded. Unlike
the earlier birth-coordinate pair/triple-square proposal, this draft
does not assume any b_i/u_i or alternating-load margin. It neither
reproves the earlier positive-entry/stability claims nor resolves those

The old full-primitive reports650089feeda25479 and504a69a1e000d6aa
described bounded numerical failures, including one length5 search.

capacity upper bound. There is no proof that every nonbasic seed has

The next allocated round must not retune the now-excluded two-tight-cut

reprove the general conditional lift as its deliverable. A different
full-flow family with at most one tight global cut, or a precise new

The prescribed gradient pattern is

 h5:    p,p,q,q,w,w;
 h6(c): p,p,q,q,q,w,w.                                   (20)

Starting at(19), use these vectors in the original updates. Their
weighted sum is P p+(H+b)q+a w. Since A=P+(H+b)+R,
Tbar=P+H+b, the terminal point is exactly w.

Let k be the second long-step index: k=3 or4. The normals X_i-G_i
at the two p queries are

 Y_1=Tbar*w+d*u+(Tbar-R)*v,
 Y_0=Y_1+a*p.

At the final q query and all earlier q queries they are

 Y_k=P*w+d*v,
 Y_i=Y_k+tau_i*q, where0<=tau_i<=H.

Here tau_i is the sum of middle steps remaining before query k. For
six steps it is H,H-c,0 at indices2,3,4. For five steps it is1,0.
The two w-query normals are a*w and0.

We now check the entire normal cone, not just adjacent interpolation.
For the p cone it suffices that a normal have nonnegative inner
products with u and u+v. For the q cone the conditions are inner
product with u<=0 and with v>=0. For the w cone the conditions are
inner product with v<=0 and with u+v<=0.

Using(18),

where Kcoef=35/16 for A=10 and391/104 for A=13. Both Kcoef>2,
while d<2 and epsilon<=1/20. Also

 <p,v>=(1-mu)(1+epsilon^2)-epsilon>0.

Therefore Y_0 and Y_1 are both in the full normal cone at p.
For the last q query,

 <Y_k,v>=0,
 <Y_k,u>=-P*gamma+R*(Tbar-P)*epsilon/Tbar<0.

Indeed P>=4, gamma>=5/31, 0<Tbar-P<Tbar, R=5/2 and epsilon<=1/20
bound the last expression by -20/31+1/8<0. Furthermore

 <q,u>=-gamma-(1-nu)epsilon<0,

Thus Y_k+tau_i q is in the full q cone for EVERY allowed tau_i,
including zero middle steps. Finally both <w,u> and <w,v> are negative,
so a*w is in the full w cone, and the zero normal is in it as well.

These checks prove G_i=P_K(X_i) at EVERY original query. They give a
single actual static function with the exact GD updates in(20).
Formula(3) now proves Q_ij<=0 for ALL ordered indices i,j in
{*,0,...,n}, not only adjacent or chosen support pairs. The exact values
are F_i=<X_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2; no independent repricing is involved.

## 7. Strict negative primitive energy

The terminal point and gradient both equal w. Put z=<u,v>=-epsilon.
Expanding(19) and using(18) in(4) yields

 V_h=||A w+P u+Tbar v||^2-A^2||w||^2
    =(P^2-2AP gamma)||u||^2
       +(Tbar^2-2A Tbar mu)||v||^2
       +2P(Tbar-A nu)z
    =2P R^2 z/Tbar.

Here P=2A gamma, Tbar=2A mu, and Tbar-A nu=R^2/Tbar.
Consequently the exact energies are

 V_h5=-(20/3)epsilon,
 V_h6(c)=-(3250/651)epsilon for EVERY0<=c<=112/31.          (21)

Thus neither family admits an original full certificate: substituting
these actual gradients into(1) would make its left side strictly negative
and its right side nonnegative. This excludes ALL30 multipliers and the
full R^6 matrix for h5, and ALL42 multipliers and the full R^7 matrix

enough to contradict any proposed PSD matrix on the full formal space.

With epsilon=1/100 the two exact negative values are

 -1/15 and -65/1302.                                     (22)

The true minimum and every original query remain as checked above.
This is a primitive-energy obstruction. It is not an objective error
upper bound and does not decide the unrestricted minimax profile.

## 8. Fixed functions exclude open boxes above the same thresholds

Fix epsilon=1/100. For each of the two base words h5 and h6(1), keep
the SAME triangle function F and SAME initial point X_0 from(17)--(19).
Set eta_box=1/100000000. For any physical word h' of the SAME length

 V_(h')(F,X_0)<-1/30.                                    (23)

Every such step remains positive. The coordinate bounds in Section5

 e_(i+1)<=4e_i+2eta_box,

Write s and s' for the two step sums, and let
z=X_n+s G_n=A w and z'=X'_n+s' G'_n. Then

 ||z'-z||<=(1+s)e_n+2|s'-s|
          <40000eta_box=1/2500,
 ||z||<13.

 |V_(h')-V_h|<27/2500.

All capacities in these two boxes still lie strictly above their

 10-5eta_box >292666/29275>Z_6/Z_1,

## 9. What changed, what is closed, and the next interface

The old full-primitive reports650089feeda25479 and504a69a1e000d6aa
described bounded numerical failures, including one length5 search.
They did not supply the explicit families or exact exclusions above.
Earlier saturated-cut drafts, including e59fe188876aa98d and
f7cee3034df8cb7f, already derived a much fuller single-cut multiplier
extraction. Accordingly Section2 is identified as a short consequence
of that mechanism, re-proved here rather than advertised as a new
single-cut theorem or used as an unverified premise.

The new work is the joint package: fixed length5/6 and b=1 thresholds;
nonbasic candidate words above those thresholds; a concrete negative
tilt of their two-cut triangle; every original query, actual minimum,
all ordered rows and exact negative energies; an entire split-middle
six-step family; and quantitative full-dimensional neighborhoods
excluded by one fixed function per box. It is not another numerical
non-discovery, a basic composition, padding or reversal argument.

The attempted mechanism tried to allocate excess mass to two separated
long steps while keeping both global cuts tight and killing the
unit-curvature terminal product with a unit step. This is now CLOSED
for the specified families and boxes. Two scalar equality witnesses
cannot be assumed compatible with one full certificate: the terminal
multiplier demanded by the earlier cut is forbidden by the later one,
and the tilted triangle makes the resulting energy deficit explicit.

What remains open is an actual full certificate for a different
length5/6 word above the corresponding threshold, in particular a
family with strict cut slack outside these excluded neighborhoods.
The present box size is deliberately conservative and is not a global
capacity upper bound. There is no proof that every nonbasic seed has
two tight cuts, is symmetric, or belongs to a triangle ansatz.

The next allocated round must not retune the now-excluded two-tight-cut
family, repeat a finite scan, transfer the four-step193/25 threshold, or
reprove the general conditional lift as its deliverable. A different
full-flow family with at most one tight global cut, or a precise new
strict-slack certificate mechanism, remains a legitimate next search.
