evidence:
# Positive correlated tails on the original ruler: exact family closure

Status: COMPLETE JOINT RESEARCH DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. No fact submission is
authorized. This is max's first round of the new two-round allocation:
completed baseline 43, proposed completed count after return 44, ceiling
45, attempted ceiling 46 including the historical interruption. Returning
this manuscript is not evidence that the outer loop has already exited.

The original all-word, all-sufficiently-large-horizon Goal remains OPEN.
The normalization throughout is W=2R: at smoothness one the payoff is
twice the final objective gap divided by the squared distance from the
initial point to the ENTIRE minimizer set.

Accepted inputs are 1252b8823bb5a290 for the original interpolation
convention, b98bb807d514e80d for K and the original benchmark,
1fca3e5dd555cb4a for the COMPLETE alternating-ray reference,
dfde2fa326c908bf for the FULL schedule-dependent complex reference,
and the UNCONDITIONAL denominator-ray assertion of 04219554e41d9750.
No conditional seed existence is assumed. No earlier unverified family
closure is a mathematical premise. All new ingredients below are proved
together, rather than promoted to facts and reused without a gate.

## 1. New state, explicit data, and result

For any physical word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) with every h_i>1, set
d_i=h_i-1. Choose eta>=1, tail coefficients t_i in [0,1], and innovation
slacks sigma_i>=0. These are explicit scalar inputs, not a Gram or
function-value feasibility oracle. Use the orthonormal basis
e_0,...,e_n of R^(n+1). Starting at

    g_n=e_n,  x_n=eta e_n,  q_n=1,  delta_n=eta-1,

construct backward, for i=n-1,...,0, by

    q_i=t_i q_(i+1)+(1-t_i)(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))/d_i+sigma_i,
    v_i^2=q_i-t_i^2 q_(i+1),
    g_i=t_i g_(i+1)+v_i e_i,
    x_i=x_(i+1)+h_i g_i.                                      (1)

Here v_i is the NONNEGATIVE square root. The reserve delta_i will be
computed by (2) below; it is <x_i,g_i>-q_i. Thus every scalar in (1)
is obtained by a finite specified recursion before the next index is
constructed. No sample is discarded or re-indexed.

Define the one static function for this full run by

    C=conv{0,g_0,...,g_n},
    F(x)=max_(v in C) {<x,v>-||v||^2/2}.

The new dependence is an overlapping future gradient plus a fresh
orthogonal innovation at each physical step. For example,
t_i=beta_m and sigma_i=0 at every i gives a genuinely changing,
positively correlated law on the original H_m below. Its dimension
and number of listed gradient vertices grow with m. Every coordinate
that survives several steps can change amplitude at all those steps.
This is not a common added gradient or an orthogonal sum of old
triangle constructions.

This draft proves that ALL choices in (1) are legal, with exact payoff

    V=(2eta-1)/r_0,  r_0=||x_0||^2
      =dist(x_0,argmin F)^2.

Nevertheless, for the ORIGINAL enclosing-m parameters

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta_m=1-1/m,
    c_m=lambda(1+1/m), a_m=beta_m/c_m,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_m c_m^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1,

the entire declared family has, for every m>=32, exactly

    sup_(eta,t,sigma) V = 1/(1+2 sum H_m).                     (T)

In particular this new positive-correlation law cannot improve on
Huber, the complete same-word K, or the complete same-word ray channel.
The exact original-B normalization and full-complex comparison are in
Section 8. The limiting family/B ratio is strictly below one.

The law leaves the nonpositive-adjacent-correlation hypotheses of
C98/C100. It also permits short-step reserves larger than the C99 cap:
already the all-t=1 choice has delta_i/q_i equal to a whole remaining
mass plus eta-1. Thus the new closure is not obtained by renaming a
previously excluded negative-correlation or capped-reserve law.

## 2. Scalar identities and actual positive semidefinite geometry

Suppose the suffix has been constructed. Its points and gradients lie
in span{e_(i+1),...,e_n}. Put q=q_(i+1), delta=delta_(i+1), t=t_i,
d=d_i, h=1+d, and sigma=sigma_i. Then

    v_i^2=(1-t)[t q+(delta+q)/d]+sigma >=0.

The vectors in (1), not merely their pairwise proposed correlations,
therefore give a real positive semidefinite Gram matrix. Taking inner
products in x_i=x_(i+1)+h g_i gives

    delta_i = delta+(1+d t)q+d sigma,                         (2)
    r_i = r_(i+1)+h^2 q_i+2h t(delta+q),                     (3)

where r_i=||x_i||^2. These identities also prove delta_i>=0 and q_i>0
at every index. All dimensions are physical dimensions, not radii.

For i<j, orthogonality of the innovations gives

    <g_i,g_j>=(product_(k=i)^(j-1) t_k) q_j >=0.              (4)

Also q_i>=t_i q_(i+1). Repeated use of this inequality implies

    <g_i,g_j><=q_i  for every i<j.                            (5)

For the concrete all-t=beta_m pilot, 0<t_i<1 and v_i>0 at every
physical index. Its gradients are all distinct, and adjacent inner
products are strictly positive. This statement follows symbolically
from (1), without evaluating any instance.

## 3. Every original ordered row, including the remote rows

Let y_i=x_i-g_i. We prove that

    <y_i,g_j-g_i><=0 for every i,j in {0,...,n},
    <y_i,-g_i><=0.                                          (6)

The second inequality is -delta_i<=0. The adjacent forward comparison
has the exact value

    <y_i,g_(i+1)-g_i>
      =(1-t_i)(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))
        +d_i(t_i q_(i+1)-q_i)
      =-d_i sigma_i <=0.                                   (7)

For a remote j>i+1, use y_i=y_(i+1)+g_(i+1)+d_i g_i. The fresh
innovation is orthogonal to g_j and g_(i+1), so

    <y_i,g_j-g_(i+1)>
      =<y_(i+1),g_j-g_(i+1)>
       +(1+d_i t_i)<g_(i+1),g_j-g_(i+1)> <=0.                (8)

The first term is nonpositive by backward induction; the second is
nonpositive by (5). Adding (7) proves the remote comparison. At i=n
there is no future vertex.

For a past j<i, write

    g_j=(product_(k=j)^(i-1)t_k)g_i+w,
    w in span{e_j,...,e_(i-1)}.

Since y_i is orthogonal to w, the corresponding expression in (6) is
(product t_k-1)delta_i<=0. This also establishes all the past
comparisons at the terminal index. Thus (6) includes every ordered
pair, however remote or in different recursive children.

The maximizer defining F is P_C(x), the Euclidean projection onto C.
Indeed completing the square turns maximization into minimization of
||v-x||^2. The projection characterization (6) gives P_C(x_i)=g_i.
For completeness the two projection inequalities at arbitrary x,z
give

    <P_C(x)-P_C(z),x-z> >= ||P_C(x)-P_C(z)||^2.

Consequently P_C is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizing affine
functions in the definition of F gives

    <P_C(x),u> <= F(x+u)-F(x) <= <P_C(x+u),u>.

The difference from the leftmost linear expression is between zero
and ||u||^2. Therefore F is differentiable, grad F=P_C, and its
gradient is 1-Lipschitz. F is finite because C is compact, and convex
because it is a supremum of affine functions of x.

The actual sampled values are

    f_i=F(x_i)=delta_i+q_i/2.                                (9)

Include x_*=g_*=f_*=0 and y_*=0. For the original convention in
1252b8823bb5a290, direct expansion gives the COMPLETE row identity

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<y_j,g_i-g_j> <=0.                                (10)

In particular Q_(i,*)=0 and Q_(*,j)=-delta_j<=0. No optimum row,
incoming terminal row, or cross-block row was relaxed.

## 4. Minimum set, true radius, and excess innovation price

Let C^polar={z:<z,v><=0 for every v in C}. Since 0 belongs to C,
F>=0. If z is in C^polar, every maximand is at most zero, so F(z)=0.
If z is not in C^polar, choose a listed vertex g with <z,g>>0;
at a sufficiently small positive multiple of g the maximand is
positive. Thus

    argmin F=C^polar,  min F=0.

Telescoping the actual updates yields

    x_0=eta g_n+sum_(i<n)h_i g_i,

a nonnegative combination of vertices. For every z in C^polar,
<x_0,z><=0, and consequently

    ||x_0-z||^2=||x_0||^2+||z||^2-2<x_0,z>>=||x_0||^2.

Equality is attained at z=0. This proves the exact nearest-minimizer
normalization in Section 1, even though the minimum set need not be
a singleton. Equations (2),(3) price the whole dense initial anchor.
At the terminal point, (9) gives 2f_n=2eta-1.

For fixed eta,t, increasing any sigma_i can only increase r_0.
To see this without ignoring its influence on earlier gradients,
observe that the recurrences (1)--(3), as maps of the suffix state
(r,delta,q), have nonnegative coefficients whenever 0<=t<=1 and d>0.
An increment in sigma adds respectively h^2 sigma, d sigma, sigma
to the current state (r_i,delta_i,q_i). These nonnegative increments
remain nonnegative at all earlier indices. Thus the best payoff in
the WHOLE declared family has sigma_i=0 for every i. This removes
arbitrary forward-adjacent normal slack by a paid monotonicity proof,
not by assuming that every optimal construction must saturate it.

Isometric embeddings do not change the distances. A finite orthogonal
sum of members of this family has a product minimizer set and payoff
equal to the radius-squared-weighted mean of its component payoffs.
It therefore cannot exceed the family bound proved below.

## 5. Exact reduction of all continuous correlations to binary choices

Set sigma=0 for the rest of the optimization. At fixed eta the
terminal state is (eta^2,eta-1,1). Each map (1)--(3) is linear in the
suffix state and affine in its own t_i. Each parameter occurs in only
one map. Their composition r_0(t_0,...,t_(n-1)) is thus affine
separately in every t_i. Repeatedly using

    p(...,t_i,...)=(1-t_i)p(...,0,...)+t_i p(...,1,...)

gives the exact convex-combination identity

    r_0(t)=sum_(epsilon in {0,1}^n)
       [product_(epsilon_i=1)t_i product_(epsilon_i=0)(1-t_i)]
       r_0(epsilon).                                       (11)

The weights are nonnegative and sum to one. The numerator 2eta-1
is the same for every term. Therefore

    V(t,eta)<=max_(epsilon in {0,1}^n) V(epsilon,eta).         (12)

This is a mathematical vertex reduction, not an enumeration that was
run. It remains valid for horizon-dependent choices and after taking
the supremum over eta>=1. The fresh-vector square roots do not need
to be affine: it is the exact radius state (1)--(3) that is affine.

For a binary choice, t_i=1 repeats the same gradient. At t_i=0 the
current gradient is orthogonal to EVERY later gradient, with norm
q_i=(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))/d_i. Thus the binary choices partition the
word into constant-gradient phases separated by selected physical
checkpoint steps. Repeated physical queries remain in the word;
only the algebra for a phase is compressed.

Write the exact partition as

    (block_0,b_0,block_1,b_1,...,b_(k-1),block_k),

where s_j is the mass of block_j and d_j^cp=b_j-1>0. The superscript
cp distinguishes checkpoint offsets from the physical indexed d_i.
Define a paid scalar A by starting at A=0 and, for each checkpoint,
updating

    T=s_j+b_j,    A <- T(T+A)/d_j^cp.                        (13)

At the end let r=s_k and X=r+eta. The exact squared radius is

    r_0=X(X+A),   V=(2X-D)/[X(X+A)],  D=2r+1.                (14)

To verify (13), denote the mutually orthogonal phase gradients by
p_j and their squared norms by Q_j^phase. Put T_j=s_j+b_j for j<k
and T_k=X=s_k+eta. At the checkpoint ending phase j, its current
coordinate is b_j p_j and is extinguished by that step. Hence the
initial point is exactly sum_(j=0)^k T_j p_j. The norm recursion
in (1), evaluated at each checkpoint, is

    Q_j^phase=(T_(j+1)/d_j^cp)Q_(j+1)^phase,
    Q_k^phase=1.

For a nonterminal next phase this uses
delta_next+q_next=(s_(j+1)+b_(j+1))Q_(j+1)^phase;
for the final phase it uses delta_next+q_next=X. Define

    A_j=[sum_(ell<j)T_ell^2 Q_ell^phase]/[T_j Q_j^phase].

Then A_0=0 and
A_(j+1)=T_j(T_j+A_j)/d_j^cp by substitution of the norm ratio.
The complete squared radius is
sum_(j=0)^k T_j^2 Q_j^phase=X^2+A_k X, proving (13),(14).
For k=0, A=0 and X=sum h+eta, so the same formula applies.

The maximum over eta>=1 is attained at

    X_*=(D+sqrt(D^2+2AD))/2,
    V_* = 2/[A+D+sqrt(D^2+2AD)].                             (15)

Indeed differentiating (14) gives a numerator
-2X^2+2DX+AD, positive before X_* and negative after it.
Also X_*>=D>=r+1, so the maximizer lies in the permitted domain.

## 6. A local checkpoint-removal lemma with both boundary cases paid

Consider a checkpoint b=1+d with ordinary mass s immediately before
it, and put T=s+b. Let A>=0 be the accumulated paid state BEFORE this
phase. Including this checkpoint changes it to

    A_b=T(T+A)/d.

If a later checkpoint c exists, let r be the ordinary mass between
b and c, and X=r+c. At c, including b produces the numerator
X(X+A_b) in update (13); deleting b produces
(T+X)(T+X+A). Their exact difference is

    Delta = X[A_b-2T-A]-T(T+A)
          = T[X(T-2d)/d-T]
             +A[X(T-d)/d-T].                              (16)

If b is the last checkpoint, precisely the same difference is the
difference of the two final radii, now with X=r+eta.

If T>2d and

    X >= dT/(T-2d),                                       (17)

both brackets in (16) are nonnegative. The condition for the second
bracket is weaker because T-d>T-2d. Deleting b then cannot increase
the radius at that same eta. If c exists, its denominator c-1 is
unchanged, and every later update (13) is increasing in its input
A; thus this local comparison propagates to the actual terminal.

There is a separate last-checkpoint argument. Suppose

    s+1>=2d,   r+1>=2d.                                   (18)

Then T>=3d and D=2r+1>=2d. At the optimizer of the split word,
formula (15), with A_b in place of A, gives

    X_*>=sqrt(A_b D/2)>=sqrt(T^2 D/(2d))>=T.

Since T>=3d, one has T>=dT/(T-2d). Thus (17) holds at the
SPLIT word's optimizer. The merged word at this same eta has at
least the split word's optimized payoff. Its own optimized payoff
can only be larger. This proves the required comparison even though
deleting the last checkpoint need not improve radius at every eta.

## 7. Applying the removal lemma to EVERY checkpoint subset on H_m

Fix m>=32, and suppress the subscript m on a,c,beta. All children
retain these same parameters. Write S_j=sum H_j and M_j=1+S_j.
Then

    M_0=1, M_(j+1)=2M_j+a c^j,
    M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j,
    A_mass=a/(c-2).                                       (19)

Here 0<A_mass<1. Indeed c>lambda>2, c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1,
whereas ac=beta<1. Moreover sqrt(2)<99/70, because
99^2>2*70^2. Therefore

    c <= (169/70)(33/32)=5577/2240 < 5/2.

For a physical step of ruler level ell, its offset is d=a c^ell.
Equation (19) gives

    d/M_ell <= c-2 < 1/2.                                (20)

Now take ANY nonempty selected checkpoint set, not necessarily a
dyadic partition. Choose a checkpoint of smallest ruler level ell
among those selected. Each of its two adjoining actual H_ell
children contains no selected checkpoint, since every level in such
a child is smaller than ell. Hence the ordinary blocks immediately
before and after it both have mass at least S_ell. Put M=M_ell.

If a later selected checkpoint c_cp exists, its level is at least ell,
so its offset is at least d. With the notation of Section 6,

    T>=M+d,   X>=M+d,   d<M/2.

The function T -> dT/(T-2d) decreases for T>2d. Thus

    dT/(T-2d) <= d(M+d)/(M-d) <= M+d <= X.

The deletion is legitimate by (16),(17). No other selected step
or physical ordinary step is altered.

If the chosen checkpoint is last, the same adjoining-child property
gives s+1>=M>2d and r+1>=M>2d. Conditions (18) apply. Hence its
deletion cannot decrease the optimized payoff either.

After deletion, choose a smallest-level checkpoint in the remaining
set and repeat the SAME argument. It applies to arbitrary subsets,
so it does not assume that the new set is dyadic. Finitely many
deletions end with no checkpoints. Formula (14) then becomes

    V=(2eta-1)/(S_m+eta)^2.

Its maximum over eta>=1 is at eta=S_m+1 and equals
1/(2S_m+1). Combining this with (12) and the monotonicity in sigma
proves the upper bound in (T) for every original parameter choice.
The all-t=1, all-sigma=0 member attains it. This proves equality.

## 8. Same-word references and the exact original benchmark price

Set Huber_m=1/(2S_m+1). Accepted b98bb807d514e80d and
1fca3e5dd555cb4a, with their COMPLETE checkpoint definitions, give

    sup V=Huber_m <= K_n(H_m) <= F_ray_n(H_m).

This comparison does not select one ray checkpoint or ignore any
feasible multi-cut choice. It does not require deciding whether
either reference is strictly larger than Huber on this word.

For clarity let C_full(h)=sup_(z in D_h) Gap_h(z), using EVERY original
interpolation cycle in D_h from accepted dfde2fa326c908bf, and the
accepted specified initial point 1 and specified minimizer 0.
Then

    sup V <= max{Huber_m,C_full(H_m)}.

There is also an explicit comparison to the UNaugmented full complex
channel: for every nonnegative word of mass S, set theta=1/(2S+1)
and P=product_(i<n)(1-h_i theta)>0. Then

    Gap_h(theta)=(2theta-theta^2)P^2 >= theta/2.              (21)

Here theta lies in the FULL D_h because its imaginary part is zero
and theta-theta^2>=0. To prove equality, all queried scalar points
Poly_i(theta) lie in [P,1]. Define a continuous nondecreasing
1-Lipschitz derivative on the real line by

    F'(x)=x                         for x<=theta P,
    F'(x)=theta P                   for theta P<=x<=P,
    F'(x)=theta x                   for x>=P,
    F(0)=0.

The matching values at the two joins make this derivative well
defined; its slopes are 1,0,theta. Its unique zero is 0. Integration
gives F(P)=(theta-theta^2/2)P^2, while at each queried positive point
its derivative is theta Poly_i(theta). This is the required one
static scalar realization. The accepted upper bound on Gap_h at

product(1-h_i theta)>=1-S theta=(1+theta)/2: prove this by induction
using nonnegative factors and partial sums at most S theta<1.
Thus Gap_h(theta)>=theta(2-theta)(1+theta)^2/4>=theta/2,
as (2-theta)(1+theta)^2=2+3theta-theta^3>=2.

Consequently the exact family supremum satisfies

    (sup V)/C_full(H_m) <= 2.

No assertion C_full>=Huber is made. The full complex supremum is
NOT replaced by the universal lens or by the single parameter in
(21); (21) is only a valid lower bound within that full channel.
The family already loses to the combined accepted references
because it cannot exceed their Huber component.

For the ORIGINAL benchmark define C_0^bench=B_0=1 and

    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_n^bench=max_(0<=k<n) Omega(C_k^bench,C_(n-k-1)^bench),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n) G(C_k^bench,B_(n-k-1)).

These are exactly the accepted recurrences, not a balanced-tree
surrogate. Equations (T),(19) give the exact normalized family ratio

    B_(2^m-1) sup V
      = B_(2^m-1)/[2 A_mass c_m^m+2(1-A_mass)2^m-1].        (22)

The unconditional assertion in accepted 04219554e41d9750 supplies

where B_1=G(1,1)=4. Meanwhile A_mass tends to one and

Therefore the exact limiting price is

For a rational strict separation, exp(1)>5/2 and

This is a fixed relative shortfall of the NEW declared family,
not a certified full-class upper improvement for unrestricted W.

## 9. Adversarial checks and the exact boundary of the conclusion

First, (T) is not a theorem for all step words. On h=(10), choose
eta=2, t_0=0, sigma_0=0. Then

    g_1=e_1, x_1=2e_1, g_0=(sqrt(2)/3)e_0,
    x_0=(10sqrt(2)/3)e_0+2e_1,
    r_0=236/9, V=27/236 > 1/21.

All data belong to the same explicit family, and its static realization,
all ordered rows and true minimum distance were proved in Sections
2--4. The last inequality is 27*21>236. Huber dominance here would
be false; the small-ruler-offset condition (20) does real work.

Second, deletion at a FIXED terminal eta is false even on the
original H_m. This guards the optimizer step in Section 6. Use only
the central highest-level checkpoint, and put

    M=M_(m-1), d=a_m c_m^(m-1), q=d/M,
    s=r=M-1, T=M+d, eta=1, A=0.

Then (16) with X=M gives

    r_split-r_merged = T M(1/q-2-q).                        (24)

For m>=32, q>sqrt(2)-1, so (24) is negative. Here is a direct
enclosing-m check rather than an illicit critical-parameter substitution.
At level 2,

    d_2=lambda(1-1/m^2),
    M_2=lambda^2-1/m-4/[lambda(m+1)].

The inequality lambda d_2>M_2 is equivalent to
m+4m^2/[lambda(m+1)]>lambda^2, which follows from m>=32 and
lambda^2<25/4. Moreover
(d_(ell+1)/M_(ell+1))=c(d_ell/M_ell)/(2+d_ell/M_ell),
and d_ell/M_ell<c-2, so these ratios increase with ell. Thus the
top-level ratio is at least the level-2 ratio. Since
1/q-2-q<0 exactly when q>sqrt(2)-1, the counterexample follows.
It does not contradict (T), which optimizes the terminal ratio.

Third, nonnegative backward coefficients larger than one do not
silently reopen this same geometry. In any legal realization with
the same fresh-innovation orthogonality and radial terminal point,
the reverse adjacent normal gives

    <y_(i+1),g_i-g_(i+1)>=(t_i-1)delta_(i+1)<=0.             (25)

For eta>1 every reserve is positive, forcing t_i<=1. For eta=1,
all reserves before the terminal one are still positive: from
delta_i=t_i(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))+d_i q_i, they are positive when
t_i>=0 and q_i>0. A legal nonzero-terminal run cannot have q_i=0,
since it would reach a minimizer and then remain there. Thus only
t_(n-1)>1 is possible, and only when eta=1. In that case
q_(n-1)>=t_(n-1)^2 by the orthogonal decomposition. Replacing this
last extension by t=1,q=1 reduces each of q_(n-1),delta_(n-1),
r_(n-1). Keep all earlier t in [0,1] and their nonnegative sigma
as derived from their original forward adjacent inequalities.
The nonnegative state maps then reduce the initial radius as well.
The replacement is a member of (1). Therefore the same upper bound
also covers this exceptional nonnegative coefficient case. This is
an optional enlargement of the obstruction, not an assumption used
to construct the pilot.

The closure DOES NOT cover negative backward coefficients; a new
innovation correlated with a second future mode; arbitrary conjugate
heights in place of the projection-value form (9); or an independently
moving transverse terminal position. It is not a closure of all
positively correlated gradients, all Markov laws, or all smooth
interpolants. It does not reinterpret the accepted finite H6 witness

1fca3e5dd555cb4a for the COMPLETE alternating-ray reference,

## 1. New state, explicit data, and result

For any physical word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) with every h_i>1, set
d_i=h_i-1. Choose eta>=1, tail coefficients t_i in [0,1], and innovation
slacks sigma_i>=0. These are explicit scalar inputs, not a Gram or
function-value feasibility oracle. Use the orthonormal basis
e_0,...,e_n of R^(n+1). Starting at

    g_n=e_n,  x_n=eta e_n,  q_n=1,  delta_n=eta-1,

construct backward, for i=n-1,...,0, by

    q_i=t_i q_(i+1)+(1-t_i)(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))/d_i+sigma_i,
    v_i^2=q_i-t_i^2 q_(i+1),
    g_i=t_i g_(i+1)+v_i e_i,
    x_i=x_(i+1)+h_i g_i.                                      (1)

Here v_i is the NONNEGATIVE square root. The reserve delta_i will be
computed by (2) below; it is <x_i,g_i>-q_i. Thus every scalar in (1)
is obtained by a finite specified recursion before the next index is
constructed. No sample is discarded or re-indexed.

Define the one static function for this full run by

    C=conv{0,g_0,...,g_n},
    F(x)=max_(v in C) {<x,v>-||v||^2/2}.

The new dependence is an overlapping future gradient plus a fresh
orthogonal innovation at each physical step. For example,
t_i=beta_m and sigma_i=0 at every i gives a genuinely changing,
positively correlated law on the original H_m below. Its dimension
and number of listed gradient vertices grow with m. Every coordinate
that survives several steps can change amplitude at all those steps.
This is not a common added gradient or an orthogonal sum of old
triangle constructions.

This draft proves that ALL choices in (1) are legal, with exact payoff

    V=(2eta-1)/Rtail_0_sq,  Rtail_0_sq=||x_0||^2
      =dist(x_0,argmin F)^2.

Nevertheless, for the ORIGINAL enclosing-m parameters

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta_m=1-1/m,
    c_m=lambda(1+1/m), a_m=beta_m/c_m,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_m c_m^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,

the entire declared family has, for every m>=32, exactly

    sup_(eta,t,sigma) V = 1/(1+2 sum H_m).                     (T)

In particular this new positive-correlation law cannot improve on

The exact original-B normalization and full-complex comparison are in

The law leaves the nonpositive-adjacent-correlation hypotheses of

mass plus eta-1. Thus the new closure is not obtained by renaming a

## 2. Scalar identities and actual positive semidefinite geometry

Suppose the suffix has been constructed. Its points and gradients lie
in span{e_(i+1),...,e_n}. Put q=q_(i+1), delta=delta_(i+1), t=t_i,
d=d_i, h=1+d, and sigma=sigma_i. Then

    v_i^2=(1-t)[t q+(delta+q)/d]+sigma >=0.

The vectors in (1), not merely their pairwise proposed correlations,
therefore give a real positive semidefinite Gram matrix. Taking inner
products in x_i=x_(i+1)+h g_i gives

    delta_i = delta+(1+d t)q+d sigma,                         (2)
    Rtail_i_sq = Rtail_(i+1)_sq+h^2 q_i+2h t(delta+q),                     (3)

Here Rtail_i_sq=||x_i||^2; R_sq denotes a generic squared-radius state.
The fresh Rtail notation avoids the accepted ray channel's different r_i.
 These identities also prove delta_i>=0 and q_i>0
at every index. All dimensions are physical dimensions, not radii.

For i<j, orthogonality of the innovations gives

    <g_i,g_j>=(product_(k=i)^(j-1) t_k) q_j >=0.              (4)

Also q_i>=t_i q_(i+1). Repeated use of this inequality implies

    <g_i,g_j><=q_i  for every i<j.                            (5)

For the concrete all-t=beta_m pilot, 0<t_i<1 and v_i>0 at every
physical index. Its gradients are all distinct, and adjacent inner
products are strictly positive. This statement follows symbolically
from (1), without evaluating any instance.

## 3. Every original ordered row, including the remote rows

Let y_i=x_i-g_i. We prove that

    <y_i,g_j-g_i><=0 for every i,j in {0,...,n},
    <y_i,-g_i><=0.                                          (6)

The second inequality is -delta_i<=0. The adjacent forward comparison
has the exact value

    <y_i,g_(i+1)-g_i>
      =(1-t_i)(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))
        +d_i(t_i q_(i+1)-q_i)
      =-d_i sigma_i <=0.                                   (7)

For a remote j>i+1, use y_i=y_(i+1)+g_(i+1)+d_i g_i. The fresh
innovation is orthogonal to g_j and g_(i+1), so

    <y_i,g_j-g_(i+1)>
      =<y_(i+1),g_j-g_(i+1)>
       +(1+d_i t_i)<g_(i+1),g_j-g_(i+1)> <=0.                (8)

The first term is nonpositive by backward induction; the second is
nonpositive by (5). Adding (7) proves the remote comparison. At i=n
there is no future vertex.

For a past j<i, write

    g_j=(product_(k=j)^(i-1)t_k)g_i+w,
    w in span{e_j,...,e_(i-1)}.

Since y_i is orthogonal to w, the corresponding expression in (6) is
(product t_k-1)delta_i<=0. This also establishes all the past
comparisons at the terminal index. Thus (6) includes every ordered
pair, however remote or in different recursive children.

The maximizer defining F is P_C(x), the Euclidean projection onto C.
Indeed completing the square turns maximization into minimization of
||v-x||^2. The projection characterization (6) gives P_C(x_i)=g_i.
For completeness the two projection inequalities at arbitrary x,z
give

    <P_C(x)-P_C(z),x-z> >= ||P_C(x)-P_C(z)||^2.

Consequently P_C is 1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maximizing affine
functions in the definition of F gives

    <P_C(x),u> <= F(x+u)-F(x) <= <P_C(x+u),u>.

The difference from the leftmost linear expression is between zero
and ||u||^2. Therefore F is differentiable, grad F=P_C, and its
gradient is 1-Lipschitz. F is finite because C is compact, and convex
because it is a supremum of affine functions of x.

The actual sampled values are

    f_i=F(x_i)=delta_i+q_i/2.                                (9)

Include x_*=g_*=f_*=0 and y_*=0. For the original convention in
1252b8823bb5a290, direct expansion gives the COMPLETE row identity

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<y_j,g_i-g_j> <=0.                                (10)

In particular Q_(i,*)=0 and Q_(*,j)=-delta_j<=0. No optimum row,
incoming terminal row, or cross-block row was relaxed.

## 4. Minimum set, true radius, and excess innovation price

Let C^polar={z:<z,v><=0 for every v in C}. Since 0 belongs to C,
F>=0. If z is in C^polar, every maximand is at most zero, so F(z)=0.
If z is not in C^polar, choose a listed vertex g with <z,g>>0;
at a sufficiently small positive multiple of g the maximand is
positive. Thus

    argmin F=C^polar,  min F=0.

Telescoping the actual updates yields

    x_0=eta g_n+sum_(i<n)h_i g_i,

a nonnegative combination of vertices. For every z in C^polar,
<x_0,z><=0, and consequently

    ||x_0-z||^2=||x_0||^2+||z||^2-2<x_0,z>>=||x_0||^2.

Equality is attained at z=0. This proves the exact nearest-minimizer
normalization in Section 1, even though the minimum set need not be
a singleton. Equations (2),(3) price the whole dense initial anchor.
At the terminal point, (9) gives 2f_n=2eta-1. Multiplying F by any
L>0 and using the physical steps h_i/L preserves all points and this
normalized payoff.

For fixed eta,t, increasing any sigma_i can only increase Rtail_0_sq.
To see this without ignoring its influence on earlier gradients,
observe that the recurrences (1)--(3), as maps of the suffix state
(R_sq,delta,q), have nonnegative coefficients whenever 0<=t<=1 and d>0.
An increment in sigma adds respectively h^2 sigma, d sigma, sigma
to the current state (Rtail_i_sq,delta_i,q_i). These nonnegative increments
remain nonnegative at all earlier indices. Thus the best payoff in
the WHOLE declared family has sigma_i=0 for every i. This removes
arbitrary forward-adjacent normal slack by a paid monotonicity proof,
not by assuming that every optimal construction must saturate it.

Isometric embeddings do not change the distances. A finite orthogonal
sum of members of this family has a product minimizer set and payoff
equal to the radius-squared-weighted mean of its component payoffs.
It therefore cannot exceed the family bound proved below.

## 5. Exact reduction of all continuous correlations to binary choices

Set sigma=0 for the rest of the optimization. At fixed eta the
terminal state is (eta^2,eta-1,1). Each map (1)--(3) is linear in the
suffix state and affine in its own t_i. Each parameter occurs in only
one map. Their composition Rtail_0_sq(t_0,...,t_(n-1)) is thus affine
separately in every t_i. Repeatedly using

    p(...,t_i,...)=(1-t_i)p(...,0,...)+t_i p(...,1,...)

gives the exact convex-combination identity

    Rtail_0_sq(t)=sum_(epsilon in {0,1}^n)
       [product_(epsilon_i=1)t_i product_(epsilon_i=0)(1-t_i)]
       Rtail_0_sq(epsilon).                                       (11)

The weights are nonnegative and sum to one. The numerator 2eta-1
is the same for every term. Therefore

    V(t,eta)<=max_(epsilon in {0,1}^n) V(epsilon,eta).         (12)

This is a mathematical vertex reduction, not an enumeration that was
run. It remains valid for horizon-dependent choices and after taking
the supremum over eta>=1. The fresh-vector square roots do not need
to be affine: it is the exact radius state (1)--(3) that is affine.

For a binary choice, t_i=1 repeats the same gradient. At t_i=0 the
current gradient is orthogonal to EVERY later gradient, with norm
q_i=(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))/d_i. Thus the binary choices partition the
word into constant-gradient phases separated by selected physical
checkpoint steps. Repeated physical queries remain in the word;
only the algebra for a phase is compressed.

Write the exact partition as

    (block_0,b_0,block_1,b_1,...,b_(k-1),block_k),

where s_j is the mass of block_j and d_j^cp=b_j-1>0. The superscript
cp distinguishes checkpoint offsets from the physical indexed d_i.
Define a paid scalar A by starting at A=0 and, for each checkpoint,
updating

    T=s_j+b_j,    A <- T(T+A)/d_j^cp.                        (13)

At the end let r=s_k and X=r+eta. The exact squared radius is

    Rtail_0_sq=X(X+A),   V=(2X-D)/[X(X+A)],  D=2r+1.                (14)

To verify (13), denote the mutually orthogonal phase gradients by
p_j and their squared norms by Q_j^phase. Put T_j=s_j+b_j for j<k
and T_k=X=s_k+eta. At the checkpoint ending phase j, its current
coordinate is b_j p_j and is extinguished by that step. Hence the
initial point is exactly sum_(j=0)^k T_j p_j. The norm recursion
in (1), evaluated at each checkpoint, is

    Q_j^phase=(T_(j+1)/d_j^cp)Q_(j+1)^phase,
    Q_k^phase=1.

For a nonterminal next phase this uses
delta_next+q_next=(s_(j+1)+b_(j+1))Q_(j+1)^phase;
for the final phase it uses delta_next+q_next=X. Define

    A_j=[sum_(ell<j)T_ell^2 Q_ell^phase]/[T_j Q_j^phase].

Then A_0=0 and
A_(j+1)=T_j(T_j+A_j)/d_j^cp by substitution of the norm ratio.
The complete squared radius is
sum_(j=0)^k T_j^2 Q_j^phase=X^2+A_k X, proving (13),(14).
For k=0, A=0 and X=sum h+eta, so the same formula applies.

The maximum over eta>=1 is attained at

    X_*=(D+sqrt(D^2+2AD))/2,
    V_* = 2/[A+D+sqrt(D^2+2AD)].                             (15)

Indeed differentiating (14) gives a numerator
-2X^2+2DX+AD, positive before X_* and negative after it.
Also X_*>=D>=r+1, so the maximizer lies in the permitted domain.

## 6. A local checkpoint-removal lemma with both boundary cases paid

Consider a checkpoint b=1+d with ordinary mass s immediately before
it, and put T=s+b. Let A>=0 be the accumulated paid state BEFORE this
phase. Including this checkpoint changes it to

    A_b=T(T+A)/d.

If a later checkpoint c exists, let r be the ordinary mass between
b and c, and X=r+c. At c, including b produces the numerator
X(X+A_b) in update (13); deleting b produces
(T+X)(T+X+A). Their exact difference is

    Delta = X[A_b-2T-A]-T(T+A)
          = T[X(T-2d)/d-T]
             +A[X(T-d)/d-T].                              (16)

If b is the last checkpoint, precisely the same difference is the
difference of the two final radii, now with X=r+eta.

If T>2d and

    X >= dT/(T-2d),                                       (17)

both brackets in (16) are nonnegative. The condition for the second
bracket is weaker because T-d>T-2d. Deleting b then cannot increase
the radius at that same eta. If c exists, its denominator c-1 is
unchanged, and every later update (13) is increasing in its input
A; thus this local comparison propagates to the actual terminal.

There is a separate last-checkpoint argument. Suppose

    s+1>=2d,   r+1>=2d.                                   (18)

Then T>=3d and D=2r+1>=2d. At the optimizer of the split word,
formula (15), with A_b in place of A, gives

    X_*>=sqrt(A_b D/2)>=sqrt(T^2 D/(2d))>=T.

Since T>=3d, one has T>=dT/(T-2d). Thus (17) holds at the
SPLIT word's optimizer. The merged word at this same eta has at
least the split word's optimized payoff. Its own optimized payoff
can only be larger. This proves the required comparison even though
deleting the last checkpoint need not improve radius at every eta.

## 7. Applying the removal lemma to EVERY checkpoint subset on H_m

Fix m>=32, and suppress the subscript m on a,c,beta. All children
retain these same parameters. Write S_j=sum H_j and M_j=1+S_j.
Then

    M_0=1, M_(j+1)=2M_j+a c^j,
    M_j=A_mass c^j+(1-A_mass)2^j,
    A_mass=a/(c-2).                                       (19)

Here 0<A_mass<1. Indeed c>lambda>2, c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1,
whereas ac=beta<1. Moreover sqrt(2)<99/70, because
99^2>2*70^2. Therefore

    c <= (169/70)(33/32)=5577/2240 < 5/2.

For a physical step of ruler level ell, its offset is d=a c^ell.
Equation (19) gives

    d/M_ell <= c-2 < 1/2.                                (20)

Now take ANY nonempty selected checkpoint set, not necessarily a
dyadic partition. Choose a checkpoint of smallest ruler level ell
among those selected. Each of its two adjoining actual H_ell
children contains no selected checkpoint, since every level in such
a child is smaller than ell. Hence the ordinary blocks immediately
before and after it both have mass at least S_ell. Put M=M_ell.

If a later selected checkpoint c_cp exists, its level is at least ell,
so its offset is at least d. With the notation of Section 6,

    T>=M+d,   X>=M+d,   d<M/2.

The function T -> dT/(T-2d) decreases for T>2d. Thus

    dT/(T-2d) <= d(M+d)/(M-d) <= M+d <= X.

The deletion is legitimate by (16),(17). No other selected step
or physical ordinary step is altered.

If the chosen checkpoint is last, the same adjoining-child property
gives s+1>=M>2d and r+1>=M>2d. Conditions (18) apply. Hence its
deletion cannot decrease the optimized payoff either.

After deletion, choose a smallest-level checkpoint in the remaining
set and repeat the SAME argument. It applies to arbitrary subsets,
so it does not assume that the new set is dyadic. Finitely many
deletions end with no checkpoints. Formula (14) then becomes

    V=(2eta-1)/(S_m+eta)^2.

Its maximum over eta>=1 is at eta=S_m+1 and equals
1/(2S_m+1). Combining this with (12) and the monotonicity in sigma
proves the upper bound in (T) for every original parameter choice.
The all-t=1, all-sigma=0 member attains it. This proves equality.

## 8. Same-word references and the exact original benchmark price

Set Huber_m=1/(2S_m+1). Accepted b98bb807d514e80d and
1fca3e5dd555cb4a, with their COMPLETE checkpoint definitions, give

    sup V=Huber_m <= K_n(H_m) <= F_ray_n(H_m).

This comparison does not select one ray checkpoint or ignore any
feasible multi-cut choice. It does not require deciding whether
either reference is strictly larger than Huber on this word.

For clarity let C_full(h)=sup_(z in D_h) Gap_h(z), using EVERY original
interpolation cycle in D_h from accepted dfde2fa326c908bf, and the
accepted specified initial point 1 and specified minimizer 0.
Then

    sup V <= max{Huber_m,C_full(H_m)}.

There is also an explicit comparison to the UNaugmented full complex
channel: for every nonnegative word of mass S, set theta=1/(2S+1)
and P=product_(i<n)(1-h_i theta)>0. Then

    Gap_h(theta)=(2theta-theta^2)P^2 >= theta/2.              (21)

Here theta lies in the FULL D_h because its imaginary part is zero
and theta-theta^2>=0. To prove equality, all queried scalar points
Poly_i(theta) lie in [P,1]. Define a continuous nondecreasing
1-Lipschitz derivative on the real line by

    F'(x)=x                         for x<=theta P,
    F'(x)=theta P                   for theta P<=x<=P,
    F'(x)=theta x                   for x>=P,
    F(0)=0.

The matching values at the two joins make this derivative well
defined; its slopes are 1,0,theta. Its unique zero is 0. Integration
gives F(P)=(theta-theta^2/2)P^2, while at each queried positive point
its derivative is theta Poly_i(theta). This is the required one
static scalar realization. The accepted upper bound on Gap_h at

product(1-h_i theta)>=1-S theta=(1+theta)/2: prove this by induction

Thus Gap_h(theta)>=theta(2-theta)(1+theta)^2/4>=theta/2,
as (2-theta)(1+theta)^2=2+3theta-theta^3>=2.

Consequently the exact family supremum satisfies

    (sup V)/C_full(H_m) <= 2.

No assertion C_full>=Huber is made. The full complex supremum is
NOT replaced by the universal lens or by the single parameter in
(21); (21) is only a valid lower bound within that full channel.
The family already loses to the combined accepted references
because it cannot exceed their Huber component.

For the ORIGINAL benchmark define C_0^bench=B_0=1 and

    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,

    B_(2^m-1) sup V
      = B_(2^m-1)/[2 A_mass c_m^m+2(1-A_mass)2^m-1].        (22)

The unconditional assertion in accepted 04219554e41d9750 supplies

where B_1=G(1,1)=4. Meanwhile A_mass tends to one and

    c_m^m/lambda^m=(1+1/m)^m -> exp(1),

Therefore the exact limiting price is

    lim_(m->infinity) B_(2^m-1) sup V = Z_1/[2 exp(1)] < 1.  (23)

For a rational strict separation, exp(1)>5/2 and
(203/100)^2<5, so this limit is strictly below 41209/50000.
This is a fixed relative shortfall of the NEW declared family,
not a certified full-class upper improvement for unrestricted W.

## 9. Adversarial checks and the exact boundary of the conclusion

First, (T) is not a theorem for all step words. On h=(10), choose
eta=2, t_0=0, sigma_0=0. Then

    g_1=e_1, x_1=2e_1, g_0=(sqrt(2)/3)e_0,
    x_0=(10sqrt(2)/3)e_0+2e_1,
    Rtail_0_sq=236/9, V=27/236 > 1/21.

All data belong to the same explicit family, and its static realization,
all ordered rows and true minimum distance were proved in Sections
2--4. The last inequality is 27*21>236. Huber dominance here would
be false; the small-ruler-offset condition (20) does real work.

Second, deletion at a FIXED terminal eta is false even on the
original H_m. This guards the optimizer step in Section 6. Use only
the central highest-level checkpoint, and put

    M=M_(m-1), d=a_m c_m^(m-1), q=d/M,
    s=r=M-1, T=M+d, eta=1, A=0.

Then (16) with X=M gives

    Rtail_split_sq-Rtail_merged_sq = T M(1/q-2-q).                        (24)

For m>=32, q>sqrt(2)-1, so (24) is negative. Here is a direct
enclosing-m check rather than an illicit critical-parameter substitution.
At level 2,

    d_2=lambda(1-1/m^2),
    M_2=lambda^2-1/m-4/[lambda(m+1)].

The inequality lambda d_2>M_2 is equivalent to
m+4m^2/[lambda(m+1)]>lambda^2, which follows from m>=32 and
lambda^2<25/4. Moreover
(d_(ell+1)/M_(ell+1))=c(d_ell/M_ell)/(2+d_ell/M_ell),
and d_ell/M_ell<c-2, so these ratios increase with ell. Thus the
top-level ratio is at least the level-2 ratio. Since
1/q-2-q<0 exactly when q>sqrt(2)-1, the counterexample follows.
It does not contradict (T), which optimizes the terminal ratio.

Third, nonnegative backward coefficients larger than one do not
silently reopen this same geometry. In any legal realization with
the same fresh-innovation orthogonality and radial terminal point,
the reverse adjacent normal gives

    <y_(i+1),g_i-g_(i+1)>=(t_i-1)delta_(i+1)<=0.             (25)

For eta>1 every reserve is positive, forcing t_i<=1. For eta=1,
all reserves before the terminal one are still positive: from
delta_i=t_i(delta_(i+1)+q_(i+1))+d_i q_i, they are positive when
t_i>=0 and q_i>0. A legal nonzero-terminal run cannot have q_i=0,
since it would reach a minimizer and then remain there. Thus only
t_(n-1)>1 is possible, and only when eta=1. In that case
q_(n-1)>=t_(n-1)^2 by the orthogonal decomposition. Replacing this
last extension by t=1,q=1 reduces each of q_(n-1),delta_(n-1),
Rtail_(n-1)_sq. Keep all earlier t in [0,1] and their nonnegative sigma
as derived from their original forward adjacent inequalities.
The nonnegative state maps then reduce the initial radius as well.
The replacement is a member of (1). Therefore the same upper bound
also covers this exceptional nonnegative coefficient case. This is
an optional enlargement of the obstruction, not an assumption used
to construct the pilot.

The closure DOES NOT cover negative backward coefficients; a new
innovation correlated with a second future mode; arbitrary conjugate
heights in place of the projection-value form (9); or an independently
moving transverse terminal position. It is not a closure of all
positively correlated gradients, all Markov laws, or all smooth

## 10. Literature, proof state, and remaining allocation

Matlas searches were performed for smooth projection-conjugate
realizations and for the separate-affinity vertex principle. The
first returned the generic Moreau-envelope Lemma 4.1 of Khanh,
Mordukhovich and Tran, arXiv:2303.08785. It supplies no special
correlation law or quantitative radius bound here, so it is not
imported. The exact local Taylor--Hendrickx--Glineur paper
arXiv:1502.05666 was reread at Sections 2.4--2.5, Theorem 4's proof
and Corollary 1. Its interpolation construction motivates the
normal-coordinate audit; all needed smoothness and pair claims
are nevertheless derived directly in Section 3, using the accepted
project convention.

Matlas identified Ben Sassi and Girard, "Computation of Polytopic
Invariants for Polynomial Dynamical Systems using Linear Programming,"
arXiv:1012.1256, Lemma 2.2. Its statement is: a multi-affine function
on a rectangle has the same minimum on the rectangle as on its
vertex set. Definition 2.1 means degree at most one in each separate
variable, with mixed products allowed. The preceding paragraph
explains the convex-combination argument. The exact PDF was
downloaded into downloads/1012.1256.pdf and the relevant definitions
and argument were read through the web PDF text extractor after
local pdftotext failed with "command not found". No package was
installed. Equation (11) gives the full needed proof independently;
no LP or polynomial computation from that paper was run or invoked.

Adversarial checks were symbolic: both row orientations, all remote
rows, both optimum rows, terminal eta=1, zero/fractional/one tail
coefficients, positive slack, the true polar minimum set, the last
checkpoint optimizer, arbitrary checkpoint subsets, and the
fixed-eta counterexample (24). No numerical evaluation, solver,
machine algebra, replay, verifier call, consult, or subagent was used.

One allocated round remains AFTER this round actually returns. The
specific positive-tail family (1), even with arbitrary positive
slack and the exceptional coefficient in (25), is now closed at
draft level and must not be retuned. A genuinely different next law
must change its dependence or value/terminal geometry. A concrete
next candidate is a TWO-future-mode backward dependence
g_i=t_i g_(i+1)+u_i g_(i+2)+v_i e_i, with mixed signs allowed and
the original full normal inequalities retained. Unlike (1), its
current reserve and radius state need the independent correlation
<x_(i+1),g_(i+2)> and cross-gradient term; the three-scalar
separate-affinity argument does not apply automatically. This is a
next research direction, not a proved legal or competitive family.

Even a competitive construction on all original H_m would leave the
all-n/all-nonnegative-word bridge to the original Goal. Neither that

## 2. Static regularity and the actual nearest minimizer

J is continuous, finite, convex and nonnegative. Its proximal objective
is coercive and strictly convex, hence has a unique minimizer y(x).
Comparison with y+t(v-y), convexity and t decreasing to0 show
g(x)=x-y(x) belongs to the subdifferential of J at y(x). Conversely,
that subgradient inequality and the quadratic expansion prove proximal
optimality. Adding the subgradient inequalities at two points gives
||g(x)-g(x')||^2<=<g(x)-g(x'),x-x'>. In particular g is1-Lipschitz.
Evaluating the proximal objective at the old minimizer gives the upper
first-order bound for F. Applying its subgradient inequality at the new
minimizer and completing the quadratic gives the lower bound. Thus

    0<=F(x')-F(x)-<g(x),x'-x><=||x'-x||^2/2.

This proves that F is convex, differentiable and1-smooth with gradient g.
Its minimum is0 and its minimum set is exactly

    K={x_1<=0, -w x_1+ell x_2<=0, -u x_1-v x_2<=kappa}. (7)

Indeed J=0 gives F=0, and an attained zero proximal objective forces
both nonnegative terms to vanish. The geometry in (7) has been rederived
for w>0: it lies below the line x_2=(w/ell)x_1<=0 and above
x_2=(-kappa-u x_1)/v>=-kappa/v. It is a triangle when kappa>0 and
the singleton0 when kappa=0. Its left vertex has
x_1=-kappa/(u+vw/ell); the denominator is positive even when u=0.

Since T+delta>0 and H>0, the closest point to X_0 is

    t_star=min(H,kappa/v), x_star=(0,-t_star),
    D=(H-kappa/v)_+,
    R^2=dist(X_0,K)^2=(T+delta)^2+D^2.                  (8)

Proof: every point of K has first coordinate<=0 and second coordinate
>=-kappa/v. These separate lower bounds on squared coordinate distances
are simultaneously attained at the displayed point, which satisfies all
three inequalities of (7). This includes both positive-part branches.
Here R denotes this local true distance, not the project's ratio in W=2R.

## Appendix A. Joint proof of the full-norm inequality

The following calculation is included in full and rechecked for the
relaxed variables used in Section4. It is not an invocation of C104 as a fact.
Equation labels in this appendix carry the prefix A.


We prove from scratch: for A,M,T>0 with T>=2A, u>=0,v>0,alpha>=0,

    delta=A-Mu-alpha>=0,
    Mv^2<=delta+u(A-Mu),

one has

    (u^2+v^2)/[(T+delta)^2+(Mv-u alpha/v)_+^2]
       <=max{A^2/(M^2T^2),1/(T+A+M)^2}.                 (A15)

This controls the horizontal contribution that the former orthogonal
argument did not need. It includes both nearest-minimizer branches.

First suppose M<=A+2A^2/T. Put P=A-Mu and d=delta, so0<=d<=P.
The constraint gives M(u^2+v^2)<=Au+d. Direct expansion yields

    A^2(T+d)^2-M T^2(Au+d)
       =A P T^2+(2A^2T-MT^2)d+A^2d^2>=0.              (A16)

If the coefficient of d is nonnegative, every term is nonnegative.
If it is negative, substitute d<=P in just that term; the result is
at least P[(A-M)T^2+2A^2T]+A^2d^2>=0 by this regime's bound on M.
Dropping the second nonnegative radius square now proves the first
alternative A^2/(M^2T^2) in (A15). No saturation or endpoint limit is
needed in this regime.

Suppose next M>A+2A^2/T. Then M>A. For fixed u,alpha put

    P=A-Mu, d=P-alpha, k=1+u, c=uP,
    x=v^2, c_0=u alpha/M, H_0=T+d.

Legal v>0 forces P>0. The ratio on the left of (A15) is

    (u^2+x)/[H_0^2+M^2(x-c_0)_+^2/x].                  (A17)

On x<=c_0 it increases. On x>=c_0, differentiation has the sign of

    H_0^2-2M^2c_0-M^2u^2
      +2M^2c_0^2/x+M^2u^2c_0^2/x^2.

The first three terms are at least

    T^2-2Mu(A-Mu)-M^2u^2
       =T^2-A^2+(A-Mu)^2>=0.

The branches agree at x=c_0. Therefore (A17) is bounded by its value
at the allowed endpoint x=(d+c)/M. There
Mx-u alpha=(1+u)d>=0, giving the bound

    F_u(d)=(Au+d)/
       { M[(T+d)^2+M(1+u)^2d^2/(d+c)] }, 0<=d<=P.     (A18)

This saturation is only an upper relaxation; no final activity is assumed.

Write b_0=Au. For u>0, c>0, differentiation of (A18) has the sign of

    G_u(d)=(T+d)(T-d-2b_0)-M(1+u)^2 H_u(d),
    H_u(d)=d[(b_0+c)d+2b_0c]/(d+c)^2.

Explicitly

    H_u'(d)=2c^2(d+b_0)/(d+c)^3>=0,
    G_u'(d)=-2(d+b_0)-M(1+u)^2H_u'(d)<=0,
    G_u(P)=(T+A)(T-A-2Au).                            (A19)

The last identity follows by substituting P=A-Mu and d+c=P(1+u):
the subtracted term at P is Mu(A+P+2Au), which combined with the
first product leaves exactly the displayed factorization.

In the present regime

    u<=A/M<T/(T+2A)<=(T-A)/(2A).

The last inequality is equivalent to (T-2A)(T+A)>=0. Hence
G_u(P)>=0. Because G_u is nonincreasing, G_u(d)>=G_u(P)>=0 throughout
[0,P]; thus F_u(d) is nondecreasing. When u=0, its formula reduces to
d/{M[(T+d)^2+Md]}, whose derivative has the sign T^2-d^2>0 for
0<d<=A. Its limit at d=0 is0. These observations also handle all
relaxed endpoint degeneracies; the actual constraint always has v>0.

It follows that (A18) is at most its alpha=0 value at d=P. Writing
t=P in[0,A], that value is

    [A^2+(M-A)t]/[M^2(T^2+(2T+A+M)t)].                 (A20)

This is a quotient of positive affine functions of t. Its derivative
has the sign of

    (T+A)[M(T-A)-A(T+A)].

If nonpositive, the maximum is its value at t=0, namely A^2/(M^2T^2).
If nonnegative, the maximum is at t=A and equals
A/{M[(T+A)^2+MA]}. In the latter case

    M[(T+A)^2+MA]-A(T+A+M)^2
       =(T+A)[M(T-A)-A(T+A)]>=0,

so the value at t=A is at most1/(T+A+M)^2. This proves (A15).
Every relaxation, both radius branches, and the u=0 and boundary cases
have been retained. This is exactly the full-norm inequality required in Section4 of this joint draft.

# Signed interval certificates: exact matching and a complete equal-tail obstruction

Status: COMPLETE JOINT RESEARCH DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max4 round43,
the first of two analytical rounds allocated after completed42 by
TASK.md and master_guidance c3f16cd4617d4d93. No numerical evaluation,
solver, machine algebra, replay, verifier, consult or subagent was used.
The original seed and the original exact-profile Goal remain OPEN.

Accepted mathematical inputs are fact04219554e41d9750, Sections10--11,
for the original primitive identity and its full-space composition, and
fact1252b8823bb5a290 for the interpolation convention used there.
All new ingredients below are proved jointly; no unverified finding is
used as a correctness premise.

The variable-step interval identity is NOT new: it was already derived
in shared cd0f93f08a50828f. Its source inspiration is Jinze Zhao,
*Constant Steps Are s-Composable: An Exact Interpolation Certificate for
Gradient Descent*, arXiv:2609.11784v1, Sections3.1--3.2. That exact local
text and its interval proof were read. No constant-step positivity theorem
is imported. Sibling8a77ec65ac2eeb52 also correctly warned that homogeneous
interval diagonalization does not solve a changing-word objective problem.

The new outcomes here are:

* an explicit, unique solution of the seven signed suffix/adjacent mode
  equations, with all twenty original multipliers displayed;
* a full original-array obstruction for EVERY word h=(u,w,t,t)>=0 in
  that construction family at sum h>=168/25;
* a nonempty dense algebraic calibration with every multiplier positive
  and the entire five-dimensional remainder zero;
* an explicit valid ConPP word at which this seven-mode representation
  forces Lambda12<0, and a polynomial twelve-edge skew correction that
  repairs that exact calibration while preserving the whole matrix.

The equal-tail restriction belongs to the chosen construction family.
Neither equality of those steps nor the seven-mode restriction nor a
zero remainder is imposed on the original cone. The broader seven-mode
family with unequal last steps is NOT decided here.

## 1. Original full-space identity and elementary boundary consequences

For h=(h0,h1,h2,h3)>=0 put s=sum h_i, C=1+s, and
P_i=sum_(j<i)h_j. Indices of all five independent formal gradients are
0,1,2,3,4. Let e be the column of five ones, and use the original matrix

    T_ii=1, T_ij=h_j for j<i, T_ij=0 for j>i,
    omega=(-2h0,-2h1,-2h2,-2h3,2s)^T,
    D=diag(h0(2-h0),h1(2-h1),h2(2-h2),h3(2-h3),-s(s+2)).

For a zero-diagonal array Lambda, let L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda and
M=D+sym(LT), where sym(A)=(A+A^T)/2. The original sufficient condition
is Lambda_ij>=0 for all i!=j, L^T e=omega, and M PSD on ALL R5.
The accepted identity is

    V_h+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g0,...,g4)>,        (1)
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    x_i=x0-sum_(j<i)h_j g_j,
    V_h=2sum_(i<4)h_i(f_i-f4)+sum_(i<4)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                             -s(s+1)||g4||^2.

Actual smooth convex trajectories satisfy every Q_ij<=0. The sign
orientation and the factor in (1) are the ones in accepted04219554e41d9750.

Every correct flow has e^T M e=0. Indeed Te=e+P,
2sum h_i P_i=s^2-sum h_i^2,
e^T D e=-s^2-sum h_i^2, and omega^T Te=s^2+sum h_i^2.
PSD therefore forces Me=0, by evaluating (e+az)^T M(e+az) for both
signs of small a. Under the flow this gives

    sum_j Lambda_ij(P_j-P_i)=2h_i(1+P_i), i<4,
    sum_(j<4)Lambda_4j(s-P_j)=2sC.                         (2)

For example, (Me)_i=h_i(1+P_i)+(LP)_i/2 at i<4, while
(Me)_4=-sC+(LP)_4/2. These expansions also prove (2) directly.

For s>0 both endpoint steps obey

    h0,h3 <= 2C/(C+1)<2.                                  (3)

For h0>1, (2) gives 2h0<=s out0, and the first diagonal gives
h0(2-h0)>=(h0-1)out0. Combining proves the first inequality;
h0<=1 is already below the bound. For h3>0, the terminal diagonal
gives out4>=s(s+2), and (2) gives
2sC>=h3 out4>=h3 s(s+2). The zero case needs no division.
Here out_i=sum_(j!=i)Lambda_ij denotes the outgoing mass. The same
proofs apply verbatim to the compressed word at any smaller length.

We will use the stronger construction requirement M=0. For any queried
index i its diagonal is

    M_ii=h_i(2-h_i)+sum_(j<i)Lambda_ij
                                  +(1-h_i)sum_(j>i)Lambda_ij. (4)

Thus a positive h_i<=1 is impossible when all Lambda>=0 and M=0.
If h_i=0, (4) forces every outgoing coefficient at i to vanish;
the zero flow then forces all incoming coefficients to vanish. Such a
vertex is isolated. Removing it compresses the zero physical step and
restricts the full identity without identifying two formal gradients.
Conversely no compression is used to justify an untested original row.

At the threshold no zero step is possible in this zero-remainder class.
Here is a bound sufficient to prove that assertion. For a positive bridge
step 1+delta with prefix capacity A and suffix capacity E, put
eta=delta/E>0. Use the scalar function with derivative
clamp(x,[-eta,1]), starting from x0=A. At the bridge query x=1;
the bridge lands at -delta, and the tail ends at -eta, with all its
gradients -eta. For this function f(x)=x g-g^2/2. Direct substitution
and the GD telescope give V_h=x0^2-(x_n+s g_n)^2=A^2-C^2 eta^2.
Its derivative is continuous, nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz, so it is
an actual convex 1-smooth function; normalize f(0)=0.
Consequently every feasible array requires

    C delta <= A E.                                       (5)

With at most two positive steps, (3) on the compressed word gives s<4.
With three positive steps, write the middle one as 1+delta. Both
endpoints are <2, so A,E<3. Equation (5) gives delta<9/C, hence
C<6+9/C, or C<3+3sqrt(2)<15/2<193/25. The all-zero case is immediate.
This proves the asserted zero-step exclusion without dropping a formal
coordinate from an allegedly feasible original array.

Define p0=1 and p_(i+1)=(1-h_i)p_i. Then Tp=e and Le=0. Hence

    p^T M p=p^T Dp=1-C^2 p4^2,                             (6)

where the last equality telescopes
h_i(2-h_i)p_i^2=p_i^2-p_(i+1)^2. When M=0 this is an equality
C|p4|=1, rather than merely a necessary inequality. In particular,
after all four positive steps have been shown >1, put r_i=h_i-1>0;
then

    C r0 r1 r2 r3=1.                                      (7)

The extra quadratic kernel is thus derived on the original full space.

## 2. The declared signed interval family

For 0<=a<b<=4, let J^[a,b] be zero outside rows/columns [a,b].
Its off-diagonal entries inside the interval are

    J_ij=(i-a+1)h_i-1           when i<j,
    J_ij=1+(b-i)h_i             when j<i,                   (8)

and each diagonal is minus its off-diagonal row sum. Put h4=0 solely
as a convention in (8); its value does not affect the final row of a mode.
In particular J e=0 for every mode.

For local indices a<=i<j<=b, put
u_i=(i-a+1)h_i-1 and v_j=1+(b-j)h_j. Multiplication gives
(JT)_ij=u_i v_j and (JT)_ji=-v_j u_i. A column before a vanishes by
the zero row sum; a column after b vanishes by triangularity. Therefore
sym(JT) is diagonal. At i in [a,b] its diagonal is

    (h_i-1)^2(i-a+1)(b-i)-(i-a)(b-i+1).                   (9)

To check (9) without omitting a term, let l=i-a and m=b-i.
The diagonal of JT is
(h_i-1)m((l+1)h_i-1)-l(1+m h_i)
=(h_i-1)^2(l+1)m-l(m+1).

The selected construction is

    N=sum_(a=0)^3 tau_a J^[a,4]
                        +sum_(i=0)^2 q_i J^[i,i+1],       (10)

with ALL seven weights tau_a,q_i real. Define actual Lambda_ij=N_ij
for i!=j and Lambda_ii=0. Since N e=0, its row Laplacian is L=-N.
Require

    N^T e=-omega, sym(NT)=D, Lambda_ij>=0 (i!=j).          (11)

Equations (11) imply M=D-sym(NT)=0 on the entire R5. No smaller
matrix, rank heuristic, numerical factorization or dropped coordinate is
being used. Conversely (11) is the precise zero-remainder family (10).
Signed mode weights are permitted; only the final actual Lambda signs count.

## 3. All seven weights and all twenty entries, explicitly

Assume here h_i>1 for i<4. Define

    S_i=sum_(a=0)^i tau_a, B_i=sum_(j=0)^i S_j, B_(-1)=0,
    U_i=h_i B_i-S_i=r_i B_i+B_(i-1),
    V_i=1+(4-i)h_i,
    K_i=product_(j=0)^i r_j^(-2)-1.                       (12)

B_i here denotes an interval-coordinate cumulative flow, NOT the
project's benchmark B_n. In fact the final outgoing terminal coefficients
are Lambda_4i=S_i, so B_i is their cumulative sum.

The mode formula gives, for every i<j,

    Lambda_ij=U_i+1_(j=i+1)*r_i*q_i,
    Lambda_ji=V_j S_i+1_(j=i+1)*q_i,                      (13)

where q3=0. Let Z_i=(4-i)B_i+q_i. By (9) the diagonal equation at i<4

    B3=C^2-1, q_i=K_i-(4-i)B_i, i=0,1,2.                (14)

For the cumulative column flow through cut i, put

                                             +(2-h_i)q_i.

All diagonal equations hold by the displayed recursion, and the first

## 5. Entire equal-tail family: statement and reductions

Write

    a0<=a<=rC<1, 0<d<=rC,
    b=C-5-a-2d>0,
    C a b d^2=1.                                        (22)

The proof splits only at d=1/2 and covers both pieces completely.

### 5.1. The whole d>=1/2 piece

On the rectangle a in[a0,rC], d in[1/2,rC], define

    F_C(a,d)=a d^2(C-5-a-2d).

For C>=C0, the last factor is positive throughout this rectangle:
its minimum is C-5-3rC, positive at C0 and increasing thereafter.
For fixed d, F_C is a concave quadratic in a, so its minimum is
at an endpoint of the a interval. At either endpoint a, its derivative
in d is 2a d(C-5-a-3d), which can change sign only from positive
to negative. Hence the minimum in d is also at an endpoint.

The four possible minimum values are

    a0(C-6-a0)/4,
    rC(C-6-rC)/4,
    a0 rC^2(C-5-a0-2rC),
    rC^3(C-5-3rC).                                      (23)

Each is positive and increasing for C>=C0: rC'=2/(C+1)^2,
so each bracket in (23) has positive derivative, and its positive
nonconstant prefactors also increase. At C0 use the rational bounds

    41/100<a0<21/50, 3/4<rC0=84/109<4/5.

They give the following respective lower bounds for (23):

    533/4000, 69/400, 2583/16000, 27/200.

For the third bracket, for example,
C0-5-a0-2rC0>68/25-21/50-8/5=7/10.
For the fourth it is >68/25-12/5=8/25.
Every displayed bound is at least 533/4000. It follows that

    C F_C(a,d) >= (193/25)(533/4000)
                 =102869/100000>1,

contradicting (22). This closes the entire d>=1/2 piece.

### 5.2. The whole 0<d<1/2 piece

Since a<1 and 2d<1,

    b>C-7>=18/25>1/2.                                   (24)

The nonnegative original coefficients Lambda40,Lambda41 give
B1>=B0>=0. The nonnegative original Lambda12 in (17) gives

    b K1+B0-2b B1>=0,

so K1>=(2-1/b)B0>=0. For equal last steps, (16) says

    3t B1=2(u+w)+3u B0-(2-w)K1.

Substitute this expression into the Lambda12 inequality. The result is

    (5+3d-2b)K1 >= 4(u+w)+(6u-3t/b)B0.                  (25)

The last coefficient is positive: u>=sqrt(2)>7/5, b>18/25,
and t<3/2 imply 2ub>252/125>3/2>t. Thus (25) requires

    (5+3d-2b)K1>=4(u+w)>0.                              (26)

In particular both factors on the left are positive. By (22),

    K1=1/(a^2 b^2)-1=C^2 d^4-1<C^2/16-1,
    5+3d-2b<17+7d-2C<41/2-2C,
    u+w=C-3-2d>C-4.

Therefore (26) would imply

    4(C-4)<(41/2-2C)(C^2/16-1).                         (27)

This is impossible for EVERY C>=C0. In fact the left side minus the
right side of (27) is

    g(C)/32, g(C)=4C^3-41C^2+64C+144.

The exact endpoint values are

    g(193/25)=546003/15625>0,
    g'(193/25)=91338/625>0,

and g''(C)=24C-82>0 on C>=C0. Thus g is positive on that whole ray.
This contradicts (27), closing the 0<d<1/2 piece and proving the claim.

Only original coefficient signs, original flow, and the full M=0
identity were used. The proof permits all seven weights to be signed
and every final coefficient to lie on its nonnegative boundary.

## 6. Hostile calibration: the seven-mode family misses a valid ConPP word

The following gives an exact reason not to extend Section5 to all
zero-remainder certificates or to all four-step words with equal tails.

Put A=1+sqrt(2), let b>0 solve b(A+4+b)=4A, and put

    C=A+4+b, kappa=C^2/16,
    h=(sqrt(2),1+b,3/2,3/2).                              (28)

This word has an actual full certificate with M=0. To specify it
explicitly, its only nonzero entries are

    Lambda01=2, Lambda10=2A,
    Lambda14=(kappa-1)b,
    Lambda21=Lambda31=3(kappa-1)/2,
    Lambda23=kappa, Lambda24=2kappa-3/2,
    Lambda32=7kappa/2, Lambda34=10kappa-3/2,
    Lambda41=kappa-1, Lambda42=kappa, Lambda43=14kappa.     (29)

All entries not listed are zero, as is the diagonal. All listed entries
are positive because C>4 and b>0. Here is a full-matrix derivation of
(29) rather than an inference from a smaller principal block.

The one-step sqrt(2) certificate has multipliers2,2A and full remainder
(2-(sqrt(2))^2)(g0-g1)^2=0. The two-step word(3/2,3/2) has

    lambda01=1, lambda02=1/2, lambda10=7/2,
    lambda12=17/2, lambda20=1, lambda21=14.

Its row Laplacian has flow(-3,-3,6), and direct multiplication with
T=[[1,0,0],[3/2,1,0],[3/2,3/2,1]] gives
sym(LT)=-diag(3/4,3/4,-15). Its entire remainder is zero.
Accepted04219554e41d9750 Section11 embeds these two child remainders,
multiplies the right one by kappa, and adds (kappa-1) times the
displayed nonnegative primitive-join interpolation combination. With
bridge index1 and right-child queries2,3,4, this gives exactly (29).
Hence every original flow is correct and the full five-by-five M is zero.

But (28) cannot have a certificate in the seven-mode class (10).
It satisfies (7), because Cb=4A and A(sqrt(2)-1)=1. Equations (16),
(19) force B0=0. Let K1=A^2/b^2-1>0; positivity follows from b<A,
which follows from C>4 and bC=4A. Then (16) simplifies to

    B1=2K1/3.

For explicit verification, its numerator is
(A+b)[b^2+(A+1)b-A]/b^2;
the bracket equals3(A-b) by b^2+(A+4)b=4A, and its denominator
2h2+h3 is9/2. This gives B1=2K1/3 exactly. Formula (17) then forces

    Lambda12=b K1-2b B1=-b K1/3<0.                       (30)

No alternative seven weights can repair (30), since Section3 proved
their uniqueness for fixed positive h. The actual certificate (29)
has Lambda13=0 and Lambda14>0, whereas (17) requires Lambda13=Lambda14.
Releasing that specific repeated forward coefficient is therefore a
necessary change for this calibration, even with arbitrary signed mode
weights and a zero full remainder.

This is a scope counterexample, not a threshold seed: no capacity gain
beyond the original basic composition is claimed for (28). Explicitly,
C is the positive root of C^2-(A+4)C-4A=0. Since A<121/50, this
polynomial at C0=193/25 is greater than89/250>0, proving C<C0.

### 6.1. An explicit full-matrix repair of that calibration

The failed relation can actually be released by a displayed homogeneous
direction, rather than just named as missing. For h=(u,w,z,v) with
b=w-1,c=z-1,d=v-1>0, define a skew-symmetric five-by-five matrix
A_cyc with zero row/column0 and the following upper entries:

    (A_cyc)12=-bcv, (A_cyc)13=b(cd-1), (A_cyc)14=bz,
    (A_cyc)23=-(1+bcd), (A_cyc)24=1-bc, (A_cyc)34=-w.

Let p_tail=(1,-b,bc,-bcd)^T on indices1,2,3,4. Direct multiplication
gives A_cyc e=0 and A_cyc(0,p_tail)^T=0. For example the first of
these four row sums is -bcv+b(cd-1)+bz=0; the corresponding p_tail
row product is b^2 c[v+cd-1-zd]=0. The other three row sums are
bcv-bcd-1+1-bc, -b(cd-1)+bcd+1-w, and -bz-1+bc+w,
respectively, and all vanish. The other three p_tail products are
bc[v-bcd-1-d(1-bc)],
b[1-cd-(1+bcd)+wcd], and
b[-z+1-bc+wc], respectively, and all vanish as well.

For any real rho put Delta L=rho A_cyc T^(-1). Since T^(-1)e=p
from (6) and the last four entries of p are (1-u)p_tail,

    Delta L e=0, (Delta L)^T e=0,
    sym(Delta L T)=0.                                   (31)

Moreover column0 of T^(-1), restricted to indices1,...,4, is
-u p_tail. Thus Delta L has zero row and column0. Its only changed
off-diagonal multipliers, Delta Lambda_ij=-(Delta L)_ij, are

    Delta Lambda12=-rho b v,
    Delta Lambda13= rho b(z+v),
    Delta Lambda14=-rho b z,
    Delta Lambda21= rho c v,
    Delta Lambda23= rho(v+1-bc),
    Delta Lambda24= rho(bc-1),
    Delta Lambda31= rho(1-cd),
    Delta Lambda32= rho[d(1+b+c)-1],
    Delta Lambda34= rho w,
    Delta Lambda41=-rho z,
    Delta Lambda42= rho(w+z),
    Delta Lambda43=-rho w.                              (32)

For an entrywise check, the tail inverse matrix used to obtain (32) is

    [ 1       0       0    0
     -w       1       0    0
      wc     -z       1    0
     -wcd     zd     -v    1 ].

Thus (31)--(32) preserve every original flow and EVERY entry of the
original full M, not just a principal block or one covariance. Actual
nonnegativity must still be checked after the change. This is not an
unconditional sign-preserving move.

At the concrete word (28), put K=kappa-1. The unique seven-mode base is

    B0=0, B1=2K/3,
    B2=1+(20+2b)K/9, B3=16K+15.

These formulas follow from (16) and K(4-b)=2(A+b), which in turn
follows from Cb=4A and kappa=C^2/16. Select rho=-2K/9 in (32).
Then Lambda12 changes from -bK/3 to0, Lambda13 changes from2bK/3
to0, and Lambda14 changes from2bK/3 to bK. The outgoing terminal
entries become K,1+K,14(1+K) at columns1,2,3. For the other changed
entries, substitution in (17) and (32) gives, in order21,23,24,31,32,34,

    3K/2, 1+K, 1/2+2K, 3K/2, (7/2)(1+K), 17/2+10K.

Together with the unchanged entries these are exactly (29), so every
sign is now nonnegative. This is a constructive repair of the actual
negative coefficient, with full-space PSD preserved identically.
It demonstrates an essential non-tree skew freedom absent from (10).
It supplies no threshold word: the repaired word still has C<C0.

## 7. What is closed, and what remains to do

Closed at joint-draft level: the entire declared seven-mode construction
on every nonnegative equal-tail word(u,w,t,t) with sum>=168/25. The
calibration in Section4 has all twenty entries positive and full M=0,
so the family is an actual dense certificate mechanism. Section6 proves
its loss of freedom by one explicit negative ORIGINAL multiplier at
a valid full ConPP word, and (31)--(32) repair that entire actual array.

Still open: the broader seven-mode family with unequal tails, the full
ten-interval zero-remainder family, every general nonzero PSD remainder,
the original threshold cone, and the original all-word exact-profile Goal.
The evidence does not show that a survivor of every old necessary test
exists, and supplies no such claimed survivor.

In particular, repeating the variable-step interval identity or changing
only the seven weights in the excluded equal-tail family cannot produce
the requested seed. A meaningful continuation must release an actual
coefficient relation, such as Lambda13=Lambda14, or the zero-remainder
restriction, and must again provide all twenty signs and full-space PSD.
The direction (32) releases that relation and is fully calibrated, but
its simultaneous signs at an actual threshold word remain unmatched.
No generic unresolved feasibility formulation is claimed as a solution.

One allocated analytical round remains after this round returns. No
numerical probe is proposed here: the two actual calibration objects and
the entire selected obstruction have exact symbolic decisions. No formal
gate, resource renewal, truth-store edit or process action is authorized
or implied by this handoff.
