evidence:
# Nested normals and signed block gradients on the original ruler

Status: COMPLETE JOINT RESEARCH DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max's second
and final round in the allocation starting after completed43. The
completed target after return is45 and the attempted ceiling is46,
including the historical interruption. No formal-verifier allowance is
available. Nothing here is an accepted fact or a completion of the Goal.

The original target is unchanged: an asymptotically matching lower bound
for every sufficiently large physical horizon and every nonnegative
predetermined word, or a certified fixed-relative asymptotic full-class
upper improvement over the ORIGINAL Zhang--Jiang profile. Throughout,
W=2R: normalized payoff means twice the final gap divided by smoothness
times the squared distance to the entire minimizer set.

Accepted inputs are1252b8823bb5a290 for the interpolation convention,
b98bb807d514e80d for the complete K lower bound and original benchmark,
1fca3e5dd555cb4a for the COMPLETE alternating-ray channel, and
dfde2fa326c908bf for the FULL schedule-dependent complex channel.
No unverified family closure is used as a mathematical premise. Every
new ingredient below is proved jointly. In particular the max44 draft
is motivation, not a predecessor.

## 1. Results and the new dependence

For each integer m>=4 retain the SAME enclosing parameters everywhere:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1, h=H_m, S_m=sum h.

There are three results, with deliberately different scopes.

1. The nested-normal construction of Section2 gives explicit real
   points and gradients, with a new independent dual-normal state and
   every chronological forward normal tied. Its natural power policy
   fails an ORIGINAL three-point interpolation cycle for EVERY p>0
   and EVERY terminal eta>1 on every H_m,m>=4. This remains a failure
   if all values are freely reassigned. The more general exact failed
   hypothesis is a convex increasing inverse-normal profile over the
   first two physical time intervals, with a positive second increment.

2. The different signed block rule in Section4 IS a legal static
   smooth-convex construction on the whole original word. It has a
   fresh orthogonal innovation at each large bridge and negative
   correlations between successive constant-gradient H_2 blocks.
   The coefficients may vary arbitrarily with the physical bridge.
   The family even permits negative backward coefficients below-1;
   legality uses their actual even products, not a unit coefficient cap.
   All original queries, remote pairs, values and the true initial
   distance are proved. But its ENTIRE declared family satisfies

       V <= (5/9)^(2^(m-3)-1).                              (1)

   This is uniform over its terminal parameter and every permitted
   variable coefficient. Consequently its payoff divided by complete
   same-word K, complete same-word ray, or the UNaugmented full complex
   channel tends to zero. Its original-B normalized payoff also tends
   to zero. These comparisons already hold strictly for m>=9.

3. Removing the reserve growth in that rule by the exact constant
   choice kappa=s+1 is impossible. The ORIGINAL physical pair(3,8)
   has a positive two-cycle, including when eta=1. Reassigning values
   cannot fix this proposed repair. Intermediate uncapped policies
   are NOT excluded by this statement.

The signed construction is not a common added gradient, a fixed
triangle, a finite orthogonal sum of such triangles, or the prior
nonnegative one-tail law. Its positive correlations inside each H_2
block also violate the nonpositive-correlation hypothesis of C100.
At the beginning of the final H_2 block its support and value reserve
exceed the short-step caps used in C98/C99. Those unverified drafts
are recalled only to identify the changed hypotheses.

## 2. An explicit nested-normal geometry and all its reverse constraints

First take an arbitrary word with h_i>1 and eta>1. Write

    tau=eta-1,
    Ttail_i=tau+sum_(t=i)^(n-1) h_t,       0<=i<=n,
    d_i=h_i-1.

Choose finite numbers Ldual_i with

    Ldual_0>=...>=Ldual_n=1.

These are inputs, not unknown feasible Gram entries. In the orthonormal
basis e_0,...,e_n set

    rdual_n=e_n,
    rdual_i=rdual_(i+1)+sqrt(Ldual_i-Ldual_(i+1))*e_i,
    delta_i=Ttail_i/Ldual_i,
    y_i=delta_i*rdual_i,
    x_n=eta*e_n, g_n=e_n,
    g_i=(y_i-x_(i+1))/d_i,  x_i=y_i+g_i,       i=n-1,...,0. (2)

Every vector is real. The physical update is literal:
x_i-h_i*g_i=y_i-d_i*g_i=x_(i+1). The dependence of g_i includes
the full future position and the independent accumulated dual normal;
it is not a scalar multiple of g_(i+1) plus a fresh innovation.

Inductively, ||rdual_i||^2=Ldual_i and

    <rdual_i,g_j>=1                 for every j>=i.          (3)

Indeed rdual_i differs from rdual_(i+1) by a vector orthogonal to
the whole suffix. Thus it pairs to1 with every already constructed
future gradient, and

    <rdual_i,x_(i+1)>=eta+sum_(t>i)h_t=Ttail_i-d_i.

Using delta_i*Ldual_i=Ttail_i in(2) then proves(3) also for j=i.
In particular <y_i,g_i>=delta_i>=0. Prescribe formal values

    f_i=delta_i+||g_i||^2/2,
    x_*=g_*=f_*=0.

Direct expansion in the accepted convention gives

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<y_j,g_i-g_j>.                                   (4)

Thus Q_(j,i)=0 for every i<j, Q_(i,*)=0, and
Q_(*,i)=-delta_i. The reverse rows remain necessary and have NOT
been removed.

There is an exact scalar form of every remaining row. Put

    Adual_i=1/Ldual_i,  Delta_i=Adual_(i+1)-Adual_i>=0,
    Epair_(j,i)=Adual_j*(1-<rdual_j,g_i>),    i<j,
    Epair_(j,j)=0.

Expanding x_(i+1) as eta*g_n+sum_(t>i)h_t*g_t gives

    d_i*Epair_(j,i)
       =Ttail_i*(Adual_j-Adual_i)
          -sum_(k=i+1)^(j-1) h_k*Epair_(j,k).              (5)

This retains every earlier/future pair. In particular

    Epair_(2,1)=Ttail_1*Delta_1/d_1,
    Epair_(2,0)=[Ttail_0*Delta_0
                    +(h_0-Ttail_1/d_1)*Delta_1]/d_0,
    Q_(0,2)=-Ttail_2*Epair_(2,0).                          (6)

Equations(2)--(6) are an explicit geometric audit, not a promise that
arbitrary Ldual satisfies interpolation. They are not offered as a
free feasibility oracle for the main problem.

## 3. The entire positive-power policy fails an actual cycle

The natural concrete policy is

    Ldual_i=(Ttail_i/tau)^p,       p>0.                     (7)

It satisfies the required monotonicity, so the real-vector construction
exists for every p>0. It also includes horizon-dependent p and eta.
Nevertheless it is NOT an interpolable trajectory on the original H_m.

The first two physical steps are

    u=h_0=1+a,  v=h_1=1+beta,  d_0=a, d_1=beta.

Let P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t and Ttail_0=T. As a function of P, the inverse
normal size in(7) is Adual(P)=tau^p*(T-P)^(-p). Its derivative is
positive and strictly increasing on these intervals. Therefore

    Delta_0/u < Delta_1/v,       Delta_1>0.                (8)

More generally the non-strict version of(8), with Delta_1>0, holds
for any convex increasing profile on the first two physical intervals.

Substitute Delta_0<=u*Delta_1/v and Ttail_0=Ttail_1+u into(6):

    Q_(0,2) >= [Ttail_2*Delta_1/(a*beta*v)]
                 *[(v-u*beta)*Ttail_1-u*beta*(u+v)].        (9)

Every factor outside the bracket is positive. For m>=4,
a<1/2, beta<1, u<3/2, v<2, and Ttail_1>n-1>=14. Hence

    v-u*beta=1-a*beta>1/2,
    u*beta*(u+v)<21/4,
    (v-u*beta)*Ttail_1-u*beta*(u+v)>7/4>0.                 (10)

Thus Q_(0,2)>0 for every policy in(7), without any restriction on
the growth of p or eta with m. From(3),(4), Q_(2,1)=Q_(1,0)=0.
Consequently

                    Q_(0,2)+Q_(2,1)+Q_(1,0)>0.           (11)

The function-value terms cancel from this sum. Changing ALL sampled
values, choosing a different minimum value, or moving a minimizer
therefore cannot make these same points and gradients smoothly
convexly interpolable. It is an actual three-point cyclic failure,
not merely an inconvenient choice of projection-conjugate heights.

The p=0 boundary has Ldual_i=1 and g_i=e_n at every sample, as follows
by induction in(2). It is the constant-gradient Huber channel and
has no positive increment in(8). Nonconvex profiles of Adual, including
profiles with strongly unequal early increments, remain outside(9)'s
exclusion. The claim is not that all nested-normal geometries fail.

Here is the reason for trying a block repair next. In a one-tail
projection extension write g_i=-(kappa/d_i)g_(i+1)+v_i*e_i and force
<y_i,g_(i+1)-g_i>=0. The identities are

    delta_i=delta_(i+1)-(kappa-1)*||g_(i+1)||^2,
    v_i^2=(d_i+kappa)*delta_i/d_i^2,
    y_i=y_(i+1)+(1-kappa)g_(i+1)+d_i*v_i*e_i.             (12)

If kappa>1 and the next normal is also tied to a future gradient g_j
with <g_(i+1),g_j><||g_(i+1)||^2, then

    <y_i,g_j-g_i>
       =(1-kappa)*(<g_(i+1),g_j>-||g_(i+1)||^2)>0.

This diagnoses the unpriced remote row in the naive strong-negative
step. The next construction puts an ACTUAL H_2 holding block after
each bridge, retains its whole mass, and audits the resulting rows.

## 4. A legal signed law on every actual H_2 block and larger bridge

For the original word let

    s=sum H_2=3+2a+beta,
    Ccap=(s+1)/2,
    Nphase=2^(m-2)-1,
    Lcount=2^(m-3).

There are Nphase bridges and Nphase+1 blocks in the exact decomposition

    H_m=(H_2,b_0,H_2,b_1,...,b_(Nphase-1),H_2).

The bridge at physical index4j+3 is

    b_j=1+d_j,
    d_j=a*c^(2+nu_2(j+1)),       0<=j<Nphase,              (13)

where nu_2(k) is the exponent of2 dividing the positive integer k.
No word has been replaced by a compressed algorithm: the individual
queries inside each H_2 are supplied explicitly below. Formula(13)
uses the SAME enclosing a,c even in the smallest blocks.

Choose ANY eta>=1 and ANY sequence

    0<=kappa_j<=Ccap,       0<=j<Nphase.

These may depend on m and on each physical bridge separately. Put
rhold_j=s+1-kappa_j, so rhold_j>=Ccap>=kappa_j. Use the orthonormal
basis e_0,...,e_(Nphase). At the end of the last block set

    G_(Nphase)=e_(Nphase),
    Y_(Nphase)=(eta-1)*e_(Nphase),
    X_(Nphase)=eta*e_(Nphase),
    q_(Nphase)=1, delta_(Nphase)=eta-1,
    Znormal_(Nphase)=(eta-1)^2.

Construct backward for j=Nphase-1,...,0 by

    delta_j=delta_(j+1)+rhold_j*q_(j+1),
    v_j=sqrt((d_j+kappa_j)*delta_j)/d_j,
    t_j=-kappa_j/d_j,
    G_j=t_j*G_(j+1)+v_j*e_j,
    Y_j=Y_(j+1)+rhold_j*G_(j+1)+d_j*v_j*e_j,
    X_j=Y_j+G_j.                                         (14)

Here q_j=||G_j||^2 and Znormal_j=||Y_j||^2; their completely specified
scalar recurrences are

    q_j=[kappa_j^2*q_(j+1)+(d_j+kappa_j)*delta_j]/d_j^2,
    Znormal_j=Znormal_(j+1)+2*rhold_j*delta_(j+1)
                  +rhold_j^2*q_(j+1)+(d_j+kappa_j)*delta_j. (15)

The quantities under the square roots are positive: q_(j+1)>0 and
rhold_j>0 imply delta_j>0. The vectors therefore realize a PSD Gram
matrix in dimension Nphase+1. Direct multiplication gives

    <Y_j,G_j>=delta_j,
    <Y_j,G_(j+1)>=delta_j,
    X_j=X_(j+1)+s*G_(j+1)+b_j*G_j.                        (16)

For example the first identity uses
t_j*delta_j+d_j*v_j^2=delta_j. For the third, the coefficient identity
rhold_j+t_j=s+1+b_j*t_j and d_j+1=b_j suffice.

Write H_2=(u,v,u), where u=1+a and v=1+beta. Define remaining
block masses a_rem,0=s, a_rem,1=u+v, a_rem,2=u, a_rem,3=0.
For every phase j and r=0,1,2,3 provide the ORIGINAL physical sample

    x_(4j+r)=X_j+a_rem,r*G_j,
    g_(4j+r)=G_j,
    f_(4j+r)=delta_j+(a_rem,r+1/2)*q_j.                   (17)

The last sample4*Nphase+3 is precisely n=2^m-1. Within each block
subtracting its next physical step decreases a_rem by that step.
At its bridge, (16) gives

    x_(4j+3)-b_j*G_j=X_(j+1)+s*G_(j+1)=x_(4j+4).

Thus every physical update is correct. Different phases have distinct
gradients because v_j>0 gives a fresh nonzero coordinate. For strictly
positive kappa_j the adjacent phases have negative inner products;
within each physical H_2 block the correlations are positive.

## 5. All pairs, every intermediate query, and the one static function

Two estimates prove all the normal inequalities. First,

    q_j >= |t_j|*q_(j+1).                                (18)

Indeed, using delta_j>=rhold_j*q_(j+1) and rhold_j>=kappa_j,
the numerator of q_j-(kappa_j/d_j)*q_(j+1) is at least

    [kappa_j^2-kappa_j*d_j+(d_j+kappa_j)*kappa_j]
          *q_(j+1)=2*kappa_j^2*q_(j+1)>=0.

Fresh innovation orthogonality gives, for i<j,

    <G_i,G_j>=Ptail_(i,j)*q_j,
    Ptail_(i,j)=product_(k=i)^(j-1)t_k.                    (19)

Iterating(18) shows |<G_i,G_j>|<=q_i. This holds even when an individual
backward coefficient has magnitude greater than1.

Second, EVERY Ptail_(i,j)<=1. A negative product already has this
property. For an even number of factors, pair consecutive bridge
positions. In the ruler in(13) every adjacent pair has one level2
and one level at least3. Write d_low=a*c^2=beta*c and
d_next=a*c^3=c*d_low. For m>=4,

    d_low=lambda*(1-1/m^2)>2,
    c>12/5,
    d_low*d_next=c*d_low^2>48/5>9>Ccap^2.                 (20)

Here Ccap<3 follows from a<1/2,beta<1. Each paired absolute product
is at most Ccap^2/(d_low*d_next)<1. This proves the second estimate
without requiring |t_j|<=1 at every bridge.

At a phase end, all future normals hold by backward induction.
The next comparison is tied by(16). For k>j+1, subtract that tie:

    <Y_j,G_k-G_j>
      =<Y_(j+1),G_k-G_(j+1)>
          +rhold_j*<G_(j+1),G_k-G_(j+1)> <=0.             (21)

The first term is the induction hypothesis and the second is
nonpositive by(18),(19). At an intermediate query in this phase,
the normal is Y_j+w*G_j, with 0<=w<=s. Its future comparisons add
w*<G_j,G_k-G_j><=0, so they also hold.

For a past phase i<j, write G_i=Ptail_(i,j)*G_j+z, with z in
span{e_i,...,e_(j-1)}. Both Y_j and G_j are orthogonal to z. Therefore
the corresponding normal comparison at EVERY query in phase j is

    <Y_j+w*G_j,G_i-G_j>
       =(Ptail_(i,j)-1)*(delta_j+w*q_j)<=0.               (22)

Same-phase comparisons are zero. The comparison with the zero
gradient is -(delta_j+w*q_j)<=0. Equations(21),(22) therefore cover
ALL original pairs, including pairs in remote recursive children,
and every intermediate holding query.

Now define a SINGLE function for the whole word by

    Cblock=conv{0,G_0,...,G_(Nphase)},
    Fblock(x)=max_(z in Cblock){<x,z>-||z||^2/2}.           (23)

Completing the square identifies the maximizer with the Euclidean
projection P_Cblock(x). The proved normal inequalities imply
P_Cblock(x_(4j+r))=G_j at each sample in(17).

For completeness, the projection inequalities at two points x,z give
<P(x)-P(z),x-z> >= ||P(x)-P(z)||^2. Hence P is1-Lipschitz.
Comparing the two maximizing affine functions in(23) gives

    <P(x),u> <= Fblock(x+u)-Fblock(x) <= <P(x+u),u>.

The difference from the left expression is between0 and ||u||^2.
Thus Fblock is differentiable with gradient P, and is convex and
everywhere finite. Its gradient is1-Lipschitz. Its values at the
samples are precisely(17).

Using(4), every physical Q equals the proved normal comparison.
In particular all optimum rows are retained: Q_(i,*)=0 and
Q_(*,i)=-(delta_j+a_rem,r*q_j)<=0. There is no deletion of an
incoming terminal row, an old query, or a cross-block pair.

## 6. Exact minimum set and paid radius

The minimum value of(23) is0 and its ENTIRE minimum set is

    Cblock^polar={z:<z,G_j><=0 for every j}.                (24)

For z in that cone every maximand is nonpositive, with value0 at
the zero vertex. If z is outside the cone, some <z,G_j>>0; a
sufficiently small positive multiple of that vertex has positive
maximand. This proves(24) in both directions.

The initial point telescopes from the actual physical updates:

    x_0=eta*G_(Nphase)+sum_(i<n)h_i*g_i.

It is a positive combination of gradient vertices. Hence <x_0,z><=0
for every z in(24), and

    ||x_0-z||^2>=||x_0||^2,
    dist(x_0,argmin Fblock)^2=||x_0||^2.

The exact radius and terminal payoff are therefore

    Rblock0_sq=Znormal_0+2*(s+1)*delta_0+(s+1)^2*q_0,
    Vblock=(2eta-1)/Rblock0_sq.                            (25)

Equations(14),(15),(25) are finite explicit scalar and vector laws;
no unknown feasible matrix or function-value optimization is hidden.
The state Znormal is a squared normal length, NOT the ambient
dimension. Multiplying Fblock by any L>0 and using h_i/L preserves
the entire trajectory and normalized payoff.

Isometric embeddings leave the radius unchanged. A finite orthogonal
sum of these functions has a product minimum set and payoff equal
to a radius-squared-weighted average of its component payoffs. The
bound below consequently covers these embeddings and finite sums too.

The extreme allowed constant choice kappa_j=Ccap demonstrates that
the construction genuinely goes beyond unit-magnitude backward tails.
For m>=4, beta>=3/4 and c<25/8 imply a>6/25, whence
Ccap>2+3/8+6/25>5/2>d_low. Thus t_j<-1 at every level2 bridge.
Equations(18)--(22), not an unproved correlation heuristic, ensure
that this choice is legal.

## 7. Uniform obstruction for the whole declared signed family

The price is forced by the repeated low bridges. There are exactly
Lcount=2^(m-3) level2 bridges, at even phase indices
j=0,2,...,2*Lcount-2, and Nphase=2*Lcount-1.

All delta_j>=delta_(j+1). At every level2 bridge,

    q_j >= delta_j/d_low.

If j>=2, the preceding phase transition then satisfies

    delta_(j-1)=delta_j+rhold_(j-1)*q_j
       >= (1+Ccap/d_low)*delta_j.

The last bridge is level2 and
delta_(Nphase-1)>=eta-1+Ccap. Iterating the previous inequality
across all but the first low bridge, retaining the intervening
nondecreases, gives

    delta_0 >= (1+Ccap/d_low)^(Lcount-1)*(eta-1+Ccap).

Since Ccap>2 and d_low<lambda<5/2,

    delta_0 >= (9/5)^(Lcount-1)*(eta-1+Ccap).              (26)

    Vblock <= (5/9)^(Lcount-1)*(2tau+1)/(2*(tau+Ccap))
           <= (5/9)^(Lcount-1).                           (27)

This proves(1) uniformly over EVERY coefficient sequence in the
stated interval, even when all parameters vary with m. It is not
a claim about every possible signed projection geometry.

## 8. Complete same-word comparisons and ORIGINAL-B normalization

Let Huber_m=1/(1+2S_m). The complete single-cut channel from accepted
b98bb807d514e80d is

    K_n(h)=max{1/(1+2sum h),
       max_(j<n) (h_j-1)_+^2/[(1+sum_(i<j)h_i)^2
                                      *(1+2sum_(i>j)h_i)]}.

The complete ray channel F_ray_n from accepted1fca3e5dd555cb4a retains
ALL feasible ordered checkpoint subsets, including the empty subset
and every single checkpoint, with its remote offsets, accumulated
areas, and full terminal maximization. Consequently

    Huber_m <= K_n(H_m) <= F_ray_n(H_m).                   (28)

No particular checkpoint subset is substituted for the full ray.
It is enough for the comparison that its complete maximum includes
these admissible witnesses; equality on H_m is not asserted.

For the full complex channel use exactly the objects in accepted
dfde2fa326c908bf: Poly_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t*z), points xi_i=Poly_i(z),
gradients gamma_i=z*Poly_i(z), and the zero optimum sample. The
legal set D_h retains every directed simple cycle C, including

    (Re z-|z|^2)*Energy_C >= 2*|Im z*Area_C|.

Here Energy_C=sum_(j->i in C)|xi_i-xi_j|^2 and
Area_C=sum_(j->i in C)Im(conj(xi_j)*xi_i). The edge weight is
<gamma_j,xi_i-xi_j>+||gamma_i-gamma_j||^2/2; ell_n is the maximum
weight of a directed path n->*; Gap_h(z)=-2ell_n. Write

    Cfull(h)=sup_(z in D_h) Gap_h(z).

This is the unaugmented FULL schedule-dependent channel with initial
point1 and specified minimizer0. It is not the universal lens.

The following elementary same-word lower bound is useful:

                   Cfull(h)>=1/[2*(1+2sum h)].            (29)

To prove it for any nonnegative word of mass S, let theta=1/(2S+1)
and P=product_(i<n)(1-h_i*theta)>0. Real theta belongs to the full

    F'(x)=x          for x<=theta*P,
          theta*P    for theta*P<=x<=P,

    F(0)=0.

It has unique minimizer0 and realizes all those points and gradients.
In the complex plane one may add (Im x)^2/2 to F(Re x).
Integration gives normalized terminal gap

theta/2, because
(2-theta)*(1+theta)^2=2+3theta-theta^3>=2 for0<=theta<=1.

Write Ucap_m=(5/9)^(Lcount-1). Equations(27)--(29) imply

    C_0^bench=B_0=1,
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,

No balanced-tree surrogate or changed enclosing parameter has been

## 9. The zero-growth signed repair fails physical pair(3,8)

The bound(26) suggests increasing kappa until rhold=0. Test precisely

                 kappa_j=s+1=:kappa_full  for every j.     (34)

Apply the SAME explicit recurrences(14),(15) without the cap. The
radicands are still nonnegative: delta_j=eta-1=tau for every phase,
and v_j^2=(d_j+kappa_full)*tau/d_j^2. The physical recursions also

Since rhold=0, the end normals satisfy

    G_0=Pbad*G_2+z, z in span{e_0,e_1},

The strict positivity includes eta=1: then q_2>0 because the

The two-cycle sum in(36) is independent of values. Even freely

## 10. Adversarial checks, literature, and exact remaining scope

The geometric proofs retain every physical query inside each H_2,
both orientations of all cross-block pairs, the optimum, and the
actual polar minimum set. Individual backward coefficients<-1 are
permitted and explicitly checked. The legal-family estimate is

approximation, numerical sign test, or a prescribed value assignment:

The new legal family is NOT all signed Markov laws. It retains a

The sufficient cap kappa_j<=Ccap is not asserted necessary. General

## 1. Statement and original benchmark

## 2. All-split comparison with primitive capacities

We prove jointly that

  G(a,lambda d)<=lambda Omega(a,d)   for all a,d>=0.       (6)

When a=d=0 both sides are zero. Otherwise put w=Omega(a,d)>0 and t=a/w.
The equation w^2-(a+d)w-ad=0 gives

  0<=t<=1,    d/w=(1-t)/(1+t).

The larger root of P(v)=v^2-(4a+lambda d)v+4a^2 is G(a,lambda d).
Since lambda^2=2lambda+1, substitution and expansion give

  P(lambda w)/w^2
    =lambda^2-4lambda t-lambda^2*(1-t)/(1+t)+4t^2
    =4t*(t-1/sqrt(2))^2/(1+t) >=0.

Also w>=a+d, so lambda w>=lambda(a+d)>=2a+lambda d/2,
the vertex of P. A quadratic of positive leading coefficient is
nonnegative to the right of its vertex only at or beyond its larger
root. This proves (6), including either zero argument.

## 4. Every fixed-first-row re-selection, with all entries explicit

## 7. A scope counterexample: the remainder restriction is not lossless

For the actual word h=(1,1,1,1), set, for i=0,1,2,3,

    Lambda_(i,i+1)=2(i+1)^2,
    Lambda_(i+1,i)=2(i+1)(i+2),

that rank-one remainder has M00=0. Thus the declared remainder choice
excludes a valid full primitive word even after arbitrary re-selection.

## 1. The original full-space certificate and the declared factor class

## 3. Necessity of the prefix formulas for EVERY positive representation

It is necessary to show that the familiar factor recurrence covers

For the induction step let 1<=k<r and abbreviate

 P=P_k, R=R_k, Y=R_(k+1), q=U_k/U_(k-1)>0.

The preceding v formula and positivity give P>R>1. The recurrences
and the product p_k=U_(k-1)D_k give

 u_k=(u_(k-1)+h_(k-1))/q,
 v_(k-1)=[p_(k+1)/(p_k q)](h_k+v_k).

The induction hypothesis supplies

 u_(k-1)+h_(k-1)=(P+R)/(1+R),
 v_(k-1)=(P-R)/(R-1).

By(3.1), v_k=u_k+delta_k with

 delta_k=2(P+t_k)/(Y^2-1)-1+t_k,
 p_(k+1)(h_k+delta_k)=P+RY.

Eliminating u_k and v_k gives the following quadratic for q:

 (1+R)(P-R)q^2-2(P+RY)q
                   -(Y^2-1)(P+R)/(1+R)=0.              (3.3)

Its two roots are exactly

 (P+R)(1+Y)/[(1+R)(P-R)],        (1-Y)/(1+R).

This follows by using
(P+RY)^2+(P^2-R^2)(Y^2-1)=(PY+R)^2
in the quadratic formula. The second root is negative, whereas q>0.
Thus the first is the only possible ratio. Inserting it gives
u_k=(P-R)/(1+Y). Adding delta_k gives the v formula, since

 (P-t_kY)(Y-1)+2(P+t_k)+(t_k-1)(Y^2-1)
                        =(Y+1)(P+1+t_k-Y).

This finishes the induction. Consequently every representation obeys

 1<R_k<P_k for 1<=k<r,
 U_k/U_(k-1)=(P_k+R_k)(1+R_(k+1))
                /[(1+R_k)(P_k-R_k)],                  (3.4)
 D_(k+1)/D_k=(P_k-R_k)(R_(k+1)-1)
                /[(R_k-1)(P_k+R_k)].                  (3.5)

The strict prefix inequalities follow from v_(k-1)>0. No uniqueness
of the full unrestricted primitive certificate has been claimed; only
the ratios inside the explicitly declared two-sequence family are forced.

## 4. Exact free-word construction and all sign conditions

For completeness, the converse also holds. Take arbitrary positive
excesses t_0,...,t_(r-1) satisfying R_r=P_r and 1<R_k<P_k at every
proper nonempty prefix. Normalize U_0=1, define U by(3.4), and set
D_k=(R_k^2-1)/(2U_(k-1)). Formula(3.5) follows by division.

For each 1<=k<r, all factor signs are nonnegative exactly when

 t_k >= (P_k-R_k)/(P_k+R_k-2),
 t_k(P_k-R_k-2) <= P_k+R_k.                              (4.1)

The denominator of the first bound is positive. Inserting
R_(k+1)=R_k/t_k into U_k/U_(k-1)>=1 and D_(k+1)/D_k<=1 proves
these two equivalences by multiplication by positive denominators.
The second inequality is left in the displayed form: division by
P_k-R_k-2, whose sign may change, would be incorrect without a case split.

To check the full identity in this converse, the u formula(3.2) follows
forward from its recurrence and(3.4). The v formula follows backward

 h_k+v_k=(P_k+R_k)/(R_(k+1)-1),
 [D_(k+1)/D_k](h_k+v_k)=(P_k-R_k)/(R_k-1).

For each k set R=R_(k+1),P=P_k,t=t_k. Then

 p_(k+1)(v_k-u_k)
  =[(R+1)(P+1+t-R)-(R-1)(P-tR)]/2
  =P+t+(t-1)(R^2-1)/2.

Adding p_(k+1)(1-t) proves the cut flow(3.1). Differences give
d_i=h_i and total flow zero gives d_r=-s. Equation(2.3) proves every
diagonal match, and Section2 proves every mixed match. Thus(1.4)
holds on ALL original formal coordinates, the original array is

There is no uncomputed PSD test. There are only the explicit scalar

For the initially proposed genuinely free parameterization, choose

the final excess be the unique positive root

              t^2+(P+1)t-R=0.                            (4.2)

This is exactly R/t=P+1+t, so it imposes R_r=P_r and nothing about

## 5. The new consequence: every contiguous block is product-admissible

For each nonempty contiguous interval I=[l,k) of physical indices,
define its mass, capacity, and product by

 H_I=sum_(i=l)^(k-1)h_i,
 K_I=1+H_I,
 q_I=product_(i=l)^(k-1)t_i.

We prove

                     K_I q_I>=1.                        (5.1)

Equality holds for the whole word. If k<r, the inequality is strict.
This is a consequence of the declared factor class, not a necessary
condition asserted for every primitive word.

For l=0, q_I=1/R_k, and(5.1) is P_k>=R_k, already proved.
Now assume 1<=l<k<=r, and write

 P=P_l>1, R=R_l>1, H=H_I>0, q=q_I,
 P_k=P+H, R_k=R/q,
 b_j=(P_j-R_j)/(R_j-1) for 1<=j<=r.

Formula(3.2) identifies b_j=v_(j-1), including b_r=0. The weighted
tail sum defining v_(l-1) decomposes exactly as

 b_l=sum_(i=l)^(k-1) h_i D_(i+1)/D_l +(D_k/D_l)b_k.

By D monotonicity and b_k>=0 this gives b_l<=H+b_k. Since
b_l+1=(P-1)/(R-1) and b_k+1=q(P+H-1)/(R-q), both denominators
are positive. Multiplication and cancellation yield

                 q>=1-H(R-1)/(P-1).                     (5.2)

The other endpoint condition R_k<=P_k gives R<=q(P+H). Combining
this with(5.2), whose right side decreases in R, yields

 q>=1-H[q(P+H)-1]/(P-1),
 q[P-1+H(P+H)]>=P-1+H.

Here P-1+H(P+H)=(H+1)(P-1+H). Dividing by P-1+H>0 proves
q>=1/(1+H), which is(5.1). If k<r, then R_k<P_k, so the second
inequality is strict and(5.1) is strict as claimed.

For a suffix [l,r), equality in(5.1) holds exactly when
D_l=D_(l+1)=...=D_r. Indeed the terminal prefix equality is exact,
and equality in the tail estimate with b_r=0 requires every positive
summand h_i D_(i+1)/D_l to have D_(i+1)=D_l. This also checks the
possibility of zero multipliers on the boundary of the factor class.

## 6. Exact extremal theorem for the larger hereditary scalar class

This section is a separate elementary proof, included here in full.
For any r>=1, call a positive vector t=(t_0,...,t_(r-1)) admissible
if, with h_i=1+t_i, it satisfies

 K_I q_I>=1 for EVERY nonempty contiguous I,
 A product_(i<r)t_i=1,       A=1+sum_(i<r)(1+t_i).        (6.1)

The empty word has capacity1. Define the benchmark kernel and recurrence
as in accepted04219554e41d9750:

 Omega(a,c)=(a+c+sqrt((a+c)^2+4ac))/2,
 C_0=1,
 C_r=max_(0<=j<r)Omega(C_j,C_(r-j-1)).                   (6.2)

We prove that the maximum capacity over(6.1) is exactly C_r. Moreover
every capacity maximizer admits a recursive maximizing split at a single
bridge index. This describes maximizers of(6.1), not every admissible
vector and not every primitive certificate.

First, maxima exist whenever the admissible set is nonempty. A singleton
condition is t_i(2+t_i)>=1, hence t_i>=c_*=sqrt(2)-1>0. Global equality
implies

 1=A product_i t_i >= A t_j c_*^(r-1) >= t_j c_*^(r-1).

Thus c_*<=t_j<=c_*^(1-r). The conditions are closed on this compact
box. The capacity is continuous, so it attains a maximum.

Fix such a maximizing vector. An interval is called tight when K_I q_I=1.
For notational convenience set K_empty=q_empty=1. For each interval put

 F_I=log(K_I)+sum_(i in I)log(t_i),

so F_I>=0, and tightness is F_I=0. Two tight intervals cannot overlap
without one containing the other. Indeed, if their consecutive left-only,
common, and right-only pieces have physical masses a>0,b>0,c>0, then

 F_I+F_J-F_(I union J)-F_(I intersection J)
 =log[(1+a+b)(1+b+c)/((1+b)(1+a+b+c))]>0,                (6.3)

because the numerator minus denominator inside the logarithm is ac>0.
If I,J were both tight, their left side would be nonpositive by(6.1),
a contradiction. Likewise two adjacent disjoint nonempty tight intervals
of masses a,c cannot occur: their union is an interval, and

 F_I+F_J-F_(I union J)=log[(1+a)(1+c)/(1+a+c)]>0.

Consider now the inclusion-maximal PROPER tight intervals. The first
observation makes them disjoint; the second says any two are separated
by at least one index outside them. Call an index uncovered when it is
in none of these maximal proper intervals, equivalently in no proper
tight interval at all.

There must be at least one uncovered index. Otherwise the proper maximal
intervals would cover the word. A single one cannot cover it because it
is proper, and multiple disjoint ones would then have an adjacent pair,
which was just ruled out.

There cannot be two uncovered indices u,v. To prove this, perturb only
t_u,t_v by t_u -> t_u+epsilon, t_v -> t_v-epsilon. Choose a sufficiently
small nonzero epsilon with epsilon(t_v-t_u)<=0. Positivity persists,
the total sum and A remain unchanged, every proper tight interval is
unchanged, and all other proper interval inequalities remain strict by
continuity and finiteness. But

 (t_u+epsilon)(t_v-epsilon)
     =t_u t_v+epsilon(t_v-t_u)-epsilon^2<t_u t_v.

The global product condition therefore becomes strictly less than1.
Starting at this perturbed vector, increase t_u alone by a positive
amount delta until global equality is restored. Such a finite delta
exists: the global product times A is a strictly increasing continuous
function of t_u and tends to infinity as t_u tends to infinity. Every
proper interval expression is nondecreasing under this increase, so all
its inequalities remain valid. The resulting admissible vector has
capacity A+delta>A, contradicting maximality.

There is therefore exactly ONE uncovered index, say j. All indices to
its left, if any, constitute a single maximal proper tight interval,
because multiple maximal intervals would need another uncovered index
between them. The same holds on its right. Consequently the left word
[0,j) and the right word [j+1,r) are each either empty or saturated
admissible words. Let their capacities be a,c and let d=t_j>0. Their
products are 1/a,1/c. The total capacity and saturation read

                  A=a+c+d,       A d=ac.                (6.4)

Thus A=Omega(a,c). Induction on r gives a<=C_j and c<=C_(r-j-1).
The kernel is increasing in both arguments, so

                  A<=Omega(C_j,C_(r-j-1))<=C_r.         (6.5)

This proves the upper bound for every admissible vector, because A was
a global maximizer. In an equality case strict monotonicity of Omega
for positive arguments forces the two children also to be maximizers,
which proves the asserted recursive structure of maximizers.

For completeness the bound is attained within the scalar class. Join
two saturated admissible child words of capacities a,c by h_bridge=1+d,
where d>0 solves d(a+c+d)=ac. An interval inside a child is admissible.
For an interval crossing the bridge, its left suffix and right prefix
have capacities x<=a,y<=c, where an empty portion has capacity1.
Its product is at least d/(xy), and its capacity is x+y+d. Because

 xy/(x+y+d) <= ac/(a+c+d)=d,

the interval is admissible. The displayed monotonicity follows directly
from the partial derivatives y(y+d)/(x+y+d)^2 and x(x+d)/(x+y+d)^2,
which are positive. Full saturation follows from d/(ac)=1/(a+c+d).
Starting from empty children and using a maximizing split in(6.2) now
constructs a saturated admissible word of capacity C_r. These are also
the actual original primitive compositions supplied by the accepted
certificate join. No auxiliary continuous phase or different recurrence
has replaced the original all-split C recurrence.

No assertion of a uniform positive gap over the whole factor family is

The full primitive cone allows M_prim>=0 on ALL R^(r+1). The class

 V_h+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij
                  =<M_prim,Gram(g_0,...,g_r)>.

Consequently, on writing mu_ij=Lambda_ji/2, zero remainder and flow

only as an auxiliary placeholder. For EVERY 0<=i<j<=r define

 mu_ij=(U_i-U_(i-1))(D_j+t_j D_(j+1)),

There is no deleted off-diagonal pair. Membership requires ALL entries

## 2. A necessary lemma for the ENTIRE zero-remainder cone

This section assumes only(1.3), not(1.4). Define auxiliary net flow
and the two incoming sums by

 d_i=sum_(j!=i)(mu_ij-mu_ji),
 I_i=sum_(j<i)mu_ji, J_i=sum_(j>i)mu_ji.

The function coefficients in(1.3) give d_i=h_i for i<r and d_r=-s.
At a nonterminal i the squared-difference terms have coefficient
-d_i-2I_i-2J_i on ||g_i||^2. A trajectory term can contribute to
this diagonal only from Qbar_(j,i) with j>i; their total contribution
is 2h_i J_i. Matching the diagonal of V_h therefore gives

           t_i J_i-I_i=(1-t_i^2)/2,  0<=i<r.            (2.1)

If 0<h_i<=1, then -1<t_i<=0. The left side of(2.1) is nonpositive,
because I_i,J_i>=0, while its right side is strictly positive. This
is impossible. Thus every positive step is strictly greater than1.

If h_i=0, then t_i=-1 and(2.1) gives I_i+J_i=0. Nonnegativity makes
EVERY incoming mu entry at i zero. Since d_i=h_i=0, every outgoing
entry at i is also zero. The corresponding entire original Lambda row
AND column vanish. This is an algebraic assertion on the full array;
it does not impose equality between any two formal gradients or values.

There is also an exact balance restriction. Substitute the actual scalar
unit quadratic f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1 into(1.3). Its gradients equal its
positions, and every Qbar_ij is zero. Put

 v_0=1, v_(i+1)=(1-h_i)v_i=-t_i v_i.

For these samples the primitive energy is

 V_h=sum_(i<r)h_i(2-h_i)v_i^2-s(s+2)v_r^2
     =sum_(i<r)(v_i^2-v_(i+1)^2)-s(s+2)v_r^2
     =1-A^2 v_r^2.

It must vanish, so

                 A product_(i<r)|t_i|=1.                (2.2)

Here no factorization, irreducibility, or rank assumption has entered.
For positive steps t_i>0; zero steps have |t_i|=1. This necessary
lemma applies to the full ZERO-remainder cone only. It does not extend
to an arbitrary positive semidefinite remainder.

## 3. Finite signed factors collapse to positive factors with zero padding

Assume now(1.4) as well. If s=0, every step is zero; Section2 makes
every multiplier zero, and A=1. Hence suppose s>0.

At the terminal, the total incoming auxiliary weight telescopes to

 I_r=sum_(i<r)mu_ir=U_(r-1)D_r.

The terminal squared-gradient coefficient in sum mu Qbar is s-2I_r.
Matching -sA gives

             U_(r-1)D_r=s(s+2)/2>0.                    (3.1)

Changing both factor sequences to their negatives preserves every
entry in(1.4). Make this change if necessary so that D_r>0. Every
terminal entry then gives

 mu_ir=(U_i-U_(i-1))D_r>=0.

Thus U_-1=0<=U_0<=...<=U_(r-1), with U_(r-1)>0.

Let a be the first index with U_a>0. If i<a, both U_i and U_(i-1)
vanish, so every entry incident to i in(1.4) is zero. Its flow gives
h_i=0. At i=a the entry mu_ar=U_aD_r is strictly positive, so this
row cannot be a zero-step row by Section2. Hence h_a>1 and t_a>0.
For every j>a the actual entry

          mu_ja=t_a U_a(D_j-D_(j+1))>=0

forces D_j>=D_(j+1). Consequently

 D_(a+1)>=D_(a+2)>=...>=D_r>0,
 U_i>=U_a>0 for every i>=a.                             (3.2)

All ACTIVE factors are already positive. Arbitrary D entries preceding
this active suffix cannot affect the array, since all earlier U entries
vanish.

Consider a zero step at i>=a. It has every incident multiplier zero
by Section2. Its terminal edge gives U_i=U_(i-1). Since i>a, the
edge mu_ia=t_aU_a(D_i-D_(i+1)) gives D_i=D_(i+1). A zero step
therefore creates exact plateaus in BOTH active factor sequences.

Let m be the number of positive steps. List their original indices as

 iota(0)<...<iota(m-1),  and set iota(m)=r.

Define the compressed word and factors by

 hhat_j=h_(iota(j)), Uhat_j=U_(iota(j)) for 0<=j<m,
 Dhat_j=D_(iota(j)) for 1<=j<=m,
 Uhat_-1=Dhat_(m+1)=0.

All Uhat and Dhat in their nonboundary ranges are strictly positive.
The U and D plateaus imply that, on every retained ordered pair, the
original formula(1.4) is EXACTLY the same formula for hhat,Uhat,Dhat.
For example U_(iota(j)-1)=Uhat_(j-1), including the first-index zero,
and D_(iota(j)+1)=Dhat_(j+1). The latter identity includes trailing
zero steps and the retained original terminal r.

Every removed row and column was already identically zero. Also its
step is zero, so x_(iota(j)) is the GD position for the compressed word
using its retained formal gradients. Restricting the polynomial identity
to the retained variables proves(1.3) for the compressed word. Conversely
its identity extends to the full original space with zero rows at the
unused independent coordinates. NO quotient relation between gradients
at duplicated positions is used anywhere.

This proves the forward reduction. Its converse is explicit: starting
from any positive-factor word, insert zero steps, copy the neighboring
U and D values across each inserted zero index, put U=0 before the
first active index, and choose the unused leading D entries arbitrarily.
Then every inserted row and column is zero and all retained entries are
unchanged. Thus the enlarged class is exactly the positive-factor
free-word class padded with arbitrary zero steps, apart from irrelevant
factor gauges and unused leading factor values.

## 4. Joint positive-factor capacity proof: coefficient and prefix identities

For this section let the positive compressed length be q>=1, and drop
hats. Thus h_i=1+t_i with t_i>0, U_i,D_j>0 in their nonboundary ranges,
and(1.3)--(1.4) hold with r replaced by q and with U_-1=D_(q+1)=t_q=0.
Nonnegative entries imply

                 U_i>=U_(i-1), D_j>=D_(j+1).             (4.1)

The first implication follows from the terminal entries. The second
follows from mu_(j,0)=t_0U_0(D_j-D_(j+1)). Conversely(4.1) makes
all entries of(1.4) nonnegative when t,U,D are positive.

For i<j, the two telescoping sums are

 sum_(a<=i)mu_(a,j)=U_i(D_j+t_jD_(j+1)),
 sum_(a>j)mu_(a,i)=(U_(i-1)+t_iU_i)D_(j+1).

The coefficient of <g_i,g_j> in sum mu Qbar is

 2(mu_ij+mu_ji)-2h_iU_i(D_j+t_jD_(j+1))
                    +2h_j(U_(i-1)+t_iU_i)D_(j+1),

where h_q=1 is an unused auxiliary value. Expanding(1.4) makes this
coefficient zero for every pair; at j=q its last term is zero.
This is a variable-step identity on the entire formal space.

Put p_0=0 and p_k=U_(k-1)D_k for 1<=k<=q. Here

 I_i=U_(i-1)(D_i+t_iD_(i+1)),
 J_i=(U_(i-1)+t_iU_i)D_(i+1),

with I_0=0. Hence t_iJ_i-I_i=t_i^2p_(i+1)-p_i. Section2 and the
terminal diagonal yield

 t_i^2(2p_(i+1)+1)=2p_i+1,
 2p_q+1=A^2.                                          (4.2)

Define prefix capacity and reciprocal product by

 P_k=1+sum_(i<k)(1+t_i),
 R_k=product_(i<k)t_i^(-1), P_0=R_0=1.

Then

 p_k=(R_k^2-1)/2>0 for 1<=k<=q,
 R_q=P_q=A.                                           (4.3)

In particular every nonempty prefix has R_k>1, even if some individual
excess t_i is greater than1.

Define the normalized weighted prefix and suffix sums

 u_k=(sum_(i<k)h_iU_i)/U_k,
 v_k=(sum_(j=k+2)^q h_(j-1)D_j)/D_(k+1), 0<=k<q.

Outgoing cut weight across {0,...,k} is p_(k+1)(1+v_k):
sum_(j>k)(D_j+t_jD_(j+1))=D_(k+1)+sum_(j>=k+2)h_(j-1)D_j.
Incoming cut weight is p_(k+1)(t_k+u_k). The cut flow is therefore

 p_(k+1)(1-t_k+v_k-u_k)=P_(k+1)-1.                    (4.4)

We prove, for EVERY positive representation,

 u_k=(P_k-R_k)/(1+R_(k+1)),
 v_k=(P_(k+1)-R_(k+1))/(R_(k+1)-1).                    (4.5)

At k=0 the first formula is u_0=0. Inserting t_0=1/R_1 and
p_1=(R_1^2-1)/2 into(4.4) gives the second. For k<q-1 the defining
tail sum is positive, so the formula implies P_(k+1)>R_(k+1).

For induction let 1<=k<q and abbreviate
P=P_k,R=R_k,Y=R_(k+1),z=U_k/U_(k-1)>0. The preceding tail gives
P>R>1. Recurrence and the p products give

 u_k=(u_(k-1)+h_(k-1))/z,
 v_(k-1)=[p_(k+1)/(p_k z)](h_k+v_k).

The induction hypothesis makes

 u_(k-1)+h_(k-1)=(P+R)/(1+R),
 v_(k-1)=(P-R)/(R-1).

By(4.4), v_k=u_k+delta_k, where

 delta_k=2(P+t_k)/(Y^2-1)-1+t_k,
 p_(k+1)(h_k+delta_k)=P+RY.

Elimination gives the quadratic

 (1+R)(P-R)z^2-2(P+RY)z
                  -(Y^2-1)(P+R)/(1+R)=0.               (4.6)

Its roots are

 (P+R)(1+Y)/[(1+R)(P-R)],  (1-Y)/(1+R).

To check them, the discriminant calculation reduces to
(P+RY)^2+(P^2-R^2)(Y^2-1)=(PY+R)^2. The second root is negative,
so the first is forced by z>0. It gives the asserted u formula.
For the v formula use t_kY=R and the identity

 (P-t_kY)(Y-1)+2(P+t_k)+(t_k-1)(Y^2-1)
                      =(Y+1)(P+1+t_k-Y).

This completes the induction, including v_(q-1)=0. Thus

                  1<R_k<P_k,  1<=k<q.                  (4.7)

The forced ratios, useful for auditing every original sign, are

 U_k/U_(k-1)=(P_k+R_k)(1+R_(k+1))
                  /[(1+R_k)(P_k-R_k)],
 D_(k+1)/D_k=(P_k-R_k)(R_(k+1)-1)
                  /[(R_k-1)(P_k+R_k)].                 (4.8)

Together with the positive denominators in(4.7), their exact sign
conditions U_k>=U_(k-1),D_(k+1)<=D_k are equivalently

 t_k>=(P_k-R_k)/(P_k+R_k-2),
 t_k(P_k-R_k-2)<=P_k+R_k.                              (4.9)

The second inequality is deliberately not divided by its possibly
negative coefficient. No equality pattern between different steps has
been assumed. One can independently choose t_0,...,t_(q-2)>0 and set
the last excess to the unique positive root of
t^2+(P_(q-1)+1)t-R_(q-1)=0; this enforces only terminal balance.
Equations(4.7),(4.9) remain necessary sign tests on that free word.

## 5. Every contiguous positive-step interval is product-admissible

For a nonempty interval I=[l,k) in the compressed positive word put

 H_I=sum_(i=l)^(k-1)h_i, K_I=1+H_I,
 q_I=product_(i=l)^(k-1)t_i.

We prove

                  K_I q_I>=1,                           (5.1)

with strict inequality whenever k<q, and equality for the whole word.
For l=0 this is P_k>=R_k, including(4.7).

For 1<=l<k<=q write P=P_l,R=R_l,H=H_I,z=q_I. Let
b_j=(P_j-R_j)/(R_j-1)=v_(j-1), so b_j>=0 and b_q=0. Splitting
the actual weighted tail and using D monotonicity yields

 b_l=sum_(i=l)^(k-1)h_iD_(i+1)/D_l+(D_k/D_l)b_k
                                             <=H+b_k.

Here b_l+1=(P-1)/(R-1), b_k+1=z(P+H-1)/(R-z), and both denominators
are positive because R_l,R_k>1. Multiplication and cancellation give

                    z>=1-H(R-1)/(P-1).                  (5.2)

The endpoint inequality R_k<=P_k is R<=z(P+H). Inserting it into
the decreasing right side of(5.2) gives

 z[P-1+H(P+H)]>=P-1+H.

Since P-1+H(P+H)=(H+1)(P-1+H), this proves z>=1/(1+H).
If k<q the endpoint inequality is strict, giving strictness in(5.1).
This is a theorem about the declared factors, not about every original
zero-remainder array.

## 6. Exact scalar extremum of the hereditary relaxation

For any length q>=1 consider positive t_i, h_i=1+t_i satisfying

 (1+sum_(i in I)h_i) product_(i in I)t_i>=1
                         for EVERY nonempty contiguous I,
 A product_(i<q)t_i=1, A=1+sum_(i<q)h_i.                (6.1)

The empty word has capacity1. Define the ORIGINAL benchmark by

 Omega(a,c)=(a+c+sqrt((a+c)^2+4ac))/2,
 C_0=1, C_q=max_(0<=j<q)Omega(C_j,C_(q-j-1)).             (6.2)

The maximum capacity in(6.1) is exactly C_q. Moreover every maximizer
has a recursive maximizing split at one bridge index. The following
argument proves the statement without importing an unverified premise.

The set is compact when nonempty. Its singleton conditions give
t_i>=c_*=sqrt(2)-1>0. Global equality gives
1=A product_i t_i>=t_j c_*^(q-1), so t_j<=c_*^(1-q). The constraints
are closed on this bounded positive box, and A is continuous.

Fix a maximizer. Write F_I=log(1+sum_I h_i)+sum_I log t_i, and set
F_empty=0. Call an interval tight when F_I=0. Two tight intervals
cannot overlap without containment. Indeed, if their left-only, common,
right-only pieces have masses a>0,b>0,c>0, then

 F_I+F_J-F_(I union J)-F_(I intersection J)
  =log[(1+a+b)(1+b+c)/((1+b)(1+a+b+c))]>0,

because the numerator minus denominator in the ratio is ac>0. Tightness
of I,J and nonnegativity of the other two F values contradict this.
Nor can two nonempty tight intervals be adjacent: their union is an
interval, and
F_I+F_J-F_(I union J)=log[(1+a)(1+c)/(1+a+c)]>0.

The inclusion-maximal proper tight intervals are therefore disjoint,
and every two are separated by at least one uncovered index. At least
one index is uncovered: a single proper interval cannot cover the whole
word, and multiple intervals covering it would include an adjacent pair.

There cannot be two uncovered indices u,v. Perturb t_u to t_u+epsilon
and t_v to t_v-epsilon, with a sufficiently small nonzero epsilon of
sign such that epsilon(t_v-t_u)<=0. Positivity is preserved. The total
capacity stays fixed, every proper tight interval is unchanged, and all
other proper inequalities stay strict by continuity and finiteness.
But the changed two-factor product is

 t_u t_v+epsilon(t_v-t_u)-epsilon^2<t_u t_v.

The global expression A product t_i is now less than1. Increase t_u
alone until this expression returns to1. Such an increase exists because
the expression is continuous, strictly increasing in t_u and unbounded.
All proper interval expressions are nondecreasing under this increase,
so none becomes invalid. The resulting feasible word has strictly larger
capacity, a contradiction.

There is exactly one uncovered index j. All indices to its left form
one proper tight interval, if any; otherwise two maximal intervals on
that side would require another uncovered index between them. The same
holds on the right. Thus the left and right children are saturated
admissible words (possibly empty). If their capacities are a,c and the
bridge excess is d=t_j, global equality says

                         A=a+c+d, Ad=ac.

Hence A=Omega(a,c). By induction and strict monotonicity of Omega,
A<=Omega(C_j,C_(q-j-1))<=C_q. Equality forces both children to be
maximizers as well. This proves the asserted upper bound and structure.

For attainment, join saturated children of capacities a,c with the
positive d solving d(a+c+d)=ac. Intervals inside a child are admissible.
An interval crossing the bridge has a left suffix of capacity x<=a and
a right prefix of capacity y<=c, where an empty portion has capacity1.
Its product is at least d/(xy) and its capacity is x+y+d. Since

 xy/(x+y+d)<=ac/(a+c+d)=d,

it is admissible. Monotonicity in x,y follows from the positive derivatives
y(y+d)/(x+y+d)^2 and x(x+d)/(x+y+d)^2. The whole joined word has
product d/(ac)=1/(a+c+d). Starting with empty children and a maximizing
split in(6.2) constructs capacity C_q. These are the accepted actual
primitive joins as well as feasible points of the scalar relaxation.

The new dependence law is the explicit scale-indexed kernel

    <v_i,v_j>=min(t_i,t_j),       ||v_i||^2=t_i.

It is nested by norm, not chronological order. Norms may repeatedly rise
and fall, so earlier coordinates can be reactivated and used arbitrarily
often. There is no fixed bound on physical dimension or coordinate jump
count. Signed intermediate gradients will be negative combinations of
two reset states. This is not a one-future-gradient law, a capped signed
H2 innovation law, or the old power profile for nested dual normals.

One restriction is deliberately retained: each H2 half-cell has constant
gradient. The frozen H5/H6 data have appreciable changes INSIDE some H2
cells. Those changes are not reproduced by this first template; they are
one explicit remaining interface. Another is the exact min-kernel itself:
the frozen data do not prove it, and it is not a lossless Gram model.

## 2. Finite Euclidean realization of the new dependence law

For any finite nonnegative list t_i, sort its distinct positive values as
0<tau_1<...<tau_d and put tau_0=0. With orthonormal vectors e_1,...,e_d,
define

    v_i=sum_(ell:tau_ell<=t_i) sqrt(tau_ell-tau_(ell-1))*e_ell.

Then the common coordinates of v_i and v_j are precisely those with
tau_ell<=min(t_i,t_j). Their inner product telescopes to min(t_i,t_j),
and ||v_i||^2=t_i. Thus this is an explicit finite-dimensional generating
rule, not a PSD oracle. Equal t_i give identical vectors; increasing and
decreasing t_i turn coordinates on and off according to scale. Nothing
here establishes smooth interpolation of a prescribed GD transcript.

## 3. Original H3 cells, values, and intended static function

Set

    s=sum H_2=3+2a+beta,
    A=s+1=4+2a+beta, b=beta*c, D=A+b,
    E=A^2-2Ab-b^2, K=A^2(2A+b),
    B_lo=beta*c^2, B_hi=beta*c^3.

Here B_lo and B_hi are bridge EXCESSES, not smoothness constants or recursive
words. Smoothness is normalized to1. In an H3 cell, the first H2 is
followed by the physical step1+b and then the second H2. Its seven
steps sum to2s+1+b.

At cell j, physical indices8j,...,8j+7, prescribe u_j as gradient at
8j,...,8j+3 and v_j at8j+4,...,8j+7. Prescribe the reset x_(8j+7)=v_j.
The second H2 then starts at A*v_j. At its preceding central query,

    x_(8j+3)=(1+b)u_j+A*v_j,
    y_(8j+3):=x_(8j+3)-u_j=b*u_j+A*v_j,
    x_(8j)=D*u_j+A*v_j.

For j>=1, the original physical bridge8j-1 has excess

    B_j=beta*c^(2+nu_2(j)),

is v_(j-1), the actual GD update gives x_(8j)=-B_j*v_(j-1). Consequently

    u_j=-(B_j*v_(j-1)+A*v_j)/D.                 (1)

All positions inside each H2 are retained, via their actual partial sums;
no query is deleted. At every prescribed sample impose the conjugate
saturation value

    f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2.                  (2)

x_star=g_star=f_star=0. For the ORIGINAL ordered residual convention of
accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290, direct expansion of(2) gives

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<g_i-g_j,x_j-g_j>.                    (3)

If every normal inequality(3) held, a natural intended single function
would be F(x)=max_(g in C)(<x,g>-||g||^2/2), where C is the convex hull
of0 and all supplied gradients. The inequalities say that g_i is the
Euclidean projection of x_i onto C, and hence give the values(2).
This intended construction is NOT asserted legal: the next sections
prove that an original row fails. No minimizer or radius is inferred from
the intended hull before interpolation is checked.

## 4. Local transition calculation and first explicit law

Consider one cell after a bridge of excess B>0. Write p=v_(j-1),v=v_j,
P=||p||^2>0,T=||v||^2, and use <p,v>=min(P,T). At the central query,

    u=-(B*p+A*v)/D,
    y=(-bB*p+A^2*v)/D.

The retained row with source gradient v and target gradient u is

    D^2*Q_(v,u)=K*T+E*B*min(P,T)-bB^2*P.       (4)

To derive(4), multiply
(v-u)=[B*p+(2A+b)*v]/D by y. The mixed coefficient is
B[A^2-b(2A+b)]=B*E, and the other two coefficients are-bB^2 and K.

For a shrinking endpoint T<=P, this row requires

    T/P<=alpha(B):=bB^2/(K+EB),                (5)

whenever the denominator is positive. For a growing endpoint T>=P it
requires

    T/P<=gamma(B):=B(bB-E)/K.                  (6)

The factorization

    K*(gamma(B)-1)=(bB-A^2)(B+2A+b)           (7)

The first explicit extrapolation law selected in plan6e9c5cb11fc77d32
was to take equality in(5) below this threshold and equality in(6)
above it, using the exact B_j and fixed enclosing-m parameters in every
cell. This produces nonmonotone reset norms and persistent state.

The following obstruction is STRONGER: it allows arbitrary reset norms
subject only to the local inequalities, not this maximal-transition law.
Thus lowering a selected factor or independently retuning all endpoint
norms cannot repair the entire declared min-kernel family.

## 5. Uniform parameter bounds on the actual words

ac0c1e866da0d926 and interval draft cd0f93f08a50828f were recalled as awareness,

## 1. Exact scope and outcome

Let r>=2 and take h_i=1+t_i with t_i>0 for0<=i<r. Define

Here B_i is a local suffix mass, not the benchmark denominator B_n. All
auxiliary symbols in this document are local and have implicit suffix add108.

The declared family uses an ADDITIVE ordered kernel

 K_ij=alpha_i+beta_j, 0<=i<j<=r.                         (1)

This has two row-times-column channels, alpha_i*1+1*beta_j, on the ordered

auxiliary terminal convention. For EVERY0<=i<j<=r define

 mu_ij=K_ij-K_(i-1),j+t_j(K_i,(j+1)-K_(i-1),(j+1)),
 mu_ji=K_(i-1),j-K_(i-1),(j+1)+t_i(K_ij-K_i,(j+1)),
 Lambda_ij=2mu_ji, Lambda_ji=2mu_ij, Lambda_ii=0.       (2)

## 2. Original identity and full mixed-coefficient cancellation

        =2(f_i-f_j)-2<g_j,x_i-x_j>-||g_i-g_j||^2,

       +sum_(i<r)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sA||g_r||^2.

## 3. All original signs and the interior flows

 H=sum_(i=l)^(k-1)h_i,
 v_l=1, v_(i+1)=-t_i v_i for l<=i<k,
 p=v_k, q=|p|=product_(i=l)^(k-1)t_i,
 A_i^out=sum_(j<l)mu_ji,
 B_i^out=sum_(j>=k)mu_ji,       l<=i<k.

These last two quantities are the actual incoming auxiliary weights
from the two exterior sides. Set formal g_i=v_i on I and g_i=0 outside
I, including the terminal, and set every f_i=0. Up to an arbitrary
translation, positions inside are v_i, positions on the left are1,
and positions on the right are p.

For an internal ordered pair, Qbar_ij=-(v_i^2-v_j^2). An incoming edge
from the left to i has residual v_i^2-2v_i; an incoming edge from the
right has residual v_i^2-2p v_i; every outgoing edge from i to the
exterior has residual -v_i^2. All-exterior residuals vanish. Using
d_i=h_i, the right side of (2) is therefore

 -sum_(i in I)h_i v_i^2
           -2sum_(i in I)v_i(A_i^out+p B_i^out).

The left side is sum_(i in I)h_i(1-h_i)v_i^2. Since
h_i(2-h_i)v_i^2=v_i^2-v_(i+1)^2, this gives the exact identity

 sum_(i in I)v_i(A_i^out+p B_i^out)=(p^2-1)/2.         (7)

This is a factor-free interval cut identity. Its exterior terms remain
signed through v_i and p. Nonnegative A_i^out,B_i^out alone give no
upper bound on the alternating weighted sum that would compare q with
1/(1+H). Deleting A_i^out for an interior interval is unjustified.
Thus this first direct attempt stops at the signed boundary moment (7).

## 5. Second mechanism: an exact interval-defect identity

The next test retains the exterior times, rather than replacing the
exterior gradients by zero. Define global prefix sums S_i=sum_(t<i)h_t
and put P=S_l. Retain H,v,p,q from Section4 and define formal gradients

 psi_i=1                         if i<l,
 psi_i=v_i                       if l<=i<k,
 psi_i=p                         if k<=i<=r.

Choose x_l=1. The complete original GD equations then give

 x_i=1+S_l-S_i                   if i<l,
 x_i=v_i                         if l<=i<k,
 x_i=p(1-(S_i-S_k))              if k<=i<=r.

Use these formal values:

 f_i=1/2+S_l-S_i                 if i<l,
 f_i=v_i^2/2                     if l<=i<k,
 f_i=p^2/2-p^2(S_i-S_k)          if k<=i<=r.           (8)

Values and positions agree at the two boundaries. This is a FORMAL
polynomial test. It is not claimed to be interpolable by one static
convex smooth function, and is not used as a primal witness. Indeed
some of its residuals below can be negative.

All within-region residuals vanish. The complete list of possibly
nonzero residuals is

 Qbar_ij=2(S_l-S_i)(1-psi_j),    i<l, j>=l,
 Qbar_ji=2(S_j-S_k)p(psi_i-p),   j>=k, i<k.            (9)

The reverse orientation between the left and middle regions, and the
reverse orientation between the middle and right regions, is zero.
For a left/right pair, both expressions in (9) apply to its respective
orientations, so no crossing pair is lost or counted twice.

For example, for i<l and l<=j<k, put d=S_l-S_i. Direct substitution is

 Qbar_ij=1+2d-v_j^2-2v_j(1+d-v_j)-(1-v_j)^2
         =2d(1-v_j),
 Qbar_ji=v_j^2-1-2d-2(v_j-1-d)-(v_j-1)^2=0.

For l<=i<k and j>=k, put b=S_j-S_k. Direct substitution gives
Qbar_ij=0 and Qbar_ji=2b p(v_i-p). For a left/right pair the same
substitution gives 2d(1-p) in the first orientation and 2b p(1-p)
in the second. This proves the full list (9).

Define the two ACTUAL weighted boundary sums

 C_L=sum_(i<l,j>=l)mu_ij(S_l-S_i)(1-psi_j),
 C_R=sum_(j>=k,i<k)mu_ji(S_j-S_k)p(psi_i-p).            (10)

Here empty sums, including C_L when l=0 and C_R when k=r, are zero.
Equation (2) evaluated on (8) is exactly

            (P+1)^2-(P+H+1)^2 p^2=2(C_L+C_R).         (11)

For an explicit check of its left side, write R=s-P-H. The prefix
contribution to 2sum h_i f_i+sum h_i(1-h_i)psi_i^2 is P^2+2P;
the interval contribution is 1-p^2; the suffix contribution is
p^2(2R-R^2). The remaining terminal terms are
-s(s+2)p^2+2sR p^2. Their sum is (P+1)^2-(P+H+1)^2p^2.

Define the hereditary defect

                    Delta_I=(1+H)^2p^2-1.

Since q>0 and 1+H>0, the requested inequality is equivalent to
Delta_I>=0. Rearranging (11) gives the precise original-array formula

 Delta_I=P[P+2-(P+2H+2)p^2]-2(C_L+C_R).              (12)

Thus the remaining coefficient inequality, with ALL original signs,
flow, and mixed matching retained, is

 2(C_L+C_R) <= P[P+2-(P+2H+2)p^2]                    (13)

for every 0<=l<k<=r. This report does not prove (13).

At the first singleton l=0,k=1, C_L=0, p=-t_0<0, and the only i<k
is i=0 with psi_i=1. Consequently every term of C_R is nonpositive,
so (12) proves that boundary case. At a general prefix, C_L remains
zero but psi_i alternates; the same entrywise argument is invalid.
At an interior interval both C_L and C_R must remain in (13).

### 5.1 What summing the prefix crossing flows does and does not provide

For l=0 write H=S_k and, for k<=j<=r, set

 F_j=sum_(i<k)mu_ij, b_j=sum_(i<k)mu_ji,
 B_j=sum_(i<k)mu_ji v_i, w_j=-B_j/p,
 e_j=S_j-S_k.

All F_j,b_j are nonnegative. The signed quantity w_j is not a factor
and is not assumed nonnegative. Multiplying (5), rearranged in its
cumulative form, by v_i and summing i=0,...,k-1 telescopes because
t_i v_i=-v_(i+1). The exact result, including j=r with h_r=0, is

             w_j+h_j sum_(m>j)w_m=F_j.                (18)

More explicitly, the left cumulative sum in (6) telescopes to
-p F_j, and the right one is B_j+h_j sum_(m>j)B_m.
This proves (18) without a separation of the two indices.

The quadratic cut (7), now with no incoming left boundary, gives

             sum_(j>=k)w_j=(p^(-2)-1)/2.              (19)

The original value flow over the prefix gives

             sum_(j>=k)(F_j-b_j)=H.                   (20)

Since e_j=sum_(t=k)^(j-1)h_t, summing (18) yields

 sum_(j>=k)e_j w_j=sum_(j>=k)F_j-sum_(j>=k)w_j.

Also, directly from (10),

                  C_R=-p^2 sum_(j>=k)e_j(w_j+b_j).    (21)

Substitute these formulas in (11). After (19)--(20) cancel the signed
total, the remaining nonnegative boundary moment is exactly

                   sum_(j>=k)(1+e_j)b_j=H^2/2.       (22)

For clarity, this last cancellation reads
1-(1+H)^2p^2=-2p^2[H+sum(1+e_j)b_j-(p^(-2)-1)/2].
Subtract1 and divide by -p^2 to obtain (22).

Thus prefix flow and the quadratic cut fix two totals, (19) and (22),
even in the full unfactored array. The remaining prefix inequality is

                   sum_(j>=k)e_j(w_j+b_j)>=0.         (23)

Backward substitution in (18) is w_j=F_j-h_j sum_(m>j)w_m;
nonnegativity of F_j alone does not provide the sign in (23).
The additional original constraints on the same array have not been
shown to force it here. At k=r-1 only j=r has positive e_j and
w_r=F_r>=0, so (23) holds for that boundary case. This observation is
not an induction through arbitrary intervals: eliminating a suffix
would change the other crossing entries and their equations.

## 6. Minimal-violation screening does not fix the missing sign

If heredity fails, choose an inclusion-minimal nonempty violating
interval I. Every proper nonempty contiguous subinterval then obeys
the proposed bound. For any l<j<k, let H_left and H_right be the step
sums on [l,j) and [j,k), and let q_left,q_right be their excess products.
Then q=q_left q_right<1/(1+H), while

 q_left>=1/(1+H_left), q_right>=1/(1+H_right).

It follows that

 q_left<=q(1+H_right)<1,
 q_right<=q(1+H_left)<1,
                         q<|v_j|<1.                 (14)

Therefore every psi_j<=1, including the two exterior constants, and
C_L>=0. The right-hand summands in (10) still have both signs when
there are internal indices of both relevant parities: p(psi_i-p) is
positive when psi_i has the sign of p and larger magnitude, and is
negative when psi_i has the opposite sign. For a singleton, the left
boundary sum remains a separate issue when l>0.

Thus even restricting (13) to an inclusion-minimal hypothetical
violation does not justify dropping the right-hand positive terms or
the left boundary. It changes the missing mechanism to a quantitative
balance between those ACTUAL edges. This is the precise obstruction
left by the second direct attempt, not a claim that (13) is false.

## 7. Exact full-array counterexample to the entrywise sign shortcut

This construction refutes only the stronger claim that every summand
of C_R is nonpositive for a prefix interval. It DOES NOT refute heredity.

Let d be the positive root of d^2+5d-4=0, put

 C=5+d, kappa=C^2/16, K=kappa-1,
 h=(1+d,3/2,3/2), s=4+d.

The polynomial is negative at0, positive at1 and strictly increasing
on [0,infinity), so 0<d<1. In particular C>5 and K>0. In original
index order0,1,2,3 define the COMPLETE matrix

 Lambda =
 [ 0,       0,           0,             Kd                 ]
 [ 3K/2,    0,           kappa,         kappa/2+3K/2        ]
 [ 3K/2,    7kappa/2,    0,             17kappa/2+3K/2      ]
 [ K,       kappa,       14kappa,       0                  ]. (15)

Every entry is nonnegative, including the two stated off-diagonal zeros.
The root equation implies dC=4 and

                    K(4-d)=2(1+d).                   (16)

capacities1 and4; it is also checked directly as follows:

 (C^2-16)(4-d)-32(1+d)
 = (9+10d+d^2)(4-d)-32-32d
 = 4-d-6d^2-d^3

 K(d-4), -3kappa+3K, -3kappa+3K,
                            6kappa-K(d+2)
 = -2(1+d), -3, -3, 8+2d,

the exact required flow.

 Lambda_child=[ [0,1,1/2], [7/2,0,17/2], [1,14,0] ].

Its flow is (-3,-3,6), its L_child T_child is exactly

 [ -3/4, -7/4, -1/2 ]
 [  7/4, -3/4, -17/2]

and its D_child is diag(3/4,3/4,-15). Hence its remainder is zero on
all three independent formal gradients. The empty left child has
capacity1 and zero remainder. Fact04219554e41d9750, Section11, applied
with right capacity4 and d(1+4+d)=4, gives

 V_h=kappa V_child-K[(3/2)Q_10+(3/2)Q_20+Q_30
                               +d Q_03+(3/2)Q_13+(3/2)Q_23].

Inserting the just-checked child identity gives exactly every entry
of (15). Therefore its FULL original remainder M is identically zero;
no restricted Gram test, quotient, or unidentified gradient is involved.

Now take the prefix interval I=[0,2). Its local data are

 v_0=1, v_1=-d, p=d/2, H=5/2+d,
 S_3-S_2=3/2, mu_30=Lambda_03/2=Kd/2.

The (j,i)=(3,0) summand of C_R is

                 (3Kd^2/8)(1-d/2)>0.                (17)

to each right-boundary term. The opposing (3,1) term is negative.
Their total is nonpositive, as required for this particular interval:

 (1+H)q=(7/2+d)d/2=2-3d/4>1.

clarity, the entire word in (15) satisfies heredity: its singleton

has product2-3d/4>1; the right two-step interval has product1;

The mixed-coefficient route was carried through in two forms:

* the isolated interval quadratic gives (7), with signed incoming
  moments from BOTH exterior sides;

  desired sign to the explicit weighted crossing bound (13). Even
  the pure-prefix reduction, with exact cut totals (19) and (22),

The first method has no bound on its alternating left and right
moments. The second needs an upper bound on their combined weighted
sum, not nonnegativity of the original coefficients individually.
Minimality of a hypothetical violating interval only gives (14).
The exact full array (15) rules out the stronger entrywise C_R<=0
argument, while continuing to satisfy interval heredity itself.

## 1. Declared scope and results

For any integer r>=2 let h_i=1+t_i with t_i>0, 0<=i<r. Put

 s=sum_(i<r)h_i, A=1+s, H_i=sum_(k<i)h_k,

The empty product is1, so R_0=1 and p_0=0. All symbols in this document
other than the cited project notation are local to C109. In particular
sigma_i is a suffix step mass, not a benchmark denominator.

The family consists of kernels on the ORDERED domain i<j of the form

 K_ij=alpha_i+gamma_i beta_j, 0<=i<j<=r,                (1)

where every gamma_i>0, 0<=i<r. The profile gamma is arbitrary and need
not be monotone, symmetric, or constant. The two channels need not
individually be certificates. Set beta_r=0 by the harmless gauge change
beta_j -> beta_j-beta_r, alpha_i -> alpha_i+gamma_i beta_r. Boundary

Every original ordered coefficient is defined by

 mu_ij=K_ij-K_(i-1),j+t_j(K_i,(j+1)-K_(i-1),(j+1)),
 mu_ji=K_(i-1),j-K_(i-1),(j+1)+t_i(K_ij-K_i,(j+1)),
 Lambda_ij=2mu_ji, Lambda_ji=2mu_ij, Lambda_ii=0.       (2)

The conclusions proved jointly below are:

* All original zero-remainder matching equations in this entire family
  have an explicit backward solution, and its full sign test is stated.
* Every NONNEGATIVE original array in this family must satisfy every

       (1+sigma_i) product_(i<=k<r)t_k >=1, 1<=i<r.   (3)

# Max48: motion on faces at the original queries

Status: complete joint analytical DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. No fact submission is
authorized in this launch. This is round48, the first of two rounds after
completed47; it does not renew the allocation. The original all-horizon,
all-nonnegative-word exact-profile problem remains OPEN.

## 1. Scope, accepted inputs, and the changed law

The former T1/T2 laws held the gradient constant inside each original H2
half. The law here replaces that assumption by affine projection motion
on an exposed segment: the tangent component changes at every physical
query. A remote support condition obstructs an orthogonal-face version.
An actual triangle then realizes the correct face transition, with every
subsequent physical query given explicitly. The latter construction is
legal for every enclosing integer m>=100, but its entire specified
family is quantitatively weaker than the complete same-word references.

The accepted mathematical inputs are:

* fact1252b8823bb5a290: necessity of every ordered smooth-convex
  interpolation inequality, including the optimum; its proof also gives
  the normalization used here.
* factb98bb807d514e80d: the full K_n reference and the exact all-split
  benchmark estimate B_n<=1+4n^(log_2 3).

  with K_n<=F_ray_n.

The supporting literature search returned Theorem4 of Jai Moondra,
Hassan Mortagy and Swati Gupta, "Reusing Combinatorial Structure: Faster

## 2. Original words and local notation

Fix an integer m>=100 and use the SAME enclosing parameters in every
child:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/m, beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    H0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1.

Thus the actual first seven steps are

    (ell,1+beta,ell,1+b,ell,1+beta,ell),
    ell=1+a, b=beta*c.

The following are local scalars, denoted A48,eta48,b48,k48,r48,chi48,
d48 in the shared glossary when necessary:

    A=1+sum H2=4+2a+beta,
    eta=a^2*beta,
    k=A/(b*eta),
    r=sqrt(b(b+1)/(A(k-1))),
    chi=1+(A-1)(b+1)/(b*k+1),
    d=chi-ell.                                             (1)

In particular k is not a horizon, a checkpoint count, or K_n; b is a
bridge EXCESS, not the original benchmark B_n. Define the partial sums
and tangent coefficients of the actual H2 by

    (p0,p1,p2,p3)=(0,ell,ell+1+beta,A-1),
    (t0,t1,t2,t3)=(1,-a,a*beta,-eta).                       (2)

For any integer i>=0, s2(i) is its number of binary1 digits, with
s2(0)=0. For a positive integer j, nu2(j) is the exponent of2 dividing
j. These are combinatorial definitions, not numerical routines run here.

All vectors and inner products below are Euclidean. An exposed-face
normal q means that the relevant face lies in the hyperplane
<q,v>=||q||^2 and the whole convex set lies in its lower halfspace.

## 4. Exact moving-face H2 block and its remote obstruction

Suppose q is a face normal, w perpendicular to q, and the four proposed
projections q+t_i w all lie in that face. Put

    x_i=(A-p_i)q+t_i w,

## 5. One actual triangle, with its actual first face transition

The illegal orthogonal second face suggests the following single static
convex set, for which we follow the TRUE projection instead. In the plane
let

    U=(1,k*r), V=(1,-a*k*r), L=(-b,r),
    C48=conv{U,V,L},
    F48(x)=max_(v in C48)[<x,v>-||v||^2/2],
    X0=(A,k*r).                                          (12)

depending only on m. Here L is a vertex label; the smoothness constant
is1 until the final scaling paragraph. The defining maximum is one
fixed function, not a Gram feasibility oracle.

The triangle is the intersection of the three halfspaces

    x <=1,
    -(k-1)r*x+(b+1)y <=(b*k+1)r,
    -(a*k+1)r*x-(b+1)y <=(a*b*k-1)r.                    (13)

The third right side is positive: a*b*k=A/(a*beta)>69/5>1 by(3).

is unique by strict concavity. It is the Euclidean projection P_C48(x),
since the objective is ||x||^2/2-||x-v||^2/2. The projection condition is

    <x-g,v-g><=0 for every v in C48.                     (14)

Necessity follows by differentiating squared distance along each segment
from g to v; sufficiency follows by expanding ||x-v||^2. Applying(14)

    <x-x',P_C48(x)-P_C48(x')>>=||P_C48(x)-P_C48(x')||^2.

    argmin F48={0}, min F48=0,
    dist(X0,argmin F48)^2=A^2+k^2*r^2.                   (15)

## 9. What the balanced choice closes, and what it leaves open

There are two distinct scoped conclusions in this joint draft.

First, ANY two fixed-face H2 blocks with core resets, the intervening
low original bridge and orthogonal nonzero normals fail the original
row(0,4). All adjacent and optimum inequalities passing does not fix
that defect. Equation(11) gives the stronger necessary correlation.
No failure is asserted for arbitrary oblique normals, intermediate
face changes, noncore endpoints, or other conjugate height laws.

Second, the explicit balanced-aspect triangle(12) is globally legal
but its true normalized payoff is less than one tenth of each complete
same-word reference in(32)--(33), and its original-B ratio tends to0.
This conclusion covers exactly the aspect ratio r in(1), arbitrary
positive spatial scaling and orthogonal embeddings of that instance,
and the objective scaling just described. It is not a claim about ALL
triangles, polytopes, or functions with changing gradients.

One useful exact interface survives if the aspect r>0 in(12) is released.
Keep A,b,eta,k fixed, and define the same triangle and X0. All first-block
formulas(16)--(19) remain valid. At4 the true projection is

    g4=L+theta(U-L),
    theta=(A-1)(k-1)r^2/[(b+1)^2+(k-1)^2*r^2].           (35)

This holds for every r>0: 0<theta<1; the residual is perpendicular
to UL, and its dot product with n_plus has the positive sign because
<n_plus,X4>-D_plus=(A-1)(b+1)r>0. Thus the residual is outward and
the remote V also passes. If q is the perpendicular foot of0 on the
upper supporting line and w=g4-q, then

    q perpendicular w, X4=chi*q+w,
    X5=d*q-a*w.                                         (36)

In(36), chi and d are EXACTLY those of(1), independent of the aspect.
The projection at5 cannot lie in the RELATIVE INTERIOR of the old upper
edge: its affine projection would have normal residual(d-1)q, pointing
inward, since d<1/8. A projection in the relative interior of that edge
requires a nonnegative multiple of its outward normal. Equivalently the
first original low step already uses more normal reserve than is
available on this face. This is an explicit normal-cone failure, not
just an inequality on the desired terminal gap. Endpoint projections,
which have larger normal cones, are not excluded by this argument.

For the balanced aspect w=0, (24)--(26) prove persistent core entry.
For a free aspect w need not vanish; the next point may instead hit
another face. No full-word estimate for those true further transitions
is asserted. Such a law must follow the actual projections at queries
inside H2, not hold the current edge for a whole block. This is a
materially different remaining interface from the closed T1/T2 carriers.

The frozen internal-H2 observation has a further qualitative warning:
motion on one fixed face makes BOTH directed Q residuals within that
face zero, as proved in Section4. The saved H6 diagnostics show a
nearly tight forward row and a substantially slack reverse row. Raw
diagnostics are not exact identities, but there is no evidential basis
for imposing a single fixed face throughout each original H2.

An eventual stronger construction on H_m would still leave the original
all-n/all-nonnegative-word lower comparison BLOCKED. That comparison is
a theorem-level requirement, not a routine induction. No such uniform
bridge or unrestricted upper separation is supplied by this draft.

## 2. Exact equivalence of the implemented original PSD model

For a word h=(h_0,...,h_(r-1))>=0 set s=sum h_i and A=1+s. Let e be
the all-ones column of length r+1, T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, with

Under the original flow, e^T D e=-sum h_i^2-s^2, while
