# Coupled ellipsoid pilot: multiplier drainage, paid radius, and the core-return gap

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED proof draft of the scoped results below.
The complete centered-ellipsoid payoff question is BLOCKED at Section 10.
This is round 47, the one analytical round authorized by TASK.md and
master_guidance eb57bb7a5bebd161. No numerical, solver, machine-algebra,
DP/replay, formal-verifier, consult, or subagent call is used. No fact is
claimed. All new mathematical ingredients are proved jointly here.

## 1. Selected concrete family and result

All norms and inner products are Euclidean. Let A be a symmetric positive
definite matrix on a finite-dimensional real space. Write

    d_min = smallest eigenvalue of A,
    d_max = largest eigenvalue of A,  kappa = d_max/d_min,
    E_A = {g : <g,A g> <= 1},
    F_A(x) = max_(g in E_A) {<x,g> - ||g||^2/2}.

I denotes the identity matrix and ||u||_A^2=<u,A u>. The d_l and x_l in
principal-coordinate formulas denote the eigenvalues of A and the
corresponding coordinates of x. Along a trajectory write g_i=g(x_i),
t_i=t(x_i), v_i=v(x_i), and f_i=F_A(x_i).

The selected family has 1 <= kappa <= 2. Thus the squared ratio of its
longest to shortest semiaxis is at most 2. Dimension, orientation, scale,
individual eigenvalues, and initial point may all depend on the ENTIRE
original word. At least two distinct active eigenvalues are permitted;
no common scalar quadratic orbit is assumed. This family is centered.
It does not include arbitrary translated or more eccentric ellipsoids.

Define t(x)=0 when x belongs to E_A. Otherwise t(x)>0 is the unique root

    sum_l d_l x_l^2/(1+t(x)d_l)^2 = 1,                     (1)

in orthonormal principal coordinates of A. Set v(x)=d_max t(x).
The actual gradient is g(x)=(I+t(x)A)^(-1)x. For every actual step h>=0,

    x_plus = ((1-h)I+t(x)A)g(x),
    v(x_plus) <= max{v(x)-h, kappa(h-2)-v(x), 0}.         (2)

Formula (2) includes zero and arbitrarily large original steps.

For the diagnostic word fix an integer m>=128 and retain its original
enclosing parameters in EVERY child and at EVERY physical query:

    lambda = 1+sqrt(2),  beta = 1-1/m,
    c = lambda(1+1/m),  a = beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1,  S_j=sum H_j,  S=S_m,  M=1+S.

For any input state, run the same static F_A through a complete H_j block.
Its actual multiplier satisfies

    v_exit <= (v_entry-S_j)_+,  0<=j<=m.                 (3)

Here (r)_+=max(r,0). In particular an exterior terminal point x_n outside
E_A forces v(x_0)>S. This is not a statement that a core terminal is zero.

Let x_0!=0, use every step of H_m, and set

    R_0=||x_0||=dist(x_0,argmin F_A),
    P_A=2(F_A(x_n)-F_A(0))/R_0^2.

The following rigorously scoped conclusions are the output of this pilot:

* If v(x_0)>=S, then

      P_A <= kappa/(kappa+2S) <= 1/M.                    (4)

  This covers EVERY exterior terminal trajectory, and also the core
  terminal branch under the stated initial condition.
* If d_min R_0^2>=M, then P_A<=1/M, whether the terminal is exterior or
  inside the core. The sufficient normal-state condition

      v(x_0)>=kappa(sqrt(M)-1)                           (5)

  implies this paid-radius condition.
* If v(x_0)<=1+a, the first original step puts the actual state into E_A
  and the entire remaining physical word stays in E_A. With

      q_m=beta^(2^m-1)c^(-m),

  the exact endpoint is x_n=(-1)^(n-1)(q_m/a)x_1 and

      P_A=(q_m/a)^2 ||x_1||^2/R_0^2
          <= (q_m/a)^2 <= c^(-2(m-1)).                  (6)

  If x_0 already belongs to E_A, the stronger exact value is P_A=q_m^2.

For the ORIGINAL all-split benchmark B_n from accepted
b98bb807d514e80d, each of the covered regimes obeys

    B_n P_A < 14848/15315 < 1,  m>=128,                 (7)

and uniformly over their horizon-dependent parameters,

    limsup_(m->infinity) sup B_n P_A <= lambda/exp(1)<1. (8)

The small shell in (6) has ratio tending to zero and is strictly below
each COMPLETE same-word K, alternating-ray, and full schedule-dependent
complex-polynomial reference specified in Section 8. The large-state
bound is below 2K and 2F_ray and below 8 times the full complex reference;
no dominance by one of those references is claimed in that regime.

The remaining core-ending initial region is explicit:

    v(x_0)>1+a,  d_min R_0^2<M,  v(x_n)=0.              (9)

Every instance not covered by the stated regimes lies here. No uniform
payoff bound on (9), no closure of all centered ellipsoids, and no
all-n/all-nonnegative-word conclusion about W_n are asserted.
Here W_n(h) is the supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2)
over all finite-dimensional convex differentiable L-smooth objectives
with a minimizer x_star, x_0!=x_star, and the actual updates
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i), as in accepted 1252b8823bb5a290.

## 2. One legal function, its actual query, and the true minimum

E_A is nonempty, compact and convex. Completing the square in its defining
maximum shows that its unique maximizing g is the Euclidean projection
of x onto E_A. Existence follows from compactness; uniqueness follows from
strict convexity of ||x-g||^2 on a convex set.

For x in E_A this gives g=x. For x outside, the left side of (1) is
continuous, strictly decreasing on [0,infinity), starts above 1, and
tends to zero. Thus its unique root t is positive, even if some x_l
vanish or some eigenvalues coincide. For g=(I+tA)^(-1)x one has
<g,A g>=1 and, for every z in E_A,

    <x-g,z-g> = t(<g,A z>-1) <= 0,

by Cauchy--Schwarz in the A inner product. Expanding squared distances
then shows ||x-z||^2>=||x-g||^2. This proves the query formula without a
black-box Lagrange multiplier assertion. Write x=(I+tA)g throughout,
including t=0 in the core.

For two projection pairs (x,g),(y,p), their two normal inequalities add
to ||g-p||^2<=<g-p,x-y>. In particular ||g-p||<=||x-y||. Comparing the two
defining maxima for F_A gives

    <g,z> <= F_A(x+z)-F_A(x) <= <g(x+z),z>.

The difference between the left expression and the middle expression is
between zero and ||z||^2. Thus F_A is differentiable, its gradient is g,
and that gradient is 1-Lipschitz. F_A is convex as a maximum of affine
functions of x and is finite by compactness.

Since 0 is feasible, F_A>=0, and F_A(0)=0. If x!=0, choose epsilon>0
small enough that epsilon*x belongs to E_A and epsilon<2. Its test value
epsilon(1-epsilon/2)||x||^2 is positive. Hence argmin F_A={0}, proving the
true minimum and the paid initial radius exactly. Multiplication of F_A
by any L>0 and use of steps h_i/L preserves every point and P_A. This is
the project's W=2R normalization.

The actual value is

    F_A(x)=<x,g>-||g||^2/2
          =||g||^2/2+t<g,A g>
          =||g||^2/2+t.                                 (10)

The last equality holds also in the core because t=0. In particular
F_A(x)=||x||^2/2 there. Actual GD gives the first formula of (2), and the
next t is evaluated at that actual x_plus by (1). No state is reset.

For any two actual samples, including the optimum sample with x=g=t=0,
the complete smooth-convex residual in the convention of accepted
1252b8823bb5a290 is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<x_j-g_j,g_i-g_j>
        =t_j(<g_j,A g_i>-<g_j,A g_j>) <= 0.              (11)

If t_j=0 the last expression is zero. If t_j>0, its final inner product
is at most 1 and <g_j,A g_j>=1. This proves every ordered remote,
adjacent, and optimum inequality at once. In particular Q_(i,*)=0 and
Q_(*,i)=-t_i. No finite list of selected interpolation rows is substituted.

When both gradients lie on the ellipsoid boundary, (11) becomes

    Q_ij=-(t_j/2)||g_i-g_j||_A^2.                        (12)

Thus for t_i,t_j>0 the ratio Q_ij/t_j equals Q_ji/t_i. A one-way zero
residual with the reverse strictly negative is impossible among two
strictly exterior queries. For three such queries the products
Q_ij Q_jk Q_ki and Q_ji Q_kj Q_ik coincide. These are scoped structural
restrictions of this centered ellipsoid, not claims about general
smooth-convex interpolation or about floating-point H6 residuals.

## 3. Genuine coupling and a fully exterior nonlinear example

In principal coordinates put

    D_t=sum_l d_l^2 x_l^2/(1+t d_l)^3 > 0

at an exterior point. Implicit differentiation of (1) gives

    partial t/partial x_l = [d_l x_l/(1+t d_l)^2]/D_t.

For distinct k,l,

    partial g_k/partial x_l
      =-[d_k x_k/(1+t d_k)^2]
        [d_l x_l/(1+t d_l)^2]/D_t.                      (13)

This is nonzero when both coordinates are nonzero. In these coordinates
the query is not a direct sum of independent scalar quadratic queries.
Each denominator shares the changing t. No reduction of the entire
family to a fixed quadratic or one common polynomial orbit is made.
Indeed the Hessian is I in the interior core, whereas differentiating
<g(x),A g(x)>=1 at an exterior point gives the nonzero left null vector
(A g(x))^T for the gradient Jacobian. That exterior Jacobian exists by
(1) and is singular. Thus this function cannot be a fixed quadratic in
any orthonormal coordinate system.

The exterior regime is nonempty and supports changed gradient directions
at every physical query. For ANY nonnegative word of sum S, choose

    A=diag(1,2),  g_0=(1/sqrt(2),1/2),
    T=4S+1,       x_0=(I+T A)g_0.

Then <g_0,A g_0>=1 and t(x_0)=T. Because every projected coordinate has
|g_1|<=1 and |g_2|<=1/sqrt(2), the actual recursion gives at every index

    (x_i)_1 >= (1+T)/sqrt(2)-S
              =(2sqrt(2)-1)S+sqrt(2)>1,
    (x_i)_2 >= T+1/2-S/sqrt(2)>0.

Every query is exterior with two positive gradient coordinates. If h_i>0
and g_(i+1) were parallel to g_i, boundary normalization and positivity
would force equality. The actual update would then require both
t_(i+1)=t_i-h_i and t_(i+1)=t_i-h_i/2, a contradiction. Thus, on H_m,
each successive gradient direction changes, while the whole trajectory
still satisfies the obstruction below. Continuous coupled boundary
motion alone does not avoid its paid-radius cost.

## 4. One-step multiplier drainage, including zero and huge steps

Take any x=(I+tA)g, t>=0, g in E_A. For h>=0 define

    u=max{t-h/d_max, (h-2)/d_min-t, 0}.

For every eigenvalue d in [d_min,d_max],

    1+t d-h <= 1+u d.

For the other sign, if h>=2 the definition of u implies
h-1-t d<=1+u d. If 0<=h<=2, the same inequality holds because
h-2<=0<=(t+u)d. Consequently

    |1+t d-h| <= 1+u d.

For y=x-hg, the vector (I+uA)^(-1)y therefore has A norm at most the A
norm of g, hence at most 1. The root characterization in Section 2
implies t(y)<=u. Multiplying by d_max proves (2). When h=0 the bound is
v(y)<=v(x), and the actual map is exactly the identity. No upper bound
on h was imposed.

The right side of (2) is not monotone in v. The block proof next does
NOT iterate it by replacing v with an upper bound inside the negative-v
term; that replacement would have the wrong inequality direction.

## 5. Every inherited H_j block drains its full original mass

The exact mass formulas, obtained from S_(j+1)=2S_j+1+a c^j, are

    alpha=a/(c-2)=beta/[c(c-2)],
    S_j+1=alpha c^j+(1-alpha)2^j.                        (14)

For m>=128, c>lambda>2, c<5/2, and 0<alpha<1. The last statement follows
from c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1>beta. The upper bound c<5/2 follows, for
example, from sqrt(2)<17/12 and (29/12)(129/128)<5/2.

Put b_j=1+a c^j. If b_j<=2 then kappa(b_j-2)_+=0<=S_j. If b_j>2,

    S_j-kappa(b_j-2)
      =(1-alpha)2^j+[alpha-kappa a]c^j+kappa-1 >= 0,     (15)

because alpha-kappa a=alpha[1-kappa(c-2)]>=0 for kappa<=2, c<5/2.

We now prove (3) by induction for arbitrary actual inputs to each block.
H_0 is empty, so the assertion is equality. Suppose it holds for H_j.
After the left copy, write its actual multiplier as w. It satisfies
w<=(v-S_j)_+. After the middle step b=b_j, (2) and w>=0 imply

    v_middle <= max{(v-S_j)_+-b, kappa(b-2), 0}.

This step bounds the reflected term by kappa(b-2), rather than wrongly
inserting the upper bound on w into its negative occurrence. Apply the
inductive assertion to the actual input of the right copy and subtract
S_j from this maximum. By (15), its second entry becomes nonpositive;
the third is also nonpositive. The first entry is at most
(v-2S_j-b)_+ after taking the positive part, including the case v<S_j.
This proves v_exit<=(v-S_(j+1))_+.

The induction keeps all original child parameters and every physical
query. It neither restarts t nor changes the function between copies.

## 6. Radius payment and the large-state payoff

Suppose v_0>=S. Then x_0 is exterior. Let z=d_min t_0=v_0/kappa and
p=S/kappa. Here p>=1 since S>=2^m-1 and kappa<=2. Write
w_l=d_l(g_0)_l^2, so w_l>=0 and sum_l w_l=1. Exactly,

    R_0^2=sum_l w_l[(1+t_0 d_l)^2/d_l].

For d>=d_min the bracket is 1/d+2t_0+t_0^2 d, whose derivative is
t_0^2-1/d^2>=0 because t_0 d_min=z>=p>=1. Consequently

    R_0^2 >= (1+z)^2/d_min.                             (16)

Every projected g has ||g||^2<=1/d_min. From (3),
t_n<=(v_0-S)/d_max. Thus (10) and (16), whether t_n is zero or positive,
give

    P_A <= [1+2(z-p)]/(1+z)^2 <= 1/(1+2p).             (17)

For the last inequality subtract the middle expression from the right
one. The numerator after multiplication by the positive denominators
is (z-2p)^2. This proves (4), without optimizing any computed orbit.

For any exterior terminal, (3) forces v_0>S, so (17) applies. For a
core terminal, P_A=||x_n||^2/R_0^2<=1/(d_min R_0^2). It follows that
d_min R_0^2>=M gives P_A<=1/M in both terminal branches. For (5),
v_0/kappa>=sqrt(M)-1>=1, so (16) again gives d_min R_0^2>=M.

## 7. The initial shell: exact core absorption and all tail products

All step excesses b_j-1=a c^j are positive. Let q_j be the product of
these excesses over the complete physical word H_j. From q_0=1 and
q_(j+1)=q_j^2 a c^j one obtains

    q_j=beta^(2^j-1)c^(-j).                             (18)

Every nonempty prefix product in H_j is at most a. For j=1 this is the
single product a. For the induction, a prefix in the left copy has the
claimed bound. At the middle bridge the product is
q_j a c^j=a beta^(2^j-1)<=a. A prefix continuing into the right copy
multiplies this by a prefix product of H_j, including the empty product
1; all those products are at most 1 because a<1. This proves the bound.
Therefore EVERY prefix product of the tail obtained by deleting only
the very first physical step is at most 1, by division by that first a.

If v_0<=1+a, then at the first step h_0=1+a,

    x_1=(t_0 A-aI)g_0.

Each t_0 d_l is in [0,1+a], so |t_0 d_l-a|<=1. Hence x_1 belongs to
E_A. The prefix-product bound now proves inductively that every actual
later point remains in E_A: the next prescribed point is its scalar
quadratic update and stays in that ellipsoid. The endpoint formula in
(6) follows from the tail product q_m/a.

Finally ||x_1||<=||x_0||. Indeed <x_0,g_0>>=||g_0||^2, so

    ||x_1||^2<=||x_0||^2-h_0(2-h_0)||g_0||^2<=||x_0||^2,

since 1<h_0<2. This proves (6). If x_0 is already in E_A, the same
prefix argument applies from the first query and gives P_A=q_m^2.

## 8. Comparisons with the COMPLETE same-word reference channels

The references are those of accepted b98bb807d514e80d,
1fca3e5dd555cb4a, and dfde2fa326c908bf, respectively. Their scopes are
not enlarged. For clarity their full definitions are recorded here.

For a word h of total mass S, put P_j=sum_(i<j)h_i and T_j=sum_(i>j)h_i.
The full single-cut functional is

    K_n(h)=max{1/(1+2S),
      max_(j<n) (h_j-1)_+^2/[(1+P_j)^2(1+2T_j)]}.

For F_ray_n(h), take ALL chronological checkpoint subsets of physical
indices, splitting h as (block_0,b_0,...,b_(k-1),block_k), with s_i the

    m_0=1/(1+s_0), O_0=0,
    m_(i+1)=((b_i-1)m_i-O_i)/(1+s_(i+1)),
    O_(i+1)=O_i+s_i m_i, 0<=i<=k-2.

Require m_i>0 and m_i>=m_(i-2) for i>=2. Define
z_term=(b_(k-1)-1)m_(k-1)-O_(k-1), and m_old=0 if k=1, otherwise
m_(k-2). Require z_term>=(1+s_k)m_old. Set
e_term=sum_(0<=i<k, i congruent k mod 2)s_i m_i^2. Optimize

    2e_term+2q z_term-(2s_k+1)q^2,
    m_old<=q<=z_term/(1+s_k).

For k=0 use z_term=1, e_term=m_old=0 and q in [0,1/(1+S)]. F_ray_n is

For the complex reference, let Poly_0(z)=1 and

and xi_*=gamma_*=0. The inner product on C is Re(conj(u)v). For

    q_ij=<gamma_j,xi_i-xi_j>+|gamma_i-gamma_j|^2/2.

For every directed simple cycle C on {*,0,...,n}, including 2-cycles,
let Area_C=sum_(j->i)Im(conj(xi_j)xi_i) and
Energy_C=sum_(j->i)|xi_i-xi_j|^2. The FULL schedule-dependent domain is

For z in D_h let ell_i be the maximum q-weight of a path i->*, with the

This is the full accepted channel, with initial point 1, minimizer 0,

Only rigorous bounds on these COMPLETE references are needed here.
With M=S+1, their accepted statements imply

    K_n>=1/(2M-1),  F_ray_n>=K_n,
    F_cx,n>= M^2/(2M-1)^3 > 1/(8M).                    (19)

For the complex bound, choose the real theta=1/(2S+1) in [0,1]. It

For either large-state regime P_A<=1/M gives

    P_A < 2K_n <= 2F_ray_n,
    P_A < 8F_cx,n.                                     (20)

No contrary ordering or equality is inferred. For the small shell,

## 9. Exact all-split benchmark comparison, proved here

Use the benchmark definitions from accepted b98bb807d514e80d:

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(k+l=n-1) Omega(C_k,C_l),
    B_n=max_(k+l=n-1) G(C_k,B_l),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2.

Every split k,l is retained. We prove B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1), without
assuming a benchmark asymptotic formula or running its recurrence.

Put eta=2lambda-1=lambda(4-lambda) and
Llin=(4x+lambda^2 y)/eta. Its two coefficients exceed 1, so Llin>=x+y.
Using lambda^2=2lambda+1 gives the explicit square

    eta^2[Llin^2-(x+y)Llin-xy]
      =(2x/lambda-sqrt(2)lambda*y)^2 >=0.

Therefore Llin>=Omega(x,y). At z=lambda Omega(x,y), the polynomial
whose larger root is G(x,lambda y) has value

    z^2-(4x+lambda y)z+4x^2
       =x[4x+lambda^2 y-eta Omega(x,y)] >=0.

Also z>=lambda(x+y)>=(4x+lambda y)/2, the vertex location. Hence
G(x,lambda y)<=lambda Omega(x,y). Monotonicity of G in its second
argument and induction in the ORIGINAL recurrences give B_n<=lambda C_n.

Put rho=log_2(lambda)>1, Dpow(t)=(1+t)^rho-1, and Lpow(u)=log Dpow(exp u).
For t=exp u>0, direct differentiation gives

    Lpow''(u)=rho*t*(1+t)^(rho-2)
      *[(1+t)^rho-1-rho*t]/Dpow(t)^2 >0.

The bracket vanishes at zero and has positive derivative thereafter.
Thus Dpow(t)Dpow(1/t)>=Dpow(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. For x,y>0 set
Z=(x^(1/rho)+y^(1/rho))^rho and t=(y/x)^(1/rho). It follows that
(Z-x)(Z-y)>=2xy, or Z^2-(x+y)Z-xy>=0. Also Z>=x+y; for this last
inequality, (u+v)^rho-u^rho has derivative in u at least zero and is
at least its value v^rho at u=0. Therefore Omega(x,y)<=Z. Zero arguments
follow directly. Induction gives C_n<=(n+1)^rho. Consequently

    B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^(m+1).                            (21)

For a finite explicit margin write delta=1/m<=1/128. Since

    c(c-2)=1+(4+2sqrt(2))delta+(3+2sqrt(2))delta^2
             <1+7delta+6delta^2,

one has alpha>(1-delta)/(1+7delta+6delta^2)>15/16. Indeed the last
inequality is equivalent to 1>121delta+90delta^2; at delta=1/128 the
numerator is 121*128+90=15578<16384, and the polynomial is increasing.
The first four binomial terms give

    (1+1/m)^m >= 8/3-1/m+1/(3m^2)>1021/384.

By (14), M>=alpha c^m, and hence for a large-state regime

    B_n P_A<=lambda/[alpha(1+1/m)^m]
              <(29/12)/(15315/6144)=14848/15315<1.      (22)

For the small shell, (6) and (21) give
B_n P_A<=lambda^(3-m), which is smaller than the constant in (22).
This proves (7).

Finally alpha->1, c->lambda, (1+1/m)^m->exp(1), and (14) implies
M/c^m->1. Equations (21) and P_A<=1/M yield (8); the small-shell bound
tends to zero. For a purely rational strict comparison,
lambda<5/2 and exp(1)>1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3 give lambda/exp(1)<15/16<1.
No equality or limiting constant for the actual B_n has been assumed.

## 10. Counterexample checks and the precise unresolved interface

The scalar drainage result loses the terminal core radius. It cannot be
strengthened into a mass-normalized objective bound on arbitrary words
using only that state: on the single step h=(2), take A=diag(1,2) and
any nonzero x_0 in E_A. Then x_1=-x_0 is in E_A, v_0=v_1=0, and P_A=1,
although 1/(1+sum h)=1/3. This is an exact counterexample to that general
shortcut, not a counterexample to an H_m-specific estimate.

There is also no lossless replacement of exterior starts by the unit
quadratic on the actual H_m. In the same anisotropic A, take

    x_0=(0,(2+a)/sqrt(2)),
    g_0=(0,1/sqrt(2)),  t_0=(1+a)/2,  v_0=1+a.

The first step gives x_1=(0,1/sqrt(2)); Section 7 proves every remaining
query is in the core. Its exact payoff is

    P_A=q_m^2/[a^2(2+a)^2] > q_m^2,

because a<1/lambda=sqrt(2)-1 implies a(2+a)<1. This refutes equality
of the whole ellipsoid family with the unit-quadratic orbit, while
remaining within the proved small-shell obstruction. A fixed-m strict
inequality persists under sufficiently small perturbations giving both
initial coordinates nonzero, by continuity of projection and the finite
GD recursion. No quantitative perturbation is needed or used elsewhere.

Two direct approaches to region (9) were tested. First, multiplier
drainage determines only that the terminal is in E_A, giving
P_A<=1/(d_min R_0^2). Its denominator is too small in (9). Second, the
exact core prefix products control an orbit ONLY after it enters the
core at a time whose remaining prefix products all stay within the
available core radius. Entry at a general internal H_j endpoint does
not supply that radius: the following bridge can multiply it by
a c^j>1 and can send it outside again. The one-step bound deliberately
discards this core radius when it replaces a reflected term by
kappa(h-2). Iterating that upper bound cannot recover the missing size.

For an all-family exclusion, one still needs an H_m-specific bound on

    sup { ||x_n||^2/||x_0||^2 :
          1<=kappa<=2, 1+a<v(x_0), d_min||x_0||^2<M },   (23)

where x_n is generated by the actual common-multiplier map (1)-(2).
These inputs necessarily have v_n=0: if v_n>0, then v_0>S, and (16)
gives d_min||x_0||^2>=(1+S/kappa)^2>=M, a contradiction.
The same calculation also shows the unknown normal state is below
kappa(sqrt(M)-1). The remaining issue is thus a concrete core-return
size estimate, not remote interpolation feasibility or an unknown SDP.

The full-family payoff question is BLOCKED at (23) in this allocation.
No argument here excludes high eccentricity, translated ellipsoids,
other curved bodies, or unrestricted adversaries. In particular accepted
e9a55f57461f253c is a fixed original H6 witness in dimension 66 and is
not an all-m assumption. Neither its data nor any stored float is used.

The exact benchmark and reference definitions are accepted facts cited
above. All further estimates, including the scalar benchmark envelope,

## 2. A jointly proved separated-switch construction

## 4. An exact value-independent three-query cycle identity

We derive the needed identity for general local data. Suppose three
consecutive gradients are v, v'=v+d, v''=v'+e, and the two steps
are a,b. Their positions differ by -a*v and -b*v'. Put

 d=-p*a*alpha*u,  e=-q*b*beta*v_dir,

Here p,q are the local dampings and v_dir denotes a direction,
distinct from the starting gradient v. The original cycle using
the first-to-third row and the two reverse adjacent rows is

 C=Q_(first,third)+Q_(third,second)+Q_(second,first).

All function values cancel. Its linear terms are

 a<d,v>+b<d+e,v'>,

and its half-squared-norm terms sum to

Regrouping gives

 C=[a<d,v>+||d||^2]+[b<e,v'>+||e||^2]
                                      +b<d,v'>+<d,e>

       -p*(1-p)*a^2*alpha^2-q*(1-q)*b^2*beta^2.      (19)

This is a literal sum of original Q rows. It assumes neither the
midpoint values nor any optimum. It is unchanged by translating all

does not assign a fictitious smooth convex function to the recurrence.

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED proof draft of the scoped statements below.

Accepted correctness inputs are1252b8823bb5a290 (normalization and the original

## 1. One growing body and the original physical word

Fix an integer m>=128. All vector norms and inner products are Euclidean. Put

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    b_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1, h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1))=H_m,
    S_j=sum H_j, S=S_m, M_j=1+S_j, M=M_m, T=2S+1,
    alpha=a/(c-2), Cax=c^m, D=Cax^2.

Every child uses this same enclosing m. Let e_0,...,e_m be the standard basis
of R^(m+1), and define the diagonal positive definite matrix and FILLED body

    d_l=c^(2l), 0<=l<=m, A=diag(d_0,...,d_m),
    E={g: <g,A g><=1},
    F(x)=max_(g in E) {<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.                 (1)

The squared semiaxis ratio is D=c^(2m), and dimension is m+1. The selected
full law allows EVERY x_0!=0 in this space. Orthogonal rotations or a common
rescaling produce equivalent instances but are unnecessary here. The actual
GD is x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i, g_i=grad F(x_i), retaining all n original steps.
We write f_i=F(x_i) and P=2f_n/||x_0||^2. Section2 proves that the unique
minimizer is0, so this denominator is the true squared initial distance.
Multiplying F by any L>0 and using h_i/L preserves the trajectory and P.

The elementary mass identities used below are

    M_j=alpha c^j+(1-alpha)2^j,
    0<alpha<1, M_j<=c^j, M_(j+1)<=c M_j,

c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1>beta, so alpha<1. The other inequalities follow
from c>2 and the two nonnegative terms in the mass formula. We shall use

    12/5<lambda<c<5/2, 3/8<a<1/2, Cax>16, S>1248.       (3)

For the upper bound on c, sqrt(2)<17/12 gives
c<(29/12)(129/128)<5/2. Then a=beta/c>(127/128)(2/5)>3/8.
The lower bound lambda>12/5 follows from sqrt(2)>7/5. The remaining bounds
follow from m>=128 and S>=2^m-1.

## 2. Exact static geometry, smoothness, minimum, and every original row

Completing the square in (1) identifies its unique maximizing vector g(x)
with the Euclidean projection of x onto E. Existence is by compactness;
uniqueness follows by strict convexity of squared distance on a convex set.
For x in E set t(x)=0 and g(x)=x. For x outside E let t(x)>0 be the unique root

    sum_(l=0)^m d_l x_l^2/(1+t(x)d_l)^2=1,
    g_l(x)=x_l/(1+t(x)d_l).                            (4)

The sum on the left is continuous, strictly decreasing for nonzero x,
larger than1 at zero, and tends to0. For the resulting g, <g,A g>=1 and

    <x-g,z-g>=t(<g,A z>-1)<=0, z in E,

by Cauchy--Schwarz in the A inner product. Expanding squared distances
proves that this g is the projection, including coordinates equal to zero.
There are no negative multipliers: projection onto the boundary SURFACE
would be a different problem for interior points.

For two projection pairs (x,g),(y,p), adding their normal inequalities gives
||g-p||^2<=<g-p,x-y>. Thus g is1-Lipschitz. Comparing the two maxima defining
F(x+u) and F(x) shows that
0<=F(x+u)-F(x)-<g(x),u><=||u||^2. Therefore F is differentiable with gradient
g, is1-smooth, and is convex as a maximum of affine functions. Integrating
the Lipschitz gradient along a segment also gives the sharper upper estimate
F(x+u)<=F(x)+<g(x),u>+||u||^2/2, used in Section5.

The feasible vector0 gives F>=0 and F(0)=0. For x!=0, a sufficiently small

Write t_i=t(x_i), including the optimum sample x_*=g_*=t_*=f_*=0. Exactly,

    x_i=(I+t_i A)g_i,
    f_i=||g_i||^2/2+t_i,

        =t_j(<g_j,A g_i>-<g_j,A g_j>)<=0.              (5)

For t_j=0 the expression is zero. Otherwise <g_j,A g_j>=1 and its other
inner product is at most1. Thus EVERY ordered adjacent, remote, and optimum

For two exterior samples, Q_ij=-(t_j/2)||g_i-g_j||_A^2, where
||v||_A^2=<v,A v>. These formulas apply to the same single F throughout.

The query is genuinely coupled. At an exterior point put
J(x)=sum_l d_l^2 x_l^2/(1+t d_l)^3>0. Implicit differentiation of (4) gives

    partial t/partial x_l=[d_l x_l/(1+t d_l)^2]/J(x),

      =-[d_k x_k/(1+t d_k)^2][d_l x_l/(1+t d_l)^2]/J(x), k!=l. (6)

This is nonzero when both coordinates are active. The denominators have
the SAME changing multiplier. In the core the Hessian is I. Outside, the

function is not a fixed quadratic, nor a sum of independent scalar modes.

## 3. An exact global state law with no loss of core amplitude

At each query retain ALL the weights

## Full original model and the exact reduction

For a physical length r, keep every h_i>=0, 0<=i<r, and every ordered
Lambda_ij>=0, 0<=i,j<=r, i!=j; put Lambda_ii=0. Define s=sum h_i,
A=1+s, e=ones(r+1), T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, and zero otherwise.
Write L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda, omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(r-1),2s)^T,
D=diag(h_i(2-h_i),-s(s+2)), and M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2.
The original constraints are L^T e=omega and M PSD on all R^(r+1).

The accepted original identity is V_h+sum Lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g)>.
Here Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0 by
1252b8823bb5a290, x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t, and
V_h=2sum h_i(f_i-f_r)+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-s(s+1)||g_r||^2.
In a direct coefficient audit the value coefficient is canceled by the flow;
the position terms are sym(L(T-I)); the gradient-difference terms are
sym(L)-diag(omega)/2. Addition of V_h's diagonal gives exactly M.
This is the full original coordinate certificate, not an actual-gradient
quotient. Every zero-step coordinate and every ordered multiplier survives.

Here is the joint algebra allowing a smaller factor. Since Le=0, the sum
of the flow residuals is zero: e^T(L^T e-omega)=0. Thus the first r flow
equations imply the terminal equation. Put H_i=sum_(t<i)h_t. Then
(Te)_i=1+H_i, including H_r=s, and under the flow equations

  e^T D e=-sum h_i^2-s^2,
  e^T L T e=omega^T T e=2s^2-2sum h_i H_i
             =s^2+sum h_i^2,

because 2sum h_i H_i=s^2-sum h_i^2. Consequently e^T M e=0.
For a PSD symmetric M this forces Me=0: for any vector z, positivity of
(e+t z)^T M(e+t z) for both signs of real t makes the linear coefficient
2 z^T Me vanish. Conversely, if the first r entries of Me vanish,
e^T M e=0 forces its last entry to vanish as well.

Let P denote the leading r-by-r principal block of M, let u=ones(r),
and let B be the (r+1)-by-r matrix formed by stacking I_r above -u^T.
For symmetric M with Me=0, its last column is (-Pu,u^T P u)^T,
so M=B P B^T. In particular M PSD iff P PSD: one implication is
principal restriction, and the other follows from this identity.

Every real PSD P has P=K K^T for a lower triangular real K with
nonnegative diagonal, including singular P. A proof by induction:
if P_00=0 then positivity of its two-coordinate restrictions forces
P_0j=0 for all j; put the first column of K equal to zero and factor
the remaining PSD principal block. If P_00>0, set K_00=sqrt(P_00)
and K_i0=P_i0/K_00. The Schur complement is PSD, since its quadratic
form is that of P on (-P_00^(-1)P_0,rest z,z); factor it inductively.
This argument imposes neither strict diagonal positivity nor a rank cap.

Hence the joint polynomial model is exactly

  (L^T e-omega)_i=0                      for i<r,
  (Me)_i=0                              for i<r,
  M_ij-(K K^T)_ij=0                     for 0<=i<=j<r,
  h_i>=0, Lambda_ij>=0, K_ii>=0.

It has r+r(r+1)+r(r+1)/2 variables and 2r+r(r+1)/2 equalities.
Full M=B K K^T B^T is read back from the original model; the dropped
terminal equations are explicitly reported. All retained expressions have
degree at most two jointly in h,Lambda,K. Finite numerical boxes below
are additional search restrictions, never asserted global bounds.

b=Lambda_10. Flow gives b=a+2h. Direct multiplication then gives

  M_00=h(2-h)+a(1-h),
  M_01=-a(1-h/2)-h(1-h),
  M_11=a-h^2,
  (Me)_0=h(1-a/2).

Since h>0 the null equation forces a=2, b=2+2h, and

h=5/4, a=2, b=9/2, K=sqrt(7)/4. Its remainder is nonzero.

the exponential series tail: k!>=2^(k-1) for k>=2, strictly for k>=3.
The lower bound in (14), with log3<2, proves positivity for S>=4.

This actual trajectory is not an exactly constant-gradient ray. On the
original H_m, put t=2h_0 in(2,3), or use the weaker t<4. Initially

increases. The first two gradients cannot be collinear.

## 1. Original word, normalization, and accepted reference scopes

Fix m>=8 and put

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
 H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
 N=2^m, n=N-1, h=H_m, S=sum_i h_i, M=1+S.

Every child uses these SAME enclosing-m parameters. The first physical
step satisfies 1<h_0=1+a<3/2. Counting occurrences of each level gives

 M=2^m+(beta/c)(c^m-2^m)/(c-2)
   =(1-zeta)2^m+zeta*c^m,
 zeta=beta/[c(c-2)] in (0,1).                         (1)

In particular M<c^m and M/c^m tends to1, since zeta tends to1 and
(2/c)^m tends to0. Also c^m/lambda^m tends to exp(1).

For any base function Phi with a proved positive gradient Lipschitz
constant Lbase and minimum Phi_star, use the actual project function

 f=(L/Lbase)(Phi-Phi_star),
 x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/Lbase) grad Phi(x_i),
 V=2(Phi(x_n)-Phi_star)/(Lbase*R_init^2),              (2)

where R_init is the distance to the WHOLE minimizer set. Thus f has
L-Lipschitz gradient and uses exactly the original steps h_i/L. The
quantity V is a single actual-instance score in the W=2R convention.

Accepted b98bb807d514e80d supplies the complete functional

 K_n(h)=max{1/(1+2S),
   max_(0<=j<n) (h_j-1)_+^2/
       [(1+sum_(i<j)h_i)^2(1+2sum_(i>j)h_i)]},

and the original ALL-split recurrence C_0=B_0=1,

 C_n=max_(0<=k<n) Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
 B_n=max_(0<=k<n) G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)),
 Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
 G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
 U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, B_n<=1+4n^(log_2 3).                 (3)

Accepted 1fca3e5dd555cb4a defines F_ray_n as the maximum over ALL feasible
chronological alternating-ray checkpoint choices, with its original
retained offsets, areas and terminal optimization. In particular

 Huber(h):=1/(2M-1) <= K_n(h) <= F_ray_n(h).          (4)

Accepted dfde2fa326c908bf defines Poly_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t*z),
xi_i=Poly_i(z), gamma_i=z*Poly_i(z), with a zero optimum sample. Its FULL
domain D_h imposes

 (Re(z)-|z|^2)*Energy_C >= 2*|Im(z)*Area_C|

on EVERY directed simple cycle C of {star,0,...,n}, where
Energy_C=sum_(j->i in C)|xi_i-xi_j|^2 and
Area_C=sum_(j->i in C)Im(conj(xi_j)*xi_i). Define the comparison

 Cfull(h)=sup_(z in D_h) Gap_h(z),                   (5)

where Gap_h is the maximal legal terminal score for those specified
points and gradients in the accepted fact. This is the full unaugmented
channel, not its universal lens and not a short-cycle screen.

One lower bound on this COMPLETE channel will suffice for several
comparisons. Set theta=1/(2M). It is real in (0,1), hence in D_h. The
actual scalar quadratic theta*x^2/2 gives

 Gap_h(theta)>=theta*Poly_n(theta)^2>1/(8M).         (6)

Indeed each theta*h_i is in [0,1/2), and multiplying the inequalities
(1-u)(1-v)>=1-u-v gives Poly_n(theta)>=1-theta*S>1/2.
This uses the maximality of Gap_h, not a false identification of Gap_h
with a quadratic value.

Accepted 04219554e41d9750 supplies the ORIGINAL ray limit and enclosure

 B_(2^m-1)/lambda^m -> Z_1,
 0<Z_1<=(sqrt(B_1)+3/100)^2=41209/10000,             (7)

where B_1=4 follows directly from (3). The proof's Section7 and the
full stated enclosure were read. No seed existence or seed consequence
from that fact is used. No new external theorem is imported.

The original problem asks whether W_n^*/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where
W_n^*=inf_(h in [0,infinity)^n) W_n(h). Its affirmative lower bound
requires one N_epsilon working for EVERY word at EVERY n>=N_epsilon.
Neither the diagnostic family (1) nor any result here provides that.

## 2. Direct finite-Gibbs calculations and all original rows

For an explicitly specified finite list of vectors v_s, positive weights
b_s, and temperature tau>0, put

 Phi_tau(x)=tau*log sum_s b_s*exp(<v_s,x>/tau),
 p_s(x)=b_s*exp(<v_s,x>/tau)/sum_t b_t*exp(<v_t,x>/tau),
 mu(x)=sum_s p_s(x)*v_s.

Differentiation of a finite sum gives, on the whole Euclidean space,

 grad Phi_tau=mu,
 Hess Phi_tau=(1/tau)[sum_s p_s v_s v_s^T-mu mu^T].  (8)

The quadratic form is a variance, so Phi_tau is convex. If the feature
diameter is Dfeat, its variance in any unit direction is at most
Dfeat^2/4. To prove this, for a random scalar T in [b,d], the nonnegative
quantity (T-b)(d-T) gives
Var(T)<=(d-E T)(E T-b)<=(d-b)^2/4.
Consequently Lbase=Dfeat^2/(4tau) is valid globally. One may also use
an explicitly proved sharper covariance bound in a particular geometry.

The EXACT probability update at the physical step is

 p_(i+1),s = p_i,s * exp[-h_i <v_s,mu_i>/(Lbase*tau)]
             / sum_t p_i,t*exp[-h_i <v_t,mu_i>/(Lbase*tau)]. (9)

This equation follows from the actual vector update; no label is chosen
after a step. Every weight remains strictly positive at every finite
query. All functions and recurrences in this manuscript are finite even
when their feature counts are large; none is evaluated by a host job.

Attainment must be checked separately. In the centered uniform examples
below, sum_s v_s=0 and the features span their stated ambient space.
Jensen's inequality gives Phi_1(x)>=0=Phi_1(0). Equality requires all
<v_s,x> equal; their mean is zero, so they all vanish and span implies
x=0. This proves the actual unique minimum, not an infimum at infinity.
The chain's attained minimum is computed explicitly in Section4.

Temperature is not a free normalization improvement. Choose x_star to
be a closest attained minimizer to the chosen initial point, and let
pi_s=p_s(x_star), z=(x-x_star)/tau and
Lbase=Ccov/tau, for a fixed proved covariance bound Ccov. Then

 Phi_tau(x)-Phi_tau(x_star)=tau*log sum_s pi_s exp(<v_s,z>),
 z_(i+1)=z_i-(h_i/Ccov)sum_s p_i,s v_s,
 V=2 log(sum_s pi_s exp(<v_s,z_n>))/(Ccov*||z_0||^2). (10)

Here sum_s pi_s v_s=0. The temperature cancels simultaneously from the
physical recurrence and the paid score at a fixed scaled initial state.
Changing that state, the features, weights, or dimension can still matter;
(10) does not exclude those choices or holding x_0 fixed while changing tau.

All original directed and optimum interpolation inequalities follow
from the actual function and its stated smoothness, as follows. For any
convex differentiable Lbase-smooth Phi and any x, define
k(u)=Phi(u)-<grad Phi(x),u>. It is minimized at x. Integrating its
Lipschitz gradient gives
k(y-grad k(y)/Lbase)<=k(y)-||grad k(y)||^2/(2Lbase).
Comparison with k(x) proves

 Phi(y)>=Phi(x)+<grad Phi(x),y-x>
                  +||grad Phi(y)-grad Phi(x)||^2/(2Lbase). (11)

With F_i=(Phi(x_i)-Phi_star)/Lbase and g_i=grad Phi(x_i)/Lbase,
(11) is exactly

 Q_ij=F_i-F_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0

for EVERY ordered pair of distinct physical queries, including BOTH
terminal orientations and EVERY optimum pair. This agrees with accepted
1252b8823bb5a290. No local-to-global inference about prescribed jets is
being used. Zero steps simply repeat an actual query.

## 4. Candidate two: coupled finite sign features and a weak support bound

Let a_chain>0 and let D=2(n+1). There are D-1 variable coordinates.
Fix the boundary values x_0=a_chain and x_D=0 only in this section, and
define on the variables x_1,...,x_(D-1)

 Phi_B(x)=sum_(j=0)^(D-1) log cosh(x_j-x_(j+1)).     (18)

The boundary indices are spatial, not time indices. This is EXACTLY a
finite Gibbs function, not a sum of quadratic surrogates:

 Phi_B(x)=log sum_(sigma in {-1,1}^D) 2^(-D)
       exp[a_chain*sigma_0
               +sum_(j=1)^(D-1)(sigma_j-sigma_(j-1))*x_j]. (19)

Equation (19) explicitly specifies every feature and positive weight.
No enumeration is needed to define this finite sum. Its Hessian is
the path difference matrix transposed, times a diagonal matrix of
sech^2 edge differences, times the difference matrix. For any variation
z with z_0=z_D=0,

 sum_(j=0)^(D-1)(z_j-z_(j+1))^2<=4sum_(j=1)^(D-1)z_j^2.

Thus the actual function is globally convex and L_B=4 is a valid
smoothness constant. We do not claim this bound is sharp. Since the
edge differences sum to a_chain, strict convexity of log cosh and
Jensen give the UNIQUE attained minimum

 x_star,j=a_chain*(1-j/D),
 Phi_B,star=D log cosh(a_chain/D).                   (20)

Start the variable vector at zero. Its true squared distance is

 R_B^2=a_chain^2*(D-1)(2D-1)/(6D).                  (21)

The finite sum of squares in (21) follows from
sum_(j=1)^(D-1)(D-j)^2=(D-1)D(2D-1)/6; the last identity is proved
by induction using the difference of the two cubic expressions.

At each physical time i the update is exactly

 x_(i+1),j=x_i,j+(h_i/4)
     [tanh(x_i,j-1-x_i,j)-tanh(x_i,j-x_i,j+1)].      (22)

The fixed boundary values are retained at every time. Induction on i
shows x_i,j=0 for all j>i: if j>i+1 both adjacent differences in (22)
are zero, including the right boundary. This holds for all finite
nonnegative steps, however large, and keeps all queries.

Put r_hor=n+1. At the terminal, x_n,j=0 for j>=r_hor. The first
r_hor edge differences sum to a_chain; all subsequent differences
vanish. Jensen gives the actual LOWER bound

 V_B >= Aprop := [r_hor log cosh(a_chain/r_hor)
                   -D log cosh(a_chain/D)]/(2 R_B^2)>0.   (23)

The numerator is positive because k log cosh(a_chain/k) is strictly
decreasing in positive k: with u=a_chain/k, its derivative is
log cosh(u)-u tanh(u)<0, as the latter expression has derivative
-u sech^2(u)<0 and is zero at u=0.

But the CERTIFICATE Aprop itself is too small. The inequality
log cosh(u)<=u^2/2 follows by integrating tanh(u)<=u for u>=0 and
using evenness. Dropping the positive subtracted minimum in (23),

 0<Aprop<=3D/[2r_hor(D-1)(2D-1)]<=3/(2r_hor^2).    (24)

The final bound uses D-1>=r_hor and D/(2D-1)<=1. This is an upper
bound on a proved lower guarantee; it is NOT an upper bound on V_B.
No assertion that (23) is attained by the physical GD trajectory is made.

This certificate failure is not repaired by making the chain's valid
smoothness constant sharp. When D>=3, at the zero variable vector an
internal edge has zero difference and Hessian contribution
(e_1-e_2)(e_1-e_2)^T. All other edge contributions are positive
semidefinite, so every valid global smoothness constant is at least2.
Using ANY such constant instead of4 preserves finite propagation and
the same constrained value in (23), and its normalized support guarantee
is at most2*Aprop. Thus all the vanishing comparisons below persist,
with at most a factor2. The original H_m domain has D>=3.

On original H_m, r_hor=N, so the COMPLETE references obey

 Aprop/Huber <=3(c/4)^m,
 Aprop/K_n <=3(c/4)^m,
 Aprop/F_ray_n <=3(c/4)^m,
 Aprop/Cfull <12(c/4)^m,
 B_n Aprop <(15/2)(3/4)^m ->0.                      (25)

The first and fourth estimates use M<c^m and (6); the last uses (3).
For m>=8, c< (9/8)(5/2)=45/16<4, and c tends to lambda<4, so
all four reference ratios vanish. The scope is the untouched-coordinate
certificate only. The coupled chain itself is not excluded: a large
physical step could create an actual error much greater than (23).
No computational or qualitative claim about that actual error is used
to discard the weak certificate route and move to the third geometry.

evidence:
# The assigned tree-Gibbs trajectory: conditional clocks and entropy payments

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. Worker max4, one
allocated round after completed48/attempted49, with completed ceiling49
and attempted ceiling50. TASK.md and master_guidance d70a595e12f4b50f
authorize this analytical investigation and explicitly forbid computation
and fact_submit. No new fact is claimed or submitted. All new arguments
are reproduced together here; no unverified finding is a premise.

## 1. Verdict and the precise remaining question

The specified terminal inequality is still UNRESOLVED. This draft proves
neither that the specified trajectory reaches the benchmark nor an
asymptotic upper obstruction for that trajectory. Its new interfaces are:

* an exact decomposition of the objective over conditional tree fields;
* an exact formula for every cumulative subtree clock, including its
  dependence on the actual endpoint ancestral coordinates;
* exact conditional relative-entropy and Euclidean-radius payment
  identities, with the squared-step and inter-iterate entropy terms;
* quantitative control of every instantaneous subtree mass by the actual
  entropy, with no assumed concentration;
* an explicit demonstration that the integrated linear occupation
  constraints alone admit endpoint zero on the ORIGINAL word;
* a finite original-benchmark comparison showing that preservation of
  the initial deepest field cannot by itself certify the target. That
  particular certificate needs amplification and an actual overstep in
  its changing conditional clock.

The last two items exclude only stated proof shortcuts. They do not
exclude this tree-Gibbs candidate. Even a positive answer for this
candidate would leave the original all-word/all-horizon bridge open.

## 2. Definitions, legality, and normalization reproduced from scratch

Fix an integer m>=8. Write

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
 H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
 n=2^m-1, N=2^m, h=H_m,
 r=2/c, Zgeom=sum_(j=0)^(m-1) r^j, w_j=r^j/Zgeom.

Every occurrence of a child word retains these SAME enclosing-m
parameters. Let S_t=sum_(i<t)h_i and S=S_n. Counting the two copies
at each join, or solving S_(j+1)=2S_j+1+a*c^j, gives

 1+S=2^m+(beta/c)(c^m-2^m)/(c-2)
     =(1-zeta)2^m+zeta*c^m,  zeta=beta/[c(c-2)].       (2.1)

Here 0<zeta<1: lambda(lambda-2)=1, c>lambda, and beta<1.

Use one orthonormal coordinate e_v for each binary word v of length
less than m. For a leaf s=(s_1,...,s_m), define

 a_s=sum_(j=0)^(m-1) sqrt(w_j)(-1)^(s_(j+1))e_(s_1...s_j),
 F(x)=log[N^(-1)sum_s exp(<a_s,x>)].                 (2.2)

The feature mean is zero, and every feature has squared norm one.
Different coordinate rows of the feature matrix are orthogonal. Rows
with disjoint supports have zero product. If one node is below the
other, the descendant row has equal positive and negative entries on
its support, on which the ancestor row is constant. Each row has
positive squared norm. Thus the matrix has row rank N-1.

Jensen's inequality applied to the exponential gives F>=0. Equality
requires all leaf logits to be equal; their sum is zero, so they must
all vanish. Full row rank then gives x=0. Consequently F has the UNIQUE
attained minimum zero at zero. The same rank argument shows that the
map from x to the N logits is onto their zero-sum subspace.

Differentiating this finite sum gives grad F=E_p a and Hess F=Cov_p(a),
where p_s=exp(<a_s,x>)/sum_t exp(<a_t,x>). To bound the Hessian, fix a
unit vector u and let A and B be the smallest and largest values of
<a_s,u>. For any random variable z in [A,B],

 E z^2 <=(A+B)E z-AB,
 Var(z)<=(B-A)^2/4-(E z-(A+B)/2)^2<=(B-A)^2/4.

The first inequality follows by averaging (z-A)(B-z)>=0.
If leaves first separate at level j, their squared distance is

             4w_j+2sum_(l>j)w_l.                   (2.3)

The quarter-distances strictly decrease with j, since the difference
between consecutive ones is w_j-w_(j+1)/2>0. The diameter bound above
therefore gives the globally valid constant

                  Ltree=(1+w_0)/2.                (2.4)

It is sharp. Choose a pair separating at the root. Prescribe equal
logits for that pair and logits smaller by T for every other leaf,
then subtract the common mean. Surjectivity of the logit map realizes
these logits at an actual finite x. As T tends to infinity the Gibbs
law tends to the equal law on that pair. Its covariance in the unit
feature-difference direction tends to the squared diameter divided by
four, namely Ltree. This establishes the global supremum.

Take t0=log(2) and the exact initial point

 x_0,(0^j)=t0/sqrt(w_j), 0<=j<m,
 x_0,v=0 on every other node.

The squared distance to the whole minimizer set is exactly

 R^2=t0^2 sum_(j=0)^(m-1)1/w_j
    =t0^2 r^(1-m) Zgeom^2.                          (2.5)

The last equality reverses the finite geometric sum. Run the actual
iteration x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/Ltree)grad F(x_i). For an arbitrary desired
smoothness L, the function (L/Ltree)F uses exactly steps h_i/L and has
the legal instance score 2F(x_n)/(Ltree R^2). All positions, values,
gradients, and the minimum are from this one finite static function.

## 3. Actual group probabilities and conditional fields

All coordinates off the all-left spine remain zero. At a point on
that spine, leaves with the same first right turn have equal logits.
A non-spine coordinate splits one such group into equal halves, so
its mean feature coordinate vanishes. Induction through every physical
step proves invariance.

Define y_(i,j)=sqrt(w_j)x_(i,0^j). For first exit k<m and the final
all-left leaf k=m, respectively, set

 q_k=2^(-k-1) (k<m), q_m=2^(-m),
 ell_(i,k)=sum_(j<k)y_(i,j)-y_(i,k) (k<m),
 ell_(i,m)=sum_(j<m)y_(i,j),
 P_(i,k)=q_k exp(ell_(i,k))/sum_(u=0)^m q_u exp(ell_(i,u)).  (3.1)

These are probabilities of the original leaves, aggregated only over
identical logits. In particular they are not free control variables.
Let

 Q_(i,j)=sum_(k=j)^m P_(i,k), 0<=j<=m,
 d_(i,j)=Q_(i,j+1)-P_(i,j)=2Q_(i,j+1)-Q_(i,j).

Then Q_(i,0)=1 and the exact coordinate update is

 y_(i+1,j)=y_(i,j)-(h_i w_j/Ltree)d_(i,j).           (3.2)

Initially the denominator in (3.1) is (m+4)/4, each side-group
unnormalized mass is 1/4, and the final unnormalized mass is 1. Thus

 P_(0,k)=1/(m+4) (k<m), P_(0,m)=4/(m+4),
 Q_(0,j)=(m-j+4)/(m+4),
 F(x_0)=log[(m+4)/4].                               (3.3)

For each time define conditional log-partitions recursively by

 A_(i,m)=0,
 A_(i,j)=log[(exp(-y_(i,j))+exp(y_(i,j)+A_(i,j+1)))/2],
 T_(i,j)=y_(i,j)+A_(i,j+1)/2.                       (3.4)

This is the conditional partition on the actual all-left depth-j
subtree with its original uniform conditional reference. The side
subtree contributes one because all its coordinates are zero. Direct
factorization gives

 A_(i,j)=A_(i,j+1)/2+log cosh T_(i,j),
 Q_(i,j+1)/Q_(i,j)=(1+tanh T_(i,j))/2,
 d_(i,j)=Q_(i,j)tanh T_(i,j),
 D_i:=F(x_i)=A_(i,0)=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)2^(-j)log cosh T_(i,j). (3.5)

Every A_(i,j) is nonnegative. In particular the objective is the FULL
sum in (3.5), rather than just its final two-leaf contribution.
The exact conditional-field update is

 T_(i+1,j)=T_(i,j)-alpha_(i,j)tanh T_(i,j)
                   +(A_(i+1,j+1)-A_(i,j+1))/2,
 alpha_(i,j)=h_i w_j Q_(i,j)/Ltree.                 (3.6)

Equation (3.6) retains the changing child partition. Dropping its last
term, or replacing alpha by a fresh copy of the original child word,
changes the actual process.

Since sum_k q_k ell_(i,k)=0, substitution in (3.1) also proves

 D_i=sum_k q_k log(q_k/P_(i,k)).                    (3.7)

The reference law is the FIRST argument of this relative entropy.

## 4. Exact cumulative subtree clocks

For any physical prefix length t and depth 0<=j<m, put

 Cclock_(t,j)=sum_(i<t)alpha_(i,j)
            =(w_j/Ltree)sum_(i<t)h_i Q_(i,j).

The complete history sum admits the exact identity

 Cclock_(t,j)=S_t/(Ltree Zgeom c^j)
               +sum_(l<j)c^(l-j)(t0-y_(t,l)).       (4.1)

To prove it, the relation d_(i,j)=2Q_(i,j+1)-Q_(i,j) and Q_(i,0)=1
give by finite induction

 Q_(i,j)=2^(-j)[1+sum_(l<j)2^l d_(i,l)].

Multiply by h_i and sum. Equation (3.2) gives

 sum_(i<t)h_i d_(i,l)=Ltree(t0-y_(t,l))/w_l.

Finally 2^l/w_l=Zgeom c^l and w_j 2^(-j)=1/(Zgeom c^j), proving (4.1).
There is also the mass version, valid through j=m:

 sum_(i<t)h_i Q_(i,j)
  =2^(-j)[S_t+Ltree Zgeom sum_(l<j)c^l(t0-y_(t,l))]. (4.2)

These formulas hold for every prefix, not just recursive block ends.
They do not assert that a nonlinear trajectory depends only on the
sum of its effective steps.

## 5. Actual entropy and radius payment identities

Let p_i^[j] be the conditional Gibbs law on the leaves of the depth-j
all-left subtree, and let u^[j] be the uniform conditional law there.
For probability vectors p and v with positive entries, define
KL(p||v)=sum_s p_s log(p_s/v_s). Set

 I_(i,j)=KL(p_i^[j]||u^[j]),
 Kstep_(i,j)=KL(p_i^[j]||p_(i+1)^[j]),
 E_(i,j)=sum_(l=j)^(m-1) w_l Q_(i,l)^2 tanh^2 T_(i,l),
 Rsub_(i,j)^2=sum_(l=j)^(m-1)y_(i,l)^2/w_l.

Every symbol uses the SAME actual iterate. Conditioned at depth j,
the subtree gradient has squared norm E_(i,j)/Q_(i,j)^2. Its actual
coordinate update has multiplier h_i Q_(i,j)/Ltree, because global
gradients in that subtree equal Q_(i,j) times conditional gradients.
It follows exactly that

 A_(i+1,j)-A_(i,j)
      =-h_i E_(i,j)/(Ltree Q_(i,j))+Kstep_(i,j),     (5.1)

 Rsub_(i+1,j)^2-Rsub_(i,j)^2
      =-2h_i Q_(i,j)(A_(i,j)+I_(i,j))/Ltree
                         +h_i^2 E_(i,j)/Ltree^2.   (5.2)

For completeness, the finite exponential-family calculation behind
(5.1) is as follows. If A is a conditional log-partition, g=grad A,
and z'=z-vg, then

 KL(p_z||p_z')=<g,z-z'>+A(z')-A(z)
              =v||g||^2+A(z')-A(z).

Here v=h_i Q_(i,j)/Ltree. Also the centered conditional feature mean
at the origin is zero, and

 <z,grad A(z)>=A(z)+KL(p_z||u^[j]).

Expanding ||z-vg||^2 proves (5.2). No limiting, continuous-time, or
independent-child approximation was taken. All probabilities are
strictly positive, so these expressions are finite. Nonnegativity of
each KL follows from -sum_s p_s log(v_s/p_s)>=sum_s(p_s-v_s)=0,
using log z<=z-1.

At the root, these give the exact telescopes

 D_n=D_0-(1/Ltree)sum_(i<n)h_i E_(i,0)
                                  +sum_(i<n)Kstep_(i,0),           (5.3)
 Rsub_(n,0)^2=R^2-(2/Ltree)sum_(i<n)h_i(D_i+I_(i,0))
                                  +(1/Ltree^2)sum_(i<n)h_i^2 E_(i,0). (5.4)

The positive Kstep terms in (5.1) and the squared-step terms in (5.2)
cannot be discarded to claim monotonicity or a terminal upper bound.
The forward conditional entropy has the additional exact decomposition

 I_(i,j)=sum_(l=j)^(m-1)[Q_(i,l)/Q_(i,j)]
          [T_(i,l)tanh T_(i,l)-log cosh T_(i,l)].    (5.5)

Indeed the conditional probability of reaching each spine node is
Q_(i,l)/Q_(i,j), and the divergence of its Bernoulli split from the
equal split is T tanh T-log cosh T. Side subtrees have zero conditional
divergence. This also records explicitly the different weights in
forward entropy (5.5) and reverse entropy (3.5). The same expansion
between consecutive conditional laws gives the further exact formula

 Kstep_(i,j)=sum_(l=j)^(m-1)[Q_(i,l)/Q_(i,j)]
   [log cosh T_(i+1,l)-log cosh T_(i,l)
      -(T_(i+1,l)-T_(i,l))tanh T_(i,l)].             (5.6)

For a single split its log probability is sigma*T-log(2 cosh T),
where sigma=+1 or -1. Taking the old-law expectation of the difference
between the old and new log probabilities gives the bracket in (5.6).
Multiplying by each node's old conditional reach probability and
summing proves the formula. Thus the payments in (5.1) have explicit
values in the same consecutive conditional fields; they are not free
nonnegative slack variables.

## 6. A quantitative mass bound without a concentration assumption

For every time i and depth 1<=j<=m, put u=2^j Q_(i,j) and
Phi(u)=u-1-log u. Then

                  Phi(2^j Q_(i,j))<=2^j D_i.        (6.1)

Split the sum in (3.7) between the subtree and its complement. The
conditional divergences are nonnegative, so D_i is at least the
binary divergence with reference mass p=2^(-j) and current mass Q:

 -p log(Q/p)-(1-p)log[(1-Q)/(1-p)].

Set u=Q/p. The inequality -log(1-z)>=z for z<1, applied to
z=p(u-1)/(1-p), bounds the second term below by p(u-1).
This proves (6.1), including Q<p. Further,

 Phi(u)-(sqrt(u)-1)^2=2[sqrt(u)-1-log sqrt(u)]>=0.

Consequently

 (1-sqrt(2^j D_i))_+^2 <=2^j Q_(i,j)
                         <=(1+sqrt(2^j D_i))^2,     (6.2)
 alpha_(i,j)<=h_i/(Ltree Zgeom c^j)
                         *(1+sqrt(2^j D_i))^2.     (6.3)

These are bounds from the actual entropy at the SAME time; terminal
small entropy alone supplies no bound for earlier clocks. The initial
state (3.3), for example, is very far from uniform at deep levels.

There is also a quantitative endpoint enclosure for (4.1). Define
U_l(D)=arcosh(exp(2^l D)), with arcosh z=log(z+sqrt(z^2-1)) for z>=1.
The nonnegative summands in (3.5) give

 |T_(t,l)|<=U_l(D_t),  0<=A_(t,l+1)/2<=2^l D_t,
 -U_l(D_t)-2^l D_t<=y_(t,l)<=U_l(D_t).

Inserting these into the exact clock formula yields

 Cbase_(t,j)-sum_(l<j)c^(l-j)U_l(D_t)
 <= Cclock_(t,j)
 <= Cbase_(t,j)+sum_(l<j)c^(l-j)[U_l(D_t)+2^l D_t], (6.4)

where Cbase_(t,j)=S_t/(Ltree Zgeom c^j)+t0 sum_(l<j)c^(l-j).
Unlike (6.3), this bounds an entire accumulated clock using the
CURRENT entropy and the elapsed physical step sum. It still does not
control the individual factors in the nonlinear update (3.6).

## 7. Why cumulative occupation constraints do not settle the target

For the ORIGINAL S in (2.1), and every m>=8, terminal y_(n,j)=0 is
compatible with ALL linear integrated gradient equations and positive
time-averaged group occupations. This is an endpoint relaxation only:
the following probability vector is not claimed to be an actual GD
history.

Set K0=Ltree Zgeom t0 and define

 Tbar_j=2^(-j)[S+K0 sum_(l<j)c^l], 0<=j<=m,
 Vbar_j=Tbar_j-Tbar_(j+1)
       =2^(-j-1)[S-K0(c^j-sum_(l<j)c^l)], 0<=j<m,
 Vbar_m=Tbar_m.                                    (7.1)

Then sum_j Vbar_j=S and 2Tbar_(j+1)-Tbar_j=K0(c/2)^j
=Ltree t0/w_j. Thus Pbar_j=Vbar_j/S, if positive, satisfies exactly
the integrated version of (3.2) with terminal zero. We now prove
positivity using the original word rather than an asymptotic schedule.

For m>=8, beta>=7/8 and c<11/4. The latter follows from
sqrt(2)<13/9 and c<=(9/8)lambda. Equation (2.1) gives

 S>=beta*c^(m-1)/(c-2)-1
   >(7/6)c^(m-1)-1>c^(m-1).                        (7.2)

For the final inequality, c^(m-1)>2^(m-1)>=128. Since
Zgeom<c/(c-2), Ltree Zgeom=(Zgeom+1)/2<(c-1)/(c-2).
Also c>2 makes c^j-sum_(l<j)c^l increase with j. Hence its largest
price in (7.1) satisfies

 K0[c^(m-1)-sum_(l<m-1)c^l]
 <t0[c^(m-1)+1/(c-2)]
 <(3/4)[c^(m-1)+5/2]<c^(m-1)<S.                  (7.3)

Here log2<3/4 follows by the strict trapezoid bound for the integral
of 1/t on [1,2], and 1/(c-2)<lambda<5/2. Thus all Vbar_j are
strictly positive, including Vbar_m. This proves the stated relaxation
claim. It does NOT construct an actual trajectory ending at the
minimum, and it does not satisfy or replace the nonlinear identities
(3.1), (3.6), or (5.1). It precisely shows what extra information a
proof using (4.1) must retain: chronological conditional response.

A separate exact counterexample rules out replacing that response by
the sum of clocks. On the root-only slice of the SAME F, all descendants
are zero and F=log cosh y. Its root update is y'=y-k tanh y, where
k=h w_0/Ltree. Start this test state at y=t0, set A=5t0/3, B=A/2,
and use physical steps A Ltree/w_0 and B Ltree/w_0. For order (A,B),
the first step reaches zero because tanh t0=3/5, and the terminal is
zero. For order (B,A), the first state is t0/2 and tanh(t0/2)=1/3,
so the terminal is t0/2-5t0/9=-t0/18. Both orders have the same total
clock A+B. These are actual states and gradients of F, but their test
start and test word differ from the assignment. This refutes the
clock-sum substitution, not the assigned terminal inequality.

## 8. The exact original threshold and a finite deepest-pair screen

Retain the original recurrences

 C_0=B_0=1,
 C_n=max_(k+l=n-1)(C_k+C_l+sqrt(C_k^2+6C_k C_l+C_l^2))/2,
 B_n=max_(k+l=n-1)[2C_k+B_l/2+sqrt(B_l^2+8C_k B_l)/2].

The exact requested bound is D_n>=eta_m, where

 eta_m=Ltree t0^2 r^(1-m)Zgeom^2/(2B_n),
 Theta_m=N eta_m=Ltree t0^2 r Zgeom^2 c^m/(2B_n).    (8.1)

The accepted fact04219554e41d9750 supplies, with Z_1 its denominator
ray constant rather than our geometric sum,

 B_(2^m-1)<=lambda^m Z_1,
 Z_1<=(sqrt(B_1)+3/100)^2=41209/10000.              (8.2)

The identity B_1=4 follows immediately from its single defining split.
Only this existing exact enclosure is used; no benchmark evaluation,
DP, replay, or unproved numerical constant occurs here.

For every m>=32, there is the explicit finite bound

                    Theta_m>51200/41209>1.         (8.3)

Indeed sqrt(2)<47/33 implies c<=(33/32)lambda<5/2, so r>4/5.
The first sixteen terms of Zgeom give

 Zgeom>5[1-(4/5)^16]>24/5,

since 4^8=65536<78125=5^7. The integral of 1/t on [1,2] is strictly
larger than its midpoint lower bound 2/3, giving t0^2>4/9. Also
Ltree>1/2. The first four terms of the binomial expansion give, for
m>=8,

 (1+1/m)^m >=2+(m-1)/(2m)+(m-1)(m-2)/(6m^2)
            >=2+7/16+7/64=163/64>5/2.

Substitute these bounds and (8.2) into (8.1):

 Theta_m > [(1/2)(4/9)(4/5)(24/5)^2(5/2)/2]
                    *(10000/41209)=51200/41209.

The exact entropy decomposition gives the familiar deepest-pair lower
certificate D_n>=(2/N)log cosh y_(n,m-1). Its being strong enough for
the target would require

             2 log cosh y_(n,m-1)>=Theta_m.         (8.4)

But preservation of the initial amplitude would give only

 2 log cosh y_(n,m-1)<=2 log cosh(log2)=2 log(5/4)<1/2.

This is below (8.3). More strongly, (8.4) requires
|y_(n,m-1)|>1, because log cosh z<=z^2/2, proved by integrating
tanh z<=z for z>=0 and using evenness. Thus a deepest-field-only
certificate needs amplification beyond the initial log2, not merely
persistence of a nonzero initial tail coordinate. The full entropy
could still reach the target through other levels.

At the last level (3.6) has no forcing term:

 y_(i+1,m-1)=y_(i,m-1)-alpha_(i,m-1)tanh y_(i,m-1). (8.5)

If 0<=alpha<=2, then |y-alpha tanh y|<=|y|: for y>=0 use
0<=alpha tanh y<=2y, and then use oddness. Consequently success of
the particular certificate (8.4), for m>=32, requires at least one
actual alpha_(i,m-1)>2. Here the largest original step is
h_max=1+beta*c^(m-2), and h_i/(Ltree Zgeom c^(m-1))<1:
use h_max<2c^(m-2), c>2, and Ltree Zgeom>1. By (6.3) such an index
must satisfy

 N D_i >2( sqrt(2 Ltree Zgeom c^(m-1)/h_i)-1 )^2.   (8.6)

This necessary intermediate-entropy condition uses that SAME actual
h_i. It does not assert that such an index occurs. In particular it
cannot be inferred from an assumed fresh isolated child law.

For orientation only, (8.1), the accepted ray limit, and the elementary
limit (1+1/m)^m->exp(1) give

 Theta_m -> exp(1) L_inf t0^2 r_inf /
                        [2 Z_1(1-r_inf)^2],
 r_inf=2/lambda, L_inf=(2-r_inf)/2.                 (8.7)

Neither this limit nor (8.3) replaces the exact finite threshold in
the remaining problem.

## 9. Two direct routes and what remains missing

Route A attempted to integrate the changing subtree clocks and use
the endpoint constraints to force residual entropy. Equations (4.1)
and (4.2) succeed exactly. The positive occupations (7.1)--(7.3) show
that their linear endpoint relaxation permits D_n=0. This is a scoped
failure of that relaxation, not evidence that the actual endpoint is
zero. The scalar test in Section7 separately defeats replacing
chronological nonlinear updates by their total effective time.

Route B attempted to obtain the threshold from survival of the deepest
initial field. The conditional decomposition is exact, and (6.1)
supplies a quantitative change-of-measure bound. The finite price in
Section8 shows that persistence alone cannot make the deepest-pair
certificate sufficient. Its amplification alternative needs an actual
conditional overstep and the intermediate entropy required by (8.6).
Neither amplification nor its absence has been established on H_m.
This route does not control the contribution of the other levels.

The remaining inequality for the completely specified trajectory is

 sum_(j=0)^(m-1)2^(m-j)log cosh T_(n,j)
             >= Ltree t0^2 r Zgeom^2 c^m/(2B_(2^m-1))              (9.1)

for every sufficiently large m, or a strict eventual reverse inequality
for this same object. T, A, and Q in (9.1) must be generated by
(3.1)--(3.6), with initial values (3.3) and the original physical word.
A next estimate must control the chronological conditional partition
changes or the inter-iterate conditional KL payments across the large
steps and their retained suffixes. A bound on final mass alone, a
uniform-reset clock, or a deepest-coordinate persistence statement
does not fill this gap. No global or trajectory-specific entropy
monotonicity has been assumed.
