# Backward initial-state design in the fixed tree-Gibbs function

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. Worker max, round52.
TASK.md and master_guidance0b8c03866bb298f5 allocate one analytical round
after completed51/attempted52, with ceilings completed52/attempted53.
No host mathematical evaluation, solver, DP, trajectory replay, machine
algebra, installation, fact_submit, formal verification, consult, or
native subagent is used. No new fact is claimed. The outer-loop count
after this session returns has not been observed.

Every new calculation used below is reproduced in this document. The
canonical draft38da1067bcd1a0c8 and independent draft1ad14d90628c1312 were
read for orientation, not imported as established premises. The accepted
input for the main calculations is the original benchmark ray enclosure
in fact04219554e41d9750. Its seed conclusions are not used. Two further
accepted reference facts are named only for the optional comparison
after the actual canonical-Huber inequality is proved.

## 1. Verdict and exact scope

There are exactly TWO actual design mechanisms in this pilot.

1. Equal fields on all nodes of one depth give an exactly invariant
   scalar subsystem of the SAME static tree function. For every m>=128
   a rigorously selected backward branch gives terminal value log cosh1,
   an explicit nonzero initial state, and its full original Euclidean
   radius. However, EVERY nonzero start in any of the three deepest
   such strata has actual score V<1/(2S), hence B_n V<7/8. This closes
   those strata only, including their backward redesigns.

2. A full-vector backward-path construction concentrated at one exposed
   leaf has a unique solution in explicit product balls. The initial
   point is specified by a uniformly convergent iteration, not by
   unproved inverse equations. Its actual terminal point, terminal
   value, all physical steps, and two-sided radius bounds are proved.
   Its actual score satisfies B_n V<9/10 for every m>=128 and
   B_n V -> Z_1/(2 exp(1))<1. It is strictly below the same-word
   canonical Huber value. This is a limitation of the selected branch.

A general coercive preimage argument is a preliminary to mechanism2,
not a third candidate. It proves existence but its generic norm bound
cannot certify B_n V>=1 for ANY terminal point on these words. The
unrestricted cheapest-preimage problem, including other branches for
our explicit terminal point, remains substantively BLOCKED. Neither
the whole tree function nor its arbitrary initial states are excluded.

The original all-n/all-nonnegative-word exact-profile Goal remains OPEN.
Even a successful tree construction on the diagnostic words would not
prove the required uniform statement over all words and all horizons.

## 2. Original words and original all-split benchmark

Fix an integer m>=128 for the rest of the document. Put

 lambda=1+sqrt2, beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
 H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
 N=2^m, n=N-1, h=H_m, S=sum_(i=0)^(n-1) h_i.

All children retain these SAME enclosing-m parameters. Solving the
recursion for the sum, or counting the copies of each bridge, gives

 1+S=N+(beta/c)(c^m-N)/(c-2)
     =(1-zeta)N+zeta*c^m,
 zeta=beta/[c(c-2)].                                      (2.1)

The largest physical step is hmax=1+beta*c^(m-2). Since
lambda(lambda-2)=1, one has 0<zeta<1 and S<c^m.

Retain the ORIGINAL recurrences, for integers k in the indicated ranges:

 C_0=B_0=1,
 C_t=max_(0<=k<t) Omega(C_k,C_(t-k-1)),
 B_t=max_(0<=k<t) G(C_k,B_(t-k-1)),
 Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
 G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
 U_t^ZJ=1/B_t.                                            (2.2)

There is no surrogate recurrence or new benchmark evaluation here.
Accepted fact04219554e41d9750 gives, with the SAME B_t,

 B_(2^m-1)/lambda^m -> Z_1,
 B_(2^m-1)<=Z_1*lambda^m,
 0<Z_1<=(sqrt(B_1)+3/100)^2=41209/10000<33/8.              (2.3)

Indeed B_1=G(1,1)=4. The full statement and its Section7 ray proof were
read. This accepted fact, not either unverified Gibbs draft, supplies
the benchmark limit and enclosure used below.

Several elementary bounds will be useful. Write epsilon=1/m. Expanding
c(c-2) gives

 c(c-2)=1+2lambda(lambda-1)epsilon+lambda^2 epsilon^2.

For m>=128, lambda<5/2 implies the last two terms total less than
8epsilon. Hence

 zeta>(1-epsilon)/(1+8epsilon)>=1-9epsilon>=119/128.

Also c<5/2: for example lambda<29/12 and
(29/12)(129/128)<5/2. Since c^m>128, (2.1) now gives

             (9/10)c^m<S<c^m.                           (2.4)

For completeness, the lower bound follows from
S/c^m>119/128-1/128=59/64>9/10.

The binomial expansion, already for m>=16, gives

 (1+1/m)^m >= 2+(1-1/m)/2
                   +(1-1/m)(1-2/m)/6
             >=2+15/32+35/256>13/5.

Because lambda^m>32, (2.1)-(2.3) imply the convenient finite screen

 S/lambda^m>(119/128)(13/5)-1/32=1527/640,
 B_n/(2S)<1320/1527<7/8.                                  (2.5)

Finally zeta->1, (2/c)^m->0, and
m log(1+1/m)->1 show

 S/c^m->1, c^m/lambda^m->exp(1),
 B_n/(2S)->Z_1/(2 exp(1))<99/128<1.                       (2.6)

For the displayed rational gap, use Z_1<33/8 and exp(1)>8/3.
The logarithmic limit follows, for example, by integrating
1-u<=1/(1+u)<=1 between0 and1/m.

## 3. The fixed function, sharp smoothness, and true minimum

Set r_tree=2/c and

 Zgeom=sum_(j=0)^(m-1) r_tree^j,
 w_j=r_tree^j/Zgeom.

For every binary word v of length j<m use an orthonormal coordinate e_v.
For a leaf s=(s_1,...,s_m) define

 a_s=sum_(j=0)^(m-1) sqrt(w_j)(-1)^(s_(j+1))*e_(s_1...s_j),
 F_m(x)=log[N^(-1)sum_s exp(<a_s,x>)].                      (3.1)

This is exactly the fixed function in TASK.md. Each feature has norm1.
The feature mean is zero. Distinct coordinate rows of the feature
matrix are orthogonal: their supports are disjoint, or the descendant
row sums to zero inside a region on which the ancestor row is constant.
Each row has positive squared norm. The matrix therefore has rank N-1.

Jensen gives F_m(x)>=0, with equality only when all leaf logits are
equal. Their sum is zero; rank then implies x=0. Thus the WHOLE
minimizer set is {0} and the minimum is0. In particular every radius
below is the actual Euclidean distance to the unique minimizer.

For finite x define p_s(x)=exp(<a_s,x>)/sum_t exp(<a_t,x>) and
g(x)=sum_s p_s(x)a_s. Differentiating the finite sum gives

 grad F_m=g, Hess F_m=sum_s p_s a_s a_s^T-g g^T.            (3.2)

The Hessian is a covariance, hence positive semidefinite. For a scalar
random variable T in [b,d], averaging (T-b)(d-T)>=0 yields
Var(T)<=(d-E T)(E T-b)<=(d-b)^2/4. Applying this in every unit direction
bounds the covariance by one quarter of the squared feature diameter.

If two leaves first separate at depth j, their squared distance is

                 4w_j+2sum_(ell>j)w_ell.

The quarter-distances strictly decrease with j, because their successive
differences are w_j-w_(j+1)/2>0. Consequently

              Ltree=(1+w_0)/2=(Zgeom+1)/(2Zgeom)            (3.3)

is a global gradient Lipschitz constant. It is sharp. The logit map
is onto the zero-mean subspace, by the rank calculation. Prescribe equal
logits on two leaves separating at the root and logits lower by T on
the others, and subtract the common mean. These are realized by a finite
x. As T tends to infinity the covariance tends to that of the equal
two-point distribution, whose variance in the feature-difference
direction is Ltree. No new fitting problem is hidden in this argument.

The full physical iteration throughout is

             x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/Ltree)g(x_i).                (3.4)

For a requested smoothness L>0 take the project objective
f=(L/Ltree)F_m. It is L-smooth and (3.4) uses exactly steps h_i/L.
The actual normalized score is

                    V=2F_m(x_n)/(Ltree||x_0||^2).         (3.5)

Legality includes every original interpolation row. To reproduce this
without importing a draft, fix x and set k(u)=F_m(u)-<g(x),u>.
Convexity makes x a minimizer of k. Integrating its Lipschitz gradient
along a step of length1/Ltree gives
k(y-grad k(y)/Ltree)<=k(y)-||grad k(y)||^2/(2Ltree).
Comparison with k(x) yields

 F_m(y)>=F_m(x)+<g(x),y-x>
                         +||g(y)-g(x)||^2/(2Ltree).

After division by Ltree this is every directed normalized original
Q_ij<=0, including both terminal orientations and all optimum rows.
There is no independently prescribed jet or label transition.

We will use

 9/2<Zgeom<6,  1/2<Ltree<1,
 11/4<Ltree*Zgeom<7/2,
 4/7<kappa_m:=c/(Ltree*Zgeom)<10/11.                       (3.6)

For the upper bound, Zgeom<c/(c-2)<=lambda/(lambda-2)
=lambda^2<6. For the lower bound, c<5/2 gives r_tree>4/5;
the first11 terms have sum greater than 5(1-(4/5)^11)>9/2. The last strict inequality
is the exact integer inequality10*4^11<5^11. The other assertions
follow from (3.3) and2<c<5/2. In particular

 Zgeom->lambda^2, Ltree*Zgeom->2+sqrt2,
                       kappa_m->1/sqrt2.                 (3.7)

## 4. Mechanism1: actual symmetric inverse branches with paid norm

For a fixed depth d in {0,...,m-1} define the full vector X_d(y) by

 X_d(y)_v=y/sqrt(w_d) if |v|=d, and0 otherwise.

Exactly half the leaves have logit+y and half have logit-y, so
F_m(X_d(y))=log cosh y. Every depth-d subtree has the same partition
sum. Thus gradients at ancestors vanish. Below depth d, each relevant
pair of halves has equal logits and gradients vanish. At a node of
depth d its Gibbs subtree mass is2^(-d), and its left-minus-right
conditional mass is tanh y. Therefore

 g(X_d(y))_v=2^(-d)sqrt(w_d)tanh y for |v|=d,
 g(X_d(y))_v=0 at other depths.                            (4.1)

This proves invariance at EVERY physical query for any new starting y.
It proves the norm identity as well:

 ||X_d(y)||^2=2^d y^2/w_d=Zgeom*c^d*y^2.                  (4.2)

Define q_d=1/(Ltree*Zgeom*c^d) and alpha_i=q_d h_i. The exact
scalar physical recurrence and its original score are

 y_(i+1)=y_i-alpha_i tanh y_i,
                 V=2q_d log cosh(y_n)/y_0^2.             (4.3)

For every d>=m-3, all alpha_i<1. Indeed

 alpha_i<=hmax/(Ltree*Zgeom*c^(m-3))
          =(c^(3-m)+beta*c)/(Ltree*Zgeom)<1,               (4.4)

because the numerator is less than1/4+5/2=11/4 and the denominator
exceeds11/4 by (3.6).

Here is a concrete backward construction, choosing d=m-1 and y_n=1.
For i=n-1,...,0 let y_i be the unique positive solution of

                     y_i-alpha_i tanh y_i=y_(i+1).        (4.5)

Existence and the branch are proved, not assumed: the function
s-alpha_i tanh s has derivative at least1-alpha_i>0, maps the real
line onto itself because its difference from s is bounded by alpha_i,
and is zero at0. At s=y_(i+1) its value is smaller than y_(i+1),
while at s=y_(i+1)+alpha_i it is larger. Thus

             y_(i+1)<y_i<y_(i+1)+alpha_i.

This also makes (4.5) an explicit inverse-branch specification using a
unique root in a displayed bounded interval. Define x_0=X_(m-1)(y_0).
By (4.1), its actual forward trajectory is x_i=X_(m-1)(y_i), and

 x_n=X_(m-1)(1), F_m(x_n)=log cosh1,
 1<y_0<1+q_(m-1)S,
 R_init^2=Zgeom*c^(m-1)*y_0^2
          <Zgeom*c^(m-1)*(1+q_(m-1)S)^2.                  (4.6)

This is a new initial point and its own true norm. The old all-left
log2 radius is not used. Every scalar state is in the SAME F_m.

Let qdeep=q_(m-1). The exact score and explicit positive bound are

 V_sym=2qdeep log cosh1/y_0^2
        >2qdeep log cosh1/(1+qdeep S)^2.                  (4.7)

It is useful to screen this whole stratum before further work. For
ANY nonzero initial y_0 at ANY d>=m-3, oddness allows y_0>0.
Equation (4.4) implies 0<y_n<=...<=y_0. With t=y_n and T=q_d S,

       y_0=t+sum_i alpha_i tanh y_i>=t+T tanh t.

For t>0, log cosh t<t tanh t, since their difference has derivative
t sech^2 t>0 and is0 at0. Also (t+T tanh t)^2>=4T t tanh t.
Combining these inequalities with (4.3) proves the ACTUAL upper bound

              V<1/(2S), hence B_n V<7/8.                 (4.8)

This is an obstruction for these specified invariant strata and all
their initial states, not only for a selected lower-bound certificate.
It says nothing about depths d<=m-4 with overstepping, simultaneous
fields at different depths, or general starts.

The constructed branch does have the correct exponential order:
using qdeep*c^m=kappa_m, equations (2.6),(3.7),(4.7)-(4.8) give

 liminf B_n V_sym >= (Z_1/exp(1))
                 *[sqrt2 log cosh1/(1+1/sqrt2)^2]>0,
 limsup B_n V_sym <=Z_1/(2 exp(1))<1.                     (4.9)

No limit of y_0 is asserted or needed. The early screen (4.8) stops
this subfamily without pursuing a sharper scalar optimum.

## 5. Mechanism2 preliminary: full preimages exist, but a generic price fails

The finite-Gibbs function satisfies ||g(x)||<=1 and F_m(x)<=||x||,
because all features have norm1. For any terminal point y and any
physical step h>=0 set tau=h/Ltree and minimize over the full space

             Psi_y(x)=||x-y||^2/2-tau F_m(x).

The quadratic term dominates the displayed linear upper bound on F_m,
so Psi_y is coercive and continuous and has a global minimizer. At
every minimizer its gradient vanishes, which says

                      x-tau g(x)=y.                     (5.1)

Thus every one-step map is onto even when its long step is noninjective.
Iterating this existence proof backwards gives an actual complete
orbit to ANY prescribed terminal point z. Its original radius obeys

       ||x_0||<=||z||+sum_i h_i/Ltree=||z||+A,
                         A:=S/Ltree.                    (5.2)

The same bound holds for every preimage, by telescoping its actual
forward path and using ||g||<=1. It is not an invertibility assertion.

The normalized payoff certified by (5.2) alone is

       Cgeneric(z)=2F_m(z)/(Ltree(||z||+A)^2).

For t=||z||, F_m(z)<=t and (t+A)^2>=4tA show

     Cgeneric(z)<=1/(2S),
                     B_n Cgeneric(z)<7/8                 (5.3)

for EVERY terminal z. This rules out this proof certificate at benchmark
scale; it is NOT an upper bound on the actual score of an arbitrary
preimage. Merely citing global solvability and (5.2) cannot solve the
assigned diagnostic target.

The next section selects and prices a concrete full-path branch. It is
the actual construction within mechanism2. It does not assume that
its selected preimages are the global minimizers used in this preliminary.

## 6. Mechanism2: one global backward branch concentrated at a leaf

Fix the all-left leaf s0=0^m and its unit feature v=a_(s0). Define

 A_i=sum_(k=i)^(n-1) h_k/Ltree, 0<=i<=n, so A_0=A and A_n=0,
 ellN=log N,
 t=A+2ellN, D=A+ellN,
 z=t v, u_i=(t+A_i)v,
 delta_min=2w_(m-1),
 Econc=(N-1)exp(2-t delta_min).                               (6.1)

The centers u_i are determined by the WHOLE original physical word.
They are reference vectors for a proved construction, not alleged GD
states. The terminal point will be exactly z.

For a leaf s!=s0 first separating at depth j,

 <v,a_s>=sum_(ell<j)w_ell-w_j,
 delta_j:=1-<v,a_s>=2w_j+sum_(ell>j)w_ell.                 (6.2)

The successive differences delta_j-delta_(j+1)=2w_j-w_(j+1)>0,
so the smallest gap is delta_min. If ||x-u_i||<=1, then

 <v-a_s,x> >= (t+A_i)delta_j-||v-a_s||
             >=t delta_min-2.

The total inactive Gibbs mass is at most Econc. Consequently, on EVERY
one of these balls,

        ||g(x)-v||<=2*Econc,  ||Hess F_m(x)||op<=4*Econc.           (6.3)

The first bound follows by summing p_s(a_s-v). For the second, in
any unit direction, variance is at most the second moment about v;
||a_s-v||<=2 and only inactive leaves contribute. This proves the
Hessian bound directly from (3.2), with no concentration assumption
on an unknown orbit.

Here Econc is quantitatively tiny. Equations (2.4),(3.6) give

 t delta_min>=2S w_(m-1)/Ltree
             =(S/c^m)kappa_m N>(18/35)N>N/2.              (6.4)

Also A<2c^m<2*3^m. Thus

 A*Econc<2*6^m exp(2-N/2)<exp(2m+3-2^(m-1))<1/1000.           (6.5)

For the second inequality use2<exp(1) and6<exp(2). For the third,
2^(m-1)>=2m+16 for every m>=8, by induction starting at8, and
exp(13)>2^13>1000. In particular A>1 and Econc<1/1000 as well.
These are analytical inequalities, not host numerical evaluations.

On the finite product of closed Euclidean balls

          Ball=product_(i=0)^(n-1) {x:||x-u_i||<=1},

use the maximum coordinate norm. Define the simultaneous map

       T(X)_i=z+sum_(k=i)^(n-1)(h_k/Ltree)g(X_k).          (6.6)

Equations (6.3)-(6.5) give

 ||T(X)_i-u_i||<=2A_i Econc<=2A*Econc<1,
 ||T(X)-T(Y)||max<=qfix||X-Y||max,
                         qfix=4A*Econc<1.                    (6.7)

The Hessian bound applies along every line segment between two points
in the same ball, since the ball is convex. Thus (6.7) is one bound
for the entire simultaneous path map. No product of loose one-step
inverse constants is used.

This defines an explicit initial point. Start X^(0)_i=u_i and set
X^(r+1)=T(X^(r)) for integer r>=0. The iterates stay in Ball. Successive
differences are bounded by qfix^r times the first difference, so the
geometric series makes them a Cauchy sequence in the finite product
space. They converge to a fixed point (x_0,...,x_(n-1)), with error

 ||X^(r)-x||max <= 2A*Econc*qfix^r/(1-qfix).                    (6.8)

Continuity gives the fixed-point equation. Applying (6.7) to two fixed
points proves uniqueness WITHIN Ball. Define x_n=z. Subtracting the
fixed-point equations at consecutive indices, including the last one,
now proves exactly

                 x_i-x_(i+1)=(h_i/Ltree)g(x_i)

for every physical i. Thus the limit construction is an ACTUAL GD
orbit for the fixed F_m, not a system of independent inverse choices.
No convergence iteration has been run on the host.

Write eps_path=2A*Econc. At the fixed point, (6.7) sharpens to

 ||x_i-u_i||<=2A_i Econc,
           2D-eps_path<=R_init:=||x_0||<=2D+eps_path.      (6.9)

In particular x_0!=0. This is the original full Euclidean radius.
Its scale is S, quite different from the old log2-spine initial radius.
The proof worked in the whole feature space and discarded no component.

## 7. Exact terminal value and actual benchmark failure of this branch

There are exactly2^(m-j-1) leaves first separating from s0 at depth j.
Define the explicit finite positive sum

 Rleaf=sum_(j=0)^(m-1) 2^(m-j-1)exp(-t delta_j).           (7.1)

The actual terminal value, not an auxiliary entropy, is exactly

 F_m(x_n)=F_m(t v)=t-log N+log(1+Rleaf)
                      =D+log(1+Rleaf),
                  0<Rleaf< Econc.                           (7.2)

The strict upper bound follows from Rleaf<= (N-1)exp(-t delta_min)
=exp(-2)Econc. Let V_leaf denote the score of the initial point defined
by (6.6)-(6.8). Its exact value and two-sided estimates are

 V_leaf=2[D+log(1+Rleaf)]/(Ltree||x_0||^2),

 1/[2(S+Ltree log N)(1+Econc)^2]
       <=V_leaf
       <=(1+Econc)/[2(S+Ltree log N)(1-Econc)^2]
       <=(1+5*Econc)/[2(S+Ltree log N)].                      (7.3)

To check the estimates, eps_path/(2D)=A*Econc/D<=Econc, D>1, and
log(1+Rleaf)<=Rleaf<Econc. For0<=Econc<=1/8 the elementary inequality
(1+Econc)/(1-Econc)^2<=1+5*Econc follows after multiplication by (1-Econc)^2:
the remaining expression is Econc(2-9*Econc+5*Econc^2)>=0.

These bounds prove an actual performance statement. From (2.5),(6.5),

       B_n V_leaf <(7/8)(1+5/1000)<9/10                 (7.4)

for every m>=128. Furthermore Econc->0 and log N/S->0, so (2.6),(7.3)
give the exact asymptotic ratio

           B_n V_leaf -> Z_1/(2 exp(1))<99/128<1.        (7.5)

The price that prevents success is proved, not merely suspected:
R_init/(2S/Ltree)->1 while F_m(x_n)/(S/Ltree)->1.

This branch also lies strictly below the same-word canonical Huber
value1/(2S+1). Indeed (6.5), Ltree<1, and Econc<1/1000 give
5*Econc(2S+1)<15/1000<1. Thus

 (1+5*Econc)(2S+1)<2S+2<2S+2Ltree log N,

where Ltree log N>1 follows from m>=128, Ltree>1/2 and log2>1/2.
Combining with (7.3) proves

                       V_leaf<1/(2S+1).                  (7.6)

Consequently it cannot improve the complete K channel of accepted
factb98bb807d514e80d or the complete alternating-ray channel of accepted
fact1fca3e5dd555cb4a: each includes the canonical Huber witness. These
two accepted facts are used only for this optional reference comparison. No
comparison with the full complex channel is asserted, and none is

The feature mean is zero. Distinct coordinate rows of the feature

## 1. Exact object and the two divergence equations

For an integer r>=1, let h=(h_0,...,h_(r-1)) be an original nonnegative

    T_ii=1, T_it=h_t if t<i, T_it=0 if t>i,
    z=T e, so z_i=1+sum_(t<i)h_t and z_r=A,
    Z_diag=diag(z),
    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(r-1),2s)^T,
    D=diag(h_i(2-h_i) for i<r,-s(s+2)).               (1)

For every real n-by-n array Lambda with zero diagonal, set

    L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
    M=D+(L T+T^T L^T)/2.

The equality space of interest is exactly

    L^T e=omega,                 M e=0.             (2)

The original certificate additionally requires Lambda_ij>=0 for EVERY

For any zero-diagonal real matrix X define two divergences

    d(X)=X e-X^T e,
    d_z(X)=X z-Z_diag X^T e=d(X Z_diag).                      (3)

Both have coordinate sum zero. The weighted matrix in (3) is X Z_diag,
whose (i,j) entry is X_ij z_j; it is NOT Z_diag X. No division by z_i is
involved.

The elementary identity driving the construction is

    2D e+T^T omega=-Z_diag omega.                         (4)

Here is every coordinate of its verification. For i<r put

Adding 2h_i(2-h_i) gives 2h_i(1+p_i)=-z_i omega_i.
At i=r the left side is -2s(s+2)+2s=-2s(s+1), also

If d(Lambda)=L^T e=omega, then

    2M e=L z-Z_diag omega=-d_z(Lambda).                   (5)

    Delta_l=z_(u_l)-z_(v_l).

For EACH ordered off-diagonal pair whose unordered pair is not a tree

such coordinates. Define N to have these entries, zero diagonal, and

    alpha_l=sum_(i in S_l) omega_i

    beta_l=-sum_(i in S_l,j not in S_l)

First consider the two-step child (X,Y). Put S=X+Y=C-1 and

    u=2S(1+X)/Y=2(p/b)(1+t a),

       =2(p/b)delta(1+lambda t).                       (5)

The full child array, in its three original coordinates, is

             0          1          2
    row0     0          2          0
    row1     2(1+X)     0          u
    row2     0          v          0.

Its divergence is (-2X,-2Y,2S), since v-u=2S. Direct substitution in
the original matrix formula gives all its entries as

    [[w0,-w0,0],[-w0,w0+w1,-w1],[0,-w1,w1]].           (6)

For example M_12=[v(Y-1)-u]/2=-w1 and M_22=-S(S+2)+v=w1;

The middle diagonal is

w1=u-S^2 show the equality by direct expansion.
To obtain the second equality for w1 in(5), expand its bracket as
2+2t a-t^2 b(a+b)=2[1+t a-lambda t^2]
=2(1-t)(1+lambda t), using(2).

    c=(C+d)/(C-d),  k=1+2c=(3C+d)/(C-d),

For this paragraph write P=2,Z=5, beta_3=X,beta_4=Y, and let

    sum_j beta_j(1-beta_j)||g_j||^2
       +[(C-d)/2-d^2]||g_P||^2+(C+d)||g_Z||^2/2.       (8)

sum beta_j Q_(j,P) equal d sum beta_j<g_j,g_P>, canceled by the

          0          1       2         3          4          5

    q=tau/(C-d), sigma=k-qR,

This is the complete symmetric filling and compensation step. Let e_i be the original coordinate

    z=T e=(1,1+X,C,C+1+d,A-Y,A)^T,
    Z=sum_i z_i=2+C+3A-2Y,
    K=6I-ee^T,
    b_l=e_(v_l)-e_(v_(l+1))             for l=0,...,4,
    S_l={v_0,...,v_l},

The edge differences in their stated order are

    -X, -Y, -(C+d), Y, X.

They are all nonzero, with absolute value greater than1. To eliminate
any implicit linear solve, the five weights are explicitly

    w_0^tree=(Z-6)/X,
    w_1^tree=[2Z-6(2+X)]/Y,
    w_2^tree=[3Z-6(2+X+C)]/(C+d),

    w_4^tree=[Z-6(C+1+d)]/X.                         (20)

Define the symmetric matrix

    H=K-sum_(l=0)^4 w_l^tree b_l b_l^T.              (21)

         0                     1                    2                    3                    4                    5

 row1    2(1+X)+eps*gamma0      0                    u+eps*gamma1         eps                  eps                  eps
 row2    eps                   v+eps*gamma1          0                    eps                  eps                  2cd+eta+eps*gamma2
 row3    eps                   eps                  2cX+eps              0                    2k+eps*gamma4         2cX+eps
 row4    eps                   eps                  2cY+eps              2k(1+X)+eps*gamma4    0                    ku+2cY+eps*gamma3
 row5    eps                   eps                  2c+eta+eps*gamma2     eps                  kv+eps*gamma3         0.           (23)

### A.5. All signs and the full perturbed spectral margin

First bound every tree weight in(19). Because K is the complete-graph

    F_l=sum_(i in S_l,j not in S_l)(z_i-z_j).

For every g perpendicular to e, (18),(22),(24),(29) give

                   =(11delta/90)||g||^2

# Arbitrary-template primitive inflation: exact interface and scope

Status: joint analytical DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max4's one authorized
round50 under TASK.md and guidance1c516691cc4c3011. No mathematical evaluator,
solver, replay, machine algebra, formal submission, consult, or subagent is
authorized or used. The unrestricted inflation claim is not established by
the results below. The original exact-profile Goal remains separate and open.

The mathematical predecessors are accepted04219554e41d9750, proof
Sections10--13, and accepted4c92d3fc4eb6153e, statement and proof Section6.
The former supplies the exact primitive identity and full binary join;
the latter uses arbitrary seeds inside those basic trees. Neither accepted
statement asserts arbitrary-template inflation. Every new calculation below
is reproduced jointly; no unverified shared finding is used as a premise.

## 1. Original full certificate and the physical word

For a nonnegative word w of length n, W_n(w) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), over all finite Euclidean
dimensions, all convex differentiable functions with L-Lipschitz
gradient and a minimizer x_star, and x_0!=x_star, under
x_(t+1)=x_t-(w_t/L)grad f(x_t). Here L>0 and the empty word is allowed.
This is the project's W=2R normalization. The letter q below follows
TASK.md and means the child WORD, not a scalar derivative from another
fact. Other locally defined letters carry the scopes explicitly given.

Normalize the smoothness to1. For a word w=(w_0,...,w_(n-1)), put
S_w=sum w_t, K_w=1+S_w, x_(t+1)=x_t-w_t g_t, and

 Q^w_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_w=2 sum_(t<n) w_t(f_t-f_n)
       +sum_(t<n)w_t(1-w_t)||g_t||^2-S_w(S_w+1)||g_n||^2.

All finite ordered interpolation residuals Q^w_ij are nonpositive on an
actual convex differentiable1-smooth function. Let Lambda^w have zero
diagonal and nonnegative entries on every ordered distinct pair. With
e the all-ones column, T^w_tt=1, T^w_tu=w_u for u<t, zero for u>t, set

 L^w=diag(Lambda^w e)-Lambda^w,
 omega^w=(-2w_0,...,-2w_(n-1),2S_w)^T,
 D^w=diag(w_0(2-w_0),...,w_(n-1)(2-w_(n-1)),-S_w(S_w+2)),
 M^w=D^w+(L^w T^w+(T^w)^T(L^w)^T)/2.

The assumed input conditions are (L^w)^T e=omega^w and M^w PSD on the
whole R^(n+1). Accepted04219554e41d9750 gives the polynomial identity

 V_w+sum_(i!=j)Lambda^w_ij Q^w_ij=<M^w,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>.       (1)

There is no quotient at a zero step, no restriction to a gradient rank,
and no support, product, reflection, or multiplier symmetry assumption.

Let h have length r, h_i>=1, capacity A=1+sum h_i, and a full input
certificate as above. Let q have length s, nonnegative steps, capacity
C=1+sum q_a, and an arbitrary full input certificate. Define

 beta_i=1+C(h_i-1),
 H=(q,beta_0,q,beta_1,...,q,beta_(r-1),q).                     (2)

There are r+1 child copies, r bridge steps, and exactly

 N=(r+1)s+r=(r+1)(s+1)-1

physical steps. There are N+1=(r+1)(s+1) formal gradients. Index a node
as (i,a), where 0<=i<=r, 0<=a<=s, at physical index i(s+1)+a. These
disjoint child node sets partition the entire formal space. The endpoints
p_i=i(s+1)+s are the bridge queries for i<r and the final query for i=r.
The full array has N(N+1) ordered off-diagonal slots. In particular, all
gradients at zero child steps are retained.

Every physical step is nonnegative because beta_i>=1. Direct summation gives

 1+sum H=1+(r+1)(C-1)+r+C(sum h_i-r)=AC.                     (3)

If r=0 the output is q; if s=0 it is h. An all-zero but nonempty q
still contributes all its formal gradients and zero physical steps.

## 2. Exact virtual data and energy decomposition

All child copies are segments of ONE actual GD trajectory for ONE static
function. For block i write z_i for its starting position, y_i=x_(p_i)
for its endpoint, e_i=g_(p_i), f_i^e=f(x_(p_i)), and

 P_i=sum_(a<s)q_a g_(i,a),
 dinf_i=P_i-(C-1)e_i,
 Dinf_0=0,  Dinf_i=sum_(k=1)^i dinf_k for i>=1.

Thus y_i=z_i-P_i and z_(i+1)=y_i-beta_i e_i. Define formal virtual jets

 X_i=[y_i+(C-1)e_i+Dinf_i]/C,
 F_i=f_i^e/C+(C-1)||e_i||^2/(2C).                            (4)

Their positions obey EXACTLY X_(i+1)=X_i-h_i e_i: indeed the change in
the numerator is

 -beta_i e_i-P_(i+1)+(C-1)(e_(i+1)-e_i)+dinf_(i+1)
 =-[beta_i+C-1]e_i=-C h_i e_i.

This is a formal algebraic GD relation; no interpolating virtual function
is asserted. Define the virtual residual

 Qhat_ij=F_i-F_j+<e_i,X_j-X_i>+||e_i-e_j||^2/2.

Expanding (4) cancels every extra norm and endpoint inner-product term:

 C Qhat_ij=Q^H_(p_i,p_j)+<e_i,Dinf_j-Dinf_i>.                     (5)

Let V_i denote the ORIGINAL primitive energy V_q of block i, relative to
its own actual endpoint. The following identity is exact on every formal
gradient and function-value coordinate:

 V_H=sum_(i=0)^r V_i+C^2 V_h(F_0,...,F_r;e_0,...,e_r).       (6)

Here the final energy uses the original steps h and the virtual data (4).
To check (6), subtract the child energies. The coefficient of f_i^e-f_r^e
for i<r is 2[(C-1)+beta_i]=2Ch_i. The coefficient of ||e_i||^2 is

 beta_i(1-beta_i)+C(C-1)
 =C^2h_i(1-h_i)+C(C-1)h_i.

The final coefficient is C(C-1)-(AC-1)AC. Since sum h_i=A-1, this equals

 -C(C-1)(A-1)-C^2 A(A-1),

which is precisely the final coefficient obtained from C^2 V_h and (4).
All internal child coefficients agree without alteration. These checks
also apply at zero child steps.

## 3. A full positive-flow candidate, and the exact missing payment

Let E_i be the coordinate restriction from all physical gradients to
the s+1 gradients of block i. Let E extract the r+1 endpoint gradients.
Embed child arrays in their original coordinate sets and put

 Lambda^0=sum_i E_i^T Lambda^q E_i+C E^T Lambda^h E.           (7)

All off-diagonal entries are nonnegative; coinciding contributions add.
The flow is exactly the required physical flow. Internal child nodes
have flow -2q_a. At a nonterminal block endpoint, its flow is

 2(C-1)-2C h_i=-2 beta_i.

At the final endpoint it is 2(C-1)+2C(A-1)=2(AC-1).

Let G be the full physical gradient Gram matrix, and define B as the
quadratic form

 B=C sum_(i!=j)Lambda^h_ij <e_i,Dinf_j-Dinf_i>.                    (8)

Combining (1), (5), and (6), the full remainder of (7) is

 V_H+sum Lambda^0_ab Q^H_ab
 =sum_i <E_i^T M^q E_i,G>+C^2<E^T M^h E,G>-B.              (9)

The first two terms are full-coordinate PSD congruences. The last term
has no established sign. Dropping it is an error. Thus (7) is an explicit
positive-flow lift, but NOT a proved PSD lift.

It actually fails for the M=0 inputs (13). In their full physical space
R^4 choose scalar formal gradients (g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)=(0,1,1,0).
Then e_0=1, e_1=0, dinf_1=a, and (9) equals -2Ca<0. These are formal
coordinates used to disprove PSD of (7); they are NOT asserted to be
an actual function trajectory. A different array certifies the physical
word, as Section4 shows.

Here is a precise additional sufficient collective payment condition.
Put K=C^2 sum Lambda^h_ij Qhat_ij. Suppose there are real numbers
0<=theta_i<=1, an actual ordered array Gamma_ab>=0 with zero diagonal,
and a matrix P PSD on all physical gradients, such that the following
POLYNOMIAL identity holds after the original physical GD substitutions:

 K=sum_i theta_i V_i+sum_(a!=b)Gamma_ab Q^H_ab-<P,G>.         (10)

Then a full certificate is explicitly

 Lambda^out=sum_i(1-theta_i)E_i^T Lambda^q E_i+Gamma,
 M^out=sum_i(1-theta_i)E_i^T M^q E_i+C^2 E^T M^h E+P.        (11)

Indeed substitute (10) into (6) and use both input identities (1).
Every array coefficient in (11) is nonnegative and every matrix summand
is PSD on the unchanged physical coordinates. Cancellation of all formal
function values implies the exact original flow; the matrix equals the
original D+sym(LT) by (1). This is an EXTRA sufficient matching condition,
not a consequence proved from the stated input primitive conditions.

For an exact formulation with no sufficient-cone narrowing, any array
with the physical flow equals Lambda^0+Xi, where Xi is a real zero-
diagonal array with zero divergence at every node. Full feasibility is
equivalent to existence of such Xi with Lambda^0+Xi entrywise nonnegative
off diagonal and the full quadratic form

 sum_i E_i^T M^q E_i+C^2E^T M^h E-B+sum Xi_ab Q^H_ab          (12)

PSD. The last sum is purely quadratic because Xi has zero divergence.
In (12), the embedded matrices are evaluated against G; B and the last
sum denote scalar quadratic forms on the same full gradient coordinates.
This is a useful exact residual interface, not a solution of that
feasibility problem. It does not discard any original array.

## 4. The virtual-oracle shortcut is false even for two M=0 inputs

Put a=sqrt(2), C=1+a, d=a-1=1/C, and take h=q=(a). Both words have
the ORIGINAL full certificate

 Lambda_01=2, Lambda_10=2C, Lambda_00=Lambda_11=0, M=0.       (13)

For completeness, the flow is (2-2C,2C-2)=(-2a,2a).
With T=[[1,0],[a,1]], the first diagonal of D+sym(LT) is
a(2-a)+2(1-a)=2-a^2=0; the second is
-a(a+2)+2C=0; and twice the off-diagonal is -2+2C(a-1)=0.
Thus (13) verifies the entire two-gradient matrix and both ordered signs.

The physical output is H=(a,2,a), with length3 and capacity C^2.
Use the single static convex1-smooth function f(x)=x^2/2, minimizer0,
and initial point x_0=-C. Its whole actual run is

 x_0=-C,  x_1=1,  x_2=-1,  x_3=d,
 g_t=x_t,  f_t=x_t^2/2.

Block0 ends at e_0=y_0=1. Block1 starts at -1, ends at e_1=y_1=d,
and has P_1=-a, dinf_1=-a-a d=-2. Consequently the virtual data (4) are

 (X_0,F_0,e_0)=(1,1/2,1),
 (X_1,F_1,e_1)=(-d,d^2/2,d).

They obey X_1=X_0-a e_0, but

 Qhat_01=-2d<0,      Qhat_10=2d^2>0.                       (14)

For the second equality, expansion gives
Qhat_10=(d^2-1)/2+a d+(d-1)^2/2=d(d+a-1)=2d^2.
For the first, Qhat_01=(1-d^2)/2-a+(1-d)^2/2=1-d-a=-2d.

Thus these virtual jets are NOT smooth-convex interpolable. Both input
certificates are M=0 and satisfy the balanced product relation. Neither
of these additional restrictions rescues this virtual-oracle assertion.

Both actual child energies are zero: on the unit quadratic the one-step
energy is x_start^2-C^2 x_end^2, and C d=1. Every actual Q is zero.
Therefore even allowing nonnegative payments by child energies cannot
make each virtual interpolation residual nonpositive separately: the
positive Qhat_10 in (14) has zero child payment available. By contrast,
the template-weighted sum is

 2 Qhat_01+2C Qhat_10=-4d+4C d^2=0.

This demonstrates why a potentially viable theorem must control the
COLLECTIVE template-weighted expression, not certify a fictitious
smooth-convex oracle pair by pair.

This example is explicitly NOT a counterexample to the physical lift.
H=(a,2,a) is the accepted binary primitive join of q with itself: the
join surplus is1, since 1(2C+1)=C^2. Its full lifted certificate exists
by accepted04219554e41d9750 Section11. Its actual V_H is zero on this run.

## 5. A sufficient closure in the proved, proper template subclass

Call a template BASIC here if it is obtained by primitive--primitive
binary joins starting from empty primitive leaves, with surplus d_v>0
at every node satisfying d_v(A_left+A_right+d_v)=A_left A_right.
This is precisely the primitive tree construction of the accepted fact,
not a definition imposed on arbitrary primitive inputs.

For every such basic template h and every arbitrary full-certificate
nonnegative child q, the word (2) DOES have a full certificate. Replace
each of the r+1 empty leaves of its tree by q. At each original node,
its two child capacities and its surplus are all multiplied by C:

 (A_left,A_right,d_v) -> (C A_left,C A_right,C d_v).

The defining surplus equation and its positive root are preserved.
The bridge becomes exactly 1+C(h_i-1), in its original inorder position.
The resulting inorder word is (2), and its length and capacity are (3).

Here is the full array transformation, including the sign proof. At
each transformed node set kappa=((A_left+A_right+d_v)/A_right)^2,
which is unchanged under the common scaling. Embed the complete left
array with factor1 and right array with factor kappa. Write p for the
bridge query, z for the node's final query, and b_j for each physical
right-child step at its nonterminal node j. Add the actual ordered edges

 (j,p): (kappa-1)b_j,    (z,p): kappa-1,
 (p,z): (kappa-1)C d_v,  (j,z): (kappa-1)b_j.                (15)

There are no omitted finite coordinates. All coefficients are
nonnegative since kappa>1, d_v>0, and the physical b_j>=0. The accepted
identity gives exactly

 M_parent=E_left^T M_left E_left
                 +kappa E_right^T M_right E_right,         (16)

with the original flow and D+sym(LT). Induction proves the full matrix
PSD and every original ordered sign. This uses one same function on
one actual GD word throughout; there is no oracle reset.

The template subclass is proper EVEN INSIDE the full M=0 class. For
h=(3/2,3/2), a full M=0 array is

 Lambda=[[0,1,1/2],[7/2,0,17/2],[1,14,0]].                 (17)

Its row-minus-column flow is (-3,-3,6). For
T=[[1,0,0],[3/2,1,0],[3/2,3/2,1]] and D=diag(3/4,3/4,-15),
the diagonal entries of LT are (-3/4,-3/4,15), and the paired
off-diagonal sums are

 (-1-3/4)+(7/4)=0,
 (-1/2)+(1/2)=0,
 (-17/2)+(3/2+7)=0.

Thus D+sym(LT)=0 on all three formal gradients; all six ordered entries
are positive. But every length2 basic primitive tree contains a length1
empty-leaf join with step sqrt(2), whereas (17)'s word has neither step
equal to sqrt(2). Hence basic-template closure says nothing by itself
about using (17), or every other M=0 word, as an arbitrary template.

## 6. Repetition and the distinction between seed and template

For a FIXED basic template h of length r>=1 and capacity A, start with
any fixed nonnegative full primitive child q^(0) of length s and capacity
C. Recursively use (2) with q=q^(k). Equations(15)--(16) give actual full
certificates at every depth; all physical steps remain predetermined
and nonnegative. The exact counts and capacities are

 length(q^(k))+1=(r+1)^k(s+1),
 capacity(q^(k))=A^k C.                                    (18)

Accepted04219554e41d9750 Section11 makes a primitive word dominant with
weights (w,sum w+1). Its full objective certificate and the accepted Huber
witness therefore give, at every depth and in the original W=2R units,

 W_(length(q^(k)))(q^(k))=1/(2A^k C-1).                     (19)

The upper bound is over every finite dimension and every admissible
smooth convex objective. It has no multiplicative loss depending on k.
Rescaling f by L restores arbitrary L>0 and leaves W unchanged.

The exponent of this family depends on A and r, NOT on the arbitrary
leaf capacity C. Thus an exponent lower bound applied to (18)--(19)
can restrict A as a TEMPLATE capacity in a recursively closed class.
It cannot restrict C as an arbitrary fixed SEED capacity. To put C in
the exponent one would have to prove the missing theorem allowing that
seed itself to serve as the template, with all the requisite hypotheses.

Moreover the accepted basic recurrence already gives
A<=C_r<=(r+1)^rho, rho=log_2(1+sqrt(2)), for basic h. No external exponent
bound is needed for that existing basic-template restriction. In
particular, (18)--(19) place no new ceiling on an arbitrary length5/6
primitive seed or on the full M=0 subclass.

## 7. Source-dependent exponent check, after the sufficient basic closure

This section assumes an EXTERNAL premise; it is not a Danus fact import.
Source: Yuhan Ye and Kaizhao Liu, *Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for
Gradient Descent*, arXiv:2609.09152v2 (2026), Theorem1.1 and definition(1),
https://arxiv.org/html/2609.09152v2 . Its applicable statement is:
there are absolute K_YL>0 and n_YL such that every integer n>=n_YL
and every predetermined h in[0,infinity)^n satisfy

 W_n(h)>=n^(-rho-K_YL sqrt(log log n/log n)).                 (20)

Its R_n divides the objective gap by (L/2)||x_0-x_star||^2,
so R_n there is EXACTLY this project's W=2R. The supremum includes
all finite dimensions and all minimizers. At L=1 its GD convention
coincides with ours. Zero and arbitrarily large nonnegative steps are
allowed; the theorem is uniform over horizon-dependent words. This is
the non-anytime theorem, not the infinitely-many-horizons anytime result.
The primary definition, statement, Section3.2 proof and its uniform
constant passage were read, including the finite-dimensional construction
and its distance normalization in Section3.1. Exact HTML/PDF/text copies
are in downloads/ye_liu_2609.09152v2.*. No formal acceptance is asserted.

Here is the deduction, applied only when actual recursive feasibility
and (19) have been proved. Put m=r+1>1 and n_k=m^k(s+1)-1. The lower
bound (20) and (19) would imply

 log(2CA^k-1)/log(n_k)
 <=rho+K_YL sqrt(log log(n_k)/log(n_k)).                      (21)

For fixed finite s,C and A>1, the left side tends to log(A)/log(m),
while the additional term on the right tends to zero. Therefore such
a recursively certified template necessarily obeys

 A<=m^rho.                                                  (22)

This implication assumes (20). It uses every depth of the ACTUAL
finite-horizon family, not an anytime embedding or a formal scalar
capacity recursion. Fixed prefactors, including C and s+1, disappear
only after division by log(n_k); no depth-dependent loss is discarded.
For the basic templates proved here, (22) is already contained in the
accepted scalar bound, so it is not a new restriction. Applying (22)
to an arbitrary length5/6 seed, or to all M=0 inputs such as (17), would
assume the very template-closure theorem this pilot has not established.

The primary background source on composition was also downloaded and
read: Grimmer, Shu, Wang, *Composing Optimized Stepsize Schedules for
Gradient Descent*, arXiv:2410.16249v2, definitions in Section2.1 and
Proposition6 with its proof. Its positive s-composable schedules include
an additional product equality. Those definitions are not silently
identified with the general full primitive input (1), and no result
from that source is a new proof premise here.

## 8. A second nonnegative-flow formula fails even with M=0 inputs

The first candidate (7) is not the only tempting generalization of the
binary join. The following chronological fan formula has exact physical
flow and nonnegative entries, and agrees with the accepted lift for the
one-step saturated template. For a general input array Lambda^h put

 b_i^back=sum_(j<i)Lambda^h_ij,    mu_i=1+b_i^back.

Scale the full child array in block i by mu_i. For each i<j add
C Lambda^h_ij on the endpoint pair (p_i,p_j). For each i>j add
Lambda^h_ij times each of the two fans

 sum_(a<s)q_a Q^H_((i,a),p_j)+Q^H_(p_i,p_j),
 sum_(a<s)q_a Q^H_((i,a),p_i).                              (23)

All coefficients are nonnegative. The nonterminal child flow is
-2mu_i q_a+b_i^back q_a+b_i^back q_a=-2q_a. The total flow of
block i is C omega_i^h, so the endpoint flow is precisely that of (7).
This verifies every required flow equation and sign, without a PSD claim.

Take the M=0 template (17) and the M=0 child q=(sqrt(2)) from (13).
Their physical word is

 H=(a,(3+a)/2,a,(3+a)/2,a),  a=sqrt(2).

Set all scalar formal endpoint gradients e_0,e_1,e_2 to zero, and let
the child starting gradients be u_0,u_1,u_2. Set every formal value to
zero. Thus dinf_i=a u_i and V_i=a(1-a)u_i^2. Because bridge gradients
vanish, z_1=y_0 and z_2=y_1=y_0-a u_1.

For the backward edge1->0, the sum of the two fans in (23) equals V_1:
the residual from the block1 start to y_0 is u_1^2/2, and that to its
own end is (1/2-a)u_1^2, both multiplied by a. The same calculation
gives V_2 for edge2->1. For edge2->0, the earlier endpoint is
y_0=z_2+a u_1, so the fan sum is instead

 V_2+a^2 u_1u_2=V_2+dinf_1dinf_2.

All forward endpoint residuals vanish on this formal assignment. The
child M matrices and the template M matrix are zero. Identity(6) gives
V_H=sum V_i. Therefore the complete remainder of (23), after the
child scalings cancel, is exactly

 Lambda^h_20 dinf_1dinf_2=dinf_1dinf_2.

Choosing (u_0,u_1,u_2)=(0,1/a,-1/a) makes this remainder -1. Hence the
second formula fails full PSD even for the explicitly positive M=0
template (17) and saturated M=0 child (13). This is another array-local
failure, NOT a valid static negative-energy witness for the physical H.
It does not establish nonexistence of a different full array.

## 9. Remaining question

The arithmetic, full energy decomposition, positive-flow candidate,
proper basic-template closure, and virtual-oracle counterexample above
are complete joint analytical drafts. They do not prove that every
full primitive h is a valid template, and they do not supply an actual
negative-energy witness for a lifted word with valid inputs. The exact
unpaid term is (8); (10) is one fully specified sufficient collective
payment hypothesis, and (12) retains the entire unrestricted array
problem. A failure of (7), or of pairwise virtual interpolation, cannot
be promoted to failure of every array for the physical word.

No new fact has been submitted or accepted in this pilot. Sections3 and8
are two distinct failed full-array constructions; Section4 is a genuine
static counterexample to their tempting oracle premise, but not to the
unrestricted inflation claim. The latter remains unresolved, including
for arbitrary full M=0 templates.

## 2. Projection function, smoothness, minimum, and all original rows

Let K be any nonempty compact convex subset of a Euclidean space with
0 in K. Define the SAME finite function at every query by

 F_K(x)=max_(g in K){<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.

Completing the square shows that its unique maximizing vector is the
Euclidean projection g=P_K(x). Existence follows from compactness and
uniqueness from strict convexity of squared distance. The exact normal
condition is

 <x-g,v-g><=0 for every v in K.                     (2.1)

Necessity follows by differentiating squared distance on the segment
from g to v. Sufficiency follows by expanding ||x-v||^2-||x-g||^2.
Adding (2.1) for two inputs proves
<x-x',g-g'>=||g-g'||^2, hence ||g-g'||<=||x-x'||.
The maximizing formulas at x and x+d give

 0<=F_K(x+d)-F_K(x)-<g,d><=<P_K(x+d)-g,d><=||d||^2.

Therefore F_K is finite, convex, differentiable, and grad F_K=P_K is

Its minimum is0, and its WHOLE minimizer set is

One direction follows directly from the maximizing formula. In the other
direction, if <x,v>>0 for some v in K, a sufficiently small positive
multiple epsilon*v is in K and has positive objective. This proves
that x is not a minimizer. It also proves (2.3) without identifying the
minimum with an arbitrarily selected point.

Let K be any nonempty compact convex subset of a Euclidean space with

                      *beta^(2n) ->0.              (4.8)

unbounded-m family is weak, even though its faces change and its normal
state is retained. It has been mapped to the previously screened
squared-distance/cone class with its TRUE minimum distance. The radial
cap has zero multiplier at x_0 and is strictly inactive at every later
projection. Per the assignment, this candidate stops here. This is not
an upper bound for arbitrary initial points of K_car, other carrier
sizes, other truncations, or general simplices.

## 5. Candidate two: remove the carrier and retain the actual mixtures

Select the centered body with no carrier

 K_ctr=conv{a_s:s in {0,1}^m}, x_0=a_(s_left).        (5.1)

Adding an explicit origin to this convex hull changes nothing. Section3
shows0 is an interior point, so (2.3) gives the UNIQUE minimum0 and

 R_ctr^2=1.                                        (5.2)

The cone generated by K_ctr is the whole ambient space. At query1 the
finite boundary really matters, as demonstrated below, so the cone
mapping from Section4 cannot be carried over.

Write the actual spine coordinates as x_(i,j)=sqrt(w_j) z_(i,j).
If p_(i,k) are the unique barycentric masses of g_i in the vertices b_k,
define q_(i,j)=sum_(k>=j)p_(i,k). Then q_(i,0)=1 and
1=q_(i,0)>=q_(i,1)>=...>=q_(i,m)>=0, and

 d_(i,j)=2q_(i,j+1)-q_(i,j),
 g_(i,j)=sqrt(w_j)d_(i,j),
 z_(i+1,j)=z_(i,j)-h_i d_(i,j), z_(0,j)=1.          (5.3)

At every query the masses are exactly selected by (3.5),(3.6) with b_k.
Equivalently they uniquely minimize
sum_(j<m)w_j[z_(i,j)-(2q_(j+1)-q_j)]^2 on the displayed monotone
q simplex. The constructive rule, not this optimization notation alone,
specifies the answer. The exact values and normalized terminal score are

 F_K_ctr(x_i)=sum_(j<m)w_j[z_(i,j)d_(i,j)-d_(i,j)^2/2],
 V_ctr=sum_(j<m)w_j[2z_(n,j)d_(n,j)-d_(n,j)^2].      (5.4)

These are a persistent m-dimensional state and every original physical
step. There is no smaller reset state or new child clock.

## 6. Actual first-H2 projections for the centered body

Define for positive integers J

 Dsp_J=sum_(j=0)^(J-1)(2c)^j,
 sigma_3=(7a-1)/Dsp_3,
 sigma_4=(15a-2-beta)/Dsp_4.                        (6.1)

For m>=128 the elementary bounds

 2/5<a<5/12, 12/5<c<5/2, 127/128<=beta<1,
 1/20<sigma_3<1/15, 1/52<sigma_4<1/40              (6.2)

hold. The bounds on a,c follow from 12/5<lambda<29/12 and m>=128.
For sigma_3 its numerator is between9/5 and23/12, and its denominator
is between721/25 and31; in particular
9/155>1/20 and (23/12)/(721/25)=575/8652<1/15.
For sigma_4 the numerator is greater than3 and less than10/3; its
denominator is less than156 and greater than17429/125>400/3.

Initially g_0=x_0 and z_(1,j)=-a for EVERY depth. The exact projection
at query1 is

 d_(1,j)=0, j>=3.                                  (6.3)

Its positive masses are exactly exit groups0,1,2. To verify this, take

 q_(1,1)=(1-a+sigma_3)/2,
 q_(1,2)=a-sigma_3 c^2, q_(1,3)=...=q_(1,m)=0.

The relation q_(1,3)=0 is equivalent to the definition of sigma_3,
and (5.3) gives (6.3). Moreover

 7/24<q_(1,1)<1/3, 0<q_(1,2)<1/20.

For the second bounds its numerator over Dsp_3 is
a(1+2c)+(1-3a)c^2. The numerator is at least
58/25-25/16=303/400>0, and at most337/250;
division by Dsp_3>721/25 gives an upper bound337/7210<1/20.
Consequently p_0=1-q_1,p_1=q_1-q_2,p_2=q_2 are all positive.

The residual y_1 has scaled coefficients -sigma_3 c^j for j<3
and -a for j>=3. Because r_tree*c=2, its inner product with b_0,b_1,b_2
is the common value w_0 sigma_3. Its inner product with b_3 is
w_0[-7sigma_3+a r_tree^3]. This is strictly smaller, because
sigma_3>a/c^3: the left side exceeds1/20 and a/c^3<1/30.
For subsequent first-exit vertices the residual inner products strictly
decrease: an increment inside the constant negative tail is
-a w_k(2-r_tree)<0. The final all-left vertex also has a smaller value
than its immediately preceding exit vertex, by -2a w_(m-1)<0.
Thus every normal condition(3.6) holds and the displayed projection is
the actual unique one.

The next ACTUAL state, after the original h_1=1+beta, is

 z_(2,j)=a beta-(1+beta)sigma_3 c^j, j=0,1,2,
 z_(2,j)=-a, j>=3.                                 (6.4)

Its next projection has positive masses exactly on exit groups0,1,2,3:

 d_(2,j)=z_(2,j)+sigma_4 c^j, 0<=j<4,
 d_(2,j)=0, j>=4.                                  (6.5)

To verify, note
1+sum_(j<4)2^j z_(2,j)=2+beta-15a,
so the definition of sigma_4 gives q_(2,4)=0. Define earlier q by
q_(2,0)=1 and q_(2,j+1)=(q_(2,j)+d_(2,j))/2.
All four barycentric masses are strictly positive, as follows.
The bounds(6.2) give

 1/4<d_(2,0)<1/2, 0<d_(2,1)<1/4,
 d_(2,2)=-a+(1+beta)q_(1,2)+sigma_4 c^2<-23/160<0,

p_1=(q_(2,1)-d_(2,1))/2>0, while p_0=1-q_(2,1)>0.
Since q_(2,4)=0, q_(2,3)=-d_(2,3)>0 and
p_2=q_(2,2)-q_(2,3)=q_(2,3)-d_(2,2)>0; finally p_3=q_(2,3)>0.

The residual at query2 has scaled coefficients -sigma_4 c^j for j<4
and -a thereafter. Its values on the four active vertices are all

No free height or separate value assignment is used. The residuals are

The third physical update in the first H2 is therefore exactly

 z_(3,j)=z_(2,j)-(1+a)d_(2,j).                       (6.6)

For every j>=4 it is STILL -a. Equations(6.3)-(6.6) are actual
projections and updates; they do not prescribe a rank-one law. In
particular the face changes between queries1 and2, and the full deep
noncore state is retained. At query3 and every subsequent query the
all-support rule(3.5),(3.6),(5.3) applies. No assertion that these four
groups remain active is made.

## 7. Two direct continuation attempts and their limits

The first attempt was to propagate a fixed exposed face, or treat a
visit to the quadratic core as permanent. Both shortcuts fail on these
very data. Equations(6.3),(6.5) give different positive supports at
queries1 and2. Also x_0 lies in K_ctr, but x_1=-a a_left does NOT.
Its unique full-leaf barycentric coefficients are

 p_s=(1+a)/N for s!=s_left,
 p_(s_left)=(1+a)/N-a<0.                            (7.1)

The strict inequality follows from a>2/5 and N>=4. Consequently
P_K_ctr(x_1)!=x_1. An initial core visit already fails to persist through
the next original step. No remote interpolation defect occurs: (2.4)
holds, and the true projection supplies the required repair automatically.

The second attempt was to simplify the full simplex projection by
thresholding its unconstrained leaf masses with the ordinary Euclidean
probability-simplex formula. This is false for the selected Haar metric.
Applying that threshold formula to (7.1) would give mass1/(N-1) on all
non-left leaves, mass0 on the left leaf, and hence

 g_wrong=-a_left/(N-1).

All those non-left leaves would have positive weights, so their normal
inner products with y_wrong=x_1-g_wrong must be identical at a genuine
projection. The values for leaves first diverging at depths0 and1 differ
by

 (-a+1/(N-1))*(2w_0-w_1),                          (7.2)

which is nonzero. This directly violates the within-face stationarity
condition. The inverse feature map changes the Euclidean metric; ordinary
thresholding is not invariant under that change of coordinates.

These are concrete failures of two attempted reductions, not a proof
that a competitive centered-tree trajectory is impossible. In particular
there is no proof that the support remains a prefix of exit groups after
query2, and no failure of such a later-only prefix conjecture is asserted.
The full state rule retains arbitrary later supports.

## 8. Full-word accounting and a quantitative conditional screen

The centered candidate has a fully paid initial radius, but its terminal
estimate remains substantive. Here is exact full-word accounting that
retains the noncore state. Set

 y_i=x_i-g_i, cex_i=<y_i,g_i>>=0.

Nonnegativity follows from (2.1) with v=0. Since
x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)g_i+y_i, direct expansion gives

 ||x_(i+1)||^2=(1-h_i)^2||x_i||^2
   +h_i(2-h_i)||y_i||^2-2h_i(h_i-1)cex_i.

None of the Pi_i is zero. Dividing by Pi_(i+1)^2 and telescoping gives
the exact quantitative terminal identity

 V_ctr=Pi_n^2*[1+sum_(i<n)
  {h_i(2-h_i)||y_i||^2-2h_i(h_i-1)cex_i}/Pi_(i+1)^2]
  -||y_n||^2.                                     (8.1)

It uses every original physical query. The bracket is not set to1.
For h_i>=2 both displayed contributions are nonpositive. For 1<h_i<2
the squared-residual contribution can be positive, and its size must
be controlled jointly with the negative terms and the terminal residual.
For this candidate the exact benchmark-matching requirement is

 Pi_n^2*[1+sum_(i<n)
  {h_i(2-h_i)||y_i||^2-2h_i(h_i-1)cex_i}/Pi_(i+1)^2]
  -||y_n||^2 >=1/B_n.                              (8.2)

No inequality(8.2), useful constant fraction of it, or converse for all
m has been proved. Equation(8.1) is an identity, not a lower bound.

A second direct continuation attempt uses a rigorously testable core
criterion instead of assuming persistence. If at an actual power-of-two
query k=2^j with 1<=j<=m-1 one has

 x_k in K_ctr and -x_k/c in K_ctr,                  (8.3)

then every later query is exactly in the core, and

 x_i=(Pi_i/Pi_k)x_k for k<=i<=n,
 V_ctr=||x_k||^2 beta^(2(n-k))c^(2-2m).             (8.4)

Indeed Pi_k=beta^k/c is positive. For even i>=k the ratio Pi_i/Pi_k
lies in[0,1], since s2(i)>=1. For odd i>=k the bit count is at least2
(the only odd positive integer with a single one is1), so the ratio
lies in[-1/c,0]. Convexity and(8.3) put every candidate iterate in K_ctr.
Induction then gives its actual gradient equal to itself at each step.

This criterion has a quantitative full-word consequence. Every gradient
of F_K_ctr has norm at most1, since it is a convex combination of unit
features. Hence ||x_k||<=1+sum_(t<k)h_t<=1+S<c^m. From(8.4), for any
k in the stated range,

 V_ctr<c^2 beta^(2(n-k))<=c^2 exp(-2(n-k)/m),
 B_n V_ctr<4lambda^m c^2 exp[-(2^m-2)/m] ->0.       (8.5)

We used log(1-1/m)<=-1/m and k<=2^(m-1). The limit follows since
2^m/m^2 tends to infinity; for example its ratio at consecutive m is
2(m/(m+1))^2, eventually at least3/2. This is a CONDITIONAL screen for
actual states satisfying(8.3), not a statement that(8.3) occurs. It is
not inferred from a single core membership or from the first-H2 data.

The first direct attempt at a global law failed by the exact face and
core counterexamples. The independent mass-threshold attempt failed
by(7.2). The remaining route is to control the true active-set evolution
in(5.3), or establish(8.3), or obtain a competitive lower estimate in
(8.2). All are genuine all-history estimates. Replacing them by a fixed
label, exact extinction, discarded tail, or an unproved induction would
change the construction.

## 9. Literature and resource record

Search stage: active_program. Program: actual growing tree-simplex
projection dynamics. Missing mechanism: an analytic all-query active-set
law with a paid terminal comparison. Mode: repair/mutation. Intent:
construction and projection-background; no whole-goal impossibility search.

Matlas searches were made for tree/simplex projection and a precise
threshold statement. The first returned no applicable tree projection
theorem (its tropical-metric and unrelated statistical results do not
apply). The precise second search returned cone normal conditions from
arXiv:2107.07257, Lemma9, and standard-simplex thresholding from
arXiv:2204.08153, Proposition2.1. Neither is imported as a black-box result.

The exact primary paper read is Weiran Wang and Miguel A. Carreira-Perpinan,
"Projection onto the probability simplex: An efficient algorithm with a
simple proof, and an application", arXiv:1309.1541, 2013, Sections1-3
and Theorem1 with proof. Its problem is min||p-y||^2/2 subject to p>=0,
sum p=1 in the STANDARD Euclidean probability coordinates. It characterizes
p_i=max(y_i+lambda_threshold,0), with the threshold fixed by the sum and
an explicit sorted-support test. The relevant proof idea is equality of
normal derivatives on the positive support, used directly in(3.5),(3.6)
and to refute the unjustified transfer in(7.2). The paper's scalar
threshold itself does not apply to the non-isometric Haar feature map.

Local files: downloads/max53_simplex_projection/1309.1541.pdf, .html,
and .txt. The PDF and HTML were downloaded. An already present local
pypdf installation extracted the text, and the relevant extracted pages
were read in bounded sections. Extraction warned that fontTools was
missing; nothing was installed. The defining equations and proof were
also read in the exact arXiv HTML, so no formula depends on an unchecked
font-encoding extraction. Source URL: https://arxiv.org/html/1309.1541.

Search is background only; every new mathematical ingredient used here
has a joint elementary derivation in this manuscript. No external result
is a correctness premise, and no formal submission was made.

Readback/retrieval disclosures: initial broad memory/tool output was
truncated, so decisive guidance, accepted facts and the original tree
definitions were reread in bounded portions. One stale filename lookup
failed with "No such file or directory"; the correct prior manuscripts
were located. A notation-cleanup patch failed its context match, made
no change, and was reapplied as a smaller patch and reread. Shared facts,
not search snippets or old local drafts,
were used for accepted benchmark scopes.

Resources used for mathematics: zero host mathematical evaluations,
zero solver or optimizer calls, zero trajectory/DP/replay runs, zero
machine algebra, zero formal verification/fact_submit, zero installs,
zero consults, zero native subagents. Host operations were file and
text processing, literature downloads/extraction, and shared-store calls.

## 10. Deliverable and open interfaces

Candidate1 has a complete, actual, unbounded-family obstruction:
explicit body, global sharp smoothness, entire minimum set and closest
distance, real face changes, all original rows, an all-physical-query
projection law, and comparisons with COMPLETE K/ray/FULL-complex and
original B_n. Its mapping to the known cone regime is the reason to stop it.

Candidate2 is a legal static centered tree simplex with a paid unique
minimum and derived, changing early mixtures. Its complete state rule
and exact full-word accounting are provided. A useful unconditional
terminal comparison is BLOCKED. Its whole-family performance is not
upper bounded here; (8.5) closes only states satisfying its explicit
criterion. No complete same-word reference comparison is claimed for
this candidate.

The original uniform every-n/every-nonnegative-word Goal remains OPEN.
Even resolving the centered candidate on H_m would be a component, not
the separate all-word theorem. All new results remain UNVERIFIED and
must not be used as fact-graph bricks. This one round does not renew any
model, computational, or formal allowance.

First bound every tree weight in(19). Because K is the complete-graph
Laplacian,

    F_l=sum_(i in S_l,j not in S_l)(z_i-z_j).

most9 crossing unordered pairs, since |S_l|(6-|S_l|)<=9. Hence

    |F_l|<81,  |w_l^tree|<81,  |gamma_l|<82.          (26)

at least2. To check the bridge pair, c>1 and d>3/2 imply2cd+eta>3,

2(303/160)(403/100)=244218/16000<16, and
tau<2a delta/(2-a)<(142/29)delta<5delta.

Let B be the leading five-by-five principal block of M_prim. For

||Pg||^2=||y||^2-(sum y_i)^2/6>=||y||^2/6. Hence

At t=99/100, equations(22),(28),(31),(32) give exactly the advertised

### A.6. Capacity, nonbasic status, and exact limits of the result

The concrete capacity is exactly

    A=a+(99/100)[(1+a)(a+b)+1].                      (33)

Using a>7/5, lambda>12/5 and p>3 gives
A>7/5+(99/100)(41/5)=4759/500>19/2. On the other hand

    A<lambda(1+p)<(121/50)(403/100)
                        =48763/5000<49/5,
    Gamma5_c107-49/5=78807/806000>0.                 (34)

Thus the sufficient hypothesis of accepted4c92d3fc4eb6153e is NOT
satisfied. Nothing here asserts an improving seed or a result on
the original asymptotic minimax target.

Here is the promised nearby justified endpoint. At t=1 the word is

    h_*=(a,b,1+rho(1+a+b),a,b),
    A_*=lambda(1+a+b).

It is an ordinary basic primitive construction under the accepted

b-1 satisfying (b-1)(lambda+b)=lambda by(2), and the final bridge

At our chosen t,

    ||h-h_*||_infinity
       <=delta max{a,b,1+rho p}<23/1000,
    0<A_*-A=delta(lambda p+1)<41663/500000<17/200.    (35)

and bridge excess d_right solving
d_right(1+C_right+d_right)=C_right, substitution of rho gives

Exact finite sufficient floors improve to A>=49/5 at length5 (17 phases, relative gap1/40000) and A>=12 at length6 (11 phases, gap1/80000); accepted Z15/Z3 also gives length5 A>=197/20 with9 phases and gap1/8000.
