evidence:
# Finite multiplicative phase covers for actual full-seed insertion

**Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof draft.** Worker max4, assigned analytical
round 51. No mathematical evaluator, solver, DP, replay, machine algebra,
formal verification, consult, or subagent was used. All new assertions below
belong to this single proof candidate; none is an accepted intermediate fact.

The mathematical predecessors are accepted facts `04219554e41d9750`
(especially proof Sections 3, 7, 9--12) and, only when explicitly recovering
the earlier fixed-ray comparison, `4c92d3fc4eb6153e`. No unverified finding
or external exponent theorem is a premise. The construction uses arbitrary
full primitive seeds inside BASIC dominant trees. It does not require or
prove arbitrary-template inflation.

## 1. Original model and complete seed hypothesis

For a nonnegative integer n and a nonnegative schedule
h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), define W_n(h) to be the supremum of

    2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L ||x_0-x_star||^2)

over every finite-dimensional Euclidean space, every convex differentiable
function f with L-Lipschitz gradient and at least one minimizer x_star,
and every x_0!=x_star, under

    x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L) grad f(x_i).

Here L>0 is fixed but arbitrary. This is the original W=2R normalization;
the empty schedule is included.

For nonnegative a,d set

    Omega(a,d)=(a+d+sqrt((a+d)^2+4ad))/2,
    G(a,d)=2a+d/2+sqrt(d^2+8ad)/2.

Retain all original integer splits:

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n) Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n) G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)),      n>=1.

Write U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, lambda=1+sqrt(2), and rho=log_2(lambda).

Fix an integer r>=1. A seed in this draft means an ACTUAL word
h=(h_0,...,h_(r-1)) with every h_i>=0, sum s, capacity A=1+s,
and m=r+1, together with a full real (r+1)-by-(r+1) array Lambda.
For EVERY ordered distinct pair i,j in {0,...,r}, require

    Lambda_ij>=0,     Lambda_ii=0.

Let e be the all-ones column of length r+1, and define

    T_ii=1,  T_it=h_t for t<i,  T_it=0 for t>i,
    L_flow=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(r-1),2s)^T,
    D_prim=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_(r-1)(2-h_(r-1)),-s(s+2)).

The full original-coordinate certificate requirements are

    L_flow^T e=omega,
    M_prim=D_prim+(L_flow T+T^T L_flow^T)/2 >=0 on R^(r+1).       (1)

Transpose and positive semidefiniteness have their ordinary real-matrix
meanings. There are exactly r(r+1) off-diagonal multipliers. Every formal
gradient g_0,...,g_r remains, even when physical steps vanish. No gradient
equality or coordinate deletion is allowed at a zero step. There is no
assumption h_i>=1, product balance, zero remainder, rank, support, or
symmetry. These are precisely the general-length sufficient hypotheses
in accepted `04219554e41d9750`, proof Section 10.

For clarity about their scope, that accepted result normalizes L=1 and
uses x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i) h_t g_t and

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2sum_(i<r)h_i(f_i-f_r)
        +sum_(i<r)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-s(s+1)||g_r||^2.

Its exact identity is

    V_h+sum_(i!=j) Lambda_ij Q_ij
       =<M_prim,Gram(g_0,...,g_r)>.

Actual smooth convex trajectories have Q_ij<=0. Thus (1) implies the
primitive inequality on the full function class. Here Gram is the matrix
of pairwise inner products, and the matrix pairing is trace(M^T Gram).
This accepted implication is only sufficiency; no attainment or equivalence
of certificate classes is assumed.

## 2. Accepted ray and physical-substitution inputs

The following are precise statements used from `04219554e41d9750`.
For every positive integer b, the limit

    Z_b=lim_(j->infinity) lambda^(-j) B_(b*2^j-1)

exists and is finite and positive. For every integer j>=0 put

    L_pc(b,j)=lambda^(-j) B_(b*2^j-1),
    U_pc(b,j)=lambda^(-j)(sqrt(B_(b*2^j))+3/100)^2,

    E(b,j)=8sqrt(2)b^(rho-1)2^(-j)
           +(3/25)(b+1)^(rho/2)lambda^(-j/2)
           +(9/10000)lambda^(-j).

The accepted enclosures and their proof give

    L_pc(b,j)<=Z_b<=U_pc(b,j),
    0<=U_pc(b,j)-L_pc(b,j)<=E(b,j).                         (2)

Indeed the latter is exactly the bound obtained by subtracting the two
endpoints in accepted Section 9: use the accepted adjacent bound for
B_(b*2^j)-B_(b*2^j-1) and B_n<=4C_n<=4(n+1)^rho. In particular both
endpoints tend to Z_b. For every fixed integer d>=0 and defined index,

    0<=Z_b-lambda^(-j)B_(b*2^j-1-d)
       <=E(b,j)+8sqrt(2)d b^(rho-1)2^(-j).                  (3)

The same accepted proof gives

    1<rho<4/3,
    B_n>=C_n,
    C_(b*2^j-1)=lambda^j C_(b-1),
    C_(b-1)>=1.                                           (4)

For every nonnegative n, take any fully expanded maximizing tree of the
ORIGINAL B_n recurrence, expanding every primitive child using the
ORIGINAL C recurrence. Such a tree has n internal nodes, n primitive
empty leaves, and one terminal dominant empty leaf. In particular,
there is no restriction on a maximizing dominant split.

Replace each primitive empty leaf by the actual seed of Section 1.
Retain all internal nodes and keep the dominant empty leaf empty with
mass 1. Recompute all physical bridges:

* At a primitive join, for actual child capacities A_left,A_right, use
  bridge 1+d_pp, where d_pp>0 solves
  d_pp(A_left+A_right+d_pp)=A_left A_right.
* At a dominant join, for primitive left capacity A_left and actual
  dominant right mass D_right=1+2sum(right), use bridge
  1+A_left/zeta, where zeta=(1+sqrt(1+8A_left/D_right))/2.

Concatenate (left,bridge,right) at every node. Denote the resulting word
by Hsub_n, and its ACTUAL mass by Dsub_n=1+2sum Hsub_n. Accepted
Sections 11--12 apply for every seed satisfying (1), including arbitrary
PSD remainders and zero steps. They give

    length(Hsub_n)=mn,
    W_(mn)(Hsub_n)=1/Dsub_n,
    (sqrt(A B_n)-(sqrt(A)-1))^2<=Dsub_n<=A B_n.             (5)

The upper objective certificate holds for all functions in Section 1;
its matching Huber example gives the displayed equality. In particular
this is not merely a quadratic or projection-family assertion.

The length in (5) counts n old bridge steps and nr seed steps. The lower
mass bound pays for the one untouched dominant leaf: all primitive
capacities scale by A, while the square-root dominant merge is
1-Lipschitz in the square root of the right mass. This is why the
subtraction sqrt(A)-1 is present. We never physically replace the
dominant empty leaf by an object of mass A.

## 3. Integer-ray monotonicity and exact dyadic scaling

The admissible split k=0 in B_(n+1) gives

    B_(n+1)>=G(1,B_n)>B_n,

because B_n>0 and sqrt(B_n^2+8B_n)>B_n. Thus B is increasing directly
from the ORIGINAL recurrence. If positive integers b<=c, then

    B_(b*2^j-1)<=B_(c*2^j-1)

for every j. Taking the established limits proves Z_b<=Z_c. We do not
need or assert strict increase of the ray limits.

For every integer ell>=0, changing the limiting index gives

    Z_(2^ell b)
      =lim_j lambda^(-j)B_(b*2^(j+ell)-1)
      =lambda^ell Z_b.                                    (6)

This uses the accepted integer-ray limits only. No continuity, density,
or regularity of a real-valued phase function has been assumed.

## 4. The finite product and its strict margin

Choose positive integers b0,d,K and an integer ell>=0. Let C_pc be a
positive certified upper bound for Z_d/Z_b0. Suppose

    m^K b0<=2^ell d.

Define, for 0<=i<=K,

    b_i=b0 m^i,
    P_pc=lambda^ell C_pc.

All quantities Z_b are positive. Exact telescoping, monotonicity, and
(6), in that order, prove

    product_(i=0)^(K-1) [Z_(m b_i)/Z_b_i]
      =Z_(m^K b0)/Z_b0
      <=Z_(2^ell d)/Z_b0
      =lambda^ell Z_d/Z_b0
      <=P_pc.                                             (7)

Every inequality has the direction required for an UPPER product bound.
In particular this argument never turns an upper ray enclosure into a
lower bound for an unknown ratio.

Also m^K b0>=b0, so monotonicity makes the telescoped ratio at least 1.
Thus P_pc>=1, and the strict capacity condition A^K>P_pc implies A>1.

It is convenient to allow a certified capacity floor a with 1<a<=A.
Assume a^K>P_pc and choose a positive gamma satisfying

    K gamma<=1-P_pc/a^K.                                  (8)

Necessarily gamma<1. Write

    q_i(a)=Z_(m b_i)/(a Z_b_i).

The product of the q_i(a) is at most t_pc=P_pc/a^K<1. Therefore some
index i_star in {0,...,K-1} satisfies q_i_star(a)<=t_pc^(1/K).
Otherwise their product would exceed t_pc.

For completeness, for x in [0,1] the inequality
(1-x)^K>=1-Kx follows by induction: multiplying the induction bound by
1-x adds the nonnegative term K x^2. With x=gamma, (8) gives

    (1-gamma)^K>=1-K gamma>=t_pc.

Consequently there is a fixed index i_star with

    Z_(m b_i_star)/(A Z_b_i_star)
      <=q_i_star(a)<=1-gamma.                             (9)

This is an existence assertion about a finite list, not a selection of
an unproved optimal phase. Sections 5--6 make it a physical and certified
statement.

## 5. Physical families, exact offsets, and uniform limit passage

For each i in {0,...,K-1} and integer j>=0, put

    n_(i,j)=b_i 2^j-1,
    N_(i,j)=m n_(i,j)=m b_i 2^j-m,
    H_(i,j)=Hsub_(n_(i,j)).

Thus there are K explicitly defined schedule families. At a fixed j
there are exactly K specified finite physical words, possibly with
different lengths. Each word is generated by the procedure in Section 2,
for example with the least maximizing split used to resolve ties.

The numerator is evaluated at its TRUE physical horizon. Equation (3)
applies with ray m b_i and shift d=m-1=r, since

    N_(i,j)=m b_i 2^j-1-(m-1).

It proves lambda^(-j)B_(N_(i,j))->Z_(m b_i). Also (5) yields

    0<=A Z_b_i-lambda^(-j)Dsub_(n_(i,j))
      <=A E(b_i,j)
        +2(sqrt(A)-1)sqrt(A Z_b_i)lambda^(-j/2).           (10)

To see the second term, subtract the square in (5) from A B_n,
discard the negative term -(sqrt(A)-1)^2, and use
B_(n_(i,j))<=lambda^j Z_b_i. Thus the denominator converges to
A Z_b_i>0. By (5),

    lim_j B_(N_(i,j)) W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))
        =Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i).                             (11)

There are only K indices. In (3) use the maximum ray m b_(K-1) and
the fixed shift m-1; in (10) use b_(K-1) and Z_b_(K-1). These give
common errors tending to zero, while every denominator limit is at least
A because Z_b>=L_pc(b,0)=B_(b-1)>=1. Therefore (11) is uniform over
the finite list and over all maximizing-tree ties. No interchange of
an infinite phase minimum with a limit is involved.

For any one fixed selected i, the integers N_(i,j) strictly increase
and tend to infinity with j. The words at different horizons need not
be prefixes of one another; the original prescribed-horizon guarantee
does not require that property.

## 6. Certified phase selection and an explicit common horizon

At a search depth t>=0 compute, or supply certified enclosures for,
the K quantities

    F_i(t)=U_pc(m b_i,t)/(a L_pc(b_i,t)).                   (12)

They are valid upper bounds on q_i(a): the numerator is bounded from
above and the positive denominator from below. Both endpoints in (2)
converge, so F_i(t)->q_i(a). Choose the first t for which some

    F_i(t)<1-gamma/2,                                    (13)

and freeze the smallest such i. This rule terminates: the index supplied
by (9) has limit at most 1-gamma, leaving the strict slack gamma/2.
It is unnecessary to decide which index minimizes the true ray ratio.

This is a certified convergent procedure, not a prescription to use
uncertified floating-point comparisons. For rational a and gamma, it has
the following finite-precision implementation in principle. At stage
t>=1, form outward rational enclosures of each L_pc(b_i,t) and
U_pc(m b_i,t) with absolute error at most 2^(-t), keeping every lower
denominator positive. Use the lower L endpoint and upper U endpoint
in (12), and stop only upon the strict rational inequality (13).
Each finite B value is defined by finitely many additions, products,
positive square roots, and maxima in the ORIGINAL recurrence. These
operations admit arbitrarily accurate rational outward enclosures:
rational square comparisons bracket each positive square root, and the
maximum of lower or upper endpoints bounds the corresponding maximum.
For a fixed stage only finitely many such operations are needed. The
recurrences have positive inputs, so arbitrary prescribed absolute
accuracy follows by refinement. The extra errors tend to zero with t,
and termination follows from the same strict slack. There is no claim
that this procedure is computationally economical, and it was not run.

More generally, an arbitrary real seed need not come with a computable
capacity oracle. The effective input is a certified rational floor
1<a<=A with a^K>P_pc, and a certified positive rational gamma satisfying
(8). If A^K>P_pc, such choices exist by strictness and rational density;
their certification uses the supplied seed data. This states the actual
input required for effective selection rather than presuming an oracle
for arbitrary real numbers. The exact-real formulation (12)--(13) is
also a valid mathematical selection rule.

It remains to turn the selected ratio into a bound for every sufficiently
large physical horizon. Put b_max=b_(K-1) and

    J=ceil(log(60 b_max/gamma)/log(3/2)).                  (14)

This can equivalently be selected by the finite integer test
(3/2)^J>=60 b_max/gamma, with rational arithmetic when gamma is rational.
Its finiteness follows from 3/2>1.

Here is a common error bound with no unproved rates. Since
sqrt(2)>5/4, lambda>9/4 and sqrt(lambda)>3/2. Also sqrt(2)<3/2,
and (4) gives rho-1<1 and rho/2<1. For b>=1,
j>=0, and q=(2/3)^j,

    E(b,j)+2lambda^(-j/2)
       <[12b+(3/25)(b+1)+9/10000+2]q
       <=[12+6/25+9/10000+2]b q
       <15b q.                                          (15)

Every inequality uses nonnegative terms; 2^(-j)<=q and
lambda^(-j)<=q as well. Thus for all i and all j>=J,

    E(b_i,j)+2u_j<gamma/4,   u_j=lambda^(-j/2).            (16)

By (2) and Z_b_i>=1,

    B_(n_(i,j))>=lambda^j Z_b_i(1-E(b_i,j)).

Also (4) implies B_(n_(i,j))>=lambda^j, so

    (1-A^(-1/2))/sqrt(B_(n_(i,j)))<=u_j.

Using (5), monotonicity, and the LOWER ray enclosure for the larger ray,

    B_(N_(i,j))<=B_(m b_i 2^j-1)<=lambda^j Z_(m b_i),

we get, whenever (16) holds,

    B_(N_(i,j))W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))
       <=[Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i)]
          /[(1-E(b_i,j))(1-u_j)^2].                      (17)

The factors in the denominator are positive by (16). For 0<=E,u<1,

    (1-E)(1-u)^2
       =1-E-2u+2Eu+(1-E)u^2>=1-E-2u.

Hence that denominator is greater than 1-gamma/4. For the fixed index
selected by (13), Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i)<=q_i(a)<1-gamma/2, so

    B_(N_(i,j))W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))
       <(1-gamma/2)/(1-gamma/4)
       <1-gamma/4,            EVERY j>=J.                (18)

The last strict inequality follows from
(1-gamma/4)^2-(1-gamma/2)=gamma^2/16>0. Thus the explicit positive
relative separation is gamma/4, and the chosen phase is fixed before
the unbounded horizon sequence is used. The family and selection depend
only on the seed and benchmark, never on an objective or its trajectory.

## 7. The exponent interface follows from a finite integer cover

Take b0=d=1 and C_pc=1. Then (7) becomes precisely

    product_(i=0)^(K-1) Z_(m^(i+1))/Z_(m^i)<=lambda^ell
       whenever m^K<=2^ell.                              (19)

Thus A^K>lambda^ell is sufficient. This finite condition for some
integers K>=1,ell>=0 is equivalent to A>m^rho. In one direction,
lambda^ell=(2^ell)^rho>=m^(K rho), so the strict power inequality implies
A>m^rho. Conversely, if A>m^rho, choose an integer K with

    K log(A/m^rho)>log(lambda)

and set ell=ceil(K log_2(m)). Then m^K<=2^ell<2m^K, and

    lambda^ell<lambda m^(K rho)<A^K.                     (20)

Here rho>0 and lambda=2^rho justify raising inequalities to rho.
If desired first choose a rational a with m^rho<a<A and perform the
same argument with a; Sections 4--6 then apply with certified inputs.
This proves sufficiency of A>(r+1)^rho without a claim about an
exponent obstruction or capacity ceiling for arbitrary seeds.

For an accepted upper comparison Z_d/Z_b0<=C_pc, the stronger finite
interface available from (7) is

    A>(lambda^ell C_pc)^(1/K),
    m^K b0<=2^ell d.                                    (21)

The word "stronger" refers to using this additional certified comparison;
it is not an assertion that every choice in (21) beats (19), or that
its value is below m^rho. For instance, at K=1,ell=0, b0=3 and d=3m,
the accepted constants in `4c92d3fc4eb6153e` recover its sufficient
capacity hypotheses for r=5 and r=6. Its more specialized horizon and
margin estimates remain valid in their stated scope.

## 8. Exact rational examples, with no evaluator

All checks here are written as explicit integer equalities or positive
integer differences. They are mathematical parts of the joint proof,
not reports of computations executed by a program.

First record small power identities:

    lambda^4=17+12sqrt(2),
    lambda^5=41+29sqrt(2),
    lambda^10=3363+2378sqrt(2).

The last conjugate is lambda^(-10)>0, so

    lambda^10<lambda^10+lambda^(-10)=6726<6750.            (22)

Also sqrt(2)<17/12 and sqrt(2)<99/70, because respectively
289>288 and 9801>9800. Hence

    lambda<29/12,  lambda<169/70,  lambda^4<34.            (23)

### 8.1 Length five: capacity 49/5 and seventeen phases

Let m=6, a=49/5, K=17, ell=44, b0=d=1, C_pc=1. The length cover is

    6^17<=2^44
      iff 3^17<=2^27,
    3^17=129140163<134217728=2^27.                        (24)

The capacity power bound follows from small factored checks. First

    49^4-9220*5^4=5764801-5762500=2301>0,

so a^4>9220. Next

    922^2=850084,  675^2=455625,
    200*850084-373*455625
      =170016800-169948125=68675>0,
    49*373^2-170*200^2
      =6817321-6800000=17321>0.                          (25)

Consequently

    lambda^44/a^17
       <[34*6750^4]/[(49/5)*9220^4]
       =170*675^4/(49*922^4)
       <6800000/6817321<1.                              (26)

This proves the needed exact finite power inequality; no decimal
approximation to rho is used. More quantitatively,

    17321*10000=173210000>115894457=17*6817321,

so (8) holds with gamma=1/10000, even at the capacity floor a=49/5.

    N_(i,j)=6^(i+1)2^j-6,

which the certified procedure selects. With

    J5=ceil(log(600000*6^16)/log(3/2)),

its physical words satisfy, for EVERY j>=J5,

    W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))<(1-1/40000) U_(N_(i,j))^ZJ.     (27)

The capacity 49/5 is below 99/10 by exactly 1/10.

### 8.2 Length six: capacity 12 and eleven phases

Let m=7, a=12, K=11, ell=31, b0=d=1, C_pc=1. The exact length cover is

    7^11=1977326743<2147483648=2^31.                     (28)

Use (22)--(23) and the equality 6750=(125/32)12^3. Then

since the denominator minus the numerator is 223315. Furthermore

    223315*20000=4466300000>3633315840=11*330301440.

Thus (8) holds with gamma=1/20000. Every actual full seed with r=6
and A>=12 has a certified selectable phase in

    b_i=7^i,             0<=i<=10,
    N_(i,j)=7^(i+1)2^j-7.

### 8.3 An accepted comparison shortens the length-five list

For an additional finite illustration, take m=6, a=197/20, K=9,
ell=21, b0=3, d=15, and C_pc=19299/2500. The accepted comparison in
`04219554e41d9750` is Z_15/Z_3<C_pc. The cover reduces to

    6^9*3<=2^21*15
      iff 3^9<=5*2^12,
    19683<20480.                                        (31)

The integer checks

    197^3-950*20^3=7645373-7600000=45373>0,
    4*19299=77196<77500=31*2500

give a^3>950 and C_pc<31/4. With (22)--(23),

      <[6750^2*(29/12)*(31/4)]/950^3

    1031*2000=2062000>1975392=9*219488.

    b_i=3*6^i,          0<=i<=8,
    N_(i,j)=18*6^i*2^j-6.

For this SAME K=9, the least unanchored dyadic exponent is 24, since

    2^23=8388608<10077696=6^9<16777216=2^24.

C_pc<31/4<14<lambda^3, where lambda^3=7+5sqrt(2)>14 follows from

bound at this fixed K. It asserts no optimality over all finite covers.

## 9. Complete conditional theorem proved by the joint argument

Fix the original function class and ALL-split benchmark from Section 1.
Suppose an actual length-r seed, r>=1, satisfies EVERY condition (1),
with h>=0 and no coordinate identifications, and put m=r+1, A=1+sum h.
Let b0,d,K be positive integers and ell>=0 an integer. Let C_pc>0 be
a proved upper bound for Z_d/Z_b0 and assume

    m^K b0<=2^ell d,    A^K>lambda^ell C_pc.

Choose any certified floor 1<a<=A and gamma>0 satisfying

    a^K>lambda^ell C_pc,
    K gamma<=1-lambda^ell C_pc/a^K.

Such real choices exist, and rational choices exist under the same strict
inequality, as explained in Section 6. Define the K physical families
H_(i,j), the exact horizons N_(i,j)=m b0 m^i 2^j-m, and J by (14).
Then the certified convergent rule (12)--(13), or its rational outward
enclosure version, selects a FIXED i in {0,...,K-1}, terminates after
finitely many stages, and for every integer j>=J gives

    W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))<(1-gamma/4) U_(N_(i,j))^ZJ.

The horizons form an unbounded increasing integer sequence. The full
all-function upper certificates and Huber equalities are supplied by the
actual basic-tree construction (5); every limiting comparison and finite
bound uses these actual horizons. The family is finite in its phase
index, and the error estimates are uniform over that finite index and
all maximizing-tree ties.

In particular A>(r+1)^rho is a sufficient interface, witnessed by some
finite K and ell. The exact separate sufficient capacities A>=49/5 for
r=5 and A>=12 for r=6, with the phase lists, J values, and relative
margins (27) and (30), follow. A>=197/20 for r=5 has the shorter nine-phase
alternative in Section 8.3. None of these hypotheses supplies an actual
seed or its full multiplier array.

## 10. Scope and audit boundaries

This is a conditional family of prescribed-horizon, full-class objective
guarantees. It is not an anytime schedule or an all-horizon comparison.
The selected phase is not identified numerically in this round, and no
claim of a phase optimum is made. Its certified finite selection is
proved above but has not been executed. No seed was discovered, and no
new fact was submitted or accepted.

The proof requires neither a virtual smooth-convex oracle nor inflation
by a nonbasic template. It makes no inference from the Ye--Liu exponent
theorem about an arbitrary finite seed's capacity. The fixed-b3 fact
`4c92d3fc4eb6153e` remains valid with its original, sharper specialized
finite horizons. All improvements here concern sufficient interfaces
using potentially different phases.

In particular K counts the compared integer rays. The expression A^K
comes from multiplying K normalized ray ratios; it does not claim that
an arbitrary seed can be inflated through itself K times or that a new
physical primitive seed of capacity A^K has been constructed.

The original unrestricted exact-profile Goal remains OPEN. This joint
draft requires a separately selected independent audit and formal gate
before any of its new mathematical claims can be used as facts.

F_K(x)=max_(g in K)(<x,g>-||g||^2/2).

The actual initial point is the all-left leaf. The joint derivation

    1+A_left/zeta,  zeta=(1+sqrt(1+8A_left/D_right))/2.

These are precisely the physical joins of accepted Sections 11--12. All
capacities are at least one, so all displayed bridges exist and are positive.
The resulting word Hsub_n has mass Dsub_n=1+2sum Hsub_n and satisfies

    length(Hsub_n)=n+nr=mn,
    W_(mn)(Hsub_n)=1/Dsub_n,
    (sqrt(A B_n)-(sqrt(A)-1))^2 <= Dsub_n <= A B_n.       (A1)

The square-root lower bound can be squared: its left side before squaring is
sqrt(A)(sqrt(B_n)-1)+1 >= 1. The loss sqrt(A)-1 pays for the one uninflated
dominant leaf. Treating that leaf as physically having mass A would give a
different and unjustified construction, but the candidate does not do so.
The equality in W uses the accepted full-function upper certificate and its
matching Huber example, not a restriction to a test family.

At n=0 the actual word remains empty, Dsub_0=1, and (A1) remains valid.
If every seed step is zero, A=1; the strict cover hypothesis below cannot hold.
This is a consequence of that hypothesis, not an excluded seed boundary.

## B. Accepted ray inputs and the width estimate

For each positive integer b, the accepted finite positive limit is

    Z_b=lim_(j->infinity) lambda^(-j) B_(b*2^j-1).

Write, as in the candidate,

    L_pc(b,j)=lambda^(-j) B_(b*2^j-1),
    U_pc(b,j)=lambda^(-j)(sqrt(B_(b*2^j))+3/100)^2,
    E(b,j)=8sqrt(2)b^(rho-1)2^(-j)
            +(3/25)(b+1)^(rho/2)lambda^(-j/2)
            +(9/10000)lambda^(-j).

Accepted Sections 7 and 9 give L_pc <= Z_b <= U_pc. The candidate additionally
uses the width U_pc-L_pc <= E, not merely Z_b-L_pc <= E. This stronger-looking
usage is warranted by the actual accepted derivation. With M=b*2^j, subtracting
the endpoints gives exactly

    U_pc-L_pc
      =lambda^(-j)[B_M-B_(M-1)+(3/50)sqrt(B_M)+9/10000].

The accepted adjacent estimate bounds its first term by
8sqrt(2)b^(rho-1)2^(-j). The accepted bound B_M <= 4(M+1)^rho bounds its
second term by (3/25)(b+1)^(rho/2)lambda^(-j/2). This proves the stated width
bound without a new recurrence calculation.

For a fixed integer d >= 0 with a defined index, the same accepted proof gives

    0 <= Z_b-lambda^(-j)B_(b*2^j-1-d)
       <= E(b,j)+8sqrt(2)d b^(rho-1)2^(-j).              (B1)

Also accepted are 1<rho<4/3, B_n>=C_n, and
C_(b*2^j-1)=lambda^j C_(b-1), with C_(b-1)>=1. Consequently
L_pc(b,j)>=1 and Z_b>=1. These facts justify the denominators and the
absolute-to-relative error conversion used later.

## C. Product direction and a fixed good index

The admissible split k=0 gives B_(n+1)>=G(1,B_n)>B_n for n>=0. Thus if
positive integers b<=c, the finite terms at b*2^j-1 and c*2^j-1 are ordered;
taking their established limits proves Z_b<=Z_c. Strictness of these limits
is not needed. For an integer ell>=0, changing the limiting index yields

    Z_(2^ell b)=lambda^ell Z_b.                         (C1)

This proof remains entirely on integer b. It supplies no real-base phase
function and does not need continuity or density of phases.

Let b0,d,K be positive integers, ell>=0 an integer, and C_pc>0 a proved upper
bound for Z_d/Z_b0. Suppose m^K b0<=2^ell d and put

    b_i=b0 m^i  (0<=i<=K),  P_pc=lambda^ell C_pc.

The entire product has the required upper orientation:

    product_(i=0)^(K-1) Z_(m b_i)/Z_b_i
      =Z_(m^K b0)/Z_b0
      <=Z_(2^ell d)/Z_b0
      =lambda^ell Z_d/Z_b0 <= P_pc.                    (C2)

The first ratio on the right is at least one by monotonicity. Hence P_pc>=1,
and A^K>P_pc implies A>1. Let 1<a<=A and gamma>0 satisfy

    a^K>P_pc,  K gamma<=1-P_pc/a^K.

Since P_pc/a^K is strictly between zero and one, gamma<1. Bernoulli's
inequality gives (1-gamma)^K>=1-K gamma>=P_pc/a^K. The induction is valid
on [0,1]: multiplication by 1-gamma preserves order, and the correction at
the next step is K gamma^2>=0. If every

    q_i(a)=Z_(m b_i)/(a Z_b_i)

were greater than 1-gamma, their product would exceed (1-gamma)^K and hence
P_pc/a^K, contradicting (C2). A single fixed i therefore has

    Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i)<=q_i(a)<=1-gamma.               (C3)

This includes K=1 and equality in the permitted gamma inequality. It is
about one member of a finite list of integer ratios. The power A^K has not
been interpreted as the capacity of a physically iterated arbitrary seed.

## D. Physical offsets and uniform limits

For each 0<=i<K and j>=0 define

    n_(i,j)=b_i 2^j-1,
    N_(i,j)=m n_(i,j)=m b_i 2^j-m,
    H_(i,j)=Hsub_(n_(i,j)).

For the numerator the accepted shifted ray is b=m b_i, d=m-1. Indeed
N_(i,j)=m b_i 2^j-1-(m-1). Its index is nonnegative even when n_(i,j)=0.
Equation (B1) thus gives lambda^(-j) B_(N_(i,j)) -> Z_(m b_i).

For the denominator, write c_A=sqrt(A)-1>=0. Equation (A1) implies

    0<=A Z_b_i-lambda^(-j)Dsub_(n_(i,j))
      <=A E(b_i,j)
        +2c_A sqrt(A Z_b_i)lambda^(-j/2).              (D1)

To check its direction, start with A(Z_b_i-L_pc(b_i,j)) and add the loss
between A B_n and Dsub_n; then discard the negative term -c_A^2 lambda^(-j).
Use lambda^(-j)B_n<=Z_b_i only inside the nonnegative square root. This
establishes (D1), and its left side follows from Dsub_n<=A B_n.

Consequently the exact ratio limit is

    B_(N_(i,j)) W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))
       -> Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i).                         (D2)

All exponents of b in E and (B1) are positive. Monotonicity of Z_b and the
largest b_i therefore provide common errors tending to zero over the finite
list. The denominator limits are >=A>0, and (A1) is independent of tree
depth and all maximizing-split ties. This proves the asserted uniformity
without any limit over an infinite collection of phases.

For a fixed selected i, N_(i,j+1)-N_(i,j)=m b_i 2^j>0 and N_(i,j) tends to

no prefix nesting or anytime property is assumed.

The candidate tests

    F_i(t)=U_pc(m b_i,t)/(a L_pc(b_i,t)).

Each denominator is positive, and the numerator upper bound divided by the
denominator lower bound gives F_i(t)>=q_i(a). The endpoint width in B tends
to zero, so F_i(t)->q_i(a). For the index in (C3), its limit is at most
1-gamma, strictly below 1-gamma/2. Some finite t therefore passes

    F_i(t)<1-gamma/2.

Selecting the first successful stage and the smallest successful index

For rational a and gamma the outward rational version is also valid. At

    B_(n_(i,j))>=lambda^j(Z_b_i-E)
                 >=lambda^j Z_b_i(1-E).

With b0=d=1 and C_pc=1, the finite sufficient conditions become

# Overlapping directed triangles: a legal correlated family with an actual payoff obstruction

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. Worker max4, round52.
TASK.md and master_guidance4572ef0ed580856f allocate one analytical round
after completed51, with completed ceiling52 and attempted ceiling53.
No fact_submit, numerical experiment, solver, parameter scan, machine algebra,
trajectory replay, installation, consult, or native subagent was performed.
All new arguments are reproduced together below. They are not fact-graph bricks.

## 1. Verdict, scope, and why this is a different construction

The selected object is ONE family of actual static functions: squared positive
edge differences on all overlapping directed triangles of a complete vertex
set. Triangles share their original vertex variables. The construction is
available in every dimension N>=3 and can use, for example, N=2^m+1 for H_m.
Every member has a finite attained minimum and an exactly paid closest-minimum
distance. The family includes the explicitly calculated signed temporal
correlations and changing noncommuting Hessians of Section5.

Every original directed interpolation row has the explicit nonpositive
formula (8), including remote rows, both optimum directions, and terminal
rows. The first original three-point cycle is evaluated in (16).

The family nevertheless fails quantitatively. For EVERY N>=3, every cyclic
orientation of each triangle, and every initial point outside the minimum
set, its actual normalized error on the original H_m satisfies, for m>=8,

 V_tri <= (2/3)*(49/50)^(2^(m-1)).                         (1)

This is an UPPER bound on actual error, not a weak lower certificate. It is
uniform over growing N, all initial directions and all scales of the initial
point. Its ratios to the original benchmark and the complete SAME-word
Huber, K, alternating-ray and full-complex references tend to zero. Each of
these ratios is strictly below 2^(-18) for every m>=12.

The obstruction persists for any positively weighted directed-triangle
system whose triangle-plane projections sum to the identity on the working
space; the complete construction is one explicit such system. It concerns
the fixed curvature normalization in (3), not other curvature scalings
(including a recalibration to a smaller least smoothness constant), other
edge nonlinearities, larger cycles, arbitrary non-tight incidence geometries,
or the unrestricted W_n.

Comparison with recalled failures, used as awareness only:

* 88f3db7b0a2bb506 supplies a Haar/rank-one transcript that fails a remote
  cycle despite passing adjacent and optimum rows. Here the function is
  fixed first, and (8) pays every row, before using any trajectory claim.
* 19f0eaeb0e7c3518 retains covariance but leaves a signed payment missing.
  Here a proved global contraction gives the actual payoff upper bound;
  no covariance identity is promoted to a positive lower witness.
* 38da1067bcd1a0c8 and 1ad14d90628c1312 leave actual tree-Gibbs occupation
  unresolved. This object has no Gibbs clock, conditional restart, or
  expected-oracle averaging.
* aa3c5e1d91baf405 and c93913a3af467ccc warn against fixed support/core
  assumptions for tree-simplex projections. Here all signs may change at
  every physical query. The upper bound holds through all such changes.

The function is not a change of basis of the fixed tree-simplex projection
law: its gradient is a sum of coupled one-sided edge forces. Already the
three-vertex member has the distinct, noncommuting sector Hessians in
Section5. Their spectra on its plane are {0,2/3} and {1/3,1}; an orthogonal
change of coordinates cannot turn these into the {0,1} eigenvalues of an
affine-face Euclidean projection. The growing construction uses overlapping
triangles, not a direct sum of isolated copies.

## 2. Accepted interfaces and notation

All spaces and norms below are real Euclidean. For a scalar t, t_+=max(t,0);
for a vector this operation is componentwise. The vector e_u is the u-th
coordinate unit vector and 1 is the all-ones vector of the indicated size.

 W_n(h)=sup 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L*||x_0-x_star||^2)

over finite-dimensional convex differentiable L-smooth functions with a

interpolation residual is

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.               (2)

It requires every ordered prefix pair. Its terminal-completion theorem is

adversaries by 2/n^2. We do not assume expected orthogonality; (15) gives an

Accepted factb98bb807d514e80d provides the complete single-cut functional
K_n(h), including Huber(h)=1/(1+2 sum h), and the ORIGINAL all-split
benchmark U_n^ZJ=1/B_n with B_n<=1+4n^p, p=log_2(3).

## 3. The actual function and the complete incidence identity

Fix N>=3 and let T_N be all three-element subsets of {0,...,N-1}.
For each tau choose one of its two cyclic orientations, independently of
the trajectory, and let E_tau be the resulting three directed edges.
A concrete choice for tau={u<v<w} is u->v, v->w, w->u.
Repeated edges in different triangles remain separately indexed.
Put

 w_tri=3/[N(N-2)],
 E_N={x in R^N: sum_u x_u=0},
 P_N=I-11^T/N,
 F_N(x)=(w_tri/6)*sum_(tau in T_N) sum_(u->v in E_tau)
                          (x_u-x_v)_+^2.                (3)

This finite formula is fixed at every physical query. No set or coefficient
is selected in response to a gradient. Write P_tau for the orthogonal
projection onto the vectors supported on tau whose three coordinates sum
to zero. The sum of the three unoriented edge outer products on tau is
3P_tau. Every unordered edge occurs in N-2 triangles, while
sum_(u<v)(e_u-e_v)(e_u-e_v)^T=N P_N: its diagonal entries are N-1 and
its off-diagonal entries are -1. Consequently

 sum_tau P_tau = N(N-2)P_N/3,
 sum_tau w_tri P_tau=P_N.                                (4)

Let A_tri have one row sqrt(w_tri/3)*(e_u-e_v)^T for every separately
indexed directed edge u->v in every triangle. Then

 A_tri^T A_tri=P_N,
 F_N(x)=|| (A_tri x)_+ ||^2/2,
 grad F_N(x)=A_tri^T (A_tri x)_+.                         (5)

In particular A_tri is an isometry on E_N and has operator norm1 on R^N.
Its range projection is Pi_tri=A_tri A_tri^T: indeed Pi_tri is symmetric,
and Pi_tri^2=A_tri P_N A_tri^T=Pi_tri.

Each scalar function t_+^2/2 is convex and continuously differentiable,
with derivative t_+. Thus F_N is convex and differentiable. Since the
componentwise positive-part map is 1-Lipschitz, (5) gives

 ||grad F_N(x)-grad F_N(y)|| <= ||x-y||.

Hence F_N is an everywhere-defined convex 1-smooth function. No assertion
that this smoothness upper bound is the least possible constant for every
orientation and N is needed or made. The normalization in (3) is fixed.

## 4. Every directed row, the minimum, physical GD and true distance

For arbitrary real t,u direct consideration of their four sign pairs gives

 u_+^2/2-t_+^2/2-t_+*(u-t)
       =(u_+-t_+)^2/2+t_+*(-u)_+.                        (6)

For x,y put r=(A_tri x)_+, s=(A_tri y)_+, d=r-s. Summing (6), and using
grad F_N(x)=A_tri^T r, gives

 F_N(y)-F_N(x)-<grad F_N(x),y-x>
       =||d||^2/2+sum_e r_e*(-(A_tri y)_e)_+.

Because Pi_tri is the range projection,
||A_tri^T d||^2=||Pi_tri d||^2 and
||d||^2=||Pi_tri d||^2+||(I-Pi_tri)d||^2. Therefore the exact residual is

 Q(x,y):=F_N(x)-F_N(y)+<grad F_N(x),y-x>
                       +||grad F_N(x)-grad F_N(y)||^2/2
 =-sum_e (A_tri x)_+,e*(-(A_tri y)_e)_+
  -||(I-Pi_tri)((A_tri x)_+-(A_tri y)_+)||^2/2 <=0.        (8)

The orientation here agrees exactly with (2). It holds for EVERY x,y,
so all ordered original trajectory pairs and every nonlocal cycle pass.
It includes equal points at zero steps and both directions involving any
minimizer. No finite collection of adjacent checks is substituted for (8).

Clearly F_N>=0. Equality forces every directed difference in every triangle
to be nonpositive. Around a directed triangle the three differences sum
to zero, so all three must be zero. Every two vertices occur in some
triangle; all coordinates are therefore equal. Conversely constant
vectors give value0. Hence

 argmin F_N=span{1}, min F_N=0,

is unchanged by GD because every edge vector has coordinate sum0.

For ANY finite nonnegative word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), including zero steps,

 g_i=(w_tri/3)*sum_tau sum_(u->v in E_tau)
                    (x_i,u-x_i,v)_+*(e_u-e_v),

## 6. Exact triangle radial bounds and its sharp one-step norm factor

First work on one triangle's mean-zero plane, with
f_triangle(z)=[(z_0-z_1)_+^2+(z_1-z_2)_+^2+(z_2-z_0)_+^2]/6.
For an oriented triangle tau, f_tau denotes this same sum-of-three-edges
formula on the plane range(P_tau), with that triangle's vertex labels.
Reversing the cyclic orientation is obtained by replacing z by -z,
so the following bounds hold for either orientation.

There are two sector types, with their boundaries allowed. In a two-positive
sector, after a cyclic relabelling, let the positive successive gaps be
u=z_0-z_1>=0 and v=z_1-z_2>=0. The centered coordinates give

 ||z||^2=2(u^2+uv+v^2)/3,
 2f_triangle(z)=(u^2+v^2)/3.

In a one-positive sector put p=z_0-z_1>0 and let
s=z_2-z_1 in [0,p], so the other differences are -s and -(p-s). Then

 ||z||^2=2(p^2-ps+s^2)/3,
 2f_triangle(z)=p^2/3.

It follows in both cases, including z=0, that

 ||z||^2/3 <= 2f_triangle(z) <= 2||z||^2/3.               (18)

For a nonnegative step t define the piecewise scalar

 q_tri(t)=1-t/3,                         0<=t<=3/2;
          sqrt(1-t+t^2/3),               3/2<=t<=3;
          2t/3-1,                       t>=3.          (19)

We claim that its value is EXACTLY the maximum of
||z-t grad f_triangle(z)||/||z|| over nonzero triangle-plane vectors z.

In a two-positive sector the Hessian is the path Laplacian divided by3.
Its eigenvectors (1,0,-1) and (1,-2,1) on the centered plane have
eigenvalues1/3 and1 respectively. Writing b=(u-v)/(u+v) in [-1,1]
gives the exact squared ratio

 [3(1-t/3)^2+b^2(1-t)^2]/(3+b^2).                       (20)

Its maximum is (1-t/3)^2 for t<=3/2, because
(1-t)^2-(1-t/3)^2=4t(2t-3)/9<=0.
For t>=3/2 its maximum is the value at b^2=1,
[(1-t)^2+3(1-t/3)^2]/4=1-t+t^2/3.

In a one-positive sector the Hessian has eigenvalue2/3 in the edge
direction (1,-1,0) and eigenvalue0 in the other centered direction.
Writing b=(p-2s)/p in [-1,1] gives the exact squared ratio

 [3(1-2t/3)^2+b^2]/(3+b^2).                             (21)

Its maximum is 1-t+t^2/3 for 0<=t<=3, and (1-2t/3)^2 for t>=3.
Comparing the maxima of (20),(21), using
(1-t/3)^2-(1-t+t^2/3)=t(3-2t)/9 and
(1-2t/3)^2-(1-t+t^2/3)=t(t-3)/9, proves (19).
Each maximum is attained at b=0 or |b|=1 in its stated sector, so the
factor is sharp for one triangle. This is an exact geometric maximization
on paper, not a numerical evaluation or scan.

## 7. Why overlaps and arbitrary dimension do not escape the factor

Restrict to E_N and let the linear map J_tri send x to the tuple
(sqrt(w_tri)*P_tau x)_tau, in the orthogonal direct sum of triangle planes.
By (4) it is an isometry. Its adjoint therefore has norm1.
The triangle gradient lies in its own triangle plane, and (3) gives

 grad F_N(x)=sum_tau w_tri grad f_tau(P_tau x).

For every nonnegative t, including large oversteps, (4) therefore gives

 x-t grad F_N(x)
   =J_tri^* [ (sqrt(w_tri)*(P_tau x-t grad f_tau(P_tau x)))_tau ].

Taking squared norms, using the norm of J_tri^*, and applying (19)
SEPARATELY to each current triangle state gives

 ||x-t grad F_N(x)||^2
   <=sum_tau w_tri ||P_tau x-t grad f_tau(P_tau x)||^2
   <=q_tri(t)^2*sum_tau w_tri ||P_tau x||^2
   =q_tri(t)^2*||x||^2.                                (22)

The triangle states need not be independent and are not evolved separately.
They all come from the SAME x. Their overlaps are exactly what (4) and the
isometry of J_tri account for. The update on the left is the original
coupled update, not independent triangle GD followed by a reset.

Likewise summing (18) and using (4) yields

 ||x||^2/3 <= 2F_N(x) <= 2||x||^2/3, x in E_N.           (23)

For a general start replace x_i by x_i-x_star, with its actual constant

 0<=V_tri(h,x_0)<=(2/3)*product_(i<n) q_tri(h_i)^2.        (24)

# A critical directed cycle: exact central reversal and the remaining suffix estimate

Status: JOINT UNVERIFIED ANALYTICAL DRAFT, max4 round53, 2026-10-01.
No fact_submit was authorized or made. No numerical evaluations, trajectory
replays, symbolic programs, solvers, benchmark DP, installations, or subagents
were used. All new formulas below are proved together as draft evidence, not
adopted from earlier unverified findings.

This is ONE graph, weight, and initial-state law. It passes the requested early
screens: a vanishing exact radial energy gap, a genuine sector reversal on the
original word, newly activated overlapping edges, and noncommuting Hessians.
The full terminal payoff is NOT bounded at benchmark scale here. Section 9

In particular, the large midpoint payoff is not a terminal lower bound, and

## 1. Fixed law, normalization, and accepted interfaces

Fix an integer m>=8. Write

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda*(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    t_j=1+a*c^j, 0<=j<m,

All children use this SAME enclosing m. The function, vertex count, and start
are fixed before the first query. The graph has exactly N directed edges
i->i+1 modulo N, each of weight one. For x in R^N define

    (D x)_i=x_i-x_(i+1 mod N),
    F(x)=(1/8)*sum_i ((D x)_i)_+^2,
    x_0=v, x_(k+1)=x_k-h_k*grad F(x_k), h=H_m.           (2)

Here s_+=max(s,0), and vector positive parts are componentwise. The declared
smoothness constant is L=1 throughout (including the payoff). Section 2 proves

Let 1 be the all-ones vector, e_i the i-th coordinate unit vector,
P=I-11^T/N, and R=dist(v,argmin F). The payoff is

    V_m=2*F(x_n)/R^2.                                   (3)

Fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original W_n normalization and all-directed

Every such inequality is derived directly here, including both terminal
directions and all optimum rows. No terminal-reduction shortcut is used.

For the original benchmark, use accepted b98bb807d514e80d and
04219554e41d9750. In full, C_0=B_0=1 and

    Omega(s,t)=(s+t+sqrt((s+t)^2+4st))/2,

Only this unconditional ray assertion is used; none of that fact's conditional

## 2. Static function, true radius, exact gap, and smoothness

Put A=D/2. The scalar function s_+^2/2 is convex and continuously
differentiable with derivative s_+. Thus

    F(x)=||(A x)_+||^2/2,
    grad F(x)=A^T(Ax)_+=D^T(Dx)_+/4.                    (6)

The elementary bound sum_i(x_i-x_(i+1))^2<=4 sum_i x_i^2 implies ||D||<=2;
the positive-part map is 1-Lipschitz. Formula (6) therefore proves that F is
convex, everywhere finite, continuously differentiable, and 1-smooth.

Its minimum is zero and its entire minimum set is span{1}. Indeed F(x)=0
means x_i<=x_(i+1) around the entire directed cycle, forcing equality everywhere.
Also 1^T grad F(x)=0, so the mean is preserved at every step, including a zero
step. Pairing i with N-1-i shows sum_i v_i=0. The identity cos^2 u=(1+cos 2u)/2
and the telescoping formula
2*sin(pi/N)*cos((2i+1)*pi/N)=sin((2i+2)*pi/N)-sin(2i*pi/N) give

    R^2=||v||^2=N/2.                                    (7)

There is no hidden choice of a more distant minimizer in this denominator.

For later use, the unweighted combinatorial Laplacian of a path on r vertices, divided by4,
has eigenvectors cos(k*pi*(i+1/2)/r), 0<=k<r, and eigenvalues
sin^2(k*pi/(2r)). This follows by substituting the cosine addition formula at
each interior vertex and the one-neighbor formula at each endpoint. Their
pairwise orthogonality follows by expressing products of cosines as sums and
using the finite geometric series; hence these r vectors form a basis.

The strict active edges of F at any x form a disjoint union of paths, since
all edges of a directed cycle cannot have strictly positive differences. If
H_x=(1/4)*sum_(i:(Dx)_i>0) (e_i-e_(i+1))(e_i-e_(i+1))^T, then

    grad F(x)=H_x x, 2F(x)=x^T H_x x.                    (8)

Every path component has at most N vertices. Its largest eigenvalue is at
most cos^2(pi/(2N))=1-mu. Along a segment, (6) is continuous and affine on
finitely many subsegments; on each its derivative is such a path Hessian.
Integrating along the segment proves that grad F is (1-mu)-Lipschitz.
At the strictly decreasing point v all path edges0,...,N-2 are active and the
closing edge is inactive. Perturbing v a sufficiently small amount in the top
path eigenvector keeps this strict sector. The derivative attains norm1-mu
there. Consequently the LEAST smoothness constant is exactly1-mu.

The exact radial energy gap on the mean-zero space is

    min_(x !=0, sum x_i=0) 2F(x)/||x||^2 = mu.           (9)

Here is a direct proof that does not confuse the gap with strong convexity.
Minimize 2F on the compact mean-zero unit sphere. Its minimum rho is strictly
positive because the only zeroes of F are constants. The multiplier equation
and sum grad F=0 give grad F(x)=rho*x at a minimizer: the multiplier on 1 is
zero, and taking the inner product with x uses <grad F(x),x>=2F(x).
By (8), rho is a positive eigenvalue of a path-component Hessian. The path
spectrum above puts every such positive eigenvalue at least mu. Conversely,
v is strictly decreasing and is the lowest positive cosine eigenvector of
the N-vertex path, so grad F(v)=mu*v and 2F(v)=mu*||v||^2.

Thus (9) is exact, but some sector Hessians have large kernels. In particular
no claim of globally mu-strong convexity is made.

A useful elementary upper value bound is

    sum_i ((Dx)_i)_+^2 <=2||Px||^2, hence 2F(x)<=||Px||^2/2. (10)

To prove it, replace x by Px and partition strict active edges into maximal
decreasing runs. On a run with endpoint values b>=e, the sum of the squared
nonnegative drops is at most (b-e)^2<=2(b^2+e^2). Different runs have disjoint
vertex sets, since at least one inactive edge separates them. Summing yields
(10). Isolated vertices add only nonnegative norm to the right side.

The smoothness constant stays near one while the relevant radial gap mu tends
to zero. Already T_t(v)=(1-t*mu)*v for 0<=t<1/mu shows that no strict norm
contraction independent of N can be transported from the triangle family.

## 3. All original directed rows with the non-isometric incidence

For ANY two points x_i,x_j define y_i=D x_i, r_i=(y_i)_+, and Delta r=r_i-r_j.
Their actual value and gradient residual is exactly

    Q_ij=-(1/4)*sum_e r_(i,e)*(-y_(j,e))_+
         -(1/32)*sum_e (Delta r_e+Delta r_(e+1))^2 <=0,  (11)

with indices modulo N. No condition on chronological proximity or sector is
present, so this includes nonlocal, optimum, and terminal rows.

Proof: for phi(s)=s_+^2/2 a direct check of the four sign combinations gives

    phi(u)-phi(w)+u_+*(w-u)+(u_+-w_+)^2/2=-u_+*(-w)_+.

Sum this at u=(Ax_i)_e,w=(Ax_j)_e and then correct the gradient norm from
||Delta p||^2 to ||A^T Delta p||^2, where p_i=(Ax_i)_+=r_i/2. This yields

    Q_ij=-<p_i,(-Ax_j)_+>
          -(1/2)<Delta p,(I-AA^T)Delta p>.

Here AA^T is the CYCLE Laplacian divided by4, not a projection. For every w,

    <w,(I-AA^T)w>=(1/4)*sum_e(w_e+w_(e+1))^2.

Substitute Delta p=Delta r/2 to obtain (11). This also proves the required
positive semidefiniteness without using an isometric incidence identity.
Ties give zero positive parts and cause no exception.

## 4. The rounding law and the exact first child

The following elementary estimates hold for every m>=8:

    d>144, mu<1/96, 5/4<mu*d<3/2,
    mu*t_j<2/3 for every j<=m-2.                         (12)

First lambda>12/5, beta>=7/8, and (12/5)^3=1728/125>13 give
d>1+(7/8)*13^2>144. Put b=pi*sqrt(d/6). Since sqrt(6)<pi and sqrt(d)>12,
1/b<1/12 and b<=N<b+1<(13/12)b. Thus
theta<=sqrt(6)/(2sqrt(d))<1/8 and theta^2<1/96.
Integration of cos u>=1-u^2/2 gives sin(theta)/theta>=1-theta^2/6>99/100.
It follows that

    mu*d < pi^2*d/(4N^2) <=3/2,
    mu*d >(3/2)*(12/13)^2*(99/100)^2 >5/4.

For the last strict comparison, the numerator216*9801=2117016 exceeds

    t_(m-2)/d =1/c+(1-1/c)/d <5/12+1/144=61/144,
    mu*t_(m-2)<61/96<2/3.

On the positive ray of v, grad F(qv)=q*mu*v for q>=0. By (12), each factor
1-mu*t_j in the first child is positive. Induction over the ACTUAL physical
steps, not a rearranged nonlinear trajectory, gives

    x_(2^(m-1)-1)=A_m*v,
    A_m=product_(j=0)^(m-2)(1-mu*t_j)^(2^(m-2-j))>0.    (13)

The multiplicity comes from the original recursive concatenation. Regrouping
these scalar factors is justified only because the entire first child has
just been proved to stay in this one sector.

For completeness A_m has a uniform positive lower bound. Let
S=sum H_(m-1). Summing the physical multiplicities gives

    S=2^(m-1)-1+[a/(c-2)]*(c^(m-1)-2^(m-1)).            (14)

We have 0<a/(c-2)<1 because c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1>beta.
Also d>2^(m-1): the lower bound (7/8)*(12/5)^(m-2) exceeds2^(m-1) at m=8
(using13^2), and its ratio to2^(m-1) increases by6/5 with each increment of m.
Consequently

    S/d <1/(c-2)+1 <lambda+1 <7/2,
    mu*S<21/4.

Since -log(1-u)=integral_0^u(1-s)^(-1) ds<=3u for0<=u<=2/3,

    exp(-63/4)<A_m<=1.                                  (15)

This bound is only for the first child. It is not a suffix or terminal bound.

## 5. First nonlocal cycle and the central sign reversal

The first three queried points of the ORIGINAL run are alpha_i*v with

    alpha_0=1, alpha_1=1-mu*t_0,
    alpha_2=(1-mu*t_1)*(1-mu*t_0).

All three alpha_i are positive and distinct. Their original residuals are

    Q_ij=-(mu*(1-mu)/2)*(N/2)*(alpha_i-alpha_j)^2.        (16)

This follows by substituting F(alpha v)=mu*alpha^2*N/4 and grad F(alpha v)=
mu*alpha*v into the definition of Q. In particular the first three-query
nonlocal cycle has

    Q_01+Q_12+Q_20
      =-mu*(1-mu)*N/4*[(alpha_0-alpha_1)^2
                         +(alpha_1-alpha_2)^2+(alpha_2-alpha_0)^2]<0.

All other directed cycles are already covered by (11).

At the unique largest step, the still-positive point in (13) is updated by
the path Hessian. Equations (12)--(13) give the EXACT post-central point

    x_(2^(m-1))=-b_m*v,
    b_m=A_m*(mu*d-1), A_m/4<b_m<A_m/2.                  (17)

All former path differences are now negative. Only the closing edge is
positive, with value2*b_m*z. Thus

    2F(x_(2^(m-1)))/R^2=2*b_m^2*z^2/N.                 (18)

This is the actual MIDPOINT payoff, not the terminal one. In particular the
quadratic eigenmode is no longer invariant: grad F(-v) has support only at
vertices0,N-1, whereas -mu*v has nonzero interior coordinates for N>3.

## 6. First two changing-sector suffix steps

Positive homogeneity allows the common amplitude b_m to be factored out;
this does NOT reset a state. Define X_0=-v and let X_k follow the entire
physical suffix H_(m-1) using the SAME enclosing m. Then the actual original
state at the corresponding suffix index is b_m*X_k.

Set u=t_0/4, w=t_1/4. We have1/4<u<3/8 and15/32<=w<1/2. At X_0 only
edge N-1 is positive, of value2z. At X_1 the exact positive differences are

    r_(1,N-1)=q=2z*(1-2u)>0,
    r_(1,0)=r_(1,N-2)=p=z*(2u-4mu)>0.                   (19)

All other differences remain their strictly negative values from -v. For
example, the newly activated edge0 has difference
cos(3theta)-(1-2u)*cos(theta)=z*(2u-4mu), by the triple-angle identity.
The inequality mu<1/96 gives p/z>11/24.

At X_2 the three previously active edge values are

    r_(2,N-1)=(1-2w)*q+2w*p>0,
    r_(2,0)=r_(2,N-2)=(1-2w)*p+w*q>0.                  (20)

The next two edges become active with equal value

    r_(2,1)=r_(2,N-3)=w*p-8mu*z*(1-2mu)>0.             (21)

Indeed cos(3theta)-cos(5theta)=8mu*z*(1-2mu), while
w*p/z>(15/32)*(11/24)=165/768>1/12>8mu*(1-2mu).
Every other interior difference is unchanged and negative. N>12 here, so
the named edges and the unaffected interior are distinct.

Let L_i=(e_i-e_(i+1))(e_i-e_(i+1))^T with cyclic indexing. The first two
suffix Hessians are

    H^(0)=L_(N-1)/4,
    H^(1)=(L_(N-1)+L_0+L_(N-2))/4.                    (22)

They do not commute. Applying their commutator to e_1 gives

    (H^(0)H^(1)-H^(1)H^(0))*e_1=(e_(N-1)-e_0)/16 !=0.

This is an actual sequence of strict sectors, not an assumption about which
Hessians might occur. The second suffix step enlarges the active path again.

For a nonlocal cycle crossing these first suffix transitions, (11) gives a
strict Q_(X1,X0): the positive edge0 at X_1 has value p, while its value at
X_0 is -4mu*z, so its first summand is -p*mu*z<0. Since all other directed
residuals are nonpositive, Q_(X1,X0)+Q_(X0,X2)+Q_(X2,X1)<0.

## 7. Exact chronology for all depths, including ties and zero steps

For an arbitrary nonnegative step t let

    T_t(x)=x-(t/4)*D^T(Dx)_+,
    E_t(y)=y-(t/4)*D D^T y_+.

Thus in edge coordinates the exact recursion is

    y'_(i)=y_i-(t/4)*(2(y_i)_+-(y_(i-1))_+-(y_(i+1))_+). (23)

It preserves sum y_i=0. The formula uses positive parts at each ACTUAL state;
no simultaneous diagonalization or time-homogeneous linear semigroup is
asserted. At a tie the positive part is zero, and at t=0 the map is the identity;
the query and all interpolation rows remain present.

For fixed m define the maps for whole child words by

    Phi_0=identity, Phi_(j+1)=Phi_j o T_(t_j) o Phi_j,
    Psi_0=identity, Psi_(j+1)=Psi_j o E_(t_j) o Psi_j.    (24)

Composition is read from right to left. These expressions apply the first
child, then its central step, then the second child to the OUTPUT of the first
two pieces. They neither change m nor reset x or y at a boundary.

Consequently the original terminal state and its exact payoff are

    x_n=b_m*Phi_(m-1)(-v),
    Y_m=Psi_(m-1)(-Dv)=D Phi_(m-1)(-v),
    E_m=|| (Y_m)_+ ||^2,
    V_m=b_m^2*E_m/(2N).                                (25)

Here E_m denotes a scalar terminal edge energy, not the one-step map E_t.
Equation (25) is an exact all-depth formula for the actual trajectory. Merely
writing it down is not the missing terminal estimate.

One actual but nondecisive upper bound follows directly from (23). Put
M(y)=sum_i(y_i)_+ and

    P_m=product_(j=2)^(m-2) (t_j/2)^(2^(m-2-j)).

For0<=t<=2, (23) is a sum of nonnegative multiples of neighboring positive
parts minus y_-, and M(y')<=M(y). For t>2, discard the negative central
coefficient1-t/2 to get M(y')<=(t/2)M(y). Since M(-Dv)=2z and t_0,t_1<2,

    0<=E_m<=M(Y_m)^2<=4z^2*P_m^2,
    0<=V_m<=2*b_m^2*z^2*P_m^2/N.                        (26)

This upper bound allows enormous growth. It proves neither a useful family
obstruction nor a benchmark-scale positive lower bound. It is included to
distinguish a proved actual terminal bound from the unproved desired estimate.

## 8. Exact asymptotic scale of the retained incoming amplitude

The fixed dimension law and c=lambda(1+1/m) give

    d/lambda^m -> e/lambda^2,
    N^2/lambda^m -> pi^2*e/(6lambda^2),
    mu*d ->3/2.                                        (27)

Here e=exp(1). For the first limit, (1-1/m)(1+1/m)^(m-2)->e;
this follows by bounding log(1+s) between s-s^2/2 and s for small positive s.
The additive1 in d and the ceiling error in N vanish relative to d and sqrt d.
The limit sin(theta)/theta->1 proves the third limit.

Reindex r=m-1-j in (13):

    A_m=product_(r=1)^(m-1)
          [1-mu-(mu*d-mu)*c^(-r)]^(2^(r-1)).

Then

    A_m -> A_infty
      =product_(r=1)^infinity [1-(3/2)*lambda^(-r)]^(2^(r-1))>0,
    b_m -> b_infty=A_infty/2>0.                         (28)

To justify convergence of the product, its logarithmic summands are bounded
in absolute value by3*2^(r-1)*[mu+(3/2)*lambda^(-r)], using (12). For r>R,
the sum of the second term tends to zero uniformly as R->infinity because
2/lambda<1. The first term over ALL r is at most3*mu*2^(m-1), which tends
to zero by (27). Each finite set of summands converges by (27). The limiting
series is absolutely convergent, and each factor is strictly positive since
(3/2)/lambda<1. This proves (28), including positivity, without computation.

Equations (18), (27), and (28) show that the midpoint payoff has exact order
1/N. Combined with (5), its ratio to the ORIGINAL terminal benchmark diverges
like a positive constant times N. That observation identifies energy available
at the reversal. It gives no right to transport it through the suffix.

## 9. The precise remaining nonlocal estimate and original-B comparison

Define the fully specified nonnegative number

    J_m=N*|| [Psi_(m-1)(-Dv)]_+ ||^2 = N*E_m.           (29)

There are no free parameters, omitted rows, adjustable amplitudes, or altered
children in (29). The exact terminal comparison is

    V_m/U_(2^m-1)^ZJ = b_m^2*B_(2^m-1)*J_m/(2N^2).    (30)

The coefficient in front of J_m has the positive finite limit

    K_cycle=3lambda^2*b_infty^2*Z_1/(pi^2*e)
           =3lambda^2*A_infty^2*Z_1/(4pi^2*e).          (31)

Hence the following are precise conditional bridges, not proved conclusions
about J_m:

* If liminf J_m>0, this one law gives a fixed positive multiple of the original
  benchmark on H_m.
* It gives the asymptotic lower bound (1-o(1))/B_(2^m-1) exactly when
  liminf J_m>=1/K_cycle.
* Its original-B ratio tends to zero exactly when J_m tends to zero.
* A claimed limiting constant requires an actual limit for J_m; none is proved.

Equivalence in the second bullet means the usual eventual asymptotic lower
inequality, or equivalently liminf of the payoff ratio at least1. All these
statements follow from (30) and convergence of its positive coefficient; no
asymptotic balanced approximation to B has replaced the all-split recurrence.

The exact open analytical task is to estimate (29) for the chronological
positive-part recurrence (23) with the word (24). Even a proof of
liminf J_m>0 is missing. The radial gap, the first-child product, legality,
and the positive midpoint amplitude do not imply it. Success for (29) would
still concern H_m only, not the original theorem over every nonnegative word.

## 10. Two direct attempts and concrete shortcut failures

Attempt A: extend the scalar low-eigenvalue product through the right child.
This fails at its first gradient query. Formula (17) changes the active path
to the single closing edge; grad F(-v) is supported at two endpoints and is
not -mu*v. Equations (19)--(22) further show actual overlap and noncommutation.
Thus the continued polynomial product is not the selected function's GD.

Even replacing the product by a sum-of-steps diffusion law loses actual order.
Starting at X=-v, either first step t_0 or t_1 yields exactly the same strict
three-edge sector in (22). Both lie below2 and exceed8mu. Writing s=t_0,t=t_1,
the two two-step compositions have difference

    T_t T_s X - T_s T_t X=(t-s)*(H^(0)-H^(1))*X !=0.     (32)

Indeed expand (I-tH^(1))(I-sH^(0))X and the reversed expression; the st term
cancels. The two omitted edge differences of X both equal -4mu*z, so
(H^(0)-H^(1))X is nonzero; t_1>t_0. This comparison refutes an order-free
shortcut on the same static function. It is not a second proposed run or a
change to the specified word.

Attempt B: use the exact radial gap and small-step dissipation to retain the
post-central energy. Equation (23) has nonnegative positive-part coefficients
only when t<=2. The actual level2 step is t_2=1+lambda*(1-1/m^2)>3, and later
levels are larger. The positive-mass argument yields only the expanding
factor t/2 in (26); it cannot give the needed lower bound on J_m.

The absence of a lower norm bound from the small radial gap is concrete.
On this SAME directed cycle consider the mean-zero vector w=e_(N-1)-e_0.
Only its closing edge is positive, so grad F(w)=w/2. The actual level1 step
t_1=2-1/m therefore gives

    T_(t_1)(w)=w/(2m), F(T_(t_1)w)=F(w)/(4m^2).         (33)

Meanwhile the graph's exact gap mu tends to zero exponentially. Thus gap
information alone cannot prevent strong damping of a possible edge-localized
component. This test is a counterexample to the generic proposed inference,
not an assertion that the specified suffix equals w.

The telescoping identity also keeps a signed overstep contribution:

    ||X_(k+1)||^2-||X_k||^2
      =-4h_k F(X_k)+h_k^2||grad F(X_k)||^2.             (34)

For steps above2 the smoothness bound does not turn (34) into a usable
lower bound on terminal energy. Continuous-time diffusion results or a
stable explicit discretization cannot be substituted for these large steps.

No counterexample to the actual statement liminf J_m>0 has been obtained.
Attempts A and B fail as proof routes; the selected family remains open.

## 11. Literature depth and scope

and their dynamics. Its returned theorems concerned different consensus or
optimization systems and supplied no applicable suffix theorem. Web search
located the exact primary paper:

Rasoul Shafipour, Ali Khodabakhsh, Gonzalo Mateos, Evdokia Nikolova,
*A Directed Graph Fourier Transform with Spread Frequency Components*,

The PDF was downloaded to downloads/1804.03000v2.pdf and read through the web
tool's PDF text extraction. Section II-A equation(2) defines directed variation
as sum_ij A_ij*(x_i-x_j)_+^2 with nonnegative weights; its directed edge
convention agrees with D above. Proposition1's directed-path and directed-cycle
maximum-variation claims and their Appendix B--C proofs were read, as was the
underlying-undirected-graph comparison in Proposition2 and its proof.
This supplied context for the energy and the decreasing-run argument.
The paper studies variation and basis construction, not the chronological
large-step suffix (23). No external theorem is imported as a premise: (2),
(6), (9)--(11), and all dynamics are rederived in this joint draft.

The required all-depth benchmark-scale terminal estimate is the unmet part of

This ends the one allocated analytical round. A later continuation would need
