# A critical directed cycle: exact central reversal and the remaining suffix estimate

Status: JOINT UNVERIFIED ANALYTICAL DRAFT, max4 round53, 2026-10-01.
No fact_submit was authorized or made. No numerical evaluations, trajectory
replays, symbolic programs, solvers, benchmark DP, installations, or subagents
were used. All new formulas below are proved together as draft evidence, not
adopted from earlier unverified findings.

This is ONE graph, weight, and initial-state law. It passes the requested early
screens: a vanishing exact radial energy gap, a genuine sector reversal on the
original word, newly activated overlapping edges, and noncommuting Hessians.
The full terminal payoff is NOT bounded at benchmark scale here. Section 9
states the exact remaining scalar energy estimate and its exact original-B
comparison. Section 10 explains why two natural proof attempts do not give it.
In particular, the large midpoint payoff is not a terminal lower bound, and
this document does not rule the family out.

## 1. Fixed law, normalization, and accepted interfaces

Fix an integer m>=8. Write

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda*(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    t_j=1+a*c^j, 0<=j<m,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,t_j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    n=2^m-1, d=t_(m-1)=1+beta*c^(m-2),
    N=ceil(pi*sqrt(d/6)), theta=pi/(2N),
    mu=sin(theta)^2, z=cos(theta),
    v_i=cos((2i+1)*theta), 0<=i<N.                         (1)

All children use this SAME enclosing m. The function, vertex count, and start
are fixed before the first query. The graph has exactly N directed edges
i->i+1 modulo N, each of weight one. For x in R^N define

    (D x)_i=x_i-x_(i+1 mod N),
    F(x)=(1/8)*sum_i ((D x)_i)_+^2,
    x_0=v, x_(k+1)=x_k-h_k*grad F(x_k), h=H_m.           (2)

Here s_+=max(s,0), and vector positive parts are componentwise. The declared
smoothness constant is L=1 throughout (including the payoff). Section 2 proves
this bound and also identifies the least constant, which is 1-mu. We do NOT
recalibrate the word by that least constant. There is no vanishing global
scalar multiplying F: its coefficient is the fixed number 1/8 for all m.

Let 1 be the all-ones vector, e_i the i-th coordinate unit vector,
P=I-11^T/N, and R=dist(v,argmin F). The payoff is

    V_m=2*F(x_n)/R^2.                                   (3)

Fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original W_n normalization and all-directed
residual Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.
Every such inequality is derived directly here, including both terminal
directions and all optimum rows. No terminal-reduction shortcut is used.

For the original benchmark, use accepted b98bb807d514e80d and
04219554e41d9750. In full, C_0=B_0=1 and

    Omega(s,t)=(s+t+sqrt((s+t)^2+4st))/2,
    G(s,t)=2s+t/2+sqrt(t^2+8st)/2,
    C_q=max_(0<=k<q) Omega(C_k,C_(q-k-1)),
    B_q=max_(0<=k<q) G(C_k,B_(q-k-1)), U_q^ZJ=1/B_q.     (4)

Every original split remains. The ray part of accepted04219554e41d9750 says

    lambda^(-m)*B_(2^m-1) -> Z_1, 0<Z_1<infinity.       (5)

Only this unconditional ray assertion is used; none of that fact's conditional
seed hypotheses is asserted to hold. Its statement and the proof's benchmark,
ray enclosure, and convergence sections were read. The prior triangle draft
89154918c70588a0 is motivation only, not a mathematical premise.

## 2. Static function, true radius, exact gap, and smoothness

Put A=D/2. The scalar function s_+^2/2 is convex and continuously
differentiable with derivative s_+. Thus

    F(x)=||(A x)_+||^2/2,
    grad F(x)=A^T(Ax)_+=D^T(Dx)_+/4.                    (6)

The elementary bound sum_i(x_i-x_(i+1))^2<=4 sum_i x_i^2 implies ||D||<=2;
the positive-part map is 1-Lipschitz. Formula (6) therefore proves that F is
convex, everywhere finite, continuously differentiable, and 1-smooth.

Its minimum is zero and its entire minimum set is span{1}. Indeed F(x)=0
means x_i<=x_(i+1) around the entire directed cycle, forcing equality everywhere.
Also 1^T grad F(x)=0, so the mean is preserved at every step, including a zero
step. Pairing i with N-1-i shows sum_i v_i=0. The identity cos^2 u=(1+cos 2u)/2
and the telescoping formula
2*sin(pi/N)*cos((2i+1)*pi/N)=sin((2i+2)*pi/N)-sin(2i*pi/N) give

    R^2=||v||^2=N/2.                                    (7)

There is no hidden choice of a more distant minimizer in this denominator.

For later use, the unweighted combinatorial Laplacian of a path on r vertices, divided by4,
has eigenvectors cos(k*pi*(i+1/2)/r), 0<=k<r, and eigenvalues
sin^2(k*pi/(2r)). This follows by substituting the cosine addition formula at
each interior vertex and the one-neighbor formula at each endpoint. Their
pairwise orthogonality follows by expressing products of cosines as sums and
using the finite geometric series; hence these r vectors form a basis.

The strict active edges of F at any x form a disjoint union of paths, since
all edges of a directed cycle cannot have strictly positive differences. If
H_x=(1/4)*sum_(i:(Dx)_i>0) (e_i-e_(i+1))(e_i-e_(i+1))^T, then

    grad F(x)=H_x x, 2F(x)=x^T H_x x.                    (8)

Every path component has at most N vertices. Its largest eigenvalue is at
most cos^2(pi/(2N))=1-mu. Along a segment, (6) is continuous and affine on
finitely many subsegments; on each its derivative is such a path Hessian.
Integrating along the segment proves that grad F is (1-mu)-Lipschitz.
At the strictly decreasing point v all path edges0,...,N-2 are active and the
closing edge is inactive. Perturbing v a sufficiently small amount in the top
path eigenvector keeps this strict sector. The derivative attains norm1-mu
there. Consequently the LEAST smoothness constant is exactly1-mu.

The exact radial energy gap on the mean-zero space is

    min_(x !=0, sum x_i=0) 2F(x)/||x||^2 = mu.           (9)

Here is a direct proof that does not confuse the gap with strong convexity.
Minimize 2F on the compact mean-zero unit sphere. Its minimum rho is strictly
positive because the only zeroes of F are constants. The multiplier equation
and sum grad F=0 give grad F(x)=rho*x at a minimizer: the multiplier on 1 is
zero, and taking the inner product with x uses <grad F(x),x>=2F(x).
By (8), rho is a positive eigenvalue of a path-component Hessian. The path
spectrum above puts every such positive eigenvalue at least mu. Conversely,
v is strictly decreasing and is the lowest positive cosine eigenvector of
the N-vertex path, so grad F(v)=mu*v and 2F(v)=mu*||v||^2.

Thus (9) is exact, but some sector Hessians have large kernels. In particular
no claim of globally mu-strong convexity is made.

A useful elementary upper value bound is

    sum_i ((Dx)_i)_+^2 <=2||Px||^2, hence 2F(x)<=||Px||^2/2. (10)

To prove it, replace x by Px and partition strict active edges into maximal
decreasing runs. On a run with endpoint values b>=e, the sum of the squared
nonnegative drops is at most (b-e)^2<=2(b^2+e^2). Different runs have disjoint
vertex sets, since at least one inactive edge separates them. Summing yields
(10). Isolated vertices add only nonnegative norm to the right side.

The smoothness constant stays near one while the relevant radial gap mu tends
to zero. Already T_t(v)=(1-t*mu)*v for 0<=t<1/mu shows that no strict norm
contraction independent of N can be transported from the triangle family.

## 3. All original directed rows with the non-isometric incidence

For ANY two points x_i,x_j define y_i=D x_i, r_i=(y_i)_+, and Delta r=r_i-r_j.
Their actual value and gradient residual is exactly

    Q_ij=-(1/4)*sum_e r_(i,e)*(-y_(j,e))_+
         -(1/32)*sum_e (Delta r_e+Delta r_(e+1))^2 <=0,  (11)

with indices modulo N. No condition on chronological proximity or sector is
present, so this includes nonlocal, optimum, and terminal rows.

Proof: for phi(s)=s_+^2/2 a direct check of the four sign combinations gives

    phi(u)-phi(w)+u_+*(w-u)+(u_+-w_+)^2/2=-u_+*(-w)_+.

Sum this at u=(Ax_i)_e,w=(Ax_j)_e and then correct the gradient norm from
||Delta p||^2 to ||A^T Delta p||^2, where p_i=(Ax_i)_+=r_i/2. This yields

    Q_ij=-<p_i,(-Ax_j)_+>
          -(1/2)<Delta p,(I-AA^T)Delta p>.

Here AA^T is the CYCLE Laplacian divided by4, not a projection. For every w,

    <w,(I-AA^T)w>=(1/4)*sum_e(w_e+w_(e+1))^2.

Substitute Delta p=Delta r/2 to obtain (11). This also proves the required
positive semidefiniteness without using an isometric incidence identity.
Ties give zero positive parts and cause no exception.

## 4. The rounding law and the exact first child

The following elementary estimates hold for every m>=8:

    d>144, mu<1/96, 5/4<mu*d<3/2,
    mu*t_j<2/3 for every j<=m-2.                         (12)

First lambda>12/5, beta>=7/8, and (12/5)^3=1728/125>13 give
d>1+(7/8)*13^2>144. Put b=pi*sqrt(d/6). Since sqrt(6)<pi and sqrt(d)>12,
1/b<1/12 and b<=N<b+1<(13/12)b. Thus
theta<=sqrt(6)/(2sqrt(d))<1/8 and theta^2<1/96.
Integration of cos u>=1-u^2/2 gives sin(theta)/theta>=1-theta^2/6>99/100.
It follows that

    mu*d < pi^2*d/(4N^2) <=3/2,
    mu*d >(3/2)*(12/13)^2*(99/100)^2 >5/4.

For the last strict comparison, the numerator216*9801=2117016 exceeds
(5/4)*1690000=2112500. Finally

    t_(m-2)/d =1/c+(1-1/c)/d <5/12+1/144=61/144,
    mu*t_(m-2)<61/96<2/3.

On the positive ray of v, grad F(qv)=q*mu*v for q>=0. By (12), each factor
1-mu*t_j in the first child is positive. Induction over the ACTUAL physical
steps, not a rearranged nonlinear trajectory, gives

    x_(2^(m-1)-1)=A_m*v,
    A_m=product_(j=0)^(m-2)(1-mu*t_j)^(2^(m-2-j))>0.    (13)

The multiplicity comes from the original recursive concatenation. Regrouping
these scalar factors is justified only because the entire first child has
just been proved to stay in this one sector.

For completeness A_m has a uniform positive lower bound. Let
S=sum H_(m-1). Summing the physical multiplicities gives

    S=2^(m-1)-1+[a/(c-2)]*(c^(m-1)-2^(m-1)).            (14)

We have 0<a/(c-2)<1 because c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1>beta.
Also d>2^(m-1): the lower bound (7/8)*(12/5)^(m-2) exceeds2^(m-1) at m=8
(using13^2), and its ratio to2^(m-1) increases by6/5 with each increment of m.
Consequently

    S/d <1/(c-2)+1 <lambda+1 <7/2,
    mu*S<21/4.

Since -log(1-u)=integral_0^u(1-s)^(-1) ds<=3u for0<=u<=2/3,

    exp(-63/4)<A_m<=1.                                  (15)

This bound is only for the first child. It is not a suffix or terminal bound.

## 5. First nonlocal cycle and the central sign reversal

The first three queried points of the ORIGINAL run are alpha_i*v with

    alpha_0=1, alpha_1=1-mu*t_0,
    alpha_2=(1-mu*t_1)*(1-mu*t_0).

All three alpha_i are positive and distinct. Their original residuals are

    Q_ij=-(mu*(1-mu)/2)*(N/2)*(alpha_i-alpha_j)^2.        (16)

This follows by substituting F(alpha v)=mu*alpha^2*N/4 and grad F(alpha v)=
mu*alpha*v into the definition of Q. In particular the first three-query
nonlocal cycle has

    Q_01+Q_12+Q_20
      =-mu*(1-mu)*N/4*[(alpha_0-alpha_1)^2
                         +(alpha_1-alpha_2)^2+(alpha_2-alpha_0)^2]<0.

All other directed cycles are already covered by (11).

At the unique largest step, the still-positive point in (13) is updated by
the path Hessian. Equations (12)--(13) give the EXACT post-central point

    x_(2^(m-1))=-b_m*v,
    b_m=A_m*(mu*d-1), A_m/4<b_m<A_m/2.                  (17)

All former path differences are now negative. Only the closing edge is
positive, with value2*b_m*z. Thus

    2F(x_(2^(m-1)))/R^2=2*b_m^2*z^2/N.                 (18)

This is the actual MIDPOINT payoff, not the terminal one. In particular the
quadratic eigenmode is no longer invariant: grad F(-v) has support only at
vertices0,N-1, whereas -mu*v has nonzero interior coordinates for N>3.

## 6. First two changing-sector suffix steps

Positive homogeneity allows the common amplitude b_m to be factored out;
this does NOT reset a state. Define X_0=-v and let X_k follow the entire
physical suffix H_(m-1) using the SAME enclosing m. Then the actual original
state at the corresponding suffix index is b_m*X_k.

Set u=t_0/4, w=t_1/4. We have1/4<u<3/8 and15/32<=w<1/2. At X_0 only
edge N-1 is positive, of value2z. At X_1 the exact positive differences are

    r_(1,N-1)=q=2z*(1-2u)>0,
    r_(1,0)=r_(1,N-2)=p=z*(2u-4mu)>0.                   (19)

All other differences remain their strictly negative values from -v. For
example, the newly activated edge0 has difference
cos(3theta)-(1-2u)*cos(theta)=z*(2u-4mu), by the triple-angle identity.
The inequality mu<1/96 gives p/z>11/24.

At X_2 the three previously active edge values are

    r_(2,N-1)=(1-2w)*q+2w*p>0,
    r_(2,0)=r_(2,N-2)=(1-2w)*p+w*q>0.                  (20)

The next two edges become active with equal value

    r_(2,1)=r_(2,N-3)=w*p-8mu*z*(1-2mu)>0.             (21)

Indeed cos(3theta)-cos(5theta)=8mu*z*(1-2mu), while
w*p/z>(15/32)*(11/24)=165/768>1/12>8mu*(1-2mu).
Every other interior difference is unchanged and negative. N>12 here, so
the named edges and the unaffected interior are distinct.

Let L_i=(e_i-e_(i+1))(e_i-e_(i+1))^T with cyclic indexing. The first two
suffix Hessians are

    H^(0)=L_(N-1)/4,
    H^(1)=(L_(N-1)+L_0+L_(N-2))/4.                    (22)

They do not commute. Applying their commutator to e_1 gives

    (H^(0)H^(1)-H^(1)H^(0))*e_1=(e_(N-1)-e_0)/16 !=0.

This is an actual sequence of strict sectors, not an assumption about which
Hessians might occur. The second suffix step enlarges the active path again.

For a nonlocal cycle crossing these first suffix transitions, (11) gives a
strict Q_(X1,X0): the positive edge0 at X_1 has value p, while its value at
X_0 is -4mu*z, so its first summand is -p*mu*z<0. Since all other directed
residuals are nonpositive, Q_(X1,X0)+Q_(X0,X2)+Q_(X2,X1)<0.

## 7. Exact chronology for all depths, including ties and zero steps

For an arbitrary nonnegative step t let

    T_t(x)=x-(t/4)*D^T(Dx)_+,
    E_t(y)=y-(t/4)*D D^T y_+.

Thus in edge coordinates the exact recursion is

    y'_(i)=y_i-(t/4)*(2(y_i)_+-(y_(i-1))_+-(y_(i+1))_+). (23)

It preserves sum y_i=0. The formula uses positive parts at each ACTUAL state;
no simultaneous diagonalization or time-homogeneous linear semigroup is
asserted. At a tie the positive part is zero, and at t=0 the map is the identity;
the query and all interpolation rows remain present.

For fixed m define the maps for whole child words by

    Phi_0=identity, Phi_(j+1)=Phi_j o T_(t_j) o Phi_j,
    Psi_0=identity, Psi_(j+1)=Psi_j o E_(t_j) o Psi_j.    (24)

Composition is read from right to left. These expressions apply the first
child, then its central step, then the second child to the OUTPUT of the first
two pieces. They neither change m nor reset x or y at a boundary.

Consequently the original terminal state and its exact payoff are

    x_n=b_m*Phi_(m-1)(-v),
    Y_m=Psi_(m-1)(-Dv)=D Phi_(m-1)(-v),
    E_m=|| (Y_m)_+ ||^2,
    V_m=b_m^2*E_m/(2N).                                (25)

Here E_m denotes a scalar terminal edge energy, not the one-step map E_t.
Equation (25) is an exact all-depth formula for the actual trajectory. Merely
writing it down is not the missing terminal estimate.

One actual but nondecisive upper bound follows directly from (23). Put
M(y)=sum_i(y_i)_+ and

    P_m=product_(j=2)^(m-2) (t_j/2)^(2^(m-2-j)).

For0<=t<=2, (23) is a sum of nonnegative multiples of neighboring positive
parts minus y_-, and M(y')<=M(y). For t>2, discard the negative central
coefficient1-t/2 to get M(y')<=(t/2)M(y). Here t_0<3/2, t_1<2, and
t_j>=t_2=1+lambda*(1-1/m^2)>3 for j>=2 and m>=8. Since M(-Dv)=2z,

    0<=E_m<=M(Y_m)^2<=4z^2*P_m^2,
    0<=V_m<=2*b_m^2*z^2*P_m^2/N.                        (26)

This upper bound allows enormous growth. It proves neither a useful family
obstruction nor a benchmark-scale positive lower bound. It is included to
distinguish a proved actual terminal bound from the unproved desired estimate.

## 8. Exact asymptotic scale of the retained incoming amplitude

The fixed dimension law and c=lambda(1+1/m) give

    d/lambda^m -> e/lambda^2,
    N^2/lambda^m -> pi^2*e/(6lambda^2),
    mu*d ->3/2.                                        (27)

Here e=exp(1). For the first limit, (1-1/m)(1+1/m)^(m-2)->e;
this follows by bounding log(1+s) between s-s^2/2 and s for small positive s.
The additive1 in d and the ceiling error in N vanish relative to d and sqrt d.
The limit sin(theta)/theta->1 proves the third limit.

Reindex r=m-1-j in (13):

    A_m=product_(r=1)^(m-1)
          [1-mu-(mu*d-mu)*c^(-r)]^(2^(r-1)).

Then

    A_m -> A_infty
      =product_(r=1)^infinity [1-(3/2)*lambda^(-r)]^(2^(r-1))>0,
    b_m -> b_infty=A_infty/2>0.                         (28)

To justify convergence of the product, its logarithmic summands are bounded
in absolute value by3*2^(r-1)*[mu+(3/2)*lambda^(-r)], using (12). For an
integer cutoff r_cut and r>r_cut, the sum of the second term tends to zero
uniformly as r_cut->infinity because
2/lambda<1. The first term over ALL r is at most3*mu*2^(m-1), which tends
to zero by (27). Each finite set of summands converges by (27). The limiting
series is absolutely convergent, and each factor is strictly positive since
(3/2)/lambda<1. This proves (28), including positivity, without computation.

Equations (18), (27), and (28) show that the midpoint payoff has exact order
1/N. Combined with (5), its ratio to the ORIGINAL terminal benchmark diverges
like a positive constant times N. That observation identifies energy available
at the reversal. It gives no right to transport it through the suffix.

## 9. The precise remaining nonlocal estimate and original-B comparison

Define the fully specified nonnegative number

    J_m=N*|| [Psi_(m-1)(-Dv)]_+ ||^2 = N*E_m.           (29)

There are no free parameters, omitted rows, adjustable amplitudes, or altered
children in (29). The exact terminal comparison is

    V_m/U_(2^m-1)^ZJ = b_m^2*B_(2^m-1)*J_m/(2N^2).    (30)

The coefficient in front of J_m has the positive finite limit

    K_cycle=3lambda^2*b_infty^2*Z_1/(pi^2*e)
           =3lambda^2*A_infty^2*Z_1/(4pi^2*e).          (31)

Hence the following are precise conditional bridges, not proved conclusions
about J_m:

* If liminf J_m>0, this one law gives a fixed positive multiple of the original
  benchmark on H_m.
* It gives the asymptotic lower bound (1-o(1))/B_(2^m-1) exactly when
  liminf J_m>=1/K_cycle.
* Its original-B ratio tends to zero exactly when J_m tends to zero.
* A claimed limiting constant requires an actual limit for J_m; none is proved.

Equivalence in the second bullet means the usual eventual asymptotic lower
inequality, or equivalently liminf of the payoff ratio at least1. All these
statements follow from (30) and convergence of its positive coefficient; no
asymptotic balanced approximation to B has replaced the all-split recurrence.

The exact open analytical task is to estimate (29) for the chronological
positive-part recurrence (23) with the word (24). Even a proof of
liminf J_m>0 is missing. The radial gap, the first-child product, legality,
and the positive midpoint amplitude do not imply it. Success for (29) would
still concern H_m only, not the original theorem over every nonnegative word.

## 10. Two direct attempts and concrete shortcut failures

Attempt A: extend the scalar low-eigenvalue product through the right child.
This fails at its first gradient query. Formula (17) changes the active path
to the single closing edge; grad F(-v) is supported at two endpoints and is
not -mu*v. Equations (19)--(22) further show actual overlap and noncommutation.
Thus the continued polynomial product is not the selected function's GD.

Even replacing the product by a sum-of-steps diffusion law loses actual order.
Starting at X=-v, either first step t_0 or t_1 yields exactly the same strict
three-edge sector in (22). Both lie below2 and exceed8mu. Writing s=t_0,t=t_1,
the two two-step compositions have difference

    T_t T_s X - T_s T_t X=(t-s)*(H^(0)-H^(1))*X !=0.     (32)

Indeed expand (I-tH^(1))(I-sH^(0))X and the reversed expression; the st term
cancels. The two omitted edge differences of X both equal -4mu*z, so
(H^(0)-H^(1))X is nonzero; t_1>t_0. This comparison refutes an order-free
shortcut on the same static function. It is not a second proposed run or a
change to the specified word.

Attempt B: use the exact radial gap and small-step dissipation to retain the
post-central energy. Equation (23) has nonnegative positive-part coefficients
only when t<=2. The actual level2 step is t_2=1+lambda*(1-1/m^2)>3, and later
levels are larger. The positive-mass argument yields only the expanding
factor t/2 in (26); it cannot give the needed lower bound on J_m.

The absence of a lower norm bound from the small radial gap is concrete.
On this SAME directed cycle consider the mean-zero vector w=e_(N-1)-e_0.
Only its closing edge is positive, so grad F(w)=w/2. The actual level1 step
t_1=2-1/m therefore gives

    T_(t_1)(w)=w/(2m), F(T_(t_1)w)=F(w)/(4m^2).         (33)

Meanwhile the graph's exact gap mu tends to zero exponentially. Thus gap
information alone cannot prevent strong damping of a possible edge-localized
component. This test is a counterexample to the generic proposed inference,
not an assertion that the specified suffix equals w.

The telescoping identity also keeps a signed overstep contribution:

    ||X_(k+1)||^2-||X_k||^2
      =-4h_k F(X_k)+h_k^2||grad F(X_k)||^2.             (34)

For steps above2 the smoothness bound does not turn (34) into a usable
lower bound on terminal energy. Continuous-time diffusion results or a
stable explicit discretization cannot be substituted for these large steps.

No counterexample to the actual statement liminf J_m>0 has been obtained.
Attempts A and B fail as proof routes; the selected family remains open.

Rasoul Shafipour, Ali Khodabakhsh, Gonzalo Mateos, Evdokia Nikolova,

## 1. Scope recovered before choosing the laws

The following are shared, UNVERIFIED drafts, not premises of the proofs below.

* 4d3911499920adbe uses that same no-+1 word. Its channels are precisely

Accepted scopes were also checked. Fact 1fca3e5dd555cb4a constructs its
specified outward alternating-ray stages, including offsets and retained

Only fact b98bb807d514e80d is needed as a mathematical predecessor below,
for the definitions and accepted bounds on the ORIGINAL benchmark. Every
new scalar calculation is reproduced in this joint draft. In particular no
shared unverified closure is imported as a lemma.

## 2. Original word, exact prefix products, and benchmark

Fix an integer m>=32 and retain this SAME m in every child. Put

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), t=1/m, beta=1-t,
    c_m=lambda*(1+t), a_m=beta/c_m,
    c=c_m, a=a_m (local aliases), b_j=a*c^j, d_j=1+b_j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j), j=0,...,m-1,
    n=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j.

The letter b_j in this document is the bridge EXCESS, not a physical step.
Let ell(i)=nu_2(i+1), where nu_2(k) is the exponent of2 dividing the positive
integer k. The actual physical step at index i is h_i=d_(ell(i)). Let s_2(i)
be the number of ones in the binary expansion of i, including s_2(0)=0.
For 0<=i<=n define

    Prod_i=product_(0<=r<i)(h_r-1)=beta^i*c^(-s_2(i)).              (2.1)

Here and below all finite sums and products are mathematical definitions;
none was evaluated by a program. To prove (2.1), binary carrying gives
s_2(i+1)=s_2(i)+1-nu_2(i+1). The ratio of its right sides at i+1 and i
is beta*c^(ell(i)-1)=a*c^ell(i)=h_i-1. Both sides start at1. In particular

    Prod_n=beta^n*c^(-m).                                        (2.2)

The S_j recurrence S_(j+1)=2*S_j+1+a*c^j gives

    S_j+1=A*c^j+(1-A)*2^j, A=a/(c-2)=beta/[c*(c-2)].          (2.3)

Since c>lambda>2 and lambda*(lambda-2)=1, we have 0<A<1, and hence
S_m+1<=c^m. These parameters also have 0<a<1, 0<beta<1, and c<3:
lambda<5/2 and c<=(5/2)*(33/32)=165/64<3.

Write C_k=1+S_circle(k), B_k=1+2*S_bullet(k), U_k^ZJ=1/B_k.
Fact b98bb807d514e80d supplies

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_k=max_(0<=r<k) Omega(C_r,C_(k-r-1)),
    B_k=max_(0<=r<k) G(C_r,B_(k-r-1)),
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4*u*v))/2,
    G(u,v)=2*u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8*u*v)/2,
    B_k<=1+4*k^(log_2(3)).

Thus, on the original physical length n=2^m-1,

    B_n<=5*3^m.                                              (2.4)

No asymptotic constant or numerically evaluated benchmark is needed here.
All payoffs use L=1 and TRUE distance to the minimizer set:

    V=2*(f(x_n)-min f)/dist(x_0,argmin f)^2.

Multiplying f by an arbitrary L>0 and using steps h_i/L preserves all
positions and this normalized payoff.

## 3. Law I: a flat minimizer interval with two unit-curvature sides

For any width w>=0 let I_w=[-w,0] and define the single static function

              (x+w)^2/2, x<-w,
    f_w(x)=   0,         -w<=x<=0,
              x^2/2,    x>0.

Let p_w(x)=min(0,max(-w,x)) be the interval projection, and put
g_w(x)=x-p_w(x). The derivative is continuous, nondecreasing, and has slopes
one, zero, one in spatial order. Consequently f_w is convex and1-smooth,
with exactly the minimizer set I_w and minimum0. For w>0 it is genuinely
nonlinear. We always normalize using distance to I_w, not distance to its
midpoint or another more distant chosen minimizer.

### 3.1 All directed inequalities and all integrated values

At every point, with y=p_w(x), we have

    x=g+y, f_w(x)=g^2/2, y in I_w.

For any two sampled points i,j, including ANY chosen optimum, the full
signed directed interpolation residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+g_i*(x_j-x_i)+(g_i-g_j)^2/2
        =g_i*(y_j-y_i)<=0.                                  (3.1)

Indeed g_i>0 implies y_i=0>=y_j; g_i<0 implies y_i=-w<=y_j;
and g_i=0 gives equality. This is an explicit all-pairs proof, including
both directions, all optimum rows, repeated points, and every plateau area.
The formula f=g^2/2 integrates the fixed derivative from the actual interval;
it is not a deletion of a previously accumulated area.

### 3.2 Actual GD, zero steps, capture, and exact revisits

Let Dist_i=dist(x_i,I_w), with Dist_0>0. At any outside point, a step h>=0 gives

    Dist_next=(1-h)*Dist_i,                     0<=h<=1,
    Dist_next=((h-1)*Dist_i-w)_+,               h>1.                (3.2)

For h<=1 the point stays on its current side or lands on its boundary.
For h>1 it either lands inside I_w or crosses to the opposite outside side.
An inside point has zero gradient and stays at precisely that same point.
This proves (3.2) directly on both sides of the interval. A zero step repeats
the complete jet. There is no restart at a different minimizer after capture.

Exact outside revisits are also legal: for any w>0,D>0, two consecutive
steps h=2+w/D take D to -w-D and then back to D. Each outside value is D^2/2.
This illustration uses the SAME law, not an additional candidate family.
Its only purpose is to make the exact-revisit convention explicit.

On our original word all h_i>1. Define Ret_0=0 and

    Ret_(i+1)=(h_i-1)*Ret_i+1,
    Ret_i=Prod_i*sum_(r=1)^i 1/Prod_r.                              (3.3)

Repeated application of (3.2) gives the exact formula

    Dist_i=(Prod_i*Dist_0-w*Ret_i)_+.                                 (3.4)

For the induction, ((b*z)_+-w)_+=(b*z-w)_+ when b,w>=0;
applying this to the preceding affine expression proves the next step.
If capture has occurred, the expression remains zero as required.

Consequently, for ALL w>=0 and every initial point outside I_w,

    V_w=(Dist_n/Dist_0)^2<=Prod_n^2=beta^(2*n)*c^(-2*m).             (3.5)

This is an upper bound on the actual error of the entire specified law,
including horizon-dependent widths, either initial side, and arbitrary
initial distances. It is not an upper bound on arbitrary scalar functions.

### 3.3 A concrete nonlinear, noncaptured trajectory and its full spatial order

Here is one exact choice with w>0 and every queried distance positive.
The Prod_i in (2.1) are pairwise distinct. To see this, all are in Q(sqrt(2)).
The nontrivial conjugation fixes beta and sends c to
c'=(1-sqrt(2))*(1+1/m). If beta^(i-j)*c^(-s_2(i)+s_2(j))=1,
divide by its conjugate. Since |c/c'|=lambda^2>1, the integer exponent
of c must be zero. Then beta^(i-j)=1 implies i=j.

Define the positive finite quantities

    Delta_sp=min_(0<=i<j<=n)|Prod_i-Prod_j|,
    Ret_max=max_(0<=i<=n) Ret_i,
    w=min{Prod_n/(2*Ret_n), Delta_sp/(4*Ret_max)}.                    (3.6)

These finite expressions define the width before the run; they are not a
numerical search or an unproved optimization problem. Start at x_0=1 and
choose the closest minimizer0, so the TRUE initial squared distance is1.
Since Ret_i/Prod_i is increasing in i, (3.6) implies

    Dist_i=Prod_i-w*Ret_i>=Prod_i/2>0,
    x_i=Dist_i if i is even, and x_i=-w-Dist_i if i is odd.         (3.7)

Every step thus crosses the whole minimizer interval. Equations (3.2)--(3.7)
give every physical point, derivative, value, and GD update without deleting
any interval or knot.

For completeness the spatial order, which is not chronological, is exact.
Put alpha=-log(beta)/log(c)>0 and order_i=s_2(i)+alpha*i. Then
Prod_i=c^(-order_i), and the order_i are distinct by the preceding argument.
For every pair, |w*(Ret_i-Ret_j)|<=Delta_sp/4<|Prod_i-Prod_j|, so Dist_i-Dist_j has exactly
the sign of Prod_i-Prod_j. Every odd-indexed point is less than -w; every
even-indexed point is positive. Among even indices, increasing order_i means
decreasing x; among odd indices, increasing order_i means increasing x.
This completely specifies the total order by explicit, distinct real keys
for each m, with NO guessed phase comparisons and no ties. The fixed
minimizer interval lies between the two groups. Other widths may have ties;
(3.1)--(3.4) still apply without changing any previously defined value.

The terminal point is -w-Dist_n, since n is odd, and

    f_w(x_n)=(Prod_n-w*Ret_n)^2/2,
    Prod_n^2/4<=V_w=(Prod_n-w*Ret_n)^2<Prod_n^2.                     (3.8)

Thus this nonlinear example has a proved exact payoff, not just a lower
certificate. Nevertheless (2.4)--(3.5) imply uniformly for the whole law

    B_n*V_w<=5*(3/lambda^2)^m ->0.                         (3.9)

The flat-minimum mechanism is weak on the original word even when its
width is chosen from the entire word and every queried point remains outside.

## 4. Law II: a one-sided Huber shelf with an actual inward return

Fix ONE function, independent of m:

              x^2/2, x<=1,
    F_sh(x)=  x-1/2, x>=1,
    g_sh(x)=min(x,1).

It is convex, differentiable, globally1-smooth, with unique minimizer0 and
minimum0. Its negative ray is quadratic and its positive ray eventually
has constant gradient. In particular the two outer ray gradients have no
finite multiplicative comparison bound of the type in e08ee0674ce368d3.
The complete function is fixed throughout the trajectory.

Define y(x)=(x-1)_+. Then at every x

    x=g+y, F_sh(x)=g^2/2+y, g<=1, y>=0, (1-g)*y=0.          (4.1)

The positive proximal value y is retained on every return to the shelf.
For ANY two points, including optimum0 and repeated queries,

    Q_ij=(1-g_i)*(y_i-y_j)=-(1-g_i)*y_j<=0.                (4.2)

This explicit factorization proves ALL directed inequalities for the entire
trajectory, including every incoming and outgoing terminal row. It uses
the integrated value in (4.1), not just the slope or a pointwise envelope.

### 4.1 Parameters of the selected return branch

Use exactly the enclosing-m d_0,d_1,d_2,d_3 from Section2 and put

    w_sh=beta^2*c,
    v_sh=w_sh-1-beta,
    R_sh=S_3+1=8+4*a+2*beta+beta*c.

For every m>=32 the following strict inequalities hold:

    0<v_sh<a*beta,
    c*v_sh<beta^2<1,
    1+beta<w_sh<2+a.                                     (4.3)

Here is an exact proof without numerical evaluation. Since beta>=31/32
and c>12/5, w_sh>(31/32)^2*(12/5)>2, the last inequality following from
12*31^2>10*32^2. Thus v_sh>0. Also

    c*v_sh-beta^2
      =lambda^2*(1-t^2)^2-lambda*(2+t-t^2)-(1-2*t+t^2)
      <=(2-lambda)*t-(lambda+2)*t^2<0.

The inequality uses (1-t^2)^2<=1-t^2 and lambda^2=2*lambda+1.
It proves c*v_sh<beta^2 and hence v_sh<a*beta. Finally

    c*(w_sh-2-a)
      =beta^2*c^2-2*c-beta
      <=lambda^2-2*lambda*(1+t)-(1-t)
      =-(2*lambda-1)*t<0.

Choose any delta in the FULL interval [0,v_sh/a] and start at

    X_0=R_sh+delta, z_sh=v_sh-a*delta>=0.                  (4.4)

The squared distance to the unique minimizer is exactly (R_sh+delta)^2.
The endpoint delta=v_sh/a is permitted and will give a genuine zero landing.

### 4.2 First ten physical steps, with the old shelf intact

The first seven steps are the actual word H_3, with levels

    0,1,0,2,0,1,0.

For 0<=i<=7 let Prefix_sh(i) be the sum of its first i physical steps. Then

    X_i=R_sh+delta-Prefix_sh(i)>=1+delta,
    g_i=1, F_sh(X_i)=X_i-1/2.                             (4.5)

All seven updates are therefore exactly the original GD updates, and
X_7=1+delta. The next three original physical levels are3,0,1, giving

    X_8=delta-b_3,      g_8=X_8,   F_sh(X_8)=X_8^2/2,
    X_9=w_sh-a*delta,   g_9=1,     F_sh(X_9)=X_9-1/2,
    X_10=z_sh,          g_10=z_sh, F_sh(X_10)=z_sh^2/2.      (4.6)

The equations follow in order from
X_8=X_7-d_3, X_9=-a*X_8, and X_10=X_9-d_1.
Their region assumptions are proved, not guessed:

    b_3-delta>=(w_sh-v_sh)/a=(1+beta)/a>1,
    X_9=1+beta+z_sh>1,
    0<=z_sh<=v_sh<1.

Furthermore delta<=v_sh/a<beta implies

    X_7<X_9<X_6, with X_6=2+a+delta.                      (4.7)

The right inequality follows from X_9<=w_sh<2+a<=X_6.
Thus X_9 is a strict inward return into the SAME spatial interval [X_7,X_6]
traversed during the last step of the earlier H_3. The shelf gradient there
is1 and its retained proximal value is y_9=X_9-1>0. Nothing is redefined on
this return. This is not an outward-only fresh-ray construction.

### 4.3 Every remaining query, spatial order, and ties

For EVERY actual physical index 10<=i<=n the exact formula is

    X_i=(-1)^(i-10)*z_sh*beta^(i-10)*c^(2-s_2(i)).          (4.8)

If z_sh=0 this means precisely that the actual point0 is repeated forever.
Assume z_sh>0. Since s_2(i)>=1 for i>=10,

    |X_i|<=c*z_sh<=c*v_sh<beta^2<1.                       (4.9)

Thus every one of these queries really has gradient X_i and value X_i^2/2.
At i=10, s_2(10)=2 gives the correct point z_sh. Binary carrying then gives

    X_(i+1)/X_i=-beta*c^(ell(i)-1)=-(h_i-1)=1-h_i.

This verifies every remaining GD update on the original physical word.
No child clock was restarted. In particular the bound (4.9) certifies every
intermediate query, not merely the endpoints of large blocks. Gradients
continue to vary inside those blocks.

Here is the complete spatial order. X_8<-1 is below every later negative
point. Every positive point of the tail is less than1. The old positive
queries are ordered

    1<=X_7<X_9<X_6<X_5<...<X_0.

The optimum0 separates the positive and negative tail points. For i>=10,
even i means positive and odd i means negative. Within either sign, their
magnitudes are proportional to c^(-order_i), with the SAME explicit keys
order_i=s_2(i)+alpha*i used in Section3.3. Thus increasing order_i gives
decreasing positive coordinates and increasing negative coordinates.
There are no ties among those keys: an equality of two magnitudes would
give beta^(i-j)*c^(-s_2(i)+s_2(j))=1, already proved to force i=j.
There are also no ties with the older groups by their strict separating
intervals. When z_sh=0, all indices i>=10 instead coincide with optimum0,
with gradient and value0. These are all ties in this construction.

The word itself has no zero steps. If a zero step is inserted, its actual
map x->x-0*g_sh(x) is the identity and repeats its jet; (4.2) remains valid.
Formula (4.8) refers to the original positive steps and can be pulled back
along their index injection. No claim transfers B_n to a new padded length.

### 4.4 Exact payoff and a uniform upper screen for this branch

The original n is odd and s_2(n)=m. Therefore

    X_n=-z_sh*beta^(n-10)*c^(2-m),
    F_sh(X_n)=z_sh^2*beta^(2*(n-10))*c^(4-2*m)/2,
    V_sh(delta)=((v_sh-a*delta)/(R_sh+delta))^2
                 *beta^(2*(n-10))*c^(4-2*m).              (4.10)

Over the ENTIRE selected interval 0<=delta<=v_sh/a, the numerator of the
fraction decreases to zero while its positive denominator increases. Its
maximum is attained at delta=0 and equals the displayed expression with
v_sh/R_sh. In particular, using c*v_sh<1, c<3, R_sh>1, and beta<1,

    V_sh(delta)<9*c^(-2*m),
    B_n*V_sh(delta)<45*(3/lambda^2)^m ->0.                 (4.11)

These are actual error upper bounds on a fully specified returning family.
For all m>=32 they already give V_sh<U_n^ZJ: lambda^2>9/2 implies
3/lambda^2<2/3, and 45*(2/3)^10=46080/59049<1. The same comparison for
Law I follows from (3.9). No guessed decimal or numerical phase is involved.

## 5. Counterchecks preventing an overstatement or a reset

### 5.1 Erasing the return's old area violates a directed inequality

On the trajectory (4.4)--(4.8), replace ONLY the value at X_9 by the falsely
reset core value g_9^2/2=1/2, leaving its position and derivative unchanged.
The earlier point X_7 has gradient1 and value X_7-1/2. Its row to point9 is

    Q_(7,9)=(X_7-1/2)-1/2+(X_9-X_7)=X_9-1>0.

This is an exact illegal directed pair, not an appeal to intuition about
history. The correct value X_9-1/2 has retained area X_9-1 and satisfies
every row by (4.2). The construction therefore directly tests the nonzero
proximal-height issue in the assignment.

### 5.2 The branch bound is FALSE for all starts of the same shelf function

Keep exactly F_sh and the same original H_m, but start at

    X_0^Hub=2*S_m+1.

Every actual query stays in the positive shelf, since even the terminal
point is S_m+1>1. Thus all gradients are1, the terminal value is S_m+1/2,

## 1. The unchanged object and its actual terminal normalization

Fix the enclosing integer m>=8 and define

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    t_j=1+a c^j, 0<=j<m,

    z=cos(theta), v_i=cos((2i+1)theta), 0<=i<N.

Every child uses this same m. Indices on vectors are cyclic modulo N. Put

    (D x)_i=x_i-x_(i+1), L_e=D D^T,
    F(x)=||(D x)_+||^2/8,

Here s_+=max(s,0), used componentwise on vectors; norms and inner

The declared smoothness remains 1. Indeed, the derivative of s_+^2/2 is
s_+, so grad F(x)=D^T(Dx)_+/4. The positive-part map is 1-Lipschitz and

Pairing i and N-1-i gives sum v_i=0. Also sum cos((4i+2)theta)=0:

## 2. Exact positive-mass accounting, including new negative mass

At physical step h_k write alpha_k=h_k/4. Differentiating the actual vertex
update gives, without a sector assumption,

    y_(k+1)=y_k-alpha_k L_e r_k,
    y'_(i)=y_i-2alpha r_i+alpha(r_(i-1)+r_(i+1)).      (6)

At ties r_i=0. Formula (6) preserves sum y_i=0. Let
n_i=(-y_i)_+ and w_i=alpha(r_(i-1)+r_(i+1)). For one step define

    O_alpha(y)=sum_(i:y_i>0) [(2alpha-1)r_i-w_i]_+,
    C_alpha(y)=sum_(i:y_i<=0) min(n_i,w_i).

Then the exact mass identity is

    M(y')=M(y)+O_alpha(y)-C_alpha(y).                  (7)

To prove it, on an old positive coordinate the new value is

summand of O_alpha. On an old nonpositive coordinate its new negative
part is (n_i-w_i)_+=n_i-min(n_i,w_i). Sum these negative parts and use

## 3. Cumulative flux and the exact first failed least-action hypothesis

The grid maximum of sin(k pi/N) is s_N, so min q*=0. Sine subtraction

## 4. A quantitative flux bound and why its total-clock closure is empty

For any mean-zero vector X, let M=sum_i(DX)_i,+,
J=N||(DX)_+||^2, and osc(X)=max_i X_i-min_i X_i. A directed path from a maximizing vertex to a minimizing
vertex shows osc(X)<=M. The mean-zero condition then gives |X_i|<=M,
and Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    M<=sqrt(J).                                      (14)

At the actual terminal time put e=q*-q_(ell_m). From (9)--(11),
D^T e=X_(ell_m). Thus neighboring values of e differ by at most M_(ell_m).
Two vertices of the edge cycle are at distance at most floor(N/2), so

    osc(e)<=floor(N/2)M_(ell_m).                      (15)

At an index minimizing q*, e_i=-q_(ell_m,i)<=0. Equations (14)--(15)
therefore imply, at every coordinate,

    q_(ell_m,i)>=q*_i-floor(N/2)sqrt(J_m).            (16)

The finite sine sum is sum_(k=1)^N sin(k pi/N)=cot(theta): multiply it
by 2 sin(theta), telescope cosine differences, and use Ntheta=pi/2.
Consequently the explicit amount of comparison flux is

    Q*_m=sum_i q*_i=[N s_N-cot(theta)]/[2 sin(theta)]. (17)

The actual total emitted flux is

    Q_m=sum_i q_(ell_m,i)=(1/4)sum_(k<ell_m) h_k M_k. (18)

Summing (16) yields

    Q_m>=Q*_m-N floor(N/2)sqrt(J_m),                  (19)

and hence the quantitative transport estimate

    J_m >= [(Q*_m-Q_m)_+/(N floor(N/2))]^2.           (20)

This is a proved scalar consequence of actual chronological transport.
It is NOT an explicit lower bound in m until Q_m is usefully bounded.
It is recorded with that limitation, not as a solution of the terminal
estimate or merely as the original nonlinear recurrence rewritten.

Consider trying to close (20) using only the total clock and the favorable
extra assumption M_k<=M_0=2z at every time. This assumption has NOT been
proved for the specified run. Even granting it gives only

    Q_m<=z S_m/2,
    S_m=sum H_(m-1)
       =2^(m-1)-1+[a/(c-2)](c^(m-1)-2^(m-1)).       (21)

The sum follows by summing t_j with multiplicity2^(m-2-j). Since
d/lambda^m->exp(1)/lambda^2, c->lambda, and 2/lambda<1,

    N^2/d->pi^2/6, S_m/d->1/(lambda-2)=lambda,
    Q*_m/N^2->(pi-2)/pi^2,
    z S_m/(2N^2)->3lambda/pi^2.                       (22)

The first limit for d follows from
(1-1/m)(1+1/m)^(m-2)->exp(1); the ceiling error in N is negligible.
The flux limit uses sin(theta)/theta->1 and s_N->1. In particular,

    lim (Q*_m-z S_m/2)/N^2
      =(pi-2-3lambda)/pi^2<0,                        (23)

because pi<4 and lambda>2. Therefore this concrete attempted clock
closure of (20) is eventually exactly the lower bound0. Proving mere
mass nonincrease would not repair it. A useful application needs a
strictly stronger, chronological or spatial estimate on the weighted
mass history, or a different terminal functional.

Support alone has a separate quantitative limitation. Positive edges can
advance by at most one graph edge per physical step, directly from (6).
But ell_m/N is asymptotic to a positive constant times
(2/sqrt(lambda))^m and tends to infinity. Its resulting light cone covers
the entire cycle well before the terminal index. It gives no surviving
unreached terminal edge. This statement does not assert actual activation
of every edge.

## 5. Every actual step avoids every sector's exact annihilation resonance

This section and the next jointly prove the explicit but very small
terminal floor (A). They do not depend on the unproved mass assumption.

For a vertex vector X, let B_X be the ordinary integer graph Laplacian
of the strictly active cycle edges, those with (DX)_i>0. Then

    grad F(X)=B_X X/4, T_t(X)=(I-t B_X/4)X.           (24)

The symmetric matrix B_X has integer entries and spectrum in [0,4].
Indeed its quadratic form is a sum over a subset of cycle-edge squares,
between zero and4||X||^2. Ties simply omit zero-contributing edges.

We show the stronger statement: for any symmetric integer matrix B with
spectrum in [0,4], I-t_j B/4 is nonsingular for EVERY j>=0 with the
specified m>=8 and the same formula t_j. For use on H_m, only j<m is needed.

Write sigma for the field map sqrt(2)->-sqrt(2). Each t_j belongs to
Q(sqrt(2)). If I-t_j B/4 were singular, w=4/t_j would be an eigenvalue
of B. It is a root of the monic integer characteristic polynomial.
If w is rational, the rational-root argument makes w an integer. If w
is irrational in Q(sqrt(2)), sigma(w) must also be a root, and

    w sigma(w)=16/[t_j sigma(t_j)] must be an integer. (25)

Here is the elementary integrality justification in (25). The monic
minimal polynomial of w over Q divides the integer characteristic
polynomial. It has integer coefficients: write that minimal polynomial
and its complementary factor as rational multiples of primitive integer
polynomials. A product of primitive integer polynomials is primitive,
since otherwise reduction modulo a common prime would have zero product
of nonzero polynomials. The monic integer characteristic polynomial is
primitive. Comparing contents and leading coefficients therefore forces
the monic minimal polynomial to have integer coefficients. Its constant
coefficient is w sigma(w). This also justifies the rational-root case.

All the possibilities can now be excluded using short exact inequalities.

* j=0: put r=(m-1)/(m+1). Then
  t_0=1+r(sqrt(2)-1) and sigma(t_0)=1-r lambda<0,
  since r>=7/9 and lambda>2. Hence sigma(w)<0, impossible for an
  eigenvalue of B.

* j=1: t_1=2-1/m and w=4m/(2m-1) is strictly between2 and3.
  It is rational and is not an integer, also impossible.

* Even j>=2: put rho=(1+1/m)/lambda, which lies in (0,1). Then
  sigma(t_j)=1-beta rho^(j-1) is strictly between0 and1.
  Therefore sigma(w)>4, outside the spectrum of B.

* j=3: put s=beta(1+1/m)^2=1+1/m-1/m^2-1/m^3.
  For m>=8, 1<s<9/8. Since lambda^2+(1-sqrt(2))^2=6 and
  lambda^2(1-sqrt(2))^2=1,

      t_3 sigma(t_3)=1+6s+s^2 lies strictly between8 and16.

  Its upper bound follows from 1+6(9/8)+(9/8)^2=577/64<16.
  The number in (25) then lies strictly between1 and2, not an integer.

* Odd j>=5: sigma(t_j)>1 and
  t_j>=1+(7/8)lambda^4>16. For the last inequality,
  lambda^2=3+2sqrt(2)>5, so 1+(7/8)lambda^4>1+175/8>16.
  Thus (25) lies strictly between0 and1, also not an integer.

In all irrational cases t_j is indeed irrational: the nonzero rational
coefficient multiplies a power of 1+sqrt(2) with nonzero sqrt(2) component.
These arguments prove nonsingularity, uniformly over every sector and tie
pattern, without computing its spectrum or following the trajectory.
In particular a nonconstant state on this mean-preserving cycle cannot
be mapped to a constant state by any of the specified steps. The next
section supplies an explicit quantitative version rather than stopping
at qualitative nonannihilation.

## 6. Determinant separation and the actual terminal lower bound

For j>=0 choose the explicit positive integer denominator

    Q_0=m+1, Q_j=m^j for j>=1.                        (26)

Then Q_j t_j belongs to Z[sqrt(2)]. For j>=1 this follows from
t_j=1+(m-1)(m+1)^(j-1)lambda^(j-1)/m^j; the j=0 expression is in
Section5. Also

    |sigma(t_j)|<2                                    (27)

for all j: for j>=1 use sigma(t_j)=1+(-1)^(j-1)beta rho^(j-1),
and for j=0 use 1-lambda<sigma(t_0)<0 and lambda<3.

Fix a sector matrix B_X of size N, and put C_j(X)=I-t_j B_X/4.
The quantity (4Q_j)^N det C_j(X) belongs to Z[sqrt(2)] and is nonzero
by Section5. Its product with its field conjugate is a nonzero integer,
whose absolute value is at least1. Thus

    |det C_j(X)| |det sigma(C_j(X))| >= (4Q_j)^(-2N).

The eigenvalues of B_X/4 lie in [0,1]. By (27), every singular value of
sigma(C_j(X)) is at most3; consequently

Every singular value of C_j(X) is at most1+t_j. Divide its determinant
by an upper bound on the other N-1 singular values. With

    Cbar_j=48 Q_j^2(1+t_j)>1,

equation (28) gives the sector-independent estimate

The constant in (29) is uniform in the actual active set at that step;

# Fixed one-step-child inflation: two full-array attempts and the remaining sign problem

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. No fact submission or
formal verification is authorized in max round57. The fixed-child closure
question and the original unrestricted exact-profile Goal remain OPEN.
This is outcome (c) of TASK.md, not an actual physical-word counterexample.

The mathematical predecessor used is accepted fact04219554e41d9750,
proof Sections10--11: the original full primitive identity and the
primitive binary join. Its identity is used in its original coordinates.
Shared4f623d6a2c835679, b53b38b27498e8a0 and 9ab42650d239f6b0 were read
as awareness of failed approaches; no unverified statement from them is
assumed. The elementary input certificates used below are checked here.
The skew-completion background in sharedff8b941536cb035e is also awareness
only: the required completion is proved in full below, and the new
fixed-child pullback and two nonbasic failure tests are explicit.

There are exactly TWO mechanisms in this pilot:

1. Distribute each input ordered edge over all four ordered pairs between
   its physical two-node blocks, and determine child weights from flow.
   The entire convex distribution family fails on a legal nonbasic input.
   A particularly simple member has all30 multipliers strictly positive
   and exact flow, but its remainder is -1/2 on an explicit formal vector.
2. Preserve the full input PSD remainder by a parity-corrected pullback,
   solve all original real coefficient equalities by an explicit skew
   completion, and retain EVERY homogeneous skew and admissible remainder
   variation. The canonical completion fails a multiplier sign on the
   same nonbasic input. The remaining inequalities are stated exactly;
   no restriction to that canonical completion is declared lossless.

No numerical evaluation, parameter sweep, solver, symbolic program,
benchmark DP, installation, consult, subagent, or formal call is used.

## 1. Original coordinates, counts, and the fixed child

Normalize smoothness to1. For any word w=(w_0,...,w_(n-1)), write
S_w=sum w_i, A_w=1+S_w, and retain all n+1 formal gradients g_i and values
f_i. Put x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)w_t g_t and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_w=2sum_(i<n)w_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)w_i(1-w_i)||g_i||^2
                                      -S_w(S_w+1)||g_n||^2.

Let e be the all-ones column, T_ii=1, T_it=w_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
omega=(-2w_0,...,-2w_(n-1),2S_w)^T, and

 D=diag(w_0(2-w_0),...,w_(n-1)(2-w_(n-1)),-S_w(S_w+2)).

A full certificate consists of Lambda_ii=0, Lambda_ij>=0 for every
ordered i!=j, L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda, L^T e=omega, and

 M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 positive semidefinite.                    (1)

Here sym(B)=(B+B^T)/2; Gram is the matrix of pairwise gradient inner
products, and the matrix pairing in (2) is trace(M^T Gram).

The accepted original-coordinate identity is

 V_w+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>.          (2)

It holds as a polynomial in every formal gradient and value, without
identifying coordinates. The signs Q_ij<=0 hold on an actual trajectory
of a single convex differentiable1-smooth function. Consequently (1)
is a sufficient primitive certificate on all such trajectories.

In this manuscript only, set a=sqrt(2), C=1+a, d=a-1=1/C. The fixed child
is q=(a). Its two-node certificate is

 Lambda^q=[[0,2],[2C,0]], M^q=0.                             (3)

Indeed its flow is (-2a,2a). The diagonal entries of D+sym(LT) are
a(2-a)+2(1-a)=2-a^2=0 and -a(a+2)+2C=0. Twice the off-diagonal is
-2+2C(a-1)=0. Thus every entry of the full matrix is checked.

The arbitrary input h has length r>=1, h_i>=1, capacity A=1+sum h_i,
and its given full certificate (Lambda^h,M^h). Define

 beta_i=1+C(h_i-1)=C h_i-a,
 H=(a,beta_0,a,beta_1,...,a,beta_(r-1),a).                   (4)

Block i has physical node2i (its start) and node2i+1 (its endpoint),
for i=0,...,r. All 2r+2 gradients remain independent formal coordinates.
There are r+1 child steps and r bridges, so the physical length is
Nphys=2r+1 and there are (2r+2)(2r+1) ordered multiplier slots. Since beta_i>=1,
every step is positive. Direct summation, using C-a=1, gives

 1+sum H=1+(r+1)a+C sum h_i-r a=C A.                       (5)

This is a fixed-child statement only. Neither arbitrary-child closure
nor an exponent-based restriction on arbitrary seed capacity follows.

## 2. A nonbasic legal input, with its complete certificate

Take h=(3/2,3/2), A=4, and

 Lambda^h=[[0,1,1/2],[7/2,0,17/2],[1,14,0]].                (6)

Its six ordered entries are positive and its flow is (-3,-3,6).
With T=[[1,0,0],[3/2,1,0],[3/2,3/2,1]] and D=diag(3/4,3/4,-15),

opposite off-diagonal entries are

 (LT)_02+(LT)_20=-1/2+1/2=0,
 (LT)_12+(LT)_21=-17/2+(3/2+7)=0.

Hence the full M^h is zero. A length2 primitive binary tree built from
empty leaves contains a length1 empty-leaf join, whose step is a by the

Its physical inflated word is

## 3. Mechanism1: every cross-block ordered pair is retained

For arbitrary input h choose t_i in[0,1], i=0,...,r, and let the two
weights in block i be pi_i=(t_i,1-t_i). For every i!=j and a0,b0 in{0,1},

 Lambda^mix_(2i+a0,2j+b0)=C Lambda^h_ij pi_(i,a0) pi_(j,b0). (9)

 mu_i=1-C h_i t_i/a for i<r,

Require mu_i>=0. These are exact formulas on the original physical

 Mmix=D_H+sym(Lmix T_H)                                    (11)

to be tested on the entire physical space.

### 3.1 The entire convex block-distribution family fails on (6)

 0<=t_0,t_1<=2a/(3C), 0<=t_2<=1.                           (12)

### 3.2 A fully positive instance with an exact negative remainder

Set all t_i=1/4 in (9). Then

 mu_0=mu_1=(10-3a)/16>0,  mu_2=(14+3a)/8>0.                (18)

Equations(6),(9),(18) specify every one of the30 ordered output entries,

The total outgoing coefficient at node0 is

so (Mmix)_00=2d+(1-a)(13/8)=3d/8.

 (Lmix^T v)_0

## 4. Mechanism2: preserve the input PSD remainder, solve real equalities

This mechanism starts from an arbitrary full input certificate, with
no zero-remainder, symmetry, support, rank, or strict-positivity assumption.
Its canonical real output will fail a sign below. The exact remaining
freedoms are then retained, rather than silently fixed to that output.

### 4.1 Two necessary moments, derived in the original coordinates

For any word w define its unit-curvature column by

 v^w_0=1, v^w_i=product_(t<i)(1-w_t), so T_w v^w=e.

For any array with exact flow, (2) on the formal constant-gradient data
g_i=1, x_i=-sum_(t<i)w_t, f_i=x_i gives e^T M e=0. Indeed every Q is0,
and 2sum w_i(S_w-sum_(t<i)w_t)=S_w^2+sum w_i^2 cancels the remaining
terms in V_w. If M is PSD, this equality forces M e=0.

On the actual unit quadratic from x_0=1 all Q are0 and the gradient
column is v^w. The telescope

 sum_(i<n)w_i(2-w_i)(v^w_i)^2=1-(v^w_n)^2

gives

                =1-A_w^2(v^w_n)^2=:chi_w.                 (20)

These identities are necessary even when coefficients are on the
boundary or M is nonzero and singular. They do not identify formal
gradients or impose restrictions on an actual function.

### 4.2 The fixed-child pullback preserves both moments exactly

Let v^h be the input column and v=v^H the full physical column. The
product of the two successive factors through block i and its bridge is

 (1-a)(1-beta_i)=(-d)C(1-h_i)=-(1-h_i).

 v_(2i)=(-1)^i v^h_i,
 v_(2i+1)=-d(-1)^i v^h_i.                                (21)

Together with (5), this proves chi_H=chi_h. Define a linear map Rpull
from all physical gradient coordinates to r+1 coordinates by

 (Rpull z)_i=z_(2i)                         if i is even,
 (Rpull z)_i=-d z_(2i)+a z_(2i+1)            if i is odd.   (22)

Here z is any formal scalar coordinate column; the same map acts
componentwise on vector gradients. Since a-d=1 and dC=1,

 Rpull e_H=e_h,  Rpull v=v^h.

Consequently the explicit full physical matrix

 N0=Rpull^T M^h Rpull                                      (23)

is PSD, satisfies N0 e_H=0 and v^T N0 v=chi_H, and is defined for every
allowed input certificate. Equations(22)--(23) are a congruence of
matrices on the full physical space, not a smooth virtual-oracle claim.
The map contains a negative coefficient on odd blocks; no entrywise
positivity is claimed for the multiplier array reconstructed from it.

### 4.3 Explicit real skew completion for all compatible remainders

In this subsection use the physical word H, let m=2r+2, and write
T=T_H,D=D_H,omega=omega_H,e=e_H,v=v^H. The vectors e and v are independent:
their first two coordinates are respectively (1,1) and (1,-d).

Take any symmetric matrix N with

# Full seven-step tangent discovery: exact dual candidate

**Status: complete joint UNVERIFIED research report.** All five authorized
jobs are consumed and the ledger is closed. There was no fact submission,
formal verification, installation, benchmark replay or subagent. The original
unrestricted gradient-descent exact-profile problem remains OPEN.

The useful output is an explicit dual over Q(sqrt(2)) for the COMPLETE
first-order cone at the frozen balanced seven-step word. The recorded exact
reconstruction satisfies all63 stationarity equations, all36 sign-price
inequalities, and an exact positive-definite LDL decomposition. It gives
the following candidate conclusion:

> Every full linearized certificate (p,Y,W) satisfies sum_i p_i <= 0.
> This conclusion covers all seven physical derivatives, all56 original
> coefficient derivatives, all36 original active signs and full R8 PSD.

This is a proof candidate with explicit algebraic evidence, not an accepted
fact. No full-neighborhood, global seven-step or original-target theorem is
claimed. In particular the discovery supplies no improving finite seed.

## 1. Inputs, exact model and scope

The active assignment is TASK.md, ONE round after completed47, completed
ceiling48/attempted49, under guidance06cd713a43322da8. The shared preceding
draft b937bb05ba1645b1 has SHA256
76a363742a60cdab32d14b828dcf7ecd58d784dfcededfd1b9510b131d67565b.
It identifies this exact cone but does not solve it. Its base uniqueness,
contact and integration claims are not imported as accepted facts here.

Accepted04219554e41d9750, Sections10--11, supplies the original full
primitive identity and composition. Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 fixes the
interpolation orientation. Accepted5e1848ee0b153f5f supplies conditional
amplification of an actual above-threshold seed only. None asserts such
a seed exists. All additional identities required below are derived jointly.

Let q=sqrt(2), l=1+q, u=q-1, and

    hbar=(q,2,q,1+l,q,2,q), Abar=l^3.

Index the eight independent formal gradient coordinates by0,...,7. Let
e be their all-ones column and let e_i be the standard coordinate columns.
For any zero-diagonal8-by8 array X, put L(X)=diag(Xe)-X. Define T0 to have
unit diagonal, entry hbar_j at i,j when j<i, and zero entries above its
diagonal. The base array has these twenty positive entries, with every
unlisted entry zero:

    01:2                  10:2l                 13:2l
    21:2lq                23:2l^2+2lq           31:2l
    32:2l^3               37:2l^2               43:2lq
    45:2l^2               47:2lq                53:4l
    54:2l^3               57:2l^3+4l            63:2lq
    65:2l^3q              67:2l^4+2l^3q+2lq
    73:2l                 75:2l^3               76:2l^5.

Call this array Lambdabar and write Lbar=L(Lambdabar). Let Z0 be the
set of the other36 ordered distinct pairs. The complete variable array
Y has Y_ii=0 and all56 other entries independently real before constraints.
For p in R7 set S=sum p_i and define

    Tp_ij=p_j for j<i, zero otherwise;
    op=(-2p_0,...,-2p_6,2S);
    D1=diag(2(1-hbar_i)p_i for i<7,-2Abar S);
    W=D1+sym(Lbar Tp+L(Y)T0), sym(K)=(K+K^T)/2;
    f=L(Y)^T e-op, n=We.

The full cone consists of f=0, Y_ij>=0 for ij in Z0 and W>=0 on R8.
The other twenty Y entries have no imposed sign. No support, rank,
reflection, equality of formal gradients or fixed shape of W is assumed.

## 2. Exact common null and lossless PSD representation

For an arbitrary word h, s=sum h_i, and full flow L^Te=(-2h,2s), put
M=D+sym(LT), D=diag(h_i(2-h_i),-s(s+2)), with T the original prefix
matrix. Since the i-th entry of Te is1+sum_(j<i)h_j,

    omega^T Te=s^2+sum h_i^2,
    e^T D e=-s^2-sum h_i^2,

so e^TMe=0. Along hbar+t p and Lambdabar+tY, the flow equation is
exact whenever f=0, and differentiation gives e^TWe=0. A symmetric PSD
matrix with zero quadratic form at e annihilates e: its quadratic form
at e+t z cannot be nonnegative for all real t unless z^TWe=0 for each z.
Thus n=0 is a necessary full-cone equation.

Let V=[I7;-1...-1], G=V^TV=I7+11^T and B=V^TWV. Its columns span
e-perp. When n=0, every vector is a sum of a multiple of e and a vector
Vz, so W>=0 on R8 if and only if B>=0 on R7. Moreover

    W>=m(I8-ee^T/8)  iff  B>=mG.

Consequently adding all8 n=0 equations and imposing this congruent PSD
condition loses no original solution. The common-null direction never
receives an epsilon perturbation. Raw readbacks contain the original
full W, every original flow equation, and the full null residual.

## 3. Both calibrations established before job1

For the singleton physical step x, choose multipliers2 and2(1+x) on the
two directed pairs. Substitution into the original two-gradient identity
gives the full remainder

    (2-x^2)(e_0-e_1)(e_0-e_1)^T.

It is nonnegative when0<=x<=q. Set x=q-t,0<=t<q. Join identical
singleton children using bridge1+u(1+x), then identical three-step
children using bridge2+x. Their respective capacities are1+x,l(1+x),
and l^2(1+x). Each balanced join has right multiplier factor l^2 and
additional interpolation factor l^2-1=2l. The accepted full join identity
therefore proves feasibility without a computation. The complete array
and its derivative are specified in frozen_model.md and in the exact
calibration artifact.

The derivative is p=(-1,-u,-1,-1,-1,-u,-1), with S=-l^2. If
d_ij=e_i-e_j, its exact remainder derivative is

    W=2q(d01 d01^T+l^2 d23 d23^T+l^2 d45 d45^T+l^4 d67 d67^T).

Every active zero-entry derivative is zero. This is a NONZERO positive

## 5. The exact dual and the candidate proof

Job5 rounded free coordinates once to multiples of2^-20 and solved exact
affine equations in the field Q(q), q^2=2. All p-box prices were set to
zero as a reconstruction ansatz. This was not a restriction of either SDP.
No optimization or parameter grid was used in reconstruction.

The appendix specifies two eight-coordinate vectors a,b (the first and
last halves of `equality_prices`), a symmetric7-by7 matrix Z through its
28 svec entries, and36 coefficients sigma_ij. All their displayed numbers
are exact rational pairs (r,s), meaning r+s q. Off-diagonal svec entries
are q Z_ij, and diagonal entries are Z_ii.

The algebraic identity certified by the63 zero stationarity residuals is

    -S = trace(Z B)+sum_(ij in Z0) sigma_ij Y_ij
         -a^T f-b^T n.                                      (D)

This is an identity for EVERY p and EVERY zero-diagonal real Y, before
any cone constraint. There is no p-normalization term because all14 box
prices are exactly zero.

Here is an explicit way to check every coefficient of(D) without a
solver. Set H=VZV^T and K=H-sym(b e^T). Write t_i for the transpose of
the i-th row of T0 and r_ij=t_i-t_j. A single unit Y_ij contributes
e_i-e_j to f and sym(e_i r_ij^T) to W. Thus the56 required identities are

    a_i-a_j-(K r_ij)_i = 0              on the20 base-positive pairs,
    a_i-a_j-(K r_ij)_i = sigma_ij       on the36 other pairs. (Y)

For each i<7 let C_i have entry1 in column i strictly below its diagonal,
and zero elsewhere. The unit p_i contribution to W is

    N_i=2(1-hbar_i)e_i e_i^T-2Abar e_7e_7^T+sym(Lbar C_i).

Its contribution to f is2e_i-2e_7. The seven remaining identities are

    2(a_i-a_7)-trace(K N_i)=1, i=0,...,6.                  (P)

The appendixed numbers and q^2=2 specify all entries in(Y) and(P).
The reconstruction artifact records each of their63 residuals as the
exact pair(0,0), using the equivalent unsimplified original coefficient
map. It retains the exact source and deterministic arithmetic procedure.

All36 sigma values are nonnegative in the real embedding q>0, and none
is zero. The following elementary rule makes their comparisons exact:
if r,s have the same sign, use that sign; if they have opposite signs,
the sign of r+s q is sign(r) times sign(r^2-2s^2). The cases r=0 or
s=0 are immediate. The nonzero opposite-sign case cannot yield zero,
because q is irrational. This is the precise rule used by the frozen
exact arithmetic, with rational operations only.

For Z, the artifact supplies Z=L diag(d_0,...,d_6)L^T with unit lower
triangular L and all seven pivots d_i strictly positive under that same
sign rule. The appendix includes L and all seven exact pairs. The LDL
recurrence is

    d_k=Z_kk-sum_(j<k)L_kj^2 d_j,
    L_ik=(Z_ik-sum_(j<k)L_ij L_kj d_j)/d_k, i>k.

These formulas prove that the supplied decomposition entails Z>0, with
no floating eigenvalue inference. All pivots were tested exactly before
division, and a zero pivot with nonzero remaining column would have been
rejected. The recorded result has no zero pivot.

For a full feasible tangent, f=n=0, every Y_ij in Z0 is nonnegative and
B>=0. If Z=L diag(d)L^T, then
trace(ZB)=sum_k d_k (L e_k)^T B(L e_k)>=0. Applying(D) gives -S>=0.
This proves the candidate first-order capacity bound from the explicit
algebraic checks. A zero tangent attains S=0, so the normalized nonstrict
problem has exact optimum0 at draft level. The strict model likewise has
optimum0: S>=m and S<=0 imply m<=0, and the zero point with m=0 is feasible.

The same identity also gives a useful equality condition: if S=0, each
active Y entry is zero, and B=0 because Z is positive definite. To see
the latter without a spectral theorem, each nonnegative summand
(L e_k)^T B(L e_k) must vanish; PSD then makes B annihilate the basis
formed by the columns of L. Consequently W=0 as well. This does not
by itself settle how a finite higher-order perturbation can behave.
