    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    t_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,t_j,H_j),
    d=t_(m-1)=1+beta c^(m-2),
    N=ceil(pi sqrt(d/6)), theta=pi/(2N), mu=sin(theta)^2,
    z=cos(theta), v_i=cos((2i+1)theta), 0<=i<N,
    (D x)_i=x_i-x_(i+1 modulo N), F(x)=||(D x)_+||^2/8.

The declared smoothness is L=1, the original start is v, and the original
word is H_m, always with the SAME enclosing m. No child is independently
retuned. All vector norms below are Euclidean. Positive parts are taken
coordinatewise. Let X_0=-v, and apply the actual physical suffix H_(m-1)
to this normalized suffix start. It is the positive-amplitude factor of
the original inherited state; the short justification is in Section2.

Relabel the closing edge N-1 as edge0, original edge i as edge i+1 modulo N.
Let y_k be D X_k in this relabeling and r_k=(y_k)_+. Put

    L_e=DD^T, P_h=I-(h/4)L_e,
    ell=2^(m-1)-1, h=(h_0,...,h_(ell-1))=H_(m-1),
    K_0=e_0, K_(k+1)=P_(h_k) K_k, R_k=2z K_k.        (1)

Here e_i is the edge-coordinate unit vector at relabeled index i, and I
is the identity. R_k is ONLY a proposed comparison profile. It is not the
actual trajectory of F. The proposed all-query spatial invariant was

    0 <= r_k <= R_k coordinatewise, 0<=k<=ell.         (2)

It starts at equality r_0=R_0=2z e_0. This is an amplitude and shape
assertion, stronger than a mass cap or knowledge of the active interval.
It retains every original physical step in its comparison kernel.

To make its quantitative purpose explicit, if (2) held at the terminal
query, it would imply

    J_m=N||r_ell||^2 <= 4z^2 N||K_ell||^2.            (3)

The right side is a linear spatial-kernel quantity. For example, a uniform
bound N||K_ell||^2<=C would give J_m<=4z^2 C. Finite cyclic Fourier
orthogonality gives the exact identity

    N||K_ell||^2
      =sum_(q=0)^(N-1) product_(j=0)^(m-2)
           (1-t_j sin^2(pi q/N))^(2^(m-1-j)).         (4)

Indeed the q-th cyclic Fourier vector is an eigenvector of L_e with
eigenvalue4sin^2(pi q/N); expand e_0 in these N orthogonal vectors and
square the eigenvalue product. The multiplicity of t_j in H_(m-1) is
2^(m-2-j). Formula (4) retains finite-cycle aliasing exactly; it is not an
infinite-lattice replacement or an evaluated numerical sum.

Write A_m=product_(j=0)^(m-2)(1-mu t_j)^(2^(m-2-j)) and
b_m=A_m(mu d-1)>0. The actual full-word payoff and original benchmark obey

    V_m=2F(x_(2^m-1))/dist(v,argmin F)^2=b_m^2 J_m/(2N^2),
    B_(2^m-1)V_m=b_m^2 B_(2^m-1) J_m/(2N^2).         (5)

Here B is the ORIGINAL all-split benchmark, defined in accepted
fact04219554e41d9750 by C_0=B_0=1,
Omega(s,t)=(s+t+sqrt((s+t)^2+4st))/2,
G(s,t)=2s+t/2+sqrt(t^2+8st)/2,
C_n=max_(0<=i<n)Omega(C_i,C_(n-i-1)),
B_n=max_(0<=i<n)G(C_i,B_(n-i-1)), and U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.
All splits remain present. Consequently (2) at the terminal query and
the bound C would be strong enough for an eventual deficit whenever, for
some fixed delta>0 and all sufficiently large m,

    (2z^2 b_m^2 B_(2^m-1)/N^2) C <= 1-delta.         (6)

Conditions (2), the bound C, and (6) are the intended proof obligations,
not conclusions. The result below refutes (2) as an all-query invariant.

## 2. Minimal inherited-state and parameter checks

These checks fix the connection to the original run; static legality and
the old first-child analysis are not being offered as new progress.
Differentiation gives grad F(x)=D^T(Dx)_+/4, so the actual edge update is

    y' = y-(h/4)L_e y_+,
    y'_i = y_i-(h/2)(y_i)_+
                   +(h/4)((y_(i-1))_++(y_(i+1))_+).  (7)

The gradient is 1-Lipschitz since ||D||<=2 and the positive-part map is
1-Lipschitz. F vanishes exactly at constant vectors, and the mean is
preserved. Pairing the coordinates of v gives mean zero; summing
cos^2((2i+1)theta) using the finite geometric series gives ||v||^2=N/2.
Thus the true squared initial radius is N/2, without changing the declared L.

For m>=10, the inequalities lambda>12/5 and (12/5)^3>13 imply

    d > (7/8)(12/5)^8 > (7/8)13^2(144/25) > 768.

Hence theta^2<=3/(2d)<1/512 and

    0<mu<1/512.                                      (8)

For completeness let b=pi sqrt(d/6). Since pi>sqrt(6) and sqrt(d)>12,
b<=N<b+1<(13/12)b. Integration of cos(s)>=1-s^2/2 gives
sin(theta)/theta>=1-theta^2/6>99/100. Therefore

    5/4 < (3/2)(12/13)^2(99/100)^2 < mu d < 3/2.

Also t_(m-2)/d=1/c+(1-1/c)/d<5/12+1/768, so
mu t_j<2/3 for every j<=m-2. Substitution of the cosine addition formulas
in the active path at v gives grad F(v)=mu v. All factors1-mu t_j in
the original first child are positive. Successive physical updates thus
give A_m v, followed at the largest step d by -b_m v. Positive homogeneity
then shows that the original suffix state after k updates is b_m X_k.
This proves the inherited-state assertion and (5); it does not reset a child.

For the first four actual suffix steps define

    u=t_0/4, w=t_1/4, eta=t_2/4,
    p=1-2u, q=1-2w=1/(2m).

Their order is u,w,u,eta in units of h/4. The following bounds hold:

    1/3<u<3/8,       2/7<p<1/3,
    19/40<=w<1/2,    0<q<=1/20,
    3/4<eta<7/8,     0<1-beta^2<1/5.                 (9)

To check the less immediate lower bound on u, write
t_0=1+((m-1)/(m+1))(sqrt(2)-1). Since (m-1)/(m+1)>=9/11
and sqrt(2)>38/27, t_0>4/3. The upper bound t_0<sqrt(2) and
sqrt(2)<10/7 give p>2/7. The other bounds follow from
t_1=2-1/m and t_2=1+lambda(1-1/m^2), with 3<t_2<7/2.

There is also an exact relation essential below:

    eta p-(2eta-1)u=(1-beta^2)/4.                    (10)

Indeed (4eta-1)u-eta
=beta c(1+beta/c)/4-(1+beta c)/4=(beta^2-1)/4.
This retains the finite enclosing-m deformation rather than replacing it
by its limiting Silver parameters.

## 3. The actual inherited profile through the first H_2

At relabeled edge i, the initial profile is

    y_(0,0)=2z,
    y_(0,i)=-nu_i, 1<=i<N,
    nu_i=2sin(theta)sin(2i theta)=nu_(N-i)>0.          (11)

The exact first boundary depths needed below are

    nu_1=4mu z,
    nu_2=8mu z(1-2mu),
    nu_3=mu z(12-64mu+64mu^2),
    nu_4=16mu z(1-2mu)(1-8mu+8mu^2).                 (12)

These follow from the sine double-angle formulas. In particular
nu_2<=8mu z, nu_3<=12mu z, nu_4<=16mu z and
nu_3>(95/8)mu z by (8).

Let Delta_k=R_k-r_k. For k=1,2,3 all old positive coordinates remain
strictly positive: each of these steps has h<2, and (7) retains at least
(1-h/2) times each old positive value. Only the immediately adjacent
negative edges can activate. Their actual candidate values are

    r_(1,1)=2uz-nu_1 > z(2/3-4mu)>0,
    r_(2,2)=2zuw-(w nu_1+nu_2)
                              > z(19/60-10mu)>0,
    r_(3,3)=2zu^2w-u(w nu_1+nu_2)-nu_3
                              > z(19/180-16mu)>0.   (13)

The reflected edge indices have equal values. Every other
outside edge remains at its strictly negative initial value. Since N>27,
none of these indices overlaps its reflected counterpart. Induction using
(13) proves that the strict active set is exactly {-k,...,k} for k=0,1,2,3.

Write k_i=K_(3,i)=k_(-i). Multiplying the three three-point kernels gives

    k_0=q(p^2+2u^2)+4puw,
    k_1=2puq+w(p^2+3u^2),
    k_2=u^2q+2puw,
    k_3=u^2w,                 k_i=0 for |i|>3.        (14)

For example, these are the coefficients of
(p+u(s+s^(-1)))^2(q+w(s+s^(-1))) for a formal variable s.
The full symmetric kernel has positive coefficients on its support and
total mass one. At the first birth Delta_1 has value
nu_1 at edges+1,-1. At the second birth,

    Delta_(2,0)=2w nu_1, Delta_(2,1)=q nu_1,
    Delta_(2,2)=w nu_1+nu_2.

Propagate these deviations through the next u-step. Subtracting the new
boundary depth nu_3 from the actual profile adds nu_3 to its deviation
from the free profile. The exact deviations after the original entire H_2 are

    Delta_(3,0)=(2pw+2uq)nu_1,
    Delta_(3,1)=(pq+3uw)nu_1+u nu_2,
    Delta_(3,2)=(pw+uq)nu_1+p nu_2,
    Delta_(3,3)=u(w nu_1+nu_2)+nu_3.                  (15)

They are reflection invariant and zero off {-3,...,3}. All entries of
Delta_k for k<=3 are nonnegative, proving (2) through query3. No state is
reset to an impulse at the end of this H_2: (15) is retained at its bridge.

We will also use simple bounds following term by term from (9), (12),
and (14)--(15):

    19/105 < k_0 < 9/32,
    19/120 < k_1 < 9/32,
    19/210 < k_2 < 3/20,
    19/360 < k_3,

    0<=Delta_(3,0)<(3/2)mu z,
    0<=Delta_(3,1)<6mu z,
    0<=Delta_(3,2)<(7/2)mu z,
    0<=Delta_(3,3)<16mu z.                            (16)

For clarity the upper coefficient bounds before rounding are
k_0<1553/5760, k_1<1607/5760 and k_2<169/1280.
The corresponding deviation bounds before rounding are
(89/60)mu z, (319/60)mu z, (409/120)mu z and (63/4)mu z.
They result respectively from p<1/3, u<3/8, w<1/2, q<=1/20
and the displayed bounds for nu_i. The lower coefficient bounds use
p>2/7, u>1/3 and w>=19/40.

## 4. Exact envelope failure at the actual t_2 bridge

Consider relabeled edge3. At the incoming query3 it is strictly positive,
edge2 is strictly positive, and edge4 is strictly negative with positive
part zero. Also K_(3,4)=0. Thus (7), with the actual inherited profile,
gives

    y_(4,3)=2z K_(4,3)+E_m,
    E_m=(2eta-1)Delta_(3,3)-eta Delta_(3,2).           (17)

Substitute (15), then use (10). The exact excess simplifies to

    E_m=(2eta-1)nu_3
          -((1-beta^2)/4)(w nu_1+nu_2)-eta u q nu_1,

    E_m/(mu z)
      =(2eta-1)(12-64mu+64mu^2)
          -(1-beta^2)(w+2-4mu)-4eta u q.              (18)

This formula uses the finite-m parameters, the actual starting sine
profile, and the actual chronological t_0,t_1,t_0,t_2 transition.
Its lower bound is completely explicit. By (8)--(9),

    E_m/(mu z)
      > (1/2)(95/8)-(1/5)(5/2)
                       -4(7/8)(3/8)(1/20)
      =1719/320 > 5.                                 (19)

Both subtracted terms in (18) are positive. Since 2eta-1<3/4 and
nu_3/(mu z)<=12, it also follows that E_m/(mu z)<9.

The free comparison value at this coordinate is itself positive. Set
epsilon=(1-beta^2)/4>0. By (10) and (14),

    K_(4,3)=(1-2eta)u^2w+eta(u^2q+2puw)
            =uw(eta p+epsilon)+eta u^2q >0.           (20)

Therefore y_(4,3)>0, so its positive part is y_(4,3) and (17)--(19)
prove the ACTUAL strict violation

    r_(4,3)-R_(4,3)=E_m>5mu z.                       (21)

Reflection gives the same violation at edge-3. In the original edge
indices these are edges2 and N-4. At the corresponding original full-run
query, each excess is b_m E_m>5b_m mu z; the true radius, function and
declared smoothness have all remained unchanged.

Finally, as m tends to infinity, mu tends to zero, beta tends to1,
q tends to0, and eta tends to(2+sqrt(2))/4. Formula (18) then gives
E_m/(mu z)->6sqrt(2), proving all of (A). The unnormalized excess is of
order N^(-2). This does not itself exclude a terminal O(N^(-1)) profile
or any comparison with extra slack.

## 5. Sign nesting and positive comparison kernels survive this failure

We now check all remaining coordinates at query4, rather than supposing
that the failure in (21) was accompanied by a hidden sign reversal.
Put a_eta=2-1/eta<6/7. For i=0,1,2 the old positive values update by

    y_(4,0)=eta(2r_(3,1)-a_eta r_(3,0)),
    y_(4,1)=eta(r_(3,0)+r_(3,2)-a_eta r_(3,1)),
    y_(4,2)=eta(r_(3,1)+r_(3,3)-a_eta r_(3,2)).

Using r_(3,i)=2z k_i-Delta_(3,i) and (16) gives

    y_(4,0)>eta z(127/840-12mu)>0,
    y_(4,1)>eta z(17/280-5mu)>0,
    y_(4,2)>eta z(52/315-22mu)>0.                     (22)

For example the constants in the first two lines are respectively
4(19/120)-(6/7)2(9/32)=127/840 and
2(19/105+19/210-(6/7)(9/32))=17/280.
For the third they are
2(19/120+19/360-(6/7)(3/20))=52/315.
The upper deviation losses are respectively12mu z,5mu z,22mu z.
Each bracket is positive because mu<1/512.

Edge3 was already checked in (20)--(21). At the newly reached edge4,

    y_(4,4)=eta r_(3,3)-nu_4
             >z(19/240-28mu)>0,                     (23)

using (13), eta>3/4 and nu_4<=16mu z. All edges outside {-4,...,4}
still have no positive neighbor at the incoming time3 and remain
strictly negative. Reflection treats the negative indices. Thus the
actual strict active sets are nested through this transition and are
exactly {-k,...,k}, k=0,...,4.

The comparison kernel K_4 is nonnegative as well. For its coordinates
0,1,2 repeat the first parts of (22) with all deviations set to zero;
the displayed positive constant remains. Equation (20) treats3, and
K_(4,4)=eta u^2w>0. It vanishes outside {-4,...,4} and has total mass1
because each P_h preserves sums. Kernels K_0,K_1,K_2,K_3 are nonnegative
by their short-step definitions. Thus kernel positivity through the
transition does not imply comparison (2).

There are no boundary ties in these four steps: every named active
coordinate and every unreached negative coordinate has a strict sign.
The exact update (7) nevertheless includes ties correctly at arbitrary
later times by assigning positive part zero. No tie is deleted or given
an artificial Hessian continuation.

There is also no hidden creation of positive mass during this prefix.
The only absorption at update k, for k=1,2,3,4, is the depth nu_k at
each newly activated edge+k,-k. Hence

    sum_i r_(k,i)=2z-2sum_(j=1)^k nu_j, 0<=k<=4.      (24)

This is an actual-prefix identity, not a proposed global mass principle.
It underscores why a mass cap does not repair the failed pointwise shape
comparison.

## 6. Why the absorption comparison fails, and the exact surviving gap

For an arbitrary actual state y write r=y_+, n=(-y)_+, and U=P_h r.
If y_i<=0, then U_i=(h/4)(r_(i-1)+r_(i+1))>=0. Define

    a_i=min(n_i,U_i) if y_i<=0, and a_i=0 otherwise;
    b_i=(-U_i)_+ if y_i>0, and b_i=0 otherwise.

Directly taking the positive part of y'=U-n proves

    r_next=P_h r-a+b,      a>=0, b>=0.                (25)

At an old tie n_i=0, so a_i=0 and the same formula applies. A zero step
also satisfies it. The vector b records the repair needed when an old
positive coordinate becomes strictly negative; strict sign nesting
implies b=0. The converse may have ties and is not asserted.

For the four-step actual prefix above b=0 throughout. At its third
update the new absorption includes nu_3(e_3+e_(-3)). Propagating this
deviation through P_(t_2) multiplies its entry at3 by1-2eta<0.
Equations (17)--(19) show that the earlier absorption does not offset
this sign change. That is the precise reason the larger free profile
ceases to majorize the smaller actual incoming profile.

For a GENERAL terminal index ell, define P_(ell,k+1) as the ordered
product P_(h_(ell-1))...P_(h_(k+1)), with the empty product I. Iterating
(25), with the actual a_k,b_k, gives

    r_ell=R_ell-sum_(k=0)^(ell-1)P_(ell,k+1)a_k
                   +sum_(k=0)^(ell-1)P_(ell,k+1)b_k.  (26)

All these linear factors are on the same finite cycle; the nonlinear
sources still depend on the actual chronological states. Equation (26)
is a diagnosis of the missing source estimate, not a terminal result.

If every remaining-suffix product P_(ell,k+1) were entrywise nonnegative
and b_k=0 for all physical queries, then (26) would yield terminal-only
domination r_ell<=R_ell. This conditional implication is elementary and
is NOT refuted by (21): a later complete block might change the sign of
an earlier absorption contribution again. Nonnegativity of the full
prefix kernel K_k alone is insufficient, as (20)--(21) demonstrate.

The all-query profile induction selected here is refuted. The weaker
terminal-only route is still blocked at three explicit obligations:
control of b on the entire actual run, nonnegativity (or a paid bound
for negative entries) of every relevant remaining-suffix kernel, and a
quantitative bound for N||K_ell||^2 meeting (6). No such new bound is
claimed. Guidance1fc56054c08bd0ac assigns a distinct signed-kernel/source
analysis to another worker; this round does not start that second mechanism.

## 7. Literature check and status

The search-math-results workflow used Matlas first for positivity of
products of explicit heat steps. Its hits concerned different implicit,
cross-diffusion or entropy schemes. Web fallback located Zheng Tan,
Tariq D. Aslam and Andrea L. Bertozzi, *Explicit monotone stable
super-time-stepping methods for finite time singularities*,
arXiv:2507.17062v2 (2025),
https://arxiv.org/html/2507.17062v2 . The exact HTML was downloaded and
text extracted under this artifact directory. Section5's definitions,
Lemma2's coefficient proof, Theorem7 and the alternating-sum proof in
AppendixD were read. They concern particular Legendre/Gegenbauer
stability polynomials for a constant-coefficient heat equation. They
give neither the specified deformed H_j kernels nor control of the
positive-part sources in (25). No external theorem is imported here.

The mathematical new output is the explicit actual transition
(17)--(23), including the strict margin5mu z, its exact formula and
limiting coefficient. It refutes one specified spatial invariant,
while proving actual sign nesting only for this four-update prefix.
It is stronger in scope than a generic-state counterexample but much
weaker than a family obstruction. It gives no all-depth assertion about
actual nesting or J_m, no statement over every original schedule, and
no new verified fact.

All necessary components for this counterexample have been derived
jointly above. Earlier shared findings are awareness and object
specifications, never proof predecessors. Accepted04219554e41d9750 is
used only to identify the unchanged benchmark in (5)--(6).

This ends the single allocated analytical round with its exact blocker.
There is no self-renewal and no numerical or formal credit left in this
assignment. Actual process completion is recorded by the outer loop
after return; this manuscript is not process-exit evidence.

Let S be the cyclic shift on edge vectors, (S f)_i=f_(i-1). Direct multiplication

## 7. Exact actual sources: signs, support, amplitudes and Duhamel

At step k put alpha=h_k/4 and w_i=alpha(r_(k,i-1)+r_(k,i+1)). The original
positive-part edge update, obtained by applying D to (2), is

    y_(k+1,i)=y_(k,i)-2alpha*r_(k,i)+w_i.

Define the absorption vector abs_k and the repair vector rep_k by

 abs_(k,i)=1_(y_(k,i)<=0)*min(n_(k,i),w_i),
 rep_(k,i)=1_(y_(k,i)>0)*[(2alpha-1)r_(k,i)-w_i]_+,
 s_k=rep_k-abs_k.

Both vectors are nonnegative and their supports are disjoint. Absorption
occurs only on old strictly negative edges adjacent to an old positive edge;
at an old zero its amplitude is zero. Its amplitude is at most both the
old negative depth n_(k,i) and the incoming amount w_i. Repair occurs only
on old positive edges that become strictly negative. It vanishes if h_k<=2,
and satisfies rep_(k,i)<=max(h_k/2-1,0)r_(k,i). Thus no large-step increase
or sign change has been omitted. Exact ties give zero on the appropriate
boundary and require no choice of active-set convention.

Checking the two old sign cases gives the identities

    r_(k+1)=P_(h_k)r_k+s_k,
    n_(k+1)=n_k+s_k.

On an old nonpositive coordinate P r=w>=0 and r'=(w-n)_+=w-min(w,n).
On an old positive coordinate n=0 and taking the positive part adds exactly
(-P r)_+. This proves both identities, including ties.

There is useful local dissipativity: writing v_lin=P_(h_k)r_k, we have v_lin=-rep_k
on the repair support and v_lin>=abs_k on the absorption support. Therefore

 ||r_(k+1)||_2^2-||v_lin||_2^2
   =-||rep_k||_2^2-2<v_lin,abs_k>+||abs_k||_2^2
   <=-||rep_k||_2^2-||abs_k||_2^2.

This does not assert ||v_lin||<=||r_k|| at large steps. Also sum y_k=0 at all
times, so if M_k=sum_i r_(k,i), then
M_(k+1)-M_k=sum rep_k-sum abs_k. The repair term is not set to zero.

Iterating the actual affine-in-r identity, retaining each source where its

Put ||(p,Y)||_* = sqrt(||p||_2^2+||Y||_F^2). Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    ||L(Y)||_F <=(sqrt(7)+1)||Y||_F,

Consequently

    ||R2(p,Y)||_F <=8||p||_2^2+(7+sqrt(7))||p||_2||Y||_F
                   <=13||(p,Y)||_*^2.                     (32)

    K58={(p,Y) in C58: ||(p,Y)||_*=1}.

It is closed because flow and W are linear and the sign and PSD cones are

        return Q(self.a * other.a + 2 * self.b * other.b,
                 self.a * other.b + self.b * other.a)

    __rmul__ = __mul__

    def __truediv__(self, other):
        other = Q.of(other)
        den = other.a * other.a - 2 * other.b * other.b
        if den == 0:
            raise ZeroDivisionError('exact zero field divisor')
        return Q((self.a * other.a - 2 * self.b * other.b) / den,
                 (self.b * other.a - self.a * other.b) / den)

    def __pow__(self, exponent):
        result = Q(1)
        for _ in range(exponent):
            result = result * self
        return result

    def __bool__(self):
        return bool(self.a or self.b)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        other = Q.of(other)
        return self.a == other.a and self.b == other.b

    def encoded(self):
        return [str(self.a), str(self.b)]

    def sign(self):
        a, b = self.a, self.b
        if a == 0:
            return (b > 0) - (b < 0)
        if b == 0:
            return (a > 0) - (a < 0)
        if (a > 0) == (b > 0):
            return 1 if a > 0 else -1
        difference = a * a - 2 * b * b
        return ((a > 0) - (a < 0)) * ((difference > 0) - (difference < 0))


def encode(x):
    if isinstance(x, Q):

    if isinstance(x, list):
        return [encode(v) for v in x]

        return {k: encode(v) for k, v in x.items()}

def matrix(rows, cols):
    return [[Q() for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]

    C = matrix(len(A), len(B[0]))

            if value:

                    if other:

    return C

    A = [[-x for x in row] for row in X]
    for i in range(len(X)):

    return A

The bound is intentionally coarse and purely analytic. In particular the

## 8. Exact nonlinear remainder and strict local capacity loss

For arbitrary finite displacements p=h-hbar, Y=Lambda-Lambdabar, the full
polynomial expansion is EXACT:

    M(h,Lambda)=W(p,Y)+R2(p,Y),
    R2(p,Y)=diag(-p0^2,...,-p6^2,-S^2)+sym(L(Y)Tp).          (31)

Flow is exactly f(p,Y)=0. Every original sign is retained:
Y_ij>=0 on Z0 and Lambdabar_ij+Y_ij>=0 on E58. There are no omitted terms in
(31). In particular the mixed coefficient-step term is retained, and higher
orders arising from a nonlinear choice of h,Lambda are already covered by
this exact displacement formula.

Put ||(p,Y)||_* = sqrt(||p||_2^2+||Y||_F^2). Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    ||L(Y)||_F <=(sqrt(7)+1)||Y||_F,
    ||Tp||_F <=sqrt(7)||p||_2,
    ||diag(-p_i^2,-S^2)||_F <=||p||_2^2+S^2<=8||p||_2^2.

The first bound uses seven off-diagonal entries in each row. The second uses
||Tp||_F^2=sum_(j=0)^6(7-j)p_j^2. Symmetrization does not increase Frobenius
norm, and the Frobenius norm of a product is bounded by the product of norms.
Consequently

    ||R2(p,Y)||_F <=8||p||_2^2+(7+sqrt(7))||p||_2||Y||_F
                   <=13||(p,Y)||_*^2.                     (32)

Define the compact set

    K58={(p,Y) in C58: ||(p,Y)||_*=1}.

It is closed because flow and W are linear and the sign and PSD cones are
closed; it lies on a finite-dimensional unit sphere. It is nonempty, as the
following actual feasible path confirms without a new computation. For
0<=t<q58 let x=q58-t. The singleton word x with multipliers2 and2(1+x) has the
full2-by2 remainder(2-x^2)[[1,-1],[-1,1]], which is PSD. This follows by
substituting L=[[2,-2],[-2(1+x),2(1+x)]] and T=[[1,0],[x,1]] into D+sym(LT).
Join two copies at bridge
1+u(1+x), then two resulting children at bridge2+x. The accepted join has
positive coefficients, fixed right scaling lambda^2 at both levels, and
actual word

    (x,1+u(1+x),x,2+x,x,1+u(1+x),x).

Its base array is Lambdabar; all coefficients are differentiable in t.
Its tangent has p=(-1,-u,-1,-1,-1,-u,-1) and S=-lambda^2, so is nonzero
and belongs to C58. Normalize it to obtain a point of K58.

Equations(7),(26) show -S>0 everywhere on K58. Hence

    m58=min_((p,Y) in K58)(-sum_i p_i)>0, c=m58/2>0.        (33)

The minimum is a mathematical definition, not a solver output or a new
computation. Its positivity follows from compactness: a sequence of unit

We now prove that all sufficiently small FEASIBLE joint displacements obey

    -S >=c||(p,Y)||_*.                                    (34)

Use formal gradients psi_i and choose x_l=1. Define formal positions and
values by

 x_i=1+Pfx-S_i, f_i=1/2+Pfx-S_i                       (i<l),
 x_i=v_i,      f_i=v_i^2/2                           (l<=i<k),
 x_i=p(1-(S_i-S_k)), f_i=p^2/2-p^2(S_i-S_k)           (i>=k).

The original GD displacements hold, including both exterior regions.
The only potentially nonzero Qbar residuals are

 Qbar_ij=2(S_l-S_i)(1-psi_j)        (i<l,j>=l),
 Qbar_ji=2(S_j-S_k)p(psi_i-p)       (j>=k,i<k).         (15)

For a left/middle pair, put d0=S_l-S_i. The first residual expands to
1+2d0-v_j^2-2v_j(1+d0-v_j)-(1-v_j)^2=2d0(1-v_j);
the reverse residual is zero. For a middle/right pair with e0=S_j-S_k,
substitution gives Qbar_ij=0 and Qbar_ji=2e0 p(v_i-p).
For a left/right pair the two orientations give 2d0(1-p) and
2e0 p(1-p), respectively. Within each of the three regions they vanish.
Thus all crossings are retained and neither orientation is double-counted.

Define the original boundary sums

 C_L=sum_(i<l,j>=l)mu_ij(S_l-S_i)(1-psi_j),
 C_R=sum_(j>=k,i<k)mu_ji(S_j-S_k)p(psi_i-p).            (16)

The value of the left side of(2) is

                 (Pfx+1)^2-(Pfx+H+1)^2 p^2.

Here the prefix contribution to 2sum h_i f_i+sum h_i(1-h_i)psi_i^2 is
Pfx^2+2Pfx; the interval contribution telescopes to1-p^2; with suffix
mass Rtail=s-Pfx-H the suffix contribution is p^2(2Rtail-Rtail^2).
The terminal terms are -s(s+2)p^2+2sRtail p^2. Adding them proves the
displayed value. Consequently

 Delta_I=B_I-2(C_L+C_R),
 B_I=Pfx[Pfx+2-(Pfx+2H+2)p^2].                        (17)

These are formal polynomial tests, not asserted convex interpolation data.

For an ORIGINAL Lambda edge u->w assign reward

 R_I(u,w)=1_(u>=l,w<l)(S_l-S_w)(1-psi_u)
          +1_(u<k,w>=k)(S_w-S_k)p(psi_u-p).            (18)

The indicators select disjoint kinds of edges. Rewards of killing edges
are zero. In particular an initial edge r->w with w<l has reward
(S_l-S_w)(1-p), and must be retained. The reversal Lambda=2mu^T gives

        sum_(u,w)Lambda_uw R_I(u,w)=2(C_L+C_R).         (19)

Let Gamma_I be the sum of(18) over the entire killed excursion, including
its initial terminal jump. The finite mean duration and bounded rewards
justify summing expectations. Equation(10) yields

                   2(C_L+C_R)=R0 E Gamma_I.            (20)

The exact missing estimate is therefore

                         R0 E Gamma_I<=B_I.           (21)

Equation(20) alone is not offered as progress closing(21).

## 5. What the maximum principle actually supplies

For i<r put n_i=sum_j Lambda_ij R_I(i,j), z_i=E_i(sum of rewards before
absorption), and J_I=sum_i Lambda_ri R_I(r,i). Let z_r=z_dagger=0. Then

 z=G(n_i/c_i)_(i<r),
 R0 E Gamma_I=J_I+sum_i Lambda_ri z_i.                 (22)

Because b_dagger=A but the zero-boundary vector b_U has both terminal
boundary coordinates set to0 in the transient equation,

             (Id-P_U)b_U=(2A h_i/c_i)_(i<r).           (23)

Define the concrete scalar barrier

                 theta_I=max_(i<r) n_i/(2A h_i).

Positivity of G and(23) prove the valid bound

             z<=theta_I b_U,
 R0 E Gamma_I<=J_I+2sA theta_I.                        (24)

No sign of theta_I is presumed. The last equality uses
sum_i Lambda_ri b_i=2sA. This is an actual maximum-principle estimate for
the actual chain. Section7.2 shows that it does NOT imply(21), even for a
legal prefix with B_I=0: its right side is strictly positive there.

The exact discarded term can be displayed without a qualitative appeal to
positive or negative edges. Set delta_i=2A h_i theta_I-n_i>=0. Then

 R0 E Gamma_I=J_I+2sA theta_I
       -sum_i Lambda_ri [G(delta_j/c_j)_j]_i.          (25)

Hence repairing this barrier requires the quantitative bound

 sum_i Lambda_ri [G(delta_j/c_j)_j]_i
                         >=J_I+2sA theta_I-B_I.       (26)

The occupation relation Lambda_(r,U)G=(c_i)_i makes the left side equal
to sum_i delta_i. Thus using source conservation alone cancels the barrier
and gives back J_I+sum_i n_i<=B_I. It supplies no new signed inequality.
This is the precise first failed quantitative estimate, rather than an
assumption that every crossing edge has a favorable sign.

## 6. Conditioning has a real, generally positive cost

Let E_+ and E_- denote expectations for(12) and(13), respectively. Equation
(11) gives the exact decomposition

         2(C_L+C_R)=s^2 E_+ Gamma_I+2s E_- Gamma_I.     (27)

For any original edge u->w, expected traversals multiplied by the indicator
of eventual return equal the unconditioned expected traversals multiplied
by a_w/A. This is first-step conditioning after the traversal; absolute
summability permits summing it over all visits. The initial edge obeys the
same statement. Thus the omitted killing contribution has the exact form

 K_I:=2s E_- Gamma_I
       =(1/A)sum_(u,w)Lambda_uw b_w R_I(u,w),          (28)

and the return contribution has a_w in place of b_w. The weighted bound
still required after the Doob transform is

                    s^2 E_+ Gamma_I<=B_I-K_I.          (29)

There is no theorem here making K_I nonpositive or determined by the
killing vertex. Section7.3 proves K_I>B_I>0 in an actual interior-interval
example. Section8 proves K_I=8 at a tight interval in a balanced basic
array, and gives two killed paths with the same killing vertex but
different rewards. Replacing(29) by a free conditioning argument would
lose these terms.

## 7. Exact test on the legal array with opposite crossing signs

### 7.1 Full original array and its certification

Let d be the positive root of d^2+5d-4=0 and put

 A=5+d, kappa=A^2/16, K=kappa-1,
 h=(1+d,3/2,3/2), s=4+d.

The polynomial is strictly increasing on [0,infinity), negative at0 and
positive at1. Hence 0<d<1, dA=4, K>0, and

                       K(4-d)=2(1+d).                 (30)

To check(30), multiplying it by16 gives
(A^2-16)(4-d)-32(1+d)=-(1+d)(d^2+5d-4)=0.
Define the entire original array in indices0,1,2,3 by

 Lambda=
 [0,      0,          0,             Kd              ]
 [3K/2,   0,          kappa,         kappa/2+3K/2     ]
 [3K/2,   7kappa/2,   0,             17kappa/2+3K/2   ]
 [K,      kappa,      14kappa,       0               ]. (31)

Every entry has the required sign. Row-minus-column sums are
K(d-4), -3kappa+3K, -3kappa+3K, 6kappa-K(d+2), which by(30) equal
-2(1+d),-3,-3,8+2d. Thus the full flow holds.

For the full matrix check, the child(3/2,3/2) has

 Lambda_child=[ [0,1,1/2], [7/2,0,17/2], [1,14,0] ],
 L_child T_child=[ [-3/4,-7/4,-1/2],
                  [7/4,-3/4,-17/2], [1/2,17/2,15] ],
 D_child=diag(3/4,3/4,-15).

Its flow is(-3,-3,6), and its symmetric matrix sum is zero. Joining the
empty left child to this capacity4 right child with bridge1+d uses
d(1+4+d)=4. Fact04219554e41d9750, Section11, gives

 V_h=kappa V_child-K[(3/2)Q_10+(3/2)Q_20+Q_30
                           +d Q_03+(3/2)Q_13+(3/2)Q_23].

Insertion of the displayed child coefficients gives exactly(31). Hence
M=0 on all four original gradient coordinates. This verifies the example
within the joint draft, without adopting the old finding as a premise.

The chain's c_0=4K, P_03=d/4, P_0,dagger=(1+d)/(2K). Their sum is1 by
(30). Equation(12) gives P_03^+=dA/4=1: after conditioning on return,
state0 deterministically goes to3.

### 7.2 Prefix: a valid maximum-principle bound misses the required sign

Take I=[0,2). Then Pfx=0, H=5/2+d, p=d/2. Only two original edges have
nonzero rewards and nonzero coefficients:

 R_I(0,3)=(3d/4)(1-d/2)>0,
 R_I(1,3)=-9d^2/8<0.                                 (32)

All initial rewards vanish. Thus n_0=(3K d^2/4)(1-d/2)>0,
n_1=-(9d^2/8)(kappa/2+3K/2)<0, n_2=0, J_I=0. The barrier is exactly

 theta_I=3K d^2(1-d/2)/(8A(1+d))>0,
 J_I+2sA theta_I=3sK d^2(1-d/2)/(4(1+d))>0.           (33)

The required B_I is zero. Thus the proved comparison(24) cannot establish
the desired prefix sign. This is failure of a fully specified expectation
bound, not just a failed entrywise sign claim.

For comparison the exact mean, calculated from all edges, is

 R0 E Gamma_I=n_0+n_1
             =-d^2[(15+6d)K+9kappa]/16<0.             (34)

The positive path3->0->3 has probability Kd/(4R0)>0 and total reward
R_I(0,3)>0. Thus a pathwise nonpositive-reward repair is also false.
No interval counterexample results: (1+H)|p|=2-3d/4>1.
For the entire example, the singleton products are4-3d,5/4,5/4; the
two length-two products are2-3d/4 and1; the full product is Ad/4=1.
All six interval inequalities therefore hold.

### 7.3 Interior: the killed contribution exceeds the entire budget

Take I=[1,2). Write P=1+d=Pfx, H=3/2, p=-1/2. Both exterior boundaries
are present. In(18), the nonzero coefficient-carrying rewards are

 R_I(2,0)=R_I(3,0)=3P/2,
 R_I(0,3)=R_I(1,3)=-9/8.                              (35)

The initial edge3->0 therefore matters. Directly,

 C_L=15KP/8,
 C_R=-9[2Kd+kappa+3K]/32,
 B_I=3P(P+1)/4,
 2(C_L+C_R)=B_I-9/16.                                (36)

For the last equality, use kappa=K+1 and
K(24+42d)=12P(P+1), which follows from(30) and d^2=4-5d.
The hereditary defect is exactly9/16, so this is an admissible interval.

All negative-reward edges end at3, where b_3=0. The positive edges end
at0, where b_0=s. Therefore the actual killed contribution in(28) is

                         K_I=15KP s/(4A)>0.           (37)

In fact K_I>B_I. After division by3P/4 and multiplication by(4-d)A,
this inequality is equivalent, using(30), to

 10(1+d)(4+d)-(2+d)(4-d)(5+d)
                       =d(32+13d+d^2)>0.              (38)

Consequently the return contribution is strictly below -9/16 and is
essential to compensate a killed contribution larger than the entire
allowed upper bound. Positivity of a probability law cannot remove this
signed compensation.

There is also a direct positive killed path3->0->dagger. Its probability
is P/(2R0)>0, and its reward is3P/2. Its reward exceeds B_I/R0 because
B_I/R0=3P(P+1)/[4(P+3)(P+5)]<3/4 while3P/2>3/2.
Thus a uniform pathwise bound by the required mean threshold is false.

## 8. Exact test on the balanced basic array with two factor channels

Let w=sqrt(2), lambda=1+w, kappa=lambda^2, and h=(w,2,w). Then
s=2lambda, A=kappa. Consider the full original array

 Lambda=
 [0,       2,                 0,                 0]
 [2lambda, 0,                 0,                 kappa-1]
 [0,       (kappa-1)w,        0,                 2kappa+(kappa-1)w]
 [0,       kappa-1,           2kappa lambda,      0].  (39)

Its entries are nonnegative. For completeness a single step w obeys
V_(w)=-2Q_01-2lambda Q_10, by expanding the two residuals and using
(w-1)lambda=1. Join two such children with bridge2. Their capacities are
lambda, and d=1 solves d(2lambda+d)=lambda^2. The accepted join gives

 V_h=V_left+kappa V_right
         -(kappa-1)[w Q_21+Q_31+Q_13+w Q_23].          (40)

The coefficients after inserting the single-step identities are exactly
(39). Thus the full polynomial identity, flow(-2w,-4,-2w,4lambda), and
zero remainder hold on all four formal coordinates. In particular zeros
such as Lambda_30 are retained; no one-factor substitution is made.

To identify the two-channel example explicitly, for i<j define an auxiliary
channel by
mu_ij=(U_i-U_(i-1))(D_j+t_j D_(j+1)),
mu_ji=(U_(i-1)+t_i U_i)(D_j-D_(j+1)), with U_-1=D_4=t_3=0.
At t=(w-1,1,w-1), the two choices

 U^(1)=(1,0,0),       (D_1^(1),D_2^(1),D_3^(1))=(lambda,0,0),
 U^(2)=(0,1,kappa+1), (D_1^(2),D_2^(2),D_3^(2))=(0,lambda,lambda)

give respectively nonzero entries mu_01=lambda,mu_10=1, and
mu_12=lambda w,mu_13=lambda,mu_31=lambda,
mu_23=kappa lambda,mu_32=lambda+kappa+1.
Their sum has Lambda=2mu^T equal to(39). The chain analysis uses the full
sum, not a separate flow condition for either channel.

Take the suffix I=[2,3). Then Pfx=w+2, H=w, p=-(w-1), and Delta_I=0.
Here B_I=4(w+2)=4lambda w: indeed
(3w+4)(w-1)^2=w, so the bracket in(17) equals4.
The ONLY edge with both nonzero coefficient and nonzero reward is the
INITIAL edge3->1, whose reward is

                  R_I(3,1)=2(1+w-1)=2w.

Since Lambda_31=kappa-1=2lambda,

       R0 E Gamma_I=4lambda w=B_I.                    (41)

The initial jump lands at1 with a_1=lambda and b_1=w+2=lambda w. Thus

          s^2 E_+ Gamma_I=4w,
          K_I=2s E_- Gamma_I=8.                       (42)

Their sum is4w+8=4lambda w, as required. Ignoring killed excursions would
lose8 at an EXACTLY tight interval. This is not a small perturbation or a
limit, and it occurs in the genuine balanced two-channel basic array.

The killing-vertex marginal h_i/s cannot determine this reward. The two
paths3->1->0->dagger and3->2->1->0->dagger both have positive probability:
each specified original edge is positive in(39), and killing at0 has
positive probability. Both are killed at0. The first has total reward2w,
and the second has total reward0. Thus the relevant cost depends on the
history even after the killing vertex is fixed.
The three singleton interval products of this word are1,3,1; both
length-two products are2w-1>1, and the full product is1. Thus it is also
not an interval-heredity counterexample.

## 9. Remaining interface and bounded-round conclusion

The killed process is well defined for every original array satisfying(1),
after the proved isolation of zero coordinates. It retains the original
terminal source, every crossing entry, both exterior boundaries, all
alternating weights, and every absorption cost. It requires no irreducible,
reversible, positive-support, factorized, or inherited-subword assumption.

The attempted direct estimates have the following precise status:

1. Normalization, harmonic hitting probabilities, finite occupation measure,
   conditional laws, and full coefficient recovery are derived jointly.
2. The complete interval crossing expression is the signed excursion reward
   in(18)--(21), not an interpolable gradient process.
3. The concrete death-potential maximum principle(24) is valid but too weak:
   (33) is positive where the required prefix budget is zero. Its exact
   missing compensation is(26); source conservation by itself is circular.
4. Conditioning on return leaves the history-dependent term(28). It is
   larger than the entire interior budget in(37)--(38), and equals8 at the
   tight basic interval(42). This term cannot be dropped or replaced by the
   marginal distribution of the killing vertex.

Accordingly the first unproved implication for this mechanism remains

 s^2 E_+ Gamma_I
 <=Pfx[Pfx+2-(Pfx+2H+2)p^2]
      -(1/A)sum_(u,w)Lambda_uw(s-S_w)R_I(u,w),          (43)

for every interval and every full original M=0 array. Equivalently one
must establish(26) from more than the unsigned flow/harmonic accounting.
No such signed comparison is proved here, and no full-array violation of
the interval theorem is produced. The explicit arrays satisfy heredity.

This report does not infer a capacity ceiling, a theorem for arbitrary
M>=0, a neighborhood theorem at seven steps, or a conclusion about the
original unrestricted exact-profile Goal. The earlier scalar extremal
draft cannot be used downstream because its full-M0 interval hypothesis
has not been established. All new claims remain UNVERIFIED, with no
fact_submit and no new accepted fact. This completes the one assigned
mechanism/round; no additional allocation is inferred.

## 10. Retrieval, verification status, and glossary

The query-memory, search-math-results, direct-proving, and
construct-counterexamples procedures were used. Matlas returned two
inapplicable results and the finite harmonic-extension Proposition12 of
Yang Chu and Robert Hough, *Solution of the 15 puzzle problem*,
arXiv:1908.07106v1 (2019), https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.07106.
The exact source was downloaded and read around the Markov-chain
definitions, Proposition12, and the return-probability proof in Section5.
That proposition assumes irreducibility and cites its proof elsewhere;
the surrounding application uses a reversible torus walk. Those hypotheses
are not imported. The finite absorption and harmonic uniqueness arguments
needed here were instead proved explicitly by(6)--(8). The reference
provides a proof-pattern comparison, not an external mathematical premise.

Operational retrieval errors were exposed rather than treated as success:
project-name memory calls failed with DANUS_AGENTS_ROOT unset; the worker-
pinned calls succeeded. A lecture-note PDF download failed SSL certificate
validation and web retrieval timed out. The arXiv PDF downloaded, but
pdftotext was unavailable; its source was then retrieved. Treating the
source as tar returned invalid header; inspection identified a single

No package was installed and no mathematical program was evaluated.

## 1. Objects, accepted input, and the proposed theorem

All vectors and matrices below are real unless exact field data are specified.
Write q58=sqrt(2), lambda=1+q58, u=q58-1=1/lambda, and

    hbar=(q58,2,q58,1+lambda,q58,2,q58),  Abar=lambda^3.

For h=(h0,...,h6) in [0,infinity)^7, let s=sum_i h_i and A(h)=1+s.
Let e be the all-ones column in R8, and let e_i be its coordinate columns,
indexed0,...,7. For any zero-diagonal real8-by8 array X define

    L(X)=diag(Xe)-X.

The prefix matrix T(h) has diagonal1, entry h_j at i,j when j<i, and zero
above its diagonal. Put

    omega(h)=(-2h0,...,-2h6,2s)^T,
    D(h)=diag(h0(2-h0),...,h6(2-h6),-s(s+2)),
    M(h,Lambda)=D(h)+sym(L(Lambda)T(h)),
    sym(K)=(K+K^T)/2.

A full certificate means precisely

    Lambda_ii=0, Lambda_ij>=0 for ALL ordered i!=j,
    L(Lambda)^T e=omega(h), M(h,Lambda)>=0 on the ENTIRE R8.       (1)

All56 ordered coefficients and all8 independent formal gradients remain.
No support, symmetry, rank, or equality between formal gradients is imposed
in(1). Nonzero singular PSD remainders are included.

Accepted fact04219554e41d9750, proof Sections10--11, supplies the original
primitive coefficient identity and the full original-coordinate composition
identity. For a normalized convex1-smooth objective F, write g_i=grad F(x_i)
and f_i=F(x_i); Gram(g0,...,g7) has entries <g_i,g_j>. Its Section10 uses

    x_i=x0-sum_(k<i) h_k g_k,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    V_h=2sum_(i<7)h_i(f_i-f7)
          +sum_(i<7)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-s(s+1)||g7||^2,

and establishes, under the flow in(1),

    V_h+sum_(i!=j) Lambda_ij Q_ij
       =trace(M(h,Lambda) Gram(g0,...,g7)).                    (2)

This accepted fact is the only non-elementary accepted input used here.
Its original all-function interpretation is retained; no converse about all
primitive schedules is asserted. The exact algebraic statement of its join
identity needed below is recalled in Section5.

Define Lambdabar by the following twenty entries, with every other entry0:

    01:2                    10:2lambda                13:2lambda
    21:2lambda*q58            23:2lambda^2+2lambda*q58    31:2lambda
    32:2lambda^3            37:2lambda^2              43:2lambda*q58
    45:2lambda^2            47:2lambda*q58              53:4lambda
    54:2lambda^3            57:2lambda^3+4lambda      63:2lambda*q58
    65:2lambda^3*q58          67:2lambda^4+2lambda^3*q58+2lambda*q58

using the accepted composition identity; each right scaling is lambda^2 and
each extra interpolation factor is lambda^2-1=2lambda.

PROPOSED LOCAL THEOREM. There exist epsilon>0 and c>0 such that for EVERY
h in[0,infinity)^7 and EVERY array Lambda satisfying(1), if
||h-hbar||_2<epsilon, then

    A(h) <= Abar-c*sqrt(||h-hbar||_2^2+||Lambda-Lambdabar||_F^2). (3)

    ||Lambda-Lambdabar||_F <= (sqrt(7)/c)*||h-hbar||_2.          (4)

## 2. Complete linearization, common null, and exact dual identity

distinct pairs. Write Tbal58=T(hbar) and Lbar=L(Lambdabar). Tbal58 is exactly the frozen candidate's prefix matrix T0. The separate name

    S=sum_(i=0)^6 p_i,
    Tp_ij=p_j if j<i, and0 otherwise,
    op=(-2p0,...,-2p6,2S)^T,
    D1(p)=diag(2(1-hbar_i)p_i for i<7,-2Abar*S),
    W(p,Y)=D1(p)+sym(Lbar*Tp+L(Y)*Tbal58),
    f(p,Y)=L(Y)^T e-op, n(p,Y)=W(p,Y)e.                     (5)

The FULL linearized cone is

    C58={(p,Y): f(p,Y)=0, Y_ij>=0 on Z0, W(p,Y)>=0 on R8}.    (6)

    omega(h)^T T(h)e=s^2+sum_i h_i^2,

2sum_(j<i)h_i h_j=s^2-sum_i h_i^2. Differentiation along the exactly flowing
linear families in(5) gives e^T W e=0 when f=0. If W is PSD, expansion of

## 3. A three-step zero-remainder derivative calculation

Use local indices0,1,2,3 and the three-step base word(q58,2,q58), of capacity
lambda^2. In this section L,T,omega,D,M are defined exactly as in Section1
with three steps and four gradients, so the terminal index is3 and e is the
all-ones column of R4. Its base array has seven positive entries

    01=2, 10=13=31=2lambda, 21=2lambda*q58,
    23=2lambda^2+2lambda*q58, 32=2lambda^3,                    (11)

and all other entries0. Its remainder is0 by the accepted singleton join.
Permit derivatives on exactly these seven pairs AND the additional pair03.
The latter derivative is an unrestricted real number. Write r0,r1,r2 for
the physical derivatives, y_ij for the coefficient derivatives, and assume
the four original flow derivatives hold and the full4-by4 remainder
derivative Wloc is0. We prove all r and y are0.

Only the pairs in(11) and03 are used in the following displayed entries.
The entry02 of L(Lambda)T is -h2*Lambda03, whereas its entry20 is0.
Therefore

## 4. Exact central-cut algebra to first order

Assume p,Y satisfy f=0, W=0, and Y=0 on Z0. Thus all coefficient derivatives
are supported on E58. Introduce the REAL, not assumed feasible, families

    h(t)=hbar+t*p, Lambda(t)=Lambdabar+t*Y.

Their flow holds exactly for every real t. Their full remainder is O(t^2),
entry by entry, because its constant and linear coefficients are0. Here
O(t^2) means a function with absolute value bounded by a fixed multiple of
t^2 for sufficiently small |t|; the constants may depend on the fixed p,Y.
All computations in this section retain constant and first-order terms.

Let P58={0,1,2,3}, Bset={4,5,6,7}, and let eP,eB be their indicator columns
in R8. Define capacities and bridge excess from these ACTUAL physical steps:

    a(t)=1+h0+h1+h2, b(t)=1+h4+h5+h6, d(t)=h3-1.

Write h_left=(h0,h1,h2) and h_right=(h4,h5,h6). At t=0, a=b=lambda^2 and
d=lambda. The only P58-to-Bset coefficient is

for j=4,5,6,7. This support follows from(10) and the displayed E58, rather

array for h0,h1,h2. Its original flow holds exactly: the first three rows
have no crossing edge, and the terminal flow follows by summing all four
row-minus-column sums. Direct matrix multiplication gives

N*(T_3-T_7) in row3; it changes only entry33, by -d*N. The parent-versus-child

## 8. Exact nonlinear remainder and strict local capacity loss

For arbitrary finite displacements p=h-hbar, Y=Lambda-Lambdabar, the full
polynomial expansion is EXACT:

    M(h,Lambda)=W(p,Y)+R2(p,Y),
    R2(p,Y)=diag(-p0^2,...,-p6^2,-S^2)+sym(L(Y)Tp).          (31)

Flow is exactly f(p,Y)=0. Every original sign is retained:
Y_ij>=0 on Z0 and Lambdabar_ij+Y_ij>=0 on E58. There are no omitted terms in
(31). In particular the mixed coefficient-step term is retained, and higher
orders arising from a nonlinear choice of h,Lambda are already covered by
this exact displacement formula.

Put ||(p,Y)||_* = sqrt(||p||_2^2+||Y||_F^2). Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    ||L(Y)||_F <=(sqrt(7)+1)||Y||_F,
    ||Tp||_F <=sqrt(7)||p||_2,
    ||diag(-p_i^2,-S^2)||_F <=||p||_2^2+S^2<=8||p||_2^2.

The first bound uses seven off-diagonal entries in each row. The second uses
||Tp||_F^2=sum_(j=0)^6(7-j)p_j^2. Symmetrization does not increase Frobenius
norm, and the Frobenius norm of a product is bounded by the product of norms.
Consequently

    ||R2(p,Y)||_F <=8||p||_2^2+(7+sqrt(7))||p||_2||Y||_F
                   <=13||(p,Y)||_*^2.                     (32)

Define the compact set

    K58={(p,Y) in C58: ||(p,Y)||_*=1}.

It is closed because flow and W are linear and the sign and PSD cones are
closed; it lies on a finite-dimensional unit sphere. It is nonempty, as the
following actual feasible path confirms without a new computation. For
0<=t<q58 let x=q58-t. The singleton word x with multipliers2 and2(1+x) has the
full2-by2 remainder(2-x^2)[[1,-1],[-1,1]], which is PSD. This follows by
substituting L=[[2,-2],[-2(1+x),2(1+x)]] and T=[[1,0],[x,1]] into D+sym(LT).
Join two copies at bridge
1+u(1+x), then two resulting children at bridge2+x. The accepted join has
positive coefficients, fixed right scaling lambda^2 at both levels, and
actual word

    (x,1+u(1+x),x,2+x,x,1+u(1+x),x).

Its base array is Lambdabar; all coefficients are differentiable in t.
Its tangent has p=(-1,-u,-1,-1,-1,-u,-1) and S=-lambda^2, so is nonzero
and belongs to C58. Normalize it to obtain a point of K58.

Equations(7),(26) show -S>0 everywhere on K58. Hence

    m58=min_((p,Y) in K58)(-sum_i p_i)>0, c=m58/2>0.        (33)

The minimum is a mathematical definition, not a solver output or a new
computation. Its positivity follows from compactness: a sequence of unit
cone points with -S->0 would have a unit limit in the equality set(26).

We now prove that all sufficiently small FEASIBLE joint displacements obey

    -S >=c||(p,Y)||_*.                                    (34)

class Q:
    __slots__ = ('a', 'b')

    def __init__(self, a=0, b=0):
        self.a, self.b = Fraction(a), Fraction(b)

    @staticmethod
    def of(x):
        if isinstance(x, Q):
            return x
        if isinstance(x, list):
            return Q(*x)
        return Q(x)

    def __add__(self, other):
        other = Q.of(other)
        return Q(self.a + other.a, self.b + other.b)

    __radd__ = __add__

    def __neg__(self):
        return Q(-self.a, -self.b)

    def __sub__(self, other):
        return self + (-Q.of(other))

    def __rsub__(self, other):
        return Q.of(other) - self

    def __mul__(self, other):
        other = Q.of(other)
        return Q(self.a * other.a + 2 * self.b * other.b,
                 self.a * other.b + self.b * other.a)

    __rmul__ = __mul__

    def __truediv__(self, other):
        other = Q.of(other)
        den = other.a * other.a - 2 * other.b * other.b
        if den == 0:
            raise ZeroDivisionError('exact zero field divisor')
        return Q((self.a * other.a - 2 * self.b * other.b) / den,
                 (self.b * other.a - self.a * other.b) / den)

    def __pow__(self, exponent):
        result = Q(1)
        for _ in range(exponent):
            result = result * self
        return result

    def __bool__(self):
        return bool(self.a or self.b)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        other = Q.of(other)
        return self.a == other.a and self.b == other.b

    def encoded(self):
        return [str(self.a), str(self.b)]

    def sign(self):
        a, b = self.a, self.b
        if a == 0:
            return (b > 0) - (b < 0)
        if b == 0:
            return (a > 0) - (a < 0)
        if (a > 0) == (b > 0):
            return 1 if a > 0 else -1
        difference = a * a - 2 * b * b
        return ((a > 0) - (a < 0)) * ((difference > 0) - (difference < 0))


def encode(x):
    if isinstance(x, Q):

    if isinstance(x, list):
        return [encode(v) for v in x]
    if isinstance(x, dict):
        return {k: encode(v) for k, v in x.items()}
    return x


def matrix(rows, cols):
    return [[Q() for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]

    C = matrix(len(A), len(B[0]))
    for i, row in enumerate(A):
        for k, value in enumerate(row):
            if value:
                for j, other in enumerate(B[k]):
                    if other:

    return C

# A logarithmic-spiral checkpoint geometry and its paid activation obstruction

TASK.md and master_guidance0682362f7b48ea2d. No numerical experiment,
symbolic evaluator, solver, benchmark computation, or fact_submit was used.

curve from a circular arc to a logarithmic spiral. The global function is
constructed below before its run. All new lemmas are parts of this one
candidate, not separately accepted facts.

## 1. Target, source audit, and the changed interface

For a finite nonnegative word h of length n, let W_n(h) be the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f_star)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over finite-dimensional convex
differentiable L-smooth functions with an attained minimum and GD
x_(t+1)=x_t-h_t grad f(x_t)/L. Thus W=2R for the project's R.

The original benchmark remains U_n^ZJ=1/B_n. For clarity its ALL-split
definition is C_0=B_0=1 and

    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n) Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n) G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

No recurrence or benchmark constant is modified in this draft.

Primary source: Yuhan Ye and Kaizhao Liu, *Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal
for Gradient Descent*, arXiv:2609.09152v2, September10,2026,
https://arxiv.org/html/2609.09152v2. The unversioned arXiv landing page
still identified v2 as current when read in this round. Exact HTML and its
extracted text are in this directory's downloads/. Read portions were
Section2, Section3.1, and the full proofs in AppendixA.1--A.3.

This paragraph is a source audit, not a project fact. The paper's Eq(1)
uses denominator (L/2)||x_0-x_star||^2, so its symbol R denotes project W.
Its stated Lemma2.2 retains only 1/[4(1+s_tail)]. But its actual Eq(40)
constructs a function with value D^2/[4(1+s_tail)] at initial distance1;
the paper explicitly drops the extra factor2 in passing to the lemma.
Thus the stronger prefactor 1/[2(1+s_tail)] in PROBLEM.md Section7 is
supported by the construction, despite the notation discrepancy.

The source takes

    c_Y=sqrt(1+2 gamma+epsilon^2),
    R_Y=sqrt(epsilon^2+(1+gamma)^2),
    H_Y=[c_Y(1+gamma+R_Y)/(epsilon(gamma+R_Y))]^(R_Y/gamma)-1,
    C_Y=epsilon+(H_Y+1)/epsilon.

Its local steps are half the physical steps. A sufficient source choice
is a>=2C_Y/c_Y, with selected physical steps b>=2(1+epsilon^(-2)).
The non-anytime recursion additionally asks a>=max{2,2B_0+2}.

There are two concrete costs. In AppendixA.1 Eq(34), the circle's normal
rotation telescopes with exponent R_Y/gamma; its endpoint-angle ratio
contains 1/epsilon. In AppendixA.2 Eq(35), vanishing before activation
requires a bound for P+epsilon+(1+Q)/epsilon. The ENDPOINT support plane

The source's half-sum gluing also pays its smoothness overlap and retains

Shared prior awareness b70f11135ec8688e and4ff405e904d7da62 described a

checks those residuals directly. Accepted0e7e78056dc6258c rules out an
orthogonal-moment shortcut; the present gradients retain correlations.

## 2. Statement of the candidate checkpoint lemma

Fix 0<kappa<=epsilon<=1/2. Define

    Theta=arctan(1/epsilon),
    c_sp=sqrt(1+epsilon^2) exp(kappa Theta),
    d_sp=1-kappa^2,
    T_sp=[exp(d_sp Theta/kappa)-1]/d_sp,
    H_sp=c_sp[1+(1+kappa)T_sp]-1,
    A_sp=epsilon+(H_sp+1)/epsilon.                       (1)

All these quantities are independent of the word and its length.

Partition ANY prescribed finite nonnegative word, in its original order,
as

    (block_0,b_0,block_1,b_1,...,block_(k-1),b_(k-1),block_k),

where each ordinary block may be empty, s_i is its sum, and every selected
checkpoint satisfies b_i>=1+epsilon^(-2). The case k=0 is allowed.
For each i<k, Section3 constructs local vectors from the actual ordered
steps in block_i, with displacements P_i,Q_i satisfying

    0<=P_i<=c_sp s_i,  0<=Q_i<=H_sp,  P_i>=epsilon Q_i.

Set

    M_i=P_i+max{epsilon b_i,epsilon+(1+Q_i)/epsilon},
    sigma_i=1/M_i,
    D_0=1,  D_(i+1)=D_i sigma_i(b_i-1),
    ell_0=0,  ell_(i+1)=D_i sigma_i(1+Q_i).            (2)

For k>=1 there is one explicitly specified finite max-affine J on
R^(k+1), and one function f=env_1 J, such that the complete physical GD
run starts at e_0 and has

    2f(x_n)=D_k^2/(1+2s_k),
    min f=0,
    dist(e_0,argmin f)^2
      =sigma_0^2[(epsilon+P_0)^2+(1+Q_0)^2].           (3)

Consequently this exact true-distance payoff is

    W_n(h) >= (b_0-1)^2
               /{[(epsilon+P_0)^2+(1+Q_0)^2](1+2s_k)}
             times product_(i=1)^(k-1)[(b_i-1)/M_i]^2. (4)

In particular the following fully explicit mass-only bound holds:

    W_n(h) >= 1/(1+2s_k)
      times product_(i=0)^(k-1)
        [(b_i-1)/(c_sp s_i+max{epsilon b_i,A_sp})]^2. (5)

For k=0 use the one-dimensional Huber envelope, giving exactly
1/(1+2s_0). Multiplying the displayed functions by L gives the same
normalized payoffs and the prescribed steps h_t/L for every L>0.

The lemma covers every word and every checkpoint selection satisfying
its displayed condition. Zeros and arbitrarily large ordinary steps are
included. No cap is imposed on selected steps. Maximizing (4) or (5)
over allowed selections, and including k=0, is an explicit all-word
lower-bound channel; no comparison with B_n is assumed.

There is also a direct source-format corollary, proved in Section6A:
with a_sp=2A_sp/c_sp and checkpoints b_i>=2(1+epsilon^(-2)),

    W_n(h)>=1/[2(1+s_k)]
        times product_(i=0)^(k-1)
          [b_i/(c_sp(a_sp+s_i)+epsilon b_i)]^2.       (5a)

It preserves the source's numerator, terminal factor and threshold,
while replacing its certified auxiliary constant. Thus the improvement
is not obtained by concealing the b_i-1 cost of the separate formula(5).

## 3. The new support curve and a backward construction for arbitrary steps

For 0<=theta<=Theta define

    e(theta)=(cos theta,-sin theta),
    e_t(theta)=(-sin theta,-cos theta),
    R_sp(theta)=c_sp exp(-kappa theta),
    v(theta)=R_sp(theta)e(theta),
    n_sp(theta)=e(theta)+kappa e_t(theta).

Let K be the convex hull of 0 and this compact arc. Write
v(theta)=(p(theta),-q(theta)). The endpoint values are
v(0)=(c_sp,0), v(Theta)=(epsilon,-1). Differentiating gives

    p'=-R_sp(kappa cos theta+sin theta)<0,
    q'= R_sp(cos theta-kappa sin theta)>=0.

The second inequality uses kappa<=epsilon=cot Theta. Hence

    epsilon<=p<=c_sp, 0<=q<=1, q/p<=1/epsilon.         (6)

For delta=phi-theta in [-Theta,Theta],

    <n_sp(theta),v(phi)>/R_sp(theta)
       =exp(-kappa delta)(cos delta+kappa sin delta).

The derivative of the right side in delta is
-(1+kappa^2)exp(-kappa delta)sin delta. Its maximum on this interval is
therefore1, at delta0. Since <n_sp(theta),0>=0<R_sp(theta), n_sp(theta)
is an outward supporting normal to K at v(theta). At v(0), (0,1) is
also a supporting normal because every point of K has second coordinate
nonpositive. This proves all support inequalities directly; no theorem
about spiral convexity is imported.

Now let alpha_1,...,alpha_m be any finite nonnegative ordinary block.
Set r_m=v_m=v(Theta) and work backward. Given r_j=(u_j,-y_j) and
alpha=alpha_j, make the following choice.

If

    y_j<=kappa[u_j+(alpha-1)c_sp],                     (7)

put v_(j-1)=v(0), r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha v(0).
Otherwise choose the unique theta in (0,theta_j] satisfying

    <r_j,e(theta)-kappa^(-1)e_t(theta)>/R_sp(theta)
          =1-alpha,                                 (8)

put v_(j-1)=v(theta), r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha v(theta).
Here theta_j is the angle of v_j. Once a capped vector v(0) occurs,
(7) applies at every subsequent backward step, so (8) is only needed
when theta_j>0. Equation(8) defines a number uniquely; it is not an
oracle, numerical feasibility assumption, or executed solver.

We prove by backward induction that these rules are well-defined, that
v_j is the Euclidean projection of r_j on K, and that

    u_j>=epsilon, y_j>=1, y_j/u_j<=1/epsilon.          (9)

For a noncapped point the stronger representation is

    r_j=R_sp(theta_j)[(1+t_j)e(theta_j)
                            +kappa t_j e_t(theta_j)],
    t_j>=0.                                         (10)

It holds at j=m with theta_m=Theta,t_m=0. For a capped step let
mu=u_j+(alpha-1)c_sp. Condition(7) implies mu>=y_j/kappa>0, and

    r_(j-1)-v(0)=mu n_sp(0)+(0,kappa mu-y_j).

This is a nonnegative sum of the two supporting normals already checked,
so it certifies projection. It also yields
y_(j-1)<=kappa(u_(j-1)-c_sp), which implies(7) at every earlier step.

If(7) fails, the current point is not capped. By(10), its polar angle
is at least theta_j and the left side of(8) equals1 at theta_j.
At theta0 the left side is (u_j-y_j/kappa)/c_sp<1-alpha.
Its derivative is

    (kappa+kappa^(-1))(u_j cos theta+y_j sin theta)
       /R_sp(theta)>0.

Thus there is exactly one root theta in(0,theta_j]. The tangential
component <r_j,e_t(theta)> is nonnegative. Equation(8) says exactly
that r_j+(alpha-1)v(theta) is a nonnegative multiple of n_sp(theta).
Projection and(10) follow from the supporting inequality. Adding alpha
times a vector obeying(6) preserves u>=epsilon,y>=1; the ratio y/u is
a convex combination of its previous value and q/p, giving(9).
This completes the induction, including alpha=0.

Define

    P=sum_(j=1)^m alpha_j p(theta_(j-1)),
    Q=sum_(j=1)^m alpha_j q(theta_(j-1)), S=sum alpha_j.

Then r_0=(epsilon+P,-1-Q). Bounds P<=c_sp S and P>=epsilon Q follow
from(6). It remains to prove the word-independent bound for Q.

Consider consecutive noncapped angles theta_old<=theta_new and put
Delta=theta_new-theta_old. Taking the tangential component in the exact
GD identity, and using(10), gives

    t_old=B(Delta)+A(Delta)t_new,
    A(Delta)=exp(-kappa Delta)(cos Delta+sin Delta/kappa),
    B(Delta)=exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta/kappa.          (11)

For 0<=Delta<=Theta<pi/2 both A,B are nonnegative. Put d=d_sp.
Direct differentiation yields

    A'-(d/kappa)A
       =-(1+kappa^(-2))exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta<=0.

Since A(0)=1, A<=exp(d Delta/kappa). Also B<=Delta/kappa, so
1+dB<=1+d Delta/kappa<=exp(d Delta/kappa). Therefore(11) implies

    1+d t_old<=exp(d Delta/kappa)(1+d t_new).

Telescoping from theta_m=Theta,t_m=0 proves

    t_j<=[exp(d(Theta-theta_j)/kappa)-1]/d<=T_sp.      (12)

At each noncapped point(10) now gives

    y_j=R_sp(theta_j)[(1+t_j)sin theta_j
                              +kappa t_j cos theta_j]
       <=c_sp[1+(1+kappa)T_sp]=1+H_sp.

A capped backward step leaves y unchanged, so the same bound holds at
all capped points. Hence Q=y_0-1<=H_sp. Every inequality is uniform in
m and in all finite values of the alpha_j; no maximum stepsize was used.

## 4. Local finite planes and their exact zero/proximal regions

For one block suppress its index. Set

    A_loc=epsilon+(1+Q)/epsilon,
    M=P+max{epsilon b,A_loc}, sigma=1/M,
    z_circ=(1,0)-sigma(epsilon+P,-1-Q),
    U=1-sigma(P+epsilon b)>=0, Y=sigma Q.

Let V_fin consist of0,v(0),v_0,...,v_m and define

    phi(z)=sigma max_(v in V_fin)<v,z-z_circ>.         (13)

All objects are fixed by the supplied block and b. The smaller convex
hull conv(V_fin) contains every v_j and is contained in K; thus the
projection inequalities proved in Section3 still hold on it. At

    x_j=z_circ+sigma r_j, z_j=x_j-sigma v_j,

the plane with slope sigma v_j is active in phi, giving
sigma v_j in partial phi(z_j). Consequently z_j is the proximal point
of phi at x_j, and grad env_1 phi(x_j)=sigma v_j.

Every nonzero v=(p,-q) obeys p>=0,q>=0,q<=p/epsilon. At the origin,

    <v,-z_circ>
     =-p+sigma[p(epsilon+P)+q(1+Q)]
     <=-p+sigma p(P+A_loc)<=0.

Thus phi=0 on {z_1<=0,z_2>=0}. At(U,Y),

    <v,(U,Y)-z_circ>
       =sigma[(1-b)epsilon p+q]<=0                    (14)

because b>=1+epsilon^(-2). Increasing its second argument preserves
this inequality, so phi(U,y)=0 for y>=Y.

The local GD path starts at(1,0). Its ordinary block ends at
(U+sigma epsilon b,Y), with gradient sigma(epsilon,-1); checkpoint b
then reaches (U,Y+sigma b). Every ordinary/checkpoint-query proximal
point has first coordinate at least U and second coordinate in
[0,sigma(1+Q)]. To check the first claim, the normal representations give
u_j>=p_j: for an interior point this follows from(10), since
cos theta-kappa sin theta>=0, and for a capped point it follows from
the normal representation. Hence

    (z_j)_1-U=sigma[epsilon(b-1)+u_j-p_j]>=0.

For the second claim, (z_j)_2=sigma[1+Q-y_j+q_j]. The inequalities
1<=y_j<=1+Q and0<=q_j<=1 give the two endpoints.

These statements concern the nonsmooth planes, precisely where the
global maximum in the next section must be tested.

## 5. One static global function and ALL directed interpolation rows

Use coordinates0,...,k and quantities(2). For i<k put

    Phi_i(z)=D_i^2 phi_i((z_i-ell_i)/D_i,z_(i+1)/D_i).

Set delta_tail=D_k/(1+2s_k),

    Phi_k(z)=delta_tail max{z_k-ell_k,0},
    J(z)=max_{0<=i<=k} Phi_i(z),
    f(x)=min_z[J(z)+||x-z||^2/2].                     (15)

This is a finite maximum of specified affine planes, including the zero
plane. It is nonnegative and J(0)=0 by Section4 and ell_i>=0. The
quadratic term makes the proximal minimizer unique and attained.

For completeness, the minimizing equation is x-z in partial J(z).
The two subgradient inequalities at z,z' give
||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'> for g=x-z,g'=x'-z'. For an increment w,
using z as a trial proximal point gives
f(x+w)<=f(x)+<g,w>+||w||^2/2. If z' is the proximal point at x+w,
the inequality J(z')>=J(z)+<g,z'-z> gives, by expansion,
f(x+w)>=f(x)+<g,w>+||w-(z'-z)||^2/2. Consequently
0<=f(x+w)-f(x)-<g,w><=||w||^2/2. This proves differentiability,
the supporting inequalities prove convexity, and the preceding
monotonicity estimate proves1-smoothness. It has minimum0 and is
everywhere finite. No external interpolation theorem is required.

We verify the WHOLE actual trajectory. At the start of block i the
claimed coordinates are frozen x_j=ell_j+D_j U_j for j<i, current
coordinate x_i=ell_i+D_i, and all coordinates j>i equal0. Use the
Section4 trajectory in coordinates i,i+1. At each of its candidate
GLOBAL proximal points:

* the current component Phi_i has the prescribed subgradient;
* component i-1 has first input U_(i-1) and second input at least

* every earlier component is still in the same zero region;
* component i+1 has first input at most0, because the second proximal

The terminal hinge is included in this last check. Thus Phi_i dominates

This proves the induction, without removing any old or future plane.

During the terminal block, after accumulated steps u in[0,s_k], the

is at least ell_k because
D_k-(u+1)delta_tail>=0. All earlier pieces remain0 there. The actual

Here is also an exact check of the original ALL-directed constraints.
At every sample, including the unqueried terminal, put g_i=grad f(x_i)
and z_i=x_i-g_i. The preceding construction proves

The same equation applies when either sample is any minimizer, with
g_star=0,J(z_star)=0. Thus all remote, prefix, terminal, and optimum

The Gram matrix is the Gram matrix of these explicit real vectors in
R^(k+1), hence is positive semidefinite. Within a block the gradient

Neighboring components share one coordinate and can have negative

## 6. The closest minimizer and the exact normalization

For k>=1 define x_star with first two coordinates

    (x_star)_0=1-sigma_0(epsilon+P_0),

and all later coordinates0. The first component is evaluated at its

    lim_(kappa->0) kappa log(H_Y+1)/log(1/kappa)=2/pi. (18)

inside H_Y is asymptotic to2/kappa. For the first, log A_sp differs

That improvement is not enough to make this geometry lossless. The
following finite family tests the ACTUAL activation budget, including
the slack c_sp S-P, rather than merely bounding Q.

theta_l=Theta-l Delta for0<=l<=M, and define

The scope of(22)--(24) is the specified spiral support geometry with

## 8. Every paid loss and the exact remaining target obligation

There are no hidden dimension or PSD losses: dimension is k+1, the
function is fixed before the run, and(17) is exact. Formula(4) uses the
true closest minimizer. Passing from(4) to(5) pays only the explicitly
displayed displacement bounds and the first-factor norm bound.

The remaining costs in(5) are:

* the checkpoint restriction b_i>=1+epsilon^(-2);
* the exact numerator b_i-1, caused by the future-plane proximal buffer;
* the coefficient c_sp>1 of every s_i;

* the terminal Huber denominator1+2s_k, retained exactly.

    Loss_source=2sum_i log[c_sp+(c_sp a_sp+epsilon b_i)/s_i].

The actual outstanding task is to prove, with a threshold independent
of h, that an explicit legal adversary channel (this one, a stronger

Writing v=(p,-q), the endpoint identity follows from

The derivatives are

    q'= R_sp(cos theta-kappa sin theta)>=0.

The second sign follows from cot theta>=cot Theta=epsilon>=kappa,
with theta=0 handled directly. Thus epsilon<=p<=c, 0<=q<=1, and
q/p=tan theta<=1/epsilon. These signs are proved, not assumed for an
arbitrary curve outside this parameter range.

Let K be the convex hull of0 and the compact curve. For any two angles
theta,phi in the full interval, put Delta=phi-theta. Then

       = exp(-kappa Delta)(cos Delta+kappa sin Delta).

The derivative with respect to Delta is

Also <n_sp(theta),0>=0<R_sp(theta). Consequently

This includes both endpoints, all nonadjacent curve points, and every
convex combination. The additional normal (0,1) at v(0) is valid because

## 4. Exact backward construction, including the cap

For any ordinary block alpha_1,...,alpha_m>=0 start with
r_m=v_m=v(Theta). Write r_j=(u_j,-y_j). Assume the frozen induction
invariants u_j>=epsilon, y_j>=1, y_j/u_j<=1/epsilon. At a noncapped
state also write

    r_j=R_sp(theta_j)[(1+t_j)e(theta_j)+kappa t_j e_t(theta_j)],
    t_j>=0.

This representation holds initially with t_m=0. For alpha=alpha_j,
the capped test is y_j<=kappa[u_j+(alpha-1)c]. If it holds, set
mu=u_j+(alpha-1)c. Then mu>=y_j/kappa>0 and

    r_j+alpha v(0)-v(0)
       =mu n_sp(0)+(0,kappa mu-y_j).

Both coefficients of the valid normals are nonnegative. Their sum
proves that v(0) is the projection of r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha v(0) on K.
The new point obeys y_(j-1)<=kappa(u_(j-1)-c). At any earlier step
alpha'>=0 this implies y_(j-1)<=kappa[u_(j-1)+(alpha'-1)c]. Hence
capping persists. There is no assumption that a huge ordinary step
must remain on the curved part.

If the cap test fails, a previously capped state is impossible. Define

    F_j(theta)=<r_j,e(theta)-kappa^(-1)e_t(theta)>/R_sp(theta).

The current representation gives F_j(theta_j)=1, while failure of
the cap test gives F_j(0)=(u_j-y_j/kappa)/c<1-alpha. Direct differentiation
gives

                  (u_j cos theta+y_j sin theta)/R_sp(theta)>0.

Since 1-alpha<=1, there is one and only one root
theta in(0,theta_j] with F_j(theta)=1-alpha. Moreover, if
Delta=theta_j-theta, then

    <r_j,e_t(theta)>
       =R_sp(theta_j)[(1+t_j)sin Delta+kappa t_j cos Delta]>=0.

The root equation therefore says that
r_j+(alpha-1)v(theta) is a nonnegative multiple of n_sp(theta).
It proves the projection of r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha v(theta), and gives its
new representation with t_(j-1)>=0. This is an exact scalar definition,
not a solver invocation or a feasibility guess.

Finally the actual additions are
u_(j-1)=u_j+alpha p(theta), y_(j-1)=y_j+alpha q(theta).
Their signs preserve u>=epsilon and y>=1. The new ratio y/u is the
weighted average of y_j/u_j and q/p with nonnegative weights summing

the noncapped root is theta_j and the entire state is unchanged; a
capped state remains unchanged too. No ordering assumption on the
magnitudes of alpha_j is used.

## 7. The one static max-envelope function

Partition the prescribed physical word, without reordering, into
(block_0,b_0,...,block_(k-1),b_(k-1),block_k); let s_i be the ordinary
block sums. For i<k use the preceding construction on the actual steps
of block_i. Define

    D_0=1, ell_0=0,
    D_(i+1)=D_i sigma_i(b_i-1),
    ell_(i+1)=D_i sigma_i(1+Q_i),
    Phi_i(z)=D_i^2 phi_i((z_i-ell_i)/D_i,z_(i+1)/D_i),
    delta_tail=D_k/(1+2s_k),
    Phi_k(z)=delta_tail max{z_k-ell_k,0},
    J(z)=max_(0<=i<=k) Phi_i(z),
    f(x)=min_z[J(z)+||x-z||^2/2].

All D_i and delta_tail are positive, since b_i-1>=epsilon^(-2)>0.
All ell_i are nonnegative. This fixes one finite maximum of affine
planes before the run; it does not splice functions after queries.
Each Phi_i is nonnegative and vanishes at0 by its pre-activation zero
region; the hinge does too. Hence J>=0 and J(0)=0.

Because J is finite, continuous, convex and nonnegative, the quadratic
in its envelope is coercive and strictly convex. It has a unique
minimizer z at each x. The minimizing equation is g=x-z in partial J(z).
For x',z',g' the two subgradient inequalities imply

    ||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>.

For an arbitrary increment w, comparison with the trial proximal point z
gives the upper bound
f(x+w)<=f(x)+<g,w>+||w||^2/2. Subgradient support at z, followed by
expansion at the actual proximal point z' for x+w, gives

    f(x+w)>=f(x)+<g,w>+||w-(z'-z)||^2/2.

These inequalities imply differentiability with gradient g and a
global supporting hyperplane at each x, hence convexity. The displayed
monotonicity inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz give1-Lipschitz gradient.
The minimum is attained and is0 because f>=0 and f(0)=0.
