their original index and cause no exception to the construction.

## 5. One finite-dimensional static function and every physical update

First suppose J<m. Apply Section4 separately in advance to each actual
incoming block Aword_i and its checkpoint b^(i), i=0,...,k-1. All its symbols receive
the subscript i: sigma_i,P_i,Q_i,phi_i,f_i,U_i,Y_i,z_circ,i.
Define positive scales and nonnegative offsets by

    D_0=1, ell_0=0,
    G_i=sigma_i*b^(i)/2
       =b^(i)/(chi*s_i+2*A+epsilon*b^(i)),
    D_(i+1)=D_i*G_i,
    ell_(i+1)=D_i*Y_i,
    delta_tail=D_k/(1+s_k).                           (20)

The basis e_0,...,e_k is the standard orthonormal basis of R^(k+1).
For any delta>0 define the one-sided Huber function

    Hub_delta(z)=0                     if z<=0,
                 z^2/2                 if0<=z<=delta,
                 delta*z-delta^2/2      if z>=delta.

Its continuous derivative is max{0,min{z,delta}}, which is nondecreasing
and1-Lipschitz. The ACTUAL function used in the theorem is

    F_m(x)=(1/2)*sum_(i=0)^(k-1) D_i^2
                    *f_i((x_i-ell_i)/D_i,x_(i+1)/D_i)
           +(1/2)*Hub_(delta_tail)(x_k-ell_k).         (21)

This is a single function fixed before running GD. The finite lists
of planes, implicit backward roots, scales and shifts are mathematical
definitions determined by the entire prescribed word. No trajectory
is replayed or numerically solved to define (21). Its dimension is
exactly k+1=m-J+1 in this nonempty case, finite at every m. Each local
maximum has only finitely many planes even though the auxiliary arc is continuous.

The function is nonnegative and convex. Every ell_i>=0, so at x=0
each local input is in {z_1<=0,z_2>=0}, and the terminal term vanishes.

The cost A in (2) satisfies the useful exact identity

This document defines a NEW scalar functional L_wide. It preserves the
old name L_sp and its restricted domain unchanged. All new algebra needed
below, including the reused hierarchy and mass-deletion ingredients, is
proved jointly here. The sole accepted mathematical input is
fact04219554e41d9750, for the original benchmark ray and saved enclosure.
The unverified geometric construction and independent analytical audit
are provenance, never correctness premises in this scalar proof.

The conclusion is an upper bound for two explicit lower-guarantee
formulas, not for the actual worst-case error W. It does not bound the
stronger exact closest-radius formula(6) of the geometric source, nor
the source-format realization after a closest-minimizer improvement.

## 1. Exact enlarged scalar definition

The immutable geometric source is finding c8fcf4ced5a34046 at
/opt/danus/runtime/projects/gd-exact-profile-20260926/research/shared_evidence/c8fcf4ced5a34046.md,
SHA2564d1e99db853eba3751a3f4761fc2c400c68eacdc9c7912b17c0b0c82d6975d2e.
Its formulas(1),(2),(7),(8) define the following numbers, without needing
any assertion about a function realizing them.

Take independently

    0<epsilon<=1/2, kappa>0.

For every such pair set

    theta_sp=arctan(1/epsilon),
    C=c_sp=sqrt(1+epsilon^2)*exp(kappa*theta_sp),
    d_sp=1-kappa^2,
    T_sp=(exp(d_sp*theta_sp/kappa)-1)/d_sp, 0<kappa<1,
    T_sp=theta_sp/kappa,                   kappa>=1,
    H_sp=C*[1+(1+kappa)*T_sp]-1,
    A=A_sp=epsilon+(H_sp+1)/epsilon,
    a_sp=2*A/C.                                           (1)

C and A are scoped abbreviations, not the accepted benchmark C_n or a
primitive-certificate capacity. The definition includes kappa=1 using
the second branch, with no division by d_sp there. Define exactly

    qmax_sp=1,                                       kappa<=epsilon,
    qmax_sp=sqrt((1+epsilon^2)/(1+kappa^2))
              *exp(kappa*[theta_sp-arctan(1/kappa)]), kappa>epsilon,
    N_sp=max{0,kappa*qmax_sp-epsilon},
    B_sp=1+max{epsilon^(-2),N_sp/epsilon}.                  (2)

No simplification of the general-kappa horizontal-normal price N_sp is
assumed. In particular, this definition does not silently substitute the
smaller old threshold when kappa>1.

Let h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) be any finite nonnegative word at its original
physical length n. A nonempty subset of its original physical indices,
listed in increasing order, induces the actual decomposition

    h=(block_0,b_0,block_1,b_1,...,block_(k-1),b_(k-1),block_k),

where k>=1 and s_i is the ordinary sum of block_i. Empty blocks and
zero physical entries are permitted. One parameter pair is fixed for
the entire selection. Define the two distinct scalar channels

    Phi_M=1/(1+2*s_k)*product_(i=0)^(k-1)
             [(b_i-1)/(C*s_i+max{epsilon*b_i,A})]^2,
             eligible when every b_i>=B_sp;                (3)

    Phi_S=1/[2*(1+s_k)]*product_(i=0)^(k-1)
             [b_i/(C*s_i+2*A+epsilon*b_i)]^2,
             eligible when every b_i>=2*(1+epsilon^(-2)).  (4)

Equation(4) uses C*(a_sp+s_i)=2*A+C*s_i exactly. Its numerator is b_i,
not b_i-1. Its terminal denominator is 2*(1+s_k), not 1+2*s_k.

Write H_base(h)=1/(1+2*sum h). Define

    L_wide(h)=max{H_base(h),
                 sup Phi_M over all pairs and eligible nonempty subsets,
                 sup Phi_S over all pairs and eligible nonempty subsets}. (5)

The supremum of an empty family in(5) means0. The supremum notation does
not presume parameter attainment. No product mixes factors from different
channels. The Huber term is included explicitly; hence the equality
proved below is attained by that term. All constants and denominators in
(1)--(5) are positive on their stated domains.

The source describes(4) as an exact payoff normalized by its specified
minimizer0 and initial distance1. We retain that convention. Interpreting
(3) or(4) as lower bounds for actual W remains conditional on establishing
the full geometry, which is not part of this scalar candidate.

## 2. Word family and the quantitative claims

Put lambda=1+sqrt(2). For a fixed real tau>0 and integer m>tau define

    beta=1-tau/m, c=lambda*(1+tau/m), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    H_(m,tau)=H_m, n_m=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j.                (6)

Every child keeps the SAME enclosing parameters(m,tau). A level is the
index j of a bridge 1+a*c^j, not the physical index of one occurrence.
Only tau=1 is the original diagnostic family; the theorem uses the
different words specified by small tau in(6).

The joint claims to be proved are as follows. For EVERY real
0<tau<=1/4, EVERY integer m>=1536, EVERY parameter pair in(1), and EVERY
nonempty subset of the physical word H_(m,tau), one has

    Phi_M<=1/(1+2*S_m),
    Phi_S<=5/[16*(1+S_m)].                               (7)

In(7) the formulas can even be evaluated on ineligible subsets; the
proof bounds that larger comparison class. Therefore(7) applies, in
particular, to each channel's own actual threshold, including equality.
Consequently

    L_wide(H_(m,tau))=1/(1+2*S_m).                       (8)

Retain the ORIGINAL all-split benchmark, defined for integers n>=0 by

    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4*x*y))/2,
    G(x,y)=2*x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8*x*y)/2,
    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(0<=i<n) Omega(C_i,C_(n-i-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=i<n) G(C_i,B_(n-i-1)),
    U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.                                      (9)

Accepted fact04219554e41d9750 gives the positive finite limit

    B_(2^m-1)/lambda^m -> Z_1.                         (10)

For every fixed0<tau<=1/4 the further claim is

    lim_(m->infinity) B_(n_m)*L_wide(H_(m,tau))
                         =Z_1/(2*exp(tau)).            (11)

In fact, the strict benchmark deficits already hold at EVERY m>=1536:

    B_(n_m)*L_wide(H_(m,1/4))<237/250<1,
    B_(n_m)*L_wide(H_(m,tau))<79/80 for1/5<=tau<=1/4.  (11a)

The corresponding limits are strictly below the same constants. These
claims use only the accepted benchmark enclosure, rederived from its
saved endpoint in Section8. No new benchmark calculation is performed.

## 3. Joint hierarchy identities and the selection mechanism

For fixed(m,tau), put

    r=c*(c-2), v=a/(c-2)=beta/r,
    M_j=1+S_j, d_j=a*c^j, b_j=1+d_j,
    u_j=d_j/M_j, M_max=M_(m-1).                         (12)

Writing x=tau/m and gamma=4+2*sqrt(2), direct expansion gives

    r=1+gamma*x+lambda^2*x^2>1>beta>0.                 (13)

Thus0<v<1 and c>lambda>2. The sum recurrence is
M_(j+1)=2*M_j+a*c^j with M_0=1. Substitution, using a=v*(c-2), proves
by induction that

    M_j=v*c^j+(1-v)*2^j, 0<=j<=m.                     (14)

It follows that

    1<=M_j<=c^j,
    0<u_j<=c-2,
    M_j<=M_max for0<=j<m.                              (15)

For the first two inequalities use c>2 and M_j>=v*c^j. For the last,
the sum recurrence has positive added terms and M_j>0.

Choose ANY currently selected checkpoint having minimum selected level
j. Its immediate complete H_j children contain only levels<j, so neither
child contains a selected checkpoint. If s and t are the actual ordinary
sums immediately before and after this checkpoint, then

    s>=S_j, t>=S_j.                                   (16)

This includes a first or last selected checkpoint: its adjacent ordinary
block is then the true initial or terminal block. Tied minimum levels
cause no problem because each child has strictly smaller levels.

Deleting a checkpoint below means deleting it from the selected subset,
not from the physical word. Its full physical step b is reclassified as
ordinary, so the two ordinary blocks merge to the sum s+b+t. All other
physical indices, step values, and the one parameter pair are retained.
Eligibility of any remaining checkpoint is unchanged.

We prove one minimum-level deletion scheme for both channels under the
same whole-word alternatives

    (I)  C>=r=c*(c-2),
    (II) A>=2*C*M_max,                                (17)

assuming C>=1, A>=2*C and2<c<=5/2. Section7 proves these assumptions
and the dichotomy for the ENTIRE enlarged parameter domain. The two
channel comparisons below are separate; neither is inferred from a
pointwise ordering of(3) and(4).

## 4. Mass channel: exact interior and terminal comparisons

Let b=b_j=1+d be a selected minimum-level checkpoint, with
M=M_j, S=M-1, u=d/M. Then0<u<=1/2 and s,t>=S.
For this channel write Q_M(b)=max{epsilon*b,A}.

If a next selected checkpoint b' exists, put R=Q_M(b'). Cancelling its
positive numerator b'-1 and all unchanged factors shows that deletion
does not lower Phi_M exactly when

    d*[C*(s+b+t)+R] <= (C*s+Q_M(b))*(C*t+R).           (18)

The right side minus the left is increasing in Q_M(b). Its derivatives
with respect to R,s,t are, respectively,

    C*s+Q_M(b)-d,
    C*(C*t+R-d),
    C*(C*s+Q_M(b)-d).

They are positive throughout s,t>=M-1 and Q_M(b),R>=A: indeed
C*(M-1)+A>=C*M>=M>=2*d. Thus its minimum is at
s=t=M-1 and Q_M(b)=R=A. Put z_M=(A-C)/M>=0. Dividing that minimum by
M^2 gives the exact expression

    E_M=C^2-C*u*(2+u)+z_M*(2*C-u)+z_M^2.              (19)

Under(I), u*(2+u)<=c*(c-2)<=C, so every grouped term in(19) is
nonnegative. Under(II),

    z_M=(A-C)/M>=C*(2*M_max-1)/M>=C,

because M<=M_max and M_max>=1. Therefore

    E_M>=C^2-(5/4)*C+C*(2*C-1/2)+C^2
        =4*C^2-(7/4)*C>0.                            (20)

Here u*(2+u)<=5/4 and2*C-u>0 justify each replacement. This proves
the interior deletion comparison in either branch of(17).

If b is the LAST selected checkpoint, the exact comparison is instead

    d^2*[1+2*(s+b+t)]
      <=(C*s+Q_M(b))^2*(1+2*t).                      (21)

Since C*s+Q_M(b)>=s+1, it suffices to bound

    d^2*[1+2*(s+b+t)]/[(s+1)^2*(1+2*t)].              (22)

For fixed s this decreases in t, because the fraction without d^2 is
[1+2*(s+b)/(1+2*t)]/(s+1)^2. Its s derivative after suppressing the
positive constant1+2*t is -2*(s+2*b+2*t)/(s+1)^3<0. Hence(22) is
largest at s=t=M-1. There it equals

    u^2*[(4+2*u)*M-1]/(2*M-1)
      <=u^2*(3+2*u)<=1.                              (23)

For the first inequality, the difference of the cross-multiplied
numerators is2*(1+u)*(M-1)>=0. For the second, u^2*(3+2*u) increases
on[0,1/2] and equals1 at1/2. This terminal comparison needs no
additional choice between(I) and(II).

Repeatedly deleting a currently selected minimum level strictly reduces
the number of selections. The comparisons keep Phi_M nondecreasing
until the empty-selection value1/(1+2*S_m) is reached. This proves
the first inequality in(7) under(17). It is a proof for an arbitrary
finite subset, not an executed recurrence or enumeration.

## 5. Source-format channel: the numerator shift is paid explicitly

Keep b=1+d, M=M_j, u=d/M, and s,t>=M-1 from Section4. Now define

    Q_S(b)=2*A+epsilon*b.

Its numerator is b itself. If a next selected checkpoint b' exists,
write R=Q_S(b'). The exact interior deletion comparison, after cancelling
the unchanged positive b', is

    b*[C*(s+b+t)+R] <= (C*s+Q_S(b))*(C*t+R).           (24)

The difference is increasing in Q_S(b), and its R,s,t derivatives are

    C*s+Q_S(b)-b,
    C*(C*t+R-b),
    C*(C*s+Q_S(b)-b),

respectively. All are positive on the larger comparison region
s,t>=M-1, Q_S(b),R>=2*A. In fact,

    C*(M-1)+2*A-b
      >=C*M+3*C-(M/2+1)>0,                           (25)

using A>=2*C, C>=1, M>=1 and d<=M/2. Therefore the smallest difference
in(24) occurs at s=t=M-1 and Q_S(b)=R=2*A. Define

    q=2*A-C>=3*C.

The minimum is EXACTLY

    F_S=(C*M+q)^2-(d+1)*[C*(2*M+d)+q]
       =M^2*[C^2-C*u*(2+u)]
         +M*[q*(2*C-u)-C*(2+u)]+q^2-q.               (26)

For the first equality, note that the merged physical sum is
2*(M-1)+(d+1)=2*M+d-1, so adding R=2*A yields
C*(2*M+d)+q. The extra1 in b=d+1 is retained in every term of(26).

Under(I), the M^2 coefficient in(26) is nonnegative. Also

    q*(2*C-u)-C*(2+u)
      >=3*C*(2*C-u)-C*(2+u)
       =C*(6*C-4*u-2)>=2*C>0,                       (27)

and q^2-q>=0 because q>=3*C>=3. Thus(24) holds in branch(I).

Under(II), use the first expression in(26). Put z_S=q/M. Since

    q=2*A-C>=C*(4*M_max-1)>=3*C*M,

one has z_S>=3*C. Moreover(d+1)/M<=3/2 and(2*M+d)/M<=5/2. Consequently

    F_S/M^2
      >=(C+z_S)^2-(3/2)*[(5/2)*C+z_S]
       =C^2-(15/4)*C+z_S*(2*C-3/2)+z_S^2
      >=16*C^2-(33/4)*C>0.                          (28)

The last step uses C>=1, so2*C-3/2>0 and substitution z_S>=3*C has
the claimed direction. Its final expression is positive for C>=1.
This proves the interior source-format comparison for both branches.

For a LAST selected checkpoint, deletion replaces the terminal factor
1/[2*(1+t)] by1/[2*(1+s+b+t)]. The exact ratio of the selected
local factor to the deleted local factor is

    R_tail=b^2*(1+s+b+t)/[(C*s+Q_S(b))^2*(1+t)].       (29)

Because Q_S(b)>=2*A>=4*C and C>=1, its denominator satisfies
C*s+Q_S(b)>=s+4. The resulting upper bound for(29) is

    b^2*(1+s+b+t)/[(s+4)^2*(1+t)].                   (30)

For fixed s, the fraction without b^2 equals
[1+(s+b)/(1+t)]/(s+4)^2 and decreases with t. Its derivative in s,
with the positive constant1+t suppressed, is

    (2-s-2*b-2*t)/(s+4)^3<0,

since b=1+d>1. Thus(30) is largest at s=t=M-1, where

    R_tail
      <=(d+1)^2*(2*M+d)/[(M+3)^2*M]
      <=(5/2)*[(M/2+1)/(M+3)]^2
      <=5/8.                                       (31)

For the last two inequalities use d<=M/2 and
M/2+1<=(M+3)/2. This is a uniform quantitative terminal contraction.
It has not been replaced by the mass-channel terminal comparison.

## 6. Finite pruning and the two different empty-selection values

For the source channel only, define the empty-product bookkeeping value
to be1/[2*(1+S_m)]. This is the value of its own displayed formula after
all checkpoints are removed from the subset. It is a comparison sink;
the functional(5) retains its actual Huber baseline1/(1+2*S_m).

Start with any nonempty selected subset, and repeatedly choose a minimum
currently selected level. At an interior deletion use(24); at a terminal
deletion use(31). Every remaining subset still has the complete children
property(16). At least one deletion is terminal, since the last remaining
checkpoint is terminal. All factors outside the local comparison are
unchanged and positive. Multiplying the comparisons therefore gives

    Phi_S<=(5/8)*1/[2*(1+S_m)]
         =5/[16*(1+S_m)].                            (32)

If additional deletions are terminal, each contributes another factor
at most5/8; only one such factor was needed in(32). The mass pruning in
Section4 gives its own bound1/(1+2*S_m). Finally

    5/[16*(1+S_m)]<1/(1+2*S_m),                      (33)

because cross multiplication reduces to5*(1+2*S_m)<16*(1+S_m).
Thus under the hypotheses and dichotomy(17), both channels are bounded
by the Huber baseline, and that baseline attains L_wide.

## 3. Definitions for reading the audit independently

All spaces are finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces; all norms and
inner products below are Euclidean. Log denotes the natural logarithm.
Fix lambda=1+sqrt(2). For each enclosing integer m>=6 put

    beta=1-1/m, c=lambda(1+1/m), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    b_j=1+a*c^j, n_m=2^m-1, S_j=sum H_j.

All H_j in this paragraph depend on this SAME m. The original benchmark
has C_0=B_0=1 and, for n>=1, takes the maximum over every integer split
0<=r<n of

    C_n=max Omega(C_r,C_(n-r-1)),
    B_n=max G(C_r,B_(n-r-1)),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2, U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

The accepted constant is Z_1=lim_m B_(2^m-1)/lambda^m. The sole accepted
predecessor gives its existence, positivity, finiteness, and lower bound
Z_1>=lambda^(-r)B_(2^r-1) for every integer r>=0.

For the geometric construction define

    K=14/5, E=1/100, kappa=K/m, epsilon=E/m,
    theta_sp=arctan(1/epsilon),
    chi=sqrt(1+epsilon^2) exp(kappa*theta_sp), d=1-kappa^2,
    T=(exp(d*theta_sp/kappa)-1)/d,
    H=chi[1+(1+kappa)T]-1, A=epsilon+(H+1)/epsilon,
    R_cut=max(A/epsilon,1+2/epsilon^2),
    J=max(1,ceil(log(R_cut/a)/log c)).

The unsubscripted H in these costs is not a word. If J<m, select the
first occurrences of levels J,...,m-1 and let k=m-J. The selected values
are b^(i)=b_(J+i), indexed0<=i<k. Their incoming ordinary sums are
s_0=S_J and s_i=S_(J+i-1) for 1<=i<k; the terminal ordinary sum is
s_k=S_(m-1). If J>=m, selection is empty and s_0=S_m.

The two finite scalar quantities audited are

    P_m=1/[2(1+s_k)] product_(i<k)
                  [b^(i)/(chi*s_i+2A+epsilon*b^(i))]^2,
    P5_m=1/(1+2s_k) product_(i<k)
                  [(b^(i)-1)/(chi*s_i+max(epsilon*b^(i),A))]^2.

The first is the exact payoff of the constructed objective about0. The
second is only a scalar comparison device in this audit. In the empty
case the actual first expression is 1/[2(1+S_m)]. The worst-case quantity
W_n(h) is the supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over
all such smooth convex functions, finite dimensions, minimizers and
initial points distinct from those minimizers, under
x_(t+1)=x_t-(h_t/L)grad f(x_t).

## 5. Backward arc: direct check of every projection case

For 0<=u<=theta_sp write

    e(u)=(cos u,-sin u), t(u)=(-sin u,-cos u),
    R(u)=chi exp(-kappa*u), v(u)=R(u)e(u)=(p(u),-q(u)),
    n(u)=e(u)+kappa*t(u).

Then v(0)=(chi,0), v(theta_sp)=(epsilon,-1). Since theta_sp<pi/2,
p>0, q>=0, and q/p=tan u<=1/epsilon. Differentiating p gives
p'=-R(kappa*cos u+sin u)<0, hence epsilon<=p<=chi. The vertical
component q can exceed1; this does not affect the proof.

For any two allowed angles u,w, Delta=w-u lies in(-pi/2,pi/2). The
ratio of <n(u),v(w)> to R(u) is

    exp(-kappa*Delta)(cos Delta+kappa*sin Delta).

Its derivative is-(1+kappa^2)exp(-kappa*Delta)sin Delta. It increases
up to Delta=0 and decreases after 0, where it equals1. Since the origin
has inner product0<R(u), n(u) supports the convex hull K_arc of 0 and
the ENTIRE arc. At u=0, the vector(0,1) supports this hull as well.
This tests remote arc pairs, rather than only neighboring directions.

For any finite list of nonnegative local steps alpha_1,...,alpha_N,
the terminal backward state is r_N=v_N=(epsilon,-1). Write each state
r_j=(U_j,-Y_j). Invariants are U_j>=epsilon, Y_j>=1 and
Y_j/U_j<=1/epsilon. For an uncapped state at angle u_j,

    r_j=R(u_j)[(1+a_j)e(u_j)+kappa*a_j*t(u_j)], a_j>=0.

For step alpha=alpha_j, the cap condition is
Y_j<=kappa[U_j+(alpha-1)chi]. With mu=U_j+(alpha-1)chi, this implies
mu>0 and

    r_(j-1)-v(0)=mu*n(0)+(0,kappa*mu-Y_j),
    r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha*v(0).

Both coefficients describe supporting normals, so v(0) is a
projection. The resulting inequality Y_(j-1)<=kappa(U_(j-1)-chi)
makes the cap condition true at every earlier nonnegative step. Its
vertical coordinate stays fixed.

If the cap condition fails, the state cannot already be capped. Put

    F_j(u)=<r_j,e(u)-t(u)/kappa>/R(u).

One has F_j(u_j)=1,
F_j(0)=(U_j-Y_j/kappa)/chi<1-alpha, and

    F_j'(u)=(kappa+kappa^(-1))(U_j*cos u+Y_j*sin u)/R(u)>0.

Thus F_j(u)=1-alpha has exactly one solution in(0,u_j], including
u=u_j if alpha=0. To check the normal coefficient, the representation
of r_j gives, for 0<=u<=u_j,

    <r_j,t(u)>=R(u_j)[(1+a_j)sin(u_j-u)
                              +kappa*a_j*cos(u_j-u)]>=0.

At the root, F_j(u)=1-alpha is equivalent to

    r_j+(alpha-1)v(u)=(<r_j,t(u)>/kappa)n(u).

This is a nonnegative supporting normal. Adding v(u) establishes the
required representation and projection at the previous state. Adding
alpha(p,-q) preserves all three invariants because p>=epsilon*q.
The elementary expansion of squared distances confirms that a
supporting-normal inequality implies Euclidean projection. No inverse
GD map was assumed globally invertible.

For two successive uncapped angles with Delta=u_new-u_old>=0, their
t(u_old) components give

    a_old=B_Delta+A_Delta*a_new,
    A_Delta=exp(-kappa*Delta)(cos Delta+sin Delta/kappa),
    B_Delta=exp(-kappa*Delta)sin Delta/kappa.

Both are nonnegative. With d=1-kappa^2>0, differentiating A_Delta
gives A_Delta'-(d/kappa)A_Delta<=0, so A_Delta<=exp(d*Delta/kappa).
Also B_Delta<=Delta/kappa and 1+dB_Delta<=exp(d*Delta/kappa). Hence

    1+d*a_old<=exp(d*Delta/kappa)(1+d*a_new).

Telescoping from a_N=0 over a total angle no greater than theta_sp
yields a_j<=T. Consequently the positive vertical coordinate is at
most chi[1+(1+kappa)T]=1+H. Caps do not increase it. If
P=sum alpha_j*p(u_(j-1)) and Q=sum alpha_j*q(u_(j-1)), then

    r_0=(epsilon+P,-1-Q),
    0<=P<=chi*sum alpha_j, 0<=Q<=H, P>=epsilon*Q.

These estimates are uniform in the number and size of the local steps.
This is the point that lets the construction include every ordinary
step in each long physical gap without a cumulative geometric error.

## 6. Finite local function, static global assembly, and exact payoff

For a physical block of sum s followed by checkpoint b, use the above
backward construction with its actual entries divided by2, so its local
sum is s/2. Put b_loc=b/2 and

    sigma=1/(chi*s/2+epsilon*b/2+A),
    z_circ=(1,0)-sigma(epsilon+P,-1-Q),
    U=1-sigma(P+epsilon*b_loc), Y=sigma*Q,
    V_fin={0,v(0),v_0,...,v_N},
    phi(z)=sigma*max_(v in V_fin)<v,z-z_circ>,
    f_loc(x)=min_z[phi(z)+||x-z||^2/2].

Here sigma>0, U>=0, Y>=0. The allowance gives

    sigma[P+epsilon+(1+Q)/epsilon]<=1.

The minimum in f_loc exists uniquely: phi is finite, convex and
nonnegative, while the quadratic makes the objective coercive and
strictly convex. If z is the minimizer and g=x-z, the subgradient
condition is g in partial phi(z). It is sufficient by the completed
square. For necessity, test the minimum at z+t(w-z), use convexity,
divide by t and let t decrease to 0. Thus no unstated envelope theorem
is required.

For two such pairs, adding subgradient inequalities gives

value bound f_loc(x+w)<=f_loc(x)+<g,w>+||w||^2/2. Subgradient support

    f_loc(x+w)>=f_loc(x)+<g,w>+||w-(z'-z)||^2/2.

These inequalities establish differentiability, global supporting
affines and convexity; the first displayed inequality gives the

For x_j=z_circ+sigma*r_j and z_j=x_j-sigma*v_j, the projection inequality

For each nonzero v=(p,-q) in V_fin,

The first uses q/p<=1/epsilon and the allowance; the second uses

Apply this construction in advance to each incoming block i and use

evidence:
# Correlated Euclidean stages: a finite calibration and an exact remote cycle

Status: JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical draft, max61. No assertion below is a
new accepted fact. This is one frame mechanism and one explicit terminal
correction, within TASK.md and guidance42998ccb0a64c7b8; the later guidance
2915a98c60a7ec96 leaves this allocation unchanged. No mathematical program,
numerical experiment, solver, executed recurrence, formal submission,
installation, consult or sub-agent was used.

The result is a complete six-step, two-checkpoint static-function
calibration with changing gradients on BOTH incoming ordinary blocks,
followed by a value-independent three-query obstruction to the natural
repeated gluing rule. The calibration is not an all-word checkpoint lemma.
The three-query obstruction does not exclude every correlated realization.

All displayed calculations are joint proofs in this draft, not deductions
from unverified shared claims. Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 is used for the
project's directed-row convention and scope. We also prove the required
envelope and row identities directly. Throughout the payoff is W=2R:

    2(f(x_n)-min f)/(L dist(x_0,argmin f)^2).

## 1. Actual frame, primal metric, dual metric, and support arcs

Let e_0,...,e_k be an orthonormal basis and 0<=r<1. Write
s=sqrt(1-r^2), u_0=e_0 and u_(i+1)=-r*u_i+s*e_(i+1).
Here r is the task's r_corr, not a covariance law for queried gradients.
Induction, using the new coordinate e_(i+1), gives

    ||u_i||=1, <u_i,u_j>=(-r)^|i-j|.                     (1)

Thus, for arbitrary real coefficients a_i,

    ||sum_i a_i u_i||^2
      =sum_i a_i^2+2 sum_(i<j) (-r)^(j-i) a_i a_j.      (2)

The coefficients are NOT orthonormal coordinates. If b_i=<u_i,x>,
the orthonormal coordinates of x satisfy

    <e_0,x>=b_0,
    <e_i,x>=(b_i+r*b_(i-1))/s, i>=1,
    ||x||^2=b_0^2+sum_(i=1)^k (b_i+r*b_(i-1))^2/s^2. (3)

For k>=1 the inverse of the Gram matrix in (1) is tridiagonal:
its two end diagonal entries are 1/s^2, its interior diagonal entries
are (1+r^2)/s^2, and each adjacent off-diagonal entry is r/s^2.
This follows by expanding (3), since b=U^T x for U with columns u_i.
For k=0 both matrices are [1]. In particular constant positive inner
products b_i=d require EXACTLY

    ||x||^2=d^2[1+k*(1+r)/(1-r)].                       (4)

This is a conditional radius cost for that prescribed array, not a
claim that every correlated witness must pay it.

Absolute row sums of the Gram matrix and its inverse give

    (1-r)/(1+r)<=lambda_min(Gram)
       <=lambda_max(Gram)<=(1+r)/(1-r).                (5)

For fixed r and growing k both extremes are approached: insert the
constant and alternating-sign coefficient columns in (2), divide by
k+1, and sum the resulting geometric series. The Rayleigh quotients
tend (1-r)/(1+r) and (1+r)/(1-r), respectively. Consequently the
conditioning can approach ((1+r)/(1-r))^2. If k*(1-r) tends to0,
the alternating-sign Rayleigh quotient is (k+1)(1+o(1)); an interior
diagonal entry of the inverse also implies
lambda_min(Gram)<=s^2/(1+r^2) for k>=2. Both types of degeneration
are relevant, depending on the joint limit.

Fix epsilon>0 and define the endpoint and its actual Euclidean data by

    w_i=epsilon*u_i-u_(i+1)
       =(epsilon+r)*u_i-s*e_(i+1),
    omega=sqrt(1+epsilon^2+2*epsilon*r),
    theta=arctan(s/(epsilon+r)).                        (6)

In the ORTHONORMAL plane (u_i,e_(i+1)), put

    E_i(t)=cos(t)*u_i-sin(t)*e_(i+1),
    T_i(t)=-sin(t)*u_i-cos(t)*e_(i+1),
    c=omega*exp(kappa*theta),
    V_i(t)=c*exp(-kappa*t)*E_i(t), 0<=t<=theta,
    N_i(t)=E_i(t)+kappa*T_i(t), kappa>0.               (7)

The endpoints are c*u_i and w_i. If delta=z-t, then

    <N_i(t),V_i(z)>/[c*exp(-kappa*t)]
      =exp(-kappa*delta)*(cos(delta)+kappa*sin(delta)).

Its derivative in delta is
-(1+kappa^2)*exp(-kappa*delta)*sin(delta). As |delta|<pi/2,
the expression has its maximum1 at0; its inner product with the
additional slope0 is strictly smaller. Thus N_i(t) supports the
convex hull of0 and the whole arc at V_i(t). At t=0, e_(i+1) is
also a supporting normal. This verifies the actual Euclidean arc.

Writing V_i(t)=p*u_i-q*u_(i+1) gives

    p=c*exp(-kappa*t)*(cos(t)-r*sin(t)/s),
    q=c*exp(-kappa*t)*sin(t)/s,
    p>=epsilon*q>=0, p<=c.                            (8)

For t>0 the first inequality follows from cot(t)>=(epsilon+r)/s;
at t=0 it follows from p=c,q=0.
For two such slopes in consecutive stages one has EXACTLY

    <p*u_i-q*u_(i+1), p'*u_(i+1)-q'*u_(i+2)>
       =-(r*p+q)*(p'+r*q').                           (9)

For stage separation d>=1 the right side is multiplied by
(-r)^(d-1). This follows by substituting (1) into the four terms.
In particular adjacent slopes have negative inner products, while
slopes two stages apart have positive ones when r>0. No assertion
about Markov dependence of all gradients follows from (9).

## 2. Two genuinely changing ordinary steps and their exact values

This section specifies a finite block without root finding. Let
Delta=theta/2 and define

    A_D=exp(-kappa*Delta)*(cos(Delta)+sin(Delta)/kappa),
    B_D=exp(-kappa*Delta)*sin(Delta)/kappa,
    t_0=0, t_1=B_D, t_2=B_D*(1+A_D),
    theta_l=theta-l*Delta, l=0,1,2,
    R_l=c*exp(-kappa*theta_l),
    v_(i,l)=R_l*E_i(theta_l),
    r_(i,l)=R_l*((1+t_l)*E_i(theta_l)
                            +kappa*t_l*T_i(theta_l)),
    alpha_l=1-exp(-kappa*Delta)*cos(Delta)+B_D
                            +(1+kappa^2)*B_D*t_(l-1), l=1,2. (10)

Both alpha_l are strictly positive. Resolving radial and tangent
components in the basis (E_i(theta_l),T_i(theta_l)) proves

    r_(i,l)-r_(i,l-1)=alpha_l*v_(i,l), l=1,2.          (11)

Indeed, cancellation of the tangent component is exactly
t_l=B_D+A_D*t_(l-1), and the remaining radial coefficient is alpha_l.
The vector r_(i,l)-v_(i,l)=R_l*t_l*N_i(theta_l) supports the
finite slope hull conv{0,v_(i,0),v_(i,1),v_(i,2)} at v_(i,l).
Hence the chronological ordinary word (alpha_2,alpha_1) has gradients
v_(i,2),v_(i,1), followed at its checkpoint query by v_(i,0)=w_i.
These three gradients have different directions when r<1.

Use the following exact coefficients of its initial state:

    r_(i,2)=A*u_i-B*u_(i+1),
    B=c*kappa*t_2/s,
    A=c*(1+t_2)-r*B,
    Z=A+r*B=c*(1+t_2),
    R0^2=||r_(i,2)||^2
         =c^2*((1+t_2)^2+kappa^2*t_2^2).              (12)

By (11), r_(i,2)=w_i+alpha_1*v_(i,1)+alpha_2*v_(i,2).
Consequently A>=epsilon, B>=1 and A-epsilon*B>=0, despite the
subtraction in the formula defining A. The same positive combination
also shows ||r_(i,l)||<=R0: all arc pairs have positive inner product,
and the backward additions in (11) strictly increase the norm.

For any scale a>0 and center C define the finite local nonsmooth piece

    phi_(i,a,C)(y)=max{0, a*<v_(i,l),y-C>:l=0,1,2}.   (13)

At x=C+a*r_(i,l), its envelope with parameter1 has

    g=a*v_(i,l), y=x-g,
    phi_(i,a,C)(y)=a^2*R_l^2*t_l,

## 5. Local activation, transfer, radius, and turning costs

The following accounts for the apparent small-angle gain and its
limits. It does not turn the failed repeated rule into a lower bound.

For a general ordered nonnegative ordinary word, a backward arc
trajectory can be constructed in the actual orthonormal plane.
Start at w=(epsilon+r,-s). Suppose the current backward point is
(X,-Y), projected to V(theta_j), with positive X,Y. For a step alpha,
if

    Y<=kappa*[X+(alpha-1)*c],

the preceding projection is c*u and the preceding point is obtained
by adding alpha*c*u. Put mu=X+(alpha-1)*c; its normal is
mu*N(0)+(kappa*mu-Y)*e_new, with nonnegative coefficients.
Otherwise choose the unique angle t in (0,theta_j] for which

    <(X,-Y),E(t)-T(t)/kappa>/[c*exp(-kappa*t)]=1-alpha. (44)

The left side equals1 at theta_j. Its value at0 is
(X-Y/kappa)/c<1-alpha, and its derivative is
(kappa+1/kappa)*(X*cos(t)+Y*sin(t))/[c*exp(-kappa*t)]>0.
The root therefore exists uniquely. Resolving radial and tangent
components shows that adding alpha*V(t) gives a nonnegative
supporting normal at that slope. The tangent coefficient is
nonnegative because the polar angle of the current point is at
least theta_j and the new angle is no larger. Backward addition
preserves X>0,Y>0 and Y/X<=s/(epsilon+r). A capped point stays
capped in all earlier steps. These observations inductively prove
the asserted local construction, including alpha=0.

At an uncapped point use the representation R*((1+t)*E+kappa*t*T).
For two consecutive backward angles separated by Delta>=0, its
normal coefficient obeys exactly

    t_old=B(Delta)+A(Delta)*t_new,
    A(Delta)=exp(-kappa*Delta)*(cos(Delta)+sin(Delta)/kappa),
    B(Delta)=exp(-kappa*Delta)*sin(Delta)/kappa.        (45)

Let d0=1-kappa^2. Differentiation gives
A'-(d0/kappa)*A=-(1+1/kappa^2)*exp(-kappa*Delta)*sin(Delta)<=0.
For kappa<1, A<=exp(d0*Delta/kappa) and
1+d0*B<=exp(d0*Delta/kappa); the latter follows from
B<=Delta/kappa and exp(t)>=1+t. Hence telescoping (45) yields

    t<=T=[exp((1-kappa^2)*theta/kappa)-1]/(1-kappa^2).

For kappa>=1, A<=1 and B<=Delta/kappa instead give t<=T=theta/kappa.
These bounds also bound the vertical coordinate at the first cap,
which is unchanged by subsequent backward cap additions.

Write the resulting initial point as A_b*u_i-B_b*u_(i+1), and let
S be the physical sum of this ordinary block. Equation (8) implies

    A_b=epsilon+P, B_b=1+Q,
    0<=P<=c*S, Q>=0, P>=epsilon*Q,
    B_b<=Bmax=c*[(1+T)/omega+(kappa/s)*T].             (46)

the downward orthonormal coordinate R*((1+t)*sin(t)+kappa*t*cos(t)),

If the local trajectory starts at D*u_i, is scaled by a, and its

The full body K_m is the convex hull of these 2^m vectors, in dimension

have zero sum and are pairwise orthogonal: disjoint subtrees have zero
product; a descendant's two signs cancel on an ancestor's constant

Let K_scaled=delta*K_m and
F_scaled(x)=max_(g in K_scaled)(<x,g>-||g||^2/2).

The projection characterization is <x-g,v-g><=0 for every vertex v.
Necessity follows by a derivative along the segment from g to v;

normal inequalities at x,x' gives ||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>, proving
1-Lipschitz continuity. The maximizing formulas sandwich

<P_(delta*K_m)(x+d)-g,d>, bounded by ||d||^2. Hence F_scaled is convex
and differentiable with the stated gradient and global smoothness L=1.
Inside the body the gradient equals x; an open ball is contained there,
so no smaller global Lipschitz constant is possible. Every gradient has
norm at most delta by convexity and the unit leaf norms. Along t*v_left

# Actual closest-distance spiral payoffs at arbitrary checkpoint count

Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical draft, with the precise scope
stated in Section 12. Worker max2, one allocated round54, plan
5d2474e58e95821e, master_guidance1886f8b90c7bdbb9. No formal gate is
authorized. No assertion in this file is a newly accepted fact.

The source realization is treated for every allowed parameter pair and
every eligible ordered selection, without a checkpoint-count restriction.
The main realization is treated at arbitrary count on the parameter band
defined in Section 9. Its complementary band remains open.

The four recalled findings172014083da57ddf,59d88015afb74486,
717b541e05f4484f,c8fcf4ced5a34046 are provenance and warnings, not proof
premises. Every new geometric and comparison ingredient needed here is
proved jointly below. Accepted fact04219554e41d9750 is used only for the
original benchmark and its saved enclosure in Section 11. Accepted
fact5b7ff4253c38b90a concerns the original tau=1 family and is not applied
to the small-tau words considered here.

## 1. Physical words, parameters, and conventions

All norms and inner products are Euclidean. A subscripted e_i denotes
the standard coordinate vector in the dimension of its occurrence;
the explicitly defined planar e(theta) below is a separate notation.
For a finite nonnegative
word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), the physical iteration at advertised smoothness
one is x_(t+1)=x_t-h_t grad f(x_t). Define its actual closest-distance
payoff by

    E(f,h)=2(f(x_n)-min f)/dist(x_0,argmin f)^2.

The construction always has positive initial distance. Its advertised
smoothness remains one; it is not retuned to a smaller Lipschitz constant.
Multiplying f by any L>0 and using h_t/L preserves all points and E.
W_n(h) is the supremum over the original full class of such instances;
an upper bound for the constructed family is not an upper bound on W_n.

Write a selection of k checkpoints in original physical order as

    h=(block_0,b_0,block_1,b_1,...,block_(k-1),b_(k-1),block_k),

where s_i=sum block_i. An ordinary block may be empty, consist of zeros,
or contain arbitrarily large steps. One pair of independent parameters
is fixed for the entire selection:

    kappa>0, 0<epsilon<=1/2,
    theta_sp=arctan(1/epsilon),
    C=chi=sqrt(1+epsilon^2) exp(kappa theta_sp),
    T=(exp((1-kappa^2)theta_sp/kappa)-1)/(1-kappa^2),  kappa<1,
    T=theta_sp/kappa,                                kappa>=1,
    H_sp=C[1+(1+kappa)T]-1,
    A=A_sp=epsilon+(1+H_sp)/epsilon.                     (1)

The two branches for T agree continuously at kappa=1. C is an arc
constant, not a benchmark denominator C_n; A is an activation allowance,
not a primitive-certificate capacity. In particular C>1 and A>=2C.

The source realization requires

    b_i>=2(1+epsilon^(-2)) for every selected i.          (2)

For the main realization define

    qmax=1,                                         kappa<=epsilon,
    qmax=sqrt((1+epsilon^2)/(1+kappa^2))
         exp(kappa[theta_sp-arctan(1/kappa)]),        kappa>epsilon,
    N_sp=max(0,kappa qmax-epsilon),
    B_sp=1+max(epsilon^(-2),N_sp/epsilon),

and require b_i>=B_sp. All thresholds include equality, and the kappa>1
normal correction is retained.

The physical hierarchy is fixed by an enclosing integer m>=1536 and
real 0<tau<=1/4:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-tau/m,
    c=lambda(1+tau/m), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    H_(m,tau)=H_m, S_j=sum H_j, n_m=2^m-1.              (3)

Every child uses this same enclosing(m,tau). No physical entry is
removed or reordered. Let H_base(h)=1/(1+2 sum h).

## 2. Actual backward blocks, including zeros and caps

For 0<=theta<=theta_sp put

    R(theta)=C exp(-kappa theta),
    e(theta)=(cos theta,-sin theta),
    t(theta)=(-sin theta,-cos theta),
    v(theta)=R(theta)e(theta)=(p(theta),-q(theta)),
    n(theta)=e(theta)+kappa t(theta),
    K=conv({0} union {v(theta):0<=theta<=theta_sp}).

The endpoints are (C,0) and (epsilon,-1). With Delta=phi-theta,

    <n(theta),v(phi)>/R(theta)
       =exp(-kappa Delta)(cos Delta+kappa sin Delta).

Its derivative in Delta is
-(1+kappa^2)exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta. Since |Delta|<pi/2,
its maximum is one at zero. The value at the added point0 is zero.
Thus n(theta) supports K at v(theta); (0,1) also supports K at(C,0).
Differentiation gives

    p'=-R(kappa cos theta+sin theta)<0,
    q'=R(cos theta-kappa sin theta),
    p>=epsilon, q>=0, p>=epsilon q.                    (4)

The sign of q' proves the qmax formula in Section 1.

For an actual local chronological list alpha_1,...,alpha_r, alpha_j>=0,
set r_r=v_r=(epsilon,-1). Given r_j=(u_j,-y_j) and its projected arc
point v_j=v(theta_j), use alpha=alpha_j. If

    y_j<=kappa[u_j+(alpha-1)C],                          (5)

set v_(j-1)=(C,0), r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha(C,0). Otherwise choose the unique
theta in(0,theta_j] solving

    <r_j,e(theta)-kappa^(-1)t(theta)>/R(theta)=1-alpha,  (6)

and set v_(j-1)=v(theta), r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha v(theta).
These definitions specify real numbers; no root search is executed.

Here is the existence and projection proof. Inductively
u_j>=epsilon, y_j>=1, y_j/u_j<=1/epsilon. Before a cap the stronger
representation is

    r_j=R(theta_j)[(1+nu_j)e(theta_j)+kappa nu_j t(theta_j)],
    nu_j>=0.                                           (7)

It holds at the endpoint with nu_r=0. If(5) holds, put
mu=u_j+(alpha-1)C>=y_j/kappa>0. Then

    r_(j-1)-v(0)=mu n(0)+(0,kappa mu-y_j),

a nonnegative combination of supporting normals. Projection follows.
The same formula gives y_(j-1)<=kappa(u_(j-1)-C), so every earlier
backward step is capped, including zero steps.

If(5) fails, the current state is uncapped. The left side of(6) is one
at theta_j by(7), is less than1-alpha at zero, and has derivative
(kappa+kappa^(-1))(u_j cos theta+y_j sin theta)/R(theta)>0. There is
exactly one root, including theta=theta_j when alpha=0. Representation
(7) shows that the polar angle of r_j is at least theta_j. Consequently
<r_j,t(theta)>=0 at the root. Equation(6) makes
r_j+(alpha-1)v(theta) a nonnegative multiple of n(theta), proving the
preceding projection and(7). Adding alpha(p,-q), using(4), preserves
the stated bounds on u_j,y_j and their ratio.

Define the actual outputs

    P=sum_j alpha_j p(theta_(j-1)),
    Q=sum_j alpha_j q(theta_(j-1)), s_loc=sum_j alpha_j.

Then r_0=(epsilon+P,-1-Q), P>=epsilon Q, P<=Cs_loc.
For consecutive uncapped angles theta_old<=theta_new let
Delta=theta_new-theta_old. Resolving the backward equation along
t(theta_old) gives the exact scalar relation

    nu_old=B_D+A_D nu_new,
    A_D=exp(-kappa Delta)(cos Delta+sin Delta/kappa),
    B_D=exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta/kappa.                (8)

Both coefficients are nonnegative. For d=1-kappa^2,
A_D'-(d/kappa)A_D=-(1+kappa^(-2))exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta<=0.
If kappa<1, then A_D<=exp(d Delta/kappa), B_D<=Delta/kappa, and
1+dB_D<=exp(d Delta/kappa). Telescoping
1+d nu_old<=exp(d Delta/kappa)(1+d nu_new) proves nu_j<=T.
If kappa>=1, A_D<=1 and B_D<=Delta/kappa give nu_j<=T directly by
summing angle differences. Therefore every uncapped state has
y_j<=C[1+(1+kappa)T]. A cap leaves y unchanged. We have proved

    0<=Q<=H_sp, P>=epsilon Q, 0<=P<=Cs_loc.             (9)

Two lower bounds from the actual slopes will supply UPPER payoff bounds:

    p(theta)+q(theta)>=1, P+Q>=s_loc,
    (epsilon+P)^2+(1+Q)^2 >=(1+epsilon+s_loc)^2/2.       (10)

Indeed R(theta)>=sqrt(1+epsilon^2)>=1 and cos theta+sin theta>=1.
The quadratic inequality is (x+y)^2<=2(x^2+y^2). It is an inequality
for actual chronological outputs, not a claim they depend only on s_loc.

For the main assembly we also need y_j>=q_j and u_j-p_j>=-N_sp.
The first follows from(7), since
y_j-q_j=R nu_j(sin theta_j+kappa cos theta_j)>=0; at a cap q_j=0.
A nonnegative horizontal normal gives u_j>=p_j. Otherwise
theta_j>arctan(1/kappa), so p_j<=kappa qmax while u_j>=epsilon.
At a cap u_j>=C. This proves both estimates for every kappa>0.

## 3. Finite local functions and their exact zero wedges

Take a local checkpoint b_loc>=1+epsilon^(-2), and a positive sigma
satisfying

    sigma(P+epsilon b_loc)<=1,
    sigma[P+epsilon+(1+Q)/epsilon]<=1.                  (11)

Let

    z_circ=(1-sigma(epsilon+P),sigma(1+Q))=(c_1,c_2),
    U=1-sigma(P+epsilon b_loc), Y=sigma Q,
    V={0,v(0),v_0,...,v_r},
    phi(z)=sigma max_(v in V)<v,z-z_circ>,
    f_loc(x)=min_z[phi(z)+||x-z||^2/2].                 (12)

Every plane remains in V, including both endpoints and every actual
projected slope. Since
(p,-q)=[(p-epsilon q)/C](C,0)+q(epsilon,-1), its coefficients are
nonnegative. Thus the exact zero set of phi is

    Z_phi={z:z_1<=c_1, epsilon(z_1-c_1)-(z_2-c_2)<=0}.  (13)

The two endpoint planes prove necessity and the conic representation
proves sufficiency. Formula(11) gives phi=0 on z_1<=0,z_2>=0.
Also <v,(U,Y)-z_circ>=sigma[(1-b_loc)epsilon p+q]<=0, so
phi(U,y)=0 for all y>=Y. In particular U>=0.

For clarity, the envelope properties used here have elementary proofs.
A nonnegative finite affine maximum J having a zero has a unique
proximal minimizer z at each x, by coercivity and strict convexity of
J(z)+||x-z||^2/2. Put g=x-z; its optimality condition is g in partial J(z).
For another pair z',g', subgradient monotonicity gives
||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>. Using z as a trial point gives
env_1 J(x+w)<=env_1 J(x)+<g,w>+||w||^2/2; if z' is the new proximal
point, the subgradient at z gives
env_1 J(x+w)>=env_1 J(x)+<g,w>+||w-(z'-z)||^2/2. These prove convexity,
differentiability, gradient g, and 1-Lipschitz gradient. Attainment and
nonnegativity prove argmin(env_1 J)={J=0}, with minimum zero.

At x_j=z_circ+sigma r_j the point x_j-sigma v_j is proximal: the
projection inequality against all v in V makes sigma v_j an active
subgradient of phi there. The actual local gradient is sigma v_j.
Consequently the local path starts at(1,0), follows every alpha_j,
reaches(1-sigma P,sigma Q), and the local checkpoint b_loc sends it to
(U,Y+sigma b_loc). Throughout the ordinary block its first coordinate
is at least U and its second belongs to[0,Y].

## 4. Source realization: one static function and every physical step

For every i<k apply Section 2 to block_i with each physical step divided
by2. In Sections4--8, P_i,Q_i mean precisely these HALF-step outputs.
Use the local checkpoint b_loc=b_i/2 and the unchanged scale

    sigma'_i=1/[Cs_i/2+epsilon b_i/2+A].                (14)

Equations(9),(1) prove both conditions(11). Define primed local objects
phi'_i,c'_(i,1),c'_(i,2),U'_i,Y'_i from(12) and let f_i=env_1 phi'_i.
Set

    G_i=sigma'_i b_i/2=b_i/(Cs_i+2A+epsilon b_i),
    D'_0=1, ell'_0=0,
    D'_(i+1)=D'_i G_i, ell'_(i+1)=D'_i sigma'_i Q_i,
    delta'=D'_k/(1+s_k).                               (15)

Define Hub_d(z) to be0 for z<=0, z^2/2 for0<=z<=d, and
dz-d^2/2 for z>=d. Its derivative is respectively0,z,d, a continuous
nondecreasing 1-Lipschitz function. On R^(k+1), from x_0=e_0, use exactly

    F(x)=(1/2)sum_(i<k)(D'_i)^2
             f_i((x_i-ell'_i)/D'_i,x_(i+1)/D'_i)
                     +(1/2)Hub_(delta')(x_k-ell'_k).    (16)

This function is fixed before its run. Each term is convex and
nonnegative; F(0)=0 by(13). Every scaled local term is 1-smooth on its
two coordinates before multiplication by1/2. Their quadratic upper
bounds count each coordinate at most twice, including the last hinge.
Therefore F(x+w)<=F(x)+<grad F(x),w>+||w||^2/2. For convex F this implies

    F(x)-F(y)-<grad F(y),x-y>
                        >=||grad F(x)-grad F(y)||^2/2. (17)

To prove it, apply the upper bound to V(z)=F(z)-<grad F(y),z> at x
with w=-grad V(x); y minimizes V. Adding(17) and its exchanged version
proves that grad F is 1-Lipschitz.

At the start of stage i the frozen coordinates are ell'_j+D'_j U'_j
for j<i, the current coordinate is ell'_i+D'_i, and later coordinates
are zero. During the actual local path x_i>=ell'_i and
0<=x_(i+1)<=ell'_(i+1). Each preceding component is in its post-checkpoint
zero wedge and each later component is in its pre-activation zero wedge.
They have zero gradient because they are differentiable nonnegative
functions at minima. The sole active term has coefficient1/2, so the
physical h_t exactly implements its local half-step h_t/2. At b_i the
next coordinate becomes ell'_(i+1)+D'_(i+1). This proves the state
induction through every original physical entry, including zeros.

In the tail the physical gradient is delta'e_k/2. Its terminal coordinate
above ell'_k is D'_k-delta's_k/2>=delta', so substitution gives

    2F(x_n)=(D'_k)^2/[2(1+s_k)].                        (18)

For any actual samples a,b, including the terminal point and every
minimizer, define the directed residual
Q_ab=F(x_a)-F(x_b)+<grad F(x_a),x_b-x_a>
                           +||grad F(x_a)-grad F(x_b)||^2/2.
Equation(17), with x=x_b,y=x_a, gives Q_ab<=0 for every pair. Thus no
optimum, terminal, or remote interpolation row is omitted. The actual
vectors live in R^(k+1), so their Gram matrix is positive semidefinite.

At k=0 use F=Hub_(1/(1+s_0))/2 from1. Its closest radius is1 and its
payoff is1/[2(1+s_0)]. This is the zero-checkpoint member of the SAME
source family, rather than a different normalization.

## 5. Full source minimum set and a quantitative dual certificate

Because every summand of(16) is nonnegative and its envelope has zero
set(13), the COMPLETE minimum set is

    C_source={x:x_i<=zeta'_i,
                 epsilon x_i-x_(i+1)<=epsilon zeta'_i-D'_i c'_(i,2), i<k;
                 x_k<=ell'_k},
    zeta'_i=ell'_i+D'_i c'_(i,1).                       (19)

It contains zero. If k>=1, e_0 violates its first horizontal constraint,
so 0<rho_S^2:=dist(e_0,C_source)^2<=1. Formula(19) retains every later
stage and the true terminal constraint; no fictitious cap on x_1 is added.

An exact all-row formula can also be recorded. Let A_rad have rows e_i^T
and(epsilon e_i-e_(i+1))^T for i<k, followed by e_k^T, with right side
t_rad from(19). For any independent row subset I, put
A_I=(A_rad)_I, r_I=A_I e_0-(t_rad)_I, K_I=A_I A_I^T,
lambda_I=K_I^(-1)r_I. Include the empty subset with value zero. Then

    rho_S^2=max_(I independent,lambda_I>=0) r_I^T K_I^(-1)r_I. (20)

For any feasible x and any nonnegative row weights lambda, completing
a square gives ||e_0-x||^2>=2lambda^T r_I-||A_I^T lambda||^2. This proves
each entry of(20) as a lower bound. At the true projection x_*, its
normal belongs to the cone of active rows: otherwise its residual from
projection on that closed finitely generated cone is a feasible small
displacement with positive inner product with e_0-x_*, contradicting
projection optimality. The cone is closed because nonnegative linear
representations can be reduced to independent subsets, a finite union
of closed injective images of orthants. Choose an independent active
representation. Activity gives r_I=K_I lambda, and equality in(20).
This is an identity, not an executed active-set calculation.

The needed quantitative certificate has NONZERO weights only on the
two first-stage rows, with all later weights zero. Let
z_bar=(c'_(0,1),c'_(0,2),0,...,0). Then

    w=e_0-z_bar=sigma'_0(epsilon+P_0,-1-Q_0,0,...)
      =sigma'_0(P_0-epsilon Q_0)e_0
         +sigma'_0(1+Q_0)(epsilon e_0-e_1).            (21)

Both coefficients are nonnegative by(9). Both first constraints are
equalities at z_bar. Therefore <w,x-z_bar><=0 for every x in the FULL
C_source, whether or not z_bar itself satisfies the later constraints.
Expanding ||e_0-x||^2 proves

    rho_S^2>=(sigma'_0)^2[(epsilon+P_0)^2+(1+Q_0)^2]
           >=(sigma'_0)^2(s_0+2)^2/8.                 (22)

The last step uses(10) with s_loc=s_0/2. Later constraints can increase
the true distance relative to this bound. There is no assumption that
the first center remains globally feasible and no reuse of the false
one-source-stage extrapolation.

Combining the EXACT terminal value(18), the EXACT transfer product(15),
and the LOWER distance bound(22) gives the UPPER comparison

    E(F,h)<=Psi_S(h;selection),
    Psi_S= b_0^2/[(s_0+2)^2(1+s_k)]
                    *product_(i=1)^(k-1)[b_i/(Cs_i+2A+epsilon b_i)]^2.
                                                              (23)

The cancellation is D'_1=sigma'_0 b_0/2: the factors1/4 from its square,
1/2 from(18), and8 from(22) cancel exactly. Every later denominator in
(23) is an EXACT source transfer denominator, not a mass lower estimate.

## 6. Unchanged hierarchy and the minimum-level operation

Define r_h=c(c-2), v_h=a/(c-2)=beta/r_h,
M_j=1+S_j, d_j=a c^j, u_j=d_j/M_j, and M_max=M_(m-1).
Writing x=tau/m gives

    r_h=1+(4+2sqrt(2))x+lambda^2 x^2>1>beta,
    M_j=v_h c^j+(1-v_h)2^j,
    0<v_h<1, 1<=M_j<=c^j, a<=u_j<=c-2.               (24)

The mass formula follows by substitution in
M_(j+1)=2M_j+a c^j, with M_0=1. Its bounds use2<c and0<v_h<1.
Uniformly on(3),

    2<c<121/50, 1/4<a<=u_j<21/50<1/2,
    0<r_h-1<2/m.                                     (25)

For explicit checks, sqrt(2)<283/200 implies lambda<483/200, and
c<=lambda(1+1/6144)<484/200. Also beta>3/4 and c<3 imply a>1/4.
Finally4+2sqrt(2)<7, lambda^2<6 and m>=2 give
r_h-1<7/(4m)+3/(8m^2)<=31/(16m)<2/m.

Among any currently selected checkpoints choose one of minimum tree
level j. Its two complete H_j children contain only smaller levels, so
contain no currently selected checkpoint. Consequently its two actual
adjacent ordinary sums s,t satisfy

    s>=M_j-1, t>=M_j-1, b=1+d_j.                      (26)

This remains true for a first or last checkpoint and for tied minimum
levels. Removing it from the selected SUBSET reclassifies its full
physical b as ordinary, merging the adjacent sums to s+b+t. The word,
parameters, physical order and all remaining eligibility conditions stay
unchanged.

In the comparisons below write M=M_j, d=d_j, u=d/M. The operation is
performed on the proved upper functional Psi_S, not on actual states.
It claims neither monotonicity of the actual F under deletion nor
preservation of its backward P,Q. That distinction is justified by(23),
which already holds for every actual source instance before deletion.

## 7. All-count source upper comparison, including the first factor

Assume temporarily either

    (I) C>=r_h, or (II) A>=2C M_max.                   (27)

Section 8 proves that every parameter pair satisfies this dichotomy.
All arguments here use C>=1, A>=2C and0<u<=1/2.

FIRST SELECTED MINIMUM, with at least one selection after it.
Let R_next=2A+epsilon b_next. Cancelling the positive next numerator
and the identical remaining factors in(23), deletion is valid exactly
when

    b(s+b+t+2)<=(s+2)(Ct+R_next).                      (28)

The difference on the right increases with s,t,R_next: its derivatives
in s,t are Ct+R_next-b and C(s+2)-b, positive on(26) since
R_next>=4C, b=d+1<=M/2+1. Thus it suffices to set s=t=M-1.
Under(I), lower R_next to4C. The difference is exactly

    M^2[C-u(2+u)]+M[4C-2-2u]+3C-1.                   (29)

Since u<=c-2 gives u(2+u)<=r_h<=C, all three grouped terms are
nonnegative. Under(II), R_next>=4C M_max>=4CM, so the difference is
at least

    (M+1)C(5M-1)-(M/2+1)(5M/2+1)
      >=(15/4)M^2+M-2>0,                             (30)

using C>=1 and M>=1. This proves the new mixed first-factor deletion.

NONFIRST, NONLAST SELECTED MINIMUM.
Let Q_b=2A+epsilon b and R_next=2A+epsilon b_next. The exact required
inequality is

    b[C(s+b+t)+R_next]<=(Cs+Q_b)(Ct+R_next).           (31)

Its difference increases in Q_b,R_next,s,t: the nontrivial derivative
terms are Cs+Q_b-b and C(Ct+R_next-b), which are positive because
C(M-1)+4C-b>0. Lower s,t to M-1 and Q_b,R_next to2A. Put q=2A-C>=3C.
The resulting minimum difference is

    (CM+q)^2-(d+1)[C(2M+d)+q]
     =M^2[C^2-Cu(2+u)]
          +M[q(2C-u)-C(2+u)]+q^2-q.                 (32)

In(I) the first coefficient is nonnegative. The second is at least
C(6C-4u-2)>=2C, and q^2-q>=0. In(II),
q=2A-C>=C(4M_max-1)>=3CM, so z=q/M>=3C. Dividing the first
line of(32) by M^2 bounds it below by

    (C+z)^2-(3/2)[(5/2)C+z]
       >=16C^2-(33/4)C>0.                            (33)

Here(d+1)/M<=3/2, (2M+d)/M<=5/2, and the polynomial increases for
z>=3C,C>=1. This proves(31), with the full numerator b=d+1 retained.

LAST, NONFIRST SELECTED MINIMUM.
The ratio of the selected local factor to the deleted one is

    b^2(1+s+b+t)/[(Cs+2A+epsilon b)^2(1+t)]
       <=b^2(1+s+b+t)/[(s+4)^2(1+t)].                 (34)

The last expression decreases in t. Its s derivative, apart from its
positive factors, is2-s-2b-2t<0. Its maximum on(26) is therefore

    (d+1)^2(2M+d)/[(M+3)^2 M]
       <=(5/2)[(M/2+1)/(M+3)]^2<=5/8.               (35)

This case needs no choice between(I) and(II).

Repeat minimum-level deletion while there are at least two selections.
Each step is covered by(28),(31), or(34) and makes Psi_S nondecreasing.
There are finitely many selections, so the process reaches ONE eligible
checkpoint. It never requires defining a fictitious empty version of
the exceptional first factor. This is an induction, not an executed
recurrence or an enumeration of subsets.

For the remaining checkpoint put X=1+s>=M and Y=1+t>=M. Then
S_m=s+b+t=X+Y+d-1, and its upper ratio is

    Psi_S/H_base(H_m)

## 1. Euclidean frame and exact local data

Set epsilon=1/2. Let e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3 be orthonormal, 0<r<1,
s=sqrt(1-r^2), u_0=e_0, and

    u_(i+1)=-r*u_i+s*e_(i+1), i=0,1,2.

Then ||u_i||=1 and <u_i,u_j>=(-r)^|i-j|: the new orthogonal
coordinate proves the norm identity, and repeated substitution proves
the cross products. These are actual vectors, not orthogonal coefficient
coordinates. In particular <u_0,u_2>=r^2.

Define the local quantities

    kappa=2*s/r, omega=sqrt(1+epsilon^2+2*epsilon*r),
    theta=arctan(s/(epsilon+r)), c=omega*exp(kappa*theta),
    Delta=theta/2,
    E_i(t)=cos(t)*u_i-sin(t)*e_(i+1),
    T_i(t)=-sin(t)*u_i-cos(t)*e_(i+1),
    V_i(t)=c*exp(-kappa*t)*E_i(t),
    N_i(t)=E_i(t)+kappa*T_i(t).

The curve endpoints are c*u_i and w_i=epsilon*u_i-u_(i+1).
For z,t in [0,theta], writing v=z-t gives

    <N_i(t),V_i(z)>/[c*exp(-kappa*t)]
       =exp(-kappa*v)*(cos(v)+kappa*sin(v)).

Its derivative in v is
-(1+kappa^2)*exp(-kappa*v)*sin(v); its maximum is1 at0.
Thus N_i(t) supports the whole arc and the slope0 at V_i(t).
At the cap t=0, e_(i+1) is another supporting normal. Consequently
every vector X*u_i+Y*e_(i+1) with X>=0 and Y+kappa*X>=0 supports
the cap. These statements also hold for any finite subcollection of
the arc.

Use the following exact two-step local backward path:

    A_D=exp(-kappa*Delta)*(cos(Delta)+sin(Delta)/kappa),
    B_D=exp(-kappa*Delta)*sin(Delta)/kappa,
    t_0=0, t_1=B_D, t_2=B_D*(1+A_D),
    theta_l=theta-l*Delta, R_l=c*exp(-kappa*theta_l),
    v_(i,l)=R_l*E_i(theta_l),
    r_(i,l)=R_l*((1+t_l)*E_i(theta_l)
                              +kappa*t_l*T_i(theta_l)),
    alpha_l=1-exp(-kappa*Delta)*cos(Delta)+B_D
                         +(1+kappa^2)*B_D*t_(l-1), l=1,2.        (2)

Resolving radial and tangent coordinates at theta_l gives

    r_(i,l)-r_(i,l-1)=alpha_l*v_(i,l).                          (3)

For example the tangent cancellation is t_l=B_D+A_D*t_(l-1),
and the radial component gives exactly alpha_l in (2). Both alpha_l
are positive. The proximal displacement
r_(i,l)-v_(i,l)=R_l*t_l*N_i(theta_l) is a supporting normal, so the
local chronological block is (alpha_2,alpha_1), with gradients
v_(i,2),v_(i,1),w_i and local envelope values

    R_l^2*(t_l+1/2), with proximal heights R_l^2*t_l.          (4)

Write

    r_(i,2)=A*u_i-B*u_(i+1),
    B=c*kappa*t_2/s, A=c*(1+t_2)-r*B,
    Z=A+r*B=c*(1+t_2),
    R0^2=c^2*((1+t_2)^2+kappa^2*t_2^2),
    ell=1+epsilon*r, beta=ell/(epsilon+r),
    M=A+beta*B=Z+s^2*B/(epsilon+r), a=ell/M.                  (5)

Equation(3) expresses r_(i,2) as w_i plus positive multiples of
the two earlier arc slopes. Writing V_i(t)=p*u_i-q*u_(i+1) gives
p>=epsilon*q>=0, so A>=epsilon, B>=1 and A>=epsilon*B.
All local arc pairs have positive inner product; backward additions
in(3) show ||r_(i,l)||<=R0.

The following explicit admissibility conditions are imposed on r:

    9/10<=r<1,
    1/7<alpha_1<1/5, 1/6<alpha_2<2/9.                       (6)

This is a nonempty parameter domain, defined by the exact formulas(2).
Indeed as r tends1, theta/s tends2/3, kappa/s tends2, and

    B_D -> 1/6, A_D -> 7/6, t_2 -> 13/36,
    alpha_1 -> 1/6, alpha_2 -> 7/36.                         (7)

These follow from sin z/z->1 and exp z->1, without any numerical
evaluation. All limiting alpha inequalities in(6) are strict. Thus all
r sufficiently close1 satisfy(6). No particular decimal r is asserted
to have passed an executed check.

Set

    S=alpha_1+alpha_2, zeta=(1-alpha_2)*(1-alpha_1),
    X= zeta*r-epsilon,
    D_end=2*epsilon^2+3*epsilon*r-zeta*(2+epsilon*r),
    L_end=zeta*ell-epsilon*(epsilon+r).                      (8)

The rational bounds in(6) imply

    28/45<zeta<5/7, X>3/50,
    D_end>37/20-25/14=9/140>0, L_end>0.                     (9)

For the last assertion, ell-r*(epsilon+r)=s^2>0 and zeta*r>
epsilon imply zeta*ell>epsilon*(epsilon+r).

## 2. Fully specified amplitude and one static function

The amplitude restrictions are explicit and are fixed before the run.
They will also allow a uniform bound on the bounded remainders below.
Let

    C_1=-w_0-a*r_(1,2), C_bd=omega+a*R0,
    Hpref=omega+(1+2*a)*(R0+c),
    V_0=c*(r*(a*Z-1)-epsilon),
    E_bd=4*c*epsilon*r+2*abs(V_0)/c,
    Y_bd=C_bd+(3/2)*E_bd+S*c,
    R_bd=3*E_bd+(S+1)*c,
    T_bd=R_bd+a*omega.

Define D_base to be the maximum of

    2*c, 8*c*r*epsilon, sqrt(8*c*r*a*Z), c*r/epsilon,
    [1+2*(epsilon+c)/r]/epsilon,
    [Hpref+r*ell]/(epsilon*r).

Define D_all as the maximum of D_base and the following positive or
nonnegative quantities:

    c/r^2,
    2*abs(V_0)/(c*epsilon*r),
    2*(4*c+E_bd)/zeta,
    4*S*c/(epsilon*r),
    Y_bd/(epsilon*r),
    sqrt(1+kappa^2)*Y_bd/(epsilon*s),
    c*((3/2)*E_bd+S*c)/(epsilon*(epsilon+r)),
    c*sqrt(1+kappa^2)*r*T_bd/(s*D_end),
    omega*T_bd/L_end,
    c*(C_bd+T_bd)/(X*r*(epsilon+r)),
    T_bd/zeta.                                             (10)

All denominators are strictly positive by(6),(9). For example take

    d=1+2*D_all.                                           (11)

Every assertion below holds for ANY d>D_all, including(11). There
is no later amendment to d, alpha_1, alpha_2 or any step after an
active set fails. The actual physical word is exactly(1).

Define x_6=C_1-d*w_1 and C_T=x_6-d*u_2=C_1-epsilon*d*u_1.
For any center C and scale b>0 let

    Phi_(i,b,C)(y)=max{0,b*<v_(i,l),y-C>:l=0,1,2}.

Fix before the first step the SINGLE function

    J(y)=max{Phi_(0,1,0)(y),Phi_(1,a,C_1)(y),
                                      Phi_(2,d/c,C_T)(y)},
    F(x)=min_y[J(y)+||x-y||^2/2].                           (12)

There are nine nonzero planes and the plane0. The third-stage cap
is q=d*u_2, with affine plane <q,y-C_T>. It is exactly the terminal
plane of the earlier six-step calibration. Its two additional arc
planes are present throughout this run. There is no sum of local
envelopes and no overlap-based change to the physical steps.

## 3. The first six steps, including every future plane

Their positions and gradients are

    x_0=r_(0,2), x_1=r_(0,1), x_2=w_0,
    x_3=-w_0=C_1+a*r_(1,2),
    x_4=C_1+a*r_(1,1), x_5=C_1+a*w_1,

Equation(3) and the steps2,1+d/a prove every GD update in(13).
The corresponding values and proximal heights are(4), multiplied
by1 for stage0 and by a^2 for stage1. Here is a joint check that

An arc slope written p*u_i-q*u_(i+1) has p>=epsilon*q>=0 and

    (r*p+q)/(p+r*q)<=beta.

                         +a*((p+r*q)*A+(r*p+q)*B)<=0,          (14)

Indeed kappa*tan theta<=1 follows from r>=9/10>

by D_base. They have zero e_3 coordinate. Every stage2 plane

Thus BOTH newly added future planes, as well as the stage2 cap,

## 4. Exact mixed gradients through the third ordinary block

Put

    p=c*u_0, q=d*u_2, v=p-q,
    D=||v||^2=c^2+d^2-2*c*d*r^2,
    V=c*epsilon*r*d+V_0,
    eta_0=V/D,
    eta_star=d*(d-c*r^2)/D,
    g_bar=q+eta_star*v,
    xi=eta_0-eta_star.                                   (18)

One has <v,g_bar>=0. Also g_bar is the shortest vector on the
whole affine line through p and q, so ||g_bar||<=c. Do not impose
a simplex constraint on eta_star: our choice d>c/r^2 implies

    eta_star-1=c*(d*r^2-c)/D>0.                           (19)

Define for j=0,1,2

    P_0=1, P_1=1-alpha_2, P_2=zeta,
    S_0=0, S_1=alpha_2, S_2=S,
    eta_j=eta_star+xi*P_j,
    g_(6+j)=g_bar+xi*P_j*v,
    y_(6+j)=C_T+eta_0*(q-p)-S_j*g_bar,
    x_(6+j)=x_6-S_j*g_bar-xi*(1-P_j)*v.                   (20)

These formulas are actual jets, not just a formal face recurrence.
We prove the proximal conditions against the entire dictionary.

First D>(d-c)^2>d^2/4. By(10), V>0 and

    0<eta_0*d<=E_bd,
    0<eta_star-1<4*c/d.

Hence

    0<eta_j<1-P_j+(4*c+E_bd)/d<1-zeta/2<1                (21)

for j=0,1,2, with the first upper bound also valid for j=0.
In particular xi<0. These inequalities use the bound on d in(10),
not the illegal assumption eta_star<=1.

The p-plane and q-plane tie at y_6: their difference at C_T is
<p,C_T>=V, and its change along eta_0*(q-p) is -eta_0*D.
They continue to tie at every y_(6+j), since <v,g_bar>=0.

Every such y has the representation

    y=-epsilon*d*u_1+E_y, ||E_y||<=Y_bd.                  (22)

Here ||C_1||<=C_bd, ||eta_0*(q-p)||<=(3/2)*E_bd and
||S_j*g_bar||<=S*c. In its (u_0,e_1) coordinates, (22) has
positive first coordinate and

    <e_1,y>+kappa*<u_0,y>
       >=epsilon*s*d-sqrt(1+kappa^2)*Y_bd>0.             (23)

The cap-support criterion of Section1 proves that p dominates
every other stage0 plane. Its value is strictly positive.

Every stage1 slope has u_1 component R_l*cos(theta_l)>=epsilon+r
and norm at most c. Therefore its unscaled evaluation at y-C_1 is
at most

    -epsilon*d*(epsilon+r)
                            +c*((3/2)*E_bd+S*c)<0.      (24)

For stage2, all e_3 coordinates are zero. Its radial coordinate is

    <u_2,y-C_T>
      =[V*(d-c*r^2)-S_j*c^2*d*(1-r^4)]/D>0.            (25)

Indeed V>=c*epsilon*r*d/2 and d-c*r^2>=d/2; the negative
term is at most S*c^2*d, and(10) makes the numerator positive.
At a positive pure radial normal the cap uniquely dominates the
two other arc slopes: R_l*cos(theta_l)<c for l=0,1.

Thus the p-plane and q-plane are exactly the active nonzero planes,
above0. Their convex combination in(20),(21) belongs to partial J(y),

The exact positive heights and values are

    H_(6+j)=<p,y_(6+j)>=V+eta_0*<p,q-p>-S_j*||g_bar||^2,

The equality <p,g_bar>=||g_bar||^2 follows from p-g_bar being

Since 0<P_2<P_1<P_0, xi<0 and v!=0, the three gradients in(20)

The third checkpoint is the step2 from x_8. The actual resulting

    x_9=x_8-2*g_8

If the two-plane face were invariant at this checkpoint, its next

    eta_9^face=2*eta_star-eta_2>1.                         (28)

The inequality is strict by(19),(21). This is the FIRST failed
full-face consistency test: the coefficient of q would be negative.
No reassignment of values changes this convex-combination defect for
this fixed function and these two slopes.

Clamping to p is not the answer either. At the proposed point x_9-p,
the leading p-plane value is d*<p,D_vec>=-d*c*r*X<0,
whereas the leading stage1 endpoint-plane value is d*a*L_end>0.

The ONE correction retains the whole J and word(1) and uses

    g_9=a*w_1, y_9=x_9-a*w_1.                            (29)

Here is the check against every plane, including the future ones.
In the orthonormal (u_1,e_2) frame,

    D_vec=X*u_1-zeta*s*e_2, X=zeta*r-epsilon>0.

For the continuous stage1 arc, its support value on D_vec is

    f_arc(t)=c*exp(-kappa*t)*(X*cos t+zeta*s*sin t).

Its derivative is c*exp(-kappa*t) times

    (zeta*s-kappa*X)*cos t-(X+kappa*zeta*s)*sin t.

At t=theta this bracket divided by cos(theta) is exactly

Its evaluation at y_9 is consequently at most

## 6. Smoothness, every original row, and the closest distance

J is a finite convex nonnegative maximum with J(0)=0. The objective
J(y)+||x-y||^2/2 is coercive and strictly convex, hence has a unique
minimizer y. Completing the square in the subgradient inequality
proves that its optimality condition is x-y in partial J(y); the
converse follows by a directional difference quotient.

Write g=x-y. For two such pairs, summing the two subgradient
inequalities gives

    ||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>.

Also testing y as a trial point at x+z gives
F(x+z)<=F(x)+<g,z>+||z||^2/2, while the subgradient inequality
gives the opposite bound F(x+z)>=F(x)+<g,z>. Thus F is finite,
convex, differentiable and has1-Lipschitz gradient g.
Its minimum is0 and its minimum set is exactly

    C_min={z:<v_(0,l),z><=0,
               <v_(1,l),z-C_1><=0,
               <v_(2,l),z-C_T><=0, l=0,1,2}.            (34)

The positive scales do not affect these inequalities. This is the
whole nonempty polyhedron, not a selected minimizer only. The least
global gradient Lipschitz constant is1: both0 and p are active at
the proximal point0, so every x=t*p,0<=t<=1, has proximal point0
and gradient x. Two distinct such inputs give Lipschitz ratio1.

For every actual query, terminal point and any minimizer write
x_i=y_i+g_i, f_i=H_i+||g_i||^2/2, H_i=J(y_i). The EXACT row identity is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
         =H_i-H_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i><=0.                    (35)

The final inequality is the subgradient inequality for J. Thus
ALL original directed interpolation rows, remote in either direction,
hold. The Euclidean Gram is positive semidefinite because all the
points and gradients are actual vectors in R^4. No sign-changing
coefficient frame is substituted for that metric.

Equation(3) gives x_0=w_0+alpha_1*v_(0,1)+alpha_2*v_(0,2).
For every z in C_min each of these three slope evaluations is
nonpositive, so <x_0,z><=0. Since0 belongs to C_min,

    ||x_0-z||^2>=||x_0||^2+||z||^2,
    dist(x_0,C_min)^2=||x_0||^2=R0^2.                   (36)

In particular0 is the unique closest minimizer even in the enlarged
R^4 function. The finite lower witness, in the required W=2R
normalization, is therefore

    W_9(h)>=
       [2*a*d*L_end+2*a*<w_1,R(d)>-a^2*omega^2]/R0^2.  (37)

For arbitrary L>0 the function L*F and steps h_t/L have the same
trajectory, minimum set, closest radius and normalized payoff.
This is a statement about(1), not about the original ruler word or
the unrestricted minimax value.

## 8. Exact full-history state and its actual cost

This section records an algebraic state for a fixed arbitrary finite

to claim that defining a proximal optimization solves the problem.

Let there be k complete finite arc stages with their centers and
scales fixed before the run. There are N=3k+1 affine planes including
the plane0, in ambient dimension k+1. Write each plane as

    L_mu(y)=<a_mu,y>+b_mu, mu=0,...,N-1,
    a_0=0, b_0=0,
    K_munu=<a_mu,a_nu>, z_mu=<a_mu,x>+b_mu.              (42)

K is the ACTUAL slope Gram. If a slope of stage i is

## 2. Source and hypothesis-exact transfer

Source: Kaizhao Liu and Yuhan Ye, *Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for
Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case*, arXiv:2609.26873v1 (2026),
https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26873v1 . Read Sections2.2,3.1--3.3,5 and
the actual AppendixA.1--A.3 proofs, including FactA.1.

The source's condition number is denoted K_cond here, not kappa. The
source's objective is

    ||x||^2/(2 K_cond)
       +(1-1/K_cond)/2 * sum_i Phi_i(x_i,x_(i+1)).       (2.1)

Its bending lemma assumes K_cond>=4, 0<beta_arc<=1/4,
s_i/K_cond<=1/16, and positive excess factor

    chi_i=product_gap(1-h/K_cond),
    eta_i=chi_i-(1-chi_i) ell_i/D_i >0.

The lemma uses selected b_i>8. Its input dynamics, before any extra

              -(1-1/K_cond)h/2 * grad Phi_i(X,Y).      (2.2)

For repairs and bridges, a nonnegative term (h f_j,0) is additionally
allowed. This term is an actual derivative of the preceding component,
not a freely injected control. The source's bending lemma requires it

The source's repair uses a Huber ridge with

    delta_H=D_i eta_i/[2+(K_cond-1)(1-chi_i)].

    repair threshold=s_i delta_H/2,
    repair outgoing amplitude=b_i delta_H/2,

## 3. A finite circular body and its elementary envelope

Fix 0<beta_arc<=1/4. Write beta=beta_arc locally in Sections3--10,
always distinct from beta_word in the ruler definition. Set

    R_circ=1+beta,
    c_arc=beta+sqrt(1+2 beta),
    p(q)=beta+sqrt(R_circ^2-(q+beta)^2), 0<=q<=1,
    v(q)=(p(q),-q),
    K_ctr=conv({0} union {v(q):0<=q<=1}).             (3.1)

The circular center is (beta,beta). K_ctr is fresh notation; the project glossary K_arc denotes an older
spiral body and is not changed. Its endpoints are (c_arc,0) and
(beta,-1). Its containing closed disk also contains0, because
2 beta^2 <= (1+beta)^2. Thus the circular radial vector
(p(q)-beta,-q-beta) supports K_ctr at v(q). The normal (0,1)
also supports at the horizontal endpoint.

Every (p,-q) in K_ctr satisfies

    0<=p<=c_arc, 0<=q<=1, p>=beta q,
    and (p,0) belongs to K_ctr.                       (3.2)

The last assertion follows because the whole horizontal segment from0
to(c_arc,0) is in K_ctr. On the arc, p>=beta and q<=1, so the third
inequality holds there and hence on the convex hull.

For a compact convex body C containing0 define the finite function

    E_C(r)=max_(g in C) [<g,r>-||g||^2/2].            (3.3)

Completing the square shows that its unique maximizer is Pi_C(r),
the Euclidean projection onto C. The projection inequalities at r,s
imply

    ||Pi_C(r)-Pi_C(s)||^2
        <= <Pi_C(r)-Pi_C(s),r-s>.                    (3.4)

In particular the maximizer is1-Lipschitz. Bounding the increment of
(3.3) above and below using its maximizers at r and r+d shows that the
linear part is <Pi_C(r),d> and the remainder is bounded by ||d||^2.
Consequently E_C is differentiable with gradient Pi_C and is1-smooth.
It is convex as a maximum of affine functions, and nonnegative because
0 is allowed. The projection criterion is

    g=Pi_C(r) iff <r-g,w-g><=0 for every w in C.      (3.5)

Its zero set is the polar cone of C: if a support value is positive,
a sufficiently small positive multiple of that supporting vector gives
a positive value in(3.3); if all support values are nonpositive the
maximum is0.

The cone of K_ctr is generated by its two nonzero endpoints, since

    (p,-q)=[(p-beta q)/c_arc](c_arc,0)+q(beta,-1).

Therefore

    E_(sigma K_ctr)(U,V)=0
        iff U<=0 and beta U-V<=0                    (3.6)

for every sigma>0.

We also use the one-sided Huber function

    Hub_delta(z)=0                    if z<=0,
                 z^2/2                if 0<=z<=delta,
                 delta z-delta^2/2    if z>=delta,   (3.7)

where delta>0. Its derivative is min(delta,max(z,0)); hence it is
convex, nonnegative, differentiable and1-smooth.

## 4. Exact local trajectory for the convex physical update

Let a_1,...,a_N be any finite nonnegative ordinary block, in its actual
physical order. Define alpha_j=a_j/2 and s=sum_j a_j. These alpha_j
are local times, not replacements for physical steps. Empty blocks
are permitted.

Construct r_j=(u_j,-y_j) backwards, with

    r_N=v(1)=(beta,-1).

If alpha_j=0 set r_(j-1)=r_j and keep its arc vector. Otherwise choose
q_(j-1) in[0,1) by

    (q_(j-1)+beta)/(p(q_(j-1))-beta)
       =max{ beta/(c_arc-beta),
               [y_j+(1-alpha_j)beta]
                    /[u_j-(1-alpha_j)beta] },       (4.1)

and put

    v_(j-1)=v(q_(j-1)),
    r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha_j v_(j-1).                     (4.2)

The denominator in(4.1) is positive because u_j>=beta and alpha_j>0.
The left side increases continuously from beta/(c_arc-beta) to
infinity, so this is a unique finite definition. No recurrence is
executed to prove any assertion in this document.

Here are the full checks for the backward prescription. The updates
give u_(j-1)>=u_j>=beta and y_(j-1)>=y_j>=1. The ratios in(4.1)
give q_(j-1)<=q_j: at an interior current point the current ratio is
(y_j+beta)/(u_j-beta), and subtracting alpha_j beta from its numerator
and adding alpha_j beta to its denominator can only lower it. At
q_j=1 there is no upper finite ratio to check. At q_j=0, the normal
cone inequality is

    y_j <= beta(u_j-c_arc)/(c_arc-beta),              (4.3)

which makes both entries of the new maximum no greater than the
horizontal endpoint ratio. Zero steps preserve everything.

For a selected interior q_(j-1)>0, equation(4.1) and(4.2) say that
r_(j-1) and v_(j-1) are collinear with (beta,beta). Since
y_(j-1)>=1>=q_(j-1), the former lies at or beyond the latter on the
outward ray. The circular normal thus proves(3.5). If q_(j-1)=0,
cross-multiplication in(4.1) instead gives

    y_(j-1) <= beta(u_(j-1)-c_arc)/(c_arc-beta).

Then r_(j-1)-(c_arc,0) is a nonnegative combination of the circular
endpoint normal and (0,1), again proving(3.5). The final point is on
K_ctr itself. This proves for every j

    Pi_(K_ctr)(r_j)=v_j,
    u_j>=beta, 1<=y_j<=y_0, 0<=q_j<=1.              (4.4)

In particular

    u_0=beta+sum_j alpha_j p(q_(j-1)),
    y_0=1+sum_j alpha_j q_(j-1),
    u_0>=beta y_0.                                  (4.5)

The last inequality follows termwise from p>=beta q. It is strict if
there is any positive ordinary step: its predecessor q is below1, so
p-beta q>0. A positive ordinary step also gives at least one actual
change of gradient before the checkpoint, because the last positive
step has predecessor q<1 and ends at q=1 after later zero steps.

Now take incoming threshold ell>=0 and amplitude D>0, and define

    M=u_0+y_0/beta,
    sigma=D/M,
    ell_out=sigma y_0,
    A=ell+ell_out/beta,
    Phi(X,Y)=E_(sigma K_ctr)(X-A,Y-ell_out).          (4.6)

This is one fixed finite smooth convex function. It is zero when
X<=ell and Y>=0, by(3.6), and its output derivative vanishes whenever
Y>=ell_out, for EVERY X. To prove the latter, replacing a candidate
gradient (p,-q) with (p,0) increases the objective by
q(Y-ell_out)+q^2/2 when q>0. Thus the unique maximizer has q=0.

Define the ordinary states

    (X_j,Y_j)=(A+sigma u_j, ell_out-sigma y_j).       (4.7)

The initial state is(ell+D,0), and (4.2)--(4.4) prove

    (X_j,Y_j)=(X_(j-1),Y_(j-1))
                   -(a_j/2) grad Phi(X_(j-1),Y_(j-1)).

Every ordinary and checkpoint query has X_j>ell and
0<=Y_j<=ell_out-sigma<ell_out. The last gradient is
sigma(beta,-1).

For ANY physical checkpoint b>2 put

    t=b/2-1,
    D_out=sigma t.                                  (4.8)

Its exact post-checkpoint state is

    X^+=A-beta D_out,
    Y^+=ell_out+D_out.                              (4.9)

Thus D_out>0, and the local function is exactly0 immediately after
its own checkpoint: its centered point is(-beta D_out,D_out), which
satisfies(3.6). A later checkpoint can lower Y and reactivate Phi.
That later effect, not a fictitious positive value at(4.9), is the
retained-value mechanism analyzed below.

## 5. One static global function and every physical update

Take any physical word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) and selected zero-based
indices t_1<...<t_k, k>=1, with b_i=h_(t_i)>2. Let block i contain
all actual steps strictly between t_(i-1) and t_i, with t_0=-1.
Let block k+1 be the complete suffix after t_k. No unselected step
is removed, permuted or shortened. Write s_i for its physical mass.

For i=1,...,k, apply Section4 to the actual ordered block i, always
with the same beta. Denote the resulting dimensionless data by
u_i,y_i,M_i and the local full trajectory by r_(i,j),v_(i,j).
Starting with ell_1=0,D_1=1, set

    sigma_i=D_i/M_i,
    ell_(i+1)=sigma_i y_i,
    A_i=ell_i+ell_(i+1)/beta,
    D_(i+1)=sigma_i(b_i/2-1),
    Phi_i(X,Y)=E_(sigma_i K_ctr)(X-A_i,Y-ell_(i+1)). (5.1)

Finally set delta=D_(k+1)/(1+s_(k+1)) and define on R^(k+1)

    F(x)=1/2 sum_(i=1)^k Phi_i(x_i,x_(i+1))
                        +1/2 Hub_delta(x_(k+1)-ell_(k+1)).
    x_0=e_1.                                       (5.2)

All parameters in(5.2) are fixed from the predetermined word and its
selected indices before GD is run. Neither functions nor past values
are modified during the run.

Each block term is convex and1-smooth on its two coordinates. The
linear map stacking those coordinate pairs and the last scalar
coordinate has operator norm at most sqrt(2), because every coordinate
is counted at most twice. The gradient of the separable sum before
composition has Lipschitz constant1. Its coefficient1/2 therefore
makes grad F Lipschitz with constant at most1. The function is convex,
nonnegative, and F(0)=0, so the minimum is attained.

For completeness the entire physical update, including every old
component, has the following exact form. At any point x let

    (P_i(x),-Q_i(x))
        =Pi_(sigma_i K_ctr)(x_i-A_i,x_(i+1)-ell_(i+1)),
    P_(k+1)(x)=min(delta,max(x_(k+1)-ell_(k+1),0)),
    Q_0(x)=0.

Then for j=1,...,k+1,

    x_j^+=x_j - (h/2)[P_j(x)-Q_(j-1)(x)].           (5.3)

This is the ordinary Euclidean gradient of(5.2). In particular, old
negative output derivatives produce the nonnegative contributions in
the adjacent input coordinate; their magnitudes are the projections
of the SAME fixed components.

The active-coordinate induction is exact even when older values are
nonzero. At the start of block i its input is ell_i+D_i and all
coordinates after it are0. The local states(4.7) have x_i>=ell_i.
