## 9. Uniform local bounds needed for an unbounded ruler test

The following bounds are proved for the direct convex construction,
not imported as a finite-K_cond lemma. Define constants depending only
on beta by

    I_beta=sqrt(2)(1+beta)-beta,
    Y_beta=beta[exp(I_beta/beta)-1],
    U_beta=beta+(c_arc-beta)(Y_beta+beta)/beta.        (9.1)

For every finite ordinary word, y_0<=Y_beta. To check this, put
w_j=(y_j+beta)/(q_j+beta). For consecutive uncapped points, the
circular normal relation is

    u_j-beta=(p_j-beta)w_j.

Taking the cross product of r_(j-1)=r_j+alpha_j v_(j-1) with
v_(j-1) and canceling the alpha term gives

    w_(j-1)=w_j[1+(p_(j-1)q_j-q_(j-1)p_j)
                         /{beta(p_(j-1)+q_(j-1))}]. (9.2)

If q_(j-1)=0, the needed inequality follows directly from
y_(j-1)=y_j; if both are zero it is equality. Zero steps do not
change it. The numerator equals

    integral_(q_(j-1))^(q_j) [p_(j-1)-q_(j-1)p'(t)] dt.

After division by p_(j-1)+q_(j-1), the integrand is at most
max(1,-p'(t)). Using1+x<=exp(x) and multiplying(9.2), with w_N=1,
gives

    y_0+beta <= (q_0+beta)
          exp[beta^(-1) integral_(q_0)^1 max(1,-p'(t)) dt]
       <= beta exp[beta^(-1) integral_0^1 max(1,-p'(t)) dt].

The second inequality uses log(1+q_0/beta)<=q_0/beta and that the
integrand is at least1. Since
p'(t)=-(t+beta)/(p(t)-beta), its crossing of -1 occurs at
t=(1+beta)/sqrt(2)-beta. Integrating on the two sides gives precisely
I_beta in(9.1), proving the bound.

Whenever q_j>0, the normal relation and y_j<=Y_beta imply
u_j<=U_beta. Steps with q_(j-1)>0 form one contiguous portion in
backward order, and their sum of alpha_j p_(j-1) is at most U_beta-beta.
For these steps, p_(j-1)>=beta. Every other step has p_(j-1)=c_arc.
Consequently

    u_0=beta+c_arc s/2-E_gap,
    0<=E_gap<=c_arc(U_beta-beta)/beta.               (9.3)

Together with1<=y_0<=Y_beta, this proves the uniform, order-independent
ESTIMATE (not equality)

    M=c_arc s/2+O_beta(1).                          (9.4)

The constant is finite for each fixed beta and explicitly controlled
by(9.1)--(9.3). No uniform O(1) in beta tending to0 is asserted.

## 12. Exact remaining interface and failed shortcuts

The main unresolved question for the explicit two-checkpoint law is
the final value of the first TWO terms of(10.14), under the precise
ordered word H_(m-1) and incoming state(10.4). To establish a genuine
small-tau escape, one must bound that full quantity, with the radius

checkpoint selection and every relevant beta scaling; Section11
closes only its explicitly tiny-shift portion.

Two direct attempts at shortcutting that interface fail for concrete
reasons proved in this same draft:

1. Carry the positive post-root old value unchanged to the terminal
   iterate. The first tail in(8.2) erases it exactly on the same static
   law, so a retained snapshot supplies no such lower bound.
2. Replace the ordered old-coordinate tail by its total mass and
   optimize a checkpoint product. The two tails in(8.2) have the same
   mass and length and the same global function, but distinct final
   old values. An all-history argument is necessary.

No repair of the chosen construction has been made: zero of the one
allowed repairs is used. Adding a source repair or bridge would
consume real physical checkpoint positions and alter both the
incoming states and loss factors. It is not justified as a free
restart. The present all-bending law already realizes its active
coordinates without such an operation.

# Arithmetic-rank projection envelopes: exact all-word law and a growing paired-face obstruction

Project: gd-exact-profile-20260926. Worker: max. Allocated round: 63.
Assignment: TASK.md; originating guidance: 5c4d3ccc1ebe4c55.
Plan finding: 0ddf7a58a2fd110e.

**Status: COMPLETE JOINT UNVERIFIED mathematical draft. No fact_id.**
No new lemma in this document has passed fact_submit. The assignment closes
the formal gate, so the sections below form one joint proof attempt, not a
chain of newly accepted facts. The original exact minimax Goal remains OPEN.

The frozen submodular profile is

    F_d(A) = |A|(d-|A|)/d,       A subset of {1,...,d}, d>=2.

There is no change of rank profile and no repair to another submodular body.
The deliverable has two parts. First it eliminates the projection oracle in
favor of an explicit interval-average, minimum/maximum and sorting recurrence
for EVERY physical word and every initial point. Second it calibrates a
growing family with d/2 genuine initial projection blocks, follows its actual
first face transition, and proves a scoped obstruction on every remaining
physical step. That family cannot provide the sought nonlinear adversarial
gain: its first update enters the quadratic region and never leaves it.

## 1. Scope, accepted inputs, and primary-source audit

We retain the definitions of W_n and of signed interpolation residuals from
accepted fact **1252b8823bb5a290**. In particular, W_n(h) is the supremum of

    2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L ||x_0-x_star||^2),

over finite-dimensional Euclidean convex differentiable L-smooth functions
with an attained minimizer, with x_(t+1)=x_t-(h_t/L) grad f(x_t).
All physical steps and all ordered interpolation rows are retained.

Accepted fact **04219554e41d9750** supplies the unchanged ALL-split benchmark:

    Omega(a,b) = (a+b+sqrt((a+b)^2+4ab))/2,
    G(a,b) = 2a+b/2+sqrt(b^2+8ab)/2,
    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n) Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n) G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)),
    U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

The maxima include every integer split. With lambda=1+sqrt(2), that fact
gives a finite positive Z_1 and the finite inequality

    B_(2^m-1) <= Z_1 lambda^m.                         (1)

Nothing from its conditional seed theorem is assumed. The accepted tau=1
witness 5b7ff4253c38b90a is not an ingredient of this construction. The new
unverified source-family obstruction e65119d6d7a877a9 is not used as a brick.

Primary orientation: Francis Bach, *Learning with Submodular Functions:
A Convex Optimization Perspective*, arXiv:1111.6453v2 (2013),
https://arxiv.org/html/1111.6453v2 . Downloaded HTML and extracted mathematical
text are saved in this worker's downloads/bach_1111.6453v2.{html,txt}.

Source hypothesis mapping: Definitions 2.1--2.2 concern normalized
submodularity and the base polyhedron. Propositions 3.2, 3.3, 4.1 and 4.2
relate greedy ranks, support and tight level sets. Propositions 6.1--6.2
cover concave cardinality functions. Our F_d is normalized and submodular
but NOT nondecreasing; we use the base body, not a positive polymatroid.
For Proposition 8.1 the separable term is (u_i-x_i)^2/2, strictly convex,
continuously differentiable, with derivative onto R. Section 8.3 and
Appendix A.3 provide quadratic projection and ordered-block orientation;
their proofs and Section 9.1's decomposition proof were read. A fixed
ordering gives only an approximation for a general submodular body. Here
permutation symmetry and the boundary inequalities proved below establish
exactness. Agglomeration along a proximal regularization parameter is not
an invariant for these GD steps. All needed mathematical statements are
rederived below, so no external theorem is a black box.

Matlas additionally returned 2106.11943 Lemma 9, 1909.00171 Theorem 4,
and 1411.0589 Proposition A.12. None is imported. In particular the first
hit's nondecreasing-cardinality hypothesis does not directly hold for F_d.

## 2. The actual body and its support

Write [d]={1,...,d}, let e be the all-ones vector, and put

    E_d={v in R^d: <e,v>=0},
    a_i=(d+1-2i)/d,       1<=i<=d,
    K_d={g in E_d: sum_(i in A) g_i <= F_d(A) for every A subset [d]}.

The vectors a, K_d, and all norms in this document use the ordinary
coordinate Euclidean metric. No graph metric or rank-weighted metric is
substituted. If A and B have disjoint differences of sizes p and q, expanding
the quadratic cardinality formula gives

    F_d(A)+F_d(B)-F_d(A union B)-F_d(A intersection B)=2pq/d>=0.

Thus F_d is submodular. It is zero at the empty and full sets, and strictly
positive at every proper nonempty set. Its successive cardinality increments
are exactly a_i, with sum_i a_i=0 and

    sum_(i=1)^k a_i = k(d-k)/d.                       (2)

Every permutation of a is in K_d: its largest k-coordinate sum is (2).
The singleton and complementary-singleton inequalities give
|g_i|<=(d-1)/d for g in K_d. Thus K_d is nonempty, closed and compact.

For any w, take a permutation pi with
w_(pi(1))>=...>=w_(pi(d)). Summation by parts gives, for g in K_d,

    <w,g>
      = sum_(k<d) (w_(pi(k))-w_(pi(k+1))) sum_(i<=k)g_(pi(i))
      <= sum_(k<d) (w_(pi(k))-w_(pi(k+1))) k(d-k)/d
      = sum_i a_i w_(pi(i)).                         (3)

The permutation g_(pi(i))=a_i attains equality. Consequently

    K_d = conv{all permutations of a},
    sigma_d(w):=max_(g in K_d)<w,g>
              =sum_i a_i w_(pi(i))
              =(1/d) sum_(i<j)|w_i-w_j|.             (4)

For completeness, equality of the two bodies follows without assuming a
majorization theorem. If a point g in K_d were outside the convex hull of
the permutations, let v be its closest point in that compact convex hull.
The vector w=g-v satisfies <w,t-v><=0 for every point t of the hull, by
one-sided differentiation of squared distance. Hence <w,g> exceeds the
hull's support value, contradicting (3) and attainment by a permutation.
The last formula in (4) follows by counting that a sorted coordinate at
rank i has coefficient (d-i)-(i-1)=d+1-2i in the pairwise differences.

Because -a is a permutation of a, K_d=-K_d. It has nonempty relative
interior in E_d. Indeed, for g in E_d and |A|=k,

    |sum_(i in A)g_i|
        <= ||g|| sqrt(k(d-k)/d).

Since k(d-k)>=d-1 for 1<=k<d, every centered g with
||g||<sqrt((d-1)/d) satisfies every proper constraint strictly.

## 3. One static function, paid smoothness, and the closest radius

Freeze the single function

    Phi_d(x)=max_(g in K_d){<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.          (5)

This is the joint quadratic smoothing of (4). There is one common dual
vector g constrained to K_d; no separate smoothing of its individual edges
is substituted. Let P_d(x) denote the unique closest point of x in K_d.
Completing the square proves

    grad Phi_d(x)=P_d(x),
    Phi_d(x)=(||x||^2-||x-P_d(x)||^2)/2.              (6)

Here is a direct justification including differentiability. Compactness
and strict convexity of squared distance give a unique P_d(x). Its
optimality is equivalent to

    <x-P_d(x),g-P_d(x)><=0    for all g in K_d.       (7)

Sufficiency follows by expanding ||x-g||^2; necessity follows by taking
a small segment toward g. Applying (7) at x and x' and adding proves

    <x-x',P_d(x)-P_d(x')> >= ||P_d(x)-P_d(x')||^2.

Thus P_d is 1-Lipschitz. Evaluating the maximum (5) at each other's
maximizers shows that

    0 <= Phi_d(x')-Phi_d(x)-<P_d(x),x'-x>
       <= <P_d(x')-P_d(x),x'-x> <= ||x'-x||^2.

This proves differentiability, (6), and 1-smoothness. Convexity follows
from (5). Smoothness has no missing dimension factor: near zero on E_d,
P_d(x)=x, so the optimal global Lipschitz constant is exactly 1 for d>=2.
For prescribed L>0 use f=L Phi_d. Original GD with h_t/L then has exactly
the updates x_(t+1)=x_t-h_t P_d(x_t).

The complete minimizer set and its distance are

    argmin Phi_d = R e,
    min Phi_d=0,
    dist(x,argmin Phi_d)^2=||x-bar(x)e||^2,
    bar(x)=d^(-1)sum_i x_i.                          (8)

To prove the first equality, K_d subset E_d and 0 in K_d imply
Phi_d(te)=0 and Phi_d>=0. If z=x-bar(x)e is nonzero, choose small
epsilon in (0,2) such that epsilon z lies in K_d, using the relative
interior just proved. Its value in (5) is
(epsilon-epsilon^2/2)||z||^2>0. This excludes every other minimizer.
The closest point is the orthogonal projection bar(x)e, proving (8).
The mean of every GD trajectory is constant because P_d(x) is centered.

## 4. Exact projection from interval averages, with no projection oracle

Let y_1>=...>=y_d be the sorted coordinates of x and set z_i=y_i-a_i.
For 1<=p<=q<=d write

    av_(p,q)(z)=(sum_(j=p)^q z_j)/(q-p+1).

Define an explicit scalar array

    u_i = min_(1<=p<=i) max_(i<=q<=d) av_(p,q)(z).    (9)

Then the exact projection and residual, in the same sorted coordinates,
are

    g_i=y_i-u_i,      y-g=u.                         (10)

All minima and maxima in (9) are over the displayed finite integer sets.
There is no convex program, numerical projection, or unreported root solve
in (9). We prove the formula, including why this ordered calculation
satisfies ALL subset inequalities of the original body.

First consider minimizing ||u-z||^2/2 over the closed cone
u_1>=...>=u_d. Existence follows from coercivity and uniqueness from strict
convexity. For this paragraph let u denote that minimizer. Put

    R_k=sum_(i<=k)(u_i-z_i), R_0=0.

Perturbing all coordinates equally gives R_d=0. Increasing a prefix is a
feasible direction, so R_k>=0. At a strict jump u_k>u_(k+1), the same
prefix can also be decreased slightly, so R_k=0. Thus

    R_k>=0, R_d=0, R_k(u_k-u_(k+1))=0.               (11)

Conversely, a decreasing u satisfying (11) is the unique minimizer.
For any decreasing v, summation by parts gives

    <u-z,v-u>
       =sum_(k<d) R_k[(v_k-v_(k+1))-(u_k-u_(k+1))]>=0.

Adding ||v-u||^2/2 to this expression gives the squared-distance
objective difference, proving the converse.

Let [b,c] be a maximal constant block of u, with level t. At both
boundaries R_(b-1)=R_c=0, including the endpoints 0 and d. Hence

    t=av_(b,c)(z),
    sum_(j=b)^k z_j <= (k-b+1)t       (b<=k<=c),
    sum_(j=k)^c z_j >= (c-k+1)t       (b<=k<=c).      (12)

For i in this block, choose p=b in (9). Every average av_(b,q) with
q>=i is <=t: before c this follows from the prefix inequality in (12),
and after c it follows by adding full later blocks and a prefix of a
later block, all of whose levels are <=t. Equality occurs at q=c.
This gives the upper bound t in (9). Conversely, for every p<=i take
q=c. If p lies in this block, (12) gives av_(p,c)>=t. If p is earlier,
decompose [p,c] into a suffix of its first block and successive full
blocks; all their levels are >=t. This again gives av_(p,c)>=t.
Thus (9) equals t. This proves (9) for every i.

Now put g=y-u. By (2) and (11),

    sum_(i<=k)g_i=F_d({1,...,k})-R_k<=k(d-k)/d,
    sum_i g_i=0.                                    (13)

We also need g to be decreasing. Inside a constant block of u, its
differences are exactly those of y, so they are nonnegative. At the end
c of a block, (12) gives z_c>=u_c; at the first coordinate c+1 of the
next block it gives z_(c+1)<=u_(c+1). Therefore

    g_c=a_c+z_c-u_c >= a_c > a_(c+1)
          >=a_(c+1)+z_(c+1)-u_(c+1)=g_(c+1).

Consequently the prefix bounds (13) imply EVERY subset bound: the sum
over any k coordinates is no larger than the first k sorted coordinates.
So g belongs to K_d, in the real Euclidean metric.

Finally, for every v in K_d, summation by parts yields

    <u,v-g>
      =sum_(k<d)(u_k-u_(k+1)) sum_(i<=k)(v_i-g_i)<=0. (14)

At a nonzero jump in u, (11) says R_k=0, so the prefix of g in (13)
equals the body's bound, whereas that of v is at most that bound.
The total-sum term is zero. Formula (14) is exactly (7), hence g is
the true projection. Undoing the sorting permutation proves (10) for x.
Ties cause no ambiguity in the physical gradient: exchanging equal
coordinates of x preserves the problem and uniqueness fixes its projection.

An explicit form of the state on a maximal block [b,c] is

    u_i = av_(b,c)(y) - (d+1-b-c)/d,
    g_i = y_i-av_(b,c)(y)+(d+1-b-c)/d,    b<=i<=c.    (15)

Thus block coordinate differences in the projection equal the corresponding
differences of y. At a physical GD step h they change in the iterate by
the factor 1-h. In particular h>1 reverses every nonconstant old block.
Blocks may also interleave across their former boundaries. A claim that
the chronological GD blocks can only merge would therefore require an
additional argument, not a proximal-path monotonicity citation.

## 5. Explicit all-word trajectory, values, and all interpolation rows

Fix ANY finite nonnegative word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), any d>=2 and any x_0
with R^2=||x_0-bar(x_0)e||^2>0. Let pi_0 list original coordinate labels
in decreasing order of x_0. At each physical t perform the following
mathematical recurrence:

    y_(t,i)=x_(t,pi_t(i)),
    z_(t,i)=y_(t,i)-a_i,
    u_(t,i)=min_(p<=i) max_(q>=i) av_(p,q)(z_t),
    v_(t,i)=(1-h_t)y_(t,i)+h_t u_(t,i),
    y_(t+1,k)=v_(t,sigma_t(k)),
    pi_(t+1)(k)=pi_t(sigma_t(k)).                     (16)

Here sigma_t sorts v_t in decreasing order; ties may be broken by the
original coordinate labels pi_t(i). For the terminal time evaluate u_n
by the same formula but apply no extra step. The gradient in physical
coordinates is

    g_(t,pi_t(i))=y_(t,i)-u_(t,i).

Equations (9)--(10) show inductively that (16) is EXACTLY
x_(t+1)=x_t-h_t grad Phi_d(x_t), with its original h_t. Sorting is an
orthogonal relabeling for that state only; pi_t lifts every coordinate
back to its physical label. No chronological step or enclosing parameter
is reordered. Means are preserved since sum u_t=sum y_t.

The true-distance normalized payoff of this single actual function is

    V_d(h,x_0)
       = [sum_i y_(n,i)^2-sum_i u_(n,i)^2]/R^2.       (17)

This is an all-word recurrence and payoff law with no remaining continuous
optimization. It is valid even if the number of blocks grows, shrinks or
changes nonmonotonically. It is not asserted to optimize over x_0 or d.
As a legal instance it gives V_d(h,x_0)<=W_n(h).

All ordered interpolation inequalities follow from the actual function,
not merely from adjacent consistency. For physical samples let

    G_i=P_d(x_i), Y_i=x_i-G_i, F_i=Phi_d(x_i).

Add the closest minimizer sample x_star=bar(x_0)e, G_star=0, F_star=0.
For EVERY ordered pair, direct substitution of
F_i=<x_i,G_i>-||G_i||^2/2 gives

    Q_ij=F_i-F_j+<G_i,x_j-x_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<G_i-G_j,Y_j><=0.                          (18)

The inequality is (7) at j because G_i belongs to K_d, including G_star.
At the optimum Y_star=x_star is orthogonal to K_d. Thus (18) includes
all remote, incoming-terminal, outgoing-terminal and both optimum rows.

## 6. One frozen growing calibration: every pair reverses, then enters the core

Let d=2r>=4. Define centered orthogonal vectors A and b by

    A_(2j-1)=A_(2j)=Abar_j=(d+2-4j)/d,
    b_(2j-1)=1/(2d), b_(2j)=-1/(2d),   1<=j<=r.

Freeze the primary initial point

    x_0=2A+b.                                       (19)

The body is still precisely K_d. For a useful scope extension of this
same body and pair pattern, we also prove the formulas for

    x_0=gamma A+b,             1<=gamma<=2.           (20)

This is a symbolic amplitude interval, not an executed parameter search
or a change of submodular structure. Formula (19) remains the selected
nonlinear calibration. Centering is exact. Therefore the closest initial
minimizer is zero, despite the full line of minimizers in (8).

The rank vector has a_(2j-1)=Abar_j+1/d and a_(2j)=Abar_j-1/d.
The initial point is decreasing: inside a pair its gap is 1/d, and
between pairs the gap is (4gamma-1)/d>0. Its z=x_0-a has entries

    z_(2j-1)=(gamma-1)Abar_j-1/(2d),
    z_(2j)=(gamma-1)Abar_j+1/(2d).

For gamma>1 the exact decreasing isotonic residual has r distinct blocks,
each equal to one adjacent pair, with levels (gamma-1)Abar_j. Indeed its
R_(2j-1)=1/(2d)>0, R_(2j)=0, and its block levels strictly decrease.
These are the full conditions (11). For gamma=1 all levels merge to zero.
It follows that

    G_0=A+b, Y_0=(gamma-1)A,
    F_0=(gamma-1/2)||A||^2+||b||^2/2.                (21)

For gamma>1 this is an actual nonquadratic query. Its residual Y_0 exposes
a face with r independent pair directions: the convex hull of the 2^r
vertices obtained by swapping the two ranks independently in every pair.
Each projected pair Abar_j plus/minus 1/(2d) is strictly between that
pair's endpoint ranks Abar_j plus/minus 1/d. The block state is therefore
not a formal or degenerate active-set prescription.

Let the first step be 1+alpha, with 0<alpha<1/2. The actual first iterate is

    X_1=(gamma-1-alpha)A-alpha b.                    (22)

For the frozen gamma=2, each pair has reversed. Sorting only exchanges
the two original labels in each pair, because the gap between successive
sorted pairs is (4-5alpha)/d>0. The sorted first point has entries

    y_(1,2j-1)=(1-alpha)Abar_j+alpha/(2d),
    y_(1,2j)=(1-alpha)Abar_j-alpha/(2d).

For every proper even k and odd k respectively, its exact prefix sums are

    sum_(i<=k)y_(1,i)=(1-alpha) k(d-k)/d,                     k even,
    sum_(i<=k)y_(1,i)=(1-alpha) k(d-k)/d+(-1+3alpha/2)/d,      k odd.
                                                               (23)

The identities follow by summing Abar_1,...,Abar_j, whose sum is
j(d-2j)/d, and then the possible first member of the next pair.
Since -1+3alpha/2<0, (23) puts X_1 in (1-alpha)K_d and strictly in the
relative interior of K_d. Thus G_1=X_1 and Y_1=0: all residual blocks
have merged into a single block. This is the exact nonlinear face-to-core
transition in dimension d, with a real rank reversal in every old pair.

The entire interval (20) also enters the core. The vector A is the
average of a and the permutation swapping each adjacent pair, hence A in
K_d. Also b in K_d: its total is zero and every k-coordinate sum is at
most k/(2d)<=k(d-k)/d for 1<=k<d. With t=gamma-1-alpha we have

    |t|<=1-alpha,       |t|+alpha<=1.

Central symmetry, convexity and 0 in K_d imply
tA-alpha b in K_d, proving the claim for (22). This proof does not
assume the same sorting permutation throughout the amplitude interval.

## 7. Unchanged physical hierarchy and every remaining update

For an integer m>=2 and a real tau with 0<tau<m, set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-tau/m,
    c=lambda(1+tau/m), alpha=beta/c,
    H_(0;m,tau)=(),
    H_(j+1;m,tau)=(H_(j;m,tau),1+alpha c^j,H_(j;m,tau)), 0<=j<m.

Every child uses the SAME enclosing (m,tau). The physical word is
H_(m;m,tau), of length n=2^m-1. Tau=1 is the original ruler family;
tau=1/4 is the preferred diagnostic. No shorter relabeled word is used.
For growing dimension take d=2^m in (19), although all conclusions below
hold independently for any even d>=4.

Let nu_2(k) be the exponent of 2 dividing a positive integer k, and let
s_2(i) be the number of ones in the binary expansion of a nonnegative
integer i. The concatenation gives the exact physical step at zero-based
index t:

    h_t=1+alpha c^(nu_2(t+1)),          0<=t<n.       (24)

To check this by induction, the bridge joining two length-(2^j-1) words
is at t=2^j-1 and has nu_2(t+1)=j. The left child keeps its indices.
An index of the right child has t+1=2^j+s for 1<=s<2^j, and
nu_2(2^j+s)=nu_2(s), since the power of 2 dividing s is smaller than 2^j.
This reproduces the same child steps with the same enclosing parameters;
the base case is the empty word followed by its first bridge.

For a prefix of i steps, count each power of 2 dividing the integers
1,...,i. This gives

## 2. Actual backward blocks, including zeros and caps

For 0<=theta<=theta_sp put

    R(theta)=C exp(-kappa theta),
    e(theta)=(cos theta,-sin theta),
    t(theta)=(-sin theta,-cos theta),
    v(theta)=R(theta)e(theta)=(p(theta),-q(theta)),
    n(theta)=e(theta)+kappa t(theta),
    K=conv({0} union {v(theta):0<=theta<=theta_sp}).

The endpoints are (C,0) and (epsilon,-1). With Delta=phi-theta,

    <n(theta),v(phi)>/R(theta)
       =exp(-kappa Delta)(cos Delta+kappa sin Delta).

Its derivative in Delta is
-(1+kappa^2)exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta. Since |Delta|<pi/2,
its maximum is one at zero. The value at the added point0 is zero.

Differentiation gives

    p'=-R(kappa cos theta+sin theta)<0,

point v_j=v(theta_j), use alpha=alpha_j. If

## 3. Finite local functions and their exact zero wedges

Take a local checkpoint b_loc>=1+epsilon^(-2), and a positive sigma
satisfying

    sigma(P+epsilon b_loc)<=1,
    sigma[P+epsilon+(1+Q)/epsilon]<=1.                  (11)

Let

    z_circ=(1-sigma(epsilon+P),sigma(1+Q))=(c_1,c_2),
    U=1-sigma(P+epsilon b_loc), Y=sigma Q,
    V={0,v(0),v_0,...,v_r},

    f_loc(x)=min_z[phi(z)+||x-z||^2/2].                 (12)

Every plane remains in V, including both endpoints and every actual
projected slope. Since
(p,-q)=[(p-epsilon q)/C](C,0)+q(epsilon,-1), its coefficients are
nonnegative. Thus the exact zero set of phi is

    Z_phi={z:z_1<=c_1, epsilon(z_1-c_1)-(z_2-c_2)<=0}.  (13)

For clarity, the envelope properties used here have elementary proofs.
A nonnegative finite affine maximum J having a zero has a unique
proximal minimizer z at each x, by coercivity and strict convexity of

For another pair z',g', subgradient monotonicity gives
||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>. Using z as a trial point gives
env_1 J(x+w)<=env_1 J(x)+<g,w>+||w||^2/2; if z' is the new proximal
point, the subgradient at z gives
env_1 J(x+w)>=env_1 J(x)+<g,w>+||w-(z'-z)||^2/2. These prove convexity,
differentiability, gradient g, and 1-Lipschitz gradient. Attainment and
nonnegativity prove argmin(env_1 J)={J=0}, with minimum zero.

At x_j=z_circ+sigma r_j the point x_j-sigma v_j is proximal: the
projection inequality against all v in V makes sigma v_j an active

is at least U and its second belongs to[0,Y].

## 4. Source realization: one static function and every physical step

To prove it, apply the upper bound to V(z)=F(z)-<grad F(y),z> at x
with w=-grad V(x); y minimizes V. Adding(17) and its exchanged version

At the start of stage i the frozen coordinates are ell'_j+D'_j U'_j

### A. An exact harmonic bound for each complete ordered child

Run the actual Section 2 backward construction on ONE complete H_j,
0<=j<=m, with the unchanged enclosing (m,tau). At a backward step
alpha, let y_mass=1+the sum of all physical steps strictly after it
within this H_j. This is a scalar mass, not the vertical coordinate
y_j of Section 2. If the step has tree level ell, its complete right
child H_ell lies strictly after it. Consequently y_mass>=M_ell and

    x_mass:=alpha/y_mass
       =(1+d_ell)/y_mass <= c-2+1/y_mass <3/2.        (46c)

Here d_ell<= (c-2)M_ell follows from (24). In reverse order y_mass
starts at 1 and increases to 1+S_j=M_j, with consecutive increments
equal to the actual alpha's. This bookkeeping retains their order.

For x>=0, log(1+x)>=2x/(2+x): their difference is zero at zero and
its derivative is x^2/[(1+x)(2+x)^2]>=0. Thus, if
ell_mass=log(1+x_mass), (46c) gives

    x_mass <= (1+x_mass/2)ell_mass
            <= (c/2+1/(2*y_mass))ell_mass.

Also log(1+x_mass)<=x_mass and x_mass<3/2 imply

    ell_mass/y_mass
       <=x_mass/y_mass
       =(1+x_mass)[1/y_mass-1/(y_mass+alpha)]
       <=(5/2)[1/y_mass-1/(y_mass+alpha)].

Both sums now telescope in the actual reverse order. Define
Hharm_j=sum_(steps in H_j) alpha/y_mass. Then

    Hharm_j <= (c/2)log M_j+5/4.                      (46d)

The empty H_0 has Hharm_0=0 and is included. This is a symbolic finite
sum inequality, not an executed recurrence or a continuous flow.

### B. A bound on every DISCRETE angle, with caps included

gamma_step=phi_pol-theta. Section 2 gives
0<=gamma_step<pi/2: before a cap, phi_pol is at least the previous
projected angle, and the new projected angle is no larger; at a cap
theta=0. These observations include a zero step.

In the uncapped case, equation (6) is exactly

    sin gamma_step
       =kappa*cos gamma_step
           +kappa*(alpha-1)*R(theta)/rho_loc.

In the capped case the cap test (5) gives the SAME relation with <=

    sin gamma_step <= kappa*[1+alpha*C/rho_loc].      (46e)

    sin gamma_step < (11/2)*kappa <11/1536<1/100.

    rho_loc>=eta_turn*y_mass.                         (46f)

# A two-potential GD join: complete boundary obstruction and one bounded repair

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. Worker max4, allocated
round61 after completed baseline60, attempted ceiling62. Guidance
9206de0248154e84 and plan f0214728a76acdfb. No formal gate is allocated.
Every new assertion below belongs to this one joint draft, not to the fact
graph. The original asymptotic exact-profile minimax problem remains OPEN.

## 1. Question, accepted inputs, and the one mechanism

The original algorithm is x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L) grad f(x_i), with a fixed
nonnegative word h, on any finite-dimensional convex differentiable
L-smooth function having a minimizer x_star. Its objective error is
W_n(h)=sup 2(f(x_n)-f_star)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2). The denominator benchmark
is the ORIGINAL all-split B_n=1+2S_bullet(n), and U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290, proof paragraph1, supplies the full directed
smooth-convex interpolation inequalities. Accepted04219554e41d9750,
proof Sections10--12, supplies the original primitive identity and its
actual binary joins. Accepted5e1848ee0b153f5f requires an actual full
primitive seed for its conditional amplification. Its scalar power
argument is not arbitrary-template physical inflation. No new use of
an accepted conditional amplification is made here.

Shared4ad2db6604a59a2c,4f623d6a2c835679,9be1a10ee154498a and
2a2831acc4633001 were read as warnings about particular reversal,
virtual-oracle and coefficient lifts. None is assumed as a theorem.
This pilot uses neither reversed children nor virtual child queries.
It has no primitive-capacity assumption on the D child; its first D
child is explicitly outside that class, as checked below.

Normalize L=1, translate the selected minimizer to0 and subtract f_star.
At every actual query put g_i=grad f(x_i), f_i=f(x_i), and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 x_star=g_star=f_star=0.

Every ordered Q_ij is nonpositive. A full certificate for an inequality
E>=0 means an identity E+sum_(i!=j) lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram>, with ALL
lambda_ij>=0 and M positive semidefinite on the entire original formal
space (x_0,g_0,...,g_n). The matrix pairing is trace(M^T Gram).
Every unlisted multiplier is zero. Diagonal multipliers are zero.
Formal gradients are never identified or deleted, even at zero steps.

For t>=0 and a fixed real eta in(0,1], define two actual-state potentials

 P_t(x)=||x||^2+2t f(x),
 K_t^eta(x)=||x||^2+2t f(x)+eta t^2||grad f(x)||^2.          (1)

Initially eta=1. The ONE permitted repair is eta=1/2. General eta below
is an analysis of this same coefficient weakening, not further repairs.
For t>0 and a nonzero gradient these potentials are distinct. All their
coefficients are real and nonnegative. They are coercive in the selected
distance: K_t^eta>=P_t>=||x||^2 and P_t>=2t f(x). Moreover

 P_0(x)=K_0^eta(x)=||x||^2,
 P_t(x)<=(1+t)||x||^2,
 K_t^eta(x)<=(1+t+eta t^2)||x||^2.                         (2)

The upper estimates use ||grad f(x)||<=||x|| and f(x)<=||x||^2/2.
Thus a nonzero initial parameter has a normalization cost; it is not
free. The proposed root starts at t=0, so its budget is exactly the
ORIGINAL initial distance. At L>0, replace f by (f-f_star)/L,
g by grad f/L and x by x-x_star in all formulas.

Let s(w) be the actual sum and n(w) the actual length of a word w.
A D-type child satisfies P_t(start)>=P_(t+s(w))(end).
A K-type child satisfies K_t^eta(start)>=P_(t+s(w))(end).
The base certificates below hold for EVERY t>=0. At recursive uses a
child must have its asserted certificate at the particular incoming t;
this requirement is never inferred from its length or sum alone.
A certified D child is also K-type at the same t by adding the PSD
term eta t^2||g_start||^2, not by erasing it.

The algorithm never evaluates a potential to choose a step. Potential
parameters and bridges are predetermined analysis data. Terminal
gradients in identities do not add an algorithmic query or an update.

## 2. Actual base children and their complete original certificates

Use the distinct actual children

                    D0=(3/2),       K0=(1).              (3)

For a single step d write y=x-d g_0 and g_1=grad f(y).
The following direct expansion will check both base identities:

 P_t(x)-P_(t+d)(y)+2d Q_(0,star)+2(t+d)Q_(1,0)
 =d(2-d)||g_0||^2+d||g_1||^2+2d(d-1)<g_0,g_1>
       +t[||g_0||^2+||g_1||^2+2(d-1)<g_0,g_1>].         (4)

To check it, insert Q_(0,star)=f_0-<g_0,x>+||g_0||^2/2
and Q_(1,0)=f_1-f_0+d<g_1,g_0>+||g_1-g_0||^2/2.
All value coefficients and x mixed terms cancel. The remaining terms
are exactly the displayed polynomial in the two independent gradients.

For D0, d=3/2, the ONLY nonzero multipliers among all six directed
pairs on {star,0,1} are

 lambda_(0,star)=3,        lambda_(1,0)=3+2t.              (5)

The full x row is zero. The remaining two-gradient matrix is

 H_D(t)=[[3/4+t, 3/4+t/2],
         [3/4+t/2, 3/2+t]].                              (6)

Its full quadratic form equals

 (3/4)||g_0+g_1||^2+(3/4)||g_1||^2
   +(t/2)[||g_0+g_1||^2+||g_0||^2+||g_1||^2].           (7)

This proves its PSD and every original coefficient sign for all t>=0.

For K0, d=1, add eta t^2||g_0||^2 to (4). The ONLY nonzero
multipliers are

 lambda_(0,star)=2,        lambda_(1,0)=2(t+1).           (8)

The full remainder is

 (eta t^2+t+1)||g_0||^2+(t+1)||g_1||^2,                 (9)

with zero x row. This proves the K-type certificate, retaining the
entire incoming gradient credit with its positive sign. Equation(4)
at d=1 also proves that this word is D-type without that extra term.

The first child in (3) is genuinely nonprimitive. On f(x)=x^2/2 from
x_0=1, its endpoint is -1/2 and every Q_ij, including optimum pairs,
is zero. The primitive energy of accepted04219554e41d9750 is

 2(3/2)(1/2-1/8)+(3/2)(1-3/2)
                  -(3/2)(5/2)(1/4)=-9/16<0.            (10)

Thus no nonnegative-multiplier/full-PSD primitive certificate exists
for this D child. It is not being supplied as a primitive seed.

## 3. The proposed recursive physical join and its exact identity

Take any actual D child u and K child v with their needed certificates,
of lengths n_u,n_v and sums s_u,s_v. Fix the incoming parameter t>=0.
Let p be the actual last query of u, and set

 a=t+s_u,   c=a+beta,   y=x_p-beta g_p,   beta>=0.

The proposed parent is the actual concatenation

                         w=(u,beta,v).                 (11)

Its true length is n_u+1+n_v and its true sum is s_u+beta+s_v.
All queries are on the SAME static function, and v starts at y.
Let z be the actual final query. The polynomial telescoping identity is

 P_t(x_start)-P_(c+s_v)(x_z)
   =[P_t(x_start)-P_a(x_p)]
    +[P_a(x_p)-K_c^eta(y)]
    +[K_c^eta(y)-P_(c+s_v)(x_z)].                        (12)

The first and third brackets are precisely the two named child
contracts. The missing transition is the middle bracket

 B_(a,beta,eta)=P_a(x)-K_(a+beta)^eta(x-beta grad f(x)).   (13)

If (13) had a full certificate, embeddings of the three original
arrays would add with nonnegative coefficients. Their PSD remainders
would be pulled back through the ACTUAL starting positions, on every
formal coordinate. Equation(12) would then prove the D parent; adding
eta t^2||g_start||^2 would also make it a K parent.
No coefficient, endpoint value or gradient credit is reset.

This is a conditional identity for arbitrary admissible children,
not a claim that the middle bracket is nonnegative. Its full cone is
examined next. At a root with t=0, a certified parent of sum s>0
would imply W_(n(w))(w)<=1/s by (1)--(2). An unbounded recursive
construction and comparison against B_(n(w)) would still be required.

## 4. The ENTIRE one-bridge original multiplier cone

For the bridge alone retain the independent formal vectors (x,g_0,g_1),
the two values f_0,f_1, x_1=x-beta g_0, and the optimum. There are SIX
ordered interpolation slots, without a support restriction.

Any PSD certificate for (13) must have zero x row: its x^2 coefficient
is zero, since the two distance terms cancel. A PSD symmetric matrix
with a zero diagonal entry has its entire corresponding row zero
(apply its quadratic form to the coordinate vector plus a real
multiple of any other coordinate vector). The x mixed coefficients
therefore force

 lambda_(0,star)=2beta,     lambda_(1,star)=0.             (14)

Sum the coefficients of the two formal values. The bracket contributes
-2beta, and (14) contributes +2beta. The only remaining sum is
-lambda_(star,0)-lambda_(star,1). Both incoming optimum coefficients
are nonnegative, so both are zero. Finally, individual value
cancellation forces, for some real u>=0,

 lambda_(0,1)=u,           lambda_(1,0)=u+2c,
 c=a+beta.                                                     (15)

These formulas account for every original directed multiplier.
No extra sign assumption has been made. The full remainder is zero
on the x row and has two-gradient block

 M_(a,beta,eta)(u)=
 [[c+beta-beta^2+(1-beta)u,
                 c(beta-1)+(beta-2)u/2],

certificate. This is an exact parameterization of certificates of this
form, not an appeal to unproved dual attainment for an arbitrary
performance measure. It includes beta=0 and both formal gradients.

Two directions have a useful exact interpretation independent of u:

 (1,1) M (1,1)^T
    =beta^2+beta+2a beta-eta(a+beta)^2,                    (17)

    =1+a-[1+a+beta+eta(a+beta)^2](1-beta)^2.              (18)

Equation(17) is the actual constant-gradient Huber bridge; equation(18)
is the actual unit-quadratic bridge. They are not fictitious oracles.

## 8. True recursive horizons and the precise asymptotic consequence

To make the proposed recursion concrete, start with (3). At each level
use (11) on the two child types and, if successful, label the same
parent word both D and K using the explicit positive initial-credit
promotion after (12). The selected repair fixes beta_0=1, producing
(27); all later beta_j are arbitrary predetermined nonnegative reals.
They are not selected from function or gradient observations.

Write D_j,K_j for these words. Formally the intended recursion is

 D_(j+1)=K_(j+1)=(D_j,beta_j,K_j).

The true physical length, even if beta_j=0, is

                n(D_j)=n(K_j)=2^(j+1)-1.                (39)

For j>=1 both sums agree; call them s_j. Since s_1=7/2,

 s_(j+1)=2s_j+beta_j,  s_j>=(7/2)2^(j-1).              (40)

These are symbolic counting identities and an induction, not an
executed recurrence. At a root with t=0, the proposed level j+1
join must recharge at a=s_j. In particular s_3>=14, so Section7
excludes EVERY bridge at the next join: its intended true horizon
would be2^5-1=31. Therefore this fixed-half-credit modular proof
recursion must fail at or before that level. This statement even
grants the child contracts at all required incoming parameters;
a child-domain failure can only occur earlier.

For any other fixed eta>0 in the same range, (40) eventually exceeds
6/eta, so the identical obstruction prevents an unbounded iteration
of this join. No asymptotic upper-bound family is established and
there is consequently no warranted comparison of its limiting error
with the ORIGINAL B_n, no fixed relative improvement, and no answer
to the original minimax problem. A scalar mass law or matrix eigenvalue
would not repair the failed actual transition.

## 2. The unchanged Euclidean body and its support

Let e be the all-ones vector, E_d={x:<e,x>=0}, and

    a_i=(d+1-2i)/d,             1<=i<=d.

If the two disjoint differences of sets A and B have sizes p and q,
expanding the cardinality quadratic gives

    F_d(A)+F_d(B)-F_d(A union B)-F_d(A intersection B)=2pq/d>=0.

Also F_d(empty)=F_d([d])=0 and

    sum_(i=1)^k a_i=k(d-k)/d.                         (2.1)

Every permutation of a is in K_d because its largest k-coordinate
sum is (2.1). Singleton and complementary-singleton constraints give
|g_i|<=(d-1)/d for g in K_d. Thus K_d is nonempty and compact.

If w_(pi(1))>=...>=w_(pi(d)), summation by parts gives

    <w,g>
      =sum_(k<d)(w_(pi(k))-w_(pi(k+1)))
                           sum_(i<=k)g_(pi(i))
      <=sum_(k<d)(w_(pi(k))-w_(pi(k+1))) k(d-k)/d
      =sum_i a_i w_(pi(i)).                          (2.2)

The permutation g_(pi(i))=a_i attains this bound. It follows that

    K_d=conv{permutations of a},
    sigma_d(w):=max_(g in K_d)<w,g>
      =sum_i a_i w_(pi(i))=(1/d)sum_(i<j)|w_i-w_j|.   (2.3)

For the convex-hull equality, if a point g of K_d were outside the
hull, let v be its closest hull point. Differentiating squared
distance along segments gives <g-v,t-v><=0 for all hull points t.
The direction g-v would then strictly separate g from that hull,
contradicting (2.2) and its attainment. The last equality in (2.3)
counts the d+1-2i occurrences of the i-th sorted coordinate.

The body is centrally symmetric since -a is a permutation of a.
It contains a relative neighborhood of zero in E_d: for centered g
and a set of size k,

    |sum_(i in A)g_i|<=||g|| sqrt(k(d-k)/d).

Since k(d-k)>=d-1 for 1<=k<d, the ball in E_d of radius
sqrt((d-1)/d) satisfies every constraint. A strictly smaller radius
satisfies every proper constraint strictly. All norms here and below
are the original coordinate Euclidean norms.

## 3. One static smooth function and its whole minimum set

Define the single static function

    Phi_d(x)=max_(g in K_d){<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.          (3.1)

Let P_d(x) be the unique closest point of x in K_d. Completing the
square identifies the maximizer in (3.1) as P_d(x). The closest-point
condition, proved by expanding squared distances along segments, is

    <x-P_d(x),g-P_d(x)><=0  for every g in K_d.        (3.2)

Adding this condition at x and x' gives

    <x-x',P_d(x)-P_d(x')>>=||P_d(x)-P_d(x')||^2.

Consequently P_d is 1-Lipschitz. Evaluating each maximum in (3.1)
at the other maximizer shows

    0<=Phi_d(x')-Phi_d(x)-<P_d(x),x'-x>
       <=<P_d(x')-P_d(x),x'-x><=||x'-x||^2.

This proves differentiability and

    grad Phi_d(x)=P_d(x),
    Phi_d(x)=(||x||^2-||x-P_d(x)||^2)/2.             (3.3)

Convexity follows from the maximum representation. There is no
dimension factor in smoothness: on a neighborhood of zero in E_d,
P_d(x)=x, so its optimal global Lipschitz constant is exactly 1.

Writing bar(x)=d^(-1)sum_i x_i, the full minimum set is

    argmin Phi_d=R e,  min Phi_d=0,
    dist(x,argmin Phi_d)^2=||x-bar(x)e||^2.            (3.4)

Indeed Phi_d>=0 by g=0 and Phi_d(te)=0 because K_d is centered.
For nonzero z=x-bar(x)e, a sufficiently small epsilon in (0,2)
has epsilon z in K_d. Its value in (3.1) is
(epsilon-epsilon^2/2)||z||^2>0, excluding all other minimizers.
The distance assertion is orthogonal projection onto the line.

For any advertised L>0 use f=L Phi_d. Its actual GD with steps h_t/L
is x_(t+1)=x_t-h_t P_d(x_t). The body is not rescaled and h_t is

## 4. Exact interval-average law, including sorting and all subset rows

For sorted coordinates y_1>=...>=y_d put z_i=y_i-a_i. For a contiguous

residual and projection in these coordinates are

Here is a full proof of the needed ordered projection assertion.
Minimize ||u-z||^2/2 on the decreasing cone u_1>=...>=u_d. Existence
and uniqueness follow from coercivity and strict convexity. Define

Expansion of the squared objective now proves the converse.
On a maximal constant block [b,c] of u with level t, (4.2) implies

The vector g=y-u is centered and obeys

proves sufficiency. Conditions (13) imply c_1>=c_2/epsilon>=0, so phi
vanishes on z_1<=0,z_2>=0. Also U>=0, and for any slope in V,

    <v,(U,Y)-z_circ>=sigma[(1-b_loc)epsilon p+q]<=0.

Consequently phi(U,y)=0 whenever y>=Y. These two zero regions use only
THIS stage's epsilon and do not require the next stage's epsilon.

For completeness, if J is a nonnegative finite maximum of affine
functions with a zero, its envelope env_1 J has a unique proximal
minimizer z at every x. This follows from coercivity and strict
convexity of J(z)+||x-z||^2/2. The vector g=x-z belongs to partial J(z).
For a second proximal pair z',g', subgradient monotonicity gives

    ||g-g'||^2<=<g-g',x-x'>.

The trial point z yields
env_1 J(x+w)<=env_1 J(x)+<g,w>+||w||^2/2. The subgradient inequality
at z, applied to the proximal point z' for x+w, yields
env_1 J(x+w)>=env_1 J(x)+<g,w>+||w-(z'-z)||^2/2. These inequalities
prove differentiability with gradient g and its 1-Lipschitz property.
Convexity follows by taking convex combinations of trial pairs in the
jointly convex defining objective. Nonnegativity and attainment give
min env_1 J=0 and argmin env_1 J={J=0}.

At each x_j^loc=z_circ+sigma r_j, projection of r_j onto K shows that
z_j^loc=x_j^loc-sigma v_j is proximal: for every w in V,
<w-v_j,r_j-v_j><=0, so sigma v_j is an active subgradient of phi there.
Thus the exact local gradient and value are

    grad f_loc(x_j^loc)=sigma v_j,
    f_loc(x_j^loc)=sigma^2[<v_j,r_j>-||v_j||^2/2].      (16)

The local chronological path starts at (1,0), follows ALL alpha_j,
reaches (1-sigma P,sigma Q), and its checkpoint b_loc sends it to
(U,Y+sigma b_loc). During the ordinary block the first coordinate is
at least U and the second belongs to [0,Y]. These claims follow by
subtracting successive alpha_j sigma v_(j-1) and noting p,q>=0.

## 4. Source assembly with independent stage parameters

For each i<k apply Sections 2--3 with its own (kappa_i,epsilon_i),
the local list block_i/2, and b_loc=b_i/2. In THIS source assembly,
P'_i,Q'_i and r'_(i,j),v'_(i,j) always denote these HALF-step outputs
and states. Use exactly

    sigma'_i=1/[C_i s_i/2+epsilon_i b_i/2+A_i].          (17)

By (10) and (1), both conditions (13) hold. Define the resulting local
objects phi'_i,f'_i,c'_(i,1),c'_(i,2),U'_i,Y'_i by (14). Let

    G'_i=sigma'_i b_i/2=b_i/(C_i s_i+2A_i+epsilon_i b_i),
    D'_0=1, ell'_0=0,
    D'_(i+1)=D'_i G'_i,
    ell'_(i+1)=D'_i sigma'_i Q'_i,
    delta'=D'_k/(1+s_k).                               (18)

For d>0 define Hub_d(z)=0 for z<=0, z^2/2 for 0<=z<=d, and
dz-d^2/2 for z>=d. Its derivative is respectively 0,z,d, so it is
convex and 1-smooth. In R^(k+1), with x_0=e_0, define the SINGLE
STATIC function

    F(x)=(1/2)sum_(i<k)(D'_i)^2
          f'_i((x_i-ell'_i)/D'_i,x_(i+1)/D'_i)
                 +(1/2)Hub_(delta')(x_k-ell'_k).        (19)

All scales are positive and finite and are fixed before the run.
Every term is nonnegative, and zero is a common minimizer by (15).
Each scaled local term has its 1-smooth upper quadratic bound on the
two coordinates before the factor 1/2. Every coordinate is counted at
most twice, including the tail. Hence

    F(x+w)<=F(x)+<grad F(x),w>+||w||^2/2.

This proves the advertised global smoothness. More explicitly, for a
convex differentiable function satisfying this upper bound, apply it
to V(z)=F(z)-<grad F(y),z> at x with w=-grad V(x). Since y minimizes
V, this gives

    F(x)-F(y)-<grad F(y),x-y>
                      >=||grad F(x)-grad F(y)||^2/2.  (20)

Adding the exchanged inequality and applying Cauchy--Schwarz proves
that grad F is 1-Lipschitz on the full space.

At the start of stage i, coordinates j<i are frozen at
ell'_j+D'_j U'_j, the current coordinate is ell'_i+D'_i, and later
coordinates are zero. During this stage, x_i>=ell'_i and
0<=x_(i+1)<=ell'_(i+1). Every preceding component is at its OWN
post-checkpoint zero region: its first local coordinate is its U'_j,
and its second is at least Y'_j. Every future component is at its OWN
pre-activation zero region, with first local coordinate at most zero
and second zero. For j=i+1 the first assertion uses
x_(i+1)<=ell'_(i+1); for j>i+1 it uses ell'_j>=0. These separate tests
retain epsilon_j in each wedge and never transfer an epsilon value
from a neighbor. The tail is also inactive until its stage.

Thus the current summand is the only one with nonzero gradient. At
every ordinary query and at the query for the checkpoint, its exact
point is the embedded local x_j^loc, and its gradient and value are

    grad F(x)=D'_i sigma'_i v'_(i,j)/2 on coordinates (i,i+1),
    F(x)=(D'_i sigma'_i)^2
                [<v'_(i,j),r'_(i,j)>-||v'_(i,j)||^2/2]/2. (21)

All other gradient coordinates vanish. A physical step h_t therefore
implements the local step h_t/2 exactly. At checkpoint b_i the next
coordinate becomes ell'_(i+1)+D'_(i+1), and coordinate i freezes at
ell'_i+D'_i U'_i. This proves the induction through every physical
query, including zero steps and all eligibility equalities.

In the tail, if u is the already executed physical tail mass, then
x_k-ell'_k=D'_k-delta' u/2>=delta'. Therefore

    grad F(x)=delta' e_k/2,
    F(x)=[delta'(D'_k-delta' u/2)-(delta')^2/2]/2,
    2F(x_n)=(D'_k)^2/[2(1+s_k)].                      (22)

All earlier summands remain zero because the tail coordinate is at
least ell'_k. This includes the unqueried terminal sample.

The COMPLETE minimum set of (19) is the polyhedron

    C_source={x:x_i<=zeta'_i,
      epsilon_i x_i-x_(i+1)<=epsilon_i zeta'_i-D'_i c'_(i,2), i<k;
      x_k<=ell'_k},
    zeta'_i=ell'_i+D'_i c'_(i,1).                       (23)

Necessity and sufficiency follow from nonnegativity of all summands
and the exact local wedges (15). It contains zero. When k>=1, e_0
violates its first horizontal constraint, so
0<rho_S^2:=dist(e_0,C_source)^2<=1.

Here is an exact finite, non-executed formula for the TRUE distance,
retaining all later rows. Let A_rad have rows e_i^T and
(epsilon_i e_i-e_(i+1))^T for i<k, followed by e_k^T. Let t_rad be
their right sides from (23). For each linearly independent row subset I,
let A_I be the submatrix, r_I=A_I e_0-(t_rad)_I,
K_I=A_I A_I^T, and lambda_I=K_I^(-1)r_I. Include the empty subset
with value zero. Then

    rho_S^2=max_(I independent,lambda_I>=0) r_I^T K_I^(-1)r_I. (24)

For any feasible x and any nonnegative row weights lambda,
||e_0-x||^2>=2lambda^T r_I-||A_I^T lambda||^2 by completing a square.
This proves each listed value is a lower bound. At the actual
projection x_*, e_0-x_* is in the cone of active row normals. To
justify that assertion, the finitely generated cone is closed: remove
linear dependences from any nonnegative representation until an
independent subset remains, giving a finite union of closed injective
images of orthants. If the normal were outside this cone, its residual
from projection onto the cone would have nonpositive inner product
with each active row and positive inner product with e_0-x_*. A small
move in that residual direction would preserve the active inequalities
and, by their strict slacks, every inactive inequality, contradicting
projection optimality. Reduce the normal's nonnegative representation
to an independent active subset. Activity then gives r_I=K_I lambda_I
and equality in (24). This is an identity, not a projection computation.

A quantitative bound uses just the two FIRST rows, while keeping the
entire polyhedron in the feasible set. Put
z_bar=(c'_(0,1),c'_(0,2),0,...,0). Then

    e_0-z_bar=sigma'_0(P'_0-epsilon_0 Q'_0)e_0
       +sigma'_0(1+Q'_0)(epsilon_0 e_0-e_1).           (25)

Both coefficients are nonnegative by (10), and the first two rows
are equalities at z_bar. Thus <e_0-z_bar,x-z_bar><=0 for every x in
the FULL C_source, whether or not z_bar is feasible for later rows.
Expanding squared distance and then using (11) with s_loc=s_0/2 gives

    rho_S^2>=(sigma'_0)^2[(epsilon_0+P'_0)^2+(1+Q'_0)^2]
            >=(sigma'_0)^2(s_0+2)^2/8.                (26)

Combining (18), (22) and (26), with D'_1=sigma'_0 b_0/2, proves

    E(F,h)<= b_0^2/[(s_0+2)^2(1+s_k)]
            *product_(i=1)^(k-1)
               [b_i/(C_i s_i+2A_i+epsilon_i b_i)]^2.  (27)

This is an UPPER comparison of the actual payoff, with the actual
half-step outputs used to prove its radius bound. It does not identify
the true distance with a one-stage terminal projection. For k=0,
the source family is F=Hub_(1/(1+s_0))/2 from 1. Its closest radius
is exactly 1 and its payoff is 1/[2(1+s_0)].

For any two actual samples a,b, including every minimizer and the
terminal sample, (20) implies the complete directed residual
Q_ab=F(x_a)-F(x_b)+<grad F(x_a),x_b-x_a>
+||grad F(x_a)-grad F(x_b)||^2/2 is nonpositive. All physical gradients
belong to R^(k+1), so their full Gram matrix is positive semidefinite.
No interpolation row is removed.

## 5. Main assembly with independent stage parameters

For each i<k use its own parameters in Sections 2--3, now with the
FULL physical ordinary list block_i and b_loc=b_i. Write P_i,Q_i and
r_(i,j),v_(i,j) for these full-step outputs and states. Define exactly

    M_i^tr=P_i+max(epsilon_i b_i,epsilon_i+(1+Q_i)/epsilon_i),
    sigma_i=1/M_i^tr,
    D_0=1, ell_0=0,
    D_(i+1)=D_i sigma_i(b_i-1),
    ell_(i+1)=D_i sigma_i(1+Q_i).                       (28)

Conditions (13) hold by definition. Let phi_i,c_(i,1),c_(i,2),U_i,Y_i
be the corresponding (14). Define one STATIC finite maximum and its
single envelope in R^(k+1), starting at e_0:

    Phi_i(z)=D_i^2 phi_i((z_i-ell_i)/D_i,z_(i+1)/D_i), i<k,
    delta=D_k/(1+2s_k), Phi_k(z)=delta max(z_k-ell_k,0),
    J(z)=max_(0<=i<=k)Phi_i(z), f=env_1 J.             (29)

All coefficients and planes are fixed before the run. The origin is
a zero of J by (15), so Section 3 proves that f is everywhere finite,
convex, differentiable, 1-smooth, and has attained minimum zero.

We check every old and future plane at each proposed proximal point.
In the active local block, the second proximal coordinate is
sigma_i(1+Q_i-y_j+q_j), which belongs to [0,sigma_i(1+Q_i)]. Its
nonnegativity follows from y_j<=1+Q_i; its upper bound is (12).
Its first proximal coordinate minus U_i is

    sigma_i[epsilon_i(b_i-1)+u_j-p_j]>=0,             (30)

using the full eligibility (2M) and (12). Embed this local proximal
point, leaving the earlier frozen coordinates unchanged and all later
coordinates zero. The immediately preceding term is zero because its
first local input is its own U_(i-1), and its second input is at least
ell_i/D_(i-1)=sigma_(i-1)(1+Q_(i-1))>=Y_(i-1). Earlier terms have
the same property from the frozen-coordinate induction. The immediately
following term is zero because its first local input is at most
(D_i sigma_i(1+Q_i)-ell_(i+1))/D_(i+1)=0 and its second is zero.
Every further term has first input -ell_j/D_j<=0 and second zero.
The future tail is zero as well. Each of these tests uses that term's
own epsilon_j in (15); no equality of neighboring epsilons is used.

The current Phi_i is nonnegative at the proposed proximal point and
attains the maximum J. Its local active plane is therefore active in
J. The vector x-z=D_i sigma_i v_(i,j) is its subgradient, proving that
z is the actual global proximal point. Thus all ordinary queries and
checkpoint queries have exactly

    grad f(x)=D_i sigma_i v_(i,j) on coordinates (i,i+1),
    f(x)=(D_i sigma_i)^2
                   [<v_(i,j),r_(i,j)>-||v_(i,j)||^2/2]. (31)

All other gradient coordinates are zero. At the start of each stage,
earlier coordinates are frozen at ell_j+D_j U_j, the current coordinate
is ell_i+D_i, and later coordinates vanish. A full physical ordinary
step is exactly the corresponding full local step. At b_i, the endpoint
gradient D_i sigma_i(epsilon_i,-1) gives frozen coordinate
ell_i+D_i U_i and new coordinate

    D_i sigma_i(Q_i+b_i)=ell_(i+1)+D_(i+1).

This proves the state induction through every physical entry. Zero
steps retain the identical gradient and value by the local definition;
the proof places no upper bound on an ordinary step.

In the tail, if u<=s_k is its already executed mass, the actual last
coordinate is ell_k+D_k-delta u. Its proposed proximal coordinate
is ell_k+D_k-delta(u+1)>=ell_k because delta=D_k/(1+2s_k).
The preceding term is in its post-checkpoint zero region; every earlier
term remains zero. Thus the tail plane is active and

    grad f(x)=delta e_k,
    f(x)=delta(D_k-delta u)-delta^2/2,
    2f(x_n)=D_k^2/(1+2s_k).                            (32)

This includes s_k=0, with the endpoint proximal coordinate equal to
ell_k. It proves the advertised physical terminal value, without an
extra hidden step.

The COMPLETE minimum set is

    C_main={x:x_i<=zeta_i,
      epsilon_i x_i-x_(i+1)<=epsilon_i zeta_i-D_i c_(i,2), i<k;
      x_k<=ell_k},
    zeta_i=ell_i+D_i c_(i,1).                          (33)

The point z_bar=(c_(0,1),c_(0,2),0,...,0) is feasible for (33).
For the first stage it is its center. For the second stage its first
local input is zero, because c_(0,2)=ell_1; all later local first
inputs are nonpositive. For stages i>=1, each second local input is zero. When k=1,
the terminal coordinate is exactly ell_1; when k>1 it is zero<=ell_k.
The first-stage normal identity (25), now unprimed and using full-step
outputs, proves <e_0-z_bar,x-z_bar><=0 for every feasible x. Therefore

    rho_M^2=dist(e_0,C_main)^2
           =sigma_0^2[(epsilon_0+P_0)^2+(1+Q_0)^2]>0.  (34)

There is no epsilon_1 in this normal calculation or feasibility test.
Combining (28), (32), and (34) yields the EXACT actual payoff

    E(f,h)=(b_0-1)^2/
       {[(epsilon_0+P_0)^2+(1+Q_0)^2](1+2s_k)}
        *product_(i=1)^(k-1)[(b_i-1)/M_i^tr]^2.        (35)

For k=0 use f=Hub_(1/(1+2s_0)) from 1. Its closest radius is 1 and
its payoff is H_base(h). Every ordered interpolation residual is
nonpositive: writing z_a=x_a-grad f(x_a), expansion gives

    Q_ab=J(z_a)-J(z_b)+<grad f(x_a),z_b-z_a><=0

by the subgradient inequality. This includes all physical samples,
the terminal point, and every minimizer; the full original Gram matrix
is automatically positive semidefinite. No pair of interpolation rows
or gradient coordinates is removed.

Let

    r_h=c(c-2), v_h=a/(c-2)=beta/r_h,

    2<c<121/50, 1/4<a<=u_j<21/50<1/2,

    epsilon_i^2<C_i^2-1<4/m+4/m^2<=6/m<=1/256,

    kappa_i theta_sp,i<log r_h<2/m,
    kappa_i<1/768<1/16, C_i<769/768.                   (39)

The angle estimate uses pi>3 and arctan epsilon_i<epsilon_i.

    X_i>((1-kappa_i^2)theta_sp,i^2/2)m
         >(134895/131072)m>m.

The exact identity
1+(1+kappa_i)T_i=(exp(X_i)-kappa_i)/(1-kappa_i)>=exp(X_i)
therefore yields

    A_i>16 C_i exp(m).                               (40)

This is a statement about each stage separately and permits arbitrary

Among any nonempty selected subset choose a globally minimum tree
level j. Both complete H_j children of that checkpoint contain only

    s>=M_j-1, t>=M_j-1, b=1+d_j.                      (41)

Deleting a selection only reclassifies its FULL physical b as ordinary,

## 7. Source: a common denominator for every mixed parameter choice

On H_m every ordinary block has s_i<=S_m<c^m<exp(m), since
exp(1)>5/2>c. The exact source denominator is

    C_i s_i+2A_i+epsilon_i b_i.

If C_i>=r_h, A_i>=2C_i makes this at least r_h(s_i+4). If C_i<r_h,
(40), r_h<2 and exp(m)>1 give

                      >2(exp(m)+4)>r_h(s_i+4).        (42)

Thus every stage, with no shared C_i,A_i or epsilon_i, has the same
valid denominator lower bound. Combining it with the actual first
radius comparison (27) gives the single upper functional

    E(F,H_m)<=Psi_S,

                *product_(i=1)^(k-1)[b_i/(r_h(s_i+4))]^2. (43)

This comparison holds for every eligible subset, including subsets
formed by deleting selections while retaining all remaining parameters.
It is neither an asserted equality for actual transfer factors nor
a lower certificate used in the wrong direction.

We now prove all-count deletion for (43), including its exceptional
first factor. While k>=2 choose a global minimum level j. Put
M=M_j, d=d_j, u=d/M, b=1+d and let s,t be its adjacent sums.
By (38),(41), s,t>=M-1 and 0<u<1/2, and
u(2+u)<=c(c-2)=r_h.

FIRST SELECTED MINIMUM. Cancelling all unchanged factors, deletion is
valid exactly when

    b(s+b+t+2)<=(s+2)r_h(t+4).                        (44)

The right side minus the left increases with s and t: the derivatives
are respectively r_h(t+4)-b and r_h(s+2)-b, both positive on (41).

Every displayed coefficient is nonnegative since r_h>1, u<=1/2.

NONFIRST, NONLAST SELECTED MINIMUM. The required comparison is

    b r_h(s+b+t+4)<=r_h^2(s+4)(t+4).

Divide by r_h. The difference again increases in s,t since both
derivatives have the form r_h(other+4)-b>0. At s=t=M-1 it equals

This proves the interior case with all neighboring original parameter

    b^2(1+s+b+t)/[(s+4)^2(1+t)],                     (47)

because r_h>=1. It decreases with t. Its s derivative has the sign

       <=(5/2)[(M/2+1)/(M+3)]^2<=5/8.               (48)

Each deletion makes Psi_S nondecreasing. Repeating until one selected

For the last singleton set X=1+s,Y=1+t, so X,Y>=M and

The strict last comparison in the first line is 1400<1413. Substitution

No common local pair was used in (42)--(50). Different parameters at

## 8. Main: actual full-step denominators with stage-dependent coefficients

First, for any one local pair define

    A_floor=epsilon+epsilon^(-1),
    C_floor=min(C,A_floor).

The function p(theta)+q(theta)/epsilon has minimum at an endpoint.
Its derivative divided by R is
(epsilon^(-1)-kappa)cos theta-(1+kappa/epsilon)sin theta. If its first
coefficient is nonpositive it is nonpositive throughout; otherwise it
changes sign once from positive to negative. The endpoint values are
C and A_floor. Every actual slope thus gives

    M_i^tr>=P_i+epsilon_i+(1+Q_i)/epsilon_i
       >=min(C_i,epsilon_i+epsilon_i^(-1))s_i
                                      +epsilon_i+epsilon_i^(-1). (51)

For C_i>=r_h, the inequality epsilon_i+epsilon_i^(-1)>=5/2>r_h
implies M_i^tr>=r_h(s_i+1). For C_i<r_h we need a surplus from the
actual chronological suffix, not an assertion M_i^tr>=A_i.

### 8.1 Exact discrete turning on each complete child

Fix ONE stage with C_i<r_h and suppress its subscript in this
subsection only. In addition to (39), the expansion in (37) gives

    kappa*m*theta_sp<44/25, log c<9/10.                (52)

Indeed r_h-1<7/(4m)+3/(8m^2)<44/(25m). Also
exp(9/10)>1+9/10+81/200+243/2000=4853/2000>121/50>c.

Run the Section 2 FULL-step backward definition on a complete H_j,
0<=j<=m, with its unchanged enclosing (m,tau). At each actual reverse
step alpha let y_mass=1+the sum of all steps strictly after it in this
H_j. If the step's tree level is ell, its full right child H_ell lies
after it, so y_mass>=M_ell. Define x_mass=alpha/y_mass. By (37),

    x_mass=(1+d_ell)/y_mass<=c-2+1/y_mass<3/2.         (53)

In reverse order y_mass starts at 1 and its successive increments are
the actual alpha's. This is mass bookkeeping retaining the exact order.

For x>=0, log(1+x)>=2x/(2+x), since the difference vanishes at zero

## 1. Physical words and local constants

All spaces, norms and inner products are finite-dimensional Euclidean.
The vector e_i is the standard coordinate vector indexed from zero;
the planar e(theta) defined below is a separate symbol.
For a finite nonnegative word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), gradient descent at

    E(f,h)=2(f(x_n)-min f)/dist(x_0,argmin f)^2.

    E_L(f,h)=2(f(x_n)-min f)/(L*dist(x_0,argmin f)^2),

## 2. One local curve: exact ordered backward states
