    Phi_i=max {U*r_i+Q*z_i-[(U+beta*Q)^2+Q^2]/2:
      0<=Q<=sigma_i,
      0<=U<=sigma_i*p(Q/sigma_i)-beta*Q}.                    (4.2)

Hence U_i>=0. If r_i<=0 then U_i=0 and

    Q_i=clip(z_i/kappa,0,sigma_i),
    Phi_i=Hub_(kappa*sigma_i)(z_i)/kappa.                    (4.3)

There are also the unconditional complementary sign facts

    U_i>0 implies x_i>A_i>=ell_i and Q_(i-1)=0;
    Q_i>0 implies x_(i+1)<ell_(i+1) and U_(i+1)=0.          (4.4)

The exact residual equations, including BOTH neighbors, are

    r_i^+=r_i-(h/2)(U_i+beta*Q_i-Q_(i-1)),
    z_i^+=z_i-(h/2)[kappa*Q_i-beta*Q_(i-1)-beta*Q_(i+1)
                                             +beta*U_i-U_(i+1)]. (4.5)

The retained value and the total normalized payoff are exactly

    V_m=2G_ret(x(N))=sum_(i=1)^k Phi_i(x(N)),
    B_(n_m)*2F(x_(n_m))/R_m^2=T_m+B_(n_m)*V_m/R_m^2,
    T_m=B_(n_m)*D_(k+1)^2/[2(1+S_(m-1))*R_m^2]
        ->T_infty=Z_1*exp(-17/4)/(2lambda).                 (4.6)

In the sum, Phi_k means exactly the last horizontal envelope, equal
to the original circular value at the actual state. The limit follows
from(3.6)--(3.9) and (lambda-2)^2=lambda^(-2). In particular
T_infty<5/64<1, using exp(17/4)>16 and2lambda>4.

Screen I assesses the previous sufficient NONNEGATIVE charge

    X_m=C_beta*sum_i sigma_i*(r_i(N))_+
         +(1/2)sum_t h_t sum_(i<k) sigma_i
                                     [theta*U_i(t)+U_(i+1)(t)]. (4.7)

The elementary cap estimate for its flux part is only

    X_flux <= (C_beta*S_(m-1)/2)
                   sum_(i<k) sigma_i*(theta*sigma_i+sigma_(i+1)).

The RIGHT SIDE after normalization has order lambda^(2k), by the
positive limiting ratio sigma_2/sigma_1 and(3.6)--(3.9). It does not
vanish or supply the required strict constant. This is a failure of
that upper comparison; it is NOT a lower bound on actual X_m.

Signed coordinate budgets do not automatically improve it. Define
H_i^U=(1/2)sum_t h_t U_i(t) and H_i^Q=(1/2)sum_t h_t Q_i(t),
with H_0^Q=H_k^Q=0. Then

    x_i(0)-x_i(N)=H_i^U+beta*H_i^Q-H_(i-1)^Q.              (4.8)

The telescoping positive weights that eliminate every H_i^Q are
proportional to beta^(i-1), since their adjacent ratio must be beta.
The bulk weights in(4.7) have adjacent ratios asymptotic to lambda-2,
with different harmless endpoint factors. Explicitly their coefficients
on H_i^U are theta*sigma_1, theta*sigma_i+sigma_(i-1) for
2<=i<k, and sigma_(k-1) at i=k. They are not those telescoping
weights. Converting between the two
can cost ((lambda-2)/beta)^O(k), and the signed endpoint displacement
has not itself been bounded on the required scale.

The crucial actual restriction is stronger than this budget for the
first coordinate. At its own checkpoint x_1=A_1-beta*D_2. Thereafter
x_1 never increases, since Q_0=0 and P_1>=0 in EVERY physical step.
Thus throughout the suffix

    r_1<=-beta*D_2<0, U_1=0.                               (4.9)

This is a property of the initialized trajectory, not invariance of
the entire input slab. Even after dropping U_1 from the cap estimate,
the sigma_1*U_2 charge retains the same lambda^(2k) scale in that
upper bound. The actual barrier will remove the U_2 charge from the FIRST
terminal component by a last-entry argument. We have not proved
that X_m itself fails to vanish, nor supplied a lower bound showing
that it overcounts by a nonvanishing amount. Its status remains open.
Only the unnecessary use of all-time U_2 to bound Phi_1 is eliminated.

## 5. Screen II: quantitative actual terminal bounds at both ends

This is the viable part of the round. A last entry uses an occurrence
of b_j in H_(m-1). Immediately following that occurrence lies an entire
H_j inside the remaining suffix. This property follows by induction
from H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j), and keeps the original order and enclosing
m. It is used only on samples AFTER the last entry, so the claimed
region persists by the choice of the last entry, not by an assumed
invariance theorem.

### 5.1 First circular component: the apparent source switches off

By(4.9), formula(4.3) applies to component1 at EVERY suffix sample.
The exact scalar residual update is

    z_1^+=z_1-(h/2)(kappa*Q_1-P_2).                        (5.1)

It includes the full P_2=U_2+beta*Q_2. If z_1>kappa*sigma_1,
then Q_1=sigma_1 and

    x_2=beta*x_1-z_1
       <ell_2-beta^2*D_2-kappa*sigma_1<ell_2.

Therefore r_2<0, U_2=0 and P_2=beta*Q_2<=beta*sigma_2.
Define gamma_1=kappa*sigma_1-beta*sigma_2. In this region every
physical step loses at least h*gamma_1/2 in z_1, with no restriction
on h. In contrast, an entry step from z_1<=kappa*sigma_1 can add
at most h*C_beta*sigma_2/2. These are different, justified caps.

Eventually gamma_1>0 and

    d*C_beta*sigma_2<=gamma_1,                              (5.2)

because the ratio of the left side to sigma_1 tends to
(lambda-2)^2<1, whereas gamma_1/sigma_1 tends to1.

If z_1(N)>kappa*sigma_1 and there was an entry during the suffix,
take its last occurrence, at b_j. All later samples remain above the
threshold. Pay the entry with C_beta*sigma_2 and the following H_j
with gamma_1. Every subsequent step has nonnegative loss. Thus

    z_1(N)<=kappa*sigma_1
                      +(b_j*C_beta*sigma_2-gamma_1*S_j)/2
            <=kappa*sigma_1+(c-1)*C_beta*sigma_2/2,         (5.3)

where(3.5) and(5.2) pay every large bridge.

The case of no entry must use the ACTUAL full prehistory. Let
S_pre=S_(m-1)+b_(m-1) be the mass before the final suffix. From
(2.5), x_1(0)<=1 and x_2(0)>=-C_beta*sigma_2*S_pre/2.
Hence

    z_1(0)<=beta+C_beta*sigma_2*S_pre/2.                    (5.4)

If all samples from t=0 were above the threshold, summing(5.1)
would give z_1(N)<=z_1(0)-gamma_1*S_(m-1)/2. This is negative
eventually: S_pre/S_(m-1)->lambda-1 and

    C_beta*sigma_2*S_pre/(gamma_1*S_(m-1))
                  ->(lambda-2)*(lambda-1)=2-sqrt(2)<1,
    beta/(sigma_1*S_(m-1))->0.

So the no-entry case cannot leave a terminal positive residual above
the threshold. If the terminal residual is below the threshold, (5.3)
already bounds its positive part. Consequently, for every sufficiently
large m, on the prescribed actual trajectory,

    (z_1(N))_+<=kappa*sigma_1+(c-1)*C_beta*sigma_2/2
               <=2sigma_1,
    0<=Phi_1(x(N))<=2sigma_1^2.                             (5.5)

This is a full terminal bound for that component. No U_2 integral,
independent two-Huber trajectory, or alternative state was substituted.
By(3.10), B_(n_m)*Phi_1(x(N))/R_m^2 tends to zero.

### 5.2 Last circular component: the small cap mismatch is paid

Write L_k=C_beta*sigma_k for the horizontal gradient cap. The actual
checkpoint formula for the active kth coordinate gives

    r_k(0)=-beta*D_(k+1)<0.                                (5.6)

This statement concerns only coordinate k at its OWN checkpoint; it
makes no assertion about the other retired coordinates. During its
active ordinary block and checkpoint Q_(k-1)=0 by output isolation,
so preceding gradients do not alter this particular formula.

At any suffix sample with r_k>L_k, x_k>ell_k, whence Q_(k-1)=0
and P_k=L_k. Thus r_k loses h*L_k/2 there. At an entry from
r_k<=L_k its increase is at most h*sigma_(k-1)/2. If the terminal
residual exceeds L_k, (5.6) guarantees an entry. Its last occurrence
at b_j and its following H_j give

    (r_k(N))_+<=L_k+(1/2) max_(0<=j<=m-2)
                                      [b_j*sigma_(k-1)-L_k*S_j]_+.
                                                                  (5.7)

No assumption of distance descent is used. Put s=S_(m-2),
T=b_(m-2)/2-1 and Delta_k=d-C_beta*T/M_k. The EXACT ratio
sigma_k/sigma_(k-1)=T/M_k follows from(1.3). Thus(3.5) implies

    (r_k(N))_+<=L_k+(sigma_(k-1)/2)
                                      [c-1+(Delta_k)_+*s]. (5.8)

To bound the possible positive cap defect, expand it BEFORE estimating:

    d*M_k-C_beta*T
       =d*(M_k-C_beta*s/2)+C_beta*(3-c)/2
                   +(C_beta*d/2)*(1-v_mass)*2^(m-2).

By(3.3),(3.4), s/M_k<=2/C_beta. Therefore

    (Delta_k)_+*s
       <=(2d/C_beta)*K_k+3+d*(1-v_mass)*2^(m-2).            (5.9)

Define the explicit nonnegative error allowance

    A_err,m=c-1+(2d/C_beta)*K_k+3
                                  +d*(1-v_mass)*2^(m-2).

Since Hub_(L_k)(r)<=L_k*(r)_+, the last retained value satisfies

    0<=Phi_k(x(N))
       <=L_k^2+(L_k*sigma_(k-1)/2)*A_err,m.                 (5.10)

All constants c,d,C_beta remain bounded, and sigma_k,sigma_(k-1)
are at most sigma_1 eventually. Formula(3.10) pays (5.10), including
the changed cap ratio and its 2^(m-2) mass correction. Thus
B_(n_m)*Phi_k(x(N))/R_m^2 tends to zero uniformly along the frozen
growing policy. The bound is quantitative and applies to every physical
bridge; it does not require exact absorption of the final component.

## 6. Screen III: why the same comparison does not close the middle

This screen was rejected as a complete uniform comparison. The exact
failure is stronger than merely saying that the middle is coupled.

Fix 2<=i<=k-1 and put L_i=C_beta*sigma_i. At a sample with r_i>L_i,
output isolation gives Q_(i-1)=0. Maximizing over P at fixed Q in
(2.1), r_i>L_i forces the UPPER circular boundary, so

    P_i=sigma_i*p(Q_i/sigma_i),
    L_i-P_i=sigma_i*[sqrt(1+2beta)
               -sqrt((1+beta)^2-(beta+Q_i/sigma_i)^2)].     (6.1)

Unlike at i=k, this cap loss need not be zero. Concavity of p gives

    0<=L_i-P_i<=(C_beta-beta)*Q_i.                          (6.2)

After the last entry into r_i>L_i, let s_entry be its step index.
As long as that terminal excursion persists, its exact signed loss is

    r_i(N)=r_i(s_entry+1)
                   -(L_i/2) sum_(t>s_entry) h_t
                   +D_i^cap(s_entry),
    D_i^cap(s_entry)=(1/2)sum_(t>s_entry)h_t*(L_i-P_i(t)).   (6.3)

This is a tail-specific cap loss, not the all-time source X_m. The
entry is bounded by L_i+b_j*sigma_(i-1)/2. Its following H_j pays
the full horizontal-cap part exactly as in(5.7). However D_i^cap
has not been paid. If Q_i>0, formula(4.4) does give U_(i+1)=0,
but the next coordinate then follows

    x_(i+1)^+=x_(i+1)+(h/2)(Q_i-beta*Q_(i+1)).              (6.4)

Thus bounding the accumulated Q_i in(6.2) requires its actual
downstream negative excursions and the NEXT neighboring gradient.
Deleting beta*Q_(i+1), or assuming a frozen output, is not legitimate.
When Q_i=0, later horizontal motion of component i+1 can recreate a
negative output at a large bridge. No entry-and-persistence statement
for a fixed quadratic core or a fixed face has been proved here.

There are two explicit quantitative failures of a cap-only closure.

First, even the always-full-cap idealization cannot pay the available
incoming horizontal estimate for a middle coordinate. The full
prehistory bound from(2.5) is

    r_i(0)<=sigma_(i-1)*S_pre/2-A_i, i>=2.                 (6.5)

Dropping -A_i and comparing its leading coefficient to L_i*S_(m-1)/2
gives the limiting ratio

    sigma_(i-1)*S_pre/(C_beta*sigma_i*S_(m-1))
                   ->(lambda-1)/(lambda-2)=2+sqrt(2)>1.    (6.6)

The bound in(6.5) is not the actual value, and does not show that an
always-positive horizontal excursion occurs. It shows why one cannot
discard that branch from a last-entry proof without a stronger actual
prehistory estimate. The endpoint proofs avoided this: the first used
its permanent negative input, and the last used its own exact negative
incoming residual. Neither argument applies automatically to a middle
input after all later checkpoints.

Keeping the omitted A_i does not repair this particular comparison:
A_i=sigma_(i-1)*y_(i-1)+sigma_i*y_i/beta, so(3.2),(3.8)
give A_i/(sigma_(i-1)*S_(m-1))->0 uniformly. Thus the positive
leading allowance in(6.6) survives that exact static threshold.

Second, the best state-independent lower bound for P_i on r_i>L_i
from this same circular geometry is its infimum beta*sigma_i. To see
why a larger fixed lower bound is unavailable, fix r>L_i and q in(0,1).
For q sufficiently close to1 put

    t=(r-sigma_i*p(q))/(p(q)-beta)>0,
    w=sigma_i*q+t*(q+beta).

At the centered point(r,-w), the displacement from sigma_i*v(q) is
t*(p(q)-beta,-q-beta), an outward circular normal. Hence the actual
projection for the SAME envelope is sigma_i*v(q). Letting q approach1
gives P_i approaching beta*sigma_i while r remains fixed above L_i.
Other coordinates can be chosen with the permanent x_1 bound intact.
These are alternative states of the unchanged function, NOT states
proved reachable from initialization. Their purpose is only to test a
uniform cap-floor lemma, not to refute trajectory-specific control.

Using that valid floor in a last-entry comparison leaves the positive
coefficient

    d*sigma_(i-1)-beta*sigma_i.

For i=2 it is a fixed positive fraction of sigma_1 eventually, by
(3.8) and beta->0. The entry at level m-2 in the maximum of the
comparison therefore leaves an allowance of order
sigma_1*S_(m-2). Multiplying the horizontal-value allowance by
C_beta*sigma_2 and the original benchmark gives order lambda^(2k),
by(3.6)--(3.9). This comparison does not even give a bounded normalized
upper estimate, let alone one below1-T_infty. This is the scale of a
FAILED UPPER BOUND, not an attained terminal lower bound.

The cap-only method is therefore rejected without pretending that
(6.3) is a closed recursion. A viable replacement must simultaneously
pay the actual incoming middle residuals and the ordered cap losses
D_i^cap, or directly bound the complete actual middle value. Both
neighbors must be retained in that estimate. No universal distance
descent or large-step Markov positivity was assumed: expansion of
distance would retain h*(2-h) times the gradient-square term, with
its negative sign for h>2. The present endpoint proofs instead pay
each large step through its following physical subtree.

## 7. Exact new handoff and limits of the result

Let

    V_mid,m=sum_(i=2)^(k-1) Phi_i(x(N)),
    epsilon_m=(B_(n_m)/R_m^2)*
       [2sigma_1^2+L_k^2+(L_k*sigma_(k-1)/2)*A_err,m].

Every quantity uses the same unchanged static function and its actual
full-prehistory trajectory. The jointly derived estimates prove, at
the UNVERIFIED DRAFT level,

    0<=epsilon_m->0,
    T_m+(B_(n_m)/R_m^2)*V_mid,m
       <=B_(n_m)*2F(x_(n_m))/R_m^2
       <=T_m+(B_(n_m)/R_m^2)*V_mid,m+epsilon_m.             (7.1)

This is a quantitative removal of two terminal contributions from
the comparison, not physical deletion of either component. They
remain in the actual gradient throughout. One CANNOT repeat the
endpoint argument by renaming component2 as component1: U_2 has not
been shown zero, and its incoming Q_1 has not been removed. Similarly,
component k-1 continues to have its original moving output and Q_(k-1).

The remaining actual quantity is V_mid,m for k-2 growing middle
components. No bound below1-T_infty for its normalized limsup is
established, and no normalized lower witness is established. The
defect D_i^cap and the incoming r_i(0) are precise unpaid mechanisms
in the failed third comparison, not a claimed substitute theorem.
We have also NOT decided whether B_(n_m)*X_m/R_m^2 tends to zero.

Accordingly the frozen policy remains OPEN. The original question
over all words and all horizons remains OPEN even if this policy were
eventually decided. The assigned one round ends with the quantitative
endpoint progress and the explicit middle comparison failure; it does
not automatically renew the allocation.

new fact, full-class objective bound, or original-target resolution is claimed.
This is worker max's single round after completed67, with ceiling68 and

The three explicit policies below have nonnegative original multipliers and
exact value flow. Their new optimum-outgoing rows fit a genuine same-word

## 1. Fixed words, original objective, and accepted inputs

Fix an enclosing integer m. Every child throughout this document uses

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta_word=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta_word/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

The physical word is h=H_m of length n=2^m-1. Put

    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S,
    p_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, 0<=i<=n.

All n updates are retained in order. The terminal gradient g_n is an original

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

The accepted interpolation convention gives Q_ij<=0 on actual trajectories.
A full certificate is

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij,             (1)

with every lambda_ij>=0, every value coefficient zero, and M(q) PSD on ALL

Other accepted inputs are fact04219554e41d9750's original all-split benchmark,

## 2. Exact same-word Huber price, before choosing any policy

Let Hub(x)=x^2/2 for |x|<=1 and |x|-1/2 otherwise. It is convex,
differentiable and 1-smooth, with unique minimizer0. Start at x_0=D.
Every actual query is x_i=D-p_i>=S+1>1, so

    g_i=1, f_i=D-p_i-1/2, 2f_n=D.

For an empty word S=0 the same calculation uses the boundary point1;
our screened words have S>0. Direct substitution in the ORIGINAL rows gives

    Q_ij=0 for finite i!=j,
    Q_(i,star)=0,
    Q_(star,i)=-(2S-p_i).                                 (3)

Write b_i=lambda_(star,i), a_i=lambda_(i,star), and q=zeta/D with
eta=zeta-1. On this exact Huber transcript,

    M(q)=D eta-sum_(i=0)^n b_i(2S-p_i).                    (4)

Thus a necessary condition for PSD is

    sum_i b_i(2S-p_i)<=D eta,
    eta>=0, sum_i b_i<=D eta/S<=3eta when S>1.             (5)

The last inequality is strict when eta>0; at eta=0 all b_i are zero.

The row price varies from 2S to S, including the terminal price S. No
nonzero optimum-outgoing row is free on this transcript. Function values
and the specified-minimizer radius are unchanged.

The price is exact as an evaluation, but it is not a sufficient PSD test.
There is a second useful restriction that keeps the x_0 mixed terms. Let
K_ij=lambda_ij on finite pairs and let B=sum b_i. The complete finite flow is

    sum_j K_ij-sum_j K_ji+a_i-b_i=2*1_(i=n),
    sum_i a_i=2+B.                                        (6)

On the entire two-dimensional original subspace g_i=v for every finite i,
x_0=x, flow gives

    M(q)=q x^2-(2+B)xv+[D+sum_i b_i(1+p_i)]v^2.            (7)

Indeed finite position terms sum to
sum_i p_i(out_i^K-in_i^K)=2S-sum_i a_i p_i+sum_i b_i p_i;
finite gradient differences vanish, and the optimum terms supply the
remaining a_i p_i and (a_i+b_i)/2. Therefore PSD also requires

    zeta >= D(1+B/2)^2/[D+sum_i b_i(1+p_i)].              (8)

For example, spending the ENTIRE budget (4) on b_n=D eta/S, eta>0,
would give M(D,1,...,1)=0, but the x_0 derivative there equals
2eta-b_n=-eta/S!=0. A PSD quadratic vanishing at a vector annihilates
that vector, as follows by evaluating it on that vector plus t times an
arbitrary direction for both signs of t. Such saturated terminal spending
therefore cannot be PSD without changing the budget allocation. This is a
budget warning, not a fourth screened policy.

## 3. Full value flow and full correction in original coordinates

Put z_i=-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t, so x_i=x_0+z_i. Under (6), (1) is exactly

    q||x_0||^2-sum_i a_i<x_0,g_i>
     +sum_i a_i[-<g_i,z_i>+||g_i||^2/2]
     +sum_i b_i||g_i||^2/2
     +sum_(i!=j finite)K_ij[<g_i,z_j-z_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].   (9)

In particular its FULL matrix is

    [[q,-a^T/2],[-a/2,C]],                                (10)

on the original n+2 coordinates. Define h_n=0 and out_i=a_i+sum_j K_ij.
Every entry of the gradient block C is

    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i sum_(j>i)K_ij,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j sum_(v>j)K_iv
                         +h_i[a_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j.  (11)

All sums in (11) are over finite labels. Half the total mass incident to i
is out_i-1_(i=n) by (6), including BOTH optimum directions. A forward
position row based at i subtracts h_i K_ij from the diagonal. For i<j,
difference squares contribute -(K_ij+K_ji) to the cross coefficient;
position rows based at i contribute -h_j sum_(v>j)K_iv, and rows based at j
contribute h_i[a_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv]. This proves (11) without omitting b.

For q>0 the exact full square completion is

    M(q)=q||x_0-sum_i a_i g_i/(2q)||^2
                +sum_(i,j)[C_ij-a_i a_j/(4q)]<g_i,g_j>.   (12)

The terminal, every mixed term, and every original gradient remain.

More generally start with any value-flow base (K^0,a^0,b^0=0) at 1/D.
Permit a signed finite modification deltaK with final K^0+deltaK>=0.
Set r_i=sum_j deltaK_ij-sum_j deltaK_ji. Exact final flow forces

    a_i=a_i^0+b_i-r_i>=0, b_i>=0.                         (13)

The complete value-free correction to the base is

    eta||x_0||^2/D-sum_i(b_i-r_i)<x_0,g_i>
     +sum_i(b_i-r_i)sum_(t<i)h_t<g_i,g_t>
     +sum_i(b_i-r_i/2)||g_i||^2
     +sum_(i!=j)deltaK_ij[<g_i,z_j-z_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].   (14)

This follows by subtracting (9) for the base. It allows reductions of old
finite multipliers, provided their FINAL signs hold. The three policies
below use particular nonnegative additions and do not exhaust (13)-(14).

A balanced optimum cycle of weight rho_i adds rho_i to both a_i and b_i,
keeps K unchanged, and adds exactly

    rho_i C_i^opt,
    C_i^opt=Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i)
           =||g_i||^2-<x_0,g_i>+sum_(t<i)h_t<g_i,g_t>.    (15)

For the sum of such cycles, deltaC has diagonal rho_i and entries
2deltaC_ti=h_t rho_i for t<i. Its x_0-to-gradient entries are -rho_i/2.
These are not just positive diagonal corrections. For example a lone
cycle at i>0, with x_0=0, g_i=1 and an earlier g_t=-2/h_t, other gradients0,
has value -rho_i when h_t>0. Adding eta||x_0||^2/D does not change that
negative value. This illustrates why (12), rather than diagonal signs,
is the required test.

For any distinct finite i,j, a directed optimum triangle of weight t_ij
adds t_ij to the three ORIGINAL rows Q_(star,i), Q_(i,j), Q_(j,star).
Its flow is zero and its complete polynomial is

    t_ij T_ij^opt,
    T_ij^opt=||g_i||^2+||g_j||^2-<g_i,g_j>
                  +<g_i,z_j-z_i>-<g_j,x_0+z_j>.         (16)

Only a_j increases. Its new x_0 cross term is -t_ij<x_0,g_j>, and
its Huber price is t_ij(2S-p_i). Both facts matter below.

## 4. The three explicit policies and their actual budgets

Define positive density v_i=h_i for i<n and v_n=S+1, so sum_i v_i=D.
Take eta>=0 and q=(1+eta)/D.

Policy I: on the asymmetric array of Section 5, add balanced optimum cycles

    rho_i=eta v_i/D.                                     (17)

Policy II: use exactly the same cycle law (17), on the source-calibrated
finite array and its original objective completion in Section 7.

Policy III: on the asymmetric array, use

    rho_i=eta v_i/(2D),
    t_(n,L_k)=eta/2, all other added triangles zero.      (18)

Here L_k is the original physical root query of the last join. Thus this
policy changes a finite row too: it adds eta/2 to Q_(n,L_k), as well as
to Q_(star,n) and Q_(L_k,star).

Every addition in (17)-(18) is nonnegative and has zero value flow. For
Policies I and II, (3) gives their EXACT new Huber expenditure

    P_H=eta/D * sum_i v_i(2S-p_i).                        (19)

For Policy III it is

    P_H=eta/(2D)*sum_i v_i(2S-p_i)+eta S/2.               (20)

For eta>0, (19)<=2S eta<D eta. Similarly (20)<=3S eta/2<D eta.
Thus these are feasible budget allocations with genuine paid costs and
positive Huber remainder, not laws rejected merely for spending too much.
At eta=0 the costs vanish. Exact sums (19)-(20), not only their upper
bounds, specify the necessary cost of each policy.

The tests below grant STRICTLY LARGER classes: arbitrary nonnegative
balanced weights, and for Policy III arbitrary nonnegative triangles
star->R_i->L_l->star, with any original left destination. Their failure
therefore includes the explicit policies without fitting a weight profile.

## 5. Complete asymmetric base, with unrestricted left completion

Consider the final actual parent (H_j,d,H_j), j=m-1, k=2^j-1. In THIS
section d=1+a c^j is the physical bridge, A=sum H_j, t=A+d,
S=2A+d, D=1+2S. The left queries L_l=l, 0<=l<=k, include bridge L_k;
right queries R_i=k+1+i, 0<=i<=k, include actual terminal n=R_k.
Let p_i^c be the child chronological masses, with p_0^c=0,p_k^c=A.

Take any nonnegative finite reference array K^c and nonnegative mu_i with

    sum_v K^c_iv-sum_v K^c_vi+mu_i=2*1_(i=k).              (21)

In particular sum mu_i=2. Reference child PSD is NOT assumed. Set

    theta=(3A+d)/(2S), s=1-theta=t/(2S),
    kappa=0 or s/(2d), E=sum_i mu_i(A-p_i^c), 0<=E<=2A.

The prescribed original rows of the base are

    K_(R_i,R_v)=K^c_iv, a_(R_i)=theta mu_i,
    K_(R_i,L_0)=mu_i[s-kappa d(A-p_i^c)/A],
    K_(R_i,L_k)=mu_i kappa t(A-p_i^c)/A,
    K_(R_i,L_l)=0 for 0<l<k,
    sum_l K_(L_l,R_i)=kappa mu_i(A-p_i^c).               (22)

All b_i are initially zero. All left finite rows and optimum attachments
are otherwise arbitrary nonnegative values satisfying full original flow.
No PSD condition on the left child is presumed. Thus these screens grant
arbitrary position-dependent left corrections already present in the base.

All prescribed signs hold: s>0,theta>0, and at repaired kappa,
s-kappa d(A-p_i^c)/A=s(A+p_i^c)/(2A)>=s/2. Put
B_i=sum_l K_(R_i,L_l)=s mu_i+kappa mu_i(A-p_i^c), and
F_i=sum_l K_(L_l,R_i)=kappa mu_i(A-p_i^c). Right flow is (21) plus
theta mu_i+B_i-F_i, hence is 2*1_(i=k).

For a completely explicit base completion, send every F_i from L_k, set
all left finite rows0, and take

    a_(L_0)=2s-kappa dE/A, a_(L_k)=kappa dE/A,
    a_(L_l)=0 for 0<l<k.                                (23)

The first attachment is at least s; all are nonnegative. Incoming-minus-

Thus (21)-(23) give a complete value-flow array for j>=1. For the empty
word use a_0=2 separately; for H_1 use the actual one-step array
lambda_(0,star)=lambda_(1,star)=lambda_(1,0)=1, and apply (21)-(23)
at subsequent levels. For h=(b) that one-step base has

    M(1/(1+2b))=||x_0-(1+2b)(g_0+g_1)/2||^2/(1+2b)
                              +(3-2b)||g_0-g_1||^2/4.

The actual b=1+a is below sqrt(2)<3/2. This checks its starting calibration;
no parent PSD is inferred. Subsequent definitions are coefficient formulas,

## 6. New full left-block test: Policies I and III fail even with free weights

On the ORIGINAL formal space choose

    g_(L_l)=v for EVERY left query, including L_k,
    g_(R_i)=0 for EVERY right query, including terminal,
    x_0=x.                                                (24)

The original positions are x_(L_l)=x-p_l^c v and x_(R_i)=x-tv.
This is a test subspace of the whole quadratic, not a quotient or a claim
that the formal assignment is interpolation-feasible.

Let B_l be total backward inflow into L_l and F_l total forward outflow.
Left finite flow is -a_(L_l)-F_l+B_l. Multiplying it by p_l^c and summing
shows that all left finite position terms contribute
sum_l p_l^c[-a_(L_l)-F_l+B_l]v^2. The optimum rows contribute
-a_L xv+sum_l a_(L_l)(p_l^c+1/2)v^2, where a_L=sum_l a_(L_l)=2s.
Backward rows contribute (sum_i B_i)v^2/2. Forward rows contribute
sum_l F_l[-t+p_l^c+1/2]v^2. All p_l^c a_(L_l) and p_l^c F_l terms cancel.
Consequently the full base (9), including every arbitrary left coefficient,
restricts to

    M_base(q)=q x^2-2s xv+Gamma_L v^2,
    Gamma_L=sum_i B_i+sum_l p_l^c B_l-t sum_l F_l
           =2s+kappa E.                                 (25)

The final equality uses sum_i B_i=2s+kappa E,
sum_l p_l^c B_l=kappa tE, and sum_l F_l=kappa E, directly from (22).
This exact cancellation is the restrictive cross-block MOMENT of the base.
It is not a general identity for asymmetric certificates.

A balanced cycle on a left label contributes
rho_(L_l)[(1+p_l^c)v^2-xv] on (24); a cycle on a right label is zero.
A backward optimum triangle star->R_i->L_l->star contributes precisely
t_(R_i,L_l)[(1+p_l^c)v^2-xv] by (16). These statements include their
x_0 mixed terms. Let U be the total weight of these left balanced cycles
and backward triangles, and let J be their sum weighted by (1+p_l^c).
Then 0<=J<=(A+1)U, and the complete modified restriction is

    M(q)=q x^2-(2s+U)xv+(Gamma_L+J)v^2.                 (26)

The right balanced weights may be arbitrary; they vanish on this test.
The triangle weights and destinations may be arbitrary as specified;
no Huber budget restriction is needed for the following obstruction.

Suppose A>=1024 and d/A>2/5. Since E<=2A and kappa<=s/(2d),

    Gamma_L<=s(2+A/d)<(9/2)s<(A+1)s.                    (27)

For q<=0, (26) cannot be PSD since its mixed coefficient is nonzero.
For q>0, set v=1 and x=(s+U/2)/q. Full PSD would require

    q >= (s+U/2)^2/(Gamma_L+J)
      > (s+U/2)^2/[(A+1)(s+U)] >= s/(A+1).             (28)

The last inequality follows by subtracting s(s+U) from (s+U/2)^2;
the difference is U^2/4>=0. This explicitly pays the mixed term: merely
raising the positive gradient diagonal would miss its simultaneous change.

Also Ds>t=A+d, so

    qD>Ds/(A+1)>(A+d)/(A+1)
                     >(7/5)A/(A+1)>4/3.               (29)

The final inequality follows from A>20. Thus the exact full-space assignment
just specified is negative at ANY proposed qD<=4/3, regardless of how the
balanced and backward-triangle weights are chosen. This proves the failure
of both explicit Policies I and III and their larger stated classes.

## 7. The full source-calibrated array for Policy II

In this section set S_j=sum H_j, A_j=1+S_j, d_j=a c^j, so the physical
bridge at level j is 1+d_j and A_(j+1)=2A_j+d_j. For any word H_j with
terminal index z define the ORIGINAL primitive history polynomial

    V_j=2sum_(i<z)h_i(f_i-f_z)
              +sum_(i<z)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-A_j(A_j-1)||g_z||^2.

Start with empty finite array Lambda^0=0. At each join let p be the
physical bridge query and z the parent terminal; i ranges over nonterminal
right-child queries. Use the following exact nonnegative weights:

    u_j=2lambda,
    v_j^w=[u_j d_j+2(A_j+d_j)]/A_j,
    k_j=1+(u_j+v_j^w)/2,
    z_j^w=2A_j,
    p_j^w=4A_j+2d_j-u_j(A_j-1)
                         =2lambda+2(d_j-A_j/lambda).     (31)

Embed the entire left finite array with weight1, the entire right finite
array with weight k_j, and add

    u_j sum_i h_i Q_(i,p)+v_j^w sum_i h_i Q_(i,z)
                             +p_j^w Q_(z,p)+z_j^w Q_(p,z).   (32)

There are no optimum rows in this finite recursion. Define P_j by
V_j+sum Lambda^j_ij Q_ij=P_j. This defines a full quadratic, without
assuming its positivity.

For a check of every coefficient, temporarily write A=A_j,d=d_j,
s=A-1,T=2A+d,K=A(A-1),K_+=T(T-1), u=u_j,v=v_j^w,k=k_j,
p^w=p_j^w,z^w=z_j^w, and r=sum_i h_i g_i over the right
nonterminal queries. For a nonempty right child, function coefficients
cancel precisely when

    u+v=2(k-1), us+p^w-z^w=2(A+d),                       (33)

which (31) satisfies. For the empty right child these equations remain
sufficient and are the chosen policy; no necessity is asserted there.
The four gradient parts of the unweighted terms
in (32) are respectively

    d<r,g_p>+||r||^2/2+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2+s||g_p||^2/2,
    -||r||^2/2+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2+s||g_z||^2/2-<r,g_z>,
    d<g_z,g_p>+<g_z,r>+(||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2)/2,
    -(d+1/2)||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2/2-<g_p,r>-<g_p,g_z>.

After adding the history differences, the correction R_j in
P_(j+1)=P_j^left+k_j P_j^right+R_j has coefficients

    R_j=(u-v)||r||^2/2+(ud-z^w)<r,g_p>+(p^w-v)<r,g_z>
                  +(p^w d-z^w)<g_p,g_z>+C_p||g_p||^2+C_z||g_z||^2,
    C_p=K-d-d^2+(us+p^w)/2-(d+1/2)z^w,
    C_z=-K_++kK+vs/2+(p^w+z^w)/2.

Substitute (31), put t_j=d_j/A_j, t_*=1/lambda,
Y=r-(A_j-1)g_z and Z=g_p-g_z. The SAME complete correction is

    R_j=(t_*-t_j)[(lambda+1)||Y||^2-2lambda A_j<Y,Z>
                           +A_j^2(2+t_*+t_j)||Z||^2].     (34)

For instance the coefficient of ||r||^2 equals
(u-v)/2=(lambda+1)(t_*-t_j), and ud-z^w=-2lambda A_j(t_*-t_j);
substitution of the displayed C_p,C_z supplies the remaining coefficients.
Thus (34) concerns all original gradients and includes every right aggregate,
bridge and terminal cross term.

The bracket in (34) is positive definite in Y,Z. Its first diagonal is
lambda+1, and its determinant divided by A_j^2 is
(lambda+1)(2+t_*+t_j)-lambda^2>=lambda>0. It vanishes on common gradients
because Y=Z=0. Consequently P_j e_j=0 at every depth, where e_j is the
all-ones gradient vector. This is an exact matrix-kernel identity obtained
by induction from (34), without claiming PSD.

# Exact two-block moments and three finite-row redistribution screens

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. This is max's single
allocated Sol/max invocation after terminal-invocation baseline70, with
ceiling71 / attempted ceiling72. No formal call, new fact, all-function upper,
or resolution of the original exact-profile problem is claimed.

The new compression permits arbitrary directed finite rows, both optimum
directions, and arbitrary changes inside either child. It is derived from the
original quadratic, not substituted for it. Three actual coefficient laws are
then specified and screened:

1. Moving the backward destination to the bridge repairs the old coarse
   obstruction. Its original-Silver calibration is fully PSD at every depth.
   On the actual perturbed word its full lift retains a negative H4 direction
   with zero displacement and zero terminal gradient. Raising the objective
   level cannot repair that direction.
2. Replacing the left finite block by a moment-matched backward bridge fan
   removes that inherited finite block. It instead forces a relative loss
   greater than half a growing physical step, and even an absolute certificate
   level greater than3/250 at the target horizons.
3. Retaining the left objective finite block and correcting its individual
   contact equations with forward-to-bridge rows preserves all signs and
   value flow. It creates a negative original diagonal already at H2. A
   budget-valid, signed, nonscalar redistribution of the FINAL right terminal
   rows through the optimum is included explicitly; it vanishes on the failed
   left direction and cannot repair it.

These are scoped failures of THESE arrays. They are not legal primal
adversaries, lower bounds for W, or general-dual infeasibility results. No
unproved positive lift or feasible recursive base is left masquerading as a
result.

## 1. Physical word, accepted inputs, and original cone

Fix one enclosing integer m>=1536 throughout, including every child, and put

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m.

The actual word is h=H_m of length n=2^m-1. Its terminal gradient is an
interpolation variable, not an extra update. The zero-perturbation calibration
means epsilon=0, a=1/lambda, c=lambda, with the same recursive physical word;
it is explicitly distinguished from the assigned positive epsilon.

Accepted inputs read in this round are:

* fact1252b8823bb5a290: the full original interpolation convention,
  objective certificate, terminal reduction and full-coordinate scope;
* fact04219554e41d9750: the unconditional original benchmark and the full
  primitive/history and objective identities, Sections10--11;
* fact5fd396eba75651e7: ONLY its scalar benchmark comparison on these words,
  Section10. Its restricted witness-family optima are not W upper bounds.

The complete findings74648afc6ca81e6c,83357ebfcaa1356b,

coefficient identities are derived again within this ONE joint draft.
No unverified finding is an accepted predecessor. Data242f8d453ac26183
motivate considering changed finite blocks, but no floating-point equality,
coefficient, zero pattern, sign, rank or feasibility premise is taken from them.

Use normalized smoothness1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. The ORIGINAL formal
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n are independent. Write

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,

For an arbitrary advertised L>0, W_n(h) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite-dimensional
Euclidean space, every convex differentiable f with L-Lipschitz gradient,
every minimizer x_star and every x_0!=x_star, with the actual updates
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Normalizing gives the formal convention
above. This is the original W=2R normalization with the specified minimizer.

Every ordered finite, optimum and terminal row remains in the model. On actual
trajectories Q_ij<=0 by fact1252. Put

    K_ij=lambda_ij for finite i!=j, K_ii=0,
    nu_i=lambda_(i,star), xi_i=lambda_(star,i),
    S=sum h_i, D=1+2S, P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, h_n=0.

All FINAL K,nu,xi must be nonnegative. Exact value flow is

    sum_j K_ij-sum_j K_ji+nu_i-xi_i=2*1_(i=n).             (1)

In particular sum nu=2+sum xi. After (1), the entire original polynomial is

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-sum_i nu_i<x_0,g_i>

                             +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j, (3)

To check (2)--(3), each optimum-incoming row contributes its displayed

## 2. Exact common-gradient compression with arbitrary finite redistribution

Consider ANY last join (H_j,d,H_j), with k=2^j-1 and physical bridge
d=1+a*c^j. In THIS section and Sections3,5,6,

    A=sum H_j, t=A+d, S=2A+d, D=1+2S, D_c=1+2A,
    p_l=sum of child steps before l, 0<=l<=k.

L_l=l include the bridge query L_k. Right labels R_i=k+1+i include the
original terminal R_k=n. On the exact original-coordinate subspace

    g_(L_l)=u for EVERY left label,
    g_(R_i)=v for EVERY right label, x_0=x,

positions are x_(L_l)=x-p_l u and x_(R_i)=x-t u-p_i v. This is a
quadratic-form test subspace, not a constraint on the original model.

Define nonnegative cross arrays and their moments

    B_il=K_(R_i,L_l), F_li=K_(L_l,R_i),
    B=sum_(i,l) B_il, F=sum_(l,i) F_li,
    pi_B=sum_(i,l)p_l B_il,
    pi_F=sum_(l,i)p_i F_li,

## 3. Screen I: moving the backward destination changes the moment

Use a child finite objective array K^c and nonnegative attachments mu_i

# Three nonlinear correlated laws: complete analytical screens

Status: JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. Worker max2, invocation60,
under TASK.md, plan e570a4da874393de, master_guidance ca0fd834c90cd90a
and elaboration f5f79a115a09ff55. The original exact-profile problem is OPEN.
No mathematical program, numerical evaluation, arithmetic replay,
optimizer, solver, executed trajectory or recurrence, benchmark DP,
formal submission, installation, consult or subagent was used.

This is one allocated analytical round, after ended baseline59, with
ended ceiling60/attempted ceiling61. It does not renew itself.

## 1. What was screened, and what the conclusions mean

Three explicit laws leave the old aligned affine elapsed-clock class.

1. A parabolic longitudinal mean has a nonzero initial transverse
   gradient and a transverse sign reversal. A path of ORIGINAL rows
   from the initial optimum constraint through every physical step
   forces every legal radius1 payoff below 1/[1+(8/3)S] whenever
   max h_t <= S/2. This includes the unchanged tau=1/4 hierarchy.
   The terminal row alone is not an adequate screening test here.
2. Accumulated centered projective-incidence innovations have an exact
   real Gram, a parabolic longitudinal mean and an arbitrary initial
   transverse offset. The palindrome moment identity pays the complete
   terminal covariance charge. If the offset makes that charge negative,
   the first original two-row cycle forces a larger scalar payment.
   Under explicit conditions containing the assigned hierarchy, every
   legal radius1 payoff is strictly below the same-word Huber payoff.
3. One static nonorthogonal Huber ridge plus a quadratic background is
   globally legal, sharp1-smooth and has a unique minimum. It has actual
   queried gate changes, noncommuting Hessians and a terminal gradient
   with negative initial-radius component. A fully explicit three-step
   bridge beats the same-word Huber value. A different four-step word
   sends the entire fixed scale family to its minimum exactly. Zero
   padding therefore defeats that whole family at arbitrarily large n.

The first two are rejected by NECESSARY original-row inequalities before
asserting that their entire proposed data arrays are realizable. No
expected-feasibility or unsigned-Gram argument is used to claim a
function. The third is an actual static function, with every original
row, the terminal value, and the true closest radius proved below.
The first two upper bounds apply only to their declared origin-anchored,
radius1 law classes. They are not upper bounds on unrestricted W_n(h).
The third annihilator is a counterexample to that fixed witness family,
not a small-error upper bound on unrestricted W_n for its word.

Every new assertion is proved jointly here and remains unverified.
No unverified shared finding is a mathematical premise. Accepted
1252b8823bb5a290 supplies interpolation necessity/sufficiency and its
explicit conjugate construction. Accepted5fd396eba75651e7 is used ONLY
for its Section10 original benchmark comparison. Acceptedb98bb807d514e80d
is used for the original benchmark definitions and scalar single-cut
comparison. Accepted0e7e78056dc6258c was read to avoid returning to its
expected-orthogonality class; its upper bound is not applied to these laws.

## 2. The original word, all directed rows, and an explicit data convention

Normalize L=1 and take the optimum sample x_star=g_star=f_star=0.
For arbitrary finite h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) >=0 define

    S=sum_(t<n)h_t, P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, q_i=P_i/S.        (1)

For S>0, q_0=0, q_n=1, and q_(i+1)-q_i=h_i/S. Zero steps
repeat q and must repeat positions, gradients and values. All expressions
below are written finite sums; none was executed by a mathematical program.
For S=0 one can use the separate static fallback F(x)=||x||^2/2,
x_0=e0, with every iterate unchanged, unique minimum0 and payoff1.
That degenerate fallback repairs no failure on the positive-mass words.

For any displayed normalized gradient-vector law v_i and scale sigma>0,
use the complete original physical arrays

    g_i=sigma*v_i,
    D_i^nc=sum_(t<i)h_t*v_t,
    x_i=e0-sigma*D_i^nc,                 0<=i<=n.     (2)

These satisfy x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i, including every zero step.
The original signed interpolation residual, with its original orientation,
is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.       (3)

EVERY ordered distinct pair in {star,0,...,n} is retained. In particular,
no incoming terminal or remote queried-prefix row is discarded.

Here is an explicit common value convention for attempted laws1 and2:

    C_i^val=sum_(t=i)^(n-1) (h_t/2)*<v_t+v_(t+1),v_t>,
    f_i=tau_val+sigma^2*C_i^val, C_n^val=0.           (4)

For these values every finite ordered row is EXACTLY

    Q_ij/sigma^2 = C_i^val-C_j^val
                  +<v_i,D_i^nc-D_j^nc>+||v_i-v_j||^2/2. (5)

Both optimum directions are EXACTLY

    Q_(i,star)=tau_val-sigma*<v_i,e0>
        +sigma^2*(C_i^val+<v_i,D_i^nc>+||v_i||^2/2),
    Q_(star,i)=-tau_val+sigma^2*(||v_i||^2/2-C_i^val). (6)

Thus the full optimum-value interval, not only the terminal upper row, is

    lower_i=sigma^2*(||v_i||^2/2-C_i^val),
    upper_i=sigma*<v_i,e0>
         -sigma^2*(C_i^val+<v_i,D_i^nc>+||v_i||^2/2),
    max_i lower_i <= tau_val <= min_i upper_i.        (7)

If all finite rows(5) pass, an explicit maximal choice is
tau_val=min_i upper_i, provided it is at least max_i lower_i.
These formulas specify every position, gradient, value and original-row
cost, rather than supplying separately chosen values for different tests.
For any directed finite cycle, its exact cost is the sum of the displayed
terms in(5); the C_i^val terms telescope. For cycles involving star,
use(5),(6), where tau_val also telescopes. No unknown expectation enters.

Only if ALL those signs pass may the accepted interpolation construction
be invoked. Explicitly, with the zero jet included, put

    K(v)=max{||v||^2/2,
             max_(0<=i<=n)[<x_i,v>-f_i+||v-g_i||^2/2]},
    F(x)=sup_v[<x,v>-K(v)].                           (8)

Fact1252b8823bb5a290 proves that passing all rows realizes these exact
jets by ONE everywhere finite convex differentiable1-smooth F with
minimum0. The Gram is the Gram of the actual displayed Euclidean vectors.
If additionally tau_val>max_i lower_i, every nonzero-jet quadratic is
strictly below the zero-jet quadratic at v=0. Finitely many continuous
quadratics then leave K(v)=||v||^2/2 in a neighborhood of0. The
subdifferential of K at0 is {0}, so argmin F={0}. Consequently the true
closest initial distance is ||e0||=1, and smoothness1 is sharp locally.

Laws1 and2 require that strict condition for a claimed TRUE-radius1
realization. No existence of a passing array is assumed in their
performance screens. Their bounds actually allow ALL common values,
not merely(4). Thus changing(4) cannot repair the stated performance
failures. If a different realization has a closer minimum, the present
origin-radius upper bound is not asserted for that different normalization.

For advertised L>0 use L*F and physical steps h_i/L. The normalized
payoff is still 2f_n/dist(x0,argmin F)^2, exactly W=2R.

## 3. Law1: a parabolic mean and a transverse sign reversal

In R^2, with orthonormal e0,e1, choose the fixed coefficients

    delta_par=1/4, nu_par=27/8, b_par=9/10,
    v_i^par=(1-delta_par*q_i^2)e0
                         +sqrt(nu_par)*(q_i-b_par)e1. (9)

Use(2) for all positions. Written componentwise these are

    x_i=[1-sigma*P_i+sigma*delta_par*U_i]e0
                       -sigma*sqrt(nu_par)*(J_i-b_par*P_i)e1,
    U_i=sum_(t<i)h_t*q_t^2, J_i=sum_(t<i)h_t*q_t.     (10)

Use(4)--(7) for one explicit value array and its ALL-row/cycle costs.
The full gradient Gram and the initial-gradient correlations are

    <e0,g_i>=sigma*(1-q_i^2/4),
    <g_i,g_j>=sigma^2*[(1-q_i^2/4)(1-q_j^2/4)
                         +(27/8)(q_i-9/10)(q_j-9/10)]. (11)

This is a real PSD rank2 Gram, not independent directions. At i=0 the
transverse component is negative and nonzero. At i=n it is positive.
The longitudinal mean is quadratic in elapsed mass, so this is not
another scalar retuning of the affine-clock law. Initial gradient and
initial radius are not aligned.

### 3.1 The original optimum-to-terminal path pays the gain

Consider ANY common values which make these gradients and positions legal
with the origin optimum and x0=e0. The row Q_(0,star)<=0 gives

    f_0<=sigma-sigma^2*||v_0^par||^2/2.

For every physical t, the actual original row Q_(t+1,t)<=0 gives

    f_(t+1)<=f_t-h_t*sigma^2*<v_(t+1)^par,v_t^par>
                              -sigma^2*||v_(t+1)^par-v_t^par||^2/2.

Summing ALL these rows, including the terminal row at t=n-1, yields

    2f_n<=2sigma-D_path*sigma^2,
    D_path=||v_0^par||^2
       +2sum_t h_t*<v_(t+1)^par,v_t^par>
       +sum_t||v_(t+1)^par-v_t^par||^2.              (12)

This is the concrete replacement for the terminal-only screen. It uses
the initial optimum row, every directed physical predecessor row and
the full finite-amplitude vector law. No value re-selection avoids it.

### 3.2 Exact cross quadrature, without a trajectory evaluation

For a written partition interval [q,q+d] with 0<=q<=q+d<=1, define

    v(q)=(1-delta_par*q^2)e0+sqrt(nu_par)*(q-b_par)e1.

Polynomial integration gives the EXACT identity

    integral_q^(q+d)||v(t)||^2 dt -d*<v(q),v(q+d)>
       =d^3*[(delta_par+nu_par)/3
                      +delta_par^2*(q^2+q*d+d^2/5)]. (13)

For the transverse term, this is the equality
integral(q-b_par)^2-d(q-b_par)(q+d-b_par)=d^3/3.
For the longitudinal term, expanding 1-2delta_par*t^2+delta_par^2*t^4
gives delta_par*d^3/3+delta_par^2*d^3*(q^2+qd+d^2/5).
Thus(13) retains the entire error, not a Taylor remainder.

Since q+d<=1, q^2+qd+d^2/5<=1. Also

    integral_0^1||v(t)||^2dt
       =1-2delta_par/3+delta_par^2/5
                        +nu_par*(1/3-b_par+b_par^2)
       =4001/2400>5/3,
    (delta_par+nu_par)/3+delta_par^2=61/48<4/3.       (14)

Write d_t=h_t/S and d_max=max_t d_t. Because sum_t d_t=1,
sum_t d_t^3<=d_max^2. Summing(13) over the EXACT original partition,
with zero intervals contributing zero, proves

    (1/S)sum_t h_t*<v_t^par,v_(t+1)^par>
                    >5/3-(4/3)*d_max^2.             (15)

If max h_t<=S/2, the right side is at least4/3. Furthermore
||v_0^par||^2=1+nu_par*b_par^2>1 and the last sum in(12) is nonnegative.
Consequently

    D_path>1+(8/3)S,
    2f_n<=1/D_path<1/[1+(8/3)S]<1/(1+2S)=H_base(h). (16)

The middle inequality follows by completing the square in(12):
2sigma-D_path*sigma^2=1/D_path-D_path*(sigma-1/D_path)^2.
The bound is over ALL scales and ALL legal common values. In particular
it also holds for every successful strict-radius1 realization in(8).

### 3.3 Exact original benchmark comparison, at the actual horizon

Keep the assigned enclosing parameters, without substituting those of a child:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta_word=1-1/(4m),
    c=lambda*(1+1/(4m)), a_word=beta_word/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a_word*c^j,H_j),
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, m>=1536.                         (17)

The word is a palindrome and its largest entry is the central
1+a_word*c^(m-1). It satisfies max h_t<S/2. To check the latter
without any mass computation, c<3 and m>=3 give

    2S_(m-1)>=2*(1+a_word*c^(m-2))
                         +4*(1+a_word*c^(m-3)),
    2S_(m-1)-(1+a_word*c^(m-1))
       >=5+a_word*c^(m-3)*(2c+4-c^2)>0.             (18)

Here 2c+4-c^2>0 on 1<c<3. Since S=2S_(m-1)+h_central,
the desired largest-step comparison follows.

The ORIGINAL benchmark is U_n^ZJ=1/B_n with ALL split indices retained.
Accepted5fd396eba75651e7, Section10, gives at THIS actual n

    B_n*H_base(H_m)<237/250,                         (19)

so every legal law1 radius1 payoff V satisfies the exact comparison

    V/U_n^ZJ=B_n*V
        < [B_n*H_base(H_m)]*(1+2S)/[1+(8/3)S]
        <237/250<1.                                 (20)

Law1 therefore cannot match the benchmark even on this original full
word. This rejects its fixed nonlinear coefficients; it excludes no
arbitrary nonlinear mean law or terminal longitudinal reversal.

## 4. Law2: accumulated real finite-field covariance with initial memory

### 4.1 The incidence design is a real simplex, with its metric proved

Choose a prime p_ff such that N_ff=p_ff^2+p_ff+1>=n+1, and put
d_ff=N_ff-1. Such a prime exists: any prime divisor of (n+1)!+1 is
greater than n+1. This is an existence argument, not a performed
factorial evaluation or prime search.

Over the field Z/p_ff Z, projective points are nonzero triples modulo
nonzero scalar multiples. Each class has p_ff-1 representatives, giving
N_ff=(p_ff^3-1)/(p_ff-1) points. A projective line is a nonzero linear
form modulo nonzero scalar multiples, with incidence defined by the
vanishing of that form. There are N_ff lines as well.

The kernel of one nonzero linear form has p_ff^2 elements. Removing zero
and passing to scalar classes gives p_ff+1 points per line. Two distinct
line forms are linearly independent; their common kernel has dimension1,
so their lines share exactly one projective point. These counts follow
by eliminating a coordinate with a nonzero coefficient, and eliminating
two coordinates for the pair. No external finite-geometry theorem is
being imported.

In REAL R^(N_ff), let 1_L be the incidence vector of line L and 1 the
all-ones vector. Put k_ff=p_ff+1 and

    u_L^ff=[1_L-(k_ff/N_ff)*1]
                     /sqrt(k_ff-k_ff^2/N_ff).        (21)

Their real inner products, by the proved counts, are exactly

    ||u_L^ff||^2=1,
    <u_L^ff,u_M^ff>=-1/d_ff for L!=M.               (22)

Indeed the distinct numerator inner product is
1-k_ff^2/N_ff=-p_ff/N_ff, while the squared denominator is
(p_ff+1)*p_ff^2/N_ff. Their quotient is -1/[p_ff(p_ff+1)].
Their Gram is therefore PSD because these are explicitly real vectors;
there is no conversion of a finite-field bilinear form into an assumed
Euclidean metric. For arbitrary real coefficients z_L the exact norm is

    ||sum_L z_L*u_L^ff||^2
      =[N_ff*sum_L z_L^2-(sum_L z_L)^2]/d_ff.        (23)

It is nonnegative also directly by Cauchy--Schwarz, extending a selected
subset's coefficients by zero to the N_ff lines.

Choose n distinct step lines and one further line, denoted u_t^ff
(0<=t<n) and u_extra^ff. Add a unit e0 orthogonal to R^(N_ff).

### 4.2 An explicit nonlinear all-history law

Choose sigma>0, nu_inc>0, 0<delta_inc<=1/2 and an ARBITRARY real
initial offset b_inc. Define

    z_i^inc=b_inc*u_extra^ff+(1/S)sum_(t<i)h_t*u_t^ff,
    v_i^inc=(1-delta_inc*q_i^2)e0+sqrt(nu_inc)*z_i^inc. (24)

Use ALL physical arrays(2) and the full common-value convention(4)--(7).
In coordinates the positions are

    x_i=[1-sigma*P_i+sigma*delta_inc*U_i]e0
                        -sigma*sqrt(nu_inc)*sum_(t<i)h_t*z_t^inc,
    U_i=sum_(t<i)h_t*q_t^2.                          (25)

Zero steps add no innovation, so repeated queries have identical gradients.
The covariance is time dependent and retains every earlier innovation.
It is not an independent fresh-gradient construction or an AR nearest-
neighbor assumption. The initial gradient has a transverse component
unless b_inc=0. Opposite temporal inner products are allowed.

Write E_i=sum_(t<i)h_t^2, and r_min=min(i,j). The exact covariance is

    <z_i^inc,z_j^inc>=b_inc^2
      -b_inc*(q_i+q_j)/d_ff
      +[N_ff*E_(r_min)/S^2-q_i*q_j]/d_ff.            (26)

The entire Gram of (x0,g0,...,gn), including all initial correlations,
is determined by(24)--(26), with

    <x0,g_i>=sigma*(1-delta_inc*q_i^2),
    <g_i,g_j>=sigma^2*[(1-delta_inc*q_i^2)
                       *(1-delta_inc*q_j^2)
                              +nu_inc*<z_i^inc,z_j^inc>]. (27)

The initial displacement is EXACTLY e0; a successful strict realization
of(8) has unique minimum0 and true radius1. No minimum is moved without
changing these law hypotheses. All pair/cycle costs are(5),(6) with
(24), not an expected sign or an unspecified combinatorial feasibility
claim.

### 4.3 Complete terminal charge, with every covariance term retained

Let A_inc=1-delta_inc>0 and set

    U=sum_t h_t*q_t^2<=S/3,
    T=sum_t h_t*P_t=(S^2-E)/2, E=sum_t h_t^2,
    eta=T/S, K_inc=1+S+eta, M=1+2S.

The bound on U is the left-endpoint inequality on each interval of the
nondecreasing function(P/S)^2, whose integral from0 to S is S/3.
The formula for T is obtained by expanding the square of sum h.

The original row Q_(n,star)<=0, for ANY legal common values, yields

    2f_n<=2sigma*A_inc-D_inc*sigma^2,
    D_inc=M*A_inc^2+2delta_inc*A_inc*(S-U)
                                   +nu_inc*C_inc(b_inc),
    C_inc(b)=||z_n^inc||^2+2sum_t h_t*<z_n^inc,z_t^inc>.
                                                            (28)

Direct use of(26) gives the complete initial-offset polynomial

    C_inc(b)=M*b^2-2K_inc*b/d_ff+C_inc(0),
    C_inc(0)=[N_ff*(E+2J_inc)/S^2-1-2eta]/d_ff,
    J_inc=sum_t h_t^2*sum_(r>t)h_r.                 (29)

No positive and negative cross term has been discarded. In particular
allowing initial transverse correlation can make C_inc(b) negative;
asserting nonnegativity for every b would be a wrong shortcut.

### 4.4 A palindrome identity pays the zero-offset part

For a palindrome h, reflection of the exact physical indices gives

    2J_inc=S*E-F3, F3=sum_t h_t^3.                 (30)

Proof: sum h_t^2 times prefix mass equals the suffix-mass sum by
reflection. Adding those sums gives sum h_t^2(S-h_t)=S E-F3.

Put p_t=h_t/S, e=sum p_t^2, f=sum p_t^3. For ANY nonnegative
p_t with sum p_t=1 the following exact identity holds:

    (n+1)e-nf-1
       =sum_(i<j)(p_i-p_j)^2*(1-p_i-p_j)>=0.       (31)

To verify it, sum(p_i-p_j)^2=n e-1 and
sum(p_i-p_j)^2(p_i+p_j)=n f-e. Subtract these two equalities.
Each last factor is nonnegative because all remaining p's are nonnegative.
Since N_ff>=n+1, e-f>=0 and N_ff e>=1, it follows that

    (N_ff+1)e-N_ff f-1>=0, N_ff E-S^2>=0.

Multiplying the numerator of C_inc(0) in(29) by S^2 and using(30)
gives exactly

    N_ff*E-S^2
      +S*[(N_ff+1)E-N_ff*F3/S-S^2]>=0.             (32)

Thus C_inc(0)>=0 for EVERY palindrome, including zero entries. This is
a proved coefficient inequality, not covariance domination by an
unverified temporal kernel.

### 4.5 The first original two-row cycle pays a negative initial-offset charge

Let h_lead be the first positive physical step. All earlier zero steps
leave q=0, z=b_inc*u_extra^ff and x=e0. Summing the TWO original rows
at this actual step cancels their values and gives exactly

    Q_(lead,lead+1)+Q_(lead+1,lead)
      =sigma^2*(h_lead/S)^2
          [delta_inc^2*(h_lead/S)^2
                    +nu_inc*(1-b_inc*S/d_ff)-delta_inc*h_lead]. (33)

The innovation has length h_lead/S, and its inner product with the
initial transverse offset is -b_inc/d_ff. This proves(33) directly,
including the initial correlation term instead of presuming it vanishes.
Legal original rows require the square bracket to be nonpositive.

Assume the explicit screen conditions

    h is a positive-mass palindrome, S>=2,
    0<h_lead<=2, d_ff>=4, S<=d_ff^2/4.              (34)

If C_inc(b_inc)>=0, (28) immediately gives D_inc>M*A_inc^2.
If C_inc(b_inc)<0, (29),(32) imply

    0<b_inc<2K_inc/(d_ff*M)<=2/d_ff,

because eta<=S/2 makes K_inc<=M. Consequently
1-b_inc*S/d_ff>=1-2S/d_ff^2>=1/2. The necessary original cycle(33)
then forces

    delta_inc*h_lead>=nu_inc/2,
    delta_inc>=nu_inc/4.                            (35)

Meanwhile completing the square in(29) gives

    C_inc(b_inc)>=-K_inc^2/(d_ff^2*M)>=-M/d_ff^2.

Since A_inc>=1/2, S-U>=2S/3 and S>=2, the COMPLETE correction in(28)
is bounded below, using(35), by

    2delta_inc*A_inc*(S-U)+nu_inc*C_inc(b_inc)
      >=nu_inc*S/6-nu_inc*M/d_ff^2
      >=nu_inc*S*(1/6-5/32)=nu_inc*S/96>0.          (36)

Here M=1+2S<=(5/2)S and d_ff>=4. Thus BOTH covariance phases give

    D_inc>M*A_inc^2,
    2f_n<=A_inc^2/D_inc<1/M=H_base(h).              (37)

Completion of the square in(28) proves the second line for every sigma.
This is a uniform screen over b_inc in ALL of R, every nu_inc>0 and
0<delta_inc<=1/2, and all legal common values. The coefficient payment
is not an amplitude or value tuning inside the old affine clock.

Completing the square in E_B identifies its unique maximizer as Pi_B(w),
the Euclidean projection. The maximizing inequalities at w and w' imply

    ||Pi_B(w)-Pi_B(w')||^2

The maximizing formula and this inequality give differentiability with
gradient Pi_B and a 1-Lipschitz gradient. Thus E_B is convex, nonnegative
and1-smooth. Its zero set is the polar cone of B: if some support pairing

support vector gives a positive envelope value.

The cone of K has extreme rays (C,0),(beta,-1). Consequently

nonnegative, (4) gives Phi_i=0.

These properties prove the active-pair chronology inductively. At block i
the active local states are (A_i+sigma_i*u_j,ell_(i+1)-sigma_i*y_j);
its input is >=ell_i, so Q_(i-1)=0 at the ACTIVE pair's queries.
Its next component vanishes, as do all still-future components.
Earlier components retain (6). The selected step produces, exactly,

    x_i(t_i)=A_i-beta*D_(i+1),
    x_(i+1)(t_i)=ell_(i+1)+D_(i+1),
    t_i=2^l_i.                                             (7)

Equation(7) specifies only that pair at its OWN checkpoint time.
It is not a simultaneous snapshot of the later retired chain.

The map stacking all adjacent pairs and the last scalar counts each
coordinate at most twice. Its squared norm is <=2. Thus the factor1/2
makes F convex1-smooth. F>=0 and F(0)=0. Its entire minimum set is

    C_min={x: x_i<=A_i,
                x_(i+1)>=beta*(x_i-ell_i), 1<=i<=k;
                                      x_(k+1)<=ell_(k+1)}.

The point (A_1,ell_2,0,...,0) belongs to it. From (5),

    1-A_1=sigma_1*u_1, ell_2=beta*A_1=sigma_1*y_1,
    A_1<=1/(1+beta^2).

For x_1<0 the squared distance from e_1 is at least1.
For 0<=x_1<=A_1 it is at least (1-x_1)^2+beta^2*x_1^2,
decreasing on this interval and attained by that feasible point. Therefore

    R_m^2=dist(e_1,C_min)^2
          =(1-A_1)^2+ell_2^2=(u_1^2+y_1^2)/M_1^2>0.        (8)

All physical samples, terminal samples and minimizers obey every ordered
smooth-convex interpolation inequality. To check this directly, apply
the 1-smooth descent inequality to F(z)-<grad F(y),z>, minimized at y;
it gives F(x)-F(y)-<grad F(y),x-y>>=||grad F(x)-grad F(y)||^2/2.
The Gram matrices are actual Euclidean Gram matrices. Scaling F by an
advertised L>0 and using steps h/L preserves (6) and the normalized payoff.



## 6. Schema B: own-checkpoint initialization and reachable retirement

This screen starts each interior i at its actual OWN checkpoint t_i;
it does not rename i as the first component. From (7),

    r_i(t_i)=-beta*D_(i+1),
    z_i(t_i)=-kappa*D_(i+1).                               (30)

For i<k the complete remaining physical word is

    (H_l_i,b_(l_i+1),H_(l_i+1),...,
                                  b_(m-1),H_(m-1)).        (31)

For i=k it is H_(m-1). The prefix ending at q_root includes all
intervening checkpoints and their ordinary blocks. Their parameters
are still the same enclosing m. Earlier coordinates in this prefix
follow (6); they are not placed back at their own checkpoint states.

In particular the incoming neighboring derivative at t_i is exactly

    Q_(i-1)(t_i)
      =-[Pi_(sigma_(i-1)K)(
          x_(i-1)(t_i)-A_(i-1),
                         ell_(i+1)/beta-beta*D_(i+1))]_2,
    x_(i-1)(t_i)=1_(i-1=1)
             -(1/2)sum_(u<t_i)h_u[P_(i-1)(u)-Q_(i-2)(u)]. (32)

This retains its full earlier physical history, including the incoming
derivative whenever it is nonzero. Nothing in (7) forces its vanishing;
no first-component isolation is imposed at retirement. The test below
exhibits a saturated nonzero value under the weaker checkpoint-margin
hypotheses, without asserting that alternative state is actually reached.
At the final-suffix start its value is the corresponding projection at
the actual coordinates given next. A clip formula for that projection
would require its OWN input bound; only the first permanent bound has
been proved in Section4.

For T>=t_i define exact finite integrals over (31)'s already executed
prefix,

    H_j^U(i,T)=(1/2)sum_(u=t_i)^(T-1)h_u U_j(u),
    H_j^Q(i,T)=(1/2)sum_(u=t_i)^(T-1)h_u Q_j(u).

BEFORE q_root the full Q_k is retained and U_k=P_k-beta*Q_k.
Put U_(k+1)=P_(k+1), Q_(k+1)=Q_0=0. Summing the full residual law,

    r_i(T)=-beta*D_(i+1)-H_i^U-beta*H_i^Q+H_(i-1)^Q,
    z_i(T)=-kappa*D_(i+1)-kappa*H_i^Q
              +beta*H_(i-1)^Q+beta*H_(i+1)^Q
                                   -beta*H_i^U+H_(i+1)^U. (33)

All H's on a line have the same (i,T). Thus (33) explicitly derives
the initialized incoming r_i(0),z_i(0) of the final suffix by T=q_root.
It also gives the ACTUAL terminal residuals by T=n. It retains both
neighbors and all later dissipation, rather than just its positive terms.

There is also a componentwise terminal-charge identity starting at this
OWN checkpoint, with no unknown replacement initial state. For i<k put
p_N=P_i(n), q_N=Q_i(n), u_N=p_N-beta*q_N, and use the FULL global
d_j(u)=P_j(u)-Q_(j-1)(u) even before q_root. Substitution of the
exact cumulative updates into the terminal maximizing formula gives

    Phi_i(x_n)=-beta*D_(i+1)*u_N-kappa*D_(i+1)*q_N
                -(p_N^2+q_N^2)/2
       -(1/2)sum_(u=t_i)^(n-1)h_u
                                  [p_N*d_i(u)-q_N*d_(i+1)(u)]. (33a)

The initial negative charge is explicit. The last bracket includes
p_N*P_i-p_N*Q_(i-1)-q_N*P_(i+1)+q_N*Q_i, with the ACTUAL
old and future gradients. It may have either sign; it is not replaced
by its positive terms. If p_N=q_N=0 the entire charge vanishes.
Paying these signed whole-future pairings from the initialized margins
is still open. The identity does not infer nonzero terminal value from
nonzero past activity.

An absorbing retired region DOES exist:

    C_ret={x: r_i<=0 for i<=k, z_i<=0 for i<k}.             (34)

If the actual suffix enters it, every retired projection is zero.
The only remaining scalar gradient acts on x_(k+1), and its excess
stays >=delta, so output isolation continues and (34) is preserved.
This proves conditional no-reactivation AFTER entrance, not entrance.

Attempt B1 sought entrance using the own-checkpoint margins (30).
Those margins, even supplemented by earlier negative checkpoint margins,
do not constitute an invariant for all states satisfying them.
The following exact test fixes that scope.

Take r_(i-1)=-beta*D_i, the own pair in (7), and still-future coordinates
zero. This is an ALTERNATIVE simultaneous state, not an assertion about
their later actual values. For i=2 it respects the permanent first bound.
Then

    z_(i-1)=beta*D_(i+1)-beta^2*D_i-ell_(i+1)/beta.

If this is >=kappa*sigma_(i-1), (18) gives the explicitly NONZERO
incoming Q_(i-1)=sigma_(i-1). These conditions hold eventually:
D_(i+1)/D_i is bounded away from0, beta=1/k, and
ell_(i+1)/beta and sigma_(i-1) are exponentially smaller than beta*D_i,
by (10)--(13). The own component has P_i=Q_i=0.
Its next component starts its next local block and has
P_(i+1)=C*sigma_(i+1), Q_(i+1)=0 eventually, since the large local
u_(i+1) satisfies the capped endpoint inequality.

Use the physical step h=b_(J+i-2), which occurs in the next complete
H_l_i. Since h*sigma_(i-1)/2=D_i+sigma_(i-1),

    r_i^+=-beta*D_(i+1)+D_i+sigma_(i-1)>0                 (35)

whenever beta*T_i/M_i<1. Also h*C<2M_(i+1) ensures its output
remains above ell_(i+1), so its new value is a positive horizontal Huber.
Both finite conditions hold eventually by (10)--(13).

Therefore the checkpoint-margin-only invariant fails under an available
physical step. The test does NOT refute retirement of the ACTUAL
initialized trajectory: the state at this later occurrence of h must be
proved reachable, and no such assertion is made. Its specific lesson is
that the actual incoming Q_(i-1), including its timing in (31), cannot
be discarded.

Attempt B2 used telescoping tail-coordinate weights. Define

    Z_i(x)=sum_(j=i)^(k+1) beta^(j-i)*x_j.

The full update, including Q_k before the root and the terminal scalar,
gives exactly

    Z_i^+=Z_i-(h/2)[sum_(j=i)^(k+1)beta^(j-i)U_j-Q_(i-1)].
    Z_i(t_i)=A_i+beta*ell_(i+1).                           (36)

The two D_(i+1) terms cancel in this INITIAL value, not by a reset.
For i=1 this weighted sum is nonincreasing. For every middle i it
retains the actual incoming source in (36), including all nonzero values.
Moreover a bound on Z_i alone does not bound positive r_i or z_i:
negative downstream coordinates can offset them. The cancelling adjacent
weight ratio is beta, whereas the scale ratios sigma_(i+1)/sigma_i
tend to lambda-2. A comparison between them loses factors of order
((lambda-2)/beta)^O(k) and does not pay the benchmark normalization.

The scoped unpaid initialized interface is now explicit: the signed
integrals in (33) up to q_root, their continuation through (31), and
entrance into (34). Neither attempt establishes their required inequalities.
The actual absorption conjecture is NOT refuted.

# Static noncommutative piecewise-quadratic fields: three exact failed screens

Project gd-exact-profile-20260926; worker max4; assigned analytical round66.
Status: one joint UNVERIFIED mathematical draft. No new fact_id, formal
submission, mathematical program, numerical evaluation, recurrence execution,
optimizer, installation, consult or subagent. This document closes only the
three specified screens. The original exact-profile minimax problem is OPEN.

## 1. Target, accepted interfaces, and the exact changed mechanism

The original target is to decide whether
lim_n W_n^*/U_n^ZJ=1, where W_n^*=inf_(h>=0) W_n(h) and
U_n^ZJ=1/B_n=1/(1+2S_bullet(n)), in the normalization
2(f(x_n)-min f)/(L*||x_0-x_star||^2). A matching affirmative proof requires
EVERY sufficiently large horizon and EVERY predetermined nonnegative word,
with a remainder independent of that word. None is supplied here.

Accepted dfde2fa326c908bf supplies full finite interpolation and the scoped
universal-lens exclusion. Accepted 1252b8823bb5a290 supplies maximal terminal
completion and the precise original directed residual. Neither fact says
that a freely prescribed switching Hessian sequence is realizable.
Accepted b98bb807d514e80d supplies the original benchmark definitions,
B_n<=1+4n^p with p=log_2(3), and the legal same-word Huber reference
H_base(h)=1/(1+2*sum h). Accepted 5fd396eba75651e7 supplies, on the current
enclosing-m word at tau=1/4 and every m>=1536,

    B_(2^m-1)*H_base(H_(m,1/4))<237/250.                 (1)

Only this scoped Huber comparison is used from the spiral fact. No primitive
history, negative minimax resolution, seed existence or discarded-prefix
claim is assumed.

The dispatch-specified shared drafts 687befe50820df21, 6e098f91c4a13444,
22347ffeb25f8830, d4ae45931cfc72a3, 97f52e264069f3ac,
8c09ef072ab9d6f9 and 5f198236d1ff200e were recalled from global memory.
They are UNVERIFIED awareness, not correctness premises. The first normal
and Jordan obstructions use c=13/5 and a=c^-17 or c^-18 with NO added1
in their bridge steps. The later near-unit Newton draft uses its own
tau=1 enclosing family. Those are not the current tau1/4 word.

The new controlling object is a SINGLE static convex C1 function with a
finite polyhedral partition. Its actual gradient changes according to
inequalities evaluated at the actual current point. Regional Hessians can
fail to commute, and the GD updates form an ordered operator word whose
letters are generated by these inequalities. No Hessian is assigned freely.
The constructions below all have explicit feedback or a reverse-side
reaction; none transports mass outward through disjoint tree generations.

For comparison, shared 89154918c70588a0/62e1d3a5b912ecbb studied a fixed
triangle-plane identity decomposition. Shared49c229ff9ff6eb2c/
0458dd4dceadebde studied outward64-ary Huber transport with pure-generation

the third family uses coupled metric projection. Their failures are derived
again below, without using those unverified claims as lemmas.

## 2. Uniform notation, diagnostic word, and normalization

All spaces are finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces. An operator norm
is the induced Euclidean norm. Positive part is z_+=max(z,0), and
negative part is z_-=max(-z,0). The superscript or subscript66 identifies
new local notation, distinct from the registered benchmark symbols.

Fix an integer m>=3 and 0<theta_66<=1/4. Put

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta_66=1-theta_66/m,
    c_66=lambda*(1+theta_66/m), a_66=beta_66/c_66,
    H^66_0=(), H^66_(j+1)=(H^66_j,b^66_j,H^66_j),
    b^66_j=1+a_66*c_66^j, n_m=2^m-1,

Every child uses this SAME enclosing (m,theta_66). Thus H^66_m is precisely
the current H_(m,tau) with tau=theta_66. No recursive child resets m.
The parameter theta_66 is unrelated to the project's Huber threshold tau.

steps of H^66_m are exactly (A_66,B_66,A_66,C_66).

The following rational bounds will be used, without numerical evaluation:

    4/3<A_66<sqrt(2)<17/12<3/2,

Indeed beta_66>=11/12, c_66<=13lambda/12, and lambda<5/2 imply
a_66>=11/(13lambda)>22/65>1/3. Also
a_66<1/lambda=sqrt(2)-1. Further B_66=1+beta_66, and

## 3. A complete scalar-to-field identity paying ALL directed rows

For 0<=eta<=1 define the single scalar C1 piecewise quadratic

    chi_eta(z)=(z_+^2+eta*z_-^2)/2,
    ell_eta(z)=chi_eta'(z)=z if z>=0, eta*z if z<=0.

These two definitions agree at0. The derivative is nondecreasing and
1-Lipschitz, so chi_eta is convex and C1. For any real s,t define

    J_eta(s,t)=chi_eta(s)-chi_eta(t)-ell_eta(t)*(s-t)
                         -(ell_eta(s)-ell_eta(t))^2/2.

Here is the exact exhaustive sign calculation:

    s,t>=0: J_eta=0;
    s,t<=0: J_eta=eta*(1-eta)*(s-t)^2/2;
    s>=0>=t: J_eta=eta*(1-eta)*t^2/2;
    s<=0<=t: J_eta=(1-eta)*(eta*s^2/2-s*t).             (4)

All four quantities are nonnegative. Endpoints satisfy adjacent formulas.
No scalar interpolation theorem is being imported.

Let T_66 be any real matrix with ||T_66||<=1, let d_66^aff be any fixed
offset vector, and define G(x)=sum_l chi_eta((T_66*x-d_66^aff)_l).
Put z_x=T_66*x-d_66^aff and v_x=(ell_eta((z_x)_l))_l. Then
grad G(x)=T_66^T*v_x, and

                         <=||T_66*(x-y)||<=||x-y||.

This proves global1-smoothness, including all partition boundaries. On an

of D are1 or eta. Consequently0<=Hessian<=I. Convexity also follows
directly from convex chi_eta composed with affine forms.

For ANY x,y, in the original directed orientation of1252b8823bb5a290,

    Q^66_xy=G(x)-G(y)+<grad G(x),y-x>
                          +||grad G(x)-grad G(y)||^2/2
     =-sum_l J_eta((z_y)_l,(z_x)_l)
       -(||v_y-v_x||^2-||T_66^T*(v_y-v_x)||^2)/2<=0.   (5)

This identity pays every ordered pair on the SAME function. In particular
it pays pairs of remote queries, pairs in either orientation at a zero

vectors are actual Euclidean vectors. There is no expected-only or
componentwise replacement for joint legality.

For the two fields below take, in R^2,

    u_66=(1,0), v_66=(-1/2,sqrt(3)/2), r_66=1/2,

## 4. Screen1: obtuse two-hinge activation feedback, then exact absorption

Put d_66=1-2A_66/3, e_66=2B_66/3-1, t_66=d_66*e_66. By (2),

    d_66>1/18, e_66>=5/18, t_66>5/324.               (9)

    x_1=d_66*u_66,
    x_2=-t_66*u_66,

## 3. Exact whole-field nonuniform real geometry

### 3.1 Explicit projective points, lines and counts

Choose the SMALLEST prime p_wm such that N=p_wm^2+p_wm+1>=k+1. This is a
definition, not a prime search executed in this round. Existence follows
from unboundedness of primes: a prime divisor of the integer
(k+1)!+1 is greater than k+1, since none of the smaller primes divides
that integer. No factorial or factorization was evaluated.

Work over the field Z/p_wm Z. Points are nonzero triples modulo nonzero
scalar multiplication; normalize a representative so its first nonzero
coordinate is1, and order these representatives lexicographically.
Lines are nonzero linear forms modulo nonzero scalar multiplication,
with the SAME representative/ordering convention. A point is on a line
exactly when its representative annihilates that linear form. Let P0
be the point represented by(1,0,0). Choose L_0 to be the line with
form(1,0,0), namely x=0; it does not contain P0. Choose L_1,...,
L_(ell-1) as the first remaining lines in the stated lexicographic order.
Since N>=k+1, these distinct selected lines form a proper subset.

There are N points and N lines: divide p_wm^3-1 nonzero triples by p_wm-1.
One nonzero form has p_wm^2 elements in its kernel, so its line has
(p_wm^2-1)/(p_wm-1)=p_wm+1 points. Two distinct forms are independent and
have a one-dimensional common kernel, hence their lines share one
point. Dually, every point lies on p_wm+1 lines and two distinct points
lie on one common line. These assertions follow by eliminating one
or two coordinates with nonzero coefficients, also for p_wm=2.

Let B be the REAL N-by-N incidence matrix, with point rows and line
columns. The point-side counts give the exact full-field identity

    B B^T=p_wm I+J_ff,                                     (3)

where I is the identity and J_ff is the all-ones matrix. In particular
B is invertible: for nonzero real z,
z^T(p_wm I+J_ff)z=p_wm||z||^2+(sum z)^2>0. Also B*1=(p_wm+1)*1.

### 3.2 Full-word point weights and their exact Gram

Use STRICTLY POSITIVE REAL point weights

    omega_P=1+1_(P=P0)
                 +(1/(1+S))*sum_(r<ell)b_r 1_(P in L_r),
    Omega_w=sum_P omega_P
            =N+1+[(p_wm+1)/(1+S)]*sum_(r<ell)b_r,
    omega_max=max_P omega_P.                          (4)

Thus 1<=omega_P<3. P0 has weight at least2 and every other point has
weight strictly below2, so the weights are nonuniform and P0 is their
unique maximizer. No negative metric weight or finite-field scalar
product is used as a Euclidean norm.

Let W be the real diagonal matrix diag(omega_P), let s have coordinates
sqrt(omega_P), and put P_w=I-s*s^T/Omega_w. This is an orthogonal
projection since ||s||^2=Omega_w. For EVERY projective line L, set

    d_L=sum_(P in L)omega_P,
    z_L(P)=sqrt(omega_P)*(1_(P in L)-d_L/Omega_w),
    A_L=z_L/sqrt(p_wm*omega_max).                        (5)

These are definite real vectors in R^N, perpendicular to s. Their
complete Gram, with no line omitted, is

    K_LM=sum_(P in L intersection M)omega_P-d_L*d_M/Omega_w,
    G_LM=<A_L,A_M>=K_LM/(p_wm*omega_max).                (6)

For L=M the weighted intersection sum is d_L. For L!=M it is the
weight of their unique intersection point. Moreover the degrees are
the fully explicit expressions

    d_L=p_wm+1+1_(P0 in L)
             +[H_pre+p_wm*b_r 1_(L=L_r for r<ell)]/(1+S),
    H_pre=sum_(r<ell)b_r.                             (7)

The bracket uses b_r only if L is a selected line, and otherwise is
H_pre. Formula(7) follows from one-point intersections and the p_wm+1
points on a line meeting itself.

There is an exact WHOLE-FIELD frame normalization. Let A be the matrix
with ALL N feature columns A_L, not only the selected temporal lines.
The unscaled feature matrix is P_w W^(1/2) B. By(3),

    A A^T=P_w W P_w/omega_max<=P_w<=I.               (8)

Indeed P_w W^(1/2) J_ff W^(1/2) P_w=P_w*s*s^T*P_w=0,
and the p_wm I term is p_wm P_w W P_w. Thus the normalization is proved on
the whole field and not guessed from a selected small Gram. For ANY
real temporal coefficient columns c,d,

    <sum_L c_L A_L,sum_M d_M A_M>=c^T G_wm d,        (9)

where G_wm is the matrix with entries G_LM in(6). This is a real PSD
Gram because the vectors
are explicitly Euclidean; no arbitrary PSD selection is substituted.

The only null coefficient column of A is a constant column. In fact,
A c=0 implies W^(1/2)B c is proportional to s=W^(1/2)1, hence
B c is constant; invertibility and B1=(p_wm+1)1 imply c is constant.
This proves nonvanishing of every nonzero coefficient column supported
on a proper subset of the lines, with no independence assumption.

# Whole-field nonregularity for every positive nonuniform point metric

Let p_wm be a prime, and put N=p_wm^2+p_wm+1. Points of the projective
plane over Z/p_wm Z are nonzero triples modulo nonzero scalars, and
lines are nonzero forms modulo scalars, with incidence by annihilation.
There are N points and N lines because each nonzero class has p_wm-1
representatives. A nonzero form has a two-dimensional kernel, giving
p_wm+1 points per line. Distinct line forms have a one-dimensional
common kernel, hence one intersection point. Dually each point is on
p_wm+1 lines and two distinct points share one line. All counts follow
by eliminating one or two coordinates with nonzero coefficients.

Let B be the real point-by-line incidence matrix. With I the identity,
J_ff the all-ones matrix and 1 the all-ones column, the point-side
counts give

    B B^T=p_wm I+J_ff, B1=(p_wm+1)1.                  (A1)

B is invertible since for nonzero z the quadratic form of B B^T is
p_wm||z||^2+(sum z)^2>0.
