                         [beta*(p(q_(j-1))+q_(j-1))].       (9)

At a transition to q_(j-1)=0 this follows from y_(j-1)=y_j;
if both q's are zero it is equality. The numerator is the integral
of p(q_(j-1))-q_(j-1)*p'(t). After division by p(q_(j-1))+q_(j-1)
the integrand is <=max(1,-p'(t)). Since w_N=1, multiplication gives

    y_i<=Y_k:=2 exp(2k),
    integral_0^1 max(1,-p'(t))dt=sqrt(2)*(1+beta)-beta<2.

For the integral split at t=(1+beta)/sqrt(2)-beta.
At uncapped points u<=beta+2k*(Y_k+beta). The uncapped backward steps
are contiguous and have p>=beta; their combined deficit from C times
half their mass is <=4k^2*(Y_k+beta). The remaining p's equal C.
Paying also y_i/beta and beta gives

    |M_i-C*s_i/2|<=K_k:=20k^2 exp(2k).                     (10)

The concave function p(q)+q/beta has smaller endpoint C. Using (5),

    M_i>=beta+1/beta+C*s_i/2>=C*(1+s_i/2).                 (11)

Let v_mass=a_word/d. Since c*(c-2)>1>eta_word, 0<v_mass<1.
Substitution in the exact mass relation gives

    1+S_j=v_mass*c^j+(1-v_mass)*2^j,
    b_j=d*S_j+c-1-d*(1-v_mass)*2^j.                       (12)

Uniformly for J<=j<=m-1 the relative leading-mass error is
O(c^(-J)+(2/c)^J). Also k*K_k/S_J->0: its numerator has logarithm
O(k+log k) and the denominator has logarithm J*log(lambda)+O(1).
Using 0<=x-log(1+x)<=x^2/2 with x=1/(4m) yields

    S_J/lambda^J->exp(1/4),
    S_(m-r)/lambda^(m-r)->exp(1/4) for every fixed r>=1.

The first amplitude ratio T_1/M_1 is (d/C)*(1+o(1)); the other amplitude
ratios are (c*d/C)*(1+o(1)). The individual relative errors are uniformly
O(K_k/S_J+c^(-J)+(2/c)^J), and k times this bound tends to zero.
Taking logarithms in the product therefore proves

    D_(k+1)=(d/C)*(c*d/C)^(k-1)*(1+o(1))
                 ->(lambda-2)*exp(-2),
    R_m^2->1, sigma_1~2/(C*S_J),
    sigma_(i+1)/sigma_i=T_i/M_(i+1)->lambda-2               (13)

uniformly for i<k. Here c*d=1+O(1/m) and log(C)/beta->2,
so C^k->exp(2). Eventually every adjacent sigma ratio is in [1/3,1/2],
and sum sigma_i^2<=2sigma_1^2.

The ORIGINAL ALL-SPLIT benchmark is C_0^bench=B_0=1,

    C_n^bench=max_(0<=r<n)Omega(C_r^bench,C_(n-r-1)^bench),
    B_n=max_(0<=r<n)G(C_r^bench,B_(n-r-1)),
    Omega(a,b)=(a+b+sqrt((a+b)^2+4ab))/2,
    G(a,b)=2a+b/2+sqrt(b^2+8ab)/2, U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

The circle constant C in this report is distinct from C_n^bench.
Only the unconditional ray conclusion of accepted fact04219554e41d9750
is used:

    0<Z_1=lim_m lambda^(-m) B_(2^m-1)<infinity,
    Z_1<5.                                                (14)

The latter follows from its b=1,j=0 upper enclosure, B_1=4, and
(2+3/100)^2<5. No seed hypothesis is assumed.

Put q_root=t_k=2^(m-1), N=2^(m-1)-1. The final suffix is the actual
ordered H_(m-1), indexed t=0,...,N. During this suffix the last excess
is D_(k+1)-delta times half the mass already read, and stays >=delta.
Output isolation gives Q_k=0, proving this claim by induction.
Thus its terminal Huber numerator is exactly D_(k+1)^2/[2(1+S)].

The retired function and its exact updates are

    G_ret(x)=1/2 sum_(i<k)Phi_i(x_i,x_(i+1))
                         +1/2 Hub_(C*sigma_k)(x_k-A_k),
    d_i=P_i-Q_(i-1), x^+=x-(h/2)d, Q_0=Q_k=0,
    V_m=2G_ret(x(N))=sum_(i=1)^k Phi_i(x(N)).

Phi_k denotes the original last circular value, exactly equal to this
horizontal Huber at these actual states. Hence

    B_n*2F(x_n)/R_m^2=T_m+B_n*V_m/R_m^2,
    T_m=B_n*D_(k+1)^2/[2(1+S)*R_m^2]
                  ->T_infty=Z_1*exp(-17/4)/(2lambda)<5/64. (15)

The useful finite-error normalizing scale is

    (B_n/R_m^2)*sigma_1^2*(1+K_k+2^m)->0.                  (16)

Indeed B_n*sigma_1^2=O(lambda^(-m+2k)); multiplying by K_k
still decays exponentially in m. The remaining term is

## 1. Frozen definitions and jointly checked local identities

All spaces and inner products are real Euclidean. Put

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), k=floor(sqrt(m)), J=m-k, beta=1/k,
    eta_word=1-1/(4m), c=lambda*(1+1/(4m)), a_word=eta_word/c,

Every child retains this SAME enclosing m. Checkpoint i is the first
occurrence of level l_i=J+i-1. Its post-step query is t_i=2^l_i.
The ordinary blocks have masses s_1=S_J and s_i=S_(J+i-2) for i>=2.
The final suffix starts at t_k=2^(m-1), has word H_(m-1), length
N=2^(m-1)-1 and mass S=S_(m-1). Set S_pre=S_(m-1)+b_(m-1).

In suffix entry, exit and persistence formulas, time0 means the actual
global query t_k, and timeN means the actual global terminal query n:
x(t)=x_(t_k+t). The checkpoint labels t_i and the full-prefix integral
endpoints T use global physical time. No initial state is replaced when
passing between these two indexing conventions.

For0<=q<=1 set

    p(q)=beta+sqrt((1+beta)^2-(q+beta)^2),
    e=sqrt(1+2beta), C=beta+e, kappa=1+beta^2,
    K=conv({0} union {(p(q),-q):0<=q<=1}).

The entire body's sections are beta q<=p<=p(q). Its horizontal cap is
C and its vertical cap is1. For compact convex B containing0 put
E_B(w)=max_(g in B)(<g,w>-||g||^2/2). Its gradient is Pi_B(w).
Hub_L denotes the one-sided Huber with gradient clip(r,0,L).

The local backward coordinates u_i,y_i use the ACTUAL order of the
ordinary block and the full circle, as explicitly defined and derived
in Appendix A. Put M_i=u_i+y_i/beta. Before running GD fix

    ell_1=0, D_1=1, T_i=b_(l_i)/2-1,
    sigma_i=D_i/M_i, D_(i+1)=sigma_i T_i,
    ell_(i+1)=sigma_i y_i, A_i=ell_i+ell_(i+1)/beta,
    Phi_i(X,Y)=E_(sigma_i K)(X-A_i,Y-ell_(i+1)),

                     +1/2 Hub_delta(x_(k+1)-ell_(k+1)), x_0=e_1.

## 3. Comparison B: actual terminal edges and chronological horizontal exits

### B1. A finite initialized edge bound on its exact horizontal guard

Define for a middle i

    Z_i=(beta C+3/4+4C^2)sigma_i,

Suppose r_i<=L_i and z_i>Z_i at an ACTUAL query. Let

If r_i<=0, (2) already implies Q_i=sigma_i. If r_i>0,

z_i=beta r_i+v_i<=Z_i, a contradiction. Consequently

### B2. Retain the actual datum at the last horizontal exit

If r_i(N)<=L_i but(16) is not known, let a_i^exit=0 when(16) holds.
Otherwise let a_i^exit=1+max{t<N:r_i(t)>L_i}. This is the actual

edge samples are high and(15) gives z_i(N)<=z_i(a_i^exit)
-gamma_i M_after(a_i^exit)/2. Define the ACTUAL exit debt

and E_i^exit=0. For a genuine exit it is a new, explicit chronological

    z_i(a_i^exit)=z_i(s)-alpha[kappa Q_i-beta Q_(i-1)
                          -beta Q_(i+1)+beta U_i-U_(i+1)](s),
    s=a_i^exit-1.                                           (22)

An exit may not inherit the initialized bound(18). No entrance to a
zero cone, horizontal guard or bounded exit edge is silently inferred.

### B3. An exact scoped failure of a source-free horizontal-exit reset

The claim that every horizontal exit automatically has z_i=O(sigma_i)
is false for the SAME frozen function, even with no incoming gradient
and no downstream horizontal gradient. The following is an ALTERNATIVE
state test, not an initialized trajectory or a lower witness.

Choose2<=i<=k-2 and a physical available h=b_(m-2), alpha=h/2, with
alpha>1 and alpha beta>C/2. Choose q in(0,1) close to1 and write p=p(q).
Set

    t=[(alpha-1)sigma_i p+L_i/2]/(p-beta)>0,
    r_i= sigma_i p+t(p-beta)=alpha sigma_i p+L_i/2,
    v_i= sigma_i q+t(q+beta),
    x_i=A_i+r_i, x_(i+1)=ell_(i+1)-v_i,
    x_(i+2)=ell_(i+2).

The vector (r_i,-v_i)-(sigma_i p,-sigma_i q)
is t(p-beta,-q-beta), an outward circle normal. Thus its ACTUAL
projection is(P_i,-Q_i)=(sigma_i p,-sigma_i q).

All earlier components can be made zero at both samples by the explicit
recursive choice x_j=min(A_j,ell_j+x_(j+1)/beta)-sigma_j for j=i-1,...,1,
using the smaller of the initial and proposed next boundary coordinate
at j=i-1; also enforce x_1<=A_1-beta D_2. Earlier coordinates then have
zero gradients and do not move. All later coordinates after i+2 are0,
except the isolated scalar x_(k+1)=ell_(k+1)+D_(k+1).
The next component has input below ell_(i+1) and output ell_(i+2),
so P_(i+1)=Q_(i+1)=0; all other retired components also vanish.

The actual step therefore has

    r_i^+=L_i/2,
    v_i^+=v_i-alpha sigma_i q
        =(alpha-1)sigma_i beta(p+q)/(p-beta)
                                  +(L_i/2)(q+beta)/(p-beta)>0,
    z_i^+=beta L_i/2+v_i^+.                                 (23)

As q approaches1, p-beta approaches0 while beta>0. For any proposed
constant cap-scale reset, (23) exceeds it. The new input is below L_i,
while the new actual edge residual is arbitrarily large. The next
component remains zero since its input is still below its translation;
all earlier zero-cone choices remain valid since x_i^+>A_i>=ell_i.
The isolated tail excess stays positive for this legal suffix step.

Thus terminal/exit input information alone does not supply a bounded
edge state. The tested normal parameter and huge initial downstream
deficit are not asserted reachable from e_1. The actual initialized
exit debt(21),(22) remains OPEN, not refuted. This is a new exit-reset
failure, distinct from the previously screened cross-time and
simultaneous-checkpoint-margin claims.


## Appendix A: joint frozen local geometry and scale derivations

## 1. Exact static function, body and physical word

For each integer m>=16 put

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), k=floor(sqrt(m)), J=m-k, beta=1/k,
    eta_word=1-1/(4m), c=lambda*(1+1/(4m)), a_word=eta_word/c,
    d=c-2,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j), b_j=1+a_word*c^j,
    S_j=sum H_j, n=2^m-1.

Every child uses this SAME enclosing m and these same parameters. Select
the first occurrences of levels J,...,m-1. Checkpoint i has level
l_i=J+i-1, physical step index 2^l_i-1 and value b_l_i.
The ordinary block masses are s_1=S_J, s_i=S_(J+i-2) for 2<=i<=k,
and the last mass is S=S_(m-1). Every entry of the word is executed.

For 0<=q<=1 define

    p(q)=beta+sqrt((1+beta)^2-(q+beta)^2),
    C=beta+sqrt(1+2beta), e=C-beta=sqrt(1+2beta),
    K=conv({0} union {(p(q),-q):0<=q<=1}),
    kappa=1+beta^2.

The complete horizontal sections of this full body are

    0<=q<=1, beta*q<=p<=p(q).                              (1)

It has the two radial segments to (C,0) and (beta,-1), and the whole
circular arc between them. No finite-plane replacement is made.

For a compact convex body B containing0 put

    E_B(w)=max_(g in B){<g,w>-||g||^2/2}.

Write Hub_L for the one-sided Huber: zero for r<=0, r^2/2 for
0<=r<=L, and L*r-L^2/2 for r>=L.

The local data of every ordinary block are defined using its actual order.
If its physical entries are a_1,...,a_N, set alpha_j=a_j/2.
Start (u_N,-y_N)=(beta,-1), q_N=1, and define backwards

    (q_(j-1)+beta)/(p(q_(j-1))-beta)
       =max{beta/e, (y_j+(1-alpha_j)*beta)/
                              (u_j-(1-alpha_j)*beta)},
    (u_(j-1),-y_(j-1))=(u_j,-y_j)+alpha_j*(p(q_(j-1)),-q_(j-1)).
                                                               (2)

The left side increases continuously from beta/e to infinity. Its right
denominator is positive since u_j>=beta and alpha_j>0. The starting
coordinates for block i are denoted u_i,y_i; set M_i=u_i+y_i/beta.
These are finite symbolic definitions, not a recurrence executed this round.

Fix ell_1=0,D_1=1 and define, before the run,

    T_i=b_l_i/2-1, sigma_i=D_i/M_i,
    ell_(i+1)=sigma_i*y_i, A_i=ell_i+ell_(i+1)/beta,
    D_(i+1)=sigma_i*T_i,
    Phi_i(X,Y)=E_(sigma_i K)(X-A_i,Y-ell_(i+1)),
    delta=D_(k+1)/(1+S),
    F(x)=1/2 sum_(i=1)^k Phi_i(x_i,x_(i+1))
                      +1/2 Hub_delta(x_(k+1)-ell_(k+1)),
    x_0=e_1 in R^(k+1).                                    (3)

We use the range in which every T_i>0; this holds for all sufficiently
large m. This is exactly the frozen circular half-sum.

## 2. Geometry, true radius, and every neighboring gradient

Completing the square in E_B identifies its unique maximizer as Pi_B(w),
the Euclidean projection. The maximizing inequalities at w and w' imply

    ||Pi_B(w)-Pi_B(w')||^2
                <=<Pi_B(w)-Pi_B(w'),w-w'>.

The maximizing formula and this inequality give differentiability with
gradient Pi_B and a 1-Lipschitz gradient. Thus E_B is convex, nonnegative
and1-smooth. Its zero set is the polar cone of B: if some support pairing
is positive, taking a sufficiently small positive multiple of that
support vector gives a positive envelope value.

The cone of K has extreme rays (C,0),(beta,-1). Consequently

    Phi_i=0 iff x_i<=A_i and
                      x_(i+1)>=beta*(x_i-ell_i).            (4)

The disk with center(beta,beta), radius1+beta supports the whole arc.
Its normal and the horizontal endpoint normal prove, in (2),

    Pi_K(u_j,-y_j)=(p(q_j),-q_j),
    u_i=beta+sum alpha_j*p(q_(j-1)),
    y_i=1+sum alpha_j*q_(j-1), u_i>=beta*y_i.                (5)

For the uncapped points the normal ratio is (y_j+beta)/(u_j-beta).
The defining predecessor ratio reduces its numerator by alpha_j*beta
and increases its denominator by the same amount, so q_(j-1)<=q_j.
At the capped endpoint the inequality y<=beta*(u-C)/e is preserved
by every further backward capped step. These facts check the normals
also at the transition and endpoints.

At any global query, define ALL gradients by

    (P_i,-Q_i)=Pi_(sigma_i K)(x_i-A_i,x_(i+1)-ell_(i+1)), i<=k,
    P_(k+1)=clip(x_(k+1)-ell_(k+1),0,delta), Q_0=0.

Every physical step is exactly

    x_j^+=x_j-(h/2)(P_j-Q_(j-1)), 1<=j<=k+1.               (6)

In particular earlier components are never reset or deleted.

If x_(i+1)>=ell_(i+1), replacing (P,-Q) by (P,0) improves its
maximization by Q*(x_(i+1)-ell_(i+1))+Q^2/2 when Q>0.
Thus Q_i=0 in that region. If x_i<=ell_i and its output is
nonnegative, (4) gives Phi_i=0.

These properties prove the active-pair chronology inductively. At block i
the active local states are (A_i+sigma_i*u_j,ell_(i+1)-sigma_i*y_j);
its input is >=ell_i, so Q_(i-1)=0 at the ACTIVE pair's queries.
Its next component vanishes, as do all still-future components.
Earlier components retain (6). The selected step produces, exactly,

    x_i(t_i)=A_i-beta*D_(i+1),
    x_(i+1)(t_i)=ell_(i+1)+D_(i+1),
    t_i=2^l_i.                                             (7)

Equation(7) specifies only that pair at its OWN checkpoint time.
It is not a simultaneous snapshot of the later retired chain.

The map stacking all adjacent pairs and the last scalar counts each
coordinate at most twice. Its squared norm is <=2. Thus the factor1/2
makes F convex1-smooth. F>=0 and F(0)=0. Its entire minimum set is

    C_min={x: x_i<=A_i,
                x_(i+1)>=beta*(x_i-ell_i), 1<=i<=k;
                                      x_(k+1)<=ell_(k+1)}.

The point (A_1,ell_2,0,...,0) belongs to it. From (5),

    1-A_1=sigma_1*u_1, ell_2=beta*A_1=sigma_1*y_1,
    A_1<=1/(1+beta^2).

For x_1<0 the squared distance from e_1 is at least1.
For 0<=x_1<=A_1 it is at least (1-x_1)^2+beta^2*x_1^2,
decreasing on this interval and attained by that feasible point. Therefore

    R_m^2=dist(e_1,C_min)^2
          =(1-A_1)^2+ell_2^2=(u_1^2+y_1^2)/M_1^2>0.        (8)

All physical samples, terminal samples and minimizers obey every ordered
smooth-convex interpolation inequality. To check this directly, apply
the 1-smooth descent inequality to F(z)-<grad F(y),z>, minimized at y;
it gives F(x)-F(y)-<grad F(y),x-y>>=||grad F(x)-grad F(y)||^2/2.
The Gram matrices are actual Euclidean Gram matrices. Scaling F by an
advertised L>0 and using steps h/L preserves (6) and the normalized payoff.

## 3. Uniform scales and the strictly scoped accepted input

Here are the bounds needed for the normalizations, derived jointly so no
earlier unverified estimate is used as a premise.

In a backward block set w_j=(y_j+beta)/(q_j+beta). Expansion of (2),
using the circular normal at uncapped points, gives

    w_(j-1)/w_j
       =1+[p(q_(j-1))*q_j-q_(j-1)*p(q_j)]/
                         [beta*(p(q_(j-1))+q_(j-1))].       (9)

At a transition to q_(j-1)=0 this follows from y_(j-1)=y_j;
if both q's are zero it is equality. The numerator is the integral
of p(q_(j-1))-q_(j-1)*p'(t). After division by p(q_(j-1))+q_(j-1)
the integrand is <=max(1,-p'(t)). Since w_N=1, multiplication gives

    y_i<=Y_k:=2 exp(2k),
    integral_0^1 max(1,-p'(t))dt=sqrt(2)*(1+beta)-beta<2.

For the integral split at t=(1+beta)/sqrt(2)-beta.
At uncapped points u<=beta+2k*(Y_k+beta). The uncapped backward steps
are contiguous and have p>=beta; their combined deficit from C times
half their mass is <=4k^2*(Y_k+beta). The remaining p's equal C.
Paying also y_i/beta and beta gives

    |M_i-C*s_i/2|<=K_k:=20k^2 exp(2k).                     (10)

The concave function p(q)+q/beta has smaller endpoint C. Using (5),

    M_i>=beta+1/beta+C*s_i/2>=C*(1+s_i/2).                 (11)

Let v_mass=a_word/d. Since c*(c-2)>1>eta_word, 0<v_mass<1.
Substitution in the exact mass relation gives

    1+S_j=v_mass*c^j+(1-v_mass)*2^j,
    b_j=d*S_j+c-1-d*(1-v_mass)*2^j.                       (12)

Uniformly for J<=j<=m-1 the relative leading-mass error is
O(c^(-J)+(2/c)^J). Also k*K_k/S_J->0: its numerator has logarithm
O(k+log k) and the denominator has logarithm J*log(lambda)+O(1).
Using 0<=x-log(1+x)<=x^2/2 with x=1/(4m) yields

    S_J/lambda^J->exp(1/4),
    S_(m-r)/lambda^(m-r)->exp(1/4) for every fixed r>=1.

The first amplitude ratio T_1/M_1 is (d/C)*(1+o(1)); the other amplitude
ratios are (c*d/C)*(1+o(1)). The individual relative errors are uniformly
O(K_k/S_J+c^(-J)+(2/c)^J), and k times this bound tends to zero.
Taking logarithms in the product therefore proves

    D_(k+1)=(d/C)*(c*d/C)^(k-1)*(1+o(1))
                 ->(lambda-2)*exp(-2),
    R_m^2->1, sigma_1~2/(C*S_J),
    sigma_(i+1)/sigma_i=T_i/M_(i+1)->lambda-2               (13)

uniformly for i<k. Here c*d=1+O(1/m) and log(C)/beta->2,
so C^k->exp(2). Eventually every adjacent sigma ratio is in [1/3,1/2],
and sum sigma_i^2<=2sigma_1^2.

The ORIGINAL ALL-SPLIT benchmark is C_0^bench=B_0=1,

    C_n^bench=max_(0<=r<n)Omega(C_r^bench,C_(n-r-1)^bench),
    B_n=max_(0<=r<n)G(C_r^bench,B_(n-r-1)),
    Omega(a,b)=(a+b+sqrt((a+b)^2+4ab))/2,
    G(a,b)=2a+b/2+sqrt(b^2+8ab)/2, U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

The circle constant C in this report is distinct from C_n^bench.
Only the unconditional ray conclusion of accepted fact04219554e41d9750
is used:

    0<Z_1=lim_m lambda^(-m) B_(2^m-1)<infinity,
    Z_1<5.                                                (14)

The latter follows from its b=1,j=0 upper enclosure, B_1=4, and
(2+3/100)^2<5. No seed hypothesis is assumed.

Put q_root=t_k=2^(m-1), N=2^(m-1)-1. The final suffix is the actual
ordered H_(m-1), indexed t=0,...,N. During this suffix the last excess
is D_(k+1)-delta times half the mass already read, and stays >=delta.
Output isolation gives Q_k=0, proving this claim by induction.
Thus its terminal Huber numerator is exactly D_(k+1)^2/[2(1+S)].

The retired function and its exact updates are

    G_ret(x)=1/2 sum_(i<k)Phi_i(x_i,x_(i+1))
                         +1/2 Hub_(C*sigma_k)(x_k-A_k),
    d_i=P_i-Q_(i-1), x^+=x-(h/2)d, Q_0=Q_k=0,
    V_m=2G_ret(x(N))=sum_(i=1)^k Phi_i(x(N)).

Phi_k denotes the original last circular value, exactly equal to this
horizontal Huber at these actual states. Hence

    B_n*2F(x_n)/R_m^2=T_m+B_n*V_m/R_m^2,
    T_m=B_n*D_(k+1)^2/[2(1+S)*R_m^2]
                  ->T_infty=Z_1*exp(-17/4)/(2lambda)<5/64. (15)

The useful finite-error normalizing scale is

    (B_n/R_m^2)*sigma_1^2*(1+K_k+2^m)->0.                  (16)

Indeed B_n*sigma_1^2=O(lambda^(-m+2k)); multiplying by K_k
still decays exponentially in m. The remaining term is
O((2/lambda)^m*lambda^(2k)), also tending to zero. No numerical
evaluation, finite benchmark replay or m>=1536 inference is used.

## 1. Scope and result

We specify THREE complete laws on the FULL given nonnegative physical word.
They genuinely retain a nonzero terminal memory, or choose an explicit
last-step-dependent terminal coefficient. No free terminal reset is used.
All returns are attached to actual positive physical steps.

The laws are:

A. Retain the final negative-memory jet, keeping word-dependent paired
   coefficients at the early queries.
B. Use constant early longitudinal coefficients, rebuild the signed
   retired memory at the actual late queries, and fit the terminal
   coefficient to the last physical two-row inequality.
C. Pay every late return locally by a curved longitudinal coefficient
   -sqrt(4-2z^2), and retain the final negative-memory jet.

On the SAME inherited-enclosing-m tau=1/4 word H_m, for EVERY m>=1536:

* A pays its initial-to-terminal and last cycles, but its FIRST physical
  two-row cycle is strictly positive.
* B pays its first, initial-to-terminal and last cycles, but its
  PENULTIMATE physical two-row cycle is strictly positive.
* C pays EVERY consecutive physical two-row cycle and its
  initial-to-terminal cycle. Its ORIGINAL central-query-to-terminal
  two-row cycle is strictly positive.

The impossibility screens hold for EVERY positive common scale, every
value array, every initial anchor and every minimizer. These are failures
of the stated coefficient laws, not bounds on unrestricted W.

A and B leave exact sum h_t*g_t=S*g_n on every word with at least four
positive steps. C leaves it on the decisive H_m words. We do NOT apply
the previous closure/HUBER argument outside its hypotheses.

We also give a completely specified static wrapper: use a law's fixed
jets only if every original directed row passes with a strictly feasible
optimum interval; otherwise choose the canonical Huber function BEFORE
the whole run. This wrapper is legal on every physical word. On H_m
each of the three wrappers is exactly the Huber fallback, with TRUE
closest radius1 and normalized payoff1/(1+2S_m). Accepted fact
5fd396eba75651e7 then gives its original benchmark ratio<237/250.
There is no stronger finite bridge or universal profile construction.

Only accepted1252b8823bb5a290 (the original interpolation inequalities
and its self-contained conjugate construction) and accepted
5fd396eba75651e7 (only its same-word Huber/benchmark comparison) are
mathematical premises. The three prior findings87225e1b68c94b70,
c47175818b62b7b9 and329c21b1c4c24404 supply orientation, not premises.
Every changed coefficient and cycle is rederived in this joint draft.
No new component below is presented as a verifier-accepted fact.

## 2. Full word, exact features, and repetition convention

Normalize smoothness to1. Let

    h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) in [0,infinity)^n,
    S=sum_(i<n)h_i.

List its positive physical steps at original indices

    i_0<...<i_(k-1), b_r=h_(i_r)>0,
    j(i)=#{r:i_r<i}, 0<=i<=n.

A compressed sample r is lifted to original physical sample i by r=j(i).
Thus every zero step repeats the COMPLETE point, gradient AND value,
including zeros before the first positive step and after the last one.
All original ordered rows remain in the construction.

For k<4 use the canonical Huber fallback in Section4.3. This common
fallback is not a fourth screened memory law. Henceforth k>=4 and

    ell=floor(k/2), r'=k-1-r for 0<=r<ell,
    A_half=sum_(r<ell)b_r>0,
    z_r=sum_(a=r)^(ell-1)b_a/A_half, 0<=r<ell,
    d_r=b_r/A_half.

In particular z_0=1, 0<z_r<=1, and

    z_r-z_(r+1)=d_r for r<ell-1,
    z_(ell-1)=d_(ell-1).

These are finite DEFINITIONS using the entire physical word, not an
executed recurrence. Our fixed real features are the orthonormal vectors

    e_ret=(1,0), u_ret=(0,1).

The explicitly retired suffix is z_r*u_ret, and the rth innovation being
retired is d_r*u_ret. Its exact Gram is

    <z_r*u_ret,z_s*u_ret>=z_r*z_s.

The purpose here is to change the temporal return law and pay its
cycles. There is no arbitrary PSD selection, and no claim that a Gram
change alone is progress.

The late query r' returns the SAME already specified suffix z_r, with
the explicit coefficients given next. The actual ratio is

    rho_r=b_r/b_(r')>0.

If k is odd, the middle query ell has gradient vector e_ret. Its step
mass is B_mid=b_ell. If k is even put B_mid=0 and there is no middle query.
Write

    E_suffix=sum_(r<ell)b_r*z_r.

Since ell>=2 and all b_r>0,

    0<E_suffix<A_half.                                  (1)

Indeed z_0=1 and z_1<1, and each z_r<=1.

## 3. Three full coefficient laws

For each law write its dimensionless vector as

    v_r=L_r*e_ret+T_r*u_ret, 0<=r<=k.

All coefficients are fixed from the given h before any function is run.

### 3.1 A: ratio-weighted retained endpoint

Define

    alpha_r=b_(r')/(1+b_r+b_(r')),
    beta_r=b_r/(1+b_r+b_(r')),
    alpha_0>0.

For early and paired late queries put

    v_r=e_ret+(alpha_r/alpha_0)*(e_ret+z_r*u_ret/2),
    v_(r')=e_ret-2*(beta_r/alpha_0)*(e_ret+z_r*u_ret/2). (2A)

Use v_ell=e_ret when k is odd. RETAIN the last actual jet:

    v_k=v_(k-1)
       =(1-2rho_0)*e_ret-rho_0*u_ret.                 (3A)

There is no change of gradient at the last physical step in this law.

Define the fully specified longitudinal and transverse return sums

    M_long=sum_(r<ell)b_r*alpha_r/alpha_0,
    M_trans=sum_(r<ell)b_r*alpha_r*z_r/alpha_0.

The pair identity b_r*alpha_r=b_(r')*beta_r gives the FULL displacement

    D_k=sum_(r<k)b_r*v_r
       =(S-M_long)*e_ret-M_trans*u_ret/2.             (4A)

No remote coefficient is discarded. Because ell>=2,

    M_trans<M_long.                                  (5A)

For the terminal vector in(3A), L_k=1+2T_k. If D_k=S*v_k,
its coordinates in(4A) would give M_long=M_trans, contrary to(5A).
Thus A is NONCLOSING for every stated given word.

### 3.2 B: constant early coefficients and last-step endpoint matching

For early and paired late queries put

    v_r=2e_ret+z_r*u_ret/2,
    v_(r')=(1-2rho_r)*e_ret-rho_r*z_r*u_ret.           (2B)

The middle vector, when present, is e_ret. The last preterminal vector is

    w_last=(1-2rho_0)*e_ret-rho_0*u_ret.
    Delta_end=e_ret-w_last=rho_0*(2e_ret+u_ret).

Define the explicit, word-dependent endpoint coefficient

    q_end=min{1, max{0,b_(k-1)*(1-2/(5rho_0))}},
    v_k=w_last+q_end*Delta_end.                       (3B)

A trailing zero does not trigger(3B) a second time: the full terminal
jet is set at compressed query k and copied at every repeated point.

The FULL displacement is exactly

    D_k=(S-A_half)*e_ret-E_suffix*u_ret/2.            (4B)

To obtain it, a paired longitudinal contribution is
2b_r+b_(r')*(1-2rho_r)=b_(r'), and the transverse contribution is
b_r*z_r/2-b_(r')*rho_r*z_r=-b_r*z_r/2.

Again L_k=1+2T_k. If D_k=S*v_k, the coordinate identity would imply
A_half=E_suffix, which(1) forbids. Hence B is NONCLOSING for every
stated word, independently of the chosen endpoint coefficient.

The endpoint cycle is rederived directly. The last vector change is
q_end*Delta_end, so its dimensionless charge is

    q_end^2*||Delta_end||^2
          +b_(k-1)*q_end*<Delta_end,w_last>
      =rho_0^2*q_end
             [5q_end+b_(k-1)*(2/rho_0-5)]<=0.        (5B)

If rho_0<=2/5, q_end=0 and the charge is0.
If rho_0>2/5, the chosen q_end is no greater than
b_(k-1)*(1-2/(5rho_0)); substituting proves the inequality.
This pays the ORIGINAL last positive physical step, not a substituted
terminal price or a fictitious reset.

### 3.3 C: curved longitudinal payment on every late return

Let

    ell_curve(z)=sqrt(4-2z^2), 0<=z<=1.

This is real and lies in[sqrt(2),2]. Set

    v_r=2e_ret+z_r*u_ret/2,
    v_(r')=-ell_curve(z_r)*e_ret-rho_r*z_r*u_ret.     (2C)

Use v_ell=e_ret when k is odd, and RETAIN the last vector:

    v_k=v_(k-1)=-sqrt(2)*e_ret-rho_0*u_ret.           (3C)

The longitudinal payment is not the old linear pair compensation.
It changes at each ACTUAL late query. Its full displacement is

    D_k=[2A_half-sum_(r<ell)b_(r')*ell_curve(z_r)+B_mid]*e_ret
                            -E_suffix*u_ret/2.      (4C)

On positive palindromes rho_r=1 and
S=2A_half+B_mid, so

    D_k=[B_mid+sum_(r<ell)b_r*(2-ell_curve(z_r))]*e_ret
                            -E_suffix*u_ret/2.      (5C)

Its longitudinal coordinate is positive, whereas v_k's is negative.
Thus C leaves exact D_k=S*v_k on every positive odd palindrome,
in particular every diagnostic H_m. No closure-based Huber bound is
used to screen C. Nothing in this draft asserts that an arbitrary
nonpalindromic C input cannot accidentally satisfy a closure identity.

## 4. Every point, one common value array, every original row, and static wrapper

The fixed initial anchor for each memory transcript is

    X_ret=6e_ret-u_ret, ||X_ret||^2=37.

For the definite full-h mapping choose

    sigma_h=1/(1+2S)>0.

The impossibility proofs will hold for any sigma>0, so we also state

strengthening of the screen, not an optimization performed here.

For each specified law define the finite prefix sums

    D_r=sum_(t<r)b_t*v_t,
    xhat_r=X_ret-sigma*D_r, ghat_r=sigma*v_r, 0<=r<=k,

For each compressed step t<k define its two adjacent price bounds

    p_t^hi=b_t*||v_t||^2-||v_(t+1)-v_t||^2/2,

    L_r^opt=sigma^2*[||v_r||^2/2-C_r^val],

Original physical finite rows are(10) with their indices j(i),j(j).
Equal compressed indices give residual0. No directed row is deleted.

For ANY two compressed finite indices s<t the exact two-row charge is

## 10. Failure synthesis and exact remaining interface

The three laws successively repair distinct original obligations:

A: final retention pays last and initial-terminal cycles, but
   variable early pair ratios increase the first gradient.
B: constant early coefficients pay first, and a word-dependent
   endpoint fit pays last, but every rebuilt negative suffix introduces
   earlier positive late cycles.
C: nonlinear longitudinal matching pays ALL those actual local returns
   and the initial-terminal cycle, but the FULL central-to-terminal
   displacement fails a different original remote cycle.

The shared obstacle is not an inability to choose a real Gram:
all gradients and points are explicit in a fixed real Euclidean plane.
It is simultaneous compatibility of longitudinal return payments over
all prefixes with the terminal jet and every remote directed row.
A payment paid on each adjacent step may spend more total displacement
than the central query can support.

These failures exclude only the displayed coefficient laws.
They do not exclude all nonclosing terminal memory, other signed
suffix laws, other curves, truly multi-mode geometries, or general
smooth-convex functions. No arbitrary-word optimality claim is made.

A next viable mechanism must specify the entire return schedule and
pay, at least, every first/last local cycle and each central-query
remote cycle with its FULL remaining displacement. It must also pay
all ORIGINAL directed/optimum rows and retain the true closest radius.
Keeping a terminal memory is not by itself sufficient.

The uniform original target still requires a static legal lower witness
for EVERY sufficiently large horizon and EVERY nonnegative word,
with payoff at least(1-o(1))*U_n^ZJ and a word-independent remainder.
Any universal comparison for a future family remains THEOREM-LEVEL.
A negative resolution still requires an all-function objective upper
certificate with fixed improvement on unbounded actual horizons.

# Coupled finite rows and depth retention: three complete analytical screens

JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT — UNVERIFIED. Worker max, invocation73 after assigned
completed baseline72; assigned attempted ceiling74. This is research evidence,
not a fact. There is no verifier submission, computational evaluation, actual
full-class upper bound, or resolution of the original exact-profile problem.

The three specified laws are: a pair of paid contact-neutral circulations;
a smooth depth ramp toward sustained inherited curvature; and immediate
mass-normalized retention after H4. Their complete arrays and entire-space
identities are below. The first law has two independent source restrictions
on the actual negative plane but pays one of them with the wrong sign. The
second starts positively on the entire plane, retains a uniformly positive
fraction of late inherited curvature, yet has already made the entire plane
negative by H9. The third starts positively on that plane at H5 but fails an
original initial-point mixed direction, including its Silver calibration.

## 1. Original target, fixed physical word, and authority

For every nonnegative physical word h of length n, W_n(h) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), over every finite-dimensional real
Euclidean space, every convex differentiable L-smooth f with a minimizer
x_star, every L>0 and x_0!=x_star, with the actual updates
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R. The original all-split benchmark is

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n)Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

Every split is an original integer split. The affirmative goal requires a
uniform all-word, all-large-horizon lower comparison. The negative route
requires an actual unrestricted W upper with fixed relative improvement on
unbounded actual horizons. No failed dual is a primal lower witness.

Fix ONE enclosing integer m>=1536 and set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    Hword_0=(), Hword_(j+1)=(Hword_j,1+a*c^j,Hword_j),
    A_j=1+sum Hword_j, d_j=a*c^j, D_j=2A_j-1.

The actual word is Hword_m=H_(m,1/4) of length n_m=2^m-1. Every child
inherits the SAME m and epsilon. Hword_j is used here to distinguish the
physical word from the conjugate quadratic H_j of fact1252b8823bb5a290.
The diagnostic epsilon=0 is the original Silver word; it is never substituted
for the assigned positive epsilon. All displayed recurrences are finite
mathematical definitions or symbolic identities, never executed programs.

Accepted inputs are fact1252b8823bb5a290 (original interpolation and formal
space), fact04219554e41d9750 Sections10--11 (primitive/history and full-space
composition conventions), and fact5fd396eba75651e7 Section10 (ONLY the
unconditional scalar benchmark comparison). Full findings9864512779c0d768,
23ca982e95eefa1f and70884c07cdfd260a and main elaboration0d9770af2df0344c were
read as awareness, not predecessors. All unverified formulas needed here are
derived together in this draft. None is promoted or reused as verified truth.

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Retain independent original formal
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, including every actual bridge and the unqueried
terminal, and every ordered finite and optimum row. Put

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    Ppos_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=sum h, D=1+2S, h_n=0.

Actual interpolation gives Q_ij<=0 by fact1252. Write K_ij for finite
multipliers, nu_i for i->star, xi_i for star->i, with K_ii=0. Every law
below has xi_i=0. All FINAL multipliers must be nonnegative. The exact value
flow and complete objective matrix are

    sum_j K_ij-sum_j K_ji+nu_i=2*1_(i=n),                    (1)
    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)K_ij Q_ij
                              +sum_i nu_i Q_(i,star)
        =q||x_0||^2-sum_i nu_i<x_0,g_i>+C(g),               (2)
    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i*sum_(j>i)K_ij,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j*sum_(v>j)K_iv
                         +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j,
    out_i=nu_i+sum_j K_ij.                                 (3)

Here C(g)=sum_(i,j)C_ij<g_i,g_j>. The full matrix is
[[q,-nu^T/2],[-nu/2,C]]. To derive (3), half the incident mass is
out_i-1_(i=n) by (1); forward position rows subtract h_i K_ij from the

The original Huber assignment x_0=D,g_i=1,f_i=D-Ppos_i-1/2 makes M(1/D)=0.
Its contact equations, including the mixed derivatives, are

    (2S-Ppos_i)nu_i=2h_i+sum_j K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j).          (4)

Indeed twice row i's sum in C is
2h_i+(1+Ppos_i)nu_i+sum_j K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j). All arrays below obey (4).

## 2. Complete source array and its actual two-dimensional negative plane

Let z be a child terminal and define the full primitive history

       +sum_(i<z)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-A_j(A_j-1)||g_z||^2.

     +v_j sum_(i right,i<z)h_i Q_(i,z)
     +w_j Q_(z,p)+z_j Q_(p,z),

    v_j=[u_j d_j+2(A_j+d_j)]/A_j,
    k_j=1+(u_j+v_j)/2,
    z_j=2A_j,
    w_j=4A_j+2d_j-u_j(A_j-1)
                           =2lambda+2(d_j-A_j/lambda).    (5)

    Ejoin_j=(t_star-t_j)[(lambda+1)||Y||^2
        -2lambda A_j<Y,Z>+A_j^2(2+t_star+t_j)||Z||^2].       (7)

    -(d_j+1/2)||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2/2-<g_p,r>-<g_p,g_z>.

The ||r||^2,r*g_p,r*g_z coefficients are (u_j-v_j)/2,

    A_j(A_j-1)-d_j-d_j^2+[u_j(A_j-1)+w_j]/2-(d_j+1/2)z_j,

                                     +v_j(A_j-1)/2+(w_j+z_j)/2.

## 3. Every contextual finite coefficient and the full original identity

At a join from Hword_j to Hword_(j+1), let k=2^j-1, use labels L_l=l,
0<=l<=k, bridge p=L_k, and R_i=k+1+i, 0<=i<=k, terminal R_k. Put

    A=A_j-1, d=1+d_j, V=3A+2d,

    s_j=(A+d)/V=(A_j+d_j)/(3A_j+2d_j-1), theta_j=1-s_j,
    x_p=x_0-sum_(l<k)h_l g_(L_l).

    K_(L_l,L_v)=(1-gamma_j)Lambda^j_lv/D+gamma_j K^c_lv
                         +2gamma_j s_j mu_l*1_(v=k,l<k),

    K_(R_i,L_k)=s_j mu_i, all other cross rows zero,
    nu_(L_l)=(1-gamma_j)2h_l/D+gamma_j(A/V)mu_l, l<k,
    nu_(L_k)=(1-gamma_j)(2s_j-2A/D)

    nu_(R_i)=theta_j mu_i, xi_i=0.                       (16)

perturbation. The source array for law A will be replaced explicitly in

All final signs hold. In particular
(A+d)D-A(3A+2d)=A^2+4Ad+2d^2+A+d>0 pays the bridge attachment
at gamma0; at gamma1 all attachments and finite rows are nonnegative.
For A>0, 1/3<s_j<1/2, while s_0=1/2. A convex combination retains signs.

JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT — UNVERIFIED. Worker max, invocation73 after assigned

not a fact. There is no verifier submission, computational evaluation, actual

The three specified laws are: a pair of paid contact-neutral circulations;

on the actual negative plane but pays one of them with the wrong sign. The
second starts positively on the entire plane, retains a uniformly positive

    C^c(u,v0)=aN*u^2+2bN*u*v0+cN*v0^2

D_3(su+theta v0)^2 leaves Rblock(u-v0)^2. In particular the right child
with common first group w and second group0 has C^c=aN*w^2.

Writing A=A_3-1,d=1+d_3, the entire H4 forms on N are

    I_N=-Edef(u-v0)^2/D_4+Rblock*w^2
       +[(Wloc-D_4 theta_3 s)w+(Tloc-D_4 s_3)v0]^2/D_4
       +kappa_3 zN^2,                                 (24)

    O_N=C^c(u,v0)+aN*w^2
       +2s_3 r_L(Wloc*w+d_3*v0)-(6s_3-2)Wloc*v0*w
       -theta_3 Wloc*w*r_R+s_3*d_3*v0*r_R
       +[1-(6s_3-2)d_3]v0^2,
    F_4=(1-gamma_3)I_N+gamma_3 O_N.                    (25)

Substitution into the FULL identities (17)--(18) proves (24)--(25).
There is no conclusion from two chosen plane vectors. Uniformly for
0<=gamma_3<=4epsilon, the complete quadratic bounds are

    F_4>(w^2+zN^2)/12>=normN/24,
    F_4<1000normN.                                    (26)

Here are the details. The numerator of 2A_2-D_3 s is

    kappa_3>27-(1717/25)(25/64)=11/64>1/6.

                              >w^2/4+zN^2/8.          (27)

The child terms in O_N are nonnegative by the explicit (23) and Rblock>0,

    O_N>=-18w^2-(63/2)|w*v0|-14v0^2
         >=-(135/4)w^2-(119/4)v0^2
         >-60(w^2+zN^2).                              (28)

The last line uses v0^2<=w^2/2+2zN^2. Combining (27)--(28) costs at most
241epsilon on either w^2 or zN^2 when gamma_3<=4epsilon. Because
241epsilon<=241/6144<1/24, (26)'s lower bound follows. Also
normN<=2(w^2+zN^2), proving its second comparison.
For the upper bound, aN<6, bN<9,cN<29 and u^2<=2w^2+9v0^2/2 imply

below65 and D_4>60, so its value is below141normN; kappa_3<D_3<29 and

## 5. Law A: two independent paid circulations, with an exact sign failure

Use gamma_j=0 in (16). Change the actual H4 SOURCE as follows, keeping
Lambda^j unchanged through H3. Define the original position differences

    ell_pair=Ppos_7-Ppos_5=b+(2-epsilon),
    r_pair=Ppos_5-Ppos_2=2b+(1+d_2),
    T_pair=ell_pair+r_pair=Ppos_7-Ppos_2.

The first circulation has sources3,6 and destinations2,5,7:

    DeltaL_3,2=-tau_pairL*ell_pair,
    DeltaL_3,5= tau_pairL*T_pair,
    DeltaL_3,7=-tau_pairL*r_pair,
    DeltaL_6,2= tau_pairL*ell_pair,
    DeltaL_6,5=-tau_pairL*T_pair,
    DeltaL_6,7= tau_pairL*r_pair,
    tau_pairL=(epsilon/2)*min{
          k_1*w_0/ell_pair, 2A_2/r_pair, k_2*u_1*b/T_pair}.  (29)

Every subtracted original entry is explicitly

    Lambda^4_3,2=k_1*w_0,
    Lambda^4_3,7=2A_2,
    Lambda^4_6,5=k_2*u_1*b.                              (30)

For the first, take the terminal->initial edge w_0 in the right H1 of
the left H2, with scaling k_1; its H3 and H4 embeddings are left embeddings
of weight1. The second is the H3 bridge->terminal entry z_2. For the third,
take the H2 right nonterminal->bridge row u_1*b in the right H2 of H3 and
scale by k_2. No other source rule adds to these entries. All are positive.
Thus each removal is at most epsilon/2 of its available entry.

The second circulation has sources10,12 and destinations7,11,15:

    DeltaR_10,7= tau_pairR*Wloc, DeltaR_10,11=-tau_pairR*Tloc,
    DeltaR_10,15=tau_pairR*Uloc, DeltaR_12,7=-tau_pairR*Wloc,
    DeltaR_12,11=tau_pairR*Tloc, DeltaR_12,15=-tau_pairR*Uloc,
    tau_pairR=(epsilon/2)*min{
         k_3(2k_1+v_1*b)/Tloc, u_3*b/Wloc,
                                  (k_3*v_2+v_3)*b/Uloc}.  (31)

The exact subtracted entries are
Lambda^4_10,11=k_3(2k_1+v_1*b), Lambda^4_12,7=u_3*b,
Lambda^4_12,15=(k_3*v_2+v_3)b. The first combines the nonterminal->terminal
edge2 of its right H1 with the H2 v_1*b row; the outer H4 gives k_3.
The second is the actual H4 backward source row. The third combines its
inherited H3 v_2*b terminal transport and its new H4 v_3*b terminal row.
Again all removals are at most epsilon/2 of the stated positive originals.

Set Lambda_pair^4=Lambda^4+DeltaL+DeltaR, and for j>=4 use (5) with the
inherited left Lambda_pair^j and right k_j Lambda_pair^j, with no additional
root correction. This places the two circulations once in EACH original
dyadic H4, with positive ancestral right weights. Their decremented rows
have disjoint source labels and are not charged twice. All final finite
coefficients are nonnegative. All other objective coefficients are EXACTLY
(16) at gamma0 with Lambda_pair instead of Lambda. This defines the whole
law, including all final optimum and terminal signs.

Both circulations have zero row sums and zero column sums. Their destination
vectors also have zero physical first moment:

    ell_pair Ppos_2-T_pair Ppos_5+r_pair Ppos_7=0,
    Wloc Ppos_7-Tloc Ppos_11+Uloc Ppos_15=0.

Therefore they preserve every original value-flow coefficient and contact
moment. With the original proximal points y_i=x_i-g_i of fact1252, their
ENTIRE original-space polynomial changes are

    DeltaP_L=tau_pairL<g_6-g_3,
                        ell_pair*y_2-T_pair*y_5+r_pair*y_7>,
    DeltaP_R=tau_pairR<g_10-g_12,
                        Wloc*y_7-Tloc*y_11+Uloc*y_15>.     (32)

To check (32), expand sum c_i d_j Q_ij. Both coefficient sums vanish,
canceling all values, source positions and pure squares; the remaining
term is <sum c_i g_i,sum d_j(x_j-g_j)>. Each factor vanishes on common
gradients, so the entire gradient derivative at contact also vanishes.
The full original matrix is (2)--(3) with these rows, and its lifted identity
is exactly (17) with the changed Psrc. No new off-diagonal is suppressed.

Writing Csrc for the gradient matrix of Psrc, the first circulation has
negative isolated SOURCE diagonal changes

    DeltaCsrc_3,3=-tau_pairL*ell_pair*(1+d_2),
    DeltaCsrc_6,6=-tau_pairL*r_pair*b.

Every other DeltaL diagonal is zero. The second has positive changes
DeltaCsrc_10,10=tau_pairR*Wloc*b and
DeltaCsrc_12,12=tau_pairR*Uloc*b, with other DeltaR diagonals zero.
These signs are explicitly retained, not treated as a diagonal PSD cure.
H2 is unchanged and passes the full gate from Section4. At epsilon=0 both
circulations vanish, giving the full Silver calibration (22).

Now evaluate the ENTIRE actual plane. On (10),

    y_2=-(ell_pair+1)u,
    y_5=-Wloc*u-(b+1)v0,
    y_7=-Wloc*u-A_2*v0,
    ell_pair*y_2-T_pair*y_5+r_pair*y_7
                                  =ell_pair(b+d_2)(u-v0).

The last equality follows since Wloc-ell_pair-1=b+d_2 and
b+1-A_2=-ell_pair. Also on N, y_15=0 and
y_11=-Wloc*u-Uloc*v0-A_2*w. Consequently

    Ppair_4|N=Psrc_4|N
       -tau_pairL*ell_pair(b+d_2)(u-v0)^2
       +tau_pairR[(A_2^2-d_2*d_3)w^2+Wloc*d_3*w*v0].    (33)

This is the full two-variable quadratic, including the new cross term.
The source restrictions phiL=v0-u and phiR=w are jointly injective on N:
if both vanish, (12) forces Tloc*v0=0 and hence u=v0=w=0. Independence
does not make (33) nonnegative. At the EXACT original vector

    v0=1, w=0, u=-Uloc/Wloc,                            (34)

both the baseline (11) and the first correction are strictly negative,
while the second correction is zero. More explicitly,

    Ppair_4(34)=-(Edef+tau_pairL ell_pair(b+d_2))rhoN^2
                        -delta3 A_3^2(2+t_star+t_3)<0.   (35)

This is the previously missed mode; the new independent left source is
nonzero there, but its paid orientation worsens it. Reversing DeltaL would
make its plane square positive, but would subtract from the EXACT ZERO
entries Lambda^4_3,5 and Lambda^4_6,2. Their zero status follows from (5):
the H3 bridge3 links outside its left child only to terminal7, and right
source6 links outside its right child only to bridge3 and terminal7.
Thus reversing this channel violates final signs for every positive size.

Place (34) in the first H4 of the left child of Hword_m, every other original
gradient zero and x_0=0. Upper source joins have zero Y,Z, and their other
H4 circulations have zero source gradients. The top objective has x_p=0,
g_p=0 and all right gradients zero, so EVERY term of the full lift except
Ppair_4/D_m vanishes. Therefore

    M_A(q)=Ppair_4(34)/D_m<0 for EVERY real q.             (36)

This is a paid two-source law with joint injectivity that nevertheless fails
the full original matrix. It does not exclude other multiple-source laws.

# Coupled finite rows and depth retention: three complete analytical screens

JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT — UNVERIFIED. Worker max, invocation73 after assigned
completed baseline72; assigned attempted ceiling74. This is research evidence,
not a fact. There is no verifier submission, computational evaluation, actual
full-class upper bound, or resolution of the original exact-profile problem.

The three specified laws are: a pair of paid contact-neutral circulations;
a smooth depth ramp toward sustained inherited curvature; and immediate
mass-normalized retention after H4. Their complete arrays and entire-space
identities are below. The first law has two independent source restrictions
on the actual negative plane but pays one of them with the wrong sign. The
second starts positively on the entire plane, retains a uniformly positive
fraction of late inherited curvature, yet has already made the entire plane
negative by H9. The third starts positively on that plane at H5 but fails an
original initial-point mixed direction, including its Silver calibration.

## 1. Original target, fixed physical word, and authority

For every nonnegative physical word h of length n, W_n(h) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), over every finite-dimensional real
Euclidean space, every convex differentiable L-smooth f with a minimizer
x_star, every L>0 and x_0!=x_star, with the actual updates
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R. The original all-split benchmark is

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n)Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

Every split is an original integer split. The affirmative goal requires a
uniform all-word, all-large-horizon lower comparison. The negative route
requires an actual unrestricted W upper with fixed relative improvement on
unbounded actual horizons. No failed dual is a primal lower witness.

Fix ONE enclosing integer m>=1536 and set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    Hword_0=(), Hword_(j+1)=(Hword_j,1+a*c^j,Hword_j),
    A_j=1+sum Hword_j, d_j=a*c^j, D_j=2A_j-1.

The actual word is Hword_m=H_(m,1/4) of length n_m=2^m-1. Every child
inherits the SAME m and epsilon. Hword_j is used here to distinguish the
physical word from the conjugate quadratic H_j of fact1252b8823bb5a290.
The diagnostic epsilon=0 is the original Silver word; it is never substituted
for the assigned positive epsilon. All displayed recurrences are finite
mathematical definitions or symbolic identities, never executed programs.

Accepted inputs are fact1252b8823bb5a290 (original interpolation and formal
space), fact04219554e41d9750 Sections10--11 (primitive/history and full-space
composition conventions), and fact5fd396eba75651e7 Section10 (ONLY the
unconditional scalar benchmark comparison). Full findings9864512779c0d768,
23ca982e95eefa1f and70884c07cdfd260a and main elaboration0d9770af2df0344c were
read as awareness, not predecessors. All unverified formulas needed here are
derived together in this draft. None is promoted or reused as verified truth.

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Retain independent original formal
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, including every actual bridge and the unqueried
terminal, and every ordered finite and optimum row. Put

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    Ppos_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=sum h, D=1+2S, h_n=0.

Actual interpolation gives Q_ij<=0 by fact1252. Write K_ij for finite
multipliers, nu_i for i->star, xi_i for star->i, with K_ii=0. Every law
below has xi_i=0. All FINAL multipliers must be nonnegative. The exact value
flow and complete objective matrix are

    sum_j K_ij-sum_j K_ji+nu_i=2*1_(i=n),                    (1)
    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)K_ij Q_ij
                              +sum_i nu_i Q_(i,star)
        =q||x_0||^2-sum_i nu_i<x_0,g_i>+C(g),               (2)
    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i*sum_(j>i)K_ij,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j*sum_(v>j)K_iv
                         +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j,
    out_i=nu_i+sum_j K_ij.                                 (3)

Here C(g)=sum_(i,j)C_ij<g_i,g_j>. The full matrix is
[[q,-nu^T/2],[-nu/2,C]]. To derive (3), half the incident mass is
out_i-1_(i=n) by (1); forward position rows subtract h_i K_ij from the
source diagonal. Difference squares and the two prefix position terms give
the three displayed off-diagonal contributions. Thus (1)--(3) retain ALL
initial-point and gradient directions. Full PSD would imply W<=q, with no
quotient or child-feasibility assumption.

The original Huber assignment x_0=D,g_i=1,f_i=D-Ppos_i-1/2 makes M(1/D)=0.
Its contact equations, including the mixed derivatives, are

    (2S-Ppos_i)nu_i=2h_i+sum_j K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j).          (4)

Indeed twice row i's sum in C is
2h_i+(1+Ppos_i)nu_i+sum_j K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j). All arrays below obey (4).
Raising q adds only (q-1/D)||x_0||^2; it cannot fix a test with x_0=0.

## 2. Complete source array and its actual two-dimensional negative plane

Let z be a child terminal and define the full primitive history

    V_j=2sum_(i<z)h_i(f_i-f_z)
       +sum_(i<z)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-A_j(A_j-1)||g_z||^2.

Starting from Lambda^0=0, at the actual join from Hword_j to Hword_(j+1)
embed Lambda^j on the left with weight1 and on the right with weight k_j.
With bridge p and terminal z, add exactly

    u_j sum_(i right,i<z)h_i Q_(i,p)
     +v_j sum_(i right,i<z)h_i Q_(i,z)
     +w_j Q_(z,p)+z_j Q_(p,z),
    u_j=2lambda,
    v_j=[u_j d_j+2(A_j+d_j)]/A_j,
    k_j=1+(u_j+v_j)/2,
    z_j=2A_j,
    w_j=4A_j+2d_j-u_j(A_j-1)
                           =2lambda+2(d_j-A_j/lambda).    (5)

Aggregate repeated actual rows. The identities u_j+v_j=2(k_j-1) and
u_j(A_j-1)+w_j-z_j=2(A_j+d_j) give divergence -2h_i at nonterminals and
2(A_(j+1)-1) at the terminal. Define the full gradient polynomial by

    V_j+sum_(i!=v)Lambda^j_iv Q_iv=Psrc_j(g).                (6)

At a join set t_j=d_j/A_j, t_star=1/lambda,
r=sum_(i right,i<z)h_i g_i, Y=r-(A_j-1)g_z, Z=g_p-g_z. Full expansion gives

    Psrc_(j+1)=Psrc_j^left+k_j Psrc_j^right+Ejoin_j,
    Ejoin_j=(t_star-t_j)[(lambda+1)||Y||^2
        -2lambda A_j<Y,Z>+A_j^2(2+t_star+t_j)||Z||^2].       (7)

For a complete audit, the four unweighted gradient polynomials of the new
rows in (5) are

    d_j<r,g_p>+||r||^2/2
       +sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2+(A_j-1)||g_p||^2/2;
    -||r||^2/2+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2
       +(A_j-1)||g_z||^2/2-<r,g_z>;
    d_j<g_z,g_p>+<g_z,r>+(||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2)/2;
    -(d_j+1/2)||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2/2-<g_p,r>-<g_p,g_z>.

The ||r||^2,r*g_p,r*g_z coefficients are (u_j-v_j)/2,
u_j d_j-z_j, w_j-v_j. The remaining bridge and terminal diagonals are

    A_j(A_j-1)-d_j-d_j^2+[u_j(A_j-1)+w_j]/2-(d_j+1/2)z_j,
    -A_(j+1)(A_(j+1)-1)+k_j A_j(A_j-1)
                                     +v_j(A_j-1)/2+(w_j+z_j)/2.

Substitution yields (7) on the whole original gradient space. Its bracket
is positive definite in (Y,Z): the first diagonal is positive and the
determinant divided by A_j^2 is
(lambda+1)(2+t_star+t_j)-lambda^2>=lambda>0.

Put v_h=a/(c-2). Direct summation of the mathematical word gives

    0<v_h<1,
    A_j=v_h c^j+(1-v_h)2^j,
    t_j=(c-2)/[1+(1/v_h-1)(2/c)^j].                      (8)

Here c(c-2)>1>beta, so t_j increases and A_j<c^j for j>0. At the first
levels,

    t_0<t_star, t_1<t_star, t_2>t_star,
    lambda d_1-A_1=epsilon[-lambda+2/(lambda(1+epsilon))]<0,
    c(lambda d_2-A_2)=epsilon[(lambda+4)
                       -(4lambda+2)epsilon-(5lambda+2)epsilon^2]>4epsilon.

Since c<5/2, lambda d_2-A_2>epsilon. Every sign in (5) holds: u,v,k,z
are positive, w_0=4+2a>0, A_1<lambda gives w_1>2lambda-2>0, and
t_j>t_star gives w_j>2lambda for j>=2. At epsilon=0, Psrc_j=0 identically

Define the LOCAL support lengths and deficit

    b=1+a, Wloc=A_2+d_2, Uloc=A_2+d_3,

    g_i=u for i=0,1,2,3;
    g_i=v0 for i=4,5,6,7;
    g_i=w for i=8,9,10,11;

(7) to the two H3 children and their H4 join gives

    Psrc_4=-Edef(u-v0)^2-k_3 Edef w^2
       -delta3[(lambda+1)Wloc^2 w^2-2lambda A_3 Wloc w v0
                           +A_3^2(2+t_star+t_3)v0^2].   (11)

    Wloc(u+w)+Uloc*v0.                                  (12)

Let N be the kernel of (12) in this three-dimensional test subspace. It has
dimension2 and terminal gradient0. On N write

    rhoN=Tloc/Wloc, u=-w-(Uloc/Wloc)v0,

of any Hword_r, r>=4, and setting all later gradients zero preserves

The following written bounds will also be used:

    29/5<A_2<6, 12/5<d_2<121/50, 29/5<d_3<6,
    14<A_3<721/50, 41/5<Wloc<9, 58/5<Uloc<12,

Indeed A_2=lambda^2-4epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]-epsilon,

d_3=lambda^2(1+epsilon-epsilon^2-epsilon^3). The rational enclosures

    lambda d_3-A_3

so delta3<21epsilon/(lambda A_3)<3epsilon/4. No arithmetic replay is used.
From (11)--(14), on the ENTIRE N,

    Psrc_4<-(epsilon/3)normN,
    |Psrc_4|<2000epsilon*normN.                         (15)

For the first bound, drop the final negative bracket and use k_3>1.
Since rhoN>1, v0^2<=2(w+rhoN v0)^2+2w^2, proving the factor1/3.

## 3. Every contextual finite coefficient and the full original identity

At a join from Hword_j to Hword_(j+1), let k=2^j-1, use labels L_l=l,
0<=l<=k, bridge p=L_k, and R_i=k+1+i, 0<=i<=k, terminal R_k. Put

    A=A_j-1, d=1+d_j, V=3A+2d,
    S=2A+d, D=D_(j+1), D_c=D_j,
    s_j=(A+d)/V=(A_j+d_j)/(3A_j+2d_j-1), theta_j=1-s_j,
    x_p=x_0-sum_(l<k)h_l g_(L_l).

The child has finite array K^c, attachments mu_i, sum mu_i=2 and xi=0.
Initialize Hword_0 with K^c=0,mu_0=2. For ANY specified gamma_j in[0,1]
set all parent coefficients to

    K_(L_l,L_v)=(1-gamma_j)Lambda^j_lv/D+gamma_j K^c_lv
                         +2gamma_j s_j mu_l*1_(v=k,l<k),
    K_(R_i,R_v)=K^c_iv,
    K_(R_i,L_k)=s_j mu_i, all other cross rows zero,
    nu_(L_l)=(1-gamma_j)2h_l/D+gamma_j(A/V)mu_l, l<k,
    nu_(L_k)=(1-gamma_j)(2s_j-2A/D)
                          +gamma_j(2d+A mu_k)/V,
    nu_(R_i)=theta_j mu_i, xi_i=0.                       (16)

This is a complete recursive array definition; there is no unassigned Schur
perturbation. The source array for law A will be replaced explicitly in
Section5. No child PSD is presumed in any screen.

All final signs hold. In particular
(A+d)D-A(3A+2d)=A^2+4Ad+2d^2+A+d>0 pays the bridge attachment
at gamma0; at gamma1 all attachments and finite rows are nonnegative.
For A>0, 1/3<s_j<1/2, while s_0=1/2. A convex combination retains signs.

At gamma0 the left source divergence -2h_l/D is canceled by its optimum
attachments and the total incoming backward mass2s_j; at the bridge use
source divergence2A/D. At gamma1 child divergence is2*1_(l=k)-mu_l.
The extra forward mass2s_j mu_l and attachment(1-2s_j)mu_l cancel every
nonterminal coefficient, and the bridge balances the incoming mass2s_j.
Right flow is child flow plus(s_j+theta_j)mu_i. Thus (1) holds and total
left attachment is2s_j. These calculations prove full value flow for (16).

For left nonterminal contact, subtraction of child (4) at gamma1 gives
V*forward_l=2(A+d)mu_l, hence forward_l=2s_j mu_l. At gamma0 source
annihilation of common gradients and the primitive completion below give
contact. Right contact uses theta_j V=2A+d. The remaining bridge derivative
follows from the other gradient derivatives, the initial derivative and
M(D,ones)=0 by homogeneity. Thus full contact (4) holds at every depth.

Define r_L=sum_l mu_l g_(L_l), r_R=sum_i mu_i g_(R_i), and

    Rchild_R=C^c(g_R)-D_c||r_R||^2/4,
    kappa_j=D_c-D theta_j^2.

These are definitions; no positivity of Rchild_R or kappa_j is assumed.
The full gamma0 and gamma1 quadratics at q=1/D are

    M_I=Psrc_j(g_L)/D+Rchild_R
       +||x_p+(A-D s_j)g_p-(D theta_j/2)r_R||^2/D
       +(kappa_j/4)||r_R-2g_p||^2,                    (17)

    M_O=||x_0||^2/D+C^c(g_L)+C^c(g_R)-<x_0,r_L>
       +2s_j<r_L,x_p-g_p>-(6s_j-2)<g_p,x_p>
       -theta_j<x_p,r_R>+(d-s_j)<g_p,r_R>
       +(6s_j-1)||g_p||^2.                            (18)

For (17), the primitive source plus left optimum rows gives Psrc_j/D and
||x_p-(A+1)g_p||^2/D. Replacing right optimum rows by
theta_j Q_(R_i,star)+s_j Q_(R_i,p) changes them by
s_j[-f_p+<g_(R_i),x_p-g_p>+||g_p||^2/2]. After cancellation the remaining
quadratic in x_p,g_p,r_R is

    ||x_p||^2/D+2(A/D-s_j)<x_p,g_p>+(A^2/D+2s_j)||g_p||^2
       -theta_j<x_p,r_R>+(d-s_j)<g_p,r_R>+D_c||r_R||^2/4.

Completion using s_j V=A+d is exactly (17). For (18) the left correction
is 2s_j sum_l mu_l(Q_(L_l,p)-Q_(L_l,star))+(6s_j-2)Q_(p,star), including
l=k with Q_(p,p)=0. The difference is
-f_p+<g_(L_l),x_p-g_p>+||g_p||^2/2. It cancels the right replacement's
value -2s_j f_p, and its gradient terms together with that replacement
give (18). This audits all finite, optimum, terminal and x_0 mixed terms.
Consequently the ENTIRE original identity for (16) is

    M_gamma(q)=(1-gamma_j)M_I+gamma_j M_O
                                      +(q-1/D)||x_0||^2. (19)

## 4. Common H2 gates, Silver calibration, and the ENTIRE initial N form

On Hword_1, K_(1,0)=1 and nu_0=nu_1=1 for every gamma_0, and

    M_1(1/D_1)=||x_0-D_1(g_0+g_1)/2||^2/D_1
                          +(3-2b)||g_0-g_1||^2/4,
    Psrc_1=(2-b^2)||g_0-g_1||^2.                        (20)

Both are nonnegative since b<sqrt(2)<3/2. For H2, put d=2-epsilon,
D=1+4b+2d, alpha=b/(3b+2d). The ORIGINAL index0 mixed Schur value for
gamma_1=epsilon/4 is exactly

    C_00-D nu_0^2/4=(2-b^2)/D
       +gamma_1[1-b+2(b^2-1)/D]
       -(D/4)gamma_1^2(alpha-2b/D)^2>epsilon/30.        (21)

Indeed 2-b^2>2epsilon,D<11, the bracket>-1/2, the last term<epsilon/1000,
giving epsilon(2/11-1/8-1/1000)>epsilon/30. This includes the original
x_0 mixed coefficient. The bridge's gamma0 Schur value is
kappa_1+(2-b^2)/D. Bounds b<10/7,d>199/100 give theta_1<59/100,
D<75/7,D_c>19/5, hence kappa_1>19/5-15/4=1/20. Changing to epsilon/4
uses bridge endpoint coefficients
C_I=2s_1+2/D,C_O=4s_1,
nu_I=2s_1-2b/D,nu_O=(2d+b)/(3b+2d).
Their C difference is2s_1-2/D with absolute value below1, and their nu
difference is2b/D-alpha with absolute value below1; both old attachments
are below1. Thus the change alters C and nu by less than gamma_1 and the Schur value by less than
7gamma_1<1/1000. Right indices2,3 have C_ii=1,nu_i=theta_1 and positive
Schur value [4-D_c+kappa_1]/4. Thus laws B and C pass all four specified
H2 isolated-gradient mixed tests. These diagonal tests do not assert full
actual H2 PSD. Law A has gamma0 and no source change through H2: (17),
Psrc_1>=0,kappa_1>0 and the full H1 Schur remainder prove its full H2 PSD.

For the gamma0 Silver calibration, write u_star=1/lambda. The physical
bridge is d=1+u_star(A+1), with u_star^2+2u_star=1, and direct expansion gives

    V^2 kappa_j=2(1-u_star)A^3+(6-8u_star)A^2
       +(1+u_star)(8u_star-2)A+(1+u_star)^2(1-2u_star)>0. (22)

Every coefficient is positive because1/4<u_star<1/2. At epsilon=0,
Psrc_j=0. From the empty full certificate ||x_0-g_0||^2 and (17), the
entire child Schur remainder and the retained squares prove full Silver
PSD at every gamma0 depth. Laws A and B specialize exactly to this law;
law C's later different gamma is screened separately, not certified by (22).

We now derive an ENTIRE plane form for ANY contextual law (16). Let
s=s_2, theta=1-s, define

    aN=2s A_2,
    bN=s(2Wloc-1), cN=D_3 theta-bN,
    r_L=2s u+2theta v0, r_R=2s w,
    Ldisp=Wloc*u+(A_2-1)v0,
    x_p=-Ldisp=Wloc*w+(1+d_3)v0 on N,
    zN=s*w-v0, Rblock=aN-D_3 s^2.

The H3 child quadratic compressed to its two common groups is

    C^c(u,v0)=aN*u^2+2bN*u*v0+cN*v0^2
            =D_3(s*u+theta*v0)^2+Rblock(u-v0)^2.        (23)

To prove (23) WITHOUT child PSD, all left-group gradients equal1 and all
right gradients0 give C_left,left=2s A_2 directly from either (17) or (18).
Group attachment masses are2s,2theta by (16); contact row sums then force
C_left,right=s(D_3-2A_2)=bN and C_right,right=D_3 theta-bN. Subtracting
D_3(su+theta v0)^2 leaves Rblock(u-v0)^2. In particular the right child
with common first group w and second group0 has C^c=aN*w^2.

Writing A=A_3-1,d=1+d_3, the entire H4 forms on N are

    I_N=-Edef(u-v0)^2/D_4+Rblock*w^2
       +[(Wloc-D_4 theta_3 s)w+(Tloc-D_4 s_3)v0]^2/D_4
       +kappa_3 zN^2,                                 (24)

    O_N=C^c(u,v0)+aN*w^2
       +2s_3 r_L(Wloc*w+d_3*v0)-(6s_3-2)Wloc*v0*w
       -theta_3 Wloc*w*r_R+s_3*d_3*v0*r_R
       +[1-(6s_3-2)d_3]v0^2,
    F_4=(1-gamma_3)I_N+gamma_3 O_N.                    (25)

Substitution into the FULL identities (17)--(18) proves (24)--(25).
There is no conclusion from two chosen plane vectors. Uniformly for
0<=gamma_3<=4epsilon, the complete quadratic bounds are

    F_4>(w^2+zN^2)/12>=normN/24,
    F_4<1000normN.                                    (26)

Here are the details. The numerator of 2A_2-D_3 s is
2A_2^2-2A_2 d_2-2d_2^2-A_2+d_2. From (14) it exceeds
2(29/5)^2-12(121/50)-2(121/50)^2-6+12/5>22; its denominator
3A_2+2d_2-1 is below22. Since s>1/3, Rblock>1/3. Also 2d_3+3>A_3 gives
s_3>3/8,theta_3<5/8. Therefore

    kappa_3>27-(1717/25)(25/64)=11/64>1/6.

Use u-v0=-w-rhoN*v0, v0=s*w-zN, rhoN<3 and s<1/2. Then
(u-v0)^2<25w^2/2+18zN^2. Dropping the positive square in (24) gives

    I_N>(1/3-5epsilon)w^2+(1/6-36epsilon/5)zN^2
                              >w^2/4+zN^2/8.          (27)

The child terms in O_N are nonnegative by the explicit (23) and Rblock>0,
not by full child PSD. Since |r_L|<=|w|+3|v0|/2, Wloc<9, d<7 and
1/3<s_3<1/2, its remaining terms give

    O_N>=-18w^2-(63/2)|w*v0|-14v0^2
         >=-(135/4)w^2-(119/4)v0^2
         >-60(w^2+zN^2).                              (28)

The last line uses v0^2<=w^2/2+2zN^2. Combining (27)--(28) costs at most
241epsilon on either w^2 or zN^2 when gamma_3<=4epsilon. Because
241epsilon<=241/6144<1/24, (26)'s lower bound follows. Also
normN<=2(w^2+zN^2), proving its second comparison.
For the upper bound, aN<6, bN<9,cN<29 and u^2<=2w^2+9v0^2/2 imply
C^c(u,v0)<106normN. In (24), the square has absolute linear coefficients
below65 and D_4>60, so its value is below141normN; kappa_3<D_3<29 and
zN^2<=2normN give I_N<250normN. The absolute remaining terms of (25)
are bounded respectively by19,5,9,2,5 times normN, and aN*w^2<6normN.
Thus |O_N|<200normN and the loose upper1000normN holds. This completes
the whole-plane gate with every mixed coefficient accounted for.

## 6. Law B: a smooth depth ramp with sustained late curvature, defeated on ALL N

Keep the original source (5) and specify EVERY contextual gamma in (16) by

    gamma_0=gamma_1=epsilon/4,
    gamma_j=(D_j/D_(j+1))*[1-(1-epsilon)^(2^j)], j>=2.    (37)

All gamma are in[0,1], so all final signs, flow and contact are already paid
by Section3. There are no new signed rows or undefined coefficient choices.
At epsilon=0 EVERY gamma is zero. Thus this law passes the original H2
mixed tests (21) and the full all-depth Silver calibration (22).
At H4, gamma_3<(1/2)*8epsilon=4epsilon; (24)--(28) therefore prove that
the ENTIRE actual N has positive F_4, not just two tested basis vectors.

For r>=4 define F_r to be this whole law's M_r on the first original H4
test N, later gradients zero and x_0=0. Define Tplane_r=D_r F_r. With
P_N=Psrc_4|N, the FULL original identities (17)--(19) give

    F_(r+1)=gamma_r F_r+(1-gamma_r)P_N/D_(r+1),
    Tplane_(r+1)=hold_r Tplane_r+(1-gamma_r)P_N,
    hold_r=1-(1-epsilon)^(2^r), r>=4.                   (38)

The source survives unchanged because displacement and terminal are zero;
the primitive endpoint's square and right child terms vanish. The objective
endpoint leaves exactly the left child quadratic F_r. This derives (38)
without child PSD or an executed recurrence. It is an identity of quadratic
forms on the entire plane. Any q has the same restriction since x_0=0.

Bernoulli's inequality gives hold_r<=2^r epsilon. The full initial bound
(26) and D_4<80 give Tplane_4<80000normN. Expanding the FIVE symbolic
identities for r=4,...,8, every inserted source term is negative by (15).
Keeping only the last one yields

    Tplane_9<80000epsilon^5 2^30 normN+(1-gamma_8)P_N
             <80000epsilon^5 2^30 normN-epsilon normN/6. (39)

Here gamma_8<D_8/D_9<1/2. Since epsilon<=1/(3*2^11),

    80000epsilon^4 2^30<=80000/(81*2^14)<1/6;

the last strict comparison is the written integer inequality
480000<81*16384. It was not evaluated by a program. Thus (39) is strictly
negative for EVERY nonzero point of N. Every later (38) has hold_r>0 and
(1-gamma_r)P_N<0, so the ENTIRE N remains strictly negative, in particular

    M_B(q)|N=F_m<0 for EVERY real q, m>=1536.             (40)

The positive H4 plane has been lost already at the finite H9 gate. There
is no proposed deep PSD induction after that failure; (40) is simply the
original-space embedding and sign-preserving identity.

This failure is not a restatement of constant epsilon/4 attenuation. The
law has a quantitatively sustained late inheritance at the natural
objective-mass normalization. Let Jret be the least integer with2^Jret>=16m.
Then Jret<=m-1 for m>=1536; the elementary inequality2^(m-1)>=16m holds
already at m=16 and is preserved when m increases. For r=Jret+t,

    1-hold_r=(1-epsilon)^(2^r)
        <=1/(1+epsilon 2^r)<1/(4*2^t).

For the first inequality, apply Bernoulli to
(1-epsilon)^(-2^r)=[1+epsilon/(1-epsilon)]^(2^r). Therefore, for EVERY
suffix endpoint k with Jret<=k<=m-1,

    product_(r=Jret)^k hold_r
       >=1-sum_(r=Jret)^k(1-hold_r)>1/2.                (41)

The finite product inequality follows inductively from(1-x)(1-y)>=1-x-y
for x,y in[0,1]. Equation (41) retains more than half of the normalized
inherited late curvature over the ENTIRE suffix, with no child reset.
It cannot revive a plane already negative at H9. No whole-word margin,
full PSD, or unrestricted W upper is obtained.

# Coupled finite rows and depth retention: three complete analytical screens

JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT — UNVERIFIED. Worker max, invocation73 after assigned
completed baseline72; assigned attempted ceiling74. This is research evidence,
not a fact. There is no verifier submission, computational evaluation, actual

The three specified laws are: a pair of paid contact-neutral circulations;
a smooth depth ramp toward sustained inherited curvature; and immediate
mass-normalized retention after H4. Their complete arrays and entire-space
identities are below. The first law has two independent source restrictions

All notation in this report is local. Its reusable dictionary is:

## 6. Complete new minimum sets, attainment and sharp normalization

All positive offsets in the anchor table are strictly positive, since
M>=2, a>0, Q>0 and R>0. At v=0 exactly the zero-offset anchors
are active. The subdifferential of a finite maximum of affine functions
is the convex hull of its active slopes: every such convex combination
is a supporting slope; a slope outside that hull is separated from it
by a direction and cannot satisfy the supporting inequality along that
direction. Therefore

    partial H_three(0)=conv{0,y,z},
    partial H_return(0)=conv{0,y,z,w}.

Each H(0)=0, so its conjugate F>=0. Optimality for the strictly
convex conjugate maximization says F(x)=0 precisely when its maximizer
is v=0, equivalently x in partial H(0). These are the COMPLETE
minimum sets, and the minimum value is attained and is zero.

The first coordinates of y,z,w are respectively 2-A, 1-A+2B,
2-A, all strictly negative. Thus each completed minimum hull lies
in x_1<=0 and contains origin. For any minimum x,
||e_1-x||^2=1-2x_1+||x||^2>=1, with equality only at x=0.
The unique closest minimum is origin and the TRUE radius is exactly
one. Completion shrinks the old minimum cone to these bounded hulls;
radius preservation has been proved from the new hulls, not assumed.

For 0<t<1/M sufficiently small, at v=t e_1 every nonzero
zero-offset anchor has strictly negative affine value, and each
positive-offset anchor has strictly negative affine value too. The
initial one requires t_P,1 t<delta_P, which is exactly t<1/M.
There is an open ball around such v on which the zero affine term
alone wins, so H(v)=||v||^2/2 there. Optimality gives F(x)=||x||^2/2
on that same open ball, with Hessian I. Since global smoothness one
was already supplied by fact1252, it is SHARP. There is no hidden
L or distance renormalization. The exact terminal values in Sections
4 and 5 are thus actual attained W=2R-normalized payoffs in R^3.

### 4.1 Complete finite source

For a depth-j child terminal z define the primitive history

    V_j=2sum_(i<z)h_i(f_i-f_z)
         +sum_(i<z)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
         -A_j(A_j-1)||g_z||^2.

Start Lambda^0=0. At Hword_(j+1)=(Hword_j,1+d_j,Hword_j), with bridge

     +v_j sum_(i right,i<z)h_i Q_(i,z)
     +w_j Q_(z,p)+z_j Q_(p,z),
    u_j=2lambda,
    v_j=[u_j d_j+2(A_j+d_j)]/A_j,
    k_j=1+(u_j+v_j)/2,
    z_j=2A_j,
    w_j=4A_j+2d_j-u_j(A_j-1).                         (12)

All unlisted entries are zero; repeated original rows are summed.
The identities u_j+v_j=2(k_j-1) and
u_j(A_j-1)+w_j-z_j=2(A_j+d_j) give nonterminal divergence -2h_i and
terminal divergence2(A_(j+1)-1). Put

       +(t_star-t_j)[(lambda+1)||Y||^2
              -2lambda A_j<Y,Z>+A_j^2(2+t_star+t_j)||Z||^2]. (13)

For an independent coefficient audit, the four new unweighted gradient
polynomials, in (12)'s order, are

gradient, every minimizer x_star, and x_0!=x_star, using the actual updates
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Write R_n(h)=W_n(h)/2. The witnesses
below use smoothness1 and the true closest initial distance to the complete
minimum set. Multiplication of their objective by any L>0 gives the same
points with steps h_i/L and the same normalized payoff.

## Definitions of the two completed functions

Fix real parameters M=M_mc>=2, B=B_mc>=2, A=A_mc>=4B+4, and
epsilon in [0,1]. These are local construction parameters, distinct from
the benchmark sequences C_n and B_n below. Put a=a_mc=1-1/M,
C=C_mc=2B+1, and let e_1,e_2,e_3 be the standard basis of R^3. Define

    nu=sqrt(2A-4),
    p=p_mc=e_1/M,
    q=q_mc=(-2e_1+nu e_2)/M,
    Q=Qnorm_mc=||q||^2=2A/M^2,
    r=r_mc=-q/2+sqrt((B/2-1/4)Q)e_3,
    R=Rnorm_mc=||r||^2=BQ/2,       <q,r>=-Q/2,
    D_mc=conv{0,p,q,r},
    F_old(x)=max_(g in D_mc){<x,g>-||g||^2/2},
    y=y_mc=-Ae_1-Mq,
    z=z_mc=y-BMq-Mr,
    w=w_mc=z-CMr-Mq,
    t_P=a e_1,              delta_P=a/M,
    t_Q=y+(M-1)q,           delta_Q=(M-1)Q,
    t_R=z+(M-1)r,           delta_R=(M-1)R,
    t_D=w+(M-1)q,           delta_D=(M-1)Q.

Here conv denotes convex hull. For each ordinary list L_i, choose any
finite nonnegative list of total mass M-1 and retain every entry, including
zeros. With concatenation in the displayed physical order, define

    h_three=(L_0,AM+1,L_1,BM+1,L_2,1+M epsilon),

## 1. Static old function and every reached query

Let D=conv{0,p,q,r} and

    F_old(x)=max_(g in D){<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.

The maximum is attained uniquely because D is compact and the objective
is strictly concave; the maximizer is P_D(x). The projection normal
condition says, for u=x-g,

    <u,b-g><=0 for every b in D.

It also says g maximizes the support J(u)=max(0,<p,u>,<q,u>,<r,u>).
Thus x=u+g, delta=J(u)=<g,u>, and
F_old(x)=delta+||g||^2/2. Conversely, any displayed pair with g in D
and this support condition is the UNIQUE projection pair. Tied support
planes do not make the envelope gradient ambiguous.

For any two old pairs, direct cancellation in the signed original
residual of fact_id 1252b8823bb5a290 gives

    Q_xy=F_old(x)-F_old(y)+<g_x,y-x>+||g_x-g_y||^2/2
        =<u_y,g_x-g_y><=0.

This works for every ordered pair, remote pairs, duplicate positions,
and the zero optimum. To check global regularity directly, the two
projection normal inequalities with each other's projected vectors give

    <x-x',P_D(x)-P_D(x')>>=||P_D(x)-P_D(x')||^2.

Cauchy--Schwarz makes the projection 1-Lipschitz. Evaluation of the
attained maximum at its two maximizing vectors bounds
F_old(x+d)-F_old(x)-<P_D(x),d> between0 and
<P_D(x+d)-P_D(x),d>, hence between0 and ||d||^2. Thus F_old is
differentiable with gradient P_D, which is 1-Lipschitz, and convex as
a supremum of affine functions. The slopes are independent: p has
nonzero first coordinate, q has nonzero second coordinate, and r has
nonzero third coordinate. Therefore D has interior, where P_D(x)=x
and F_old has Hessian I. Its least global smoothness is exactly one.

Because 0 is a vertex of D, F_old>=0 and its complete minimum set is

    {x:<p,x><=0, <q,x><=0, <r,x><=0}.

Indeed this condition makes every objective term nonpositive. If any
of the three inner products is positive, a sufficiently small positive
multiple of that vertex belongs to D and makes the objective positive.
The p inequality puts all minima in x_1<=0; origin is the unique
closest one to e_1 and the true distance is one.

## 5. Complete new minimum sets, attainment and sharp normalization

All positive offsets in the anchor table are strictly positive, since
M>=2, a>0, Q>0 and R>0. At v=0 exactly the zero-offset anchors
are active. The subdifferential of a finite maximum of affine functions
is the convex hull of its active slopes: every such convex combination
is a supporting slope; a slope outside that hull is separated from it
by a direction and cannot satisfy the supporting inequality along that
direction. Therefore

    partial H_three(0)=conv{0,y,z},
    partial H_return(0)=conv{0,y,z,w}.

Each H(0)=0, so its conjugate F>=0. Optimality for the strictly
convex conjugate maximization says F(x)=0 precisely when its maximizer
is v=0, equivalently x in partial H(0). These are the COMPLETE
minimum sets, and the minimum value is attained and is zero.

The first coordinates of y,z,w are respectively 2-A, 1-A+2B,
2-A, all strictly negative. Thus each completed minimum hull lies
in x_1<=0 and contains origin. For any minimum x,
||e_1-x||^2=1-2x_1+||x||^2>=1, with equality only at x=0.
The unique closest minimum is origin and the TRUE radius is exactly
one. Completion shrinks the old minimum cone to these bounded hulls;
radius preservation has been proved from the new hulls, not assumed.

For 0<t<1/M sufficiently small, at v=t e_1 every nonzero
zero-offset anchor has strictly negative affine value, and each
positive-offset anchor has strictly negative affine value too. The
initial one requires t_P,1 t<delta_P, which is exactly t<1/M.
There is an open ball around such v on which the zero affine term
alone wins, so H(v)=||v||^2/2 there. Optimality gives F(x)=||x||^2/2
on that same open ball, with Hessian I. Since global smoothness one
was already supplied by fact_id 1252b8823bb5a290, it is SHARP. There is no hidden
L or distance renormalization. The exact terminal values in Sections
3 and 4 are thus actual attained payoffs in the W_n=2R_n normalization
in R^3.

Every convex quadratic in any finite dimension diagonalizes, and its
normalized error is a convex combination of t product_j(1-h_j t)^2
for 0<=t<=1. Zero eigenvalues contribute no objective gap; choosing a
farther minimizer only increases the denominator. Consequently the
entire quadratic channel is bounded by
Q_n(h)=max_(0<=t<=1)t product_j(1-h_j t)^2.
Conversely, for each t in (0,1], the scalar quadratic f(x)=t x^2/2
from x_0=1 attains that expression; a constant function gives zero
at t=0. Continuity on [0,1] gives the maximum, so this expression is
exactly the full convex-quadratic channel asserted in the statement.

[0,1], |P_N(t)|^2<=min(1,1/(T_Cheb t)). The second bound uses
|Cheb_(2N+1)(sqrt(t))|<=1. For the first, set sqrt(t)=sin(phi):
the odd Chebyshev identity reduces to
sin((2N+1)phi)/((2N+1)sin(phi)). The finite unit-complex-number
identity sin(k phi)/sin(phi)=sum_(j=0)^(k-1)
exp(i(k-1-2j)phi) for positive integer k gives
|sin(k phi)|<=k|sin(phi)|; the zero-sine case follows by continuity.
At t=0 the polynomial value is one, which is the meaning of its
displayed min bound at zero.

## 8. Original all-split benchmark and actual padded horizons

Here C_n,B_n are benchmark sequences, distinct from construction scalars
C,B. Use EXACTLY the accepted all-split recurrences

    C_0=B_0=1,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n) Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n) G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)),
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

Accepted fact_id b98bb807d514e80d gives B_n<=1+4n^rho_crude, rho_crude=log_2(3). This UPPER
bound is the direction needed to prove reference channels small
relative to U. Since rho_crude<8/5 by 3^5<2^8, M>=2N^2 and actual
n<=16N show

    B_n max(K_n,Q_n,sup_(Lens_n) Gap_h)->0.

The slowest reference decay is M^(-4/5)=O(N^(-8/5)), whereas
B_n=O(N^rho_crude). Fixed cosh(2) constants do not affect the limit.
Thus all three named channels are o(U_n^ZJ) on each selected family
at its actual horizon.

To prove V>U a LOWER bound on B_n is necessary. The all-split
recurrences directly give C_n>=Omega(C_(n-1),1)>C_(n-1), and
balanced splits give C_(2^j-1)>=lambda^j for lambda=1+sqrt(2).
Selecting the split j=n-1 in B_n gives
B_n>=G(C_(n-1),1)>=2C_(n-1)-1. For d_N=floor(log_2 N),

B_n>=lambda^(d_N+3). Meanwhile M<=5N^2<20*4^(d_N). Hence
the common attained payoff satisfies

                       (lambda/2^(7/6))^(d_N) >1.

base is >16/15>1. The payoff exceeds U at EVERY claimed
N>=2^60 and the ratio diverges. No fitted profile constant, assumed
benchmark asymptotic, balanced-only defining recurrence, or DP was used.
