## 9. Precisely defined collapsed policy and its zero-tail boundary

This comparison retains the construction's p=e_1/M, initial point e_1,
first ordinary list and selected bridge AM+1. It treats ALL remaining
steps before the final bridge as one ordinary block, whose total is
M_2-1. Directly counting the original masses gives

    M_2=(B+2)M          for h_three,
    M_2=(B+C+3)M=(3B+4)M  for h_return.

Its specified static second slope is

    q_2=(-2e_1+sqrt(2A-4)e_2)/M_2,
    ||q_2||^2=2A/M_2^2.

For the static envelope over conv{0,p,q_2}, a first-stage proximal
point u=(1-t/M)e_1, 1<=t<=M, has p support (1-t/M)/M>=0,
q_2 support -2(1-t/M)/M_2<=0, and zero support0. Thus p is active
and x=u+p has projection p onto that triangle. The projection
regularity argument of Section 1 applies to this compact convex triangle
as well, proving that F_col_old is a legal member of the collapsed class.
After the first bridge, X=-Ae_1. At ordinary partial
mass s with t=1+s in [1,M_2],

    <q_2,X-tq_2>=(M_2-t)||q_2||^2>=0,
    <p,X-tq_2>=(-A+2t/M_2)/M<0.

Thus every physical query of THIS collapsed policy is legal, including
the old BM+1 and CM+1 steps now acting as individual ordinary entries.
Let y_2=X-M_2 q_2. The last queried jet is x=y_2+q_2,
g=q_2, f=||q_2||^2/2. For EVERY legal smooth-convex completion
of THIS entire prefix with its retained zero optimum, the descent
inequality at that jet gives

    f(y_2)<=f(y_2+q_2)-||q_2||^2/2=0.

Since the retained optimum has value zero, y_2 is forced to be a
minimum. The final physical step 1+M epsilon reaches
y_2-M epsilon q_2, and smoothness about this forced minimum gives

    2f(x_n)<=2A(M epsilon/M_2)^2.

The true radius for every such completion is also one, rather than
an assumed inherited denominator. The retained initial jet is
g_0=p and f_0=1/M-1/(2M^2). For any new minimizer x_star of value
zero, the original interpolation necessity from fact_id 1252b8823bb5a290 gives

    Q_(0,star)=f_0+<p,x_star-e_1>+||p||^2/2
             =x_star,1/M<=0.

So all new minima have first coordinate <=0, and the retained origin
is the unique closest one to e_1. This proves the bound for every
completion of that precise prefix with TRUE radius one.

When epsilon>0, the collapsed upper is positive and division is
legitimate. The three-stage witness-to-upper ratio is at least

    [B(B+2)^2/2](1-1/(2B^3)),

and the return witness-to-upper ratio is at least

    (3/4)(3B+4)^2.

Both factors exceed one and diverge on the chosen growing words,
where epsilon=M^(-1/3)>0. In the return parameter range epsilon>0
is automatic. Thus the substantive advertised growing-family comparison
holds, with exactly the stated collapsed policy as the comparison class.

multiplicative inequality has equality at this boundary; its ratio is not

## 10. Original normalization and scope

For either attained function F, its minimum is0, the unique closest
minimizer to e_1 is0, the squared radius is1, and its least global gradient
Lipschitz constant is1. Thus V=2F(x_n) is exactly the project's W_n=2R_n
normalized payoff. Replacing F by L F for any L>0 makes the prescribed
updates x_next=x-(h_i/L)grad(L F)(x)=x-h_i grad F(x), with the same points
and the same payoff. Therefore W_n(h)>=V for the complete function class
in every stated case.

For each of the two specific padded word families, Sections 6--8 prove
V>U_n^ZJ at every integer horizon above its stated threshold, V/U_n^ZJ
tends to infinity, and the three exactly named reference channels are
o(U_n^ZJ), including the canonical Huber augmentation of the universal
lens. All padding counts and benchmark subscripts use actual physical
indices. These are selected-word lower witnesses and comparisons with
specified reference classes only. There is no bound on unrestricted W_n
from above, no extension to all nonlinear scalar witnesses or the full
complex legal region, and no arbitrary-word partition theorem. The original
arbitrary-word exact-profile theorem remains OPEN.

The screened words require an ORIGINAL full objective certificate, not a
matrix involving only three block endpoints. For one chosen X and every

between formal gradients. Every displacement and initial mixed term must

## 5. THREE complete conditional destination/scale-dependent laws

A dyadic node inside Hword_r of depth d and offset o means the actual
embedded child word Hword_d with query indices o..o+n_d. These nodes
are specified equivalently by offsets o=k*2^d,0<=k<2^(r-d).
For each PROPER node of depth d=s+2>=4, define three original queries

    i1(vnode)=o+2^s-1,
    i2(vnode)=o+2^(s+1)-1,
    i3(vnode)=o+3*2^s-1,
    end(vnode)=o+2^(s+2)-1,
    wt(vnode)=A_s.                                   (20)

The node label vnode is distinct from an original receiver index v.
The physical steps at these three queries are1+d_s,1+d_(s+1),1+d_s.
For each finite base terminal receiver v=p_l, make exactly these THREE
choices of eligible sets and total fractions:

    Law A: Elig_v contains ALL proper dyadic vnode of depth s+2>=4
           with end(vnode)<=v; rhoPath=256epsilon=64/m<=1/24.
    Law B: Elig_v contains exactly the EVEN-depth proper vnode,
           depth=s+2>=4 with s even and end(vnode)<=v;
           rhoPath=4096epsilon=1024/m<=2/3.
    Law C: SAME Elig_v, ZPath_v, conditional probabilities and fraction
           as Law B, but append ORIGINAL query0 to its prefix path.

For each specified law separately, set

    ZPath_v=sum_(vnode in Elig_v) A_s,
    cond_(vnode|v)=A_s/ZPath_v on Elig_v, zero elsewhere. (21)

node ends at15<=p_r<=p_l and is allowed in both choices. For r<=4
the eligible sets are empty and all three laws make no change. At r>=5 set

    omegaPath_(v,vnode)=rhoPath alpha_v^base A_s/ZPath_v. (22)

For every listed v and vnode, replace exactly2omegaPath of the old
terminal edge n_r->v by the FOUR edges

    n_r->i3(vnode)->i2(vnode)->i1(vnode)->v.           (23)

This is the path in Laws A and B. Law C replaces the same terminal
mass by the FIVE-edge path

    n_r->i3(vnode)->i2(vnode)->i1(vnode)->0->v.        (23c)

Its original indices are all distinct; i1>=3 and v>i3. In particular
no coordinate at the first physical query is omitted or identified.

Every index is an ORIGINAL query and
i1<i2<i3<end<=v<n_r. This changes both terminal and prefix rows;

Eligibility and normalization depend on v; node mass depends on s.
For example the last receiver's prefix admits right-child nodes that
the root receiver's prefix excludes. The law is not separable pi_i*alpha_v.

Here are every FINAL terminal probability and finite/optimum multiplier,

    alpha_star^path=astar_r,

## 6. Complete path polynomial, terminal square and contact defect

For original indices n,k,i,v, direct cancellation gives

    Q_(n,k)+Q_(k,i)-Q_(n,i)=<g_n-g_k,y_k-y_i>, y_i=x_i-g_i.

The values cancel. The position terms give <g_n-g_k,x_k-x_i>;
the gradient-difference terms give -<g_n-g_k,g_k-g_i>.
Applying this identity successively along(23), or expanding its four

    Mpath(q)=Mbase(q)+2sum_(v,vnode)omegaPath EPath_(v,vnode),

           +<g_i3-g_i2,y_i2-y_v>

Every original position in y uses the unchanged physical prefix. There

At a common gradient, y_i-y_v=Ppos_v-Ppos_i. Differentiating(25)

                            +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j. (4)

by(2). A forward position term contributes -h_i K_iv on its source

source i's later destinations give the second term, and source j's
earlier destinations and optimum row give the last term. This derives
ALL diagonals, off-diagonals and the initial mixed column -nu/2.
For q>0, full PSD is equivalent to

    Cgrad-nu nu^T/(4q)>=0 on the ENTIRE gradient space.    (5)

Let e be the all-ones gradient column, csum=Cgrad e,
X=sum xiCert_i, E=sum(1+Ppos_i)xiCert_i, Hprice=D X-E.
Summing(2) gives sum nu=2+X. Multiplying(2) by Ppos_i and summing
gives sum K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j)=2S-sum(nu_i-xiCert_i)Ppos_i.

    M(x_0=r,g=t e)=q r^2-(2+X)r t+(D+E)t^2.           (6)

The one-sided Huber function is zero on z<=0, z^2/2 on[0,1], and

Thus Hprice<=(zeta-1)D is ONE whole-word allowance. Completing the

      -(2+X)(nu^T v)(csum^T v)/2+q(csum^T v)^2]
          /[q(D+E)-(2+X)^2/4]                         (8)

when the denominator is positive. It is obtained by inverting the

No common, initial or singular direction is deleted.

                    +(dcontact^T v)^2/[D(zeta-1)].     (9)

## 3. Explicit base signs and value flow

We prescribe a base, not a PSD-selection oracle. Its coefficients are

    v_h=a/(c-2),

    A_2=lambda^2-epsilon[1+4/(lambda(1+epsilon))],

For instance A_2=3+2b-epsilon and the displayed formula for b give

Define a primitive finite array Lambda^j on0..n_j, starting Lambda^0=0.

## 6. Complete path polynomial, terminal square and contact defect

For original indices n,k,i,v, direct cancellation gives

    Q_(n,k)+Q_(k,i)-Q_(n,i)=<g_n-g_k,y_k-y_i>, y_i=x_i-g_i.

The values cancel. The position terms give <g_n-g_k,x_k-x_i>;
the gradient-difference terms give -<g_n-g_k,g_k-g_i>.
Applying this identity successively along(23), or expanding its four
rows, yields the WHOLE original polynomial

    Mpath(q)=Mbase(q)+2sum_(v,vnode)omegaPath EPath_(v,vnode),
    EPath=<g_n-g_i3,y_i3-y_v>
           +<g_i3-g_i2,y_i2-y_v>
           +<g_i2-g_i1,y_i1-y_v>.                    (25)

This is EPath in Laws A/B. Law C's complete path polynomial is

    EPath_C=EPath_B+<g_i1-g_0,y_0-y_v>.              (25c)

It follows by the same triangle expansion of i1->0->v. Law C is
constructed directly from the base by(23c), so it decrements no original
prefix row: the minus term in the comparison with B is paid by B's
explicit ADDED i1->v row, not an undeclared original edge.

Every original position in y uses the unchanged physical prefix. There
is no x_0 contribution to a position difference, so the entire mixed
column remains -mubase/2. Equations(4),(24),(25) specify all coefficients.

Using the ACTUAL alpha^path and prefix rows in(24), accepted
1252b8823bb5a290(c) gives the exact full terminal completion

    V_path=x_n-sum_(j in J_pre)alpha_j^path y_j,
    R_path=q||x_0||^2-2sum_(j in J_pre)alpha_j^path delta_j
              -||V_path||^2+sum_(i!=j in J_pre)lambda^pre_path_ij Q_ij,

    Mpath=||g_n-V_path||^2+R_path.                    (26)

Here J_pre={star,0,...,n-1}; lambda^pre consists exactly of the prefix

w_t^path=astar_r+sum_(i<=t)alpha_i^path,

These are explicit finite coefficients, not a free feasible-set oracle.

At a common gradient, y_i-y_v=Ppos_v-Ppos_i. Differentiating(25)

Every other component is zero for that path; overlapping components are

## 2. Law A: a real parameter rule from the whole word

Domain of A and B: h contains at least two entries strictly greater than1.
Select the two largest such entries; rank by decreasing value, then by
earlier original index to break ties. Write their chronological indices
j<k. This is ONE specified pair, not an optimization over unspecified
interpolation or certificate data. Retain all original blocks and put

    P=sum_(i<j)h_i, S=sum_(j<i<k)h_i, T=sum_(i>k)h_i,
    a_sel=h_j-1>0, b_sel=h_k-1>0, M_sel=S+1,
    sigma=1/(P+1), Delta=b_sel/2,
    ell=(M_sel+Delta)/a_sel,
    kappa=Delta/(2T+1), C_sel=M_sel+b_sel.

Here ell,kappa are positive real numbers. They are fixed from h BEFORE

    E_Q=M_sel*(ell+1)-a_sel*ell,

    chi=1/[ell^2+kappa*ell+(E_Q)_+/a_sel+(E_R)_+/a_sel].       (A1)

The symbol (u)_+ means max(u,0). All denominators are positive and finite.
In the real plane with e1=(1,0), e2=(0,1), set

    v=(-ell*chi, sqrt(chi-ell^2*chi^2)),

## 3. Law A: every initialized query, all support guards, actual terminal

For any compact convex D, the attained maximizer in
max_(g in D)(x.g-||g||^2/2) is the UNIQUE Euclidean projection of x
onto D. For u=x-g its exact necessary and sufficient condition is

    g in D, <u,z-g><=0 for every z in D.                     (A4)

Sufficiency follows by expanding ||x-z||^2-||x-g||^2. Necessity follows
by differentiating that distance along each segment from g to z.
It suffices to check the vertices of D_A. We now check ALL four at
EVERY original query, including selected bridges and zeros.

First sector: for original i<=j, set p_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, 0<=p_i<=P.

    x_i=(1-sigma*p_i)e1,
    g_i=p_A,
    u_i=x_i-p_A=sigma*(P-p_i)e1,
    delta_i=<u_i,p_A>=sigma^2*(P-p_i),
    f_i=delta_i+||p_A||^2/2.                                (A5)

The zero support is below p_A. The q_A comparison is nonpositive
because its first coordinate is negative. The r_A comparison is
sigma^2*(P-p_i)*(kappa*ell*chi-1)<=0 by(A3).
These include BOTH future slopes. At the selected query x_j=p_A,
u_j=0; all support ties leave the projection gradient uniquely p_A.
Its ACTUAL update is

    x_(j+1)=p_A-(1+a_sel)*p_A=-sigma*a_sel*e1.                (A6)

Middle sector: for j<i<=k let mu_i=sum_(j<t<i)h_t, 0<=mu_i<=S.
Then

    x_i=sigma*[-a_sel*e1-mu_i*v], g_i=q_A,
    u_i=sigma*[-a_sel*e1-(mu_i+1)*v],
    delta_i=sigma^2*chi*[a_sel*ell-(mu_i+1)],
    f_i=delta_i+||q_A||^2/2.                                (A7)

The middle height is PAID and strictly positive at EVERY such query:

Induction on original indices using(A5)--(A12) proves every actual

No reset or rescaling of an inherited state took place.

## 4. Law A: global legality, every row, minimum, true radius, actual Gram

The projection normal inequalities at x,x' give
<x-x',g-g'> >= ||g-g'||^2. Thus the projection is1-Lipschitz.
Evaluation of the two attained maxima bounds
f_A(x+d)-f_A(x)-g.d between0 and(g'-g).d, whose absolute value
is at most||d||^2. This proves differentiability with continuous
gradient g=projection_D_A(x), global convexity, and1-smoothness.
The nonempty interior of the triangle D_A has gradient x and Hessian I,
so the least global smoothness is exactly1. The function is finite
everywhere, and all parameters were fixed before GD.

The COMPLETE attained minimum set and minimum value are

    C_A={z:z1<=0, <v,z>=0}, min f_A=0.                       (A14)

Indeed all slope inner products are nonpositive there. Conversely a
positive inner product with a vertex makes f_A positive by taking a
sufficiently small positive multiple of that vertex in D_A. Opposite

For EVERY ordered pair of actual samples, including terminal and any

g_star=f_star=0, Q_(i,star)=z.g_i<=0 and
Q_(star,i)=-u_i.g_i<=0. Repeated actual jets have Q=0.

    <u,w>=sigma^2*[a_u*a_w-ell*chi*(a_u*b_w+b_u*a_w)
                                      +chi*b_u*b_w].         (A16)

For (x0,g0,...,gn), use coefficient(1/sigma,0) for x0, (1,0) for
each first-sector gradient, (0,1) for each middle gradient, (0,-kappa)
for each last-sector gradient including gn, and(0,0) for origin.
Positions have their explicit coefficients in(A5),(A7),(A11).
The two-dimensional metric in(A16) has positive determinant
chi*(1-ell^2*chi), so these are actual REAL Euclidean Grams and are PSD.

template, not optimization of an unknown feasible interpolation/PSD set.

anchor list with at most3 affinely independent slopes. Choose its first

y_a-y_0 and let e_I have components delta_a-delta_0. Set

## 9. What a combinatorial selector can and cannot inherit

A finite ordered tree that only assigns these COMPLETE-WORD scalar
channels to leaves, combines them by orthogonal direct sums, and then
applies one synchronized full-prefix completion at the root, is
contained in the analyzed family. Indeed each binary orthogonal sum
multiplies squared initial radii by its two nonnegative weights.
Flattening the tree yields their leaf weight products, summing to1;
associativity of orthogonal sums yields exactly (4.1). The root
completion is exactly (4.3), regardless of tree shape. Zero products
are discarded. Hence (8.16) includes all such finite tree selectors.

This assertion does NOT include a tree that changes a child's physical
prefix, applies intermediate completions that change subsequent
gradients, uses nonorthogonal coordinates, or starts a child at a new
point. Each of those would be a different construction requiring its
own global realization and initial radius proof.

For a plain orthogonal sum even before completion, normalized payoffs
are sums sum_r w_r v_r and cannot exceed their largest leaf payoff.
The root completion can exceed that sum, because its plane maximum is
synchronized, but the original final query yields (7.1). Thus the
nontrivial coupling is accounted for and still cannot manufacture
lossless Omega/G composition on the hierarchy. No scalar capacity
identity supplies missing physical cross-coordinate transport.

The required change is therefore in the earlier physical prefix:
it must escape this convex squared-radius allocation of single-switch
scalar trajectories, or use additional inter-sector geometry that
alters the last jet while paying all its remote guards. Merely adding
all cuts, optimizing their weights, repeating channels, increasing
dimension, changing the tree shape, or maximizing the synchronized
terminal extension does not do that. This is the precise scope of the
whole-law obstruction. A globally paid nonorthogonal or multi-switch
prefix remains open; no impossibility for those mechanisms is claimed.

Every other argument is proved jointly below. In particular prior unverified
bb1edc657a2239e2 and related reports are awareness, not premises.

## 1. Normalization, the original word, and its literal products

Work first at smoothness1. For one actual function f with attained minimum0,
write

    E(f,h)=2 f(x_n)/dist(x_0,argmin f)^2,
    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i grad f(x_i).

Initial minima are excluded. E uses W=2R, not the normalization R. Multiplying
f by any advertised L>0 and using physical steps h_i/L preserves all points
and this payoff. Every general-word statement below permits all finite
nonnegative steps, including zero, huge and unordered steps, unless its
explicit geometric guard restricts that word/initialization pair.

For the diagnostic fix m>=1536 and keep this SAME m in every child:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, A_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S_j=sum H_j, S=S_m=A_n.

The physical entry at index i is 1+beta*c^(v2(i+1)-1), where v2(k) is the
exponent of2 in a positive integer k. This follows by locating the central
entry of each literal recursive child. Let s2(i) count the ones in the binary

    p_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t)=(-1)^i beta^i c^(-s2(i)),

2^r contributes 2^r-1 to the middle sum. This proves (1) symbolically; no
trajectory, product, or recurrence was executed. All p_i are nonzero here.
The last physical step is 1+a. In particular all original steps exceed1.

Put v_mass=beta/[c(c-2)]. Counting the occurrences of each level gives

    S_j+1=(1-v_mass)2^j+v_mass c^j,
    1/2<v_mass<1, 2<c<5/2, 0<a<1/2,

For the mass formula, sum the finite geometric sum
S_j=2^j-1+a(c^j-2^j)/(c-2). Since c>lambda and lambda(lambda-2)=1,

241/100<lambda<121/50; the latter follows by squaring the corresponding

For clarity the benchmark is always the ORIGINAL all-split one:

    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    Gbench(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,

at its exact stated scope, gives

## 2. One actual projection function and every original row

Let D be any of the explicitly specified compact convex bodies below,
containing0, and put C=cone(D). Their cones are closed. Define ONE function
before GD by

    J(y)=max_(v a listed vertex of D)<v,y>,
    F_D(x)=max_(g in D){<x,g>-||g||^2/2}.             (4)

The zero plane is included, explicitly or as a convex combination of the
listed planes. All offsets in the three laws are0. The metric is Euclidean
identity; no uncharged change of metric or expected Gram is used.

The unique maximizer in (4) is g=P_D(x), characterized by

    g in D, <x-g,w-g><=0 for every w in D.           (5)

Adding (5) for two points proves
<x-y,P_D(x)-P_D(y)> >= ||P_D(x)-P_D(y)||^2. Thus P_D is1-Lipschitz.
Comparing the two maximizers in (4) bounds its first-order remainder between

For actual samples, including the terminal and any minimum, write

    g_i=P_D(x_i), r_i=x_i-g_i,

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2

All original vectors are real vectors in the stated space, so the WHOLE

The complete minimum is

    min F_D=0, argmin F_D=C^polar,
    C^polar={x:<x,v><=0 for every listed vertex v}.  (7)

One direction follows by comparing every term in (4) with0. If x is not

## 3. All-prefix completion and a general zero-height boundary

Retain EVERY original queried jet 0<=i<n and the optimum jet(0,0,0). The
maximal complete-prefix function from accepted1252 is, for these projection
jets,

    H_pre(u)=||u||^2/2+max(0,max_(i<n)(<r_i,u>-delta_i)),
    F_pre(x)=sup_u(<x,u>-H_pre(u)).                  (8)

All coefficients are mathematical functions of the fixed old function,
initial state and full known word; (8) defines one static function BEFORE its
own run. Induction on every physical index gives the same old prefix and
terminal POSITION. Its terminal gradient is its own unique maximizer in(8).
It is never silently assigned the old terminal gradient. Accepted1252 gives
all ordered rows for this actual function, including every own minimizer.

Its ENTIRE minimum set is

    R_pre=conv({0} union {r_i:i<n,delta_i=0}).         (9)

Indeed F_pre(x)=0 iff x is a subgradient of H_pre at0. At0 exactly the

Every other static convex1-smooth K interpolating the ENTIRE same prefix
and optimum has K<=F_pre pointwise and reaches the same x_n. For n>=1 its last outgoing
terminal row, with its actual terminal gradient unrestricted, gives

    K(x_n)<=delta_(n-1)+||x_n-r_(n-1)||^2/2.         (10)

This is completion of the terminal-gradient square in Q_(n,n-1), and uses

Here is a useful boundary that is not restricted to projection functions.
Assume n>=1. Suppose an actual convex1-smooth prefix with minimum0 has

    f_i=||g_i||^2/2 for EVERY 0<=i<n, g_0!=0.       (11)

For i<n-1 its original row Q_(i+1,i)<=0 becomes exactly

Using (10) now gives the complete bound

    E(K,h)<=product_(i<n)(1-h_i)^2.                 (12)

This keeps the unqueried terminal free. It does not require its height to be

## 4. The genuinely dependent finite character dictionaries

Choose an integer q>=2, let G=(Z/2Z)^q and N=2^q. For every nonzero a in G
use the real character chi_a(s)=(-1)^(a dot s), with the dot product modulo2.
All N orbit weights are1/N. The N-1 character coordinates are DEPENDENT:

    chi_a(s)chi_b(s)=chi_(a+b)(s), a!=b, a,b!=0.

They are not N-1 independent sign bits. Pairing s with s+t for a character

## 5. Law I: exact whole-word scalar equivalence, and its precise limit

Choose ANY nonempty proper subset A of G, let p=|A|, r=N-p, and set

    u_A=(1/p)sum_(s in A)z_s,
    R_plus=sigma*sqrt(r/p), R_minus=sigma*sqrt(p/r),
    e_A=u_A/R_plus, x_0=t_0 e_A, t_0!=0.            (18)

    P_(D_I)(t e_A)=clip(t,[-R_minus,R_plus])*e_A.    (19)

    x_i=t_i e_A, g_i=phi'(t_i)e_A,
    t_(i+1)=t_i-h_i phi'(t_i), f_i=phi(t_i),

    Hprice=sum_i(2S-P_i)xiCert_i=D*Xin-Ein.                    (10)

This is one WHOLE-WORD Huber charge. It is not renewed at each node.
For a transverse column v with e^T v=0, write nuv=nu^T v and csv=csum^T v.
If Delta=q(D+Ein)-(2+Xin)^2/4>0, completing both x_0 and the common
gradient gives the exact additional expenditure

    Price(v)=[(D+Ein)nuv^2/4-(2+Xin)nuv*csv/2+q*csv^2]/Delta. (11)

Indeed the common block is [[q,-(2+Xin)/2],[-(2+Xin)/2,D+Ein]],
and its coupling to v is (-nuv/2,csv). Inverting this 2-by-2 matrix
gives(11). Full PSD requires v^T C v>=Price(v) for every such v,
in addition to PSD of the common block. If that block is singular,
its kernel must annihilate every coupling. These are full-space
conditions, not claims that the charges have been paid.

## 4. Two explicit GLOBAL laws and their entire polynomial

At the final depth m abbreviate mu=mubase^m. In the following formulas
the coefficients eta,chi are arbitrary nonnegative scalars. Define

    K_ij=Kbase_ij+eta*mu_i*mu_j, i!=j; K_ii=0,
    nu_i=(1+chi)mu_i,
    xiCert_i=chi*mu_i,                         0<=i,j<=n. (21)

The two concrete laws are

    Law A: eta=64epsilon, chi=0;
    Law B: eta=0, chi=128epsilon.                     (22)

For a calibration child r<5 use eta=chi=0; for r>=5 use(22) with
the SAME enclosing epsilon. At epsilon=0 both laws use eta=chi=0 at
every depth. The scope extension to arbitrary eta,chi in(21) is an
exclusion of the whole fixed two-parameter family, not another law
or a parameter search. No retuning is performed after the obstruction.

Every final coefficient is a finite formula supplied by(15),(18),(21).
There are no decrements, so no zero coefficient is subtracted from.
All finite pairs, including pairs INTO and OUT OF the actual terminal,
are retained. Law A adds equal mass to each pair i->j and j->i;
Law B adds equal mass to i->star and star->i. Thus every original
value equation(5) stays exact. These are global balanced circulations,
not source-dependent terminal paths or changes of physical GD steps.

Their total additions over the ONE word are

    finite addition = eta*(4-sum_i mu_i^2) <=4eta,
    outgoing optimum addition = 2chi,
    incoming optimum addition = 2chi.                (23)

In A the finite addition is at most256epsilon=64/m<=1/24.
In B each optimum addition is256epsilon=64/m<=1/24 and their
combined addition is at most1/12. There is no per-node allowance.

For the entire original vector family define

    Tmu=sum_i mu_i g_i,
    Xmu=sum_i mu_i x_i,
    Vmu=sum_i mu_i[||g_i||^2-<g_i,x_i>].              (24)

give the exact polynomial

           +eta*[2Vmu-||Tmu||^2+<Tmu,Xmu>]+chi*Vmu. (25)

In the eta term the x_0 contributions cancel; the chi term contributes
-chi<Tmu,x_0>. The full initial mixed column is therefore
-(1+chi)mu/2 as required by(21), and its Schur expenditure is
(1+chi)^2 mu mu^T/(4q). The terminal diagonal and every incoming
terminal row are retained by(7),(21); a unit terminal-square coefficient
from an incoming-free theorem is NOT assumed for this new array.

Here is the exact terminal completion for the ACTUAL altered array.
The base terminal has total outgoing mass2 and no incoming rows, so
Cbase_nn=1. The final original terminal entries are

    K_(i,n)=eta*mu_i*mu_n for i<n,
    K_(n,i)=Kbase_(n,i)+eta*mu_n*mu_i for i<n,
    nu_n=(1+chi)mu_n, xiCert_n=chi*mu_n,
    gammaTerm=C_nn=1+eta*mu_n*(2-mu_n)+chi*mu_n>0.

Every coefficient in this identity is fixed by the finite formulas

## 5. Whole-word common/contact payment for the two laws

Set Pbar=sum_i mu_i P_i and Utail_i=sum_(j>i)mu_j. From(21),

    Xin=2chi, Ein=chi(2+Pbar),
    Hprice=chi(2D-2-Pbar), 0<=Pbar<=D-1.              (26)

At q=21/(20D), both laws have a positive initial/common block. For A
its determinant is1/20. For B, chi<=1/48, and

       >=21/20-(49/48)^2>0.                         (27)

A has Hprice=0. These checks do not imply full PSD. They retain the

For clarity, the full contact vector can also be written explicitly.

    dfin_i=eta*mu_i*(P_i-Pbar/2),                    (29)

and Vmu's gradient-matrix row sum is

+sum_i mu_i<g_i,sum_(t<i)h_t g_t> and take its gradient row sums.

    csum=D*mu/2+dfin+chi*cstar.                       (31)

Equations(11),(21),(26),(31) give the EXACT remaining transverse

No bound paying this transverse expenditure is claimed.

For A alone, dcontact=csum-D*mu/2=dfin. Completing the common block
at q=zeta/D, zeta>1, gives the simpler exact expression

                  +(dfin^T v)^2/[D(zeta-1)].        (32)

At zeta=1 the singular common block instead requires dfin=0.
As mu has positive weights at different physical prefixes, A at
epsilon>0 does not satisfy that singular-contact requirement.
At zeta=21/20 the cost in(32) is finite but remains a real full-space

## 6. General balanced-circulation contact obstruction

This calculation is not limited to the rank-product law. Let J_ij>=0
be ANY zero-diagonal finite-node array with equal row and column sums
at every node. On ANY finite nonnegative word define

    R_J(g)=sum_(i!=j)J_ij[<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].

Its value terms cancel by balance and its x_0 terms cancel in position
differences. Let C_J be its full symmetric gradient matrix. At common
gradients, R_J(e)=0. Its row-sum vector satisfies

    (C_J e)_i=(1/2)sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j),
    P^T C_J e=(1/4)sum_(i,j)J_ij(P_i-P_j)^2.         (33)

For the first equality, the derivative of the source gradient gives
sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j). The derivatives of the positions cancel because
row and column masses agree. The difference-square derivative vanishes
at e. Divide the derivative by2. For the second equality, expand the
sum of squared differences and use balance to equate the P_i^2 and
P_j^2 sums. This proves both equalities directly without invoking a
graph theorem.

It follows that C_J e=0 if and only if every positive J_ij joins
equal P_i and P_j. Necessity follows from the nonnegative sum in(33);
sufficiency follows from its first equality. With nonnegative h,
P_i=P_j means all intervening steps are zero, hence x_i=x_j as a
FORMAL identity even with independent gradients. In this case

    R_J(g)=(1/2)sum J_ij||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.           (34)

Conversely, if some positive edge has unequal physical prefixes,
C_J e!=0 while e^T C_J e=0. Taking v=C_J e and expanding
R_J(e+t v)=2t||C_J e||^2+t^2 v^T C_J v shows a negative value
for sufficiently small negative t. Thus C_J is not PSD. In particular,
on a strictly positive word EVERY nonzero nonnegative balanced finite
circulation is an indefinite correction, despite exact value balance.

Moreover no collection of such additions can cancel its physical-
prefix contact work: the right side of(33) is additive and nonnegative.
At an exactly contacting base with zero incoming optimum rows and
q=1/D, the common kernel condition forces C_J e=0. Hence no nonzero
nonnegative finite circulation preserves full PSD at that exact level
on a positive word. This is NOT a statement at q>1/D, about signed
changes with paid decrements, about changed optimum profiles, or about
arbitrary full certificates. The explicit paid test in the next
section is needed to exclude our concrete laws at larger q.

Consider any original gradient assignment supported strictly within

    sum_(i in support)h_i g_i=0.                     (35)

All later formal positions are zero. On the supported indices(18)
gives mu_i=2h_i/D. Therefore Tmu=0 exactly. By(24),(25),

## 6. General balanced-circulation contact obstruction

This calculation is not limited to the rank-product law. Let J_ij>=0
be ANY zero-diagonal finite-node array with equal row and column sums
at every node. On ANY finite nonnegative word define

    R_J(g)=sum_(i!=j)J_ij[<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].

Its value terms cancel by balance and its x_0 terms cancel in position
differences. Let C_J be its full symmetric gradient matrix. At common
gradients, R_J(e)=0. Its row-sum vector satisfies

    (C_J e)_i=(1/2)sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j),
    P^T C_J e=(1/4)sum_(i,j)J_ij(P_i-P_j)^2.         (33)

For the first equality, the derivative of the source gradient gives
sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j). The derivatives of the positions cancel because
row and column masses agree. The difference-square derivative vanishes
at e. Divide the derivative by2. For the second equality, expand the
sum of squared differences and use balance to equate the P_i^2 and
P_j^2 sums. This proves both equalities directly without invoking a
graph theorem.

It follows that C_J e=0 if and only if every positive J_ij joins
equal P_i and P_j. Necessity follows from the nonnegative sum in(33);
sufficiency follows from its first equality. With nonnegative h,
P_i=P_j means all intervening steps are zero, hence x_i=x_j as a
FORMAL identity even with independent gradients. In this case

    R_J(g)=(1/2)sum J_ij||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.           (34)

Conversely, if some positive edge has unequal physical prefixes,
C_J e!=0 while e^T C_J e=0. Taking v=C_J e and expanding
R_J(e+t v)=2t||C_J e||^2+t^2 v^T C_J v shows a negative value
for sufficiently small negative t. Thus C_J is not PSD. In particular,
on a strictly positive word EVERY nonzero nonnegative balanced finite
circulation is an indefinite correction, despite exact value balance.

Moreover no collection of such additions can cancel its physical-
prefix contact work: the right side of(33) is additive and nonnegative.
At an exactly contacting base with zero incoming optimum rows and
q=1/D, the common kernel condition forces C_J e=0. Hence no nonzero
nonnegative finite circulation preserves full PSD at that exact level
on a positive word. This is NOT a statement at q>1/D, about signed
changes with paid decrements, about changed optimum profiles, or about
arbitrary full certificates. The explicit paid test in the next
section is needed to exclude our concrete laws at larger q.

# Global finite circulation and two-way optimum flow: original-space obstruction

JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT — UNVERIFIED. Worker max, allocated invocation77
after observed baseline76, ceiling77/attempted78, cap1. No controller
completion/counters are inferred. TWO concrete laws are screened. No
mathematical program, numerical/arithmetic replay, executed recurrence,
trajectory execution, optimizer, formal call, fact_submit, installation,
paid consult or subagent was used. No automatic renewal is allocated.

The result is a scoped failure, not the original theorem. It excludes
every nonnegative mixture of a complete finite-node rank-product
circulation and a common-profile two-way optimum circulation on the
specified inherited base. This includes arbitrary mixture coefficients,
not merely the two displayed choices. The obstruction is a negative
direction of the FULL original matrix. It is explicitly NOT an
interpolable primal run or a lower bound on W.

A second, general calculation shows why Eulerian balance alone cannot
give a free PSD correction: a nonnegative balanced finite circulation
has a strictly positive physical-prefix contact moment unless all its
edges join identical physical prefixes. Every claim and calculation
in this report belongs to this ONE joint unverified draft.

## 1. Target, accepted inputs, and original variables

For every finite nonnegative physical word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)) and
L>0, define W_n(h) as the supremum of

    2(f(x_n)-min f)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2)

over every finite-dimensional Euclidean space, every convex C1 function
with L-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer x_star, and every x_0!=x_star,
under x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R, where R_n(h)=W_n(h)/2. The original benchmark is

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n)Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.        (1)

All splits k are integers. The original question is whether
lim_n B_n inf_(h in [0,infinity)^n)W_n(h)=1. No schedule restriction
in the present certificate experiment is a restriction of that target.

Fix ONE enclosing m>=1536. Define

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    Hword_0=(), Hword_(j+1)=(Hword_j,1+a*c^j,Hword_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum Hword_j, A_j=1+S_j,
    d_j=a*c^j, D_j=2A_j-1, t_j=d_j/A_j, tstar=1/lambda. (2)

All children retain these SAME m and epsilon. The final actual word is
h=Hword_m=H_(m,1/4), with length n=n_m and D=D_m. The auxiliary symbol
Hword is distinct from a conjugate quadratic in fact1252b8823bb5a290.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 was read in full. It supplies the exact
smooth-convex interpolation convention, full formal-space certificate
interpretation, and incoming-terminal-free selection theorem. The
present circulation may add incoming terminal rows, and no selected
terminal support theorem is misapplied to the altered array.
Accepted fact04219554e41d9750, Sections10–11, supplies the complete
primitive/objective conventions. Accepted fact5fd396eba75651e7,
Section10, supplies only the unconditional benchmark consequence

    B_(n_m)/D_m < 237/250, every m>=1536.                 (3)

Therefore a genuine full PSD certificate at q=21/(20D) would imply
B_(n_m)W_(n_m)(h)<4977/5000, a fixed relative gap. Neither new law
has such a certificate. In fact both fail at EVERY real q.

The complete previous joint report d031c723cebd5dde was read as
unverified awareness. No result from it is adopted as a premise by
citation. The base definitions and every needed identity are given
and derived within this joint draft. TASK.md, guidanceff3d21d24d20197e,
and plan1fa89a2e348197ec govern this invocation. Latest guidance
58e2501222fb10fe was read and explicitly leaves this allocation unchanged.

Normalize L=1 and the optimum jet to x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep
EVERY original independent formal vector (x_0,g_0,...,g_n), including
every zero-step query if present. Put h_n=0 and

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
    P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=sum h, D=1+2S,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.          (4)

Actual legal samples have Q_ij<=0 by fact1252b8823bb5a290. The general
algebra below allows all finite nonnegative words: zero, huge and
unordered steps included. The eventual failure claim concerns only(2).

## 2. Complete matrix and all endpoint charges

Let K_ij>=0 be all ordered finite-node multipliers, K_ii=0. Let
nu_i>=0 multiply Q_(i,star), and xiCert_i>=0 multiply Q_(star,i).
Full value cancellation is

    sum_j K_ij-sum_j K_ji+nu_i-xiCert_i=2*1_(i=n).           (5)

No original row is omitted from the array; an unspecified coefficient
is explicitly zero. Once(5) holds, the full polynomial is

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum K_ij Q_ij
                        +sum nu_i Q_(i,star)+sum xiCert_i Q_(star,i)
        =q||x_0||^2-sum nu_i<x_0,g_i>+Cgrad(g).           (6)

Writing out_i=nu_i+sum_j K_ij, every entry of its gradient matrix is

    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i sum_(v>i)K_iv,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j sum_(v>j)K_iv
                         +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j. (7)

Half the total incident mass is out_i-1_(i=n), by(5). The source
position in a forward row supplies the diagonal -h_i K_iv. For i<j,
the gradient-difference terms give -(K_ij+K_ji), source i's later
destinations supply the second term, and source j's earlier
destinations and outgoing optimum row supply the last term. Thus(7)
derives ALL entries, including the independent terminal diagonal and
initial mixed column -nu/2. For q>0 the entire PSD condition is

    C - nu nu^T/(4q) >= 0.                              (8)

Let e be the all-ones column in R^(n+1), csum=Ce, Xin=sum xiCert_i,
Ein=sum(1+P_i)xiCert_i. Summing(5) gives sum nu_i=2+Xin. Weighting(5) by
P_i and summing yields the exact common-gradient block

    M(x_0=r,g=t e)=q r^2-(2+Xin)rt+(D+Ein)t^2.             (9)

For completeness the finite position contribution is
sum K_ij(P_i-P_j)=2S-sum(nu_i-xiCert_i)P_i; inserting the optimum
contributions gives e^T C e=D+Ein. Nothing is discarded at n or star.

The one-sided Huber function Hub_1 is 0 on z<=0, z^2/2 on[0,1],
and z-1/2 on z>=1. Its full minimum set is (-infinity,0]. Starting
at D gives all gradients1 and positions D-P_i>=1. Its OWN closest
radius is D. On this actual static trajectory, all finite and outgoing
optimum residuals vanish, while Q_(star,i)=-(2S-P_i). Consequently

    M(D,e)=(qD-1)D-Hprice,
    Hprice=sum_i(2S-P_i)xiCert_i=D*Xin-Ein.                    (10)

This is one WHOLE-WORD Huber charge. It is not renewed at each node.
For a transverse column v with e^T v=0, write nuv=nu^T v and csv=csum^T v.
If Delta=q(D+Ein)-(2+Xin)^2/4>0, completing both x_0 and the common
gradient gives the exact additional expenditure

    Price(v)=[(D+Ein)nuv^2/4-(2+Xin)nuv*csv/2+q*csv^2]/Delta. (11)

Indeed the common block is [[q,-(2+Xin)/2],[-(2+Xin)/2,D+Ein]],
and its coupling to v is (-nuv/2,csv). Inverting this 2-by-2 matrix
gives(11). Full PSD requires v^T C v>=Price(v) for every such v,
in addition to PSD of the common block. If that block is singular,
its kernel must annihilate every coupling. These are full-space
conditions, not claims that the charges have been paid.

## 3. Explicit inherited base on the actual hierarchy

Here is the base used in the experiment. These definitions fix every
coefficient without a feasibility oracle. Summing the finite geometric
series in the word definition gives

    v_h=a/(c-2),
    A_j=v_h c^j+(1-v_h)2^j,
    t_j=(c-2)/[1+(1/v_h-1)(2/c)^j].                    (12)

Since c(c-2)>1>beta, 0<v_h<1. Hence t_j increases and t_j<c-2<1/2.
Put b=1+a, the first physical step. Direct expansion of(2) gives

    b=sqrt(2)-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)],
    A_1=lambda-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)], d_1=1-epsilon,
    A_2=lambda^2-epsilon[1+4/(lambda(1+epsilon))],
    d_2=lambda(1-epsilon^2),
    lambda d_2-A_2
       =epsilon[1+4/(lambda(1+epsilon))-lambda^2 epsilon]. (13)

The last bracket is positive since lambda^2<6 and epsilon<=1/6144.
Also lambda d_1-A_1=-epsilon[lambda-2/(lambda(1+epsilon))]<0.
It follows that

    t_0,t_1<tstar<t_2,
    0<t_j-tstar<lambda epsilon for j>=2,
    A_j>=2^j, 7/5<b<sqrt(2), A_1>12/5, A_2>5.          (14)

For A_1 use lambda>241/100 and 2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]<epsilon;
then A_2=2A_1+1-epsilon>5. The scalar estimates in this proof are
written inequalities, not machine evaluations of any hierarchy.

Define a primitive array Lambda^j on0..n_j, starting Lambda^0=0.
At a join of two Hword_j copies, let p=n_j be the bridge, z=n_(j+1)
the terminal, and i range over nonterminal queries of the right child.
Embed the left array with weight1 and the right array with weight k_j;
add precisely

    i->p: u_j h_i,  i->z: v_j h_i,  z->p: w_j,  p->z: z_j,
    u_j=2lambda,
    v_j=[2lambda d_j+2(A_j+d_j)]/A_j,
    k_j=2+lambda+(lambda+1)t_j,
    w_j=4A_j+2d_j-2lambda(A_j-1), z_j=2A_j.             (15)

The unrolled coefficient of any original ordered pair is the finite
sum of these four indicators over every dyadic node, weighted by the
product of k_l over precisely the ancestors whose right child contains
that node. Left ancestor weights are1. Repeated pairs are summed.
This finite sum/product is the intended explicit formula; no recurrence
has been executed. All entries are nonnegative. For w_j, write
w_j=2lambda+2(d_j-A_j/lambda); use(14) at j>=2, w_0=4+2a,
and w_1>2lambda-2. The identities
u_j+v_j=2(k_j-1) and u_j(A_j-1)+w_j-z_j=2(A_j+d_j)
prove primitive divergence -2h_i at each nonterminal query and
2(A_(j+1)-1) at the terminal.

Define

    V_j=2sum_(i<n_j)h_i(f_i-f_(n_j))
         +sum_(i<n_j)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
         -A_j(A_j-1)||g_(n_j)||^2,
    Psrc_j=V_j+sum Lambda^j_iv Q_iv.                    (16)

At a join set r_R=sum_(i right,i<z)h_i g_i,
Y=r_R-(A_j-1)g_z and Z=g_p-g_z. The four weighted-row types before
their scalar multipliers in(15), with value parts suppressed only
after their stated divergence cancels them, have gradient parts

    d_j<r_R,g_p>+||r_R||^2/2+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2
                                            +(A_j-1)||g_p||^2/2;
    -||r_R||^2/2+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2
                              +(A_j-1)||g_z||^2/2-<r_R,g_z>;
    d_j<g_z,g_p>+<g_z,r_R>+(||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2)/2;
    -(d_j+1/2)||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2/2-<g_p,r_R>-<g_p,g_z>.

Collecting r_R^2,r_R*g_p,r_R*g_z and the diagonals gives the full identity

    Psrc_(j+1)=Psrc_j^left+k_j Psrc_j^right
      +(tstar-t_j)[(lambda+1)||Y||^2-2lambda A_j<Y,Z>
                           +A_j^2(2+tstar+t_j)||Z||^2]. (17)

For example the three listed coefficients before adding V and children
are(u_j-v_j)/2, u_j d_j-z_j, w_j-v_j. Substitution of(15) gives(17).
The bracket is positive definite: its determinant divided by A_j^2
is (lambda+1)(2+tstar+t_j)-lambda^2>=lambda>0.
Thus positive epsilon does NOT make these primitive children PSD.

Define objective arrays Kbase^r and mubase^r with Kbase^0=0,
mubase^0_0=2, and zero incoming optimum rows. At a join of two depth-j
children put A=S_j, bjoin=1+d_j, Dp=D_(j+1), Dc=D_j, and

    s_j=(A+bjoin)/(3A+2bjoin), theta_j=1-s_j.

With maps L_l=l and R_i=n_j+1+i, let

    Kbase_(L_l,L_v)=Lambda^j_lv/Dp,
    Kbase_(R_i,R_v)=Kbase^j_iv,
    Kbase_(R_i,p)=s_j mubase^j_i,
    mubase_(L_l)=2h_l/Dp for l<n_j,
    mubase_p=2s_j-2A/Dp,
    mubase_(R_i)=theta_j mubase^j_i.                    (18)

All other entries are zero. The bridge optimum coefficient is positive
because (A+bjoin)Dp-A(3A+2bjoin)=A^2+4A*bjoin+2bjoin^2+A+bjoin>0.
Here s_0=1/2 and 1/3<s_j<1/2 for j>=1. Each right query has unchanged
flow since s_j+theta_j=1. Left primitive flow is canceled by its
displayed optimum rows and the bridge row. Thus(5) holds and
sum mubase=2. The base has no incoming terminal row.

To make(18) an explicit finite formula, in a depth-r word take the
right-spine node of depth l at offset o_l=2^r-2^l and bridge

[o_l,p_l]. For each of that node's right queries add
s_(l-1)mubase^(l-1)_i into p_l. These are all finite rows.
The optimum weight of a left nonterminal i at that node is

    (2h_i/D_l) product_(t=l)^(r-1)theta_t;

the optimum weight at p_l is

    [2s_(l-1)-2S_(l-1)/D_l] product_(t=l)^(r-1)theta_t;

and its final optimum weight is 2product_(t=0)^(r-1)theta_t.
Each query is in exactly one such left block, bridge, or final category.
The same explicit product formula within the relevant right child
specifies every weight used in a spine edge. Together with(15), this
gives every base coefficient as a finite sum/product on original indices.

Write Cbase^j for its gradient matrix and Mbase_j(q) for(6). At a join,
let T_R=sum_i mubase^j_i g_(R_i), x_p=x_0-sum_(l<n_j)h_l g_(L_l),
Rchild_R=Cbase^j(g_R)-Dc||T_R||^2/4, and
kappa_j=Dc-Dp theta_j^2. Expanding all original rows(18) gives

    Mbase_(j+1)(1/Dp)=Psrc_j(g_L)/Dp+Rchild_R
      +||x_p+(A-Dp s_j)g_p-(Dp theta_j/2)T_R||^2/Dp
      +(kappa_j/4)||T_R-2g_p||^2.                    (19)

remaining polynomial before completing squares is

    ||x_p||^2/Dp+2(A/Dp-s_j)<x_p,g_p>
    +(A^2/Dp+2s_j)||g_p||^2-theta_j<x_p,T_R>
    +(bjoin-s_j)<g_p,T_R>+Dc||T_R||^2/4.

Expanding the two squares in(19) reproduces this polynomial by
s_j(3A+2bjoin)=A+bjoin. No child PSD is asserted at epsilon>0.
The common-gradient contact identity is

    Cbase^j e=D_j mubase^j/2.                         (20)

Indeed Psrc is zero with zero derivative at all-common gradients by(17).
At x_0=Dp and all gradients1, x_p=Dp-A and T_R=2; both squares
in(19) have zero vector argument. Induction from ||x_0-g_0||^2
therefore gives zero value and derivative of the full quadratic, which
is precisely(20). Contact is algebraic, not a PSD claim.

## 4. Two explicit GLOBAL laws and their entire polynomial

At the final depth m abbreviate mu=mubase^m. In the following formulas
the coefficients eta,chi are arbitrary nonnegative scalars. Define

    K_ij=Kbase_ij+eta*mu_i*mu_j, i!=j; K_ii=0,
    nu_i=(1+chi)mu_i,
    xiCert_i=chi*mu_i,                         0<=i,j<=n. (21)

The two concrete laws are

    Law A: eta=64epsilon, chi=0;
    Law B: eta=0, chi=128epsilon.                     (22)

For a calibration child r<5 use eta=chi=0; for r>=5 use(22) with
the SAME enclosing epsilon. At epsilon=0 both laws use eta=chi=0 at
every depth. The scope extension to arbitrary eta,chi in(21) is an
exclusion of the whole fixed two-parameter family, not another law
or a parameter search. No retuning is performed after the obstruction.

Every final coefficient is a finite formula supplied by(15),(18),(21).
There are no decrements, so no zero coefficient is subtracted from.
All finite pairs, including pairs INTO and OUT OF the actual terminal,
are retained. Law A adds equal mass to each pair i->j and j->i;
Law B adds equal mass to i->star and star->i. Thus every original
value equation(5) stays exact. These are global balanced circulations,
not source-dependent terminal paths or changes of physical GD steps.

Their total additions over the ONE word are

    finite addition = eta*(4-sum_i mu_i^2) <=4eta,
    outgoing optimum addition = 2chi,
    incoming optimum addition = 2chi.                (23)

In A the finite addition is at most256epsilon=64/m<=1/24.
In B each optimum addition is256epsilon=64/m<=1/24 and their
combined addition is at most1/12. There is no per-node allowance.

For the entire original vector family define

    Tmu=sum_i mu_i g_i,
    Xmu=sum_i mu_i x_i,
    Vmu=sum_i mu_i[||g_i||^2-<g_i,x_i>].              (24)

Value cancellation and Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i)=||g_i||^2-<g_i,x_i>
give the exact polynomial

    M_(eta,chi)(q)=Mbase_m(q)
           +eta*[2Vmu-||Tmu||^2+<Tmu,Xmu>]+chi*Vmu. (25)

For the finite term, sum over unordered pairs mu_i mu_j(Q_ij+Q_ji).
The difference-square part is 2sum mu_i||g_i||^2-||Tmu||^2 because
sum mu=2. The position part is <Tmu,Xmu>-2sum mu_i<g_i,x_i>.
This proves(25) with every coordinate, including x_0 and g_n, present.
In the eta term the x_0 contributions cancel; the chi term contributes
-chi<Tmu,x_0>. The full initial mixed column is therefore
-(1+chi)mu/2 as required by(21), and its Schur expenditure is
(1+chi)^2 mu mu^T/(4q). The terminal diagonal and every incoming
terminal row are retained by(7),(21); a unit terminal-square coefficient
from an incoming-free theorem is NOT assumed for this new array.

Here is the exact terminal completion for the ACTUAL altered array.
The base terminal has total outgoing mass2 and no incoming rows, so
Cbase_nn=1. The final original terminal entries are

    K_(i,n)=eta*mu_i*mu_n for i<n,
    K_(n,i)=Kbase_(n,i)+eta*mu_n*mu_i for i<n,
    nu_n=(1+chi)mu_n, xiCert_n=chi*mu_n,
    gammaTerm=C_nn=1+eta*mu_n*(2-mu_n)+chi*mu_n>0.

With C from(7), put

    vterm=(nu_n/2)x_0-sum_(i<n)C_(i,n)g_i,
    Rterm=q||x_0||^2-sum_(i<n)nu_i<x_0,g_i>
              +sum_(i,j<n)C_ij<g_i,g_j>-||vterm||^2/gammaTerm.

Then the COMPLETE original polynomial, without a re-selection, is

    M_(eta,chi)(q)=gammaTerm*||g_n-vterm/gammaTerm||^2+Rterm.

Every coefficient in this identity is fixed by the finite formulas
above. Thus the actual terminal expenditure ||vterm||^2/gammaTerm
is retained, and full PSD is equivalent to PSD of the entire Rterm.
It is not enough to check individual prefix planes or the common block.

## 5. Whole-word common/contact payment for the two laws

Set Pbar=sum_i mu_i P_i and Utail_i=sum_(j>i)mu_j. From(21),

    Xin=2chi, Ein=chi(2+Pbar),
    Hprice=chi(2D-2-Pbar), 0<=Pbar<=D-1.              (26)

At q=21/(20D), both laws have a positive initial/common block. For A
its determinant is1/20. For B, chi<=1/48, and

    q(D+Ein)-(1+chi)^2
       >=21/20-(49/48)^2>0.                         (27)

The final strict inequality follows by cross multiplication:
21*2304>20*2401. B's WHOLE Huber charge is paid within that advertised
slack, since

    0<=Hprice/D<2chi<=1/24<1/20.                    (28)

A has Hprice=0. These checks do not imply full PSD. They retain the
same whole-word D and do not rescale a child or count slack twice.

For clarity, the full contact vector can also be written explicitly.
The finite addition has row-sum vector

    dfin_i=eta*mu_i*(P_i-Pbar/2),                    (29)

and Vmu's gradient-matrix row sum is

    cstar_i=mu_i*(1+P_i/2)+(h_i/2)*Utail_i.          (30)

To derive(29), vary all gradients around the common value1. Balanced
finite position variations cancel; the remaining row-i position
difference is eta mu_i(2P_i-Pbar), half of which is the matrix row sum.
For(30), write Vmu=sum mu_i||g_i||^2-<Tmu,x_0>
+sum_i mu_i<g_i,sum_(t<i)h_t g_t> and take its gradient row sums.
Thus the final row-sum vector is

    csum=D*mu/2+dfin+chi*cstar.                       (31)

Equations(11),(21),(26),(31) give the EXACT remaining transverse
expenditure, including every common, initial and terminal coupling.
No bound paying this transverse expenditure is claimed.

For A alone, dcontact=csum-D*mu/2=dfin. Completing the common block
at q=zeta/D, zeta>1, gives the simpler exact expression

    Price_A(v)=(csum^T v)^2/D
                  +(dfin^T v)^2/[D(zeta-1)].        (32)

At zeta=1 the singular common block instead requires dfin=0.
As mu has positive weights at different physical prefixes, A at
epsilon>0 does not satisfy that singular-contact requirement.
At zeta=21/20 the cost in(32) is finite but remains a real full-space
expense. The counterdirection below defeats both laws even before
any initial Schur expenditure is deducted.

## 6. General balanced-circulation contact obstruction

This calculation is not limited to the rank-product law. Let J_ij>=0
be ANY zero-diagonal finite-node array with equal row and column sums
at every node. On ANY finite nonnegative word define

    R_J(g)=sum_(i!=j)J_ij[<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].

Its value terms cancel by balance and its x_0 terms cancel in position
differences. Let C_J be its full symmetric gradient matrix. At common
gradients, R_J(e)=0. Its row-sum vector satisfies

    (C_J e)_i=(1/2)sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j),
    P^T C_J e=(1/4)sum_(i,j)J_ij(P_i-P_j)^2.         (33)

For the first equality, the derivative of the source gradient gives
sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j). The derivatives of the positions cancel because
row and column masses agree. The difference-square derivative vanishes
at e. Divide the derivative by2. For the second equality, expand the
sum of squared differences and use balance to equate the P_i^2 and
P_j^2 sums. This proves both equalities directly without invoking a
graph theorem.

It follows that C_J e=0 if and only if every positive J_ij joins
equal P_i and P_j. Necessity follows from the nonnegative sum in(33);
sufficiency follows from its first equality. With nonnegative h,
P_i=P_j means all intervening steps are zero, hence x_i=x_j as a
FORMAL identity even with independent gradients. In this case

    R_J(g)=(1/2)sum J_ij||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.           (34)

Conversely, if some positive edge has unequal physical prefixes,
C_J e!=0 while e^T C_J e=0. Taking v=C_J e and expanding
R_J(e+t v)=2t||C_J e||^2+t^2 v^T C_J v shows a negative value
for sufficiently small negative t. Thus C_J is not PSD. In particular,
on a strictly positive word EVERY nonzero nonnegative balanced finite
circulation is an indefinite correction, despite exact value balance.

Moreover no collection of such additions can cancel its physical-
prefix contact work: the right side of(33) is additive and nonnegative.
At an exactly contacting base with zero incoming optimum rows and
q=1/D, the common kernel condition forces C_J e=0. Hence no nonzero
nonnegative finite circulation preserves full PSD at that exact level
on a positive word. This is NOT a statement at q>1/D, about signed
changes with paid decrements, about changed optimum profiles, or about
arbitrary full certificates. The explicit paid test in the next
section is needed to exclude our concrete laws at larger q.

## 7. Entire zero-displacement restriction of BOTH global corrections

Consider any original gradient assignment supported strictly within
the root's first left child, with x_0=0, zero gradient at that child's
terminal, and

    sum_(i in support)h_i g_i=0.                     (35)

All later formal positions are zero. On the supported indices(18)
gives mu_i=2h_i/D. Therefore Tmu=0 exactly. By(24),(25),

    D[M_(eta,chi)(q)-Mbase_m(q)]
      =(2eta+chi) sum_(i in support)h_i(2-h_i)||g_i||^2. (36)

Here is a direct verification retaining all prefix positions. Since
x_i=-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,

    sum_i h_i<g_i,x_i>
      =-(1/2)||sum_i h_i g_i||^2+(1/2)sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2
      =(1/2)sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2.

Multiplying Vmu by D consequently gives exactly the diagonal sum
in(36). Every unsupported term in Vmu has gradient zero, and Tmu=0
kills BOTH global rank terms in(25), including their terminal and
remote-query contributions. Thus(36) is an entire subspace identity,
not a selected-edge or conditional-covariance approximation.

## 8. The inherited base itself is negative on a deep original wave

We now strengthen the earlier two-coordinate screen by retaining the
negative terminal-source accumulation at ALL depths. Let pterm_j be
Psrc_j evaluated with only its terminal gradient equal to1. Define

    Fterm_j=A_j^2(1+t_j)-2A_j+(lambda+1).

Substitute Y=-(A_j-1), Z=-1 into(17). The bracket is precisely Fterm_j,
and the left child is zero. Thus the finite closed expression is

    pterm_j=sum_(l<j)(tstar-t_l)Fterm_l
                              product_(v=l+1)^(j-1)k_v. (37)

This is a symbolic finite formula and has not been executed. At depth1,
pterm_1=2-b^2<3epsilon. At depth2, k_1<7,
0<tstar-t_1<epsilon, and Fterm_1<13, so

    pterm_2<34epsilon<2epsilon*A_2^2.                 (38)

For the last inequalities use(13),(14): k_1<2+5/2+(7/2)/2<7;
tstar-t_1=(lambda epsilon-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)])/(lambda A_1)
<epsilon; and Fterm_1=A_1^2-(1+epsilon)A_1+lambda+1<13.
Also A_2>5 makes34<2A_2^2. The step from depth2 to depth3 adds a
negative term and multiplies the normalized old term by a number in(0,1).
It follows that pterm_3/A_3^2<2epsilon, regardless of its sign.

For every l>=3, monotonicity of t_l and the exact relation
t_(l+1)=c*t_l/(2+t_l) give

    t_3>c*tstar/(2+tstar)=(1+epsilon)tstar,
    t_l-tstar>(2/5)epsilon.                          (39)

       <[2-(6/125)(j-3)]epsilon.                    (42)

## 9. All nonnegative mixtures fail: no parameter retuning can repair them

On(43), the full diagonal sum in(36) is

    b(2-b)(Hstep/b)^2+Hstep(2-Hstep)
       =2Hstep[1-(1-1/b)Hstep].                             (46)

Since b>7/5, 1-1/b>2/7. Also j>=62, d_j>2A_j/5 and A_j>=2^j,
so Hstep>7. Therefore the quantity in(46) is strictly negative.
Combining the complete identities(36),(44) with(45),(46) proves,
jointly within this unverified draft, that

    M_(eta,chi)(q;43)<-epsilon*A_j^2/(20D)<0          (47)

for EVERY m>=1536, EVERY62<=j<=m-3, EVERY eta,chi>=0,
and EVERY real q. This includes eta=chi=0 and arbitrary unbounded
mixture coefficients. Positive coefficients only make this direction
worse. Thus no nonnegative tuning of the two specified global
generators can produce a full PSD certificate on this base. Laws A
and B are stopped at this declared-domain obstruction; no third law
or tuned variant is proposed.

This is broader than failure of the three previous conditional paths:
it permits every finite-node pair of the rank-product generator,
includes the independent incoming terminal rows, includes both
optimum directions with nonzero whole-word expenditure, and excludes
the complete nonnegative cone of the two global generators. It still
does NOT exclude other circulations, non-product weights, signed
reallocations with paid decrements, different optimum profiles,
different bases or arbitrary certificates.

In particular(43) is NOT a primal hard function. It has x_0=0 and
a later x_i=0 but different assigned gradients. A differentiable
static function cannot have those two gradients at the same point;
also an actual start at the normalized optimum0 cannot have nonzero
gradient. Its only purpose is to test PSD on the required independent
original variables. No W upper or lower bound follows from(47).

## 10. Exact Silver and zero-step calibrations

At epsilon=0 the actual word in(2) has A_j=lambda^j,
d_j=lambda^(j-1), t_j=tstar. All coefficients eta,chi in the TWO
concrete laws vanish. Formula(17) gives Psrc_j=0 at every depth.
For the base objective completion(19), set A=S_j and
bjoin=1+tstar(A+1). Direct expansion yields

    (3A+2bjoin)^2*kappa_j
      =2(1-tstar)A^3+(6-8tstar)A^2
       +(1+tstar)(8tstar-2)A+(1+tstar)^2(1-2tstar)>0. (48)

Every coefficient is positive because1/4<tstar<1/2. The empty base
is ||x_0-g_0||^2. If the right child is PSD at1/Dc, its exact initial

At the advertised larger q, add(q-1/D_r)||x_0||^2. This is a proof

For the finite positive-epsilon calibration depths1 and2 the concrete
laws make no addition. At depth1 direct expansion gives

    Psrc_1=(2-b^2)||g_0-g_1||^2,
    Mbase_1(1/D_1)
      =||x_0-D_1(g_0+g_1)/2||^2/D_1
                         +(3-2b)||g_0-g_1||^2/4.   (49)

Here D_1>19/5, D_2<75/7 and
theta_1=(2b+2-epsilon)/(3b+4-2epsilon)<59/100.
For the upper ratio use b<10/7 and2-epsilon>199/100; the ratio
increases with b and decreases with that bridge. Cross multiplication
gives the claimed bound. Consequently D_2 theta_1^2<15/4 and
kappa_1>1/20. Equation(19), the PSD source in(49), and the full
right-child Schur remainder prove depth2 PSD with x_0 retained.
These finite calibrations do not establish positive-epsilon large-depth PSD.

For arbitrary zero entries in a word, ALL algebra(4)–(11),(21),(25),
(33) and the general balanced-flow statements keep every formal query.
If P_i=P_j, nonnegative steps make x_i=x_j a formal identity, but
g_i and g_j are still independent and remain in(34). No gradient
identification or compression is made.

For an explicit all-zero-word calibration, use the accepted direct
base Kbase=0, mu_n=2, mu_i=0 for i<n, D=1. The finite generator in(21)
is exactly zero. The two-way optimum generator yields the entire form

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2(1+chi)<x_0,g_n>
                              +(1+2chi)||g_n||^2.   (50)

Every other original gradient has a zero coefficient. Its exact PSD
condition is q>0 and q(1+2chi)>=(1+chi)^2. Thus Law A has the usual
all-zero threshold q=1, and Law B at chi<=1/48 is PSD at q=21/20
by(27); at q=1 it fails if chi>0. For the empty/depth<5 calibration

This explicitly records the extra endpoint cost instead of hiding it
behind zero-step compression. No assertion about an arbitrary positive
word's PSD is inferred from these zero-word checks.

## 11. Remaining theorem-level obstacle and resource handoff

The attempted global laws do not survive. The exact mechanism is not
an unpaid scalar Huber budget: Law B pays that WHOLE budget and both
laws have a strictly positive initial/common block at21/(20D). Their
complete original gradient matrices still have(47). On the decisive
subspace the dense finite and optimum corrections both collapse to

their nonnegative ratio, or inflating q cannot repair an x_0=0 failure.

Separately,(33) explains why finite Eulerian balance cannot be promoted

the exact charge(11) must still be paid in the entire transverse space.
A new construction must change the signed original-space action on
the zero-displacement subspace, for example through a different
non-product support/profile or a paid reallocation of existing rows.
Those are unproved possibilities, not supplied laws or solved lemmas.

The missing global nonnegative-coefficient PSD construction at an
objective level with a fixed gap against(1), or a static primal lower
witness ruling out that direction, remains a THEOREM-LEVEL obstacle.

## 2. An explicit all-word selector and backward knot rule

Everything in this section is a finite symbolic definition from the
entire known word. No mathematical recurrence was executed in this round.

Select, in chronological order, precisely the strict record steps

    h_j>2 and h_j>max({0} union {h_t:t<j}).              (2.1)

Let their count be k. If k=0, use the canonical Huber fallback specified
below. If k>=1, write the ORIGINAL word as

    (block_0,b_0,block_1,...,b_(k-1),block_k),
    block_i=(alpha_(i,0),...,alpha_(i,r_i-1)),
    s_i=sum_(v<r_i)alpha_(i,v).                         (2.2)

The integer r_i is the physical length of block_i. Empty blocks are
allowed. No step is reordered or deleted; zero steps retain their indices.

For every0<=i<=k put

    eta_i=1/[4(1+s_i)],
    P_(i,l)=product_(0<=v<l)(1-eta_i*alpha_(i,v)),
    P_i=P_(i,r_i),
    T_i=(P_i^(-1)-1)/eta_i.                            (2.3)

An empty product is1. Every factor is positive, because each
alpha_(i,v)<=s_i and eta_i*s_i<1/4. The elementary product inequality
product(1-z_v)>=1-sum z_v for0<=z_v<=1 follows by multiplying the
two-factor identity(1-z)(1-w)=1-z-w+zw and inducting. Thus

    3/4<P_i<=1, 0<eta_i<=1/4.                          (2.4)

Another exact identity is

    T_i=sum_(l<r_i)alpha_(i,l)*P_(i,l)/P_i >= s_i.     (2.5)

Indeed P_(i,l)-P_(i,l+1)=eta_i alpha_(i,l)P_(i,l);
sum and divide by eta_i P_i. Each P_(i,l)>=P_i. These are
symbolic identities, not evaluated trajectory or numerical products.

Define the final gradient magnitude q_k, terminal radius R_k, initial
radius A_k and initial gradient magnitude p_k for the last block by

    q_k=1, R_k=1/eta_k,
    A_k=1/(eta_k P_k), p_k=1/P_k.                      (2.6)

Let D_i=b_i-1>1 for i<k. For stage k-1 set

    q_(k-1)=A_k/D_(k-1), R_(k-1)=q_(k-1),
    A_(k-1)=R_(k-1)+T_(k-1)q_(k-1),
    p_(k-1)=q_(k-1)/P_(k-1).                         (2.7)

For i=k-2,...,0 define backward

    q_i=[A_(i+1)+A_(i+2)-p_(i+2)]/D_i,

## 2. The real centered simplex and its static smooth objective

Let N>=3 be an integer, let E_N={x in R^N:sum_j x_j=0} with the
inherited Euclidean metric, let u=(1/N,...,1/N), and choose sigma>0.
The intrinsic real dimension is N-1. Define every slope and every offset by

    v_j=sigma(e_j-u), 1<=j<=N,       offset_j=0,
    D=conv{v_1,...,v_N},
    J(y)=max_j <v_j,y>,
    F(x)=max_(g in D)(<x,g>-||g||^2/2), x in E_N.                (5)

There is no additional coordinate, positive carrier, variable metric, or
rescaling of an iterate. The Gram of the REAL slopes is

    <v_i,v_j>=sigma^2(1_(i=j)-1/N).                            (6)

For a literal R^(N-1) realization, an orthonormal basis of E_N is

    b_k=(e_1+...+e_k-k e_(k+1))/sqrt(k(k+1)), 1<=k<N.

The matrix U with these columns satisfies U^T U=I and U U^T=I-11^T/N.
The exact isometry X -> U X turns the slopes into sigma U^T e_j,
and leaves the scale sigma and all inner products unchanged. No Walsh
representation is needed or invoked.

The maximizer g=P_D(x) is unique by strict convexity of squared distance.
It is characterized by

    g in D, <x-g,v_j-g><=0 for ALL j.                           (7)

Adding the corresponding inequalities at x and x' gives
<x-x',g-g'>>=||g-g'||^2, hence P_D is 1-Lipschitz. Evaluating (5)
at the two maximizers bounds the differentiability remainder between 0
and ||x-x'||^2; thus F is everywhere finite, convex, differentiable,
and grad F=P_D. Its least gradient Lipschitz constant is exactly1:
0 is interior to D in E_N, and the gradient equals x near0.

Its COMPLETE minimum set and value are

    argmin F={0}, min F=0.                                    (8)

To see uniqueness, for nonzero x in E_N some x_j>0. Then
<x,v_j>=sigma x_j>0 and a sufficiently small positive multiple of
v_j belongs to D and makes the expression (5) positive. The value at0
is zero. Thus the exact initial closest radius is always ||x_0||.

## 3. Exact threshold and every ordered row

Write x=(sigma/N)w with sum_j w_j=0, and let theta be the unique real
number satisfying

    (1/N)sum_j (1+w_j-theta)_+ =1.                             (9)

It is nonnegative: at theta0 the sum is at least sum_j(1+w_j)=N.
Set P_j=(1+w_j-theta)_+. Then

    g_j=(sigma/N)(P_j-1),
    y_j=(x-g)_j=(sigma/N)min(1+w_j,theta),
    delta=<y,g>=sigma^2 theta/N,
    2F(x)=(sigma^2/N)(2theta+(1/N)sum_j(P_j-1)^2).              (10)

These are exact finite-coordinate expressions, not expectations. The
probability-simplex coordinates of g/sigma+u are P_j/N.

For completeness, sum P_j=N implies sum min(1+w_j,theta)=0.
On every coordinate with P_j>0 the residual equals sigma theta/N;
on the others it is no larger. Consequently <y,v_j><=sigma^2 theta/N
for every j, with equality on the active support. This proves (7)
against every vertex, including all remote ones, and proves (10).
It also proves delta=0 iff x lies in D; a first zero height by itself
says nothing about later heights.

For ANY two actual samples, terminal and optimum included, put
g_i=P_D(x_i), y_i=x_i-g_i, f_i=F(x_i). Direct expansion yields

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<y_j,g_i-g_j><=0.                                   (11)

Thus ALL ordered remote, opposite, optimum and terminal rows hold on
ONE fixed function. Every Gram is the actual real Euclidean Gram.
The same argument covers repeated points, without deleting any query.

Under a physical step h=1+d>1 the exact coordinate map is

    w'_j=w_j+h-h(1+w_j-theta)_+,
         =w_j+h                    on an inactive coordinate,
         =-d w_j+h theta           on an active coordinate.    (12)

In particular active coordinates reverse their relative order. No
order-preservation assumption will be made.

## 4. A fixed finite Cartesian inverse-folding law

The following domain is the ENTIRE domain of the construction analyzed
here. Choose any finite word with h_t>1, set d_t=h_t-1, and choose a
terminal list z_1,...,z_b of real numbers, b>=2, with mean0 and at
least two distinct entries. The list, b, and sigma may depend on the
whole known word and, on the diagnostic, on m.

For each t choose a rational number p_t in (0,1), write
p_t=A_t/D_t with integers 1<=A_t<D_t, and let q_t=1-p_t. Do not
interpret p_t as an approximate face mass. It is the EXACT count
fraction of a Cartesian address set. Use coordinates labeled by

    omega=(k,j_0,...,j_(n-1)),
    1<=k<=b, 1<=j_t<=D_t,
    N=b product_(t<n) D_t.                                   (13)

Define the fixed branch label H_t by j_t<=A_t and L_t otherwise.
(Branch labels H_t,L_t in this section are not the physical words H_j
or the endpoint magnitudes below.) Define all coordinate levels BEFORE
the forward run by

    w_n(omega)=z_k,
    theta_t=d_t q_t/p_t,
    w_t(omega)=w_(t+1)(omega)-h_t             if label L_t,
    w_t(omega)=h_t q_t/p_t-w_(t+1)(omega)/d_t if label H_t.      (14)

These are finite mathematical definitions, not executed trajectories.
Equivalently put alpha_t=1, b_t=-h_t on L_t, and alpha_t=-1/d_t,
b_t=h_t q_t/p_t on H_t. Then the explicit initial level is

    w_0(omega)=z_k product_(t<n)alpha_t
        +sum_(t<n)b_t product_(r<t)alpha_r.                    (15)

Choose precisely the following guard, and no hidden cone or radius guard:

    max_omega w_(t+1)(omega) < d_t/p_t, EVERY 0<=t<n.           (16)

The domain is nonempty for every terminal list and every word h_t>1.
Starting backward, if R=max w_(t+1)>0, the purely mathematical choice

    p_t=1/[2(ceil(R/d_t)+1)]                                  (17)

is rational, lies in (0,1), and gives the strict guard. This fixes all
parameters before the actual forward run. No p_t, face, or threshold
is changed after observing that run. Every other rational array
satisfying (16) is allowed in the theorem, however uneven or m-dependent.

The actual initial state is x_0=(sigma/N)w_0. The objective is exactly
(5) with the full N-vertex simplex, not a projected or normalized path.

## 5. Full evolution, multilevel gradients, and genuine face returns

All averages below are literal arithmetic means over the full coordinate
set (13). Because w_(t+1) ignores address j_t, every future level occurs
with EXACTLY the fraction p_t of H_t addresses and q_t of L_t addresses.
Thus, if the mean of w_(t+1) is zero, (14) gives mean

    q_t(-h_t)+p_t h_t q_t/p_t=0.

Backward induction gives sum w_t=0 for every t. On the H_t addresses,

    1+w_t-theta_t=1/p_t-w_(t+1)/d_t >0,

and on L_t addresses,

    1+w_t-theta_t=w_(t+1)-d_t/p_t <0.                         (18)

The average positive part is p_t*(1/p_t)=1 because the future mean
is zero. Hence (9) identifies the ACTUAL threshold as theta_t. Substituting
into (12) gives exactly w_(t+1) on BOTH branches. Induction through EVERY
original index proves that (14) is the whole actual forward trajectory.
This proves, rather than prescribes, the active faces.

Every queried height is strictly positive:

    delta_t=(sigma^2/N)d_t q_t/p_t >0, 0<=t<n.                (19)

There are at least two different future coordinate values at each t:
the original terminal list is nonconstant, and either branch in (14)
is injective on future values. At time t the H_t positive projection
values therefore include at least two distinct numbers, while the
L_t coordinates have projection value0. The INITIAL PROJECTION has
at least THREE distinct coordinate levels; in fact this holds at
every queried time. The initial input levels have at least four
distinct values: each branch has at least two, and the strict threshold
separates the two branches. Thus this is not a two-group barycentric line.

For n>=3 each address pattern H_t,L_(t+1),H_(t+2) exists, as do all
other patterns. Its coordinate leaves and then re-enters the active
face, always under positive queried heights. Entire earlier active
subsets can split into active and inactive parts at the next step.
These are actual cap returns on the one objective; no fixed active face,
permanent core, face expectation, or sign absorption is assumed.

## 6. Exact true radius, terminal formula, and the width price

To avoid confusing endpoint magnitudes with the smoothness L, put

    ell_t=-min_omega w_t(omega), r_t=max_omega w_t(omega),
    Wd_t=ell_t+r_t, V_t=(1/N)sum_omega w_t(omega)^2.

Every nonconstant mean-zero state has ell_t,r_t>0. All are finite.
Since the same full future list occurs on both branches, (18) gives

    ell_t=ell_(t+1)+h_t,
    r_t=h_t q_t/p_t+ell_(t+1)/d_t,
    Wd_t=h_t(1/p_t+ell_(t+1)/d_t),
    Wd_t >= (h_t/d_t) Wd_(t+1).                              (20)

Here the LAST inequality uses the guard r_(t+1)<d_t/p_t. To check
the extremes without an ordering assumption, the lowest L_t value is
-ell_(t+1)-h_t. The lowest H_t value is greater than d_t/p_t-h_t,
so the former is the minimum. The greatest H_t value is
h_t q_t/p_t+ell_(t+1)/d_t; it exceeds every L_t value since the
greatest L_t value is less than d_t/p_t-h_t, and their difference
is greater than 1/p_t+ell_(t+1)/d_t. This proves (20).

The exact variance and gradient-norm formulas are

    V_t=(q_t+p_t/d_t^2)V_(t+1)+h_t^2 q_t/p_t,
    G_t:=(N/sigma^2)||g_t||^2=q_t/p_t+p_t V_(t+1)/d_t^2,
    dist(x_0,argmin F)^2=||x_0||^2=(sigma^2/N)V_0.             (21)

Cross terms vanish by the exact mean-zero identity, not by randomness.
An explicit formula for V_0 is

    V_0=V_n product_(t<n) Avar_t
           +sum_(t<n) Bvar_t product_(r<t) Avar_r,
    Avar_t=q_t+p_t/d_t^2, Bvar_t=h_t^2 q_t/p_t.                (22)

At the ACTUAL terminal, let theta_n be the unique solution of

    (1/b)sum_(k<=b)(1+z_k-theta_n)_+=1,
    G_n=(1/b)sum_(k<=b)[(1+z_k-theta_n)_+-1]^2.

Then the exact attained terminal formula on the original static function is

    E(F,h)=(2theta_n+G_n)/V_0.                                (23)

No assumption places this terminal in the quadratic core. Because
F(x)<=max_j<x,v_j>=sigma max_j x_j, one also has

    2theta_n+G_n <= 2r_n.                                    (24)

Thus the formula covers arbitrary terminal offsets, negative tails,
terminal levels, and terminal active sets in the whole declared domain.

For later estimates define the positive finite products

    T_h=product_(t<n)h_t/d_t,
    T_pre=product_(t<n-1)h_t/d_t.

The exact first branching cost can be written

    Bvar_0=h_0 Wd_0-(h_0^2/d_0)(ell_n+S-1).                   (25)

This follows from Wd_0=h_0(1/p_0+ell_1/d_0),
ell_0=ell_n+S, and ell_1+d_0=ell_0-1. In particular it remains
valid for arbitrarily large terminal ell_n. There is no bounded-radius
or bounded-terminal-level assumption.

## 7. Every full-prefix completion and its OWN radius

Let C_pre be the class of ALL finite-dimensional convex differentiable
1-smooth functions K which preserve EVERY queried triple
(x_t,g_t,f_t), 0<=t<n, from the construction and the optimum triple
(0,0,0). Extra Euclidean coordinates are allowed by isometric embedding
of the original vectors. Each K has an attained minimum0. By induction
its GD run reaches the same x_n; its terminal gradient is its OWN
gradient, with no prescribed value.

The class is nonempty because F belongs to it. Accepted1252 gives its
pointwise maximal member on E_N as

    H_pre(v)=||v||^2/2+max(0,max_(t<n)(<y_t,v>-delta_t)),
    F_pre(x)=sup_v(<x,v>-H_pre(v)).                            (26)

All coefficients are fixed by the full old word and old function before
F_pre's own run. As every delta_t>0, the active affine function at0 is
uniquely the zero function; therefore partial H_pre(0)={0}. Equivalently
F_pre(x)=0 iff x=0, since Fenchel equality at v0 is equivalent to
x in partial H_pre(0). Thus its COMPLETE minimum is {0}, its value
is0, and its true initial radius is also sqrt((sigma^2/N)V_0).
It need not be a simplex projection at unqueried points. All ordered
interpolation rows hold for it by accepted1252, including its actual
terminal. A change of function is never made DURING either run.

For an arbitrary K in C_pre, complete the terminal-gradient square in
its ORIGINAL outgoing row Q_(n,n-1)<=0. Because the actual last step
is h_(n-1)=1+d_(n-1), this gives

    2K(x_n) <= 2delta_(n-1)+d_(n-1)^2 ||g_(n-1)||^2
              =(sigma^2/N) U_last,
    U_last=(d^2+2d)q/p+p V_n,                                (27)

where d,p,q refer only to the last index. This does not assume an
old terminal gradient or an old terminal height.

Every number z_k lies in [-ell_n,r_n]. Averaging
(z_k+ell_n)(r_n-z_k)>=0 yields V_n<=ell_n r_n. The last guard
gives p r_n<d. Using h=1+d at that last index, (27) implies

    U_last <= h^2/p+d ell_n
             <= h^2(1/p+ell_n/d)=h Wd_(n-1).                 (28)

Paying each completion's own radius is essential. For ANY of its own
minimizers z, its original initial optimum row gives

    <g_0,x_0-z> >= f_0+||g_0||^2/2=delta_0+||g_0||^2.

Taking the closest such minimizer and using Cauchy--Schwarz proves

    rho_K^2:=dist(x_0,argmin K)^2
       >= (delta_0+||g_0||^2)^2/||g_0||^2
       >= ||g_0||^2+2delta_0
       >= (sigma^2/N)(1+2d_0)q_0/p_0.                       (29)

In particular rho_K is strictly positive. When 0<d_0<1/2,

    (1+2d_0)/h_0^2=1-(d_0/h_0)^2>8/9,
    rho_K^2 > (8/9)(sigma^2/N) Bvar_0.                       (30)

Thus the whole completion class has a paid radius bound, even when
its complete minimum set differs from that of F or F_pre. Pointwise
maximality is NOT used to transfer a radius.

## 9. Direct proof attempts and why the construction does not give a gain

The first attempt was to use all binary face choices, fixed in advance,
to produce real repeated cap returns without a carrier or an assumed
monotone order. Equations (14)--(19) meet that geometric requirement
on the full original physical word, with at least three projection levels.
The terminal expression (23), however, must pay the initial V_0.
The endpoint identity (20) forces a factor h_t/(h_t-1) at EVERY
inverse fold. The many original short leaves therefore impose the
exponential width price (31). The first branch already converts that
price into the radius charge (25), not merely into a rare uncharged
extreme coordinate. This kills the whole allowed parameter domain.

The second attempt kept ALL those positive-height prefix jets and freed
the terminal by using the maximal smooth-convex completion (26).
The exact original last outgoing row bounds its possible gain by (27).
More strongly, (29)--(34) pay the radius separately for every completion,
so allowing another minimizer or additional ambient coordinates cannot
repair this particular prefix. This is a full-prefix completion failure,
not a restatement of scalar symmetry or zero-height annihilation.

No extra law is asserted from merely solving the finite threshold
recurrence. The first requested attained improvement over the whole
K/ray channel was NOT obtained. The original schedule-uniform
all-split B_n comparison remains completely unpaid.

## 1. Claimed scoped conclusion and the unchanged benchmark

For every integer m>=1536 fix the SAME enclosing parameters

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/(4m), c=lambda*(1+1/(4m)),
    a=beta/c, d_j=a*c^j, b_j=1+d_j,
