## 2. One global function, all minima, actual normalization and all rows

The single derivative is alpha_plus*x on the positive ray and alpha_minus*x
on the negative ray, with value0 at0. It is continuous and nondecreasing.
On each ray it is 1-Lipschitz. Across0, for u,v>=0,

    |f'(u)-f'(-v)|=alpha_plus*u+alpha_minus*v<=u+v.

If both curvatures are positive its complete minimum set is{0}. If just one

If both vanish it is all of R and there is no initial point of positive

When the minimum set is a ray, a legitimate initial point lies strictly on

For every actual sample, including the unqueried terminal and every minimizer,
write g_i=f'(x_i), f_i=f(x_i). Use the convention of fact1252b8823bb5a290:

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+g_i*(x_j-x_i)+(g_i-g_j)^2/2.              (2.2)

## 3. Exact two-state composition, including equalities

    s=min({j in[0,m-1]:q*b_j>=1} union{m}).               (3.3)

These are weak crossing thresholds: equality is explicitly included.
Since b_j strictly increases, r<=s. All factors in P_r(p) and P_s(q)
are strictly positive. For any curvature u whose first weak threshold is r<m put

    eta_r(u)=P_r(u)*(u*b_r-1)>=0.                         (3.4)

For a unit initial radius, A_m(F),A_m(S) below are the terminal magnitudes.
The payoff is its squared magnitude times the terminal curvature.

CASE I: r=s=m. There are no crossings or threshold hits at any query:

    A_m(F)=P_m(p), A_m(S)=P_m(q),
    V_F=p*P_m(p)^2, V_S=q*P_m(q)^2.                     (3.5)

Exclude the flat initial sign when its curvature is0, as in Section2.

CASE II: r=s<m. For either starting ray with curvature u, let v be the other
curvature, and put N=2^(m-r-1). Then

    A_m(u)=[eta_r(u)*P_r(v)]^N
                   *product_(j=r+1)^(m-1)(v*b_j-1)^(2^(m-j-1)),
    V_u=v*A_m(u)^2.                                     (3.6)

A nonzero terminal is on the other ray. A zero expression denotes absorption,
not a prescribed nonzero sign. Thus (3.6) remains exact if one curvature is
exactly1/b_r and the other is larger: it does NOT incorrectly declare both
starting signs killed. Only the starting ray whose eta factor is zero dies.

To prove (3.6), all H_r subwords preserve each sign and multiply it by P_r
at that curvature. Contract the notation to the ORIGINAL H_r subwords and
the intervening checkpoints of levels>=r. There are2^(m-r) such subwords
and2^(m-r)-1 checkpoints. Provided the trajectory has not hit zero, the
checkpoints all cross. The level-r checkpoints occupy even zero-based
checkpoint indices, hence all take the starting curvature u. Every higher
checkpoint occupies an odd index and takes v. Half the H_r subwords take
each curvature. A level j occurs2^(m-j-1) times. Multiplying precisely these
factors yields (3.6). If an equality is encountered, its zero factor gives
the same absorbed result; alternatively continuity gives that endpoint.

CASE III: r<s. Define the strictly positive denominator and fixed ratio

    D=P_r(q)*(1-q*b_r), R=eta_r(p)/D>=0,
    K=0 if s=m, and K=2^(m-s)-1 if s<m.                  (3.7)

Then the exact full terminal formulas are

    A_m(S)=|P_m(q)|*R^K,
    A_m(F)=|P_m(q)|*R^(K+1),
    V_S=q*P_m(q)^2*R^(2K),
    V_F=q*P_m(q)^2*R^(2K+2).                            (3.8)

Use R^0=1, also when R=0. Nonzero terminals are on the q ray. If q=0,
the F-start formula can give positive terminal magnitude on the flat ray,
but its objective is exactly0. This does not turn it into a non-minimizer.

For a proof, H_(r+1) sends every surviving starting sign to S, with gains

    A_(r+1)(S)=P_r(q)^2*(1-q*b_r),
    A_(r+1)(F)=eta_r(p)*P_r(q)=R*A_(r+1)(S).             (3.9)

The report-local R in (3.7) is a gain ratio, distinct from the original
performance normalization R=W/2. If Map_j has the constant surviving output
and gain ratio R, applying (3.2)
preserves the same gain ratio. Its S-input gain is squared and multiplied
by |1-q*b_j| if that checkpoint preserves the q sign, and by
R*|1-q*b_j| if it crosses. At equality the whole map is zero. Up to the
first q threshold, its S gain is P_j(q). For all later levels, multiplication
of the factors R with their exact tree multiplicities gives total exponent
sum_(j=s)^(m-1)2^(m-j-1)=2^(m-s)-1. This proves (3.8).
At an equality q*b_s=1, its P_m(q) factor vanishes, so both starts die.
If p*b_r=1, R=0: the F start dies immediately, and the S start dies on its
first excursion to F if one occurs. These cases agree with (3.1).

Equations (3.5),(3.6),(3.8) are exact finite terminal products for ALL curvature
pairs and ALL m in (1.1), not just fixed-parameter limits or a numerical run.
The state map (3.1) also gives every intermediate query and objective:
x_t=sign_t*A_t, g_t=alpha_sign_t*x_t, f_t=alpha_sign_t*A_t^2/2.
Thus it fixes the full actual history and Gram as well as its terminal.

For clarity about the final leaf, if Case II has r>=1, that leaf preserves
the terminal ray v and is already counted inside P_r(v). If r=0 it crosses
from the initial curvature u to v and is included among the level0 factors.
In Case III with r>=1 the final leaf preserves S. If r=0, s>=2 it also
preserves S; if r=0,s=1 a surviving penultimate level1 checkpoint crosses
S to F, and the final leaf crosses F to S. Equality at that penultimate
checkpoint kills the state. All these are physical updates, not truncations
before the leaf. Zero states stay zero in every case.

## 4. Uniform elementary estimates used in the joint proof

We derive every additional bound here rather than importing an unverified
draft. From m>=1536, beta>99/100 and (1.6),

    2/5<a<21/50<1/2, 2<c<5/2, a*c=beta<1,
    c*(c-1)<(121/50)*(71/50)<7/2.                       (4.1)

For example a>(99/100)/(121/50)=99/242>2/5. Also S_1=1+a>d_1=beta,
and the original recurrence gives

    S_(j+1)-d_(j+1)=2(S_j-d_j)+1+(3-c)*d_j>0.

Consequently S_j>d_j for j>=1. Since m>=3, S_(m-1)>3 and

    1+2S_m<2c^m,
    1+2S_m=4S_(m-1)+2b_(m-1)+1<7S_(m-1).              (4.2)

The first inequality uses M_m<=c^m; the second uses b_(m-1)<S_(m-1)+1.

For every j>=2 we will use

    S_j/b_j>7/5,             (S_j-b_0)/b_j>9/10.        (4.3)

At j=2, S_2=3+2a+beta>479/100 and b_2=1+beta*c<171/50, so
S_2/b_2>479/342>7/5 (2395>2394). Also
S_2-b_0=2+a+beta>339/100, so (S_2-b_0)/b_2>339/342>9/10.
For induction b_(j+1)=c*b_j-(c-1)<c*b_j. If S_j>t*b_j then
S_(j+1)>(2t+1)b_j>t*c*b_j for t=7/5, since c<5/2<2+1/t.
If S_j-b_0>t*b_j then S_(j+1)-b_0>(2t+1)b_j+b_0>t*c*b_j
for t=9/10 by the same comparison. This proves both bounds for every j>=2;
no false assertion of monotonicity of S_j/b_j is needed.

If r>=1 and u has first weak threshold r, then
u*b_(r-1)<1<=u*b_r and

    0<=eta_r(u)
       <=(1-u*b_(r-1))*(u*b_r-1)
       <=(b_r-b_(r-1))^2/(4*b_r*b_(r-1))
       <(c-1)^2/(4c)<1/4.                              (4.4)

Indeed all omitted factors of P_r(u) lie in(0,1]; the middle quadratic
has the displayed maximum by completing its square. With t=b_r/b_(r-1),
1<t<c and (t-1)^2/t=t-2+1/t increases for t>1. Finally (c-1)^2<c for
2<c<5/2. If r=0, eta_0(u)=u*b_0-1<=a. Hence in ALL cases

    eta_r(u)<=a; for r>=1 it is <1/4.                   (4.5)

For any pre-threshold scalar block, all its factors belong to(0,1], and
1-z<=exp(-z) for z>=0 gives

    P_j(t)<=exp(-t*S_j).                               (4.6)

Whenever r<s, P_s(q)/D is a product with nonnegative integer exponents
of pre-threshold factors, so it is at most1. It retains a factor
1-q*b_(s-1) when s>=r+2. When s=r+1 it equals P_r(q).
Deleting the factors of D deletes exactly the mass S_r+b_r from P_s.
In particular for r=0 it gives

    P_s(q)/D<=exp(-q*(S_s-b_0)).                        (4.7)

For later use, exp(7/5)>4: its Taylor terms of orders0 through5 already
sum to more than4. Also exp(9/10)>2 by its first three terms, and e>5/2
by its first four terms. These are inequalities between exact series terms,
not floating-point estimates or evaluated mathematical programs.

## 5. Product envelope for all high-level factors

This is an algebraic estimate inside the same joint proof. Suppose a
nonnegative sequence of complete block gains has initial value J at level t
and for subsequent levels is squared and multiplied by factors at most
z*c^ell, ell=0,...,k-1. Expanding the finite product, its final value is at most

    J^(2^k)*z^(2^k-1)*c^(2^k-k-1)
        =J*c^(-k)*(c*z*J)^(2^k-1),        k>=0.          (5.1)

For k=0 the expression is J. The exponent identity follows by induction:
the weighted sum of ell over ell=0,...,k-1 is2^k-k-1. Formula (5.1) involves
no division by J or z and remains valid when either vanishes (0^0=1 only in
the empty-product cases). It is an upper bound for actual products, never
an independently asserted transfer factor.

## 6. Case III with a q threshold: uniformly priced returns

Assume r<s<m. If a threshold equality already gives absorption, the desired
upper bound follows directly. The following formulas also include those
zeros. Set k=m-s>=1, and define

    J_s=P_s(q)*max(1,R),
    E_s=c*R*q*d_s*P_s(q).                               (6.1)

At levels j>=s, 0<=q*b_j-1=q*d_j-(1-q)<=q*d_j. The exact gain recursion
used to prove (3.8), followed by (5.1) with z=R*q*d_s, gives

    max(A_m(F),A_m(S))
        <=J_s*c^(-k)*E_s^(2^k-1).                      (6.2)

Here R is fixed by the two curvatures and their ORIGINAL lower block; it is
not re-chosen at a return. We now price BOTH factors J_s and E_s uniformly.

First,

    E_s<4/5                                             (6.3)

for every r<s. If s>=r+2, put y=q*b_(s-1) in[0,1). By (4.5) and the retained
factor noted after (4.6),

    E_s=c*q*d_s*eta_r(p)*P_s(q)/D
       <=c^2*eta_r(p)*y*(1-y)
       <=c^2*a/4=c*beta/4<5/8<4/5.                     (6.4)

If s=r+1 and r>=1, the ratio P_s/D=P_r(q) retains1-q*b_(r-1). Put
y=q*b_(r-1) in[0,1). Since q*d_s<=c^2*y, (4.4) gives

    E_s<=c^3*eta_r(p)*y*(1-y)
       <=c^2*(c-1)^2/16<49/64<4/5.                    (6.5)

If r=0,s=1, then E_s=c*q*d_1*eta_0(p)<=beta^2*q.
Here q<1/b_0<5/7<4/5, proving (6.3) in the remaining case.

Second, for s>=2,

    J_s<1/4.                                           (6.6)

Indeed q*b_s>=1, so (4.3),(4.6) give P_s(q)<=exp(-S_s/b_s)<exp(-7/5)<1/4.
If r>=1 then R*P_s(q)=eta_r(p)*P_s(q)/D<1/4 by (4.4) and the quotient
bound1. If r=0, (4.3),(4.7) give
R*P_s(q)<=a*exp(-9/10)<a/2<1/4. This proves (6.6).

For s=1,r=0 we instead have J_1=max(1-q*b_0,eta_0(p))<1/2: since
q>=1/b_1, b_1=1+beta<2 and b_0>7/5, its first entry is less than3/10,
and its second is at most a<1/2.

The true terminal objective is q times the squared magnitude. Since
q*b_(s-1)<1, we have q<c/d_s. For s>=2, (4.2),(6.2),(6.3),(6.6) give

    (1+2S_m)*V
      <[c/(8a)]*c^(-k)*(4/5)^(2*(2^k-1))
      <=[1/(8a)]*(16/25)<1/5<1/2.                     (6.7)

The middle expression is decreasing with integer k>=1 because c>1 and
4/5<1; at k=1 it has the stated value. We used a>2/5 in the final inequality.

For s=1 the same calculation using J_1<1/2 gives

    (1+2S_m)*V
      <[c/(2a)]*c^(-k)*(4/5)^(2*(2^k-1)).              (6.8)

Now k=m-1>=2. Its value is at most
(4/5)^6/(2*a*c)=(4/5)^6/(2*beta)<(2/3)*(4/5)^6<1/2.
Thus ALL separated-threshold pairs with a q crossing are covered, including
arbitrary m-dependent r,s,p,q. No bounded-away-from-zero condition on q was used.

## 7. Case II: synchronized thresholds, including both high curvatures

First let r=s=0. Every surviving step crosses; its magnitude multiplier is
at most b_j-1=d_j since both curvatures are at most1. Thus

    A_m(u)<=product_(j=0)^(m-1)d_j^(2^(m-j-1))
           =beta^(2^m-1)*c^(-m).                       (7.1)

The equality follows because the total exponent of a is2^m-1 and that of c
is2^m-m-1, with a*c=beta. Terminal curvature is at most1, hence

    (1+2S_m)*V<2*c^(-m)*beta^(2*(2^m-1))<1/2           (7.2)

for m>=3, which includes every claimed horizon. Threshold hits only reduce
the product to0.

Next let 1<=r=s<m and fix either initial curvature u, other curvature v.
Put t=r+1, k=m-t, J=eta_r(u)*P_r(v), and E=c*v*d_t*J. By (4.4),

    J<1/4.                                             (7.3)

The same y=v*b_(r-1) in[0,1) calculation as (6.5) gives

    E<=c^3*eta_r(u)*y*(1-y)
      <=c^2*(c-1)^2/16<49/64<4/5.                     (7.4)

Notice that v here may be either the larger or smaller curvature. Both lie
in the same threshold interval, which is all this estimate requires.
Using the EXACT product (3.6), all its higher factors are at most v*d_j,
so (5.1) gives A_m(u)<=J*c^(-k)*E^(2^k-1).
Also v<1/b_(r-1)<c^2/d_t. If k>=1, (4.2) yields

    (1+2S_m)*V_u
      <[c^2/(8a)]*c^(-k)*(4/5)^(2*(2^k-1))
      <=[c/(8a)]*(16/25)=2c/(25a)<1/2.                 (7.5)

The last strict bound uses c<5/2 and a>2/5, so its upper endpoint is1/2.
This is uniform even when r and both curvatures depend arbitrarily on m.

If k=0, only the highest-level checkpoint crosses: r=m-1 and the exact
terminal is J. By (4.4),(4.6),

    V_u=v*eta_r(u)^2*P_r(v)^2
        <=(1/16)*v*exp(-2v*S_(m-1))
        <=1/[32e*S_(m-1)].                            (7.6)

The elementary maximum of z*exp(-2Az), z>=0, is1/(2eA) for A>0,
as follows by differentiating; no numerical maximizer is used.
Equation (4.2) makes (1+2S_m)*V_u<7/(32e)<1/2. This completes Case II.

## 8. No q crossing, small curvatures, and all boundary cases

If r=s=m, (3.5),(4.6) and the same exponential maximum give, for either
legitimate initial curvature u,

    V_u<=1/(2e*S_m),
    (1+2S_m)*V_u<7/(6e)<7/15<1/2,                    (8.1)

where S_m>3 and e>5/2 were used. In particular arbitrarily small,
horizon-dependent curvatures are included.

If r<s=m, a start on S has this same bound. For a start on F, (3.8) reads
A_m(F)=eta_r(p)*P_m(q)/D. The quotient deletes from the original product
exactly one copy of H_r and its following b_r, retaining only factors in(0,1].
Since S_r+b_r<=S_(m-1)+b_(m-1), the remaining mass is at least S_(m-1).
Consequently (4.5),(4.6) imply

    A_m(F)<=a*exp(-q*S_(m-1)),
    V_F<=a^2/(2e*S_(m-1)),
    (1+2S_m)*V_F<7a^2/(2e)<7/(8e)<1/2.                (8.2)

For q=0 the actual terminal on S has zero objective, so (8.2) is still valid.
If there is no crossing from the positive-curvature ray, its formula is
instead (3.5) and it remains covered by (8.1). This addresses the entire
nontrivial zero-curvature boundary with its own true closest radius.

The weak-threshold definitions and zero factors in Section3 handle all

## 9. Counterexample screen and exact scope of the limitation

The direct-proving plan first obtains the complete products, then prices the
gain ratio. The tempting shortcut R<=1 is FALSE, so it is not used. For an
exact all-word example choose first physical level b_0=3/2, p=1 and q=3/5.
At that level the F-input magnitude becomes1/2 on S while the S-input
magnitude becomes1/10 on S; hence the ratio is5. Both use the same static
quadratic with curvatures1 and3/5. This tests the shortcut only; it is not
the hierarchy (1.1). The actual proof bounds the combined quantities
J_s=P_s(q)*max(1,R) and E_s, which retain the contraction that a bare R loses.

A second fragile inference is that equality of q*b_r with1 kills BOTH
initial signs in Case II. It need not: at the first H_(r+1), a strictly
crossing u start uses u, not q, at the checkpoint and lands on q only after
it. Formula (3.6) gives eta_r(u)*P_r(q)>0 in that case, while a q start dies.
The state machine and final-leaf checks deliberately preserve this distinction.

Overlapping scalar returns are legal and are not eliminated by our hypotheses.
For example, on f(x)=x^2/4 with physical word(1,6,1,6,1), (2.1) gives
1,1/2,-1,-1/2,1,1/2. The same positive interval is revisited and the same
derivative x/2 is used. This is a simple explanatory example already known
from the previous round; its computation here is a written finite identity,
not a trajectory program, and it is not used to prove the hierarchy bound.

Our limitation rests on homogeneity on EACH ray: a ray's curvature does not
vary with radius, so every H_j is a two-state homogeneous map. Once its two
inputs have the same output ray, their gain ratio freezes. A spatially shifted
or multi-knot fixed derivative can lose both properties; no bound for that
larger class follows. Similarly, this does not merely reapply the prior
disjoint-inward argument: no radial ordering of repeated visits appears in
Sections3--8, and every large step inside every child is retained.

This law is globally legitimate on every nonnegative word by Sections2--3.
No fallback is needed for its feasibility. A positive general-word witness
exists within it by choosing p=q=1/[2*(1+sum h)], starting from1: all
multipliers are positive and the objective is positive. This elementary
existence observation supplies no exact-profile lower strength. On the

# Paid short-leaf pairs and uniform dyadic fans on the original space

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical draft, worker max79. The original target is OPEN.
This is one bounded invocation under TASK.md and guidance29dd9d75f3f7d055:
two explicit coefficient laws, zero mathematical programs, numerical replay,
formal submissions or subagents. No statement below is a newly accepted fact.
All new identities and failure arguments are derived together, not used as
independently accepted intermediate results.

The two proposed additions genuinely change the Huber contact derivative.
Their entire initial/common Schur charge is displayed, with one global
objective allowance. Nevertheless an ORIGINAL H4 block direction annihilates
every adjacent short-leaf pair and gives a nonpositive sum at each uniform
dyadic fan. Its inherited base action is strictly negative. Thus neither law
is PSD at the requested level, or at any other objective level. The same
calculation covers arbitrary nonnegative weights in the specified additive
support classes. It does not cover a changed base, signed reallocations,
nonuniform within-cell fan weights, or the unrestricted full dual.

## 1. Original target and exact accepted scopes

For every integer n>=0 and word h in [0,infinity)^n, W_n(h) is the supremum
of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over all finite-dimensional real
Euclidean spaces, convex differentiable L-smooth functions with an attained
minimizer x_star, and x_0!=x_star. The original physical updates are
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i), where L>0. Thus W=2R.

The ORIGINAL benchmark is C_0=B_0=1 and

    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n)Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

All splits are integers. The target asks whether
lim_n B_n inf_(h in [0,infinity)^n)W_n(h)=1; an affirmative lower statement
requires, for every eta>0, a word-independent N_eta such that every actual
n>=N_eta and every such word has B_n W_n(h)>=1-eta.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original interpolation convention,
the full independent-vector certificate, and exact terminal completion.
Accepted fact04219554e41d9750 supplies its stated primitive/objective
composition identities and benchmark, not an unconditional primitive seed.
Only the benchmark conclusion of fact5fd396eba75651e7, Section10, is used:

    B_(2^m-1)/D_m<237/250 for every m>=1536, tau=1/4.       (1)

Here D_m and the SAME-enclosing-m word are defined in Section2. A full-class
bound W_(2^m-1)(H_m)<=21/(20D_m) would therefore imply
B_n W_n(H_m)<4977/5000 on unbounded ACTUAL horizons. This draft does not
obtain that bound. A failed certificate supplies no upper or lower bound on W.

## 2. Fixed physical hierarchy

Fix m>=1536 throughout and set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c, tstar=1/lambda,
    Hword_0=(), Hword_(j+1)=(Hword_j,1+d_j,Hword_j), d_j=a*c^j,
    n_j=2^j-1, A_j=1+sum Hword_j, S_j=A_j-1,
    D_j=2A_j-1, t_j=d_j/A_j, h=H_m=Hword_m, n=n_m, D=D_m.

Every child retains this enclosing epsilon. In original indices,
h_i=1+a*c^level(i), where level(i) is the largest integer l with
2^l dividing i+1, for 0<=i<n. In particular every even query has
physical step b=1+a. The index n is the unqueried terminal; set h_n=0
only as notation in matrix formulas. No terminal step is executed.

The exact scalar identities, which are not executed recurrences, are

    A_j=v_h*c^j+(1-v_h)*2^j, v_h=a/(c-2),
    A_(j+1)=(2+t_j)A_j, t_(j+1)=c*t_j/(2+t_j).

They follow by summing the physical concatenation and solving its geometric
sum. Since c(c-2)>1>beta, one has 0<v_h<1. Consequently t_j increases
strictly and 0<t_j<c-2<1/2. For the final inequality,
lambda<17/7 and epsilon<=1/6144 imply c<5/2.
Direct substitution gives

    b=sqrt(2)-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)],
    A_1=lambda-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)], d_1=1-epsilon,
    A_2=lambda^2-epsilon[1+4/(lambda(1+epsilon))],
    d_2=lambda(1-epsilon^2),
    lambda*d_2-A_2
      =epsilon[1+4/(lambda(1+epsilon))-lambda^2 epsilon]>0. (2)

## 3. Every inherited primitive and objective coefficient

The inherited array is rederived here. Its prior unverified reports are
awareness, not premises. A primitive depth-j array Lambda^j has indices
0,...,n_j. Start with Lambda^0=0 and zero diagonal. At a depth-(j+1)
node, put p=n_j, z=n_(j+1). Embed the left Lambda^j with factor1 and
the right Lambda^j with factor k_j. For each nonterminal right query i add

    Lambda_(i,p) += u_j h_i, Lambda_(i,z) += v_j h_i,
    Lambda_(z,p) += w_j,    Lambda_(p,z) += z_j,
    u_j=2lambda,
    v_j=[2lambda*d_j+2(A_j+d_j)]/A_j,

    w_j=4A_j+2d_j-2lambda(A_j-1), z_j=2A_j.           (3)

All unspecified contributions are zero and overlapping ones are summed.
Equivalently, for every dyadic node of depth l+1 and offset o=k*2^(l+1),
write its indicated four local original-index row contributions from (3).
Multiply each by the product of k_r over strict ancestors whose right child
contains that node, and sum over nodes. This is a finite sum/product formula

## 4. Full polynomial identities for the base

    ||x_p||^2/Dp+2(S_j/Dp-s_j)<x_p,g_p>
    +(S_j^2/Dp+2s_j)||g_p||^2-theta_j<x_p,T_R>
    +(1+d_j-s_j)<g_p,T_R>+Dc||T_R||^2/4.

Expanding the two squares agrees because
s_j(3S_j+2(1+d_j))=S_j+1+d_j. Neither Rchild nor kappa_j is assumed
nonnegative for the deformed hierarchy.

At the full Huber contact tuple x_0=D_j, g_i=1, every square argument
and each Y,Z in (6) is zero. Induction from Mbase_0=||x_0-g_0||^2
also makes the derivative of Rchild zero at its common-gradient vector.
Thus, writing e=(1,...,1),

    Cbase e=D mu/2, e^T Cbase e=D.                     (8)

For the actual m>=1536 (indeed m>=2), one useful original entry is
Cbase_00=2/D, with mu_0=2b/D: only the
first primitive depth1 term (2-b^2)||g_0-g_1||^2 contributes to the first
gradient diagonal in the left source, and the x_p square contributes b^2/D.
These statements are jointly derived here, not imported from the last report.

## 5. The two explicit additions and every final sign

The physical non-leaf checkpoints are the odd indices p<n. If level(p)=l,
then 1<=l<=m-1 and p=o+2^l-1 for a unique cell offset
o=k*2^(l+1), 0<=k<2^(m-l-1). Define the complete cell of original
gradient indices as o,...,o+2^(l+1)-1, and its short-leaf set

    E_(l,o)={o,o+2,...,o+2^(l+1)-2}.

These are actual even queried indices; every one has h_i=b. No terminal
gradient is a member of a leaf set or checkpoint set.

LAW A, preceding leaf. For each non-leaf p of level l put

    omega_p=epsilon*A_l^2/D,
    J^A_(p-1,p)=J^A_(p,p-1)=omega_p.                  (9)

LAW B, whole-cell fan. For each (l,o) and p=o+2^l-1 put

    gamma_(l,o)=epsilon*A_l^2/(D*2^l),
    J^B_(i,p) += gamma_(l,o), J^B_(p,i) += gamma_(l,o)
                         for every i in E_(l,o).      (10)

All other entries of J are zero and all stated contributions are summed.
The two laws are different supports, not two fits of the old optimum-row
transport. The factor 2^l makes their total added mass identical at every
scale, allowing a direct comparison without silently increasing a budget.
For either law the FINAL original coefficients are

    K_ij=Kbase_ij+J_ij (i!=j), K_ii=0,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i, lambda_(star,i)=0,
    q=21/(20D).                                      (11)

All final multipliers are nonnegative. Symmetry J_ij=J_ji preserves every
value-flow equation (5). The optimum profile is fixed as a deliberate
restriction of these two laws; no claim is made that a general slack-spending
construction may be reduced to this restriction. No decrement is hidden.

Each law has the ONE entire-word multiplier-mass account

    T79=(epsilon/D)sum_(l=1)^(m-1)2^(m-l-1)A_l^2,
    sum_(i!=j)J_ij=2T79.                             (12)

This is not a sufficient PSD budget. The actual global objective/contact
budget, including all cross terms between cells, is given next.

## 6. Every full entry, the changed contact, and its ONE Schur budget

For ANY array of the form (11) define out_i=mu_i+sum_v K_iv. The entire
matrix C in

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-sum_i mu_i<x_0,g_i>
                       +sum_(i,j)C_ij<g_i,g_j>

has entries

    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i sum_(v>i)K_iv,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j sum_(v>j)K_iv
                         +h_i[mu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j. (13)

The complete original matrix therefore has initial entry q and initial
mixed entries -mu_i/2. To derive (13), flow says half the incident row mass
equals out_i-1_(i=n). A forward row sourced at i contributes -h_i K_iv
to its diagonal. For i<j the difference squares give -(K_ij+K_ji),
rows out of i ending after j give the second term, and rows out of j ending
at/before i or at the optimum give the last term. This also accounts for
every physical intermediate gradient in a nonlocal pair.

For an unordered pair represented by u<v let L_uv(g)=sum_(t=u)^(v-1)h_t g_t
and ell_uv=Ppos_v-Ppos_u. The exact added polynomial per unit weight is

    Q_uv+Q_vu=||g_u-g_v||^2-<g_u-g_v,L_uv(g)>
             =<g_u-g_v,y_v-y_u>.                     (14)

For v=u+1 across b this is
(1-b)||g_u||^2+(b-2)<g_u,g_v>+||g_v||^2. Its determinant is -b^2/4,
so it is indefinite whenever b>0. It is not a free PSD correction.

At g=e the value of (14) is zero, but its gradient is
ell_uv(e_v-e_u). Consequently define the entire contact-defect column

    d79=(1/2)sum_(unordered {u,v},u<v)J_uv*ell_uv*(e_v-e_u).

Here e_i denotes the standard coordinate column, distinct from e. Then

    Ce=D mu/2+d79, e^T d79=0, e^T C e=D.              (15)

For A the formula is d79=(b/2)sum_p omega_p(e_p-e_(p-1)). For B it is
(1/2)sum_(l,o)gamma_(l,o)sum_(i in E_(l,o))(Ppos_p-Ppos_i)(e_p-e_i),
with signed Ppos_p-Ppos_i valid on both sides of the checkpoint. Each is one
finite original-index vector, not separate contact credits. Both are nonzero:

    Ppos^T d79=(1/2)sum_(u<v)J_uv(Ppos_v-Ppos_u)^2>0.           (16)

All physical steps are positive and each law has a positive added edge.
Thus Ce=D mu/2 is NOT assumed; it is false for both candidates.

At x_0=D,g=e the complete value is (qD-1)D=D/20. Its initial/common
two-by-two block is

    Bcommon=[[q,-1],[-1,D]], det Bcommon=qD-1=1/20.

This is the ONE scalar allowance for the whole word. Write arbitrary
gradients as g=t e+v with e^T v=0, first in one real coordinate and then
coordinatewise in a Euclidean space. Set u=mu^T v and z=d79^T v. Their
mixed column with (x_0,t) is (-u/2,Du/2+z). Exact inversion gives

    (-u/2,Du/2+z) Bcommon^(-1) (-u/2,Du/2+z)^T
       =D u^2/4+u z+[q/(qD-1)]z^2
       =D u^2/4+u z+21z^2/D.                        (17)

For clarity the numerator before dividing by qD-1 is
D(qD-1)u^2/4+(qD-1)uz+qz^2. Thus all contact, common-gradient and
initial costs have been charged exactly once. In particular the last term
is the square of the WHOLE sum d79^T v and includes all cross-cell terms.
It cannot be paid anew from 1/20 at every node.

Equivalently, the entire remaining gradient matrix is

    R79=C-D mu mu^T/4-(mu d79^T+d79 mu^T)/2
                                      -(21/D)d79 d79^T,
    R79 e=0.                                        (18)

Full PSD at q=21/(20D) is equivalent to R79 being PSD on the entire
e-perpendicular space, or equivalently on all gradient coordinates since
R79 e=0. Equations (17)--(18) are a necessary-and-sufficient expenditure
identity, NOT a claim that either law pays it successfully. The direct
negative full-polynomial test below disproves that claim.

## 7. Actual terminal-square expenditure

Neither added support touches n. The final incoming-terminal coefficients
remain zero by the explicit formulas, not by deleting rows from a supplied
certificate. Full terminal flow is therefore sum_j lambda_(n,j)=2 and
C_nn=1. More explicitly the receivers are star and the right-spine bridges

    p_l=2^m-2^l-1, 0<=l<m,
    alpha_star=product_(v=0)^(m-1)theta_v,
    alpha_(p_l)=s_l product_(v=0)^(l-1)theta_v.        (19)

An empty product is1. All other alpha_i are zero. The finite telescoping
identity sum_l s_l product_(v<l)theta_v=1-product_(v<m)theta_v shows these
are probabilities. They are exactly lambda_(n,j)/2 from (4), including
the adjacent final bridge p_0=n-1. No unqueried gradient is discarded.

The exact vector in the terminal square is

    Vterm=alpha_star x_0
         -sum_(t<n)[h_t w_t-(w_t-w_(t-1))]g_t,
    w_(-1)=alpha_star, w_t=alpha_star+sum_(i=0)^t alpha_i.

The complete remainder is

    M(q)=||g_n-Vterm||^2+Rprefix,
    Rprefix=q||x_0||^2-2sum_(j in {star,0,...,n-1})alpha_j
                    (f_j-||g_j||^2/2)-||Vterm||^2
                  +sum_(i!=j in {star,0,...,n-1})lambda_ij Q_ij. (20)

The prefix flow cancels every f_j. Formula (20) follows by expanding the
terminal rows, as in
fact1252b8823bb5a290(c), and retains the actual negative square cost.
Equivalently put vterm=(mu_n/2)x_0-sum_(i<n)C_in g_i; then Vterm=vterm
and Rprefix=q||x_0||^2-sum_(i<n)mu_i<x_0,g_i>
+sum_(i,j<n)C_ij<g_i,g_j>-||vterm||^2.
Since the added rows contain no terminal gradients, they do not alter
C_in or vterm. They add their FULL (14) expressions to Rprefix.

## 8. Original-space block direction and its complete base action

Put

    W79=A_2+d_2, Bfirst=b+1+d_1,
    Edef=(t_2-tstar)A_2^2(lambda+t_2)>0,
    delta3=t_3-tstar>0.

W79 is the physical mass of steps0,...,3 and of steps8,...,11.
The notation is local and does not replace W_n(h). In the ENTIRE original
formal space assign scalar values

    x_0=0,
    g_i=1 for i=0,1,2,3;
    g_i=-1 for i=8,9,10,11;
    g_i=0 for every other i=0,...,n.                 (21)

The two active four-step blocks have identical physical words. Hence the
total displacement is W79-W79=0. All positions from index12 onward are0;
g_7=g_15=g_n=0. These are chosen test values, not equality constraints
on formal coordinates and not a legal primal trajectory.

In the first H3, its left H2 gradients are all1, its right H2 all0,
so both child Psrc terms vanish by (6), and Y=0,Z=1 gives -Edef.
The H3 beginning at8 gives the same -Edef. At their H4 join,
Y=-W79,Z=0. Thus the COMPLETE source polynomial is

    Psrc_4=-(1+k_3)Edef-delta3(lambda+1)W79^2<0.     (22)

For every containing source ancestor all its right gradients, bridge and
terminal are zero, so Y=Z=0 and (6) propagates exactly (22), with left

    Mbase(q;21)=Psrc_4/D<0 for EVERY real q.           (23)

No positive-epsilon primitive child or quotient feasibility has been used.
The parameter signs came from the exact SAME-m (2).

## 9. Law A: every preceding-leaf symmetric pair vanishes

Every edge in (9) connects an even index to the next odd index. Assignment
(21) is constant on every such pair, including pairs outside its support.
Thus g_(p-1)-g_p=0 and its ENTIRE (14) polynomial is zero. All preceding
gradient costs and cross terms cancel exactly; no diagonal-only inference
is involved. Summing every added pair gives

    M_A(q;21)=Mbase(q;21)=Psrc_4/D<0.                 (24)

This proves a stronger, precise scope: for the fixed inherited base, ANY
nonnegative weights omega_p on this support fail for every q. Allowing
different scale laws, horizon dependence, arbitrary magnitudes or zero
weights cannot change (24). The new support is not a repair of the earlier
H4 defect. This is a formal PSD obstruction, not an interpolable witness.

## 10. Law B: every full-cell fan has nonpositive action

For a cell define its UNWEIGHTED full polynomial

    F_(l,o)=sum_(i in E_(l,o))<g_i-g_p,y_p-y_i>, p=o+2^l-1.

Then M_B-Mbase=sum_(l,o)gamma_(l,o)F_(l,o), with no omitted rows.
We evaluate every nonzero cell on (21), including cells whose checkpoint
is zero but whose source leaves are nonzero.

At l=1 each cell comprises four consecutive gradient indices; (21) is
constant on that cell. Its fan is zero. At l=2 only the cells o=0 and
o=8 can contribute. For o=0, p=3 has gradient1. The left leaves0,2 have
the same gradient and contribute zero. The right leaves4,6 have gradient0,

    F_(2,0)=F_(2,8)=-2d_2<0.                        (25)

At l=3 only the first cell is active, with p=7, g_p=0 and y_p=-W79.
Its nonzero source leaves are0,2,8,10. Their original proximal positions

    1-W79, 1-W79+Bfirst, 1, 1+Bfirst.

Their sum is 4-2W79+2Bfirst. Since
W79=2b+2+d_1+d_2 and Bfirst=b+1+d_1, this is

    F_(3,0)=-2(b+d_2-1)<0.                          (26)

The positive terms1 and1+Bfirst have been explicitly paid by the negative

whose sum is again -2(b+d_2-1). Every other source and checkpoint has

All cells not listed are either disjoint from the support or were covered
by the constant-cell calculation. Hence the ENTIRE added value is

    M_B(q;21)-Mbase(q;21)
      =-2d_2[gamma_(2,0)+gamma_(2,8)]
       -2(b+d_2-1)sum_(l=3)^(m-1)gamma_(l,0)<0.      (27)

law or extra search. Arbitrary unequal within-cell weights are NOT covered.

                              +(3-2b)||g_0-g_1||^2/4.

# Paid short-leaf pairs and uniform dyadic fans on the original space

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical draft, worker max79. The original target is OPEN.
This is one bounded invocation under TASK.md and guidance29dd9d75f3f7d055:
two explicit coefficient laws, zero mathematical programs, numerical replay,
formal submissions or subagents. No statement below is a newly accepted fact.
All new identities and failure arguments are derived together, not used as
independently accepted intermediate results.

The two proposed additions genuinely change the Huber contact derivative.
Their entire initial/common Schur charge is displayed, with one global
objective allowance. Nevertheless an ORIGINAL H4 block direction annihilates
every adjacent short-leaf pair and gives a nonpositive sum at each uniform
dyadic fan. Its inherited base action is strictly negative. Thus neither law
is PSD at the requested level, or at any other objective level. The same
calculation covers arbitrary nonnegative weights in the specified additive
support classes. It does not cover a changed base, signed reallocations,
nonuniform within-cell fan weights, or the unrestricted full dual.

## 1. Original target and exact accepted scopes

For every integer n>=0 and word h in [0,infinity)^n, W_n(h) is the supremum
of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over all finite-dimensional real

## 3. Every inherited primitive and objective coefficient

The inherited array is rederived here. Its prior unverified reports are

    Lambda_(i,p) += u_j h_i, Lambda_(i,z) += v_j h_i,
    Lambda_(z,p) += w_j,    Lambda_(p,z) += z_j,
    u_j=2lambda,

    w_j=4A_j+2d_j-2lambda(A_j-1), z_j=2A_j.           (3)

The last two additions occur once per node, not once per right query.
All unspecified contributions are zero and overlapping ones are summed.
Equivalently, for every dyadic node of depth l+1 and offset o=k*2^(l+1),
write its indicated four local original-index row contributions from (3).
Multiply each by the product of k_r over strict ancestors whose right child
contains that node, and sum over nodes. This is a finite sum/product formula
for EVERY Lambda^j entry, without an optimizer or a computed recurrence.

All signs are positive: w_j=2lambda+2(d_j-A_j/lambda)>2lambda for j>=2;

show that divergence is -2h_i at every primitive nonterminal and 2S_j

# Independent audit of the frozen benchmark package

Auditor: max4, invocation 77. Status: UNVERIFIED independent mathematical review.
Verdict: no_gap_found_at_declared_scope.
This verdict is not verifier acceptance and is not a resolution of the original minimax problem.

Frozen source: DRAFT_UNVERIFIED.md in this directory.
SHA256: 34ea5110540b43c7598efb96dc5692a5ce93ab5594199bf9af0052f4be65cf4a.
The source was read in full and has not been edited.

## Scope and dependency audit

I checked all three assertions together: both all-n/all-split power envelopes;
the same-enclosing-m hierarchy ratio for every integer m>=1536; and the
conditional 799/800 implication. The full-function upper 17/(16D_m) is NOT
proved and is NOT an input fact. The statement's last assertion is an implication
with precisely that hypothesis.

The permitted accepted fact b98bb807d514e80d was read in full. It identifies the
original mass recurrences and W normalization. None of its coarse estimates is
needed. In particular, neither 04219554e41d9750's saved endpoints nor the earlier
unverified envelope 48010339bbfbce4f is a proof premise. Fact search produced
no duplicate of this complete package. Broad initial memory queries were
truncated; the full controlling guidance f6b7cc9ddb9c8d02 and needed inputs were
then obtained in bounded reads. An rg search for local skill files returned no
matches (exit 1); it was not a mathematical failure.

A Matlas query about the primitive power inequality returned two unrelated
theorems (1609.04774 Theorem 2.5 and 1703.09411 Lemma 3.4). Neither is used.
A web terminology search distinguished convexity in log coordinates from
ordinary log-convexity; no source theorem enters the proof. The full calculation
is provided below and in PROOF.md. No external_refs entry is needed.

## Independent attack: normalization and final implication first

For every finite nonnegative word h, W_n(h) is the supremum of twice the
objective gap divided by L times the squared distance to the chosen minimizer.
Removing that numerator factor defines R_n(h), so W_n(h)=2R_n(h).
W_n_star is the infimum over all such words, and therefore
W_n_star<=W_n(H_m) at n=2^m-1. Multiplication is by B_n>0, since U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.
Thus an upper estimate for B_n, combined with a lower estimate for D_m, gives
the required UPPER ratio B_n/D_m. The direction is correct.

Under the stated unproved hypothesis, the resulting ratio is strictly below
(17/16)(47/50)=799/800 for every integer m>=1536. Since 2^m-1 is an unbounded
sequence of actual integer horizons, the liminf over all horizons is at most
799/800. This requires no existence of a global limit and no supremum exchange.
There is no unconditional conclusion about W_n(H_m).

## Independent attack: same-m mass and endpoint m=1536

Every bridge 1+a*c^j is positive: epsilon=1/(4m) lies in (0,1/6144],
beta=1-epsilon>0, c=lambda(1+epsilon)>lambda>2, and a=beta/c>0.
Concatenation gives length(H_j)=2^j-1, S_0=0, and
S_(j+1)=2S_j+1+a*c^j. Hence A_j=1+S_j satisfies
A_(j+1)=2A_j+a*c^j, A_0=1.

Let v=a/(c-2). Substituting (1-v)2^j+v*c^j into the recurrence gives
2(1-v)2^j+(2v+a)c^j, which is the proposed next term because
2v+a=cv. The initial value is 1. Since lambda(lambda-2)=1 and c>lambda,
c(c-2)>1; consequently 0<v<1. This proves A_m>=v*c^m without changing m at
any child.

The denominator expansion is
c(c-2)=1+2(lambda+1)epsilon+lambda^2 epsilon^2.
The bounds lambda<5/2 and lambda^2=2lambda+1<6 give
v>(1-epsilon)/(1+7epsilon+6epsilon^2).
The comparison to 1-8epsilon follows by multiplying the positive denominator:
(1-8epsilon)(1+7epsilon+6epsilon^2)
=1-epsilon-50epsilon^2-48epsilon^3<1-epsilon.
All factors used when multiplying lower bounds are positive for m>=1536.

Keeping only the first three nonnegative binomial terms gives
(1+1/(4m))^m>=41/32-1/(32m). Also 2^m>m for every integer m>=1
(by induction), hence lambda^(-m)<1/m. Expansion of the resulting product is
2(1-2/m)(41/32-1/(32m))-1/m
=41/16-99/(16m)+1/(8m^2).
Discarding the last positive term gives a strict lower bound. At m=1536,
41/16-99/24576=(62976-99)/24576=20959/8192.
The cross products are 20959*47=985073 and 8192*120=983040.
Their difference is 2033>0. The endpoint is included; no eventual unspecified
threshold was substituted. Together with B_(2^m-1)<=(12/5)lambda^m this proves
the strict ratio 47/50 with the correct direction.

## Independent attack: primitive envelope

First lambda^3=7+5sqrt(2)>14 because (7/5)^2<2.
Thus lambda^15>14^5=537824>524288=2^19, and rho>19/15>1.

For t>0 set E(t)=(1+t)^rho-1>0 and Q(z)=log E(exp z).
Writing t=exp z gives
Q'(z)=rho*t*(1+t)^(rho-1)/E(t).
Differentiating once more and collecting the numerator gives
Q''(z)=rho*t*(1+t)^(rho-2)
 *[(1+rho*t)E(t)-rho*t*(1+t)^rho]/E(t)^2
=rho*t*(1+t)^(rho-2)
 *[(1+t)^rho-1-rho*t]/E(t)^2.
The bracket has value zero at t=0 and strictly positive derivative for t>0,
so Q is convex. Its midpoint inequality at z and -z yields
E(t)E(1/t)>=(2^rho-1)^2=2.

For positive x,y and T=(x^(1/rho)+y^(1/rho))^rho, multiplication gives
(T-x)(T-y)>=2xy. Equivalently T^2-(x+y)T-xy>=0.
Its negative root is strictly negative and T>0, so T>=Omega(x,y).
If x=0 or y=0, the asserted inequality is equality directly; at x=y=0 both
sides vanish. No use of log 0 or division by 0 is needed.
Omega is coordinatewise nondecreasing on the closed nonnegative quadrant
because both its linear part and the polynomial under its square root are.
Induction uses k+1 and n-k, both positive for every allowed integer split,
whose sum is n+1. The n=0 case is equality.

## Independent attack: sharper scalar inequality and global maximum

It suffices to use p=19/30 in (5/6)x^(2p)+(1-x)^p<=1 because the bases are
in [0,1] and p>0. Endpoint powers are well-defined including base zero.
Let Psi(x)=(5/6)x^(19/15)+(1-x)^(19/30).
Its derivative on (0,1) is
(19/18)x^(4/15)-(19/30)(1-x)^(-11/30).
A critical point therefore satisfies
x^(4/15)(1-x)^(11/30)=3/5,
equivalently x^8(1-x)^11=(3/5)^30.

The logarithmic derivative of x^8(1-x)^11 is
(8-19x)/(x(1-x)); it is negative on (8/19,1).
For x>=2/3 the left side is at most 2^8/3^19. The strict comparison to the
critical value follows from the exact integer identities
2^8*5^30=238418579101562500000000
<239299329230617529590083=3^49.
These are integer products, not a floating point approximation. The powers
can be checked by successive integer multiplication, for example from
5^10=9765625, 3^10=59049 and 3^9=19683. No program was run for them.
Thus every critical point lies strictly below 2/3.

Substituting the derivative relation gives the exact critical value
g(x)=(1-x/2)/(1-x)^(11/30).
Its logarithmic derivative is
-1/(2-x)+11/[30(1-x)]
=(19x-8)/[30(1-x)(2-x)].
It decreases then increases on [0,2/3], so its maximum there is at an endpoint.
g(0)=1 and g(2/3)^30=2^30/3^19<1, since
2^30=1073741824<1162261467=3^19.
Psi is continuous on [0,1], differentiable in its interior, with endpoint
values 1 and 5/6. Even though the derivative is singular at x=1, an interior
maximum must be critical and endpoints are checked separately. This exhausts
the possible maximizers without assuming how many critical points exist.

## Independent attack: dominant induction

For x,y>=0,
sqrt(G(x,y))=(sqrt(y)+sqrt(y+8x))/2.
Squaring proves this identity. The expression is the larger nonnegative root
of z^2-sqrt(y)z-2x=0, and is positive unless both x and y vanish.
For a positive trial z, nonnegativity of this polynomial puts z above that
root; the other root is nonpositive. G is coordinatewise nondecreasing.

Set kappa=12/5. At every split, A=k+1>=1, F=n-k>=1, N=A+F=n+1.
The trial z=sqrt(kappa)N^(rho/2) has nonnegative root polynomial exactly when
(2/kappa)(A/N)^rho+(F/N)^(rho/2)<=1.
This is the scalar inequality with p=rho/2>19/30. Strong induction on B_n,
using the already established C bound, controls each split and hence its
full maximum. B_0=1<=12/5 is included.

## Editorial changes authorized for the new package

The new statement expands W_n_star and R_n and the full objective class.
The proof uses E_be,Q_be,Psi_be,g_be,A_be_j,v_be,kappa_be for local auxiliaries
to avoid clashes with unrelated project glossary entries. H_j, S_j, a and c
are explicitly local hierarchy notation. Positive-root endpoint language is
made precise: a root at (0,0) is nonnegative, not strictly positive.
The derivative calculations, signs, finite-horizon n=0 case, positivity of
every multiplying factor, and subsequence liminf argument are expanded.
These are editorial expansions, not changed constants, quantifiers, hypotheses,
or conclusions. No weakened statement is proposed.

No mathematical program, numerical/arithmetic replay, trajectory or recurrence
execution, optimizer, solver, benchmark DP, installation, paid consult, or
subagent was used. Administrative reading, hashing, JSON serialization and
receipt handling are separate from the mathematical reasoning.

Choose integers r>=1 and q>=r; both may depend on the whole word. Put
N=3r+q. Partition the original N coordinates into three groups G_1,G_2,G_3
of size r and a remaining set I of size q. Choose any real sigma>0. Write
u_N=(1/N,...,1/N) and use the Euclidean subspace

    E_N={x in R^N: sum_l x_l=0}.

There are exactly N fixed real slopes, all offsets zero:

    s_l=sigma(e_l-u_N), 1<=l<=N,
    D=conv{s_l:1<=l<=N},
    F(x)=max_(g in D) [<x,g>-||g||^2/2], x in E_N.           (3)

Their exact Gram matrix is

    <s_l,s_k>=sigma^2(1_(l=k)-1/N).                          (4)

The function does not change during the run. The maximization in (3) is
over the entire convex hull, not merely over the original vertices. The
original affine dictionary is max_l <s_l,x>, with all its offsets zero;
(3) is the fixed quadratic smoothing used throughout this report.

Existence of a maximizing g follows from compactness of D; strict concavity
of the quadratic gives uniqueness. Completing the square identifies g as
the Euclidean projection of x onto D. Its exact condition is

    <x-g,v-g><=0 for every v in D.                            (5)

For two inputs x,x', sum the two corresponding inequalities to obtain
<x-x',g-g'> >= ||g-g'||^2. Hence ||g-g'||<=||x-x'||. Evaluating (3) at
each other's maximizers gives a nonnegative first-order remainder bounded
above by <x'-x,g'-g>, hence by ||x'-x||^2. Therefore F is differentiable,
convex, finite everywhere, and grad F=g is 1-Lipschitz. Convexity also
follows directly by taking the supremum of the affine functions in (3).

Zero is in the relative interior of D in E_N. Indeed a centered vector w
with every w_l> -sigma/N belongs to D because w/sigma+u_N has positive
entries summing to one. Thus for any x!=0, a sufficiently small t in (0,1)
satisfies tx in D and

    F(x)>=(t-t^2/2)||x||^2>0.

Since F(0)=0, the COMPLETE minimum set is exactly {0}. The smoothness
constant is exactly 1, since grad F(x)=x in a neighborhood of zero.
Set f=L F for general L>0. The original GD update then uses grad F and
the same original h. The OWN closest-minimum radius is ||x_0||.

The subspace E_N is an ordinary Euclidean space of dimension N-1, not a
variable metric. An explicit orthonormal basis is
(e_1+...+e_k-k e_(k+1))/sqrt(k(k+1)), 1<=k<N; its coordinates identify
(3) with a function on R^(N-1) without altering any inner product.

## 3. The two-dimensional transverse triangle and exact metric

Let U=G_1 union G_2 union G_3 and define the actual face barycenter

    c_face=sigma(1_U/(3r)-u_N),
    alpha^2=||c_face||^2=sigma^2 q/(3rN), b=sigma/sqrt(r).

Define T={z in R^3:z_1+z_2+z_3=0} and its centered triangle

    K=conv{e_j-(1,1,1)/3:1<=j<=3}
     ={z in T:z_j>=-1/3 for every j}.

The isometry J:T->E_N puts z_j/sqrt(r) on every coordinate of G_j and
zero on I. It is orthogonal to c_face. Thus

    ||R c_face+b Jz||^2=alpha^2 R^2+b^2||z||^2,
    kappa=b^2/alpha^2=3N/q<=12.                              (6)

The last inequality uses exactly the law's count condition q>=r. It is not
an estimate valid for all possible group counts.

For z in T, let tau be the unique real number satisfying

    sum_(j=1)^3 (z_j+1/3-tau)_+=1.

Set p_j=(z_j+1/3-tau)_+ and v=p-(1,1,1)/3. At tau=0 the left side
is at least sum_j(z_j+1/3)=1, so tau>=0. The residual z-v has value tau
on every positive-p coordinate and at most tau on every zero-p coordinate,
and its sum is zero. Therefore <z-v,w-v><=0 for every w in K. This proves
v=P_K(z), including all boundary cases, without a projection black box.
Define

    Phi(z)=<z,v>-||v||^2/2.

The same calculation as (3)-(5) makes Phi a convex 1-smooth function with
gradient v. The residual identities give

    Phi(z)-||v||^2/2=<z-v,v>=tau.                            (7)

For z in K, v=z, tau=0 and 2Phi(z)=||z||^2<=2/3. The last bound follows
by convexity of squared norm and the squared norm 2/3 of each vertex.

For ANY R>=1 and ANY z in T, the full ambient simplex projection at

    x=R c_face+b Jz

is exactly

    g=c_face+b Jv.                                           (8)

To check against every original vertex, the active upper residual level is

    sigma[(R-1)q/(3rN)+tau/r],

and the residual on I is -sigma(R-1)/N. Their difference is
sigma[(R-1)/3+tau]/r>=0. Other upper residuals are no larger. Thus (5)
holds for all N original vertices, including those declared inactive. If
R>1 the residual inequality for I is strict. At R=1 equality is harmless:
the projection is still unique, and every coordinate in I still has zero
barycentric weight.

The full function value and height are therefore

    F(x)=alpha^2(R-1/2)+b^2 Phi(z),
    F(x)-||g||^2/2=alpha^2(R-1)+b^2 tau.                     (9)

This is a genuine two-dimensional triangle process plus the actual common
direction. It is not the earlier affine-plus-scalar-Huber decomposition.

## 4. A concrete finite inverse rule, with every threshold guard

Fix the entire finite word h with h_i>1 before choosing the instance.
Choose a terminal z_n anywhere in K and R>=1. Ties between equal coordinate
values below are broken by the fixed index order 1<2<3. No coordinates or
group copies are created during the construction or the forward run.

Proceed symbolically backwards in the original chronological indices. For
one original step h=1+d, d>0, and a known centered future vector y, sort
its coordinates y_(1)>=y_(2)>=y_(3), retaining their original identities.
Choose the set A by exactly this rule:

    if 3 y_(1)<d:             A={1,2,3};
    else if y_(1)-y_(2)<d:    A={indices of y_(1),y_(2)};
    otherwise:               A={index of y_(1)}.             (10)

All comparisons are exact real comparisons. Strict inequalities in the
first two branches fix the rule at equality too; no limiting preimage is
silently admitted. Write k=|A| and set

    tau=[sum_(j in A)y_j+d(1-k/3)]/k,
    z_j=(h tau-y_j)/d           for j in A,
    z_j=y_j-h/3                for j outside A.              (11)

For k=3, tau=0 and max y<d/3. For k=2, tau=(-y_(3)+d/3)/2>0 and

    tau+d/3=(y_(1)+y_(2)+d)/2>y_(1).

For k=1, tau=y_(1)+2d/3>0 and tau+d/3=y_(1)+d>y_(1), since y_(1)>=0.
Consequently in EVERY branch

    y_j<tau+d/3 for every coordinate j.                      (12)

For j in A, (11) gives z_j+1/3-tau=(tau+d/3-y_j)/d>0.
For j outside A it gives z_j+1/3-tau=y_j-(tau+d/3)<0.
The active positive parts sum to

    [k(tau+d/3)-sum_(j in A)y_j]/d=1.

Summing (11) gives sum_j z_j=0. Hence tau really is the threshold of z,
its exact active set is A, its projected gradient v has p_j>0 exactly on
A, and direct substitution yields

    z-h v=y.                                                 (13)

This proves ALL inverse guards, for every possible future vector, rather
than just the guards of the displayed short suffix. In particular it covers
all previously visited and all subsequently specified supports when the
finite inverse dictionary is traversed forward.

Apply (10)-(11) at i=n-1,...,0, with y=z_(i+1), h=h_i. Denote the resulting
thresholds and projected gradients by tau_i and v_i. At i=n take tau_n=0,
v_n=z_n, and p_n=z_n+(1,1,1)/3. Every z_i is finite because the word is
finite, every h_i is finite, and every d_i>0. This is a textual finite
selection rule; no recurrence or trajectory was executed by a program.

An explicit affine-product expression for every chosen initial coordinate
can also be given. Once A_i is fixed, let M_i be block diagonal with
active block -I/d_i+h_i 11^T/(k_i d_i), inactive identity block, and zero
cross blocks. Let (b_i^aff)_j=h_i(1/k_i-1/3) on A_i and -h_i/3 elsewhere.
Then

    z_i=M_i z_(i+1)+b_i^aff,
    z_0=(M_0...M_(n-1))z_n
        +sum_(i=0)^(n-1)(M_0...M_(i-1))b_i^aff.              (14)

An empty product is identity. This is not a product of independently chosen
best histories: every A_i is selected from its one already fixed future.
The formula is part of the same joint derivation, not a computed artifact.

Equal original coordinates cannot split in the forward run: the same
threshold map applies to each. Formula (13) also shows directly that any
equality in a constructed predecessor is retained in its prescribed future.
Distinct predecessors may merge. The fixed group sizes never change.

## 5. Every original physical point, row, Gram entry, and radius

Put S_i=sum_(t=i)^(n-1) h_t, with S_n=0, and R_i=R+S_i. The initial point
and all its actual iterates are

    x_i=R_i c_face+b Jz_i, 0<=i<=n,
    g_i=c_face+b Jv_i,
    F_i=alpha^2(R_i-1/2)+b^2 Phi(z_i).                        (15)

In literal original coordinates, for l in G_j and l in I respectively,

    (x_i)_l=sigma[R_i q/(3rN)+(z_i)_j/r],
    (x_i)_l=-sigma R_i/N;
    (g_i)_l=sigma[(p_i)_j/r-1/N],
    (g_i)_l=-sigma/N.                                        (16)

The ambient threshold applied to (x_i)_l/sigma+1/N is

    theta_i=(R_i-1)q/(3rN)+tau_i/r.                          (17)

It gives positive-part barycentric entries (p_i)_j/r on G_j and zero on I.
The latter guard is exactly -[(R_i-1)/3+tau_i]/r<=0, strictly negative at
every queried i<n. The triangle active/inactive guards are (12). Thus the
whole known word fixes every original coordinate and every threshold.

Equations (13) and R_i-h_i=R_(i+1) prove
x_i-h_i g_i=x_(i+1) at each of the n original steps. At every queried index,
R_i>1, so (9) gives strictly positive height. This includes all leaves and
bridges, not just the five queries used to demonstrate rotation.

For the actual vectors, the complete Gram entries are

    <x_i,x_j>=alpha^2 R_i R_j+b^2<z_i,z_j>,
    <x_i,g_j>=alpha^2 R_i+b^2<z_i,v_j>,
    <g_i,g_j>=alpha^2+b^2<v_i,v_j>.                           (18)

In particular (18) specifies the full original formal-vector Gram on
(x_0,g_0,...,g_n), including the real terminal gradient. It is PSD because
the vectors in (16) are real vectors in one Euclidean space. No rank or
support restriction is imposed on a claimed full PEP upper certificate.

For ANY ordered pair of samples i,j, expand (3) at their actual gradients:

    Q_ij=F_i-F_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
        =<x_j-g_j,g_i-g_j><=0.                              (19)

The inequality is the normal condition (5) for sample j, applied to g_i in
D. Include the optimum sample x_star=g_star=F_star=0: then Q_(i,star)=0
and Q_(star,i)=-[alpha^2(R_i-1)+b^2 tau_i]<=0. All remote, reversed,
incoming and outgoing terminal rows are included. No prior row is replaced
by an expected face or an averaged group history.

Because argmin F={0}, the OWN squared radius is exactly

    R_init^2=||x_0||^2
             =alpha^2(S+R)^2+b^2||z_0||^2>0.                (20)

At the terminal z_n in K, equations (9) and (20) give the quantitative exact
terminal formula

    E=2F(x_n)/R_init^2
      =[2R-1+kappa||z_n||^2]
        /[(S+R)^2+kappa||z_0||^2].                          (21)

This is the original W=2R score of f=L F about its unique true minimum.
The entire initial transverse history is present in the denominator. The
common direction contributes alpha^2(S+R)^2; it has not been declared free.

## 6. Actual rotation on the final five original queries

For every diagnostic m>=1536 choose the concrete terminal point

    z_n=(a/4,0,-a/4).                                        (22)

It is strictly inside K. All r>=1, q>=r, sigma>0 and R>=1 are allowed;
for a single completely specified member one can take r=q=sigma=1 and
R=S+1. Earlier coordinates are determined by (10)-(14), not by a reset.

We first justify the coarse inequalities used in this finite symbolic suffix
calculation. Since epsilon<=1/6144<1/1000, beta>999/1000. The elementary
bounds 12/5<lambda<17/7 give c<(17/7)(1001/1000)<49/20. Therefore

    2/5<a<5/12,  beta>999/1000, beta^2>19/20,
    u:=1/(4beta)<13/50.                                      (23)

For the lower bound on a, beta/c>999/2450>2/5. The upper bound follows
from beta<1, c>lambda>12/5. The bounds for beta^2 and u follow by squaring
or multiplying positive rational quantities; they involve no numerical
evaluation of an orbit.

The last five original d_i=h_i-1 values are

    a, beta*c, a, beta, a,

in forward order, because H_m ends in H_3 and a*c=beta. Put
d_2=beta*c=beta^2/a. Starting from (22), the last two inverse steps use the
full-triangle branch and give

    z_(n-1)=(-1/4,0,1/4),
    z_(n-2)=(u,0,-u).                                        (24)

Their guards are 3a/4<a and 3/4<beta. At i=n-3, full support fails because
3u>3/4>a, but the top-two gap is u<a by (23). Thus A_(n-3)={1,2}, and

    tau=(u+a/3)/2, h=1+a,
    z^E:=z_(n-3)=(h/6+u(a-1)/(2a),
                         h/6+u(a+1)/(2a), -u-h/3),
    v_(n-3)=(1/6-u/(2a), 1/6+u/(2a), -1/3).                (25)

The associated positive barycentric weights are
1/2-u/(2a), 1/2+u/(2a), and zero. In particular both active weights are
strictly positive, and the edge is a real active face.

The entries of z^E have strict order z^E_2>z^E_1>z^E_3: the first
difference is u/a>0, while the second is

    z^E_1-z^E_3=h/2+u(3a-1)/(2a)>0.

At i=n-4 the full-triangle inverse is valid. Indeed

    3a z^E_2=(h/2)(3u+a)
       < (17/24)(39/50+5/12)
       =6103/7200<9/10<beta^2.

Thus 3 max z^E<d_2 and

    z_(n-4)=-z^E/d_2.                                       (26)

Its ordered coordinate identities are 3,1,2. For the next inverse at
i=n-5, full support fails since

    3(z_(n-4))_3=a(3u+h)/beta^2>a,

using 3u+h>1>beta^2. The top-two gap is

    (z^E_1-z^E_3)/d_2
      =[a h+u(3a-1)]/(2beta^2)<a.                            (27)

For the strict inequality, (23) and h<3/2 give
a(2beta^2-h)>(2/5)a>4/25, while
u(3a-1)<(13/50)(1/4)=13/200<4/25. Thus A_(n-5)={3,1}.

The actual support sequence at those five original queries is therefore

    {1,3}, {1,2,3}, {1,2}, {1,2,3}, {1,2,3}.                (28)

The terminal also has full support. Every group participates. In the
original N-coordinate simplex, a displayed group in (28) means all its r
actual copies are active, with the exact weight p_j/r from (16).

There is no scalar-line reduction: v_(n-2)=(u,0,-u) and
v_(n-1)=(-1/4,0,1/4) are distinct points on the line with second coordinate
zero, whereas the second coordinate of v_(n-3) in (25) is strictly positive.
These three transverse gradients are noncollinear. By the isometry J,
the same is true of the three ambient gradients after their common carrier
is restored. No fixed vector plus one fixed scalar direction contains them.

This is a symbolic proof for every m>=1536 using the actual suffix of the
same enclosing word. It is not a computed five-step replay or a substitute
for the full-word accounting in (20)-(21).

## 7. Whole-law comparison, including all earlier leaves and bridges

The proof of the obstruction requires no estimate that discards the initial
history. Instead it uses the nonnegative term that history contributes to
its OWN radius. For every allowed terminal and count choice put

    eta=kappa||z_n||^2, 0<=eta<=12*(2/3)=8.

Equation (21) gives

    E <= (2R-1+eta)/(S+R)^2.

For D_word=1+2S>eta, the exact completed-square identity is

    (S+R)^2-(D_word-eta)(2R-1+eta)
       =[R-(S+1-eta)]^2>=0.

The numerator is positive because R>=1. Therefore

    E <= 1/(D_word-eta) <= 1/(D_word-8) if D_word>8.          (29)

This is uniform over EVERY finite r,q with q>=r, every sigma>0, every R>=1,
every z_n in the closed K, every branch history selected by (10), and all
the resulting original initial points. Boundary terminals and exact inverse
threshold equalities are included. The bound is not merely local in m.

For z_n=0 the rule always selects all three coordinates, all z_i=0, and
choosing R=S+1 gives by (21) the attained score

    E=1/D_word.                                              (30)

For the rotating members (22), the more specific terminal charge is
eta=kappa a^2/8<=3a^2/2<25/96. Hence they even obey
E<=1/(D_word-3a^2/2), by the same proof whenever its denominator is
positive. No estimate of z_0 is assumed here.

On (2), D_word=D_m and S>n=2^m-1>=m>=1536, so D_m>3073>760.
The accepted comparison in fact931b9653ce0f7201 gives B_n/D_m<47/50.
Applying it in its correct direction
to the positive UPPER bound (29),

    B_n E < (47/50) D_m/(D_m-8) < 19/20.                    (31)

The last inequality is equivalent, with positive denominators, to D_m>760.
Also D_m>136 yields

    E<=1/(D_m-8)<17/(16D_m).                                 (32)

Equation (32) holds only for THIS constructed class. It does not meet the
full-function hypothesis of the conditional theorem in the accepted fact.
It cannot be substituted for W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D_m).

Because the COMPLETE K_n(H_m)>=1/D_m and F_ray_n(H_m)>=K_n(H_m), we also have

    E/K_n(H_m)<=D_m/(D_m-8),
    E/F_ray_n(H_m)<=D_m/(D_m-8).                             (33)

Both comparison denominators retain every original leaf, bridge, and
feasible checkpoint choice. Neither is replaced by a selected local cut.
Since D_m>1+2(2^m-1) tends to infinity, the right sides tend to one uniformly
over the whole law. Combining (29) and (30) further gives

    1 <= D_m sup_(this law) E <= D_m/(D_m-8) -> 1.           (34)

Thus the new face rotation has been made legal and quantitatively priced,
but it cannot deliver a nonvanishing benchmark gain in this count and
terminal domain. The actual optimum inside the narrow bracket is not
evaluated. In particular (33) does not assert E<=K_n or E<=F_ray_n.

## 8. Scope attacks and the remaining vector question

The direct-proving screen has established, inside this one unverified draft,
the legal real geometry, all guards, own radius, noncollinearity, exact
terminal formula, and the uniform comparison for the declared law.

The counterexample screen found two reasons not to overextend it:

1. The metric bound kappa<=12 genuinely uses q>=r. For the algebraically
   same face geometry with q=1 and arbitrary integer r, the exact metric
   ratio is kappa=3(3r+1), which is unbounded. For a terminal triangle
   vertex, eta=(2/3)kappa=2(3r+1), also unbounded. This refutes extending
   the particular estimate eta<=8 to all copied three-group counts. It
   does NOT refute a performance bound there, because the initial
   transverse charge kappa||z_0||^2 remains to be paid. No second law is
   claimed analyzed on that larger domain.
2. The terminal restriction z_n in K is also load-bearing. For a general
   transverse terminal z, formula (9) has 2Phi(z), not ||z||^2, and
   2Phi(z) is unbounded along an outward vertex ray: for
   w=e_1-(1,1,1)/3 and t>=1, the normal condition gives P_K(tw)=w,
   so 2Phi(tw)=(2t-1)||w||^2=(2t-1)*2/3. The inequality
   2Phi(z)<=2/3 cannot simply be imported outside K. This is a scope
   failure, not a realized high-error trajectory on H_m.

These checks invalidate the two tempting extensions before either is used
as a proof step. They leave a precise open direction: the actual
two-dimensional triangle profile with no uniformly positive inactive
fraction, or with unrestricted terminal amplitudes, needs a joint estimate
of terminal value versus the complete initial transverse norm. The present
bounded-terminal carrier proof supplies no such estimate. It also excludes
neither a full simplex with no permanently inactive coordinates nor a rule
whose participating group union changes over the whole history.

No fixed two-group tuning, independent Cartesian inverse duplication,
coordinate creation/splitting, free carrier, expected face, unpriced extreme
coordinate, or function change was used. The scalar-amplitude lane remains
separate: the transverse process here has three noncollinear gradients.

## 9. Retrieval, resource record, and handoff status

Skills applied: query-memory, search-math-results, direct-proving, and
construct-counterexamples. The active search was a mutation of the mature
centered-simplex inverse program, targeting all-history support rotation
with a fully paid radius.

Matlas returned 1808.02681 Theorem4.1, 2012.00990 Proposition4, and
1410.7012 Lemma36; none supplied the required GD mechanism or entered this
proof. Web search located the standard simplex threshold reference:
Weiran Wang and Miguel A. Carreira-Perpinan, "Projection onto the probability
simplex: An efficient algorithm with a simple proof, and an application",
arXiv:1309.1541 (2013), https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.1541. The exact local
extracted paper downloads/1309.1541_public_pdf_text.txt, Section3, including
Theorem1 and its KKT proof, was read. It concerns Euclidean projection of
a finite real list onto nonnegative weights summing to one. Its threshold
normal-condition method informs (7)-(12); all required claims are proved
here directly. No external mathematical result is an unproved premise.

Some initial broad batched retrieval outputs were truncated; the selected
inputs and scopes were subsequently read in bounded calls. No conclusion
is based on unseen truncated text. The accepted benchmark fact was read
in full through its final conditional conclusion.

Resource use: one analytical invocation; one substantive mechanism;
ZERO mathematical programs, numerical/arithmetic trajectory replays,
executed recurrences, optimizers, solvers, benchmark DP, formal calls,
fact_submit, installations, paid consults, or subagents. File writing,
text retrieval, text parsing, and integrity/readback checks only.

This report is to be published as a full global-memory proof_attempt with

The original target is OPEN. No finalization, outward publication,

## 2. Fixed function, physical word, and elementary parameter bounds

global glossary entries:

    epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon, c=lambda(1+epsilon),

The bounds needed below are deliberately coarse and proved symbolically.

## 5. Exact symmetric-interval image: the new analytical mechanism

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,

    B_n=max_(integer 0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)),

The original question is whether lim_n B_n inf_h W_n(h)=1. An affirmative
answer must have the original uniform quantifier over every nonnegative
word and every sufficiently large actual horizon. A negative answer needs
a rigorous full-function upper bound beating the benchmark on unbounded
actual horizons. No restricted-function or restricted-row computation is
such an answer.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the normalization, the original

In particular its deletion of incoming ACTUAL-terminal rows does not delete

Fix the SAME enclosing integer m>=1536 and set

    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c, d_j=a*c^j,

lambda_ij with finite flow out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n) has a full certificate

## 2. Mechanism I: chronological storage with a last-leaf objective interface

This is a completely new original-index array; it does not use inherited
Lambda or Kbase. It starts from original optimum-sector rows and finishes
with a two-gradient objective interface on the last physical leaf.

For each physical i define the scalars and vector expression

    kap80_i=max(1,h_i-1),
    r80_i=2h_i                 if h_i<2,
        2h_i(h_i-1)          if h_i>2,
    s80_i=h_i*abs(h_i-2),
    z80_i=g_i                 if h_i<2,
        x_i-g_i             if h_i>2.

These definitions refer to the actual h_i; no gradient is identified with
another gradient. Let jlast=n-1, Dleaf=1+2b, qleaf=1/Dleaf, and

    Ppre=product_(0<=i<jlast)kap80_i^2,
    w80_i^I=qleaf*product_(i<t<jlast)kap80_t^2  (i<jlast),
    q_I=qleaf*Ppre.

Every nonzero original multiplier of Law I is

    lambda_(i,star)=lambda_(star,i)=w80_i^I*r80_i, i<jlast;
    lambda_(jlast,star)=1;
    lambda_(n,star)=1;
    lambda_(n,jlast)=1.                                  (I.1)

All other rows have coefficient zero. The support has no incoming actual
terminal edge. All signs are positive. Prefix sector pairs are cycles;
the three last rows cancel f_(jlast) and give terminal flow2, so every
finite flow is correct. The full initial point, both endpoint gradients,
and the endpoint value are present in this law.

The original-row identities are

    kap80_i^2||x_i||^2-||x_(i+1)||^2
           +r80_i(Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i))=s80_i||z80_i||^2,    (I.2)

and, writing X=x_(jlast), u=g_(jlast), v=g_n,

    qleaf||X||^2-2f_n+Q_(jlast,star)+Q_(n,star)+Q_(n,jlast)
      =qleaf||X-Dleaf(u+v)/2||^2
                      +(3-2b)||u-v||^2/4.              (I.3)

For (I.2), Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i)=||g_i||^2-<x_i,g_i>.
When h_i<2, direct expansion leaves h_i(2-h_i)||g_i||^2.
When h_i>2, it leaves h_i(h_i-2)||x_i-g_i||^2.
For (I.3), expanding the three rows gives

    qleaf||X||^2-<X,u+v>+||u||^2+(2b-1)<u,v>+||v||^2.

Expansion of the displayed two squares has exactly these coefficients.
Since b<3/2 both square coefficients are positive. Multiplying (I.2)
by w80_i^I and adding (I.3) proves the ENTIRE identity

    M_I(q_I)=sum_(i<jlast)w80_i^I*s80_i||z80_i||^2
       +qleaf||x_(jlast)-Dleaf(g_(jlast)+g_n)/2||^2
       +(3-2b)||g_(jlast)-g_n||^2/4.                    (I.4)

There is no omitted displacement or residual. This gives a full-function
upper-certificate draft at q_I, not at the requested q=17/(16D).

At any real original cut r<s<=jlast, the same identity reads

    [product_(r<=i<s)kap80_i^2]||x_r||^2-||x_s||^2
      +sum_(r<=i<s)[product_(i<t<s)kap80_t^2]r80_i
                              (Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i))
      =sum_(r<=i<s)[product_(i<t<s)kap80_t^2]s80_i||z80_i||^2. (I.5)

Two consecutive blocks compose by multiplying the first identity by the
second block's product and adding, with its ACTUAL common x_s. At a
dyadic parent, the actual one-step bridge is an additional such factor.
The child displacement is always sum h_i g_i and x_s=x_r-sum h_i g_i.
These are context-dependent suffix weights, not fictitious resets.
They solve all-depth positivity for this law analytically, but the
product growth costs too much. Section7 excludes *any* useful coefficient
choice on a much richer support, without assuming scalar-only storage.

## 3. Mechanism II: dense checkpoint circulation and full terminal storage

The second family permits real mixed boundary information and all enclosing
context. Its coefficient support is much larger than Law I. Let

    Leaf={0,2,...,n-1}, Check={1,3,...,n-2}.

There are Nleaf leaves and Nleaf-1 queried checkpoints. Allow these rows:

  (a) both optimum rows for EVERY original finite index, including n;
  (b) EVERY ordered pair of distinct checkpoints;
  (c) EVERY leaf-to-checkpoint row Q_(ell,p), ell in Leaf, p in Check;
  (d) checkpoint-to-leaf rows Q_(p,ell) when |p-ell|=1;
  (e) EVERY outgoing actual-terminal row Q_(n,i), i<n.

Call this support E80. It contains both directions of every adjacent
queried-prefix pair, complete checkpoint coupling, all outgoing leaf
links to all checkpoints regardless of ancestors, and the whole terminal
fan. It permits optimum-to-terminal. It excludes incoming queried-to-
terminal rows and remote checkpoint-to-leaf / leaf-to-leaf rows.

For the support-level obstruction later, EVERY nonnegative coefficient
on E80 is free, with arbitrary dependence on m and full ancestor context.
Storage may be any quadratic form in x_0, actual boundary positions and
boundary gradients, with value terms and all real mixed inner products.
It may use arbitrarily many such boundary coordinates. The only restriction
is that its telescoped original-row certificate uses E80. No reduction
to a scalar metric is presumed.

Here is an explicit FULL feasible coefficient law inside that family, as
a starting point. It proves existence of a genuine changed base and makes
every added cost auditable. Put

    Pfull=product_(i<n)kap80_i^2,
    w80_i=product_(i<t<n)kap80_t^2,
    Kprod=product_(i<n)(1+h_i),
    alpha80=epsilon/[(n+2)^2*Kprod^2],
    eta80=alpha80/[4(S+2)(n+1)^2],
    q_II=Pfull+1.

Start with coefficients lambda_(i,star)=lambda_(star,i)=w80_i*r80_i for i<n,
lambda_(n,star)=2, and every other entry zero. To these add eta80 on
each directed edge of each of the following cycles, counting overlaps:

    A_(ell,p): ell -> p -> star -> ell,
                           for every ell in Leaf and p in Check;
    B_(p,r):   p -> r -> p, for every unordered pair in Check;
    C_(p,ell): p -> ell -> p, for every |p-ell|=1;
    T_i:       n -> i -> star -> n, for every 0<=i<n.      (II.1)

The arrow denotes the ordered Q source and receiver, not a GD update.
All cycles use original indices. Formula (II.1) specifies EVERY entry
without an optimization problem or unknown PSD block. More explicitly,
write rcheck=Nleaf-1. The finite entries are

    lambda_(p,r)=eta80                (distinct p,r in Check),
    lambda_(ell,p)=eta80*(1+1_(|p-ell|=1)),
    lambda_(p,ell)=eta80*1_(|p-ell|=1),
    lambda_(n,i)=eta80                (0<=i<n).

The optimum entries, including EVERY incoming one, are

    lambda_(ell,star)=w80_ell*r80_ell+eta80,
    lambda_(star,ell)=w80_ell*r80_ell+rcheck*eta80,
    lambda_(p,star)=w80_p*r80_p+(Nleaf+1)*eta80,
    lambda_(star,p)=w80_p*r80_p,
    lambda_(n,star)=2,
    lambda_(star,n)=n*eta80.                              (II.2)

is strictly positive where its indicator is one. Each cycle has zero
value flow at each vertex, and the initial array has only terminal flow2.
Hence the full original value cancellation holds exactly. In particular
there is no implicit subtraction of an incoming optimum cost.

Let Cyc be the list in (II.1), and write Q_C=sum_(i,j in cycle C)Q_ij.
The exact entire-word composition identity is

    M_II(q_II)=||x_0||^2+sum_(i<n)w80_i*s80_i||z80_i||^2

It follows by (I.2) on ALL physical steps and
||x_n||^2-2f_n+2Q_(n,star)=||x_n-g_n||^2.
Every Q_C is kept with its original mixed terms and both original
displacements. Individual cycles are NOT asserted PSD.

For a cut or dyadic composition, apply (I.5) to each physical child and
the actual bridge, multiply by the enclosing suffix product, and then
add the cycles assigned to that parent. One unambiguous assignment is
the smallest dyadic node containing all finite vertices of a cycle;
if that set is not contained in a proper node, assign it to the root.
Rows involving n are assigned to the root. There is no need to discard
crossing cycles: their exact Q_C polynomials form the boundary coupling.
This is a complete additive identity, not a claim of local child PSD.

For completeness, the all-depth PSD expenditure is explicit. Every
w80_i>=1 and s80_i>=epsilon. At level1, s80_i=(2-epsilon)epsilon>=epsilon.
At level0 use b>1 and 2-b>1/2. At higher levels h_i>3, so s80_i>3.
Let z=x_n-g_n and let Vnorm^2=||x_0||^2+sum_(i<=n)||g_i||^2.
The triangular change of coordinates from (x_0,z80_0,...,z80_(n-1),z)
to the original vectors has the following elementary bound:

    Vnorm^2 <= (n+2)^2*Kprod^2
                   [||x_0||^2+sum_(i<n)||z80_i||^2+||z||^2]. (II.4)

Indeed, for h_i<2 one has g_i=z80_i and x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i z80_i;
for h_i>2 one has g_i=x_i-z80_i and
x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i z80_i. Induction using factors1+h_i bounds

Thus the first three terms of (II.3) are at least alpha80*Vnorm^2.

After deleting its value terms, every individual Q row has absolute

The number of row occurrences over all cycles is exactly

    Lcyc=3Nleaf(Nleaf-1)+(Nleaf-1)(Nleaf-2)
                          +4(Nleaf-1)+3n

Use exactly the earlier H4 direction: x_0=0, g_0,...,g_3=1,
g_8,...,g_11=-1, and every other original gradient, including g_n, zero.

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-sum_i mu_i<x_0,g_i>

differences give the first term, forward rows out of i crossing j give
the second, and rows out of j reaching index<=i or the optimum give
the third. Incoming optimum rows have no initial mixed term. Thus no
nu_i or displacement contribution has been silently omitted.

Let e be the all-ones gradient column and Ppos80_i=sum_(t<i)h_t. Then

    U80=sum_i mu_i=2+sum_i nu_i,
    V80=e^T C e=D+sum_i nu_i(1+Ppos80_i).                 (5.2)

For any variation v of the gradients orthogonal to e, put

    M_I(q)=||g_n-Vlast||^2+Rlast,

The negative square cost in that prefix remainder is retained by (I.4)
and (5.1); no terminal gradient is fixed by a quotient assumption.

Law II has incoming optimum-terminal mass n*eta80. Define

    Aterm=1+n*eta80,
    Bterm=(1+n*eta80/2)x_n
                       -(eta80/2)sum_(i<n)(x_i-g_i)

Its exact ACTUAL-terminal completion is
