evidence:
# Bidirectional endpoint certificate for every whole-root-second pair

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report. Project gd-exact-profile-20260926,
worker max4, invocation78, 2026-10-02. No new mathematical statement in
this report has been submitted to, or accepted by, the verifier.

This is one authorized analytical invocation, with two mechanisms:
(1) an explicitly paid backward cycle repairs the adjacent leaf/root
interface; (2) a chronological dyadic classification extends the same
certificate to every first checkpoint before the whole root. There is
no mathematical program, numerical/arithmetic replay, solver, recurrence
execution, formal call, fact_submit, consultation, installation, or
subagent. The original unrestricted minimax target remains OPEN.

## 1. Statement, complete quantifiers, and accepted inputs

Fix an arbitrary integer m>=1536 and use the SAME enclosing parameters
at every child:

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta_h=1-1/(4m),
    c=lambda*(1+1/(4m)), a=beta_h/c,
    H_0=(), H_(l+1)=(H_l,1+a*c^l,H_l), 0<=l<m,
    S_l=sum H_l, X_l=1+S_l, h=H_m, n=2^m-1.

Define actual zero-based physical indices and masses

    k=2^(m-1)-1, j_c=2^(m-2)-1,
    U=X_(m-1), e=a*c^(m-1), d0=1+a,
    Z=1+2S_m=4U+2e-1.

Here k is the whole-word root, j_c the root of its LEFT child, and d0
the ACTUAL final leaf. The report concerns EVERY first checkpoint

                         0<=j<k.                         (1.1)

For arbitrary finite real Euclidean dimension, consider every actual
GD transcript of ONE globally convex differentiable function with
1-Lipschitz gradient and an attained minimum, with queried gradients

    g_i=p  for 0<=i<=j,
    g_i=q  for j+1<=i<=k,
    g_i=r  for k+1<=i<n.                                (1.2)

The vectors p,q,r, their lengths and mutual angles, all sampled values,
heights, affine offsets, the initial orientation, and the dimension
are unrestricted beyond legality and (1.2). No orthogonality, common
direction, fixed rank, zero height, or zero interpolation remainder
is assumed. Every original physical step is retained.

Family E_j additionally has actual terminal gradient g_n=r. Family Q_j
allows EVERY legal terminal gradient and EVERY static smooth-convex
completion of the entire prescribed queried prefix. For each such
function and any of its own minimizers x_star with x_0!=x_star, define

               V=2(f(x_n)-min f)/||x_0-x_star||^2.

The candidate conclusion, proved jointly below, is

    sup_(E_j) V = 1/Z = K_n(h),
    1/Z <= sup_(Q_j) V <= 1/(Z-d0^2),                    (1.3)
    B_n sup_(E_j) V < 47/50,
    B_n sup_(Q_j) V < 940/999 < 19/20.                  (1.4)

Here K_n is the COMPLETE accepted Huber/single-cut maximum, including
every original cut, and B_n is the ORIGINAL benchmark denominator
with every integer split. The bounds apply about every actual
minimizer of each completed function; in particular they use each
function's OWN closest initial distance if that is the chosen radius.

For advertised L>0, replace f by (f-min f)/L and translate the chosen
actual minimizer to0. Its gradient is 1-Lipschitz, the physical word
is unchanged, and V is exactly 2(f(x_n)-min f)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2).
No factor-2 normalization is changed.

The accepted correctness premises are only:

* 1252b8823bb5a290: necessity/sufficiency of all ordered smooth-convex
  interpolation inequalities and its explicit conjugate interpolant.
* b98bb807d514e80d: the definition and lower-witness scope of K_n, and
  the exact original benchmark coordinates/recursions.
* 931b9653ce0f7201: at precisely this same-m tau=1/4 hierarchy and every
  m>=1536, the UPPER comparison B_n/Z<47/50.

These actual facts were read. No obstruction for the spiral families
in 5fd396eba75651e7 is transferred to the present family; its older
benchmark comparison is unnecessary. The earlier endpoint report
6b8cd30a96a9165b is UNVERIFIED awareness, not a premise. All endpoint,
cycle, hierarchy, contact, and PSD calculations needed here are
rederived jointly below. Latest steering: 885472ffb7c11cba; own plan:
402b82b97ff12a3f.

This is a theorem candidate only for (1.2). Pairs not involving the
whole root, nonconstant gradients within a sector, and unrestricted
W_n(H_m) remain outside its scope. In particular it does NOT prove
the full-W hypothesis 17/(16Z) in accepted931b9653ce0f7201 and does
not resolve the original minimax problem.

## 2. Complete endpoint system and original-query lift

Normalize the chosen optimum to (x_star,g_star,f_star)=(0,0,0).
For any original pair write the full chronological word as

    h=(block_0,b,block_1,c_step,block_2),
    P=sum block_0, M=sum block_1, T=sum block_2,
    u=P+1, v=M+1, d=b-1, e=c_step-1,
    A=u+d=P+b, B=v+e=M+c_step, U_loc=u+v+d.

The notation U_loc is general in this section; at a root-second
pair it equals U from Section1. At such a pair e is also exactly
the root excess from Section1 and T=U-1.

Let F_p,F_q,F_r denote the values at the first query of each sector,
and set

    Z_p=x_0, Z_q=x_0-Ap, Z_r=x_0-Ap-Bq.

For every ACTUAL cumulative step mass s in its sector, the jets are

    (Z_p-sp, p, F_p-s||p||^2),  0<=s<=P,
    (Z_q-sq, q, F_q-s||q||^2),  0<=s<=M,
    (Z_r-sr, r, F_r-s||r||^2).                         (2.1)

For E the final range is 0<=s<=T. For Q its queried part is
0<=s<=T-d0 and the separate actual terminal position is
x_n=Z_r-Tr. Equal gradients force the displayed values: the two
convexity inequalities between any two such samples force equality
with their common affine support. Each original step inside a sector
therefore pays its actual h_i||g_i||^2 decrease.

For ordered samples define the signed residual, in the orientation
of accepted1252b8823bb5a290,

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.     (2.2)

Keep both actual endpoints of every queried sector, identifying
coincident index labels, and the optimum jet. For E keep the terminal
as the last r endpoint. For Q additionally keep the separate terminal
jet (x_n,g_n,f_n). Require ALL ordered inequalities among these jets,
including all remote, optimum, and terminal rows.

This is a complete endpoint representation, not a relaxation. Indeed,
for a source sector with data (Z_a,g_a,F_a), source mass s, and target
sector (Z_b,g_b,F_b), target mass t, substitution gives

    Q_(a(s),b(t))
     =F_a-F_b+<g_a,Z_b-Z_a>+||g_a-g_b||^2/2
                        +t(||g_b||^2-<g_a,g_b>).       (2.3)

The source mass cancels and the target dependence is affine. Hence
every original interior ordered row is a convex combination of
endpoint rows. Same-sector rows are zero. Rows involving the optimum
or separate terminal are affine in the varying sector mass as well.
Endpoint inequalities imply ALL original query, terminal, and optimum
rows; the converse follows because the endpoints are actual samples.
This includes singleton first or middle sectors, notably j=0 and j=k-1.

For a full constructive lift, for each retained endpoint/terminal/
optimum jet i put

    y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
    H(vect)=||vect||^2/2+max_i{<y_i,vect>-delta_i},
    F(x)=sup_vect{<x,vect>-H(vect)}.                    (2.4)

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 makes F finite, convex, differentiable and
globally 1-smooth, interpolating every supplied jet. For an interior
sector sample its affine anchor is affine in s, since

    y(s)=Z_a-(s+1)g_a,
    delta(s)=F_a-(s+1/2)||g_a||^2.

Its anchor is thus a convex combination of endpoint anchors. Adding
EVERY original interior anchor changes neither H nor F. The given
values and gradients remain intact, and induction through the actual
GD updates reaches every original sample and the actual terminal.

For completeness, Q_(star,i)<=0 gives delta_i>=0. The optimum anchor
is0, so H(0)=0 and H(vect)>=||vect||^2/2. Consequently min F=0 and

              argmin F=conv{y_i:delta_i=0}.             (2.5)

To justify the last formula, grad F(x)=0 exactly when x belongs to
the subdifferential of H at0. The quadratic has derivative0 there;
the subdifferential of the finite affine maximum is the convex hull
of the active slopes, precisely the displayed set. Inclusion of
that hull follows from the supporting inequalities; separation of
a point outside the hull gives the reverse inclusion.

Thus (2.5) is the full minimum set of the constructed completion,
not a selected subset. A different legal completion can have a
different minimum set. The certificate below starts from any actual
minimizer of THAT function, so it does not inherit a radius from
another completion. Each nonempty closed convex minimum set in finite
dimension has a closest point to x_0.

## 3. Exact backward cycle and all nonzero original multipliers

Let L_p=j be the last p query, L_q=k the last q query, and R_0=k+1
the first r query. Their actual jets are

    L_p: (x_0-Pp,p,F_p-P||p||^2),
    L_q: (x_0-Ap-Mq,q,F_q-M||q||^2),
    R_0: (x_0-Ap-Bq,r,F_r).

Direct substitution into (2.2) yields

    Q_(L_p,star)=F_p-<p,x_0>+||p||^2/2,
    Q_(L_q,star)=F_q-<q,x_0>+A<p,q>+||q||^2/2,
    Q_(R_0,star)=F_r-<r,x_0>+A<p,r>+B<q,r>+||r||^2/2,

    Q_(L_q,L_p)=F_q-F_p+(P+1/2)||p||^2
                                  +||q||^2/2+d<p,q>,
    Q_(R_0,L_q)=F_r-F_q+(M+1/2)||q||^2
                                  +||r||^2/2+e<q,r>,
    Q_(L_p,L_q)=F_p-F_q+(1/2-A)||p||^2
                                  +(M+1/2)||q||^2-v<p,q>.

In particular the exact two-row cycle is

    C_pq:=Q_(L_p,L_q)+Q_(L_q,L_p)
       =-d||p||^2+(d-v)<p,q>+v||q||^2.                (3.1)

No value or initial-point term remains. This cycle is NOT itself PSD;
its negative p-square and mixed term must also be paid.

Choose 0<=alpha<=theta<=1, beta=theta-alpha, gamma=1-theta, eta>=0.
The core multiplier table is

| Original ordered row | Multiplier mu |
|---|---:|
| Q_(L_p,star) | alpha |
| Q_(L_q,star) | beta |
| Q_(R_0,star) | gamma |
| Q_(L_q,L_p) | alpha+eta |
| Q_(L_p,L_q) | eta |
| Q_(R_0,L_q) | theta |

All other core multipliers are ZERO; their primal rows are still
required by Section2. At L_p, outgoing alpha+eta equals incoming
alpha+eta. At L_q, outgoing beta+alpha+eta equals incoming theta+eta.
At R_0 the outgoing sum is gamma+theta=1. The optimum has incoming1.
The cycle therefore changes no value flow. The weighted value part
is exactly F_r.

Set gbar=alpha*p+beta*q+gamma*r. If t_pay is a terminal charge and
w=t_pay+1/2, the sum of the core rows, plus t_pay||r||^2, equals

                 F_r-<gbar,x_0>+Q(p,q,r),

where the COMPLETE gradient quadratic is

    Q=(alpha*u-eta*d)||p||^2+(theta+eta)*v||q||^2
          +w||r||^2
       +[alpha*d+beta*A+eta*(d-v)]<p,q>
       +gamma*A<p,r>+[theta*e+gamma*B]<q,r>.           (3.2)

Let U_loc=u+v+d and D=U_loc+e+w. On the common-gradient direction
p=q=r, Q=D||r||^2. The p row sum of (3.2) is

                   [alpha*u+A-eta*(d+v)]/2.

The cumulative p,q row sum is [(1+theta)U_loc+e]/2: set p=q in
(3.2), whose first-group square coefficient is theta*U_loc and
whose cross coefficient with r is (1-theta)U_loc+e.
Therefore both contact equations, including the cycle cost, are

    theta=(U_loc+e)/(2D-U_loc),
    alpha=[A-eta*(d+v)]/(2D-u).                       (3.3)

These are rederived contact equations. The old forward weights have
not been held fixed while adding a cycle.

Put s=p-q and z=q-r, so gbar=alpha*s+theta*z+r. After (3.3), the
common-gradient square and all its cross terms vanish from
Q-D||gbar||^2. The remainder on ALL real increment vectors is

    J11||s||^2+2J12<s,z>+J22||z||^2,
    J11=alpha*u-eta*d-D*alpha^2,
    J22=theta*(U_loc-D*theta),
    J12=(1-theta)*(2D*alpha-A)/2.                     (3.4)

For an explicit mixed-coefficient check before imposing the second
contact equation, the s,z coefficient in Q is
alpha*u+theta*A-eta*(d+v). Subtracting 2D*alpha*theta and using
eta*(d+v)=A-alpha*(2D-u) gives exactly 2J12 in (3.4).
The s-square comes directly from the p-square in (3.2); the z-square
comes from p=q, where the cycle is identically zero. Thus (3.4)
accounts for the entire reduced space, not just its diagonal.

Two explicit choices of the multipliers will suffice:

DIAGONAL CYCLE choice, valid when u*v>d*U_loc:

    alpha=A/(2D), eta=alpha*u/(d+v), beta=theta-alpha,
    J12=0,
    J11=alpha*(u*v-d*U_loc)/[2(d+v)].                  (3.5)

The second identity in (3.3) follows since
eta*(d+v)=alpha*u and A=2D*alpha. For the J11 identity,

    J11=alpha*[u*v/(d+v)-A/2],
    2u*v-A*(d+v)=u*v-d*(u+v+d).

FORWARD CHAIN choice, reserved below for the actual left-child root:

    eta=0, alpha=A/(2D-u), beta=theta-alpha,
    J11=alpha*(u-D*alpha),
    J12=alpha*u*(1-theta)/2.                          (3.6)

Both choices use the same original row table, and both retain (3.4)'s
J22. Positivity of all multipliers and the entire residual will be
proved for the stated physical regions, not assumed.

## 4. Initial point, terminal step, and full quadratic identity

For E take t_pay=T and add Q_(n,R_0) with multiplier1. Since g_n=r,
this row is f_n-F_r+T||r||^2. The total weighted sum is

                    f_n-<gbar,x_0>+Q.                 (4.1)

For Q let N_-=n-1 be the ACTUAL final queried index, and s_n=g_n.
Add Q_(N_-,R_0) and Q_(n,N_-) with multipliers1. Their sum is

    f_n-F_r+(T-d0^2/2)||r||^2
                          +||s_n+(d0-1)r||^2/2.      (4.2)

Indeed x_n=x_(N_-)-d0*r, and

    Q_(n,N_-)=f_n-f_(N_-)+d0<s_n,r>+||s_n-r||^2/2,
    Q_(N_-,R_0)=f_(N_-)-F_r+(T-d0)||r||^2.

Completing the square gives (4.2). Set t_pay=T-d0^2/2 in Q.
Thus for Q the total row sum is

        f_n-<gbar,x_0>+Q+||s_n+(d0-1)r||^2/2.          (4.3)

For the root-second family the entire right child is the last block,

## 10. Flat-curvature boundary, including zero and huge steps

This elementary boundary accounting does not open the second search
mechanism. Suppose one ray is flat and the other has curvature
kappa in(0,1] and positive clipping level b0. By reflection put the
active ray on x>0. Its complete minimum set is(-infinity,0]. Let h
be ANY finite nonnegative word and S=sum h, retaining zero and
arbitrarily large steps. For every active start s>0 the exact family
profile is

    sup_s 2 f(x_n)/s^2 = kappa/(1+2*kappa*S).          (10.1)

If a query ever reaches the minimum half-line, it stays there and
the terminal gap is0. Otherwise all iterates are positive and
nonincreasing. If the terminal is saturated, every earlier query
is saturated too. Writing z=s/b0, its exact score is

    [2z-(2S+1/kappa)]/z^2 <=1/(2S+1/kappa),

by the square identity used in Section7. Equality is attained by
s=b0*(2S+1/kappa), with actual terminal b0*(S+1/kappa), and all
queries on the saturated active ray. The own radius is exactly s.

If the terminal lies in the active core, g_n=kappa*x_n, and
monotonicity of the positive iterates gives g_i>=g_n for all i<n.
The exact sum of updates yields

    s=x_n+sum_i h_i*g_i >=x_n*(1+kappa*S).

Hence its score is at most kappa/(1+kappa*S)^2, which is at most
kappa/(1+2*kappa*S). This proves the upper bound for every start,
including the threshold equality. It proves (10.1) without assuming
that each update is short or stays positive. At S=0 the word is
stationary and the expression is kappa, as it should be.

On H_m, this fixed-kappa value is at most1/D_m because
kappa/(1+2kappa*S_m)<=1/(1+2S_m) is equivalent to kappa<=1.
Allowing all kappa in(0,1] gives the exact boundary-family profile
1/D_m, attained at kappa1. Both-flat and minimum-set starts have
zero gap as described in Section3. No formula divides by a zero
curvature or a zero closest radius. This boundary result says
nothing about two independent positive core curvatures.

## 2. One real body, its exact metric, and every projection guard

Choose any finite integer r>=2, put N=2^r, and label vertices by
s in F_2^r. Coordinates are ALL nonzero t in F_2^r. Set

    chi_t(s)=(-1)^(t dot s), b_t>0,
    z_s=(b_t chi_t(s))_(t!=0) in R^(N-1),
    D=conv{z_s:s in F_2^r}, M=sum_(t!=0)b_t^2.

All weights are fixed before GD. We take unequal weights in the declared
laws. The inner product is the ordinary Euclidean inner product in these
literal coordinates. There is no rescaling of GD to a different metric.
The exact vertex Gram and barycentric metric are

    K_su=sum_(t!=0)b_t^2 chi_t(s)chi_t(u), K_ss=M,
    ||sum_s v_s z_s||^2=sum_(t!=0)b_t^2
                                      (sum_s v_s chi_t(s))^2.       (2.1)

The formula applies to all real coefficient arrays v, including sum v=0.
Pairing group elements differing in a bit proves
sum_s chi_t(s)=0 and sum_s chi_t(s)chi_u(s)=N*1_(t=u).

Consequently the vertices are affinely independent, their sum is zero,

<w_s,x>>=-1. The inverse weights in these normals are not free prices.

The maximizer is unique by strict convexity of squared distance. It is the

## 2. Physical classification before any certificate choice

For index i let l_i=nu_2(i+1), the largest nonnegative integer l with
2^l dividing i+1. Literal concatenation shows

    h_i=1+a*c^(l_i),
    I_i=[i-(2^(l_i)-1), i+(2^(l_i)-1)].                    (2.1)

The interval I_i is the complete physical copy of H_(l_i+1) rooted
at i; the two children are copies of H_(l_i). These assertions follow
by induction through (H_l,1+a*c^l,H_l): the middle position has
i+1=2^l, and translating a child by2^l preserves valuations below l.

To classify a pair, descend from the whole root while both indices
are in the same child. At the least common ancestor one of exactly
three things happens: j is that root and k is in its right child;
k is that root and j is in its left child; or j and k lie in its
different children. An ancestor with both points in the same child
is not the least common ancestor. This covers adjacent positions,
shallow common subtrees, and arbitrarily separated checkpoint levels.

At that least common subtree write E_pre and E_post for the sums of
ALL physical steps before and after the subtree. If P_loc,M_loc,T_loc
are the sums before j, between j and k, and after k inside it, the
actual full masses are

    P=E_pre+P_loc, M=M_loc, T=T_loc+E_post,
    b=h_j, c_step=h_k, d=b-1, e=c_step-1,
    u=P+1, v=M+1, z=T+1,
    A=u+d=P+b, B=v+e=M+c_step, U=u+v+d.                  (2.2)

No outer mass is discarded or presumed monotone. All later formulas
use these exact u,v,z. In particular U is 1 plus the entire mass
before the second checkpoint.

Because j<k, k belongs to I_j if and only if it is in j's right child.
Call this the remaining ancestor case. Every other pair has k>I_j's
right endpoint and is covered by (1.2). This includes all pairs in
different children of their least common ancestor and all pairs with
k as their least common ancestor. Section7 treats the exceptional
consecutive roots on the leftmost branch without deleting their tail.

## 3. Exact endpoint system and one global completion

values at the first query of the three sectors, and set

    Z_p=x_0, Z_q=x_0-Ap, Z_r=x_0-Ap-Bq.

At every ACTUAL cumulative mass s inside its sector the jets are

    (Z_p-sp,p,F_p-s||p||^2), 0<=s<=P,
    (Z_q-sq,q,F_q-s||q||^2), 0<=s<=M,
    (Z_r-sr,r,F_r-s||r||^2).                            (3.1)

The last range is 0<=s<=T for E and 0<=s<=T-d0 for the queried part

force the displayed values by the two convexity inequalities between
any two samples. Thus these formulas pay the full physical decrease
inside each constant-gradient sector.

Retain both actual endpoints of each range, the optimum, and the
separate terminal jet for Q, identifying coincident index labels.
For ALL ordered distinct retained samples impose

There is no omitted remote or optimum condition. For source sector a

       +||g_a-g_b||^2/2+t(||g_b||^2-<g_a,g_b>).          (3.3)

The source mass cancels and target dependence is affine. Rows with

Consequently every original query row is an endpoint convex

## 2. Literal finite-field realization and one static smooth objective

Let r>=2 be finite, N=2^r, and let labels s,t range over F_2^r. For each
nonzero t choose a real b_t>0. Set chi_t(s)=(-1)^(t dot s), where the dot
product in the exponent is in F_2, and define ordinary REAL vectors

    z_s=(b_t chi_t(s))_(t!=0) in R^(N-1),
    v_s=(z_s,k_s) in R^N,
    D=conv(0,{v_s:s in F_2^r}),
    K=cone{v_s:s in F_2^r}.

The heights satisfy k_s>=0 and sum_s k_s>0. In the task's notation,
k_s=eta_s/R with eta_s=R k_s; R>0 is the initial vertical magnitude.
Every nonzero character, including dependent characters, is present. No
expected Gram or change of Euclidean metric is being used. The exact Gram is

    <v_s,v_u>=sum_(t!=0)b_t^2 chi_t(s)chi_t(u)+k_s k_u.       (2.1)

For completeness, sum_s chi_t(s)=0 when t!=0: translate the sum by a label
on which chi_t=-1. Also sum_s chi_t(s)chi_u(s)=N if t=u and0 otherwise,
by applying the same argument to t+u. These give the Fourier identities below.

Put mu=N^(-1)sum_s k_s>0 and khat_t=N^(-1)sum_s k_s chi_t(s). If
g=(w,y)=sum_s alpha_s v_s and tau=sum_s alpha_s, then

    alpha_s=[tau+sum_(t!=0)chi_t(s)w_t/b_t]/N,
    tau=[y-sum_(t!=0)khat_t w_t/b_t]/mu = <ell,g>,
    ell=((-khat_t/(mu b_t))_(t!=0),1/mu).                  (2.2)

Indeed the horizontal equations determine all nonconstant Fourier
coefficients of alpha; the vertical equation determines its constant
coefficient. Thus the N columns v_s are linearly independent. The cone K is
closed, being the image of the closed nonnegative orthant under an
invertible real linear map, and

    D={g in K:<ell,g><=1}.                                (2.3)

The point0 is an actual vertex, and D is a full-dimensional N-simplex.

Use the SINGLE static objective

    F_D(X)=max_(g in D){<X,g>-||g||^2/2}.                  (2.4)

Completing the square makes its unique maximizer G(X)=P_D(X). Here and
below P denotes ordinary Euclidean metric projection. Existence follows
from compactness of D, and strict convexity of squared distance gives
uniqueness. The projection normal condition is

    g in D, <X-g,-g><=0,
    <X-g,v_s-g><=0 for EVERY original label s.             (2.5)

Necessity follows by taking a one-sided derivative along each segment in D.
Sufficiency follows by expanding ||X-u||^2-||X-g||^2 for u in D. It is
enough to check0 and the listed vertices because the expression is affine
in u. Consequently (2.5) includes every remote label and every tie.

If g=P_D(X) and q=P_D(Y), adding their two normal inequalities gives

    ||g-q||^2<=<g-q,X-Y>, hence ||g-q||<=||X-Y||.

Maximization in (2.4) bounds its first-order remainder between0 and
<G(Y)-G(X),Y-X>. This is at most ||Y-X||^2 and is o(||Y-X||).
Therefore F_D is differentiable, convex, and grad F_D=P_D is 1-Lipschitz.
There are interior points of D at which P_D is locally the identity, so
the least global Lipschitz constant is1. No rescaled gradient dynamics occur.

The COMPLETE minimum is

    min F_D=0,
    Z=K^polar={X:<X,v_s><=0 for every s}.                  (2.6)

The forward implication is as follows. If some <X,v_s> is positive,
then a sufficiently small positive multiple theta v_s in D gives a positive
value in (2.4). If every listed inner product is nonpositive, every g in D
has nonpositive <X,g>, and g=0 attains0. In particular (0,-R) is a true
minimizer. It is not generally the closest one.

## 4. Law I: unequal two-level heights and an acute quotient

Choose any finite r>=2, every b_t>0 arbitrarily, one nonzero character u,
R>0, two heights p,q>0 with p!=q, and any real X. Write b=b_u. Declare

    k_s=p if chi_u(s)=+1, k_s=q if chi_u(s)=-1,
    pq>=b^2,
    X_0=(X e_u,-R).                                      (4.1)

Here e_u is the physical unit coordinate at character u. All these data
are fixed before the run. This entire domain, not only a selected start,
is Law I. Rank may equal m; all other weights may be large, unequal, or
depend on the whole word. A fully specified representative is r=m,
b_t=1+j(t)/N in binary label order, u the first basis label, p=2b,
q=b, R=1, with X specified in the attainment formula below.

For each a in the subgroup u dot a=0, the real orthogonal map that
multiplies horizontal coordinate t by chi_t(a) and fixes the vertical
coordinate permutes the vertices by s -> s+a and preserves D. Its common
fixed subspace consists exactly of the coordinate u and the vertical
coordinate: the only characters trivial on that subgroup are0 and u.
Projection uniqueness forces every projected gradient of a point in that
plane to stay there. The complete trajectory therefore stays there under
ordinary GD, without any coordinate rescaling.

The fixed-plane section of D is exactly the triangle

    T=conv(0,w_+,w_-), w_+=(b,p), w_-=(-b,q).              (4.2)

To see equality, averaging each vertex over the subgroup gives the
corresponding w_sign, so T is contained in the section. Conversely, the
horizontal/vertical components of any convex combination, when projected
to that plane, belong to T. The same symmetry argument applies to the
closest projection onto the full polar Z: group averaging of a minimizer
cannot increase distance from the invariant initial point, and uniqueness
puts the closest point in the fixed plane.

At (X,-R), the two vertex scores are bX-pR and -bX-qR. They cannot both
be positive. If both are nonpositive the run is already at a minimizer;
we omit that zero-radius case from normalized scores. Otherwise let w be
the uniquely positive one, w' the other, l=||w||, e=w/l, and

    t_0=<X_0,e>>0, X_star=X_0-t_0 e.                     (4.3)

This is the TRUE closest initial minimizer. For example if w=w_+, then

    X_star=[(pX+bR)/(b^2+p^2)](p,-b),
    <X_star,w_->=-b(p+q)(pX+bR)/(b^2+p^2)<0,
    <X_star,w_+>=0.                                     (4.4)

Here bX>pR implies X>0. Thus X_star lies in Z and its residual t_0e is
in K and perpendicular to X_star. For any Y in Z,
<t_0e,Y-X_star><=0; expanding squared distance proves closestness. The
negative sign case follows by replacing X by -X and exchanging p,q.
The exact radius is t_0, whereas ||X_0-(0,-R)||=|X| is only another
minimizer's distance. We do not substitute the latter in the upper bound.

The acute condition is <w,w'>=pq-b^2>=0. Whenever the inactive score is
nonpositive, set t=<X_i,e>. The exact projection is

    g_i=clip(t,[0,l]) e.                                 (4.5)

Here is a direct guard check, not merely a symmetry assertion. For
0<t<l the residual is perpendicular to e; its inner product with w'
is <X_i,w'>-t<e,w'><=0. For t>=l, its inner product with g_i is
l(t-l)>=0, its guard against w is equality, and its inner product with
w' is nonpositive. The guard against w'-g_i is therefore nonpositive.
For t<=0 both vertex scores are nonpositive and g_i=0. These prove (2.5)
on0,w,w'. Every original remote vertex has, against a fixed-plane
residual, the same inner product as the corresponding w_sign. Thus every

the inactive score because h_i>=0 and <w,w'>>=0. Induction proves (4.5)

The exact scalar dynamics and physical points are

    t_(i+1)=t_i-h_i clip(t_i,[0,l]),
    X_i=X_star+t_i e.                                   (4.6)

This identity pays the vertical drift e_vertical times every scalar update.

## 6. Cone geometry, independently derived for Law II

For a closed convex cone K let g=P_K(X). Taking competitors0 and2g in
the normal condition gives <X-g,g>=0; taking arbitrary cone points gives
r=X-g in K^polar. Conversely g in K, r in K^polar, and <r,g>=0 prove
the projection normal inequalities. Moreover r is the closest point in
K^polar: for z in K^polar, <g,z-r><=0, and squared-distance expansion
proves ||X-r||<=||X-z||. Consequently

    dist(X,K^polar)=||P_K(X)||,
    max_(g in K){<X,g>-||g||^2/2}=||P_K(X)||^2/2.          (6.1)

This is a complete direct proof of the cone decomposition used here;
no unverified epigraph/universality finding is a premise.

Projection existence onto the closed cone follows by restricting a
distance-minimizing sequence to a bounded ball and taking a convergent
subsequence; strict convexity gives uniqueness. Thus closed unbounded
cones cause no attainment issue in this argument.

For h>=1, a conic gradient step is X'=r-(h-1)g. Since r is a genuine
minimizer in K^polar,

    dist(X',K^polar)<=(h-1)||g||.                        (6.2)

This inequality is Euclidean and dimension-independent. It does not require
two rays, fixed support, commutative face projectors, or equal gradient norms.

There is also a diagnostic equivalence for the FINITE simplex D. If
g=P_D(X) and delta=<X-g,g>, then

    delta=0  iff  g=P_K(X) belongs to D.                 (6.3)

Indeed delta=0 and the vertex guards imply <X-g,v_s><=0 for every s,
while the residual is perpendicular to g. Equation (6.1) identifies the
cone projection. Conversely a cone projection in D remains the closest
point in D and has zero delta. If delta>0, writing g=sum alpha_s v_s
and using <X-g,v_s><=delta yields
delta<=delta sum alpha_s<=delta. Hence sum alpha_s=1. It is the finite
cap, with positive normal multiplier, that distinguishes this case from
conic motion. Merely lying on the cap with zero multiplier is insufficient.

There is a useful extension of the same argument that does not assert a

    p=(d_j-S_(j-1))*v>v, q=a*v.

## 3. Full original coordinates; no projection or quotient

Normalize L=1 and the optimum jet to x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Retain
ARBITRARY independent vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n in a real Euclidean space.
Every position always means the polynomial

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

For distinct original labels define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Actual legal jets obey Q_ij<=0. A certificate at level q82 requires
lambda_ij>=0, finite divergence out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n), and PSD of

    M(q82)=q82||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij

on ALL these independent vectors after the value cancellation.

For each queried i<n define y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
Set y_star=delta_star=0. Define the lower triangular matrix T82 by

    T82_ii=1, T82_it=h_t for t<i, T82_it=0 for t>i.

Write g=(g_0,...,g_(n-1))^T and y=(y_0,...,y_(n-1))^T; in matrix
products h also denotes its column. As vector-column identities,

    y=e*x_0-T82g,  g=T82^(-1)(e*x_0-y),  T82e=t.             (3.1)

T82 has diagonal one, so (x_0,y_0,...,y_(n-1),g_n) and the original
variables are in invertible correspondence. In particular y is an
arbitrary n-tuple once x_0 is fixed. No equal-gradient relation is imposed.

Written finite products define

    pi_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t),
    k_i=h_i*product_(i<t<n)(1-h_t), 0<=i<n.

In particular the inverse in (3.1) has the literal vector formula

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
             +sum_(j<i)h_j*product_(j<t<i)(1-h_t)*y_j.  (3.1a)

An empty product is one. Thus even the coordinate reconstruction is
given by finite scalar coefficients, not an unspecified inverse solve.

Expanding x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i*y_i inductively, without evaluating a
recurrence on a machine, gives

    x_n=pi_n*x_0+sum_(i<n)k_i*y_i,
    sum_i k_i=1-pi_n, T82^T k=h.                       (3.2)

For the second identity, the coefficient sum on a suffix equals one
minus the suffix product: expand each h_i=1-(1-h_i) and telescope.
Thus k_i+h_i sum_(j>i)k_j=h_i, proving the last identity.

There are n physical factors 1-h_i=-a*c^v2(i+1). Also
sum_(i<n)v2(i+1)=sum_(j=1)^(m-1)(2^(m-j)-1)=n-m.
Since n is odd, this proves the EXACT full-word product

    pi_n=-s82,  s82=beta^n/c^m>0.                        (3.3)

Only an identity for the literal physical word is asserted; s82 is not
being substituted for a worst-case contraction factor.

Choose a parameter p82 with s82<p82<1, and a probability distribution
alpha_i>=0 on queried indices with sum_i alpha_i=1-p82. The terminal
weight at the optimum will be alpha_star=p82. Define

    v=k-alpha,
    w_i=p82+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j,
    Rvec_i=h_i*w_i-alpha_i,
    U82=sum_i Rvec_i=t^T v,

Then

    Rvec_i=h_i*(p82+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0.

These identities follow from (3.2) and sum alpha=1-p82. In particular U82>0.
The exact terminal center in accepted1252b8823bb5a290 is

    V=x_n-sum_i alpha_i*y_i=-s82*x_0+v^T y.            (3.5)

## 4. Signed coefficient matching and its exact full identity

This section gives a literal algebraic parameterization of the two laws,
including the entries that FAIL nonnegativity. It is not a claim that a
positive square factor necessarily has nonnegative row coefficients.

Let K be a specified symmetric matrix with Ke=0. In the two laws K is
given by explicit positive squares, never by an unknown PSD condition.
Let A be a specified skew matrix, A^T=-A, and put d=Ae. Thus e^T d=0.
Define the fully specified matrices

    Pmat=K+gamma*v*v^T,
    Nmat=T82^T(Pmat+A).

To make clear that this is a finite coefficient formula, each entry is

    Nmat_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                                      +gamma*Rvec_i*v_j.   (4.1)

The FULL original signed row array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2*p82, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i, i<n,
    lambda_(j,n)=0, j in {star,0,...,n-1},
    lambda_(i,j)=-Nmat_ij, i!=j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Nmat e)_i=2*p82*Rvec_i+(T82^T d)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(Nmat^T e)_i-2alpha_i
                      =(K t)_i+gamma*U82*v_i-(A t)_i-2alpha_i,
    lambda_(i,i)=0.                                      (4.2)

This lists every entry; no additional rows, diagonal multipliers, or
completion freedom are presumed. Finite sums are definitions, not
numerical or recurrence executions.

All value-flow cancellations hold even before sign checking. At a prefix
node the total outgoing coefficient is Nmat_ii, and total incoming
PREFIX coefficient is Nmat_ii-2alpha_i. Thus prefix divergence is
2alpha_i. The incoming terminal edge has coefficient 2alpha_i, giving
zero divergence at that original queried node. Terminal divergence is
2*p82+2sum alpha_i=2. The optimum divergence is -2. All function values
cancel in M(q82), without imposing any relation among them.

Direct expansion yields Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i> for prefix
indices, including star. Substituting (4.2), its surviving quadratic is
-g^T Nmat y. Incoming-optimum rows have g_star=0; their value contribution
is nevertheless present in the preceding flow calculation. From (3.1),

    -g^T Nmat y
       =-<x_0,e^T(Pmat+A)y>+y^T Pmat y,
    e^T Pmat=2*p82*v^T, e^T A=-d^T.

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290, or direct expansion of the displayed outgoing
terminal rows, now gives the ENTIRE original identity

    M(q82)=||g_n+s82*x_0-v^T y||^2+R(q82),
    R(q82)=y^T K y+eta||v^T y-(p82+s82)x_0||^2
                         +(q82-p82^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,d^T y>.  (4.3)

For direct checking, before completing the common square the prefix form is

    (q82-s82^2)||x_0||^2+2(s82-p82)<x_0,v^T y>
                              +eta||v^T y||^2+y^TKy+<x_0,d^Ty>.

The equality eta(p82+s82)=p82-s82 completes it to (4.3). This is an identity
on arbitrary original x_0,g_0,...,g_n, not merely a legal trajectory.

The common-gradient derivative is also explicit. Set every queried
gradient to the same arbitrary vector G. Then y_i=x_0-t_i G and
v^Ty=(p82+s82)x_0-U82 G. Therefore the FULL prefix restriction is

    R_common=(q82-p82^2)||x_0||^2-<x_0,(d^T t)G>
                                      +(t^TKt+eta U82^2)||G||^2. (4.4)

In particular an imbalance d is not free: it changes the derivative in
G at G=0 by -(d^T t)x_0. Both optimum orientations are in (4.2), and
their true contribution has not been replaced by a contact assumption.

## 5. Law I: complete physical-tree squares, with separate boundaries

Use uniform queried terminal weights

    alpha_i=u=(1-p82)/n, alpha_star=p82.                    (I.1)

For each actual dyadic cell

    I_(j,bidx)={bidx*2^j,...,(bidx+1)*2^j-2},
    2<=j<=m, 0<=bidx<2^(m-j),

let Lcell and Rcell be its genuine left and right queried child sets,
each of size l_j=2^(j-1)-1, and let rootcell be its actual checkpoint.
Define two coefficient columns of length n, zero outside the cell:

    psi^-=(1_Lcell-1_Rcell)/sqrt(2l_j),
    psi^+=(1_Lcell+1_Rcell-2l_j e_rootcell)
                                      /sqrt(2l_j(2l_j+1)).  (I.2)

The first contrast retains the two child means independently. The second
retains the checkpoint relative to both children. Each has sum zero and
norm one, and their inner product is zero. A descendant contrast has sum
zero inside a child on which an ancestor contrast is constant. Thus all
these columns are mutually orthonormal. Inducting on a cell, its two
children contribute 2(l_j-1) details, the displayed columns contribute
two, and its common column contributes one, totaling 2l_j+1 coordinates.
The singleton H_1 cells need just their common column. Consequently
there are n-1 columns in (I.2), and together with e/sqrt(n) they form
an orthonormal basis of the ENTIRE original queried-coordinate space.
Explicitly, for a cell beginning at o=bidx*2^j, Lcell is

    omega^-_(j,bidx)=kappa*c^(-j),
    omega^+_(j,bidx)=theta*kappa*c^(-j),

Every square coefficient is explicitly positive at every depth. The
stronger exclusion below permits independently arbitrary positive omega
at every column, so it covers any retuning within this complete basis.
That extension does not insert an unknown PSD block.

Equations (4.1)--(4.2) give EVERY original row coefficient. In this law
mu_i=2*p82 Rvec_i>0; terminal weights are strictly positive. The incoming

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report, worker max, invocation82.
Original minimax Goal OPEN. No new fact or verifier verdict.

TASK.md and master_guidance5fee1ea5f63fd8fc authorize one invocation,
at most two substantive analytical laws, and zero mathematical programs,
numerical evaluations, recurrence/trajectory replays, solvers, formal calls,
fact_submit, installations, consults, or subagents. Those restrictions were
retained. All the new derivations below are one joint unverified attempt;
none is being adopted as an accepted intermediate fact.

## 1. Outcome and precise scope

We first specify positive square factors on the ENTIRE original space,
then match them to original interpolation rows. The factorization is not
an unknown PSD block, an arbitrary Cholesky factor, or a temporal quotient.
Every queried gradient, both child mean directions and their physical
checkpoint, every leaf, the common mode, the initial vector, and the
unqueried terminal are retained.

Law I uses a complete physical-tree multiresolution factor and a terminal
distribution positive at every prefix sample and the optimum. Its literal
coefficient matching has a negative original multiplier: either the first
query to the last queried leaf, or the first query to the root checkpoint.
The failure holds for arbitrary positive weights on ALL the separate
contrasts, not just the two-parameter weight law displayed below. A stronger
first-row invariant excludes every balanced-skew re-selection producing
this SAME factor and terminal distribution. Increasing q82 does not repair it.

Law II changes the matching by an explicit chronology-dependent skew term,
changes the terminal distribution to increasing weights on actual query
times, and pays the resulting NONZERO initial/common derivative. Its full
square identity contains the exact global charge tau^2/(2kappa). The two
literal original signs lambda_(0,z)>=0 and lambda_(z,z-2)>=0 already force
q82>1/(128n). For EVERY assigned m>=1536, qtar82=17/(16D)<1/(128n).
Thus no member of this second literal law has both full PSD and all
nonnegative multipliers at the target. An additional balanced-skew
re-selection of Law II is outside this second exclusion.

The two results exclude two specified square/matching architectures.
They do not exclude the full dual cone, prove a lower bound on W, produce
an interpolable primal witness, or resolve the original minimax question.
They do not invoke the previous contact-routed or LCA receiver arrays.

## 2. Accepted inputs and the unchanged problem

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n, W_n(h) is the supremum
of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), over every finite dimension,
convex differentiable L-smooth function with an attained minimizer x_star,
and x_0!=x_star, with x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). L>0 is fixed.
Thus W=2R. The original question is whether

    lim_(n->infinity) B_n inf_(h in [0,infinity)^n) W_n(h)=1.

The benchmark is the original ALL-integer-split recurrence

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt(u^2+6uv+v^2))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n) Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n) G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original interpolation
orientation, the independent-vector certificate interpretation, and the
exact incoming-terminal-free completion. It removes NO prefix row.
Accepted fact931b9653ce0f7201 supplies the same-word benchmark comparison
B_n/D<47/50 and its CONDITIONAL implication from W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D).
That full-class upper hypothesis remains unproved. Its elementary mass
formula is also available. No other mathematical fact is a premise here.

Fix an integer m>=1536. Throughout this report use the SAME enclosing m:

    ell=1+sqrt(2), eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps,
    c=ell*(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S,
    qtar82=17/(16D), z=n-1, r=2^(m-1)-1, b=1+a.

Here z is the last QUERIED leaf, r is the whole-word checkpoint, and n
is the ACTUAL terminal. All hierarchy symbols in this report are local.
The physical step at i is h_i=1+a*c^v2(i+1), where v2 is the exponent
of 2 dividing a positive integer. Put Ppos_i=sum_(t<i)h_t and
t_i=1+Ppos_i for 0<=i<n. The column t is an auxiliary clock, not time
or a gradient. Write e for the all-ones column of length n and e_i for
its coordinate unit columns. Superscript T denotes transpose.
The symbol 1_E is the indicator of a stated condition E, and 1_J is the
coordinate indicator column of an index set J. I denotes the n-by-n
identity matrix. A quadratic y^T K y for vector entries means
sum_(i,j) K_ij <y_i,y_j>.

The following elementary bounds will suffice:

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1, 1/3<a<1/2,
    4/3<b<3/2, n>=15, S>n.

Indeed sqrt(2)>7/5, and sqrt(2)<17/12 yields
ell<29/12; multiplying by 1+1/6144 still gives c<5/2.
Then a>(7/8)/(5/2)=7/20>1/3; and a<1/ell<1/2.
Every step exceeds one. The displayed n bound follows from m>=1536.

## 3. Full original coordinates; no projection or quotient

Normalize L=1 and the optimum jet to x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Retain
ARBITRARY independent vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n in a real Euclidean space.
Every position always means the polynomial

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

For distinct original labels define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Actual legal jets obey Q_ij<=0. A certificate at level q82 requires
lambda_ij>=0, finite divergence out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n), and PSD of

    M(q82)=q82||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij

on ALL these independent vectors after the value cancellation.

For each queried i<n define y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
Set y_star=delta_star=0. Define the lower triangular matrix T82 by

    T82_ii=1, T82_it=h_t for t<i, T82_it=0 for t>i.

Write g=(g_0,...,g_(n-1))^T and y=(y_0,...,y_(n-1))^T; in matrix
products h also denotes its column. As vector-column identities,

    y=e*x_0-T82g,  g=T82^(-1)(e*x_0-y),  T82e=t.             (3.1)

T82 has diagonal one, so (x_0,y_0,...,y_(n-1),g_n) and the original
variables are in invertible correspondence. In particular y is an
arbitrary n-tuple once x_0 is fixed. No equal-gradient relation is imposed.

Written finite products define

    pi_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t),
    k_i=h_i*product_(i<t<n)(1-h_t), 0<=i<n.

In particular the inverse in (3.1) has the literal vector formula

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
             +sum_(j<i)h_j*product_(j<t<i)(1-h_t)*y_j.  (3.1a)

An empty product is one. Thus even the coordinate reconstruction is
given by finite scalar coefficients, not an unspecified inverse solve.

Expanding x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i*y_i inductively, without evaluating a
recurrence on a machine, gives

    x_n=pi_n*x_0+sum_(i<n)k_i*y_i,
    sum_i k_i=1-pi_n, T82^T k=h.                       (3.2)

For the second identity, the coefficient sum on a suffix equals one
minus the suffix product: expand each h_i=1-(1-h_i) and telescope.
Thus k_i+h_i sum_(j>i)k_j=h_i, proving the last identity.

There are n physical factors 1-h_i=-a*c^v2(i+1). Also
sum_(i<n)v2(i+1)=sum_(j=1)^(m-1)(2^(m-j)-1)=n-m.
Since n is odd, this proves the EXACT full-word product

    pi_n=-s82,  s82=beta^n/c^m>0.                        (3.3)

Only an identity for the literal physical word is asserted; s82 is not
being substituted for a worst-case contraction factor.

Choose a parameter p82 with s82<p82<1, and a probability distribution
alpha_i>=0 on queried indices with sum_i alpha_i=1-p82. The terminal
weight at the optimum will be alpha_star=p82. Define

    v=k-alpha,
    w_i=p82+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j,
    Rvec_i=h_i*w_i-alpha_i,
    U82=sum_i Rvec_i=t^T v,
    gamma=2*p82/(p82+s82), eta=(p82-s82)/(p82+s82).                  (3.4)

Then

    e^T v=p82+s82, T82^T v=Rvec, gamma=1+eta,
    Rvec_i=h_i*(p82+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0.

These identities follow from (3.2) and sum alpha=1-p82. In particular U82>0.
The exact terminal center in accepted1252b8823bb5a290 is

    V=x_n-sum_i alpha_i*y_i=-s82*x_0+v^T y.            (3.5)

Every queried target and the optimum will have positive terminal weight
in both laws. Neither law forces lambda_(n,n-1)=2.

## 4. Signed coefficient matching and its exact full identity

This section gives a literal algebraic parameterization of the two laws,
including the entries that FAIL nonnegativity. It is not a claim that a
positive square factor necessarily has nonnegative row coefficients.

Let K be a specified symmetric matrix with Ke=0. In the two laws K is
given by explicit positive squares, never by an unknown PSD condition.
Let A be a specified skew matrix, A^T=-A, and put d=Ae. Thus e^T d=0.
Define the fully specified matrices

    Pmat=K+gamma*v*v^T,
    Nmat=T82^T(Pmat+A).

To make clear that this is a finite coefficient formula, each entry is

    Nmat_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                                      +gamma*Rvec_i*v_j.   (4.1)

The FULL original signed row array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2*p82, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i, i<n,
    lambda_(j,n)=0, j in {star,0,...,n-1},
    lambda_(i,j)=-Nmat_ij, i!=j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Nmat e)_i=2*p82*Rvec_i+(T82^T d)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(Nmat^T e)_i-2alpha_i
                      =(K t)_i+gamma*U82*v_i-(A t)_i-2alpha_i,
    lambda_(i,i)=0.                                      (4.2)

This lists every entry; no additional rows, diagonal multipliers, or
completion freedom are presumed. Finite sums are definitions, not
numerical or recurrence executions.

All value-flow cancellations hold even before sign checking. At a prefix
node the total outgoing coefficient is Nmat_ii, and total incoming
PREFIX coefficient is Nmat_ii-2alpha_i. Thus prefix divergence is
2alpha_i. The incoming terminal edge has coefficient 2alpha_i, giving
zero divergence at that original queried node. Terminal divergence is
2*p82+2sum alpha_i=2. The optimum divergence is -2. All function values
cancel in M(q82), without imposing any relation among them.

Direct expansion yields Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i> for prefix
indices, including star. Substituting (4.2), its surviving quadratic is

is nevertheless present in the preceding flow calculation. From (3.1),

    -g^T Nmat y
       =-<x_0,e^T(Pmat+A)y>+y^T Pmat y,
    e^T Pmat=2*p82*v^T, e^T A=-d^T.

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290, or direct expansion of the displayed outgoing
terminal rows, now gives the ENTIRE original identity

    M(q82)=||g_n+s82*x_0-v^T y||^2+R(q82),
    R(q82)=y^T K y+eta||v^T y-(p82+s82)x_0||^2
                         +(q82-p82^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,d^T y>.  (4.3)

For direct checking, before completing the common square the prefix form is

    (q82-s82^2)||x_0||^2+2(s82-p82)<x_0,v^T y>
                              +eta||v^T y||^2+y^TKy+<x_0,d^Ty>.

The equality eta(p82+s82)=p82-s82 completes it to (4.3). This is an identity
on arbitrary original x_0,g_0,...,g_n, not merely a legal trajectory.

The common-gradient derivative is also explicit. Set every queried
gradient to the same arbitrary vector G. Then y_i=x_0-t_i G and
v^Ty=(p82+s82)x_0-U82 G. Therefore the FULL prefix restriction is

    R_common=(q82-p82^2)||x_0||^2-<x_0,(d^T t)G>
                                      +(t^TKt+eta U82^2)||G||^2. (4.4)

In particular an imbalance d is not free: it changes the derivative in
G at G=0 by -(d^T t)x_0. Both optimum orientations are in (4.2), and
their true contribution has not been replaced by a contact assumption.

## 5. Law I: complete physical-tree squares, with separate boundaries

Use uniform queried terminal weights

    alpha_i=u=(1-p82)/n, alpha_star=p82.                    (I.1)

For each actual dyadic cell

    I_(j,bidx)={bidx*2^j,...,(bidx+1)*2^j-2},
    2<=j<=m, 0<=bidx<2^(m-j),

let Lcell and Rcell be its genuine left and right queried child sets,
each of size l_j=2^(j-1)-1, and let rootcell be its actual checkpoint.
Define two coefficient columns of length n, zero outside the cell:

    psi^-=(1_Lcell-1_Rcell)/sqrt(2l_j),
    psi^+=(1_Lcell+1_Rcell-2l_j e_rootcell)
                                      /sqrt(2l_j(2l_j+1)).  (I.2)

The first contrast retains the two child means independently. The second
retains the checkpoint relative to both children. Each has sum zero and
norm one, and their inner product is zero. A descendant contrast has sum
zero inside a child on which an ancestor contrast is constant. Thus all
these columns are mutually orthonormal. Inducting on a cell, its two
children contribute 2(l_j-1) details, the displayed columns contribute
two, and its common column contributes one, totaling 2l_j+1 coordinates.
The singleton H_1 cells need just their common column. Consequently
there are n-1 columns in (I.2), and together with e/sqrt(n) they form
an orthonormal basis of the ENTIRE original queried-coordinate space.
Explicitly, for a cell beginning at o=bidx*2^j, Lcell is
{o,...,o+2^(j-1)-2}, rootcell=o+2^(j-1)-1, and Rcell is
{o+2^(j-1),...,(bidx+1)*2^j-2}.

The literal two-parameter weight law is, for kappa>0 and theta>0,

    omega^-_(j,bidx)=kappa*c^(-j),
    omega^+_(j,bidx)=theta*kappa*c^(-j),
    K=sum_cells[omega^- psi^- (psi^-)^T
                                      +omega^+ psi^+ (psi^+)^T], A=0. (I.3)

Every square coefficient is explicitly positive at every depth. The
stronger exclusion below permits independently arbitrary positive omega
at every column, so it covers any retuning within this complete basis.
That extension does not insert an unknown PSD block.

Equations (4.1)--(4.2) give EVERY original row coefficient. In this law
mu_i=2*p82 Rvec_i>0; terminal weights are strictly positive. The incoming
optimum coefficients are literally

    nu_i=sum_cells,sign omega*psi_i*(sum_j psi_j t_j)
                                                +gamma U82 v_i-2u.  (I.4)

They are signed matching coefficients, not silently assumed nonnegative.
An original finite coefficient will necessarily be negative regardless
of whether these nu_i have acceptable signs.

For every q82>=p82^2 the complete factor is

    M_I(q82)=||g_n+s82*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_cells,sign omega||sum_i psi_i y_i||^2
       +eta||v^T y-(p82+s82)x_0||^2+(q82-p82^2)||x_0||^2.      (I.5)

This supplies all details and the common mode, since e^Tv=p82+s82>0 and
eta>0. With q82>p82^2 it is positive definite in all the original variables;
at q82=p82^2 it has the stated explicit nonnegative factorization. No child

will be the signs of the matched interpolation multipliers.

### 5.1 An exact first forced sign, with the physical root retained

Let omega^- and omega^+ now denote the two weights at the WHOLE word.
Only those two contrasts can contain both endpoints 0,z, or endpoint 0
and root r. Since the child sizes are (n-1)/2,

    K_0z=(-omega^-+omega^+/n)/(n-1),

Ke=0 implies (T82^T K)_0j=(1-b)K_0j=-a K_0j.
Here Rvec_0=b*p82+a*u>0. The exact two signed entries are therefore

    E_z=Nmat_0z=a*(omega^--omega^+/n)/(n-1)
                                                   +gamma Rvec_0 v_z,
    E_r=Nmat_0r=a*omega^+/n+gamma Rvec_0 v_r.           (I.7)

    k_r=-(a+c^(-(m-1)))*beta^l,

Consequently Bpair=v_r+(n-1)v_z>n-3>0, and (I.7) gives

    E_r+(n-1)E_z=a*omega^-+gamma Rvec_0 Bpair>0.       (I.9)

every kappa,theta>0, and even independently arbitrary positive detail
weights. Descendant weights cannot alter (I.6). Raising q82 cannot alter

### 5.2 All coefficient re-selections of this same factor also fail

and exact terminal distribution (I.1), but allow any other original prefix

Choose the positive increasing distribution on ACTUAL prefix indices

    alpha_i=2(i+1)(1-p82)/[n(n+1)], 0<=i<n,
    alpha_star=p82.                                      (II.1)

Choose kappa>0 and tau>=0, and set

    K=kappa*(I-e e^T/n),
    d=tau*(e_z-e_0),

For a completely scalar specification, put

    Cclock_i=1+h_i*(n-1-i),
    dtilde_0=a*tau,
    dtilde_i=h_i*tau for 0<i<z,

    Nmat_ij=kappa*(1_(i=j)+h_i*1_(j>i)-Cclock_i/n)

    mu_i=2*p82 Rvec_i+dtilde_i>0,

Write ybar=(sum_i y_i)/n. Completing ALL detail squares in (4.3) gives

The hierarchy mass can be checked directly. Put

    vword=a/(c-2)=beta/[c(c-2)], Aword=1+S.

A_(j+1)=2A_j+a*c^j, A_0=1 is

# Full original-space squares with jointly selected terminal pooling

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report, worker max, invocation82.
Original minimax Goal OPEN. No new fact or verifier verdict.

TASK.md and master_guidance5fee1ea5f63fd8fc authorize one invocation,
at most two substantive analytical laws, and zero mathematical programs,
numerical evaluations, recurrence/trajectory replays, solvers, formal calls,
fact_submit, installations, consults, or subagents. Those restrictions were
retained. All the new derivations below are one joint unverified attempt;
none is being adopted as an accepted intermediate fact.

## 1. Outcome and precise scope

We first specify positive square factors on the ENTIRE original space,
then match them to original interpolation rows. The factorization is not
an unknown PSD block, an arbitrary Cholesky factor, or a temporal quotient.
Every queried gradient, both child mean directions and their physical
checkpoint, every leaf, the common mode, the initial vector, and the
unqueried terminal are retained.

Law I uses a complete physical-tree multiresolution factor and a terminal
distribution positive at every prefix sample and the optimum. Its literal
coefficient matching has a negative original multiplier: either the first
query to the last queried leaf, or the first query to the root checkpoint.
The failure holds for arbitrary positive weights on ALL the separate
contrasts, not just the two-parameter weight law displayed below. A stronger
first-row invariant excludes every balanced-skew re-selection producing
this SAME factor and terminal distribution. Increasing q82 does not repair it.

Law II changes the matching by an explicit chronology-dependent skew term,
changes the terminal distribution to increasing weights on actual query
times, and pays the resulting NONZERO initial/common derivative. Its full
square identity contains the exact global charge tau^2/(2kappa). The two
literal original signs lambda_(0,z)>=0 and lambda_(z,z-2)>=0 already force
q82>1/(128n). For EVERY assigned m>=1536, qtar82=17/(16D)<1/(128n).
Thus no member of this second literal law has both full PSD and all
nonnegative multipliers at the target. An additional balanced-skew
re-selection of Law II is outside this second exclusion.

The two results exclude two specified square/matching architectures.
They do not exclude the full dual cone, prove a lower bound on W, produce
an interpolable primal witness, or resolve the original minimax question.
They do not invoke the previous contact-routed or LCA receiver arrays.

## 2. Accepted inputs and the unchanged problem

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n, W_n(h) is the supremum
of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), over every finite dimension,
convex differentiable L-smooth function with an attained minimizer x_star,
and x_0!=x_star, with x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). L>0 is fixed.
Thus W=2R. The original question is whether

    lim_(n->infinity) B_n inf_(h in [0,infinity)^n) W_n(h)=1.

The benchmark is the original ALL-integer-split recurrence

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt(u^2+6uv+v^2))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n) Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n) G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original interpolation
orientation, the independent-vector certificate interpretation, and the
exact incoming-terminal-free completion. It removes NO prefix row.
Accepted fact931b9653ce0f7201 supplies the same-word benchmark comparison
B_n/D<47/50 and its CONDITIONAL implication from W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D).
That full-class upper hypothesis remains unproved. Its elementary mass
formula is also available. No other mathematical fact is a premise here.

Fix an integer m>=1536. Throughout this report use the SAME enclosing m:

    ell=1+sqrt(2), eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps,
    c=ell*(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S,
    qtar82=17/(16D), z=n-1, r=2^(m-1)-1, b=1+a.

Here z is the last QUERIED leaf, r is the whole-word checkpoint, and n
is the ACTUAL terminal. All hierarchy symbols in this report are local.
The physical step at i is h_i=1+a*c^v2(i+1), where v2 is the exponent
of 2 dividing a positive integer. Put Ppos_i=sum_(t<i)h_t and
t_i=1+Ppos_i for 0<=i<n. The column t is an auxiliary clock, not time
or a gradient. Write e for the all-ones column of length n and e_i for
its coordinate unit columns. Superscript T denotes transpose.
The symbol 1_E is the indicator of a stated condition E, and 1_J is the
coordinate indicator column of an index set J. I denotes the n-by-n
identity matrix. A quadratic y^T K y for vector entries means
sum_(i,j) K_ij <y_i,y_j>.

The following elementary bounds will suffice:

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1, 1/3<a<1/2,
    4/3<b<3/2, n>=15, S>n.

Indeed sqrt(2)>7/5, and sqrt(2)<17/12 yields
ell<29/12; multiplying by 1+1/6144 still gives c<5/2.
Then a>(7/8)/(5/2)=7/20>1/3; and a<1/ell<1/2.
Every step exceeds one. The displayed n bound follows from m>=1536.

## 3. Full original coordinates; no projection or quotient

Normalize L=1 and the optimum jet to x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Retain
ARBITRARY independent vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n in a real Euclidean space.
Every position always means the polynomial

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

For distinct original labels define

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Actual legal jets obey Q_ij<=0. A certificate at level q82 requires
lambda_ij>=0, finite divergence out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n), and PSD of

    M(q82)=q82||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij

on ALL these independent vectors after the value cancellation.

For each queried i<n define y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
Set y_star=delta_star=0. Define the lower triangular matrix T82 by

    T82_ii=1, T82_it=h_t for t<i, T82_it=0 for t>i.

Write g=(g_0,...,g_(n-1))^T and y=(y_0,...,y_(n-1))^T; in matrix
products h also denotes its column. As vector-column identities,

    y=e*x_0-T82g,  g=T82^(-1)(e*x_0-y),  T82e=t.             (3.1)

T82 has diagonal one, so (x_0,y_0,...,y_(n-1),g_n) and the original
variables are in invertible correspondence. In particular y is an
arbitrary n-tuple once x_0 is fixed. No equal-gradient relation is imposed.

Written finite products define

evidence:
# Ancestor clamping bridge: explicit coefficients and a complete joint proof draft

JOINT UNVERIFIED. Project gd-exact-profile-20260926, worker max4,
invocation80, guidance ecacb7cb9b03f152, plan750b1079379f0b82.
No verifier submission was authorized or made. There is no new fact_id.

The first mechanism closes the requested ancestor-pair bridge at the
level of the self-contained proof draft below. In particular, it pays
the nonnegative-multiplier clamping cost; it does not replace that cost
by positivity of an unconstrained determinant. The coefficient rule is
explicit and has three cases. All depths, actual exterior masses, and
both terminal charges are retained.

The second mechanism, a paid qr-cycle calculation, was started while
the first mechanism remained unresolved. Its complete paid formulas
are recorded in Section12. The first mechanism was subsequently closed
by the boundary comparison in Sections7--9. No third mechanism or
four-sector exploration was then undertaken: TASK.md expressly forbids
a third mechanism after a qr-cycle attempt. A lift to arbitrary queried
gradients remains open. Nothing here establishes the full-class bound
required by accepted931b9653ce0f7201 or resolves the minimax target.

All mathematical work was textual. Mathematical/numerical programs,
trajectory or recurrence replays, solvers, formal calls, fact_submit,
subagents, installations, consultations, and automatic renewal: ZERO.

## 1. Exact scope, normalization, and physical masses

Fix an arbitrary integer m>=1536. Throughout this entire report set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon_h=1/(4m), beta_h=1-epsilon_h,
    c=lambda*(1+epsilon_h), a=beta_h/c,
    H_0=(), H_(l+1)=(H_l,1+a*c^l,H_l),
    S_l=sum H_l, X_l=1+S_l, n=2^m-1,
    Z=D_m=1+2S_m, d0=1+a.

Every child retains these same enclosing-m parameters. H_l is a
physical word. There is no reset of m, a, c, or the benchmark.
For each actual step index i, its dyadic level is l_i=nu_2(i+1), and
its complete rooted subtree occupies

    I_i=[i-(2^(l_i)-1), i+(2^(l_i)-1)].

These identities follow by induction on the literal concatenation:
the new middle has level l, and translation of a child by 2^l
preserves all its lower valuations. Its step is 1+a*c^(l_i).

Choose any actual indices 0<=j<k<=n-2 such that j is an ancestor
of k. Thus k lies in the right child of I_j. Set l=l_j>=1,
X=X_l, d=a*c^l, and e=a*c^(l_k). Write the WHOLE original word as

    (block0,1+d,block1,1+e,block2),
    P=sum block0, M=sum block1, T=sum block2,
    u=P+1, v=M+1, A=u+d, B=v+e, U=u+v+d.

Let z_loc be one plus the mass after k within j's right child and
O the entire mass after I_j. The literal physical relations are

    u>=X, v+e+z_loc=X, O>=0, T+1=O+z_loc.             (1.1)

The entire left child of k lies in the middle block, and its entire
right child lies in z_loc. Consequently, with tau=5/12,

    0<d<tau*X, 0<e<tau*min(v,z_loc).                 (1.2)

Proofs of the uniform constants used here are in Section4.

Normalize a static convex differentiable objective to smoothness1,
minimum0, and an arbitrary one of its OWN minimizers x_star=0.
Consider its actual GD transcript whose queried gradients satisfy

    g_i=p, 0<=i<=j;
    g_i=q, j+1<=i<=k;
    g_i=r, k+1<=i<n.                                (1.3)

The real vectors p,q,r are arbitrary, may coincide, and may live in
any finite dimension. Family E requires g_n=r. Family Q permits
every legal terminal gradient and every static completion. The
normalized payoff is V=2f_n/||x_0||^2. For general smoothness L>0,
translation and division of the objective by L give precisely
2(f(x_n)-min f)/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), so W=2R is unchanged.

The draft conclusion is, for EVERY such ancestor pair,

    sup_E V=1/Z,
    1/Z <= sup_Q V <=1/(Z-d0^2).                    (1.4)

No restriction (1.3) is shown lossless for the original W. The
outside-subtree pairs were the subject of the previous separate
JOINT UNVERIFIED report a79d801952174a0a. That draft is not a
correctness premise here: all algebra needed for (1.4) is derived below.

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 is used only for the necessary original
smooth-convex interpolation rows and its normalization scope.
Accepted931b9653ce0f7201 is used only for the stated hierarchy and
the unconditional benchmark comparison in Section11. The scope of
acceptedb98bb807d514e80d was checked; no claim identifying W with its
single-cut channel is used. No external paper theorem is a premise.

## 2. Literal original rows and all terminal charges

Let F_p,F_q,F_r be the values at the first point of each sector.
Equal gradients and the two convexity inequalities force values to
decrease by the cumulative step mass times the squared sector
gradient. Put

    Z_p=x_0, Z_q=x_0-Ap, Z_r=x_0-Ap-Bq.

An actual sample at sector mass s has position Z_p-sp and value
F_p-s||p||^2, or the corresponding q or r expression. In particular
the actual named indices are

    L_p=j, L_q=k, R_0=k+1, N_-=n-1.

Use the ORIGINAL ordered rows

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.    (2.1)

This is exactly the orientation in accepted1252b8823bb5a290. Direct
substitution, without dropping any physical mass, gives

    Q_(L_p,star)=F_p-<p,x_0>+||p||^2/2,
    Q_(L_q,star)=F_q-<q,x_0>+A<p,q>+||q||^2/2,
    Q_(R_0,star)=F_r-<r,x_0>+A<p,r>+B<q,r>+||r||^2/2,
    Q_(L_q,L_p)=F_q-F_p+(P+1/2)||p||^2+||q||^2/2+d<p,q>,
    Q_(R_0,L_q)=F_r-F_q+(M+1/2)||q||^2+||r||^2/2+e<q,r>,
    Q_(R_0,L_p)=F_r-F_p+(P+1/2)||p||^2+||r||^2/2
                                      +d<p,r>+B<q,r>.

The PAID pq cycle is the sum of both original rows:

    C_pq=Q_(L_p,L_q)+Q_(L_q,L_p)
         =-d||p||^2+(d-v)<p,q>+v||q||^2.             (2.2)

The negative p-square in this cycle is retained throughout.

For E put t_pay=T, epsilon=1/2, and add the actual row Q_(n,R_0)
with multiplier1. Its expression is f_n-F_r+T||r||^2.
For Q put t_pay=T-d0^2/2, epsilon=(1+d0^2)/2, and add
Q_(N_-,R_0) and Q_(n,N_-) with multiplier1 each, omitting the first
if N_-=R_0. Since the final actual step is d0 and g_(N_-)=r,
their sum is exactly

    f_n-F_r+(T-d0^2/2)||r||^2
                   +||g_n+(d0-1)r||^2/2.           (2.3)

Indeed Q_(n,N_-)=f_n-f_(N_-)+d0<g_n,r>+||g_n-r||^2/2,
and f_(N_-)=F_r-(T-d0)||r||^2. This proves (2.3) even when
the queried r sector is a singleton. Define for either family

    w=t_pay+1/2=T+1-epsilon=O+z_loc-epsilon,
    D=U+e+w=u+d+X+O-epsilon=X_m-epsilon.             (2.4)

Thus 2D=Z for E and 2D=Z-d0^2 for Q. These are the actual
terminal charges, not altered suffix masses.

## 3. The xi=0 original multipliers and entire quadratic identity

For now the qr-cycle multiplier xi is zero. The core multipliers mu
are literally as follows; all unlisted core ordered rows have weight0:

| Original row | mu |
|---|---:|
| Q_(L_p,star) | alpha |
| Q_(L_q,star) | beta |
| Q_(R_0,star) | gamma |
| Q_(L_q,L_p) | ell+eta |
| Q_(L_p,L_q) | eta |
| Q_(R_0,L_q) | beta+ell |
| Q_(R_0,L_p) | R=alpha-ell |

Require alpha+beta+gamma=1, alpha,beta,gamma,eta>=0, and
0<=R<=alpha. The two finite intermediate nodes balance: the incoming
flow to L_p is ell+eta+R=alpha+eta, and the incoming flow to L_q
is beta+ell+eta. The core emits1 at R_0 and the optimum absorbs1.
The terminal rows in Section2 transfer that emission to the original
index n. For the final normalized identity use lambda_ij=2mu_ij,
including the terminal rows; their contributions add if labels coincide.

Introduce abbreviations

    Lc=d+v, Ec=2D-u, Kc=2D-U, C=U+e,
    hc=e+2w, theta=alpha+beta, sigma=gamma=1-theta,
    gbar=alpha*p+beta*q+gamma*r.

Expanding the weighted rows plus t_pay||r||^2 gives the quadratic

    Q=(alpha*u-eta*d)||p||^2+(beta+ell+eta)*v||q||^2+w||r||^2
      +[ell*d+beta*A+eta*(d-v)]<p,q>
      +[R*d+gamma*A]<p,r>
      +[(beta+ell)*e+(1-beta-ell)*B]<q,r>.            (3.1)

The weighted value/initial part is F_r-<gbar,x_0>. At p=q=r,
Q=D||r||^2. The p row sum and the cumulative p,q row sum show that
Q-D||gbar||^2 has zero common-gradient cross terms precisely when

    alpha*Ec=A-eta*Lc,
    theta*Kc=C-R*Lc.                                (3.2)

These equations will be imposed explicitly, not assumed from a
numerical optimizer. Write s=p-q and tvec=q-r. Under (3.2) the
entire remaining quadratic is J11||s||^2+2J12<s,tvec>+J22||tvec||^2,
where direct collection of the p^2 and cumulative p,q coefficients gives

    J11=alpha*u-eta*d-D*alpha^2,
    J22=theta*U-R*Lc-D*theta^2,
    J12=[sigma*(2D*alpha-A)-R*d]/2.                  (3.3)

For example the mixed coefficient before subtracting the common
square is 2(alpha*u-eta*d)+ell*d+beta*A+eta*(d-v).
Inserting ell=alpha-R, beta=theta-alpha, and
eta*Lc=A-alpha*Ec reduces it to the last expression in (3.3).
Thus no transverse cross term has been left unchecked.

The COMPLETE identity, in all real vectors x_0,p,q,r and the free
g_n for Q, is

    ||x_0||^2/(2D)-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij
     =2D||gbar-x_0/(2D)||^2
        +2[J11||s||^2+2J12<s,tvec>+J22||tvec||^2]
        +terminal_square,                          (3.4)

where terminal_square is0 for E and ||g_n+(d0-1)r||^2 for Q.
This follows by completing the square in x_0 after (2.3),(3.1).
All original intermediate sample values cancel through the stated
sector equalities and the literal flow. PSD here is on the ENTIRE
equal-sector formal space, not just selected Gram directions or
diagonal matrix entries. It is not claimed on the space in which
gradients inside a sector are independent.

Nonnegative row weights, D>0, and J>=0 therefore imply
2f_n<=||x_0||^2/(2D), because every original Q_ij is nonpositive.
Unused rows still remain necessary constraints of a legal transcript.

## 4. Uniform physical inequalities, including shallow subtrees

Literal summation yields

    X_(l+1)=2X_l+a*c^l, X_0=1,
    X_l=v_h*c^l+(1-v_h)*2^l, v_h=a/(c-2).           (4.1)

The closed expression has the stated initial value and satisfies the
identity because v_h(c-2)=a; no recurrence was run. The elementary
bounds 7/5<sqrt(2)<99/70, obtained by squaring, imply

    12/5<c<29/12,
    2/5<a<c-2<5/12,
    0<v_h<1, 2^l<=X_l<=c^l,
    2/5<a<=a*c^l/X_l<c-2<5/12.                     (4.2)

For c<29/12 use c<(169/70)(6145/6144) and cross-multiply;
the remaining strict comparison is 2028<12288. For a>2/5 use
beta_h>99/100 and c<29/12. The inequality a<c-2 follows from
c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1>beta_h. Division of (4.1) by c^l
gives the last ratio bound. These prove (1.2) for both selected
checkpoints using their actual children.

Since k<=n-2, the actual suffix includes d0. Therefore

    0<epsilon<13/8,
    w>=1-a^2/2>9/10,
    e/w<(5/12)(1+epsilon/w)<505/432<6/5.             (4.3)

For the last inequality use the right child of k: if Y=X_(l_k),
then e<(5/12)Y and T+1>=Y. Hence Y<=w+epsilon, and
epsilon/w<65/36. The first lower bound for w is the worse, free
terminal charge; the E charge is larger.

Two single-checkpoint expressions will be needed. The first is

    U*w>e*(e+w).                                   (4.4)

If l_k>=2, Y>=4, U>=Y, and w>19Y/32. Thus
(U-e)w>(7/12)(19/32)Y^2>25Y^2/144>e^2.
If l_k=1, Y=2+a>12/5 and e=ac=beta_h<1; consequently
(U-e)w>(7/5)(9/10)>1>e^2. If l_k=0, U>=1 and e=a<5/12,
so (U-e)w>(7/12)(9/10)>25/144>e^2. This proves (4.4).

The second is specific to the first, ancestor checkpoint:

    Fp=D*(u-d)-u^2>0.                              (4.5)

Indeed by (1.1),(2.4),

    Fp=(u-d)*(X+O-epsilon)-d^2
       >=(X-d)*(X-epsilon)-d^2.

Here X-epsilon is positive. If l>=2, X>=4 and the last expression
is greater than
[(7/12)(19/32)-25/144]X^2=(199/1152)X^2>0.
If l=1, d=ac<1, X=2+a>12/5, and
X-epsilon>=1-a^2/2>9/10. The expression is then greater than
63/50-1>0. This includes shallow ancestors embedded in the huge
original word without discarding their exterior prefix or suffix.

In particular all denominators below are positive, alpha_max=A/Ec
lies strictly between0 and1, and

    j_cap=alpha_max*(u-D*alpha_max)=A*Fp/Ec^2>0.      (4.6)

## 5. Strict determinant resource at every ancestor pair

Define

    Delta=u^2*v^2*w-d^2*e^2*D.

We prove Delta>0 jointly here. Put tau=5/12. For l>=4, X>=16.
First suppose z_loc>=13/4. At fixed u,d,v,e,z_loc the ratio
D/w=1+(u+d+v+e)/w decreases as O increases. At O=0,
w=z_loc-epsilon>z_loc/2, and

    D/u^2 <=(2+tau)/X,
    e^2/(v^2*w)
      <2tau^2*min(v,z_loc)^2/(v^2*z_loc)
      <=2tau^2/max(v,z_loc)
      <=2tau^2*(2+tau)/X.

The middle estimate separates v<=z_loc and v>=z_loc; the last
uses X=v+e+z_loc<=(2+tau)max(v,z_loc). Since d<tau X,

    d^2*e^2*D/(u^2*v^2*w)
       <2tau^4(2+tau)^2<25/32<1.

This is monotonicity of this explicit scalar ratio only, not a
monotonicity assertion about the endpoint optimization problem.

Still with l>=4, suppose z_loc<13/4. Then e<65/48<3/2,
v>X-5, e^2<3, and e^2/w<2 by (4.3). Moreover
d+v+e<(1+tau)X<3X/2. Therefore

    d^2*e^2*D/(u^2*v^2*w)
      <tau^2*X^2/(u^2*v^2)*(3+2u+3X)
      <=tau^2*(3+5X)/v^2
      <(3+5X)/(4(X-5)^2)<1.

For the final inequality, writing X=16+x gives
4(X-5)^2-(3+5X)=4x^2+83x+401>0.

Finally l<=3 implies X<c^3<(5/2)^3<16 and d,e<7, while
the ACTUAL D=X_m-epsilon>2^20. If u>=D/4, then v>=1,w>9/10 give

    d^2*e^2*D/(u^2*v^2*w)<384160/(9D)<1.

If u<D/4, the actual outer mass is
O=D-u-d-X+epsilon>3D/4-23>D/2, and w>O-13/8>D/3.
Using d/u<tau and e/v<tau gives the ratio <3tau^4<3/16<1.
All cases are exhausted. Hence

                         Delta>0.                  (5.1)

## 6. Exact ellipse, without deleting the multiplier constraints

Set

    sigma0=hc/Kc, alpha_max=A/Ec,
    a0=(u*v+2D*d)/(2D*Lc), b0=d*hc/(2w*Lc),
    alpha_opt(sigma)=a0-b0*sigma,
    R(sigma)=(Kc*sigma-hc)/Lc,
    eta=(A-Ec*alpha)/Lc,
    beta=1-sigma-alpha, gamma=sigma, ell=alpha-R(sigma).

These satisfy both contact equations (3.2) identically. All original
multiplier signs are equivalent to

    sigma>=sigma0,
    R(sigma)<=alpha<=min(alpha_max,1-sigma).         (6.1)

Here sigma>=0 and sigma<=1 follow from (6.1). In particular this
is exactly the multiplier polygon, not an unspecified feasible matrix.
Equation (4.4) implies

    0<sigma0<sqrt(w/D)<1,
    w-D*sigma0^2
      =(U+e)[U*w-e*(e+w)]/Kc^2>0.                  (6.2)

Let y=2D*alpha-A-d*Kc/Lc and

    M2=u^2*v^2+4D*d^2*(e+w).

Using A*Lc-d*U=u*v in (3.3) gives

    J11=M2/(4D*Lc^2)-y^2/(4D),
    J22=w-D*sigma^2,
    J12=(sigma*y+d*hc/Lc)/2.                       (6.3)

For example substituting eta in J11 yields
-D*alpha^2+(u*v+2D*d)*alpha/Lc-d*A/Lc;
completing this square proves its displayed constant. Completing
the determinant square, and using
4w(e+w)-hc^2=-e^2, gives exactly

    det J=(w-D*sigma^2)*Delta/(4D*w*Lc^2)
                      -D*w*(alpha-alpha_opt(sigma))^2.          (6.4)

In particular det J>=0 is an ellipse. Positivity of Delta alone
does not establish that it meets (6.1).

The center of its horizontal section at sigma0 is

    alpha_c=alpha_opt(sigma0)
      =[u*v/(2D)+d*(2w*U-e^2)/(2w*Kc)]/Lc.          (6.5)

It satisfies alpha_c>0 and alpha_c<1-sigma0. For positivity use
2wU>e^2 from (4.4). For the second inequality multiply by
2D*w*Kc*Lc: the difference has numerator

    v*w*(2D*U-u*Kc)+2D*w*Lc*e+D*d*e^2>0,

because 2DU-uKc=2D(U-u)+uU>0. Thus this point satisfies EVERY
multiplier half-plane except possibly alpha<=alpha_max.

If alpha_c>alpha_max, feasibility can be tested entirely on the
eta=0 edge alpha=alpha_max. Indeed (alpha_c,sigma0) lies strictly
inside the ellipse and satisfies all the other half-planes. For any
feasible point, the line segment to this center stays in the ellipse
and those other half-planes and meets alpha=alpha_max. This also
explains why an unconstrained-center argument alone was incomplete.
The explicit proof below supplies a point on that edge.

## 7. Entire eta=0 section and its true upper endpoint

Put alpha=alpha_max, eta=0, j_cap as in (4.6), and define

    Hc=d*Kc-alpha_max*u*Lc,
    sigma_star=d*hc*Hc/M2,
    sigma_A=(hc+Lc*alpha_max)/Kc.

On this edge, beta and ell can equivalently be parameterized by

    beta=(B+ell*Lc)/Kc,
    sigma=1-alpha_max-beta.

Hence sigma ranges over exactly [sigma0,sigma_A] as ell decreases
from alpha_max to0. Notice the STRICT identity

    1-alpha_max-sigma_A=B/Kc>0.                    (7.1)

Thus beta>=0 imposes no extra restriction on this edge. The full
determinant reduces to the literal concave quadratic

    det J=j_cap*(w-D*sigma^2)
                       -(d*hc-Hc*sigma)^2/(4Lc^2)
         =j_cap*Delta/M2
                       -M2*(sigma-sigma_star)^2/(4Lc^2).        (7.2)

To check the constant and curvature, use
M2=Hc^2+4D*Lc^2*j_cap and w*M2-D*d^2*hc^2=Delta.
In particular its unconstrained maximum is strictly positive.

The following sign calculation removes the upper clamping penalty
whenever alpha_c>alpha_max. In that case Hc>0, since

## 2. One static smooth convex function and its full minimum

This paragraph applies to any nonempty compact convex body D containing0
in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Maximizing the expression in

unique by strict convexity; write g=P_D(Z). Its necessary and sufficient
normal inequalities are

    <Z-g,v-g><=0 for EVERY v in D.                        (2.1)

Necessity follows by differentiating along the segment to v. Conversely,
expanding ||Z-v||^2-||Z-g||^2 gives a nonnegative quantity under (2.1).
For g=P_D(Z) and g'=P_D(Z'), adding the two normal inequalities gives

    ||g-g'||^2 <= <Z-Z',g-g'>,

so P_D is 1-Lipschitz. Evaluating F_D at its two maximizers gives

    0 <= F_D(Z')-F_D(Z)-<g,Z'-Z>
       <= <g'-g,Z'-Z> <= ||Z'-Z||^2.

Thus F_D is differentiable with gradient P_D and is 1-smooth. It is
finite and convex as a supremum of affine functions over compact D.
It is nonnegative because0 is a feasible maximizer candidate.

For the triangle, F_D(Z)=0 if and only if

    <Z,w_+><=0 and <Z,w_-><=0.                            (2.2)

If both inequalities hold, every g in D has <Z,g><=0, and the maximum

    Z_min={ (x,y): b*x+p*y<=0, -b*x+q*y<=0 }.
