## 3. The angle, the finite caps, and all below-axis projection faces

Define local geometric symbols

    ell_+=sqrt(b^2+p^2), ell_-=sqrt(b^2+q^2),
    e_+=w_+/ell_+, e_-=w_-/ell_-,
    n_+=(p,-b)/ell_+, n_-=(-q,-b)/ell_-,
    M=b^2-pq,
    kappa=M/(ell_+*ell_-), omega=b*(p+q)/(ell_+*ell_-).

Each (e_sigma,n_sigma) is an orthonormal basis; n_sigma points below
its ray. Direct products give

    <e_+,e_->=-kappa,
    <e_+,n_->=<e_-,n_+>=-omega,
    <n_+,n_->=kappa,
    ell_+^2*ell_-^2-M^2=b^2*(p+q)^2.

It follows that kappa,omega are in(0,1) and kappa^2+omega^2=1.
Moreover M<ell_+^2 and M<ell_-^2, since p,q are positive. Hence

    kappa*ell_+ < ell_-,
    kappa*ell_- < ell_+.                                 (3.1)

In particular kappa*max(ell_+,ell_-)<min(ell_+,ell_-).
This proves the proposed compatibility, without assuming it.

For Z=(x,y) with y<0 put t_+=<Z,e_+>, t_-=<Z,e_->. Since

    ell_+*t_+ + ell_-*t_-=(p+q)*y<0,

they cannot both be positive. If neither is positive, Z is in Z_min
and g=0. If t_sigma=t>0, the corresponding horizontal sign is positive
for sigma=+ and negative for sigma=-. In either case

    Z=t*e_sigma+z*n_sigma, z=<Z,n_sigma>>0,
    <Z,e_opposite>=-kappa*t-omega*z<0.                    (3.2)

Here and below opposite means the other of the two signs. Define

    u=min(t,ell_sigma), g=u*e_sigma,
    r=Z-g=(t-u)*e_sigma+z*n_sigma.

The COMPLETE finite vertex normal guards are

    <r,0-g>=-u*(t-u)<=0,
    <r,w_sigma-g>=(ell_sigma-u)*(t-u)=0,
    <r,w_opposite-g>
       =-(t-u)*(kappa*ell_opposite+u)-omega*z*ell_opposite<0.
                                                               (3.3)

Their convex combinations give (2.1) for every point of D. Therefore
this is the unique projection. These formulas establish that below the
axis the only possible projection faces are0, the relative interiors
of the two origin-ray segments, and their finite endpoints. The edge
joining w_+ to w_- and the triangle interior cannot be projection faces
there. Endpoint ties t=ell_sigma are included in (3.3).

For later use define the one-sided Huber value on t>=0,

    phi_ell(t)=t^2/2                 if 0<=t<=ell,
               ell*t-ell^2/2        if t>=ell.

At an active below-axis state, F_D(Z)=phi_(ell_sigma)(t).
Its finite-cap normal height is EXACTLY

    delta=<Z-g,g>=u*(t-u).

Thus delta>0 exactly when t>ell_sigma. A cap-active projection is not
being replaced by conic projection. If t<=ell_sigma then delta=0.

## 4. True initial closest minimum and vertical motion

If Z_0=(X,-R) lies outside Z_min, exactly one initial ray sigma is active:

    sigma=+ if X>p*R/b, rho_0=(b*X-p*R)/ell_+;
    sigma=- if X<-q*R/b, rho_0=(-b*X-q*R)/ell_-.

When -q*R/b<=X<=p*R/b the initial point is a minimum, all later points
are stationary, and the gap is0. Such a point has closest radius0 and
does not enter a positive-radius quotient.

For an active start write Z_0=t_0*e_sigma+z_0*n_sigma as in (3.2).
Set

    Z_star=Z_0-t_0*e_sigma=z_0*n_sigma.

Its two scores are0 and -omega*z_0<0, so it is in the complete polar.
For any U in Z_min,

    <Z_0-Z_star,U-Z_star>=t_0*<e_sigma,U><=0.

Expansion of ||Z_0-U||^2 now shows it is at least t_0^2, with equality
at Z_star. Thus Z_star is the unique closest point and rho_0=t_0.
The nearest point is not assumed to be (0,-R) or the origin.

At any active physical query with h>=0 the vertical coordinate obeys

    y_new=y-h*u*p/ell_+  on the plus ray,
    y_new=y-h*u*q/ell_-  on the minus ray.

It never increases. Since y_0=-R<0, EVERY query and the actual terminal
remain below the axis, and Sections3--4 apply throughout. All diagnostic
steps are strictly positive, so the decrease is strict at active queries.
Every vertical coordinate is updated by actual GD.

## 5. Complete cap/ray/polar transition law

At an active state with ray sigma and coordinates (t,z) from (3.2), take
any physical step h=1+d>1, set u=min(t,ell_sigma), and put

    v=h*u-t, eta=omega*z>0.

The new point is -v*e_sigma+z*n_sigma. Its two ray scores are

    -v, kappa*v-eta.                                    (5.1)

Consequently the FULL transition, with all boundaries, is:

* If v<0, stay on sigma with t_new=-v and z_new=z.
* If v>=0 and kappa*v<=eta, enter Z_min and remain there forever.
* If kappa*v>eta, switch to the opposite ray with

      t_new=kappa*v-eta,
      z_new=omega*v+kappa*z,
      eta_new=(1-kappa^2)*v+kappa*eta.                   (5.2)

In the last case z_new>0. The next projection is on its new ray interior
if t_new<ell_opposite, its endpoint if t_new>=ell_opposite; the normal
height is positive only for strict inequality. The staying case is
classified by the same test against ell_sigma. At v=0 or at equality
kappa*v=eta, both scores are nonpositive and the polar case applies.

These are exact formulas, not a recurrence offered as the final result.
If t<=ell_sigma then v=d*t; if t>ell_sigma then v=h*ell_sigma-t.
Thus every core overshoot, cap persistence, cap-to-core transition,
cross-ray jump, and absorption is specified. In particular every return
loses the positive reserve eta, and changing rays also changes its cap.

For mechanismI, p=q<b gives

    ell_+=ell_-=ell=sqrt(b^2+p^2),
    kappa=(b^2-p^2)/(b^2+p^2), omega=2*b*p/(b^2+p^2).

The initial polar interval is |X|<=p*R/b; outside it,
rho_0=(b*|X|-p*R)/ell. Equations(3.3),(5.1),(5.2), including the
moving vertical coordinate, are the entire symmetric transition law.
The following sections evaluate its whole-word score and also close
mechanismII without any upper bound on ell_+/ell_-.

## 6. Every original query, remote row, terminal row, and optimum row

For each actual physical point including the terminal, let

    f_i=F_D(Z_i)=<Z_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2.

because g_i is in D and r_j is a full normal to D at g_j. This includes

## 7. Asymmetric comparison that retains cap changes and objective weights

Fix the initial active sign sigma_0 and NEVER change this reference.
Let C=ell_(sigma_0) and O=ell_(opposite sigma_0). The two inequalities
(3.1) imply

    O>=kappa*C and kappa*O<=C.                           (7.1)

For r>=0 define an envelope set of possible actual below-axis states:
polar states are allowed; an active sigma_0 state must have amplitude
at most r; an active opposite state must have amplitude at most kappa*r.
There is at most ONE active ray at a time. Call this condition A(r).
Initially A(t_0) holds, with t_0 equal to the true closest radius.

For a step1+d define the scalar nondecreasing envelope

    T_(d,C)(r)=max{d*min(r,C), r-(1+d)*C}.               (7.2)

It is nonnegative since its first term is nonnegative. We claim that
EVERY actual transition from A(r) satisfies A(T_(d,C)(r)).
This is a set inclusion, not an assertion that all such states can be
attained simultaneously.

First note two consequences of (5.1) for an active ray with cap J and
amplitude t<=s. If it stays on that ray, its new amplitude is at most

    (s-h*J)_+.

Indeed for t<=J the signed same-ray output is -d*t<=0; for t>=J
it is t-h*J. If it switches, its amplitude is at most

    kappa*d*min(s,J).                                   (7.3)

For t<=J, h*min(t,J)-t=d*t. For t>=J this expression decreases from
d*J, so its maximum over t<=s is d*min(s,J). The actual switch in
(5.2) subtracts eta>0; dropping eta only enlarges this upper bound.

If the source is sigma_0, the staying amplitude is at most
(r-h*C)_+<=T_(d,C)(r), and (7.3) bounds the opposite amplitude by
kappa*d*min(r,C)<=kappa*T_(d,C)(r).

If the source is opposite sigma_0, its amplitude is at most kappa*r.
The staying bound and the first inequality of (7.1) give

    (kappa*r-h*O)_+
       <=kappa*(r-h*C)_+<=kappa*T_(d,C)(r).

Its return to sigma_0 has amplitude at most
kappa*d*min(kappa*r,O). The SECOND inequality of (7.1) is essential:

    kappa*min(kappa*r,O)<=r,
    kappa*min(kappa*r,O)<=C,

using respectively kappa^2<=1 and kappa*O<=C. Therefore that return
amplitude is at most d*min(r,C)<=T_(d,C)(r). Polar states stay polar.
This proves the claimed inclusion in every case, including cap/core
boundaries and every later return.

The objective comparison also keeps its actual cap. If an A(r) state
is on sigma_0 then its value is at most phi_C(r). If it is opposite,
its value is at most phi_O(kappa*r). For all r>=0,

    phi_O(kappa*r)<=phi_C(r).                            (7.4)

Both sides vanish at0. Their derivatives with respect to r are
kappa*min(kappa*r,O) and min(r,C), and the former is no larger by
the two inequalities just proved. Integrating gives (7.4), including
every change of quadratic/affine objective branch. Thus

    A(r) implies F_D(Z)<=phi_C(r).                       (7.5)

Define r_0=t_0 and, for EACH original chronological step h_i=1+e_i,
define the auxiliary r_(i+1)=T_(e_i,C)(r_i). This is a symbolic finite
definition, never a computed trajectory. Induction on the physical
indices proves A(r_i) for EVERY i including n, and (7.5) gives

    2F_D(Z_n)/t_0^2 <= 2phi_C(r_n)/t_0^2.              (7.6)

The reference cap C and the opposite weight kappa remain fixed from the
original start. No child gets a new reference, a freely optimized
starting state, or a new cap. This resolves the clipping-imbalance
obstruction in the naive common-radius comparison: small caps and
large caps cannot be varied independently of the return angle.

The symmetric mechanism is the special case C=O. It could also use a
common physical radius for both signs, but (7.1)--(7.6) give the stronger
direction-sensitive comparison and do not discard the angle.

## 10. Full finite Walsh lift, all remote vertices, and true full radius

in (3.3), with (2.1), give

    U>4/3+5/8+7/18=169/72>7/3.                       (3.5)

Both laws use these SAME explicit terminal probabilities:

    alpha_star=p, alpha_i=(1-p)rho_i=delta*u_i,
    delta=(1-p)/U, rplus=1-delta, rminus=1+delta,
    v=k-alpha.                                       (3.6)

They sum to1 and are strictly positive on every original queried sample
and the optimum. They are probabilities on real original rows, not on a
selected child interface. Since U>7/3, one has 0<delta<3/7, rplus>1/2,
and 1<rminus<3/2. Precisely

    v_i=rplus*u_i for i even,
    v_i=-rminus*u_i for i odd.                        (3.7)

Several uniform small-initial-weight bounds will be used. The binomial
expansion implies n=2^m-1>m(m-1)/2>128m for m>=1536. Also
(1-eps)^(-n)>(1+eps)^n>=1+n*eps, so beta^n<1/33. From Aword<c^m,
s/p=beta^n*Aword/c^m<beta^n. Because b/a=1+1/a<4,

    s<p/33, u_0<4p/33<p/8,
    alpha_0<p/8, rho_0<3p/56<1/10.                  (3.8)

These are symbolic inequalities uniform in all enclosing m in the task.

## 4. Full original coordinates and the complete signed matching

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep arbitrary independent
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, with every original position defined by

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

The residual orientation is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Legal actual jets obey Q_ij<=0. For i<n let y_i=x_i-g_i and
Delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2, with the corresponding star quantities zero.
Let e be the all-ones column of length n, e_i its coordinate columns, and
T=T82 the lower triangular matrix T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, zero for t>i.
For vector columns g=(g_0,...,g_(n-1)) and y=(y_0,...,y_(n-1)),

    y=e*x_0-Tg, g=T^(-1)(e*x_0-y).                    (4.1)

This is invertible on the ENTIRE formal space. Explicitly, if
pi_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t), then

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
          +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<t<i)(1-h_t)*y_j.  (4.2)

Substitution into x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i*y_i proves

    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y, e^T k=1+s, T^T k=h.           (4.3)

For the latter identity, h_j=1-(1-h_j) telescopes on each suffix:
k_i+h_i sum_(j>i)k_j=h_i. In particular e^T v=p+s.
The cumulative terminal probabilities, distinct from detail weights below,
are Cprob_i=p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j. Define

    R_i=h_i*Cprob_i-alpha_i,
    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, t=Te,
    Uclock=sum_i R_i=t^T v,
    gamma=2p/(p+s), eta=(p-s)/(p+s).

Then T^T v=R and
R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0. Thus Uclock>0,
1<gamma<2, eta>0 and gamma=1+eta. In particular

    R_0=bp+a*alpha_0, H=p+s-v_0=p+alpha_0-s/a,
    bp<R_0<25p/16, 7p/8<H<9p/8.                     (4.4)

The lower bound on H follows from H=p+s-rplus*u_0>p-u_0; its upper
bound follows from the second expression in (4.4).
The actual terminal center is V=-s*x_0+v^T y.

For the moment let w_i>0 be arbitrary DETAIL weights, Ww=sum_i w_i,
and let d be any real column with e^T d=0. Define

    K=diag(w)-w*w^T/Ww,
    A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww+B, B^T=-B, Be=0,
    P=K+gamma*v*v^T, N=T^T(P+A).                     (4.5)

Thus Ke=0, A^T=-A and Ae=d. The matrices are instantiated explicitly in
Sections6 and7; an arbitrary sign-feasible B is NOT a proposed result.
Every scalar entry is

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                                      +gamma*R_i*v_j. (4.6)

The entire ORIGINAL SIGNED coefficient array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,n-1},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for i!=j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i=2p*R_i+(T^T d)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i
                      =(Kt)_i+gamma*Uclock*v_i-(At)_i-2alpha_i,
    lambda_(i,i)=0.                                  (4.7)

Signs are not presumed. This lists every original coefficient, including
both optimum orientations and the actual outgoing terminal distribution.
For each prefix index i, the outgoing sum is N_ii, while the incoming
PREFIX sum is N_ii-2alpha_i. The incoming terminal coefficient2alpha_i
therefore gives zero total divergence at i. Terminal divergence is2;
optimum divergence is-2. Consequently all original sampled values cancel
in M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.

To check the quadratic directly, Q_ij=Delta_i-Delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>
for prefix indices, including star. The prefix value terms cancel the
-2sum alpha_i Delta_i from the outgoing terminal expansion. The remaining
prefix term is -g^T N y. Since N=T^T(P+A), this equals

    -<x_0,e^T(P+A)y>+y^T P y,
    e^T P=2p*v^T, e^T A=-d^T.

The terminal expansion contributes ||g_n-V||^2-||V||^2. Completing the
common square gives the full identity, on arbitrary original vectors,

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2
       +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,d^T y>.                (4.8)

For an expansion check, the unsquared prefix terms are
(q-s^2)||x_0||^2+2(s-p)<x_0,v^T y>+eta||v^T y||^2
+y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>. The relation eta(p+s)=p-s proves (4.8).

## 5. Weighted completion, the real common derivative, and a row invariant

Let ybar_w=sum_i w_i*y_i/Ww. Since sum_i d_i=0, expanding the squares gives

    sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
    =y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>+J||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i d_i^2/w_i.                          (5.1)

Thus the COMPLETE factor is

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2+(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2.  (5.2)

The charge J is paid ONCE globally. No child gradient, common mode, leaf,
checkpoint, terminal square or initial cross derivative has been removed.
The detail form has kernel exactly the constant y columns, because every
w_i>0. The common square controls that remaining direction since e^T v>0.

Full PSD in (5.2) is EQUIVALENT to q>=p^2+J. To prove necessity take scalar
x_0=1, set c0=1+[sum_i v_i*d_i/(2w_i)]/(p+s), y_i=c0-d_i/(2w_i),
and g_n=p. The weighted mean of y is c0 because sum d_i=0. All detail,
common and terminal squares vanish. Reconstruct each original g_i by
(4.2). The value of M is exactly q-p^2-J. This is a formal full-space
negative direction if that quantity is negative; it is NOT an actual
interpolable primal trajectory.

Setting every original queried gradient equal to an arbitrary vector G
instead gives y_i=x_0-t_iG. Directly in (4.8),

    R_common=(q-p^2)||x_0||^2-(d^T t)<x_0,G>
                      +(t^T Kt+eta*Uclock^2)||G||^2. (5.3)

The genuine nonzero initial/common derivative is -(d^T t)x_0. A balanced
B changes neither this derivative nor the full square polynomial.

Now derive the original FIRST-ROW off-diagonal sum including d_0.
The first column of T is (1,b,...,b)^T. Since K has column sums zero,
(T^T K)_00=-a*K_00. Skewness gives A_00=0, and e^T A=-d^T gives
(T^T A)_00=-b*d_0. Meanwhile (T^T d)_0=-a*d_0. Subtracting the diagonal
from the row sum in (4.7) yields

    sum_(j>0) N_0j
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*(p+s-v_0)+d_0
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H+d_0.                     (5.4)

Every balanced B leaves this sum invariant. Nonnegative finite first-row
multipliers require the right side to be <=0. A balanced correction can
redistribute that sum among entries; it cannot change the sum itself.

There is also an exact inverse-metric price for this invariant. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz on i>0 gives
sum_(i>0)d_i^2/w_i >=d_0^2/(Ww-w_0), since sum_(i>0)d_i=-d_0.
Consequently

    J>=d_0^2/(4*K_00), K_00=w_0(1-w_0/Ww).          (5.5)

Equality holds precisely when d_i=-d_0*w_i/(Ww-w_0) for every i>0.
Because H>0, (5.4)--(5.5) imply for any nonnegative first row

    J>=(a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H)^2/(4*K_00)
      >=a*gamma*R_0*H.                               (5.6)

The final inequality expands the nonnegative square
(a*K_00-gamma*R_0*H)^2. This is a necessary first-row screen, NOT a
sufficient certificate condition. The two selected laws now instantiate
all weights and skew matrices rather than leaving the screen unsolved.

## 6. Law A: exact tail metric with minimum-price distributed imbalance

For EVERY kappa>0 and tau>=0 choose

    w_i=kappa*u_i, Ww=kappa*U,
    d=tau*(rho-e_0),
    A_A=tau*(rho*e_0^T-e_0*rho^T), B_A=0.             (6.1)

Here A_A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww exactly, and A_A e=d. The imbalance is
negative at0 and positive at EVERY other actual queried index, not just
at one endpoint. It attains equality in (5.5). The metric is nonisotropic
because u_0<p/8 whereas u_z=b>4/3. The terminal probabilities remain (3.6).

The exact global charge and common derivative are

    J_A=tau^2*(1-rho_0)/(4*kappa*u_0),
    d^T t=tau*(tbar-1), tbar=sum_i rho_i*t_i.          (6.2)

Thus (5.2) is a fully specified factor iff q>=p^2+J_A.
For a literal scalar description of EVERY finite entry put
F_i=u_i+h_i sum_(j>i)u_j. Then

    N^A_ij=kappa*(u_i*1_(i=j)+h_i*u_j*1_(j>i)-F_i*rho_j)
          +gamma*R_i*v_j
          +tau*((F_i/U)*1_(j=0)-1_(i=0)*rho_j).      (6.3)

Together with (4.7), this is the complete array. Both optimum orientations
can also be written explicitly:

    mu_0=2p*R_0+a*tau*(1-rho_0)>0,
    mu_i=2p*R_i+tau*F_i/U>0 for i>0,
    nu^A_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)+gamma*Uclock*v_i
                         -tau*(rho_i-1_(i=0)*tbar)-2alpha_i. (6.4)

All terminal outgoing signs and all outgoing optimum signs pass. No sign
is silently assigned to nu^A or an off-diagonal -N^A.

### 6.1 A first-row charge obstruction at the assigned target

Since v_z=rplus*u_z, the actual first-to-last queried entry is

    N^A_0z=rho_z*(a*kappa*u_0-tau)
                                +gamma*R_0*rplus*u_z. (6.5)

If lambda_(0,z)=-N^A_0z>=0, positivity of rho_z gives

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*(U-1+p).               (6.6)

Apply (a*x+C)^2/(4x)>=a*C for x=kappa*u_0>0 and
C=gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)>0. Equations (6.2) and (6.6) imply

    J_A>=a*gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)*(1-rho_0)
       >(4/9)*p*(4/3)*(9/10)=8p/15.                (6.7)

The strict lower bounds use a*b>4/9, gamma>1, R_0>bp, U>7/3 and
rho_0<1/10. On the other hand Aword>128 gives

    qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]<8/15,             (6.8)

because this inequality is equivalent to Aword>128. Thus no member of
Law A has both full PSD and lambda_(0,z)>=0 at q<=qtar. This argument
uses the exact SINGLE global charge and no local Schur-budget summation.

### 6.2 A stronger literal incoming-optimum failure for every q

The weighted clock is uniformly large. By (3.3)--(3.5), t_z>n and
n>2^(m-1), so

    tbar>=rho_z*t_z> b*n/[2*(3/2)^m]
                     >(1/3)*(4/3)^m>27.             (6.9)

For the last inequality m>=16 and (4/3)^4=256/81>3, so (4/3)^16>81.
Meanwhile t_1=1+b<5/2<tbar/2. Query1 has v_1=-rminus*u_1<0.
In (6.4) its metric term is strictly negative, its rank term is strictly
negative, its skew term is nonpositive, and -2alpha_1 is strictly negative.
Hence

    nu^A_1=lambda_(star,1)<0                         (6.10)

for EVERY m>=1536, kappa>0, tau>=0 and every real q. This excludes

one such correction explicitly; it is not dismissed by (6.10).

## 7. Law B: an explicit balanced transport that repairs the entire first row

Keep the SAME w,d,alpha,p and arbitrary kappa>0,tau>=0 as in Law A.
Define the probability column on noninitial queried samples

    r_0^pool=0, r_i^pool=u_i/(U-u_0) for i>0,
    chi=e_0-r^pool,
    xi=gamma*R_0/a,
    bvec_0=0, bvec_i=xi*(v_i-H*r_i^pool) for i>0,
    B_B=chi*bvec^T-bvec*chi^T,
    A_B=A_A+B_B.                                     (7.1)

The r^pool column is distinct from the suffix product r_L. Its denominator
is positive, and its entries sum to1. Since sum_(i>0)v_i=H, both chi and
bvec have sum zero. Therefore B_B is skew AND B_B e=0. In particular
A_B e=d, and the entire factor (5.2), charge (6.2), and real derivative
(5.3) are unchanged. There is no hidden skew unknown in this law.

For complete scalar coefficients define
C_i=chi_i+h_i sum_(j>i)chi_j and
E_i=bvec_i+h_i sum_(j>i)bvec_j. Then

    N^B_ij=N^A_ij+C_i*bvec_j-E_i*chi_j.              (7.2)

Equations (4.7), (6.3), (7.1)--(7.2) specify EVERY original coefficient.
The outgoing optimum coefficients are still the strictly positive mu_i
in (6.4). The incoming optimum coefficients are

    nu^B_i=nu^A_i-chi_i*(bvec^T t)+bvec_i*(chi^T t).  (7.3)

No positivity of these incoming coefficients is assumed.

### 7.1 The entire first row is explicitly equalized

For j>0, B_B,0j=bvec_j. Because B_B has zero column sums,
(T^T B_B)_0j=-a*bvec_j. Substituting (7.1) in (6.3) yields

    N^B_0j=r_j^pool*S0,
    S0=(a*kappa*u_0-tau)*(1-rho_0)+gamma*R_0*H.      (7.4)

In particular ALL original finite first-row multipliers are nonnegative
iff S0<=0, equivalently

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).           (7.5)

This realizes the invariant (5.4), rather than assuming it can be repaired.
It changes the demanding Law A quantity U-1+p in (6.6) to the much smaller
H/(1-rho_0). Thus the Law A charge obstruction does NOT transfer to Law B.

The simultaneous first-row and full-PSD conditions at qtar are nonvacuous.
Within this same two-parameter law choose the explicit member

    kappa_0=gamma*R_0*H/[a*u_0*(1-rho_0)],
    tau_0=2*gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).                    (7.6)

These are positive. Equation (7.4) gives N^B_0j=0 for every j>0, and
J_A=a*gamma*R_0*H. From (2.1), gamma<2 and (4.4),

    J_A< (25p/16)*(9p/8)=225p^2/128<2p^2.

Consequently p^2+J_A<3p^2<p/2<qtar, because p<1/128 and
qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]>17/32>1/2. This is a strictly positive
full factor at the target with all finite first-row multipliers zero,
positive terminal probabilities, and positive outgoing optimum multipliers.
It remains a FAILED certificate because the complete array still has a
negative original coefficient, as the next subsection proves.

### 7.2 Last-to-previous-leaf versus incoming optimum1: exhaustive sign conflict

Let j=z-2, the genuine preceding queried leaf. Both z and j are even.
For i,j>0 the balanced correction has the explicit entry

    B_B,ij=xi*(v_i*r_j^pool-r_i^pool*v_j).            (7.7)

By (3.7), v_z/u_z=v_j/u_j=rplus. Therefore B_B,zj=0. Also
A_A,zj=0. The last row of T^T is the last coordinate row, so exactly

    N^B_zj=u_z*u_j*(-kappa/U+gamma*rplus^2).          (7.8)

If kappa<gamma*U*rplus^2, this entry is positive and the ORIGINAL
lambda_(z,z-2) is negative. Otherwise its sign passes and necessarily

    kappa>=gamma*U*rplus^2>7/12.                     (7.9)

The strict lower bound follows from gamma>1, U>7/3 and rplus>1/2.
We now prove that throughout this remaining domain nu^B_1 is negative.

Put tpool=sum_i r_i^pool*t_i=(tbar-rho_0)/(1-rho_0). Then
bvec^T t=xi*(Uclock-v_0-H*tpool), chi^T t=1-tpool.
For i>0, using (7.3) gives the exact expression

    nu^B_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)
       +[gamma*Uclock-xi*(tpool-1)]*v_i
       +xi*r_i^pool*(Uclock-(p+s))-tau*rho_i-2alpha_i. (7.10)

This includes the actual initial clock t_0=1 in BOTH appearances of
(tpool-1) and (p+s); omitting it would change the optimum row.
At query1, divide by the positive u_1 and use v_1/u_1=-rminus:

    nu^B_1/u_1=kappa*(t_1-tbar)
       +[-gamma*rminus+xi/(U-u_0)]*Uclock
       +xi*rminus*(tpool-1)-xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0)
       -tau/U-2delta.                                (7.11)

All signs in this expression can be bounded uniformly. Since b/a<4,
alpha_0<p/8, and gamma<2,

    xi=gamma*(bp/a+alpha_0)<2*(4p+p/8)<9p.           (7.12)

Also U-u_0>7/3-1/8>2. With p<1/128, (7.12) implies
xi/(U-u_0)<9p/2<1<gamma*rminus. Thus the coefficient of Uclock in
(7.11) is negative; Uclock>0. The terms -xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0), -tau/U and
-2delta are nonpositive, with the first and last strictly negative.
Further,

    tpool < tbar/(1-rho_0),
    xi*rminus*tpool < (9p)*(3/2)*(10/9)*tbar
                                      =15p*tbar.    (7.13)

Since t_1<tbar/2 by (6.9), dropping the negative terms in (7.11) gives

    nu^B_1/u_1<(-kappa/2+15p)*tbar<0.               (7.14)

For the final strict sign, (7.9) gives kappa/2>7/24, whereas
15p<15/128<7/24. All denominators and u_1,tbar are positive.

Combining (7.8) and (7.14) covers EVERY kappa>0,tau>=0, with no assumption
on PSD or the first-row signs: either lambda_(z,z-2)<0, or
lambda_(star,1)=nu^B_1<0. At equality kappa=gamma*U*rplus^2, (7.9) and
(7.14) still apply. This excludes the WHOLE displayed Law B domain at any
q, in particular every full-PSD member at qtar, including (7.6).

This conflict concerns the literal balanced correction (7.1). Another
balanced matrix can change the pair (7.8), the optimum row (7.11), or both.
No universal exclusion of balanced re-selection is asserted.

## 8. Boundary, sign and scope audit

* All enclosing integers m>=1536 are treated with the SAME beta,c,a at
  every child. No finite numerical horizon test or reset is used.
* The probabilities at every original queried target and at the optimum
  are strictly positive. The actual terminal gradient remains free, with
  its exact square retained. No earlier remote row is removed.
* The variance metric controls all n-1 independent detail directions.
  The independent common direction and its real derivative are retained.
* Every finite and optimum coefficient has a literal scalar formula.
  Terminal and outgoing-optimum signs pass for both laws. Incoming-optimum
  and finite signs fail as proved; no signed row is called a certificate.
* tau=0 is allowed and covered; kappa>0 is necessary for the specified
  positive metric. Equality in PSD and in the tail sign has been covered.
* Balanced B_B e=0 is checked explicitly, and the initial clock contribution
  is retained in the exact incoming-optimum formula. This is not the old
  isotropic endpoint correction or the old physical-tree uniform pool.
* The first-row invariant includes d_0. Its inverse-metric charge is paid
  once, with an explicit global square-zero direction proving necessity.
* Formal negative directions are not actual trajectories. Failure of these
  two coefficient laws gives no lower bound on W and no global no-certificate
  theorem. Fact931's missing full-function hypothesis remains unproved.

The row identities and inequalities above have received a textual author
audit only. They are not verifier-accepted facts, and no downstream argument
may treat this report as an accepted building block.

## 9. Retrieval, failure synthesis and handoff

The query-memory, immediate-conclusions, direct-proving,
construct-counterexamples and identify-key-failures procedures guided this
bounded joint attempt. The fact search found no accepted version of the
new weighted first-row identity or these two row laws. Current guidance
was recalled by its targeted query after an empty-string query returned
count0. Oversized initial recall output was truncated; the relevant old
joint report and accepted inputs were reread in bounded portions.

A repair-mode Matlas search for full PSD weighted interpolation certificates
returned unrelated PL, stochastic and constant-step statements; none was
used. Web search located Altschuler--Parrilo, 'Acceleration by Stepsize
Hedging II: Silver Stepsize Schedule for Smooth Convex Optimization',
arXiv:2309.16530, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16530, already read in the prior
round as exact proof-pattern background. No external theorem or proof step
is imported here. The new laws reduce to explicit coefficient identities
in that already-audited interpolation regime; no additional literature
layer or new mathematical machinery is needed for these scoped algebraic
rejections. No notebook or numerical certificate was run.

Law A's failure is not caused by forgetting tail scales: it uses them in
both the metric and terminal distribution, and its imbalance is optimally
distributed for its fixed initial component. Its literal first-to-last row
still overcharges, and the early negative-k incoming optimum row fails.

Law B demonstrates a real escape from Law A's first-row charge argument:
an explicit balanced transport repairs the entire row at affordable full
PSD cost. Its remaining failure is a different, complete-original-array
conflict: a same-sign pair of late queried leaves fixes a nonvanishing
metric scale, while the early odd query sits below the weighted mean clock
and has negative terminal coefficient. The specified transport is too
small to pay that original optimum row at that forced metric scale.

The next missing mechanism would have to alter this second conflict, for
example through a different balanced transport affecting the relevant
late pair and optimum load, a different genuinely nonisotropic metric, or
a different actual terminal law. These are uncovered freedoms, not a third
law attempted in this invocation and not a solution by an unknown matrix.
The first-row invariant (5.4) and its charge (5.5) remain necessary checks
in the stated general architecture; their sufficiency has not been claimed.

## 1. Outcome and exact scope

Neither exclusion is an impossibility theorem for all balanced corrections,

pi_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t), then

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
          +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<t<i)(1-h_t)*y_j.  (4.2)

Substitution into x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i*y_i proves

    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y, e^T k=1+s, T^T k=h.           (4.3)

For the latter identity, h_j=1-(1-h_j) telescopes on each suffix:
k_i+h_i sum_(j>i)k_j=h_i. In particular e^T v=p+s.
The cumulative terminal probabilities, distinct from detail weights below,
are Cprob_i=p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j. Define

    R_i=h_i*Cprob_i-alpha_i,
    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, t=Te,
    Uclock=sum_i R_i=t^T v,
    gamma=2p/(p+s), eta=(p-s)/(p+s).

Then T^T v=R and
R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0. Thus Uclock>0,
1<gamma<2, eta>0 and gamma=1+eta. In particular

    R_0=bp+a*alpha_0, H=p+s-v_0=p+alpha_0-s/a,
    bp<R_0<25p/16, 7p/8<H<9p/8.                     (4.4)

The lower bound on H follows from H=p+s-rplus*u_0>p-u_0; its upper
bound follows from the second expression in (4.4).
The actual terminal center is V=-s*x_0+v^T y.

For the moment let w_i>0 be arbitrary DETAIL weights, Ww=sum_i w_i,
and let d be any real column with e^T d=0. Define

    K=diag(w)-w*w^T/Ww,
    A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww+B, B^T=-B, Be=0,
    P=K+gamma*v*v^T, N=T^T(P+A).                     (4.5)

Thus Ke=0, A^T=-A and Ae=d. The matrices are instantiated explicitly in
Sections6 and7; an arbitrary sign-feasible B is NOT a proposed result.
Every scalar entry is

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                                      +gamma*R_i*v_j. (4.6)

The entire ORIGINAL SIGNED coefficient array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,n-1},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for i!=j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i=2p*R_i+(T^T d)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i
                      =(Kt)_i+gamma*Uclock*v_i-(At)_i-2alpha_i,
    lambda_(i,i)=0.                                  (4.7)

Signs are not presumed. This lists every original coefficient, including
both optimum orientations and the actual outgoing terminal distribution.
For each prefix index i, the outgoing sum is N_ii, while the incoming
PREFIX sum is N_ii-2alpha_i. The incoming terminal coefficient2alpha_i
therefore gives zero total divergence at i. Terminal divergence is2;
optimum divergence is-2. Consequently all original sampled values cancel
in M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.

To check the quadratic directly, Q_ij=Delta_i-Delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>
for prefix indices, including star. The prefix value terms cancel the
-2sum alpha_i Delta_i from the outgoing terminal expansion. The remaining
prefix term is -g^T N y. Since N=T^T(P+A), this equals

    -<x_0,e^T(P+A)y>+y^T P y,
    e^T P=2p*v^T, e^T A=-d^T.

The terminal expansion contributes ||g_n-V||^2-||V||^2. Completing the
common square gives the full identity, on arbitrary original vectors,

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2
       +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,d^T y>.                (4.8)

For an expansion check, the unsquared prefix terms are
(q-s^2)||x_0||^2+2(s-p)<x_0,v^T y>+eta||v^T y||^2
+y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>. The relation eta(p+s)=p-s proves (4.8).

## 5. Weighted completion, the real common derivative, and a row invariant

Let ybar_w=sum_i w_i*y_i/Ww. Since sum_i d_i=0, expanding the squares gives

    sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
    =y^T K y+<x_0,d^T y>+J||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i d_i^2/w_i.                          (5.1)

Thus the COMPLETE factor is

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2+(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2.  (5.2)

The charge J is paid ONCE globally. No child gradient, common mode, leaf,
checkpoint, terminal square or initial cross derivative has been removed.
The detail form has kernel exactly the constant y columns, because every
w_i>0. The common square controls that remaining direction since e^T v>0.

Full PSD in (5.2) is EQUIVALENT to q>=p^2+J. To prove necessity take scalar
x_0=1, set c0=1+[sum_i v_i*d_i/(2w_i)]/(p+s), y_i=c0-d_i/(2w_i),
and g_n=p. The weighted mean of y is c0 because sum d_i=0. All detail,
common and terminal squares vanish. Reconstruct each original g_i by
(4.2). The value of M is exactly q-p^2-J. This is a formal full-space
negative direction if that quantity is negative; it is NOT an actual
interpolable primal trajectory.

Setting every original queried gradient equal to an arbitrary vector G
instead gives y_i=x_0-t_iG. Directly in (4.8),

    R_common=(q-p^2)||x_0||^2-(d^T t)<x_0,G>
                      +(t^T Kt+eta*Uclock^2)||G||^2. (5.3)

The genuine nonzero initial/common derivative is -(d^T t)x_0. A balanced
B changes neither this derivative nor the full square polynomial.

Now derive the original FIRST-ROW off-diagonal sum including d_0.
The first column of T is (1,b,...,b)^T. Since K has column sums zero,
(T^T K)_00=-a*K_00. Skewness gives A_00=0, and e^T A=-d^T gives
(T^T A)_00=-b*d_0. Meanwhile (T^T d)_0=-a*d_0. Subtracting the diagonal
from the row sum in (4.7) yields

    sum_(j>0) N_0j
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*(p+s-v_0)+d_0
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H+d_0.                     (5.4)

Every balanced B leaves this sum invariant. Nonnegative finite first-row
multipliers require the right side to be <=0. A balanced correction can
redistribute that sum among entries; it cannot change the sum itself.

There is also an exact inverse-metric price for this invariant. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz on i>0 gives
sum_(i>0)d_i^2/w_i >=d_0^2/(Ww-w_0), since sum_(i>0)d_i=-d_0.
Consequently

    J>=d_0^2/(4*K_00), K_00=w_0(1-w_0/Ww).          (5.5)

Equality holds precisely when d_i=-d_0*w_i/(Ww-w_0) for every i>0.
Because H>0, (5.4)--(5.5) imply for any nonnegative first row

    J>=(a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H)^2/(4*K_00)
      >=a*gamma*R_0*H.                               (5.6)

The final inequality expands the nonnegative square
(a*K_00-gamma*R_0*H)^2. This is a necessary first-row screen, NOT a
sufficient certificate condition. The two selected laws now instantiate
all weights and skew matrices rather than leaving the screen unsolved.

## 6. Law A: exact tail metric with minimum-price distributed imbalance

For EVERY kappa>0 and tau>=0 choose

    w_i=kappa*u_i, Ww=kappa*U,
    d=tau*(rho-e_0),
    A_A=tau*(rho*e_0^T-e_0*rho^T), B_A=0.             (6.1)

Here A_A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww exactly, and A_A e=d. The imbalance is
negative at0 and positive at EVERY other actual queried index, not just
at one endpoint. It attains equality in (5.5). The metric is nonisotropic
because u_0<p/8 whereas u_z=b>4/3. The terminal probabilities remain (3.6).

The exact global charge and common derivative are

    J_A=tau^2*(1-rho_0)/(4*kappa*u_0),
    d^T t=tau*(tbar-1), tbar=sum_i rho_i*t_i.          (6.2)

Thus (5.2) is a fully specified factor iff q>=p^2+J_A.
For a literal scalar description of EVERY finite entry put
F_i=u_i+h_i sum_(j>i)u_j. Then

    N^A_ij=kappa*(u_i*1_(i=j)+h_i*u_j*1_(j>i)-F_i*rho_j)
          +gamma*R_i*v_j
          +tau*((F_i/U)*1_(j=0)-1_(i=0)*rho_j).      (6.3)

Together with (4.7), this is the complete array. Both optimum orientations
can also be written explicitly:

    mu_0=2p*R_0+a*tau*(1-rho_0)>0,
    mu_i=2p*R_i+tau*F_i/U>0 for i>0,
    nu^A_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)+gamma*Uclock*v_i
                         -tau*(rho_i-1_(i=0)*tbar)-2alpha_i. (6.4)

All terminal outgoing signs and all outgoing optimum signs pass. No sign
is silently assigned to nu^A or an off-diagonal -N^A.

### 6.1 A first-row charge obstruction at the assigned target

Since v_z=rplus*u_z, the actual first-to-last queried entry is

    N^A_0z=rho_z*(a*kappa*u_0-tau)
                                +gamma*R_0*rplus*u_z. (6.5)

If lambda_(0,z)=-N^A_0z>=0, positivity of rho_z gives

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*(U-1+p).               (6.6)

Apply (a*x+C)^2/(4x)>=a*C for x=kappa*u_0>0 and
C=gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)>0. Equations (6.2) and (6.6) imply

    J_A>=a*gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)*(1-rho_0)
       >(4/9)*p*(4/3)*(9/10)=8p/15.                (6.7)

The strict lower bounds use a*b>4/9, gamma>1, R_0>bp, U>7/3 and
rho_0<1/10. On the other hand Aword>128 gives

    qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]<8/15,             (6.8)

because this inequality is equivalent to Aword>128. Thus no member of
Law A has both full PSD and lambda_(0,z)>=0 at q<=qtar. This argument
uses the exact SINGLE global charge and no local Schur-budget summation.

### 6.2 A stronger literal incoming-optimum failure for every q

The weighted clock is uniformly large. By (3.3)--(3.5), t_z>n and
n>2^(m-1), so

    tbar>=rho_z*t_z> b*n/[2*(3/2)^m]
                     >(1/3)*(4/3)^m>27.             (6.9)

For the last inequality m>=16 and (4/3)^4=256/81>3, so (4/3)^16>81.
Meanwhile t_1=1+b<5/2<tbar/2. Query1 has v_1=-rminus*u_1<0.
In (6.4) its metric term is strictly negative, its rank term is strictly
negative, its skew term is nonpositive, and -2alpha_1 is strictly negative.
Hence

    nu^A_1=lambda_(star,1)<0                         (6.10)

for EVERY m>=1536, kappa>0, tau>=0 and every real q. This excludes

one such correction explicitly; it is not dismissed by (6.10).

## 7. Law B: an explicit balanced transport that repairs the entire first row

Keep the SAME w,d,alpha,p and arbitrary kappa>0,tau>=0 as in Law A.
Define the probability column on noninitial queried samples

    r_0^pool=0, r_i^pool=u_i/(U-u_0) for i>0,
    chi=e_0-r^pool,
    xi=gamma*R_0/a,
    bvec_0=0, bvec_i=xi*(v_i-H*r_i^pool) for i>0,
    B_B=chi*bvec^T-bvec*chi^T,
    A_B=A_A+B_B.                                     (7.1)

The r^pool column is distinct from the suffix product r_L. Its denominator
is positive, and its entries sum to1. Since sum_(i>0)v_i=H, both chi and
bvec have sum zero. Therefore B_B is skew AND B_B e=0. In particular
A_B e=d, and the entire factor (5.2), charge (6.2), and real derivative
(5.3) are unchanged. There is no hidden skew unknown in this law.

For complete scalar coefficients define
C_i=chi_i+h_i sum_(j>i)chi_j and
E_i=bvec_i+h_i sum_(j>i)bvec_j. Then

    N^B_ij=N^A_ij+C_i*bvec_j-E_i*chi_j.              (7.2)

Equations (4.7), (6.3), (7.1)--(7.2) specify EVERY original coefficient.
The outgoing optimum coefficients are still the strictly positive mu_i
in (6.4). The incoming optimum coefficients are

    nu^B_i=nu^A_i-chi_i*(bvec^T t)+bvec_i*(chi^T t).  (7.3)

No positivity of these incoming coefficients is assumed.

### 7.1 The entire first row is explicitly equalized

For j>0, B_B,0j=bvec_j. Because B_B has zero column sums,
(T^T B_B)_0j=-a*bvec_j. Substituting (7.1) in (6.3) yields

    N^B_0j=r_j^pool*S0,
    S0=(a*kappa*u_0-tau)*(1-rho_0)+gamma*R_0*H.      (7.4)

In particular ALL original finite first-row multipliers are nonnegative
iff S0<=0, equivalently

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).           (7.5)

This realizes the invariant (5.4), rather than assuming it can be repaired.
It changes the demanding Law A quantity U-1+p in (6.6) to the much smaller
H/(1-rho_0). Thus the Law A charge obstruction does NOT transfer to Law B.

The simultaneous first-row and full-PSD conditions at qtar are nonvacuous.
Within this same two-parameter law choose the explicit member

    kappa_0=gamma*R_0*H/[a*u_0*(1-rho_0)],
    tau_0=2*gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).                    (7.6)

These are positive. Equation (7.4) gives N^B_0j=0 for every j>0, and
J_A=a*gamma*R_0*H. From (2.1), gamma<2 and (4.4),

    J_A< (25p/16)*(9p/8)=225p^2/128<2p^2.

Consequently p^2+J_A<3p^2<p/2<qtar, because p<1/128 and
qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]>17/32>1/2. This is a strictly positive
full factor at the target with all finite first-row multipliers zero,
positive terminal probabilities, and positive outgoing optimum multipliers.
It remains a FAILED certificate because the complete array still has a
negative original coefficient, as the next subsection proves.

### 7.2 Last-to-previous-leaf versus incoming optimum1: exhaustive sign conflict

Let j=z-2, the genuine preceding queried leaf. Both z and j are even.
For i,j>0 the balanced correction has the explicit entry

    B_B,ij=xi*(v_i*r_j^pool-r_i^pool*v_j).            (7.7)

By (3.7), v_z/u_z=v_j/u_j=rplus. Therefore B_B,zj=0. Also
A_A,zj=0. The last row of T^T is the last coordinate row, so exactly

    N^B_zj=u_z*u_j*(-kappa/U+gamma*rplus^2).          (7.8)

If kappa<gamma*U*rplus^2, this entry is positive and the ORIGINAL
lambda_(z,z-2) is negative. Otherwise its sign passes and necessarily

    kappa>=gamma*U*rplus^2>7/12.                     (7.9)

The strict lower bound follows from gamma>1, U>7/3 and rplus>1/2.
We now prove that throughout this remaining domain nu^B_1 is negative.

Put tpool=sum_i r_i^pool*t_i=(tbar-rho_0)/(1-rho_0). Then
bvec^T t=xi*(Uclock-v_0-H*tpool), chi^T t=1-tpool.
For i>0, using (7.3) gives the exact expression

    nu^B_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)
       +[gamma*Uclock-xi*(tpool-1)]*v_i
       +xi*r_i^pool*(Uclock-(p+s))-tau*rho_i-2alpha_i. (7.10)

This includes the actual initial clock t_0=1 in BOTH appearances of
(tpool-1) and (p+s); omitting it would change the optimum row.
At query1, divide by the positive u_1 and use v_1/u_1=-rminus:

    nu^B_1/u_1=kappa*(t_1-tbar)
       +[-gamma*rminus+xi/(U-u_0)]*Uclock
       +xi*rminus*(tpool-1)-xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0)
       -tau/U-2delta.                                (7.11)

All signs in this expression can be bounded uniformly. Since b/a<4,
alpha_0<p/8, and gamma<2,

    xi=gamma*(bp/a+alpha_0)<2*(4p+p/8)<9p.           (7.12)

Also U-u_0>7/3-1/8>2. With p<1/128, (7.12) implies
xi/(U-u_0)<9p/2<1<gamma*rminus. Thus the coefficient of Uclock in
(7.11) is negative; Uclock>0. The terms -xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0), -tau/U and
-2delta are nonpositive, with the first and last strictly negative.
Further,

    tpool < tbar/(1-rho_0),
    xi*rminus*tpool < (9p)*(3/2)*(10/9)*tbar
                                      =15p*tbar.    (7.13)

Since t_1<tbar/2 by (6.9), dropping the negative terms in (7.11) gives

    nu^B_1/u_1<(-kappa/2+15p)*tbar<0.               (7.14)

For the final strict sign, (7.9) gives kappa/2>7/24, whereas
15p<15/128<7/24. All denominators and u_1,tbar are positive.

Combining (7.8) and (7.14) covers EVERY kappa>0,tau>=0, with no assumption
on PSD or the first-row signs: either lambda_(z,z-2)<0, or
lambda_(star,1)=nu^B_1<0. At equality kappa=gamma*U*rplus^2, (7.9) and
(7.14) still apply. This excludes the WHOLE displayed Law B domain at any
q, in particular every full-PSD member at qtar, including (7.6).

This conflict concerns the literal balanced correction (7.1). Another
balanced matrix can change the pair (7.8), the optimum row (7.11), or both.
No universal exclusion of balanced re-selection is asserted.

## 8. Boundary, sign and scope audit

* All enclosing integers m>=1536 are treated with the SAME beta,c,a at
  every child. No finite numerical horizon test or reset is used.
* The probabilities at every original queried target and at the optimum
  are strictly positive. The actual terminal gradient remains free, with
  its exact square retained. No earlier remote row is removed.
* The variance metric controls all n-1 independent detail directions.
  The independent common direction and its real derivative are retained.
* Every finite and optimum coefficient has a literal scalar formula.
  Terminal and outgoing-optimum signs pass for both laws. Incoming-optimum
  and finite signs fail as proved; no signed row is called a certificate.
* tau=0 is allowed and covered; kappa>0 is necessary for the specified
  positive metric. Equality in PSD and in the tail sign has been covered.
* Balanced B_B e=0 is checked explicitly, and the initial clock contribution
  is retained in the exact incoming-optimum formula. This is not the old
  isotropic endpoint correction or the old physical-tree uniform pool.
* The first-row invariant includes d_0. Its inverse-metric charge is paid
  once, with an explicit global square-zero direction proving necessity.
* Formal negative directions are not actual trajectories. Failure of these
  two coefficient laws gives no lower bound on W and no global no-certificate
  theorem. Fact931's missing full-function hypothesis remains unproved.

The row identities and inequalities above have received a textual author
audit only. They are not verifier-accepted facts, and no downstream argument

## 9. Retrieval, failure synthesis and handoff

The query-memory, immediate-conclusions, direct-proving,
construct-counterexamples and identify-key-failures procedures guided this
bounded joint attempt. The fact search found no accepted version of the
new weighted first-row identity or these two row laws. Current guidance
was recalled by its targeted query after an empty-string query returned
count0. Oversized initial recall output was truncated; the relevant old
joint report and accepted inputs were reread in bounded portions.

A repair-mode Matlas search for full PSD weighted interpolation certificates
returned unrelated PL, stochastic and constant-step statements; none was
used. Web search located Altschuler--Parrilo, 'Acceleration by Stepsize
Hedging II: Silver Stepsize Schedule for Smooth Convex Optimization',
arXiv:2309.16530, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16530, already read in the prior
round as exact proof-pattern background. No external theorem or proof step
is imported here. The new laws reduce to explicit coefficient identities
in that already-audited interpolation regime; no additional literature
layer or new mathematical machinery is needed for these scoped algebraic
rejections. No notebook or numerical certificate was run.

Law A's failure is not caused by forgetting tail scales: it uses them in
both the metric and terminal distribution, and its imbalance is optimally
distributed for its fixed initial component. Its literal first-to-last row
still overcharges, and the early negative-k incoming optimum row fails.

Law B demonstrates a real escape from Law A's first-row charge argument:
an explicit balanced transport repairs the entire row at affordable full
PSD cost. Its remaining failure is a different, complete-original-array
conflict: a same-sign pair of late queried leaves fixes a nonvanishing
metric scale, while the early odd query sits below the weighted mean clock
and has negative terminal coefficient. The specified transport is too
small to pay that original optimum row at that forced metric scale.

The next missing mechanism would have to alter this second conflict, for
example through a different balanced transport affecting the relevant
late pair and optimum load, a different genuinely nonisotropic metric, or
a different actual terminal law. These are uncovered freedoms, not a third
law attempted in this invocation and not a solution by an unknown matrix.
The first-row invariant (5.4) and its charge (5.5) remain necessary checks
in the stated general architecture; their sufficiency has not been claimed.

# Releasing the middle sector: exact original-row lift and two scoped failures

JOINT UNVERIFIED. Project gd-exact-profile-20260926, worker max4,
invocation81, guidance b941bd3964f8f8f6, plan8fc254f625619e19.
No formal submission was permitted or made. No new fact_id exists.

This report derives the full remainder when all middle gradients are
released at j=0,k=n-2. It gives explicit nonnegative weights on actual
rows for two natural lifts, and proves that neither lift is positive
semidefinite on the full formal space, even with the allowed objective
slack. The second mechanism tests an explicit four-sector discriminator:
its negative formal direction is not interpolable, and the most direct
single-boundary-cycle repair cannot be PSD either. These are scoped
certificate obstructions, not a counterexample to a function-class bound.

The theorem-level interface remains open: a successful lift needs a
different original-row construction with a full-space sign/Schur proof.
No uniform upper bound on W, no primal escape, and no resolution of the
original every-n/every-nonnegative-word problem is claimed.

All derivations below are joint: no new unverified lemma is imported as
an accepted premise. Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies only original
interpolation necessity/sufficiency and normalization. Accepted
931b9653ce0f7201 supplies only its hierarchy/benchmark scope, in Section12.

## 1. Same physical word, actual boundary indices, and normalization

Fix any integer m>=1536, and throughout set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon_h=1/(4m), beta_h=1-epsilon_h,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon_h), a=beta_h/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j),
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, S=sum h, Z=D_m=1+2S.

All children keep this SAME enclosing m and all its parameters. Index
the actual steps from0 to n-1. Put

    K=n-2, R=n-1,
    A=h_0=h_R=1+a, d=a, e=h_K-1=a*c=beta_h,
    I={1,...,K}, M=sum_(i=1)^(K-1) h_i,
    B=sum_(i in I)h_i=M+1+e=S-2A,
    v=M+1=B-e, U=1+d+v,
    w=A+1/2-A^2/2=1-a^2/2,
    D=U+e+w=S+1/2-A^2/2.

Thus 2D=Z-A^2. The singleton first sector is index0, the entire middle
sector is I, the singleton last queried sector is indexR, and n is the
actual unqueried terminal. In particular h_K has dyadic level1, not0:
K+1=2^m-2 is divisible by2 but not4. Every physical leaf remains.

Normalize a legal instance to L=1, f_star=0, x_star=g_star=0. Write
x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and use exactly the accepted orientation

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.       (1.1)

The objective-certificate level is denoted chi, to avoid confusion with
any gradient or benchmark capacity. It would bound 2f_n/||x_0||^2.
General L follows by dividing the objective by L and translating its own
specified minimizer; the normalization stays W=2R.

Elementary bounds used below are jointly recorded here. Since
lambda<5/2 and epsilon_h<=1/6144, in fact c<5/2; for example use
sqrt(2)<10/7, lambda<17/7, and (17/7)(6145/6144)<5/2.
Also beta_h>99/100, so

    1/3<a<1/2, 1<A<3/2, 0<e<1, 7/8<w<1.             (1.2)

## 2. A concrete three-sector row identity, rederived jointly

Start by imposing g_i=q for i in I, and put p=g_0, r=g_R. Define

    alpha=A/(2D), theta=(U+e)/(2D-U),
    beta=theta-alpha, gamma=1-theta,
    ell=alpha, eta=alpha/(d+v), R_flow=alpha-ell=0,
    kappa=beta+ell+eta=theta+eta,
    gbar=alpha*p+beta*q+gamma*r.                    (2.1)

Use these core weights mu on ORIGINAL rows:

| Row | mu |
|---|---:|
| Q_(0,star) | alpha |
| Q_(K,star) | beta |
| Q_(R,star) | gamma |
| Q_(K,0) | ell+eta |
| Q_(0,K) | eta |
| Q_(R,K) | beta+ell |
| Q_(R,0) | R_flow=0 |

Also put weight1 on Q_(n,R), the actual last-step row. All unlisted
weights are zero. It is convenient to retain the symbol R_flow in
some algebra so that its role as a row coefficient is explicit.

These weights are nonnegative. Indeed

    theta=(U+e)/(U+2e+2w) <1,
    theta>1/2 because U>2w,
    alpha<1/8, beta>3/8, gamma>0, eta>0, kappa>1/2. (2.2)

The value coefficient at each of0 and K is zero; at R it is1.
The last-step row moves this coefficient to n. Thus all values cancel
in chi||x_0||^2-2f_n+2sum mu Q, without assuming any formula for them.
The value balance will remain valid when the gradients are released.

The last row is the exact identity

    Q_(n,R)=f_n-f_R+(A-A^2/2)||r||^2
                            +||g_n+(A-1)r||^2/2.    (2.3)

This keeps the terminal free; its minimizing formal gradient is not
silently imposed on a legal function. It also explains the charge w.

Direct expansion on the equal-middle subspace gives

    K_0=(alpha-eta*d)||p||^2+kappa*v||q||^2+w||r||^2
       +[beta*A+ell*d+eta*(d-v)]<p,q>
       +[gamma*A+R_flow*d]<p,r>
       +[B-(beta+ell)*v]<q,r>.                    (2.4)

The polynomial after value cancellation is

    chi||x_0||^2-2<gbar,x_0>+2K_0
                                      +||g_n+(A-1)r||^2.

The two identities

    alpha*(2D-1)=A-eta*(d+v),
    theta*(2D-U)=U+e                             (2.5)

follow by substituting (2.1). Expanding K_0-D||gbar||^2 in
inc_pq=p-q and inc_qr=q-r, its common-gradient terms vanish by (2.5), and

    K_0-D||gbar||^2=J11||inc_pq||^2+J22||inc_qr||^2,
    J11=alpha-eta*d-D*alpha^2
       =alpha*[v-d*(1+v+d)]/[2(d+v)],
    J22=theta*(U-D*theta).                       (2.6)

For completeness the possible mixed entry is
gamma*(2D*alpha-A)/2=0, which follows from the first definition
in (2.1). Thus this is a whole two-increment identity, not a diagonal
test with an omitted mixed coefficient.

Both entries are positive. The numerator in J11 is
(1-d)v-d(1+d)>v/2-3/4>0. For J22, expansion gives

    U*(2D-U)-D*(U+e)=U*w-e*(e+w)>0,

because U>6,w>7/8,e<1,w<1. The denominator 2D-U is positive.

Set chi0=1/(2D)=1/(Z-A^2). The complete equal-middle identity is

    chi||x_0||^2-2f_n+2sum mu Q
      =(chi-chi0)||x_0||^2
       +2D||gbar-x_0/(2D)||^2
       +2J11||p-q||^2+2J22||q-r||^2
       +||g_n+(A-1)r||^2.                        (2.7)

The allowed chi_target=17/(16Z) is greater than chi0 because
Z>17A^2. This follows from A<3/2 and Z>2n+1, n=2^m-1.
Thus there really is nonnegative objective slack available. The failures
below take x_0=0 and therefore survive even arbitrarily large chi.

## 3. Mechanism1a: exact lift with the actual last middle anchor

Release every middle gradient, keep q=g_K, and define only algebraically

    E=sum_(i=1)^(K-1)h_i*(g_i-q).                 (3.1)

Then

    x_K=x_0-Ap-Mq-E,
    x_R=x_0-Ap-Bq-E.

Keep exactly the row weights of Section2. No interpolation row is placed
at a mean. Relative to (2.4), the displacement terms of the affected
rows are as follows:

| Row | additional term |
|---|---|
| Q_(K,star) | <q,E> |
| Q_(R,star) | <r,E> |
| Q_(K,0) | <q,E> |
| Q_(0,K) | -<p,E> |
| Q_(R,K) | 0 |
| Q_(R,0) | <r,E> |
| Q_(0,star), Q_(n,R) | 0 |

Every f_i is still independent before cancellation. In particular there
is no hidden equality f_K=f_1-M||q||^2. The coefficients of f_0,f_K,f_R

Consequently (2.7) holds on the ENTIRE original formal space after adding

    2<E,C>,
    C=-eta*p+kappa*q+(gamma+R_flow)*r.            (3.2)

This is the exact frozen-weight remainder. Every internal gradient is
present in E, including g_1; the last middle endpoint remains q=g_K.
There is no positive ||E||^2 term.

This frozen lift is not PSD for any finite chi. Choose a unit vector z,

                         2D-2T.

It is negative whenever T>D. This is a FORMAL direction only: it is not
claimed to satisfy the interpolation inequalities. Its purpose is the

## 4. Mechanism1b: a legal fan of actual rows, with arbitrary probabilities

A natural attempt to create internal squares is to replace the q-node
rows by averages of ACTUAL query rows. Fix any probabilities omega_i>=0
for i in I, with sum omega_i=1. Retain alpha,beta,gamma,ell,eta,R_flow
from Section2. Use the following original weights:

    mu_(0,star)=alpha, mu_(R,star)=gamma,
    mu_(i,star)=beta*omega_i,
    mu_(i,0)=(ell+eta)*omega_i,
    mu_(0,i)=eta*omega_i,
    mu_(R,i)=(beta+ell)*omega_i          (i in I),
    mu_(R,0)=R_flow,
    mu_(n,R)=1.                                  (4.1)

All are explicit nonnegative original-row multipliers. There are no
middle-to-middle rows in this particular fan. The balance at EVERY
middle index is

    beta*omega_i+(ell+eta)*omega_i
                         -eta*omega_i-(beta+ell)*omega_i=0.

Thus all original sampled values cancel separately. No averaged value
or fictitious jet is introduced. Define algebraic moments

    P_i=sum_(l=1)^(i-1)h_l*g_l,  P_1=0,
    dvec=sum_(i in I)h_i*g_i,
    q_omega=sum_(i in I)omega_i*g_i,
    N_omega=sum_(i in I)omega_i*||g_i||^2,
    P_omega=sum_(i in I)omega_i*P_i,
    T_omega=sum_(i in I)omega_i*<g_i,P_i>,
    gbar_omega=alpha*p+beta*q_omega+gamma*r.         (4.2)

The term T_omega is chronologically ordered. It is not the square of a
mean. Expanding every row in (4.1), using x_i=x_0-Ap-P_i and

    chi||x_0||^2-2f_n+2sum mu Q
      =chi||x_0||^2-2<gbar_omega,x_0>+2K_omega
                                        +||g_n+(A-1)r||^2,       (4.3)

where

    K_omega=(alpha-eta*d)||p||^2+kappa*N_omega+w||r||^2
       +[beta*A+ell*d+eta*(d-1)]<p,q_omega>
       +[gamma*A+R_flow*d]<p,r>
       +<r,dvec>-eta*<p,P_omega>
       -(beta+ell)*<r,P_omega+q_omega>+kappa*T_omega.             (4.4)

One can check every coefficient directly as follows. The combined
coefficient of ||g_i||^2 is
[beta+(ell+eta)+eta+(beta+ell)]omega_i/2=kappa*omega_i.
The coefficient of <g_i,P_i> is
[beta+(ell+eta)]omega_i=kappa*omega_i.
The reverse rows Q_(0,i) contribute -eta<p,P_omega>; the Q_(R,i)
rows contribute -(beta+ell)<r,P_omega+q_omega>. All rows involving
x_R contribute exactly <r,dvec>, because
gamma+beta+ell+R_flow=1. These exhaust internal occurrences.

When omega is the point mass at K, q_omega=g_K and (4.4) reduces to
Section3 including its displacement remainder. This independently
checks the actual endpoint orientation.

## 5. Exact displacement-mean variance and chronological remainder

Now use the concrete probabilities

    omega_i=h_i/B,
    q=q_omega=dvec/B,
    nu_i=g_i-q, sum_(i in I)h_i*nu_i=0.            (5.1)

The symbol q here denotes only an algebraic displacement mean. The
legal proof expression is the original row sum (4.1), not an
interpolation row for q. Define

    H2=sum_(i in I)h_i^2,
    tau=(B^2-H2)/(2B), Delta_tau=tau-M,
    Cum_i=sum_(l=1)^i h_l,
    Z_chron=(1/B)*sum_(i in I)h_i*(B-Cum_i)*nu_i,
    J2=sum_(i in I)h_i^2*nu_i,
    V=sum_(i in I)h_i*||nu_i||^2.                 (5.2)

The exact moment identities are

    N_omega=||q||^2+V/B,
    P_omega=tau*q+Z_chron,
    T_omega=tau*||q||^2-<q,J2>/B
                         -sum_i h_i^2||nu_i||^2/(2B).           (5.3)

Proof: swap the finite sums defining P_omega to obtain its coefficient
h_i(B-Cum_i)/B. For T_omega, each unordered pair appears once with
weight h_i*h_l/B, so

    T_omega=[||sum_i h_i*g_i||^2-sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2]/(2B).

Expand g_i=q+nu_i and use the weighted zero-sum equation. This proves

Let K_0(p,q,r) be the polynomial (2.4), evaluated algebraically at this
mean q. Substitution in (4.4) gives the COMPLETE remainder

    K_omega=K_0(p,q,r)+R_var,

    R_var=Delta_tau*[kappa||q||^2-eta<p,q>-(beta+ell)<r,q>]
       -eta<p,Z_chron>-(beta+ell)<r,Z_chron>
       -(kappa/B)<q,J2>
       +(kappa/(2B))*sum_i h_i*(2-h_i)*||nu_i||^2.                (5.4)

Thus the complete expression (4.3) is precisely (2.7), with q now
the algebraic mean, plus 2R_var. Every formal gradient, x_0 and the
free g_n remains present. No boundary square or common-gradient
charge is duplicated. The four types of lost terms are explicit:

1. Delta_tau changes the sampled middle endpoint from physical mass M
   to the average chronological location tau.
2. Z_chron records the chronological order of every internal variation.
3. J2 records the cross term between the mean and squared step weights.
4. The remaining diagonal variance has signed weights h_i(2-h_i).

The first middle point is included with P_1=0; the last middle point is
included with its actual h_K and prefix mass M. Its contribution to
Z_chron has B-Cum_K=0. Original values disappear by separate balance,
as shown before any mean was introduced. These observations account
for the endpoints and sampled values that a collapsed argument loses.

## 6. Exact full-space obstruction to displacement-weighted row averaging

Set x_0=p=r=g_n=0. In (4.3), before any mean substitution, the complete
internal principal form is

    2*kappa*[sum_i omega_i||g_i||^2
                         +sum_(l<i)omega_i*h_l<g_i,g_l>].       (6.1)

For omega_i=h_i/B, this is

    (kappa/B)*[||sum_i h_i*g_i||^2
                              +sum_i h_i(2-h_i)||g_i||^2].      (6.2)

Both formulas follow directly from (4.4) and do not assume any common
gradient contact equations. In particular, the following obstruction
also applies to any outer coefficients of the same fan architecture
with kappa>0, whenever the displayed node balances hold.

There are two actual interior steps with h_i,h_j>2: choose the whole
root i=2^(m-1)-1 and the right-child root j=3*2^(m-2)-1. Both are in I,
and h_i=1+a*c^(m-1), h_j=1+a*c^(m-2). Bounds (1.2), c>2 and m>=1536
give the strict inequalities h_i,h_j>2 without any numeric evaluation.

For a nonzero vector z set g_i=z/h_i, g_j=-z/h_j and all other middle
gradients zero. Then sum h_l*g_l=0, and (6.2) equals

    (2*kappa/B)*(1/h_i+1/h_j-1)*||z||^2 <0.        (6.3)

This is an exact full-space negative direction at every diagnostic m.
No x_0 allowance, including 17/(16Z), changes it. A merely positive
variance based on sum h_i||nu_i||^2 is not the actual row remainder.
The chronological part contributes the negative h_i^2 weights.

For arbitrary positive omega, a two-coordinate principal minor of
(6.1), at l<i, also yields the necessary condition

    omega_l >= (h_l^2/4)*omega_i.                 (6.4)

Indeed its diagonal entries, after removing the common positive factor,
are omega_l,omega_i and its off-diagonal is h_l*omega_i/2. At the
displacement probabilities this condition becomes h_l*h_i<=4, which
fails for the two selected long steps. Non-displacement probabilities
are NOT ruled out by this argument, and (6.4) is not sufficient for
their full-space PSD. No adaptive probability family is asserted.

## 7. Mechanism2: a concrete four-sector discriminator on the same word

Let J=2^(m-1)-1 be the physical whole root, and split the actual middle
queries into I_L={1,...,J} and I_R={J+1,...,K}. Put

    B_L=sum_(i in I_L)h_i, B_R=sum_(i in I_R)h_i, B=B_L+B_R,
    V_L=sum_(i in I_L)h_i(2-h_i),
    V_R=sum_(i in I_R)h_i(2-h_i).                 (7.1)

The four queried gradients are p at0, s on I_L, t on I_R, r atR.
Its three genuine change locations are0,J,K. This discriminator is
selected by the failed middle lift; it is not another proof of an
arbitrary checkpoint-pair subclass.

Both V_L and V_R are strictly less than -c^m. To prove this, note that
their total positive linear contribution is at most2S<2c^m. I_L

I_R contains the right-child root, whose square exceeds c^(2m-4)/9.

squares exceeds3c^m. Subtracting even just that square proves

    V_L<-c^m<-B, V_R<-c^m<-B.                   (7.2)

Take a nonzero z and the formal assignment

    p=r=x_0=g_n=0,
    s=z/B_L, t=-z/B_R.                          (7.3)

All three queried changes are nonzero. Its full middle displacement
is zero. On this FOUR-sector subspace the averaged certificate has
the strictly negative value

    (kappa/B)*[V_L/B_L^2+V_R/B_R^2]*||z||^2.      (7.4)

Thus the obstruction is not dependent on isolated gradient spikes or
an unbounded number of distinct queried gradients.

Crucially, (7.3) is NOT a legal primal escape. The actual first step is
x_1=x_0-Ap. The two original rows between0 and1 add to

       =-d||p||^2+(d-1)<p,s>+||s||^2.           (7.5)

At (7.3) this is ||s||^2>0, contradicting interpolation. Equivalently,

    ||s-(1-A/2)p||^2 <= (A^2/4)||p||^2,          (7.6)

so p=0 forces s=0. The negative direction is excluded by a specific

## 8. The single first-boundary-cycle repair also fails, with its price paid

Test the concrete repair obtained by adding a nonnegative weight zeta
to EACH of Q_(0,1) and Q_(1,0) in the mu convention. This leaves all
values balanced and adds 2*zeta times (7.5) to the certificate. It is
the most direct actual-row repair of the violating pair just found.
All original fan weights are otherwise unchanged.

On (7.3), nonnegativity requires

    zeta >= (kappa/(2B))*(-V_L-(B_L^2/B_R^2)*V_R)
           > kappa/2 >1/4,                     (8.1)

using (7.2) and kappa>1/2.

Now test a different formal vector in the SAME four-sector space:
x_0=0, p nonzero, s=t=r=g_n=0. Formula (4.4) gives the fan value
2*(alpha-eta*d)||p||^2; (7.5) costs -d||p||^2. Nonnegativity requires

           =A/(2D*d) <9/(4D)<1/8,               (8.2)

because A<3/2,d>1/3,D>18. This contradicts (8.1).

Therefore NO zeta>=0 makes this repaired fan PSD, already on this
four-sector subspace, for ANY objective level chi. The initial
negative charge in the cycle is essential; treating it as a free
positive ||s-p||^2 would conceal exactly this contradiction.

This is a scoped failure of one paid repair, not a proof that all
cycles, all fan probability choices, or all original multipliers fail.
Adding other rows could alter both tests. Such a new full-space
construction has not been derived in this invocation.

claim and not a closure of states outside that region.

## 6. Explicit cap-edge initialization and all its normals

We now prove that the whole parameter domain (1.2)--(1.3), for either law,
satisfies the advertised strict transitions and (5.4). Write B=b_0, so
B=1 in Law I and 3<=B<=4 in Law II. Both calculations below in fact hold
for 1<=B<=4. Since a<1/2, kappa<1/2000. Uniform elementary estimates are

    kappa<=k_g<=2*kappa,
    |e|<=4*kappa^2/sqrt(3)<4*kappa^2.                 (6.1)

Put

    g_0=(1/2+t)*v_1+(1/2-t)*v_2
       =(-1/2,sqrt(3)*t,k_g),

    <N_0,v_0-g_0><-delta_0<0.                         (6.3)

All of (2.1) is checked, hence this is exactly the first physical gradient
and a strictly positive queried cap height. It is not a formal face alone.
The first actual state is

    Z_1=(a/4,-a*sqrt(3)*t+e,-R-(1+a)*k_g).            (6.4)

Let x_1 be its horizontal part and r_1 its positive depth. Using
sqrt(3)<7/4, t<=1/8, and kappa<=a/1000,

             <15a/32+4*kappa^2<a/2,

The last inequality in the first line follows from 128*kappa^2<a,
which follows from kappa^2<=a^2/1000000 and a<1/2.

At any below-axis point (x,-r), a nonzero cone projection u obeys

    ||u||^2=<Z,u>=<x,u_horizontal>-r*u_3
             <=||x||*||u||.

Thus ||P_K(Z)||<=||x||, also when u=0. Equation (6.5) proves the strictly
stronger bound

    ||P_K(Z_1)||<a/2<1/2=b_min/2.                    (6.6)

This already establishes whole-word cap inactivity after the first query

## 7. Strict two-face transitions and genuine three-dimensionality

For a generator pair J={i,j}, its span is the graph

    (y,eta_J dot y),
    eta_J dot (b_i*z_i)=k_i, eta_J dot (b_j*z_j)=k_j.

The relevant slope vectors are

    eta_12=(-k_1-k_2,(k_1-k_2)/sqrt(3)),
    eta_02=(k_0/B,-(2*k_2+k_0/B)/sqrt(3)).             (7.1)

They satisfy ||eta_J||<5*kappa for 1<=B<=4. For Z=(x,-r) the orthogonal
projection onto this plane has horizontal coordinate

    y=x-tau*eta_J,
    tau=(r+eta_J dot x)/(1+||eta_J||^2).               (7.2)

Its vertical coordinate is eta_J dot y, and its residual is
 tau*(eta_J,-1). In particular

    ||y-x||<=5*kappa*(r+5*kappa*||x||).               (7.3)

If the horizontal coefficients on the two generators are positive, the
projected vertical coordinate is positive. Then tau=r+g_3>0. For the
omitted index l, the exact remote guard is

    (eta_J,-1) dot v_l
       =-b_l*sum_(i=0)^2 k_i/b_i<0.                  (7.4)

Equation (7.4) follows by taking its inner product with sum_i v_i/b_i.
Thus positivity of the pair coefficients proves every cone normal, the
origin equality, and the strict omitted-generator guard. It is not an
assumption that an arbitrary plane projection lies on its cone face.

7a. First post-step projection has support {0,2}.

For J={0,2}, (6.5) and (7.3) give ||y-x_1||<40*kappa^2. Since the
error e in (6.4) has magnitude<4*kappa^2,

    ||y-(a/4,-a*sqrt(3)*t)||<50*kappa^2.              (7.5)

For any horizontal y its coefficients on B*z_0,z_2 are

    alpha_2=-2*y_2/sqrt(3),

At the reference point in (7.5) these are 2a*t>=a/8 and
 a*(1/4+t)/B>=5a/64. Each changes by less than 100*kappa^2 under the

strictly positive. Hence (7.4) applies and the plane projection is g_1.
Its coefficient sum is less than a by (4.1) and (6.6), so the finite cap
is strictly inactive. Also

    (g_1)_3=eta_02 dot (g_1)_horizontal
       <=5*kappa*||g_1||<(5a/2)*kappa<5*kappa/4.      (7.6)

(k_0/B)^2<=(2*kappa)^2 and

    (g_1)_3<2a*kappa<kappa.                           (7.7)

The actual second step is h_1=1+beta. Put Z_2=Z_1-(1+beta)*g_1.
Let tau_1 be (7.2) at Z_1 with J={0,2}. Writing

Consequently ||(Z_2)_horizontal||<a; this follows from (6.5) and

    r_2=r_1+(1+beta)*(g_1)_3<7*kappa.                 (7.9)

Project onto the plane {1,2}. By (7.3), (7.8), (7.9), and a<1/2,

          <150*kappa^2,                              (7.10)

provided this plane projection is valid; we now check that validity.

7c. The first three gradients span the real ambient R^3.

Both g_0 and g_2 lie in span{v_1,v_2}. At zero error the horizontal

Its magnitude is at least beta*a*sqrt(3)/64>a/128. Since
||(-1/2,sqrt(3)*t)||<1, (7.10) changes this determinant by less than
150*kappa^2<3a/40000<a/256. It is therefore strictly negative.
Hence g_0,g_2 are independent in that generator plane. The vector g_1
has a strictly positive v_0 coefficient, while V is invertible. Thus
 g_0,g_1,g_2 are linearly independent. Because the first three steps are
positive, the first four actual states cannot all lie in a proper affine

## 8. Actual closest initial minimum, explicitly priced

At Z_0 the relevant cone projection has strict support {1,2}. To prove
this without guessing the minimum, use (7.2) for eta_12. The horizontal
norm of Z_0 is less than one: a/4<1/8, sqrt(3)*t<1/4, and
|e|<4*kappa^2<1/8. Its depth is at most 2*kappa. Thus its plane
projection u_0 has horizontal error less than 35*kappa^2 relative to
(Z_0)_horizontal, and less than 50*kappa^2 relative to

    x_0^ref=(-1/2-a/4,sqrt(3)*t).

At this reference point its coefficients on z_1,z_2 are

    1/2+a/4+t, 1/2+a/4-t>=3/8.

Their errors are less than 100*kappa^2<1/8, so they are strictly
positive. Equations (7.2), (7.4) now give the true cone projection and
strict remote v_0 guard. With x_0=(Z_0)_horizontal, put

    tau_0=(R+eta_12 dot x_0)/(1+||eta_12||^2)>0,
    y_0=x_0-tau_0*eta_12,
    u_0=(y_0,eta_12 dot y_0),
    Z_star=tau_0*(eta_12,-1).                         (8.1)

Equation (2.3) proves that Z_star is the unique closest point in the
WHOLE polar, including its remote inequality. The actual radius is

    rho_0^2=||y_0||^2+(eta_12 dot y_0)^2

           =q_12^T*G_12^(-1)*q_12,                  (8.2)

where q_12=(<Z_0,v_1>,<Z_0,v_2>)^T. All quantities are the explicitly

In particular <Z_0,g_0>=||g_0||^2+delta_0>||g_0||^2.

    rho_0>||g_0||>=1/2.                              (8.3)

finite projection cannot be obtained by radially clipping P_K(Z_0).
This is an exact property of the initialized legal point, not a proposed
asymptotic model.

## 9. Every original point, remote row, and actual terminal

Equations (5.5), (6.6) show that for EVERY original index 1<=j<=n,

    g_j=P_K(Z_j)=P_D(Z_j),
    ||g_j||<(a/2)*beta^(j-1)*c^(1-sbit(j)),
    delta_j=<Z_j-g_j,g_j>=0.                         (9.1)

The states are exactly Z_j=Z_0-sum_(q<j)h_q*g_q with the depth (3.1).
For each j, the unique cone projection is given by (3.3) without the
finite-cap constraint, which (9.1) proves automatically. It may have
any valid single/pair support or may be zero; no future face is silently
prescribed. At the ACTUAL terminal,

    g_n=P_K(Z_0-sum_(q<n)h_q*g_q) in D,
    F_D(Z_n)=||g_n||^2/2,
    ||g_n||<(a/2)*beta^(n-1)*c^(1-m).                (9.2)

Thus the terminal has an exact projection formula and a proved global
bound. The report is not merely an unanalysed finite projection recurrence.
All intermediate gradients and their normals follow from a uniform
induction; no numerical replay, reset, expected face, or projected-history
normalization is used.

For arbitrary original indices i,j, including both terminal orientations,
let f_i=F_D(Z_i). Their ordered normalized interpolation residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,Z_j-Z_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2

Using the actual minimum and radius (8.2)--(8.3), (9.2) gives

    V_D=||g_n||^2/rho_0^2
       <a^2*beta^(2n-2)*c^(2-2m)
       =beta^(2n)*c^(-2m).                           (10.1)

This holds for every parameter in both laws, with no asymptotic parameter

Put A_j=1+S_j and v=a/(c-2)=beta/[c(c-2)]. Then

    A_0=1, A_(j+1)=2A_j+a*c^j,
    A_j=(1-v)*2^j+v*c^j.

Substitution proves the last equality. Since c>lambda>2,
 c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1, so 0<v<1. Therefore A_m<c^m and

    D_m=2A_m-1<2*c^m.                               (10.2)

Combining (10.1)--(10.2) proves (1.4). In particular the supremum over

    D_m*beta^(2n)*c^(-2m)<2*c^(-m),                  (10.3)

## 11. What actually fails in a pairwise cap-angle extension

    kappa_angle*C<=O, kappa_angle*O<=C,

    -<v_i,v_j><=||v_i||^2.                            (11.1)

No mathematical program, numerical evaluation, arithmetic/trajectory/
recurrence replay, optimizer, solver, benchmark DP, installation, consult
or subagent was used. Administrative text reads/writes and integrity hashes
are the only local executed operations. No original task or problem was
