# Independent common square, positive incoming load, and two row-clock obstructions

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report. Worker max, invocation85.
Original exact-profile minimax problem OPEN. No new fact or formal submission.

## 1. Outcome and exact scope

This report jointly rederives the enlarged common-square architecture and
all its original interpolation coefficients. The paid zero-sum column is
zeta, whereas the actual skew divergence is

    d=zeta+(p-s)(v-z).

Separating z from v changes the architecture, but does not grant free
sign-feasible transport. The outgoing optimum vector depends on zeta,
not on d alone. Both the incoming total/clock moments and the complete
first-row total/clock moments are derived below for GENERAL z.

Law I uses a clock-zero endpoint common column independent of v, a
strictly positive incoming optimum load nu=(1/64)e_0 at the INITIAL
query, and an explicitly scaled positive source/last/tail metric. Its full
polynomial is PSD below the target and all optimum signs pass. Its
first-row total has the required sign. Nevertheless its endpoint clock
defect is negative uniformly in every enclosing m>=1536, for every
skew completion preserving the selected actions. In the ideal endpoint
metric, EVERY compatible endpoint incoming load cancels exactly from
this defect. The positive load in this law therefore changes individual
terms without repairing their net obstruction.

Law II changes terminal probabilities to the actual last queried index
and adds a specified metric mass1/16 at the penultimate query. It keeps
the independent clock-zero common column and the positive incoming
load1/64 at index0. This changes the failing moment: the full first-row
TWO-moment screen now passes, as do full PSD and all optimum signs.
However a different invariant, the last queried row tested against the
PENULTIMATE clock, is strictly less than -1/16. It forces a negative
original finite multiplier from the last query to an earlier-than-
penultimate query. Every balanced correction annihilating e and t
preserves this obstruction.

These are exclusions of TWO fully specified laws, including every
remaining balanced skew in each law. They are not an impossibility
result for the general architecture or for the full dual cone. No
formal residual vector or negative coefficient is presented as an
interpolable primal trajectory. No full-class upper bound on W, and
therefore no resolution of the original problem, has been obtained.

This is ONE joint proof draft. All new calculations are unverified;
none is adopted as a separately accepted premise. The only accepted
facts used are1252b8823bb5a290 and931b9653ce0f7201 at the scopes specified
below. The older reports and the main advisory supplied directions only.

## 2. Problem, accepted interfaces, and physical word

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n and smoothness L>0,
W_n(h) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite Euclidean
dimension, convex differentiable L-smooth f with an attained minimizer,
and x_0!=x_star, under x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R.
The original question is whether W_n_star/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where
W_n_star=inf_(h>=0)W_n(h), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, and the original all-split
benchmark has

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt(x^2+6xy+y^2))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the signed residual orientation and
full terminal-square certificate interpretation. Only incoming edges
at the ACTUAL unqueried terminal may be deleted; no queried-prefix
coordinate or constraint is removed. Accepted931b9653ce0f7201 supplies
the word below, its mass formula, and B_n/D<47/50. Only CONDITIONAL on
the still-missing full-class W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D) for every m>=1536 does
it imply the799/800 separation. That missing hypothesis is not proved.

Fix arbitrary integer m>=1536 and keep its parameters in EVERY child:

    eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    b=1+a, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, l=n-1, r=l-1,
    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S, p=1/(1+S), qtar=17/(16D).

The indices l,r are the last and penultimate QUERIED samples, different
from the actual terminal n. We use the following short local scalar
aliases throughout this report. Their public glossary names carry85:
p=p85, s=s85, qtar=q85, T=T85, U=U85, J=J85, P=P85, H=H85,
X=X85, r=r85. These explicitly scoped aliases do not change any
existing project-glossary definition. The matrix for the chronological
coordinate change is Ltri, distinct from scalar T; a superscript T
means transpose. In Section3 only, Len is an integer suffix length.

The physical last three steps are (b,1+beta,b). Put hgap=1+beta=2-eps.
Elementary bounds from m>=1536 are

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1, 1/3<a<1/2, 4/3<b<3/2.

The accepted mass formula, also obtained by substitution in
1+S_(j+1)=2(1+S_j)+a*c^j, is

    1+S_j=(1-vword)2^j+vword*c^j,
    vword=beta/[c(c-2)] in(0,1).

Consequently

    2^m<1+S<c^m, c^(-m)<p<2^(-m)<2^(-20).             (2.1)

Let e be the all-ones column on the n queries and e_i its coordinate
columns. Define clocks

    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, T=t_l=1/p-b,
    Delta=T-1=1/p-b-1, t_r=T-hgap.

They are strictly increasing, t_0=1 and t_1=1+b. In particular

    3/(4p)<Delta<1/p, Delta-b>1/(2p),
    0<hgap/Delta<4p<1/128.                            (2.2)

## 3. Tail quantities and the bounds actually needed

Write sbit(L) for the binary digit sum. For0<=L<=n put

    rtail_L=product_(j=n-L)^(n-1)(h_j-1)
           =beta^L*c^(-sbit(L)),
    s=rtail_n=beta^n/c^m,
    k_i=h_i product_(i<j<n)(1-h_j),
    u_i=|k_i|, U=sum_i u_i, rho_i=u_i/U.

The suffix formula follows because h_(n-j)-1=a*c^v2(j), and
sum_(j=1)^L v2(j)=L-sbit(L). With L=l-i one has

    u_i=rtail_L+rtail_(L+1), k_i=(-1)^i u_i,
    u_0=(b/a)s, u_l=b, u_r=a(1+beta), u_(l-2)=ba beta,
    U>7/3.                                          (3.1)

For the last inequality the last three terms exceed4/3,5/8,7/18,
whose sum169/72 exceeds7/3. Every rho_i is strictly positive.
The following source bound is especially useful:

    0<s<u_0<p^2/64, rho_0<1/10, s<p.                (3.2)

For a symbolic proof,2^m-1>16m^2 for m>=16 by induction, starting at16.
Also beta^(-4m)>(1+1/(4m))^(4m)>=2, so beta^(4m)<1/2.
Thus beta^n<2^(-4m), while b/a<4 and p>c^(-m) yield
u_0/p^2<4 beta^n c^m<4(5/32)^m<1/64. The other inequalities follow.
No arithmetic, recurrence, or trajectory was evaluated by a program.

Telescoping the terminal update gives

    e^T k=1+s, Ltri^T k=h, t^T k=S,                  (3.3)

where Ltri_ii=1, Ltri_ij=h_j for j<i, and zero otherwise.
For Law I let tbar=sum rho_i t_i and set

    alpha=(1-p)rho, V=t^T(k-alpha)=(1-p)(1/p-tbar).

The necessary uniform bounds are

    32<V<512m^3, p V^2<1/1024.                       (3.4)

Here is the full derivation, to avoid importing the previous unverified
report. The binary product and its digit-weighted sum give

    Ztail=sum_(L=0)^n rtail_L
         =product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+beta^(2^j)/c),
    U=2Ztail-1-s,
    Mtail/Ztail=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)
                    2^j beta^(2^j)/(c+beta^(2^j)),
    Mtail=sum_(L=0)^n L rtail_L.

Choose j with m/2<2^j<=m. Bernoulli's inequality gives beta^(2^j)>=3/4,
and c+beta^(2^j)<7/2; hence Mtail/Ztail>3m/28. Also ns<1. Therefore

    sum_i rho_i(l-i)>(Mtail/Ztail-1)/2>3m/56-1/2.

The suffix after query i has mass at least b+(l-i). As1-p>1/2,
the formula for V makes V>32 for m>=1536.
For the upper bound, Len=L+1 final steps lie in H_d where d is the least
integer with2^d>Len. Thus their mass is smaller than c^d<(2^d)^2<=4Len^2.
Since u_i<2 beta^L and U>2,

    V<4 sum_(L>=0)(L+1)^2 beta^L
      =4(1+beta)/(1-beta)^3<512m^3.

The series identity follows by multiplying by(1-beta)^3.
Finally2^m>2^30 m^6 for m>=128: the base compares2^128 with2^72,
and the induction step follows from
(1+1/m)^6<=sum_(j>=0)(6/m)^j<=64/61<2.
Using p<2^(-m) gives pV^2<2^(-12)<1/1024.

Law II instead chooses alpha=(1-p)e_l. It has

    V=b(1-p), alpha_0=0, v_0=u_0, v_l=a+p,
    0<V<3/2, pV^2<1/1024.                            (3.5)

In BOTH laws alpha_star=p, v=k-alpha, E=p+s, F=p-s>0,
eta=F/E, e^T v=E, and

    R=Ltri^T v,
    R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j)-alpha_i>0.            (3.6)

Indeed R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i.
Moreover0<v_0<u_0 in Law I, v_0=u_0 in Law II, and R_0<2p in both.
For Law I use alpha_0=((1-p)/U)u_0, with (1-p)/U<3/7.

## 4. FULL original-space identity with an independent common column

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep x_0,g_0,...,g_n
arbitrary and independent, substituting ONLY the actual GD recursion.
The accepted residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

For i<n set y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Then

    y=e*x_0-Ltri*g,
    g=Ltri^(-1)(e*x_0-y),
    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y.                                (4.1)

Ltri is invertible with diagonal1. More explicitly, with
pi_i=product_(j<i)(1-h_j),

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
             +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<j'<i)(1-h_j')y_j.

Thus this change spans ALL original queried-gradient directions.
The actual terminal gradient remains independently free.

Choose any z with e^T z=E, positive weights w_i, and zero-sum zeta.
Let Ww=sum_i w_i and define

    K=diag(w)-ww^T/Ww,
    P=K+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    d=zeta+F(v-z),
    A^T=-A, Ae=d, N=Ltri^T(P+A).                     (4.2)

The complete signed multiplier array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,l},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for distinct i,j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i.           (4.3)

Diagonal multipliers vanish. In scalar entries,

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(r'>i)(K_(r',j)+A_(r',j))
                          +R_i v_j+eta Zout_i z_j,
    Zout=Ltri^T z.                                  (4.4)

The formula defines every original ordered pair; none is hidden behind
an existence assertion. The finite prefix outgoing total at i is N_ii,
its incoming total is N_ii-2alpha_i, and the actual terminal adds incoming
2alpha_i. Hence finite-node divergence is zero, terminal divergence2,
and optimum divergence-2. All sampled values cancel in

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.

For prefix nodes including star,
Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>; the remaining prefix quadratic is
-g^T N y. Using(4.1) it is
-<x_0,(Pe-d)^T y>+y^T P y. The terminal expansion, with -2f_n
included, is
||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2-||-s*x_0+v^T y||^2-2sum alpha_i delta_i.
Those delta terms cancel the prefix value terms. Now

    Pe=Ev+Fz,
    2s v-Pe+d=-2Fz+zeta,
    eta E^2=p^2-s^2.

Substitution proves the COMPLETE identity

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
         +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2
         +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,zeta^T y>.           (4.5)

Let ybar_w=sum w_i y_i/Ww. As e^T zeta=0, completion gives

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(zeta_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
       +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2
       +(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i zeta_i^2/w_i.                      (4.6)

This pays the initial charge ONCE. It retains every detail, the common
square and its derivative, and the actual terminal square.
Full PSD is equivalent to q>=p^2+J. For necessity take scalar x_0=1,
y_i=c0-zeta_i/(2w_i), where
c0=1+[sum_i z_i zeta_i/(2w_i)]/E, and g_n=-s+v^T y.
Every displayed square vanishes. Reconstruct the queried gradients by
(4.1). This is a formal-space test, not a primal interpolation claim.
In particular g_n need NOT equal p when z and v differ.

For the actual common queried-gradient direction g_i=G, y_i=x_0-t_i G.
Put V=t^T v, Z=t^T z, theta=t^T zeta, X=t^T Kt. The full prefix remainder
is exactly

    (q-p^2)||x_0||^2-theta<x_0,G>
                      +(X+eta Z^2)||G||^2.          (4.7)

The real common derivative theta has not been discarded.

## 5. General optimum moments, complete first-row moments, literal skew

From Pe+d=2p v+zeta, the outgoing optimum vector is

    mu=2pR+Ltri^T zeta.                              (5.1)

The incoming vector is

    nu=Kt+Vv+eta Zz-At-2alpha.                       (5.2)

Since e^T A=-d^T and t^T At=0, its EXACT moments are

    M0=e^T nu=2pV+theta-2(1-p),
    M1=t^T nu=X+V^2+eta Z^2-2alpha^T t.              (5.3)

A nonnegative nu necessarily has M0>=0 and M0<=M1<=T M0.
Conversely the isolated two-moment problem has the nonnegative endpoint
solution

    nu_target=((T M0-M1)/Delta)e_0
                          +((M1-M0)/Delta)e_l.      (5.4)

This is not sufficient for the finite multiplier signs.
For ANY specified compatible nu_target let

    rvec=Kt+Vv+eta Zz-2alpha-nu_target,
    tmean=(e^T t)/n, cvec=t-tmean*e, Ve=cvec^T cvec>0,
    A0=(d e^T-e d^T)/n,
    fvec=rvec-tmean*d+(d^T t)e/n,
    A=A0+(fvec cvec^T-cvec fvec^T)/Ve.               (5.5)

The two moment identities imply e^T rvec=-d^T t and t^T rvec=0.
Thus e^T fvec=0 and cvec^T fvec=0. Multiplication shows Ae=d and
At=rvec, with both terms skew. This is a literal entrywise completion.
Every other completion is A+C with C^T=-C and Ce=Ct=0.
Such C leaves the polynomial, mu,nu and all moment tests below unchanged.

For the first row define

    S0=sum_(j>0)N_0j,
    P0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-1)N_0j,
    G0=P0-Delta*S0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-T)N_0j.

The first row of Ltri^T is b e^T-a e_0^T. Write

    Lcol=Pe-d=2s v+2F z-zeta.

Then N_0j=b Lcol_j-a(P_0j+A_0j), and N_00=b Lcol_0-aP_00.
As mu_0=2pR_0-a zeta_0, the complete general first-row sum is

    S0=aP_00+zeta_0+2pR_0-2bs v_0-2bF z_0.          (5.6)

Using(P+A)t=2Pt-2alpha-nu yields the complete clock identity

    P0=b(2sV+2FZ-theta)-2a(Pt)_0
                                  +2a alpha_0+a nu_0-mu_0,
    (Pt)_0=(Kt)_0+Vv_0+eta Zz_0.                    (5.7)

These formulas explicitly include BOTH optimum directions.
If all finite lambda_(0,j)>=0, equivalently N_0j<=0, then necessarily

    S0<=0, Delta*S0<=P0<=b*S0.                      (5.8)

Indeed b<=t_j-1<=Delta for all j>0. When S0=0 all off-diagonals must
vanish. These are exact invariant screens, not sufficient row signs.

There is another invariant at the actual last query l. Its row in
Ltri^T is e_l^T, so N_ll=P_ll, (Nt)_l=2(Pt)_l-2alpha_l-nu_l.
Testing its earlier entries against t_r, the penultimate clock, gives

    Hlast=sum_(j<l)(t_j-t_r)N_lj
         =2(Pt)_l-2alpha_l-nu_l-t_r mu_l-hgap*P_ll.  (5.9)

Nonpositive N_lj require Hlast>=0, since t_j<=t_r for j<l.
A negative Hlast forces N_lj>0 at some j<r, not merely at r.

## 6. The shared explicit common column, incoming load, and paid imbalance

Both laws fix the genuinely independent common column

    z=E(T e_0-e_l)/Delta, e^T z=E, t^T z=0.          (6.1)

It differs from v: for example every odd interior v_i is negative and
nonzero, whereas z_i=0 there. The independence is not a scalar rescaling.
Set the NONZERO incoming load

    ellload=1/64, nu_target=ellload*e_0.              (6.2)

For each law's own alpha,V define

    theta0=2(1-p)-2pV=2p alpha^T t,
    theta=theta0+ellload,
    Xreq=theta0/p-V^2+ellload.                       (6.3)

Select positive base weights what_i as specified for that law and put

    tbase=sum what_i t_i/sum what,
    Vbase=sum what_i(t_i-tbase)^2,
    scale=Xreq/Vbase, w_i=scale*what_i,
    K=diag(w)-ww^T/sum w,
    zeta=(theta/Xreq)Kt.                             (6.4)

This fixes every scale from the actual word before row-sign work.
It gives t^T Kt=Xreq, e^T zeta=0 and t^T zeta=theta. Moreover

    J=theta^2/(4Xreq).                              (6.5)

Indeed(Kt)_i=w_i(t_i-tbar_w), whose squared inverse-weight sum is
Xreq. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz shows the same law minimizes this charge
at fixed theta for its metric. By(5.3), M0=M1=ellload. Thus(6.2) is
exactly compatible. Define d by(4.2), A by(5.5), then EVERY scalar
multiplier by(4.3)--(4.4). The literal law sets C=0; our obstructions
will cover every extra skew C annihilating e and t.

### 6.1 Positive metric, full PSD, all optimum signs

For both laws1<theta0<2. In Law I use V>32 and pV^2<1/1024 to get
pV<1/32768 and then theta0>1. In Law II use V<3/2 and(2.1).
Consequently

    Xreq>(1023/1024)*theta0/p>0,
    Xreq<2/p+ellload, 1<theta<3, theta/Xreq>p.        (6.6)

The last follows because theta-pXreq=ellload(1-p)+pV^2>0.
Every base weight is positive because p^2 rho_i>0, and the two unit
endpoint masses make Vbase>0. Hence all metric weights are positive.

## 1. Verdict and exact scope

The assigned selector has NOT been refuted, and its uniform all-function
inequality has NOT been proved. Only Mechanism1 was opened. Its required

(optimum plus two selected anchors) remains unopened. There is no third law.

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the full original interpolation model
and maximal prefix extension. Accepted931b9653ce0f7201 supplies the

## 2. Original model, hierarchy, and normalization

Normalize L=1, an actual selected minimizer x_star=0, and f_star=0.

    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i,     g_i=grad f(x_i),     f_i=f(x_i).

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,

We will use only the following deliberately loose parameter bounds:

    12/5<c<5/2, 1/3<a<1/2, 1<A<3/2, T>18,
    D>36, S/T<15/2, D/T<16, D<2*c^m.

Here are their symbolic justifications. Since sqrt(2)>7/5 and
sqrt(2)<10/7, and epsilon<=1/6144,
12/5<c<(17/7)*(6145/6144)<5/2. Also beta>99/100, so
a>(99/100)/(5/2)>1/3, while a<1/lambda=sqrt(2)-1<1/2.

## 4. Every exact physical update and every reordering

All original steps have h>1. Put k=h-1>0. In the following table an ordering
such as213 gives the identities of the old coordinates in new descending
order. The displayed output is the NEW ordered gap pair(U,V).

CORE, u+2v<=1:

  order321: (U,V)=(k v,k u).                             (4.1)

This follows from q'=(1-h)q=-kq; it includes ties.

VERTEX, u>=1:

  h<=u:       order123, (U,V)=(u-h,v);
  u<=h<=u+v:  order213, (U,V)=(h-u,u+v-h);
  h>=u+v:     order231, (U,V)=(v,h-u-v).                 (4.2)

Indeed the labeled adjacent differences after the actual step are u-h and v.
The sign of u-h and then of u+v-h gives exactly these three orders. The last
two old coordinates remain ordered because their gradient coordinates agree.

EDGE, 0<=u<=1 and u+2v>=1: define w=v-h(1-u)/2. Then

  w>=k u:     order213, (U,V)=(k u,w-k u);
  0<=w<=k u:  order231, (U,V)=(w,k u-w);
  w<=0:       order321, (U,V)=(-w,k u).                 (4.3)

Here the labeled adjacent differences are -k u and w. Thus the old second
coordinate is never below the old first; the signs of w and w-k u give the
complete list. No order-persistence assumption enters (4.1)--(4.3).

For each output use precisely these next-query guards:

  next C iff U+2V<=1;
  next V iff U>=1;
  next E iff U<=1 and U+2V>=1.                          (4.4)

Inside a row of (4.1)--(4.3), every boundary in (4.4) is affine in u,v.
Together with u,v>=0, the current face boundaries u+2v=1,u=1 and order
boundaries h=u,h=u+v,w=0,w=k u, this retains all guards. The A,B update is
A'=(2U+V)/3,B'=(U+2V)/3, so the table is also an explicit map in A,B.

The formulas agree on shared boundaries. At u+2v=1, w=-k v and the edge
row becomes(k v,k u), the core formula. At u=1, w=v and (4.3) becomes the
applicable vertex row. The adjacent rows agree when w=0,w=k u,h=u or h=u+v.
No additional branch is inserted by allowing closed inequalities.

The exact new squared norm is

  core:   k^2 Q(u,v);
  vertex: (u-h)^2+(u-h)v+v^2;
  edge:   k^2 u^2-k u w+w^2.                            (4.5)

These are permutation-invariant norm expressions for the raw differences.
In particular the edge cross term has its displayed MINUS sign.


## 5. Exact hexagonal image at every radius and every original step

Define G(x)=max_i|<x,v_i>| and C_R={x:G(x)<=R}. In the ordered chamber,

  G=max(2u+v,u+2v)/2,
  C_R={u,v>=0:2u+v<=2R, u+2v<=2R}.

Let k=h-1>0 and M_h(R)=max_(x in C_R)G(T_h x). The exact formula is:

If h>=2,

  M_h(R)=kR,                                      0<=R<=1;
  M_h(R)=max{k,R-h/2,(R+h-3/2)/2},                 R>=1.       (5.1)

If 1<h<2,

  M_h(R)=kR,                                      0<=R<=1/2;
  M_h(R)=max{k min(R,1),R-h/2,h(2R-1)/4},          1/2<=R<=3/2;
  M_h(R)=max{k,R-h/2,(R+h-3/2)/2},                 R>=3/2.     (5.2)

Endpoints agree. In particular the actual leaf has h=1+a<3/2, the level1
bridge has h=1+beta<2, and every higher bridge has h>=2. No leaf is replaced
by an artificial h=2 step. These formulas are nondecreasing in R.

Proof. In the core the image is -kx; its maximum G is k min(R,1).
For R<=1/2 the entire hexagon lies in D, so this already proves (5.2)'s
first part. For R>=1/2, in the edge chart the labeled post-step dots are

  s'_1=v/2+(1-3h/4)u-h/4,
  s'_2=v/2+(3h/4-1/2)u-h/4,
  s'_3=-(u+2v)/2+h/2.                              (5.3)

The feasible interval and ceiling for its ordered coordinates are

  0<=u<=U_R:=min(1,(4R-1)/3),
  (1-u)/2<=v<=min(2R-2u,R-u/2).                    (5.4)

The ceiling changes at u=2R/3. The negative parts of s'_1 and s'_2 are
at most k min(R,1), since their values on the lower edge boundary are
-k(1+3u)/4 and k(3u-1)/4 and u<=U_R. Also s'_1<=s'_2. The third coordinate
contributes at most max(k/2,R-h/2); k/2 is covered by the core term.
At the upper ceiling, s'_2 equals

  R/2-h/4+3ku/4,                 u<=2R/3;
  R-h/4+3(h-2)u/4,              u>=2R/3.           (5.5)

For h<2 these slopes have opposite signs. The maximum is at u=2R/3
when R<=3/2 and at u=1 when R>=3/2, giving respectively h(2R-1)/4 and
(R+h-3/2)/2. For h>=2 the maximum is at U_R. For R<=1 it is k(R-1/2),
dominated by kR; for 1<=R<=3/2 it is R+h/2-3/2, dominated by k; for
R>=3/2 it is (R+h-3/2)/2.

There is no vertex region for R<1. For R>=1 its post-step dots are

  (2u+v)/2-h, (v-u+h)/2, -(u+2v)/2+h/2, u>=1.

The first and third absolute values are bounded by max(k,R-h/2).
The only further candidate, the positive second dot, has maximum
R+h/2-3/2 for 1<=R<=3/2 and (R+h-3/2)/2 for R>=3/2. The former is at
most k when h>=2. When h<2 it is at most h(2R-1)/4, because their
difference is (2-h)(3/4-R/2)>=0. Negative second dots are covered by the
first-coordinate positive bound. This proves all claimed upper bounds.

For attainment, the core term is attained by x=min(R,1)v_1. A maximizing
term R-h/2 is nonnegative and is attained at the edge-axis point with
u=0,v=R. In the middle part of (5.2), the edge term is attained at
u=v=2R/3, which satisfies (5.4). In the outer part, the mixed term is
attained at u=1,v=R-1/2. For (5.1), if this outer term is strictly larger
than k then R>h-1/2>=3/2, so this last point is allowed. If it ties k,
the core point suffices. All proposed maximizing cases are thus realized.

## 6. Paid norm and objective conversions

For every actual x,

  G(x)^2<=||x||^2<=4G(x)^2/3.                      (6.1)

For example, in the chamber u>=v, the difference
4G^2/3-Q=(u-v)(u+2v)/3 is nonnegative; in the other half chamber
interchange u,v. The lower bound follows because each v_i is a unit
vector. Both constants are attained: on a vertex axis and at u=v.

The always valid objective estimate is Psi(x)<=||x||^2<=4G(x)^2/3.
For every R>=3/2 the SHARP objective maximum on C_R is

  max_(G(x)<=R)Psi(x)=2R-1.                        (6.2)

Indeed in a vertex chart Psi<=2R-1. In an edge chart Psi=z-1/4+y^2
with z<=R and y^2<=3/4, so Psi<=R+1/2<=2R-1. In the core Psi<=1,
also below 2R-1. The point Rv_1 attains equality. Notice that the
edge-axis point -Rv_1 instead has Psi=R-1/4. This distinction survives
even for arbitrarily large R; a gauge radius is not an objective value.

## 7. Explicit same-m complete-H_j envelope estimates

Write E_j(R) for the chronological composition of the EXACT M_h maps
over H_j, with E_0(R)=R. It is only a scalar enclosing radius. From
monotonicity, every actual run satisfies G(T_(H_j)x)<=E_j(G(x)), where
T_(H_j) denotes the complete actual composition on the one fixed F.
It does not follow that E_j is the true image of the whole block.

Put S_j=sum H_j and eta=a/(c-2). Directly from the literal word,

  1+S_j=(1-eta)2^j+eta c^j,    0<eta<1.            (7.1)

For clarity, A_j=1+S_j obeys A_(j+1)=2A_j+a c^j; substitution proves
(7.1), starting at A_0=1. We use the same enclosing m throughout.
Useful coarse rational bounds are

  2/5<a<5/12, 99/100<beta<1, 12/5<c<5/2,
  12/5<beta*c<5/2, 1-eta<8epsilon.                 (7.2)

Here lambda>241/100 and lambda<29/12 follow by squaring their positive
sqrt(2) comparisons. Because epsilon<=1/6144, c<49/20 and beta>99/100,
so a>99/245>2/5; a<1/lambda=sqrt(2)-1<5/12. Also beta*c=lambda(1-epsilon^2)
>(241/100)(999/1000)>12/5 and is below lambda<5/2. For the last inequality,

The exact ruler prefix products are

  P_ell=product_(r=1)^ell(h_(r-1)-1)
       =beta^ell c^(-sbit(ell)),                   (7.3)

where sbit(ell) is the number of binary ones, and P_0=1. The ruler entry
is beta*c^(nu_2(r)-1); counting each power-of-two divisor of the integers
1,...,ell gives sum nu_2(r)=ell-sbit(ell), proving (7.3).
In particular P_ell<=a<1 for every nonempty prefix and
P_block,j:=product_(h in H_j)(h-1)=beta^(2^j-1)c^(-j).

The following are quantitative complete-word statements, not unevaluated
max-plus expressions:

  E_j(R)=P_block,j R,                                  0<=R<=1;
  E_j(R)<=max(R,a c^(j-1)),                       R>=0,j>=1;
  E_j(R)<=max(R-S_j/2,C_hex,j),                       R>=0,j>=1;
  C_hex,j=(3a c^(j-1)-S_(j-1))/2.                    (7.4)

For the first line, formulas (5.1)--(5.2) give M_h(r)=(h-1)r for
0<=r<=1 for EVERY original step. For the two short steps this follows
from k>=a>2/5: on 1/2<=r<=1 both r-h/2 and h(2r-1)/4 are at most kr.
Every original prefix product is at most1, so no intermediate scalar
radius leaves this interval. This proves the whole-block equality.

The other two lines follow from the pointwise bounds

  M_h(R)<=max(R,h-1),
  M_h(R)<=max(3(h-1)/2,R-h/2),                    (7.5)

valid for every h>1 and R>=0. To check the second, the mixed outer branch

middle branch is at most the outer mixed branch, since their difference
is k(R-3/2)/2<=0; the core term is at most k. The first bound follows

k-1/2, and the short middle branch is at most R. The largest k in H_j
is a c^(j-1), proving the second line of (7.4).

Composing the second max in (7.5) by distributivity gives the upper bound
max{R-S_j/2, max_i[3(h_i-1)/2-(mass strictly after i)/2]}.
An occurrence of a level-l bridge is followed by its complete H_l right

## 8. Exact complete-word failure of the scalar relaxation

For every j>=1 choose the scalar initial radius R_0=S_j+1. At every actual
position, let A_i be the original mass already executed. Then

  R_i=S_j+1-A_i/2,
  M_(h_i)(R_i)=R_i-h_i/2,
  E_j(S_j+1)=S_j/2+1.                             (8.1)

This is a symbolic proof for every j, not an executed recurrence. Here is
why EVERY branch choice is valid. Let Hmax=1+a c^(j-1). From (7.1),

  S_j> [c/(c-2)](Hmax-1)-1 >5Hmax-6>4Hmax-5.

Thus R_i>=S_j/2+1>2Hmax-3/2>=2h_i-3/2. Also R_i>3/2 since S_j>1.
In the outer formulas (5.1)--(5.2), R-h/2 dominates the mixed branch
exactly when R>=2h-3/2. It also dominates k there, since h>1. This proves
the induction in (8.1), including the real last leaf.

Combining the separately sharp conversions (6.1)--(6.2) with this exact
scalar path gives the certificate value

  [2E_j(R_0)-1]/R_0^2=1/(S_j+1).                  (8.2)

Its ratio to the baseline1/(1+2S_j) is
(1+2S_j)/(1+S_j)=2-1/(1+S_j). It exceeds17/16 because S_j>1>1/15.
For j=m it tends to2 as m tends to infinity, since S_m>=2^m-1.
This is a precise, unavoidable loss for the relaxation that keeps only the
scalar radius, uses these exact one-step images, and applies the sharp
separate initial-norm and terminal-objective conversions. Any weaker
one-step bounds or weaker separate conversions cannot repair that loss.
It does NOT exclude a bound retaining an objective or directional state.

The incompatibility is concrete. Start the ACTUAL fixed F at
x_0=-(S_j+1)v_1. Every point is on the same physical edge-normal ray with
z_i=S_j+1-A_i/2>1/2 and y_i=0. Its actual gauge is exactly R_i, so ONE
legal trajectory attains all the scalar image radii in (8.1). But its
actual terminal value is S_j/2+3/4, not S_j+1. Its terminal point is on
an edge axis, whereas the maximizer of (6.2) is on a vertex axis. The
initial Euclidean bound is already exact on this edge ray. No orientation
switch can be inserted at the terminal of this static trajectory.

Alternatively, the actual start +(S_j+1)v_1 stays in the same vertex
through the terminal and finishes at v_1 with Psi=1. Neither of these
legal starts realizes (8.2) as its normalized objective. No full-word
triangle counterexample is claimed.

## 9. Actual fixed-face criteria, and why large radius is insufficient

For a particular vertex, order the other coordinates so its upper gap is
u_0 and the remaining gap is v_0>=0. The condition

  u_0>=S_m+1                                      (9.1)

is necessary and sufficient for that SAME vertex chart to hold at all
queries AND the terminal. Under this condition the gap at any prefix is
u_0-A_i>=1 and the other gap is unchanged. Conversely, if the chart holds
through the terminal, its affine update gives u_n=u_0-S_m>=1.

For a fixed physical edge, write x=z n_E+y t_E. The condition

  z_0>=1/2+S_m/2, |y_0|<=sqrt(3)/2                 (9.2)

is necessary and sufficient for that edge chart to be valid throughout,
including terminal. Necessity uses z_n=z_0-S_m/2>=1/2 and initial edge
membership. Sufficiency follows from z_i=z_0-A_i/2 and
|y_i|=P_i|y_0|<=|y_0| using (7.3). Boundary choices are harmless.

Both fixed-face classes have normalized payoff at most1/D_m. Indeed
D_m P_block,m^2<1 because (7.1) gives D_m<2c^m and P_block,m=beta^n c^(-m).
In a vertex chart the difference between ||x_0||^2 and D_m Psi(x_n)
is (s_0-D_m)^2+t_0^2. In an edge chart it is
(z_0-D_m/2)^2+(1-D_m P_block,m^2)y_0^2. The equalities at x_0=D_m v_1 and
x_0=-(D_m/2)v_1 are legal by (9.1)--(9.2). Thus the classes actually
attain1/D_m. This is not extended to the face-changing domain.

There is no scalar large-radius criterion for fixed faces. Choose
0<delta<a, u_0=1+delta and v_0=T with T arbitrarily large. This is a
strict vertex query. The first actual leaf1+a gives ordered gaps
U=a-delta in (0,1), V=T-a+delta. For T large enough U+2V>1, so the next
query is strictly on an edge. Meanwhile ||x_0||^2=u_0^2+u_0 T+T^2 tends
to infinity. This family rules out assuming that all large starts have
one face. Criteria (9.1)--(9.2), not radius alone, identify the histories
to which the fixed-face sharpening applies.

## 10. Mechanism2: a remaining-mass potential with longitudinal storage

For d>=1 define the explicit function

  U_d(x)=max_(g in D){2<x,g>-d||g||^2}
        =d Psi(x/d)
        =||x||^2/d-dist(x,dD)^2/d.                 (10.1)

Completing the square proves every identity. In particular U_1=Psi and
0<=U_d(x)<=||x||^2/d. Formula (3.4), applied at x/d, evaluates U_d without
an optimization oracle: in the scaled core it is Q/d; in a scaled vertex
chart it is 2s-d; in a scaled edge chart it is z-d/4+y^2/d. The scaled
guards are respectively u+2v<=d, u>=d, and u<=d<=u+2v. Thus both the
longitudinal coordinate and the transverse square remain explicit.

The concrete universal law tested in this mechanism is

  U_d(T_(H_j)x)<=U_(d+2S_j)(x), all x, d>=1, j<=m.  (10.2)

It is a proposed all-block inequality, NOT a proved theorem. At j=m,d=1
it would imply the baseline triangle estimate. It is stronger than that
estimate because of the extra subtracted distance in (10.1), and because
it quantifies over all trailing masses and all child levels. We do not
describe proving (10.2) as a minor remaining technical task.

## 11. Direct short-step payment and an exact long-step obstruction

There is a useful direct theorem for one step on ANY nonempty compact
convex body D. Let d>=1,h>0, g=P_D(x), q=P_D((x-hg)/d). Then

  U_(d+2h)(x)-U_d(x-hg)
     >= B(d,h)||q-g||^2,
  B(d,h)=h[(2-h)(d+2h-1)-h]/(d+2h-1)^2.           (11.1)

Proof. Put theta=h/(d+2h-1) in (0,1] and z=theta*g+(1-theta)*q in D.
Write x=g+w with <w,q-g><=0, the original projection inequality. Evaluate
the maximum U_(d+2h) at z and put e=q-g. Subtracting U_d(x-hg), whose
maximizer is q, gives

  -2theta<w,e> + [d-(d+2h)(1-theta)^2]||e||^2.

The coefficient of <g,e> has canceled because
theta(d+2h-1)=h. The first term is nonnegative, and the square coefficient
equals B(d,h) after expansion. This proves (11.1) directly, including
boundary projections and without any smoothness or external black box.

For 0<h<=3/2 and d>=1 one has B(d,h)>=0: the numerator bracket is at
least (2-h)2h-h=h(3-2h). Therefore every actual short leaf satisfies

  U_d(T_(1+a)x)<=U_(d+2(1+a))(x).                  (11.2)

For 3/2<h<2 the same proof works if
d>=h/(2-h)-2h+1. This condition is stated, not assumed for every actual
level1 step. In particular it must be checked against the real suffix mass.

The proposed ONE-STEP U payment is false at every long bridge h>2, even
on actual reachable inputs. Choose a nonzero x sufficiently near zero
that x and (1-h)x are in the triangle core. Its scaled versions also lie
in the core. Then

  U_d(T_h x)=(h-1)^2||x||^2/d
             >||x||^2/(d+2h)=U_(d+2h)(x).         (11.3)

At any specified original bridge this x is reachable by taking an
appropriately small nonzero initial point along the same axis: the finite
prefix products are all nonzero, so the initial radius can be chosen to
keep the entire prefix in the core and attain the specified tiny bridge
input. No arbitrary cloud of unrelated states is used in this test.

This failure does NOT refute (10.2), which groups both real children with
their bridge. Nor does the short-step result prove that block law by
iteration. The exact interface is the compensation from BOTH complete
child runs, not an unearned monotonicity across the bridge.

## 12. Joint derivation of forecasts and the block-charge interface

For the actual seven projection charts f define orthogonal projectors and
offsets P_f,b_f by

  core: P_f=I,b_f=0;
  edge: P_f=t_E t_E^T,b_f=n_E/2;
  vertex: P_f=0,b_f=v_j.

Their ranges are orthogonal to their offsets. In the actual chart,
P_D(x)=P_f x+b_f and Psi(x)=||P_f x||^2+2<b_f,x>-||b_f||^2.
These are exactly the cell formulas derived in Sections2--4.

At each original position i, including the terminal, set

  s_i=sum_(t=i)^(n-1)h_t,
  d_i=1+2s_i,
  p_i=product_(t=i)^(n-1)(h_t-1),
  L_i^f(x)=p_i^2||P_f x||^2+2<b_f,x>-d_i||b_f||^2. (12.1)

Empty suffixes have s_n=0,p_n=d_n=1. At the actual update, the projected
coordinate is multiplied by -(h_i-1) and the offset coordinate is shifted
by -h_i b_f. Hence

  L_i^f(x_i)=L_(i+1)^f(x_(i+1))                   (12.2)

when f is the actual present chart; no future chart persistence is used.
Choose the smallest face containing the projection at each actual point,
and let sigma_i be its chart. Define

  Delta_i=L_(i+1)^(sigma_(i+1))(x_(i+1))
                    -L_(i+1)^(sigma_i)(x_(i+1)).       (12.3)

For any COMPLETE chronological block of positions b,...,e-1,

  sum_(i=b)^(e-1)Delta_i=L_e^(sigma_e)(x_e)-L_b^(sigma_b)(x_b). (12.4)

For the full word L_n=Psi, so this is the true terminal identity. A chart
change after the last original leaf is included. The explicit correction
is p_(i+1)^2<x',(P_new-P_old)x'>+2<b_new-b_old,x'>
-d_(i+1)(||b_new||^2-||b_old||^2), with x'=x_(i+1).
In particular mass terms are retained in every change of face dimension.

The proposed new storage is the fully explicit, possibly signed quantity

  Z_i(x)=U_(d_i)(x)-L_i^(sigma_i)(x).                 (12.5)

It is NOT a constant attached to a face, nor a transverse square alone.
In the scaled core, for example, it is

  vertex actual: Q/d_i-2s+d_i;
  edge actual:   Q/d_i-z+d_i/4-p_i^2 y^2;
  core actual:   (1/d_i-p_i^2)Q.

Other cases follow from the displayed scaled chart formulas (10.1).
Some Z_i can be negative; no unproved positivity is imposed at every cut.
Identity (12.4) now gives the exact block-payment interface

  sum_block Delta_i
    =Z_b(x_b)-Z_e(x_e)+U_(d_e)(x_e)-U_(d_b)(x_b).  (12.6)

An actual inequality on the LAST difference would be progress. Merely
rewriting it as (10.2) would not be. Section13 proves such an inequality
on a concrete all-m family containing the old strict vertex-switch test.

For context, the exact full initial reserve, also jointly derived, is

  R_initial=||x_0||^2-D_m L_0^(sigma_0)(x_0)
     =||(I-P_sigma0)x_0-D_m b_sigma0||^2
                  +(1-D_m p_0^2)||P_sigma0 x_0||^2.   (12.7)

Orthogonality and completing the square prove the equality; positivity
follows from D_m p_0^2<1 proved in Section9. The full target would require
sum_i Delta_i<=[R_initial+||x_0||^2/16]/D_m. That equivalent global
comparison remains UNPROVED. The new storage does not establish it by
definition.

Fix the original same-m parameters and abbreviate

  A=1+a, B=1+beta, K=beta*c, t=(K+2)/4,
  S_2=2A+B, S_3=2S_2+1+K.

evidence:
# Clock-balanced terminal pool: endpoint success and a column-capacity obstruction

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report. Worker max, invocation86.
Original exact-profile minimax problem OPEN. No formal submission or new fact.

## 1. Outcome and scope

The prescribed new terminal mixture has clock V=2 exactly. Its positive
metric, literal skew completion, all terminal and optimum multipliers, and
full original-space PSD identity are explicit below. Both complete endpoint
row-moment screens pass, uniformly for every enclosing m>=1536:

    first-row S0<-p/16, G0>p/64, P0-b*S0<0;
    last-row Slast<-1/8, Hlast>1/4000, Jlast<0.

Nevertheless the law is impossible, INCLUDING EVERY skew correction C with
Ce=Ct=0. The last queried column has total 2alpha_l, but its invariant
diagonal is P_ll. The exact guards give

    alpha_l>19/20, P_ll<1/3,
    sum_(i!=l)(-N_il)=P_ll-2alpha_l<-3/2.

Consequently at least one original incoming finite multiplier to the last
query is negative. This is a failure of a column mass, not either endpoint
row moment, and not a numerical test of the literal completion alone.

The second mechanism derives a finite transport formulation retaining the
forbidden diagonal AND the full symmetric-factor equality. Its last-column
cut excludes an entire family: terminal mass alpha_l>=1/2, the same
clock-zero endpoint common column, t^T Kt<=3/p, and at least 256p of the
NONLAST metric weight at clocks <=(T+1)/2. Every positive metric satisfying
these conditions fails for every skew completion and every nonnegative
incoming optimum load. This includes a precisely specified family with any
number of sparse interior metric atoms, arbitrary positive last weight,
and a positive tail regularizer. No probabilistic existence theorem is
used or assumed sufficient for the coefficient law.

All these statements are one jointly derived UNVERIFIED proof draft.
Accepted facts1252b8823bb5a290 and931b9653ce0f7201 are used only at their
stated scopes. Earlier unverified reports supply directions, not premises.
This excludes specified coefficient architectures, not the unrestricted
dual cone, not legal primal trajectories, and not the original minimax
problem. It proves no full-class upper bound on W.

## 2. Original problem and accepted interfaces

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n, W_n(h) is the supremum
of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite Euclidean
dimension, convex differentiable L-smooth f with an attained minimizer,
and x_0!=x_star, using x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R.
The original question asks whether W_n_star/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where
W_n_star=inf_(h>=0)W_n(h), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, and the ALL-SPLIT benchmark is

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt(x^2+6xy+y^2))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the signed interpolation convention and
full terminal-square interpretation. Only incoming edges at the actual
UNQUERIED terminal n may be deleted. No queried gradient or prefix pair
is deleted here. Accepted931b9653ce0f7201 supplies the physical word and
mass formula below, and B_n/D<47/50. Its799/800 separation is CONDITIONAL
on the missing full-class bound W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D) for EVERY m>=1536.
That hypothesis remains unproved.

Fix an arbitrary integer m>=1536 and use its SAME parameters in every child:

    eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    b=1+a, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, l=n-1, r=l-1,
    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S, p=1/(1+S), qtar=17/(16D).

Here l and r are last and penultimate QUERIED indices. The terminal n
remains distinct. All short symbols in this report are local aliases;
public names for newly published quantities carry the suffix86, avoiding
any reassignment of project glossary entries. In particular rho below is
a probability VECTOR, not the benchmark exponent. Ltri is a matrix; T is
a scalar clock; superscript T denotes transpose.

Let e be the all-ones column on n queries and e_i its coordinate columns.
Define the strictly increasing clocks

    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, T=t_l=1/p-b, Delta=T-1,
    hgap=1+beta=2-eps, t_r=T-hgap.

The last three physical steps are (b,hgap,b). The needed scalar bounds are

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1,
    2/5<a<sqrt(2)-1<5/12, 1-2a>a^2,
    7/5<b<17/12, 0<eps<=1/6144.                    (2.1)

For the lower bound on a, sqrt(2)<10/7 gives
 a>7*6143/(17*6145)>2/5; the last inequality is equivalent to
35*6143>34*6145. The upper bound uses beta/(1+eps)<1 and
sqrt(2)<17/12. The strict quadratic inequality follows by squaring
1+a<sqrt(2). Bounds on c follow directly from eps<=1/6144 and these
rational bounds for sqrt(2).

The exact mass is

    1+S_j=(1-vword)2^j+vword*c^j,
    vword=beta/[c(c-2)] in(0,1).

It follows either from the cited mass formula or by substituting in
1+S_(j+1)=2(1+S_j)+a*c^j. Therefore

    c^(-m)<p<2^(-m)<2^(-40),
    3/(4p)<Delta<1/p, Delta-b>1/(2p),
    dclock:=1/Delta satisfies p<dclock<4p/3,
    rclock:=hgap/Delta satisfies 0<rclock<4p.        (2.2)

Every elementary small-p comparison below uses this SAME all-m bound;
there is no limit-only argument or evaluated recurrence.

## 3. Tail probabilities and the exact mixed terminal clock

For integer suffix length Len in[0,n], write sbit(Len) for its binary
digit sum and define

    rtail_Len=product_(j=n-Len)^(n-1)(h_j-1)
             =beta^Len*c^(-sbit(Len)),
    s=rtail_n=beta^n/c^m,
    k_i=h_i product_(i<j<n)(1-h_j),
    u_i=|k_i|, U=sum_i u_i, rho_i=u_i/U.

Here v2(j) is the exponent of2 dividing the positive integer j.
The suffix formula follows from h_(n-j)-1=a*c^v2(j) and
sum_(j=1)^Len v2(j)=Len-sbit(Len). With Len=l-i,

    u_i=rtail_Len+rtail_(Len+1), k_i=(-1)^i u_i,
    u_0=(b/a)s, u_l=b, u_r=a*hgap, u_(l-2)=b*a*beta.

The last three terms exceed4/3,5/8,7/18, whose sum169/72>7/3;
thus U>7/3 and every rho_i is positive. We will use

    0<s<u_0<p^2/64, rho_0<1/10, s<p.               (3.1)

For completeness, 2^m-1>16m^2 for m>=16 follows by induction (the
base is the integer inequality at16, and doubling dominates the next
quadratic). Also beta^(-4m)>(1+1/(4m))^(4m)>=2, so beta^(4m)<1/2.
Then beta^n<2^(-4m). Using b/a<4 and p>c^(-m) gives
u_0/p^2<4 beta^n c^m<4(5/32)^m<1/64. The remaining bounds follow
from U>7/3 and p<2^(-40). All these are symbolic inequalities.

Let Ltri_ii=1, Ltri_ij=h_j for j<i, and zero otherwise. Finite
product telescoping gives

    e^T k=1+s, Ltri^T k=h, t=Ltri*e, t^T k=S.      (3.2)

Define the two endpoint terminal-clock values

    Vtail=t^T[k-(1-p)rho], Vlast=b(1-p).

We need Vtail>32, which is rederived here. Put

    Ztail=sum_(Len=0)^n rtail_Len
         =product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+beta^(2^j)/c),
    Mtail=sum_(Len=0)^n Len*rtail_Len.

Expansion over binary digits gives

    U=2Ztail-1-s,
    Mtail/Ztail=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)
                       2^j beta^(2^j)/(c+beta^(2^j)).

Choose j with m/2<2^j<=m. Bernoulli's inequality gives
beta^(2^j)>=3/4 and c+beta^(2^j)<7/2, so Mtail/Ztail>3m/28.
Since ns<1 by beta^n<2^(-4m) and n<2^m, a direct index shift yields
sum_i rho_i(l-i)>(Mtail/Ztail-1)/2>3m/56-1/2.
Indeed the numerator of this mean is 2Mtail-Ztail+1-ns, its denominator
is U<2Ztail, and the numerator is positive. The suffix from i through
the last step has mass at least b+(l-i). As
Vtail=(1-p)sum_i rho_i(1/p-t_i) and1-p>1/2,
this proves Vtail>32 for every m>=1536.

Now set the EXACT proposed law

    xiT=(2-Vlast)/(Vtail-Vlast),
    alpha=(1-p)[(1-xiT)e_l+xiT*rho], alpha_star=p,
    v=k-alpha, E=p+s, F=p-s, eta=F/E.

Here Vlast<17/12<2<Vtail. Since b>7/5 and p<1/21,
Vlast>4/3. Hence 2-Vlast<2/3 and
Vtail-Vlast>30, so

    0<xiT<1/45, sum alpha_i=1-p,
    V:=t^T v=(1-xiT)Vlast+xiT Vtail=2,
    alpha_l>19/20, a+p<=v_l<1/2,
    0<v_0<u_0, 0<alpha_0<u_0,
    e^T v=E, eta in(0,1).                           (3.3)

For alpha_l use (1-p)(1-xiT)>(1-p)44/45>19/20.
Since alpha_l<=1-p, v_l>=a+p. Since b<17/12 and alpha_l>19/20,
v_l<7/15<1/2. At index0, alpha_0/u_0=(1-p)xiT/U<1, proving the
source guards. Define

    R=Ltri^T v,
    R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j)-alpha_i
       =h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0.

The identity follows by subtracting Ltri^T alpha from (3.2).
In particular R_0=bE-a v_0<2p.

## 4. Complete original-space coefficient identity

Normalize smoothness to1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep
x_0,g_0,...,g_n independent formal vectors and substitute ONLY the
actual GD updates. From fact1252b8823bb5a290 use the signed residual

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

For every queried index set y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2.
Then

    y=e*x_0-Ltri*g, g=Ltri^(-1)(e*x_0-y),
    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y.                               (4.1)

The unit-diagonal triangular matrix Ltri is invertible; hence this
coordinate change retains every original queried-gradient direction.
The actual terminal gradient g_n is independent of these coordinates.

For ANY positive weights w_i, let Ww=sum_i w_i and

    K=diag(w)-ww^T/Ww.

For any z with e^T z=E and any zeta with e^T zeta=0 define

    P=K+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    d=zeta+F(v-z),
    A^T=-A, Ae=d, N=Ltri^T(P+A).                    (4.2)

For distinct original indices the literal signed array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,l},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for distinct i,j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i.          (4.3)

Diagonal multipliers vanish. Each matrix entry is explicitly

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                            +R_i v_j+eta Zout_i z_j,
    Zout=Ltri^T z.                                  (4.4)

Thus no finite pair is omitted or replaced by a feasibility assumption.
The total finite-prefix outgoing mass at i, including its optimum edge,
is N_ii; the incoming prefix mass is N_ii-2alpha_i; the terminal adds
2alpha_i. Finite-node divergence is zero, terminal divergence is2,
and optimum divergence is-2, even before any sign claim.

For prefix indices, including star,
Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>. The remaining prefix quadratic
is -g^T N y=-<x_0,(Pe-d)^T y>+y^T P y. The terminal contribution
WITH -2f_n included is

    ||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2-||-s*x_0+v^T y||^2
                                         -2sum_i alpha_i delta_i.

Its value terms cancel the prefix divergence terms. Since
Pe=Ev+Fz and eta E^2=p^2-s^2, the full identity is

    M(q):=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij
      =||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
        +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2
        +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,zeta^T y>.           (4.5)

With ybar_w=sum_i w_i y_i/Ww and e^T zeta=0, this becomes

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
      +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(zeta_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
      +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2+(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i zeta_i^2/w_i.                      (4.6)

The initial charge is paid once. Necessity of q>=p^2+J follows by
setting scalar x_0=1, y_i=c0-zeta_i/(2w_i),
c0=1+sum_i z_i zeta_i/(2w_i E), and g_n=-s+v^T y;
then every square vanishes. Equation (4.1) reconstructs all gradients.
Thus full PSD is equivalent to q>=p^2+J, on the entire original formal
space, not just on legal trajectories. On the actual common queried
gradient direction g_i=G, put X=t^T Kt, Z=t^T z and theta=t^T zeta.
The entire prefix remainder is

    (q-p^2)||x_0||^2-theta<x_0,G>+(X+eta Z^2)||G||^2.

The common derivative has not been discarded.

## 5. The literal metric, paid column, skew, and all optimum signs

The fixed common column and incoming optimum load are

    z=E(T e_0-e_l)/Delta, Z=t^T z=0,
    ellload=1/64, nu_target=ellload*e_0.

This z is not proportional to v, since its interior coordinates vanish
and every odd interior v_i is strictly negative. Choose

    xiM=a(1-a)-a^3/8, sigma=xiM/(1-xiM), omega=p^2,
    what=e_0+e_l+sigma e_r+omega*rho,
    theta0=2-6p, theta=theta0+ellload,
    Xreq=theta0/p-4+ellload=2/p-10+ellload,
    tbase=sum_i what_i t_i/sum_i what_i,
    Vbase=sum_i what_i(t_i-tbase)^2,
    scale=Xreq/Vbase, w_i=scale*what_i,
    zeta=(theta/Xreq)Kt.                            (5.1)

One has 0<xiM<1/4 and0<sigma<1/3: positivity follows from
1-a-a^2/8>1-5/12-25/1152>0, and xiM<a(1-a)<=1/4.
Every what_i is positive. The two unit endpoints imply
Vbase>=Delta^2/2 by minimizing their two square terms over the center.
Also Xreq>0. Consequently all w_i>0, X=Xreq, e^T zeta=0,
t^T zeta=theta, and

    J=theta^2/(4Xreq).

Useful exact bounds are

    1<theta0<2, 2<theta<3,
    Xreq>(1023/1024)*theta0/p, Xreq<2/p,
    1<Xreq/Delta<2, |Xreq/Delta-2|<8p,
    theta/Xreq>p.                                  (5.2)

For the first lower bound on Xreq, theta0/p>1024*4 and
Xreq=theta0/p-4+ellload. For the ratio, subtract2 from
[2-(10-ellload)p]/[1-(b+1)p]; the numerator difference is
(2b-8+ellload)p, negative in absolute value less than8p after division
by1-(b+1)p>3/4. The lower ratio1 follows directly from the same formula.
Finally theta-pXreq=ellload(1-p)+4p>0.

General multiplication in (4.2) gives

    mu=2pR+Ltri^T zeta,
    nu=Kt+Vv+eta Zz-At-2alpha,
    e^T nu=2pV+theta-2(1-p),
    t^T nu=X+V^2+eta Z^2-2alpha^T t.                (5.3)

The last two identities use e^T A=-d^T and t^T At=0. Here
alpha^T t=1/p-3, V=2 and Z=0, so the two moments in (5.3) are both
ellload, precisely matching nu_target. A literal skew realizing both
Ae=d and this nu is as follows:

    rvec=Kt+2v-2alpha-nu_target,
    tmean=(e^T t)/n, cvec=t-tmean*e, Ve=cvec^T cvec>0,
    A0=(d e^T-e d^T)/n,
    fvec=rvec-tmean*d+(d^T t)e/n,
    A=A0+(fvec cvec^T-cvec fvec^T)/Ve.               (5.4)

The two matching moments imply e^T rvec=-d^T t and t^T rvec=0.
Hence e^T fvec=0 and cvec^T fvec=0. Direct multiplication proves
Ae=d and At=rvec; each summand is skew. Every other compatible skew
is A+C with C^T=-C and Ce=Ct=0. Equations (4.3)-(4.4) and (5.4)
define every actual coefficient, with the literal law taking C=0.

All terminal multipliers are nonnegative. Incoming optimum multipliers
are exactly ellload at index0 and zero elsewhere. Every outgoing
optimum multiplier is strictly positive: zeta_i has the sign of
t_i-tbase, changes sign only once, and has zero sum. Every proper
suffix sum is positive, using either the negative preceding prefix or
the strictly positive remaining tail. If zeta_i<0, then
sum_(j>i)zeta_j>=-zeta_i, giving

    (Ltri^T zeta)_i=zeta_i+h_i sum_(j>i)zeta_j
                                  >=(h_i-1)(-zeta_i)>0.

If zeta_i>=0 the expression is positive as well, including i=l.
Together with R_i>0 this proves mu_i>0 for all queries.

Full PSD also passes. By (5.2),

    J<(theta0*p/4)(1+ellload/theta0)^2*(1024/1023)
      <(4225/8184)p.

Since4225/8184<67/128 and p<1/128, one gets

    p^2+J<(17/32)p<17p/[16(2-p)]=qtar.             (5.5)

Thus PSD and every optimum sign are valid for this SIGNED coefficient
law. The remaining finite coefficients must still be nonnegative to
constitute an upper-bound certificate; Section7 proves they cannot be.

## 6. Both endpoint row-moment screens pass

All identities in this section follow from (4.2)-(5.4), not from
assumed finite multiplier signs. They are unchanged by every C with
Ce=Ct=0.

For the first row define

    S0=sum_(j>0)N_0j,
    P0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-1)N_0j,
    G0=P0-Delta*S0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-T)N_0j.

The first row of Ltri^T is b e^T-a e_0^T. Since
Pe-d=2s v+2Fz-zeta and (P+A)t=2Pt-2alpha-nu, direct multiplication gives

    S0=aP_00+zeta_0+2pR_0-2bs v_0-2bFz_0,
    P0=b(2sV+2FZ-theta)-2a(Pt)_0
                                  +2a alpha_0+a nu_0-mu_0.       (6.1)

If every finite first-row multiplier is nonnegative, then

    S0<=0, Delta*S0<=P0<=b*S0,                      (6.2)

because b<=t_j-1<=Delta for j>0. These necessary conditions comprise
the complete total/first-moment screen for that row; they are not
individual coefficient signs.

Put Y=-(Kt)_0=w_0(tbase-1)>0 and dclock=1/Delta. Normalize clocks by
xclock_i=(t_i-1)/Delta in[0,1]. For any base what define

    B=sum what, M=sum what*xclock, M2=sum what*xclock^2,
    B0=what_0, H=M2-M^2/B,
    f=B0*M/B, k0=B0(1-B0/B).

Here H>=1/2, B<5/2, f>2/5, H<=B/4<5/8, and

    Y=(Xreq/Delta)f/H>1/2,
    K_00/Y=dclock*(B-B0)/M.

Since B-B0<3/2 and M>=1, (2.1)-(2.2) give
 aK_00/Y<(5/6)p, while theta/Xreq>p.
Writing S0=aK_00-theta Y/Xreq+Bsource, the remaining term is

    Bsource=2pR_0-2bs v_0-2bFz_0+a(v_0^2+eta z_0^2)<7p^2.

For this use R_0<2p, v_0<u_0<p^2/64, and0<z_0<2p.
Therefore

    S0<-p/12+7p^2<-p/16.                           (6.3)

### 6.1 First-row clock, with finite errors and the load retained

Write K_00=Xreq/Delta^2+eK and Y=Xreq/Delta+eY. Expansion of (6.1)
using R_0=bE-a v_0, z_0=ET/Delta and Z=0 yields

    G0=Gendpoint+Epert,
    Epert=a(2eY-Delta eK)+theta(Delta-a)eY/Xreq,
    Gendpoint=(a/Delta)[btheta0-4-(p^2-s^2)T^2]
       +2bs(2-ET)
       +v_0[2apT+2bsDelta-4a]-aDelta v_0^2+2a alpha_0.           (6.4)

The incoming load cancels exactly in Gendpoint: before cancellation its
first bracket is Xreq-Ttheta-(p^2-s^2)T^2 and there is +a nu_0;
Xreq-Ttheta=btheta0-4-Delta*nu_0. This uses the ACTUAL load ellload,
not a zero-load substitution.

As theta0=2-6p and pT=1-bp,

    btheta0-4-(p^2-s^2)T^2
                  =2b-5-4bp-b^2p^2+s^2T^2.

The bounds (2.1)-(3.3) now give

    |Gendpoint-a*dclock*(2a-3)|<20p^2.              (6.5)

Here the term a*dclock*(4bp+b^2p^2) is <7p^2; the s^2 term is
<s^2/p<p^2; 2bs|2-ET|<6s<p^2; the v_0 bracket has absolute value
<4 and contributes <p^2; aDelta v_0^2<p^2 and2a alpha_0<p^2.
The displayed20p^2 safely bounds their sum.

For an AUXILIARY calculation omit omega*rho only, retaining unit masses
at0 and1 and mass sigma at1-rclock. Put

    Dclock=1-2xiM*rclock+2xiM*rclock^2.

Direct use of the base moments f,k0,H in (6.4) gives the exact interior
metric correction

    Eint=(xiM*rclock/Dclock)
      [theta(1-a*dclock)(1-2rclock)
                               -2a Xreq*rclock*dclock].        (6.6)

This is an auxiliary formula; the positive tail weights are restored
below. One has 1-2p<Dclock<=1 and
 |1/Dclock-1|<rclock. The bracket differs from theta in absolute value
by less than35p, using a*dclock<p, rclock<4p, theta<3 andXreq*dclock<2.
Thus

    |Eint-xiM*hgap*dclock*(2+ellload)|<106p^2.       (6.7)

Indeed comparison first with xiM*rclock*theta costs <100p^2, and
replacing theta by2+ellload costs <6p^2.

Adding omega*rho changes B,M,M2,B0 by at most omega. Both old and
new H are >=1/2, and the old f,k0 are <=1. Direct quotient subtraction
bounds the changes of f,k0,H by2omega,4omega,5omega respectively;
hence each ratio f/H,k0/H changes by at most32omega. The exact metric
part of G0 is

    a(Xreq/Delta)(2f/H-k0/H)

    epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=(1+sqrt(2))*(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    d_j=a*c^j, h_j^lev=1+d_j,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,h_j^lev,H_j),

## 2. Static function, actual integrals, and all ordered rows

The exact radial objective F(r)=f(r)=f(-r), r>=0, is

    2F(r)=kappa*r^2,                        0<=r<=1,
    2F(r)=(r-v)^2+kappa*v,                  1<=r<=u,
    2F(r)=2B*r-C_tail,                      r>=u.    (2.1)

At r=1, the first two values are kappa. At r=u, r-v=B and
2F(u)=B^2+kappa*v=2B*u-C_tail. Thus values and first derivatives
match at both knots. The middle interval disappears at B=kappa.
At kappa=1, v=0 and the function is the usual unit-curvature Huber
function, irrespective of whether B is greater than1.

The derivative g is continuous and nondecreasing, with slopes kappa,
1, and0 on the relevant intervals. Partitioning any interval at its
finitely many knots proves |g(x)-g(y)|<=|x-y|. Hence f is finite,
convex, differentiable, and globally1-smooth. When a piece disappears
the same assertions remain valid. Since G(r)>0 for every r>0,
the unique minimum is0 at x=0. The true initial distance is |s|.

For every physical index including the terminal, define

    x_0=s, x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g(x_i),
    g_i=g(x_i), f_i=f(x_i).

Also include x_star=g_star=f_star=0. For x<y set Delta=g(y)-g(x).
Monotonicity and the Lipschitz bound give 0<=Delta<=y-x and, on [x,y],

    g(t)-g(x)>=max(0,Delta-(y-t)),
    g(y)-g(t)>=max(0,Delta-(t-x)).

Integrating gives both directed convexity remainders at least Delta^2/2.
Consequently all ordered rows, not just adjacent or outgoing terminal
rows, obey

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+g_i*(x_j-x_i)+(g_i-g_j)^2/2<=0.      (2.2)

Equal positions give equality. These are actual samples of one fixed
function, so repeated visits cannot assign different derivatives or
values. The full Gram matrix is PSD because each of its quadratic forms
is a square of a real linear combination of actual scalar vectors.
No formal gradient or zero-step convention is deleted.

For arbitrary advertised L>0 use L*f with physical step sizes h_i/L.
The iterates remain x_i and the payoff remains 2*f(x_n)/s^2.
In particular, when the actual Lipschitz constant is smaller than1,

A same-side noncrossing segment of mass T from radius R to terminal
radius r, with terminal gradient p=G(r), satisfies

    R>=r+T*p,
    2F(r)<=2r*p-p^2.

The second inequality is the actual optimum row from Section2.
Hence 2F(r)<=2R*p-(1+2T)*p^2<=R^2/(1+2T).
This proves the full-word no-crossing claim for every kappa,B.

For exactly one strict crossing, let it be a level-k step h=1+d_k,
with actual prefix/suffix masses P,T, source radius y and gradient p.
The noncrossing prefix gives R>=y+Pp>=(1+P)p.
Its crossing lands at z=h*p-y<=d_k*p, and the noncrossing suffix gives

    2F(terminal)/R^2
      <=d_k^2/[(1+P)^2*(1+2T)].                    (10.1)

Set C=A_k, N=S_m-S_(k+1), x=P-S_k, so 0<=x<=N and T=S_k+N-x.
The denominator is

    (C+x)^2*(2C-1+2N-2x).

Its derivative is 2(C+x)*(C-1+2N-3x); its minimum on [0,N]
is at an endpoint. The endpoint difference, value at N minus value
at0, is N*(2C(C-1)+N(2C-1))>=0.
Thus its minimum is C^2*(2C-1+2N). Since
D=4C+2d_k-1+2N and d_k<C/2, at N=0,

    d_k^2*(4C+2d_k-1)/(C^2*(2C-1))
       <(5C-1)/(4*(2C-1))<=1.

Adding the matching 2N terms preserves the comparison because d_k^2<C^2.
This proves (10.1)<=1/D for every physical cut, including k=0.

Finally consider a trajectory every update of which is either a strict
crossing or a same-side stay queried on a saturated tail. Inequality(7.1)
and the exact tail stay bound each actual radius by the unit-Huber
interval step from its preceding radius. Chronological composition and

This includes every history whose queried AND terminal points all lie

A final SAME-SIDE middle-to-core entry is a separate case. Its output

## 2. Scalar envelope, boundaries, gradient, and minimum

Let L>=0, K=[0,L]e_1 in R^2, lambda=(1,T) with T>0. Minimizing in
Y=(y,0) gives

    Phi(x,z)=phi_L(x)+z^2/2,
    phi_L(x)= min_(0<=y<=L) [y+(x-y)^2/2],
    y(x)=clip(x-1,0,L),
    g_L(x)=phi_L'(x)=x-y(x).                           (3)

Here L denotes normalized segment length, not the advertised smoothness
constant. All calculations use advertised smoothness1. Multiplying Phi
by any original smoothness constant L_orig>0 and using steps h_i/L_orig
leaves the trajectory and the normalized W=2R score unchanged.

The minimizer y(x) follows either from the derivative 1+y-x or from the
projection normal. Substitution gives the complete formula

    phi_L(x)=x^2/2,                  x<=1,
             x-1/2,                1<=x<=1+L,
             L+(x-L)^2/2,          x>=1+L.             (4)

At x=1 the adjacent values are1/2 and the adjacent derivatives are1.
At x=1+L the adjacent values areL+1/2 and the derivatives again are1.
For L=0 the two exterior formulas coincide with x^2/2 and the middle
interval is a point. Thus g_L is continuous and nondecreasing, with
successive slopes1,0,1. Integrating its slope on a partition at the two
breakpoints proves global1-Lipschitz continuity. Consequently phi_L is
convex, differentiable, and1-smooth. Its unique minimizer is0, its
minimum is0, and

    0<=phi_L(x)<=x^2/2                                (5)

because y=0 is always an available trial in (3).

The projection statement retains ALL normals: for every x, the selected
y(x) satisfies (x-1-y(x))(v-y(x))<=0 for every v in[0,L]. The vertical
component of X-lambda does not affect projection onto this horizontal
segment. Hence grad Phi=(g_L(x),z)=X-P_K(X-lambda) at every point,
including every original query, the terminal, and0. One fixed global
function is used throughout, so no separate row-feasibility oracle is
needed. The unique minimum of Phi is also0 at(0,0).

## 3. All exposed segments in all dimensions and exact orthogonality

Every nondegenerate segment allowed by the accepted representation has
the form K=[0,ell]e with ell>0 and e a unit vector. In fact0 cannot be an
interior point of a nondegenerate segment on which a linear functional is
strictly positive away from0: the two opposite directions would have
opposite heights. Thus0 is an endpoint. Write

    lambda=alpha*e+w, w perpendicular to e, alpha>0,
    X=alpha*(x*e+z), z perpendicular to e,

Direct substitution into the defining minimum, with y=alpha*t, yields

    Phi(X)=alpha^2*(phi_L(x)+||z||^2/2).               (6)

The normalized coordinates obey exactly the original advertised
smoothness1 updates

    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_L(x_i),
    z_(i+1)=(1-h_i)*z_i.                             (7)

The factor alpha^2 cancels in the normalized objective/radius quotient.
Initial orthogonality is precisely

    x_0+<u,z_0>=0.                                   (8)

This accounts for all dimensions and all orientations, as follows.

* If u=0, (8) forces x_0=0. The horizontal coordinate stays0 and any
  admissible nonzero initialization is purely perpendicular quadratic.
  In dimension1 there is no such nonzero initialization.
* If u!=0, put T=||u||. All solutions of (8) with x_0=s are

  z_0, including one perpendicular to u in higher dimension, has the

* For K={0}, the function is ||X||^2/2 regardless of lambda. Every
  admissible nonzero orthogonal initialization has that same score.
  If a particular ambient dimension and lambda admit no such point,

## 4. The full-word quadratic factor and the exact weighted score

Define

## 6. Every no-crossing or one-crossing trajectory, all L and amplitudes

Here a strict crossing means consecutive nonzero iterates with opposite

## 6. Mechanism1: exhaustive history split in the invariant-core region

**III. A crossing occurs and the trajectory ever enters the core.**

A previous core entry would have been absorbing, so r>1.

       >v*(1+(1+P)/d_k)
       >=v*(1+A_k/d_k)
       >v*(1+1/(c-2)).                            (6.3)

Section7 bounds this using the true largest step and same-m mass.

**IV. Crossings occur but the core is never entered.**

After a crossing, either some point enters the core or every point stays

Consequently a complete H_j started anywhere inside the closed core

## 5. The actual first-crossing price in a nonreversing child

Consider any complete H_b with kappa*(1+d_(b-1))<=1; for b=0 there
are no steps. Core entry is absorbing in H_b.

Suppose an actual trajectory in H_b has a first strict sign crossing,
at a level-k physical step h=1+d_k. Let r be its source radius,
p=G(r), and P its actual original prefix mass inside H_b.
Core absorption forces r>1. For every exterior source,

    r>=p+v.

Before the first crossing all radii decrease, and every queried gradient
is at least p. The complete left H_k immediately preceding this occurrence
gives P>=S_k. Therefore, for the original radius R_b of this child,

    R_b>=r+P*p>=v+(1+P)*p.

Strict crossing means (1+d_k)*p>r>=p+v, so p>v/d_k. It follows that

    R_b>v*(1+(1+P)/d_k)
        >=v*(1+A_k/d_k)>v Q.                         (5.1)

This is a price measured from the actual child's original start.
When H_b is the initial H_J of H_m, it is measured from the ORIGINAL
full-word start R. It does not reset that denominator.

The same proof also gives a local no-crossing criterion used below:
a start with radius at most v Q cannot have a strict crossing in H_J.
A zero hit is absorbing.

## 6. The first reversing bridge and its complete right child

From the definition of positive J,

    kappa*(1+d_(J-1))<=1,
    kappa*(1+d_J)>1,
    v>=a/(1+a)>2/7,
    v<t<=c*v,
    0<q=t-v<3v/2,
    q<(3/5)*t,
    Q>3,  L_J>7/5.                                   (6.1)

The bound on v uses J>=1 and hence kappa*ell<=1.
The t upper bound follows by multiplying
kappa*d_(J-1)<=v by c. The q/t bound follows from q<3v/2.

Assume the initial H_J has actual terminal radius y<=1.
Its level-J bridge has actual landing radius z=q*y<=q, and the
sign reverses unless y=0. No core approximation is made if z>1.

The following complete H_J, begun at z, has NO strict crossing:
its own core is absorbing, while an exterior first crossing would
require z>v Q by (5.1), contrary to z<=q<3v/2<v Q.
It must enter the core by its actual terminal. Otherwise all queried
and terminal radii exceed1 and every gradient is at least kappa,
so its final radius would be at most

    z-kappa*S_J<=q-L_J*t<0,

a contradiction. A same-side terminal core entry is included here.

To bound the returned radius, use the scalar comparison update

    C_h(r)=r-h*kappa*min(r,1).

This comparison map is nonnegative and nondecreasing on [0,infinity)
because every effective step of H_J has h*kappa<=1. Along the ACTUAL
noncrossing trajectory, (2.3) gives

    r_next=r-h*G(r)<=C_h(r).

Induction through the physical steps therefore bounds its final radius
by the composition of these comparison maps from z. This is an inequality
for the original fixed function; B has not been replaced or rescaled.

For r>0 define b(r)=log(r) if r<=1 and b(r)=r-1 if r>=1.
For an effective step 0<=alpha<=1,

    b(r-alpha*min(r,1))<=b(r)-alpha                 (6.2)

whenever the output is positive; a zero output stays zero.
Inside the core this follows from log(1-alpha)<=-alpha.
For a tail stay it is equality. For a tail-to-core transition it
follows from log(w)<=w-1 at w=r-alpha.

The final comparison radius lies below1, because
b(z)<=max(0,z-1)<L_J*t for z>0. Summing (6.2) and exponentiating
therefore bounds the actual returned radius by K_fr(z)*exp(-L_J*t).

For 0<=y<=1,

    K_fr(q*y)<=y*K_fr(q).                                   (6.3)

For q<=1 it is equality. If q>1 and q*y<=1, it follows from
q<=exp(q-1). If q*y>=1, the derivative of exp(q*y-1)/y has the

Assume 0<R<=v Q. By (5.1) the initial H_J has no strict crossing.

radius would also exceed1, and every queried gradient would be at

## 2. One static function, side cells, and exact word factors

    eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))*(1+eps),

Choose arbitrary positive finite L,H and define

    R=sqrt(L^2+H^2), u=L/R, v=H/R,

* Transfer A: the combined auxiliary/radial exchange Xi is nonnegative.
  On D0=[-1,1], x0=1/100, and d=1, the entire actual H4 stays in the
  quadratic core, and Xi<-6|x7|^2. Every physical and auxiliary normal
  vanishes. The same inequality fails on the inherited cap/cap left H3,
  where Xi<-16(k/C)^2 and BOTH physical H2 reserves are zero.
* Sole repair B: allow the exchange to consume the ENTIRE left H3 bridge
  square and both of its normal terms, while retaining the parent bridge
  as a separately nonnegative term. The candidate Xi+B_i>=0 is false on
  the ONE fixed body D0=[-k/C,1], start x0=C, and the explicit finite
  parameter d=1+2hK(k/C)/sqrt(delta). Its exact residual is
  -delta+h^2K^2(k/C)^2/D^2<-3delta/4, where delta>0 is defined in (8.1).

These are counterexamples to the stated transfers, NOT to H4 U. The core
example has full H4 ratio below3479/10000. The cap/cap example has a
strictly positive parent-prefix U gap; the unused parent bridge pays its
negative repaired exchange. Thus the broader idea of a simultaneous
combination of ALL bridge terms remains open. We do not label a formal
negative coefficient a counterexample, or claim that the entire aligned
H4 strategy is impossible.

One substantive mechanism, including its sole repair, was used. No H5/H6
search or second all-depth mechanism is opened. There is no all-body H4
proof and no quantified all-depth total loss. The stopping point is the
exact parent-bridge payment needed by the cap history, in (8.5).

## 2. Projection identities, every remainder, and radial terms

Projection optimality is <x-P(x),g-P(x)><=0 for g in D0. It follows
by differentiating squared distance on segments; conversely the square
expansion proves sufficiency. Strict convexity gives uniqueness.
Adding the two projection conditions proves
||P(x)-P(y)||^2<=<x-y,P(x)-P(y)>, hence P is1-Lipschitz.
The maximum defining F is attained at P(x); its two maximizing
inequalities bound the first-order remainder by
||v||||P(x+v)-P(x)||. Thus F is convex, differentiable and grad F=P.

At any physical or auxiliary sample of F define the signed ordered row

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2
     =<x_j-g_j,g_i-g_j><=0.                         (2.1)

For a word of mass T, input X and endpoint Y, its physical primitive
energy is

 V=2sum h_i(f_i-f_N)+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                      -T(T+1)||g_N||^2
  =||X||^2-||Y+T P(Y)||^2.                         (2.2)

The equality follows by telescoping the squared physical iterates and
substituting f_i=<x_i,g_i>-||g_i||^2/2. It does not assert V>=0.

For N>0, p=P(X/N), and any Z in D0 define

 R(X,N,Z)=N||p-Z||^2+2<X-Np,p-Z>.                  (2.3)

Both terms are nonnegative. If Z=sum theta_i g_i is a convex mixture,

 R=N||p-Z||^2-2N sum theta_i Q_(i,p).

The sample p has input X/N. Also, without omitting its normal term,

 N R(X,N,Z)=||X-NZ||^2-||X-Np||^2.                 (2.4)

For a word of mass T with trailing d>=1 put N=d+2T,
qY=P(Y/d), and Z=(X-Y+(d+T)qY)/N. The physical gradient weights in
X-Y are the actual nonnegative steps, and the extra qY weight is d+T;
their sum is N, so Z belongs to D0. Expanding (2.4) gives

 U_N(X)-U_d(Y)
   =[V+L(T,Y,d)]/N+R(X,N,Z),                       (2.5)

 L(T,Y,d)=2T<Y,P(Y)-qY>
                     +T^2(||P(Y)||^2-||qY||^2).   (2.6)

For 1<=d1<d2 and q_i=P(Y/d_i), optimality gives
d1(||q1||^2-||q2||^2)<=2<Y,q1-q2>
<=d2(||q1||^2-||q2||^2). Consequently both the squared-norm and
inner-product differences are nonnegative, proving L>=0. Thus every
subtraction of L or R below is an actual subtraction of a nonnegative
term, not an ignorable error.
