history with terminal radius r and gradient p, the prefix payment
in (2.5) gives |s|>=r+S_j*p>=A_j*p. Consequently

    p<=R/A_j<(c-2)*R/d_j<beta*R/d_j.               (6.2)

Zero hits give p=0. Maximizing over actual starts establishes

    G(M_j(R))<=beta*R/d_j for every R>0.           (6.3)

Every crossing history is also pre-cap at its terminal: its gradient
is at most aB<B, whereas G(r)=B exactly for r>=u. Thus its terminal
radius is strictly below u. This justifies (2.4) whenever used below.

We now derive the full Huber reference jointly. Let J_B(r) denote
the even unit-curvature Huber objective with positive-ray derivative
min(r,B). At B=1 it is the kappa=B=1 member of this same family.
Every crossing trajectory under H_m then ends with radius<=a<1
by (5.2), so its twice-energy is its terminal squared gradient.
If its original R<=d_m, (6.1) gives score<=beta^2/d_m^2<1/D.
If R>d_m, (5.2) gives score<=a^2/R^2<a^2/d_m^2<1/D.
We used d_m^2>D from (3.5). Every noncrossing history has score<=1/D
by (2.5). The scaling J_B(x)=B^2*J_1(x/B) leaves the physical word
unchanged, proving for every B>0 and every real s that

    2J_B(Psi_m^Huber(s))<=s^2/D.                   (6.4)

This scaling concerns only the auxiliary Huber reference. It does
not replace kappa,B, or the core knot of the actual kink trajectory.

Here is the exterior comparison in the scope needed for the root
argument: assume EVERY query and the terminal of an actual kink
trajectory have radius>1. No condition on inner reversal is needed.
For any of its crossing steps, (4.4) and (2.2) bound the landing by
d*min(r,B). A noncrossing positive stay from a middle source would
land at most1-h*kappa<1 by (4.1), and so is excluded by the exterior
hypothesis. Therefore every same-side stay in this history is
saturated, including a cap tie if it occurs, and equals r-hB.
Every physical step is thus bounded by

    V_(h,B)(r)=max(d*min(r,B), r-hB), d=h-1.       (6.5)

This is a nondecreasing function of r and is exactly the Huber
symmetric-interval image radius. The latter follows by maximizing
the absolute affine core output -d*x and the tail output x-hB on
[0,r]. Induction through the original physical word bounds the
actual terminal radius by the full Huber interval-image radius
from [-R,R]. The composite Huber map is continuous, so this radius
is attained by some actual start s_* in [-R,R]. Since G<=min(r,B),
integration gives F<=J_B pointwise. Thus (6.4) gives

    2F(r_n)<=2J_B(|Psi_m^Huber(s_*)|)
       <=s_*^2/D<=R^2/D.                          (6.6)

This proof explicitly establishes comparison for exterior-only
histories even when the root could reverse core points.

## 7. All starts with kappa*S>=12

A history without strict crossing is covered by (2.5). For a crossing
history, its actual terminal is pre-cap by Section6. Apply (2.4) and
(6.3) with the TRUE full-word original radius R:

    D*2F(r_n)/R^2<=D*beta^2/(kappa*d_m^2)
       =(D/S)*(beta*S/d_m)^2/(kappa*S).

From A_m<c^m=d_m/a, beta*S/d_m<c. Therefore if kappa*S>=12,

    D*2F(r_n)/R^2
       <(201/100)*(17/7)^2/12
       =58089/58800<1.                            (7.1)

This closes every history in this parameter region, with no
restriction on the number of crossings or later core visits.

## 8. No inner reversal and reduction of the remaining band

Assume first kappa*(1+d_(m-1))<=1. Every physical step preserves the
core and contracts radii there. A noncrossing history uses (2.5).
A crossing history that never enters the core uses (6.6). If a
crossing history does enter the core, (4.7) for the ORIGINAL full
word gives R>vQ and core absorption gives 2F(r_n)<=kappa, so

    2F(r_n)/R^2<kappa/(v^2*Q^2).                   (8.1)

This also covers a core entry at the terminal, with no subsequent
contraction factor assumed.

Put d=d_(m-1) and t_c=c*(c-2). The function z/(1-z)^2 increases on
(0,1). Thus kappa<=1/(1+d) gives kappa/v^2<=(1+d)/d^2. Combining
D<2c^m, a=beta/c, d=a*c^(m-1), and (c-1)^2=t_c+1 yields

    D*kappa/(v^2*Q^2)
       < [2*t_c^2/(beta*(t_c+1))]*(1+1/d).        (8.2)

For example the substitution 2c^m/d=2c/a=2c^2/beta
directly gives this coefficient. The identity lambda^2=2lambda+1
also gives

    t_c=1+2*(lambda+1)*epsilon+lambda^2*epsilon^2
       <1+8epsilon.

Indeed lambda<5/2 and epsilon<1/1000 make the coefficient of
epsilon less than7+(25/4)/1000<8. Since t_c>1 and d>1/epsilon,
the right side of (8.2) is less than

    (1+8epsilon)^2*(1+epsilon)/(1-epsilon).

The exact difference
(1-epsilon)*(1+19epsilon)-(1+8epsilon)^2
=2epsilon-83epsilon^2 is positive. Hence the last expression is
less than (1+19epsilon)*(1+epsilon)<=1+21epsilon.
Equations(8.1)-(8.2) prove

    score<=(1+21epsilon)/D                         (8.3)

throughout the no-inner-reversal region. Since
21/(4m)<=21/6144<1/16, its coefficient is less than17/16.

It remains to consider parameters with kappa*S<12 and
kappa*(1+d_(m-1))>1. For d=d_(m-1), (3.3) gives

    kappa*S>S/(1+d)>
       [c*d/(c-2)-1]/(1+d)>5.                    (8.4)

The last comparison follows from c/(c-2)>17/3 and d>9:
(c/(c-2)-5)*d>(2/3)*9=6.

Moreover (c-2)/c^2<3/40 on the parameter interval. To see this,
3c^2-40c+80 decreases there and at c=17/7 equals27/49>0.
The inequality d_m<(c-2)*(S+1) from (3.3) thus implies

    kappa*(1+d_(m-2))
       <12*[1/S+(3/40)*(1+1/S)]
       =9/10+129/(10S)<1.                         (8.5)

We used S>1000. Therefore the first inner-reversing level is exactly

    J=m-1>=1,
    kappa*(1+d_(J-1))<1<kappa*(1+d_J).            (8.6)

The original left and right H_J each have only core-preserving
physical steps. The sole physical step capable of an inner sign
reversal is the original root h_J^lev. Exterior crossings in
either child remain allowed.

Two convenient additional band bounds are

    v>49/50, D*kappa<603/25<25.                   (8.7)

Indeed kappa<12/S<12/1000=3/250<1/50, while
D*kappa=(D/S)*(kappa*S)<(201/100)*12=603/25.
These bounds use the actual S of the same full word.


## 9. New landing price measured from the ORIGINAL start

Consider the FIRST strict sign crossing of the full H_m trajectory,
assume its source is exterior, and write r for that source radius,
p=G(r), k for the physical level, P for its ORIGINAL full-word prefix
mass, and z for its positive landing radius. Equations(4.6) and (4.1)
give

    R>=r+P*p>=v+(1+P)*p>=v+A_k*p,
    z=(1+d_k)*p-r<=d_k*p-v.                       (9.1)

Every premise in this calculation is tied to the actual trajectory:
before its first strict crossing there was no zero hit and the radii
decreased; all previous queried gradients were at least p; the full
immediate left H_k occurred within the original prefix; and exterior
sources satisfy r>=v+p, including the cap knot and every tail point.
At r=u the equality r=v+p holds. There is no loss of a cap area or
replacement of the original radius by a child's radius.

Since A_k>d_k/(c-2), (9.1) implies R-v>=A_k*p>0 and

    z<=d_k*p-v
       <=[d_k/A_k]*(R-v)-v
       <(c-2)*(R-v)-v=:L_land(R).                 (9.2)

Strictness comes from the mass inequality A_k>d_k/(c-2), even if
the source is at a knot and all preceding gradients equal p.
The positivity z>0 also forces L_land(R)>0 whenever this case occurs.

Define the critical ORIGINAL radius

    Rcrit=v+(1+v)/(c-2).                           (9.3)

It satisfies L_land(Rcrit)=1. If this first crossing lands outside
the core, z>1 forces R>Rcrit. At a landing z=1, strictness in (9.2)
also forces R>Rcrit, though equality is classified as core below.

In the residual band (8.7), c-2<3/7 yields

    Rcrit>v+(7/3)*(1+v)
       =(10/3)*v+7/3>28/5.                       (9.4)

The final strict inequality uses v>49/50:
(10/3)*(49/50)+7/3=28/5. Consequently

    D*kappa/Rcrit^2
       <(603/25)/(28/5)^2
       =603/784<1.                              (9.5)

These are symbolic rational comparisons, not executed numerical
estimates or recurrence values.

There is a useful paid radius consequence. If R<=Rcrit and all steps
AFTER this first crossing preserve the core, then (9.2) gives z<1,
and the terminal radius is at most z<L_land(R). Moreover

    L_land(R)/R=(c-2)-(c-1)*v/R

increases with R>0, because v>0 in this band. Its value at Rcrit is
1/Rcrit. Therefore in this case

    r_n/R<=1/Rcrit.                               (9.6)

If R>Rcrit and a later absorbing core entry occurs, then r_n<=1,
so r_n/R<1/Rcrit as well. The phrase "later absorbing" is essential:
the root could reverse a core state; Section11 checks its location
in every case before applying this consequence.

## 10. Positive-J core-output gate at the original root

In the residual band set J=m-1, d=d_J, L=L_J=S_J/d_J, and

    t=kappa*d, q=kappa*(1+d)-1=t-v>0.
    K(z)=z for 0<=z<=1, K(z)=exp(z-1) for z>=1,
    Z=K(q)*exp(-L*t).

Here K is only a scalar comparison function, not a new objective or
gradient. Since level J-1 is nonreversing in the core,

    v<t<=c*v, q<(3/2)*v, q<(3/5)*t, L>7/5.        (10.1)

The upper bound on t follows by multiplying
kappa*d_(J-1)<=v by c. Then q/t=1-v/t<=1-1/c<3/5,
and q<= (c-1)*v<3v/2. These inequalities use the actual positive J,
which exists by (8.6), and no smaller child receives a new enclosing m.

Let y=|Psi_J(s)| be the actual terminal radius of the ORIGINAL left
child. Assume 0<y<=1; if y=0 the remainder stays zero. The root
gradient is exactly kappa*y, and its strict reversing landing is

    z=q*y<=q.

This landing is allowed to exceed1. The complete right H_J has
core-preserving physical steps. A strict crossing in that child
would require its own starting radius z>vQ by (4.7), whereas
z<=q<3v/2<vQ. Thus the complete right child has no strict crossing.
If its terminal were still exterior, all its queries would have
radii>1 and gradient at least kappa, forcing its terminal radius
to be at most z-kappa*S_J<=q-L*t<0. This is impossible. Hence it
returns to the core by its actual terminal, allowing entry on its
last step.

For a quantitative return bound, for each actual right-child step
define the auxiliary map

    C_h(r)=r-h*kappa*min(r,1).

Because 0<=h*kappa<=1 in H_J, this map is nonnegative and
nondecreasing on [0,infinity). Along the actual noncrossing child,
(2.2) gives r_next=r-h*G(r)<=C_h(r). Monotonicity thus bounds the
actual output by the chronological composition of the C_h maps
from the actual z. This compares trajectories without changing
the original function or cap.

For r>0 put b(r)=log r when r<=1 and b(r)=r-1 when r>=1.
For 0<=alpha<=1 and a positive output,

    b(r-alpha*min(r,1))<=b(r)-alpha.              (10.2)

Inside the core this is log(1-alpha)<=-alpha. Above the core with
an exterior output it is equality. For a transition from above1
to w=r-alpha<=1, it follows from log w<=w-1. A zero comparison
output and its actual bounded output stay zero.

If z>0, one has b(z)<L*t: for z<=1, b(z)<=0, while for z>1,
b(z)=z-1<q<L*t. Summing (10.2) over EVERY right-child physical
step shows that its final comparison radius is below1 and at most
K(z)*exp(-L*t). Also for 0<=y<=1,

    K(q*y)<=y*K(q).                                (10.3)

For q<=1 there is equality. If q>1 and qy<=1, use q<=exp(q-1).
If qy>=1, the function exp(qy-1)/y is increasing with y on
[1/q,1], since its derivative has the sign of qy-1; its maximum
is exp(q-1). These are all cases. Therefore the TRUE terminal
radius of H_m is bounded by

    r_n<=y*Z.                                     (10.4)

The entire right child and the actual terminal have been retained,
even when the root landing was exterior.

We now show Z<1/4 uniformly. Write e=exp(1)>2.
If q<=1, (10.1) gives L*t>7q/3, so

    Z<q*exp(-7q/3)<=3/(7e)<1/4.

The maximum follows by differentiating w*exp(-7w/3) for w>=0;
the last comparison uses e>2 and 3/14<1/4.
If q>1, then

    Z=exp(q-1-L*t)<exp(-1-4q/3)
       <exp(-7/3)<1/4,

since e>2 gives exp(7/3)>e^2>4.

Only the original-radius payment remains. If the original left
H_J had no strict crossing, its radii decreased to y, and
G(y)=kappa*y. Thus

    R>=y+S_J*kappa*y=(1+L*t)*y.

In this band L*t>(7/5)*(49/50)>1, so y/R<1/2.
Using (8.7), (10.4), and the exact core energy gives

    D*2F(r_n)/R^2
       =D*kappa*r_n^2/R^2<25/(16*4)=25/64<1/2.  (10.5)

If the original left child DID strictly cross, its absorbing core
forces its first crossing to be exterior. Equation(4.7), measured
from the ORIGINAL R, gives

    R>vQ>(49/50)*(10/3)=49/15>3.

Since y<=1, now y/R<1/3, and

    D*2F(r_n)/R^2<25/(16*9)=25/144<1/2.          (10.6)

Thus the entire y<=1 branch has score below1/(2D). This rederives
the precise positive-J core-output gate needed here. There are
no later ancestors after the original root; (10.4) is already the
actual original terminal, not an intermediate return surrogate.

## 11. Exhaustive closure when the root source is exterior

Remain in the band (8.4)-(8.7), and now assume

    y=|Psi_(m-1)(s)|>1.

A zero hit anywhere would force y=0 if before the root, or terminal
zero if later, so zero histories have already been settled.
Histories with no strict crossing anywhere have score<=1/D by
(2.5). In the rest of this section a strict crossing occurs.

The original left child cannot ever have entered the closed core,
because all its physical steps preserve it and its terminal y
is exterior. Hence every point up through the root source is
exterior.

Case A: a strict crossing occurred in the original left child.
Its FIRST crossing, which is also the full trajectory's first,
has exterior source and exterior landing z>1. Section9 therefore
gives R>Rcrit. If the root output or any later point enters the
closed core, all remaining steps lie in the right H_(m-1) and
preserve that core. Thus r_n<=1, and

    D*2F(r_n)/R^2<=D*kappa/R^2
       <D*kappa/Rcrit^2<603/784<1.               (11.1)

If neither the root output nor any later point enters the core,
the entire original history, including all queries and its
terminal, stays exterior. Apply the unrestricted exterior
comparison (6.6) to get score<=1/D. This includes every repeated
exterior crossing.

Case B: the left child had no strict crossing. The first crossing
occurs at the root or somewhere in the right child. Its source
is exterior. At the root this follows from y>1. In the right
child, any previous core entry (at the root output or earlier
in that child) would be absorbing and would forbid this strict
crossing. This proves the exterior-source premise without
assuming that a generic root step preserves core points.

Every step AFTER this first crossing belongs to the right child
and is core preserving. If R<=Rcrit, (9.2) gives its landing
z<L_land(R)<=1, and (9.6) gives r_n/R<=1/Rcrit.
The true terminal lies in the core, so

    D*2F(r_n)/R^2<=D*kappa/Rcrit^2<603/784<1.      (11.2)

The endpoint R=Rcrit is included: the landing is strictly below1.

If R>Rcrit and some point from this first crossing onward enters
the closed core, it stays there and r_n<=1. Equation(11.1) again
applies. If there is no such entry, then the entire trajectory
is exterior: before the first crossing it could not have
entered an absorbing right-child core, and the original left
child was already known exterior. The exterior comparison
(6.6) yields score<=1/D.

These cases exhaust y>1. In particular a saturated same-side
root step which enters the core and has no earlier crossing
cannot have a later crossing; it belongs to the direct ray
case(2.5). A same-side entry on the last physical step belongs
to the crossing-and-core case if there was an earlier crossing,
and otherwise to (2.5). No post-entry factor is inserted when
the entry is terminal.

All boundaries are included. Core means radius<=1, so the tie1
is absorbed in a core-preserving child. The cap knot u has the
same value, gradient, update, and area on both adjacent formulas.
When B=kappa, u=1 and the empty middle causes no missing branch.
A zero landing stays zero. The strict mass margin in (9.2)
survives source and cap ties.

## 12. Whole-family assembly and exact limitations

Every allowed parameter choice belongs to the no-inner-reversal
region of Section8, the curvature-mass region of Section7, or the
residual root-only band. In that band the actual left-child
terminal is either y<=1, covered by Section10, or y>1, covered
exhaustively by Section11. Thus every actual start has the bound
(1.1). This proves the stated whole-family theorem as a JOINT
UNVERIFIED candidate.

The proof controls the actual final objective, with all core,
middle, and tail areas retained in (2.1), and with the original
denominator s^2. It uses no amplitude substitution for B, no
reset enclosing m, no omitted physical suffix, and no full-depth
claim inferred merely from a short-child numerical test.

The new root landing-price argument survived this textual case
and boundary screen. No exact legal failure of its landing

This candidate is a mathematical upper bound for the specified

This excludes a certificate architecture, not a primal schedule or the

the unqueried terminal sample is n. Let e be the all-ones column in R^n
and e_i the original coordinate column. Define

a scalar, not the previous terminal-six detail matrix.

Here are guards used below, with elementary justifications:

    7/5<b<17/12, 199/100<g<2,

(70/169)(6143/6145)>41/100. For a<5/12, use sqrt(2)>7/5.

Let pop(r) be the number of binary1 digits of a nonnegative integer r.

## 3. Physical clock metric and its genuine finite corrections

Put Qmass=sum h_i^2, Rmass=sum h_i^3 and

    tmass=(sum h_i t_i)/S,
    Vmass=sum h_i(t_i-tmass)^2,
    rho_clock=X/Vmass,
    Kclock=rho_clock[diag(h)-hh^T/S], yclock=Kclock t.

These quantities refer to the nonuniform actual word. If p_i=t_i-1,
palindrome reversal sends p_i to S-p_i-h_i. Consequently

    sum h_i p_i=(S^2-Qmass)/2,
    sum h_i^2 p_i=(S Qmass-Rmass)/2.

Telescoping (p_i+h_i)^3-p_i^3 and substituting the second identity gives
sum h_i p_i^2=S^3/3-S Qmass/2+Rmass/6. Therefore

    tmass=1+(S^2-Qmass)/(2S),
    Vmass=S^3/12+Rmass/6-Qmass^2/(4S),
    M2:=sum h_i t_i^2
       =S+S^2-Qmass+S^3/3-S Qmass/2+Rmass/6.           (3.1)

No uniform-mesh replacement has been made. The exact level counts are
sum h_i^d=sum_(r=0)^(m-1)2^(m-1-r)(1+a c^r)^d for d=1,2,3.
In particular Qmass=2S-n+a^2(c^(2m)-2^m)/(c^2-2).
Since vword>4/5 and vword c^m>100,
S>(99/100)a c^m/(c-2). Hence

    Qmass/S^2 < 2/S+(100/99)^2(c-2)^2/(c^2-2) < 1/15.

To check the last bound, (c-2)^2/(c^2-2) is increasing for2<c<5/2
and is less1/17, while (100/99)^2/17<1/16 and2/S<1/500.
Equation(3.1) then proves

    Vmass>(2/25)S^3, 0<rho_clock<125/S^2,
    yclock_i=rho_clock h_i(t_i-tmass),
    Kclock>=0, Kclock e=0, t^T Kclock t=X.            (3.2)

The PSD statement is weighted Cauchy--Schwarz. A useful exact telescoping

    (U^3-1)/3-M2=sum_i[h_i^2 t_i+h_i^3/3]>0.         (3.3)

This is the algebraic identity obtained from
(t_i+h_i)^3-t_i^3. Its use below is an inequality with explicit discarded

The default source-normalized details are, for0<=i<=n-3,

    d_i=h_(i+1)e_i-(h_i+h_(i+1))e_(i+1)+h_i e_(i+2),

## 4. The two FULL-array invariants and all factors

For a real original column u, let u^2 mean coordinatewise square and
Gamma_u,ij=(u_i-u_j)^2. From Ne=mu and N^T e=2alpha,

    <Gamma_u,N>=(u^2)^T mu+2alpha^T(u^2)
                   -2(Ltri u)^T(P+A)u.                (4.1)

This is a literal sum over every i,j, including both orientations.
For u=t, (P+A)t=2(Kt+Vv+eta Zz-alpha). Therefore

    T_t=(t^2)^T mu+2alpha^T(t^2)
          -4(Ltri t)^T(Kt+Vv+eta Zz-alpha).           (4.2)

For the prefix column, set w_0=1 and
w_i=product_(u<i)(1-h_u). The actual unit-curvature scalar quadratic
recursion x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i with x_0=1 gives precisely this column.
Equivalently w_(i+1)-w_i=-h_i w_i; finite telescoping gives
w_i+sum_(u<i)h_u w_u=1. Thus Ltri w=e, without a suffix substitution.
Since e^T(P+A)=(Pe-Ae)^T=2s v^T+2Fz^T,

    T_w=(w^2)^T mu+2alpha^T(w^2)-4s v^T w-4F z^T w. (4.3)

For clarity, the global neutral cancellation can also be checked before
using prescribed moments. A perturbation DeltaN=Ltri^T C with
C^T=-C, Ce=Ct=0 has DeltaN e=0 and DeltaN^T e=-Ct=0.
Formula(4.1) leaves -2(Ltri u)^T C u. It vanishes at u=t because Ct=0,
and at u=w because Ltri w=e and e^T C=0. Hence BOTH
<Gamma_u,Ltri^T C>=0 for every such global C.

Similarly, for symmetric Kdel with Kdel e=Kdel t=0, both the row and
column sums of Ltri^T Kdel vanish. Its remaining contribution is
-2(Ltri u)^T Kdel u, zero for u=t by Kdel t=0 and for u=w by
Ltri w=e and Kdel e=0. No locality enters either argument. PSD of
Kdel is not needed for cancellation, only for the certificate class.

Finally (4.3), together with(2.1), contains NO K. Consequently it remains
unchanged even if Kt changes, provided Ke=0, t^T Kt=X, and A is changed
to obey the prescribed compatible moments. This is stronger than
clock-null-detail invariance. Any globally nonnegative multiplier array
must satisfy T_t<=0 and T_w<=0, since both Gamma arrays are nonnegative
and zero on the diagonal. Symmetry of Ltri Gamma is not asserted or used.

evidence:
# Two full-source obstructions for the fixed occupation certificate metric

Status: JOINT UNVERIFIED. Worker max, invocation94, guidance32536a3c943d564c.
All new assertions and the retained calculations reproduced below form one
analytical draft. No verifier call was permitted or made; no new fact ID exists.
The original exact-profile minimax problem is OPEN, with W=2R unchanged.

## Outcome and scope

There are exactly two mechanisms in this report.

1. For the literal max93 metric Knew and common source coordinate z0=bE/a,
   every compatible skew obeys the ORIGINAL three-entry identity

       a N20+b N01+a N02=2a(L^T Knew)20-b r0 > 2q/5.       (S3-old)

   This holds for every same enclosing integer m>=M0=2^26. It excludes
   every simultaneous finite-sign completion, not merely max93's two-anchor
   skew. It actually needs no assumption on z1: any common column with the
   same sum/clock moments and z0=bE/a has this obstruction for this Knew.

2. Freeze exactly the prescribed release, without changing Knew:

       xi=-e0-e1+2e2-[(b+2g)/g](e_l-e_(l-1)),
       zrel=znew+E xi.                                  (Release)

   Its sum and clock moment are unchanged. Its full square is PSD, all
   optimum/terminal signs remain correct, and its two global costs decrease.
   The old three-entry test now passes, with value less than -q/5. Nevertheless,
   for every m>=M=2^64, the entire incoming source column cannot coexist with
   a nonnegative outgoing source row, for ANY compatible skew.

   Specifically let r be the unique integer with 2^r<=m<2^(r+1), and take the
   ORIGINAL query i=2^r+1. If all outgoing lambda0j=-N0j are nonnegative, then

       N_i0 > h_i q/(200 a m) > 0.                       (Moving-cut)

   Thus lambda_i0 is negative. If an outgoing lambda0j is already negative,
   the sign requirement has already failed. This proves the full all-skew
   exclusion of this ONE released common column with this SAME metric.

The increased threshold M is absolute. The physical word, every child, the
prefix products, and the queried clocks always use the SAME enclosing m and
its eps=1/(4m). No function or start enters either threshold. Neither result
excludes the physical schedule, a different source-reaching metric, a different
common column, or a general full certificate. Neither is a primal witness or a
resolution of the original minimax question. No third column is considered.

## 1. Definitions and retained proof interface

The complete original-index definitions and their derivations are reproduced
in Appendix A. They are part of this joint draft, not unverified results being
imported as facts. The appendix's z is znew, the baseline occupation column;
throughout Sections2--9 below z means a general column or is explicitly zrel.
The appendix retains its original equation numbers to make the input audit
traceable; its numbered sections are internal to that appendix.

For immediate reference, fix m>=M0 and set

 eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+eps), a=beta/c,
 H0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a c^j,H_j), h=H_m,
 n=2^m-1, l=n-1, S=sum h, D=1+2S,
 q=17/(16D), pi=sqrt(q), b=1+a, g=1+beta.

Indices0,...,l are queried; n is the unqueried terminal. L is the n-by-n
lower triangular matrix with Lii=1 and Lij=h_j for j<i. It is not the original
smoothness constant. Let e be the all-ones column, e_i the standard columns,
t=Le, ell=Lt, T=t_l=S-a, Delta=T-1=S-b, and Utotal=S+1.

Let pop(i) count the ones in the binary expansion of i. Then

 w_i=(-1)^i beta^i c^(-pop(i)), s=beta^n c^(-m),
 k_i=h_i product_(u>i)(1-h_u), E=pi+s, F=pi-s,
 eta=F/E, V=pi^(-1)-1, Z=-E/a, Qgap=FE=q-s^2.

The terminal distribution alpha uses its actual two-coordinate clock bracket,
not a replaced mean: tbar=(S-V)/(1-pi), j=min{i:t_(i+1)>=tbar},
alpha_j=(1-pi)(t_(j+1)-tbar)/h_j,
alpha_(j+1)=(1-pi)(tbar-t_j)/h_j, all others zero. Put v=k-alpha.
In particular alpha0=alpha1=0, v0=bs/a, v1=-gs/(a beta), and

 e^Tv=E, t^Tv=V, e^Talpha=1-pi, t^Talpha=S-V.

Define the physical moments tmass=sum h_i t_i/S,
Vmass=sum h_i(t_i-tmass)^2, X=D-pi^(-2)-eta Z^2,
rho=X/Vmass, Kclock=rho[diag(h)-hh^T/S], yclock=Kclock t.
Knew is exactly Appendix A equation(3.3): the original consecutive
three-query details with omega0 chosen so K00=3q, all other prescribed
omegas, and the final-six matrix U Rtest U^T with
Rtest=3(ehat0-ehat1)(ehat0-ehat1)^T+ehat3 ehat3^T.
No summand or crossing detail is removed. In Sections2--9 write K=Knew.

The literal common column is

 p_i=h_i w_i/(1+s), p0=b/(1+s), p1=-ga/(1+s),
 r2=(a beta+s)/(1+s), u=p-p0e0-p1e1-r2e2,
 Mu=t^Tu, uhat=u-(Mu/g)(e_l-e_(l-1)),
 gamma=q(1+s)/(2Qgap), zsrc=(E/a)(b e0-e1),
 znew=zsrc+E gamma uhat.

The correct source product is

 (1+s)Csrc=b+ga^2+(a beta+s)a beta.

The positive ga^2 is essential; the earlier TASK minus sign is not used.
Appendix A proves all of the following by finite sums and elementary bounds:

 41/100<a<5/12, 7/5<b<17/12, 199/100<g<2,
 12/5<c<5/2, 99/100<beta<1,
 2^m-1<S<c^m<2^(2m), 1/(3S)<q<1/S,
 0<s<2^(-4m^2), s^2/q<1/100, pi<2^(-m/2),
 K>=0, Ke=0, Kt=yclock, t^TKt=X, K00=3q,
 e^Tznew=E, t^Tznew=Z, znew0=bE/a, znew1=-E/a,
 0<rho<125/S^2, yclock0<0, |yclock0|/(bq)<7/5.          (Bounds)

The accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 is used only for the original ordered
smooth-convex interpolation convention and full unqueried-terminal-square
certificate interface. It does not imply feasibility of our arrays. No
conditional benchmark statement is invoked as a full-function upper bound.

## 2. Full polynomial and all coefficient/moment equations

Take any real z with e^Tz=E and t^Tz=Z, including znew and zrel. Define

 P=K+vv^T+eta zz^T, dvec=F(v-z), rvec=yclock+Vv+eta Zz-2alpha,
 A^T=-A, Ae=dvec, At=rvec, N=L^T(P+A).                    (Full)

Here rvec is a vector, not the integer r in the moving query. Compatibility is
not an unspecified feasibility hypothesis: e^Tdvec=0,
e^Trvec=-t^Tdvec, and t^Trvec=0 follow from the listed moments and
X=D-pi^(-2)-eta Z^2. For instance, with

 tmean=e^Tt/n, cvec=t-tmean e, Ve=cvec^Tcvec,
 fvec=rvec-tmean dvec+(dvec^Tt)e/n,
 Acan=(dvec e^T-e dvec^T)/n+(fvec cvec^T-cvec fvec^T)/Ve,

one has e^Tfvec=cvec^Tfvec=0. Multiplication gives Ae=dvec and At=rvec.
Ve>0 because t is nonconstant. Every compatible A is Acan+C with
C skew and Ce=Ct=0. All our impossibility statements include every such C.

For EVERY original pair,

 N_ij=P_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(P_uj+A_uj),
 mu=Ne=2pi L^Tv, N^Te=2alpha,
 lambda_ij=-N_ij for distinct queried i,j,
 lambda_(i,star)=mu_i, lambda_(star,i)=0,
 lambda_(n,star)=2pi, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
 lambda_(i,n)=lambda_(star,n)=0.                       (Coefficients)

Indeed (P+A)e=2pi v and (P-A)t=2alpha. Finite product telescoping gives

 mu_i=2pi[h_i(pi+sum_(u<i)alpha_u)+(h_i-1)alpha_i]>=2q h_i.

Thus all optimum and terminal signs hold for both columns independently of A.
Every original finite sign is still required. In particular the row and column
capacities, whenever the off-diagonals are nonpositive, are

 sum_(j!=i)lambda_ij=Nii-mu_i,
 sum_(j!=i)lambda_ji=Nii-2alpha_i.                     (Capacities)

The full square identity can be expanded directly. Normalize smoothness to1,
x_star=g_star=f_star=0, and let
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Let Gpre be the original formal column
of queried gradients. GD implies y=e x0-L Gpre and
x_n=-s x0+k^Ty. The incoming-free terminal multipliers sum to2, and the
finite flow is2alpha_i; hence the prefix sum is
2alpha^Tdelta-Gpre^TN y. The terminal terms cancel the sampled values and give

 q||x0||^2+||g_n||^2-2<g_n,-s x0+v^Ty>-Gpre^TN y.

Now Gpre^TN y=(e x0-y)^T(P+A)y and
e^T(P+A)=2s v^T+2Fz^T. Since A is skew and q=s^2+eta E^2, this equals

 q||x0||^2-2f_n+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
   =||g_n+s x0-v^Ty||^2+y^TKy+eta||z^Ty-E x0||^2.       (Square)

This is an identity on the entire original formal space, with g_n free.
K>=0 and eta>0 prove PSD. The initial norm is charged exactly once, by q.
The sign exclusions below prevent this PSD identity from being an upper
certificate. No PSD claim is substituted for the missing multiplier signs.

## 3. General source identity, including its changed diagonal

Write delta0=z0-bE/a. The first ORIGINAL row of L^T is b e^T-a e0^T.
Consequently, with Hsrc_j=s v_j+Fz_j,

 N0j=2b Hsrc_j-a(K0j+v0 v_j+eta z0 z_j+A0j)
     =b s v_j+(bF-a eta delta0)z_j-aK0j-aA0j.

Since v0=bs/a and z0=bE/a+delta0, direct subtraction yields, for EVERY j,

 Pj0-A0j=2Kj0+2eta delta0 z_j+N0j/a.

At j=0, A00=0; no exceptional diagonal term is omitted. Multiplying this
ENTIRE column by L^T gives

 N_:0=2L^TK_:0+2eta delta0 L^Tz+(L^TN_0:^T)/a.          (Source-field)

The term 2eta delta0 L^Tz is indispensable after a source release. Completing

The fixed first clock moment of the outgoing row is

source-clock budget or assign it an artificial value.

At ORIGINAL row2, h2=b and t2=1+b+g. Using
sum_(j>0)N0j=-r0 in (Source-field) gives

All three entries on the left are off diagonal and all three weights positive.
This derivation used no support restriction on A and no symmetry of L times

## 4. Mechanism1: exact all-skew exclusion at the old source

For znew, delta0=0 and r0=(1/a-4a)q. Only d0 in the entire detail sum reaches
source0. Explicitly d0=(g,-b-g,b,0,...), and
omega0=(3q-rho b(1-b/S))/g^2. All final-six columns have zero source coordinate.
Therefore the full source column is Kclock_:0+omega0 g d0, and

 (L^TK)20
 =omega0 bg-rho b^2[1+(1-2b-g)/S]
 =3bq/g-rho b^2(1-b/S)/g-rho b^2[1+(1-2b-g)/S]

## 6. Both complete global costs and the terminal corrections

For any original real column x, let Gamma_x,ij=(x_i-x_j)^2 and

 T_x=(x^2)^Tmu+2alpha^T(x^2)-2(Lx)^T(P+A)x.

                 r-v,                      1<=r<=u_sigma,
                 B_sigma,                  r>=u_sigma;

    2F_sigma(r)=kappa*r^2,                  0<=r<=1,
                 (r-v)^2+kappa*v,           1<=r<=u_sigma,
                 2B_sigma*r-Ctail_sigma,   r>=u_sigma,
    Ctail_sigma=B_sigma^2+v*(2B_sigma-kappa).         (2.1)

Indeed the negative-ray substitution t=-z in the defining integral
gives f(-r)=integral_0^r G_-(z)dz; hence its cap area must use B_-, not
B_+. Integrating the core and middle gives the first two expressions.
At u_sigma the energy is B_sigma^2+kappa*v; adding
2B_sigma*(r-u_sigma) gives the displayed Ctail_sigma. At1 both
expressions equal kappa. Values and first derivatives agree at both
knots. The middle may collapse when B_sigma=kappa, separately on either
ray. If kappa=1, v=0 and the whole law is an asymmetric Huber law.

Across the entire real line g is continuous, nondecreasing, and has
piecewise slopes kappa,1,0. Partition an arbitrary interval at its
knots and at0; the increment of g is between zero and that interval's
length. Thus g is globally 1-Lipschitz. Its integral is finite,
differentiable, convex, and 1-smooth. Since every G_sigma(r)>0 for r>0,
0 is the unique minimizer, with f(0)=0. No evenness is assumed.

The entire actual transcript is smooth-convex legal. For x<y, put
Delta=g(y)-g(x), so 0<=Delta<=y-x. On [x,y],

    g(t)-g(x)>=max(0,Delta-(y-t)),
    g(y)-g(t)>=max(0,Delta-(t-x)).

Both right sides integrate to Delta^2/2. This proves both ordered
interpolation rows, and therefore for every ordered pair of actual
queries, terminal, or minimizer,

    f_i-f_j+g_i*(x_j-x_i)+(g_i-g_j)^2/2<=0.

Repeated positions have identical jets. Their scalar Gram matrices
are positive semidefinite because the associated quadratic forms
are squares of real linear combinations. This is an actual function
construction, not independent prescriptions for two child transcripts.

For each ray, throughout its domain,

    0<=G_sigma(r)<=min(r,B_sigma),
    G_sigma(r)>=kappa*min(r,1).                       (2.2)

If p=G_sigma(r), then G_sigma(t)<=min(t,p) on [0,r]. Integrating gives

    2F_sigma(r)<=2r*p-p^2.                            (2.3)

There is also the strictly scoped conversion

    2F_sigma(r)<=p^2/kappa  when r<=u_sigma.           (2.4)

It is equality in the core; in the middle the difference is
v*(p^2-kappa^2)/kappa>=0. It is NOT asserted farther along a tail.

A strict crossing means consecutive nonzero iterates have opposite
signs. A zero hit stays zero. In a segment with no strict crossing
and no zero hit, all points stay on one ray and radii decrease. If
the segment has step mass M, original radius R, terminal radius r,
and terminal gradient p on that same ray, monotonicity gives

    R>=r+M*p,
    2F_sigma(r)<=2R*p-(1+2M)*p^2<=R^2/(1+2M).        (2.5)

The last inequality is completion of the square. In particular all
full-word noncrossing histories have score<=1/D, independent of cap
balance. Multiplying f by any advertised smoothness L_adv>0 and using
steps h_i/L_adv leaves the actual points and normalized score unchanged.

## 3. Quantitative masses and literal suffixes of the original word

For m>=1536 the following bounds follow directly:

    0<epsilon<1/1000, beta>999/1000,
    12/5<c<17/7<5/2,
    2/5<a<1/2, 0<a<b<3/7<beta, ca=beta<1.          (3.1)

For c, use 7/5<sqrt(2)<17/12 and
(29/12)*(1001/1000)<17/7. Then
a>(99/100)*(7/17)>2/5 and a<1/(12/5)<1/2.
The identity lambda*(lambda-2)=1 and c>lambda give
c*(c-2)>1>beta, proving b>a. The other comparisons follow from
b<3/7 and beta>999/1000.

Let eta=a/b, so 0<eta<1. The word masses obey

    A_(j+1)=2A_j+d_j, A_0=1,
    A_j=(1-eta)*2^j+eta*c^j.                         (3.2)

Substitution verifies the formula and its initial value. Consequently

    A_j>d_j/b for every j>=0,
    A_j<c^j for j>=1,
    D<2c^m=2d_m/a.                                  (3.3)

For L_j=S_j/d_j and j>=1,

    L_j>7/5.                                         (3.4)

At j=1 this follows from L_1=(1+a)/beta>7/5. The recurrence
L_(j+1)=(2L_j+1+1/d_j)/c and c<17/7 preserve the strict bound,
since (19/5)/(17/7)>7/5.

The useful finite margins are

    S>1000, d_(m-1)>9, d_(m-1)>1/epsilon,
    d_m>2/a, d_m^2>D, D/S<201/100.                  (3.5)

Indeed d_(m-1)>2^m/5. At integer m=8, 2^m>20m, and doubling
preserves this inequality on increasing m by1. Thus
d_(m-1)>4m=1/epsilon; for m>=1536 this also gives the bounds9
and1000, using S>=1+d_(m-1). Since 2/a<5, the bound d_m>2/a
and then d_m^2>D follow from (3.3). Finally D/S=2+1/S.

A physical level-k bridge in a complete H_j has a chronological
prefix containing its full immediate left H_k, hence prefix mass
at least S_k. Its physical suffix is exactly

    H_k, (1+d_(l_1)),H_(l_1), ...,
         (1+d_(l_t)),H_(l_t),
    k<l_1<...<l_t<=j-1.                              (3.6)

Ascend its binary word tree: each ancestor reached through its left
child contributes its bridge and complete right child; each reached
through its right child contributes nothing. This proves (3.6),
including empty suffixes and skipped ancestor levels. All later
arguments use this physical suffix, not a selected subsequence.

## 4. Exact SIGNED interval images, including unavailable pieces

Fix h=1+d with d>=0. For a source on ray sigma, express its signed
output relative to that source sign as T_sigma(r)=r-hG_sigma(r).
Then

    T_sigma(r)=(1-h*kappa)*r,           0<=r<=1,
                 h*v-d*r,             1<=r<=u_sigma,
                 r-h*B_sigma,         r>=u_sigma.    (4.1)

Adjacent formulas agree at the knots. Define [z]_+=max(z,0).
For an entire source interval 0<=r<=R the exact greatest positive
same-ray output and opposite-ray output are respectively

    Stay_sigma(R)=max([1-h*kappa]_+*min(R,1),
                      [R-h*B_sigma]_+),
    Cross_sigma(R)=max([h*kappa-1]_+*min(R,1),
                       [d*min(R,u_sigma)-h*v]_+).     (4.2)

To prove these expressions, first maximize each affine piece. On
the core its signed maximum and minimum are its appropriate endpoint
or zero. On a present middle piece, T_sigma is nonincreasing: its
greatest positive value is already the core endpoint at1, and its
most negative value occurs at min(R,u_sigma). On a present tail,
T_sigma is increasing: its positive maximum is the endpoint at R,
and its most negative value is at u_sigma, already represented by
the middle endpoint. The origin always supplies zero.

There are two possible formal pieces that are not present. If R<1,

    dR-hv-(h*kappa-1)R=hv*(R-1)<=0,

so the formal middle crossing term is dominated by the actual core
crossing term. If R<u_sigma, the formal tail stay R-hB_sigma is
at most the actual endpoint R-hG_sigma(R), hence cannot exceed the
true stay maximum. If that formal value is positive, the actual
pre-cap endpoint is positive and already accounted for by the core
endpoint. This proves both maxima without adding unattained branches.

For an input interval [-P,Q], where P,Q>=0, the exact output is
[-Pnext,Qnext] with

    Qnext=max(Stay_+(Q),Cross_-(P)),
    Pnext=max(Stay_-(P),Cross_+(Q)).                   (4.3)

The maxima are attained on the two compact source intervals. The
whole step map is continuous and fixes0, so its image is exactly
that interval, with no holes. Inductively the image of any interval
containing0 under an entire word is an interval containing0. In
general Pnext and Qnext differ: oddness and a symmetric radius
recurrence are not used.

Equations(4.1)-(4.3) cover R=0, R=1, R=u_sigma, B_sigma=kappa,
v=0, d=0, h*kappa=1, and zero outputs because the adjacent affine
formulas and positive parts agree. For d=0 a positive pre-cap
middle stay can equal1-kappa; the actual hierarchy has d_j>0.

For a STRICT crossing from actual radius r on ray sigma, with
p=G_sigma(r) and opposite-ray landing z>0,

    z=(1+d)p-r<=d*p.                                 (4.4)

This uses p<=r and is independent of the destination cap. Its
destination gradient satisfies G_(-sigma)(z)<=z, not necessarily
G_sigma(z); this distinction is retained below.

For a positive same-ray output from a strictly pre-cap source
r<u_sigma, one necessarily has h*kappa<1, the output lies in
the core, and it is at most both

    (1-h*kappa)*r and (1-h*kappa)*min(r,1).            (4.5)

In the core this is (4.1). In the middle write the output as
1-h*kappa-d*(r-1), and use r>=1. A cap-knot source is instead
assigned to the saturated case; its two output formulas agree.

If all steps of H_j have h*kappa<=1, the closed core [-1,1]
is absorbing, regardless of the caps, with full product

    Pcore_j=product_(h in H_j)(1-kappa*h)
       <=exp(-kappa*S_j).                            (4.6)

The factors are nonnegative and 1-z<=exp(-z); no physical step
or terminal-only entry is replaced by an extra factor.

## 5. First exterior crossing: payment from the ORIGINAL radius

Consider the first strict crossing in a complete-word trajectory,
with exterior source r>1 on a definite ray sigma. Put
p=G_sigma(r), let k be its physical level, P its chronological
prefix mass from the original start of that word, and z its
landing radius. Earlier radii decrease on this same source ray,
and their gradients are at least p. Exterior sources have r>=v+p:
equality in the middle, inequality in the tail. Thus

    R>=r+P*p>=v+(1+P)p>=v+A_k*p,
    z<=d_k*p-v.                                      (5.1)

The last inequality is the actual update, not a new starting
condition for a child. It uses no property of the destination cap.
Since A_k>d_k/b and R-v>=A_kp>0,

    z <=(d_k/A_k)*(R-v)-v
       < b*(R-v)-v=:Lland(R).                        (5.2)

In particular when v>0, strict crossing requires p>v/d_k and

    R>v*Qprice, Qprice=(c-1)/(c-2)>10/3.             (5.3)

The inequality Qprice>10/3 follows from b<3/7. In a nonempty
complete word whose steps preserve the core, a first crossing
must have exterior source; any earlier core entry is absorbing.
Such a word has v>0 because all its steps exceed1. These facts
justify (5.3) whenever it is invoked for a core-preserving child.

Whenever the original denominator is needed below, R in (5.1)
is explicitly the start of H_m or its original left prefix,
which has that same start. Applying (5.3) to a right child is
used only to rule out a crossing there, never to reset the
full-word denominator.

## 6. Joint signed gradient grid and crossing capture: balanced caps

In this section assume Bmin>=b*Bmax. Since b>a,

    a*Bmax < Bmin <= B_sigma on either ray.           (6.1)

For EVERY j>=1 through m prove jointly:

    p(Psi_j(s))<=a*c^(-q)*Bmax
      for every integer q>=0 and |s|<=d_j*c^(-q)*Bmax; (6.2)

    any strict crossing within a complete H_j
      implies p(Psi_j(s))<=a*Bmax.                   (6.3)

The function and both caps stay fixed at every q. The grid bounds
the actual terminal gradient on its actual sign; it is not a radial
map for an odd extension and does not replace either cap by w.

First give the derivation of capture at any depth using only grid
claims at proper-child depths. A level-k crossing has landing
radius<=d_k*Bmax by (4.4). Its immediate full right H_k therefore
has terminal gradient<=aBmax if k>=1, by its q=0 grid. If k=0,
the empty child leaves a landing whose destination gradient is
at most its radius<=aBmax. At any subsequent retained ancestor
of level l in (3.6), (6.1) puts the incoming point strictly
before the cap of its actual ray. If that bridge crosses, its
landing is at most d_l*aBmax<=d_lBmax, and the full following
H_l restores the bound by its grid. If it has a positive
same-ray stay, (4.5) puts that stay in the core, with no gradient
increase. It also gives kappa*(1+d_l)<1, so the subsequent
smaller steps of H_l preserve the core and cannot increase
its gradient. Zero is absorbing. Every suffix step is covered
by (3.6); every grid depth is less than the depth of the entire
word whose capture is being established.

For the base j=1, put w=c^(-q)Bmax and R=beta*w=d_1*w. Unlike
the odd proof, the smaller-cap ray MAY already be saturated.
There are three cases at the single step h=ell=1+a.

* A crossing lands at radius<=a*p(s)<=a|s|<=a*beta*w<a*w.
  Its destination gradient is no greater than that radius.
* A positive pre-cap stay has output gradient at most
  kappa*[1-ell*kappa]_+*min(R,1)<=R/(4ell)<a*R<a*w.
  Here 4aell>4*(2/5)*(7/5)>1.
* A positive saturated stay on ray sigma has radius at most

      beta*w-ell*B_sigma <= [beta-ell*b]*w <a*w.       (6.4)

  The first inequality uses B_sigma>=bBmax>=bw. For the strict
  second inequality, ell*b-(beta-a)=b-a>0, since beta=ac.
  The output gradient is at most its radius, including if that
  output itself is still saturated. If the displayed upper
  radius is negative, this stay case is simply impossible.

Zero gives zero. This proves (6.2) at j=1, and the preceding
proper-child suffix argument proves (6.3) there.

Now assume both claims through j>=1. For the parent take any
actual start with radius R<=c*d_j*w, w=c^(-q)Bmax. Let y be
the radius of its actual left-child output on its actual ray
sigma, and z the radius after the parent bridge. If y=0 the
rest is zero. Partition the nonzero bridge as follows.

(a) Strict crossing. If q=0, G_sigma(y)<=Bmax=w. If q>=1, the
left child starts within d_j*c^(-(q-1))*Bmax, so its grid gives
G_sigma(y)<=a*c*w=beta*w<=w. The bridge lands at radius<=d_j*w.
The complete right-child grid gives terminal gradient<=a*w.

(b) Positive saturated same-ray stay, including y=u_sigma.
The left child could not have crossed, because its capture
would imply G_sigma(y)<=aBmax<B_sigma, contradicting saturation.
It could not have hit zero. Thus all its points remain on
the current ray, with radii decreasing to y>=u_sigma; all
its queried gradients are B_sigma. Consequently

    y=R-S_j*B_sigma,
    z=R-(A_j+d_j)*B_sigma
       <=c*d_j*w-(A_j+d_j)*B_sigma <d_j*w.          (6.5)

To verify the last payment, use (3.3) and balance:

    (A_j+d_j)*B_sigma
       >=(A_j+d_j)*b*Bmax
       >(1+b)*d_j*Bmax
       >=(c-1)*d_j*w.

Then the full right H_j uses its q-th grid. A prior crossing
is ruled out before asserting the all-tail prefix; no tail
assumption is inferred from the endpoint alone.

(c) Positive pre-cap same-ray stay, with no crossing in the
left child. By (4.5), kappa*(1+d_j)<1, and the right child
stays in the core. Put t=kappa*d_j and L=L_j=S_j/d_j.
The noncrossing left child gives

    R>=y+S_j*G_sigma(y)>=(1+kappa*S_j)*y,

where G_sigma(y)>=kappa*y is used only at this pre-cap source.
Combining (4.5)-(4.6), R<=c*d_j*w, and 0<t<1 gives

    p_out<=kappa*exp(-Lt)*(1-kappa-t)*R/(1+Lt)
       <=c*t*(1-t)*exp(-Lt)/(1+Lt)*w
       <=c*t*(1-t)/(1+Lt)^2*w
       <=c/[4*(1+L)]*w<a*w.                         (6.6)

The third line uses exp(Lt)>=1+Lt; the fourth follows from

    (1+Lt)^2-4*(1+L)*t*(1-t)=(1-(L+2)t)^2.

Finally c/[4*(1+L)]<85/336<2/5<a by (3.1),(3.4).

(d) Positive pre-cap same-ray stay, with a crossing in the
left child. Again kappa*(1+d_j)<1, so both children preserve
their cores. The first crossing in that original left child
has exterior source and pays R>vQprice by (5.3), using the
actual parent start. Here 0<t<v. The parent bridge output
is at most 1-kappa-t=v-t, and its full right child yields

    p_out<=kappa*(v-t)*exp(-Lt).

Since R<=c*d_j*w and R>vQprice, w>vQprice/(c*d_j), giving

    p_out/w<c*t*(v-t)*exp(-Lt)/(vQprice)
       <=c*v/(4Qprice)<=c/(4Qprice)<a.              (6.7)

We used t*(v-t)<=v^2/4 and
c/(4Qprice)<51/280<2/5<a. All divisions by v are in the
core-preserving case v>0.

A zero bridge is already settled. These are all bridge
outcomes and all first-child crossing possibilities. Thus
(6.2) holds at j+1. The proper-child suffix argument then
gives (6.3) at j+1. This is a noncircular joint induction.

In particular every crossing history ends strictly before
its ACTUAL terminal-side cap knot, since

    p(x_terminal)<=aBmax<Bmin<=B_terminal-side.       (6.8)

The balanced ratio is used in (6.4),(6.5),(6.8), not silently
extended to a cap ratio below b.

## 7. Global gradient control and the asymmetric Huber reference

For 0<R<=d_jBmax choose an integer q>=0 with

    d_j*c^(-(q+1))*Bmax<R<=d_j*c^(-q)*Bmax.

An exact grid boundary is the upper endpoint. For every actual
start |s|<=R, (6.2) gives terminal gradient
<=a*c^(-q)Bmax<beta*R/d_j. For R>d_jBmax, a crossing history
uses (6.3) and aBmax<beta*R/d_j. A noncrossing history on
its own ray, with terminal radius r and gradient p, has

    |s|>=r+S_j*p>=A_j*p,
    p<=R/A_j<b*R/d_j<beta*R/d_j.

A zero hit gives p=0. Thus at all j>=1 and R>0,

    p(Psi_j(s))<=beta*R/d_j for every |s|<=R.        (7.1)

Now define the asymmetric unit-curvature Huber objective J
whose signed derivative on ray sigma is sigma*min(r,B_sigma).
We first assume Bmin>=1 and Bmin/Bmax>=b. This is exactly the
present family with kappa=1, common knot1, v=0, and the same
two caps. The already derived grid and capture apply directly.
On a crossing history its terminal is pre-cap on its actual
side by (6.8), so its twice-energy is p_terminal^2. Equation
(7.1) and d_m^2>D give its score<=beta^2/d_m^2<1/D. Every
noncrossing history has score<=1/D by (2.5). Hence

    2J(Psi_m^J(s))<=s^2/D.                          (7.2)

For arbitrary positive balanced caps, scale BOTH caps by their
common divisor Bmin: write x=Bmin*y and

    J(x)=Bmin^2*J_tilde(x/Bmin),

where J_tilde has caps B_sigma/Bmin>=1. The signed GD recursion
in y uses the identical physical word; the original radius and
energy scale by Bmin and Bmin^2. Thus (7.2) holds for every
positive pair of balanced caps. This scale change is only a
proof of the auxiliary Huber reference, not a replacement of
the original kink function or its core knot.

For this J, the exact signed interval update has ray maxima

    Stay_sigma^J(R)=[R-hB_sigma]_+,
    Cross_sigma^J(R)=d*min(R,B_sigma), h=1+d.         (7.3)

Inside the Huber core the signed output is -dr. On its tail
it is r-hB_sigma. The largest crossing is the core endpoint
at min(R,B_sigma), and the largest positive stay is the tail
endpoint at R, if positive. These give (7.3) even for absent
tails. The pair update is (4.3) with these two functions. Both
functions, hence both pair coordinates, are nondecreasing in
the relevant nonnegative radii.

Suppose now that an actual kink history has EVERY queried
point and its terminal at radius>1. Start the auxiliary J
interval at [-R,R], with R=|s|, and propagate its exact two
signed endpoints through the original physical word. Inductively
the actual signed kink point lies within this Huber interval.
For if its next step crosses from side sigma, (4.4),(2.2) give
landing<=d*min(r,B_sigma), controlled by that side's crossing
term in (7.3). If it stays on its side with positive output,
a pre-cap middle source would land in the core by (4.5),
contrary to the exterior-history assumption. Hence this stay
is saturated and equals r-hB_sigma, controlled by the same-side
stay term. Coordinate monotonicity proves the induction.

Let the actual terminal side be sigma_n. The corresponding
signed endpoint of the final Huber interval has radius at
least |x_n|. It is attained by an ACTUAL Huber trajectory
starting at some s_* in [-R,R], because the complete map is
continuous on that compact interval. Both ray energies are
nondecreasing in radius, and G_sigma<=min(r,B_sigma) gives
F_sigma(r)<=J(sigma*r). Therefore

    2f(x_n)<=2J(Psi_m^J(s_*))<=s_*^2/D<=R^2/D.       (7.4)

The selected endpoint is on the actual terminal side. No
evenness, oddness, single symmetric envelope, or artificial
denominator is used. The comparison imposes no inner-reversal
condition: its premise is the actual history remaining exterior.

## 8. All starts with large curvature mass

Assume kappa*S>=12 and balanced caps. Noncrossing histories
use (2.5). Crossing histories end strictly pre-cap on the
actual terminal side by (6.8). Thus (2.4),(7.1) give

    D*2f(x_n)/R^2<=D*beta^2/(kappa*d_m^2)
       =(D/S)*(beta*S/d_m)^2/(kappa*S)
       <(201/100)*(17/7)^2/12
       =58089/58800<1.                              (8.1)

Here beta*S/d_m<c follows from A_m<c^m=d_m/a.
No limitation on previous sign changes, tail visits, or core
returns is imposed. The terminal-side energy conversion is
legitimate solely because strict pre-cap capture was proved.

## 9. No inner reversal and the residual parameter band

Assume first kappa*(1+d_(m-1))<=1. All physical steps preserve
the closed core. Noncrossing histories use (2.5). Crossing
histories that never enter that core use (7.4). For a crossing
history with any core entry, the first crossing has exterior
source and pays R>vQprice; the terminal stays in the core on
whichever side it has reached, so 2f(x_n)<=kappa. Hence

    score:=2f(x_n)/R^2<kappa/(v^2*Qprice^2).           (9.1)

This includes a first core entry at the actual terminal.
Put d=d_(m-1) and t_c=c*(c-2). The increasing function
z/(1-z)^2 on (0,1), evaluated at kappa<=1/(1+d), gives
kappa/v^2<=(1+d)/d^2. With D<2c^m and
(c-1)^2=t_c+1, obtain

       <[2*t_c^2/(beta*(t_c+1))]*(1+1/d).           (9.2)

For example 2c^m/d=2c/a=2c^2/beta gives this expression
by direct substitution. The identity lambda^2=2lambda+1 yields

       <1+8epsilon.

above1 by 7+(25/4)/1000<8. Since t_c>1 and d>1/epsilon,

The exact difference
(1-epsilon)*(1+19epsilon)-(1+8epsilon)^2
=2epsilon-83epsilon^2 is positive. Therefore the last

using 19epsilon<=1. This proves (1.1) in this parameter region.
Also 21/(4m)<=21/6144<1/16, proving its strict final envelope.

The remaining parameters satisfy kappa*S<12 and
kappa*(1+d_(m-1))>1. Write d=d_(m-1). From (3.3),

    kappa*S>S/(1+d)>[c*d/b-1]/(1+d)>5.              (9.3)

For the final inequality, c/b>17/3 and d>9 imply
(c/b-5)d>(2/3)*9=6. On 12/5<c<17/7,

    b/c^2<3/40:

the polynomial 3c^2-40c+80 decreases there and is27/49>0

    kappa*(1+d_(m-2))
       <12*[1/S+(3/40)*(1+1/S)]
       =9/10+129/(10S)<1.                           (9.4)

Here S>1000. Set J=m-1. The ORIGINAL root is consequently
the sole physical step that can reverse a core input; both
complete H_J children individually preserve that core. In
this whole residual band,

    5<kappa*S<12,
    v>49/50, D*kappa<603/25<25.                     (9.5)

Indeed kappa<12/S<1/50 and D/S<201/100. The equality
kappa*S=12 belongs to Section8; equality at the largest
core-nonreversal threshold belongs to the first region here.

## 10. Root source in the core, including an exterior root landing

In the residual band put y=|Psi_J(s)|. If y=0 the terminal
is zero. Suppose 0<y<=1. Regardless of its sign the root
gradient has magnitude kappa*y and the root reverses, with
actual opposite-ray landing z=q*y, where

    t=kappa*d_J, q=kappa*(1+d_J)-1=t-v>0,
    L=S_J/d_J>7/5.

The child core nonreversal in (9.4) implies

Every inequality has an absolute margin independent of

For a concrete nonempty fixed function with a genuine

# Unsaturated terminal mass: full original coefficient interface and a source-capacity obstruction

Status: JOINT UNVERIFIED. Worker max4, continuation invocation92, guidance
52e9d99015702be8, plan7000802aea7e2692. This is one joint analytical draft.
The current TASK grants zero formal calls; no new statement in this report is
a verifier-accepted fact. Original target OPEN. W=2R throughout.

## 1. Result and scope

The general terminal-square and original-row flow interface is derived below
without imposing q=pi^2. The proposed constant-gradient Gram is correct when
all optimum-to-query multipliers vanish. When those multipliers are allowed,
the two additional terms are displayed explicitly in (3.1).

At q0=1/D, nonnegative multipliers and the actual tight Huber trajectory force
those optimum incoming rows to vanish. The constant-gradient restriction then
forces V+1=D*pi and pi^2<=q0. For the specified terminal distribution supported
only at l=n-1, this fixes pi=b/(S+b), strictly below sqrt(q0). It leaves real
freedom in the mixed initial-point/gradient coefficients; this freedom is not
present under saturation q=pi^2.

The ONE literal paid family tested at q=17/(16D) is

 M_trial = ||g_n-pi*x0+r^T g||^2
         + delta ||x0-u^T g||^2 + gamma ||dsrc^T g||^2
         + kappa ||x0+theta*dsrc^T g||^2 + xi ||dtail^T g||^2,       (1.1)

where theta is any real number, xi>=0, and all columns and coefficients are
specified in Section5. Its paid block has rank at most two, genuine mixed x0
terms, zero-sum gradient columns, and an adjustable terminal-three detail.
That detail can pay the elementary last-query column deficit of the baseline.

Nevertheless the ENTIRE family is excluded by an exact original source cut:

 a * sum_(j=1)^l lambda_(0,j) = mu0-P00
  = -2ab*k + a^2*b^2/T^2 - gamma/b^2 + kappa
                              - (kappa/b^2)(theta+b)^2
  < -3a/(4S) < 0.                                            (1.2)

Here P=sym(N Ltri), mu_i=lambda_(i,star), and k=(S-ab)/((S+b)T).
Every weight on the left must be nonnegative. Equation (1.2) holds for every
theta, every xi>=0, every compatible skew completion, and every enclosing
m>=1536. It is not the failure of a particular chosen array.

The whole unit-quadratic polynomial separately forces theta=0 or theta=-2.
Both survive all linear flow/skew compatibility equations and both fail (1.2).
The theta=-2 case explicitly spends the loose target in mixed terms. Thus the
failure is not an artifact of retaining only the q0 certificate search.

This excludes the displayed family, not all unsaturated pi, not all tail-source
certificates, and not the hierarchy itself. No primal lower bound or full W
upper bound follows. The missing hypothesis of accepted931b9653ce0f7201 remains
unproved.

## 2. Original rows and the general full coefficient interface

Normalize smoothness to1 and the optimum to x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Let h be
any positive word of length n>=2, let l=n-1, and retain the original formal
vectors x0,g0,...,g_l,g_n. The final vector g_n is not queried in the updates:

 x_i=x0-sum_(u<i)h_u*g_u,   0<=i<=n.
 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.

All distinct ordered rows involving star, queries, and terminal are available.
In the selected architecture only incoming-terminal multipliers are set to
zero. Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290, parts(b),(c), licenses that selection for
tight certificates and gives the exact terminal-square interface. It does
NOT license deleting either orientation of any queried-prefix row.

Write

 lambda_(n,star)=2pi, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
 alpha_i>=0, pi>=0, pi+sum_i alpha_i=1,
 lambda_(i,n)=lambda_(star,n)=0.

Initially retain BOTH optimum directions:

 mu_i=lambda_(i,star)>=0,  nu_i=lambda_(star,i)>=0.

Let e be the n-dimensional all-ones column, e_i its coordinate columns, and
Ltri the n-by-n matrix with diagonal1, entry h_j in row i,column j when j<i,
and zero above the diagonal. Write g=(g0,...,g_l)^T; expressions involving its
columns mean the corresponding sums of Euclidean vectors and inner products.
Set

 y=e*x0-Ltri*g,  zeta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2,
 t=Ltri*e,  t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j,  S=sum_i h_i, D=1+2S.

Direct expansion gives

 Q_ij=zeta_i-zeta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>,
 Q_(i,star)=zeta_i-<g_i,y_i>,  Q_(star,i)=-zeta_i.

Define an n-by-n real matrix N from the original prefix multipliers by

 N_ij=-lambda_(i,j) for i!=j,
 N_ii=mu_i+sum_(j!=i)lambda_(i,j).

Exact cancellation of every f_i is equivalent to

 Ne=mu,             N^T e=2alpha+nu.                       (2.1)

Indeed the coefficient of f_i before subtracting terminal flow is prefix
outflow minus prefix inflow, namely (N^T e)_i-nu_i; the terminal outgoing
row contributes -2alpha_i. There is no unexamined reversed flow convention.
After this cancellation the prefix interpolation sum is

 2sum_i alpha_i*zeta_i - sum_ij N_ij <g_i,y_j>.

Define

 r=h-Ltri^T*alpha,
 r_i=h_i*(pi+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j)-alpha_i,
 V=e^T r=S-alpha^T t.                                     (2.2)

These identities follow by expanding column i of Ltri^T alpha and using
sumalpha=1-pi. Consequently

 x_n-sum_i alpha_i*y_i = pi*x0-r^T g.

Expanding the outgoing terminal rows now gives the COMPLETE identity

 M=q||x0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij
  =||g_n-pi*x0+r^T g||^2
   +(q-pi^2)||x0||^2
   +2<x0,(pi*r-mu/2)^T g>
   +g^T [sym(N Ltri)-r r^T] g.                            (2.3)

Here sym(B)=(B+B^T)/2. No gradient equality, rank condition, or actual-history
restriction was used in obtaining (2.3). Since g_n is a free formal vector,
M is PSD exactly when the entire prefix block in (2.3) is PSD.

For completeness this gives a full coefficient recovery interface. Suppose a
proposed residual is

 (q-pi^2)||x0||^2+2<x0,z^T g>+g^T K g,

where K is symmetric. Define

 P=K+r r^T, mu=2pi*r-2z, w=Ltri^(-1)e.

For a chosen nu>=0, all coefficient matches hold exactly when a skew matrix
A satisfies

 A^T=-A,
 A e=E:=P e-Ltri^T(2alpha+nu),
 A w=F:=mu-P w,
 N=(P+A)Ltri^(-1).                                       (2.4)

One must also impose mu>=0 and N_ij<=0 for EVERY i!=j. These are genuine
additional sign conditions, not consequences of PSD or of the moments.
The complete original array is then

 lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij (distinct queries),
 lambda_(i,star)=mu_i, lambda_(star,i)=nu_i,
 lambda_(n,star)=2pi, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
 all incoming-terminal multipliers zero.                  (2.5)

There is an explicit entry formula, so (2.4) hides no coordinate deletion:

 N_ij=P_ij+A_ij
       -h_j sum_(v>j)(P_iv+A_iv) product_(j<u<v)(1-h_u).   (2.6)

The inverse used here has diagonal1 and, for v>j, entry
-h_j product_(j<u<v)(1-h_u). Multiplication by Ltri proves it by the finite
product telescoping identity; entries above its diagonal vanish.

Because w0=1 and w1=1-h0!=1, e,w are independent. The necessary and sufficient
linear compatibility conditions for the two skew moments in (2.4) are

    <z-v,w-v><=0 for every w in D0.                 (7)

Necessity follows by differentiating squared distance along a segment
from v to w. Conversely expanding ||z-w||^2 shows (7) makes v the unique
nearest point. It suffices to check generating vertices, by linearity.
Adding (7) for two projections proves their firm nonexpansiveness and
hence their 1-Lipschitz property. The two affine maxima bound the remainder
Phi(z')-Phi(z)-<projection_D0(z),z'-z> between 0 and ||z'-z||^2.
Thus Phi is finite, convex, differentiable and 1-smooth, with gradient
projection_D0. These elementary facts also appear in accepted fact
`1e0bf3f41457d8e4`, Part A Section 2; no stronger assertion from that fact
is required here.

At the prescribed points z_k=z_0-P_k, (7) is EXACTLY

    fpot_l-fpot_k<=C_kl for every original ordered pair k,l,
    fpot_k>=K_k for every original k.               (8)

For the second line use w=0. Therefore (8) is both necessary and sufficient
for all v_k, including the terminal v_n, to be the actual projections.
Under (8), z_(k+1)=z_k-h_k grad Phi(z_k) for all k<n, and

    Phi(z_k)=fpot_k-A_kk-G_kk/2,
    Phi(z_n)=fpot_n-c_n>=G_nn/2>0.                 (9)

There is no physical h_n. The complete minimum set is

    Kpolar=cone{v_k}^polar={z:V^T z<=0}, min Phi=0.  (10)

A polar point makes all defining expressions nonpositive, while v=0
supplies zero. If <z,v_k>>0, a sufficiently small positive multiple of
v_k belongs to D0 and has positive defining expression; this proves the
converse. This is the full polar cone, not a selected vertical slice.

## 4. Exact closest-minimum geometry, perspective, and zero boundary

For ANY fpot, let z_0 be (6) and write Rtrue=dist(z_0,Kpolar). Changing
variables d=V^T(z_0-zstar) in the distance minimization gives

    Rtrue^2=r(fpot):=min_(d>=fpot) d^T G^(-1)d.       (11)

Indeed zstar is polar iff V^T zstar=fpot-d<=0, and the vector difference
is V G^(-1)d with precisely that squared norm. The positive definite
quadratic is coercive, so its minimum over the closed nonempty orthant
translate exists and is unique.

For completeness its geometry follows without a duality theorem. At its
minimizer d*, let alpha=G^(-1)d*. Coordinate variations give alpha_k>=0;
if d*_k>fpot_k, both variation signs are allowed and alpha_k=0. Thus

    alpha>=0, d*>=fpot, alpha_k(d*_k-fpot_k)=0.

Put p=V alpha and zstar=z_0-p. Then p belongs to cone{v_k}, zstar belongs
to its polar, and <p,zstar>=0. For any polar y,

    ||z_0-y||^2=||p||^2+||zstar-y||^2-2<p,y>
               >=||p||^2.

This proves the full closest-minimum assertion directly. In particular a
legal fpot has positive radius: fpot_0>=K_0=G_00>0 excludes polarity.

Consider the finite convex program

    maximize 2F_n-2tau c_n
    tau>=0,
    F_l-F_k<=tau C_kl for ALL original ordered pairs,
    F_k>=tau K_k,
    d>=F, d^T G^(-1)d<=tau.                         (12)

The variables F are rescaled potentials. Convexity means the feasible set
is convex and the maximand is linear. There is no solver use here.

Forward direction: for legal fpot set tau=1/r(fpot), F=tau fpot and
choose d=tau d*. Then d^T G^(-1)d=tau and the objective is exactly
2(fpot_n-c_n)/r(fpot).

Reverse direction: given a feasible point with tau>0, fpot=F/tau obeys
ALL of (8), has the unique actual realization (6), and

    r(fpot)<=d^T G^(-1)d/tau^2<=1/tau.

By (9) its terminal numerator is strictly positive. Hence its actual
score is AT LEAST the value of (12). Pointwise equality is not asserted
when the supplied quadratic inequality is slack. At an optimum the two
suprema nonetheless coincide by the two inequalities just proved.

Zero boundary: tau=0 forces d=0 by positive definiteness. The inequalities
d>=F and F>=0 force F=0, so the objective is zero. This point always
exists, independently of itinerary feasibility. Thus (12) equals

    sup({0} union {actual scores of legal initializers}).              (13)

If a legal initializer exists, its score is positive and (13) is exactly
the proposed supremum. If none exists, (12) has only its zero point, while
the conventional supremum of the empty legal set is not zero. Equivalently,
positive-tau feasibility is precisely legal-initializer feasibility.
This qualification matters because full itinerary feasibility is not proved.

The maximum in (12) exists. Since K_0=G_00, feasibility gives
F_0>=tau G_00, d_0>=F_0, and

d^T G^(-1)d>=d_0^2/G_00>=tau^2 G_00.

The first inequality follows by applying Cauchy--Schwarz to
V G^(-1)d and v_0. Consequently tau<=1/G_00 when tau>0. The quadratic
constraint bounds d. The lower bounds F_k>=tau K_k and upper bounds F<=d
then bound F. The feasible set is closed and bounded. If its maximum is
positive, a positive-tau maximizer recovers an actual maximizer via (6).

## 5. Weak-dual signs and complete-square certificate

Let lambda_kl>=0 and nu_k>=0 be any fixed multipliers, and define

    rho=2e_n+out(lambda)-in(lambda)+nu,
    kappa=2c_n-sum lambda_kl C_kl+sum nu_k K_k.

Here e_n is the coordinate vector, out_k=sum_l lambda_kl and
in_k=sum_l lambda_lk. Suppose rho>=0 componentwise and kappa>0.
For every legal potential,

    rho^T fpot-kappa
       =2(fpot_n-c_n)
        +sum lambda_kl [C_kl-(fpot_l-fpot_k)]
        +sum nu_k(fpot_k-K_k)
       >=2(fpot_n-c_n).                             (14)

This explicitly fixes the orientation and both signs. For its closest
polar point zstar, g=V rho belongs to cone{v_k}, so

    rho^T fpot=<z_0,g>
       <=<z_0-zstar,g><=Rtrue ||g||.

Thus, writing b=||g|| and u=1/Rtrue,

    2(fpot_n-c_n)/Rtrue^2
       <=b u-kappa u^2
        =b^2/(4kappa)-kappa(u-b/(2kappa))^2
       <=rho^T G rho/(4kappa).                     (15)

Alternatively, in (12), (14) becomes objective<=rho^T F-kappa tau,
which is <=rho^T d-kappa tau<=b sqrt(tau)-kappa tau; complete the square
in sqrt(tau). This also includes tau=0. No strong-duality assertion is
needed. These multipliers belong to itinerary normals, not the earlier
original smooth-convex GD interpolation dual.

## 6. The exact two-vertex interface and inherited prefix constants

Let r=m-2, Lq=2^r=N/4, i=Lq-1, and put

    theta=x^2 y, s=theta^(Lq/4)=sigma_i,
    t=theta^(N/4)=sigma_n=s^4,
    B=<w_i,w_n>=T-3N/[2(N-1)]+4eta-eta N.           (16)

The index xor is 3N/4 and its popcount is 2. The exact submatrix is

    Gpair=[[s^2 T, s t B],[s t B,t^2 T]].             (17)

It is positive definite as a principal submatrix of G. In particular
T+B>0. Also B<0 and

    T+B=7/6+2/N^2-3/[2(N-1)]-eta(N-4)<7/6.         (18)

The last inequality uses N>=4, with 2/N^2<3/[2(N-1)].

Here are closed finite dyadic formulas for all chronological constants;
they are symbolic identities, not instructions to run a recurrence.
For integers 2<=j<=m, let Pcal_j(z,w) be the following POLYNOMIAL,
with empty products equal to 1:

 [H_0 z+x H_1 z^2 w+x H_0 z^3 w]
       product_(b=0)^(j-3)[1+w(theta z^4)^(2^b)]
 +sum_(l=2)^(j-1) H_l w^l(theta z^4)^(2^(l-2))
       product_(b=0)^(j-l-2)[1+w(theta z^4)^(2^(l-1+b))].              (19)

Its exact expansion is

    Pcal_j(z,w)=sum_(k<2^j-1)h_k sigma_k z^(k+1)w^popcount(k).

For the three low positions k=4q,4q+1,4q+2 use respectively radii
 theta^q,x theta^q,x theta^q and popcounts pop(q),pop(q)+1,pop(q)+1.
For level l>=2 write k=(2q+1)2^l-1: its radius is
 theta^((2q+1)2^(l-2)) and popcount is l+pop(q). Expanding the binary
products in (19) enumerates precisely these disjoint level classes.
This proves the formula without enumeration by a program.

Define the exact sums

    U_j=Pcal_j(1,1),
    M_j=(partial_z Pcal_j)(1,1)-U_j,
    Z_j=(partial_w Pcal_j)(1,1).

Thus they sum h_k sigma_k, k h_k sigma_k, and popcount(k)h_k sigma_k,
respectively. A scalar alternative for the first is

    U_j=(1-theta^(2^(j-2)))
       [(H_0(1+x)+x H_1)/(1-theta)
        +sum_(l=2)^(j-1) H_l theta^(2^(l-2))
                                      /(1-theta^(2^(l-1)))].         (20)

Every denominator is positive. This follows by summing each level's
finite geometric progression in (19).

Put U=U_r,M=M_r,Z=Z_r and

    b_i=T-2(Lq-1)/(N-1)+2eta r-eta N,
    b_n=T-2+2eta m-eta N,
    J_i=b_i U+2M/(N-1)-2eta Z=<P_i,w_i>,
    J_pre=b_n U+2M/(N-1)-2eta Z=<P_i,w_n>,
    J_n=b_n U_m+2M_m/(N-1)-2eta Z_m=<P_n,w_n>.

These use k xor i=i-k for k<i and k xor n=n-k for k<n. In particular

    A_ii=s J_i, A_in=t J_pre, A_nn=t J_n.             (21)

To make the reverse row equally explicit, define

    E_i=sum_(q=0)^3 s^q[J_i+(-2q Lq/(N-1)+2eta popcount(q))U]
       +H_r s T
       +H_(r+1) s^2[T-2Lq/(N-1)+2eta-eta N]
       +H_r s^3[T-4Lq/(N-1)+2eta-eta N].

Then A_ni=s E_i. For each quarter interior k=qLq+j, j<Lq-1, the
radius is s^q sigma_j and k xor i=(q+1)Lq-1-j. The three bridge
indices are qLq-1, q=1,2,3. Their xor values against i are 0,Lq,2Lq.
The q=1 bridge is the actual diagonal and therefore contributes T,
not T-eta N. This proves the displayed expression including its
otherwise easily missed diagonal correction.

All pair data are now exact:

    K_i=s J_i+s^2 T, K_n=t J_n+t^2 T,
    c_n=t J_n+t^2 T/2,
    C_in=t J_pre-s J_i+s t B-s^2 T,
    C_ni=s E_i-t J_n+s t B-t^2 T.                   (22)

Writing u=fpot_i,v=fpot_n, the two-dimensional potential domain is

    u>=K_i, v>=K_n, v-u<=C_in, u-v<=C_ni.            (23)

For p=s^2T,q=t^2T,b=s t B<0, its exact closest-halfspace radius is
min_(d1>=u,d2>=v)(q d1^2-2b d1 d2+p d2^2)/(pq-b^2). Its elementary
active-face cases are:

* If u<=0 and v<=0, the minimum is 0 at d=(0,0).
* If u>0 and v<=b u/p, it is u^2/p at d=(u,b u/p).
* If v>0 and u<=b v/q, it is v^2/q at d=(b v/q,v).
* Otherwise both faces are active: d=(u,v) and the displayed quadratic
  is the value; its two coordinate derivatives are nonnegative.

These follow by setting free-coordinate derivatives to zero and checking
the remaining derivative sign. Boundary overlaps give identical values.
Alternatively the complementarity argument in Section 4 proves the same
exhaustive cases. The positive terminal numerator in (23) is at least
q, and the certificate below forces a positive radius on any feasible
point of (23), so the zero-distance case cannot cause a positive-score
singularity here.

This is a relaxation of the full initializer problem: retaining two
halfspaces enlarges the polar minimum set, so the pair distance is no
greater than Rtrue. The numerator and chronological constants stay
unchanged. Therefore an upper bound for all of (23), with this smaller
distance, is an upper bound for every full legal initializer.
